entry: One of the first Fusion Pokémon documented in Kanto. Research suggests it photosynthesizes at quadruple the rate of a typical Bulbasaur.
author: fixthewifi

entry: It has a striking resemblance to its evolution. Scientists say that the fusion has caused unexpected growth in its DNA to create this appearance.
author: soup1900

entry: The bud on its head blooms as it matures, with the petals drooping down to form a brittle carapace over time.
author: kandyman

entry: Despite their spherical appearance, POKENAME are unable to properly roll to travel. The bulbs on their backs store the electricity that powers them, so they would rather hop than risk damaging it.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME excitedly run about on their short legs. Their lack of balance doesn't hinder them; when they fall, they simply roll back onto their feet. If their bulbs touch the ground, they release an explosion of sparks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME function as a hivemind of seeds from the same plant. Their bodies are divided into faces and bulbs, with the faces handling navigation and fighting, while the bulbs gather energy.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The leaves atop POKENAME sprout from a single bulb, creating a miniature ecosystem within its body. The three heads communicate telepathically, with its leaves extending outward to repel anyone who interrupts them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME wear clay skulls to honor their Bulbasaur ancestors, decorating them with flowers to celebrate life. They wield vines from their bulbs as whips, striking hard enough to carve into the ground.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With masterful vine control, POKENAME carve tunnels or pull fallen trees to create shelter. Their decorative skulls crack as they mature, reflecting the blooming of their bulbs as they grow into warriors.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A POKENAME's limbs are made of coiled vines, allowing them to extend for greater reach or powerful leaps. POKENAME are proud fighters, but in kicking matches, their legs often tangle together.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: While POKENAME possess incredible punching strength, they prefer meditating in sunlight to fighting. When forced to fight, they wrap vines around their fists to cushion the first blow as a warning shot.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME grab berry bushes with their long tongues and shake them to gather all of the berries. Their tongues contain saliva with special nectar that helps plants grow, resulting in more frequent berry supplies.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A POKENAME's body constantly produces spores lighter than air, allowing it to fly. When angered, POKENAME release spores to poison foes, leaving them immobile until enough spores regenerate for flight.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Exposure to direct sunlight dramatically speeds up the evolution process. POKENAME will use its vines to move out of shadows if necessary.
author: kandyman

entry: The bulb at the center of POKENAME acts as a power plant, gathering sunlight and producing spores light enough to lift its body. POKENAME mix these spores with poison to spray as a defense.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME charge into battle, lashing with vines. They only use their horns if their enemy is directly in front, wrapping them in vines before delivering the finishing blow.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's large bulbs provide energy for long runs, so they keep them protected with their tails. They use their long horns to pick berries and share them with pre-evolutions.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME cradle and protect a bulb in their special pouches. The bulb gathers energy through photosynthesis, which transfers to the POKENAME's body, creating a symbiotic relationship.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Unlike most Bulbasaur fusions, POKENAME lack a bulb of their own. Instead, they offer their pouches to stray Bulbasaur, caring for them as if they were their own.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME travel just below the water's surface, with the tips of their bulbs above to absorb sunlight without attracting predators. Disturbing their bulbs triggers furious bubble sprays.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME fires a torrent of seeds at a high velocity from its mouth. Where these seeds land, various plants sprout if conditions are adequate.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME use sharp spines to protect their bulbs, with the smooth interiors cradling them securely. They propel through water by spraying bubbles from their bulbs or snouts.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME use their leafy tails to blend into algae and seaweed. They rest in sunlit spots to gather energy, allowing them to travel farther as they search for coral reefs to tend.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Preferring deep waters, POKENAME require less sunlight than most Bulbasaur fusions. Green spots on their bodies absorb light and produce spores to disguise them in murky waters.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hide amongst tree branches that are growing new leaves, their colouration and bulb helping them blend in with the leaf buds. Their eyesight is poor and they sometimes cluster together on bare branches, believing themselves to be disguised.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The dust from POKENAME's wings accelerates plant growth. Certain flowers tend to grow in its wake. If you want to find POKENAME, follow the flowers.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME likes to be in the sun while it takes in heat and turns it into energy. It rarely gets angry when bothered and likes to keep things peaceful.
author: krsgaming

entry: By gripping rocks with its vines, POKENAME withstands even the strongest ocean currents. It absorbs energy from sunlight, often basking quietly along the shore as the waves lap around it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its vines to anchor itself to rocks and prevent the ocean currents from dragging it away. It feeds on solar energy, so it is often found lying on the shoreline.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME drift along shores, absorbing sunlight and storing energy in their jewels. At night, the glowing jewels appear like constellations scattered along the beach.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME wave their hands in intricate patterns to help plants grow with their psychic powers. Though the motions seem random, they eagerly show off their unique performances.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME use their blade-like arms to dig into soil and plant rows of seeds. They only wield their blades in combat if someone or something threatens their gardens.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME gather leaves from the forest to fashion into elaborate gowns. They pride themselves on their performances, singing in grassy fields at sunrise to welcome the new day.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME spin their arms rapidly to generate electricity and charge their bulbs. Once fully charged, the bulbs glow brightly and can release electrified spores.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME release highly flammable spores from their bulbs. These spores billow like smoke, surrounding foes to weaken them before setting them aflame.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's tail sprays spores that look like flames, constantly shrouding its surroundings in green smoke. These spores absorb sunlight in the air and divide. POKENAME relies on reabsorbing these spores to supplement its nutrition.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME wrap leaves around their horns to avoid tearing through trees as they tend to seeds. Unwrapped horns can slice trees in half in the blink of an eye.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are very popular on farms, where they use their vine tails to help pull plows. The leaves around their necks help them gather sunlight for energy even while they work in the fields.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Unlike Magikarp, POKENAME intentionally leap onto land to absorb sunlight through their leafy fins. However, they still struggle to navigate back into the water efficiently.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME feed on flowers and can be seen swarming from meadow to meadow in the spring. They use the bulb on their back alongside their patterned wings to mimic the flowers they land on, disguising their presence and helping to keep themselves safe.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back contains a potent poison. When threatened, it vibrates the leaf at the tip of its tail as a warning.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME lead parades of Pokémon through forests to celebrate springtime. They gather leaves underfoot, planting sprouts as they travel and watering them on their return to lakes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME transport lost or tired Pokémon great distances, gently cradling them in their bulbs. The temperature in the bulbs is regulated by photosynthesis and POKENAME's ice powers.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME use their gelatinous bodies to navigate tree roots. When they find a secluded spot, they emerge slightly to let their bulbs absorb sunlight, mimicking sprouts to blend in.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are highly adaptable and able to thrive in nearly any environment. It is believed that the bulbs on their back sprout flowers of different functions depending on the climate they live in.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The tail-bulb of every POKENAME stores immense potential for genetic deviation, making every one unique. When they finally bloom, there's no telling what kind of plant may grow from it.
author: chinigan

entry: Living in forest rivers, POKENAME use their fins to reflect sunlight to repel attackers. They dip their tails into rivers and release spores from their bulbs to help purify the water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Living deep within rainforests, POKENAME use their bulbs to store energy from electricity instead of sunlight. They run across treetops during storms, acting as lightning rods to catch stray bolts before they can strike trees.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Living in tropical climates, POKENAME use their leafy tails and manes to absorb energy from sunlight and store it in their bulbs. The excess energy from their photosynthesis runs hot, allowing them to produce flame from their bulbs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Said to have been programmed to help create digital landscapes, POKENAME float through fields to plant seeds. While the seeds are completely organic, POKENAME always seem to buzz in an odd chorus of five notes whenever they start their work.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: By transforming into simple geometric shapes, POKENAME is able to operate in older devices. It can store lots of data in its body, so it can accumulate a large amount of nutrients without changing its weight.
author: oreee0230

entry: A POKENAME's shell is made out of chloroplasts, allowing the body to constantly gain energy from photosynthesis even when hiding within them. The additional weight of the shell causes POKENAME to tire out more frequently.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When curled up, POKENAME looks like a fallen flower bud. POKENAME often floats on the water surface to absorb sunlight, letting the current carry it to distant, unfamiliar places.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME use their vines to help carry their shells during travel or protect them during photosynthesis. If their shells ever crack, they will shoot off spiny seeds as both a defense mechanism and a way to grow a new one.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A wild POKENAME will protect the unarmored bulb on its back with its life. This bulb contains nutrients vital to its future evolution.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: Said to be remnants of ancient plants, POKENAME crawl onto shore during the day to absorb nutrients from sunlight. At night, they return to the water, shedding any spare leaves along the waves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME fashion blades out of the leaves that grow from their arms and use them to fight over sunny territories on beaches. They design the blades with specialized curves that help them catch the water as they swim.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME spread their wings high in the sky to absorb sunlight, casting a fearsome shadow below them. It is believed that these Pokémon ruled ancient forests from the treetops, their piercing cries causing leaves to fall from trees.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight with the bulb growing on its back to store enough energy to take flight. With its powerful jaws, it bites anyone it perceives as a threat to the forest it inhabits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight with the bulb growing on its back to store enough energy to take flight. With its powerful jaws, it bites anyone it perceives as a threat to the forest it inhabits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME wander through forests to gather as many berries as they can. Whatever they don't eat is stored in their bulbs for later. If a POKENAME gets tired before their next meal, they will share the berries with smaller Pokémon before they sleep.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Said to appear on the first or last day of winter, POKENAME's spores can either help collect or clear snow. The frost that POKENAME creates can preserve plants through the winter, allowing them to grow back stronger the following spring.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME flies cloaked in storm clouds, charging its bulb with lightning before producing radiant beams when the storm clears. These concentrated beams of energy will accelerate the growth of plants they touch.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Said to have been brought to life from a stray sprout caught in a wildfire, POKENAME gathers fire along its wings to redirect it away from nature. Once cloaked in flame, POKENAME will emit light to aid in photosynthesis in its environment.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The leafy flower buds along POKENAME's wings do not sustain flight, but help to gather energy from sunlight that it expels along its tail to soar. When POKENAME is fully charged with sunlight, it can swiftly recover from any injury.
author: oreee0230

entry: Carefully coiled around their bulbs, POKENAME will lash out at anyone that threatens them.  Those that take the time to properly train POKENAME will find them to be deeply loyal and affectionate.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME store energy from photosynthesis in the bulbs on their tails. This energy travels along the POKENAME's body, allowing them to produce mystical flames from the orbs on their necks or beams of radiant light from their horns.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Despite their large stature, POKENAME are very docile and friendly Pokémon. If angered, they will shoot a stream of flames from their mouths. These flames contain mystical powers, only harming those that have incurred a POKENAME's wrath.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Exposure to direct sunlight will dramatically speed up the evolution process. POKENAME will use its vines to move out of shadows if necessary.
author: kandyman

entry: The bud on its back carries so much pollen that it must expel at least half its contents daily, lest it become too heavy to fly.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME has been known to drop from tree branches onto prey and unsuspecting Trainers. If the initial ambush fails, it immediately flees.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME shows great interest in plant life and is very protective of nature itself. It's capable of materializing flora out of thin air.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Said to have planted a seed that sprouted into the first tree in Kanto, POKENAME flies throughout the region to look after the growth of forests and budding sprouts. When POKENAME laughs, flowers bloom around it in vivid colors.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It darts through forests at dizzying speeds, never so much as grazing a tree trunk. While it is the unrivaled master of the untouched wilderness, POKENAME's psychic powers wane and become inhibited wherever humans have made inroads.
author: anonymous_16803

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back absorbs sunlight and purifies the surrounding air from toxins and pollutants. If overwhelmed, the leaf on its head wilts, forcing it to rest under the sun until fully restored.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By storing solar energy in its bulb, POKENAME filters nearby air of poison and smog. Should its strength wane, the leaf on its head withers, and it lies motionless beneath the sun until its vitality returns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back can absorb toxins from the air and act as a natural purifier. Since this process tires it out, it needs to rest under the sun for long periods to regain its energy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME carry seeds in the bundles around their neck. When an area is affected by a long drought, these bundles shrivel up so that more resources can be allocated to the bulb on their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through the antennae on its head to keep the leaves around its neck lush and green. Its breath has the power to restore sickly plants to health.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As the leaves on POKENAME's neck absorb sunlight, they release a sweet, soothing scent. These leaves are shed once a year and are used in bitter herbal medicines.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME mow down their foes with flaming, razor-sharp leaves. Once they have achieved victory, they love to receive affection from their Trainer through belly rubs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight and nutrients through the bulb on their back and get minerals by hunting small Pokémon. They rely on their vines to restrain prey before they bite down with their jaws.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Even though POKENAME wake up bright and early to get their daily dose of sunlight, they are sluggish and grouchy as they awaken. Bothering them in the first few moments of the morning has led to many bitten hands.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each POKENAME produces a slightly different nectar in the bulb growing on its back. They live in large communal groups in the wild and harvest each other's bulbs in a ritual resembling group grooming in other species.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME hop between branches to strengthen their wings. If they fall, they must catch themselves with a Vine Whip before hitting the ground.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME wrap themselves around their bulbs to keep them warm while they sleep. They trot around the perimeter of forest clearings while scattering spores that help enrich the soil.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are very active at night, flying between tree tops in competition for the highest point in the canopy. During the day they cling tight to their perch and sun themselves, letting the warm daylight lull them to sleep.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The bulb on the heads of POKENAME produces a nectar that is highly prized by both people and Bug-Type Pokémon. The flavour of the nectar varies through the day and is sweetest in the middle of the night.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Fusing with Bulbasaur has made Ledyba even more sensitive to the cold. POKENAME spends most of its time gathering energy from the sun to survive days with cold weather.
author: darkweavile428

entry: It's said POKENAME inhabits the remote forests of the world where rivers flow clean and the cosmos fill the skies. Curious by nature, it closely examines any plant unfamiliar to it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's silk is mixed with cellulose, making it more adaptable than a those made with protein fibers. Because this silk is less sticky, POKENAME work together to weave large webs to throw at prey and entangle them.
author: oreee0230

entry: From the bulb on its back, it secretes a venomous silk used to weave intricate webs that protect its shelter. Although it lives deep within the forest, POKENAME sometimes wanders into clearings in search of sunlight to absorb.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spends the day asleep, gathering power inside its bulb. At night, it awakens with vigor, using its four wings to glide quickly through the dark forest in search of tender leaves high in the treetops.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The leaves growing along its body also function as wings, allowing POKENAME to glide short distances while foraging for food. It usually leaves its nest very early in the morning to drink the dew that clings to the blades of grass.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME constantly emits poisonous spores to safeguard its territory. The incapacitated trespassers are then either carried out or eaten.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME's buds hide bulbs of light. Thanks to its insulated plant tissues, POKENAME can use electricity more frequently without worrying about electrocuting itself.
author: oreee0230

entry: The bulbs on its head are highly sensitive receptors. POKENAME uses them to communicate with family in shallow waters. In a pinch, this Pokémon will over-charge these bulbs to send an electrical current throughout the water that deters enemies.
author: ludacriswell

entry: On sunny days POKENAME will absorb the sun's rays and on cloudy days it will charge electricity. As a result, POKENAME is often full of energy.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME thrives in the night, feeding on the moon's glow for energy. When a shooting star crosses the sky, it instinctively begins a journey to trace its fall, a mysterious behavior scientists have yet to understand.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It bounces its body to move forward. With each hop, it releases a bit of sweet-smelling pollen into the air.
author: .izik

entry: When exposed to sunlight, it becomes so energized that it can't stop singing. Its soft, bouncy body lets it rebound in all directions. It has to use the vines sprouting from its back to anchor itself when it needs to stay put.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can tuck itself into its bulb-like shell for protection and camouflage. If a predator gets too close, it can also spray a pollen meant to reduce aggression in others and pacify them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME only appears before people who are kind to plants and bestows good luck upon them. It is said that groups of POKENAME regularly migrate to the same forest to gossip about those they give blessings to.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME thrives among weeds, where it hides from larger predators. Its affinity for untended plants allows it to flourish in places other Pokémon avoid.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spread their wings wide while basking in sunbeams, absorbing energy. The seed on its back grows larger over time. It is said that when the seed is ready, it will portend an enigmatic vision of the future.
author: vic1312

entry: Instead of flying, it glides using the leaves that make up its plumage. To change directions, it must shed these leaves in a very precise manner.
author: kandyman

entry: Ranchers will often feed their leftover crops to POKENAME, as the seeds that pop out of their bulb help revitalize the fields. After they are well fed, their leafy mane gives off a healthy green glow.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME store large amounts of electrical energy in their fur and the bulb on their back. In areas lacking reliable transportation, Trainers periodically bring POKENAME to sell electricity.
author: oreee0230

entry: After the rainy season ends, POKENAME comes out to dance in the sunlight. The bulbs on its head gather and store energy from the sun, preparing it for the next rainy season.
author: mistycloud

entry: POKENAME are a rare sight not due to their scarcity, but due to their skill at mimicking young saplings. They are adept at blending in with new growth trees, discernible only by their habit of waving their bulbs around even if there's no wind.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME soar through the sky on wind currents to travel to beautiful places throughout the world. They rarely need to rest for nutrients because the bulb on their back absorbs sunlight and nourishes their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stores the energy it gathers from sunbathing in the bulb that grows on its head. Once warmed enough by the sunlight, it can take flight and ride the wind currents to move to a new area.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can only take flight when wind currents are strong enough to carry it aloft. The pollen it showers from its bulbs is capable of coaxing grass to sprout even through asphalt.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME conducts photosynthesis through its skin cells to gain energy. However, it still loves eating trash just for the fun of it.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME spends its days alternating between frantic foraging and lounging in the sun. Even while resting, this Pokémon is always on alert.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME often purges gardens to better suit its tastes, destroying plants it dislikes. It hates eggplant and will crush them with the heavy fist on its tail, leaving behind only a gross mess.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME use their 360-degree vision to survey their territory, seeking sunny spots to nap for the day. They will settle in bright sunlight, gathering energy in their bulb over time.
author: vic1312

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's head begins to throb when it is nearing evolution. When it opens a stream of goo bursts from it, instantly fertilising nearby fauna. It is toxic to other Pokémon though, causing a stinging sensation lasting a whole day.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is typically found in tropical swamps due to its hunting method. It sinks its head low enough in the water, leaving only the bulb exposed. It eats whatever mistakes it for a lily pad.
author: maximus10k

entry: POKENAME love to laze in bright sunlight, their joy emphasized by the glow of their chest gem. They only wrap their tail-like vines around a Trainer they trust in, aside from using them in battle as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are more active at night than most Grass-type Pokémon. They're often found asleep in a moonbeam.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME emits a scent reminiscent of sage, which other Pokémon find calming. It often carries dried leaves in its mouth, offering them as gifts to those it trusts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its beak to dig into the ground and hide Berries, which it leaves to ferment before eating. Its bulb releases a floral fragrance that induces drowsiness in Pokémon and humans.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have grand revelations about the world around them, but their lack of maturity makes their insights hard to believe. They can become so upset that they hide themselves away from other Pokémon to soothe their egos.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A pack of wild POKENAME will use the bulbs on their backs to disguise themselves as plants on farms. They will lie in wait until night, when they will get up and feast on all the crops in the fields when the farmer is none the wiser.
author: oxitape.

entry: Most of POKENAME's nutrients are supplied to its green leaves. This large green structure allows it to use sunlight with remarkable efficiency.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME can be found near forest areas emitting puffs of pink pollen from their bulbs, which contain essential nutrients for plants. Caterpie often trail behind POKENAME, knowing that the tastier plants grow because of them.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: People often mistake POKENAME for an Oddish fusion. It's only when they see its face that they realise it is no Oddish.
author: watermelonchild

entry: POKENAME have leafy sprouts on their back. On sunny days, these leaves curl open to absorb sunlight, curling back into a bulb at dusk to conserve energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME keep their incisors at a manageable length by gnawing on tough vegetation and discarded scraps. Despite their short legs, they move quickly.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: This Pokémon's head contains an enormous amount of nutrients. It spends much of its time fleeing from herbivores who mistake it for a seed.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME is often seen floating aimlessly towards brightly lit areas. During rainy days, it would hide itself underground for protection.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME float towards whatever light they can find in ancient ruins. They produce vines that take the shape of the letter B.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME takes the shape of the letter B and appears at various ruins. Its flower buds can be flattened to the same thickness as its body and can immediately puff up when needed.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's body is covered with tiny buds that accumulate energy from impacts. It enjoys basking in the sun and typically remains docile so long as its tail is not attacked.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's tail has limited cognitive abilities and relies on its head to give commands. Although its neural pathways stretch several meters, when the main head gives the order to strike, the tail can instantly unleash powerful Grass-type moves.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME collects moss to cover its body, helping it stay hidden from predators. The moss also serves as insulation, keeping it warm during cooler nights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by thick leaves that shield them from danger. Whenever they need to fight back, they shoot out seeds from the spikes on their body until they run out of seeds or their foe loses interest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back requires a lot of nutrients to flourish, so it is constantly foraging for food. Many species subsist largely by rummaging through trash, causing the pollen the bulb produces to be foul in stench.
author: sk372

entry: Groups of POKENAME often squabble over food even if there is excess. Their sensitivity to pollution means they are rarely seen in urban environments.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: Although POKENAME's claws look like a single bud when pressed together, the claws are actually made up of three buds. Although they are soft, the claws can grip with lots of pressure once they absorb sunlight.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME collects a large amount of withered plants inside its shell, and then hangs itself in a cool and ventilated place using vines. Although the fermented liquid has a fragrant scent, its most suitable use is as a fertilizer.
author: oreee0230

entry: In particularly high-stress situations, POKENAME shoves its mouth full of berries to calm its nerves. The bulb on its back swells as it stores the excess nutrients.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Its body consists of an unknown liquid. When deprived of enough sunlight, the liquid hardens and renders POKENAME unable to move.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME secretes a dense, corrosive liquid that burns organic matter it touches. Debris such as fallen leaves or tree branches burns without sinking into the liquid, leaving behind ash and smoke.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME is extremely friendly, and eager to share the nutrients within its bulb with others. Unfortunately, its body is entirely compost, and smolders too hot for most other Pokémon to withstand.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME diligently grooms its bulb and feathers to remove anything that might disrupt photosynthesis. Its long neck makes reaching everywhere easy.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME nest within thick shrubs and bushes with their bulbs exposed to collect sunlight and rainwater. POKENAME will search and root for underground water with their noses, though they often end up disturbing gardens in the process.
author: infinex21

entry: The sunlight POKENAME absorb is funneled into their branches, which grow rapidly to conceal their appearance. Due to deforestation, sightings of these Pokémon have become increasingly rare.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME swim in tropical waters and love to stay in the shallows, sunning the bulb on their back. Their bulb builds up and stores oxygen, which POKENAME can shoot out as a concentrated bubble stream.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME collect seeds within their tails to keep them warm and protected while their leaves photosynthesize. The seeds planted after being held by POKENAME will grow big and strong in vibrant colors.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The bulb atop its head absorbs sunlight as POKENAME flies above the lush jungle canopies where it nests. It must take in large amounts of energy through photosynthesis to improve its flight performance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It continuously absorbs sunlight through the bulb on its back, fueling endless flight across its vast territory without rest. By powerfully beating its wings, POKENAME releases soothing spores that calm everything in its surroundings.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When startled, POKENAME will rattle the seeds contained in the bud on the end of its tail. These seeds are considered a delicacy when sun-dried.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME is often found at the bottom of dense kelp forests. Oblivious Pokémon that wander into its territory are immediately shot with massive seeds.
author: schwaus

entry: It is a rare Pokémon that has been spotted in the wild only in lush and open areas. It has incredible hearing ability; by manipulating roots to drum the ground through its ability to control plants, it can send messages to faraway POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME help farmers plow fields by dragging equipment behind them. This serves as great entertainment while also keeping them in sunlight to nourish the bulb on their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be found cultivating bags of rice on websites throughout the internet and gain energy from children submitting answers to quizzes. Their glee whenever a child submits a correct answer motivates many children to keep playing the game.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because POKENAME do not need to eat, many are selected to help astronauts in outer space. Their vines both provide maneuverability and a source of oxygen for space stations.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME is one of the most gentle Pokémon to live. If it finds an injured creature, it'll wrap their wound up in vines like a bandage.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME gathers the energy needed to create illusions using the bulb on its tail, which converts sunlight. It feeds on the mold that grows on tree bark, helping the forest remain healthy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME love to collect different-colored flowers and arrange them around their territories in various formations. They will often leave a signature, which varies between each individual, upon their floral arrangements using their paint-like fluids.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spin in sunny clearings, exercising or conserving energy depending on how they spin. When attacking foes, POKENAME extend their vines to strike multiple times while spinning.
author: oreee0230

entry: Its curious nature leads it to kiss things as a way of exploring its surroundings. If POKENAME particularly enjoyed kissing something, a puff of pollen in the shape of a heart floats from the bulb on its head.
author: sk372

entry: Curiosity leads POKENAME to kiss at things as it explores its surroundings. If something tries to avoid being kissed, vines sprout from its head to grab and reel in its target.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight using their bulbs on their backs, storing it within their bodies. By stabbing their horns into a tree, they can release this energy, boosting the trees growth significantly.
author: santon5512

entry: The bulb on the tails of POKENAME has dry leaves and loose seeds, enabling it to make a rattling noise when they shake their tail. They use this as a warning and can fling the seeds at high velocity at their foes if threatened.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can absorb large amounts of sunlight due to the surface area of its patterned belly. Using this energy, it can go months without eating.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME spews bright flames from its mouth when it is healthy. Ironically, these flames can set fire to the bulbs on its head, damaging them.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME constantly exposes its bulb to sunlight to improve the quality and flavor of the milk it can produce. Because of its gentle and courteous nature, it is highly appreciated by farmers and is frequently found in rural areas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Even though the bud in the flower pot has not yet bloomed, POKENAME can still release a fragrance with healing effects. POKENAME wanders around the forest, always ready to offer help.
author: oreee0230

entry: According to legend, POKENAME wanders the world absorbing the energy of thunderstorms. Inside its green bulb, it contains enough energy to light up a city for weeks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: According to legend, POKENAME wanders the world absorbing the energy of thunderstorms. Inside its green bulb, it contains enough energy to light up a city for weeks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME infuses water around them with nutrients that help plants germinate. Once it masters this power, it evolves.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME love to eat mossy rocks, though they can settle for rocks mixed with moss as well. The bulb upon a POKENAME's head grows steadily as it naps in bright sunlight.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is found rooted atop high mountains. Its plant tissue contains high amounts of calcium, strengthening its body to resist harsh sandstorms.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME often appears in tropical cyclones, bathing in the sun's rays in the cloudless eye of the storm. It bends sunlight using the ocean's natural refraction to focus light onto its body, rapidly absorbing solar energy.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME loves sleeping on and eating solar panelling, much to the annoyance of energy companies. A single panel can keep a herd fed for a week.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME emerge from hiding after a period of heavy rain to blow clouds away and make room for the sun, creating rainbows in the process. They release seeds from their bulb to take opportunity of the sunlight and freshly watered soil.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME excitedly gather berries to brew into potions within the bulbs they carry. Once their concoctions are ready, they plant the bulbs that will grow into beautiful trees with leaves of various colors.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME have a mineral rich body, dense with a crystal lattice predominantly formed of emeralds that give them their green hue. Their rock-hard bodies protect the delicate bulbs growing from their head.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The more electricity POKENAME consumes, the larger the bulb at the tip of its tail becomes. Petals can be seen poking out as it approaches evolution.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME are herbivorous creatures that have shown to be knowledgeable enough to raise their own crops. They do, however, have a bad habit of forgetting their stockpiled seeds in their long fur.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME work together in small groups to create small gardens in the wild, each with a plethora of flowers and bushes. They collect and store seeds in the bulb on their back to bring back to their garden, where they plant and care for these seeds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It fires small seeds from its arms that grow incredibly quickly once they hit the ground. POKENAME has commonly been used to help reforestation efforts.
author: mistymagius

entry: With the drills on its body, POKENAME bores holes into trees where Sentret can take shelter. It needs plenty of sunlight to move its large body, so it spends the entire day basking in it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME seems to be controlled by the bulb on its head. It rarely moves, as its tendrils can grab anything nearby, but it becomes extremely energetic in the sun.
author: lootererswillbeboated

entry: Inside POKENAME's bulb is the organ that generates the powerful electricity within its body. It channels this power directly into its vines, which whip around while electrically charged in order to defend its bulb from harm.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME burrow into the desert sand to rest during the day, leaving their bulbs above ground to absorb nutrients from sunlight.
author: raza

entry: It uses its sharp fangs to bite into fruit and suck out all of the juices, though it can also do this with hard nuts. A fragrant aroma wafts from its plant bulbs, though the specific scent is influenced by what it has eaten.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has a seed on its head that it gains nourishment from as it grows. It protects this new growth with sharp leaf-like appendages that sprout from the sides of its head. POKENAME tend to use photosynthesis, but also enjoy the taste of berries.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME fly around their opponents, releasing clouds of spores from their bulbs to poison them and wear them down. Outside of battle, they reduce the toxicity of the spores to heal damage done to their allies instead.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME, despite needing sunlight in order to photosynthesize and grow its bulb, spends most of its time in the shade. When it finally goes into the sunlight, it feels sudden urges to use its energy by unleashing powerful moves all around it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME climb trees by relying on their specialized toe pads. Each pad has miniature vines that cling to whatever surface they are on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME always tries to expose its lush tail to sunlight so that it can feed through photosynthesis and remain at full strength. Despite its mild nature, it does not hesitate to chase away anyone who threatens to cause damage to the woods.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often trip and stumble due to the bulb upon their heads, though they always get back up. They use vines to hold their foes before blasting them with fireballs.
author: infinex21

entry: The feathery leaves sprouting from the bulb on its head help POKENAME blend into the surrounding foliage. POKENAME enjoys bathing in sunlight to warm its body and nurture its bulb.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME shoot out razor-sharp leaves from the bulb on their back. These leaves are so sharp that a single graze causes a cut.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When this Pokémon does not eat, POKENAME relies on the energy stored in the muscles of its legs to keep it going. If POKENAME relies too heavily on this ability, it will become slower in fights due to a lack of nutrients.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: In combat, POKENAME sprouts vines from its arms to ensnare its foes. Once they're pulled into range, it unleashes kicks with blinding speed, chaining strikes in rapid succession.
author: potato_tub

entry: The bulb growing on POKENAME's head is directly affected by the emotions of Trainers surrounding it. If it seems dull and neglected, POKENAME's bulb has absorbed negative energy.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME have bulbs atop their heads that absorb emotional energy from their Trainers. A fresh, brightly colored bulb means that they have plenty of positive energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are determined to make their Trainer proud, as the health of the bulb on their head absorbs the positive energy from their Trainer. A shriveled and withered bulb is a sign of neglect.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its power to see the future to ensure the sun's rays always hit the seed on its back. If POKENAME predicts a threat to its Trainer, the bulb blooms instantly, releasing psychic pollen that halts the foe.
author: de_19.

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight through their heads, channeling this energy into their Razor Leaf attacks. At full power, the leaves along their arms are capable of cutting  through trees with a single swing.
author: santon5512

entry: No matter how much sun POKENAME takes in, its body does not warm up; the energy of the light is completely absorbed. Besides sunbathing, POKENAME has no other needs and sometimes sneaks out of Poké Balls to fly towards sunlight.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME tend to keep to themselves. If it feels that the bulb on its back is threatened, however, it will attack with its poisonous horns.
author: incognito1234

entry: As it grows, POKENAME's ability to communicate with other POKENAME reaches further and further. The limit to how far a POKENAME can potentially contact another is not known. When flowers bloom across its body, it is ready to evolve.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The more sunlight the grassy bulb on its head absorbs, the more energy POKENAME's brain will have to solve even the most complex problems. It is so heavy that when it walks, it leaves tracks in the ground, making it very easy to follow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: No one can wake POKENAME as it naps in the sun. However, when the sun sets, it becomes far more energetic than its sleeping habits would suggest.
author: mysteriouswraith

entry: POKENAME resembles a flower bud in a flowerpot. In battle, POKENAME releases spores that, when inhaled, interfere with its opponent's abilities.
author: oreee0230

entry: Thanks to the bulb on its head, POKENAME can sense the auras of living beings around it. Its muscles are as hard as steel because it trains daily by punching the trunks of large trees.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The plant growing on the back of POKENAME is slow-growing, requiring a lot of sunlight and nutrients to blossom. They spend their days curled up in the sun warming the flower bulb, waiting for it to bloom.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The plant growing on the back of POKENAME is slow-growing, requiring a lot of sunlight and nutrients to blossom. They spend their days curled up in the sun warming the flower bulb, waiting for it to bloom.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The flower blooming on the back of POKENAME is immature and still fragile. They keep their leaves furled around the fragile petals, keeping the flower safe until it's fully ready to bloom.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It lures in its foes with its innocent-looking head and sweet fragrance. Once the foe's guard is down, it will strike them down with its massive body.
author: soup1900

entry: It cares deeply for fellow fused Pokémon. It is often caught in a dilemma between protecting its own bulb and those of other POKENAME.
author: fixthewifi

entry: The carnivorous sprout on POKENAME's head is newly developed and not very intelligent, relying on the body to guide it. If it's not fed regularly, it throws a tantrum and tries to rip itself from the body.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wanders around, using its cute appearance to lure prey close. POKENAME's big, colorful  mouth can hide in its hair when not chewing.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME have limited options for feeding because their tentacles have not yet developed mouths to capture small Bug-type Pokémon with. They rely on eating anything that crosses their path, as their heavy body prevents them from chasing prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME struggle to keep their head raised when they charge at foes, leading them to trip over themselves. Over time, they slowly develop neck muscles to keep their head raised to protect the flower bulb on their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If a member of its evolutionary family is threatened, POKENAME will lash out violently with its horns to protect it, even at the risk of damage to its own bulb.
author: fixthewifi

entry: POKENAME lives in hidden, greenery-filled caves deep underground. To find one naturally is considered a sign you are near an awe-inspiring sight.
author: veteranadventurer

entry: POKENAME's chlorophyll-powered body assumes a less corporeal form than other Grass-type Pokémon. The skull-shaped formations on its front instill great fear in all who witness it.
author: honowo

entry: POKENAME often appears in cemeteries to care for the flowers placed before the graves of the deceased. Rumor has it that its body is hollow and that it is moved solely by the bulb it carries atop its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It often appears in cemeteries to care for the flowers placed before the graves of the deceased. Rumor has it that its body is hollow and that POKENAME is animated solely by the grassy bulb that surrounds its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The body beneath POKENAME's flower bud is incorporeal, allowing it to hide in tall grass. It is said that when it encounters lost ghosts, POKENAME uses the large mouth on its abdomen to swallow them and send them to the afterlife.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME is a beloved low-maintenance pet, content to float on the surface of water and absorb rays of sunlight. It will often be released back into the sea before evolving, as most owners can't handle its colossal size increase and bad temperament.
author: ecstaticwoop64556455

entry: Specimens of POKENAME are extremely rare to encounter, as they are said to spend most of their lives resting under the sun of their home dimension. The energy they store within the bulb on their back could give rise to new species of Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME drinks the clear waters of lakes to help the bulb on its back grow healthy and strong. It is an incredibly gentle and patient creature, which is why it is often considered a good Pokémon for young Trainers beginning their journey.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME absorbs pure lake water to nourish the bulb growing on its back. Its mild temperament and patience make it a trusted companion for novice Trainers taking their first steps into the world.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Thanks to the two leaves on its head, POKENAME can locate sources of clean water where it can drink. It spends most of its time absorbing as much solar energy as possible into its body to become stronger and stronger.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME absorbs pure lake water to nourish the bulb growing on its back. Its mild temperament and patience make it a trusted companion for novice Trainers taking their first steps into the world.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The plants that grow on POKENAME's back regularly bear fruit and berries over time. The flavor is simple, but the fruit is quite nutritious, particularly for young Pokémon's development.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have large ears to protect the bulbs on the back of their heads. These ears act as solar panels, absorbing sunlight to produce energy through photosynthesis.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It is a poor walker, possibly due mostly to the growing plant bulb on its back. Sometimes it lies still after falling, which usually happens if it has overexerted itself. It will lie still and bathe in sunlight until it has regained its strength.
author: infinex21

entry: It is very energetic and playful, despite how it fervently rejects any help from others. One of its favorite pastimes seems to be sliding on its belly atop mud, even if it has to make the mud itself.
author: infinex21

entry: Colonies of POKENAME help maintain the bodies of water they live in. POKENAME use the pure water to help the bulbs on their heads grow. Any pollution or polluters are attacked without mercy.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME store water within their heavy bodies to keep their hardy bulb from drying out and wilting. If they ever have an excess of water, such as from absorbing rain, the excess will drain from their noses.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME slowly graze through large spans of grass as they suck up and eat the hordes of bugs they encounter. Some have been utilized by lawn cutting businesses.
author: camtft

entry: When bludgeoning won't do the job, this haunted, club-like Pokémon expels plant-based projectiles from its seed head.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is particular about which Trainers it allows close, as it often chases Trainers out of the forests they live in. It is said that those who lose to a POKENAME meet an unfortunate end.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME use the horns on their head to move roots at the bases of trees, creating a sleeping spot. They sleep with only their heads and bulbs above ground, gathering energy in the morning through photosynthesis.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME appear in overgrown factory grounds. Starting their lives as amorphous balls of plant mass, they seek out scrap metal to inhabit and protect themselves.
author: ocxin

entry: POKENAME's body features a mane of leaves that absorb electric particles from the air. The energy is stored in the bulb on its back, which it uses to unleash powerful electrified attacks against its foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Parts of POKENAME's body are covered with leaves as hard as steel. In fact, even seeds shot from its bulb are coated with a thin layer of metal, though they can grow after being planted like any normal plant.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be seen napping around lakebeds, quietly absorbing sunlight through the bulb on its tail.
author: fuzzythelion

entry: POKENAME swim gracefully in swampy areas with large bodies of water. Each autumn, they shed their leaves, which are prized as ingredients for making dye.
author: flickeredflame

entry: This Pokémon is popular among gardeners for its cuteness. Its long, ribbon-like vines are used to absorb additional sunlight while photosynthesizing.
author: melodydelune

entry: An extremely kind and nurturing Pokémon, POKENAME uses its vines as an extension of its limbs. It enjoys using these to play with many small Pokémon.
author: volvonovic

entry: Despite their large stature, POKENAME are very nurturing Pokémon. They burrow with sprouts, gathering sunlight in their large ears and enriching the soil through photosynthesis to grow new trees.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME can be found living in deep rivers in tropical rainforests, spraying water into the air to water the plants around them. Once the entire rainforest is soaked with their water, they create channels to spread their domain.
author: oreee0230

entry: The thick, heavy leaves on POKENAME's back are specialized for extreme water retention. This adaptation allows the Pokémon to survive when a drought comes for long periods without needing to find a fresh water source .
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME is known for shaping continents by launching seeds from its back that sprout into dense forests. As it evolves, the trees that it once planted become more resilient.
author: over9001

entry: Soaring at high altitudes, POKENAME absorbs sunlight without being affected by greenhouse gases. It always stays in the sun's rays and is drawn to meteors.
author: oreee0230

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back is immune to the effects of time manipulation. Even with its temporal powers, it must wait patiently for the bulb to grow naturally.
author: soup1900

entry: It fiercely defends the large bulb growing on its back. Rumors say the bulb contains an entirely separate dimension inside it.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Wild POKENAME are almost never active during the day. At night, they can be found haunting young Trainers who did not choose Bulbasaur as their starter Pokémon.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The bud cannon that's on POKENAME's back also functions like a vacuum, sucking in nutrients to help sustain itself. It has artificial mechanisms that photosynthesize sunlight for the Pokémon.
author: soup1900

entry: The bud behind POKENAME keeps oozing venom, but most of it seeps into its shell before dripping onto the ground. During battle, the venom is squeezed out onto enemies with force.
author: oreee0230

entry: Their strange bulbs glow on nights of the full moon. It is said that a POKENAME's bulb contains Moon Stones that channel their mystical powers and allow them to fly.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's bulbs are filled with different spores. The left shoots out poison, the right one stuns, and the back makes you sleep.
author: xenophacilus

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back is filled with air that expands when heated up, allowing them to float during the day. They float about in large groups, holding on to one another with vines.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is even more difficult to spot than other species of Ninjask due to the plants on its body helping it to blend in with other greenery. It grows leaves around its head to muffle its normally loud cries.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Whenever POKENAME gets excited, cursed energy seeps out from the bulb on its head. Trainers who abandon Grass-type Pokémon may find POKENAME stalking them.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by ethereal plasma that bends to allow them to slip through narrow gaps. They rescue children and small Pokémon stuck in crevices by extending tentacles made of this plasma.
author: oreee0230

entry: Appearing in gardens under the light of the full moon, POKENAME release a strange, mystical light from their bulbs that helps flowers bloom in vivid color.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its fragrant cotton is used to stuff the pillows found in all the world's top five-star hotels. When POKENAME is not taking long naps in the sun, it enjoys chasing leaves blown by the wind.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lies in dense forests, using its appendages to grab and eat small Bug-type Pokémon. It then uses the nutrients to nourish the bulb. No one knows what plant matter is inside the coffin.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME relies on its electrified webs for hunting, as its legs are fragile. Its webs are mixed with photoreceptors, allowing them to remain charged with electricity for long periods of time without maintenance.
author: oreee0230

entry: It hangs around the treetops of dense forests waiting for prey. POKENAME will drop poisonous thorns, hoping to prick and incapacitate wild Pokémon below.
author: sly.crook

entry: POKENAME's bulb is filled to the brim with flammable liquid. It waddles slowly to avoid spilling a single drop.
author: xenophacilus

entry: POKENAME float above the jungle forests, lighting the way for people and Pokémon alike. They are regarded as beneficent, as POKENAME are never seen damaging the forest using their flames.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have seed pods along their vines that reach towards the sky to absorb sunlight. When another plant covers their sunlight, they burn the plants around them until they can feel the sun again.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bulb atop POKENAME's head is said to hold ancient secrets that were thought to be lost to time. While it is capable of wandering dark ruins, it prefers to soak in the sun's rays.
author: oreee0230

entry: They can often be spotted with flowers on their tails. Each tail can grow a different flower species on it depending on the POKENAME's environment.
author: kitarchen

entry: POKENAME gathers solar energy in the bulb on its back to boost its fire powers. It rubs its many tails against trees and bushes, spreading sweet pollen that ripens fruit in an instant.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hide among the short grass at beaches, gathering energy from the sun while they sleep. Sometimes, large groups of POKENAME join together to imitate grass and avoid preying bird Pokémon.
author: leandermalurt

entry: POKENAME injects vitality into plants to unlock newfound growth, allowing these plants to mature early. Once these plants fully ripen, POKENAME sucks chlorophyll from the plants to nourish its own body.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a Bulbasaur and usually operates in places where wild Bulbasaur are scarce. The bud on POKENAME's back may feel like other parts of its fabric body, but this part can also absorb nutrients and grow as well.
author: oreee0230

entry: The heads on each of POKENAME's vines are not as strong as the one on its body, but can extend to grab objects and feed themselves. POKENAME can use the leaves on its back to fly when needed.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME channels sunlight through the bulb on its back to intensify its fiery abilities. By brushing its tails across plants, it releases a fragrant dust that ripens nearby fruit in moments.
author: fiordaliso

entry: An enormous flower bud sprouts from its tail. The large growing bloom inside radiates mystical heat.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's presence uncontrollably mutates any plants in its surroundings. Scientists believe this is due to POKENAME's unstable DNA.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The bulb covering its head protects its powerful mind. It senses beings with small, paper-like growths that emanate psychic energy.
author: rhysanthemum

entry: POKENAME rarely move from one spot because they rely on their vines to do everything. From building dams to putting food in their mouths, their vines work nonstop to give them everything they need to survive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can sense the soul of nature growing around it and rushes to help plants it feels are suffering. It lives in the undergrowth, using vines to swing quickly from branch to branch.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As long as POKENAME receive sunlight, they do not need to breathe. On sunny days out in the open ocean, they can be found upside-down to nourish the bulb with the sun's rays. Many bird Pokémon perch on their stomachs to rest.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME stores electricity inside the bulb on its back, using the energy in battle when needed. Its grassy-scented fur has the ability to calm anyone who comes into contact with it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As POKENAME sing, they sway back and forth, rattling the seeds inside their bulb. If people fall asleep from the soothing song, POKENAME spray spores from their bulb in anger.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME actively consumes minerals, making the bud on its back as tough as metal. When it evolves, the outer layer of its bud is shed and can be used as a special high-strength material.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME hides beneath the sand, leaving only its green bulb exposed so it can sustain itself by absorbing sunlight. When someone approaches its position, it bursts out of the ground and snaps its jaws shut on the unfortunate intruder.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hides beneath the sand, leaving only its green bulb exposed so it can sustain itself by absorbing sunlight. When someone approaches its position, it bursts out of the ground and snaps its jaws shut on the unfortunate intruder.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The cactus on POKENAME's back can store a large amount of water during the rainy season. POKENAME buries its body in the sand and uses the water-filled cactus to lure small Pokémon.
author: oreee0230

entry: To prevent its wings from being damaged by the desert sun, POKENAME spends most of the day safely within oases. The bulb on its back not only converts sunlight into energy but also stores water, allowing it to survive even in scorching habitats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live in ponds that are heavily infested with weeds. They tend to sleep on the surface on their sides, absorbing sunlight and playing dead for predators.
author: smashbear

entry: Wild POKENAME are drawn to tall areas, such as mountains, so they can be closer to the sun. They will flee to protect their plant bulbs, even though their bodies are quite strong.
author: infinex21

entry: The plates of its shell function like leaves. These plates peel and shed every few days to give way to more vibrant and tougher plates. Each shed plate holds many nutrients and can be ground up and used in various ways.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's gears turn steadily, nourishing the bulb attached to the second gear. It can use its vines to turn the bulb's gear faster, overclocking it and making it erupt pollen to agitate attackers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rotate their gears throughout the day to ensure all the bulbs receive the same amount of sunlight. Once all their bulbs are fully charged with sunlight, they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If it doesn't absorb enough solar energy, POKENAME cannot create its illusions. To avoid being bothered by other forest Pokémon, it sometimes takes on a human appearance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Although the rest of its body has matured, its seed remains as it is. Scientists believe the seed will remain dormant for the entirety of its life.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME prioritizes developing a mature appearance, even though its body size remains unchanged from fusion. Because the surface area of its leaves is small, it needs to spend almost the entire day basking in the sun to continue growing.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME has to be careful not to accidentally burn its bulb with the flame on its tail. If that happens, it can take weeks for the bulb to grow back.
author: benevolent

entry: POKENAME naps during the day to absorb more sunlight. When night falls, it uses the flame on its tail to replicate sunlight, giving it energy to walk.
author: dandistorted2

entry: POKENAME inflate their bulbs to fly. As they sing, they scatter seeds from their bulbs, creating beautiful gardens where people can rest.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It happily gathers seeds during the daytime then spreads them at night. When it concentrates, it can make the seeds grow faster.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flower buds emit a pleasant fragrance, but are also full of venom. Once it senses a threat, POKENAME will squeeze out the venom to shoot at foes while retreating to a safe distance.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME floats gently through the air, drifting aimlessly over forests and fields. It occasionally latches onto plants below, leaving behind a trail of spores.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are standoffish when they are first captured but respond well to affection and respect. Whenever they are happy, they release a sweet aroma from the bulbs on their ears.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produces nut-like spores that taste similar to pecans. In autumn, it scatters these spores across the forest floor, enriching the soil for the next season.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wanders through city gardens feeding on negative emotions, particularly anger and resentment. It is most active during the day, as its body converts sunlight into energy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a bubble of thick sap that allows them to photosynthesize using the surface of their bubble. This ability increases the amount of chlorophyll within the sap, turning it into a light green hue.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although it has no discernible sensory organs, POKENAME can perceive its surroundings through its psychic abilities. While it can adapt to various harsh environments, it will go into hibernation if it does not get sunlight for a long time.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME has two independent brains, one shaped like a bulb. When this Pokémon absorbs enough solar energy, the bulb-shaped brain synchronizes with the other, unleashing powerful psychic powers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME burrow into the ground with only their eyes and bulbs exposed. Their bulbs refract light in small sparkles to resemble the spines of a cactus and keep away predators.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME expands its body size by inhaling. Its belly can stretch 20 times its original size, increasing the available surface area it has to absorb sunlight.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME sleep on the sides of caves during the day, exposing only their bulbs to sunlight. At night, they gather berries and plant them near their caves for easier access.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME traps the souls of other weak Pokémon it consumes within the bulb. It is nocturnal, gaining energy from the sun while it rests to sustain its nightly hunts.
author: crumple_2

entry: It gnaws on power cables until the bulb on its back is fully charged. Despite its small size, POKENAME fearlessly repels threats by electrifying its grassy vines.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If left unattended for long enough, even one POKENAME can grow a root system that will absorb all the nutrients from an entire acre of land, leaving the crops within completely ruined.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME tusks are hard as stone yet have a composition akin to leaves. They crush up berries to eat, and get their other nutrients via the sunlight absorbed through their bulbs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are aggressive, and relentlessly attack nearby bug Pokémon. It often rests in the sunlight, which heals its green feathers.
author: adam941

entry: POKENAME strategically builds its nest so that it is always bathed in sunlight. Due to its gentle nature, it prefers a diet rich in Berries rather than hunting other creatures.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME sink their fangs into trees to absorb nutrients for their bulbs, often leaving withered trees near cave entrances. Drinking too much can make their bulbs too heavy to fly.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time absorbing the sunlight, and its leaf-like appearance helps it avoid any trouble.
author: zweizweihander

entry: POKENAME crawls along tree branches in search of the shiniest, most colorful fruit to eat. Its eyes are underdeveloped and have not bloomed yet, so it struggles to see objects that are not vibrant.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The lower body of a POKENAME absorbs energy from sunlight during the day and glows faintly at night. POKENAME draw in prey with this glow and shoot them with poisonous needles to knock them out.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are enveloped in still developing leaves that cushion their rolling. These developing leaves cling close to their body to prevent tears, as these leaves are meant to last until they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME roll through the jungle in a blur of celadon green to protect the forest they call home. When they inevitably come across loggers, they unleash a flurry of poisonous pollen to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides in hollow flower buds and eats snow to hydrate. When rolling in the snow, it picks up so much snow that it finds itself embedded in a giant snowball.
author: oreee0230

entry: When in battle, POKENAME shoots the freezing air trapped inside its body through the bulbs on its head. When its internal temperature begins to rise, it lies in deep snow banks to restore its sub-zero temperature.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME uses the vines wrapped around its waist to snare unsuspecting climbers in the snow. Once caught, they are dragged silently back to its home.
author: ambrosia04

entry: Smaller than the bulbs they carry, POKENAME live in gardens, relying on people or Pokémon to care for them. Healthy POKENAME with a good home grow darker green bulbs with budding signs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME dances using its vines as ribbons. The age and health of a POKENAME is indicated by the size and color of the bulb on its back.
author: robbery_666

entry: The bulbs on POKENAME's wingtips absorb sunlight and excess electrical energy generated by its dancing. When cheering fervently, the bulbs grow larger and produce small clouds of electrically charged spores.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME gives off an eerie presence, unsettling those who venture too close. Its movements are slow and deliberate, leaving others unsure whether to approach or retreat.
author: .izik

entry: When in danger, POKENAME maneuvers around the foe with graceful choreography, spreading poisonous pollen with each flutter of its wings. When the threat succumbs to the toxins, POKENAME flees silently from the battle.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME are found in garbage cans and dumpsters where they eat spoiled food. They typically have low self-esteem and are thrilled whenever a Trainer wants to have them on their team.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on their bulbous tail to swim, rocking the tail back and forth to propel them through the water. As they swim, they release seeds that float in the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are despised by fishermen because they often cut fishing lines with their sharp fins and eat the bait at the end of hooks. When POKENAME feel particularly mischievous, they yank on fishing lines to drag fishermen into the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are known for being docile, normally, but fierce when provoked; to them, provocation can be wrought by harming plant life. They secrete a substance similar to resin from their vines, which they apply to trees to mend any damages.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are constantly dizzy and tired, as they spend most of their energy from photosynthesis on growing new leaves. They often fall asleep standing up without realizing, taking a few more steps before their bodies settle to rest.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is little more than a seed carried on the wind. Its cotton turns stark white if it doesn't get consistent sunlight -- usually indicating a POKENAME that prefers to roost in the shade.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME is little more than a seed carried on the wind. Its cotton turns a vivid green if it gets a lot of sunlight, which confident POKENAME tend to do.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME flies in the billowing white clouds, collecting sunlight for the seed on its back to grow.
author: deciduowl

entry: POKENAME nourish themselves by soaking in sunlight and spend several hours a day just sunbathing. They produce sticky spores from their bulbous heads to defend themselves, as the corrosive spores eat through fur and skin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's leaves are incredibly thick and can be seen with large bite marks taken out of them. Its thorns eject a mild poison that is mainly used to physically weaken its opponents.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME smears mucus on flower buds to mix toxins from poisonous flowers, integrating the chemicals into its own body. It only drinks from small puddles to avoid contaminating larger sources of water.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through its mineral body, causing its rocky limbs to shed and reform into denser, more resilient armor. With each cycle, it grows stronger, its evolving shell reflecting the intensity of the sun it has endured.
author: ilija09

entry: POKENAME is wrapped in a leafy bulb that leaves only one eye exposed. This leafy bulb is made out of an incredibly tough material, giving its vines the capacity to uproot trees.
author: oreee0230

entry: Strong enough to support the bulbs on their head, POKENAME care for the gardens they call home. They gather nutrients in their bulbs and bury themselves among flowers, enriching the soil as they rest.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The bud on POKENAME's back releases chemical signals to warn nearby Grass-type Pokémon about any present danger. It dislikes physical contact, even with other plants.
author: oreee0230

entry: The long fronds sprouting from the heads of POKENAME contain large colonies of symbiotic algae, allowing them to subsist on photosynthetic energy. Their fronds are tipped with toxic spikes to ward off predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The seed on its head floats in the water, allowing it to perform photosynthesis and rest. Its vines shred Corsola to pieces.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME have long thorny leaves that sprout from their back, trailing behind them as they run around. The leaves are adapted to be able to retain moisture, keeping their bodies damp for days after leaving the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The seed on its back has grown large enough for it to take shelter inside. It absorbs nutrients by napping in bright sunlight.
author: apixelperfectionist

entry: POKENAME are encased with thick tentacles that allow it to bunker down when in danger. POKENAME rarely moves and only does so with the changing tide, ensuring a delicate balance of sunlight and water.
author: oreee0230

entry: Vines hanging from POKENAME's arms entangle foes during battle. While it is a solitary creature, it tolerates the presence of other Pokémon while it is sunbathing.
author: oreee0230

entry: The bulb on its head constantly absorbs the desert sunlight, converting it into energy for all its activities. It protects oasis trees by driving away any danger with the sharp thorns that grow along its arms.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME sets traps made out of sand that look like flower buds. This trap absorbs moisture from nearby creatures, making prey too tired to escape.
author: oreee0230

entry: Each green granule that makes up POKENAME's body is wrapped in plant tissue. Those who are pricked by the cactus on its head feel numb, as though POKENAME is trying to control them.
author: oreee0230

entry: It buries its claws in the soil to absorbs nutrients into the bulbs on its back. It repeats this process daily to avoid having to compete for food.
author: itsmebrewsky

entry: POKENAME catches small prey like Krabby or Corpish by quickly snagging them with its vines. The scent that comes from its bulb smells like cooked fish, drawing the attention of Trainers and Pokémon alike.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME live in cold regions away from the many predators in warmer climates. As sunlight is weaker in these regions, POKENAME can absorb faint light found at dawn and dusk.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME accumulates nutrients during a single polar day to last an entire year, storing that energy in its flower bud. Its green sail absorbs energy in low light conditions as long as the sun is shining; excess energy is crystallized as dust.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME is extremely loyal to its Trainer and will defend them at all costs. The bulb on POKENAME's tail will release dangerous spores if threatened.
author: syl_theguy

entry: Wild POKENAME often live alone, focusing on gathering nutrients for its buds. The tips of its vines grow woody spikes, which can flex and are used in battle.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are found in forests, singing a soothing melody to relax nearby Pokémon. Its song is known to promote growth in plants.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME stores solar energy in the bulb on its head. Its sweet melodies can control the blooming of flowers on any plant.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As POKENAME absorbs moonlight, the rings along their backs glow brighter and brighter, brimming with energy. Once full, they release this energy as shimmering spores which look like stars in the light while also boosting plant growth around them.
author: santon5512
