entry: POKENAME releases its psychic power from the bulb on its head. To fully recharge, it requires a long rest under sunlight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The leaves from POKENAME's bulbs have grown to wrap around their main body. They spend most of their time hiding among tree roots, draining nutrients to grow their leaves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The bulb around POKENAME's head is way thicker than it looks. It acts as both a shield and a storage for energy.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: Once their bulb grows too large for their body, they shed it so a new one can grow. These discarded bulbs are used to make curative items.
author: itsmebrewsky

entry: POKENAME uses its antennae to detect Pokémon from underground, then pops out of the ground to spray any predators with toxic spores. It is popular with beginner farmers, as they let POKENAME blend in with other crops.
author: sockedpuppetart

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight into the bulb on its back, storing enough energy to create small flames. Although normally gentle by nature, it will not hesitate to unleash its full power to protect its Trainer.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It uses its lush vines to hang from the willow branches that grow along the riverbanks it calls home. POKENAME would do anything to eat a Persim Berry, as they are its absolute favorite.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME move swiftly through the forest, hopping between branches with great agility. When encountering enemies, POKENAME wrap pebbles in bitter foam and throws them to disrupt their enemies' concentration.
author: oreee0230

entry: It spends all day absorbing solar energy into its large bulb. When the need arises, it will release a Solar Beam capable of burrowing a mile deep into the ground.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through its green shell to maintain an internal smolder. When needed, POKENAME can increase humidity to release smoke or ignite renewable vines to launch an attack.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's flower bud absorbs the grudges of forest creatures that have succumbed to deforestation. POKENAME remains vigilant toward anything foreign, including humans, and will attack if they come too close.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME prefer to live on farms, where they use their vines to help tend the soil. POKENAME use their toxic spores to paralyze any insects after the crops and then take them away as their own food.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If it rests long enough under sunlight, its body begins to produce a sweet fragrance reminiscent of cotton candy. POKENAME can extend the vine on its tail to deftly grasp the foods it favors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have elastic pants made out of leaves. By stretching these pants, they increase the surface area that can absorb sunlight to gain more energy. Those who can stretch the pants over their head are most likely to become leaders of a group.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME can barely move on land because of the weight of its flower bud and its short, stubby legs. Its swimming ability is much better by comparison, so it prefers to stay in the water.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME will continuously absorb sunlight to thicken the cell walls of its body, even if it becomes too heavy to fly. If it encounters danger that its body cannot endure, its bulbous body peels apart to change form.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME isn't a meteor, but a massive seed. When it falls from the upper atmosphere, it buries itself deep in the ground so the sprout on its back can begin to grow.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME naps during the day to absorb more sunlight. When night falls, it uses the flame on its tail to replicate sunlight, giving it energy to walk.
author: dandistorted2

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back can be detached and thrown, causing a harmless explosion of seeds. Gardeners often use this to sow in bulk quickly.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME start their day by grooming their bulbs. In doing so, the spices that they excrete perk them up.
author: frokachu

entry: Nobody knows what the true body of a POKENAME looks like, only that it contains a bulb the head protects. The bulb can connect to nearby roots, allowing POKENAME to command plants at will.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Grass-type Pokémon feel a certain subservience when encountering POKENAME's beauty. POKENAME can revive plants from the brink of death, restoring vitality to plants caught in disasters.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME keeps close to the ocean's surface so its seed can collect sunlight. Unfortunately, this makes it easy prey for Pelipper.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lives in rivers, keeping close to the surface so its seed can collect sunlight. This seed is full of nutrients, so Pokémon like Pidgey will often peck at it.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME uses its vines to cling to tree trunks while running, helping it drift without slowing down. It mainly feeds on berries found in the forests where it nests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: With its vines, POKENAME can grab the fruits and Berries it feeds on to stay healthy and energized. The colorful patterns on its wings change depending on the region it inhabits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body is protected by a tough bulb that shields it from any kind of harm. To gather food, it extends its long vines, which can stretch for several meters, allowing it to remain safely inside its shelter.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spreads tiny vines into the surrounding soil, turning it green. POKENAME spends most of its time underground, only surfacing to check its surroundings while laying down vines.
author: oreee0230

entry: A collection of three sprouts sticking out of the ground signals a nearby burrowed POKENAME. They create root networks around their bulbs, sprouting small forests or gardens.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is a gentle and patient creature that spends most of its days feeding through photosynthesis under the sunlight. If it rains for too many days in a row, it begins to feel weak and appears sad and disheartened.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When the sun reaches its apex in the sky, groups of POKENAME skate along lake surfaces to absorb the light. The water reflects more sunlight onto their bulb, allowing them to store more energy for evolution.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have three heads; the one with a bud on its head is responsible for spreading vines, while the other two heads are responsible for keeping watch. If any of the heads detect a threat, the tiny vines sprout and strike with sand and stones.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME live in the highest branches of trees, where the coins on their foreheads blend into the leaves. In the mornings, they poke their heads through the leaves to absorb sunlight for photosynthesis.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: They nap in bright sunlight, photosynthesizing using the bulb on its back. The pollen contained in its flower tail revitalizes and nourishes plants. POKENAME is popular among gardeners for this reason.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME always sleeps during the day, basking in the bright sunlight. When the sun sets, it becomes uneasy and wanders randomly until it finds a bright enough spot to nap in again.
author: soup1900

entry: Thanks to its psychic powers, POKENAME can levitate leaves and move them at will to train its focus. It always meditates under the sunlight so the bulb on its head can absorb as much energy as possible.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prowls the wilds with feline grace. Its charm and sharp foliage make it an enchanting and dangerous sight.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME emits electrical currents that accelerate the development of nearby plants. It leaks electricity from its ears when excited.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME generates electricity that accelerates plant growth when discharged. It leaks electricity from its bulbous head when it is depressed.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME has nutritious nectar oozing out of its shining buds. Those tasked with raising children often help POKENAME in exchange for this nectar, feeding it to their young.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME is highly valued by farmers for its tireless nature and is often seen hauling heavily loaded carts. To keep its energy reserves full, it rests for long hours under sunlight, storing nourishment within the bulb on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: On sunny days, POKENAME remains motionless under the sun to conserve energy. If the sunlight disappears, its natural predator instincts activate until sunlight returns.
author: oreee0230

entry: When the bulb on POKENAME's head glows green, it can speak to plants. However, this ability causes severe headaches, making it a rare sight.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If it does not absorb enough sunlight with the bulb on its head, POKENAME's movements may become unstable and confused. If you see it wandering aimlessly, it is recommended to expose it to the sun as soon as possible.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME bask in the tall grass, the bulbs along their bodies absorbing sunlight. By using Razor Leaf, these Pokémon can cut down any threat with their tails.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME blends perfectly among the algae on the bottoms of lakes and rivers to avoid being caught. When it feels threatened, it spits a mixture of water and mud from its mouth to blind its attacker and then flees.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swim through rivers at incredible speeds. When resting, they submerge their bodies completely, leaving only their bulb visible like a leafy lily pad.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's spinning provides energy for the bulb on its head. Once it rotates enough, the bulb will release a potent pollen that can help rejuvenate plant life and soil in old and barren areas.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's appearance changes with the weather. The bud under its body can not only absorb moisture from the air but also predict the weather.
author: oreee0230

entry: Provided there is a source of water relatively nearby, POKENAME taking on this form are extremely healthy due to the ample sunlight and may even evolve sooner than POKENAME in other conditions.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME takes on this form when it rains. Unless it is in a sun shower, it retreats into a secluded place until the sun comes out again.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME cleanses its body through the absorption and expulsion of rainwater. Once this rainwater is flushed through its body, it can be harnessed as liquid fertilizer.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME takes on this form when it rains. Unless it is in a sun shower, it retreats into a secluded place until the sun comes out again.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME enlarges its body by forming parts of itself out of snow, allowing it to enjoy the scarce sunlight filtering through the snow clouds. Its green wisps are a mixture of ice crystals and pollen.
author: oreee0230

entry: Although it can absorb sunlight to sustain itself, POKENAME often searches for fruits to supplement its nutrition. The size of the bud on its back directly reflects POKENAME's recent physical condition.
author: oreee0230

entry: If POKENAME does not absorb enough sunlight, the leaves on its back curl up, preventing it from flying. It is a kind and patient creature, especially toward smaller Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When struck by the wind, its long tail spreads a sweet minty fragrance with calming properties. POKENAME warms the bulb on its head under the sun to amplify the reach of its psychic powers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is so round that, when moving on land, it prefers to roll to get around. Inside the bulb on its back, it stores energy and nutrients that keep it in excellent shape; as a result, POKENAME rarely gets sick.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives on the tallest treetops to better absorb the sun's rays. When it is not on the treetops, POKENAME will become enraged and attack anyone who comes near.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's leaf-shaped whiskers have sensitive tactile and light-sensing abilities. Through the guidance of older members of its herd, POKENAME can develop an accurate sense of direction by measuring sunlight with its whiskers.
author: oreee0230

entry: Its lithe body allows it to swim swiftly among rocks as it searches for food. POKENAME lives only in warm waters to promote the growth of the seed that sprouts on its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's green fur perfectly hides the large bud behind its head. It often attacks other Grass-type Pokémon who try to take their usual sunbathing spot.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are agile and energetic, using vines around their limbs to swing through treetops. When upset, they lash their vines at the source of their anger, often tangling themselves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME likes to float on the surface of the sea, pretending to be a rootless aquatic plant. Once other creatures come close, POKENAME will spray venom and escape to another location.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's fur resembles grass or leaves more than typical fur. They store energy from photosynthesis in their bulbs, releasing it as fire from their mouths.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Covered in grass-like fur, POKENAME stand atop hills at dawn to gather sunlight. Their roar generates intense heat and light, capable of burning or growing forest sections in minutes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If POKENAME's wings are damaged during flight, the bulb on its tail will open and it will drift to the ground in a manner akin to a dandelion.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME waddle around shallow water, splashing each other with their leafy tails to play and stay hydrated. They swim while keeping their tails at the surface of the water to absorb sunlight and maintain their energy.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its translucent skin reveals a thin, black vine running through its body. Much like the rings of a tree, the number of swirls on its abdomen indicates its age.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME extend their vines across rivers to help catch stray Bulbawag that have drifted too far downstream. POKENAME share the sweet nectar from the bulbs on their hands with those they care about, so they always have their vines out for protection.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Some POKENAME develop small, cactus-like spines on their vines and bulbs. These individuals are notably more aggressive than their gentle counterparts and secrete a slimy toxin rather than a sweet nectar.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME wrap themselves in their leaves to hold water along their bodies while their leaves absorb sunlight, making sure they're always ready for a fight. At night, they briefly unwrap their leaves to refill on water before sleeping.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Growth inside its translucent abdomen is highly unstable, often bursting through the skin as bulb-like fists and thrashing vines. With little sense of touch, it strikes reflexively—sometimes toppling trees before realizing it has moved.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Some POKENAME possess evolved ears that grant them enhanced hearing. Each spring, they patrol the shores where Bulbawag eggs are laid, responding instantly to the faintest disturbance and striking intruders without hesitation.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The twin bulbs on its back store solar energy, granting POKENAME tremendous strength in bright sunlight. Despite this power, it spends most days sprawled along riverbanks, lazily soaking up the sun.
author: char_latte3412

entry: This Pokémon devotes all its energy to growing, sleeping for most of the day. It only wakes up briefly in order to teleport to sunny spots.
author: r.isk

entry: The POKENAME uses its spoon to connect to plants around it, letting them grow at a much faster rate. It is often seen in neglected gardens.
author: nope11275

entry: POKENAME channel healing power through the spoons they carry. Any sprout planted in a hole dug by their spoon grows quickly into a sturdy and beautiful plant.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When a POKENAME is meditating the spoon it has will spread pollen throughout the nearby area. While in this state they are observant and aware.
author: krsgaming

entry: When a POKENAME is focused, its bulbs will produce pollen. It is said that the pollen can instantly heal any plant.
author: krsgaming

entry: Playful by nature, POKENAME release spores with their punches that energize opponents. They only use their spores to encourage intense battles, never to hinder their foes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME use their vines to create boxing rings in the forest to train for battle. A fog of spores drifting from a forest clearing is a sign that a group of POKENAME are hosting a tournament.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are considered protégé champions of the forest, known for their incredible strength. They often have trouble using their second pair of arms after evolving, so they use vines to stay organized.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are formed when a budding sprout gains sentience and forms a body from its developing roots. POKENAME wrap their bodies around trees to blend in with the leaves and drain energy in hopes of blooming someday.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When retracted into its shell, POKENAME is often mistaken for a large seed by park rangers and buried. Thankfully, it is an adept digger.
author: kandyman

entry: Having grown a false body around the plant they sprouted from, POKENAME use their wide mouths to collect and eat berries all at once. The nutrients are converted into energy for their central bulb.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With their bulbs now making up most of their body, POKENAME focus on collecting enough food and energy to bloom. They use their vines to gather fallen trees, dissolving them in their bulbs for nutrients.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Nobody knows what the inside of a POKENAME looks like beneath their outer bell. It is only known that they sprout vines that help them navigate around the water until they find sunny spots to rest.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME use their multitude of vines to protect the bulbs growing from their heads. It is unknown where these vines stem from, but POKENAME seem to be able to regenerate or multiply them near instantly.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME sleep at cave entrances or on cliff walls, blending in with mossy rocks. They use their durable bodies and large arms to protect the bulbs on their backs as they roll around.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Unaccustomed to using their arms, POKENAME navigate mountain slopes primarily with their vines. As they roll down mountains, they scatter seeds to create new forests.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME chooses to plant the flowers on its head, as they are not a part of its body. By sharing these flowers, it not only locates minerals to supplement its diet but also finds sunny spaces for sunbathing, all without engaging in battle.
author: oreee0230

entry: An entire ecosystem has sprouted around POKENAME's body, with their former bulbs hardening into rocks after evolution. The flowers on their body can be launched in explosive barrages or grown into vines for attacks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME store heat generated from photosynthesis in the bulbs on their back. Flaming vines sprout from these bulbs, letting them deliver strong attacks while speeding past opponents.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Heat gathered through photosynthesis erupts from POKENAME as a fiery mane. In battle, they run in complex patterns, aiming vines through the mane to ignite them for attacks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME wander lake shores to bask in sunlight but often delay, going out late in the day. This incomplete photosynthesis leaves them with less energy, perpetuating the cycle.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If its tail has turned yellow, it is a sign of its old age and longevity. Unlike Wartortle, algae on its shell does not mean it is very old.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME sit by lake shores in forests, resting the bulbs on their tails in the water. Wild Pokémon often drink nectar from their bulbs, but POKENAME are usually too dazed to notice.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The bulbs surrounding POKENAME's body are always electrically charged. When enough energy has built up, these bulbs will glow bright green.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The central brain of POKENAME's three bodies is stored in the bulb on the back of the main body. When releasing electricity, the bulb unfurls slightly, and the screws on their bodies glow.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME has traded Farfetch'd's leek for a vine that grows from its body. It uses it like a whip to deliver powerful lashes from a long distance.
author: crazynaturekitty

entry: POKENAME are mischievous and resourceful, using their natural camouflage in tall grass. Using their vine whip, POKENAME can be seen teasing other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have larger bulbs than many other Bulbasaur fusions to support two heads with the photosynthesis of one body. They stand in sunny fields, turning back and forth to heat their heads evenly.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME cannot absorb sunlight because their feathers do not have chlorophyll. The red bulb on their back has turned red after absorbing pigments from their feathers, and allows them to lure and trap insects.
author: oreee0230

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back has sprouted into a leafy patch, allowing all three heads to absorb sunlight evenly. The heads often squabble as they maintain the leaves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Preferring more tropical climates to many Seel fusions, POKENAME swim along jungle rivers with their bulbs above the water to absorb sunlight. POKENAME will rest among rocks in shallow water, using vines to help arrange makeshift beds.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are considered protectors of tropical rivers, using their horns to clear debris. POKENAME shelter smaller Pokémon using their large bodies, even letting some drink nectar from their bulbs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Excess spores from a polluted plant have condensed into a sentient sludge. The sludge protects the bulb as it grows, trying to salvage the sprout it once was.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Spores from a polluted plant have mutated into a monstrous form. When POKENAME fight, they scatter sludge that can pollute or mutate nearby plant life.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is a large, bipedal, reptilian Pokémon. Its most notable feature is the bulb on its back which was planted on it at birth.
author: kames

entry: The top of POKENAME's shell contains chloroplasts that aid in photosynthesis. When sand collects in their shells, they use it to grow plants and leave them along the shore.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Collections of algae gather within POKENAME's shell, forming a miniature ecosystem. They command the algae to grab targets like vines, constantly gathering materials to grow.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Just before dawn, strange flickering green flames can be seen emanating from garden sprouts. These flames are actually POKENAME spores, tending to the plants.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are said to form when wandering spirits possess budding sprouts. They silently fly at night, draining life force from unsuspecting prey to help their bulbs bloom.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When lost spirits possess budding plants, they absorb the nutrients of living things around them until they are able to grow a full body. These spirits wander as POKENAME to continue building their strength, the bulbs on their backs slowly blooming.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It is said that POKENAME formed when Onix near the surface of the ground sprouted bulbs for photosynthesis. The bulb's roots have grown through their rocky body, forming a network of extendable vines.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME release spores from their bulbs that put people and Pokémon to sleep, absorbing energy from their dreams. The sweeter the dream, the brighter their bulbs bloom.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When POKENAME swings its bulb, it transmits healing energy to plants surrounding it. Its hypnosis abilities are weak, so it uses two pendulums.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME exist in a symbiotic relationship where the bulb provides warmth and shelter for the main body. In return, the main body defends the bulb with extendable claws powered by vines sprouting from it.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME supplements its nutrients by filtering soil. If its pincers accidentally break, they can fully regenerate after being exposed to sunlight for half a day.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME run sideways along beaches in order to find spots to burrow near the water. They gather seawater in their large claws and boil it using energy from photosynthesis, using the distilled vapor to water their bulbs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME can be seen climbing tall trees using suction cups on its feet. This helps provide sunlight for the seed on its back.
author: curerry

entry: Fusing two Caterpie together has resulted in a Pokémon greedier and hungrier than anything twice its size. It will eat anything its teeth can pierce, but prefers bitter and toxic fare.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME operate as a unified collective to protect their kin from dangerous predators. While one silky net may be an inconvenience, several nets can pin down a predator for hours. Many eggs and cocoons remain safe thanks to their efforts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses discarded parts of Metapod shells as protective armor. Its club is used mainly to knock tasty leaves and berries down from trees for it to eat.
author: sk372

entry: In desperate moments, it won't hesitate to use unwitting Caterpie as makeshift clubs for self-defense. It tries not to damage its impromptu weapon too much.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a patient and strategic fighter. It uses String Shot to slow its opponents, and once they're ensnared in its silk, it strikes with crushing kicks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have far more elaborate head crests than unfused Caterpie. Pokémon researchers have found these crests to be covered with acute sensory hairs that POKENAME use to detect the pheromones of other POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This unfortunate fusion is a Caterpie who failed to fully pupate, leaving its soft head exposed and the rest of its chrysalis body unable to move.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are common prey for many aquatic Pokémon in the wild because they have few defenses against predators. It is said that one in every thousand POKENAME make it to evolution.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on their speed to escape predators because their horn is typically not hard enough to fight back. It is said that one out of thousands of POKENAME reach adulthood.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are said to be Caterpie who gained power so fast that they skipped their Metapod evolution stage entirely.
author: kiwikelly

entry: The amphibious POKENAME is quicker than it looks. It uses its eyes on each arm to pick a safe direction, then desperately scuttles away from predators.
author: haypile

entry: In the winter months, it will use its blades to chop into freezing trees. Once it reaches the center, it will suck out any sap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME weave dresses out of silk to make themselves look pristine and regal. They take great care of their appearance and spend hours making sure their hair and dress are photogenic.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can use its long arms to climb trees with great precision. This is helpful when it is hunting for the most delicious leaves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's horns emit a sweet scent that attracts Pidgey to perch on them, then snap shut when the sensitive chitin is triggered. Once caught, its prey is viciously ripped apart and devoured.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Herds of POKENAME will graze on fields for days at a time. They will consume this grass faster than it can grow back, oftentimes leaving entire fields bare and dead.
author: santon5512

entry: One of the most common fusions of the Kanto region. To ward off its enemies, it releases a poisonous gas from its antennae.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME burst out of the ground at unsuspecting prey, swallowing them whole. They are known for eating twice their body weight every day.
author: adsfw11

entry: POKENAME is most often seen in the wild during the autumn season, indulging in feasts of fallen and dried leaves. Some people have taken to using POKENAME as an easier way to clear their yard of foliage.
author: sk372

entry: For self-defense, POKENAME possesses an electrified mane as well as the ability to spit electric silk from its mouth. It also uses the thread to pluck and slightly cook berries hanging from high branches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fires strands that function as adaptable electronic cords. The threads adjust to nearly any port but dissolve within a day.
author: .izik

entry: One of the most common fusions of the Kanto region. To ward off its enemies, it releases a poisonous gas from its antennae.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are a popular fusion for young Trainers around Viridian Forest to use when they are just beginning their journey. POKENAME are easy to raise and has a relatively mild poison that makes them safe to handle whilst still being useful in battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As it consumes tree sap from a trunk, it will excrete a horrible smelling liquid. This fluid discourages predators from attacking.
author: .izik

entry: It has a strong appetite for fresh leaves straight from the branches. A hungry POKENAME can strip a verdant tree bare in about an hour.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME shed scales that resemble crisp leaves that fall from trees during autumn. Children love to stomp on their scales to release a satisfying crackle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It will fly from tree to tree, skewering fruit on its stingers. It consumes the fruit during flight to minimize downtime.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a distinctive scent from the leaf on its head to disorient predators. It spends most of its time foraging for ferns to feed on and grow stronger.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This variant of POKENAME secretes a scent from its leaf that only others of its kind can detect, guiding them toward a safe shelter. It feeds primarily on Berries to grow and strengthen itself.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Though adapted to crawl across surfaces, POKENAME stomps through forests and stretches its long neck to eat leaves from tall trees. It often breaks branches in its clumsy attempts to climb them before it metamorphoses.
author: ecstaticwoop64556455

entry: POKENAME has a voracious appetite, nibbling on anything it can get its hands on if it has not been fed. Lilypads seem to be its favorite foods, so it is best to keep it away from any Lotad nearby.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's powerful bite allows it to feed on tough plants and berries. Occasionally, it has been known to prey on small Pokémon as well.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME likes to tear down webs connected to trees. It uses these webs to hold Berries in order to deliver them to other POKENAME.
author: schierke

entry: It scouts an area determined by its pack. Should it see a friendly face, it will tilt its body back and forth while smiling.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon dreams of being able to grow wings and fly. To make up for its current inability to do so, it will curl up into a ball and bounce around through the forest like a pinball.
author: fireblade141

entry: Though unusual for insects, a male POKENAME performs a dance to attract females. It appears to have developed this ability from its Hoothoot DNA.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME antennae are attuned to pick up pheromones that drift through the night air. They can navigate to one another through pitch darkness thanks to this sharp sense of smell.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself amongst peas and grapes. If you notice a strange smell, one is probably hiding in yours.
author: holgast

entry: During the day, POKENAME sleeps in hollowed-out tree trunks, evading predators. When dusk arrives, it ventures out into the open, munching on leaves and flowers.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It releases an appetizing scent to lure prey to its web. After snugly wrapping it in webbing, POKENAME injects the trapped prey with poison to melt it down.
author: megashit100000

entry: POKENAME spits a sticky silk from its mouth at other Flying-type Pokémon to make them fall to the ground. Thanks to its four swift wings, it can fly nimbly even through very dense forests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: With its wings, POKENAME flies swiftly from tree to tree to feed on ripe, sweet berries. At the slightest sound, it flees at full speed, as it is particularly timid by nature.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME creates nets out of silk to carry berries to its nest. It rarely shares with its siblings because of its insatiable appetite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The lures of POKENAME are filled with silk. They get larger as it ages and grows closer to evolution.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It lets loose bolts of electricity from the antennae on its head. Its body will even spark intermittently while it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits out thin silk threads to control its movement while floating. It often drifts aimlessly in the wind, bouncing lightly off of objects.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's diet consists of young tree sprouts and leaves, and it chomps at any new plant growth it can find. Local superstition holds that the saplings it doesn't devour will grow ten times healthier, so it's commonly kept at orchards.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: POKENAME are raised for their soft, abundant silk. They were bred to shed the silk instead of spinning it into cocoons before evolution.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME is the leader of its home nest. There can be several POKENAME per nest, who manage it cooperatively.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are found in places with moderate weather and may flourish under a variety of conditions. Instead of focusing on growing stronger and evolving further, wild POKENAME tend to focus on repopulation.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has weak leg muscles, so it drifts in the wind towards leafy bushes. Sometimes it gets stuck in bushes, which makes them easy prey for predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eat twice their body weight in leaves daily to nourish the flower atop their head. During summer, the heat from the sun's rays makes them excited and causes them to release this energy by chasing other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME catch wind currents with the silk balls that are attached to their bodies to glide from bush to bush. When they are not eating to satisfy their voracious appetite, they play chase with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are very soft, juicy and defenseless, so they rely on their intimidating cry to scare away predators. If that fails, they will run away.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It's not very strong, so it wriggles into dirt and pretends to be a tuft of grass. The horns atop its head are smelly and foul-tasting.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME are constantly eating leaves to satisfy their voracious appetite. The constant flapping of their wings allows them to zip away when they spot predators nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have an insatiable appetite and must eat thrice their body weight in leaves to remain a healthy weight. They zip between bushes and tree branches to maximize the time they spend eating leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eats anything, even toxic substances. These substances are removed and expelled through their gills, so young Trainers are encouraged to never touch wild POKENAME.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME mark their territory by releasing an odor from the red antenna on their head. This wards off predators that disturb its sun bathing.
author: curerry

entry: POKENAME are said to raid food pantries, quickly devouring everything in sight. They, however, are actually shy Pokémon who feed solely on wild seeds.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME stalk Trainers in forests and cast spells over them. Once enchanted, Trainers describe feeling a sudden voracious appetite that makes them eat all their snacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is incredibly weak and often needs to use its psychic abilities to crawl along tree branches. It rarely battles, preferring to remain hidden.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME are weak Pokémon, so Flying-Type Pokémon often hunt them as an easy source of plentiful food. POKENAME endure those attacks stoically and rarely fight back.
author: sontyp

entry: This common plant-eating pest is typically found in gardens. Experienced POKENAME have a stubborn and fiery temperament and will quickly return to a garden it has been chased out of, seemingly out of spite.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lines forests with sticky webbing to catch bugs. It gently grasps prey in its claws before crushing them into a delicious paste.
author: amityblamity

entry: Using its hooked claws, it scales trees to find large leaves to feed on. It will spew sticky threads to entangle predators while it makes its escape.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME forage for Berries to store supplies for the winter months. They do not like sour food, so Berries such as the Belue Berry are tossed out instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often employed by high-end restaurants for their pleasant demeanor and surprising professionalism. They are easily compensated as well, only asking for a nice plate of fresh leaves after a job well-done.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME moves, its body makes a slurping sound, and it leaves behind a hot, sticky ooze. This ooze hardens as it cools, and makes an ideal habitat for small boring insects, as it is full of nutrients.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: As POKENAME moves, its body makes a slurping sound, and it leaves behind a hot, sticky ooze. If a small Pokémon walks into this ooze while it is drying, it can get stuck, and must try to get the help of others to free itself.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its shoulders are coated with fuzzy red down, which is protected by a sticky layer of oil. This oil irritates the skin and makes all Pokémon less likely to grab it, though other POKENAME are strangely immune.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME live amongst the leaf litter in forests, rooting around under it for fallen fruits or fresh mushrooms. Their antennae are highly sensitive to the scent of decay and they gravitate toward fallen trees.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's coarse hair covers all of its body and protects it from predators. Interestingly, it's actually soft and silky to the touch.
author: mepp.

entry: It voraciously munches on seaweed. Some POKENAME have even been known to cling to and prey on passing Dhelmise.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME are social Pokémon, traveling in packs of up to a hundred. Though sluggardly, they protect their ilk by slithering about in a dense weave to disorient airborne predators.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME likes to play in mud, even though it hates being dirty. Attempting to clean it may result in it releasing an awful stink from its feeler if it's accidentally touched.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: When predators like Pidgeotto fly too close, POKENAME fires a string coursing with electricity at them. This buys it enough time to scurry away to safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eats brightly colored flowers that grow on bushes, which dye its antlers red. Sometimes its antlers get stuck in bushes, causing it to cry for help.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Considered weak by many, POKENAME spends all day training, hoping to grow stronger. It tends to pick fights against opponents far stronger than it.
author: jackythewannabe

entry: POKENAME hones its skills by striking nuts and berries that grow on trees. It will occasionally wrap its limbs in the silk produced from its mouth to increase its strength and defenses.
author: sk372

entry: Deep within forests, POKENAME group up in areas where Electric-type Pokémon previously were. They feed off of the static left behind from them.
author: dyanz0

entry: POKENAME can be seen in forests using its silk to climb trees and eat bird Pokémon eggs. If hungry, it will also immobilize unaware prey from behind before attacking them.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME hold higher authority over packs of Caterans, but they also have lower intelligence. They will sometimes try to eat things several times their size and become stuck.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Lacking its pattern, POKENAME uses its silk to immobilize prey, before constricting and fainting it with its poison. It is very territorial, marking its territory with silk strings.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME seems strong, but it is really quite puny. It cannot climb trees due to its build, so it kicks and headbutts trees in hopes leaves will fall, which it devours.
author: cocosquid.

entry: It is always awake due to a weak electrical current running through its body. If you hold the tip of its tail, the current will run through your skin and make your palm tingle.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME love bouncing atop their bulbous tail but often end up with a stomachache when they bounce after eating. Bouncing on their tail also uses up a lot of energy and makes them voraciously hungry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's three eyes sometimes wander in three different directions. Scientists say this is how POKENAME detects predators on land, in the sky, and in the shadows -- but Trainers of POKENAME say it's just looking for entertainment.
author: haypile

entry: When stressed, POKENAME stands still to make itself look like a plant. Unfortunately, that strategy is rarely effective.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME has a surprisingly thick exoskeleton for such a small Bug-type. Testing reveals that it incorporates hard silicates into its body from the rocks on which it feeds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME make pranks and parties fun by releasing aerosol string, a brightly colored plastic string that is propelled out from their body. While children love seeing this trick, parents groan at the prospect of cleaning up this string after a party.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wraps other Pokémon's Eggs in soft silk, believing it is helping to keep them safe. While friendly, this habit sometimes causes confusion among Trainers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waits in the canopy during thunderstorms with its tail pointed to the sky. Once lightning strikes it, the surrounding leaves are fried in an instant, turning into delicious fare for this Pokémon.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME patrols the forest, ensuring all the Pokémon living there are safe. If it spots a Metapod in danger, it swiftly strikes down the threat.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME prefers the roots of hardy bushes to the leaves of tall trees. As soil makes is introduced into its diet, this Pokémon's skin grows tougher and thicker.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: It perches on branches within vibrant and lush trees, gorging itself on many leaves each day. It can flap its wings so quick that the mere vibrations cause every leaf on a tree to be knocked loose.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME travel in large herds, ramming into anything that disturbs them. When POKENAME sleep, their herd huddles together into one big clump, facing their shells outward to make a safe fortress.
author: adsfw11

entry: POKENAME's nose is filled with a horrid stench that repels enemies but also makes itself repulse from disgust. Its molting is highly irregular since it sheds random parts of its body at a time instead of the whole body at once.
author: soup1900

entry: Using its tail, a POKENAME can topple even the strongest foes. At night, it slaps a lake's surface repeatedly to declare its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates a nest in a fruit tree using its sticky silk. The tree that this Pokémon chooses usually has the least amount of predators in the area, good foliage for hiding, as well as bountiful fruit to sustain POKENAME's voracious appetite.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Its green hide pattern allows it to blend in with the forest. If detected, it emits a strong odor, curls up into a ball, and bounces away.
author: articwulfi

entry: While its spines initially appear to be a leafy bush, they're actually hard as rocks. While it feasts on roots underground, these spines defend its personal space, as POKENAME are notoriously antisocial.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME climbs trees with ease, feeding on their leaves. If any unaware prey is below its tree, it will roll into a spiny ball and attack from above.
author: articwulfi

entry: Female POKENAME are hatched with whiskers that fall out as they age. They are more analytical and cautious than male POKENAME, testing each morsel of food with care to check if it's safe to eat.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME spits long strands of silk to gather a variety of foods that are out of its reach. A popular children's book features the adventures of a very hungry POKENAME.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME eat leaves off bushes and retain the twigs for the creation of their dams. They need to eat twice their body weight in leaves to have enough energy to build dams.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During the springtime, POKENAME releases a sweet smelling pollen from the flower on its back. This pollen is soothing to both humans and Pokémon.
author: curerry

entry: During hot seasons, the flower on POKENAME's back produces a pleasant scent. This scent is commonly used to make Bug-type lures and luxury perfume.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME uses its large jaws to devour any plant matter it can find. Its insatiable hunger drives it to attempt eating even much larger Grass Pokémon, regardless of the danger.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME crawls on the sea floor, nibbling on any seaweed it passes by. It's often found clinging onto Dhelmise, mistaking their green-colored bodies for food.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME have metallic crystals laced within their chitin, making them surprisingly tough for their diminutive size. They prefer to avoid conflict where they can, curling into a ball to protect their soft underbelly when threatened.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The blunt force trauma from the skull of a POKENAME scares away most predators. Only a select few that can melt their metallic skulls stand a chance at biting into a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's stiff body makes it walk around quite clumsily. POKENAME bravely guards Caterpie and other Bug-type Pokémon as they eat.
author: mepp.

entry: Animals of the forest have been observed bringing food to wild POKENAME. They continue growing larger and lazier with age.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME has become too heavy to live on trees. Thanks to its great physical strength, however, it no longer has to hide, but can put enemies to rout.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME prefers not to engage in battle, using ultrasounds and its strong odor to repel enemies. However, if endangered, it will use its poison barbs to attack its predators.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME feed primarily on tree berries, with Oran berries being their favourite food. They become very protective of trees that are to their liking, exuding a foul smell to drive off rivals when they feed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Ancient myth states that since the dawn of time, POKENAME has devoured 1,000 leaves a day. Scholars debate whether its divine power is fueled by this diet, or if it simply really likes leaves.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME have a beak edged with sharp chitin that allows them to bite through even the toughest of plant stems. They are a nuisance to gardening communities due to their habit of chewing through orderly gardens.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in forest canopies, often going their entire lives without touching the ground. They complement their climbing abilities with ropes made of silk.
author: staghorn

entry: The horn on POKENAME's head is filled with a mild poison that is non-toxic to Trainers. It has a large appetite and will eat anything that even slightly looks like a leaf.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME defend themselves by spewing sticky threads at threats. These threads will expand and become stickier when exposed to water. Although they are quite weak, POKENAME refuse to accept handouts, even from their Trainers.
author: infinex21

entry: This strange bug wards off predators by using its body to swing a flail made of its own silk. It quickly spins it back together if it's damaged.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME must eat twice their weight in vegetation a day to prepare for evolution. They fiercely defend their territory from others of their kind to prevent food from becoming scarce.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME secretes a sticky silk that it spits onto its prey's legs to slow them down. The red horn on its head glows brightly whenever it senses danger.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME work long hours in factory settings to keep machinery running smoothly. During the few hours they get to rest, many spend time eating as many leaves as they can before returning to work.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's mane is made entirely out of silken thread generated from its mouth. It seems to have a connection to its illusion powers, as POKENAME with less thread casts smaller-scale illusions.
author: sk372

entry: Its long, segmented body allows it to squirm its way through narrow openings. Anything POKENAME can stick its head through, it can squirm through.
author: melodydelune

entry: Legends say this Pokémon came to be when a Caterpie with an insatiable hunger consumed an entire forest, growing to an enormous size. Unable to carry its own weight on land, it slumbers in the deep ocean.
author: mistymagius

entry: This massive Pokémon wanders forests, terrifying children with its loud stomps. Despite this, it is still just as skittish as an ordinary Caterpie.
author: chartanon

entry: In rare sightings of this Pokémon, it can be seen collecting leaves at night. On full moon nights, it can be seen with other POKENAME enjoying a leaf feast.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME have extremely strong legs, allowing them to cover 100 feet in a single bound. They seem to a have a fondness for leafy vegetables, lettuce in particular.
author: mistymagius

entry: By examining fusion eggs with ultrasound, scientists have found that POKENAME's body grows out of the bottom of a regular Caterpie's head.
author: holgast

entry: Thanks to its acute hearing, it can avoid bird Pokémon. It has been seen using its tiny wings to allow it to eat leaves from trees.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME uses the small flame on its head to search for leaves to eat at night. This light never flickers, even in strong wind.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME's flames produce a strong, terrible odor that repels many predators. It is thought to subsist on wandering spirits, ridding areas of supernatural phenomena with its voracious appetite.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are formidable yet gentle giants and move slowly to avoid crushing their kin below them. Many serve as guardians to their kin to ward off Flying-type predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to a genetic failure, POKENAME has five legs. However, this does not make it faster than a Vulpix.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME have the precocious ability to shoot flames, which scares away most of their peers. Even though they have long wings, they prefer to remain on the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use buttons for its Caterpie disguise, and roams among other Caterpie. Some POKENAME have mismatched buttons for eyes, making it easy to spot in the wild.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME only comes out at night, using its antennae to sense its surroundings. Despite being very weak, POKENAME will not hesitate to headbutt anything that it deems a threat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are almost always hungry and constantly eat leaves from bushes and trees. In exchange for giving them lots of food, Trainers can get a ride atop POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With its voracious appetite, it can spend the entire day eating leaves. If disturbed, it may curse whatever interrupted it for up to one thousand years.
author: articwulfi

entry: A POKENAME will use its strong legs to grab fruit off of the top of trees. It prefers Bluk Berries due to their dry taste.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME takes hours to move along a branch. However, once it has eaten all the nearby leaves, it uses string to swing at high speeds to a new tree.
author: chorb33

entry: Despite their formidable size, POKENAME can be easily satiated with crops like potatoes, corn, or beans. Prepared farmers may keep POKENAME in their fields, acting like a bouncer to keep more harmful pests far away.
author: chinigan

entry: Using its ability to produce silk and its lung capacity, it forms sticky balls to shoot at its foes. However, this does little more than leave a bruise.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME live in caves, primarily feeding on moss. Their tough exoskeleton protects them from most predators.
author: mepp.

entry: If two POKENAME spy the same leaf, they will headbutt each other to battle over who will eat the meal. Their stubborn nature means the leaf is often snatched by another Pokémon while the POKENAME duke it out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produce energy for factories by spinning their twin gears. Even though POKENAME need lots of leaves to function, they are easy to find and can be swapped out easily.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are an important part of factories as their cheap and reliable rotation ensures that factories can consistently function throughout the day. When they are not working, they ravenously eat leaves from the nearby forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It climbs into tall trees and mimics a branch. This unassuming disguise hides it from predators while it feasts on high-up leaves.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: It secretes a smelly oil from its tail that keeps its flame alight. The flame is too weak to actually burn anything; rather, POKENAME uses it to communicate with others of its kind.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME tends to eat all the leaves it can see. However, if it finds an apple it considers perfect, it won't hesitate to devour it.
author: articwulfi

entry: Its eyes are far bigger than its stomach, so it will eat anything. POKENAME often falls out of trees after eating the leaf it's standing on.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME enjoys nibbling on fresh carrot leaves, favoring the most vibrant green ones. It sometimes hides in gardens, blending in with leafy plants.
author: .izik

entry: If accidentally awoken, a POKENAME will hop up and down to spread an orange pollen. If inhaled, this can cause weakness, or even paralysis.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a membrane that dissolves through plant matter on contact. By rubbing themselves against shrubs, they can devour leaves in a matter of seconds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce a soft, delicate silk that can be spun into plush, diaphanous fabric. They are often encouraged to eat lots of leaves because they produce more silk when they are full.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using its big ears, it can hear prey from 250 meters away. Should it see a traveler walking through a forest at night, it will swoop down onto them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME possess incredible eyesight, and utilize their vision in hunting more than most bat Pokémon. Occasionally, when hanging upside down, POKENAME are mistaken for Metapod due to their color.
author: corndogyip

entry: POKENAME is a Yamask fusion with no memories of its former life. Instead, its mind is preoccupied with only one thought: to eat, and keep eating, forever.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME is often found clinging to bug zappers, enjoying the heat and energy. This annoys humans, as it disables the device.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME use static electricity to stick to surfaces, enabling them to walk up even the smoothest of walls and even walk across ceilings. The silk they spin from their mouth has a slight charge to it, granting it these same sticky properties.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The flaps bordering POKENAME's mouth mimic eyes, making it seem more imposing to smaller creatures. It primarily frightens off Caterpie so it can steal their meals.
author: sk372

entry: Its voracious appetite compels it to eat more than twice its body weight daily, which is possible through its high appetite. POKENAME flies to the upper forest where it can eat berries that other Pokémon cannot reach.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Should it sneeze, it may accidentally spray embers across the ground. If not kept in check, a forest fire can start.
author: .izik

entry: It can shoot its strings at pinpoint accuracy, even in the darkest of settings. It can sometimes be seen eating leaves in a cave.
author: ichosuzu

entry: This Pokémon hunts in the dark for prey, sucking their blood with its fangs. However, if it doesn't find any decent target, it will stick to a diet based on leaves.
author: articwulfi

entry: It was once believed that POKENAME was formed when scared Trainers stepped on a Caterpie to squash it.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It spends most of its time on sewer walls, eating mold. As it gets older, it will consume less and less until it can survive on a single bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can roll around for days without getting tired thanks to their slow metabolism. They enjoy rolling in open fields where they can race against other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live among normal Caterpie, acting as their protector. They will shoot sticky silk at any threat to drive them away.
author: adsfw11

entry: With its innocent, wide-eyed stare, POKENAME is often mistaken for harmless. In truth, it has an insatiable appetite, devouring frozen leaves and icy moss at alarming speeds.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME is very vulnerable, so it hides in the soil and photosynthesizes to gather the energy it needs to evolve.
author: kiwikelly

entry: If it sees a forest clearing, it will have an overwhelming urge to dance. Should it be seen by someone, it will grow embarrassed and hide.
author: .izik

entry: The silk POKENAME produces from its feathers is very sticky, so POKENAME must dance and flail its wings vigorously to throw the silk at its enemies.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It spins its silk into fashionable cocoon accessories, which are often then stolen by poachers, as POKENAME is very slow-moving and defenseless.
author: kiwikelly

entry: The ends of its wings are exceptionally sharp. To gather food, it will do an elegant dance and cut down large quantities of leaves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's head is filled with a light, noxious gas, allowing it to "swim" through the air. Should it feel threatened, it'll release it through its horns to deter predators.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME scatters a trail of autumn leaves as it moves slowly through the forest. Other Pokémon gather and store these nutritious leaves in preparation for cold winters.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Its upper body resembles a Caterpie, highlighted by its petal, making it irresistible to bird Pokémon. When it spots its target flying overhead, it flaps its petals to release a paralyzing toxin.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME voraciously seeks to devour anything that moves as a method for staving off its unbearable hunger pains. It fires torrents of String Shots to ensnare its quarries, then sucks the nutrients out of its trapped prey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lies motionless on the seafloor and waits for unsuspecting Pokémon to attempt to eat the Caterpie-like lure attached to its body. Those who consume the decoy gradually get their life source drained.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME possesses a multitude of feelers that sense fluctuations in the air, letting it know if other creatures are around. Incredibly timid, it rarely has the courage to come out from beneath its own tendrils.
author: sk372

entry: The claws of a POKENAME are used in many upscale restaurants as a garnish. The tangy-sweet flavor is coveted by culinarians.
author: .izik

entry: Using their long necks, POKENAME eat leaves off tall trees. They spin large frills made from a fine silk on their heads, appearing larger than normal to ward off predators.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is fighting the mushroom on its back to maintain control of its body. It must keep eating leaves to prevent losing itself.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME chews lazily on jungle vines, filling the air with a subtle paprika-like aroma. This scent is said to ward off predators, though some simply find it pleasant.
author: .izik

entry: Any time it shakes its fur, a waft of green dust is shaken loose. The dust will change color on a person's skin based on their mood.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are commonplace in many temperate forests, where they are typically seen eating leaves and twigs. They are particularly timid and likely to flee upon hearing any sharp noise.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME weaves strands of silk inside hollowed-out pumpkins. These silk-lined pumpkins are considered lucky by those who find them.
author: .izik

entry: The wings of this Pokémon are filled with toxic and paralyzing dust. If a bird Pokémon tries to attack it, it will flap its wings repeatedly to create a poisonous fog.
author: articwulfi

entry: It snacks on nectar and flower petals, giving its fur a delicious floral flavor. To keep predators from snacking on it, it produces a foul odor from the horn on its head, which also ruins its own flavor.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time in the trees, searching for apples to eat. They secrete a caramel-like mucus from their mouths, which they coat the apples they find in before consuming them.
author: santon5512

entry: Not yet able to fly, POKENAME utilizes its strong arms and tail to climb enormous trees. With its gentle flame, it heats up huge leaves to make them crunchier before it devours them.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: This Pokémon is known for creating subterranean tunnels covered in silk. If anyone touches the silk, it will alert a horde of POKENAME.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME produce a special silk that is spun into wedding dresses. These expensive dresses have a unique scent that varies based on the diet of POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have an insatiable appetite for leaves and bark and are constantly on the move to find more food. If anyone tries to interrupt their feeding session, they sting foes with the twin spikes on their tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time eating leaves high up in the trees. When threatened by Flying-type Pokémon, they will don their spikes, warding predators off.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME travel in swarms and can strip lush trees bare in 20 minutes. Their small wings only allow them to fly for a short time before having to take a long rest.
author: adsfw11

entry: Although it may seem like three different Pokémon, POKENAME is a single Pokémon with three heads. Each head fights constantly for dominance, especially when food is involved.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME weave a net made of hydrophobic silk that maintains its shape when wet. This unique trait of their silk allows them to throw silk nets to pin down predators while they escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spins its silk into balls, which it loves to play with and chase around. Thanks to its antenna and whiskers, it's an excellent hunter.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME shakes its tail at predators to deter them with a horrific stink. It becomes fixated on its own tail and will chase it, forgetting about the threat entirely.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: It hangs from tree branches to catch its prey off-guard. Its whiskers can sense an injured target from up to 100 yards away.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon eats leaves to control its mental powers. For this reason, a hungry POKENAME is dangerous, as it generates psychic waves that get stronger as it loses control.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME feed on algae and kelp on the seafloor, using their incredibly sensitive antennae to look out for predators. When threatened, they will release a putrid smell from these antennae before quickly fleeing.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME live in mangrove swamps, constantly gorging themselves on leaves and fruit that fall into the swampy water. They frequently overeat, projecting their discomfort outward at other Pokémon and causing debilitating stomach aches to those nearby.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses its webbed appendages to dive into deep waters in search of algae. If it spots a predator, it swiftly flees.
author: articwulfi

entry: This Pokémon is always angry, even when sleeping. It has only been seen at peace while eating leaves.
author: articwulfi

entry: This Pokémon is always angry due to its hunger. If it is ever disturbed while eating, it will pursue whatever disturbed it until it beats it in combat.
author: articwulfi

entry: Many POKENAME do not survive to their next evolution because they lack any effective defense mechanisms against local predators. Only one in ten POKENAME learn to weave silk laced with their greasy sweat, which is bitter to their predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is known for being a very loyal Pokémon. If it detects a menace, it will protect its Trainer by barking and releasing a very strong odor.
author: articwulfi

entry: This Pokémon stashes leaves in its mane for its young. The quality of the fire inside it is directly linked to the amount of leaves it eats.
author: articwulfi

entry: The diminutive flame on its tail is weak and lukewarm. In recent times, it has grown in popularity as a greenhouse pollinator.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME is an easy prey on land, being attacked by bird Pokémon. Despite this, it wanders the forest searching for fallen leaves.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME's antenna helps it detect even the smallest movement of its enemies, making it able to predict their moves. POKENAME is thus a great boxer.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Its hearing is terrible. Due to this disability, it senses disturbances by using its antennae and teleports away without a second thought.
author: .izik

entry: The dowsing rods that POKENAME carry act as an extension of their antennae and help them detect their surroundings. When threatened, POKENAME release a horrible stench from one rod while wrapping the foe in string from the other.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: This Pokémon spends all its time training to develop its muscles. Because of this, it consumes large quantities of leaves.
author: articwulfi

entry: If a bird Pokémon tries to attack it, POKENAME will grab and choke it with its muscles. It lives in deep forests where it trains daily.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME devours enormous trees to buff its muscles before it wrestles with other POKENAME. They create elaborate masks and gloves with silk and proudly show them off during fights.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: It happily runs across entire forests searching for Yellow Apricorns. Should it find one, it will attempt to devour the entire fruit in one motion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has no teeth, so instead douses its food with a foul, corrosive liquid. It laps up the resulting concoction once it's mushy enough to drink.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: This Pokémon hangs motionless in trees, waiting for prey. When it spots one, it shoots silk strings to immobilize it before lunging at it.
author: articwulfi

entry: This Pokémon mimics a Caterpie to attract prey. Once the prey is in its mouth, it dissolves them with acid.
author: articwulfi

entry: This Pokémon can be found hanging from trees by its tentacles, usually feeding on leaves. If disturbed, it will use its poisonous tentacles to attack its foes.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME uses its tentacles to immobilize prey. If that's not enough, it will produce silk from them to trap its target in a cocoon.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME is commonly seen feeding on leaves in trees. If a Pokémon comes too close, it will drop on it, using its hard body to cause harm.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME are rolled into the desert to bring greenery back into arid land. Their rocky bodies have everything needed to turn deserts back into forests over the span of decades, as each POKENAME has a mini-biome full of seeds and moss.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can often be seen in the forest, feeding on fallen leaves. If it detects a menace, it will swiftly run away between the trees.
author: articwulfi

entry: Bird Pokémon often try to attack POKENAME without success, as none can rival its running speed. When it finds time to rest, it feeds on fallen leaves before dashing off again.
author: articwulfi

entry: To prevent being fully eaten, POKENAME allows predators to take and eat its tail off as a concession. With it constantly molting, it easily regrows the tail back in a few days to become whole again.
author: soup1900

entry: It melts holes in the rinds of tough fruits with its toxic spit, then hungrily gulps down the juices inside. POKENAME is an infamous menace on farms growing Watmel Berries.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Having lost its suction pads, POKENAME uses its silk to stick to trees and climbs with its three-fingered claws to get the highest leaves. If it falls in the process, it will hide in its shell and produce a strong odor.
author: articwulfi

entry: Although it looks like the Metapod on its tail is taking nutrients from this Pokémon, it is actually POKENAME who absorbs them from Metapod to fuel its evolution.
author: articwulfi

entry: The horns on its sides crackle with electricity. When a bird Pokémon bites down, it zaps them with all the might it can muster.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME has a very strong magnetic field around its body. It uses this magnetic field to disrupt bird Pokémon migration paths, luring them far away from its position.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME is often attacked by other bird Pokémon, who see it as prey. It tries to defend itself with its leek, without much success.
author: articwulfi

entry: One of their heads will always be on the lookout for threats as the other head eats. Though they can defend themselves with sticky threads loosed by their mouths, they may sometimes get tangled in their own threads.
author: infinex21

entry: Thanks to its antennae, it can produce a very strong odor capable of paralyzing its foes. If endangered, it releases a scent so intense that it can be smelled from miles away.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME is a biohazard and highly dangerous due to its voracious appetite. As it devours waste, its toxicity reaches alarming levels.
author: articwulfi

entry: POKENAME carries Caterpie across large bodies of water to find food and form new colonies. In return, the colony gives POKENAME the largest berries.
author: mirpebble

entry: POKENAME carries with it young Caterpie on its shell. When its antennae lead it to a plant rich with fruit, it voraciously gobbles every one of them up while its passengers strip the plant bare of its leaves.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal Pokémon that lick leaves and Grass-type Pokémon to siphon their energy and nutrients; their dens are riddled with wilted leaves as a result. They will try to scare away others but quickly flee if their efforts fail.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME releases a sweet aroma from its red horn to lure small Pokémon to itself. Inexperienced POKENAME often fall victim to their own tactic.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME uses its hypnotic lure to put entire swarms of Bug Pokémon under its control. It forces them to fight for it in combat because of its lackluster combat prowess.
author: mistymagius

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back contains unstable electrical energy, and disrupting it could cause a large explosion. It uses its wire-like vines to siphon energy from plant matter.
author: mistymagius

entry: During stormy nights, swarms of POKENAME emerge to draw lightning bolts with their rod-like antennae. They are aggressive Pokémon, often shocking each other for fun.
author: mistymagius

entry: This rare Voltorb fusion resembles a Master Ball. No one knows what causes this fusion to take on that appearance.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Fragments of its old shell are often found near training grounds, where experienced Trainers seek them out. These fragments are melted down and used in the layered construction of a Level Ball.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When this POKENAME underwent self-fusion, something strange happened in its genetics, causing it to look like a split of the four main varieties of Poké Ball.  Researchers believe this might mean there are varieties of Voltorb yet undiscovered.
author: infranscia

entry: POKENAME's appearance has changed into one resembling an old prototype design for the Pokéball. Its behavior seems less volatile in this form, and it is less prone to exploding.
author: sk372

entry: It combines Voltorb's self-destructive tendencies with Electrode's enhanced power stores. POKENAME's smug grin reflects its explosive potential and the ego fed by the fear it inspires.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is divided into six Pokéball–shaped units, all linked telepathically. It often dwells in Pokémarket warehouses, skillfully camouflaging itself among shelves and inventory boxes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's heads resemble various types of Poké Balls. When they fall off, Trainers will often try to pick the discarded heads up, only to be met with a nasty shock.
author: reflecbeat

entry: This Pokémon picked up the shell of a Voltorb and wore it as a helmet. It is now fused to its head, and POKENAME borrows some of its power.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It is a rather solitary and irritable Pokémon, to avoid contact with others, it usually hides in bushes or undergrowth. If someone bumps into its hard shell, it may get so angry that it blows itself up.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Sparks emanate at the end of POKENAME's vines, signifying the potent electricity it possesses within. Severed vines have been used as materials for highly-conductive electrical wiring in some regions.
author: sk372

entry: It is thought that the Pokéball pattern on its wings are meant to intimidate predators away. POKENAME will fly at potential threats while spinning, mimicking the image of an incoming Pokéball trying to catch the predatory Pokémon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME absorbs electricity by gripping power lines with its strong hands. If it takes in too much at once, it explodes violently without warning.
author: .izik

entry: Bearing a striking resemblance to the Pokémon Vivillon from the Kalos region, POKENAME is its own species, despite the puzzling similarities. The innate electrical voltage stored in its wings is perhaps the biggest key difference between the two.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: In emergencies, POKENAME explodes to defend its Trainer, flinging sharp pins in all directions - sometimes injuring its Trainer as well.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a volatile presence when it appears on a computer screen. It must be carefully dealt with, lest it explode and damage the user's files and data.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was only documented recently, possibly due to Voltorb's mysterious origins and Porygon's artificial creation. It moves through levitation, but disruptions in the electromagnetic field greatly affect its mood and physical abilities.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME keeps to itself until whatever it has deemed a foe comes too close, upon which it begins to lunge after them. After emitting a soft hissing sound, it explodes. Despite Porygon's artificial origins, POKENAME smells like moss.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME keeps to itself until whatever it has deemed a foe comes too close, upon which it begins to lunge after them. After emitting a soft hissing sound, it explodes. Despite Porygon's artificial origins, POKENAME smells like moss.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME exists in an extremely volatile state as it prepares for its next evolution. The heat inside its shell reaches dangerous levels as it undergoes metamorphosis, and any interruption of this process can result in a catastrophic explosion.
author: houseoffallingflowers

entry: POKENAME shoots explosive bursts of electricity towards large birds that come too close. It is otherwise a solitary creature that glides through the skies in search of its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generates electricity within itself by smacking its large belly. If it smacks its belly quickly enough in short succession, it can create enough energy to trigger a powerful explosion.
author: sk372

entry: Care must be taken after a POKENAME sheds its skin, as the discarded layer is still volatile. Improper handling will lead to it bursting into a shower of sparks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME smack together their spherical forelimbs to discharge electricity and intimidate Pokémon and people alike. They live in large swarms, with each one being willing to throw themselves at their foes and explode to protect their territory.
author: infinex21

entry: The electric arc between its top appendages will increase in intensity as it gets angry. It will start shocking itself if it doesn't calm down.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Due to poor electricity control, POKENAME often explodes spontaneously when frightened. It tries to stay calm but struggles during storms.
author: .izik
