entry: POKENAME hides its small frame with the skull of a fallen Salamence. Timid and not terribly strong, it rarely pokes itself out from the shelter until it's time to evolve.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses illusions to masquerade itself as other Pokémon so it won't be lonely. If its friends discover it in its true form, however, it gets embarrassed and flees in a panic.
author: sk372

entry: Wearing the skull of a fallen Charizard fills POKENAME with vigor and bravery. It fights much more confidently, but this confidence falters instantly should someone manage to remove its helmet.
author: sk372

entry: Their tears act as a natural flame accelerant, which they have learned to use in crafty ways with their own flames. If their flame attacks ever seem to be ineffective, they will resort to swinging their bone club instead.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME practice developing their proficiency over boney implements by skewering fruits and vegetables with boney spikes. Once they have enough food ready, they start a fire and roast these skewers until they become a delicious meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spits dirt downward to catch foes off guard before dragging them into the air. As hunger sets in, it struggles to lift heavier targets.
author: .izik

entry: Highly timid, POKENAME tries its best to be brave when trouble approaches. It usually manages a few seconds of flailing its club about before it inevitably hops away in terror.
author: sk372

entry: When threatened, POKENAME produces spores to protect itself. People who inhale it report feeling intense bouts of sadness afterwards.
author: mepp.

entry: This Pokémon is rumored to be the spirit of a child. Stories tell that it refused to part with its mother's skull, even after POKENAME passed.
author: welliss

entry: POKENAME has a difficult time trusting in others. When under stress, it hardens the normally gelatinous covering around its skull until it gets as rigid and sturdy as solid bone.
author: sk372

entry: The strange, dripping material surrounding POKENAME has a consistency somewhere between slime and sand. Research is still determining whether the head or the crossbones is the true core and source of its powers.
author: sk372

entry: It rams its skull into enemies, frightening them with sudden, forceful impacts. This aggressive tactic makes it a fearsome protector of its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to project an aura of confidence and charisma, but is actually highly self-conscious. If something knocks the skull off of its face, it will sob uncontrollably until it manages to cover itself again.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME usually holds its mother's skull. POKENAME takes this skull wherever it goes as a reminder of its deceased parent.
author: thisisnotaplaceholder

entry: POKENAME is a tiny Pokémon frequently formed when a lost Joltik finds shelter inside of an abandoned skull. Over time, the skull becomes its permanent home, fusing with POKENAME's body.
author: bebop

entry: POKENAME sleep in skulls of Pokémon much larger than themselves and carry the skulls to ensure they have a safe sleeping spot at night. They ward off curious creatures with a jolt of electricity before retreating into their makeshift home.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME are often found near graveyards, people believe them to be spirits of the departed. However, recent research has found they simply feed on minerals commonly found in headstones.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME grinds the bones it carries against the its tusks, in order to sharpen them both for battle. Broken tusks grow back and cause it little issue, but bones breaking while sharpening cause it to go into a panicked fluster.
author: sk372

entry: In ancient times, it was used to guard castle dungeons, keeping intruders at bay. Its unwavering loyalty made it a formidable sentinel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME create nests made of skulls and bones when it comes time to roost. The quiet chirping songs they sing during these moments have a decidedly melancholy feel to them.
author: sk372

entry: Small flames flare up from the nostrils of POKENAME's skull-helmet when it's agitated. It uses bones leftover from previous hunts to help build its nests.
author: sk372

entry: It cries like a baby whenever it doesn't get its way, drawing attention to itself. This behavior makes it difficult for Trainers to manage.
author: .izik

entry: Its diamond-like eyes grant it perfect vision in the darkest environments. This ability makes it a formidable explorer of underground tunnels.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are desert scavengers, living lonely existences in harsh environments. They gather the sun-bleached bones of long passed Pokémon to use as protective armour for themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME keep their tough outer exoskeleton turned outward to protect themselves from the harsh heat of their desert home. Bony spurs jut from their bodies to give them extra grip as they roll around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's extra skull layer around its cranium gives it ample protection from blows. It has a belligerent personality, but chewing on bones keeps its more aggressive impulses at bay.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was first discovered after being revived from a fossil found in a mix of amber and sediment. The bony portions of its body are thought to be incomplete yet are fully functional. Its amber crest is as durable as steel.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME carries a bone with it at all times, and sharpens one end of it over time. It uses the pointed end to chisel away at large ice blocks, digging itself out a den for when night falls.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the ground to sleep, appearing to be a simple skull and foliage. If something gets too close, it instinctively waves its bone around and spreads an annoying pollen around that provokes sneezing fits.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cheers valiantly for its allies in battle, sparks showering from the pom-poms it holds. If the ally still loses, it falls to the ground, despondent at having failed to support them enough.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME twirls its bone like a professional baton twirler. The faster its bone is twirled, the more upbeat it's feeling.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME rummages through dumpsters and landfills to find detritus to consume. It uses bones as armor and weaponry to deal with other scavengers that might try to steal its trashy meal.
author: sk372

entry: Traveling in small schools, hungry POKENAME can reduce creatures to bones in a few moments of a feeding frenzy. Even the bones are not wasted, held in POKENAME's jaws to use as self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME aggressively picks fights with other fierce underwater denizens, most often Sharpedo. The larger and deeper the scar on its skull is, the more respect it garners from others of its kind.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wield their boney club like a sword to protect themselves from dangerous Pokémon. Their horned mask conceals their face as they wander through haunted forests searching for the right Trainer to befriend.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With a glowing red eye and many bone accessories, POKENAME cuts a frightening visage. It's actually quite weak-willed, however; if its appearance and roar don't scare something off, it panics and flees into the forest.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's scent is tied to its mood, and is primarily a noxious aroma due it often being in a state of depression. The tears it sheds are a type nectar known for being particularly sweet.
author: sk372

entry: It brings the bones of lost travelers back to their hometowns, guided by an innate sense of direction. This behavior has led to legends of it being a guardian of wandering souls.
author: .izik

entry: A silent and deadly hunter of the night, POKENAME swoops down and uses the bone club it carries to knock out prey in one strike. A second swoop follows, snatching up its target to be taken back to its lair.
author: sk372

entry: Though it resembles a Noivern, this Pokémon cannot make high-pitched noises to orient itself in the dark. Instead, it has a thick bone plating on its throat that, when struck with POKENAME's club, creates a loud sound that it then uses to echolocate.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME have sticky liquid bodies that are vulnerable to harm from larger Pokémon. To protect themselves they gather up bones to stick to themselves as armour.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With a sensitive heart, POKENAME is prone to crying at the drop of a hat. The tears it sheds are a thick and viscous fluid that often leaves sticky streaks trailing down from its eyes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's pollen clouds cause strong hallucinations in victims. In ancient times, people thought it caused them to glimpse into the afterlife, giving it a feared reputation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is incredibly forlorn, bonding with the first person to show it kindness. Its attachment is so great that it sometimes lashes out at family and friends, fearful they will take its beloved companion from it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME decorates the underside of its wings with bones. This macabre display not only intimidates some of its opponents, but it can pluck them from its wings to throw as projectiles in battle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the sand and pretends to be the skull of a fallen creature, until something wanders too close.  It leaps from the sand with a cry, and comes down with a spiky-limb punch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects bones of those who've fallen in the desert. However, it will be friendly to those still alive and follow them around.
author: ohok3441

entry: Occasionally a murder of Murkrow will follow a POKENAME around. POKENAME provides them with protection while the Murkrow lead it to new bones.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME roams the dark dunes of deserts at night. It seems almost apathetic, as it shows no reaction no matter what happens and stays on its path.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are scavengers and tend to avoid battle. However, if one can't, it will thwack opponents with its staff until they faint.
author: ohok3441

entry: If the skull on its head is stolen, it will attempt to chase after the thief, but its slow speed usually prevents it from catching them. If they escape, POKENAME will begin bawling uncontrollably, unable to be consoled unless the skull is returned.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's mushrooms have a brittle texture and a terribly bitter and sour taste, so few bother to pick them from it. The unique flavor is actually quite liked by certain Ghost types, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME takes on the appearance of a friendly sanctum for small Pokémon to gather under for safety. Its extreme loneliness makes it very clingy, however, so those that enter beneath its skull dome are not allowed to leave.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are used as a camp ground for Cubones to rest. However, despite originally being believed to be created by the Cubones, POKENAME are an actual living Pokémon.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME's mask grows colder as it stores energy within its body. This makes it especially frigid shortly after waking.
author: .izik

entry: Friendly and unfailingly loyal, POKENAME makes for a devoted, if slightly over-attached, pet. Its most beloved bonding activity is playing fetch with its Trainer using its favorite bone.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skull rattles rapidly while it howls. The bone itself is as hard as granite, amplifying the sound across rocky terrain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carries a strange mushroom with it that dispenses heavy amounts of spores with a single shake. Living things that come in contact with the spores have their eyes become extremely irritated and watery for several hours.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skull scale is extremely sensitive to debris. If dust settles on it, the Pokémon cries for hours until tears wash it clean.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME throws its bone at diamond clusters in cave walls. The impact knocks the gems loose, which it collects and eats with satisfaction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home inside the skulls of other dead Pokémon. The remnants of rotting meat serve as a great fertilizer for POKENAME's mushrooms to grow, while the skull itself provides protection from larger predators.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME's compound eyes let it easily spot oncoming threats and move to avoid them. When alone, it has a habit of chewing on the bone it carries to calm its nerves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME practices casting fire magic, using the bone it carries as its staff. It ignites the tip with its flame breath before flinging the fireball at its target.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hide in sandy places where their natural camouflage keeps them hidden. They practice throwing bones to improve their aim.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME secrete foam-like bubbles that offer protection and that serve well to keep their skulls clean. These bubbles can be eaten by others and are surprisingly good sources of calcium as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME throw boney boomerangs that can bounce between targets in quick succession. They can extend the range of their projectiles by coating them with a bubble to minimize air resistance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses its foamy bubbles to clean its skull and its bone club; during summer, these bubbles also help it to stay hydrated. Because it will often throw stones and its own club at foes, it has remarkable accuracy.
author: infinex21

entry: When upset, copious amounts of steam pour out from the eyes of POKENAME's skull-like shell. Sometimes, the steam clouds take the shape of Cubone or Marowak before dissipating.
author: sk372

entry: Its shell has taken the form of a skull to better defend itself by intimidating others. It feeds on coal to keep its internal flames strong, though the vapors and smoke it releases have stained the skull with traces of coal.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME likes to target those traveling at night through forests for its pranks. Using a bit of ghostly energy, it throws hexes of bad luck from its bone, using it like a magic wand.
author: sk372

entry: To mark territory, POKENAME slams its bone into alley dumpsters. The dents it leaves behind serve as signals to others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: Bones grow from POKENAME's core and jut out of holes in its exterior. It fires these bones as a self-defense method, the hollow holes glowing a faint, colorful energy until a new bone grows and fills the gap anew.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME emits a strange energy that lets it control the broken off bone shards of its shell-like casing. Using this, it manipulates them into weapons and armor to keep itself safe from attackers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME keeps a stash of bones stored at its home since its tendency to light them causes them to calcify and become fragile. When feeling sad, instead of crying, it repeatedly bashes an object with its bone to let its emotions out.
author: soup1900

entry: Their saliva and sweat act as accelerants that allow them to easily ignite their own bone clubs. Their flames become increasingly more intense when faced with a foe stronger than they are.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME roast meat with their flaming bone skewers that ensure an even temperature throughout the meat. Once the food is ready, they offer extras to wild Pokémon as a gesture of kindness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It wears the skull of another unfortunate Diglett on its head for protection. POKENAME was first discovered after sightings of "Diglett ghosts" became increasingly more common.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME appears to be drawn to feelings of loneliness. It leaps from the water into the arms of those feeling isolated, and cries for them out of sympathy.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers hoping to raise POKENAME are advised to adopt them in pairs. It is easily prone to lonesomeness, and needs the presence of another of its kind in order to not become depressed.
author: sk372

entry: When hungry, POKENAME leaves its bone in its bowl to alert its Trainer. It tries to obey every command for fear of being abandoned and left alone.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are desert Pokémon that use the noses of their skulls to search for buried remains within the sand. They search for the densest bones to crack open so they may feed on the rich marrow within.
author: infinex21

entry: A herd of POKENAME running through the desert is often mistaken for a small sandstorm due to how fast they move. Their skulls are stained with tears wrought by the sand they kick up into their own eyes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's back is covered with a bony carapace to keep itself safer from predators. It rarely crawls down from its home on branches, using thread shot from its mouth to reel in food from the forest floor.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carries a duo of bones and skulls with it at all times. It has been observed speaking to them regularly, and some observers swear to have faintly heard responses on occasion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have an affinity for bones that makes them well-suited to helping on archaeological digs. Their three heads are able to work together to find the bones of long-dead creatures, guiding their trainers toward them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME pilfer bones from graveyards and store them in their dens. The bones that end up in their care are typically held in better condition than buried bones, as they dust and polish bones to ensure the bones do not decompose.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Easily upset, POKENAME cries constantly and loudly. Its decibel levels while crying could cause cave-ins, so many other creatures kick it out of their dens on sight, making it even more despondent.
author: sk372

entry: Before rival POKENAME get into a shoving match to express dominance, they use their collected bones to beat the ground as a customary pre-battle ritual. The loser will have to forfeit some of its bones to the victor.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME take fastidious care of bones kept in their dens, preserving the bones with utmost care. Museum curators have recently begun befriending POKENAME in an effort to find bones to display in museums.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoy cheering on their friends with their boney baton. They often wave a flag attached to their baton and produce sparks whenever they are excited.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME toss their boney baton into the air whenever they cheer on their teammates. Their energetic zeal causes them to release sparks whenever they are excited, especially when their teammates are about to win.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are incredibly loyal to their Trainer and will do anything to protect them. Whenever their Trainer experiences the mildest inconvenience, they get so irrationally angry that they experience a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are reckless creatures that often get hurt even though they wear a thick skull atop their heads. Keeping POKENAME safe when they play is of utmost importance to avoid headaches, literally and metaphorically.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME throw bony boomerangs to attack opponents, but the bones often circle back to hit their heads. No matter how hard they try, the boomerangs always slip through their hands and end up hitting them in their faces.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tend to be gloomy creatures that feel a forlorn sadness whenever they are left out of activities. Trainers can easily remedy this by giving them a buddy so that they do not feel lonely.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME slowly drift along the ground, only increasing in speed when they're carried along by the wind. Under clear skies, they occasionally pause and look up to admire the view, as if remembering something to cheer them up before they continue on.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It takes time to carefully clean cemeteries, showing respect for the departed. This unusual habit earns it admiration from others.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever POKENAME get angry, they slam their clubs against their skull, screaming from the pain. This display of dominance scares most Pokémon into giving them food in an effort to quell their anger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often play alone because their boney mask makes them too scary for other Pokémon. They throw flaming bone clubs through the forest so that they can play fetch with themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's skull briefly turns white hot before unleashing fire-based attacks. The heat intensifies depending on the strength of the flames it produces.
author: .izik

entry: During hot summer nights, it howls at the moon. People who hear this howl describe suddenly feeling immense grief.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Their slender, yet strong, tails are clad in a bone-like armor, allowing it to serve as a strong weapon. The bone clubs they wield are always changing based on the prey they last hunted. They always seek greater challenges.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are known to skewer meat onto their wings and rest over searing flames to cook meat to their liking. Bits of meat get caught on their wings, so they allow Flying-type Pokémon to have a bite if they help pick meat off their wings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wear small skulls that fit snugly on their head when they are underwater. When they are above water for an extended period of time, the skull shrinks from losing moisture and becomes prone to falling off their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME was a common sight in the past as part of the many pirate crews. It used its large bone club to help its partners in crime board other ships and plunder their belongings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fights with a great strength tinged with a great sorrow. It's fairly common to see its eyes heavy with tears even as it battles opponents with all its might.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME appear to be crying, though the tears are merely a reflex to keep their own skin from drying out. This serves to make other Pokémon see them as meek, so they must always keep their bodies well-trained for battle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME defends itself from multiple angles with the telekinetically controlled bones of deceased Marowak. In serious situations, it reforms the entire skeleton to battle an opponent alongside it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collect bones of other Pokémon to wear as armor, even though they can easily teleport away. Measuring brain activity of these Pokémon reveals that these bones are associated with family and connectedness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can use its psychic powers to manipulate small and light particles, such as sand. It also is able to manipulate foes and favored items such as a bone it may carry around. It can't seem to use telekinesis on many other objects, however.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME add psychic energy into their throws to amplify the range of their boney boomerangs. It is said that the cry of the deceased Pokémon can be heard as the boomerang whizzes by, but scientists have yet to record such noises.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wears and wields several bones across its body. Using its powerful mind, it can control these skeletal pieces all at once in battle, giving it a wide range of attacks to use on foes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wear a set of armor made out of bones that protect them from physical attacks. While a normal throw can send boney boomerangs a long distance, with additional psychic energy they can easily clear a football field with a single throw.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It waves its bone at lightning storms, absorbing the electric charge into its body. This energy boosts its strength, making it even more formidable.
author: .izik

entry: It channels all its grief into powerful punches, unleashing its sorrow with each strike. This coping mechanism makes it a relentless fighter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wields bone clubs in two hands while the other two remain empty-handed, letting it excel in two combat methods. Some more aggressive POKENAME have been seen fashioning bone gauntlets for their fists.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have roots and vines wrapped around their skull. When another Pokémon tries to eat them, they throw sharpened bones covered with a poisonous sap to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They can withdraw most of their bodies into their shells and use jets of water to launch themselves at foes. Some POKENAME love to smack their own shells like drums using their bone clubs.
author: infinex21

entry: The bulbs poking through the skull POKENAME wears help it navigate, sensing surroundings with bio-electric pulses. Its sting causes allergic reactions near the eyes, resulting in irritation, excessive tear production and even blindness in some cases.
author: sk372

entry: When it swings its bone, it lets out a blood-curdling howl. This chilling sound strikes fear into anyone who hears it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scare away Pokémon that eat rocks by slamming a bone club against their thick skull helmet. They always carry this club wherever they go and hug this bone when they sleep to ensure it does not get lost.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The first sightings of POKENAME in the past caused slight mass panic due to its ghastly appearance, leading to many horror stories about them. Fortunately, modern times let people realize the species is harmless and in fact quite shy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's morbid appearance and odd-colored flames gave it a dark initial reputation. Old folk tales say it would appear to chase down and forcibly drag innocent souls to the underworld.
author: sk372

entry: It feels angry and forlorn, though it cannot remember the reason why.  It finds some tranquility when in the presence of Slowpoke and Cubone families.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims through riverbanks in search of opponents to test its mettle against. The more scratches its shell and skull helmet show, the more battle-hardened POKENAME becomes.
author: sk372

entry: When it starts to cry, it unleashes bursts of electricity that shock those nearby. These fits make it unpredictable and dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: The POKENAME trio can separate to better evade or attack foes. The center member directs the other two with waves of its magnetically-charged bone.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers up bones from old nests to use as a tool. It is intelligent enough to draw symbols in the ground with its bone in order to better communicate with humans.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their bone clubs as weapons and to ground up berries and plants; some will mix these ingredients together to make a meal. Each bone club has a different flavor and scent that clings to them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME emits echoing chirps from within its skulls while sleeping. The sound is calming to others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: The skulls upon both of its heads are stained with tears, wrought by one head stealing food from the other every so often; both heads are equally at fault. It communicates with others of its species by knocking its skulls together.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME possess highly aerodynamic bodies and powerful legs, cutting through the vast deserts and plains with ease. POKENAME charge their prey down with superior speed, and lance them with their protruding skull like a spear.
author: gdottb

entry: POKENAME love performing tricks for people at aquariums throughout the world. Whenever they toss their boney club into the air, they always manage to catch it with ease.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME scavenges old bones from forests and caves. The bones it wears are bleached smooth due to its highly corrosive body.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME peruses graveyards, exhuming anything it finds to grow it's collection of bones. It can be repelled from an area with an average garden hose.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME lives in foul smelling swamps, lurking beneath the soft soil. Although POKENAME is typically passive, if anyone mistakes it for a mound of mud and tries to take its Thick Club, it attacks furiously.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME have bodies of shifting sand held together by a sticky, albeit toxic, material within. This same material serves as their digestive fluid, allowing them to quickly dissolve any prey they swallow whole.
author: infinex21

entry: The skull on its head constantly oozes a putrid-smelling sludge. You can locate it from 20 miles away from its smell alone.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's large size belies its tender heart, and it is quite emotional. When sad or angry, the water it shoots from its cannons fires at twice the usual strength.
author: sk372

entry: Holding it with its tongue, POKENAME wields a bone as a weapon with surprising dexterity. The pointed teeth of its skull give it a painful bite force as well, should its bone-club prove ineffective.
author: sk372

entry: The bone-like protrusions on the side of POKENAME's shell can launch out and home in on targets. Once they've connected and knocked out a foe, the bones fly back and slot into place.
author: sk372

entry: It spits sand at foes to disorient and confuse them. This sneaky tactic often gives it the upper hand in combat.
author: .izik

entry: It frequently drops its skull, bursting into laughter before sobbing uncontrollably. This strange behavior confuses both allies and foes.
author: .izik

entry: Rumors say it steals bones from graveyards, adding them to its collection. This eerie behavior unsettles both humans and Pokémon alike.
author: .izik

entry: Its entire body is coated in a bone-like rock. Archaeologists once unearthed a slumbering POKENAME by mistake, believing it to be a large fossil.
author: frokachu

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is gentle and non-confrontational. It prefers gently nudging or batting away problems with the bone on its tail rather than using its massive stone-and-bone-covered body.
author: sk372

entry: Contrary to popular belief, the white material covering POKENAME's body is not bone but a rock with a texture similar to Chalky Stone. Its tail, however, is actual bone and much more brittle.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It uses psychic power to redirect its bone mid-flight, ensuring precision strikes. This skill makes its bone an unpredictable weapon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's skull helmet protects it somewhat from the psychic assaults of other Pokémon. Rapping the bone it carries against its pendulum causes it to generate extremely powerful hypnotic waves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects bones from the beaches to make a den for itself. Though a home made entirely of bones seems intimidating, POKENAME is quite friendly and docile.
author: sk372

entry: When it shakes or clacks its claws together, they make an eerie hollow rattling sound that is effective at frightening off predators. The claws themselves are somewhat brittle and ill-equipped for prolonged combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bashes the ground with the club held in its mouth to warn away potential attackers.  If the warning isn't heeded, it spits the club like a projectile before rolling  forward quickly to get close and trigger a devastating explosion.
author: sk372

entry: Familial love allows the spirit of a Marowak to stay tethered to the mortal realm. Though it is no longer alive, the ghost will stay by its side and protect it always.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are said to channel spirits into the flames on their staff, with each new spirit adding to the strength of the fire. If their staff does not strike on the first pass, it is likely to hit when it boomerangs back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its tongue to fling its bone at high speeds. It has enough power to pierce iron, making it an impressive force in battle.
author: .izik

entry: The horn at the end of POKENAME's skull can easily pierce steel. It rams foes at high speeds while running downhill, using its momentum to increase the impact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is so durable that there has never been a specimen seen with a crack on its bony armor. It lives among Rhyhorn colonies, keeping watch over the young in particular.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is said to communicate with the souls of fallen Marowak. It takes it upon itself to care for any and all Cubone it comes across, to soothe the matron spirit it communes with.
author: sk372

entry: Its motherly instincts kick into action whenever an attacker approaches it. A swing of its Bone Club can snap a tree in half.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Despite its already tough exoskeleton, POKENAME has adapted the skulls and bones of its fallen foes into armor for added protection. Its razor-sharp scythes effortlessly slice through opponents, making it a formidable force in battle.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME dress in bones and proudly flaunt their scars. Babies are abandoned at birth; adults are broody and stern, secluding themselves to weep.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME have long been prone to rampaging so much that they developed extra hard exoskeletons. Their exoskeletal heads are harder than diamond, though their horns are remarkably brittle.
author: infinex21

entry: These maternal Pokémon will protect young Pokémon of any species. They are almost always willing to carry those they care for upon their backs and can do so for long periods of time without needing to rest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's syrup-like body imitates piles of bones deep in crypts. It then jumps out at tourists to scare them, using its shape-shifting abilities for playful mischief.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often form in packs of 9, acting as a family when together. POKENAME has an unusual habit of eating wet mud and bones, which is why its skeletal structure can still be seen.
author: animecreep4

entry: The bright flames this Pokémon makes are fueled by a special mineral, which gives them their color. POKENAME loves playing fetch with its bone.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME carries bones that appear to be formed from countless lines of digital code. It is said that those who are true pacifists cannot perceive these weapons at all.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME search through archeological digs for a new skull. When another POKENAME challenges them for a skull upgrade, they gnaw on each other's limbs until one gives up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is the best-recorded attempt at reviving prehistoric life. Though strong, it's surprisingly docile, and its blades are brittle.
author: patch_bros

entry: POKENAME seemingly has no muscles, making its ability to fly a scientific wonder. When this Pokémon moves, its bones rattle unsettlingly.
author: gnom3

entry: Despite its tattered wings, POKENAME can take to the skies, catching spiraling winds that take it high above. It's able to fly in the ozone layer as the lack of air and the building pressure doesn't affect its ancient bones.
author: _pixelar_

entry: They have grown large with muscle and fat, to the point they can never fully remove their skull "helmets" without breaking them. They are adept hunters who can use the bones and meat of their prey for sustenance and as weapons.
author: infinex21

entry: Ancient records mention POKENAME flying into large battles, and using its hard skull to charge at any combatants. Its appearance signified that everyone needed to focus on defeating it. For this reason, POKENAME is seen as a symbol of unity.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME make their nests in the skeletons of giant Pokémon. Their stingers are rarely used to sting, instead opting for blunt force.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME's tail is made of thousands of sand particles that cycle between heating, rising, cooling, and falling, creating endless scorching sands. It uses this to deter predators from attacking from behind.
author: chewquy

entry: POKENAME hunts by ambushing unsuspecting prey and rapidly jabbing them with its long, sharp bone weapon. It produces silk that it uses to weave sophisticated traps and in conjunction with its bone to travel quickly by harpooning through the trees.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME was often seen as an assistant to priests of ancient tribal civilizations. It was believed that using and wearing the bones of fallen Pokémon allowed it to draw from their spirits and gaze into the afterlife.
author: sk372

entry: Though POKENAME has overcome the grief of a lost friend, it carries their memory in its heart. It fights to protect young Pokémon wherever it goes.
author: leshii

entry: During thunderstorms, POKENAME absorbs electricity into the orb on the tip of its bone. It uses the charged weapon to defend its territory and young.
author: mepp.

entry: The skull on POKENAME's head is forged from multiple metallic elements and is extremely hard. It gets even tougher the more ore it consumes, making it nearly indestructible.
author: .izik

entry: While raising their young, POKENAME are intensely protective and will be quick to attack anyone who gets too close. If stoked into a rage, they will fly erratically, repeatedly slamming their large bodies into everything around them.
author: fireblade141

entry: The bones of its rivals are worn by POKENAME as a monument to its strength and triumph over others. It's thought that ancient tribes used POKENAME's markings as inspiration in their magical practices.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often used to search through the aftermath of lava flows for anything that was unfortunate enough to be caught up in it. They unearth the remains and carry them to the local cemetery, delivering the bones to the groundskeeper.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Wild POKENAME search through the aftermath of lava flows for anything that was unfortunate enough to be caught up in it. They consume the remains left behind, incorporating the minerals from the charred bones into their shell.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The orange substance atop POKENAME's head also saturates its entire body, and when enraged, it will shake its head wildly to launch the goop at its foes. The blade it thrashes about in combat is made of sharpened bone.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME are desert scavengers that leave nothing of their prey behind. Their beaks and talons are sharp enough to break through the tough shells of other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME chews on the bones of undersea creatures to gain nutrients. If it neglected to do so, its teeth and water-spitting capacity would stagnate, leaving it less able to defend itself from larger creatures.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME can often be found in over its head fighting battles it can't win. It strengthens the bone armor on its head by knocking it into foes.
author: gasmaskblacky

entry: This Pokémon has pride in the toughness of its bone armor. Fearing no confrontation, it barrels towards foes with reckless abandon.
author: gasmaskblacky

entry: POKENAME throws its bone with its tail to knock out prey, accurate over 300 feet. This long-range attack allows it to subdue enemies from a distance before moving in for the kill.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is not a good milk supplier; however, it is nimble and territorial, making it a popular guard for Miltank herds in arid regions.
author: gasmaskblacky

entry: Wishing to honor the memories of those close to its heart after their death, POKENAME burns their bones down to ashes and scatters them across the world with its wings.
author: milchik

entry: You can find POKENAME on the tops of trees. However, it is considered a pest in most regions, as it hurls bones at unsuspecting Trainers.
author: lyrebird.rainwing

entry: POKENAME are almost always surrounded by piles of bones. They nest around as many as possible to try to scare off other Pokémon from their nests.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME spins its bone to charge electricity, then unleashes the energy in big bursts. This attack is potent enough to overwhelm its foes with its sheer electrical power.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often act as shamans to Weavile packs, providing healing to injured members and acting as a guide to the group. While hunting with its pack-mates, it calls forth icy winds from its staff, distracting prey.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Its many vines have subsumed countless prey and would-be predators, with their many bones entangled within. POKENAME use these bones to strike their opponents and their long arms to claw at them with smaller bones held together with vines.
author: infinex21

entry: It wields a large, refined bone of a foe as a giant blade to fight with. POKENAME can use its vine-like cape to make long leaps and strike from above with cleaving chops.
author: infinex21

entry: The bones that jut out of POKENAME's back can channel its electricity. It charges its Thunderbolts between these bones.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME collects discarded biological material and even the remains of fallen beings and buries them. This material acts as compost; within several years, the areas POKENAME has visited may become lush with plant life.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The skulls and tusks of these Pokémon are colder than solid ice, yet tougher than diamond. Many tundra explorers and Rangers ride upon these Pokémon, as they can endure harsh cold and harbor enough strength to shatter most obstacles.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its bone to carve lines into stone to mark its territory. Small groups were recently seen near Rock Tunnel creating visible signs of their presence.
author: .izik

entry: Able to run across the desert at eighty miles per hour, POKENAME is constantly seeking challengers. When fighting, its kicks are a blur of motion, until it decides to finish the foe with an aerial double bone club strike.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Despite being a master of unarmed combat, POKENAME insists on fighting with a set of bone tonfa. Waiting until night, they ignite the tips confounding other Pokémon's night vision.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME frequently utilizes man-made items when fighting. Some professors studying POKENAME behavior have questioned whether it likes hurting other Pokémon.
author: cal_nd_stuff

entry: POKENAME have a morbid curiosity for death because they understand that death is a painful subject for many. This early mental maturity allows them to empathize with others whenever a loved one is lost.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are heroic Pokémon that go out of their way to protect the innocent. By twirling on their long legs, they can fling their boney boomerang with enough force to crack through shells.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME often care for young, lost Pokémon even if they are other species. The bone-shaped protrusion that appears to run through its chest is a medium through which it can call upon otherworldly powers to defend others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME act as protectors of orphaned Pokémon. Anyone who harms a young Pokémon is sure to get a beating.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Even if POKENAME whacks you 100 times, the wooden stick it carries will never hurt you as long as you believe it won't. Sometimes, POKENAME appears in the dreams of those without a loving person to take care of them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME emerge from a keystone full of the resentment of the spirits that have died from habitat loss. They slam their bones against concrete roads to cause potholes in an effort to slow the deforestation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its bone club serves as a conduit for its aura, allowing it to channel its aura and form weapons from it or to release it as condensed blasts. By imbuing the bone club with aura, it can ensure its Bonemerang attack strikes true.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME isolate themselves in caves, avoiding all social interaction, especially with humans. Legends claim the skull on their back holds a distressed spirit that watches over them.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its bony skull is so tough that it could topple a building without cracking. When nervous, POKENAME lashes the ground with the club it holds in its tail, creating seismic tremors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have a set of razor-sharp serrated teeth that jut out from their skull and can pierce through rocks. Their bite releases a corrosive toxin that makes healing after a bite difficult.
author: ghostslythe

entry: By roaming ancient ruins, POKENAME ensure the protection of ancient royalty from tomb raiders. If they encounter an intruder inside the ruins, they trap them in a bony cage before ushering them out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collects large amounts of water in its mouth and mixes it with its own stomach acid. This giant reservoir of bone dissolving water quickly becomes a deadly trap for anyone staying in it to long.
author: thezekrom

entry: POKENAME are known by many to be overseers of abandoned graveyards, tending to the truly forgotten. Tales tell of POKENAME howling mournfully in the twilight as spirits of the departed, man and Pokémon, join it in harmony.
author: beatdoof

entry: The shell of POKENAME is covered in a surprisingly fertile soil. Though rare, following desert rains its shell can bloom with short-lived plant life and desert flowers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The shell of POKENAME is covered in a surprisingly fertile soil. Though rare, following desert rains its shell can bloom with short-lived plant life and desert flowers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rely on bone tools to make their lives easier. From clubs to bash prey to rudimentary nails used to make tents, POKENAME are clever creatures that experiment with the tools available to them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Considered one of the most sapient Pokémon known, POKENAME mark their territories with various paints that they also apply to their skull-clad heads. They live in small groups, and the one with the most decorated bone club is the leader.
author: infinex21

entry: Deep in the heart of the desert, POKENAME digs for skulls of ancient Pokémon. When found, it dusts them off and adds any outstanding specimens to its collection. If one is especially magnificent, it replaces its helm.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME magnetize stones in order to scoop up and collect various bones and skulls from the depths of canyons and caverns. They construct the bones into armor for their stony bodies to protect themselves from cracking.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME was crafted from the remains and still-present spirit a battle-hardened beast, as evident by its movements in battle.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The two blades are made of exquisitely sharpened bones. POKENAME's fighting style is extremely aggressive, hacking away wildly at opponents with both swords, as if taking out repressed anger out on its opponents.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME soars across vast deserts and arid plains. It has a dependable nature and is often seen protecting weaker Cubone fusions from threatening foes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is a fierce hunter that moves smoothly through desert sands as if it were water. It seizes its prey with seaweed-like tendrils before constricting them and dragging them beneath the sand.
author: sk372

entry: A side-effect of POKENAME's fusion causes its wings to wither down to bone. It grieves endlessly about this and often lashes out in frustration.
author: phantom640

entry: Wherever ancient burial grounds are kept, POKENAME visits, usually appearing as a researcher. It digs through the graves, stealing fossilized bones to use as weapons, then knocks out any witnesses.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME live in dry, arid habitats. Their numbers have recently dwindled, causing sightings to become rare. Old rural legends claim POKENAME raid farms to devour Miltank and other domestic Pokémon, though these stories remain unproven.
author: bitoboy.

entry: POKENAME ordinarily keeps to itself in the wild, until it senses the sorrow of those who have lost a family member. Drawn to their sadness, it lightly touches them with its ribbon, which allows the person to feel a sense of catharsis.
author: sk372

entry: Its saliva is a highly-concentrated, toxic substance that can corrode many things, including bones and some metals as well. They only use this on others if cornered, otherwise they will fight with just their pure, brute strength.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has sections of exposed bone to streamline its flight through the ozone layer. It comes down from the sky to feast on bones, absorbing the calcium to strengthen its own skeletal structure.
author: thezekrom

entry: White fur grows and clings to its head like a skull with a flowing mane. Its claws are harder than bone and secrete a dark energy that chills victims to their own bones.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME finds scattered bones, it waits until nightfall to dance for them one last time, honoring their spirit with a graceful ritual. Onlookers say the air around it grows still and reverent as it moves.
author: curazy

entry: It wields the bone of a foe bested long ago, which it has refined into a blade so it may continue to challenge others and grow. The mushrooms at the tip of its tail release invigorating spores that it shares with its opponents after fair fights.
author: infinex21

entry: Fueled by loss and hardship, POKENAME developed psychic powers and now uses a mystic fire to control the bones it uses as weapons. Despite how tough and unforgiving they are in battle, they are very kind otherwise.
author: lootererswillbeboated

entry: If POKENAME's bone skull is in contact with moonlight, it gains a slight pink shimmer. This effect makes it especially striking under the full moon, adding to its mystique.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME places the safety of its territory and its loved ones above everything else, including itself. It will recklessly charge headfirst into battle if its nest is encroached upon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME roams the quarries at night, searching for motherless Cubone. POKENAME's bulky armor protects its foundlings from harm.
author: thropp

entry: POKENAME stay on mountain cliffs, overlooking their territory to spot their next prey. When they catch suitable prey, the two heads left and right grab their victim while the large middle one delivers bone-crushing attacks.
author: thezekrom

entry: POKENAME uses its bone club to vault off of cliffsides. It can vault up to 5 miles in a single bound, and pretends it's flying through the air.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's bone club emits a faint aura that lets it gently put people into a restful slumber. It stays near the sleeper, using the club just as effectively for defense should an attacker draw close to them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tries to keep a tough yet stoic disposition, as it is eager to look strong and well beyond its years. It may build its nest in many different ways, such as in a wall with rocks, or on the ground with debris.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME, remaining mostly active at night, knocks out foes with its large bone before drinking their blood. Its swift and brutal attacks make it a fearsome nighttime predator.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are frail and utilize their skeleton-like figures to camouflage themselves within various hazardous terrains. Their bodies are brimming with electricity that they release against anyone who touches them, frying them within seconds.
author: infinex21

entry: Hordes of POKENAME can be found wandering abandoned mineshafts using the pickaxes they carry to mine nutritious minerals. They are also used when infighting occurs, especially over rare or particularly tasty mineral veins.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME can travel long distances through the desert without needing to stop for water. Their tough hides slow water loss from their bodies. They are hardy Pokémon and can resist most dangers thanks to their bony plates.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME may seem menacing and dangerous, but it only wants to play fetch. The only problem is that its bone can be lifted only by the strongest Pokémon and thrown by very few.
author: chewquy

entry: POKENAME are believed to be born from desecrated remains inhabited by malicious spirits. Their bodies are clad in many bones, some growing from within, and they wield a long, unbreakable bone club.
author: infinex21

entry: Both POKENAME's helmet and wings are made of hardened cartilage. Its wings do not allow flight, but curiously can maintain its weight for gliding. As it glides, the wind whips through its ears creating supersonic waves.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The extra skull POKENAME holds is where it both stores its energy and fires it at foes in the form of a powerful laser. When angered, it goes on a destructive rampage, using Bonemerang to chop down all buildings in its path.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME follows weary travelers in deserts and forests at a distance, watching them. It will steal from Trainers who turn their back.
author: ohok3441

entry: The weapons POKENAME carries are meant to scare off potential threats. In battle, they will take them apart to use as clubs.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME roams the desert at night and is said to hunt people who have done something wrong. Its exact intentions are not known to anyone.
author: chorb33

entry: The Honchkrow around POKENAME are typically bonded Murkrow rather than new additions. Sometimes they will be adorned with bones too.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME roams the desert at night and is said to hunt people who have done something wrong. Its exact intentions are not known to anyone.
author: chorb33

entry: If the skull is cracked, POKENAME will hide its face until it finds a new mask. The horns are believed to be part of its body rather than décor.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME lure in unsuspecting prey by pretending to be in need of help, only to whack those nice enough to come close.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME is thought to be the result of a Sandygast forming a symbiotic bond with a Cubone that fell into its trap. This bond has allowed them both to reach their evolutions, turning them into an apex predator that throws bone shards at new victims.
author: doodledoo

entry: The bone at the end of POKENAME's tail is incredibly solid, strong enough to shatter a boulder with a single swing. It travels alone, only interacting with others when it sees young Pokémon in need of protection.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known to travel in packs, fiercely protecting each other. They battle by headbutting foes before striking with their clubs. POKENAME are used at dig sites to help excavate fossils, uncovering them by dusting them off with their tails.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME uses the bones of fallen foes as armor to protect its weak points. Each piece is treasured and will only be replaced if broken beyond repair.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME scuttles around caverns, pretending to be a hollow skull to avoid predators. It is said that if one listens closely, the faint and eerie cry of a Marowak can be heard echoing within the skull-like growth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to thwack new objects with their large bone club until they find objects that create a pleasant noise when they're struck. Wild POKENAME will hoard such objects and use them to produce music, but also to communicate with each other.
author: infinex21

entry: In Sinnoh, POKENAME is thought to be a servant of Giratina, always appearing in desperate times. It makes the situations worse, its skull focus belching flames while its body causes dust to pick up to sand storms.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME have an innate paternal instinct that causes them to watch over young Pokémon, no matter their species. They protect them from the shadows and dispatch threats with throwing stars made of compressed water.
author: infinex21

entry: Blue flames roar within and without its skull-shaped shell as it moves, veiling it in a haze of heat and smoke. The flames it breathes are focused enough to melt solid bone within minutes, so there is often little left of its prey.
author: infinex21

entry: The horns on POKENAME's skull release large clouds of grey powder when it is distressed. This cloud can disorient foes, making it a potent defense mechanism.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hold onto their bony boomerang with a steady hand and are always ready to defend their flaming tails. Being trusted to touch their tail is a sign of high trust and respect.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME scrapes the bone it carries across its skull to set it aflame, lighting it like a match. Its fighting style gets fiercer once its bone is on fire, so Trainers should take care to make sure it doesn't get carried away in battle.
author: sk372

entry: Theories state that POKENAME has its own private collection of bones buried underground, each one suited to handle various situations.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME regularly burrow through fossil-rich rock layers, picking up the bones of long-dead Pokémon as they do. They wear these bones as armour, protecting themselves from harm whenever they need to surface for food or water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often come into conflict with Marowak, both Pokémon regularly travelling to Pokémon burial grounds. Whilst POKENAME dig through the grounds in search of a meal, Marowak fight them off to protect the bodies laid to rest.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The bony covering over POKENAME's skull gives its cries a reverberating effect and increases its bass levels. It can cause seismic activity in its immediate surroundings using its powerful voice.
author: sk372

entry: While they may look like predators, wild POKENAME are actually opportune scavengers, circling from a safe distance while other predators finish their prey.
author: kingd8

entry: POKENAME roam the deserts, picking the rotting meat clean from bones long-abandoned by other scavengers. Their stomachs have adapted to the point where they can no longer even digest fresh meat.
author: kingd8

entry: POKENAME wear the skull of another Pokémon and rely on it to protect them from attacks. Attacks that vibrate the skull cause them to experience painful headaches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The mucus POKENAME spits out is extremely harmful, being able to melt through metal. Due to this, some believe their spit has spectral properties that accelerate the corrosion. The bone POKENAME carries is said to be their most private possession.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: Exposure to rain and its own tears have eroded its skull cap, giving it sharper edges that help intimidate others. It oft forgets its own strength and breaks the bones it wields as clubs.
author: infinex21

entry: The star present on POKENAME's skull changes color as it grows smarter and more psychically proficient. Gold is considered the highest rank, though rumors persist of a level beyond even that.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses powerful telekinesis to control sand and wind alike and create sandstorms at will. Whirling bones propelled by dusty tornadoes will assault any that disturb its solitude.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its bone to dislodge boulders from mountain ledges, then lifts them to train its strength. This constant training ensures it maintains peak physical condition.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME possesses a physique and strength near unparalleled, and maintains a quiet, somber persona. Some say it trains constantly because it fears the possibility of lacking the strength to protect its loved ones.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are commonly used by archaeologists to lift heavy fossils or rocks out of the ground without the use of machinery. They have even uncovered fossils belonging to Pokémon such as Aerodactyl and Dragonite.
author: rumia_archer

entry: POKENAME are always flying in search of greater challenges and prey alike. They can throw their bone clubs with enough force to crack a tree, though then must rely on their bodies or their flames until they can acquire a new club.
author: infinex21

entry: Its bone mask is said to hold a horrible curse. Legends say if the mask is worn by someone with impure thoughts, it heavily restricts lung function.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wear the bones of other Pokémon as a sort of macabre armor. When a bone becomes too smooth or brittle to function, POKENAME bury the bone before replacing it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite their terrifying appearance, these Pokémon are incredibly friendly. Their form is meant for intimidation. Their flames will only harm those they wish them to, making them popular steeds of the past and the present.
author: infinex21

entry: Its bone is worn with use from battle and from being used to make its meals. If it ever loses this tool, such as when throwing it at a foe, it will not rest until it finds the bone again.
author: infinex21

entry: The skulls on each head are so solidly built that it's often said nothing can survive being hit by all three in tandem. POKENAME dashes across arid dry lands at night, leaping through the air with a piercing cry.
author: sk372

entry: Its bones are filled with a very potent sludge, even compared to the ooze that makes up its body. If one of its bones breaks during battle, it will release an odor so foul it can incapacitate an unprepared battler.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The willpower stored in its skull attempts to form a solid, proud body. It never seems to get all the way there, but it improves every day.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME have a stoic expression that makes them seem cold and aloof, even though they are affectionate Pokémon. They protect those they love by throwing bony boomerangs and blocking incoming attacks with their sturdy shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME default to a stern expression, which makes them seem aloof, but they are rather affectionate once they warm up to others. Their water-propelled bone cannon easily shatters rocks on impact.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME relies on its outer shell to throw bony projectiles at foes that boomerang back after striking once. If a foe is too close to reliably hit with projectiles, POKENAME can swing and bludgeon foes with long bony spikes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's skull is harder than tungsten, allowing it to use it effectively while tunneling at high speeds. It breaks apart ore deposits to eat, making its skull even stronger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spins its bone with psychic powers to hypnotize anyone watching its circular movements. It has a habit of abducting Cubone cubs and raising them as its own offspring.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses the bones it carries as a makeshift lance and shield. It doesn't neglect training its own body, balancing itself on its bone-spear and practicing its kicking techniques when alone.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's kicking-based fighting style is emulated by many professional martial artists. Though it focuses almost exclusively on kicks, it has a formidable fist strike able to send a foe flying with a mere one-inch punch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's hands have become legs as well, gaining the same strength and extendable nature its legs normally possess. This gives it unparalleled combat capabilities with a unique four-kick fighting style.
author: sk372

entry: Its legs are now much springier and more powerful, allowing it to run at high speeds and leap great heights. It has been recorded that it can kick at such high speeds that the friction from the air ignites the leg doing the kicking.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME are masters of "eight-limbed" combat, using feet and fists as well as knees and elbows. POKENAME let out high-pitched yells while training.
author: kingd8

entry: A masterful fighter, it spends its entire life training both its deadly punches and its lethal kicks. All of its limbs can contract and extend like springs, granting POKENAME remarkable speed and agility.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can retract and extend its spring-coiled tongue. Their tongue is not very effective for eating.
author: themicelegion

entry: Each of POKENAME's heads can stretch out over long distances, allowing it to spread its poison gases farther and faster. It slams its heads into opponents to inflict massive damage.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME land with their wings tucked to try and blend into their surroundings. If a predator approaches, POKENAME will rapidly unfurl their wings to launch them back, taking the opportunity to kick off the ground and fly away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME possesses incredible balance, hopping from branch to branch in search of fruit to eat. If attacked, they will jump high into the air, flipping before delivering a devastating axe kick.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME excels at combatting others using its long and heavy tail. Its tail strength is enough that it could easily knock a Wailord unconscious with a single swing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dates back 300 million years ago. Researchers believe that it uses its long legs to scuttle along the ocean floor, allowing it to quickly flee predators.
author: shyguy11011

entry: It has limbs that can stretch long distances, so it combines that with its hefty weight to keep its opponent on guard; there is always the possibility it will suddenly spring its body directly into the foe instead of merely throwing a kick.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME fights by creating clouds of sand with its wings before launching unseen kicks into the dustcloud. Its powerful legs let it leap high in the air as a quick takeoff for flying.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The singular leg of POKENAME has more muscles than a human, most of which help them keep balance. They train day and night to strengthen those muscles, as falling over makes it nearly impossible to get up without assistance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's feet are equipped with large claws, which allow it to latch onto prey from afar using its stretchy legs. POKENAME will attach its prey with silk before letting them go, later tracking them down as its excitement for capturing grows.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME darts around the battlefield with its wings while striking opponents with lightning-fast kicks. It avoids using Sand Attack, considering it an underhanded tactic unless absolutely necessary.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's extendable legs pack a powerful punch for its size. Its electric control is still developing, so only about half of its kicks are able to be enhanced and charged up with electricity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME remains airborne in combat, kicking from above with its stretchy legs. It uses this same strategy to snatch prey in its talons. After a battle, it thoroughly restores its plume, a decorative mark of pride in the species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Unlike most Grass-type Pokémon, POKENAME has evolved to photosynthesize sunlight using its flowers instead of leaves. POKENAME often hides in bushes or shrubs and uses its extendable flower stems to capture energy at maximum efficiency.
author: ludacriswell

entry: Unlike most Grass-type Pokémon, POKENAME has evolved to photosynthesize sunlight using its flowers instead of leaves. This variant is exclusively found in rainforest biomes and uses its extendable flower stems to reach above native plants for energy.
author: ludacriswell

entry: Unlike most Grass-type Pokémon, POKENAME has evolved to photosynthesize sunlight using its flowers instead of leaves. This variant is exclusively found in tropical biomes and uses its extendable flower stems to reach above native plants for energy.
author: ludacriswell

entry: Unlike most Grass-type Pokémon, POKENAME has evolved to photosynthesize sunlight using its flowers instead of leaves. This variant is exclusively found in arctic biomes and uses its extendable flower stems to reach above native plants for energy.
author: ludacriswell

entry: POKENAME is often called a bean on legs, a nickname so common that scientists refer to a group of them as a 'pulse'. In battle, it uses quick kicks to fling mud into opponents' eyes, making it hard to avoid its devastating kicks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is often called a bean on legs, a nickname so common that scientists refer to a group of them as a 'pulse'. In battle, it uses quick kicks to fling mud into opponents' eyes, making it hard to avoid its devastating kicks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME stretch out their legs as they walk to reach up into the treetops and blend into the branches. They hook themselves along a branch and retract their legs off the ground to hide among the leaves and sleep.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME relies on its singular leg to launch barbed kicks toward its opponent. If the impact of the kick is not enough, the venom from its barbs may cause the opponent to pass out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though its horn is as powerful a weapon as its legs, POKENAME only uses it in battle as a last resort. It much prefers victories that come only from its kicking prowess.
author: sk372

entry: The muscles in its neck act like a spring, allowing it to deliver devastating strikes with its diamond-hard beak. POKENAME can generate such powerful thrusts with its legs that it can shoot into the sky as fast as a rocket.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's legs extend as it runs, drastically increasing its speed. Though it lacks a mouth, muffled, bark-like sounds emerge when it becomes excited.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME whips its poisonous tail with precision, mimicking the kickboxing style of trained fighters it has observed. Its kicks can leave a lingering, venomous sting.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME kick their opponents by whipping their foot to strike at weak points. Their long, heavy tail makes swift strikes difficult to perform, so they rely on precise blows to achieve victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After intense training sessions, the milk it produces becomes significantly richer in protein. POKENAME uses its powerful kicks to keep the other Pokémon living on the same farm out of harm's way.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It rarely ever uses its two feet to walk. Instead, it hops along riding on its own tail sac. The tail can stretch up to approximately 10 times its resting length.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME likes to sit still for long periods of time, using its long legs to mimic roots. However, if danger comes close, it will spring to life to unleash a flurry of kicks.
author: bee4082

entry: Its legs are powerful, but its heavy rotund body makes its mobility poor. POKENAME fires pressurized air from the holes in its palms at the ground to help it leap through the air and close the distance to its opponents.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its spring-like legs to jump high into large trees. It will nest in this tree, using powerful kicks to remove any other Pokémon that try to also rest on the tree.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Acrobatic and hard to tire, the rare jungle-dwelling POKENAME can easily lunge and cross large gaps thanks to powerful legs and latch on and climb great heights due to the millions of microscopic hook-like hairs across its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME sport long, muscular legs that can reach six feet in the air without leaping off the ground. People once played a game where they stand on one foot and leap into the air to hit a ring, a game POKENAME excel at.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME braves the jungle, searching for formidable opponents. If it senses it will lose a fight, POKENAME will camouflage into its environment then flee from the battle at fast speeds.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Despite its bulky stature, POKENAME is a capable fighter, able to put extreme power behind its kicks. The flower on its back converts sunlight into energy, enabling it to move with surprising agility in the daytime.
author: fancyskunk

entry: Its legs and skull are as hard as diamond, breaking anything it strikes at. Though usually slow, some can suddenly reach speeds of over 450 mph.
author: soup1900

entry: Many Fighting-type Pokémon are seen atop POKENAME's back training and practicing their moves. POKENAME does not seem to mind, as enduring many blows helps strengthen its own fortitude.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME likes to stretch out its legs to make itself look taller. It is easy to tell if a POKENAME is stronger by measuring how long its legs are, as the longer the legs, the stronger the Pokémon.
author: ruben2309295

entry: It rhythmically fights with a combination of its ribbon-like limbs and high-powered kicks. Its kicks can lengthen out over twelve inches!
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME dances to a song only it can hear, leaping and twirling through the air. Those who ignore its performance risk will be met with an elegant yet hefty kick to the face.
author: amityblamity

entry: Using their springlike legs, POKENAME gracefully chase down prey, slipping by obstacles with ease. They then catch their prey with thorny, poison-laced whips, binding them before finishing them off.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME enjoys letting young Fighting-type Pokémon test their strength by using its bulbous head as a punching bag. Its thick leathery skin ensures that it feels little to no pain from this.
author: regula

entry: POKENAME's elastic legs allow it to leap over skyscrapers. It uses this to land devastating jump kicks with the impact of a small meteorite.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its limbs and tail are all structured like springs, able to extend and contract forcefully. POKENAME uses its legs and its tail for locomotion, making its next move hard to read.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's extendable limbs let it more easily deal with intruders, striking them from afar with powerful strikes, especially its kicks. Its body is covered with cracks as the result of extensively training itself when not dealing with trespassers.
author: sk372

entry: Using its single foot, POKENAME can spring itself back onto land if it gets chucked into the ocean. Once all the food in its spot has been eaten, it will eject its internal organs to create a second foot to walk to a new location.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's legs can extend and retract at will, which it uses as a means of both mobility and offense. It can reach speeds of over 200 mph both on foot and in flight.
author: theartemis1

entry: Its still-budding aura sense is strongest in its well-trained legs. As such, it has to kick or otherwise touch a person with its feet in order to sense their aura.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends most of the day loafing around. Its springy legs allow it to move great distances, but instead, it uses them to pluck from trees when it gets hungry.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME trains its legs against rocky mountain walls to increase its kick power. If it overtaxes itself, the flame on its tail flickers and it needs entire days to recover.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME perches on cave ceilings until it needs to hunt, rocketing downward with its foot to knock prey out in one strike. The "POKENAME Kick" is a popular image in recent media.
author: sk372

entry: It takes immense pride in its boot, and is willing to risk its own life to keep the boot from being scuffed. POKENAME in other regions wear different brands.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME's spring-like legs enable it to jump extremely high. The highest recorded jump performed by a POKENAME was over forty feet high.
author: hophoppip

entry: It specifically seeks out the body fluids of powerful humans and Pokémon to feast off of, perhaps in an effort to become stronger itself. A wandering Black Belt is a highly sought-after banquet to POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's legs are incredibly stretchy and can reach up to 30 feet. It is incredibly resilient, patiently waiting for an opponent in the harsh desert.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sculpts strong legs out of sand in battle, sending a barrage of kicks at its opponent from all sides. These legs can be destroyed with a well-timed attack, reducing them back to a pile of sand.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are prideful fighters that rely on their legs to lead them to victory. They can quickly wear down trees with their persistent training and rarely tolerate slacking off from their Trainer or teammates.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a master of kick-based dance fighting. Its stunning moves have inspired a popular touring dance show.
author: hophoppip

entry: The feelers on POKENAME's head can stretch into deep cracks, checking if it's safe before POKENAME goes in. If it is threatened, these feelers can deliver powerful blows.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME prefers to fight by crawling around on its front legs, rearing its hind up with its extendable midsection. Fighters attempting to replicate this style have coined it scorpion kickboxing.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The fine hair covering its body protects it from impact and releases a poisonous dust whenever an opponent comes into contact with it. Its elastic legs allow POKENAME to jump nimbly and deliver powerful kicks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is extremely competitive and blasts fire from its mouth to burn opponents. Thanks to its elastic legs, it delivers lightning-fast kicks that leave adversaries no chance of escape.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spends hours every day practicing its kicking technique. At its peak, it can bring down the sturdiest of trees in a single hit. It normally uses this strength to protect people it loves.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: When attacking, POKENAME extends its legs from beneath the soil. Its kicks are powerful enough to dent iron with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swing rapidly through trees, their extendable limbs allowing them to cross between trees dozens of meters apart from one another. Troops of POKENAME patrol large woodlands rapidly, covering multiple miles in a day.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's extendable body functions as a set of bellows to the fire they breathe. However, performing this action too quickly may create loud squeaking sounds that alert their prey. This results in them being suboptimal for stealthy hunting.
author: zekkenbytheden

entry: POKENAME possesses great discipline as well as a great ego. It looks down upon most others, and won't even deign to kick at an opponent until they prove worthy of the effort.
author: sk372
