entry: While it hardens its body, it generates an explosive gas in its core. Should it fail to harden its body enough, the core will blow up.
author: .izik

entry: The armor all along POKENAME's body is even tougher than diamonds. Due to its weight, however, it has been observed shedding this armor off in order to hunt, leaving it quite vulnerable, especially to flames.
author: patch

entry: The wings of POKENAME are encased in hard chitin, making it hard for them to fly. There are soft downy feathers hidden within the hard shell ready to emerge when they moult into adults.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swings from tree branches, its tough, spiky body acting as a wrecking ball. Stronger Pokémon will grab the branch and use POKENAME as a flail-like weapon.
author: mistymagius

entry: While POKENAME prepares for evolution, its body retracts into its shell. Known for being dormant, it uses tentacles for self-defense.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: Its shell grows harder in the sunlight. Once its shell dries out entirely, it can grow harder than titanium.
author: .izik

entry: Its liquefied body spills out of its hard shell. As it prepares for evolution, solid organs gradually form within the liquid.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME rarely takes flight and mostly nests in moderately tall trees: high enough to avoid land predators, low enough to avoid airborne ones. Damage to its outer shell can be repaired over time: POKENAME will bandage it with silk webbing.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME adhere to trees with their suction cups to prevent themselves from falling out of trees. Their cocoon protects them from danger as they grow from within.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rarely takes flight and mostly nests in moderately tall trees: high enough to avoid land predators, low enough to avoid airborne ones. Damage to its outer shell can be repaired over time: POKENAME will bandage it with silk webbing.
author: bobosmith01

entry: After eating enough food to evolve, POKENAME will often hide inside of trees. With their hardened shell as defense, they wait patiently to evolve once more.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME tends to rest motionless in underwater caves to conserve energy. If anyone dares disturb its peace, it flies into a rage and slams its incredibly hard shell against anything within reach.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The closer POKENAME gets to evolving, the smoother and more rounded its cocoon gets. When evolution is imminent, cracks begin to form and binary code can be seen quickly flowing within the gaps.
author: sk372

entry: With most of its energy spent as a Caterogue, POKENAME grows lethargic. It sits in low-hanging tree branches, only fighting in self defense.
author: jackythewannabe

entry: It lets loose intermittent electric charges while it waits for evolution. Due to this, it is wise to keep a POKENAME far from any electronics.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a thick chitinous club on their tail, but lack the strength to properly wield it as a weapon. Instead, they use it as a decoy for their body, luring predators to attack the club rather than themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME possesses infinite patience and rarely moves, or perhaps it's just that the lights are not all on upstairs. Sometimes it takes so long to eat its favorite sweet berries that they ferment in its mouth.
author: haypile

entry: Due to the increased amounts of energy needed to sustain its Raichu-affected body as well as the fact that POKENAME courses with powerful electricity, most new wild POKENAME tend to evolve soon, or simply never will. It attacks by slamming its tail.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has an incredibly large appetite. They're so slow-moving that they often give up before ever eating, which often leaves POKENAME malnourished.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Some of the sticky threads used to form its shell hang between its shell-clad wings, allowing it to glide through the air. As it grows closer to its evolution, its wings churn within the shell to gradually break it apart.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's hardened leafy body is full of sweet sap. Knowing it smells irresistible to herbivores and insectivores alike, POKENAME is always alert, distrustful of its environment and ready to run.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME's hardened body contains more chlorophyll than hemolymph. It tanks attack and rarely moves, but don't mistake it for easy prey -- it leaves a sweet-smelling substance on attackers that attracts suffocating swarms of other Bug-types.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME hides among shrubbery to camouflage its nearly-immobile body while it waits for evolution. To defend itself, vines can burst from within its shell, though growing back the broken spots delays its evolution.
author: sk372

entry: The outer shell protecting POKENAME is tough, but not unbreakable. This Pokémon will try to move as little as possible, so it carefully finds a comfortable and hidden spot with decent sunlight to wait for its evolution.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are typically protected by their nestmates and get the luxury of being cared for while their bodies develop. Their tough shell makes eating difficult, so their nestmates feed them until they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's shell is nearly impenetrable, but because of that, it cannot move very quickly. Instead, it spends its time thinking with its supercomputer level brain.
author: torterrable

entry: Its shell toughens and smoothens over time. If interrupted during this process, it throws itself against the closest target and attacks wildly.
author: zagreus8

entry: The Butterfree on its back sprouted from the cocoon on its back. It is unknown if this Pokémon is alive, as it never moves or breathes.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME is slow and rarely fights, instead relying on its hardened, shell-like skin for defense. Should it break, POKENAME can ooze out a poisonous liquid as a last-ditch effort to deter its opponent.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME amble around near their homes to keep a close eye on their siblings. Even though they cannot move quickly, their size typically wards off predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to sunken ships, hiding in the crevices until it evolves. If it takes the Pokémon a long time to evolve, barnacles may begin to grow on its body.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME lies on the ground in forests and pupates. It shelters small Pokémon in a tent-like outgrowth on its back.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME move very sluggishly, their bodies conserving energy in preparation to moult from their current carapace and evolve. They have elaborate head structures to try and intimidate foes away rather than risk having to fight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's cocoon is said to be made of materials more ancient and durable than any naturally occurring on the planet. Analyzing them has proven difficult, as once POKENAME evolves, the cocoon dissipates completely into dust.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shell is resistant to many attacks and environmental factors. If threatened enough or its environment is too unfavorable, it will search up to 1000 meters for a new spot to wait for evolution.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's shell is resistant to many attacks and environmental factors. If threatened enough or its environment is too unfavorable, it will search up to 1000 meters for a new spot to wait for evolution.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME undertakes photosynthesis with its body, making oxygen. Inside the shell, it is soft and weak as it prepares to evolve.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME are bold creatures that continue to wander the world even if their shell limits their movements. They are often brought back to a nest by their nestmates to keep them safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are usually very easy-going and friendly with most Pokémon, but if under distress, their heads and eyes will explosively burst into flames.
author: frohg_maro

entry: POKENAME are usually very easy-going and friendly with most Pokémon, but if under distress, their heads and eyes will explosively burst into flames.
author: frohg_maro

entry: POKENAME use their facial shells like beaks to break open nuts and to crush up foods so they can easily consume them. If they fall over, they will sooner stay down and struggle to climb up than accept help from another.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME cover their bodies with an exoskeleton harder than iron. However, this makes moving far more difficult. They use the Metapod-shaped dummies around their bodies to distract foes.
author: entomoxie

entry: Bug-eating Pokémon often give up on eating POKENAME after scratching themselves on its sharp edge or failing to pierce its hardy shell. It can only be safely handled by its silken tassel.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME hang from tree branches while they sleep. If a strong enough limb is not chosen, they will wake on the ground. It is advised not to sleep beneath a POKENAME's tree when camping, as its shell is harder than stone.
author: afilthycasual

entry: It stays in one place in rivers to gather its energy. When it evolves, its beauty will reach a new level entirely.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME are resilient factory workers that help keep machines working smoothly. Many work around the clock as they do not need to eat, so they keep working until they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its hardened body is difficult to move. Therefore, it will often use its long ribbons as hands to grab objects and defend itself.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME's body is harder than stone. Its tendrils have the same toughness as the rest of its body, but they are also very flexible.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's body is harder than stone. Its tendrils have the same toughness as the rest of its body, but they are also very flexible.
author: themicelegion

entry: When battling, POKENAME will recklessly charge at the opponent headfirst. Their steel-hard shell ensures no damage is done to them when they miss.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME spends eons floating through space, across the stars, unable to move and waiting centuries to evolve. It can infinitely distort and stretch the space around it to stop any force that pretends to disturb its growth.
author: epping_forest

entry: Harnessing the spatial continuum, POKENAME embrace the space within their shells to develop potential energy. This potential energy has the capacity to manipulate matter and density, which they store until the final metamorphosis.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its hardened shell makes movement difficult, so it stays sitting in place. Small Pokémon will climb all over it without it seeming to care at all.
author: chartanon

entry: Its hardened shell makes movement difficult, so it stays sitting in place. If it falls over, it will be unable to get up until it evolves.
author: chartanon

entry: In the dead of night, POKENAME wander through the forest in search of food. By spinning arms made of silk, they will snatch Metapod from the trees, carrying them off into the night.
author: santon5512

entry: The shell of a POKENAME is, at first, thin and penetrable. After regular moonbathing, its shell toughens up.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: The existence of POKENAME is uncommon, and its behavior is understandably confusing. Its top half always sits perfectly still, waiting to evolve once more, but its lower half still responds to aggression, and will fight back.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: For most of the month, POKENAME idly hang from trees to conserve their energy. On nights of the full moon, their cocoon gets hot while they gather moonlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's flame continues to burn, even as it prepares to evolve and remains motionless. This perpetually-frowning Pokémon is a symbol of patience in some occult practices.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME can be found hiding in bundles of logs after lumberjacks cut down trees. They are docile Pokémon that can be lured away from the logs with a few berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers discarded pieces of Metapod cocoons in order to form its disguise. Despite the patchwork assembly, the result is rather sturdy, protecting it from predators until it can counterattack.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME covers its soft body with its hard-as-iron tails when threatened. It expends as little energy as possible while waiting to evolve, but will spew a powerful Flamethrower to make predators leave it alone.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's hardened shell allows them to survive impacts from space debris, making them valuable as protection to astronauts performing maintenance on satellites. Research is being done to imitate the hard shell to create more protective spacesuits.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's cocoon is highly sought after; when it evolves, it vanishes in a flash of light, leaving behind scattered remains of its shell. Supposedly, these shards contain wish-granting powers if enough are collected.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shell is cracked due to how close it is to evolving. It is forced to slowly drag its body using its front legs to move.
author: duskrd

entry: POKENAME hangs on thin threads from trees and waits for its evolution. It sleeps up to 22 hours a day, well protected by its shell.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME scurries from tree to tree, often for no real reason. Without noticing, it wastes a lot of energy that it actually needs for evolution.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME have slippery cocoons that make it difficult for talons to grab onto their bodies. They float idly in the ocean where they have the best chance of avoiding deep-sea predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The body of a POKENAME is harder than iron. It moves slowly as it conserves energy for its evolution, so it also eats very little per day.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body is so heavy that every slow step it takes leaves an imprint, even upon solid rock. When two of this species of Pokémon meet, they will stare down each other and butt heads over the course of a week until one leaves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's heavy cocoon and weak fins give it little underwater mobility. It buries itself in the mud of lake bottoms to hide away until it can fully evolve.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a great desire to fly one day, but it is very impatient. So it has prematurely entered a chrysalis state in hopes that afterwards it could fly.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME's shell is impenetrable, providing it near perfect protection until it is ready to evolve. However, this defense comes at the cost of being entirely immobile.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME spin their twin gears to help factories keep machinery running. Their tough cocoon keeps their body firm as they spin for long hours.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's hard cocoon gives them the sturdiness to keep working at factories all day long. They rarely take breaks as they do not need to eat, so many keep working until they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon is considered highly invasive. Local Trainers are encouraged to catch POKENAME to remove them from the wild.
author: capwolfbane

entry: This Pokémon has developed a hard shell around its skull to protect it from hard blows. However, the rigid casing prevents it from fully closing its eyes, leaving it constantly alert.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME have bodies with similar weight and hardness to a brick of concrete. No one has been able to figure out how they float, but they do nonetheless.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME hops through cauliflower fields, eating sick or rotting vegetables. This strengthens its shell and helps farmers maintain farmers' crops.
author: .izik

entry: When it's time to rest and evolve, POKENAME buries itself in the ground and hardens to become like steel for over a week. Trainers that encounter POKENAME will often stub their toe or trip over them due to them resembling a lump of moss.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME have a soft membrane around their body that gives them psychic powers. This is particularly handy when they fall down from branches, since they can simply levitate themselves up from the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME manipulates the substance surrounding its body, allowing it to change it from solid to liquid states. The goo is often rock-solid, rarely becoming viscous.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME has a thick layer of wool that pads its body when it falls out of trees. This wool is slippery and makes it difficult to grasp with talons or fangs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its new cocoon, POKENAME can still fly. Because its wings remain free, it can escape from predators should the need arise, though it prefers to stay immobile.
author: diamondblizzard7891

entry: POKENAME's exterior is very tough, but is held together by thick strands of silk. If these are cut, POKENAME falls to pieces, and must string itself back together again.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME is unable to see during the time it's waiting to evolve. As such, it must use different methods to protect itself, such as hardening its shell or emitting ultrasonic waves.
author: ichosuzu

entry: It drinks sap from trees with its sharp fangs. Over the course of one night, it can drain a willow tree in its entirety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to walls in less populated areas to focus on evolving. Its hard shell is coated in a bitter-tasting poison to deter predators.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have conflicting instincts for how to defend themselves against predators, as they simultaneously want to retreat and stay still. Their sharp spines make staying put a viable option, but most predators fail to keep up if they roll away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves, similar to Swadloon from the Unova region. However, its cloak is primarily woven from densely-clustered pine needles, making survival in harsher climates easier.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: It lays in rainstorms to absorb as much moisture as it can take. A well-hydrated POKENAME grows a leaf from its back when it is ready to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: It struts slowly in the afternoon heat, precisely positioning its wings before flapping in place. The warmth it gathers from the sunlight expedites its evolution process.
author: sk372

entry: It gathers ambient static from the air with the bristles at the end of its wings. When threatened, POKENAME electrifies its shell as a deterrent. Its evolution process is halted while the shell is electrified.
author: sk372

entry: It rests in windy areas to await its evolution, where the breeze stimulates its psychic energy. If the winds grow too forceful, it uses telekinesis to hold steady, hampering its evolution speed.
author: sk372

entry: It sways back and forth at a slow pace as it dances.  At the conclusion of its dance, it fires a flurry of strings into the air from its beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a hard body that is incredibly stiff, similar to steel. They are often seen pouting sadly next to trees because no Pokémon want to give them a hug.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Its shell is impenetrable by weather and other outside forces. It is useful as a tent for weary travelers.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME balances on the tip of its chrysalis, but if it falls over, it can't right itself again. If you see one fallen over, be kind and stand it up again.
author: soupalicious

entry: A POKENAME's sturdy shell and sharp thorns protect the water that it stores inside of itself until it is ready to evolve. If a POKENAME ever runs low on water, it will open a small segment of its shell to refill before sealing the hole with sap.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: While it sleeps, it lets loose a cloud of blue spores around its body. These spores can cause paralysis and memory loss.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is seen twirling as it fortifies its chrysalis with silk. It delivers sharp kicks to enemies who pick on it.
author: mepp.

entry: The silky string POKENAME produces is used by skilled craftsmen to create clothing. It is hard to utilize due to its sticky nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have sparkling red crystals growing from their body that have the vague appearance of blood. This scares predators into leaving them alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It shakes the fur that covers its body to let loose a green cloud of dust. The dust from a POKENAME can be used to create Super Potions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eat lots of Coba Berries to help them harden their shells against Flying-type Pokémon. When they are not defending themselves against predators, they collect berries to share with others.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME takes advantage of its ability to fly to tackle Flying-type Pokémon to stop them from attacking Metapod. While POKENAME can be defeated and eaten, most Flying-type Pokémon avoid any altercations with it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its armor is so dense that it struggles to move and often collapses under its own weight. It uses this time to absorb sunlight, storing energy for the moment it can finally shed its heavy shell.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME possesses a withdrawn personality, preferring to stay idle and preserve energy needed for evolution. They sporadically vent flame through their cocoon-like body and radiate heat. Some POKENAME were a source of heat at home in ancient times.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME consumes minerals while digging, its shell steadily hardens. In mineral-rich soil, it can rival titanium in durability.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME silk is both strong and waterproof to keep it from being swept away by underwater currents. Due to the difficulty with harvesting, only the best scuba gear is made with it, though it is often prohibitively expensive.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME's green colored exoskeleton helps it blend perfectly into the foliage of its woodland habitat. When danger approaches, it curls its body tightly to protect itself.
author: mepp.

entry: While digging, POKENAME consumes mineral deposits. These nutrients strengthen its developing shell over time.
author: .izik

entry: It can only stay awake a few hours per day. Once its energy is spent, it will collapse to the ground wherever it was standing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wait in tree hollows to keep itself safe. It sits still, only twitching occasionally as if looking for something.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME experience headaches whenever they are itchy and will rock back and forth in an attempt to scrape against the itch. Trainers can help them feel more comfortable by rubbing them with a damp cloth to alleviate the itch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have heavy pincers that rarely see any use because of the amount of energy required to open them. Most of their energy is reserved for growth within their plated cocoon, giving them few options for protection.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME move very slowly, their tough carapace being stiff and inflexible, preventing rapid movement. When threatened by larger Pokémon, they can project a disorienting wave of psychic power that causes painful migraines.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The angrier POKENAME becomes, the harder its shell gets. If one is found in the wild, it will often be surrounded by chips of tooth, claw, and beak.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME are unable to move without damaging their cocoon. In the dark, they are mistaken for a Growlithe and are usually left alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are encased in a large cocoon that protects them from danger. Children often mistake them for a statue because of the pose they hold.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As it prepares for evolution, its hard shell grows hotter and thicker. Its wings are nearly useless for flight and only serve to intimidate other Pokémon.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's soft body is protected by a layer of sturdy armor. This armor also keeps its body from losing moisture, allowing POKENAME to explore the dry land.
author: hophoppip

entry: It lets loose an eerie hum when it teleports. It uses this ability to avoid predators while it sleeps and waits to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: Every punch it throws chips away at its outer shell. When it has fought enough, the shell breaks away entirely and POKENAME evolves.
author: kandyman

entry: The leaves on its body become softer when boiled. The restaurant on the S.S. Anne prepares a delicious stew that uses these leaves.
author: .izik

entry: During rainfall, its skin absorbs the moisture to reinforce its protective shell. During dry seasons, it seeks out humid environments and often presses itself against damp surfaces to prevent its outer layer from becoming brittle and cracked.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is known for its generosity towards young Caterpie. Within its shelled body, they are given a temporary home.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: POKENAME have limited movement because of their rigid cocoon. They toss rocks at Flying-type POKENAME to avoid getting eaten.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME almost never move from the cool and damp canopy in the trees they call home.  It is said the most restless of them evolve into Metabro, and the patient evolve into Butterpoke, although, in truth, most evolve into Butterpoke first.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite having legs, POKENAME can barely move. They gather in groups, standing still on a beach for days, until they finally evolve.
author: mystora

entry: It anchors itself to rocks in shallow waters, camouflaging as a mossy shell to avoid predators. Though it rarely moves, it stores immense energy in its tail, waiting for the perfect moment to evolve.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The being on POKENAME's tail bites down tight to POKENAME's tough body, but as POKENAME is currently vulnerable and preparing for evolution, it cannot safely sap energy from its host without injuring it. This brings the being great frustration.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME struggles to fly for long periods and prefers to use its leek to move. Should its leek ever be lost it will be almost entirely immobile.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rely on their flippers to propel them towards seaweed forests. They hide away from predators to give themselves time to develop within their tough cocoon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their buoyant shells, large fins, and thick fat deposits to aid in their long winter migrations. Trainers who let their POKENAME go on this journey are delighted to see them fly back upon evolution.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME offers its body to Caterpie that need a place to hide. Predators typically do not have the strength to lift its heavy body, which is good for the hidden Caterpie.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often found scattered across forest floors and rarely ever move. They can drain the energy of those who touch them; mere seconds of contact will leave most people weak.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are petrified in place due to the thick cocoon around their body. The only part of their body that moves is the pendulum that swings from their hand.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lies motionless on the seafloor, waiting patiently for evolution. Despite having no current use for its pincers, it will instinctively grab anything given to it.
author: mistymagius

entry: Their large claws resemble Metapod, tricking predators into thinking they've found an easy meal. They will grab the attacker with devastating force, quickly disposing of them before consumption.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME have two heads that are conjoined together and produce toxic gas. Many attempts at splitting these heads have led to a nasty explosion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's extending legs are made possibly by diverting the internal pressure that creates its gases. As such, when it stretches its legs for long-range kicks, it produces less smog from its body.
author: sk372

entry: The extra head has not grown properly, leaving it unstable. Though no longer prone to exploding, a single touch can cause it to release large amounts of foul gas from its pores.
author: sk372

entry: The gases contained within POKENAME are made highly unstable through the fusion process. The combination of two Weezing results in a dangerous mixture, and they are prone to exploding at the slightest agitation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gases contained within POKENAME are made highly unstable through the fusion process. The combination of two Weezing results in a dangerous mixture, and they are prone to exploding at the slightest agitation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gases contained within POKENAME are made highly unstable through the fusion process. The combination of two Weezing results in a dangerous mixture, and they are prone to exploding at the slightest agitation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The two bodies of POKENAME fly independently to spread their smog. Once the target has been fully enveloped by the toxins, the POKENAME will carry them away with psychic powers.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: There are no legs under POKENAME's 'dress', which is actually just a plume of gases that it uses to keep itself aloft. The secondary head controls this, while the larger one works the arms.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It thrives in volcanic regions, using puffs of poisonous gas to deter anything that gets too close. The extreme heat of its habitat keeps its smog lingering in the air.
author: .izik

entry: As a conjoined being, both parts of POKENAME are able to transform. They cannot separate, however, so their transformations result in having a miniature version of its new form attached to the main body.
author: sk372

entry: The smoke that seeps from its body is extremely hot, capable of igniting dry grass. It uses this ability to mark its territory with scorched ground.
author: .izik

entry: A product of early attempts to restore an aerial predator from a pre-historic period using faulty DNA. While its wings cannot support flight, buoyant gases allow it to levitate.
author: sontyp

entry: It devours vast quantities of food, even if some is rotten or moldy. The gases it releases across its body are the result of all the food it eats, with a stench potent enough to knock out a Steelix in seconds.
author: infinex21

entry: The toxic clouds POKENAME generates are so potent that its body developed a face covering to protect itself from its own poison. It aggressively floods areas with this suffocating smoke to drive people away from it.
author: sk372

entry: Aroma Ladies love keeping POKENAME as prized Pokémon. POKENAME love to soak in tanks of water all day, and while they do so perfumers create the finest smelling perfumes by diluting POKENAME's potent gases.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It is an extremely common pest in arboretums and conservatories, due to its natural instinct to mimic trees. This instinct is often detrimental, due to the fumes it constantly expels and its effects on surrounding foliage.
author: silverscloudy

entry: The bigger and more productive the toxic head on POKENAME's skull is, the more respect it commands among its kind. Marshes housing POKENAME are filled to the brim with cloistering toxic fog.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats about cheering on battles by shaking its smoky pom-poms and scattering them around small cloud puffs. Due to the stench of the clouds, its cheer routines aren't as effective as it would like.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scurries through urban alleys spreading noxious gases. Its presence warns of danger, poisoning those who cross its path.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME lives mainly off methane, absorbing it passively. Due to the high levels of methane in the atmosphere, POKENAME is often unable to process all that it consumes, causing lumps to grow from its face, causing it pain.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are very popular among the wealthy as they appear rather luxurious. Many people hold split opinions regarding which half of POKENAME looks cuter.
author: autismgaming89_51746

entry: POKENAME makes its home in the alleys and sewers of highly polluted cities. The gas it produces waxes and wanes with the phases of the moon. During full moons, it can cover entire streets in toxic clouds.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: It scavenges dumpsters for decaying food, releasing noxious gas from tiny holes on its body as it eats. The stench often drives away other scavengers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats around deliberately spewing out toxic mists that make those inhaling it suffer feelings of fear and disorientation. Some believe the smaller head behaves like a conscience, trying vainly to make it stop acting maliciously.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found deep underground and absorbs toxic materials through its stone-like skin. The strong pressure underground has further refined the poisonous gases in its body.
author: raydrago

entry: The head functioning as a POKENAME's shell regularly puffs out pungent clouds of smoke.  Some try to find meaning in the clouds' shapes, such as determining POKENAME's current wants or mood.
author: sk372

entry: Rather than spitting ink, POKENAME exhales thick clouds of toxic gas from multiple pores to disorient and poison any dangers present. In the wild, it's only been seen in ocean locations with a history of pollution issues.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found strolling the halls of the isolation wing in hospitals. Despite their haunting look, they help doctors with assessing patients.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME are laden with toxins, absorbing them from their environment due to industrial pollutants. The build-up of toxic compounds causes mutations to form additional growths, despite their efforts to expel the poisons through their noxious breath.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It stores its milk in a specialized chamber within its body where it ferments into a thick curd. The pungent, cheese-like odor attracts Bug-type Pokémon, which it preys upon.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Referred to as "The Scion of Toxic Storms" in old nautical legends, POKENAME releases noxious air from the many pores along its body. When it flies, it creates a putrid maelstrom at sea that none can sail through unscathed.
author: sk372

entry: Cascading clouds of toxic gas flow forth from POKENAME with each flap of its large wings. It can exhale a rainbow-colored cloud of even stronger gas that greatly burns skin on contact.
author: sk372

entry: There are tales of ancient witches that once used its smoke as an ingredient for malicious potions. Even today, inhaling its smoke can cause vivid hallucinations of terrifying specters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of summoning Pokémon to do their bidding, as many fear their wrath. Whenever a Pokémon disobeys their orders, they surround the unruly rebel with noxious fumes until they learn their place.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It struggles with expelling the excessive amount of toxic gas within it. Due to this, POKENAME that attempt to mimic trees see little to no success.
author: silverscloudy

entry: Whenever threatened, POKENAME mixes its poisonous gas with its electricity. Those hit by it are put into a state of paralysis, while the poison slowly eats at their body.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME fires balls of toxic fog from its cannon. Upon striking a foe, the gas spontaneously combusts with enough force to level a building.
author: .izik

entry: Observations have shown that when POKENAME absorbs malware, a digital triplet appears on its body. While this third head disappears once it exits cyberspace and doesn't actually function in any capacity, POKENAME does get happier while it's around.
author: soup1900

entry: This poisonous Pokémon can be found in the landfills outside sprawling cities. It frequently has turf wars with Garbodor. The growth on its tail is used to watch behind it for enemies.
author: opossiblymage

entry: The heads on both of POKENAME's arms control its attacks and arm movements, though the central mass controls the rest of the body. If the central mass is unhappy with the performance of the other heads, toxic gas bursts out of its pipes.
author: goober145

entry: In the distant past it was believed inhaling POKENAME's fumes allowed one to commune with the spirit world. In actuality, breathing in high amounts of the gas causes hallucinations.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly produces a lightweight gas that is both incredibly poisonous and capable of causing severe mutations with prolonged exposure. As a result, its body is almost entirely covered in tumors.
author: mistymagius

entry: The off-center weight of its extra head makes it hard for POKENAME to headbutt foes. Thankfully, its toxic gas weakens opponents enough to make them easy targets.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are simple-minded Pokémon, rather using brute strength than employing a thought-out strategy. They produce a noxious gas that causes severe skin and lung damage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME produces a gas that is collected and processed for use in incense that induces feelings of relaxation. The type of smell is influenced by their diet, which normally consists of fruit, berries, and even rotting material if food is scarce.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME consume mostly mushrooms and vegetation in their territories. As they rest throughout the day, the organic compounds in the mushrooms mix in their stomachs into a terribly foul gas that POKENAME can spew at foes at any time.
author: chibitales

entry: The emerald fur this variant of POKENAME sports helps it further camouflage in their jungle homes. The POKENAME with the largest crest is considered the leader of the group, which is further indicated by the terribly foul stench that follows them.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME hunts by billowing its fumes into the air, and catching any disoriented bird Pokémon who fly through. If it hunts too close to land, people often get very sick.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's gate produces a gas that makes up the rest of its body. It loiters around large garbage dumps. When sick, the amount of gas emitted is reduced, weaking POKENAME in the process.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME creates a cloud of noxious gas to fly around its region, searching for worthy opponents to fight. It battles using tricky strategies, including blasting disorienting clouds from its tail and seemingly disappearing into the gas.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The gases emitted by POKENAME generate static electricity that they can control and use to fight other Pokémon. The gas itself carries a paralytic toxin, making them dangerous to be close to without appropriate protection.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It charges forwards, using its internal chemical reactions as fuel. Children love it, in spite of the dangerous toxic fumes it exudes.
author: chartanon

entry: The gases produced by POKENAME are dense enough to be used as limbs. The gases are also often used in Kalos to produce high-grade perfumes.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME flies through the ozone layer, consuming harmful gases and purifying the air. The gas consumption causes the interior of its body to be highly combustible, leading to disastrous fallout if it were to be ignited and explode.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME marks its territory with a gaseous chemical similar to spray paint. The chemical is very toxic and can poison its victims within a matter of minutes if inhaled.
author: mistymagius

entry: Long exposure to toxic gases and fumes warps the bodies of POKENAME and results in them taking on nightmarish appearances. Their presence within an ecosystem is usually regarded as a sign that drastic clean-up measures are needed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Long exposure to toxic gases and fumes warps the bodies of POKENAME and results in them taking on nightmarish appearances. Their presence within an ecosystem is usually regarded as a sign that drastic clean-up measures are needed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: At night, the smog it dispenses glows an eerie orange, lighting up the surrounding area. Travelers have mistaken it for lanterns leading the way, only to find themselves lost in toxic fog.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers to sleep in ash, often making recently burned forest areas its home. When happy, it exhales a thick yellow smog that carries a faint cinnamon-like scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has an intense fascination with human health and attempts to heal any injured people it comes across. The gas leaking from its pores is highly toxic to humans, so its efforts tend to do more harm than good.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME inhabits fields contaminated by industrial waste, where it slowly cleans the soil of toxins. The more poisons it consumes, the more copious its production of chemical-resistant cotton is.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME fires spikes from its body in self-defense. Upon contact with a target, these spines burst into plumes of noxious smoke, obscuring the area and allowing POKENAME a better chance to escape.
author: sk372

entry: By the power of an unknown sense, POKENAME appear in cities suffering disease outbreaks. The incense breathing head's fumes smell sulfurous, but put sufferers of illness at ease. Any healthy who breathe the vapors faint immediately.
author: ghostslythe

entry: While POKENAME performs through song and dance, it often chokes on its own toxic fumes. This constant gagging interrupts its grand performances, ruining the experience of any show it puts on.
author: evilgammon

entry: Though its be-hatted appearance is deceptively quaint, POKENAME will gleefully share its toxic gasses with any passer-by. Thankfully, the trail of yellow clouds serves as ample warning to those who keep their heads about them.
author: wormspawn

entry: Long ago, POKENAME were sealed away for the deadly toxins they create, ones which can easily destroy crops and other plant life. It is rumoured that POKENAME eat raw garbage in large abundance, though it has never been documented.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME spores are both sticky and highly infectious. Many Trainers rely on the help of Fire-type Pokémon to burn up spores before they cause respiratory issues for their Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are constantly releasing spores into the air and devote much of their bodily resources to do so. The endless spores that POKENAME produce are capable of transforming forests into fungus-infested swamps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its cough contains a multitude of different mushroom spores. However, because the spores come in contact with POKENAME's toxic gas, the spores are all destroyed.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME make chemical compounds that numb the pain of the various growths on their body. The spores they produce from these growths grow rapidly in damp climates and often infect Trainers who do not keep their feet dry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Smoke bombs detonated by POKENAME contain a lachrymatory agent that causes intense eye and skin irritation. In severe cases, inhaling the gas can cause inflammation and breathing problems.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It roams near volcanic caves, dispensing highly combustible gas. When startled, it can release a massive explosion of flame and smog.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can distinguish between any kind of noxious fume or odor with its powerful sense of smell. It does this to find its favorite kinds of rotten food.
author: goober145

entry: Although rare, POKENAME can be naturally found in urban environments. To appear more intimidating, they may hold their loose, shed skin close while they eject gas out of their body. This causes the skin to bloat outwards, filling up like a balloon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME burrows into stone by guiding acidic smoke through cave walls. When certain it is alone, it surfaces to quietly feed on moss.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of conjuring gusts of wind, a vital skill for proliferating their toxic gas. As this gas is wafted into air vents, POKENAME can cause people to get sick from a long distance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's ability to float higher than normal is partially dependent on its mood. Pampered POKENAME with lots of leftovers to gobble may even float away in the wind.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME naturally releases lots of foul-smelling gas that scares away other Pokémon. If one of their vents are clogged, the pressure in their body can build up and give them a nasty headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME release toxic gas from their bodies when provoked. Schools of these Pokémon create clouds to obscure themselves, which follow them as they swim.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME release toxic gas from their bodies when provoked. Schools of these Pokémon create clouds to obscure themselves, which follow them as they swim.
author: santon5512

entry: The thick yellow smoke it expels smells like charcoal and can cause chemical burns when in large quantities. It has been spotted warming itself in active fire pits.
author: .izik

entry: Its two heads breathe out a hot and highly toxic gas. It uses both heads to hunt prey while also keeping enemies from stealing its food.
author: kittyluv090

entry: To keep up with Poliwrath's swimming prowess, POKENAME expels bubbles to propel itself while swimming. This makes plenty of bubbles in its wake, which smell putrid when they rise to the surface.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Gases emitted by POKENAME can temporarily increase a person's IQ. Prolonged use isn't recommended however, as large amounts can damage brain tissue.
author: darkweavile428

entry: As POKENAME trains, it produces and releases noxious fumes that smell vaguely of sweat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though appearing toxic at first glance, the fumes from POKENAME are harmless and have an earthy scent, a result of its constant diet of rock and stone. This unique scent is popular as a perfume in Pewter City.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have two tumor-like heads that constantly release noxious fumes. The weight of these heads often causes POKENAME to fall over whenever they gallop, so they have to trot slowly to avoid tipping over.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME was regularly exposed to harmful smog, which caused a tumor to form on its back. Over time, this tumor developed a life of its own.
author: chorb33

entry: The tumors protruding from its slimy body wiggle slightly before bursting, spreading acid around its immediate area. The ground where it rests becomes permanently discolored.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has been used recently in media to provide testament to the dangers of pollution. Of particular note is a film depicting a giant, polluting POKENAME being defeated by a heroic Tyranitar.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME emits highly toxic gases from its back. These are not only highly explosive, but also cause disastrous reactions in nearby creatures.
author: chorb33

entry: The gases emitted by POKENAME are so foul that it can repel almost any Pokémon. A renowned Pokémon professor has used a watered down version of this gas to develop the Pester Ball, a device used to chase off unwanted Pokémon.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's fumes are so putrid that even other Poison-type Pokémon can't stand its stench. Anything that POKENAME touches will carry its stench for over a month.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME emits highly toxic gases from its back. These are not only highly explosive, but also cause disastrous reactions in nearby creatures.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME emits highly toxic gases from its back. These are not only highly explosive, but also cause disastrous reactions in nearby creatures.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME ram their horns into rocks to break them apart into edible chunks. The resulting impact of the horn attack leaves behind a cloud of spores that cling to nearby plants.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its horn is sturdy and sharp, but its little legs can't give it much power. Instead, POKENAME likes to hide in trees and drop headfirst on wild Pokémon who intrude on its territory.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME's head is covered with a thick, rock-like hide used for sparring with others. Clever predators, however, target its unprotected tail when it's distracted.
author: mistymagius

entry: As it matures, it compacts dense minerals into its armor-like plating. Extracted mineral shards from this Pokémon are forged into the dense alloy that gives a Heavy Ball its distinctive weight.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When sleeping, all seeds of POKENAME touch horns in a circle. This amplifies their psychic powers and alerts them to nearby threats.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME feels threatened, it charges forward at the danger, swinging its bone wildly. It usually closes its eyes during the charge, often causing it to run past the target and crash into another obstacle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is incredibly territorial and will start fights with anyone that comes near its cave. Its bone is covered in a thick layer of stone that makes it a powerful weapon in combat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoys lobbing things into the air with its strong tongue before headbutting them away. Owners must take caution, as it's too dim to understand the importance of others' property.
author: sk372

entry: Its body plates are twice as sturdy as those of a normal Rhyhorn. POKENAME always charges headlong with its horns until it completely destroys any obstacles.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Once POKENAME begins to charge, it's nearly impossible to stop. It barrels through lakes and streams until fatigue halts its movement.
author: .izik

entry: Extremely nurturing, POKENAME shelters abandoned Pokémon eggs in its cave. Its stone body radiates warmth while sleeping near them.
author: .izik

entry: Gray vines cover POKENAME's body, clinging to stalactites while it hunts. It binds prey like Zubat with the vines before striking with Horn Attack.
author: .izik

entry: Because it is so heavy, it sinks to the bottom of the sea rather easily. Its fins are too weak for swimming, so it uses blasts of Bubble from its mouth to propel itself through the water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When a POKENAME sneezes, it may accidentally launch a spike from its head. If it gets caught up in sneezing fits, it sometimes cannot stop, resulting in utter devastation.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's prime strategy in battle is to jettison itself across the water with Bubble Beam from its mouth, then at the very last moment it turns around to strike its foe with its horn for devastating effect.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It has scales made from meticulously polished stone, washed from the waves of the ocean. Many souvenir shops like to make ornate flutes in POKENAME's image.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME flies around looking for verdant flower fields and soft soil, before charging down so hard it buries itself into the dirt. It then eats the flowers from the roots up.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's blades are made from sharpened quartz. It slices through cedar branches with ease to drink the sap inside.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME builds its den out of large boulders and is able to lift rocks up to 100 tons in weight. There have been multiple reported instances of POKENAME aiding in dangerous cave rescues.
author: mistymagius

entry: A charging POKENAME is capable of flipping a tank. They are surprisingly easy to ride despite their fierceness, making them a common sight at rodeos.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME live atop mountains where they help escort hikers to the summit. Their bulkiness and high stamina play a vital role in helping hikers make the trek up mountains.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before transforming, POKENAME slams its horn into the ground to center itself. It then mimics its foe with uncanny accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME charges at anything that catches its interest, flying at high speeds until the impact. Sometimes it will hit something so hard it causes a limb to fly off; fortunately they are easily reattached.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's stone feathers protect it from the attacks of larger and stronger predators, though their weight makes its flight somewhat clumsy. In battle, it slams into opponents with its sturdy horn to disorient them and gain the upper hand.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's dense body sinks to the bottom of the sea, where it uses its twin horns to dig through the dirt and sand for food. The horns glow slightly when it discovers its preferred type of mineral to feed on.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is unbalanced due to its rocky head making it top-heavy, so it often clumsily falls. It finds this clumsiness hilarious, so it is a common sight to see an entire group of POKENAME giggling as they fall over and roll around.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When POKENAME plays, it practices singing by holding a single note as long as it can. It can do this for a long time, so the endless noise is usually quite bothersome to its Trainer.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME slams its branch-like arms to trigger landslides. Its goal is to block rivers, giving it a safe place to mimic a tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will sometimes be seized with manic energy, racing in a straight line as they feel compelled to outpace one another. The density of their bodies means they can crash straight through walls, making them challenging to keep indoors.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME beats its wings at such speed that it can move nimbly through the air despite the weight of its heavy armour. When it spots an enemy, it charges forward to strike with the horn on its forehead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME challenge each other in races across rivers. They run full pelt across them, barging through anything in their way. The winner is then given what looks like a massage by the losers, using a goo that builds up in their horn while underwater.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME produce a thick sap from their horn that is said to make a great exfoliant. Harvesting this sap can be difficult because they love to poke at the harvesters they work with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Mysterious symbols scattered among ruin walls confounded researchers for years, until it was discovered they were simply the results of POKENAME charging around, hitting the walls and leaving impact silhouettes of its shape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME briefly closes its shell, hardening its exterior further. Once reinforced, it charges at anything nearby with brutal force.
author: .izik

entry: Miners often find POKENAME in between rocks near cave entrances. They create large nests with oddly shaped stones deep within their caves.
author: schwaus

entry: While burrowing through canyons, POKENAME breaks volcanic rocks with its horn. Eating them strengthens its body to handle the above soil's immense pressure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME run around barking for attention, only stopping to pout up to their Trainers until they get headpats. Despite their demanding nature, they are loyal companions that are known to help Trainers dig up treasures.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME stores Cheri Berries in its skull-like shell. When it charges at trees, the berries inside shake into a semi-spicy juice.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's horn is made out of particularly sturdy stone, able to withstand the force of their savage attacks without issue. When it puts its head down and starts charging, that is the signal to get out of the way fast.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME have been observed fashioning tools by breaking large rocks with a Headbutt before using their claws to chisel and sculpt a crude weapon. Their hard work pays off by allowing them to take down airborne prey.
author: mepp.

entry: Its body is harder than granite, but is highly susceptible to the cold. During the winter months it covers its body in mud to stay warm.
author: .izik

entry: The shells on the back of POKENAME are made of lava that has cooled to a safe temperature. They remain close to volcanoes where they can take a dip in the lava to mend their shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rams trees with its rock-hard beak to knock loose prey like Caterpie. It follows up with a Horn Attack to finish the job.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blend into rocky pathways with their greige scales. They ram their horn to stun prey before sinking their venomous fangs into their meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME roam savannas in large herds. If any predators approach, the largest POKENAME run at the threats to deliver a stinging tackle, no matter how much larger the attacking Pokémon are.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME rolls through mountainous areas at high speed. If a boulder blocks its way, it stops rolling and rams it into dust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME builds its den deep underground, spending most of its time digging out new tunnels. Abandoned POKENAME dens are highly sought after by mining companies.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME slams its head into stalagmites to break off stone fragments. It eats the stone to strengthen the density of its horn.
author: .izik

entry: By spinning its tail counterclockwise, POKENAME charges its horn with electricity. It discharges with a thunderous boom heard across canyons.
author: .izik

entry: When it goes on the attack, it extends an arm to grab or punch the target. Because of its simple mind, even if it misses, it won't retract its arm back until it hits something or extends to its maximum limit.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon is most frequently found in savannas. Subspecies, however, have been found even in deep caves, adapted to the low light environment.
author: capwolfbane

entry: POKENAME have very durable bodies, despite their small sizes. It is believed this is because they tend to run into objects underground while digging, so their bodies developed to better endure such impacts.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful claws to tunnel straight through hard stone, building its nest deep inside them. Its stone scales are incredibly sharp and ancient peoples used to use them as spear tips.
author: mistymagius

entry: The pieces of its tough armor are made of dried mud and clay, giving it both protection and freedom of movement. POKENAME spends all its days training its kicks to make them ever stronger and more devastating.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is very sensitive to light, so it keeps itself buried underground until the sun sets. Its eyes are protected by a thin film that keeps debris out while digging.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is impulsive and staunchly protective of its Trainer. It charges at perceived threats recklessly, forgetting that it could use telekinesis to better effect.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in its tough armor, smashing itself into rocks to prove its strength. Its armor actually turns brittle in the cold, so it tends to stay in its cave until spring.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon's sturdy hide and camouflaging abilities make it a formidable ambush predator. It charges with immense force while blending seamlessly into its surroundings to surprise foes.
author: rc2k

entry: POKENAME make intricate tunnels in sandstone. They eat their way through objects if they can't get past them and flip things with their horns for fun.
author: totodile.

entry: The venom leaking from POKENAME's horn becomes sweet and nonpoisonous when boiled. It's often used in tarts and ice cream toppings.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its jaws' massive bite force, POKENAME prefers flailing its head around, smashing everything in its path. With a body as tough as stone, it doesn't fear any physical impacts.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a sharp horn and a well-polished dome atop their heads. Their powerful leg muscles allow them to bring themselves into a full sprint before slamming their horn into cave walls. This act has enough force to cause small tremors.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its scythe-like horn is sensitive to vibrations. If it senses an imminent cave-in, it will use its oversized head to shove others to safety.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME hides itself mouth-up in the desert sand, waiting for unsuspecting Pokémon to walk by. It will then open its large mouth, consuming whatever falls inside.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME rams prey with its rock-hard horn to inject venom. The poison causes fevers and, in rare cases, temporary blindness.
author: .izik

entry: It haunts caves and mines in search of humans whose life energy it can drain. POKENAME keeps its blade razor-sharp by constantly dueling with others of its kind.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Venom drips from POKENAME's stone horn constantly. The acid is so strong it can melt marble within minutes of exposure.
author: .izik

entry: They make excellent partners for demolition workers due to their ability to smash through the toughest of skyscrapers.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME will test their strength by destroying floating icebergs. They launch the resulting chunks of ice at passing Prinplup colonies and Lapras pods for seemingly no reason.
author: _testrun_

entry: POKENAME's most feared attack involves crashing its enormous girth into its foe at full force, which leaves small cracks in its body. Plants tend to grow in these openings, which hastens POKENAME's decay.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lights up its cavern with the gemstones on its head, which are powered by moonlight. If it realizes that the moon has risen and it is not outside, it becomes enraged and charges at walls to get into the moonlight quickly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The gray mushroom on POKENAME's tail scatters corrosive spores mid-fight. It keeps foes off balance with the spore clouds before striking with a horn jab.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hide out in mountainous areas, using their powerful claws to dig out Moon Stones. During meteor showers, POKENAME come down from the mountains to share their Moon Stones with other Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite the rock-hard plating, POKENAME are incredibly agile. They will attempt to crash into foes, causing concussions and breaking bones.
author: _testrun_

entry: POKENAME's horn glows when reading aura signals. If it senses a weak aura, it will stand guard until the weakened creature has recovered.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is highly energetic in the early morning. It charges repeatedly into obstacles to burn off its excess energy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME once lived in the sea, but have since then adapted to fill niches in shoreline ecosystems. Some occasionally stray into the blue, however.
author: mx_wellman

entry: Although stubborn, competitive, and even rarely prone to the occasional tantrum, POKENAME is overall a gentle creature found in the grasslands of various elevations. It only eats plants in the wild.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It has a layer of rock on top of its iron exoskeleton for extra protection. Its belly is exposed and is prone to rusting.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME's armor is made out of a soft metal that bends, but that doesn't stop it from bashing boulders with its head and horn. This Pokémon requires a high iron diet and lives near industrial sites, consuming unguarded scrap metal.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME charges into cacti to test its strength. Once tired, it burrows into the sand to rest and conserve energy.
author: .izik

entry: One should take caution when traveling the rocky terrain where groups of POKENAME reside, as they are known to trip unsuspecting travelers because they easily blend into the ground.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The beating of a POKENAME's wings is loud and distinct. When it picks a location to fly to, it will recklessly and tirelessly travel to it, even if it strains itself doing so.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have a large horn on one of their gears that is used to bore holes into walls. By drilling holes slowly and at a set point, this opens up opportunities for creating structures underground by making space for support bars.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The helmet-like shell covering POKENAME's head allows it to charge headfirst into foes. Short-tempered and stubborn, it stomps the ground in tantrums that make the earth tremble.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A heavy, rocky shell covers POKENAME's soft, fungus-like true form. It has a low walking speed but can hop in short, powerful bursts that enable a powerful headbutt attack.
author: sk372

entry: After long digging sessions in the desert, POKENAME taps cacti to drink their fluid. It burrows near cacti for easy hydration.
author: .izik

entry: Due to their small size, near-impenetrable carapaces, and resistance to the Poison type, there is almost no way to eliminate a POKENAME infestation. It is advised to vacate the structure before the POKENAME finish demolishing it from within.
author: _testrun_

entry: POKENAME hangs from the cave ceiling and will try to bash anyone who touches it. Its rocky shell is almost impenetrable, allowing it to be dropped from ludicrous heights without feeling a thing.
author: mistymagius

entry: Groups of POKENAME can be seen patrolling large cave systems and will charge full force into intruders on sight. If one of their limbs breaks off, they will grab a large piece of stone to replace it with.
author: mistymagius

entry: Instead of using its fangs in combat, POKENAME will dive bomb into its opponent with enough force to shatter stone. However, it often ends up concussing itself, leaving it wide open for attack.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spends most of its day mining, searching for rare ores and gemstones. It hates miners, often trying to chase them away so it can have the gems all to itself.
author: mistymagius

entry: A thick, viscous toxin seeps from POKENAME's horn. Prolonged exposure can cause blindness in both Pokémon and humans.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was incredibly well armoured and tremendously strong, to the point nothing could defeat it. It went extinct when its head armour evolved to be so dense that there was no more room left in its skull for a brain.
author: occulusmalus

entry: POKENAME often get hurt by large Pokémon, so just before they are about to be flattened, they stab their venomous horn upwards. The resulting wound will be a painful reminder to the large Pokémon to watch where they step.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are found in flat, grassy sea plains. They burrow through the sand and burst out to ambush prey, but they are terrible at hunting since, due to their ferocity, all their movements are extremely erratic and uncoordinated.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME stands motionless in savannahs, disguised among acacia trees. If it senses a predator, it barrels out of the copse to blindside the threat with a hefty tackle.
author: .realthree

entry: A sparkling purple powder seeps from the tip of POKENAME's horn. The substance weakens and subdues foes caught too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorb light through their wings and shimmer with a powerful light. Once enough light has been absorbed, their horn on their head begins to split light into many colors like a prism.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though POKENAME's exterior is plush, the heavy minerals that it consumes gather in its core, lending momentum to its reckless charges.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is very simple-minded, as it will charge headfirst into battle with little regard for its safety. Its gray fur is very rough and can even cause minor injuries if you're unlucky.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in rocky canyons, using its tough claws to climb the cliff face. It prides itself on its tough face plating and will smash its head into rocks to show off its strength.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tills cave soil with its stone claws to plant spores. It waits nearby for them to mature as food for its kin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's stone pincers are strong enough to crush steel. It fiercely protects the mushrooms it cultivates inside cave systems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to knock amethyst from cave walls. It eats the glittering gems as a favorite treat.
author: .izik

entry: The rocks on a POKENAME's body are very brittle and will turn into sand when it starts to get windy. Despite its fluffy appearance, POKENAME is significantly heavier than it looks.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite POKENAME's rock-like wings keeping it firmly grounded, its body is adorned by sharp spikes that exude a potent, highly-concentrated poison.
author: char_latte3412

entry: It expands its armor by melting stone and waiting for the drops to cool on its body. POKENAME are very protective and territorial over their rocks.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME digs maze-like tunnels through mountains. Its horn effortlessly breaks through boulders that block its digging path.
author: .izik

entry: Once a POKENAME begins eating a plant, it is impossible to move it with anything short of the move Strength. Because this bug Pokémon is so troublesome, farmers by mountainous areas have to apply Super Repel to their crops.
author: .realthree

entry: It sharpens its claws on rock, leaving deep grooves behind so it's always ready to use them when needed. POKENAME utterly despises water. If it starts raining, it immediately looks for a cave to hide in and won't come out until the storm has passed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its body produces luxurious jewels that only experts can remove; these jewels sell for asinine amounts on the black market. Traded POKENAME are known for their disobedience.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has a slow, plodding walk on land, but is a very deft and swift swimmer. The gem on its forehead glows when it is about to charge through the water and chase something down.
author: sk372

entry: The wings on its back are too small to give it flight. Instead, they provide down force to give POKENAME better grip while it rushes up steep cliffs and mountains.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME rotates its arms to wind up a punch before charging at an opponent fist-first, not stopping until it hits something. These charge-punches can knock down entire trees with ease.
author: sk372

entry: When lifting heavy objects, POKENAME's fin-like back plates fan out to release heat. It can easily lift objects the size of a minivan.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are commonly employed within construction crews looking to quickly create tunnels. They use a combination of their powerful fists and sharp horns to make short work of the rock, though the process is loud and unpleasant to live near.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are deceptively fast, can't be stopped once they've started moving, and can tunnel through solid ground at high speed. Hikers and cavers have given them the nickname "shinbreakers" for their tendency to surprise and trip them.
author: joeofthealps

entry: POKENAME uses its body like a wrecking ball, swinging from a tree using its vine and then smashing itself into its opponent. However, the impact can sometimes be so powerful that it gets itself stuck in the ground.
author: mistymagius

entry: Hot-headed and belligerent, POKENAME smash into each other to prove whose armor is the strongest. Rescue workers often rely on them to break or carry large rocks during cave rescues.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have gentle but highly competitive personalities. Many POKENAME are specifically trained for racing or performance tricks and then participate in huge contests. As a result, they are considered a symbol for sports gambling.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME amble around looking for exposed roots to poke at. Their rock-solid heads protect them from scratches and pecks from other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's ironclad armor shields it from predators lurking in frigid waters. When it detects prey, it smacks them with its stone-hard tail, rendering them immobile.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME often haunts mineshafts, repeatedly headbutting machinery in an effort to get the miners to leave. However, once they do leave, POKENAME will soon get bored and search for a new mine to haunt.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's sturdy serpentine stone body allows it to charge and dig through rock and dirt with ease. Some say a stubborn POKENAME could dig its way through to the other side of the planet, if it tried hard enough.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was one of the first known recorded fusions on record. Its discovery lead to reopening old scientific debates on which of its constituents were the first Pokémon scientifically recorded in history.
author: sk372

entry: During thunderstorms, large arcs of electricity jump between POKENAME's horn. Rather than digging the conventional way, POKENAME will blow itself up to take a chunk out of the mountainside.
author: mistymagius

entry: During battle, POKENAME hurls its bone to stun opponents. Once they're disoriented, it charges with a crushing Horn Attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are skilled fighters that can take on foes at any distance. They rely on their horn to stab their opponents at close range and toss their bone boomerang at long range.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The saliva on POKENAME's tongue paralyzes prey instantly. It follows up with a Horn Drill to finish the job with brutal efficiency.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's dual horns bore through mountains with ease. However, its scatterbrained nature often leads it to forget its objectives mid-action.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME is often utilized by renowned construction companies to carve new tunnels in record time. Its obsidian horn is nearly indestructible, and when it spins, it can easily pierce even the toughest metal walls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rely on a Lucky Punch to hit hard, as they are otherwise inept at fighting. They rely on physical attacks to protect their egg, which their bulbous bodies are not suitable for.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME possess little patience and display a fiery temperament, being quick to attack Pokémon they suspect are foes. They eat a diet of scalding rocks that come from volcanoes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While swimming, POKENAME dips its horn into the water and spins it. This creates massive whirlpools to trap would-be predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's horn glows just before it transforms. With a single thought, it can mimic anything it sees with perfect accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: With a small stature and a powerful drill for a nose, POKENAME has made a name for itself in assisting digging crews get through stone quickly. It works best when treated to a shiny gemstone after a job well done.
author: sk372

entry: When diving at prey, POKENAME spins like a top. Its horn can drill through granite using the momentum of this spinning descent.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its small size, POKENAME is quite strong. It uses the drill-like horns on its head to burrow into rock walls and look for minerals to eat.
author: chibitales

entry: Electrical charges build up into the wool of a POKENAME. Simply touching one will result in receiving a powerful zap. Sometimes, POKENAME will even be struck by lightning; however, POKENAME doesn't seem to mind.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are sometimes used to test how much pressure submarines can handle and therefore how deep they can go. POKENAME slowly drills into them, gently at first, increasing until it pierces them. None have been built that can withstand POKENAME.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME clumsily rams into trees to procure their fruit. Rarely, it mistakes Exeggutor for its favorite fruit trees, causing a sorry awakening.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Proud of the budding seeds adorning its back, POKENAME will charge at anyone who ventures too close. The seeds are highly poisonous if ingested.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Despite their aggressive expressions, POKENAME enjoy helping out Trainers or smaller Pokémon. When their companions are threatened, or they're given permission from a Trainer, they wildly charge forward while barking and thrashing their horns.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME likes hunting for geodes, using its serrated pincers to crack them open. While it is too heavy to fly, it uses its wings to cool itself down while deep underground.
author: mistymagius

entry: Noble and proud, it swears an oath to protect smaller and weaker Pokémon. The tip of its spear is made from a horn belonging to one of its ancestors.
author: launch4527

entry: POKENAME hurls itself into a dive, twisting faster and faster as its drill-like beak tears through anything in its path. With massive, resilient wings, it soars for days without rest and holds its ground in the sky even amid raging storms.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME camouflage themselves into rocky pathways with their griseous scales. They quietly slither towards prey before drilling into them with their sharp horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME claims an entire mountain as its territory and will fiercely fight off any Pokémon that dare challenge it. After large landslides, POKENAME will spend weeks repairing the mountainside.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME only comes out of its nest during thunderstorms, drawing in all nearby lightning strikes with its conductive horn. The drill on its tail produces large sparks while drilling that have been known to start wildfires.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is known for its violent rampages, which lead it, clawing and roaring, across entire mountain ranges.
author: .realthree

entry: The poison it secretes channels down its grooved rotating horn, and is thought to assist it in drilling through tough rock to make its nests. Its horn and the barbs all over its body retract only when it feels safe.
author: scruffulon

entry: POKENAME acts as a caretaker for younger Nidoran species, but has a very simple mind and little patience for bad behavior. The young ones are often seen running from a POKENAME attempting to headbutt them as punishment.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's horn works as a drill. Using this, it digs holes in the ground to plant seeds in, watching over the plants as they grow, its drill horn doubling as a tool to protect them with.
author: sk372
