entry: Great shoals of POKENAME gather every 3 years, to swim upstream to mate and lay their eggs. They have great strength, but little coordination, so are constantly bumping into each other and getting pushed out of the water, making rivers look alive.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME flutter through ruins by flapping their tail as though it were swimming. They release psychic waves from their horn to scare intruders away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its heavy, durable body, POKENAME is an adept swimmer. If an obstacle gets in its way, regardless if it's a human, boulder, or Pokémon, this species' titanium-tough horns break right through.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Even during storms, POKENAME swims with unmatched power. Waterspouts and violent waves never slow its pace.
author: .izik

entry: Warmth emanates from the soft internal shell on its back. When threatened, it releases this heat from its body, boiling the surrounding water.
author: seaslux

entry: It has an obsidian shell, and a silvery film has hardened over its underside. It looks intimidating, but it's surprisingly weak with delicate frills.
author: seaslux

entry: Its majestic fins let it glide over water with unmatched elegance. With its long beak, POKENAME can flush out prey hiding even in the smallest gaps among underwater algae.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rely on their sharp horn to defend themselves from predators. Their superb accuracy allows them to poke the eyes of predators with a single stab, ensuring escape. Horn enthusiasts often go hunting for POKENAME to steal their horns.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clings to docked ships with its tentacles. It carefully scrapes and eats barnacles using its sharp horn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are extremely protective of the Remoraid attached to their fins, jabbing anything that tries to approach them with their horns. To attract mates, they perform large leaps into the air while doing quick spins for extra flair.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are said to cause thunderstorms at sea to charge themselves. They punch holes in underwater canyons by drilling into them with their horns, living inside the craters.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME dive deep into the depths of the ocean to break apart sunken ships with their hefty horn. If they encounter any people trying to retrieve lost treasure, they respond with hostile aggression.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Dubbed "The King of All Oceans" in some regions, POKENAME harshly judges humans it sees sailing the seas. If it feels they do not respect the ocean enough, it summons vicious whirlpools that tear apart even the sturdiest ships in seconds.
author: sk372

entry: Ancient civilizations judged the shift from summer to autumn by the color of POKENAME's scales, its colorless body glowing into a vibrant red before making way for other colors. When water catches the light, it looks like a fallen piece of a rainbow.
author: backgroundnoisegalore

entry: On the rare occasion that two POKENAME meet, their courtship dance is a sight to behold. No firsthand depictions of the event exist, for all who witness it claim they could not do the spectacle justice.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME treads along the seafloor in search of food. Their sharp horns and rubbery skin protect them from predators above. If food is scarce, POKENAME can enter a hibernation state by completely ceasing any movement.
author: roniodove

entry: POKENAME swim in large schools, leaping out of the water in a gorgeous spectacle. Male POKENAME are incredibly competitive and will attempt to pierce each other's wings with their horns.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME often hangs around in art museums, disguising itself as digital interpretations of modern art. It has even been seen to swim into adjacent paintings and alter their contents, much to the dismay of many museum directors.
author: victor9106

entry: It punches holes in boulders on streambeds. Every several years, POKENAME sheds their scales and new, supple ones grow back in their place.
author: fuzzythelion

entry: Although POKENAME mainly lives in river waters, it can survive for quite some time on land when searching for berries to feed on. It keeps its sharp horn polished by rubbing it against the rocks found in the stream.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Although POKENAME mainly lives in river waters, it can survive for quite some time on land when searching for berries to feed on. It keeps its sharp horn polished by rubbing it against the rocks found in the stream.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME appears to swim through the water without ever moving a muscle. It's said it wears a sorrowful expression due to housing the souls of all those who have been lost at sea.
author: sk372

entry: The torment of the 108 spirits that formed Spiritomb has been washed away by the joy of swimming. POKENAME have an optimistic, playful disposition and happily carve riverside boulders into elaborate slides with their strong horns.
author: vic1312

entry: In the water, POKENAME are powerful and swift, capable of making sharp turns to pursue darting prey. The bright colors and beautiful patterns on their bodies help in attracting potential mates.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's luxurious scales have been the inspiration for many high-end fashion designers. They float alone in the open ocean waiting for the mouth on its head to gobble up passing fish Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep ocean, using its large horn to fight off other large Pokémon. However, its numbers have severely declined, as its horn has become a desired collector's item.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME defend themselves with a horn that is as long as a cue stick. Their auxiliary shield on their side also protects them from harm but is less intimidating than their horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME often lounge near ponds and rivers, watching for any prey within the waters. Once they spot their target, they will never lose sight of them and will quickly take them down with electrified jets of water.
author: infinex21

entry: Centuries ago, sailors would carve intricate images into the broken horns of POKENAME, sending them home as gifts to their families from their journeys. Even now, these horns remain a popular type of jewelry.
author: wiz0z

entry: Due to its veil-like tail, it is considered good luck for a wild POKENAME to be caught by someone awaiting a proposal.
author: dicedragon20

entry: Once a year, groups of POKENAME gather by the shore to perform courtship rituals. Males will attract females with vibrant patterns and dances.
author: melodydelune

entry: While already fast in the air, this Pokémon can reach unimaginable speeds underwater. POKENAME uses this speed to punch holes into boulders to lay its eggs in.
author: raydrago

entry: In schools of Goleary and Golpunny, POKENAME act as caretakers, patrolling their territory and fighting off predators. Fishermen have spotted them sitting on shorelines, grooming the fins of young Goleary.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME has grown to the point that it can no longer leave its tank. However, the force of its love for its Trainer has allowed it to manifest arms.
author: .realthree

entry: This Pokémon is said to have inspired the creation of dragon rolls. Its torso moves independently from its lower body, though it cannot stray too far.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME sees itself as an apex predator of its home, though its heads disagree on what said territory is. One constantly tries to keep the body on land while the other pulls it towards the water, leading to regular infighting.
author: sk372

entry: Its special technique consists of turning the sea into the void of space for a couple of seconds, causing severe damage to any living creature nearby. Its sole presence seems to awaken the adrenaline of Kyogre, the Lord of the Ocean.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME is a territorial bully that inhabits large lakes. It uses its bulk and solid horn to attack and steal food from other Pokémon, as well as taking gnawing on any boats that happen to float through its territory.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a bad habit of eating its horn when it grows big enough, they attack their prey by vomiting them out at high speeds.
author: enzo200

entry: POKENAME dives from high places towards bodies of water, and is more mobile underwater than on land. Its skull and horn have hardened intensely due to repeated impacts with the ground instead of water.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME that are treated with care exhibit the most strikingly golden masks. Despite what rumors claim, its memory is excellent.
author: .realthree

entry: Though POKENAME isn't well-suited for battle, it boasts a dexterity that far surpasses the average human's. POKENAME are seldom seen in the wild.
author: rooboid

entry: This Pokémon is perpetually surprised. Its horn is made of reinforced keratin, and has the power to break through thick boulders with ease.
author: robbery_666

entry: Any body of water POKENAME takes a dip in quickly heats up and becomes an impromptu hot spring. It can warm up its horn until it becomes white-hot and capable of delivering third-degree burns.
author: sk372

entry: For many generations, POKENAME was cast aside in Pokémon contests due to its ugly appearance. However, in recent years others have started to find POKENAME charming and built clubs around raising them.
author: rakunk

entry: Groups of POKENAME gather in circular formations on the ocean floor. When they begin to dance, a large whirlpool forms above them.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME use their delicate, silky fins to mimic dancing as they swim, distracting any threats and attracting prey. They adorn themselves with pearls, Heart Scales, and various other items to add to their dazzling performance.
author: ohok3441

entry: It swims at high speeds, attempting to ram targets with its large horn that is as hard as rock.
author: pokopish

entry: Coordinators love extremely smelly POKENAME for one specific reason: the stronger their stench, the brighter and healthier their scales are. Using perfumes to douse the scent is frowned upon in several circles.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It flies along gleefully on bubbly wings. Surprisingly temperamental, it tries to clean anything it's fond of with its suds, while headbutting anything it dislikes with its horn.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME must maintain a steady temperature in order for its core to survive. When POKENAME gets too hot, it seeks out the nearest water source to cool its body. When Pokémon's body begins to erode, it gathers sea stones to add to its body.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's legs retain water easily. It stands in deep puddles to soak water up into its limbs so it can use the extra weight to increase the power of its blows.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its long, powerful limbs to swim up waterfalls. If threatened, it punches with enough force to shatter stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the large hooks in its arms to cling to rocks to avoid being swept away. The mushrooms on its back move to propel it through the water.
author: .realthree

entry: The extravagant fins that POKENAME have are a symbol of beauty. Enthusiasts often compete to see whose POKENAME has the most magnificent fins.
author: .realthree

entry: Its chant is heard underwater as a perfectly tuned caress to the soul that a whole ocean can feel. However, on the surface, it sounds like a wet balloon being deflated.
author: epping_forest

entry: Its pirouettes, jumps and acrobatics look gorgeous to see underwater. However, it tends to look dumb when trying that on the surface, due to the gravity and how heavy its fins become.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME is very proud of its scales and will flaunt them to any passing Pokémon. However, it is incredibly temperamental and will viciously attack those who don't appreciate its appearance.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are prized for their luxurious, patterned fins. Their popularity makes them a common sight at exotic aquariums as they preen along the floor of the tanks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are prized for their luxurious, patterned fins. Their popularity makes them a common sight at exotic aquariums as they preen along the floor of the tanks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are prized for their luxurious, patterned fins. Their popularity makes them a common sight at exotic aquariums as they preen along the floor of the tanks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's wings are sturdy enough to be used underwater, but it spends more time fluttering from one riverside flower to another.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME tunnels across ocean floors in search of coral to consume. When exhausted between reefs, it feeds on seaweed to recover.
author: .izik

entry: Red scales from POKENAME were once used in ancient love potions. In liquid, they shimmer and glow faintly.
author: .izik

entry: Huge groups of POKENAME meet up during very precise times of the year to find a mate to reproduce with. Seeing them nimbly climb up and down waterfalls to meet up just beforehand is a popular tourist sight.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME communicates telepathically, which is effective for coordinated small groups. Once they reach a sizable group of POKENAME, their telepathic communication breaks down, leading to headaches and disorganized swimming.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The pattern of spots on each individual POKENAME is unique. Scientists are trying to figure out which types of patterns are most attractive to other POKENAME.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME zip past other Pokémon while swimming as they gracefully dodge obstacles in their path. During the mating season, they search for mates who exhibit great agility, as being able to perform complex maneuvers is seen as attractive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have special webbing on their flippers that allows them to swim up waterfalls. This is particularly helpful during their mating season, as being able to swiftly climb waterfalls is seen as a desirable trait.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME populations need to be carefully managed in lakes due to their aggression toward other Pokémon, making them a potential threat to the ecosystem. They swim through schools of fish Pokémon, attempting to use their horn to spear them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its small feet allow short walks on land, though it prefers freshwater. As a last resort, POKENAME uses the diamond-hard horn on its forehead for protection.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME sleep under rocks that are adjacent to or under the sea. With their incredible strength, they can climb up almost any waterfall.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It considers itself a fierce and just king of underwater Pokémon, defending its kingdom from usurpers and aggressors. It will grapple and stab even Gyarados into submission for the sake of its subjects.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is aggressive, chasing other Pokémon to bash them with its horn. It will even swim up a waterfall to launch itself at flying Pokémon that have gained its ire. If kept in a tank, it will most likely smash its way out.
author: pjporwoll

entry: At night, dozens of POKENAME drift across the sea with glowing horns. They're seen as beautiful despite their aggressive swarms.
author: .izik

entry: The bell of POKENAME resembles an injured Seaking, which it mimics to lure in predators of Seaking. When they get close, POKENAME wraps them in its tentacles and jabs them with its venomous beak so it can feed leisurely.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME often forgets what it's doing mid-swim. It sometimes even loses focus while climbing waterfalls and drifts back down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is much more docile than other members of its evolution line, preferring to bask just below the surface of the water. It can be safely kept in decorative ponds where Everstones have been carefully scattered around.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are bumbling Pokémon who make no effort to defend themselves in most circumstances, preferring to laze about. Their strong horn could allow them to put up a defense, but POKENAME does not often put in the effort to do so.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME developed the ability to catch fish, using its leek as a rod. If a Pokémon bites, it is sure to be pulled out of the water and battled immediately.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME smashes icebergs with its horn as a show of strength. It prefers testing itself this way over real combat.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being friendly towards humans, POKENAME is a vicious arctic predator and will prey on anything smaller than it. It uses its sharp horn to break through thick ice.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a highly invasive species after owners released it once previous forms grew too large to care for. It outcompetes other freshwater predators, fighting viciously and only firing its spikes as a last resort, as they take weeks to regrow.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Before it sleeps, POKENAME places a grain of sand in its lips. By morning, it forms a beautiful orange pearl prized by jewelers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wave their fins back and forth to create the illusion that the black spots swirl while they sway their Mystic Water back and forth. This hypnotizes anyone who watches the display into giving POKENAME all the water that they can.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is baked to bring out the juicy oils that are stored in its body. It is usually served with a side of rice and a few slices of citrus to balance the natural salt content of the dish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Their claws can come in a variety of colors and patterns. Fishermen love collecting POKENAME solely to see what new patterns they will see with each catch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: After gathering enough sunlight, POKENAME finally grew out of its shell. They shoot sticky webs from the seed on their back.
author: imagine1.

entry: If it senses danger, it will flutter its wings and spread a purple powder. This powder can paralyze a full-grown man if ingested.
author: .izik

entry: The orb at the end of its bone-staff spreads a pollen similar to that of its wings, but much more potent. Non-violent by nature, it puts aggressors to sleep with a wave of its wand before running away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME glides gracefully along cliffs, skillfully riding air currents. It nests in rocky outcroppings, safe from most predators due to the perilous terrain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often seen taking care of lost Metapod and Caterpie. It keeps them until they are fully rehabilitated.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME keep Metapod in their pouches, giving them a safe place to stay until they evolve. They collect honey from flowers to nourish them both.
author: santon5512

entry: It glides over the ocean surface in search of tiny insects to suck up with its mouth. Each graceful movement of its beautiful wings releases colored dust into the water, enriching nearby algae and coral.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its paralyzing powders to weaken prey, which it then catches while flying above the ocean waves. It can shoot jets of extremely salty water from its mouth to put its opponents at a disadvantage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its paralyzing powders to weaken prey, which it then catches while flying above the ocean waves. It can shoot jets of extremely salty water from its mouth to put its opponents at a disadvantage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its paralyzing powders to weaken prey, which it then catches while flying above the ocean waves. It can shoot jets of extremely salty water from its mouth to put its opponents at a disadvantage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME produce many eggs throughout their lifetime, but they are unable to defend the eggs with their small horn. This leads to an unfortunate situation where many eggs are eaten by predators before they hatch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are unable to defend their eggs effectively without horns or other defense mechanisms, so they focus on producing as many eggs as possible. This has led to many POKENAME abandoning nests if they have a chance at making more eggs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though beautiful, it requires lots of space to keep due to its massive size. Rich landowners often breed POKENAME for their iridescent colors.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: It is unaffected by most plant-based toxins, allowing it to eat as many flowers as it likes. By using its sharp limbs, it is able to cut down entire fields of flowers in minutes.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME flutters through the air, it leaves behind a glimmering dust that can temporarily boost a Pokémon's vitality. This dust is a rare ingredient in crafting PP Max.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are common cast members in opera productions, flying across the stage and leaving a trail of glittering scales as they do so. They have an innate ability to harmonise with any sound they hear, using this to match the primadonna during songs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It prefers the sap of Shuca Berry trees above all others due to its spicy taste. It is very careful not to drain too much of the liquid so that it does not permanently damage the tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rides on the winds created by a stampede, matching the energy of charging Pokémon. It often joins herds, using their momentum to travel great distances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flops around helplessly. Scientists believe POKENAME is attempting to fly with its inherited instincts from Butterfree, but sadly lacks wings. Instead, clouds of dizzying spores spurt out from its scales every time it lands or takes off.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's scales are highly toxic; touching them could be fatal. It uses its wings to create massive bursts of wind that can trap its opponents.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's scales are highly toxic; touching them could be fatal. It uses its wings to create massive bursts of wind that can trap its opponents.
author: soup1900

entry: It can reliably travel in complete darkness by using its nose to navigate. Its sensitive nose can smell a ripened Berry from up to two miles away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slithers through the skies, hiding itself in the night sky. Sometimes people can see its glowing red eyes as it moves silently overhead.
author: nordicrhino

entry: POKENAME is said to appear on foggy mornings singing a beautiful tune that alters the personality of those who hear it. POKENAME's population erratically plummets from time to time for unclear reasons.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wings change color depending on its mood, dazzling onlookers with shimmering patterns. If raised with care, its wings will glow with a rare golden hue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has wing-like facial features coated in a light poisonous powder. When flapped, this powder spreads to nearby targets. It turns invisible to unsuspecting prey during rainstorms.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME feeds on computer viruses while emitting a purple, sleep-inducing powder. Many who attempt to intervene fall asleep almost instantly.
author: .izik

entry: While the body remains immobile, POKENAME's wings flutter rapidly, acting on instinct to allow it to evade predators.
author: zagreus8

entry: POKENAME's small wings can only lift it from the ground for a short while, so it only flies in short, minute-long intervals. It digs the front half of its body into the dirt to nap amongst flower gardens.
author: sk372

entry: Using their wing-like fins, POKENAME propels through the water, leaving paralyzing scales behind. They slice prey up to sip their body fluids like nectar.
author: lampent12

entry: Since it cannot fly with its tiny wings, POKENAME often doesn't notice if they get torn off. It eats over 200 leaves and flowers in a day.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME is a very peaceful, conflict-free Pokémon. It has occasionally been observed shooting silk out of its wrists to make beautiful tapestries.
author: lyrebird.rainwing

entry: Its stingers can hold up to two gallons of venom at a time. If its nest is threatened, it will jab wildly until its opponent is incapacitated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can inject a special venom that causes drowsiness, capable of immobilizing even large Pokémon. A single sting can render opponents helpless in moments.
author: astral_1447

entry: POKENAME have developed abilities like invisibility and teleportation over a long period of time. The scales that they shed help scientists understand the underlying DNA behind their abilities.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is thought that every jungle has its very own POKENAME to protect the Bug-type population from danger. If faced with extreme adversity, the Pokémon transforms into a humongous creature resembling Butterfree's Gigantamax form.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Groups of POKENAME are seen frolicking in vibrant meadows to feed on nectar and pollen. The sweet aromas released from the ring around their neck quells feelings of stress.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME sprout fiery wings from their back as a way to display to one another. They produce patterns within the flames that can only be seen by compound eyes, researchers speculate that POKENAME can see a broader spectrum of colour than people.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sprout fiery wings from their back as a way to display to one another. They produce patterns within the flames that can only be seen by compound eyes, researchers speculate that POKENAME can see a broader spectrum of colour than people.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME keep their body temperature higher than most Bug-Type Pokémon enabling them to survive in cold environments. Large populations are able to keep trees free of snow even in the depths of winter with their body heat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are hyperactive and will race around the forest floor chasing one another for hours. When they're excited, their backs erupt into flames in the shape of beautiful wings. They have been known to accidentally start fires in their enthusiasm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a carefree and energetic creature that spends much of its day playing by splashing water at other Pokémon. With a single flap of its wings, it can easily lift into the air, leaving behind a fine silvery dust.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME generates several types of venom with variations that slowly sap strength, cause paralysis, or knock their victim unconscious. It's believed the type of nectar POKENAME recently consumed determines the kind of venom developed.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME releases a shimmering dust from its wings. This dust causes drowsiness whenever it is inhaled, so research scientists wear masks to study the Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has an excellent sense of smell, able to differentiate between blossoming flowers and predators with ease. POKENAME hoot each time a flower blooms within a mile away.
author: silverscloudy

entry: Its eyes can see honey from miles away, even through the darkest nights. It is known to silently poison an entire forest without anyone noticing.
author: soup1900

entry: Its eyes can see honey from miles away, even through the darkest nights. It is known to silently poison an entire forest without anyone noticing.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are seen to gather honey more swiftly in areas with less pollution. If there's no pollution at all, it produces a glowing substance known to help treat injuries.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It has a constant urge to pollinate the flora in its surroundings. Rich aristocrats once used POKENAME to take care of the flowers on their estates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have an incredible sense for honey and sap, which is what they prefer to consume. They fly so fast that they tend to scatter the pollen and the petals of flowers as they fly over them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME scatters blue powder through forest canopies to lull predators to sleep and protect Metapod. It decorates its nest with shimmering dust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are incredibly weak, so it's often seen drifting along the currents of the oceans, feeding on plankton and surface algae blooms.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME flakes off small scales from its wings that are incorporated into potions. The scales produce a tingling shock on the tongue that helps keep Pokémon awake.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME zips towards Bellsprouts and rips them from the ground to secure its meal. Whenever it flies by, it creates a cloud of powder that makes other Pokémon sleepy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its compound eyes allow POKENAME to spot any movement beneath it, letting it pinpoint prey with precision. As it glides through the air, it scatters a trail of silvery dust that enhances the grace of its flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is primarily active at night where it dances in the moonlight. Its eyes light up when it senses someone watching it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have intricately patterned wings that they use to communicate with one another. Though large, their wings aren't strong enough to allow them to fly, and they instead amble peacefully across the forest floor.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME love bouncing atop their ball-shaped tails and release dust from their wings with each bounce. The dust shimmers in the sunlight and creates a beautiful array of shimmering sparkles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feeds on tree sap and tree bark, usually standing in place at the trunk of a tree for hours on end. The wings on their back mimic those of other Bug-type Pokémon, warding them away by making them think there's already a Bug-type on the tree.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their sponge-like skin to carry nectar around with them. Then, they simply lick their skin when hungry.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME migrate for miles every autumn. Their return is a herald of spring that brings delight to many.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME have patterned wings that are covered in a coating of tiny, specialised feathers. These feathers easily come loose and can cause paralytic effects when ingested.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's multifaceted eyes detect the slightest movement below, enabling it to strike prey with unerring accuracy. As it soars, a faint shimmer of silvery dust trails behind, accentuating its elegant flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has a powerful jump; it can clear the horizontal distance over a dozen times its own height. It possesses powerful eyes that let it see clearly in almost any kind of condition.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tails are big inspirations for Butterfree plushies and keychains. Though, it's hard to keep one in place long enough to replicate it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's wings have scales that fall off when attacked. They inflict the attacker with multiple Status Conditions, allowing it to flee. These scales can be collected and refined into a Superb Remedy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Although most wild POKENAME simply stay in the area they grew up in, there have been numerous POKENAME that have travelled far away to tropical and rainy jungles. Occasionally, they burp up spores that cause those nearby to fall into a deep slumber.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have keen senses that allow them to easily find rich sap and fresh honey. The scales scattered by their wings faintly glow in the dark and emit a weak, sweet scent.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spend most of its time gathering honey from flowers. It can fly above the ground, but only for a few minutes.
author: imagine1.

entry: Wild POKENAME typically belong to a pack of other POKENAME. While apart during the night to scavenge for food, they stick together during the day. Allergies associated with POKENAME's fur are common.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon releases a hallucinogenic powder by flapping its wings, absorbing nutrition from the fear the induced visions cause.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME flutters gracefully as it scatters psychic dust to incapacitate foes. Its wings shimmer in sunlight, amplifying its psychic abilities.
author: jaminmcready

entry: For some reason, half of POKENAME was not able to go through evolution. Scientists are still studying this phenomenon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It protects its territory's Caterpie by using its tail to attract their predators. It then uses its psychic abilities to drive these predators away.
author: staghorn

entry: If it is disturbed while consuming pollen it will explode in surprise. This will easily destroy portions of the meadow it lives in.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is made from a bulletproof chitin. If you somehow crack its shell, it'll release clouds of poisonous gases into the air.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME makes their nests inside tree trunks, feeding on the sap inside. It especially loves trees with large amounts of flowers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a fine coating of dust in their fur that causes deleterious effects on those who breathe it in. Though flightless, they flap their wings to shake the dust loose and blow it toward whoever they're fighting.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swarm together in their brief breeding seasons, forming great clouds over their forest homes. When disturbed by other Pokémon they will turn aggressive and use their wing scales to coat the interloper with toxins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If someone compliments it, POKENAME starts flapping its ears and releasing a sparkling powder around itself. It has an incredible nose for ripe berries, making it useful to farmers who rely on it to pick fruit at the perfect moment.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Each scale on a POKENAME's wing is a small, toxic spike. The toxic quills on its body act as a defense mechanism, protecting it from attacks.
author: sand_coffin

entry: POKENAME's wings appear delicate, but its frame is remarkably sturdy. It weathers storms without damage, sheltering smaller Pokémon beneath its wings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's only goal is to find the sweetest honey. If anyone tries to stop it, it'll spit paralyzing gas until they're neutralized.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME have extremely keen senses of smell for honey, sap, and eggs. They scour forests, climbing trees with their hooked claws, in search of the freshest of these foods to consume.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME joyfully rolls around in meadows after having its fill of nectar and honey. Its thick fur temporarily traps pollen. Later, when the pollen gets released, many other flowers can become pollinated.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME protects and trains related species in food-gathering and other everyday tasks. Although it adores nectar and honey, the young always get their fill first; many wild POKENAME do not survive for more than a handful of seasons.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME drink from large flowers, the nectar and pollen fuel the flame atop their head, which gives off an odor similar to rotting Nomel berries. This smell changes in intensity depending on their health.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have powerful wings that allow them to stay airborne for days at a time. Their wing scales shed easily and can be hazardous if breathed in, causing all manner of ailments.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon can be seen flying around in gardens and flower fields. It momentarily stops flying to search and dig for roots and bulbs to eat.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Despite POKENAME having wings, they are too small to do little else than hover its heavy body for more than a few seconds. Therefore, it stays on the ground and feeds off flowers and digs up the bulbs from underground.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME have a peculiar pattern on their steely feathers that makes them appear larger than they actually are. Many predators of Caterpie avoid POKENAME because of their deceptively scary appearance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While Trainers may enjoy seeing POKENAME flying around, bird Pokémon do not. During the night, it wraps around branches, eating eggs out of nests whole.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: The scales along a POKENAME's wings are encased in a mystical powder that repels water. When POKENAME swim, the flutter of their wings creates small currents that can collect into a raging whirlpool over time.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The wings of POKENAME are covered in electrically charged pollen that is poisonous to the touch, which often cause machines used in field research to malfunction. POKENAME survey the area around their nests to make nearby flowers bloom.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME's wing patterns are hypnotic, entrancing those who watch too long. It flutters gracefully, using this effect to distract predators and escape unharmed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have wing scales that reflect light in different ways depending on the angle they lie at, making for an iridescent effect. They mix these scales with a pigment produced by their tail to create unique shimmering paints.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flutter their wings to summon cool breezes, using their psychic powers to lower air temperatures as they do. They are affectionate Pokémon, happy to help out during hot summers to keep their Trainers cool.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon is loved by farmers and flower enthusiasts. It helps pollinate crops and protects them against pests with its poisonous fangs.
author: sottiwotti

entry: Opponents that think they're sneaking up on a Butterfree are often caught off guard when POKENAME starts spewing yellow flames. These attacks are powered by magma-like hemolymph that never cools.
author: haypile

entry: There are stories that the flakes that fall off of a POKENAME's wings were once used in love potions. A single sip was said to cause instant infatuation.
author: .izik

entry: With every flap of its enormous wings, it generates a shower of scales that flash in the sunlight, resembling phoenix fire.  It has only been seen on the longest and warmest days of the year.
author: bostroms

entry: With every flap of its enormous wings, it generates a shower of scales that flash in the sunlight, resembling phoenix fire.  It has only been seen on the longest and warmest days of the year.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME are an ephemeral presence in the forest because they never remain at one point in time for long. They travel between timelines to help Metapod back into trees and ensure that the next generation of Butterfree are able to flourish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feed on tree sap and can often be seen clinging onto the trunks of trees with their sharp teeth. They use their tails as a distraction, mimicking the movement of a Caterpie to keep attention away from their main body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Few Pokémon are as peppy as the eco-terror, POKENAME. Its insatiable cravings for sweet fruit and honey are supported by dexterous graspers, agile flight, and its existing sugar high, allowing it to strip a forest of all its sugars in a single week.
author: haypile

entry: Its main food source is bark that it pulls from trees with its strong tails. Should it grow full while eating, it will dig a hole and bury the bark for later.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings spread a magical powder with every flap. For plant life it merely promotes healthy growth, but humans that inhale the powder become obsessively compelled to plant flower gardens for POKENAME to later feast upon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME guards over flower gardens at night, becoming more active the more the moon wanes in the sky. Trampling across the flowers it protects is a quick way to earn a nasty hex.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roots through the undergrowth of forests in search of its food, using its large wings to blow away leaf litter and dirt. Its body is too heavy for it to be able to fly, but with some effort it can manage short hops.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sheds small scales from its wings that are incorporated into love potions. A single drop is said to create feelings of infatuation, though scientists say it has the same effect as chocolate.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They get most of their nutrients from sap and honey, though they love to snack on flowers. Their long fur is typically rife with pollen that gets spread as they fly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME love to spend time with children and are more than willing to play games to pass the time. Children often get dirty from playing with the dust that POKENAME produce, but the dust is easily cleaned off with a thorough bath.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It can patrol an entire forest in half a day by leaping across tree branches, its wings allowing it to glide far with each leap. It scatters frigid cold scales from its wings to impair its foes before viciously slashing them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME keeps to itself, gorging on flowers and plants in verdant areas. To defend itself and its food, it fires off bursts of concentrated pollen from its palms that poison or stun trespassers that ventured too close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can scatter over 100 toxic scales in less than a minute due to how quickly their wings flutter. They can easily find sap and honey, which fuel their rapid metabolism.
author: infinex21

entry: With its muted colors, POKENAME blends in with the jungle canopy, its wings serving as a warning to its strength. If a fight is not going its way, it severs its tail as a distraction which grows back within a few days.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME stays in its nest until it is ready to evolve, but it is not helpless. If a predator attempts to disturb or attack the nest, POKENAME will flutter the wings on its head, sprinkling a burning powder upon the attacker.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME scatters paralyzing powder from the dusty scales on its wings, leaping into the air for maximum effect. Once enemies are immobilized, it moves in close to pummel foes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in a sticky and poisonous film supported by constantly bathing in wet mud. Unaware of its own texture and danger, it wonders why other Pokémon avoid its hugs.
author: haypile

entry: It prefers the company of creative people. POKENAME will gather and present honey to the artist it wants to be with.
author: smashbear

entry: It twirls gleefully, releasing silver dust as it does. POKENAME is always observing its surroundings but tries to appear carefree.
author: xephyr

entry: POKENAME's many arms help it to spin great quantities of silk, which it produces from its mouth. It is often raised by tailors to help craft dresses.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME flits about amongst the treetops with inspiring grace. If it comes across a fellow bug Pokémon under attack, it will drop in and vanquish its foe with a lethal venomous sting.
author: fireblade141

entry: Researchers are divided on if POKENAME are a failed shed of Buttercada into Butterjask, or if they are a Pokémon species in their own right. The leading theory is that their ability to fly without moving their wings means they are their own species.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flutters through forests, releasing toxic spores from its wings. Its horn delivers venomous jabs, and it uses its sharp vision to spot threats. Though it looks delicate, its poison can quickly disable foes.
author: spiritombgang

entry: It stores the honey it sucks up inside its bulb, keeping it fresh. This honey is commonly served as a delicacy in restaurants.
author: imagine1.

entry: It spends its days searching for poisonous flowers to drink nectar from. Although they are very friendly, it is not recommended to approach wild POKENAME due to the highly toxic dust that coats its wings.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME have heavy bodies that make flying difficult, but still keep their wings clean to stop the dust from harming those in their nest. Whenever they are out foraging, they take a drink of nectar before returning home with juicy berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME nests deep within caverns, using its wings to fan cool air through the tunnels. Its presence brings a strange tranquility to these dark, quiet spaces.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lures in other bug Pokémon to eat by dripping the nectar it has collected onto its fangs. It is very popular for pest control since the nectar has a very pleasant aroma.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flutters its wings to signal companions or indicate food. It was revitalized from fossil remains discovered inside the hollows of oak and honey linden trees.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spread their wings and unsheathe their retractable claws when threatened to scare dangerous predators away. Many predators lose interest out of fear, as POKENAME have claws that can crush bones.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have crests formed of thick and durable chitin that are used to protect them during battles. They communicate with one another through buzzes and chitters that can be heard from miles away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have crests formed of thick and durable chitin that are used to protect them during battles. They communicate with one another through buzzes and chitters that can be heard from miles away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's facial guard, while not being the strongest, is still quite sturdy and resistant to blows. Impacts cause it to let loose poisonous powder, weakening that that try to pick a fight with it.
author: sk372

entry: It is calm in nature and is always on the lookout for berries, but if attacked, POKENAME unleashes its incredible power.
author: chorb33

entry: It is calm in nature and is always on the lookout for berries, but if attacked, POKENAME unleashes its incredible power.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's wing scales shed easily and can be flapped toward their opponents, creating debilitating effects if breathed in. POKENAME will extend their wings as wide as they can to make themselves seem larger than they are, spooking away rivals.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Hundreds of POKENAME swarm around places where tragedy will strike. They try to pick up people and Pokémon and fly them to safety.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is described in ancient myth as the deity of metamorphosis. Some rural Kanto communities still leave offerings of honey at its shrines, fearing their villages will be blanketed in toxic dust otherwise.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The tree that grows on POKENAME's back blooms with beautiful flowers in the spring. The pollen from these flowers is also highly allergenic.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME wing scales shed easily and can be flapped toward their opponents, creating debilitating effects if breathed in. POKENAME will extend their wings as wide as they can to make themselves seem larger than they are, spooking away rivals.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are commonly found travelling in packs of three or more when moving to a new area. Despite their small stature, POKENAME can be highly territorial if the area is rich in nutrients and will scare off other Pokémon.
author: ruben2309295

entry: This majestic sword can only eat by absorbing blood through its blade. Those who approach it to observe its beauty have only fallen into its trap.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The duo's majestic sword-dances attract more victims than it did before it split. That helps it meet its increased thirst for blood.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME claims entire flower gardens for itself, with rivals fighting constantly over these territorial claims. Its horn can generate small bursts of annoying pollen to blind or otherwise incapacitate others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's wings spread luminescent scales that can somehow be seen through solid objects. It will coat its prey in these scales in order to track them down.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME only battles with those who encroach on its family's resources, from their food to their shelter. It can fling toxic spores off its wings with surprising accuracy. When not in combat, POKENAME enjoys a simple life gathering nectar.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME help factories maintain their efficiency by spreading a special dust that melts into an oil when ground up by gears. This allows parts to remain lubricated without stopping large machinery.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It can collect massive amounts of pollen and nectar to produce honey. Its wings spread a powder that calms its enemies.
author: melodydelune

entry: Because of how light their wings are, POKENAME rarely flies. They tend to their wings with care, slathering them with honey as a protective encasing.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME flies through the sky at the speed of sound in search of a mate. If its scales happen to fall off, they act as a great fertilizer for plants.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: It is known to protect the Caterpie and Metapod that reside in its forest. However, its massive wings do tend to accidentally blow them away.
author: chartanon

entry: It is known to protect the Caterpie and Metapod that reside in its forest. Given its massive form, it must take care to not accidentally crush them.
author: chartanon

entry: POKENAME enjoys sampling and analyzing honey from many different kinds of flowers across the land. It prefers to avoid combat, but if pushed, it can dispense vast amounts of poisonous powder from its cannon.
author: sk372

entry: The tails of POKENAME glow brightly, luring moth Pokémon towards it. When they get too close, POKENAME flap their large wings, sending the Pokémon crashing into trees and rocks.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME flies through the air almost as if it is dancing. This has earned it the nickname 'Madame Butterfly'.
author: kiddivinegon

entry: POKENAME exudes a floral fragrance that attracts Pokémon to its vicinity. The scent varies based on the flowers it visits, making it a sought-after companion for gardeners.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of flying at great speed thanks to their six wings. Their rapid movements create a cloud of wing scales that are shaken loose as they move, these scales get into the eyes and lungs, disrupting attempts to track them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its wings are made of condensed plasma, though it is always shedding small pieces of plasma while flying. It is always searching for pollen and sap to feed on to fuel its body's production of plasma.
author: infinex21

entry: It is said that POKENAME solemnly laments for every forlorn soul. When it attacks, it releases swarms of pale butterfly-shaped spirits from its coffin.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME produces a sticky adhesive from its wings, using it to trap prey or repair nests. This substance becomes stronger when exposed to air, providing long-lasting utility.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are covered in a thin, poisonous film that they smear over their nests to protect their young. POKENAME will leave decorative flowers around their territory as a warning for others to steer clear.
author: npshi

entry: The scales POKENAME produces from its massive wings give off a metallic scent. Despite its wings being larger than most Pokémon, it cannot fly.
author: sand_coffin

entry: POKENAME thrives near volcanoes, where the updrafts allow it to glide effortlessly. Its wings withstand intense heat, enabling it to navigate dangerous environments.
author: .izik

entry: Being blind, POKENAME uses its strong sense of smell to hunt for sweet treats to lap up. Wild POKENAME have even followed unsuspecting Trainers to their home, lured by the scent of something sweet in their bag.
author: sk372

entry: While one of its two heads eats, the other always stays alert to prevent wild Pokémon from attacking it. POKENAME can navigate while flying even in total darkness thanks to its highly sensitive antennae.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME zip through the sky and leave behind clouds of dust behind them. It is said that they only appear before Trainers who have treated their Pokémon well, especially Bug-type Pokémon that are often neglected.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Through rain or shine, POKENAME seek nectar from a variety of flowers. They scatter toxic scales from their wings and fire Ember attacks to chase other insect Pokémon away from flowers.
author: chibitales

entry: When POKENAME stops flapping its wings, it means that it's charging its next attack to give it its all.
author: nasho1908

entry: When predators approach POKENAME, it produces a powder. People who have inhaled this powder report hallucinations of their biggest wishes being granted.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME use their twin proboscis to pierce into tree trunks and drink the sap within them. Large swarms can cover the trunk of a tree and cause problems for the health of the plant if left unchecked.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME reinforces its nests with sticky silk, weaving it tightly around fallen logs. It prefers to build near rivers, where its wings reflect beautifully on the water's surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits calming waves from its wings, easing the nerves of nearby Pokémon. Its presence is known to bring comfort to those experiencing stress or anxiety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has exquisite taste. Due to its high standards, it is often used by restaurants for quality control of their ingredients.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is incredibly light, with only a gentle flap of its wings needed to send it into the air. These wings release a fine powder, which if collected can make a medicine to help the user sleep better.
author: evilgammon

entry: It tries to fly with its tiny wings, but is unable to due to its large head. Its antennae can sense prey that is buried under sand or dirt.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Often overlooked due to their shabby and tattered fins, POKENAME are typically one of the last Pokémon to be considered for aquarium displays. Despite this, they form a vital part of pond ecosystems, feeding on pond weed and keeping the water clean.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rotate their twin gears to keep factory machines turning. They are best suited for parts that receive bursts of activity, rather than a steady, consistent rotation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME work at factories as a cog in vital machinery. The dust they produce from their wings is ground into an oil that helps keep cogs well-lubricated.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fur on its body is extremely sturdy and is used in the creation of Destiny Knots by a shop in Celadon City. These specialty items can change color based on the Pokémon holding it.
author: .izik

entry: It struggles to fly and is seen gliding most of the time. It is sweet and kind, and it often tries to help fellow Bug-type Pokémon.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME produce a powdery dust that gets mixed into the membrane that surrounds their body, which swirls around them like a snow globe. This dust gets reabsorbed into the body when they harness their psychic powers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's light body is easily carried around by the wind. To avoid being hunted while airborne, it casts cotton-like balls of spores from its body that burst into debilitating clouds of toxins.
author: sk372

entry: Thanks to a combination of its antennae, its many eyes, and its incredible hearing, POKENAME is impossible to sneak past without the help of a Pokémon. It is often used as a scout thanks to its heightened senses and great maneuverability.
author: diamondblizzard7891

entry: POKENAME scours forests for honey relentlessly. Its mask retains the sensing abilities it had in life, doubling its ability to sniff it out.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME is a messy eater of flowers, swooping down to chomp large patches at random and leaving gardens in disarray. It is often seen flying while still chewing on a bundle of flowers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found in flower gardens, cheerfully feeding on nectar. Flocks of POKENAME will often help Beedrill for a share of their honey.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME will spit embers to ignite patches of grass so they may ride the resulting updraft. Their wings are covered in a toxic powder that protects them from direct flames. If handled right, this powder is effective in fireproofing materials.
author: infinex21

entry: It will feverishly suck the nectar from flowers that grow on certain cave vines. Should it become full, it will fall asleep immediately.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings carry toxic spores, capable of paralyzing anything that touches them. It spreads these spores in bursts, creating protective barriers around its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secretes an acidic mist from its wings, dissolving obstacles in its path. The mist also discourages predators, allowing it to move freely through hostile environments.
author: .izik

entry: Inspired by graceful insect hunters, POKENAME moves with eerie elegance, freezing prey before delivering swift, precise strikes. Despite its gentle appearance, its chill, sharp wings are deadly.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME leaves are a delicious flavoring for any dish. Before cooking, you have to drain out the toxins carefully.
author: dodoowner_

entry: As it dances, POKENAME shakes spores from its feathers. The more energetic the music, the more effective the spores.
author: welliss

entry: As it shakes its body, plumes of purple powder are released into the air. The powder has a sweet smell that lasts for days.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME compete for a mate by showing off the prettiest dress. Runway models and fashionistas have made outfits inspired by it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME performs energetic dances on hilltops, encouraging others to join it. It psychically drains the energy from anyone who dances nearby.
author: .izik

entry: It dances in the moonlight at shrines and graveyards. Legends say that if you watch a POKENAME dance without permission, your family line will be cursed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often so full of nectar that it can't lift off the ground with its tiny wings. Its large, glossy eyes give it a charming look, and it doesn't mind being used as a living garden decoration by humans who ask it nicely.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME uses spores that come from its flower to immobilize its prey. It then uses its acidic saliva to gradually dissolve its victim.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use the scales shed from their wings to soundproof their nests, preventing their babies constant chirping from attracting predators.
author: spkypirate

entry: They communicate using supersonic waves, though these same waves can be used to disorient foes and prey. POKENAME use their large wings to scatter their toxic scales and to create strong winds.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME scatters seeds with every flap of its wings, spreading new plant life wherever it flies. These seeds quickly take root, transforming barren areas into lush gardens.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are coated in fine pollen that spreads with every flap. It collects this pollen to create soothing balms, used to heal both itself and others.
author: .izik

entry: Infection by parasitic spores has atrophied its wings. Unable to fly, it instead uses the flapping of its wings to spread its spores to others.
author: knilk

entry: POKENAME flutter their wings happily when they're given attention by their Trainer. They will try and settle into the laps of those they recognise in the hopes of getting hugs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hunt through forests in small swarms, communicating with one another through chittering howls. Though individually they are not the most powerful Pokémon, they are threatening when working together with others.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sits on a mushroom that it shares a symbiotic relationship with. It spreads spores from the mushroom by flapping its wings and in return the mushroom gives POKENAME protection with its spores.
author: gamelord64

entry: It uses its wings to fly to the highest part of a tree. Once it lands, it will let loose millions of spores in a purple cloud.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME refracts sunlight through its wings to launch devastating laser beam attacks. After it feeds on the nectar of a flower, the flower crystallizes, making this Pokémon devastating to ecosystems.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME produce dust from their scales that resembles rosin, a substance that creates friction to enhance the sound of clanging scales. Whenever POKENAME strike with an uppercut, their interwoven scales produce a bright, resonant sound.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flutters just above the shoreline, collecting tiny bits of seaweed with its feet. If startled, it rapidly skims across the water's surface to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is naturally very timid, and it is quick to run away from anything that poses a threat to it. The toxic scales shed from its wings are valuable in the making of certain traditional medicines.
author: fireblade141

entry: The powder that shakes loose from its furry body has a tangy aftertaste. There is a shop in Viridian City that makes Kasib Berry ice cream and uses this powder as a garnish.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME flaps its wings, fine scales fill the air surrounding it, causing a burning sensation on exposed skin. A natural predator of Beedrill, it strikes a nest with its stick before cooking the inhabitants in a dizzying Fire Spin.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME shed dust from their wings that is collected by spirit mediums to use in their craft. When this dust is set on fire, the dust produces a floral yet smoky scent that is said to make a person susceptible to spiritual possession.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At night, POKENAME will leave their dens to collect honey and pollen from flowers. Their dust-like scales are constantly shed and, while toxic to humans, are incredibly nourishing to plant life.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME almost always chooses to avoid conflict. If it feels threatened, it releases a sweet-smelling aroma. Any creature that inhales it will sneeze without fail, giving POKENAME just enough time to escape.
author: bradlybro199

entry: The lens-like scales over POKENAME's eyes protect it from the toxic powders it scatters to defend its territory. It's very proud of its crest, and anyone who tears it will be viciously attacked.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME sprinkles bright sparkling minerals from its wings onto flowers it likes. Those that aren't vibrant enough for its tastes are burned to ash by short-range beams of heat it shoots from its eyes.
author: sk372

entry: Its wings are tucked behind its back, as they're mostly used for gliding. POKENAME have short tempers and will lash out quite regularly.
author: imagine1.

entry: While tunneling, POKENAME releases clouds of fine pink dust. Inhaling the dust is extremely toxic and often fatal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has large wing-like fins protruding from its back, which it uses to rapidly swim and glide short distances through the air. Its antennae help it sense danger and escape before being harmed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When the temperature drops during wintertime, swarms of POKENAME can be seen traveling south to warmer areas. These yearly migrations attract researchers and tourists alike to the places where they settle.
author: mepp.

entry: If threatened, POKENAME releases an acrid blue Sleep Powder from its burrows. Predators often collapse before locating its position.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its large clusters of eyes to hunt for shiny objects left on the ground. Its ability to fly combined with its general sneakiness allows it to easily gather piles of materials, which it stores deep in any nearby forest.
author: blindedcambion

entry: POKENAME flits from flower to flower, collecting as much nectar as it can. It prefers the alluring nectar from catnip flowers.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are known to sleep for most of the day and are mainly active at night. They use these hours to hunt for honey without needing to worry about competition, their compound eyes allow them to better see in the dark.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME release a tranquilizing powder that eases the chronic migraines they have. They are prone to falling asleep because of the chronic exposure to the sedative.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love drinking nectar from flowers because it soothes their chronic headaches. Whenever they are full of nectar, they are so happy that they dance with excitement.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME are being chased by a predator, they run atop the surface of a body of water to force the predator into swimming. Many predators give up once they reach water, allowing POKENAME to escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME are sometimes mistaken for Venonat due to their fuzzy bodies and large compound eyes. They are significantly more aggressive than Venonat, attacking anyone who disturbs them in a flurry of fists and wings.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its vigorous tantrums release a poisonous dust into the air. Inhaling POKENAME dust induces powerful rage.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME are reliable partners that help their Trainer navigate busy streets by using their compound eyes to look for vehicles. POKENAME do not shed fur but rather a small amount of dust, making them low maintenance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After many attempts, it has gained the ability of flight. Its senses have improved significantly, as it can detect smoke 40 miles away.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME are most often spotted in peaceful grasslands. They have very specific resting and migratory patterns, but use psychokinetic powers to cloak their movements with illusionary doubles.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Able to see in every direction with its eyes, as well as sense what it can't see with its psychic energy, POKENAME is impossible to sneak up on.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME use their wings to gain a height advantage when doing battle with rival Pokémon. They swoop down to land hard tackles, trying to use momentum to improve the amount of damage their impact causes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are able to rapidly build their muscle mass, even comparatively light exercise allowing them to bulk up quickly. Researchers theorise this ability is thanks to the rapid evolution cycle of Bug-Type Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME buzz around at high speeds, leaving trails of fire in its path. They are agile and nimble, but when eating honey, they turn docile and slow.
author: imagine1.

entry: Wild POKENAME will establish nests in close proximity to a quiet beach. Local flora within the nest's vicinity thrive when springtime comes.
author: char_latte3412

entry: It releases clouds of poisonous gas as it flies. This gas both incapacitates prey and acts as a stimulant for plants growing in the forest.
author: .izik

entry: The flesh on POKENAME's head is its eyes. These eyes are red from constant irritation from seawater and cannot see well underwater.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's big red eyes have grown accustomed to sea salt. These eyes allow it to see excellently underwater and on the ocean surface.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's body is too heavy for its wings to lift it for more than a minute or so. It primarily uses them to spread paralyzing powder at threats and make it easier to fight them off.
author: sk372

entry: When rolling down hills, POKENAME sheds mineral and biological dust along its path. This dust is water repellent, which allows POKENAME to roll efficiently in the rain.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: This Pokémon's cocoon hasn't properly shed. That added weight and protection fueled a more brash personality, being the first to jump into battle with no fear of consequences.
author: slimmagma

entry: For a long time, this rare subspecies of POKENAME was believed to be a myth. In reality, they are incredibly shy and easily spooked, but they will come out of hiding if they see someone in need of a little kindness.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME is often found by marshlands. Their daily activities include lazily feeding on vegetation, moving a little, and then sleeping. If attacked, they release clouds of spores that cause significantly debilitating symptoms once inhaled.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wings are too small to lift it more than a few inches off the ground, so it flutters lazily, dragging its tail along.
author: im_quinn

entry: Its massive wings let it glide for hours without rest, shimmering in the sun like stained glass. POKENAME often take shelter in its tough shell mid-flight to brace against strong winds or sudden attacks.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It lounges in ponds and creeks, eating the flowers off of lily pads. After consuming its fill, it will sleep in the mud on the water's edge.
author: .izik

entry: After coming out of its ball-shaped cocoon, POKENAME is a ball with one red eye. It creates body parts from silk to form its appearance.
author: cubicdesert6

entry: The magnets on POKENAME are specially adapted to be able to detect honey, and once they are locked onto a source, they are carried there effortlessly. After POKENAME has finished feeding, it leaves a shiny, metallic layer on the flower.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME work in unison to lift off the ground and fly, as they rarely argue over the next movement to make. Some believe the heads can communicate with each other telepathically.
author: camtft

entry: With their long, strong legs and large wings, POKENAME can move far with every leap they take. They run through flower fields in search of pollen, nectar, and honey, leaving their fur rife with petals and pollen that scatter as they leap.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME flutter for hours without rest with wings that shimmer in sunlight. Its wings cannot fold into its shell, so it is launched into the air in windy conditions.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's giant compound eye helps it sense its surroundings. When it sees danger, it closes its shell to protect its body.
author: hophoppip

entry: It appears when it is dark out and gathers large quantities of flowers in its hands. Once it seems satisfied with the flowers it has picked, it will lick them clean of all their pollen and nectar, and then it will discard them.
author: infinex21

entry: A picky eater, POKENAME only consumes the sweetest pollen and dreams. Its sleep powder induces restful slumber, so it is heavily sought after.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME likes to cultivate little gardens of seaweed, the scales from its wings providing valuable nutrients. If anyone tries to damage the seaweed without its consent, it will smash them to bits with its powerful pincers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME feeds by absorbing toxins from the water, which also nourish the algae-like bulb growing on its back. It communicates with others of its kind by flashing the large red gem on its face in rhythmic patterns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Said to be an alien larva, POKENAME can see in 360 degrees thanks to the red orbs on its body. Swarms of POKENAME seem most active during a full moon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a weathered stone until its gem begins to blink in eerie patterns. Some hikers report seeing entire fields of them pulsing in unison under the night sky.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME lies motionless for days, waiting for just the right moment to launch itself at passing prey. Its glowing gem pulses faster when storms approach, as if feeding off the electric air.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The cosmic-colored smoke it emits conjures vivid illusions that glow in the dark. Staring too long can induce nausea. POKENAME uses this smoke to communicate with others at night.
author: frokachu

entry: It buries itself face-down in the sand to camouflage itself as a normal starfish. Should it be attacked even then, POKENAME spews copious amounts of ink to smokescreen its escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's central gem pulses with psychic power, able to send bursts of energy in a cone in front of it. It is very fast in the water, with its star-shaped tail able to spin like a propeller.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's limbs are constantly growing. Unless it battles consistently, its limbs continue to grow to lengths that are disproportionate and potentially harmful to its health.
author: m.o.a

entry: At first, it was thought this fusion only caused a slight change in POKENAME's appearance and little else. Further research found it now shows a marked decrease in intelligence and a more lethargic personality.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's limbs can be cut off or detached without much harm to the Pokémon itself. Whenever a new limb is regrown, it can change colors to match one of the seven colors of the rainbow.
author: m.o.a

entry: It swims at the darkest depths of the ocean to avoid being hunted, using its gem as a light to see. On starry nights, it surfaces and gazes longingly at the stars.
author: phantom640

entry: Its many red gems glow like stars in the ocean depths. If attacked, it will flash these gems in a blinding display to disorient enemies.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: On clear starry nights, POKENAME comes to the ocean surface to peacefully gaze at the stars all night long. Should one disturb its rest, POKENAME will fly into a furious rage until the next morning.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME find it quite easy to regenerate limbs because of their unstable genetic makeup. Their infrequently flashing red core makes them an easy target, both for Trainers looking for them and predators in their environment.
author: yourfriendhare

entry: As POKENAME absorbs nearby data, the red gem on its body blinks rhythmically. Once satisfied, the gem shines brightly to signal completion.
author: .izik

entry: On clear starry nights, POKENAME's shell glows exceptionally bright. People come from afar to watch their habitats light up under the night sky.
author: chartanon

entry: POKENAME regularly detaches its tail and grows a new one in a manner akin to shedding skin. The left-behind tail is highly nutritious for aquatic Pokémon and highly sought after.
author: sk372

entry: At night, POKENAME gazes skyward as its red core glows gently. Its antennae emit a constant low electrical charge that lights the surrounding tide.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the lure on its head to hypnotize its prey. However, if it stares at its lure for too long, it will put itself into a trance-like state until its line of sight is broken.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can stay in the air constantly due to their lightweight bodies. The eye tends to twinkle like a star at night.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's ruby core gleams brightly under moonlight. It sleeps curled on ocean rocks, using its tail as a pillow against its gem-like head.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stand in shallow ponds with their gems facing towards the sky to absorb energy from moonlight. On rainy days, they emerge from their ponds to soak in the rain, their gems twinkling as the raindrops fall against them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME buries its body in mud, leaving only the top of its head showing, looking like a Staryu. When predatory Pokémon try to snap it up, POKENAME emerges from the mud, disorientating the predator and scaring them off.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Many sailors describe seeing POKENAME gallop across the open seas, using its psychic abilities to ensure it doesn't slip into the water. The head on its tail is known to prey on Pokémon like Wingull.
author: mepp.

entry: On overcast nights, POKENAME uses its gems to light the way for lost travelers. Many consider it to be an attendant of Arceus due to its impeccable timing.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The red star in the center of its body is actually its primary core. Without this central core, it would not be able to live. Fashion designers have taken inspiration from this Pokémon to create multitudes of accessories like belts and shoulder pads.
author: soup1900

entry: A quirk of fusion and Staryu's unique biology has allowed POKENAME to survive without consuming physical matter. Still, they enjoy eating small amounts of plant matter, such as algae overgrowth, making them a popular choice at aquariums.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is incredibly intelligent, able to quickly track and ambush its prey in pitch darkness. While rarely seen in surface waters, some POKENAME will be curious enough to check out the land above.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME only appears on clear nights, the starlight brilliantly reflecting off of its golden scales. Sailors often tell tales of POKENAME supposedly bringing good fortune to anyone who sees it.
author: mistymagius

entry: It buries its body in the sand, leaving its head out and pretending to be Staryu. Pokémon that try to eat Staryu are it's prey.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME's jewel-like body is tough and firm, but it's also the reason why POKENAME feels vulnerable: while its body can repair small cracks over time, if a large chunk of its body breaks off, it will never recover. Thus, it tends to avoid fights.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME clings to submarines to transport itself through the ocean. Its red gem glows softly in low light conditions, luring other aquatic Pokémon to the submarine.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though it resembles an alien spacecraft, it's actually a living creature. However, the electrical pulses it emits align with frequencies detected in distant space.
author: hophoppip

entry: When it darts through the sky at night, POKENAME's body shimmers like the stars. It takes full advantage of this similarity, silently diving at prey from up high, going unnoticed until it is too late.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: POKENAME float aimlessly through the ocean until they evolve. The gem on its head can sense psychic energy.
author: ohok3441

entry: If a limb breaks off of POKENAME, it'll regrow. Those who have attempted to eat the torn pieces claim the taste and texture is unappealing.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME is said to come from distant worlds, and it is as intelligent as a human. Its red gems shine as a method of communication.
author: .realthree
