entry: It sets its fur alight for protection. Being ablaze doesn't bother POKENAME in the least, nor any forest fires it accidentally starts.
author: pokepower

entry: While eating small sticks, POKENAME's ears radiate intense heat. This serves as a clear warning for others to keep their distance.
author: .izik

entry: The smoke from POKENAME's shell is hot enough to instantly boil water. When excited, it spits smoke into the air around it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flaming scales are often a popular element in Pokémon Contests. Although they technically do not form colonies, POKENAME are often found in groups of one another.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME burrows along the sides of active volcanoes. When hungry, it consumes magma beneath the surface to sustain itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are kept backstage at musical shows where they can unleash their fiery powers to make performances pop to life. They often wear headphones to lower the volume around them and would experience headaches without them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME reside inside volcanos or near pools of lava, basking in their heat. If the temperature falls below 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit, they will be thrown into a fit of rage.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME thrives on chemical energy from hydrothermal vents found deep underwater. It is rarely seen on land, except near volcanic craters.
author: sonicdestroyer12

entry: POKENAME howls happily outside of its volcanic den on moonlit nights. Should someone wonder too close it will dispatch them with a swift Flame Wheel.
author: .izik

entry: Proud of both its physique and its flame prowess, POKENAME puts on shows for any who would watch. Between flexing poses and plumes of fire exhaled in a variety of shapes, it makes for quite the spectacle.
author: sk372

entry: Its body is made of burning igneous rock. POKENAME will spew molten rock at anyone it finds a threat, even though it can't shoot very far.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME carves homes near rich coal deposits underground. It devours the coal to stoke the blazing fire burning in its belly.
author: .izik

entry: It gets its energy by immersing itself in lava, so it doesn't need to eat or drink. If you see a wild POKENAME galloping away from a volcano, it is a sure sign that the volcano is going to erupt soon.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's competitive nature means all three heads try to one-up the other in fire prowess. Some have even observed the heads angrily breathing flames on each other when competition gets too heated.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are found living in and around magma pools surrounding northern volcanoes. These Pokémon have thick, fire-resistant fat that allows them to swim in the boiling lava lakes, as well as the ice-bound waters of the north.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: A sulfuric stench and honking laugh are signs of a nearby POKENAME. It feeds on flammable vapors, and may cause deadly explosions.
author: robosoup

entry: This shiny POKENAME has a more sickly-sweet odor, compared to its sulphuric counterparts. Certain chemical pollutants will lead to this color.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME's body is made of superheated gas that can cause third-degree burns with a single touch. It grabs onto foes before breathing flames on them.
author: .izik

entry: The rocks that make up its body are incapable of melting, even if submerged in magma. POKENAME tends to live deep below the surface, mostly under active volcanoes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME feed on plant sap, using their viciously sharp teeth to bite through even the thickest wood to get to their food. They have powerful pincers on their back that they use to deter predators from attacking them whilst they're feeding.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It crushes berries with its tight grip. It prefers berries that haven't ripened because they are more difficult to juice.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grab onto foes with their large pincers and then explode in a series of sparks. Unfortunately, the explosion leaves them dizzy for a while afterwards, so if they don't defeat their opponent on the first try, they likely won't get a second.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME clusters under leaf piles. Only its chief head has pincers, which it uses to command the rest of its cluster through sharp telepathic pulses.
author: .izik

entry: A unique Exeggcute variant, fused with Pinsir. Those merged with Pinsir consume regular Exeggcute for energy; a mysterious symbiotic relationship.
author: xyloldi

entry: POKENAME is an ambush predator, conserving energy by mimicking a palm tree before using its psychic powers to pull prey into its maw. The large horns act as deterrents against Pokémon seeking to feed on its leafy crown or inert heads.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME subsides on nectar from Pokémon like Victreebel by feeding while staying at a safe distance thanks to its long tongue. The tongue is the majority of its body and is very exposed, so it uses its fierce appearance to scare off threats.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Portions of its shell fall off as it waits for evolution. These pieces are ground up for use in creating X Defense supplements.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME charges down anything smaller than itself in order to bludgeon and fling them with its horn. Once battered and stunned, it pounces and uses its massive weight to pin its prey down beneath it and eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an opportunistic hunter, even residing near Pokémon Centers in order to potentially hunt injured Pokémon. Due to this cruelty, the Chansey line consider it a mortal enemy.
author: sk372

entry: To protect its young, POKENAME places the child in the large, spiked pouch in its belly. The spikes look fierce, but actually are soft enough not to harm the baby POKENAME when it tries to squirm out.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The pincers on POKENAME's wings behave on instinct, clamping down violently on anything that passes through the gap. Though effective for capturing prey, the added weight leaves it grounded and potentially vulnerable to becoming prey itself.
author: sk372

entry: Powerful limbs allow POKENAME to climb up even the most slippery and perilous of surfaces. Prey is grappled with these same limbs until they are unable to move and then are swallowed whole by POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though it possesses decently strong limbs for clubbing foes, POKENAME's true strength lies in clamping them together, possessing a powerful gripping force that crushes its opponent after weakening them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has now developed wings that are as sharp and as deadly as its horns. Flying at blistering speeds, if it misses skewering an enemy with its horns, it slices them with its wings instead.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp wings to slice and weaken foes before finishing them off with its sharp horns. If it can't tear an enemy with its horns, it flies up and crashes down with them to smash them apart.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME use their large pincers to break into breweries and smash open barrels. They are particularly fond of mead and other sweet drinks, which helps build up reserves for their evolution.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These Pokémon aren't picky eaters; they will devour anything edible. Farmers hate POKENAME because they eat entire crops and carry away farm Pokémon.
author: mrbapcik

entry: It hides on beaches, trapping any unsuspecting foe it finds with its pincers. It rarely moves, as its shell is very heavy.
author: imagine1.

entry: They are known to bite onto barrels in mead breweries, tapping into the drink on the inside. They depressurize the barrel, which allows them to drink a bitter but nutritious liquid.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's stomach is directly fed by the gigantic mouth that rips through its entire body. This large mouth is capable of swallowing most Pokémon whole.
author: soup1900

entry: Mead brewers who encounter a POKENAME infestation will hire exterminators, as they are aggressive and hostile. They are known to jab holes into barrels to access the sweet liquid inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives as deep in the most remote forests as possible in an attempt to avoid humans and other Pokémon. It uses telekinesis to lift aggressors up and draw them towards its pincers, which crush them with ease.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME feels threatened, it sets the spiked horns on its back ablaze. It feeds through a mouth that extends through its belly, favoring a diet rich in resin and ripe berries.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many POKENAME will scout the land, searching for large prey. Once a POKENAME has spotted a suitable target to feed the whole nest, the entire group of POKENAME will run the Pokémon down, using their large mandibles to crush the foe into submission.
author: firefist738

entry: POKENAME's spiky limbs can slam together with great force. The moment it senses something gets caught in its webbing, it descends quickly to crush the struggling prey in an instant.
author: sk372

entry: Once within range, POKENAME will paralyze its target. It will slowly consume the prey using its massive maw lined with hundreds of hooked teeth.
author: _testrun_

entry: With POKENAME now in a larger form, it may choose to plant itself in more dangerous hunting grounds. Intentionally off-putting mimicry draws prey, large and small, in closer to investigate, where it then lunges with powerful, crushing jaws.
author: arcul

entry: POKENAME are blind and rely on scent to navigate. When with others of their kind, they cough up a gel that informs others to not bite them. A test of character involves being covered in this gel then standing in a POKENAME nest: safe but terrifying.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are blind and rely on scent to navigate. When with others of their kind, they cough up a gel that informs others to not bite them. A test of character involves being covered in this gel then walking into a POKENAME nest, safe but terrifying.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its gaping mouth may seem ominous, but POKENAME is actually very polite. However, it is prone to tripping and ramming its horns through furniture.
author: beespoon

entry: POKENAME feed on tree sap, using their viciously sharp teeth to pierce through even the thickest of tree bark to get to their food. They use the horns on their head to spar with one another, prying other POKENAME off the best feeding spots.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME feed on tree sap, using their viciously sharp teeth to pierce through even the thickest of tree bark to get to their food. They use the horns on their head to spar with one another, prying other POKENAME off the best feeding spots.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is known for burying its body in forests and emerging to pierce its victims as a painful trap. It feeds on smaller Bug-type Pokémon nightly.
author: samu_games

entry: Whether it aims to pinch or flip its opponent varies on a tactical basis. When two POKENAME fight, they will always choose opposite tactics.
author: staghorn

entry: The pincer that protrudes through the head of POKENAME has caused it's vision to be reduced. It struggles to find food because of this.
author: toxicrown

entry: POKENAME only expose their horrific mouths before they consume prey or to scare away others. Their shells are harder than solid rock.
author: infinex21

entry: It lives in underwater caves where it uses its tentacles to harpoon prey before devouring them. This Pokémon has inspired countless terrifying tales, especially popular among sailors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME blend into dusty trails with their taupe scales and only expose themselves when they ambush prey. They unhinge their jaws to open their many mouths wide enough to swallow prey whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its torso mandibles to devour prey and digest it into milk. Due to this digestion process, POKENAME's milk is considered a meat product.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME crushes geodes with its massive pincers to feast on the glowing crystals inside. It leaves behind piles of cracked stone in mountain passes.
author: .izik

entry: With pincers strong enough to bend hard metals, POKENAME rampage forests for honey. They're known for pairing up with Heracross fusions, due to POKENAME relying on them to crack open trees for tree sap.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME utilizes its progenitor's faux tears in tandem with its innate mimicry to lure curious prey in close. When the prey enters striking range, it uses powerful jaws to crush and tear.
author: arcul

entry: A frightening creature of the deep woods, POKENAME uses its pincers and countless tentacles to bind and crush prey for consumption. It's not uncommon to see it holding a few struggling creatures in its tentacles to save for later.
author: sk372

entry: It has the ability to climb all sorts of surfaces, even vertical ones, thanks to the microscopic hooks on its feet and the claws on its hands. It must rest somewhere flat, however, due to the large pair of pincers it carries.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are respectful creatures that enjoy sparring with other wild Pokémon to improve their combat prowess. Whenever they meet a Trainer, they bow so low that their pincer touches the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME in the wild hovers around abandoned Pinsir nests, usually clinging to nearby trees. It's said if one disturbs the empty home, POKENAME will open its body and suck the interloper's soul away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp teeth to shred bark and lap up sap. While feeding, small venomous spines rise from its back to ward off potential threats.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME camouflages, its mouth and teeth cannot change color, so it must use the scenery even more to blend in. It is nearly impossible to see when it feeds since it uses its teeth to chew into a tree for sap while blending in with the bark.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME fully condensed into its shell upon fusion, which makes burrowing and hiding easier. It uses electromagnetism to regulate body temperature.
author: entomoxie

entry: Dark power surges from this small, near immobile Pokémon. The vortex is filled with the teeth of countless different Pinsir, endlessly spinning.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: While drinking sap from cedar trees, POKENAME's back pincers snap rhythmically. If POKENAME is provoked, they deliver a venomous pinch strong enough to paralyze.
author: .izik

entry: The claw on POKENAME can crush anything it grabs with 5,000 pounds of pressure. It creates a border of decimated trees to outline its territory.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's manic grin signifies its intent to hunt something. Aggressive in behavior, it charges down anything standing between it and its prey using the incredibly tough horns on its equally-durable skull.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME typically is classified as an herbivore, but there are rare and specific cases where it may prey on other Pokémon. It creates enormous burrows underneath sturdy trees to act as a nest to raise its young.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME use their large, long maws to scare their opponents. Their tails are strong enough to send a boulder flying.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME typically is classified as an herbivore, but there are rare and specific cases where it may prey on other Pokémon. It becomes inactive during the cold season and remains in hiding underground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spars with others in its pack during play, using careful pincer strikes. These mock battles rarely injure, but they help build dominance hierarchies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME would be an excellent tool for logging and demolition, if it wouldn't claim the limbs of all those attempting to wield it.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Using its blade to cut logs and its shield to scoop up leaves, POKENAME can log and clear an entire forest within an hour. The strength and durability of a POKENAME can be determined by the thickness of the prongs of its blade.
author: soup1900

entry: A single prick from POKENAME's venomous pincers causes vivid hallucinations of long-lost loved ones. Some cultures believe these visions reveal fated futures.
author: .izik

entry: It attacks by charging pincers-first towards its targets. Its large mouth allows it to swallow most prey in a single bite.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly territorial Pokémon that does everything to protect its family members. Its massive spiked horns are stronger than iron, allowing it to face any battle with pride.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swallows its prey whole, incinerating them in its oven-like stomach. If buried in the ground, it is often mistaken for a volcano.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME displays immense strength, able to destroy whole trees with its mouth and pincers. Feared in stories for its massive size and unnerving look, it roams deep forests and hunts anything it considers prey.
author: riel.vndxgrxvnd

entry: POKENAME has swift swordplay with the mandible on its hand. It also has dozens of thorny whips, as thin as silk, concealed on its body.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Despite its fearsome appearance, it only feeds on rotting logs. Its ravenous appetite makes it an excellent decomposer.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME darts through tree canopies with blinding speed. When it finds a sweet tree, it rams it to crack the bark and drinks the sap inside.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats above cedar trees before slashing them open with its pincers. It drinks sap greedily, using its rear limbs to swat away intruding bugs.
author: .izik

entry: A violent Pokémon with a voracious appetite, POKENAME can easily handle three foes at once by clamping down on each of them between its two mouths and its set of horns.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME use their large pincers to capture and constrict their opponents before blasting them with a beam of pure electricity loosed from their mouths. Due to how their bodies are structured, they are able to gallop swifter than a Ponyta.
author: infinex21

entry: During a Pokémon battle, POKENAME crush their opponents with their toothy appendages. If they fail to crush through shells or armor, they slam their opponents into the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When enraged, POKENAME's pincers glow red hot. It can unleash intense flames from its mouth that are hot enough to melt steel on contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to the undersides of fishing boats using its pincers. It travels long distances this way, seeking new coral-rich feeding grounds.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its jagged maw, POKENAME is entirely herbivorous. When it emerges from its underground nest, POKENAME's appearance greatly scares people and Pokémon alike.
author: mepp.

entry: From high tree branches, POKENAME scans the forest with its aura. When a weak target rests, it leaps down and strikes with precise pincer blows.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bounds across the battlefield with restless energy. Its pincers snap repeatedly as it builds momentum before launching into combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME devours small Pokémon and prefers other Bug-types; it especially loves to feast on Surskit. POKENAME is particularly clumsy at anything beyond swimming in a straight line with its mouth open, especially when first fused.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Each of POKENAME's gears contains a single spiky horn. It rotates quickly when near prey to slam these horns together and crush its target beneath their powerful pressurized grip.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME clings to maple branches and drinks sap with its pincers. If a predator approaches, it releases its grip and explodes without hesitation.
author: .izik

entry: Their pincers are strong enough to crack open the shells of some Pokémon. POKENAME clatter their fangs together to perform echolocation due to their lack of eyes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hides under mud or leaves waiting to zap prey by biting its charged teeth on their ankles. Especially daring POKENAME hang from trees using the pincers to drop on the heads of passing victims.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Due to its eyes having become extra mouths, it is now blind. However, it is also agressively hungry, and will try and eat whatever it can grab.
author: skymaster426

entry: The venom inside POKENAME's pincers carries a strong lavender scent. It's rare and highly prized for use in luxury perfumes and exotic colognes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clamps onto cliffs with its pincers to sleep. If startled, it releases its grip and rolls away with incredible speed to escape danger.
author: .izik

entry: To impress a female and intimidate other rival males, a POKENAME will rear up and display the rows of teeth located along its neck and belly. If the rival won't back down, it will attack, biting down and injecting poison through its fangs.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME obscure their faces to hide their jagged mouths. When they demask, they attack viciously with shear-like claws.
author: .towerxvi

entry: POKENAME hide in tall grass where they can easily ambush small Pokémon. Once their hooked teeth latch onto something, it becomes difficult to remove them without getting a tooth stuck.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is fiercely territorial on the dance floor, attacking others to steal the spotlight. Its talons leave deep scratches in the flooring wherever it performs.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When cheering others on, POKENAME creates a sharp whistle by curling its teeth into a chamber in its mouth. Sadly, its large horns often block it from lifting its arms fully in the air, interrupting its routine.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME sharpens the keratin clumps near its waist with its beak to form thorns. Some even carve patterns into them with their nails, which are also honed by constant pecking.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Though POKENAME's body is tough, its wing flags are fragile and often tear in battle. Luckily, they can repair themselves naturally within a day.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's appearance, especially its rows of serrated teeth, unnerves even the most daring individuals. Despite this, it typically avoids any interaction with humans out in the wild.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME drools constantly, its saliva smelling like Aguav Berries. This attracts small bug Pokémon, which it ambushes with a swift and brutal Guillotine.
author: .izik

entry: These bug Pokémon are incredibly territorial. They live within cold caves and can breathe a frigid mist that will freeze any prey solid before swallowing them whole.
author: infinex21

entry: After feeding on sap, POKENAME scatters spores in the tree bark. These fungi spread rapidly, turning entire trunks into hidden mushroom farms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is known as one of the most dangerous Pokémon, as no matter how large the opponent may be, it never backs down from a fight, striking with a barrage of massive horns along its head and its terrifyingly elongated jaw.
author: rock_rock_rock

entry: POKENAME parasitizes trees by planting spores after drinking sap. While touching infected trees, it can detect footsteps from up to five miles away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its massive pincers to break driftwood into pieces. It shares meals with its swarm while a few stand watch for danger nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its horns and teeth to chew through thick trees and branches. Large armies of POKENAME are used by logging companies.
author: mistymagius

entry: Swarms of POKENAME usually arrive in a cloud of poisonous dust that chokes out all forms of plant life. Once they pick their prey, they will tear them apart with their serrated jaws, leaving no remains behind.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's horns produce an incredibly nutritious honey that is highly sought after by bakers. If POKENAME is fed a diet of medicinal herbs, the healing properties of these leaves are transferred into the honey.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: While digging underground, POKENAME uses its strong pincers to break open tree roots. It favors maple trees for their rich sap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an effective pet for homes that have a tendency towards insect problems. It waits until a bug nest is nearly full, then pounces and inhales the whole colony into its maw in a bountiful feast.
author: sk372

entry: Nothing makes POKENAME happier than the shiny pearl on its head. It has a tendency to hold onto the pearl too tightly, so it has to replace it regularly.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It roots around for spicy berries during colder seasons for warmth. The spice gives it a headache, however, which causes psychic power to surge and results in felled trees and branches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's terrifying visage spells doom for any insects in the vicinity. The small bugs get inhaled into its massive mouth before being incinerated by the flames within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dwells by ponds as an omnivore, eating nectar and scraps from predators. Its body is still developing, so POKENAME avoids taking on foes that firmly outclass it, but it outwardly shows no fear whenever it can.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses high-pressure water jets to blast open tree trunks. Once the bark splits, it eagerly drinks the sap stored inside.
author: .izik

entry: It employs brutal methods for complete victory. In addition to crushing grapples and thrusts of its pincers, it may toss the foe far into the sky and then wait for them to land until they are no longer able to move.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Some towns tell stories of POKENAME taking loose teeth under pillows and replacing them with Pokédollars. According to the tales, cavity-filled teeth are consumed by the mouth on their torsos, and no money is given.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's mouth acts similarly to a paper shredder, allowing it to shred through thick plant matter with ease. Gardeners will often use POKENAME to get rid of excess plant waste.
author: mistymagius

entry: Everything it eats is absorbed by the Shellder on its tail. It latches onto riverbanks with its pincers and devours anything that floats past.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's pincers are made of dense, fused feathers. With enough speed, they can crack open boulders in a single synchronized strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME terrifies children with its many teeth, each sharpened to a point. It instills a sense of dread that carries onto a person's dreams, which become full of bad dentist visits and teeth falling out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is said to be the wandering spirit of a slain bug Pokémon. Its wraithlike body makes an ominous susurrus that can be heard when it is close. It remains motionless until it sees a living thing, at which point it will immediately attack.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME is said to be the wandering spirit of a slain bug Pokémon. Its wraithlike body makes an ominous susurrus that can be heard when it is close. It attacks by lashing out with a severed horn that's thought to be from its living body.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME grips trees with its powerful pincers and shakes them to knock down fruit. It then shares the fruit with other Pokémon in the area.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME grips trees with its powerful pincers and shakes them to knock down fruit. It then shares the fruit with other Pokémon in the area.
author: noel5229

entry: If it sees someone picking on the weak, POKENAME intervenes by blowing a stinging powder at them. It has a very gentle nature; it uses its horns to crash into tree trunks and give the fallen fruit to other Pokémon in the area.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are very aggressive and will headbutt anything that moves. However, their carapace isn't tough enough to resist the sheer amount of blunt force, so POKENAME is constantly covered in bruises.
author: mistymagius

entry: When angered, the five outer eggs rotate around the center, creating psychic energy that levitates POKENAME in the air and allows it to charge forward to headbutt the target of its ire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wear skulls as helmets to protect themselves from danger, but these skulls often block parts of their vision. Whenever they go charging at something, they often trip because of this obscured vision.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When its temper flares in combat, it becomes relentless. It won't stop chasing and striking a target until it's unconscious or POKENAME's bone club shatters and it's forced to find a replacement.
author: sk372

entry: The tongue-like organs on its head let POKENAME touch objects to discern if they would be tasty or not. Non-tasty objects that get licked will be batted away with a swing of POKENAME's head.
author: sk372

entry: When their many tails are not enough to keep Bug-Type Pokémon from landing on them, they swat the pests away with their tongue. By staying in close-knit herds, they can help the young and elderly keep pests off their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will rock back and forth, ramming their shells into each other in a fight for dominance. To onlookers, these battles are extremely anticlimactic.
author: santon5512

entry: The fusion of Rhyhorn and Tauros has given it a massive horn to better charge at foes with. However, it often charges into things and gets itself stuck, the new horn lodged deep within the object it crashed into.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME designates its territory as no-conflict zones. Should it spy infighting from any people or Pokémon, it aggressively charges and ends the fight by knocking them out with its heavy egg and powerful Headbutt.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an extremely aggressive and territorial fusion that often protect herds of Miltank. Unfortunately, they may become protective of domesticated Miltank and rampage against farmers; removing these POKENAME can be quite the ordeal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It furiously charges at others that come to close to flower fields it has claimed, especially other POKENAME. Should two POKENAME clash, they headbutt each other until one is left knocked out among the flowers.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME charges at its opponent, its coarse mane builds up static electricity. This Pokémon is commonly found in badlands.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME have naturally durable leather that many leatherworkers use to produce handbags and belts. However, their prickly horns scare away most poachers from hunting them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many people attempt to ride a wild POKENAME, so many in fact that it has become a spectacle to watch. It is said that if a POKENAME doesn't buck you off, it sees you as an equal, allowing the rider to catch it.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME meat is tender and succulent with hints of smoky flavor. It is said to be especially delicious when paired with soy sauce to bring out its natural savor.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are herbivorous insects that are most often found in thriving grasslands. Their body is filled with bitter and poisonous fluid, so predators stay away from them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Similar to certain breeds of Tauros found in Paldea, POKENAME can swim by using its tails as a propeller.
author: musicsheep.

entry: When angered, POKENAME's mane will set ablaze. While the fire burns, POKENAME violently thrashes until either the fire dies out or it faints.
author: musicsheep.

entry: If a POKENAME appears on your computer, move the cursor slowly. Moving too quickly will be seen as a challenge, leading to POKENAME charging across the screen and potentially causing major damage to one's data.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can't move any of its body parts, as it can only watch angrily. Beware, because when they finally evolve, they'll remember everything with a photographic memory and will look to destroy anything that angered them during this stage.
author: epping_forest

entry: An infamously violent Pokémon, POKENAME uses its pronged tail to anchor itself while it slams into trees to knock them over. It preys on the tree-dwelling Pokémon that scatter from the branches afterwards.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME is extremely temperamental and territorial, but far too lazy to actually attack anyone. It simply glares at interlopers from afar.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: POKENAME can't move any of its body parts, as it can only watch angrily. Beware, because when they finally evolve, they'll remember everything with a photographic memory and will look to destroy anything that angered them during this stage.
author: epping_forest

entry: Escaping the range of its sting is nearly impossible. It will go after disrespectful opponents, stronger Pokémon taking advantage of the weak, weak ones allowing it to happen, beautiful and ugly creatures, and, most of all, the color red.
author: epping_forest

entry: Angry at the world, POKENAME immediately flies straight into anything that it deems a threat. It constantly judges its surroundings to determine if it should prepare for another battle.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its spiky mane ignites when POKENAME gets mad. Due to its belligerent tendencies, this happens often, and when it does, most Pokémon run away in fear. The fire on its body can blaze at over 500 degrees Celsius.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME will try to ram themselves into anything, even though their bodies are so light they don't do much damage. Their horns are still developing.
author: mistymagius

entry: Just before charging its enemies, POKENAME releases electric sparks from the fluff covering its body. Its horns are so strong that they can even break rocks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME coats its horns with electricity to make its ferocious charges even more fearsome. It only allows people who have earned its complete trust to shear its thick wool.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME enter a visceral rage whenever they see the color red. Their sharp talons attack the source of the color, often ripping apart clothing in the process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their tail-like arms as whips, keeping predators at bay. Farmers often use these Pokémon to help herd cattle, their rock-hard bodies able to tank charges.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME look like mishapen Politoed, but don't let their small size fool you. These Pokémon have short tempers, aggressively attacking anyone that gets near. They let out a loud, deep croak, calling in herds of their kind to help aid their attack.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME will scrounge through dumpsters in search of food. They can easily drive away other scavengers with their aggressive temperament.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME attacks by using its tails like a whip with sudden and surprising force. It is herbivorous and lives in the grassy highlands.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Sunlight is crucial to POKENAME's well-being, but care must be taken to ensure it doesn't absorb too much; if it does, it overheats and goes on a rampage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will flick its tails when angry, shooting a mild poison, a warning to those nearby to stop irritating it. Despite its small size, there have been several recorded instances of brutal goring.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME cannot see due to its mane covering its eyes. It can sense light through its fur, allowing it to attack opponents by sensing their shadow.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME keep predators away from their herd by whipping them with sharp tentacles that resemble tails. Particularly persistent predators get blasted with a poisonous pollen that causes any cuts to sting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Since POKENAME is always hungry, it spends most of its day searching for food to eat or stockpile. If anyone approaches its hoard, it flies into a rage and charges with full ferocity, striking with its rock-hard horns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Both heads have the same size brain and the same urge to charge at intruders. It's not unheard of to see a POKENAME rapidly charging forward and backward as both heads struggle for control.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME attempts to charge down and smash anything in sight with its sturdy shelled body. If a target manages to outrun it, it can launch detachable horns at high velocity to strike from long distances.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its three tails and its resilient skull to help it knock down and grab berries to consume. The berry juice its body creates has a strong bitter aroma and taste.
author: sk372

entry: Combative and stubborn, POKENAME patrol their large territories to make sure no rivals are making their home nearby. When they do encounter a rival, they use their massive horn and powerful club-like fists to battle for the territory.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If a member of its swarm is injured, POKENAME flies into a furious rampage. Its horn strikes can flatten trees by the hundreds before it tires.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of delivering devastating, ice-powered blows with their bludgeoning weapon. They are incredibly agile in battle.
author: theartemis1

entry: Its powerful sense of smell allows it to easily find food within even the densest forests. If any of its hoarded food is stolen, it will fly into a destructive rage.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are haughty Pokémon that enjoy teasing other members of their herd with their electrified tails. The shocks from their tail are quite weak so other herd members usually ignore them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It calls down bolts of lightning when it stomps its powerful hooves against the ground. Anything caught upon or between its horns will be quickly met with powerful jolts of electricity before being thrown aside.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME swings among trees claiming entire forests as its territory. Highly aggressive, it descends on any intruders and beats them mercilessly with the palms on its three tails.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in prairies. It flies low over the ground as it follows the Grass-type Pokémon it preys upon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is highly temperamental and unpredictable. During a tantrum, it charges around wildly until all its energy is spent.
author: mepp.

entry: It is not a very fast Pokémon, but it is extremely defensive. It whips foes with its three tails and rams into them with its horns.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME were once hunted for their leather hide and made into shoes by cobblers. With the advent of plant leather, they now roam freely in plains and fields.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME whip members of their herd with their electrical tails to cause stampedes. As members of their herd are galvanized by the shock, POKENAME direct the direction of the stampede to protect the herd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When fighting, POKENAME covers its hard hooves with burning flames to make its attacks even more devastating. It gets irritated easily, so it is advisable to proceed with extreme caution in its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live together in a herd and dig a system of wide tunnels that are only outdone by hardworking Diglett. They roll around in dirt to rid themselves of any attached pests.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME displays leaves on its horns when angered. It is not recommended to approach POKENAME when it is displaying this warning sign.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Leatherworkers once made POKENAME into hats and clothing, but nowadays they roam freely in frigid environments. Their large bodies and warm fur allow them to endure subzero temperatures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes its home in the forest where there are plenty of thick trees for it to ram during its rampage. If there are no suitable trees, it will stampede in a circle out of frustration, often getting stuck in this loop.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME are often used by farmers to help herd runaway cattle. Despite their small size, they can wrangle creatures weighing more than a ton.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is extremely sensitive to the emotions of others, able to passively sense them within a certain radius. At the slightest presence of anger, it flies into a rage and attempts to ram anyone nearby.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME taunts larger opponents with its cape. When the opponent charges, POKENAME swiftly dodges and attacks.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Hidden in POKENAME's tail, many tiny barbs contain a mild poison that causes skin irritation. In battle, it charges in circles around the opponent, hoping to clip them with its horns or brush them with its barbed tail.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is usually quite docile, but it will fiercely stand its ground if it thinks its young is in danger. Its horns are sharper during mating season.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite its body being docile, the mouth on POKENAME's head is always agitated and tries to gnaw anything in its path. POKENAME is often domesticated for its tough dark-brown hair.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its head is covered by an extremely solid metal mask that allows it to ram any surface without injury. POKENAME clashes with others of its kind to prove its strength and claim leadership.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its head is covered by an extremely solid metal mask that allows it to ram any surface without injury. POKENAME clashes with others of its kind to prove its strength and claim leadership.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite their reputation for aggression, POKENAME prefer eating berries and fruits. They roam in groups of 5-10 in the wild and are fiercely protective of their herd.
author: azalde

entry: When sensing disaster approaching, POKENAME charges quickly into nearby towns and forcibly pushes and frightens people away from the endangered zone. Though well-meaning, the brute-force method of helping gives it a poor reputation.
author: sk372

entry: Known as the 'Embodiment of Gluttony', POKENAME possesses an insatiable appetite. Its stomach resembles a bottomless pit, and it will rampage endlessly if deprived of food. Once full, it falls into a deep sleep.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Herds of POKENAME are said to wander the cosmos. It is rumored that the strength of their stampedes is capable of altering space and time.
author: antler_zero_

entry: Small Pokémon often use the peculiar landform on its back as a safe training arena. Before charging with its horns, POKENAME stomps the ground so forcefully that it triggers potent tremors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's horns are laced with a weak poison, causing sluggishness in those affected. Even though its legs are small, they are very strong, allowing for fast charges in battle.
author: evilgammon

entry: Though it is mostly content to feed on grass, POKENAME is partial to tree sap. Its serrated blade can saw through the trunks of even the thickest trees when it decides to enter a feeding frenzy.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Herds of POKENAME can be found stampeding across open plains. They are often kept as pets for rodeo herding.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME are often found in the workforce of local police due to their intolerance for immoral actions. POKENAME occasionally patrol areas by their lonesome to discreetly hunt for all sorts of criminals, from petty vandals to Team Rocket members.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME electrifies its horns before charging at full speed. It is an extremely proud Pokémon that is difficult to tame and train.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When all three stars on its tails glow, it means it is furious and about to unleash its full ferocity. POKENAME stamps its hooves on the ground to generate violent electric shockwaves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Herds of POKENAME play by locking their horns in play fights. They have high stamina and can run for hours without rest.
author: melodydelune

entry: Enraged easily, POKENAME charges directly at the source of its ire. Once it makes contact, it uses its tails to relentlessly strike its target.
author: bacondlx

entry: The angrier POKENAME gets, the more heated its body becomes. If angered enough, its many tails ignite to become a blazing inferno that propels it forward and makes its charge attacks even more devastating.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can release spores from openings on their horns. The angrier a POKENAME, the more noxious the spores. Their hooves and horns are tougher than iron.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's already aggressive nature is exacerbated if it witnesses badly-behaved children. Its zipper-mouth opens up to let loose an otherworldly bellow just before it attacks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tend to live in large herds with each other. Whenever any in the herd are hurt or threatened, the entire herd is quick to strike back.
author: entomoxie

entry: Wild POKENAME have only been naturally found in desolate badlands west of the Unova region. For a trusted Trainer, they can carry many people, Pokémon, and supplies. To anyone else, they'll drive after them at full speed.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME are very territorial and will viscously whip anyone who comes near. The whips can get quite hot and will leave nasty burn-like scars on the victim's body.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a cute yet rustic look that makes them a great candidate for petting zoos. Their aggressiveness gets dampened by all the affection they receive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's broad wings allow it to swoop down on its prey with unmatched speed. A pair of iron-hard horns atop its head are used to strike foes and prey alike, with enough force to topple even the trees in its path.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Due to the fur over its eyes, POKENAME has poor vision. It instead relies on its strong sense of smell to perceive intruders to charge down and nail with the sharp horns on its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is considered one of the wildest of animals, rampaging violently and indiscriminately. POKENAME has even been observed thrashing and lashing out in its sleep, never stopping its perpetual raging.
author: sk372

entry: You can tell a POKENAME is angry by the pitch of its song. Its voice drops to a whisper when it is about to charge.
author: mrpeach774

entry: POKENAME uses the flames on its tails to heat the horns on its head, making it even more dangerous. Although it has a very impulsive temperament, it can be quickly calmed in the presence of sweet-tasting food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The flowers on POKENAME's arms emit a fragrance that temporarily affects the level of various hormones in those who catch the scent. This causes the victim to have heightened levels of both anger and engagement in unnecessary risk-taking.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will clash with each other in the air, often fighting until one is knocked from the sky. At night, they will seek out sleeping herds of Tauros, piercing their thick hide with their fangs before consuming their blood.
author: santon5512

entry: Brave and headstrong, it rushes into battle without thinking. Its club and horns are made of the same material, using them to break through earth and rock to mark its territory.
author: silverscloudy

entry: It is usually asleep. It absorbs the life force of those in its domain, little by little. If awakened, it flies into a rage and lashes out at anything nearby.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wings are too fluffy and delicate to be washed in water, otherwise its feathers will get moldy from the moisture trapped beneath them. Instead, this Pokémon cleans itself with the sand and dust from under its hooves whenever it runs.
author: milchik

entry: Despite their intimidating appearance, POKENAME are quite gentle, usually seen lumbering slowly next to their Trainer. Should their Trainer stumble, POKENAME will react with quick reflexes to prevent a fall.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is quick to anger and has no issue charging full force at anyone that irritates it. It will even grab its opponents to smash them into any hard surface it desires.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its charging tackle isn't very strong on its own, but the mushrooms on its back release spores on impact that weaken the muscles of its foe, leaving them more susceptible to follow-up headbutts.
author: sk372

entry: Fusion has given POKENAME the rampaging temper of Tauros with Lycanroc's agility and focus. This makes it much more dangerous when angered, as its quick movements make avoiding its charge next to impossible.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME habitats have put up signs warning travelers about its presence. Tourists falsely confuse its cute, wide-eyed appearance for innocence, when it is actually quite aggressive towards strangers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are easy to enrage with any sudden, physical contact; even a hard nut falling upon one's head would enrage it. They emit thick smoke as they thrash around, their hooves burning so hot that they sear the ground.
author: infinex21

entry: While POKENAME's sting isn't life-threatening, its venom can cause excruciating pain lasting over three days. Unless provoked, it only seems to target Tauros and Miltank.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME love to charge at each other, but their heads are so soft that they bounce off each other. They spin their tails as they run, leaving the smell of oil, caramelised onion, and grilled meat behind them.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: While usually found on farms, farmers prefer other Pokémon for field work. POKENAME has little patience and may abandon tasks suddenly, lashing out in a fit of rage.
author: jangodiot

entry: The garden atop POKENAME are made up of seeds from whatever they eat. The hump stores rainwater caught, keeping both POKENAME and their plants nourished.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME, when placed in a farm, has consistently taken the role of herding other cattle Pokémon. They are most happy when assisting others or working.
author: ohok3441

entry: In the wild, POKENAME have been found in herds of various Pokémon, even species that are more solitary. Many have even been spotted with various plant Pokémon growing in their head dish.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME uses the flames on its tails to heat the horns on its head, making it even more dangerous. Although it has a very impulsive temperament, it can be quickly calmed in the presence of sweet-tasting food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Trainers need to be wary of standing behind POKENAME, as these temperamental creatures whip anyone behind them with their flaming tails. They are often remorseful after the fact.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME travels in large herds while tunneling across prairies. Their constant churning of soil greatly improves plant growth.
author: .izik

entry: Fast food restaurant in Kanto and Hoehn sometimes have signs warning about POKENAME, who to the untrained eye might be confused for a normal hamburger. They enjoy eating fried potatoes, often stealing them from customers if left alone.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's formidable muscle strength is tied to its temper. It will sometimes pull on its own tail to hurt and anger itself in order to get a power boost in battle.
author: sk372

entry: When threatened, POKENAME will crack its vines like a whip to scare off its attacker. It will also use it vines to swing from trees and to catch it prey like a lasso.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME migrate across plains and paddle across rivers with their legs and tail to reach greener pastures. They let out a satisfied cry and kick their hooves into the air after completing their yearly journey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The rare POKENAME is always found carrying a birch stick with leathery whip-like ends. It has no problem using it in combat; POKENAME shows as much skill at repairing the branch as it has skill in wreaking havoc on foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It will aggressively charge at anything encroaching its territory. Its two heads may lock on to different targets to chase down, leading to sudden and erratic direction changes mid-charge.
author: sk372

entry: Its three heads are always arguing, thus it is always angry and ready to rampage over the smallest of things. Its rampage tends to end when its three heads ram one another, thus dazing, or knocking out, themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: Many claim it is a haunted Tauros skull that spews toxic gas. If left alone, herds of unsuspecting Tauros may run through the gas, spiking the POKENAME population.
author: lampent12

entry: Some say it is the incarnation of the deadliest Tauros. It haunts pastures, attacking entire herds and driving farmers mad.
author: spagalapof

entry: The bulb growing on its back can absorb impurities from the water, though if POKENAME isn't careful, it risks becoming poisoned itself. Its vines are too thin to lift objects, so they simply dangle from its body without a purpose.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are pitifully weak and worthless in battle, but they are valuable as fishing bait. An entire industry exists for breeding tens of thousands of them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is pathetically weak in battle. However, it is valued as a food, and it is commonly served on top of sushi.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is said to contain enough power to run a small household. Despite its use as a power source, it is unable to turn this energy into attacks.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives in fetid swamps, hiding away from dangerous Pokémon. It ventures out to collect discarded bones to build its nest.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's punches are extremely slow; it takes an entire minute for it to get ready and throw one at an opponent. Its punches are so horribly weak that it will hurt itself if it punches a pillow.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's punches are extremely slow; it takes an entire minute for it to get ready and throw one at a foe. Its punches are so horribly weak that it will hurt itself if it punches a couch cushion.
author: soup1900

entry: Their bodies are too hard for most unevolved Pokémon to pierce through before POKENAME flops away. Unfortunately, nothing stops a swift Flying-type Pokémon from hauling it away to its nest in its thick talons.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME drift around at sea, as their fins are small and are easily washed away by currents. The fin on their head is often mistaken for a crown, and they spit out ink when in danger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wander throughout the ocean. Their fins are large, allowing them to change course as they please. They will eventually have a very large crown fin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are kept in backyard ponds as pets. Their bright orange scales and their yellow horns and whiskers make them popular choices among fish enthusiasts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many Trainers struggle to keep POKENAME as pets due to their large size, as they prefer wide enclosures. As such, having a happy POKENAME is a sign of wealth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME contains what appears to be a Magikarp in the center, controlling its actions. It's thought that POKENAME channels strange energy into it, ensuring a more powerful evolution in its future.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tries to captivate audiences with its dance moves. However, whether on land or in the water, its body movements are too awkward and jittery, so it always fails to impress.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are a placid and weak species that tend to wander aimlessly across plains and farmland, grazing without thought or care. Touching its whiskers will send it into a thrashing rage.
author: sk372

entry: A legendary creature of the sea, restored to its ancient glory through fusion technology. Its power, however, is still weak and pathetic.
author: brienie

entry: POKENAME live on aquatic plants and spend their days underwater hiding amongst the plant fronds. They have poisonous barbs along their back to discourage predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for shiny Gyarados by fishermen. Encountering one is said to be a sign of both good and bad luck.
author: staghorn

entry: This Pokémon is often sold by con artists under the guise that it is a rare red Gyarados. Its true identity can be revealed by its lack of teeth and its orange fins.
author: astral_1447

entry: It likes to help humans across the water, but has weak swimming skills, so it can only ferry a single person at a slow pace. Lapras herds tend to keep POKENAME around out of pity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's frail genetic makeup is easily influenced by outside factors, ruining its ability to adapt in environments. As a result, it struggles to survive anywhere without requiring assistance.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have adapted to be graceful swimmers despite not being very fast. It is said when on land they awkwardly flop about, despite having four working paws. Despite their reputation, researchers speculate their whiskers detect incoming rainstorms.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME are said to have once been fairly strong, however they have grown weaker over decades. They are said to be comprised of water-like molecules which allow them to vanish underwater despite their bright red scales.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME washes up in spam emails, old forums and riverbanks. Criminals use it to get sensitive information, which it hates but is too weak to fight.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME's shell restrains its swimming capabilities, making it a great hindrance rather than a benefit. The shell itself is also soft, making it rather ineffective in defending POKENAME.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's tough shell protects them from most attacks as they float on the water's surface. They are often carried away by Pelipper and Sharpedo due to their lack of mobility.
author: santon5512

entry: Slithering across the ocean floor, POKENAME lack major fins or flippers to help them swim. Their mouths help them travel by biting onto other aquatic Pokémon, latching on and traveling great distances in search of food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon has very weak musculature, but a very hardy body. It will violently flop around and thrash while out of water, but it will not be harmed.
author: ziggaway

entry: Often seen lazing around on the beach, POKENAME sleep for 12 hours a day. While awake, they dive into the ocean to help other aquatic Pokémon find food and shelter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Experiments to fuse a Magikarp with the strongest lifeform were a success. However, it was still not enough to give Magikarp any noteworthy power.
author: brienie

entry: Photographers pose POKENAME during certain holiday festivals due to their resemblance to other Pokémon. They are aloof and uninterested in photo shoots, and so are bribed with berries to focus on the camera.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flock together along the water's edge and will squabble with one another for the best drinking spots. They're fast but weak, their fights rarely causing any lasting damage despite how frenetic they can get.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is an extremely fast swimmer that can jump out of the water and glide many meters before diving back into the depths.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are rotund and squishy, with two long antennae that conduct electricity. At night, POKENAME gather in large groups to produce a dazzling array of lights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is rotund and squishy, requiring electric whiskers for protection. Unfortunately, its electric power is so weak that an attacking predator would feel no more than a faint static tingle, leaving POKENAME effectively defenseless.
author: sk372

entry: Rotund and bipedal, POKENAME has a long tail with a fin at the end, used for both bouncing and swimming underwater. When scared, POKENAME raises its tail above its head to appear larger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Found near lakes and ponds, POKENAME are aloof and sleepy, sleeping up to 18 hours a day. They get angry when anyone pulls their whiskers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gather on the water's surface, feeding on scraps left behind by other Pokémon. When threatened, they inflate the three water bubbles around their bodies and float away on the wind.
author: fancyskunk

entry: Its meat is inedible, and due to its rapid reproduction and adaptability to harsh conditions, POKENAME is an ecological threat. Its overpopulation of water bodies leads to severe eutrophication, making the environment uninhabitable for most Pokémon.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME is a relatively isolated Pokémon that hides high in trees if it feels like it is being threatened. It can blow small gusts of wind to dislodge food from the high places it hides in.
author: dill360yt

entry: POKENAME enjoy lurking in the mud, as it helps keep their skin hydrated. The fins and whiskers can detect early signs of earthquakes through the vibrations in the mud.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME joyfully flops in muddy puddles after heavy storms. If disturbed during playtime, it retaliates with powerful jets of water from its mouth.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have gifted minds, but wasted potentials. They waste their intellect smugly pondering meaningless, useless and senseless topics all day.
author: leeto64

entry: POKENAME are capable of absorbing impurities in water with the flower on their back, which has a yellow tint from their constant use. POKENAME rely on their vines to scare predators away, since the vines make them appear like a big predator.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because POKENAME are so small, they congregate in massive groups of at least 50 individuals. The longer POKENAME live together, the more synchronized their movements become, to the point a large group can appear as a single, large Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's shell is ineffective at protecting it from bird pecks since its fins always stick out. Its explosions can be barely felt even directly next to it, making this attack a non-threat.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is commonly seen around tall waterfalls, using its claws to climb to the top. However, it always gets tired before it can reach its goal.
author: staghorn

entry: Despite their weak muscles, POKENAME stubbornly persist in burrowing ever deeper underground. It is believed that if they go deep enough, the pressure will force them to evolve.
author: .jerden

entry: When hungry, POKENAME tears into fishing nets to feast on the haul within. After long swims, it flops onto rocky shoals and spends several hours drying to avoid oxidizing.
author: amityblamity

entry: Because of its horn, POKENAME often gets stuck between rocks or reefs while swimming, taking several hours to free itself. It has a strong fondness for honey and ripe Berries, which are commonly used as bait to lure it out of the waters it inhabits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's scales are so hot that if they stray from the water for too long, they'll lose their fish-like shape and become a molten puddle until returned to the water.
author: glimmerowo.3024

entry: POKENAME will dip their jowls into rivers to sense potential food. However, they cannot swim, often getting swept away when they try to get food.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME swim together at the surface of placid lakes, honking at one another to communicate. They feed by diving beneath the water and searching for plants, though they are poor swimmers and cannot dive deep.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This weak Pokémon has a remarkable sense of smell. It survives by digging into river mud and gathering smaller prey for sustenance.
author: metalocif

entry: POKENAME gather around underwater hydrothermal vents, which provide a soothing warmth and a place to rest after searching for food. If the sea becomes polluted, the coral stalks become discolored, causing POKENAME pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are fast and precise swimmers, able to snatch a snack out of a sailor's hand high above the ocean's surface. Crowds of POKENAME often appear if food is scattered across the ocean surface.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates a large amount of ink within its body to use as projectiles, but because its mouth muscles are rather weak, the ink only comes out in a copious dark dribble instead.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will house Magikarp in their bags, attempting to care for them. Due to their lack of awareness and poor motor skills, these Magikarp don't typically survive for long.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME lure prey by hiding their body in long grass next to water, moving their tail behind their head and wriggling to appear like a beached Magikarp. When prey comes near, they constrict and swallow it whole.
author: darkwolfe

entry: POKENAME are an aquatic Pokémon species that float in the world's many oceans. Its stomach can expand to hold three times its normal capacity in food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is weak and slow, struggling even in its natural habitat. Despite its aquatic nature, it often has difficulty swimming, floundering on both land and water.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are considerably weak, though their large bodies trick most others into believing differently. They take great pride in how clean they keep their scales and in how long their barbels grow.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has tiny fish Pokémon living in its watery mane. They remove small insect Pokémon and debris from its fur while POKENAME protects them. When this Pokémon gets angry, it boils its mane, accidentally killing the fish in the process.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's abysmal ability to swim results in it often being found drifting along in a current. As it passes through polluted water, it naturally creates a purified path in its wake.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: The tail of POKENAME helps them balance when walking on land. They have trouble swimming with their tail, so POKENAME will usually stay in shallow waters.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME is a devious little ne'er-do-well always intent on casting hexes on others. Fortunately for its victims, its spell-casting ability is rather pitiful, and most of its curses fizzle out uselessly almost immediately.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are completely unable to swim and have been known to drown if unsupervised near water. POKENAME are rumoured to be extinct in the wild, however, so many are kept by Trainers for their appearance that they are not listed as endangered.
author: darkwolfe

entry: POKENAME are often found swimming in icy lakes. However, their bodies are not suited for the cold, leaving them shivering and even frozen solid most of the time.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can perform incredibly high jumps from both water and land, hurling itself miles into the air. Unfortunately, the wind often carries it somewhere far from where it initially hopped, which will cause POKENAME to Splash around in frustration.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME must make do with the leftovers of other Pokémon, as its body is still too weak to swim with any speed. Its only line of defense is the venomous crest on its forehead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often get stuck in tide pools. Their stubby legs don't permit movement on land so they hide in mud, using their toxic spines as protection from coastal predators until the tide rolls back in.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME work at water treatment plants where they are monitored by workers to ensure that people receive safe and drinkable water. The flower on their back constantly filters out impurities and is capable of purifying five liters a minute.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Schools of Magikarp are sometimes protected by one or more POKENAME. They gather stragglers when the group is ready to move, refusing to leave anyone behind.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Its hair-like protrusion mimics a Magikarp, tricking opponents into thinking it's too weak to fight back. However, this often causes more problems for POKENAME than anything else.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a vicious hunter, using its fishing-rod-like appendages to trick other Water-Pokémon. If anything bigger or stronger than it gets hooked and thrashes, POKENAME will be pulled along with the movement as it cannot anchor itself.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME are very weak. Despite being carnivores, they lack appendages to hunt with, causing them to be constantly short of food, with their only form of sustenance being Surskit. However, their outer shell is as hard as stone.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: Despite their large stature, POKENAME are physically unimpressive Pokémon that struggle to perform in battle. They are reliant on their scaly hide to protect themselves but offer little in the way of offense even with their bulk.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite its massive size, POKENAME is lacking in speed, strength and defense. It floats around slowly and aimlessly, only surviving due to predators not bothering to hunt it due to the bland taste of its meat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME puts up the guise of being a grand and powerful Pokémon, able to summon and create anything it wants. In reality, it is extremely weak and powerless, its attacks being even punier than a droplet of water.
author: soup1900

entry: The glass bulb on POKENAME's back usually has baby Magikarp residing in them. Legends say the water can grant eternal life as no one has ever seen a Magikarp die in the bulb.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME's horn is blunted, severely hampering its combat use. It seeks out others of its kind so that it has safety, but often ends up tangled in reeds or kelp.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When POKENAME defends its territory, it can be seen flailing its arms about in an attempt to be intimidating. This attempt is usually unsuccessful.
author: brienie

entry: This legendary warrior once inspired many aquatic combat styles, but is now too weak to fight. It spends its days training Magikarp on its back.
author: squawkabairdy

entry: Despite its weight, POKENAME will flop around frantically. Since it is as heavy as a large rock, carpet cleaners will use POKENAME as an opportunity to have it pound out dusty rugs. Its magnetic body helps in finding metallic debris.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: A legendary and ancient blade, lost deep in the ocean. It is said whoever wields POKENAME will become weaker than ever before.
author: brienie

entry: POKENAME wildly flops when someone tries to pick it up. However, it is so weak that it quickly gives in to being used by local fisherman to gut fish.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Aegislash yearn for battle instinctively. Some have used this trait and taken them to another battlefield, of spice and smell and delicious food.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME are often employed at seafood restaurants, particularly those that serve Magikarp cuisine. Their skill with the blade means that every meal is perfectly cut and portioned.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wiggles its ears and swings its tail in a threatening display to ward off opponents. Once the threat has passed, it collapses from exerting so much energy.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME wishes to take up a blade in defense of the sea. Still, its youth hinders it from seeing real combat.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME have been known to defend the ocean in times of peril. When they are not defending the ocean, they can be found constantly training.
author: brienie

entry: By swimming in circles, POKENAME create whirlpools to drive predators away. They often get themselves caught in them instead, causing them to wash up on nearby beaches.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME have remarkably weak swimming muscles, so they are easily swept away by strong enough currents; as a result, many have been found stranded on shores. Their lower bodies have tough, glossy scales that many adore.
author: infinex21

entry: Though weak in terms of power and speed, they are able to live in any body of water. They use their long whiskers to feel their surroundings.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME slaps the surface of the water to create loud cracking sounds that frighten even fierce predators away. If it is attacked, it dives into the water and speedily swims away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are so rare that very few fishermen have ever laid eyes upon one. This prized fish is still highly sought after, as its meat is praised for its luxuriously exquisite flavor.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can barely control its powers of time, only being able to fast forward or rewind time by a few seconds at once. Any attempts to manipulate time for longer will always fail and may cause it to distort time instead.
author: soup1900

entry: Those who admire their reflection in a pool of water for too long may be spirited away by POKENAME. Wherever it takes you is very wet.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: When angered, POKENAME emerges out of the water to strike down anyone who would bring harm to the environment. Unfortunately, it takes a while to adjust to breathing air, so it needs additional time to splash about and find its bearings.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME waddle out of ponds together under the full moon, splashing through puddles and dancing with one another under the moon's light. If they are disturbed, they run back to their ponds as quickly as they can, fins flapping as they do.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lights up its flame at night to try and attract prey. The act of doing so is exhausting for it, though, so by the time anything is drawn close enough to hunt, POKENAME is too tired to do so.
author: sk372

entry: Its hulking body is controlled by the Magikarp within its core. Despite now being a fearsome fighter, the Magikarp is still vulnerable to Flying-type Pokémon plucking it up and carrying it away.
author: staghorn

entry: After starring in a Pokéstar Studios production, POKENAME became a popular armored superhero mascot. It is portrayed as the protector of all Magikarp, eternally battling its rival Maginette for control of the seas.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: If POKENAME is stepped on, it spits the water inside its body that it swallowed to avoid drying out on land. It then flops back into the ocean to rehydrate before ejecting water to propel itself back to shore.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is a mischievous Pokémon said to steal keys. It is believed that the keys it carries have never successfully opened any lock.
author: brienie

entry: Caught by many Old Rod users, POKENAME has a surprisingly strong swimming ability. However, when kept in a fish tank, it becomes lazy, spending hours sitting on the bottom.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's many large fins give them unmatched speed underwater. Sadly POKENAME are also notoriously slow to react, causing them to often ram headfirst into things at high speed.
author: danarchosyndacalist

entry: When moist, it can travel at 90% the speed of light. However, due to the friction and heat it makes while moving, it dries out in less than a nanosecond.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME are remarkable swimmers with superb control over their various fins and flippers. Due to their elongated form, children enjoy surfing on their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is often described as a sac of air; it ineffectually hops around and may even float through the air when it rains. In this way, it has a widespread population. It does little else.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's rigid, sturdy body gives it strong defense against predators. Unfortunately, its limbs are too weak to hold itself up for long, ruining its mobility on land and practically making it impossible to swim.
author: sk372

entry: They say with great power comes great responsibility; most Trainers think raising POKENAME is too much responsibility and give up before it evolves.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: POKENAME's odd body composition, consisting of gears interlocking at an odd angle, leaves it weak and ill-equipped to function as gears or for swimming. It's considered rather useless as a result.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very easy for fishermen to catch because they swim very close to the surface of the water to stay warm. If their bodies get too cold, their fins stop working, rendering them unable to swim.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME is a weak swimmer who can only flail helplessly in water. However, it can leap over entire waterfalls in a single bound, so Trainers shouldn't dismiss its potential.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Although POKENAME can see properly, it can only seem to move at random. This will usually result in POKENAME colliding with obstacles that get in its way.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME are builder Pokémon capable of building small coral fortresses. They dispute their reefs with the Feeolett, against whom they have been in conflict for centuries.
author: elevn.

entry: Its weak wings cannot maintain flight for long periods of time. A gentle breeze is enough to send POKENAME flying off course for miles.
author: melodydelune

entry: With its evolution, its wing power has increased. Now instead of being flung off for miles by the breeze, it is only yards.
author: melodydelune

entry: Whilst theoretically capable of strong flight with its powerful wings, its atrocious sense of balance means it mostly ends up flapping about uselessly in circles, screaming with impotent rage.
author: occulusmalus

entry: Found in the mud of drained lakebeds, POKENAME is considered one of the most pitiful Pokémon in terms of both strength and appearance. Even as food, they are considered bland and tacky at best.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's favourite snack is big, beautiful gemstones. Unfortunately, its teeth are too weak to crack the jewels, forcing it to instead attempt to swallow them whole, often choking as a result.
author: sk372

entry: In the water, it has a reputation for ferocity and relentlessly chasing its prey. It even chases them onto land, where it will start flopping helplessly.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME are fished up by young anglers in the Kanto region. Expert fishers teach children how to safely remove and toss POKENAME back into the water because their scales can cause itchiness if handled carelessly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its dancing to call forth hundreds of Magikarp. These Magikarp are used to overwhelm enemies by using their sheer quantity, while POKENAME does a flopping-like dance to distract them.
author: soup1900
