entry: POKENAME loves to flop around on abandoned beaches full of trash and other litter. It was forced to adapt to its surroundings due to its weak body constantly getting stuck in discarded plastic bags.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME feed off of discarded scraps of food that get tossed away into trash cans. Whenever they are shocked, they can leap up to two stories into the air to escape capture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though it has ferocious, aggressive tendencies, POKENAME's small teeth are incapable of piercing skin. Unable to properly hunt as a result, it bitterly resorts to being an undersea scavenger instead.
author: sk372

entry: It is so weak that even clouds lift and carry it away. However, due to its many water predators, this is actually beneficial for POKENAME.
author: jreposo

entry: Shiny POKENAME offers a beautiful sight to those lucky enough to spot it between the clouds. Nevertheless, it is just as weak as regular POKENAME.
author: jreposo

entry: It is debatable whether the Magikarp inside POKENAME is controlling it or merely residing in it. Whatever the case, POKENAME reacts with aggression should anyone try to interact with it.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its large size and tenacious grip, POKENAME are disliked by sailors, who have to pry POKENAME off their ships. Despite this, POKENAME continue to latch onto ships to move quickly across the sea.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its large arms to bunker and protect itself from attacks, injecting venom into dangerous Pokémon. Their bright coloration serves as a reminder to predators to avoid POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are said to be the most sought after fusions for fishing enthusiasts, as they can help store or provide a wide variety of equipment. POKENAME rest on shorelines and extend lures out into the water to catch prey and drain their life force.
author: raza

entry: Due to its weak muscles, POKENAME rarely has the strength to lift up its long neck. It communicates by blowing a small amount of slow-moving cold bubbles at others.
author: sk372

entry: The diverse scale patterns of a Magikarp mixed with the temperament and trainability of a Rockruff make POKENAME a surprisingly popular show Pokémon.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME's gasping face is the subject of much ridicule. Though it seems uncomfortable out of the water, it will follow its Trainer anywhere.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's gasping face is the subject of much ridicule. Though it seems uncomfortable out of the water, it will follow its Trainer anywhere.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its garish colors to scare away predators. This often backfires, however, as those same lurid colors make them easy for prey to spot too.
author: quackquackattack

entry: New research has revealed that POKENAME can move at 99.99% the speed of light for a brief moment. Due to low intelligence, it does not realize how fast it was moving until the moment is over.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: When threatened, POKENAME begins to thrash violently, splashing muddy water into a predator's eyes to create an opening for escape.
author: fertve

entry: POKENAME live in shallow ponds, diving as deep as they can if they feel like they're in danger. If their escape fails, they become agitated, fluttering their fins and flopping out of the water in an effort to get from one pond to another.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The taiyaki on POKENAME's head gives off such a delicious aroma that it constantly has to run away because many Pokémon try to eat it. It can often be found panting near a water source, which it needs to keep its scales from drying out.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swim close to the surface of water to keep themselves warm. At night, they sleep in small clusters to preserve their body heat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When it spots a loving couple on the shore, POKENAME leaps from the water and flops helplessly nearby. The reason for this behavior remains a mystery to marine biologists.
author: .izik

entry: Since Luvdisc is a commonly used symbol for romance, POKENAME is usually considered to be a symbol of a less desirable relationship, or one that won't last very long. Still, some groups paint POKENAME as a symbol for a lasting friendship instead.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Since Luvdisc is a commonly used symbol for romance, POKENAME is usually considered to be a symbol of a less desirable relationship, or one that won't last very long. Still, some groups paint POKENAME as a symbol for a lasting friendship instead.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Since Luvdisc is a commonly used symbol for romance, POKENAME is usually considered to be a symbol of a less desirable relationship, or one that won't last very long. Still, some groups paint POKENAME as a symbol for a lasting friendship instead.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME digs in a swimming motion, sturdy scales shed from its body. These scales take years to break down and provide no nutrients to the soil.
author: .izik

entry: If there is a strong wind, POKENAME stays hidden since it is not strong enough to fly. It nests on sea coasts, feeding on shells and seaweed brought to shore by the current.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's wings are too dense to catch winds to fly into the air properly. Any prey it tries to grasp in its beak can easily slip out and swim away from it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is commonly found at the bottom of wishing wells. Some think it believes the coins within contain "wish energy", and that it wants to use that energy to wish to evolve sooner.
author: sk372

entry: Its red fur would be extremely luxurious, but POKENAME's long stays in the water tend to make it frizzy and give it a bad smell. Unfortunately, this Pokémon cannot survive for long outside of saltwater.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It uses its boneless body to slip through small cracks. Sleeping fishermen often awake to a full, sleeping POKENAME in their bait boxes or chum buckets.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It will tug its whiskers during battle in order to enhance the normally weak psychic emanations it produces for its attacks. This leaves it with a splitting headache afterward, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in swamps and lakes, feeding on plants that grow near the bottom. Its poor senses often lead it to swim right into the mouth of hungry Quagsire.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are commonly found flying about near rivers, too weak to avoid being blown about by passing winds. They are commonly employed by fishmongers who tie a leash to them and then to a stall to act as advertising.
author: dualblades1147

entry: POKENAME rolls to get around because it is too weak to swim well. It is often mistaken for a beachball.
author: waltersby

entry: Despite being physically frail, POKENAME are remarkably aggressive and territorial. They will put on fierce displays, mock charging at Pokémon and Trainers alike to try and scare them off before a fight has a chance to happen.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While possessing reasonable physical resilience, POKENAME is nonetheless incredibly weak and slow; it moves no faster in the ocean than it would on land.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME attempting to chain their electricity together end up shocking and damaging themselves instead. Due to this, they end up fighting alone even when in a school, making them easy prey to hunt.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are easily caught by fishermen thanks to their dull intellect, but fishermen have to be careful to not get zapped by them. They were once featured as an electrifying cut of sashimi in magazines and newspapers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's average size and weak attacking power make it defenseless against Pokémon stronger than itself. The flesh of POKENAME, being mildly poisonous, is fortunately enough to deter most potential predators.
author: gileme__

entry: Its beauty and speed, combined with an incredibly obedient nature, make POKENAME a popular mount for children. Its fins can be trimmed harmlessly, making for a popular, if rare, post-ride snack.
author: lycanw_8d

entry: POKENAME are capable of flying a short distance from their aquatic home to look for berries. If they spend too long outside of water, their body temperature rapidly drops, preventing them from flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is naturally a slow swimmer due to its bulbous body, and its movements are limited to its small fins. They avoid predators by confusing them with the spiral on their bellies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While flopping on dry land, POKENAME is utterly helpless. On rare occasions when it balances upright, it unleashes hypnotic waves from its spiraled belly.
author: .izik

entry: Strong and sturdy, sometimes POKENAME in an area will drag each other by the whiskers to assert dominance. POKENAME may drag another across lakes, and even oceans if particularly bulky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are slippery creatures that are hard to pin down. Even when they are caught by fishermen, they always have the option to teleport away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though POKENAME are typically found in weed-choked ponds, heavy rainfall and flooding can displace the Pokémon into streams. Their weak muscles force them to move with the current, and they become easy prey for predators.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME only wants to be friends with other Pokémon. Unfortunately, it has no control over its own feeding instincts, leading it to regularly swallowing anything that comes near, releasing a horrific, shrill scream whenever this happens.
author: occulusmalus

entry: It has weak swimming capabilities, and even the poison of its stingers is incredibly mild, useless for defense. POKENAME often ends up washed up on shore, staring pathetically at passersby.
author: sk372

entry: The bulb on POKENAME acts as a small nursery for aquatic Pokémon. The long golden tentacles guide these baby Pokémon to shelter in the bulb.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clumsily drags itself around a muddy lake bottom, searching for shellfish to eat. With weak muscles and poor fine motor skills, it has been known to spend hours struggling to open a single clam.
author: dylonk25

entry: It is unknown why POKENAME's back half is missing, with scientists believing that its hind legs were eaten away by other Pokémon over time. It doesn't seem bothered by this, as the legs still function the same as if they still had muscles on them.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When at rest, it plays with the whiskers on its face for amusement. Based on reports of POKENAME trying to consume or pull off these whiskers, it's thought that POKENAME does not realize they are a part of its body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an uncaring Pokémon, always staring out into space and not minding anything that happens to it or its surroundings. In contrast, the Shellder on its tail is always ferociously thrashing about and sucking all the nutrients from POKENAME.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME tends to roam about with a comical grace, its two heads arguing over which direction to swim or run. Despite its clumsy appearance, it can surprisingly launch itself high into the air, creating a splash wherever it goes.
author: thepandasharky

entry: It comes onto land to rest, as swimming for too long leaves its muscles weak and exhausted. Observers find its tired and pitiful panting on land rather endearing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often appear as sea buoys at a distance, as they travel in groups and are bright orange in appearance. Their long tails swim quickly out of the way before any collisions occur.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is found in factories near beaches or other bodies of water. They often float atop the water, as they cannot sink.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its blobby, formless appearance is the result of being removed from the pressurized depths it calls home. Surprisingly, this has little effect on its overall well-being.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME latches onto Slowpoke tails like Shellder, though no evolution takes place. Instead, POKENAME uses its host as a way of migrating to a new body of water to reside in, as its own swimming capability is quite weak.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often found along the riverbed, searching for food and shelter. Despite its size, it is considered a weak bottom-feeder.
author: presicho

entry: They burrow in the mud at the bottom of lakes and ponds. They are hardy enough to survive in any body of water, and actually seem to prefer it when the water is dirty.
author: .jerden

entry: Though overall weak, its claws have a strong gripping power. It often uses them to hitch a ride on larger Pokémon while they hunt, grabbing and eating whatever scraps remain afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can only move slowly through dense undergrowth. However, its barbs spread a strong venom, so hikers should be careful in the forest.
author: chorb33

entry: The horn on its head secretes an extremely weak toxin. It can be dangerous in large quantities, but usually it just causes a mild rash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME only uses its legs to climb up trees, preferring to just roll around. The venom it produces is dangerous, but it does cause a paralyzing pain similar to a taser.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a habit of grabbing smaller Bug-Type Pokémon and wielding them as weapons. They are avoided by small Pokémon for fear of being the next one to be picked up.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wield Weedle as weaponry, flailing them around with little regard for their safety. Its thick carapace protects it's from the Weedle's sting.
author: mistymagius

entry: The tips of POKENAME's feet bear venomous spikes, which it uses to weaken foes struck by its kicks. A highly competitive Pokémon, it constantly trains to better itself.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The spike on its head holds an incredibly potent poison. As it gets closer to evolution, the poison becomes more deadly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its big red proboscises to search for toxic mushrooms. It eats said mushrooms to make its poison more potent and vicious.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: Slow-moving and defended only by mildly toxic stingers, POKENAME live in dense kelp growths. They rely heavily on their drab camouflage and lack of sudden movements to avoid drawing attention from predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Since the deep sea lacks leaves for it to eat, POKENAME has turned to a diet of seaweed and moss instead. If attacked, it has the option of either jabbing the assailant with its horn or using its fin to swim away.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME swim in lakes and rivers where their unusually bright scales make them unappealing to predators. Their sturdy horn stings anything that is in front of them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Still physically frail, it evolved extra stingers that secrete and coat the wings with a fine poison to deter predators who would hunt it. Wrapping itself in its wings akin to a cocoon is a typical defensive maneuver.
author: sk372

entry: Coastal homes sometimes find that their gaming devices have apparently changed color or size overnight. These altered consoles are actually POKENAME in disguise. They crawl into homes seeking wood and warmth.
author: .realthree

entry: When unable to find enough food to find in the wild, POKENAME often harasses people into feeding it by surrounding them with illusory walls that sting on contact. Thankfully, POKENAME is easily distracted by new smells.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's scythes secrete the same poison found in its horn, used for self-defense. Though mild, it only takes a single light cut for the poison to take effect and result in strong bouts of nausea and dizziness.
author: sk372

entry: Its keen sense of smell allows it to pinpoint trees laden with Oran Berries, its favorite food. It brandishes its sharp scythes to ward off rival Pokémon, but despite its fearsome appearance, it prefers to flee from battles whenever it can.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME tries to act fierce, it only makes people laugh. If this clownish bug falls over, it has trouble getting back up.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME rely on the stingers on their tails to scratch itches on their backs. A flick of the tail produces a loud snap that scares away potential predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's noses are so sensitive that it can distinguish its favorite leaves by smell alone. However, each head prefers a different kind of leaf, which often causes conflict during mealtimes.
author: sautomagically

entry: The horns on its head and tail secrete a very mild poison. The poison's effects vary depending on its surroundings: burning, dehydration, paralysis, blindness, light sensitivity, chills, rashes and numbness have all been reported.
author: sk372

entry: It keeps Flying-type Pokémon at bay by releasing electric discharges from the spines surrounding its neck. During the day, POKENAME dashes frantically from bush to bush, stockpiling as many ripe Berries as it can find.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prefers to be left alone, retreating into trees or computers when approached, depending on what's nearest. Its horn secretes a venom that's particularly caustic to Steel types.
author: sk372

entry: The fusion process that produces POKENAME creates genetic instabilities that cause them to become unusually long. They sometimes mistake their own tail segments as the heads of other POKENAME and attack them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The only part of its body that moves is its head, which will poke anyone who tries to grab it. Research suggests POKENAME can remember anyone who touched it by smell alone, even after it evolves.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME navigate using their sense of smell, able to differentiate between at least six smells at the same time. Every week since being born, they shed their skin and the poison in their horns becomes more potent.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME scurry quickly along the grounds of forests, jabbing at anything in their way using their poisonous horns. They are always searching for food, a task made easy due to their strong sense of smell.
author: infinex21

entry: Although a single POKENAME sting will just cause swelling, multiple stings can be very dangerous. Trainers should avoid areas where they hear the characteristic buzzing sound made by its wings.
author: sautomagically

entry: Their keen eyes allow them to see where roots peek above the ground's surface, allowing them to pluck the nutrients from their home. One root may last POKENAME a week, so they are at risk of being overfed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They are known to challenge each other to duels, wrestling with their tails to avoid the challenger's stinger. This strengthens their tails for when they must fight over a limited number of berries, giving them an advantage over other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They forage for food at night, hopping between berry bushes to shake them down. When the sun rises, POKENAME fly off the ground to rest in the trees above the forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each of POKENAME's sharp quills can inject venom into prey. Its proboscis can smell the scent of this venom from up to eight miles away.
author: silverscloudy

entry: The fluid in POKENAME's body allows its String Shot to be used for communication over long distances. Unfortunately, it often runs out of string before it can escape from a chasing Pokémon.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: It flies on starlit nights, glowing venom dripping from the stinger on its tail. It will trace the patterns of unknown constellations in the dirt with its stinger. Astrologists record the patterns, seeking meaning.
author: vic1312

entry: A patient and powerful hunter, POKENAME are known to lie perfectly still for days, concealed amongst dry leaves, and wait for the perfect opportunity to strike with their deadly stingers.
author: corndogyip

entry: It holds a Charti Berry whenever it wants to fly in the sky, as it takes little effort to knock it down from the sky. It lives deep in the forest to avoid the risk of any rocks flung around.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Electric power is stored and concentrated within its stingers. As a show of intimidation towards predators, it taps the two stingers together, causing sparks to fly out around it.
author: sk372

entry: Each morning, POKENAME hums a gentle tune to itself. If disturbed while singing, it retaliates with a swift Poison Sting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell consists of the discarded cocoon of its family members. When POKENAME is ready to evolve, it will form a hard, calcium carbonate shell.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME has a difficult time hiding from predators because of its large body. Whenever it is being chased, it will hide in some bushes until the predator loses interest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wool is very some of the softest in the world. POKENAME forms colonies that scout for Berries together.
author: themicelegion

entry: When confronted with a predator, they flap their leafy wings and ram their stingers into their foe. Many POKENAME gather into groups to maximize their chances of escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a strong sense of smell, able to sniff out its preferred food from many yards away. POKENAME fights for food and territory by battling one another using the stinger on its tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME zip past other Pokémon around them to reach the tastiest leaves. They move so quickly that it is difficult for predators to grab onto them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The poison that POKENAME produces has been found to lose its toxicity when mixed with Red Juice. Hives containing young POKENAME are raided and cooked alive in the juice as a type of stew.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The poison that POKENAME produces has been found to lose its toxicity when mixed with Red Juice. Hives containing young POKENAME are raided and cooked alive in the juice as a type of stew.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is covered in over a billion microscopic hairs. They are sharp enough for certain living beings to be able to be pricked by them and injected with a venom, although human skin is tough enough to typically be unable to be pricked.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is covered in over a billion microscopic hairs. They are sharp enough for certain living beings to be able to be pricked by them and injected with a venom, although human skin is tough enough to typically be unable to be pricked.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME live in large social groups and have been observed to bump noses often. Researchers suspect this is a form of communication among the species. Leading theories suggest they are transferring scents of where the preferred food is located.
author: afilthycasual

entry: The bud on its back constantly produces a paralyzing poison that POKENAME uses to hunt. It can also transmit the poison to the horn on its head.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can sniff out food from several kilometers away thanks to its exceptional nose. It would do anything to get a meal, even challenging Pokémon far stronger than itself by baring its fangs or displaying the spines on its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic horn to sense danger while foraging for leaves. It is afraid of other Pokémon and often cries when around them.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are popular with many Trainers thanks to their chubby, plush features. It is advisable to be careful when handling them as their stinger can cause nasty injuries if improperly touched.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A fusion that lacks in aggression, POKENAME solely eats plants and fruit. From its stinger leaks a mild poison that can cause irritation and inflammation.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME aggressively posture before entering a battle, wielding their spines and stinger to try and intimidate their foe into backing down. They are not nearly as brave during battle, scared of taking hits.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Hikers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it hides under piles of leaves, and may use its many poisonous stingers when stepped on. POKENAME's body expands as it eats leaves, allowing it to consume several times its weight each day.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME is incredibly frail, and it will hide in rock piles to avoid predators. Despite having a venomous sting, it barely has any effect on Pokémon larger than it.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its claws and horns are venomous, though the venom is only strong enough to cause acute pain. It can track prey and find food with ease thanks to its strong sense of smell.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hovers around areas where Kakuna gather in wait for evolution. It swoops and poisons those who would prey on the Kakuna to protect the vulnerable cocoons, though primarily to prey on the would-be predators itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a very timid and shy creature. It rarely attacks humans, but if threatened, it will use its horn and tail-spike to inject a searing pain, so caution is adviced.
author: krune

entry: It slinks from tree to tree, eating leaves and bird eggs. Although its horn and tail both contain poison, its sting is more irritating than actually harmful.
author: sautomagically

entry: If someone annoys it too much, POKENAME waves the stinger on its proboscis until it is left alone. It digs small holes in the ground with its paws to store the food it gathers throughout the day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME are incredibly persistent combatants, and may even bite their opponents.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME has an incredible sense of taste and is able to detect even the most subtle of poisons before it swallows any materials it wanted to consume. It is not immune to poison, however, so it has to keep an eye out for other POKENAME's stinger.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although its body is large, its mouth is only big enough to eat bird eggs and leaves. As a result, it must eat massive amounts of food each day to maintain its size, making it a devastating invasive species.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME glide across rivers and lakes to find the best leaves to consume. It is said that Trainers can meet a POKENAME by lingering by their favorite leafy bush.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A forest-dwelling Pokémon that nests in the crevasses of trees. It has a powerful sense of smell; if it even thinks it detects an unfamiliar scent, sparks fly from its tail. Touching any of its legs results in one feeling a slight buzz.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME travels alongside groups of Weedle and copies their movements. Whenever it tries to use its stinger, a bright pink dust is ejected instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lines the nests of other Pokémon with soft silk to help protect their Eggs. Its string is both durable and surprisingly warm.
author: .izik

entry: A forest-dwelling Pokémon that nests in the crevasses of trees. It has a powerful sense of smell; if it even thinks it detects an unfamiliar scent, sparks fly from its tail. Touching any of its legs results in one feeling a slight buzz.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is able to attack from a distance using the sharp stinger on its long tail. The potent venom it produces is so powerful that it can cause full-body paralysis within minutes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its big, soft body makes it a food of choice for bird Pokémon. It defends itself by shooting venomous spikes from its hands.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It's been said that a sting from one of POKENAME's tendrils feels like getting struck by lighting. Those with a fear of bugs despise this Pokémon.
author: 8xviktor

entry: If it senses a spike of joyous feelings in the area, POKENAME will fly above and fire off String Shot onto those around it in celebration. Cleanup tends to be difficult.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME burrow below trees to eat roots and make nests. When they are cornered by a predator, they either jab at the predator with their stinger or retreat into their burrow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can track the slightest hint of a scent thanks to their acute sense of smell. They are common partners for Rangers because they can track poachers or lost travelers and quickly find them.
author: infinex21

entry: The venom in POKENAME's horn is extremely cold. The toxins can numb entire limbs, so it's quite dangerous despite its goofy appearance.
author: robbery_666

entry: As a result of a reversed value somewhere in the code that makes up POKENAME's body, POKENAME's venom acts as an antidote for humans afflicted by toxins from fusions. More and more parks have begun to keep a POKENAME on hand in case of emergency.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME smashes herbs into paste using its tail before eating them. Its red nose detects spoilage and helps it avoid rotting plants.
author: .izik

entry: When using the horn on its head or tail to strike a foe, POKENAME injects the opponent with a poison that burns the target. The injection site becomes inflamed and swollen if it is not treated immediately.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The "spines" on its back are made of bunched-up silk.  While they are too soft and flimsy to pose any real threat, they appear sharp enough to deter some predators when POKENAME curls up defensively.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME is an extremely shy creature that makes its home in the undergrowth, retreating at the slightest sound. The poisonous stinger above its head serves as a defense against predators.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live high in the branches of tall trees to keep themselves safe from larger Pokémon. They feed on the softer bark of the high branches, gnawing out hollows that they can use for shelter when they start to evolve.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME stick together in groups to collectively sting any predators that they encounter. Even though some still end up eaten, many survive with a dream of vengeance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is an extremely shy creature that makes its home in the undergrowth, retreating at the slightest sound. The poisonous stinger above its head serves as a defense against predators.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The bud on its back constantly produces a paralyzing poison that POKENAME uses to hunt. It can also transmit the poison to the horn on its head.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME releases toxic pollen from the flower on its back. The stinger on its head is considered vestigial, as its size prevents it from utilizing its horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The barbs on POKENAME's body are actually ingrown teeth from its monstrous head. These teeth inject poison on contact, but only full bites deliver a dangerous dose.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's proboscis allows it to smell out high-quality leaves around the forest. It is also very slow, moving as fast as paint dries.
author: beatdoof

entry: A POKENAME's legs are soft and squishy, despite its slimy look. The large horn on POKENAME's head is used to swipe branches away.
author: hatsune_miko

entry: Male POKENAME fight each other in battles of dominance using their large horns. They fight for the right of passage to crawl onto land and evolve. The combatant who is afflicted with poison first is considered the loser.
author: xiapher

entry: The poison from POKENAME's horn is highly potent, with a single drop being enough to render almost anything immobile. Careful studies are being undertaken to see if it could lead to the creation of a powerful catch-all antivenom.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rely on the stinger on their forehead to avoid predators, but lack any defenses for their rear. This leads many adventurous POKENAME to getting snatched up by an opportunistic Flying-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are energetic and run around forests searching for the best leaves and berries to feast upon; they accept nothing but the best. Only when they have eaten their fill do they become less energetic.
author: infinex21

entry: They are too prideful to live together, despite being rather weak. If two POKENAME ever cross paths, they will clash with their venomous horns until one of them surrenders or has their horn broken.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has built onto Cateredge's evolutionary strategy by adding silk spikes to make its flail a greater deterrent.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME have a sharp point at the end of each stinger that is capable of piercing shells. While they have no cutting edge, a well-placed jab from a stinger can render their target immobilized.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on their many stingers to get out of trouble. The spines on their back and their horn serve a nasty concoction of venom that will leave whoever it stings hobbled over in pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When defending itself from predators, it jabs its spiked ribbons into them, filling them with a numbing poison.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME are found only in regions with large seasonal shifts in humidity. To evolve, they coil around sturdy trees during summer. As the air dries, a reaction causes their skin to harden and crystallise, triggering their transformation.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME distort space around them to move closer to leafy bushes without using their muscles. Whenever they spot a Trainer, the space around them becomes infinitely vast, which discourages Trainers from pursuing capture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Spores shed from POKENAME can be refined into a medicine that counteracts the effects of many fusions' toxins. However, collecting the spores is a difficult task, as POKENAME's own venom is potent enough to incapacitate a Tauros with a single prick.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME ensnares foes with silk before striking with a surprise Shadow Ball. Its attacks are eerily silent until the moment of impact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats around the forest, looking for any damaged Kakuna. It rehabilitates any weakened Kakuna it finds until they evolve into Beedrill.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME made itself a Weedle costume to look less frightening and try to befriend the Flying-type Pokémon in the area. However, because of its disguise, it's often mistaken for prey and ends up having to run away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its sticky string like a whip to execute complex martial arts moves. It can swing, trip, and strike with startling precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a highly developed sense of smell that lets it detect electricity even from afar. It constantly searches for cables to gnaw on, boosting the energy stored within its small body.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has powerful jaws that it uses to trap prey that are careless enough to wander within striking range of its burrows. Trainers travelling through areas known to be home to POKENAME are advised to make liberal use of Repel.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The pointed cogs adorning POKENAME's body are composed entirely of silk, but are capable of hardening to a toughness resembling steel.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a child and plays alone in quiet parks. Once isolated, it traps a target in string and drags them into the forest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crawls slowly along tree branches and commonly uses its horned-tail to carve small notches in the bark. Its body gives off faint warmth, which deters smaller predators from approaching.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME binds clusters of seeds together using sticky string. It devours them all at once, often leaving nothing behind.
author: .izik

entry: At first glance, a POKENAME's fluff looks soft and harmless. However, touching it will result in your hand being covered in a sticky, rubbery glue that can stick your fingers together for up to a week if untreated.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Spores leaking from POKENAME's body cause paralysis in predators like Pidgeotto. It then strikes with its sharp horn to drive them off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keep their secondary stinger hidden with their long flowing bodies. When the right opportunity strikes, they unleash a flurry of jabs from their hidden stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gain nutrients by dissolving leaves in the fluid around their body. The fluid around their body recedes when they use their stinger, creating a moment of vulnerability to attack dangerous foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies in eerie nighttime swarms. Together, they strike with a flurry of Poison Stings to weaken prey for easy capture.
author: .izik

entry: Every POKENAME carries a totem of the Kakuna it never got to evolve into while it was alive. Even if it evolves now, it will not look the same as the totem it carries.
author: crumple_2

entry: It stores static electricity in its stinger until it's ready to make a surprise strike on an unsuspecting victim. The jolt is still incredibly minor and rarely regarded as anything more than a momentary nuisance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's spikes contain a venomous toxin capable of temporarily paralyzing smaller targets. When threatened, they can fire these spikes in all directions.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME use their sense of smell to find aromatic berries to pluck off trees, eating as much as twice their body weight in a day. They require plenty of food, as their bodies break down nutrients quickly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before attacking, the horn on POKENAME's head glows red-hot. It charges and strikes with fiery precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lies flat on meadow grass, perfectly still like a trap. When prey draws near, it lunges forward with a sudden Bug Bite.
author: .izik

entry: Acidic mucus drips from POKENAME's nose and melts through bark. It uses this method to reach and consume fresh tree sap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a worryingly common fusion that is undesirable to farmers. It will plant itself in crop fields, eating and sucking out all the nutrients and minerals in the soil until it is unsuitable for growing any sort of plant inside of it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME performs a lively samba in fields of daisies during summer. It only pauses to nibble on nearby flower petals and sleep.
author: .izik

entry: After eating a Pomeg Berry, POKENAME dances a rapid jig atop trees. Its beak bobs with each joyful step.
author: .izik

entry: By beaches, POKENAME twirls in a graceful dance, swaying its arms rhythmically. It releases soft powder from the feathers on its waist as it moves.
author: .izik

entry: As winter nears, POKENAME dances quietly with the chill wind. Its large red nose sniffs out hidden berries buried beneath the snow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to eat trash, especially wrappers. They wade through landfills in search of these wrappers and carry them back to their forest homes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats silently over marshes at night, spitting out nearly invisible string. Prey often becomes ensnared before realizing it's being hunted.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME can be found in forests, eating the branches off of other trees.
author: grassy311

entry: POKENAME sneaks up on prey to deliver a quick sting before flying away. With an incredible sense of hearing, it listens to the sound of its poisoned victim's deteriorating heartbeat and breathing, waiting patiently for their eventual collapse.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME forages around bug nests, snacking on the discarded pieces of cocoons left behind from evolution. The poison in its horn is mild, but numbs victims quickly enough to let it fly away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME release a slimy venom from their stingers that cause an unbearable itchiness. This venom is also secreted when they crawl, allowing them to stick and crawl up walls.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME release toxic spores into the air that have a redolent scent. People report experiencing dizziness and nausea after prolonged exposure to the aromatic POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: From the ocean floor, POKENAME launches silk threads at passing boats. If it hits, it tries to drag them under the waves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME covers patches of ground plants with its many legs. Its poisonous spikes keep predators away while it munches to its heart's content.
author: hophoppip

entry: The mushrooms are no longer deadly to the host, but are now quite poisonous if consumed. This seems to have had the interesting side-effect of making POKENAME no longer able to secrete poison from its horn.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drains vitality from plant life, leaving entire forests full of dried up trees. Anyone who is jabbed by the needle on its head will be compelled to bring it mounds of leaves until they eventually succumb to the poison.
author: darkweavile428

entry: An omnivorous Pokémon with a powerful sense of smell, POKENAME is particularly sensitive to extreme changes in weather. As a result, it grows moody when the seasons change, or when moves such as Hail are used.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's hair holds enough poison to kill three Trainers. If you've come in contact with it, you must contact your local hospital immediately.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The wild POKENAME uses the poisonous spikes on its mushroom as a deterrent for things not to step on it. Although very painful, the venom in its spikes is completely non-lethal and is used in a lot of modern medicine.
author: big_clanker

entry: POKENAME's bladelike leaves hold a far deadlier venom than the stinger atop its head. Even small cuts can leave lasting wounds that take exceptionally long to close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shaggy fur and powder-covered body irritates its nose, causing it to sneeze and release its powder in bursts. Some Trainers find it very endearing and adorable, but will suffer the consequences when they observe up close.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: At night, POKENAME floats through pumpkin patches. Its venom-tipped spikes deter wildlife from damaging the precious crops.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME develops the muscles in its tail by carving shapes into trees. Its stingers ooze with a hot venom that sizzles when exposed to air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protects itself from predators by burying itself under the ground and leaving the spike atop its head exposed.
author: melodydelune

entry: Instead of injecting poison, POKENAME's needle sucks out poison from whatever it pierces. While it has a natural high tolerance for toxins, some potent poisonous compounds cause it substantial pain and discomfort.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's slow, bulky bodies are ill-suited for speed, so they often eat the leafy scraps other Bug-type Pokémon leave behind. Many are elated when they reach a bush first and will sting anyone who tries to steal their leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drills into large tree roots with sharp spikes to drink sap. Once finished, it tunnels onward to the next tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will often be distracted by simple things, making it a Pokémon only really suitable as a house pet. Sometimes, it will make a ball out of its own String Shot and play with it like any domestic cat Pokémon.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME rubs its face against those it cares about. Unfortunately for them, it also has a poison stinger on its head.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME uses its venomous tail to sting unsuspecting travelers. It then steals their jewelry, adding the treasures to its silk-lined nest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME need to release the venom from their stinger, or they will suffer from a migraine from the pressure. They can artificially release the venom by jabbing into rocks, but this behavior risks damaging their stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are a common meal for many Flying-type Pokémon. Their stingers and muddy splashes have little effect on their predators, so they rely on numbers to survive attacks, as predators are scared of writhing balls of POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Lone POKENAME are an easy target for bird Pokémon, so they tend to live in large colonies for protection. The sheer number of stinger-tipped tails will drive off even the hungriest beaks.
author: occulusmalus

entry: POKENAME becomes irate and throws a tantrum whenever it does not receive its favorite food. Once it calms down, it will begrudgingly eat whatever food is presented.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If someone tries to bother its Trainer, POKENAME threatens them by pointing the stinger on its forehead. Thanks to its incredible sense of smell, this Pokémon is often used in rescue teams to help locate missing people.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When laid flat, its segmented body can skitter surprisingly fast. Anyone struck with the stinger on its tail is instantly immobilized and their wound cauterized.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME roll as they bob along the surface of the water, mainly using their tails to propel themselves as opposed to their tiny arms. The bubbles they create with their horns shine brightly and colorfully to warn predators of the toxins within.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Due to its strong sense of smell, sneaking up on POKENAME before it teleports away is near impossible. It is docile enough to be lured close with its favorite type of leaf, however.
author: sk372

entry: Working together to form colonies in the forest, POKENAME are highly social and co-operative. When threatened by flying Pokémon, most of the colony defends their home while a small group tries to draw the threat away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The marks on its leaves were thought to be signs of illness, until research found that POKENAME occasionally nibbles its own leaves. This seems to cause no harm, and its leaves grow back if fully consumed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME withdraws into its shell whenever there is danger and only leaves its stinger exposed. Any bird Pokémon that pecks at the shell may accidentally strike its stinger and get poisoned in the process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The powerful acid of a POKENAME requires special enzymes to break down biological matter. When POKENAME stings another Pokémon, they transfer some of the enzymes to activate the caustic power of the venom.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protects its long tail at any cost. If it finds itself in a dangerous situation, such as facing a powerful Scyther, it will coat its tail in tough and durable silk webbing so that its tail is protected even if POKENAME hides in its shell.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME march together in small flocks, hoisting sharpened sticks up with one wing. They jab at other Pokémon with these sticks to get what they want, working together to bully them away from food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME strut through forest clearings in small flocks with their heads held high, acting confident to ward off predators. When disputes arise within the flock, the two competing POKENAME will square off and rear up as tall as possible.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME travel in groups to protect themselves from predators. When threatened, they surround the predator and sting them with each of their heads repeatedly until the predator gives up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has enough room to store two Weedle in each cannon, making them great places to hide whenever predators are nearby. It can be seen hobbling through forests with bug Pokémon in its cannons, peacefully finding bushes to eat leaves from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME draw closer to evolution, the gas they emit becomes more and more foul smelling. While this does keep POKENAME safe, their innards are so toxic most Pokémon cannot eat them safely anyway.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is most often found in rotting, deserted houses where it rips apart the walls with its claws to consume the decomposing wood. Its body is covered in hairy bristles, which it will brush along the neck of unaware explorers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME chases after intruders on its stumpy legs, trying to sting them with its venomous tail. When alone, it munches on crumbling bits of rotten buildings while grumbling to itself.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Because its feet are too short to reach the ground, POKENAME must learn new ways to ambulate after fusion.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME waits near bike racks. If a human mistakes it for a real bicycle and sits on its back, it races off towards the nearest forest with them. Since every abductee has escaped by simply dismounting, it's unknown what POKENAME hopes to accomplish.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME will swallow anything that can fit in its mouth. If it doesn't eat its own body weight in food daily, it flies into a fury and thrashes until exhausted.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME inhabits remote waterfalls far away from human civilization. Although it appears cold and distant, it becomes vulnerable and emotional once given a hug.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its kicks are so devastatingly powerful that they can alter the natural course of a waterfall. POKENAME's temperament is so aggressive and fierce that even its own Trainer often struggles to get through to it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its kicks are so devastatingly powerful that they can alter the natural course of a waterfall. POKENAME's temperament is so aggressive and fierce that even its own Trainer often struggles to get through to it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are fierce protectors of Magikarp and are known to abduct those mistreated by a Trainer. Many POKENAME store Magikarp in their pouches to monitor its growth, barging into Pokémon Centers seeking medical attention when it is ill.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hunts small fish with a combination of stealth and ferocity. It blinds prey with ink while hiding among kelp, before swimming quickly and snatching it up with its vicious bite.
author: sk372

entry: The poison POKENAME creates induces intense aggression, mania, and hallucinations. As a result, it is considered too dangerous to consume even by the most hostile and famished Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite being rather aggressive by nature, POKENAME have very delicate and frail bodies. If they are angered enough, they will create a huge current of water to knock away the aggressor.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Socialite Trainers enjoy looking after POKENAME in specially constructed reserves. POKENAME are rather territorial and need room to swim, so it is rare to see more than two share a pond.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is much more aggressive that it appears at first glance, and does not take kindly to intruders in the flower gardens it calls home. It paralyzes a target with spores from its wings before blasting them away with a powerful Hyper Beam.
author: sk372

entry: Children often mistake POKENAME for masks at the beach due to their fins and shape. When picked up, POKENAME closes its eyes and spins rapidly, hoping to be let go.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has a ferocious and vindictive attitude towards all it comes across, but aside from a nasty bite, it is largely unremarkable and ineffective. It tends to act more passively in the presence of Magikarp.
author: sk372

entry: If two POKENAME meet, they will fight to the death, no matter what. It's thought that their aggressive and independent instincts are so great that POKENAME actively seek to be the last, and only, of their kind.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its massive size, POKENAME moves swiftly both in water and along the rocky coasts where it digs its den. A single powerful swing of its sharp scythes can slice even huge boulders clean in half.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Old sailors' tales speak of a ferocious Pokémon able to cleave through the bow of a vessel with just a lash of its tail, its fangs large enough to rend a dozen sailors in a single bite. This Pokémon is believed to be a juvenile POKENAME.
author: kingd8

entry: Despite its fierce appearance, POKENAME is actually extremely gentle and afraid of battling others. Outside the underwater caves it uses as shelter, you can find the scales it sheds during molting.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is a Pokémon with a fearsome temper, known for summoning violent storms with the power contained within its red pearls. Although extremely difficult to train, once its trust has been earned, it becomes an extremely loyal companion.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Feared for its wrath, POKENAME can unleash the power of its blue pearls to conjure violent tempests. Training it is a daunting task, but once it accepts a Trainer, it remains steadfastly loyal.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME goes around oceans to destroy ships and strand sailors. Its rampages at sea create violent and stormy waters that can sink ships and flood nearby islands.
author: soup1900

entry: Though its size may be huge, these giants are found near rivers and lakes where they guard sections and demand tolls to pass. Once the toll is paid they expand the foam around their neck to create a platform for others to climb on and ride across.
author: doxtordaemon

entry: When a POKENAME roars, the flames along its neck flare with enough heat to instantly evaporate any water they touch. Its tail strikes are strong enough to create small tidal waves.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME are angered, their bulbs grow brighter due to releasing more electricity. The central bulb acts as a focus for the other two, helping to aim and direct the electricity as they charge.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is an aggressive creature capable of spouting powerful jets of salt water from its mouth. Though its body has adapted to marine life, it can soar above the waves to drive away boats that enter its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME still struggles to fly in strong winds, so it relies on its tail to swim and its goggle-like eyes to navigate around in the water. It's mostly harmless.
author: dill360yt

entry: In cold water, POKENAME is calm and playful, often seen frolicking with other Water Pokémon. But when the temperature rises above 5°C, it becomes violently aggressive, attacking anything that moves until it faints from sheer exhaustion.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Thanks to its psychic powers, POKENAME can raise the tide at will. If it deems its Trainer in danger, it flies into a rage; a single strike from its tails would be enough to sink a small boat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This Pokémon stalks rivers and lakes at night, lying in wait for prey. POKENAME attacks make up a large percent of all Pokémon attacks in Kanto.
author: capwolfbane

entry: The heavy bulb in the middle of POKENAME back makes it awkward and irritable. Their first response to being approached is violence, as POKENAME will lash out with their long tails.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: Covered in battle-forged scales, POKENAME lurks in deep riverbeds. Though feared for its appearance, it remains docile unless threatened.
author: presicho

entry: It lives in aquifers deep underground. If humans extract too much water, it will tunnel up to the surface and shake the earth with its rage.
author: .jerden

entry: POKENAME are territorial, scaring off other Pokémon using their sharp barbs and spiky bodies. The sharp barbs release a poison that numbs opposing Pokémon, allowing POKENAME to push them out of its territory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are violent Pokémon, thrashing about and launching powerful Fire Blasts at those that come within reach of them. Folk tales claim their violence causes volcanoes to erupt, holding them responsible for the destruction caused.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Flocks of POKENAME live around large lakes and chase off any other Pokémon that try to stake their claim on their feeding grounds. They are aggressive and will attack anyone that gets too close to them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are fast and vicious, hunting for prey by barreling through the sea and biting with their sharp teeth. Despite this, POKENAME often avoid sinking ships and beaches, preferring isolated targets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many a tale has been passed down amongst sailors about POKENAME. Should a ship run afoul of it, it will chase it down across entire oceans, not resting until it sends the boat sinking to the briny deep.
author: sk372

entry: Many have claimed the secret to taming a POKENAME is to climb on its back and pull its whiskers like reins. Pokémon Centers and hospitals regularly put out PSAs to discourage this idea.
author: sk372

entry: According to folk legend, POKENAME is responsible for hurricanes and typhoons. Its roars have been described as a relentless, deafening howl that shakes the ground along with it.
author: acid_pen

entry: It is said that POKENAME appears only once every hundred years to purify the contaminated waters of lakes. Its body is so hot that even a touch of its paws can turn frozen lakes into steaming hot springs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's brain has altered to the point where it only naturally thinks about combat and destruction. It is especially difficult for Trainers to handle its following rampages if it ever manages to lose a battle.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's brain has altered to the point where it only naturally thinks about combat and destruction. It is especially difficult for Trainers to handle its following rampages if it ever manages to lose a battle.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The horns and tendrils on POKENAME's head generate massive levels of electrical voltage. Extremely violent, a rampaging POKENAME will decimate all its surroundings with titanic storms of lightning until little remains.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often found in accompanying wild Gyarados. It acts to curb their violent tendencies, pushing them away when they move to attack. For whatever reason, Gyarados never turn aggressive on POKENAME itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a very territorial Pokémon that will attack anything it feels threatened by.  It uses its wings to make strong winds to blow enemies away.
author: dill360yt

entry: POKENAME leaps from high seaside cliffs to glide in search of prey. Its large body, strong pincers, and sheer brutality make for a menacing predator.
author: wigglypon

entry: It uses its strong tail to swim up rivers and waterfalls. It will smash any man-made object it encounters; boats, bridges, and even concrete dams.
author: staghorn

entry: An adept glider, POKENAME will skim just above the water's surface, viciously snatching and squeezing any unsuspecting prey with its strong tail.
author: char_latte3412

entry: If the weather is not cold enough for POKENAME's liking, it will go on a rampage, destroying everything in its path. To prevent this, people will often guide POKENAME to snowy mountains as spring draws near.
author: darkweavile428

entry: It digs complex underwater tunnels, creating an elaborate network. Prey dragged into these tunnels are never seen again, lost in the depths forever.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME wishes nothing but to sing in front of a live audience, but its performances always end in destruction. Due to its inherent violent nature, one bad comment about its horrendous vocals will send it into a rampage.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: An old children's book tells the story of a POKENAME who was the brave leader of an underwater city. It cares deeply about protecting its environment.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME alternates between episodes of extreme violence and eerie stillness. It is often found in coastal towns that have been devastated by storms.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME's true form is actually the small fish in the center of the body. Its arms and tail are constructs that it controls telekinetically.
author: pastamanjase

entry: POKENAME has rarely been spotted out at sea, with researchers unable to get close due to its volatile nature. It has been reported that POKENAME emerges from the ocean floor every 108 minutes, bellowing out into the sky before disappearing.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME can be found meditating by the most turbulent waterfalls, focusing on controlling its inherently overwhelming rage. If it becomes surrounded by a violent and overwhelming atmosphere, the area may soon be entirely consumed in blue flame.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME most often appears flying through harsh storms, enduring the brutal flying conditions as if they were light breezes. It parts water in half using its scythes, allowing no escape for underwater foes.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon can move frighteningly fast and strike with brutal ferocity. When a wild POKENAME is spotted, there is oft a bounty set for its capture before it can go into a destructive rage.
author: infinex21

entry: Its fierce fangs contain poison which can kill a human but a Pokémon may survive. Its huge tail is strong enough to launch Pokémon into the sky.
author: .afantasticTrainer

entry: The flower on POKENAME's back can vary in colour depending on its diet and sunlight exposure. However, due to its often vicious and violent nature, these flowers are nearly always pale yellow.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: POKENAME are very protective of their siblings. Trainers fishing for Magikarp are often surprised by their savagery as they fight tooth and claw to save their brethren.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME will never attack Pokémon it considers weaker than it. However, if its anger reaches a critical point, it will violently attack anything within its line of sight until nothing remains.
author: mistymagius

entry: A fearsome hunter, POKENAME is the apex predator of the lakes it inhabits. With a single strike from its tail, it can unleash powerful waves that topple trees and homes.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: Only fools have enough courage to disturb a sleeping POKENAME. Once awakened, this Pokémon goes on a rampage.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME thrash their tails with enough force to fell fully grown trees, putting on these displays of power whenever they spy a rival encroaching on their territory. Battles between two POKENAME can take days to fully resolve.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's jaws have enough bite force to crush boulders. They use their powerful bites in battle to attack their rivals with vicious crunches. Battles between two POKENAME can take days to fully resolve.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's jaws have enough bite force to crush boulders. They use their powerful bites in battle to attack their rivals with vicious crunches. Battles between two POKENAME can take days to fully resolve.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It frequents Dragon-infested waters, picking fights with any it comes across. Most foes expect it to be enraged and ferocious, but POKENAME is also extremely clever.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Never fight POKENAME at full power. On the rare occasion POKENAME cannot overpower an opponent, it uses deception and trickery to put itself in a winning position.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is said to be possessed by the vengeful soul of a Gyarados, once slain by the very blade that now forms its body. Only those with unshakable will can grasp its hilt without being consumed by its seething rage.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME is said to be possessed by the vengeful soul of a Gyarados, once slain by the very blade that now forms its body. Only those with unshakable will can grasp its hilt without being consumed by its seething rage.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME's complex swordplay is matched only by its ceaseless fury. When enraged, its twin blades strike without rest until nothing remains of its prey.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME can destroy entire cities with a single swing. Many of the deadliest warmongers in ancient myth are depicted wielding it, but whether they controlled it or it controlled them remains unknown.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME can destroy entire cities with a single swing. Many of the deadliest warmongers in ancient myth are depicted wielding it, but whether they controlled it or it controlled them remains unknown.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME ranges along the coast of oceans, amphibiously able to nest along the shore or in underwater caves. It rams boats with its crest, which is harder than diamond, seeking to sink what it perceives as challengers to its territory.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME dreams of one day becoming like the heroes who protect the weak. Now, though, it fishes out Water-type Pokémon in hopes of a big catch.
author: nellnast42

entry: Despite its cruelty in combat using its water cannon arm, POKENAME has been found to live by a code of honor, leading it to defend weaker Pokémon.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME is a fearsome sea predator that attacks ships during the stormiest nights. Its massive, muscular body can deliver devastating blows, while its sharp claws are strong enough to pierce even metal hulls. It is known to be a solitary hunter.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a lone predator of the seas, known to strike during fierce storms. Its powerful claws can tear through metal, and the force of its blows is said to shatter the hulls of entire ships.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives on beaches where they hunt for food at sea and rest in the sand. When its territory is threatened, POKENAME can create hurricane-force winds with its wings and will pursue aggressors relentlessly.
author: hinochi.

entry: The scales of POKENAME's lower bodies are so desired that many poachers have made careers of solely hunting them. Poaching has reduced due to the efforts of Pokémon Rangers and the increasingly high aggression that POKENAME have begun to display.
author: infinex21

entry: Although typically docile and kind, it swiftly turns aggressive when the lake it resides in is disturbed. Its long, thin antennae can easily pick up on shifts in the water, even from a single soda can landing within its lake.
author: infinex21

entry: A sudden mutation caused POKENAME to sprout wings, driven by its desire to spread its rage further in the sky and land. When its not rampaging, it slumbers in deep ocean canyons.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: Legends say the first POKENAME came from a Magiveon that swam up a mighty waterfall by only splashing.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME has a volatile temper, especially when protecting its young, and rampages with the strength of the most devastating natural disasters. Emergency response rangers are stationed near known nesting sites with well-trained teams.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This dragon-type Pokémon is so well-known for its tough skin that it's said to be the strongest kind in the world. Researchers have yet to determine whether or not the “X” on POKENAME's stomach is truly a birthmark.
author: thistleblower

entry: POKENAME is a destructive creature believed to originate from a different dimension of some kind. It can emerge from shadows, laying waste to the surrounding area before once more vanishing into the darkness.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon twists and curls elegantly as it flies. Trainers are advised not to confront it, as it will fly into a rage seemingly upon sensing any amount of deceit within a person's heart.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME has a volatile temper, especially when protecting its young, and rampages with the strength of the most devastating natural disasters. Emergency response rangers are stationed near known nesting sites with well-trained teams.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a volatile temper, especially when protecting its young, and rampages with the strength of the most devastating natural disasters. Emergency response rangers are stationed near known nesting sites with well-trained teams.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a volatile temper, especially when protecting its young, and rampages with the strength of the most devastating natural disasters. Emergency response rangers are stationed near known nesting sites with well-trained teams.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a volatile temper, especially when protecting its young, and rampages with the strength of the most devastating natural disasters. Emergency response rangers are stationed near known nesting sites with well-trained teams.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's moods change and shift depending on the phase of the moon. They are happy and playful during the full moon, but are aggressive and feisty during a new moon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Devastatingly cruel, POKENAME wraps its electrified feelers around ensnared victims and torments them with jolts of electricity for days on end.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME nests and thrives in harbors and along coastal docks, where it can hunt the Magikarp it craves. When food is scarce, it attacks fishing boats with its powerful claws to aggressively steal their catch.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A Mimikyu disguising itself as a Gyarados. But to go one step further, it has made itself an inflatable Trainer, as an attempt to blend into society.
author: funkytomate

entry: POKENAME hide underwater, attracting their Flying-Type prey by using their Magikarp-like heads as bait. Tales tell of POKENAME destroying entire docks in bursts of rage; only the most experienced of trainers can get POKENAME to obey them.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME's large mouth and stout body enable it to consume a range of foods, causing the flower on its back to bloom a bright pink and yellow. It is extremely vicious in its hunt for food.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: POKENAME swim silently through rivers in search of meals. If two of them get into a fight, they will furiously snap their jaws at each other, accidentally letting their prey escape while they compete.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME dive deep into the ocean in search of pearls to consume. They use the tail on their head to frighten boats away from their hunting grounds.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: A single sighting of POKENAME is enough to close a lake for weeks. It moves from one body of water to the next, devouring most of the local wildlife before continuing on. Fishermen who remain despite its presence risk becoming prey themselves.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME may live both in and out of water. Although their ferocious appearance has been depicted in movies and plays, their rarity and hair-trigger temper make it almost impossible for them to appear in such productions.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body overflows with destructive energy, which allows it to go nearly anywhere underwater without fear. This energy seeps into every cell of its body, causing it to demolish anything that remotely gets in its way without a hint of empathy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME roars, nearby buildings collapse due to the violent waves of energy that are unleashed through its throat. It will do anything to survive, including devouring small Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body overflows with destructive energy, which allows it to go nearly anywhere underwater without fear. This energy seeps into every cell of its body, causing it to demolish almost anything that gets in its way without a hint of empathy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's brain is actually larger than a human's, but it appears to lack even remotely the same amount of intelligence. It doesn't need to be smart: sheer strength allows POKENAME to survive in almost any environment.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME dancing is a sign of territorial aggression, a warning to any who see it. One should back away slowly as it dances, lest one wants to contend with flame, scalding water and a razor-sharp beak.
author: sk372

entry: It may be highly aggressive and territorial, but it only finds courage when around other POKENAME. Power oozes from its body so strongly that other Pokémon can't help but be naturally intimidated by its presence.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It has a most vicious, destructive nature towards anything that catches its ire, even slightly. With its speed and strength, it has torn entire ships to shreds in seconds.
author: sk372

entry: It barely moves, mostly floating wherever the clouds carry it. It feeds on Pokémon that enter its mouth attempting to prey on the Magilu living there.
author: jreposo

entry: This Pokémon is a glutton, but it's bad at getting food. It teams up with a Magilu to catch prey.
author: jreposo

entry: What appears to be a miniature Gyarados inhabits POKENAME's center. POKENAME has a similar violent temperament to its passenger, firing off powerful beams of energized water and decimating anything nearby when it goes on a rampage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are a sedentary but hostile species of Pokémon, as they use their tentacles to jab at prey, injecting venom into them. Their camouflage allows prey to move closer without noticing POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spend their time polishing their incredible fighting skills in mountain lakes. Every so often, one will descend from its home to destroy all it deems unworthy.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: Although kind-natured and innocent, POKENAME are not often kept as family pets. Their juvenile lack of discipline and destructive biting power result in most pieces of furniture being chewed to bits.
author: enemyphase

entry: Without strict obedience training POKENAME are prone to throwing tremendously destructive tantrums. As such, they are highly sought after by Trainers attempting to prove themselves.
author: enemyphase

entry: POKENAME deceives fishermen by mimicking a helpless catch before yanking them into the depths. Its jagged teeth shimmer just beneath the surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME ruthlessly attacks weaker-looking Pokémon as a show of dominance. However, as soon as they fight back, it flops away in cowardice.
author: soup1900

entry: While peaceful when alone, POKENAME becomes driven to violence and destruction when removed from its habitat. Its arms have a mind of their own, making it a formidable foe.
author: woobent

entry: The Pokémon lives in undersea caves, sometimes displacing anything already inhabiting them in the process. If it cannot satisfy its hunger, it will get frustrated and start smashing through coral reefs in rage.
author: fireblade141

entry: It saunters around the deep sea, acting like a mobile volcanic vent. Pokémon who feed off volcanic emissions often swarm POKENAME.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Whenever they are angry, they vent that frustration into their maracas. Eventually, this anger turns into joy as they begin to add rhythm into the shaking.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a violent amphibian Pokémon that attacks anything in the area, with the exception of Charmander. The more angered it is, the larger the fire on its tail grows; one case records the visible orange flame growing dozens of feet tall.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's small stature does nothing to curb its violent and aggressive tendencies. It's given a wide berth due to superstition that those bitten by POKENAME will lose the ability to feel love, replaced with rage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is infamous for its violent courtship. To impress a potential partner, POKENAME will destroy large swathes of reef. The most destructive individual is deemed the most desirable.
author: chrysomelinae

entry: POKENAME fires torrents of water at others of its kind while digging to establish territory. Each individual commands a wide underground domain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very protective of their personal space, hissing and arching their tail if anyone tries to pet them. Those foolish enough to get too close find themselves getting aggressively clawed and bitten.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME get angry, they scream loud enough to displace the water around them and create tsunamis.  Rangers that work along coastlines take in abandoned POKENAME to ensure that they're given a good home and kept calm and happy.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is perpetually angry and violent due to the pain of its constant headaches. The stronger the headache, the more intense its rampage; a strong enough migraine can even make it release a massive Hyper Beam.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is said to be so full of anger that it has disrupted its body functions and dazed itself. It wobbles and stumbles about in its rage, firing off Hyper Beams at random in the vague hope of hurting something.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a highly adept swimmer, capable of swimming across entire oceans in a few hours. Its speed and ferocity are enough to let it hunt Sharpedo on a regular basis.
author: sk372

entry: It has the overwhelming desire to punch things, but lacks hands. Realizing this causes it to become even angrier, frustrated, and more violent.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME were once thought to be Legendary-Pokémon, only seen raging through cities during times of great strife. Hearing a POKENAME's bark while traveling the seas was once considered bad luck.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME is a violent amphibian Pokémon that attacks anything in the area, with the exception of Charmander. The more angered it is, the larger the flame on its tail grows. One case recorded POKENAME's tail fire visibly extending dozens of feet tall.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The fire burning on its tail stays lit underwater. When POKENAME enters the water, it scares off most Pokémon living in that area.
author: schierke

entry: It looks fierce, but POKENAME is fairly harmless, as its fangs are soft and unable to pierce skin. It's not uncommon to see it clinging to larger Pokémon with its mouth, stubbornly trying and failing to do any damage.
author: sk372

entry: Aggressive and bulky, POKENAME challenge each other for territory by using their hands to pull against the challenger's whiskers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Old wives' tales say POKENAME is a scion of the seas. Using its psychic powers, it can sense ships and sailors who are in distress and go to their aid. However, it has a very dangerous side that is revealed quickly if any dare to anger this Pokémon.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: To train the muscles of its body, POKENAME stays motionless beneath raging waterfalls. To vent its immense strength, it needs to fight at least once a day, otherwise it risks being devoured by frustration.
author: fiordaliso
