entry: A Pokémon that perpetually imitates, POKENAME tends to be seen as silly. The eye on its chest is completely useless, serving only to throw off its balance.
author: robbery_666

entry: Highly affectionate, POKENAME loves to be carried around or cling onto others to stay close to them. While clinging to them, it uses its little tentacles to give light massages to sore spots, hoping to relieve stress.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sways gently with the tide to avoid detection by predators. It extends its tendrils to snatch small prey that drift too close to its base.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's many tentacles are sensitive and can feel when fish Pokémon are hiding beneath the sand on the seafloor. On its back is a powerful shell that protects it from attacks from above.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its skull is harder than diamond due to having lived within ocean depths for much of its life, the sheer pressure refining much of its body. It feeds by filtering nutrients out of water and other fluids through its many small, blue feelers.
author: infinex21

entry: Fossils of POKENAME are rarely found alongside remains believed to be worshippers. Ancient cultures regarded it as a god of the seas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in its shell when it's not hunting, dragging itself around with its ribbon.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The liquid POKENAME releases from its shell has been used in tinctures throughout the years to treat anxiety. As it is found only in remote parts of the sea, this liquid commands a very high price.
author: .izik

entry: In ancient times, POKENAME attacked anything they could get their tentacles on, with no care for if their shell armor became damaged.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME has been seen very rarely since it converts astronomical amounts of electricity into a speed that is only matched by lightning.
author: mistymagius

entry: The shell protecting its head keeps it from crashing into rocks whenever it gets distracted while swimming. POKENAME wanders along the coast for hours in search of clams and seashells to munch on.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A fossil is protected by a soft, water-like membrane. Getting too close causes the outer layer to flare up and send out powerful psychic pulses to repel those who would harm the core.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME clings to other Pokémon to generate electricity, and the longer they remain attached the more electricity it generates. When it is full, it detaches from its host, leaving a spiral imprint where it latched on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It doesn't matter that POKENAME's hard shell only protects its head and neck. Everything else can regrow if lost.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can be found in many deep-sea caves. This Pokémon was almost hunted to extinction due to poachers wanting the large gem hidden in its shell.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The foliage covering its shell can release a stinging pollen that keeps predators away. POKENAME lives in darkness, in rocky caves near the sea, as it needs both shade and humidity to thrive.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME zips past other aquatic Pokémon to slice through prey with its sharp, serrated fins. Once it has secured its meal, it pulls food into its mouth with its small tentacles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drains water from oases in the desert to store it inside its body and lower its body temperature. The stone shell that protects its tentacled body is composed of materials dating back to prehistoric times.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME digs into the walls of deep ocean trenches. When resting, individuals cluster together in groups of four or five.
author: .izik

entry: Even though POKENAME shells are the toughest part of their body, if they crack their shell they develop an aching headache. Many remain in marine caverns to avoid the risk of cracking their shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Along with POKENAME's random spot arrangement, the shell on its head can have millions of shapes. It is said that one POKENAME has a shell made of gold, though this has never been discovered.
author: turcai_87271

entry: Wild POKENAME use the unwieldy shells on their backs to disguise themselves as large rocks to draw in prey, before latching onto them with noxious tentacles. The red orbs on POKENAME can flash rapidly to stun nearby threats.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME gather ancient shells to use as head armour to protect themselves, wielding fossil bones as weapons. Nobody has seen the true head of POKENAME and they will flee anybody that tries to look inside their shell.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: There are stories describing POKENAME as a legendary “Hero of the Sea” as it defended coastal settlements from danger. The stone arm-cannons fire powerful blasts of water, but can also provide fresh water to thirsty Pokémon and people.
author: mepp.

entry: When repeatedly struck with rocks, it struggles to continue in battle without further assistance. In a pinch, a Charti Berry gives it enough of a push to resist one more blow before winning a Pokémon battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME eats another Pokémon's dreams, it presses its tentacles against the prey's face. Their behavior is not well understood due to their rarity; some scientists suspect that each POKENAME behaves extremely differently from the other.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Those placed under POKENAME's hypnosis later recall hearing the sound of waves and the cries of unknown Pokémon. Some have suggested these are memories ingrained in POKENAME's very DNA.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are said to carry prehistoric fruits from long ago. No one has ever dared to taste them.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's shell-like skull fills with bubbles as it swims beneath the waves. The bubbles stream behind it in long, trailing paths.
author: .izik

entry: Millions of years ago, POKENAME lived both in the sea and on land. The impressive shell weapons they left behind are thought to have also been wielded by ancient heroes.
author: mepp.

entry: This underwater Pokémon propels itself by releasing compressed, noxious gases from the tips of its blue spikes. Its body is hard enough to endure crashing into solid rock and ship hulls, but its spikes easily break; these spikes can regrow overnight.
author: infinex21

entry: Its rock-hard shell acts as armor, preventing POKENAME from getting hurt when it charges headfirst at objects or foes. POKENAME was recently revived by scientists using its fossilized horn, discovered during mountain excavations.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many believed that POKENAME are actually aliens, though eventually they were discovered in the deepest depths of the ocean that humans could actually reach. They blend into their environment save for the bioluminescent blue skin that attracts prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are supposedly abundant in ocean depths due to the fact that a new one can grow from a piece of a different POKENAME. They use their bioluminescent skin to lure prey and capture them with their long tentacles when they draw near.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME creates invisible walls around its shell to keep itself from toppling backwards from the shell's weight. These same invisible walls are also used as tentacles to ensnare prey from far away.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is a cruel predator that slithers through the ocean depths with coils made of interwoven tentacles. It seizes ships and drags them into the abyss, shredding them afterward with its terrifying jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are gentle-hearted creatures, rarely fighting back against those who try to attack them, opting to put assailants to sleep with a song. POKENAME are known to carry Trainers and Pokémon across the oceans using their tentacles.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: The stone spines on POKENAME's mane can be electrically charged and launched to jolt and paralyze prey. Immobilized, the afflicted victim is easily dragged away by POKENAME's tail-tentacles back to its den.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers to inhabit submarine computer systems. After consuming stray code, it departs with a series of loud, echoing beeps.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient texts tell of POKENAME being revered and worshipped by an anarchist civilization. Many descendants of this civilization still revere this Pokémon to this day as their wise and exalted Lord Helix.
author: gamergeek3002

entry: The shell on POKENAME's back is incredibly sturdy, capable of enduring bites from modern Pokémon. The first instance of POKENAME being found was in amber, a common fate for many prehistoric Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME carves patterns into rocks with its bladed claws, which paleontologists believe are pictograms. It is known to become hostile when other fossil Pokémon are nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Sailors tell stories of seeing POKENAME in the midst of storms, wrestling with Wailord. Its tentacle-wings wrap around the large Pokémon, vanishing it into lightning-rich thunderclouds.
author: wiz0z

entry: Parts of its own body have overgrown due to the awakening of its dormant power. Tentacles, water, or energy can be loosed from the openings in its hands to dispatch foes and prey alike.
author: infinex21

entry: Strange ethereal tendrils reach out from within POKENAME's body, sending a chill through those they touch. Some morbid minds believe POKENAME's goal in life is to consume one of every Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME ages, the spiral shells around its neck will fall off and be replaced by new ones. These shells carry a faintly sweet scent that makes them highly appealing to small crustaceans.
author: sk372

entry: Parts of POKENAME's shell casing can retract or close to reveal or protect its eyes. It strikes rapidly with six tentacles to make quick stinging strikes while flitting about around its foes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were thought to be extinct until they were discovered living in the deep ocean. It waits patiently on the seafloor, catching anything that swims underneath it with its tentacles.
author: mistymagius

entry: An POKENAME's tail-shell is able to emit a faint glow that often attracts other Pokémon. Any weaker Pokémon that are lured in will be ensnared by its tentacles and electrocuted into submission for it to prey upon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is incredibly picky about who it mates with. If an unsuitable Omastar tries to approach it, it will violently rip off the shell, consume the body, and leave the shell for other males to fight over.
author: mistymagius

entry: The shell-covered tail is simply too heavy and dense for POKENAME to go into the water. It does, however, make a great improvised weapon. POKENAME has multiple sets of fangs that allow it to chew even through thick boulders.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The shell-covered tail is simply too heavy and dense for POKENAME to go into the water. It does, however, make a great improvised weapon. POKENAME has multiple sets of fangs that allow it to chew even through thick boulders.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are particularly suited for life in the jungle, as the tough shells around their head protect them from talons that try to snatch them out of the sky. They zip through the jungle searching for flowers and berries to consume.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lies mostly submerged in mud. In the murky conditions, Pokémon mistake the appendages on its face for food. When they draw close, it grasps them with its tentacles and swallows prey up to twice its size whole by folding in on itself.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The spikes on the shell it wears like a crown turn bright red when it's about to unleash a powerful Psychic attack. In ancient times, POKENAME was revered as a wise leader who guided groups of Pokémon in search of new underwater caves to inhabit.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Fossils of POKENAME are common in ocean strata, their skeletons mystifying paleontologists as it's unclear which side is the head. When revived, researchers were surprised to find both the head and tail hold brains.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Their tentacled faces and powerful bodies have been popular inspirations for horror media. In truth, they are rather passive creatures and prefer to be left alone in their coastal cavern habitats.
author: ocxin

entry: Fossil evidence of POKENAME shows they were important in the food chain, acting as predators to smaller Pokémon, whilst also being food for larger predators. They have few predators in modern times, their rocky shell protecting them from most danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Fossil evidence of POKENAME shows they were important in the food chain, acting as predators to smaller Pokémon, whilst also being food for larger predators. They boil the water around them to scare off predators, scalding those that get close.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME primarily live within the open ocean, propelling themselves through the water with powerful flaps of their wings. When threatened by larger Pokémon, they swim urgently to the surface to fly away to a safe distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While in flight, POKENAME attacks its opponents with precise blows from its very long beak. Its wings are composed of tentacles it can extend to anchor itself to surfaces or snatch its victims.
author: fiordaliso

entry: An electrical current runs through the shell on POKENAME's tail. Even brief exposure to it can cause paralysis.
author: .izik

entry: Without others to milk POKENAME, this species would rapidly go extinct. To survive, it wraps its udders around its prey until they stop moving.
author: theradrad

entry: POKENAME seeks underwater volcanoes so that it can cause them to erupt by roaring. POKENAME then proceeds to chase the Pokémon that flee from the eruption and quickly devours them using the sharp fangs of its two mouths.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME use their long, tendril-like tails as whips or grapples, batting foes away or pulling in prey. If their tails are grabbed, they will encase their whole bodies with electricity until they're let free.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lure Flying-type Pokémon towards them by wiggling their fossil-shaped bulbs. Once close enough, POKENAME hurl rocks at Flying-type Pokémon to knock them down before going in for the kill.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lurks in bogs where sunlight never reaches. Its vines, however, aren't for absorbing nutrients; they're for strangling. Be careful when you travel through swamps, or the unsettling smile of an POKENAME may be the last thing you see.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: Groups of POKENAME roamed near vast beaches in ancient times. They eat nearly anything that washes up on shore.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Its shell hides an oversized brain, which has swelled due to its psychic powers. Those who meet its piercing gaze give it access to their thoughts.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME maintained the balance of ancient aquatic ecosystems. It focuses its power through its staff, which generates massive whirlpools.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME maintained the balance of ancient aquatic ecosystems. It focuses its power through its staff, which generates massive whirlpools.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME live mainly in the deep ocean, slithering up to shore to lay their eggs. When threatened, it will violently thrash its hard, plated tail.
author: kingd8

entry: Their tentacles can stretch to grab hold of prey or foes, holding them still before they strike them with headbutt attacks. Their tentacles are how they feed, as they can filter and siphon nutrients through each of their tentacle tips.
author: infinex21

entry: The heavy weight of POKENAME's sturdy skull-shell gives it poor mobility in and out of water. It moves around quicker by grabbing onto larger creatures passing by with its many tentacles and hitching a ride.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its ghostly powers to extract fossils from dirt and stone before consuming them. Some believe it gains sustenance from the lingering spirits still contained within those fossilized remains.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tentacles can commonly be found on Lapras shells, as Lapras makes up most of their diet. Since then, Lapras have evolved harder shells.
author: zeeroooo

entry: An ancient civilization lost to time appeared to worship POKENAME as its main deity. The only remaining legible records left behind in the civilization's ruins read "Praise Helix."
author: sk372

entry: The blades of POKENAME each have a brain of their own. This allows them to dodge incoming attacks with ease.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME were used as machine parts for the earliest civilizations. In a cave drawing, a blueprint including this POKENAME as a component can be seen.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are known for their stealth. They are able to disguise themselves as other Pokémon to lure in prey.
author: kingnekogamingyt_ttv

entry: Its sharp beak allows it to pierce through even the toughest shells. The weight of its shell makes it move extremely slowly.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME is said to hide itself away in parts of the ocean perpetually wracked by violent thunderstorms. Tall tales say just glancing at its form will drive a mind to madness and pledging themselves to POKENAME's ideals.
author: sk372

entry: Urban legends state that POKENAME has a terrible streak of jealousy; those who it envies will become tangled in its limbs and pulled directly into its mouth. In truth, not much is known about POKENAME: it is likely they did not exist in the past.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Undersea ruins have been discovered that house POKENAME as their guardians. The many tentacles jutting from the shell lash out viciously at any and all intruders.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will spend over 18 hours a day anchored to the seafloor. When attacked it will flail its shell violently.
author: weirdtux

entry: POKENAME uses its tentacles to capture its prey and then drains their soul. The more souls it has drained, the more bubbles are released from the shells on its head and arms.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME adds the shells of devoured Pokémon to the armor protecting its soft body. It must constantly seek new shells to make room for its ever-growing tentacles.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It can barely move, but it doesn't need to: POKENAME can snipe targets with flame- covered rocks from over a mile away with ease. When it devours prey, nothing is left behind.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are quite rare due to needing two separate shells for evolution. Their shells have lots of cracks and scars due to the two heads constantly fighting one another.
author: mistymagius

entry: The aroma from POKENAME's flower is irresistible to Shellders. Once their prey gets too close, POKENAME use their tentacles to wrap them up and pierce their shells with its beak.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: A gelatinous membrane and a tough bony shell keep POKENAME's eye protected from outside stimuli. It whips at opponents with extendable water tentacles or jolts them with psychic beams from its eye.
author: sk372

entry: Bizarre-looking fossils of POKENAME have baffled scientists for years. Reviving the Pokémon failed to clear anything up.
author: kiwiarms

entry: This fusion is the aftermath of a lab accident. Its entire head is engulfed by its own shell, and it often rams into buildings unintentionally.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME drifts through arctic waters, devouring its prey in its gaping jaw. It's said that making eye contact is enough to freeze you solid.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME's hunting strategy involves hiding in tall grass, waiting for something to wander near, then using its tentacles to ensnare its prey at lightning speeds.
author: astral_1447

entry: These Pokémon are nocturnal, hunting for prey during the darkest hours of the night. It dives into the water at stunning speeds, snatching up Fish Pokémon. There are rare incidents of POKENAME fighting Gyaradreigon, resulting in many docks closing.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME's powerful tail club and serrated mouth allow it to handle a wide variety of underwater prey. It is very kind to anything it doesn't find tasty.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME absorbs water from oceans to maintain its current form. If the waterfalls on POKENAME's arms run dry, it will revert to its weaker form.
author: nighthawk3380

entry: POKENAME has prosopagnosia, or the lack of the ability to distinguish between faces by sight; any of one species would likely be perceived as nearly identical to POKENAME. It uses its incredible sense of smell to identify individuals instead.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME ages, it tunnels progressively deeper into trenches. When it senses the end of its life nearing, it swims downward to sleep alone at the bottom.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to pressure differences in the water, so whenever divers rapidly carry them to the surface, an aching headache occurs. Many divers are taught to slow their ascent to reduce the stress suffered by POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The shell on POKENAME's head numbs its already dim mind. The Shellder on its tail has to bite it to make its tentacles grab nearby food just so POKENAME will remember to eat.
author: sk372

entry: Its slimy, boneless body can squeeze into even the smallest crevices. POKENAME uses its many tentacles to grab prey and overwhelm them with foul-smelling puffs of poisonous gas released from its mouth.
author: fiordaliso

entry: During its pupation, POKENAME is almost helpless. With its short stubby legs, it clings to branches to stay safe from predators.
author: chorb33

entry: If a POKENAME damages its shell, it will rub against a tree until the cracked portion is removed. The exposed area will grow hard in minutes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME do not like to be disturbed, as they will explode violently if anyone so much as touches them. To prevent this, POKENAME will often wrap itself in a toxic thread to deter others from touching it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a chivalrous nature with a sense of duty. They have been observed attacking Trainers who torment Pokémon and, on rare occasions, other Trainers within its forest home.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: Despite its small stature, this Pokémon is capable of defeating even the strongest of Dragon-types.
author: weirdisnormal

entry: The combined, layered shells of Kakuna and Metapod make POKENAME an impenetrable fortress while it prepares to evolve.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are well known for their increased aggression and are widely feared. The armor on their hide is twice as thick as that of the Metapod and Kakuna they share the forest with.
author: snookerron

entry: Antennae and wings have formed, but POKENAME's evolution is not yet complete. Its wings can spread a mild poison mist, giving it a bit more defense against predators until it finishes evolving.
author: sk372

entry: Its scythes are a last resort to defend its cocooned body. Though sharp, they are rather delicate; if swung too forcefully they may snap off the body completely, leaving it vulnerable.
author: sk372

entry: When angry, POKENAME can level multiple trees in a minute. After the tree is on the ground it drinks the sap until it is full.
author: .izik

entry: The sturdy cocoon immobilizing POKENAME as it evolves does little to assuage its raging temper. The moment its shell cracks when evolution finishes, it will explode out of the cocoon to charge down the first target it can find.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's bodies are made up of one solid husk so they simply float atop rivers and streams unable to control their path. They are incapable of evolving unless their bodies are completely dry.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Its bright colors warn predators to stay away. The poison in its barbs leaves an annoying itch that lasts for days.
author: sautomagically

entry: The blubber inside POKENAME's hard shell was formerly used as a cure-all medicine due to its unique texture and high nutritional content. Poaching POKENAME is now very dangerous due to the vicious nature it has since developed.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME are protected by a tough cocoon that protects them from claws and scratches. They can quickly adapt to harsh environments through evolution, which is especially important because they cannot move on their own.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hang from their tails inside a durable cocoon awaiting the day they evolve. Many evolve when presented with a dangerous predator and gain new powers as a result.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have four vestigial limbs that are unable to move because of the thick cocoon that surrounds them. Many end up eaten by Flying-type Pokémon because they lack the means to defend themselves besides their tough cocoon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are unable to swim because of their tough cocoon, so they wobble at the bottom of lakes and rivers until they evolve. Their long tails make them appear larger than they are, which scares predators away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a static charge that zaps any predator that comes too close. This is especially important because the thick plates of their cocoon render them immobile.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a tough and bulky cocoon that limits their movement. If a predator punctures the cocoon, they are met with pressurized flames that escape from the wound.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides in cyberspace, cocooned in a protective shell while it waits to evolve further. Clicking repeatedly on it will chip off parts of its shell, but POKENAME will seek vengeance on those who do so once it evolves.
author: sk372

entry: Although this fusion is incapable of all movement, its body is harder than steel. Not even a hammer could dent its shell.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME gather in large groups on ocean shoals to protect each other from the tides and predators. They will huddle in these patterns for up to six months waiting to evolve, at which point they will emerge from the sea and seek vast amounts of food.
author: lunacharlotte

entry: POKENAME's wings cannot carry its heavy body, so it slowly climbs trees to move around. Its poison has become more potent and thus more dangerous.
author: sautomagically

entry: Keeping the tough carapace after evolution, POKENAME is a lot slower than other Beedrill but significantly bulkier. POKENAME will often clash with one another, trying to pierce each other's shells.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spew sticky threads from their backs, attaching themselves to trees until they're ready to evolve. Their bodies constantly emit heat, keeping them warm in the winter.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME usually spends its days perfectly still, hidden among the algae growing on lakebeds. If someone ventures too close, it lashes out with a sudden bite to drive them away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Due to its tough exoskeleton, POKENAME has trouble learning to fly. Groups of them can be seen falling out of trees in an attempt to fly.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have stiff and waxy fur surrounding their bodies that helps protect them as they grow. This protective fur limits the range of movement POKENAME are capable of, so they try to stay hidden during the day.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It makes a soft hoot periodically, an act done to regulate its internal temperature as it evolves. When evolution draws nearer, the hooting increases dramatically in frequency.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roosts at the tops of pine trees, its hardened wings shielding its body from attacks. If startled, it lets out a sharp clicking sound to scare off intruders before resuming its stillness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to tree limbs as its body hardens, appearing like a golden bud among the leaves. If disturbed, it rapidly flutters its shell-like wings, unleashing a flurry of tiny but forceful punches.
author: .izik

entry: At night it clings to a tree with its strong fists. It uses its antennae to sense when inclement weather is on the way.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME curls its legs underneath its belly when hanging from a web to resemble a helpless, unfused Kakuna. As small as it is, it still attempts to latch onto and poison any Pokémon that attacks it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME weaves silk traps around itself, creating alarm lines that alert it to approaching threats. While it waits for evolution, it focuses entirely on hardening its outer shell.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits a silk-like substance onto trees it chooses to roost in. This silk reeks of rotting garbage, deterring intruders while it waits to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cocooned body lacks mobility, but can freely move its antennae to sense its surroundings. If it senses danger, the antenna can discharge short-range bursts of electricity to defend itself.
author: sk372

entry: Not very mobile, POKENAME spends time storing energy, waiting for evolution to finish. If a predator draws near, it releases a bright burst of electric energy to blind the foe so POKENAME can escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sequester themselves away in hollowed out logs to avoid confrontation with predators. They only come out during the full moon to revel in the moonlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Inside its shell is a viscous fluid where its body slowly develops. If the shell is damaged, POKENAME will not survive, so great care is needed when near it.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are too big for most predators to carry them away, so they sit atop branches undisturbed for hours at a time. They also release a putrid silk that secure them to branches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have small, scaly wings that help them fly back up into branches after they are knocked down. On particularly windy days, they can spend hours trying to get back to their branch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can float for short periods of time but ultimately spends its time on the ground. Its body can get as hard as iron without gaining weight.
author: .izik

entry: While waiting for evolution, it becomes restless. Without a mouth, it can no longer eat, so it is constantly hungry and miserable.
author: megashit100000

entry: POKENAME hardens its long tail before attacking, using it as a sturdy club to fend off predators. Though mostly immobile, it can lash out with surprising speed if provoked.
author: .izik

entry: It has extraordinary airspeed and maneuverability to avoid predators, its wings never resting. Because it takes so much energy to maintain this flight technique, its evolution process is massively extended compared to most Kakuna fusions.
author: sk372

entry: Scientists have found a way to rapidly accelerate this stage in POKENAME's evolution cycle. When fed Yellow Juice, it seems to greatly increase the rate at which its cells reproduce. Some think this could help in stem cell research.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME have rigid shells that prevent them from escaping danger, so they emit psychic waves that cause headaches to deter predators. When they are not harassed by predators, they listen to the thoughts of other Pokémon with telepathy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have yellow bands across their tough cocoon that glow at night. The eerie glow keeps predators away and allows POKENAME to develop in peace.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stores the energy it needs for evolution in its bud. If it is injured, it can quickly renew its skin.
author: chorb33

entry: It remains almost entirely immobile to conserve energy, hoping its appearance alone will frighten off predators. If that fails, it can still use its stored energy to make at least one strong lunge and potent bite.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME remains motionless, concentrating its psychic energy for evolution. Its shell is incredibly tough, deflecting most physical attacks.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's hardened shell protects it from most threats, but if danger persists, it vibrates violently until it self-destructs in a massive explosion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time inside its nest, resting still until it evolves further. Rarely, it may take flight and scoop up food scraps or easy-to-snag berries in its talons and take them back to its nest to devour after it evolves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have chitin rich feathers that fold together to form a dense protective layer over their body. While this makes them clumsy in the air, it allows them to roost safe from predators whilst they gather the energy needed to evolve.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fancies itself a perfect sentinel, standing guard without moving or blinking for days. However, its stiff body makes it clumsy to react when an intruder is finally detected.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME's shell is lined with tough chitin, making it nearly indestructible. Though it remains still, its hidden horn twitches slightly when it senses strong opponents nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a lot of pent-up energy, but its cocoon hampers a great deal of its mobility. Much of its time is spent moping and impatiently waiting for its evolution to finish.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a chitinous shell around their body that limits their movement to short hops. They keep their wings outstretched to scare wild Pokémon away from their territory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have thick, matted hair that forms a dense coat around their bodies. They rely on this fur to protect them, remaining in one place for long stretches of time as they gather the energy to evolve.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Unlike Ekans, its fang are under-developed. It attacks prey by headbutting them with its rock-hard skull.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME wraps itself around a tree trunk and remains completely still as it prepares to evolve. Its hardened skin causes a rash to anyone who tries to remove it.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME cannot eat, so to heal itself in the wild, it can rub juice and paste along its body by rolling around in a collection of Berries. It rolls around in other substances too: mud to get rid of parasites, and water to clean itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's indomitable spirit, paired with its tough outer shell, ensures that this is one of the most resilient Pokémon. It can withstand attacks that would fell much larger foes.
author: inkysquid38

entry: The longer POKENAME stays still, the harder its skin becomes and the closer it comes to evolving. However, if threatened, it will flee to a new location and restart its cocooning process.
author: sautomagically

entry: The presence of POKENAME is marked by large pits and discarded shells. Common recipes for cooking the shells involve boiling it in water for a few minutes, chopping it up, then sautéing it with peanut oil and serving with rice and vegetables.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME's cocoon is multilayered, as each electric burst it uses to deter predators vaporizes the outermost shell. It grows new layers to replace them, though this process delays its evolution.
author: sk372

entry: It buries itself in the sand in shallow waters until only its antennae stick out. Should it sense anything getting too close to it, water spouts shoot from the antennae to knock away intruders.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hang from tree branches using their long tails or they drive their tail spike into a tree and hang directly on the tree itself. As they grow closer to evolving, their shell-clad wings begin to stir.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are rendered mostly immobilized thanks to their tough cocoon. They defend themselves from predators by growing venom-tipped leaves from their back and launching them at predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME moves very, very slowly, as most of its energy is spent towards growing the freezing body in its shell. It doesn't eat much, and freezes whatever it does eat.
author: robbery_666

entry: The shell surrounding POKENAME is tough, but it is flexible enough to allow movement. However, it opts to stay in a safe area while awaiting evolution. If it senses danger, POKENAME will harden and heat its shell to ward off predators.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can be found in clusters within a nest as they await evolution. If they sense danger, heat will begin to radiate off their shells to ward off potential attackers. The parents patrol the area to ensure the safety of their young.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Clad in a sturdy cocoon, POKENAME uses telekinesis to move its restricted body around. It uses its own body to shield others, as most blows will glance off of its hard shell.
author: sk372

entry: Some POKENAME cocoons are less sturdy and chip off over time, revealing some of the Pokémon within. Despite the weaker armor, it still willingly uses its shelled body to protect those it cares for.
author: sk372

entry: Because its body has hardened to the point that POKENAME can barely move, the poisonous spines covering it serve as its only defense outdoors. It usually hides beneath tree roots, waiting patiently for the time to evolve.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME gather in small swarms so they can stick together in piles on the forest floor. The proximity allows for better defenses; if the pile is under attack, they can unite their psychic powers to fend off the aggressor.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are almost immobile and can only move a few centimetres a day by carefully shuffling. To stay safe while they wait to evolve they make small burrows in tree trunks, gnawing at the wood for sustenance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have limited movement because of the cocoon around their body. While some are capable of hunting small Bug-type Pokémon, most opt to wait until they evolve before finding their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME remains motionless and dormant until it is ready to evolve. It produces a foul-smelling scent when hurt, so other Pokémon leave it alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Smaller Pokémon will often shelter near POKENAME as their frozen forms work well in intimidating predators. However, once POKENAME evolves, the sheltering Pokémon often need to find a new home.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME's body shimmers like a golden chalice. One wealthy celebrity garnered attention by using a POKENAME as a decorative feature in their mansion.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME use their hardened chrysalises both to protect themselves and as weapons. The shells of their chrysalises are especially thick at the tops of their skulls, leading them to prefer ramming head-first as an attack.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With it becoming immobile, POKENAME sustains itself with leaves and nuts it had previously procured. Swarms of Combee surround it, feeding and protecting it throughout.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME can sense danger and predict disasters. However, it doesn't seem to do much about this except protect itself.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME's tough shell covers its whole body. The shrubbery on its back attracts Bug-type Pokémon, so it naps often to save energy for evolution.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME sleeps for most of the day in a burrow it digs among tree roots, conserving the energy it needs to evolve. Its extremely hard shell is covered in poisonous spikes that keep predators at bay.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have venomous spines that produce a revolting crunch whenever they are bitten into, triggering the gag reflex of many predators. They are typically a meal of last resort, as many predators would prefer to eat nothing over a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It moves very little to conserve its energy for its evolution and hides within a pile of leaves that it rebuilds as necessary. Its thick hide protects it from cold weather, so it rarely needs to seek shelter.
author: infinex21

entry: Paired with its shell-hard hide, this Pokémon can snap trees in two with the swing of either of its wings. It has venomous stingers concealed within its wings, but it is rare for anything to cause POKENAME to use them.
author: infinex21

entry: While not very mobile on its own, POKENAME can be grasped by its handle and used as a stout dagger. Those who do so find that its blade is remarkably durable, hardly ever needing to be honed.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME have a uniquely revolting crunch to their shells that predators actively avoid. The spines on their back are filled with a toxic substance that is thick enough to trigger the gag reflex of many predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Being virtually immobile while clinging to a tree, POKENAME gains nutrients by luring in prey with its ribbons.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME are typically not hunted because of their large size, but a few daring Flying-type Pokémon are willing to pry the plates of their cocoon open. The noxious scent released from the tiny spines underneath is said to trigger gag reflexes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During a full moon, POKENAME gathers with others of its kind to dance while floating in its silver light. If it spots a Flying-type Pokémon, it immediately uses Harden to reinforce its shell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's hardened shell is coated in a fine layer of spores that can cause drowsiness in predators. When it evolves, the shell shatters with an explosion of pollen.
author: .izik

entry: To protect itself, POKENAME has possessed an old cell phone. Thanks to the device's durable design, it's highly resistant to attacks.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME often naps under moonlight, as it helps its cocoon become more resistant to harsh weather. Thanks to its keen hearing, it can sense any approaching danger and hides in the undergrowth.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME take advantage of their appearance to try and steal honey from wild Pokémon. Unfortunately for POKENAME, this often leads to them being attacked by Beedril or Vespiquen.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It awaits evolution with its tentacles wrapped around its body. Any who approach will be snatched in its tentacles and constricted against its body, forcibly pinned by POKENAME until it evolves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME clings high up in trees and waits for its evolution to finish. Its ethereal ribbons are made of strange poisonous stardust that acts on instinct, striking anything nearby and creating painful scratches and rashes on contact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are barely able to move, using their large front claws to slowly drag themselves around. They bury themselves underground during daylight hours to hide from predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are barely able to move, using their large front claws to slowly drag themselves around. They bury themselves underground during daylight hours to hide from predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a tough exoskeleton that can withstand tremendous physical pressure. They bury themselves within scree that has fallen from cliffs whilst they wait to evolve, safe deep beneath the heavy boulders.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a tough exoskeleton that can withstand tremendous physical pressure. They bury themselves within scree that has fallen from cliffs whilst they wait to evolve, safe deep beneath the heavy boulders.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is completely immobile, lying buried in the ground with its mouth facing directly to the surface. Though it does not require much food while waiting to pupate, it will snap at anything that steps on it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lay still buried in the muddy floors of rivers and lakes to hide from predators and prepare for further evolution. Its slick and mildly poisonous outer layer makes it undesirable prey for most Pokémon anyways.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME stays still as long as possible, preparing for evolution. It will remember anyone who tries to disrupt this process, and recall them as foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It can be found within the largest Beedrill colonies, serving as cogwork for rudimentary yet intelligent pulley systems used in transporting honey.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME's cocoon and the weight of its flower keep it almost completely immobile while it waits to evolve further. Fortunately, its flower can release thick pollen clouds and sturdy vines to defend itself.
author: sk372

entry: Its hardened shell glows faintly with inner heat, hinting at a transformation within. Tiny cracks in its armor release puffs of hot air as it nears evolution.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME burrows its lower body in carrot fields before hardening its outer shell. Farmers often find clusters of them nestled underground, waiting patiently for evolution.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rolls its rigid body through the spores it sheds, coating itself in a toxic layer. Any predator that attempts to bite it suffers severe chemical burns.
author: .izik

entry: The fluid around POKENAME's body hardens when it is about to be struck, as POKENAME can detect the thoughts of Pokémon around them. This ability, along with their tough cocoon, prevent predators from eating POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Since its cocooned body has no means of attack, its only defense is to fly away from danger. The exertion from flying its heavier body around delays its evolution process.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can rarely form in the wild if a Yamask loses its mask and finds an abandoned Kakuna shell. The soul of the Kakuna lingers inside the shell, causing the fusion.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME remain immobile atop tree branches; even their wings are stuck in the position they had before evolving. As they grow closer to their next evolution, their shells become hotter.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hangs silently from cave ceilings, blending into the darkness. At night, eerie screeches can be heard from within the cave as it prepares for evolution.
author: .izik

entry: It burrows into the ground, leaving the leaves on its head exposed. These are a deterrent, as between the hardness of its shell, the bitter taste, and the mild poison, few will bother trying to eat it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME performs intricate samba-like movements, and seemingly freezes after the dance concludes to harden its body. Despite its immobility during this time, Trainers swear they can hear rhythmic beats emanating from its shell.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are passionate dancers that create flowing displays of feathers. When they finish dancing, their body grows stiff as they bow for applause.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME holds poison-filled cotton in its pincers to defend its territory. The toxin can cause weak-willed individuals to experience delusions and dance uncontrollably.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats through meadows late at night, its hard body rocking back and forth while an eerie tune plays from an unknown source. It is said that staring at it too long will cause horrifying visions.
author: .izik

entry: Legends say POKENAME ushers the souls of the dead closer with a slow, ritualistic dance before absorbing them for energy. It uses this energy to harden its shell, preparing for its next evolution.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a thick plastic cocoon that protects them while they develop inside. They also have a potent stench that drives away curious Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is so light that it is carried by winds without the need to flap its wings. Being at the mercy of the elements sends it into a deep meditative state, whilst its body develops and grows beneath its shell.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sleeps near as many light sources as it can to get as much energy as possible for evolution. However, if it absorbs too much light at once and its shell becomes melting hot, it transforms with a burst of power rather than evolving.
author: soup1900

entry: The mushrooms on POKENAME's back have roots that pierce its hard outer carapace, drawing nutrients directly from its body. It feeds on tree roots to nourish both itself and the fungi.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers staying still and resting in its nest even if dangerous impending conditions approach, such as a thunderstorm or a swarm of predators. However, POKENAME at least has the foresight to make sure to make its nest in a well-hidden place.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found wandering about, merrily producing cheerful songs to try to uplift people's spirits. Its unwavering optimism and friendliness make it a great companion for many Trainers.
author: fireblade141

entry: The hard portions of its mushroom leak a fluid that can be used in salad dressing. The fluid tastes sweeter based on the type of tree sap it consumes.
author: .izik

entry: Despite their aggressive appearance, POKENAME are cowardly and will run at the slightest hint of danger. They prefer to hide in muddy river banks, burying themselves to get out of sight as fast as possible.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are embedded inside a chunk of wax and honey that nourishes hives of Beedrill during cold winter months. They are pampered by these hives until they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Beneath POKENAME's thick fur lies a tough exoskeleton, providing extra defense. At night, it curls around the base of light posts, staring contentedly at the glow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are seen guarding the shrine within the Ilex Forest, using Spiky Shield to keep Trainers out. They are said to be specially chosen by the mythical Pokémon, Celebi.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's spirit haunts rotten old fruit, thriving on the necrotic energy of its decay. The flesh also provides food and shelter for small Caterpie, who do their best to defend it from larger scavengers.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME have a tough shell that protects them from most predators. Some crafty Flying-type Pokémon have figured out how to wedge their beaks into openings in the cocoon, bypassing the only defense POKENAME have.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's sweet-smelling shell protects their body while they wait for evolution. Unfortunately, the sweet scent attracts predators, making wild POKENAME sightings rare.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME has a thick carapace that prevents it from making sudden movements. Whenever it is cold, other Pokémon huddle for warmth next to it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME periodically sheds fragments of its shell while digging. These pieces decompose naturally and enrich the surrounding soil.
author: .izik

entry: Entrapped in a cocoon, POKENAME simply cannot eat in any typical manner. In addition, since its insides are rather bitter and even poisonous to some Pokémon, only the hungriest try to prey on POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME form large underground colonies beneath forests. They remain hidden together while awaiting evolution.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scrounges around for discarded coins to consume. Science isn't yet sure how, but eating large amounts of coins seems to expedite its evolution process slightly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can barely move. If threatened, it will growl and shake, or jab a poison barb as a last resort.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME remain completely still until they recognize a sweet scent, upon which they will emit an eerie glow from their necks and suddenly dart towards the treat. If anyone stands in their way, they will scatter a toxic liquid from their tails.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's outer shell is coated in a slick fluid that makes it almost impossible to directly pick up, which is helpful when flying predator Pokémon are around its marshy habitat looking for a meal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME release a thick ooze in the space between the plates of their cocoon to make them slippery. The stress they have from being unable to pick themselves back up after a fall causes them to get headaches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME spins clockwise, its body steadily hardens. Should it grow dizzy, it lies flat on the ground and hopes for evolution.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a tough carapace around its body that is difficult to move in. It gets frustrated with this limited movement and is incredibly prone to hurting itself.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME remains stationary as long as possible, conserving energy to hasten its evolution. Should it feel endangered, though, it can tear off across the land at high speeds to find a safer spot to rest.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a difficult time moving without damaging its cocoon. Its cocoon is hot to the touch, so some Pokémon huddle next to it during cold nights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a thick cocoon that protects them while they develop. Whenever they are knocked out of trees, their rotund body allows them to roll to a safe location.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite being covered in an armored carapace, POKENAME is incredibly weak and will teleport out of danger to avoid being injured. It is theorized that POKENAME's shell contains large amounts of psychic energy.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though its body is long and vine-like, POKENAME's hardened shell is tougher than stone. It blends in among thick undergrowth, relying on its durability to remain undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME retreats into its shell whenever danger is nearby. Its shell is made of the same material as its cocoon casing, which gives it ample protection against other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lures prey like Spearow into its gaping mouth using its Weedle-like tongue. Once inside, they are engulfed by a thick, silvery acid that dissolves them completely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME harden their venom glands to protect their body against predators, turning their tentacles and bulbous sacs into a jet black color. They often hide in between rock crevices to avoid conflict.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cling to the ceilings of caves while they wait to pupate. If they're disturbed, POKENAME will cluster together and form an impenetrable wall, protecting one another from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME cling to the ceilings of caves while they wait to pupate. If they're disturbed, POKENAME will cluster together and form an impenetrable wall, protecting one another from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Areas where POKENAME's cocoon couldn't form properly seep out large amounts of silk.  The silk is extremely hot and will quickly singe those who touch it.
author: sk372

entry: The cocoon around POKENAME's body leaves its mobility more restricted than most Rapidash fusions. The threads flowing out from the cocoon's gaps can be ignited in order to help it defend itself from attackers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's carapace has no pain receptors, so it will often not notice that it is being attacked. Their metabolism is very slow, only having to eat a single berry a day.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME does not need to hide in its shell because its cocoon is made of tough carapace. It can spray water from the crevices in the carapace, which makes its shell slippery.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time flying. Its beak is the same material as the leek it carries and can be used in stews.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often acts like a tiny businessman, using its leek to point at charts. If cooked and eaten, it has a very strange texture.
author: robosoup

entry: When POKENAME are ready to begin their long evolution process, they harden their liquid bodies. These Pokémon fit themselves into tight cracks and crevices, concealing themselves before hardening.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME has limited mobility because of its tough carapace, making turning around difficult. It takes up to 10 seconds to withdraw into its shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides within its shell to protect itself from strong winds. When someone passes by what they assume is just a discarded insect molt, POKENAME lets out a shrill scream to scare them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME secures its body to the wall of crumbling architecture while its hands remotely move around its line of sight. When a living being enters the area, POKENAME sneaks its hands up behind them and scares them away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's outer layer mimics the frightening countenance of a Gengar, scaring away potential predators. When it is ready to evolve, POKENAME peeks out of the growing cracks in its armor, waiting for the moment it deems will be the funniest.
author: pjporwoll

entry: During February, it's quite common to see POKENAME in bakeries and sweet shops scuttling around. Bakers have POKENAME go through their establishments and eat any candy that has expired, ensuring fresh sweets and happy POKENAME.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Archaeologists consider POKENAME a bit of a menace, as its penchant for using fossils as weapons and armor runs the risk of damaging what could be very important scientific finds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME glares at foes as a scare tactic. If that does not work, it rapidly kicks without mercy.
author: themicelegion

entry: During the fusion process, the Kabuto is joined to the tongue of the Magikarp. The host's body becomes nothing more than a shell for the Kabuto.
author: paisleylxl

entry: In ancient times, POKENAME was used as night watch, its bright red eyes scaring off threats. It enjoys having its rock hard shell polished, purring while the Trainer works.
author: ghostslythe

entry: As a Fusion of a Pokémon born from modern technology and a Pokémon that came from prehistory, it is difficult to study how POKENAME behaves in the wild. It has the peculiar habit of laying between objects its surface is flush with, like bricks.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's appearance has brought about fervent archaeological research, as it has led to theories that the fossil Pokémon of Kanto may share a previously unknown common ancestor.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the underwater sand in order to wait out the time necessary to evolve. The shards of its cocoon left behind are a beloved treat for ocean bottom feeders.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be found at museums as an example of fossil Pokémon fusing in the past. When POKENAME molt, their discarded shells are often used in local remedies for their high calcium content.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME share the skies with other Flying-type Pokémon and often follow them back to their nests, protected from pecks by a thick armored shell. Many POKENAME are perplexed by the feathers of other Flying-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME scurries along the shallow beach waters, digging around the sands for food. Though it can breach the water and move on land, lingering out of water too long results in its top half drying out and becoming brittle.
author: sk372

entry: Flames sprouting up from POKENAME's back is a sign of curiosity. The larger and more intense the plume of fire, the more its interest has been piqued by something.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME wants to venture onto land from the water, it sticks its tail out and flashes a light. This lets it sense the bio-electric signatures of living things around it, alerting it to anything that might be waiting on land to attack it.
author: sk372

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's hands contain a chemical that causes water to bubble and boil on contact. It uses this to bring small creatures to the top of ponds so it can feed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is called the “underdog of the fossil world.” Though small and often underestimated, it uses its agile tail to outwit larger foes, flipping them into the mud. Fossil records show it once thrived by surviving where others perished.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When in danger, POKENAME can split itself into two halves that operate independently and make it easier to confuse and escape predators. Some think the fossil in its center is somehow the source of this ability.
author: sk372

entry: When there is nothing around, POKENAME emerges from the mud to feed. At the slightest sign of danger, it scurries back into the mud, completely submerging itself. It is a weak fighter, and Trainers must work hard to stop it from hiding mid-battle.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: With its iron-hard shell, POKENAME blocks incoming attacks while its night vision–enhanced eyes glare its foes into submission. Due to their sensitivity to sunlight, Trainers' sunglasses often go missing.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME wants to be left alone. The ribbon-like growths from its head are made of rock and form a terrifying display to scare off other Pokémon and cave explorers. If anyone gets too close, it disappears through a wall.
author: leandermalurt

entry: POKENAME will approach humans and beg, attempting to appeal to others with its cute appearance for easy meals. If denied however, it won't hesitate to get aggressive and use its claws and stinger to steal food.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is so slow that battles are often over before they even get out of their shell. Some Trainers try to increase their Speed by coaxing them out of their shell and throwing berries at them to dodge. Most hit them without them even flinching.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME quickly climbs frozen lake banks, allowing it to hunker down inside rocky fields. When uncovered, it jumps scarily fast, clawing with pointed, knife-like nails only to escape from view.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME fossils are found in deep ocean rock layers, with researchers speculating that they swam across the ocean. When modern specimens were found, researchers were surprised to see they crawl across the ocean floor in swarms rather than swimming.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME was originally believed to be an ancient ancestor of Corsola dating back 300 million years. However, recent re-evaluation suggests that POKENAME was a parasitic species that would live inside shells constructed from discarded Corsola shells.
author: lunacharlotte

entry: POKENAME have tough sepia scales that allow for lightweight mobility and protection against sharp claws. Their venom is harvested by scientists to compare with ancient, fossilized venom.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME latches onto sea cave walls, using Conversion on its shell to mimic any nearby moss or stone and blend in seamlessly. It will stay still for days on end.
author: .izik

entry: It collects fossils, cleaning them with its brush-like tail. What, exactly, POKENAME does with these fossils is unknown.
author: admiralvermin

entry: POKENAME get mistaken for logs because of their sienna scales that blend into the forest floor. Each claw underneath their hood has ancient venom that causes searing pain when injected into their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends most of the day in the ocean but scuttles onto land to sleep. It digs holes in the ground to submerge its underside in. If something steps on its exposed shell, it quickly scurries away in a panic.
author: sk372

entry: Legless variants of POKENAME are rarely spotted in the wild and spend the majority of their time floating around the waters. They hop onto land briefly to nap during the warmest parts of the midday.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tail has developed a remarkable sharpness while retaining its electric power. It stabs the blade into prey, paralyzing them with electricity before tossing them into its wide torso-spanning maw.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is believed to be hollowed-out Kabuto shell possessed by a multitude of spirits. POKENAME gathers up fossil remains into its ghostly vortex, though none are sure if it does this for sustenance, to strengthen itself, or simply to hoard them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its rocky body as camouflage among the seabed. When a Pokémon draws near, its head extends and it drains them of their body fluids. If the prey's body is too tough, it first melts them by spitting acid.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The longer claws on a POKENAME are not as tough as a Kabuto's claws, but they are far more dextrous and can reach into tight crevices with ease.
author: entomoxie

entry: They are able to live for thousands of years before developing into their final form, as they live off ginkgo seeds. Those seeds have helped POKENAME develop a hard shell around themselves that resists damage.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using POKENAME's Diglett-like appearance as camouflage, it moves unseen through Diglett colonies. When it finds one alone, it swiftly captures the Pokémon with its claws and pulls it into the darkness that makes up its body.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Multiple eyes poking from the single large socket give POKENAME a strong sense of sight. The eyes can fire small beams of light that disrupt the internal magnetism of others, disorienting them.
author: sk372

entry: This deepwater pair are thought to have created a sword blade eons before humans did. The elongated partner polishes the rounded one's caudal spike.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME shells are hard but not durable, as while their shells are scratch resistant, they easily crack when bludgeoned with enough impact force. Their blades are made of a stronger material that easily slices through foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Blending in with rocky terrain, POKENAME's ponderous speed is offset by their ability to slash through cliff faces. They are often used as security for movie studios due to looking like mascots.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Over the millions of years it has existed, it adapted feelers to pull prey under its shell to eat. When threatened, it will disguise itself as a rock.
author: melodydelune

entry: A behemoth of land and sky, POKENAME can widen tunnels made by Onix or take flight to search for food; it isn't picky on which it chooses.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: Throughout history, some who saw POKENAME flying through the sky mistook it for a harbinger of destruction. It was increasingly shunned as a result.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME is able to reach out and grab distant objects and prey via shadows emanated from its underside. There is evidence it lived among and even led Kabuto colonies in the past.
author: sk372

entry: Living in arid, dusty environments, POKENAME use their ears as fans to dissipate heat. At night they navigate carefully, using their infrared vision to avoid predators and locate cacti for water.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Some theorize that this Pokémon is able to live forever, as it can roll its state of development back to a zygote as often as it wants. POKENAME spends its long centuries collecting and fossilizing dead organisms around itself.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME's body and limbs carry a remarkable resemblance to Kabuto. It occasionally lives among small groups of Kabuto, protecting them from predators in exchange for food offerings from the smaller Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: The false eyes on POKENAME's many tails help confuse predators. They also serve as the spot where flames will generate when POKENAME produces potent little fireballs to pelt at its opposition.
author: sk372

entry: The organs of POKENAME have been identified as a combination of water and a gelatinous substance. If a threat approaches from the rear, POKENAME will shoot concentrated bursts of this substance from its shell.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: While it is a rare Pokémon sought after by collectors, many Trainers lucky enough to obtain a POKENAME are displeased, finding it dull and slow to react; POKENAME's low heart rate and miniscule levels of brain activity allow it to conserve energy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found living in caves along the ocean shoreline. To hunt, they dip their tails into the water, wait for a fish to arrive, and zap.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME's large false head is used largely for intimidation attempts to scare off predators and competitors for food. It still possesses a painful bite, however, so one should not underestimate it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can breathe out small bursts of fire from the gap in its torso, but it must regulate its usage. The fire it breathes is directly sourced from its tail-flame, and will leave it very weak if overused.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be commonly found on rocky beaches among the fossil-containing stones. It draws ancient psychic energy from the surrounding fossils, and the older they are, the more powerful POKENAME becomes.
author: milchik

entry: Sometimes, when fossil enthusiasts crack the beach rocks open, POKENAME can be found residing inside. The two brightly glowing orbs visible inside the crack in this Pokémon's armor are its brains.
author: milchik

entry: It swims in the deepest parts of the ocean, searching for gems. It's naive and curious, but hides from predators in caves.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME trudges along the seafloor, filtering food from the mud it stirs up. During mating season, it hauls itself onto frozen beaches en masse.
author: robosoup

entry: The crystalline protrusions from POKENAME can adapt to blend in seamlessly with local bushes. Burrowing next to shrubs, they feed on the roots of the very same plants used as camouflage. This parasitic process repeats until they are ready to evolve.
author: ludacriswell

entry: POKENAME hides in the shadows of caves and forests. When threatened, the spheres on its head burst, releasing a cloud of harmful spores.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: Spots on POKENAME's flower make it look as if it has multiple eyes. This throws off most predators long enough for POKENAME to belch out a cloud of stinky pollen from its flower to help make its escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME regularly digs holes to bury itself in, submerging its lower half in soil. It seems to find comfort in being partially underground, or at least coated with a fine layer of fresh soil.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lurks beneath the surface of shallow water to blend in among the rocks. If Trainers pass by with food, POKENAME will suddenly dart out to grab their snacks before swimming out to sea to enjoy the meal.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If POKENAME existed millions of years ago, then it's generally accepted that it hunted in very shallow streams, eating particles and small buried Pokémon by pressing its stomach-mouth into the dirt. It can't stand getting its tail wet.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While digging, POKENAME's shell hardens as stones grind against it. Individuals often tunnel alongside others, seemingly comparing shell strength.
author: .izik

entry: The material that makes up the claws of a POKENAME resembles nails. The brittle claws often break when POKENAME go on an angry rampage but grow back quickly as well.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The hole in the center of POKENAME's stomach is its only mouth. It doesn't have to chew its food unless the food is bigger than its mouth.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME will hook themselves to the ceilings of caves, waiting for unsuspecting prey to pass below. Once they spots their target, they drop from the ceiling, sinking their teeth into them before expelling a powerful acid from their mouths.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's eyes are capable of seeing even in the dark depths of the ocean floor, where it roots around for food. Although slow of mind, its tail is sensitive; touching it will result in an instinctive and surprisingly quick swinging attack.
author: sk372

entry: Historians say that when a Gastly possesses a Dome Fossil, it will begin to absorb the ancient memories of the long-gone Kabuto and eventually turn into a POKENAME.
author: regulavish

entry: POKENAME digs up fossils to use as special pendulums for hypnotizing others. It primarily targets Rock types, and siphons nutrients from their bodies as they slumber.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME only eats when it is able to pull the leaves from branches itself and refuses leaves plucked by other Pokémon. By scraping its claws against branches, it can quickly rip several leaves off in quick succession.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fights off others by using fossils it digs up in order to club others. Archaeologists the world over have tried to barter the important artifacts from it, but to no avail.
author: sk372

entry: With toxic scales, POKENAME will weaken underwater prey from the air before diving down to finish them off with a flying headbutt. Their waterproof wings let them dive up to 10 feet before swooping back up.
author: lampent12

entry: Scientists originally believed POKENAME's fossil was a mix of two separate fossils. To their shock, the Pokémon revived with bony wings that could support its weight, as well as slice through steel.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's limbs are powerful and sharp, but it rarely uses them for fighting. Instead it uses them to cleave apart trees, roots, berries and anything else it feels like consuming at the time.
author: sk372

entry: Using its genetically enhanced psychic powers, POKENAME crushes boulders around its body for armor. Despite its extra weight, this Pokémon can close distances faster than a plane to crush opposition with its claws.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Almost every talon on POKENAME's claws is incredibly long and sharp. Once it pins down prey, it slowly and meticulously cuts away, carefully carving off its favorite parts to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is awkward; its heavy scythes hinder flight, and its airy wings clog in water. It adapts by skimming the surface in hops, swimming with its arms while keeping its wings dry to fly.
author: glacierwing

entry: Long believed to be part of a hive mind, POKENAME were recently discovered to have psychic abilities. Groups of between twelve to twenty would wait burrowed into rocks and coordinate perfectly to attack their natural enemy Golem.
author: ghostslythe

entry: It sleeps in deep caverns underwater, usually in caves abundant with coral. Its main head rests while its other eyes keep an eye out.
author: imagine1.

entry: The scythes that POKENAME uses as legs are extremely sharp. Using its agility and strength, POKENAME can cut down swathes of opponents in mere moments. The shell it resides in provides protection whilst it rests.
author: nyoomymph

entry: The oxygen-dense atmosphere of the prehistoric past allowed POKENAME to grow to an enormous size. It minces combatants with its steel-sharp horn.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME are crafty creatures that scale cliffs with their sharp scythes. They target nests of Flying-type Pokémon to steal their eggs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In the summer, flocks of POKENAME steal wheat from fields by harvesting with their scythes. Their grain stores allow them to live in their snow-capped mountain habitat.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: In ancient times, POKENAME was a fearsome winged predator whose shell could withstand even the fiercest impacts. Scientists have managed to revive it by using its fossilized feathers found in stone.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live amongst dense kelp forests, their rocky hide and naturalistic shape letting them blend in with rocks along the sea floor. Despite their fearsome appearance, they use their scythes to harvest kelp to feed on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Whatever POKENAME cannot cut through, it coils around, suffocating its prey. It has the ability to slither atop the surface of water.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Researchers found POKENAME was the apex predator of Kanto pre-history. While it is heavily armored with impressive four-foot razor claws, what most don't expect is how well this Pokémon can swim.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME uses its scythe-like tails to grab and cut its prey. Its head is very durable and it can swim at incredible speeds.
author: imagine1.

entry: Souls of extinct Pokémon are said to surround POKENAME. It is unclear if the legends refers to these ancient Pokémon causing these extinctions or if they rallied the souls after the fact.
author: static.mcawesome

entry: With incredible aerial speed and razor-sharp blades, POKENAME was an apex flying predator of the ancient world. Fossil records of its habitats indicate it preyed on even the most gargantuan of prehistoric Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is thought to have evolved from living in water to on land. In the jungle, it clears a path using its large scythe.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Agile fighters who use their shed rock-like skin as shields, POKENAME are found defending desert Oases from Ground type meddling. Honorable to a fault, before the battle begins it salutes with its bone sword.
author: ghostslythe

entry: If POKENAME or its Trainer is attacked, it immobilizes the assailant with telekinesis before raking its sharp blades across them as a warning before it releases them. Very few aggressors choose to ignore this threat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME in ancient times protected villages with their rock-hard armor and skull-splitting scythes. Resurrected by science, they now defend walking paths against predatory Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: An extremely intelligent hunter, POKENAME sits at the bottom of rivers and uses its claws to capture prey. They are sometimes mistaken for rocks when the water dries up.
author: torterrable

entry: POKENAME hides among kelp and seaweed, part of its body retracted to better camouflage itself. When unsuspecting prey draws near, the Kabutops-like upper half emerges and cuts them down with its scythes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's highly curved blade makes it unique among Honedge fusions. It prefers to attack in sweeping figure-eights, conserving its momentum and rotating so that its true edge is always facing the opponent.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Nesting above active volcanoes, POKENAME dives with its young into the lava. When they emerge, their rocky scales are toughened to diamond hardness.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Its sickle-like tail allows it to cut through prey with ease. When swimming, POKENAME will tuck its tail up against its body.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME beaches underwater prey by raising the sea floor beneath them before finishing them off with its scythes. However, its large body makes it terrible at swimming after prey, so it prefers to hunt purely on land, where its powers are stronger.
author: soup1900
