entry: The rocky crust of POKENAME's shell is thin and fragile, cracking and exposing the molten lava within with even small movements. They can unleash powerful Eruptions from their shell by deliberately breaking it open.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They aggressively snort small flames out of their nose, burning away dead grass and shrubbery while hunting. Truffles found and lightly roasted by POKENAME have a unique taste and texture, making them a delicacy in many parts of the world.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: When this Pokémon builds up enough swimming speed, its flames erupt, allowing POKENAME to rocket through the sky at over 300 meters per second before returning to the waves.
author: kobold_hijinks

entry: POKENAME's powerful legs and flaming wings make it uncommonly nimble. It attempts short flights while further honing its flames.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME sleeps within running servers, feeding off the heat they naturally produce. As it sleeps, a thin layer of black smoke seeps from its skin.
author: .izik

entry: With rock-hard skin, fireproof fur, and hot flames on its back, POKENAME is practically invulnerable to many types of attacks. It is incredibly nimble, darting around the battlefield by digging and sprinting in bursts.
author: nyoomymph

entry: The tendency of POKENAME to leap through tree branches and ambush prey is a growing cause of forest fires.
author: nexusshenanigans

entry: The flames along a POKENAME's back are hot enough to melt sand. POKENAME shape and cool the molten liquid with their claws to form the glass spines along their back.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME colonies have recently been discovered within a cave in the Orre region. Their claws will set aflame as they deliver devastating piercing punches to their foes.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME has a lot of potential, but struggles with discipline. It requires plenty of love and attention, as it tends to call it quits during a training session due to a lack of confidence.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Emotional energy helps fuel POKENAME's flames. When exposed to positive energy from its Trainer during battle, the flames surge with intense heat.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is often described as having a sassy and fiery personality. It has little patience for the antics of others, and threatens them with bursts of flame from its body if they agitate it too much.
author: sk372

entry: You can recognize a dam created by POKENAME from the light plumes of smoke that appear overhead. They're a favored companion of charcoal burners for their love of both collecting and burning wood.
author: craigprime

entry: The burning flame atop POKENAME's head is the only part of it that is particularly active. It uses the flame to heat up the delicious berries that fall down from trees near its vicinity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME trains its martial arts by the riverside from dawn 'til dusk. When it can snatch a fish from the river without getting wet, it is ready to evolve.
author: mogorian_gray

entry: POKENAME's flames are a formidable addition to its blade, flaring and releasing intense heat during combat.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's flames are a formidable secondary defense to its blade, flaring and releasing intense heat during combat.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its fur is completely non-flammable; however, it secretes an oil into certain parts of its body to engulf them in flames to ward off predators.
author: melodydelune

entry: Despite its lamplike appearance, POKENAME cannot be used as such, due to its uncontrollable ferocity. Any foe reckless enough to challenge it will find themselves engulfed in its devastating Fire Spin.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: This small Pokémon likes to be left alone. If it is threatened, the flames on its body will flare up.
author: themicelegion

entry: If rival POKENAME meet in the wild, they will try to intimidate the other by flaring their fires up to see who burns hotter. If neither backs down from the display, they charge their heavy bodies into each other and begin fighting for dominance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can control the amount of fire making up its wings, allowing it to dodge away from an attack in a single flap when enough fire is produced. It emits a supersonic Screech and produces superheated air to intimidate foes.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are known to bury eggs in the ground near volcanoes, as geothermal heat keeps their eggs warm. This practice is thought to have originated from a time when the volcanic peaks were still covered in snow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In some regions, POKENAME is regarded as a friendly guardian of volcanic peaks. The fire that wreathes its body flares up when it senses danger nearby.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME attack with explosive ferociousness, as they have little regard for their own safety. The fiery flames on their back melt through their opponents without regard for anyone's safety, so their Trainer often needs to step in to calm them down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its warm, comforting aura wards off bad dreams. The flames on its head and wings grow stronger during a solar eclipse.
author: cait_sith

entry: When resting, POKENAME raises the temperature of the soil around its body. This intense heat discourages predators from approaching its nest.
author: .izik

entry: It's said to use its tail flame to rocket boost through currents. This Pokémon wants to be hugged but most who try end up perishing.
author: berryslip

entry: POKENAME hunt for other burrowing Pokémon, digging toward their hidden homes swiftly as they search for food. Their flames help to keep their own tunnels from collapsing, baking the dirt around them and hardening it into a single smooth tube.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite its intense heat, POKENAME carries itself with refined grace. Nimble and lithe, it slips past attacks with effortless poise, rarely showing any sign of strain.
author: lesbian_garlicbread

entry: POKENAME float through the air atop a jet of fire, creating a trail of glass behind them as they travel across the desert sands. They twirl rapidly in combat, slamming into their foes with a powerful Flame Wheel.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have an explosive temper that causes their body to erupt with scorching flames. Once they enter into this hostile state, the only way to cool them down is to burn through all their energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The more hyped up in combat that POKENAME gets, the more of its body lights up with flames. It's entirely possible to see two POKENAME battling while every inch of their bodies are coated with blazing fire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME trains intensely in volcanoes and deep caves. Trainers avoid provoking it due to the uncontrollable power of its flames.
author: brunodaescola

entry: It moves on land by bouncing around, producing heat energy. POKENAME uses this energy to ignite its tail and attack foes from behind.
author: vaporvenator

entry: POKENAME can be found basking in volcanic regions. It shrouds itself in lava and waits to hunt passerby Pokémon.
author: vaporvenator

entry: POKENAME intimidates its foes with the foul-smelling odor of its flames. During summertime, its stench intensifies exponentially, but some POKENAME owners believe that it is a good thing.
author: skyrvr

entry: When it's time to frighten a victim, POKENAME flares its fiery hands up to twice their normal size, emitting a cackling peak of laughter as it does so. It prefer to hide in old furnaces until it's ready to scare someone.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can manipulate its own flames with telekinetic powers, shaping fire into forms or movements that can lull anyone who watches them for too long. It is believed to feed on the dreams of sleeping humans and Pokémon to keep its flames strong.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Flames jet from its back in order to vent its energy and keep from overheating. Should these flames recede, it's a sign that POKENAME is preparing to unleash a massive wall of flame from its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME collect clay so that they may treat their bones and make them more flame resistant. Their innate knowledge to use clay like this is widely studied. It appears to be because their own flames burn with dangerous potency.
author: infinex21

entry: During battle, POKENAME obscures itself with a haze of intense heat and pelts its opponent with fireballs and Bonemerang attacks. It displays enough intelligence to be able to use its bone to season and stir foods while cooking them with its flames.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be found in the waters around the Alolan islands, enjoying the heat of the volcanic islands. Large schools of POKENAME can be dangerous to divers due to the heat they give off boiling the water around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When angered, this Pokémon will start furiously shooting off the red-hot spikes along its shell and spewing scalding water from its mouth. Steam can often be seen rising from all over its body when it finally tires out.
author: fireblade141

entry: When approached, POKENAME breathes a thick cloud of steam at others in order to obscure their vision. The last thing most of its prey see are piercing red eyes from within the sweltering mist.
author: sk372

entry: With its control over fire, POKENAME will create a large shimmering haze to hide itself. It will then strike forward from the air with speed, catching its foes off-guard.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME ignites its wings in flames as a show of strength and dominance over others. Rivals clashing against each other will flare their fire up particularly fiercely, in some cases tripling the apparent visual size of their wingspan.
author: sk372

entry: This insect is often seen hunting defenseless prey during forest fires. Its stingers are known to grow red hot when angered.
author: puppetmaster64

entry: POKENAME is a Typhlosion that evolved a bit differently. Its blue fire is intensely hot, so hot that Trainers have gotten burns by standing near it.
author: thisisnotaplaceholder

entry: Pokémon fusion has restored long-since-dormant DNA in POKENAME. This form of POKENAME has not been recorded for over 150 years. It was a first partner Pokémon for youth in Hisui, now called Sinnoh.
author: lupa

entry: In order to perfect its fiery skills, POKENAME seeks much tougher opponents to challenge. It will often becomes fierce rivals with Charizard.
author: ratmerchant

entry: POKENAME wreathe themselves in flames when they fight with other Pokémon, especially focusing their flames around their strong jaws. Their flame-clad fangs can bite and melt through most metals with ease.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lure in Pokémon by using their flames to create bright light. When prey swims too close, POKENAME burn them to a crisp before feasting.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME immolates itself for defense, bursting with powerful flames across its whole body. As the flames roil on, the scent of burning wood fills the air.
author: sk372

entry: The pollen orbs of POKENAME's body can be ignited in order to give it better self-defense. On occasion, they will also catch on fire when a supportive POKENAME gets too energetic in cheering on its allies.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is covered in a thin toxic, flammable film. When it feels threatened, it triggers a reaction that causes it to combust. They are very skittish, and this occurs even when they are in no danger.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME love playing around active steam geysers, or bathing in hot springs to absorb volcanic nutrients.
author: weedspagon_real

entry: POKENAME is always meditating to keep its emotions in check. If it is ever disturbed, powerful flames will erupt from the volcano-like crown upon its head.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have fur that is coated with an oil that is highly flammable. Their fangs create sparks when struck together at a specific angle, allowing them to ignite themselves at a moment's notice to scare off aggressors.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's steel-like body is hard to damage and painfully hot to the touch. Its pincers can act as flamethrowers, or it can wield blades of pure flame capable of slicing through metal.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME moves slowly, its body crackling with quiet heat. The ground beneath it hardens into smooth black stone, guiding travelers as they navigate unfamiliar terrain.
author: mgfox_66676

entry: POKENAME are capable of bursts of speed when flying by abruptly erupting with flame. They can only maintain these speed bursts for a few minutes at a time, the flames taking a lot of energy to use.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME may still have physical wings, but the heat of their flames makes it impossible to check. They propel themselves with great jets of fire.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME have holes on their backs that erup in flames. These holes act like exhaust nozzles, intensifying their flames and increasing their destructive speed until they only leave fire and debris in their wake.
author: slavman9057

entry: POKENAME will infiltrate computers, consuming image files of things that are flammable. Their flames will grow hotter the more they eat, often causing the computer to overheat if they are left unattended.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's flames around its neck flare up when it turns aggressive. It must take care, as its antlers are flammable, and if its fire burns too strongly it may set them ablaze.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dashes across land while leaving behind raging flames and heat hazes in its wake. Energy stored inside its body eventually gets released into an intense Flare Blitz that causes loud thundering on impact.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon is extremely hot-tempered. Its powerful eruptions of energy can create thunderstorms above it.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME is perpetually cloaked in searing flames. When it flies into a rage, it burns away forests and dries up rivers with no remorse.
author: mepp.

entry: When enraged, POKENAME generates an enormous electromagnetic field while superheating the air with its red-hot magnets. Rescue teams value its ability to detect survivors and electronic equipment buried beneath volcanic debris.
author: skyrvr

entry: By rapidly buzzing its flaming wings, POKENAME creates sonic waves alongside a heat haze to disorient its opponent. Its bite force is strong enough to crush thick tree branches.
author: chibitales

entry: Despite its intimidating look, POKENAME is extremely affectionate. Studies show that the flames around its neck may have healing properties.
author: kilo_forte

entry: Flaring the flames on POKENAME's back allows it to boost its speed when it swoops after prey. Once it latches onto something, its stinger delivers both paralyzing venom and a blisteringly painful burn.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon is the ultimate survivalist. It has adapted to having hyper-insulative fur that can be set alight at will to ward off the cold.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME has a belligerent and bratty personality, angrily chirping and flaring its flame up at random when in a bad mood. Despite its small stature, it can breathe and flare up intense fire in formidable amounts.
author: sk372

entry: Even when POKENAME's flames are at rest, segments of its hide still glow red-hot from the heat it emanates. It ignites its fire just before rolling at opponents, turning itself into a burning, whirling fireball.
author: sk372

entry: The bodies of POKENAME are engulfed in flames whenever they become enraged. Their flame-charged punches and kicks create explosions upon impact.
author: cobalt0135

entry: They are often blamed for volcanic eruptions as they tunnel through the earth. They emit flammable gas from their mouths which ignites when enraged.
author: hummusishome

entry: The wheels of flame blazing from their brows and tail can be launched as fiery discuses with surprising accuracy despite the brute strength they typically show. Their spiked cheeks hold organs responsible for maintaining their heat.
author: deadshields

entry: The flames around its neck change color depending on the emotions it senses around it. Although POKENAME is not particularly mature yet, its fire attacks are so powerful that they can incinerate a tree in an instant.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is very sensitive to its Trainer's emotions. If its Trainer gets angry, POKENAME gets angry as well, the flames around its neck become big and hot.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: POKENAME flares up the fire around its neck to keep others at bay, as it has a rather standoffish personality. The only exception to this rule is its Trainer, for whom it happily retracts the burning ring of flame.
author: sk372

entry: A valiant hero who would give its life to save those it cares for. The cross flames on its back burn through its soul the more power it calls for.
author: theeggoverlord

entry: POKENAME wander through forests, cleanly burning and clearing out flammable brush to prevent wildfires. The charred flower constantly burning on a POKENAME's back releases a thick smog that's poisonous to humans in large amounts.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Cocky in combat, POKENAME loves to let its opponents think they've got it cornered, before its false mouth belches a plume of flame, catching them off-guard and opening them up for a vicious counterattack.
author: sk372

entry: Living deep beneath volcanoes, POKENAME swim through lava like water, their durable skin impervious to heat. It is believed that earthquakes during eruptions are caused by POKENAME hastily relocating before they're caught in the blast.
author: sk372

entry: Island villages worshipped POKENAME as a volcano god. Massive beach designs were drawn as offerings, believed to bring it great joy.
author: .izik

entry: What at first appears to be an active volcano upon its back is actually a petrified tree leaking a magma-hot sap. When enraged, these Pokémon stomp about and release flaming Seed Bombs from the petrified trees upon their backs.
author: infinex21

entry: The heat of POKENAME's blade ignites anything it touches, even when it isn't aflame. On contact, it can even generate explosions.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: A telltale sign of the presence of POKENAME in an area are the thin, burnt slice marks it leaves when training its flaming blades on rocks and trees.
author: bee4082

entry: When its rage peaks, POKENAME will rub their ribbons together to create large explosions. Trainers should be wary if they enter their habitat.
author: melodydelune

entry: Within their tails is a boiling, corrosive liquid similar to napalm. They will spit streams of this liquid during battle and follow-up with a rock-shattering strike from their tails.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its fiery appearance, POKENAME reside deep in the ocean. It spends its time around geothermic vents, absorbing the heat from them before swimming to the surface and leaping out, emitting a burst of flame as it does.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME's flames grow exponentially stronger as it descends toward the Earth, fed by the thickening air. A harbinger of heatwaves, it burns entire forests simply by flying low over the canopy.
author: ambrosia04

entry: Legend states that POKENAME pushed the continents apart with explosive force. Wherever it steps, ash and ruin are left in its wake.
author: dylonk25

entry: It coats itself in a heat-absorbent liquid to prevent accidentally burning others. In battle, it withdraws the liquid from volatile areas, unleashing intense flames and explosions.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It tests its endurance by sinking its tail into pools of lava, competing against other POKENAME. The tails of veterans are entirely composed of magma.
author: char_latte3412

entry: While POKENAME is naturally docile, it has a fierce temper. When its rage is set off, it creates a huge explosive blast from its fur, burning everything around it while camouflaging itself with a draconic aura.
author: beatdoof

entry: The emotions of those who wish on POKENAME fuel its sealed flames. Once every 1000 years, these flames break free and it awakens.
author: coridiant

entry: POKENAME uses its gem-like eyes to create beams of heat hot enough to melt through rock. It vents the intense amount of heat in its body through the flames on its back.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME prefers volcanic and ashy areas to call home. The flames that emit from its body flicker in accordance to the volcano's dormancy. Should they blaze up suddenly, an eruption is imminent.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly spews intense flames from inside its body. Despite this, its body is cold to the touch.
author: mistymagius

entry: In place of wings, POKENAME is coated in fire, allowing it to burn foes. However, the sound of the flames sometimes cause it to get disoriented.
author: canada

entry: Wild POKENAME live in the sides of dormant volcanoes and are very protective of their territory. They often eat Rawst berries. When not eating, they like to fly around into other POKENAME territory to challenge them to see whose fire is bigger.
author: coolbuddy1432_56671

entry: Though shy and timid by nature, POKENAME will often let its emotions out in a truly explosive manner. Extreme care is required during these outbursts.
author: dagoth.lluna

entry: Its flames are so bright, it can be spotted from over 100 miles away. It'll guide hikers lost in the mountains back to safety.
author: typhloquil

entry: During a Pokémon battle, POKENAME shoots destructive plumes of lava from its back that explode into obsidian shrapnel. Trainers collect the obsidian shards after a battle ends to sell them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: All the flaming feathers on POKENAME's sides molt once it finishes evolving. These feathers are said to ward off even the most terrifying nightmares.
author: cait_sith

entry: The flames all over its body become even more intense when it is enraged. The scalding water it uses in battle is so hot that POKENAME's attacks can strip the scales off of dragon-type Pokémon's bodies.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME has a symbiotic relationship with the fungus grown on their back. The mushrooms serve as good kindling to enhance their flames and the fungus uses the released smoke to carry its spores.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME heats the ground beneath its prey to burning temperatures. The soil can become hot enough to scorch exposed flesh.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are so heavy that their every step leaves a deep imprint, even on solid rock. Flames erupt from their humps when they are angered or during battle.
author: infinex21

entry: When angry, POKENAME erupts flame from its body. Since it is always angry, it only stops once it is completely depleted of energy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: They are extremely rare to find in the wild. Untamed POKENAME are vicious; tamed POKENAME are mild-mannered and affectionate.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are characterized by their fire breathing and large wings. Their wings are closer to the wings of a Crobat than many Dragon-type Pokémon, which is one of many reasons why they are not Dragon-type.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In the wild, POKENAME uses its 5,000 IQ to make dynamite using a secret recipe. It lights the fuses of them using the fire on its moustache.
author: reese1017600

entry: POKENAME lure Bug-type Pokémon towards their fiery maw with a sickly-sweet scent that proliferates through the air. Once their prey is in close range, they roast their prey with a powerful burst of flames.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A Pokémon's body secretes a flammable sweat that often intensifies their flames when they run. They are clever enough to create small explosions with their own sweat by stomping their flaming hooves upon the ground or directly against opponents.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon is a central figure in Celestic Town's annual Hallows Eve festival and is regarded as a living link to Sinnoh's past.  Many Sinnohian natives believe POKENAME to have the ability to commune with their ancient ancestors.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Fusion seems to have triggered dormant genes in POKENAME's Typhlosion half. It sometimes zones out and stares into space, which some say is how it communes with spirits.
author: hophoppip

entry: They battle one another for territory using violent explosive attacks. These duels are extremely hazardous, and should only be observed from afar.
author: vaporvenator

entry: When POKENAME's rage peaks, its smelly flames intensify so much that anything they touch immediately catches on fire. As it moves, a strong poison trails behind it, killing plants and trees on contact.
author: skyrvr

entry: POKENAME's shell begins to glow red-hot when it prepares to shoot fire from its twin cannon nozzles. The flames burn hot enough to liquefy solid stone in a matter of seconds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skull helmet keeps its upper jaw from being able to move. It cannot be removed, as its head has developed to fit the skull. Its unending tears and fierce aggression indicate this causes it pain, but that has yet to be fully confirmed.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can hover, but prefers rolling around in its watery habitat, playing with other Pokémon. It helps fight forest fires by floating with Pokémon Rangers on the ground and protecting them and their Pokémon with its omnidirectional water spray.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hunts by leaping from the water and biting at anything flying above. Once it latches onto something, it doesn't let go, dragging its prey beneath the water's surface.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skin can become slick and nearly frictionless, allowing it to dart through water at incredible speed. It leaves a faint shimmer as it swims.
author: .izik

entry: They use their hairlike tentacles to dig up sand while looking for prey, once they find them POKENAME their prey before excreting acid. On nights of a new moon, it is said that POKENAME's victims can be heard on shorelines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME pollinates aquatic plants across the marshes it inhabits. While doing so, it often gets distracted by prey swimming in the water, jabbing its stinger towards it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are mischievous creatures that enjoy chewing on things they are not supposed to. Treating them with respect is of utmost importance if a Trainer wants to avoid getting cut by their razor-sharp leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It likes to curl up in its shell when it naps. When it wakes, it nips at the first thing it sees as a sign of affection, not understanding how strong its jaws actually are. There is a proverb to let sleeping POKENAME stand up on their own.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME sprays jets of water at passing travelers to knock food from their hands. With a cackle, it snatches the meal and vanishes beneath the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME propel themselves to higher areas using strong blasts of water from their mouths. They can live in water or on land. They are often found dancing around gleefully.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME is easily stirred to emotion, especially by people. When excited, it reflexively bites anything that comes near its open mouth.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME are said to bring bad luck to whoever they meet. This often means getting bitten by their sharp teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is playful and competitive to a degree that most Trainers find exhausting. Surprisingly, its bite force is relatively weak.
author: staghorn

entry: A POKENAME's body is essentially a mobile, steaming, bubbling brook. It concentrates lots of hot water in its jaw and bites foes, scalding them.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME sleeps in the mud of lakebeds at night, its skin perfectly mimicking the texture of the ground around it. Its large jaws open and close periodically while it dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found by subterranean rivers; as they grow older, they wander further and further away from the body of water. Although some find it cute when they nibble on pebbles, it has a sharp glare that leaves even evolved Pokémon shaken.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found by subterranean rivers; as they grow older, they wander further and further away from the body of water. Although some find it cute when they nibble on pebbles, it has a sharp glare that leaves even evolved Pokémon shaken.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found by subterranean rivers; as they grow older, they wander further and further away from the body of water. Although some find it cute when they nibble on pebbles, it has a sharp glare that leaves even evolved Pokémon shaken.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME likes to play in puddles during the rain. Unfortunately, when it gets excited, it also tends to let out an electrical shock.
author: projectalpha22

entry: POKENAME uses its tail as an air pump to bounce to places. Sometimes it forgets that it can do this and stares at the ground, afraid to jump down.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME's ravenous appetite causes it to bite down and rarely let go of anything that looks remotely edible. More than a few Trainers have adopted one simply because it bit their bag and refused to let go for hours or even days.
author: sk372

entry: It can be given a Liechi Berry to improve its strength in a pinch, which makes its jaw stronger until the battle is over. It chomps down on opponents with enough force to break boulders.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It tags alongside its Trainer, its protective nature making it wary of any strangers drawing near. Even faces familiar to the Trainer must be wary; if they aren't familiar enough to POKENAME, they risk getting bitten.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bites with its sharp teeth to cut down trees. Its powerful jaws allow it to make quick work of logs, which get turned into natural dams.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has an intense urge to bite anything near it as a way to relieve its aggressive urges. Anything that tries to escape gets caught by vines from its flower, and dragged closer so it can chomp down on them.
author: sk372

entry: Southern cities once believed POKENAME to be a god of waterfalls. Its shed fangs were preserved and used in ceremonial worship.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lurk in murky water, preferring swamps and slow moving rivers. They carry symbiotic plants on their back to help disguise them in the mud, waiting patiently for their food to come to them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lurk near the surface of the water, using the plant growths on their back to disguise themselves amongst the reeds. It is advised to assume that there is always a POKENAME present, regardless of if you can see one.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The hooked spikes on POKENAME's blade easily tear through skin and severely injure foes. Its slices are like powerful bites, crushing foes up as it drains the life energy out of them.
author: soup1900

entry: In the water, they will snap their powerful jaws down on prey and hold them in place with their feelers.
author: melodydelune

entry: Once POKENAME bites onto something, it refuses to let go. Even if it was forcibly knocked back, it would expel its innards, jaws included, so that it would remain connected to its target.
author: sk372

entry: It will share the accessories on its ring, but only if traded something equally pretty or valuable. Any who try to take them by force will be given a nasty bite from its powerful jaws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found in swamps, building its dens out of wooden logs and tree roots. While it needs to repair its dens every few days, POKENAME prefers to spend most of the day gnawing on large logs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fangs are made of steel due to its diet of metals and ores. Its jaws are strong enough to break off pieces of solid metal and chunks of ore.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will bite just about anything it can get its jaws on. It is a very impatient Pokémon, preferring to just attack than to wait for the perfecting opening to strike.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is very dangerous, as its powerful jaws will clamp down on anything that moves near it. There are rumors that POKENAME lurk in sewers, though this appears unlikely since POKENAME are often observed basking in the sun.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The face on the mask changes its expression to match POKENAME's mood. If the mask shows its teeth, take care; POKENAME is in a mood to bite anything that comes close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME distracts opponents with passionate, dramatic dances. Once its foes are entranced by its rhythm, POKENAME closes in to deliver a devastating bite with its powerful jaws.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME fills dumpsters with water before tearing into rotting food. The soggy texture makes the food easier to swallow and more to its liking.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME loves to play with just about everyone, Trainers should exercise extreme caution around it. Its powerful jaws and sharp teeth can rip through the bottom of tanker ships.
author: mistymagius

entry: Young POKENAME excitedly try to bite anything that moves. They are even seen landing on the bodies of Quagsire to nip at them repeatedly, though their fangs aren't sharp enough to actually harm the Pokémon.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's anchor is actually an elongated tooth that it uses to impale its prey like a harpoon. It will sometimes have to break the tooth off if it gets jammed in the ground, waiting for two weeks for it to grow back.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME shoots water from its mouth that is extremely poisonous. Prolonged exposure to this water can cause blindness, making it a dangerous adversary in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will chew on basically anything and has been known to damage an underwater pipe or internet cable. However, POKENAME is quite docile and only feeds on seaweed and kelp.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME haunts the shores of lakes and rivers with a gang of its own kind, delighting in playing pranks on those it finds near the water. It often wrestles for fun, so it is not unusual to see it with a black eye on its face.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME digs near riverbanks to create concealed pitfalls. It uses fragrant herbs as bait to lure prey like Poliwag.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a contentious reputation as a pet mostly due to its way of showing affection. The longer it holds onto you after biting, the more it loves you. The longest recorded POKENAME bite is currently 6 hours.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dives into park fountains to steal coins from the bottom. It will flee into a nearby river to store its coins.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are deceptively powerful creatures that can break rocks with their jaws. When they inevitably break one of their teeth on a rock, the nerve damage goes right to their brain and gives them a searing headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The jaw of POKENAME can open surprisingly wide, allowing it to consume food that's almost its size. However, its bite strength is very low, so even a full-force crunch feels like a nibble.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME punches underwater boulders to train its strength. Once exhausted, it emerges from the lake to rest in the sunlight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clamp their jaws around anything that interests them and pull it back into their shell for safekeeping. If they're caught biting onto a person or larger Pokémon in their excitement, they will hide in their shells to avoid being scolded.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It has a tendency to bite down onto large machines, though nobody is sure why. Due to the magnetism in its jaws, it's difficult to pry it off once it's bitten down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the magnets on its head to pull metal objects that have caught its attention toward itself. It tends to nest near water sources because it needs to keep its body moist to amplify the power of its electric attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live in polluted swamps. This Pokémon communicates through biting: gentle affectionate nibbles for friends, and harsh chomps for foes!
author: bobosmith01

entry: It uses both the cannons on its back and its sharp maw to attack opponents in battle. After a hard fight, it enjoys eating a Precooked Burger, as do many Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will use its coin to lure predators closer to it. POKENAME will then bite with their powerful jaws, scaring Pokémon larger than it away.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME splashes water with its bone to communicate with others of its kind. If a curious onlooker approaches too closely, it snaps at them in warning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME expels toxic bubbles which it defensively pops using its spiked crest. This buoyant Pokémon is rather easygoing, and it can often be seen floating down rivers that pass through cities.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME swim in groups so they can attempt to raze prey much bigger than themselves. It is during this stage that POKENAME seems to reproduce the most.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Once POKENAME have clamped their teeth onto their prey, they use the static generated as it tries to wrestle free to subdue it.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME are cantankerous creatures that get easily irritated when they have indigestion. After a round of hunting, they swallow stones so that they can break down bones and other tough materials in their stomach.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME glides through rivers with serpentine grace. Its powerful jaws and dragon-like instincts make it a formidable hunter in both land and water.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME dives into lakes to hunt for fish Pokémon and carries them back to its nest. Its hooked, serrated teeth ensure that prey cannot escape once trapped in its jaws.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME catch winds coming down from the mountains during storms and fly through the air with their jaws agape. When they violently slam into prey, they latch on with their strong jaws, never to let go first.
author: vic1312

entry: It tries to disguise itself as a regular flower to lure in its prey and entrap them in its massive jaws.  Unfortunately for POKENAME,  few are fooled.
author: bostroms

entry: The fur of a POKENAME is consistently damp, even when living in arid climates. Its jaw has enough power to finely grind down rocks.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME are affectionate creatures that bite the ears of those they adore. Whenever two POKENAME fall in love, they bite each other's ears to signal romantic interest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME bites, it will clamp its jaw shut and lock the target into a vice-like grip. With the opponent trapped, it will fly up high with them in tow before releasing its hold and sending them plummeting back down.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME restrains and clamps down on its prey by biting down with its fangs. The longer the fangs remain latched onto its prey, the more venom is injected.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will often be seen walking around with a large rock carried in its mouth. It shatters the stone by crunching down with its jaws as an intimidation display.
author: sk372

entry: Cocky and boisterous, POKENAME is often seen picking fights with larger Water-types by smacking them with its club. If it is disarmed of its weapon in the ensuing battle, it doesn't hesitate to bite down with its sharp teeth instead.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon has a bite force of over 5,000 pounds. Trainer's occasionally mistake it for a beach ball floating in the water. This is still one of the leading causes of limb loss in the region.
author: huh.7

entry: POKENAME naps while sunbathing, with the secondary head warding off curious predators. When hungry, it sits on the shore and cries, while the secondary head waits beneath the surface to strike.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lurk out of sight in swampy water, blending into the native plant life thanks to their symbiotic growths. They have powerful jaws and it is near impossible to break free of them if they bite onto you.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It can blow shimmering bubbles from its mouth that mesmerize other Pokémon, calming their aggressive behavior. If anyone misbehaves or threatens creatures POKENAME cares for, it won't hesitate to fight back with its powerful jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME submerge themselves in rivers so that only their eyes, ears, and tails are above the water. Groups of them raise the ambient temperature of the water surrounding them and, when they are excited enough, can cause it to boil.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drift along the surface of rivers, remaining motionless and letting the current carry them. Their many tails are patterned to look like drifting detritus, floating at the surface and allowing them to surprise their prey.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Their horns and shells are as hard as steel, yet have the composition of iron. POKENAME have strong jaws and they can struggle to let go of something once they have bitten down.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME bash their own bodies against one another to settle territory disputes. Their jaws and fangs can bite through solid rock, so their clashes often leave one another clad in scars.
author: infinex21

entry: When a POKENAME clamps down with its jaws, it will refuse to let go under any circumstances. It has a tendency to go after Fire-type Pokémon since their fire-based attacks help regulate POKENAME's cold-blooded body.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME have further-developed jaws capable of quickly shredding through the hulls of many ships. Though they often live and hunt amongst their own kind, POKENAME will insist upon fighting amongst themselves until an alpha of the pack is decided.
author: infinex21

entry: Though it takes on an appearance similar to Krokorok, POKENAME behaves much differently. It leads a solitary lifestyle, and uses its stone tail to send intruders flying if they dare intrude in its territory.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lumbers around arid areas, though never strays too far from a source of water. Its powerful stone jaws clamp down so strongly that nothing tossed inside its mouth has any hope of escaping.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers a quiet solitude, making the rowdy and boisterous Primeape its natural enemy. While it prefers an honest fight, it happily relies on its sharp teeth when its opponent cheats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME run down opponents before bashing them with a combination of their long snouts and the spikes on their heads. When they get serious, they pull up their spare skin to protect their bodies while they clamp their jaws down on foes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Living beneath riverbeds, POKENAME senses vibrations through flowing water. It erupts upward at high speeds to snap at passing prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's teeth act like natural conductors, quickly and efficiently shocking their prey. The hook-like shape of the teeth also allows them to embed into the prey, leaving no chance for escape.
author: dualblades1147

entry: POKENAME holds hot water within the hump on its back. When startled, the hump acts like a geyser, spewing boiling water in all directions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have many sharp teeth that grow back if a tooth is damaged. The growth of a new tooth presses against their brains, which can give them a headache if they need to regrow lots of teeth at the same time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After evolving from its previous form, POKENAME experiences heightened aggressiveness. If raised in a safe and loving environment, POKENAME will feel conflicted about using its coin.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: While Bulbasaur is known to walk slowly on land, POKENAME uses its wings to fly around. These wings also help keep POKENAME warm during the winter.
author: themadcactus

entry: Wild POKENAME are frequently found on the outskirts of forests, having the advantage of both sticking to the sides of trees and flying across twigs.
author: themadcactus

entry: POKENAME soars high above the forests, casting shade with its leafy canopy. It disperses seeds and pollen, fostering life wherever it flies.
author: anarchaz

entry: The Pidgey head is the only one with consciousness as the Exeggutor body is only a diversion. Despite its small wings, it is still able to fly using its unusual psychic powers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can't help gorging itself on every source of food it can find. In lean times, it finds Pokémon in need and regurgitates food to share.
author: leshii

entry: POKENAME's wings expel puffs of toxic gas as it flies, leaving a faint purple haze in the air. It prefers to roost near industrial zones, where the pollution enhances its strength.
author: .izik

entry: Possessing no limbs, wild POKENAME rely on string to move large distances. The feathers inhibit it during rain or snow, giving little advantage.
author: themadcactus

entry: A POKENAME can remember everywhere it's ever been. It uses its time in its hard shell to perfect its mental cartography.
author: bee4082

entry: When POKENAME spots prey, it charges at full speed to knock it out with its body, hard as stone, before it can escape. To keep its beak sharp, it rubs it daily against extremely hard surfaces.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hunts for insects among dead leaves. It will furiously peck at anyone who tries to see what lies under its vines.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME love to glide through the sky on a gentle sea breeze. When they are not flying through the sky, they are swimming underneath the sea looking for seaweed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon makes its nests out of sticks and strings. Any Pokémon that tries to steal a POKENAME's eggs will end up stuck in a web.
author: themadcactus

entry: Instead of eating bugs, POKENAME relies on eating flower nectar and dew, which is more difficult to come by given the increased size and body weight. It requires at least 1 pound of nectar and dew every day to fill POKENAME's stomach.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: It has strong swimming muscles, allowing it to swim against most currents easily. It goes on land to feed, eating the worms and small bugs that inhabit the riverside.
author: sk372

entry: Their sharp beak is coated with a venomous layer of saliva that dissolves shells and nuts over time. This allows them to obtain exclusive food sources unavailable to other forest Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs through the dirt with its beak, frantically searching for Evolution stones. It can persist for days, never stopping until it unearths one.
author: .izik

entry: During battle, POKENAME shakes its body vigorously to cloud itself in the dirt or sand stuck in its fur. It takes advantage of the opponent's confusion by leaping behind them and striking with burning talons.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME hovers around near where Pidgey flock, looking to steal some of the food they scrounge up. Its cry is a louder, shriller version of Pidgey's, and effective at sending a flock flying away so it can swipe a meal.
author: sk372

entry: Its sense of direction and smell make POKENAME a surprisingly powerful hunter. It occasionally even uses its poisonous horn to add some flavor to what it catches.
author: ichosuzu

entry: POKENAME remains motionless in trees, blending in with its hardened, brown feathers. If disturbed, it will release a cloud of fine dust that causes mild paralysis before taking flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's claws are as hard as stone and are sharpened by tearing into nearby surfaces where it nests. During colder months, it migrates to warmer regions, flying for days to reach them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The wings growing from its head are strong enough to let it fly, though only for short periods. When their plumage turns snowy white, it means POKENAME has recently molted, and it will take weeks for its feathers to regrow stronger than before.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a gentle creature that feeds mostly on berries or the leftovers from stronger Pokémon. It skillfully uses the pair of wings on its head to soar to safer places to live.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME coat their wings with dust to avoid parasites from latching onto them. They buzz around with their stingers and talons to search for small Pokémon to turn into prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a very tiny bird Pokémon that lets itself float on the wind wherever it may want to go. It has the power to teleport if anyone comes near.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a very tiny golden bird Pokémon that lets itself float on the wind wherever it may want to go. It will teleport away if it feels endangered.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: When POKENAME is about to battle, it cloaks its back in vivid flames to warn its opponent. Despite having a pair of wings, it prefers to hop along the ground while searching for food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Though small in size, POKENAME is very fast in both water and air, reaching speeds of up to 50 miles per hour. POKENAME is also very territorial, so trust may not come so easily.
author: malumwenmonkey

entry: This fusion's plumage is highly attractive to other Pidgey. Scientists worry this will negatively impact their courting rituals.
author: kiwikelly

entry: These skittish Pokémon are known to observe campers go about their day. When spotted, they are nearly impossible to catch as their sleek wings and light bodies allow them to escape quite easily.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is too fat to fly. It makes its nest in burrows at the base of trees.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME glides through the morning mist, its wings coated in a fine, reflective dust. It flutters above flower fields, leaving behind tiny sparkling trails as it moves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of both trapping and hunting prey. Hosting one of their webs in the eaves of one's house practically guarantees a pest-free home.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME exhibits features of Pidgeot's Mega Evolution. It flies at ridiculous speeds for its small stature to the point that it often has difficulty stopping properly.
author: sk372

entry: Despite it resembling an immature Pidgeotto, POKENAME is far from it. Its bigger body allows it to glide through deep forests and hunt prey at tripled speeds, but being bigger means that it requires much more food than a normal Pidgey.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME is easily swept away by strong wind as it flies, which often frustrates it. POKENAME has a short temper and will split trees in half with a lightning bolt, leaving it dizzy and exhausted.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME flutters playfully through meadows, singing a high-pitched melody as it flies. Those who hear its tune often feel a sudden drowsiness, making it an effective deterrent for predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME chirps joyfully at sunrise, spreading a calming energy wherever it flies. Its eggshell glitsens in the sunlight if it is healthy.
author: .izik

entry: It lingers by its nest after gaining flight, which helps it develop deeper bonds with Pokémon and people nearby. People who give it a Genius Feather are said to have good luck for a week.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before building a nest, POKENAME uses its psychic abilities to determine if the area will flood in the future. If safe, it weaves a sturdy nest using gathered weeds and vines.
author: .izik

entry: The dark markings by POKENAME's eyes reduce the glare it encounters when it stares in the direction of the sun. It is difficult to surprise due to its awareness.
author: .realthree

entry: It travels in large herds for protection. It is bad at flying, so it typically uses its wings and tail feathers to attract mates instead.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME's head feathers don't shine as brilliantly as an ordinary Pidgeot, making it more vulnerable to being rejected by a potential mate. Despite this setback, it still retains its incredible feats of speed and strength.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME soar through the sky alongside groups of Hoppip. Whenever a gust of wind scatters these groups, POKENAME help locate lost Hoppip to return them to the group.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is fast and agile in the air. It flies from place to place, never staying in one spot.
author: themicelegion

entry: A fusion used commonly by beginner Trainers. POKENAME are generally easy to train and enjoy searching for Berries to share with their Trainers.
author: vaporvenator

entry: POKENAME relies on its excellent thievery to survive in the wild. It uses its quick feet to run around, and it uses its wings to fly away.
author: omegarockster

entry: POKENAME clings to trees with its sharp talons. Its long neck allows it hunt for its prey with speed and ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's way of hunting for prey is different based on their nature. While some POKENAME rely on the wind to float towards and catch prey as it passes, some will instead bury themselves in the dirt and eat whatever is living inside it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: When flying, POKENAME extends its wings and unleashes a loud buzzing noise. This makes it very noticeable to the prey it chases.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have adapted to mostly live off Energy Root. They do not seem to mind the bitter taste and are found pecking at the base of trees to unearth the root. They use the root to produce a bitter film that predators despise the taste of.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has an inquisitive personality, often observing the activities of others from a safe distance. One can tell if it is particularly intrigued by something if the jewel on its forehead sparkles and flickers brightly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's capacity for reading minds and sensing moods is particularly effective in regards to avian Pokémon. It can soothe an angry flock of birds in just a few moments with its mental abilities.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME make their nests near highways because the warm exhaust from vehicles keeps the general vicinity warm. When traffic comes to a halt, POKENAME attempt to solicit treats from cars.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's swift aerial movements and powerful beak make it a perfect pick for learning simple but effective strategies. This makes it a common first fusion for beginner Trainers.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME's require more energy in their larger bodies, so they have developed sharper beaks and prioritize hunting on land than in the skies.
author: themadcactus

entry: POKENAME is primarily active in the morning when looking for twigs for its nest. Its wings allow it to evade predators.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon flutters around creating intricate flight patterns that some believe carry hidden messages. Its mysterious behavior has puzzled researchers for generations.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It uses its psychic abilities to run faster. POKENAME starts mastering its telekinetic powers at a young age by lifting Berries from bushes.
author: .izik

entry: By creeping and hiding in tall grass, POKENAME close the distance between themselves and their prey without being detected. Once in position, they kick up blinding sand to confuse their prey before landing a lethal blow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME perches against tree trunks, listening for the sounds of Pidgey hunting. When it catches one that is just about to eat, it swoops down with an ear-piercing shriek, scaring off the Pidgey and stealing its hard-earned meal.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME don't hesitate to tear apart the bases of trees in order to find small, edible Pokémon. However, when domesticated, POKENAME are surprisingly patient and tolerant, and have a sharp memory.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME tries to interject itself into Pidgey communities and assert itself as the de facto leader by bullying others into submission. This usually results in it being chased off by the whole flock.
author: sk372

entry: It leaves behind puddles of sticky berry juice, then hides nearby. Once enough insects are stuck, it goes to feast on the mixture of tasty juice and bugs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects Hondew Berries in its beak and stores them in hidden nests. Its feathers carry a faint honey-like scent, making POKENAME a favorite target for hungry Bug-type Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is self-aware of how odd its long neck and tiny head appear to others, but more often than not, other Pidgey admire it. They even rely on POKENAME to use its long neck to dig for Bug-type Pokémon from the ground.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Despite it being covered in a massive number of feathers, POKENAME is pretty lightweight due to how small their actual body is. The feathers are great heat insulators and are commonly in pillows.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME glides over swamps in search of prey, striking from above with its venom-coated beak. A single peck can be enough to paralyze a Poliwag instantly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME infiltrate computers to search for image files of branches or wood. They gather these files to make nests within empty folders to give themselves a place to lay their eggs.
author: santon5512

entry: As majestic as POKENAME are, many are hurt by cars on roads that cut through their natural habitat. Campaigns from environmental groups urge drivers to slow down to protect POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A thick, inky brown goo seeps from POKENAME's tail feathers, giving off an intensely pungent odor. This foul-smelling substance is used to repel predators from its nesting grounds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their beaks to examine their surroundings, curiously pecking at anything they find. These Pokémon are constantly worried about their appearance, preening their feathers to ensure they look their best.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME have loose, dry feathers lining their tail and wings. When they feel threatened they shake them vigorously, creating a dry rattling sound to warn away danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fluff their wings up to make themselves appear bigger than they actually are. They do this whenever they want to scare off another Pokémon, whether that's a rival or a predator.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When in groups, POKENAME will compete with each other to see which one can produce the biggest flame. Many try as hard as they can, but most can only make enough fire to light a few sticks.
author: universal9449

entry: POKENAME's appearance is misleading when viewed from below as it flies. Some claim that when struck by lightning, it discharges powerful electric energy in return, often scorching the ground beneath it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME play pranks on each other to make each other laugh. The less amused they appear to be, the more they actually enjoyed the joke.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Whenever it gets cold, some people opt to give them a Health Feather before turning it back towards the wild. The feather helps it endure life's troubles by giving it a little extra heat to keep warm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can strip a Watmel Berry tree bare in less than an hour. It knocks the berries loose mid-flight with powerful wing beats before devouring them.
author: .izik

entry: A Spicy Curry, when made with an herbal and pungent masala, gives it an adrenaline boost that helps it win Little Cup tournaments. After a round of battles, it enjoys a fresh mango lassi to help cool down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wings have scales along the back that allow it to negate electricity from wild Pokémon while it flies. POKENAME can be seen bathing itself in sand and mud before blowing it off by flying around at top speeds of 100 mph.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME will accidentally kick up sand into its eyes if it swings its arms too low to the ground. While it can remember where a location is, it always takes a very long and convoluted path to reach that destination.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME flock near small towns, taking shelter in the trees nearby. Their inner fires make their feathers warm to the touch. Many children befriend POKENAME by offering them berries and seeds, and these Pokémon will follow them afterwards.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Spending most of their days in the safety of the nest, POKENAME cry out to their parents when they get hungry. If this Pokémon goes too long without eating, it will spit fireballs in a temper tantrum.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The feathers on its back are pointed and can tense enough to cut tough hides. It burrows using its strong claws and glides through the air when it leaps out of the ground.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have stiffened feathers sprouting from its back. While difficult to use for flight, these feathers are strong defensive structures and function as protective spines.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fight dirty, both literally and figuratively. In combat, this Pokémon will use its feathery arms to whip up sand and dirt to blind its opponents. While the foe is disoriented, POKENAME rushes forward and deals harsh blows with its kicks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME cry loudly from within their nest to get the attention of their caregivers. Whenever they are about to fall, they teleport back into the nest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a soft and demure personality, often taking Pidgey flocks under its wing to care for them. It soothes the birds by singing with a cooing melodic voice.
author: sk372

entry: When two POKENAME confront each other over a single mate, they begin to scream at each other, each attempting to be louder than the other. These fights tend to last for up to two hours, and by then, the mate they were fighting for will have left.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: The wings are a vestigial structure, too small to support wild POKENAME. POKENAME have sharper beaks and keener eyes to seek prey on land.
author: themadcactus

entry: POKENAME nest in alpine regions, finding hollows amongst tree roots to hide their nests from predators. Their chirps and cries can be heard echoing through the forests, turning frantic and aggressive should someone get too close to their nest.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It uses its rock-solid skull to headbutt trees, dislodging fruits, nuts and bugs for it to eat. Overzealous POKENAME occasionally end up knocking the entire tree down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME take to the air by running and leaping, then they glide on the wind. They will dive with the tops of their heads aimed forward toward any foe or prey and strike with devastating force.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME nest in alpine regions, finding hollows amongst tree roots to hide their nests from predators. They are fiercely protective of their nest, fluffing up their feathers to appear bigger to scare off anyone that finds them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME cannot fly with its tiny wings. Instead, it will curl its body and wrap its wings around its eggs to keep them warm if it gets too cold outside.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME's impeccable hearing allows it to hear bug Pokémon crawling 10 feet underneath the ground. Several Trainers have had to be rescued from falling into one of these holes created and left by POKENAME.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: It lives life in subzero conditions and has limited flight mobility. People give it a Resist Feather as good luck, as it develops bonds and grudges that last a lifetime.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its heavy body and iron bones mean that its wings are completely incapable of lifting its weight. Despite this, it is an agile flier thanks to its innate magnetism.
author: staghorn

entry: Tame POKENAME are often used by farmers, as they both function as a garden shovel and pest control. In the wild, POKENAME use their knife-like beaks to eat hard fruits like oranges.
author: thescribe

entry: POKENAME both fights and forages via quick stabbing maneuvers with its paired blades. In the wild, it stabs through fruits and shares the meal with the head on the opposite sword.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are small yet clever creatures that make full use of their metallic blades daily. From cutting open nuts to chopping twigs for their nest, these blades are an essential part of everyday life.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses both its ribbons and beak to look for seeds to eat. It is popular among rookie Trainers for its docile nature and ease of training.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME avoids all fights by sending any attackers away to other realms using its power of space. No matter what dimension it has brought itself to, it always knows the exact world it has marked as its home.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have plush and beautiful plumage that make them very popular with Pokémon Breeders. The feathers on their head are fast growing and well-suited to being styled in multiple different ways.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have plush and beautiful plumage that make them very popular with Pokémon Breeders. The feathers on their head are fast growing and well-suited to being styled in multiple different ways.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME chirps obnoxiously at the exact same moment each day, down to the nanosecond. The timing seems to be picked entirely at random.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Commonly found in suburbia, POKENAME gathers seeds from birdfeeders and stores it within itself. However, this causes it to be targeted by Rattata.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is a very sought-after wild fusion for beautiful- and rare-pet owners. Its wings and tails are soft as silk, and it only become more valuable as it evolves.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME can set its beak ablaze by scraping it against rocks, making its strikes significantly more powerful. It spreads its broad wings wide to appear larger and intimidate rival Flying-type Pokémon that dare challenge its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME cover their bodies in cloth and feathers, infiltrating Pidgey nests while the parents are away. Once one of the parents returns with food, they chirp and beg to be fed, blending in with the rest of the brood.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME has tails that can ignite and spin in rapid succession, enabling flight. When it is done flying, it needs to take a nap because of the amount of energy used.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its tail feathers to adjust its position mid-air, allowing it to deliver precise aerial kicks. Its movements are swift enough to counter even the most agile opponents.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long, flexible arms to reach inside trees and grab its prey. It cannot fly well, which results in most POKENAME being an easy target for even the weakest of predators.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME uses its tail to lure out bug Pokémon, simulating a ray of sunlight for it to follow. It stuns bigger bug Pokémon by whipping its tail at them, paralyzing their bodies from the outside.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's wings create soft, soothing vibrations as it flies, lulling nearby Pokémon to sleep. If it gets angry, it will puff up its chest and let out a loud, echoing chirp in frustration.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in kelp forests to avoid predators, pecking anyone that intrudes with its sharp beak. If POKENAME receives an offer to join a Trainer's team, it will swim in circles around the Trainer with gleeful delight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The feathers of a wild POKENAME are completely immune to fire. Researchers found that the skin of the creature, while not flammable, can be burnt.
author: themadcactus

entry: The fire on its tail burns brightest on days with clear weather. It hides underground from rain to protect its flame.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME perches on tree limbs, digging its talons deep to absorb nutrients. When it has fed enough, the bud on its body pulses rhythmically.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's gas-filled, feathery body allows it to float gently over flower fields. Its talons are deceptively strong, capable of seizing prey like Bellsprout in an instant.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soars over carrot fields, searching for diseased or damaged crops. It plucks them from the ground with its beak, keeping the fields healthy.
author: .izik

entry: The extra bundle of feathers covering POKENAME's shoulders give it extra warmth, and allow it to withstand colder environments. Despite this, it still chooses to remain in warm places with sunlight anyway.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's squishy body allows it to squeeze inside trees and eat any and all bug Pokémon it finds. It is able to remember every feasting spot by leaving a small portion of its body nearby.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: A quiet Pokémon that is found floating around from time to time in places of fair weather. If possible, it travels in a pack. It dislikes conflict.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME screeches into the holes of trees and cave walls, causing small Pokémon to come out, stumbling and confused. There is no set schedule for when POKENAME are awake or asleep, as they only rest when they need to.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's feathers store static electricity, crackling softly as it flaps its wings. When it perches on power lines, it absorbs small amounts of energy to maintain its strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their tough and sharp tusks to mark their way so they never get lost. These markings are a boon to many, even other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's keen eyesight allows it to detect even the slightest movement in tall grass. Once it spots prey, it launches a precise blast of flame from its beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME decorates its nest with colorful Apricorn shells it finds in the forest. POKENAME defends its territory by breathing scorching flames from its sharp beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME shakes its feathers rapidly to scatter glowing embers in the air, creating a dazzling display at dusk. If threatened, it ignites its beak, making itself appear threatening.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME beaks have sharp teeth that they use to puncture the skin of their prey, sucking out their vital energy. When not in combat, they use their teeth to preen their feathers, keeping their body free of parasites.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME perch outside of mines, lying in wait for people to bring in hauls of gems. Once they spot a telltale shine of crystal, entire flocks of POKENAME will descend to gather gems to bring back to their nests.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The tips of POKENAME's feathers secrete a clear, paralyzing toxin. When threatened, it flutters its wings to scatter the venom and stun larger predators before escaping.
author: .izik

entry: Scientists theorize that Tyrunt could have looked similar to POKENAME in ancient times. Its beak-like jaws are powerful enough to crush small boulders.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME primarily gets around by hopping, as its leaves weigh heavily on its tiny frame. Shed leaves can be steeped in water to brew an herbal tea popular in coastal parts of Kanto.
author: sk372

entry: When confronted with danger, POKENAME will kick its feet and clap its wings, brushing sand and dirt into its attacker's eyes and giving them enough time to escape. They can be very affectionate with their Trainer and will dance to impress them.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Due to the excess feathers on its arms, POKENAME cannot fly. When it tries, it flails wildly, which is often mistaken for cheering from a distance.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME secretes a Chesto Berry-scented sap from its beak to lure in unsuspecting prey. Once they get close, it dispatches them with a sudden Gust attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are covered in soft, fluffy down that repels dust and dirt. It glides effortlessly through the sky, leaving behind delicate trails of shimmering feathers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits distressed chirping noises to lure in unsuspecting prey like Ekans. Once close enough, it drags them beneath the sand's surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is not afraid of heights and crawls over branches. It is in constant search of food, as the fungi on its back slowly extract its nutrients.
author: chorb33

entry: It has an abundance of pride in its abilities. Trainers value POKENAME for their ability to spot hidden items from yards away.
author: schwaus

entry: When POKENAME gets its feathers wet, they shake violently to dry off. This draws predators' attention, causing them to scatter and dive, getting wet once again.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hates fighting and usually hides in tall herbs or sand. If it's startled, it may attack with its sharp beak, as hard as wood.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: POKENAME's eyes can spot even the smallest bug Pokémon in the smallest crack of a tree trunk. It rubs its body against trees to release powder that causes bug Pokémon to crawl out paralyzed or poisoned.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME lurk in graveyards where they have easy access to food offerings from grieving families. It is considered a bad omen if POKENAME refuse to eat food offerings that are left behind.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Flocks of POKENAME often get lost because of how pervasive light pollution is in their environment. Scientists have engineered new lamp posts that minimize how much light faces upward, helping POKENAME avoid getting lost.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME perches on lily pads, waiting for prey like Feebas to emerge before striking with precise pecks. On rainy days, it spreads its wings wide to collect raindrops, cooling itself in the humid air.
author: .izik

entry: The long, wide beak easily allows this Pokémon to gather Berries from bushes with ease. It uses its tail to roast the gathered Berries.
author: themadcactus

entry: When this bird Pokémon is seen flying on foggy mornings, it is said that its tail acts as a beacon for lost travelers, leading them towards shelter.
author: themadcactus

entry: Wild POKENAME often molt their own feathers and use them for dens because they won't catch fire the way twigs do.
author: themadcactus

entry: When the skies are calm, it roosts up high to scan the horizon. To find a blue POKENAME feather is considered very lucky.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME nest on the ground, gathering up fallen twigs and mixing them with mud to form a protective ring around their young. Young POKENAME burrow down through the middle of their childhood nest as soon as they're old enough to move.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swims through the air as if it were water, instead of flying. It is extremely shy, and there have been no recorded sightings of a wild POKENAME at rest.
author: linhasxoc

entry: When a Pokémon POKENAME chases decides to turn and fight back on it, POKENAME kicks sand in their eyes to get them running again. If the foe isn't scared, it jumps into some tall grass to hide away.
author: soup1900

entry: Whenever POKENAME fly, they carry a clump of dirt with them that is incredibly difficult to remove. This piece of dirt resists being washed off by water, which makes seeing their undersides nearly impossible.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are a common nuisance for farmers because POKENAME love to eat the roots of crops. Whenever they need to make an escape, they carry a clump of dirt that protects their underside while they fly away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME inhabits soil near cliff faces. Its piercing morning chirps are infamous for driving nearby residents away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tends to live with its flock in rural towns, using rooftops and balconies as artificial shelters while building its nest. It always flies in groups to maximize hunting efficiency.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME tends to nest among the rocky cliffs overlooking the sea together with the flock that it never leaves throughout its entire life. It squawks loudly every time it is about to use any of its moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME makes its nest with stolen money or belongings between the sticks and twigs of its base. If it finds a shinier nest from another POKENAME, it will attempt to fight for ownership of it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME use their paws in tandem with their talons to grasp large prey. During mating season, they spend hours preening and may even steal shiny objects near cities to attract potential mates.
author: corndogyip

entry: POKENAME forages by quickly scratching at dry, dusty earth, then pecking the ground to snatch up dislodged seeds or Bug-types. POKENAME will also kick dust into the eyes of predators to disarm them.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is a patient hunter that can lie in wait for an entire day, biding its time before pouncing on its prey. Its feathers are smooth as silk, and it uses them to build luxurious and comfortable nests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Even though their bodies are not able to fly well, POKENAME still tries to glide across trees for its prey. Even after hitting its head several times on the way down, POKENAME will still climb back up and try again.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME in the wild often act as mentors to Pidgey flocks, training and keeping the small birds in line. Though very patient by nature, they won't hesitate to punt one of their trainees if they get too uppity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME becomes highly agitated if the wind ruffles its feathers too much. It dive-bombs intruders from treetops, striking repeatedly with its talons until it feels its pride is restored.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is fiercely loyal and will chirp loudly to warn its Trainer of danger. If threatened, it exhales bursts of warm air from its beak, singeing any would-be attackers.
author: .izik

entry: Having developed claws, this Pokémon will take Berries from bushes with their claws, peeling Berries with thicker skins before roasting them.
author: themadcactus

entry: A POKENAME's wings cannot support it alone, but its lungs are constantly filled with hot air, making it lighter than it should be.
author: themadcactus
