author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME awaken in the early hours of the morning to get every drop of sunlight it can. Many Trainers have been awoken to the sounds of entire flocks of POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME secures its foot to cave walls while sleeping, its mushroom-like body glowing faintly in the dark. As it rests, it makes soft, echoing hoots that soothe other Pokémon nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits piercing supersonic hoots to disorient foes. It follows up with a swift dive and a startling Astonish attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carries what appears to be an old-fashioned wooden clock around on its lower limb. The clock lacks proper functionality, but the rhythmic click inside of it truly does go off once every second.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Just before it explodes, POKENAME lets out a rapid series of hoots and performs a small hop. The blast leaves behind only scattered feathers and ash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's singing is helpful for making Trainers fall asleep at night. Its singing is so effective that it frequently puts itself to sleep.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME always emerges into the moonlight at the very second night falls. Ten minutes before morning begins, it begins hooting rhythmically as it plants one rooted foot into the soil.
author: soup1900

entry: Its exceptional sense of rhythm allows POKENAME to execute perfect dance steps. It is believed that its performances can calm the souls of the departed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: They sprout black feathers from their trunk when awake and wave their feathers to keep track of time. These feathers are said to help the children regain memories of when they were younger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its internal clock is highly precise. It memorizes the schedules of small nocturnal Pokémon to improve its hunting.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time dwelling in the dark nests it builds high up in shady trees. When its rotational organ detects prime mushroom growth times, it descends to begin scavenging.
author: steamedveggies.

entry: POKENAME loves to go on late night walks with its Trainer, dragging them eagerly forward along moonlit paths. They have a particular fondness for going out at the full moon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME keeps a strict foraging schedule, timing its every move to avoid danger. If disrupted, the break in routine causes it debilitating levels of stress.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roams near lampposts at night, releasing green Sleep Powder from its feathers. Its prey rarely sees it before dozing off.
author: .izik

entry: They control vines to give themselves a secure grip to hang upside down from. This allows them to wave their black feathers, which helps them maintain their perfect sense of time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its small wings to dig at remarkable speeds. If threatened, it bursts from the soil and flies away instantly.
author: .izik

entry: During the day, POKENAME rest at depths where little to no sunlight can penetrate. They have internal mechanisms that do not require visual cues to tell them when night falls, allowing them to rise to the surface at sundown.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Throughout history, many famous explorers were known to keep POKENAME around as they could fly and scout long distances. Records show that they were also used as timekeepers.
author: mepp.

entry: It likes to pilfer coins from passersby, but observation has noted that the attempts at stealing adhere to a strict schedule, allowing locals to help travelers plan their time to avoid being robbed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are fastidious with their timekeeping and refuse to deviate from their daily routine. Whenever something unexpected happens, the delay in their schedule causes them to develop a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME bounces around jabbing at its foes, but its attacks are fairly repetitive and predictable. Because of this, smarter Pokémon can easily outwit it.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME have trouble sleeping, often suffering from bouts of insomnia due to their constant need to be on the move. They grow increasingly irritable as they grow more tired, becoming prone to getting into fights when they're exhausted.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME makes for a tricky pet to raise, as it adheres to a strict daily schedule for feeding, recreation and so forth. Any deviation from this schedule tends to cause it stress.
author: sk372

entry: They prefer to wade in shallow water, as their inept legs prevent them from running away. They use their sense of time to avoid predators by traveling when their predators are asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can often be found in shallow streams on dark nights. It hunts Magikarp and Bug-type Pokémon that stray too close to the shore, using the spiral pattern on its belly to hypnotize its prey.
author: snookerron

entry: The hands of POKENAME's clock are made of organs visible through its transparent belly. It always shows the correct time.
author: milchik

entry: They challenge other Pokémon to sparring matches, fighting with a high level of precision and dexterity. It is said that they have low stamina however, as no fight lasts longer than exactly ten minutes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wake up the same time every day to catch aquatic Pokémon. By pressing an ear to their shell, a person can listen to the internal ticks that maintain a POKENAME's sense of time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often hunt in packs. The synchronized ticking within their shells helps them coordinate their movements, the pack lunging forward when they hear their leader's shrill, ringing call.
author: victor9106

entry: POKENAME is an expert navigator and can never get lost under normal circumstances, as it possesses several organs that act as dedicated navigational instruments, like a map, compass, and even an altimeter. Only its size limits its use for explorers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It adheres to a strict schedule of nightly dream consumption. If one feels a disturbance in their sleep at the same time every evening, a POKENAME is likely to be residing nearby.
author: sk372

entry: It has incredible jumping power and easily goes from place to place in the night. From the bulb on its back can a dazzling powder that stuns foes be released.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rely on the bulb on their backs to maintain a sense of time. They can determine what time it is by listening to the soft ticking of their bulb.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is most active during dusk and uses the falling night to devour foliage. It will ruthlessly attack other small Bug-type Pokémon that dare to compete with its meal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME sobs loudly at night, releasing deep hoots between each cry. These sounds serve as long-distance communication with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: These bird Pokémon hunt in flocks and communicate by striking their horns with their bone clubs. POKENAME never waste any part of their prey and use the bones both as tools and as markers for their territories.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal hunters that live mostly in deserts. These clever Pokémon use the remains of their prey as weapons and tools, even though their claws are strong enough to gouge rock.
author: infinex21

entry: It can see in darkness without much effort. When it uses its psychokinetic abilities, its eyes will glow purple for a short period.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides silently through the night, its wings shimmering under the moonlight. With the ability to hypnotize foes, it uses its mesmerizing patterns to create illusions and escape danger.
author: thepandasharky

entry: It hangs from branches while wrapped in its silk to be carried by the wind. Though its horns are sharp, they are often too heavy for it to use as a weapon.
author: silverscloudy

entry: When POKENAME spreads its wings, its gelatinous body shudders. It can transform into anything it sees while doing this motion, using its versatility to adapt to any situation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is excellent for Trainers who wish to remain punctual. It has a perfect sense of time and memory, setting an alarm on every electronic in a person's house to make sure they do not forget an appointment.
author: sk372

entry: The only part of POKENAME that moves is its head, tilting back and forth with the passing seconds. It's assumed it's counting down the exact number of seconds it will take for it to complete evolution.
author: sk372

entry: This lazy, dopey-looking Pokémon is a welcome sight in the forest, as it is more than happy to cuddle up to any passing Pokémon or Trainers.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME uses its superior eyesight at night to patrol the forest near its hive. Should a predator get too close, it will jab at them with its stingers, protecting its territory with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME become active at sunset, the dimming light triggering an internal sense of time and encouraging them to begin their day. Their night vision is poor and they rely on their sensitive feathers to feel air currents to navigate in the dark.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's lithe body makes it highly aerodynamic, able to take off and maneuver through the air silently and gracefully. This makes it very efficient at both hunting and evading attacks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's nest is stuffed to the brim with herbs it finds throughout the forest it resides in. It lets out soft hoots while it sleeps through the day, adding to the tranquil atmosphere of its home.
author: .izik

entry: The older and wiser a POKENAME gets, the more powerful its psychic powers become. The long beard is a symbol of longevity and respect amongst POKENAME.
author: ilazerheart

entry: Highly intelligent, POKENAME captures prey with carefully-planned web placement, borne from many nights of careful observation. It knows the perfect place to set its trap based on its prey's daily habits.
author: sk372

entry: They form groups to stalk prey at night, using a series of groans and buzzes to communicate. Their buzzes remind people of the sound of an accordion, so some aristocrats keep them as pets for their musical talents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hunts solely at night and is rarely seen due to the speeds it can achieve thanks to its four wings. Its eyesight is so sharp that it can navigate even the thickest of forests and easily spot any foes or food no matter how dark it may be.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefers to fly through stormy nights, relishing in the high winds as it tests its flying prowess. The turbulent skies fuel its strength, making it a formidable force in the air.
author: .izik

entry: Because POKENAME stay awake all through the night, Trainers frequently have a hard time keeping them awake during the day. These strong-willed Pokémon often refuse to battle so they can nap instead.
author: .realthree

entry: The feathers behind POKENAME's head stick straight up when it has a vision. It can see up to 20 years in the future with ease, often predicting outcomes of events far ahead of time.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to receive regular visions of the future, and is often seen in quiet contemplation. Many believe its mind is constantly racing with thoughts on how to continue shaping the perfect future.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME soars through the night, patrolling its territory from above with perfect vision. It can reach flight speeds capable of challenging jets and private airplanes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME meet in groups at night to dance, which have been observed to correspond with the constellations overhead. The leaf skirt exudes an aroma used in perfume favored by clubbers and students for its ability to keep those smelling it awake.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lets loose a Bluk Berry scent from the rock-hard feathers on its head to encourage Hoothoot in the area to nest on it. Their presence seems to calm it, creating a serene environment for the birds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travels low near the water's surface during the nighttime hours, searching for prey. Its flight pattern is jagged, allowing it to make quick turns and unpredictable movements to catch its targets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives beneath the water, but preys on land-dwelling creatures. Its small wings only allow it to fly a few metres above the ground and make it hard to sneak up on prey, but it is covered in a gel that dulls the senses of anything nearby.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME patrols its territory at night, its beak glowing a dull yellow as it travels. Its eyes can see through dense fog with ease, allowing it to keep a sharp lookout during the darkest hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hoots sound oddly human-like despite it not knowing how to speak any human language. It does this to disorient travelers and corner them, using the unsettling sounds to keep them off balance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME moves in spurts: it can hop or flap its wings almost exactly once per second. Foes trying to catch it off guard will find that its feathers have corrosive properties.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has a sense of timing to the second. The connection between this and the clock-like growth on its back has not yet been adequately studied.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rummages through dumpsters at night, using its beak to dig for scraps. It turns its head fully around every few moments to watch for predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets loose psychic waves when it spreads its wings. If it ever gets tired of flying, it will lower itself to the ground steadily with telekinesis, gracefully landing on its feet.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME gets startled while flying, it will immediately explode. As such, it avoids flying during thunderstorms, as the thunder distresses it, triggering a premature detonation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pulls its feathers close to its body while digging through the soil. Should it find root vegetables, it will eat them without hesitation, savoring the earthy flavors of its underground finds.
author: .izik

entry: Many wild POKENAME have proven to be the best nocturnal predators. Swift, precise, quiet, and unfailing are some of the most used adjectives to describe POKENAME.
author: k1n1t0.xo

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beak and claws to burrow out nests inside of tree trunks, sheltering within them during the day. At night they call out to one another with incredibly loud screeches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Flocks of POKENAME dart through forests at night. They will gang up on prey like Weedle, surrounding it to ensure there is no escape before diving in for the capture.
author: .izik

entry: The shell on POKENAME's back works as a functioning clock. However, these clocks are usually inaccurate, and seem to work on times based in other regions.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME uses its long neck to pursue startled prey into their burrows. It is more active in twilight hours, so many hikers have been startled when glimpsing the skull-shaped chest plumage in the low light.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is a nighttime predator that may either hunt independently or in a group. When it howls, POKENAME's concertation blossoms, and it may begin using a variety of unique and uncommon hunting strategies.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its high intelligence helps it formulate hunting plans that rarely fail. Its hooting cry has a distinctly artificial tone to it, and has been noted to disrupt the time-keeping function of technology in its vicinity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME jumps from high cliffs and glides with its wings, using its antler's psychic abilities to stabilize its movements. The psychic energy from its antlers allows it to navigate through the air with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME must be milked at least once a day, or it becomes too heavy to take flight. If anyone approaches the farm where it lives during the night, it drives them off without hesitation.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME cares for sick or injured Hoothoot in the soft pouch on its body. If danger approaches, it curls its body forward to shield the pouch.
author: mepp.

entry: After building its nest with nearby saplings, POKENAME keeps watch during the night hours. It will pelt predators with Apricorns thrown from its two tails, using its agility to defend its home.
author: .izik

entry: It hunts only on the darkest of nights with gangs of Murkrow and Hoothoot alike. It commands them ruthlessly, keeping each of its goons in line with a psychic attack.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME channels an odd power through the stone-hard feathers on its head that can make a foe fall asleep. Once they slumber, it flees quickly, leaving the opponent unaware of its departure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME may be an excellent hunter, but it often falls over while trying to impersonate its Trainer. Walking on two legs is difficult for it.
author: smashbear

entry: POKENAME will pick up and incubate the eggs of other Pokémon and nurture them until they're ready to hatch. Most Pokémon will allow them to hang around their nesting sites to look after their young.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In thunderstorms, they ground their tail in the ground and spread their wings, daring lightning to hit them. The electrical charges stored in their body supercharge their brains.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME are most active on cold, dark nights. They hunt in groups, swooping down to catch prey while hidden under the cover of darkness.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME often sleeps through the day, being primarily active at night. However, at least one head is always awake to keep an eye out.
author: moopse

entry: Although it doesn't have the ability to fly, it loves to hide in trees. The problem is that it is too heavy for the branches, causing them to fall.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME performs pirouettes and twirls while dancing during combat, using its wings to keep balance. The graceful movements not only confuse foes but also add an elegant flair to its battle style.
author: .izik

entry: Intelligent and kind, POKENAME watches over those lost in the forest at night. It silently repels those who would hunt them with psychic powers, and many are unaware their safe passage was due to POKENAME's protection.
author: sk372

entry: This variety of POKENAME is widely believed to have been cursed once upon a time. Nobody knows why it has only one arm, but it does not seem to be held back by its lack of said appendage.
author: cinnamoone_redfield

entry: POKENAME silently soars through the night sky without moving its wings. Folklore says that its horn halo glows particularly bright when ferrying a good person to the afterlife.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is always on high alert, keeping a lookout for anything that could threaten its nest. It has a very resilient digestive system, allowing it to consume poisonous plants and berries.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can carry logs of up to 100 lbs while flying. It uses these logs to build dams, contributing to its impressive construction skills and the maintenance of its home environment.
author: .izik

entry: The older POKENAME is, the longer and thicker the vine on its back gets. This Pokémon was admired by humans since ancient times for its wise look, and some cultures believe that it was POKENAME who originally taught people to tell time.
author: milchik

entry: A strong venom accumulates in POKENAME's beak, which will be dispensed if it has to defend its home. Its nest is decorated with flowers it gathers from around the nearby forest.
author: .izik

entry: Their large yellow feathers can alter their color in darkness so it does not alert prey while it hunts during the night. It first targets prey that are lost and in despair.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A thick brown poison comes off POKENAME's feathers when it is stressed. The poison smells awful, despite being relatively harmless, and is used to ward off threats in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: The horn coming out of POKENAME's head is made of the same material that forms its beak. It is filled with a corrosive poison that POKENAME can spray out at distances of up to 20 feet, causing severe irritation and damage.
author: .izik

entry: The thick feathers that grow from the end of POKENAME's arm are extremely sharp and able to pierce steel. It flies in spiral patterns when fighting, using its agility and sharp feathers to overwhelm its opponents.
author: .izik

entry: With powerful eyesight, hearing, and quick speed on the ground and in the air, POKENAME is an unparalleled hunter. The beak on its tail possesses a tongue-like organ that can discharge incredible amounts of electricity with just a tap.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME watches over heavily forested mountain areas, treating the inhabitants as its subjects. It is highly intelligent and prefers peaceful coexistence, not hesitating to cast out Pokémon that pick too many fights in its domain.
author: sk372

entry: Clockmakers rely on POKENAME to help adjust clocks to the correct time. From grandfather clocks to watches, POKENAME ensure that the correct time is displayed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This intimidating fusion of Zoroark and Noctowl has a fierce reputation as a ferocious and aggressive predator which should not be taken lightly. There is some truth to this as they are very protective of their young.
author: elfail0

entry: The ribbon-like feathers on POKENAME's head are used in scarves across Sinnoh. While they are not known to keep wearers warm, they are highly valued for their beauty and fashionable appeal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have powerful tails, venomous horns, and superb vision. Despite their bulk, POKENAME are surprisingly agile.
author: essie

entry: POKENAME floats silently through the night, siphoning energy from the dreams of those it flies over and storing it in red cyclones to use for attacks.
author: moopse

entry: Despite not being a Psychic type, this fusion shows an aptitude for psionic abilities. Some theorize some eldritch power lies deep within it.
author: jaycielantern

entry: POKENAME can often be seen floating quietly in the night sky. These large, round Pokémon attract local Hoothoot, who see it as a guardian.
author: moopse

entry: In battle, POKENAME shields its body with its massive ears, contemplating multiple battle factors to calculate the best course of action. Once it's formulated a plan, it leaps out of its shielding and fights back with powerful kicks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME soars through forests and urban areas at night in complete silence. It unleashes a shrill song to communicate with others, which alongside its stealth and unblinking, red eyes has led to many believing it is a bad omen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its loud cuckoo-clock mechanism to startle passersby. Then, the hands on its clock face begin spinning wildly and its chimes toll, adding on to the confusion.
author: ilazerheart

entry: It is an urban legend that when the clock strikes midnight, anyone who hears all twelve chirps from POKENAME will perish. Its heartbeat syncs with the rhythm of the pendulum inside its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is an urban legend that when the clock strikes midnight, anyone who hears all twelve chirps from POKENAME will perish. Its heartbeat syncs with the rhythm of the pendulum inside its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Six times a day, POKENAME will cough up a fireball that floats above it and bursts into a shower of sparks. It appears to be merely recreation, though none are sure why it never deviates from that exact number.
author: sk372

entry: Sometimes while at rest, POKENAME will expel its innards out of its body in a way that mimics the hands of a clock. The positions the hands take is always a perfect match for the current time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME quietly observes its target in the darkness, analyzing the best time to strike. It spreads embers in front of fleeing prey, sending them scurrying the opposite direction, often right into its waiting talons.
author: sk372

entry: It is unknown if the eyes on POKENAME's wings are real or not. Some people swear that they've seen them move, while others consider it a hoax.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME makes little noise as it flies through dark forests thanks to the structure of its wings. It traps unaware prey in a vicious Fire Spin before diving in to finish them.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's feathers crackle with electricity during combat. When angry, they spark uncontrollably, releasing bursts of power that can shock foes and leave them temporarily stunned.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always knows what time it is and relies on its internal sense of time to sing lullabies at the same time every night. Without POKENAME, wild Pokémon find it difficult to fall asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its small size, POKENAME are surprisingly ferocious and will not shy away from opponents many times their size. They are astonishingly stealthy as well, able to stalk prey through even the thickest foliage in silence.
author: elfail0

entry: The yellow goo formed around POKENAME's feathery body is incredibly sticky. This sweet slime is frequently used in oatmeal or biscuits at cafes, making it a sought-after ingredient for local treats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its strong beak to drill into a cave ceiling to make a den. Its persistence allows it to create a secure home, protected from the dangers that roam the caves below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers are very hot to the touch. They can cause third-degree burns if touched, making it a dangerous creature to approach or engage in close combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts exclusively at night, hiding away in its cave once the sun rises. Its large beak is great at breaking through tough nuts and berries, allowing it to devour them in a single bite.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME's ruby eyes glow ominously, enemies fall under its Hypnosis. Once successfully immobilized, POKENAME claws at them with vicious intent.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's body has baffled researchers since they were first fused. The wood-like material that composes their body is toxic.
author: ohok3441

entry: Thanks to their large bodies, POKENAME are clumsy. They have a tendency to stumble around and fly into windows.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's leaves wobble slightly to let loose a strong Iapapa Berry scent, using this to attract prey. This natural aroma lures in curious creatures which it captures with its swift flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen doing its slow and swaying dance in the evening, before it takes off in flight to hunt. It's believed it is communing with the spirit of its ancestors, who aid it in its subsequent search for prey.
author: sk372

entry: Feather-like leaves grow from any tree stump POKENAME possesses. The leaves have a very bitter taste, and when they fall, they leave behind a lasting impression on any creature that dares to nibble them.
author: .izik

entry: Though it stands perfectly rigid, its eyes dart around, taking in its surroundings with perfect clarity. Once it sees the opportunity to hunt, it moves with calculated perfection, its prey disappearing from the forest in total silence.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal Pokémon who are most active on moonless nights, where their night vision allows them to find any prey. They neutralize their targets with ultrasonic waves before descending upon them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be completely stationary for up to weeks at a time, keeping a watchful eye on its surroundings. If it does spot its prey, it moves so fast that its prey doesn't have time to react.
author: mistymagius

entry: Ancient legends speak of POKENAME as bad omens, harbingers of misfortune and malice on moonlit nights. In truth, POKENAME have little interest in people and are often aloof and disinterested, even toward their Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As the moon rises, POKENAME signals the start of the hunt by spreading its wings wide. Its flock answers with haunting cries in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: The feather-like leaves covering POKENAME's body are commonly used in dyeing clothing. Their rich color and texture are prized for making vibrant and durable dyes, popular in artisan markets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal creatures that follow bright lights, easily getting lost. Despite this, they always manage to return to their nest by dawn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stalk their prey from the treetops at night. Their exceptional eyesight and agility make them formidable hunters.
author: garret95

entry: The glow from POKENAME's feathers can put a person to sleep, bringing with it sad dreams. Its soft glow lulls its victims into a peaceful slumber before they're consumed by melancholy visions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's paper-thin wings allow for it to fly through the air in complete silence, allowing it to catch prey off-guard. Ancient people used to use POKENAME as a covert messenger during war times.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME perches in pumpkin patches at night, using its superior eyesight to watch for Pokémon that try to steal the crop. Its Wing Attack is used to fend off intruders, defending its patch with fierce dedication.
author: .izik

entry: The rich chocolate-like flavor of its plumage makes it a popular fusion. Many Trainers have been known to fuse a Noctowl and Slurpuff just to satisfy a chocolate craving.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME only digs after sunset and sleeps during the day. At dawn, it carefully grooms dirt from its feathers before resting again.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can use their telekinesis to synchronize clocks without any mistakes. They often forget that they have this ability and are quite shocked when they see the results of their labor.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are calm and tactful creatures that observe Trainers from a distance. If the Trainer they observe meets their arbitrary requirements, they reveal themselves and allow capture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Unlike Hootkey, POKENAME is very intelligent and can easily avoid foes. However, it can also be very brutal with its prey. It should not be underestimated.
author: ayutac

entry: POKENAME are similar to Hawlucha in many ways, but are a bit smarter and more temperamental. They are adaptable and can learn Fighting and Flying-type attacks easily.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME tilts its head 180 degrees before unleashing flames from its beak. This is a telltale sign for combatants to know when to evade, as its fiery breath can be extremely dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: It is highly sought after as a companion due to its loyalty and intelligence. Approach with caution, as it will only allow select humans to fly on its back.
author: bostroms

entry: Its wisdom is well known throughout riverside villages. It observes the failed hunts of Hootwag to ensure it does not repeat its mistakes.
author: snookerron

entry: POKENAME have a tendency to make nests next to small ponds, using the spiral on their belly to hypnotize prey and feasting until they are full. Once their new nest can no longer satisfy their binge-eating habits, they move on to another pond.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME exerts psychic waves when it extends its wings. This can cause a foe to become confused, making them vulnerable to follow-up attacks or a quick escape.
author: .izik

entry: Rare eyewitness accounts have spotted wild POKENAME participating in late-night bouts of sparring against various Pokémon. Though nocturnal, it is known to be proud and showy by nature.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are employed at retirement homes to help guide the elderly in late night walks and bring dishes to multiple people at once. Those with troubled pasts have reported a sense of dread when they make eye contact with POKENAME.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's stomach makes up most of its body, allowing it to swallow small Pokémon whole. It hunts during the night, spotting and swallowing their prey before they even know it was there.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a keen sense of timing, allowing them to synchronize with each other down to the exact millisecond. If a Trainer is ever late in front of their POKENAME, it will jab them with a toxin that will stun them for as long as they were late.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME gathers stones to keep within its home in the upper parts of tree trunks. Once its keen eyes spot prey running below, it uses its strong stone arms to hurl the rocks and knock out its target.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has been observed holding its stick at different angles depending on the hour. No matter the time and position, it is always capable of wielding its weapon with calculated precision.
author: sk372

entry: When the speckled rocks on POKENAME's midsection begin to turn, foes begin to feel dizzy and as if the world beneath them was trembling. POKENAME only goes after Berries or foes that are properly weak and disoriented.
author: bobosmith01

entry: An oil that coats POKENAME's feathers can cause extreme exhaustion and fatigue. It uses this to make its prey fall asleep before feeding on their dreams, leaving them weakened and disoriented.
author: .izik

entry: It converts sunlight into a poisonous fluid and stores it inside the seed on its back. The poison is very potent, but POKENAME is too timid to use it in battle.
author: megashit100000

entry: It awakens the moment the sun hits the horizon. Once up, it immediately begins eating leaves until its belly is full.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's unblinking eyes are always on the lookout for potential dangers around it. It leaves star-shaped indentations in the ground after it explodes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swarm flower fields to smack flowers with their boney clubs. This sudden burst of movement forces pollen to spread throughout the air, pollinating the flowers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME avoids conflict by skittering away on its extensible legs. If cornered, it squeezes its eyes shut and flails with all six limbs, hoping to intimidate predators with the apparent display of martial prowess.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: It lets out a whistle when it spots a sunrise. The sunlight seems to nourish its body, causing it to sway back and forth with delight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long vine-like arms to grab and eat petals, avoiding movement from its ingrained spot in the flower field. It spends most of its day absorbing nutrients from the soil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release pheromones from their poppy-colored wings to gather groups of Ledyba into one area. Once gathered, POKENAME lead the group to gather nectar or berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's two razor-sharp scythes scare off most Pokémon. However, it has a gentle nature and only uses them when in danger.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME moves quickly on the ocean floor by running on their hands, pushing themselves off every step.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME uses the horn on its head to poke holes in tree bark and sip the sap inside. It hums softly while feeding, attracting other bug Pokémon to join the meal.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's polka dot pattern and many evolutions make it very popular among bug type enthusiasts. It welcomes Oran Berries as gifts.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME roams websites consuming images that feature flowers. After devouring 20, it settles quietly on a desktop, concealed behind files.
author: .izik

entry: Normally kept tucked close to its cocoon, POKENAME can extend its fists short distances in order to deter predators. Its sensitive antennae and strong eyesight let it remain wary of anything approaching its surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is constantly drifting between being partially conscious and being in the early stages of a typical sleep cycle. When frightened, it emits a foul-smelling fluid from its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It will shed its skin often. Researchers hypothesize that the black-dotted patterns left behind on its skin are directions for other POKENAME to gather with each other.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME live together en masse, and among one another are quite agreeable. However, if alone or if threatened, POKENAME turn violent and stubborn.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME protects its nest with Safeguard when Ekans draws near. It flies in coordination with its siblings to distract attackers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps watch from the tops of hills. If it spots a predator, it will cry out for its allies while using Reflect to keep the enemy at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME perches on telephone poles in the early morning to hoot at the rising sun. Its rhythmic cries are said to calm nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Errors during the fusion process that produces POKENAME result in them having significantly more limbs than their unfused counterparts. They use these extra arms to scuttle quickly, but they struggle to properly control them for combat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spin webs that take the appearance of stars. Each web has a unique scent tied to each individual POKENAME.
author: gotfyr

entry: POKENAME are a rare site in the wild. Their webs consist of a multiple star shaped patterns that glow under a starry night sky.
author: gotfyr

entry: These blue horned variants of POKENAME are an even rarer find. It is rumored that those with blue horns have the most authority over other POKENAME.
author: gotfyr

entry: POKENAME shock predators to give themselves an opportunity to escape. Their long appendages also regrow over time, so they are not worried about losing a limb or two to ensure escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generates dangerous electricity. Due to its cute appearance and friendly nature, other Pokémon do not attack it, and even humans who dislike bugs do not consider this creature a pest. Once captured, it is often considered a family member.
author: lutrax

entry: POKENAME lets out an incessant buzz whenever it gets upset. This buzz upsets other baby Pokémon in the area, creating a cacophony of buzzes and crying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stick together in large groups at all times. For example, they huddle together for warmth during the cold season, and they all get together in the early hours of the morning to eventually fly with one another during the warm season.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME grab onto berries with the hand on their tail, which has tiny bumps to improve their grip. Once they latch onto a berry, they buzz away with a new sweet treat in hand.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are considered pests by gardeners because they siphon nutrients away from root systems and eat flowers. Removing a POKENAME infestation is difficult because they are quite fast and reproduce rapidly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Hordes of POKENAME live in mound-like structures that are full of water. They crawl over each other to pass on information, which is surprisingly rapid, with messages being sent from deep underground to those at the surface in a few seconds.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Most physically active during the early morning hours, POKENAME spends most of its day basking in sunlight. Personalities and social hierarchy varies dramatically between each group of POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: At night, when this Pokémon is alone, POKENAME will let out soft cries akin to the sound of a person in mourning at a funeral. During the early morning hours, POKENAME will sit in the rays of the sun to warm up before resting.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME lives in warmer climates, feasting off grass and small Bug-type Pokémon. It has an unpredictable personality and can unexpectedly attack those nearby.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If POKENAME consumes too many flower petals, its body becomes unstable. Even a light tap can trigger an abrupt explosion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives burrowed under the dirt until the last few minutes of the sun being on the horizon, and then retreats as the cold settles in deeper. Each POKENAME has a unique pattern of spots and stripes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have a cacophonous cry that instills fear in farmers. Groups of POKENAME sweep over farms, eating anything in their path.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love honey and will do anything to get more. They are known to collude with other POKENAME to swarm hives and steal honeycombs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hates being apart from others of its own kind. Therefore, POKENAME will secrete scented pheromones that other POKENAME can track by sniffing the ground.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Schools of POKENAME are able to travel together very quickly underwater. Despite their minuscule size, Team Aqua values POKENAME for their ability to overwhelm opponents with sheer numbers.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: Male POKENAME beat their wings rapidly while howling to impress mates. The louder the howl, the greater their chance of attracting a partner.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's trunk possesses a sense of smell strongly attuned to sweet aromas. The berries and mushrooms it finds and forages are delectable, if almost sickeningly sweet in taste.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be seen on the outskirts of settlements, feeding in fields and farmland. It is skittish and prone to fleeing at the first sight of Trainers or hostile Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's multiple arms allow it a controlled and more intricate touch to its brushstrokes when painting. Stars are often a major theme in the drawings it creates.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME regularly uses its skill in combat to protect the cities in which it resides from crime. Its work is so renowned that one stars in a popular TV show based in Lumiose City from the Kalos Region.
author: neo_technomon_8392

entry: POKENAME hunt through jungles for smaller Bug-Type Pokémon that they can swallow whole. When confronted with a threat that's larger than them, they flash the eyes on their hood and puff up to try and scare the danger away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is rather placid and happy to keep to itself, but holds a surprise for anybody approaching to hunt or milk it: what appear to be udders are six extendable fists ready to pummel anything making the mistake of bothering it.
author: sk372

entry: During winter, POKENAME hibernate deep within seaside caves, beating their wings to circulate warm air. Due to their cute appearance and gentle demeanor, they have become very popular online, with thousands gathering each spring to watch them emerge.
author: santon5512

entry: It is only found in the wild just as light starts to fill the sky, but before the sun is fully over the horizon. It lets out baneful, high-pitched screeches if discovered and quickly becomes timid.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is usually a very timid Pokémon. However, when it gets cold, it warms itself with stored electricity and can become quite aggressive.
author: zedsmith64

entry: As a group of five, POKENAME raid unprotected and unwatched wastebins in rural areas to gather food. In the Sinnoh region, they adore Honey Trees.
author: bobosmith01

entry: During the day, POKENAME bury themselves in the sand to escape the heat. They are fascinated by artificial light, and anything that glows at night will often have several POKENAME surrounding it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME secretes a heated oil from its stubby white wings that waterproofs its feathers. Trainers who partner with it often use soft brushes to spread the oil across the feathers on its head, occasionally suffering minor burns in the process.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME create large tunnels by working in unison with other POKENAME. They space themselves with enough space so that their rose-red spines don't interlock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though most of the spines on POKENAME's back are removable without issue, the dark spines are not, and POKENAME will become quite agitated if they are tampered with. Some believe they are directly attached to highly sensitive nerves.
author: sk372

entry: They swarm to people with a positive disposition, lured in by happiness and joy. They are otherwise elusive and shy, hiding from people and other Pokémon in bushes or caves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They prefer to travel in small colonies, as they are timid when in isolation. They have been incidents where colonies of POKENAME saunter into towns and chew on wooden foundations to sharpen their teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is very affectionate. If anyone compliments POKENAME's unique pattern of spots, it bounds over and nuzzles them happily. However, its immense weight often knocks the unfortunate admirer to the ground.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME can be seen roaming across the forest floor during the early morning, feeding on leaves that are coated in the morning dew. Their arms are stubby and ill-suited to battle, meaning they rely on swipes with their tail to fight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME was worshipped as a god of posies in ancient cultures. Floral offerings were placed before wild individuals in hopes of abundant harvests.
author: .izik

entry: During the spring, millions of POKENAME migrate north, slowly hobbling forward in a straight line for hundreds of miles. If separated from the group, they become incredibly anxious, finding the nearest place to hide until next spring.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME secrete soothing scents from the tips of their tails. These Pokémon use these scents to communicate with others; by utilizing their ribbon-like appendages, they can partly influence how this scent flows.
author: infinex21

entry: Timid by nature, POKENAME refuse to travel anywhere unless they are in a group for safety. Typically, groups of POKENAME travel by night, using the moon to navigate.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Large colonies of POKENAME like to cluster together on cave roofs. Be careful when passing underneath, as these Pokémon are very skittish and will fire waves of spines at any perceived threat.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME can be found foraging for fallen berries in the early morning in forests, cooking any food they find with their flames. They search for their food in small groups, yipping excitedly when a particularly large patch is found.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon spends its days sleeping in the tall grass inside forests. Some myths say if you wake it, it causes bad luck for nine generations!
author: skleegamer

entry: POKENAME acts with immense bravado until it gets stood up to, upon which it timidly flees screeching in fear. It rolls around to build up static electricity so it can use bursts of light to attract others of its kind.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The small shape on POKENAME's tail attracts hungry Flying-type Pokémon. Once close enough, POKENAME pounces and attacks with its electricity.
author: .realthree

entry: On windy days, POKENAME can be seen drifting just above the treetops, collecting berries with its extra-long arms. Once the wind dies down, it will stop to rest in the trees until the wind picks up again.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME prefers hot and humid environments. It can communicate with other POKENAME by emitting a scent. Each kind of scent means something different.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME bursts into flames if startled while eating petals off flowers. The fire rarely harms it but scorches nearby plants.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses Ingrain beneath tulip fields, merging with the underground root systems. Its body glows faintly with floral energy while resting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flutters carelessly over sunflower fields, descending to pluck seeds from the buds. It will bring them back to its nest for eating during the evening hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are most active just as the sun begins warming the area and before the morning dew begins to evaporate. They particularly love moist fruits. Their reclusive and shy nature belies their substantial power.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rolls aimlessly around grassy, green zones with plenty of hills. It seems generally harmless, but strangely turns aggressive when in the presence of Sandslash and other similar Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME keep the flower on their head curled up until they meet another POKENAME. They playfully communicate, which causes the flower to transform into a wide, beautiful bloom, showering onlookers with sweet-smelling pollen that causes drowsiness.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME holds down Pokémon that try to eat from its flower fields with its strong arms. Once grappled, it unleashes a powerful Bug Buzz.
author: .izik

entry: It doesn't mean any harm; however, POKENAME will often relax in vibrant flower fields only to find that it has trampled all vegetation around it.
author: char_latte3412

entry: It often travels alone, cautious and easily startled. However, amidst rarely-seen packs, it reveals a harsh, brutal demeanor.
author: char_latte3412

entry: It is said that those stabbed by its rock spike will turn into a POKENAME themselves. The superstitious will carry fresh citrus to protect themselves.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME's biggest threat isn't a predator, but the allure of bright lights from cars. Many environmental groups have proposed limiting speed limits to minimize harm to both people and Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats gently over meadows, releasing bursts of light from its torso. These glows serve as courtship signals to potential mates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats peacefully on the surface of ponds while eating lily petals. It uses Mega Drain if anyone gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: If disturbed while feeding on flower roots, POKENAME bursts from the soil and strikes with Mach Punch. The force is strong enough to send a Kakuna flying.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME steals coins from food vendors with quick jabs. It uses Light Screen to vanish from sight and escape without a trace.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are normally aloof Pokémon that are unfazed by events going on around them. When they see their trainer,  their wings buzz with excitement as they give a happy yowl, rushing over to rub their cheek against them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME huddle in tight circles during winter. The colder it gets, the more intense their headaches become - sometimes creating small psychic storms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are highly aggressive due to frequently being underestimated. Despite their lack of strength, they can wallop foes by cycling their punches with their four arms, eventually wearing their opponents down.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME swims at a leisurely pace in the ocean, feeding on kelp and the smallest organisms. The spots on its back can pulse with short-range bursts of energy to repel pests and predators.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers report seeing ponds of red water during the spring. This phenomenon may be explained by POKENAME spawning periods, when dozens hatch at the same time from submerged eggs.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME secretes sweat that smells like Cheri Berries during training. This scent draws in others of its kind to form group workouts.
author: .izik

entry: The vine-like body of POKENAME tastes extremely bitter, which causes most predators to avoid targeting it. It wriggles its limbs all around in combat. Each POKENAME has a slightly different color that is imperceptible on first glance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME feed on pond weed, using their shells to capture air so that they can breathe underwater. Their shells are patterned with black spots, the number and position of the spots enabling Pokémon researchers to identify where they're from.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME feed on pond weed, using their shells to capture air so that they can breathe underwater. Their shells are patterned with black spots, the number and position of the spots enabling Pokémon researchers to identify where they're from.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It uses its furry ears to balance while flying and swimming. The aromatic water it uses in attacks is often used in perfumes.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The only time POKENAME is found flying is when they're asleep. POKENAME loaf around in the air for a few minutes before returning to the ground once they wake up.
author: illuminatedphantom

entry: It uses its furry ears to balance itself while flying and swimming. The aromatic water it uses in its attacks is often used in perfumes.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: It communicates using the aromatic fluid it secretes from its eyes. A happy and healthy POKENAME will be fully encompassed by this fluid.
author: apixelperfectionist

entry: Easily rattled, POKENAME whacks anything that startles it with its little glove pendulum. The whacks barely do any damage, however.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME whir their wings to communicate with one another, making loud buzzing noises within different parts of the forest. They are not aerodynamic enough to be able to fly, but can glide short distances.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Lightweight and friendly, POKENAME propels itself through the air by blowing bubbles that move it backwards. It's said somewhere there exists a flute that can summon POKENAME forth with its song.
author: sk372

entry: This heroic Pokémon appears on starlit nights, pummels evildoers with a rapid barrage of kicks and punches, then dramatically vanishes. POKENAME's exploits have been serialized in a popular comic book.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Most POKENAME use their fight-or-flight responses well. Their light bodies can dodge attacks while consistently dishing them back out.
author: entomoxie

entry: Predators avoid POKENAME due to their poppy red wings, which resemble a group of Ledyba at a distance. Their sweet-smelling wings draw in flower Pokémon that they drink nectar from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its fighting style consists of strongly gripping its opponents with its horns, while throwing uppercuts until they faint. It cherishes finally being able to fly, and loves to reach high altitudes just to free fall and repeat.
author: epping_forest

entry: Several orbs embedded in POKENAME's back can separate and operate independently from it. These aid it greatly in fighting opponents, but even more so in helping it deal with malware when inhabiting cyberspace.
author: sk372

entry: Due to the cocoon and the body within being frail, POKENAME uses its four fists to vigorously defend itself. The scarf-like frill around its neck billows in the breeze, even when there is no discernible wind.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts only at night, lurking in forest glades where the air is at its purest. With a flap of its mighty wings, it whips up violent winds. Should its prey endure, it closes in and delivers a decisive bite with its powerful jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it falls on its back, it's impossible for a POKENAME to get back up on its own. With its soft belly exposed, it flails its six short limbs around to avert potential aggressors.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME's flames are composed of burning pollen spores. It takes care of other Pokémon, giving them warmth through its pollen as it flies over them.
author: chaozura

entry: Its life force is thought to be linked to starlight. Naturally, POKENAME becomes more active during the night, though it has been exceedingly rare to find one at all.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: After punching a foe relentlessly, POKENAME stings them with yellow venom. It drags defeated prey back to its hive as a trophy.
author: .izik

entry: Allegedly, keeping a POKENAME will bring you good luck. It enjoys basking in the sun and is very sensitive to the cold.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME collects rose petals and rubs them into its fluffy tail. The scent is said to calm nearby Pokémon during territorial disputes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have very keen eyesight, able to see for miles on clear days. They fly up high when the weather is clear and will swarm toward meadows with fresh flowers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME do not develop any extra strength over unfused Ledian, but they are capable of landing punches at a much higher rate. They use their speed offensively, chasing away threats to the swarm before problems can develop.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME do not develop any extra strength over unfused Ledian, but they are capable of landing punches at a much higher rate. They use their speed offensively, chasing away threats to the swarm before problems can develop.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME do not develop any extra strength over unfused Ledian, but they are capable of landing punches at a much higher rate. They use their speed offensively, chasing away threats to the swarm before problems can develop.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: After evolution, POKENAME prefer to live a more solitary life from eachother. If it senses danger it will protect both itself and others for justice.
author: alliveir

entry: POKENAME have a strong sense of justice and will defend any Pokémon that are in danger. They bounce off their elastic webs to travel at high speeds.
author: gotfyr

entry: POKENAME flies confidently through thunderstorms. It patrols flower meadows and drives off any Pokémon that threaten the blooms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sometimes mistaken for an aquatic Pokémon, so children may toss one back into a pond or lake. Despite the confusion, they do not seem to mind being tossed around, and some wiggle their antennas with glee.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has trained its arm muscles to a level where its wings are no longer needed. Instead, POKENAME can be seen furiously punching the air to fly.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME adores the scent of flowers, creating nests near flowerbeds. If it spots someone recklessly running through the meadow, it will furiously glide towards them, driving them off.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME produce a sweet aroma and shiny sparkles that are made into perfume. The soft fragrance is bottled into small sets that come from multiple POKENAME, which makes the perfume a great gift for dates.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats above lavender fields before gently descending to feast. The scent of crushed blooms follows it wherever it goes.
author: .izik

entry: It travels around cities, stealing bouquets from florists. It then places these flowers in its nest, masking the harsh city stench.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Most POKENAME live as the leader of a colony of Ledyper in large mounds. Should one of their subjects evolve into another POKENAME, they both battle and the loser must leave the colony to try and start their own.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has huge eyes, perfect for taking in light in the early morning or late evening when they are most active. They keep their distance from larger Pokémon, baring their large fangs when threatened but preferring to run.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Inhaling too much pollen drives POKENAME into a wild frenzy. It bites anything nearby; foe, friend, or even its Trainer.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses psychic powers to gently lift pollen from flowers and eat it. It drifts through fields, preferring older flora over newly blossomed ones.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's scaly ligaments shut in the cold but open and flare out in the heat. Warm nights are POKENAME's favorite; they may even detach from the tree they hang from to bounce around happily.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a staunch defender of insect Pokémon. If it spots a bug being picked on, it descends with heroic flair and retaliates on the aggressor with a flurry of punches from its four metallic claws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sees the world through heat vision. Its molten body is dotted with bits of bug-like exoskeleton, boosting its defensive capabilities.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME are naturally early risers, waking as soon as the sun rises and continuing to remain active throughout the day. This, combined with their willingness to haul equipment strapped to their shells, makes them a popular companion amongst Hikers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME adorns its nest with wildflowers that it clutches in its beak. It reacts aggressively to intruders, landing strong punches without hesitation.
author: .izik

entry: When prepared with rice and seaweed, POKENAME make for a hearty and filling meal. Their stomachs look like a single piece of gnocchi and store most of their vital organs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: All POKENAME are known to be appreciaters of great sceneries. If you were to see one in your files, it is a sign that you have great taste. They feast on datas of flowers.
author: blaizegamer

entry: POKENAME appear during meteor showers, dashing across land and sea as if chasing the falling stars. Areas where the meteors fall often have a source of natural spring water nearby, leading some to believe it was left by POKENAME as a blessing.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME soars above meadows and releases powerful electric shocks at threats like Fearow. Its sparks often set nearby petals aglow.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME flies up mountains to feed on starlight. When the sun rises, it rolls down the mountain, ricocheting off trees as it goes.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: POKENAME's appearances in morning action shows have made it popular with children. It strives to keep up the image of a hero of justice as a result.
author: nvisionluminous

entry: POKENAME's poison strengthens after consuming large quantities of lily of the valley. The petals leave a bitter residue on its ears.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME snacks on riverbank flowers for energy. When full, it gathers mud and logs to build a small lodge as shelter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are good-natured, attempting to save weak Pokémon from stronger ones. They often end up in worse condition than the one they try to save.
author: kingd8

entry: POKENAME are large, flightless Bug-Type Pokémon that will swarm together in forests to feed, creating large clearings as they do. Their wings are soft and flexible, fluttered as a means of display rather than being used as a means to fly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME whir their wings in a low-pitched drone to warn away other Pokémon from their feeding grounds. If their warnings fail to deter potential competitors, they will launch a flurry of rapid-fire punches instead.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its wings are covered by a huge, jaw-like carapace that's hard as rock and can clamp down on attackers. In the wild, POKENAME are shy and hide from humans, but might be lured closer by presenting shiny or glittering objects.
author: sontyp

entry: When enraged, POKENAME will grapple foes with its huge arms and hold them out so that its smaller arms pummel them. However, the small arms are so weak that it feels more like getting tickled.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's wings make an incredibly loud noise when they are whirred, the buzz audible from many miles away. They use this sound to warn away other POKENAME, staking their claim to their territory.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME consumes entire patches of peonies to refine its venom. Its fangs drip a faint pink toxin afterward.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fights with its blade and fist simultaneously. In the moonlight, its blade sparkles and makes glowing trails with its swings.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This elusive Pokémon is only spotted during meteor showers when the night sky is filled with Minior. Its dazzling tail mesmerizes anyone who looks at it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME holds a life-long dream of being able to fly to the stars. Its marvelous and destructive power derives from star energy.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME displays great affection toward its Trainer during the early morning. Its black ribbons shimmer in the sunlight as it hovers nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often engage in territorial fights with each other. Their fast-moving fists and powerful wings cause a cloud of dust to shroud the area around these fights.
author: gileme__

entry: At night, POKENAME like to soar high in the sky, drawn to the stars and moon above. Some say they fly so high that they can touch the very moon itself.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Myths say that when the stars align, POKENAME will descend from the stars. According to legend, wherever it lands will be completely purified.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME spits clear webs around its daisy fields. It uses these webs to trap pollen and deter intruding Bug-types.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eyes are extra sensitive to the morning light, enabling them to see across great distances during the early hours of the day. They create wisps of fire that match these wavelengths, allowing them to locate each other with ease in the forest.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME generates fireballs in its fists and hurls them at opponents. The heat scorches flowers around its nesting grounds.
author: .izik

entry: By day, POKENAME collects flower seeds to plant near its dams. Once the number of flowers there satisfies it, POKENAME moves on to a new home.
author: .izik

entry: Some parts of POKENAME's body are covered in an exoskeleton, while others have fish-like scales. It swings its tail so quickly it produces a bug-like buzzing sound.
author: leonian1586

entry: It vents its frustration at being unable to fly by punching trees and any Pokémon that cross its path. As POKENAME is primarily nocturnal, it waits for nightfall to roam in search of ripe fruit to soothe its nerves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME imitates humans wandering in flower fields. Swarms of them using illusions to disguise themselves as flower-pickers have confused travelers for decades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are large, flightless Bug-Type Pokémon that will swarm together in forests to feed, creating large clearings as they do. Their wings are soft and flexible, fluttered as a means of display rather than being used as a means to fly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME disperses potent sleep-inducing pollen from its glowing floral arms. A single breath can render a foe unconscious.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen hopping from tree to tree in search of berries to eat. When it is attacked, it will strike its attacker with its curled-up fists with the same force as a champion-level boxer.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fists grow scalding hot when it strikes. After punching, it escapes by flying in unpredictable S-shaped patterns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live alongside Ledyba colonies, as their leaves are trimmed when Ledyba eat them. If their leaves get too big, they fall over, unable to get up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The liquid excreting from POKENAME's mouth has an otherworldly smell, similar to the scent of Minior. The substance glows faintly in the dark, illuminating new-moon nights.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Using its four arms, POKENAME coats its opponents in lots of sticky slime, immobilizing them to get the advantage. This Pokémon only fights when provoked, though, and is actually peaceful and gentle in nature.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME reside alongside Ledyba colonies, as their common predators have difficulty hunting both of them at the same time. POKENAME use an aromatic mist to put predators to sleep before the colony carries the threat away from their homes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During the day, POKENAME retreats into a shell created by its numerous spiky appendages. It emerges at night to bask in the starlight.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME hovers above flowerbeds, growling at any intruders picking the flowers. If the trespasser attempts to run away, it will closely zip behind it, barking violently.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME howls while flying through meadows under moonlight. Its cry is said to ward off predators lurking near flower beds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sporadically shoot beams of light around them. Ancient legends speculate that each beam of light is triggered by a dying star.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many people and Pokémon find themselves entranced by POKENAME's beautiful song and dance, and it will sometimes choose to perform for others. Even in battle its attacks are highly stylized in form.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME is known to take people living in air-polluted towns. It then brings them to the middle of remote forests, showing them the cosmos.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME uses Agility while tunneling through meadows to rapidly locate flower roots. Once it has eaten its fill, it surfaces and naps peacefully in the sunlight.
author: .izik

entry: On a clear night, POKENAME can be seen running in a straight line, leaving a trail of stardust behind it. It spends the day resting and eating berries.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: On starry nights, POKENAME assemble in fields and practice battling against each other in honorable duels. While two POKENAME fight, any spectacting POKENAME clap and buzz in harmony to cheer them on.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's wings have become incapable of flight after fusion. Instead, it uses them alongside its whiskers to sense the movements of nearby people and Pokémon.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME naps in vast flowerbeds, enjoying the scent of the surrounding flora. If you happen to wake it up, it will go on a seemingly never-ending rampage.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME goes on large rampages, punching everything in sight with its powerful fists. The only thing able to calm it down is the sight of the galaxy.
author: dodoowner_

entry: During dusk, POKENAME runs across the lands, its gaze fixed on the moon. It's said that the Pokémon is attempting to chase the moon itself.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME spend much of the day underwater in safety but emerge after dark to strengthen their limbs on shore. More active on starry nights, they are constantly vigilant for nocturnal predators.
author: afilthycasual

entry: A shiny layer of mucous constantly covers its body that gets brighter the more starlight is absorbed. Trainers swear they can tell what mood their POKENAME is in based on this fluid's scent.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Each punch thrown by POKENAME is equivalent to one thrown by a child. However, its six arms punch faster than the eye can see, making it an effective fighter.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME swarm together to river banks during the morning, sunning themselves to warm up their bodies. Once they are sufficiently warmed up, they spend the day diving in and out of rivers searching for weeds to feed on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lets loose a Razz Berry scent while flying over poppy fields to attract prey like Rattata. Once they approach, it traps them in sticky pollen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's leaves release a citrus-scented nectar that smells like fresh lemon. This aroma attracts Bug-type Pokémon, which it swiftly captures with its vines.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME haunts isolated villages, licking individuals it finds outside. Witnesses report a strange sensation, like thousands of Caterpie are crawling on their skin.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's pincers grow so large that it is unable to fly more than a foot; it uses flight in combat to bring its pincer down on a foe like a hammer. POKENAME prefer to live in environments where they can view the stars and hear ocean waves.
author: laughing_dan

entry: It meticulously maintains its ball of silk. It's very proud of it and always tries to show it to other Pokémon.
author: missingmilkman

entry: When the wind picks up, POKENAME uses its silk to balloon to more lush trees. It only does this in mild breezes where it can maintain control. If the wind is up and a POKENAME is spotted on the ground, a storm may be approaching.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME is skittish around strangers and primarily blends into tall grasses while waiting to shock prey with their electric webs. This webbing can be harvested to produce electrical cables and cording.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME hides in large bushes and tall grasses while waiting for prey to wander into their webbing. This webbing produces small electric shocks they can feel in their nervous system when there is a change in frequencies.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: Each egg in a POKENAME clutch covers itself with silk as an added layer of defense. If any member loses part of their armor, the rest of the group will work to weave a replacement posthaste.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a bit skittish and very quick to go on the offensive. It keeps its bone club connected to its hand via webbing, swinging it around like a whip to beat at potential threats from afar.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's legs and mandible set it apart from other fusions of its kind. They allow it to move around and consume food, unlike its stationary brethren that rely on stored energy to evolve.
author: afilthycasual

entry: After evolution, POKENAME has learned to sleep sitting down with the egg-shaped rock in its pouch in order to prevent theft. Some say it also uses the rock as a weapon.
author: lucasdesouza7

entry: POKENAME ejects silk from each of its vines to trap prey like Rattata. It weaves the threads fast and silently, rarely missing its target.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are extremely vulnerable to attack and tend to remain completely still, only moving when necessary. They utilize their webs to trap and slow any predators who try to take advantage of their stillness.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME weave wings for themselves out of a sticky silk produced from their mandibles. These wings damage easily and regularly need repair, POKENAME typically sheltering with tree canopies to fix them during the day.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's horn never stops growing. It tends to fork and splinter as a result of it rubbing its horn against rocks and trees to keep it at a manageable length. Bug Catchers sometimes collect these as good luck charms.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Many POKENAME live in forests, but some have spread into villages. They can climb on ceilings and crack almost anything with their strong jaws.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is often considered a good choice for first time fusion Trainers due to its happy nature and love for its Trainer. However, this Pokémon tends to get into mischief by creating webs in unwanted places and can be unpredictable.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: After undergoing an aquatic mutation, POKENAME can become invisible in marsh waters. They weave webs into the roots of aquatic trees to ensnare swimming prey and conserve energy.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME is considered a challenge due to the speed at which it produces webs. These webs hold an electric charge that can be used to power electronics; in the wild they are often used to ensnare fast-moving opponents.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME use their mandibles to attach to trees while they wait to evolve, though some tire and fall from their perch. Reintroducing them to a tree will make them grateful, but many altruistic hikers have received a nasty bite.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME leaves its roost within mountain caverns to descend to nearby forests for hunting. It spits out super-heated thread from its mouth that wraps around prey and cooks it within seconds.
author: sk372

entry: This flying Bug Pokémon uses its green feathers to blend in with trees, where they build small nests of web. This web is also said to be used to create traps for unsuspecting Pokémon.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: It regularly coats its webs with juice from Oran Berries to attract its prey. The webs are extremely strong and can stay sticky for months.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME hoard halfway-digested Berries and Pokémon in the place they call home. In addition to its acidic spit, it can also emit a sticky substance that preserves food for later consumption.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are a common nocturnal fusion found in the woodlands of Johto. The pattern on their stomach looks vaguely like a grimacing face, which is thought to scare off potential predators.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME prefers to hunt without getting physically involved. Instead, it ensnares foes in the darkness of night by using both illusions and webs until they tire out before POKENAME snatches them up.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are very clumsy Pokémon. They aren't used to their wings yet, resulting in many hunts ending with them crashing into an object, prey or not.
author: gotfyr

entry: After evolving, POKENAME are more bold in their approach to hunting. They fly at high speeds using their sharp top horns to skewer their prey.
author: gotfyr

entry: POKENAME's abdomen mimics a larger predator to fool potential attackers. This method has proven very effective, since even regular hunters of POKENAME are mostly warded off by its intimidating appearance.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME is highly territorial with sharp eyes and strong claws. It uses its many webs to trap unsuspecting Pokémon, before swooping down to carry away prey and ignore larger trapped opponents.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME secretes a thin silk from its mouth, which it uses to weave intricate webs to slow down the Pokémon chasing it. With a single touch, it can channel electric energy into the web, making it even more effective.
author: fiordaliso
