entry: POKENAME produces a valuable silk thread that it uses to carry berries it has collected. It is said this thread makes a very helpful potion ingredient used to increase the potency of any brew.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: The wool that POKENAME grows over its body is very sticky and tricky to shear off properly. Once removed, it is primarily used for the making of particularly strong fishing nets.
author: sk372

entry: The tail of a POKENAME is made of incredibly soft silk. These Pokémon shed their tails every 3 months, and the discarded silk is sought after by tailors across the world.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME creates webbing from its body that allows it to soar through the air by catching air currents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are occasionally seen in small packs that work together to weave basket-like mechanisms to carry a variety of items. They will collect anything from nuts and berries to lost items from Trainers.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME hang from branches by grabbing onto them with their many legs. They prank other Pokémon by creating nets made out of silk and tossing them onto their victims.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME find the best spot to absorb sunlight between tree branches and make their web there. They spin their web at night so that they can spend most of the day sunbathing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: From the tip of POKENAME's tail it produces a toxic web. This requires a lot of energy, so POKENAME only ever build small webs, though each POKENAME has a unique web pattern, like a human fingerprint, so researchers can easily monitor groups of them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's sensitive fur allows it to predict the slightest changes in the weather. Through utilizing its webbing on opponents and allies alike, it is said to allow them to read minds and intentions.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: This Pokémon is a highly effective hunter at dawn and dusk. POKENAME's bright yellow patterning has a slight glow that is often confused for the rising or setting sun. Their webs blend in with the shadows found in forests.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME spins sticky silk to snatch shiny trinkets from unsuspecting travelers. It decorates its tangled nests with stolen treasures.
author: .izik

entry: The sacs on POKENAME's leaves are filled with a potent poison that can be refined into a chemical for film development. This liquid ensures precise contrast in photographs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fastidiously groom themselves with their mandibles, sometimes spending multiple hours cleaning through their fur. Their mandibles produce webbing, resulting in their fur having an unpleasant rough and sticky texture.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME weave intricate webs laced with odd runes resembling letters. These patterns act as a trap to confuse and lure in prey before POKENAME descend and carry them away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME glides around on its own webbing. It can patch up any damage done to the web in a matter of seconds, even mid-glide!
author: gp423

entry: POKENAME love hugs and offer them to anyone willing to be hugged by their many legs. Whenever someone rejects their hug, they become dejected until another person gives them a hug.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME responds to potential threats or prey by dive-bombing them and spitting webs to incapacitate the target. While not dangerous, this makes it a severe nuisance.
author: linhasxoc

entry: POKENAME are slow moving Pokémon that will puff up and bristle their spikes when they feel threatened. They move inside people's houses over winter when searching out warm shelters. They're dangerous housemates as their spikes drip with poison.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A POKENAME's four pincers can each spew a sticky thread to entangle their opponents. They will pummel their enemies with rapid Bullet Punches, using their threads to pull them back into their strikes if they try to flee.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends most of their days hidden in their shell to avoid predators. Using their sensitive webbing, they are able to detect when prey has been caught, and will only leave their shells to collect their meals.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME spins its webs around the lower areas of forests, catching insects attracted to the honey-like scent its webbing emanates. The threads can be consumed by humans without issue, and have a faintly sweet taste.
author: sk372

entry: The poisonous liquid that makes up its body isn't actually very toxic.  Its real strength comes from the thread it weaves, which is durable enough to hold a boulder suspended in the air.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME make small nets out of silk webs to throw over their prey to ensnare them. Once they are stuck in the webbing, POKENAME wait until their prey tire themselves out, then sink their fangs in.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Young Spinarak weave webs through its antlers. As it bounds through the forest, bugs become caught in the webs and feed the cluster to maturity.
author: missingmilkman

entry: POKENAME uses its tail to artistically spin its webbing into gorgeous art that entrap prey up to the size of Pidgey. Psychics have it weave while a customer describes their dreams, then interprets that person's fortune from POKENAME's design.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are incredibly acrobatic, using webs to swing and maneuver around their opponents. They use these webs to tie their foes up, restraining them for an easy victory.
author: santon5512

entry: Despite the many rumors people spread about POKENAME, they are merely friendly Pokémon that weave replicas of other Pokémon out of silk to give to others as gifts. Alas, most POKENAME are left to wallow in solitude.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its creepy appearance, POKENAME is caring and affectionate. It covers the egg-shaped rock in webs when it sleeps in order to protect it.
author: lucasdesouza7

entry: POKENAME cannot stick to or climb trees due to its legs not supporting its weight properly. Instead, it shoots thin sticky webbing from its mouth at fruits and other snacks to drag them down to it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roll themselves in their own silk webbing like a protective cocoon when they rest within their burrows. They weave their webbing using their multiple arms to entrap foes before biting with their venomous fangs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME do not hunt for food, instead using their webbing to fully utilize photosynthesis. With their webbing as part of their nervous system, they can locate sunny areas by sensing warmth.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME makes its nest among dried lava flows. Its ash-colored webs blend in with the pumice, while being heat resistant enough to allow it to catch Fire-types.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The markings on its head are meant to deter predators, and hide the fact that POKENAME is in fact incredibly timid. Sibling pairs have been seen accidentally frightening each other and running away simultaneously.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spreads thin strands of psychic energy-infused webbing around its home to alert it to any intruders. Trained POKENAME often keep a thread connected to their Trainer so they always know where they are at any given time.
author: sk372

entry: With their exceptional hearing, POKENAME will find the homes of other Bug Types and set up their webs nearby. This invites unwanted competition from intelligent Flying Types that understand what the presence of these webs mean.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME spins webs strong enough to trap a charging Rhyhorn. When many gather together, they weave artistically intricate webs that indicate psychic communication among the swarm.
author: pjporwoll

entry: A family of POKENAME will spin their webs together over or on water to create a leak-proof dam. If any member of the colony is threatened, the whole group will web up the attacker and drag it into their lodge to eat together.
author: pjporwoll

entry: A family of POKENAME will spin their webs together over or on water to create a leak-proof dam. If any member of the colony is threatened, the whole group will web up the attacker and drag it into their lodge to eat together.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME carry their eggs on their back until they hatch, using their physical bulk to protect their delicate passengers from harm. The multiple legs sprouting from its spine are tipped with spinnerets, which they use to weave a nest around the eggs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's webs are coated in a poison that slowly weakens small Pokémon caught in them. They are considered a household pest, but also help keep the home free of other Bug-type Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lives in icy caves, and delicately carves out the ice to look like a web. This is POKENAME's pride, and if anything dares to break it, they pounce on the unsuspecting creature from above, paralysing them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME creates web network systems in caves to sense prey. It wanders the dark ceilings and plunges into them while they struggle in the sticky web.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its violent nature causes it to attack foes even larger than itself. The poison that secretes from its horn is enough to knock out a Vigoroth.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are rather meek Pokémon despite their sharp claws and poisonous mandibles. They use their silk webbings to create webs to hide upon and to create tripwires to alert them to anything that approaches.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME feel a deep love for their Trainer and often show it by weaving bows from their webbing and presenting them as gifts. It is said these bows radiate positive energy and can calm aggressive Pokémon.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: Despite their gargantuan size, their fangs remain small and underdeveloped. They rely on massive web networks to subdue their prey before they sink their fangs in.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon spins its web from the tip of its tail and stores the excess in the balls around it. POKENAME's web-covered hat is very sticky and catches small unsuspecting Pokémon that mistake it for a delicious mushroom.
author: milchik

entry: They can move as fast as electrical bolts. They weave expansive, complex webs by darting about while spitting out their sticky threads.
author: infinex21

entry: It can instantaneously form venomous horns anywhere within its self-enveloping fluid. It expels lasso-like strings of this liquid to capture its prey, controlling the liquid telekinetically.
author: silverscloudy

entry: POKENAME is often found hiding among bushes and trees late at night. They utilize glowing webbing to lure prey into their traps. When properly trained, the thread produced from their webbing can be used to make glowing nets.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME collect keys to include in their webs simply due to enjoying the way they sparkle in the light. Despite their overprotectiveness for the keys they collect, they let this sparkling draw in unsuspecting prey.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: It can lie motionless for years at a time, waiting for prey. When prey finally comes near, sometimes it still doesn't feel like moving.
author: missingmilkman

entry: Electricians prize POKENAME for its electrically charged silk. The threads are used for delicate wiring in unstable power zones.
author: .izik

entry: It floats aimlessly, catching prey in its web. It's theorized that it consumes its victims' souls, then brings them to the afterlife.
author: hiimbasil

entry: When attacked, POKENAME will fire a net of webbing from the top of its head, hopefully immobilizing its opponent. It will even use its web like a parachute to allow it to safely jump down from tall trees.
author: mistymagius

entry: The yellow liquid that envelops itself is its external nervous system. It can freely manipulate the shape of this liquid, though it prefers to form legs.
author: silverscloudy

entry: The horn-like organ on its core glows when it uses its psychic abilities. Its secondary core is in charge of removing any external objects from the special liquid it is surrounded by.
author: silverscloudy

entry: The webbing on its wings does not grow naturally, so it spends most of its time rebuilding its wings with its own silk. The silk is incredibly sticky, which allows POKENAME to carry small berries on its wings.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME secretes highly flammable webs at high velocity from the stinger on its head. It uses this ability to entrap its opponents, then ignites the web with a weak ember.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME fashions itself pom-poms made of its silky, sticky web. It lives in dense forests and stands on the sidelines of battles between larger bugs like Heracross and Pinsir, cheering them on.
author: opossiblymage

entry: Newborn POKENAME rush to gather berries before the rest of their siblings can awaken, as their siblings can number upwards of 100 at a time. They seek out the Kee Berry over all others to ensure they are tough enough to defend their berry stashes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is most active at night. It is difficult to tell if it is asleep, as its eyes remain open and its body remains very still regardless.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wings are wrapped in a sticky silk, allowing it to catch small insects as it flies. The silk is both soft and flexible, making it an excellent material for many different bedding items.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fur is made of thin strands of silk, allowing it to climb any surface with ease. It nests in abandoned buildings, spinning webs large enough to catch a bus.
author: mistymagius

entry: The silk webbing between each of their feathers allows them to catch the air when they spread their wings. Their signature move is a Flying Press that pins their foes down as they bite them with their mandibles and inject their poison into them.
author: infinex21

entry: Its mesmerizing mushrooms are sought after by many people and Pokémon alike. It likes to live in seclusion, hiding under dead leaves and trapping smaller prey with its sticky silk.
author: frokachu

entry: Once POKENAME spins a web, it will become so aggressive that it will even bite its own Trainer should they come too near. These bites contain a venom that, while not fatal, will make the recipient feel weak and sluggish until it is treated.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME weave their webbing into harps to play sweet music that has been rumored to lure in unassuming Pokémon. They are highly elusive, researchers say that they will only appear to dance for those who offer it music it likes.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME's silk is not very good at making webs, so it prefers to make a burrow instead. the hair on its body keeps it body warm and allows for it to hunt during the winter months.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spins webs between pumpkins while it sleeps. If it senses movement, it strikes with Night Shade to protect its haunted patch.
author: .izik

entry: Floating just beneath the water's surface, POKENAME uses webbing as strong as steel to snare prey. Its leafy body shifts colors with the seasons for camouflage.
author: .izik

entry: The webs POKENAME spins glow a variety of radiant colors in the dark. The effect is slightly hypnotic, drawing in insects to become ensnared and become its next meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lines its underground pitfalls with sticky webs. Trapped prey are carefully wrapped and stored for later consumption.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates its intricate web design by attaching its waterproof thread to coral branches. Threads accidentally attached to Corsola often break when the Corsola moves, resulting in the whole web collapsing and exposing POKENAME to predators.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME tunnels are completely filled with webs to aid them in catching food. Each of the three heads monitors the webs for vibration, working together to triangulate the source in hopes of food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME meticulously weave eyes onto their wings to scare potential predators away and intimidate prey. These woven eyes also catch wind currents to give themselves great mobility.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will often spend most days perched, waiting for prey to become ensnared in its slightly golden webbing. However, most cannot resist pouncing after round items, especially if they sparkle.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: The web that comes out of POKENAME's mouth is a remarkably strong adhesive. This has recently started to be used in building projects, as it is far cheaper than cement.
author: turcai_87271

entry: POKENAME produces tenuous strands of silk from its horn. Whenever its silk-producing gland gets clogged, pressure builds up beneath the horn, causing a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The webbing between the flippers of POKENAME allow them to stick to prey. They seal the mouths or gills of their prey to suffocate them and secure their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME were domesticated early in history to produce silk for dresses. These dresses have endured the test of time, as many can be seen in museums today.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clings to a web until it spots suitable prey, then leaps from its perch, using horns and fangs, fists and feet, and even its tail to pummel its target into submission with relentless anger.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its paranoid nature, POKENAME will construct webs to detect and teleport away from intruders. It will forage berries by teleporting to and from nearby bushes.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME's silk is incredibly strong, a single thread being able to withstand up to 10 pounds of force. Survivalists will often use POKENAME silk to make tools and clothing.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its vines are covered in a sticky poison that slowly seeps in through the skin; even mild exposure could result in a bad rash. It frequently hides in ivy waiting to ambush the unwary.
author: afilthycasual

entry: They crawl along beaches at night in search of prey. They seem to enjoy stabbing other Pokémon with the poison barb at the end of their tentacles.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME use their webs to scale and cling to the sides of mountains. They leave their prey dangling over cliffs, saving them for later.
author: santon5512

entry: Webs spun by POKENAME are sturdy and extremely sticky. They make these webs between rocks and other nooks to catch aquatic prey and slow them down enough for POKENAME to catch up and strike.
author: chibitales

entry: Usually quite sluggish, this Pokémon will construct intricate web systems to catch its prey. The only problem is that when something gets caught in it, it's too lazy to move.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: The outer heads obey the third, unaware that it is just a face. Its decision making is flawed and clumsy, yet predators still flee from it.
author: missingmilkman

entry: POKENAME can retract their limbs and head completely within their shell when they sleep, leaving the impression of a long-dead husk and keeping them safe. Their emergence when they wake often scares any arachnophobe that happens to be nearby.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It forgoes hypnotism, instead paralyzing its prey with fear. Young Spinarak live within the shelter of the webs around its neck.
author: missingmilkman

entry: This Pokémon tends to live in abandoned buildings for peace and quiet. POKENAME will spin intricate webs in decrepit door frames to catch prey.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME wields a part of a deceased Ariados as a weapon in combat. It smears poison from glands in its mouth across the weapon, making just a single wound from it inflict a debilitating condition.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spin masks made of web to ward off predators. The spear they hold secretes a toxic poison from its tip, which is able to fell much larger Pokémon.
author: santon5512

entry: Once POKENAME chooses an opponent, it quickly spins a large cage of webbing to act as a boxing ring for the match. Its opponent isn't allowed to escape unless it bests POKENAME in a fight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hangs from tree branches, attached to them with a sticky silk webbing. The webbing dissolves in water, which may cause it to fall onto the ground during a rainy season.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in caves, using their long spindly legs to feel around in the darkness whilst keeping their body safe. They emerge in swarms to find food, nearby residents are advised to avoid breathing in the paralytic wing scales they leave behind.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The tips of their fingers allow them to touch their own silk without it getting stuck to them, which allows them to weave their strands into many different shapes. They often love to create portraits of others made purely of their own silk.
author: infinex21

entry: It endlessly weaves complex silk patterns between its pincers. It feeds on anything that moves, scuttering violently towards its prey on all six legs.
author: missingmilkman

entry: POKENAME spins a myriad of small webs across branches to catch insects in. Once it finds one stuck in its trap, it poisons them with the secretions from its horn before consuming them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME weave a strong web in the shape of a tail that aids them in attracting prey like Shellder. They are sometimes trained by sailors to use their webs to better secure cargo for long voyages.
author: pjporwoll

entry: A POKENAME's fur is actually a fine silk that it has woven around its own body for protection. Due to its natural warmth, many weaker Pokémon are easily tempted to embrace this silk and will become trapped to later serve as a meal for an POKENAME.
author: infinex21

entry: It sheds flakes of its shell in order to grow. The flakes are extremely sticky and dissolve in the rain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are elusive and rarely leave the caves they live in. These same caves are lined with many webs that ensnare plenty of prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use the glow of their purple crystals to lure prey into their strong webs. They will finish them quickly with their venomous Bite attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: While completely harmless to its own kind, the honey in an POKENAME nest is poisonous if ingested. Prolonged consumption can cause blindness.
author: .izik

entry: It produces a thick guava nectar from its mouth and can hold a gallon of the nectar until it drools out. To help with this issue, Trainers dilute and drink this sweet drink while petting its flower petals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This rare variant of POKENAME lost its wings and needles but developed a firm grasp to use needle-like weapons. Its silk is now used to dash and extend its needle. It is highly intelligent and capable of deep thoughts, but still territorial.
author: lutrax

entry: The tips of its feet are extremely sticky. It has the ability to climb up completely vertical surfaces and cling to the ceiling.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has incredible eyesight, necessary for both climbing walls in caves and also hunting while flying. It makes no sound at all while moving.
author: ziggaway

entry: Despite appearances, POKENAME are easily agitated. Many Trainers have needed medical attention after trying to hold wild POKENAME in their hands.
author: gotfyr

entry: This Pokémon can sometimes be observed gazing up at the night sky while holding a peculiar flower. Some believe it is mourning the loss of someone.
author: hypernovahusky

entry: Each POKENAME sees itself as the ultimate super villain. Their evil schemes make them quite the nuisance to both Pokémon and Trainers alike.
author: gotfyr

entry: POKENAME weaves dense, venom-laced webs that paralyze those who get trapped. It moves stealthily among the trees and strikes from behind, sinking its powerful white pincers, protruding from its mouth, into its unsuspecting prey.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its legs can secrete webs, which it uses to form wings. POKENAME forms large webs in which it stores prey, flying at victims that try to escape.
author: maxiundmicky

entry: POKENAME are mostly active at night, crawling through tree branches and constructed webs. When they are dirty, they use their many legs to groom their wings, pulling out twigs, leaves, and parasites that get caught in their feathers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lives deep within the darkest of forests, emitting a faint glow from its lure when prey stumbles near. Those who follow seeking escape from the dark will find themselves soon ensnared in its webs.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its light weight, even the smallest breeze will carry it. It clings tightly to any surface when it sleeps in fear of floating away.
author: .izik

entry: The bloom on POKENAME's head opens in light and closes at night. Being nocturnal, it is rarely seen awake with an open bloom.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME spends hours crafting its webs into sturdy nets. It hunts by swooping down and tangling its prey in the sticky netting before swiftly flying back to its nest.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: It runs in circles during thunderstorms while holding its mouth open to the sky. Once it drinks enough water it will fall asleep in the closest pond.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's are surprisingly docile, only becoming aggressive when they or their friends are threatened by another Pokémon. Their simple mindset makes them annoying to befriend, but they are a powerful companion once befriended.
author: roninthedev

entry: Its nest is made of a mixture of tree bark and a thick red silk. Should it be disturbed while eating, it will scream like a human.
author: .izik

entry: The sacs on POKENAME's leaves are filled with poisonous spiders that are aggressive in nature. Though their bites are not fatal, they are capable of knocking out an adult human.
author: unchatzarb

entry: This Pokémon uses the silk threads it produces to locate and trap prey. It will also gnaw on these threads to file down its ever-growing teeth.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME live together in small colonies, lurking in the treetops. Together, they spin letters out of web, often creating complex sentences of an unknown language in the canopy.
author: santon5512

entry: If struck by a powerful punch, POKENAME spits adhesive silk onto its opponent's fist. It then swings the trapped foe around, slamming them into the ground with incredible force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME perch at the corners between two branches, weaving intricate nets that hang below them. They use their upper legs to run along and shift between different branches, scooping up any prey beneath them and dragging them into their nests.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME burrow holes into the ground with their tails, retreating inside to wait for prey. They set up strings of toxic threads around their den that act as tripwires, alerting them when it's time to pull their fallen prey inside.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME colonies create a vast network of funnel webs deep within forests. The areas they call home are difficult for people to traverse and require specialist gear to avoid getting stuck in the undergrowth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Trained POKENAME are highly valued in construction. They use their wings, webs, and sticky claws to access hard-to-reach locations and perform structural repairs.
author: linhasxoc

entry: POKENAME wanders throughout the forest, constantly releasing sticky silk from its barbs. It later retraces its steps, feasting on small Pokémon caught in its silken trail.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's den is filled with many large webs that both protect its home and catch free food. Before hibernation, it will create a cocoon filled with its prey to consume once spring comes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Bright yellow poison seeps from POKENAME's shell. The yellow color is a warning sign of the poison's potency.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME weaves webs to span between outstretched limbs, weaving them into a tight and light enough structure that they can function as wings. It is clumsy in flight, but can travel long distances between forests.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This aquatic Pokémon captures its prey with precise blasts of sticky webbing from its mouth. The webbing is less sticky underwater, so it shies away from fights against swimming enemies.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME weaves webs to span between outstretched limbs, weaving them into a tight and light enough structure that they can function as wings. It is clumsy in flight, but can travel long distances between forests.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has a pair of legs where antlers would normally grow. This Pokémon will startle itself if these legs accidentally brush any part of its body.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME stay low to the ground during battle, placing down webs to trap their opponents within the arena before they strike. If backed into a corner, POKENAME will rapidly extend webs from their backs to sling away and loop back around for a kick.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME covers the egg-shaped rock in webs, then slings it at the prey's head, causing a painful concussion. After that, it finishes the foe with a horn stab.
author: lucasdesouza7

entry: POKENAME is extremely timid, constantly relocating its nest and never staying in one area for more than a day. Should it be spotted, it spits a web at the observer that is hot enough to melt stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's horn constantly creates thread that becomes a flowing mane over its body. It swings its head around while visiting swampy areas, collecting large amounts of bugs in the web for it to consume later.
author: sk372

entry: The fangs of an POKENAME can be ground up to create various forms of lipstick. This blend is used in Lumiosa City by fashion gurus.
author: .izik

entry: Webs spun in the shape of magic circles are a clear sign that an POKENAME is near. Depending on the shapes spun with these webs, they will be imbued with the powers of different curses that ensure none can pose a threat to this Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: It makes its home in rock formations near the sea. Should any amount of water touch it, the POKENAME will let loose a scared shriek.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nest within caves or the canopies of trees, quietly observing all that cross nearby. They are too fearful of being treated poorly due to their looks to ever show themselves, but they will leave sculptures made of silk for others as gifts.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME utilize a fast-acting nerve agent in their tails to quickly immobilize foes before dragging them to their nests to feed on them.
author: yourfriendlycap

entry: Few insects are as threatening as POKENAME. It hides in abandoned labs and factories, generating magnetism and keeping a look out with its large eyes.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: Despite how large they appear, POKENAME can effortlessly cling to cave ceilings. They will let many of their vines drape to entice and ensnare prey before pulling them within.
author: infinex21

entry: Over time, POKENAME will choose a specific tree in a forest to spin its webs around in particular. Keeping the tree free of pests in this way allows the plant to flourish and grow more vibrantly in the coming months.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is carnivorous and uses venom to soften up prey. Although rare outside mountains or forests, POKENAME can be found anywhere due to its incredible gliding and climbing abilities.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are expert climbers, jumping from tree-to-tree with little effort. Its claws are coated in poison, which it uses to quickly incapacitate its prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME use their tough claws to tunnel through cave walls and to weave their silk webbing into webs. They will lurk upon the ceilings of caves and drop, with their sharp quills aimed down, upon prey.
author: infinex21

entry: It can accurately spray jets of water from up to a mile away. Its eyesight is extremely advanced and able to pick up heat signatures.
author: .izik

entry: Dangerously clever, it will string up its own silk threads around its territory and prance along them; at a glance, most think it to be walking on air. It uses its psychic power to swiftly cast about and control countless threads simultaneously.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are often horribly judged for their appearance. Its said that those who treat them with kindness will be blessed with the most luxurious silk outfits and a loyal companion whose webs will keep all foes at bay.
author: infinex21

entry: Unable to move, its hollow body appears to be held together by spider silk. No one knows where POKENAME comes from or what it does in the wild.
author: ziggaway

entry: Its diet consists of tree roots and leafy herbs. Should it smell a root underground, it will use its sharp claws and fangs to rapidly dig into the soil.
author: .izik

entry: Able to secrete a toxic web from its horn, it shoots it at its foes to rope them in for a follow-up horn attack. While the toxin is relatively weak, it's enough to induce strong migraines and sluggishness for around an hour before wearing off.
author: evilgammon

entry: The web deployed by an POKENAME is made up of a thin and sturdy metal. This web can be broken down and used in the construction of airplane engines.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME binds logs together with its sticky web to create sturdy lodges. The webbing resists water damage, staying intact even when fully submerged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will adopt young Spinarak without a home, carrying them on its back as it lumbers through the forests. It uses a combination of strong silk and powerful vines to gather food for them until they can hunt on their own.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME weave an egg sack on their back that they carry with them at all times until the eggs are ready to hatch. Their young are far smaller than an adult POKENAME but they grow rapidly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME weave funnel webs at the mouths of caves, hiding within the craggy entrance for prey to wander in. Their bite is venomous; in combat they dart forward to deliver a swift bite before retreating and waiting for their poison to work.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Using the decoy on its head as a disguise, it infiltrates Ariados nests and absconds with an armful of eggs. If exposed, it puts on an innocent act.
author: wigglypon

entry: It weaves a complex maze of webs. Pokémon caught in the webs are devoured. Those who reach the end of the maze will meet POKENAME. They, too, are devoured.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spend lots of time maintaining their nests, weaving curtain-like sheets of webbing to block sight into their homes. Many seamstresses study the patterns POKENAME create to inspire their own work.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The green web that comes from its body is slightly luminous. When in complete darkness, its eye lets off an eerie glow.
author: .izik

entry: To conceal its bright body, POKENAME relies on the trunks of large forest trees and their deep shadows. When small birds or Bug Pokémon draw near, it fires a String Shot from the mouth on its stomach, dragging its prey into the hollow.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME occasionally comes up from its dark undersea dwelling to go on land and rest near forests and let Spinarak climb atop it. It then ferries the small spiders off to a new home before returning to the sea.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME create glorious displays of webs that detail the history of the known universe. To ensure nothing damages their works of art, they blind Trainers with a layer of silk webs before luring them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It stores pressurized venom in its horn and can fire it at high speeds. It can hit a stationary target from up to 1 mile away.
author: .izik

entry: In battle, it darts from tree to tree, spitting sticky threads and setting up traps for foes to get stuck in. When it sees an opportunity, it leaps down and pummels the foe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: In battle, it darts from tree to tree, spitting sticky threads and setting up traps for foes to get stuck in. When it sees an opportunity, it leaps down and pummels the foe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The webs POKENAME spin are coated in a debilitating toxin that is absorbed through skin contact. Their spinnerets do not produce this toxin; instead, they use limbs sprouting from their flanks to gather toxins from their spines to add to the silk.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Wild POKENAME spend their time creating intricate webs and traps using their silk webbing when they are not hunting or battling. The horn upon an POKENAME's head is iron-hard and contains a toxin oft used to make potent remedies.
author: infinex21

entry: The retractable claws of their uppermost arms secrete a potent poison that can impair a foe from a deep-enough cut. The silk webbing they spit and weave is as tough as some metals, making it prized by many artisans.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's wings are used to emit sonic waves that stun prey or that scare away predators. Their silk webs are rather keenly attuned to sounds, and many guitarists prefer to use this silk webbing for their strings.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have been studied by both tailors and scientists for their unique method of spinning thread. As their bodies turn and push the web around an axis, their webbing is extruded to keep their designs light and secure.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its fearsome appearance, this Pokémon actually imparts calmness. POKENAME stores tranquility in its horn, with its ribbons acting as antennae.
author: ziggaway

entry: Legends claim POKENAME once towed continents using its indestructible webs. Even now, it creates incredibly strong silk that researchers theorize surpasses any man-made material.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME has a reputation as a vigilante, admired by many and scorned by few. It shoots webs from its hands to swing around and snare its foes.
author: violet_zero

entry: POKENAME flap their wings so quickly that they easily tear when met with a speck of dust. Many weave silky, webbed wings as replacements whenever this occurs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The cloth of its body is made of incredibly strong silk. POKENAME seeks out those that wantonly kill spiders in order to place curses on them.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME expand their own plasma like a large web to intimidate others and to catch, and subsequently fry, small prey. They produce and spit sticky threads that can conduct strong electrical currents without being damaged.
author: infinex21

entry: One of the more aggressive arachnid fusions, POKENAME covers a large area surrounding its home with electrically-charged webbing. It's nearly impossible to traverse through its territory without being shocked or ensnared.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its bright markings to ward off potential predators. It has less tails when younger, and is thus less effective at this tactic.
author: ziggaway

entry: It fires a sticky web from the seafloor to catch boats from below. Once it latches onto a vessel, it will drag it under the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swings from branch to branch with the webs shooting out of its mouth. It can also neutralize prey with this ability.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This clever Pokémon collects smaller bugs in its webs and then keeps them tied up on its body. POKENAME then trades large amounts of them with other Pokémon for larger meals.
author: mistymagius

entry: These Pokémon struggle to stand on their thin legs, often having to use their own webs to give them a perch. Despite this, their multiple legs make for effective weapons that they will rapidly jab their foes with until they submit.
author: infinex21

entry: They rarely use their lower limbs. On their tail tip is a fake third head to prevent ambushes since the two true heads are often busy arguing.
author: chromaerym

entry: It rarely uses its lower limbs. On its tail tip is a fake third head to prevent ambushes, since the two true heads are often busy arguing.
author: chromaerym

entry: Often found only in large caves, these bug Pokémon use their wing-like limbs to grapple and cling to the ceilings and carefully watch all who pass below. They will spew webbing from their three heads to ensnare and drag away their prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are skittish and evasive bug Pokémon that typically lurk within the depths of forests, jungles, or caves. They only emerge at night to forage for berries and nuts, before seemingly disappearing into thin air.
author: infinex21

entry: These highly-intelligent bug Pokémon are able to understand the thoughts of others within a mile radius and can even feel their emotions as well. They are often found in cities and towns watching people and Pokémon alike with ample curiosity.
author: infinex21

entry: It prefers to chew on jungle vines rather than any live prey. It can quickly consume 50 lbs of vines per day.
author: .izik

entry: It frantically chews wood whenever it is anxious. Should an POKENAME become over-stressed, it can level a small forest.
author: .izik

entry: Some researchers believe that the thick hide of POKENAME is actually just shells that contain their true forms. They eat rocks and minerals and will entrap their cavernous homes to protect themselves from intruders.
author: infinex21

entry: The silk that comes from an POKENAME's mouth has the same consistency as silver. Artisans in Wisteria Town melt it down and craft goblets from it.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon typically dwell within the sandy depths of deserts, waiting to churn the sand beneath their prey and drag them into their awaiting maws. They lay tripwires of silk webbing about to alert them when something is approaching them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME flutter their wings both for flight and to loose sonic waves to help them navigate through their desert territories. Their legs are so strong they can latch onto their foes and constrict them until their venom knocks them out.
author: infinex21

entry: It dangles a lure that resembles Spinarak in front of its prey. Once the victim is distracted, POKENAME injects a deadly venom through a bite to the neck.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME feeds on strong negative emotions and stores them in its horn. The stronger the emotions, the stronger the silk it will produce.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME dangles a sweet-scented silk thread from trees to lure Bug-types at night. Its gelatinous body pulses with yellow light in rhythm with its heartbeat as it waits to strike.
author: .izik

entry: Its honey-like gelatinous body emits a sickly sweet scent that lures most Bug Pokémon into its durable webs. Its body throbs and glows with a honey-gold light in tandem with the beating of its two hearts.
author: infinex21

entry: Its body is covered in a sticky, pink web. If dissolved in water, this web can be used as a vitamin supplement.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hairs will irritate unprotected skin. Its venom paralyzes prey in mere seconds.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME live on the underside of tree branches, hidden in the shadows. Hikers that walk trails in the forest are recommended to keep an eye out for them, as any sudden movements that startle POKENAME can cause it to shoot poisoned barbs.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It uses its webbing to ensnare its prey. Once it gathers enough food in its web, it flies it back to its nest to feed its young.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are found in deep underground caves, using their threads to navigate back to their nests. They're considered ideal partners for spelunkers.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME create a slingshot-like web that they use to fire off long-range attacks at opponents. They sometimes end up caught within their own web and require help.
author: camtft

entry: The webs that come from this Pokémon's body are cold to the touch. The lower the temperature of the web, the higher its strength.
author: .izik

entry: It will claim a forest as its own once per year. It swings a clump of poisonous leaves with a thin string of silk to deter predators from its home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body over-produces its poisons and silk, to the point it overflows from various points of its body. This, combined with its potent stench, makes it very difficult for it to socialize with others, making it lonesome.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses silk threads across its body to amplify the ultrasonic waves it emits. It prefers the juiciest, messiest fruits, if it can find them.
author: ziggaway

entry: The webbing of an POKENAME's wings helps them to ride upon wind currents that flow throughout the canyons they make their nests within. They spit and weave more silk webbing to focus or disperse their powerful sonic waves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the markings of its body to disguise itself as a normal Vileplume. Once something flies overhead, it extends its claws to grab its prey and web them up quickly for later consumption.
author: sk372

entry: Its body is filled with a white viscous venom. When it sees something it wants to eat, it vibrates rapidly while drooling.
author: .izik

entry: There are sticky hairs on its palms that allow it to scale large walls with ease. It is active mainly at night, where it searches tall buildings for prey.
author: .izik

entry: The silk webbing of POKENAME is often used to make dream catchers that prevent most nightmares. Strangely, their silk webbing glows at night and eventually turns black when it has been used for too long.
author: infinex21

entry: A less common color variant of POKENAME, but not classified as 'Shiny'. Its spores grow into mushrooms that stay anchored to the earth with sturdy silk strands.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME spins its webbing at a rapid pace, able to completely encase its prey within a couple of seconds. In combat, it will wrap its opponent in a cocoon of silk before slashing them in half with its powerful scythes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Some desolate places call these Pokémon "bells of death," but they are harmless to larger creatures and prey only on insects.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME is so extremely poisonous that nothing will prey on it, meaning it has no natural fear of predators. As a result, it is unusually friendly and inquisitive, and with proper handling, makes an excellent pet.
author: occulusmalus

entry: POKENAME make their webs around lamps and streetlamps. Standing underneath these nests is unwise due to POKENAME's toxic dust and threads.
author: mistymagius

entry: The pumpkin-scented silk POKENAME dispenses from its mouth is similar in consistency to syrup. It is used in many pie recipes due to the sweetness it gains after being heated, making it a secret ingredient in desserts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spins combat armor so it can fight opponents much more powerful than itself. It attaches a silk thread to those it cares about, which it can sense with its spiked crest.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The adhesive threads POKENAME spreads across its pitfalls are incredibly strong. Under the right conditions, they can restrain even a raging Primeape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scuttle through underground tunnels at high speed, leaving a trail of web behind themselves as they do. If they feel threatened, they retreat back through their webs, pulling the strands closed behind them to prevent pursuit.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will often attach a coin to their webbing to lure in unsuspecting prey. However, they can be swayed as prey that deliver shiny objects to them are often spared in exchange for the item.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME produces highly valued silk that's made out of gold. Because of this, it's typically only owned by very wealthy Trainers.
author: novellavaria

entry: Despite its fearsome appearance, POKENAME loves its Trainer and will spend the night sitting on the ceiling above their bed waiting for them to wake up and play. It will sit for hours in complete silence so as not to disturb them.
author: soupalicious

entry: POKENAME can spit an acidic web, which dissolves anything caught in its threads to make it easier for later consumption. A way has been found to neutralize the acid, which allows weavers to spin the threads into fine, near-weightless silk.
author: _pixelar_

entry: This Pokémon's horn slowly releases its latent psychic abilities. It still infrequently gets headaches, and may become aggressive during an episode.
author: ziggaway

entry: Its quick temper and tendency to get violent is already enough of an issue, but POKENAME is even more dangerous due to the purple fists it possesses generating a highly paralytic poison that leaves victims unable to fight back.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its superior sense of smell to track prey. Should an POKENAME be doused in water, it loses any scent it was tracking.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has small barbs on the end of its arms, allowing it to scale any vertical surface with ease. It is quite adept in combat, effortlessly taking hits while jabbing its opponent 10 times a second.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sleep for days on end and hide in the nooks of trees. They only awaken to dine on whatever has been caught in their web.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Each POKENAME's coloration is slightly unique. For some reason, POKENAME try to hide this fact: if two or more are knowingly in the same area, they use their psychic abilities to create an illusion that they are identical, even if they are foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are often seen in pairs in the wild, and struggle to survive if on their own. Sometimes they will get surprised by their companion, causing them to point at each other in confusion.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME mimics a trapped Machoke with its lower body to lure in unsuspecting prey trying to free it.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME weaves webs quickly mid-battle to reel distant foes back into grappling distance. It waves champion belts made of tightly-woven webbing to give to those who give it a suitable challenge.
author: sk372

entry: Occasionally, a thick, green fluid drips from its mouth in the evenings. This acid overflows when it consumes too much protein or sodium in its diet.
author: .izik

entry: They scuttle through forests in search of large prey to devour. POKENAME jump on the heads of strong Pokémon and inject them with a lethal neurotoxin.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME's purple flames will not burn a person, but are toxic and will poison those it does not trust if touched. During POKENAME races, those trailing behind try to spit webs to trip up those ahead of them.
author: sk372

entry: It spins haphazardly-shaped webs to catch prey in, but by the time something is caught in the web, POKENAME has forgotten about the hunt. It usually plays with the caught creature for a few minutes before releasing it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME create nets out of silk webbing to capture prey in the water. They inspire many silk weavers with the complex patterns that can be found in their nets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sticky, toxic webbing POKENAME spins is made of its own sludge, so it shrinks as it spins larger, more intricate webs. Once it ensnares prey, it consumes the victim as well as its own web to regain its lost size.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME weave simple webs that they use to capture air bubbles, taking these air bubbles with them underwater so that they can breathe. They are slow-moving in the water, their shell making their movements cumbersome.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's multiple pointed legs have great strength, letting it cling to cave walls and ceilings with ease. It drops down from these perches to web up Rock-type Pokémon to drain nutrients from them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME treads along the sea floor, picking at small fish and clams to consume. Its large claw is coated with a sticky webbing that ensures once it grabs something, there will be no escaping its grip.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are unable to fly because the bulb restrains the back muscles that are needed to launch into the air. They are capable of gliding for short periods of time if thrown off a ledge.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its mother's skull has fused with its head and wings as armor. With its wings being given extra strength, it can use them as blades to attack.
author: skymaster426

entry: Having gained ultrasensory reflexes, POKENAME continues to seek opponents strong enough to withstand its powerful punches.
author: togetik

entry: POKENAME create noxious fumes to weaken their foes long before they are seen. By the time their prey realize they are inhaling these fumes, they are already too lethargic to escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The giant head of POKENAME is always annoyed and bothered by the other heads. It constantly dreams of when it was its own Pokémon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It spins rapidly, using its wings as blades to slash through obstacles. This spinning flight creates a whirlwind that disorients opponents.
author: .izik

entry: It tracks prey while flying rapidly using its four wings, the lower wings helping it to rapidly adjust its path. When the time is right, it swoops down to grab its prey with its pincers and proceeds to crush them.
author: infinex21

entry: Due to its uneven wings, POKENAME cannot fly. It shambles miserably across the floor in search of leaves to eat, held down by the extra appendages.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: Its wings generate powerful air currents that splash water toward enemies. This tactic keeps opponents at bay while it takes flight again.
author: .izik

entry: Before transforming, it uses sonar to fully assess the abilities of its opponent. This careful observation ensures it becomes an exact and effective copy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is thought to have once been able to both fly and swim very fast. Over time, its shell has grown much larger and heavier, weighing POKENAME down, making it much slower when swimming and unable to fly.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: The fire on POKENAME's back mirrors its temper. When the flames roar, it's about to strike with venomous teeth. One beat of its four wings can sweep its flames onto any target, leaving no escape.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Though POKENAME resembles a predator, they are actually herbivores. Their fire possesses neuro-paralytic properties.
author: mrbapcik

entry: When encountering a wild POKENAME, take great caution, as its amplified toxic power and supersonic speed could leave you incapacitated in mere moments.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: Its four wings allow POKENAME to dive rapidly to snatch small prey with its claws. Both its beak and talons are infused with a deadly toxin, which it uses without hesitation to weaken other Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fly through the night in search of criminals to carry away into the dark. The next day, the criminals reappear outside of police stations and desperately turn themselves in as if in an inebriated stupor, leaving police baffled, but grateful.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: In some places, it is worshipped for its grace and ferocity. From its six wings, it is dubbed "The Seraph of Death".
author: gellyfishsh

entry: POKENAME seem to have accepted their newfound vision, however begrudgingly. They can often be found sulking in dark places, glaring at any light that creeps through.
author: howlingstarr

entry: Flying erratically in the dark, POKENAME cannot avoid ramming into stalagmites and cracking its eggshell armor, which only agitates it more.
author: anonymous_16803

entry: Having its legs evolve to effectively become wings, POKENAME spends much of its time in the water. The wings help it swim just as much as they allow it to fly.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Wild POKENAME gather and hang upside down from the branches of fruit trees. Concealed by their wings, they are often mistaken for Wiki Berries.
author: rihse

entry: The poisonous film on its body is so noxious that any nearby Pokémon will slip into unconsciousness, allowing POKENAME to suck blood at its leisure.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME's inherently carefree nature has diminished its predatory edge. It relies on the remnants left behind by others to satisfy its bloodlust.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The power of affection, love, and loyalty has allowed POKENAME to reach this form. It stalks throughout the night to hunt and gather without making a single sound, then brings whatever it has found to its den to share with whomever it is closest to.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The power of affection, love, and loyalty has allowed POKENAME to reach this form. It stalks throughout the night to hunt and gather without making a single sound, then brings whatever it has found to its den to share with whomever it is closest to.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The power of affection, love, and loyalty has allowed POKENAME to reach this form. It stalks throughout the night to hunt and gather without making a single sound, then brings whatever it has found to its den to share with whomever it is closest to.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The power of affection, love, and loyalty has allowed POKENAME to reach this form. It stalks throughout the night to hunt and gather without making a single sound, then brings whatever it has found to its den to share with whomever it is closest to.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME assumes this form whenever it has absorbed large amounts of energy. This energy can be from the bond between Trainer and Pokémon, the moon, or other unnatural sources. Its appearance brings to mind a phenomenon occurring in a distant region.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The power of affection, love, and loyalty has allowed POKENAME to reach this form. It stalks throughout the night to hunt and gather without making a single sound, then brings whatever it has found to its den to share with whomever it is closest to.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The power of affection, love, and loyalty has allowed POKENAME to reach this form. It stalks throughout the night to hunt and gather without making a single sound, then brings whatever it has found to its den to share with whomever it is closest to.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The heavy bud growing on POKENAME's back keeps it from flying, despite its four wings. POKENAME bites anyone daring to touch its petals with venomous fangs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its powerful teeth can crush through onyx with ease. This unmatched biting force makes it a formidable hunter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME extravagantly wave about their wings as they perform mysterious chants and eerie shrieks to prank wandering travelers. If anyone tries to approach a POKENAME during its mischief, it will disappear in a single flutter of its wings.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Flying backwards, it drills into the ground with unmatched precision. This tactic allows it to carve tunnels and escape from threats.
author: .izik

entry: Using its claws, it carves stone to create intricate statues near its den. These sculptures serve as both decoration and territory markers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often prowls the forests looking for fairy Pokémon to devour. It holds its prey with the tight grip of its metallic pincers before finishing them off with Poison Fang.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Acidic juice from its shell is splashed at enemies, leaving them stunned. This juice doubles as a defensive mechanism and deterrent.
author: .izik

entry: It can carry entire trees through the air for up to 10 miles. This incredible strength allows it to build nests in remote areas high above the ground.
author: .izik

entry: By synthesizing the toxins in its teeth, scientists created a powerful remedy for seasickness. It can fire pressurized water jets so strong and precise they can pierce stone.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will rest atop water after flying for hours. If it gets knocked onto its back, it'll flail until it tires itself out or manages to flip over.
author: ohok3441

entry: Their diet includes luminescent corals. Thanks to this diet, they glow beautifully in the dark.
author: mrbapcik

entry: It uses its massive, wing-shaped ears to leap to incredible heights and then drops like a wheel to bowl over its foes. Its fangs are laced with a potent toxin, which it uses to weaken prey and drive out intruders that dare trespass on its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can blitz through the air while spinning at a rapid pace, making it difficult to stop without risking injury. It frequently gets dizzy after spinning, which Trainers exploit to catch it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By flapping its wings, it generates powerful wind blasts that knock down obstacles. These gusts are strong enough to topple even the toughest opponents.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME induce spellbinding hallucinations that can last for hours and cause delusions. They stalk Trainers who are under the influence of their hallucinations to lead them out of their caves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies swiftly and silently through the night, followed by its Zukrow minions. Should one of its cronies disobey an order, POKENAME will sink its fangs into them and drain them of blood.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's four wings assist with its balance as it dances about in its cavernous home. Its swaying movements have been known to attract Zubat swarms, who watch intently as if hypnotized.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its fins to modulate its magnetic field, giving it extremely precise control over its position and speed.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME are apex predators that hunt other Flying-type Pokémon. They zip past obstacles in their way to sink their venomous fangs into their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's hind legs are so short that it has to drag itself along the ground. If it wants to move faster, its wings will keep it hovering above the ground while its front legs charge forward.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: This small Pokémon glides from tree to tree at night. It stalks prey from high places with its great eyesight.
author: themicelegion

entry: It can fire the spines on its back like missiles, launching them at distant targets. This attack leaves opponents struggling to avoid the sharp barrage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's movements are near silent as it utilizes the quiet wings on its head to maneuver through the caves it calls home. As an ambush predator, POKENAME uses its toxic talons to slash into and pin down its prey until the foe stops moving.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME uses its wings to stir up intense gusts of wind to blow back opponents. The cannon on its arm can launch tornados in the direction it is facing. During combat, POKENAME will jump up, then dive bomb foes with an intense kick.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is a feared predator due to its toxic bite, as even a small graze can leave debilitating effects. It uses its psychic abilities to sense vulnerability in its opponent before striking with blinding speed.
author: mepp.

entry: Scattered logs can be seen on the cavern ground where POKENAME resides. It steals wood from nearby forests, attempting to create dams on the cave ceilings, seemingly never understanding the folly of this endeavor.
author: sk372

entry: It leaps from tall plateaus with grace, gliding through the air effortlessly. Its precision in flight allows it to strike targets with pinpoint accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pollen is a particularly potent respiratory irritant that they spread by flapping their wings. At night, POKENAME roam around the forest releasing clouds of pollen to mark their territory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Their giant jaws open four ways and are dripping with a viscous, toxic saliva. The tongues of these jaws can lash out with enough force to break a rock and secrete a numbing venom from their tips.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's arm strength is great enough that only a single flap is needed to take off from the ground. It glides from region to region, depriving entire forests of their fruits and berries.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's piercing screeches were said to warp minds into worship. Those with bad hearing were immune to this effect.
author: .izik

entry: Ghost-, Poison- and Bug-type Pokémon flock to the withered trees on POKENAME's back, often making small communities together. POKENAME doesn't seem to mind, but does seem to immensely enjoy its rare moments of solitude.
author: sk372

entry: At night, POKENAME crawls out of rocky crevices to take to the skies in pursuit of prey. Due to its small size, it is sometimes targeted as a meal by larger Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME has impressive agility. It darts around and strikes opponents with poison-laced chops and kicks. POKENAME resides deep in the mountains.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flies fastest while in its scabbard, employing four silent wings in total. Its blade consumes blood.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's fangs drip with a corrosive poison that conducts enough electricity in each drop to power a small car. Using its wings to silently glide upon prey and its gleaming eyes to spot even the slightest movement, it is an elite predator.
author: middlec

entry: POKENAME can flap its many ribbons in a mimicry of wings, attaining something close to flight. It seeks out Zubat colonies in the wild, using its ribbons to calm them down and lower their aggression towards travelers.
author: sk372

entry: It lives in dark cave recesses and uses its wings to create wind. It fools cave-dwelling Pokémon into thinking that they are near an exit before it attacks.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME are agile swimmers, their front and hind limbs both used to propel them through the water. Myths surround them as the heralds of storms, speaking of their speed coming from hurricane-whipped oceans.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's four wings give it great control of its aerial movement. It hides itself in dark upper corners of caverns, targeting prey below and taking shots at them with the energy cannon on its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flutters and hops, but never flies, since its bones are too dense. Its face and demeanor are often associated with imps.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME glide silently through the night, rattling their mushroom caps to scatter their spores over their prey. Once their prey is taken out, they extend their arms to carry them away into the darkness of the night.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: This Pokémon is known to be one of the fastest in the world. POKENAME is a silent but speedy predator, as most Pokémon it attacks will never realize who attacked them until it is too late.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon is known to be one of the fastest in the world. POKENAME is a silent but speedy predator, as most Pokémon it attacks will never realize who attacked them until it is too late.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME form colonies inside abandoned manors and hang from the ceiling. They chase after intruders to siphon away the life force from them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME cling to high cave ceilings. When prey walks below, POKENAME will drop down on it, cleaving it in half with its axe-like tusks.
author: kingd8

entry: POKENAME is a fairly slow flier, but due to its four equally sized wings, it can crawl faster than either of its components.
author: hophoppip

entry: Some say this is the fastest flying Pokémon alive. In battle it will fling forth its feathers with lightning speed, the venom-drenched quills being so sharp that they stab like poisoned kunai.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME only travels in the pitch black of night, and only at supersonic speeds. It has been theorized that it cannot travel any slower.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME sticks to walls using a gelatinous coating that is also quite toxic. Despite only having one wing, it uses its psychic abilities to levitate above the ground.
author: mistymagius

entry: It unleashes powerful bursts of noise that confuse and disorient its foes. The intensity of these sonic attacks makes it hard to counter.
author: .izik

entry: It spits acid with sniper-like precision, hitting targets from impressive distances. This corrosive attack makes it a dangerous foe in battle.
author: .izik

entry: It emerges from its cave at night to hunt for nocturnal prey. Its wings form updrafts of turbulent air to knock airborne prey out of the sky.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is an aquatic predator able to attain sudden bursts of speed, able to dart forth and clear multiple yards in a fraction of a second. It can see clearly even in areas where no light shines.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It steals gravestones as a mischievous prank, scattering them in random places. This strange behavior leaves graveyard keepers puzzled.
author: .izik

entry: It nests deep within gorges, where the acoustics amplify its echolocation. These isolated locations provide it with both safety and hunting grounds.
author: .izik

entry: It hides within storm clouds, waiting patiently to strike at the perfect moment. Its sudden ambush leaves prey with no chance to react.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flutters the wing-like antennae on its head to feel the air currents in the caves in inhabits. If its skin dries, it loses its way.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME ventures from its cave as soon as the sun begins to set. However, if it's not humid enough outside, it soon returns to its home.
author: .realthree

entry: When threatened, it lies down and displays the large false face on it's lower back. It then lunges forward, brutally slamming into the enemy.
author: moopse

entry: Though lacking the false face on its back, this Pokémon still instinctively lies down when threatened.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME houses a host of dangerous toxins that it produces through absorbing light. It uses the spiked portions of its body to inject venom into combatants.
author: ohok3441

entry: It feeds on moss to keep its fur glossy and well-maintained. This unique diet also keeps it nimble and ready for flight.
author: .izik

entry: Using swift wingbeats, it knocks Apricorns off trees with remarkable accuracy. This behavior helps it access food and store it for later use.
author: .izik

entry: Each night, POKENAME sings an enchanting melody as it lounges. It's believed that this melody is used to lure in both partners and prey.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME emits piercing screeches to loosen peridot from cave walls. Once the gems fall, it swoops down to consume them immediately.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found in caves, using their stick to create fiery bat-like flames. These flames are multi-purpose, used by POKENAME to both light their way as well as to burn those that disturb them.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are solitary Pokémon and will often fight with each other over territory. If it is disturbed during the day, it will quickly bite its attacker before swiftly flying away, leaving them to deal with its venomous bite.
author: mistymagius

entry: It flies quickly through fields at night, scattering poisonous powder. Should it see that its prey was affected, it will strike immediately.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME zip by in a shadowy blur to surprise prey. Once they close the distance, a burst of flames roasts their prey before venomous fangs sink into the fresh meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs into cave walls using powerful wing beats. Loose boulders are dislodged effortlessly as it clears a path forward.
author: .izik

entry: It is both impressively agile and flexible: it is able to effortlessly bound and rest its body on the slightest indent of rocky cavern walls. It watches over mining spots, waiting to dart downwards and snatch any glittering jewels that may be found.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A fearsome predator, POKENAME ambushes unsuspecting prey. It bites down on its target and swiftly subdues it with a paralyzing poison before carrying it back to its pack.
author: mepp.

entry: A nocturnal predator, POKENAME prefers ambushing unsuspecting prey. It bites down on its target and swiftly subdues it with a paralyzing poison before carrying it back to its pack.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME prefer to live in pitch-dark caverns where light cannot irritate their eyes. Their squishy bodies allow them to harmlessly bounce off obstacles, leaving behind a poisonous ooze.
author: chibitales

entry: Trainers employ POKENAME at vineyards, encouraging them to work out their anger by squishing berries for wine. Many guests get intimidated when they see POKENAME licking red juice from their fists, afraid they're drinking blood from their victims.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's frail wings cannot lift its body. Fortunately, in can easily fly with its telekinetic abilities.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Despite its powerful poison and brutal fighting abilities, POKENAME is surprisingly merciful. After it defeats other Pokémon, it merely sucks some of their blood and leaves them be.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are considered symbols of February celebrations, often regarded as a harbinger of love. There exist conflicting depictions of this, with some saying they spread love through an arrow, while others depict POKENAME biting humans.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly dangerous apex predator. Its bite can inject its prey with a potent toxin that will melt their insides due to the flames hidden within it.
author: edeniteiron

entry: POKENAME use their large wings to both propel through the water and launch into the air. They tuck their wings into their shells to plummet quickly before shrugging off the impact from landing with a laugh.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME envelops prey in the webbing of its tentacles, using the spikes along the arms to drain its quarry. The webbing allows it to glide short distances, so POKENAME climbs high along seaside cliffs to nest and watch for food.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME cling onto cavern walls with one pair of arms while collecting rocks with the other. They melt down rocks with acid to snack on them and then let the remains fall away to form stalagmites below them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With its hard body, it dives into enemies with tremendous force. This aerial assault leaves its opponents battered and off-balance.
author: .izik

entry: Caves that have wild POKENAME are considered dangerous due to POKENAME's ability to camouflage itself against dim ceilings while perched upside-down. It will let go and purposely fall onto a trespasser's head at crushing speeds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It can only fly with the assistance of psychic powers, which lift its heavy body into the air. This strange method allows it to glide at surprising speeds.
author: .izik

entry: It strikes with a sharpened leek, jabbing at enemies in close combat. This unconventional weapon makes it both unpredictable and dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever it needs a snack, POKENAME eats bugs and other critters from cavern walls. It uses its wings to soar above the ground, as other Pokémon nest higher than where its neck reaches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has adapted to echolocate in the water using Supersonic. It is stealthy enough to drain the blood from a Wailord without being noticed.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It retracts its wings into its shell to protect them from any harm. It can fly over its foes without them noticing before slamming them with its body.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's solid shell and four wings give it a strong defense and excellent maneuverability. To attack, it closes its shell and drops down from above to crack its sturdy body on top of its target.
author: sk372

entry: Loyal and vengeful, POKENAME will viciously harass anyone who upsets its friends and allies. It plays mild pranks on those it trusts, but becomes despondent if the prank offends its target.
author: pjporwoll

entry: From outside a child's window, it feeds on dreams without needing to enter the room. This eerie ability leaves its presence unnoticed by those asleep.
author: .izik

entry: Its wings are so sharp they can slice cleanly through marble. This precision makes it a terrifying opponent in flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their wings to row through the water, filling their shell with bubbles to aid in their buoyancy. They are not very fast swimmers, their shell too bulky to be streamlined.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their wings to row through the water, filling their shell with bubbles to aid in their buoyancy. They are not very fast swimmers, their shell too bulky to be streamlined, but they can use their cannons to provide a brief burst of speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flap their wings to aid in leaping around the ground before they take flight. They gather twigs to build protective nests around the bulbs on their backs, but grow frustrated when they fall apart during flight.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: They are not safe from being hunted by other Pidgeotto, and their distinct plumage unfortunately gives them away during the lush spring and summer seasons. As a result, they are most active in autumn.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME seeks out Pidgeotto nests and sleeps among the eggs, blending in perfectly. When it wakes, it uses psychic powers to push out any unhatched eggs and claim the nest as its own.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME propels itself through the sky by expelling puffs of poisonous gas from its beak. It uses its sharp talons to swipe at foes that get too close.
author: .izik

entry: There is a seamstress in Wisteria Town that makes wedding dresses with POKENAME feathers. Their sheen is unmatched in quality.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its vines to ensnare foes before launching a flurry of aggressive pecks. The vines move independently, making escape nearly impossible.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spreads its powerful wings and lets out a deafening roar to defend smaller Pokémon. This intimidating display often causes predators to back away in fear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appoints itself as a guardian of its home forest. It protects Caterpie and Weedle families by swooping down to peck and claw at would-be hunters.
author: sk372
