entry: POKENAME chirps loudly while constructing invisible walls mid-air with its psychic powers. It uses these barriers to create aerial obstacles, confusing predators and opponents alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roost in the roofs of opera houses and can sometimes be heard chirping along to the performances. Some operas have even been written taking this into account, with POKENAME becoming unwitting stars.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME runs at full speed across the prairies where it lives to gain the momentum needed to take flight. It is an incredibly fierce Pokémon that battles rivals and enemies using both its sharp beak and its rock-hard horns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are docile Pokémon that can break through tough fruit by pecking with their venomous beaks. When threatened, they kick up dust to momentarily blind predators while they escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME oozes its way up tall trees to hunt for prey from the canopy. It flaps its wings to send goop-like feathers onto targeted prey, which slows them enough for POKENAME to hunt them down.
author: sk372

entry: Despite the fun colors, Liteblue Mail is the standard for professional correspondence between universities. POKENAME are both fast and careful with letters and packages they deliver, as seen by how often they transport goods between facilities.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stores data from consumed viruses within its tail feathers. It learns from this information, making future feedings more efficient.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggles to use its wings due to being in a cocoon state. Instead, it simply uses String Shot to swing from one tree to another, hoping to eat just enough bug Pokémon to get by and evolve.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: It is no longer able to partake in Little Cup tournaments and may occasionally lash out as a result. Even so, a Bitter Curry to match its angst helps it calm down so it can support others in battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The wings on POKENAME's head allow it soar effortlessly across the sky. It is said that POKENAME will appear in front of people and Pokémon who dream of flight.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME zooms through forests with its loud buzzing wings, too fast for the eye to follow. It dives toward anything that moves, jabbing it with its sharp stingers before retreating.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is a very strong bird Pokémon, its claws are razor sharp. It will whip up a tornado without effort if it feels threatened.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a tiny bird Pokémon that uses the wind to float anywhere it may want to go. Its blue feathers seem to hold an ancient psychic power.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a tiny bird Pokémon that uses the wind to float anywhere it may want to go. It will whip up a gust of wind if it feels endangered.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a tiny bird Pokémon that uses the wind to float anywhere it may want to go. Its bland appearance belies a hidden power that hasn't been seen yet.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a tiny bird Pokémon that uses the wind to float anywhere it may want to go. Its golden tail feathers seem to hold an ancient power.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a tiny bird Pokémon that uses the wind to float anywhere it may want to go. Even though its look is bland, it sparkles brighter than the sun.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: It patrols the rivers where its family group lives from the sky, which it reaches thanks to its powerful wings. Although it is capable of striking from a distance with its water-based attacks, POKENAME prefers close-range combat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME instinctively catches and consumes more prey than its body can handle. However, in an act of kindness, it shares its meals with other Pidgey in the group.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME tirelessly patrols its territory while gliding, keeping an eye out for danger. If it spots a predator, it waves its paws and lets out a sharp cry to warn others.
author: .izik

entry: Before fusion became widespread, POKENAME were mistaken for injured Pidgeotto. Several Trainers had to hurriedly explain to Pokémon Center nurses that they didn't push their Pokémon too far in battle.
author: afilthycasual

entry: At night, POKENAME's psychic powers strengthen, allowing it to glide effortlessly through the air without flapping its wings. It hunts silently, using its keen intellect to track and capture prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies mostly in the morning to harvest pollen, using its hands to gently gather from flowers. After a long day of work, it rests in colorful fields, blending in with the blossoms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nests are held together with sticky silk and are often left in the open to lure in egg-eating predators. Unwary invaders may find themselves stuck and preyed upon in turn.
author: afilthycasual

entry: The golden plumage of POKENAME is highly sought after, as it is said to contain latent power. POKENAME is more reckless than its flock, constantly putting itself in danger.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rapidly flap their head wings when excited or agitated. They are very young, so they are inept at retaining energy. The moment they perch atop anything metal, they release all of their stored electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has a difficult time extricating itself from Ariados webs and can often be found wrapped in silk for days. After finally freeing itself, it doesn't take long before it becomes trapped again.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME detects a past disaster near its nesting site using its psychic abilities, it will immediately relocate. It prefers nesting in areas where the energy feels undisturbed and safe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is one evolution away from perfection in every remarkable talent of the Pidgey line. Unfortunately, its lack of a long, flowing lock of hair gives it a disadvantage at looking intimidating to rivaling Pidgeots.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME releases electricity from its wings as it flies, leaving a faint static charge in the air. Even its loose feathers retain an electric charge when touched, giving a slight shock to those who handle them.
author: .izik

entry: Their flower dresses are made of leaves and dahlia petals, which help them absorb sunlight. Their dresses also offer them a slow descent when they are done flying through the skies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a difficult time grooming their own feathers, so they roll across the ground to give themselves a dust bath. Their beaks are too small to reliably peck at prey, so they rely on the flower on their head to generate nutrients.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies low over watercress gardens, carefully watching the surface for prey like Poliwag. When it spots one, it swiftly snatches it up with its sharp talons.
author: .izik

entry: Its cries are obnoxiously loud. Those who own POKENAME tend to either release them into the wild or evolve them as quickly as possible.
author: vaporvenator

entry: POKENAME awaken at sunrise each day to find the best places to absorb sunlight and ride on gentle gusts of wind to quickly move from one spot to another. They stay put during cloudy days to avoid getting tired.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's feathery wings beat furiously as it zips across ponds and lakes. It skims the water's surface at incredible speeds, snatching up insects in mid-flight.
author: .izik

entry: It is encouraged not to give POKENAME Soda Pop as they can easily get addicted and get cranky if they don't constantly receive cans. There is no known way to get them to break the habit except by evolving them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME often accompany sailors out at sea searching for a quick bite. Some are adopted as they help sailors find wind currents to speed up travel.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies through forests and fields in search of the right tree to make its nest. The bulb on its back is sensitive to humidity and temperature changes, so it competes with other POKENAME to pick the best nesting tree.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although POKENAME appears quite bulky, it can soar through the air with remarkable skill thanks to its powerful wings. While flying, it releases trails of poisonous dust from the majestic flower on its back to weaken its prey or enemies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: While fast in flight, it is very clumsy. It tends to start trouble by crashing into trees, disturbing its inhabitants.
author: vaporvenator

entry: Its thick, colorful head plumage is used for courtship rituals. Female POKENAME search out the male POKENAME with the thickest, most vibrant plumage.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: It uses its keen eyesight to observe its surroundings while exuding a strange aura. Wild tales suggest it can influence others' thoughts with its cryptic presence.
author: jaminmcready

entry: By channeling its psychic power through both of its beaks, POKENAME can emit powerful telekinetic waves. This unique ability allows it to push back foes and manipulate small objects mid-flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fiercely defends its nest by latching onto intruders with its talons. If the foe resists, it will detonate in a blinding explosion, sending debris flying in all directions.
author: .izik

entry: With its thick, sturdy beak, POKENAME digs into mud to uncover roots, which it eats. It will often leave behind small burrows that other Pokémon later inhabit.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME launch themselves from tree branches to swiftly close the distance between themselves and their prey. By slamming their claws down onto their prey, the overwhelming force created can even crack dense shells.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The crest of hair on POKENAME's head gives it a sense of authority among other Spearow. Sometimes, it will exude so much authority that a flock of Spearow might consider POKENAME greater than their leading Fearow.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME uses its strong jaws to snap fruit tree branches, carrying them back to its nest. It stores fruit there to feed and raise its young.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies menacingly around its territory, using its eye-patterned pincers to scare away any potential intruders. It can instantly spot any invader, to which it comes over to bash them repeatedly with its pincers.
author: soup1900

entry: The body shape and feather colors of POKENAME are enough to confuse both sides of its fused cousins. The side that POKENAME falls with depends on which half of its mind is greater, which changes frequently.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME have venomous saliva that they can deliver with a quick peck. They are cowardly Pokémon and flutter backward rapidly whilst they wait for their venom to do its work.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When hunting, POKENAME releases a loud trumpet-like noise from its trunk to startle prey like Caterpie. Once its target is disoriented, it swoops down for a powerful tackle.
author: .izik

entry: Most POKENAME live in cities. They perch along office buildings, beeping and chirping at passersby.
author: .realthree

entry: With powerful wingbeats, POKENAME breaks berry tree limbs and catches the falling fruit with its psychic abilities. It carefully sorts through them, only eating the ripest berries.
author: .izik

entry: While soaring through the air, POKENAME performs somersaults and backflips before delivering powerful strikes. Its wings enhance its mobility, allowing it to dodge and reposition mid-fight.
author: .izik

entry: During thunderstorms, POKENAME raises its talons to the sky to absorb electricity. The static energy charges its body, making its attacks more powerful for a short time.
author: .izik

entry: By flapping its large wings, POKENAME generates powerful gusts of hot wind to scorch its foes. It prefers battling in dry, arid areas where it can intensify the flames with its wind-based attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soar through the skies above dense jungles, their bodies trailing behind them as they fly. Flocks of POKENAME feature heavily in classical mythology for the cultures around their environment.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in rough mountainous terrain that is difficult to traverse on the ground. They cross crags and ravines by coiling up then leaping, spreading their hood and wings wide to glide across the gaps.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flies high enough to be inside the clouds while charging up electricity, and creates a raging lightning storm as a result. Only a few Trainers have ever witnessed a POKENAME do this.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME enjoy traveling long distances while taking in the sights and sounds of the world around them. Sailors often find POKENAME following in their wake, as the sailors lead them towards new places to discover.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When tired of flying, POKENAME will land in residential gardens and stand completely still. Its rigid posture and earthy coloring make it resemble a lawn ornament, fooling both people and Pokémon alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always saves the last berry from a tree to replant it nearby. It uses powerful gusts to shake berries loose from branches, eating its fill before securing future food sources.
author: .izik

entry: It takes great pride in coaching baby Pokémon on how to win Little Cup battles, despite no longer being eligible. After a round of coaching, it eats a plate of Dry Curry before initiating spars between itself and consenting baby Pokémon nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME hunt in the sky, they also nest in the ground. They dislike the rain and prefer dry, sandy areas; they have no trouble seeing even in a sandstorm.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When this Pokémon creates a nest, it considers any area it can see from its home to be its territory. POKENAME will use its talons, beak, and fire attacks to fend off opponents who encroach on its land.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Their wings are strong and fold up tightly as they burrow through the ground, using the momentum to leap and glide. POKENAME have many sharp and rigid feathers along their backs that they can shed and launch at foes or prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME flies around land that it considers its territory to seek out prey. Once this Pokémon spots a target, it will dive from the sky before outstretching its taloned claws and dropkicking the foe. With its fresh catch, it returns to its nest.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Still learning to stay balanced in the air, POKENAME will often teleport if it feels like it's falling. Once on the ground, this Pokémon covers itself in dust to protect against parasites.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The delicate feathers around POKENAME's waist flutter softly when it is reading someone's emotions. If it senses strong negative feelings, it will take flight and circle above them in a calming dance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies along the edges of streams, collecting reeds with its sharp beak. These reeds are woven into the structure of its lodge to help insulate it from the elements.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are adept combatants, using their wings to dart around their opponents and attack from unexpected angles. They strike through a combination of pecks and back swings with the spikes on their paws.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is too heavy to fly, so it uses its wings to defend the flower on its back. It can be seen basking in the sunlight whenever it is not finding food to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When a POKENAME isn't digging for some small, juicy Pokémon, it sits and watches Pidgerino brawls to admire a potential partner. It relies on Pidgerinos to fly up into the trees to get more food for them due to POKENAME's smaller wings.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME can only "fly" by gliding on wind currents with the help of their feathered arms. They can run fast enough that their Headbutt attacks can split a tree in one strike, though the impact of these attacks will typically leave them dazed.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's talons are coated in a debilitating toxin that is delivered through slashes of their fore-talons. Trainers keeping POKENAME are advised to make use of protective gloves when handling them to avoid accidentally poisoning themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME make loud, keening cries to one another that can be heard across large distances. Their nests are often found on mountain cliff faces away from predators; they will peck at anyone that tries to get close.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Large in size but meager in appetite, it is nonetheless crafty. It slashes whole branches off trees, then sweeps away the leaves with its singular wing to find the bug Pokémon hidden within.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME brawls happen in groups of 5 to 10 to decide the leader. The fights are so intense and violent that it attracts any Pidgerina that hears their battle cries and clashing of horns and talons.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's head feathers are as sharp as blades. A single strike from its head can slice clean through iron with terrifying ease.
author: .izik

entry: Soaring around its territory, this Pokémon acts as a defender of weaker Pokémon in the forests it inhabits.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME fight in a frenzy of feathers and claws, fully committing to their battles with their entire bodies. Their aggression makes them dangerous hazards for hikers travelling through their territories.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: During a waning moon, POKENAME's feathers begin to molt. The fallen feathers shimmer faintly under the night sky, leading some to believe they carry mystical properties.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs spiral dances during full moons. Flocks gather in the sky, gliding in eerie synchronized patterns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME curls its warm tails around itself when resting, using them to stay warm on top of cold hilltops. It flutters between trees during the day, leaving behind a soft trail of heat.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are pompous creatures that take fastidious care of their feathers and tails. They become incredibly irate when anything dirties their magnificent body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In the early morning, POKENAME flies to the water's edge and scrapes up clay with its paws. It carefully applies the clay to reinforce its lodge, ensuring it remains sturdy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can read the auras of those nearby, detecting malice with ease. If it senses a threatening presence, its tail feathers glow a brilliant gold before it takes flight to alert its allies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be heard across alpine mountains for many miles, their distinctive and complex songs carrying far through the air. The volume of their songs increases when people draw close to their nests as they love to perform for an audience.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a human berry picker to lure unsuspecting prey. Once they lower their guard, it strikes with a barrage of sharp, relentless pecks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fossils are often mistaken for Archen. In the modern day, POKENAME is one of the most ferocious predators on land and in the sky.
author: ozydamians

entry: Feathers from POKENAME are used in pillows for the wealthy. Their softness is coveted by those who desire a good night's rest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME patrols its vast territory from the sky. They gather in lush forests after it rains to feast on soil.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME hierarchy is based on the length of its feather crest. Because of this status check, the most dominant POKENAME is unable to split or leave behind any of its body to remember feeding spots, as its feathers will shrink with it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME cling to tree branches and loudly sing to one another. When a flock of them groups together, they will harmonise with one another in a beautiful lullaby, often sending listeners to sleep.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have an uncanny ability to mimic any sound they hear, using the ability to fit into communities of other Pokémon. Their ability to do this led to a brief craze where toy companies attempted to create replicas of them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As POKENAME lands, it releases bursts of sparks from its talons to discharge built-up electricity. The resulting crackle can sometimes be mistaken for a thunderclap.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME will patrol their territory daily, their tusks making it all the easier for them to fly swiftly through the air. Anything that dares invade their territories had best beware their deadly Aerial Ace attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: When soaring through the night sky, POKENAME releases tiny embers from the tips of its feathers. This glowing trail creates a mesmerizing sight but can be dangerous in dry areas.
author: .izik

entry: Before eating, POKENAME spits small flames from its beak to cook its food. It has an instinctual sense for perfect roasting temperatures and will never overcook its meals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME silently abduct small bug Pokémon and clench onto their prey with sharp talons. By the time they return to their nest, their prey has exhausted themselves from struggling.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can't fly, but instead, it can flap its many wings to add to its height when it jumps.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is a lot more mobile than it appears. Its light body weight and small size mean a single huge flap of its wings can send it soaring a mile away.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: When POKENAME sees its favorite food, its funky, mind-numbing drool comes out at a rapid pace. The only Trainers who manage to withstand owning a POKENAME tend to feed it a food it doesn't love but still tolerates.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: The cotton covering its wings makes its flight completely silent, so its prey never hears it coming. POKENAME uses the excess cotton to make its nest softer, so it wakes up feeling well-rested every morning.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It tends to forget that it cannot fly so it will sometimes throw itself out of trees in an attempt to take off. Its feathers are incredibly sharp, and it will fight with other POKENAME to see whose feathers are sharper.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is very capricious in its actions. It almost seems as if the mushroom on its back is temporarily gaining control of its locomotor abilities.
author: chorb33

entry: It uses its claws to climb trees and mountainsides alike. Wild POKENAME often throw rocks and sands at Trainers that enter their territory.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME populate steep mountainsides, where they build elaborate nests. Its nests are cleverly constructed with large rocks and logs.
author: schwaus

entry: Sleeping on a pillow filled with POKENAME feathers leaves one well rested and energetic when they wake. Due to POKENAME's rarity, these pillows are often sold for extremely high prices.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME crawls aimlessly through the branches of trees. It seems almost apathetic, as if it is not in control of its senses.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME flaps its wings to blow its powder all over the forest trees and ground. It can then sense places where the powder is disturbed to attack and consume small Pokémon that are affected by it.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: The scales on POKENAME's wings are more like tiny feathers. It mostly eats bug Pokémon, though its claws are too small for grasping prey.
author: robosoup

entry: On full moons, the pond where POKENAME sleeps glows blue. Scientists are baffled, as the water's chemistry remains unchanged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stalks the edges of ponds, waiting for an unsuspecting Magikarp to leap out of the water. It snatches its prey with its sharp talons, then flies off to its nest.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The clay casing on POKENAME's body is remarkably durable. It shields its eyes and feathers from harsh winds and flying debris during storms.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME's body glows orange as it flaps its wings. It flies in figure-eight patterns with its flock, creating brilliant light displays.
author: .izik

entry: Scientists debate if POKENAME is a bird, reptile, dragon, or dinosaur. There is no question, however, that its deadly claws, beak, teeth, and talons are all sharper than steel.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful beak to shatter buried boulders. If its beak damaged, it feeds on tree roots to slowly restore the beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is known to adopt romantic couples within its territory and patrols for their safety. If one of the pair is in danger, it will swiftly come to their rescue, pecking the threat until it retreats.
author: linhasxoc

entry: It is often associated with greed in old myths, the best-known being the tale of a POKENAME flying too close to the sun in pursuit of its shiny light.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME may look like it is searching for prey as it circles the skies, but this is not the truth. It is chasing its tail, and will keep going until it gets dizzy.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are careful when choosing their nests, relying on their sensitive whiskers to detect the prevailing wind currents in the area. They choose spots that are sheltered from strong gusts, often nesting high in the treetops.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's somewhat clear head allows it to see Pokémon hiding inside trees. However, it usually ends up misjudging and gets attacked by something far bigger and more dangerous than it can handle.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME train Pidgey flocks on how to coordinate their attacks to secure meals. Many picnic baskets have been raided thanks to the guidance of POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's air control in combat is outstanding compared to other winged Pokémon. It is able to remain in the air while punching, kicking, and even being upside down.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's flight and fight technique is comparable to Hawlucha, with a focus on air-based combat. It is able to deliver steel-bending blows even without a ground to support its weight.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Specialized Trainers often choose POKENAME to scout for rare Pokémon and materials. Its enhanced sense of smell and far-reaching cry allow it to find anything it's commanded to and call for help up to 10 miles away.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: If anyone dares to ruffle even a single feather, POKENAME flies into a burning rage. Every time it breathes fire from its sturdy beak, its body temperature rises so high that its belly becomes red-hot.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its impressive size is matched only by its cleverness. POKENAME has been observed to drop sharpened stones on prey from above and roast the meat over a fire.
author: ozydamians

entry: When cornered by a dangerous Pokémon, POKENAME will spin its body around rapidly with its wings, making the spiral on its chest appear to spin. Most Pokémon that see it will feel their weight shift to the side without any contact.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME uses its large wings to build momentum before crashing into its enemies. If the battle grows too intense, it teleports to a safe location to recover its strength.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The wings and glistening mustache of POKENAME give it telekinetic powers that allow it to avoid attacks automatically in the air. It has been observed that POKENAME has made Kadabras display an emotion researchers dub as mustache envy.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME trains tirelessly all day to make its muscles increasingly powerful. When it wins a duel, it has the habit of gifting one of its feathers to its opponent, inviting them to improve so they can meet again in future matches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spends several hours doing nothing but sucking up and melting dirt in its mouth, hoping it will consume any buried bug Pokémon in the process. 90% of its diet ends up being just dirt.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME glides through the forests in search of Oran Berries. Their shells give them the bulk to shove past other bird Pokémon, allowing them to pluck the ripest fruits.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With its small wings, POKENAME flies over the rivers it inhabits to make sure no danger threatens itself or its group. The shell covering its back and abdomen sometimes hinders its maneuvers, so it often chooses to swim instead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To show their dominance over one another, POKENAME will try to rip out the feather-like leaves on top of each other's heads. POKENAME with their leaves ripped off are far less likely to find a mate.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's wings are just about strong enough to keep it airborne. Because of this, it is able to drop down onto big rocks to break them open and eat any minerals and bug Pokémon it finds hiding inside.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Before taking flight, it emits sharp cries to inform the rest of its flock and coordinate with them. The more vigorously it flaps its wings, the more the fiery tufts on its head blaze, radiating an intense red glow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Somewhat smarter than normal, POKENAME can see where a bug Pokémon may end up in its reach and prepares to strike for that moment. It usually miscalculates and misses its mark 75% of the time.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME flies low over rivers to survey its surroundings and protect its companions. When its shell makes flying difficult, it relies on its strong swimming abilities instead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME patrols rivers from just above the surface, ever watchful over the companions it guards. When its shell proves too heavy for sustained flight, it takes to the water, where its swimming prowess more than compensates.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME clean themselves by sand bathing to prevent parasites from sticking to them. They spin their shell to disperse sand into the air so that their wings are properly coated.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is the star ingredient in 'Confit de volaille aux poireaux,' a delicacy served aboard the S.S. Anne. Its leek is flame-grilled, and its meat is marinated in a Custap Berry sauce before being perfectly charred.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers merge into its skin to make it furry, warm, and waterproof. This change in its body allows it to dive into cold water to scoop up fish Pokémon, and even rest on top of the water.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: The mud-like paste covering POKENAME's feathers is highly toxic. Despite the heaviness of the sludge, it still manages to fly long distances, leaving behind trails of polluted droplets.
author: .izik

entry: The thick, toxic paste covering POKENAME's body can cause dizziness to anyone within 20 feet. As it flies, it unintentionally scatters small droplets of ooze, leaving a pungent scent in its wake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a lengthy bathing process that includes both sand bathing and immersing their body in water. When they are not cleaning themselves, they chase after Bug-type Pokémon by flying over fallen logs and shooting bursts of water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to its heavy build, POKENAME can fly only at low altitude and for just a few minutes at a time, preferring to move by swimming instead. It frequently battles others of its species for territorial dominance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME flies around town tracking citizens, memorizing their habits. At night, it lands on rooftops and uses its psychic powers to feast on their dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can see clearly up to three kilometers ahead. When in flight, it scans the horizon for shiny materials that it can craft pendulums from.
author: noel5229

entry: Inside the bulb on its back, it stores the energy it needs to make its antennae shine brightly. It lives on the ocean floor, feeding mostly on dead algae.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often finds itself as a lure for fishermen, as its glowing antennae and wriggling body serve as the perfect bait for fishing. Those who survive a few rounds of fishing may end up evolving.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The many antennae sprouting from POKENAME's head simultaneously emit light and psychic energy. This is meant to lure in Pokémon and Trainers alike for no other reason than it enjoys company.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Whether in the water or out, POKENAME guides others to safety with illuminating light. Underwater it uses the bulbs on its cranium, while on land it uses a secretion it covers its bone club with that glows in the dark.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME communicate with each other by touching their glowing electrical bulbs together; when these bulbs touch, they produce bright flashes. Their golden clubs conduct electricity better than most other materials.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefers to avoid fighting and emits bright flashes of light from its two yellow organs to momentarily blind foes while it flees. Using its golden club, it catches lightning bolts to replenish its energy.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are known to be extremely curious. If it's in danger, it'll shoot electrified ink from its mouth.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its dazzling lights captivate both friends and foes, mesmerizing those who watch. This light show serves as both a defense and a way to attract prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fins shimmer and gleam in the dark. Renown for their beauty, aquariums sometimes house and train several POKENAME to act as members of a living lightshow.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It extends its antennae out of the water during thunderstorms. Should it be struck by lightning, it will store the electricity within its body.
author: .izik

entry: The lights on its antennae emit blinding Flashes. This will disorient other Pokémon, giving POKENAME better access to nectar.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Each end of their tentacles can light up. When several POKENAME gather together, they perform some kind of ritualistic dance, twirling and lighting up their tentacles in a very particular fashion. Scientists are unsure of its purpose.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME drifts through the currents, its five electrified arms floating in every direction in search of prey to paralyze and capture.
author: kiwikelly

entry: The lights at the end of POKENAME's hair glow brightly in the dark, illuminating and accentuating its dance moves. Its dance is vaguely hypnotic; viewers are compelled to keep watching until the performance finishes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stomp their hooves to produce flashes of light from their luminous bulbs before charging at an enemy. Their horns channel electricity to help ensure they finish off their foes.
author: infinex21

entry: If it is to be kept in a tank, it is important to make sure an electric filter is not installed. Should it get too close to one, its body will spark.
author: .izik

entry: In the dark, some scuba divers mistake it for a submarine. Before they realize their mistake, they get eaten by POKENAME.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME use their lanterns to dive deep below the water to catch their prey. Some trainers ride them to explore areas too dark for regular divers.
author: huh.7

entry: POKENAME's fur bulbs produce heat and a warm, comforting light. They also regrow fast, so they're often shorn off to make fairy lights and winter holiday decorations.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME works effectively as an antivirus program in cyberspace. Its nose and tail emit a glow that draws in malicious programs, so it can purge them once they draw close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats near the ocean bottom, tethered to the sea floor via a strong thread from its bottom. Attackers are repelled by painfully bright flashes of light from its antennae.
author: sk372

entry: Because it eats so much food, POKENAME is very bouncy. It's so bouncy that children are often found jumping on it like a trampoline.
author: pokebio

entry: This energetic Pokémon lives lakes and swamps. Its body makes a hydrophobic oil that it secretes on its fur.
author: themicelegion

entry: The glowing liquid in POKENAME's stingers is a powerful neurotoxin. It can shoot them out in the water like torpedoes to paralyze its prey.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It secretes a special oil that causes the ends of its tails to burn bright yellow. POKENAME uses its tails as whips to disorient prey.
author: spookoftheoldways

entry: When threatened underwater, POKENAME will use their tails as makeshift fists. Their tails however are squishy, so it commonly bounces off of the opponent.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME are very trusting with other Pokémon and Trainers, nuzzling with them as a greeting. Underwater exploration teams befriend these Pokémon to offer light in the deep ocean.
author: teatedtiten

entry: During the night, the orbs at the end of POKENAME's eyebrows pulse at exactly one-minute intervals. If the orbs begin glowing out of sync, it is a sign that POKENAME is growing ill.
author: sk372

entry: The bright, glowing antennae on POKENAME's head allow them to send signals at long range. POKENAME are a very social Pokémon, and on rainy nights, they can be seen communicating all across the sky.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: POKENAME hides in the ocean depths and uses its luminous antennae to lure unsuspecting prey toward its position. When the victim gets close enough, it lunges forward to strike with its venomous jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's tendrils act like wires, both conducting and absorbing kinetic energy, usually latching onto larger Pokémon.
author: heyo346

entry: Its many dazzling, electric lures attract any deep sea Pokémon that sees it shining in the darkness. It wraps its prey in its gleaming tendrils, paralyzing them with powerful electric charges.
author: cartoonhostage

entry: In eastern regions, spotting this rare POKENAME near the surface is believed to serve as a warning of an incoming natural disaster. In western regions, however, they are seen as a rare and lucky sight that brings promises of good fortune.
author: boggyboat

entry: This Pokémon loves shining its light through thick fog, illuminating the path ahead. Sailors often rely on its glow to guide them through misty waters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often too underdeveloped to properly retain, or discharge, electricity. Their tails have a bulbous organ that helps them store some of their electrical charge, however.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are friendly Pokémon who often provide a guiding light for lost Pokémon and lost Trainers. Those who often traverse dark areas tend to have a POKENAME handy.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often clap their fins together when happy, the yellows of their bodies faintly glowing as well. The eldest POKENAME is the one with the longest antenna and is often well-respected among its own kind.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME generate electric pulses along the side of their head. This has the unfortunate side effect of zapping their brain, so POKENAME become less intelligent and clumsier as they age.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It blinds Pokémon it encounters on the seafloor and flees before a battle can break out. The lunar cycle appears to influence its mood, making it hyperactive during a full moon and nearly lethargic during a new moon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME feels threatened, it makes the petals of the bud on its back glow, blinding nearby enemies. Because of the weight of the bulb it carries, it is forced to swim very slowly underwater.
author: fiordaliso

entry: These sea-dwelling Pokémon are hard to see unless they emit light from their antennae, which they only do to entrance their targets. They seemingly have no need to feed on solid matter, instead gaining energy from the distress of others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is protective of small insects, flashing its light to attract them at night so they will flock to it and remain safe. Anything that tries to hunt the bugs will be zapped by lightning.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is made of highly conductive minerals. It finds its way through deep underwater caves by detecting the magnetic fields of the world.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It expels glowing foam to ward off attackers, creating a dazzling barrier. The foam sticks to anything it touches, making escape difficult.
author: .izik

entry: These aquatic Pokémon often use the luminous bulbs at the end of their tails to play tricks on others. Their most typical trick is to use their lights to misguide others, though they will also temporarily blind them with bright flashes.
author: infinex21

entry: Rival POKENAME fight by flashing the glowing patterns on their torsos at each other until one of them is forced to cover its eyes from the blinding light and admit defeat.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME generate heat from their shells to keep them warm even in the dark depths of the ocean. The process causes any water within their shells to boil, leading to the shells glowing slightly and leaking bubbles through the cracks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lives much deeper than most other Corsola, using its internal electricity to light up the dark depths. Due to the many hydrothermal vents it lives near, it has adapted to withstand the more acidic conditions.
author: mistymagius

entry: It can electrocute prey at short range or shoot jets of water at them at long range. A skilled POKENAME can even electrify its own water projectile.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It glows dimly when sick, signaling to other Pokémon that it needs help. This subtle glow ensures it is never left alone during difficult times.
author: .izik

entry: Pods of POKENAME glide over the sea at night and look like twinkling galaxies from afar. Seeing them is said to be a sign of good luck for sailors.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are often kept by fishermen and hunters, as they excel at catching small game and fish. They can quickly launch their twin tails like harpoons, tasering prey before they even know POKENAME is upon them.
author: kiwikelly

entry: The bulb on a POKENAME's tail glows brighter the more it is shaken. They typically live within small bodies of water and defend themselves with a numbing poison.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME communicates with others of its kind by shooting electrical waves. When lightning storms occur at sea, it floats to the surface, mistaking the lightning for another POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many rubber bath toys have been fashioned in the image of POKENAME. Real POKENAME, however, are digital in nature and tend to glitch out when submerged in water.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME's antlers light up when it senses danger. When this happens, it gallops away with high speed.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME relies on its markings to scare away predators. In reality, it cannot defend itself due to its mouth being too small to bite anything.
author: kiwikelly

entry: The egg that POKENAME carries is full of so much electric energy that it could power a small town for several weeks, if POKENAME didn't defend it so fiercely.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME is said to appear in front of divers lost in the depths of underwater caves and share its air bubbles with them. Survivors say this Pokémon even guided them back to safety.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are often found in bodies of freshwater, their tail bulbs emitting at least a faint glow. They will flee to land to avoid predators and may even discharge their electricity into the water.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spins its tails incredibly fast during battle. This allows it to rapidly generate electricity before striking.
author: .izik

entry: The lights of this Pokémon's antennae have a hypnotic effect on people and many other Pokémon, even at low lumens. It only comes close to the ocean surface at night, as it prefers darkness, leading to eerily calm tides within its territory.
author: infinex21

entry: Their twin tails respectively discharge negative electricity and positive electricity at any threats that have drawn too near. They can tap the tips of their tails together to produce bright flashes of light.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is quiet but extremely friendly, to the point it sometimes gets itself in trouble. It may greet what is actually a dangerous predator in complete earnestness. They especially like to find Remoraid to become close friends with.
author: bobosmith01

entry: With their luminous tail-bulbs, they will misguide lost Pokémon and electrify them to better prey upon them. They will blind strong foes with bright flashes of light and swim away without a trace.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME keeps its babies safe inside the water-filled cavity in its body. Together, they attack prey with up to 15,000 volts of electricity.
author: mistymagius

entry: Wild POKENAME are often found closer to beaches, where they often make little caves within the sand to rest within. They can curl up into a ball with their luminous bulb perfectly centered.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME live in riparian areas. They travel in pairs of opposite electrical charges and will coordinate discharging electricity from their antennas together to shock their foes.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It glides just below the surface of the ocean, camouflaged by its cloak's countershading. When it hears prey, it clamps onto them with its claws and tails, electrocuting them until they stop moving.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: This Pokémon is very dimwitted. The lights on its back are extremely bright. Looking directly at said lights can cause blindness.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME buries itself in sand at the bottom of lakes, leaving only its spikes above ground. When a prey swims by, it shoots its spikes at them.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME hides in mud with only its crest visible. If it is touched, it delivers a shock to ward off predators.
author: lighthouse.keeper.

entry: A POKENAME's antennae light up in the presence of strong emotions; exposure to emotions seems to cause them to generate electricity. If a POKENAME feels threatened enough, it will discharge electrical bolts, although it lacks precision.
author: infinex21

entry: By utilizing psychic powers, POKENAME can move swiftly deep underwater. They generate electricity by moving and in the presence of fervent emotions, with their many yellow bulbs glowing brighter the more electricity they generate and store.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their lower six organs to produce alluring light via electricity to lure in prey, which they will close their lower halves around. They propel themselves with latent psychic powers, allowing them to take captive prey back to their nests.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon is skilled at sensing danger. Its ears discharge electricity and release various horrible toxins, creating a deadly combination.
author: alliveir

entry: The bulb in POKENAME's flower only lights up when its Trainer has a genius idea. Or so the Trainers say, at least.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It uses the poisonous feelers on its limbs to perceive its surroundings. POKENAME communicate using electric signals from their tail and ears.
author: alliveir

entry: POKENAME's antennae contain small amounts of electricity, able to briefly stun those hit by them. It can cause these antennae to flash on and off with a bright light, which it uses for communication or to signal others of its species for help.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME likes to plant itself into the ocean floor, where it blends in with other bioluminescent foliage. It gets agitated if its stalks are grabbed.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's head glows brightly when it is preparing to charge at something. Though soft to the touch, upon impact the bulb releases a powerful electric burst of stored energy.
author: sk372

entry: Its tail emits loud electric signals that act as a beacon. Some have been seen firing high frequency signal beams at their enemies.
author: alliveir

entry: Its lights serve as a beacon for lost sailors, guiding them to safety. It swims tirelessly, ensuring its glow is always visible from afar.
author: .izik

entry: The undulating appendages on POKENAME's body can shine with a light bright enough to light up the deepest trench of the ocean. If it were to use all of its bulbs at once, the flash would likely cause permanent blindness to all who saw it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME communicate with each other using flashing lights emitted from their ears. They generate, store, and release electricity through their singular horn, which also contains a paralytic agent.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's prominent blade is primarily composed of a liquid ectoplasm charged with a small electric current to give it its yellow glow.
author: char_latte3412

entry: They emit bright flashes of light from their ears when startled and may either release an electrical bolt from their horn or attempt to charge forward and stab with their horn. When their tail bulbs are full of electricity, they glow rather brightly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME constricts prey with its luminous tendrils before delivering a deadly shock. It is found inhabiting warm seas.
author: mepp.

entry: Wild POKENAME have a tendency to be drawn toward bright lights, thinking they are the luminous tail bulbs of their own kind. Their yellow spines glow as they prepare to loose a bolt of electricity from their horn.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rests at the seafloor, within the deepest trenches of the ocean. The light from its antennae, even from those depths, is potent enough to be seen from above the water.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's resemblance to Palkia's Origin form has sparked interest from paleontologists. Some have used it to support the theory that Chinchou have been around since ancient times.
author: hophoppip

entry: On new-moon nights, POKENAME emerges from hiding, illuminating the ocean. It dances until the break of dawn.
author: dodoowner_

entry: In the wild, it's only been found within a single seaside cave. The bioluminescent mushrooms that cover its body glow beautifully in the dark.
author: hophoppip

entry: At the end of POKENAME's ribbon is a singular light filled with only negative electricity. As its feelings of hatred grow, its electrical powers build until even its own body becomes overwhelmed and starts to tingle.
author: soup1900

entry: Caves where POKENAME reside are filled with electric webbing. POKENAME soak intruders with Water-type attacks, driving them into the webs and subsequently paralyzing them. The bulbs above its abdomen emit a bright Flash.
author: chibitales

entry: Nocturnal by nature, it glows gently in the darkness, providing faint illumination. It is most active in heavily forested areas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scours the ocean floor for any objects that light up, so it can hang them on its body. It can create an electrical circuit with its body, causing all the objects to light up at once.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME always waves its tails in beautiful patterns that mimic the movement of flames. Astute Trainers can easily tell POKENAME's mood from the speed at which its lures oscillate.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It bobs happily on waves, its glowing body lighting up the water around it. Its playful nature makes it a popular sight among beachgoers.
author: .izik

entry: By vibrating its four wings rapidly, POKENAME generates powerful electric waves to keep other wild Pokémon away. Many are convinced that when it takes flight, a storm is about to arrive.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME charges its head electrically by generating positive and negative energy via its antennae. It loves to give out headbutts.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is not a fast swimmer. However, thanks to its hard shell and its ability to electrify its surroundings, it hardly fears predators.
author: chorb33

entry: The luminous bulb on POKENAME's tail glows in response to its emotions. When enraged, the light intensifies until the tail becomes scorching hot. It lives in large family groups along the coasts of southern seas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep dark ocean, generating so much electricity that its entire body illuminates the dark depths. It stays around hydrothermal vents so it has a constant source of energy.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME resides in dark caves near the ocean. Its vision is weak, so it uses its bioluminescent bulbs to light its way.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME scours the ocean floor for food, eating whatever it can dig up with its tusks. Its body is capable of withstanding immense amounts of pressure.
author: dylonk25

entry: When POKENAME gets excited, sparks jump between its two antennae, causing its temperature to rise. These antennae will flash aggressively when anything encroaches on POKENAME's turf.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Its wings are specially adapted to help it both fly and swim, acting like flippers underwater. Despite its unassuming expression, it is extremely territorial, fending off both birds from the air and fish from the sea.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When skies are gray and there is less sunlight, POKENAME help Trainers with seasonal depression stay happy. By shining their luminous bulbs, POKENAME act like a mood light to brighten their Trainer's day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in caves found near beaches and can be seen hanging upside-down from ceilings. They help lost children escape the caves by shining their bright lures so that children follow them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Old stories claim POKENAME use the pale light of their lures to lead unwary travelers into foggy seaside caves. In truth, they usually use them to lead people out of those same caves.
author: karagar

entry: POKENAME are regularly reported using their antennae. They have been seen using their lights to illuminate paths through the darkest depths of the ocean, while their antennae are poisonous and make anyone who touches them for too long ill.
author: th3randomguy

entry: POKENAME have a soft luminescence that shines through their eyes, so whenever their parents are away, they close their eyes to avoid attracting predators. Once their parents have returned with food, they can safely open their eyes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Groups of POKENAME make mesmerizing light displays deep within the ocean. When a Pokémon draws near, they swarm it until nothing remains.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its teeth glow when it bites, leaving glowing marks on its prey. This unusual trait makes it easy to track once it has attacked.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives among coral reefs, using its appendages to grasp drifting seaweed to eat. Goldeen are commonly seen hiding in POKENAME's crown.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its glowing lures blink in an odd pattern to communicate with others of its kind. Should an enemy get too close, it will let loose an electric shock.
author: .izik

entry: Its venom glows a bright yellow, warning others to stay away. The glow becomes more intense when it feels threatened.
author: .izik

entry: Long ago, its venom was used to brew a potion that cured seasickness. The recipe for this ancient remedy has since been lost to time.
author: .izik

entry: This shy, tough-skinned Pokémon lurks in the deep seas. Its glowing antennae guide it through the darkness as it seeks out kelp to eat.
author: akujules

entry: It lives in dark trenches, using its luminescent mushrooms to illuminate the darkness. It feeds on glowing algae, which allows its mushrooms to glow brightly.
author: mistymagius

entry: Sightings of a city under the water are usually just POKENAME. The thick brine it holds around its arms helps conduct electricity to its lights.
author: .realthree

entry: It can manipulate electricity by dancing. Researchers are studying whether POKENAME's vocalizations affect electrical currents, and how it could be utilized.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: It dwells in the murky depths where it uses bioluminescence to find its way. In these shadowy waters, it blends in effortlessly with its surroundings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's rocky bodies leave them trapped in the deep ocean, making them quite rare. They use the bioluminescent gems on their bodies to blind predators.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's armored body glows brightly in the dark. Its appearance has inspired the aesthetic of a popular laser tag arena.
author: hophoppip

entry: At night, POKENAME tunnels through the seafloor in search of prey. It releases electrical pulses to stun targets before attacking.
author: .izik

entry: Its antennae gems hold opposite electrical charges that shine brilliantly when discharged. These gems are highly coveted, but are rare due to POKENAME's shy nature and deep-sea habitat.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It is said that a couple shocked by the same POKENAME's antennae will share an eternal love. Some coastal towns host festivals where lovers seek its light for good fortune.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME are usually found in tropical areas at the bottom of the ocean. If threatened, one head keeps watch and the others hide in their hole.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Although typically found near the ocean floor, POKENAME is a valuable companion for pearl divers. It uses the flashing bulb on its head to light the diver's way, allowing them to search in deeper waters.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME abate their frequent migraines by staring at the bioluminescent light attached to their head. They often lose track of time because they spend so long staring at the light.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a childlike curiosity that distracts them from their swimming. Sometimes they forget that they have an antenna lure and stare at it for hours.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The lights on POKENAME's chin can be seen from over 15 miles away. It uses them to lure in unsuspecting prey, swiftly trapping them in its whirlpool-like wings and drowning them.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME absorbs energy from the wind, using the power to light up its bulb. If it spots a lost sailor on a dark, stormy night, it will guide the individual back to the shore.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME shine bright in the darkest depths of the ocean. Whenever they open their shells, they lure many other Water-type Pokémon to their demise before slamming shut.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on an ancient method of hunting for prey that involves shining a bright light to lure predators. Once their prey are sufficiently close, a single bite ensures their prey cannot escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are easily spotted in the depths of the ocean thanks to the bioluminescent lure dangling from their body. They can often be found lurking inside sunken ships.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME erratically fly around, often bumping into boats and shorelines due to its poor vision in sunlight. When frustrated, they dive deep underwater where they can see better.
author: frokachu

entry: Slapping their tails seems to help them build up electricity, which sets their bellies aglow. This is often how they often scare away threats, because when their bellies glow bright it reveals many of their internal organs.
author: infinex21

entry: Before it teleports, POKENAME's tail glows bright and releases a blinding flash to help aid it in escaping predators. Faint bits of electricity can be seen coursing over its body after it teleports.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has an electrical organ in its mouth that emits large amounts of light, luring its prey directly into its mouth. POKENAME are commonly used by deep-sea divers as underwater flashlights.
author: mistymagius

entry: It steals oars from rowboats, causing confusion among sailors. The stolen oars are often found stashed in underwater caves.
author: .izik

entry: During storms, it tries to flash its lights in sync with lightning strikes. This habit fascinates researchers, though its purpose remains unknown.
author: .izik

entry: It often hangs out near the shore, not moving much. It hunts prey by dipping its tail underwater and discharging electricity into the surrounding area.
author: mrpimbus

entry: POKENAME were popular Pokémon amongst artists prior to the advent of electrical lighting, the glow of their tails bright enough to illuminate an entire room at night. Some artists still take them as companions, using their smooth shells as a canvas.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The Shellder on POKENAME's tail is a parasite that absorbs POKENAME's neurological signal to power its electric abilities. POKENAME thus rarely ever reacts to anything and relies on its Shellder to defend itself.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Three Pokémon have formed a bond to share electricity with one another, making the whole more powerful. POKENAME sprays streams of electrified water at enemies to paralyze them.
author: cartoonhostage

entry: POKENAME connects its two heads to different objects for bridging and generates electricity. It is often used in industry.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME connects its two heads to different objects for bridging and generates electricity. It is often used in industry.
author: chorb33

entry: While sleeping, it blinks its lights in a rhythmic pattern. This gentle glow attracts smaller Pokémon, which rest beside it.
author: .izik

entry: It dispenses shining pearls from its mouth, leaving them scattered across the ocean floor. These pearls are highly sought after by collectors.
author: .izik

entry: Blinding flashes of light erupt from its body, disorienting enemies. It uses these bursts to confuse predators and make a swift escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs tunnels in underwater caves, eating everything in its path. The crystals it consumes make POKENAME strongly magnetic.
author: kiwikelly

entry: It hates prolonged exposure to sunlight and retreats to shady waters during the day. Its lights glow brighter in the safety of darkness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a bioluminescent Pokémon that can rarely be found on beaches not far from port cities. If its pincers happen to be cut off or damaged, its health begins to decline.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME swim through the deep sea while illuminating the orbs on their backs, drawing in prey to the source of light. Their orbs constantly secrete and bubble with poison, wearing down prey and allowing POKENAME to enjoy their meal.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME curls its tail around coral and flashes its antenna to confuse predators. The disorienting light gives it time to escape.
author: .izik

entry: After cloaking the area in a Smokescreen, POKENAME sends jolts of electricity through the water. This tactic deters predators like Sharpedo.
author: .izik

entry: Bead Mail is given to POKENAME to ferry to submarines or underwater laboratories because it produces a special bubble to prevent the mail from getting wet. Marine biologists rely on this type of mail to receive important correspondence.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As it swims up waterfalls, POKENAME's antenna glows a bright yellow. During the night, schools of POKENAME can light up an entire riverbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its bright head lamp to illuminate forests and fields during the night. By doing this, it can get nectar with little competition from other Pokémon.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME spins through the sea with its star-shaped body. If it collides with a ship's hull, it discharges sparks as a warning before retreating.
author: .izik

entry: Lurking on the ocean floor, POKENAME's lure gives the illusion of a woman drowning or being pulled under. Despite many superstitions, it turns out POKENAME just prefers to stay in the deep dark, and uses their lure to interact peacefully with others.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME's antennae emit a captivating light that attracts unsuspecting prey. Though the light is a beautiful sight, what follows is truly horrific.
author: mykoloth

entry: POKENAME inhabits the darkest ocean depths, where no sunlight arrives, feeding on anything it finds. Its luminous antennae serve to draw innocent Pokémon into its jaws or dazzle them with Flash.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can withstand the pressure of the abyssal zone of the ocean. It uses its bioluminescence to see in the deep ocean.
author: jona_hehe

entry: POKENAME lures in deep-sea prey with its hypnotizing lights and hauntingly beautiful song. When the prey draws close, POKENAME devours it in one bite.
author: kingd8

entry: POKENAME is a cheerful and energetic Pokémon that loves the dark. It is known to play excitedly with the glowing orbs on its head, leaping and tumbling around the moment they flicker to life when it's sufficiently dark.
author: ambrosia04

entry: A POKENAME has a row of shiny dorsal ridges down its back. They glow brightly with electricity, allowing it to see even in the darkest waters.
author: t.i.a.

entry: POKENAME's glowing fur makes it sought after for deep-sea excursions. The flame sac in its body is able to keep it warm even in the chilly depths.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME swims through online forums, releasing bursts of electricity that distort text across open windows. When a large group gathers, it can overload and disable an entire site.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME went extinct because of how bright their shells are. Predators could spot them sleeping in the ocean from a mile away.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME dives into the deep sea to hunt. It cuts through the water at an incredible pace, creating blinding flashes of light with its body that leave fish too stunned to avoid the grip of its snapping jaws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a voracious eater, oftentimes enticed by its own lure to walk forward endlessly.
author: durgerking

entry: POKENAME is a voracious eater, oftentimes enticed by its own lure to walk forward endlessly.
author: durgerking

entry: There have been many a story of Trainers lost in caverns being rescued by POKENAME. Illuminating a path with the orb on its head, it carries them safely to the nearest exit, before leaving in a bright flash of light.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are skilled hunters in both the sea and the skies. They use their luminescent appendage to hunt in deep waters.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are skilled hunters in both the sea and the skies. They use their luminescent appendage to hunt in deep waters.
author: theartemis1

entry: The lights at the end of POKENAME's tail are fueled by its psychic powers, and can change colors at will. It enjoys using this ability to make light shows for friendly underwater denizens.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims to great depths aided by the lamp on its head. Should prey draw near, it forces the surrounding water to boil, cooking its meal almost instantly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its lure to attract unsuspecting Pokémon in the darkest waters. Once they are distracted, it latches on with its jaws faster than they can react.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME release luminescent fluids that instantly evaporate into gaseous ribbons in the air. The colors of the fluid change depending on the mood of the Pokémon. In some regions, people release POKENAME at the end of festivals.
author: wiz0z

entry: The bulb and spots of POKENAME glow a distinct shade of red at night. Common knowledge amongst sailors claims that seeing the glow of POKENAME is a sign of great fortune and smooth sailing in the near future.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME will lure in prey with its fruit-shaped lure. Once its prey is close enough, it will ensnare it with a web woven between its legs.
author: weirdtux

entry: In times of extreme distress, POKENAME's lights flash so brightly they can permanently blind nearby creatures. It rarely uses this ability due to the intense strain it causes on its body.
author: .izik

entry: If you see two faint lights in the darkest depths of the ocean, swim as fast as you can back to the surface before you become POKENAME's next meal!
author: phantom640

entry: Its glowing lures resemble prey, enticing Pokémon much larger than POKENAME. With its sharp teeth, it can even pierce the tough scales of Gyarados.
author: cartoonhostage

entry: Its four bulbs store electricity and glow the more they have stored. The bulbs on a POKENAME's cheeks are how it will primarily release electricity, which it will often do when it has generated too much.
author: infinex21

entry: Bright, yellow lights dancing within ocean depths are often these Pokémon who love to dance in groups at night. Although rare, they may come to the surface and dance together atop rocks jutting out amidst the water.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME enthusiastically dig on beaches, using their whiskers to light up when they tunnel especially deep. Due to their natural brightness, movie studios use them for extra lighting.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME uses the light on its head to draw others closer so it can embrace and stick to them with its many fins. Wailord and occasionally Gyarados have been spotted with a few POKENAME clinging along for a ride.
author: sk372

entry: Groups of POKENAME can be found calmly floating atop small lakes at night. They are sensitive to sunlight, so they are rarely seen during the day.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Before modern boat lamps, POKENAME were used to light the way for small boats in dense fog. Their perceptive eyesight can pick out obstacles from several feet away. This didn't stop some from intentionally damaging boats by not alerting the driver.
author: chibitales

entry: Its many orbs can emit bright light in an instant, allowing it to easily daze most foes. The orbs within its tendrils move in ways that make their lights mesmeric to most. It feeds on fear and anguish but has no apparent desire to cause bodily harm.
author: infinex21

entry: It swims and burrows along the deepest parts of the ocean floor. The orbs on its body create a brilliant light when aggravated or hunting.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME flashes the orbs on its head brightly when frightened, blinding and stunning potential foes. It has a very jumpy personality, so it often ends up flashing those who mean it no ill will.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have been discovered dwelling over 10,000 feet underwater. It attracts prey by flickering its light before devouring them in the blink of an eye.
author: mepp.

entry: It's a nocturnal Pokémon, and it can breathe in water and on land. It gathers hundreds of Berries and shares them with their young.
author: dodoowner_

entry: As POKENAME treads the sea floor, the bulb on its back stimulates the growth of algae, constantly replenishing its food supply. It illuminates its surroundings for miles, blinding potential predators.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME searches tunnels for prey, blinding them by flashing its light before striking. For a long time, merchants have kept one for sailing at night, when it climbs onto the prow and shines its beacon to signal other ships and highlight obstacles.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its antennae shine so brightly that it risks being mistaken for a large vessel when it glides above the ocean waves. POKENAME has a very friendly temperament toward sailors, whom it sometimes accompanies on their sea voyages.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its antennae shine so brightly that it risks being mistaken for a large vessel when it glides above the ocean waves. POKENAME has a very friendly temperament toward sailors, whom it sometimes accompanies on their sea voyages.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its orbs are weak so it can't protect itself. POKENAME relies on Lanbok to help it in battles so it can learn their techniques and become stronger.
author: not_stakings_alt

entry: Despite its rubber bath-toy-like appearance, POKENAME is well known for its use as a coding assistant in rooting out faulty code. However, being near any active computer equipment causes its lure-like appendages to flash rapidly in excitement.
author: beatdoof

entry: According to legends, people started revering underwater herds of POKENAME, seeing their bright lights and connecting them to supernatural incidents on shores. They are very playful and bond quickly to either their herd, or Trainer.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME has very bright orbs on its tail which can fend off predators. You can tell which POKENAME is the alpha depending on the orb size.
author: not_stakings_alt

entry: The quicker its tail fin moves, the brighter the bulb on its head will glow. POKENAME will rub their cheeks to direct their internal electricity to their cheek pouches before discharging said electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: Friction from water currents causes a static charge to build within these Pokémon, the power of which is stored within their many orbs. They harness their electricity to emit bright and alluring lights in order to torment their foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME, a mischievous trickster, confounds foes with cunning tactics in battle, adding an unpredictable edge to its character.
author: soinetwa

entry: POKENAME discharge electricity mainly through the bulbs upon their tails, often swinging them around to deter threats. When they cry out, their cheek pouches often emit bright lights.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live deep in the rainforest, where the illuminated tips of their vines glow like stars in the canopied gloom. They are semiaquatic and can attract and trap prey equally well in the deep brush or the murky rivers.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME lives within a natural containment suit filled with water that keeps its body insulated to prevent accidentally electrocuting others. The water bubble over its head allows it to breathe when not swimming.
author: alestrius

entry: POKENAME uses the energy it gains from photosynthesis to illuminate its antenna. When threatened, it will blind its opponent with an intense burst of light and run away.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME sometimes hangs the orb above its head too low on its face, causing it to blind itself when it releases light. Any cable or wire it travels through while inside cyberspace glows very brightly.
author: soup1900

entry: It has the ability to control the water in the air, which allows it to stay healthy even during relatively dry days. Colorful seeds that can shine in different colors grow over its tail, making it a festive sight regardless of the time of year.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's bulbs can generate high amounts of light and heat. Beneath the water, the bright flashes repel predators, and when it pokes above the water, it launches fireballs at creatures flying by, purely for sport.
author: sk372

entry: Whether curled into a ball, or on two feet, POKENAME seems to try to zip around, as if it feels it's got to go fast.  Unfortunately, its speed is about average for a Pokémon.
author: infranscia

entry: POKENAME is able to easily wrestle prey it has lured in with its light using only its antenna, even if they are larger than it. With its tail fin being bioluminescent, it can create giant, blinding waves with a splash.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's light is able to penetrate mud, making it great at finding lost items left under the sludge. If it sits in mud for long enough, its light-creating bacteria will begin to absorb the mud and cause it to glow as well.
author: soup1900

entry: Even in the deepest and murkiest of waters, POKENAME's light is powerful enough to completely light the area. When danger approaches, it brightens up to alert other Pokémon to safety before using its immense strength to handle the threat itself.
author: soup1900

entry: When a storm approaches, POKENAME brightens up completely to alert all Pokémon able to see its light. However, anyone too close to it will become blinded and dazed. In these cases, POKENAME, no matter its weight, will carry them to safety.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lurks deep in the ocean and makes its home in dark crevices where its lure produces the only light around. Prey Pokémon often mistake its lure for young Chinchou; POKENAME takes advantage of this and strikes at its unsuspecting target.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME trudges the ocean depths as if looking for treasure. Sailors claim this Pokémon is born from the souls of greedy divers who perished searching for lucrative shipwrecks.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME live in the dark depths of the sea. The lights on POKENAME's head are used to attract other Pokémon, which POKENAME will feast on.
author: fairybell16

entry: Often called the 'Lighthouse of the Trenches,' this behemoth Pokémon lives in deep waters. Its glowing orbs guide sea Pokémon and illuminate the ocean depths.
author: lemage22

entry: POKENAME are intelligent underwater Pokémon that drape themselves in the parts of wrecked ships. This has had the effect of strengthening their physiques, especially due to underwater pressure. The bulbs along their bodies can emit blinding lights.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME emits light in a circular pattern around it in search of prey hiding in dark waters. If it stays on the surface for long enough, Wingull will start flying in and build nests on top of it.
author: soup1900

entry: During Pokémon contests, a Trainer may include a Blue Scarf in their aquatic routine, as it matches the color of their scales. The dazzling array of both electricity and their scales provides a beautiful display of light.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Rumor has it that the patterns on its body inspired a famous painting. It sleeps under the sun, as if to recharge its glowing markings.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME lives in flooded caves in icy regions. It claims entire cave complexes as its territory, but also allows other Pokémon to live in them.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME lives in flooded caves in icy regions. It claims entire cave complexes as its territory, but also allows other Pokémon to live in them.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME produces light from its lure while hiding itself using illusions. Prey that get close are stunned by a burst of light and eaten in one gulp.
author: bunkachunka

entry: POKENAME lure aquatic Pokémon towards their feelers with the bright light they emit. They offer hugs to those that approach them.
author: quackquackattack
