entry: POKENAME rests at the bottom of the ocean, where little to no light reaches. If one sees the illumination coming from the multiple orbs along its wings, it is too late to escape from POKENAME's grasp.
author: sk372

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's body glow exceptionally bright. They guide sailors to shore, absorbing some of their life energy upon doing so, but never enough to cause any real harm.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME reside deep underwater, often hiding within small caverns and caves. During a full moon, large groups of POKENAME begin to surface, the lights on their heads making the surface look like an ocean of stars from above.
author: santon5512

entry: The glowing growth aids them in navigating during the nighttime. They utilize their luminescent appendage for hunting.
author: mrbapcik

entry: A formidable predator, POKENAME uses the appendage atop its head to lure prey to the bottom of the ocean. When a Wailmer dives down to the depths, it is usually not seen again.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME rests on ocean floors while feeding on kelp. Its antenna glows faintly, providing just enough light to ward off scavengers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a star due to its bright orbs. Myths say that anyone who beats it can make a wish, but this has never been confirmed.
author: not_stakings_alt

entry: POKENAME floats on the sea's surface while sleeping. Its softly glowing antennae make large pods resemble constellations at night.
author: .izik

entry: They frequently mistake a Prism Scale for a Deep Sea Scale, so whenever they get their hands on a Deep Sea Scale, they hold onto it. They fight over scales, as they feel uncomfortable in their own bodies and want to evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It hides from predators in coral reefs. However, it is also easily distracted, following anything that sparkles or glows.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME spends its life wandering the ocean floor in search of fallen Wailord corpses. When it finds one, it will feed for weeks, zealously defending its meal from all comers.
author: dylonk25

entry: At night, the radius of POKENAME's light can encompass its entire territory. If two of their lights even mildly overlap, a blinding, merciless war will ensue between them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lives in dense swamps. When the sun has set, it comes out of the water and emits light from its antennae to communicate with other POKENAME.
author: mepp.

entry: Do not be fooled by POKENAME's comical appearance, for it belies a conniving undersea hunter. It stuns prey with painfully bright flashes from its lure, leaving them helpless to avoid its razor-sharp teeth.
author: sk372

entry: Merrily swimming through kelp forests, POKENAME provide bright light from their orb-shaped organs. They make great partners for divers and swimmers, especially those that enjoy a midnight dip in the ocean.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME ingrain their lower halves along the seabed near other plants and lure prey with patterns of lights using their yellow, bulbous organs. When prey comes near, they will grab them with their claws and electrocute them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME likes to lurk in swamps and wait for prey to approach. It lifts up the orb on its back to draw the prey in, where it can spit mucus at it.
author: not_stakings_alt

entry: The fusion of Lanturn and Necrozma allows POKENAME to act as its own food source. It has never been witnessed eating or drinking.
author: nur1

entry: POKENAME use their bioluminescent orbs to lure other Pokémon in dark ocean depths. Their thorns can latch on to their prey, glowing brighter in the process.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's luminous antenna stores glowing venom. If it detects a threat, it redirects the fluid to its spikes for defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flashes its antennae to stun prey like Magikarp. Once disoriented, it finishes them off with a precise Psyshock attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can illuminate dark paths with bioluminescent spores to ensure their Trainer can see where they are going. This is particularly helpful in forested areas, as POKENAME need spores to harness this ability.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME is a fierce combatant, it spends most of its time meditating inside sunken ships or dark caverns. It illuminates the orbs on its head during meditation, warning other Pokémon not to disturb its focus.
author: pjporwoll

entry: While POKENAME is a fierce combatant, it spends most of its time meditating inside sunken ships or dark caverns. It illuminates the orbs on its head during meditation, warning other Pokémon not to disturb its focus.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME silk can be used as net material. Fishermen love to have this Pokémon stick around, in case they run out of netting.
author: dodoowner_

entry: While sleeping beneath the seafloor, POKENAME leaves its glowing antennae exposed. If prey approaches, it discharges a sudden and powerful shock.
author: .izik

entry: Those who stare at POKENAME's glowing antenna are overcome with feelings of first love. The memory vanishes as soon as they look away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses all three of its lanterns while digging to illuminate their path and increase visibility. In unison, their lights are bright enough to be seen from above ground as a faint glow moving underground.
author: sk372

entry: The catabolism of foodstuffs in POKENAME's stomach is so intense that it produces a glow that permeates its body. If its light dims, Trainers are urgently advised to take it to a Pokémon Center.
author: anonymous_16803

entry: By emitting a bright Flash from their lure, POKENAME blind and disorient prey before pouncing. POKENAME rivals hunting too close together may end up dazing each other if they both use this ability.
author: chibitales

entry: Mesmerized by their own lure, POKENAME spend hours staring at the bulb of light in front of their faces. They shoot bolts of light when interrupted.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have lures on the back of their head that draw curious Pokémon to investigate. They are difficult for other Pokémon to keep up with, especially when they are capable of swimming up to 60 miles an hour, or nearly 100 kilometers an hour.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lure prey towards themselves with the glow of the lure before piercing with their electrified tusks. They were once hunted for these tusks, but after a ban on poaching, they are now no longer endangered.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in the darkest depths of the ocean, waving their bright lures to draw in unsuspecting Water-type Pokémon. Once their prey is close enough, POKENAME slam shut to ensure their struggling prey does not escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Rather than for any type of hunting, POKENAME uses the light-emitting organ on its head solely to defend itself. Blinding flashes or paralyzing jolts of electricity are the typical way to stun others so it can swim away.
author: sk372

entry: Although they look intimidating, most POKENAME are trained as service Pokémon. They can act as a guide for the visually impaired or communicate for their Trainer. They can illuminate the bulbs on their head, which can be translated using Morse code.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME lives deep underwater, illuminating trash with its psychic powers to attract its prey. Once near, it paralyzes its prey with over 800 volts of electricity before consuming it.
author: mepp.

entry: It's not uncommon to see a POKENAME work with local lifeguards, especially during the stormy seasons. They often help find people lost at sea during the night.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: After POKENAME uproots itself, it only has a few hours to plant its feet again before its glowing lights dim and go out.
author: .realthree

entry: The more a POKENAME resembles a plant, the better it can hide from predators. At night, its light helps Pokémon find their way.
author: .realthree

entry: Hiding away in the darkness, POKENAME deploys a lure from its mouth that resembles a friendly Lanturn. By the time prey realizes the Lanturn is fake, it is too late to escape becoming POKENAME's meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wiggle their glowing tentacle lures to draw in prey, before hardening the lures into barbs that inject poison. They then spit out a caustic acid, which digests food it touches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's body will glow and flash with its change in mood. The orbs on the tentacles are lit up to confuse prey and enemies alike.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME experience rhapsodic glee whenever they run alongside beaches. Their mane produces a vibrant glow that many artists try to replicate in paintings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME create resplendent arrays of light as they run along the beach at night. The faster they run, the brighter their glowing lights become.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Spending hours on the deep seafloor, POKENAME will stare at their own glowing lure. If disturbed, they become angry and shoot small shockwaves to the source of interruption.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses its natural light to hunt in the deepest waters. It hides in its shell when threatened, but the glow from within often gives it away.
author: delexious

entry: POKENAME can be found at beaches with lighthouses, as they are drawn in by the light. This is because their bulbous lure absorbs light from other bright sources.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spits electrically charged pearls that glow yellow for hours. These pearls are sometimes collected by divers for use in lanterns.
author: .izik

entry: Many Pokémon are attracted to the light POKENAME gives off. Unfortunately, POKENAME is single-minded in creating underwater tunnels, so collapsing rocks sometimes strike other wild Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME exudes bright light than can be seen for kilometers. It accompanies Trainers on long voyages to provide light and hypnosis at night.
author: noel5229

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's back releases a soft, energizing glow when charged with electricity. It produces small seeds that only sprout during thunderstorms.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As it runs, it will generate small amounts of electricity. If it sees a fruit in a tree, it will use the electricity to drop it to the ground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generates electricity as it rolls, building a charge with each movement. However, its poor control often causes accidental discharges, startling itself in the process.
author: moga6

entry: The tiny bones these Pokémon wield are believed to have come from another Electric-type Pokémon, though this has yet to be verified. Without this bone, POKENAME struggle to control their own electricity and become despondent.
author: infinex21

entry: Its electrical capability is strong, but its body lacks the strength to properly contain it. As such, its body has shattered, loosely connected to and covering its electrical core while puffing out small storm clouds.
author: sk372

entry: It periodically shudders in its sleep, letting loose a burst of sparks. Due to this, POKENAME must avoid sleeping near others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggles to effectively retain its stored power and, as a result, swims with a weak electric barrier surrounding it at all times.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME shares electricity with others by creating electrical arcs between its horns. Schools of POKENAME swim to the surface during thunderstorms to draw in lightning strikes.
author: mistymagius

entry: It generates static electricity through small muscle movements inside its shell. This can be used to defend from predators as well as communicate with other POKENAME.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Although many kinds of Pokémon dwell in the forests that POKENAME resides in, it generally goes out of its way to avoid any kind of confrontation while gathering nectar, likely due to its inability to properly control its electric powers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is inept at retaining electricity and often releases it into the surrounding water. It is advised to steer clear of it while swimming.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: While POKENAME's miming techniques are skilled, it still occasionally loses control of its electricity. Instead of placing up a Barrier, its hands may wind up discharging electricity in front of it instead, causing issues.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME are surprised, they release all of the electricity built up in their body, electrocuting themselves and those swimming around them. Thankfully, the shock is nothing more than a mild zap due to their underdeveloped electric sacs.
author: chibitales

entry: The small electric currents in POKENAME react to its strong sense of smell. When threatened, it can release both electricity and poison, though it struggles with self-control.
author: moga6

entry: It is adaptable, making it unpredictable in battle. Every small bolt of electricity released strengthens its bond with its Trainer, helping POKENAME control its energy and shape its future evolution.
author: moga6

entry: It stays motionless, storing electrical energy within its body. Over time, the energy intensifies, causing its shell to glow with a faint electric charge, which can be released accidentally or intentionally.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME may accidentally release a jolt of electricity while eating. It may have trouble sleeping sometimes, as POKENAME might leak electricity while resting, waking itself up startled.
author: mbavenger64

entry: When on the offensive, POKENAME puts everything it has into its attacks. Unfortunately, this means it often hurts itself with overwhelming electricity, or it may leak its poison everywhere before actually hitting the opponent.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although it is incredibly powerful, POKENAME has trouble handling its powers. POKENAME often releases large shocks of energy from its cheek sacs, making it extremely dangerous to be around.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: When POKENAME absorbs electricity, it must release it quickly. These bolts of electricity are known to cause strange emotions and molecular changes in many living things.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME is playful, friendly and even a bit mischievous. It lacks complete control over its vast capabilities, so at times it may accidentally discharge psychic energy, typically resulting in inadvertently levitating objects near it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are herbivores and eat vegetables, fruits, and berries. When they stumble into campgrounds, they are particularly fond of stealing Mixed Mushrooms, as they are not endemic to where they live.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME show their excitement by dancing around and rhythmically snapping their jaws together. If anything gets caught between their teeth, they will instinctively clamp down and release electricity.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME struggles to fly when overcharged. It releases static from its feathers while it's on the ground before rising to the skies.
author: .izik

entry: It jumps over tall grass to keep watch. Each bounce makes a zap sound.
author: fouguri

entry: POKENAME is inept at retaining electricity. It hopes to intimidate its predators by looking like a bee.
author: fouguri

entry: As it sleeps, POKENAME rocks back and forth, causing its feathers to emit tiny sparks. These gentle discharges illuminate its surroundings with a faint, flickering glow.
author: .izik

entry: The static electricity in POKENAME charges the fluid it secretes, making it mildly shocking. It uses this to communicate but may accidentally shock its friends.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME doesn't know whether to help the Pokémon it sees in trouble or hide and watch. It enjoys playing with its peers, releasing sparks and hitting each other while flying. When it gets scared, it releases an electric shock from its cheeks.
author: drack8786

entry: POKENAME are still young and can't control their electricity. They spend most of their time on Electrowebs that absorb their stray Thunder Shocks.
author: codewolfie

entry: A few obscure records from Johto's distant past describe creatures similar to POKENAME. Research is being done to determine if POKENAME once looked like this in the past, or if the records are of a now-extinct relative.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME like to cuddle and rub their cheeks against others to show affection. If they nuzzle with other Electric-type Pokémon, a big amount of static electricity builds up; anyone who touches them in this state receives a nasty, but harmless, shock.
author: _pixelar_

entry: It's the Hero of Oblivia's charming partner! It electrifies its ukulele to create music that calms upset Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: On nights where the moon shines bright, many POKENAME will dance around in a ring near clear lakes. Their erratic electrical discharges become calm during this time, as they will form a circuit by joining hands.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's bouncy body stores electricity. It sings continuously to help control its energy, and the more it sings, the brighter its body becomes.
author: moga6

entry: It builds up static electricity in its fur while it sings. Since it is not yet skilled at storing electricity, POKENAME is prone to accidental electrical discharge when especially focused on its musical performances.
author: abiapollo

entry: POKENAME latches onto its foe with sharp fangs before unleashing a powerful Thunder Shock. This surprising tactic allows it to escape from larger predators.
author: .izik

entry: They will often discharge small electrical sparks while they stand still to absorb sunlight. They love to roll around in water, the marks on their cheeks glowing as they do so.
author: infinex21

entry: On days when the sun shines brightly, pairs of POKENAME will gleefully dance hand-in-hand, spreading a weak electric current through the grass.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: The gills on POKENAME's face crackle with electricity. Before entering water, it usually dips them in to discharge the buildup. When too excited, it forgets, resulting in a sharp crack as it's blasted backward, left dazed but completely unharmed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME can be found at police academies training to become fledgling detectives. They practice collecting evidence and helping people solve crimes alongside officers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A wild POKENAME has a bulb on its back that is said to produce enough electricity to power a house when it blooms. These bulbs almost never bloom, however, taking years to store enough electricity.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: Spoiled and petulant, POKENAME will inevitably throw tantrums if it doesn't get its way. It screeches and flaps its wings, sending out electric sparks all around it until it calms down.
author: sk372

entry: At the slightest sign of danger, POKENAME quickly retreats into its tough, rocky shell. Touching POKENAME while it is in this defensive posture will result in a very mild electric shock.
author: fancyskunk

entry: According to Unovan legend, a scientist transformed himself into a POKENAME. Trainers from other regions often find references to this legend tiresome and overdone.
author: fancyskunk

entry: According to Unovan legend, a scientist transformed himself into a POKENAME. Trainers from other regions often find references to this legend tiresome and overdone.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME have poor control over their internal temperature. They are prone to inadvertently releasing bursts of fire from their shells, startling them and causing them to also electrocute those nearby in surprise.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The fire and electric energy of POKENAME are unstable, but with training, it grows into a loyal companion with sharp instincts and impressive teamwork.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME sinks its fangs into prey to discharge the constant electricity it produces, as it has a difficult time stopping its own production of energy. The numbness left from the bite allows venom to spread quickly without resistance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sparks uncontrollably when within 10 feet of a device infected with malware. These shocks are strong enough to injure even itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels its electric energy during intense training. If it skips a day, its sparks grow erratic and it may discharge electricity uncontrollably.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME's electrical powers are weak, so it has trouble delivering shocks from afar. It prefers to run up its opponent and give them an electrifying smooch.
author: hophoppip

entry: This energetic Pokémon struggles to store electricity, often releasing it by accident. When this happens, POKENAME spins its arms rapidly to stabilize and recharge its lost energy.
author: moga6

entry: Once it begins to release electricity, it cannot stop. To reaccumulate electricity, it uses its strong body to tightly coil around transformers or power cables.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME store electricity in a special band around their stomach and release these that energy through the top of their head. They are easily frightened by other Pokémon and need constant reassurance that they are doing well.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It mimics the movements of others while building up static energy in its body. If startled during its act, POKENAME releases a sudden electric spark that surprises its audience.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME stores electricity in the round pebble it carries, which helps focus its charge. Accidental shocks are still common when it gets excited.
author: moga6

entry: When a POKENAME gets too excited, it releases shocks of electricity from its tail. It also does this when it feels threatened, so it is best to approach with caution while catching one.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: Though POKENAME has better control over its electricity than Pichu, it still has not fully mastered it. Accidental electrical bursts can still occur, but fortunately the discharges no longer harm POKENAME itself.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME is capable of storing enough electricity to power a city; however, it struggles to contain it. When startled, POKENAME can release large jolts of energy, enough to stun small children.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: POKENAME are still learning to generate electricity and often burp out sparks after a warm meal. If they are fed a Rowap Berry, they produce a static charge around their body that is painful to touch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has difficulty retaining its electricity. While swimming, it will often release a burst of electricity that's then conducted by the water.
author: melodydelune

entry: When digging, POKENAME regularly emits weak flashes to briefly illuminate its surroundings so that it does not lose its bearings.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME produces small ice crystals that are charged with large amounts of electricity. However, the ice isn't very conductive, so the stored electricity ends up sparking everywhere.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon's downy feathers are always fuzzy and sticking out from all the constant static electricity leaking out. It bursts out with little fireballs when startled.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: When digging, POKENAME regularly emits weak flashes to briefly illuminate its surroundings so that it does not lose its bearings.
author: chorb33

entry: When digging, POKENAME regularly emits weak flashes to briefly illuminate its surroundings so that it does not lose its bearings.
author: chorb33

entry: When digging, POKENAME regularly emits weak flashes to briefly illuminate its surroundings so that it does not lose its bearings.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can sense people's energy levels. If it's low, it may give them a shock to put more pep in their step.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME stores electricity within its body, but heightened emotions cause sudden surges. When in fear that its Trainer is in danger, it discharges violent bursts of electricity that are capable of felling trees.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are naturally shy and avoid combat. They are generally weak, but have incredible hearing and have sharp barbs hidden under their fur. Anyone injected by the poison leaking from their barbs will develop a painful rash.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME use small electric shocks to stimulate plant growth in their local environment, using the resulting shrubs as building material for dams. Where large populations are present the soil has a slight negative charge and can cause static shocks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite its fiery devotion to looking fierce, POKENAME is still inept at controlling the muscles in its jaw, therefore they are often found in packs helping each other learn.
author: poppyisconfused

entry: Male POKENAME generally protect female POKENAME in times of crisis. If they cannot flee or hide from a predator, all POKENAME in the den will try to release all of their stored electricity and toxins in a last-ditch effort to keep themselves safe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is small and nimble in the air, but being poked by its blade is no major threat. The electricity it produces is like a static shock.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME valiantly tries to stab opponents with its blade. However, because the blade is rather dull, it just does a strong poke instead.
author: soup1900

entry: To intimidate foes and dissuade them from coming closer, POKENAME stomps on the ground over and over. It is found in peaceful grasslands with others of its kind.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The ends of POKENAME's ribbons crackle softly when it is excited. Those nearby may accidentally receive a brief, mild shock.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are terrible at storing and releasing electricity from their cheeks, so they often use their claws to get their food instead. POKENAME are quite ferocious, especially with their quite unnerving appearance.
author: slothboy1028_94690

entry: POKENAME resides high up in the sky, near the ozone layer. It descends during stormy weather to soak up the electricity within the storm clouds, its body crackling with energy as it weaves through them.
author: sk372

entry: The six tails of POKENAME spark with electricity and give off comforting heat. When focused, it creates floating fire and electric orbs, though their unpredictability often surprises it.
author: moga6

entry: Due to its small size and inexperience, POKENAME struggles to maintain its composure. When startled, it ejects its inner organs, which delivers a nasty shock if touched.
author: glacierwing

entry: POKENAME is the result of a Mimikyu possessing a Pichu. While it seems unpleasant to Pichu, being possesed actually helps it control its electricity.
author: adoster

entry: Its electricity connects to its aura, which allows POKENAME to share its emotions. In moments of distress, the aura flares, releasing unstable energy that can shock those nearby.
author: moga6

entry: Extremely timid, POKENAME makes its home in hollowed logs, avoiding danger at all costs. If discovered, it releases a sudden bright spark to disorient its predator before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME instinctively channels electricity through its tail, but its lack of control sometimes results in shocking itself. It quickly shakes off the jolt and continues playing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is always seeking companionship and new friends, nuzzling up against other fish as it swims. It unfortunately cannot control its electricity well, so it often accidentally shocks others this way and cause them to avoid it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates electricity by spinning its body parts. It stores the energy to power its movements, but sometimes releases it when startled.
author: moga6

entry: It hides behind illusions, mimicking people or Pokémon to protect itself. However, its lack of control can cause its illusions to falter and lead to accidental discharges when it becomes too excited or startled.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME has a difficult time managing its powers and easily gets tired after shooting sparks or breathing out embers. The flame on its tail dims whenever it gets tired, so Trainers tend to keep snacks ready to help keep it active.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using static electricity, POKENAME clusters together in large masses. When the energy discharges, the swarm is scattered, leaving each POKENAME at the mercy of even the slightest wind.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME attempts to ambush its prey before paralyzing them with its electrified jaws. However, due to how wild its electricity is, it often gives away its location before it can strike.
author: mistymagius

entry: Due to its large ears, POKENAME struggles to fly. The rapid flapping of its wings produces small amounts of static electricity that stimulate its muscles.
author: mudkip0433

entry: POKENAME can be found crawling within wall cavities of buildings, where it chews on electrical wiring and absorbs charges from small devices. When discovered, it will unleash a pitiable cry that lowers the defenses of even the hardest heart.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME charges its feathers with electricity as it performs to prepare its attack. A misstep can send an accidental shock flying in every direction.
author: moga6

entry: The dreamy dance of POKENAME charges the air around it with static electricity. It is said that those who watch its performance too closely may feel a faint, shocking touch.
author: moga6

entry: Born from discarded electronics and waste, POKENAME constantly leaks small electric shocks. Its trash-like body emits a faint smell, though it does no harm unless provoked.
author: moga6

entry: The Pichu in POKENAME's center appears to control the body's movements. It hasn't fully mastered its strength, so sometimes it discharges far more electricity with an attack than it means to.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its cute appearance, POKENAME are typically handled by professionals due to its lack of control of both its strength and electrical powers.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME rubs its charged scales together to generate electricity. However, if it generates too much energy, the scales will start to vibrate uncontrollably.
author: mistymagius

entry: This timid Pokémon is easily intimidated by large opponents. It uses electric shocks to stun said foes long enough for it to make a hasty escape.
author: fireblade141

entry: Magneton and Nosepass tend to gather around POKENAME. It stores electricity in the Thunder Stones embedded in its body.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME struggle to develop a static charge on their own, so they rub against other furry Pokémon to develop a static charge. This charge causes their sensitive fur to stand on end.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have sensitive hairs across their body that stand on end whenever they develop a static charge. Their fur returns to normal when they discharge electricity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sugary, floss-like fur of POKENAME is both soft and sweet, shedding as it ages. If eaten, it delivers a small static shock, tingling the tongue with electricity.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its fluffy appearance, POKENAME is not safe to touch, as its body cannot yet control the electricity coursing through it.
author: chaotic_aspergers

entry: POKENAME gnaws on underground power cables to absorb electricity. This habit frequently causes unexpected power outages.
author: .izik

entry: The three heads of POKENAME are always squabbling with one another since they constantly shock each other with their uncontrollable electricity.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoy play fighting but often get too excited and paralyze weaker Pokémon. Against tougher playmates, POKENAME may end up paralyzing itself.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME are highly curious and playful by nature, always happy to see new faces and places. They can't store too much electricity in their body at any given time, so they run around and send sparks flying whenever excited or angry.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's energy is infectious. Not only does its cheering inspire the people and Pokémon around it to work harder, but the electricity produced for its electric pom-poms can be used to recharge electrical devices.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME sees that its friends are having a hard time, it cheers them on, no matter what the challenge is. If possible, it will also use its electrical powers to help.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are forgetful creatures that need reinforcement to properly learn a lesson. Whenever they use their psychic powers, offering them a Leppa Berry can help Trainers reinforce the powers with positive emotions.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It bites small prey and injects them with venom. POKENAME cannot digest its own venom, and constantly has stomach aches.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME love to tease other Pokémon and are known to swim up to their friends to deliver a small zap. Their mischief usually begins and ends at a single shock, as they can only produce a few watts of electricity at a time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Static electricity is built up in POKENAME's fur as it fights. It has not yet mastered how to control this electric charge.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME often go on desultory quests to find a particular berry or a friend, only to forget what they were doing. Whenever they are lost, they shoot fiery sparks into the air in the hopes that their Trainer finds them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are novice fighters that rely on their fists to win battles. Whenever they lose, they release sparks as they enter into a temper tantrum.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to its underdeveloped electric powers, POKENAME often shocks itself while trying to use them. However, its hard shell keeps it protected.
author: killerrene64

entry: POKENAME stores the energy generated during thunderstorms in its shell. It is still developing the ability to control electricity, causing it to discharge when overwhelmed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It often forgets why it started sparking, accidentally releasing electricity while daydreaming. Its relaxed nature makes POKENAME approachable, but its sudden shocks can catch others off guard.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME struggles to retain its electricity, causing accidental bursts of power that charge its magnetic body. The stronger the charge, the more metallic objects it attracts, often becoming stuck to its sides.
author: moga6

entry: It wields a plant stalk to help pulverize berries and crack open nuts, though it can also use it as a weapon. Its stalk is charred because it often releases electricity accidentally.
author: infinex21

entry: Its two heads habitually argue over food and over which will remain awake for the night. If the beaks of its two heads touch, electricity discharges and zaps them both.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's Light Ball helps it store electricity and prevent unwanted shocks. Its amiable personality makes it a great beginner Pokémon.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME have a piece of the moon embedded in their back that glows. The intensity of the glow waxes and wanes with the phases of the moon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although they can eat a variety of natural and processed foods, POKENAME seems to be most energetic under the full moon. It is thought they get most of their power from the moon's rays.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The interior of POKENAME's sphere defies geometric principles: It's larger on the inside than it is on the outside.
author: .realthree

entry: Several POKENAME will stay close together as a circle of Clefairy, Butterfree and their fusions protect them. At night, their protectors will dance together and sing to POKENAME, which seems to help speed up the evolution process.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It consumes gravel to aid in digestion, grinding it down within its tough body. This diet also contributes to the hardening of its rocky exterior.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings glitter with the captured light of stars. Some believe that POKENAME came from space, its sparkling wings acting as camouflage.
author: .realthree

entry: Since POKENAME's voices aren't fully developed yet, their songs are very irritating. They will use their voices to their advantage by creating an annoying noise to deter predators.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME school together under the full moon and will jump out of the water to try and bathe themselves in moonlight. Why they do this is unclear, but legends say that if a POKENAME can jump to the moon it will undergo an incredible transformation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If a group of POKENAME infests a system, exposing it to direct moonlight will force them out. Even brief illumination causes them to spring free from the hardware.
author: .izik

entry: According to local rumors, POKENAME are often seen in places where some moon pieces have fallen. It won't hesitate to bite anything that awakens it.
author: ._term.

entry: During the day it is always tired, as it spends the night flying upward trying in vain to reach the moon with its small wings. POKENAME lives in large groups where each member cares for the others.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It steals hats from passing travelers to line its nest. The more elaborate the hat, the greater its value in this Pokémon's growing collection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rarely travels alone, surrounding itself with others of its kind until they resemble a floating flower. The sight of such a swarm is believed to bring good fortune.
author: vracken

entry: POKENAME is sensitive to electromagnetic changes in the atmosphere. If an aurora is visible in the night sky, POKENAME are especially prone to accidental electric shocks.
author: linhasxoc

entry: POKENAME becomes incredibly shy during a full moon, hiding behind objects or other Pokémon. Its songs on those nights are barely above a whisper, yet they still carry a sleep-inducing effect.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to bounce around at night, and will find others to do it with. It can roll around for miles and not get tired.
author: captainjefejefe

entry: POKENAME has a very exploratory nature, using the evening breeze to carry it to parts unknown to explore. When traveling in groups, POKENAME link hands and perform aerial dances together.
author: sk372

entry: While travelers sleep, it sneaks in to gnaw off and steal their shoelaces to build its nest. This peculiar habit leaves many waking up in confusion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love playing in the moonlight, but tend to get tired after a few minutes. If one finds a Moon Stone, it will show it off to others and toss it around.
author: frokachu

entry: During the day, POKENAME waters crops using a mixture of water and a nutrient-rich gel. At night, it rests in the freshly watered fields to absorb moonlight and ease its tired body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's fur grows indefinitely without proper care, often leading to severe matting. In the wild it relies on its family to manage its coat, while domesticated POKENAME require frequent trips to the groomer.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's necklace appears to be made of lunar stone, making it highly valuable. Would-be poachers should beware, however, as it also allows it to channel moonlight into powerful beams of energy to defend itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have been said to gather on moonlit nights. Rumour has it these gatherings have inspired poems about interplanetary creatures.
author: fixthewifi

entry: It digs in spiral patterns, creating intricate burrows beneath the earth. These twisting paths serve as both a home and a defense, confusing potential intruders.
author: .izik

entry: It shreds tree bark to build comfortable bedding, creating soft nests. This habit ensures it always has a cozy place to rest, no matter where it travels.
author: .izik

entry: Many wild POKENAME gather together on the night of the full moon bringing Sitrus Berries to eat. They feast until they're full and then sing until they rest at daybreak.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME glow pink in strong moonlight, and will move a bit faster than normal. Due to only being active near volcanoes on clear nights, this Pokémon is not often seen.
author: frokachu

entry: Strong scents bother it, causing it to avoid flowers or fragrant foods. It prefers areas with neutral smells, making it quite particular about its environment.
author: .izik

entry: It sleeps curled up inside hollow tree trunks, seeking warmth and safety. Its small size allows it to squeeze into spaces other Pokémon avoid.
author: .izik

entry: It collects fossils, breaking them free from cave walls with its small fists. These treasures are proudly displayed in its nest as a sign of strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME constantly grooms the pink puff of fur on its head. It refuses to leave its nest if even a single strand is out of place.
author: .izik

entry: When groups of POKENAME gather under the full moon's light, sparks fly in the vicinity. The color of each spark varies from POKENAME to POKENAME, so their displays can be just as mesmerizing as they are dangerous.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It consumes fallen leaves to fuel the flame within its belly, keeping it warm. The more leaves it finds, the hotter its flame becomes.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME is struck while gazing at the moon, it retaliates with incredible force. Legends say that if it is attacked during a full moon, the counterattack will place a curse upon the aggressor's family.
author: .izik

entry: It mimics the behavior of plants, standing still to avoid threats. Rain frightens it, and it seeks cover whenever storm clouds gather.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME watches a dance routine under a full moon, it can perfectly mimic it after a single viewing. Once learned, it will remember and be able to perform the dance forever.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eat many sorts of berries throughout the day but keep Maranga Berries in a pile away from the other berries. On nights of the full moon, they each take a Maranga Berry and eat them to gain a slight boost to their mental acuity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies through starry nights protected by a flying saucer. If it spots an interesting object, it uses a tractor beam to pick it up.
author: chorb33

entry: As a prank, it steals tools from construction sites, causing chaos among workers. These antics often leave construction crews baffled.
author: .izik

entry: Unfit for the wild, POKENAME lacks any self-preservation instincts. Without a caretaker, it would continue smiling sweetly as it slowly starves.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Oblivious to its large stature, POKENAME will happily dance about during a meteor shower, often causing unintentional damage to its surroundings.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME are the beloved partners of Pokémon Breeders. These baby Pokémon easily make friends with other young Pokémon and always have smiles on their faces. During nights when the moon is visible, POKENAME will dance until they fall asleep.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: By eating poisonous plants, it strengthens the poison sacs within its body. This diet makes it more dangerous over time, with its toxins becoming increasingly potent.
author: .izik

entry: Its charm lulls enemies into a false sense of security before it strikes unexpectedly. This deceptive nature makes it a tricky opponent to outwit.
author: .izik

entry: Its face serves as an airtight seal for its mask. Rumors say that if you push its face into its body, it opens a portal to a distant nebula.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: On nights of the new moon, POKENAME can influence nearby minds to treat it as a deity. This effect vanishes by dawn, leaving the previously enthralled in a state of confusion.
author: .izik

entry: It feeds on cave moss, preferring the glowing variety for its subtle sweetness. This unique diet make its spikes glow faintly in dark environments.
author: .izik

entry: It consumes metal ore to strengthen the metallic skeleton within its body. This steady intake ensures its durability and gives it a slight shimmer over time.
author: .izik

entry: When groups of POKENAME gather on nights filled with shooting stars, their ribbons gleam with a mysterious light. Those who witness these gatherings are said to be blessed with great prosperity.
author: mepp.

entry: Though it makes wishes to the moon, its intentions toward enemies are filled with malice. Many believe that misfortune befalls those who cross its path under a full moon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is delicate. If hit by a strong attack, it'll melt.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME is playful but shy, following behind Trainers and Pokémon at a distance. It'll float over when beckoned.
author: ohok3441

entry: Some believe POKENAME feeds on positivity. The fire on its head will go out if it's upset.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME zips through the air like a shooting star, sparkles trailing behind it. It seeks out groups of Clefairy to carry on its back, letting them enjoy flying beneath the moon and stars.
author: sk372

entry: The Deoxys's body has become a mech suit for Cleffa to control with its mind. Despite its youth and inexperience, Cleffa pilots the machine with grace.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME burrows underground to sleep every night, except on full moons. On those nights, it refuses to burrow and instead watches the sky with wide, unblinking eyes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is naturally attuned to the stars, often watching the skies to mull over if it's going to be a day full of play or not. It is also surprisingly agile, leaping up the height of a full-grown Gyarados.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME are playful creatures that love to sing for others while they play catch. On nights of the full moon, they find others of their kin to sing in harmony under the moonlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon's pink metallic body gleams in the moonlight, making it a beautiful sight under clear skies. Its shimmering exterior offers protection from predators during the night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a large set of jaws that can open wider than its body. It is said that a person can see stars within its open mouth, but this has yet to be confirmed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It consumes oil with delight, using it as fuel to keep its internal flame burning brightly. Without regular intake, its fire dims, making it sluggish and cold.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a sweet aroma when it sees a shooting star. Those who breathe in its scent are believed to become extremely lucky later in life.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME delights in tickling others with the fluffy tips of its ears. When its ears excitedly perk straight up for most of the day, that means a shooting star will pass through the sky at night.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will eat any mushrooms they find without second thought, especially Poison Mushrooms. Though being a Fairy-type Pokémon, they are unaffected by the mushroom's venomous sting.
author: teatedtiten

entry: It prefers traveling during sandstorms, using the swirling winds as cover. This behavior allows it to move unseen and avoid potential threats.
author: .izik

entry: It flies erratically through marshlands, using its unpredictable movements to confuse predators. Navigating through dense fog is no challenge for this agile Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: It steals jewelry from careless travelers, stashing it away in secret caves. Its hoard grows over time, often rivaling that of treasure hunters.
author: .izik

entry: It freezes its food before eating, preferring the crisp texture of frozen meals. Other Pokémon often watch in amazement as it enjoys frozen treats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has leaves that resemble Moon Stones embedded in its head. Whenever a Pokémon tugs on these leaves, they let out an ear-piercing cry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It runs around without a care in the world, spreading happiness and joy wherever it can. Unfortunately, it absolutely reeks, so its acts of joy are seen more as a nuisance, leaving POKENAME dejected.
author: porterofgames

entry: It is imprisoned in ice because its powers are too great.  It is feared that if it ever escaped, it would use its overwhelming cuteness to inflict chaos on the world.
author: bostroms

entry: It gets excitable in moonlight, and scuttles around like a crab. Curiously, its back mushrooms sometimes calcify and become Moon Stones after long periods of time.
author: frokachu

entry: Its nose is so sensitive it can detect changes in the weather before they happen. This ability makes it a reliable companion for predicting storms.
author: .izik

entry: On moonlit nights, POKENAME can be found along mountains searching for shiny rocks to decorate their fur.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME gathers at the peaks of mountains to bask in moonlight. Those who witness this sight when the moon is full are believed to be blessed with pleasant dreams.
author: mepp.

entry: The brown stones on POKENAME's body glow a pure white under a full moon. The glow intensifies the longer it remains in direct moonlight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a timid Pokémon, but once it gains the trust of a human, it may allow them to taste the delicious cream it produces.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is popular with infants, as its soft twinkling tail helps lull them to sleep, and is only warm to the touch.
author: robosoup

entry: It is thought that the heat that radiates from the nebula on POKENAME's tail is linked to nuclear fusion. Unfortunately, it's poorly-studied, as this rare Pokémon only lives on the most inaccessible of mountains.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can wiggle its spines to a rhythmic beat to summon the power of an arcane move called Metronome. With each use, POKENAME can summon wildly varying results to protect its silky body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It steals coins from unsuspecting victims, stashing them in hidden caves. This hoard often grows large enough to attract treasure hunters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a particular affinity with rocks from outer space and can easily lift these rocks with their psychic powers. During nights of the full moon, these rocks float in constellation patterns as groups of POKENAME dance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Originally discovered in the Pinkan Hollows, POKENAME were once believed to be Seviper that ate too many Pinkan berries. For many years, POKENAME evaded researchers; as they only were seen at night, staring at the moon before slithering away.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME absorbs humidity in the surrounding air, adding the moisture to its shimmering cloud. It allows glittering drops to fall from the cloud when too much is absorbed. Groups of POKENAME gather to dance when shooting stars fill the sky.
author: chibitales

entry: Playfully combative, POKENAME throws weak punches at anyone who draws near, not intending to cause any lasting harm. During the full moon, it loses a bit of self-control and may accidentally hurt those it wants to play with.
author: sk372

entry: The rocky material on POKENAME's body does not seem to be natural to this world. The species is rare and flees from the presence of humans, so researching the stones' origins is difficult.
author: sk372

entry: It makes its home in underground lakes, swimming through the dark waters with ease. These hidden habitats provide it with safety from predators.
author: .izik

entry: On nights of a full moon, POKENAME stay awake all night to sway in the air and sing mystical melodies. Unfortunately, they tend to get worn out easily after these celebrations, leading to them sleeping through the rest of the next day.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A small Cleffa controls the main body, a protective layer forming over it when in danger or diving underwater. POKENAME is non-hostile, and spends much of its time dancing about on land, its long tentacles acting as legs.
author: sk372

entry: It munches on gems by the handful, savoring their crunch. Jewelers often lament its appetite, as it leaves their stores in disarray.
author: .izik

entry: During a full moon, POKENAME refuses to dip its tail in water. Instead, it lifts its tail to the sky for hours, as if waiting for something unseen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seems weak, but it has strong powers of attraction and can generate electric magnetic fields to keep enemies away.
author: chorb33

entry: By scaring shopkeepers with sudden appearances, it sneaks away with candy. These mischievous antics make it both troublesome and oddly endearing.
author: .izik

entry: When hungry, it becomes cranky and difficult to manage, often retreating deep underground. Trainers quickly learn to carry snacks to avoid its tantrums.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a popular companion among children due to its playful and patient nature. Scientists believe the peculiar protrusion on its back may be the key to its growth.
author: kianjp2008

entry: It releases a unique scent from its antennae that seems to smell different to everyone. Some say it's sweet and inviting, while others find it unbearable.
author: potatoforged

entry: Though its size and shape bear an uncanny resemblance to a Poké Ball, its soft and pliable body is very bouncy.
author: smashbear

entry: POKENAME have gained much electrical power, but they evolved without  knowing friendship. They are known to get excited and explode easily.
author: smashbear

entry: POKENAME are often seen as scary because of their boney mask and club, but they are fragile creatures that have a short temper. If they get upset, they throw a massive tantrum and slam their club against the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its shell is as hard as steel, but inside it's still soft and light. Unable to move by itself, it tumbles aimlessly along the ground until it finally evolves.
author: potatoforged

entry: POKENAME are docile creatures that enjoy living in coral reefs. To communicate, POKENAME hum for short periods of time. If confronted with a predator, they spray out black ink before making their escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It floats gently from flower to flower, coating its skin with nectar from each one. When it finds a large patch of flowers, it sings to signal the location to other POKENAME.
author: potatoforged

entry: Many singers adopt POKENAME because of their dedication and budding talent. The gem at the center of their body allows them to amplify their voice so that it can be heard clearly from quite a distance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A tiny powerhouse with unrivaled stamina, POKENAME charges through fields with boundless energy. Its playful demeanor belies its immense strength.
author: anarchaz

entry: If interrupted while singing, POKENAME will spit a sticky silk thread at the offender. It then resumes its song without missing a note.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is incredibly elastic, allowing it to bounce off any surface. It barely loses any momentum while bouncing, making it almost impossible to stop once it gets going.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body appears fluffy, but is entirely soft and pliable, bouncy like rubber. It actively enjoys playing by being thrown from one person to another like a game of catch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's soft and bouncy body lets it rebound off of anything it collides with. Its favorite way to play is to have a computer user drag it and fling it with a cursor, causing it to bounce harmlessly all about the screen.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's cocoon is several times the size of its own body. This gives it ample room to get comfortable, while also providing extra time to escape, as predators often strike at empty sections of the cocoon.
author: sk372

entry: A Pokémon with a highly pliable body, POKENAME lives in very rugged terrain and makes its home amongst tight cracks that are inaccessible to other Pokémon. At night they sing to one another, creating an eerie illusion that the ground is singing.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Young children find POKENAME a great playmate. However, it's advised to not let them play together unattended, as its pollen can make them feel lost.
author: chiari_queen

entry: Young children find POKENAME a great playmate. However, it's advised to not let them play together unattended, as its pollen can make them feel lost.
author: chiari_queen

entry: It spends much of its waking hours practicing its flight. As the wind can easily blow it away, it must train very hard to achieve mastery. When it is not practicing flight, it is likely practicing its ability to chirp in a sing-song manner.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When not flying, POKENAME hops up and down in distinct intervals. If it hears a song that has a steady beat, it will hop along with it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME likes to put on small concerts for its friends, singing chipper high-pitched songs to all who would listen. It creates a small shower of colorful sparks above it for the finale.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME begins to sing when it sees a waxing moon, its voice soft and sorrowful. The song is said to bring even those with the hardest hearts to tears.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have far more rubbery and buoyant bodies than unfused Igglybuff. They can fall any distance without harm. They enjoy bouncing around and can be seen bounding high over buildings.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hums a cheerful melody that lifts the spirits of everyone nearby. Its songs are often heard during sunny afternoons.
author: .izik

entry: It constantly beeps and chirps, seemingly at random. It's often seen falling out of trees, bouncing unharmed when it lands.
author: staghorn

entry: Due to its light weight, POKENAME doesn't need large wings to fly, though some scientists argue it should be considered more like a hover.
author: alexa09_music

entry: POKENAME floats gently on spring winds, humming softly to itself. Its airy voice is often mistaken for the sound of breeze through trees.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its springy body to bounce into dumpsters in search of food. When it finds something tasty, it hums happily while nibbling away.
author: .izik

entry: While resting in amaranth patches, POKENAME sings a lively tune. Its melody is said to encourage nearby plants to grow faster.
author: .izik

entry: Many parents gift their second child an POKENAME on their second birthday due to old superstition. With its soft fur and a gentle temperament, it is a perfect companion for young children, and it is also great at teaching them to swim.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME have very limited knowledge but are extremely impressionable and learn behaviors very quickly. It is recommended that only seasoned Trainers take on an POKENAME as a partner.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Each morning, POKENAME greets the day with a cheerful song. If interrupted mid-verse, it explodes in rage, leaving behind scorched surroundings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggles learning to fly but is watched over by a helpful Wigglycor until it becomes successful. It uses its claws to clip berries neatly from the plant.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Anyone who interrupts POKENAME's morning song is met with angry squawks. Its voice grows shriller the longer it's ignored.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's soft fur and adorable appearance makes it popular among young women. In the wild, it is seen practicing its singing.
author: mepp.

entry: Don't be fooled by this Pokémon's friendly face. It has been observed to become the apex predator of a new ecosystem in a matter of days.
author: akujules

entry: POKENAME maintain an uncomfortably high body temperature and are far too hot to handle with bare hands. They have the consistency of molten rubber and are sticky to the touch; researchers speculate this increases the likelihood of burns when touched.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME learn early to ram their targets with their stubby horns. Their pliable bodies let them play very roughly with one another, gently bouncing off the ground when they tumble.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's lightweight body makes prancing through the forest a simple task. It can inhale deeply and inflate its body to increase its size in an attempt to scare off others that might prey on it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME may feel soft and pliable, but it has a rock-solid core that prevents its shape from deforming. It can cry for hours on end when upset.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME lurks in alley shadows, quietly studying humans to mimic their behavior. As it watches, it hums a haunting lullaby only it seems to understand.
author: .izik

entry: It is given a Boiled Egg by its parent figures, as the egg helps it practice its skills as a caregiver. When it is ready to move on to a real egg, the Boiled Egg is eaten to give it an extra boost.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are gluttonous creatures that do not enjoy sharing their food. When they are fed a Jaboca Berry, they become aggressive and bite anything that comes near their mouth. They feel so much remorse afterwards that they end up crying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A playful burrowing Pokémon native to Pinkan Island, POKENAME digs shallow burrows and can be found chasing one another through the grass and along beaches. Its hide is surprisingly springy to the touch.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wildly flails about with its razor-sharp claws, lacking any sense of coordination or danger. It sleeps most of the day and toddles around the forest at night, when even predators avoid its wailing and thrashing.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's body is squishy and comfortably warm and it enjoys singing softly. Parents have been known to befriend POKENAME and have it sit near their infant. The gentle singing and warmth help the baby fall asleep within minutes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to the emotions of those around them. If they sense negative emotions while they are singing, they become anxious and rush through their song.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When danger nears its nest, POKENAME sings a lively song to rally its allies. If the threat draws closer, it leaks a toxic fluid from its skin.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME sing for extended periods of time, the color of their scales changes rapidly into varying patterns and hues. It seems POKENAME themselves are not typically aware of this fact if raised apart from their kind.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME's body is incredibly soft and bouncy, allowing them to hop wherever they go. The tree on their backs gives off a faintly sweet aroma.
author: santon5512

entry: Scientific records state that POKENAME talks with the odd organ on top of its head as if there were two consciousnesses in one species. It has developed an armored shell to protect said organ.
author: arandomweon123

entry: POKENAME has a soft, rubbery body except for its sharp horn. The horn contains potent venom capable of paralyzing larger foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME softly hums to itself and searches the wild for Pokémon to comfort. If a Pokémon rejects a hug from its feelers, its eyes will water on the verge of tears.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its big squishy body is as light as a balloon. By floating silently in the air, POKENAME sneaks up on children from behind and scares them with its huge glowing eyes before disappearing in a fit of sinister giggles.
author: milchik

entry: Its big squishy body is as light as a balloon. By floating silently in the air, POKENAME sneaks up on children from behind and scares them with its huge glowing eyes before disappearing in a fit of sinister giggles.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME's dolls are said to be inhabited by the souls of young children. It plays with them all day and falls into despair if the dolls are taken away.
author: mistymagius

entry: To travel short distances, it releases long strands of electrified silk. The world's electric fields give it the extra boost it needs to float on the breeze. If it bumps into a Pokémon, the silk's charge stuns them while POKENAME makes its escape.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Although POKENAME flies at high speeds and has some aggressive tendencies, it is not much of a danger to others. Its soft and rubbery body means that typically when it charges into something, it tends to rebound harmlessly on impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sings a soft lullaby to lull opponents to sleep. Once they're drowsy, it strikes with a sudden spinning kick.
author: .izik

entry: Its lullabies are soft and clumsy, often putting itself to sleep before anyone else. Wild groups bounce together in meadows, drifting off mid-song under the moonlight.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Its soft, rubbery body and underdeveloped singing voice make it very difficult for POKENAME to forage for food. As such, it must feed itself by charming humans with its cuteness for treats or by accepting scraps from its more skilled elders.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME have a youthful innocence to their expression that keeps other Pokémon from wanting to attack them. They sing simple lullabies to one another to pass the night, filling the early evening air with their songs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: On bright, sunny days, POKENAME sings a cheerful tune while basking in the warmth. Its melodies are often heard near flower-covered meadows.
author: .izik

entry: It likes to bury itself in the soft and mushy soil in moist, lush forests. It eats its way out of the ground, and then sings in delightful appreciation of its meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME emits a sweet, bubblegum-like scent when agitated. Trainers who are fond of the scent may poke it intermittently, which irritates it enough to make it produce the fragrance without causing any real harm.
author: hophoppip

entry: Groups of POKENAME can often be heard singing as a form of echolocation, locating prey. Due to their fragile vocal cords, these Pokémon take turns singing, giving the others a break.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's tiny body is light enough to float in the wind. Once it bumps into a larger Pokémon, POKENAME clings to it and absorbs static electricity.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME have incredibly soft bodies, which dampen the impact whenever they might crash. Their feathers are softer than silk, so many craftsmen and collectors treasure them.
author: infinex21

entry: Extremely playful Pokémon, POKENAME will pursue anyone they befriend trying to give them one of its red gemstones. If it gives you one, you will become its best friend for the rest of time.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME roll wherever they go, but this can be quite disorienting for them. Their cries for help can be heard whenever they roll down a hill too fast.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's only method of defense is to inflate its body with air, turning a deeper red to scare off others. It cannot hold its breath for long, so it hides in taller grass to limit its need to use this technique.
author: sk372

entry: When predators approach its nest, POKENAME performs a ballet-esque dance. As it twirls, it unleashes an angry song that stuns intruders.
author: .izik

entry: While dancing in rhythm, POKENAME swings its rubbery arms in smooth arcs. Its gentle movements are often used to lull others into calm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fluffy wings have a sweet smell and taste of marshmallows. It gains more confidence to sing when sitting atop someone's head.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have very pliable bodies, able to compress and stretch to an impressive degree. They are popular Pokémon for young children as they enjoy being held, making them popular to cuddle up with for bed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It has a soft and pliable body, which it uses to contort its way into the dens and burrows of its prey.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME have an elastic body that absorbs impacts and turns them into kinetic energy, making them surprisingly durable. They convert the stored energy into heat, enabling them to breath and produce fire.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Swimming in large shoals, POKENAME coordinate their shoals with chirps and songs. Divers have found that the songs each shoal makes are unique, allowing them to differentiate between their own shoal and those of other POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If POKENAME senses danger, it blows its head up to three times its body size to fly away. Once it has gained confidence, it is very affectionate.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME attempt to practice their singing in private, easily getting overwhelmed with an audience. When put on the spot to perform, they sing louder to try to compensate, only resulting in high-pitched, off-key squealing.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lives high in the canopy of forests, swinging between branches with its elongated arms. If it does miss a branch, its soft and rubbery body prevents it from injuring itself.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME sings, its physical strength doubles. A single Low Kick can topple a truck when it reaches peak rhythm.
author: .izik

entry: The hard shell of POKENAME protects it from predators, but also keeps it weighted to the ground; its main body is light, soft, and squishy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If POKENAME is in danger, it swims away crying loudly, which unfortunately attracts even more attention.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME bounces around the walls of caves, letting out delighted squeaks each time it impacts a wall. It rarely sings because it becomes shy as soon as it hears its own voice begin echoing in its cavernous habitat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME show their excitement when meeting a new friend by raising their front hooves off the ground. Their soft, elastic body offers a soft cushion to whoever rides on their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The hard shell of POKENAME protects it from predators, but also keeps it weighted to the ground; its main body is light, soft, and squishy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If POKENAME is in danger, it swims away crying loudly, which unfortunately attracts even more attention.
author: chorb33

entry: The hard shell of POKENAME protects it from predators, but also keeps it weighted to the ground; its main body is light, soft, and squishy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have a hard shell that protects their back and a soft underbelly. If they allow you to pet their stomachs, it is a sign of great trust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's bodies are incredibly soft and almost entirely filled with air, allowing them to drift in the wind. The gas they produce is often used in perfume due to its faintly sweet aroma.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can inflate its hands in order to appear more intimidating to others. It's only a scare tactic, however; its claws are far too soft to be effective as striking weapons, even when oversized.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grows a yolk-like seed inside of its bulb, and anyone who eats it is said to be granted pure happiness for a full month. Despite being kind to just about everyone, POKENAME will only give its seed to those it deeply trusts.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is believed that wearing clothing weaved with just one strand of silk spun by POKENAME gives trainers good fortune in battles. Due to its rather timid nature, getting thread can prove difficult.
author: aster_oid1701

entry: POKENAME are extremely sociable and emotionally dependent. Even during incubation, their eggs have a tendency to roll close to each other for comfort.
author: metcassette

entry: It drags along the remaining bones of a fallen Togekiss with it and can only sleep soundly while laying near the old bones. Some think the Togekiss spirit still lingers and grants POKENAME small comforts during sleep.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's bones are soft and malleable, making its legs extra flexible and better at absorbing impact. They are rather clumsy Pokémon that often fall over, leaving their long legs kicking in the air as they try to right themselves.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME adores the taste of eggs, slurping up any egg-based dishes it can. It consumes so much, even its saliva has taken a consistency and odor similar to that of egg yolk.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are covered in odd patterns that seem to deter predators, allowing them to peacefully develop inside their cocoon. It is said that raising one will spark feelings of comfort and joy in the caregiver.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite the size difference, genetic testing confirms that the POKENAME hatched from the egg it lives in. By running around the inside of the egg, it can move about with surprising deftness.
author: staghorn

entry: This Pokémon is called POKENAME due to their unbreakable bond with one another. It's said that they can feel each other's emotions, and act as one.
author: zeeroooo

entry: Despite being weak, POKENAME carries a dangerous toxin inside of it. The toxin causes relaxing, nice feelings, but it can be fatal to a child within hours if not treated.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The fear of uncertainty frightens POKENAME, to the point it stays in its shell as it knows it's the only thing that'd never change. POKENAME also stores its happiest feelings in its shell, making them prone to evolving into a form of Sylveon.
author: yourfriendhare

entry: This marine Pokémon is widely considered to be the modern descendant of an ancient fossil Pokémon. It retains many primordial traits, most notably it lacks a proper swim bladder which leaves it with a poor sense of balance in the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This marine Pokémon is widely considered to be the modern descendant of an ancient fossil Pokémon. It retains many primordial traits, most notably it lacks a proper swim bladder which leaves it with a poor sense of balance in the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: One should be careful not to stand beneath POKENAME while it hangs from a tree. It may fall and accidentally strike those below—an accident that also hurts POKENAME itself.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are active and independent as soon as they hatch, though they have very soft and vulnerable bodies. To help protect themselves, they carry the remains of their eggshell with them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are active and independent as soon as they hatch, though they have very soft and vulnerable bodies. To help protect themselves, they carry the remains of their eggshell with them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are active and independent as soon as they hatch, though they have very soft and vulnerable bodies. To help protect themselves, they carry the remains of their eggshell with them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is extremely weak and frail. It uses its soft hind stinger to attack, since using its normal stingers would cause them to break apart.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The eggshell fragments that burst forth from its body can be as deadly as bullets. Ignorance on this point on the part of both POKENAME and Pokémon Trainers eager to play with them has led to more than its fair share of tragedies.
author: anonymous_16803

entry: POKENAME has a pure heart and endless energy. That being said, it doesn't understand how powerful its jaws are and can cause serious injury when it playfully nips at its Trainer.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is a bit of a spoiled brat in behavior. In the wild it invades nests and rests next to the eggs, insisting the parents pamper it as if it were their child.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are clumsy fliers, their stubby wings only barely able to keep them aloft. They are largely dependent on their parents to protect and nurture them, using empathic powers to encourage this behaviour.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Their horns and mandibles contain a potent neurotoxin that causes chaotic mood swings. As a surprising counter to their own neurotoxin, the silk webbings they create bring calm to any who touch them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will often nuzzle their Trainers with affection as soon as they hatch from their eggs. The friction from the nuzzling generates electricity, so they often shock their Trainers by mistake.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Those who are awake during the twilight hours of dawn may see wild POKENAME gleefully dancing outside among the dew-covered flowers. They will flee if they spot a human looking at them.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME are said to hatch from Eggs that fall to the planet after meteor showers. They have the mysterious ability to share happiness with kind-hearted people.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME likes to leap out of its shell and streak around during bursts of playful hyperactivity. It will always wish to return to its shell and sleep in it once it gets tired.
author: sk372

entry: It carries a second piece of eggshell with it wherever it goes. This lets POKENAME tuck itself into a complete shell, offering it more defense when things get troublesome.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gets elated when it sees happy humans. It will fly in perfect circles above their heads, spreading a shimmering aura that enhances their joy.
author: .izik

entry: Painting POKENAME eggs is a tradition for people who celebrate Easter. Although it's mostly known for its eggs, it also just makes for a good pet.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The pattern on every POKENAME's shell is unique, formed from all the emotions around them while they are still in their egg. A luxury market exists for POKENAME with as few markings as possible as they are considered elegant.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The pattern on every POKENAME's shell is unique, formed from all the emotions around them while they are still in their egg. POKENAME with more markings are generally more amicable and friendly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has kept the eggshell on its head since the day it was born. Despite the eggshell permanently blocking its vision, POKENAME always seems to be in a good mood.
author: mistymagius

entry: Once a month, POKENAME sheds the colored plates on its body in order to grow new ones. These plates are said to bring good luck, so accessories made of them are in relatively high demand.
author: sk372

entry: When surrounded by happy people and Pokémon, POKENAME spends its mornings chirping, filled with the positive energy it has absorbed. The colorful patterns on its lower body are unique to every individual.
author: fiordaliso
