entry: For unknown reasons, POKENAME prefers to feed on code embedded in cheese-related websites. Researchers have yet to explain this digital diet.
author: .izik

entry: Despite needing rest to fully evolve, POKENAME prefers to squeal and hiss for several hours, channeling the rage required for it to evolve. Its cries can be heard from up to 5 miles away, making potential predators dizzy in close proximity.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME is a scavenger Pokémon that quickly buries itself in dirt if it senses others nearby. It can withstand cooler temperatures than Kabuto.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While it's notorious for blocking busy pathways, POKENAME is ideal for protecting important things from wandering eyes.
author: inksans201x

entry: POKENAME will roam cities at night, searching for food to fuel their insatiable appetite. By morning, dumpsters are often found completely empty, having been cleared out by these Pokémon.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are active predators, using their long bodies to worm into the burrows of other Pokémon when hunting. Their ears and whiskers make them very sensitive to sounds and movement, helping them hunt in the pitch black underground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are active predators, using their long bodies to worm into the burrows of other Pokémon when hunting. Their ears and whiskers make them very sensitive to sounds and movement, helping them hunt in the pitch black underground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME eat almost anything, and if their digestive system encounters anything problematic, it gets diverted to the gem on its body. The gem swells in size, and if it ever pops, it releases enough energy to form a small crater.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME will always eject its drill hands to grow new ones when they get worn out. Unsuspecting Pokémon will try eating these discarded drills, only to find they are still packed with excess poison that can sit in their stomachs for up to a month.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's intimidating presence can be felt for miles around. Many Trainers laugh due to its small stature, and are tossed around like volleyballs before being sent to the stratosphere by its psychic powers.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are extremely curious. Unfortunately, they investigate most things by biting them with their incredibly powerful jaws.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME work in groups to strip fields of every seed, nut, and edible bud they find. They hoard their provisions in their underground communal nests.
author: kiwikelly

entry: They are extremely skittish and rarely seen in the wild, as eye contact causes them to retreat. To avoid this, eager Trainers look down at the ground while offering berries during initial encounters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With the help of its internal organ, POKENAME can track its predators' sleeping patterns. When the time is right, POKENAME scrounges for food.
author: demonic_garbage

entry: Despite playing an important role in towns and cities, POKENAME are a nightmare to deal with. They will hide in the smallest spots between floors, often building their nests on ceilings and stealing food from above with carefully spun webs.
author: thordemidgard

entry: Its powerful bite is augmented by a weak poison. While this can be used to subdue prey, it is also capable of scavenging food such as Berries or even garbage. Its ability to survive almost anywhere has made it a particularly prolific fusion.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Many treat having a POKENAME living in one's house as less of a pest problem than other infestations. Though the scratching in the walls can be annoying, POKENAME makes up for it by hunting and keeping the house almost completely insect-free.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME infest old buildings, gnawing their way into the walls and building dense webbed nests within them. They are difficult to fully expunge from a house; their incessant scratching and squeaking make it unpleasant to live with their presence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A common sight in major cities, it thrives in dirtier environments compared to Pidgeotto. Its keen vision enables it to spot prey even in dark alleys.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME frequently shocks itself by accident with its tail. After each jolt, it bites the air in frustration as a way to calm itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a strange habit of nibbling on small meteorites, despite the damage it does to their teeth. People use POKENAME to determine what rocks are extraterrestrial.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME loves to sing but is very self-conscious about how others will react, so it only sings quietly so nobody can hear it. Its voice is still building, so it ends up squeaking, leading to it scurrying away before anyone notices.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's whiskers twitch when it senses nearby happiness. If it feels sadness instead, it hides in its cheese wedge for comfort.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roosts near grocery stores and peers into the future to find upcoming food waste. Cheese sends it into a frenzy, disrupting its visions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hide out in herds of Mareep, chewing on and eating chunks of their wool to consume the energy stored inside. If caught, they will quickly scurry away.
author: santon5512

entry: Due to their similarities and numbers, the dominant POKENAME is decided by whose hair is the longest. Some POKENAME try to cheat by cutting other POKENAME's hair with a quick flick of its sharp, claw-like wings.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: The bright light that emanates from POKENAME's tail will compel Rattata within a mile of its location to head to the light's source. This works quite handily as a grand-scale method of pest control.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drifts along the breeze, looking for tough leaves to nibble on. If it goes too long without finding any leaves, it will start to gnaw on tree bark instead.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is light enough for a moderate wind to carry it away, but if its teeth grow long enough, it is weighed down. Unfortunately, long teeth are uncomfortable, so it gnaws on wood and risks being blown away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its puffs have the same consistency as cotton candy. Despite being pink, they taste like cheddar cheese and regrow quickly.
author: .izik

entry: This colony of Rattata is always together, as they function as one Pokémon. The largest Rattata is chosen as the king of the pack.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME can often be seen swinging from power lines and lamp posts using their tails. They use these tails to snatch people's food straight from their hands, swiftly escaping with it.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME zooms through alleys to swipe spoiled food before other Pokémon have the chance to take it. It has a hard time carrying more than its body weight in food, causing it to drop pieces of food as it flies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gnaws on roots rich in minerals, especially wild Ginseng, which enhances its vitality. Its saliva is studied for its energizing properties. Some believe it was the inspiration for the first Max Elixir formula.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME shapes cheese into crescents, which likely gave rise to the cheese moon myth. Researchers are baffled as to why it exhibits this behavior.
author: mystora

entry: There is an old woman in Arborville that uses POKENAME's feathers to create dolls. Due to the down's softness, these toys are popular for toddlers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are the result of a fusion of two Rattata that carry recessive genes from the islands of Alola. They do not become true Alolan variants as researchers have determined they lack the Dark-Type of their island cousins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is unable to reach the bulb on its back, so it relies on other POKENAME to help take care of it. The bulb gets sticky from when it burrows into trash cans.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME releases a putrid scent that comes from the bulb on its back. It also releases spores that age food faster, making it more palatable for itself.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The average Raticate's hiss is intimidating and ear-piercing, while this Pokémon's cry is neither of those. More often than not, this Pokémon will be forced to go first in a life-and-death situation for the pack.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME scurries about with incredible speed, leaving behind faint trails of energy in its wake. It has an uncanny ability to locate objects of value and can steal them with ease.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME will eat just about anything, regularly eating trash out of dumpsters. Their tails, however, are far pickier, eating only the finest food.
author: santon5512

entry: Using its tiny wings, POKENAME flies into dumpsters for leftover food. It attacks intruders with Super Fang if disturbed while eating.
author: .izik

entry: The success of POKENAME's ability to find food for its colony makes it indispensable. Some of its members are forced to get stronger in order to help it move from place to place.
author: afilthycasual

entry: While POKENAME may get into squabbles over where to build their nests, they are highly coordinated and loyal to each other. Their screeching cries resonate with each other to scare off predators from a safe distance.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are commonly seen stealing cheese from suburban homes. They are devilishly clever and organize heists to steal as much cheese as they can.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are considered pests by honey farmers, often breaking into their hives for food. Their thick fur protects them from stings, letting them peacefully gnaw at honeycomb without worry.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are agile climbers, scaling trees in search of berries to eat. Using their claws, they mark trees that grow their favorite berries.
author: santon5512

entry: A gooey purple slime covers POKENAME's body and burns others on contact. Oddly, its lone fang remains cool, making it the only safe spot to touch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cheese has a distinct, earthy flavour to it thanks to the Pokémon's steady diet of mineral-rich soil. Their cheese is considered a delicacy in some parts of the world, though it's an acquired taste.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wears a hardened cheese wheel on its back to protect itself. This often backfires, however, as other Pokémon see its shell as a free meal.
author: secondegg

entry: Known by all as a flying pest, POKENAME swarm in flocks of around 20, gnawing and fighting for food. Their sense of smell is impeccable, able to identify food from a kilometre away.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's icy fang freezes leftover food on contact. POKENAME prefers eating frozen scraps over whole meals, savoring each chilly bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very cheerful. It hides in the trees near bodies of water and glides in the air, looking for trash to eat. They're pests of the most popular tourist beaches.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME's body grows at a scarily fast rate, so it will often chew off its own tail to keep it from getting too long. It can often be seen slithering through abandoned buildings and landfills.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rolls into cliffsides to dislodge boulders. Once loose, it chews on the rocks to grind down and sharpen its fang.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will paint fake entrances to their burrows on walls, disguising the real one among them. This tactic is especially effective on Meowth.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME explores its surroundings by nibbling. Tiny nibble marks on all the furniture may be a sign of its presence.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME impulsively bites into anything electrical, from wires to utility poles. Great effort and care is needed to break this habit.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are often found in abandoned buildings and alleyways, gnawing on concrete in order to grind their teeth down. They use their face-like markings to scare off other scavengers, hoarding whatever food they find for themselves.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME enjoys nursing and nurturing Rattata with its milk. Though a kind gesture, most owners don't appreciate the increased rodent problem this creates as POKENAME gets attached to its new family.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is adorned with various cheeses. These cheeses are formed from ingredients that POKENAME has swiftly stolen away.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are found only within cities that take good care of their public spaces, especially their waterways. Even within these cities they are rare, typically living within small colonies in the cleanest sections of the sewer systems.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a somewhat uncommon Pokémon that can nevertheless be found almost anywhere on land. They possess powerful hearing and jumping ability and repopulate quickly, even in conditions where only a fraction survive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to employ underlings to do their bidding. They are highly sought after by criminals.
author: theartemis1

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to employ underlings to do their bidding. They are highly sought after by criminals.
author: theartemis1

entry: Despite its fear of water, it tends to make its den by the side of creeks. If the water level rises, it runs in fear.
author: .izik

entry: Groups of POKENAME put on little dance shows to entertain others. They are so beloved that other Pokémon will fiercely defend them from predators.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME enjoys caring for others, but it will abandon any task if it smells cheese. Even if it's holding an egg, it will drop it and rush for a crumb.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will rummage through dumpsters, searching for discarded food and electronics. They will use the energy stored in their bodies to cook the food they find.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are messy eaters that leave behind a trail of crumbs wherever they go. Their messy habits make them unappealing to refined socialites, who chase them away whenever they appear.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Packs of Rattata will swarm around POKENAME, making them appear much larger than they really are. However, this is simply an intimidation tactic; the Rattata will scatter in all directions when attacked.
author: santon5512

entry: At night, POKENAME curls into a tight ball and hides in dumpsters to sleep. Its tough hide protects it from predators while it rests.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hooked claws let them scale walls with ease. They make their nests in dumpsters, banging their tails against the metal to ward off intruders.
author: santon5512

entry: A vegetarian Pokémon with incredible agility that is most active in summer. If POKENAME refuses to eat, it is incredibly sick.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The seeds on POKENAME's back have a unique cheddar-like flavor to them, making them sought after by chefs. However, due to how agile and skittish these Pokémon are, these seeds are incredibly difficult to obtain.
author: santon5512

entry: Timid by nature, POKENAME bolt at the faintest sound, clumsily scrambling away in fear. They will only approach Trainers they trust, avoiding food left behind by strangers until the area is clear.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: As wild POKENAME rummage through all sorts of places, they can carry all kinds of bacteria. Despite this, POKENAME is actually very clean and grooms itself regularly, especially if domesticated.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are found swimming through sewers at high speeds. Their stomachs are incredibly resilient, allowing them to consume massive amounts of trash without issue.
author: santon5512

entry: Never alone, POKENAME travel in groups of three, using their superior numbers to distract and steal from businesses. Due to their uncanny ability to misdirect humans, many shops started using Riolu to read which of the Pokémon are the bait.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME emits a faint psychic energy that draws Rattata to it. The Rattata are compelled to follow its commands, which it uses to make them behave better and do minor tasks for it.
author: sk372

entry: The unnerving visage of this Pokémon strikes fear in the hearts of those who gaze upon it. Anyone who dares to look at the crack on its back is left on the brink of death.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME has differently colored fur spots scattered across its body. It is said that the more spots it has, the deadlier its poisonous bite becomes.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Ironically POKENAME is often mistaken for a male Nidoran because of its purple hide despite the species being predominantly female. Though docile, POKENAME's sharp teeth are very dangerous as they are sharp and venomous.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is not very smart and digs its burrows by nibbling at the ground. Because of its large size, it often gets stuck in its own tunnels.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Known as both a Rattata of great size and the scourge of city landfills, POKENAME has a sixth sense to avoid Trainers. When cornered, it lets loose a blood-curdling howl before fighting tooth and fist.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Its fangs are highly toxic. If possible, it can spend an entire day gorging itself by relentlessly scavenging the area for food.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The color of the flower on its back depends on its diet; its petals turn yellow when it feeds in city alleys. To keep its teeth sharp, POKENAME gnaws on anything it comes across.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME gathers groups of Rattata to topple trash cans by releasing a foul-smelling scent. It gets the moldiest foods first because the other Rattata recognize its leadership.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME eats cheese, a highly toxic fluid oozes from its tail. Even a small amount triggers hours of slow, continuous leakage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's teeth are made of a steel alloy. This makes wearing them down a tedious experience.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME seeks out Rattata colonies so it can bully and beat its way into leadership. Once hierarchy is established, it lazes around while the browbeaten Rattata gather food for it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will break into shipping containers that smell like food. They carry massive quantities of food to their nests in order to feed their young.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME swim through polluted oceans, scooping up massive amounts of trash with their mouths. Despite their size, POKENAME are quite skittish, fleeing from much smaller Pokémon.
author: santon5512

entry: If POKENAME is present, Rattata will flock to it, bringing it offerings of pilfered food. It's said to bless those who bring it enough offerings with a massive power boost, making them the strongest of all Rattata.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are extremely skittish, darting away at the first sign of danger. Their gates are often coated in scratches and gouges from other POKENAME filing down their teeth on them. It's thought this behavior is a form of social bonding.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME make their homes amongst the roots of trees, creating intricate burrow networks within forests. They use their sharp teeth to feast on roots and tubers in safety underground, nourishing the plant growing from their head.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME carries a horde of young Rattata on its back. The Rattata see it as their leader and fight to defend it.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME will break into restaurants during the night, raiding their kitchens for high-quality food. They carry this food on their backs, taking it back to their packs so they can feast.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME has a keen sense of hearing and can detect the wails of other Pokémon from miles away. When it sleeps, it buries itself underground and covers itself in dirt so it can't hear anything.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is a greedy, opportunistic creature. It occasionally teams up with others of its kind to steal meals from other Pokémon, but the alliance will inevitably fall apart as each tries to hoard all the food for themselves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are found in dark alleyways where they hunt. They target larger victims the hungrier they are, so are fed to deter attacks on humans.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It cuts objects and victims indiscriminately with its scissor-like incisors, which it sharpens on rocks.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is incredibly stubborn, often spending weeks trying to chew its way into people's homes with little results. Its spines contain a potent chemical that, while poisonous, has seen uses in many pharmaceuticals.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are found in landfills, scavenging for trash to eat. By flapping their wings, they can kick up whirlwinds of dust and garbage to keep predators at bay.
author: santon5512

entry: Skittish in nature, POKENAME loves to explore its area. Trainers are advised to keep stimulating toys around if seeking this Pokémon.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME reside in trash dumps, consuming massive amounts of garbage to sustain themselves. They will often fight among themselves over territory, driving out other scavengers entirely.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME crawls out once night falls in order to steal some food to ensure its survival. It is capable of carrying an entire fridge out of somebody's home.
author: over9001

entry: POKENAME haunts the dreams of many urban residents, filling them with Rattata and Raticate. These dreams revolve around stealing food from pantries. Many are convinced the dreams are real because their pantries end up pilfered.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Rattata flock to POKENAME on instinct if they sense its presence, looking up to it and following its commands. POKENAME has an honest and honorable personality, so its influence makes the Rattata more well-behaved.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME chews on rocks to find Moonstone dust deposits. While the dust is tasty, the rocks chip off part of its fangs, leaving them sharp and jagged.
author: kiwikelly

entry: This POKENAME has possessed a computer mouse. Its teeth are made of plasma, but it can still gnaw through wood with ease, much to the dismay of anyone who finds one on their desk.
author: hophoppip

entry: It sings lullabies to the moon at night. During the daytime you can hear it humming the same haunting melody.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME consumes so much cheese that its fluff has taken on the qualities of its favorite food. Though taverns have tried many methods to drive POKENAME out of the kitchen, it will always return whenever food is available.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective of its tails. Even the slightest touch triggers a vicious bite strong enough to break bones.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME may seem weak because of their size, but their bite can crush bones. Even so, they prefer not to reveal their strength to avoid scaring Pokémon around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are notorious pests that make their homes inside large blocks of cheese. They can use their strange powers to control the actions of humans.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's tails grow constantly, often getting tangled in each other. These Pokémon are extremely cunning, stalking their prey through the night before delivering a vicious bite.
author: santon5512

entry: Those who treat Rattata as friends and not pests are said to rarely be visited by POKENAME, which grants a wish for their kindness. It runs away instantly if the person tries to touch its cheese helmet, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's whiskers can somehow detect the best trees for dam building. Scientists remain baffled by the precision of its selections.
author: .izik

entry: Using its faint sense of aura, POKENAME determines whether the last person who touched its food was good or evil. It refuses to eat from wicked hands.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and notoriously shy. When spotted, they emit a sudden bright light from their bodies and flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and notoriously shy. When spotted, they emit a sudden bright light from their bodies and flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and notoriously shy. When spotted, they emit a sudden bright light from their bodies and flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is commonly found in temperate foothills, where it sings to lull other Pokémon to sleep so it can steal their food. It quickly becomes attached to anyone who gives it food, so insomniacs find it to be a good companion Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hates having to move around in its iron shell and will spend all day trying to chew through it. While keeping its teeth from growing too long, it doesn't seem to accomplish much else.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is very skittish, and will wave its tail at anything it sees as a threat. This often leads to forest fires.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME inflates itself to float over grasslands and urban areas in search of food to steal. With a healthy diet of Qualot Berries, its coat grows into a soft material that is loved for light scarves and pillowcases.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are cuddly and extremely social, building their nests close to Pokémon parks. When other Pokémon are distracted, they will gather their shed fur to add to the nest, particularly favoring Mareep wool.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME propels itself through desert sands by wiggling its tail rapidly. Its strong jaws let it chew through cacti without injury.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME echolocates with its high-pitched squeaks, which it uses to find its prey. It then takes them down with its Super Fang attack.
author: kiwikelly

entry: A wild POKENAME will follow living Rattatas, attempting to warn them of the fate it has suffered. Only the mask can be seen by these Rattatas, causing them to flee in fear.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME inadvertently lets out a bit of electricity every time it bites down on something. Though relatively harmless, enough playful or loving nips to a friend can cause uncomfortable tingling.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME chews on tough tree roots to sharpen its fang. If a root is too hard, it explodes in frustration, scattering needles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will act friendly and comfortable around a regular flock of Fletchlings, only to steal their food at the last second. This behavior showcases how it uses its mixed traits to its advantage.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME lurks near farmers markets and watches for cheese. It startles shoppers with Air Cutter, swooping in to snatch any dropped food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as roadkill to deter predators. The pattern of its faux tire marks is different for each individual, like fingerprints.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME make their homes in jewelry stores, stealing gems and jewelry to hoard in their dens. Many suspected robberies have turned out to simply be infestations of these Pokémon.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME have remarkable scent detection capable of detecting when something about a food changes, such as during fermentation. Their teeth allow them to easily break open nuts, too, so they are popular with chefs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are extremely stubborn, often getting into needless fights with wild Pokémon. They are known to be difficult to train.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME lives in frigid climates that are extremely cold and low in moisture. It collects and stores mushrooms in its burrow, which it takes care of like trophies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in large colonies deep within frozen caves. They freeze gathered berries with their icy breath to preserve them, stockpiling the frozen food inside their hidden nests.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME is considered a pest amongst gardeners as it loves to nibble on plant roots. The leaves on its head are incredibly bitter but are often chewed to help relieve toothaches.
author: mistymagius

entry: The pom-pom-like fur on POKENAME's arms smells faintly of cheese. As it cheers, tufts fall off and leave a sharp aroma drifting through the crowd.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is a common pest in cities, especially ones with an active foodie scene. Despite its unpleasant reputation, some keep it as a pet as it is not picky about its food and is emotionally affectionate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a common pest in cities, especially ones with an active foodie scene. Despite its unpleasant reputation, some keep it as a pet as it is not picky about its food and is emotionally affectionate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is made of trash and vaguely resembles the form of a Rattata. It scours dumpsters at night for discarded food. Standard Rattata form a symbiotic relationship with it, sharing food in exchange for the protection of the large Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hide within bushes during the day, only their leaves poking out to allow them to photosynthesise. At night, they scurry out in search of plant roots to chew on for the nutrients they can't get from sunlight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It produces a unique type of fruit on its head that has similar properties to cheese. The fruit is apparently delicious if you can get past its repugnant smell.
author: mistymagius

entry: The flowers on POKENAME' heads release a toxic pollen. The more trash these Pokémon consume, the more toxic their pollen will become.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME rummage through trash in search of food. While the mushrooms on their backs may look appetizing, they are extremely toxic.
author: santon5512

entry: Rattata form a symbiotic relationship with POKENAME, bringing them food in exchange for a home. The two will defend each other from any danger.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are obsessive with keeping their coats clean, spending hours every day grooming their fur. Their fur is made up of a rocky fibre and wears down their teeth rapidly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This elusive nocturnal Pokémon is incredibly tough to spot, catch, and thus, research. Because of this, scientists are divided into two camps: some believe POKENAME's wings are made of moon rock, while the others think they can be made of cheese.
author: milchik

entry: The fungus growing through these Pokémon's brains has full control of them, sending them into a constant search for food. POKENAME will often be seen walking headfirst into danger in pursuit of trash, usually failing.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp fang to loosen granite from cave walls. It then eats the exposed gems, favoring those with a bright shine.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often absorb cheese into their bodies, aging it over many years. Cheese aged by POKENAME is considered to be a delicacy in the Kalos region.
author: santon5512

entry: The more POKENAME eats, the sturdier its head gets. This is why it usually lives where food is available, whether it's on a plantation or near the bins of a restaurant.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: POKENAME are commonly used in the food industry to help with the ageing and fermentation of certain cheeses. Their back is coated in a fungus that gives dairy products a strong flavour if left in place for a long time.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Even though POKENAME are considered pest by most people, they can actually be quite helpful as they like to eat things covered in mold. Because of this however, POKENAME fur is often covered in large amounts of bacteria.
author: mistymagius

entry: The silk POKENAME produces is highly valued in textile production. Shorts woven from its silk are incredibly comfy and easy to wear, making them the preferred choice of Youngsters.
author: .izik

entry: Years ago, a world-famous animation first broke out with a cartoon starring a POKENAME. Today, that character is the mascot for one of the largest animation studios in the world.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME are found in low orbit, occasionally falling back to the surface. Their diet consists entirely of space junk, their teeth well-suited for tearing through metal.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME breeds prolifically with its colony near the granaries, drawn by the smell of food. Since it risks setting fire to the fields when it runs, farmers are always looking for ways to drive it away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME cautiously wades through trash to avoid setting it on fire. It chews on metal cans and other hard pieces of trash to trim its front teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs beneath restaurant dumpsters and chews through the metal undersides. It steals discarded food without ever fully surfacing.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME are commonly found in forest streams and lakes. They've become quite proficient at stealing bait from fishing hooks and are thus quite the nuisance to patient trainers.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME will eat just about anything, often scavenging through dumpsters for food. When threatened, they will bare their teeth in an attempt to scare predators off, though they will flee if this does not work.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME squeak with excitement whenever they manage to find food in garbage cans. If another scavenger tries to take their food, then they dart away in a zigzagging pattern.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though small, POKENAME are incredibly robust and can survive in the harshest of conditions. Its gutsy spirit means that it will try to take on the toughest foes.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: POKENAME's fangs are constantly growing, so it consumes as many hard seeds as possible to grind them down. A POKENAME hunting is a rare sight, though it is said that when it dives, its feathers unfurl to reveal beautiful wings.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: During the spring, a wild POKENAME gathers berries to attract nearby Rattata. Up to three may live comfortably within its soil-like body, using it as a moving shelter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects coins from park fountains and chews them to strengthen its fang. Some say it can bite through steel with enough training.
author: .izik

entry: The gem on POKENAME's head glows brightly when it chews on hard objects. The glow reflects its joy and satisfaction.
author: .izik

entry: To keep its migraines at bay, POKENAME must eat, which is why it always wanders frantically in search of food. Its hydrophobic fur allows it to swim for long periods while staying dry.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's wings have the appearance, scent and taste of fresh cheese. Rattata and Raticate flock to it constantly, causing it to have an attack-on-sight mentality for the sake of self-preservation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME let out high-pitched squeaks to communicate with one another. Due to their tails unfortunately resembling cheese, Rattata will often cling to and bite holes in them.
author: santon5512

entry: When someone holds food that POKENAME wants, it repeatedly rams into them with Rollout until they drop the food. Its victim can only watch helplessly while their meals are devoured by this greedy Pokémon.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME is naturally agitated and frequently chomps on its tail to hold back its rage. When it hangs from branches using its tail, it sometimes forgets and bites it anyway, falling and becoming even more enraged.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME stab their teeth into cave ceilings to latch onto them, with large groups huddling together for warmth. Their whiskers are incredibly sensitive, allowing them to sense their surroundings in order to make up for their lack of vision.
author: santon5512

entry: It will often bully other Pokémon in the area into sharing their food. If a rival encroaches on their territory, they'll try to menace each other. If neither retreats, an intense but short battle determines the victor.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME's sharp fangs can cleave through most stones. If a rock resists its bite, it flies into a rage and begins gnawing wildly until satisfied.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves playing fetch, but Trainers are warned to use durable objects. Its fang can easily destroy softer toys on the first bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur gives off a strong cheddar aroma. Because of this, packs of Rattata will often follow them, hoping to be led to food.
author: santon5512

entry: Swarms of them infest busy cities in search for food. Some regions have even started offering rewards for capturing enough of them.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME hates anything that comes within its body of water. It doesn't matter if it's food or a full-sized Trainer, it will nibble on it until it's devoured or it flees.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Their whiskers are very sensitive, able to sense their environment even while they're asleep. When they detect danger, they will teleport away in an instant.
author: santon5512

entry: It is bursting with energy and constantly seeks ways to strengthen its muscles. To test its punches, POKENAME often provokes Pokémon larger and stronger than itself, engaging in brief skirmishes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are typically found in Kalos, where they train their bodies in the southern mountains. Their keen sense of smell and taste afford them unique culinary skills, and they can even be found serving in restaurants around the world.
author: wickedwiccan

entry: It is recommended that you never disturb a POKENAME while it is eating. These Pokémon will defend their food ruthlessly, throwing punches capable of sending attackers flying.
author: santon5512

entry: It sneaks into picnics and tries to steal food, leaving a trail of acid that destroys the belongings of lots of Trainers. Its arrogant attitude has made it gain a whole club of haters.
author: epping_forest

entry: Groups of POKENAME are said to frequent sewers. Their shell makes it easy to slide through the pipes.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME will eat just about anything that will fit into its mouth, mostly so it can keep its teeth from growing too long. In desperate times however, it will start chewing on it own leaves.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME reside near crowded piers, eating discarded food that gets dropped into the ocean. These Pokémon are commonly caught by fishermen, unable to resist any bait they use.
author: santon5512

entry: Hardy and resilient, POKENAME easily scrambles across rocky terrain with its two arms. It is constantly searching for food, and is prone to lodging itself in crevasses or crags to find it.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's teeth grow rapidly, often causing discomfort. To manage this, these Pokémon eat a diet of nothing but rocks, grinding down their teeth while absorbing the minerals to toughen their skin.
author: santon5512

entry: If startled while digging through trash, POKENAME flees in panic, completely engulfed in flames. The blaze trails behind it like a comet until it calms down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an extremely lazy creature that sleeps at least 16 hours a day. To avoid fighting other Pokémon, it tends to rest hidden in small abandoned burrows dug by other Pokémon before its arrival.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Even though it was meant to be like a pest that's hard to get rid of, many Trainers have adopted POKENAME as an ideal house pet. Its soft tail and tiny ears warm the hearts of many, so they don't realize their food gets stolen at night.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME's tail is constantly in pain from the mousetrap implanted on it. It will constantly gnaw on its tail, attempting to get the trap to fall off.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME discharges strong electric pulses from its tail. The shock is powerful enough to paralyze small Pokémon and careless Trainers alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eat trash constantly, though they seem strangely attracted to cheese and can locate it from afar. Their two heads will hungrily eat while the third keeps watch for danger.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME seems to be a naturally talented cook, grabbing any ingredients it can get its hands on and making them into soups and stews. It leaks a rich oil that is full of herbs and spices.
author: mistymagius

entry: The two heads constantly fight over leftover food scraps. If they go too long without food, the heads will start chewing on each other's necks.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are skilled scavengers, seeking out dumpsters and other trash to eat. Their heads constantly fight over food, often getting tangled up in each other.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can survive in the coldest temperatures, their bodies well-suited for swimming. Their strong teeth and horns allow them to easily burrow into the bottom of icebergs, making nests inside.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME chew holes in the ice, dropping in on their prey from the surface. Their fangs grow rapidly, leaving them gnawing on icebergs when not hunting.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can commonly be found at cheese factories, as the bacteria on their bodies aid in the fermentation process. However, they have a tendency to sneak into the storage areas and eat all the cheese they can.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in the sewers, absorbing all of the nasty pathogens into its slimy body. It hates sunlight and will quickly slink back into the darkness when the sewer is opened.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's water cannons change in scent and pressure based on its diet. In the worst-case scenario, a POKENAME's Hydro Pump can blast as hard as a fire hose and smell like sewage.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME are cunning thieves, often stealing pearls from oysters. They collect anything shiny that they see, hoarding trash and trinkets in their burrows.
author: santon5512

entry: Much like the Pure Incense sold in shops, POKENAME utilize their wisps to avoid danger. Their incorporeal form also helps them escape danger by floating away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are timid creatures, breaking into houses in search of food while trying to be as quiet as possible. If caught, they will disappear immediately, often going into hiding for weeks.
author: santon5512

entry: There have been instances of POKENAME causing mass power outages by biting into electrical wires. They do this purely out of spite and malice.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Its teeth can easily bite through solid rock. It lives in extensive colonies in abandoned mines.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME love collecting shiny objects such as coins or jewelry. Using their claws, they will pickpocket unsuspecting people, stealing valuables from their purses and pockets.
author: santon5512

entry: Each of its vines end in a flower that mimics a hand. It uses these to drum on its bulb, creating a sound like bubbling water.
author: holgast

entry: It uses the hand on its tail to cling to a branch while it waits to evolve. The palm of the hand is extremely adhesive.
author: .izik

entry: It grabs petals off of flowers an uneven pattern. It methodically counts them on a tree top after it collects a handful.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a docile temperament and enjoys socializing with others. In recent years it has been taught sign language, allowing it to act as an interpreter for those who are hard of hearing.
author: mepp.

entry: It is a mischievous and playful Pokémon that seems unaware of its own strength. It will roll balls, happily gallop around, and lovingly tackle their Trainer. It uses its tail to swat away unwanted encroachers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has an extremely stretchy tongue that is shaped like a hand. It is able to extend and retract this hand at will.
author: themicelegion

entry: This form of POKENAME was specifically bred for domestication. They are commonly found in preschools as playmates for children.
author: themicelegion

entry: This breed of POKENAME has a great sense of hearing. It uses its stretchy, tendril-like arms to slap foes from a distance.
author: themicelegion

entry: It makes a very aggressive yodeling noise at night. When multiple POKENAME get together, campers will leave the forest.
author: .izik

entry: The venom in its stinger can render a human unconscious in seconds. It giggles at its foe as it gets knocked out.
author: .izik

entry: It swings the hand on its tail wildly as it eats to deter others from stealing its meal. Each swing has the power to break bones.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever it spots a Silver Razz Berry, it becomes completely fixated on it, watching it intently as it moves. This distraction makes it an easy target for a well-placed Pokéball.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It digs out a hole and covers it in branches to create its berry hoard. It will do this multiple times a day during the autumn months.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have an awe-inspiring sense of rhythm. They love to slap the palm of their tail against their stomachs, which produces a resonant thud.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flutters between blooming Nanab Trees, sipping nectar as it goes. Its tail twitches rapidly whenever it finds a particularly sweet flower.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases sticky silk from the fingerlike tips of its tail. It uses this silk to build nests and immobilize prey before approaching.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to wave to people who pass by. When it's tired in flight, it'll give itself a slight massage.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its wings are not fully grown yet, so it mainly relies on its tail and its jumping ability for traversal. They are usually seen hanging around trees of varying heights.
author: cascadeguy

entry: POKENAME's arm-like tail is incredibly sticky. It uses it while flying to snatch food away from inattentive Pokémon and Trainers.
author: projectalpha22

entry: The wool on POKENAME's body naturally smells like bananas. Just before releasing electricity, the scent strengthens to nauseating levels.
author: .izik

entry: With a simple flick of its tail, it has the ability to paralyze, poison, or cause slumber. Once it incapacitates its enemy, it steals their valuables.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travels by floating on the wind. It uses its prehensile tail to grab tasty nuts and fruits from the trees it drifts over.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME floats over the jungle canopy in search of ripe fruit. When it lands, it softens its fall with its dexterous tail.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: Through fusion, POKENAME have gained an extra hand, allowing them to swing through the trees twice as fast as a typical Aipom. Despite this, POKENAME will typically use this extra hand to carry berries or even Bounsweet as they swing.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME gathers atop Nanab Trees to feed together. If threatened, the entire group unleashes Razor Leaf in perfect unison to drive foes away.
author: .izik

entry: Submerged just below the water's surface, it lives along riverbeds where Persimmon trees grow. It works together with other POKENAME to shake down trees before sharing the fruits with each other.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives along riverbeds where Carambola trees grow, lazily meandering downstream. If it spots a particularly ripe fruit, it bounds up to shake the tree and then dives into the river to share the fruit with others.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses its large hand to steal objects that are too large or heavy for its beak. A flock can abscond with a TV or other electronics.
author: holgast

entry: It distracts its target with one head, while the other attempts to steal their food. The heads never fight, and encourage the other to do mischief.
author: pokepower

entry: The head of POKENAME is kind and gentle, but the tail is a mischievous prankster. It often chases its own tail to teach the tricky appendage a lesson.
author: evilgammon

entry: Should it become startled, an POKENAME will burst, flinging wooden spikes into the immediate area. These spikes are sharp enough to pierce metal.
author: .izik

entry: The saliva that drips from its mouth has a slight paralytic agent. Pharmacists in Orsay City are using this to create an upgraded Paralyze Heal.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME does not get its way, it slaps its hand-shaped tail against the ground in anger. It may even hurl nearby objects until it calms down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs upside-down in trees and uses its tail to stuff berries into its shell for later use. It can do this even while asleep.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME were once utilized by traveling clay merchants to pull their wagons. It can reliably carry 500 pounds without breaking a sweat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its stretchy tail to grab food from afar. Its excellent precision allows it to even steal Chansey eggs right from their pouches.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME enjoy swinging from tree branches and eating honey. Their hand at the base of their tail allows them to dexterously grab pieces of honeycomb and flee before they are stung.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fiercely guards gathered Nanab Berries with its pack. Before attacking, it barks sharply, then unleashes a Swift at foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waves its hand-shaped antlers rhythmically before striking. The motion allows it to channel psychic power and craft brief illusions.
author: .izik

entry: Aspiring, self-taught artists, POKENAME paint on rocks and trees in their tropical habitats. When they run out of paint, they travel to local towns and steal paint tubes from art supply stores, but only in reds, greens, and blues.
author: jackster

entry: POKENAME produces Nanab-scented milk that is remarkably sweet. Bakers prize it for cakes and pies. Curiously, it creates this flavor even when it has not eaten Nanab Berries.
author: .izik

entry: Despite their hands' lightweight appearance, they are very heavy. Each hand weighs more than an average-sized pickup truck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail appears to hold a lightning bolt–shaped object of great electrical power. It wields it akin to a spear, jabbing at opponents and firing electric bolts from the tip.
author: sk372

entry: Each of its many tentacles ends in a primitive yet surprisingly dextrous hand. Its uses them to swing through trees with blinding speed for its size.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME will grab anything that swims by with its opposable tentacles and will hold onto them until it is ready to eat them. If one of the tentacles is bitten off, they will grow back in about 14 days.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are active and playful. However, if they are tasked with something they don't find amusing, they become listless and lazy.
author: jreposo

entry: It is often described as laid-back, stubborn, and obssesed with bananas. There are rumours that an POKENAME Island may exist.
author: jreposo

entry: Currently classified as a Shiny form of POKENAME, this is thought by some to be its original form. Its rivalry with Cacdile dates back generations.
author: jreposo

entry: Ancient texts claim POKENAME can duplicate its hand-like limbs up to 1,000 times at once. Scholars debate these accounts, as no living witness has confirmed such displays.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME won't hesitate to drop from its perch among treetops to strike down at any intruders in its territory. The fingers of its hand-like tail have tiny points that can deliver poison to those unable to avoid its smack.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's vine-swinging hand and blade can make for a swift death in the forest. Thankfully it prefers grabbing and cutting fruits and nuts instead.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Generally found playing together in fields near woods, they scarper when they sense danger. During forest fires, they use their tail to grab young Pokémon, carrying them to safety, risking their own life to save others.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It fires sharp needles from the end of its tail. A thin metallic alloy coats its entire body, protecting it from assault.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's toothy grin is terrifying to many. Its teeth are impenetrable. All its feet are equipped to grab like a human.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's feelers become highly agile as a result of the fusion process, increasing both mobility and grip strength. It has been observed petting other living beings with its appendages as a means of calming their emotions.
author: robobunnybutt

entry: What appear to be POKENAME's fingers are actually retracted thorny whips it hides from view. Those that underestimate it will find it able to lash out with spiked vines with deadly precision.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their multiple hands to quickly swing across branches and vines. They steal berries and other items from unsuspecting Pokémon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It uses its tail to balance its flight. Should the end of the tail be injured even slightly, it will fly clumsily until it heals.
author: .izik

entry: A children's hospital's patients swear that a creepy Aipom waves at them from an open vent at night. Others report losing their vinyl glove balloons.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME are not blind, but because of the hair covering their face, they will still end up bumping into everything.
author: mystora

entry: Using the adhesive properties of its hands, it climbs the walls of homes. It peeks through windows at night, searching for prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a laid-back personality that is mistaken for indolence. It is never in a hurry to move because its tail does most of the work.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The hand on its tail flashes rapidly to distract its foe. The light from its tail can be seen from over a mile away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use the hands on their tails to secure themselves to walls of caves while they sleep. They work in packs, linking their tails together to gather and transport minerals for food.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Before attacking, the flame on POKENAME's tail takes on a hand-like shape. It burns palm-shaped prints near Apricorn Trees to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: During thunderstorms, it uses its hands to grab onto trees or other sturdy objects. Once the storm passes, it sleeps for days to refill its stamina.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seems to have decided that if they didn't have hands, they would grow them instead. They grab high-hanging berries with impish glee.
author: 22ndsolstice

entry: POKENAME gnaws into electrical cables near businesses to feed on the current. If threatened, it casts a powerful Electroweb and channels electricity through its paw-like tail to shock predators.
author: .izik

entry: Many POKENAME are smarter than humans. There are stories of ancient civilizations using POKENAME for drawing up schematics for inventions.
author: .izik

entry: It uses the hand on the end of its tongue to reel in prey. Using its large fangs, it skillfully drains the life force of its enemy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its tail-hand to prevent prey from escaping its grasp. It will then encircle and bite its opponent from behind.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME is most active at dusk and dawn. Their leaves are bitter and poisonous; those who try to feast on them are in for a nasty surprise.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Should it spot a lost traveler, it will cheer obnoxiously at them. Because of this habit, some believe that POKENAME love seeing others suffer.
author: .izik

entry: The sound of multiple flutes can be heard while an POKENAME floats. The faster it moves, the more intense of a noise can be heard.
author: .izik

entry: It uses the hand on its tail to swing from branch to branch. As it swings, it lets loose clouds of pollen into the air.
author: .izik

entry: The amnesia-inducing effects of Gloom's noxious honey have been neutralized by fusion, making POKENAME's honey theoretically safe to eat - though most say that it tastes terrible.
author: bee4082

entry: At dawn and dusk, it hoots and hollers to find its kin. It has an extra lung inside its hand-tail, letting its raucous cry go on for ages.
author: pokepower

entry: A group of POKENAME will cling together to form a simulacrum of a large cloud. The structure is then carried effortlessly along the wind.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME clambers down beaches at frightening speed thanks to its many limbs. It has been known to suddenly jump from palm trees.
author: .realthree

entry: It attacks its opponents with a flying press, then holds them in place with its tail-hand as it pummels them with punches and kicks.
author: holgast

entry: It fakes having stiff limbs, moving in an off-kilter fashion. Sudden bursts of acrobatics make it unpredictable, tripping up foes and stealing food.
author: pokepower

entry: Its body continuously produces sand from an unknown source. Glassblowers in Cerulean City utilize this glass in jewelry crafting.
author: .izik

entry: The mushrooms on its body resemble hands. When startled, it will release a purple powder that is toxic if inhaled.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME take great pride in building up their body using their singular hand. Their body usually falls apart as they flail to protect themselves.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME is incredibly popular in circus shows, supplanting Mr. Mime. It can perform many impressive feats of acrobatics and dexterity.
author: holgast

entry: Clumps of its mushroom can be used in recipes for Heal Powder. The mushroom itself smells like bananas and hand sanitizer.
author: .izik

entry: The hand-like portion of POKENAME's tail is extremely savory and used in a variety of fried dishes. It is considered a rare delicacy due to POKENAME's avoidance of humans and the speed at which they run away.
author: .izik

entry: When sleeping, POKENAME swats the hollow pumpkin-like part of its body with its tail. The eerie, bongo-like sounds echoing through pumpkin patches unsettle travelers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hypnotically waves its head, paws and tail when dormant. Along with its uncanny stare, this has lead to many considering it unnerving.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME may seem docile, but it only takes a few incendiary words to spark anger in the primate. These sudden bursts of aggressiveness make them an unpopular choice among parents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are intrepid fighters who are not afraid of getting their hands dirty with underhanded tactics. Their third hand allows them to quickly shift positions and surprise their foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It dazes other Pokémon with the pattern on its stomach, before stealing soft fruits from them like peaches or nectarines. After finishing its stolen fruit, it scurries away before the dazed Pokémon snaps out of it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its mind has the ability to do complex math without much effort. Scientists in Alola utilize it to research wormholes and other phenomena.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME were employed during the time of kingdoms to entertain royals. They were proficient in both acrobatics and feats of strength.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Its eerie smile and stare is seen as unnerving by humans. Large groups of POKENAME hang together, swaying from trees.
author: holgast

entry: It unwillingly has the ability to remotely view anyone making a joke within a 10-mile radius. Should it hear a funny joke it will laugh for hours.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its hand to grab onto live wires. It consumes large amounts of power in this way, taking out entire substations.
author: .izik

entry: The bizarre POKENAME is often mistaken for a form of Unown. Not much is known about where it comes from or how it survives in the wild.
author: bee4082

entry: An POKENAME's stick will harden after one day should it be separated from its owner. A shop in Milyfa Town sells these sticks as back scratchers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its large, tail-like appendage to latch onto unsuspecting people at night. It does not wish to do harm however, merely to frighten.
author: projectalpha22

entry: POKENAME needs lots of sunlight for the bulb on its back to grow. It searches for the best place to soak up sunlight before resting there.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to each head always being at different stages in their life cycles, a single group of POKENAME is virtually immortal. However, since only one of them is ever fully grown at a time, they are not much use in battle.
author: mistymagius

entry: In particularly sunny areas, POKENAME's heads can grow to gargantuan sized. However, if they grow too big, they will end up falling off and eventually growing into a new POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME mold tools and weapons out of mud and rock to better defend themselves; the stems sprouting from their helmets are part of their actual bodies, however. To keep themselves from being overfilled with water, they weep the excess.
author: infinex21

entry: It has a commensal relationship with the large sprout it wields; the sprout turns sunlight into nutrients that are absorbed by it. There is some debate if the relationship is symbiotic, since this Pokémon makes sure to protect the sprout from harm.
author: infinex21

entry: As POKENAME photosynthesizes, it becomes gradually stronger and faster. If without sunlight for a prolonged period of time, it will begin to lose energy, leading to its body starting to wilt.
author: evilgammon

entry: Pink plumes from a POKENAME have a signature smell -- floral, earthy, and sickly sweet. Unfortunately for POKENAME, it's highly flammable and often faints from explosions of its own making.
author: haypile

entry: Green plumes from a POKENAME smell like a novel, heady mix of garden greens and smog. Unfortunately for POKENAME, it's highly flammable and often faints from explosions of its own making.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME have special markings on their cocoon that help them blend into their surroundings. They try to remain as still as possible to avoid being detected by predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be seen happily charging and prancing about open fields in the sunlight. The moment it reaches a point where there is no sunlight however, it flops onto the ground and becomes sullen.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are so hyper that they struggle to stop running once they begin. They tend to scatter Seed Bombs from their back as they run around.
author: infinex21

entry: Its horn and crests protect the sprout emerging from its head. When this carefully-tended sprout breaks off in battle, it loses all signs of intelligence and flies into a rage.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME is known for its kind nature. It is often seen placing struggling sprouts into its pouch, tending to them until they become strong and healthy.
author: mepp.

entry: Although POKENAME's vines protect its main body from direct attacks, they still make it a target. These vines are filled with nutrition, so flying Pokémon may try to snag one. POKENAME grows weak in cold weather.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The seedling joey inside the pouch is tethered in place by roots and filaments. The last researcher who tried to separate it from the host POKENAME disappeared somewhere without ever sharing the results.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME often stay close to the surface of water and rarely dive deeper. This is to ensure they are collecting enough sunlight to sustain themselves.
author: kitarchen

entry: POKENAME shoots seeds it has collected in its mouth as a defense mechanism. It can swim through dirt as though it were water.
author: themicelegion

entry: For moves like Leech Seed, it spits seeds out of its tube-like mouth. If a Trainer asks POKENAME to use a Water-type move instead, POKENAME will usually splash them with its fan-like fin leaves in protest.
author: haypile

entry: Its petals spin in a rotating motion to help it swim gracefully up strong streams. The horn on POKENAME's forehead is its only method of defense, so it chooses to flee most battles until it evolves.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME hang from branches where plenty of sunlight shines. Their growth can get stunted if they do not receive enough sunlight, so some may opt to fall from the branches if it means reaching a sunny patch of grass.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce special seeds that quickly snap when they make contact with the ground. When faced with a predator, they can dodge attacks by snapping a short distance away with their seeds. If they run out of seeds, they are likely to be eaten.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Since Pokémon Fusion has become more commonplace, many natural conservationists have praised POKENAME's natural-born tendency to pollinate all kinds of flora, spreading pollen and seeds wherever it goes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lays flat and pretends to photosynthesize. What looks like leaves are actually highly mobile arms that fold closed around anything that gets too close.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME can stand upright on any two of its brown limbs, sometimes making it appear upside-down or sideways. It prefers drifting over walking -- its leaves provide enough surface area that it can float peacefully on the surface.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME's expression never changes, whether it's sunbathing, getting pranked, or slicing something to shreds with its scythes. Some fans find the reliability soothing, while others find POKENAME to be an unsettling pest.
author: haypile

entry: When POKENAME sways, the sprouts around its skirt open and close their cotyledons. It can move each sprout independently with psychic power to make them wave hello or ensnare a foe. There are a lot more sprouts hidden in wait under the skirt.
author: haypile

entry: Students who let POKENAME out of its Poké Ball in school get complaints from neighboring classrooms that it smells distractingly like popcorn. POKENAME keeps its shell crispy and tough by grooming itself with flame breath at a controlled temperature.
author: haypile

entry: This Pokémon is said to remain docile underneath a rural forest, absorbing its nutrients for further evolution. POKENAME attacks anything that comes near its habitat with vines and roots.
author: aquaxena

entry: Residing in large bodies of water near verdant locales, POKENAME has an ill temperament that contrasts with its cute expression. However, despite its size, it is rather weak, so its attempts at rampaging fall a bit flat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to play in rich mud and dirt, which provides them with many nutrients to absorb as well. Exposure to evolutionary stones causes their leaves to change, with the changes being more noticeable the longer their exposure.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME collects discarded microchips from city dumps and buries them in fields. These chips aid in navigation and assist it with pollination.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME falls from a tree, it always lands face-down. This is due to a unique density distribution, ensuring the sprout on its back ends up facing the sun.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME will eat anything it can get its hands on. Once it has eaten enough food to match its body weight three times over, it will bury itself in the dirt of a reclusive sunny meadow, and wait to evolve.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The seeds within their wings are filled with electricity that is generated when their bodies metabolize sunlight. They love stormy weather and will happily fly through thundering clouds.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME likes to be in the sun, so it seeks out hot, grassy plains to nest in. Seeds that fall from this Pokémon are very nutritious, and their taste is reminiscent of popcorn.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: It pollinates toxic plants using spores stored in its abdomen. The powder it scatters fertilizes soil while poisoning nearby Pokémon. Areas it inhabits grow lush and repel intruders, but prolonged exposure to its pollen can warp crops.
author: jaddies

entry: To save energy in order to hasten evolution, POKENAME rarely takes to the air and flies. It huddles together in small groups, eating nuts, berries and pine cones that fall from trees.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME erratically bounces across barren land. With each bounce, it releases a handful of native seeds from an opening in its head. In just a few days, a lush jungle starts to sprout.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME constructs large, intricate burrows in fertile ground, often interfering with farmers. It is rarely seen outside its den, as it conserves energy needed to evolve.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME take lots of naps throughout the day, as they only sleep for 10 minutes at a time before waking up. Once they awaken, they make sure they are still getting enough sunlight before falling back to sleep for another 10 minutes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their punches to make perfect holes for seeds. This efficiency has made POKENAME favored by farmers.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME are great at identifying weeds and fungi. They fly around farmsteads eliminating any plants that may threaten the farm.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME make silk webs over sunny patches to give themselves a place to soak up sunlight. When another Pokémon runs into their web, they bite down with venomous fangs to discourage the Pokémon from breaking their web in the future.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are aquatic Pokémon who use their glowing, bulb-like antennae to guide themselves through dark waters. As they mature, the tips of their antennae begin to unravel.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME bury their bodies, with their arms aboveground, to better feed on nutrients and water in the ground. If anything grabs their stems, they discharge all of their energy and black out.
author: infinex21

entry: When shooting stars fill the sky, many POKENAME appear and unfurl their leafy curls as if absorbing the light. They will not move much after the event is over, subsisting only on rain and dew until they are ready to evolve.
author: chibitales

entry: They hide in the bushes when people come nearby since they are often mistaken for berries. After people leave, they harvest different types of berries that help protect them from predators, such as the Occa Berry or Kebia Berry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although POKENAME float on the wind to spread the reach of their population, it also means they become easy pickings for Flying-type Pokémon, who adore their nutrient-filled body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME likes to plant itself in rich, fertile lands. Its compact dirt shell allows for it to relocate if the local soil has become unsuitable.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME have wool dyed with chlorophyll that gives off a yellow hue. They love to rest in the sunlight and graze in fields of grass. Their wool is made into yellow summer dresses.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are found globally and are always observed to be flying westward. Researchers have observed that they spend the morning sunning themselves and, as the sun begins to set, they will take off and fly toward it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME launches off the ground, it disperses a cloud of fertilizer that speeds up the growth of nearby plants.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME are small Pokémon that scurry across grassy plains and fields of flowers. They enjoy nibbling on leaves and petals, even though they metabolize sunlight absorbed through their leafy tails.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME swing from branch to branch with their vine-like tail. Whenever they are tired from swinging around, they find the tallest branch they can reach and soak in the sunlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through its wings, often searching for sunflower patches to find the best spot. The sprout on its head grows bigger the closer it is to evolution.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME Eggs are laid about a metre underground, then covered with earth. Newborn POKENAME emerge only after heavy rain softens the ground, allowing them to burrow up from the mud, absorbing important nutrients as they do.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are dark brown because the chlorophyll is absorbed by the seedling on their back. They fiercely protect the seedling on their back because they are unable to process nutrients if it becomes damaged.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a small seedling on their back that they share nutrients with. The seedling absorbs chlorophyll they produce from their body and leaves behind a dark brown pigment in the process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often bloated due to the nutrients they have stored within their bodies for the sake of their evolution. Their tails are like stretchy vines that they use to reach hard nuts to chew on, which help to keep their fangs sharp.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME cluster in trees on the branches facing toward the sun. They will move around the tree throughout the day, jostling for the highest position to catch the most sunlight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The wings of POKENAME are covered with a coating of chlorophyll that allows them to absorb sunlight while flying. At night, they wrap themselves in their wings to conserve energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tunnels deep underground, then it extends its steel-tough roots to the surface to absorb sunlight. Its roots are troublesome as they are difficult to remove and undermine human constructions.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are light sleepers that awaken whenever they do not feel sunlight and will quickly move to get back in the sunlight. This causes them to remain awake at night, which makes them great nighttime guards.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collects seeds in tall grass and stores them on its head. It then flies high above empty fields and distributes the seeds.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The stem on POKENAME's head is actually quite tough, being resistant to virtually any blade. It likes to sit in tall trees, absorbing sunlight through its yellow fur.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME harness the energy of the sun to gain quick reflexes, which they rely on to run past other Pokémon and steal honeycombs. During rainy seasons, they are unable to eat honey and beg for food from Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are a popular Pokémon for large garden centres thanks to their affinity for young plants. They are employed to plant seeds in nurseries, then periodically travel across the nursery beds to deposit fertile soil for the sprouting plants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME gather soil atop their back, binding it to themselves with sticky mucus. They use the soil to grow small plants. Researchers speculate that this behaviour helps them camouflage themselves and avoid predators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME love to roost in fertile soil, resting their feet within the nutritious loam whilst fanning their wings out to absorb sunlight. They take to the sky and search for shelter if it ever starts to rain.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Flocks of POKENAME often dig small holes and plant themselves into soft dirt throughout the winter, before coming back out as spring arrives. POKENAME will use the droplets of water from ice and rain to collect nutrients for their upcoming evolution.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME are capable of releasing powerful flames on a sunny day, as the power of the sun increases the temperature of their flames. The inverse occurs on rainy days, as their flames grow weak in the wet conditions.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drink and store water with their trunks, often spraying themselves or others of their kind to keep the stems on their heads nourished. Their trunks are strong enough to lift rocks as big as they are.
author: infinex21

entry: During the day, POKENAME can be found napping while upright in sunny patches of grass. At night, they get aggressive and tackle each other with their leafy antlers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trains under intense sunlight to build power. In the rain, its punches become weak unless it has trained thoroughly.
author: .izik

entry: It doesn't know it is big and poisonous. It fearfully thrashes its leaves about to scare off even small predators, which creates a haunting but iconic rattling sound.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME can be milked for a sweet sap, though only for a small amount every day. The fluid is sweetest after absorbing plenty of sunlight and nutrients, so the early morning is the best time to milk it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wander from field to field in search of the most fertile soil they can find, settling down and planting their feet in the ground when they find a suitable location. Farmers can find their crops ruined by an arriving group of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite its mischievous personality, some unconventional gardeners swear by using POKENAME as a farmhand due to its unique talents. Seeds sown by this Pokémon appear to sprout much faster than normal.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME mainly relies on sunlight and morning dew to sustain itself while it waits to evolve. POKENAME will usually find a smooth pebble and carry it wherever it goes, though it doesn't typically move far to conserve energy.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's connection to both solar power and atmospheric electricity don't serve it well. It will often fry its own leaves when emitting thunder, and it creates self-dampening interference when trying to photosynthesize.
author: haypile

entry: After storms, POKENAME will use their claws to slash branches off trees, letting rainwater fall for them to drink. Their bodies are incredibly light, letting them glide with the wind as they move.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's sweet and friendly disposition is wasted by its habit of burying itself motionless in sand all day, only leaving its head sprout above ground. On cold nights, POKENAME surfaces to collect dew on its tough skin.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME acquire energy through photosynthesis, using their leafy tails to absorb water; often enough, they absorb moisture from the ground. They often rest atop rocks bathed in warm sunlight, exuding fresh, aromatic air all around them.
author: infinex21

entry: While POKENAME's outside appearance may look like a tasty meat stick, this Pokémon has soft brown feathers and gets into trouble easily. What appears to be a bone is actually the stamen that releases heated pollen.
author: kittenthepiratekat
