entry: Wild POKENAME curl up or lay flat to disguise themselves as grass shrubs. Their claws are strong enough to dig holes big enough for them to sleep in and their grassy quills can harden for a short time to defend themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME grows seeds on its back which can be plucked out by professional gardeners. When planted, they grow into berries with a strange, bitter taste.
author: jaminmcready

entry: A timid sort, POKENAME only comes up from underground during the early mornings to take in sunlight.  On windy mornings, it extends its leaf-like tongue out as well in order to catch pollen carried by the breeze.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME enjoys spending time in the sun and is known to sunbathe for hours at a time. Its large mouth can store several liters of water, which it uses to nourish the sprout atop its head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spend hours in flower fields absorbing sunlight. Whenever it rains, they form a cup with the leaves on their back to ensure they remain properly hydrated.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have darkened pigmentation because of the seeds in their pores that grow across their entire body. These seeds absorb chlorophyll and leave behind a naturally dark brown hue.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME secrete an oily toxin through their skin that causes a nasty rash when exposed to ultraviolet frequencies. They happily laze in the sun, content to rely on their natural defences to keep themselves from being disturbed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is so fascinated by every flower it finds that it replaces the one growing on its head almost every day. It takes great care of the soil to keep its flowers healthy and can often be seen happily running through fields with its newest find.
author: jaminmcready

entry: This Pokémon frolicks and plays on bright sunny days, but digs a burrow and hides on cloudy days. Sometimes, the sprout on POKENAME's head is visible above the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tends to rest on the shores of ponds to absorb as much sunlight as possible, as it is essential for its evolution. After the sun sets, it hides underwater to avoid fighting other Pokémon and wasting energy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body consists largely of a sharpened seed. They use this edge to plant themself into the flesh of a Pokémon and take root, feeding off of its life energy until they can evolve.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Wild POKENAME absorb, filter, and disperse the very water they live and swim in. If they ever run low on nutrients, the vivid colors of their leafy bodies begin to dull.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME feels especially happy, it releases hundreds of seeds, which will eventually grow into Sunkern. In foreign regions, this behavior may introduce Sunkern as an invasive species.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The head of a POKENAME is actually its main body. Its lower body is mostly dirt and rock held together, and controlled, by their many vast and tough roots.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME only comes out in the early morning, to bask in the first rays of the sunrise for nourishment. As it photosynthesizes, it radiates a strong warmth around it that evaporates the morning dew.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to eat other plants, especially carrots, and take great care to keep their own leafy bodies clean. They will scatter thick plumes of their soft leaves to conceal themselves and flee when attacked.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME soaks up sun rays to expedite its growth. After absorbing enough solar energy, it can raise its temperature high enough to burn everything around it.
author: sly.crook

entry: Their many tails glow with the sunlight absorbed through their leafy manes. They can harness the power and heat of this sunlight to produce warm flames.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its tendrils to dig out holes in the soil to plant seeds in. It's believed that its touch manipulates the properties of the soil to perfectly adapt to the seed it plants to maximize its potential growth.
author: sk372

entry: It creates a hole in the soil and covers it with leaves to trap prey. Unfortunately, the small sprout on top of its head pokes out, leaving this tactic less effective than POKENAME realizes.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME constantly tries to keep turning, but its vines continuously get in the way. Only when the sun is at its highest point does POKENAME turn - yet it never stops smiling through the struggle.
author: misfit0521

entry: POKENAME digs itself into the ground to hide. If someone accidentally steps on its leaf, it emits a painful flame.
author: chorb33

entry: The surfaces of its eyes are always covered with a thin layer of freshwater tears, and it can cry on command to share this water with needy plants. It is covered in soft fur which is permanently marked by its dark tear trails.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME chews on small plants to gain additional nutrients separate from its photosynthesis. Once it finishes eating, its bud opens up and spreads pollen that will aid plant growth in the area.
author: sk372

entry: Its sprout grows longer if the people around it hold grudges or envy. If this sprout grows long enough, it will attempt to drag those people into sunflower fields.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: They can determine weather forecasts, planting dates, and other farming data, which has allowed them to replace the almanac. They determine this information by sinking their roots into the soil to communicate with plant-based Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME extends its body's vines underground to gather nutrients. If threatened, it shuts its eyes and explodes without warning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soar through the skies with their leafy wings, absorbing sunlight to keep themselves from tiring. Their cheerful cries at the break of dawn have long served as nature's alarm clocks for many living near forests.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its appearance, POKENAME is a very gentle creature. It has been observed spreading seeds in an effort to preserve forest habitats.
author: theartemis1

entry: The wispy wings of POKENAME gather moisture from the air as they fly from field to field. In drier months, the water collected in their wings is showered out as soft rain, helping the seeds of other Grass-types grow to adulthood.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Tiny seeds grow within the slime on POKENAME's back. These seeds are extremely bitter and are often ground into dust to make Heal Powder.
author: .izik

entry: The ooze-covered seed on POKENAME's back occasionally sprouts fragrant leaves. When dried, the leaves are used to craft inexpensive Full Incense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's slimy tail ends in a seed that absorbs sunlight as it sleeps. When angered, it channels this stored energy into a devastating Dragonbreath.
author: .izik

entry: Few things annoy a POKENAME more than being reminded it doesn't have hands. It learned to grasp with its leaves to compensate.
author: haypile

entry: By remaining in a motionless state, POKENAME absorbs and stores sunlight. It has trouble blending in with the open fields it occupies and lashes out when approached to deter further interruptions.
author: wavypavy_1

entry: The seeds on its back have sunk their taproots deep into POKENAME's main body. Attempts at removal found that each seed maintains its own separate role: the right seed is responsible for navigation, while the left is responsible for communication.
author: haypile

entry: Loyal and obedient, POKENAME makes for a good pet. Its most active in the mornings, so owners should be prepared to wake up early so it can soak in the sunrise for sustenance and energy.
author: sk372

entry: Restless Pokémon are naturally drawn to POKENAME, who happily accommodates them. A Pokémon who sleeps in the bed of grass on POKENAME's back will have wonderful dreams.
author: haypile

entry: The bed of grass on POKENAME's back is surreally soft and cool. Sleep study trials suggested that succumbing to a snooze on POKENAME's back may be good for reducing inflammation and, by extension, increasing longevity.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME grazes on wild herbs in quiet forests. If spotted, it flees at high speeds and hides inside hollow logs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends as much time in the sunlight as it can. The more solar energy it absorbs, the more pyrotechnic feats it can perform with the twigs it gathers up each day.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collect dew on their wings, which mixes with the toxic powder that their leaves produce. When provoked, they rapidly shake their wings to splash this toxic dew on foes.
author: santon5512

entry: Every POKENAME forms around a seed that it will host for its entire life. It provides the seed nutrients and the seed shares some energy created by photosynthesis. Farmers like to collect these seeds as they are very sturdy and resilient.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Its only effective defense is fire, which it can emit. However, this drains POKENAME of a lot of energy, so it usually avoids combat.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME make their homes in sunflower fields, relying on their bright yellow camouflage to keep them safe from the prying eyes of predators. They feed on the petals of sunflowers, absorbing the energy stored within them in preparation for evolution.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spend nearly their entire lives on a single flower, only ever leaving this plant if they are attacked. Their slow metabolism allows them to live subsisting only on the nectar of the flower.
author: dualblades1147

entry: POKENAME digs its way towards various sunny spots, needing large amounts of sunlight to keep its three heads energized. Grass Pokémon know that a POKENAME hole is a sign of a prime location for photosynthesis.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME requires sunlight exposure to have enough strength to glide through the air. As the sun sets, its wings begin to weaken, so it finds a safe place in tree canopies to roost until the morning.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its feline appearance, its behavior is completely Sunkern-like. It likes to stand completely still to conserve energy, and it often goes hungry because it does not recognize anything other than dew as sustenance.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME are low-maintenance Pokémon that enjoy lounging in the sun, remaining motionless save for the gentle swish of their tail. They rarely need feeding and are able to get most of their energy from the sunlight on their body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When it gets a headache, POKENAME goes outside and clears its head completely to feel better. You'll often see POKENAME standing around with a perfectly vacant stare.
author: haypile

entry: Regardless of actual gender, two POKENAME facing each other will always assume the other POKENAME is male. Female POKENAME will try to cozy up to one another, while males will try to engage in swimming competitions.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME owners are recommended to let it absorb as much morning sunlight as possible, as the solar rays keep its temper even for the day; too little light and it will throw tantrums all throughout the evening.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its size, it is very weak. It digs into soft, nutritious fields with its claws and raises its tail to gather energy for evolution.
author: chorb33

entry: Its flipper is a modified leaf. It's happiest when it can float with that leaf perpendicular to the sun.
author: haypile

entry: Its limbs are loosely attached by twined stems. If it punches too hard and loses a limb, it will simply grow that limb back.
author: haypile

entry: The swirls on its body direct the absorption of heat from sunlight. When this heat warms its muscles, POKENAME starts eagerly dishing out punches with its seed-coat-protected fists.
author: haypile

entry: Nothing pleases a POKENAME more than an all-day nap in a sunny garden. The leading hypothesis for its home gardens' vitality is that a POKENAME makes a psychic web connecting the plants, facilitating communication like a strange mycorrhizal network.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME carefully picks out prime spots to dig holes for it to place flowers and other plants into. Once planted, it stimulates the flower with its psychic powers to nurture it and help improve its future growth.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME sleeps, psychic energy manifests around it and displays the contents of its dreams. It usually dreams of the same thing it does all day -- creating gardens for younger Pokémon to enjoy.
author: haypile

entry: It lives in the same region for years. In the first year, it starts a garden from seed, using its supercomputer brain to track the soil and the needs of every individual sprout 24 hours a day. Then it slowly teaches the garden to thrive on its own.
author: haypile

entry: If it isn't getting exercise, POKENAME is basking in the sunlight, synthesizing nutrients to get even stronger. It dislikes excessively rainy or snowy days.
author: bobosmith01

entry: One of POKENAME's limbs is a growing bud. As POKENAME grows, so too does the bud. When it evolves, the bud transforms alongside it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Because it is weak and afraid of fire, seeing the flame at the end of its own tail startles it. It puts on a brave face, though.
author: haypile

entry: The more sunlight POKENAME absorbs in the morning, the more clear and refreshing the water it produces is. It enjoys spending the afternoon tending to any plants that need nourishment.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its gaping mouth to trap bugs, which slowly dissolve into nutrients that keep its sprout happy and verdant. It thinks it's friends with the bugs, but if you asked the bugs, they probably wouldn't agree.
author: haypile

entry: Its gaping mouth holds rainwater and occasionally an unfortunate bug that fell in. Brown-lipped POKENAME are found in shadier regions and have a more relaxed nature.
author: haypile

entry: Its gaping mouth holds rainwater and occasionally an unfortunate bug that fell in. Red-lipped POKENAME tend to attract more prey to dissolve in their watery depths.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME themselves aren't sure whether they'd prefer to sit in a flower box or drift like seaweed. If you peer closely through the dark sunlight absorbers on their heads, you might see they're hollow inside.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME can't use the CO2 in the water when it submerges, so it brings its own bubbles. When it breaches, it funnels surface air into its canister-like cranial terrariums while exhaling pure oxygen that can make other Pokémon dizzy.
author: haypile

entry: This fusion marks the start of a great combination in the wild. With Geodude arms, POKENAME can move to the best spot for its dew-based diet, and better hide into the ground. If attacked by a Spearow, POKENAME will punch a change of mind into it.
author: lutrax

entry: While Sundude consumes water and light, POKENAME has begun eating rocks and dirt as well in order to harden its outer shell. Most frequently, it eats spots out of hills, which is where it and its brethren will burrow for the night.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME regularly climbs to mountaintops in order to be as close as possible to the sun. This Pokémon also loves rainy days as the water drips through the cracks in its skin. As the plant system within it grows, POKENAME must shed its rocky skin.
author: lutrax

entry: POKENAME frolic in sun-kissed meadows and plains. Their gentle temperaments make them a great Pokémon for novice equestrians and children alike.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is always happy because it never feels exhaustion due to never moving, and never feels suffering thanks to only having a tiny plant brain. It coos during the rain and loves living near rivers.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME carry seedlings wherever they go in a little tote on their back. They wrap long vines around their shell to keep the tote in place as they shuffle through forests and swim in lakes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In order to take up more water, POKENAME transformed its tail into roots to reach deeper into the ground. If you need to move it, you can safely detach its tail; it can grow a new one. The detached tail may psychically mutate into its own plant.
author: haypile

entry: Its three bodies are fuzzy on top, but as hard as seed coats otherwise. The iron-rich fuzz helps it hold a charge which it utilizes to dish out electric attacks.
author: haypile

entry: The branch a POKENAME holds amplifies its power. It will try to peck anyone who wants to steal its branch, but its rounded bill doesn't hurt much worse than a rubber clog.
author: haypile

entry: The branch a POKENAME holds amplifies its power. Its goofy grin is a good indicator of its peaceful mood, until you try to steal its favorite branch, in which case its frown is reportedly unsettling.
author: haypile

entry: When one of POKENAME's heads starts doing something stupid, the other will peck its leaves in gentle warning. Since POKENAME overall isn't very bright, this makes it seem like it's constantly preening.
author: haypile

entry: One of the heads is always sleeping. It seems it doesn't get enough energy from photosynthesis to keep all three heads online at once. Its body could store lots of energy, but it uses that energy up for running as soon as it collects any.
author: haypile

entry: It loves to melt holes in cement to reach the soil underneath. Its acids and enzymes seem to be specialized for this purpose, and they hardly work at all on organic material.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME carry a seedling within their mouths and will do everything within their power to protect it. They toss yellow balls of toxic sludge towards herbivorous Pokémon to discourage them from taking a bite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME purposefully deluge the soil they carry with water to ensure that the flowers they carry can grow big and strong. The flowers spray out any excess water in powerful bursts.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME thinks it can become invisible, and often shakes its leaves to make rustling noises, pretending it's a poltergeist. Unfortunately, it's delusional -- its bright yellow coloration is always easy to see.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME prefer places that get equal sun and shade. While they often stay in one place to conserve energy, they are friendly to those who come near.
author: honestly_vitali

entry: Entire hillsides have shifted without warning when a sleeping POKENAME stirs beneath the soil. Farmers often mark its resting places, as the land left behind grows richer and more fertile each season.
author: jaminmcready

entry: A sprinkle of POKENAME's spores can put you to sleep, but people who become dependent on this sleep aid may develop uncontrollable urges to bask in sunbeams, causing sunburns. Lobbyists want to make POKENAME spores a controlled substance.
author: haypile

entry: When POKENAME isn't putting others to sleep, it's taking naps of its own. If POKENAME can't find a sunny spot, it uses its psychic powers to remove obstacles like clouds or roofs.
author: haypile

entry: The stripes on POKENAME's body distract its opponents from noticing that they're being put into a trance. Entranced people and Pokémon are then gently directed to leave POKENAME alone.
author: haypile

entry: The flower it swings like a pendulum twists too much to entrain the eye, but that's not how POKENAME hypnotizes you anyway. It's the spores you have to watch out for.
author: haypile

entry: If you've never had POKENAME meat, you may be surprised that it tastes more like a root vegetable than a crustacean. The claws grow back, but POKENAME isn't docile during harvesting -- beware its bite force.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME have a fully developed flower in the bulb on their back but are not yet mature enough to bloom. They bask in the sunlight and eat as much as they can to speed up their growth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have two main sources of food: leaves and sunlight. They often struggle to balance their diet because the places with the brightest sunlight do not have many leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Sharing sunlight as they absorb it means every flower head on POKENAME is always as vibrant and jubilant as the rest. Gifting someone a POKENAME is considered a romantic gesture in some island regions.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME gets older, its once vibrant petals will start to grow dull no matter how much sun they get. POKENAME tend to be popular gifts amongst elderly communities.
author: mistymagius

entry: One can judge the general health of POKENAME by looking at the sprout growing on its bone club. A healthy POKENAME has its sprout standing firm and tall.
author: mepp.

entry: Its long tongue is usually used to lap up water, not to fight. After taking in enough water, it will find a wide-open field and bask in the sun. The chubbier the POKENAME, the healthier it is.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The upper part of POKENAME's cocoon absorbs sunlight to fuel and hasten the evolution process. Once complete, its evolution will burst from the cocoon in an eruption of bright sunlight.
author: sk372

entry: The overgrown flower upon its head absorbs sunlight to fuel their metabolisms. This flower also obscures their sight, causing them to run about without stopping until they collide with something.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME often cause small tremors as they happily stomp about. They can fire their seed-like horns at opponents with powerful force.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME happily grows all kinds of flowers in its bushy foliage. It gives them out to Trainers to make them happy.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME thrives in sunny areas. Due to its near-boundless supply of energy and warm body, it is suspected that many microorganisms make nests under its vines and may even help POKENAME by attacking viruses.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME constantly seeks the freshest soil to fill its pouch for the sake of its child's development. Solar energy the parent absorbs will naturally filter to said soil and then be absorbed by its young.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME pokes above the water's surface and spits streams of water at the ground nearby, hoping to help plant life grow. POKENAME is at its happiest when its home is surrounded by blooming flowers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flutter through the air with their petal-like wings to find the best branches to rest in. They spend much of their day basking in the sunlight from branches high above the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are brimming with solar energy and can work long hours to help people cultivate plants. From topiary cuttings to gardens, POKENAME are a popular choice for people needing help with horticulture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME change color when exposed to lots of sunlight. Some may even burst into flames, but they enjoy this.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight and fire in equal measure for energy, the mark on its torso glowing as it does so. It can fire flames from this mark, or from the petals circling its face.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME holds a faux sun high above their head. It collects light and concentrates it perfectly down upon their head.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME enjoys wide open, sunlit fields to run around in, and maintains a relatively easy disposition among humans. The only time it gets aggressive is when butting heads over a prime spot for absorbing sunlight with a rival POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: These Pokémon live within lush forests or jungles, coiled around themselves with grass flowers growing all around them. When the sun is covered by clouds, they fly into a thrashing rage.
author: infinex21

entry: Their tail leaves change when they are exposed to specific evolutionary stones. Wild POKENAME are a common sight in open fields, gardens, and farmlands. They will go wherever they can find rich nutrients and bathe in bright sunlight.
author: infinex21

entry: Water is absorbed and stored with the large leaves at the tips of their tails. Their green hides glisten with the stored water that they secrete like sweat. POKENAME love to float in water when the sun is shining bright.
author: infinex21

entry: They metabolize sunlight to acquire nutrients and to generate electricity, which is stored in their vibrantly yellow petals. POKENAME petals are used in many anti-paralytic remedies and in some medicinal stimulants.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have leafy bodies that are soft, warm, and lined with myriad seeds. When their tail-like buds open, they scatter seeds and reveal a gentle flame within.
author: infinex21

entry: While inhabiting a computer, POKENAME can keep it powered by sunlight alone. During this time, it emits a gentle floral aroma.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather in large groups on sunny beaches to rest. The large shell on its back can take in sunlight and release it in a powerful Solar Beam if it feels threatened.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME bears an ancient shell that radiates sunlight. It brings life to barren lands, revitalizing ecosystems with its solar energy.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time basking in the sunlight in large fields. It is hardly ever seen on cloudy days.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME will only eat a peeled courgette, slurping it slowly into its mouth like a noodle. If given an unpeeled one, it tosses it aside with a dramatic sigh.
author: jaminmcready

entry: As winter turns to spring, POKENAME is said to fly by, taking the snow with it as the first flowers bloom. It lives in cold areas that nevertheless have plenty of sunlight.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME photosynthesizes its energy from the sun, and its large body requires a lot. This leads them to flock together and follow the sun, and most wild POKENAME have never been in darkness.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: On cloudy days, POKENAME surrounds itself with a mystical aura to clear the skies and let in the sun. Farmers have long regarded the presence of this Pokémon as a sign of a plentiful harvest.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are cheery Pokémon who love to bask in the summer sun. Its nutrient-rich scales can help plants grow when they fall off.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME converts solar power into psychic energy. This causes it pain, making it easily irritated.
author: ohok3441

entry: This rare fusion is only seen on bright summer days. When POKENAME floats high in the sky, it absorbs enough solar energy to appear as a second sun to observers below.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME stores excess solar energy from photosynthesis in the flower on its head. It is a very positive Pokémon and seems to be especially cheery on sunny days.
author: mistymagius

entry: During the spring and summer months, POKENAME release a calming aroma that energize the weary and calm the anxious. Shedded petals from POKENAME have been used in expensive perfume brands.
author: greaterjagras

entry: POKENAME drifts through swamps camouflaged as lily pads and allows other Pokémon to rest on its back. When someone threatens its home, it bursts from the water, clamps its jaws on the threat, and "death rolls" them under the water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It stands motionless in sunflower fields, camouflaging seamlessly with the flora to avoid predators. Should POKENAME be spotted, it bounces away at high speeds.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are often underestimated by Trainers and Pokémon. They use this to their advantage, unleashing attacks while their enemy's guard is down.
author: dicedragon20

entry: When needing to go deep into thought, POKENAME will position itself directly at the sun to maximize its thinking power. However, if this mental focus continues on past sunset, it will lose all train of thought and must start over the next day.
author: soup1900

entry: When POKENAME takes flight with its leafy wings, it moves without making a sound. It only moves when the sun is shining, using its light as a source of power to move more nimbly.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have the ability to fire seeds from their arms like cannons. They fly above farmsteads, firing at anything that may be a threat to the crops.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME flies up high for most of the day, absorbing sunlight into its four wings.  Once it has absorbed enough, it can shine the petals on its wings brightly and share the sunlight with flowers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have bright chartreuse wings that maximize the solar energy they collect while flying. When injured, they crawl to sunny spots under a leafy canopy to quickly recover.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME walk along the seabed, their flower-like antennae shining brightly even in deep waters. Although their light looks to be sunlight at first, they are actually produced by the strong electricity flowing within their bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live in open fields amidst flowers, with their own faces and petals always aimed toward the sun. They are considered very aloof and discharge their own energy when startled.
author: infinex21

entry: The many grass-like feathers of a POKENAME are renowned for their curative properties due to the rich nutrients they contain. However, if one is picked before it is shed, it will nearly instantly wilt.
author: infinex21

entry: When bright sunlight shines down on POKENAME, the heat energy makes its flower spin, lifting it straight into the air. It is said that the feeling it experiences at these times is pure joy.
author: stevethebarbarian

entry: From dawn to dusk, POKENAME rides the winds across the region, absorbing as much sunlight as it can. It spreads this energy into all flowers it comes across, helping them thrive.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Although wild POKENAME can easily blend in with flowers, they are so skittish that they will quickly flee if anything gets close to them. The petals around their heads glow faintly during the day.
author: infinex21

entry: Energy from the sun is absorbed in enormous quantities from POKENAME, allowing it to transfer that energy to any nearby organism. Farmers welcome this Pokémon into their fields with open arms, as they view it as a blessing.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME's head grows rapidly as it absorbs solar energy, but its body lags behind. As a result, it is often seen shuffling along in a heap, struggling to support the weight of its oversized head.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's head grows rapidly as it absorbs solar energy, but its body lags behind. As a result, it is often seen shuffling along in a heap, struggling to support the weight of its oversized head.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The main body tries to be serious, while the Sunflora on its back is always smiling and chipper as it absorbs sunlight. Often the Sunflora will prod and poke the body in order to get it to crack a smile, which it rarely does.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME favor hard nuts and tree bark as food. They burrow their tails into the ground to absorb water and nutrients while also absorbing sunlight through their petals.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME keeps its shell closed at night but opens it during the day to soak up sunlight. Once it absorbs enough light, it explodes and scatters seeds that propagate into enormous flower patches in an instant.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME bounds about in sunny groves, smearing sap from one tree to the next to share it with others. It detests using its horn in self-defense, as it messes up the arrangement of leaves surrounding it.
author: sk372

entry: They produce a sweet nectar from their face and lick the liquid that drips onto their paws. It is known to chase after sunlight and stops producing nectar at night.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are content to spend most of the day lazing in the sunlight, only moving periodically to ensure their flower is still facing toward the light. They grow more active at night, seeking out mineral rich rocks to feed on to nurture their soil.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live on the flanks of dormant volcanoes, feeding on tuff deposits to strengthen their shells. The high mineral content of their shells makes them ideal for new plant life to sprout, with clusters of POKENAME looking like moving meadows.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Ironically, POKENAME gain energy from lunar radiation and each night find a new clearing to bask in the moonlight. By sunrise, they have stored enough energy to scare off threats with Fire Blast.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME greets computer users with a bright expression and a cheery disposition. Many believe something sinister and soulless lies behind the smile, though most have determined the belief to be simply paranoid rumors.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers energy by absorbing digitally-written information and lines of code in computers, a process called codexynthesis. This process must be watched over, as there are well-known cases of POKENAME's personality turning misanthropic.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME can be found galloping across grassy meadows in the daylight, always facing towards the sun. Those who stare into POKENAME's face for too long go blind for a few hours before their vision gradually returns.
author: andromeda102037

entry: POKENAME often accompany the lonely and sad through their darkest times. Their paintings are said to bring color back into one's life.
author: inksans201x

entry: POKENAME are often seen in groups, spinning together, converting sunlight into energy. They move in herds in search of more sunlight, sharing energy with one another. When night falls, they close their petals and root themselves in the ground.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME is a very jubilant serpent Pokémon always searching for heat sources, particularly sunlight. When sunlight is not easily available, it will coil around nearby people or Pokémon, embracing them tightly to share in their warmth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drink water through their leafy vines, capable of filtering out any pollutants. Their grassy manes are often shimmering from how well-nourished and watered they are.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME picks out sunny spots to bask in, the sunlight helping to strengthen its shell as well as expedite its evolution. The brighter and warmer the day, the bigger the joyous smile on POKENAME's face.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are most often seen outside their mountain dwellings, absorbing massive amounts of sunlight. Many carve holes in the walls of the mountains so that even within the caverns, there are still spots to bask in the sun's rays.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's happy disposition and adorable features have garnered it quite a positive reputation among pet owners. Some regions even hold beauty competitions solely featuring POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have rocky lower halves reminiscent of a Bonsly. Their lower halves are like pots that store water to keep their grassy upper halves from drying out.
author: infinex21

entry: Its bright, yellow petals contain its electricity and are shed when it stores too much. Although it becomes more aggressive while waiting for its petals to regrow, these petals are valuable for many people.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is usually seen sitting among large flower gardens, singing and snacking on the plants around it. Though almost always keeping a sunny disposition, it starts crying once it's eaten all the flowers nearby.
author: sk372

entry: It shoots fennel seeds from its arm cannon by accelerating growth in its microbiome. It absorbs sunlight to produce a batch of seeds before releasing a flurry of them toward its opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: According to folklore, spotting this Pokémon in the sky brings a year of good fortune. When the sun shines, POKENAME can fly for hours without tiring.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME always has a gaping smile on its face. Some people find this smile quite sinister. The pollen it creates can make anyone sneeze.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME make for popular companions for farmers due to their habits of hopping up to the highest point they can reach and chirping when they see the sun. They shake their petals about to scatter embers, absorbing light for energy to grow.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME stands guard over cornfields, chasing off intruders with powerful kicks. The sunlight gives it tremendous strength, and it must run all day to burn off its excess energy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is always up for a dance, moving more vibrantly the more direct sunlight is upon it. Other POKENAME are compelled to join in if nearby, forming entire troupes of smiling, blissful dancers.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME tend to vast gardens of flowers and other plants, their expansive flower-like skirts capable of scattering nutrient-rich pollen whenever they unfurl. They can condense stored solar energy into powerful attacks to protect their gardens.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME gather on sunny days to pair off and spar with each other, making sure to respect their opponent with honorable practices. This valor has been highly prized historically, with artwork of POKENAME appearing in medieval manuscripts.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME hide amongst other Sunflora, slowly draining their energy while they're unaware. Despite this, they are still very friendly to everyone.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME shimmer in sunlight with their goldenrod petals and sit atop hills to gain and store lots of solar energy. At dusk, they release the stored solar power with a beam of light that is shot into the sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Families of POKENAME cluster together in the early morning before sunrise, facing toward the East to wait for the first rays. They spend the first half of the day basking together, using the energy from the light to synthesise toxins in their spines.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses the false flower on the back of its head to lure in unsuspecting insect Pokémon near. The flower expels a stunning poison on the victim, leaving them helpless to resist becoming POKENAME's prey.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is always smiling and dancing on sunny days. It lives in meadows and drags itself along by its powerful roots to find good spots to sunbathe.
author: michaelkai

entry: Though quite powerful, POKENAME are friendly and docile, spending their days lazing among verdant flowerbeds. Being offered one of their shed petals is considered a sign of a prosperous future in some regions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its skull as protection for its vital organs. The main body can only be defeated once the skull underneath is destroyed.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME always faces toward the sun, using its innate magnetic powers to track the direction of the sun even at night. It makes for an excellent garden companion as it will carry plants with it as it follows the sunlight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In order to make seeds that will grow into the next generation of POKENAME, they must steal a plant and hijack its biology to grow a baby POKENAME instead. All of the life energy of the plant and the parent is spent in this process.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME were loyal to ancient people who shared a love for the sun. POKENAME continue to guard what remains of their temples.
author: _testrun_

entry: During particularly sunny days, POKENAME enjoys gliding over open fields, scattering the pollen produced by the flower on its tail. The more sunlight its petals absorb, the more energized and lively this Pokémon becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The more sunlight its petals absorb, the more energized and lively this Pokémon becomes. On cloudy days, however, POKENAME tends to grow extremely irritable and may drive away anyone who approaches too closely with powerful swings of its tail.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often sleep during the day, their heads bobbing on the surface of their lake homes as they absorb sunlight. Their bouquet-like tails sprout new flowers the older they become and are often trimmed and used as presents between human lovers.
author: infinex21

entry: During the day, POKENAME is constantly rotating so at least one of its heads is always facing the sun. At night it goes dormant, converting the energy generated from rotating into nutrients to sustain itself.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME photosynthesizes, it releases an aroma similar to honey. Many Trainers report being attacked by Ursaring when traveling with this Pokémon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The long, sharp-looking leaves at its side conceal rock-hard claws. Its petals absorb sunlight that its body turns into energy, which is often stored within its two horns. It can release precise, albeit weaker, Solar Beams from its horns.
author: infinex21

entry: While quite charming, It is often prone to mischief. Even when gravely injured, the smile on its face never falters.
author: inksans201x

entry: POKENAME's head constantly emits radiant light. Staring into it for too long mesmerizes anyone. After minutes of looking at it, people fall into a deep sleep while standing.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME takes to the sky at sunrise, following the sun from east to west on its daily journey. It comes back to the ground at sunset, resting throughout the night until it repeats the cycle on the next day.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Even in combat, a POKENAME will always orient itself towards the sun. It can fight opponents in any direction without turning its body.
author: staghorn

entry: It gains its energy from the sunflower on its head. It regularly sheds the nutrient-dense seeds on its tail, which can be roasted into a salty snack.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a sunflower to blend seamlessly into fields and gardens. If spotted by a predator, it reveals its hidden wings and takes off at incredible speeds.
author: rakunk

entry: During the day, POKENAME gathers sunlight with its leaves and converts it into energy, storing it in the abdomen. When the sun goes down, POKENAME uses this energy to cover large distances with blinding speed and spread its seeds everywhere it flies.
author: milchik

entry: Due to fusion, it becomes gleeful and forgiving during the day. At night, its buried grudges resurface, resuming its search for vengeance.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The gel that coats its body is amazing at photosynthesis, producing enough energy in an hour to last it two days. Scientists think the gel could be useful in creating high-tech solar panels.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are very friendly Pokémon that love to bathe in sunlight as the petals around their heads drink it in. They can create weak balls of bright, yellow flames and play with them often.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME fashions a disguise in an attempt to join Sunflora in the wild and bask in the sunlight. Unfortunately, its disguise becomes dry and brittle quickly, falling apart from the heat and requiring constant repairs.
author: sk372

entry: The more sunlight POKENAME absorbs during the day, the brighter its wings glow and the more cheerful its smile gets. With enough sun energy accumulated, this Pokémon can illuminate an entire flower field akin to a small sun.
author: milchik

entry: With POKENAME's psychic powers, it is capable of understanding human speech. It is seen endlessly flying towards the direction of the sun.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is often found in lush fields, basking in the sun. Although docile, POKENAME will viciously attack those who disturb its peace.
author: thropp

entry: The high amounts of sunlight it absorbs during the day allows it to continue to be extremely active during the night as well. A sleeping POKENAME is one that has been dangerously deprived of sunlight.
author: sk372

entry: Always following the sun, POKENAME marches from east to west every day, powering up its body. When the sun sets, it uses Will-o'-Wisp in whatever direction it happens to be facing. Plants in its vicinity seem to grow especially fast.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME photosynthesizes sunlight for energy and releases oxygen and a mysterious gaseous substance as byproduct that brings contentedness and happiness to those that inhale it. Strong gusts of winds blow them away, however.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though POKENAME's rugged steel frame appears solid, it is actually composed of soft plant fibers that efficiently absorb sunlight. It is renowned for using Sunny Day to transform fields of flower buds into vibrant seas of blooming color.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: At night, POKENAME's bottom head roams to find damp mud to absorb nutrients through their roots. When the sun rises, POKENAME's flower head finds sunny patches of land to absorb sunlight from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are energetic creatures that love to run around as they absorb sunlight, but are sad on days that are cloudy or rainy. Scientists are currently studying the effects of seasonal affective disorder on wild Pokémon like POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have pores across their entire body that store seeds. These seeds produce chlorophyll that tints their skin a chartreuse color while POKENAME bask in the sunlight to gain energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although POKENAME always emits a small flame from its tail, its body is flammable. It is always careful not to ignite itself when attacking.
author: chorb33

entry: The seeds that POKENAME drop cause those who eat them to become bitter and hateful. If you roast these seeds, they lose this attribute.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME rests in a static location to absorb nutrients and sunlight. Gardeners have a difficult time removing it from their gardens because of its tough barbs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon photosynthesizes constantly to produce electrical energy. Stepping on one will release a flood of potent electric spores that can even cause paralysis.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME cheerfully strolls around the forest without a care in the world, absorbing sunlight with its flower. However, if you try to wake it while it's sleeping, it will fly into a rampage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lies in large flower fields, its tail outstretched in wait for a Pokémon to come by. Once a pollinator lands on a flower, it secures a meal.
author: mundane_frog

entry: This duo of Sunflora and Oddish delight in each other's company; POKENAME is never seen without a smile on both faces. They march together beneath the sunlight, singing a happy duet together.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME dances, dormant seeds beneath the soil begin to stir and bloom as if cheering it on. Entire hillsides have burst into color from a single performance, leaving behind trails of wildflowers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME often take up the role of protector to entire fields of Sunflora. Any intruders will soon fall under a deadly and incurable curse.
author: cristata

entry: Their wings get larger and larger as they photosynthesize. POKENAME evolve when they reach their maximum wingspan. Oddly, their feathers have a strong and particular fragrance reminiscent of vegetable oil.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tend to be extremely rare in the wild. They radiate a special energy that causes plants to grow and others to feel overjoyed. However, such constant and intense energy output results in most wild POKENAME passing away in mere days.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wings are truly spectacular. Its fluffy wings are actually tipped with special pods that, after floating to the ground, seed themselves into the soil and bud into newborn chicks following the winter season.
author: chiari_queen

entry: POKENAME thrives at the base of mountains where flower fields bloom in the sunlight. POKENAME replaces broken pieces of its body with surrounding stones and secures them with vines that grow along its frame.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Vegetation took over an empty steel shell, resulting in this Pokémon. Mechanical sounds can be heard from it during strong sunlight.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME loves to strike poses dramatically with the sun behind it before leaping into battle. The more it is allowed to bask in the sun before a fight, the more bombastic its moves become.
author: sk372

entry: Inhabiting southern tropical areas heavy with sunlight, POKENAME is a friendly and gentle giant of a Pokémon. When it opens its frill fully, it generates a warm light akin to the sun's rays for others to bask in.
author: sk372

entry: As long as it receives sunlight, POKENAME is always very nice and friendly. However, as soon as night turns, its demeanor turns violent and angry, lashing out its frustration by using Razor Leaf against objects.
author: soup1900

entry: Known as 'Devourer of the Sun' in ancient myths, POKENAME reflects sunlight off its body as it blots the sun, causing floral mutations and anomalies to sprout from all living beings near it.
author: beatdoof

entry: These Pokémon lay in great, open fields for most of their lives as they bask in the sunlight cast upon them. When they get up to dance away their excess energy, they also scatter around countless seeds that become fields of beautiful flowers.
author: infinex21

entry: Often nicknamed 'Gentle Giant', smaller Pokémon tend to follow POKENAME around for their friendship and protection. Wherever it travels, entire ecosystems and flower fields sprout in its place.
author: rakunk

entry: Its umbrella-shaped leaf is capable of storing a massive amount of luminous energy, which is subsequently released in the form of flames. It also uses it to cover itself from bad weather.
author: tioghi

entry: POKENAME releases puffs of steam from its shell that both regulate its body temperature and purify the air around it. The sunflowers blooming on its back track the sun's movement across the sky throughout the day, closing when night falls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Because of how fragile its leaf-like wings are, it only takes flight when the weather is clear. It prefers to walk on the ground most of the time, its feet drawing water and nutrients from the soil beneath.
author: mistymagius

entry: An unattended POKENAME will run after the sun twice daily, at sunrise and sunset. Trainers often have to track them back down by following the sound of their joyous song.
author: danarchosyndacalist

entry: POKENAME will often sit in other people's gardens, cheerfully absorbing sunlight. While some people see POKENAME as a nuisance, others welcome their positive attitude with open arms.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stands rigidly in forests or fields and absorbs sunlight. If an enemy approaches, it launches fire that has been known to light forest fires.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME produces leaves that are harvested for its ability to neutralize stomach acid, which helps with acid reflux. It requires lots of sunlight and plenty of clean water to sprout big leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dances in place happily, and behaves as if it considers everyone its best friend. Some say it houses a much darker personality lurking just beneath its smiling face.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often finds its way into urban gardens, making its home within the soft soil. Because of its friendly personality and cute appearance, many residents wind up adopting it and letting it live there permanently.
author: sk372

entry: Prides of POKENAME prowl through flower fields, amusing themselves by chasing after one another's tails. They form tight-knit families through this play, happily sitting together afterward and facing toward the sun to absorb its energy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It tries to remain in sunlight for as long as possible. This is because it begins suffering intense headaches the moment it no longer feels sunlight on its skin.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME require specific levels of sunlight for their mental function. Too little light causes them to fall asleep from lack of energy, too much causes them headaches as they photosynthesise too much sugar.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A POKENAME absorbs large amounts of sunlight even as it dashes quickly through grassy fields, often seen as a mere blur of yellow and green due to the speeds it can reach. Its grassy fur is extremely warm to the touch.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME constantly absorbs solar energy. Once it has collected enough, it can ignite entire firestorms. But it has to be wary of its flammable body.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME enjoy basking in the sunlight but are often interrupted by predators looking for an easy meal. Thankfully, not only does their shell cushion attacks from predators, but it also allows them to continue to photosynthesize to a limited degree.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME thrive on sunlight, their slender bodies growing longer the more sun exposure they get. During the summer month, sunflower oil will start dripping out of their mouths.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME takes food scraps and rotten produce and converts them into mulch inside its stomach. By resting in bright sunlight, it accelerates the rate at which the mulch is produced.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During the day, POKENAME climbs to the tops of mountains to absorb sunlight. At night, this Pokémon digs shallow burrows to rest, and while sleeping in said burrows, it appears to casual bystanders as just a simple rock.
author: lutrax

entry: If you happen to be on the peak of a mountain during a sunny afternoon, you could see a myriad of POKENAME enjoying the sunlight; however, be careful when climbing in the evening, as during that time herds of POKENAME may be rolling down carefree.
author: lutrax

entry: POKENAME devours nutritious soil in order to stay healthy. Excess energy is used to repair and replace rocks on its body. Some POKENAME have been seen creating compost piles in the wild.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME used to be a popular Pokémon racing breed. However since its speed depended on the sun, it was deemed too unreliable.
author: codewolfie

entry: This Pokémon lazes by sunny riverbeds, happily swirling its tail in the water and taking in the sunlight. Some have described it as being the pinnacle of blissful ignorance.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever POKENAME need special nutrients that cannot be made with photosynthesis, they search for berries to add to their meals. They often go after berries that have fallen into the water as they are easy to swim to.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs light through its sunflower stalk throughout the day. When threatened, it redirects the stored energy into sharp beams that can startle or repel predators.
author: ilija09

entry: It runs across the land at high speeds during the day, keeping its heads in the sunlight for as long as possible. Only when the sun is hidden does it finally stop moving and rest, until it detects the next ray of sunshine.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to laze on cold surfaces due to how warm their bodies get as they absorb sunlight. When they clap their leaves together or their tail against the ground, they scatter small leaves and petals from their bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's sludge-like substance is actually a concentration of sap and pollen. Allergists make medicine out of the substance to help with people's springtime hay fever.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME gather soil in the pipes extending from their shell, growing vines in the safety of their body. When two POKENAME meet, they exchange seeds to share plant species and try growing new plants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spends its day planting seeds wherever it can. The most beautiful gardens are said to be around areas where this Pokémon gathers.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME spends its day planting seeds wherever it can. The most beautiful gardens are said to be around areas where this Pokémon gathers.
author: noel5229

entry: Despite their wings, POKENAME are flightless Pokémon. They use their wings to communicate with one another through dense forests, the trees filled with loud buzzing through the summer months.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It is said that it evolves when it is able to sustain supersonic speeds for long periods of time, which is why it is given unnecessary X Speed boosters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each portion of its body flies in a fixed pattern. It coordinates flight patterns each night before it falls asleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can vibrate the bone it carries to mimic the sounds of a Yanma's beating wings. Yanma often respond to the sound like an emergency call, flying in to keep POKENAME safe from harm.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its keen eyesight and aerial maneuverability to ensure its devastating blows connect with its opponent.
author: grayslashjay_8566

entry: Its wings allow it to to escape from danger with ease. Its eyes can detect even the swiftest of movements.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are skilled at capturing prey much larger than themselves. By pretending to be unaware, they lure in would-be predators before capturing them with invisible walls created by their vibrating wings.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME fly just above the surface of the water, struggling to lift their body with their small wings. Even a small ripple in the water can send them off-balance and send them splashing down.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME crawl across the forest floor with amazing speed in search of the tastiest leaves. They rarely use the venomous stinger on their head because they can always make a speedy escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With 360-degree vision, those that try to sneak up on POKENAME will find it transforming to defend itself before they even get close. It typically excludes changing its eyes during transformation, so that it may retain its vision as a precaution.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its developing body being restrained by its cocoon, POKENAME can still actively avoid danger thanks to its light weight and strong wings. Its wings never stop moving until evolution is finished.
author: sk372

entry: It lets out a high-pitched shriek when the sun goes down. The sound is loud enough to cause the water on a pond to ripple.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather in large swarms once the sun sets, buzzing their wings in harmony with each other. The vibrations from all their wings can cause an entire house to shake.
author: mistymagius

entry: With Yanma's 360-degree vision and Noctowl's 180-degree head rotation and acute night vision, no attack can take it by surprise.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME's feathers are made of a thin chitin, creating a crackling sound as it flies. Its Bug Buzz is strong enough to break apart boulders, making it a powerful force when needed.
author: .izik

entry: It can be seen flying in a zigzag pattern all across lakes. The beats of its wings generate a plethora of static electricity, which it uses in battle.
author: schwaus

entry: Too heavy to fly, POKENAME use their wings to charge up static electricity and shoot shock waves as its main form of attack.
author: t.i.a.

entry: POKENAME fly so quickly that most only see streaks of the light produced by the orb on their tail. They flutter their wings at increasing speeds to generate electricity within themselves before they take off in search of food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's wings only allow it to maintain flight for a few minutes at a time. It typically lets the wind carry it instead, using its wings to adjust its flight path slightly.
author: sk372

entry: Quick fliers with superb senses of sight and hearing, POKENAME are experts at stealing food. One need only look away for a moment, and it will have snatched a new meal from them with hardly a sound.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can move at incredible speeds thanks to the constant flapping of its four wings. Its tail has prehensile properties and can grasp fruit or other objects, which it then carries safely back to its nest.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The wings atop POKENAME's head spin like a rotor. By day, it rests in sunlit clearings; at night, it buries its face in mud to absorb nutrients.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have an unparalleled field of vision, making it very hard to sneak up on them. Historically, rural communities would use them as scouts and alongside guards, as POKENAME are quick to alert their Trainers if anything is amiss.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME makes extremely precise movements with its wings and can fly through gaps no wider than its body by folding its wings down as it passes through. POKENAME shows are held during Kanto winters with Trainers from all regions travelling to them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its body is too stocky for its wings to lift it, so POKENAME uses them only to produce powerful buzzing sounds. To shield itself from the sun, it rolls in mud, keeping its skin cool and moist.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's keen vision and amazing speed allows it to effortlessly take down prey. It's commonly seen hunting after the sun sets.
author: mepp.

entry: It does laps around local landmarks to time itself and improve its speed. It will make a minimum of 50 flights per day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME whir their wings to pump air inside of their bulbs, keeping the opening closed as they build up the internal pressure. When they are ready to release seeds they launch them using the stored pressure, able to fling their seeds many metres.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's goggle-like eyes allow it to see clearly beneath the water's surface. It dives from the sky with precision to catch its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travel in thick swarms, working together to take down larger prey. They latch on with their pinchers at their base and buzz their wings in unison, lifting things much larger than themselves.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME skims the water's surface at high speed. If anyone approaches its nest, it crashes into them and self-destructs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can adjust their trajectory in an instant, so they not only rarely crash but they also rarely lose a foe they are tracking. A flock of POKENAME will use their cries to warn one another of danger and to coordinate their quick attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its 360-degree vision, POKENAME possesses a fragile constitution. Still, it maintains composure in the face of danger.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME uses its high speed and sharp claws to effectively raid Beedrill nests for their honey. However, if another POKENAME tries to raid the same nest, they will end up fighting with each other instead.
author: mistymagius

entry: Courageous little thrill-seekers, POKENAME enjoy pushing the limits of what their aerial capabilities can do. A favored exercise is leaping from tall mountains and free-falling to see how close they can come to impact before flying off.
author: sk372

entry: It constricts its body around prey hard enough to break bones. Should it notice an enemy nearby, it will fly away with the prey still imprisoned.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's impressive field of vision is restricted by their bulk, and they get incredibly frustrated by things surprising them. They deal with their frustration by ramming their tusks into nearby trees, disrupting treetop Pokémon constantly.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME speeds across marshes with unmatched agility. When it spots prey, it delivers a midair punch with astonishing force.
author: .izik

entry: The sound of crackling static can be heard when POKENAME flutters its wings. Catching one can prove difficult, as it moves sporadically and can paralyze others on contact.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The flames within POKENAME's body intensify as it flies. Its glowing body leaves behind a faint trail of heat in the air.
author: .izik

entry: The flap of its wings can electrocute other bug Pokémon it flies by. Large groupings of POKENAME create elaborate lightshows at dusk.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME flies so fast that time slows down around it. Because of this, POKENAME's lifespan is about 50 percent longer than other Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: From POKENAME's tail and fluttering wings, unpredictable sparks are formed. POKENAME has incredible vision and can easily snipe faraway targets with electricity.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME break into the winter stores of Rattata and gorge themselves on berries. Unfortunately, they stuff themselves so full that their small wings cannot get their rotund little bodies off the ground.
author: vic1312

entry: Flitting among the treetops, POKENAME feed on the new growth of trees to supplement their photosynthesis. Their speed is unmatched, and they delight in chasing other canopy-dwelling Pokémon.
author: vic1312

entry: It uses the wings sprouting from its forearms to glide as it jumps from branch to branch within the forests where it lives. POKENAME has 360° vision, allowing it to effortlessly spot any type of threat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is driven by a strong desire to help others. Though it has great potential, it doesn't know how to tap into this power.
author: jackythewannabe

entry: POKENAME blast through the air at high speed, flying over the marshes they call home. They frighten smaller Pokémon from within the marsh grass, flushing them out into the open and descending in a vicious fervor.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time hunting for berries, having a particular interest in Salac Berries. They make their nests in hollow trees, filling them to the brim with as many berries as they can find.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME aggressively flap their wings to warn humans of danger. Unfortunately, they're too tiny for Trainers to hear them.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Living along lakes, POKENAME will buzz around fruiting plants to eat. Their eyes allow them to see approaching threats 360° around them.
author: melodydelune

entry: A hive grows on POKENAME's back, which migratory Yanma instinctively use to rest within while journeying. Its underbelly glows to signal a safe haven to nocturnal Bug-type Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This heroic Pokémon is always on the lookout for danger with its keen, insectoid eyes. When it senses an enemy, it poises to strike.
author: havic0970

entry: POKENAME is unable to walk, but is a masterful flyer and swimmer. It spends most of its time in the shallows, hunting small insects and crustaceans, and avoids predators by darting in and out of the water.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite being able to fly in any direction, POKENAME will always be facing north. It likes to fly as fast as it can, knocking out any bird Pokémon in its path.
author: mistymagius

entry: When it frantically beats its wings, it can disorient the Pokémon around it, leaving them vulnerable to precise strikes from its blade. POKENAME typically inhabits the heart of dense forests and thick jungles, where sunlight struggles to penetrate.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME love to race against each other, preferring to stay grounded than to use their powerful wings. Instead, they use them to create damaging shockwaves that are strong enough to smash bulletproof glass.
author: mistymagius

entry: While flying through marshlands, the sound from POKENAME's wings induces calm in those nearby. The effect intensifies the faster it flies.
author: .izik

entry: As the sun sets, POKENAME rise into the air on the warm updrafts produced by the swamps they call home. They utilize the large, compound eye on their underbelly to spot a new place for them to land and rest at during the day.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME are incredibly skittish, as they will frantically burrow themselves into the ground when they sense the slightest movement. Despite their small wings, POKENAME can beat them so fast that they can hover above the ground slightly.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's eyes are very sharp, giving it a wide range of clear vision. Though still developing, they also allow it to faintly see the auras of others, even through solid obstacles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lands atop streetlights to absorb electrical energy. Its wings buzz loudly as it drains the current.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's red markings and tough exoskeleton deter predators who want a quick snack. This makes up for its developing wings, which cannot support its weight for long flights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With their hard skulls and erratic flying, POKENAME can cause severe damage to cities. Even reinforced glass can't withstand a determined POKENAME.
author: currentlymuffin

entry: POKENAME rapidly flap their wings to propel themselves at incredible speeds and feed oxygen into the flames on their tails. Their long, flexible bodies allow them to take turns smoothly while adjusting their tails as needed.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is coated in a green fluid once used in speed-enhancing medicine. The practice was discontinued due to causing erratic behavior in Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME buzzes at high speeds over tall grass, scattering pollen that helps the surrounding plants grow. It can fly easily in even high winds.
author: .izik

entry: With 360 degree vision, ultrasonic waves for detection and precision flying capabilities, it is near impossible for prey to avoid POKENAME hunting them, nor for a predator to sneak up on POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME charges through the air and slams its spiked metallic body into predators like Pidgeot. The impact leaves dents even in steel plating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have wings that allow them to glide for short, but quick, bursts. These quick moves also allow them to avoid fights while cutting into trees with their tusks so they can suck at the sap directly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME flap their wings at 60 times per second to lift their bodies. They are unable to drink nectar because of their short beaks, so they buzz around to find berries to peck at.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has great aerial mobility, able to change directions without turning its body. It will spot its prey from above and then dive towards the ground at supersonic speeds.
author: mistymagius

entry: While flying over marshes, POKENAME spits fire to clear its path. The heat from its flames can dry entire patches of swamp grass.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dances at such a blistering speed that its wings create a buzzing sound as they whizz through the air.
author: .realthree

entry: As POKENAME sashays through the tall grass, its many wings vibrate to disguise its footsteps as rushing wind.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME darts around swamps late at night. If it spots travelers, it mimics the cries of children just to unsettle them-for its own amusement.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are not that physically strong, but it uses its speed to punch up to 200 times a second. It will try its best to protect weaker Pokémon, but it is not always successful.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME vibrates the many wings in its ruff, producing an ominous buzzing that sounds like an entire swarm of dangerous bug Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME howls, its wings flap with wild energy. The sound echoes through cliffs and can startle nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Despite having wings, POKENAME floats to move around. However, when it does uses them, it can go at 100 kph.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME keep wandering in high-traffic areas where they get run over. Fear not, as they don't die, and their body will re-inflate itself in a day.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME scurries through the waterlogged undergrowth of humid marshes. If something rustles the reeds, all the nearby POKENAME will launch into the air without warning, flying noisily away.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME have specialized compound eyes that prevent dust from getting into their eyes. This is especially important since dust tends to brush past them as they zip past other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a peaceful Pokémon. When in danger, it releases thick smoke from its exhaust vents. Known for its docile nature and control over heat and fire, it's considered a good companion for beginner Trainers.
author: ahenci

entry: Though its wings allow only brief flight, POKENAME glows faintly from its torso at night to lure in prey like Venonat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are made of sugary, brittle layers that break off easily. Bakeries prize them for use as edible cupcake decorations.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME darts across marshes at high speed. Upon finding deep water, it dives in and falls asleep, its lily pad keeping it afloat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME beats its wings to whip up dust clouds, then rolls around playfully in the dislodged dirt to keep its fur healthy and soft. Even while grooming, it stays alert to danger with its 360-degree vision.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's wings beat rapidly as it channels psychic energy. The vibrations in the air sharpen its focus before it strikes.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME's body weight prohibits true flight, its large wings add a few extra inches to its jump height. This gift is mainly used for elbow drops.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME can run across the ground at high speeds before retreating into its shell and crashing full-force into opponents. After knocking a foe down this way, it always makes sure to pose and adjust its "glasses" in a cool manner.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers to scurry along the ground and engage opponents face-to-face. Its legs are surprisingly powerful despite their small size.
author: char_latte3412

entry: While it can't fly, the stiff membrane on its back can be used to glide. It uses its visor to lock onto enemy Pokémon from far above.
author: hushpuppy

entry: POKENAME swoops at a target from above, smacking it with its leek before retreating to wait for another chance to strike.  As it has weak defenses, these hit-and-run tactics are its best bet for successful hunts.
author: sk372

entry: While POKENAME has a shell to defend itself from enemies, it can also flee quickly using its wings, making small waves as it darts across the sea.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Due to its massive weight, POKENAME's wings are some of the strongest of all Pokémon. However, it still only flies short distances, frequently grabbing onto rocks or cliffsides with its many small legs to rest.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME vibrates its wings in a hypnotic tone that causes drowsiness. It feeds only on pleasant dreams, ignoring nightmares entirely.
author: .izik

entry: The pendulum POKENAME carries is actually a mere distraction, meant to keep a target's focus occupied. The actual hypnotic effect it wields comes from the strange hum it emanates with its rapid wingbeat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a bulb on their back that secretes a slimy, toxic film which covers their skin, protecting them from sunlight. Though the film is poisonous in its liquid form, it can be mixed with sugar and boiled to make a sticky, sour candy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The antennae on top of a POKENAME's head secrete a liquid that they cover themselves in. This liquid is foul-smelling and designed to repel predators. Unfortunately, most predators don't mind the smell and have led to overhunting.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: If two gills of POKENAME ever make contact, even with another of its kind, it triggers an explosion. To prevent this, they often coat them in mud, which makes POKENAME resemble a Dive Ball, leading to careless Trainers picking them up by mistake.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: These Pokémon have only been documented since the adoption of subsea electrical cables. They form colonies around them, and play games until they tire, whereby they nuzzle into the cables and charge up.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: These Pokémon have only been documented since the adoption of subsea electrical cables. They form colonies around them, and play games until they tire, whereby they nuzzle into the cables and charge up.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Clusters of POKENAME float happily on the surface of shallow marshes. Their bobbing movement resembles drifting seeds, making them easy to overlook.
author: .izik

entry: Losing heads seems to be painless for POKENAME and as long as one head remains, it can regrow the others. If the heads are gently heated, a liquid will ooze from the orifices and can be used as a low-calorie alternative to sugar.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's eyes hold a great sadness so deep that most that meet its gaze are moved to tears. POKENAME will comfort them with a quiet nuzzle, then continue its never-ending journey to a future it still dares to hope will be brighter.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME approaches humans with a hopeful gaze, gently nudging its bone towards them. It longs for a simple game of fetch. If ignored or refused, it collapses in a heap and cries itself to sleep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME appears to have impressive abs from a distance, but up close, is just a natural pattern on its skin. This gave rise to people calling others a POKENAME, used to describe someone who seems appealing at first, but hides an unpleasant nature.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Having lost what it once valued most, POKENAME finds itself without purpose.
author: fuade

entry: POKENAME live in cold water and are prone to licking ice. Although this doesn't cause them pain it can render them immobile for a few minutes while they wait for it to melt.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: During the height of industrialisation, POKENAME were paraded through the streets every Thursday to absorb pollution from around people's homes. Once fully inflated, they were taken downwind, where they expelled the toxins with Clear Smog.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME often hang above bodies of water, undergoing metamorphosis. When threatened they drop into the water, where their outer skin instantly hardens. Whilst they are safe in this state, they cannot grow, so must venture out of the water again.
author: whatagooddaytodie
