entry: POKENAME loves rotting broccoli and putrid parsnips. When paired with Purple Nectar, it becomes so happy it releases a sticky goo. This secretion is highly potent, just one sample can be refined into as many as 10,000 bottles of X Sp. Atk.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Similarly dense Pokémon often struggle to get around in wetlands, but POKENAME is well adapted to them. Its wide feet ensure it doesn't sink, and it always has 4 points of contact with the ground, including its tail, which can hold its entire weight.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Although especially lithe in water, when POKENAME is on land it struggles to move its great girth. It rests its horn against objects to help it remain upright, which often causes them to become punctured.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME secretes a healing mucus from its pouch that is prized by Pokémon Centers. It's often found near sick or injured Pokémon, singing softly while coating them in the goo. Its presence alone is said to speed up recovery and ease pain.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME frequently gets stuck or tangled up. It meeps remorsefully, waiting for a Pokémon or Trainer to rescue it. Once freed, they nuzzle their rescuer, leaving a pleasant-smelling film on them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Unlike most Pokémon, POKENAME's pouch can seal completely like a Sleeping Bag. A special organ produces a sticky secretion that keeps it shut. This is vital for protecting its young, who can't breathe underwater until they reach full maturity.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME defends itself by squirting ink that reacts with fish scales, causing a burning sensation as they begin to erode. It is harmless to humans and ancient cultures used the ink in tattoos, believing its properties helped prevent infection.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME defends itself by squirting ink that reacts with fish scales, causing a burning sensation as they begin to erode. It is harmless to humans and ancient cultures used the ink in tattoos, believing its properties helped prevent infection.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lay clutches of eggs at the bottom of lakes and squirts a gel over them to protect them. When they hatch, the young Pokémon eat through the gel, giving them enough energy to survive on their own.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME flops helplessly from pond to pond, splashing about as it moves. During this time, it uses its horn to deter predators from taking advantage of its struggle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends winters in the ocean, but in summer, it swims upriver to glacial lakes, unable to tolerate temperatures much above freezing. Attempts to keep it in captivity fail as it buries itself in a corner and refuses to eat.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME often hang above bodies of water, undergoing metamorphosis. When threatened they drop into the water, where their outer skin instantly hardens. Whilst they are safe in this state, they cannot grow, so must venture out of the water again.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Every POKENAME's wings are unique as they get their colouration from the types of flowers they visit. Their wings need to be kept constantly wet otherwise they will shrivel up and be unable to hold the POKENAME's weight.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The gills along each arm grow longer with age, eventually covering the body entirely. Through these gills, POKENAME taps into Psychic energy, allowing it to read minds and sense intentions before a single move is made.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: After evolving, POKENAME still desires Water Stones. Older members of the species have been known to keep up to 3 in their nest, guarding them from other Pokémon, even Wooyu. Much mythology surrounds this behaviour.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME dances happily whenever someone looks at it, its mouth becoming a big grin. Onlookers cannot help but join it in its dance, which grows increasingly erratic. Should one complete the dance, POKENAME will gift them an item.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is adept at catching prey in water, with its large eyes well-suited to judging refraction and maximising light. When on land, this leads to over-stimulation and it stumbles around clumsily. Some Trainers have taken to making it sunglasses.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Causing chaos wherever it goes, POKENAME turns TV aerials the wrong way, clogs gutters, and shorts out appliances by discharging electricity at random. However, the moment it's scolded, it curls up into a tight ball, believing that it can't be seen.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME constantly emits a hot mist from its body, turning enclosed spaces into sweltering steam rooms. When it uses Fire Punch, the sudden heat flash-vaporizes nearby moisture, engulfing foes in a scalding haze that leaves severe burns.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When young, POKENAME go through a fierce teething stage, driven by an instinctual urge to bite anything they can. Within each litter, the alpha is determined by whichever manages to bite through the rocks that make up their nest.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When young, POKENAME go through a fierce teething stage, driven by an instinctual urge to bite anything they can. Within each litter, the alpha is determined by whichever manages to bite through the rocks that make up their nest.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Known for its violent outbursts, it would behoove any onlookers to stand clear when POKENAME runs amok. They make their homes atop seaside cliffs, where their constant trampling accelerates weathering, often leaving behind deposits of Chalky Stone.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives in shallow marshes, where it buries itself in mud to stay cool. If it beaches itself while playing, it will flop around helplessly until it manages to submerge again.
author: .izik

entry: The gills on a newborn POKENAME are so small they can't breathe underwater, so must forage on land. They are vulnerable at this stage, but when they have grown, they can stay underwater for hours at a time.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its highly sensitive gills can detect the presence of its favorite algae even from many miles away. Despite its large size, POKENAME is extremely gentle and often carries smaller Pokémon on its coils to bring them to safety.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are usually motionless, content to let the world pass by. Ocean currents carry small stones into crevices on their body, where over time they're polished smooth. After many years, these fragments wash free, often mistaken for Beach Glass.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are usually motionless, content to let the world pass by. Ocean currents carry small stones into crevices on their body, where over time they're polished smooth. After many years, these fragments wash free, often mistaken for Beach Glass.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is usually found gurgling in a language reminiscent of human baby gobbledygook. This strange speech captures the imagination of other Pokémon, who offer it trinkets like Poké Toys or Tropical Shells in exchange for stories.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is usually found gurgling in a language reminiscent of human baby gobbledygook. This strange speech captures the imagination of other Pokémon, who offer it trinkets like Poké Toys or Tropical Shells in exchange for stories.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME occasionally suffers from sudden bouts of nausea as its unstable DNA struggles to settle into a fixed form. Some Trainers claim that giving it an X Sp. Def to hold eases the symptoms, while others insist a muddy cabbage works just as well.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME occasionally suffers from sudden bouts of nausea as its unstable DNA struggles to settle into a fixed form. Some Trainers claim that giving it an X Sp. Def to hold eases the symptoms, while others insist a muddy cabbage works just as well.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is coated in a sticky, poisonous film that offers protection and helps it blend seamlessly into water. The substance bends light around its body, rendering it nearly invisible. When it uses Acid Armor underwater, it's almost untouchable.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is coated in a sticky, poisonous film that offers protection and helps it blend seamlessly into water. The substance bends light around its body, rendering it nearly invisible. When it uses Acid Armor underwater, it's almost untouchable.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Long ago, it is said that a POKENAME carried a Gold Leaf to the heart of the steppe, where lightning never ceased. Struck by a mighty bolt, its body was changed forever. Even today, its fur can knock out a full-grown Pokémon with a single touch.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses a gentle form of Fire Fang on its young, not to harm them, but to teach them self-defence through play. When danger approaches, they instinctively burrow into the mud, hiding everything but their gills, which twitch to sense vibrations.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME enters cyberspace by secreting a slime onto subsea cables, creating a conductive path that lets it phase into digital systems. It has a deep fear of games that contain snakes and may crash a system if it finds itself on the same data layer.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME enters cyberspace by secreting a slime onto subsea cables, creating a conductive path that lets it phase into digital systems. It has a deep fear of games that contain snakes and may crash a system if it finds itself on the same data layer.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's cute looks belie their vicious nature and appetite. They lure in smaller Pokémon by acting docile and playful, then launch Spike Cannon attacks. They thrive in cold lakes.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lay dormant at the bottom of small bodies of water. Their gills can absorb the tiniest sustenance suspended in the water. They use so little energy in this state, that other Pokémon assume they are dead.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: With weak eyesight and a poor sense of smell, POKENAME dwells deep within underground aquifers. It spends its days crafting a perfectly round Polished Mud Ball, which females use to judge potential mates.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hunts silently at depths reaching 5 km, its tough shell easily withstanding the crushing pressure. Its arms are precise enough for delicate tasks, and it has even been known to assist in surgery when human doctors are scarce.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hunts silently at depths reaching 5 km, its tough shell easily withstanding the crushing pressure. Its arms are precise enough for delicate tasks, and it has even been known to assist in surgery when human doctors are scarce.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is incredibly friendly to humans. It loves playing with children on sunny days, joyfully floating alongside them in pools.
author: akujules

entry: POKENAME expels water from its body, which instantly evaporates due to its intense internal heat, creating lift for short bursts of flight. However, it must frequently return to water to rehydrate its skin, or it risks overheating and drying out.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's favourite move seems to be Dragon Rage, which it uses to cheer itself up, but causes its skin to dry out. Trainers have to be careful to keep it happy, otherwise it will devastate the local area.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Before the advent of fusion technology, POKENAME were believed to be hunted to extinction. Trophy hunters prized the crystal on their necks, polishing and displaying them as a rare Marble. The largest known collection ever assembled contained 21.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Although quite clumsy in its everyday movements, watching POKENAME perform Dragon Rush is truly a spectacle to behold. Targets are sometimes stunned by its majesty and don't even try to get out of the way.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are very territorial and will dive at anything that gets too near, striking with their stingers. They lay their eggs in the mud near water but seem to forget about them as soon as they are laid.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME delights in the simple pleasure of telekinetically lifting mud and letting it rain over itself like a shower. Other Pokémon bring it offerings of food, and those who present its favourite, courgette, are sometimes rewarded with evolution.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME delights in the simple pleasure of telekinetically lifting mud and letting it rain over itself like a shower. Other Pokémon bring it offerings of food, and those who present its favourite, courgette, are sometimes rewarded with evolution.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Said to be born of pure serendipity, POKENAME drifts through sprawling wetlands, trailing ribbons of Psychic energy in its wake. It's rarely seen, but those who do spot one say it gifts them a single Silver Leaf, as proof of being pure of heart.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Said to be born of pure serendipity, POKENAME drifts through sprawling wetlands, trailing ribbons of Psychic energy in its wake. It's rarely seen, but those who do spot one say it gifts them a single Silver Leaf, as proof of being pure of heart.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME drifts lazily along rivers, soaking up sunlight. When something threatening flies overhead, it dives out of sight. At just the right temperature and humidity, which varies for each member, it becomes hyperactive, and surprisingly powerful.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In summer, the leaf atop POKENAME's head flourishes as it absorbs sunlight. It enjoys the gentle care of Trainers who prune it regularly. When paired with roasted eggplant, the leaf adds a fragrant touch, making for a summer treat.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME can sniff out sick trees and rub its body against them, secreting a substance that kills most parasites. The counterpart of any dedicated forester, its healing secretions are now being studied for potential use in treating human disease.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sprays scalding water from its back, but only in extreme danger. The attack causes it visible pain, as the heat damages its own skin. Fortunately, its body heals quickly, a trait researchers believe evolved to support this risky defence.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Before going to sleep, POKENAME covers itself in mud to draw out toxins and invigorate its skin. It is easy to spot, however, as when it is having a good dream, it spurts water from its back and head.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME gathers mud and shapes it into a mound large enough to sleep in, then uses Flame Wheel to bake it solid. It spends the night inside, often with smaller Pokémon it befriends. At dawn, it moves on, building a new shelter each evening.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's first instinct with something new is to bite it, first lightly and playfully but then harder if the object is a threat or food. To stay safe while sleeping, it sinks into mud with only its nostrils, eyes, and gills exposed.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has no true teeth, only tough, ridged gums. When it bites at prey, they often escape with little more than bruises, leaving it to rely on a diet of hardy plants and slow-moving insects to survive.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME build their nests on riverbanks. They attract mates with a distinctive call similar to that of a Pidgey's, except POKENAME simultaneously expel great volumes of water. This causes it to sound more gurgled, followed by a big splash.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME thrashes its tail to churn riverbeds, kicking up fine sediment. It then coats its body in the thick mud, which helps trap moisture and protect its sensitive skin. This allows it to spend longer periods on land without drying out.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives along riversides and reacts to the slightest hint of danger by slapping its tail against the water's surface. The sharp crack it creates can startle predators and serves as a warning signal to alert others in its group.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is coated in a slippery film, allowing it to climb predators with ease and snatch their catch before slipping away. Though risky, it's rarely caught. It occasionally steals from humans too, mistaking shiny objects for food.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is always screeching. Some say it can sense weather patterns and is trying to warn others. Its mud-nests wash away in heavy rain, though POKENAME always depart before the first drop falls.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is always screeching. Some say it can sense weather patterns and is trying to warn others. Its mud-nests wash away in heavy rain, though POKENAME always depart before the first drop falls.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's wings are better adapted for water than air, allowing it to slice through currents at speeds up to 90 km/h. On land, however, it becomes calm and sociable, often seen huddling with others, behaviour it never displays while underwater.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time buried in mud, lying in wait for unsuspecting prey. It draws in nutrients from its environment, concentrating them into a potent toxin, then strikes with Cross Poison to swiftly paralyze and immobilize its victim.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spits a sticky string to reel in prey and drag them into its marsh-side den. Once inside, it submerges them in the mud before making its next catch.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME is capable of great aerial speed, it rarely utilizes it. The brutal airflow of flight is painful to handle for its external gills.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME claim whole river systems as their territory and are very protective of them. They fly for hours at a time, keeping an eye on their territory, but have never been found further than a kilometer from a river.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Found near the ocean floor, POKENAME is rarely seen. It thrives in waters below 3°C, but when forced into warmer environments, it generates bioelectric pulses in its gills. These trigger evaporative cooling, helping it regulate its body temperature.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME glows due to bioluminescent bacteria that feed on a mucus it secretes. It can control how much mucus is produced, adjusting the luminance of its glow. When threatened, it releases a sudden surge, blinding predators and escaping in the flash.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Very few POKENAME colonies exist, but each holds hundreds of individuals. Incredibly social, they recognize every member and are often seen splashing in water or playfully tickling each other with bursts of static electricity.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Very few POKENAME colonies exist, but each holds hundreds of individuals. Incredibly social, they recognize every member and are often seen splashing in water or playfully tickling each other with bursts of static electricity.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spend most of their lives curled up underwater, motionless. If disturbed, they release a mild toxin. On full moon nights, they float to the surface, absorbing moonbeams. They've never been seen eating and may subsist solely on lunar energy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME constantly seeks validation, eagerly running errands for its Trainer. Though well-meaning, it often misunderstands tasks. If asked to deliver Fab Mail, it may believe it's a gift and keep it close, cherishing it like a treasured possession.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Very timid by nature, POKENAME often uses Baton Pass to call in an ally and avoid danger. However, with patience and dedicated training, a determined Trainer can awaken its hidden potential, transforming it into a cold-blooded, relentless fighter.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME tries to spread joy by releasing a shiny film onto those below. Unfortunately, this film closely resembles bird droppings. Oblivious to the annoyance it causes, it cheerfully frolics away, believing it has brightened someone's day.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are often seen staring blankly off cliffsides, seemingly contemplating their own verticality. They attempt to learn Brave Bird by flinging themselves off ledges, only to bellyflop with a splash. They never learn but never stop trying.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME was once revered by several oceanfaring tribes, who believed it could speak of the future. They obeyed its cryptic commands without question, fearing that to ignore them would invite disaster or doom upon their people.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's damp, fluffy coat grows rapidly and must be trimmed with insulated Shears. Its wool is often spun into heirloom garments, passed down as a bequest through generations. When threatened, it discharges static strong enough to jolt a Rhydon.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's damp, fluffy coat grows rapidly and must be trimmed with insulated Shears. Its wool is often spun into heirloom garments, passed down as a bequest through generations. When threatened, it discharges static strong enough to jolt a Rhydon.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME claim whole river systems as their territory and are very protective of them. They fly for hours at a time, keeping an eye on their territory, but have never been found further than a kilometer from a river.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The droppings of POKENAME are toxic to other Pokémon but are a wonderful fertilizer for plants. POKENAME's territory is always full of magnificent flora, and sweet, juicy berries.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME must keep their fur damp, as if it dries out too much electricity builds up in it, and zaps anything nearby, or even itself. It likes walking alongside its Trainer but has to quickly scamper to keep up, making for an amusing sight.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sees itself as far superior to its unevolved forms and takes offense if they approach. Believing it's the epitome of beauty, it dances in the rain expecting gifts. If none come, it pelts onlookers with mud in a dramatic tantrum.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME swims through shallow ponds, using its long tail to gather up cattails to eat. It builds small floating nests from gathered plants, drifting peacefully on the water's surface.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME sees another Pokémon drowning, it forms an air bubble infused with Vivid Scent to envelop and calm them as it guides them to safety. Once ashore, it offers a soothing mud bath. Its gentle nature has left it with no natural predators.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is theorised that a distant relative of POKENAME once lived in forestlands but adapted to icy waters as the climate changed. When it performs Body Slam, vestigial notches along its sides become visible, thought to be remnants of climbing limbs.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in maintaining its territory, meticulously clearing away twigs, stones, or anything that spoils the view. It digs half-metre-deep pits, fills them with water, and lounges inside, enjoying the serenity of its perfect domain.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's lightweight body allows it to hop playfully across the surface of ponds. It enjoys snacking on lily pads as it bounces along.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is lighter than water, allowing it to effortlessly float along rivers and streams. It often helps smaller Pokémon cross the river on its lily pad.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME produces a slimy film from its gills, which it uses to blow unusually durable bubbles, nearly impossible to pop. These increase its surface area, allowing it to be carried by the wind across oceans, to spread its offspring far and wide.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The gills on a POKENAME both enable it to breathe underwater, and also to sense subtle changes in the environment. When water currents shift, POKENAME dart away, expecting danger.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's tail is incredibly sensitive, capable of detecting scents and sensing its surroundings. It often swims with just its tail above the surface, using it to snatch berries from overhanging branches and pass them down to eat while submerged.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight, gradually swelling as it stores energy. Once it reaches a peak, it suddenly bursts inside out with a loud pop, evolving into a Wooflora. Despite the dramatic transformation, the Wooflora emerges completely unharmed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Following their violent evolution, POKENAME seem more cautious of sunlight. They spend their days following the shade, always half in and half out of the light. They swap sides every hour or so to prevent drying up.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's wings flap at such speed that the buzzing it creates is audible from up to 100m away. This makes it easy for predators to sneak up on it without it hearing, only saved by its impressive 360 degree eyesight.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's wings flap at such speed that the buzzing it creates is audible from up to 100m away. Having its eyes detached from its head allows it to see all around it, and stabilise its vision even when moving its head.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is very sensitive to warm weather, hiding deep below the surface during heat waves. Trainers who keep POKENAME as pets will accommodate this by feeding it ice cubes.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: They are rotund and soft as a pillow, as their bodies are made up of mostly water and blubber. They release a low, resounding bellow that sounds like a tuba whenever they awaken each day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a playful soul, often seen chasing waves along the shoreline. If given a Fluffy Tail, it rolls on its back to nibble and bat them with its paws. When deeply bonded with someone, it expresses affection through gentle, affectionate bites.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Each year, many Woovee gather at Alola's Altar of the Moone. From dusk, they howl at the moon, and by morning, all have evolved into POKENAME. This is the largest known congregation of its kind. Many ecologists travel great distances to witness it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It gathers moss and reeds during the day to build its nest. It spits mud onto the nest in order to strengthen it against the elements.
author: .izik

entry: The gills on a POKENAME both enable it to breathe underwater, and also to sense subtle changes in the environment. When water currents shift, POKENAME dart away, expecting danger.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spend their days on riverbanks soaking up sunlight. At night they graze and protect sleeping Marill and Wooper, researchers do not know what benefit POKENAME gain from this.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's webbed paws make it a surprisingly good swimmer. Its whiskers help sense movement in cold bodies of water, where it typically hunts.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Spotting a POKENAME in the wild is considered an ill omen, as they often appear just before a shipwreck occurs. They feed on the fear of drowning sailors, yet do allow some to cling to them as flotation, saving a few lives in the process.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Entering a POKENAME's territory triggers a splitting headache, a psychic test to sense intent. If you mean no harm, it allows gentle petting. If it senses hostility, it coats itself in a toxic film as a warning to stay away.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Always eager to help, POKENAME loyally trails behind its Trainer. It secretes a substance with properties similar to both sunscreen and aftersun. Researchers are currently working to replicate it for commercial skincare use.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are most active on Friday, with their two minds perfectly in sync. With surprising briskness, they dart through wetlands, using Assurance to punish foes who dare strike first. Some Trainers believe their mood predicts the weekend's luck.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are most active on Friday, with their two minds perfectly in sync. With surprising briskness, they dart through wetlands, using Assurance to punish foes who dare strike first. Some Trainers believe their mood predicts the weekend's luck.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Usually lazy, they become incredibly active when their two minds are perfectly in sync. With surprising briskness, they dart through wetlands, using Assurance to punish foes who dare strike first.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hangs from trees over water, producing a thick, sweet-smelling drool that lures Bug Pokémon. Once they begin licking it, the drool explodes in a flash of gas and sound, stunning the victims long enough for POKENAME to feed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives sealed within a layered mud-shell that hardens over time. It only opens when feeding, launching its sticky tongue to catch prey. No one has ever seen inside, and any attempt to pry the shell open ends in explosive failure.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives splashing within a layered mud-shell that hardens over time. It opens fully when feeding, launching its sticky tongue to catch prey. No one has ever seen the bottom, and any attempt to get close ends in explosive failure.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME keeps its eyes closed when above ground to protect them from the sunlight. They dry out quickly, so it prefers to stay in mud. POKENAME's tunnels often suffer cave-ins, but it manages to wriggle to safety.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The spikes that cover POKENAME are used to inject venom into foes. It nests on cliffsides, mixing a sticky secretion with mud to build sturdy homes. These nests remain fixed even in harsh winds, thanks to the strength of the reinforced mixture.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The spikes that cover POKENAME are used to inject venom into foes. It nests on cliffsides, mixing a sticky secretion with mud to build sturdy homes. These nests remain fixed even in harsh winds, thanks to the strength of the reinforced mixture.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: During its evolution, POKENAME breaks apart and each boulder becomes slightly sentient. The lead head is still the most dominant, but the others can now offer assistance. Sometimes, they all work together and can dig at a devastating pace.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is becoming a growing trend to breed smaller and smaller POKENAME and keep them in a handbag as a fashion statement. This can impact the Pokémon and there have been calls to ban this practice.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME form large colonies and are very social. At dusk and dawn, they all fly together and play. Their confidence is greater than their skill however, and many fly into each other and fall to the ground, luckily, they are very rarely hurt.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The spikes on the bottom of POKENAME are theorised to be what remains of vestigial legs this Pokémon once had. It now spends its time in the water, though occasionally will be found in a river delta wallowing in mud.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Every month, an active POKENAME sheds its skin, as every time it wins a fight it grows a little. To protect its vulnerable new skin, it covers itself in a poisonous film. When the skin has become hard, even a blade struggles to pierce it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends its days gathering sea beet, a relative of beetroot, and Yellow Nectar along the coast. It ferments these, producing a bitter, mildly alcoholic juice. These are its only sources of nutrition and have kept their populations very low.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends its days gathering sea beet, a relative of beetroot, and Yellow Nectar along the coast. It ferments these, producing a bitter, mildly alcoholic juice. These are its only sources of nutrition and have kept their populations very low.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to dig out surprisingly complex nests to shelter them from the sun. Some have even been documented forming brick-shaped mud blocks and leaving them to bake in the sun for later use.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: For reasons still unknown, POKENAME gather on the first Tuesday of every month to compete in brutal Beat Up contests. The last one standing evolves on the spot. Oddly, no blood is shed, only trails of thick, sticky gel are left behind.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME harvests toxins from sea sponges and transforms them into a sweet, honey-like substance using a gel it produces. In some coastal regions, a controversial delicacy involves roasting POKENAME with okra and fennel, glazed in its own syrup.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME loves splashing in water and catching fish, but its eyes aren't suited for seeing underwater. With their Trainer's permission, they will spend hours happily frolicking beneath the waves in child-sized Scuba Gear, which fits it perfectly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Some believe POKENAME to be the largest extremophile, as it is found around geothermal vents deep underwater. The slime it produces protects its sensitive organs and allows it to happily absorb nutrients from water that can reach 80°C.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In some regions, food was traditionally cooked by letting a POKENAME slither over it. Their intense body heat and coating of slime created a deep-fried effect. Due to how hard they are to handle, this method was reserved for special occasions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life flying over cold open ocean or along the coast, grabbing any Pokémon unwary enough to cross its path. Hunting it is seen as bad luck, inspiring the phrase 'a POKENAME around your neck' to mean carrying a heavy burden.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME roams among mangrove roots, forming a symbiotic relationship with the trees. It feeds on detritus and harmful insects, while its muddy secretions fertilize the soil. It often naps curled around the roots during low tide.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME blows bubbles while sleeping on its back in coral reefs. Its peaceful floating is a common sight in warm tropical waters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in warm seas but is prone to overheating. To cool down, it releases a heat-dispersing substance through its gills. It is most active in winter, when vibrant corals bloom on its back.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME swallows food whole but can't digest it without eating mud. Though this fills its gut with pathogens, it can neutralise them with specialised enzymes. This process gives its slime antibiotic properties, and researchers are studying it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Quite at home in a mire, it takes great pleasure from firing a Gunk Shot at anything that gets too close. The Wooper head that can sometimes be seen is actually an organ that can force its way out, splitting the septum, but causing no lasting damage.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Living near frozen ponds, POKENAME delights in making and giving snowballs to visitors. It considers this an act of goodwill, though some Trainers have been pelted unexpectedly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feeds by burying its head in mud, searching for worms and insects. Its gills are razor-sharp, and due to its clumsy nature, Trainers often cover them for safety. Many injuries have been caused simply by POKENAME turning around too quickly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME can be found near hydrothermal springs near volcanic areas. Their footsteps sound like hot-water bottles sloshing.
author: pankiwi

entry: After it evolves, their heads swell up with the hot water they store in their bodies. They inflate their tail to balance their heavy head.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME live their life being constantly picked on. Other Pokémon prey on them only to be viciously poisoned by the substance oozing from POKENAME's skin. POKENAME take revenge by eating any unprotected eggs.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When scared, female POKENAME lay dozens of small eggs with sticky shells distracting predators enough to escape. The few eggs that fall to the bottom of the sea get coated in sand, hiding them. POKENAME rarely lays eggs any other way.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is incredibly gentle and has never been seen starting a fight unprovoked. Its loud, trumpet-like call echoes across wetlands, often scaring off predators before they get too close. It uses its sturdy tail to splash water when excited.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Though it doesn't truly sleep, it still gets tired and can act sporadically. Trainers discovered that giving it Dream Mail to hold before uploading it to a PC causes it to emerge hyper-alert, as if the data mimics the effects of restful dreaming.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME will sometimes stand on its hind legs to reach high branches, often sharing what it finds with others. It tends to form small mixed-species groups, each member helping to compensate for the others' weaknesses.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME produces a pink fluid from its tail and takes great joy in rolling around in it, often making it appear more pink than blue. Researchers believe this behaviour deters predators, as the fluid has an unpleasant taste that discourages hunting.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives to spar. It is very accommodating of the feelings of others though, and so if battling a weaker foe will often handicap itself. Sometimes it will tie its hands behind its back, or spend the whole battle on one foot.
author: whatagooddaytodie

author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The dexterity that POKENAME exhibits is striking to watch. As well as its legs, it also uses its tail to strike foes. Young POKENAME struggle with blisters on the tops of their heads and must train for hours daily to build up durability.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Castles used to keep several POKENAME in case of siege. They purified well water if it was poisoned, with their lips turning bright pink if the water was contaminated.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME finds small puddles of water which it secretes an oily substance into. It then waits for thunderstorms, covered in mud. The substance attracts lightning, which strikes the water and allows POKENAME to absorb all the nutrients of the mud.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME patrol cold waters. If they come across large rocks or chunks of ice, they wrap themselves around them and crush them until they split. Female POKENAME will refuse to choose a partner whose territory has uncrushed rocks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In some areas, humans have developed a relationship with POKENAME in which they gather the milk-like substance produced from POKENAME's gills. It is unknown how POKENAME feels about this, though it shows discomfort during the milking process.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME loves to run. It is said that whenever it is close, it brings with it a thunderstorm. This is used to explain why it can go from clear and sunny to dark and stormy in a matter of moments.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME just can't seem to get enough of eating mud. Trainers rarely keep it for long as it sneaks out in the middle of the night to go on a feeding frenzy, then tracks in so much mud on its return that it takes over an hour to clean up.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME digs into rocks in rock pools, becoming almost indistinguishable from its surroundings. It then fills its mouth with mud or sand as camouflage and leaves it open, waiting for unsuspecting prey to wander in.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME digs into rocks in rock pools, becoming almost indistinguishable from its surroundings. It then fills its mouth with mud or sand as camouflage and leaves it open, waiting for unsuspecting prey to wander in.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When POKENAME yawns, it can cause minor tsunamis, and due to this, they were hunted to near extinction. Recently, a colony of them was discovered in a mid-ocean ridge, generating currents that made sea trade easier.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives a quiet life, grazing on kelp and seagrass and avoiding conflict. However, if its young are threatened, it releases a devastating Aeroblast, so powerful it clears entire hectares of ocean life and sends shockwaves echoing for miles.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME form such strong bonds with humans that they will often approach Trainers, trying to befriend them. In fact, although their overall population numbers are healthy, some scientists think they are almost extinct in the wild.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is sometimes found frozen in icebergs, enjoying the chill. Its shimmering colours draw tourists from afar. At any moment, it may erupt in a burst of flame, melting the ice and soaring into the sky in a dazzling display.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Every 7 years, POKENAME lays a single egg where forest meets marsh. Its yolk can revive the most barren landscapes. Whenever one is found there is a painful choice, save the land now, or let a rare, powerful life be born to protect it in the future.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Many communities believe that spotting a POKENAME in the wild brings good luck. However, rising temperatures have forced them to migrate closer to the poles. As sightings become rarer, calls are being made for urgent action to protect them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is often seen with a bright, cheerful smile. However, it frequently bumps into anything in its path, seemingly unaware of obstacles right in front of it.
author: zebrarook_

entry: Each POKENAME has two tails with different roles, one for movement, where the gills grow short and sturdy, and one for fine tasks, with gills acting like fingers. Some are born left-tailed, others right-tailed, akin to being left or right-handed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its friendly face has earned the nickname "Friendly Water Ghost," but don't be fooled by its appearance. The POKENAME is also known for hunting wild Pokémon in the swamps by drowning them.
author: alexandre_vulgo_xande

entry: The bubbles on POKENAME's head allow it to transfer substances with its environment. Any waste it generates diffuses out, and useful minerals are transported in. If a bubble pops, POKENAME faints, though will reform if no further harm comes to it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is obsessed with preening and dressing up, delighting in receiving a Hat Dye Kit from its Trainer. When it tires of a hat, it will offer it as a gift, expecting a new one in return. If ignored, it may sulk or spray water in protest.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME looks after the rock it keeps as if it were its own egg. Every evening it gives it a mud bath while gently cooing to it. It doesn't let anyone touch it except its own Trainer.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME form such strong bonds with humans that they will often approach Trainers, trying to befriend them. In fact, although their overall population numbers are healthy, some scientists think they are almost extinct in the wild.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME regularly electrocutes itself by jumping in and out of water. To counter this, it expels a gel from its skin that dissipates the electricity into its surroundings. This way, it doesn't harm itself, but those nearby are not so lucky.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are often seen close to or within human populations, following the people within in hopes of gaining food from them. With their cute face and simple demeanor, most Trainers can't help but give them the treats they seek.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are playful and often wrap around the legs of swimmers. This can be dangerous as their skin secretes a mild toxin, though incidents are rare as they prefer colder waters. Coastal signs now warn visitors to keep a safe distance.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME searches for holes in the ground and fills them with its thick, antimicrobial drool. Slightly toxic to others but beneficial to itself, it uses these puddles to soak and heal its skin. Over time, entire networks of “healing wells” can form.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The tips of POKENAME's tails lack nerves, as each strike releases a shock so powerful it burns the ends. Luckily, they heal rapidly. After a short soak in water, the damaged tips regenerate fully, ready to deliver another jolt.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is said that POKENAME visit the sorrowful, gently placing a wing on their forehead to absorb their grief. They convert this into a goo and spread it across marshes, where vibrant flowers bloom soon after. Catching one is considered bad manners.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME regularly electrocutes itself by jumping in and out of water. To counter this, it expels a gel from its skin that dissipates the electricity into its surroundings. This way, it doesn't harm itself, but those nearby are not so lucky.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is only found in desert oases, limiting their natural population. If the oasis they live in dries up, they can bury itself in the sand. Here, they can remain for up to a year, until the rainy season brings clouds to fill the oasis again.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The tips of POKENAME's ears shine faintly in cold weather, though researchers aren't sure why. Within their species, this shimmer is highly prized. Those with the brightest glow are often showered with offerings of kelp, their favourite food.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: As ice thaws in spring, POKENAME travel down rivers, surfing along the snowmelt. They leave behind a goo that other Pokémon have come to use as proof of the end of winter.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME was once relied upon to haul logs from forests to lumber yards, working tirelessly day and night. This often led to exhaustion, prompting a tradition of resting them on Saturday evenings, a practice some say inspired the weekend.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME makes its home in giant kelp forests, tying the stalks together near the base to form dense shelters. If anything starts nibbling at the kelp, it lets out a low, rattling growl to scare them off, fiercely protective of its underwater home.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME often claims an entire lake as its territory. Even those that have coexisted for years may suddenly clash if their paths cross. These rare battles are fierce, often felling trees and devastating the surrounding habitat.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lie down in the muddy shallows of marshes and feast on plant life when no sun is available for photosynthesis. They have an aloof and carefree personality, but are by no means unkind.
author: bobosmith01

entry: On sunny days, hidden leaves along POKENAME's back unfurl to both absorb solar energy and shade its skin. With this energy, it can move with incredible bursts of speed to ambush prey with precision. The leaves retract again when the sun fades.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Fire builds in POKENAME's belly, and when it gets the hiccups, tiny bursts of flame escape its mouth. In cold weather, it snuggles up to other Pokémon to share its warmth, becoming a beloved companion in wintry habitats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Generations ago, conmen made fortunes selling products made from POKENAME's spines. When ground into powder and mixed with starch, it forms a runny paste that dries harder than superglue, but once wet again, it turns back to liquid.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has a highly unusual anatomy, its jugular vein runs externally through one of its gills. Researchers believe this adaptation protects its airway, as performing Blast Burn superheats its body, turning the surrounding air into scalding steam.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is more comfortable around people and rarely gathers with its own kind in the wild, meeting up only once a year. Normally docile, it will become unexpectedly aggressive if anyone makes the mistake of grabbing its tail.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME sleeps behind waterfalls during the day, coated in mud. At night, it stands silently on cliffs, staring at nearby humans without blinking for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is more comfortable around people and rarely gathers with its own kind in the wild, meeting up only once a year. Normally docile, it will become unexpectedly aggressive if its Trainer is threatened.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's skin is highly sensitive and begins to crack and flake if left dry for long. When out of water, it secretes a faint hum to signal distress. Trainers who raise one keep moisturiser or a spray mist on hand at all times to keep it healthy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful tail to gather rocks, which it coats in mud to form a nest. Once dried, the hardened shell keeps it cool and shaded. If no rocks are nearby, it will trigger a small rockslide to collect the materials it needs.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME doesn't have vision based on light but rather based on emotions. They stick close to other Pokémon, warning them when they detect predators, in exchange for protection. They are almost impossible to lie to, as they can sense true intentions.
author: whatagooddaytodie
