entry: Living in jungle rivers, POKENAME's leaf-like fins help it camouflage. The sweet aroma produced from the flower on its head is collected and added to perfumes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are often found in mangrove swamps, living amongst the submerged roots of the trees. They spend most of the time at the surface of the water, photosynthesizing and allowing their flowers to be pollinated by Bug-type Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are popular Pokémon to keep in ornamental ponds thanks to the elaborate flowers that they use as a tail. They typically linger near the surface of the water, hanging upside down with their flower exposed to the air.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They form tight-knit groups of 6 or 7 that bond for life. These POKENAME clusters are known colloquially as "floresces."
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: When POKENAME spins rapidly, it hurls razor-sharp leaves at its foes. It inhabits warm seas, where the gentle climate keeps its star-shaped body healthy and vibrant.
author: fiordaliso

entry: At low tide, many POKENAME are stranded on beaches with few ways to get back into the water until high tide returns. Fortunately, they can defend themselves against predators by whipping them with slippery vines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoy performing quirky little tricks that revolve around flowers. A common trick they like to perform revolves around transforming a vine into a bunch of petals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wings are too small to support its body for long periods of flight. Instead, it hangs from trees with its scythes and leaps down onto unsuspecting prey.
author: amityblamity

entry: POKENAME are far from modest creatures and want all the attention to be on them. They crack vine whips and create fluttering leaves to draw focus towards themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although the leaf on POKENAME's head is not hard, it is very sharp. During the day, POKENAME uses the vine in its mouth to eat fruits and tender leaves, and at night, it digs underground to avoid the cold.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME initiates duels to compete for leadership of its herd. Its mane becomes more vivid with each battle it goes through, so leaders of its herd often have bright red manes.
author: oreee0230

entry: To make sure both flowering buds on its body get enough sunlight, POKENAME has to partially reveal itself above the water's surface, either swimming sideways, or by alternating swimming right side-up and upside down.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME use their bulbs to hide among flower bushes, eating away at the leaves within. Once they have finished their meal, they will plant sprouts along the base of the bush to help it grow back sooner.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME moves through the water with surprising grace. While it swims, it uses the vines on its body to snatch up prey. Once the prey stops moving, it devours them. As a result, POKENAME rarely needs to photosynthesize.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a part of nearby plants. If small Pokémon come close, it may try to nibble on them.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's mane and bulb tail grow larger in size when in sunlight as they absorb nutrients. They tend to stay in dense rainforests as they are able to completely vanish with the rain from storms.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME gathers energy from lightning storms; its leaves crackle with excess electricity. It can also absorb sunlight to ensure it is always full of energy.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's leaves contain fire-resistant chemicals. When it eats too much and creates too much heat, it goes to a cool, ventilated place to spread its leaves and dissipate heat.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME is used within digital tools as an assistant to help users identify specific types of flowers or plants encountered during their excursions. If it discovers a variety never seen before, it emits a high-pitched cry.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's buds are hard, and its leaves are tough. By wrapping its body with leaves, POKENAME can protect itself from danger.
author: oreee0230

entry: When hunting, POKENAME tightens its bud and lunges forward to bite with its sharp teeth. Its flower bud is made out of lightweight petals, making it faster than a heavily armored Omastar.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME perch high in flowering trees, disguising themselves among the blooming flowers while they wait to evolve. If a predator approaches the tree they call home, they will spray a volley of poisonous needles from their bulbs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lives deep within marine caves, where it can peacefully let the pink bud on its back bloom fully. Its small legs allow it to climb any surface with ease.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The pink buds on its back and tail release a sweet aroma that lures other Pokémon toward it. POKENAME flies gracefully through the forest, using its strong wings to dart between the branches of the trees it calls home.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME loves to nap in gardens and becomes impossible to move once asleep. It is recommended to leave broken cucumbers nearby, as it finds their smell disgusting and will slowly shuffle away.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Whenever POKENAME flaps their bushy wings, the area around them is flooded with the warm aroma of flowers. This alluring scent lingers long after POKENAME take off into the sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's scaly skin sheds with a petal attached that can purify poison. These petals are valuable, but lose their power if removed from the shed skin, quickly withering away.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME uses vines to secure itself to a tree. Each part of POKENAME's body has a venomous sting and is especially potent in its leaves and vines.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME fly using the large fronds around their bulbs. They hide among the treetops before flying out in a storm of leaves, its prey only seeing their poisonous stingers once it's too late.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With a single psychic pulse, POKENAME can accelerate the growth of plants around them. Despite this power, they cannot force the flower on their tail to bloom faster.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorb impurities in the air through the leaves on their back to cleanse the air around them. They need a steady supply of sunlight to complete the process, otherwise their leaves will wilt from excess toxins.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The flower on POKENAME's neck produces a pleasant scent when exposed to sunlight. Because POKENAME has the ability to revitalize plants, ancient texts described it as a spirit that brings blessings of spring.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME absorb so much sunlight through photosynthesis that their body temperatures rise dramatically. During dry seasons, these Pokémon have been known to accidentally set brush ablaze while basking.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can be found in the rivers of tropical rainforests, only their bulb and eyes poking above the water line. They are playful Pokémon, but have a poor sense of the threat they can pose and can give a nasty bite to the unwary.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be found in the rivers of tropical rainforests, only their bulb and eyes poking above the water line. They use the vines on their back to grab interesting looking things on the shoreline and bring them close to bite on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lounge on river banks sunning themselves and keeping their flower pointing toward the sun. They are grumpy if woken up, snapping at whoever disturbs their sunbathing time.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The antennae on POKENAME's head can accurately separate plants from prey. The flower bud on its abdomen sprays a toxic gas when it cannot attack fast enough with its stinger.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME gather scattered leaves to form their nests. Once they are happy with their nests, they use any leftover leaves to create a smaller version around the bulbs on their backs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME will hang motionless in the water for days on end, only their bulb visible above the water. When they do move, it's to hunt for food, and they are capable of a surprising burst of speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME gather together into groups with their backs to the sun to sunbathe, using their tails to support themselves. As they sunbathe, they each take turns keeping guard.
author: oreee0230

entry: Though POKENAME's floral buds are immature, they can expel potent pollen that can cause drowsiness. POKENAME nap in the sunlight, occasionally falling into a deep sleep due to their own pollen.
author: silverscloudy

entry: Due to the sharpness of POKENAME's petal crown, they occasionally rush into battle headfirst. The pink coloration around their eyes faintly glow at night, distracting and intimidating their prey.
author: silverscloudy

entry: POKENAME have an especially difficult time surviving during winter because the flower bulb on their back exposes them to freezing temperatures. They often sleep in another Pokémon's burrow to keep warm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's prominent flower bud is quite conspicuous, so it ambushes prey from a nearby tree. If the prey caught in its web resists its poison, they may be released so it can find prey that is easier to capture.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME builds nests using silk threads, branches, and leaves. When it goes hunting, it spins silk from its abdomen to cling to tree branches, waiting for the right moment to ambush prey.
author: oreee0230

entry: At night, POKENAME silently sneak up on Bug-type Pokémon before plucking prey from the forest floor. They leave blooming flowers in their wake as they hunt.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are fiercely territorial, releasing poisonous spores if anyone gets too close. They use their large wings to create gusts, spreading the spores around their nests to protect their blooming bulbs while they sleep.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The trickster, POKENAME, will wait for prey below muddy water and pose with three of its flowers exposed. When a pollinator comes near, it shocks them with an unexpected jolt of electricity. Sometimes, it even catches small birds this way.
author: ludacriswell

entry: When an POKENAME's bulb blooms, it lets off a sweet smell that can be too strong for weak Pokémon. This bulb blooms every spring and closes in the fall.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: POKENAME can be found sulking when it cannot stargaze. If taken for a trip to see the starry night sky by its Trainer, it bestows good luck onto them.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME will happily dance together under the starry sky. If a shooting star passes, they will try to chase it together.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are anxious yet capable creatures that are easy to frighten. If startled, they unleash a flurry of vines to whip whatever surprised them until they calm down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are wrapped in petals to protect their delicate bodies. Whenever a Trainer helps them clean their bodies, they are blessed with good luck for a month.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use the leaves on their back to help them steer as they glide along the air. They scatter leaves as they flap their wings, collecting them with gusts of wind and directing them back to their nests.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's tail uses electric power to photosynthesize. Luckily POKENAME doesn't have to leech off of power plants because sunlight that is absorbed by the orb is instantly converted into electric power.
author: creaturecore

entry: Groups of POKENAME gather along the riverbanks to sing songs. Their stomachs release a satisfying thud when slapped with a vine whip, giving them the perfect percussion instrument to go along with their croaking.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME constantly pumps pollen from the flower bud on their back to keep themselves airborne. They are most active during spring and are a nightmare for people who are allergic to pollen.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By bending the leaves on their back, POKENAME control the direction they glide in. After gliding for long periods of time, they sunbathe in a patch of grass to nourish the flower on their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends its entire day searching for food to nourish the flower blooming on its back, making it grow even more beautiful. When it is happy, it naturally releases a strong fragrance that can lift the spirits of anyone who breathes it in.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is worshiped in remote areas and is repaid by taking care of the fields. Although crops can still grow without POKENAME, this relationship is beneficial to both sides in villages without Trainers.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME live in marshy areas covered with flora, using its large leaves to float on the water without being seen. The flower on its head releases poisonous spores when agitated.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME often lie flat with their mouth open to wait for lily pads to float into their mouth. The flower bulb on their back makes them easy to spot in the wild.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can simultaneously restore health and accumulate psychic energy with sunlight. If necessary, POKENAME can convert energy stored in its buds into psychic energy, but this will lead to prolonged weakness.
author: oreee0230

entry: Wild POKENAME are more active during the full moon. Their spots reflect the moonlight with an eerie glow.
author: 22ndsolstice

entry: Black seeds grow from POKENAME's blossom at night. These seeds can be refined into oil, which serves as a key component in the fuel for vehicles like the ZERO-ONE.
author: .izik

entry: It collects seeds from far-off places to plant flowers in a secret garden. It is considered bad luck to pick one of POKENAME's flowers at night.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME gain great insights into the world around them and are always eager to share their knowledge. They pride themselves on their vast knowledge and rarely hold their tongue.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To enrich the flower growing upon its back, POKENAME spends its day foraging through fields. When pleased, it releases a sweet scent believed to soothe even the weariest heart.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME develop a fruity, musky scent from the flower bud on their back. To fuel this massive bud on their back, they absorb sunlight through their skin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs through garbage cans near parks and trails to scavenge tasty treats for itself. Due to the large bulb on its back, sometimes it gets stuck in garbage cans.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A flower blooms on POKENAME's head. POKENAME can use channel mystical energy to rapidly grow and manipulate the petals of the flower.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME hovers gracefully, its broad leaves capturing sunlight for energy. When it captures enough light, it radiates heat to nearby plants.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life either basking in the sun or protecting its flower bud. The rest of its body soaks up any attacks made against it. Sometimes, simply staring at its bulb the wrong way can scare it away.
author: oreee0230

entry: It is a shy woodland creature with oily skin. Its breath smells like pungent herbs, typically too strong for the average person to enjoy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Flocks of POKENAME take over fields of flowers for weeks, sipping nectar to fuel their journey to the next field. They will guard their chosen site with flurries of intense Razor Leaf attacks, driving away anything that comes too close.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME collects a large number of flowers in its shell and then uses vines to tie itself to a tree to camouflage itself. The flower tea fermented inside its shell is very fragrant, but most bug Pokémon dislike it.
author: oreee0230

entry: Right after eating honey, the flower on POKENAME releases a sweet, fragrant aroma. During winter, it is almost never seen outside its den, as it cannot tolerate the cold.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It hides amongst flowers and other foliage to hide from predators. However, its bulb melts under high temperatures, rendering its disguise useless under hot weather.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME uses corrosive liquids to dissolve rocks to supplement nutrients. Its buds gradually warm up as activity increases.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's feathers have a pleasant herbal scent. As a result, keeping these feathers in one's home is popular among rich business owners.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The bud on POKENAME's back gives off a sweet scent when it's ready to bloom. As POKENAME uses its nose to look for food, this sweet smell will sometimes confuse it.
author: mistycloud

entry: The branches on POKENAME's head are loved by many Pokémon and are also an excellent spice. When there is a supply of pure water, the branches of POKENAME regenerate very quickly, which is why many Trainers raise POKENAME for profit.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME live in the shallows of lagoons and are usually seen with just their flowers above the surface. They use their sucker-covered tentacles to anchor themselves to the floor, letting them resist tidal flow.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has a bag-like tail filled with soil. When it basks in the sun, this soil gains more nutrients, which it uses to fertilize plants waiting to bloom.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME lives in packs that are hostile to outsiders. The flames in its mouth have a unique ability to strip the life from its enemies while preserving nutrients in the ashes.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME rattle their tails and release a stinging pollen when someone gets too close to them. If the warning is ignored, they bite onto whatever invades their space.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whenever POKENAME are thirsty, they suck in water from their trunk and spray it onto the flower on their back. This muscular trunk can uproot berry bushes with a single tug.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME water the flower on their back by using their long trunk. This trunk can also grab onto sticks that make for the perfect back scratcher.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to the immense tensile strength of the vines on its back, POKENAME is commonly used as a beast of burden.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME gain energy from children solving puzzles on the internet, as each correct answer gives them a burst of light to absorb. In exchange, POKENAME help increment a counter to indicate a bag of rice is donated to a charitable organization.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are doting creatures that love their Trainers. If their Trainer gets hurt, they wrap the wound with vines and give their Trainer kisses on the head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fluid secreted from their tails is poisonous to most things and is flung to defend themselves. They sometimes use it to leave markings on their own flowers and leaves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is quite gentle, enjoying the company of various Bug-type Pokémon that come to pollinate its flowers. Bouquets made from POKENAME's flowers are very popular all year-round.
author: mepp.

entry: When POKENAME produces its milk, the flower on its back releases a sweet aroma that can spread for many miles. If anyone dares to damage the farm it lives on, it punishes them by striking with its horns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The buds carried by POKENAME have the power to numb pain, as simply being nearby can soothe inflammation. The weight of the flowerpot is negligible, but the size of the flower obscures its vision.
author: oreee0230

entry: The pot that POKENAME carries on its back is filled with a liquid that turns into incense as soon as it flows out. While there is a legend that POKENAME can bring wealth, approaching it is difficult as the plants around it produce sparks.
author: oreee0230

entry: The flower bud atop its head continuously grows as its leaves absorb sunlight. It will often lie in fields of grass and flowers, sometimes blending in so well that others accidentally step on it.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME flies to areas with lots of sunlight by propelling itself forward with a burst of air. Although the gas released carries a floral fragrance, the sand particles in it may cause lung disease.
author: oreee0230

entry: As POKENAME continues to grow, many different species of plants grow on their back. Many small Pokémon retreat behind POKENAME when running from predators, as they often intervene to scare the predator away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME requires lots of energy for its bulb, which constantly zaps energy from its body. Trainers are known to give it batteries to eat, as they are a safe and quick method of energizing their POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bulb on POKENAME's head constantly sheds petals, leaving a trail behind it as it runs through the woods. If threatened, it will use the vines on its head to launch skyward and dropkick its foes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's head looks like a flower bud, but it is made out of a stony shell. The real flower bud lies within the gap on its head and releases a viscous, bitter brine that flows like honey.
author: oreee0230

entry: When POKENAME absorbs too much sunlight, it dispels this energy through the bud on its tail. This causes plants nearby to suddenly grow.
author: soup1900

entry: It is a rather rotund Pokémon, yet it does have strong muscles to support the growing plant atop its head. It will shake trees to loose the nuts and fruits within them, but sometimes damages the tree in the process.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a territorial creature and will clear plants growing within its domain. Its slender flower buds can sense plants that sprout.
author: oreee0230

entry: During spring, tiny flowers bloom across POKENAME's body. Though they taste like plain soil, the flowers are highly nutritious and valued as emergency food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rest atop tall trees with their leafy wings spread apart. To knock free fruits, or to open nuts, they loose shockwaves with beats of their wings. They tend to leave trails of rich pollen behind them as they fly.
author: infinex21

entry: The bud on POKENAME's body has no scent whatsoever, no matter how big and healthy it gets. The bud only ever blooms when directly exposed to blue light; no other types of light affect the growth of the bud.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are arboreal Pokémon that form tight-knit communities, looking after one another when sick or injured. They use the flowers on their tails to communicate, using the unique scents of their tails to identify one another.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME dwells in dense forests, blending among ferns and leaves to ambush small prey. The bud on its back releases a soothing aroma that eases stress and relieves headaches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME traverse the forest floor and use the dense undergrowth to hide in when they anticipate predators. They peer out of the bushes with their long neck while they wait for danger to pass.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It will often scatter leaves and seeds at foes and then use its flames to set it all ablaze. Its strong legs let it jump around, and its vines help it better navigate forest homes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rarely exposes its head and limbs above ground, tunneling just below the surface. The flower on its back has a bitter taste and a foul scent, ensuring it never needs to worry about predation.
author: oreee0230

entry: In dry seasons, masses of small flowers grow from POKENAME's skin. It uses sharp claws to groom them from its kin, as leaving them too long can cause caustic burns.
author: .izik

entry: When injured in combat, POKENAME can draw nutrients from the bulb on its head and receive a burst of energy to keep fighting. After combat, POKENAME will find a sunny place to lie down and rest, replenishing the bulb's lost energy.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME splash around and play in jungle rivers, communicating with loud cries to one another through the dense undergrowth. They leave the water during the hottest parts of the day, cuddling together to snooze in the sun.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time partially submerged in the mud of swamps, passively absorbing nutrients from around them and from sunlight. They are capable of a surprising turn of speed when disturbed, but prefer to flee rather than fight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can sense the feelings of others. If it notices someone is feeling down, it will emanate a sweet scent in hopes of brightening the Trainer's mood.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are strongest when their Trainer believes in their success, as this positive energy invigorates them. They can overcome adversity with powerful Vine Whips if their Trainer believes in them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has strong psychic abilities and needs deep concentration while in the sun to focus its powers. It can predict when flowers will bloom, and will bring its Trainer over to enjoy the flowers together.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME hover high up amongst the crown of trees, staying close to the flowers in the canopy. They are strangely unaffected by the weather, remaining entirely stationary even as the trees around them sway in the breeze.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME absorb water through their skin and the cacti on their back. When mature, the cacti fall onto the ground behind them, creating a source of nutrition for desert scavengers.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in poisonous thorns that protect the bud growing on its back. The fragrance of its still-closed petals can soothe anyone who breathes it in, which is why it is often used in the preparation of certain tranquilizers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are able to change their colouration by concentrating or dispersing the chlorophyll in their skin. They use this ability to hide amongst foliage and ambush Bug-Type Pokémon with their long, sticky tongue.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It doesn't need to eat for long periods of time thanks to its powerful photosynthesizing abilities. It is believed that when two POKENAME interlace their vines, an evolution will occur.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The sturdiness of POKENAME's legs is said to rival steel. Energy from the sun causes its budding agility to begin to bloom into something grander.
author: mysteriouswraith

entry: POKENAME resembles a flower bud in a planter. When it releases spores, it steals the life of plants within its range.
author: oreee0230

entry: An unexplained occurrence during the fusion process caused Ivysaur's bulb to sprout early. Its body can barely support the weight of the tree.
author: fixthewifi

entry: POKENAME is a proud fighter. It swoops down on unsuspecting Fighting-type Pokémon for duels. Pokémon fusion has given it a majestic visage reminiscent of human Karate masters.
author: lupa

entry: The bulb on its back is not fully ready to bloom yet. It is quite sluggish since it uses most of its energy to grow its bulb.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME often gather in sunny spots to absorb sunlight. Because of its gentle nature, it is extremely rare for fighting to occur when they come together.
author: _._starry_._

entry: Although the back of POKENAME's head is actually a big mouth disguised as a flower bud, the liquid that flows out is real nectar. Because the bud-shaped mouth cannot open very wide, POKENAME tends to prefer capturing smaller prey.
author: oreee0230

entry: The many smaller buds snap and grab small insects to feed to POKENAME's true head in the center. Due to meals taking a long time to reach its stomach, it often overeats and winds up sluggish after feeding.
author: sk372

entry: The mouths on its vines chew and digest food before giving it to the main mouth to absorb nutrients. Although the main body crawls slowly, the vines can detach, move quickly, and remain active for several weeks.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are ancient Pokémon that predate land plants. Revived fossils show that they lived at the water's surface photosynthesising, leading Palaeontologists to theorise they were key to filling the early atmosphere with oxygen.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in shallow waters in tropical regions, floating near the surface of the water whilst hiding amongst water plants. They get most of their energy from sunlight but will hunt smaller Pokémon if the opportunity presents itself.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use the flower on their tail as a lure, drawing attention away from their body with its bright petals. They use this distraction both to ward away larger Pokémon and to help them lay ambushes on their own prey.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Ancient flora sprouts from its head and back. The bulb on its head is surprisingly tough, and can be used to beat down prey.
author: bunkachunka

entry: POKENAME use their armoured head to help protect the delicate flower growing upon their backs. They always face their foes head on, refusing to expose their vulnerable backs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their armoured head to help protect the delicate flower growing upon their backs. They always face their foes head on, refusing to expose their vulnerable backs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME pollen is a major irritant for a majority of Pokémon and people. Large families of POKENAME that flower at the same time are able to drive other Pokémon from their territory purely through the pollen they release.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's bulb needs more nutrients to bloom, so it roams in search of spots to soak up sunshine. It chases off bug types that prey on weaker grass type Pokémon.
author: porpoisemerchant

entry: POKENAME's legs have grown strong to allow it to leap through the canopy of the massive forests that grow in the ancient caves it calls home.
author: veteranadventurer

entry: This Pokémon can be found floating through the tropical oceans, hanging around near rainforests and jungles. It can spin the leaves on its back like a fan, propelling itself through the water or creating whirlpools.
author: ecstaticwoop64556455

entry: The bud on POKENAME's back oozes a pigment that changes the color of its shell. This pigment is also a widely used agricultural fertilizer.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered with grass, which relies on the sunlight that passes through POKENAME's leaves to survive. The grass provides perfect camouflage, both in color and in smell.
author: oreee0230

entry: Although the buds on the tree on POKENAME's back look like peaches, they are not suitable for consumption. These buds, which never bloom, lock in a charming scent and are often picked to be used as fragrance.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME live in tropical jungles, staying high in the canopy and never coming down to the ground. They swing across vast distances in search of fruit, scattering pollen from their flowers in their wake.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME traverse through small but sudden hops. Before evolving, they find a secluded warm spot and stop moving.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME form tight knit family groups that contain multiple generations. The adults take turns watching over the young and elderly whilst their peers search for fruit, navigating home by the unique combination of scents from their flowers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fight with a nimble combat style that makes them popular with Black Belts, using every part of their body to rain down blows. What appears to be a tail is actually a flexible vine that can extend or retract, granting incredible mobility.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME, even if wild, are very diligent about keeping themselves and their leaves clean, so they are often seen near, or in, streams and rivers. The longer their leaves are, the more prideful and uppity POKENAME will be.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will lie on their bellies in patches of nutrient-rich mud, their plant bulbs facing toward the sun. This seems to keep them cool and further nourished as they let their bulbs absorb and process sunlight.
author: infinex21

entry: Though still a functional club, POKENAME prefers to put its opponents to sleep with the aroma emanating from its bulb.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The foliage on POKENAME's back conceals poisonous thorns that protect its heavy bulb from predators.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME's overgrowth has started to bloom. As it grows heavier, it can put more force behind its swinging attacks. A well-aimed strike could slice through stone pillars.
author: ocxin

entry: Seen around lakes deep in the forest, POKENAME has a large bulb on its tail. With enough sunlight, this bud will bloom into a large flower.
author: fuzzythelion

entry: Seeing an POKENAME is said to be a good omen; however, it's advised not to get too close, as its feelers can deliver painful, whipping blows to its enemies.
author: flickeredflame

entry: The petals of POKENAME emit a pleasant floral scent when it is happy. POKENAME can often be found napping in the sun.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME live together with those of similar species. Competitive and desperate to evolve further, they tend to eat additional food rather than just photosynthesizing. However, they always make sure young Nidoran have plenty to eat first.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body has a complex array of plants sprawling across its body. When it releases its power, plants grow uncontrollably over a wide area, causing a burst of greenery to emerge from the soil.
author: oreee0230

entry: Living in the ozone layer allows POKENAME's flower bulbs to absorb large amounts of sunlight. It holds this charge when it descends to the ground, letting it unleash a powerful Solar Beam as its first strike in combat.
author: sk372

entry: It can distort space such that its vines can extend to near-infinite lengths. As the bulb on its back grows, so too does the gravity in POKENAME's vicinity.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It releases spores from its leaves to lull opponents to sleep. Anyone affected by these spores experiences wretched nightmares.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME can absorb moonlight as readily as it can absorb sunlight. It rests in open fields during the day and awakens at night to play.
author: oreee0230

entry: The leaves on the arms of POKENAME have a unique fragrance, while the flower bud on its head is actually odorless. Relying on the highly toxic trichomes on its leaves, POKENAME can effectively hunt prey like Rattata.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME have an elaborate head flower that covers their eyes, leaving them to rely on their other senses to navigate the world. These flowers enable them to establish societal hierarchies, larger and more elaborate flowers denoting higher status.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's plasma mimics the shape of a flower bud and allows it to stabilize electric charges. POKENAME is often trained to use its plasma vines to temporarily maintain power supply during blackouts.
author: oreee0230

entry: The bud on POKENAME's back emits a strong fragrance under the moonlight. Once it hears Trainers nearby, wild POKENAME will stop moon-gazing and hide.
author: oreee0230

entry: Though its bulb gives off a pleasant aroma, Pokémon Rangers caution Trainers against getting too close, as POKENAME's nectar is incredibly flammable. The bulb requires both sunlight and the life force of nearby creatures in order to grow.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME flutter across the jungle, searching for pollen to ignite their flame. POKENAME are protectors of the jungle, attacking people who cause damage to the jungle forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME burn pollen from within their flowers to produce thick hazes of smoke that conceal their flames. They incapacitate people who cause destruction to the jungle and carry them out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME actively hunt for empty jungle ruins to settle in. The plants sprawling across their body fill in cracks and wounds that may have accumulated over the years. These plants rely on the core's energy to continue growing.
author: oreee0230

entry: The grassy fur of POKENAME is filled with tiny, highly fragrant buds that it uses to attract other members of its species. After resting for many hours under the sun, the flames it can control become more intense.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have their eyes covered by the petals growing down from the crown of their heads, obscuring their vision. They overcompensate for their poor vision by being particularly aggressive, pre-emptively attacking anything they think is a threat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's fur is highly nutritious for plant growth. It's leafy tails are actually plants that grew on its body.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME are described as lazy and uncooperative because they rarely move from one spot. They release a network of vines to move sticks and branches to create dams.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in jungles with dense foliage. When hunting, POKENAME ensnares prey with its vine-like tail before electrocuting them with a powerful shock.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME feed on mineral rich rocks and mud to provide nutrients for the flower blooming on their back. Their flowers have a uniquely rich, earthy smell to them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are able to blend into dense undergrowth easily, the flowers and leaves lining their spine easily camouflaging them. They spend their days lazing out of sight, confident that should they be found their thick body armour will protect them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME constantly produce small yet heavy seeds on their leaves, so whenever they are about to fly, they rapidly vibrate their wings to shake the seeds off. These seeds are swiftly picked up by hungry Pokémon, leaving few seeds behind to sprout.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After absorbing sunlight, POKENAME search the lakebeds for anything shiny. They seem particularly excited by the bright scales of other Pokémon.
author: smashbear

entry: The bulbs on their heads grow heavier with every day, so their bodies are always dense with muscle. They long for the day that their bulbs will bloom into flowers and will flee to keep to their bulbs safe.
author: infinex21

entry: The plates of their shells have the composition of roots and help carry nutrients and water from their flower buds to their actual bodies. Though their legs are small, they are dense with muscle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME slowly opens up its flower bud by rotating its gear-shaped body. When the flower bud is ready to bloom, it evolves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bud on POKENAME's back contains a specially shaped cavity that can amplify its singing. Since its leaves can also be used for breathing, POKENAME's singing can continue without needing to take a breath.
author: oreee0230

entry: Its flower is in a special state of blooming and not blooming at the same time. This gives it a unique aroma no other flower has.
author: soup1900

entry: The more vibrant the bud on its tail is, the more energetic POKENAME becomes. A smoke-like aroma from the bud indicates that it's about to bloom.
author: soup1900

entry: It is very proud of the bulb on its tail. If the plant ever withers away, POKENAME will die with it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME soar through the sky releasing clouds of pollen beneath them. When resting, they wrap their vines around tree branches to prevent themselves from being blown away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The more loved POKENAME feels, the brighter the pink buds on its ears become. After absorbing enough energy, it can leap gracefully into the air thanks to its powerful, athletic legs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are in near constant competition for berries and often miss out on a meal because of their slow bodies. They release spores that can cause Pokémon many times their body weight to fall asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have tiny flowers sprouting from the top of their heads, a sweet scent emanating from them. The nectar from these flowers makes a wonderful perfume and POKENAME are very sought after by aromatherapists.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: These forest Pokémon are often seen hanging from branches, their leafy bodies swaying in the wind. POKENAME are said to feed on negative emotions, which might explain why they drop nuts and berries on passersby.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME release psychic waves that cause plants in the nearby flowers to rapidly mature. Once in full bloom, POKENAME eat these flowers by absorbing them into their sap bubble that rapidly dissolves the flower into its base components.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fly out at night to pollinate flowers by rubbing the flower on their back against wildflowers. Their weak, underdeveloped eyes face away from the sun when dawn arrives to absorb sunlight with the bulb on their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are parasitic Pokémon, using their sharp incisors to bite through tree bark and feed on the sap within their branches. Large infestations can leave an afflicted tree looking as though it's in full bloom despite being very unhealthy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME connect their roots to other plants in the nearby area and steal vital nutrients from crops and wildlife. Their thorny exterior makes it difficult to uproot them without specialized techniques.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME now have enough energy to self-sustain without vines. They instead have a small flower on their head that photosynthesizes for them.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Seeding sprouts from its tiny frame, POKENAME glides with petal-formed wings. Its legs, sturdy yet agile, bear its floral adornment.
author: anarchaz

entry: The bodies of POKENAME are mostly made up of their flower, fine downy leaves surrounding their face as petals trail out from behind their bodies. They hang upside down from tree branches when they sleep and can be easily mistaken for tree flowers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It uses its gaping maw to snatch large fruits and nuts, which it will then drain dry of all their juices using its sharp fangs. Though it will also eat the drained fruit, it will spit out the nuts without a care for where they land.
author: infinex21

entry: The waxy leaves that form POKENAME's shells smell like rubber. To escape predators while they prepare for evolution, they whirl their entire bodies and slam their flexible bulbs into the ground, bouncing away to safety.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME slowly rotates its body to allow equal light to strike its leaves. A well-cared-for POKENAME may allow Trainers to pick its leaves for use in salads.
author: busilisk

entry: POKENAME keep low in the undergrowth when they're feeding, using the leaves and flowers covering their bodies to camouflage themselves. When they're feeling endangered, they rear up and rustle their leaves in a threat display.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME roams the tropical rainforests it calls home. The flower on its back seems to have mellowed its stubborn nature, though it will attack Pokémon who irritate it using its vines.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: When frightened or cold, POKENAME wraps its cloak-like leaves tightly around its body. Its flower will only bloom when POKENAME is happy and feels completely safe.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME drift silently through the air, twirling in the sunlight and revelling in attention. They are jealous Pokémon and will puff out a Sleep Powder at anyone they view as a rival for attention.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME releases spores whenever it is excited. These spores are toxic to other Pokémon, so it becomes confused whenever they refuse to play with it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's vines are thicker and longer than its pre-evolution's, causing them to be heavier and less ribbon-like. The bulb on its back gives off a spicy scent when it's ready to bloom.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME has a body that is covered with various plants. Its body can support the growth of these plants by allowing them to feed off its sludge, but then they become toxic to Trainers and Pokémon.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME swim through the ocean by rocking their flowery tail back and forth to push them through the water. The petals left behind get eaten by small aquatic Water-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bulbs on the back of POKENAME act as a propeller in the absence of a fin. The bulbs spew vitamins and minerals that are extremely nourishing to the plants on the sea floor.
author: bradlybro199

entry: This Pokémon never seems to rest, though it does appear to move slower when exposed to sunlight; moonlight, however, fills it with energy. An POKENAME's bulb-like head will release a pungent aroma as it grows nearer to opening when it evolves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is protective of its forest home to an almost overzealous degree. The instant it senses an intruder, it sends out multiple vines to grab and toss them away.
author: sk372

entry: The dew on its leaves contains a potent poison secreted from the bulb. POKENAME is unaware of the danger, and offers the dew to passersby anyway.
author: volvonovic

entry: POKENAME flaps aggressively to get high in the sky, where it can better disperse its pollen and attract Bug-type friends. Its white cotton is evidence of its tidy crepuscular lifestyle.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME flaps aggressively to get high in the sky, where it can better disperse its pollen and attract Bug-type friends. Its green photosynthetic cotton is a sure sign it's getting lots of nutrition and sunlight.
author: haypile

entry: An POKENAME is covered with a thin layer of slime that keeps its bud fresh. It has a ravenous appetite as it awaits evolution.
author: .realthree

entry: A sweet-smelling yet highly poisonous nectar flows from the top of POKENAME's head, which it uses to lure prey. Because of its underwhelming and clumsy movement, many of its prey are not afraid even when they realize POKENAME is nearby.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME prefers to live in bright deserts surrounded by the sun, absorbing the glowing rays. To protect the cactus on its head, it abstains from hunting to minimize its risk of injury.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME connect their vines to root systems to siphon nutrients from other plants. They carefully maintain the bulbs on their back by clipping damaged leaves and drinking lots of water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME expends a small amount of nutrients to produce a small decoy that looks like a Bulbasaur. Its bud can reach four meters high and envelops foes in a sandy tomb when it hunts.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME will come up and rest their head on their Trainer's lap whenever their Trainer sits down. Their leaves fan out and form a blanket across their Trainer, passively absorbing energy from sunlight while POKENAME snoozes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fluff out their petal mane when they engage in territorial disputes. The POKENAME with the healthiest and most vibrant mane is usually the one to make the other back down.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fluff out their leaf mane when they engage in territorial disputes. The POKENAME with the healthiest and most vibrantly green mane is usually the one to make the other back down.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In many ancient settlements, failing to show gratitude upon seeing POKENAME was regarded as a provocation to the settlement. Many people were willing to give everything just to hear POKENAME's singing.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME scatter pollen wherever they go, dancing and twirling through clouds to give themselves a beautiful flourish. Many influencers enjoy taking photos of POKENAME, as these clouds of pollen accentuate their beauty.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its petals release an incredibly sweet fragrance that soothes the dreams of anyone nearby. It is believed that POKENAME watches over forests and appears to oppose great evils.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The parasitic flower on its back boosts its immune system in exchange for nutrients. POKENAME drinks sweet tree resin to keep its petals fragrant and brightly colored.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME consumes large amounts of debris it encounters to supplement its nutrition. POKENAME concentrates the waste from the debris on its outermost petals and periodically sheds them.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME likes to decorate its body with vines, flowers and the like to make itself feel prettier. It will even use its own vines to pluck flora off of other Pokémon if it finds them appealing enough.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME accumulate seeds inside their flower bud, waiting for the right opportunity to strike. A burst of these small pellet seeds wrap around their targets to prevent escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The scent of POKENAME's bud often attracts predators. However, its leaves are as sharp as blades, protecting the growing bud from serious harm.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: POKENAME can be quite shy and hide in flower petals to avoid making eye contact with other Pokémon. When they are particularly anxious, they release toxic spores to scare away those they do not want to interact with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wooden shell is hard and restores itself quickly. The bud on POKENAME's head may look like a vulnerable weak point, but it is extremely tough because of its high cellulose content.
author: oreee0230

entry: Its lush fur will become more vibrant during the tropical season. Due to its humid environment, POKENAME radiates excess heat from the leaves in its ears.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its fern-shaped wings are coated in an incredibly irritating substance, preventing other Pokémon from accidentally trying to eat them. It drinks the juice of the sweetest berries deep in the forest to help the pink bud on its abdomen bloom.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME remains firmly buried in the ground unless disturbed. The cosmic energy it emits causes nearby plants to grow warped and strange.
author: robbery_666

entry: When the bud on its tail blooms, a tiny flame is revealed. It will sometimes intentionally do this in battle to surprise foes who attack it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's round red nose releases a sweet apple-like scent. While pleasant, the aroma unintentionally attracts nearby predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found swimming in marshlands in great schools. Their favorite food is the pink flowers formed when lily pads bloom.
author: victor9106

entry: POKENAME become active at sunrise, stretching their leafy wings to take in sunlight. Bug-type Pokémon are known to nibble on the edges of their wings, leaving them with small holes and unique patterns.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME leaves its hiding place only to let the petals protecting its body stay healthy and vibrant. If someone discovers its location, it releases a soothing pollen that puts predators to sleep.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In order to accumulate nutrients for its buds, POKENAME's endless appetite causes it to eat all nearby plants. In the forests that POKENAME are native to, people report seeing plants being dragged underground to be eaten by an POKENAME.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME spreads its vines up to 100 meters beneath the soil to locate water. Once found, it digs directly toward the source with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives high in forest trees, spending its time observing those down below. The petals and leaves that grow on POKENAME can be brewed into a soothing tea.
author: mepp.

entry: The bud on POKENAME's head can secrete a thick sap, which contains chemicals that most predators find repulsive. This sap can be processed to extract various spices and seasonings.
author: oreee0230

entry: Plant-based food is not nutritious enough for the three buds, so POKENAME often prey on other Grass-type Pokémon. The scent of the buds makes prey docile, allowing POKENAME to drag them into the ground the moment they relax.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME use their ivy-like tails to swing from branch to branch, often picking up items and money dropped in forests while they travel. They carry Bulbath from the lower branches where they are born to the canopies where they mature.
author: alextheperson

entry: POKENAME's tail is not yet strong enough to hold up its flower bud. When it shakes under the strain, POKENAME will immediately chase it, tantalised by its movement.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: To enhance its abilities, POKENAME spends the entire day meditating under the sunlight, absorbing chlorophyll through the petals on its head. Its mastery of Zen Headbutt makes it a formidable opponent in battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To enhance its abilities, POKENAME spends the entire day meditating under the sunlight, absorbing chlorophyll through the petals on its head. Its mastery of Zen Headbutt makes it a formidable opponent in battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Moving gracefully and almost without sound, POKENAME blends perfectly into the undergrowth. Its whiskers detect warmth from sunlight, allowing it to pinpoint clearings where it can absorb solar energy to nourish the flower on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME relies on the bulb on its head to speak with plants. Prolonged communication with plants causes strong headaches that may take hours to recover from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME release toxic fumes from the buds along their bodies, warding off predators. The closer these buds are to blooming, the more potent this poison becomes.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME relies on the bulb on its back to speak with plants. Prolonged communication with plants causes powerful migraines that may take hours to recover from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are swift swimmers that can cross lakes in a few seconds. They have a unique swimming method that ensures the bulb on their back remains above water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME opens its mouth, the upper part of its head completely hovers in the air under the influence of psychic power. It only moves while in sunlight and falls asleep when it is dark.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME leaves a fragrance behind when it flies. The bud under its neck produces honey, which is often used for brewing.
author: oreee0230

entry: With its long vine-like tendrils, it retrieves objects and Pokémon that have fallen into the water, carrying them safely back to land. It needs to live near large bodies of water to keep the fragrant flower on its back healthy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: These Pokémon are always quick to anger, most likely due to the overgrowth of leaves and vines that have overtaken most of their bodies. When an POKENAME starts exhaling spores out from its nose, it is about to fly into a rage.
author: infinex21

entry: Its flower bud opens halfway and the leaves along its body stand on end when it flies into a fit of rage. These fits of rage seem to boost its circulation, which results in the leaves growing even more robust.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's sense of smell ignores the scent of its own flower, letting it identify unknown scents in its territory. It can blast jets of fire from either its mouth or the flower and it increases the potency of the fire by napping in sunlight.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME runs to always seek sunlight for its bulb, even crossing dangerous habitats to keep up with the passage of the day. Since it travels through many regions, the flower on its back becomes healthily pollinated by a variety of other plants.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The bud on its tail spouts an intense flame that doesn't harm its flora. It will burn down dead trees and shrubs to allow room for new ones to grow.
author: soup1900

entry: The large bud growing on its backside makes walking cumbersome. Many POKENAME will instead drift aimlessly in quiet ponds, allowing their buds ample time to absorb nutrients from the sun.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The bud on its tail is always damp, yet it never seems to be overwatered. It gives off a sweet aroma that positively affects whatever it swims in.
author: ichosuzu

entry: POKENAME rubs nectar onto its belly to lure bug Pokémon close. Once they have gathered close enough, they are lulled into a slumber with its hypnotic spiral.
author: oreee0230

entry: Though similar in appearance to standard Ivysaur, the unusual flowers budding from POKENAME's back and hands thrive only within an underwater environment.  Ponds in which these Pokémon are found are said to be nearly completely free of algae.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Before using its psychic powers, the flower on its head releases an intense tulip-like scent. It spends most of its life peacefully sleeping beneath forest trees.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Although POKENAME spends twice as many sleeping hours compared to the time it spends awake, it seems to recover faster while napping in sunlight. Wild POKENAME only appear on sunny days, teleporting away to distant places as soon as it is cloudy.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's buds release powerful psychic energy to supports its weight and levitate in the air. Its spoon seems to be able to fertilize the soil, but only Trainers it trusts are allowed to use this powerful tool.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME trains for hours every day to keep its muscular body in shape and deliver devastating Fighting-type blows. Since it never wants to damage the flower blooming on its back, it never turns its back on its opponents.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME use their own vines to weight train, straining their arms against their vines in order to strengthen them both. They are powerful enough to hoist over 500 kilograms in a single hand.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Although the leaves on POKENAME's head can also absorb sunlight, it still needs to eat to support its high level of physical activity. As it exercises, its flower buds become more vibrant.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME wrap their roots around trees to siphon nutrients from their host. They are protective of the flower bud on their body and will sprout vines to defend it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gather to photosynthesize on hills and get as much sun as they can. They are extremely clumsy and fall over quite often.
author: imagine1.

entry: When POKENAME hangs on a tree, it uses flower buds as a counterweight. If it eats too much at once, it may be forced to spend the night on the ground because the weight of its body and flower buds becomes too great for its muscular tentacles.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through the crystals on its head to focus its energy into laser beams. A stranded POKENAME will try to use vines to grab rocks to pull itself back into the sea, but on a flat beach, it can only wait for the tide to rise.
author: oreee0230

entry: The bud on POKENAME's head can release powerful ultrasonic energy. POKENAME can grow new vines at will and absorb water through them to multiply their length dozens of times.
author: oreee0230

entry: They are found above the clouds on mountaintops, photosynthesizing to grow the bulbs on their backs. The cold conditions in these areas slow their growth, and it often takes years for the bulb to bloom.
author: joeofthealps

entry: POKENAME can often be seen clinging to cliff sides to expose their leaves to the most sunlight possible. Fiercely protective of its bulbs, it has been known to knock rivals out of its favored basking spots and onto the heads of unsuspecting hikers.
author: joeofthealps

entry: POKENAME are typically docile creatures that enjoy soaking up the sun's rays for the flower on their back. However, they become incredibly aggressive whenever they sense that a tree is chopped down, and cause mudslides to scare away lumberjacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The casing around an POKENAME's bulb is constantly heated and cools as it runs, protecting the budding flower inside as if it were made of diamond. Its leaves generate heat after absorbing sunlight, which can last until the next sunrise.
author: oreee0230

entry: The buds and leaves at the end of POKENAME's tail are resistant to flames. When it runs quickly, the flame on its back leaves a trail.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME lures other wild Pokémon toward it by releasing a distinctive aroma from the flower at the tip of its tail. Because it's very lazy, it uses its psychic powers to pick fruit from trees so it doesn't have to climb.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If its bulb grows too large, it'll lose the ability to stand on its hind legs. When people see this, they often mistake POKENAME for a Grotle.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The plant at POKENAME's tail acts like a symbiote. The plant nourishes POKENAME with a continuous supply of energy while POKENAME constantly replenishes the water and minerals used.
author: oreee0230

entry: All of its electricity is now stored in the bulb at the top of its head. It uses its magnet-shaped vines to expel said electricity.
author: mariod246

entry: The charge from its bulb has attracted two other Ivytons. Together, they triple their electric power.
author: mariod246

entry: POKENAME enjoy flaunting their feathers, so they grow flowers that they can practice their grand gestures with. If they fail to charm their opponent in battle, their flowers will grow into powerful thorny vines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have two heads, but only one can communicate, as the flowery head has no eyes and no mouth. It often grows angry at the other head for disrupting pollination but has no effective means to stop it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its three heads help it to maintain balance with its heavy bulb and not fall over. Its long legs are extremely strong as a further result, so it can run for long periods without rest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends long periods of time drifting in the sea. It holds its tail high above itself to photosynthesize energy for evolution.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME take sludge and consume it to produce a green fertilizer from the flowery bulb on their back. Plants that absorb this fertilizer often mutate and develop strange growths, baffling scientists.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The slime it is made of can be used as a poison for weeds and is highly appreciated by gardeners. It doesn't allow anyone to approach the bud it carries, and if someone tries to touch it, POKENAME releases Poison Gas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The inside of its hard shell is where this Pokémon grows its flora, which then pokes out at the bottom to produce a tail shape. When in danger, it will retract this floral tail back into its shell.
author: soup1900

entry: It absorbs sunlight to charge its cannons. Once it is fully charged, it'll fire two powerful Solar Beams that can tear through concrete.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME produce a hazy fog around their bodies that nourishes nearby plants. Their gaseous bodies allow them to slip through damaged walls and reappear on the other side.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's poisonous body has a strong floral fragrance. The areas it inhabits are filled with plants that resist its toxins.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are connected with a set of rigid vines that span their entire body. The network of vines releases minerals that get absorbed into the rocks that comprise their body, making them tougher than the rocks around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feeds off people's dreams to sustain itself. It lulls people asleep by releasing spores while also creating a hypnotic array of petals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses a combination of Hypnosis and powders when battling. Its playful disposition and green thumb make it a popular pick for rural families.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME can absorb nutrients from the soil by filtering it through its mouth, only spitting out dry dust and gravel. If its claws are damaged, it can swiftly regenerate them in just half an hour, as long as it has enough energy and sunlight.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME lives along rocky coastlines, as the flower on its back needs seawater to keep blooming. A generally peaceful creature, it produces bubbles from its mouth to communicate with others of its kind.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME gnaw away at the frames and doors to cellars or pantries. While it is common belief that they are after the cheese stored within, they actually break down the wood grain of the structures to gather nutrients for their bulbs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A POKENAME will constantly seek to eat as much cheese as it can. Once it is full it will begin its evolution process.
author: .izik

entry: Hordes of POKENAME live in abandoned power plants, feasting on the leftover electricity. To show dominance over the rest of the hordes, they will sometimes try to bite through each other's metal shell for more electricity.
author: mistymagius

entry: It will vibrate its whiskers to quickly generate large amounts of electricity. Should one of the whiskers fall off, it will regrow within a day.
author: .izik

entry: It seems that only one of the six egg-shaped creatures is alive. The rest move ominously with psychic energy.
author: .izik

entry: Only one of the 'heads' seems to be sentient. The rest seem to be mask-shaped bark that grow from the trunk.
author: .izik

entry: It gnaws on bones to maintain its teeth, as well as to shape the bones into weapons and armor it can use in battle. When it crafts a new weapon, it passes the old one onto its young.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in caves and tunnel networks that have very few sources of food. They will gnaw on bones to extract marrow from them, going so far as to carry bones with them to feed off when they get hungry.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wield their long tails as whips during battles with other Pokémon, lashing out with them at high speed. Their tails are reinforced internally with dense bones to help them survive the impacts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses its tail like a whip. It often lords over a pack of Rattata that it works to the bone.
author: atlas3339098

entry: Rumor has it that a POKENAME once fled to the sewers with a group of Squirtle in tow. The Squirtle would soon become the nightly vigilantes of Saffron City, with POKENAME as their wisened mentor.
author: violet_zero

entry: POKENAME thrive in sewers, eating trash and thrown-out food to survive. They are incredibly skilled fighters, their tails helping them balance as they unleash flurries of kicks at foes.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is a hardy brawler and will fight on until its last breath. However, any shots to its teeth can cause this Pokémon excruciating pain.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME live together in groups in dirty sewers. Both the gas it emits and its bite transmit numerous diseases.
author: chorb33

entry: A POKENAME is very protective of its nest despite its immobility. Its whiskers can detect even the smallest temperature or climate change.
author: .izik

entry: In rare cases, the tails of Ratfings become so entangled that they can no longer detach and form POKENAME.
author: chorb33

entry: On windy days it will sit on top of large hills and shake its whiskers. This seems to cause the egg on its stomach pouch to wiggle in delight.
author: .izik

entry: It is not quite known how many tails POKENAME actually has. Some specimens have been found to have as few as 4, but others have had as many as 50.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME plays its flute, every Rattata nearby will follow POKENAME. When POKENAME stops playing its flute, all of the Rattata will go away .
author: drip_capybara

entry: POKENAME can be found chewing on the barnacles of boats. Should it run out of barnacles, it will begin chewing on the boat itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a very invasive fusion that hoards flowers from grassy fields, picking every flower there in minutes. They use the nectar from the flowers to create a cheesy-smelling dew from their antennas to feed their young.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: On days where waves are extremely heavy, a group of POKENAME will wrap their tails together to avoid being separated.
author: .izik

entry: If fed cheese, extra tails erupt from POKENAME's body as it screeches for more. It will trap people behind a Barrier if it senses more cheese nearby, thick saliva dripping from its maw.
author: .izik

entry: It dips its tail in lava to test the temperature. Should it be too cold it will blow flames at it in an attempt to heat it further for bathing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a chaotic arrangement of teeth that shred through most food. They can easily shred gamy meat and break apart bones but have a difficult time eating fatty parts of prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Once a POKENAME finds a wedge of cheese it will fiercely defend it until it is exhausted. The horn's poison is weak and barely causes itching.
author: .izik

entry: After eating new food from a dumpster, POKENAME instinctively transforms into it. During this time, it cannot revert, even if threatened.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swim near beaches in search of trash, using their sharp fangs to tear through garbage. They use their tails like rudders to steer as they swim.
author: santon5512

entry: Created in a Team Rocket lab, POKENAME was originally made to hack financial info for companies. It was ineffective and later abandoned.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its paws to angrily pull itself across the ground at any enemy that gets too close to its nest. It then squeaks to alert its allies.
author: .izik

entry: Its whiskers 'taste' the ocean floor for things it can eat. Should it find anything delicious it will descend upon its prey and quickly consume it.
author: .izik

entry: A combination of traits make this fusion suitable for a uniquely arboreal lifestyle. It swoops down from trees to snatch food from passersby.
author: vaporvenator

entry: POKENAME's whiskers are able to sense cheese from miles away. They will constantly gorge themselves on cheese, storing extra in their fur for later.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are very active Pokémon that are difficult to pin down thanks to their sinuous bodies. Their fur grows quickly and comes away from their body easily, letting them pull free from even the tightest grip.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have rough, coarse fur that helps to protect them from the worst impacts of status effects. Their tails have no fur at all and can be moved rapidly, letting POKENAME use it as a whip to attack with.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While its fur may often look disheveled, POKENAME carefully preens itself to avoid matting.  Eating anything that moves, it gnaws on the bones of its prey to wear down its ever-growing front teeth.
author: empty_set

entry: A POKENAME queen produces two kinds of honey. One that is safe and consumable to its hive, and one that is toxic to wild Pokémon. POKENAME hives are always filled with this toxic honey, which can make an Ursaring's luckiest day turn instantly sour.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: It hides in reeds by small streams and ponds to stay away from others. If it is discovered, it will let off a sweet odor from its leaf.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its front paws to dig into the ground. It then feeds on plant roots with its sharp beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME forage for wild berries throughout the year to store up supplies for winter. Their diet mainly consists of Lum Berries, which cure them of any ailments they may have.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wraps its body around trash cans to keep others away from its find. Once it's done eating, it abandons the can without a second glance.
author: .izik

entry: It quickly spins its tail to fly for short distances. It prefers to perch in dying trees so that it can chew on the decaying bark.
author: .izik

entry: If it senses cheese being eaten in someone's dream, POKENAME perches outside their window. It then uses Dream Eater to consume the fantasy.
author: .izik

entry: It hops from grass patch to grass patch looking for Berries. Should it find even one, it will greedily store it in a hollow log.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will wag its tail slowly before taking flight. Once in the air, it will look for food to bring back to its favorite log.
author: .izik

entry: After cocooning prey in its silk, POKENAME will consume the webbing along with its meal. The recovered extra nutrients from the web help maintain its large teeth, keeping them strong and clean.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are solitary hunters, often taking down Pokémon twice their size with their incredibly toxic bite. They make nests in filth-filled alleys and often fight each other over the best spots.
author: mistymagius

entry: It can chew through wood in seconds, and it leads a colony of other bat-like Pokémon. It is considered by homeowners to be one of the worst pests.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The feathers that cover its body are extremely abrasive. It needs to be careful when caring for its young to avoid scratching them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will actively steal items from travelers who aren't paying attention. Regardless of the item, it will chew on it until nothing is left.
author: .izik

entry: It frequently trips while playing. Occasionally, parts of the shell will fall off of its body and it will scramble to pick them up.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its tail to keep its balance, wobbling around occasionally. It makes small chittering noises while it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: The whiskers on either side of its body are used to sense changes in the humidity. Should it become too humid it will shake back and forth.
author: .izik

entry: If fed cheese, POKENAME's visions of the future become erratic. It repeatedly sees mundane images, like a coat being zipped or grass being stepped on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have rows of dentine lining the edges of their wings; these tooth-like structures rattle against one another seemingly randomly. Researchers have determined that this happens a few minutes before POKENAME receive visions of the future.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The purple wool on its head generates electricity as it rests. If the wool grows too long it will let loose sparks while walking.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers to make its nest near Green Apricorn trees. Should the tree grow old, POKENAME will use its fangs to cut it down from the base.
author: .izik

entry: Sparks crackle from POKENAME's fangs when it's angry. During this period, it may shock nearby friends or foes without realizing it.
author: .izik

entry: The ball on its tail is made of a wood-like substance. While it walks a sound of something rattling around inside can be heard.
author: .izik

entry: Its fluffy ears are actually unable to hear sound. It will store different nuts and Berries within them.
author: .izik

entry: The fluffy balls on each arm are filled with a sour liquid. Should one fall off, it will flee from the area while squeaking.
author: .izik

entry: The flower on its head rotates slowly as it moves. When it is angry it will spin fast, causing spores to float around the area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats in the sky to soak up as much sunlight as possible. If sunlight is not available, POKENAME sustains itself on bark.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: POKENAME protects young Rattata by housing them in its fluffy extremities. In turn, the weight they add helps stop POKENAME from being blown away in the wind.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Trainers should avoid petting POKENAME unless offering its favorite food. This agile and slippery Rattata has the bite force of its evolution and can leave painful wounds that take a long time to heal.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Its knotted tails act like a third arm, mainly being used to swipe things that catch its eye. When in danger, POKENAME can chew off its tail to use as a distraction.
author: mistymagius

entry: It needs to drink copious amounts of water every day. Should it not drink enough the sprout on its head will fall off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will fiercely defend even the smallest amount of water. It sits near puddles and actively growls at anyone who gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can fly faster on an empty stomach. It will goes days without eating so that it can have an easier time hunting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will nibble at dams built by Bidoof to ensure proper flow of waterways, where it swims with its webbed feet in search of food.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME likes to swim lazily in the river, often losing its way and bumping into boats. When it does this, it seizes an opportunity to gnaw through the hull in search of snacks.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME goes around intentionally ruining expensive items like handbags and clothing by chewing large holes in them. It will even chew through gold jewelry just out of spite.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its head grows a spongy cheese-like substance. Should anyone get too close to its head, it will use telekinesis to fling them away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME topples over trash cans by shooting vines from the bulb on its back. It rummages through the resulting pile of trash in search of rotten food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Reports state POKENAME commands small legions of Raticate in secret. These legions work together to assert control over routes.
author: planatical

entry: The hairs on its head grow as fast as its fangs. It often has to pare down its luscious locks by chewing on them.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME's sharp instincts make it a master scavenger. It leaves behind faint glyph-like marks wherever it searches, which some researchers believe serve as warnings to others.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It harasses its opponent by squeaking, attempting to provoke a strike. If successful, it will retaliate by sinking its fangs into the attacker.
author: .izik

entry: The back half has taken on the appearance and disposition of the front half's Alolan variant. It is far greedier than the main head, fighting it for every meal despite not being able to digest.
author: sk372
