entry: POKENAME conceals a set of wings in its dark pelt, allowing it to launch graceful jumps. Its refined bearing makes it coveted for Pokémon Contests, yet its flame-handling skills and unyielding horn also grant it strength and versatility in battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME burrows into the sides of maple trees using its horn, remaining hidden while it drinks the sap. If disturbed, it tunnels deeper into the bark to escape detection.
author: .izik

entry: Using its wings for balance, POKENAME performs acrobatic martial arts techniques. Its kicks are so precise and powerful they can shatter marble slabs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fight each other for the best spots in trees. Their slow nature means that fights may take weeks to complete.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: While running, POKENAME often underestimates its speed, causing it to slam into obstacles as it cannot stop in time. Whatever it collided with ends up demolished while the Pokémon remains unharmed and continues to race around.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME lives in great redwood forests, propelling itself from tree to tree with its wings. It uses its horn to excavate nutritious sap.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: A wild POKENAME is a rare sight to see, living only in the tangled underwater roots of mangroves. POKENAME are completely solitary and will fight other aquatic Pokémon for territory.
author: mochauspocus

entry: POKENAME will gather in large groups in the spring. They will compete to see who can throw their opponent the farthest. They can't throw very far due to their small size.
author: elite01.

entry: Using the liquid surrounding its body, POKENAME absorbs any honey it finds as food. This can cause it to swell when it obtains too much.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME floats effortlessly between trees, cracking bark with its horn. It feeds on the sap within, leaving trails of stripped trunks behind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feeds on certain species of cactus that produce a sweet, milky sap it finds irresistible. The horn-shaped protrusion on its tail is used as a weapon to fend off other desert Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME locates large honey sources and then sticks to them, warding off predators with its many spikes.
author: incognito1234

entry: Once it sinks its fangs into a tree, it refuses to let go until it's had its fill. If POKENAME is not forcibly removed, it may drain a tree completely of its nutrients and leave it a wilting husk.
author: sk372

entry: The many claws near its neck let it attach to trees to better eat the sweet sap from their bark. It is a curious sort, and seems unaware of its size and stature potentially being frightful to smaller creatures.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a singular horn that they rely on to deter predators. Their dreams are often filled with nightmares of getting eaten by Flying-type Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dances to better focus and utilize its psychic powers. Using telekinesis, it pries other creatures off of trees so it alone can peel off the tree's bark and get to the sweet sap beneath.
author: sk372

entry: A mischievous creature, POKENAME like to poke humans with its horn before quickly disappearing.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME secretes acid from the tip of its horn to bore holes into trees, allowing it to drink the sap inside. Its body emits a faint, sweet scent that attracts other Bug-type Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: A very stubborn Pokémon, POKENAME is usually seen trying to lift objects many times its own weight, oftentimes failing.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME has the ability to produce a thick, earthy honey from its tail. This honey is a popular delicacy in many regions.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME has been seen frequently aiding logging companies, using its large horn to help carry large tree trunks. After large storms, POKENAME can be seen trying to clear away debris.
author: mistymagius

entry: They seek out the bitter sap from plants that are avoided by other bug-type Pokémon. They combine this sap in their gut with a sandy grit, creating a substance that makes a great base for toothpaste.
author: vic1312

entry: It growls and barks to warn others not to come too close to its den, but if its warnings are ignored it charges with its rock-hard horn. POKENAME can be easily lured out with honey, which it is extremely fond of.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME loves to drink tree nectar. If anything tries to take from a tree it has claimed, POKENAME attacks it viciously with its horn and claws.
author: ferdirenz

entry: POKENAME collects sap from nearby pine trees and carries it back to its massive mushroom colonies. The fungi on its back thrive on the rich nutrients, allowing them to grow even larger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has no interest in Pokémon weaker than itself; it usually scares away smaller Pokémon by rubbing its wings together, which sounds like clanging scales. POKENAME are known to attack Exeggutor in the wild, chewing on their leaves.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME rests its horn on the ground to sense vibrations of nearby movement. If it detects danger, it flees without hesitation.
author: .izik

entry: It idolizes Heracross and great fighters. Even its clumsy imitations of their moves are effective, thanks to the toxic powder it kicks up.
author: pokepower

entry: After consuming enough birch sap, POKENAME emits a bright light from its torso. The glow pulses in time with its breathing.
author: .izik

entry: Drawn to trees under streetlamps, POKENAME feeds on their illuminated sap. If disturbed while eating, it retaliates with a burst of Stun Spore.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's powerful horn can rip right through even the toughest of tree roots, making groups of them a danger in forested areas. However, POKENAME is usually careful to not uproot trees, as they love the Honey that tree-dwelling Pokémon can produce.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME headbutt one another as a sign of affection. As sweet honey is not found underwater, POKENAME instead acts as a scavenger and peacefully dines on the fatty remains of discarded prey.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Using their horns, they work together to dig at incredible speeds. It has the power to smash clean through buried obstacles, such as boulders.
author: wigglypon

entry: A tough carapace and horn give POKENAME ample defenses against larger threats. Many sets of armor from Johto's distant past bear a striking resemblance to POKENAME's appearance.
author: sk372

entry: When a suitable tree is found, POKENAME beat their wings together to create a low hum, attracting others to their location. They latch themselves onto the tree and begin drinking its nectar, their lights growing brighter the more they eat.
author: santon5512

entry: It bashes its horn against trees to dig and pry its way within to get to the sweet sap within. The taste of the sap helps soothe the pain of the headache it gets from using its horn.
author: sk372

entry: The clouds POKENAME conjure rain with drops of sweet tree sap. Forests where POKENAME dwell can become quite sticky after a battle.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's lack of visual emotion is often mistaken for callousness. But it selflessly uses its horn to gouge trees, releasing sweet sap, then calls its packmates to feast. It never drinks sap from a tree it tapped, a mark of honour among its kind.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME joust over active volcanoes, duelling with their mighty horns. Their segmented armor is tough as steel and burning hot to the touch.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME fights its opponents by flipping them over with its long horn. It has a difficult time winning drawn-out, protracted fights because of its low stamina.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When tucked into its shell, the horn sticks out from the front. Small feelers let it sense if predators are near, and it can strike the ground with its horn to propel itself away from danger if needed.
author: sk372

entry: A sweet-smelling acid drips from POKENAME's mouth to lure in prey. Once close, it charges with its horn to deliver a brutal strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live deep underground, only digging out from their burrows in search of honey. They battle by rolling into their target at full force before attempting to flip them over.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME are rather weak for the first year they are born and spend their time strengthening their legs and their horns. They use their flames to make themselves look more intimidating than they really are.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME use their strong horns to throw boulders and some Pokémon out of their way as they run. They use their foreclaws to dig into trees to draw forth the sap within and lap it up.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the horn on its forehead to move large boulders that block its path as it swims at high speed in rivers. It has a habit of stockpiling as much fruit as possible in its hiding place and then eating it once it is ripe.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses the leek it carries in combination with other flavorful grasses as a lure. It sets a trap for leaf-loving insects and waits until they get close, then attacks from above with its horn to knock them out.
author: sk372

entry: The larger head is adept at sensing opportune places to feed as well as nearby predators, while the smaller head takes care of defending itself with its mighty horn.
author: sk372

entry: As a young fusion, a typical POKENAME uses both arms to explore the world. These arms naturally express how a POKENAME feels at any given moment, serving as flexible eyebrows.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can use their arms to attack, but they can also be used to emulate extra heads while forming the eyebrows on the main head. This expressiveness allows them to communicate clearly while intimidating other Pokémon as needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are often found in the cold arctic waters, where they use their horns to smash through ice chunks that may be blocking their path. If you're lucky, you can catch them basking in the sun, trying to attract partners by showing off their horns.
author: universal9449

entry: POKENAME's internal body heat heats the water it fires from its cannons to scalding temperatures. Using its horns, it can sense oncoming rain.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: It scurries along the bottom of the sea, rarely seen above water. Nobody knows what is inside its shell.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME use their antennae to feel the current in the water, in order to discern their surroundings and sense other Pokémon. The size of the antennae determine the age and gender of a POKENAME.
author: krune

entry: While the smog produced by POKENAME appears similar to ghostly smoke, it's actually stunning powder. Inhaling it can be deadly.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME have a variety of vocalizations they can make that sound like laughter. The horned plating on its head comes in different shapes and sizes.
author: ohok3441

entry: Due to the shape of its horn, POKENAME cannot tunnel through earth as fast as Onix. However, the horn does give it an edge in battle, due to its reach and power. Foes are flicked away effortlessly if they face POKENAME!
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rises early to collect honey from nearby woods. In the afternoon, it spars with friends and shares honey with them as a post-battle treat.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME are very rarely found without a skull attached to their back, favoring skulls of larger predatory Pokémon. When unable to strike with their razor-sharp claws, they fire a pressurized stream of water through the skull's mouth.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have many small, hooked claws that make it easy for them to climb trees or scale rocks. They wait for opportunities to steal eggs to eat, favoring the eggs of bird POKENAME.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is cold and bitter after the death of its mother. It steals eggs from nests to make others experience the same pain.
author: welliss

entry: POKENAME uses the weapons it carves to establish dominance over Sneasel tribes. It unites them under its banner, typically to reign in their more sneaky and devious mannerisms.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME use Smokescreen before ambushing prey, as they can easily see through the smog. Some POKENAME have been known to steal the treasures and precious items of other undersea Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME love the taste of berries and are known to steal them from other Pokémon to satisfy their hunger. Fortunately, they leave behind a sparkling dust wherever they go, creating a trail for astute Pokémon to follow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using its wings for an extra boost, POKENAME moves faster than a race car and maneuvers sharply. Generally seen in pairs, each takes turns attacking while confounding their foes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME vainly maintains its appearance, taking special care of its feathers, which are used for intimidation. It pretends to be injured, then attacks any who stop to help it, at least stealing their valuables before fleeing into frozen mountains.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's leaf emits a soothing, minty aroma, which it uses as a distraction to steal snacks from the affected creature. It easily becomes jealous if not enough attention is paid to it, making this Pokémon not recommended to new Trainers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME diligently sharpens its talons against trees and rocks. Flocks hunt at night, often getting into fights with other nocturnal bird fusions over prey.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME skitters up to enemies to poke them with its little blades. It loves destruction.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME clings to arctic cliff faces, listening for passerby from whom it can drain blood. It has a suspicious disposition, only really trusting one other being at a time and losing faith in them at the slightest betrayal.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Inhabiting colder waters, POKENAME lures creatures closer with the hypnotic glow of its appendage. Once something draws near, it cuts them with tiny claws hidden in its hands that carry a chilling, immobilizing poison.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is constantly crying in frustration because it wants to eat itself, but can't. Never leave two POKENAME alone in a room together, or you'll end up with just one POKENAME.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME spreads feelings of impulsiveness among kleptomaniacs, urging them to steal whatever they see fit.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME helps pickpockets steal from unsuspecting tourists. It slashes purses so the contents fall onto the ground before running off with the stolen goods.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are very agile and sharp-cutting creatures with shockingly bendable limbs. They have also been reported to be the reason many tree branches have suddenly snapped off, due to the fact that they like to use their tails to hang from them.
author: th3randomguy

entry: POKENAME lay hundreds of eggs at a time. Most of them are tiny and will never develop into Pokémon. The fathers eat them, absorbing energy and triggering a hormonal response that makes them begin to change their behaviour to become more paternal.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lay hundreds of eggs at a time. Most of them are tiny and will never develop into Pokémon. The fathers eat them, absorbing energy and triggering a hormonal response that calms them down and causes their behaviour to become more paternal.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: By reading air currents using the fine fur that covers their bodies, POKENAME predict the feeding patterns of nearby Flying-type Pokémon. Sneaking into nests under cover of night, they will poke holes in eggs and slurp up the nutritious innards.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME steals food from Pokémon weaker than itself, threatening them with its extremely sharp incisors. During the day, it sleeps in the burrows it digs beneath tree roots, as it cannot stand sunlight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME flock around bakeries in the hopes of getting a few pieces from customers that leave. In response, bakeries have a sign to discourage feeding wild Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hunts its prey during snowy nights, using the icy terrain and low visibility to its advantage. However, it loves to go for insect hives, licking the frozen honey like a popsicle.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can be found at parks around the world where they eat leftovers from picnics. Their cynical nature causes them to scare away other Pokémon that try to eat the scraps alongside them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When berries are buried beneath deep snow, POKENAME's feather twitches wildly. It digs with sharp claws until it finds the fruit.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are surprisingly fast, going for their prey's legs first so they have no means of escape. They prefer to hunt at night as their tiny eyes are very sensitive to light.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are rumored to aviate small planes to make quick getaways after stealing trinkets from Trainers. They enjoy shiny objects and carry a sack full of such items so they can show off their collection.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME seeks out unprotected Pokémon nests and steals their eggs, storing them in its sack-like tail. It has also been known to swipe valuables from unsuspecting hikers.
author: kokoria_

entry: POKENAME nests high in the mountains, its iron armor protecting it from the extreme cold. It divebombs its prey from above, spearing them with its sharp metal talons.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is highly intelligent and independent, so it requires a dedicated and empathetic Trainer to teach it commands. It is very distrustful of new presences, leading it to attack if its owner is not present or to remain warily close to its owner.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are shrewd creatures that rely on deception to secure their prey. They pretend to be injured by slithering in an odd pattern before surprising their prey with a lethal bite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rolls at high speeds through canyons. As it spins, it leaves a slick path of ice in its wake, making pursuit nearly impossible.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is rather dexterous with the large claws it wields. Using them, it can meticulously sort through files and quickly shred apart those that are no longer needed.
author: sk372

entry: Holding its antler-like wand aloft, POKENAME casts precise Ice-type attacks. Frozen prey are often left standing mid-step.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME marks its territory with painted graffiti. Each POKENAME has a unique style and signature. During territorial disputes, POKENAME will paint over each other's graffiti.
author: musicsheep.

entry: A territorial Pokémon. If any rival POKENAME shows up in the wrong place at the wrong time, it is made a quick example of. Its tail color represents its gang affiliation.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Natural-born underlings, they flock to the strongest individual nearby. They follow orders diligently as long as it causes mischief.
author: jackythewannabe

entry: They seek out the nests of Pokémon and work together to defeat the parents. Once their prey is defeated, they eat both the parents and their eggs.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME have sharp claws that allow them to sprint on solid ice. They would make excellent sled Pokémon, but they will not tolerate being harnessed.
author: danarchist

entry: It hides among the snow-covered coniferous trees of boreal forests. Its sharp claws leave gouges in tree bark as it climbs.
author: cait_sith

entry: Intelligent and devious, they steal anything they think might be useful: stones to pelt others with, Pokémon Eggs to eat or otherwise keep hostage, and even the nests of other Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a vain sort, obsessed with jewelry in particular.  Trainers should expect to regularly gift and bribe it with bracelets and necklaces if they ever hope to have POKENAME obey.
author: sk372

entry: While timid on their own, large packs of POKENAME can ambush Pokémon six times their size with ease. They are incredibly clever, often leading their prey into icy areas where they have the advantage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME glides across frozen lakes with speed and balance. It uses its feathered crest to steer while skating at high velocity.
author: .izik

entry: After waiting in the shadows, POKENAME uses its dexterous, retractable blades to crack open unguarded eggs or rip into vulnerable victims.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's metal claws radiate bitter cold. A single scratch from them can freeze flesh and armor alike.
author: .izik

entry: Often called The Nightmare, POKENAME is infamous for choosing villages to terrorize. It only attacks at night and will scare off guard Pokémon. Trainers report their hordes are filled with loose change.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME prowls ice caves in search of prey, releasing a soothing venom from its claws. This weakens the reaction time of anything it slashes, allowing it to gain the upper hand in combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME climbs trees by stretching its arms out and digging its claws into the bark. It shows off its feathered cap with pride.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: While it naps, POKENAME's head feather sways slowly. It only wakes for short bursts to eat before dozing off again.
author: .izik

entry: The tail feathers of POKENAME crackle with electricity when it wags. Sparks light up the snow around it like a static storm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cute appearance hides a cunning demeanor. POKENAME uses its sweet voice to lure Pokémon to sleep, then sneaks into their nests to steal eggs to eat.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME are incredibly cunning, often tricking stronger Pokémon into letting their guard down before swiftly striking their weak spot. It hunts in the darkness of night, targeting weak Pokémon wandering the forest alone.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME gather in small packs for hunting operations. Using illusions to disguise themselves, they take hapless targets by surprise and overwhelm them with quick hit-and-run strikes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are cocky creatures that take on foes much larger than themselves. Their weak claws and small embers lead most of them to defeat. They are also incredibly sore losers and are known to push themselves to unhealthy limits.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a mischievous nature. They often are spotted following mountain hikers, camouflaged by their snow-like fur, occasionally stealing items when given the chance.
author: lucioleuh

entry: Large hordes of POKENAME can be seen napping during the day in their frozen caves. Once night falls, they will hunt in small groups to take out any Pokémon wandering the dark tundra.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME carry items resembling Razor Claws to ensure that their strikes will carry enough power to finish off their prey in one blow. Rumors claim that these blades come from Sneasel that have passed on.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: In frozen caverns, POKENAME builds nests out of frost-covered stones. It fires electric bursts to ward off intruders and light its den.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME steals Dragon-type eggs from their caves with such agility that it is rarely caught. If its claws break, they regrow within seconds, even sharper than before.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME stalks its prey, Pokémon or human, before silently draining as much blood as will allow it to fly. The pink feather becomes more vibrant after an especially nutritious meal, which is a mark of pride for POKENAME.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are trained to steal documents or rare items through surreptitious techniques passed down by evil organizations. They are given gems as a reward but enjoy stealing for its own sake.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME waits along trails wailing and shaking in its coat-like covering, waiting for passerby to stop and help. It looks for an opportunity to steal from the generous helper and scampers away with a high-pitched giggle.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME freezes parent Pokémon with a chilling breath, then steals their eggs. It vanishes before the ice even starts to thaw.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME brushes snow up into the air as it glides, creating miniature blizzards to hide its presence. It only lifts its claws right before it strikes, using the remaining silent snowfall to disappear unnoticed.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are thought to be some of the smartest Pokémon, comparable to Slowking. They hunt by using ethereal dances to mesmerize their prey before striking them with a fatal blow. Studies show their venom can temporarily paralyze a Piloswine.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME looks more intimidating than it actually is, but doesn't stand for bullying. It spits a glob of sticky slime at bullies, immobilizing them so it can get close and punish them with its claws.
author: sk372

entry: While not all that impressive in battle, POKENAME has mastered the art of losing its opponents in the snow. It lives in solitude, only hunting at night so it can conceal itself in the shadows.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wears a jet-black cloak that allows it to hide perfectly in the dark. Although it has a rather gentle disposition, its shady appearance has earned it a reputation as a thief and liar, and so its actions are often misinterpreted.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME dazzles its opponents with flashy colors before embedding them with sharp icicles protruding from its celestial body. Each color has a different fruit flavor.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME love to fight, but hate to lose. Because of this, they often use underhanded and unfair tactics, such as ambushing and throwing dust into the eyes of their opponents.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME uses its razor-sharp claws to carve through ice and permafrost, creating massive tunnel networks under the ground. An ambush predator, POKENAME emerges from below, grabs its prey, and drags it into the frozen caverns it creates.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME are incredibly selfish creatures that have a natural hoarding instinct. Developing their sense of empathy is necessary to stop them from fighting over food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME styles itself as a gentlemanly thief. If POKENAME notices someone misbehaving, the person will mysteriously apologize the following day.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's incessant migraines have led to its vindictive and petulant personality. Even the smallest annoyance leads it to lash out with its psychic powers. Persim Berries can help it find some relief from the headaches, lessening its anger as well.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hunts in frozen lakes, using its powerful claws to dive straight through the ice. However, it stays underwater most of the time since the water is warmer than the outside air.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have resilient stomachs that can handle diets of rotten berry juice and aging meats. They carve out sturdy underground tunnels where they build primitive tools, structures, and toys.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME adores crime, as it cherishes the dream of helping its Trainer get away from the forces of law. It will take the strongest of wills and purest of hearts to raise this fusion in the ways of justice and goodhearted actions.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME adores crime, as it cherishes the dream of helping its Trainer get away from the forces of law. It will take the strongest of wills and purest of hearts to raise this fusion in the ways of justice and goodhearted actions.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME loafs about, only moving to patiently fish for food with its tail. While it usually has a mischievous expression on its face, POKENAME is far too lazy to act on any schemes formed with its cunning intellect.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's feather holds a powerful magnetic charge. In factory ruins, it attracts bolts, wires, and scraps as it sneaks through.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to surprise one another, playfully hiding behind rocks before jumping out with a goofy smile on their face. Despite how clumsy they can be, they are surprisingly good at evading predators.
author: mistymagius

entry: When attacking, the feathers on POKENAME's tail freeze into rigid blades. It uses them to carve through ice with swift, slicing motions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits out freezing pearls when startled. A direct hit can leave foes completely encased in ice.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feather glows icy blue when channeling Ghost-type attacks. It leaves a cold aura in the air as it floats silently through the night.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its terrifying mouth and canine teeth, its bite is nothing worth mentioning. Even its claws are dulled down and weak. POKENAME relies on scare tactics rather than power.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME loves to sneak into nests of other creatures to feed on unprotected eggs. It is easily spotted by Flying-type predators due to its colorful feathers, but will fight back viciously with its razor-sharp pincers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The honey produced by the jar on POKENAME's back is toxic to humans, but is an exceedingly effective pesticide. Gardeners raise POKENAME to wander their land so pests will be attracted to the honey and be poisoned when they eat it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Due to its sensitive tongue, it enjoys a bland, healthy diet to help get started with its day. It is happy with porridge and a bit of salt, which make them a cheap pet to have around.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love to raid Combee nests for their honey. They actually use the honey to stick silk and twigs together to make their nests.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME subsists mainly on honey, giving their bodies a consistency and smell similar to it. Beedrill often mistake POKENAME for lost honey, bringing them directly to the hive where they feast on the reserves.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are omnivorous creatures that eat a variety of food on a daily basis. They can evolve to quickly adapt their bodies to certain kinds of food to survive, but most prefer to keep their varied yet balanced diet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often accidentally fall for honeypot traps as they believe that the traps involve actual honey. This leads many types of firewalls to force POKENAME out of PC systems, causing many to feel sad.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will shake or even break trees to get a hold of their fruits to mix with Beedrill pollen to make their own honey. Though they will consume their own honey aplenty, they also love to share some of it with others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME loves sweet berries and will often store hundreds of them inside of hollow trees. However, the berries will slowly start to ferment, creating a sweet puree that is quite popular on toast.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME pulls pranks on other Pokémon but reacts with candor whenever it is in trouble. Despite its mischievous nature, it does not enjoy seeing people or Pokémon hurt by its antics.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME study hives that produce honey to calculate the best time to raid the nest. They often enlist the help of other Pokémon because of their limited movement.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gather swarms of Bug-type Pokémon to hunt for food as a group. POKENAME often leads the group to hives where they collectively steal honey for POKENAME to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generally lives alongside its own kind for protection, as their vaguely sweet-smelling fur makes them targets for certain predators. It is incredibly elusive, yet surprisingly friendly and affectionate, especially in its younger years.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a very kind Pokémon, often befriending others for no reason but to make them happy. However, if you offer it something sweet like honey, it will never leave your side.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a simple mind, but possesses great psychic potential. When the crescent moon on its head glows, it receives a short vision of the immediate future.
author: sk372

entry: This variant of POKENAME travels inseparably with a rock-hard tree branch, which it uses as a tool to attempt honey-gathering in hard-to-reach areas.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Its green forearms are coated in a very sweet honey. During the summer, Combee will swarm POKENAME, mistaking it for a nectar-producing tree.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME can control the direction it drifts by turning its cotton sails to catch the wind at just the right moment.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's sweat and saliva smells a bit like what it last ate. However, it almost never smells sweet; this is due to POKENAME's body absorbing almost all sugary content in whatever it has eaten. They are most often found in the woodlands.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME steal honey from hives by swiping honeycombs with the hand on their tail. Once they run a safe distance away, they tear the honeycombs into pieces with their claws.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love to eat honey and are willing to put themselves in danger to obtain honeycombs. They are most active during sunny days, where the sunlight gives them a boost of speed to escape Pokémon that defend hives.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail is coated in a gel that is poisonous enough to knock out almost anything that touches it. They poke it into beehives to collect honey, causing more damage to the bees than they cause to it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The biggest POKENAME generally has secured the largest amount of sugar and fat during the season before hibernation, so it has the respect of its peers. They are most playful in the summer months and only then enjoy physical affection from friends.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is thought that POKENAME fall to ground during meteor showers. Its eye twinkles with starlight, even during the day.
author: missingmilkman

entry: When frightened, POKENAME releases a honeylike scent to warn others. If the threat comes closer, it panics and detonates in a small explosion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME claim their own berry trees to nest in and will often fight other POKENAME if they get too close. However, they let Bug Pokémon stay with them, only so that bigger Pokémon will go after the bugs first.
author: mistymagius

entry: When a POKENAME is attacked, it hides inside its hard shell, as the Pokémon has no natural means to attack back. To store food for the winter, it creates a honey-like substance inside its shell using Berries it forages.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME are most active during the full moon. They watch the sky mournfully as though waiting for a change in the phase of the moon. Sinnoh researchers think this difference to unfused Teddiursa hints at latent Ursaluna gene expression emerging.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are most active during the full moon. They watch the sky mournfully as though waiting for a change in the phase of the moon. Sinnoh researchers think this difference to unfused Teddiursa hints at latent Ursaluna gene expression emerging.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is quite popular due to its large size but amiable disposition, often seeking to cuddle anything smaller than it. It's so softhearted it will tremble before any battle, even against weaker foes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in volcanic caverns and rarely leave alone. When they do, they can harvest any pollen and berries in the area, cooking them with their own body heat. However, they never stray far from their dens for food.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME has a pleasant and sweet aroma. Its fatty body also adds temptation to predator Pokémon, so related species often end up having to protect it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Almost all POKENAME adore sweet and dry Berries. To clean themselves, they rub their furry body against stony surfaces; the fact their typical habitats are near mountains assists with that act.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME leaps into the air, it trails honey from its wings. As a result, it is very easy to follow.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME have especially keen noses and can sniff out Beedrill hives across great distances. Some gourmands have started training POKENAME to sniff out valuable truffles buried underground.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lives high in the mountains amongst alpine forests. Using its keen sense of smell it tracks down hives filled with Honey and will ram into the trees until the hive drops to the forest floor.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rolls into trees to knock down Beedrill hives. It smashes them open for honey, then rolls away before the swarm can attack.
author: .izik

entry: Preferring to navigate at night when the Bug types that produce Honey are asleep, POKENAME will travel great distances in search of its favourite food. When it finds a tree housing a nest, it uses its immense strength to topple it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: After eating even an ounce of honey, POKENAME's rolling speed triples. It can even roll straight up vertical cliffs with its newfound momentum.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's high consumption of honey means that the milk it produces is particularly sweet in flavor. It's often shy about sharing its milk, but is easily convinced when offered sweets in exchange.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is incredibly irritable when hungry, and rips through entire trees looking for food. During the winter, it blocks the entrance of its den with large rocks before beginning hibernation.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME releases a sweet scent from the holes on its head, attracting pollinating Bug Pokémon. However, it doesn't actually need to be pollinated, it just likes the sweet taste of their nectar.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is always very sleepy. The pillow it sleeps on could send even a raging Primeape into slumber.
author: toxicrown

entry: POKENAME have robust bodies with plenty of antibodies for Beedrill venom, due to how often they pillage their hives for honey. Their furs carry a sweet scent and are typically very sticky from all the honey they consume.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is at its most gleeful when it is gliding from tree to tree in the woods. It has an immature, naive, but extremely kind nature.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are skilled climbers, using their claws to scale tall trees in search of Combee hives. They stab into these hives with their claws, consuming the honey inside.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME don't stray far from their childhood den when they're young, waiting patiently for their parent to return. If they feel they're in danger, they make a plaintive cry before curling up, relying on their plated skin to protect them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's leafy bits change color with the seasons, growing pale in the winter months. During the spring they become golden-brown, and emit a pleasing honey-like aroma.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in temperate forests and travels closer to tundra climates when it is close to evolving. It gorges itself on honey nearly nonstop and relies on its impressive stature to intimidate any would-be attackers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Incredibly dense fur and a flame-producing organ keep wild POKENAME warm during winter hibernation. They do not learn to be social, and they avoid potential predators at all costs.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's preferred home is one lush with mud puddles and trees bearing honey. It's almost constantly seen caked with both mud and honey all over its fur.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon is extremely shy around people. The easiest way to befriend one is to present it with honey.
author: toxicrown

entry: POKENAME's spines emit pheromones that mimic those of Beedrill, allowing it to sneak into their hives unnoticed. It takes large chunks of honeycomb back to its den and feasts on them for days.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is not that smart, usually following its incredible sense of smell to find food. It loves sweet things like berries and honey, which can lead to it wandering into markets and bakeries.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is said to induce insomnia in those nearby, leaving its Trainer sleepless for hours on end. Some Trainers report witnessing POKENAME assume disturbing forms in the darkness, though such accounts are mostly attributed to tricks of the light.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME has a metallic shielding around its skull as well as its claws. The metal around the claws is used to more easily climb and dig into trees to obtain honey.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME starts pacing and growling an hour before storms arrive, making it a perfect partner on long hikes.
author: curazy

entry: POKENAME are said to be the spirits of trees cut down before their prime. They hide inside hollow logs until the new moon, when they become extremely active, devouring sweet sap from nearby flora.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though placid in the presence of humans and other Pokémon, POKENAME maintains a strong rivalry with others of its kind. Its quite common to see them charging at and headbutting into each other, particularly over food.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can grasp the crescent-shaped blade on its forehead and hurl it at tree branches to knock down beehives full of the honey it loves. It is a very shy creature and hides in the bushes as soon as it notices a human nearby.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its ribbons to gather up extra honey and lick it off of them later. It gathers and consumes so much that even when cleaned off, the ribbons still carry the scent of honey.
author: sk372

entry: The hibernation of a POKENAME follows the lunar cycle, so they are only active during nights of the full moon. Outside of their monthly cycle, they are otherwise nearly impossible to awaken.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME appear to mimic claw machines, using a small plushie as their eyes to see. POKENAME are popular with children, as they will gladly exchange plushies for honeyed snacks.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: As POKENAME ages, the tuft of fur on their heads grows longer and curves more and more. The oldest of POKENAME begin developing small dark spots on this tuft, reminiscent of craters on the Moon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The crescent flame and melting wax on POKENAME's head emit a scent very close to fresh honey. This unfortunately causes it to be accosted by Teddiursa and even the occasional Ursaring.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME does its best to appear innocuous by choosing buttons that help it appear cuter. It avoids confrontation with other Pokémon and will run away when upset.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The only thing that POKENAME's heads agree on is a love for honey. This leaves them often fighting over the snack and winding up coated and sticky, and often biting each other as they try to lick the stains off the other.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wanders around the forests, hopping from tree to tree in search of berries. When threatened, it will inflate its body to intimidate would-be attackers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME consumes a variety of foods rich in nutrients: avocados for fat, honey for sugars, and, as an omnivore, blood for iron. Its saliva numbs the nerves of its prey while it feeds unnoticed.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are often found in fields near Vespiquen hives. They are always on the hunt for honey, and will not eat anything other than it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: A honey-like drool drips from POKENAME's mouth at all times. The sweet scent attracts small insects to it, making it easy for it to slurp up the stuck bugs for a meal.
author: sk372

entry: The plant atop POKENAME's fuzzy head sprouts small nuts known to neutralize toxins. Herbalists often follow it in hopes of gathering the nuts for potent Antidotes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a strong fighter and swimmer. When using all of its strength, it can even swim through honey while eating enough for the energy it needs.
author: entomoxie

entry: A small child, POKENAME searches for the sweetest honey it can find to nourish itself. The sweeter the honey, the sweeter its leaves turn.
author: pory

entry: POKENAME are very friendly to humans and are great helpers in orchards and apiaries. In exchange for help with harvesting, POKENAME asks for portions of honey as payment.
author: arcul

entry: POKENAME floats silently through moonlit skies. POKENAME collects anything that sparkles, and if disturbed, it lets out a hum that calms even the most aggressive foes.
author: curazy

entry: POKENAME is popular among novice Trainers for being exceptionally easy to tame. This is partly due to its love of honey, which quickly earns its trust when offered as a treat.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME is popular among novice Trainers for being exceptionally easy to tame. This is partly due to its love of honey, which quickly earns its trust when offered as a treat.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME often hides in berry bushes, providing it a reliable source of food and protection. Once harvested, its gourd has an incredibly sweet flavor, which makes it perfect for making pies.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can be seen handing out baked goods to anyone it meets. However, even if you refuse to take its treats, POKENAME will regularly show up to your door until you eventually give in.
author: mistymagius

entry: Stolen food items are often the result of the disarming eyes of a POKENAME. The true victims of a POKENAME's antics, however, are Beedrill, which store their honey in underground hives.
author: xiapher

entry: The best way to catch a POKENAME is to put a dollop of honey on one's bait when fishing. Entire schools have been seen flocking to a single piece of bait, so great is POKENAME's love for the sweet treat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects spare coins it finds and builds a collection. Once it gathers enough, it goes into human civilizations and attempts to barter its coins for tasty treats such as honey.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a fondness for sweet foods, prowling through their trainer's apartment in search of food to eat. They are agile Pokémon, able to reach high shelves to knock containers to the floor, breaking them open to get to the food inside.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME really loves to eat honey and will go to great lengths to acquire it. If it is ever interrupted while eating or trying to get honey, it will fly into a violent rage.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME have an insatiable sweet tooth, hunting through forests in search of honey. When they find a tree with honeycomb hanging from it, they punch at the trunk until they shake the honeycomb free.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: After a long day of training, POKENAME love to rest by a cozy fireplace with a piece of honeycomb as a treat. They keep the fireplace lit by releasing embers from their mouth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has to prepare its body for long hibernations by gathering mushrooms to eat. If threatened, it lets out a howl, drawing Ursaring to its defense.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME can be found in the Kitakami region, assisting with the production of mochi. POKENAME exhibit lots of enthusiasm when mochi pounding, and is prone to create messes.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME has a playful sense of pride in its musculature, always looking for a way to show off and impress others. It often expects to be rewarded with sweet honey treats for these displays of strength.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spews out sweet honey from its mouth which it uses to stick itself to tree branches. While the honey is incredibly tasty, it often attracts strong Bug Pokémon to POKENAME's location.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite its color, the substance POKENAME produce is toxic and should not be consumed. The residue that POKENAME suffuse over every surface has a sweet aroma that attracts bug Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Some believe POKENAME is the spirit of deceased orphan Teddiursa. It floats through forests, its haunting wail causing Teddiursa to cry and Ursaring to go into grief-stricken rages.
author: sk372

entry: A stony crescent grows from POKENAME's head early in its life, glowing faintly during full moons. Despite this eerie glow, its behavior remains curiously unchanged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's strong arms let it wield the bone club with great effectiveness in battle, but its preferred use is more mundane: POKENAME enjoys smearing the bone with honey or sweet juices, saving them to lick up later.
author: sk372

entry: Easy to anger, POKENAME goes on charging rampages through the forests, bowling over trees and anything in its path. The only thing that can stop its charge is the scent of honey, whereupon it becomes very docile.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers should never approach an unattended POKENAME cub, or they risk being relentlessly stalked by its mother for years to come.
author: kingd8

entry: POKENAME are highly feared predators of tropical seas, often indiscriminately attacking anything that comes too close. Some suggest certain shapes or patterns can ward off POKENAME, though these claims have yet to be verified.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is most obsessed with honey, nectar, and pollen, in that order. If its powerful nose detects even a single waft of these, it will awaken and fly right to the source, combating those who get in its way.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though it looks aggressive, POKENAME takes its antics and attempts to entertain very seriously. Its usual act involves the upper arms arguing with the lower arms during their miming.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an extremely territorial Pokémon. Fishermen know it as "King of Mountain Lakes", due to it claiming a vast area surrounding the water.
author: moopse

entry: A bit sullen and antisocial, POKENAME tends to stick to its own devices, though it is easily lured closer with the promise of honey. If fed enough sweet treats, it will eventually open up and behave in a more upbeat fashion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loves to dance and performs a special dance where the dancer squats and thrusts one foot out in turns. This dance has grown popular on the internet because of its association with memes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because of POKENAME's appearance and slow-moving nature, it is often mistaken for a large children's toy.
author: stabbycat

entry: Inhabiting islands lacking berries, POKENAME gets its food by attacking passing ships and robbing their cargo. Its ferociousness has caused ships to plot courses that avoid islands where it lives entirely.
author: soup1900

entry: Inhabiting islands lacking berries, POKENAME attacks passing ships and robs their cargo to gain its food. Its ferociousness has caused sailors to plot courses that avoid islands where it lives entirely.
author: soup1900

entry: The rowan berries that grow on POKENAME's neck are beloved by all bear Pokémon. These Pokémon can be found standing at the edge of swift rivers, grabbing fish Pokémon out of the water with their long necks.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME hide inside large logs, feeding on any small insects that try to disturb it. If its log is ever destroyed, it will rampage through the forest until it finds another suitable log.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have the ability to communicate silently amongst one another through a language of their own. The ring around their fur can radiate light during the night; a series of flashes can have its own meaning, creating complex messages when strung.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have the ability to communicate silently amongst one another through a language of their own. The ring around their fur can radiate light during the night; a series of flashes can have its own meaning, creating complex messages when strung.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's claws can be detached and used as throwing projectiles against opponents, as they regenerate over time. It's thought that this might have inspired the creation of shuriken in the past.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats through dense forests guided by scent alone. Its nose can detect fruit-bearing trees from over a mile away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very protective of its honey and will fiercely attack anyone who gets too close. However, if it can't win the fight, it will lob some of its honey at the attackers to slow them down before fleeing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME produces a sticky, honey-like substance in its core, which it can fire as projectiles. The impact is powerful enough on its own, and the syrupy thickness often impedes an opponent's movement.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME growls deeply at intruders near its cave, though it's mostly for show. If approached further, it panics and burrows out of sight.
author: .izik

entry: The kind of berries POKENAME forages impacts the flavor of the honey it excretes from its stinger. It will break into campsites to steal food, but the unfamiliar food disrupts its sensitive stomach, thus hampering its honey production.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME slumbers deep beneath mineral-rich mountains, its rumbling snores echoing throughout the caverns. It occasionally surfaces, knocking over trees in search of honey and berries to supplement its diet, before returning to hibernation.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Living in the mountains, POKENAME uses its claws to steal food from Hikers. It hauls backpacks and picnic baskets to its cave to raid for meals.
author: .izik

entry: More aggressive than the average Teddiursa, POKENAME tend to live more solitary lives fending for themselves. They are protective of Teddiursa however, and won't hesitate to claw viciously at anything that threatens them.
author: sk372

entry: Forest areas where POKENAME are known to reside are closed off during the winter months. While these Pokémon are hard to wake from hibernation, they are ferociously cranky when woken up early.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's body is made entirely out of honey, which their shells secrete. Using their sticky bodies, they climb up walls and trees to get away from Teddiursa trying to eat them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME live in alpine regions, soaring over forests in search of hives to gather honey from. They use their talons to snatch hives before they can be attacked, flying off with them and then dropping them at a safe distance to smash them open.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Even though POKENAME do not need to hibernate, they enjoy sleeping throughout most of the day. During the few hours of daylight that they are awake, they slam their bodies against trees to knock down berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME does not need to hibernate, as its incredibly thick fur protects it from the extreme cold. It can be seen headbutting trees to knock down berries for it to eat.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though it has a gruff appearance, POKENAME enjoys sharing gifts from its bag with young children that behave well. It's been noted that all the gifts it hands out are related to honey in some way.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME aggressively leaps up raging rivers to follow its favorite prey, Magikarp.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's heavy body makes flying for long distances difficult, so it claims only small patches of territory. If angered, it may pluck one of its sharp feathers from its wings and use it as a throwing weapon.
author: sk372

entry: An agile climber, POKENAME often rolls down curved trunks to build speed. It uses this momentum to chase down prey in bursts.
author: .izik

entry: While very strong, POKENAME tend to only use that strength to knock down Berry trees and eat the Berries. It is surprisingly docile when unprovoked.
author: therider

entry: POKENAME hides away in caves until the moonlit night falls and it can hunt. The ring on its chest reflects moonlight and casts hypnosis on victims who see it, stunning them and leaving them open to be constricted.
author: sk372

entry: Extremely protective of their eggs, POKENAME growl at anyone who gets too close. If a Trainer takes proper care of an POKENAME, they will be rewarded with loyal affection, but the eggs will remain the POKENAME's priority.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME loves honey but struggles to climb up trees to get to the hives. So instead, it will constantly headbutt the tree until the hive falls and cracks open, spilling out honey for it to lick up.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME usually nests near maple trees, feeding on the sweet sap they produce. It will claim a single tree as its territory and try to fight off smaller Pokémon who attempt to steal its food.
author: mistymagius

entry: It rushes through dense forest at high speed, deftly navigating through tree tops and tree bases. If it deems a tree obstructs its path too much, POKENAME uses its wings to topple it.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME mixes mystical herbs and flowers into its honey pot, creating honey with various magical effects.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's thick coat is resistant to the cold, allowing it to hunt during harsh snowstorms when other Pokémon wouldn't dare. It is a vicious predator, taking out Pokémon double its size.
author: mistymagius

entry: This mellow Pokémon can be found lounging deep in dense forests. Its mass of fur and long arms are useful for both survival and snuggling.
author: moopse

entry: POKENAME is rumoured to be an amalgamation composed of scrap robots. However, its true origins are shrouded in mystery.
author: the_smirker

entry: A wild POKENAME preys on other Pokémon as a primary food source. It lives in harsh winter conditions; if a blizzard grows too strong, it uses its incredible sense of smell to find the underground den it dug out prior.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A wild POKENAME preys on other Pokémon as a primary food source. It lives in harsh winter conditions; if a blizzard grows too strong, it uses its incredible sense of smell to find the underground den it dug out prior.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If you see an POKENAME curl into a ball, do not assume it has gone on the defensive; it rolls into opponents at high speeds to cut and crush them with its bulk and sharp spines.
author: sk372

entry: It is generally recommended to not approach wild POKENAME. While they appear shy and timid, if they feel provoked, they will attack by using supernatural powers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: They take great pride in their plush, luxurious coats, but will not hesitate to get dirty to protect their young.
author: quote.lass

entry: When exposed to a full moon, POKENAME's aura powers become much stronger, allowing it to sense prey miles farther than it normally can. When it finds a beehive, it uses aura to vaporize it, leaving only the honey behind to be licked up.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME cut down trees with its wings to easily access the berries in them. It will fly at sonic speeds to mercilessly chase down thieves who steal berries from its territory.
author: soup1900

entry: Urban legends warn not to go deep into forests at night or you may run afoul of POKENAME. The tales say that if you see its diminutive frame, it's already too late to escape its fearsome maw that lunges from the darkness.
author: sk372

entry: While they spend most of their time lounging peacefully, POKENAME's bursts of energy are fearsome, capable of reshaping the land. They fiercely guard their territory, drawn especially to areas rich in honey.
author: helix2b

entry: POKENAME do not like being disturbed, chasing away anyone that interrupts its nap. It hunts on full moons, hiding in the shadows cast by the trees.
author: mistymagius

entry: Many a terrifying tale is told about sightings of POKENAME in the night. As the stories go, a victim sees a glowing ring in the dark, becoming so hypnotized by the sight they never see spectral claws ready to descend upon them...
author: sk372

entry: Ancient tomes describe POKENAME as growing 1,000 paws when enraged. No modern record has confirmed these terrifying accounts.
author: .izik

entry: The landscape carried on the backs of POKENAME reflects that of their home. During blood moons they undergo an eerie transformation, their landscapes taking on a haunted appearance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The landscape carried on the backs of POKENAME reflects that of their home. During blood moons they undergo an eerie transformation, their landscapes taking on a haunted appearance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's honey is said to be delicious and incredibly fortifying. Many adventurous souls have died trying to get a taste.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME is an apex hunter, able to track and take down Pokémon even twice its size. Due to its excellent vision, once its prey is spotted, POKENAME will not lose sight of it until it is taken down.
author: mistymagius

entry: This vicious Pokémon will hunt down anything that is too weak to fight it off, most notably human children. However, it will never venture outside of whatever domain it has claimed for itself.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME uses a honey-like secretion from its ribbons to mark territory. Circles drawn on tree trunks using this special sparkling honey indicate the trees have been claimed as POKENAME's.
author: sk372

entry: While inactive on nights of a new moon, POKENAME are extremely powerful when the moon is full. Their impressive ability to hear and smell allows them to easily avoid or pursue other Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A team of Teddiursa carry POKENAME's strings to keep it from blowing away. The Teddiursa coordinate their movements to make POKENAME slash with its claws.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is said to host all of the malice and grudges it has had for its past owners. Even trying to touch it will unleash its built-up hatred in a brutal show of power.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME protects its body in a thick coat of honey. This honey not only protects it from harm, but being encased in this honey reverses aging. However, if anything other than POKENAME eats this honey, they fall into a coma.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME absorbs extreme amounts of energy during the night. It is always bouncing and frolicking from foot to foot, even in combat. In regions with long daylight hours, such as near the equator, it becomes sluggish and weak.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It cleaves through trees with its fearsome tusks, sending honey-filled hives crashing to the ground so it can feast on their contents. Fiercely territorial even toward its own kind, it engages in brutal battles with rivals over control of its domain.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is rarely seen outside caves. When it emerges from its den, it is only to mend its body together with sticky honey. It resumes its hibernation immediately afterwards.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME climbs high trees to slash claw marks deep into bark. On moonlit nights, it becomes more aggressive toward trespassers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hoards everything sweet, with a preference for honey. It will often steal campers' supplies or plunder the pantries of homes in remote areas.
author: lucioleuh

entry: POKENAME releases pheromones to attract Combee. After they build hives on its branches, it scares them away and consumes the honey they left behind.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The power of POKENAME comes from absorbing sunlight into its wings. After a full week of sunbathing, POKENAME is strong enough to break apart mountains.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME are quite timid Pokémon, hiding out in caves and dense forests. They secrete a strong-smelling honey from their skin to attract the company of Combee.
author: santon5512

entry: Despite its immense strength, POKENAME is quite a docile Pokémon and is quite friendly towards humans. It loves sugary foods and will even raid villages for their sweet treats.
author: mistymagius

entry: The cuddliest Pokémon that exists, POKENAME is a true friend and is very popular with children and some adults.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME use music and a pleasant aroma to lure small Pokémon inside them. Once inside, POKENAME subject them to frightening hallucinations, feeding off their fear for nearly five hours before spitting them out.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses its singing to calm bees and allow their hive to be worn on its head. Then, using its enchanted movements, it controls the bees to create all the honey it wants for its liking.
author: soup1900

entry: In autumn, POKENAME devours flowers with urgency. It hibernates in hollow logs through winter, sealing the ends with leaves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is made of a large block of honeycomb protected by a thick layer of fur. The honey it produces is described to be absolutely delectable and is often used in professional restaurants.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME chews deep grooves into bark to claim its territory. It favors walnut trees and uses Headbutt on any intruder that nears its grove.
author: .izik

entry: The fake Pinap Berry on POKENAME's head gives off a honey scent, attracting other Pokémon toward them. If this berry is touched, their spiked headcrests will snap shut like bear traps.
author: santon5512

entry: It uses fiery strikes to intimidate Beedrill guarding hives filled with the honey it craves. When hungry, POKENAME becomes especially aggressive and irritable, so it should be approached with caution.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's dense fur helps keep dirt off them as they dig. Their keen sense of smell lets them smell buried food from miles away.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are solitary Pokémon that maintain large mountain territories. Their roars are audible for miles, warning away competition. They seek out any transgressor that ignores their warning, their gem gleaming an angry red while they search.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME raids Beedrill hives to gather delicious honey. Being uncoordinated, it always ends up with quite a bit of honey in its fur.
author: hophoppip

entry: The snowflakes from POKENAME's clouds are made from crystallized honey. Children enjoy catching the sweet snowflakes on their tongues.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's leaf-wings are comprised of a sweet and succulent honey-like substance. It constantly has to shake off bevies of smaller Pokémon that climb onto it to sample its flavor.
author: sk372

entry: Pokémon Rangers track POKENAME populations and provide updates on their location to Hikers in the area. POKENAME can prove dangerous to unwary travellers as they will charge at anyone encroaching within their mountainous homes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME patrols around deep forests, guarding the denizens within from harm. Stoic by nature, it never makes the first strike, but responds mercilessly to those who would choose violence against it or those it protects.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a solitary creature that lives in verdant forests. It has a fondness for honey and always keeps a large supply stored in its den. Its thick fur has developed to make it harder for Beedrill or Vespiquen to drive it away from their hives.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME patrols around deep forests, guarding the denizens within from harm. Some variations of the species are notably more pacifistic, shielding smaller Pokémon from attacks as they retreat to safety together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's spiked fists are strong enough to stop a speeding semi-truck in its track with one punch. Rivals will test their strength by punching each other directly in the center of their circular chest patterns.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is quite the playful creature. It pretends to walk on all fours and then float while on its hind legs to scare hunters and hikers.
author: patch_bros

entry: POKENAME holds itself to a high standard in appearing strong and stoic. This front is rather easily broken when offered honey, as it can't resist ecstatically gorging on the sweet treat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can split logs and boulders with a single punch and otherwise totally shatter any hiding spot. If POKENAME is chasing you down, trying to protect yourself is not an option.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It gathers power within its body by basking under moonlight, then channels it for attacks through its yellow markings. If all its energy is expelled, it enters a long hibernation until the next full moon.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME hibernates in caves, curling up and appearing as a large boulder to most. Anything that causes it to wake up will suffer powerful and painful claw swipes in retaliation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protects young forest Pokémon from poachers. With its tremendous strength and speed, it can scoop up helpless young and fend off attackers with powerful swipes or kicks before retreating faster than most can keep pace.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very mischievous troublemakers, using sticks to poke at hives in hopes of getting honey. This often leaves them fleeing in terror, however.
author: santon5512

entry: It scratches claw marks into trees that grow particularly flavorful fruit. The three heads will sometimes argue over whether a tree's fruit is worthy enough to be marked.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends most of the day sleeping in its cave, only waking up to hunt for food. If anything ends up waking it, it will fly into a rage, smashing anything in its path with its rocky body.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is born when lava pours onto the flower buds that bloom around volcanos.
author: theheroict

entry: POKENAME searches for immense rocks to melt and consume, even boring through mountains to find particularly mineral-rich ore. Once it has fed enough, it stops moving to begin hardening into its pupa state.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Packs of POKENAME gather in competitions, taking molten ores to forge into the most impressive jewelry with their clubs. Due to their bodies' ability to keep metal molten, blacksmiths and goldsmiths seek them out.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A scourge of the seas. Wherever you spot this giant skull floating in the sky, you're surely going to find many ghosts.
author: theheroict

entry: POKENAME drip blobs of hot lava wherever they go. Sometimes bubbles of toxic gas are trapped in the lava that explode whenever they are popped.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a brief stage in the life cycle of this evolutionary line with it at its most vulnerable as it is immobile and exposed. Its magma body offers protection, but Water-type predators can spray it enough to crystallize its body to rock.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME swim magma rivers, grouping together in small schools. During eruptions, one can witness several of them attempting to swim up the streams to climb the volcano's rim and enter its insides.
author: sk372

entry: The heat emanating from POKENAME allows it to gently descend when leaping from mountainous crags. The shell contains magma wings that are still forming, so it protects the shell at all costs.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lives in volcanic caves, using its molten body to cling to the cave walls. It can fire a beam of intense heat from its eye powerful enough to melt through lead.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body is made of searing lava, and even brushing against it can cause severe burns. Its pair of wings allows it to dart close to its foes, which it then slashes with blazing magma scythes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Since its body is composed of magma, it rarely strays far from volcanic areas where it can recover its strength. Its two scythes are so scorching and sharp that it can slice any obstacle in half.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are incredibly hot within a self-contained area, but the surrounding area remains normal. Many people have figured out that POKENAME can safely melt trash without leaving behind residue or ash.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live by subsuming various rocks, though they seem to prefer sulfur. Their frequent consumption of sulfur has led them to produce a poisonous chemical within themselves that also keeps their bodies partly-solid.
author: infinex21

entry: While typically slow-moving, POKENAME can make sudden and swift movements in battle. As its amorphous body is composed of extremely hot material, even getting hit with small flung droplets can cause severe burns.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Due to how often they must rest, POKENAME sleep in flowing magma or lava to keep their bodies from cooling and hardening. When awake, they gorge upon flammable material and drink magma or lava.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME only appear for the duration of active volcanic eruptions. Even in the short time they are out of hibernation they create enough smoke to blacken 5 square miles of sky for a week.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Their wings and arm-stingers are made of solid magma that has yet to fully turn to stone thanks to the chemical produced within themselves. This chemical is poisonous to most others, even some Poison-type Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rests inside of volcanoes, absorbing the lava into its body and rendering the volcanoes dormant. When POKENAME awakens, a sudden and powerful eruption will follow.
author: wiz0z

entry: It lives in volcanic areas. It releases a spicy aroma that can make a foe's eyes water with even the faintest of scents.
author: _jix

entry: By mimicking a Quilava's body plan and morphological features, POKENAME has achieved a decent boost to its speed.
author: mx_wellman

entry: Their bodies are made of magma that often drips from them as they fly about. POKENAME dive into magma and lava to "fish" for prey but also to help keep their own bodies from cooling and hardening.
author: infinex21

entry: The heat from within POKENAME causes its body to constantly expand, resulting in constant molting. The molted shells turn red over time and melt into the lava underneath POKENAME's body, allowing hotter and hotter temperatures and more expansion.
author: weirdmageddonprepper_93813

entry: Their wings have developed enough to easily create strong gales that scatter their magmatic drippings at foes. Their talons are hot enough to melt some metals, as shown by how often POKENAME prey upon some Steel-type Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: In icy cold regions of the world, POKENAME are friendly bus companions who work alongside drivers to deliver people to their destination. They keep the bus warm and jumpstart the engine when it runs out of electricity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A POKENAME egg only hatches once the baby within has reached a sufficient temperature to melt through its shell. It loves to cuddle up to other Fire-types, sharing its warmth with its fellow Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME never sleeps, instead constantly witnessing possible futures of the creatures and objects it looks at. Allegedly, staring into its smoke and smelling its fumes will cause one to witness what it sees in their future.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME nest within volcanic pits or pools of lava, so their bodies are always hot and dripping with lava. They are mostly docile, though when agitated will fight fiercely using their rock-hard talons and by spitting balls of magma at foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have a hard time resting because they need to constantly keep their bodies warm enough to avoid solidifying. They gnaw on coal to both sharpen their teeth and fuel the fire in their bodies.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME sprout from forests that grow near lava. They reach internal temperatures that are as hot as magma, which make them difficult for new gardeners to handle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Adapted to live in extremely hot conditions, POKENAME produces a gel that evaporates to cool it, similar to sweating. The gel has a much higher specific heat capacity than water, allowing a single drop to absorb as much heat as a litre of water.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Adapted to live in searing conditions, POKENAME produces a gel that evaporates to cool it, similar to sweating. The gel is collected and used by some athletes to regulate body temperature whilst exercising.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME live in and around volcanoes, regularly replenishing their molten bodies from the lava. They're able to fly by using volcanic gas buildup within their bodies, the excess belching out of them in black billowing clouds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's fangs are extremely heat-conductive, able to retain their structure despite its internal heat. This allows its bites to be amplified with blazing energy, strong enough to rip through metal.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are incredibly hot Pokémon which can melt through almost anything. Because of this, they are used to engrave letters on metal blocks. They frequently group to form messages which can range from dire to funny.
author: jeeveseatsfish_20788

entry: The core of POKENAME is presumed to rival some of the hottest known substances on the planet. It is so potent that POKENAME is slowly dissolving itself from the inside out as it ages.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME devour abandoned mining equipment by melting the metal into a slurry. They then slurp the metallic liquid, which gets incorporated into their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers in noisy flocks near volcanic cave mouths. It pecks at fresh wood and saplings, consuming them after they catch fire.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are not used for flying, but generating warmth to regulate its body temperature. Outside of its volcanic home, it must heat itself constantly, or its body would harden and become brittle as it cools.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fur stays toasty at all times. If hugged too tightly, it may drip a single bit of lava that can scorch the skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have trouble maintaining a cohesive body shape due to the intense heat of their bodies. Their bodies have a very low silica content, enabling them to flow rapidly across the ground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's body burns so hot that its shell has no time to cool into rock. While this does mean it is more vulnerable to attacks, it also allows POKENAME to move through small gaps it otherwise couldn't have.
author: mistymagius
