entry: Because its body is usually covered with cooled magma, some are tricked into believing it is low on energy.  In truth, POKENAME are very adept at controlling their energy output, and can burst into a lithe, flaming form in the blink of an eye.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME's entire body is made of molten steel, save for the heat-resistant plating on its head. It exclusively hunts other Steel-type Pokémon, melting their metal parts into its own body.
author: secondegg

entry: Ancient tablets state that a POKENAME caused a violent eruption of Mt. Ember 5000 years ago. Its mantle-like shell can withstand any physical attack.
author: red.89

entry: POKENAME's lenses protect their eyes from the extreme heat of magma pits they inhabit. They expand the flames on their backs to intimidate enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live deep inside volcanic craters. Those who are lucky enough to catch a glimpse of the elusive Pokémon are said to have their spirits invigorated.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are usually seen perched on the edges of volcanos, waiting for prey. They swoop down, snatching their prey in their jaws and dropping them into the volcano.
author: bigoljax

entry: The ring around its shell constantly rotates, providing a renewable source of accessible energy. A single POKENAME stores enough energy to heat and power large foundries.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME encases its large fur in stone to prevent it from catching on fire or being melted away by its fire and magma. However, it must break some of this stone off when using illusions to change its appearance since they're too difficult to hide.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's feelers are coated in a thin layer of constantly shifting lava. It uses this to keep its body perpetually hot, somehow altering the flow at a moment's notice.
author: .izik

entry: It is seen as an aggressive, but respected leader to Slugma and Magcargo. POKENAME protects them with its hardened shell of rock.
author: germs2128

entry: POKENAME are rather large Pokémon that live near underwater volcanoes and other hotspots within the ocean depths. Their bodies are too hot to be touched, which helps to ward off physical attacks of other underwater Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends little time on land above the surface since its magma body cools and hardens the longer it's up there. Therefore, it spends most of its time slumbering in red-hot caves underground, where hot lava floods the majority of its home.
author: soup1900

entry: Said by some to be the epitome of volcanic fury, POKENAME is a figure of destruction in island mythology. The magma within its shell is believed to reach incalculable, impossible temperatures.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies high in the sky above volcanic regions, descending during eruptions to feed on volcanic gases. It was once believed to be a harbinger of destruction, as its only sightings were followed by cataclysmic events.
author: secondegg

entry: Sinnoh tales describe POKENAME working together to cool magma to create the various regions. These stories claim that POKENAME manipulated time to accelerate the cooling process, leading to their own bodies to harden and dim.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME can manipulate lava and stone, compressing it into spheres it can teleport at will. Living within active volcanoes, trespassers find themselves pelted by these orbs hurtling with the force of falling meteors.
author: sk372

entry: Though it's overflowing with lava, POKENAME never burns the ground because any that drips off of it is immediately teleported away. Some believe it is teleported directly into the ground, transforming many stable mountains into explosive volcanoes.
author: stevethebarbarian

entry: Despite lava typically being a burning hot liquid, POKENAME's lava flips that logic on its head, being a warm, solid material instead. Its most violent and main attack involves blasting large rock fragments at foes that melt into magma upon contact.
author: soup1900

entry: There are legends that speak of this Pokémon, claiming that its movements cause volcanoes to become active. Its six eyes can each watch different things at the same time.
author: infinex21

entry: It lives in remote volcanic craters. If it senses intruders in its territory, it will sneakily lull them to sleep before horrifically enveloping them with its magma body.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are prone to violence, always assuming they're under threat. Many incidents have been caused in Team Magma bases due to them trying to experiment on POKENAME.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME appears to be the subject of ancient legends in some regions, that speak of kingdoms becoming too greedy and being melted away for their hubris by the powers of a molten dragon.
author: sk372

entry: It is said that POKENAME emerge from volcanic pools to dance on moonlit nights. They collect moon stones and attach them to their rocky shells.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's tail is made of molten, conductive rock that can generate electricity within it by spinning rapidly. It often fights by hurling globs of magma and fireballs at its opponents.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's magmatic body and flames turn blue when it is fully charged with electricity. In this state, the balls of flame and magma that it tosses become rather explosive.
author: infinex21

entry: The only parts of POKENAME's body that can cool and solidify into stone are the sections where it blasts out hot flames. The rest is made of hot, bubbling magma that is under constant threat of spilling from its body if it unleashes an attack.
author: soup1900

entry: When POKENAME attacks, it lets out a blast of lava before freezing it over with an ultracold Ice Beam to encase the target in hard obsidian. However, after the attack, its magma body destabilizes, so it also cools it into obsidian to keep it intact.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME allow portions of their magma-like bodies to collect in layers and cool into stone to better concentrate their flames. They cycle heat through their limbs to ensure they can move freely despite the stone weighing them down.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME floats lazily over active volcanoes, drifting through smoke and ash. It's often mistaken for a wayward splash of lava.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME senses danger, it hardens its magma body into a shell. If pressured, it bursts from its shell and delivers a fiery kick hot enough to boil iron.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME scatter sparks from their caps that can start small fires. Groups of them are often brought together to ignite ritual bonfires at solstice celebrations. They engage in combat with one another at these events, providing a steady drumbeat.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME are quick enough to be barely seen by the human eye. The fire coming out of their shells can accidentally light their wings ablaze.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are revered as defenders by certain northern communities, as they burst from lava pools when someone intrudes into their volcanic territory. However, researchers now know that POKENAME are playful and pop out to scare people as a joke.
author: vic1312

entry: Inside the shell is magma spinning so fast that it acts as an electric generator, producing an electromagnetic field that encloses POKENAME's liquid body like a membrane.
author: imaginita

entry: The outer layer of POKENAME has a similar property to silica sand. This helps professional glassblowers get the materials to make soda-lime glass.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME build up energy from deep within volcanoes before launching themselves into the air in an attempt to fly to the moon. POKENAME habitats and migrations are regularly recorded to avoid them being confused for the signs of an active eruption.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Lava occasionally leaks out of the cracks of POKENAME's shell, though it quickly cools. This slowly builds up their shells, growing larger and larger each day.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME often swim through lava rivers, constantly on the hunt. Their usual diet consists of Magmar and Ponyta.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME possess an intimidating appearance and often scare explorers who stumble upon them. Truthfully, they are quite friendly and offer their rocky bodies as a bridge across active lava flows, using their arms to grip each bank.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME are sometimes used by nurses to ease aching joints. POKENAME will wrap heated webbing around afflicted areas, spreading a slow, gentle heat throughout.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Their fluid legs make locomotion awkward. To travel long distances, POKENAME use their feet to weld themselves to passing vehicles. They will also attach themselves to Steel-type and Rock-type Pokémon.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for actual candles due to their lava hiding their faces at certain angles. This causes unknowing customers to burn their hands trying to grab them.
author: bigoljax

entry: The glowing liquid inside POKENAME's glassy head is cooler than lava but still burns to the touch. It uses it to defend itself from predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lurks in cold, dark areas, providing an alluring source of warmth and light. However, it is said that those who stay near it for too long will be compelled closer and closer to its flame, until ashes are all that remains.
author: secondegg

entry: While POKENAME has overwhelmingly powerful and dangerous stone tusks, they are too brittle to be used effectively in combat. Therefore, it prefers to delicately attack using only the searing edges of the tusks where flowing lava outlines them.
author: soup1900

entry: Powered by the magma within its core, POKENAME is mainly found within ancient ruins in cold regions. For this reason, researchers theorize that ancient civilizations once relied on them for warmth.
author: secondegg

entry: At first, POKENAME has a single rocky tail, filled with lava. When this tail cracks, the lava leaks out and cools, forming an entirely new tail each time.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME must spew up much of its magma innards in order to view or interact with its surroundings in any capacity. It enjoys spending much of its time soaking in boiling magma pools.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dives at incredible speeds, searing its prey at intense temperatures through its claws. Its precision and velocity ensure the process is almost painless for its victim, making it a feared but efficient hunter in the skies.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME can be spotted in groups of Magcargo, attempting to imitate their behaviors. Occasionally, they will concentrate on trying to reach an absurdly hot temperature. Unfortunately, this always fails, leaving POKENAME very tired.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The volcanic rock scales on the body of POKENAME can move at their will. They use this to defend their viscous bodies from impacts when flying through eruptions. It is said that the arrangement of scales may mean something to other POKENAME.
author: vic1312

entry: If POKENAME don't stay in constant volcanic temperatures, then their magma bodies will begin to cool, often inhibiting their vision. This leaves these Pokémon wandering aimlessly, bumping into walls until the rocky shell breaks off.
author: santon5512

entry: As they rise from volcanic craters, POKENAME's roars can be heard from miles away. Many strong trainers are called to calm a POKENAME's rampage.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME use their burning-hot wings to soar through the air with ease. The two smaller "heads" of a POKENAME lack brains and seem to only serve to help channel and spew fire and magma.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME struggle to take flight on their own due to their bulky bodies. They position themselves within future eruptions to launch themselves in the air. They will fly towards strong sources of emotion once airborne, often passionate Trainers.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME have bodies composed of molten lava, their internal temperature high enough to cause most materials to melt. Their skin is rock that has cooled on contact with the air, their tails often being comparatively cooler than their bodies.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Space telescopes have observed POKENAME drifting above the upper atmosphere, where it orbits the planet for a while before launching itself back down to the planet. It is often mistaken for a meteorite.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME were once thought to grant wishes to those who cast something beloved into flames. A volcano-obsessed cult used to venerate them, conducting regular ritual sacrifices in their honor.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME often slumber within magma inside volcanoes. When expelled by eruptions, they are mistaken for shooting stars as they streak across the sky.
author: infinex21

entry: Due to their instinct to dam up flowing streams, POKENAME are often deployed by disaster mitigation teams at active volcanic eruptions. Using a combination of cooling magma and rocks, they redirect lava flows away from nearby towns.
author: vic1312

entry: To train itself, POKENAME travels long distances while slowly increases the size and weight of the shell on its back. When two POKENAME meet, they will drop their shells and engage in a friendly sparring match.
author: wiz0z

entry: Sustained by its own body heat, POKENAME can go weeks at a time without moving at all. It never uses its limbs to travel, preferring to slide across the ground like a lava flow.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME's sheer boundless energy lets it move at a quicker, more relentless pace than most Magcargo fusions. Bits of lava fling about as it swings its limbs wildly while moving, so giving it a wide berth is recommended.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have extremely buoyant bodies that allow them to avoid completely melding with the volcanic lakes they live in. Their lower halves made of cooled magma help to defend them, but also allow them to fight back with strong Body Slams.
author: infinex21

entry: When excited or in danger, POKENAME's body glows with heat. By directing more energy to its tail, it can control how brightly it glows and send signals to its allies from a distance.
author: imaginita

entry: When calm, POKENAME's body slowly cools into a brittle carapace. Adept Trainers will know when something has caught this Pokémon's attention, even if it remains still, because sparks will start crackling through the shell.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME have bodies composed of molten lava, their internal temperature high enough to cause most materials to melt. Their skin is rock that has cooled on contact with the air, webs of cracks crossing across them whenever they move.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Instead of the sweet, sleep-inducing music Jigglypuff usually sings, POKENAME sings in a manner similar to death metal. This causes opponents to run away in shock and fear.
author: bigoljax

entry: Groups of POKENAME live deep in volcanic caverns, eating the iron-rich basalt from dripping magma. If the cavern collapses, they simply gnaw their way through the rubble.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME tempers its stone body to a durability comparable to steel by bathing in and drinking from lava flows. Cracked stones on its body are evidence of past territorial disputes.
author: ilazerheart

entry: Wild POKENAME hide beneath volcanic rock and wait for prey to pass overhead. They snap their maws shut and cook prey alive within.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's fiery wings have to flap at a very rapid speed in order to exert enough strength to lift its hefty shell. When in flight, its wing-beat makes a deep sound akin to sizzling.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often found living in the sparse, shallow magma pockets left in an extinct volcano. While they don't have much magma to swim in, they typically don't mind or care since they barely move to begin with.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lug large shells made of cooled magma around to protect their softer tops from aerial Pokémon. Sometimes, Pokémon that try to attack them from above will bounce off and they will crawl over them, often cooking them alive.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can spin the magma stored in its shell like a turbine, which creates electricity that it uses to float above the ground. When the magma cools, POKENAME must crawl on the ground until it can consume more.
author: oddwalls

entry: If POKENAME cannot escape a threat by floating away, it will eject balls of lava at its pursuer as a last resort. Losing too much of the lava reserves in its shell will bring it crashing to the ground.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a human child near volcanic environments to lure travelers to its location. It attempts to trick them into lava-filled crevices before feeding on them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shed drips of lava and the scales along their bellies occasionally. Trainers who raise POKENAME often have the small, fragile scales polished and turned into jewelry.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME can mimic lava bubbles by inflating themselves. Their lava is more warm than hot, making them great heaters.
author: bigoljax

entry: To deter their foes, POKENAME will intake air and superheat it to expand their bodies to a gargantuan size. Once they are safe, they will deflate their bodies completely and lie flat in the sun, recharging their energy stores for the next battle.
author: notadoctor75

entry: With a body consisting of hardened volcanic ash, POKENAME seal their bud to protect the pilot flame within. The magma at their core carries toxic materials within, making the ash that blows off them hazardous to breath.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME extends short-range vines of lava from the stone flowers on its hands. Interestingly, the magma from these flowers retains a faint floral scent, one that is fairly popular in Hoenn.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has been observed using its tendrils to grab hold of wild Slugma and lift them away. It dumps the other Pokémon into nearby volcanoes, though why it does so is not known.
author: sk372

entry: By uncoiling its rocky ears, a threatened POKENAME can strike with the force comparable to that of a flaming cannonball. They group together on especially cold nights.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME live in craters, plugging themselves into any vents that they can find. Volcanic gasses build up within the blocked vents, eventually launching them high into the air like a mortar.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME glide along the slopes of recently erupted volcanoes, consuming rocks that contain heavy metals and leaving behind soil primed for new plant growth. Island communities prize them for their restorative capability post-eruption.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME can force negative emotions like anger within their opponents. They do this by spitting raspberries and burning the undersides of their opponent.
author: bigoljax

entry: The rock inside the lava layering is POKENAME's true body. They build their layering up more by rolling in magma.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME rest in quivering, slimy orange clusters of up to five at the base of volcanoes. Even during winter, this can raise the surrounding temperature to sweltering levels up to 100 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: What looks like magma on POKENAME's top is actually bright orange cotton, prized not only for its quality but also for its warmth. Clothing made from POKENAME cotton remains warm in even the coldest temperatures.
author: oddwalls

entry: They burrow through hot desert sands to prevent their molten bodies from cooling down. Wherever they have burrowed, they leave tunnels of glass.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME must flap its wings constantly to keep them from cooling and hardening enough to limit its flight. It hunts by falling upon prey and letting the heat of its molten body cook them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's bodies constantly produce dust-like embers, usually blowing away in the wind. These embers can accidentally light bushes aflame, almost causing forest fires.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME clutches a special chunk of volcanic rock tightly to itself, guarding it fiercely. It is said that if one were to forcibly part it from the stone, its body would lose cohesion and turn into a lifeless puddle of magma.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME find their niche in absorbing energy from other Fire-type Pokémon. Their semi-molten bodies allow them to withstand extreme temperatures and help them stick fast to their chosen host.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME's body glows brightly but gives off little heat. Because POKENAME can cling to stone walls with their rocky spines, miners use them as lanterns when navigating caves.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME possess a horn of volcanic stone. The shards they shed as they age and grow are incredibly sharp. People in ancient times would collect these shards to use as cooking knives.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's tusks are made of molten magma at the edges.  This allows them to slice through obstacles like a hot knife through butter.  If one is broken, the POKENAME can restore it by dipping it meticulously into lava.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME stands motionless on pedestals in ancient tombs for hours to watch over them. When it spots an intruder, it spits lava at them in rapid bursts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time clinging to the inner rims of active volcanoes. The stones around its torso shield its most sensitive parts, and play a crucial part in helping it evolve later in its life.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME soars through the sky spewing molten lava from its mouth. Its glowing trail lights up the night like falling stars.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides within its shell unless disturbed. If it feels something touch the shell, the stone cracks open and POKENAME's lava body spills out to burn the whatever bothered it.
author: sk372

entry: It carries around a large volcanic rock it uses as a shield. When weakened, it will make a new shield with its high-temperature claws.
author: melodydelune

entry: Its rock shield was once composed by different layers of brimstone, coal, iron and different gems like diamonds and emeralds.  Nowadays, they all have merged into an opaque irregular slag.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME bore their way through solid rock, creating complex tunnel networks that can stretch for miles. They leave grooves in the ceiling of their tunnels to mark where in the network they are, feeling their way through the dark with their antennae.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Almost all of POKENAME's body is covered by a layer of cooled, hardened lava, protecting the body while it evolves. When evolution draws near, it will roll up the side of the nearest volcano, diving in to complete its transformation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's saddened expressions are caused by the loss of their once quick movements. They aimlessly glide around instead, finding small comforts to soothe their wounded hearts.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME has an almost irresistible urge to bite and gnash things with its heated jaws. At times, it may tear chunks of cooled and hardened magma from its own body just to sate this compulsion.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME roars, its jagged stone fangs glow red-hot. One bite can leave molten cracks in solid rock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in snowy regions, and many Pokémon rely on them for warmth. During strong blizzards, there appears to be a bubble around them due to the snow melting before it can touch the ground.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME struggle to find a home for themselves, as they're too hot for the arctic but also too cold for volcanoes. Because of this, many trainers like to take them in, giving them a warm home that many longed for so long.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are like living fireballs that have a paradoxical ability to rapidly cool and freeze moisture around them. Their own ability causes the outer layer of their bodies to always be cooled and hardened into a durable shell of rock.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sits in pools of magma in active volcanoes, beckoning travelers to follow it into the depths. It is not intelligent enough to figure out why this does not work.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: When POKENAME bury themselves in the dirt at sundown, their ashen leaves drop off and regrow overnight. Gardeners collect fallen POKENAME leaves for use as fertilizer.
author: oddwalls

entry: It uses its wings to whip sweltering gusts into its opponents. The shell on its back is strong but brittle, so POKENAME tries to always attack facing forward.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME seeks to use its cheering dance routines as a way to imbue others with its fiery and electrifying spirit. Though most prefer pom-poms made of fire, some POKENAME have been seen wielding ones made of pure lightning.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often known as "Flaming Hot Garbage." Although true, it still hurts the Pokémon's feelings.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The smell of hot garbage emanating from this Pokémon causes any human not acclimated to it to become violently ill.
author: naga_sake

entry: These Pokémon have magmatic bodies clad in dense, volcanic rock that are otherwise very hollow. Although they can eat anything flammable, they seem to prefer to consume waste, which causes them to expel toxic fumes as the waste burns away within.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME travel through the planet's mantle, seeking explosive volcanic eruptions. They travel in vast schools, with some scientists postulating that in sufficient numbers, they can trigger eruptions due to their migration.
author: vic1312

entry: Fast enough to even speed through ground, POKENAME make lava canals as they move. They use the tips of their noses to melt through prey.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME appear after volcanic eruptions, forming out of the burnt tree stumps. Despite the stump being coated in a layer of heat-resistant ash, POKENAME's molten body will slowly burn it away.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is said that POKENAME will create its own natural habitat by starting a forest fire wherever it wishes to reside. It will only feel at home once every other tree around it has burned down.
author: spookypookie.

entry: The flower-like protrusion on its head can release an eruption of strong-smelling ash.  Some like the smell, but if the ash makes contact with skin, it will cause a painful burning sensation.
author: imaginita

entry: It takes its favorite fruit into its shell, cooks it with its body heat, and eats it. If something peeks in, it unleashes sonic blasts out the entrance towards them.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME's ears are strong enough to listen for prey deep down in caves. They tuck their bodies in before spinning, using the tips of their stone wings to dig down to these caves.
author: bigoljax

entry: Floating on wings of volcanic smoke, POKENAME travel to cold areas, perching on people's heads to keep them warm. Rarely, large flocks of these Pokémon have even been known to block out the sun.
author: secondegg

entry: The feathers of a POKENAME are like a big cloud of black smoke. Their tails of bubbling magma often drag below them as they fly at low altitudes.
author: infinex21

entry: Wherever POKENAME travels, it leaves a trail of sticky, burning slime. It is considered a major nuisance by many, as its slime is incredibly difficult to remove, and has been known to cause wildfires.
author: secondegg

entry: The magma of POKENAME's body is very viscous, making them quite slow. To avoid capture from predators, POKENAME detonate their shells, letting loose sharp obsidian shrapnel in all directions.
author: wiz0z

entry: The orange boiling slime covering POKENAME's body smells of burnt fruit and gasoline. Despite resembling lava, it is closer in consistency to glue and when cooled has been used in book bindings.
author: .izik

entry: Some old murals depict Pokémon reminiscent of POKENAME. POKENAME are docile dwellers of magma pools, and their volcanic rock shells are even hotter than their bodies due to the heat flowing within them.
author: infinex21

entry: Flames pour from the rock-like ears of POKENAME when they face a powerful opponent. If they believe themselves to be outmatched, they will withdraw inside of their shells and vent all of their stored heat until their opponent leaves them alone.
author: infinex21

entry: Steam and incredibly hot magma leak out from the cracks of POKENAME's stone body. It is believed that it was considered a sacred guardian, and the volcanoes it lived near were considered holy spots.
author: sk372

entry: Its body was once all molten, but being quickly cooled turned most of it into obsidian. Its insides still retain a large amount of heat.
author: jaycielantern

entry: The small circles on POKENAME's chest are actually their true eyes. They use their false set of eyes as a way to distract before going on the offensive.
author: bigoljax

entry: Wild POKENAME are often submerged in magma or lava, acting as floes of solid rock for others to walk upon. If they feel threatened, they can release a thick, paralytic gas from their shells.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives near the craters of volcanoes. It looks somehow pained as it rages around in search of fire, which serves as its energy source.
author: ._term.

entry: It loves to hug trainers it comes across, which makes it unintentionally dangerous due to its immense body heat. Unlike Bewear, it can control its strength and can even be safely hugged if one is properly equipped to withstand its heat.
author: secondegg

entry: The oozing algae covering the anchor is the true body of POKENAME. It secretes an oil that allows it to light itself aflame underwater. These bright flames can be seen from the surface, giving rise to tales of ghosts beneath the water.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME often live near underwater volcanoes. Their tentacles are made of hardened magma.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: POKENAME's tentacles are covered with rock hard enough to be as strong as steel. Those who try to attack these tentacles will suffer harsh burning that lasts for weeks.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME intentionally weakens its shell and cools its body heat to eliminate its combat advantages, preferring to rely on skill alone. Pro wrestlers adorn their masks with POKENAME's fiery feathers for good luck.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME is usually called hot-headed due to its fire, but it's actually quite the contrary. It lights up caves and forests for travelers.
author: dodoowner_

entry: A POKENAME's hat is made out of a very tough obsidian. It uses it to protect its Trainer from lethal attacks.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's spines are bits of lava from its body that have cooled and hardened after exposure to the air. It can fire them off in large volleys to deter intruders, new spines forming in their place within seconds.
author: sk372

entry: The mushroom-shaped shells upon their backs are actually how they vent excess internal heat. They have learned how to move just quick enough to not fully cool and harden but slow enough to not be fully melting.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can usually be seen dotting volcanic areas, residing near active rivers of flowing lava. It protects young Slugma by letting them hide within its stone castle, which it seals up when approaching danger is sensed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME looks like the volcanoes that once drove it to extinction. It makes its home in mountainous environments.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Capable of super-cooling magma near instantly, POKENAME can walk straight across magma pools, provided they are moving at a steady pace. The shards of volcanic glass they leave behind were historically prized by local indigenous groups.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME make great pets, as their lava isn't as hot as it seems. However, owners and trainers still need to keep careful of the fire coming out of POKENAME's tail.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are often seen in packs, usually hunting down Pokémon like Rapidash. However, packs can dwindle quickly, as one kick from Rapidash can knock them out.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME usually hunt alone, focusing on weaker prey. However, if hungry enough, POKENAME will sometimes dig for fossils to satisfy their hunger.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME uses shed bits of cooled lava to form a makeshift mic stand to use during its performances. Against all odds, this homemade tool does somehow make POKENAME's voice louder and have more reverberation.
author: sk372

entry: Some rituals documented from ancient island settlements paid homage to POKENAME, believing that their fiery dancing kept volcanoes from erupting and destroying the land. Their lava-like hair reaches temperatures well over 1,000°F.
author: chibitales

entry: Born from a great solar flare that faced the moon, It is said a POKENAME's presence once stopped the eruption of a volcano, saving many lives.
author: frokachu

entry: While POKENAME uses its big stone teeth to intimidate foes, it uses them sparingly since they break and crumble very easily. It uses psychic powers to shape its spouting flames to look like snazzy, eye-catching fins.
author: soup1900

entry: Their large, cone-shaped shells serve as shields for their softer bodies and as a means to store and vent excess heat. Their pincers are the hottest parts of their bodies, capable of softening most materials with their heat as they slice through.
author: infinex21

entry: In this form, POKENAME contains the energy of innumerable active volcanoes. They're very friendly, but they struggle to control their heat when excited, causing destruction wherever they go.
author: hero.drawing

entry: POKENAME rapidly cool off sections of their molten body to forge into plated armor. They use this armor to protect their bodies in battle and to create deafening earthquakes that intimidate threats into thinking that a volcano is about to erupt.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME spend most of their lives meditating under falling lava inside of volcanoes to strengthen their shells. They will provoke any threat that they see as a display of superiority.
author: nexusshenanigans

entry: POKENAME slept deep underground for so many millennia while experiencing astounding pressures and temperatures that much of their bodies have melted into magma. These molten forms grant them unique abilities to manipulate heat.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: A thick shell of volcanic rock covers their head, it is relatively brittle but distributes force effectively. This defense protects POKENAME from most blows to their head. They will retreat to allow the shell to repair itself when broken.
author: vic1312

entry: The mushroom's nature seems to have been altered by fusion, and POKENAME is often driven mad as a result. The orange goop it spews burns through anything it touches like lava, and the fusion's tough carapace makes its slamming attacks deadly.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME spreads a heated dark crimson powder from its body around its nest. Contact with this powder can cause chemical burns that scar if not washed off immediately.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME like to compete with each other by seeing how far their flames can shoot out. Some even try to challenge other Pokémon like Magmortar, though they usually lose.
author: bigoljax

entry: While POKENAME sleeps, the lava in its ears cools and hardens. This temporarily limits its hearing until it warms up again.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rest in caves filled with gases and smoke from their bodies. Those that inhale these fumes will gain temporary psychic abilities, including muddled visions of the future.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME prefers to live near warmer water sources such as hot springs. It frequently soaks plant life in the water for extended periods before eating it, effectively cooking it first.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are usually spotted in groups of three. They meditate on stones in their volcanic habitat, balancing on one leg the entire time.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body stays molten as long as it has eaten enough. When enraged, it vents scalding smoke from its back in great plumes.
author: .izik

entry: The orange boiling slime covering POKENAME's body drips off as it moves. The spots in the soil where it lands spread nutrients that help nearby plant life grow rapidly once the slime cools.
author: .izik

entry: The fluff of POKENAME is highly desired, as it tastes like sweet oranges when consumed. POKENAME will only allow those it trusts to have some; for others, the fluff can be heated to triple-digit degrees to ward off foes.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Despite POKENAME looking like it could burn your hand off with singeing flames, its temperature can go up to a maximum of 110°F. Despite that, they are known to reach their maximum temperature only if aggravated.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: POKENAME's body is constantly cooling, so it sheds thin layers of volcanic rock to keep its entire body from hardening. It can hide in its rocky skin to protect itself, but if it stays in this state for too long, it will be unable to break free.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME floats on the surface of lava flows, preferring the hotter temperatures of an active volcanic eruption. Small Pokémon have occasionally been seen using them as stepping stones to get across.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME's hat keeps their bodies safe from rainfall due to water causing their bodies to lose shape. Their hats can also be used to cook berries and meat.
author: bigoljax

entry: Despite constantly dripping magma, POKENAME's dances thankfully don't fling their magma at others. They're often the Pokémon of choice during fire festivals.
author: bigoljax

entry: Many of the fireballs launched during volcanic eruptions are actually POKENAME. Despite the explosive force that sends them flying, they often land fully intact.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are often seen in the skies above volcanos, nearly above the atmosphere. Some mistake them for shooting stars during their descents.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME have sharp but fragile claws that they use to tear their foes apart. The volcanic rock scales they occasionally shed were once collected by ancient peoples. They used the scales to line their weapons and decorate ritual accessories.
author: vic1312

entry: As POKENAME tunnels underground, it leaves behind a trail of lava, scorching the plant roots above it. POKENAME can be tracked by following the paths of burnt grass.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME whips lava-covered appendages at coal and plant life to absorb and condense them into carbon. After a month of storing this within its body, odd green diamond-like gems appear on it that many claim can grant a wish if touched while sleeping.
author: .izik

entry: The crystals along a POKENAME's body are crystallized magma. These crystals do not melt and never seem to cool off, leading many to use them to help them stay warm in colder environments.
author: infinex21

entry: Due to POKENAME's shells being shaped like hearts, they're commonly seen in romantic restaurants in tropical regions. They seem to be fine with this, as they're regularly fed by the waiters and chefs.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME bore up to 60 miles deep into the planet to bathe in fresh magma. It was once thought that POKENAME could create new volcanoes, but the tunnels they dig are too narrow for magma to reach the surface.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME hangs from trees, attempting to mimic an acorn. However, it frequently has to move to a new tree due to unintentionally burning down its previous one.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME flies constantly in search of warmth, only stopping to rest when it is in a sufficiently hot area. Its rock-like feathers are very brittle, and will crumble into dust if it is not handled carefully.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME can often be seen flying around volcanoes, appearing to feed on the lava itself. The insides of their beaks get hot enough that some fishermen have trained them to cook fish.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME are commonly found loitering around forges, hoping to pocket any still-molten metal to shape into coins and other shiny baubles. Blacksmiths will often keep spare scrap metal heated in their shops to distract this Pokémon.
author: notadoctor75

entry: By blowing air through its horns, POKENAME can perfectly mimic the sound of a volcanic eruption. It expels a large amount of hot air and smoke in the process, often frightening away its opponents before a battle can even begin.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME's flaming tail grows incredibly large when bathed in full moonlight. This is a beautiful sight from afar that hikers frequently regard as a good omen for their travels.
author: .izik

entry: Using the immense heat and pressure within its shell, it produces a variety of gemstones. It is very prideful, decorating itself with these gems in a vain attempt to appear more beautiful.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME's stone parts are the result of the electricity in its body running more rampant and hardening specific sections. Touching these hardened spots results in getting a small shock from the stored energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's taillights help lead them through darker caves. These taillights are considered valuable by poachers, causing POKENAME to be under threat.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are typically avoided by Volbeat since, while their bursting flames are very eye-catching, they also can burn those who get close. While POKENAME's light is typically dim, if their stone shell breaks off, they start shining like a star.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME enjoys being used as a kiln in schools because of the guaranteed protection and food. It has been noted that if POKENAME finds a piece of pottery of low quality, it will eat the piece. How it judges quality has yet to be determined.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The hump of hardened magma on POKENAME's back acts as a thermal regulator. It can store heat to maintain the POKENAME through winter, or expel excess heat in the summer.
author: imaginita

entry: The volcanoes on POKENAME's back build up larger each time it erupts. Some can even grow to nine feet in length if POKENAME erupts as soon as it's done building up magma.
author: bigoljax

entry: A large amount of steam builds up within POKENAME's beak, the only part of its body made of hardened lava. It needs to vent this steam out regularly, lest it start developing painful headaches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's large stone claws are hard, yet brittle. It fights carefully except when facing serpent-like Pokémon, whereupon it fights with such ferocity that it often chips and breaks its own claws.
author: sk372

entry: Due to their bodies not being completely solid, POKENAME's poison mixes with their lava. They use this to their advantage, coating their tails with this mixture and stabbing their prey.
author: bigoljax

entry: When beneath the moonlight, POKENAME's magma burns hotter and boils in an almost aggressive manner. The hardened stone bits of its body have been discovered to have a similar makeup to rocks recovered from the moon.
author: sk372

entry: Some have said the magma within POKENAME's body burns hotter than the sun, but this is false. However, it has been noted that the heat of its body does increase dramatically when exposed to direct sunlight.
author: sk372

entry: Its dark, obsidian spikes absorb solar energy, which is stored within its rocky shell. It is believed that the inside of a POKENAME is as hot as the sun itself.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME were once under high threat of poachers due to the symbols on their foreheads. However, due to most of their population being relocated to volcanos, poaching attempts have dropped significantly.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME live within undersea volcanoes or around hydrothermal vents to keep themselves warm even in the deep sea. When traveling in colder climates, they fold their claws over the opening of their shells to preserve heat.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is a ferocious ambush predator, in spite of its slow speed. It sneaks up on its prey, trapping them in its magma-filled claws.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME swim around geothermal vents where the water is incredibly hot. The minerals that come from the geothermal vents are absorbed into their bodies and help maintain their tough shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME moves by spinning upon its singular foot, which also keeps its magmatic body from fully cooling; even when it rests, it slowly spins in place. It can spin fast enough to generate strong heat, at which point it exudes flames from its head.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are often found residing in ruins of ancient cities destroyed by volcanic activity. Archeologists and explorers who encounter it are advised to flee, as it blasts intruders with blazing hot beams from its hands.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME are responsible for a substantial increase in volcanic activity in areas where they are densely populated. The rocky armor that covers its body is actually fruit that it produces, which can be harvested as a rare delicacy.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME's cries can become so ear-piercingly loud that the bits of stone casing present on its body will disintegrate. It is often seen hanging from juts of volcanic rock since that is one of the few materials its lava won't melt through.
author: soup1900

entry: On colder nights, POKENAME are always finding ways to stay warm. Some Trainers report that they find their POKENAME falling asleep by dryer vents, the gentle heat having lulled them to sleep.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: During volcanic eruptions, POKENAME can be found sliding down lava flows and landing in the sea. They clap happily as they bounce on the surface of the water.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME's body is held back by the weight of its shell, causing its already fiery disposition to get worse as it fails to strike those far away. Once it manages to attack someone and vent its rage, it is utterly relentless.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spouts fire at objects it's curious about and inhales the smoke, usually to figure out their smell and taste. Its hard, rock-plated head protects it from volcanic debris.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME are usually found in huddles on the coasts of islands after volcanic eruptions. They seek out the lava rivers the volcano creates, resting peacefully near them.
author: bigoljax

entry: When sealed and submerged, POKENAME appear to be a mundane rock. This confounded geologists who observed seemingly random hot springs appearing overnight. Traditional communities at higher elevations have used POKENAME for heating for centuries.
author: vic1312

entry: With a body of magma and volcanic rock, POKENAME effortlessly swims through lava in volcanic isles. It dislikes the presence of others, spitting out globs of magma mixed with bits of stone at anyone who catches its ire.
author: sk372

entry: While most of POKENAME is made of hot magma, its nose consists of cool, hardened stone, which allows it to show its love and affection with others. However, avoid being near it if it catches a cold, since it will sneeze lava out of its nostril.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can send pulses of sound waves through the top of its head to forcefully push lava and have it erupt out like a volcano. It is said to be able to increase the love and warmth of others by emitting these same waves out at low frequencies.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's shell limiting its movements makes its already raging temperament even wilder. Once it gets angry enough, it can exhibit enough strength to gain a burst of ludicrous speed and chase down the nearest target it can find.
author: sk372

entry: They crawl out of magma pools using their arms to hunt. If threatened, a POKENAME can hide under its shell, but as the shell is merely hardened skin, it's brittle and not the best for defense. Most will try to escape back into the lava instead.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME are found inside underwater volcanoes, feeding off whatever reaches the ocean floor. These Pokémon have been observed maintaining extreme temperatures of heat despite being fully submerged within the sea.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME are very loyal pets. However, their high body temperature often leads to them living outside of their family homes. As such, POKENAME have become symbols of guardianship and protection when seen outside of a building.
author: wiz0z

entry: Despite the often laborious movement of magma, POKENAME are incredibly fleet-footed Pokémon. They form their shells from lightweight pumice instead of sturdier cooled magma rock. The jet of fire that arises from their shell flares at high speeds.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME use their shell to roll due to the lack of mobility of their magma-like body. When their shells are damaged by this rolling, their brittle shells scatter debris that they often use as fiery projectiles.
author: zekkenbytheden

entry: POKENAME sits at rest often, its body quietly smoldering as it conserves its energy. When it senses humans in danger nearby, it uses that stored energy to dash off at breakneck speeds to rescue them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME travels the world through magma veins, testing the resolve of those it challenges with an overpowering heat from its body. If its foe is able to withstand this initial assault, it will engage them in battle, using even stronger flames still.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME has been seen being employed by stronger Pokémon to protect their nesting areas. It stands firm with a resilient heavy stone torso, fighting off intruders with its magma fists.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever threatened, POKENAME bash their hardened bellies as loud as they can. If their warnings are ignored, POKENAME will slam their rock hard fists hard into their opponent's skulls.
author: bigoljax

entry: The shell on the back of POKENAME is formed from the parts of its skin that have cooled into hardened magma. It works to keep itself in a perpetual state of exertion so that the rest of its body never has the chance to harden.
author: badtothebow

entry: It spends all day napping in the craters of volcanoes, only waking in the hottest part of the day to eat. If it senses that even the smallest part of its body is beginning to cool, it instantly teleports to a hotter area.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME absorb metal into their bodies and rapidly cool themselves down in order to forge the metal into spoons. The spoons collect and direct their oozing bodies, ensuring that a POKENAME's flames only burn what it wants them to.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When its body aches from training, POKENAME submerges in lava to relax. Once fully rested, it can lift a pickup truck without much effort.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME visit volcanic vents to slather themselves in fresh magma. Afterwards, they cool themselves in pools of water, adding a new layer to their already powerful bodies.
author: wiz0z

entry: With their incredible strength and high heat, POKENAME are able to punch holes through other Pokémon. However, they rarely do this, as they don't wish for unnecessary violence.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME use their increased body temperature to power steam locomotives. For long journeys, POKENAME eat four handfuls of coal at a time to burn long enough.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME move their thin, ashy bodies in short, jerky movements. When threatened, they blast balls of magma at their attackers from their mouths. The ash from their bodies contains extremely high concentrations of heavy metals.
author: vic1312

entry: Its shell has hardened into pure obsidian, making it incredibly heat-resistant. It burns its attackers by spraying lava from its mouth.
author: secondegg

entry: A POKENAME's body is made out of hot lava. It uses the magma inside of its stomach to melt its food.
author: bluefire7_9

entry: Their leaf-like covers prevent them from leaking the bubbling-hot, poisonous liquid inside of them all over themselves. Unfortunately, this practice causes the excess heat inside to vent out from their sides almost constantly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live at the very bottom of the ocean, staying completely still. They do this to disguise themselves as deep sea vents, snatching prey that get close enough.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME sleeps within boulders near lava pools. If it senses a volcanic eruption is imminent, it reflexively detonates within the boulder, scattering stones in all directions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps belly-down in lava pools, using its rocky shell to float. The heat seeps into its core and keeps it energized.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to the walls of volcanoes with others of its kind. They drop into the lava one at a time, comparing splash height to determine their leader.
author: .izik

entry: As it gallops, POKENAME leaves puddles of lava where its hooves strike the ground. The trail glows long after it passes.
author: .izik

entry: The stone saddle on POKENAME's back is cool enough to make it easy for a human to ride it. Though faster than many Magcargo fusions, POKENAME's top speed is rather average.
author: sk372

entry: Years of fishing out fragments of hard lava with its tail has formed a shell on its back. It is so hot that bits of the shell would melt on occasion.
author: alliveir

entry: POKENAME's shell forms cracks over time that spout out the fire from beneath periodically. This makes older POKENAME more dangerous as it gives them greater amounts of flame to defend themselves with.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME's liquid body seeps into its shell, its life force makes it come to life. The tip of its shell can blast boiling hot magma at enemies.
author: alliveir

entry: POKENAME are like floating balls of magma mostly encased in a protective layer of molten rock. Their molten rock shells are composed of a magnetic material that gives them a slight electric charge and is thought to be what allows them to float.
author: infinex21

entry: The stone magnets on all three components of POKENAME work in tandem to great effect. However, the magnets are brittle and may fall off if jostled, inhibiting their coordination until new ones can form.
author: sk372

entry: The molten rock of their bodies are lined with magnetic materials that keep their three heads connected together. Due to them always being stuck together, their rock shells have begun to melt into their bodies due to the heat.
author: infinex21

entry: The contents of its soupy body are highly nutritious, but piping hot. Small amounts of POKENAME's soup can be eaten at a time without causing harm.
author: admiralvermin

entry: Unable to regulate its own body temperature, its heads are at risk of hardening into stone if they cool off too much. To counteract this, they take turns dipping themselves into lava flows to heat up.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME squawks loudly as it dashes across volcanic terrain. Each footstep leaves behind a faint trail of scorched dirt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs holes that act like air vents inside of volcanoes so it can breathe clean air after swimming inside lava for hours. It despises water since it would harden its magma body to rock and restrict its movements for play.
author: soup1900

entry: Residing in the waters around polar volcanoes, POKENAME raise their young on large pumice islands. Their shells are also composed of pumice, which helps POKENAME control their buoyancy while diving.
author: vic1312

entry: The glowing orange sludge covering POKENAME's body is hot to the touch. When resting, it retreats into its shell and hides in a dark environment while giving off a putrid trash-like scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME power large locomotives with their body heat. They vent noxious smoke through an exhaust pipe to keep workers safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The lava in POKENAME's shell reaches 12,000 degrees Fahrenheit, hardening its shell to an obsidian-like rock. It takes water into the barrels of its cannons, superheats it, and then blasts opponents with scolding jets of steam.
author: ilazerheart

entry: Because their tongue burns much hotter than the rest of their body, POKENAME will always leave it sticking out. Since POKENAME bury themselves in sand to sleep, divers will see groups of orange tongues sticking out of the seabed.
author: oddwalls

entry: The fractures in POKENAME's shell expose its soft core and weaken its defenses. It compensates by increasing its temperature to unbearable levels and firing sharp spikes at foes.
author: oddwalls

entry: POKENAME collects rocks to consolidate its gelatinous body, slowly eating them to stay alive. The rocks shed by a POKENAME are said to be as hard as diamonds.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME are often seen in the depths of volcanic areas, as their bodies are composed entirely of molten rock. It has become common to compare someone's breath to that of POKENAME, due to the poisonous gas that escapes their mouths.
author: jangodiot

entry: The charcoal-scented fumes rising from POKENAME's lava are extremely toxic. Prolonged exposure can cause intense paranoia and an odd onset of hydrophobia.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are seldom seen in the wild, as they bury deep within the world's mantle. On the rare occasion one is spotted above ground, nearby towns are evacuated, as they only ever surface in response to intense volcanic activity.
author: secondegg

entry: These Pokémon made mostly of magma dig so deep under volcanic regions that they have begun to form shells made of obsidian. They occasionally surface directly within pools of lava to keep the rest of their bodies from cooling off too much.
author: infinex21

entry: If POKENAME eats a nice, pleasant dream, its body cools down and hardens as it comfortably lounges around. However, if it eats a nightmare, its body boils as flames erupt and previously cooled rocks melt back to magma.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's magmatic pendulums have the ability to cause any other being to fall asleep. However, due to the heat they radiate, its hard for them to sneak up on their victims.
author: bigoljax

entry: When POKENAME's lava-like skin touches water, it quickly cools and hardens into a grey carapace.  However, this shell is brittle and will crack if the POKENAME gets fired up or is hit by an attack, revealing a new layer of fiery skin beneath.
author: imaginita

entry: The lower halves of their bodies are made of volcanic rock with some amounts of boiling water to keep them from getting too hot. When the rock of their large pincer cracks, steam pours out from within.
author: infinex21

entry: The lava in POKENAME's shell is so hot and dense that the shell has become a miniature volcanic cluster. POKENAME sprays water onto its back to cool and harden the magma, gradually thickening its shell.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME use their long beaks to grab berries out of treetops. They often get into duels with each other, clashing their beaks into each other. No matter how intense the fights get, POKENAME always stick to a code of honor to not attack their bulbs.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME rely on their beaks to peck at Grass-type Pokémon that hide inside tree crevices. If their prey tries to escape, they launch stringy silk to pin them down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The feathers on its orb-like body are filled with static electricity. When it flies near hair salons, it causes chaos by ruining hairstyles with stray shocks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME zooms past power plants and radio towers, leveraging magnetic fields to fly faster. They race each other as a display of dominance, as the fastest POKENAME gets to drain batteries first.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME knocks Metapod from trees to hunt for food. It carries them back to its nest, piercing them with its beak before feeding.
author: .izik

entry: Their wings can be used almost like hands, at least enough to grab hold of foods and the remains of their prey. Even while holding something, they can still fly and attack by throwing objects or by pecking with their long beaks.
author: infinex21

entry: This aggressive bird Pokémon dive‑kicks its prey from above with pinpoint precision, stunning them before they can react.
author: sanserof

entry: Beneath its feathers, POKENAME hides an incredibly tough shell that shields its body from attacks. Its long beak allows it to suck sap from trees, feeding and growing stronger every day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: While its body resembles smooth stone, it is covered in tiny, hard feathers. These feathers enhance its agility, making it difficult to target in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a doting yet strict parent, encouraging its young to hunt for food on its own. It trains the child's flight by flapping its wings, providing strong gusts of wind the young must fly against.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME nests on seaside cliffs and hunts land and aquatic prey. While its adapted body allows it to dive deeper underwater than a Fearow, its bulky body and lack of a long neck reduce aerial agility.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: POKENAME drink nectar from flowers with their long beaks. They flap their wings rapidly to keep their body in a fixed position while they drink. They flap their wings about 60 times a second to maintain their airborne position.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have the ability to perfectly mimic the sounds that any other Pokémon makes. They do this whilst entertaining freshly hatched Pokémon, flourishes of their feathered wings adding to their performance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME primarily feeds on tiny fish in small ponds. It dips its stinger into the water to leak poison into it, then uses its beak to spear the sickened fish that float to the surface.
author: sk372

entry: When it becomes enraged, blazing flames flare along its ears and crest, extinguishing only once POKENAME has calmed down. It feeds primarily on small insects, which it captures with precision thanks to its long beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME tears through the sky, terrorizing low-flying planes. Its thick plumage keeps it warm at high altitudes, so it nests in icy mountain caves.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME tears through the sky, terrorizing low-flying planes. Dense plumage keeps it warm at high altitudes, letting it nest in icy mountain caves.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME tears through the sky, terrorizing low-flying planes. Dense plumage keeps it warm at high altitudes, letting it nest in icy mountain caves.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME tears through the sky, terrorizing low-flying planes. Dense plumage keeps it warm at high altitudes, letting it nest in icy mountain caves.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME is notoriously bad at building its own nests. Instead, it uses its impressive size to push out other Pokémon from their homes. Though not the most polite approach, this tactic ensures it always has a comfortable place to sleep.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME's large crest and wings serve to make them seem larger to potential predators. Their dance-like movements allow them to deftly cross the battlefield and wreathe opponents in intense flames.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses the beak-like stingers on its arms to spear through fish and larger insects for consumption. It flies up to high canopies to eat, hoping to remain far away from any that would potentially steal its hard-earned meals.
author: sk372

entry: Despite POKENAME's belligerent nature, its small size hardly makes it a threat. It spends most of its time bugging other Pokémon for scraps of food.
author: mepp.

entry: It drums its beak on trees to communicate with its allies, coordinating group hunts. These rhythmic signals ensure effective teamwork.
author: .izik

entry: Unwary Trainers may mistake POKENAME for Hoothoot when encountering them for the first time. Unlike Hoothoot, POKENAME will aggressively defend their nest and the surrounding territory with a combination of hypnotic powers and their sharp beaks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME grow impressively large head plumage in a vivid red, using the feathers as a warning to other Pokémon to keep their distance. Should their warning be ignored, they will strike with their long beak and agile neck.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It tumbles through the air in a chaotic movement while punching, aiming to knock foes off balance. This aerial technique makes it unpredictable in combat.
author: .izik

entry: It stays high in the trees, waiting to launch onto its prey. When it approaches, POKENAME will fly onto its food and sting it with venom.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are prideful creatures that have a cardinal-red beak. They hunt Bug-type Pokémon by creating a skewer of living prey on their beak before bringing them back to their nest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite POKENAME's massive wingspan, its small size hardly makes it a threat. It spends most of its time bugging other Pokémon for scraps of food, swatting at them with its wings.
author: mepp.

entry: There are reports of POKENAME becoming so enraged that its feathers harden to the strength of iron. With this enhancement, its Wing Attack can topple buildings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME possesses all the best and most helpful traits of the Pidgey and Spearow line. Its speed, size, strength and shining feathers have often confused researchers, thinking that POKENAME is the missing link of the three legendary birds of Kanto.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: As POKENAME grows, it will shed its wings, which can take 3 to 4 weeks to regrow. Without its wings, the electricity in its beak becomes amplified.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME grows, it will shed its wings, which can take 3 to 4 weeks to regrow. Its wings store electricity like batteries.
author: .izik

entry: If it catches a strong wind, it can glide for miles without flapping its wings. It flexes its head crest to help it turn in the air.
author: cait_sith

entry: It floats lazily through meadows, enjoying the breeze. If it gets stuck on an obstacle, it uses its sharp beak to free itself with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends nearly its entire lifetime in the sky, thanks to its large, cotton wings. Its cotton spores commonly cause seasonal allergies.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: POKENAME are popular with Kanto Bird Keepers, their intelligence making them easy to train whilst their build allows them to fly at high speeds and over great distances. During battle they use their long beak to peck at their foes during a dive.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If it detects the scent of cheese in a home, it drills its beak into the roof to gain entry. This behavior makes it a persistent scavenger.
author: .izik

entry: Blending up a Via Seed with other berries into a Colorful Shake and giving it to POKENAME will make them start to dance uncontrollably for a few minutes. There have been many viral videos of this put to music.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME clash with other POKENAME with claws, beaks, and vines. Despite the ferociousness of the exchange, they leave the bulb undamaged as a sign of mutual respect to each other.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its beak conceals rigid, tooth-like structures that latch onto foes. Once it bites down, it refuses to let go for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can rapidly repel itself away from any surface to launch at incredible speed. At top speed, POKENAME can punch its beak through several feet of steel.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME uses its long beak to prune wilting flowers at grave sites. Some say it mourns the dead, but there are no actual facts that can back this up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soars at incredible speeds, leaving shimmering trails in the air. Its single eye is said to pierce through any deception, and it often fixes its gaze on things others overlook.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Utilizing both of its brains, it can subtly manipulate a person's thoughts. With proper training, it even helps people break bad habits.
author: .izik

entry: It will spend time on the side of cliff walls breaking off small stones. It will fling small stones to taunt travelers.
author: .izik

entry: It monitors foes from afar, carefully observing their movements for signs of danger. If it detects a threat, it lets out a loud caw to alert its flock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can rapidly puff up their bodies, expanding to two or three times their normal body size. When they do this, they become buoyant in air, able to swim around through the sky.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: By skillfully flapping its wings, it creates gusts of icy wind that slow its opponents. When it spots an object of interest, it snatches it with its long beak and swiftly takes flight before it can be caught.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The bubbling material on its body is mud-like in texture but grows intensely hot when it moves. The heat can reach temperatures capable of melting steel.
author: .izik

entry: Sporting an extra pair of wings and feathers of a deeper brown, DNA improvements of POKENAME lead to them often dominating unfused Fearow in competitions to find a partner. This can lead to rejected Fearow become less predatorial while hunting.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: POKENAME uses long-range spouts of water shot at quick speed to stun targets from a distance. Once stopped in their tracks, it swims forward quickly in an attempt to spear them with its pointed beak.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a proud fighter. It swoops down on unsuspecting Fighting-type Pokémon for duels. Pokémon fusion has given it a majestic visage reminiscent of human Karate masters.
author: lupa

entry: POKENAME are incredibly fast despite having no limbs. Their muscles, especially near the tail, can coil up and act like a spring in a pinch letting POKENAME soar to great heights before tunneling down into the ground to capture their prey.
author: faeflame

entry: Its ears have hollow bones that enable limited flight, while its feathers efficiently capture air currents. This unique adaptation makes it surprisingly agile.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its large size, a POKENAME can fly faster than most humans can run. It has the ability to divebomb a target from hundreds of feet away.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its wings to kick up strong gusts of wind to blow away trespassers in its territory. Those unable to be pushed away or those who return after ignoring this warning risk getting charged at and potentially skewered.
author: sk372

entry: It migrates in great numbers, navigating using magnetic orbs on its antlers. The POKENAME with the brightest crest is the leader of the flock.
author: cait_sith

entry: The red, paint-like fluid dripping from its tail emits a bitter scent. It uses this liquid to create intricate designs on rocks and trees.
author: .izik

entry: It perches coiled around tall trees, before using its wings to glide far distances and hunt unsuspecting prey. Having POKENAME glide over you while adventuring is said to be an unlucky omen.
author: sk372

entry: When its milk supply is drained, it uses a powerful Drill Peck to crack open trees and consume their sap. This sustains it in times of scarcity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME electrifies its long beak to stun opponents and gain the upper hand in battle. It has a habit of pecking at high-voltage power lines to recharge its energy, unintentionally causing power drops or blackouts in nearby cities.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As its name implies, POKENAME likes to strike fear into its targets by hunting them down while screaming out of its many mechanical lungs.
author: funkytomate

entry: POKENAME's long beak is used to dig deep into the dirt, helping not only with navigation, but also with snatching up prey. Its favored target is Trapinch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective of its young, willing to do anything to keep them safe from danger. Though its feathers are sharp, they are as delicate as leaves.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME lashes out with its wings to deliver a powerful blow as well as using its long beak to peck at anyone who attacks its home jungle.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME's long beak burns with intense heat, leaving singed marks wherever it strikes. In battle, it swings its beak like a saber, scorching foes with each slash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME make their nest on the ground where they can better hunt for food. When these Pokémon spot a potential meal, they will lower their stance and wait for the prey to get close before attacking with their long and heated beaks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's long beak is used to dig deep into the dirt, helping not only with navigation, but also with snatching up prey. Its favored target is Trapinch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have large wings that keep these powerful Pokémon airborne with only a few flaps. POKENAME avoid fighting when they can, but will protect themselves using martial arts if a fight is unavoidable.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When POKENAME spots prey, they'll launch themselves at high speeds, twirling and corkscrewing through the air. Each POKENAME has its own choreography.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME is able to utilize its elegant wings with its excellent footwork to create an elaborate and captivating ritual dance for attracting a mate.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME is able to combine its elegant wings with its excellent footwork to create an elaborate and captivating ritual dance for attracting a mate.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME are highly agile combatants, using their wings to outmanoeuvre their foes before landing a slash with their arm blades. Their agility and finesse make them popular Pokémon with Black Belt Trainers, who often aim to learn their style.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A weak toxin is stored at the tip of its beak, which leaks out when it becomes angry. The dripping venom leaves faint trails on the ground.
author: .izik

entry: The friction from POKENAME's frantically beating wings generates the distinctive red lightning it is known for. They are highly sought after as exotic pets, but breed rapidly and can easily become an invasive species.
author: octolinggrimm

entry: Normally POKENAME uses its extendable tongue to catch small bugs to satiate its hunger. However, its beak can also elongate slightly in a quick burst, making it effective at spearing fish swimming close to the surface.
author: sk372

entry: It rams its head into trees to make sap leak out, often knocking itself unconscious in the process. This reckless method is both endearing and clumsy.
author: .izik

entry: Depictions of POKENAME were found in ancient tombs of kings. Due to their ability to read auras, they were kept close to prevent assassinations. In modern times, they dig through forest soil with their staves in order to control pest populations.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are home to many small bird Pokémon that nest in their wings. The flower on their back release calming spores that calm angry predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It soars gracefully over prairies using its large wings. From its beak, it can fire tiny barbed needles with surprising accuracy to fend off attackers.
author: .izik

entry: Legends state POKENAME's beak could shatter an entire mountain in one strike. Shockingly, three such incidents are recorded in historical documents.
author: .izik

entry: The potent toxin secreted from its beak glows faintly in the dark. This eerie luminescence serves as both a warning and a threat to predators.
author: .izik

entry: It spins like a top, charging magnetic energy through its beak. When fully unleashed, its magnetic force is powerful enough to sink a cruise ship.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME were a popular subject of statues amongst many medieval societies, their likeness lining many castle pathways. Anthropologists theorise that this was to allow nobles to station POKENAME as concealed guards to surprise invaders.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The needle-like blade of POKENAME is retractable into its body and extends quickly when startled. This sudden movement catches many by surprise.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The horn on its head resembles a sharp beak, hollow inside and filled with potent poison. It injects this toxin into foes with precision during battle, leaving them incapacitated.
author: .izik

entry: Intruders in POKENAME's domain will be tormented by illusions that cause them to lose themselves in the woods. It watches its victims high up in the forest canopy, striking the moment they collapse from fatigue.
author: snomisgod.

entry: Its large, powerful wings allow POKENAME to remain airborne for long periods of time without needing to land.
author: melodydelune

entry: If pursued while flying, POKENAME wiggles its talons unpredictably, triggering strange and chaotic abilities. This has led to many Trainers avoiding conflict with it, unsure of what might happen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scatters an incredibly toxic brown powder as it flies through forested areas. Anything that touches the powder can develop a fever that lasts for days.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies above the nests of other Pokémon, emitting a soft, hypnotic melody from its beak. Once the inhabitants fall asleep, it swoops down to snatch an Egg for its next meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can easily soar up to 200 feet; however, its ghostly attachment to its urn-like body pulls it back to the ground if it overextends.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME line their nests with a thick silk that they produce from their abdomen. The silk has a static charge that attracts loose feathers, making for a plush and comfortable environment for them to lay their eggs in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Nicknamed "The Emperor of the Skies", POKENAME fires internal energy from its wings to fly at Mach speeds, charging towards those who gain its ire.
author: ansleehariot

entry: It hunts for small Pokémon by forcing them out of their habitat with controlled embers. Although unprovoked attacks from POKENAME are extremely rare, they are well-documented.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives atop towers or skyscrapers. It swiftly flies between cities to hunt smaller flying Pokémon, and uses its beak and talons to secure its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies so efficiently that it can go its whole life without landing. Because it can make itself invisible, most people only witness it as the sensation of a cool breeze by riversides.
