entry: POKENAME can store several thousand volts worth of electricity in their cheeks. When this happens, they often get excited and run around continuously until they discharge.
author: jadey.1557

entry: POKENAME has gills that allow it to live underwater, however due to the vast amounts of electricity it stores in its cheeks, other aquatic Pokémon will often avoid it. Because of this, wild POKENAME will usually live together in small groups.
author: jadey.1557

entry: If a screensaver activates while POKENAME inhabits a system, it delivers a small electric shock to move the mouse. Its dislike of idle screens remains unexplained.
author: .izik

entry: The Thunderstones within its shell can store inordinate amounts of electrical energy.  When the time is right, POKENAME conducts this incredible voltage through its tentacles.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME has highly conductive forearms, which it utilizes by stabbing opponents and shocking them. Sometimes, this Pokémon ends up being a hazard if its Trainer is careless, as it can easily electrify bodies of water if it ever decides to swim.
author: jangodiot

entry: It appears to simply be a very large Raichu at first glance. If its feet don't give away that it's part Snorlax, its appetite will.
author: faelocke

entry: POKENAME's behavior isn't aggressive even when it has stored a lot of electricity in its pouches due to being part Snorlax. If its pouches are low on electricity, POKENAME will feel tired and might fall asleep to regather electricity.
author: mbavenger64

entry: POKENAME runs at incredibly high speeds, becoming nearly imperceptible to the human eye at its peak, leaving trails of static wherever it goes. Anyone present during its run reports their hair standing on end and a smell of burning in the air.
author: .izik

entry: This kindhearted Pokémon has been known to guide ships during storms, using its body to absorb lighting strikes as it flies.
author: melodydelune

entry: Its stingers are known to pack a punch of 11,000 volts when used to attack. When captured, many use rubber caps to prevent shocking.
author: supersonicloki

entry: Although POKENAME's shocks are incredibly powerful, it is surprisingly passive. It can sometimes be found handing flowers to small children who stumble upon it.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: Their necks and tails are wreathed in strong flames that crackle with sparks of electricity. They will swing their flaming tails at foes and wherever the tip strikes, they will explosively release electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME are typically docile and avoid confrontation. The bright colors of their feathers and relative ease of training have caused many wild POKENAME to be caught.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are rarely seen outside of thunderstorms, spending most of their days sheltering within tree hollows. When a storm starts, they take to the air, their tail trailing behind them as they try to catch the lightning.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Local legends say that if a Pikaian defeats a thousand consecutive enemies with its Comet Punch and is struck by lightning on the last one, it will evolve into POKENAME. Scientists are still trying to prove whether this legend is true.
author: drack8786

entry: POKENAME has mastered its control over electricity. The electricity POKENAME generates between its tails can be sent out in disruptive currents.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME flies on its four wings through thunderstorms, gathering electricity from nearby lightning strikes. The flapping of its wings produces large amounts of static electricity.
author: mudkip0433

entry: POKENAME's senses easily surpass those of humans: powerful vision allows it to spot other Pokémon and objects of import, and powerful hearing allows it to detect those approaching from great distances. Only its sense of taste is comparable.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although cute, a wild POKENAME can be incredibly dangerous for Trainers. POKENAME can release large amounts of electricity at once if it becomes aggressive.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: If the tips of their tails touch anything metal, they discharge all of their electricity and become aggressive. To avoid this, some POKENAME wrap their long tails around their small bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon accumulates electricity in its body and tail, but it's so small it often needs to discharge. It secretly does so by recharging batteries that cross its path, and can never resist recharging a kid's night light.
author: lukanbeetle

entry: POKENAME use the broken remnants of egg shells to protect their bodies, trying to keep themselves safe from harm. They have poor control of their electrical powers and the shell they use often ends up charred and blackened by their shocks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are a popular companion of power line engineers, their ability to sense electrical fluctuations making them invaluable in finding faults in lines. They take great pride in helping fix up broken down infrastructure.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can rub its tail through its wool to generate static electricity. It normally does this as self-defense when it feels threatened.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: POKENAME enjoys flying through nearly any conditions, but it dislikes the extreme cold. It loves flying through the skies after a thunderstorm.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found outside power plants, ambling around the fields and playing with one another near the generator buildings. They are drawn to the electrical output and will migrate elsewhere if the power plant ever shuts down.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be found outside power plants, ambling around the fields and playing with one another near the generator buildings. They are drawn to the electrical output and will migrate elsewhere if the power plant ever shuts down.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It collects electricity by building up static when it wafts through the air. If it generates too much, it will discharge a powerful Thunder, even in the middle of a cloudless day.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME enjoys flying through nearly any conditions, but dislikes extreme cold. It especially loves flying through the skies after a thunderstorm.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME enjoys flying through nearly any conditions, but dislikes extreme cold. It especially loves flying through the skies after a thunderstorm.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will gnaw through wires relentlessly, absorbing the energy inside. They keep their tails raised in the air, constantly scanning their surroundings.  This makes them extremely hard to catch, often infesting homes for years.
author: santon5512

entry: All of its potent electrical power is centered in the large tip of its tail. POKENAME makes a show of juggling balls of condensed lightning with its tail before lobbing the projectile at its foes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their tails to ground them as they discharge excess electricity from their cheek pouches. They often hop about in puddles of water to keep themselves moisturized.
author: infinex21

entry: It plants its tail into the base of wilting plants and shocks them back to life. The plants it revives this way often take on a zigzag pattern.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME bounces up and down, which generates electricity that it stores. It likes to jump into cold water and discharge this electricity, giving anything swimming nearby a nasty shock.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: This Pokémon's electrified vines are employed in construction to lift and manipulate metal beams. Its calming hum helps workers stay focused in high-stress environments.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Its long whiskers quiver near large sources of electricity, which it eagerly consumes. When fully charged, its tail glows as brightly as a street lamp.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its tail attracts strange signals from the environment, causing it to spark violently when overloaded. These sparks leave marks that look like fragments of a forgotten writing.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME wander around during lightning storms, pleasantly greeting each other even as they're struck by lightning. While the body of the struck POKENAME doesn't seem to react in the slightest, its tail energetically sways back and forth every time.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME live deep underground where they store geothermal power in their bodies. They have been seen hunting Gyarados by tunneling under the seafloor and breaching up into the water, attacking from below to zap their prey.
author: hedaunis

entry: POKENAME blasts thousands of volts of electricity to take down any foe that tries to take over its territory. When it can't handle the threat by itself, it flies up high and bursts electricity like a firework to signal others to help fight.
author: soup1900

entry: In battle, POKENAME charges into the enemy while cloaking itself with electricity. It is also capable of firing powerful surges from its pincers.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME keeps its lengthy tail almost completely coiled within its shell. This lets it take attackers from behind by surprise when it springs out and swings like a massive whip in their direction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its tail like a board to slide swiftly down snowy slopes. When hunting, it attacks its prey by electrifying its razor-sharp claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's shell has a magnetic field, though the range does not extend far. Some sightings of POKENAME have noted coins and nails sticking to their shells.
author: bigoljax

entry: Showing no regard for their unfused counterparts, POKENAME lives mainly on a diet of Pikachu. POKENAME are one of the few Flying types to prey on them, able to withstand their electric shocks. Their call sends all small Pokémon running for cover.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is incredibly energetic and excitable. It will often weave around Trainers feet while on walks, with electricity sparking off its tail.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME are fast swimming Pokémon that use electrical pulses to stun other Pokémon in the water. Their long, trailing tail acts to signify their success to other POKENAME, with longer tails indicating a more desirable partner.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They have a very festive nature that they take very seriously. POKENAME give out gifts to other Pokémon, but will shock anyone being naughty.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME is a friendly, gentle soul that travels with and safeguards humans and Pokémon alike. It can generate electricity in great amounts to defend them, as well as small controlled amounts to gently soothe those who hold onto it while swimming.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME store electricity throughout the length of their bodies and cause the fur of nearby Pokémon to stand on edge. They release this built-up electricity whenever they bite down with their fangs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rise from the deep ocean during thunderstorms, attracted by the lightning. As the storm rages, they prey on Water-type Pokémon who have been disoriented by the violent waves. They swim at burst speeds of over 35 miles per hour.
author: chibitales

entry: Should POKENAME shock a computer, the system will shut down instantly. Oddly, when booted back up, it will perform twice as fast as before.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often show up with paint stuck to their ochre bodies and feature dynamic art that look flashy and pop out to art audiences. The art they produce often inspire advertising companies to mimic their style to give their message an extra boost.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME discharges large amounts of electricity through its fangs, paralyzing its prey almost instantly. However, it is generally friendly outside of battle and only hunts small Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a nurturing parent, often caring for young Pokémon of many species. When too much electricity builds up in its body, it becomes aggressive and hides away to safely discharge the excess.
author: jonclyd

entry: A Yellow Scarf allows POKENAME to stand out against the crowd as their tough and gritty personalities surface. They are also known to hold Thunder Stones with them to bring out their boldness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a very rare, docile creature. Legends say that it once guarded both sky and sea and caused major storms to those who threatened the ecosystem. POKENAME is almost never seen in the wild, so catching one is seen as good luck.
author: zoro_the_zoura

entry: Each one of POKENAME's thunderous quakes lets loose extremely powerful thunderbolts that cause gigantic wildfires and massive landslides. Each time its armored body is hit, electricity builds up inside of it, prolonging these rampages.
author: soup1900

entry: Each one of POKENAME's thunderous quakes lets loose extremely powerful thunderbolts that cause gigantic wildfires and massive landslides. Each time its armored body is hit, electricity builds up inside of it, prolonging these rampages.
author: soup1900

entry: Through the yellow tips of their tails, POKENAME can absorb and discharge electricity, up to about as much electricity as it takes to power Goldenrod City. They are closely monitored because they may go berserk if they store too much electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hunts down wild Magikarp by shocking them with its lightning-shaped tail. The amount of electricity released by its tail is enough to perfectly cook food, making POKENAME useful for providing meals.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: This playful Pokémon weaves through shadows, crackling with electric energy and mischief. With a flick of its tail, it conjures ghostly illusions to confuse opponents, striking with surprising speed and agility.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME carries around the Thunder Stone that evolved it as a memento. It is often seen cradling this item as if it were its own child.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME uses its oversized tail to launch powerful lightning bolts into the sky that obliterate objects they strike down upon. As electricity courses through its body, its horns discharge instantaneously, giving foes no time to react to its attacks.
author: soup1900

entry: Researchers theorize this form may be one Raichu took naturally in a distant past of Kanto history. It has yet to be determined why Raichu can no longer naturally take this form.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME refuses to obey its Trainer's commands until it has satisfied its hunger. Right after eating a Berry, its electric attacks become much more powerful.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are employed as workers for breakfast restaurants because they love pancakes so much. Customers are advised to check for POKENAME's paralyzing saliva on their meals before eating.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Only the most courageous evolve into POKENAME, at least in the wild. It allows other members of its pack to hunt even during intense storms: any lightning bolts are drawn to its horn and are absorbed painlessly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Having journeyed here from Alola on cargo ships, POKENAME is an invasive species that is known to electrocute attackers or predators. Other than that, it's mostly passive.
author: aberry8286

entry: POKENAME charges itself with electricity on the surface, then leaps into the air and crashes into the ground, tail first, to dig itself in.
author: chorb33

entry: This Pokémon's default flying speed is so incredibly fast that an observer can only make out a brief blur. In battle, it flies circles around its foes, easily darting around to repeatedly target any weak points it can find with lightning attacks.
author: fireblade141

entry: This Pokémon has mastered controlling its electricity. The combination of electricity and fire makes it very warm to hold.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME uses the positioning of its tail as a counterbalance when walking to avoid toppling over.  POKENAME will excitedly cheer on its friends, occasionally spitting fire when it gets overexcited.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When POKENAME energizes its spikes and tail, curls up and shoots off, it can even shatter entire houses and rock formations when it hits them.
author: chorb33

entry: This Pokémon can lash out with electricity-powered kicks that can stun five foes at once. It then finishes off with a mighty Flamethrower.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The expanding and contracting of POKENAME's muscles help it generate electrical energy to store for future use. Due to this Pokémon's constant training, its body is constantly charged and creates powerful shocks upon contact, in or out of battle.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME unleash powerful kicks charged with enough electricity to power an entire town. Their movements are quite agile, allowing them to use various physical strikes in combination while still avoiding plenty counterattacks.
author: infinex21

entry: The black feathers atop POKENAME's head act as a natural visor against bright sunlight. By levitating on an electromagnetic field and using its tail like a surfboard, it can rush past opponents while unleashing powerful kicks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Raichu's tail has become a whip that POKENAME now utilizes as a weapon. With the strike of its whip, it makes a booming crackle reminiscent of thunder and lightning.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: The combination of psychic energy and electricity resulted in a Raichu-like manifestation that acts as a guardian for POKENAME. In battle, they fight with a profound sense of teamwork and choreography.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME concentrates electricity into its blade-like elbows, refining its strikes while ensuring no stray bolts harm its allies. Should this power become unstable, its chivalrous nature gives way to fierce aggression.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME concentrates electricity into its blade-like elbows, refining its strikes while ensuring no stray bolts harm its allies. Should this power become unstable, its chivalrous nature gives way to fierce aggression.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME's body resembles a Thunder Stone, and even emits a faint energy similar to the stone. There are unfounded rumors that staring into the hole in its back will forcibly reverse the evolution of Pokémon that evolve through Thunder Stones.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME energizes its spikes and tail, curls up and shoots off, it can even shatter entire houses and rock formations when it hits them.
author: chorb33

entry: When POKENAME energizes its spikes and tail, curls up and shoots off, it can even shatter entire houses and rock formations when it hits them.
author: chorb33

entry: When POKENAME energizes its spikes and tail, curls up and shoots off, it can even shatter entire houses and rock formations when it hits them.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME channel their electrical powers through their teeth, giving their bites a painful shock. They use this ability to help them chew down trees, biting into the trunk and shocking the sap to make it explode, toppling the tree quickly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME channel their electrical powers through their teeth, giving their bites a painful shock. They use this ability to help them chew down trees, biting into the trunk and shocking the sap to make it explode, toppling the tree quickly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME retains Lucario's ability to read auras. If it senses bad intentions from a person, it will not hesitate to Thunder Punch them in the face.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: The flower on its back hums with stored electricity, often used to jump-start dead generators in rural areas. Its well-meaning nature is offset by its clumsiness, as it frequently zaps itself while trying to assist.
author: jaminmcready

entry: A folktale describes trainers spotting thunder stones that disappear at a glance. These stories have been discovered to be about POKENAME playing pranks on wild Pikachu that were desperate to evolve.
author: poppyisconfused

entry: POKENAME walk together in groups, following their leader in single file. When the group feel threatened, they will huddle together and pool their electric powers, launching a single gigantic thunderbolt as a team.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME squabble with one another for prime nesting locations, regularly stealing stones and sticks from each other to build better nests. When disputes turn aggressive, they will flap their wings and fire shocks at one another.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME strut around constantly displaying their electrical powers as a way to display their superiority to others. The constant show of power is draining and they have to periodically hide themselves away to recharge.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Electricity builds in POKENAME's nose, eventually forming a mustache of unstable static. Once it can be safely discharged, POKENAME sneezes as violently as a lightning strike, creating booming thunder.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME's blade vibrates and it panics at the slightest sound. It prefers solitude, but when cornered, its vibrations enhance its damage.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: When POKENAME rubs its two blades together, it releases thousands of volts of electricity in the form of electric sparks. As it builds energy, its attack patterns grow faster and more aggressive until it disregards defense entirely.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME punishes those who defy its orders by scorching them with its electric blade. It can discharge all of its built-up electricity through its shield to counterattack any retaliators who try to fight back.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have a strategic mind and battle in a very methodical manner. This works as a double-edged sword as their preparedness can let them take down those less prepared, but they are inflexible and can be vulnerable to chaotic conditions.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Over time, a POKENAME typically amasses itself a small following of Electric-type Pokémon. It trains them thoroughly, often providing its own electricity to boost their strengths when they falter in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a tail that resembles the head of a glaive and can cut through thin layers of steel. When it needs an extra boost, it pumps its tail full of electricity to give it an edge in combat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A POKENAME prehensile tail will ensure that its gears never stop spinning. So long as its gears continue to spin, the lightning-bolt styled parts of its body will glow with electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME mimics the cries of lost children to lure concerned travelers. Once they're close, it delivers a powerful electric shock and drags them away.
author: .izik

entry: It communicates with other POKENAME by connecting their lighting-shaped ribbons and sending shocks between them.
author: melodydelune

entry: A result of two different evolution stones, POKENAME are spotted only on rare occasions. It burrows its caves into mountains, filling it with surges of electrical energy. This also provides shelter for smaller electric and ground Pokémon.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME is capable of running 3 million volts through its veins, which is 30 times stronger than a Raichu's body can emit. Scientists believe this is due to Groudon's ability of maintaining immense power.
author: over9001

entry: Parts of POKENAME are covered in what appear to be Thunder Stones. These help amplify its ability to create powerful thunderstorms.
author: partypooperrex

entry: Because they consume large amounts of electricity, even a small flock of POKENAME can trigger citywide blackouts. It latches onto the side of structures with its barbed appendages, puncturing until it finds an energy source to drain.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Their cheek pouches store static electricity that builds up in their fluffy fur. Too much of it can make them clingy and needy.
author: faelocke

entry: POKENAME likes to dance gracefully in grassy fields. When multiple POKENAME dance together, their tails glow brightly with electricity.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Despite their cute appearance, Trainers are advised against creating POKENAME as their thunderous buzz of a cry can cause hearing damage.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME will lie around in abandoned places like old schools or houses waiting for someone to come by and pick them up. They wait until they have been carried for a while and then give a vicious shock to the person that found them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its body is composed of highly-charged plasma, which allows it to suspend a piece of Thunder Stone within the ring-like part of its form. This Thunder Stone piece serves to further amplify its electrical energy.
author: infinex21

entry: During a full moon, POKENAME's electrical powers intensify dramatically. It can summon lightning strikes strong enough to level a house.
author: .izik

entry: Because of its appearance, POKENAME is often mistaken for a grounded nimbus cloud. Travelers have been known to be shocked by it.
author: supersonicloki

entry: POKENAME swims through the desert sand while hunting. Once it finds its prey, it discharges 100,000 volts, causing most Pokémon to faint instantly.
author: bunkachunka

entry: Using its tail, POKENAME can quickly draw up webs made of lightning anywhere it pleases. These webs dissipate after zapping unsuspecting bugs, which become charred meals for POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's modified tails lets it sense electrical patterns. They also sense what they touch, discharge extra electricity, and grab and hold things.
author: totodile.

entry: A house inhabited by multiple POKENAME will frequently suffer from power outages due to their heavy consumption of electricity. If it stores too much, the lightbulbs on its arms will shatter, causing uncontrollable fires.
author: thatdanguy23

entry: POKENAME's claws and tusks are made of lightning, only visible once it readies itself for combat. The more it surges its massive electrical energy, the longer and sharper its tusks and claws grow.
author: sk372

entry: Ancient tomes describe POKENAME standing in villages during storms. It would absorb lightning bolts to shield the settlement from destruction.
author: .izik

entry: When it dives at prey, its tail stiffens and straightens out. Spectators lucky enough to view this phenomenon describe it as a living thunderbolt.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Inside the head of its disguise is a powerful electric bulb. If the bulb is exposed, it will shock anyone nearby until covered again.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME is attracted to large sources of electricity, especially power plants, where it feeds on the energy and causes blackouts. As it absorbs energy, its body heats to extreme temperatures and it accelerates to speeds humans struggle to see.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME store electricity in their luxuriously soft tails. After they unleash the potent power from one of their tails, the tail puffs up from the static electricity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Feisty by nature, POKENAME is always eager to prove itself to others in combat and impress them with its prowess. With enough effort, it can flare an electrical aura all around its body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fur is constantly brimming with electrical energy, powering their incredibly active and aggressive lifestyle. When POKENAME run, you can see a trail of lightning flow behind them.
author: dualblades1147

entry: Carrying through life with a playful personality, you may find a POKENAME goofing around with lampposts and power lines.
author: supersonicloki

entry: POKENAME do not tolerate interruptions during their public performances and put great effort into ensuring their symphonies are awe-inspiring. Hecklers are shocked and ushered out without mercy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers dry, arid environments. This helps it direct its electrical attacks without its power becoming absorbed by the water molecules in the air.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME hides among inanimate balloons and uses its cute appearance to be bought by a family. Once it is brought to their home, it will begin to feed on the power of all their electronic devices until it is discovered as the culprit.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is able to store over 10,000 volts of electricity in its body, making it prone to static electricity. It also loves to hug kind Trainers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME use their conductive gel to communicate with one another, sending complex electrical impulses that are amplified by their bodies. Pokémon Researchers are studying this communication method and attempting to apply it to engineering.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses its tail as a lightning rod to absorb electricity. It then flings itself at opponents to violently electrocute them.
author: gamertag1001.

entry: Flocks communicate with each other through a combination of chirps and electrical sparks from their tails. If they get agitated, POKENAME will not hesitate to shock the source of their anger.
author: chibitales

entry: It will grab any prey it lays eyes on. Once captured, POKENAME sends a small electric current through its talons to keep its meal from moving.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME is possessive of the building it has designated as its feeding ground, aggressively chasing away other energy-consuming Pokémon. Some workspaces will leave burner devices out as treats to placate the inadvertent POKENAME guardian.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's sharp fangs are charged with electricity, shocking its prey until they become paralyzed. Despite its electrical power, POKENAME is very friendly and loves to playfully nuzzle its Trainer.
author: mistymagius

entry: Wild POKENAME protect their Thunder Stones. If someone tries to steal them, they go berserk. They hit wild Pikachu with the Stones to force evolution.
author: donutsbg

entry: POKENAME generates static electricity by rolling. When it rolls downhill, the sound of thunder echoes behind it.
author: shreks_stepfather

entry: Its two tails act as the perfect lightning rods during a thunderstorm. This way, it can safely carry up to 3 people at an incredible speed, until finding proper shelter.
author: epping_forest

entry: In a matter of seconds, POKENAME can coat its sharp teeth with electric sparks, which it uses to paralyze its prey. Its aggressive temperament seems to calm down during thunderstorms, as if the rumble of thunder soothes it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME freeze water around them by releasing a flurry of ice crystals. Once the water has been frozen, they unleash powerful bolts of lightning into the ice to create beautiful displays of light.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shake their pom-poms to literally energize their teammates, collecting static electricity along the fluff. As more and more energy builds, a POKENAME's motivation can rumble as loud as roaring thunder.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: One should not get deceived by the fact that it doesn't smell bad. Its body releases high amounts of mercury, lead, and battery sulfate, highly toxic to the environment.
author: epping_forest

entry: The bulbs on POKENAME's head store the electrical energy it uses for its attacks. It secretes a poison that closely resembles battery acid.
author: knilk

entry: POKENAME's crystalline body is made of the same mineral as a Thunder Stone. The Raichu encased inside appears to be asleep, but retains full control of the fusion's electrical abilities.
author: hophoppip

entry: When POKENAME has too much stored electricity, it will scatter electrically charged pollen. This pollen can be used to power large machinery.
author: darkweavile428

entry: With their soft, plush bodies, POKENAME are popular Pokémon with young Trainers. They enjoy being carried around and being squeezed, the yellow patches on their cheeks giving small sparks of joy when they're played with.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME build static as they move, their fur and fluffy bodies generating electrical potential whilst they fight. They deliver this electrical energy as punches, shocking their foes with powerful strikes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will only breach the surface during thunderstorms to absorb lightning strikes. It wraps its opponent with its long chain before blasting them with 1,000,000 volts of electricity.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lets loose small electric pulses from its tail to attract prey. Once they are close, it attacks with its sharp venomous spikes, pinning them to the seafloor for an easy catch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generate electricity through the friction of their feathers, especially when gliding through the air. Though they can fight with electrical bolts, they prefer to fight up close. They have been known to grapple foes and shock them.
author: infinex21

entry: The parasitic fungi growing within the body of POKENAME force the Pokémon to constantly feed so that they have enough energy for themselves and their parasites. The fungi discharge excess energy as electricity, using the shocks to protect their host.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The fur around its neck appears to contain little pieces of thunder stones. This Pokémon is naturally very playful, but its fur is usually highly electrically charged, so it is easy to get shocked accidentally.
author: fireblade141

entry: When too full of electricity, POKENAME sings songs in a quick, high-pitched voice to passionately let its energy out. If someone insults it during its singing, it screams out lightning bolts to paralyze them and forcefully change their feelings.
author: soup1900

entry: When too full of electricity, POKENAME sings songs in a fast, high-pitched voice to passionately let its energy out. People who annoy it during its singing are met with screams of lightning bolts that force them to change their attitudes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses its long tail as a balance to stand on top of and do fantastic tricks and showy moves while keeping its voltage grounded. It gathers electricity with its tail right before big performances so it has enough energy for its sparking shows.
author: soup1900

entry: After discharging electricity, the mushroom noticeably shrinks and shrivels. POKENAME must be careful to let itself recharge, lest its protective cap dry out completely and leave it helpless.
author: sk372

entry: The heart-shaped Thunder Stone on its head is highly coveted. However, it fiercely attacks anyone who attempts to take it, no matter how strong they are.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It can regrow the Thunder Stones on its body indefinitely, making it highly sought after by Electric-type Trainers. However, it only gives them to those who can defeat it in a fierce duel.
author: h0bojoe

entry: A simple shake of its scales can release up to 100,000 volts of electricity. The Thunder Stones growing from its body are famed as some of the purest ever discovered.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Special organs within POKENAME's largest hands store electrical charges. When forced into close-quarters combat, it dispels the stored energy on contact to create powerful shockwave punches that blow its foes away.
author: sk372

entry: It absorbs sunlight with its petals to recharge energy. It often dances in the breeze, releasing gentle sparks that mesmerize onlookers.
author: dammaskk

entry: POKENAME have shards of Thunder Stones embedded in their body and cause their rocky bodies to glow a citrine yellow. Whenever they are full of electricity, they discharge it in small bursts while chasing their tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The mushroom growing on the backs of POKENAME require a lot of electrical energy to grow. This energy requirement pushes POKENAME to dig out electrical cables, biting into them to feed on the power running through them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME develop a static charge by rubbing against another Electric-type Pokémon. This causes their hair to stand on end until they discharge the electricity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have the ability to predict weather patterns with remarkable detail. When groups of POKENAME gather at high altitudes, a devastating storm is always sure to appear.
author: turron_turron

entry: Its scales contain large amounts of chemical energy, and when struck by an attack, they discharge all of their electricity at once. Ancient people dried POKENAME's scales and used them in energizing elixirs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has grown to like the attention its fur gets. It understands people's love for the fluff, and is much less likely to shock those who try to touch it.
author: chaotic_aspergers

entry: POKENAME raids power plants to feed on the energy in generators. When full of electricity, its cheeks are covered in a fire so hot it does not go out even in the rain.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lashes its tail from beneath the ground to discharge electricity. It retracts the tail into the dirt to recharge between attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dashes fast enough to run across water. As it runs, it builds up massive amounts of electricity, which it discharges violently upon stopping.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Sparks left behind in POKENAME's wake can cause wildfires if left unchecked. Theoretically, it could dash around the world in a single day if it didn't have to stop and discharge itself every so often.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME tunnels toward power plants to chew through buried wires. It feeds directly on electricity, storing the energy within its body.
author: .izik

entry: The happier and healthier this Pokémon is, the more puffy and light its fur will appear! When sad or ill, the static charge held in its neck fur will bleed out, deflating the fur and making it lax.
author: chiari_queen

entry: POKENAME generates a gallon of venom a day. On days it doesn't eat, it has to spit out its excess venom.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME generate electricity in their cheeks. When they generate too much electricity, they get a headache that can only be relieved by a sudden discharge.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its long yellow tail to catch lightning bolts from the sky, protecting nearby trees and homes. Thanks to its psychic powers, it can move by levitating gracefully through the air.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fights with a very chaotic style; its quick, erratic movements often cause opponents to lower their guard. Its favorite technique is Thunder Punch, with which it usually finishes duels against its rivals.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If it cannot discharge the electrical energy stored in its body, it flies into a furious rage and becomes uncontrollable. POKENAME has a very violent fighting style, overpowering opponents through sheer brute force.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME shoots blazing flames and potent lightning from its mouth, which makes quick work of anything standing in its way. Its proud and defiant personality makes it difficult to catch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME channels its psychic and electrical powers through the thunderstone it clutches. It mixes these energies in battle, throwing its opponents around with telekinesis, followed by shocking them with powerful thunderbolts.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME controls large amounts of electricity with its might. Delivering powerful thunderbolts can mess with its opponent's neurons. It can be seen meditating on tall mountains when thunderstorms roll in.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rubs its fists together to charge them with electricity before striking with devastating, spark-filled punches. Energetic and tireless, it can run for hours without getting exhausted.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME are about to strike with a Thunder Punch, their cheeks sparkle. Even with this knowledge, many fighters still lose matches against the powerful POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a bright clementine-colored head that stores electricity. They help electricians safely run wires through houses by sprouting roots that snake through small spaces.
author: quackquackattack

entry: People often worry that the sheer power of its electric attacks is too much for POKENAME's shell to handle. Luckily, its shell is more than capable of withstanding such power.
author: killerrene64

entry: Sparks from the stones on POKENAME's body are dangerously strong. Even light contact can result in sudden paralysis to unprotected skin.
author: .izik

entry: Bearing a resemblance to Golem's Alolan counterpart, POKENAME is less aggressive by comparison, but contains far greater stores of electricity. An angered POKENAME could carve chunks out of a mountain with its lightning bolts.
author: sk372

entry: Its mane and tail are made of a hot plasma that on contact, will cause nasty burns all over the victim's body. Its internal electricity allows for POKENAME to run up to 80 mph.
author: mistymagius

entry: Lightning trails behind POKENAME when it gallops at full speed, taking off with a sound akin to a thunderbolt when it runs. During heavy rain and thunderstorms, it prances happily among the thunder and lightning.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shell is not just used for protection, but also for storing large masses of electricity that can be discharged later through its tail.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: POKENAME produce a powerful electrical field that allows them to float along the planet's magnetic lines. They move slowly and will always align their magnets along the polarity of the field, sometimes getting caught near powerful generators.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is commonly found in power plants, using its magnets to siphon off the electricity. In combat, it fires powerful blasts of electrical energy from all of its magnets at once.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME appear on ponds and rivers during thunderstorms. If offered food by humans, they prefer it to be burnt.
author: snookerron

entry: POKENAME use their prehensile tails to knock down hanging fruits and split them in half for their two heads to share. They turn aggressive if they store too much electricity, and their two heads will turn on each other.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME builds up internal stores of electricity as it races across the land. When it finally stops, it releases the stored-up energy in a powerful burst, creating vicious electric storms all around it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME blasts torrents of electrified water towards opponents in a Pokémon battle, soaking and paralyzing them in the process. When needed, it withdraws into its sturdy shell to repel attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME release powerful bursts of electricity that target parts of the brain that regulate sleep. Flying-type Pokémon are particularly susceptible to fall asleep after a powerful shock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By charging its pendulum with static, it can use it as a makeshift compass to find the closest source of electricity, which it feeds on.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME use the bolt on their arm as a lightning rod, storing the electricity within themselves once struck. They will roam beaches for food, grabbing prey with their large claws before delivering a devastating surge of lightning.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME eat copious amounts of food on a daily basis. While their natural diet consists of leaves and berries, domesticated POKENAME love to eat pies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These Pokémon throw explosive fits if they grow too hungry. They love to eat batteries and Thunder Stones, both of which help amplify their electrical currents.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME fly into explosive fits of rage if they are awakened from their slumbers, and will only calm down after stuffing themselves with food. Some people, unfortunately, engage in "POKENAME Tipping" which involves sending a POKENAME rolling.
author: infinex21

entry: Traveling in a clutch of around six, POKENAME only separate as a group in order to forage food. Once they've found it, they group back together, refusing to eat until the entire group is assembled.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are almost always chewing on a bone, which they use as a club to defend themselves. Their saliva is incredibly sticky, allowing food and debris to collect on these bones, which they later eat in one gulp.
author: infinex21

entry: Eating rotted matter increases the potency of the poison gas that POKENAME emits. Because of this, POKENAME tries to wait until its food rots, but it often can't control itself and ends up eating the food while it's still fresh.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME eat food left before them while their bodies develop. They prefer pies above all else, so many empathetic people leave behind pies for them to snack on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME subsists off of berries that fall from trees. Unfortunately, its heads have different tastes, and will often move in conflicting directions.
author: hortensia_xxiii

entry: POKENAME charge and ram trees to knock free fruits and berries to gorge upon, but they may also charge toward the source of a delicious scent. When they start running, they struggle to stop.
author: infinex21

entry: Its horn has its own sense of 'smell'. POKENAME uses this horn like a dowsing rod to track down food, and unhinges its jaw to gulp the meal down.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME store berries in the pouch in front of their stomach. They are particularly fond of Chilan Berries because the berry helps them shake off hordes of Rattata that try to steal from their pouch.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Recently evolved POKENAME are voracious creatures that eat any and all food in the nearby vicinity. They leave behind few crumbs when they are finished eating.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is always cheerful and gets joy out of making people and Pokémon happy. POKENAME are made of a slimy substance.
author: kingnekogamingvt

entry: POKENAME have a strange quality; contact with their goop-like body leaves the person or Pokémon joyful and laughing, as if being tickled. Interactions with POKENAME show that they prefer eating sweets instead of berries.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Their appetite is enormous, as their bodies require a diet twice their body weight to maintain a healthy size. Cheaply made doughnuts help fill them up with calories.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME was initially thought to be cannibalistic in early scientific reports, until further research revealed that it simply devours its own shed skin immediately after molting.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known to eat as many as 17 distinct meals a day, with different food preferences for each one. The wrong food at the wrong time can lead to a tantrum.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Ancient civilizations revered POKENAME and would make yearly offerings of food to the Pokémon. If POKENAME rejected the tribute, it was feared that a great famine would ensue.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are incredibly greedy, attempting to steal berries from other Pokémon's nests. However, they are too lazy to build a big enough nest to store all these berries, so they end up dropping out of the nest.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME strings together chains of berries so that it always has a snack while flying around. POKENAME in the wild sometimes get into tug-of-war matches over these food-strings.
author: sk372

entry: Interestingly, POKENAME's favorite snack is the webbing of other arachnid Pokémon. Left unchecked, it could remove the webs of an entire colony of Ariados in an hour, and still feel peckish.
author: sk372

entry: It spits sticky silk webbing to procure and secure food for itself, favoring fruits and berries above all else. If anything tries to steal its food, it will use its fangs to inject a soporific venom and knock them out.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME fly rapidly through forests, swallowing whole any fruits or berries they can find. Many other Pokémon hunt POKENAME, even if just to keep POKENAME from stealing their food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME flies between Occa Berry trees, gathering berries to eat later. When full, its belly jiggles as it flies, making it a comical and endearing sight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are still learning to create sparks with their hands. Feeding them a Custap Berry helps them charge up lots of electricity that they release from their feet, sending them flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gather under the night sky to snack while watching the moon and stars. Their diet ranges from berries to evolution stones, so they can be quite a nuisance to Trainers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME gather under the night sky to snack while watching the moon and stars. Their diet ranges from berries to evolution stones, so they can be quite a nuisance to Trainers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Their fluffy wool is so rife with static electricity that debris is oft caught within. When happy, such as when gorging themselves with food, their tail orbs faintly glow.
author: infinex21

entry: Their absentminded flying causes them to catch onto kites as they glide past. They are known to rest atop cliffs and ask for help when this happens, unable to untangle themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often resort to eating Durin Berries that people throw away. They scurry between garbage cans to find whatever they can eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Every day, they will eat their body weight in berries, picking and examining each fruit they come across, discarding the unripe ones. Wild POKENAME are considered pests within berry orchards, as troops can ruin a farmer's harvest for the whole year.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME lobs globs of mud at berries in Salac Berry Trees, gathering them up and coating them in mud before eating. This unique method of collecting and preparing its food helps it enjoy the berries in a special way.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is soft and gentle, and takes naps to give itself time to digest food. Despite its cuddly appearance, its body is covered in a protective slime that makes hugging it difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swoops in and pilfers trinkets from passersby. It has no use for what it steals, but will only return it to those who give chase if they present it with food to trade back what it stole.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME keep an assortment of fruits and berries with them at all times. Whenever they inevitably get hurt by another Pokémon trying to defend their horde of food, they bite down on a Salac Berry and flee as fast as they can.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its long fur tends to pick up and track twigs, fruits, and other vegetation as it wanders through forests and fields. It sleeps often due to having to share much of its nutrients with the bulb atop its back.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME move very slow, eating whatever scraps or fallen vegetation they come across. If threatened, they shake strongly to scatter many soporific spores from their flowers.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its rock-hard fangs to fell Wacan Berry trees before gorging on the fruit. It will use Scary Face if anyone gets close while it eats, protecting its bounty.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats up to Cheri Berry trees to feast on fruit. It can drain ten trees in a day before vanishing into the night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hates sleeping, so it carries a Poké Flute in each pincer, playing them whenever it gets sleepy. It keeps a hoard of chestnuts around its nest, eating them as night falls.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME flies between Coba Berry branches, eating as many berries as it can before others of its kind find the tree. Its quick consumption helps it avoid competition from its flock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can greatly expand at rapid speeds by swallowing large quantities of water, which causes their venomous quills to stand on end. They catch small prey with their large mouths as they swim and swallow them whole.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME eat berries infrequently, only doing so to create more of their main source of energy, juice. Despite all urges to do so, POKENAME have to refrain from drinking all of the juice they make, as it could lead to death.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME has a habit of sneaking into towns and raiding candy shops, storing its loot inside its oversized beak. Trainers often find mysterious candy wrappers in its nest as evidence of its mischief.
author: rakunk

entry: They use their snouts to root for vegetables, though sometimes come across buried food. They are indifferent about what they eat, so long as their would-be food is not poisonous.
author: infinex21

entry: It uses its tough tusks to dig for food and water, though it sometimes taps trees for sap. It can swallow food whole and spend weeks digesting it, helping it survive harsh winters better than some.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's hunger and greed can lead it to snatching food from others before curling into a ball and rolling away. The high speed and momentum often lead to it getting sick once it finally stops.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's psychic powers amplify after eating a Payapa Berry. Many nutritionists claim the berry eases its mind, allowing it to think clearer and focus its abilities more effectively.
author: .izik

entry: The paint on POKENAME's tail primarily consists of the pulped remains of its berry meals, so its drawings always retain a faintly sweet smell after being painted. Fittingly, most of its artwork includes food in some form.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its superior leg strength to jump to the top of Charti Berry trees. While it prefers the berries on the topmost branches, it eventually eats all of them as it descends back to the ground.
author: .izik

entry: Though their bodies have remarkable constrictive power, they swallow food whole and thus their bodies are too stuff to utilize it well. They favor large fruits and vegetables, though have been witnessed devouring Pokémon eggs as well.
author: infinex21

entry: Though their bodies have remarkable constrictive power, they swallow food whole and thus their bodies are too stuff to utilize it well. They favor large fruits and vegetables, though have been witnessed devouring Pokémon eggs as well.
author: infinex21

entry: It is a rare Pokémon who holds a small but ever-present flame in its gut. It has surprising intelligence and adores food; it can be spotted spitting up embers to roast all kinds of things before eating them, even using simple tools to assist it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses lightning strikes to knock over trees, causing berries like Oran and Pecha to fall. These are its favorite foods, and it devours them eagerly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can use their own tails to bounce and reach hanging fruits and berries. They can eat most things in one bite with minimal chewing.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite their laidback attitude and willingness to listen to instructions, POKENAME are not advised as good companions for first time Trainers. They have an insatiable appetite and will quickly eat through the savings of the unprepared.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The nutrients absorbed from eating so many berries allows POKENAME to grow its own on some of its vines. These also get feasted upon when ripe, and have been noted to be rather juicier than the average berry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have large tusks made of solid ice, which help to clear avalanches and to break down trees. They eat once a month in large swathes, spending the rest of the month digesting the food and resting often.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time lazily snacking on food around muddy locales. It often dips the meal it is about to eat in mud, to add texture and flavor.
author: sk372

entry: Living at the outskirts of human civilizations, POKENAME travels into towns and cities to find people to show its plodding, lumbering dances to. It's considered customary to gift it food as payment for the performance.
author: sk372

entry: It has a very strong body to help support the large flower upon its back. It will swallow entire bushes whole if they exude a sweet enough scent, even if they are merely flower bushes.
author: infinex21

entry: Both mouths are just as hungry as each other. The bigger one usually gets the scraps.
author: birchbot

entry: The more a POKENAME eats, the longer a nap it will take afterwards, taking its time digesting its meal. No impact, no matter how great, can wake it from a post-meal snooze.
author: banquoviaquo

entry: POKENAME have an abiding love for Sitrus Berries: so much so that after devouring them, they press the discarded peels to their crowns in order to continue enjoying the scent.
author: banquoviaquo

entry: POKENAME eats and eats, but it is never satisfied. Scientists believe there is something akin to a black hole in its stomach, for POKENAME never creates any kind of biological byproduct. Oddly, it doesn't appear to actually need to eat to survive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME only eats vegetables and prefers the crunchiest ones. However, it despises broccoli, often refusing to eat or even fleeing from it entirely.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The cheesy liquid secreting from POKENAME is a very well-seasoned condiment. It is used in many dishes, such as mac and cheese, pizza, and mozzarella sticks.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME ravages homes, farms, restaurants, and warehouses for their food. It absorbs food particles through its spoon and forked blade.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME move quite swiftly and have oft been seen snatching and fully devouring food from others within seconds. They will eat moldy or rotten food without issue, so sometimes people leave such foods out for these Pokémon to eat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its ribbons to nab at any bits of food it can find. If something else reaches for food it wants, it smacks them with its ribbons, which cause the struck victim to suddenly lose all traces of appetite.
author: sk372

entry: Farmers that live in POKENAME territory train Pokémon like Lucario to drive off these voracious food thieves under the moonlight. They will even break into homes to devour food if they smell it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: A somewhat meek Pokémon, POKENAME prefers wolfing down vegetables over battling. If its meal is disturbed, however, it will throw itself at the offender with the full force of its weight.
author: lampent12

entry: Many Pokémon have once tried biting the spores on POKENAME's tail, thinking that they were Oran Berries. Actual Oran Berries it has stashed on and around it are avoided due to the fear of them being spores.
author: soup1900

entry: To be able to fly at fast speeds, POKENAME need to consume their weight in food every day. Their favorite food is tree sap, lapping it up in reckless abandon and not even noticing when they get stuck to the tree because of the sticky sap.
author: _pixelar_

entry: During full moons, POKENAME gathers with others of its kind to feast on Nomel Berries. Entire orchards can be wiped out in one night, with even unripened berries being devoured.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits jets of water to knock Rabuta Berries off of trees. It then gathers them up and brings them back to its lodge, where it stores them for later consumption.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has the ability to see the aura of trees and picks a tree to eat from based on the color of the aura. Scientists are still trying to determine if its choice is based on the health of the tree or another unseen factor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are so indolent as to be almost immobile for 90 percent of their life. They lay around in clearings or near civilization, opening their mouth at passersby in the hopes of food being shared with them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a slow metabolism that causes most of what they eat to become blubber. Trainers are advised to abstain from overfeeding POKENAME because having too much blubber causes them discomfort.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's first instinct when discovering something new is to attempt to eat it. Its teeth, mouth and digestive tract are covered with a strong metallic layer, so eating rough, pointed or even toxic items won't bother it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a big mouth and an even bigger appetite. It will constantly chomp things with its mouth, even boulders. Its iron stomach can digest anything without issue.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME will eat until its stomach is nearly bursting. Afterwards, it will hide yet more food in its mouth for later. Sometimes it will forget the food is there until it is hungry again, which does not take long.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Prone to living in desert regions, POKENAME will plant itself into the sand, forming a cone-shaped pit. It will then try to inhale everything around it to fill its endless stomach.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It has little care in the world, eating all it wants and going about its way. The component that evolves first determines its path later in life.
author: miecreates

entry: Despite having a large appetite, POKENAME can't eat much in a single sitting. POKENAME will spend a large portion of their day floating in and out of the branches of berry plants, plucking one or two ripe berries at a time.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME hops around in a constant search for food. It stores food in the fluff around its waist, but will jostle it all loose from the persistent hopping.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME float around in a ball of liquid eating anything they come across. They rapidly digest food that enters into their bodies, liquifying food in a matter of seconds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats near Spelon Berry trees to pluck fruit to eat that it stores within its fluff. Sometimes, it gathers so many berries that it becomes too heavy to float, causing it to drop to the ground in search of its next snack.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon feed on the emotions of others and reflect those emotions with their own expressions. They are always carrying a berry, seemingly fond of Oran Berries the most, and never share it unless it may save a friend.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME enjoys roasted berries, spitting small fireballs at ones growing on trees to cook them before eating. Its tongue is covered with burn marks from not waiting for berries to properly cool down before trying to eat them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies from coconut tree to coconut tree to eat the coconuts. It will eat even the shell in seconds, without caring about the flavor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a glutton by nature. It enjoys stuffing its mouth with rocks and minerals. However, small Pokémon sometimes fall victim to its episodes.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME rolls through forested areas with its mouth open, eating just about any vegetation it rolls over. Its body can digest nearly any plant life, making it a versatile eater.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's poison becomes more potent after eating Chople Berries. Many scientists believe this is due to a chemical reaction in its stomach, creating new toxins that concentrate in its fangs.
author: .izik

entry: Their jaws are strong enough to crush the toughest nuts into a fine pulp. They tend to teethe on tree bark and rocks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are sloppy with their food and leave crumbs wherever they go. They do not have to eat since they can photosynthesize glucose, but they enjoy the tactile sensation of eating leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In addition to its beloved Berries, POKENAME has a powerful affinity for all kinds of seeds. The stashes of fruit and seeds it creates can grow so huge that the stash may start acting as fertilizer or even an ecosystem for small Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are messy eaters that enjoy eating leaves off other Pokémon. A single meal of leaves can last them the entire day, though they will continue to eat regularly because they enjoy the tactile sensation of food in their mouths.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses sound waves to knock Durin Berries from trees. Its single-mindedness while eating makes it unable to do anything else, focusing solely on devouring the berries.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies near Kasib Berry trees, searching for rotting fruit on the ground. It prefers the softer fruit, as it is easier to chew, making for a more enjoyable meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are deceptively voracious creatures that need to eat thrice their body weight to remain healthy. Their high metabolism comes from the goo they use to dissolve food, as it requires lots of nutrients to produce.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a difficult time separating friend from food, as their voracious appetite leads them to nibble on companions until they find adequate food to consume. Many Pokémon find their antics charming and love to give them berries to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses strong punches to knock over Tanga Berry trees, gorging itself on the berries that fall. Its enthusiasm for feasting leads to a messy but satisfying meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its strength to knock Magost Berries from the trees near its den. If someone gets too close while it eats, it uproots the nearest tree and hits them with it to fiercely defend its meal.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being able to survive with little food, POKENAME will consume anything it can find. If someone tries to take its food, it will bash them with its thorny arms.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's blanket-like body occasionally houses other Pokémon in exchange for berries or silk. It uses that silk to create its decorations.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME tends to avoid moving. If it needs to, it'll drag itself to a new location or catch a ride on another Pokémon.
author: ohok3441

entry: While typically hidden, POKENAME does have back legs. The blanket-like segment of its body is attached to its back like a cape.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME performs happy dances while it eats, breaking into masterful spins between bites. It appears to both chew and dance even while asleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a voracious appetite, as it needs to consume twice its body weight to remain healthy. Whenever it finishes eating, it releases a burst of psychic energy before falling asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The mushroom inhabiting POKENAME grows to appear as and taste like delicious food to help the spores spread to other organisms.
author: .realthree

entry: The mushroom inhabiting POKENAME grows to appear as and taste like delicious food to help the spores spread to other organisms.
author: .realthree

entry: The mushroom inhabiting POKENAME grows to appear as and taste like delicious food to help the spores spread to other organisms.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses Psybeam to knock Liechi Berries from trees. The more it eats, the more vibrant and beautiful the luster of its fur becomes, adding a shimmering effect to its appearance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a diet that mainly consists of twigs, as it is too slow to snatch berries before other Pokémon take them. If a Trainer gives it an Oran Berry or a Sitrus Berry, its elation causes it to roll around in excitement.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its long arms to catch Watmel Berries when they fall from trees. When it is full, it lets loose a strong pumpkin-like odor, signaling that it has had its fill.
author: .izik

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's head is close to a pie in consistency and regrows monthly. Many bakeries sell these along with their own freshly baked pies, as they are highly sought after for their unique texture.
author: .izik

entry: When happy, their tail flames flick about and when angry their flames rage uncontrollably. They are happiest when stuffing their faces with plenty of food, though seem to care little for what exactly they eat.
author: infinex21

entry: Using its tough claws, it can climb trees and easily crack open tough nuts. It prefers to roast any of its food with its own flames before eating, and gets agitated when it has to eat food raw.
author: infinex21

entry: Be careful when you're on a picnic, as a POKENAME might just pop out of the ground to steal your food. They have very quick reflexes, popping in and out of the ground within a single second.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flocks to coastal towns and is considered a pest as it greedily consumes any food left unattended. Its favorite food to snatch up is French fries.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hides collected berries inside hollow trees and cliff crevices. Some of these forgotten caches later grow into new berry patches.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME eat foods whole with minimal chewing and will even eat canned foods, including the cans. They spend most of their time sleeping, eating, and grooming their long fur.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME constantly gorges on snacks, as the act of eating nullifies its almost eternally aching head. The longest recorded time between it stopping eating and suffering a new headache is four minutes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swings from tree to tree with surprising agility. It will attack anyone that refuses to give it food.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's greed and hunger are equally intense, so one should give it plenty of space when it feeds. Staring for too long will be considered a challenge and incite it to violently defend its meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to fight, though they always have to rest for a long time after just one battle. They love to hoard food for themselves to gorge upon after they wake up, even if it means stealing that food from others.
author: infinex21

entry: Its massive appetite is due in part to the calories needed to maintain its strict training regimen. Eating and training are so intertwined it will often be seen with a full mouth even while exercising.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME consumes hundreds of berries to fuel its muscles and provide it with energy. Whenever it's not exercising, it dreams about its next meal.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is prone to intense workouts as well as intense gorging to keep up its strength and calorie intake. It's not uncommon to see two of its arms carrying food while it trains with the others, switching hands as appropriate.
author: sk372

entry: They always have food on hand, often holding two pieces of food in two of their hands while fighting with their other two hands. They only will fight with all four arms and hands when angered enough.
author: infinex21

entry: A sweet-smelling drool drips from POKENAME's mouth, attracting insects where it lands. The hungrier it is, the sweeter the drool becomes in order to draw more bugs quickly so it can eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is rarely seen at the surface, its voracious appetite leading it to eat its way through the ground in search of minerals. The tunnels left behind in its wake are often used by hopeful prospectors hunting for rare metals.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME eats anything, and the more variety in its diet, the tougher its rocky hide becomes. Because of its impervious nature, Pokémon Rangers train it to enter wildfires so it can move dirt and boulders to smother the fire.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's two favorite things are eating and running. However, because it eats so much on a regular basis, its speed and stamina are rather subpar, and it gets tired easily.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its incredible appetite, POKENAME often forgets to eat due to its slow-wittedness. It has been spotted chewing on its own tail when feeling too lazy to forage.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME eats moss off rocks in large quantities, especially during the winter months. It is most active in colder temperatures, preferring the chill to warmer conditions.
author: .izik

entry: Their semi-fluid bodies help to store food to eat later, though it has a bad habit of forgetting about such food and it ends up getting subsumed instead. They can often be found near sewers and garbage dumps, feeding on leftovers and waste.
author: infinex21

entry: Their semi-fluid bodies help store food for later, though they often forget about it and end up subsuming it instead. They are commonly found near sewers and garbage dumps, feeding on leftovers and waste.
author: infinex21

entry: The gases of their bodies are soporific to most others, though too much exposure can result in a coma. Their mouths are massive, allowing them to easily swallow foods whole without having to chew.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often lurk in darkness, waiting for an opportunity to snatch up food for themselves. They have been known to frighten and prank others just to steal their food.
author: infinex21

entry: Disturbingly, its mouth extends to half of its total body and it can open it from the horizontal half to swallow foods whole. It will follow others if it thinks they have food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the berries it gathers from the ground to motivate itself whenever it doesn't feel like doing something, sometimes even hypnotizing itself. If someone stares too long at the pendulum's motion, it immediately begins to feel hungry.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME absorbs water into the bulb on its back to stay hydrated in case it needs to walk on land to look for food. Its antennae are incredibly sensitive and can detect an approaching storm several days in advance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME floats in acidic waters so if a thunderstorm hits, it can easily absorb the electricity from them. They are also common around power plants.
author: mistymagius

entry: It picks up fish bones to use as headgear and a club for defense. On moonlit nights, it can sometimes be seen drawing the outline of a Mantine in the sand, then curling up and resting in the center.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bursts from the water with tremendous force. It uses its horn to smash unsuspecting prey like Wingull mid-flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flutters around beaches, preferring to feed from flowers that grow nearer to seawater. It likes to play with beach-goers by tickling them with its antennae.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loves helping rear young children, using charades as a way to turn learning things like numbers and shapes into a game. Upon a right answer, POKENAME claps and embraces the child to reward their efforts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can often be found on tropical islands, dancing playfully at the ocean's edge. Feliform Pokémon like Meowth have an odd fondness for this Pokémon's moves.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: Living in trees near coastal areas, POKENAME is a friendly and nonviolent little bug. Its horn is venomous, but it only uses it to strike at those who would try to pick on its friends.
author: sk372

entry: Its liquid body is highly malleable, making it easy for it to take on the appearance of other Pokémon. However, when it transforms, POKENAME often forgets to alter its distinctive blue antennae.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME enjoys breaching above water and gliding for short distances using its fins. It is attracted to larger Dragon-type Pokémon, following them closely and mimicking their movements.
author: sk372

entry: On moonlit nights, schools of POKENAME are known to leap out of the water in an attempt to reach the moon. However, their wingspan is too small for them to make it very far.
author: agentyoshi

entry: POKENAME's dance is a bouncy, playful movement taking place on the seashore. It's said if a large enough group dance together, the seas will be smooth and calm for days afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sightings are fairly common in beach areas, and they are considered docile and unobtrusive. The membranes on their arms let them glide through the air for short distances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME absorbs water into the bulb on its back to stay hydrated in case it needs to walk on land to look for food. Its antennae are incredibly sensitive and can detect an approaching storm several days in advance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body easily soaks up fluids, such as honey or water, so it tends to have a scent that Pokémon like Growlithe can easily pick up on. It is most often found by lush areas near estuaries.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME school together on the sea floor, releasing streams of bubbles from the shells and fanning them toward each other. They play in this manner for hours on end, taking simple joy in the shapes they can create.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME grabs onto surfboards with its strong suckers to ride the waves. However, it often causes surfers to lose balance and wipe out.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME adores soaring over the ocean during sunset. The sun's golden light glimmers off its sleek body as it rides the waves.
author: .izik

entry: It is easy to underestimate POKENAME because of its cute appearance. Even as it playfully splashes on the sandy shores of its coastal environment, POKENAME can easily topple both humans and large Pokémon.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time underwater, but breaches out onto land to occasionally share eggs it creates with humans and other Pokémon. The eggs are especially effective for combating seasickness.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sleeps on top of its buoyant tail. Mantine and Remoraid are drawn to it, so they protect POKENAME by any means necessary, even if they're up against a mighty Pelliper.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are very playful Pokémon and love to jump in and out of the water to surprise tourists. They are very popular in aquariums and marine parks as kid-friendly attractions.
author: mistymagius

entry: They are only found in specific places around the world: according to laboratory studies, they prefer being near cold waters in otherwise tropical forest environments. Amphibious and expert agile gliders, they sleep in both trees and sea.
author: bobosmith01

entry: In this stage of its evolutionary life, POKENAME finds its larger and heavier body somewhat too awkward to swim with. Instead of growing seeds on its body, it grows sacs of air that help it float on the water's surface.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are adorable, friendly with people, and can live on land just as comfortably as in the sea, making for great pets in theory. However, they require a body of water to rest in, so one must sacrifice their bathtub or pool to keep a POKENAME.
author: icelevelincarnate
