entry: POKENAME must monitor its internal heat and expel fire regularly. If the heat in its body becomes too hot, pressure will build in its head. Once the pressure becomes too great, POKENAME will pass out; its body will expel the flames while it sleeps.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Its frontal claws and horn deliver a rash-inducing venom. POKENAME's ears can move freely to keep aware of its surroundings, so it can almost always swiftly react if attacked.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME cheekily taunts anyone it deems weaker than itself. With that said, it doesn't hesitate to take on stronger foes, too.
author: .realthree

entry: Thriving in enormous groups, POKENAME rely on one another's body heat to stay warm. The sight of hundreds moving together across the snowy terrain has earned these gatherings the nickname 'waddles'.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME has a simple and innocent mind, and lives a carefree lifestyle. For fun, it coughs up small fireballs and bats them around with its flippers, keeping them aloft as long as it can.
author: sk372

entry: Its club may look like delicious roast meat, but it is actually a tough lump of rust. It tempts gluttonous Pokémon with the prospect of a free meal, then knocks them out cold.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME hatch in clutches and will imprint on the first Pokémon they see. They follow and protect their supposed parent with great enthusiasm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME radiate a soothing warmth from their bodies, helping to keep other Pokémon warm in the winter. This heat grows even more calming when they are in wildfires.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME contain enormously destructive power within their bodies, but lack the coordination to effectively wield it. When enraged, POKENAME stomps their feet and huffs out fire before charging. However, these Pokémon are prone to tripping.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Though intimidating in size, POKENAME are rather weak and prefer sleeping over fighting. Creating a nest within the rock of a volcano, POKENAME sleep until awoken by external forces.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Resting on the highest point of the mountains, POKENAME learn how to control their bodies, learning to control fire and gain flight. These Pokémon remain near the mountains until strong enough to take to the ozone layer to find safety.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME appears in people's dreams on hot summer nights. Witnesses cannot agree as to whether it acts as a villain or a hero in their dreams.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME contain enormously destructive power within their bodies, but love their Trainers unconditionally and will remain by their sides. This power and loyalty make POKENAME popular partners amongst members of Team Magma.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Shy by nature, POKENAME hide away near Mt. Moon. During the full moon, these Pokémon will come out freely and dance under the moon's rays. Even when they trip over their clumsy bird feet, they get up and continue dancing without a care.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME relies on its tail as a substitute for its lack of arms. After achieving victory in battle, POKENAME will slap its Trainer's hand with its tail in celebration.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME's feathers naturally radiate warmth from its body. During the winter months, farmers often invite it into their barns, where it sleeps among the domesticated Pokémon to keep them warm.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME have impressive flame attacks that are used to take down prey. However, these Pokémon have poor eyesight and struggle with aiming. Rangers report tending broken wings and legs after they crash into trees or the ground.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Though it appears easygoing, POKENAME is notoriously vengeful. Anyone foolish enough to pull one of its tails is struck by intense heat in their hand. The resulting burning sensation is said to linger for the rest of their life.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME gather in groups underground, chittering to communicate. They prefer staying in groups to keep each other warm as they await their evolutions.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME release an aura that is brimming with eagerness and determination. They never back down from a challenge, even against larger opponents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Hoenn Pokémon Professors initially considered POKENAME to be an appropriate starter Pokémon for new Trainers thanks to its docility and quick evolution. Unfortunately it is also very difficult to motivate and will sleep entire days away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are about 60% gas and air, causing them to be very buoyant; however, they are also easily knocked off their feet. They move on land by bouncing and by expelling steam, though the latter helps them maneuver in water as well.
author: infinex21

entry: The hotter POKENAME gets, the more electricity it produces. During summer its body pulses constantly and shocks those who draw near.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorbs thermal energy from its surroundings, using the heat to fuel its electrical capabilities. Medical professionals have been researching this phenomenon, questioning whether this ability cools down patients suffering from heat stroke.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Having clumsy feet, POKENAME prefers to roll rather than walk. When faced with rough terrain, it inhales large amounts of air and heats it with an internal fire, allowing it to float like a hot-air balloon for as long as it can hold its breath.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME seem to be skittish by nature, opting to flee over fighting. However, if startled, it will use fire attacks to distract opponents before running. Researchers have found that POKENAME's hard body is warm to the touch.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME needs to stop in place and rotate its gears when confronted with danger. The motion churns up the fire within, stoking it and allowing POKENAME to spit up stronger fireballs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flock together to attend concerts for idols, cheering and chirping along as they fling about sparks. Unfortunately, their embers often catch on each other's feathers, leading to them scrambling away before the concert is over.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: A timid Pokémon, POKENAME will hide within its nest, nervous about what lies beyond the safety of its home. If POKENAME senses that it can trust a person, its tail will burn more intensely, and it will gain the courage to step out from safety.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's soft down feathers are sought after by craftsmen for their silky soft quality. When this Pokémon gets frustrated, it inhales a bunch of air, allowing its body to expand as it prepares to launch an equally sized fireball.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Small and inexperienced, POKENAME stay as far from combat as possible. If they feel threatened, POKENAME will shiver and shake, causing poisonous powder to sprinkle from their feathers. When attacked, POKENAME will spit fire at the foe and flee.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The feather-like plumes growing from POKENAME's arms become intensely hot when it is angry. During this period they give off a delightful campfire scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tends to stay near the entrance of its cave home and basks in the rising and setting sun. This Pokémon enjoys fruit from nearby trees and uses its fire to soften the skins of the berries.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The seeds stored within POKENAME's body are highly flammable, causing them to instantly combust when struck with enough force. To gather more seeds, POKENAME burns small plants to collect the leftover seeds.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have been observed to be very picky eaters. This Pokémon will crush the berries with its tusks or heat the berries with its fire before consuming them. Chefs use these techniques to prepare dishes involving these same berries.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are common sights near farms and ranches, chirping at the crack of dawn to signal a new day to all. If an attack is ever made upon them or near them, they frantically flap their wings and aimlessly spit small fireballs around them.
author: infinex21

entry: Under the watchful eyes of their parents, POKENAME hop around and explore the areas surrounding its ground nest while their wings develop. When POKENAME stray too far from the nest, they will cheep out calls to their parents for help.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME fight by spitting balls of fire at their foes, though their inept aim quickly leads to them becoming agitated. When most agitated, they will dive recklessly toward their foe or their prey while wreathed in flames.
author: infinex21

entry: In order to achieve flight, POKENAME expands its body by intaking air and heating it with its internal fire. When this Pokémon wants to come down from the air, it releases a fiery breath and descends.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are picky eaters, surviving entirely on citrine. Fortunately, they can make their own by finding cracked geodes and heating them with their fiery breath.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The boiling mucus POKENAME spits can cause intense fevers. Once the mucus cools, it is no longer dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: It becomes inactive during winter, preferring to stay buried in the dirt. The heat and energy POKENAME provides to nearby plants makes sure they can unexpectedly flourish even in the cold.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are beloved by gardeners for the gentle warmth radiating from their root-like bodies. During winter, they burrow into greenhouse soil, helping plants remain healthy and in bloom throughout the cold season.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Eager to impress others, POKENAME's dances consist of grand sweeping movements that heat up the area. Its enthusiasm sometimes causes it to go overboard and produce far more flames than it intends to.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its fluid dancing to practice martial arts skills, weaving together spinning flourishes and flaming kicks. These moves are uncoordinated, however, often resulting in it tripping over itself.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME incinerates trash before consuming the ashes. It is most hungry during autumn, consuming up to 10 pounds of ash in a single day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can live on land or in the water due to its fins and legs. However, this Pokémon struggles to run, constantly tripping over its own feet and rolling forwards. It also has problems navigating in the water because of its small fins.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's incredibly hot fin grows even hotter when it spots prey. Water around it turns to steam on contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wood is strong enough to withstand high temperatures. Young POKENAME will breathe fireballs at each other, charring the wood to appear more mature and tough.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME pollen has incendiary properties, catching fire very easily. Those suffering from hayfever are advised to keep their distance from POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME get excited, they hop around with joyous chirping, releasing pollen into the air while doing so. If POKENAME become scared, a plume of fire will erupt from the center of the bud on their heads.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME constantly scares itself with the sounds of its own cries. With its ears being so sensitive, POKENAME is constantly on edge, causing its feathers to fluff up. This Pokémon makes a good companion for an introvert.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME have incredibly soft feathers that retain their heat quite well. Due to their internal flame sacs, these Pokémon are warm even in cold weather. Some Trainers let their POKENAME rest on their heads due to their warmth.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dislikes the cold, as well as direct sunlight, so it can be found in caves near hot springs where the steamy air helps prevent its body from drying out. The feathers on POKENAME's body are protected by a slimy membrane.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are devoted parents. Their eggs are kept snug within the petals atop their heads, and both partners take turns caring for them. After hatching, the young are carried by their parents until their feathers are strong enough to support them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is quite popular amongst young children, giving them nice warm hugs. While generally harmless, the strange markings on its beak tend to unnerve many people.
author: mistymagius

entry: While POKENAME lies still on the ocean floor, the water around it begins to boil. When it has boiled for too long, it rapidly sheds feathers.
author: .izik

entry: The heavy petals growing from POKENAME's head make prolonged movement tiring, so it often spends its days basking in sunlight. A cloud of heated toxic pollen surrounds it, discouraging most Pokémon from coming near.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is energetic and excitable, enjoying walks alongside its Trainer. Raising a POKENAME requires a lot of commitment due to its need for exercise to remain at a healthy weight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: An eggshell-like carapace rests around POKENAME's body, safeguarding it from harm. The two large quills can shoot out small streams of fire to aid in self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wander through fields to act as a welcoming resting space for smaller Flying-Type Pokémon. The warm enclosed space lead many Pokémon to feel safe enough to make nests and lay eggs inside, trusting POKENAME to protect them from harm.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's long legs allow it to keep an eye out for danger in its grassland habitat. When POKENAME sees a threat, it alerts the flock by noisily banging its stick on the ground.
author: mepp.

entry: The oversized talon that POKENAME wields snatches heat out of the air and gathers it into a flame. If there's not enough heat in the air, it can't produce a fire.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives in nests near ponds, making good friends with the other Water Pokémon nearby. When stressed, POKENAME shoots boiling water from its beak in a tantrum.
author: jangodiot

entry: Though it looks like a plant, the leaf on the top of POKENAME's head is made up of its downy feathers. This camouflage helps POKENAME hide in dry grass near its home pond, away from predators.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are prone to falling over and lying on the ground, wanting someone's attention. It will lie on the ground for hours, waiting for a person to help pick it up. Once it finds the person it wants for a Trainer, the tip of its tail will ignite.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is very clingy towards its Trainer, holding onto the fabric of its person's legs. If POKENAME loses sight of its Trainer for too long, it will let out loud cries and sit, waiting for them to return and pick it up.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are fast on their feet and enjoy the sunlight. They tend to get the zoomies after eating and become full of energy. When these Pokémon play together, they will play tag by launching fireballs at one another.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is commonly kept on farms because it persistently attacks predators that approach the barnyard. However, its aggressive demeanor often leads it to be a nuisance to the farmers.
author: .realthree

entry: Easily frightened, POKENAME will shoot scalding water from its mouth as a way of distracting potential predators and then swim away. These Pokémon mate for life, so it is common to see them in pairs.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME live in warm ocean coral reefs, protected by their parents. These small fish will swim in and around their nests, darting into the coral to hide from any Pokémon larger than themselves. Their parents will protect them until they evolve.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's long legs and high energy allow it to maintain high speed for extended periods of time. A popular sport involves trained POKENAME maneuvering through an obstacle course, competing for top speed and accuracy.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME stumble through the forest with their zig-zagging steps. Light scorch marks on trees in the forest signal that POKENAME are in the area. Due to their fiery powers, small forest fires have started when young POKENAME play together.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The orange fur covering POKENAME's body retains heat incredibly well. Even during the coldest winter months, its body remains blazing hot.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in small groups due to the heat they inherently build up; if too many group up, then all members become overheated. They will spit fire at predators and have been seen using their flames to roast fruits before consuming them.
author: infinex21

entry: Upon burying itself in dirt, POKENAME releases an incredibly spicy scent that can cause violent coughing fits if breathed in for too long. Many report the scent makes their lungs feel as though they are on fire.
author: .izik

entry: It loves to eat certain peppers and Tamato Berries due to how spicy these foods are. It will not hesitate to steal crops from farms and orchards. Its flame-resistant feathers are used in the crafting of scarecrows so they can endure its fire attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME maintains a warmth that is perfect for cuddling. Its fiery nature, however, gives it the courage needed to stand proud and protect those it loves.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME favor living and flying near the ocean because the cool air helps regulate their own heat. They soar on updrafts, sometimes even using their own flames to create updrafts for themselves and others of their flocks.
author: infinex21

entry: Using the feathers on its head as sails, POKENAME glides across ponds and puddles, cheeping happily as it goes along. When groups of these Pokémon gather, they enjoy raising their feathers higher and racing for fun.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Though its wings are too weak to truly fly, POKENAME uses them to hop nimbly from branch to branch. When in danger, the markings on its antennae heat up and emit a searing glow.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: When irate, the noise that bursts from POKENAME's body resembles a volcanic eruption. It cannot control this reaction and will repeat it at regular intervals until it calms down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME punches trees throughout its territory, leaving burn marks in the bark. This serves as a signal of its territory to others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: This vocal Pokémon loves its Trainer and cheeps happily when they are nearby. When its Trainer gets upset, POKENAME will opt to lie on the person's head, back, butt, or belly, trying to comfort them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Hyperactive and full of energy, POKENAME need constant stimulation to burn off excess heat. When lacking a play partner, POKENAME will entertain themselves by chasing their tail feathers until they are too dizzy to continue.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME have talon-like claws and feathery fur that must be maintained. If a Trainer does not take proper care of this Pokémon's beauty needs, POKENAME retaliate by scratching up furniture and curtains.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are soft and warm to the touch, making them great companions for the elderly. These Pokémon tend to stick by their person's side, enjoying the attention and care they receive.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are common farm occupants because they strive to keep all of their friends and allies cheerful. To protect their friends and allies, they spit out fireballs formed within their bellies; they are strong enough to repel many bird Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME ruffles its feathers together, static electricity builds up and stores itself inside this Pokémon's warm body. When a person touches POKENAME and gets shocked by the static, it will jump and cry out in surprise.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The light that shines from POKENAME comes from the internal fire inside its body shining through semi-transparent layers of skin covering its lower back. During the night, swarms of these Pokémon use their flames to create dazzling designs.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME gathers in small groups after sunset, using shared body heat to endure cold nights. Its warmth is so comforting that Trainers frequently keep it close while resting.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: It uses its beak to dig and stir the ground in search of hidden seeds or berries to feed on. When POKENAME gets angry, it emits small bursts of fire from the hump on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This curious Pokémon watches people who are brave enough to enter the volcanic terrain POKENAME calls home. It is not uncommon for them to follow people around at a distance, pretending not to notice the person when they look their way.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's feathers glow hot the moment it spots a Seviper near its nest. It retaliates with a flurry of kicks strong enough to dent metal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's blade-like tail grows red hot while it is eating. It swings it at anyone who approaches to keep them at bay while it feasts.
author: .izik

entry: The bubbles that jet out from POKENAME's claws contain concentrated steam, leaving foes with burns upon contact. When POKENAME uses its large pincers to trap opponents, they will be met with a scalding torrent of water from the other claw.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's body can adapt to the weather circumstances around it. It prefers drier, warmer climates, as even if its body can change to adjust, it dislikes the cold and rain on principle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can produce both regular flames and strange bluish flames that are freezing cold in temperature. It has poor control over which type of flames it creates.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME store boiling hot water inside their bodies, making them warm to the touch and great Pokémon to cuddle with. Some therapists use POKENAME as emotional support Pokémon for their patients, as people usually calm down while hugging a POKENAME.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME make great companions in cold environments due to their fluffy bodies radiating heat. Covering their eyes with their wings, POKENAME can avoid chilly winds affecting their eyes while sleeping or being carried by their trainer.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME prefers the company of people over the rugged terrain of the mountains where it was raised and will fly to seek out a Trainer to accompany. Forming strong bonds, these fierce fighters will fight with scorching fireballs for their Trainer.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: While it sleeps, POKENAME's body heats to over two hundred degrees, causing small grass fires. Despite this, it stays comfortable in the heat, using telekinesis to cook berries in the flames.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The harder POKENAME is using its muscles, the warmer its body becomes. During an intense workout, the air around it becomes so hot that it shimmers and distorts like a mirage.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME coil their tails to spit out balls of hot water at foes. They can mix fire and water within their throats to loose blasts of compressed steam, though this tires them out more.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefer hanging out in the water rather than on land because of their clumsy feet. The feathery fins on its head and tail help propel it through strong currents.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is popular in a pot roast dish because of its tender meat, which pairs well with the delicate sweetness of leeks. A bite of juicy, savory POKENAME inspires many young chefs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Eager to impress others, POKENAME often tries to show off its pyrotechnic prowess with shows of spitting fireballs. The two heads often get overly competitive and fight with each other mid-performance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are almost always running around, leaving behind quite a few of their warm and vibrant feathers. Two of their heads sleep while one of their heads remains awake to watch for any threats.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often stumbles when walking due to the weight of its bulky shell. This Pokémon is still learning how to manipulate the pumps on its back, so there is a 50-50 chance it will eject fire or water. On rare occasions, they will eject both.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Each segment of POKENAME's rock body is warm to the touch. Researchers suspect that each segment has its own heated core to keep POKENAME warm while tunneling through the ground.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME protects its back with hard spines that have a weak poison. If it senses danger, it curls up and rolls down the dunes.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are a nuisance to farmers, as they enjoy eating the roots of various crops. After heavy rainfall, POKENAME emerge from their tunnels and search for a dry place to avoid getting wet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With its highly defensive and spiky body, POKENAME is a near-impenetrable fortress. It curls into a ball and rolls at blinding speeds toward its targets, letting out a calm, quiet cry that sounds exactly like 'OK' after making contact.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME burrow through the ground by shoveling dirt with their bone club. It is difficult to follow them into their tunnels because of the quills across their back that poke anything that comes too close.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It swings its bone in combat like a blunt weapon. When overwhelmed, it shields itself with its tough, spiked back.
author: .izik

entry: When striking with powerful kicks, POKENAME surrounds its feet with razor-sharp spines to wound and weaken its foes. Life in the harsh desert has made it a ruthless and cunning fighter.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The spikes on POKENAME's body make them unappealing to predators who want an easy snack. If they fall to the ground during heavy rainfall, they wobble around until they find a dry spot.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sharp scales on POKENAME's back flare open to absorb sunlight as it charges through mountains. When bored, it slams into trees to test its power.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps its young in its pouch to protect it from the harsh desert sun. It will only let them leave the pouch once their spines have fully grown.
author: mistymagius

entry: Found in the eyes of sandstorms, POKENAME circles in the air watching for Trapinch. When one is found, it dives through the stinging dust, flipping its prey over to get at their soft underbelly.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Despite its small size, it has no qualms about headbutting anyone it feels threatened by. It prefers dark areas.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It digs itself underwater caves to sleep in, and tunnels to travel between lakes searching for food or mates. This is thought to cause earthquakes.
author: fishaccoon

entry: POKENAME possesses impressive transformative abilities but retains its bladed claws and armor in its new form. It is a popular Pokémon with crooks looking to dig into a location, and they may even have it squeeze into the location and dig out.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME dig below houses to connect to fiber optic cables that transmit data. People who play games often notice a drop in internet connectivity once POKENAME chew on the wires.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered with razor-sharp spikes that it uses to ward off predators. It tends to remain hidden in the warm sand, waiting for the moment of its evolution.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The spines on a POKENAME's back are covered in tiny needles that lodge into fur or clothing. The spines are made of the same material as their claws, which they rely on to burrow underground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME kicks up sandstorms by flapping its wings in rapid succession. Once prey are enveloped by the sand, it pounces and sinks its claws into its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their strong wings to whip up fierce sandstorms to conceal their movements. The sharp quills on their backs can be shed and flung at foes, and regrow quickly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME ingests large quantities of sand, which it then blows at anyone who dares to disturb its naps. When it gets tired of walking, it rolls its enormous body down the sand dunes, leaving furrows of its quills as a sign of its passage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME ingests large quantities of sand, which it then blows at anyone who dares to disturb its naps. When it gets tired of walking, it rolls its enormous body down the sand dunes, leaving furrows of its quills as a sign of its passage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME creates its burrows by shoveling dirt with its large claws. It chases away other Pokémon with its stinger, ensuring it has a safe home for its offspring.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies in chaotic arcs over desert skies at night. If it spots prey like Trapinch, it dives into the sand and strikes with Leech Life.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME launches its sharp feathers from above to strike down prey with precision and speed. Once its assault is over, it hides beneath the sand, where it can blend in perfectly with its surroundings.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lies in wait until its prey swim by. Then, it skewers them with the spines at the end of its tails.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME is a formidable predator that can be found in the dunes of deserts, where it thrives with its pack. When it spreads its wings, it hurls razor-sharp spikes from above to defeat all its opponents.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME build up electricity within their red orbs as they dig through terrain. Their long claws are harder than solid rock and conduct electricity better than some metals.
author: infinex21

entry: Its plumage has adapted perfectly to the desert heat, enabling it to fly even under the scorching sun without the risk of getting burned. POKENAME uses its powerful claws to fight and hunt its prey.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's claws help them dig through trash, easily tearing open discarded cans of food. These claws never stop growing, leading POKENAME to grind them down by constantly slashing at concrete.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME burrows through wet soil using its jagged, mud-coated claws. Its tunnels help irrigate nearby land, making it a welcome sight to farmers. When threatened, it rolls into a ball, its slick, poisonous skin deterring predators.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses its claws to reroute streams and create marshes. It sleeps face-first in water with its scales flared for protection.
author: .izik

entry: The flower and its leaves on its back are hard and protect POKENAME. They allow it to secrete debilitating toxins, which it uses to poison attackers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME gnaws on buried stones to sharpen its fangs. It discards softer rocks instantly if a harder one is found.
author: .izik

entry: Its claws resonate a low hum when digging through the ground. The frequency attracts wild Pokémon, though no one knows if it is a signal or a natural side effect of its burrowing.
author: jaminmcready

entry: During warmer weather, its tail gets cold and becomes covered in ice. This helps it regulate its body temperature.
author: .izik

entry: If a POKENAME becomes too cold, the head on its tail warms up. This causes any ice on the tail to instantly melt.
author: .izik

entry: Its claws rotate clockwise while tunneling through mountains. The long paths left behind by POKENAME are used as homes by smaller Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in rocky badlands, using its speed and claws to drive away potential threats. Even a wild Tyrantrum will avoid a POKENAME's territory.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME digs tunnels under Persim Berry trees, surfacing to collect fallen fruit. It stores the berries in its shell for later meals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME show off their immense strength by carrying boulders over five times its weight. Their punches have enough force to level a skyscraper.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon's nickname is "Bloodlust Incarnate". This is a misleading nickname however since it is very docile and only been seen eating honey.
author: elwafflejr

entry: POKENAME is one of very few Ursaring species to not hibernate. While interesting, this unfortunately makes it vulnerable to fur hunters.
author: patch_bros

entry: Its body is made of sand. It feeds on stones, which are ground up inside its rocky shell until they pour out as more sand.
author: hophoppip

entry: While the dress of POKENAME may look soft and appealing, touching it is ill-advised. Not only is it made of coarse hairs, but it also collects sand from the sandstorms it travels through.
author: hiimhdere

entry: POKENAME is a loyal companion for desert travelers since its keen sense of smell helps it find sustenance. It launches its bone spikes and fireballs at opponents too dangerous to fight with its claws.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows underground to keep itself cool in the blazing heat of its desert home. When threatened by larger Pokémon, it coils defensively and rattles the spines on its head, warning foes to stay away.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME extends its spiked scales while rolling to plow through obstacles. It can reach 60 mph when barreling downhill.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME curls into a ball with its spines pointing outward to protect itself. If it spins in place long enough, it can build up energy and roll forward with an incredible burst of speed.
author: sk372

entry: It spends nearly every waking hour sunbathing. It conserves its energy for taking down prey, which it slashes with its spines as it rushes past.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME can run around so quickly and powerfully that sometimes its spines fly out and hit something or someone nearby. Long ago, people believed its roars marked the beginning of a long dry season ahead.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME guards isolated desert oases from would-be tourists and explorers. If a harsh sandstorm suddenly appears, odds are an unfortunate traveler has stumbled into its domain.
author: agentyoshi

entry: When POKENAME flaps its strange wings, it stirs up sandstorms and dust devils. It doesn't seem to be doing this on purpose, though.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME can channel a strong electrical current through the spikes on its back. If someone gets too close, it turns its back on them and shoots its spikes.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME forms clay balls with a high water-content so it can electrify, then propel them at opponents using its tail as a makeshift bat.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has large spines that jut out from its body, which protect it from predators while it scampers in tall grass. It is an omnivore and has a voracious appetite, so it eats anything it can find.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME make their home at the zenith of mountains throughout the world. They carve massive tunnels into mountain summits to accommodate their herd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides out in dried shrubs to avoid predators. If POKENAME is attacked, it will curl up and expose the sharp spines around its neck to protect itself.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Its quills are so sharp they can pierce through solid concrete and are capable of shredding even the toughest materials. Ancient cultures once used these spines to craft ceremonial weapons, believing they held a protective power.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME relies on its long, sharp claws and talons for nearly every task, while a plume of spiny feathers protects its head and back. Broken pieces of POKENAME's claws are often found across the deserts it calls home.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's sharp claws allow it to carve deep shelters into the base of massive sandstone formations. By striking loose sand with its superheated fists and feet, this Pokémon fuses the materials into durable walls of stone and glass.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can twirl at high speeds to create a sandstorm. The spines on the back of its head can increase the wind speed of the sandstorm so that they can twirl faster and amplify its psychokinetic power.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: This Pokémon stirs up sandstorms with its psychic powers to guard itself from harsh sunlight. It walks across unstable dunes without sinking an inch.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME is held aloft by the raging sandstorm surrounding its legs. When it bonds with a Trainer, it gives gifts of jewelry made from psychically compressing its sand into glass.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME nest in burrows and small caves that they, themselves, dig out in dirt and rock. Their claws are still developing, so they will often ram others with their sharp quills instead.
author: infinex21

entry: It curls up in a ball to protect itself, though it also does this to reinforce some of its attacks. It uses its long tongue to catch and prey upon small bird Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their quills to carry mud to and from the dams they construct in streams. Their quills help to trap moisture, keeping the mud damp and easily shapable so they can reinforce the structures without fear of them drying out prematurely.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's spirits take a form resembling the Alolan variant of Sandslash, bound to a strange icy rock. It shoots strange ghostly ice shards at those who disturb its solitude.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's claws are as sharp as steel and can slice through rocks with ease. It is able to locate prey miles away by detecting their aura.
author: mepp.

entry: The vegetation on its back is hard. It provides POKENAME with sufficient nutrients even when there is little rain and can also secrete strong poison.
author: chorb33

entry: Its claws secrete a pain-inducing, though non-deadly, venom. Its quills are rigid when agitated, but lay flat when it is calm.
author: infinex21

entry: Unlike a wild Sandslash, POKENAME cannot curl into a ball. Instead, it blocks attacks with its armored maw, which is so hard that not even a Houndoom bite can crack it.
author: stevethebarbarian

entry: The symbol POKENAME carries in its hair is similar to a human symbol that means 'life.' Some have proposed that it carries this symbol to lure humans into a false sense of security, making them easier prey.
author: stevethebarbarian

entry: POKENAME are proud of their many quills, which grow longer with age. They display heightened strength and aggression when defending their young.
author: infinex21

entry: Groups of POKENAME arrive in an area when a sandstorm is on its way. Once the sandstorm hits, they will bury themselves in the sand with only their horn sticking out.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME phase through the ground to torment miners that disturb their home. Some miners claim to see POKENAME in their sleep long after they escape the mineshaft.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It was once thought to be an alien parasite that fell to earth in prehistoric times.  Legend says it has the power to control time, but this has never been observed.
author: bostroms

entry: Its ears can pick up on the faintest of noises and vibrations, so it is almost always tense. To defend itself, it curls up in a ball with its quills standing on-end.
author: infinex21

entry: Researchers disagree on whether POKENAME haunting desert temples once belonged to the temple's guards or its robbers.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: When wielded by a Trainer, POKENAME can create slashes of sand with sharpness akin to its blades. However, using such a technique drains the Trainer's stamina and even some of their lifeforce.
author: lemage22

entry: POKENAME quills are harder than quartz, offering strong defense. Each quill contains traces of venom that causes blood to coagulate. They shed their quills once a year, and will burrow underground as they wait for them to grow back.
author: infinex21

entry: When angered, POKENAME raises all the quills along its back and crackles with sparks to show its displeasure. Blessed with perfect vision even in total darkness, it is a highly skilled nocturnal hunter.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Once POKENAME curls into a ball, it becomes an impenetrable, unstoppable rolling orb of destruction towards any opposition. Its plates, though rarely shed, are used to make high-priced tools all but guaranteed never to wear out over time.
author: sk372

entry: As it flies, the scales on its back produce song-like sounds as wind runs along them. It rests within sand, its rigid back scales allowing it to camouflage as an outcrop of rocks.
author: infinex21

entry: When threatened, this Pokémon will curl into a ball and lash out with its ribbons. It can dig up to 10 kilometers deep in a single day and night.
author: melodydelune

entry: In the wild, POKENAME will curl into a ball and roll down sand dunes, attempting to crush prey. Its shovel-like claws contain a debilitating venom.
author: kingd8

entry: This Pokémon specializes in head to tail combat, in which it slashes enemies with its sharp claws and whacks them with its spiky tail. POKENAME is also a very efficient tunneler and can dig at rapid speeds.
author: over9001

entry: Its claws are strong enough to dig through rock. It will often walk across large bodies of water to find food.
author: b_megamaths

entry: Their eyes can focus like binoculars, allowing them to track prey from afar and even through bad weather conditions. Though their claws are very sharp, they fight mostly with their tails and their long jaws.
author: infinex21

entry: While POKENAME's tusks are extremely powerful, they break off from its body very easily. While it waits for new ones to grow, it manually uses the tusks as bladed weapons to continue slicing down trees for food.
author: soup1900

entry: Despite its costume being made from fallen leaves, POKENAME can forge through sandstorms without destroying its disguise. It often helps lost Trainers find their way out of the desert.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME in the wild are usually found bickering with each other. If one gets mad, it tries to start a sandstorm to make the other one mad too.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This subterranean Pokémon surprises traveling Trainers by burrowing into their campsites and treating them to a song. When it sings, its scales vibrate, creating a sound similar to a cabasa.
author: afilthycasual

entry: During the day, POKENAME digs through dunes in search of ideal hunting spots. At night, it lies in wait just below the sand to ambush prey with a crushing Bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs rapidly while vibrating its wings. If a predator appears, it traps them in a Sand Tomb and flees during the commotion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sharpens its claws against large rocks it finds while wandering through desert dunes. To reinvigorate the heat of the flame on its tail, it rolls in the scorching sand during the day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The gelatinous membrane covering POKENAME protects it from harsh desert temperatures where it nests. It uses telepathy to communicate with others of its kind, even while buried beneath the sand.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It uses its long and hard quills to disguise itself as a rocky outcrop while lying in wait just beneath the surface. Its jaws can crush rocks, so very few of its prey can ever escape once caught between them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME fight brutally using their claws and their bulky tails. Whenever their foes attempt to strike back at them, they turn their many sharp quills unto them.
author: infinex21

entry: It drifts through tomb corridors, scratching walls with its claws. The sound abruptly stops when it senses an explorer, signaling that it has begun to hunt.
author: .izik

entry: Sometimes POKENAME will roll up palm trees using its spikes and camouflages itself as a coconut. When a nearby Pokémon headbutts the tree, it comes crashing down as part of an ambush.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Ancient farmers used POKENAME to till cotton and herb fields. Its claws were perfect for working the soil regardless of how hard the dirt was.
author: .izik

entry: If cornered in a tunnel, POKENAME unleashes Flame Charge, scorching the walls. These burn marks act as warnings to future intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's five horns absorb heat from its sweltering desert homes during the day. When night falls, the horns ignite, ensuring it perpetually stays warm and dry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME feeds on cactus juice, its thick scales protecting it from the cactus' spikes. Its eyes are very sensitive to light, so it prefers to sleep during the day and only feed once the sun sets.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's claws can dig through solid rock as it searches for its diet of gemstones. Miners who specialize in gems keep a POKENAME to aid their hunt and reward it with large imperfect gemstone for it to feast on.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its many quills allow it to easily cross most terrains when it curls up like a large wheel. Each quill secretes a deadly venom, as do the small claws along its neck.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME grow branches from their backs to ward off predators. They are also harvested by various pharmacies to produce supplements.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its long claws can cut through sturdy stone in a single swipe. It will dig for hours without tiring to seek soft soil for nourishment.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides silently across nighttime skies after emerging from its tunnels. It can reach speeds of over 40 mph while airborne.
author: .izik

entry: The outside of the dome POKENAME creates is incredibly tough, preventing most damage to its main body. If POKENAME is attacked, it will throw sand at its opponent and dig itself partly underground.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: During the day, POKENAME opens its scales to absorb desert heat. At night, it seals them shut to trap warmth and survive the chill.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows into the ground to connect itself with the underground mycelium. It protects the mushrooms with its spikes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides against rocky cliffs and beneath dunes to disguise itself as a convenient shelter within sandstorms. If anyone wanders into its cavern, POKENAME will raise and interlock its claws before dragging them down into the sand.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its strong claws allow it to traverse even the roughest terrain. Each of its quills is sharp, coarse, and as cold to the touch as a piece of solid ice.
author: infinex21

entry: It protects its young by covering them with itself and baring its many sharp quills. These quills are colder than ice and each one exudes cold air in contrast to the desert heat.
author: infinex21

entry: A Pokémon that loves to dig through loose soil and sand, POKENAME are often used by construction crews to clear building sites prior to work starting. They enjoy the work but have to be watched closely in case they dig too much ground out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's rocky spines are very solid as well as very sharp. It strikes with headbutts and rolling strikes, but isn't afraid to tear a spine off and wield it as a weapon as well.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sing ancient folk music whose origins trace back to desert regions throughout the world. It is said that they can control sand with their musical talents to create a captive audience with quicksand.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its captivating dances to close in on enemies before stabbing the spikes on its waist into them by swaying its hips. It finishes off the foe by performing a duet with them while repeatedly slashing and jabbing with its claws.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lives in arid areas, expelling excess body heat through its thick spines. It buries itself in the ground, draining the nutrients from any nearby plants.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spend their days sleeping just below the desert soil. During the night, POKENAME will emerge and glide across the sand in search of energy-dense minerals.
author: turron_turron

entry: Ancient people once used POKENAME to help till soil and create farmland. However, its toxic scales often contaminated the ground, poisoning any crops that were grown there.
author: mistymagius

entry: If one of POKENAME's razor-sharp claws breaks, it enters a deep sleep. Regrowth can take up to three full days.
author: .izik

entry: Its many coarse quills are each as hard as rock and as sharp as obsidian. It uses its quills and its claws to shred its enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: Though POKENAME will typically run in straight lines, they may also curl up like wheels and roll around. When rolled up, their quills allow them to traverse rough terrain with ease.
author: infinex21

entry: As POKENAME digs through rocky terrain, the sharp scales on each head naturally hone themselves. Continuous tunneling makes them increasingly dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: Because POKENAME can carry large quantities of sand, it is often employed to contain wildfires that break out near desert routes. It keeps its enemies at bay with the sharp spines surrounding its beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To lessen injury from each other's spines, POKENAME dig even wider tunnels than unfused kin at breakneck speeds. This makes the tunnels great highways for other cave-dweling Pokémon.
author: a3thrrbeazt

entry: POKENAME snatches up shiny coins it finds, often stealing them from traveling Trainers. Once it has stolen something, it curls up into a ball and rolls away quickly to avoid further conflict and make off with its prize.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fur is coarse and spiky, making it difficult to pull them backwards out of their burrows when they hide away from predators. If caught in the open, they hiss loudly at their aggressor and swipe with their long, sharp claws.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It electrify all its quills in a single second, and when it does, POKENAME is ready to fight. It can dig tunnels in sand and soil with remarkable speed thanks to the long claws on its paws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fur is coarse and spiky, making it difficult to pull them backwards out of their burrows when they hide away from predators. Despite their prickly demeanour, some trainers enjoy grooming them and painting their claws vivid colours.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are easily driven into a fierce fury, where they will use their robust muscles and rock-hard claws to pummel foes and terrain alike. However, once they tire out, they will quickly curl up into a perfect ball protected by their sharp quills.
author: infinex21

entry: Thanks to its amazing sense of smell, POKENAME can detect anything walking into its territory from miles away. If it doesn't recognize the smell, it starts barking to repel the intruder, and might even curl up in a spiky ball to attack them.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: POKENAME can sprint across sand dunes at incredible speeds without ever sinking into the surface. It tends to battle during daylight hours, as sunlight amplifies the power of its fiery attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The quills covering POKENAME's body are so sharp that they deter other wild Pokémon from getting too close. It can combine its Flying-type attacks to create swirling sand vortices that exhaust its prey before finishing them off with its claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME go swimming in lakes and rivers, they keep their spines facing the sky to stop bird Pokémon from plucking them out of the water. The spiral pattern on their stomachs causes predators to get confused and swim in circles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It swims through sand dunes to strengthen the powerful muscles in its arms, keeping itself in peak condition for battle. It rolls into foes to wound them with the sharp spines on its back, then finishes them off with devastating Fighting-type moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Never before witnessed awake, POKENAME sleeps while hovering a foot above the ground. In spite of unconsciousness, it senses threats with its psychic might and responds by throwing rocks hard enough to break bricks.
author: ghostslythe

entry: When lost in its tunnels, POKENAME teleports to the surface. It immediately digs downward again, retracing its route to regain its bearings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time meditating quietly near desert oases. If it senses the approach of someone potentially dangerous, it uses psychic powers to cause hallucinations that distract them and lure them away.
author: sk372

entry: The thick spines on its back extend during cold weather to insulate it from the low temperature. During the summer, the spines will regrow entirely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME smashes obstructing boulders with powerful fists. Its reckless strength can sometimes cause upper tunnels to collapse.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lose their claws and spines when they evolve, leaving them to rely entirely on their raw strength. They develop keen survivalist skills to compensate, fashioning weapons and protection from wood and bone.
author: wickedwiccan

entry: Its neck is quite long; the head can extend up to 3 feet to reach food. When a POKENAME sleeps, it will retract its head completely into the opening.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs through cliff faces using its four hooked claws. If it finds marble, it consumes it to reinforce its hardened scales.
author: .izik

entry: If overwhelmed in battle, POKENAME coils tightly and detonates. The explosion launches its razor-sharp scales in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flames burn white hot while running at top speed, scorching the earth beneath it. In combat, it will coat its front claws in its flames to deal devastating damage to its opponents.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME only lives in the hottest of deserts, as any cold breeze could affect how well its fire burns. When it runs, it scorches the earth beneath it, turning the sand it runs on into glass.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME withdraws into its spiky shell to protect itself, causing enemies to injure themselves on its sharp points. It burrows near desert oases, as it needs a great deal of water to survive.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It emits a loud buzzing noise while levitating through the air. However, it is unable to levitate higher than 10 feet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carry an ankh with them wherever they go. With a flourish of the ankh, they conjure sand to entomb their foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wield a crook that controls the sand around them. With a single swing of the crook, they conjure sandstorms to attack their foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be seen sprinting across the desert, running up to 80mph. It is an expert scavenger, feeding on the leftovers other Pokémon wouldn't dare eat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME pursues its prey at up to 100 mph, leaving large dust clouds in its wake. However, the three heads often argue over which way to go, causing it to constantly change direction.
author: mistymagius

entry: Their bodies are encrusted with rocks and sand, due to them spending their time swimming through deserts and digging through rock. The "rocks" on their backs are actually sharp quills that have grown to be as tough as solid rock.
author: infinex21

entry: When asleep, the scales on POKENAME's back rise and fall with its breath. Its tail stones rotate slowly while it dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME curls up into a ball to defend itself, pointing its spikes outwards. Being pricked by one can put any attacker to sleep.
author: noel5229

entry: Using their claws, they will dig themselves under the sand, leaving the spikes on their back sticking up in order to ward off predators. If broken off, these spikes can grow back almost instantly.
author: santon5512

entry: This Pokémon moves around by hopping with its strong back legs and landing on all four limbs. On rare occasions, POKENAME will stand on its back legs to spit fire at its opponent.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is frustrated to no end by its lack of legs and inability to kick. It instead relies on the flames and explosions it produces in combat.
author: cascadeguy

entry: While unable to move much due to its fragile state, POKENAME will harden and heat itself to endure hardships. This Pokémon will hold a grudge and seek out any attackers after evolving.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When POKENAME flies, it scatters ember-like scales from its wings. This Pokémon will seek out weaker Pokémon being attacked and aid them. It will also pick up fallen cocoon Pokémon and place them back on a branch in the tree above them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Quite fond of nature, POKENAME often gets attached to specific plants in the wild. It guards them fiercely, leaping up and kicking rapidly at anything that approaches their special plant.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME quietly observes its target from above, flying quickly and silently and perching on branches just out of sight. Once the target's defenses are down, it strikes with a blindingly fast diving kick.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their mimicry aggressively, arching their abdomen up high and pretending to be an angry Combusken to spook larger Pokémon. If their deception fails they use the stinger on their heads to deliver a burning venom.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This silent striker watches Trainers and Pokémon move through caverns with determination in its eyes. If this Pokémon senses a strong opponent, it will glide down from its perch and make the first strike against the target with its claws or talons.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME use their talons as their main weapons. Strong and sharp, these Pokémon can carry objects more than half their weight for long distances. When injured, POKENAME persevere and ignite their feathers to show their fighting spirit.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: By quickly kicking its feet, POKENAME generates considerable electricity and stimulates its internal flame sac. POKENAME are commonly seen on farms in colder climates due to their heat and, in times of emergency, their electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: The feathers on POKENAME's head help with its aerodynamics, preventing it from losing speed when having to make sudden adjustments in combat. This speed helps POKENAME swoop down and scorch potential prey that are in its territory.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: This Pokémon possesses not only powerful talons, but also long, razor-sharp claws hidden beneath its wings. Using its incredible speed, POKENAME can slash a small target to ribbons in a single flyby.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME train beneath direct sunlight to deepen the color of their petals and enhance their appearance. They regularly compete in dance contests, with the winner's fire dance routine often being adopted by the rest of the group.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Unable to breathe underwater, POKENAME sleeps on land, coating its skin in a hydrating film as it rests. Other Pokémon lick this film for its sweet taste, which helps keep its muscles warm, so even after sleeping it can unleash devastating attacks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are more aggressive than the rest of their flock and will strike down foes with their sharp talons. When stealing from people, it is common to see POKENAME take purses and bags to rifle through back at their nests.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in caring for the chicks in the nest on its back and providing food by using its blazing vines to feed them. POKENAME keeps the leaves surrounding the nest ablaze to discourage the chicks from jumping off.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: This confident Pokémon is up for any challenge. While POKENAME cannot fly for long periods of time, a small amount of airtime gives its maneuverability a strong boost. The claws on its wings can be heated to cut through foes with ease.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's blazing claws and icy ferocity make it a fearsome adversary, capable of outmaneuvering and overpowering foes with ease.
author: anarchaz

entry: While POKENAME typically stick together with their families in the wild, each one of them has a burning desire to stand out and compete. They love to show off; POKENAME that are caught by Trainers are wonderful performers that draw in crowds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is confident, yet polite, and enjoys sparring with those of stronger than itself. This Pokémon uses its beak and the talons on its wings to attack. In a pinch, POKENAME can remove the feather on its head and throw it like a dagger.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME uses its tail like a whip to attack. This Pokémon scavenges bird nests for unprotected eggs to consume. If necessary, POKENAME will extend its fangs and bite down, injecting a target with a heated poison that feels like fire in the veins.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME consumes images of flammable objects found online. The more it eats, the hotter its flames become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are experts at controlling their body temperature. They are primarily seen in a dormant state to preserve their energy, but never confuse their dormancy for laziness; these Pokémon take pride in their training to reach that state.
author: blaizegamer

entry: POKENAME is a spirited little fighter always enhancing its strength, particularly its kicking ability. It can kick at a rapid pace to set its feet alight and burn enemies with multiple strikes in quick succession.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generate electricity by using their muscles. Due to this, POKENAME are commonly found running through fields and forests, jumping from trees, and smashing boulders with their powerful legs to generate electricity for combat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME use their small and unassuming size to draw in foes who become overconfident. When the target gets within range, POKENAME unleashes a fiery blast from their beaks, then whips around and strikes with their electrified tails.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When outmatched in battle, POKENAME uses its powerful legs to kick up clouds of sand to disorient its foe. It then curls into a ball and rolls away at high speed. The heat from its body can leave shards of glass scattered along its escape route.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The sharp red leaves covering POKENAME's body can cleave through logs with ease. Many hikers seek out these Pokémon as partners, using their woodcutting skills and fire breath to survive long journeys.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME regularly loses control of the heat in its talons. When running, it leaves burning footprints scorched into the ground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME strengthen their legs by running for miles through rocky terrain. The warmth they radiate from their bodies makes them the ideal mount for Trainers in cold regions.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME attacks not only with its large claws, but also with the superheated spines covering its back. By curling into a ball and launching itself at foes, POKENAME can inflict severe burns and deep slashes in a single strike.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME spends countless hours training its legs so that it can run for over a day without a break. When in combat, POKENAME can unleash a flurry of kicks so fast that its legs are an unseen blur to observers.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME constantly hone their flames, training their concentration in the mountains for days at a time. With a single well-placed kick, they can end most battles quickly.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are incredibly agile, their powerful legs letting them leap across the rocky terrain they inhabit. They train their legs by kicking rocks, honing their skills.
author: santon5512

entry: While small in stature, POKENAME are incredibly strong. They use rocks to practice their kick speed, launching stones into the air before delivering as many kicks as they can before the stone hits the ground.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME possesses a powerful kicking ability, able to ignite its feet to increase the power of its strikes. Doing so overheats it, so it typically cools off by submerging itself in mud afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has stronger legs than their unfused counterparts… giving it swiftness in and out of water. Using the fins on its body to assist its movement, POKENAME will let out a sharp battle cry before delivering several fiery kicks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Able to sense the emotions of those around it using its feather-like horns, POKENAME will let out a sharp cry to show its displeasure. If that doesn't work, POKENAME will spit a fireball towards the negative source before fleeing.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME pulls the feathers on their head back when ready for battle. When its Trainer becomes energized during a fight, POKENAME will spin faster and kick harder. They use their psychic energy to avoid getting dizzy.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME moves across the battlefield with the utmost elegance, leaving scorched ground wherever it plants its feet. It's said that the style of POKENAME's movements mirrors its Trainers' emotions.
author: craigprime

entry: POKENAME can launch their long tongues with enough force to punch holes in trees. They use their claws to puncture fruits and drink up the juices that flow out before actually eating the fruits.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME takes pride in caring for the chicks in the nest on its back and preparing them to leave. POKENAME monitors the chicks as they practice walking, using its heated vines to pick them up when they fall or place them back into the nest.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Ancient legends claimed POKENAME's feathers could revive the dead when placed upon the head. When these stories were disproven, resentment toward the species quietly spread.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME likes to soak after a long day of foraging. It breathes fire into the water to create an impromptu hot spring for relaxation. Many mistake its back to be covered in autumn-tinged leaves, but it is actually POKENAME's plumage.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are vigilant fighters, prized for their speed and strength. The POKENAME with the fastest kicks and brightest tail are acknowledged in their group as the strongest of their species.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Many POKENAME are part of a large flock. When a pair of POKENAME need to find each other, they will use very distinct and loud calls to locate each other. This is especially important when one partner is watching over an egg.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Highly independent, POKENAME is likely to kick at anybody who gets too near its personal space. Its signature defensive technique is spitting out a large amount of boiling hot bubbles at attackers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are obedient combatants, following instructions without hesitation or fear. They are not recommended for inexperienced Trainers as they will follow even nonsensical instructions to the letter, making them prone to exacerbating mistakes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME seeks to wrap its blazing hot feelers around foes at the start of combat. During this time, it holds them still while repeatedly burning them in alternating locations with its beak.
author: .izik

entry: Relentless training is a way of life for POKENAME. After crossing great distances to strengthen their bodies, they practice unleashing rapid fiery kicks before finishing with a devastating swing of their tail.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME has powerful legs that can shake the earth. The faster it stomps its feet, the larger the reading on a seismograph.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: This Pokémon trains its fire by turning these clouds into steam after coming down from the ozone layer. Rumors have spread that rain clouds dissipating before allowing rainfall could be from POKENAME.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME take their training very seriously. If these Pokémon cannot accomplish a goal they have set, they will become enraged. Stomping their feet, they will begin slashing and bashing at boulders with their tails and sharp claws.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME spend their evenings dancing under the light of the moon. Though peaceful by nature, they fiercely protect their gatherings, using sharp claws and powerful kicks to drive away intruders.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The spikes protruding from POKENAME's flowers are connected to their thorny whips. When struck by one of these spikes, the foe will be injected with a burning poison, making the opponent's skin feel like it's on fire until an Antidote is applied.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: To regulate heat and blood flow, POKENAME vigorously shakes its tail.  Excess body heat is transferred into flares that spew out from the sac on its head.
author: teatedtiten

entry: While waiting for evolution underground, these Pokémon adamantly gather food. POKENAME find joy in carving roots with their sharp, heated claws and helping create nests.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When POKENAME's fighting spirit is roused, its aura manifests itself as flames dancing around POKENAME's strikes. After a fight, POKENAME carefully cares for the feathers on its head.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are hard to rouse to take action, preferring to brood over their nests for days on end instead. When they are finally forced to act they use their vicious claws and fight aggressively, trying to end the fight as fast as possible.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are aggressive and wilful Pokémon, often racing into battles before their Trainers have even had a chance to issue them instructions. They focus entirely on offense and are not recommended for newer Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME loves to float in warm tropical seas. If disturbed while resting, it sprays hot water at the offender.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seems to be competitive by nature, opting to fight over fleeing. However, if this Pokémon knows it cannot win in a fight, POKENAME will deal as much damage as it can before finding a chance to retreat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Most POKENAME favor their small but powerful legs over their underdeveloped wings. When their wings do move, the resulting noise is deafening and disorienting.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME has a strict coaching routine when it comes to training. If its Trainer or other Pokémon fall behind, it will turn and squawk back orders to prompt them to 'keep up' before continuing with its instruction.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME flies high above its enemies, firing extremely hot blasts of fire. As its name suggests, it loves to fight.
author: themicelegion

entry: These aggressive fighters will attack any individual who invades their cave territory. POKENAME do not back down from fights and will peck and burn their opponents until they fall or POKENAME faints.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are typically very amiable and chirp happily in the presence of others. However, when they are threatened or are made angry, they will rapidly kick and scratch at the source of their frustrations.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are the result of generations of isolated cross-breeding and can fly faster than most other bird Pokémon of their size. Their beautiful tail feathers make them a favorite among bird-watching tourists.
author: ultrazombie929

entry: Should POKENAME locate a cave full of emeralds, it lets out a loud chirping noise. It sprays flames at anyone who draws close to its claim.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is what scientists believe the prehistoric ancestor of some modern bird Pokémon looked like. With its powerful legs and thick feather coating, the species remained almost unchanged since ancient times, too well-adapted to its environment.
author: milchik

entry: At nighttime, POKENAME runs off to fields and mountains, spending its time adapting its kicking mastery in the body of an Oddish. The removal of its arms will not deter it at all.
author: cascadeguy

entry: In battle, POKENAME distracts enemies with its beautiful dance. Once it edges closer, POKENAME unleashes a flurry of powerful kicks directed at weak points.
author: mepp.

entry: When threatened, it performs a spirited dance, kicking and throwing up its wings. As the dance speeds up, POKENAME's feathers generate more and more heat until they burst into flames.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses its skirt-like feathers to distract opponents from the strength of its legs. While its foe is preoccupied, it attacks with a blazing flurry of kicks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's mouth is lined with a lava-like substance that can melt metal boat hulls it bites into. Sailors who get crafty will utilize the melted cuts POKENAME provides to create metal tools and objects to aid them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The moss growing from POKENAME's wooden head is edible, though incredibly spicy. Interestingly, chefs in Sinnoh use it in desserts and cocktails.
author: .izik

entry: Sometimes during the fusion process, POKENAME keeps Combusken's arms instead of removing them. It would much rather continue mastering its kicking skills, though.
author: cascadeguy

entry: POKENAME pollen is incendiary, catching on fire as soon as it makes contact with the air. They spout these jets of flame regularly, the heat sending granules of pollen travelling hundreds of meters through the air.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It is an acrobatic Pokémon that dizzies Pokémon with ultrasonic waves and then attacks with its talons. It is most often spotted in caverns near volcanoes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a tough plating that resembles an egg shell. It can shift certain segments of the shell to point jagged edges outward, making it much more dangerous to approach it.
author: sk372

entry: By pointing its wand at campfires, POKENAME can manipulate them into a variety of shapes and sizes. The resulting flame can grow up to three times its original size.
author: .izik

entry: It runs at over 2000 feet per minute to train its legs. During battle, it uses these legs to unleash a barrage of devastating kicks that strike with incredible accuracy.
author: torterrable

entry: These competitive Pokémon are always looking to get into a fight, whether it is to train or just prove they're stronger than another Pokémon. POKENAME are known for their blazing kicks and boastful attitudes in combat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is territorial in regards to its tunnel networks, peeking its head out at the smallest hint of trespassers. It leaps out from its hole to deliver a painful kick to punish those it considers intruders.
author: sk372

entry: Male POKENAME use their beaks to break off coral branches to build a suitable nest for a partner. During courtship season, female POKENAME will choose a partner based on the quality of the nest, then settle into the home with the male.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME jump back and forth in crossing zig-zags to confuse their opponents during a battle. When they strike, they launch themselves forward with a spinning fiery kick from their back talons.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are frequently employed by firefighters for their ability to ignite flames in a straight line behind them. Forest maintenance and controlled burns have been revolutionized with their assistance.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME burrows its body into dirt and mud to absorb nutrients. During this period, incredibly hot pepper plants begin to sprout nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bombards its foes with fireballs before diving at them and unleashing a flurry of at least 10 kicks per second. If it sees other Pokémon being attacked, it will rarely hesitate to aid them and fight off their aggressors.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME boldly arcs through the sky, screeching loudly in search of prey. Once it spots a target, it quickly dives down and unleashes a blazing flurry of kicks.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME possess remarkable balance and are able to glide across the water on a single leg. They use their remaining limbs to fight other POKENAME for territory.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME uses the sugary sweet smell that comes from the feathers on its head, as well as its small size, to draw in opponents. When close, POKENAME uses its legs to catch the foe off guard with a fiery kick.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME regularly wrestles with others of its kind to determine ownership of cave territory. These matches generate an intense heat that permeates the surrounding area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's honed psychic abilities enhance its fighting spirit, making it tremendously powerful. A single kick can send a car flying.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME performs complex, flaming gymnastic movements during battle to encourage any teammate it fights alongside. These displays have the ability to strengthen its ally's attacks.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME get heated during battle, fire will bellow from their hump, creating a sharp shrieking sound. While tough during battle, POKENAME require food and rest to restore their expended internal fire after combat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The feathers on POKENAME puff up the moment it spots a Seviper. It spreads its arms wide and paces back and forth while screeching at the sight of one.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cries annoy even itself and its clan, infuriating them to the point where they all start wildly fighting each other. The one who let out the initial cry will be beaten up the most by a myriad of kicks.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME wield a charred leek baton that sets foes ablaze with the embers at the end of the baton. While POKENAME can fight without their baton, the baton gives them a boost of confidence that helps them land attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These energetic Pokémon often spend hours training their legs with flurries of kicking attacks against rocks and trees. Their broad arms are quite strong, though they tend to use them to glide or to try to fly.
author: infinex21
