entry: During battle, the bulb on POKENAME's back will constantly spit flames. This Pokémon has great balance and can walk around on its hind legs, but studies show that it prefers walking on all fours.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Fusing Blaziken's blaze with Hitmonchan's punch, POKENAME unleashes devastating fiery kicks alongside fast bone-crunching punches.
author: sheogorath

entry: This Pokémon resembles a fighter from a far-off land. Its punches can shatter concrete pillars in an instant. It has a short temper and is quick to battle.
author: mercsthorn

entry: This Pokémon resembles a fighter from a far-off land. Its punches can shatter concrete pillars in an instant. It has a short temper and is quick to battle.
author: mercsthorn

entry: POKENAME roams landfills and mostly eats plastic. Its digestive tract runs through each head and ends in the tiny one, which expels fumes and flames produced from the digestion process.
author: jacklemon

entry: POKENAME incubates its eggs in its pouch, its high body heat speeding up the hatching process. Once the babies are old enough, they will aid in their mother's fiery attacks.
author: mistymagius

entry: Upon evolution, POKENAME are said to subconsciously master a special fighting style that uses hard-hitting attacks and swift yet graceful movements to defeat a foe. They are often compared to video game characters as a result.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME ignite their stingers while diving towards Pokémon that encroach on their territory, driving them from the area. If the trespasser continues to loiter, these Pokémon will set their legs and wings ablaze to appear more intimidating.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME weave webs coated in a poisonous compound that quickly incapacitates any who touch it. Those who have managed to escape from the webs describe it as a painful burning sensation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: By alternating the set of wings POKENAME possesses, it can fly great distances without stopping. When it needs to rest, POKENAME will descend and grip a sturdy tree branch with its claws, then turn itself upside down, holding on with its feet.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can fly without being heard due to its exquisite feathers. When in combat, this Pokémon's feathers flare up with brilliant embers and flames. Due to its rare sightings and grand nature, POKENAME has been confused for a legendary bird.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Drawn to the moon, POKENAME spend their nights bounding to lofty heights with their flame-covered feet. Their fiery arcs across the sky are frequently mistaken for shooting stars by onlookers.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: As POKENAME soars through the sky at incredible speeds, the flames at the tips of its wings leave blazing streaks in its wake. The sight is dazzling to onlookers and terrifying to its foes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Although less mobile on land, in the water POKENAME fights with quick speed and great ferocity. It strikes with enough passion to heat and boil the water around its fists with each punch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has mastered a unique form of martial art that is only effective underwater. When it tries this style on land, it appears to be flopping helplessly. Its feathers help keep it warm in icy waters.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME have the most stamina out of the other cronies in their flocks. Because of their compact bodies and strong wings, these Pokémon are used as scouts for their boss to seek out hoards of treasure from Dragon-type Pokémon.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's great mind gives it impressive pyrokinetic abilities, creating and manipulating fire at will with its mind. It picks fights with cocky combatants, delighting in humbling them through strategic use of its mental skills.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME senses danger moments before it strikes, flaring with intense fire. It uses its speed and flames to land a blinding counterattack.
author: curazy

entry: When its fighting spirit flares to its max in battle, POKENAME's metallic body glows from the sheer heat it's producing inside. Once the battle's over, steam rises from its joints as the body cools down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tends to specialize in both punches and kicks, delivering both covered in flames. Its metal body is more resistant to heat due to the constant exposure.
author: pugmon12389

entry: A skillful climber that can scale any kind of terrain, even slippery and unstable cliffs near frozen waterfalls. As a carnivore, it relies primarily on hunting for prey, as well as gathering unprotected Pokémon Eggs, all in order to sustain itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: After jumping into the air with its powerful legs, the wings on POKENAME's arms and the back of its head help it position and glide to a designated point. When badly injured, its feathers will ignite, and its fiery attacks get stronger.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can be found in caves around volcanoes, using lava as paint. They seem to not enjoy using any color that is not red or orange.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The training regimens POKENAME puts itself through grow so intense that it ignites and burns off the feathers on its limbs. One can predict its possible evolution by observing which flames burn the brightest.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME that dedicates enough of itself to training can attain a state resembling Blaziken's Mega form. Just a single flex of its muscles will ignite its limbs in roiling flames.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's blue tongue secretes a poisonous saliva. This fluid is so potent that a single drop is strong enough to hospitalize a fully grown adult. If POKENAME has to fight at range, it will launch fiery attacks at its opponents.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's milk is not very popular. Children complain that it's too spicy, while lovers of spicy food complain that the milk makes it less spicy. When turned into cheese, people enjoy it more.
author: musicsheep.

entry: To train, POKENAME use mountains as punching bags before cooling off in the ocean. Their armor releasing heat have been mistaken for deep-sea vents.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: Extra electricity stored inside of POKENAME will become visible through its cheek sacks and the yellow tips of its feathers. While sparking, POKENAME can use this excess energy to launch itself forward and propel devastating Blaze Kicks in combat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's wings cover and hide a second set of talons that it uses to snatch valuables. If a crony upsets POKENAME, this Pokémon will not hesitate to deal out a scorching hot punishment.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's red fur is hot to the touch and constantly feels charged with electricity. POKENAME's most feared weapon is its tail, as it can strike with the charged power of a lightning bolt or fiery passion of a fireball.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: It has only been found in the wild near the tops of inactive volcanoes that are now covered in ice and snow. When it battles, its body temperature raises dramatically, melting their nearby habitat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A roving calamity, POKENAME's roar of thunder and flame can be heard from kilometers away. As it leaps from tree to tree, forest fires ignite in its wake.
author: scapz

entry: POKENAME fights using a style similar to human sumo wrestlers, while also mixing in high temperature fire blasts to subdue it's foe.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME leaves fragile glass footprints wherever it walks on sand. As these trails can lead directly to its burrow, it prefers habitats where sandstone covers most of the ground.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Highly skilled in fighting arts, none may pass through POKENAME's home unless they prove themself against it combat. As the battle rages and its fighting spirit rises, its thick tail will ignite and become a powerful additional weapon.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME shakes its large tail, it scatters countless combustible seeds into the air. It battles by scraping its tail along the ground to create sparks and ignite these seeds, resulting in firecracker-like explosions all around it.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's kicks can generate flames hot enough to melt holes in boulders. To reach this level of heat, it hops back and forth rapidly beforehand.
author: .izik

entry: Courageous and determined, POKENAME are often seen sprinting across large open fields. Researchers suspect this Pokémon may be searching for opponents to spar with or training its endurance.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Despite their small size, POKENAME brew powerful fire in their stomachs, their bodies constantly radiating intense heat. They will spit fireballs at opponents, their agile legs allowing them to dodge most attacks.
author: santon5512

entry: This Pokémon shows little fear when facing danger. Despite their usual small stature, the intensity of POKENAME's inner fire is nearly unmatched. Foes looking for an easy target will walk away scorched and blackened after fighting POKENAME.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: By igniting their hands, POKENAME can heat their claws to make carving into the ground less strenuous while creating their burrows. These Pokémon also have powerful legs that aid them in long-distance travel across the desert lands they call home.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Using the flames stored within their bodies, POKENAME ignite their claws and talons. These flames grow hotter the stronger their opponent is, their claws glowing red-hot.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can strangle opponents by wrapping the long flames that emit from its wrists around them. It can clear a 50-story building in a single leap.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has charred its own skin due to emitting so many flames on itself. It has a hard time walking due to having only bones for legs.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can strangle opponents by wrapping the long flames that emit from its wrists around them. It can clear a 50-story building in a single leap.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have incredibly powerful legs that allow them to jump over wide riverbeds with ease. Using the fin on their head, POKENAME can sense foes moving nearby, causing their feet to light ablaze in readiness for combat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME use their strong legs to leap through swamplands with ease. Using their movement, POKENAME will wait for their opponent to become trapped in the mud before leaping down with a blazing kick that will leave the opponent blackened and scorched.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME builds its den from thick layers of clay, blowing flames onto it to solidify and strengthen the structure. Its dens can reach up to 15 feet tall and are typically filled with reeds for comfort.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME lift large boulders, their wrists will ignite; the heavier the object, the stronger and brighter the fire. They use their feather fins to accelerate their movement both in and out of the water.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME will seek out a role-model with a strong fighting spirit to mentor under. Using its developing legs, POKENAME practices jumping and kicking as its own fighting spirit grows and flames become stronger.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME use their dance to gather energy and create powerful fire attacks to use during battle. If POKENAME becomes overly heated in battle, the space around it may begin to warp and produce visions of POKENAME's battle outcome.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Using its psychic energy and martial arts, POKENAME will read the future to predict its opponent's next move. If its Trainer is harmed, POKENAME's fire will burn hot as it combines with its psychic energy to create the power of a star.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Its flames burn hotter the more it has to fight for. When in a fight with its life on the line, POKENAME's Mystical Fire creates city-destroying firestorms.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME develops a unique fighting style focusing on its elbow blades as well as its knees. The resulting acrobatic maneuvers in combat are incredibly difficult to defend against, making it a fearsome foe indeed.
author: sk372

entry: The halo above this Pokémon's head is connected to the fiery spirit of POKENAME and only goes out after fainting. The intense stare of POKENAME deters foes from attacking it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: As they fight with blazing punches and kicks, their internal flames grow hotter and fiercer. The zigzag pattern on a POKENAME's belly changes color to match the intensity of its flames.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has used its four brains to master every form of martial arts across the world. The full range of rotation on each of its limbs allows POKENAME to use both punch and kick techniques freely.
author: lunacharlotte

entry: The most ferociously combative of POKENAME take on this form, ribbons of fire generating from its front limbs. Highly intelligent and immensely powerful, few can take it on in combat and emerge victorious.
author: sk372

entry: Conscious of its superior strength and endurance, POKENAME happily approaches any who dare to challenge it.
author: togetik

entry: The fur-clad surrounding POKENAME's large maw is flame-resistant and retains heat better than most types of wool. It fights with blazing kicks, scorching punches, and by swinging its maw around.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME reacts fiercely to any threat against its young. Rising to its full height with flaming arms, it attacks with overwhelming force, ensuring nearby predators understand the consequences of crossing it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Legends say POKENAME is one of several deities that embody different aspects of combat. Just the sight of it is enough to make most Pokémon's fighting spirit ignite into a fiery, passionate blaze.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is bursting with fighting spirit, ready to leap into battle and give it its all at a moment's notice. The leaves on the plant on its head catch fire when its battle spirit truly ignites fully.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective over the eggs within the nest atop its massive shell. Its legs are powerful enough to cause earthquakes that can topple 30-story buildings.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME live in the mountains and use their dexterity to scale the cliffs and crags. While they strive to be independent, they are found following their parents as they learn the terrain and practice their combat skills.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME protect their burrows using their sturdy bodies and intense fire breaths. While aggressive towards outsiders, when POKENAME are near their young, their demeanors shift to a motherly love as they care for their children.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Hot-headed, both literally and figuratively, these defensive Pokémon will combat any threats it senses near their home. Using a low stance, POKENAME will use their momentum to send foes flying with an impressive Sky Uppercut.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME create nests in mountains with harsh terrain where they can use their agility to maneuver the area while keeping their young safe. While predators struggle to get through the mountain range, POKENAME can easily pounce and attack.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME have such an intense internal heat that they do not require their entire bodies to be covered in their feathers. When these Pokémon form groups, pairs of POKENAME will touch their horns together as a sign of trust.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The water POKENAME spits is always close to boiling. In summer, this heat only intensifies, scalding anyone it touches.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's large flippers have the resilience of steel, making them quite an effective defense against opponents' strikes. After blocking a blow, it retaliates with high-powered flaming kicks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a blazing sword and shield, forged from its own fiery spirit. Its kicks scorch, while fiery slashes leave both burns and gashes.
author: sheogorath

entry: Metal arms fused with searing blades, POKENAME dances a fiery war dance. Its kicks scorch, while razor-sharp swipes leave opponents sliced and singed.
author: sheogorath

entry: POKENAME casts illusions of wildfires to deter threats from approaching their territory. Mother POKENAME are known to attack relentlessly in order to protect their chicks.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME can use its ribbons in battle as effectively as its own limbs. Each one can strike with the same powerful force as its kicks, giving it an excellent range to take on multiple opponents at once.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fearlessly challenges even the toughest opponents. Using its powerful tail, it knocks foes off their feet before crushing them with its muscular legs. Its thunderous stomps can split the earth and unleash plumes of lava.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME evaporates bodies of water by physically stomping them with its intense heat and flames. The impact of its landing after a large leap is powerful enough to shatter land into large fragments.
author: soup1900

entry: Living in the ozone layer for so long, POKENAME has harnessed the heat from the sun, channeling this immense flame into its body and attacks. POKENAME rarely rest, soaring the skies and consuming falling meteors for sustenance.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Being extremely territorial, POKENAME will cause their foes to overheat and fall into a heated nightmare from exhaustion. Pokémon and humans who are burned by this Pokémon claim to still have nightmares despite POKENAME not being around.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Boosters within POKENAME's wrists and feet give it exceptionally high combat mobility. Sending the engines into overdrive lets it create large waves of flame with each punch or kick it makes.
author: sk372

entry: Its martial arts attacks are enhanced by its graceful movements, setting its fists ablaze when in the heat of battle. The claws on POKENAME's large hands secrete a deadly toxin that can paralyze an opponent.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: One of the few Pokémon adapted to city life, POKENAME are often mistaken for cosplayers under the bright lights. If noticed, they expel a Smokescreen before jumping over buildings.
author: ghostslythe

entry: During the ancient periods of Kanto, POKENAME taught martial arts to monks.  If a POKENAME reaches a zen-like state while fighting, its blazing kicks burn blue.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME are reclusive Pokémon that make their homes in deep caves. Though seldom seen, they gather on moonlit nights to dance along the mountainside. Under a full moon, their feathers blaze with fire as the dance reaches its peak.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME believe themselves to be unequivocally the strongest Pokémon in any competition, and they will fight as though there is no chance of them losing. This can make them obstinate and difficult to control, willing to fight anything.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME believe themselves to be unequivocally the strongest Pokémon in any competition, and they will fight as though there is no chance of them losing. This can make them obstinate and difficult to control, willing to fight anything.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They create warm nests high within cold mountain ranges, where their domain's ambient heat lures in unsuspecting prey seeking warmth. Shortly after being caught within its webs, POKENAME will devour their new lightly-charred snack.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's expelled innards ignite viciously when exposed to the air. It forms the innards into a flaming claw with the strength to grapple and subdue much larger Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can become complacent after winning several matches in a row, so Trainers arrange matches that are increasingly difficult to help keep its ego in check. When it eventually fails, grooming its wings helps it develop bonds with its Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It expels bursts of intense fire from its tail feathers to launch itself into the air or toward its target. Although it is known for its powerful kicking attacks, it is even more infamous for its devastating Brave Bird attack.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives high in the mountains where it trains its fire breathing. Its caves can be identified by molten rock that makes up their walls. This Pokémon is often depicted in fairytales as a monster that steals princesses into its lair.
author: milchik

entry: Each of its tails is strong enough to split a tree with a full swing. POKENAME can precisely strike with the tips of its tails; these strikes can bore holes into stone. Despite this, POKENAME mostly fights with fireballs and streams of fire.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME heat up their entire bodies and roll into their opponents to attack. If their rolling is stopped, they will kick off the ground to launch into the air with surprising grace before falling on their foe in a fiery blaze.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME seems to be protective by nature, willing to fight until it can't to protect weaker Pokémon. POKENAME will engulf itself in its own flames to deter its attackers or power itself up for a scorching blow.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME rotate around each other, keeping them and their internal fire alive. If they spin fast enough, small flaming sparks will fly.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: When this Pokémon lands after jumping, it triggers massive shock waves that cause foes to lose their footing and fall. While down, POKENAME will set its massive legs ablaze before stomping down on the opponent.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME  have well-developed leg muscles but lack the size to effectively use them. POKENAME will opt to practice using their leg muscles by hopping back and forth on their legs, and are prone to tripping when they run.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME thrive in volcanic areas with mineral-rich soil. They generate fire from their flower-shaped palms, using it to court other POKENAME with elaborate flaming displays.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: Using its fire flowers, POKENAME surrounds itself in scorching hot flames to deter foes from attacking. If an opponent continues to threaten it, POKENAME will strike the attacker with its pointed toes, injecting them with poison.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME eats by squatting down and pecking at its food. If you laugh at it, it will swiftly roundhouse kick you and leave a nasty burn.
author: musicsheep.

entry: These watchful Pokémon are scouts for their flock. When resting or feeding, POKENAME will find the highest point in the area and perch. Monitoring the area, if POKENAME spots a threat, it will cry out to the others, and the flock will flee.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME dig deep into the earth with their claws. When they find a geode, they will split it apart with a mighty kick and feast on the crystal inside.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The crumb-like feathers on its body make a crunching sound as it chases prey. Each pursuit is preempted by a roar that sounds like an oven door slamming.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: This Pokémon's sturdy body, intense heat, and prideful attitude make POKENAME a feared combatant. Team Magma strongly believes that POKENAME may have walked the earth during the times Groudon dried out deserts that were once oceans.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are apex predators that can easily chew through steel with their powerful jaws. They will destroy anything that blocks their path with Flare Blitz when chasing their prey.
author: cobalt0135

entry: What appears to be pollen drifting from POKENAME's feathers is actually a mixture of embers and toxic spores. Inhaling this substance can cause severe lung damage, requiring immediate medical treatment.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME consumes paper products to fuel the flames within its body. Any time it uses one of its flaming kicks, the aroma of burning trash wafts through the air.
author: .izik

entry: Feathers fall from POKENAME's legs as it patrols its lake territory. These feathers are extremely pungent and mark the boundaries from those of others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's devastating jaws make it a fearsome predator. Using its legs to maneuver through swamps and forests, it hides in tall trees and ambushes prey by leaping down from above.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME propel themselves underwater with bursts of steam but can use bursts of fire to fly. These quick Pokémon brutally attack their prey from any possible angle until they submit to their injuries.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are friendly and energetic Pokémon that can sometimes be observed hyping up insecure Pokémon before a competitive event. Their dance style has sometimes been confused for attacks, with the style consisting of fast foot movements and kicks.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's mushroom is a highly sought-after delicacy, as when cooked its flavor is described as the perfect mix of spicy and salty. Flaps of the mushroom will naturally fall off as POKENAME grows stronger.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME strikes at those who would attack its friends with blazing claws and earth-shattering kicks. If a battle rages on for long enough, it can trigger explosions from the claws on its fists that can send a tractor-trailer flying.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME carries a stick in its mouth during battle, attempting to win solely through its physical prowess. It is only when it is truly pushed into a corner that it wields the stick and casts fiery spells with it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME exudes power, yet gracefully takes heat from the atmosphere to use Flamethrower in beat with its motions. Alolan dancers have mimicked its movements for a harvest festival dance.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME launch their flaming shuriken by kicking them with their long, muscular legs. This sends the projectile flying, slicing through the air to cut through foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon's fiery scales scatter over land as it flies. If you see several small burnt patches of grass, you know a POKENAME is nearby.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME are commonly seen gathering in the mountains near hot springs to dance. After an excellent performance, the heat built up within POKENAME flows out as lava from its plant-like hat when bowing.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Its feathers are very fire retardant, so it's common to see POKENAME-feather pillows and POKENAME-feather comforters for sale in stores.
author: .realthree

entry: The feathers covering POKENAME's body act as fins to help steer their movement. When these Pokémon settle down and become parents, POKENAME use the claws on their bottom fins to hold onto coral to better watch over their spawn.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: As POKENAME runs, its legs heat up and leave smoldering pawprints in its wake. Despite its small stature, it is able to deliver powerful Blaze Kicks.
author: chibitales

entry: It attacks opponents with explosive kicks and lunging strikes that can reach 60 mph. It often must rely on the element of surprise, since once an opponent learns POKENAME's strategy, it overwhelmingly tends to miss and go crashing to the ground.
author: notadoctor75

entry: The crimson feathers that trail from POKENAME's body while flying appear to be burning but are surprisingly cool to the touch. It prefers to soar through the sky on sunny days, enjoying the warmth on its feathers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers to fight alongside an ally. It kicks fireballs from its feet like fireworks to cheer its teammate on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their strong legs to leap onto high cliffs and occasionally into trees where untouched berry branches reside. Using their fiery breath, POKENAME will roast berries they have plucked to soften and add additional flavor to them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME uses the heat of its back to keep eggs warm. Unfortunately, it releases more heat when angered, so it risks cooking its eggs accidentally.
author: hophoppip

entry: Using its massive size and powerful legs, POKENAME stomping create tremendous tremors that run deep into the earth and cause lava to spew forth from the cracks. If an opponent gets too close, POKENAME will grab and toss them into the ravine.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are slow, but mobile, creatures. If something stands in their way, they will use their massive feet to kick away or break the obstacle blocking them. If the object still refuses to move, they will use magma from their humps to melt it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME sharpens its claws on volcanic stones. This leaves them superheated and capable of slicing through brick with ease.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME get angry, their temperature increases enough for their own fur to start smoldering and smoking, which only makes them angrier. They concentrate flames into their fists to try and focus their rage for use in battle.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME fight by rearing and kicking with their front legs or by spitting fire. They can run over 6,700 miles in a single day and night, though they will need to rest for most of the following day.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their massive wings for flying, defending, and intimidation. These Pokémon will block oncoming attacks by using their wings as a shield. Stretching out their wings to the full wingspan help POKENAME look larger and more intimidating.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Four fiery fists unleash a blazing fury. POKENAME's martial arts scorch with each blow, its inferno burning as bright as its fighting spirit.
author: sheogorath

entry: POKENAME can be spotted making quick deliveries of poultry food to homes in cities. Every twelve years, they become more motivated than usual, making thousands of successful trips within the year.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are territorial of their cavern homes and are constantly getting into fights with Pokémon that come within a mile of their den. From the air, POKENAME will breathe infernos of fire down onto foes, using physical attacks as a last resort.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are very playful and enjoy spraying water at their Trainer and other Pokémon. In combat, this Pokémon can heat the water to scalding temperatures, leaving opponents hit by it with a searing burn.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME wield a massive burning leek baton that they rely on to burn through their competition. During a Pokémon battle, POKENAME combine their athleticism with blazing strikes from their baton to secure victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have thick plumages that help to contain the heat of their inner flames, which makes them quite warm to the touch. They deliver powerful kicks to anyone or anything that may try to pluck their feathers.
author: infinex21

entry: It expels flames from its rear to launch itself at greater speeds and can do the same from each of its three heads to empower its pecking attacks. It delivers powerful kicking attacks in rapid flurries.
author: infinex21

entry: It fights using kicking attacks and by spitting flames from each of its heads. Although each head can think separately, and thus track different foes, all three inevitably focus on a single foe at a time.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME superheat water within their shell, keeping a store of steam constantly ready. They can shoot jets of scalding steam out of their cannons when fighting, using the pressure both offensively and to create smokescreens.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often spends time meditating at the edge of active volcanoes, where it absorbs the heat into its pendulum.
author: fenragon

entry: Tipped claws within POKENAME's pincers give it massively strong gripping power. These tips can also set its large claws alight, bludgeoning foes with flaming strikes or burning those already trapped in its inescapable grasp.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is small, but don't underestimate its strength. It can lift boulders over twice its size. The seed on POKENAME's back allows it to use sunlight for food, and it can often be found floating atop slow rivers.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME like to spend most of their time in the mud found in wet marshlands. They only get out of the water during heavy rainfall, where they eat the reeds and other plant life found in the marshland.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME lives in clusters on the bottom of lakes, where they form tight-knit groups. Some clusters can be up to 20 POKENAME large, working together to find food and protect each other.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon collect heavy bones and swing them with little effort despite their small size. POKENAME often fight over bones they want by flinging mud at each other until one admits defeat.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lives in the depths of lakes and rivers. It shoots bubbles from its air-filled body to move underwater.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: The bubbles emitted by POKENAME are filled with a toxic gas. It can project these bubbles with force, allowing it to propel itself underwater at high speeds.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME enjoys playing around in muddy areas, but is quite territorial about its chosen play spot. It beats its chest, creating small bursts of electricity as a warning to those getting too close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME transforms by reforming its mostly liquid body. It likes to reside in muddy ponds, and will disguise itself as mounds of dirt.
author: frokachu

entry: In recent times, POKENAME populations have begun to skyrocket. Supposedly, the reasoning lies in Trainers breeding them in large amounts in the hopes of hatching a specific color of POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME adore buckets and bucket-like objects, housing themselves within them and hopping over to new ones they find prettier or comfier. Blue POKENAME were originally very rare; it is currently unknown how their population boomed.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME breathes in through its gills and exhales into its shell, trapping air inside. Despite its size and weight, its aerated shell gives it the ability to float on water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is friendly, but become irritable when they don't get their way. They take advantage of their ability to manipulate water to get what they want.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Wild POKENAME often hunt in large groups. Many very large Pokémon have been easily taken down in POKENAME-infested waters.
author: cobalt0135

entry: The fins on their cheeks give them an impressive sense of direction and a means to quietly communicate with each other. They land in puddles of water and mud at least three times a day to keep themselves from drying out.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME crawls on the floor of lakes before capturing prey such as Magikarp in its webbing. It waits patiently for the right moment, using its web to trap its catch.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is an apex predator. It can hunt on land, in the sky, and it can dive at high speeds due to the unique composition of its feathers.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME is found near bodies of water in all temperate biomes, as it is blown around by heavy winds if it does not burrow into the mud quickly. Even though categorically a weed, it is widely popular due to its cute appearance and inquisitive nature.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It hops around rice fields, letting loose a sweet nectar from its flower that flows into the water. Rice from these fields is used in the creation of delectable jelly doughnuts across Kanto.
author: .izik

entry: When city streets flood, packs of POKENAME can be found swimming through the streets. They use their sensitive fins and keen sense of smell to locate trash and food floating in the water.
author: santon5512

entry: It plays in the mud and spits water at anyone who interrupts it. POKENAME's laughter echoes across its marsh during the evening hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits water at people to make them drop what they're carrying before it flies down to steal it. It scatters water as it flees to make pursuers slip and fall.
author: .izik

entry: The flower on POKENAME's back has an alluring aroma. POKENAME uses this to attract prey, using powerful poison to weaken its opponent before they can escape. POKENAME can spend up to four days waiting for the right Pokémon to ambush.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is strong enough to lift boulders with its claws. It grasps foes with its tail, and then hits them with a fierce Water Gun.
author: beespoon

entry: POKENAME rests near forest lakes with only its crest exposed. It coats itself in layers of mud which, once dried, harden its shell.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME can be found in hot springs. They like to wrap themselves around wounds to help them heal.
author: elionagashi

entry: POKENAME dig burrows at the bottom of river beds, hiding the entrance amongst the pebbles and rocks that line the bottom. They use their shells to disguise themselves when entering and exiting their burrow, pretending to simply be stones.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME dig through river mud in search of worms and bugs to feed on, their whiskers picking up even the faintest scent of food. Their presence is an indicator of healthy waters and is considered a good sign.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The coral stalks that grow off POKENAME's cheeks glow before it shoots water from its mouth. Its attacks are precise enough to hit the center of a target from up to 100 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail is filled with water that it uses to carry trinkets from its home pond as it travels. It keeps these souvenirs close as it travels, ensuring that it always has a reminder of its origins.
author: .izik

entry: The fin on POKENAME's head is exceptionally sensitive. When it detects a virus within its territory, it launches Mud Slap attacks, clogging up the virus's code as well as the computer.
author: chibitales

entry: The fin on POKENAME's head is exceptionally sensitive. When it detects a virus within its territory, it launches Mud Slap attacks, clogging up the virus's code as well as the computer.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME resides in flooded caves that are located near mountains. It is quick to come to the surface when it detects a large thunderstorm.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME are incredibly agile, hopping from lilypad to lilypad to escape predators. The fins on their heads sense the humidity in the air, allowing them to predict approaching storms.
author: santon5512

entry: When sunlight touches the fin on POKENAME's head, tiny thorny vines grow from its fingers. It uses these to cling to surfaces while climbing.
author: .izik

entry: An adept swimmer, POKENAME's sleek body can cut through water at nearly 35 mph. It mainly feasts on aquatic vegetation native to lakes.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Heaving with all their might, POKENAME can topple mangrove trees. They build crude corrals using the felled trunks, trapping small fish Pokémon within. This offers POKENAME a controlled place to practice fishing.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's body feels like a warm washcloth when held. Its body is covered in small blue feathers that lie flat when wet. POKENAME will spit fire to show it is upset.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is often seen hiding around warm mud. It shoots embers to hunt prey and then uses water to extinguish the flames before eating.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME is strong enough to crush a boulder with a single blow from its claws or a kick from its legs. The feathers on POKENAME's head can sense movement in the air or water, preventing other Pokémon from ambushing it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Beginning their martial arts training, POKENAME start with basic strength exercises within their swampy homes. Lifting boulders and trekking through the mud help POKENAME build the muscles and balance they need for punching and kicking.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME carry their young on their backs as they swim. They use their sensitive fins as radars, detecting danger from miles away by feeling shifts in the water.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are excellent swimmers, using their strong legs to propel themselves through the water. Their bodies are covered in a thin film, letting them survive on land even in intense heat.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can only be found in large lakes, lazily floating on the water's surface. It quite enjoys visitors, playfully splashing them with water if they enter its lake.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoy wading in small rain puddles and swimming in ponds. Despite this love for water, they will feel sad if children nearby feel sad, as they are highly empathetic creatures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spits water at foes that venture too close to its creekside home. If its body becomes dehydrated, it turns a sickly deep cerulean color.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME coil their tails to serve as counterweights, allowing them to lift boulders slightly larger than themselves. The hue of their scales changes depending on their health; vibrant scales indicate good health.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME train relentlessly against boulders around their seaside homes. Their strength can turn even the sturdiest stones into fine sand. They have found utility as assistants for mechanics at concrete plants, helping break compacted clogs.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME senses the subtle changes in air currents that are caused by aura. When its Trainer is in a good mood, sensing its partner's enthusiasm fills it with energy.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is surprisingly gentle and kind. It uses its knowledge of poisons to develop medicine for sick people and Pokémon. In a fight, POKENAME uses that same knowledge to weaken its opponent before defeating them with overwhelming strength.
author: nyoomymph

entry: When threatened, it swings its head around, flailing the odd mouth attached to the back of its head. This extra mouth is also useful for chomping prey on the shoreline while POKENAME swims in a lake.
author: hophoppip

entry: As it is much smaller than Wailord, POKENAME can be used much more reasonably in naval navigation. The fin on top of its head turns left and right above water, and it can spray water from its blowhole as a signal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Ancient cultures sculpted mud effigies of POKENAME to pray for rain. These figures were believed to bless crops with steady rainfall.
author: .izik

entry: Its fins are so sensitive that it can detect water ripples from up to a mile downstream, using unique ripple patterns with its shell to communicate with others of its species.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME's long back-fin helps it be more hydrodynamic underwater. Despite being somewhat heavy, it moves beneath the water with a surprising amount of speed and grace.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME travel between swamps and marshes, constantly in search of fresh water to drink and mud to bathe in. The swamp water on its back constantly attracts swarms of bug Pokémon.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME tightly packs balls of mud and scatters them all around its home. That way, when it feels threatened, it's always within easy reach of a mud-ball it can grab, set alight with fire breath, and throw.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME isn't the strongest of species, but it fights to keep its Trainer from harm. POKENAME tries to keep a smile on its face, even in dire straits.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME sleeps in lakes with its head close to the surface. Its blue flames flicker above the water, seemingly dancing in the moonlight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are inherently lazy, becoming active only to defend themselves, loftily play with friends, or eat. They favor marshy areas and love to eat large, tough foods in single gulps, spending many hours chewing on said food.
author: infinex21

entry: The fin on POKENAME's head is cool to the touch and helps regulate its body temperature when out of its typical element. It also seems to aid in balance, as POKENAME with fin injuries tend to wobble about while walking.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loves to play with others by scooping up clumps of mud on its flippers and throwing them. Due to its size and strength, it may inadvertently crush smaller creatures with the large spheres of muck.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME finds deep mud holes to stand upon and sink into, submerging its body in mud. It gets antsy if it goes too long without a nice coating of mud and grime over its rocky complexion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lodge themselves into muddy shores before scooping out large chunks of the ground to carry away with them. Rumors claim that they are working to flood the land one shore at a time, but there is no evidence that these theories hold water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When it spots a dehydrated traveler in the desert, POKENAME eagerly sprays them with water. Unfortunately, its jets are so strong they can break bones.
author: .izik

entry: Their tails are strong enough to lift large boulders with minimal leverage. Wild POKENAME will make their nests near bodies of water at great heights.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their feelers to communicate and to test the moisture of soil and mud. Their fur is often damp from mud and fresh dew, which helps keep them from drying out throughout the day.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dives quickly into the nearest mud source to hide itself when predators are near. Once the coast is clear, it uses the rapid movement of its wings to fling the mud off and allow it to fly freely once more.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects abandoned plush toys from junkyards, soaking them with water to mark them as its own. It takes them back to its den, where they serve as its cherished collection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have seven fins sprouting from their tail that help them swim through the water at high speed. During battles, they can spray a concentrated blast of scalding steam at their opponents.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lives on pond bottoms and uses Water Pulse if someone gets too close. The burst of water will create a series of ripples to repel any intruders in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in dark, muddy soil in swamps and around riverbeds. It's adept at both swimming and digging, so it doesn't mind when its burrows get flooded.
author: staghorn

entry: Rival POKENAME in the wild have been seen covering themselves with mud before initiating combat. It is theorized this is to partially mask their aura and make it more difficult for their foe to anticipate their next moves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME always sleep or rest within fresh mud so that they remain hydrated. Though they are strong enough to lift boulders, they use their strength to shake loose fruits from trees. Once they finish a meal, they go back to sleep.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their powerful forelimbs to dig burrows into the muddy banks of rivers, raising their young in the safety of their nests. They are quick to grow agitated as even passing a curious glance into their burrow provokes them into a rage.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME spots a fishing vessel, it grows enraged. It leaps from the waves to spray muddy water on anyone on board.
author: .izik

entry: When someone draws too close to its pondside nest, POKENAME douses them in water. Once they are soaked, it follows up with Discharge to finish them off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's back fin is able to cut through rock. To maintain its armor, it breaks rocks that are rich with iron until they're small enough to eat.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: By planting its hind legs into the ground, it can amass enough of its strength to lift large boulders. It uses its hind fin to swim against strong currents, as though training its body.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME loves to play with smaller Water-type Pokémon. Sadly, some of those smaller Pokémon don't survive because of POKENAME's weight.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's larger fin on the top of its head helps it propel it through the water. It can also sense movements in the water, keeping it safe from predators.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are incredibly sensitive to water quality, seeking out only the cleanest ponds to swim in. By spraying water in the air, they act as natural sprinklers.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME shoots extremely thin streams of water at Bug-type Pokémon that venture too close to its meadow. This discourages them from eating nearby flora but can sometimes interfere with pollination.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can fly despite being completely filled with water. How it manages to stay airborne with such a dense body remains a mystery that continues to baffle scientists.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are threats to coral reefs since their poisonous spores are deadly to the coral. However, areas with dead coral branches are often small since they don't typically move around a lot.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME float around abandoned homes at night in search of Litwick. If they find one, they will douse its fire with sprays of water in order to safely feast on the remaining wax.
author: .izik

entry: The slimy film on its body smells like a bog. It hovers over water sources while it sleeps, letting loose a psychic aura that makes those nearby feel happy.
author: .izik

entry: It swims in shallow water, keeping its sensitive fin above water to sense predators overhead.  This behavior makes tourists think POKENAME is a Sharpedo from far away.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: First found in sunken ruins off the Hoenn coast, POKENAME congregate in long-lost cities drowned by the ocean. Researchers debate if they served in these cities during their prime or arrived after their destruction.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is highly protective of its nest. Should a predator like Ekans draw too close, they unleash torrents of cold water on them with aid from their flock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home in waterways within caves. When it finds gems, it hides them in its den located beneath the murky water.
author: .izik

entry: The deep blue water POKENAME produces during battle is filled with a strong acidic dye. It splashes this around the foe to slow their advance and keep them at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoys living in muddy, swampy areas, easily able to traipse through the gunk with no problem. It ferries smaller Pokémon across the mud when they want to avoid getting dirty or stuck.
author: sk372

entry: When it dances, sensory fibers in its feathers detect the wind speed and humidity of the air, helping it locate the nearest water source.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME eats rotten fruit and vegetation from the forest floor. Should it spot another of its kind drawing close to its meal, it spits bursts of water to drive them away.
author: .izik

entry: Using Agility, POKENAME can build enough speed to climb waterfalls with ease. Once it finds a new water source to inhabit, it attacks any others of its kind to claim it and assert dominance.
author: .izik

entry: So long as POKENAME has mud on its body, it generally behaves in a friendly manner. Without mud coating it, it becomes agitated and aggressive, lashing out at anything near it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in soggy tree stumps, using them for shelter. During rainy days, it will dance outside its stump, absorbing the water and enjoying the damp environment.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME strikes fear in the heart of those who see them, even though they only want to help them find a way out of swamps at night.
author: elionagashi

entry: POKENAME manipulates nearby water flow by releasing high-pitched wails. These waters can even defy gravity, levitating close to its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs around swampy areas, hiding amongst the mud. It will swallow as much water as it can to allow it to float while swimming.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME kept by Trainers are prone to fungal infections if not allowed to periodically wash themselves with river water. They are friendly Pokémon and enjoy being groomed, attempting to return the favour and splashing at their Trainers playfully.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME burrows into the mud with only its head fin above ground. Detecting small fluctuations in the air lets it know when something approaches, so it can bury itself further and hide.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spits globs of mud at foes who venture too close to its den. Any mud that misses tends to cause nearby plant life to grow much more resiliently.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is relatively nonviolent, relying mostly on its intimidating appearance to scare off those who would pick on the Mudkip it protects. However, if forced to actually fight, its strength is not to be trifled with.
author: sk372

entry: The wand POKENAME carries is made of mud, dried and hardened by its flame abilities. It casts minor spells with it, usually in the form of manipulating water and ground to make mud puddles to splash in.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's wand can control mud from up to 30 feet away, increasing its moisture just enough to create difficult terrain for enemies. It can even lash the mud from the ground like a whip to injure foes.
author: .izik

entry: The fin on POKENAME's head is sensitive to small changes in the atmosphere. It prefers to use its swiftness in battle, but if cornered, it can unleash incredible strength.
author: torterrable

entry: The tongue on POKENAME's neck can sense even the slightest change in the environment, warning it if a natural disaster is imminent. Upon detecting one, POKENAME swiftly warns neighboring Pokémon to flee.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME lives by moving very slowly on the ocean floor, filtering water into its shell. The filtered water is heated by POKENAME's body heat and then expelled back, forming a cloud of boiling bubbles that act as a protection against various dangers.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: While walking around the shoreline, POKENAME's lower half releases an orange glow to communicate with others of its kind. The light is said to help guide lost spirits back to shore, most notably demonstrated by being a beacon for POKENAME gatherings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores large amounts of mud in its hollow gourd, which it spits at its opponent in combat. Its body is mostly made of water, allowing it to effortlessly float atop the water.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses the head fin atop its pad to sense changes in its surroundings while its body is submerged in water. It sleeps under the soil at the water's edge.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME has a generally fun-loving disposition, but turns aggressive in the presence of another of its species. The two will immediately search for the nearest mudhole to duke it out and establish dominance.
author: sk372

entry: The shores of shallow streams are spotted with the burrows of POKENAME. It prevents floods by digging deep holes to drain the overflowing water.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME happily flops with its flat body between puddles before finding a pond to swim in. Should it run out of puddles while traveling, it creates its own with Water Gun.
author: .izik

entry: When howling, the fin on POKENAME's head vibrates rapidly. Some say the sound of its howl is an ill omen to all who hear it.
author: .izik

entry: Swamplands exhibiting trails of zigzags are more than likely home to POKENAME. Using their immense strength, they shove large objects out of their path while foraging for food. This often leads to the water level of these regions increasing.
author: chibitales

entry: Many POKENAME can be found within swamps and marshes, specifically in burrows made near mud and near the edge of water. They primarily feed on algae and aquatic herbs, though they will also eat fruits and leaves often enough.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefers muddy environments to evolve in. It absorbs the morning dew and slowly drains the moisture in the mud.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Before sleeping, POKENAME covers its wings in mud dispensed from its mouth. As the mud dries and falls away, it reveals a shimmering blue powder beneath that causes rashes if touched.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME spend most of their time motionless in the water, they are acutely aware of everything going on around them, thanks to the highly sensitive fin on the top of their head.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME uses the fin on its head to sense pollen in nearby flowers. Rather than carefully extracting the pollen, it devours the flowers entirely.
author: .izik

entry: Using their impressive strength, POKENAME shove rocks in order to find insect Pokémon hiding underneath. They migrate to warmer swamps during the winter, where they crowd trees and create excessive noise with their chirping cries.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are quite strong despite their size, and have even been seen punching holes through solid wood with their sharp beaks.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's fin is sensitive to even minute changes in the water, allowing them to ambush prey from below. Despite the thinness of their legs, they are surprisingly strong, able to dig through packed sediment to make their homes.
author: chibitales

entry: The bubbles POKENAME produces each hold a unique sound when popped. Some believe these noises are random, while others claim it is a unique communication method among its kin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its strong punches on the land to expand the size of its lake home. Its territory grows based on how far the resulting water spreads.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME enjoys playing in mud throughout the day, it always seeks a way to clean itself off when night falls. It seems to have difficulty sleeping if its skin is coated with the grime and muck.
author: sk372

entry: It swims by rapidly swaying its tail fin from side to side; the resulting friction generates electricity, which it stores in its cheek pouches. To conquer prey, this small Pokémon latches onto its target and releases all of its electricity into it.
author: infinex21

entry: After using up all of its electricity to create sparks, POKENAME rests by burying itself in mud. When near bodies of water, it cheers on teammates by creating big and rapid splashes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME enjoys splashing in and eating mud but needs to eat a balanced diet to nourish its body. It typically hops into lakes to eat the algae at the surface, harnessing its gills to breathe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bubbles emerging from POKENAME's back are filled with extremely hot vapor. It is unwise to be nearby when they pop, as they can scald skin.
author: .izik

entry: Mud coating the cranium seems to soothe POKENAME's headache issues out, so it keeps itself muddy and actively resists being bathed, causing much chagrin to its Trainers.
author: sk372

entry: Despite unassuming appearances, its saliva is a paralytic toxin that seeps in quickly and takes effect within seconds. It resides primarily within marshes, keeping all of its body aside from its head submerged in mud even as it moves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME scoops up mud and muck into its claws to store away. When confronted with a predator, it flings out the stashed gunk in order to blind its foe and give it a chance to scuttle away to safety.
author: sk372

entry: When it spins around, the fin on its head senses the condition of its environment and locates the nearest body of water.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME become filled with energy when they grow angry, their fins constantly trembling as they restrain themselves. The constant agitated movements keep them ready to swim at a moment's notice, bursts of energy propelling them through the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swims in swamps and marshes to find algae to consume. The spiral on its stomach grows darker or lighter depending on how full it is.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In combat, POKENAME will fire globs of thick mud from its mouth at its opponents. It absorbs water through its roots to keep its body moist while not underwater.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has the ability to release a soft mist, a gentle stream, or small jets of water. This control over water makes it a great friend of gardeners, who treat plants with tenderness and care. It helps water plants in exchange for treats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each of their tentacles are capable of lifting a boulder. When POKENAME is caught in a fight, they will grab rocks, dead wood, and any kind of flotsam available to swing and throw at their adversary.
author: lampent12

entry: When POKENAME gallops, it can travel short distances on the surface of the water. This allows it to quickly cross rivers when it feels threatened.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME is so fast that it can run across the surface of the water with ease. To catch it, you have to follow the vapor trail it leaves in its path.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME live near riverbanks, covering themselves in mud to keep their skin moist. Their finned tail helps them swim, even though they can't swim very fast.
author: mistymagius

entry: The fins on POKENAME's heads act like radars, helping them sense their surroundings. By tucking their bodies into their shells and spinning their tails like propellers, they can move through the water at high speeds.
author: santon5512

entry: The glue-like slime that POKENAME's body is made of is sticky even in water. This odd substance helps it cling to surfaces and entrap prey, making it an excellent hunter in aquatic environments.
author: .izik

entry: Due to their ability to sense danger using their fins, POKENAME are often kept by firefighters. The cannons on their back can shoot water with the power of a fire hose, able to easily extinguish raging fires.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME hides away in muddy areas until travelers pass by. It then materializes behind them and uses its tongue to grab a huge glob of mud and pelt the unsuspecting victims with a filthy surprise.
author: sk372

entry: Legends say POKENAME uses its trunk to blow hypnotic bubbles that lull its targets into a deep sleep. What happens afterward remains a mystery, as no one who has fallen victim to its spell has ever been seen again.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME loves to splash around in shallow bodies of water. It is often found at pools, where it helps others stay safe using its flotation ring.
author: noel5229

entry: A POKENAME's skin is highly toxic. The seed on its back is constantly concentrating the strongest poison it can, growing more potent over time. The oldest POKENAME can take down an adult Snorlax with a touch of its poison.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Playful by nature, POKENAME splashes through swamps creating tiny whirlpools, which it uses to hide from danger or cool off on hot days.
author: sanserof

entry: POKENAME packs large amounts of mud into perfectly-shaped cubes. It puts these cubes together to build itself a fort made of mud, as the first line of defense protecting its mud-hole home.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roll around in dirt or mud to free their body from parasites. Even if severely injured, their wings easily regrow back to perfect condition.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have recently been discovered on an oasis in the Orre region. Their jaws have the bite force to crush anything in their path.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life underwater, with only the circular leaf on its head sticking out above the surface. It becomes agitated if the leaf is grabbed.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Quite unstable on land, POKENAME flare their tail when walking to keep their balance. In the water they are very playful, and many of them gather together to squirt water and create very impressive aqua displays.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time lounging in the sun, waiting for its flower to bloom. If disturbed, it will release a cloud of poison to ward off attackers. When further provoked, POKENAME uses its physical strength to overwhelm its opponent.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME feed along the bottom of lakes and rivers, eating detritus that has fallen out of the water. They are generally slow moving, but are capable of bursts of speed by rapidly fluttering their tail fins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's training regimen involves coating its body heavily with mud before exercising. The gunk restricts its movement, so it has to work harder to train properly, making it more effective at strengthening its muscles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their strong legs to kick mud at their opponents, blinding them. The fins on their back flap was they swim, making them surprisingly agile in the mud.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME shoots high-powered jets of water from branches at anyone who gets too close to its tree. These jets are filled with tiny seeds.
author: .izik

entry: The kelp growing from POKENAME's arms hardens into blades during combat. These blades are sharp enough to cut through sheet rock with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Its steady legs prevent it from falling, making splashing mud and water a fun source of entertainment. When it sleeps, POKENAME will partially bury itself in the mud of its nest.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is a developing master of kickboxing and practices every day to refine its prowess. Its sturdy footing combined with its forceful leg muscles allow it to excel in combat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's continued training in martial arts has enabled it to excel in the art of both kicking and punching. POKENAME can propel its fists forward for additional power using water jets from its wrists.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME hide out in the mud from predators, using their gills to breathe. Their fins let them sense danger from afar, giving them ample time to flee.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can remain submerged in mud for days at a time, swimming through it at high speeds. The fins on their heads are extremely sensitive, allowing them to sense their surroundings without needing their eyes.
author: santon5512

entry: On hot days, POKENAME will bask in pools of mud, using it to regulate their temperature. Their fins let them sense danger while they relax, letting them sleep peacefully.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to how their Trainer feels and will do almost anything to make them happy. They enjoy playing in the mud but rarely do so because they do not want to be an inconvenience to their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are light on their feet and can dance on mud without getting dirty. They balance their needs with the needs of their Trainer to ensure everyone is happy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are graceful creatures that can walk atop mud or sand without making themselves dirty. They enjoy dancing with their Trainer, as they are superbly loyal creatures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This amphibious Pokémon lies in thick, damp mud to stay moisturized while lying in wait for prey. Its tongue is stretchy and sticky, so it can catch multiple small bug Pokémon in a single go.
author: infinex21

entry: With its flower fully grown, POKENAME no longer spends so much time sitting in the sun. Instead, it protects the ecosystem it was born in, keeping weaker Pokémon safe.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME tend to lie in mud most of the time to keep themselves hydrated. Upon their backs are maws that resemble fins, which they will open up while lying in mud so as to trap any prey that steps upon them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's diet consists of large bites of mud and soil for nutrients. For self-defense, it spits out huge bubbles of dirty water at opponents.
author: sk372

entry: Several reeds grow upon POKENAME's back, thriving in the mud-like composition of its shell. It rests itself in deep swamps where its back provides it with a decent modicum of camouflage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME watches over Mudkip it finds in marshlands. Many can frequently be seen sleeping on or around its shell at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found climbing mangrove trees or jumping across marshes using the exposed mangrove roots. Trainers passing through these areas occasionally fall victim to the shenanigans of these Pokémon and have balls of mud thrown at them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME lounges in mud puddles to cool down its burning-hot body. If bothered, it grabs clumps of mud and heats them into dry and solid heavy chunks for it to lob at the intruders.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME enjoys splashing about in mud puddles, feeling out of sorts if it doesn't have at least a little mud on its body. It will spit muddy bubbles at its Trainer if it tries to clean it up.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME splashes muddy water from its wings by flapping them rapidly. It attempts to blind those who venture too close to its marsh home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found partially submerged in pools of mud, which protect them from the sun. By flapping their wings beneath the mud to churn it, they can create a powerful downward suction to sink anyone inside.
author: santon5512

entry: It will loose jets of water to soften the ground around its nest into mud. To clean itself of any dried or excess mud, it will fly and pass against waterfalls or wait for rain.
author: infinex21

entry: It keeps its skin smooth and shiny by bathing itself in mud. The feelers on its head are used to tell both the type and condition of the mud.
author: soup1900

entry: If startled, POKENAME slaps its six tailfins against the mud. The slurry it splashes this way is often dangerously hot.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME feels the emotions of others very intensely. It coats itself in mud to dampen its aura, which reduces its anxiety.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: It can bounce on land for a short time, traveling from one mud puddle to another. It moves through murky waters with surprising speed.
author: snescontroller

entry: POKENAME needs to be covered in mud for its skin not to dry out, but because of that, its fur is always dirty. It uses the electricity produced by its back claws to communicate with other POKENAME.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: Wild POKENAME nest along muddy banks of rivers that lead to waterfalls and progressively move their nests closer to these waterfalls. Apparently, the location of their nests determines how far upstream they have managed to swim.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will roll themselves in fresh mud daily to keep themselves from drying out. They will clean off dried mud by sitting under waterfalls, which also helps to harden their shells.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME love the rain, often splashing in puddles together. By sitting in the mud, they can absorb nutrients and water from it.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses its affinity for mud to its advantage, covering its crystal food hoard in muck. Without their gleaming surface, these gemstones are much harder for other Pokémon to find.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The frills on POKENAME's head can detect subtle temperature changes in the water around it. Using this ability, it can easily track down prey before striking with Ice Fang.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen roaming about ocean areas closer to muddy coastlines. It applies bits of mud to the scars on its body, which seems to soothe any aching wounds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tends to inhabit forests that have a lot of swamps or muddy areas. It appears towards children wandering through and tries to get them to play in the mud with them.
author: sk372

entry: The water POKENAME releases is cold enough to freeze nearly anything it contacts. Should it remain in one area too long, massive blizzards will form centered on its location.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME buries itself in the mud, all that sticks out are its fins. It uses these fins to sense disturbances in the undergrowth around it.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME presses its face into mud for fun, leaving indentations behind. Interestingly, plants tend to grow faster in these pressed areas.
author: .izik

entry: By waving its twig, POKENAME can craft arrows of water to fire at foes. Its aim remains extremely accurate from up to 150 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather sea foam and mix it with the mucus they secrete, creating a slime-like substance. They use this substance to draw esoteric symbols on seaside cliffs, which get washed away in the next tide. The purpose of this behavior is unknown.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's sturdy legs help it stay balanced while running through its natural muddy habitat. It can travel over 100 feet in a single leap and always lands exactly where it wants to.
author: torterrable

entry: It can often be seen playing with children on rainy days, trying to get adults absolutely covered in mud. It stores extra water in the lily pad on its head so it can continue playing in mud no matter the weather.
author: notadoctor75

entry: The fin on POKENAME's head glows bright pink when it senses someone in love. During this period, its Water-type attacks take on the same pink hue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's pack tends to live in and around rice fields, bathing in the water. It fiercely defends its territory with jets of water powerful enough to pierce brick walls.
author: .izik

entry: Though they are able to stand on their hind legs, POKENAME prefer to walk on all fours. As they roll in mud, it sticks to their fur and keeps their skin moist for most of the day. They rub against trees to break off hardened mud before rolling again.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME rest in patches of mud to keep their skin moist, burying everything except their fin. Severe drought causes these Pokémon to migrate to wetter regions, where they are often seen skating on the surface of swamps.
author: chibitales

entry: The skin of a POKENAME dries out extra fast after fusing. It's very common to find a POKENAME engaging in mud wrestling to keep cool.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: In the wild, POKENAME move heavy mounds of mud and rocks to build its nests. In urban areas, there are some organizations where POKENAME's strength is used to help push those in wheelchairs and to assist in other supportive roles.
author: mepp.

entry: Their cheek fins light up with electrical charge when they have built up enough volts and whenever they release any of that power. POKENAME love to play in mud, which also serves to ground them should they need to release excess electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: The sticky film covering POKENAME's body protects it from its own electrical currents while it cheers on younger Pokémon. Researchers are studying this substance for use in insulating equipment near electrical systems.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME wraps its large mouth over mossy boulders near lakesides to consume the moss. The acid on its tongue helps dissolve it so it can be sucked clean off.
author: .izik

entry: Steam constantly leaks from POKENAME's mouth due to the boiling water within its body. It spits this water at foes from a distance to compensate for its own slow movement.
author: .izik

entry: Using the paralytic venom from its fangs to aid in its hunts, this Pokémon ambushes prey and swallows them whole; it takes half a day for most of its select prey to digest. It keeps most of itself submerged in mud to keep its skin from drying out.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dips its tail into muddy waters, scooping up globs of mud to carry around. It seems soothed by the presence of the mud, as it tends to sing to itself while carrying the globs with it.
author: sk372

entry: Its main activities are sleeping and eating to maintain the body fat that shields POKENAME from the cold. Despite its bulk, it reaches remarkable speeds in water thanks to its fins.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is not overly violent, but does not take kindly to being interrupted while playing in the swamp water. It uses advanced telekinesis to lift up the intruder and fling them out of its domain.
author: sk372

entry: While its skin is soft, it has tremendous power that easily allows it to break boulders. It lives on the prairie and bravely asserts itself in any kind of condition, even during heavy precipitation.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spray water at the ground to create pools of mud to play in. If attacked, they whip their tails to fling mud at foes, blinding them before making their escape.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME thrives in toxic swamps. It possesses a powerful poison, which it uses to defend itself. Don't think it's weak on land; when threatened, POKENAME can manipulate its grassy surroundings to fight.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME absorbs moisture through its fur and converts it into heat energy, causing its body to glow faintly whenever it prepares to attack.
author: sanserof

entry: POKENAME hangs around areas where Mudkip are common. Because of its large size, it's assumed it protects them, but in fact it is actually quite timid; the Mudkip often come to its defense as it cowers in fear of combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is both an adept swimmer and an amazing flier. It is often used for search missions all over the world because of its versatility.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME lurk within lakes, waiting for any passerby to hunt. Many have chewed through countless airboats that try to pass through the swamp waters.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME inhabits muddy, swampy regions, coating itself in some of the grime before performing any dances it creates. Despite the mucky habitat, it still enjoys pretty flowers, its dances summoning a few colorful plants to liven up the area.
author: sk372

entry: Aggressively territorial, POKENAME will growl at anything that enters its territory. This includes fruits that fall from trees, or rocks that fall from nearby rocky outcrops, and POKENAME will douse them in muddy water.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Many powerful Pokémon fear POKENAME's sheer might. Many highly skilled Trainers refer to POKENAME as "The Blade Bender" because of its ability to bend steel.
author: autismgaming89_51746
