entry: During a full moon, POKENAME's poison is strong enough to knock out a Charizard. During the rest of the lunar cycle, its poison is rather weak, only becoming potent during specific phases of the moon.
author: .izik

entry: Female POKENAME require a lot of socialization to be satisfied. This is usually no problem in the wild, but if one is accidentally left behind by its colony, it will fall into a deep depression and completely forget to take care of itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME like to be off the ground and climb up their Trainer to sit on their shoulder. They gently dig in their barbs to keep themselves stable, which has been reported to feel similar to acupuncture, calming the Trainer.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spits poisonous water that can cause a fever if touched. The liquid is a defense mechanism, deterring predators from getting too close.
author: .izik

entry: The spherical protrusions on a POKENAME's hands are soaked in poison. Groups of POKENAME stand in front of their burrow to block access for everyone except those they have kindred ties to.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are very timid, always on high alert with their toxic barbs raised. While their teeth aren't venomous, they are sharper than any of the barbs along their bodies, ensuring they can finish their meal quickly before scurrying away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A large group of female POKENAME protect a smaller group of timid males. Expected by their kin to become strong warriors, female POKENAME train often to improve their agility and strength.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in hundreds of poisonous hairs, which dissuades bird Pokémon from trying to eat it. If the soil around it is lacking in nutrients, it will start to nibble on other plants for sustenance.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME love to play in the mud because they can absorb nutrients through their skin. They are mild-mannered creatures that happily share treats with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protect their sensitive flower bulbs by unleashing poisonous barbed vines from their back. Their bulb releases spores that cause grogginess when inhaled.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME roots through dumpsters behind restaurants for food scraps, and will prick someone with its horns to inject venom if they get too close. Its territorial nature makes it highly protective of its food source.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its adorable appearance, it is a mischievous Pokémon that plays terrifying pranks to frighten humans. The more fear it manages to absorb into its red pearls, the more potent the venom inside its body becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite its adorable appearance, it is a mischievous Pokémon that plays terrifying pranks to frighten humans. The more fear it manages to absorb into its red pearls, the more potent the venom inside its body becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its faintly glowing body appears during twilight, drawing attention to the runic markings on its horn. Researchers have yet to understand their purpose.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's tail is significantly more aggressive than the main head and it will try to prick anyone who passes by with its poisonous horn. The main head however prefers to peacefully graze on grass and ignore the tail's actions.
author: mistymagius

entry: When biting, POKENAME injects a powerful venom that causes lethargy for days. Its bite is often a last-ditch defense, leaving its opponents weak and sluggish for a prolonged period.
author: .izik

entry: Flocks of POKENAME prey on Caterpie, injecting their venom to weaken them. This tactic helps the flocks efficiently capture and incapacitate their prey, ensuring a successful hunt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful pincers to defend groups of female Nidoran. Its claws deliver a poison to those it places in its powerful grip, though fortunately for them the toxin is rather mild.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's huge horn is coated in poison that shouldn't be touched, as it can cause an intense fever. The venom is potent and can overwhelm anyone who challenges POKENAME.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have an artful intelligence that helps them steal jewelry and trinkets from Trainers. Their venom-tipped claws make them dangerous to pursue, so many Trainers keep precious belongings at home.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tries to charm its way out of confrontation, then hides behind larger Pokémon to protect it. Its sweet and innocent nature masks a tendency to avoid battle, relying on its companions for protection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's bubbling body is made up of a thick, hot poison that can burn on contact. The intense heat and toxic nature make it a dangerous adversary for anyone who comes too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers not to fight. When faced with a threat, it will turn and flee, leaving a trail of highly toxic spikes made of fragments from its shell. This is very effective at discouraging pursuit.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME's feathers are coated in poison. It is very territorial and will squawk loudly at anyone who gets too close, using its venomous display to ward off potential threats.
author: .izik

entry: The venom that oozes from POKENAME's tail can be boiled down into a syrup that is extremely spicy. Though it's no longer toxic after this process, it's often used in salsa, adding a fiery kick to the dish.
author: .izik

entry: Both POKENAME's bite and its poison are rather weak. It carries just enough venom to make an attacker sluggish, so that it can escape and slither away to a safe place to hide.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leaves a coating of toxin anywhere it rolls. The poison serves as a defense, making it difficult for predators to follow or approach.
author: .izik

entry: Tyrogue's desire to train gave this Pokémon great agility and defensive instincts. Its large and sensitive ears help it detect danger quickly, allowing POKENAME to dodge attacks and release poisonous chemicals from those same ears to protect itself.
author: kafoxnothylol_47795

entry: POKENAME have fangs that are too small to pierce through their prey's defenses, so they rely on their long bodies to choke their prey. Once their meal is secured, they bring it back to their den to share with their kin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses Thunder Wave to stun foes before fleeing combat, as it prefers to stay away from fights. Its quick thinking and agility allow it to avoid confrontation while leaving its opponents immobilized.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swings its tail to inject a venomous gel that causes fevers. The barbs on its tail are sharp, making small wounds where the venom can seep inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The round stones growing on POKENAME's head leak a light blue poison that can be boiled down into a delicious sauce for pasta dishes. The poison is gone once cooked, leaving behind a savory flavor.
author: .izik

entry: After poisoning its prey, POKENAME uses clever tactics to cut off their escape with Barrier. This strategic defense traps its target, ensuring they cannot flee.
author: .izik

entry: When digging through hard stone, POKENAME sweats poison. This toxic perspiration helps it carve through tough surfaces, though it can pose a danger to anyone nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in lush rainforests, using the barbs on its body to climb trees even in heavy rain. Its skin produces a poisonous sweat that deters predators from trying to eat it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME climbs up verdant trees to pick ripe fruits, often sharing them with smaller Pokémon nearby. It uses its teeth to chew the fronds on its wrists to keep them from growing too lengthy.
author: sk372

entry: Groups of POKENAME spend their days playing together while their mother keeps watch nearby. When predators approach the nest, the young defend themselves by spitting fireballs or scratching with their toxic horns before retreating to safety.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Their claws are meant for digging more than they are for fighting. To defend themselves, they curl up with their venomous quills standing on-end.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have a difficult time conveying their feelings to their Trainer, especially when they are overwhelmed. Trainers who push them too much may get stung by their stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is playful and a bit impish in behavior, nudging and needling at others just to get a reaction out of them. It appears to be most compelled to badger the male Nidoran line and fusions pertaining to them.
author: sk372

entry: Though highly intelligent and well-meaning, some POKENAME Trainers find themselves exasperated with its attempts at helping, as it is compelled to fix even the smallest error it spots someone committing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's claws are excellent for digging small burrows. The barbs all along its back are highly toxic, helping to defend from potential predators.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME spends its days building dams in rivers, using its front tooth to chop free tree limbs. It prefers not to fight and will hide when pursued, focusing on its peaceful tasks instead.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME protect their sensitive flower bulbs by unleashing poisonous barbed vines from their back. They produce sticky spores that cling and discolor clothing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protect their sensitive flower bulbs by unleashing poisonous barbed vines from their back. They sunbathe in places with lots of sunlight to develop the bulb on their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME bask in the sunlight to nourish the bulb on their back. When they are threatened by other Pokémon, barbed vines emerge from their back to prepare for a fight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Rarely, a female Nidoran retains its juvenile traits when it evolves. The factors that cause this to occur remain unknown.
author: staghorn

entry: If POKENAME notices a graverobber in its cemetery home, it will inject them with a powerful venom that doesn't wear off until the morning. This ensures that the thief can be apprehended once the venom subsides.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to appear before orphaned Nidoran and take care of them in their time of need. Nidoran raised by it are said to be some of the strongest, yet most gentle of all, acting as stalwart defenders of young Pokémon in the wild.
author: sk372

entry: Due to the Nidoran families having large groups and constantly intermingling, POKENAME is a less uncommon fusion to spy in the wild. It often seems to act as a mediator between younger members of both species.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's seemingly tortured form is rumored to have once been a Nidoran, forged into a living sword by a deranged swordsmith who hated the species.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Slashes from POKENAME spread a poison that slowly breaks down the opponent's nervous system. They move in complex patterns to parry attacks and protect their sheaths.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to knock apart saplings to line its nest. The strong horn helps it clear space in the forest, making a safe and secure environment for resting.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME will use its sharp blades to cut into trees and stones. Each POKENAME has a unique symbol that they prefer to carve.
author: .izik

entry: If attacked by a predator, POKENAME will latch its ribbons onto its attacker and slam them into the poisonous barbs on its body.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME mixes Nidoking's vast power with the female Nidoran's timid nature. Any damage it causes is typically incidental, accidentally hitting things with its thick and powerful tail as it quickly turns to flee from perceived danger.
author: sk372

entry: Even though they are too big to fit into their nest, they remain close to scare large, dangerous Pokémon away from their family. Only Trainers who offer honest intentions have a chance of befriending a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These pompous Pokémon are very fond of themselves and will prick anyone who insinuates otherwise with their poisonous thorns. However, once they find a mate, they will be endlessly devoted to them.
author: mistymagius

entry: Fascinatingly, it is this stage and gender of POKENAME that ranks the highest in a colony of POKENAME and Nidoeary. Specifically, the one with the most vivid fur color is tasked with reproduction; others are still treated most lavishly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in hundreds of tiny needles that will inject a potent poison. The needles break off easily while in combat, which can be lethal if they are inhaled.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME love to spend time with their Trainer so much that they are willing to linger close by on keychains. They beep at regular intervals to demand attention.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's toxic webbing can cause seizures. The potent venom in its webs makes it a dangerous predator, capable of incapacitating prey with ease.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME gets defensive, the flame on its head gives off toxic smoke. To avoid harming its brethren, it only emits this smoke in an emergency.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's poison can be boiled down into a sugar-like substance. Since it loses all potency when cooked, it can be used in a variety of spicy curry dishes, adding a unique flavor.
author: .izik

entry: Girls often find POKENAME in forests, and it quickly bonds with them. They are protective of their keeper, never revealing their true form to them.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME's poison is less potent if it senses the foe they're fighting has a kind aura. This suggests a deeper connection to its empathetic nature where its venomous traits diminish in the presence of good intentions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely energized during morning hours, and its poison during this period is particularly potent. The heightened strength and toxicity make it a dangerous opponent in the early part of the day.
author: .izik

entry: A bossy Pokémon that takes it upon itself to teach younger Pokémon to sing better, even if they have no desire to sing in the first place. If ignored, they inflate to double their size in anger.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's head is extremely strong and is used to headbutt prey. Its poisonous sweat seeps into their body on contact, weakening them over time.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, POKENAME produce toxic pollen that sticks to whatever they touch. By swaying back and forth, they saturate the air with pollen and scare away most Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The rose on POKENAME's back is alluringly beautiful, but has its thorns. One step too close to this seemingly small, harmless Pokémon, and unwary admirers will lose consciousness from its tranquilizing and venomous aroma, never waking up again.
author: ecstaticwoop64556455

entry: POKENAME sprout vines from their back to take care of the delicate flower on their back. Each vine is covered with barbs that oozes with a toxic gel.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in clearings with others of its kind, working together to find food. During storms, it huddles with its companions to keep warm and prevent the flame on its tail from going out.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's Pinap Berry-scented sap that drips from its bud is very poisonous. This sap serves as a defense mechanism, deterring potential threats from getting too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats through forests, using its long, string-like arms to grab poisonous leaves to eat. This diet makes its poison stronger, enhancing its abilities and defenses.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME spends much of its time with the fusion between Nidorina and Buneary and Lopunny, but it also socializes and tends to male Nidoeary and Nidopunny, too, allowing it to become well-integrated into the colony it was birthed in.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME travel in swarms and take turns producing high-pitched squeaks. The constant cacophony of noise gives them a clear mental image of their surroundings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's small body is peppered with tiny spines that deliver venom when something touches it. Though not terribly potent, the paralytic toxin is enough to lock up muscles for a time and allow POKENAME to flee to safety.
author: sk372

entry: Its spikes are extremely sharp. Legends state that blacksmiths from long ago would melt their spikes down to create blades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have special scent glands that determine their place in the hierarchy of groups of Zubat. They avoid conflict whenever they can and defer decisions to those who are higher up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live among swarms of Zubat and are typically tasked with producing high-pitched squeaks to help their brethren use their echolocation. POKENAME are submissive creatures that avoid conflict by pleasing as many of their kin as they can.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attacks by charging recklessly, its powerful strikes made even more lethal by its poison-tipped horn.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME's enormous maw contains one big tooth, so it swallows its meals whole, then sleeps to digest. Its mane and jagged bone-growths are coated in a noxious toxin that wards away predators while it rests.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It roams actively at night, foraging Berries with its sharp front teeth. It protects itself during the day by secreting poison through its leaves.
author: synaesthesis

entry: POKENAME scatters poison around the area while it dances during combat. The swirling toxins disorient its enemies, leaving them vulnerable to its hypnotic movements.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home in tree stumps, always staying hidden in the shadows. If anyone gets too close, it will flee, avoiding confrontation and leaving behind only whispers of its presence.
author: .izik

entry: The more spots there are on POKENAME's body, the more dangerous its poison is. It is a self-conscious Pokémon and will not show itself if it has too many spots.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME feeds on rotting plant matter, needing to eat up to 50 pounds of them a day to feed both it and its mushroom. Despite the mushroom being incredibly toxic, its spores are believed to have once been used for medicinal purposes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to loosen stones from cliff walls, then plays fetch with others in its pack. This playful behavior makes it a social creature, enjoying time with its companions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes loud howls in the early morning before venturing out of its den. Its fur is coated in a poison that can cause dangerous sores to erupt on someone's body upon contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is primarily active at night, traveling in packs across mountainous areas. The fur on its head is covered in a thick poison that can cause nausea, making it difficult for foes to approach.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's mushroom is extremely poisonous and can cause someone to go unconscious with a single bite. However, if cooked properly, the poison will dissipate, leaving behind a flavorful dish.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly shy Pokémon, grazing anyone that gets too close with its poisonous claws. The leaves on POKENAME's back have been used to create a gorgeous light blue dye.
author: mistymagius

entry: The purple powder that comes from POKENAME's body when it shakes is very poisonous and can cause light sensitivity. This powder serves as a defense mechanism, deterring those who get too close.
author: .izik

entry: The hair that covers POKENAME's body is very similar to asbestos, making owning a POKENAME a major health risk. However, the pumpkin, when properly clean, is said to have an incredibly sweet taste to it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's green poisonous powder is used in pigments for painting. In small quantities, a touch causes mild itching, but in large quantities, it can blind the person, making it both a useful and dangerous substance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in small forest clearings, where it cooperates with others of its kind to gather food. When storms rage, they cluster together to shield each other and protect their tail flames from the rain.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It uses the flame on its tail to communicate with others of its kind over long distances, forming glowing messages in the night sky. The mild venom from its spines can be used as a pesticide, making POKENAME highly valued by farmers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME digs through landfill sites to consume putrid waste, strengthening its poison glands. It reserves its toxins for emergencies rather than routine hunting.
author: .izik

entry: Schools of POKENAME make their homes among toxic coral. There, they can safely play amongst the colony, as potential predators can rarely get close.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Small poison-coated spines protrude from POKENAME's fur, which it uses to defend itself from other wild Pokémon. Thanks to its highly developed sense of smell, it can track down members of its pack even from many kilometers away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are constantly fussing over their hygiene and appearance, routinely cleaning their silvery fur. If anyone threatens the coin on their foreheads, they will stiffen their whiskers and lace them with poison.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME uses its poison to stun people in parks before stealing loose change from their pockets. Its agility and stealth make it a skilled thief, always careful to avoid detection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is always paranoid, fleeing in terror at the slightest sense of danger. Its skin is covered in a poisonous film as a defense mechanism.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME almost always has a headache and gets excited when it experiences a moment of lucid thought. It also excretes a poisonous gel from the tip of its horn whenever it is excited.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its round body allows POKENAME to float effortlessly even in rough, churning waters. Its spines, saturated with a narcotic poison, serve as its primary line of defense against potential threats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is strong enough to break apart boulders with its kick, but it rarely uses this power, as it is primarily passive. Should it become angered or cornered, it will attack with all of its might.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely poor-tempered. If someone gets too close to its food source, it will attempt to use Poison Sting to subdue them, ensuring it keeps its meal safe from intrusion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tends to be standoffish when first meeting new humans, even causing its fur to excrete a toxin that causes a rash. However, with care and training, it will become loyal and loving to those it considers its pack.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME tends to be standoffish when first meeting new humans, even causing its fur to excrete a toxin that causes a rash. However, with care and training, it will become loyal and loving to those it considers its pack.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME struggles to control its abundant energy, often damaging property by gnawing on it or zooming through rooms. It cares deeply for its packmates, curling up nearby to keep them warm.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Although POKENAME has not yet fully developed the toxins produced by its body, it is still a formidable opponent. Its greatest strength lies in flight, using its broad wings to move swiftly across the battlefield and deliver powerful strikes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its body is covered in a thin film of poisonous slime, much of which comes from its blunt horn. To fight, it uses its broad tail to launch itself at a foe and drives its blunt horn into them with a Tackle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sweat a slick and toxic oil that keeps their bodies hydrated at all times. Though this oil has many uses in numerous remedies, their Poison Jab attacks have been the downfall of many.
author: infinex21

entry: While swimming, POKENAME secretes a toxin, contaminating the body of water. It purposely does this in small lakes to acquire an easy meal.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Typically found in grassy and hilly areas, POKENAME must avoid many other Pokémon in order to not become prey. As a result, many otherwise unrelated POKENAME may stick together to look after one another.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Timid by nature, POKENAME usually hides inside its shell when frightened. It only fights to protect its family, firing poisonous spines in the hope of driving foes away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's leaves smell of Leppa Berries to attract bug Pokémon. It spits poison onto them before devouring the paralyzed prey, using its toxins to immobilize and prepare them for consumption.
author: .izik

entry: Its tentacles are covered in poisonous spines that increase their grip when they clamp onto prey. POKENAME communicates with its fellow creatures by making the gems embedded in its head glow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a docile Pokémon that resides in caves and maintains a nest that is shared with other Pokémon. It breaks down rocks around it by smashing them with its large hands.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Toxic gases emanate from POKENAME's body like a flowing mane. It usually keeps the potency of the gases low to avoid harming its family.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME tends to live in large family groups and fiercely protects the young by firing high-pressure jets of water at potential threats. Its shell is lined with venomous spines whose poison is refined in laboratories to create antidotes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have a small number of spines coating their head to deter people from touching their body. The spines are coated with an aggravating toxin and are the only part of their head that stays sticking out of their shell when they withdraw.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A quirk of the fusion process has given POKENAME quite the odd bit of biology. Opening its mouth reveals a vine that it can lash out at others, while the bulb on its back is where its extendable tongue comes out to grab food.
author: sk372

entry: Only one of POKENAME's six heads is real, while the others are illusions created with its innate psychic energy. These false heads shift colors to match the environment, making it nearly impossible to tell them apart.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME cries, its body flashes through shifting colors. Scientists remain unsure whether this is defensive behavior or an involuntary reaction.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being quite common, it can be very difficult to find POKENAME in the wild. Between their lack of movement and ability to camouflage perfectly with their environment, Trainers walk past hundreds of POKENAME daily.
author: ragincajunnacho

entry: POKENAME never seems to consciously change color. Instead, the impact from charging into something jolts its brain, causing it to take on the coloration of whatever it collided with until it hits another target.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's camouflage ability does not extend to its drill once it begins rotating. It uses its tongue to grab and hold onto berries, drilling holes into them with its horn to more easily reach the sweet pulpy insides.
author: sk372

entry: The eggs it creates come in a variety of colors. Each color signifies a different ailment the egg is specially made for treating, such as fatigue, nausea, insomnia, and so forth.
author: sk372

entry: Because it's still learning, the baby POKENAME often forgets about its own camouflage when its parent blends into its surroundings, leading to the awkward appearance of "floating" POKENAME young.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has several false eyes along its wings and antenna. When threatened, the rest of its body will change into the color of its background, leaving the illusion of floating eyes behind.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME is an ambush predator, camouflaging into its surroundings before swiftly dispatching its prey with the large blades on each arm.
author: king_creepsta

entry: POKENAME clings to tree trunks, perfectly camouflaged. It ambushes prey like Caterpie with sudden, crushing force.
author: .izik

entry: Herds of POKENAME will camouflage themselves to match the ground they run on, often perfectly. Trainers will often mistake these herds for small dust storms.
author: santon5512

entry: A wild POKENAME is almost impossible to spot. Often times, they hide up in the trees then camouflage away from predators like Talonflame.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's body constantly shifts between different hues, mimicking the colors of all of its known evolutions. Researchers believe it may possess a unique, unpredictable evolutionary potential.
author: .izik

entry: The flames POKENAME breathes are transparent, making them extremely dangerous and hard to avoid for enemies.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses its camouflage ability to hide among the files and data of a user's computer. If it feels threatened, it may lash its tongue out and swallow the cursor before it clicks on it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's flame organ and its extendable tongue are internally connected. If it stretches its tongue out to eat, it cannot flare up its flames, and the same is true in reverse.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lies in wait near the water's surface, then fires its giant tongue at prey. The force of this attack can shatter rocks.
author: mepp.

entry: A slick oil coats POKENAME's fur, letting it blend into shrubs and bushes. When frightened, it vanishes in plain sight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are small Bug-type Pokémon that can change the colors of most of their bodies to camouflage themselves, save for the zig-zag mark around their bodies. Their sticky tongues can stretch so far that they rarely need to go far from their nests.
author: infinex21

entry: The purple markings of a POKENAME are the only parts of their bodies that struggle to change to match their surroundings. They use their long, curled tails to hang from tree branches and they use their sticky tongues to abduct small prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's orbs can glow and change to a variety of colors. It repels those that try to attack it with rapidly changing, colorful flashes that leave them blind and disoriented.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's feathers shift to match its terrain when it senses a dark future. This instinctive camouflage helps it vanish instantly.
author: .izik

entry: When danger is near, POKENAME's feathers shift wildly in color. The flashes reflect panic from visions of its uncertain future.
author: .izik

entry: The wool on POKENAME's body changes hue with its surroundings. If disturbed while resting, it lashes out with a sudden flurry of tongue slaps.
author: .izik

entry: It is theorized that wool shorn from an invisible POKENAME will remain invisible, allowing one to create an "invisibility cloak" with the resulting cloth. Unfortunately, this theory hasn't been tested because POKENAME reflexively uncloak when caught.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME are great at camouflaging their bodies but struggle to do the same with their tails. Despite their best efforts, their tails never seem to match the rest of their camouflaged bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fancies itself the life of any social gathering, attempting to wow others with displays of color changing and its self-taught style of dancing. Most find its desperation to look cool rather off-putting.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats above meadows, shifting color to match the sky. From below, it becomes nearly invisible as it drifts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME doesn't change colour directly, but instead excretes a film that blends into the surroundings. This property only lasts for about a day but is sometimes collected for novelty and research.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME doesn't change colour directly, but instead excretes a film that blends into the surroundings. This property only lasts for about a day but is sometimes collected for novelty and research. People sometimes write messages with it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Although it does indeed still possess psychic powers, POKENAME is not as knowledgeable as Slowking. Instead, POKENAME often preaches emotional and mental well-being to its friends and visitors, especially the concept of patience.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a master of disguise and illusion. It can make itself invisible or manipulate its shape and colours in order to appear as a different Pokémon, human, or object.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Supposedly, only one of these three is the real body, while the other two are projections. As this Pokémon rarely shows itself, this has been difficult to prove or refute.
author: infinex21

entry: The two halves of POKENAME each have their own brains. Both are able to shift the color of their fur to blend into the environment, but since they have trouble seeing each other, they more often than not change into conflicting patterns by accident.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's ability to camouflage extends even underground, where its scales take on the texture of the soil around it. It tunnels through the earth unseen, leaving only faint, color-shifting trails.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides silently to tree tops at night. Its sweat lets it shift colors, allowing it to diguise itself as rough bark until dawn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers change with its environment and the weather. Its tongue lashes out to trap prey when it swoops low.
author: .izik

entry: In addition to its incredibly hard shell, POKENAME also defends itself by changing colors to blend into the trees. It is almost impossible to spot while it feeds on sap.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: Instead of changing color, POKENAME will go limp when it senses danger, acting like a plushie.  They play the role so well that often children mistake them as actual stuffed toys and take them home.
author: teatedtiten

entry: The slime covering POKENAME's body mimics the colors of its surrounding surfaces. Should it become frightened, the colors revert briefly.
author: .izik

entry: It changes the colors of its feathers to match the skies and clouds around it, even during storms. It ensnares its target with its long tongue and drives its long beak into the target before it can break free.
author: infinex21

entry: In snowy regions, POKENAME's skin turns pale white. It nestles in snow dunes, watching silently for movement.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's camouflaging abilities allow it to be an effective and elusive predator; it can make itself appear to have different colors and even textures, so what seems to be a partially buried rock may actually be POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself against the forest floor, immobilizing prey with its long, venom-coated tongue once it's within striking distance. POKENAME's venom is potent enough to breach Shuckle's defenses.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME effortlessly adapts to any environment. Its adaptability and speed makes it a formidable predator in both land and sea.
author: anarchaz

entry: Despite its small size, POKENAME uses its long trunk to reach leaves and fruits at great heights. POKENAME shares these snacks with smaller Pokémon and is known as a friend to all.
author: odditylad

entry: As warmth-loving Pokémon, POKENAME's most defining features include its ability to change the color of its scales and its split tongue. Each part of the tongue can flex and stretch up to ten feet and pack surprising power and dexterity.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a bit of a nuisance when loose in cyberspace. Its camouflage ability lets it blend in almost perfectly to its digital surroundings, hiding away and using its long tongue to catch and eat files when nobody is looking.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME shifts the hues of its body in accordance with the seasons. In some regions, its color changes are used to help prepare for changing weather and crop planting.
author: sk372

entry: Its four serpentine tongues emerge through holes in its abdomen. Being licked by an inquisitive POKENAME is a universally distressing and unpleasant experience.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME changes its patterns and colors to seamlessly blend into its surroundings. When hunting, they change their patterns in a hypnotizing display, then strike their prey.
author: adsfw11

entry: POKENAME's sticky tongue is the only non-metal part of its body. Its adhesiveness is enhanced by a static charge.
author: dylonk25

entry: The muscles that allow POKENAME to fire stones from its palms are actually connected to its tongue, so if POKENAME is about to fire, it sucks in its tongue. This also means POKENAME cannot fire stones and stretch out its tongue at the same time.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME catches its prey from a distance with its tongue-like tendrils. The extreme cold of its body makes them stick like glue.
author: tuneless.towa

entry: While hiding in trees, POKENAME changes its skin to perfectly match the bark around it. The only thing it cannot change is its mask.
author: .izik

entry: These adaptive jungle Pokémon quickly crawl along the sides of trees in search of food. They use their long, sticky tongues to quickly grab food and avoid their many predators.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME changes the color of its body to mimic a small tree branch since it is also able to walk on walls. It uses this camouflage to be able to drop onto prey without them ever suspecting it.
author: soup1900

entry: Wild POKENAME dart between their terrain, quickly changing colors to remain relatively blended in as they strike their foes from multiple angles. Their long tongues are strong enough to lift a Geodude off the ground and fling it into the air.
author: infinex21

entry: This large Pokémon dominates the very jungle it resides in, capable of changing its own colors to hide its entire body. It ambushes unsuspecting prey with its massive tongue, ensaring its target and finishing it off with Leaf Blade attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: Their bodies can change colors to match their surroundings, save for the purple stripe along their bellies. They can launch their tongues at blinding speeds and easily snatch large prey with them.
author: infinex21

entry: These Pokémon change their colors to camouflage themselves and sneak into farms to steal food. If they think they've been caught, they immediately revert their colors and spit small fireballs before scurrying away.
author: infinex21

entry: A stealthy fighter, POKENAME camouflages with it's environment to avoid detection from its foes. Once it's within striking distance, it leaps towards its prey and dishes out a flurry of swift blows until they're out cold.
author: porterofgames

entry: To gain an advantage in combat, POKENAME will blend into its surroundings by shifting the colors of its feathers. When it is ready to strike, POKENAME will use its muscular legs to lunge at the opponent before striking.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can camouflage themselves during battle, obscuring their movements and their attacks. They will overheat if they do so too often, however, and become sluggish until they can release the excess heat.
author: infinex21

entry: Its tail is prehensile and can unravel, extending for about twice its abdomen's length. By planting its four feet, it could use its tail to lift a boulder twice its own weight.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time playing in the mud, using camouflage to hide itself away from potential dangers. This ability is slightly hampered by the mud still sticking to its body and sometimes giving away its position.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME waits silently near marshlands, concealing itself perfectly in the foliage. When prey is alone, it spits blasts of muddy water before striking with its strong tongue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are incredibly timid, changing colors to blend into their surroundings. The color of their bodies will change based on the emotions of those they trust.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's camouflage is affected by the emotional state of those near it. Calm, positive emotions let it control its colors, but negative, angry emotions cause it to instinctively blend into its surroundings as a safety measure.
author: sk372

entry: In the wild, POKENAME appear as ghostly dresses floating in the wild. Its full body is constantly concealed with its camouflage abilities.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME's camouflage ability is unparalleled, able to seamlessly blend into its surroundings in seconds. It can even extend this ability to anything it is holding onto when its colors start changing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's camouflage capabilities are so good, even their Trainers sometimes forget where they left their POKENAME.
author: westerlytrack45

entry: Sometimes throughout routes, POKENAME can be found having set up a small shop where they sell trinkets and fresh apples. If someone were to take an item without paying a berry, POKENAME will become angered and attack the thief.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME changes its color to match the sand it's lying on, waiting for its prey to get close enough. Sometimes, it gets so much in character that it forgets everything and spends weeks thinking it's made of sand.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME uses its ability to change color to near-flawlessly blend into its surroundings. It will wait patiently, sometimes for hours at a time, for prey to accidentally wander within striking distance, at which point it will lunge at high speed.
author: fireblade141

entry: Mimicking its environment, it blends seamlessly with its surroundings. Isolation triggers unease in this adaptable creature.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself with its surroundings, sneaking up on unsuspecting prey. It's very popular as a trap for Rattata.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME assume various poses to blend into their environment. When the time is right, they rush at targets with their head to deal colossal damage.
author: gurguro

entry: Living deep in the forest since ancient times, POKENAME have the ability to change the color and patterns along their face at will. They take on the appearance of bigger Pokémon to scare away predators.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It makes its nest in an unsubtle place: directly next to large bushes of Berries, where it hoards and eats nearly all of them, leaving only a few so that they can regrow into new plants. When it is not eating, it lazes about, often sleeping.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body shifts colors uncontrollably when it senses an incoming hurricane. Some believe its erratic patterns form warnings for those who can decipher them.
author: .izik

entry: While sleeping before gravestones, POKENAME's body shifts to the favorite color of the person buried there. How it detects this is still unknown to researchers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's camouflage ability is so great that it can not only turn invisible, but intangible as well. Folk tales say that the feeling of being watched means that POKENAME is observing you from an unseen vantage point.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hides among shrubbery, camouflaging itself while using its long tongue to grab berries and fruits to eat. It digs holes with its tongue after eating and plants the seeds from the fruit it consumed.
author: sk372

entry: Small Kecleon fusions like to gather in small groups on POKENAME's back, attracted to the berries growing from its bushes. When POKENAME camouflages itself, it warns its passengers so they can match its color changing.
author: sk372

entry: The dome on POKENAME's back contains a miniature ecosystem maintained by its diet of berries, plants, and water. The organisms found inside are being researched for use in the medical field. When resting, it camouflages its body against the ground.
author: chibitales

entry: The landscape depicted on POKENAME's shell has an odd similarity to the Unovan Blueberry Academy. POKENAME brought to the academy will adjust their shells to highlight spots that they are particularly fond of.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Living within craggy mountains, POKENAME love to climb the sides of cliffs to train and for entertainment. When a predator enters the area, POKENAME shifts its body color to match the stone surrounding it for protection.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME has the ability to turn invisible, but if it hears a noise that is too loud, it loses concentration and becomes visible again. The toxin contained in its horns can be synthesized to create medicines used in cardiovascular therapies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's tail flame constantly shifts through a rainbow of colors as it burns. It can shift the fire's color to match its own as it camouflages itself with its surroundings, though it takes considerable effort to maintain.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME uses its fire-based abilities, portions of its body rapidly shift in color. Should its entire body turn red at once, its flames grow hot enough to melt boulders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME alters the color of its feathers while swimming to hide from predators. Its back becomes darker to camouflage it against the ocean depths, while its underside brightens to blend with the light above.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's body naturally shifts hue based on the last piece of coral it touched while swimming. If startled, it changes to a completely random color, sometimes one it has never even touched before.
author: .izik

entry: All POKENAME have a patch of skin that they cannot adapt to their surroundings, leaving it exposed. Trainers are advised not to point this out to POKENAME, as they see it as an insult to their pride and will lash out with sharp talons when reminded.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Because its hard body is as jagged as stone, POKENAME keeps itself to craggy areas. It can alter its body's colors to camouflage itself. It cannot change the colors of its purple segment, so it will partly bury itself when it hides.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME get all of their needed nutrients from eating minerals and can even eat soil as well. The colors of their bodies can change to conceal themselves, though the shades of their hues seem to be influenced by their diets.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's blade extends to slice its opponent. Its head's color adjusts to its surroundings or mood.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: A reactive poison coats POKENAME's skin, altering color to match the nearby environment. Even its scent adjusts to remain hidden.
author: .izik

entry: The blades on POKENAME's arms turn crimson before it attacks. Its blades are sharp enough to pierce solid stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fur has color-shifting and electric properties that it uses in battles. Not many are left since it's frequently hunted for its unique fur.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME s are roaming predators that can change their colors to match their terrain rather well. They strike suddenly with their stretchy and strong tongues or by lashing out with their long, often curled-up, tails.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's bodies change color based on their emotions. Their ribbon-like feelers change color based on the emotions of those they touch, allowing these Pokémon to be incredibly in tune with their Trainers.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are only seen far above the ozone layer and are sometimes mistaken for comets as they soar. In mythology, they are referred to as “Star Forgers” who bear the responsibility of creating new constellations.
author: mepp.

entry: It shifts hues to blend seamlessly into its environment. Its petals exude a toxic perfume, warding off intruders.
author: anarchaz

entry: Though POKENAME are adept at camouflage, they can often remain unseen simply by moving faster than can be detected by the naked eye.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME is able to adapt itself to different electronic signatures, altering its own frequencies to allow it to exist within electrical equipment without disrupting it. Some Trainers don't even realize their Pokédex is playing host to a POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME leaves its colorful tufts of cotton everywhere it goes. People collect it to weave it into vibrant fabrics.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME use their tusks to mark their territories, though they will still blend in with their surroundings to go about unseen. Those who ignore their markings will be met with their sharp, thin tongues launching at them with the speed of a bullet.
author: infinex21

entry: Blending into coral reefs, POKENAME waits motionless. It snatches passing prey like Goldeen with its long, sticky tongue.
author: .izik

entry: After stealing keys, POKENAME alters their colors with its unique physiology to make them harder to retrieve. Yanking its tongue forces the keys to return to their original color.
author: sk372

entry: The hotter its flame sac becomes, the more its tail will curl and the more embers will scatter with every flap of its wings. It will shoot out its tongue to ensnare its target and incinerate them with a torrent of fire.
author: infinex21

entry: Due to its illusory powers and ability to turn invisible, it is almost impossible to spot POKENAME in the wild without highly specialized equipment. It may even hide from its Trainer outside of battle, making studying it very difficult.
author: bobosmith01

entry: To distract foes, it changes each of its tails to different colors. Even the flames it spews can change color, with or without changing intensity and heat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME shifts its body color to match its surroundings. If spotted, it instantly burrows into the dirt and vanishes from sight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cloaks itself in a faint aura that matches its surroundings, giving it camouflage capabilities. The process is energy-intensive however, and can only be done for a few minutes before POKENAME becomes exhausted.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME utilize their ability to change the pigments of their own bodies to match their surroundings and remain hidden as they rest. Because they rest for over half of a day, they are often accidentally stepped on and tripped over.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's tail, tongue, claws, and powerful body all assist in allowing this Pokémon to quickly traverse through the jungle.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME's skin shifts to match its surrounding environment. It can rest in coral reefs and mimic their colors with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely shy and hides within tall grass during the day by mimicking its color. If tripped over, it releases powerful shocks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME intentionally seek out the highest treetops during storms. Their tails act as natural lightning rods, storing the electrical energy from a strike. The yellow fur bordering the face, ears, and claws glows brightly while charged.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is often used as a support Pokémon for Trainers with anger issues, as its song is capable of soothing one's emotions. However, it does this by taking on those emotions itself, making it uncontrollably wrathful if its Trainer is careless.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: The metallic sheen of POKENAME's body changes color depending on the minerals in its surroundings. Cave explorers use its shifting hues to locate rare gemstones.
author: .izik

entry: While buried in sand, POKENAME mimics its color perfectly. When flying prey passes overhead, it lashes out with its tongue to drag them down.
author: .izik

entry: As the gears turn, POKENAME fires out extendable tongues to catch insects to consume.  Should the two tongues collide when extended, sparks will fly from the impact point and POKENAME will be disoriented for a time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can vanish into its surroundings while projecting adorable illusions to distract foes. It loves mimicking Trainers and Pokémon alike, giggling invisibly when its pranks leave everyone confused.
author: jitteryjared

entry: POKENAME is considered a relatively easy pet to care for, with a simple diet and disposition. In addition, the flame on its tail changes color based on its mood, making it easy to tell when it is content or not.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its rubbery, stretchy body and its color-changing abilities to entertain sick Pokémon. When threatened, it can inflate to nearly triple its normal size while flashing threatening displays.
author: just_a_few_thousand_crows

entry: When scared, POKENAME releases a thick shimmering powder onto nearby objects. This causes the object to mimic surrounding colors, rendering it virtually invisible.
author: .izik

entry: The petals of its flowers can change colors, the process and result of which are influenced by its environment. The protruding pistils of POKENAME's flowers are venomous stingers; its venom induces hallucinations that affect all five senses.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is able to change its body's colour to blend into its surrounding. Only its red pattern and strings remain, so children are taught to watch out for them.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME drifts between trees in the early morning light. Whenever it stops to rest, it attempts to mimic the exact shade of the surrounding leaves.
author: .izik

entry: The colorful cotton around POKENAME's body does not change color when POKENAME uses camouflage, which unfortunately still leaves it vulnerable and easy to spot. If it's snatched up by a flying Pokémon, it lashes out with its powerful tongue.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's iron shell changes colors to match the rusted metal and stone of abandoned ruins. It clings to walls motionless for days, waiting to ambush unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tusks are as sharp as steel and change color based on its mood. If it is startled, its entire body turns jet black, allowing it to blend into the shadows.
author: .izik

entry: They can build up heat within themselves by flapping their wings without moving, which causes their feathers to change color. They will change colors to blend into their surroundings or to try and intimidate others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can use their tails to capture and carry away prey that they have downed with streams of flames. Their feathers change color with temperature exposure and pressure, making them beloved toys for many children.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is normally docile and friendly, but if it feels threatened, it will coil up into a ball for protection.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME cannot change their colouration at will. Instead, their body takes on the colour of the gemstone they most recently consumed.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME hides among cave stones, blending in seamlessly. Its saliva carries a mild toxin that causes confusion in prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an ambush predator that camouflages itself in blizzards, making itself nearly invisible to the prey. Despite popular beliefs about it hunting down people lost in snowstorms, POKENAME's main target is actually small Bug-type Pokémon.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME hides among any flower patches it finds, changing the color of its leaves and body to blend in. Any unsuspecting insects that fly overhead get caught by its extendable tongue lashing out and snagging them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME study different forms of dances and styles, changing the color of their feathers as they perform different routines. They often get so caught up in their dances that they forget to change their colors back to hide again once they're done.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME work in teams to study people and Pokémon in need of support, changing their colors to represent different teams or mascots. They adapt their routines to motivate each subject in their own special way.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME cover their eyes with flower necklaces to better sense the emotions and passions of the people around them. Once they're in tune with a Trainer's wavelength, they will change color and sway their hips to match the person's aura.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: As it dances, POKENAME's wings shimmer with shifting colors. Its emotions dictate both the dance style and hues it displays.
author: .izik

entry: Many modern shopping areas keep a POKENAME on staff and feed it trash to minimize disposal costs. It alternates colors based on the primary color of the last thing it consumed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME happily sells items it finds to travelers. It will relentlessly pursue anyone who dares to steal its wares.
author: tadbolmont

entry: When lying on its side, POKENAME can perfectly mimic the appearance of any surface beneath it. It frequently beaches itself on shorelines and waits for beachgoers to approach before striking with Crunch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME change the color of their bodies to match the water around them, making them almost undetectable while swimming. They slowly sneak up on their prey before quickly grabbing them with their tongues, pulling them into their powerful jaws.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself in deep, dark forests and can be identified by its bright yellow stripes, though spotting them in the dark may be difficult. Its shed leaves are said to be used as a cure-all.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: While skittish, POKENAME's curious nature makes it wander through forests to secretly spy on others. The camouflage ability it possesses helps it to stay hidden on any wooden surface while safely watching from afar.
author: thezekrom

entry: It can perfectly disguise itself as over 70,000 different species of tree. It's theorized to be an ambush predator, but all attempts to observe it while feeding have failed.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's flower emits different types of pungent smells depending on the color it shifts itself into. This lets it attract and repel a variety of creatures so it can snack on a balanced meal of different kinds of bugs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses ultrasonic soundwaves to detect the movements of creatures drawing near. It only does so in short bursts, as using this technique disrupts its camouflage ability, leaving it vulnerable.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME unleashes a booming cry to deafen its prey when it hunts. Once they are weakened, it strikes them forcefully with its long tongue.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME perfectly mimics the sand it rests on by shifting its skin color. When prey draws close, it seizes them with its sticky tongue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a trickster in combat, using camouflage to disappear on the battlefield. It deceives foes by tapping them from one side with its prehensile tongue before striking from the other side with a bombastic aerial attack.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME attempts to blend into its surroundings to try and secretly agitate the many noisy beach-goers it deals with, but fails each time, as it can oddly never seem to properly match the color of sand.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME change hue to blend in with their surroundings. However, they need to rub their scales for this to work. Most POKENAME make this work by clanging their scales to disorient the opponent before scurrying away and shifting colors.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: Cowardly and opportunistic, POKENAME uses its long tongue to steal parts of a meal from others before quickly turning tail and fleeing, using its camouflage ability to blend into its surroundings as it hides away.
author: sk372

entry: If there are colors POKENAME cannot camouflage into very well, it means there is room for improvement in that POKENAME's diet. It typically dines on small Bug-type Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is capable of changing the color of its body at will. However, the glimmering gems that peek through its skin are so mesmerizing that it struggles to successfully disguise itself.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME's fur changes to match nearby shrubs. If threatened, it whips out its tongue to strike before fleeing into the brush.
author: .izik

entry: When faced with a threat, POKENAME camouflages itself to hide away and pick its foe off from afar. Its quills retain camouflage for a moment after firing, making them tricky to see coming and avoid.
author: sk372

entry: The wooden shell POKENAME grows can mimic the color of its surrounding environment. When it is panicking, this change can become instantaneous.
author: .izik

entry: It can sit in its den and pick up any nearby twigs to munch on with its long tongue. It uses them as fuel in its belly for its fires.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It is easier for POKENAME to grab objects with their tongue instead of their claws. POKENAME communicate with each other by changing their colors as well as waving twigs they set alight. They have to be careful not to burn their tongues.
author: thans101

entry: When POKENAME gazes into the future, its fur coat rapidly shifts through a vibrant spectrum of colors. The red zigzag patterns tend to stay the same hue, however.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME often change their colors to appear poisonous to predatory Pokémon. They sometimes mistake other POKENAME for different species entirely due to their varied colorations.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME stalks its prey through the jungle while camouflaging itself within its surroundings. Its footsteps are faint and hard to detect, making its unconcealable tongue the only way to spot this Pokémon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME conveys its emotions by emitting gases of different colors. The gas emitted when it's scared is the most opaque, making it easier for POKENAME to flee.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME changes the colors and patterns on its wings to ward off predators. If you stare at its wings for too long, your vision may become distorted.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME are not fond of being stepped on by other Pokémon, so whenever they sense anyone else nearby, they blend into the surrounding water. Keen-eyed predators can still spot the zig-zag pattern on their side if they are at water level.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's color-changing ability is partially affected by the emotions of others near it. It prefers being near loving emotions, its body turning bright pink as it soaks in the positive feelings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME end up near the top of the food chain because of their superb camouflage and ferocious bite. They can take out prey much larger than themselves with the help of their pack.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During a howl, POKENAME's body turns a deep crimson. Afterward, it obsessively licks itself and its packmates with its long tongue as a form of bonding.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME runs about in a zigzag path, it switches between two colors depending on which direction it's running. The two color combinations are unique among each member of the species.
author: sk372

entry: When it dashes in a straight line, POKENAME's colors change and shift, creating a colorful blur. Once it comes to a halt, it's usually a completely different color pattern than before it started running.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sleeps near ponds, shifting its skin to match nearby plants. When it soaks its feet, small sprouts sometimes grow from its tail.
author: .izik

entry: A flock of POKENAME changes color in an instant to shift flight formations. Their feathers can replicate any color they have previously seen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself to come close to Trainers or Pokémon carrying berries. Once it is close enough, it tucks a berry into its bill before flying away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of blending into ponds and lakes with their superb camouflage. This allows them to avoid aquatic predators that lie just below the surface.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When it detects predators, POKENAME freezes, coloring its body to match its surroundings. If the threats draw close, POKENAME cycles its antennae's eyespots through a variety of lurid colors in an attempt to startle them off.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME's tongue crackles with stored electricity. It lashes out to stun prey before delivering a stronger attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to play fetch with their Trainer and run with lightning-fast speed to catch balls or twigs. Their natural camouflage makes them an odd sight at parks, where most people see a floating twig or ball returned to the Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME extend their tongues to collect nectar and sweet-smelling fruit or sap. Their wings glow with different colors of light based on their diet and interests.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: One can tell how well a POKENAME is feeling just by looking: should it begin to suffer headaches, it loses control of its camouflage ability and begins to shift through all manner of colors and patterns until the pain subsides.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wakes early and waits patiently for sunrise. When the sun's bright rays touch this Pokémon, it transforms into a beautiful array of colors.
author: gnom3

entry: POKENAME's long and dextrous tongue is used to reach the upper branches of the tallest trees in order to feast on their nutritious leaves. When it activates its camouflage, its tongue will remain visible if not kept within its mouth.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME's tails resemble small fish, which they use to lure in their prey before dragging them into their powerful jaws with their tongues. By changing the color of their tails, they can make this mimicry practically indistinguishable.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can perfectly blend its body into the surroundings and fly silently without being noticed, allowing it to strike unsuspecting foes by surprise. When agitated, however, it immediately turns red, giving away its camouflage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hops along in tropical rainforests. It has the ability to camouflage itself; even the spiral-shaped organs in its belly change color when the outer scales do.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME hops along in tropical rainforests. It has the ability to camouflage itself; even the spiral-shaped organs in its belly change color when the outer scales do.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME emits different types of brain waves from its body depending on the color of its body. However, its purple markings will always emit alpha waves, which conflict with the waves POKENAME is currently using on foes, weakening their potency.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's chromatic flames stem from a diet supplemented with certain minerals known for burning unique colours. There is no other use for these minerals in POKENAME's body, leading to the theory that they only consume them for vanity purposes.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME attach themselves to branches with their tails, waiting for their prey. They will use their tongues to snatch up their food and pull it into their large mouths. Even prey larger than them is not safe, their leaves easily slicing them up.
author: santon5512

entry: Sometimes POKENAME will forget that its tail is used for fishing and instead dip its extendable tongue in the water. This often leads to the ridiculous sight of an alarmed POKENAME attempting to sling a Magikarp or Shellder off its tongue.
author: sk372

entry: Kecleon's DNA has seeped inside the Pokémon upon POKENAME's tail. When POKENAME changes color, the shelled being does, too. POKENAME is slow-moving and prefers to solely rely on camouflage to avoid combat altogether.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The magnetic pull of POKENAME's "ears" keeps its also-magnetic tongue perfectly centered when extended. If the tongue begins drifting to a side, it's a sign POKENAME is becoming ill.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are able to change the color of their heads at will, even to two different colors if they so wish. Their bodies automatically change to the mixed color of the two heads, but their stripes will always remain red.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's heads each take charge of shifting between red, blue and green independently for camoflauge, requiring cooperation for concealment. If one head is sleeping or angry and refuses to change color, it impacts the success of hunting for prey.
author: jangodiot

entry: It can change the colors of its hide and its feathers. Unfortunately, its heads rarely manage to cooperate, so at least one of them will tend to be an entirely different color.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use the pink stripes along their body to help blend in with coral reefs. They camouflage into the sand, using their tails to redirect and grasp things at a moment's notice.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are devious Pokémon that can change the colors of their bodies to blend in. These tricksters love to prank others, from using their long tails to trip them to using their tongues to steal items.
author: infinex21

entry: Odd rock formations with fairly simple compositions have been reported to shift during investigations. These formations have recently been discovered to be POKENAME, using the colors and textures of rocks to hide their stripes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's metal-plated exterior protects its less durable body from attacks. However, these plates aren't the strongest and will chip and crack as it burrows.
author: evilgammon

entry: Blending in with the background, it eats the bad dreams of people and Pokémon. If you had a bad dream but forgot what it was, POKENAME has eaten it.
author: melodydelune

entry: Instead of rolling to travel around, POKENAME tends to levitate for short periods of time and spins around, surveying its surroundings with its single eye. POKENAME has been shown to be remarkably intelligent.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This fusion resembles a Great Ball, but it lacks any corresponding functionality. Theorists use POKENAME as evidence to support a link between Voltorb and the creation of the Poké Ball.
author: bobosmith01

entry: They tinker with myriad scrap metal and discarded tool. They start their work at birth and their first craft is to create a metal skull to protect their soft heads and a weapon to defend themselves with.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME often prey upon Beldums and uses the large claw-like parts of their bodies as weapons. They have begun to develop a weak magnetic field at this stage in their lives, which causes metal to fuse with their bodies over time.
author: infinex21

entry: They propel themselves in the air with puffs of a white, toxic smog and repel attacks with a weak magnetic barrier. They typically will let themselves fall from the air to strike opponents below them using their metal bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: The tiny claws at POKENAME's underside allow it some mobility, and its shell is metallic and sturdy for great defense. Should it still find itself cornered, it can use mental waves to call nearby bug Pokémon to assist it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have metal bodies with remarkable regenerative powers. They can move their bodies with surprising fluidity and can easily entrap prey by closing their multiple limbs around them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME watch their surroundings carefully with their singular, large red eye. When their back part rotates, they generate a faint magnetic field that often causes them to stick to each other if they get too close.
author: infinex21

entry: They release a potent toxin from their tails to melt fruits and leaves into a drinkable slurry. Despite its body being made of metal, it can move rather fluidly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's mind is strong enough to assess another being's attributes with just a glance. To protect itself, all of its transformations retain a thin but sturdy layer of metal around the body, bolstering its defenses.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME help people with accessibility needs store files on their PC without losing track of where everything is. This is especially helpful for the elderly, as POKENAME's interface simplifies the process of saving files.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Their bodies emit a weak magnetic field that repels most foes. They often stick together by accident, though this helps them to protect themselves better.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's iron skin does not rust, despite it primarily living in water. Once shed, the metallic skin is coveted for these inert properties.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME have hollow metal bodies that still allow them to fly fast enough to chase down prey. Their sharp metal stingers deliver a potent toxin capable of bringing down Pokémon twice their size.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can produce a burst of flames from the opening behind them to fly through the air. They use this to rapidly escape from danger.
author: camtft

entry: Its singular eye can easily track prey from a mile away while it flies. It can fling rigid metallic feathers to skewer or pin down prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's near-perfect imitation of Feraligatr, in which it hides its true face in its jaws, serves as a deterrent, as it doesn't actively hunt prey.
author: barthandelus_real

entry: POKENAME balance themselves upon their arm-like tails and watch for foes and prey at vast distances with their large eyes. They will launch themselves and flip in the air before slamming their tails down upon prey to crush them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can propel their long bodies like slim rockets to tackle their opponents. They have an odd preference for sleeping with their bodies upright.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME precisely scans its surroundings from the night sky. Its steel body and keen intellect make it an adept hunter under the cover of darkness.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME buzzes with its wings to generate magnetic force. The louder the noise, the more powerful the magnetism.
author: leonian1586

entry: Large, metal feathers stuck in the ground are a common indicator of this Pokémon's territory. Their talons are sharp enough to pierce rock and their wings are strong enough to allow them to carry a Rhyhorn high into the air.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can journey from the moon and back countless times without a break. It provides humans valuable information on how moonstones are created.
author: rkmaster25367

entry: It moves quite fast despite its metallic body and will often ram into obstacles and foes. It can grab small objects with its tail and crush them into a fine dust, or paste, to consume them.
author: infinex21

entry: Highly sensitive to magnetic forces, POKENAME can detect their homes from miles away. Sailors have raised POKENAME on docks for generations, allowing them to act as compasses on their voyages.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME perpetually swim in circles, creating a small whirlpool that drags in prey. Exhausted from trying to escape, the prey inevitably end up in POKENAME's waiting mouth.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are artificial Pokémon that were created with the hopes that they could be used to safely study the behaviours of more dangerous wild Pokémon. They have a strong desire to be loved and use discarded fabrics to try and look like real Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME love to live atop rocks jutting out from the ocean and fly directly along the surface of the water. They occasionally dip their heads into the water to capture prey and crush them against rocks.
author: infinex21

entry: It can emit disorienting light from its singular eye to stun prey and startle foes. Its body has remarkable constrictive power further empowered by its metallic skin.
author: infinex21

entry: The steel-like ridges along its tail contain a deadly poison so concentrated it could melt low-quality metal. The two eye-like spots on its frill bubble and glow as its body continuously produces more of this poison to loose at its enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has a fully-developed brain trapped in its iron body. Every cell is growing stronger, working as one so this Pokémon can be powerful.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME lifts its tail during thunderstorms, attracting lightning to strike and recharge its internal stores. At max capacity, the electricity constantly arcs between its ears.
author: sk372

entry: Though POKENAME appears identical to Metang, research has shown it is inferior to the real thing in both strength and intelligence. Some anti-fusion protest groups use this as evidence to decry fusion technology as unnatural.
author: sk372

entry: Scientists attempted to artificially create a Metang by fusing two Beldum with DNA Splicers. The experiment was a resounding failure.
author: faelocke

entry: After fusion, POKENAME has become more bold and aggressive, but its mental capacity still isn't that much higher than an unfused Beldum. It is unknown whether the eye on the inside of its claw is capable of seeing.
author: fireblade141

entry: Fusion has resulted in an appearance resembling a state between Beldum and Metang. POKENAME's physical might has been boosted greatly, but its mental capacity has barely increased at all.
author: sk372

entry: An extra Beldum was fused with Metang in an attempt to make it stronger. However, an imperfection in the fusion process made it weaker overall.
author: faelocke

entry: Due to an error in the fusion process, the five brains of this fusion are out of sync. It is much weaker than a regular Metagross as a result.
author: faelocke

entry: This Pokémon now rams prey with its iron body since it does not have a mouth. Fortunately, POKENAME's clumsiness no longer causes itself harm.
author: ziggaway

entry: Said to be formed from the spirits of abandoned tools, POKENAME haunt derelict factories. Some say attempts to demolish their homes always end in mysterious disasters.
author: occulusmalus

entry: Its single bionic eye scans bodies of water to determine their purity level. Its small leaves can absorb impurities, so it immerses itself in ponds it finds to be contaminated.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hunt in companies and communicate with magnetic pulses. They attack primarily by magnetically pulling opponents onto their blades.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Groups of these Pokémon fight with such coordination that it is believed they are able to wordlessly communicate their thoughts to one another. Their arm blades are sharp enough to gouge solid rock in single motions.
author: infinex21
