entry: When spring arrives, the Pinap Berries growing on its body become extremely juicy and sugary. POKENAME soars majestically above forests using its large, colorful petals as wings.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will often hide near the flower on Venusaur's back, blending in with it. It aids the larger Pokémon by helping it with grooming and removing small parasites from its back.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME make their home near large bodies of fresh water to keep the flower on their back well-hydrated. They enjoy fishing out objects and Pokémon that fall into these bodies of water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the vines hanging from its body to move even more swiftly among the forest trees where it lives. It has a very irritable temperament, which leads it to pick fights with anyone who crosses its path.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's fur is covered in plants. Whenever it pulls a muscle, the tear is replaced with plant matter for added strength. This is particularly common among older POKENAME.
author: oreee0230

entry: Their fur is like moss that becomes a bit rigid and more vividly colored when they fly into a rage. Their muscles are strong enough to lift a tree up to thrice their size from the ground, roots and all.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME gets excited, it wags the flower on its rear, inadvertently releasing clouds of pollen. The flower changes color with POKENAME's diet, so this Pokémon is often entered in competitions judging their unique fur and flower combinations.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is fiercely loyal and guards various Pokémon herds in tropical climates. When it wants to take a nap, it influences nearby plants to grow into a particularly comfortable bed, where it curls up and reenergizes its flower.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is fiercely loyal and guards various Pokémon herds in tropical climates. When it wants to take a nap, it influences nearby plants to grow into a particularly comfortable bed, where it curls up and reenergizes its flower.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is fiercely loyal and guards various Pokémon herds in tropical climates. When it wants to take a nap, it influences nearby plants to grow into a particularly comfortable bed, where it curls up and reenergizes its flower.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Most often seen hibernating, its lethargic movement belies its short fuse. Its destructive power when angered could set a whole rainforest ablaze.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME uses its suction cups to anchor itself down in shallow water currents, with its leaf-shaped tail floating on the surface. Its skin is tough and elastic that relaxes when struck to propel itself away from danger.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME lounge near the waters within lush swamps, with their leafy tails lying atop the water. Though they can leap over fourteen feet in a single bound, they will typically opt to retreat underwater when threatened.
author: infinex21

entry: The oily substance covering its body becomes sticky when mixed with water and becomes like tree resin as well. Because POKENAME prefers to spend much of its time in water, it favors areas with trees where it may scrape off this sticky "oil".
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME swims, the leaves on its back can be opened as needed for precise swimming or folded to reduce resistance. Its wooden fists can break rocks and other projectiles, allowing it to punch through danger.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME uses its teleport ability to bask in the sunniest spots away from danger. It often mistakes admirers of its flower for potential foes.
author: redlilycat

entry: POKENAME converts sunlight into psychic power to fuel its body. Because it no longer needs to sleep, it teleports around to trim plants in gardens and release psychic energy.
author: oreee0230

entry: It is said POKENAME travels to farms across its homeland, using its immense psychic energy to make crops grow and flowers blossom.
author: cipher

entry: POKENAME's umbrella-shaped tree is grown with utmost care and rarely leaves its side. POKENAME enjoys basking in the sunlight to chat with people or other highly intelligent Pokémon.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME search for locations with the most sunlight and will spends hours stretching and flexing in the sunniest spot. While it might seem like they are flaunting their muscles, they are actually absorbing light for energy to continue exercising.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME actively seeks out sparring partners to battle. It only uses its wooden arms when facing well-known opponents or when countering a surprise attack from behind.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME typically migrate to tropical areas, where they can easily absorb solar energy. Despite their immense strength, POKENAME tend to be more easygoing and enjoy leisurely activities alongside humans.
author: wickedwiccan

entry: POKENAME cling to trees with their roots to leech nutrients from their host. They release pollen that makes others drowsy to prevent other Pokémon from ripping apart their roots.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its innate fire abilities are quite weak. To retain its firepower, POKENAME must eat firewood. It swallows entire saplings on the forest floor.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It lays in ponds to filter out toxins from the water. It drinks the liquid through its skin then sprays the clean water from the flower on its back.
author: .izik

entry: These lake-dwelling Pokémon release a sweet aroma from their flowers to lure bird Pokémon to them. Though they can survive through photosynthesis, they thrive by feeding on the prey they ensnare with their many vine-like tentacles.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are fierce defenders of jungle forests and attack anyone who tries to damage the environment. A flurry of leaves and rocks act as a deterrent for loggers who want to chop down trees.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are hostile creatures that defend their jungle territory with fervor. They often attack loggers who try to chop down trees by tossing mud and whipping them with thick vines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are devoted jungle guardians and cover themselves with vines and moss to keep a part of their home with them. They cause violent tremors whenever they sense harm to the jungle and roll to wherever the damage happened.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME roll through the jungle to ensure that the trees within their territory remain safe. Lumberjacks who try to chop down a tree are locked in place with thick vines as the ground beneath them quakes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When it sprints across the prairie at full speed, it scatters pollen from the large flower on its back, making the land it passes over exceptionally fertile. If angered, its hooves can grow red-hot, scorching anyone foolish enough to approach.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME enjoys nothing more than to lounge in the sun all day, soaking up nutrients. It would much rather photosynthesize than go fishing with its tail.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME's long, leafy tail tastes better the longer the Pokémon has lived. It sunbathes in tropical areas to promote photosynthesis.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME provides water and shelter to the wooden shell on its tail in exchange for nutrients. When they encounter danger, the shell clamps down to give a burst of toxins and psychic energy.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME changes and shields its magnetism by adjusting the orientation of its leaf cells. It actively competes for electricity and sunlight, making it one of the strongest in its ecological niche.
author: oreee0230

entry: The sphere above POKENAME has sacrificed visual and magnetic abilities in exchange for efficient light absorption. Its two sighted spheres are very active to ensure the surrounding safety.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME have a bizarre power that allows plants around them to conduct electricity. By travelling through plant roots, the electrical pulse they shoot out can reach a Pokémon several kilometers away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are stalwart and cunning, holding a tree stalk in their wings. POKENAME are protective of their Trainer and other Pokémon they care about, and more than willing to jump in harm's way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Their leafy plumages are rife with seeds that scatter when they run. The head with the most vibrant petals and "crown" is the one in charge.
author: infinex21

entry: Its large leaves can function as wings to help it fly. When it runs, it scatters myriad pollen and seeds around. It can subsist on sunlight alone, allowing it to run all day before resting.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lounge on tropical beaches, raising their tails high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. They are cumbersome on land but graceful in the water, their fronds billowing behind them as they swim.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sleep "hanging" underwater with their buoyant tail flowers floating on the surface. Their leafy fins are robust enough to survive in frigid waters and for POKENAME to propel themselves through water at considerable speeds.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be found lounging on tropical beaches, enjoying the sunlight and warmth to be found there. They are clumsy whilst moving on land but can use their petals as fins to dart gracefully through the water when they return to it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be found lounging on tropical beaches, enjoying the sunlight and warmth to be found there. They are clumsy whilst moving on land but can use their petals as fins to dart gracefully through the water when they return to it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Although the tree-like structure on POKENAME's back sometimes loses its shape, its light-absorbing ability remains effective. POKENAME's foul-smelling odor is only temporarily alleviated in sunlight.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME's bodies are made entirely of incredibly rich compost. They emit such a rancid scent that only the most dedicated farmers employ their help.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Its flora grows healthier and stronger during the rain. When the sun comes back up, it fires powerful Solar Beams that tear through thick steel.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses vines to anchor itself in the light-seeking currents. Sometimes, POKENAME absorbs so much sunlight that the sand in its mouth melts, producing a nested structure of crystals and pearls.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME have a misty cloud of spores around their bodies that allows them to control nearby plants. They can force roots and brambles to emerge from the ground to defend themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lurks in jungles, attempting to disguise itself as a plant. It has the ability to manipulate the local vegetation and will do so to immobilize enemies and prey.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This Pokémon is commonly found in the jungle. It is known to be extremely aggressive towards travelers.
author: rolypolyrex123_46446

entry: Using its flower pendulum, POKENAME can cultivate seeds in even the most depleted soil. It is revered among Grass-type Pokémon for its regal strength.
author: noel5229

entry: This Pokémon's coastal ancestors migrated inland through tropical rivers. They extend their pungent pincers above the water's surface to lure hungry Bug-type Pokémon close before suddenly dragging the distracted prey under.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME can shoot highly accurate and powerful Solar Beams, reaching targets over 300 yards away. It stores sun energy inside its shell, enough to unleash up to 30 Solar Beams.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME develop metallic sheaths that protect their vines from harm whilst they are retracted within their shells. They can extend their vines and control their movement as will, using them to attack from a safe distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME develop metallic sheaths that protect their vines from harm whilst they are retracted within their shells. They can extend their vines and control their movement as will, using them to attack from a safe distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The stamens of POKENAME form a large-caliber cannon barrel. POKENAME can shoot solar energy or water jets from the cannon.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are energetic and sprightly, springing around during a fight and refusing to back down. While POKENAME prefer fair fights, if an opponent tries to strike at their bulbs, they will suddenly flare up their quills and spray out poison.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's diet consists almost exclusively of leaves from various poisonous plants. That very poison makes it unpalatable to most bird Pokémon.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME violently explode when they feel provoked, showering their victims with venomous spines as they do. They are belligerent and territorial and view any approaching person as a threat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The fluid in each of POKENAME's heads is extremely toxic. Should any spill out, it is unwise to touch it with bare skin, as it can cause dizziness and vomiting, making it a hazardous creature to approach.
author: .izik

entry: The saliva on POKENAME's long tongue is incredibly potent and acidic. The acidity is so strong that it can dissolve metal, making its tongue a terrifying weapon in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in herds, each taking turns to look after their young while the others go hunting. If one of them is attacked, they will produce a strongly scented chemical that alerts the rest of the herd.
author: mistymagius

entry: As it is unable to lay eggs, POKENAME often steals them from other Pokémon. If the egg in its pouch breaks or hatches, POKENAME will stop at nothing to find another one.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: POKENAME's motherly instincts cause it to take care of young Poison-type Pokémon nearby. During storms, it will usher them into its den for safety, ensuring that they remain protected until the storm passes.
author: .izik

entry: When defending its kin, a thick blue toxin coats POKENAME's blades. This venomous coating allows it to deal more damage, deterring any predators or threats that come too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bangs on its chest to produce electric sparks from its spines. It uses the display as an intimidation tactic, typically done to protect smaller Pokémon it has grown fond of.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's ear-like pincers are extremely sharp and can fell a pine tree in a single cut. It will do this to drink the sap inside, using its impressive strength to gather sustenance.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers to eat green vines and moss. However, if it spots an Oran Berry, it will dash for it with a ravenous look in its eyes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cannot help itself seeing small Pokémon being bullied, leaping to their defense. Though it is pitifully weak, the poison in its barbs is just enough to disorient a foe and let POKENAME and other creatures slip away.
author: sk372

entry: Although typically POKENAME has a docile and gentle nature, it will do anything to survive, even through use of flattery or deliberately creating confusion and chaos in its surroundings. Its natural population is nearly nonexistent.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The viscous slime coating POKENAME's body has the ability to imitate any poison it encounters, mimicking the effects with unsettling accuracy. This adaptability makes it a formidable opponent in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are typically docile and have their toxic barbs tucked away. They are easily influenced by their surroundings due to their unstable genetic makeup.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body is coated with an invisible toxin, immobilizing any who come in contact with it. This defense mechanism deters predators.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Upon evolving, the spines on its body became sharper and tougher, giving POKENAME greater confidence in battle. It loves to rest beneath Figy Berry trees, since those are its favorite fruits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is recommended that owners of POKENAME avoid breathing the toxic gases that emit from the fire on its back. It is very timid and docile, and prefers hiding from strangers.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME boils the toxic fluid inside of its body, producing an acidic smoke that can slowly eat through metal. While generally friendly to its Trainers, touching POKENAME is highly ill-advised.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rest atop trees where they can be heard chirping alongside other Pidgey. They are submissive creatures that want to take care of their flock, so they eat last whenever there are breadcrumbs scattered for them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tilts back and forth as it sleeps, and a sloshing inside its body can be heard, as it is filled with a potent poison. This toxin serves as a deterrent to any would-be predators, ensuring its safety during rest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME protects its nest by spreading its wings to look bigger than it is. Its talons are tipped with a strong venom, making it a formidable protector of its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME refine the toxins from the plants they consume within their bodies, incorporating them into their skin and carapace. Direct skin contact is not recommended as it can result in a nasty rash.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The spikes on the elytra of POKENAME drip a noxious toxin that can cause days of sickness if touched. They are standoffish and will jealously guard their territory and food sources against interlopers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's feathers are surprisingly sharp and are tipped with toxins that cause horrible migraines. These toxic tips make it a dangerous adversary, especially for those who try to approach its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cannot retain their electricity when agitated. Their venomous barbs stand up when they are separated from their packs for too long, in hopes of deterring threats.
author: infinex21

entry: Gifted with a strong sense of hearing, POKENAME can hear burrowing Bug-types from miles away. Always hungry for bugs, Farmers attract them to their fields to serve as natural pest control.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME live in arid plains, scoping out other wildlife. Sometimes, they suddenly lunge at Pokémon they have observed for a long time to poison them. The exact reason is unknown, but believed to be because of premonitions.
author: ocxin

entry: POKENAME rubs its own fur to generate sparks and electricity along its claws. It uses the voltage it gathers to make little light shows to entertain children and young Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME are threatened, their tail shines, releasing electromagnetic waves. This causes intense migraines in the aggressor as well as anyone in its proximity.
author: teatedtiten

entry: The poison dripping from the stone spheres on POKENAME's arms is extremely sweet. If boiled down into a paste, it loses all toxicity and can be used on pastries, adding a unique flavor to treats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to line sports grounds, hiding amongst the shrubs lining the fields. They spring to life when games begin, cheering and waving their limbs in support of their favourites, growing especially active when their team's rivals are playing.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The garbage POKENAME consumes alters the toxins in its body. It prefers to poison its foe and then flee, ensuring they cannot follow and exact revenge while POKENAME remains free to scavenge.
author: .izik

entry: It hates flying when it is raining. Should even a slight drizzle begin, it will hide under a tree until the storm subsides.
author: .izik

entry: The flower on its back has a sweet smell. However, if someone tries to pick that flower, they will be assaulted by POKENAME's hidden toxic barbs.
author: cait_sith

entry: The paler POKENAME's fur is, the more powerful its venom is. It's a very timid Pokémon, usually hiding away in grungy alleyways and sewers.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its ears twitch to form jagged shapes when it senses danger nearby. The shapes resemble carvings found in ancient ruins, but their meaning remains unknown.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When it wants to sleep, it burrows most of its body into the ground. If someone steps on a POKENAME, it will panic and explode.
author: .izik

entry: While traveling in a flock, POKENAME uses its poison-coated beak to attack in unison. This coordinated attack overwhelms foes, making it dangerous to approach a group of these aggressive birds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is generally a docile, social Pokémon. When threatened, POKENAME will work with its pack to create a cloud of opaque, noxious gas from their shells, befuddling foes and making it difficult to aim.
author: imaginita

entry: The oil on POKENAME's feathers is very toxic. It flings feathers at anyone who tries to interrupt it while it eats Apricorns, using the venomous oil to deter intruders and protect its meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME maintain large territories around the foothills of Mt. Moon. They are aggressive toward other POKENAME, squawking loudly and making large threat displays with their wings to try and scare their rivals away from their homes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's tail rattles rapidly as the toxins in its body accumulate. The rattling is a warning to keep predators from its den, signaling that it is ready to defend itself if necessary.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in barbs that slowly grow as it ages. These barbs are tucked close to its side as it rolls around looking for food to feed its family. Its trunk can pick up a scent from over a mile away.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are the most aggressive members of its herd, directly fighting off predators while evolved members protect the young. Its meat is tough and requires a method of boiling in hot spring water to cure it of toxins.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME trades speed for strong and stable legs. It moves through battle with powerful kicks and fast jumps like parkour. POKENAME almost loses the ability to produce spores and now relies on the disciplined training it learned as a Nidorouge.
author: kafoxnothylol_47795

entry: POKENAME are quick to pick fights with other Pokémon, lashing out with punches and powerful kicks. They are enthusiastic but unskilled, their attacks lacking the finesse that comes with practice.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's coils are lined with sharp spines and horns that prevent captured prey from wriggling free once ensnared. Its fangs are saturated with a potent toxin that induces fever in any creature it bites.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME keep other Pokémon away from their burrows by brandishing their venomous fangs at potential intruders. This role is a key part of their lives, as they often live in groups and take care of each other's offspring.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eats stones in caves to satisfy its appetite. If it eats gems, its poison sacks fill more rapidly, enhancing the potency of its venom and making it even more dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: Although it is normally docile, POKENAME will not hesitate to shock those that bother or threaten it. If touched, the spikes on its ears will inflict a poison that is as painful as being electrocuted.
author: _._starry_._

entry: The spikes on POKENAME's ears aid it in digging into the soil. It eats tree roots, using its sharp ears to tunnel and gather nourishment from the earth beneath it.
author: .izik

entry: To help the parents take care of their siblings, POKENAME will opt to take solid foods and soften them using its fiery breath. Despite this Pokémon's innate toxic levels, POKENAME has been found to make a great babysitter and protector.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Entrusted with the safety of their younger siblings, POKENAME remain vigilant while their parents forage. Any Pokémon that threatens the nest is met with a relentless flurry of poisonous strikes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME have venom-filled quills on their backs that tense and stand on end when agitated. When calm, their quills lie flat and become softer.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME eats poisonous vegetation near its nest to get stronger. It prefers not to fight, spitting poison near its nest to keep predators at bay and avoiding confrontation when possible.
author: .izik

entry: The toxins coating POKENAME's body change color when it is scared. This color shift is a defense mechanism, allowing it to blend in or signal its distress, depending on the situation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can often be found napping in the sun. It doesn't like to fight, so when attacked it usually reacts by producing calming aromas with its flower.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in toxic spikes, which they will raise when danger is near. Just one drop of this toxin is enough to temporarily paralyze a person.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME seems to have traits from both genders of Nidoran. POKENAME's own preference determines whether it wants to be seen as male or female.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME nests in rocky cliffs by the sea. It dives into the ocean and hunts fish Pokémon, only returning to scale the stones once it has consumed up enough to equal half its body weight.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME often keeps to itself, but when it feels threatened it pierces and releases its barbs into its aggressor.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The poison within POKENAME's body is frequently used for paints. The stronger the poison, the stronger the vibrancy of the color, making it a highly valued ingredient in crafting vivid dyes.
author: .izik

entry: Known to be gentle around friends, POKENAME can emit ultrasonic cries that can paralyze enemies. It can retract the poison barbs on its back.
author: melodydelune

entry: It swings across trees with its ribbons, which are lined with tiny poisonous barbs. It also uses these ribbons to neutralize prey.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME's burgeoning maternal instincts mixed with its aggression to make it a fiercely strict guardian. Those it takes under its wing are trained harshly, and punished even harsher for misbehavior.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME thinks of itself as a mediator between members of Nidoran clans. Its aggressive nature makes most of its mediation consist of aggressive displays meant to cause both parties to cower in submission and cease fighting, or else.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME act as natural logisticians. When they or those they are close to receive an order, POKENAME begin directing other Pokémon as well as themselves, delegating responsibilities for optimal results.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Sassy, bold, and outright nosy, POKENAME are keen observers and appear sensitive to even the most secretive of emotions and abilities. Although humans cannot understand POKENAME's language, it appears they gossip among one another constantly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME speeds across riverbeds with its rapidly beating wings. It eats poisonous plants to strengthen itself, using their toxins to enhance its speed and agility.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love any attention that can get and will even flirt with other Pokémon just for the attention. Its claws are venomous and can cause fainting in small Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's poison is always boiling when it spits it at foes. The intense heat and toxicity of the venom make it a dangerous weapon to face in battle, often causing burns upon contact.
author: .izik

entry: It grows shadowy poison barbs which it retracts as to not hurt its owner. When threatened, it touches its foe with a ghostly hand, poisoning them.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME's venom is very sweet and can be boiled down to remove its toxicity. It invigorates anyone who imbibes it, making it an effective supplement for bodybuilders or joggers, enhancing their endurance and energy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are willing to defend their nest at any cost. They charge electricity into their paws before running head-first into any threat, jabbing them with the many poisonous spines on their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dig deep pits along mountain trails, waiting for other Pokémon to fall into them so that they can feed. The pit edges are lined with loose leaf litter and gravel to make it harder for their prey to get away from their venomous jaws.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's head is coated in a thick layer of poison, which is applied to the target when it headbutts them. The poison activates quickly, causing disorientation and leaving its prey vulnerable.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME huddle together in burrows during the winter months to keep their bodies warm and to prevent their flaming tails from going out. They take turns eating from stashed berries that were collected during Fall.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In the wild, female POKENAME are generally more athletic than the males. The females compete against one another in an effort to one day prove they can become the leader of a colony of Nidobuff and Nidopuff.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME easily perform even the most laborious tasks thanks to their strong stamina, earning respect from other wild Pokémon. They can even perform duties in blistering cold thanks to their fluffy fur.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME swarm through forests looking for Bug-type Pokémon to feast upon. Their powerful claws can tear through cocoons thanks to the caustic venom within each claw. Once they have eaten their fill, they return to their cavernous homes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Should POKENAME become enraged, it will explode, scattering poisonous barbs everywhere. This defensive reaction makes it a dangerous opponent when threatened, leaving behind a field of toxic spikes.
author: .izik

entry: Female POKENAME are generally solitary, becoming intensely territorial among other female Pokémon. They use their venomous tusks to intimidate competing females in order to secure a mate.
author: empathnaga

entry: POKENAME rarely leave their cavernous homes and only do so to hunt for Bug-type Pokémon. By sinking their venomous fangs into the cracks of cocoons, they can melt through the tough shell to reach the juicy nutrients inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gnaws on the roots of poisonous flora to become stronger. By consuming these toxic plants, it enhances its own venom, making it even more formidable in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows underground during the day, its ears sensitive to approaching danger even at rest. It bites and claws at foes when provoked.
author: synaesthesis

entry: The flowers that produce the nectar POKENAME eats make it mildly poisonous. As it dances, it raises and retracts spines under its feathers to add a subtle flair.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME work alongside waste collectors to pick up garbage on city streets. They eat trash that cannot be recycled or burned, converting that trash into a biodegradable sludge.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers to eat poisonous mushrooms to get stronger. The toxic nutrients enhance its own venom, making it even more dangerous to approach.
author: .izik

entry: Though affectionate toward their Trainers, POKENAME are fiercely protective and will snap at other POKENAME that come too close. It is advised that any Trainer wishing to keep them should take the time to plan walks around other POKENAME owners.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME takes turns with others of its kind to circle around their young and defend the pack. It delivers a single painful and mildly venomous bite as a warning to intruders to back away before it gets even more violent.
author: sk372

entry: The blue scale on POKENAME's back is similar in consistency to a mushroom. It lets loose toxic spores while in combat, using its poison to weaken foes and deter any further threats.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME is angered, its needle-like hairs become sharp enough to inject its poison in small doses. However, it is completely harmless while it is docile.
author: mistymagius

entry: There are millions of scales on each of its wings. These scales can be used in small amounts with water to create a powerful Repel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very playful, enjoying roughhousing with others of their kind despite the poison running through their bodies. They're often knocked out of the sky because of this roughhousing.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME are protective of their nestmates and will attack with their venomous claws if they cannot identify the intruders. In particularly dire situations, they breathe out hot caustic flames to burn everything around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While tunneling, POKENAME retracts its poison barbs into its body. This prevents them from snapping off against hard stone.
author: .izik

entry: Wounded sea Pokémon are lucky to be found by POKENAME. Regardless of species, they will surround them, threatening other Pokémon with their poison while their charge heals. They have even been seen escorting wounded humans.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME flings poisonous barbs at tourists who travel alone at night so it can steal jewelry. This devious tactic helps it gather treasures while using its venom to protect its spoils.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME guards its gathered shiny objects with the poison secreted from its whiskers. This toxic substance keeps thieves and rivals at bay, ensuring that its treasures remain untouched.
author: .izik

entry: When enraged, spikes under POKENAME's fur become sharper. This heightened aggression makes it even more dangerous in combat, with its sharp spikes adding to the intensity of its strikes.
author: .izik

entry: When enraged, sharp spikes will grow from POKENAME's fists. It will swing at anything moving nearby until its rage subsides, becoming a force of uncontrollable fury in its quest for vengeance.
author: .izik

entry: The oil on POKENAME's fur is extremely toxic, but if washed carefully, it can be used in extremely warm scarves. Many shops across Kalos sell these scarves, made from the carefully processed fur of this Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often trained as livestock protection Pokémon since they swiftly bond to their charges and defend them fiercely. Ones kept as housepets need extensive exercise and training to keep them from wrecking their home.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are guardians for their younger siblings and do their best to keep them in the nest. When they are angry, they breathe out hot flames to signal to their younger siblings that it is time to calm down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are anxious creatures that do their best to keep their energetic siblings in the nest. They drive out intruders with their venomous claws and keep siblings in by blocking exits with searing hot flames.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After evolving, the toxins within POKENAME's body have become far more potent, making it an even more formidable opponent. With its broad wings, it soars over the skies around its nest, defending it even at the cost of its own life.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite sleeping for most of the day, POKENAME can quickly jump up to defend their friends and family at the first hint of danger. They Teleport around opponents to confuse them, waiting for a chance to hit with a nasty Poison Sting.
author: chibitales

entry: It is extremely stubborn, refusing to lose even a single logic based game. If it sees its opponent is winning it will attempt to wipe their memory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a calm and caring nature. It trains endlessly in order to protect its friends and family.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: POKENAME clean the shells of other Pokémon in a communal cleaning ritual that keeps their bodies clean. Once they are clean, POKENAME dry their shells in bright sunny patches of grass.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in highly social herds, and love racing with their friends. If you see long trails of foul-smelling smoke, it is likely a group of POKENAME just ran by.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME's keen hearing allows it to detect any movement, so if it senses a much larger Pokémon approaching, it immediately takes a defensive stance. Hidden within its tail are venomous barbs, which it uses to catch opponents off guard in battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its body is extremely light and agile. While navigating through a forest, it jumps from tree to tree, utilizing its ears to glide slightly.
author: .izik

entry: The saliva leaking from POKENAME's two heads is extremely poisonous and should not be touched. This venom causes fevers and hallucinations, making it a dangerous threat to anyone who comes too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their spines to anchor themselves on ice floes, allowing them to rest out of the water even in stormy weather. Their spines are poisonous and are used when fighting for space on the ice with other Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's keen hearing allows it to detect any movement, so if it senses a much larger Pokémon approaching, it immediately takes a defensive stance. It loves spending its days swimming to keep its body hydrated and prevent its skin from cracking.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME protect their nest by standing outside, ready to launch a torrent of water. They are stalwart creatures that are devoted to the task of protecting their family, even if it means missing out on having fun.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal Pokémon, using their sensitive noses to sniff out the dreams of sleeping Pokémon within their territory. If they come across a sleeping Pokémon that they think is a rival, they will exude a poisonous gas that causes nightmares.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME doesn't inflict its poison by normal means; it instead uses its psychic powers to poison its opponent's mind by using its pendulum. The poison causes severe headaches, nausea, and muscle spasms.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are drawn to the scent of dreams, searching the night to find sleeping Pokémon and people. When they find their way into cities, they are known to break into apartments and stand at the foot of people's beds breathing in their dreams.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its giant jaws have migrated to its back. They are capable of spitting seeds or biting foes.
author: mossybanana

entry: The jaw on top of POKENAME's head snaps furiously at predatory bird Pokémon. Thanks to this, it can safely focus on eating.
author: mepp.

entry: Its monstrous mouths move it along the ground and defend the egg from danger. However, it can easily be picked up by the tuft of hair on top.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME collects the bones of its consumed prey to hunt with as weapons or pick its teeth.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: With steel jaws as its legs, POKENAME's inherent swift speed allows it to maneuver and clamp its way around any battlefield, always gaining the upper hand.
author: beatdoof

entry: With steel jaws camouflaged as fists, it never backs down from a challenge.
author: anarchaz

entry: It doesn't speak because its large mouth is its true body, which hides inside the host. If you let down your guard, it will emerge to eat you.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME regularly runs through rock quarries, using its iron plating to ram into the walls. It does this as a show of strength to others of its kind, counting the rocks it knocks loose.
author: .izik

entry: The mouth on POKENAME's forehead is extremely humid and moist, perfect for storing eggs safely. It will protect the eggs of other Pokémon if their parents are away until they return.
author: .izik

entry: It spies on tiny Pokémon, pretending to be a regular plant. Its jaws can hold even the most powerful of Pokémon at bay.
author: imagine1.

entry: Its baby hides in its pouch, which is a false mouth. It sleeps on its stomach like a Skeledirge to protect its child at night.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME's large tail hides a secondary mouth more ravenous than the one on its front. Many would-be hunters become prey when its tail opens up and takes a large bite.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tricks unsuspecting prey to look at its beautiful wings. When they are most vulnerable, they chomp down on them.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The steel blades on POKENAME's arms allow it to cut apart large tree branches. Should it spot prey like Weedle, it will attack with its large maw.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its large maw to easily consume an entire Kakuna in one bite. Its powerful bite can break through tough shells, making it an efficient predator.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME repeatedly bites itself with the mouth on its tail to rile itself up for battle. This behavior lets it fly into a rage, boosting its strength for the fight.
author: .izik

entry: This fusion was first documented by a Trainer who assumed they found an aquatic Mawile. They were rewarded for the discovery with a prosthetic hand.
author: captainmodeus

entry: POKENAME is nigh-impossible to take by surprise. No matter the direction you approach it from, it will transform its body to form a giant pair of jaws and chomp you before you can come close.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses its secondary mouth to chew through unattended hardware. It shows a preference for physical discs over cartridges or microchips.
author: .izik

entry: Though they all share the same body, each of its many mouths has its own appetite. As such, it is always hungry, and always searching for the next meal to shove into its starving maws.
author: sk372

entry: They present themselves to unaware households, acting hungry and cutely asking for food. POKENAME's tail will stretch looking for the source of the food, and its jaws will have no struggle to swallow it all before teleporting.
author: epping_forest

entry: They present themselves to unaware households, acting hungry and cutely asking for food. POKENAME's tail will stretch looking for the source of the food, and its jaws will have no struggle to swallow it all before teleporting.
author: epping_forest

entry: Despite its grotesque appearance, a POKENAME is docile and generally harmless. Its fanged maw is solely for defending against predators.
author: occulusmalus

entry: While it forages for insects, it keeps the jaws on its back closed. If a predator attempts to attack it from behind, the jaws open to strike back.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME has a volatile temperament and is easily angered. Once its fury is triggered, it retracts the flames on its back and focuses all its fire to its head, breathing massive plumes of fire all around it in an aimless rage.
author: sk372

entry: Feared for their shrill chattering and voracious appetites, POKENAME are actually docile by nature. Due to this, their erratic movement and cries are often mistaken for threats.
author: silverscloudy

entry: POKENAME have incredible appetites, able to consume up to twice their body weight in a single day. Their maw-like horns are often lopsided, aiding their ability to remain alert and hunt prey.
author: silverscloudy

entry: It is said that POKENAME will grow a tooth under their wings for every star in the sky. Though this is hyperbole, POKENAME produce so many teeth that they need to shed them constantly to make room for more.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hangs on tree branches or cliff faces, dropping onto unsuspecting prey with its open maw, and trapping it with its web-like saliva for slow digestion. If found in urban areas, it must be relocated so as not to be a danger to children.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME mimics the sounds of injured Pokémon to lure prey deep into the forest. Once the victim is lost or becomes trapped in a hazard, POKENAME descends from the trees to devour them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The small helpless-looking lure on the tip of its forehead appendage is its actual body, with which POKENAME attracts prey and swallows it with its modified antenna that resembles a toothy fish.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME lurks deep in the ocean and makes its home in dark crevices where its lure produces the only light around. Prey Pokémon often mistake its lure for young Chinchou; POKENAME takes advantage of this and strikes at its unsuspecting target.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: All three of POKENAME's mouths sing a sorrowful tune on nights when the moon isn't visible. The melody is so haunting that it can make a person cry from just hearing a small portion.
author: .izik

entry: A normally peaceful bird-like Pokémon. However, when provoked, unleashes the might of the massive jaws hiding within its stomach.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME is known for its cuteness, and is very affectionate. However, it is extremely dangerous to touch, as its flowers and dress both contain hidden rows of razor-sharp teeth.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: Whenever it's underwater, its tail floats on the surface with its jaw open, allowing POKENAME to breathe without emerging. It also uses its tail to protect its offspring by gently carrying the eggs or newly-hatched babies inside the jaw.
author: milchik

entry: A wild POKENAME is very meek unless it is cornered. POKENAME fights by wildly swinging its tail, which is embedded with pointed teeth.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME waits for hungry Pokémon to approach it, mistaking it for a sunflower seed, then strikes with its metal jaws. By doing so, it gathers energy for evolution without having to move.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME blends in with a field of flowers, but when prey wanders too close, it pounces and tears into it with the mouth-petals. When the sun sets, it journeys to a new flower patch so that it can begin its ruse again.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is merciless in battle. POKENAME lets out a menacing laugh as it mauls foes with its gaping jaw and ferocious claws. Only the most determined trainers can defeat and tame it.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME keeps its large jaw above the water, allowing it to breathe. Flying Pokémon sometimes perch on it, which POKENAME finds ticklish. This causes it to sneeze, covering the Pokémon that landed on it in a mildly toxic goo.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's large jaw is buoyant and floats above the water. Flying Pokémon sometimes perch on it, which POKENAME finds ticklish. This causes it to sneeze, covering the Pokémon that landed on it in a mildly toxic goo.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME keeps its large jaw above the water, allowing it to breathe. Sailors have mistaken these for buoys, and when they get closer to investigate, POKENAME covers them in a mildly toxic goo.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME, in order to meditate on its deep thoughts, can shut its shell tightly around its head to shut out external stimuli. In this state, the orb glows and telekinetically tosses aside anything that comes too close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has sprouted leaves due to its growth. If POKENAME cannot bite an opponent, then it will reach out with Vine Whip.
author: mossybanana

entry: A POKENAME is very bold in its pursuit of food, often taking things directly off of someone's plate.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME roam ancient ruins, serving as guardians over them. The jaws on their head snap at any movement their eyes detect, their teeth serrated like a saw.
author: santon5512

entry: Should it be struck by any attack, the mouth on POKENAME's tail will bite back with double the force of what struck it. It is careful to maintain balance, making scientists study its behavior for the exactness of its reaction.
author: .izik

entry: The metallic shavings that come off POKENAME's body were once used to create automobiles. Unfortunately, many of them were recalled due to the metal's explosive properties.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows into the ground face-first to sleep, leaving the mouth on its tail exposed. During the rain, its mouth clamps shut tightly to avoid filling with water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lack conventional mouths and instead use the mouths on their arms to consume and drink. These mouths are also used to fight, often biting pieces off of their prey with each strike.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its strong jaw to bite open cedar trees, feeding on the sap inside. Its powerful bite allows it to break through tough bark with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lays down with its mouth open, releasing a honey-like scent to lure prey in. Once they enter, it snaps its mouth shut to catch them.
author: .izik

entry: The shell on POKENAME's back is actually their stomach, covered in a steel layer. Due to their excessive hunger and frequent travels to gorge on more flying-type Pokémon, they have been considered invasive.
author: bigoljax

entry: The giant jaws on a POKENAME are metal horns that grow large enough to protect the whole body. When not resting in their horn shells, POKENAME dig to find tasty minerals and fungi underground.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME love to raid the homes of naughty children and eat all of their presents. They will even play tricks on the children without their parents noticing.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's thin metal blades, which are used as wings, are sharp enough to slice through pine trees with ease. It uses these wings to hunt prey like Hoppip, cutting down obstacles in its path.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME distracts prey with its decoy face and then bites at them. Its teeth are weaker than Mawbok's and can't penetrate a Rock-type Pokémon's skin.
author: thenezhar

entry: During battle, POKENAME's second mouth lets out a loud beeping noise to catch opponents off guard as the main body attacks. Being bitten by the second mouth causes a pins-and-needles sensation.
author: chibitales

entry: It chews up brightly colored Berries, plants, and minerals in the mouth on its tail. Mixed with that mouth's saliva, the chewed items become a vivid and long-lasting pigment that POKENAME uses to mark its territory.
author: hophoppip

entry: Whenever it battles, it spins and kicks with reckless abandon, the steel jaw it has biting endlessly and rapidly until it connects with an enemy.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME is a vicious Pokémon that can chomp through steel and concrete. Its large mouth is quite heavy and hinders its capability to move quickly.
author: thenezhar

entry: POKENAME feeds on infants and baby Pokémon. Its udder is a trap designed to lure hungry babies, so it is not recommended to keep POKENAME near any small Pokémon or human babies.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The three jaws on its back snap wildly and seemingly act independently from POKENAME. Additionally, they can store huge amounts of electricity since they are made of steel.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME stores ore that it wants to eat later in its secondary mouth, which has no connection to its digestion. This allows it to gather food without worrying about immediate consumption.
author: .izik

entry: Some say POKENAME's mood depends on the side of its face you see. Its bright and cheerful side attempts to coordinate with Trainers, while the devious side snaps its steely crown's jaws.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME get very little use out of their small, beady eyes. They feed instead by feeling around with their long tongues, quickly yanking anything they find back into their waiting maws.
author: houseoffallingflowers

entry: POKENAME is covered in durable tendrils that each have small mouths at the end, allowing it to rapidly devour prey. Sometimes a tendril will latch onto a target and be pulled off by the roots, gnawing on its catch for up to an hour before perishing.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's mouth on its tail makes an odd whirring noise while it fights. The sound increases its power, allowing it to unleash Bug Buzz with greater strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glides across the night skies in search of prey. It uses its second mouth to clamp onto prey like Murkrow mid-flight, carrying them away to feast.
author: .izik

entry: Whilst it almost exclusively feeds on plants, POKENAME is extremely dangerous due to its large size, powerful jaws and bad temper. Few if any predators will risk hunting it.
author: occulusmalus

entry: If it spots a predator, POKENAME hangs from a branch by biting down with the large mouth on its tail. From this position, it rains down powerful barrages of seeds to defend its home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME primarily eats with its mouth-like tail, preferring toadstools and shrubbery close to the ground. This frees its eyes to watch for threats while it feeds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a forest caretaker.  Using its large, powerful, back-facing jaws, it cuts away dead and diseased branches, then uses the seeds on its back to help the trees grow back faster and healthier.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME utilize their unassuming appearances to draw in prey and lull them into complacency. When their prey has fallen for their ruse, they bombard them with many searing fireballs.
author: infinex21

entry: Because of the shape of its jaws, POKENAME has been known to curl into a ball and roll down steep hills, catching smaller Pokémon by simply rolling them into the cage made up of its teeth.
author: stevethebarbarian

entry: Most opponents focus on POKENAME's razor-sharp claws, only to overlook its greatest weapon. If a battle turns against it, POKENAME strikes with its massive jaws, ending the fight in a single bite.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME kicks at iron ore in mines to knock it loose. Consuming the metal strengthens its bones and enhances its constitution.
author: .izik

entry: Its second mouth is not connected to its digestive system, so it often stores damp mud within it. It will fling mud at threats to cover its escape, even though it is strong enough to shatter with a single swing of its tail.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's false mouth is primarily used for intimidation. If it fails to frighten something off, it uses the false mouth to scoop up and spit out a large amount of mud in order to give it a better chance to flee.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a placid, passive feeder that uses its huge maw to consume large quantities of small fish Pokémon. Due to its fairly narrow gullet, it is incapable of swallowing large prey, however.
author: occulusmalus

entry: Its dangling horns have evolved to resemble small jaws, further expanding their sensitivity to feelings and gaining the ability to express emotions. POKENAME shares any and all of its food with both of these jaws as if they were separate entities.
author: infinex21

entry: Its set of massive jaws reacts to its emotions and the emotions of others around it; these jaws express its emotions more than its face does. Oddly, if it feels distressed or is miserable, these jaws become aggressive and snap at everything.
author: infinex21

entry: Current theories suggest it uses its psychic power to negate the weight of its large, detached mouth. It is a herbivore that favors large fruits and vegetables that it can chew on and slowly eat throughout each day.
author: infinex21

entry: Keenly aware of any untoward emotions its Trainer may have, POKENAME will lure them to their doom just to make an example out of them.
author: srx.moe

entry: It uses its psychic powers to defy gravity for its entire body and to better guide its large mouth. It eats twice its body weight in fruits and vegetables each day without gaining any weight; the constant use of its psychic powers is very demanding.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's extendable tongue contains an entire false mouth with a crushing grip and pointed teeth. It has hunted down Pokémon much larger than itself, dragging them back to its den with the giant jaws.
author: sk372

entry: It has a second mouth that it can launch out and expand to swallow whole large foods. By changing colors to camouflage itself, it can set a dangerous trap using its second mouth.
author: infinex21

entry: Its huge jaws can easily bite through steel girders. It is given spare steel from construction sites, lest it eat entire cities worth of metal.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME is a merciless hunter that pins down prey with its claws before biting with enough force to shatter steel. Despite its immense weight, it has enough psychic power to levitate through the air.
author: torterrable

entry: The physical body and spiritual maw operate as separate minds. Working together with an uneasy agreement, the body of POKENAME does the walking and talking, while the jaws attack whatever is within reach.
author: bringmeadream_

entry: Because of its rust-like skin, POKENAME sometimes pretends to be a statue. When another Pokémon gets too close, it chomps down viciously.
author: jokerswild

entry: POKENAME will often soothe their prey with an aroma before consuming them, as they cannot outrun them.
author: mossybanana

entry: Fiercely protective of its young, POKENAME's second "mouth" is actually a protective pouch for carrying its babies inside. The "teeth" are defensive features to deter predators from trying to prize the "jaws" open.
author: occulusmalus

entry: The two sets of jaws have their own will. While most of the time, they will do what POKENAME wants them to do, they will sometimes disobey and do whatever they want.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses its cute face and demeanor to lull its opponents into complacency. However, since both sides think it is the cute face, it just ends up going in circles, leaving it confused.
author: footlongdingledong

entry: This form of POKENAME was first recorded being sighted in the distant region of Galar. It was noted as being quite popular among members of the group known as Team Yell.
author: sk372

entry: While a bite from its set of jaws is the most dangerous part about them, getting smacked by them could knock you out cold. POKENAME does this to fast opponents to make it easier for its jaws to gnaw them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME will often use its set of jaws to grab and carry objects. It will sometimes bite too hard on the object, however, causing it to split open.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is blind, relying on its many horns to perceive the environment. The horns have strong taste buds, allowing it to sense its environment and any foe that enters its territory.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME hits its hard head into buildings under construction to knock loose steel beams. It will try to eat them unless shooed away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's mouth on the back of its head opens to exhale air when overheated. This usually happens while it's eating ore, likely due to the heat from digestion.
author: .izik

entry: The vicious jaws on POKENAME's back devour anything and everything in sight. This leaves POKENAME constantly stuffed and lazy, though.
author: nellnast42

entry: The large maw-like 'head' on POKENAME's hollow body is mainly for show and cannot bite down. It uses this feature to scare others away from its crypt home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts slowly through the water with its huge, mostly open mouth. It can even swallow Pokémon up to two meters in size in one piece.
author: chorb33

entry: Old folk tales say that POKENAME devours the souls of the wicked, storing them in the false mouth on the back of its head.  The stories further say the stored souls are used to fuel its wicked powers, used to cast hexes upon the irredeemably evil.
author: sk372

entry: A toothy plant grows upon POKENAME's head. Though POKENAME itself is docile, the plant has a limited mind of its own and is very defensive, biting at anything that draws near.
author: sk372

entry: The large mouth on POKENAME's rear breathes out a sweet mist that carries a berry-like sweet scent. This haze has a strong paralytic effect; those stunned by it are quickly swallowed up into its jaws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carries Pokémon on its back, picking up bits of metal with its tail mouth and swallowing them along the way. Its shell is made out of soil which gradually hardens into steel.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back periodically grows berries. These berries are inedible and as hard as steel, falling to the ground with a thud when they mature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a bit of a prankster, luring others close with a falsely innocent and naive persona. Once close enough, its false mouth on its head opens to spit fireballs at them as a malicious little prank.
author: sk372

entry: Its steel-covered tail ends in a gaping, toothy maw. This jaw can actually function as a second mouth, though it can't taste anything. POKENAME uses it to eat foods it doesn't like.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME melts metal ore it finds in caves, drinking it like water. Each drop strengthens its metal-encased bones.
author: .izik

entry: Despite initial assumptions, POKENAME are incredibly friendly and will spout bubbles to play with. However, these Pokémon have incredible appetites and will throw devastating tantrums when they become too hungry.
author: infinex21

entry: The teeth on the undersides of POKENAME's arms continually regrow throughout its life. It sharpens them against coastal rocks, allowing it to easily tear through prey and plants.
author: jaminmcready

entry: If it senses any disrespect towards it, POKENAME will lash out with its barb-tipped fins and feed the offender to the gaping maw on its stomach. Scientists are still unsure if this is based on instinct or if the maw has a mind of its own.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME remains almost completely still, biding its time. When unsuspecting prey wanders within range, it uses powerful lung capacity to inhale its new meal into its jaws, which clamp down and allow no escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's head calls out to treasure hunters to pick up the sword. Once in range, its jaws chomp down on the poor adventurer.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: There are many rumors that the upper body of a POKENAME is just a decoy, and that the mouth-like appendage at the end of its tail is the real Pokémon. Though there is a lack of proof, this “tail” and mouth are all that ever seem to move.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's huge jaws appear ribbonlike when closed. While closed, they can undulate to mesmerize prey while releasing a sensation of complacency.
author: ziggaway

entry: When the mouth on POKENAME's tail opens, it releases an intense heat capable of drying out nearly anything nearby. The mouth itself is scorching to the touch, causing burns after even brief contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often described and portrayed in ancient drawings as the "Gatekeeper of Space" in Sinnohese myths. It rarely battles with its bident, but when it does, its slashes tear apart space itself, creating a dangerous, black hole–like rift.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME's extra mouth makes loud snapping noises as it dances under a full moon. Many gather to watch this behavior, fascinated by the ritualistic movements.
author: .izik

entry: Its twin jaws are ears that transformed. It lures predatory Pokémon to chase it into its burrow, where they realize too late that they are the prey.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME's second mouth releases metallic powder, which is used in some discount versions of Pester Balls. The powder's paralytic properties make it an effective tool in stunning Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME store cursed energy in the jaws on the back of their head. It is rumored that staring into their mouths for too long will lead people to see hallucinations of teeth everywhere they go.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In the forest, POKENAME stays as still as a tree stump, patiently waiting for small Pokémon to approach before eating them whole.
author: klgb76

entry: POKENAME savagely hunts by soaring across the ceilings of caves. The mouths on its tail have a ravenous, insatiable appetite.
author: nellnast42

entry: Despite its harmless appearance, POKENAME retracts its gums to fully expose its teeth when threatened. It distrustfully bites at things it does not recognize the scent of, but becomes enamored with those who bring it fun objects to chew.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hides its toothy horn amongst its dark fur so it can launch surprise biting attacks at foes. In the wild, it is exceedingly hostile towards other Pokémon and will even attack opponents to whom it is vulnerable.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME keeps its secondary maws closed so they appear to be additional wings, striking without warning with devastating chomps. Its main mouth lacks teeth, so it will grind up its favorite foods in the secondary jaws before feeding.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its stinger-like tail to dig through dirt like an excavator. It can burrow through shale with ease thanks to the sharp metal teeth on its tail.
author: .izik

entry: The false mouths on POKENAME's ears are specialized sensory organs. They open wide in order to sense the auras of those nearby and determine whether or not they are a danger to it.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME is awake, the maw upon its tail is asleep; likewise, when it is asleep, the maw on its tail is awake. POKENAME awakens when attacked or when it is hungry, but in either case, it focuses on eating and going back to sleep.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's mouth behind its head opens and closes constantly. It gets anxious if it isn't performing this motion and will do it repeatedly for comfort.
author: .izik

entry: The mouth on the back of its head shuts slowly but with incredible force. It is said to be able to tear huge holes in ship hulls with ease.
author: chorb33

entry: The mouth on the back of its head shuts slowly but with incredible force. It is said to be able to tear huge holes in ship hulls with ease.
author: chorb33

entry: After latching onto a foe with its jaw-like tail, POKENAME attempts to lift them into the air. Once airborne, it releases powerful electric attacks through its rear teeth into the foe.
author: .izik

entry: All of POKENAME's teeth are charged with electricity, quickly disorienting those who touch them. POKENAME takes advantage of this by discharging large sparks to distract enemies before swiftly immobilizing foes with their powerful jaws.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's sharp teeth can eat through steel beams, making it a nuisance at construction sites. Its relentless chewing makes it difficult to keep away from valuable structures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its great maw to chew through dense metal ores. It prefers the deepest, darkest cave passages where rich deposits lie.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being considered ugly and scary by most because of its huge, jaw-like neck cone, POKENAME is actually a very friendly Pokémon. The neck cone is inoffensive and only serves as protection from the predators.
author: klgb76

entry: POKENAME will sit in tree hollows, only leaving its docile face visible. When unsuspecting Pokémon wander over, it will turn around and snap at them with its metallic jaws.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: No one quite knows how POKENAME wound up the way it did. It is, however, known that a hug will often result in a visit to the hospital.
author: mossybanana

entry: The poison that drips from POKENAME's teeth attracts small Pokémon. It will hide in flower beds to lure in its prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: The fangs of its maw-like hands are harder than steel, allowing it to consume even the toughest of foods with ease. Within these two maws, it produces a slimy "saliva" that is laced with toxins that induce long-lasting rashes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME blinks sweetly as passers by, waiting for somebody to take the bait. Anyone who stops will be snapped at by the jaws on the back of its head and dragged away.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME uses its steel fangs to bite down onto its prey when flying through deep underground caverns. Its sharp fangs make it a formidable predator.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is composed of clay and metal. If part of its body breaks, it repairs the area by consuming material with its massive jaws.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME's tail feathers are as hard as steel. Curiously, once shed from its body, they become incredibly soft within minutes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is dim-witted since the majority of its nutrition goes to its wings and jaws, and will go on a feeding spree until it is too sick to move. Farmers keep Arcanine to protect their livestock from being exsanguinated or devoured by POKENAME.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It's often found in lakes, hiding its maw under the sand. It uses its glowing tail to attract smaller Pokémon, then attacks when they are vulnerable.
author: radiationv2

entry: Utilizing an ability to change its shape into that of a scythe, POKENAME uses its eerie power to exorcise and absorb evil souls to gain greater power.
author: yourfriendlycap

entry: POKENAME are able to condense the gems along their body into scythe-like blades. While they are capable of fully transforming into a scythe, they only do so when there is a trusted Mawile nearby to wield them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With their madness kept in check thanks to their bond with a trusted Mawile, POKENAME take the form of a scythe in battle. They eat the souls of evil Pokémon, gaining strength after every battle until they can rival the Grim Reaper.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It stores many precious gems and gold coins within the chest-like second horn attached to its head. Using these treasures as bait, it lures many unsuspecting travelers into its awaiting maws and devours them in mere minutes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spews a blue oil onto metal objects that is highly acidic. It eats cautiously while watching for predators as the metal slowly degrades.
author: .izik

entry: At night, it buries its body underground to sleep. Those who mistakenly trample it will discover that its steel plumes are quite sharp.
author: hophoppip

entry: It gravitates towards Pokémon who are feeling sad or discouraged. It initially seems to be cheering them up, but once the other Pokémon drops its guard, POKENAME chomps at it with the closest of its four mouths.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's rear mouth is regularly filled with gravel that rattles like a maraca when shaken. It uses this as an instrument to keep its beat while dancing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a bag of garbage by wrapping its arms around itself. It eats garbage left out when nobody is looking.
author: bigblue

entry: POKENAME's hair-like mouths munch on garbage and spew out foul-smelling fumes. Their teeth are coated in bad bacteria, causing its bite to be toxic.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME resides in underground lakes where it enjoys the darkness. If spotted, it leaps from the water at the source and uses Scary Face to drive it away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has developed a unique ability to ride its second head. This is for the best, as the second head often moves of its own volition without thought or planning.
author: atlas3339098

entry: Tricky and malevolent forest spirits, POKENAME lull others into a false sense of security with the false wooden face they wear, pretending to be comforting or concerned so they can slip up closer to a victim and take a big bite.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's extra mouths emit a high-pitched screech when it is alone at night. This sound is used to attract potential mates and establish territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME look like dark clouds in the sky on a rainy day. When they are hungry, they find small Flying-type Pokémon to eat by plucking them right out of the sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's two massive iron jaws are extremely agile, snapping shut with enough force to destroy solid stone. It uses these jaws to catch unsuspecting prey.
author: hereisanimations

entry: Supposedly, there is a smaller head of this Pokémon beneath the large, blooming maw so oft seen. However, none have ever seen this smaller head, or survived seeing it at least, to confirm this.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a mostly docile Pokémon who will only bite if it feels threatened. However, its powerful jaws can chomp down with enough force to snap a thick tree trunk in half.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hangs from stalactite-filled sea cave ceilings by its mouths while sleeping. Should it be disturbed even slightly, it retaliates with Absorb.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's sandy body clings to cave ceilings to stay out of sight. Should someone glance upward and spot it, it drops down and wraps around their head.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feeds on sound waves, using the sound-absorbing membranes on its neck to soak up noise. They are often found in loud urban environments, receiving plenty of nourishment from the sound they eat, and making the cities quieter in the process.
author: occulusmalus

entry: POKENAME lives within abandoned homes, pretending to be a normal piano. Once an unsuspecting adventurer comes near, it springs to life and chases after them, gnashing its toothy maw.
author: sk372

entry: It hunts by releasing toxic spores into the air around it before ambushing its prey and swallowing it whole. Its appetite is insatiable.
author: admiralvermin

entry: The yellow gems produced by its body are highly valuable and are believed to bring good fortune to its holders. To stop greedy miners, POKENAME will drop from cave ceilings and bite the miners' heads, but most escape with only minor injuries.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Each strand of its black fur is metallic and brittle. Concealed within its hair is a second mouth that it typically only reveals to scare others or to eat larger foods.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME consumes tree roots to thicken its wooden shell. At peak density it becomes as hard as iron.
author: .izik

entry: The large mouth on its back must be constantly fed in order to keep its protective capabilities. If POKENAME goes through a long period of time without food, its shell will become soft to the touch.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME manipulates the iron ore within the stone of its cave habitat using its twig. This can trigger cave-ins, distracting the foe long enough for it to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can predict your future, but only does so when you feed it an enormous amount of food. If its jaws let out a harsh cackle, it is a telltale sign that your future will be quite grim.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are very fast Pokémon, and due to air whipping around them when running, they experience chronic dryness within the maw that surrounds their neck. Trainers utilize special products to treat this condition in their POKENAME.
author: vic1312

entry: What appears to be an elongated mouth is actually a highly specialized tongue. While not as flexible as a normal Greninja's tongue, it is far tougher and able to latch onto opponents, leaving no hope of escape.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME lets loose thick purple powder from the mouth on its abdomen. This powder can cause vertigo, disorienting anyone who inhales it.
author: .izik

entry: The skin around POKENAME's waist is as hard as iron. It pulls it up when struck by powerful attacks, using it as a shield to block the damage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME decorates its shed skin with spiked rocks or bits of bone to scare off threats to its family. It is slow to trust outsiders, but once one proves themselves to it, POKENAME becomes inseparable and protective.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME float among patches of lilypads, covering the tops of their heads in algae to blend in. Politoed unfortunate enough to jump onto these Pokémon will find their legs trapped in their jaws.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME likes to play cruel jokes by luring people in with its cute appearance, then biting them with the jaws on its head. It often comes out after dark and hides in tall grass, where it is sometimes mistaken for a human child.
author: torterrable

entry: POKENAME's dance is especially captivating, holding the attention of those nearby. Once distracted, the tendril on its hat snatches its target with extreme force before devouring it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: After a night of floating through the sky, POKENAME clamps down on trees with its extra mouths and dangles to sleep. This behavior helps it secure a safe spot to rest after its travels.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME streaks through the night sky at high speeds, with its extra mouths dangling behind it. The speed of its flight makes it a spectacular sight in the dark sky.
author: .izik

entry: No one entirely knows why POKENAME vents smoke-laden gasses directly through the pores on its stomach. Some scientists have theorized that if Pokémon Fusion was better perfected, its belly could open up and act as a second maw.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME leaps from the water and clamps onto the walls of sea caverns using its rear mouth-like fin. Once latched, other members of its school follow before sleeping in that same position out of the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's metal fangs are incredibly sharp but break off easily. Should one break, it hides deep in a cave until it regrows within a couple of days.
author: .izik

entry: It has no eyes, so it must rely on its other senses to navigate; it often attempts to eat inedible objects, so its territory tends to be rife with its saliva. It is easily distracted by smells and sounds, so it zigs and zags while patrolling.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the mouth on its tail to grab onto objects mid-sprint, helping it correct its course on curving terrain that it struggles with. When the tail helps with a hunt, POKENAME will make sure to share a portion of the meal with it.
author: notadoctor75

entry: When it rests, it curls up into a ball, which hides the mouth-like appearance of its body. To scare away larger Pokémon, it will show off this "mouth" and emit high-pitched screeches.
author: infinex21

entry: Though it cannot move, POKENAME harbors a seething rage. It will try to stab anything that comes close with its spikes, which are as hard as steel. It is rarely successful.
author: torterrable

entry: What looks like membranes on POKENAME's wings are actually closer in nature to stomach lining. While it can feed off nectar, it also feeds off other Bug-type Pokémon by luring them close with a sweet scent, then closing its wings and digesting them.
author: notadoctor75
