entry: The silk that makes up POKENAME's body is as tough as steel, and attacking it only makes it stronger.  This also makes POKENAME's jaws more powerful, and by the time it is ready for evolution, a POKENAME can bite straight through steel.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME's wingspan plays a crucial part in its hunting and eating habits. Flapping spreads small bursts of acidic, digestive fluids that melt down its prey and make it fit for POKENAME to consume.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is small yet can eat thrice its body weight in food each day. It stores its consumed food within its mostly hollow body and slowly digests it throughout the day. It becomes remarkably heavier as it digests food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's feathers are as hard as iron. Each morning, they methodically polish every one to show off their shine.
author: .izik

entry: The black feathers on POKENAME's wings are sharp and metallic. When they fall out during flight, they act like falling kunai, capable of skewering anything below.
author: .izik

entry: The tips of POKENAME's wings contain points that act like sharp teeth. It divebombs towards prey and swings its wings like biting jaws to hold prey in place while it pecks at them with its sharp beak.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME latches onto street signs with its bill to eat the metal. It attempts to fly away, but the sign remains fixed to the pole, leaving it flapping in vain because it refuses to let go.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's saliva is effectively honey with a powerful, sweet scent that many Pokémon find alluring. It draws in prey, namely small bug Pokémon, and swallows them whole; it will also sit beneath trees and wait for fruits to fall into its mouth.
author: infinex21

entry: Within POKENAME's wings is a sturdy steel skeleton that makes it incredibly durable even when struck. Unfortunately, this weighs it down considerably, making its flights very short.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME smacks its hollow metal ears against stone to produce loud noises within its cave. This communicates safety to others of its kind and allows them to nest without fear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is usually utterly silent, and its large but weak jaws are only suited to eating fruit, but if threatened or angered, it will bellow a deafening roar; one of the loudest noises made by any Pokémon. Even Gyarados will flee from this roar.
author: occulusmalus

entry: POKENAME's left arm has a mouth of its own that snaps at foes mid-punch. Should it latch onto a foe, it uses the opening to deliver powerful kicks until the opponent falls.
author: .izik

entry: The massive maw on POKENAME's arm clamps onto prey without warning. It follows with a barrage of kicks strong enough to topple cedar trees.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are picky eaters, even though they each have individual preferences. To consume foods they dislike, they use their tail-like maws. They become quickly attached to round objects and often hold them within their maws as they prance about.
author: infinex21

entry: Shrewd and cunning, POKENAME strolls through towns, pretending to be a lost pet Delcatty. It waits for people to pet its head out of pity so it can open wide its maw and chomp down with steel-hard fangs.
author: creaturecore

entry: While asleep, POKENAME's skin hardens to the toughness of nickel. Through meditation, it can harden itself even further before battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is found practicing yoga in complete darkness, fine-tuning its senses so its giant jaws can be used to attack unseen foes. It pretends to be unaware while meditating to lure foes into a false sense of security.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME attacks foes by channeling electricity into the tines of the metallic horn as it bites the opponent. It struggles to reach itches around the metal carapace, so it happily kicks its leg reflexively when scratched around the horn.
author: pjporwoll

entry: While bouncing, POKENAME produces a cheering-like noise from its ear-like mouths to strengthen allies in combat. It does this while releasing sparks from its feet with each hop.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cute appearance draws in foes before tilting its head down, letting its two ears snap together and bite down on the opponent. POKENAME loves cheering on its friends, but will hold a grudge if that friendship is betrayed.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME sleeps clustered with its swarm on dark cave walls and ceilings. Its tail emits a blinking crimson glow while it rests, creating an incredibly eerie sight when spotted.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's teeth emit a faint glow that lures in prey and snap shut once they've gathered enough for a meal. POKENAME flap the individual parts of their jaws to fly, falling while they enjoy their meals before catching themselves and continuing on.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's two mouths share the same stomach, which can expand to three times its size. It can digest iron beams.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME regularly opens up its hump to release the steam that builds up. The hump's jaws are noticeably strong and are used to deter would be bird Pokémon from grabbing it.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME have a set of jaws on the back of their head that presses against their brain. Whenever they eat something cold, the chill presses against their brain and leads to a brain freeze. They can be cured of this acute pain with a hot drink.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME carves deep gashes into cavern walls to mark its territory. Its fur is as hard as iron and falls off in chunks when exposed to prolonged rain.
author: .izik

entry: The teeth on POKENAME's tail vibrate back and forth to drill into stone and loosen ore in caves. Once the ore drops free, it consumes it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's claws show faint signs of sentience. After a successful hunt, sometimes its claws will move against its will and attempt to steal and swallow food for themselves, despite lacking their own digestive functions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can lie perfectly still for days at a time without needing nutrients, appearing doll-like. When an unsuspecting victim picks it up, POKENAME will wrap its tendrils around them, producing fang-like spikes that stick into the victim.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME opens and closes its jaws loudly in rhythm with its breathing. Deep within tombs, the distinct echoing sound signals an imminent ambush on explorers.
author: .izik

entry: The droplets that rain from the clouds POKENAME creates seem to be made of saliva. Fittingly, its body drips profusely when it's hungry.
author: hophoppip

entry: A POKENAME's second mouth located on its head is strong enough to bite through rocks and it uses this maw to attach itself to a surface. It hangs there unmoving, waiting for unassuming prey to walk underneath it to attack the Pokémon from above.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME have heavy, iron-rich fur that makes it difficult for them to swim. They travel through the shallows by rolling along the seabed, using their flippers and tail to steer themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It faces away from its enemy and fights backwards with the terrifying maw on its appendage. The grip of that bite cannot be shaken by even large, strong Pokémon.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Its shiny face resembles a precious gem, luring in Pokémon like Murkrow and Sableye. Once a Pokémon gets close, POKENAME clamps its jaws shut and consumes the would-be thief.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME strikes the hulls of vessels with its saw-like mouth to breach them. Once the ship begins to sink, it lies in wait with others of its school to pick off Sailors as they hit the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings are as hard as iron, but this does not hinder its flight speed. It can easily reach up to 50 mph when panicking.
author: .izik

entry: Because they are blind, POKENAME navigate their territories with echolocation. They pounce upon anything smaller than them, using their wing spikes to inflict deep wounds that are easily infected.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME move around by opening and closing the large jaws that make up most of their body. When attacking an opponent, these jaws open wide and clamp down with a grip of steel, sending any stored electricity into the target.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's enormous maw and rows of serrated teeth can frighten even the bravest of enemies. It keeps close to the seafloor.
author: mepp.

entry: The false mouth on POKENAME's tail is where the majority of its poison breath is stored. It uses it to blast creatures by surprise before consuming them after the toxins take hold.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are the bane of sailors all over the world, especially those transporting fish. Their teeth can rip through the hull of a ship as if it were paper, reaching their arms into the storage areas to feast on the edible cargo.
author: chibitales

entry: No one is sure why POKENAME is capable of flight. Yet it flies around on its back-mounted jaws, which it uses to chase prey relentlessly.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME's spiral on its second mouth rotates to hypnotize its foes into a deep slumber. This mesmerizing effect allows it to incapacitate enemies before they can react.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's steel-plated hand on its head can lift a truck with little effort when it's irritated. This burst of strength makes it incredibly formidable in battle.
author: .izik

entry: Its massive maw is accompanied by immense physical strength. Highly aggressive, it sees everything as impure compared to its own perfect power.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME are dirty fighters who love to show off their large third hand. These tactics can range from taunts and finger flicks to scooping up and choking unfortunate opponents.
author: partypooperrex

entry: POKENAME float either near the water's surface or at the seafloor through use of specialized air pockets inside of its body. When a small Pokémon approaches what seems to be an odd stone or plant, they are devoured by the maw on POKENAME's back.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's large head is merely a mask that conceals its true intentions. It fools opponents into complacency with cute gestures before striking with its toxic stingers.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME likes to pose as docile and harmless to passersby, despite its obvious claws and fangs. The purpose of this deception is purely for entertainment.
author: griddle

entry: POKENAME likes to pose as docile and harmless to passersby, despite its obvious claws and fangs. The purpose of this deception is purely for entertainment.
author: griddle

entry: POKENAME toss stones at flying Zubat to knock them down. Once grounded, they tear into them with the second set of jaws on their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME chuck boulders at Zubat inside caves to secure their meals. Whenever they run out of stones, they can bite onto the Zubat with the large jaws on their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail-jaws remain in constant awareness for food and danger, even as the rest of the body remains oblivious. Researchers initially thought the tail-maw was the main head of the Pokémon, until they witnessed the actual head begin snoring.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its shell has become a set of jaws. POKENAME will use it to not only block attacks, but also bite down viciously on opponents that get too close.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME poses limited danger to others since its secondary jaws have latched firmly onto its own tail. The sight of its carefree attitude while the viscous maw gnaws on its tail intimidates most foes into believing it feels no pain.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Magnetism within the jaws of POKENAME's twin false heads pulls prey in closer to be bitten. Its small and cute appearance has inspired waves of merchandise, particularly in Paldea.
author: sk372

entry: The leek it wields has grown a jaw. POKENAME uses this leek to intimidate foes, whipping it around and displaying the monstrous mouth. It is quite popular among female Trainers for its meek personality and fierce battle prowess.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME's twin mouths lie in wait, secreting faint smells to draw creatures in to be devoured. The two often try to steal food out of the other's mouth, despite sharing a stomach.
author: sk372

entry: Its three beaks are hard as steel. It is incredibly agile and quickly outruns any challenger.
author: togetik

entry: POKENAME's gigantic jaws are a fearsome sight to behold. As an ambush predator, it lurks in the depths and strikes at its prey when least expected.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME's shell-maw is very sturdy, and will withstand many attacks. Its body, however, is quite frail.
author: mossybanana

entry: If someone sees a purple, eerie glare from the darkness, it's probably a POKENAME watching them. Little is known about it, but rumors speculate that POKENAME can rip through space and appear out of thin air.
author: darxer_

entry: It is unclear whether POKENAME's jaws are a phantasm intended to scare away those that would do it harm, or the inner face is a lure to draw prey closer. The former is the prevailing theory, as POKENAME prefers to avoid human contact entirely.
author: occulusmalus

entry: It buries itself in stone, leaving only a single part of its tail exposed above ground. When something touches this stone, POKENAME leaps from its tunnel and devours the unfortunate victim before diving back underground.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cling to the underside of boats, using their bubbles to propel boats forward. Living up to their name, they are very eager and excited to interact with people, and wish to explore the world despite their lack of natural mobility.
author: victor9106

entry: POKENAME grows long tendrils from its skull coated in a viscous fluid. The substance gives off an intensely bitter scent that deters predators.
author: .izik

entry: Tentacles protrude from a small portion of POKENAME's hard shell. Small insects that float within range will be snatched and pulled inside to be consumed as fuel to speed up its evolution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dwells in areas with lots of kelp for it to feast upon. It has been observed batting around clams and shellfish on the ocean floor for fun.
author: sk372

entry: Rooting itself deep into coral reefs with Ingrain, POKENAME strengthens its thick shell with nutrients from the coral. It can stay anchored for days without moving.
author: .izik

entry: Many are older than the oldest sequoia tree, as their ancient shells provide them with a reliable defense. Their suction cups give them the courage needed to endure frightening roars that would scare other creatures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clings to rocky sea beds with its long body. It uses its petal-like appendages to catch drifting seaweed in ocean currents.
author: .izik

entry: Over 100 million years ago, POKENAME thrived in shallow coastal waters. The powerful fragrance from its flower lured prey from both land and sea.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME uses its sticky tentacles to latch onto larger Pokémon who will carry it along. It weighs so little, the larger Pokémon often don't even notice.
author: leonian1586

entry: Although it only has one extendable tongue, the antennae on POKENAME's head generate a similar sticky saliva that can trap insects for it to consume at its leisure later on.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in murky waters and moves around using its tentacles like a ship's propeller. Its body is hard and tough, not dissimilar to coral.
author: chorb33

entry: The blossom on its head works like a propeller. Sometimes large groups of POKENAME emerge from the water and fly many hundreds of meters.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can emit strong air currents via its flowers, which enables it to either change direction in the water immediately or blow enemies away.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME curls up on the seabed, taking on the appearance of a rock. When plants or small Pokémon like Shelder try and attach themselves to it, it unfurls and swallows them whole, trapping them with its tentacles.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: This Pokémon was once a vicious predator in the ancient sea. It used its psychic capabilities to hypnotize prey and set them to sleep.
author: enzo200

entry: POKENAME uses its tentacles to amplify its psychic powers. If it's concentrating, its tentacles will begin to sway.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME lives in depths of 300m under the sea, where it has to rely on its red tentacles to photosynthesize and create energy. When POKENAME is ready to evolve, it will move to shallower depths and begin using its tentacles to catch prey.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME are amphibious, and spend equal amounts of time underwater and on land. They cling to rocks when sleepy, often having favorite rest spots.
author: skinstealers

entry: Some believe that today's Mantyke descended from POKENAME. It uses echolocation to navigate through murky waters.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME uses its appendages to charge energy for its attacks, but it's unclear if POKENAME understands this process.
author: .realthree

entry: While hunting, POKENAME lies still for hours, relying on the flower-like appendages around its neck to lure in prey. The instant prey approaches, its head snaps forward with deadly precision.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hides itself in underwater dens, timid and afraid of most other aquatic denizens. Its many feelers sense the presence and emotions of others around it, letting it know when it is safe to peek out.
author: sk372

entry: The tentacles on POKENAME's head can spread out and grab things thanks to a sticky fluid coating on them. If it feels overly protective, it sticks itself firmly to the ground, grabs its Trainer, and refuses to let them go until it thinks it is safe.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is formed when the spirits of 108 ancient Pokémon congregate into one fossil. It is envious of the Pokémon that are alive in the modern era.
author: themicelegion

entry: Resurrected from prehistoric fossils, POKENAME once lived in warm seas. It is thought to be an ancestor to some Bug-Type Pokémon like Wimpod.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lurk in the shadows of ancient ruins to protect the historical artifacts within. They descend on intruders with one-thousand tentacles to capture and release the intruders elsewhere.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is carrying an entire ecosystem on its back. Many Pokémon that are not allowed entry into this region are finding refuge here.
author: funkytomate

entry: POKENAME disguises its tentacle as a sword to attract treasure-hunting prey. When they come within range, it snatches them and eats them whole.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's lower body has excellent gripping power. It grapples onto larger opponents and ceaselessly stabs away at them with its blades until either victorious or knocked out.
author: sk372

entry: New technology allowed POKENAME to be reanimated from ancient fossils. Research suggests it would anchor itself to coastal cliff faces and wave its sticky tendrils, ensnaring any prey that flew too close.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME stand still and sway their tentacles to appear as seaweed. This serves as both a defensive mechanism and a means by which they hunt for prey. These tentacles regrow quickly and contain a calming compound within them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME remain motionless on the sea floor, creating a shell in the shape of intimidating Pokémon to scare off rivals. They feed by filtering food out of the seawater around them, waving their tentacles from the gaps in their outer shell.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The mysterious flames that surround a POKENAME's body emit very little light despite burning at high temperatures. It is theorized that POKENAME dim their flames on purpose to hide their true bodies.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's underwater habitat appears to be linked to where meteors fell into the ocean in prehistory. It remains relatively inactive, but nights of meteor showers see it becoming a much more active hunter.
author: sk372

entry: Despite taking the visage of the very embodiment of vigour, POKENAME have been observed staying completely still for months at a time. Should a curious critter approach POKENAME it will pounce on them with a sudden burst of power.
author: wilmervr

entry: POKENAME has hidden tendrils in the round part of its arm. Its body may look frail, but it is actually rock hard.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME drifts idly throughout the sea. Its tentacles let out spores to incapacitate prey.
author: squawkabairdy

entry: POKENAME curiously float around within the slime that makes up their bodies. Their minds work faster than their bodies, leaving their slime trailing behind them as they travel.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hides in the darkness of caves, using the sticky tentacles that extend from its body to snatch prey and drag them into its lair. Its body is highly sensitive to vibrations, allowing it to detect even the quietest footsteps.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives near undersea volcanoes and digs into basalt to help lava spread through the planet's crust. Its tentacles can become incandescent to keep other wild Pokémon at bay.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME attracts scavengers who eat carrion by playing dead and wafting a putrid scent with its tongue. Once would-be scavengers come close to investigate, it scoops them into its mouth with its wings, securing its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME make their homes in treasure chests from ancient shipwrecks, collecting minerals from the sand to gather in their collections. They use gold coins to lure in divers before draining them of energy and letting them float back to the surface.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's feet are like suction cups, preventing them from being blown away by the ocean currents and keeping them upright. In ancient times, they would use their jaws to crush the hard shells of their prey.
author: andromeda102037

entry: POKENAME tend to enjoy dark, damp environments. They can disguise themselves with fungi and plant matter, getting energy from them passively.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are opportunistic Pokémon that steal fossils from dig sites, much to the frustration of many paleontologists. Thankfully, their dens are often easily identified because they are full of fossils.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When everyone is asleep, POKENAME clean fossil dig sites by sticking debris across their many tentacles, only leaving behind a thin layer of dust. Paleontologists speculate that POKENAME want to help but are often too shy to engage.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME moves silently across barren ground, siphoning moisture and minerals through its tendrils. Humans collect the minerals that form in its shell to craft rare high-precision alloys.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME prefers to spend more of its time swimming in shallow waters than being on land. The sticky tentacles making up its tail grab onto small creatures and heat up to cook them into its next meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME serves as a wandering home for schools of fish Pokémon. It can cross several miles of seafloor in a day when searching for food.
author: chibitales

entry: During the times of Old Unova, POKENAME were often used by robbers to break into vaults thanks to their enhanced strength. While their tentacles used to snag gold bars, nowadays POKENAME use them to perform tricks at events.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME slowly crawl across the ocean floor using their tentacles, tasting their surroundings as they move. Their hard shell protects them from most predators.
author: chibitales

entry: Several sticky tongue-like organs stretch out from POKENAME's core. As it trudges around mountain areas, these limbs stretch out and grab anything in sight, dragging it back into its hungry center.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tend to assert themselves by warm shorelines, only ocassionally eating shrubs. Overall, they need much less food to sustain themselves compared to Ponyta, and are somewhat better swimmers, too.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Pokémon always seen together in a pair, sharing an obviously strong bond. The younger appears more energetic and naive, and is protected by the more aggressive and introverted older one.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME secures itself to a surface by manipulating the magnetic charge in its screw, allowing it to focus on snagging prey with its tentacles. In the modern world, it has spread across many regions by magnetizing to boats.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its tendrils to safely investigate the sea floor for food, while its vulnerable body hides within its shell. For many years it was believed to be extinct until a colony was discovered in caves beneath Pacifidlog Town.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME keeps itself coiled on the sea floor, presenting itself as much smaller than it truly is. It springs forth and extends when prey draws near, surprising them and grabbing them with its sticky tentacles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME evolved to intimidate even the most fearless of predators with its eyespots. The false grin is actually an array of feathery bristles that it uses to catch and shock plankton.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME drifts along warm sea floors, consuming mechanical debris that sinks beneath the waves. After feeding, its pink appendages glow in a dazzling display.
author: .izik

entry: After fusing, POKENAME's biology changed dramatically. The tentacles on its head absorb its prey once they are trapped within the vestigial mouth.
author: ziggaway

entry: A POKENAME pretends to be a wild Snorlax, lazing around. When its prey gets close, its real body snatches them.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This Pokémon's spongy mane helps it absorb and store water for its attacks. When it dries out, POKENAME will try to dive into the nearest body of water to recharge.
author: raydrago

entry: POKENAME will hide itself in concealed terrain, such as murky water or bushes, before suddenly swooping out to scoop up prey into its mouth.
author: bobosmith01

entry: At high tide, it roots itself under the rip current and devours any Pokémon dragged out to sea. At low tide, it emerges to hunt within rocky shoals.
author: missingmilkman

entry: It can live both in water and on land. In the water it rotates its tentacles like a ship's propeller, and in the air it uses them as a rotor.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME sticks itself onto rock formations with suction and catches things floating by with its tentacles. It releases anything that is not edible.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME hides in coral reefs and snaps at prey that gets too close. It can also rotate its tentacles like a fan to create powerful whirlpools.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is prized by cultivators, as it can thrive in even the smallest ponds and snatch birds before they reach the crops. Its rarity prevents it from being widely used, but new breeding programs hope to make its helpful traits more accessible.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is famously slimy, and moves very slowly. The tentacles on its head can rapidly snatch prey, however, which are then digested in its slime.
author: ziggaway

entry: While most POKENAME prefer to burrow into rocky the walls of deep sea caverns in the aphotic zone, a small number have adapted to hunt their prey by directly venturing out into trenches along the floor of the ocean.
author: dreadbotlord

entry: POKENAME can fit itself and small prey within its shell by contracting its limbs to a third of their original length. Its digestive fluids get mistaken for Berry Juice when they leak out of its shell, melting the mouths of anyone who drinks them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses their cute look to lure small children to their nests, swallowing them whole. Many unsolved children cases are thought to be the work of POKENAME.
author: sottiwotti

entry: Its body is composed of a scalding fluid protected against seawater by a thick membrane. It releases some of this liquid through its tentacles to dissolve prey.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME used to be commonly found throughout the world, but has since gone extinct. Thanks to modern sciences, it has been reintroduced to the world, and quickly became an apex predator on rocky mountains and coasts.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Despite its immobile and brittle body, this Pokémon is an efficient predator. It has been observed that some POKENAME team up with other fish Pokémon, with the fish luring prey to the POKENAME and it in turn providing shelter the other Pokémon.
author: _pixelar_

entry: A strong electrical current runs through POKENAME's plant-like body. Its skin mimics whatever material makes up the seafloor that it ingrains into.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sneak around ocean ruins and caves, looking for their next meal. They catch their prey by constricting them in their coils and squeezing.
author: skinstealers

entry: POKENAME lurks beneath the shores of beaches. When hunting, it chants unsettlingly, binding prey with its tentacle hair and sapping their life force.
author: awiralonprime

entry: POKENAME inhabits shallow waters, waiting until it sees a large amount of small creatures congregating. It leaps out of the water and rolls around, its sticky appendages capturing the tiny morsels to be dragged back into the water for consumption.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives on the ocean floor, typically covering its body with seaweed and kelp. Its massive extendable arms reach out and snatch large fish that swim too close, making them easy meals.
author: sk372

entry: By flapping their tentacle-like wings, POKENAME are able to cause waves strong enough to send sand flying. They do this to reveal hidden Omastar, which are typically a POKENAME's favorite meal.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: The feet of POKENAME are vestigial; it now uses its sticky appendages to move itself. It is said that once this Pokémon grabs something, nothing can unstick it if POKENAME doesn't want it removed.
author: ayner

entry: As an ambush predator, POKENAME will hang from thick branches using its sticky tendrils. The residue it leaves behind will grow moss on the branches.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: If it is dried out, it will curl up into a ball until returned to the water. Washed up POKENAME are often mistaken for beach toys.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME extends sticky tendrils from either of its hands to immobilize opponents. The tendrils also work effectively to catch small insects, one of its preferred sources of sustenance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its coloring to masquerade as a regular Kecleon, utilizing yellow eye-like patterns to fool its prey. Its "tongue" is actually a prehensile tentacle, with which it pulls its prey into the fake mouth to be feasted upon within.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME's jaws can create a digestive fluid that melts its prey. This causes the Pokémon to always prefer eating with these jaws.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME hides on the ocean floor, erupting from the sand to attack prey Pokémon. The true length of its body has yet to be discovered.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Its diet consists mostly of coral and plant life on the sea floor. It will sometimes eat seashells and barnacles if no plant life is available.
author: .izik

entry: This prehistoric Pokémon is said to have lived in tropical waters, using its fans to hypnotize prey and scare off enemies.
author: planatical

entry: The tendrils growing from POKENAME's head are coated with a faint layer of a sticky substance. It prances through forests catching bugs to eat with its ribbons.
author: sk372

entry: Due to Rotom's penchant for electric-powered machines and Cradily only being populous in the past, wild POKENAME are difficult to study. They roam deep undersea caverns; approaching with a submarine causes them to attempt to hijack it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It disguises itself as a prehistoric sea creature and sneaks into museums, hoping to endear itself to archaeologists. However, its distinctive odor keeps it from making any friends.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME run through laundromats, gathering socks from dryers for use in their costumes. They often throw red socks into white washing machine cylces to make the socks the pink color they desire.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME has limited eyesight, but its feelers on its neck make up for that with intrinsic senses of its surroundings. The moment an insect buzzes by, the feelers snatch it up and throw it into POKENAME's mouth.
author: sk372

entry: The eyes on POKENAME's body are false markings; its real eyes reside within its always-gaping mouth. The tendrils on its back extend to grab onto anything it latches onto, making it increasingly difficult to pry off as it feasts on the prey's blood.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon adapted its tentacles to detect movement and subtle changes in the water around it. These appendages do increase POKENAME's drag, though.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME flutter elegantly above the sea floor by oscillating their long arms. They drift down on top of their prey, trapping their victims before dissolving them for a liquid meal.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: Despite being quite slow, it is hard to escape a POKENAME due to its immense strength and stretchy tentacles. It hunts in coral reefs, smashing the coral with its arms before grabbing any Pokémon hiding away.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's headbutt doubles as a way to grapple its foe. The sticky tentacles on its head latch onto its opponent with a powerful grip, allowing it to lift them up and swing them around with relative ease.
author: sk372

entry: It keeps the tendrils on its head tied back as a sign of tolerance. When another Pokémon disrespects it, POKENAME unties its tendrils and uses them to unleash stinging attacks.
author: hophoppip

entry: A rare and enigmatic Pokémon, POKENAME resides on the seafloor. It uses its shiny body to reflect what little light reaches it, drawing in prey before it quickly lashes out with its tentacles to ensnare them.
author: banjosaurus.

entry: They ensnare their prey with their bodies before biting into them. Their fangs then release a digestive fluid, turning their prey into soup that POKENAME sucks out.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME often live alone, prompting them to crawl towards humans in excitement upon seeing them. Humans unfamiliar with how a POKENAME moves often run away afraid.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME hides, camouflaging itself with the seabed, ready to ambush its prey. It poisons Pokémon with the tentacles on its body, which are often mistaken for sea anemones.
author: _cradily_

entry: POKENAME are said to have great regenerative capabilities, as damaged tentacles can regrow within a day. Many who try to hurt them find themselves covered in a sticky corrosive gel that eats away at fur or feathers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is very loyal and protective of its Trainer. It stands guard by their side constantly and will whip out sticky appendages from around its neck to ward off perceived potential dangers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME shoots out Hydro Pumps from the prehensile tentacles on its back. It can bend the direction of the torrent to shoot into hard to reach places, making it a great helper for cleaning crews.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the silt of the seafloor, extending its tentacles above to draw in prey before dragging them below to feed. When startled, it jets from its hiding place by blasting water to propel itself away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is found in all oceans, keeping its shell closed while feeling for prey with its tendrils. It grabs the target and reels it into the shell for digestion, but if trained well it will instead incapacitate its catch for its fishing companion.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Those put to sleep by POKENAME's hypnosis dream vivid visions of a prehistoric world. Some scientists think exploring these dreams further could lead to archaeological discoveries.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME have terrifyingly short lives, thanks to the lack of any organs aside from its eye and brain. There have been attempts at giving POKENAME a longer lifespan, but there haven't been any results.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME swings its bone-like boomerang in wide arcs across the battlefield. If it misses, it follows up with Brine to keep foes off balance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME masters the exceptional hunting skills of ancestral Pokémon from a prehistoric period. In modern times, however, these tactics are millions of years out of date.
author: gaogao028

entry: By flapping its stone wings, it can dash at great speed towards its enemies and strike them with its claws. POKENAME has recently been revitalized by fragments of fossilized exoskeleton found near ancient forests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in ever-stormy plateaus. With a range of vision of nearly 360º, it is an unparalleled hunter.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME roams websites devoted to prehistoric databases, feeding on stored data. If left alone, it can empty a website within hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its claws to grip undersea cliffsides and eat kelp. If disturbed while eating, it unleashes a Mud Shot to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scuttles across the seafloor, chewing on rotten plant life. Its hard shell protects it from anchors dropped by passing ships.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in fast-flowing rivers where it continually sheds its skin to grow larger. Its feathers have been seen vibrating for reasons not yet known.
author: torterraguy26

entry: It is rumored that POKENAME's mood can influence the weather: If POKENAME gets annoyed, a rainstorm will break out. It wraps its stone coils around prey that have been foolish enough to approach the waters where it dwells.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME stomps around on its small legs. Its legs are easy to snap because of their size. Its stingers are not poisonous, just painful.
author: themicelegion

entry: Because POKENAME does not have claws and cannot photosynthesize, it now eats any plants found close to the water and the small bug Pokémon found in them.
author: torterraguy26

entry: The feelers on POKENAME's sides alert it to fluctuations in temperature and air pressure. Using this, it can tell when a cold front is approaching, and dig itself a den to hoard food in and wait until warmer weather arrives.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can only look into the past. While this ability hasn't been seen as very useful, geologists have praised this Pokémon to no end, as it has helped them solve mysteries about the world before humans came along.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME hides amid underwater plants in an attempt to camouflage itself. The many eye-stalks on its hands give it strong vision, but also present multiple weak points foes can take advantage of.
author: sk372

entry: The stalks jutting from the sides of POKENAME's head are its actual eyes. The eye-like pattern on its face changes depending on its mood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in rivers and are very sensitive to artificial light. Because they are so rare, if a population is found, any future development that takes place is subject to strict lighting limits.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is thought to be a missing link between Anorith and Dunsparce. Its large eyes suggest that it had yet to evolve to an underground lifestyle.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME live in hot springs, feeding on minerals found in the water, which makes up the scale-like layers of their hard shell. Because of their habitat, their shells are often hot to the touch and may leave burns.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's eye stalks can shift and rotate to a degree, giving it a wide range of vision. This helps increase the accuracy of the bullet-like shots of water it spits from its mouth at others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes paintings that resemble drawings from ancient times and prefers using red paint or charcoal. The true meaning of its drawings is ambiguous because they can be interpreted in many different ways.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its three large eyes are majorly helpful in its pursuit of aquatic prey in warm seas. Its lack of opposable arms is not deemed helpful by scientists.
author: hophoppip

entry: Wielding its large serpentine appendage, POKENAME reaches far to catch unsuspecting prey. Its mimicry face grinds food that is then brought to its actual mouth.
author: gaogao028

entry: POKENAME has lived in the same swamp since ancient times, where it has used the same hunting method for eons. It hides in the mud until prey is close enough to pounce on and coats them with mud to prevent escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fake red eyes on POKENAME begin to glow and enlarge when they raise their arms up high, intimidating opponents.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME's dress contains eight wings that it uses to swim through the ocean. It's been seen rescuing divers that have swum too deep.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME chews through trees and rocks with equal efficiency to build the dams it calls home. If a tree falls on its hardened back it doesn't even notice.
author: gerbopotato

entry: POKENAME have eight appendages around their head that grab moss around them that they rely on as their main source of food. POKENAME get excited whenever their Trainer talks about evolution, as their whole body seems to shake with excitement.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are usually very shy, but they will appear at villages when they feel incoming danger to warn people. However, it can only feel disasters that have happened long in the past, making it easy to predict their location.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME's eyes are quite powerful, able to see clearly for miles in all directions. Even the tiniest of bugs won't escape its sight as it hunts for them around the coastal forests it tends to inhabit.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in the dark depths of the sea. Despite living in darkness, the leaves on its shell produce nutrients via photosynthesis from the bioluminescence of other deep sea Pokémon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME will submerge itself in a body of water for days on end. It prefers to find pure spring water in forest biomes. Some say the presence of an POKENAME at a water source is a sign that it is clean and safe to drink.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Long thought extinct, paleontologists were stunned to discover POKENAME still living in small colonies on the ocean floor. With their slow and gentle habits, they can support tiny but thriving ancient ecosystems on their backs.
author: gerbopotato

entry: This sword has dismissed its warrior spirit to connect with the one inside a 100,000,000-year-old Claw Fossil, remembering its ancient techniques.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's impressive size and wingspan cuts an imposing visage, but its behavior is simple and non-confrontational. It spends much of its time in the air, swooping down only to dig up tree bark and feast on insects hiding beneath.
author: sk372

entry: It's said POKENAME fur was a consistent source of silk in ancient times. Its mane is silky smooth and was yearned for back then.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's eyes, attached to the end of ribbon-like feelers, give it a wide range of vision. However, the ribbons are easily blown about by the wind, hampering the effectiveness of its sight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME resides near shorelines, patrolling the area for prey swimming within the shallows. It sends out shadowy tendrils into the water to ensnare creatures to eat, preferring being on land to diving into the water itself.
author: sk372

entry: Opponents rarely realize where POKENAME is looking due to their pseudo eyes. When an attack comes, it bounces harmlessly off this species' rock-hard hide before getting burned by a boiling hot Tail Whip.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME soars along coastal areas, its many wings able to pick up faint changes in the wind and judge the ocean's currents. A curious sort, it sometimes approaches humans on the beach to observe them up close.
author: sk372

entry: The markings on POKENAME's face, coupled with its large size, are effective scare tactics to frighten off some predators. It submerges itself halfway into the sand at the ocean bottom, filter-feeding for most of the day.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has sung the same banal lullaby every day since ancient times. The lullaby has since become less effective at lulling other Pokémon to sleep, but the habit of singing continues with each day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trudge along the bottom of deep trenches, using their claws to break open iron deposits to eat. The armor along their backs is incredibly tough, protecting them from falling rocks.
author: santon5512

entry: This prehistoric Pokémon used to stalk beaches, scanning the shore for prey. Once prey was spotted, it would swoop in and snatch it with its claws.
author: zerocipher

entry: POKENAME keep a reticent expression that is mistaken for contempt or apathy. Despite this misconception, they show their affection by bringing gifts dredged up from bodies of water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Playful POKENAME congregate in ancient calderas, sunning themselves and practicing their fire. They click their flint-like claws together and fan the flames with the wings on their heads.
author: gerbopotato

entry: POKENAME's membrane is resistant to changes in temperature and can even be waterproof. However, it can tear if the change in temperature or an applied force is too strong and sudden, such as when it is hit by a move in battle.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have small feathers on their body. The feathers are usually soft and completely harmless, but they can be hardened on command to fend off enemies when they feel endangered.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: Shorelines where POKENAME nest are very clean. Their tendency to swipe at people's feet causes them to go litter somewhere else.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is covered in red spots that act as multiple fake eyes in an attempt to appear bigger to nearby predators.
author: camtft

entry: The feathery plumage hides gills that allow POKENAME to function underneath the water as well as on land. Due to its mass, it doesn't swim well, instead walking along the ocean floor and digging for food.
author: sk372

entry: Since POKENAME is almost entirely gelatinous and boneless, it can slip into even the tiniest holes to take shelter. The stone claws on its hands are the only solid part of its body, allowing it to defend itself from predators.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's eyes have a full 360 view around itself both above water and beneath the waves. Its plated claws slice through any prey not fast enough to escape.
author: ohok3441

entry: The mushrooms growing on POKENAME's back are a type thought to have gone extinct millions of years ago. As the fungi can only grow on POKENAME itself, care is taken to protect the species to help further scientific research.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME clings onto the bottom of piers, feeding off algae until it's strong enough to fend for itself. It relies on the loud sounds of boats to deter predators.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The fusion process has recombined POKENAME's fuzzy exterior into rocklike armor. It uses this exterior as camouflage as much as defense, sneaking to ambush tinier prey along rocky riverbanks.
author: gerbopotato

entry: POKENAME court each other by touching their wings together and beating them in unison. When being hunted by aerial predators, they use their two claws to grip onto coral so they can't be scooped away.
author: soup1900

entry: Its large eyes are on its legs. The reason for this is unknown, but its believed to be useful for keeping watch below when POKENAME is climbing trees.
author: hophoppip

entry: The eyes of an POKENAME are embedded in their chest. Their legs are particularly armored, allowing them to climb trees without getting hurt. Their fear-inducing head mask scares away most bird Pokémon.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME glide across water in search of weaker aquatic prey. The sturdy shell on their heads protects them from surprise attacks by bird Pokémon.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME has large antennae that are too large to be used as intended, and instead are predominantly used to intimidate stronger Pokémon. The large eyes on those antennae are actually its real eyes, so it is a common weak spot.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME will meditate at the bottom of the sea for hours on end, letting the ocean current pick it up and sweep it away. When it finishes its daily meditation, it will look around for a single piece of seaweed to eat.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME swim along the ocean floor at incredible speeds. The wings along their bodies are razor sharp, allowing them to slice through both prey and predators with a single pass.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's rigid exoskeleton helps protect it from attacks. It was once a popular food in medieval times, being prepared with a variety of herbs and spices.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's fur billows as if it is being blown, even when there is no breeze. This is because its fur is actually made of overlapping fins that it instinctively uses for swimming.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are pleasantly warm to the touch and enjoy being close to both people and other Pokémon. They make excellent companions at Pokémon Daycares and will happily look after any eggs that may turn up within them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are hot to the touch, their bodies containing an intense fire. They periodically discharge this heat by exhaling great gouts of flame.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are hot to the touch, their bodies containing an intense fire. They periodically discharge this heat by exhaling great gouts of flame.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swing around using a very long rope-like object. The claws at the tips of these ropes can embed into walls, allowing POKENAME to scale large mountains with ease. The ropes are actually part of their bodies.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME lives in murky waters, tricking prey into thinking that it is an ordinary Anorith. When they approach, POKENAME lunges, dragging down prey with its muscular limbs.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: Each of POKENAME's heads has enormous eyes that take up nearly a quarter of its size. Its two minds cannot seem to work together to walk, so it is a slow walker.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME have three false heads with hard beaks. They can swing these beaks with tremendous force, easily tearing through even the thickest hides. Additionally, POKENAME can also run faster than most human vehicles.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME's body is composed mostly of the crude oil that came from ancient decomposed Anorith. It is often found near offshore rigs.
author: ferdirenz

entry: Its body is made of a thick, poisonous tar made from fossils long ago. It uses its protruding spikes to cling onto prey and bring them closer to the body.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: Skeletons of POKENAME were once mistaken for Corphish skeletons, as both have multiple legs and large claws. However, POKENAME can be brought to life with fossil technology, dispelling the myth of genetic similarity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rolls around the depths of the ocean, shuffling its claws through the sand to dig for food. If it thinks it has chanced upon a prey's den, it creates a small explosion with one claw to blow away the sand and reveal the morsels within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are armored with a rock solid cocoon that protects them attacks. Scientists believe that they have existed since ancient times due to recent discoveries in fossil evidence.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They nest in cramped caves, warding off all life not accustomed to its dense, red smog. While hazardous in its natural state, this gas is under examination for use as a powerful antibiotic agent.
author: bukie

entry: Resembling a robot or drone-like creature, it rolls around on a scaly wheel and can shoot boiling or freezing water from its arm-cannons.
author: spencerrdevv

entry: Using its head-mounted false eyes, POKENAME makes itself appear larger to scare off Ursaring. While it is heavily armored, it uses its superior strength to take to the sky confusing its ground-based predators.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME crawls along the ocean floor. When it sees prey, it shakes its tail to kick up sand. If this happens often and viciously enough, it can create whirlpools.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME hunted by hiding beneath the ocean sands, springing forth when large prey swam near and tearing into them with quick movements of its bladed arms. Fossil records indicate its preferred prey was Lapras.
author: sk372

entry: Paleontologists recently found a cluster of POKENAME fossils near Mulberry City. The fossils show that they flocked together in large numbers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are seen hovering low above desert sands. They use the grains to sharpen their claws, and in dire situations, their bodies have adapted to allow them to eat the sand as well.
author: rumia_archer

entry: This Pokémon is impossible to constrict or restrain. Its body is covered entirely in hard armor permanently slick with slime that POKENAME secretes.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME have sharp, armored wings that protect them as they soar through the air. They rely on their wings to strike down prey before flying away with their meal gripped in between their talons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME float along the shoreline to hunt, tilting their bodies forward while extending their claws. The recoil from yanking up their target causes their entire bodies to tilt backwards, then sway back and forth, helping to disorient their prey.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME can thrive in the harshest aquatic locations along strong tides and storms. Armor protects the body, which can suction to any wet surface.
author: ziggaway

entry: Fossils of POKENAME are found in Galar, fossil researchers there resurrecting the fossil Pokémon from fragmentary remains. In life, POKENAME anchor themselves to the sea floor and lash out at passing Pokémon to try and catch them as food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Fossils of POKENAME are found in Galar, fossil researchers there resurrecting the fossil Pokémon from fragmentary remains. In life, POKENAME anchor themselves to the sea floor and lash out at passing Pokémon to try and catch them as food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A land-dwelling Pokémon that can support small organisms on its back. It enjoys a small drizzle, but hides during downpours. POKENAME has virtually no physical weak point: even in areas where it cannot see, it is well protected by its armored scales.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A land-dwelling Pokémon that can support small organisms on its back. It enjoys a small drizzle, but hides during downpours. POKENAME has virtually no physical weak point: even in areas where it cannot see, it is well protected by its armored scales.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is said to be possessed by a prehistoric grudge from hundreds of millions of years ago. Its body is made of extremely dense keratin, which can cut through steel.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Despite its ruthless nature, it will protect anyone being attacked. It is said that this is because it has been treated well by people.
author: imagine1.

entry: It swims through the sand at high speeds, ambushing any small Pokémon. The eyes on its wings are for intimidation.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME's ribbons can harden to the consistency of stone during combat. It waves them in erratic motions to deflect incoming projectiles with surprising ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can launch boulders from the cannon on its back as if they were powerful projectiles. Its tempered steel exoskeleton not only makes it extremely durable, but also increases the damage of its claw strikes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME was a fearsome hunter in ancient times, relentlessly slicing up prey with its prized tusks. When fossil Pokémon went extinct, these tusks were used as blades by humans to slice open metal armor.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME weave their furry tails into braids so that they do not trip over themselves. Their retractable claws are rarely seen because their small size makes them less than ideal for attacking.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME weave their tails into one long braid to reduce the chance of their fur getting caught in their armor. Their lightweight armor gets heavy when soaked in water, so many POKENAME live in arid climates to minimize this risk.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's soft, warm fur was long used to craft thermal jackets for mountain climbing. The stone armor covering its body becomes incandescent when this Pokémon is pushed under intense strain.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many assume the sunglasses-like area is POKENAME's eyes, but they are actually on the side of its head. This aggressive Pokémon dominated the ancient world, bullying smaller creatures into giving it food or face the consequences.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skin is covered with armor plates. This allows it to move even faster through the water, and protects it from harm when ramming objects.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME is primarily found in cooler, wetter regions of the world, subsisting on moss, algae and the occasional insect. The frills on its neck and head are coated with a very faint layer of frost.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were ancient herbivores that had few enemies. Its layered armour prevented many hard hitting attacks, but it is theorized a strong fighting type Pokémon rendered it extinct.
author: frokachu

entry: The large claws on its paws allow for an easy hunt. The hard shells on POKENAME's back protect it from any surprise attacks while it's resting.
author: captainzscourge

entry: POKENAME lives in small groups nestled around shallow waters. It uses its front claws to groom others of its kind, keeping the scales on their heads nice and clean.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swim deep under water, using the red glow from their claws to lure in prey before they strike. POKENAME are highly attuned to their surroundings, detecting any motion in their environment through the feathers along their bodies.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are able to slink all their limbs into their shell to fully protect themselves. They may reach up to sixty miles per hour rolling down a hill to escape from a foe.
author: camtft

entry: While possessing an amazing intelligence and psychic powers, its body is weak and ungainly on land. When in the water, POKENAME is a great swimmer because of its paddle-like arms.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: Attacks that hit POKENAME's strong, tough muscles aren't felt by it. Giant steel slabs look like holey cheese in mere seconds after POKENAME has punched them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME smashes its skull on hard surfaces in emotional agony when thinking of its late mother.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME cannot stop running once they begin, so there are often warning signs in place near their habitats. The impact of their headbutt attacks is strong enough to snap a tree in half.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their hard heads to crack open and slurp down shellfish and mollusks. If challenged by another POKENAME, they will butt heads until one concedes.
author: holgast

entry: While POKENAME usually has a mild personality, it becomes ferocious and stubborn when it comes to food. It lives deep in the jungle.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When these Pokémon are agitated, they drum their fists against their hard heads. This display also causes them to generate extra electricity that may fly loose from their spikes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME bathes in water constantly to keep its cranium clean and pristine. It's not aggressive by nature, but anything that causes its dome to become filthy is in for a painful, pointed charging headbutt.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sheds its skin regularly, which leaves its domed skull soft and weakened afterward. It immediately goes around headbutting things to quickly toughen it back up.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME loses its temper, its rocky head is engulfed in blazing flames. Stubborn and impulsive, it may even headbutt its own Trainer if not properly trained.
author: fiordaliso

entry: These small Bug Pokémon use their silk webbing to entangle prey and predators. When they manage to wrap enough of their webbing around a foe, they will pull themselves toward them and use their hard abdomens to deliver a concussive blow.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live only within caves and caverns. When a foe walks into their webs, they drop from the ceiling above, using their entire rock-hard body to deliver a powerful concussive blow directly to their head.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spend hours polishing their shell and the dome on their heads until they are smooth and solid. When threatened, they bop their heads against the threat until it goes away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Archaeologists say spotting one POKENAME near excavation sites brings luck and helps uncover rare artifacts. Its wings can lift its stone body only a few meters off the ground.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME sits atop trees waiting for the perfect moment. When prey wanders below the branch, it drops down and delivers a hard blow with its rocky head.
author: terrabits

entry: Should POKENAME's skull ever get damaged, a slimy gel is excreted from the wound which contains great healing properties. This was exploited in the past, with many POKENAME coming to harm, and so now it is illegal to sell the gel.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's most vital organs tend to be protected by solid blue plating, such as its spine or its admittedly small brain. Its legs have the ability to regrow if somehow severed.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are usually quadrupedal, but they can stand on two legs by using their heavy tails as counterweights. Fossilized POKENAME tracks can be easily identified by the furrow left by their tails.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's skull is made of a very tough gemstone. Its ghostly energy is stored within.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME does not take kindly to others trespassing in the ruins it inhabits. It spins through the air and tackles at others, the spines on its cranium causing painful gashes if it connects.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bash their thick skulls into trees to knock down nests, eating their eggs. Using their claws, they can cut through even the most sturdy defenses.
author: santon5512

entry: While the head of POKENAME was incredibly tough, fossils show that it often dislodged its shell after tackling opponents. Many shells have been found in early human settlements, leading to a theory that they may have served as rudimentary ovens.
author: notadoctor75

entry: In prehistoric times, POKENAME thrived in shallow oceans. Over time, as oceans got deeper and coral reefs dwindled, many are struggling to survive. Conservationists have created sanctuaries for POKENAME to ensure their long-term survival.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME headbutts palm trees to make coconuts fall and catches them with its horns. Young POKENAME turn this into a game, tossing fruit with their trunks and catching it mid-air.
author: leandermalurt

entry: POKENAME is incredibly reckless as it loves to charge into just about anything. While its armor is as hard as stone, it is also flexible enough to resist shattering against harder surfaces.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME use their heads to knock down obstacles. POKENAME must headbutt and dig their way out of the caves they hatched in to meet their parents.
author: totodile.

entry: Some POKENAME have different horn placements depending on where they live. Some POKENAME horns shed in winter and regrow in spring.
author: totodile.

entry: To keep the tops of their heads smooth, they rub coarse leaves along their heads. They can loose electricity from the small spikes on the sides of their necks.
author: infinex21

entry: When it strikes its tail against its hard head, electric sparks fly about. It uses its tail to break open nuts and to crush berries before eating them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dig trenches through the ground at high speed, keeping their heads just above the soil so that they can see where they are going. If they spot another POKENAME whilst digging, they will veer toward them and deliver a powerful Headbutt.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a bit overly zealous in its defense of its beloved Trainer. Unless taught otherwise, its first instinct towards unfamiliar people is to freeze them with psychic powers before using a charging headbutt.
author: sk372

entry: To catch its prey, POKENAME headbutts the prey with mighty force, then chomps down with its head appendage while they are stunned.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME hides amongst the rocks to ambush its prey, mainly Clauncher and Omanyte. It can extend its neck out faster than a bullet, smashing anything in its way into tiny pieces.
author: mistymagius

entry: It breaks walls inside caves to create paths, making exploration easier. This behavior often transforms complex cave systems into navigable trails.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME smacks opponents with its spiked club to severely injure them. It was apparently used by cavemen long ago as their preferred weapon of choice.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME attacks foes by bashing them repeatedly with its two spiked clubs. Unlike a Doublade, it has no complex attack pattern, so even basic defensive tools can counter its strikes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's territorial nature leads it to charge at anything moving within its perceived domain. It headbutts its target before wrapping its ribbons around them, holding them in place so it can keep headbutting them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME used to live on the seafloor, rolling around and crushing hard shells of Pokémon like Kabuto to eat. Scientists theorize that POKENAME's weight caused them to struggle to reach the surface to breathe, leading to their initial extinction.
author: milchik

entry: The hard plating on POKENAME's head produces a sharp clanging that varies in pitch depending on how it was struck. It headbutts things and uses the tone created to help it tune its singing.
author: sk372

entry: The stones that fall off its body were once used in ancient times to craft armor. These relics remain highly sought-after by collectors and historians.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hard head is mainly for defense. It can also use it for headbutting attacks, but its stubby legs make charging difficult to pull off.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME can be found in small burrows headbutting their siblings in a mad scramble for the attention of their parents. While their parents hunt for food, POKENAME will bury themselves in the desert sand to hide and keep warm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Be careful exploring caves where POKENAME reside, because of their thick skulls, they have little regard for their surroundings. If they don't smash into you directly, there is a chance of them causing stalactites to fall.
author: mistymagius

entry: Legends speak of an underground tomb near Pewter City where groups of this Pokémon stand as guardians. Their watchful presence ensures no intruders enter these halls.
author: .izik

entry: It snacks on stalagmites, wearing down the formations over time. The mineral-rich diet also makes its headbutts even more powerful.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers foods high in iron, which help strengthen its already robust skull. This diet gives it an edge in headbutt battles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the echoes of its large and spacious head to whinny noises that resemble ringing bells. The iron-like ball on its tail also echoes these same sounds, but only when smashed against thick ice.
author: soup1900

entry: Whenever a challenge is issued between two POKENAME, they run at each other at full speed, not backing down until the large scales on their forehead collide. The one that withstands the resulting ringing longer is declared the winner.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME slams its rock-hard skull into clusters of amethyst, shattering them into tiny shards. It eagerly devours the crushed gemstones, strengthening its sturdy body.
author: .izik

entry: Lacking senses of self-preservation, POKENAME charges at anything to see if its dense skull can damage it. While charging, it pulls up the loose skin to not trip, which absorbs much of the impact.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Unlike other meteor-like Pokémon, POKENAME's core is just as hard as its outer shell. With its armor shed for extra speed, it can hammer all the way through entire mountains, but it also severely lacks in accuracy against smaller targets.
author: milchik

entry: Rival POKENAME in the wild compete against each other by butting their solid craniums against each other. Each impact causes the fire on their tails to flare up explosively.
author: sk372

entry: In battle, POKENAME swing their tails around like flails. They are obsessed with keeping their tails cleaned and polished. The gleam of their polished tails tends to distract them, even during battle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is very territorial. Its Rollout feels like being hit by a heavy bowling ball going 20 mph, so it's advised to stay away from POKENAME pods.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It headbutts trees to knock free fruits and nuts, then roasts them with its flames. Many gatherers have a POKENAME on hand to help collect many fruits and nuts, though must keep them in line so they do not topple any trees by mistake.
author: infinex21

entry: It watches over playgrounds, intervening when it spots bullies. Its protective nature has earned it the trust of children.
author: .izik

entry: Its skull is so thick that no thought can possibly penetrate it. It likes to laze about near the riverside and will stubbornly headbutt anyone that tries to move it.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Although POKENAME can survive in extreme heat or cold, they are still sensitive to sudden changes in temperature. As a result, any naturally formed population tends to remain in a predictable area. They headbutt one another to show affection.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It cracks open boulders to eat the crystals hidden inside. These minerals give it the energy it needs to maintain its strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME basks in the sun to gather energy. It rams into trees to gather ripe berries as well as help strengthen its power.
author: mepp.

entry: If POKENAME taps the bone it carries onto its solid skull, it's a challenge. Rivals in the wild charge into each other to see who has the stronger headbutt, and the loser forfeits their prized bone.
author: sk372

entry: While it hunts for food, it seeks any nests of Flying-type Pokémon. When it finds one, it rams into it at full force, destroying the nest.
author: skymaster426

entry: When POKENAME see an intruder in their territory they will fly above it and drop head-first into the target. Because they frequently miss, their territory can be easily identified thanks to the large number of craters.
author: alumed

entry: POKENAME are capable of flying at supersonic speeds, racing across the skies. They have extremely hard heads and use these to battle with one another, a collision between two POKENAME sounds like a thunderclap.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are capable of flying at supersonic speeds, racing across the skies. They have extremely hard heads and use these to battle with one another, a collision between two POKENAME sounds like a thunderclap.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rubs its head against bushes or rocks to polish the head crest on its head. After a Pokémon battle, it enjoys swimming in shallow water to cool off.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These small Pokémon weave their silk webbing into small webs that can launch them like miniature springboards. They will launch themselves at their opponents like small boulders that will pulverize them into submission.
author: infinex21

entry: The spikes lining a POKENAME's abdomen can shoot out threads of durable webbing that ensnare their opponents. They will often reel themselves in via these threads to deliver a rock-shattering blow with the blunt tip of their abdomen.
author: infinex21

entry: Due to their rather unique profile, they fail to imitate much of anything. When their disguise inevitably fails, they resort to violently headbutting instead.
author: frokachu

entry: It enjoys swimming in river rapids. Its hard head protects it when it inevitably rams into rocks or rafts.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME battle one another in contests of strength, seeking to ram into one another and send the loser tumbling down the mountainside. They are incredibly slow Pokémon, and the impacts between them rarely result in any real harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are very territorial and will clash in a head-to-head duel if they come across another of their own kind. Due to their slow speed, these battles are usually anticlimactic.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME is loud and abrasive, barking out orders to any Pokémon smaller than it. Most learn not to resist its commands, lest they be on the receiving end of a violent and crushing headbutt.
author: sk372

entry: If POKENAME spends too much time in the jungle, its rocky body becomes covered in ivy and grass. When it encounters another of its kind, it rams into the other with its rock-hard head to instantly determine which one is tougher.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it meets another of its species, it rams into them with its rock-hard head to immediately determine which one is stronger. On its back it carries several seeds capable of releasing spores that enhance the blooming of nearby trees and plants.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A fastidious Pokémon, POKENAME can throw punches that can shatter brick walls while taking great care of its personal appearance.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: The crystals growing on POKENAME's body are extremely sturdy; only impact with another POKENAME will chip them. Their rarity and vibrant shine make crystal shards a highly prized commodity.
author: sk372

entry: Its skull cannot crack no matter how many times it's used as a battering ram in battle. A POKENAME on the beach pushing against a cruise ship can prevent it from running aground.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Its cranium is so sturdy that it's thought to be completely invulnerable. Once, a misfired cannon shot struck a nearby POKENAME; the cannonball shattered on impact, and POKENAME neither flinched nor noticed.
author: sk372

entry: Its body is made up of many small magnets. Every morning, it shakes violently to loosen debris that have accumulated on its base.
author: .izik

entry: Using its feelers, a POKENAME will ensnare its foe and pull itself in toward them to deliver a crushing Headbutt attack. Even a tamed POKENAME will sometimes weakly headbutt its Trainer if they are riddled with doubts or concerns.
author: infinex21

entry: During ancient times, POKENAME would attract prey with a sweet aroma, then bash it with its skull, which is as hard as iron.
author: darkweavile428

entry: The spikes around its skull are what make POKENAME's headbutts devastatingly brutal. Its limber form allows for quick turns if necessary.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME flies at extremely high speeds, ramming into anything in its path. Its rocky carapace protects its body from these high-speed impacts.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME charges into its foes, the keys jingling along with it. This tackle is more effective than one might first believe.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's heads are quite lopsided due to the bowling balls they carry, attempting to mimic the tough skulls of Rampardos. They swing their heads around wildly, though these attacks often miss due to how slow and predictable they are.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME flies around and shatters everything in its path by smashing them with its three heads. Lacking any intelligence, it sometimes forgets its other two heads even exist, leading to it losing fights it otherwise would have won easily.
author: soup1900

entry: Groups of POKENAME hang from cave ceilings as they sleep, dropping headfirst onto intruders if awoken. By slamming their thick skulls together, they can create reverberations through the air, which they use to echolocate and find food.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME live deep within caves, eating minerals in order to harden their heads. If provoked, they will slam their heads into the cave ceiling, causing the stalactites around them to fall onto their targets.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME delivers crushing headbutts to its opponents in battle, knocking down even the sturdiest of Pokémon. Its rocky skin is near impervious to physical attacks, and its primal fury is ferocious to behold.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME is made up of two halves that work in tandem with each other. One half roots themselves into the ground, sapping fossil fuels from the ground to fuel them both. The other defends the first from danger, ramming into predators at high speeds.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's defence is unmatched, shrugging off even the mightiest of blows. After being hit, it retaliates with a devastating headbutt at astonishing speed, then slips back into its defensive stance.
author: evilgammon

entry: Because of POKENAME's small brain making its rage easy to trigger, combined with its ability to fly, this Pokémon can only be handled by a very skilled Trainer. If POKENAME crashes into the ground at full speed, the sheer impact forms a large crater.
author: milchik

entry: By repeatedly slamming their heads into the ground, POKENAME tunnel through the earth. The tremors that these Pokémon cause are often mistaken for small earthquakes.
author: santon5512
