entry: Its three heads were once one, which most believe is how they function with such excellent coordination. They will synchronize their headbutts to help tenderize tough ground, shatter solid rock, or to pummel an opponent from below.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are quite dim-witted, constantly hitting their heads into walls and other Pokémon. This leaves them with constant headaches, which they attempt to relieve by slamming their head some more.
author: santon5512

entry: Their charcoal-black furs are hot to the touch, though they will tend to be warm for their trusted Trainers. POKENAME can achieve great speeds, which carries into their devastating headbutt attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: In other regions, POKENAME forms packs to tackle Passimian down and steal their Berries.
author: malxire

entry: Oreburgh City uses POKENAME to expedite mining, since they can mine as fast as three humans combined. When not helping excavate, they chase Sableye away from digs.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Despite the sheer weight upon the backs of POKENAME, they are still able to move at a decent pace. They submerge themselves slightly in the winter months to hibernate and camouflage.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME have a thick shell around the flower bulb on their back that is made of fossilized leaves. They also have a circular bony protrusion around their head that protects their brains when they headbutt foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hurls its bone at cave stalactites to knock them down. It eats the fallen stone chunks to harden its metallic cranium.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fashions its weapon from rocks and uses it to crack open tough berries. Some researchers hypothesize that early humans began crafting stone tools after observing POKENAME.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME clangs its fist against the shield on its arm as a challenge, seeking strong opponents to fight. Striking the shield on its head temporarily enhances its body's electrical generation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for speed bumps so many people drive their cars over them. This results in their body tensing up and expanding outward, leading to a traffic accident.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME seems determined to act as an antivirus, even if it is directed to do other actions. It is suspected either Shieldon's defensive abilities or its lack of familiarity with the inner workings of software causes this behavior.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's shells are practically impenetrable, reliably keeping them unharmed until they are ready to evolve. These Pokémon are often the sole survivors of forest fires.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's rotund body has grown so large and thick, other Pokémon tend to hide behind it as it shields them from threats. Its thick fat is as durable as steel.
author: maxissaa

entry: This Pokémon has extremely strong wings. It bashes it thick, rocky head against trees to knock out Berries or bug Pokémon.
author: themicelegion

entry: What looks like a soft coat of wool is actually dense rockwool. It serves as a thick layer of armor for POKENAME.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are prehistoric Pokémon that had been thought to be extinct until a live population was found in Eterna Forest in Sinnoh. They have a sturdy seed sprouting from their back, the husk of which is several inches thick and difficult to crack.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It has rough hooves and an armored trunk that protect it when sliding down hills. Younger POKENAME may need an Assault Vest to further cushion them from harm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME carries a heavy shield as tall as it is to give it better defenses in combat. If a battle turns desperate, it may toss the shield aside and fight with a berserk fury.
author: sk372

entry: It breaks rocks with its head to get to the tasty ore inside. It becomes aggressive if anything sneaks up on it from behind.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME's feathers harden over time, causing them to have once been classified as scales. Its feathers are tougher than iron and have prismatic sheens when they are properly polished.
author: infinex21

entry: It is still developing its dance and mimicry skills, and is quite self-critical. If POKENAME fails to perfectly copy a dance or action, it hits its own resilient skull plate while throwing a tantrum.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME play with each other by launching small rocks from their hands at the other, reflecting them back at the thrower by bouncing the stones off of their solid skulls.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME always stands close to its Trainer, regarding itself as something of a bodyguard. It creates psychic shields in front of itself and its allies, bouncing attacks back before flinging its constructs at the attacker.
author: sk372

entry: Liquid metal flows from POKENAME's faceplate, which it can control and weave into its attacks. It uses this metal to form snapping mouths that let it attack from range.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's armor is tougher than steel. It slams its head into cave walls to dislodge ores, which it then consumes to reinforce its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's unbreakable face shields it from nearly any impact. It uses its durable head to deliver powerful headbutts to knock down trees, providing berries and fruit for smaller Pokémon.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME sharpens its blade by rubbing it against trees and rocks. While its eye is on its handle, the soul inhabiting it lies inside the face plate where the eyes of a Shieldon would be.
author: soup1900

entry: A well-organized group of POKENAME can take on enemies much larger than their individual size. They congregate primarily in rocky plateaus.
author: ferdirenz

entry: It avoids conflict as much as it can, though it will rarely hesitate to leap to the defense of others. Its face and head are tougher than diamond, so it can endure and repel most attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: Pokémon Fusion has not perfectly adapted Lopunny and Shieldon together: while the ears grant powerful defense and the legs bring surprising nimbleness, it often combines into POKENAME falling flat on its face mid-battle.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The stone shields on its arms allow POKENAME to skillfully block enemy attacks in close combat. This Pokémon was recently revitalized from fossils discovered in the mountains.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME does not fear battle as its thick, iron shield can resist most attacks. However, it prefers to stay out of the rain as it could lead to its shield rusting.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon frequently rams headfirst into opponents. Years of doing this give POKENAME severe brain damage, which researchers are trying to find a fix for. It's made POKENAME an extremely endangered species.
author: huh.7

entry: POKENAME has a hard time flying due to its heavy faceplate. It hangs from cavern roofs to build strength, occasionally dropping onto unsuspecting Pokémon or even Trainers.
author: evilgammon

entry: Ancient tapestries show POKENAME guarding city gates. Its head was used to deflect arrows and stones during great sieges.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a hoarder of metal, digging through scrap heaps and smelters to find anything to add to its collection. It wears its metal mask when stealing, often adorned with stolen trinkets.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME swoops down from above, delivering strong headbutts in battle that send opponents sprawling. It can only stay in the air for a limited time, however, as the metal on its body weighs it down.
author: evilgammon

entry: This Pokémon lived in shallow rivers about 100 million years ago. Researchers believe it went extinct due to the climate, because almost nothing could penetrate its armored shell.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME rely on the frills on the side of their face to signal danger to other members of their pack, bending them horizontally whenever predators are nearby. This allows them to swiftly prepare a stampede to attack the threat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Steel constantly grows from POKENAME's body, occasionally being harvested by hikers to take as souvenirs. This steel has an unusual shine to it, and is rumoured to possess a protective charm.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's main tactic in battle is to use repeated headbutts to knock its opponent to the ground, something it excels at thanks to its iron faceplate. They are rarely seen alone, often attacking in gangs with a flurry of headbutts.
author: evilgammon

entry: The hide on its face is covered in small grooves which filter the soil that it pushes. Those who follow it may find rare gems it has left behind.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: Many sleeping POKENAME have awoken to find themselves in a Trainer's pack or amongst a gaggle of eager Clefairy, mistaken for a Moon Stone while dormant.
author: banquoviaquo

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in strong armor, making it less timid as most attacks glance off its body. It typically only teleports away when stubborn aggressors won't leave it alone.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's face plate is removable and able to be used as a shield. It's lightweight and durable, allowing for its effective use in battle.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME thrive in underground aquifers formed millions of years ago. Multiple POKENAME have also been found in city fountains during the summer months, as the warm water emulates the heat of aquifers.
author: jojojax164

entry: Scientists are unsure why Shieldon appears to reverts back to its fossil form when it fuses with Geodude. Many people have been fooled by POKENAME's appearance, thinking they had just found an ancient Armor Fossil.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME always tries to keep its body flat to the ground, using its faceplate to shield the rest of its body from damage. It charges toward its opponent in battle, building momentum before ramming with its horn.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME protects itself with a fossilized Shieldon skull, which is as hard as steel. The fossil also serves as an intimidating false face.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME carries a big fossilized pickaxe, which it uses to attack or dig up relics. The massive shield it carries is also a fossil that it dug up by itself.
author: thezekrom

entry: POKENAME are elusive creatures that reside deep within caves. When threatened, they hide behind the shields they carry, waiting for the perfect moment to strike with their powerful legs.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic abilities to shield itself from attacks. The shape of this shield almost looks like a prehistoric Pokémon.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME is extremely territorial, rushing to protect its fields against intruders. It starts its charge from miles away, building momentum to strike with a devastating headbutt.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME swims through sand as if it were water. It is quite temperamental and gets angry at anyone or anything that stands in its path.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME act like a firewall that monitors cyberspace network traffic to protect people's PCs. Viruses rarely get past the incredibly restrictive shield that POKENAME provide, ensuring data remains safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME act like a firewall that monitors cyberspace network traffic to protect people's PCs. Viruses rarely get past the incredibly restrictive shield that POKENAME provide, ensuring data remains safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's extremely resilient cocoon stores the kinetic energy of strikes made against it. If something attacks it, the force they applied will be immediately rebounded back, injuring its attacker while its shell remains unharmed.
author: sk372

entry: While POKENAME have blades made out of sharpened bone, their flat face is made of cartilage instead. This is because the frills on their face are mostly decorative and serve as measures of health during courtship season.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When two POKENAME meet, they will fly to each other and slam their heads together in a display of dominance. This sound is often mistaken for thunder.
author: fenragon

entry: The leaves growing off POKENAME's body can be shot off as rapid projectiles that slice like knives. These leaves can also be shot into the ground, causing them to grow into large barriers to protect weaker Pokémon in battle.
author: evilgammon

entry: When POKENAME takes a nap, the four metallic ring shields on its neck vertically expand to sheathe its body, transforming it into an impenetrable bastion. Its presence is said to inspire feelings of safety and protection in all nearby.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are typically passive until they are provoked, curling up when aggravated. If they are continually antagonized, POKENAME will rub their armored arms together to cause a large explosion before running away.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME due to being incredibly bulky, they are able to shrug off most attacks from other Pokémon. Almost like a trade-off, they move extremely slowly on land; in water, however, they can swim as fast as a jet boat.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: Any food that is too large for POKENAME to eat, it crushes against the riverbed with its face. It leaves an imprint, and fossils of this have been found from thousands of years ago.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It charges through marshlands to create large divots in the mud. This allows waterways to expand more easily.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are slow moving Pokémon that trudge through mountain passes in small family groups as they follow the movement of the sun. They are hardy and rugged, their skin rich in minerals that toughen against physical impacts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The top and bottom layers of POKENAME's body are nigh-impenetrable, with only the small area between them being vulnerable. To protect its weak spots, it fires high-speed metal shards from the holes on its sides.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's enormous brain results in it possessing an enormous intellect. This Pokémon can be found at high elevation areas, where it can be seen gibbering at the sky above. It has been theorized that this behavior results from its yearning to fly.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME, despite their very docile nature, are often caught by officers. That the Pokémon are a very good shot and that they can protect anyone behind them are often given as a reason. After work, POKENAME like to feed on berries and relax in water.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME travels quickly across the land defending the weak, stopping bullies mid-strike with its sturdy skull. It gives the perpetrators one chance to back away and avoid conflict, acting mercilessly to those who don't heed the warning.
author: sk372

entry: Its enormous, shield-shaped skull can withstand mortar fire. Unfortunately, this also makes it top-heavy, and only the elite can stand at full height.
author: rihse

entry: POKENAME's iron tail is too heavy for it to swing. It must slowly push it to travel.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's shield repels any direct attack, while its armored body burns to touch. It has a righteous and enduring spirit.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's muscles are as tough as steel, allowing it to carry its two-ton shield effortlessly. They are valiant warriors who protect innocent Pokémon from threats over ten times their size.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are not typically used in battle due to their desire not to harm others, instead choosing to protect. Many POKENAME are recruited by notable figures as bodyguards, as their presence alone prevents threats from even attempting an attack.
author: retrodox

entry: POKENAME's shield is said to be nearly as unbreakable as its will to protect its Trainer. Despite its fearsome appearance, it has a gentle and caring nature.
author: cinnamoncreampuff

entry: POKENAME is highly protective of its Trainer, standing before it as a bodyguard. It quickly responds to any sudden movements nearby by erecting psychic shields around its Trainer, boxing them in completely until they are sure it is safe to exit.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME digs bunkers in the earth to provide cover for allies in battle, before retreating back into the ground once the structure is built. If the bunker is breached, it will burst out of the ground, slashing and chomping in a wild frenzy.
author: evilgammon

entry: It is unknown whether the shield attached to the hair of this Pokémon is extremely lightweight, or if POKENAME is extremely strong. Whatever the case, its bite can reduce solid stone to gravel and is sturdy enough to deflect many crushing blows.
author: evilgammon

entry: Between a heavily-armored, spiked head, its large, heavy tail, and its thick, muscled legs, this Pokémon is clearly fast, destructive, and dangerous.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME are a more aggressive species compared to their unfused counterpart. Rather than a defensive approach, wild POKENAME try to pierce enemies with their spikes. Despite this, POKENAME are far more effective when used defensively in real battle.
author: retrodox

entry: A POKENAME's shell always resembles a medieval castle of its home region. In some cases, they are the only surviving evidence of the castle's design.
author: staghorn

entry: Ancient civilizations based castles and sacrificial temples on POKENAME. This Pokémon always faces exactly north, eerily like certain famous pyramids.
author: ziggaway

entry: As POKENAME get older, their tails gain wear and tear. They need to be properly maintained and sharpened by their Trainer to keep their effectiveness.
author: retrodox

entry: During battle, it can make its own feelers rigid and brace itself against attacks by stabbing them into the ground. It will bar the path of anyone who approaches its den and/or its young.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME's only weak spot is its stomach. The rest of its body is heavily armored.
author: themicelegion

entry: Its mushrooms are made of a metallic alloy that is both tough and stretchy. Its punches are strong enough to pulverize a tanker hull.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon, sometimes called the Cabinet Monster, has organs within its mechanical exterior. It usually avoids hurting humans unless they cheat at its game, though it has been known to eat the occasional maintenance man.
author: hophoppip

entry: Its armored hide deflects all incoming strikes, making frontal attacks futile. Its imposing presence is often enough to deter would-be adversaries.
author: anarchaz

entry: Being too heavy to climb onto webs, POKENAME will make use of cave tunnels left behind by Onix. If it has young that it needs to defend, it can block up these tunnels with its rocky body.
author: notsaying.

entry: This Pokémon's horns grow with a razor's edge, but POKENAME prefer defence to offense so regularly blunt their horns by striking them against rocks and their packmates horns. When threatened, POKENAME come together to form a wall with their horns.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME is a pure-hearted Pokémon that serves as a nearly unbreakable wall for the defenseless. It will jump in front of any weaker Pokémon in battle to shield them from incoming attacks.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME battle by flying headfirst into their opponents before using their talons to finish them off. However this isn't the only use of their plates, as some POKENAME attack other males of their species to prove themselves the strongest.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME's shield-like face masks a frail body. Legends say those who glimpse beneath the armour are cursed, though none have lived to confirm it. It is found amongst ancient ruins, hiding in a shadowy corner and moving to stay always out of sight.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is found traversing the dry steppes of the world, where large expanses of the ground are covered by grass. Its slow body does not cause issues when it can take all the time in the world on the steppes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their surprisingly dense bodies to dive directly into Pokémon that enter their territories. POKENAME can crash into the ground at high speeds while sustaining only minor injuries.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME's highly ornate head, back, and tail seem cumbersome and impractical. However, they actually provide protection and are used for courting.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME are extremely reckless, battling by going into a headlong rush and thrashing wildly, their jaws tearing foes apart. With scales as tough as diamond and jaws that could shred through steel, POKENAME were unmatched in the ancient world.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME's durable body makes it able to take a head-on collision from a speeding car and barely flinch. Its rocky leaves are less sturdy, however, and may fly off after a sufficiently powerful impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has occasionally been spotted by people just waking up, vanishing as soon as it realizes it has been seen. It is said it watches over sleeping people, defending them from spirits that would cause the sleeper to suffer nightmares.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's thick armor and sharp iron claws allow it to pulverize any passing ships. It will often make its home in sunken ships and will fiercely fight other POKENAME for the larger ship.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's physical shielding may appear somewhat limited by its verticality, but it uses its psychic abilities to extend illusory duplications of those shields to create entire walls.
author: banquoviaquo

entry: POKENAME rides a surfboard that it carved by smashing its head into stone. Over time, the weathering from the waves it rides on wears it down, forcing POKENAME to make new ones.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Every POKENAME has a unique jingle and pattern on their banner-like bodies. Banner bearers in medieval times rushed into battle with POKENAME in tow, serving as a point of orientation for knights on the battlefield.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's heavy plating gives it a supremely slow swim speed, but makes it near impervious to predators. A rampaging Gyarados was once knocked unconscious after it charged straight into a POKENAME aimlessly swimming by.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME grabs prey with its long tentacles, it never lets it escape. Its head is protected by a thick stone helmet, whose spikes keep away anyone who tries to strike it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The super-tough defensive parts of POKENAME's body are still malleable to an extent. It can shift the location of these sturdy plates on its body, letting it defend itself from those who would try to attack its weak points.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shell is made of an unbreakable rock. If it thinks it is going to be moved or attacked, it plants itself in the ground and awaits safety.
author: turcai_87271

entry: POKENAME is an aggressive fusion that lives in small groups and often attacks small towns. It uses its hard shield and axe to fight its enemies.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME is an aggressive fusion that lives in small groups and often attacks small towns. It uses its hard shield and axe to fight its enemies.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME is found slacking for around 18 hours a day. This helps it store the energy needed to grow big and strong.
author: pkmkprestoyt

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time sleeping inside trees. It only wakes up to devour every leaf on the tree in a feeding frenzy, then goes straight back to its constant hibernation.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its grumpy expression, POKENAME prefers lounging in the shade. It lazily licks fruit off trees with its long, rubbery tongue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lumbers around slowly in tall grass areas, poking around for food and swatting at anything that bothers it with its huge arms. Its vines, if removed and steamed, make a meal that invokes drowsiness in those that eat it.
author: sk372

entry: Because the joey spends most of its time sleeping and requires little food, POKENAME is a rather lax parent. It is one of the few Kangaskhan fusions that allows others to hold its young for extended periods.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME takes its time consuming the nectar of entire fields of flowers. It violently punts anything that comes too close while it is eating; even much larger Pokémon can be sent flying by its kick.
author: sk372

entry: While usually docile, there was a report of a scientist that tried to wake up and move a POKENAME from where it made its bed. This is no longer done.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Extremely sedentary, POKENAME is rarely seen airborne, perching on a single branch for most of its life. A few small bugs or a single berry will keep its hunger satisfied for a month.
author: sk372

entry: On overcast days, POKENAME becomes unusually lethargic. It swats at intruders using fur-covered leaves that can leave allergic reactions on contact.
author: .izik

entry: Tiny and lazy, POKENAME only needs to feed once a week, loafing the rest of its time away. Even yawning is treated like a strenuous activity for POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often hold a languid expression because of how persistently groggy they are. They are a sedentary species that eats mud, which is plentiful after a heavy rain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is prone to experiencing atrophy of its muscles because of its sedentary lifestyle. It needs nutrient-rich Berry Juice to keep its muscles strong.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in a constant lack of motivation, which makes it tough to train even for experienced Trainers. If inspiration happens to strike this moody Pokémon, it'll release all its pent-up energy into drawings before losing the spark again.
author: milchik

entry: Highly attached to their Trainer but extremely lazy at heart, POKENAME uses psychic powers to subtly influence its Trainer to live a more indolent lifestyle like it does.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found hanging motionless on the trunks of fruit trees. There's a great force hiding within its seemingly hollow shell that can only be unleashed if POKENAME is heavily disturbed or just very hungry.
author: milchik

entry: Its strength is assumed to be great enough to move mountains, but its inert willpower leaves it floating in the air. A light breeze can whisk it away.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Though it spends most of its time lazing about, POKENAME uses its ability to camouflage into any surroundings to ambush prey or steal from nests. If it gets in trouble, it can use its incredible strength to defend itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME stores berries in its false mouth so it can lengthen the time between hunts for food. Occasionally, it may injure itself trying to store too much at once in this effort to be lazy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's oversized head is 90% bone, which makes it harder than steel. Since its skull is so thick, its brain is very tiny.
author: jokerswild

entry: POKENAME's fur has grown long and bulky due to its rest periods, which can sometimes last up to three days. When it is active, it is always focused on finding food to gorge upon, utilizing its vast strength to remove all obstacles in its way.
author: infinex21

entry: Power radiates from every inch of POKENAME's body, but it rarely moves, too lethargic to unleash its vast strength. Stories say if it were to unleash its true power, the planet itself would rupture.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time sleeping in the sun, using photosynthesis to fuel themselves. They release their excess energy through their fur, boosting the plant growth in the areas where they rest.
author: santon5512

entry: It rarely moves, so an ecosystem of small Pokémon flourishes on its back. This suits POKENAME just fine, as it can feed on leftover bits of their meals that fall from above, letting it remain sedentary longer.
author: sk372

entry: It knows precisely where to strike to cause maximum damage. Fearing it, many Trainers dare not speak its name.
author: weedspagon_real

entry: POKENAME utilizes its shield to wait out openings in their opponents' defenses. When it feels like it, it should only need to strike once.
author: loadedace

entry: It uses its lack of arms as an excuse to laze about. POKENAME will move to different locations, both on the surface and underwater, but only to try more exotic ways of lazing around.
author: epping_forest

entry: The single arm protruding from one of its gears is strong enough to shatter a large boulder in a single strike. Unfortunately, or thankfully, this Pokémon's strength is exhausted in a single strike and it will have to rest before it can strike again.
author: infinex21

entry: Just a simple brush from POKENAME's ribbons causes waves of lethargy to overwhelm a person. This effect leaves the afflicted party feeling lazy and listless for at least a week.
author: sk372

entry: Legends say it sleeps somewhere far above the clouds, and that should humanity's follies wake it from its slumber, it will descend with great fury and put all of humanity to rest.
author: sk372

entry: While powerful enough to move continents, it never takes battling seriously. Trainers of POKENAME often unfuse it out of frustration after a week.
author: faelocke

entry: POKENAME enlists help from Drifloon in order to fly, as it's too heavy to float on its own power. It commands them to carry it to areas rich in fruit, so it can drop down and gorge itself.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its incredible strength and blades capable of cleaving stone in an instant, POKENAME prefers to laze about all day. Should it need to eat, it rises briefly to cut fruit from nearby trees before settling back down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's singing is quite cacophonous, as it doesn't bother to practice and hone its skill. Listeners often feign sleep to make it stop more quickly; the resulting indignant wrath is still less painful than its song.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself in shady places, leaving its open mouth exposed while it waits for prey to walk into it. It often falls asleep while waiting and ends up scaring away potential prey by snoring.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is usually content to float placidly in water, ignoring most of its surroundings. Should something agitate it, however, it will fly into a thrashing rage potent enough to give a Gyarados pause.
author: sk372

entry: One half of POKENAME's brain is asleep at any given time, which conserves energy but slows POKENAME's reaction time. However, POKENAME is devastatingly swift and powerful when it does act, easily besting most wild Pokémon that dare to come close.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME only fights for the fun of it and only fights opponents that will give it a good challenge. However, it is not afraid to fight dirty if its opponent gets the upper hand.
author: mistymagius

entry: Many falsely assume the two Pokémon work in tandem to trap unfortunate victims, but in reality the Slaking is trying to save any creature Palossand tries to sneakily capture and hide within itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME mushrooms cause wild mood swings when consumed, with the consumer swinging from frenetic, angry energy to slothful lethargy. POKENAME themselves exhibit these same mood swings and are best avoided.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rarely moves but will attack with brutal force if its space is disturbed. It builds nests beneath fruit trees and guards them fiercely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in the shallows of rivers and lazily wait for ripe fruit to drop from overhanging trees. When angered, it trashes about with enough power to shatter rocks.
author: mepp.

entry: It appears to spend most of the day in a state of deep meditation. However, close examination reveals that it's merely snoozing.
author: hophoppip

entry: The best time to see one of these Pokémon is after a volcanic eruption. POKENAME prefers shield volcanoes.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME loves battling more than anything, however it is extremely lazy. It exclusively fights sitting down and will stop attacking and sleep if too exhausted.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME spend the majority of their time slumbering, fidgeting and twitching in agitated sleep. When roused, they fly into a rage that can last for hours, racing around and tearing apart anything they can get their hands on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its wings have atrophied from lack of use and even the fire on its tail hardly smolders when it deigns to move around. If angered, however, POKENAME's fire will erupt into a blazing inferno used to immolate the target of its ire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME experience a debilitating malaise whenever they have to train, often feeling lazy or unwilling to practice. Despite this weakness, their muscles miraculously remain tough and without atrophy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The physical prowess of POKENAME is unmatched. However, its strength has made it sedentary and arrogant.
author: griddle

entry: If two POKENAME meet, they'll battle until either one or both of them collapse from exhaustion. This is how they form bonds.
author: dragonzzilla

entry: POKENAME uses extremely flashy moves to defeat opponents. It is deceptively lazy, as its power is truly effortless.
author: cyprexx

entry: POKENAME lies under berries, patiently waiting for the berries to fall into its mouth. However, it is too lazy to pick up any other berries so if any berry falls next to it, it will be left to rot.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though it is a powerful and fast Pokémon, it is often too apathetic to move. Only Trainers with great patience and perseverance can hope to tame a POKENAME over time.
author: frokachu

entry: At any given moment, at least one of POKENAME's heads is sleeping. This is inconvenient as it means the other heads have to drag it around.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME plant seeds into the ground before pouring a special nectar from their bulbs to help the sprouts grow. While the plants do grow big and strong, no matter the species of plant, it will be poisonous to humans.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's skull is coated in a white, sticky poison that can cause convulsions on contact. When it cries, the toxin seeps onto the surrounding ground.
author: .izik

entry: It ruthlessly attacks foes by charging at them with the venomous horn on its forehead. It despises getting wet, so during rainstorms POKENAME hides deep inside caves until the weather clears.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many Trainers are tempted to play with POKENAME's young, not realizing their poison is strong enough to faint a Slaking. If they continue to annoy the pup, the mother Pokémon sends them flying with a Mega Punch.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's wings are filled with tiny scales that are extremely poisonous. Even brief contact can cause intense nausea.
author: .izik

entry: It uses alluring dances to hypnotize foes. It controls poison and spreads it through the air.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Usually found in rivers, POKENAME keeps its body submerged, while keeping its eyes and ears above the surface. Due to its coloration, most will not see it. When prey is spotted it lunges surprisingly fast, landing a venomous bite.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME hides its young in its shell, concealing them from any danger. If a Pokémon figures out its hiding spot, it will send them flying with a devastating Crabhammer.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME make nests along craggy cliffs where they can see the world below them. They are incredibly protective of these nests, so Trainers are advised to bring a piece of jerky as a distraction while navigating the jagged cliffs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A truly rare sighting; POKENAME has enough poison in it's horn to fell even the largest of Wailords!
author: supersonicloki

entry: POKENAME have thick scales coating their serpentine bodies, protecting them from the rocky terrain they live in. Their scales protect them from one another when battling for territory, allowing them to slam one another with powerful blows safely.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flies with its psychic powers in the daylight, its coloration providing camouflage against sightings. It seeks out toxic spills, absorbing the poison into itself and bringing nature back into equilibrium.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are renowned for their ability to mimic sounds, keeping their nests safe by copying predator growls. They imprint onto objects that make sounds, and follow Trainers to defend those objects with venomous pecks.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are alert and vigilant creatures that stand guard outside burrows to ensure the safety of those inside. When they spot a predator, they usher their kin into the burrow before having a standoff with the threat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have toughened skin and carapaces. Their stiff coatings mean they are not particularly mobile Pokémon, but anything that does manage to take a bite out of them finds them to be foul tasting and unappetising.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can weave intricate webs in which it traps prey, finishing them off with venomous claws or fangs. It tends to infest trees previously inhabited by Ariados, having driven them away with its brute strength.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME feed kindred members of their nest poison from their stone spheres. Their young have special enzymes that process and neutralize the poison once ingested and are nourished by the remaining paste.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite their size, their bodies are extremely tough, able to withstand attacks from much larger foes. They are quite skittish, however, fleeing when outnumbered.
author: santon5512

entry: The flower on POKENAME's back can release a fine powder that puts anyone who breathes it to sleep; this dust is even used to make strong sleeping agents. Its spines are laced with potent toxins to protect the flower's petals from other Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The massive arm at the end of its body carves intricate symbols into rock or soil. These markings seem to serve as territorial warnings, though some suspect they hold deeper meanings tied to ancient knowledge.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are never seen outside their shells, constantly sheltering inside them. They move around using their powerful arms, lumbering from one feeding site to the next.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME dig through the ground, creating huge tunnels. Some are found to reach a depth of over six-tenths of a mile underground.
author: krune

entry: Despite its fragile appearance, POKENAME's chitin is tough as diamonds. When threatened, it uses spurs built into its claws to deploy venom, incapacitating its foes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Roving bands of POKENAME inhabit mountain passes, using their claws to scale rock faces. When humans pass underneath, the Pokémon drop down and use paralyzing poison on their axes to steal what they can.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's shell is filled with a poisonous mixture that is constantly steaming out of between the plates. If it is inhaled, it can cause the victim to feel as though they were on fire.
author: clownatosis

entry: POKENAME's broad wings allow it to majestically fly for days without tiring. Its long beak and the spines along its back are coated with potent toxins, which it uses to overpower foes and drive intruders from its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Groups of POKENAME were used during the ZERO-ONE's aquatic testing phases. They are valued for their strength and their mother-like care for anything struggling to swim.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has special fangs that hold venom back when it bites onto its children. It does this to carry the children to safety whenever there is danger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wields its tail like a whip. It has been recorded piercing through 4 feet of concrete.
author: winchbeef

entry: POKENAME burrow through mineral veins, gorging themselves on rare earth elements to prepare themselves for evolution. They are jealously protective of their feeding ground, as battles between POKENAME over food can sometimes cause minor earthquakes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hunt by ambushing prey and restraining them with their massive tail. Once the prey is subdued, they inject venom through their fangs and drag them back to their nest, where baby Nidoran wait for their return.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Every winter, POKENAME descends from their mountain homes to fish for Poliwag on frozen lakes. Using razor-sharp claws, they drag their favorite treats from the depths, then impale them on venom-laced horns.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The fronts of their bodies are their softest spots, with the rest of their bodies covered in thick scales. By launching themselves with their tails and curling into balls, they deliver crushing tackles.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a pack hunter, always hunting prey in groups of four. It takes turns in specialized roles to distract prey before the group strikes with razor-sharp, venomous claws.
author: ghostslythe

entry: To protect its young, or its eggs, it will clutch them against its belly and turn its back lined with sharp quills toward the nearest threat. Its horn carries a strong venom, which it will ram into foes with a forceful tackle.
author: infinex21

entry: When their children are threatened, POKENAME become relentless defenders. The scales covering their bodies provide excellent protection, allowing them to rush attackers and batter them with crushing strikes from their fists, legs, or tails.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Found training in swamps, POKENAME ingests local poisonous fauna to gain immunity. If attacked, their sweat contains a cocktail of all ingested poisons, making a single strike lethal.
author: ghostslythe

entry: With a sixth sense, POKENAME can tell when earthquakes or toxic spills are about to occur. If sensed, it quickly puts its young on its back, tramples anything in its path, and uses a venomous bite on anything resisting.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME colonies are able to clear large swathes of woodland, working together to chew down trees and pile them together into elaborate dams. These dams are put at the boundaries of their territory, controlling the water flow in and out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The auras around POKENAME's horns and claws are aerosolized poison. Though its movements seem ponderous, one breath is enough to drop a Snorlax.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME protects local Nidoran by sprouting barbed vines from their back and releasing toxic pollen into the air. In return, Nidoran provide POKENAME with berries and affection.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their bulk to knock down trees and create large clearings in forests. They patrol these clearings and use them as display grounds, shaking their large frills and stomping the ground to scare off competition.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lazes around for most of the day. Its thick hide protects it from any real damage. Despite doing almost nothing all day, it thinks itself superior to everyone.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are highly protective of their young, defending them from any danger they may face. Their armor is as hard as steel, making them the perfect shield for their children.
author: santon5512

entry: Anyone who bullies POKENAME's young will be sliced by this Pokémon's wings. It uses its hard scales to swim through ice floes and take on the icy waters to protect its children swimming behind.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have lots of other Pokémon they look after, so they change polarity to take care of one group at a time. If Pokémon of the wrong polarity approach POKENAME, they are repelled until it is their turn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME seeks other Nidoran-related fusions in order to fight for and protect them diligently as family.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The twin flails of POKENAME strike hard and fast against all opposition. Though normally it carefully coordinates its attacks, if a child is in danger it goes berserk with protective instincts and enters a whirling frenzy to smash the threat.
author: sk372

entry: Highly defensive of its young, POKENAME's back barbs bristle and ooze poison if it senses anyone or anything straying too close.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Packs of POKENAME patrol storm-tossed badlands with their young. They absorb the ambient ozone in the air and use it to help replenish the venom they spend on hunting.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a stone armor that shields it from tearing blows during territorial battles. If one of its venom-soaked horns breaks, it hides away in its den until it grows back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Encased in rugged stone plating, POKENAME endures brutal clashes over territory without flinching. Should a venom-laced horn snap off, it retreats underground, waiting in silence for it to regenerate.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hunt through the use of illusions, masking their appearance and pretending to be small and unassuming Pokémon. Their illusions are elaborate enough to even fool other POKENAME, which results in fierce battles when the deception is revealed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Extremely protective of those it cares about, this Pokémon will stake its life to ensure the safety of its young and Trainer.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME is powerfully aggressive, but also has a strong maternal instinct to protect anything smaller than it. Some have even been seen getting into fights with Kangaskhan over who could better protect the child.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon is known for its robust scales and impactful punches. POKENAME's nails grow at a rapid rate on its hands and feet. It uses them to inject its target with poison by piercing them.
author: over9001

entry: POKENAME act as the guards for unevolved POKENAME. They appear to be the most intelligent out of the colony they care for, and therefore give orders in place of the colony's leaders if the situation calls for it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME act as the guards for unevolved POKENAME. They appear to be the most intelligent out of the colony they care for, and therefore give orders in place of the colony's leaders if the situation calls for it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME act as the guards for unevolved POKENAME. They appear to be the most intelligent out of the colony they care for, and therefore give orders in place of the colony's leaders if the situation calls for it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A POKENAME's legs have incredible strength, allowing them to jump far in a single bound and kick with devastating power. It emits a toxic oily secretion onto its fur to keep it clean and nearly shining.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Known for its powerful kicks, this Pokémon can be heard throughout the night leaping through the forests.
author: supersonicloki

entry: Created when a substitute doll is destroyed by toxins, POKENAME haunts toy stores. Late at night it will rearrange entire aisles, mischievously giggling and jumping out at guard Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Using the toxic barbs on the sides of its skull, POKENAME can pierce through the thickest hides. Intense territorial disputes between these Pokémon cause localized earthquakes, with each slamming its opponent into a daze for a finishing barb strike.
author: ghostslythe

entry: It communicates only with its owner, being very secretive. It keeps its form hidden in its scaly body, and attacks by extending shadowy needles.
author: houndrys.

entry: On nights when the moon is full, POKENAME gather in a single large group to pair with one another. Their tails are such a deep obsidian that they mirror the night sky. Some astronomers even use POKENAME to study constellations.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have a strong venom that can take down a large Tauros but struggle to produce more than a small fire. They are protective of the fire on their tail and refuse to let other Pokémon near it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: There is only one female POKENAME in each colony of Nidopuff, where it acts as their leader. They can inflate their bodies to many times their normal size. When they exhale, poison gas is emitted from their orifices.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's ears are powerful in all senses of the word. When they suddenly stretch forward, they exert enough force to topple a truck. POKENAME's sense of hearing is also impeccable and even rivals the elusive Clefairy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite its small size, POKENAME's poison is surprisingly potent. Its shell is thick and durable, and its tackles can easily uproot a tree.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME is aggressive and will attack anything to prove its strength to itself. When defeated, it often returns to fight the same opponent until it finds a way to be victorious.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME viciously attacks any perceived threat to its offspring. When it leaves its nest to hunt, it rubs its young with its mane which has a low-level toxin that wards off predators.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME thrive in high altitude environments, as its hide is both tough and cold resistant. Their hide has been discovered to be a great material in the making of hiking equipment.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME performs dances for people that it likes. This dances spreads mind-controlling poison through the air to lure the person to its home.
author: themicelegion

entry: Though small in stature, POKENAME can send foes flying with harsh tackles from its horn. Its leaves can absorb moonlight to regain energy at night.
author: synaesthesis

entry: The leaf-like moss growing from between POKENAME's hard scales is used in many remedies. When ground up, it can be used to treat burns and abrasions, providing relief and healing properties.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses sound waves from its ears to stun prey before surrounding them in Toxic Spikes. This strategy allows it to immobilize and weaken its prey before moving in for the final strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses Toxic to stun other flying Pokémon while it travels. It then takes them back to its den for others of its kind to feast on, making it a dangerous hunter of the skies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very protective of its young and will show no mercy to anything that threatens them. When agitated, its skin secretes a deadly poison that makes it volatile in combat.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hard scales on POKENAME's body make it aerodynamic, allowing it to perform flying kicks with ease. This enhanced agility gives it a significant advantage in aerial combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers living in extremely cold climates, where its body produces a thin, clear poisonous liquid that leaks from its spikes. This toxic substance acts as both a defense and as a hunting aid.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME listen intently for approaching Pokémon, staying on guard against rivals for their food. They violently shake their bodies and loose a cloud of poisonous dust when they get into fights.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME weaves toxic spells using a radioactive Moon Stone focus, ensuring they hit with its psychic powers. To avoid harming its Trainer, it encloses the radiation in a psychic field.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME antennae can sense even the slightest air movements, alerting them to approaching Pokémon long before they see them. They violently shake their bodies and loose a cloud of poisonous dust when they get into fights.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are typically found at night, using the light of the moon to navigate. When two POKENAME pass by one another, they will angrily flutter around and try to knock the other off their flight path with gusts from their wings.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When the light in POKENAME's torso pulses, its venom is at peak potency. Waking it during its sleep may trigger in it a panic attack worsened by hallucinogenic toxins.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows into cliffsides with its horn to sleep. If it detects a coming rockslide, it braces with Defense Curl to avoid serious harm.
author: .izik

entry: After flying, POKENAME embeds its horn into cliff walls to rest. Once lodged in the stone, even strong wind gusts cannot dislodge it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME injects mild toxin into tree roots with its horn to soften them. It rips the roots into pieces and digs as deep as 100 ft before feeding.
author: .izik

entry: Living in eroded caves made by raging rivers, POKENAME are strong enough to swim up rapids. If threatened, they dig their venom-laced claws into the foe and peck viciously.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME secrete a potent venom in their fur that poisons any Pokémon that touches them. They will consume some of their own venom before getting into fights, letting it drive them into a frenzy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME secrete a potent venom in their fur that poisons any Pokémon that touches them. They will consume some of their own venom before getting into fights, letting it drive them into a frenzy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is spunky and opinionated, refusing to follow orders that it disagrees with. It loves to play, sassily barking at its Trainer so they will give chase and it can run away in a flash of fire.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is willing to lay down its life to guard the flocks in its care. As it grows older and becomes more of a pet than a worker, its Trainer should still let it patrol the fields occasionally so its pride is not hurt.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Ancient drawings in Kalos depict POKENAME barreling through armies of knights. When faced in the modern age, most assume it will use flaming attacks, only to be shocked with poisonous breath.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME takes after wrestlers, and enjoys tackling foes to the floor. This, unfortunately, can knock them unconscious.
author: notsaying.

entry: A single dictionary is unable to encompass the lexical complexity of their language, which is used to educate their children on how to survive in the world. The nuances of their cries and grunts remain a topic of study for linguists.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is ready for anything. Its punch has been known to be fatal to smaller creatures.
author: supersonicloki

entry: This Pokémon is only known to flinch when it pulls a muscle. It seeks out and challenges other Machoke fusions.
author: supersonicloki

entry: POKENAME practices a variety of fighting styles that prepare it to take on all kinds of foes. If a POKENAME grabs ahold of an enemy while in combat, it will inject a powerful toxin into them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A toxic positivity personality at any gym; strong Trainers seek POKENAME out when they want to push their limits as a Trainer and as a human.
author: supersonicloki

entry: POKENAME flail their leaves wildly around when battling against other POKENAME in the wild, trying to intimidate their rivals into submission without having to actually fight. If forced to battle properly, they will try to bite at their foe's stem.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME waddle from tree to tree in search of a place to spend their day. The ideal tree has excellent access to light from the sky as well as fertile soil for them to root through; they will battle with one another over these locations.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hang from the lower branches of trees, trailing their thorned vine down toward the ground. Should anything walk into the trailing vine, they lash out, aiming to catch the unfortunate passerby with their venomous stinger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The combination of Nidoqueen's tough scales and Golem's boulder-like body allow POKENAME to shrug off most attacks. It does occasionally have to shed its skin, which leaves it vulnerable, but it always grows back stronger than ever.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME fight using their impressive bulk, slamming their tough shells into one another with body slams that can shatter tree trunks. They are prone to aggression and will readily battle other POKENAME on sight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's tongue is coated in poison, which it uses to subdue anyone who gets too close to its kin. This toxic attack allows it to protect its family and territory with lethal force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home in forests that are near sources of high pollution. An increasing presence is a sure sign of coming ecological damage.
author: veteranadventurer

entry: Despite its solitary nature, POKENAME ventures into nearby villages when it senses an approaching tornado. It releases a shrill cry to warn those in its path.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME strives to become the best at fisticuffs, but has difficulty finding regular sparring partners. Rumors circulate about its fists cursing any hit by its punches, so few are willing to train alongside it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME appears before others and blows smog that takes the form of images of imminent disasters. Many misinterpret the smoke as a curse rather than a warning, giving POKENAME a poor reputation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live on mountains. When they sense disaster, they panic and tirelessly charge to warn anyone nearby, running over anything in their way.
author: totodile.

entry: Some POKENAME have different styles of plating and shorter faces. POKENAME can become enraged if their warnings go unheeded.
author: totodile.

entry: If it senses a disaster, it will begin frantically giving out its eggs to help. Despite its kindness, many still believe POKENAME caused the disaster.
author: fountainihili

entry: When POKENAME sits motionless at the bottom of the water, its fur waving with the current disguises it as seagrass.
author: .realthree

entry: The shimmery scales shed from Pokémon's wings can be made into life-saving medicine for certain rare illnesses with no other known cures.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Whenever an POKENAME washes up, it is seen as an ill omen, though some believe returning it to the sea appeases the fates. Those that look directly into the gem are said to go into a trance-like state, murmuring about stars and distant planets.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME thrives around power plants. It uses its horn like a lighting rod to prevent storms from destroying power lines.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME live in dormant volcanoes. Seeing them elsewhere means a nearby mountain will erupt soon.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are born with two horns, but one inevitably breaks off as it battles other POKENAME. Some collect the broken horns to use as luck charms.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are able to predict natural disasters by sensing changes in their environment. They appear in settlements near where the disaster is predicted to occur, using their transformative abilities to try and convey the danger to residents.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's horn is very sensitive to its environment. It is said that the type of natural disaster POKENAME witnesses will influence its evolution.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Building trust with an POKENAME takes quite a bit of time, as it is naturally a very solitary Pokémon. It is quite serious and hates being startled.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Where it surfaces from the ocean, a great tsunami will soon arrive. POKENAME will then stand stalwart on the beach, shielding others from the waves.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: During storms, POKENAME's lightning-shaped horn absorbs electrical energy, storing it in the gem on its forehead. Other Electric-type Pokémon sometimes gather nearby to recharge from its stored power.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as pop-up ads on weather websites during seasons with dangerous weather, hoping to be accidentally clicked. Once activated, it converts the interaction into energy to consume.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resemble an error message about a sprite that is installed on the PC. Once a person clicks on the error message, an ominous warning appears to warn the user that their system is infected and has to pay POKENAME or lose access to the PC.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When it senses an impending disaster, it flies around the area, releasing a bone-chilling scream. Though many believe that it is cursing the land, POKENAME is actually warning people of the danger ahead.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME are known for their ravenous appetites and aggressive natures in regard to defending their territories. Because these Pokémon are especially fond of vegetation, farmers consider the sight of POKENAME to be an ill omen.
author: infinex21

entry: After fusing, POKENAME loses the ability to control its powers, leading to apocalyptic hailstorms that follow in its wake. Even a single sighting of POKENAME often leads to panic in nearby communities.
author: alestrius

entry: POKENAME is said to bring about great disasters in the form of terrible thunderstorms. When battling, it surrounds itself with lightning before fiercely charging in.
author: mepp.

entry: Some legends claim that POKENAME harbor immense power within them, with further claims that said power will manifest in disasters. They are incredibly elusive and seem to be remarkably attuned to the emotions of others.
author: infinex21

entry: Many years ago, a fisherman claimed to see POKENAME darting out of tall grass and into the sky. A few seconds later, a lightning bolt soon claimed the tall grass and set it ablaze. It's possible that POKENAME can see far into the future.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The pollen POKENAME spreads from its leaf smells like basil and accelerates plant growth. If it senses an approaching flood, it encourages trees to grow rapidly to absorb the excess water.
author: .izik

entry: The sensitive leaf on their head guides them to places where natural disasters are bound to happen. The grey skies before a storm provide just the right level of light for POKENAME to sunbathe in; otherwise they either starve or fall ill.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME's fur is extremely valuable, but it is said that anyone who cuts it off of an POKENAME will suffer one hundred years of bad luck.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME, now blessed with the speed afforded to it by its powerful wings, travels great distances to warn people of coming danger.
author: sejha

entry: POKENAME creates images made of sparks above it in an attempt to warn others of impending disasters. Because its powers are weak, however, the images are vague or misinterpreted, and its warnings often go unheeded.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's large horns help them tune their psychic abilities. They're highly revered in certain cultures thanks to their pitch-perfect Future Sight.
author: kiwikelly

entry: Should it sense someone with terrible luck, it will fly in circles over their home to release any bad omens. It prefers to fly in a clockwise motion.
author: .izik

entry: It is believed that POKENAME can sense when someone's death is near. When it perches on a rooftop and sings its eerie song, someone in the household will die exactly three days later.
author: amiel997

entry: In ancient times, people placed stone statues of POKENAME on rooftops, believing they would bring good fortune and protect their homes from disasters.
author: ambrosia04

entry: When a disaster nears, the orb on POKENAME's tail grows intensely warm. Its water attacks heat up as well, becoming hot enough to burn skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a tree while waiting for its instincts to confirm an upcoming disaster. If it senses danger, it shakes violently to warn nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very friendly. Children like to use the symbol on its head as a spinner to play fortune-telling games.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME age slowly and are rarely found in areas inhabited by humans. Before performing a Solar Beam, POKENAME's petals glow brightly as they unleash a cataclysmic burst of energy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are docile enough to be easily kept around humans but still have the instincts of an Absol. They are kept at rocket launch sites to detect if a natural disaster or extreme weather will interfere with a launch.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME floats lazily in rivers, unaffected by the chaotic world around it. However, if it detects an approaching flood, it will let out a deep bellow to alert nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has the power to predict disasters when its forked tail quivers. However, it will only share its knowledge with a Trainer it deems worthy.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's flower has begun to bloom in the presence of high pollution. It can slow the poisoning of the environment, but can't stop it alone.
author: veteranadventurer

entry: It watches people in the city from the tops of buildings. When it foresees a cheese-related disaster, it jumps into action.
author: .izik

entry: When a disaster is impending, POKENAME will command a group of Unown and Unown fusions to spell out a warning message. It becomes panicked when there are too few Unown forms to create the right words.
author: hophoppip

entry: If POKENAME senses an incoming hurricane, it channels psychic energy through its rear head to gently urge Pokémon and people away. If they do not listen, it forces them back with powerful psychic waves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appear where earthquakes destroyed towns. Despite superstitions, this is simply because the tremors woke them from their underground slumber.
author: kiwikelly

entry: This mischievous Pokémon tempts Trainers with dangerous dares. Only the most courageous know that POKENAME's presence guarantees their safety.
author: kiwikelly

entry: A flock of POKENAME is considered a bad omen across multiple cultures around the world, but singular POKENAME actually make for great pets.
author: kiwikelly

entry: The berry juice POKENAME makes in its shell causes terrifying visions of doom and calamity that can make even the bravest Trainers cower in fear.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME often appear on compromised trees to eat their soft wood and sap. Arborists often use them to predict if a tree is about to fall or break.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are prized for their beautiful feathers and fur. However, they make terrible pets, as they will destroy everything their owner holds dear.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME reside deep below the icy tundra, where it is comfortably cold and dry. They are a rare sight in the wild, as they were once hunted to near extinction.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Feared by many, POKENAME only appears when danger is near, its presence a silent warning cloaked in strength. Its thick fur protects it from harsh winter seasons.
author: curazy

entry: The honey-like scent from POKENAME's fur becomes incredibly strong before a violent storm. The aroma lures smaller Pokémon into its den, providing them shelter and safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travel between volcanoes and mountainsides, watching for impending eruptions or rockslides. They store lava within their shells and cleave through boulders with their horns, working to protect people from the foreseen disasters.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its sensitive branches detect changes in ocean temperature and acidity. When large groups of POKENAME surface, it's a sign of severe climate change.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME patrol their territory to ensure that nothing has gone awry. If something is amiss, they let out eerie howls to alert the rest of their pack.
author: kiwikelly

entry: This Pokémon lives a lonely and solitary life. While it has been observed approaching packs of Houndoom in the wild, POKENAME is always rejected.
author: rihse

entry: POKENAME is rare in the wild but features heavily in Hoenn folklore that foretells impending disasters. Legend states that the worst omen is to witness one eat its own tail until it disappears.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its nose can somehow smell earthquakes before they occur. It will bury its head in the dirt if it senses danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's thick fur keeps it warm as it rolls through snowy mountains during brutal winters. If it detects a severe blizzard approaching, it trumpets a warning from its trunk.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME show up long before a PC is compromised to sell antivirus software to help ward against viruses. Their warnings are often ignored and eventually result in the PC being taken over by a virus.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME show up long before a PC is compromised to sell antivirus software to help ward against viruses. Their warnings are often ignored and eventually result in the PC being taken over by a virus.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Looking at POKENAME's horns causes visions of terrible disasters. Some believe those are omens, while others think it's POKENAME's defense mechanism.
author: kiwikelly

entry: This species overwhelms its foes with speed and cunning rather than brute strength. Highly perceptive, it can identify weak points and openings at a mere glance.
author: xillo

entry: POKENAME is rare in the wild but features heavily in Hoenn folklore that foretells impending disasters. Legend states that the worst omen is to witness one eat its own tail until it disappears.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's long tongue darts out during poor weather to detect scent changes that indicate severe storms. If it senses an impending disaster, it lets out a piercing screech as a warning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME signals warnings of imminent natural disasters with subtle changes in the patterns on its wings. Its fearsome appearance has made it a common Pokémon to appear alongside villains in fiction stories, despite its benevolent nature.
author: pjporwoll

entry: As POKENAME is only found on foggy mountaintops, not many people have seen it. Inspired by myths describing it as a legendary guardian spirit, an author wrote a popular novel where a brave girl saves the world with her POKENAME companion.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME wanders around the world, sensing the flow of calamity with its horn. It always lets tragedies happen, just to travel back in time and see how exactly they can be avoided.
author: epping_forest

entry: Some say that if you are cursed by an POKENAME, you are destined to meet your end no matter how hard you try to avoid it. They can be seen wandering around cities recently hit by natural disasters.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME possesses the ability to foresee disasters, crying when it receives the precognitive visions. Researchers have found it cries differently depending on the kind of disaster, and use this to more quickly decipher its warnings.
author: sk372

entry: Using their ability to sense incoming natural disasters, POKENAME will follow thunderstorms to race against other POKENAME. If they detect a different disaster nearby, POKENAME use stored electricity to send small signals as a warning.
author: npshi

entry: Supposedly, its large eye allows it to witness natural disasters that may befall a locale it witnesses. Each head is capable of thinking individually, but they may also think as one on a level comparable to a Metagross.
author: infinex21

entry: It is believed that an POKENAME is the last thing someone will see before passing away.
author: kiwikelly

entry: In the past, many thought a swooping POKENAME intended to steal their life away with its scythe-shaped tail. It is now known it is actually diving to protect them, pushing them away from perceived danger.
author: sk372

entry: If POKENAME senses an upcoming tornado, it screeches loudly while flinging sand erratically. This chaotic display serves as a warning to those nearby to seek shelter.
author: .izik

entry: Known as "The Fist of Ill Omen", an POKENAME wins fights by knowing its opponent's moves before they ever make them. If it knows it cannot win, it will recklessly attempt to take its foe down with it.
author: mileysakiko

entry: Always one step ahead, POKENAME predicts worst-case scenarios, absorbing the emotions of those around it to maintain the balance between light and darkness.
author: wolfythehunter

entry: It is said that an POKENAME that's well taken care of can alter the future to one where its Trainer lives a happy and prosperous life.
author: kiwikelly

entry: With captivating grace, POKENAME predicts moments of change with great accuracy, but its calm nature means its predictions are not feared, but embraced.
author: wolfythehunter

entry: With the power to foresee catastrophic events and the heart of a protector, POKENAME uses its energy to guide others through the darkness, dispelling the shadows with its power and presence.
author: wolfythehunter

entry: Many POKENAME have lived long lives, with some even having outlived their Trainers and even being passed down within some families. They have a keen sense for most dangers and if they consider their Trainer worthy, will guard them from said dangers.
author: infinex21

entry: The scythe POKENAME wields causes many to fear it as a reaper of souls. However, it is in truth a gentle soul who only uses the weapon in defense of those who cannot protect themselves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hide their feelings behind a solemn expression to give off an air of confidence. They were once held in high esteem because they served as bodyguards for nobility.
author: quackquackattack

entry: With its capability to sense disasters enhanced, POKENAME now strives to both warn those of danger, but take matters into its own claws to protect lives. Its scythe grows sharper the more lives it vows to defend, making it incredibly deadly.
author: merclipse

entry: POKENAME appear near unmarked graves. It is said to ferry forgotten souls to the world beyond, guiding those with no one left to remember them.
author: imeavie

entry: POKENAME use their color-changing fur to communicate with humans. Scientists have yet to fully decipher this intricate language.
author: kiwikelly

entry: By channelling its aura, POKENAME sharpens its senses and can detect threats from over 50 km away. Its remarkable speed and instincts guide it in combat to deliver devastating attacks.
author: danieru4729

entry: POKENAME are powerful cave-dwelling Pokémon that will attack anyone who crosses their path mercilessly. It's believed that only Trainers with determination can command the respect of POKENAME.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is a nocturnal hunter that feasts on forest-dwelling Pokémon. Rather than navigating through the forest, it uses its razor-sharp appendages to slice down the trees.
author: patch

entry: POKENAME is often found at the edges of ecological disaster zones, warning away trespassers and absorbing the pollution within to heal the area.
author: veteranadventurer

entry: The teeth of an POKENAME are about as sharp as a high-grade kitchen knife. Poachers frequently harvest these teeth to sell for a moderate price.
author: .izik

entry: This self fusion closely resembles Absol's Mega Evolution.  While the Mega form emits an intimidating aura, intensifying common misunderstandings of Absol, this fusion is able to emit a calm aura, revealing its true, protective nature.
author: infranscia

entry: Ancient tomes claim that peering between POKENAME's fingers allows one to see future disasters. However, this has been proven untrue on multiple occasions, though some still believe in the legend.
author: .izik

entry: Many POKENAME will gather in an area where a natural disaster is soon to occur, ready to take the spirts of all who do not survive to the afterlife.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME's sharp horn is extremely sensitive to changes in its environment, leading it to be seen as hyper-aware to natural disasters. Broken bits of this Pokémon's horn were collected in the past in the hopes they would serve as early warning signs.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME mostly wanders rugged mountains. A cut from this scythe is said to curse the victim with approaching disaster.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME mostly wanders rugged mountains. A cut from this scythe is said to curse the victim with approaching disaster.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The two blades of POKENAME are said to represent good and bad luck. The first one that strikes seals its enemy's fate for the rest of its life.
author: kiwikelly

entry: This valiant fusion is said to help and protect those upon whom a disastrous fate will fall. It is unknown whether or not it is effective.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME are said to be agents of fate, as they work together in small groups to prevent small-scale disasters, or cause them to come about.
author: kiwikelly

entry: POKENAME's piercing eyes can see through heavy storm clouds to detect brewing disasters. If it senses imminent danger, it howls into the sky, sending warning sparks through the air.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has the peculiar ability to sense incoming sea storms, and thus has developed the habit of appearing to sailors just before tsunamis. This has led to the mistaken belief that spotting one at sea is a sign of great misfortune.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME seem to be keenly aware when a severe change in their surroundings is about to occur. Some fables claim that a terrible storm will follow in the wake of an POKENAME that flies overhead.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME was first discovered in the irradiated ruin of a research facility. The hands of its clock creep toward midnight whenever it senses that the humans and Pokémon around it are not in harmony, or a great disaster has occurred.
author: quietcognition

entry: Many believe POKENAME are cursed. Though their protective illusions appear perfect, any group meeting one is beset by disasters.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is highly renowned within disaster management and emergency response teams. It is capable of sensing discord not only in the natural environment but also within human beings through its ribbon-like feelers.
author: robobunnybutt

entry: POKENAME are drawn to those with troubled spirits and will offer comfort or their very strength to aid them. Their feelers can lash with such swiftness that they can churn the very air into potent Razor Wind attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its strength and intimidating appearance to frighten villages into evacuating before disasters strike. In the past it was believed to be the cause, but now it's known that it merely acts the villain to hasten people fleeing to safety.
author: sk372
