entry: When emerging from the water, POKENAME twirls the sprout on its head to dry off. This releases a pleasant nectarine scent into the surrounding area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have an uncanny ability to locate sources of water, even if they are underground or otherwise obscured. Quite a few Pokémon Rangers have at least one POKENAME in case of emergency.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its feelers to stir soil and plant seeds, nurturing the ground around it. Gardens tended by POKENAME always produce some of the hardiest of plants.
author: sk372

entry: After one year of growth, the seed on POKENAME's head detaches and floats away, carried on the wind. If the seed lands in fertile soil, it will grow into a small garden, creating a small ecosystem of different plants.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME has a round, plant-like head atop a sleek, alien body radiating vibrant energy. It controls the forces of nature and psychic powers. It has yet to properly develop its Grass-type powers.
author: thepandasharky

entry: Twigs sprout and grow slowly from POKENAME's body. It snaps these off after a point and uses them as a weapon in battle to help hone its combat prowess.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sleeps for many hours each day, and the first thing it does when it wakes up is pad damp mud or soil upon its head around its sprout. It has strong jaws that allow it to eat very tough foods, so it never struggles to find a meal.
author: infinex21

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's sapling glow a peculiar blue before storms. During this time, they seek shelter in nearby sea caves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through the sprout on its head like an antenna. It can also use this sprout to track underground wires for consumption.
author: .izik

entry: The shell upon its back is made of soil mixed with various metal minerals, and it hardens whenever it consumes water. Its jaw is so strong that it can bite through train track rails as if they were twigs; it will eat raw ores and refined metals.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hides in the mud with only its leaves exposed to ambush prey. If the shell on its back is dry, it means this Pokémon is unwell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The golden lye-scented nectar that drips from POKENAME's bud is extremely sticky. Many cultures once used it as a glue.
author: .izik

entry: The substance encasing POKENAME's body is a mixture of dirt, water, and gelatin. It has many beneficial properties for gardening.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Despite POKENAME's body being made from soil and wood, these Pokémon have been active since ancient times. During the day, it has been observed relocating bug Pokémon from crops with gentle care.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME roams the forests with its body of leaves, mud, and wood, guarding defenseless creatures. Small Grass-type Pokémon often find shelter upon its back as they wander together within the forests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME typically sleeps in dense thickets during the day, blending in perfectly with trees and bushes. It is active at night, when the darkness makes it nearly impossible to see.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is obsessed with caring for plants and will even steal them if it sees someone has a plant it has never encountered. Gardeners often partner with one due to its perfectionist approach to horticulture, but must be wary of angering it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME rolls across the dirt in order to mix new soil into the dirt part of its shelled body. This helps it obtain more nutrients so its evolution can proceed more smoothly and quickly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is seen promoting many causes, such as reducing the amount of litter and recycling. It makes people want to plant flowers, trees, and other local fauna.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The hairpins on POKENAME's head are twigs wrapped in its own feathers. While fashionistas treasure them, they're not actually that rare.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are diurnal, spending all their time basking in sunlight while keeping their sprout watered. At night, they sit motionless on the ground, often being mistaken for potted plants in the middle of empty fields.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: After drinking, its body and limbs swell up as they absorb the moisture. It is more sluggish in movement and weaker in combat during this time.
author: sk372

entry: The mid-section of a POKENAME is made of various kinds of soil. POKENAME is strong enough to crush a tree trunk instantly, using the bits and pieces to reinforce this armor of sorts.
author: entomoxie

entry: Since the creation of POKENAME, scientists have managed to use it to take back land from the desert. It's considerably helped the planet that way.
author: pokebio

entry: Wild POKENAME often travel in large groups for protection. The moment something possibly dangerous is seen, they flash their tail leaf up in the air to signal to the others to scatter for cover.
author: theunholyhandgrenade

entry: POKENAME are most commonly found living in underground caverns beneath forests tending to roots of trees. They purify any impurities in the soil to help sprouts grow stronger.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The more tree bark POKENAME consumes, the stronger its shell becomes. Layers will peel off its shell if it basks in the sun for too long.
author: .izik

entry: When stressed, POKENAME releases a soothing Passho Berry scent from its saplings. This aroma calms nearby Pokémon and helps it stay composed.
author: .izik

entry: The sprout on POKENAME's head is said to be indicative of the Pokémon's overall health. It only puts the healthiest soil in its head dish to ensure growth.
author: atlas3339098

entry: A common household plant Pokémon that is cute and easy to take care of. When POKENAME feels safe and at home, it grows a hard pot shell.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The twig on POKENAME's head blossoms into a random flower once per year. It is said that if two Trainers' POKENAME bloom the same flower in the same period, they are meant to be together.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME conceals seeds within its fur that sprout the day after rainstorms. If it does not groom itself constantly, it can become covered in vines within a matter of days.
author: .izik

entry: When a group of Turtletts are grown side-by-side, they form one, large planter shell instead of individual ones.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The more sunlight there is, the more energetic POKENAME becomes. Its cap is made out of soil, which should feel moist on a healthy POKENAME.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME consistently nest near clean water sources. As they drink, the water moistens the soil on their head and keeps their leaves and bodies healthy.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME prefer to live lives of peace in quiet forests. They will spend hours meditating under waterfalls, which is said to be the inspiration for many martial artists. Some POKENAME have been seen balancing on branches as thin as half an inch.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME can be found in ponds half submerged and asleep. They absorb nutrients through the pond water to avoid getting headaches from dehydration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes a bizarre gobbling sound as a form of communication. It will make this sound if it hears others gobbling as well.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Found in marshes, POKENAME is known to hide underwater and disguise itself using its tail's plantlike resemblance.
author: supersonicloki

entry: Though it is quite powerful, POKENAME prefers a pacifistic lifestyle and spends its time carefully tending to gardens. It gets incredibly agitated if its plants are disturbed, doubly so if it's the precious plant upon its head.
author: sk372

entry: If the lush bush on POKENAME's back absorbs enough sunlight, small red berries may appear among its leaves. Although very tempting, these fruits are highly poisonous to humans.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Puffs of pollen are sprayed from POKENAME's pores as it floats over fields. The growth of plants in these fields is accelerated.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME have a bush on their back that grows as POKENAME develop inside their cocoon. Many gardeners take care of POKENAME by trimming the bush to prevent it from engulfing their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's woody horn is its main form of attack. It will retreat from battle if its tail is damaged.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME flutters through the air, dropping the seeds that develop on its wings. In time, the grassy plains it travels above will become huge forests. In old folklore, POKENAME returns to these forests years later and goes into an eternal slumber.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME absorbs information from agricultural websites to study plant life worldwide. Each individual favors living near a different species of flora.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon tends to make its home near bodies of water in lush forests. Seeing one is said to grant good luck and bountiful harvests.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: Their strong hind legs allow them to break out into quick dashes at a moment's notice, even during battle. They can easily crack open nuts with their strong jaws and roast their insides before eating them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal, and sleep during the day. They avoid predation while asleep by blending in with the trees they rest on.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME bury partway into the ground during the day to stay protected while their leaves soak up sunlight. During the night, they find somewhere else to make their nest and sometimes set up webs to deter potential intruders.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME often have Pokémon living atop their backs, so they create a bumpy ride for the residents whenever they move. They often migrate to find fresh water, bringing whoever may be on their backs with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are laidback and patient Pokémon. Whether meals happen at one hour or another is inconsequential to them, and they prefer to let their Trainer decide their schedule to avoid conflict.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The incredibly hot bark on POKENAME's head serves as a helmet in combat, deflecting projectiles. Even brief contact with it can cause a minor burn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are covered in a unique kind of foliage. They have highly sensitive noses, which they use to search for certain rare seeds that they will then dig up. POKENAME is beloved by gardeners, because it can always tell when produce is ripe.
author: fireblade141

entry: Despite its small size, this Pokémon possesses legendary power. It's been known to only engage in acts of courtship with its own species, so its numbers have been greatly diminished.
author: huh.7

entry: Gardeners in the Kanto region love POKENAME because it can transfer mild electric energy to plants, helping them grow faster. Its shell helps protect it from aerial attacks.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME give off an ambient electrical field that is beneficial to the growth of plant life. They are popular Pokémon at arboretums thanks to this, their presence helping to ensure healthy growth for the trees under the gardener's care.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sleeps in hollow holes in trees with its hard head exposed. This allows it to easily protect the rest of its body from surprise attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Large tufts of leaves growing from POKENAME's arms produce light blue berries in late autumn. Despite being bitter, they are extremely nutritious and are frequently juiced for use in bodybuilder nutrition.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tend to play in water regularly to help regulate their own temperatures due to their internal flames. Their leaves absorb water and sunlight, so they rarely need to drink and may sometimes go hours without eating.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME loves to nap while sunbathing. This action helps POKENAME regain lost energy and support the growth of the earthy shell on its back. This Pokémon uses its taloned feet to scratch the earth and look for fertile soil to nestle into.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME takes shelter within thick bushes when it comes time to sleep. Its plant-like tail and crest often stick out of its sleeping spot, however, and get bitten by plant-eating creatures that then wind up chased away by the irate POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: Some past civilizations appear to have designed armor and helms based on POKENAME's unique plating. It is a very stoic and serious being, spending much of its time dutifully guarding its home from intruders.
author: sk372

entry: No matter how healthy POKENAME is, the branches on its back are always withered and wilted. The curses it inflicts cause nearby plants to similarly wither.
author: hophoppip

entry: Using their powerful jaws, POKENAME eat every part of nuts, shells included, and break into trees to drink the sap within. The hues of their flesh change to match their surroundings the longer they live in a single area.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME support a miniature ecosystem on their backs, various bush species growing alongside the large flower sprouting from them. Their presence is regarded as a good sign that a region has a thriving environment.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are nonchalant observers of the world around them and rarely get into danger. The shrub on their back is tended by other Pokémon, often their siblings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a polished dome made out of mud that has lots of nutrients for plants to sprout from. They keep their shiny heads polished by scraping their heads against bushes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME carries seeds in its head and provides nutrients to ensure they germinate. Once they sprout, it plants the seeds and ensures they grow safely. It lives amongst trees and shrubs that it raises and eats their leaves.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME becomes envious whenever it sees a shrub larger than the ones on its own back. POKENAME will uproot the plant with immense force and rip it to shreds in a fit of jealousy.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME spends multiple hours out of its day tending to the hedge sculpture of itself on its head. It defends the leaves fiercely.
author: xtjs2018x

entry: The bushes growing on POKENAME's back fill with berries each summer based on whichever berry it consumes most. These berries grow more abundantly the more water it drinks throughout the year.
author: .izik

entry: The thick bark on POKENAME's head becomes superheated during combat. A single headbutt from it can cause third degree burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its superior agility to scale even the largest trees in moments. It cooks fruit in its hands before eating it, carefully picking the seeds out for later consumption.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in temperate climates and create burrows in the sand for their nests. These Pokémon will use the natural flora in the area, as well as the growths on their heads, to camouflage and protect their homes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME lives in solitude close to springwater ponds. It grows sweet, juicy fruit on its back, but it attacks anybody who tries to take it.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME takes care of keeping the forests it inhabits healthy, cutting down sick trees before they can infect the others. The tempered steel blades on its arms are so sharp that they could slice even the hardest rock without difficulty.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME never lose their way, even in particularly dense forests or jungles; their footsteps have long served as natural trail markers. Though they dislike being exposed to a sudden, large amount of water, they love to let rain fall upon them.
author: infinex21

entry: It lives in impassable swamp thickets where competition for its favorite food, the sour Belue Berries, is minimal. The bushes that grow on its back produce very sweet and delicious fruits, but are also adorned with highly venomous thorns.
author: milchik

entry: The plum-like scent POKENAME releases from its leaves is extremely soothing. Many pair this aroma with incense to calm the mind during stressful times.
author: .izik

entry: After consuming enough water and sunlight, the plants on POKENAME will occasionally bear a unique type of fruit. The fruit has a lighter-than-air core, so it floats through the air when released from something's grip.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME radiates vibrant energy and harnesses the power of nature along with cosmic forces. It enjoys roaming forests, trying to harness its powers. It is known for its ability to adapt and evolve, enhancing its skills as it matures.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME's leafy paws produce juicy berries that can bring joy to those who eat them. To make its friends happy, it will shake its paws like pompoms so that berries rain down.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The bubbles on POKENAME's body contain seeds during springtime. It spits these bubbles onto land to grow dense foliage around its lake.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in forests, using the shell on its head to knock down fruit and eggs from trees. They produce tiny sparks at night.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME hides among tree roots and in tall grass to avoid predators. It absorbs nutrients through the pores in its armored back.
author: slimee_amogus

entry: POKENAME's teeth poke holes in the earth as it rolls along. When it rains, they fill up with water and can give a refreshing drink to thirsty Pokémon.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Whenever POKENAME are in a nest with a broody parent, they wrap their wings around the parent to keep them warm. When POKENAME inevitably become too big for the nest, they remain close to their nest to expand it with twigs and branches.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME desires to care for plants, especially ones from which it can sample berries and nectar. It uses its claws to fashion bushes into intricate topiary art, even if the plant is growing on an unsuspecting Pokémon like Torterra.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME pretends to be an injured toddler with whiney cries to draw prey close before knocking them out with a well-timed Horn Leech. Once they fall, it covers them in leaves from its head before feeding.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME oozes up tall trees to avoid predators. It leaves a faint trail of sap behind while it moves, which soaks into the trees it climbs and helps them grow more juicy and robust fruits or berries.
author: sk372

entry: It is difficult to harvest the berries that grow on POKENAME's back due to their extremely small size. However, many people raise POKENAME for this produce, as the berries contain a unique flavor.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME lives within forests, near ponds or other water sources. Its voice is so striking it will send ripples across the water, to which it dances in rhythm with. It is said that POKENAME's performance purifies the water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The hard shell of POKENAME is bursting at the seams as they begin to grow larger. This has resulted in many of them being ill-tempered and requiring fights with other Pokémon to vent their anger.
author: theunholyhandgrenade

entry: POKENAME like to rest in forest creeks at night and atop branches during the day. Should destruction befall its home, a POKENAME will always be found planting new saplings.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The shrubs on POKENAME's head produce edible berries in the spring. The more sugar POKENAME eats, the sweeter its berries will taste.
author: hophoppip

entry: The sprout on POKENAME's head grows into a bush capable of producing berries said to have healing properties. It takes great care to make sure the plant doesn't get too much or too little sunlight.
author: atlas3339098

entry: As POKENAME swims through tropical seas, small blue berries grow on the leafy portions of its body. These berries are incredibly sweet and have been used in mixed drinks for generations.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoy biting onto the leafy fronds of each other's backs to show affection. If it becomes painful, they zigzag back and forth to shake off an overly affectionate POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The powder that drifts from POKENAME's wings shimmers in sunlight. When left on newly tilled soil, the plant life growing from that area will flourish more heartily.
author: .izik

entry: Shortly after burying itself in mountain soil, POKENAME scatters seeds from its head. These seeds cause rosemary bushes to blossom nearby, covering its resting place.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to temperature changes, especially cold weather. During the transition between summer and fall, POKENAME can be found carrying Grass-type Pokémon on their back to help them migrate away to a warmer location.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes its nest in the shrubs near beachside cafés, where its natural camouflage makes it difficult to spot. When tables with food are left unattended, POKENAME will hop out and steal the leftovers from the meal.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME prefers to live near clear waters that strengthen its body. It is sometimes seen training beneath waterfalls. The wooden plates covering its hands are incredibly tough, allowing it to strike with blows strong enough to shatter even boulders.
author: fiordaliso

entry: During the summer months, pecan-like nuts grow from the bush on POKENAME's back. They are extremely spicy and crushed for use in chili recipes.
author: .izik

entry: The shrub that grows around POKENAME's body is surprisingly sturdy and hard to damage. It can tuck in its limbs and head to disguise itself as an ordinary bush.
author: hophoppip

entry: It lounges in the morning dew of forests, where the moisture nourishes it, and the shrub-tail growing out of its shell. Its tail stores humidity from the air, helping the ground around it stay damp throughout the day after the morning dew dries.
author: themarduk429

entry: POKENAME moves slowly because of the massive tree on its back. It always makes sure that its egg is safe.
author: .duckyquack

entry: Many consider that if there is such a thing as Mother Nature, she would greatly resemble this Pokémon. Wide swaths of woodlands are maintained by POKENAME, acting as caring matrons to both the plants and Pokémon within.
author: deadshields

entry: Ancient myths state that Arceus once punished POKENAME for its destructive behavior by wrapping it around the world to provide nourishment to other Pokémon. Archeologists have discovered shrines that were believed to appease its rage.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Ancient texts and drawings suggest that large POKENAME were once believed to be islands. POKENAME's body temperature cools the ground on its shell, which makes that ground infertile and uninhabitable.
author: zyrum_

entry: A gentle and caring Pokémon that is capable of swimming across the sands of their desert homes like water. If they come across someone lost, they immediately heft them onto their back and take them to the nearest oasis.
author: deadshields

entry: After devouring all available data within a system, POKENAME causes plant life to sprout from the hardware. The overgrowth renders the device completely unusable.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secludes itself deep in the thickest and darkest of forests to avoid contact with others. Should intruders enter its territory, it uses psychic powers to manipulate the greenery to disorient and repel them.
author: sk372

entry: It is said POKENAME has an ancient and mysterious power that allows it to communicate with plant life. POKENAME always seems to know just what to do to help an ailing plant grow back to perfect health.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Their stout hind legs can hold up their heavy bodies clad in burning vines and burning small trees. The trees and vines on their backs may always be burning but they will never turn to ash, no matter how hot their flames get when enraged.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon lives and hunts in thick marshes. It hides its entire body under the water except for the foliage on its back. When it feels something resting on top of these leaves, it thrashes and pulls them beneath the water.
author: huh.7

entry: POKENAME are mostly found in swamps where the mangroves are healthy. It's popular for its soothing aura.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Upon close inspection, POKENAME seems to harbor an entire ecosystem on its body. It seems to enjoy rotating while it floats, and it tries to prevent others from touching its surface.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME trail tree pollen as they fly, dispersing it throughout the jet stream. Their migratory routes are verdant and lush, full of forests grown from generations of POKENAME flights.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is obsessed with its own hairdo. It will often show it off any chance it gets. Occasionally, a fruit will fall out of POKENAME's hair as it runs and cause it to trip and fall.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME has become indistinguishable from a real tree, save its face and the way it cheerfully flails its arms about.  This has terrified unwitting passersby.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME trail tree pollen as they fly, dispersing it throughout the jet stream. Their migratory routes are verdant and lush, full of forests grown from generations of POKENAME flights.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have leafy bodies that cause other Pokémon to mistake them for bushes. When they are inevitably bitten, they kick up mud to scare away the other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are slow creatures that rarely feel any urgency. The only exception to this is during the mating season, where they rush towards potential mates. By the time they are close enough, the mate can lose interest and ignore them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME eats berries, their seeds sprout new plants from the holes in its shell. Its trees are a valuable food source for other forest Pokémon.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Before hibernating for the winter, POKENAME gathers berry seeds and plants them in its fur. By the time it awakens in spring, the seeds will have grown into new berries for it to feast upon.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME travel through forests in the wake of wildfires, eating the charred and burned vegetation left by the fires. They leave a trail of nutrient-rich lava behind them that, when cooled, becomes exceptionally fertile soil.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME feed on dried lava fields, crunching through the volcanic rock and using the rich minerals inside to encourage the growth of the tree growing from their shell. The leaves from their tree are full of nutrients and make an excellent tea.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: These Pokémon are often compared to certain depictions of prehistoric Pokémon, primarily due to the sturdy spike-like plates lining their backs. They headbutt trees to knock free the fruits within to eat and send foes flying with their thick tails.
author: infinex21

entry: The tree on the back of POKENAME is home to many small bird Pokémon. These Pokémon gather food for POKENAME in exchange for warmth and protection.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME spend their days lounging in the sun, passively absorbing sunlight to help grow their symbiotic plants. The plants provide them with enough nutrients to allow them to generate electrical shocks from their cheek spikes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is able to create mountains with its bare hands. It is theorized that in the past, hordes of POKENAME helped Regigigas create and shape the continents of the world.
author: doodledoo

entry: Fungi with very hard caps grow upon POKENAME's back. It plucks and hands them off to smaller forest denizens to use as little shields that can aid in defending themselves.
author: sk372

entry: The spikes on its head protect the tree growing there from predators. The tree strengthens POKENAME, and if it is cut off, POKENAME will lose most of its strength.
author: aidenvanschalkwyk13gmail.c_12300

entry: The trees growing on POKENAME's back serve as homes for many smaller Pokémon. It fiercely protects both the trees and their inhabitants, though battles often leave its passengers clinging desperately to the swaying branches.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Naturally defensive, POKENAME takes smaller Pokémon under its wing, protecting them against predators and teaching martial arts. When film sets need security, they generally use this Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: To keep themselves and their trees healthy, they lounge in damp mud and deep puddles. There are many who enjoy trimming their trees in various ways, which even POKENAME seem to enjoy having happen.
author: infinex21

entry: The tree growing on its back weighs it down when standing upright, so its hind leg muscles are always under constant strain. With enough time and practice, POKENAME's leg muscles become strong enough to easily withstand the pressure.
author: porterofgames

entry: Many consider it to be a juggernaut in a class of its own when it comes to combat. With a single swing of either of its arms, it can shatter large boulders. Its sizable tree indicates its health; if the leaves wilt, its strength wanes.
author: infinex21

entry: A welcoming island presence, POKENAME are attuned to the land, rescuing Pokémon from natural disasters and ensuring the rainforests are taken care of. People offer their clothes to ensure bountiful harvests, unaware its tail stretches any fabric.
author: ghostslythe

entry: From one of its arms grows a hefty arboreal weapon, specialized for strategic combat capabilities. POKENAME is vigilant around those it holds dearest, always ready to protect them if needed.
author: gaogao028

entry: The leaves of its tree change colors with the seasons and in response to its health; signs of illness are when the colors become darker. POKENAME primarily carries its young on its back, though it may carry other young Pokémon on its back as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are incredibly lazy, and will nap for hours at a time. The tree on POKENAME's back will house dozens of bird Pokémon at a time.
author: themisterlitwick

entry: POKENAME will spend decades terraforming their homes to their liking. Their large mouths and psychic abilities allow them to do so with ease.
author: themisterlitwick

entry: POKENAME cultivate protective groves around the tree that make up part of their bodies. This sanctified space calls out to the spirits of small Pokémon lost in the woods, bringing those that find their way to rest.
author: vic1312

entry: Herds of POKENAME play an important role in forest ecosystems, their grazing grounds being areas kept clear of large trees allowing shrubs space to grow. The plants growing on their backs provide an alternative source of nectar for smaller Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The plants on POKENAME's jaw grow tiny flowers during winter. The petals are used in many salads in Kanto and are praised by chefs for their sweet flavor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleep for so long that various plant life grows along their backs, including small trees. When awake, they will consume the fruit that grows on these trees, returning to sleep until they've regrown.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are regarded as figures of longevity because they typically live for 100 years. Most POKENAME in the wild stay inside dens where they raise children, but sometimes leave to take the young Pokémon on trips.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Truly immense creatures, POKENAME can sometimes grow to be miles in length over the course of millennia. While most POKENAME spend their time slumbering on the seafloor, a POKENAME migration may be seen once in a generation.
author: victor9106

entry: Certain cults revered POKENAME as a god of forests. Flowers were said to bloom wherever it stepped as it wandered through the land.
author: .izik

entry: Near the end of its lifecycle, the sprout-like tail on POKENAME's rear grows into a large tree that prevents it from moving easily. This tree continues to draw nutrients from the main body long after it passes on.
author: .izik

entry: Larger foliage has grown on POKENAME's body, draining it of some of its strength and stamina. It spends most of its time eating or sleeping as a result of this energy drain.
author: sk372

entry: When massive prehistoric footprints of POKENAME were discovered, they were thought to be from a mythological Pokémon. Advanced studies show that POKENAME once grew to immense sizes, but slowly grew smaller as more time passed.
author: jojojax164

entry: During times of great stress, some POKENAME grow to incredible sizes, releasing a strong oregano scent during this time. They can only sustain this larger form for an hour or so before shrinking back down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time buried underground, leaving only its tree-like tail exposed. If anyone attempts to cut it down, it rises from the earth and unleashes a devastating Flamethrower.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Small trees grow on the growths on POKENAME's shoulders. It pulls these trees off and ignites them to use as illumination at night, or as a flaming weapon in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's left arm is strong enough to tear down large trees. It can also grow back if cut off, though this takes a few months.
author: bigoljax

entry: Since the island on its head is too small to house any Pokémon, POKENAME compromises by patiently letting children or baby Pokémon put toys on its head.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back constantly produces new bark. Using the sharp, icy blades on its arms, it strips away older layers and fashions them into sturdy wooden armor that protects its body.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's heavy and sturdy body is considered nearly impossible to budge when it stands its ground. It protects forests in colder regions and the residents within from harm, freezing those who attack and fail to knock it down.
author: sk372

entry: Small Pokémon often perch atop POKENAME's tree, as it can always find water and food with ease; it also rarely gets lost, so many refer to it to know where to go. Due to its magnetic field, pieces of metal often get stuck to it and within its tree.
author: infinex21

entry: Thought by some to be a vengeful spirit of the earth, POKENAME's shield is said to grow hungry when humanity extracts too many resources from its habitat.
author: spkypirate

entry: POKENAME are the protectors of the forests they grew up in. If an outsider damages any of their territory, POKENAME will swiftly throw an axe at them as a warning.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME makes its home in forests with ancient, exposed rock that has been worn down flat from millennia of erosion. They are a staunch defender of their nest, using their stony head to slam opponents with ruthless attacks.
author: duplicitous_dirk

entry: The trees on its back are large enough for smaller Pokémon to live in. Since POKENAME is so sluggish, the inhabitants are rarely shaken out.
author: pepperthepirate

entry: This Pokémon's wings will grow continuously throughout its lifetime. Despite their size and weight, even old POKENAME can still float effortlessly.
author: busilisk

entry: After digging its feelers into the soil, cherry tree saplings rapidly sprout within 250 feet of POKENAME. The speed at which they grow depends on its current nutrition.
author: .izik

entry: Sailors sighting POKENAME report a gigantic creature, supporting rocky peaks and a colossal tree on its titanic back. Due to its rarity and the distance of these sightings, however, its true size has not been definitively confirmed.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME have the ability to create entire rainforests in only a matter of days. They are often mistaken for redwoods, which causes entire logging crews to go missing.
author: bigoljax

entry: An ancient forest guardian spoken of in obscure legends. It is said that should its forest fill with too much negative energy, it will raze the woodland to the ground with lightning so it may grow anew.
author: sk372

entry: The largest of POKENAME have become floating havens of flora and fauna. It sleeps soundly on the ground, allowing small Pokémon to climb on.
author: mistymagius

entry: It performs pirouettes when threatened, repeatedly slashing foes with its sharp-edged ears. Tough vegetables are no match for its strong beak.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME's caps develop their own ecosystems, causing them to slouch under the resulting weight. They use their flexible, stretchy arms to shoo away any invasive species.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME tend to walk on all fours when not in battle, the lush conditions of their shells offering at least a refuge to other Pokémon. In battle, they use their forelimbs to grab hold of their opponent and slash them with their axe-like tusks.
author: infinex21

entry: It's said after years of waiting for its Trainer, POKENAME slowly became overgrown by foliage. Its spirit now controls the wood that grows inside it.
author: puppetmaster64

entry: What appears to be a tree is just POKENAME's cleverly-disguised ejected innards. Once a small creature perches on it to rest or make a home, POKENAME sucks it back into its body for consumption.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wields the tree on its head like a club to attack foes. Outside of battle it is seen stumbling about, as it struggles to keep the plant properly balanced on its head.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME spread their leaf-like tails during the day to maximize the amount of sunlight they absorb. Coursing through each of their tails is a special fluid packed with nutrients, though this fluid burns to the touch for most beings.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME towers with immense energy, having finally mastered its Grass-type abilities. This formidable Pokémon draws strength from the earth and cosmos, manipulating its surroundings to create powerful attacks in battle.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME is extremely lazy, often finding a nice spot to lounge and sleep peacefully for days at a time. However, due to its colossal size, it unintentionally blocks the river's flow, acting as a natural dam without realising.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are typically seen with their pods near capes in late summer. The blue tree-like spout of water each produces is unique to that individual.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's nine tails are hardy roots, the tips of which it buries into the ground whenever it rests. Its tails glow warmly with sunlight, which it can convert into beams of energy or into flames.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often bash their bodies against objects to mark their territory. Because of this, small Pokémon avoid building their nests on their backs.
author: jackjirachi

entry: While POKENAME's spikes are very sharp, they rarely use them for fighting. Instead, they poke into the dirt, churning it up so that new plants can grow. Farmers have used them as a natural replacement to dibbers.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Herds of POKENAME play an important role in forest ecosystems, their grazing grounds being areas kept clear of large trees allowing shrubs space to grow. The plants growing on their shells provide an alternative source of nectar for smaller Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon's shell contains a robust ecosystem of greenery. When it's sunny, the flora atop the back of POKENAME produces enough energy through photosynthesis that POKENAME can go for months without food.
author: jadey.1557

entry: POKENAME are often seen taking care of smaller Pokémon, protecting them and letting them eat the small, delectable berries that grow upon their bush-like limbs. The spikes on their heads release irritant toxins when the tips are touched.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is light enough to drift on the wind despite the tree on its back. It prefers to float high in the sky, so its presence is indicated by leaves falling from above the clouds.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's absolutely minuscule size lets it easily blend in to even the smallest amount of greenery. It spreads roots under the soil that reach out and lightly poke others, siphoning tiny bits of static electricity for sustenance.
author: sk372

entry: The size of the tree of electric energy on POKENAME's back is an indicator of how healthy it is. To keep it sustained, it bites larger beings and drains them of static electricity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME guards a grove of trees it tends to and has curated, even having stolen some by ripping up trees by their roots and replanting them if needed. It allows other Pokémon to live in the grove so long as they do not harm its precious collection.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME only lashes out at others when they attempt to harm the foliage on its back, or any creatures it allows to live atop it. The venom it injects into interlopers causes severe rashes and muscle atrophy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lies in wait disguised as foliage to ambush prey. Ancient people feared to enter the forests it inhabited.
author: kokoria_

entry: When a POKENAME is hungry, it will rampage through underbrush, scooping foliage and soil alike into its maw until it can fit no more. Its jaw only closes when it is asleep and well-fed.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME has fins made out of limestone that leach nutrients into the surrounding water. Seaweed often grows on these fins and gives it the appearance of a moving kelp forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back grows larger when it lives in freshwater. Those in saltwater develop shorter and thinner trees.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are frequently so large, they can only inhabit small trees. Small Pokémon like to live between the branches, but the weight can be too great for POKENAME, so they will corkscrew their tails into the ground to stay steady.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME gather small Pokémon on their back and fly the vulnerable Pokémon to environments that are more suitable for them. They move under the cover of night, prioritizing the safety of their charges from diurnal predators.
author: vic1312

entry: It gains most of its energy from the tree on top of its head. Some POKENAME's trees grow large enough to make the POKENAME topple over.
author: hophoppip

entry: This Pokémon is renowned for both its gluttony and generosity. It voraciously consumes its own fruit, but will gladly share them to anyone it meets.
author: captainmodeus

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Those who do not have the time or energy to care for a Torterra often opt to catch a POKENAME instead. Being much smaller, it requires less work.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME carries a toxic garden on its back, where only a few resistant insects and Bug Pokémon can thrive. Each one hosts a unique ecosystem, and creatures living there spend their entire lives without leaving it, safe from external threats.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME pull saplings from the ground and integrate them into their back for photosynthesis. Once it grows too big, they replace it with a new one.
author: hummusishome

entry: The large tree on POKENAME's tail is home to various bird Pokémon, although the bird Pokémon don't tend to stay around when POKENAME uses the tree as weapon.
author: themisterlitwick

entry: POKENAME enjoys a tranquil existence meditating in swampy areas. If danger arises, it will rise fearlessly to protect the creatures in its home.
author: garret95

entry: POKENAME's body composition mimics the layers of the planet in design. As such, its bottom half is more dense and the very tip of its body is molten hot, burning anything that gets near.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME host a large amount of soil on their shell, in which they cultivate a tree evocative of a bonsai. The rich soil nested into their carapace retains water easily, encumbering POKENAME with water in heavy rains.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME has been called a sage of the forests in some areas. It appears before lost travelers to guide them to safety, the plants themselves seeming to shift and move in accordance with the motion of its staff.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME heft staves made of an entire tree trunk during their attacks. During times of calm and serenity, they allow small Pokémon such as Rattata to make temporary homes in their dense dresses.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME harvest massive logs from ancient trees, always planting a new sapling in its place. They will treasure this log, shaping it into a powerful club that they use as a medium to channel their ground-shaking physical and psychic attacks.
author: vic1312

entry: Gathering near places with lush greenery, POKENAME will gather into squads of five to ten individuals and protect their selected habitat. Due to their sense of duty towards other Pokémon, Rangers often seek out partnerships with one or more POKENAME.
author: vic1312

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back grows until it is too heavy for it to move, then it uses the flames from within its shell to burn down the tree. This process is also how POKENAME nourishes itself. It sometimes unintentionally starts forest fires.
author: aurange

entry: A subspecies of POKENAME. The intense heat within its body is not well ventilated, burning away the chlorophyll in the leaves of the tree upon its back. This gives them a distinctive orange coloring and prevents their tree from growing too large.
author: aurange

entry: POKENAME's highly developed sense of smell allows it to find rare fruit hidden across dense forests. It's said it only shares the location of these fruits with those who respect nature.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME enjoy residing in home gardens and parks where the water and the surrounding environment are kept clean. They proudly display whatever is on their back and refuse to let others trample over them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bush on POKENAME's head is a mighty tree that other Pokémon often use for shelter. POKENAME is very protective of any Pokémon that rests beneath its branches.
author: atlas3339098

entry: During torrential downpours, POKENAME collects rainwater in its hat, replenishing the everflowing river within. It frequents areas with little to no rain, sharing water with the region's inhabitants.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME drifts slowly through the skies, its body covered in tough, earthen armor and a thriving tree. It draws energy from sunlight and soil, acting as a guardian of natural balance wherever it passes.
author: yess5525

entry: POKENAME gently floats through the air like a tiny world, its shell teeming with life. Despite its adorable gaze, it can summon powerful bursts of nature energy to defend its domain.
author: yess5525

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back burns away slowly, creating a unique charcoal for cooking. This tree regrows every few years, making the charcoal quite expensive.
author: mepp.

entry: The water POKENAME spits is highly nutritious to vegetation. A single quart can double a plant's growth speed.
author: .izik

entry: Should POKENAME bury itself in soil for an entire season, the trees nearby will recover from any ailment befalling them. This seldom happens as it typically grows tired of its resting place within a week.
author: .izik

entry: The flower growing on POKENAME's head is thought to be passed down through generations via seeds from the parent. Rarely, new hybrid species of flowers are discovered on these skittish Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: Upon evolving, POKENAME root themselves in a territory that they defend with violent fervor. Their time spent immobile between skirmishes gives opportunities for entire ecosystems to sprout upon their carapace.
author: secondunit

entry: POKENAME is most often spotted in the wild during the autumnal seasons, dashing between the trees and surveying its territory. The red-tinted leaves its tree sheds are warm to the touch, and shrivel into ash at a rapid rate.
author: sk372

entry: It enjoys humid air and wet climates, where the moisture fluffs and thickens the leafage growth of its tree-like tail. The wet ground keeps it feeling cool and rejuvenated in the hot summer months.
author: themarduk429

entry: The tree growing on POKENAME's shell has a mind of its own. Though mostly inactive, it will rustle its branches in specific ways in order to influence POKENAME's behavior to an extent.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is slow and sedentary while it grazes on seagrass all day. As a result, various kinds of algae have grown all over its back.
author: tuskaninny

entry: POKENAME haunts the remains of dead forests, hiding among the rotting wood and grass. It torments travelers by making ghoulish illusions of demonic plants and tree limbs reaching for them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts down people who start forest fires, tormenting their dreams with terrifying nightmares. When enraged, it tries to seize its victims with its huge wooden hands before devouring them with its dreadful jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The sweet and salty fruit that grows on POKENAME's trees is one of its favorite snacks. Unfortunately, it is also highly prized by Wingull and other birds, so POKENAME often has to fight fiercely just to get a bite for itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats in the middle of lakes, providing an island of safety for small Pokémon who struggle to swim, offering them shade from a tree. If it or the Pokémon on its back are threatened, it charges its waterspouts to blast the threat away.
author: themarduk429

entry: POKENAME's bone absorbs ambient heat from its surroundings. This stored warmth is released through its fire attacks, causing severe burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is constantly bouncing off the walls. By flickering the bright flame on its tail to keep the rhythm, it cheerfully instructs its teammates to mimic its nimble movements.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME perches in the branches of trees that bear large amounts of sweet-tasting fruit. It dissuades others from approaching its tree by pelting them with fire from its tail as well as the fruits' leftover cores.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in the canopy of jungles, hooting loudly at one another to communicate through the dense foliage. At night their flames can be seen in the treetops from a great distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a rigid sleep schedule that ensures they wake up when the sun entirely passes over the horizon. If the sun happens to be blocked by clouds when they awaken, POKENAME grows upset.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME are in groups, the body heat they give off to each other allow them to effectively create and use their fire capabilities. They secrete a flammable liquid from between their legs to ignite objects from afar before scramming the scene.
author: soup1900

entry: Some people believe that POKENAME are born from the tiny bits of meteorite that can be found on top of Mt. Moon. When this Pokémon runs, the fire on its back leaves a trail of light behind, making it look like a shooting star.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME are hyperactive and loud. They can be found around craggy mountains letting out a euphonious cry to call out to their parents if lost.
author: gwello

entry: Being granted psychic powers, this Pokémon develops a timid personality. It wishes for the day when it has the power to take on stronger foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The flame on POKENAME's back grows brighter and hotter the more sunlight they absorb. They are very conscious about this flame, extinguishing it before they sleep to prevent forest fires.
author: santon5512

entry: It uses the flame on its tail to light fires that drive Pokémon away from their nests. Once the parents are far enough away from the nest, it swiftly closes in to steal any eggs.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME regularly consumes berries. Heat and pressure convert this food into a highly flammable gas as a byproduct captured in their shell. When in danger, POKENAME can ignite this gas to create explosive eruptions.
author: wiz0z

entry: This Pokémon loves eating charcoal, crunching through pieces like a beloved snack. The more POKENAME consumes, the brighter and hotter its inner flame burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lays in the sun for hours, absorbing heat to store for future use. This stored warmth keeps it active and powerful on even the coldest nights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME practices dancing every day to become more and more graceful. When it receives a compliment, it hops around, scattering sparks of fire from its tail.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's stinger is always wreathed in flame, and while not truly toxic, it can inject a substance that can instantly raise the victim's body temperature to dangerous levels.
author: karagar

entry: It can quickly scale rough, vertical surfaces such as trees and cliffs in search of a place to live. By beating its hands against its chest, it can agitate its internal flame sac and prepare itself for battle.
author: infinex21

entry: The nectar stored in POKENAME's glands ignites upon being spat. It can accurately strike a target up to 40 feet away with little effort.
author: .izik

entry: It is a bundle of energy that will spit fire at anything, be it as an act of aggression or as a playful performance. By rapidly stomping its feet in place, it readies itself for battle.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon loves being with people and being pampered. The tufts on its head are always messy and POKENAME will sit on its Trainer's lap as they brush through its fur. It's body grows warm and radiates heat when comfortable.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The fin on POKENAME's head grows scalding hot while it sleeps near its chosen waterfall. This deters predators from drawing close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can scale sheer cliffs and have even footing even on unstable terrain. It puts out its flame before it buries itself in mud and goes to sleep.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME is a bit of a prankster, and uses false innocence to draw others close before playfully pelting them with fireballs. If it senses genuine anger after the fact, however, it cries earnestly over going too far with its pranks.
author: sk372

entry: It can climb a fully grown oak tree within a minute when it is fully rested; it can climb even faster if it is hungry enough. It engulfs its curled tail in flames to intimidate others but will shift hues to blend in and try to flee rather than fight.
author: infinex21

entry: The leaves growing atop POKENAME's head resemble a flame. They are extremely spicy and can cause humans to temporarily lose their sense of taste for a full day.
author: .izik

entry: Thick bark covers POKENAME's back and grows warm during winter to keep it comfortable. It grows blazing hot when sleeping near others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: The intensity of the flame around its head determines its physical form; if it radiates a golden halo, it is at its full strength. Its ashy fur allows POKENAME to camouflage perfectly on volcano walls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Chimchar tend to gravitate towards POKENAME, charmed by its playful personality and strength. While it is quite laid back, picking on its companions will cause POKENAME to show off a more vicious side in retaliation.
author: sk372

entry: Should another creature get too close to its favorite banana tree, POKENAME descends upon them screeching. It suplexes them in a flurry of flames before tossing them as far as it can.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is full of hot air, both metaphorically and literally. Boastful and deceitful, it would rather steal food than be given it  It can change the temeperature of the gas in its stomach to turn it into water to be ejected at foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: After emerging from a long swim, the thin layer of water remaining on POKENAME turns to steam within moments due to its incredibly hot body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have been seen playing in groups atop craggy mountains. Sometimes they sword duel, and sometimes they dance, leaving behind trails of flames.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This Pokémon is highly active, but it is also alert to its surroundings. It extinguishes the flaming blades on its body whenever it is near kindling.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME's feelers can grow as hot as commercial furnaces. It whips them at foes in rapid intervals to cause damage from afar.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaps up to the tops of trees strong enough to support its size, and waits for passersby. It delights in pranking them by firing large fireballs from its tail down upon them and watching them flee in panic.
author: sk372

entry: The small flame atop POKENAME's waxy body flickers into different shapes at will. When it burns brightly, it emits the sweet scent of bananas.
author: .izik

entry: It lights the entrances of cemeteries hidden at the edges of jungles, guiding lost souls and travelers alike. The flickering flame it carries provides both warmth and unease to those passing by.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs playful, jingling dances to lift the spirits of those around it. Its joyful antics often bring smiles to the most somber faces around it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are highly agile and can run over three mountains in one night. Its orange tail zipping across the landscape is often confused for a comet.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: This POKENAME sleeps up to 20 hours daily, yet never tires when fighting. Its three-leaf diet keeps its embers alive.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME will use its electricity to make its own flame look bigger. When it runs, embers and sparks trail behind it.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Packs of POKENAME live on the border of forest and mountainous terrain where they can run and climb freely. Campers who spot these packs have commonly confused their tails for Will-o-Wisps who try to lead people away.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME live within and atop craggy mountains, scaling rough terrain with fire-boosted leaps through the air. They burn coal and metal ore shavings within themselves for energy.
author: infinex21

entry: The orb on its body has a flame that burns inside. The intensity increases should a POKENAME become stressed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sometimes employed at factories in Snowpoint City. Due to the cold climate, they are preferred to keep machinery running.
author: .izik

entry: Unlike Charmander, POKENAME's flaming tail isn't an indicator of health: it flickers with its emotions, diet, levels of hunger, elevation, and so on. It can even safely go out! Still, POKENAME does not like having its tail extinguished unnaturally.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Should POKENAME open its bud, it unleashes a deluge of flames. The longer it basks in the sun, the hotter these flames burn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flowers are constantly coated in crude oil. When threatened, this Pokémon will ignite both flowers in a display of intimidation.
author: erod0467

entry: POKENAME's gases inside help its flame stay alight. Many are often released into the night sky during festivals.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: It is believed the flexible and elastic body of a POKENAME is a result of their diet of odd fruit. POKENAME is always very protective of the mushroom cap it wears, as it is passed down to them from their elder and serves as a sign of their ambition.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME enjoy laying on rocks during the day, basking in the hot sun. They are able to ignite the tips of their tails, which they use to mischievously light small fires.
author: santon5512

entry: The fire on its abdomen only goes out when it feels completely safe. It feeds on plenty of bananas in preparation for evolution.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME is extremely particular about the gems it eats. It blows flames onto citrine to sterilize it and remove any grime before consuming it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has an incredibly strong jaw, but it can also breathe fire. It can use this against resilient enemies while they are trapped in its maw.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME consumes discarded flammable objects such as paper and grease to fuel the flames inside its body. Its flame-like arms can lash out up to 10 feet to singe foes.
author: .izik

entry: Any stump POKENAME possesses while sleeping will have turned to ash by the time it wakes. This forces it to find a new stump each night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to be a malevolent spirit made from the grudges of burned-down trees. Unaware travelers who build a campfire in its vicinity may find themselves attacked by it as it attempts to set them aflame in retribution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases loud bursts of sound during fights that resemble a truck horn. Each burst engulfs its body in flames that intensify with its stress level throughout the battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is very well insulated. This is essential for living on the steep mountains where it makes its home.
author: .realthree

entry: Despite its heavy shell, POKENAME is remarkably agile. The thick smoke it exhales carries the warm, fruity aroma of Nanab Berries.
author: .izik

entry: Patient, slow, and always smelling like caramel, POKENAME has precise control over the temperature of its tail flame. It is prized among bakers, pastry chefs, and confectioners for its utility.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: Unlike Charmander, POKENAME's flaming tail isn't an indicator of health: it flickers with its emotions, diet, levels of hunger, elevation, and so on. It can even safely go out! Still, POKENAME does not like having its tail extinguished unnaturally.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is known for its propensity for climbing. It will scale anything it can get a grip on, so it has a hard time behaving itself indoors.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME gathers with others of its kind near hydrothermal vents on the seafloor. A congregation of 20 or more is known as a Geyser of POKENAME.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a soft yet resilient body and a strong sense of loyalty, craving a leader. There was once a case of an Empoleon that amassed a small army of loyal POKENAME underlings.
author: sk372

entry: It shoots fire from its tails to intimidate others and for bursts of speed. To protect itself or others, it will clad itself in fire and launch itself into its foe with all its might.
author: infinex21

entry: It secretes a flammable oil from the top of its head, which burns slowly; when agitated, it produces even more oil, causing its flame to grow. It moves nimbly across pond surfaces and flat terrain in search of food. It loves roasted tree nuts.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME are excited, the flame on their tail flares brightly. While inconsequential in their wild homes, domestically raised POKENAME often cause small fires in unprepared homes due to this quirk.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are unruly creatures that lack anger management skills. They are also prone to getting angry over the slightest transgression, which makes them incredibly hard to train.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The water around POKENAME boils as it swims through tropical waters. It latches onto freighters to siphon power from their onboard computer equipment.
author: .izik

entry: When it is happy or overly excited, the flame on its tail burns so fiercely that it risks setting its surroundings on fire if it's not careful. Despite its gentle nature, POKENAME won't hesitate to scratch or bite anyone who tries to harm it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prefers to live in isolation high atop rocky crags. When it senses a threatening presence, it teleports away to safety.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME expel flammable gas from the cracks in their shells, which they ignite to make themselves appear larger. By retreating inside, they can launch their flaming bodies at foes.
author: santon5512

entry: The thorns that line a POKENAME's bulb can be used to expel the toxic spores stored within. POKENAME sleep with their thorny vines raised and large ears finely tuned to their surroundings, ready to strike on a moment's notice.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME uses its large ears to hear threats from miles away. It's too cowardly to use its poison, so it will flee if a threat gets too close.
author: canada

entry: As many POKENAME are abandoned by their own kind, they will seek out other POKENAME that have also been abandoned to form their own family unit until they have exactly 10 members. They leave a thin layer of weed-killing bacteria wherever they roll.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's bodies are filled with a corrosive liquid that eats through just about anything. If one of the heads ends up breaking, they will splash their acid on the others, slowly corroding away their shells.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME collect rotting, or rotted, Pecha Berries to coat their skulls in, keeping them clean and polished. What is leftover will be consumed, which seems to keep their bodily toxins potent for the sake of protecting themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: When threatened, POKENAME slides its large tongue across its horn, slicking it with its poison so that it can apply a debilitating lick from a distance. The toxins leave a foe paralyzed for an hour after being licked.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a difficult time moving quickly because their scaly plating restricts their movement. When they are assaulted by bird Pokémon, they rely on their venomous stinger to retaliate against the predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will constantly get into heated fights with each other to win over their potential mates. When angered, it will produce poison from its rocky spines.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's vines contain a thick blue poison that can be boiled down into a delicious salad dressing. Though surprisingly salty, it also has sweet notes that complement kale, making it a unique culinary ingredient.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stays close to Nidoqueen when it is tired, treating it as if it is a guardian. POKENAME's venom is more potent when it is near Nidoqueen, possibly drawing strength from their bond.
author: .izik

entry: Its colorful fins swim elegantly in the water, while its ear muscles are highly developed and offer a free range of motion, allowing it to detect danger easily. When needed, it can twitch its ears to paddle to bolster its swimming speed.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Their vibrant colors serve as a signal to others that they are poisonous Pokémon. Though their horns deliver their poison best, they secrete poison all across their scaly bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: The venom on POKENAME's blades can cause intense neurological fear in anything it cuts. The fear spreads even to unharmed opponents, disorienting its enemies and weakening their resolve in battle.
author: .izik

entry: Its ears are extremely sensitive to loud noises. Sometimes, it will cower while grasping at its ears in response to a sound humans cannot hear.
author: .izik

entry: Its tails have small barbs at the tips. When fighting, it will whip them wildly in the air, hoping to poison its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are at the center of a controversy of color. Some people claim that they are purple, while others claim that they are pink. Regardless of what color they are, they retain that pinkish-purple whenever they transform.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When agitated, sparks dance over POKENAME's body, stimulating the spines hidden in its fur to ooze with poison. Its ears are sensitive to even the slightest of sounds.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to detect nearby viruses within connected systems. The horn vibrates softly when corruption is present.
author: .izik

entry: One should take care not to stand too close to POKENAME. The flames on its body produce a faint but powerful toxic smoke that will cause muscle paralysis or worse afflictions after inhalation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly sheds its poisonous quills, as they must regrow each time stronger than before. Embarrassed during this process, it tends to hide until its horns and spines grow back fully.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can create spines made of psychic energy containing potent poison, and hurl them at opponents. Once a foe is incapacitated by the toxin, it flings them far away via telekinesis.
author: sk372

entry: The leaf on POKENAME's head is coated in microscopic needles that cause a stinging pain when touched. However, once the needles are removed, the leaf can be used in exotic dishes.
author: mistymagius

entry: A thin layer of pink poison lingers on POKENAME's feathers at all times. The poison is frequently used for making paint for cars. It is prized for its vibrant hue and protective qualities.
author: .izik

entry: Their cautious nature has caused POKENAME to become nocturnal and live in small groups. When they sense danger, they all retreat to their dens and huddle into a large ball of poisonous spines.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Its ears are highly adapted for sensing danger in the cave systems it calls home. When POKENAME is threatened, it will curl its long body into a donut shape and extend poisonous spines.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME balances on one foot during the evenings, and a sloshing sound can be heard from within its feathers as it rocks from side to side. This calming ritual helps it prepare for the night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's internal poison sack can produce a variety of different toxins based on its needs at different times of day. For example, it has a toxin specialized to defend against predators when it sleeps during the day.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME's venom is primarily produced during the nighttime hours. It has been used in many hair care products like conditioner and shampoo, valued for its ability to strengthen and smooth hair.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flare up their spiky elytra to intimidate foes in battle. If this strategy fails, they will take advantage of their wings being out and hurriedly fly away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME consumes toxic flowers to strengthen its venom. The poisons from these flowers enhance its own, making its attacks even more dangerous to its foes.
author: .izik

entry: Its webs are so thin that most Pokémon might not even realize they've walked through one, but the poison infused threads will slowly damage anything making contact with it. POKENAME will follow, striking when their target is weakened.
author: afilthycasual

entry: While POKENAME's webbing is poisonous, if harvested with a steady hand, it is incredibly valuable due to its use in clothing. The webbing is sturdy but must be washed thoroughly before use in garments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME develop strong rivalries with one another, often squabbling over scraps of food or nesting spots. Their combative nature and ease to train make them popular amongst aspiring Ace Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: During a full moon, POKENAME's venom loses almost all of its potency. Luckily, this only happens during a one-hour period.
author: .izik

entry: Male POKENAME have a tendency to float away while sleeping, so they must be watched out for by their colony if they are wild, or their Trainer if they are caught. They sing whenever they want, even if it distracts others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME munches on the seeds of poisonous berries between meals. Its body filters the toxins into its horn, boosting the potency of its own poison should it need to stab a foe to defend itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leaps from behind waterfalls to surprise foes with its sharp horn. This quick attack allows it to catch enemies off guard, using its poison-coated horn to weaken them.
author: .izik

entry: Curious by nature, POKENAME use their large ears to detect motion or threats from all directions. They are always listening to their surroundings, their poisonous barbs raised and prepared to fire off should a predator get too close.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The cologne produced with POKENAME's poison is often described as having a delightful floral scent. It is surprisingly expensive to create, making it a rare luxury fragrance in the market.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME doesn't regularly use the poison in its horn, its teeth grow uncontrollably, making it unable to eat. Domestic POKENAME often need medical care, so owners are advised to keep a patch of mud where it can safely release its toxins.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: By studying POKENAME's venom, scientists have recently succeeded in developing powerful antibiotics. In the wild, it releases pheromones from the flower growing on its head to lure prey into its territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are considered serious pests, chewing their way into suburban homes to eat their garbage. They can be quite hard to get rid of because their poisonous fur just attracts more POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its arrow-shaped ear can channel sound waves and energy into focused bursts. Its body resembles the male symbol, which is thought to be a defensive display to confuse predators.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's poison causes memory loss but also grants the person affected short-term telepathy. This curious mix of abilities can leave victims confused, but with fleeting moments of telepathic connection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bites things it likes to show affection. However, it must be careful, as biting for too long will transfer a burning venom that can cause discomfort to its target.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's poison is used by cosmetic companies to make cologne. Many describe the scent as light and airy, making it a popular fragrance for those seeking a subtle, fresh aroma.
author: .izik

entry: Despite POKENAME's small stature, it can lift over 20 times its own body weight.  Its tough carapace is covered in thick, poisonous spines which are strong enough to pierce through a Metapod's shell.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's venom is used in cologne and has a honey-like scent. It doesn't last long, but was once used as a machine lubricant due to its viscosity and pleasant aroma.
author: .izik

entry: The boiling pink poison covering POKENAME's body is extremely hot. If cooled, it will break off and lose all potency, making it harmless once it solidifies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is constantly on guard, using its large ears to listen for danger.  If it detects a threat, it will move to strike first by channeling the toxins produced in its shell through the long horn on its head.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME uses its horn to knock sticks from trees to make its nest. This tactic helps it gather materials efficiently, allowing it to construct a sturdy and secure home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's poison induces an intense burning sensation. Its venom acts quickly, leaving a painful and burning aftermath that makes any encounter with it dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's poison is shared between its horn and fangs, so after using one, both are depleted and useless for a time. The more vibrant the color on its tail, the more venomous the specimen.
author: sk372

entry: While rolling, the poison sacks in POKENAME's body swirl, getting more and more potent. It is unwise to get in its path while it rolls.
author: .izik

entry: Tyrogue's fighting spirit drives POKENAME to battle. Its forelimbs grew into large claws that strike with great force. In intense fights, POKENAME releases poisonous energy that strengthens its attacks against other Pokémon.
author: kafoxnothylol_47795

entry: POKENAME's tail contains a powerful neurotoxin that is used to paralyze its opponents. Despite how potent its poison is, POKENAME prefers to just eat berries instead of hunting for prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hard stone sphere on POKENAME's head oozes a mild venom that can be used in stir-fries. When heated, the poison cooks out, leaving a strong garlic-like flavor that adds a unique taste to dishes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME throws its poisonous quills like throwing darts, mischievously pinning other Pokémon to tree trunks. While these quills are poisonous, they are only strong enough to cause mild nausea in humans.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses its tail as a lightning rod to absorb the energy of thunderbolts during storms. If someone threatens another member of its family, it attempts to strike them with the venomous horn on its forehead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hides beneath the sand, keeping its ears exposed to sense for danger. If someone ends up stepping on POKENAME, they will be met with tons of poisonous spines in their foot.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's poison is used in cologne and is easily harvested. It has a maple and woodsy scent, offering a refreshing and natural fragrance that's both affordable and popular.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers can sense air currents, allowing them to detect movement whenever they check their surroundings. While small, POKENAME's toxic horn can deal significant damage before it runs away.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's personality is a bit prickly, only truly trusting its Trainer and often not even letting its Trainer's other Pokémon near it. It can soften up in behavior over time, but the process takes quite some time.
author: sk372

entry: Some believe that today's Nidoran descended from POKENAME before they developed their gender differences.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME uses its hard horn to dig up mud and saplings, which it uses to build dams. This industrious nature makes it a skilled builder, capable of shaping its environment to suit its needs.
author: .izik
