entry: POKENAME uses its psychic powers to reinforce its beak while swimming. At top speed, it can break an iceberg clean in half.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME take turns caring for their young, teaching them basic survival skills, and taking great pride in those who learn quickly. If baby POKENAME become separated from their parents, they camouflage themselves and wait for a parent to return.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are formidable foes in Pokémon battles but still have a lot to learn. They are known to get upset after losing a battle, so Trainers make sure to stock up on treats to feed their broken egos.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sap of their flowers has properties reminiscent of soap, but it is also very aromatic and sweet; thus, it attracts many other Pokémon. POKENAME act annoyed by the presence of Pokémon, yet they typically carry them on their backs nonetheless.
author: infinex21

entry: In frozen regions, snowy villages worshipped POKENAME as a demigod. Ice effigies were carved in its likeness, believed to bring health if formed during the cold season.
author: .izik

entry: It spends weeks in solitude gathering water within its body, becoming incredibly dense and heavy. The stored water sustains the plant growing atop its head for months during periods of drought.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME will butt heads with another for dominance. It prefers the company of Pokémon other than its own kind, offering to give them rides.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The cold mist that emanates from POKENAME's shell can freeze human skin with prolonged exposure. Many doctors use brief isolated bursts of it for cryotherapy.
author: .izik

entry: Making its home in secluded coastal caves, POKENAME prefers a life of solitude. The light from its tail serves as a warning to other Pokémon to keep their distance.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME likes to live alone in solitude, training itself to be more agile. Interrupting it causes it to lash out, shooting out a multitude of burning-hot bubbles from its tail at whoever intrudes upon it.
author: sk372

entry: The bubbles drifting from POKENAME's head are filled with an incredibly hot gas. It can redirect them toward foes with a thought, though it lacks perfect control and often misses its mark.
author: .izik

entry: Fusion has given POKENAME a massive ego, rendering it almost incapable of working with others unless it is the de facto leader. Rivals in the wild will never stop competing to prove their superiority over one another.
author: sk372

entry: This dapper self fusion of Prinplup sports a refined appearance.  Unfortunately, this only helps to fuel it's belief that it is better than any other Prinplup.
author: infranscia

entry: POKENAME's pride can cause it to struggle with finding friends or partners, but once it does, it will bond with them and defend them with its life.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME's feelers expand into paddles while it swims through tropical waters. During this period, it can reach speeds of up to 40 knots.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fashion their shed feathers into hoods to help them hide deep in the sea, hiding their flowers beneath false flippers. Their flowers contain spores that spread out in the water, paralyzing prey for an easy meal as they swim by.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When POKENAME attacks using its mighty wings, droplets of cool water are sprinkled from its head. This water regulates its temperature as it fights.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its slippery slime to slide around on its stomach. Though its wings are small, they can deliver wicked blows strong enough to snap even the thickest of trees.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME is easily offended, so it should be treated with the utmost respect. Otherwise, it will inflict a curse upon the person who slighted it.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME love the attention they get after a good Pokémon battle. They demand lots of attention from their Trainer and can have a hard time working with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers to swim in cold waters, becoming sluggish if the sea grows too warm. During the summer, it migrates to icy seas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefer to hunt independently rather than with a pack. Standing on its hind legs and using its electrified tail, POKENAME can whip its body around to impact opponents and leave them paralyzed.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are obsessed with strength and their appearance, constantly strengthening and maintaining their steel armor. They will sit in rushing water for hours, letting it polish and clean their bodies.
author: santon5512

entry: Although it prefers to remain by itself, the scent of its flower attracts a myriad of Pokémon to it. Perhaps consequently, it trudges down to the seabed every day and feeds mostly on algae and seaweed.
author: infinex21

entry: These solitary Pokémon patrol their icy territories with diligence. The flame on their tail can withstand several hours underwater before they must surface.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME gathers in large clusters on shorelines with others of its kind. During winter, they wander into port towns, releasing a pleasant peppermint and kale scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME thrives in icy climates, its petals growing more vibrant the colder the temperature gets. Despite the cold, they never grow brittle and instead develop a more leathery texture.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are arrogant by nature. The more important they think they are, the bigger their head will become. If not grounded, they will be so buoyant that they will rise forever.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: If you live near the coast, you may see wild POKENAME in the forests when the temperature dips. These proud Pokémon prefer damp places, so they come out to play in the snow.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp beak to scratch into the rocks along the riverbanks to mark its territory. It is so proud that it won't even accept help from members of its own family.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its strong beak to break gems free from cave walls. Once loosened, it sprays them with high pressured water to clean them before eating.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has developed natural grooves on its body to allow it to more easily travel in snowy areas. It often spends its days hardening its body by rolling at top speed into glaciers.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: POKENAME dances across a lake's surface the moment the sun begins to rise, especially when onlookers are nearby. It appears to be encouraged to dance longer when more people are watching.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's beak is strong enough to break through almost any refuse. This gives it a wide variety of options when selecting trash to eat.
author: .izik

entry: Any stump or log POKENAME possesses becomes incredibly wet within moments. If left unattended, the wood will rot away entirely by the end of the following day.
author: .izik

entry: The shovel on POKENAME's head dispenses extremely cold water when it is angry. It fires this like a rifle at anyone who draws too close.
author: .izik

entry: The gems on POKENAME's body glow brighter whenever it uses a water-based attack. They go completely dark only when it is asleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME competes with others of its kind by spraying high pressured jets of water to knock over trees. The victor is whoever fells the tree fastest.
author: .izik

entry: Its upper limbs are both powerful enough to snap the thickest of trees in half and resilient enough to shield from a bomb blast. Though it prefers to live a solitary life, it will still hurry to defend a friend in danger.
author: imaginita

entry: When focusing intensely on its twig, POKENAME can move small icebergs. This focus demands intense effort and can render POKENAME unconscious if it attempts to move one too large.
author: .izik

entry: By intensely focusing their psychic energy, POKENAME create large bubbles on the tips of their wand. Fights between rival POKENAME are often intense, leading to bubble-shaped craters in the local area.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME fold their arms to become streamlined, allowing them to efficiently hunt in the icy waters they call home. They get defensive if other POKENAME enter their hunting ground. Trainers are advised not to raise more than one at a time.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME trains strictly in solitude, afraid a rival will steal its signature techniques. The shurikens it creates are capable of splitting an iceberg in two.
author: dodoowner_

entry: While dancing, POKENAME causes nearby water to shoot upward like geysers from areas within 20 feet of its body. Though harmless, this can be a dazzling sight for onlookers.
author: .izik

entry: Most POKENAME prefer to live in isolation, as living in a group tends to cause constant power struggles over each other fighting for the right to lead. In the rare instance that a group stays formed, the presiding POKENAME is truly exceptional.
author: craigprime

entry: POKENAME slides on its fin across snow to leave heart-shaped markings that differ slightly from one individual to the next. It does this to mark its territory near the water it inhabits.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend many hours alone, grooming water-resistant oils into their fur. They will gather in small squads, diving on an angled trajectory towards the artic sea bed, collecting mollusk Pokémon and bringing them back to the surface to eat.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME is a prideful loner who often clashes with its own kind whenever it crosses paths with them. Its small beak allows it to easily utilize compression as it fires water and bubbles at its foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is very prideful and fussy. While it can eat from a pet food bowl, it will only do so if the food was supplied by its Trainer, and if a sufficient amount was put in.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME prefer solitude; when confronted with another, they fight each other for dominance with their electricity and sharp claws. It lives near icy seas.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's large flipper-like ears generate a small electrical current. With the right application, it can be used as an effective massage technique to stimulate circulation and muscle recovery.
author: sk372

entry: The water POKENAME spits is charged with a negative electrical current. It uses this to keep predators like Sharpedo at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roam the icy peaks of mountains alone. It is unknown if POKENAME do not associate with each other because each believes itself to be the most important, or simply because they are too dull witted to form groups.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME have long flippers that allow them to swim quickly underwater. They act with a regal discipline because they want other Pokémon to respect them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME slashes through icebergs with its incredibly sharp claws to carve out its den. It leaves the entrance submerged underwater.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is quite antisocial, prone to backhanding anybody that gets too close to it with its powerfully-built claws. If that isn't enough, it can spray freezing-cold water from its claws as well to repel nuisances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME form colonies within city parks, swimming around through the large ponds that can be found within them. They are fiercely individualistic, racing one another to be the first to any food that is thrown into the water by visitors.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are aquatic and cannot fly. However, they sometimes do bounce across stretches of the ocean by forcefully slapping the surface of the water.
author: danarchosyndacalist

entry: POKENAME lives in underground lakes deep within caves. It uses its wings to swim in interesting patterns with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's thick fur protects it from the cold as it dives into frigid water to hunt for food. When threatened, it releases an ultrasonic wave to disorient enemies.
author: mepp.

entry: These Pokémon take great pride in their stored electricity. To settle disputes over strength, multiple POKENAME may attack a single target, competing to see who can maintain an electrical current the longest.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME releases pulses of electricity while swimming through cold seas. Should a submarine collide with it, the resulting discharge could shut down navigational equipment entirely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a mild venom as it swims through freezing waters. Swimming in water it inhabits can have dizzying side effects.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend so much time underwater that the flame on their tail is often left smoldering. They rely on their large wings to glide through icy cold water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME tends to be solitary, as it has a growing ego that leads it to compete with any other POKENAME, often in swimming contests. Due to its stubbornness, it refuses to accept a loss, leading to near-endless rematches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME haughtily ignores many potential playmates, only spending time with those that thoroughly impress it. It spends most of the time in water as it becomes embarrassed by its awkward movements on land.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are prideful and overconfident in their own abilities. They have a habit of picking fights with stronger Pokémon if they feel they've been slighted, relying on their cannons to equal out any discrepancies in strength.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It has a strong sense of pride, so it puffs out its shell whenever it refuses to listen to its Trainer. It uses its long, yellow tongue to burrow underground whenever it wants to hide from its Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is talented in the art of converting digital pages to paper. They don't move much but need to be fed ink every now and then.
author: aberry8286

entry: It defends itself from predators by jabbing at them with its three horns, which secrete a weak, neurotoxic venom. It scrapes at algae with its beak to keep its body nourished, while its bulb survives through photosynthesis.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a tremendous cook, and in the wild searches for the freshest seaside ingredients to feed its young. When its chick is threatened, it breaks the foe with high-pressure Hydro Pumps.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME has crown-like protrusions that give it a regal appearance. It is friendly and magnanimous, and enjoys chasing other Pokémon in its fish tank.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME expresses disdain towards Pokémon that receive more attention than itself. Trainers can help calm a rambunctious POKENAME by offering words of encouragement and praise.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It keeps its horns sharp by grinding them against the hardest rocks it can find; it's only satisfied when it can impale a tree with them. It uses its wings to swim swiftly and skewer prey upon its horns, surfacing when its horns are heavy with food.
author: infinex21

entry: A viciously strong Pokémon inhabiting the frigid northern waters, POKENAME often receives tribute from small Ice- and Water-type Pokémon. In exchange, it beats down on even the fiercest of aquatic hunters that try to prey on its subjects.
author: sk372

entry: The POKENAME with the largest horns is the leader of its pack and will proudly show off its might in battle to prove itself time and time again. They can spew powerful jets of frigid water from their beaks, even from high in the sky.
author: infinex21

entry: Once considered to be a king of the oceans it inhabited, POKENAME exerts considerable power over water. It is said a sprawling city was washed below the waves in the past due to angering this Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: Their antennae grow longer in tandem with their horns as they grow older, which serves to garner more respect from others of their kind. They are docile Pokémon who solely focus on keeping the plants in their domains healthy and alive.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME make their nests in hot springs and can coexist peacefully with any visitor that relaxes with them in the water. Any malicious invader that disturbs their peace will be met with explosive fury.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Colonies of POKENAME live in frigid seaside caverns. Its sharp metallic wings can slice through nearly any obstacle with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: In the wild, POKENAME preside over kingdoms of Poliwag. However, if one meets a Trainer it considers to have kingly qualities, it will follow their commands completely, albeit grudgingly.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME with long horns are the leaders of their flocks, though this does not stop others of their flocks from challenging them. If any of their three horns are broken, their morale plummets and they will exhibit signs of depression.
author: infinex21

entry: It has a very hostile demeanor. When two POKENAME fight for territory, they may create avalanches and earthquakes around them.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME loves to go on long swims. Despite its considerable power, it prefers to order other Pokémon around, like a captain does its crew.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Their impressive horns never cease growing, so even though they are a source of pride for them, they must routinely whittle them down. POKENAME use their sharp forelimbs to cut into trees and gorge upon the released sap.
author: infinex21

entry: It is strong enough to uproot a large tree without even using its powerful horn. It has a fragile sense of pride that makes it easy to provoke it, even over the smallest of things.
author: infinex21

entry: Smug and self-important, POKENAME expects nearly every other being to respect and praise its strength. Its skill and dexterity with the trident it wields are masterful, so its ego is not entirely unfounded.
author: sk372

entry: The tar-like substance covering POKENAME's body is incredibly cold. It squirms across the seafloor at surprising speeds in search of kelp to feed on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in shallow waters amongst coral reefs. They are docile by nature but also of little worth to any fisherman who catches them, so they are always thrown back.
author: fireblade141

entry: Its cobalt-blue gems are the greatest source of its pride. Should its gems ever be made dirty, it flies into a rage that lasts for nearly a whole week. Its talons are said to be so sharp that they could gouge solid diamond.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are popular with many antivirus companies due to their ability to pick up on stray data using their steel horns. It is not uncommon to see trained POKENAME floating around computers all over the world looking for any malware.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME prefers to avoid combat, flashing its hood in an intimidation display to frighten off potential foes. If forced to defend its pride, it fights by spitting venom and slashing with its icy wing and tail blades.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The trident horns and glacier mask adorning POKENAME's face are said to be a marker of divinity for a waddle of Piptar that rescues it from the ocean. The shinier and glossier these features are, the more worthy it is of being the waddle's emperor.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME leads its own waddle in the most frigid parts of the polar oceans. Those who disturb its colony will find themselves permanently frozen and encased, nothing more than a trophy for the waddle.
author: beatdoof

entry: As POKENAME flaps its giant wings, water bodies around it will start bubbling up, engulfing the surroundings in a massive tidal wave. However, it would only do so if it notices other Pokémon nearby not respecting its majesty.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME hunt in groups of at least five, swiftly "skating" along ice while using their wings to quickly adjust their movements and seal off their prey's escape. With their sharp wings, they make precise cuts that quickly fell their targets.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lies in wait in frozen arctic areas, waiting for Pokémon like Dewgong to breach onto land. Once it spots a target, it leaps out from hiding, swinging its razor-sharp flippers wildly to cut them down.
author: sk372

entry: It will capture lightning bolts through its three horns and store the power inside itself, up to around 100,000 volts worth. By striking together its sharp wings, it will challenge others to a battle so it may work off some of its stored energy.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME concentrates the vibrations of its wings into the crests on its head, turning them into oscillating blades. They use these blades to cut their nests into icebergs and cliffsides.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME live together in small groups around the waters of colder regions. The membranes on the back of each wrist are sturdy and act as makeshift shields for defense in combat.
author: sk372

entry: Sometimes referred to as “The Forest Emperor”, POKENAME commands absolute loyalty from the denizens of its home. Though it is prideful and egotistical, it will defend those weaker than it from harm until it collapses.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's horns show its power, and it sharpens them on thick trees with pride. Its flippers are actually large modified scales growing over its arms, sharp enough to cut through any plant of the jungle.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: The horns extending from its beak are a testament to its age and power while also being a source of pride. It spits compressed, scalding hot water at its foes with considerable precision, though it must brace itself due to its small stature.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have very sharp "wings" that allow them to easily cut into dirt and rock and burrow quickly. The longer and sharper their quills are, the more respected they are among their species.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME with long horns are said to have lived long lives and are said to be the most respected among their kind. They fight with martial arts that utilize their blade-sharp wings and their powerful legs to deliver devastating chops and kicks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME clash against each other, slamming the plates on their faces against each other in competitions for territory. The loser has to cover the victor in mud as an act of submission after losing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is rarely satisfied with the size of its mud-hole home. It uses its sharp limbs to carve into the land before flooding it to increase its muddy domain, regardless of any other creatures it inconveniences to do so.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims through rivers at high speeds. Should it spot someone fishing on its territory, it bursts from the water and douses them in foul-smelling mud.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a stoic, taciturn expression and does not openly express its affection for its Trainer. This is because it telepathically conveys its affectionate thoughts directly to its Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using the sharp edges of their flipper-like wings, POKENAME brace themselves to fire out compressed water jets or their long tongues. Their tongues can shoot out with enough force to break apart a chunk of solid ice.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have a regal appearance thanks to their crown and their stoic disposition. They protect their Trainers from harm by deflecting attacks using their aura.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sharp and rigid petals of their strange flowers have long been used in some tools and weapons, though they contain a medicinal sap within them as well. The longer their horns are, the more respect they garner from their peers.
author: infinex21

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME latches its rear jaws onto icebergs to avoid drifting. It prefers these cold waters for rest and has trouble sleeping in tropical climates.
author: .izik

entry: Due to its coloring and scavenged accessories, sailors often mistake POKENAME for manmade buoys or sunken ship remains. The frills on its head are capable of photosynthesis even among the frozen waters of the northern oceans.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: POKENAME exudes an oppressive aura of majesty and dominion, influencing nearby Pokémon to protect and serve it. Luckily, the only things POKENAME ever demands are solitude during its naps and the occasional meal of fish.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Referred to as the Empress of the Waves by many, POKENAME's wake is sought out by Surfers due to their size. When an Electric-type attempts to battle, it burrows to the sea floor, causing whirlpools to pull the foe down.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The blades on POKENAME's legs are as hard as steel, allowing it to slice through icebergs as though they were paper. Paths carved by POKENAME are often used by ships transporting cargo through arctic waters.
author: chibitales

entry: Known as the Emperor of the Seas in some cultures, this ruthless Pokémon is capable of creating underwater earthquakes powerful enough to cause giant tsunamis should its pride be hurt. The trident-like spikes on its back are able to attract storms.
author: milchik

entry: The crown on POKENAME's head is made of sturdy golden wood. They bash it into foes who draw too close to their nest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stands tall and proud, showing its sturdy, gold wood crown. It replenishes it by drinking fresh glacier water.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The tree on POKENAME's back always appears to be covered in snow. Even in the heat of summer, it never melts.
author: .izik

entry: The superheated bubbles emanating from POKENAME's head can scald skin on contact. It prefers a defensive fighting style, tricking opponents into swinging into the bubbles to deal damage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are well known for their special way of caring for their eggs: swaddled between their feet. Protective of their unhatched young, POKENAME will squawk and get into horn fights with others who dare come too close.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME keeps the blue metal at the tips of its wings extremely shiny as a point of pride among its allies. Should it become dirty even briefly, it swims at high speed to remove the debris.
author: .izik

entry: Sporting the largest horns of all, this self fusion readily takes leadership of its flock.  Oddly, it's stricter than most Empoleon; some say too much.  On the flipside, it will even more fiercely protect all it holds dear.
author: infranscia

entry: Said to be imbued with the spirit of the Empoleon it was poached from, POKENAME cleaves fleets of poaching ships in revenge.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME guards its territory from atop icebergs, intimidating invaders with its martial prowess by cleaving ice floes in half.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME uses its three horns to stab anyone attempting to be more elegant than it. While the ribbonlike feelers on its front are light and soft, they can easily slice down a door into pieces with their thin, sharp ends.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME guards underwater temples of an ancient civilization that sank beneath the sea long ago. When POKENAME sees an intruder, it attacks them with its razor-sharp blades.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Nicknamed the "Water Dahlia" by locals, POKENAME lives around shallow but quick-moving streams, particularly in the far south of the planet. An omnivore and an autotroph, it can get its energy from eating fish Pokémon when it cannot photosynthesize.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Nicknamed the "Water Dahlia" by locals, POKENAME lives around shallow but quick-moving streams, particularly in the far south of the planet. An omnivore and an autotroph, it can get its energy from eating fish Pokémon when it cannot photosynthesize.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is seen as emblematic of a ruler that watches over its domain with kindness and grace. Underestimating it is a poor choice, as it wields a trident and its own oversized ears with incredible strength and finesse.
author: sk372

entry: Said to have been born from a fallen sailor lost at sea, POKENAME wanders the open ocean. It is known to rescue people from sinking ships, guiding them safely to the surface.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are often seen as a sign of luxury and are usually owned by either those who are successful or those who are simply lucky. POKENAME are usually sent out during classy celebrations.
author: jangodiot

entry: When not keeping watch from its nest or hunting, POKENAME preens. Over time, POKENAME's territory has shifted closer to both the equator and the poles: they can withstand high heat and the cold and, in fact, hunt the best in these conditions.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Using psychokinetic pulses, POKENAME can propel themselves through water at speeds rivaling even those of a fully-grown Sharpedo.
author: bugtoad

entry: The steel horns on POKENAME's head grow longer with age, attesting to its survival skills and thus making it more favorable to potential mates. The longest horns ever recorded reached from the head to the top of the tails.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's hard body allows it to dive deep into ocean trenches without difficulty. It can descend to 400 feet below the surface without issue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fan their tails in a display of imperial dominance whenever they feel the need to exert their superiority. They are proud and wilful Pokémon; Trainers are advised to take a firm hand when working with them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's three horns are made of sturdy iron, which they use to break away stone in search of mineral deposits. They consume large amounts of minerals every day, which help to strengthen their horns.
author: santon5512

entry: Once known as the "Prince of Snow's Harvest", it was considered good luck to spot one walking near a village in late winter. This was believed to bring bountiful crops and rich soil.
author: .izik

entry: The three horns on POKENAME's head are used for fighting. Those with the largest horns find it easier to pop rivals and are seen as the leaders amongst their group.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME proclaim themselves the rulers of any cave they live in, demanding crystals from other Pokémon in exchange for protection. Simpler Pokémon obey without question, while smarter ones quickly realize their promises are empty.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The POKENAME with the largest horns atop its head gains the loyalty of its group and is deemed its leader. It is often seen guarded by Venipede.
author: _adamos.

entry: The king of the ice age, POKENAME was a predator to early humans before the invention of Poké Balls and have been revived due to Pokémon fusion.
author: creep0202

entry: POKENAME clashes with others of its kind through bashing and scraping their metal masks against each other. Once triumphant, an POKENAME shoots water from the tips of the trident as a mark of celebration and dominance.
author: sk372

entry: The loud cries POKENAME produces from its ears sound like scraping metal. It uses this to warn others of its kind gathering kelp beneath the sea's surface about approaching predators.
author: .izik

entry: Nicknamed the King of Slimes, POKENAME often gather groups of their unevolved and younger brethren, even including unfused Goomy. The leader acts as the guardian for the entire group, retaliating against threats with intense Water-type attacks.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lounges atop icebergs in icy waters to lord over nearby Piplup. Should they face danger, it leaps into action and bashes the threat with its hardened body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims in frigid arctic waters, using its bladed arms to cleave through any ice in its way. This Pokémon's regal attitude can make it hard for Trainers to control.
author: fireblade141

entry: The blue wooden greatsword POKENAME carries is as hard as iron. It wields it in battle like a skilled knight defending a kingdom.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crafts tridents from birch wood found near the water's edge. With it, it can control nearby water and bring it to a boil at a glance.
author: .izik

entry: Bubbles released from POKENAME's trident are full of psychic energy, causing those struck by them to be pushed back from the impact. Rivalling POKENAME often try to break their opponent's horns, causing the loser to be cast out.
author: chibitales

entry: These prideful Pokémon use races to determine who is the leader. Their sharp horns, beaks, and feet are capable of slicing through glaciers when they swim.
author: torterrable

entry: It can run across land and sea alike with incredible speed.  If there is anything in its way, POKENAME will throw shuriken made of compressed water ahead to slice it to shreds and run right through.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME's golden crown releases an icy cold powder when it is upset. When inhaled, the victim loses control of the nerves throughout their body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has bold crests, showing elegance and strength. Cunning yet obstinate, it dominates jetties, delivering lethal kicks. It musters fierce gangs under its rule, vying for power in waterfront turf wars.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's metallic body cuts through icy waters with ease, allowing it to reach high speeds. Entire schools travel in organized formations through the sea in search of places to leave their eggs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME want other Pokémon to respect them but are often baffled when they receive that respect. Whenever they lose their cool, they fluster and apologize profusely, which can be a headache for Trainers to deal with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's trident-shaped beak creates a hydrodynamic wedge in front of it when swimming, helping it move swiftly through the water. It is common to see two POKENAME racing one another in order to establish which is the superior Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lay claim to large swathes of glacier as their territory, typically making their home within a meltwater lake. They fling orbs of icy water at those that would challenge them, relying on the freezing temperature to sap their foes' strength.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have long lifespans, which are denoted by the length of their three horns. When enraged, steam rises from their bright blue fur.
author: infinex21

entry: These prideful Pokémon are quick to battle if they are struck in any way or if they feel as though they are being challenged in some way. Their blue-white flames burn hotter and longer when met with water, akin to Class D fires.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are considered difficult to train due to their haughty natures and a desire to be physically stronger than everyone. POKENAME in the wild are easy to find, since they make grandiose ice palaces to live in.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME will often develop heated rivalries, competing in high-speed races to prove their superiority. Because of their competitive and cutthroat nature, their races have become a popular spectacle.
author: mistymagius

entry: All three heads of an POKENAME are extremely elegant. If one of the heads makes a mistake, they blame it on another. They never get along.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The central head is the one that eats, while the other heads prepare the food by tenderizing it, pulverizing it, or merely by cutting it up. Each head believes itself to be the most important, so they often end up fighting among themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful beak to shatter ice floes, dunking its prey into the frigid ocean. As its pride is easily injured, it rarely gathers with others of its kind, preferring to lead pods of Dewgong.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME strut around with a regal bearing, confident in their superiority to all other Pokémon around them. Their haughty attitude makes them unpopular with others, but their bulk and tough shell make challenging their superiority complex difficult.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Calling polluted factory waters home, POKENAME uses its coloration to confound Tentacool's normally stellar sight. When one swims by, this Pokémon extends its reach with Shadow Claws, grasping its prey and taking them down to the depths.
author: ghostslythe

entry: These Pokémon sharpen their trident-shaped horns by scratching them against its rocklike pincers. It can get carried away doing this and fall over.
author: themicelegion

entry: The stone on its back constantly absorbs heat and energy from the sun. POKENAME has a strong magnetic charge, powerful enough to cause electronic devices within a three-meter radius of it to malfunction.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many campers have to keep a close eye on their belongings whenever POKENAME are active since they steal metal items when they ruffle through bags. Thankfully for most Trainers, they are quite slow and can only drag small objects along with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Facing and heading north most of the time, POKENAME appears to be on a long pilgrimage. It is thought to be in search for the rest of its family.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME barely moves and is often mistaken for a statue or a weirdly shaped rock. If pointed in any direction other than north, it will slowly rotate until its nose points northward.
author: atlas3339098

entry: When sleeping, POKENAME points its nose straight up directly to the sky. Its flames grow dim during this time, leading researchers to believe that this position calms it for an unknown reason.
author: .izik

entry: Its nose is used to navigate the currents of the seas it inhabits. Its rock-hard body defends it from predators.
author: melodydelune

entry: Its magnetic body draws in granules of iron from the sea floor, which meld together to form its protective outer shell. As a result of its weight and rigidity, however, it swims at a near glacial pace.
author: houseoffallingflowers

entry: POKENAME is widely regarded as an excellent Pokémon for transportation as well as navigation, as it innately knows the four cardinal directions. It is also known to save people lost at sea and bring them back home.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: Although they have compass-like properties, they do not point north. Scientists theorize that they are aligned with a magnetic field on the moon.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME can sense the emotions of people around it through the red beads on its neck, being especially drawn to sorrow. Often mocked for its large nose, it can usually be found by following the sound of its crying.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The top of POKENAME's head is highly magnetic, always pointing north, much like a compass. If two of these Pokémon are near each other, they will both spin wildly.
author: santon5512

entry: Since POKENAME tends to stay motionless for days at a time, it's often mistaken for a peculiar statue. It uses the magnetic properties of its nose to generate force fields that keep away those who try to disturb its meditative stasis.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In its natural habitat, POKENAME is always found hanging from a tree's northern side. Its magnetic aura attracts metallic minerals which it adheres to itself to form its shell.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Flocks of POKENAME will have one leader with an extremely magnetic beak. The magnetic powers of their beaks allow them to communicate somehow with others of their kind and lets them form organized groups.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their nose and ears to pinpoint magnetic fields and areas of interest. Because of this, they're commonly used in underground rescues.
author: totodile.

entry: Its nose ring is made of solid rock. It uses it to trap prey and prevent it from getting away.
author: iolitetigerdragon

entry: POKENAME's magnetic nose remains oddly cool compared to the rest of its bubbling molten-hot body. It prefers to live in volcanic areas, thriving on the heat while its magnetic nose remains unaffected.
author: .izik

entry: When tired of flying, POKENAME sticks its magnetic nose to the metal sides of stopped train cars. It will dangle there until the train starts, jostling it awake and preparing it for its next journey.
author: .izik

entry: Its magnetic nose draws it towards the eggs of Steel-type Pokémon. Unable to crack the shells with its bite, it instead swallows them whole.
author: busilisk

entry: POKENAME has poor vision, so it navigates by smell and by nuzzling things. Its hair is made from metal fibers, and protects its face.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's nose is heavy and magnetic. It always faces north, which makes moving around rather difficult, as POKENAME must resort to carrying its large nose atop its head.
author: goldegummybear

entry: POKENAME's large nose gives it a strong sense of smell, used to find muddy and swampy areas to relax in. It's believed that it looks for mud with higher mineral content, discernible thanks to its heightened smell capabilities.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever POKENAME inhales deeply, its psychic senses let it essentially smell the emotions around it. Positive emotions have a more appealing scent, so POKENAME is drawn towards those with that type of aroma.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will stand still for hours and pretend to be a rock, purely for its own amusement. If discovered, it rubs its arms together to produce an irritating screech.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME cannot see well, instead using their nose and the holes on their feet to smell their surroundings. It's thought they can map an entire continent by smell and are intelligent enough to remember specific places for decades.
author: chibitales

entry: Instead of almost always pointing north like Nosepass, POKENAME's giant nose seems to point to the nearest graveyard. Ironically, it seems to dislike even the mere presence of metal, despite Probopass's inclination to magnetize metal filings.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Deep rumbling breaths can be heard from its false mouth, puffs of steam emitting from what appears to be a nose. When sleeping, it always makes sure this mouth is pointed north, for unknown reasons.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME sneezes, tidal waves as large as buildings are formed. This has caused POKENAME to be a banned fusion in many regions.
author: scotsman

entry: POKENAME's large nose and shell are highly magnetic. It tries to stay clear of mineshafts, as a single minecart can leave it stuck for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their strong magnetism to help pull them along hazardous terrains and make their homes atop sheer cliffsides. Hikers let POKENAME run ahead of them on a trail to ensure they can always keep track of which way is North.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: It is said caves leading north are actually the tunnels created by POKENAME training. Any iron rubble created in this process clings to the magnetic tip of their tail.
author: enemyphase

entry: Due to its north-facing snout, POKENAME have had to develop impeccable reflexes. It is nearly impossible to sneak up on one without activating its fighting instinct and sending it into a frenzy.
author: enemyphase

entry: POKENAME create their nests out of small pebbles and stones that lack magnetic properties. Should a rock have a magnetic material within, POKENAME will kick it into the water and avoid it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is commonly used as a reaction image on many social media platforms.
author: valtsuri

entry: POKENAME's extremely magnetic nose attracts Steel type Pokémon to its den when it senses they are upset or sad. It then wraps them in its feelers, which appears to soothe them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's large nose lets it sniff out interlopers before they've even gotten near it. It hops out of sight before leaping into action and striking intruders with its heavy stone ears and feet.
author: sk372

entry: A part of the electric aura surrounding POKENAME will always be pulled north, making it a reliable source of navigation for many explorers.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME frequently gets its magnetic nose stuck to the sides of cruise ships unintentionally. While struggling to break free, it often causes considerable damage to the vessel.
author: .izik

entry: A strong electrical current runs through POKENAME's nose. It communicates with others of its kind by touching noses together.
author: .izik

entry: The electrical current that runs through POKENAME's nose helps its packmates understand its emotions. When several POKENAME connect their tails together, it creates a powerful electromagnetic field to deter predators while the group sleeps.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's red nose has strong magnetic properties, so it can easily find metal ores. Although it will happily eat ores that it finds, it is possible to train it otherwise; because of this, it is a common companion for some miners.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME's head can rotate 360 degrees even while its body remains still, allowing it to face magnetic north at all times. Sometimes, one will be born that points south instead.
author: kiwiarms

entry: The bud atop POKENAME's head always faces north. When it's warm, the bud opens, spreading magnetic waves.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: It uses its two big noses to sniff out nearby items. When POKENAME drinks mineral-rich springwater, its magnetism strengthens.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful ears to smash rocks, looking for magnetic material. It coats its fur with this material to allow it to detect its surroundings through its magnetic field.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its nose protrudes beyond its protective gel, allowing it to smell food and allies. The nostrils release excess gel, which has magnetic properties.
author: krune

entry: Using magnetism, POKENAME flies through the air, following the latest scent that piqued its curiosity. Despite being made of stone, its body is actually quite lightweight.
author: sk372

entry: Although blind, POKENAME can use its sixth sense of direction to guide it. Planes use it as a compass if the GPS breaks or loses connection.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The magnetic pulses from POKENAME's nose allow it to communicate silently with its flock. These conversations can disrupt nearby radio signals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leech material out of rock faces to eat. In olden times, POKENAME were used to deliver messages due to their impeccable sense of direction.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME hides in deep caverns, their numbers being greater in magnetic areas. While their teeth are not sharp, their powerful jaws are strong enough to crush small boulders.
author: mistymagius

entry: With its adept nose and keen magnetic sense, POKENAME can detect the minerals it loves to eat from a great distance away.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME always prefers stones with the highest metal content. Once it has eaten one, it turns in the direction of the next magnetic stone.
author: chorb33

entry: Its horn can emit a strong magnetic field, attracting iron-rich stones. It then reverses the field's polarity to fire them as dangerous projectiles.
author: chorb33

entry: It can emit strong magnetism via its horn to attract stones with a high metal content. It then changes polarity to fire them as dangerous projectiles.
author: chorb33

entry: It can emit strong magnetism via its horn to attract stones with a high metal content. It then changes polarity to fire them as dangerous projectiles.
author: chorb33

entry: A pack of POKENAME can search for prey with its magnetic abilities. Said abilities can also help boats lost at sea.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The magnetic stones on POKENAME's head emit a Spelon Berry scent that attracts prey. It will use Thunder Wave to render them helpless, making them easy to capture and consume.
author: .izik

entry: They have been a pivotal part of the creation of a global atlas, as their sensitivity to magnetism allows them to follow precise geographical patterns. Nowadays, they spend their time in museums, helping curators preserve sensitive maps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The end of POKENAME's anchor is extremely magnetic. It drags it across the seafloor to collect metal objects that it then sleeps on at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always faces the sun, constantly shifting its position to line itself up perfectly. Once it hits midday, POKENAME will lie on its back, pointing its nose straight up.
author: mistymagius

entry: When resting in the desert heat, POKENAME always points its nose north. It has trouble sleeping if it is not pointing in that direction, as its orientation is somehow vital for its rest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are assembled of particles of magnetic sand that concentrate around metal structures. They gather minerals from rocky shores and condense them within their grains to continuously build up the structures they cling to.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The more seeds POKENAME eats, the more magnetic its nose gets. It uses this magnetism to sense the world around it, allowing it to navigate through environments with a unique sensitivity.
author: .izik

entry: The magnets coming from POKENAME's ears become incredibly strong right before it unleashes a fire-based attack. The flames it unleashes are hot enough to melt iron.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces a white smoke when healthy, but makes dark gray smoke when it is injured or not getting sufficient nutrients. When it gets annoyed, steam is generated more vigorously and is expelled from all of its vents at once.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME pulls up its sagging hide before releasing magnetic waves from its nose. When it senses ore, it violently headbutts cave walls to dig and feed.
author: .izik

entry: The pad atop its head houses a spike that acts like a compass's needle, always pointing due north. Despite its heavy, rocky body, it is a capable swimmer that can absorb minerals from water.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have an odd attraction to people who are in a happy romantic relationship and will point in their direction when they sense couples nearby. Thorough investigation reveals that this attraction ignores magnetism, baffling scientists.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It's said that no two heads of any POKENAME are the same, making them as unique as fingerprints. When one head sneezes, the others follow suit, the vibrations of which can cause devastating earthquakes.
author: sontyp

entry: The top of POKENAME's head is extremely magnetic. Should it bury itself in the ground near roads, it unintentionally attracts metal objects dropped by nearby Trainers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the magnetic nose on its face to detect coins. It seeks them out to add to its horde, constantly on the lookout for new treasures to collect.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses magnetism to cause large rocks to slam into it so that it can toughen up its body. This training eventually makes POKENAME so resilient that even sheets of metal will shatter if rammed into its body.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME emits a strong magnetism, which is even more potent around its nose; because of its magnetism, it can easily find ores to feast upon. When it discovered an Iron Ball, it instantly took to playing with it and would not let anyone touch it.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's paws are extremely magnetic and allow it to cling to metal surfaces. It uses this ability to enhance its agility, allowing it to steal valuables from those in its territory with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME usually remains sedate, but upon smelling certain trigger smells will fly into a frothing rage. The scents that trigger the anger are different for each individual, so preventing tantrums is difficult.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is adorned with a fuzzy coat of iron filings. It navigates via a mix of echolocation and magnetic field detection.
author: hophoppip

entry: It has been said that pressing the nose of a POKENAME during its rampage will calm it down instantly. Due to the ferocity of its raging, this has yet to be scientifically verified.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME's nose is facing north, its strength triples. It can easily lift a pickup truck at this time, using its enhanced magnetic power to dominate its surroundings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is rather vain about its physical appearance, polishing and chiseling its stone form into the build it finds perfect. The only part it refuses to adjust is its massive nose, thinking it already flawless.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are usually found on remote islands, blankly staring into the distance while barely moving an inch. Ancient people used to believe that POKENAME were the reincarnations of their former elders.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's nose directs it toward veins of magnetic minerals, which it then excavates and consumes. Miners train it to lead them to these veins and reward it with chunks of the mineral.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a specialized sense of smell, able to identify the type and quality of any stone or gem offered to it. Many appraisers keep one on hand to help with determining the value of any given jewel they come across.
author: sk372

entry: The flames on POKENAME's body are actually thin magnetic wires. They billow like flames as it gallops across meadows, giving the illusion of fiery energy in motion.
author: .izik

entry: The thin-haired magnetic wire-comprised mane on POKENAME's body can get very hot if it runs too fast. It needs to take multiple stops throughout the day to ensure it doesn't overheat and cause harm to itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's heads often argue to the point of attempting to peck at each other. Due to their noses possessing the same magnetic polarity, this just causes their heads to be repelled back, preventing any real violence.
author: sk372

entry: Its nose is believed to be sensitive enough to detect smells from miles away. Unfortunately, this ability is impeded by POKENAME's own horrible stench.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME can be identified by the deep, ethereal noise it makes as it breathes. If you hear spectral snorting every night, you're being haunted by POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its magnetic nose to find iron deposits and eat them. It can sense these hidden resources from over one mile away.
author: .izik

entry: Constantly stressed, POKENAME vents its anxiety by running around at high speeds and tackling into others. One can tell if POKENAME is on a rampage by the high-pitched yowl of a scream it makes before it runs about.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's increased body temperature made its Mini-Noses harder to control. Scientists study them to better understand the magnetic fields of stars.
author: spriter

entry: Wherever POKENAME goes, little blocks seem to form for it to jump up to and break. A very successful and long-running video game franchise stars a POKENAME as its main character.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts for magnetic Pokémon, waiting for them to leave their caves before silently ambushing them. Its body is so magnetic that small metal objects get attracted to its body as it flies overhead.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME cannot fully control their magnetic powers yet. Trainers often find them getting dragged by magnetic rocks, where they stay stuck until they either evolve or get eaten.
author: _cradily_

entry: As POKENAME wanders through marshes, cans and bottlecaps stick to its body. When tired, it naps on a slope, letting its weakened magnetism slide the junk off.
author: .izik

entry: The magnetic sand on top of POKENAME emits such a strong magnetic field that it will always point north. Many hikers will keep these Pokémon to avoid getting lost.
author: santon5512

entry: It uses its magnetism to attach itself to lamp posts, remaining there motionless for hours or days at a time. Some suggest that it is simply trying to blend in, thinking it is disguised as a person.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Encased in a veritable fortress of a shell, POKENAME spends near the entirety of its life attached to a tree trunk. The little flag on its head is an antenna, which it uses to communicate remotely with other POKENAME.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are considered a pest to ships, often found eating away at the hulls and rotors. A popular way to remove them is to tickle their mustache, distracting them enough to be scooped off.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME manifests a large hammer for itself to wield to defend itself and demolish things. To keep it from wrecking something important, many task it with deleting junk data, which it seems to enjoy immensely.
author: sk372

entry: It paints enormous, colorful murals on mountainsides. It is followed everywhere by a mini-nose that can undo any unsatisfactory brushstroke it makes.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME are obsessed with shiny rocks, often putting them in their pouches for safe keeping. Some universities have POKENAME assist with engineering.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Magnetism in POKENAME's body allows it to levitate as long as the trio of rocks circle it evenly. When upset, lightning courses across the large mustache on its face.
author: sk372

entry: Murals depicting POKENAME suggest people thought of it as a minor guardian deity in the past. According to legend, it would breathe a rainbow mist on a chosen few, who would be granted a body as strong and rugged as stone.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a Pokémon with the ability to use the magnetic field to search for hidden treasure. The dowsers on the side of its body will always point to buried treasure.
author: cobalt0135

entry: The iron filings composing its lower nasal area greatly conduct the high-voltage energy which it discharges into foes. For this reason, when POKENAME sneezes, it may unintentionally let loose a violent electric pulse.
author: gaogao028

entry: A combination of magnetism and psychic powers lets POKENAME manipulate the positions of people and terrain around it. It often reaches its floating hands out and grabs its Trainer to pull them close, worried for their safety.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a gentle, slow-moving creature inhabiting the forests. It rarely gets involved in conflict, but if pressed, the two small stone drones that float alongside it help fight on its behalf, due to its slow speed in combat.
author: sk372

entry: According to legend, POKENAME acts as a proud and unpredictable representative of spirits that lost their life deep within secluded caverns. Its ethereal form hides inside the red nose-shaped stone when inactive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: According to legend, POKENAME acts as a proud and unpredictable representative of spirits that lost their life deep within secluded caverns. Its ethereal form hides inside the red nose-shaped stone when inactive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its back acts as a solar-powered super magnet. On sunny days, its magnetic field is capable of pulling planes from the sky.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: Though its charge is slow and lumbering, few things can stand the impact of POKENAME's headbutt. It has been observed carefully grooming the mane around its neck, using magnetism from its horn to remove any debris.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME reflects magnetic waves using its shield, making it a great help in protecting high-tech electronics from getting damaged. It is surprisingly fast, using its own magnetic field to levitate off the ground.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can create powerful magnetic fields that keep opponents at a distance while it naps. To draw food closer, it inhales through its large nostrils without even trying to get up.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When levitates, POKENAME looks like a ship sailing through the sea that its mustache emulates. It has small units that follow it wherever it goes.
author: merumsb

entry: POKENAME produces a strong magnetic field from the crystals on its back. Certain Pokémon like Nosepass and Magneton hang around POKENAME in hopes to evolve.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME possesses a high level of focus and endurance, allowing it to become a seasoned fighter. It enjoys meditating on cliffsides.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME train by crushing boulders beneath their knuckles, while their magnetic whiskers collect the debris to strengthen their defenses. Due to this, a POKENAME's beard length directly indicates their strength.
author: enemyphase

entry: POKENAME controls the mini-nose at the end of its chain through magnetism. At rest, the mini-nose points due north.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The head with the red nose is the core of this Pokémon's body and the one that controls the other three heads. The core's nose will always point North and the noses of its other heads will each point in one of the other cardinal directions.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's nose is extremely magnetic and warm to the touch. The mucus that drips from it can be used by medical professionals to create soothing philtres.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's eyes can see vast distances with ease. It focuses in on those who enter its territory and once locked on, sends its little drones off to harass them for trespassing.
author: sk372

entry: Curiosity and a mild hypnotic effect compel many to follow after POKENAME's red flame in the dark. Once they draw near, it siphons some of their life force via deeply inhaling through its large nose.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's large mustache muffles and distorts its singing voice, giving its song a very strange, deep and warbling tone. The song is only half as effective at putting others to sleep as a result.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often found carrying a bunch of Probobuff, to make sure they don't get stuck to magnetic rocks. They like singing to their babies, but the metallic sounds they make discomfort for other species.
author: _cradily_

entry: Garden statues of POKENAME outnumber the actual Pokémon. Because the ferrous dust it leaves enriches soil, it's used as a symbol of fertile land.
author: .realthree

entry: The hair on a POKENAME's head is made from a highly magnetic material. If their hair stands up it is an indication that there are precious metals or gemstones nearby.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME can emit a powerful EMP via the electromagnet in its head, deactivating everything electronic in its vicinity.
author: chorb33

entry: It performs cheerful dances, waving around the balls of magnetized iron fillings on its wing tips. Besides cheering on allies, POKENAME's dances also generate powerful magnetic fields.
author: hophoppip

entry: Ghostly energy causes metal to collect around the heads on its arms. It's thought to direct souls to the afterlife.
author: moopse

entry: It poses with its limbs at strange angles, which allows it to fine-tune the effects of its natural magnetic field. If it senses a threat, it will attack using thousands of magnetized needles.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME have highly sophisticated directional skills. Unfortunately, their bizarre appearance makes them unappealing to Trainers.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME tears apart sunken ship hulls with its claws. Shredded metal clings to its magnetic body, forming a makeshift armor that strengthens its defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME surfaces near hidden deposits of magnetic metals. It is commonly used by manufacturing companies to sniff out rare minerals.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME illuminates caves with its various bulbs to search for moss and lichen covered-rocks. It brushes its moustache-like growth over the stones to dislodge the moss and lichen, which it collects to eat later.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME will anchor its heavy body into the cave ceilings. It eats by using magnetism to bring metal-rich rocks into its mouth. When it has depleted a cave, it uses its body to drill for a deeper cavern.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Using its strong magnetic field, it coats its fur in metal to act as armor for its body. Its punches are equivalent to boulders being thrown.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME regularly needs to keep its wings free from debris so that it is not weighed down by metallic objects, as its wings are made out of ferrofluid. Its flaming tail can melt metal into a liquid, nonmagnetic state.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is heavier than it appears, so its primary method of attack is jumping onto a foe's head. It seems to have a strong inclination of viewing turtle-like Pokémon as rivals.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a surprisingly prolific jumper. Its fists can break bricks simply by jumping from underneath them.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Most POKENAME live in the mantle of the planet. The magnet on their back can launch chunks of iron into the stratosphere.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME contains a surprising amount of magnetic power within its compact body. The stone cap on its head levitates when it exerts a large amount of its powers.
author: sk372

entry: A long time ago, four POKENAME lived with humanity and protected their cities. Nowadays, once a year during a festival, an ancient song is used as tribute to them.
author: doodledoo

entry: POKENAME's steel fangs quickly drain the life from its victims. The sack on its back is thought to hold its unfinished food.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The sharp stinger on the tail of POKENAME acts more as a deterrent than a real weapon. They are not strong enough to swing it with any force but will raise it menacingly when they feel endangered.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It feeds on electricity until it is charged enough to levitate.  Then, it uses its blue-cloth wings to direct its movement, swooping with shocking speed to attack.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME wields its blade with honor and fierce dedication, determined to protect those it holds dear. It often places itself as a warrior that guards families of Marowak and Cubone in the wild.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its small stature, it is quite brave, and it often finds itself in combat with Pokémon much stronger than it. It wields a bone sword as its primary form of offense.
author: fireblade141

entry: Despite its small stature, it is quite brave, often finding itself in combat with foes much stronger than it. It wields its bone sword in combat as its primary form of offense.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME are known to quickly stretch their bladed leg at others and slice them down without warning. It is believed that these Pokémon taught pirates how to walk with peg legs.
author: soup1900

entry: Each time POKENAME stabs a foe, it drains a bit of their life energy from them. Anyone who survives three minutes of POKENAME volleying stabs at them at bullet-like speeds will honorably have all their life force returned back to them.
author: soup1900

entry: The shroud wrapped around POKENAME shields it from the outside world, acting as a protective cocoon. The steel blade protruding from its head is reserved as a last resort, drawn only when a Pokémon poses a real threat to its safety.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It uses its chains to trap and constrict enemies. The loud rattling sound it makes as it runs is feared far and wide.
author: hophoppip

entry: Moving at blinding speeds, POKENAME runs up to Pokémon and hits them with its sheath to knock them unconscious. Once it has done so, it uses its scythe to reap all of their life energy.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has two scythes, but one is always covered inside of its sheath. This allows it to interact with other beings without slicing them apart and reaping their life force.
author: soup1900

entry: Legends state that POKENAME act as psychopomps,  guides for Pokémon who have perished in icy regions. It is said that the misty tendrils of fog swirling around their spearheads are souls drifting between this world and the next.
author: eloquent_panda

entry: During cold nights, POKENAME uses life energy to keep itself warm. Once it has gripped its prey with its horns, the blue cloth will wrap around and squeeze the life force out of the victim.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is often found eerily alone in lakes, as all other Pokémon have either fled or fallen to its wrath. Rumor has it that its sword-like tail collects the souls of its prey, further increasing its power.
author: h0bojoe

entry: When POKENAME drains foes of their life force, it inherits a part of their genetics. Enough DNA from certain groups of species may cause this Pokémon to mutate.
author: soup1900

entry: Clutching a blade in its mouth, POKENAME goes off on various adventures across the land. A strange little creature accompanies it, loudly drawing its attention to things and often coming across as a nuisance to POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often used inside of video games for its weapon abilities. It has very limited movement, only being able to attack and cleave like an actual sword.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lives inside a long shell in the shape of a blade. The sides of the shell are sharp, so anything that touches its shell will get cuts on itself.
author: soup1900

entry: Each time POKENAME molts its shell, the sword lodged in it falls out. During this short phase where the shell is weak and regrowing, it holds onto this blade with its tiny claws to stab at hungry predators that try to approach it.
author: soup1900

entry: Flying high in the sky, POKENAME uses the blade on its tail to strike prey from above. It then uses its sharp fangs to break through tough hide and extract the life force from its prey.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME flies around the world, following cloud trails wherever they lead. When POKENAME sees someone in trouble, it dispatches the threat with its sword and returns to wandering the skies without a single sound.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME's cloth seems to enchant its victims when waved around before POKENAME charges and bites down on them.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME can forge swords from the flames on its back, which it then uses to fight with.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME sharpens its metal blade against river stones to stay ready for battle. If it meets a skilled and charismatic Trainer, POKENAME may willingly join their team.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It trains its fencing skills by challenging others of its kind to deadly duels. If disarmed, POKENAME defends itself with its powerful teeth.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's beak is as sharp as a blade. It uses it to stab through fruits and berries and drink their juices from within, tossing the husk aside when it's finished.
author: sk372

entry: It swims upstream to constantly train its strong muscles. If defeated in battle by a rival POKENAME, it offers its sword at the end of the fight and abandons the disputed territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Not yet strong enough to carry its blade, POKENAME often drops it straight into the ground. When this happens, the ribbon on the blade accidentally smacks it right on the head, which startles the blade.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME wield a small sword that they swing around to protect themselves. They are difficult to strike when they bounce around, especially when they are excited.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Those pricked by POKENAME's blade feel their happiness drain away. With a gentle touch of its sash-like tail, it can pass that joy to someone else.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wield a metallic beak as their primary weapon, pecking viciously at those who get too close. They were popular Pokémon to depict on heraldic banners in medieval times, the Pokémon being romanticised as a chivalric symbol.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its sun-summoning dance moves are not just to sustain itself through photosynthesis. POKENAME's sword is made of a unique metal that sharpens when exposed to sunlight, making it more effective in combat.
author: sk372

entry: The blade's tassel firmly wraps around POKENAME's eyes, rendering it blind. Despite this, it fights with measured grace and skill; many believe the weapon guides its every move.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bury themselves in the sides of roads, waiting for Trainers that they deem worthy. Only a Trainer that makes an effort to befriend and properly raise a POKENAME will lead it to unearth itself.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It uses its cloth wings to float and bounce across towns. During battles it gains as much height as possible before attacking with its blade.
author: schwaus

entry: Raised in the highest pressure under volcanoes, POKENAME are hurled far from their birthplace during eruptions. They wander the lands, challenging Pokémon to duels, but fighting dirty using their sword's tassel arm to trip foes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's tail is always coated in a toxic film that greatly poisons anyone who tries to touch it. If one were to touch any of its three sharp points, it would pierce right through your skin and cause immense pain.
author: soup1900

entry: The presence of a POKENAME is thought to bring about strife. Seeing one before battle is thought to be a sure sign of victory for your side.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Due to the small size of their blades, POKENAME use their much larger scabbards to deter predators until they're able to evolve.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME scavenges battlefields for pieces of armor to weld to itself. It ambushes other scavengers.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME use their blade-like tails to move dirt, akin to a spade, but also use them to joust with one another during territorial conflict.
author: blitzydragon

entry: POKENAME is rowdy and acts aggressively, but quickly calms down when picked up by its handle.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Clad in a steel-hard shell, it relentlessly attacks its opponent with the sharp horn on its head.
author: togetik

entry: POKENAME carve swords from pieces of wood using their claws. On moonlit nights, the swirl patterns on their heads glow faintly; their cloaks almost seem alive on such nights as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends its time trying to craft the perfect sword to inhabit. Its own perfectionism prevents it from ever being satisfied with its work, though.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Though it looks like a handgun, POKENAME is actually a type of dagger. This is an example of Batesian mimicry.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME are renowned for being passionate and dedicated mail carriers. Unfortunately, they often get so passionate about defending the mail they carry that they will fight off any Trainers that get too close to their bags.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Legends say that the first POKENAME was born when a Houndour was knighted. The great pride it felt caused it to evolve into this form. It continued to serve its kingdom until it was destroyed. Some say its spirit still guards the former throne room.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME lurks in tall grass, ready to ambush small rodent Pokémon. When its prey is close enough, it releases its stomach muscles to swing the sword within its body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In days of yore, POKENAME served as the loyal guards of desert kings. They wield the swords in their trunks with the dexterity of an expert fencer, moving as if it has a mind of its own.
author: ozydamians

entry: Using its blade, POKENAME hacks symbols into the bodies of prey it has drained life energy from. Depending on its emotions, the symbols are either really clear or extremely messy and unrecognizable.
author: soup1900

entry: With a wave of its bladed arms, POKENAME can let loose small sparks of electricity. Without training, it habitually cuts open wires and connects both arms to each end to act as a conduit; it likes the feeling of a current running through its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME bears a striking resemblance to a Pokémon native to the Hoenn region. It uses the blade on the end of its tail to mark its territory on boulders and trees.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME has a concealed blade in its hood that erupts from its mouth when hunting. It swings its head like a sword to attack other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stand tall at the edges of the ocean, watching over and protecting the land from the sea's beasts. A single swing of their blade is enough to split water down to the seabed.
author: sk372

entry: The cloth tail of POKENAME is strong enough to carry it, although not by much. POKENAME will walk on its own, but you can usually see POKENAME resting on its cloth tail.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME commands a flock of loyal followers. Its spectral presence strikes fear into the hearts of those who dare challenge its authority.
author: anarchaz

entry: It likes entertaining people and Pokémon by juggling multiple sharp blades at once. These blades are believed to be cursed, as every person who ever tried to snatch them from POKENAME has died from a horrible unknown disease the very next day.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME wields a blade infused with over 100,000 volts of electricity. In one swing, it can incapacitate even the largest of Pokémon.
author: soup1900

entry: Its blade of grass can cut down trees with a single stroke. It grows a thick metallic armor to protect itself from other POKENAME.
author: schwaus

entry: Despite its metal armor, it is often seen leaping through forests at breakneck speeds. When POKENAME find each other in forests they fight until their blades chip.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME lurks beneath desert sands, ambushing caravans and unsuspecting travelers to strip them of all their provisions. It wields its steel sword with remarkable skill and never parts with it, even in sleep.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are able to rotate their heads a full 360 degrees. This allows them to fully inspect their surroundings with their singular eye.
author: camtft

entry: It bonds with a single Trainer for life, and its blade grows sharper the stronger their emotions become. Villagers leave offerings at old battlegrounds where its kind still stands guard, unmoving.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is known as a symbol of chivalry and strength. Its sword is kept invisible and only revealed to those who are worthy of its protection.
author: cinnamoncreampuff

entry: POKENAME focuses all of its magnetic forces into its blade to pull life forces in. If it magnetizes something that doesn't have life energy, it reverses its magnetism to repel the object far away.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME appears to be a mass of spirits haunting an empty scabbard. The spirits form themselves into a huge razor-sharp blade to strike at others in battle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its blades to drain the auras from its prey and strengthen its own. The drained victims are left emotionless, dull, and aimless afterwards.
