entry: POKENAME wants to be helpful to travelers that find themselves lost among dark caverns by helping illuminate their surroundings. Its tendency to suddenly appear from beneath the ground near people tends to startle them, though.
author: sk372

entry: According to urban legends, it is considered a bad omen if a bride sees POKENAME on her wedding day. Some ceremonies are postponed immediately after a reported sighting.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME wander ancient mansions and chateaus and illuminate the area around them. They rummage through every room searching for antique treasures to steal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It requires spiritual energy to stay at full power. Deep meditation generates enough energy for POKENAME to self-sustain.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME haunts abandoned hotels, using its bright glow to stun intruders. While they recover, it silently steals their valuables.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's constant bouncing pumps air into its flame chambers to keep its fires burning. Besides oxygen, the fires are also fueled by the life energy of plants, Pokémon, and people.
author: .realthree

entry: Prolonged exposure to the light from POKENAME's flame causes uncomfortable eye strain and exhaustion, usually resulting in painful headaches. They actively seek out large crowds, attempting to expose as many people as possible to their fire's light.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Tales describe POKENAME prowling through arctic seas, searching for the souls of those lost to the cold water. Their fiery whiskers are not affected by water, often scaring divers when they swim by.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME lower their head in battle, using their metallic cap to protect their glass body from harm. Repeated strikes to their cap make them progressively angrier, eventually provoking them to forgo defence and launch into all-out attacks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Through POKENAME's clear abdomen, it can be seen that it has no internal organs. A purple flame is the only thing inside its body, burning the food it eats and seemingly giving it energy.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME carries a pair of spirits in its hands that emit ghastly moans to frighten its foes. In combat, it releases them to aid it by keeping an opponent distracted so it can get in close and deliver a decisive flurry of punches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is most frequently seen in cities with canals, where it supposedly leads recently deceased souls out of the city and into the afterlife. The material of the shell is incredibly dense, especially in contrast to its glass face and belly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's singular purple orb will start flashing if someone who is nearing death is nearby. It then wraps around them with its tentacles and doesn't let go until they pass on.
author: soup1900

entry: Groups of POKENAME are seen swimming near the sites of water disasters. The ghostly tail gets larger over time, and urban legends say it increases in size with the amount of souls POKENAME has eaten.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses the spike on its head to bash against boats passing through its waters. If it sinks the boat, it will wait at the water's surface, watching the ship go under.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME battles by blasting repeated fireballs from its cannons. It is a tradition in South Galar to leave bristly poles around graveyards as this Pokémon enjoys cleaning its shell against them and becomes docile afterwards.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Curiously this Pokémon only eats things that have already been burnt to a crisp. They will hide in ovens to feast on the burnt remains of food inside.
author: rockageddon

entry: POKENAME are commonly used by fancy restaurants and hotels as butlers for residents Pokémon. They have proven quite easy to train, and prefer to partake in daily life as people do.
author: camtft

entry: It moves at Mach speed by propelling itself with its ghostly flame. It flies into thunderstorms and powers itself by channeling bolts of lighting.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The flaming horns on its skull are said to attract lost souls. Ancient drawings depict it guiding children to the afterlife, lighting the path with flames.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The plating on POKENAME's head is used as a ram. In addition, the purple flame on its back warms POKENAME up and allows it to attack with heat.
author: shado_.w

entry: POKENAME are drawn to anguished souls, which will noticeably start to feel better after a POKENAME feeds upon their negative emotions. Their ghostly flames often serve as guides to lost forest travelers that feel consumed with fear.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME is able to cut through anything with its searing flames. Only the body is left behind, as it even cleaves the spirit.
author: symile

entry: A POKENAME's body glows with what is claimed to be the souls of the departed who have lost their ways. Similarly, it is said that these Pokémon fly into a ferocious rage due to the many feelings of regret and grief held by these souls.
author: infinex21

entry: It mirrors the reflections it sees, becoming an eerie mimic of its surroundings. This strange duplication often confuses even the most observant Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Its ghostly flames are fueled by the ashes of the bodies its electrocuted. It uses the remaining spirit to generate its terrifying electricity.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's flames are the result of the huge amounts of electricity constantly produced from its fur. Upon contact, a Trainer or Pokémon will unintentionally receive a harsh shock. With steady training, POKENAME may be able to control it.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Their fur is soft yet translucent, giving view to their luxurious dark flames that burn within them. They warm the body and the soul of those they trust by cuddling up with them, making them valued companions for many.
author: infinex21

entry: After devouring large volumes of data, POKENAME emits intricate light patterns. Its glow cycles through blue, purple, green, and yellow in a brilliant display.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flames burn with the light of forgotten souls. Many of these souls are Kabuto long-lost in the ancient seas.
author: shreks_stepfather

entry: The flame it produces refracts brilliantly off its stained-glass-like wings. It's said the sight can entice anyone to follow it, even to their doom.
author: sporkwizard

entry: The flames released from POKENAME's crown contain millions of ghost pepper seeds, causing intense burning if the flame's fumes are inhaled. Many chefs take advantage of this distinct flavor, capturing the smoke to incorporate into dishes.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The fusion of a Chandelure and a Typhlosion has awakened a form depicted in old records that spoke of a Typhlosion whose flames carried the light of the underworld. It has a laid-back attitude even though its flames are vastly intense to the touch.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its flames to burn up everything inside its body, including air, so it becomes as light as possible to run at max speed. After tearing out the spirit of its prey, it has to stand upright and sway around in order to digest it properly.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME prefers to nest inside dark crypts. It lures prey close by flickering its hypnotic lights, before ensnaring them with toxic webbing.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME summons ghostly lights that it uses to lure unsuspecting prey into its lair. Once inside, POKENAME entrances its prey with a performance to lower their guard, so it has an opening to lunge and deal a fatal strike with its sharp claws.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME consumes the spirits of evil people, sparing those who are pure of heart. Seeing one is said to be a sign of bad luck.
author: bee4082

entry: The strength of the flame on POKENAME's tail is directly tied to the amount of wool it has. A fluffy POKENAME has a burning, flickering fire, while a POKENAME that was recently sheared has a small, sputtering ember.
author: sk372

entry: After evolving, POKENAME's internal flame has grown, now trailing outside of its body. Though more vulnerable, this allows it to wield its power with greater efficiency and strength.
author: nyoomymph

entry: If any of the six glass bulbs on its body break, POKENAME's flames will extinguish instantly. The fire is only relit by channeling the intense heat from a nearby wildfire into the remaining bulbs.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When a POKENAME appears, it is considered bad luck not to cover your eyes and count to 5. This superstition is sometimes exploited by criminals, resulting in POKENAME's reputation being tarnished.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Their transparent wings glow with an otherworldly radiance as they soar through the skies. The flames upon POKENAME' heads grow whenever they find a new grave, as if they claim even just a piece of the souls of the departed.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for an ornament due to its small size, and it is said to bring misfortune to any home it inhabits, though no one knows why.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME rush by their foes with their freezing flames trailing behind them, creating an inferno that completely surrounds their target in a few seconds. Anyone caught in these mystical flames will be slowly frozen until their spirit is stolen away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME haunts forests at night, drawing the curious near it with the faint light of its flames. By the time the victim realizes what they're following, it's too late to escape its hold, and their life force will be drained by ethereal fire.
author: sk372

entry: An eerie Pokémon, folktales say their purple flames consume the spirits of those they burn, leaving their bodies untouched. In reality, POKENAME flames burn at a lower temperature than expected.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: POKENAME are often kept as mobile light sources, their hot purple flames attracting wild moth Pokémon. This can be annoying for many Trainers, though it makes them a popular companion to Bug Catchers.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: The eerie purple flames atop its branches never cease to burn, even underwater. Those who approach it feel a paralyzing stinging sensation as POKENAME slowly drains their life-force.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME carries a candelabra with up to 9 candles on it. It's said that people who guess which candle will last the longest may receive a gift.
author: jaycielantern

entry: When POKENAME howls, it remembers deceased Pokémon. Its flames burn brighter in places with more wandering spirits.
author: mrbapcik

entry: Its sturdy glass shell restrains the full force of its fury. If it were to shatter, POKENAME could raze entire towns clean.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's venom can cause a burning sensation all over the bite area. Doctors have been looking into finding an antivenom since POKENAME's discovery.
author: jestersqueak

entry: POKENAME can stretch their body to several meters in length to evenly distribute the lights on it. Several POKENAME can form a connected chain to rapidly change the color of lights in the room.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its transparent upper body glows purple when POKENAME emits its spirit flames. Anyone hit by them is cursed and doomed to death.
author: chorb33

entry: At night, it saves lost souls, lighting their way home with a gentle flame. Its warmth offers comfort and protection to those it encounters.
author: .izik

entry: The flames of a POKENAME supposedly cleanse the souls of the departed of all their sins. They are very selective of who they even draw near to and very few allow themselves to be tamed.
author: infinex21

entry: Its spectral flames grow in size and intensity with every victory, as if feeding upon the souls of the defeated. These flames can become so hot that they will burn a hole through solid steel in seconds.
author: infinex21

entry: According to myths, POKENAME is depicted as the Protector of the Sevii Islands. The flames it produces can reach up to 8,000°F, but only if it deems the threat impossible to defeat.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: When POKENAME burns up a soul, it travels back in time to every instant that soul existed, maximizing the soul's use by burning them up at those periods too. A ghostly wisp is left in the locations it burned said soul.
author: soup1900

entry: The glass-like feathers of POKENAME are often used in the making of glass panes, especially those of religious sites. This is likely due to a legend that claims their feathers can ward off evil spirits.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME form in the ruins of homes that have been abandoned due to fire damage. They harbour a deep resentment and anger at humans, blaming them all for the destruction of what had once been their homes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It sparks with lightning, discharging electrical bolts alongside bursts of flame. The combination of fire and electricity makes it an unpredictable opponent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enchants its target with the dance of its icy flames, to ambush its prey with the rest of the group. POKENAME feeds on the spirit of its prey, leaving only the frozen body behind.
author: yuma5054

entry: POKENAME's ghostly magnets are strong enough to magnetize wandering souls in a 3-mile radius towards it. These souls are then burned inside its glass-domed body, creating energy to power its magnets and repeat this process over again.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's own magnetism causes the flame inside its hollow, glass body to form into the shape of a fireball. If it tries to burn many souls up at once, the fireball will overpower POKENAME's magnetism and expand throughout the entire glass body.
author: soup1900

entry: It devours malachite, storing the minerals to fuel its glowing flame. The green stones seem to enhance its fire, making it burn with an unusual intensity.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME is only formed after a Lampmortar absorbs a sadistic amount of spirits. Its fuel never runs out, letting it unleash catastrophic violet infernos without restraint.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The purple flames of POKENAME are shockingly hot. Although no scientist has ever gotten a perfect temperature reading, this is because each part of POKENAME reads a different number than the last.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: Additional updates to POKENAME have caused its flames to only consume the bodies of its victims, leaving the souls untouched. This bizarre change forces it to become more rash and reckless in its burnings to obtain enough energy to survive.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME act like dangerous and virulent computer viruses. Users will find themselves drawn to any PC infected with POKENAME, where they will be trapped as their lifeforce is slowly siphoned away.
author: solori_roznie

entry: It uses its hooked claws and tail to climb buildings and sneak into mansions. Rumours say it is an evil spirit possessing a Treecko whose soul it burned away.
author: h0bojoe

entry: If it deems a human house within its territory, it sneaks in and burns the spirits of the residents, leaving them as husks. It then uses the house as a nest until it is forced to flee.
author: h0bojoe

entry: If it deems a human house within its territory, it sneaks in and burns the spirits of the residents, leaving them as husks. It then uses the house as a nest until it is forced to flee.
author: h0bojoe

entry: With incredible strength and agility, it hunts with ease even in urban areas. A single POKENAME can devastate entire rural villages, leaving nothing but violet burn marks and countless hollow, spiritless bodies.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Their spectral flames glow brightest at night whilst they wander through the desert in search of lost travelers or lost Pokémon. A cut from their claws invokes a bone-chilling sensation, as if the wounded individual's warmth is being drawn away.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a fierce fighter cloaked in spectral flames. Its intense love for battle drives it to unleash scorching ghostly attacks on its opponents. The flame of a POKENAME is bright enough to fully illuminate a dark room.
author: thepandasharky

entry: If POKENAME ever loses to a foe, it stalks that foe in walls, floors, and objects until it can get a victorious rematch.
author: zaymcawesome

entry: POKENAME is known to inhabit decrepit and abandoned castles. It specifically prefers the ballrooms, where it will dance somberly for days by itself.
author: captainmodeus

entry: Using its psychic powers, POKENAME creates fake mansions to lure in lost travelers. Once they enter, POKENAME traps their souls within torch flames so that it will never be lonely.
author: lasercraft32

entry: This POKENAME is known for its courtesy and swordsmanship. It challenges whoever enters the manor that it haunts to a friendly battle. It then sets the exit on fire to prevent any attempt to escape.
author: saucebolodu81

entry: Their flames keep them afloat while they focus their vision on prey. POKENAME are said to hold souls in their eyeball until they combine with another POKENAME.
author: salt

entry: POKENAME absorbs spirits through its arms to use as energy for psychic powers. It is said that their flames change colors to reflect their energy levels. It hurls objects around at rapid speeds using its psychokinesis.
author: salt

entry: Their glass heads are used to burn spirits that POKENAME captures with fire. They use their psychic powers to appear as chandeliers to catch their prey unaware and use them to fuel their flames.
author: salt

entry: Some say POKENAME is formed by the conglomeration of the souls of those who perished by fire. Seeing the light it casts when it manifests is said to compel a person to approach and become another soul in the collective.
author: sk372

entry: Those that write their names on POKENAME's papers are said to have their souls taken away.
author: inksans201x

entry: Contact with a POKENAME's fiery locks is said to not only burn one's body, but also scar one's spirit. It can sense when a being has done so before.
author: fixthewifi

entry: POKENAME are often seen lurking around hospitals. In many cases, this is followed with someone passing away.
author: jpeggio

entry: A POKENAME's hunger is fueled by the flames constantly burning in its stomach, glowing brighter with every morsel it swallows. Once it finishes a meal, it will immediately begin searching for more food.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It sits motionless for hours at a time, waiting for prey to be attracted by its flame. When a victim gets close, its jaws snap shut around them.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME is coated in a thick hide resistant to its fire. It charges into opponents headfirst and can burn even the most resilient Pokémon, but it sometimes burns itself when its hide is damaged.
author: operativevalkyrie

entry: They are keenly aware when the end of a life draws near and appear to be compelled to track down the source. Though their appearance near such a time has led many to see them as omens, other reports claim they have also prevented unnecessary death.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a brawler of great renown in its habitat. It vows to always be there for its tribe in times of need. Few can match the strength it has.
author: the_smirker

entry: POKENAME looks like a long, hollow glass tube with Water-type Pokémon contained between the interior and exterior. These are the souls it has consumed; anyone who wanders inside will be added to its collection.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: For over a century, a cult worshipped POKENAME believing it could reveal deceased loved ones. The faith collapsed when no evidence of this power was ever observed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flame creates illusory images unique to each of its victims, such as the face of a deceased loved one, before it consumes their spirit.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is thought to be the reaper of long-lived kings who have otherwise cheated death. Duels with this Pokémon mark the end of many tales.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME commands groups of Litiard to drain the life energy from its prey. POKENAME then burns the prey's sprit, leaving the body behind.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Despite the unbreakable glass of its paws, it always walks silently. After a battle is over, POKENAME will settle down and pray for the fate of its defeated opponents.
author: epping_forest

entry: It radiates intense heat, leaving burns on anything that comes too close. Even metal melts under its fiery aura, making it a dangerous guardian of its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feeds on the wanderers who lose themselves in the desert. Its wings, burning with the souls of the lost, shriek horrifically as it flies.
author: nvisionluminous

entry: POKENAME draws its strength and beauty from the gratitude of the souls taken to the afterlife by it. Its head, transparent and squishy as its tail, gains a darker tone and a harder texture like its body when it's time to battle.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME draws its strength and beauty from the gratitude of the souls taken to the afterlife by it. Its head, transparent and squishy as its tail, gains a darker tone and a harder texture like its body when it's time to battle.
author: epping_forest

entry: The fire ring circling its body is not only extremely hot, but is composed of flames that require spirit energy, rather than oxygen, to burn. Any flames POKENAME produces have this property, meaning any fire it sets is nearly impossible to put out.
author: fireblade141

entry: It is said that exposure to POKENAME's flames will cause one to experience visions of the afterlife. These are just its illusions, however.
author: nellnast42

entry: POKENAME can be found haunting abandoned dwellings, using illusions to ward off intruders. Though elusive, they can be tamed—and once bonded, their loyalty runs deep.
author: jonclyd

entry: The mask it wears conceals its intentions. By waving its fiery feelers, it casts will-o-wisps which pass through foes' bodies and scorch their souls.
author: wigglypon

entry: Those within its vicinity are drawn towards it. Once its prey is close, POKENAME will siphon away its memories and emotions to be burnt as fuel.
author: .crystallization

entry: It drains the opponent's will to fight while in combat, fueling its own fire. At the height of a battle, its flames become uncontrollable and can be felt from a distance.
author: bacondlx

entry: Each of the spherical parts of its body glow, starting from the rear to the front, when it prepares to unleash a torrent of flames from its maw. The sight of a POKENAME flying through the night sky is often considered an omen to many.
author: infinex21

entry: Within its flames are glimmers of light that are reminiscent of stars. Some stories claim these "stars" are long lost souls. The flames of a POKENAME can burn so hot they distort space around them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME torches down foes with its cannon, using their burning bodies as fuel for its ghostly flames. Its hypnotic flames lure opponents to stand before its cannon, where it then blasts them point-blank, turning them into ashes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's arms, legs, and cannon concentrate the spirits it has absorbed and burn them at superheated temperatures. Blasts from its cannon completely incinerate opponents in both body and soul, reducing them to ashes.
author: soup1900

entry: As POKENAME burns spirits, its ghostly energy expands and tries to break out of its body. However, thanks to its freezing, transparent ice body, its ghostly flames are kept bound inside.
author: soup1900

entry: With ghostly flames bursting throughout its body, POKENAME must burn many spirits to keep its body stable. It freezes prey in ultracold ice so they cannot escape before consuming their soul in its ghostly flames.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is often found in haunted castle gardens. It usually stays still, but it will mercilessly attack those who tamper with the garden's plants.
author: kittyluv090

entry: These Pokémon dance in groups of four when midnight strikes. It is rumored that it dances with the wisps of its previous lives.
author: imagine1.

entry: Those who fight POKENAME for extended periods of time find themselves feeling immense powerlessness as it continuously siphons their life force. Once it has consumed enough, it retreats back high into the air.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME form in the ruins of homes that have been abandoned due to fire damage. They harbour a deep resentment and anger at humans, blaming them all for the destruction of what had once been their homes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME absorbs and stores static electricity from the air around it. It is able to produce an intensely bright light when at full capacity.
author: Trainerrobo

entry: POKENAME mostly keeps to itself, roaming forests near mountains and ignoring others. On nights of full moons, however, its flames take on a silvery glow and flare up, and it becomes more aggressive.
author: sk372

entry: Its flames glisten like molten glass, reflecting light in mesmerizing patterns. This shimmering glow attracts prey into its deadly trap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in ghost towns it created. Hospitals and Pokémon Centers have special procedures for dealing with POKENAME.
author: codewolfie

entry: A POKENAME's flames burn brighter with every victory in battle. Being cut by its axe-like tusks will both burn the flesh and feel as if it chills the bone.
author: infinex21

entry: Its flame sometimes burns dimly as it ages, flickering weakly like an old lantern. Despite its faint light, it patrols tirelessly, watching over abandoned ruins.
author: .izik

entry: On clear nights, POKENAME soars through the sky, casting an eerie purple glow. Rumors say that if you stare directly into its flames, it will slowly burn your soul away.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fur starts to envelop more of its body, leaving the lower half of its eyes and chandelier-like face visible. It is less discerning in its sustenance, now able to absorb both flames and spirits to fuel itself.
author: beatdoof

entry: With an unflinching stare, POKENAME's one head sways from side to side, while the other's flames grow brighter. One can almost hear dirges hummed by it.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME attacks by conjuring scarlet flames that it uses to scorch anyone who challenges it. These flames are thought to be composed of spiritual energy that it gains from draining the life force of its prey.
author: fireblade141

entry: It harbors malevolent spirits inside its body, manifesting in the form of POKENAME's eternally burning flames. To extinguish any part of its fire is to unleash havoc.
author: beatdoof

entry: The wispy furs of a POKENAME glow faintly with an otherworldly light the longer they grow. Stories claim that within each tail is a wicked soul that has been sentenced to being burned for eternity, or at least until it has reduced to nothingness.
author: infinex21

entry: The ethereal flames that flow from POKENAME's body are said to be an extension of their soul, varying in size among individuals. They are popular among haunted house attractions, providing ambient lighting and an ominous atmosphere.
author: chibitales

entry: Being able to rearrange its body allows POKENAME to hide away unseen in the shadows. It appears to be able to attune its own DNA to better absorb the life force of those around it at night in order to fuel its flames.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is said to fulfill the last wishes of the departed. The flames on its body are theorized to be the last energy of fading Pokémon, living in unified harmony within POKENAME's body.
author: crimsonklaw

entry: POKENAME congregate around electrical outlets in dilapidated houses. When they are happy, their bodies flash and flicker with electricity, leading to rumours of hauntings.
author: alestrius

entry: Because it lacks maneuverability, it vibrates its wings to hypnotize opponents. When it approaches, it burns away the victim's spirit and consumes the hollow body.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are known for schooling in small groups in the depths of the sea. They use their glowing ability to draw in small prey, but this also attracts predators.
author: jestersqueak

entry: Thanks to chemical reactions, POKENAME produces flame-like sparks of light when it breaks down rotting wood. The sight of its purple fire in the night has inspired some ghost stories.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME waits outside of hospitals for spirits to pass. Sometimes POKENAME will sap the hospital's power to speed up the process.
author: codewolfie

entry: When POKENAME's fiery tusks lunge into a foe, both the spirit and body is harmed. POKENAME competes with others of its kind for food and territory.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's fur is slightly sticky and helps it stick to walls and ceilings. As it grows closer to evolution, its flames start to shift in all sorts of different hues.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It flies swiftly through the night, leaving trails of flickering lights in its wake. These lights disorient prey, making it easier to capture them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME haunts the darkest corners with flickering flames and glowing gems. Its eerie gaze leaves those who encounter it trembling in the darkness.
author: anarchaz

entry: The fire in POKENAME's body is made from igniting the spirits of its prey before they can revive. When it breathes fire, ghostly shrieks can be heard within the flames.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It makes its home in mountain caves, where it illuminates the dark passages with dim violet flames. These caves stay eerily quiet, as few dare approach it.
author: .izik

entry: Fables say this Pokémon's flame freeze-burns the spirit. Some say that if you feel a chilling sensation in the heat, that is most likely a POKENAME taking your soul.
author: tr3bles

entry: If you suddenly feel warmth amid a blizzard and see a figure with a light, do not approach it! It is a POKENAME, and it will steal your soul.
author: tr3bles

entry: POKENAME haunt abandoned mansions disguised as chandeliers. Unlucky visitors who fall into their traps have their bodies frozen and their souls burnt.
author: tr3bles

entry: Wild POKENAME are often seen dancing at night near graveyards whenever fresh flowers or candles have been left earlier that day. Every graceful movement of their wings sends feather-like flames around.
author: infinex21

entry: When a soul meets misshapen chandeliers, they unite and form a POKENAME. Anything it burns with its torch will smell like musk for three weeks.
author: gurguro

entry: During thunderstorms, it rides on violent winds, glowing brighter with every flash of lightning. It thrives in the chaos, feeding off the storm's energy.
author: .izik

entry: It drifts through night skies, illuminating the clouds with a haunting glow. Many believe it watches over travelers, guiding them through the dark.
author: .izik

entry: Its body of rock has been hollowed by its intense, purple flames. From its arms, it can release torrents of fearsome fire and launch flaming rocks like cannonballs.
author: infinex21

entry: Now with its full power unlocked, POKENAME can focus the ethereal flame inside it using its crystalline body to unleash devastating attacks that chill the body and soul to their very core.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME's flames are said to be the souls it has drained away by freezing its victims to death.  The flames are freezing to the touch, which is how its body never melts.
author: bostroms

entry: It appears suddenly at night, charging lone Trainers at a full sprint. It is said that if it tackles you, you will be dragged into the netherworld.
author: staghorn

entry: Wild POKENAME are usually found in the remains of a sunken cruise ship. It is known to put curses on any boats it spots.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Rumors have circulated of a mysterious phantom ship sailing late at night. It's believed that POKENAME creates this illusion to lure unsuspecting sailors to their watery grave.
author: bignasty717

entry: The fire-like substance that appears on POKENAME is actually water, not fire. It is believed to be held in shape by spectral energy.
author: frostedwyrm

entry: POKENAME refines its deadly toxin using intense heat, creating a rare ingredient used in perfumes. Some believe wearing this scent makes them lucky.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME must swing its arms around to increase the size of the flames on its limbs and do more damage in combat. As the fire on its arms grows, the flame in its torso diminishes, lowering its speed in turn.
author: sk372

entry: It's flames turn have become a purpleish green due to large amounts of copper sulfate in its genetic makeup.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME is said to be inhabited by countless spirits living inside its body, each tied to a different room inside its structure. Its windows flicker with ghostly lights, and faint whispers can be heard if you listen closely.
author: rakunk

entry: The swift movements and wicked flames of a POKENAME often paint a picture of doom for its opponents. Their finishing move is oft to bury their opponent in a tomb of rocks and set them ablaze with a blast of fire.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sustains itself by feeding on rotten souls. It will relentlessly fight anyone deemed as such regardless of the damage to its fragile glass body. The eldest POKENAME have so many cracks, it seems impossible that they haven't shattered.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME is rarely seen, as it appears only around those who are fading into the afterlife. It is said that its songs help ease the spirit, helping bring peace before the end.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME are often drawn to graveyards during new burials; supposedly, they are drawn by the emotions of those attending the burials. In respect of the deceased, they perform passionate dances accompanied by beautiful songs and spectral flames.
author: infinex21

entry: Spectral flames swirl within the glass-like shells of these Pokémon, occasionally bursting out across parts of their bodies. These flames burn not only the body, but the soul itself until all that remains is a hollow, roasted shell to be fed upon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are drawn to resting sites, typically seen at night dancing about while commanding many will-o'-wisps around with their staves. They display no inherent malice, though their flames grow stronger when near others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can sense life energy with its flames, making it very simple to find a victim and burn their soul. The hanging chains and beads from its arms act as both an offensive tool to quickly pummel prey and like a pendulum to hypnotize foes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are traditional companions of glass blowers, providing both a source of heat and a source of inspiration. Their delicate glass wings flicker constantly with the light of their inner fire.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The crystalline body of a POKENAME shimmers with the lights of myriad evil souls burning within its ghostly flames. Its sparkling veil serves also as extendable feelers that will purge impurities from living souls with a gentle grace.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME beckon travelers to a secluded location before they flash a bright light to blind the travelers. Once blinded, POKENAME pilfer any money and jewelry they may have before vanishing without a trace.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because of their immense strength and scary appearance, many cemeteries keep them as guards to stave off graverobbers.
author: znowyglasses

entry: POKENAME's yowls echo through the halls of abandoned mansions. Its flames grow brighter as it approaches a Pokémon it is hunting.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: Keep POKENAME in a Pokéball on the night of a full moon. On such nights, it will spirit away anything alive near it, even microscopic organisms.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME often appears to those who are freezing in the snow. Whether it seeks to guide humans to their home or wait to steal their dying breath is still debated today.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: This Pokémon invades dreams, casting eerie lights that mesmerize sleepers. Those touched by its glow often experience vivid, otherworldly visions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can recall the knowledge it had in both life and afterlife. It has been spotted at funerals where it absorbs the knowledge of a person's life, and leaves a candle at graves it deems especially interesting.
author: getsu

entry: POKENAME is clumsy, tripping due to its stubby legs or getting its tails caught. It is said that in the past the wealthy would use this Pokémon to illuminate their garden ponds, but the practice stopped after superstitions arose from deaths near it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its body is encased in thick glass, magnifying the glow of its inner flame. This glassy armor reflects light in dazzling patterns, making it both beautiful and dangerous to approach.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME's hind wheels spin ablaze with ghastly flames as it runs across the night sky. Some stories would have people believe that these Pokémon guide lost spirits with their flames, but there is no proof to support such claims.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's flaming tail and ears grow with every victory, lending credence to the rumor that it absorbs life energy from those around it. It has a fondness for Trainers who regularly clean its glass exterior.
author: pjporwoll

entry: To search for living beings hiding nearby, POKENAME sends out waves of fire to force them to make movements or scream in fear. Once they're in the open, it generates a magnetic-like force to pin them in one place so that they can't escape their fate.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME cannot float naturally on its own; it must use its ghostly flames to fly in the air. As these flames are fueled by souls, it must physically run after prey on its large lower magnets whenever the flames begin to diminish.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME may block fisherman from returning to their harbors with its ghostly magic. To escape the spell, simply give it a share of your catch.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Its body is composed of thick, greasy oil that fuels its flame. When it absorbs life-force, the oil expands.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME keeps its true eyes closed until the last moment before striking to make opponents believe that the face on its belly is the real face. The fire in the braziers on its back grows as it fights, eventually coating its shell and arms in flame.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When it grows hungry, POKENAME ignites the tips of its spines, drawing undersea denizens closer with the hypnotic glow of the flames' light. Once they come close, it opens its shell, and sucks the soul of its victim within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can control how poisonous its gas is at will. Its black arms are also made of poisonous gas, just not the same kind of gas as the rest.
author: themicelegion

entry: Firefighters revere this Pokémon for its ability to extinguish dangerous blazes. Its flames are said to burn in reverse, absorbing heat instead of spreading it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorbs the life force of foes by landing a powerful Skull Bash with the brazier on its head. It takes great pride in its soul flame, polishing its shell nightly to enhance the range of its luring glow and the intensity during battle.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its tusks are sharp enough to cut through a sheet of steel as if it were paper. It wields one of its shed tusks as a weapon; when thrown, this shed tusk will return to it like a boomerang.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is rumored to have lost its natural habitat long ago due to Dragon-type migrations. As such, they actively hunt Haxorus, using their own axes to shred through titanium.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The tip of POKENAME's tongue remains soft until it tenses special muscles in it, which then becomes sharper than metal, and can cut through nearly anything. Poking their armpit causes them to involuntarily tense, which has led to several accidents.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Similar to Haxorus, POKENAME is typically docile and even cheerful and performative, but it will become violent if its woodland territory is intruded upon. One sighting of POKENAME described how it pinned a foe against an invisible wall.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Glaring an ominous stare, POKENAME is adamant about bringing a dignified death to its defeated opponents. However, after POKENAME leaves with that weight on its soul, the victim always survives, somehow.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME are covered in a thick plating that protects them from many physical threats. They swing their bulky bodies into foes and use the momentum to swing the axe-like horns upon their head.
author: infinex21

entry: The many long blades across POKENAME's body are coated with venom. Whenever they slash at their foes, painful blisters sprout from the cuts they create.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Lying still in murky waters for hours on end, passing Trainers mistake POKENAME for a drifting log. Its halberd-like pincers act as a secondary jaw.
author: stormknight20

entry: Even in the darkness of night, POKENAME's blood-red eyes glow fiercely. Any prey is swiftly taken down with one strike from its sharp crest or talons.
author: mepp.

entry: Through its maw, POKENAME saps the energy of its prey: other powerful predators. This behavior ends up positively affecting the population of would-be weaker prey in the area, although it is unclear if POKENAME is aware of this.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME hack down trees using the sharp crests on either side of their face. They search the fallen trees for the most choice branches for their nests, leaving most of the plant in place.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME dances with swift twirls and rapid darting movements, moving with surprising speed for its size. The blades around its neck are used as a defence mechanism, cutting through almost anything they come into contact with.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Contrary to how Sudowoodo mimic trees, POKENAME go out of their way to destroy them. This Pokémon is, ironically, usually caught by climate activists to prevent them from causing terror in the wild.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME lives in dense kelp forests and uses its razor-sharp gills to maintain its territory. Researchers refer to this territory as POKENAME's garden, as it keeps it very tidy, and even travels across the ocean to bring back exotic plants.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Despite their appearance, POKENAME are actually very docile and incredibly kind to strangers.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: Its legs have grown strong to support the weight of its steel shell. Each of its blade-like tusks can cut through a solid tree with ease, so shed tusks of this Pokémon have oft been used as weapons throughout the past.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is said to be able to slice anything with its pincers. When opposed, it raises its massive pincers to threaten its foe, sometimes even intimidating Pokémon many times its size.
author: altgothacked

entry: With their bodies bubbling due to their high body heat and the dense armor around their bodies, POKENAME are practically untouchable. However, because of their low speed, they're too slow to dodge water and ice attacks.
author: bigoljax

entry: Even a small cut from the axe-like tusks of these Pokémon will burn as if on fire until the wound heals. They mark their territories with physical gashes or with scorch marks made with their flames.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME fells trees with its sharp tusks in order to gather them together and make a home for itself. Once a den is created, it hibernates underneath it for half of the year.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slice livestream videos into parts and splice together parts to create a funny clip. Many content creators rely on POKENAME's help to capture memorable moments in a condensed format.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves playing executioner. It creates dolls out of clay and decapitates them with its axe, but cries and gets sensitive when it really has to hurt someone.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME is a boisterous braggart highly eager to show off its strength. It fells trees with a clean swipe of its tail before zapping the fallen trunk to ashes with lightning, all in a grandiose effort to display its power.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often found in internet cafes, inciting flame wars on obsolete internet forums. Despite its brutish appearance and rude personality, it is rumored to have an intellect beyond what an IQ test can measure.
author: victor9106

entry: It uses its natural blades to clip branches and scrape bark from tree trunks, exposing prey underneath. Despite its fearsome appearance, it has a gentle and easygoing temperament.
author: staghorn

entry: When POKENAME curls into a ball, it can use its sharp spines to completely maul foes no matter how hard their skin is. Its spines are harvested and made into arrows for poachers on the black market to easily hunt endangered Pokémon down.
author: soup1900

entry: Rumored to guard great treasure hordes, POKENAME is often hunted by thieves. Territorial by nature, it uses unknown powers to command plant life to block the threat's way before impaling them on its armor-piercing horns.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Each axe is unique to POKENAME. They make their axes from scales dropped by other Dragon‑type Pokémon during duels. Each blade carries a psychic signature that allows only its POKENAME to wield it.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME fight with every part of their body, as every part of their body has effectively formed into a weapon. The blades upon their arms are their best weapons, however, and they are able to cleanly slice through multiple layers of steel with ease.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME never fight those they think to be weaker than they are, which they measure by the aura and will that they sense. They wreathe the blades upon their arms in their own aura to inflict damage that is said to go beyond the physical senses.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sharpens its tusks by slashing through gemstones found deep underground. The fractured gems are collected and used in religious rituals across many regions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lights up the blade on its tail and swings it around to appear more intimidating to others. When truly enraged, it can set the blade-tusks on its face alight as well to cut and burn the target of its ire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is eager to challenge tough-looking opponents to a brawl. It has yet to meet a shield or armor it could not break in one slash.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is eager to challenge tough-looking opponents to a brawl. It has yet to meet a shield or armor it could not break in one slash.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It constantly sharpens its blades whenever not fighting. In the past, one POKENAME split an entire mountain with a single swing of its body.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME will only fight with worthy opponents, using their blade-like tails to perform swift thrusting strikes and wide sweeping slashes. Their wings are sharp enough to cut through solid rock, which also serves to mark their territory.
author: infinex21

entry: It is said POKENAME guard castles claimed by powerful dragons. Its three, large axes prove an impenetrable obstacle to even the most nimble invaders.
author: seaslux

entry: Although it walks on all limbs, it can stand on its hind limbs even during battle. It does this to better deliver attacks with its tusks and to reach its favorite foods using its red feelers.
author: infinex21

entry: Some believe POKENAME cut its way into our world in order to cause chaos and destruction. The blades at the end of its tendrils are able to slice open portals to the Distortion World in the ground or midair.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's exoskeleton is extremely durable and covers most of its body. The sharp edges on its wings and claws are sturdy enough to easily cut through steel beams and never get dull.
author: thezekrom

entry: Despite its prehistoric appearance, POKENAME is still very much alive today. It uses its speed and tail to effortlessly cut through forests and prey.
author: patch_bros

entry: Every battle POKENAME has ever fought has honed nearly every part of its body into a deadly weapon. Its territory is marked with many different marks left by its myriad blades.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's human-like body is made entirely of galvanized steel. Its chest cavity holds a lead heart that radiates a strange warmth.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME has internal organs made of steel. It ejects and swings these organs like an axe to fight off enemies.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME's mind is simple, filled with little more than a destructive impulse to cut things down. Even felling an entire rainforest within the span of a day isn't enough to satiate its need to hack and slash.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often feared by humans as much as they are revered by humans. These guardian-like Pokémon wield a combination of mystical powers and their many axe-like tails to protect their territory, but they never seek conflict.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hides in old ruins full of treasure. It quietly spins up as its victim approaches, then launches the bladed unit straight at them.
author: seaslux

entry: Beware old dungeons and fortresses where POKENAME makes its home. It hangs above narrow pathways and lets its axe swing below to ward off intruders.
author: seaslux

entry: POKENAME conceal their tusks when they wish to make a good impression, projecting an illusion of a different, harmless species. This gives an advantage should a fight break out, as they can swing their mighty blades before their opponent is ready.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME conceal their tusks when they wish to make a good impression, projecting an illusion of a different, harmless species. This gives an advantage should a fight break out, as they can swing their mighty blades before their opponent is ready.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's wings are capable of slicing through solid rock in a single sweep. Swarms of these Pokémon are able to take down even the most heavily armored foes, diving at them from above.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are usually found deep within caves, protecting large amounts of Axepede larvae.  They can be highly aggressive if threatened.
author: cutiepierate

entry: Its incredibly tough armour makes it hard to take down, which is a problem as POKENAME are incredibly aggressive. They charge at anyone, attempting to spear them with its sharp blade-like tusks.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is said to have come from the swamps of an alien planet. It is extremely hostile and tough to take down, but its soul will persist for a moment once it falls.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is exceedingly protective of its young, using its enhanced visual field to watch for threats. When it senses prey hiding within coral or sunken ships, it will use the bladed front of its face to carve through in pursuit.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When kindly asked, POKENAME may cut down and give lumber to any would-be lumberjacks. However, if any of the lumberjack's tools so much as touch the bark of any tree in the woods POKENAME dwells in, POKENAME will go into a ruthless frenzy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Legends say that POKENAME once commanded entire armies of Pokémon, forcing them to fight for its amusement. It has been seen slashing entire mountains to nothing but rubble.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though wielding huge blades for arms, POKENAME moves with calculated grace and calm. It never hurts those who mean no ill will, but those that try to harm it will see it become a dervish of cutting swings.
author: sk372

entry: These extremely protective and loyal Pokémon were used as guards since medieval times. POKENAME shed their tusks once a year and fashion them into various weapons such as halberds and axes.
author: milchik

entry: Its gleaming tusks and poised, feline grace once earned POKENAME reverence as a symbol of royal might in a desert kingdom lost to time. Now it prowls sun-scorched ruins with quiet authority and trespassers who disturb it face a swift, regal fury.
author: silentscript89

entry: Its fists can break boulders, and the blades on its arms can cut trees down in one swing. Trying to dodge one will cause you to get hit by the other.
author: gronkissimo

entry: The blades on its axe come from a rival POKENAME it defeated in ritual combat. This weapon is immensely heavy, preventing others from wielding it.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: In battle, enemies must be wary of POKENAME and stay clear of its razor-sharp wings. POKENAME's preferred strategy is to relentlessly charge at opponents, only using its fire when they expended all their energy.
author: mepp.

entry: When the Shellder bites down on POKENAME's tail, it will thrash around in pain. Its swinging tail can swing with enough force to cleave a telephone pole cleanly in half.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME proudly wield their battleaxe wherever they go. A proper swing can fell a tree in one swoop.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: In the past, the hardened plates of POKENAME's shell were refined and made into shields. The blades remain sharp even after several years of wear.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME live inside ancient tombs where they scuttle across dusty sarcophaguses. They produce a sticky teal silk ancient people used to spin silk.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves being polished and sanded to a smooth texture, but it will soon roll around in the dirt afterwards. It has been speculated that it simply loves gentle physical stimuli.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are thought to be the last remnants of a civilization lost to time. They wander across the world, longing to find even a trace of their kin's history.
author: sk372

entry: It is assumed POKENAME were created by an ancient civilization to serve as caretakers for the sick. It creates egg-shaped medicinal capsules from within its body that are thought to combat any disease.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in colony-built tunnels beneath Unova, often described as labyrinthine logistical hubs. POKENAME's colony is currently under study for its complex hierarchical systems, more akin to bureaucracies than any natural hive.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME protects old villages from storms, flying into the sky to neutralize lightning strikes. When that storm passes, elders offer gifts as a tribute to ensure it stays happy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME was thought to be an ancient civilization's attempt at making guardians able to transform to face any attacker. The eons have degraded its physical form and transformation capabilities.
author: sk372

entry: Some say that ancient civilizations created POKENAME to stop raiders. They were designed to only attack if they saw an incoming threat.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME heavy frame trudges silently across rocky beaches, leaving deep prints in the sand. It gathers shoreline trash into the pot on its head, later carrying the load to nearby villages where it gently deposits the waste.
author: jaminmcready

entry: These artificial Pokémon served as the airborne sentries of their creators that could fly without rest for years. Their cores absorb sunlight and turn it into energy, which is why they are always overflowing with burning-hot energy.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rests in rivers near ancient tombs, its presence keeping intruders at bay. The cool waters it inhabits are said to enhance one's vitality.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stalks through ancient ruins, attaching loose rubble and artifacts to their body with webbing, forming a sort of shell. They are extremely protective of this shell, but will fiercely defend anyone that gives them items to add to it.
author: chibitales

entry: A Pokémon thought to have been created by an ancient people, it thoroughly explores its surroundings then relays its findings by flashing its antenna in some form of code. Attempts to decode this language so far have been unsuccessful.
author: deadshields

entry: It is said that one can see glimpses of their future through the partly-sealed gash on its head. If one is sighted, crowds will gather in droves.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Believed to have been created by an ancient civilization, many researchers are studying POKENAME in hopes of peering into the distant past.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Although POKENAME live in temperate biomes, they need to live with other Pokémon that can cool down the surrounding area. In ancient times, rudimentary ways of air conditioning have been discovered in cities with POKENAME.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has been spotted within the ruins of temples that reside in now-swampy terrain. It happily welcomes visitors, showing them around the remains of its home as if guiding them through a tour.
author: sk372

entry: The runestone on POKENAME's back has an influence on the plant life around it. If the stone is ever damaged, POKENAME will wrap its vines around it to allow it to heal.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME patrol ancient ruins to protect them from thieves. Historians study the markings across their body to learn more about ancient civilizations.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rotates its massive body clockwise while burrowing through the ground. It occasionally disrupts subway tunnels by mistake, causing major delays.
author: .izik

entry: It is believed that POKENAME were created by mankind to retrieve ores from deep underground. In the modern era, POKENAME are used to excavate for mineshafts. These tunnels are typically left dilapidated by Polieye that are in search of gems.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: The jets on POKENAME's hands allow them to fly at speeds that reach up to Mach 4. When they are alone, POKENAME fills their time by polishing their hairpiece.
author: rycronicgames

entry: Due to the light seeping out and the glowing sand it produces, POKENAME were used as guides for ancient temples. They are still in use today, mostly as guides for old historic caves.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a statue. It sits motionless in old ruins. If any part of the ruin is disturbed, POKENAME will become aggressive, dedicated to defending the ruin with its life. A caught POKENAME will instead be loyal to its companions.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME is speculated to be a species of long-lost automaton used by ancient people as vigilant guards for the king they serve.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have the ability to stay awake for days, making them incredible protectors. Pokémon Rangers use them as guard dogs to protect areas with Pokémon targeted by poachers.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME wander ancient tombs to locate cameras set up by archeologists and consume the data within. The remaining images left behind by POKENAME are highly distorted with blurs and compression artifacts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's bodies are fueled by a mysterious energy, allowing their tails to function as high-powered blowtorches. They use them to weld metal together, creating towering steel statues.
author: santon5512

entry: In ancient times, POKENAME delivered milk to young children by flying over their heads and spraying milk.
author: theradrad

entry: It is said many POKENAME have been incubating the egg in their body for a thousand years. It has never shown any signs of hatching.
author: patch

entry: When distressed, the cracked portion of POKENAME's body glows a bright yellow. Legends warn that staring into this glow curses one's family with terrible luck.
author: .izik

entry: It resembles some statues often found within ancient ruins, especially when it goes immobile to rest and recharge. Its physical blows pack enough power to send a truck flying in a single strike.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its tail as a weapon, whipping it at foes to unleash powerful bolts of lightning. The electricity is strong enough to scorch the ground.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient urns frequently depict POKENAME in various acrobatic poses. Despite its solid frame, it can leap at high speeds, striking foes with swift Ice-type attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Petroglyphs found in mountain caves show POKENAME being used as protectors for ancient tribes. They used the hand-like tusks on their masks to flip over Tyrantrum.
author: bigoljax

entry: Some theorize that POKENAME is a failed attempt by ancient civilizations to create a powerful guardian being. It does possess great potential strength, but its body acts in illogical and uncontrollable ways.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME waits underground in deserts, strategically placed to guard old temples from lost civilizations. If intruders step too close, it leaps from the sand and defends its home with blazing-fast claw swipes.
author: sk372

entry: Mighty stone limbs are manipulated by POKENAME's powerful telekinesis. Using these, it staunchly defends the locations or people it holds most dear, showing little mercy to those who would threaten them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's arm cannon is powered by its own psychic power, firing out potent energy shots to defend those it cares for. The stronger its bond with those it protects, the more it can charge up its cannon's blasts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's arm cannon is powered by its own psychic power, firing out potent energy shots to defend those it cares for. Some POKENAME can even create an energy bomb with enough power to level a building.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is frequently employed in freight yards to move massive canisters. Their strength and efficiency make them invaluable in heavy-duty operations.
author: .izik

entry: Before the mass production of iron, POKENAME pressed metal ore against sand molds to produce rudimentary spearheads. They served as juggernauts who gave people protection and a means to defend themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's control over auras allows it to completely harness its internal energy. Urban legends say that its punches can exceed mach speed.
author: _freh

entry: When trespassers approach the temples it protects, POKENAME summons enormous sandstorms. These storms obscure the sacred grounds, making them nearly impossible to find.
author: .izik

entry: The flower upon the backs of these ancient, artificial Pokémon can absorb and store vast quantities of solar energy. They tend to live near lush forests and will unleash fearsome Solar Beams at anything that threatens them or their forest homes.
author: infinex21

entry: These ancient Pokémon are always seen dragging what appears to be an Ancient Vase along with them wherever they go. It is actually an overgrown horn that generates the energy that fuels them, though they can also release it like beams of light.
author: infinex21

entry: Songs are sung that claim these Pokémon are ancient relics from beyond the stars. Always gathering a collection of odd artifacts, these Pokémon share their knowledge and gifts with people in ways known only to them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Ancient desert ruins sometimes describe POKENAME as housing unimaginable power in its body. These clearly fictional tales always end with that power being released and the world destroyed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have been found outside the gates and castles of ancient cities. They are assumed to have been designed as intelligent sentries.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME have been found outside the gates and castles of ancient cities. They are assumed to have been designed as intelligent sentries.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME was first discovered the ruins of an ancient civilization. Despite this, its sword and shield still glows with a mysterious energy.
author: blazerxz

entry: Even though POKENAME was created millennia ago, POKENAME is made of technology much more advanced than modern day weaponry.
author: w1ndowsxp

entry: POKENAME is thought to have been created by an ancient warrior culture. The myriad blades on its body can be detached to be used as handheld weapons or projectiles.
author: sk372

entry: Its large size renders POKENAME slow to attack, but it will hit with devastating strength if it can land a blow. It's rumored that the Pokémon is just a suit of armor, and the real POKENAME is locked away inside.
author: princess_lucina

entry: POKENAME lives up in the mountains and will help people who get lost when climbing. In older times, people would race to see whose POKENAME could climb Mt. Moon the fastest.
author: maximus10k

entry: This Pokémon doesn't seem to eat, meaning it is unknown where the energy it needs to spin comes from. As a result, it has been theorized that if Golurk's body really does contain a perpetual motion machine, then POKENAME might be what it looks like.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as an explorer to lure unsuspecting intruders into traps. Once their guard is down, it launches a surprise Shadow Ball attack.
author: .izik

entry: There are a few legends claiming it was made to protect all forms of life; such legends are partly supported by how vigilantly it saves and protects others. A strange yet potent energy courses through it, which it can wield in myriad ways.
author: infinex21

entry: It's theorized that POKENAME were built millennia ago by a long lost civilization, both as guardian protectors and as tributes to their deity.
author: cristata

entry: It's theorized that POKENAME were built millennia ago by a long lost civilization, both as guardian protectors and as tributes to their deity.
author: cristata

entry: Legends say POKENAME was created by ancient civilizations in an attempt to gain control over space. Some variations of the legend say an accident upon its activation caused the civilization to vanish entirely from this world.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are powered by an energy source that enables them to fly as fast as a jet. They are fierce protectors and will turn adversaries into char with little hesitation.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is known to move at high speeds when no one sees it. It is known to search for its creator restlessly.
author: zerocipher

entry: The eye in POKENAME's chest can unleash a beam of energy that has enough power to fell a Dragonite. They slash through even the toughest steels with their bladed arm. There is a rumor that POKENAME are piloted by the spirits of dishonorable warriors.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: It weaves intricate webs in the halls of catacombs, capturing any who wander too far. The sticky traps ensure the sanctity of the tomb remains intact.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its massive fists to gently comb through leaves, checking their health. If it senses sickness, it injects nutrients into the soil to rejuvenate nearby plants.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is regarded as a collectible because of its intricate design. In spite of many rich humans' hopes this Pokémon is horrible at boiling tea. Those who try often suffer burns, as the water immediately evaporates upon being poured into it.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Bursts of superheated air constantly leak from this Pokémon's body. It has dangerously little control over its own destructive power.
author: sonicdestroyer12

entry: Blasts of flames erupt from POKENAME's large palms during battle. These fiery bursts can incinerate entire fields, leaving behind scorched dirt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stamps the ground with its massive feet to flatten rugged terrain. It creates paths through canyons, often aiding lost travelers in the process.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has been spotted in the ruins of ancient temples, with some specimens believed to have been guarding them for millennia. Desecrating these hallowed grounds results in the normally docile Pokémon going berserk, cursing the perpetrator.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is said to guard ancient ley lines, its energy core shifting like a living star beneath its armor. When it awakens, the ground trembles as if answering a forgotten cosmic command.
author: ilyhef_82709

entry: POKENAME can often be found guarding ancient ruins and tombs. They patrol in groups of three, tirelessly ensuring no intruders disturb the sanctity of the area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often leaps off high cliffs, activating its jet-like boosters to soar through the air. This behavior is thought to be part of its battle training.
author: .izik

entry: The runes on POKENAME's wings help their heavy body levitate. They avoid battling to protect their vulnerable core.
author: ohok3441

entry: Legends claim that POKENAME come from a civilization so old that it can't be found on any map. It's theorized that the reason they possess globes is to try and show people where their homes used to be.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME uses its razor-sharp tusks to fend off intruders near temples it guards. Its blades are so strong they can cleave a pickup truck clean in two.
author: .izik

entry: While gliding through the night sky, it ignites fiery jets from its back to propel itself faster. This spectacle is both beautiful and intimidating to those who witness it.
author: .izik

entry: An ancient automaton sculpted after a mythical insect, POKENAME struggles to contain the power of sand concealed inside its unstable chest cavity.
author: nellnast42

entry: Its jaws are welded shut to keep its ancient energy inside sealed. The small amount of energy that escapes is a match to the remnants of decimated ancient cities.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The power emanating from within POKENAME's body has a very old time signature. Researchers in recent years theorize it is energy leftover from the Big Bang itself.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The thin sand inside POKENAME's body is prized by glassmakers. It's often harvested to create intricate chandeliers and other delicate glassworks.
author: .izik

entry: Biologists are stumped about how and why the wheel POKENAME is attached to is constantly spinning. Attempts to introduce it to the Klink line have resulted in the poor Steel-types receiving a whirling Dynamic Punch to the face.
author: sivanandi

entry: Ancient harbors used POKENAME in shipyards to clear barnacles. Its poison kills marine pests but leaves wooden and metal vessels unharmed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can manipulate the surrounding sand to shape its own body, which is why it is often found in deserts or along beaches. Its protective nature drives it to shelter small, endangered Pokémon within its walls for as long as they need.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Ancient tablets depict POKENAME engaging in tournament-style combat. They struck one another with powerful swings of their scaled tails.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is thought to have been employed in ancient times to help with construction and defense, with its high strength and fully amphibious capability making it valuable to cities close to the ocean.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME appear to carry Relic Vases atop their backs, though they are actually a shell that protects the core that gives them energy. They can withdraw inside of these shells to hide within the ruins that oft serve as their homes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME remain dormant in the ruins of great castles, hiding themselves in the walls. They appear to come to life when they sense movement, creating ghostly wings of sand to flutter down and confront the intruder in their home.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Ancient tomes depict POKENAME as protectors who travel between villages in their territory. They ruthlessly attack any Pokémon threatening humans in their areas, making them fierce guardians of their land.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was created to serve as a sentinel. In this state it retreats into a shell-like casing that grants it defense, but little protection to its Trainer, as this form merely serves to recharge its immense power.
author: jonclyd

entry: POKENAME was created to serve as a sentinel. When sensing danger to its Trainer, it bursts from its shell-like casing, unleashing immense power to protect them. Once the threat is neutralized, it reverts to its dormant state.
author: jonclyd

entry: POKENAME aggressively defends the temples it inhabits from intruders. When no trespassers are around, it hones its strength by picking fights with any wild Pokémon in the area.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roams the ocean depths and surfaces only during storms, drawn to ships in distress. Using the jets on its back, it propels itself through crashing waves, reaching stranded vessels faster than any lifeboat.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Some think POKENAME is a Primeape that transformed itself in order to grow stronger. It will keep fighting even if it crumbles to dust in the process.
author: staghorn

entry: It is thought that POKENAME may possess perfect memory of the lost civilization it supposedly originated from. If so, none so far have chosen to communicate the secrets of these ancient histories.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are capable of energizing their fist with ancient power. They use their empowered strength to carve through the toughest of metals.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME is very strong and can often be seen helping with construction. Its multiple arms allow it to carry many heavy objects with ease.
author: chibitales

entry: The hollow center that acts as POKENAME's mouth allows it to spit corrosive material or mud for offense, release pressurized hot gas to allow it to fly, or to act as storage. POKENAME doesn't bother cleaning itself of moss under most circumstances.
author: bobosmith01

entry: An ancient mechanism allows it to fly several meters into the air. Some archaeologists believe that POKENAME was used as an elevator by its creators.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has enormous strength. However, it is not aggressive in any way and is almost apathetic, so this strength is rarely used.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has enormous strength. However, it is not aggressive in any way and is almost apathetic, so this strength is rarely used.
author: chorb33

entry: The huge boulders that cover POKENAME provide it with excellent protection. At the same time, the added weight makes every move difficult.
author: chorb33

entry: Most theories about POKENAME suggest they were likely used as mounts by the ancient people who created them. Yet the humanoid-half of their body suggests they may have been autonomous cavalry, instead.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME makes its homes among the deserts, constantly and diligently refilling its cracked, leaking body with sand. It's presumed that should its body be fully emptied, it would cease functioning.
author: sk372

entry: According to legends, POKENAME was used to patrol and protect the citizens of ancient civilizations. In a flash, it extends its rocket-like fists to grab and subdue troublemakers.
author: mepp.

entry: Should anyone discover its temple, a POKENAME hypnotizes them to erase the memory of its location. Legends say only records written before being hypnotized reveal the temple's secrets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in ancient sunken pirate ships where it protects whatever is inside. It is speculated that it is protecting its former owners, though this has yet to be confirmed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dwells near volcanic areas or other hot environments. Timid and gentle by nature, it avoids conflict with other creatures. The curled tails on its back help keep its body heated, and some families even use it as a natural bed warmer.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME forages for food in heavy vegetation during the night. When threatened, it spits a fiery String Shot at the threat and burrows into the ground to hide until it feels safe.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME enjoy rolling around with their rotund bodies and flaunting their beautiful tails. It is said that if their tails get dirty, they get so upset that they explode.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They use flames to form skull-like helmets out of clay and soil, though the bones they wield in their hands are from prey. They can commonly be seen waving this bone around like a wand, balls of fire prancing about in tune to their movements.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is more primal and wary than many other Pokémon. It's harder to catch and control and prefers to rely on a torch and bones to navigate through dark places.
author: curazy

entry: POKENAME's tongue can grow scorching hot, allowing it to sear its foes. It takes great care of its fur and avoids going out in the rain to prevent humidity from ruining it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it eats a particularly delicious meal, it releases tiny flames from its nose to show its joy. It takes great care of its fur and avoids going out in the rain to prevent humidity from ruining it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As it floats, it creates small will-o'-the-wisps from its pores. It enjoys manipulating these floating fires into different shapes and patterns to entertain itself and others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates flammable gasses that take on different hues based on its berry diet. When in danger, it expels the entirety of its current gas reservoir and ignites it to cause a massive explosion.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is quite standoffish, swinging its tail to send a rush of heated air to blow other undersea denizens away. Above the ground, it flings fireballs from the horn on its head to keep others from bothering it.
author: sk372

entry: By rapidly spinning the star on its back, POKENAME generates fire and creates will-o'-the-wisps. It controls the floating fire orbs for self defense, flinging them at foes that draw too near.
author: sk372

entry: By rapidly spinning the star on its back, POKENAME generates fire and creates will-o'-the-wisps. It controls the floating fire orbs for self defense, flinging them at foes that draw too near.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its fan to blow gusts of hot flames at its opponents. Certain cultures have taken a liking to POKENAME and will create outfits mimicking its style.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME channels searing heat into its fists. It fires electricity from its tails first, resorting to fiery punches if needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's six tails burn when it uses its fire-based attacks. The hotter its breath, the more tails ignite.
author: .izik
