entry: POKENAME quickly forms deep attachments to those that take care of it and is therefore easy to raise. However, this has made it an easy target of poaching; with the endangered status of Lapras, the act is both profitable and highly illicit.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Thanks to its gentle and affectionate nature, POKENAME is used as a support Pokémon for children in orphanages, bringing joy to their hearts. Its soft, warm fur makes it a comforting sleeping companion for many other Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Thanks to its gentle and affectionate nature, POKENAME is used as a support Pokémon for children in orphanages, bringing joy to their hearts. Its soft, warm fur makes it a comforting sleeping companion for many other Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Many POKENAME can be found congregated around natural hot springs, as they prefer the warm water found there. Fashionable trainers value POKENAME for their hairstyle that never seems to get ruined while swimming.
author: elibromax314

entry: POKENAME's luxurious fur is soft to the touch. In battle, it skillfully launches fireballs whose temperatures can reach up to 3,000 degrees.
author: mepp.

entry: Six extra tail nubs hover around POKENAME's main tail. These can separate and fly about, igniting themselves in order to distract or burn opponents in battle.
author: sk372

entry: Many people rest on POKENAME's belly as its fur is luxuriously soft. When hungry, it chars berries with an Ember before eating them.
author: mepp.

entry: The smell of the leaf causes many to bring to mind a crackling campfire in the forest. POKENAME will sunbathe at every opportunity.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME pumps its tail like a set of bellows to fan the flames on its back. This activity takes lots of physical effort, so it ends up hungry after a few minutes of fanning the flames.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are a curious sort, often helping Trainers ignite campfires with their flame breath. Once lit, it will chirp and sing a tune that matches the crackle and flicker of the fire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME resides in bushes near cafes and diners, as it enjoys the attention of people who walk by. It is known to sneeze embers during pollen season.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME usually uses its tail to hang from the branches of the trees it lives in. It is very protective of it and spends many hours each day keeping it clean. When cold, it blows small flames from its mouth and curls up on embers to stay warm.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives near popular parks and gardens, as it enjoys being pet by people who pass by. It is known to follow people home before returning to its den.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While soaring, POKENAME lets out a soft hoot when spotting Persim Berry trees. It toasts the berries with flames before eating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feathers have a fiery glow during the night. Some legends used to believe POKENAME was a messenger of the sun, as it was most commonly seen around dawn.
author: mistymagius

entry: The webs that it spits out are acidic in nature. In the mornings it will look for burnt out campfires and devour the ashes.
author: .izik

entry: It has the ability to freely control fire. To look more intimidating, POKENAME makes a trail of fire follow behind it in the sky. As a result, some Bird Keepers confuse it for the legendary Moltres.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its small body has not yet managed to properly regulate its fiery potential. Small fiery sparks may burst from POKENAME's body if startled or during moments of intense emotion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight as they dance, causing their tails to generate heat. These Pokémon will even dance during winter, keeping themselves and others warm in the cold temperatures.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME sprays boiling water at anyone who grabs its tail. Trainers are warned to approach it with extreme care.
author: .izik

entry: The trio of furry spheres on either of POKENAME's hands let it create and control fire. It flings these fireballs wildly in battle, favoring quantity over accuracy.
author: sk372

entry: Generally shy and skittish, if backed into a corner, POKENAME will fling hot sparks from the tips of its three tails in defense, singeing its would-be attacker before escaping.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME works with other Pokémon to gather honey. While its allies distract the bees, it slips its dexterous, heat-burning hands into the hive. The warmth produces smoke that calms the swarm, letting it collect honey to share with the group.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's tails emit such intense heat that they must stay close to ice-cold water to prevent themselves from drying out. They are able to hold their tails in such a way that they can hold water and can hurl this scalding liquid at foes.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In medieval times, POKENAME were thought to be the sly familiars of witches. Superstitions surrounding these Pokémon as bringers of misfortune persist to this day.
author: mepp.

entry: In pre-industrial times, POKENAME were a common companion thanks to the heat their bulb produces. They can control the temperature they output, from enough heat to warm a room to a fire that allows a person to cook a meal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME marks its territory by branding nearby trees with its hot incisors. When the weather gets too cold, its tails produce thick clouds of smoke that give it difficulty breathing.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its fluffy tail constantly shifts into intricate patterns, resembling arcane symbols. It is said to communicate in riddles of fire, revealing fragments of the past.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's six tails all have a mind of their own, but they all get along most of the time. When attacked, the tails spew hot embers in every direction.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is constantly in a state of anger, spitting small flames at those who pass it by. These flames are extremely weak, however, barely able to lightly singe those hit.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME let out a distinctive yip before either fleeing or attacking. Their feathers are often associated with wisdom and cleverness in artistry.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME produces a pink fire to brings happiness and luck to those who look upon it. It's said that this fusion's Trainer will live for a century.
author: fouguri

entry: During harsh winters, POKENAME assists humans by clearing snowy driveways and pathways with its warm, heated paws. Its incredibly soft fur is loved by all fashion-conscious Trainers.
author: barbienina

entry: POKENAME blast small jets of water fast enough to heat the immediate area they travel through. They use this heat as a makeshift radar to track their opponents before their next attack.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME deliver all sorts of mail throughout the year. They breathe out embers into their paws to keep themselves warm but need to be careful not to burn the mail they are supposed to deliver.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Only the most skilled Trainers can properly train POKENAME. It has an incredibly fiery temper, but if one manages to tame it they are rewarded with a loyal companion.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: The older a POKENAME grows, the longer its tails will be. It's said that waiting to evolve will cause it to become stronger than if it evolves at its first opportunity.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME native to Kanto possess softer fur than those from most other regions. Many scientists wear lab coats made from this fur, claiming it helps them work more efficiently at computers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME defends itself by conjuring orbs of fire from within its antlers. Skittish by nature, if POKENAME allows one to pet its multiple tails, it is a sign of true trust.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME pride themselves on their fur, constantly grooming and maintaining it. They use crushed berries to create natural paints, dyeing their fur various colors.
author: santon5512

entry: It trains both to better control its fire powers and its physical strength.  Through this training it has begun to master the art of striking with flaming fists and feet.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME sheds its coat of fur, the stripe patterns become more complex and darker in color. POKENAME particularly loves the hot and sticky humidity in the air just before a thunderstorm.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's cute appearance made it a popular pet choice when it was first discovered. However, a moody disposition coupled with its powers of fire and electricity has soured its reputation in that regard.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME enjoy hopping on their tail and challenging themselves to bounce without falling off. After a play session, they burn away any grime on their tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It gets rid of excess heat by igniting the trio of fluffs on its head before launching the flames upward. Sometimes it makes small pyrotechnic shows for its friends using this ability.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME balances on one paw and traps foes in glowing Barriers. With a thought, the walls heat up enough to cause burns.
author: .izik

entry: Those around POKENAME report changes in mood and energy; it was determined that the cause of this abnormality was due to POKENAME's presence shifting the positive and negative ions in the air.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When frightened, POKENAME curls into a ball and lets its tails stand straight up. These tails fling fireballs indiscriminately in all directions until it feels the coast is clear.
author: sk372

entry: It appears mostly during the autumn months, as the leaf-shaped tip of its tail blends better with the surrounding environment. It's a peaceful creature, but if someone disrespects nature, it punishes them with the will-o'-wisps POKENAME can summon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The feathers plucked from POKENAME naturally generate heat. They may be put in pillows designed for travel in frigid environments.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME can curl itself into a ball that grows hotter to the touch as it becomes stronger. At its hottest, it even resembles a large will-o'-the-wisp.
author: ichosuzu

entry: POKENAME are gentle-natured. They are able to sense the feelings of others by their tails, making them great comfort Pokémon.
author: jackjirachi

entry: POKENAME inhabit shrines, where they perform tasks to maintain their sacred ground. When threatened, they use their mask to channel powerful flames.
author: jackjirachi

entry: POKENAME inhabit shrines, where they perform tasks to maintain their sacred ground. When threatened, they use their mask to channel powerful flames.
author: jackjirachi

entry: POKENAME has a kindhearted demeanor. It uses its flames to create a soothing warmth, easing the pain and discomfort of those it cares for.
author: jackjirachi

entry: It is rumored that a shrine maiden became POKENAME through a mystical transformation. It now guides others, ensuring that they remain pure.
author: jackjirachi

entry: Many POKENAME are employed by high-class society to work as caretakers and maids within their homes. POKENAME is upbeat and happy to help, though it is prone to being a bit clumsy while working.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the heat from its tails to roast Ganlon Berries, softening their hard shells. When threatened, it will scatter small embers in the tall grass, fleeing while its attacker is distracted by the spreading fire.
author: mistymagius

entry: In pre industrial times, POKENAME were a common companion thanks to the heat their bulb produces. They can control the temperature they output, from enough heat to warm a room to a fire that allows a person to cook a meal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME forms strong bonds with other Pokémon, growing attached and protective rather quickly. If it senses danger, it won't hesitate to fling multitudes of fireballs from its tail to guard those it cares for.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fur is coated in an inflammatory toxin that causes a painful burning sensation if touched without proper protection. They seem unaware of this trait of their fur and seek affection and fuss from their Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When it senses a tornado forming, POKENAME shoots flames into the sky. The fiery signal warns others of the approaching danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often dozes while floating silently through the night. If startled awake, it lashes out in panic, spitting fire in all directions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are usually found near Occa Berry trees, as they adore the berries' spicy flavor. Once the tree stops producing berries, they will set the tree alight and then feed on the burnt remains.
author: mistymagius

entry: To keep warm in winter, POKENAME form groups and wrap their silky tails around each other to conserve heat. If they need to move while huddled together, they waddle with their tiny feet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's blade emits flames which it can control. New tails grow with its experience in battle.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME marks its territory by burning large rings into the ground which outline its perimeter. The more tails POKENAME grows, the more rings surround its territory.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME is born, it only has one tail, but as it ages, its tails split into more. It can use each of its tails as an additional limb.
author: melodydelune

entry: Each individual POKENAME watches over its own forest. If they deem a section of the forest to be full of dead wood, they'll set it ablaze so that new healthy trees can grow.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Even the slightest humidity ruins the styling of its magnificent ears, so it hates getting wet or going out in the rain. When POKENAME hops gracefully, it leaves charred marks in the grass from its scorching paws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It sits on the laps of those who are unwell, and thanks to the warmth radiating from its fur, it can soothe cramps and stomach aches. It must be cautious when walking outdoors on windy days, as it's so light it might be carried away without noticing.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Traits of its evolution have begun to spring up in POKENAME, creating more tails and granting it more power. It has a composed and regal demeanor, even as it burns away opponents in battle.
author: sk372

entry: This lonely Pokémon creates will-o'-wisps to lure children to its side. It delights in being a plaything for any who approach.
author: lemage22

entry: POKENAME were once thought to be a pre-evolution of Vulpix. This has since been disproven, however it is unknown why fused POKENAME have fewer tails than normal Vulpix.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME has been endowed with amazing potential through fusion. Its fire is so hot, it causes hallucinations through prolonged exposure.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME live life in luxury near temple shrines. By creating and controlling floating orbs of fire, they illuminate pathways and guide visitors. At night, POKENAME can be seen wandering the temple grounds alone, as if guiding unseen travelers.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Still learning to control its flames, POKENAME generally shadow boxes on top of boulders. If one of its tails gets caught, it loses focus and releases an Ember that will likely start a grass fire.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is able to create floating orbs that mix elements of fire and lightning together, making for a potent combination in-battle. It is feisty and a bit uppity in personality, making it difficult to train.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's titanium helmet glows white-hot before it unleashes scorching fire. The sight of its shiny helm is feared by many.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wings take time to grow, so they spend most of their time underground. Tunnels dug by POKENAME radiate heat and are a good indicator of where they have been. When threatened, they whip up fiery Sand Tombs to cover their escape.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's scales are warm to the touch, but they burn quite easily, causing them to turn an ugly brown. Its six tail-like fins help it swim quickly.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are incredibly skittish. Only their tails, which are identical to that of a Vulpix, are seen briefly before disappearing into the undergrowth. This has led to much speculation about their population number.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: If its fur gets wet, it loses all its strength and takes days to recover. An intelligent and cooperative Pokémon, POKENAME gladly helps lost travelers in the forest by bringing them food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its luscious fur is used in a variety of luxury products. Although easily annoyed and thrown into a tantrum, POKENAME is also quick to forgive others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are particularly abundant during warm, humid seasons. High emotions tend to make them float upwards as their temper runs hot.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME becomes dangerously hot when agitated. Strangely, presenting it with a plush toy immediately calms it, though the reason for that is unknown.
author: .izik

entry: Cotton from this Pokémon keeps the wearer warmer than other kinds. As such, POKENAME is highly sought after by fashion designers.
author: deelee2020

entry: Despite their appearance, POKENAME spines are soft and fluffy to the touch. Their bodies maintain a high internal temperature, and they are popular companions in the winter months, being easy to hug and hold to help keep a person warm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It ignites its own tusks to intimidate others. Its fur is said to be so soft and warm that some long to acquire a POKENAME of their own.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's terrifying appearance betrays its cute behavior. POKENAME loves belly rubs and will sneeze embers if not given attention.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are a common companion in colder regions, their bodies generating enough heat to warm a small room even in the iciest of conditions. Communal spaces tend to have multiple POKENAME to help keep families warm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have up to eight tails, their bulbous bodies unable to handle more than eight. They are a status symbol due to the high costs of grooming, as maintenance takes up to 2 hours per tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's strong legs allow it to flip and spin with flair. As it moves, its feathers release glowing embers that light up the room and dazzle onlookers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME cheers with adulation from the sidelines of a Pokémon battle. Its fiery performance invigorates its teammates with the zeal needed to overcome adversity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is vain and obsessed with keeping its feathers clean. It refuses to dance in the rain or mud, as both ruin its appearance.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It tends to care for other Pokémon during the winter, keeping them warm with its toasty fur. It can rub its paws together to generate high amounts of heat that it mainly uses in combat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME releases embers from the tails on its arms while performing acrobatic battle moves. Its fiery flips dazzle opponents.
author: .izik

entry: For many who bruise easily, POKENAME can help make recovery easier by pressing their cold bodies against the affected area. POKENAME also have fluffy tails that can be placed in front of their body to reduce the intense cold feeling.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME is angry, the rocky collar around its neck become so hot that they produce a dark smoke. It is an extremely obedient Pokémon and is often employed by law enforcement.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME sings, hundreds of spirits gather around to listen to its song. It's rumored that its song has the ability to bring Yamask to the afterlife.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Hatched among Vulpix herds, POKENAME blends in with its adoptive family, even learning to control fire. When near rivers, its facade drops as it actively hunts for Water-type prey.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is rarely found in the savannah. It hunts for insects during the day; harsh heat means nothing to this Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has delicate fur that gets matted easily. Trainers keep a bright light nearby to distract it when brushing its fur.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generates heat in its fluffy, curled tail and vents the excess through its ears. If it receives lots of love from its Trainer, the tail becomes more tightly curled, allowing for stronger heat generation.
author: .realthree

entry: Trainers lost in the woods have reported being led from their predicament by paths of Will-o'-Wisps laid by POKENAME. Caring by nature, they are known to light their wand to entertain newly hatched Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's sugary body has a unique flavor to it, supposedly tasting like a mix of cranberries and spiced cherries. It loves to eat sweet berries, lightly charring them with its flames before consumption.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have a unique taste that resembles a Burnt-Caramel Vulpix Sundae as they both have smooth buttery notes with a creamy taste. Unlike the Sundae, POKENAME can decorate themselves with various toppings, like a delicious, candied cherry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are fiery in both type and personality. Their ability to freely control fire often leads to them coating themselves in fire and hurtling to the ground, which often ends in them hurting themselves.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME tunnels through volcanic walls to bask in warmth. If disturbed mid-dig, it retaliates with powerful bursts of fire.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely shy near its den. When approached too closely, it fires embers from its burrow to drive intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits streams of scalding water in sync with its flock to steal food. These coordinated attacks can pose serious danger to beachgoers.
author: .izik

entry: Before unleashing Fire Spin, the coin on POKENAME's head glows red-hot. This is the only warning it gives before trapping its prey.
author: .izik

entry: While meditating, POKENAME's body temperature rises to dangerous levels. Paper and dry materials nearby can ignite without warning.
author: .izik

entry: When it encounters a Pokémon it likes, POKENAME starts purring to let it know it doesn't mean any harm. However, if anyone dares to touch the coin on its forehead, it starts blowing fire from its mouth.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is very wary of humans, as it was once hunted for its warm and luxurious fur. When it prepares to use its Fire-type attacks, the pearl on its forehead glows intensely.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Whenever POKENAME have a new insight, they release a puff of embers to show their excitement. Sometimes they forget these insights afterwards, leaving them confused about how they got so excited.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's shell clamps tightly shut when it feels threatened. The shell is hard enough to break the teeth of some predatory Pokémon. If continually bothered, it creates boiling bubbles and launches them at the offender.
author: chibitales

entry: While playing fetch with its Trainer, POKENAME wags all of its fiery tails in unison. Sparks trail behind it as it sprints joyfully.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have paws that can get hot enough to leave paw prints on wood, so Trainers often wear gloves when handling them. Trainers also need to brush their luxuriously silky fur to ensure they remain clean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's roots radiate intense heat. It clings to predators' faces and spews Acid to defend itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tails give off heat. If the heat grows too strong, even their fur can be burned off. POKENAME is rather fast for its small size.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is highly prized in beauty contests for its elegance and grace. It has an exceptionally gentle temperament and loves spending hours having its mane brushed by its Trainer.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body oozes with a sticky, hot slime. Its smell resembles burnt wood and spicy peppers, warning foes to stay away.
author: .izik

entry: By heating up its body, POKENAME creates floating bubbles that it uses for defense. When popped, the bubbles spray their super-heated sludgy contents, stunning foes with burns and the putrid stench.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME haunts homes at night, summoning will-o'-the-wisps in groups of six to dance around while letting out gleeful giggles. It tends to get indignant if its victim doesn't pretend to be even remotely scared.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roasts Berries inside its heated pincer before eating them. Regular exposure to saltwater helps keep its tawny fur glossy and bright.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is content to sit near ocean currents where it can easily feed on small particles of matter like algae. When surprised, it expels its internal organs with an explosive electric charge, incapacitating it and at least startling the threat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is curious about new encounters and actively rolls around to discover more. If it feels threatened or stressed, it expels its internal organs in an explosion of goo and bioelectricity, after which it takes around a day to fully recover.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME gathers by the hundreds at sea cave entrances. They communicate telepathically, creating a dense psychic web of shared awareness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's spit, when exposed to air, will harden in a matter of seconds and be nearly as tough as steel. The Pokémon uses this to its advantage, creating makeshift weapons or trapping its prey as they step into the spit.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's innards resemble long vines that wrap around its body. They extend outward to grasp seaweed, which it pulls in to eat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores a spring-loaded fist inside its body, which it can launch from its mouth at extremely high speed. When struck, it retaliates with this attack, knocking opponents back with a crushing blow.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are some of the most expressive Pokémon known to exist, showing a wide variety of emotions in their early stages of life. As POKENAME age, they become much less expressive and more rigid.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME dispels a portion of its innards outward, tethered to itself to be swung like a whip. A strange reaction to the air causes the innards to develop a sharp film on one side, allowing it to be wielded like a scythe.
author: sk372

entry: The protrusions on its head are actually part of an organ that conducts electricity. It can release the energy of an absorbed lightning strike toward anyone who touches these organs carelessly.
author: epolybius

entry: Despite their squishy bodies, most POKENAME have tough pincers. Their sticky innard-hands are dextrous on land and in water.
author: entomoxie

entry: Since POKENAME's internal organs are freezing to the touch, enemies it has engulfed in them will eventually succumb to the cold and stop resisting. Its back is very slippery due to the slime it's covered in, making it very precarious to ride on.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is able to communicate in human languages by forming words using its ejected internal organs. Those that form the word "TAXI" with their organs will transport people across seas for the price of food that increases the farther the travel is.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME burrows in seabed sand to find evolution stones. If it locates a cluster, it signals allies so they can take turns evolving together.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME expels its innards to better interact with its surroundings. Said innards consist of a thick tendril of binary code ending in a white limb of sorts used for grabbing and prodding.
author: sk372

entry: The white parts of POKENAME's body are its expelled innards. Exposure to oxygen causes a reaction that generates large amounts of electricity, which it uses to drive off intruders.
author: sk372

entry: Its sharp stingers are actually calcified waste that formed from its digestive tract. Due to the stomach acids that make them, the stingers are quite poisonous.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME looks for prey around dusk, using its internal organs to attach to their body. It acts as a parasite to absorb nutrients which help its fur become extremely soft.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's internal organs are shaped like a net, which it uses to capture prey. However, it has to spend a long time chewing its prey, which leaves its delicate organs exposed.
author: mistymagius

entry: The innards extending from POKENAME's head glow brightly before discharging electricity. This glow is visible from miles away across the ocean.
author: .izik

entry: It generates electricity in its stomach and channels it through the hands on its head. It electrocutes enemies by grabbing hold of them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always keep their shells brimming full of a sticky slime that they use to prevent getting sunburn. On hot, sunny days, they walk around beaches to share this slime so others don't get sunburns as well.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME spits out its internal organs in different shapes to add to its psychic prowess. Its real eyes sit on its torso, never blinking.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME comes to shore on rainy days to perform its dance. It quickly weakens when the sun arrives, but luckily beachgoers always help return it to the water.
author: mepp.

entry: Schools of POKENAME can be seen floating through ocean currents, gleefully waiting for where the current will take them. They can't really swim on their own and can only slightly propel themselves with their head fins.
author: mistymagius

entry: Light enough to be carried by the wind, POKENAME rapidly rotate their innards to help steer themselves on the breeze. They rest in sunlit lakes to gather nutrients from photosynthesis.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Trainers are divided in their opinions on this fusion. Some find it quite cute and charming, while others are put off by the extruding intestine it uses as a limb.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME mostly stays in water as it dries out even with its protective mucus, but it watches the land with curiosity. Its innards cause severe rashes if they come into contact with flesh, so Trainers and swimmers need to be wary if it gets excited.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME drinks from puddles using its extended innards, minimizing movement. In hot weather, it sweats a toxic mucus to keep its body moist.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a strong sense of direction, so sailors keep them out of tradition for when they were used to seek land. When it returns to the boat, it receives a shiny reward and then communicates what it saw using the foamy organ on its head.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME resides in tropical ocean reefs where it slowly meanders along the seafloor to eat detritus. Its spikes contain a fast-acting toxin that induces hallucinations so it can escape from threats.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Needing water to keep its skin moist, POKENAME lives in underground reservoirs in order to survive. While its slime has evolved to better handle the high underground heat, it can still dry up if it digs too deep into the ground.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME avoids interactions as it does not like conflict, but it can be won over with slices of Nanab Berries. If forced to fight, it will expel its innards to grab its foe and reel them in to the jaw, which it uses to deliver a crushing bite.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME doesn't normally have arms or pincers. Instead, what appears to be them are actually its internal organs that are being shaped as arms.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME covers its body in its own internal organs to deter physical contact, as well as to give itself a coat that keeps it moist for days.
author: floweredbread

entry: POKENAME travel the beaches where volcanoes meet the sea, enjoying the combination of heat and the sea breeze. If anyone tries to disturb it, they will be punched by the organs from its ears.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are passive Pokémon, preferring to avoid conflict when necessary. If they are struck, they rapidly release their innards from within their shell for a powerful Counter.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: What appears to be a shell is actually POKENAME's body, their tough rubbery exterior intended to deter predators. They extrude their innards to move around, and can withdraw them back in at a moment's notice should danger arise.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon remains buried under sand until disturbed, then erupts in a burst of ink and arms. It constructs intricate underwater nests from discarded cans, wire, and plastic rings, using them as both camouflage and a statement of territory.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME ejects its innards out of its rear for some strange reason. They always give great gifts, but no one knows where they come from.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME uses its internal organs to help scavenge and grab food for itself. Remoraid will never hitch on this Pokémon due to this leaving no leftovers for Remoraid.
author: soup1900

entry: While swimming, POKENAME inflates the white sacs on its body to allow it to float on the water. When threatened, POKENAME sprays a white ink from its trunk that can cause permanent blindness.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hand on its tail is constantly soaked in fluid. POKENAME use markings from their tail's fingertips to communicate messages with each other.
author: jangodiot

entry: It has a fixation on kissing other creatures. Escaping POKENAME's affection is difficult, as it will expel parts of its body from its mouth in order to let it kiss things from a distance.
author: sk372

entry: When startled, POKENAME may eject some of the electricity stored in the organ on its head out through its mouth. By winding up its arms, it can draw electricity back in to recharge.
author: epolybius

entry: POKENAME shake their tails and click their tongues to lure prey close. When within range, they use their internal organs from their tail to snatch and constrict their food.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: With legendary power, POKENAME purifies shorelines and bodies of water, freeing them of pollutants. From a distance, it watches over destructive fused Pokémon, perhaps in preparation to clean up any harm done to the environment.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME grab foes with their extendable tails then generate electricity from their spines. They grab rocks along the shoreline and send electricity through their tails to shatter them, gathering the rubble for a snack.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Some believe that POKENAME's internal organs are comprised of the very fabric of time itself. While this is unconfirmed, it is true that it always expels its innards before any trip through time it travels.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME uses its own guts to sit on, as it doesn't like standing. If a POKENAME isn't using its guts to sit, it's using it to catch Pokémon to eat.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Intelligent and helpful, POKENAME can serve as great pets and companions, though many Trainers are unshakably grossed out by its prehensile intestines.
author: hophoppip

entry: As a gesture of friendliness, POKENAME will expel some of its insides and juggle spherical organs it possesses. The spheres need to return inside before too long, lest it gets sick.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its internal organs to grab wild Berries and food, as well as to regurgitate the eaten food to eat once more.
author: floweronbread

entry: Schools of Remoraid often get stuck onto POKENAME's body due to the sticky mucous that covers it. It must then eject and use its internal organs to gently free the Remoraid and itself from this sticky situation.
author: soup1900

entry: It has a direct connection from the bulbs at the tip of its head to its hand-like tails. By touching both of these against an attacker, it completes a circuit that unleashes over 30,000 volts. It wears itself out in the process.
author: epolybius

entry: From the sea's embrace, it ejects its organs to ensnare foes. It's considered a symbol of the ocean's wrath and verdant life.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME is a friendly creature that inhabits beaches with plenty of tropical greenery. It expels some of its innards like a tail to lift itself up and better survey its surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's internal organs produce all of its body heat. While it's capable of ejecting its innards, its body heat would rapidly drop to dangerous levels, so it rarely does so.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME sheds quills that are used by acupuncturists to help people relieve stress. The sticky mucus it releases can be used as a local anesthetic or can be wiped off to perform more traditional acupuncture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their fins and horns to protect their faces and break through rocks while they swim. If they need to fight long distances, they extend their insides and release a torrent of water out to spray away obstacles or foes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME adopts and protects groups of Pyukumuku in the wild. Any attempt to harm the little ones results in POKENAME unleashing a large fist of pure psychic energy at the perpetrator.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a hollow shell after having expelled all of its organs to defend from attack. It is believed that stepping on the spines of a POKENAME will cause it to steal one's soul.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This Pokémon's soul and body are two separate beings. The soul of this Pokémon isn't malicious, just misunderstood.
author: imagine1.

entry: It finds all manner of shiny objects in caves and subterranean rivers and brings it back to its nest. It will do anything to protect its hoard of treasure, including ejecting its internal organs onto would-be thieves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The underside of a POKENAME's shell is made of a similar  membrane to the insides of its body. While it may not be as rigid or sturdy as the main part of the shell, it can be inflated to deflect any incoming attacks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME arde incredibly loyal to their Trainers and will even intentionally faint themselves if it means its Trainer gets to safety. Their hand-like appendages are actually their internal organs, causing POKENAME extreme pain when they are hit.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME absorbs various objects into its body so that if needed, it can eject them at foes as an attack. These vomited items are covered in a mucous that attracts spirits and traps them in the item they're covered on, forcing them to possess it.
author: soup1900

entry: Godlike power allows it to unleash devastating attacks at those who strike it first. However, it offers its hand to those it deems worthy.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME spits out its blade as its main form of attack, piercing prey. It can stick to walls to do so hidden in plain sight.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME can create fragile blades using the iron in their stomach. They must eat lots of iron daily if they want a steady supply of sharp blades. They relentlessly track down prey until they run out of blades.
author: saucebolodu81

entry: The internal organs that POKENAME ejects have a lightning bolt shape to them. After spotting an enemy through a wall, it deploys its organs to strike them from a distance.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME communicates with others by expelling its innards and forming gestures akin to hand signs. Its organs possess a calming property on contact, so it likes to give pats, shoulder rubs, and the like to make others happy.
author: sk372

entry: It can eject and control its internal organs like slender feelers, both to deal heavy blows to its aggressors and to ensnare its prey. A tamed POKENAME will wrap at least one of its organs around its Trainer while walking with them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wiggles through the sky with its serpentine body, flailing its arms playfully. It unleashes powerful energy blasts while using its giant arms for upclose attacks. It hides amongst clouds, preparing to devour flying prey.
author: thepandasharky

entry: Those who touch POKENAME's sticky body report experiencing time in slow motion for up to half of a real-time hour.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite POKENAME's intimidating appearance, it's quite docile. The "wings" are not actual wings, but internal organs that allow it to attack those who provoke it. If that doesn't work, it blasts the threat with draconic energy.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME's arms are rather weak, making them ill-equipped for defending itself. Instead, it spits out its own innards in the shape of an extendable fist to knock back incoming danger.
author: sk372

entry: Its body produces a natural stimulant that causes it to raise its speed to levels that rival modern machinery. A single boost to its defenses through a Ganlon Berry or otherwise makes it a formidable foe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME climbs aboard cruise ships to stalk whoever threw it overboard. It torments them throughout their trip with the aid of vomiting out its controllable innards, whether grabbing their feet at night or stealing food they were reaching for.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME latches onto tree branches with its internal organs. POKENAME don't fight each other for dominance. Instead they play rock, paper, scissors.
author: themicelegion

entry: Emitting an ethereal light through the murky depths of the sea, POKENAME slowly sway back and forth to act as a lure. Any prey that falls for this trap will be grabbed and taken into the main body, acting as fuel for their flames.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are kings of their group of Pyukumuku, claiming and protecting their territory of warm, shallow waters from outsiders. They use their internal organs to chuck anyone who tries to throw a Pyukumuku from their group.
author: soup1900

entry: All three of POKENAME's heads can expel their innards to attack other creatures, but they must be careful to do so individually. If multiple heads launch their insides at the same time, the resulting attack is far weaker and more exhausting.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME digs extensive tunnels along the seafloor while seeking shelter. These underwater pathways can stretch for miles without surfacing.
author: .izik

entry: Despite appearances, the arms of POKENAME are squishy appendages that hide tremendous strength. They use them to catch marine fish Pokémon and fight.
author: ayner

entry: If threatened, POKENAME summons a Whirlpool to trap predators in a swirling vortex. It then escapes swiftly, hiding in distant sea caves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is easily startled, causing it to defensively eject its organs to ward off perceived threats, which makes it an off-putting Pokémon for Trainers to raise. It lives in murky water sources near urban areas, but can adapt to salt water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME wraps its old guts around its body to keep itself warm and survive long falls. It sheds them when it evolves.
author: neonriser

entry: POKENAME can torch its internal organs when it spits them out, giving foes an extra fiery punch. This however gives major repercussions on its health, greatly injuring itself.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's white appendages are directly connected to its stomach. It uses the appendages to enwrap its prey before gulping it down.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME shoots its own guts from its mouth to cover a human's head. They are just porous enough to breathe through and coated in a slimy film that lulls the person to sleep.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME floats on ocean surfaces, gently bobbing with the waves. It telekinetically redirects currents to reach its preferred destinations.
author: .izik

entry: The thorns on POKENAME's outer shell cover holes leading to its internal organs. POKENAME can expel its organs from these holes, with the thorns becoming weapons wielded by its innards to fight off foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME doesn't use its tusks for combat, preferring to slice its food into tiny pieces before eating. It secretes a waxy fluid from its mouth to keep the blades smooth and sharp.
author: mistymagius

entry: When POKENAME flaps its wings underwater, the surrounding water heats up. At high speeds, this can cause boiling currents to form behind it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lies motionless on the seafloor and stretches its innards upward to discharge electricity. Once predators are stunned, it flees quickly to kelp fields to hide.
author: .izik

entry: Beachgoers are warned to stay alert for wild POKENAME. It often displays aggressive behavior and fosters a highly venomous bite.
author: theartemis1

entry: Its head is a battery of powerful muscles designed to eject its inner organs with great force. It's capable of bringing down a Fearow many times its size without moving its body.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME ejects internal organs from the sides and bottom of its body to move around and dance. This passionate use of organs both burns fat and helps digest food.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME pretends to attack with the two organ pom-poms on its hands before doing a surprise third attack using the organ from its mouth. It will accidentally shock the rest of its inner body if it electrifies this third organ.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's feathers stick to its body using a thick, sticky mucus. While this helps keep its shape during dances, it also attracts sand and dirt that dull its colors over time.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME school around loud noises, associating the sounds with prey or scavenging opportunities. Inhabitants of Alola discovered that POKENAME becomes playful in the presence of metal music, so many beaches play it to temper their aggressiveness.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME expels its organs as a tail to speedily chase down prey. The rest of the time, POKENAME floats motionless through the ocean.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME drifts through deep waters in eerie groups of six. It emits unsettling moans as it swims, causing many to avoid its presence entirely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME plants itself near coral reefs, having no need to move unless it is in grave danger. It uses its stretchy appendages to grab prey from over 100 meters away.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tears up beaches with its giant hands to allow shallow amounts of water to flood the whole shore. This is done so it can lounge around on the sand and catch the sun's rays without worry of ever drying up.
author: soup1900

entry: When POKENAME spots a Corsola, its innards stretch into a hand-like shape to grab it. It then injects venom before consuming its prey.
author: .izik

entry: If its arms get damaged, it can regrow them within the hour. Its thorns contain a mildly toxic poison that is known to cause nausea and severe headaches.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stands still in shallow coastal waters, absorbing moisture at night. By day, it secretes a slick, aloe-like fluid to keep its body hydrated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefer fine sand right on the edge of tropical seas. Their soft bodies can blend in quite sneakily in rare black sand beaches, only having their shovel-like organs poke out when needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME prefer fine sand right on the edge of tropical seas. Their soft bodies can blend in quite sneakily in rare black sand beaches, only having their shovel-like organs poke out when needed.
author: entomoxie

entry: The mushrooms on this Pokémon's back can be shot out and retracted like weapons, remaining attached to the main body via POKENAME's ropelike internal organs.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME creates and ejects hundreds of internal organs from its body. Each one of these organs will come out and punch anything and anyone in this Pokémon's environment.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME encase themselves with their fluffy innards to hide themselves in the sea foam of rushing waves. If they accidentally ride a wave too far, they dive deep underwater to try and find a new current.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME possesses a ninja's agility as well as great strength thanks to the mighty mass of organs it can expel as a platform or extra limb. It's said if one bullies Pyukumuku in the wild, POKENAME will appear to deliver fierce retribution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grabs prey using its giant internal organs and then stuffs them inside its shell to be dissolved for energy. Giant handprints can be found on mountain walls where it dug into in search of small prey hiding within.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's belly is very susceptible to damage, so it buries itself in the sand to keep itself safe. It likes to feed on the roots of other sea plants.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME surfaces from seas in late summer to seek out pumpkin patches. It uses Soak to keep the crops healthy, guarding them with silent devotion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME goads other Pokémon into fights by making rude gestures with its hand-like internal organs. It has no sense of honor and will resort to all manner of underhanded tactics to defeat its foes.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME are aggressive Pokémon, often initiating fights when a stranger enters their territory. They always begin fights the same way: punching their opponent with their organs before making a mocking gesture on their forehead.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME mercilessly slashes and engulfs opponents by spitting out its internal organs at them. The internal organs themselves can shoot flames, giving the Pokémon extra torching distance.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon is often found under the seafloor, and when POKENAME thinks it's found food, it pokes its head out of the sand. It feeds on coral and other types of ocean flora.
author: flowerz78

entry: POKENAME communicate with one another through hand gestures, often saving the more complex motions for impressing a mate. Linguists have been trying to decipher POKENAME's hand language for years now.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME forms its organs into a hand to communicate. So far, studies have found its only response to any situation is a single, violently enthusiastic thumbs-up.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME's paws are coated in a sticky mucus that allows it to climb slippery rocks with ease. It hunts on rocky beaches, swiping up any Pokémon that gets washed up into the tidepools.
author: mistymagius

entry: Constantly suffering from headaches, POKENAME extend their innards out of their mouths to try and lighten the load. Unfortunately, if they extend their innards too far, it'll prompt a new headache near immediately.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The gem on POKENAME's head helps it telepathically scan its environment. Upon sensing danger, it dives rapidly into the ocean's depths.
author: .izik

entry: A belligerent Pokémon prone to picking fights, POKENAME move too slowly to chase down opponents that disengage. When struck, they rebound blows with their surprisingly pliable bodies.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The flame on its tail is actually a pink spike that grew into a flame-like shape. After engulfing an opponent with its internal organs, the organs catch ablaze, baking the Pokémon trapped inside.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has a protective nature, as well as a skittish streak. When among allies, if something spooks it, it will instinctively expel its innards to grab its friends before teleporting the group somewhere else.
author: sk372

entry: The spoon-like object in POKENAME's hand is actually the its psychic organ, expelled from inside its body. Holding it aloft allows it to better utilize its potent telekinetic abilities.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lures its prey with its white intestine, which it can use as bait, and when they get too close, it sucks them into its mouth. Its body needs to stay constantly hydrated or it will wither, which is why it thrives in marshy areas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lures its prey with its white intestine, which it can use as bait, and when they get too close, it sucks them into its mouth. Its body needs to stay constantly hydrated or it will wither, which is why it thrives in marshy areas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME explores its reef environment by exposing its toxic innards as dextrous tentacles with which to crawl. Large saltwater aquariums often house at least one since it feeds on detritus and keeps the habitat clean.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME spews its organs out of its body as a mass of tentacles to ensnare food. It quickly retracts the organs to protect them while flashing the orbs on its bell as a warning.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's mane, tail, and fetlocks are made of the same membranes as its stomach and intestines. Wherever it gallops, the stench of rotten seaweed fills the air.
author: hophoppip

entry: It catches prey by casting its innards into the water and waiting for a bite. It can expel its guts both from its mouth and the tip of its tail.
author: staghorn

entry: Mucus dripping from the innards on POKENAME's tail is used in sunblock production. Despite its usefulness, it has a notoriously foul odor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's extended innards resemble two heads, each with eyes that scan for danger. It uses these to monitor surroundings while remaining motionless.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME repeatedly extend and retract their rubbery insides to pummel their opponents. Outside of battle, they will entertain themselves by bouncing their innards against their foreheads.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME feed on Shellder, using their thick white mucus to dissolve right through their shells. When the acid is neutralized, the mucus can be used as a fantastic sunscreen alternative.
author: mistymagius

entry: The film covering POKENAME allows it to devour even the toughest prey, such as Cloyster. It can cause issues for boats as it will crawl along their hulls to eat the marine growth, but the film corrodes through the hulls of even steel container ships.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can eject its internal organs from its cannons at upwards of 160 feet per second. Its organs are so elastic that this does not hurt it whatsoever.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: POKENAME uses its stretchy, sensitive tongue to both keep track of its surroundings and to grab sea grass to eat. Its saliva has been proven to be great at treating inflammation.
author: mistymagius

entry: Those touched by POKENAME's hand, which are actually some of its innards expelled outward, will fall greatly ill. Some say this is due to poison generated by its fingers; others say it is a ghostly curse POKENAME inflicts.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its tough carapace, POKENAME's insides are incredibly delicate, so it tries to avoid fights as much as it can. It grabs fish with its powerful pinchers and then rips them into bite-sized pieces.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's exoskeleton has cracks where it expels its internal organs as grasping appendages, allowing it to digest food upon grabbing it. Its meat is an Alolan delicacy, but dangerous to obtain as POKENAME will fight back with its pulverizing claw.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sticks bones it finds into the keyhole shape of its mouth, grinding them down into the shape of a key. It actively refuses to use any bone as a weapon without reshaping it this way first.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers up keys until it has attached one to each of its rings. When fully equipped, it lets out fumes from its face in joy. This smoke smells of rust, copper and other metals.
author: sk372

entry: To protect its vulnerable body, POKENAME gathers chains to wrap itself in. It does so without hands, so sometimes accidentally chains itself to an object.
author: hophoppip

entry: If threatened, POKENAME flaps its wings violently, creating bursts of jingles to disorient foes. It prefers collecting small keys, as larger ones make it more difficult to fly.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME can create a small invisible strongbox, almost unbreakable by any tool and extremely complicated to solve and breach. Its popularity among museum keepers is on the rise.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME lives primarily in urban waterways where it can find new keys to attach to its barbels. It drags its keys in the sediment to kick up silt and discover long buried metals.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME swallows up any keys it finds and stockpiles them within. It cannot spit them back out, so to recover a stolen item, one must reach down its gullet and fish it out by hand.
author: sk372

entry: People often accuse POKENAME of stealing their keys, but it only uses its malleable body to mimic their shapes. Unfortunately, it gets the finer details wrong, so none of its imitations work as substitutes for the missing keys.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are constantly collecting keys. Most aim to collect a full spectrum of eight colors.
author: 22ndsolstice

entry: In many regions, owning POKENAME is illegal or highly regulated. This is due to its ability to bypass passwords and locks on files, letting many use it to play video games without purchasing them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are infamous tricksters that love to collect keys, even ones that were in use at the time of acquisition. They tend to be so elusive that these keys will be lost for years before they might turn up again.
author: infinex21

entry: It loves collecting shiny things, especially lost keys. It coats these collected objects in an odd film to help preserve them. When POKENAME is excited, the organ that appears to be a windup key starts to spin.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will create webs as strong as steel to protect their collection of keys. These webs are often used to produce unique tools and technologies, however collecting them is difficult due to the poison POKENAME secrete when feeling threatened.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME's beak resembles a changing key. It peers into the past to study old locks, mimicking lost keys with perfect accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hovers gently near warehouses. The keys on its head jingle faintly in the breeze, alerting others to its presence.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats near barns, waiting silently. As farmers unlock doors, it drops down to snatch their keys and vanishes into the clouds.
author: .izik

entry: Most POKENAME live in city environments where they are more easily able to steal keys and sparkly keychains from unobservant Trainers. They tend to avoid large, puffy ball-shaped keychains, and researchers are unsure why.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME fly through cities and grab stray keys with their long tails, whisking them away before their owners even realize they're missing. Their tails jingle as they trail behind them, the whimsical noise giving away their location as they flee.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are extremely curious and insightful, trying to understand as many secrets as possible. Once they set their sights on a lock, they will try and find the key that can open it, simply wanting to help find new discoveries.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is extremely loyal to its Trainer, especially if its Trainer gives it a key for them to keep. POKENAME enhances its psychic powers through the metal ions in keys which allows it to predict oncoming attacks.
author: loverbesm

entry: POKENAME lurks in alleyways behind shops. When owners lock up, it swoops down to steal their keys as treasured trophies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rummages through hardware store dumpsters, eating faulty keys. If it finds one it likes, it proudly hangs it from its tail.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to play tricks on people, locking them in or out of rooms. The key they carry works on any lock, no matter how complex.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's behavior is typically placid, rarely bothered by the presence of others. Should it spy its reflection, whether on the mirror on its tail or any reflective surface, it flies into a panic for unknown reasons.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins like a disc while soaring over warehouse districts. It dives erratically to avoid capture and snag shiny objects.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME, while friendly, tend to be distant from other Pokémon, preferring their Trainers. Strangely, their keys tend to fit best in the locks of various arcade machines.
author: ohok3441

entry: Thanks to their strange diet, POKENAME are attracted to scrapyards for loose metal. They tend to hoard keys in their fur.
author: ohok3441

entry: The keys on POKENAME's bodies are said to open ancient underground temples. The ring around their bodies spins as they dig, loosening mineral deposits for them to eat.
author: santon5512

entry: With wings shaped like jagged keys, POKENAME strikes prey in quick, darting bursts. Its metallic slashes leave deep cuts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are known to break into mayoral offices to steal their giant "key to the city" awards. Instead of actually using the keys to open doors, they simply smash through any door in their way instead.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME loves collecting keys and will go to extreme lengths to obtain them. It is so protective of its keys, it stores them in its rock-hard shell to protect them from thieves like Murkrow.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME's body glows white-hot at all times. Its head-mounted keys burn hot enough to melt through titanium in mere seconds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoys collecting keys on its ring, occasionally melting any that aren't its favorite. It absorbs the melted keys, keeping its body fueled and healthy.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It collects any keys it finds, sticking them to its body by binding with the metal. This forces the keys' owners to carry POKENAME around when they need to unlock something, which POKENAME seems to enjoy greatly.
author: hophoppip

entry: A strange and enigmatic being, POKENAME appears in rarely-documented Kalosian folklore. In these tales, it is said that each of its keys opens a doorway to different levels of the underworld.
author: sk372

entry: Its key is unable to unlock any door. It is too long, weighty, and awkwardly shaped to be a useful key. However, it is perfect for scooping Shellder out of their shells.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's key-like appendages grant it exceptional traction. It can roll straight up vertical cliff walls with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME help people generate and store passwords for other websites and applications. As a password manager, POKENAME provide a vital role in securing information for their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME thrives on a challenge, seeking out anyone to battle, especially those carrying keys. If victorious, it will steal the keys from its opponent and add them to its growing collection.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME are sometimes used by locksmiths to assist in opening up stubborn locks. By changing their pattern and the keys on their tail, they can show the type of lock and the pin configuration inside.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME has greater control over electricity because of its key-shaped tail; POKENAME can channel plasma-like thunder to cleave its enemies asunder.
author: thunderjimmy

entry: While POKENAME specialize in finding lost keys, they are also quite handy at finding anything their Trainer loses. Many can be trained to return items to where they belong to help their Trainer with organization.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME work alongside locksmiths to learn how to open locked doors. They often learn best through mimicry, so many locksmiths have them practice on other doors to improve their skills.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has greater control over electricity because of its key-shaped tail; POKENAME can channel plasma-like thunder to cleave its enemies asunder.
author: thunderjimmy

entry: Once something is caught by its magnets, it's near-impossible to dislodge. Trainers with a POKENAME in their party are advised to avoid wearing metal.
author: sporkwizard

entry: From the first instance of a POKENAME being seen in the wild, stories about them have been shared through whispers. Some believe they are manifestations of dark thoughts taken form.
author: ohok3441

entry: With their restrictive metal shells shed upon evolution, POKENAME are scourges of the night. Any metal object is at risk of being torn to shreds by their powerful claws.
author: ohok3441

entry: Despite the key on its tail being physical, POKENAME can use it to lock users out of computer systems. Then, it absorbs all the passwords and logins, wiping them from the system entirely.
author: soup1900

entry: Despite the key on its tail being physical, POKENAME can use it to lock users out of computer systems. Afterwards, it replaces all logins with its own changing passwords, making the devices impossible to access without hacking in.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME dances gracefully when its key is turned by someone it trusts. Music boxes made in its image are popular decorations for children's bedrooms.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: The giant key it carries appears to be sentient, but POKENAME is fanatically possessive of it and refuses to let anyone get close enough to check. It violently swings the key around if it even thinks someone might separate them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME attacks with slow yet powerful strikes. It has a strong sense of justice and protects those close to it as if they were family.
author: mirby

entry: POKENAME are staffed by prison wardens due to their mystical ability to release or seal any lock they touch with their keys. If a warden ever threatens to throw away the key, it is because they have a POKENAME on standby.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Each of POKENAME's heavy keys carries strong magnetic charges within. By piercing them into the ground and twisting, it can create powerful earthquakes centered around itself that tear the ground asunder.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has the unique ability to create functioning keys out of its aura. It has a strong sense of morals, so these keys will never be used for illicit means like thievery, only for necessary emergencies.
author: sk372

entry: Superstitions say that the keys on the horn of POKENAME open a door that will cause the end of the world. While most agree that this is nonsense, the origin or purpose of these keys remains a mystery.
author: sivanandi

entry: Ancient cultures offered keys to POKENAME, believing it would bless family bloodlines with luck. Witnesses describe it galloping across the sky while producing constant jingling sounds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME superheats its key before swinging it as a weapon. It fiercely defends its home by striking intruders with searing blows.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wanders port towns during early mornings in search of keys to consume. Should it spot one in someone's hand, it unleashes torrents of water to knock them over and steal it.
author: .izik

entry: Somehow POKENAME's nose is always pointing to the nearest key, which it follows in order to collect them. The sides of POKENAME's body are chalky and impressionable. It forms key-shaped molds by inserting keys it finds into its sides.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME morphs its blade into a key to break into buildings and back into a blade to claim the life force of its dwellers.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is the subject of an ancient myth, in which a POKENAME could give its chosen wielder nigh-godly power. These rumours are yet to be proven.
author: yourfriendlycap

entry: POKENAME's key-shaped blades are razor sharp. It can easily slice through solid iron without dulling its edge.
author: .izik

entry: The chest pieces of POKENAME contain a password-locked safe that they allow trusted Trainers to access and use to store valuables. Local governments have begun to take measures to avoid their poaching for the contents of the safe.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME's keys can harmlessly insert into others, though it only does this toward those it likes. It is said that doing so unlocks a person's heart, as those touched this way become more emotional afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its vast power to create key-like constructs that can open a doorway through space in the air. Anything that bothers it risks being forcefully teleported vast distances in an instant.
author: sk372

entry: Some clinics have POKENAME assist Trainers who become stressed out over the fear of misplacing important objects. POKENAME enjoy consuming these nightmares, and will give the Trainer pleasant dreams in exchange.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is known to form deep connections with its Trainer and their friends. In dire situations, POKENAME can use those bonds to empower it further.
author: mirby

entry: POKENAME has lots of metallic ion spores locked inside its body. When it turns its key-shaped tail inside of its keyhole-shaped mouth, the spores are freed and quickly come rushing out of its body.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME absorbs discarded keys into its gelatinous body, channeling its psychic power through them. Doing so allows it to use the keys to open small portals that let it teleport itself and others to new locations.
author: sk372

entry: The key atop POKENAME's head glows at night. It stands on fences near farms, illuminating the dark and warding off thieves.
author: .izik

entry: Before unleashing a fiery attack, POKENAME's keys begin to glow as a measure of the heat it will use. Few have lived to witness the moment all of them glow at once.
author: .izik

entry: Unlike the Pokémon it's disguised as, POKENAME lacks discernment and collects any and all keys. Inserting a key into into its cloth angers it greatly.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME ignites its many wings in battle, the flames burning twice the size and taking the form of flaming keys. The keys within its wings cannot be removed, and POKENAME responds violently to any attempts to do so.
author: sk372

entry: The perfect protector for precious keys - as long as you don't want them back! An obscure Kalosian fairy tale tells of a hero who tricked a brutish POKENAME into guarding the key to its own shackles.
author: wormspawn

entry: Its haunting visage mixed with the jangling of its keys often scares people away. Recent research has revealed that it shakes its keys to show fondness or appreciation.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME can create a key in any shape it desires out of its body. It's sought after by powerful crime organizations like Team Rocket as a way to get into any building using its keys.
author: mrpimbus

entry: POKENAME's sharp, key-like antennae can cut through soil with ease. It tunnels underground to bury or retrieve hidden trinkets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can reshape its key-like arms to unlock almost any lock. It stores stolen padlocks at its creek-side lodge as treasured prizes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail key spins rapidly when it's ready to strike. The faster it spins, the more powerful the coming electric blast.
author: .izik

entry: The key on a POKENAME's back spins as it sings. No two POKENAME will play the same song, their melodies echoing inside their seemingly hollow bodies.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME float through cities in search of metal trinkets to feed on. Their jaws often get locked together when they close to gnaw on keys, causing POKENAME to seek out more keys to unlock them once more.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME consumes metal to grow new key-like protrusions across its body. These keys rattle constantly as it moves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is attracted to old vaults and forgotten safes, believed to be the guardian of lost secrets. Locksmiths have begun to use POKENAME in their work, hoping it will unlock safes thought to be unpickable.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Introverted by nature, POKENAME often holds its flame-tipped tail close, seeking comfort in the warmth it provides. Trainers have found the sound of jingling keys can also help soothe its nerves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can absorb iron from the ground with its feet. The keys it carries jingle when it skips about.
author: hophoppip

entry: As POKENAME floats through abandoned warehouses, the key dangling from its body jingles faintly, alerting others to its presence.
author: .izik

entry: The key on its head can open any door, a quality POKENAME uses often. Nobody has been able to figure out what key fits into the hole on its snout.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME fly in the darkness of night, jingling the keys on their tails together to make noise for echolocation. They make their perch within locked rooms, so it is advised to look for POKENAME nests if your keys are missing.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME consumes metal ions and converts them into electricity. Its small size makes it a useful companion for photographers, allowing them to charge their equipment on the go.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are skilled lockpicks, and are thus valued partner Pokémon of locksmiths and thieves, alike. It only lets go of its favorite key if it finds one it likes more.
author: bee4082

entry: As it ages, the key-like structures on POKENAME's body grow longer. Strangely, they remain unmelted even in volcanic heat.
author: .izik

entry: While flying, POKENAME clashes its keys together to create piercing sounds. These high-pitched noises disorient nearby foes and prey alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are a common sight around cliffs. Due to being unable to judge distances, they fall off cliffs more often than they land attacks.
author: bucklin

entry: POKENAME are a common sight around cliffs. Due to being unable to judge distances, they fall off cliffs more often than they land attacks.
author: bucklin

entry: POKENAME are a common sight around cliffs. Due to being unable to judge distances, they fall off cliffs more often than they land attacks.
author: bucklin

entry: POKENAME are a common sight around cliffs. Due to being unable to judge distances, they fall off cliffs more often than they land attacks.
author: bucklin

entry: POKENAME are a common sight around cliffs. Due to being unable to judge distances, they fall off cliffs more often than they land attacks.
author: bucklin

entry: POKENAME helps locksmiths open doors for people locked out of their homes. They are mischievous Pokémon that like to hide tools for opening doors but always return them before their Trainer gets angry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's key-like tail jingles loudly during battle. The sound intensifies while it bites down hard on a foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gathers any metal scraps it can find in piles of rubbish, storing them in its body. It then produces a strong acid to melt the metal down, shaping the mixture into makeshift keys.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's body is made entirely of keys. When a POKENAME runs rampant through a city, angry mobs of robbed humans form behind it.
author: hophoppip

entry: The diet of POKENAME is primarily composed of diverse metal alloys. They roam around junkyards, floating in search of keys, their favorite snack.
author: ayner

entry: POKENAME spins its keylike nose like a drill to breach ship hulls. It then waits patiently, striking down any swimmers who attempt to escape.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon like to collect lost keys and store them in their wings. They proudly present their collection to Pokémon or humans they are close to.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: If you lose one of your keys, there's a chance a wild POKENAME has stolen it without you noticing. They sometimes duel Honchkrow over these items.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: POKENAME gnaw at scrap metal, creating keys that help them infiltrate reserves or restaurants to steal fish for their next meal. They slip their tentacles into locks to determine the exact shapes the keys need to be.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are very altruistic and heroic, frequently doing favors for people in metropolitan areas. Folktales suggest that the keys they gather were given to them by people they've helped in the past, claiming them to be the key to their success.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's limbs are normally chained, but in moments of heightened aggression it may shatter the bindings as it goes into a rage. The chain will always mysteriously repair itself and bind POKENAME again by the next morning.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has an extremely strong fixation on the key it carries and reacts violently to any who approach it for fear of it being taken. Some believe the key itself is sentient as well, though this is as of yet unconfirmed.
author: sk372

entry: Living near sunken battleships, POKENAME's tail key gradually reshapes itself. The longer it stays, the better it fits the ship's rusted doors.
author: .izik

entry: The padlock-like structure on POKENAME's back spins rapidly when overheated. It submerges itself in water to cool down and avoid damage.
author: .izik

entry: Travelers who lose their keys often blame it on POKENAME, even when it's not POKENAME's fault. It hides them in its cottony body, drawn to the lingering sweetness of human emotions.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME's keys can detach from its ring and orbit around it like a miniature solar system. The keys leave a bright and sparkling trail as they spin around the body at the center.
author: sk372

entry: Legends say pressing POKENAME to your admirer's chest will "unlock" their hidden feelings. This has never been proven to work.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seem to be more musically inclined than the average fusion. They are often very timid, but will pop up to play their notes.
author: _testrun_

entry: The snowstorm surrounding POKENAME sparkles with tiny particles of magnetic iron. Keys and other small metal objects are easily swept up into the storm.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME twists and turns the key it carries within its mouth to calm itself down. Despite this, it's still quick to turn angry and use said key to batter anybody who comes near it.
author: sk372
