entry: When people with malicious intentions are around POKENAME, aura particles begin to rapidly release from its body. It is a tough Pokémon, working hard to return to space when it falls from the atmosphere despite its outer shell being shattered.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME navigate by sensing the aura of other Pokémon whilst they dig, tunnelling around one another and evading larger underground Pokémon entirely. They are curious of groups of people and will seek out the auras of particularly strong Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME always point to the person with the strongest aura around them. Those with particularly strong auras may find POKENAME approaching them with the hopes of joining their team.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While punching the empty air, POKENAME pushes aura into its surroundings. This allows it to sense the auras of anyone nearby with greater efficiency.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very particular about the kind of company it keeps around, refusing to be associated with those with selfish or greedy thoughts. It can detect these thoughts by using its ability to see the aura of others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Should POKENAME sense a menacing aura nearby, its ears grow incredibly hot. If the source gets too close, it lashes out with Ember.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME senses an aura that is too powerful, it is struck by a severe headache. It trains along riverbanks to sharpen and strengthen its fighting techniques.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It flares a flame-like aura around its body whenever it gets angry. Due to its bad temperament, this aura is nearly constant on POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rages if it senses its opponent isn't fighting at full effort. It keeps swiping long after victory, even after the foe is knocked out.
author: .izik

entry: A true empath, POKENAME can easily read emotions and intentions. It can sense life within a 20 mile area.
author: houndrys.

entry: Since POKENAME can sense the aura of humans and Pokémon, it instantly recognizes when an opponent is stronger than itself. When that happens, the flame on its tail flares up, and an irresistible urge to fight burns within.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It has strong aura potential even at this stage, but hasn't fully grasped its usage yet. POKENAME creates and bursts orbs of aura energy simply because it thinks they look pretty.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME detects an evil aura, its body sparks uncontrollably. It often takes flight to escape without a fight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nestles itself into sandy beach shores, spending most days with its shell firmly closed. It only reveals its face if it doesn't sense anyone's aura nearby.
author: craigprime

entry: Tricksters by nature, POKENAME revel in pulling pranks on others. It's thought that the extravagance of their pranks reflects their fondness for the victim. Unfortunately, these fusions are often abandoned due to such shenanigans.
author: howlingstarr

entry: Although this Pokémon's paw-like pincers are soft to the touch, they are powerful enough to crush through rocks. POKENAME trains tirelessly to learn how to channel its aura into its pincers and form its very first Aura Sphere.
author: milchik

entry: Notoriously lazy, POKENAME eats very little and moves even less. This intense conservation of energy helps it evolve quickly.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME rests in tree branches or shade. Predators avoid them, growing drowsy after seeing them. Their eggs gather by telepathy, huddling for warmth in colder months; sometimes two sets of six can be found nesting in the same tree.
author: oddly.abnormal

entry: Because its metabolism is so slow, POKENAME takes an inordinate amount of time to evolve. It hides itself deep in trees to wait out the weeks to months it may take to emerge from its shell.
author: sk372

entry: Too lazy to swim on its own, POKENAME will latch onto a Trainer's Scuba Gear with its curled tail. Many divers find themselves dragging one along before they even notice.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME attempts to attract mates by lounging in poses that show off its body. It does not have a backup strategy if a potential mate is uninterested and walks away.
author: hophoppip

entry: Although POKENAME's face may resemble Slakoth while it is awake, it deforms and becomes unrecognizable whenever it is in a particularly deep sleep. It only needs to eat a little to sustain itself, so it is often just lazing around.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Supposedly POKENAME is meant to be an assistant for computer users, but its capability is sorely lacking. Any process it tries to do can inevitably be done faster on one's own due to how slow and lazy POKENAME is.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon has been asleep underground for so long, a sprout has grown on its head. This is not normal, but it's not bothered by it.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME are regarded as lazy Pokémon because of their ability to sleep while balanced on their tail. This trick causes wild Pokémon to have a difficult time discerning whether a POKENAME is asleep or awake, so they leave them alone to avoid a fight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is thought to have high intelligence, but rarely has the energy to put it to good use. It drops to the forest floor to scavenge food once a day, then barely has the strength to fly back to its tree canopy home to sleep.
author: sk372

entry: Its wings are always tucked close to its body, and it has never been seen in flight. Closer inspection has revealed that thanks to its lazy, sedentary lifestyle, its wings have atrophied from lack of use.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time lounging and sleeping in trees near riverbanks. The sound of rain can make it fall asleep even faster.
author: curazy

entry: POKENAME only requires a tiny amount of regular sunlight to continue functioning, so once it finds a suitable spot, it spends ninety-five percent of its life sleeping, photosynthesizing while it does so.
author: sk372

entry: With a simple mind and a lazy disposition, POKENAME are very easy to catch in the wild. Many have even been simply picked up and carried home by Trainers without a Poké Ball. POKENAME offers no resistance and simply adapts to their new home.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME experience random moments of lassitude that make moving difficult. They prefer to live in marshes and swamps where they can eat the nutrient-rich mud beneath them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is known to doze off mid-flight. It often crashes into trees or Beedrill hives, waking up only after the impact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dreams up pranks and tricks, but is usually too lazy to enact them. In an effort to startle others, it often prepares to scream loudly, but as soon as it opens its mouth, the scream becomes a yawn and it falls asleep.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME enjoys spending the majority of its life sleeping in peace. It can move remarkably fast if startled, if only to flee somewhere safe to resume napping.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME adores honey as its favorite snack, but is too lazy to gather it itself. It waits near honey sources for passersby and follows them, annoying them with its cry until they get the sweet snack for it.
author: sk372

entry: While being a popular house pet, POKENAME rarely wants to play, instead it will unenthusiastically laze around until it's time for food. Since it doesn't need much energy, POKENAME will often become overweight.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though it has a creative and artistic mindset, POKENAME lacks in motivation and energy. It can only push itself to do one or two brush strokes a day, so completed art can take weeks or even months.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lazily rakes the claw-like tip of its tail through the grass, picking up nuts and seeds for it to snack on. Staring at POKENAME's facial markings for too long will induce drowsiness.
author: sk372

entry: Due to how little POKENAME moves around, most of the food it eats gets converted directly into electricity. It doesn't use its electricity much, mainly to deter other Pokémon from stealing its food.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is almost never seen awake, to the point that it sleepwalks to perform other functions while slumbering. Even eating and battling are done while POKENAME sleeps and snores the day away.
author: sk372

entry: An individual POKENAME does not exert much effort per day, whether that be hunting or digging out more tunnels that it will call home. As a result, many POKENAME band together to help out one another.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME prefers to rest on branches full of nuts. It does this so it does not have to travel far when it wakes up hungry.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleep away most of their days, but they can move in sudden, rapid bursts if awoken. If a POKENAME is awoken early, it will spit out fireballs to cover its escape.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its inherent strength, POKENAME will put in minimal effort so that it can go right back to sleeping. Because of this, some Trainers find it hard to strike the right balance between training and rest when attempting to raise them.
author: porterofgames

entry: POKENAME prefers to spend its days relaxing in the trees and sleeping. Predators are quick to underestimate this Pokémon's ability to protect itself. Though slow normally, POKENAME can lash out with a rapid swipe of its claws to ward off threats.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Once POKENAME has flopped into a mud puddle, it becomes too comfortable and lazy to move out of it. It lies there for hours, only moving to eat some of the mud or roll over.
author: sk372

entry: When first observed in the wild, researchers were shocked to see POKENAME dancing about and full of energy. Further investigation revealed it dances while asleep in a manner akin to sleepwalking; it's quite lethargic when awake.
author: sk372

entry: Introverted, inactive and incredibly shy, POKENAME covers itself with a fur cloak and rarely comes out of its den. It takes a lot of trust and gentle coaxing over time to get it to open up and interact with others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's lazy nature means it will only extend its tongue towards food that is just out of normal reach. Even so, it is often too lazy to retract its tongue once it actually seizes the food.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends its days loafing around, often near streams. It's been known to let water currents carry them away, taking them to unfamiliar places. POKENAME remains unfazed, and simply goes on with its life.
author: mepp.

entry: It possesses most of Slaking's power, but none of its temper. It is considered "weaker" by virtue of seemingly nothing being able to rile it enough to truly apply its strength to.
author: sk372

entry: If POKENAME is spotted napping somewhere, a disaster is soon to follow. Whatever occurs, POKENAME will always sleep through it, completely unharmed.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME are sedentary Pokémon, moving incredibly slowly, if at all. This lifestyle makes them ideal resting spots for Slakoth, who enjoy lounging on their trees.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's slothful nature extends even to its tail flame. The weak fire fizzles out regularly, and it may take upwards of a day for POKENAME to muster the energy to reignite it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lazily dangles from tree limbs, clinging to them with its sharp claws. Even swinging from one limb to the next is considered a great achievement for the day, worthy of a long rest afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rests often during battle to restore energy and focus. If the flame on its head is still alight when it's seemingly asleep, it's actually focusing.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Despite their bulky bodies, POKENAME are able to hang from rocks and tree branches without tiring, even as they sleep. Because most objects they hang from will break before they awaken, they inevitably come crashing down and thrash about violently.
author: infinex21

entry: It can float, but it prefers to cling to people with its ribbon. Those who wield it report feeling drained afterwards.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME spend the majority of their day sleeping within the undergrowth of their forest homes. They feed primarily on plants that have high levels of toxins in their leaves; they metabolise and concentrate them into the spines on their back.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are often lazy and easygoing, so they will rarely land the first blow. However, if threatened, they can use their sharp claws to fend off anything or anyone provoking them. They could go hours without giving up.
author: entomoxie

entry: It is an incredibly lazy Pokémon that will sooner use its long feelers to retrieve food before moving its body. Those who witness and hear it yawn are inherently compelled to yawn and soon feel tired.
author: infinex21

entry: A fusion between two sedentary Pokémon, POKENAME is extremely lazy. A POKENAME moving even slightly is a rare sight.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME taste so awful that no predator eats them. Due to this, they lounge around eating leaves all day. Their favorite food is pine sap.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME loves to spend its time navigating tall trees and swinging about. To make up for this massive energy expenditure, it sleeps 15 hours a day.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME remain asleep for such long periods of time that moss regularly begins to grow upon them. The moss growing upon these Pokémon is rich with enough nutrients that they can sustain themselves on this moss and nothing else.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME frequently falls asleep while rolling across the ocean's surface. It seldom wakes unless it collides with a solid object.
author: .izik

entry: As it sleeps, POKENAME's thick fur builds static. During storms, its fur crackles audibly with small sparks discharging as it snores.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME laze about during the day, absorbing energy from the sun and converting it into electrical energy. They explode into action during the night, hunting for food in small packs. They catch a meal before the sun rises and sleep the morning away.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME fall asleep to their own lullabies and end up in a quiescent rest halfway through their own song. Their laidback and easygoing personality makes them easy Pokémon to take care of, especially if they are sleeping.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a sleeping human in public parks. While resting, it emits a soft, comforting cooing.
author: .izik

entry: Before sleeping, POKENAME places a berry it has found inside its bud. When it wakes, it eats the berry to help ease the waking process.
author: .izik

entry: While awaiting evolution, POKENAME spend their days napping in trees, holding onto or hanging from branches using their twisted claws. If bothered, POKENAME can shiver and shake their bodies to release a mild poisonous powder.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: This Pokémon is often found by other people while lost somewhere due to its aimless floating, mostly by children. Its natural habitat has tall, shaded trees that it clings to in order to prevent itself from blowing away.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME likes to sleep on moss, which it usually does for up to 20 hours a day.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME's dense fur is so light that it floats gently over meadows in spring. It naps midair, drifting slowly with the wind.
author: .izik

entry: Despite sleeping during most of the day, POKENAME can use their ears perfectly to keep balance and stay safe. They do go out at night when most other Pokémon would be asleep or unable to see them.
author: entomoxie

entry: Despite sleeping during most of the day, POKENAME can use their ears perfectly to keep balance and stay safe. They do go out at night when most other Pokémon would be asleep or unable to see them.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME laze about during the day, refusing to listen to anyone and getting grumpy if they're disturbed before nightfall. Offering a POKENAME a ruby will cause it to excitedly wake up willing to cooperate in exchange for its favorite meal.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Even while asleep, POKENAME rolls at high speeds. It leaves behind a potent trail of poison that puts pursuers to sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lazily sits around in flower patches soaking up sun and moonlight. It digs a hole and submerges most of its body in the dirt to hibernate once winter rolls around.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are lethargic yet opportunistic. They tend to follow other carnivorous Pokémon to consume bits of meat left behind after a recent meal. Their sensitive noses and slow movement help conserve energy as they travel between meals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While Trevenant sleeps, POKENAME mounts its back and extends vines into its mind. It uses this connection to subconsciously control nearby trees.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases clouds of licorice-scented pollen while asleep. The aroma is strong enough to lull nearby Pokémon into a nap as well.
author: .izik

entry: When it snores, POKENAME emits low-frequency pulses from its ears. The blasts can cause temporary deafness if one gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: Many people believe that letting a POKENAME rest on their heads will help them sleep better. However, while their feathers are incredibly soft, there is no scientific data to back up this claim.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are too weak to lift the shell of their armor, instead resting inside of it, soaking up the heat during the day. At night, they will slowly shuffle around in search for warmer areas to continue their rest.
author: shyguy11011

entry: Until it evolves, POKENAME only moves when another is touching it or is persistently nettling it. It relies entirely on its mother or Trainer to encourage it to do things as simple as eating.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME hibernate for most of the year, and it is only awake to collect berries for its den. If you try to wake it, it will viciously attack you with its sharp claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lazes around tree trunks eating fungi and molds. The mushrooms growing on its back are valued as an ingredient for medicinal sleep aids.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fur is so soft and comfy that it is in a constant state of drowsiness. Travelling Trainers will often use POKENAME as a makeshift pillow.
author: mistymagius

entry: These sleepy Pokémon tear open pillows to use as nests. In places where wild POKENAME live, special pillows with spicy stuffing are sold to deter POKENAME.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME lazily sits in its pumpkin patch, stealing all the water and nutrients for itself. It releases a sweet scent from its belly that calms anything that tries to attack it.
author: mistymagius

entry: On humid days, POKENAME naps atop its soft lily pad. A golden sap oozes from its body and is often harvested for biscuit glazes.
author: .izik

entry: Though not often seen, POKENAME does possess a tail flame, smoldering faintly at the tip. If it concentrates, it can make the flame flare to life for a time, but the effort leaves it quite exhausted afterward.
author: sk372

entry: Some say that sleeping near a water source inhabited by POKENAME will cause you to find the love of your life within a week. Due to its rarity, this has yet to be scientifically proven.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleep in large piles near cliff bases. If one is disturbed, the entire pack awakens and swarms the intruder without hesitation.
author: .izik

entry: Trainers often report POKENAME being in a paradoxical state of being energetic as well as slothful. During battle, they switch between bouts of energy and excitement to being lazy and barely awake, only moving to dodge attacks.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME yawns frequently, releasing threads coated in drowsy silk. Predators often fall asleep mid-chase after inhaling it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lazily anchors itself to the ceiling of a tree hollow to await evolution. It often ends up falling from the ceiling, but lands softly on the hollow floor and continues to wait while watching the days pass.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME spends nearly the entire day sleeping so all its energy can go towards evolution. Its tough cocoon allows it to shrug off attacks.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME tend to be quite lethargic, preferring to spend most of the day on their back. If their pollen is inhaled, the subject begins to fall asleep.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: While being perfectly capable of flying, POKENAME doesn't move much. It often enjoys relaxing, but will walk when it needs to find food.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME only sleeps where it's least convenient for its Trainer and will try its best to ignore their commands. It prides itself on its laziness.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are quite popular as pets, as they are easy to care for. Many people find their nonchalant attitude charming.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are the star of a popular line of sleep medication, adverts featuring them showing just how quickly POKENAME fall asleep on the medicine. In truth, they need little motivation to sleep and often sneak away to quiet places for a quick catnap.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME makes for a moderately low-maintenance pet due to its generally inactive lifestyle. However, it is too lazy to even groom itself, so constant care of its matted fur on the owner's part can be a hassle.
author: sk372

entry: While sleeping near a lava pool, POKENAME occasionally coughs up puffs of smoke. This smoke is hot enough to cause burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a very lax personality, spending most of its time soaking in the sun's rays at the beach. Digging itself a hole in the sand to sleep in can take hours due to its slow movements.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is actually quite territorial, but also too lazy to do much of anything about intruders in its territory. The most it manages is making indignant huffing noises until the interloper leaves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's lethargic tendencies are so strong that it can sometimes fall asleep mid-flight. It responds quite aggressively to anything that wakes it up, including an inevitable collision with the ground.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's training sessions are lackluster, consisting of short walks and lifting small rocks to keep its muscles active. Despite the low-effort training, it's stronger than it seems.
author: sk372

entry: It spends its life in search of the perfect opponent. Upon finding such a foe, it forfeits immediately.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME has a languid expression that rarely changes because it is always tired. It takes at least 10 seconds for its muscles to move its mouth into a smile.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are constantly awake and eating, chewing through tree trunks and branches at every hour of the day. They eat faster when other POKENAME are nearby, trying to gorge before their food gets eaten by others.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Each part of POKENAME thinks independently, rarely syncing up. Even in sleep, one or more sections remain twitchy and alert.
author: .izik

entry: Carrying the missing claw of a Vigoroth allows POKENAME to defend itself with the limb's sharp points. When it is upset, it goes into a vicious tantrum, thrashing about and swinging the dismembered claw about wildly until it collapses.
author: sk372

entry: It will aggressively lick anything that it comes across, tasting it and marking it with its saliva. Because of its overactive body functions, its tongue never dries out no matter how long it remains out of its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: Excess internal production causes POKENAME's two heads to constantly cough out thick clouds of smoke. Inhaling the smoke causes intense surges of energy that lead to heavy exhaustion when the adrenaline wears off.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME smashes boulders with its head and immediately seeks another. It charges nonstop, seemingly never running out of stamina.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly eager to help tend to the sick or injured, but its appearance combined with hyperactive tendencies often causes more harm than healing.
author: sk372

entry: Hoenn herbalists harvest POKENAME's vines to make cheap energy tinctures. The vines regrow quickly, making it easy to farm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is insanely protective of its young, flying into a defensive flurry at even the faintest hint of possible aggression. Despite the frantic motions, the child stays asleep through all its parent's antics.
author: sk372

entry: Easily excitable, POKENAME flaps its wings incredibly fast when overly stimulated. It is a common sight to see it blow away flowers it wishes to consume because it got too excited when getting close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can fly through the air via turning horizontally and rotating at rapid speeds. While spinning, its sharp claws extend further, turning it into a whirling, slicing aerial hazard.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's lanky limbs allow it a flexible reach in battle, flailing its arms around wildly to club and claw opponents into unconsciousness. In rare moments of placidity, said limbs also allow it to give surprisingly nice hugs.
author: sk372

entry: With wild energy, POKENAME tears bark from trees to drink sap. If startled mid-meal, it retaliates in a frenzy of claw slashes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is in a constant state of energized rampage, charging head-long towards anything that catches its eye. It only stops when it ends up charging into something solid enough to knock itself unconscious.
author: sk372

entry: A quirk in POKENAME's programming causes it to be filled with a ceaseless need to move about. Even when hovering in a mostly stationary fashion, its limbs and head will constantly rotate.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are quite active despite their bulky physique. By giving them a Chesto Berry, they can quickly awaken themselves from a nap without the grogginess that typically occurs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME bounds from branch to branch, never staying still. It feeds on fruit blossoms, pollinating trees as it moves through the canopy.
author: .izik

entry: It uses the claw-like appendage on its head to dig holes in the dirt to hide in. POKENAME enjoys surprising passersby by popping out of its hole and "waving" its claw at them playfully.
author: sk372

entry: Despite POKENAME's small size, it is unafraid of any threat. It valiantly patrols the forest, punishing unruly Pokémon with its powerful red appendages.
author: mepp.

entry: Herds of POKENAME sprint across fields, buzzing with energy. They transfer mild charges to each other as they run in sync.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's smog clouds reflect its vitality. The most powerful specimens can barely be seen through the storm surrounding them.
author: dylonk25

entry: It scrapes its claws along tree trunks in order to burn off energy. Because it is so hyperactive, trees in areas with POKENAME presence are often all but stripped bare of their bark.
author: sk372

entry: The pollen from POKENAME induces bursts of energy in nearby Pokémon. It's often surrounded by small groups unable to sit still.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often seen riding the gale-force winds of tornados and hurricanes. It uses its powerful claws to slash through incoming debris.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME leaves behind a trail of bright red petals as its lightning-fast metabolism causes its petals to grow and fall off at a rapid rate. It thrives off of sunlight and will often migrate to find sunnier areas.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wedges itself between trees using its gills, which it can cause to become rock-hard by inflating them with a gel. When in this pose, it expends all its energy trying to move forwards, rarely succeeding but ending the day exhausted.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME dives deep into muddy waters and digs into the mucky bottom to create tunnels to hide itself in. It may even create tunnel networks between nearby bodies of water if given enough time.
author: sk372

entry: Oft considered a pest, POKENAME almost never sleep, instead opting to break into and eat entire stocks of food supplies from urban businesses and homes. Initiatives have been started to drive them out of major cities, with little success.
author: agentyoshi

entry: POKENAME can be seen rolling down hills at breakneck speeds, protecting itself with its iron-thick claws. If you try and pick it up, it will go into a frenzy and try to rip you apart with its claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has an incredibly short attention span, and it will sting its Trainer multiple times a day just to get a rise out of them. However, it can spend hours a day repeatedly gliding from small trees without getting bored.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is always eagerly searching for sweet sap to taste, digging into trees with its claws. Its overeager nature means it often tears away too much of a tree's trunk in search of sap and causes the tree to fall.
author: sk372

entry: Even with its small size, it is able to cause quite a lot of mayhem. It is incredibly energetic and its favorite pastime is causing mischief.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME move with a frenetic urgency, seemingly unable to stay still. Their constant movement keeps their liquid bodies from ever fully setting, and even when they rest, they fidget and move in their sleep.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME must always stay within the coldest of regions for its health. Between its excessive energy and the heavy fur coat, warmer temperatures would cause it to easily overheat to deadly effect.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is restless and full of energy despite being encased in a hard, immobile shell. It moves in brief, erratic hops, which usually cause it to land on its side and become stuck.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME runs wild across the plains, trumpeting constantly. It's thought that it's attempting to create music, but its overly energetic nature results in atonal, discordant songs that repel listeners.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's internal programming is always running on overdrive, causing it to zoom around screens constantly, becoming a visual nuisance. Clicking and holding it causes it to thrash about wildly, as if remaining still is painful to it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cannot sit still: the overwhelming energy in its body prevents it from properly resting or focusing for very long. If it cannot constantly channel its energy, its already-dangerous levels of stress can cause severe physical complications.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is in constant pain, struggling to move as it flails frantically. It is incredibly dangerous, as a single swipe from its tail claw is enough to cut a tree clean in half.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME impulsively shoves any small objects it can grab into its mouth, seemingly not caring if it can digest them or not. If it can't find something to fit in its mouth, it will constantly lick random objects.
author: mistymagius

entry: At dawn, POKENAME's vines flail unpredictably, grabbing anything in reach. It remains restless until calming down late into the evening.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to ambush random Pokémon, bombarding them with a flurry of quick strikes before they can react. While usually nocturnal, POKENAME has enough energy to go five days without sleep.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are usually found in the jungle, frantically climbing trees and swinging from vines. They love Custap berries as their bodies need lots of sugar to fuel their energy needs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoys dancing for others, but its hyperactive nature causes its dances to be unfocused and disorienting to most observers. It sulks and runs off if not applauded for its efforts.
author: sk372

entry: Brimming with energy, POKENAME behaves in a wild, unbridled manner. It's constantly focused on entertaining itself with fights or games, to the point it may begin neglecting things like food or hygiene.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon regularly faints because it has more power than its body can handle. POKENAME is always creaking because its body is always close to bursting with excess energy.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: If sleep-deprived, POKENAME secretes a red toxin that energizes others on contact. Victims become restless, unable to sleep.
author: .izik

entry: Because its body is so hyperactive, POKENAME has little to no control over its color change ability. Its constantly changing hues shift in an almost psychedelic pattern that can disorient friends and foes alike.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is known to hang from trees in the jungle, dropping on unsuspecting prey. The large sprout on POKENAME's back produces acidic liquid that wilts any plant life it touches.
author: adsfw11

entry: POKENAME's clear poison grants bursts of hyperactivity followed by deep fatigue. It secretes more of this toxin when provoked in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's massive jaws are highly impulsive and react on instinct, chomping wildly at the mere scent of food in its vicinity. It takes considerable effort on the main body's part to reign it in once it gets going.
author: sk372

entry: It is considered highly dangerous due to having Slaking's strength with Vigoroth's inability to calm down. Even vicious and territorial Pokémon flee when POKENAME is seen rabidly charging through the area.
author: sk372

entry: If one spots pillars of light rapidly appearing and disappearing in the distance, it's likely a sign that POKENAME is present. Full of boundless energy, it cannot stay still and teleports constantly to blow off the excess steam.
author: sk372

entry: The bushes along POKENAME's back grow and shed rapidly. They are constantly bashing their shells against trees to shake off dead leaves and branches.
author: santon5512

entry: In its den, POKENAME coats the entrance in poison using its horn. It attacks intruders with Throat Chop before they can flee.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its wild personality and unstoppable amounts of energy, POKENAME is quite friendly towards its Trainer. However, be cautious, as POKENAME loves to tackle them at full force to show affection.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's eyes are extremely powerful, ceaselessly observing its surroundings and never being seen blinking. Lightning crackles along its limbs as it scampers about, due to excessive electrical generation in its body.
author: sk372

entry: Always brimming with excessive energy, POKENAME's ribbons whip around frantically at all times. One should keep their distance, as these ribbons are tipped with sharp claws that can cause painful gashes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's ribbons constantly thrash about around it due to its excessive energy. When on the defensive, it can sharpen the edges of the ribbons, using them to cut and slash at anything drawing too close.
author: sk372

entry: Chilan Berry-scented spores drift from POKENAME's head as it runs. Breathing them in triggers bursts of energy and erratic, playful movement within its own body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is perpetually in motion, flying around in random haphazard patterns to burn off a limitless supply of energy. Even the few moments it spends sleeping, its body still vibrates and its wings still twitch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins its webs at an incredible speed, creating complex woven structures in mere minutes. It moves so fast it builds up electricity, transferring it into the webs, which crackle and arc as it spins.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's flame burns with surprising vigor as it dashes through the forest to light up dark spots. However, it often crashes into trees by accident, sometimes starting small wildfires.
author: mistymagius

entry: A claw extends from POKENAME's mouth to crush coral with ease. It's highly selective, spitting out pieces it deems unworthy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets out a bellowing roar when it spots prey, sending them fleeing. It revels in the wild chase, driven by its boundless energy.
author: .izik

entry: Using aura senses, POKENAME searches for energetic Pokémon. Once found, it challenges them to rapid-fire sparring bouts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are so full of energy when they are awake that they are always moving at least one part of their bodies. Their constant physical actions, including their fervent beating of their paws upon their chests, keep their muscles well developed.
author: infinex21

entry: When the red tuft on its head suddenly stands on end, it is a sign that a storm is approaching. POKENAME moves swiftly among the tree branches it inhabits, using its long claws to cling to trunks while gathering fruit.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are impatient and impulsive, often running headlong into dangerous situations. Their aggressive shouts have a mildly soporific effect, leading Researchers to theorise they could send people to sleep if they made longer calls.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is known for using its powerful jaws to dig rapidly through the ground. It often has sudden bursts of energy, charging through tunnels and attacking anything that moves.
author: _lazygod_

entry: POKENAME rotates furiously as it moves, radiating chaotic energy. This motion builds electricity that discharges on contact.
author: .izik

entry: In order to intimidate, POKENAME inflates its body before exhaling, waving its arms about while hooting wildly. For most, this has the opposite effect and makes it look rather comical instead.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has an almost endless appetite due to its body's rapid metabolism. It chews through soil, often uprooting gardens and even trees within forests with its excessive eating.
author: sk372

entry: The jelly-like substance around POKENAME's head spikes up when it's feeling incensed. Some energy drinks use the jelly as an ingredient.
author: hophoppip

entry: In groups, they watch Pokémon and Trainer alike with disdain and pull pranks on them. The length of their hair indicates their rank in the hierarchy.
author: ayner

entry: In combat, POKENAME spins its metal body while surging with energy. While spinning, it focuses to unleash devastating attacks.
author: .izik

entry: During early mornings, POKENAME is brimming with energy. It slams tree trunks with its finned head, leaving deep grooves to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME almost never sleeps, so it has to gobble down as much food as it can find to keep going. It can drain an entire watermelon of all of its fluids in less than 30 seconds.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME yearns to release all of its pent up energy, but it is too busy shivering in the cold to do anything about it.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME is completely blind, as the fruits on its head have eye-like markings to distract predators. While the fruits are incredibly bitter, they contain as much caffeine as fifteen shots of espresso, making them incredibly dangerous to consume.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its body constantly produces large amounts of adrenaline, so it ends up rampaging all over the forest. Despite how violent it can get, POKENAME doesn't like to intentionally hurt humans.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME leaps around frantically from tree to tree, spreading its spores. If inhaled, these spores induce hyperactivity and aggression in those affected, lasting a few hours before they collapse from exhaustion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cannot sit still if it tried, constantly twitching and shaking even while unconscious. While it has not been confirmed, Scientist theorize that POKENAME has the fastest heartbeat of any Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME never sleep and can be seen zipping around the forest all day and all night. However, they need to eat a lot of berries to keep going, usually feeding on Custap and Salac Berries specifically.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME floats on high to crash down into the ground at breakneck speed, before repeating the process. It does this to burn off an exceedingly vast supply of surplus energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are constantly active, burrowing without pausing to rest and seemingly never needing to sleep. Their claws make digging through even tough rocks trivial, making them popular with miners.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are highly energetic and aggressive, scattering a flurry of dust with every beat of their wings. Anyone who inhales the dust will get a sudden burst of unfiltered energy, flying off the rails and losing their inhibitions.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are sometimes abruptly seized with a mad energy, racing around at high speed and clawing at those unfortunate enough to be in their path. They can only be calmed from this state by an offering of a plate of fish Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's strong limbs and almost limitless energy allow for it to pursue its prey for up to 12 hours without tiring. Its hunts don't last that long, however, since POKENAME can run up to 60 mph.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's metabolism has hypercharged its psychic powers to the point of overwhelming its mind. It waddles around in a daze, its telekinesis uncontrollably lifting and flinging things around it without it even noticing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME regularly work themselves up into a frenzy, breathing rapidly and charging at others for even the smallest perceived aggression. They rapidly swipe at the subject of their ire, brutally wielding powerful muscles and sharp claws.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: An overabundance of stamina means it's all but impossible for POKENAME to remain in one place. It teleports around constantly, seemingly at random, just to burn off excess psychic energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are strong and energetic creatures that enjoy carrying things. Many are employed at moving companies to help people settle into a new home, lifting boxes and furniture to and from trucks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are handy creatures that help new homeowners carry furniture. A single POKENAME can lift a bed and a sofa without breaking a sweat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its lack of limbs, POKENAME struggles to sit still due to its boundless energy. Its tongue is coated in a potent stimulant that can cause insomnia for up to 3 days.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME raises its arms high so the eyes on its limbs can give it a better view of its surroundings. If it spots something interesting, it makes speedy leaps and bounds to hunt down the object of intrigue.
author: sk372

entry: Its face is too soft and its teeth are too fragile to be used for digging. Instead, POKENAME pulverizes stone with its hulking arm-like tail.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME roll around on popular beaches, and due to their appearance, many tourists assume them to be volleyballs. Those unfortunate enough to use it for a game will get soaked by gallons of water when they decide to bump or spike it.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for beach balls because of their brightly colored body. POKENAME explode when tossed into the air, dispersing a dense saltwater mist around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To attract prey, POKENAME produces bubbles that small Pokémon like to play with. These bubbles contain neutralizing toxins which will paralyze the target.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Walking is difficult for POKENAME as they are constantly off balance. They would walk on all fours if the size of their head was a bit smaller.
author: hummusishome

entry: It enjoys floating in the shallows with schools of its kind, releasing playful jets of water. These gentle currents provide protection to smaller sea Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: It gracefully glides through the water, spinning in circles to create mesmerizing whirlpools. These whirlpools help it catch smaller prey with minimal effort.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggle to communicate with their kin because of vibrations from container ships that sail past their native habitat. Many resort to stabbing with their horns to communicate distress.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dwells near the water's edge. While it will go ashore to play with people and Pokémon, it must be careful not to be played with too roughly: it cannot easily regenerate limbs like Staryu.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME swim near beaches with their long, blocky flippers. They filter feed for small aquatic Pokémon to build up their bulky bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon uses its tooth comb to catch its food. With its nutrient rich diet, it grows fast.
author: _sadfroggy

entry: POKENAME trudge close to the banks of ponds and drag their leaves across the surface. In this way, they wet them with drops to cool themselves down.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME regularly jumps into lakes and rivers to cool off. In doing so, the buds on its body soak up water. They can hold it for months.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has a gentle and sociable disposition, which makes it a popular partner for Pokémon Trainers. It can emit refreshing water from its neck.
author: chorb33

entry: It produces pulses of light while swimming in the deep sea, guiding lost Pokémon toward safety. Fishermen have learned to follow its glow to find schools of smaller fish Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Its glowing orbs are visible even in the darkest ocean depths. Many sailors mistake it for a guiding light, unaware of the deep-sea creatures lurking nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a protective bubble shell around their body that protects them while they roam beaches. Whenever the bubble pops, they rush back to the sea to restore their bubble.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It bounces playfully on the ocean's surface, using its rubbery body to create large splashes. Coastal towns often see them playing together during festivals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is so light that, with a gentle breeze, it can take off and fly through the sky. It can regulate the water levels in its body through bodily absorption and spurting through the blowhole on its head.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When hatched, POKENAME starts small in size, but it steadily grows until it eventually evolves. It prefers to travel in steady sea currents.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME creates a constant flow when underwater, drinking and expelling hundreds of litres of water a second. Pods of POKENAME can even create small global ocean currents.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME creates a constant flow when underwater, drinking and expelling hundreds of litres of water a second. Other Pokémon are often dragged into these currents but are spat out unscathed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME waddles through shallow waters with a carefree smile, using its tail to stir up mud. Though it looks harmless, it often causes trouble by accidentally dislodging fishing nets and dragging them to the depths.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME travels in small, tight groups, using their spiked bodies to protect one another. They communicate with low frequency calls to coordinate their movements as they drift through the sea in search of food.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME shells were prized by mariners in antiquity, with many expeditions setting out with the goal to hunt them and sell their shells as beautiful ornaments. POKENAME pods are now only found deep in the ocean, migrating along underwater mountains.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It enjoys resting on coral beds, covering its body in shards of broken coral for camouflage. When startled, it spits them out at high speeds as a defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful tentacles to propel itself through the water with surprising speed. Its enormous mouth can vacuum up large schools of fish, which it then spits out in concentrated bursts to stun nearby prey.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It enjoys riding ocean currents alongside large groups of its kind, sometimes hitching rides on larger sea Pokémon. The smoother the current, the happier it seems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are popular subjects for coastal photographers because they appear elegant while surfing. After intense physical activity, POKENAME enjoy resting and hydrating in tide pools.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME are hatched and raised for some time in underground lakes before leaving with their parents to go out to the ocean. The larger they become, the closer they are to evolution.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flies thanks to the steam it produces. The chemicals in its wings change color based on temperature.
author: ohok3441

entry: Despite its internal temperature, POKENAME's thick skin makes it safe to ride. It can travel long distances in both sky and sea.
author: ohok3441

entry: Its playful nature makes it a favorite among divers, often approaching them curiously. It emits joyful squeaks while gliding just beneath the waves.
author: .izik

entry: Although small, POKENAME can inhale nearly two gallons of water; they only inhale that much when they plan to walk on land. Though they typically walk along the seabed, their legs are developed enough to be used for swimming.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body fills with air as it travels with its pod from port to port. It begs from the waves for tourists to toss food into the ocean.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a clumsy but ambitious creature. It often trips and falls while walking on land.
author: neonriser

entry: It spouts water from its nostrils whenever it surfaces and as a playful act with friends. Although often outgoingly playful, POKENAME is shy for a period of time before and after resting, changing its hues to avoid being perceived.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is found near dams made by other Bidoof and Bibarel, where it bathes in the sun and enjoys the fruits of the other Pokémon's labour. In return, POKENAME uses its body to temporarily block any leaks in the dam.
author: thescribe

entry: POKENAME spends its days rolling around the shore, using its inflated body as a giant cushion to bounce off rocks. Its massive size often causes unintended chaos, sending waves crashing and startling local wildlife with its clumsy antics.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The intensity of the water ejected from POKENAME's blowhole increases alongside its level of happiness. POKENAME bites onto a sturdy tree when feeling extreme joy to anchor itself against the immense pressure of the resulting blast.
author: jaminmcready

entry: During floods, POKENAME carries small Pokémon on its shell. Because it loves to roll, it sometimes forgets they are there and flings them through the air as it spins during travel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME regularly dives beyond 800 feet in search of food. By filter-feeding in the deep, it consumes much larger quantities of drifting organic matter than it can near the surface.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When ships lower their anchors, it tends to attract POKENAME. It stares at the anchor for hours, studying its movements.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME eat pearls and use the magnetic field to traverse the seabed to hunt for Clampearl that hold them. They also hunt Spoink whenever POKENAME are on land.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Wild POKENAME use the magnetic field to determine where to migrate across the vast ocean. They often travel in groups and will use their magnetic waves to communicate with each other.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME only harvests the life force of schools of small fish. It enjoys splash-offs with beach goers.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Though it smacks the life force out of small schools of fish, POKENAME also enjoys splashing water at beach-goers and being hit like a beach ball.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME stores moisture from the air in its blades. When released, it creates a sudden storm that drenches everything nearby.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's body fills with a balanced mixture of air and seawater that allows it to roll across the ocean's surface with ease. While at top speed it releases a calming aura to those it passes by.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are typically found stalking along the flooded shoreline in the aftermath of tsunamis. Pokémon Researchers actively debate why they do this, the leading theory is that they are brought ashore by the powerful currents creating the tidal wave.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It likes to play fight with its stretchy arms. When POKENAME drinks a lot of water, its tail inflates to the size of a beach ball, being just as bouncy as one.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The lid that POKENAME holds is made out of a gemstone similar to lapis lazuli. If the lid happens to break, POKENAME will replace it with whatever material it can find.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time resting on the ocean floor by using their spiny appendages to latch onto rocks for stability. POKENAME have become a notorious pest to fishermen, often attaching to boats and stealing catches.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME floats above the ocean's waves with a cloth balloon, remaining close to pods of Wailmer and Wailord. While its compatriots are confused by its inability to dive, they enjoy tossing POKENAME around like a beach ball.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates underwater tunnels within the silt of the seafloor. Should a predator enter, it chirps loudly while unleashing high pressurized water jets at them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are adapted to tolerate high salinity in their diet. Extremely lethargic, they lie along beaches, feeding on seawater and vegetation washed ashore.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME fills its body with air to roll across the ocean's surface with ease. At full inflation, it can grow gigantic in size, on rare occasions reaching the height of a cruise ship.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bounces in and out of the waves to charge electricity within its body. It will randomly launch incredibly high for unknown reasons, sometimes reaching 100 feet into the air.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have huge gullets and can launch massive lightning bolts from their mouths. They will channel electricity in front of them with a mouth open wide, swallowing water and filtering out microscopic nutrients.
author: vic1312

entry: A POKENAME will eagerly rescue drowning humans and Pokémon, allowing them to use its body as a living life raft. Once they are saved, however, it has little interest in bringing its passengers back to shore.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME dwells within kelp forests, blending in with the surrounding leaves as it filter feeds. Its buds function as fins, allowing it to swim with surprising agility. If a predator approaches, it releases a poisonous toxin and quickly escapes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: It can absorb over a ton of compost in a day. When its stomach is near to bursting it belches out a massive spray of spores.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME lives inside a bubble that provides it water to breathe with. When the bubble pops, POKENAME suffocates.
author: barry63_madrel

entry: POKENAME searches through sunken ships for lost jewelry. Should it find any gems, it consumes them without hesitation or checking for onlookers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has numerous nostrils, and spouts water in all directions when it emerges from the sea to take a breath.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME blow jets of water to scare nearby Pokémon. When threatened, they can leap even higher, showing true fear to any who witness this rage.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME hunt in small groups. It is very cowardly on its own and roams the ocean until it finds a new group if it loses its old one.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME collects air through its nostrils, which it stores in its body. When it sees prey, it expels it for additional acceleration.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME lives in abandoned lighthouses, leaving once the sun sets to fly along the coast. It periodically releases loud flute-like bursts as it goes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are able to move through both air and water, though their heavy stature prevents them from flying for very long. By slamming their wings together, they create sonic booms to drive away predators.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME will release diluted, poisonous water from its blowhole when threatened or when it gets too excited. It often latches onto the bottoms of boats and uses its powerful jets to blast away any dangerous Pokémon that approach.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME need very little water to survive, but will swell larger to hold any excess water within their bodies. Once a year, a flower will bloom atop its head. Smaller POKENAME tend to have the prettiest and most fragrant flowers.
author: darkweavile428

entry: This buoyant Pokémon has no concept of personal space and excitedly crashes any boat party it sees.
author: .realthree

entry: Its vibrant blue scales shine brilliantly under the sun as it floats near coral reefs. If disturbed, it unleashes powerful psychic waves to scare away threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME duel on sunny beaches, but will immediately stop if either begins to dry out under the harsh rays. Due to this, many fights don't last over an hour.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hops along pond edges searching for prey like Ledyba. It launches into the air and dispatches them midflight with a powerful Bounce.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can often be spotted around lighthouses, ensuring the safe travels of its keepers. Sailors' stories tell of POKENAME that used its bubbles to lift a sinking ship back to the surface.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is most commonly seen on farms near large lakes and oceans. Farmers enjoy its presence because it naturally regulates water levels. Its bioluminescence allows it to see clearly in the dark.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is most commonly seen on farms near large lakes and oceans. Farmers enjoy its presence because it naturally regulates water levels. Its bioluminescence allows it to see clearly in the dark.
author: entomoxie

entry: When two POKENAME play together, their heart-shaped fins create elegant water patterns. Many believe seeing them leap together is a sign of everlasting love.
author: .izik

entry: When playing, POKENAME bounces face-first across waves near tropical towns with others from its pack. Groups of POKENAME are known as volleys.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body becomes extremely fluffy when exposed to saltwater. Many say it resembles a beach ball as it rolls through the waves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME make their burrows within coral reefs, nestling within them for safety. They extend their trio of heads into water currents to filter feed, gradually cleaning water of pollutants as they do.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Water bursts from the holes on POKENAME's back to form a pair of glimmering, water-like wings. Despite being composed of water, these wings somehow grant it the ability to fly for short periods.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can often be found a short distance from beaches where it floats idly on the ocean's surface. Whenever it is harassed by another Pokémon, it dives or flies away depending on which Pokémon is being mean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rolls on its side through coastal skies, somehow staying airborne without frequently flapping its wings. It can maintain this flight for hours, defying explanation.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME spots an approaching wave, it punches it repeatedly. This does nothing to stop the wave and ultimately just sweeps POKENAME along with the current.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's rotund body and tail are incredibly buoyant, making floating on water easy. With a friendly disposition, it happily lets inexperienced or tired swimmers cling to it while floating towards the shore.
author: sk372

entry: It can't stand to be hungry and eats over a metric ton of food every day. It will slowly roam land and sea to find food to eat.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME experience many headaches because of the noise pollution caused by offshore oil rigs. Whenever the noise becomes too intense for them to handle, they press their flippers against their head in pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It playfully races against fast swimmers, using jets of water to propel itself forward. Trainers believe swimming alongside it enhances endurance.
author: .izik

entry: When surfacing for air, POKENAME sometimes knocks over small boats. It mistakes the people in the water for its playmates and tries to play by bumping into them. Thankfully, it only lasts for a few minutes before POKENAME gets bored and swims away.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lets out a triumphant cry after every meal and taunts other members of its pod by slapping its blubbery stomach. Whenever it gets into a fight, it relies on its weight and heavy slaps to overwhelm foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a fun-loving Pokémon that enjoys relaxing on the beach. Its favorite means of relaxation is trying to fight other wild Pokémon.
author: usaginezumi

entry: POKENAME are curious creatures that often bump into boats that go through their wetland home. They enjoy playfully spraying water at those inside the boats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Docks use POKENAME's strength to help pull ships into harbors. They are quite impatient, often spouting water in anger should a delay occur.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME produces a toxic fat that has long been used to make candles. When burned for extended periods, these candles release a spicy aroma.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often seen drifting in shallow waters, with its tentacles twitching in unexplained patterns. Researchers have been unable to determine its purpose, but its presence seems to cause strange disruptions in local marine ecosystems.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME often waddles onto land by using its small fins to support its bulk as it shuffles through city streets. While harmless, it often causes minor chaos by blocking roads and sneaking into markets in search of food.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME live in frigid conditions where the temperatures never rise above the freezing point of water. Their thick blubber keeps them warm as they traverse the icy water, as the fat makes up more than a third of their body weight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A POKENAME's skin is known to dry out quickly when not underwater. Because of this, POKENAME encase themselves in bubbles of water mixed with low-potency chemicals to help keep their skin moisturised.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME makes the star on its tail shine brightly whenever it feels threatened. It can produce a delicate, luxurious silk used to craft elegant evening gowns.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME wears the skull of a deceased Electric-type Pokémon of great power so it may grow as strong as its parents. Although its head is too large for the bone, it serves its purpose by boosting POKENAME's morale.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Despite the poor camouflage of POKENAME, they are rarely attacked by larger Pokémon. When researching why this was, it was discovered that their chrysalis carries a static charge that causes painful shocks when touched.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The tendrils coiled around POKENAME have a similar structure to electrical wire, letting them easily carry high voltages. Newly hatched POKENAME cannot control their electricity, resulting in wild bursts of lightning from their cables' yellow ends.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME have wing scales that each carry a slight electrical charge. When they feel threatened, POKENAME can send an electrical pulse through their wings that causes them to abruptly light up, blinding their assailants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is able to flatten itself paper-thin and course electricity through its body. It often hides on trails or in doorways and shocks unsuspecting Trainers who step on it.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME generates electricity by absorbing sunlight, its yellow leaves glowing brightly when fully charged. Campers often keep POKENAME as they act as solar-powered batteries.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can rub its fur together to build up static electricity. The individual strands of hair on its body form a network that channels this energy into a single point on its back.
author: danonzer

entry: POKENAME flares up the electric patches of its body as a way of socializing with others of its kind. Showering sparks on each other is considered a gesture of deep friendship between POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: They are most active just after rainy days, when bug Pokémon scurry out of their dens. While wild POKENAME have an aggressive disposition, properly trained POKENAME are quite friendly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is just light enough for its tail to lift it into the air. It uses this to appear taller and to see above tall grass.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through the talons on its feet. It often perches high in trees and drops down to shock unsuspecting Trainers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: If it concentrates hard enough, POKENAME can use its electricity to make the spots on its back light up. Groups of them playfully compare flashing patterns and colors when gathering together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's webbing contains a faint electrical charge that causes it to glow in the dark. This light attracts insects into the webbing at night, allowing it to capture plenty of potential meals.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly rubs its cheeks to ease the ache of stored electricity. Sparks leak from the star on its tail when it struggles to hold the charge.
author: .izik

entry: It relies on its parents and siblings to avoid being picked off by buzzard-like predators, as it has few methods of self-defense. One such method requires inhaling lots of air before exhaling all at once to fly away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail lights up to communicate with partners in the dark. At night, a flock of POKENAME resembles the stars in the sky!
author: alliveir

entry: They float on the winds to move around. If they encounter a thunderstorm, their bodies glow with electricity.
author: 22ndsolstice

entry: POKENAME has a capricious personality and are easily distracted by its surroundings. Trainers tend to bribe it with food to ensure that it focuses during training.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME covers itself in mud to help regulate its temperature and protect it from high UV rays. All its fur begins to crackle when danger is nearby, and may cause the mud to explode off its body if the danger gets too close.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME crackles with energy from the feather on its head. The brightness of the sparks reveals its health and mood.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has a love for Honey. It can be found by hives of Combee, using the light emitting from its tail to distract them while it eats its fill.
author: curvingapollo

entry: POKENAME travel in groups of three to four for safety when moving about in the woods. If one of them becomes separated from the others at night, they light up with a flare of electricity to make themselves more visible and reunite with their friends.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's thick fur shines when it eats. It uses its tail to send jolts of electricity through the nearby ground to immobilize small prey.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME is very hyperactive, always running around and attempting to play-fight anything it sees. As it runs, small sparks of electricity jolt and crackle all over its body.
author: evilgammon

entry: Due to its internal heat and electrical stores, POKENAME's body is always warm to the touch. It is quite amicable and loves to cuddle, though petting it will cause one's hair to stand on end.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME coils tightly around its foe while rattling its tail. As it tightens, it builds a charge, then releases a burst of electricity all at once.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can sneeze out bolts of electricity from its snout. These flashes of electricity can momentarily blind people or other Pokémon but are otherwise harmless.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It creates paintings under UV lights with the solar charged paint from the tip of its tail. POKENAME shocks those who mock its art.
author: luludracon

entry: POKENAME is incredibly energetic and can go for almost 3 days straight without rest. Its fur stores large amounts of static electricity, causing its strikes to give its opponent a powerful shock.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME zips across the sky on its star-shaped tail, leaving bright streaks of light behind it. It must recharge its tail after flight, generating more electricity by absorbing starlight.
author: mistymagius

entry: While dancing, POKENAME stores electricity in the pom-pom on its head. Interrupting its routine often results in a shocking retaliation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME find lost eggs and store them in their fur pouch to keep them warm. POKENAME can generate small amounts of electricity by rubbing its furry legs together, which they use to light up their tails to entertain babies or fend off predators.
author: laughing_dan

entry: While tunneling, POKENAME builds electricity in its tail. Electricians study its tail tip, which can deliver precise shocks strong enough to disable larger foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found near trees that have been struck with lightning more than once or near wooden power poles. Their fur crackles and stands on end if they sense danger; they use their electricity to emit a bright flash and then attempt to flee.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME fires strong bursts of electricity from the yellow leaf on its tail. The power of this electricity diminishes considerably if it does not get enough sunlight during the day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prowls the forest with feline grace. Its agile movements and powerful strikes make it a formidable hunter in the dense foliage.
author: anarchaz

entry: The feathers making up POKENAME's star-shaped tail turn white when it falls ill. Even after falling out, they retain a slight electrical charge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a very excitable personality. When this Pokémon hops with excitement, its body will begin to generate electricity, radiate heat, and in some cases, its tail and fur-like feathers will begin to glow.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Ruffling POKENAME feathers causes static electricity to build around their bodies. However, due to their clumsy feet, POKENAME have a bad habit of shocking themselves after falling.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME run in packs through fields in order to generate electricity using their muscles. While strong fighters in combat, the feathers on POKENAME will dazzle and glow when an opponent becomes too much for one to handle alone.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's favorite method of recreation is first jumping into a muddy puddle to coat itself in grime. It then makes a short burst of electricity that scatters the mud around its surroundings and leaves it completely dry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a playful creature often seen waddling around in small groups in marshy areas. When it claps its hands, it creates small bursts of harmless electric sparks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is quick to form psychic connections with those it considers friends. When in the presence of intense emotions, it converts its psychic energies into a latent, static charge.
author: turron_turron

entry: Holistic healers prize the material produced by POKENAME for its positive charge. They produce diverse lines of skin creams and other wellness products with the material as a prime ingredient.
author: vic1312

entry: Rumors claim that POKENAME are the souls of Shinx that never got to live past a very young age. The halo-like item above its head supports that theory, but there is no scientific study that confirms this.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Its perfect camouflage allows POKENAME to go invisible. However, the electricity in its fur makes it sparkle, giving away its position.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME nibbles down trees using its big buck teeth. After they fall, it brands them using electricity and its star-shaped tail.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Despite its look, POKENAME's tail is stiff and made of steel. Its tail is notorious for accidentally breaking nearby objects when POKENAME gets excited.
author: retrodox

entry: When the sky gets dark and stormy, groups of POKENAME come out of hiding and play in the thunderstorm. They absorb electricity through their fur, their tails glowing brightly when fully charged.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's eyes are clouded over, giving it little sense of vision. It sheds sparks around its body with an eerie shriek when it senses the presence of others nearby.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME is petted by a Trainer, the sprout on its head releases small sparks as a sign of affection. This sprout is highly conductive and is able to channel electricity generated from within its body.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When POKENAME drinks water, its shell hardens, generating electricity as it does so. The leaf on its head acts as a conductor and absorbs lightning strikes.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME can scale sheer cliffs, leaving a trail of sparks behind it. Its flame glows more intensely when in trouble.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME spines contain a painful paralytic poison; the sensation of being stung is described as similar to receiving a sharp shock. They are irritable and will charge at anyone they dislike, making them difficult first-time Pokémon for new Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's tail can generate a good amount of both fire and electrical energy. POKENAME is still practicing controlling these elements, exhausting itself if it uses too much of either at one time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME clenches its fists tightly to control the electricity leaking from its head. Should it miss with these lashes, it follows up with an uppercut forceful enough to topple a sycamore tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generates electricity inside while it swims, using it in attacks once it's out of the water. When it feels tension and danger, it lets off sparks and runs off to safety.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's beak glows like a light bulb when it uses electricity to attack or communicate with its allies. A single small jolt can convey complex plans.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spines contain a painful paralytic poison; the sensation of being stung is described as similar to receiving a sharp shock. They are irritable and will charge at anyone they dislike, making them difficult first-time Pokémon for new Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon fights with a steel blade which it infuses with electricity. It is incredibly adept at parrying every attack that is thrown its way before retaliating with a single decisive strike.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Its stars emit a gentle glow that has the power to calm agitated Pokémon around it. When its Trainer is in danger, POKENAME charges its fur with electricity and doesn't back down even in the face of terrifying enemies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its stars emit a specific light frequency that lowers cortisol in aggressive Pokémon. When threatened, POKENAME triggers a high-voltage field that improves both defense and offensive capabilities.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's curious nature compels it to hop after anything it finds remotely intriguing. When particularly excited, it uses internal electricity to increase its speed, leaving trails of lightning behind its legs with each stride.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is known as 'Thunder Cloud' by some for being as soft as a cloud and the constant static it emits. Its fluffy coat requires daily brushing, often leaving its Trainer's hair to be just as fluffy as a result.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: The star-like parts of POKENAME's tails glow red-hot during battle. The stronger its electric attacks, the hotter they burn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME charges ore found in its tunnel walls with high amounts of electricity that can last up to three days. Touching one acts as a landmine, shocking the victim with enough force to knock over a truck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly energetic Pokémon, playfully running around all day and night. It stores large amounts of electricity in its fur and is able to channel it into powerful physical attacks.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body crackles with electricity, giving it short bursts of energy that make it extremely hyperactive. Once this energy wears off, it returns to its lazy state.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME glow constantly, but are silent and elusive. It is rumoured that POKENAME can look deep into a person's soul and see every secret they keep.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME have a positively precious face, and their trainers cannot help but forgive them when they get up to mischief. They have a tendency to gnaw on television cables, seeking the rich, flavorful energy within.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's armor conducts the electricity stored within their bodies, allowing them to deliver electrically charged headbutts. Their fur sparkles in the light, distracting and blinding opponents as they charge forward.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME makes for a horrible pet. While it may seem cute with its gigantic forehead, many pet owners forget about its equally big bite. Countless pieces of furniture fall victim to its dreaded "biting fit" that even reinforced steel fails to stop.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME mimics humans using illusions while it hunts. Tiny sparks left in its footsteps are the only clue it was ever there.
author: .izik

entry: The star on its tail emits flickering lights that vary in intensity depending on its mood. By rubbing its teeth together, POKENAME can generate small sparks, which it uses to ignite tiny fires to stay warm while it sleeps in its den.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live among vast fields of wildflowers, keeping watch with their keen hearing. If anything threatens the meadow, their buds bloom open as their tails crackle with electricity to warn intruders to stay away.
author: kittenthepiratekat
