entry: POKENAME whir their wings when they're feeling content, creating a low, droning purr. The noise attracts other POKENAME in the area, as they hope to also find that same inner peace.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will clap its wing-like fins together when it feels joyful. This can be dangerous, as its clapping is so rapid that the beating causes small sonic booms that damage nearby objects and hurt other Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: By emitting ultrasonic vibrations with their fins, POKENAME are able to effortlessly swim through sand. Some past civilizations have used POKENAME to transport people and goods across deserts using sleds.
author: chibitales

entry: By emitting ultrasonic vibrations with their fins, POKENAME are able to effortlessly swim through sand. Some past civilizations have used POKENAME to transport people and goods across deserts using sleds.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have dull scales that make them unappetizing to predators. Being ignored by predators gives them ample time to cultivate seeds that grow underwater.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its large eyes, humanlike lips, and stench confuse birds, allowing POKENAME to be surprisingly resilient in nature.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: Its comical shape makes it both too awkward for bird Pokémon to get a hold of and endearing enough for Trainers to catch it out of sheer pity.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's rotund body is rather light, floating to the top of the ponds it inhabits. Predators quickly learn not to hunt it, as a single touch while it bobs on the water's surface leads to POKENAME exploding violently.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have dull scales on their cocoon that make them unappetizing to bird Pokémon. They hang from branches above the forest where they are ignored and left alone by most Trainers. They wobble with excitement whenever a Trainer notices them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As meek and unassuming Pokémon, POKENAME rarely call attention to themselves. To avoid predation, they squirt ink into a predator's eyes so that they can escape. Many are naturally shocked when Trainers want them to join their team.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Large schools of POKENAME appeared near Frond Island within the last year. They are extremely territorial and attack anyone fishing in the area.
author: .izik

entry: Because of the holes in its fins, POKENAME struggles to swim. When defending its nest, however, it forcefully launches itself at invaders with its sharp horn.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME have very dull wing scales that flake off easily, leading many Trainers to simply dismiss them out of hand. Those Trainers who do care for them find that these Pokémon respond well to affection and are happiest when praised.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Believing itself to be ugly, POKENAME is timid and tends to hide its face. Only a patient and comforting Trainer can turn a POKENAME into a confident battler.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME feeds on grass near secluded lakes. It lacks Tauros's penchant for rage, so small bloodsucking Pokémon like Zubat often perch on it and feed; all POKENAME does is roll and gallop around to try and shake them off.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is extremely hardy and can survive most environments. However, when it comes to Pokémon battles, its often used last as it has no strength.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: It freezes in surprise if anyone looks at it, refusing to blink. This reaction releases an icy chill that spreads through the surrounding water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often used to make people and Pokémon feel better about themselves. When it transforms, it's always uglier than its target.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: It is considered an "old-school" Pokémon. POKENAME are well-suited to performing repetitive tasks.
author: .towerxvi

entry: POKENAME commonly sit upon the bottom of large bodies of water. They sleep for up to seventeen hours at a time before coming up for a breath of air.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME is a rare sight at hot springs. It loves soaking up the warmth and steam. When it's spotted by someone, however, it quickly runs away.
author: archserpent

entry: Although POKENAME is quite aggressive and protective of its territory, its ugly appearance makes its power unrespected by intruders. Even if its wings are greatly injured and lack many feathers, it still has the strength and hardiness to fly.
author: soup1900

entry: The lures that resemble a Prism Scale and Oran Berry do not actually have any corresponding functionality or purpose. POKENAME is shy and comes up only in still spots of water to consume plant-life.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The light on its antenna resembles an Oran Berry, blinking blue in the sea's depths. It uses this lure to attract unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: When it spots someone on the shoreline, it approaches with a friendly demeanor. It then shoots jets of cold water to distract them and steal items.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was once thought to be a strong swimmer, because of its powerful tail-fin. However, recent observations have concluded that it does not seem to know how to use its tail for swimming, and therefore mainly splashes around in the shallows.
author: thescribe

entry: POKENAME has trouble moving on both land and water. It makes use of thick clusters of plants to hide in.
author: notsaying.

entry: The fins on its body are coated with a thin slime that can induce deep sadness in anyone who touches it. This defense ensures it is rarely disturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is self-conscious about its looks, using mental powers to make itself look more appealing to Trainers. Those that still accept it when it finally lets the illusion pass will have gained an unfailingly loyal friend for life.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spend so much time ignored by Trainers that whenever one approaches them with genuine interest, they become flustered and confused. Once part of a team, POKENAME will show affection by hugging their Trainer with vines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have poor grooming habits, often allowing their fur to get matted and ugly when not taken care of by their Trainer. This leads them to hide themselves away, preferring to not be seen lest they be judged.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a repulsive appearance that resembles a freshly hatched Flying-type Pokémon. Their fuzzy bodies make them unpopular for Trainers, especially since they have difficulty flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Shy and elusive, it unleashes a powerful Pin Missile into the water when spotted. These sharp projectiles deter any potential threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have speckled wings that make them seem like sickly Pokémon. Their default expression rests in a sad frown that scares baby Pokémon, so they try to cover their face when communicating with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Living in warm brackish water, POKENAME clusters together in groups for protection against predators.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME is a weak Pokémon rarely encountered in battles. Instead, it is often captured and consumed as a food source.
author: sand_coffin

entry: It uses the suction cups on its tentacles to cling to piers, observing the sea. If noticed, it panics and scrambles into the water to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appear on PCs with a cooldown marker and a counter if there are more than one POKENAME. People can pick up POKENAME with their cursor to move them and can shift them from one box to another.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many Pokémon avoid it because of its unattractive appearance, so POKENAME is eager to evolve in the hope of becoming magnificent. If anyone rejects its kisses, it hides among the seaweed underwater out of shame.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This Pokémon can usually be found slithering along polluted beaches. POKENAME's face has become popular online as a reaction image.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is not popular on farms due to its shabby appearance and faint, sickly stench. Despite this, those who have drunk POKENAME milk freely admit it is one of the best-tasting among Miltank-related fusions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has learned to protect itself from the Pokémon that think it is easy prey. Rumor has it that its true beauty lies within its hideous shell.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: POKENAME has a very shy and introverted nature, since many Trainers tend to overlook it because of its appearance. It lives in large groups with others of its kind along the shores of small lakes, usually rich in the algae it loves to eat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has a sullen and downtrodden personality, with a posture to match. Its low self-esteem means it becomes fiercely loyal and attached to those who show it genuine kindness and affection.
author: sk372

entry: Happiny has been noted to find Feebas's appearance very cute and endearing. The pair become inseparable in the wild, and Feebas become markedly stronger and healthier after the bond is formed.
author: sk372

entry: It tries to play with others, but is often bullied away for its shoddy appearance. It's unfathomably loyal to those who look past its exterior and treat it with kindness.
author: sk372

entry: When it is mocked by other Pokémon for its appearance, POKENAME digs a hole at the bottom of its lake and stays there for days, crying. It combs the beaches in search of objects that might make it look prettier and more elegant.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rarely interacts with other Pokémon, ashamed of its hideous appearance. It will somberly dance across the river's surface when it thinks no one is watching.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is highly self-conscious about its appearance. It protects those it cares for with psychic powers from afar, too ashamed of its looks to be in close proximity to them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in constant misery and rarely shows any hint of joy. The kindest of Trainers might coax a smile out of this sorry Pokémon, though.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME is a bit overly-affectionate to those it considers friends. At any moment, it may approach and decide to smother a friend with kisses from its fake mouth's huge lips.
author: sk372

entry: For people who can afford large water tanks, POKENAME are often chosen to purify the water. By feeding off specks of food and algae, they ensure that other Pokémon in a tank have clean, pure water to drink from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's legs are barely strong enough to hold up its heavy, sturdy cranium, so it has to rest constantly. Being struck directly from the front causes a reflexive reaction that makes it make an absurd facial expression.
author: sk372

entry: Though it is simpleminded and weak offensively, POKENAME is surprisingly hardy, resisting harm from both predators and harsh environments. It often shields smaller Pokémon from harm by letting them hide in its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME appears to be self-conscious about its appearance, disappearing quickly in shame if something manages to spot it. Those that leave gifts for it to retrieve later are said to be blessed with good luck for their kindness and acceptance.
author: sk372

entry: Due to constantly molting its feathers, it cannot swim in water that is too cold. It is so ashamed of its appearance that it almost never wants to go to shore.
author: mistymagius

entry: For a long time, experts believed the spots on its feathers were caused by a strange illness. POKENAME spends most of its time underwater searching for algae to feed on.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is found in muddy lakebeds and riverbeds. It is eager to be used as a weapon by any Trainer, but is unimpressive and unwieldy.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The underside of its body glows at night, resembling a stunning colorful stained-glass pattern. Artists are often inspired by this ethereal beauty.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its pair of majestic wings, POKENAME prefers to stay hidden underwater to avoid being seen. This has led to the belief that it lost the ability to take flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's powerful wings allow it to take flight directly from the water. This is rarely seen, however, as it much prefers to wallow beneath the waves.
author: danarchosyndacalist

entry: POKENAME shies away from others, as it feels self-conscious about its appearance. It still wants to make others happy, though, so it hides itself and rubs its feelers on people in secret, acting as an unknown comforter.
author: sk372

entry: Despite harboring immense power capable of parting seas, this Pokémon's poor physiology diminishes any force that it could've otherwise unleashed.
author: slowforest

entry: POKENAME constantly sheds scraps of its skin, so it has a shabby appearance. Those who see through to the truth find it's a beautifully kind Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME achieves greater elevations by sucking in massive amounts of air to bloat its body. Holding its breath for too long causes it visible distress.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is hairless, but it retains fur on its head and ears. POKENAME tends to swim with its ears above the water to keep its fur neat and dry.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME mournfully watch Pokémon Trainers from the long grass, too self-conscious of their unkempt appearance to approach. They create dancing lights in the air to try and draw Trainers to them, the lights disappearing just before they're found.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Incredibly shy, it spits globs of Gastro Acid into the water around itself when spotted. This tactic serves as a distraction while it escapes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggle to make disguises to hide in, finding only poor quality materials with a shabby appearance. They dislike their natural appearance and this is preferable, allowing them to search for higher quality materials without being observed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite their blindness, POKENAME can live in the toughest of environments, eating anything that comes their way. Though unattractive at first glance, Pokémon Hunters know better and have been hunting them down for their scales after they evolve.
author: beatdoof

entry: Despite its ugly, dilapidated appearance, it is able to swim incredibly fast. It is known to dominate lake ecosystems.
author: .towerxvi

entry: It wraps itself in seaweed and sleeps beneath lakes. It can supposedly grant wishes, but nobody has bothered to try.
author: .towerxvi

entry: Its singing is atonal and discordant, but manages to make others fall asleep all the same. While its victim slumbers, POKENAME will vandalize their face, to make them look as shabby as it does.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is found in shallow pits by the shore, where they hide from predators. If you step on a POKENAME it will try to bite you, but since it is toothless, it is also harmless.
author: thescribe

entry: After fusing, POKENAME's body grew longer, similar to its evolution. Though its appearance is still considered by most to be shabby, it seems much happier with its new form.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME alternates between staring at its prism scale and at blankly into the distance every few hours. It will rarely stop this cycle to eat algae.
author: duskrd

entry: POKENAME are often the secret success to community and city gardens. Planted in soil beds, the mists they produce are natural pest repellents.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: Due to its ugly appearance and Drifloon's reputation, children are warned against going near POKENAME.  It has no ill motives however; all POKENAME wishes for is to be held by a happy child.
author: sk372

entry: Its ugliness deters other spirits. As a result, sailors like to use POKENAME to fend off ghost ships and bad luck.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: At the bottom of coastal waters, it is common to meet small groups of POKENAME walking together. They defend their territory against Magiolett.
author: elevn.

entry: Some Trainers have the feeling that they might be hurting their POKENAME's feelings. In truth, POKENAME are just always feeling down.
author: funkytomate

entry: Preferring solitude, it buries itself in sand near the sea. If accidentally uncovered, it releases a mild spark to scare away intruders before finding a new hiding spot.
author: .izik

entry: It stares intently at food before eating, but the slightest movement from others scares it. It quickly hides, waiting for the danger to pass.
author: .izik

entry: All of its leaves fall off as soon as they grow. Its trunk is very weak, so it is prone to wilting.
author: .towerxvi

entry: POKENAME are rarely known to be aggressive. This may be due to nobody trying to pick them up or show them affection.
author: .towerxvi

entry: Its anchor has broken off and flipped upside down, making it look caught in a perpetual frown.
author: .towerxvi

entry: While it still craves Corsola branches, it struggles to consume them without any teeth. Due to this, some populations of POKENAME are malnourished.
author: typhloquil

entry: POKENAME stand mournfully in the rain, lamenting that their presence drives away bird Pokémon. They long to be beautiful and try anything they can to stand out and draw attention to themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME watches with jealousy as sandcastles get built on the beach. Seething with envy, it often lashes out and destroys the finished structures in petty vengeance, making its reputation very poor among beach-goers.
author: sk372

entry: It watches picnicking travelers from nearby lakes, pretending to be shy if spotted. It splashes water and winks in hopes of receiving free food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely shy and hides in remote lagoons. If cornered, however, it lashes out with claws sharp enough to cleave concrete into pieces.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that prejudice against ugly Pokémon summons it to appear at the periphery of populated areas. Bullies who hear its cries are cursed with bad luck.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME are incredibly enthusiastic about approaching boats. They pop out of the water to watch them pass by, but they often end up in the way instead.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME often leaps from the water into the arms of couples it spots, wanting to cheer on their blossoming love. Unfortunately, its shoddy appearance often leads to it being tossed back into the depths.
author: sk372

entry: Its constant headaches cause it to psychically relive embarrassing moments from those around it. This makes its headaches worse, creating a vicious cycle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often laughed at by young children for the odd way it swims around. It can often be seen carried away slowly by river currents, floating in the water whilst somehow remaining perfectly upright.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME miserably cries from loneliness since Pokémon and Trainers reject its unsightly appearance. The more it cries, the more beautiful its voice becomes, leading to evolution.
author: pokebio

entry: It perches on lily pads, glaring at passing Trainers with a judgmental stare. If approached, it trips over itself in a frantic attempt to escape underwater.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME does not breathe well on land, and does not swim well either. They always seem tired, but loyally obey their Trainers and try fighting.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME are covered in scales that are as tough as their shell. They are regarded as ugly Pokémon because their scales are a dull and unappealing color.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Living in deep underwater caves, it avoids attention at all costs. When spotted by divers, it emits a bone-chilling Screech and flees into the darkness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lie amongst the pebbles and stones at the bottom of riverbeds, their drab stony hides helping them to blend in. Given the opportunity, they gather precious stones and jewels, covering their bodies with them to try and look pretty.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lie amongst the pebbles and stones at the bottom of riverbeds, their drab stony hides helping them to blend in. Given the opportunity, they gather precious stones and jewels, covering their bodies with them to try and look pretty.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's body is made of sedimentary rock. It blends in with the stones at the bottom of a riverbed, allowing it to ambush prey.
author: hophoppip

entry: It uses psychic powers to sense the thoughts of those who approach. If it detects interest in interaction, it goes completely still, pretending to be unnoticed.
author: .izik

entry: Its body consists of corrosive slime that drifts across the water's surface. The slime absorbs plant life it touches, extracting vital nutrients.
author: .izik

entry: Its acidic slime spreads thinly across the surface of ponds. When prey enters the water, the slime wraps around them instantly, trapping them.
author: .izik

entry: It produces stunning blue pearls within its shell. When pursued, it tosses the pearls onto nearby sand, hoping to distract the pursuer with treasure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather on the undersides of abandoned fishing boats. They emanate a putrid gas, akin to rotten fish.
author: .towerxvi

entry: Those that have witnessed POKENAME have regarded it as utterly horrifying to behold. This has given it incredibly low self-esteem, as it is not trying to be scary in the least.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scavenge food off the seafloor. They use their claw fins to attract mates, and their tails to stir up sand on the seafloor to evade enemies.
author: totodile.

entry: Despite being a fish, POKENAME live their lives on dry land. With tall grass hiding their legs, they often startle people by appearing to 'swim' through the air while chasing prey.
author: kiwiarms

entry: The shells on their backs are said to be full of nutrients gained from bathing in sunlight. These shells are harder than diamonds, so nothing has yet been able to break through them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME crawls onto the top of branches carrying berries, headbutting them until the treat falls to the forest floor. It then divebombs head-first to the ground after it, the tough shell on its cranium protecting it from the impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scavenge around the graveyards of Dragon-type Pokémon, using the bones of long dead Pokémon to protect themselves and use as weapons. They are protective of their chosen weapons and armour, wearing them constantly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME scavenge through the remains of larger Pokémon that have died in the mountains for suitable bones to use as weapons. They prize the bones of Dragon-type Pokémon the most and can swing them with enough force to shatter boulders.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses its long tongue to knock foes off balance before ramming them with its skull. Its skull becomes harder than granite if its diet is rich in minerals.
author: .izik

entry: The vines that writhe around POKENAME's body are as hard as bone, despite their flexibility. It uses these vines to uproot shrubs and devour them whole.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have hardened skulls that they use to spar with one another, butting heads to establish dominance. They will try and fly into other Pokémon head first to attack, but their top flight speed is too low to cause much harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If POKENAME fails to slice through a tree during training, it headbutts the trunk until it falls. Once successful, it strikes a triumphant pose atop the fallen tree.
author: .izik

entry: Its jealousy towards flying Pokémon has turned to aggression. If it spies one flying above its waters, it will launch itself from the water at high speed in an attempt to headbutt them out of the sky.
author: sk372

entry: It wants to fly without the use of shapeshifting, launching its gelatinous body from great heights as practice. Fortunately its soft form makes the impact with the ground painless.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME crashes its head against objects on computer screens, hardening it over time. These impacts often cause damage to programs, so its appearance is seen as a nuisance to most.
author: sk372

entry: While POKENAME always hope of flying into space, their bodies cannot handle altitudes too high up. If they try to continue further, their bodies will start to fail before shutting down and falling headfirst back into the ground.
author: soup1900

entry: Although POKENAME has achieved Bagon's dream of flight through its powerful wings, it lacks the stamina to fly for extended periods of time. Therefore, POKENAME is always willing to train in order to strengthen its endurance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although POKENAME has achieved Bagon's dream of flight through its powerful wings, it lacks the stamina to fly for extended periods of time. Therefore, POKENAME is always willing to train in order to strengthen its endurance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although POKENAME has achieved Bagon's dream of flight through its powerful wings, it lacks the stamina to fly for extended periods of time. Therefore, POKENAME is always willing to train in order to strengthen its endurance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Having grown far too heavy to get off the ground, POKENAME spends its days eating its feelings away, dreaming about the open sky and weeping silently.
author: kecleonfan352

entry: POKENAME whiles away its days with constant eating and sleeping. Dream analysis shows that a majority of its dreams involve it being able to fly through the skies.
author: sk372

entry: It clamps its mouth around a foe's head before attempting to ensnare them with its long body. Its body is covered in tiny, soft scales that glow when wet.
author: .izik

entry: Stubborn and impulsive, POKENAME will charge down the first thing it sees entering its territory. Despite the heavy and deadly stingers it wields, its main force of attack is a high-speed diving headbutt.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swoop at one another headfirst, using their hardened skulls to bash into their rivals at high speed. The sound of the clash between them is loud enough to be heard from hundreds of meters away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is surprisingly clever, able to solve complex logic puzzles. It's a favored companion of programmers.
author: hophoppip

entry: It can secrete a venom-soaked web from its jaws, using it to trap its prey. It battles other POKENAME to maintain dominance over its hunting grounds, driving away weaker individuals with devastating blows from its head, reinforced by bony plates.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME frequently gets distracted when swimming, turning its head to look at everything. It sometimes accidentally headbutts rocks or other Pokémon, which sends it spinning away, dazed but unhurt.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: With enhanced intellect thanks to the biting shell upon its skull, POKENAME sees the folly of leaping off cliffs in vain hopes of flight. It now spends time pondering less self-destructive ways of achieving its dream.
author: sk372

entry: The shell of its head has grown to encase the leaves of the bulb upon its back, protecting it but also restraining its growth. It must always move when awake to ensure that its legs can support its shell and bulb.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME frequently leaps off rocky outcrops in a desperate attempt to fly. When it inevitably fails, it slams the ground with its horn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is constantly toughening itself up by carrying its weighty shell everywhere it goes.  If attacked, it will slam its head into this shell, creating an explosion of magma.
author: imaginita

entry: The skin covering its body its extremely coarse to the touch. One should avoid petting a POKENAME to prevent injury.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME casts itself from the highest peaks to practice for the day it will finally fly. Its massive size and strength mean the impact tremor it creates hitting the ground can be felt from hundreds of yards away.
author: sk372

entry: Despite being strong and muscular, POKENAME struggles to fly due to its heavy weight and relatively small wings. It never stops trying though, as it dreams of reaching the top of a rainbow one day.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME are very intelligent creatures. When they're not scavenging the remains of a more powerful Pokémon's prey, wild POKENAME play dead and attack whatever approaches them.
author: autismgaming89_51746

entry: POKENAME throws itself into battle with others using the bone-like blades in its arms. It mixes these strikes with powerful headbutts to make sure the covering over its skull remains hard and sturdy.
author: sk372

entry: It makes a low-frequency noise that sounds similar to a bell while it flies. It clamps onto the sides of cave walls with its fierce jaws.
author: .izik

entry: It eats ore in order to absorb their nutrients. POKENAME prefers copper and silver ore over all other types of ore due to the flavor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME longingly stare at the sky, hoping to someday fly amidst the clouds. Although bird Pokémon love to land upon its large flower, it will shake them off and snap at them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME attacks by headbutting its opponent, which is made possible with its reinforced head crest. Its large leg muscles also allow it to wind up power before unleashing a powerful slam.
author: quackquackattack

entry: For the longest period of time, the only proof of this Pokémon's existence was a single photograph in a magazine. It is quite striking.
author: barthandelus_real

entry: POKENAME has the ability to generate illusions that distort its surroundings, a trick it usually uses to hide the entrance to its cave. It is a short-tempered Pokémon, and if someone makes it lose its patience, it retaliates with a powerful headbutt.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's ribbon has a numbing agent that soothes pain, which it uses primarily on itself. It leaps off high areas and lands on its head, attempting to fly, so it often needs relief for the pain in its cranium.
author: sk372

entry: The muscles in POKENAME's legs allow it to kick with destructive force and bound away quickly if in a rough spot. It stares at bird Pokémon in the sky, envious of their ability to fly.
author: chibitales

entry: Its skin can dry out quickly and crack. Due to this, wild POKENAME tend to stay close to rivers, creeks, and other bodies of water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME performs backflips in an attempt to mimic professional fighters. Its heavy skull often causes it to stumble mid-routine, frustrating it greatly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is most energized at sunrise, wildly swinging its arms while gazing at the morning sky. During this time, its skull glimmers with a faint blue hue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME throws itself off cliffs several times a day in hopes of one day achieving flight. This results in its armored top half becoming harder than steel over time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grows stronger by recklessly charging at anything it perceives as a threat. The thick scales that run across its back shine like polished stones.
author: mepp.

entry: The helmet on its body is made of an extremely hard metal. It smashes its helmet into trees to break branches off and eat the fruit.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will tap friends and loved ones with their hard heads, though if they get too excited they may strike them with a Headbutt. They love to roast their foods with their flames before eating, even if the food was already cooked.
author: infinex21

entry: The muscles in POKENAME's ears are so strong, a single punch can knock the wind out of a Snorlax. Its cotton-like fur often gets matted and must be groomed to maintain its health.
author: chibitales

entry: Even though they can float through the air, envy drives POKENAME to use their sharp horn to attack other flying Pokémon.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to winged Pokémon in hopes of learning the secrets of flight. It zaps its host with static electricity when they stop flying to startle them into taking off again.
author: soup1900

entry: Since ancient times, blacksmiths have used POKENAME to forcibly shape metal. This is due to the Pokémon's high tolerance to heat.
author: .izik

entry: It pierces enemies with the spikes on its arms. Should the spike break off, it will regrow slowly over the course of one week.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to fly in the sky and perform aerial maneuvers for the sheer thrill of the wind against their face. They release happy little high-pitched screeches whenever they perform a successful maneuver.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's hard forehead is coated with a sticky, white poison. A single Headbutt leaves foes covered in a residue that causes dizziness and clings to clothing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are slow, but have powerful hind legs that can allow them to leap great distances. They are hardy Pokémon and will ram into obstacles with enough strength to shatter boulders.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME in the wild duel each other by ramming their heads together until one gives up. Whenever they achieve victory, they release a triumphant roar that can be heard from a mile away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The plates covering its head allow it to unleash headbutts so powerful they can leave dents even in a ship's hull. POKENAME is a very aggressive creature, so it is advised to approach it with extreme caution.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its ears are comprised of flexible, impact-resistant bundles of muscle fibers. It can wrap its ears around its head to better protect its skull.
author: staghorn

entry: The cotton-like substance on its wings comes off in clumps as it flies. Its wings are extremely soft and were once used to stuff mattresses.
author: .izik

entry: It releases a sticky substance while it moves across the ground. The slime it leaves behind smells like rotting vegetables.
author: .izik

entry: Its shell has grown thick and sturdy from constant attempts to fly, giving it strong defenses. The shell's growth has now obscured its vision, however, making it a bit clumsy.
author: sk372

entry: The scales on POKENAME's body, as well as its skull, glisten during heavy rain. These scales are sometimes harvested by jewelers to craft decorative shower curtains.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits telekinetic waves through its antennae, using them to levitate discarded toys in an effort to simulate flight. It nests near toy stores, hoping to find the perfect abandoned toy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a hot-tempered Pokémon that breathes searing flames at anyone who approaches. Its anger stems from shame over its inability to take flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It can burrow through solid rock with ease. It hunts its prey by burrowing under them and launching them into the air with a powerful headbutt.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME leaps from the water and headbutts anything it deems as being disruptive to romance in its vicinity. Conversely, it's been observed headbutting avian Pokémon and attempting to disturb their mating rituals.
author: sk372

entry: It tunnels through the ground at extremely high speeds. Should it encounter a rock, it will use its thick skulls to break through the stone.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME are very cute, they make terrible companions. They have highly destructive habits and are prone to behavioural issues that make them hard to manage.
author: pix3l_655

entry: Eyewitness reports claim a blue glow surrounds POKENAME at night. It's said to shine brightest under a full moon.
author: captainjefejefe

entry: POKENAME balances on the edge of cliffs before hurling its heavy stone body off head-first in an attempt to achieve true flight. When it impacts the ground, it emits a bright flash of warm sunlight.
author: sk372

entry: As if to show off its powerful wings, this Pokémon will eagerly engage in aerial battles. It has proven to be a problem for aerial craft, as it has also tried to fight with planes and jets.
author: infinex21

entry: It uses its strong jaws to break open coconuts, which seem to be its favored food. It spends much of its days attempting to climb tall palm trees to get closer to the sky above; this may be why its head is so tough, as this protects it from falls.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are slow moving Pokémon that lumber through mountain ravines in the certainty that very few things can truly threaten them. Their shells are nearly five inches thick, protecting them from most physical threats.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When a ruckus is heard at night, POKENAME has likely caught the scent of dreams of flight, and will not respond to outside interference even from the most trusted of Trainers as it drains away these dreams, even from those wide awake.
author: lovelover75

entry: POKENAME uses its Dragon Fang to increase its draconic energy. Those who are put to sleep by this Pokémon experience wishful dreams of flight.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME need not eat nor drink to thrive; they need only to sit and bathe in sunlight and rain. They only move if they feel they are not being bathed in enough of either.
author: infinex21

entry: Each of the eggs has a very hard scaly shell. No one understands how this fusion can fly if it does not have any wings.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME often feel empowered to bully other Pokémon because they have thick, protective plates around their head. When they are inevitably humbled by another Pokémon, they often throw a tantrum to release their frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are very selfless and can be seen throwing themselves into danger to protect weaker Pokémon. While not usually worrying about their own safety, they will go into a panic if their egg gets damaged.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's wings are actually made of thin scales which allow them to block incoming attacks. Despite its friendly nature, it will constantly have territorial disputes with other POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: It looks gelatinous at a glance, but POKENAME is actually coated with a thin yet sturdy shell around its soft insides. A transformation unlike its shapeshifting capabilities is taking place within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are rarely seen, as they are constantly afraid of damaging their exposed bodies. They hide in small burrows, only peeking their armored heads out to check for danger.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are known to inhabit mountainous regions. If approached, they retract into their shells to flee by rolling down slopes. In hopes of one day taking flight, they spend years journeying to become strong enough to scale even the highest peaks.
author: aurange

entry: POKENAME knock heads together hard as a form of greeting, their armour is so thick they do not feel it. Unfortunately, they also do this to those of other species, which often stuns them. POKENAME watch over them as they recover but never learn.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The flower bulbs upon their backs struggle to grow due to the shells encasing their leaves and much of the bulbs themselves. The petals of these flower bulbs grow more vibrant as they near their evolution.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's long legs are deceptively strong, able to send heavy Pokémon like Metagross flying with a single kick.
author: lyrebird.rainwing

entry: The segments of POKENAME's body rotate in sequence from tail to head. When the rotation speeds up rapidly, it's a sign that its evolution is imminent.
author: sk372

entry: As a rather dimwitted Pokémon, POKENAME makes its habitat in the same location as Magcargo, and will often join their colonies, forgetting that it is not one of them. Surges of draconic energy from its shell remind POKENAME of this fact.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Despite its size, it digs voraciously in search for mushrooms. Only the most plump of POKENAME manage to evolve.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME's bodies are mostly muscle, allowing them to support the heavy shell around their necks. When provoked, they will slam this shell against the ground to deter predators, the shell breaking off once they're ready to evolve.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can be found on the tallest peaks, patiently waiting for its desired evolution. However, if they are too impatient, they will throw themselves off the cliff before they are ready to evolve.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time resting at the foot of rainbows, conserving energy for its evolution. The shell it sheds is said to bestow luck unto those who carry its fragments.
author: badtothebow

entry: POKENAME sleeps curled in a ball deep within icy caves. Its frilled plating wards off ambushes, and the surrounding air drops by ten degrees as it slumbers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's steel armor helps protect them from attack, giving them ample time to escape from danger. By curling up into a ball, they are practically untouchable, able to withstand both intense heat and crushing force.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's tough scales do not grow naturally, so it can be seen collecting other Dragon Pokémon's scales. It has trouble getting around, usually scaling cliff faces with its strong arms and claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can be found digging out large cave systems, with its tough scales shielding it from falling debris. While not fazed by most attacks, it will chase away anyone that disturbs its digging.
author: mistymagius

entry: The shell coating much of POKENAME's body gives it additional protection, but hampers its speed and maneuverability somewhat. Despite this, it is an efficient hunter, able to prey even on vicious creatures such as Hydreigon on occasion.
author: sk372

entry: It needs only sunlight to sustain itself, but it moves very slow to conserve some of its nutrients for its evolution. Most of its central body is protected by a hard shell that it can withdraw its legs into.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's exterior shell is almost impenetrable, but the heavy weight and huge size means it swims at an incredibly slow pace. It filter-feeds at the ocean bottom, awaiting the day it sheds its shell and can swim more freely.
author: sk372

entry: A thick iron shell shields POKENAME's head from cave-ins and ambushes. It constantly searches for iron ore, which it consumes to reinforce its armor.
author: .izik

entry: Wings have developed early for POKENAME, but its heavy shelled body remaining means it's not as agile as it could be. It is still overjoyed to have attained some measure of flight, and glides about happily whenever it can.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body has almost fully changed, with only the wings left to develop. It is anxious and restless, impatiently waiting for when it evolves fully and can finally achieve flight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its feelers to gather moss from the walls of its cavern home. At night it covers itself in this moss to avoid confrontation while it waits to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's heavy shell around a lighter-than-air center means it can only fly at slow speeds and low altitudes. Despite this, it seems overjoyed at being capable of any type of flight at all.
author: sk372

entry: The heavy plating on its hands and ears makes it hard for POKENAME to move quickly. Instead, it uses these plates to bat away threats and moves to a safer location.
author: chibitales

entry: Ancient records tell of POKENAME aiding in mountain rescues. Its heavy plating allowed it to march through avalanches unscathed, carrying survivors to safety.
author: .izik

entry: Due to their protective padding, POKENAME can be incredibly reckless, often headbutting Pokémon far stronger than themselves. When they are bored, the two heads will start headbutting each other for fun.
author: mistymagius

entry: In tight-knit packs, POKENAME scuttles through caverns in search of silver ore. A single group can consume over 50 tons in just one week.
author: .izik

entry: Because of it's accelerated growth due to fusion, POKENAME has tripled it's normal shell size to accommodate for it's quickly growing body.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME rarely ever moves until it has evolved. The plates that composed the outer armor for POKENAME are oddly warm to touch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The heaviness of POKENAME's shell causes it to weigh down aerial Pokémon it clings onto. The more static electricity it absorbs, the faster the cells within its body change, and the closer it gets to evolution.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's scales are quite resistant to damage, but it doesn't grow them quickly enough to really aid it in battle. It usually hides away in isolated caves, only coming out once it has grown enough scales.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME glides through tunnels, emitting sonar pulses from its metallic body. It can map an entire cave system in pitch-black darkness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is tough but elastic, allowing it to roll on any terrain it chooses. They tend to roll down large hills to build speed; once they start rolling, they are almost impossible to stop.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a heavily armoured back that protects it from larger Pokémon. When threatened, it curls into a ball to shield its softer underbelly from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's tough carapace and rough scales protect it from predators. It darts fearlessly across open waters, picking off prey before they can react to its presence.
author: mepp.

entry: While it mostly stays in its shell, it has a tendency to headbutt passing Trainers. It doesn't move very much, usually getting around by rolling around in its shell.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME mushrooms have thick, chitinous layers that protect their soft body from harm. They can pull themselves totally inside the bell of their mushroom, hiding away until the danger's passed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While POKENAME often gets into sparring matches with one another, they pride themselves on their defensive maneuvers. Their scales are both tough and flexible, preventing them from being bent out of shape.
author: mistymagius

entry: In battle, POKENAME hoists its loose skin over its head and stiffens it into a metal-like shield. POKENAME charges headfirst into foes, confident in its armor.
author: .izik

entry: The muscular plates covering its body allow it to fight fiercely without worrying about getting hurt. In the wild, this variant of POKENAME tends to nest on the rocky peaks of Hoenn.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In the wild, this form of POKENAME tends to make its home in the rocky caves located in Kanto. When it fights fiercely against another Dragon-type Pokémon, the flame on its tail swells to great proportions.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a protective band of muscle that absorbs the impact of any blow. It soars through the sky with majesty, challenging others of its species to see who can reach the highest altitude.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have never been observed outside of their shells, the true structure of their head remaining unknown to researchers. Their shells are several inches thick and are reinforced with crystalline growths, forming an incredibly tough defence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It needs to absorb a considerable amount of solar energy to keep its iron body functioning, so it spends as much time as possible basking in sunlight. When the gear on its back spins, it releases a metallic dust that is toxic to those who inhale it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can revolve so fast and generate so much electricity that they eventually explode.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This strange gear assembly launches its components at a force that can easily crack a skull.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's long, metallic tongue crackles with stray sparks as it eats discarded electronics found in junkyards and landfills.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generally hides away in junkyards, where the shape of its metal cocoon lets it masquerade as a simple scrapped gear and be ignored by most until its evolution can complete.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME spots something in its territory, its gears churn at high speeds to power up a running charge. Once it hits something, the impact temporarily shorts out its gears, leaving it stunned.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME consist of a few basic parts, most notably the turnkey on their back. Young engineers are often tasked with maintaining POKENAME as part of their studies, replacing worn components as necessary.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME adores mimicking machinery by turning its gear-shaped head. Although it delights in this, many people find it creepy or off-putting.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Unfortunately, POKENAME's steel bodies are quite susceptible to rust. They would likely be extinct if not for their fast rate of reproduction.
author: dylonk25

entry: The gear spinning inside POKENAME's body generates the energy needed to fuel a transformation. The bigger the form it wants to change into, the longer it has to churn before it can transform.
author: sk372

entry: Often found near landfills, POKENAME digs through heaps of discarded electronics. Its gears whirr and spin furiously while it feeds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a fairly popular gift for young children. Turning the crank on its side plays a tune, and POKENAME pops out of the box at the climax of the song, before singing its own digitized rendition.
author: sk372

entry: Some think that POKENAME's body has a defective design, as the gears in its chest occasionally jam and leave it unable to use psychic powers. It can forcibly turn and start its gear on its own, but doing so seems to be a painful effort.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME needs to rid itself of excess heat by venting dark flames from its back. The fire creates acrid black smoke as well, and some have raised environmental concerns about the potential pollution it could cause.
author: sk372

entry: Before using its strongest moves, POKENAME readies itself by revving its internal combustion, making flames erupt from its tail. The sound has been likened to a miniature version of a car's engine.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a unique mechanism in their mouths that functions like a mousetrap. When pressure is applied to the tongue, they snap their mouths closed to ensnare food or limbs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The key on its back can be wound to increase POKENAME's electric powers in battle, but caution is needed; winding it too much will cause it to overload and uncontrollably send jolts of lightning all around it.
author: sk372

entry: They are known to float using an Air Balloon, helping them avoid damage from sand, dirt, and grit. They work in factory facilities that are recovering from toxic spills, as they double as backup generators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generate electricity by rotating the gear around their neck. They work in factories where they power large machinery that produces car parts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME commonly helps out in laundromats, where it helps fold clothes. When all the washing machines are occupied, it will allow Trainers to use its sanitizing mouth as a replacement.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME inhabits abandoned factories, swinging from pipe to pipe. When it detects a predator nearby, it bangs its cymbal-like hands together to alert others.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME tilts its head back and forth as it walks. The motion is necessary for forward momentum, as mechanisms in its head connect directly to those in its feet.
author: sk372

entry: A quirk in POKENAME's body causes it to become incredibly thirsty the moment it spots water. It will repeatedly dip its head into water and pull back to drink, until all the liquid is drank.
author: sk372

entry: This variant of POKENAME can replenish energy through the Berries it feeds on, allowing it to remain active even during prolonged rainy periods. When the gear on its back begins spinning counterclockwise, it signals that POKENAME is ready for battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are Pokémon powered by clockwork, the speed at which their gears turn varying depending on how much sunlight they receive. Under the midday sun they are warm enough that their gears can run at peak efficiency, letting them move at speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME glides through construction sites at night, chewing through bulldozers. It digests metal to reinforce its own grinding gears.
author: .izik

entry: Despite POKENAME's steel exoskeletons, they are lighter than a Heracross. They are notorious among Bug Catchers for breaking traps set for Bug-types with their jagged limbs and eating the bait.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: Its hand extends with multiple tools, each designed for a different task it faces. When POKENAME is agitated, thick smoke pours from the vents on its head, growing heavier with the intensity of its emotions.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME constantly eats coal or soil, which it burns in its body to power itself. It can reach speeds of up to 35 mph.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's heavy body and stiff movements make flying nearly impossible for it. It's blade-like wings can be fired off as projectiles that will return to POKENAME's body after use.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME charges across wastelands while rolling at high speed. Sparks fly from its gear as it discharges bursts of electricity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to prance daintily through the forest, but most onlookers describe its movements as strange and uncanny. Odd radio waves seem to emanate from its metallic antlers at night.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes its home in abandoned textile factories, gnawing on forgotten machines. Its body hums with electric energy as it feeds and powers up.
author: .izik

entry: Though highly elusive, POKENAME has been sought out due to a curious functionality it has exhibited. Machines that have stopped functioning due to water damage will begin working again after a short amount of exposure to POKENAME's presence.
author: sk372

entry: It can temporarily detach its limbs to attack from afar, though they must return shortly  before they run out of power. If deprived of all its limbs, it radiates intense magnetic waves to disorient others until it can retrieve its body parts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hides itself in toy stores, blending in among the products on display. When an unsuspecting Trainer brings the Pokémon home, POKENAME begins snacking on the household's electronics.
author: dodoowner_

entry: In battle, the gears on POKENAME's body rotate faster to generate intense heat. It's said that many famous inventors were blessed with a surge of inspiration after witnessing its magnificence.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME work alongside toymakers to produce fun contraptions to capture the attention of children. On the rare occasion that there is no work, they juggle gears to pass the time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's telepathy allows it to predict its foes' attacks in battle. Its determination increases to meet the aggression it senses in its opponents.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: While POKENAME has a variety of tool extensions on its arms, evolution has made it strongly favor using its chainsaw arm. Trainers often have to repeatedly teach POKENAME what it can and can't rip up.
author: beatdoof

entry: The individual gears rotate and generate energy, which is converted into magnetic waves via the antenna on the head.
author: chorb33

entry: Researchers have occasionally mistaken a curled-up POKENAME for some sort of sandy, mechanical artifact. Trying to pick it up will result in it burrowing deep into the ground.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME lives near factories and power plants. It can be seen absorbing carbon dioxide from the smokestacks.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's strength has been significantly improved thanks to its cybernetics and can see targets from up to 200ft away!
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME works alongside people in factories and construction sites, where its small size allows it to reach into tight spaces. It enjoys the tactile sensation work provides, needing reminders from its Trainer to rest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The metal on POKENAME's body can absorb sunlight to use as energy. Many broccoli farmers employ it to defend and work their farmlands.
author: .izik

entry: It generates the energy it needs to live by always moving its legs, even while asleep. Its internal flames remain strong as long as it has energy; if its hard body ever cools, it is a sign that it is in poor health.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME runs through mountainous terrain to generate the energy it needs to live. When POKENAME rests, its gear head slowly spins. This Pokémon wakes up when it feels its reserves are growing low and begins running again.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's gear-shaped head rotates regularly to keep its energy up. It enjoys taking dips in mud puddles, but must be careful lest the mud gunk up its gear, slowing its rotation and causing physical issues.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes its nest near hydroelectric power plants, latching onto them to siphon power at night. During the day, it has an odd ability to increase the plant's productivity.
author: .izik

entry: The rate at which POKENAME's gear turns depends on the emotions around it. Positive emotions let it turn smoothly, while negative emotions cause it to lag, which in turn causes POKENAME to act sickly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's large ear-gears are finely tuned to its surroundings, giving it excellent hearing and senses. When startled, the gears churn quickly and enhance its mobility so it can better flee from danger.
author: sk372

entry: An oily coating allows POKENAME's metal body to shift color with its surroundings. It hides in derelict factories, perfectly camouflaged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME operates heavy machinery by using its psychic power, its advanced calculations allowing it to produce precise movements. It helps researchers working with corrosive acids to discover and produce new chemicals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses subtle psychic waves to influence factory workers during repairs. It finds deep satisfaction in watching machinery run smoothly.
author: .izik

entry: When fed logs, it dispenses planks of wood which it then uses to construct simple crafts.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME has protective instincts, primarily for young and small Steel-type Pokémon. The large gear on its back can churn at high speeds to let POKENAME breathe a hot steam that obscures the area, facilitating escape for it and its charges.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's bodies are quite rigid, using the massive claws on their heads for more fine-tuned movements. They are often used in scrapyards, helping to dismantle cars and move heavy scrap.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME haunts abandoned technical warehouses. It makes itself home in the leftover gears and wires, taking one for its own face.
author: lesbian_garlicbread

entry: Turning the key on POKENAME's head a few times boosts its energy, hastening its speed and increasing its strength. Turning too much will cause it to act haywire or even collapse completely, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fire burns an odd silvery color. It will become furious if one attempts to stop the gears from spinning.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME's large ear-gears are finely tuned to its surroundings, giving it excellent hearing and senses. When startled, the gears churn quickly and enhance its strength, improving its ability to combat danger.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefer tobogganing to waddling as the sliding action helps turn the gears and provide them the energy needed to survive. If they are on flat, snowy land, POKENAME will use their feet to propel themselves across the icy surface.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME remains stationary until its key is turned. Once properly wound up, it marches forward at a steady pace, puffing out steam from its large nose with a high-pitched whistle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's gears cause its blade to vibrate, cutting into the body of its victims. It is continuously powered by the life force it harvests.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME starts combat in a defensive stance, absorbing blows and gathering energy through its rotating gear-shield. Once fully charged, it enters attack mode, unsheathing its blade as the light on its gear turns red.
author: sk372

entry: The many gears comprising POKENAME's internals work in conjunction to provide it energy and mobility. Churning at max power simultaneously, POKENAME can move incredibly fast, but becomes incredibly aggressive as well.
author: sk372

entry: If the gear on POKENAME's head is halted, it becomes frozen in place, unable to attack. Once the gear restarts, it continues with furious speed.
author: deelee2020

entry: Many gears turning across POKENAME's body give it vast reservoirs of energy for offense and defense. Its tactics in battle are incredibly basic though, smashing about with little strategic thought involved.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME trundle forward on reinforced wheels, racing forward at high speed when they spy another Pokémon encroaching on their home territory. They fight by whirling their arms at high speed and slamming their tails into their foes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a colossal being made entirely of steel, with massive indestructible gears that keep its limbs in constant motion. Legends say it has enough power to reverse the world's rotation if it ever wished to.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Originally thought to be ideal for assembly-line labor, this Pokémon has adapted its functions to suit combat situations. Its cannon modulates based on enemy composition, feeding on external data to predict and counter its opponent's moves.
author: jaminmcready

entry: These Pokémon were found to be extremely useful as high-output capacitors when linked to machinery through the gear on their backs. While it is unknown how much energy they can store, they are able to output at 100,000 MWh for extended durations.
author: the_cardinals

entry: Its bulb emits a natural blue glow that shifts in intensity with its emotions. When calm, the light flickers gently, but during moments of excitement or fear, it blazes brightly, illuminating its surroundings.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The blue lightbulb in POKENAME's core resembles a flame but emits no heat. At night, it perches atop cranes, letting loose tiny sparks as its bulb glows.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME claims abandoned electronics warehouses as its territory. If disturbed, it emits a piercing metallic cry and discharges static bursts.
author: .izik

entry: As it burrows beneath Lum Berry trees, POKENAME's neck gear spins rapidly. It knocks Berries loose by releasing bolts of electricity.
author: .izik

entry: The dams POKENAME builds are made of a mix of metal scraps and wood. Despite this, they never seem to rust.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME build up energy by rapidly hitting metal. This makes them a nuisance in cities, so some choose to place metal dummies by the outskirts of town for POKENAME to punch instead.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME trains by striking steel beams, leaving large dents behind. It frequents construction sites, where no visible metal goes unharmed.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME loves playing around children. Its tail sparks with static energy as it runs excitedly, but the charge often shocks kids who get too close, driving them away before it can make friends.
author: jaminmcready

entry: To deter predators, POKENAME emits a petrifying screech. This cry is so intense that witnesses report temporarily losing their hearing.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This Pokémon seems unaccustomed to having a third gear, so it sometimes falls out of sync, resulting in all three gears locking and grinding. However, when the gears are perfectly in sync, POKENAME's power is noticeably boosted.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME's gears spin faster the more fired-up it is. Interlocking with other gears is dangerous, as it can grind to a halt if they don't fit perfectly.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME releases clouds of yellow grease-scented powder when happy. Machines nearby operate at twice their normal speed when exposed to this powder.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's flower-shaped gears hum with electricity. It uses stored power to defend its kin from aerial predators like Skarmory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats above wild habitats to scan biometric information for scientists. Its metallic shell stabilizes its movement in tough weather conditions, which makes scanning easier.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each POKENAME will eventually develop a different diet from one another: some will only eat organic foods, while others will just consume minerals. Rarely, there are POKENAME that only rely on magnetic energy in order to live.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The fluff on this Pokémon's body resembles steel wool. It's used frequently to clean medical equipment as it never rusts.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME are mechanical, artificial Pokémon that are used to search hostile environments during search and rescue missions. Despite their small size, they are strong enough to carry travellers to safety from the depths of the desert.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often shelters within abandoned factories, where the remaining machinery acts as its primary food source. Old industrial plants swarm with this Pokémon.
author: daemonkill22

entry: POKENAME defends ancient tombs by unleashing horrifying Shadow Balls. Its tail gear vibrates with ghostly energy before each attack.
author: .izik

entry: While absorbing electricity, POKENAME's gears spin at high speed. It can retain power for months depending on the intensity of the charge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its nests in abandoned mechanical equipment. When a flock inhabits a machine, it sometimes whirrs back to life for short periods.
author: .izik

entry: The metal surrounding POKENAME's body is constantly hot. High-end grills are rumored to use parts from it for consistent heat.
author: .izik

entry: It absorbs the iron in the blood of its prey to heal and add onto itself while leaving scraps on its pressure plate to attract its next prey.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Tiny holes across POKENAME's tin body leak a thick, green poison. Contact with the fluid causes severe irritation.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon's interlocking body allows it to speed through the forest like a mountain bike. It is the source of many natural dirt trails.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its movement is stiff and slow, but it is determined and persistent.  If it chooses to bite at something, it will pursue them no matter the time or distance it takes, until its jaws clamp around its chosen target.
author: sk372

entry: The thick steel shell covering POKENAME is freezing to the touch. Rain freezes instantly upon contact with its frigid frame.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaves are surprisingly healthy, and they're a good source of iron and fiber. They don't taste all too well, though.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is an autonomous Pokémon that was designed to fill itself with garbage, empty itself in the nearest dumpster, and repeat the process.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in metal scales that spark when it leaps from the water. It can leap up to 10 feet above the surface to bite prey such as Wingull.
author: .izik

entry: Its gears work like a wind-up motor. The longer POKENAME rotates it, the faster it can whizz off in one direction.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are said to be born from the spirits of working children during the industrial era. It wanders around abandoned factories and will chase out anyone who tries to rebuild it.
author: mistymagius

entry: Huge colonies of POKENAME can be found in areas that are rich in oil, which they use to lubricate their joints. Their cries are often likened to the striking of typewriter keys.
author: snookerron

entry: It hovers using the magnetism generated by its spinning wings. Flocking POKENAME link wings when at rest; if a predator approaches, it only takes a single POKENAME spinning up for the entire flock to take flight.
author: staghorn

entry: The shovel protruding from POKENAME's gears regularly emits a low-tone signal that causes nearby machines to malfunction slightly. It has difficulty turning this signal off, especially while it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is typically found living near abandoned, rusted machinery. The mushrooms on its back appear normal but are actually made of metal, and can only be safely consumed by Steel-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers with a POKENAME can determine its mood by how fast it's interlocking gears are turning. It contains a near infinite energy, some Trainers aren't able to keep up with POKENAME's playful nature.
author: schwaus

entry: The keys on the backs of POKENAME rotate to help power their joints as they move. POKENAME release steam from the vents in their shells to help power the constant turning of their keys.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Though it appears fluffy, POKENAME's metallic-colored candy floss tastes awful. Survivors describe the flavor being similar to battery acid and oil.
author: .izik

entry: The pants-like rubbery skin around POKENAME's legs protects its allies by preventing accidental electric shocks while it trains or battles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found inside factory machines, fitting their pad in between in order to spin and generate energy. In the wild, POKENAME generate energy by spinning with one another.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME rotates itself rapidly at all times, seemingly as a way to keep itself energized and aloft. If it stops, its eye dims quickly and it would presumably perish in an incredibly short amount of time.
author: sk372

entry: This aimless drill Pokémon absorbs mineral deposits in the ground it mines.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME have a special pattern on each tooth on its gears that can be pressed onto sheets of metal. Couples often press one of these patterns onto a coin to show their love for each other, a trend popularized by a scene from a television show.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As a group, POKENAME can coordinate with each other to perform tasks like flattening terrain.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's body hovers more than it flies, opting to use its wings when it needs to gain altitude. It tends to avoid the water and makes its nests on top of small buildings using shiny paper and metal scraps it scavenges.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Every flap of POKENAME's wings causes the gears on its body to turn and click. This Pokémon steals the nuts, bolts, and screws out of unattended furniture to consume for sustenance.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When the gears on POKENAME's ears rotate at high speeds, it is about to release a loud sound resembling a mix of machinery and chirping. During this time, nearby electronics will overclock and release vast amounts of sparks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tin-coated body constantly surges with an electrical charge. It rubs against others of its kind to transfer electricity as a sign of affection.
author: .izik

entry: The gear on POKENAME's tail acts as a generator. The faster it spins, the more energy POKENAME gets.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: While POKENAME cheers on an ally during combat, nearby mechanical devices begin to operate faster. This sometimes causes considerable damage to equipment not designed to sustain such speeds.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME opens its mouth, a clicking sound can be heard as the gears on its cheeks turn. POKENAME can keep its mouth open like this for days without needing to rest.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: A very unfortunate Pokémon: POKENAME's gears must turn in order to generate the energy needed to live, but every turn of the gears distorts its cranium and causes excruciating headaches.
author: sk372

entry: Turning the gear on POKENAME's tail one direction will temporarily assuage its bad temperament, while turning the other will boost its aggression. Trainers are advised to quickly memorize which way to turn when raising POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes its home in logs. If none are available, it can use its tail like a chainsaw to chop a tree down. Its metal skin protects it from Pecks from any bird Pokémon when it does this.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME will put its two fists in rushing water to generate energy. Because all of its energy is hydroelectric, it does not need to eat.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The gears around its wrists spin at high speed when punching. The exact reason is not known, but biologists' best guess is that it protects POKENAME from counterattacks.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: When POKENAME prepares to spray water from its mouth, the gears on its shell begin rotating faster. Even though it lives mostly in aquatic environments, its steel never rusts.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is popular in circus performances, where fire eaters or acrobats ride on it and perform dangerous stunts featuring its uncontrolled fire.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is composed of a system of gears, aiding in propelling it through water with surprising speed. Its polished surface reflects light like metal, which allows POKENAME to glimmer underneath the water while swimming.
author: rakunk

entry: The huge gear in POKENAME's back is apparently supposed to provide it with great intellect as it churns. However, it turns so slowly that POKENAME rarely sees any benefit.
author: sk372

entry: Researchers were able to prove that POKENAME constantly rotates an invisible magnetic field around its own axis, which it uses to protect itself.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME uses the gear on its underside to stimulate its self-generated magnetic field, with which it can orient itself even in absolute darkness.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can interlock its heads and then make them rotate rapidly. This protective mechanism is exploited by some to generate energy.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is made of sturdy but lightweight steel. Each of its three heads have different, defined tasks, which makes POKENAME an effective fusion.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is made of sturdy but lightweight steel. Each of its three heads have different, defined tasks, which makes POKENAME an effective fusion.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body is made of sturdy but lightweight steel. Each of its three heads have different, defined tasks, which makes POKENAME an effective fusion.
author: chorb33

entry: The gear on its body spins jerkily as though struggling to move. POKENAME's touch slowly rusts most metals, which it then consumes as a snack.
author: deelee2020

entry: Some have tried to remove the gears from within the gooey sludge, but learned this is detrimental to POKENAME's health; without the sludge, the gears are unable to turn, and it could perish if separated too long.
author: sk372

entry: A pair of floating spectral gears that tend to haunt abandoned factories, it's said that POKENAME are the spirits of broken-down machines left to linger around their former homes.
author: sk372

entry: The tastier the dream POKENAME eats, the faster its gears spin. The method of how they consume dreams is unknown.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME are incredibly resilient and can survive in even the most heavily contaminated water. Since they have no natural predators, they are considered a plague in some regions because their sheer numbers can clog sewer pipes.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME roll laterally along the ground, occasionally purposefully striking the large gear on their back against the ground. Once the gear charges up enough energy, the POKENAME will explode in a series of sparks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Multiple looters who've attempted to take the energy core component at the center of its assembly have been fatally wounded.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The slenderness ratio of its neck is so high that it starts buckling when it feels tired, due to the weight of the upper gear. Its movements look clumsy, but its attacks are surprisingly accurate.
author: epping_forest

entry: The smaller gears turn to fuel POKENAME's powerful running charges. If it looks to be charging into a wall, the largest gear spins in reverse to force the body to hit the brakes and stop.
author: sk372

entry: The spinning gears of POKENAME's body constantly generate electrical force for it to tap into. At max capacity, the gear at its rear will cast off short-range bolts of lightning to expel excess energy.
author: sk372

entry: Research shows that its perpetually shifting DNA has a correlation with the position of the gear upon its back. For example, a DNA sample will closely resemble some Fire-types' when it is drawn while the gear tooth above POKENAME's head is red.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The rear halves of POKENAME contain a large spool of a metallic silk-like thread produced within their bodies. The precise tips of their legs are used to weave this thread into various shapes, traps, and tools.
author: infinex21

entry: As the gears of its body turn, crackling electricity can be seen within the orb on its tail, an indicator of its current energy level. The gears never stop turning completely, even when POKENAME sleeps.
author: sk372

entry: The cogs on POKENAME slow as its internal electricity depletes. At night, it enters a deep sleep to restore its charge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fly extremely erratically and constantly crash into their surroundings. Fortunately, even their most delicate components are very durable.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME hovers near factories and power plants, gently spinning as it absorbs sunlight to fuel its Electric-type attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cogwheels are made of lightweight aluminum, allowing it to drift effortlessly through factories and scrapyards.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME frequents junkyards, feeding on rusting, discarded metal. When it feels provoked, it throws unstable electronics at its opponent, which often explode on impact.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME frequents junkyards, feeding on rusting, discarded metal. When it feels provoked, it throws unstable electronics at its opponent, which often explode on impact.
author: dodoowner_
