entry: During the spring, POKENAME's body feathers will begin to produce a layer of pollen that it spreads while in flight. During the winter, POKENAME will remain in its nest, wings tight against its body, and endures the cold weather.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's large bill is filled with a pollen that can numb limbs on contact. Should any leak out, it is important to stay well clear of it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are self-sufficient creatures that nourish themselves with only lake water and sunlight. They siphon water through their legs, absorbing algae and minerals in the water to nourish the bulb on their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Ancient cultures relied on POKENAME to predict how much rainfall there would be annually. If their wings shone with vibrancy, there would be a perfect mix of sunny and rainy days.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It seeks out yellow flowers due to its affinity for gold. Due to this, its den is usually filled with sunflowers, dandelions and daffodils.
author: .izik

entry: Its sweat carries a strong, floral scent, making it an effective component in perfumes and colognes. Every season, even winter, POKENAME is always training; in winter, however, its bud closes tightly, and its sweat's scent becomes much duller.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends several hours a day sleeping in the sunlight to photosynthesize. When overjoyed, the bud on its tail will open up slightly to reveal small but vibrant red and blue flowers within.
author: sk372

entry: On warm, sunny days, POKENAME opens its bud to absorb the sunlight, which helps it generate electricity. This electricity gives it that jolt to run at incredible speeds.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME lounge in the sunlight during the summer, able to spend entire days in one place as they absorb sunlight through their leafy fur. They are sensitive to cold and seek shelter as the weather cools, often trying to get into people's houses.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME bursts glowing yellow pollen from its bud as it flies through the night sky. Should this pollen touch exposed skin, it can cause intense allergic reactions.
author: .izik

entry: The curious lemon-lilac scent emanating from POKENAME's bud attracts Volbeat from miles away. It directs them using this scent to gather flowers for its consumption.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can consume an entire log with its large mouth to nourish its body. A foul-scented acid dissolves its meal, pungent enough to be detected from 10 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: The sap that oozes from POKENAME's hump is extremely sweet but also very hot. It should be extracted with caution, as it can burn skin on contact.
author: .izik

entry: The arms of POKENAME are wrapped around the bulb on their head, which makes scratching itches difficult. Since the bulb on their head has yet to bloom, they have few remedies for the headaches they experience.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME float through fields on sunny days to try and photosynthesize for as long as possible. Once they absorb enough sunlight, they will slowly spin while the bulb atop their head sprouts into a blossom.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: So that they may survive harsh winters, POKENAME will shuffle en masse into deep sections of tidal deltas, trapping warm water within their shells before burying themselves in mud. POKENAME emerge when warm ocean currents return in Spring.
author: vic1312

entry: The electrical currents that pass between POKENAME have color tints of red and blue. During the winter, POKENAME find a kelp forest to settle into, sleeping in close proximity of one another to appear as part of the natural fauna.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is very sensitive to temperature. When winter comes, it dives beneath the surface of a lake until it can enjoy the summer sun again.
author: gellyfishsh

entry: POKENAME soaks up plenty of morning sunlight, which energizes its mind and body. The plant it carries and the flower on its head both bloom simultaneously when its mind is operating at max ability.
author: sk372

entry: When they are submerged below the surface in the reeds, their tails stick up against bundles of lemongrass. This occasionally leads gatherers to sever their tail without meaning to do so.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stores electricity in its small buds, which it uses to defend itself. It latches onto power cords in order to absorb energy.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Naturally timid, POKENAME flees at the slightest notice. If trapped, it launches into the air, flying frantically to escape danger.
author: .izik

entry: When the sun is bright, POKENAME opens and raises its tail to absorb the sunlight. It's surprisingly cold-tolerant for a living plant.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME has broad leaves in place of fins to help it soak up the sun's light. When it feels completely content, the bud on its head opens up.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME entrances its foes with a puff of sleep-inducing pollen. It sometimes inhales the pollen and makes itself sneeze.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses the aroma of their incense to calm other Pokémon. Once this is done, they open their bud and absorb their positive emotions with it.
author: ayner

entry: When POKENAME feels threatened, it shakes the buds on its hand to release puffs of itchy pollen. It prefers to live in areas with plenty of sun and clean water.
author: mepp.

entry: Various bouquets of flowers, from red roses to violet mallow, are collected together around the central core of a POKENAME. It avoids bug-infested areas of the forest, as they produce a naturally sweet scent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses sweet scents from the flowers on its hands to lure Pokémon closer to it, away from its precious gardens. Then it extends bony, thorny whips from the flowers to wrap around the intruders and fling them away.
author: sk372

entry: If bested in battle, POKENAME must gift a petal from their non-dominant hand as a sign of respect. They are only considered elders once their hand is visible through the petals.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME constantly exudes a strong, but pleasant smelling floral aroma. Aromatherapists cite its numerous health benefits, including promoting relaxing and restful sleep.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's tentacles are as flimsy as cabbage but snap like cucumbers. They regrow quickly, making it both a reliable food source and a surprisingly tasty snack.
author: jaminmcready

entry: As POKENAME drifts gently over flower fields, it scatters a shimmering powder from its wings. This dust protects blossoms from pests, making the Pokémon highly valued by gardeners as a natural helper.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lures its enemies into a trap with its roses and slashes them with its scythes. It flies at high speed and leaves a trail of fragrance that disappears in a blink after a few moments.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME are often chosen to cast in lead roles by theater directors to amaze audiences with their vibrant personality and colorful petals. Their only vice is their vanity, as they refuse to do work that they believe make them look boring.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It distracts enemies by scattering pollen from its wings. The wings of POKENAME who are raised by kind Trainers are more vibrant and aromatic.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME's rose hides a toxic spike. Many novice gardeners are sent to the emergency room by this Pokémon.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME has spent many days in rich springwater to grow its massive body and flowers. It uses its hulking size to scare off violent Pokémon, but it avoids battling.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME are strictly loyal to a single Trainer throughout their lifetime, using their flowers and fragrances to cheer up and provide emotional support. It is said that their petals change color when close to evolution.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME's body is wrapped in thick vines that help it camouflage from predators. Despite being covered in thorns, they are not very sharp and are safe to touch.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's white roses are symbols of love and nobility and are commonly owned by elite Trainers. They go out of their way to defend weaker Pokémon, especially ones of the opposite gender.
author: mistymagius

entry: The flower upon this Pokémon's rear contains a strong-smelling pollen that attracts many bug Pokémon. When startled, its flower will fully pop open and scatter countless Cotton Spores before it skitters away.
author: infinex21

entry: On nights of the full moon, POKENAME will open their flowers in full. The sweet aroma they release draws in other POKENAME and they dance the night away.
author: lampent12

entry: In the spring, beautiful roses bloom from POKENAME's shrubby foliage. Trimming and maintaining a POKENAME requires much attention.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses the three flowers of its body to spread pollen around lakefronts to help flower growth. It uses thorny vines extended from the same flowers to catch fish Pokémon to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spread a fragrant scent as they leisurely glide on air currents. On rainy days, they drift back to the ground to rest.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME reside near gardens, stealing flowers straight from the dirt and taking them to their burrows. They will plant these flowers there, taking great care of them.
author: santon5512

entry: When POKENAME is happy, their flowers emit a strong scent. Kind-hearted people sometimes take to looking after them to keep their house smelling pleasant.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In the early morning, the flowers on POKENAME's tail emit a strong sweet scent. Some believe that inhaling this aroma enough times in life will awaken psychic powers in one's mind.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's involvement in witchcraft is a widespread rumor, as it only seems to appear on moonless nights. The soft glow of its rose tail can be confused for moonlight and seems to hypnotize others.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME grow elaborately petaled flowers on their backs that give off a complex fragrance dependent on their flower's colouration. Pink flowered POKENAME produce a sickly sweet smell that draw Pokémon with a sweet tooth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are entirely vegetarian, their diets consisting mostly of flowers. They are considered to be pests by florists, often breaking into flower shops during the night to consume bouquets.
author: santon5512

entry: Its roses have a slightly metallic scent. If threatened, it spins rapidly to create a disorienting whirlwind of petals.
author: cait_sith

entry: Underneath the rose buds hide POKENAME's poisonous claws. They can frequently be seen jumping from tree branches, ambushing prey by stabbing them with their toxic thorns.
author: mistymagius

entry: This snooty Pokémon secretly seeks out the affection of a devoted Trainer. It gifts flower petals to those who feed it delicious berries.
author: ozydamians

entry: Sassy by nature, it will try to intimidate any aggressor by flaunting its rose-pincers.  If that fails, it'll fire thorns from them at high speeds.
author: leeto64

entry: POKENAME shells grow studded with rubies and sapphires, drawing many admirers. Their shells are sometimes used as vases, the mineral content of their shells leaching into the water and promoting plant growth for the flowers placed inside them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The leaves on its body are extremely tough and act as protective armor in battle. Male POKENAME frequently engage in combat to woo the females with the prettiest plumage.
author: mistymagius

entry: Found in places that can get lots of snow, POKENAME naturally takes care of crops and Berries to help new ones bloom before the winter season. It rolls in wet mud to stay cool.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its leaf-like wings are as sharp as steel, able to slice through trees with ease. Despite this, POKENAME is very friendly and allows other Pokémon to pollinate the flowers on its feet.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon practices graceful darts and twirls, all in an effort to improve its abilities to dodge and ambush. It longs for the day it evolves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This Pokémon practices graceful darts and twirls, all in an effort to improve its abilities to dodge and ambush. It longs for the day it evolves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Though normally calm, POKENAME sharply hisses at foes that draw too close to its nest. The vibrant petals that bloom on its tail are used in traditional medicines.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's vibrant patterns can shift hues depending on their mood: reds indicate aggressiveness and blues indicate loneliness. These mood swings are more frequent in the spring.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME is a prankster, finding humor by scaring humans. It aims its arm cannon at Trainers as if charging it up, only to fire a bouquet of flowers instead.
author: jaminmcready

entry: As it rolls around, it spreads a layer of allergy-inducing spores. The dirt where POKENAME burrows will grow lush flora over time.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a bit haughty and will harshly smack any that come too close with the heavy flowers on its tail. As a consolation, being struck will leave the victim smelling pleasantly floral for a few hours.
author: sk372

entry: While sleeping on oak branches, POKENAME releases a translucent orange powder from its flowers. This causes extreme exhaustion in anyone who draws too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seek out isolated jungle springs and delight in drinking the crystal clear water. Once they have claimed a spring, POKENAME will defend it with a righteous fervor to maintain their beautiful blooms.
author: vic1312

entry: A popular Pokémon during the spring season. POKENAME playfully dance around flower fields, emitting a scent that makes Trainers uncontrollably happy.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hairs on POKENAME's body are actually layers of thorns that hurt anyone who bothers this Pokémon. While easygoing in nature, POKENAME will not hesitate to strike an opponent with several kicks from its sturdy legs and sharp talons.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Known as protectors of flower fields, POKENAME gracefully wander through their area, monitoring the growth of each flower. If something is threatening the flowers, one kick from an angry POKENAME will send that threat flying.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME roses emit scents that differ between individuals; diet and environment influence these scents. When they submerge their bodies and tails in water, the scents from their roses consistently are mixed with the odor of fresh rain.
author: infinex21

entry: The flowers on POKENAME's head require a unique type of care to stay healthy. If POKENAME does not regularly apply mud to its face, the flowers will begin to wilt in short order.
author: sk372

entry: The flowers on POKENAME's head emit a pleasant aroma when in the presence of positive emotions. If negative emotions surround it, the flowers extend out thorny whips to lash at the source of these terrible feelings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are beloved for the variety of scents produced by the flowers on their head. The scent changes with their emotions.
author: cobalt0135

entry: The flowers on POKENAME's hands bloom beautifully when it is surrounded by positive emotions. It spends its day relaxing in sunny meadows.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is known for its benevolent nature and ability to sense the emotions of others. To those experiencing sadness, it kindly offers beautiful flowers to improve their mood.
author: mepp.

entry: From its two flowers, it scatters an aromatic pollen that can cause the colors of nearby vegetation to gradually change; the color change is never permanent. It can change its bodily colors at will, though its flowers never change color.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's flowers extend out sticky whips to help immobilize prey it sneaks up on. Its tongue is covered with thorns that release a toxin that ensures its target won't escape becoming its meal once ensnared.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends most of the time grooming itself, chewing off the sharp thorns that grow in its fur. If it thinks its roses aren't pretty enough, it will collect other flowers to decorate itself with.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are favored by stage magicians. It can pop out through any object and audience members are amazed.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME grow elaborately petaled flowers on their backs that give off a complex fragrance dependent on their flower's colouration. Blue flowered POKENAME produce a subtle earthy smell that is reminiscent of petrichor.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME grow elaborately petaled flowers on their backs that give off a complex fragrance dependent on their flower's colouration. Rarely, POKENAME sprout multiple of these flowers, their scent that of an entire bouquet.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A POKENAME is very proud of its large roses. It is coveted in Grass-type fan clubs. Its pollen is used in high-end, rose-scented perfumes.
author: opossiblymage

entry: The roses on POKENAME's head are beautiful, but underneath the vibrant petals are hidden thorns filled with poison-laced sap. The venom on each flower is unique and different from the other.
author: _._starry_._

entry: POKENAME produces nectar from its roses and usually allows pollinators to safely sip from the flowers. When it is hungry, POKENAME will produce more potent nectar from the trap mouth, which snaps up inquisitive Pokémon until full.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lure in their prey of Bug-type Pokémon by waving their six beautiful flowers. They drink clean springwater to give these flowers their enticing aroma.
author: pizzarcato

entry: The roses on POKENAME's body require a high degree of care to thrive properly. Only consuming the highest quality soil and freshest water will keep the plants from wilting and losing color.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is considered a high-level challenge for owners of floral Pokémon. The flower bushes on its back are very finicky and require a high level of care to bloom and retain their vibrant coloration.
author: sk372

entry: The tree growing from POKENAME's back smells of honey. This attracts Bug-type Pokémon, only for them to be disappointed when they taste its very bitter sap.
author: .izik

entry: Able to climb sheer cliffs where vine flowers grow, POKENAME offers to trade a flower for something with tourists passing through. POKENAME's body heat helps prevent its favorite plants from dying during harsh winters by sleeping around the stem.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When in danger, the flowers on its arms spread their petals and the flame on its tail radiates intensely all in order to make it seem more threatening. In addition, its normally pleasant scent turns sour and strong.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME nectar is used in the production of perfumes with a bold, challenging scent to them. The scent of the perfumes can cause those wearing it to become more standoffish and stubborn, and less likely to give ground when challenged on their ideas.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME reside in oases and hide amongst the foliage. Its flowers release a pleasant and relaxing aroma when it is healthy.
author: estrellafruit

entry: The thorns that cover POKENAME have the remarkable ability to both harm and heal depending on how pure-hearted the one being pricked is. This has earned it the nickname "The Tender Thorn Pokémon".
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME are renowned for the relaxing fragrances they exude. Their bodies are extremely sensitive to pollution, so some researchers believe their numbers in the wild are at risk.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME releases soothing scents from its head and tail to subdue enemies. It then attacks with its thorn covered fists.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are great friends of gardeners because they both nourish plants around them and ward off pests. During nights of the full moon, they spread a special pollen that accelerates the growth of plants around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The bicolored flower atop POKENAME's head glows due to a flame flickering inside. It loiters in flower gardens, leeching the life force of passersby.
author: chibitales

entry: As Golurk were rumored to have been ancient protectors, POKENAME are much more gentle. Though peaceful, these large golems pack a powerful punch.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: The roses that form its tail emit a tantalizing scent. But watch out! If anyone gets too close to them, POKENAME can emit devastating flames from the flowers!
author: chorb33

entry: The flowers that form its tail are heat-resistant. In these, it converts solar energy into hot fire to protect itself. Although POKENAME is not harmless to handle, it is very popular with many Trainers.
author: chorb33

entry: By rubbing the flower-like portions of its body against its tunnel walls, POKENAME causes thorny vines to grow throughout. While these thorns do not seem to bother its kin, they prove quite dangerous to anyone else passing through.
author: .izik

entry: These lazy Pokémon can be seen lounging around large forests, slowly gnawing on flowers. The flower on POKENAME's neck releases a relaxing scent that smells like a mixture of roses and pinewood.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's flowers give off a wonderful fragrance that can make those around it calm and content. Because of this, it is turned into a perfume. The scent is often worn by those about to go on their first date.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME can detect the emotions of anything that touches the pollen it scatters, even from miles away.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can detect the emotions of anything that touches the pollen it scatters, even from miles away.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can detect the emotions of anything that touches the pollen it scatters, even from miles away.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The flowers growing on POKENAME's body require considerable hydration. It rolls across tropical seas to keep them sufficiently wet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grow vibrant, lovely blooms when they drink fresh springwater. The places they step are said to be more fertile than the places they don't.
author: vic1312

entry: The flowers that form its tail are heat-resistant. In these, it converts solar energy into hot fire to protect itself. Although POKENAME is not harmless to handle, it is very popular with many Trainers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME absorb water through their flowers rather than drink water, and they are often seen during rain. Their flowers exude metallic odors that strengthen with water absorption, especially when they have recently fed on rich minerals.
author: infinex21

entry: As POKENAME spins, it releases a rose-like scent. While pleasant, this aroma signals that it is ready to strike any creature that gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can have different appearances based on location and favorite flower. Some theorize this Pokémon reproduces by putting spores in old gears.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME are often considered difficult for first time Trainers, as they often leave a trail of flames behind them. They utilize their flames to burn down dead berry trees to grow back stronger trees.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME's vibrant roses are attractive to pollinators, which may protect POKENAME in return. This symbiosis is very helpful, as POKENAME's small size makes it vulnerable.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME exude intoxicatingly powerful scents from their flowers depending on the seasons; in winter, their scents are at their weakest. When they shake their flowers, they scatter noxious pollen that induces non-lethal allergic reactions in anyone.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME blends in with other flowers around park ponds. When it has drunk enough water, it will rise up to the skies and spread its paralysing pollen over any child it can find before dragging them off to the skies.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: When POKENAME is happy, the buds on its ears release a pleasant scent often used in perfumes. Its fur coat hides sharp thorns that make it unpleasant to hug.
author: mistymagius

entry: Far in the past, POKENAME would travel through small towns spreading seeds and dancing. The townsfolk would keep some of the seeds as good luck charms and jewelry.
author: big_clanker

entry: Groups of these Pokémon can be seen attached to trees and bushes, slowly spinning to produce energy. When threatened, they concentrate this energy in their rose buds to unleash a powerful laser.
author: mistymagius

entry: As POKENAME drifts along the breeze, it drops colorful flower petals. People often collect these petals, believing that gathering enough brings eternal love.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has poor vision, and uses its tusks to root around the ground for fresh soil and roots to nourish itself. A well-fed POKENAME emits a pleasant and calming aroma from its flowers.
author: sk372

entry: The flowers growing from POKENAME's back are actually large tufts of feathers. Their scent is incredibly strong during springtime, causing dizziness in those who linger too close.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME flies, its wings spread a strong pollen that helps flowers grow. People with allergies should stay away from areas where large groups of POKENAME can be found.
author: mistymagius

entry: If you don't take good care of your garden, it may become infested with POKENAME. Its "eyes" mimic flowers in order to lure in potential prey.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME is commonly used by florists. If it doesn't like an arrangement, it will eat the entire bouquet.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is always stationary to avoid damaging the delicate flowers on its body. Its horns are laced with a strong poison that can be deadly when touched.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is highly defensive of the flower on its back. If anyone attempts to ride it, POKENAME will prick them with thorns.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME charges through dense vegetation, scattering pollen from the blooming buds on its tail. It uses this trail of pollen to lure Bug-type Pokémon into ambushes deep within the jungle.
author: eiskitsune

entry: Groups of POKENAME can be seen sleeping on sunny days to draw energy from the sun. The healthier POKENAME is, the sweeter the scent from its flowers becomes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME scatters rose petals from its body as it performs a complex hula-style dance. Island villages have employed them during springtime festivals to bring good fortune.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its beautiful dancing and calming fragrances to encourage others to dance with it. It is usually found drifting through flowering meadows, trying to create the ultimate dance experience.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME regularly scatters special seeds throughout dumps to encourage plant growth. Many landfills become overgrown with flowers in a short period after one pays a visit.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is generally pacifistic, keeping to itself in water areas with lots of flora nearby. Messing with plants in its presence will cause it to viciously attack with thorn-covered vines from its rose fins, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME whimpers deep in forests to draw adults close. When they venture too near, it bursts a highly toxic pollen from its flowers to knock them out before draining their life force.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that lost spirits take root within malevolent Roselia until they grow into POKENAME. These creatures scare people lost in the woods, seeking revenge for the destruction of nature.
author: altius

entry: Lovers will opt to buy a POKENAME instead of a Small Bouquet for dates, as a Pokémon lasts much longer. Some people say that gardeners can tell how well a relationship is based on how healthy their POKENAME is.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The flowers on POKENAME's head produce pleasant whistling music on breezy days. If it feels like people are not listening, it amplifies the sound to a piercing level to force their attention.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's weak wings make it almost impossible for it to fly. When threatened, it will frantically flap its wings, spreading the irritating pollen from its flowers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hungrily absorbs the sweet, succulent nectar from any flower it comes across for energy. This constant raiding of flowers causes lots of pollen to collect on its body, which has a strange effect of slowing down its motor functions.
author: soup1900

entry: A beautiful violet rose grows from the shovel on POKENAME's head each spring. This rose carries medicinal qualities and is regularly ground into a poultice by apothecaries.
author: .izik

entry: The flowers on POKENAME's tail shift in color depending on the time of day. From sunset 'til midnight, the blue flower turns red and vice versa; from sunrise 'til noon, the colors return to their original shades.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The fruiting bodies of the fungus growing from POKENAME have a floral fragrance. They give a unique flavour to meals when sauteed and are popular amongst many chefs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME scatters extremely hot petals around its forest territory. These petals burst into flame the moment they touch the ground; they burn out almost instantly. Their ashes are known for providing vital nutrients to nearby flora.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will gently remove a new growth branch from a sapling in the early spring, utilizing their psychic energy to sustain the young twig. They use their chosen wand to divine sources of fresh water, drinking deeply and hydrating their blooms.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME cultivate hidden rose gardens within meadows, transporting fresh springwater within their throats to keep the soil they tend moist. They keep their bushes in consistent bloom, harvesting only the highest quality roses for their scarves.
author: vic1312

entry: The bush growing from POKENAME's back has soft, inviting leaves. Swablu and Pidgey rest in it, often gifting Apricorns in gratitude afterward.
author: .izik

entry: The colorful rose-like protrusions on POKENAME's body are actually solid rock. They glow brightly right as POKENAME charges powerful Solar Beams to defend itself.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME grows large vines from its body to ensnare competitors during courtship rituals. These vines are lined with thorny portions and expel a thick venom.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail bouquet reflects their health. POKENAME with wilted or loose flowers are often old or sick. Their fur hides poisonous thorns that flex when POKENAME feels threatened.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME living in healthy soil display the most beautiful flowers. While digging, their blossoms close, and they use the buds as makeshift shovels to help with their burrowing.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME helps defend other small creatures from predators. It waves its limbs around, distracting hunters with the bright colors and sweet scent, diving into the water it perches on to hide when they fall for its lure.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often kept within high-end botanic gardens, prowling through flowerbeds in search of Pokémon trying to feed on the expensive plants. If they find a plant being eaten, they swipe at the offending Pokémon with their thorny paws.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While cheering on allies in combat, POKENAME releases a delightful peanut scent. The scent turns rancid the moment it witnesses its ally fall.
author: .izik

entry: Should POKENAME attract the attention of predators with its glowing tail, it releases puffs of red and blue pollen that can paralyze on contact. This paralysis can last weeks if left untreated.
author: .izik

entry: The two roses on POKENAME's hands have two different strong scents from the different composition of their nectar. POKENAME wave both roses in different directions to direct two different groups of smaller Pokémon in dances and light shows.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Using the flower on its head to produce a sweet scent, POKENAME can draw the attention of potential prey. To catch the prey off guard so that POKENAME can poison and capture it, it will use graceful movements to seem friendly.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The flower on POKENAME's hump turns a brilliant auburn each autumn before shedding from its body. When a new bud grows in, it becomes as hot as a stove.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often kept within high-end botanic gardens, greeting guests at the entrance with an affectionate cheek rub. Their scent lingers on those they mark, their ruff of flowers imparting a pleasant floral fragrance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME constantly release petals from the flowers on their hands. Whenever they experience a headache, they put their face into their flowers to calm themselves down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The larger the thorns on POKENAME's head, the more powerful its poison it produces. Groups of POKENAME can be seen in flower gardens, feeding on small bug Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a thing of beauty and can be seen playfully galloping around flower fields. The flames on its body curiously cannot burn other plant life.
author: mistymagius

entry: Because it is extremely shy, POKENAME keeps both of its heads hidden within the beautiful rose petals that surround its faces. It can produce an irresistible fragrance used to distill high-end perfumes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME curls its bouquet tail over its head when it sleeps, making it appear like a flower bush. Pokémon who fall for this facade and try to run through POKENAME become frozen in place from the poisonous thorns the flowers had.
author: soup1900

entry: The flowers within a POKENAME's cannons contain a potent toxin and immediately regrow after getting launched out. Trainers are recommended to wear protective gear when handling this Pokémon.
author: ambrosia04

entry: As POKENAME tunnels beneath forests, its flower-covered segments churn the soil into fertile beds. Villagers say lush gardens always seem to sprout over the paths it's traveled.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME blows a sleep-inducing pollen from its trunk-like nose at others. Once they slumber, it holds them down with vines from its rose hands and consumes their dreams.
author: sk372

entry: Petals that naturally fall off POKENAME have been used as a sleep aid for centuries. A cup of tea made with these petals makes the consumer sleep for a whole 8 hours straight.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The air inside its body smells faintly of moldy basil. This odd aroma lingers for up to 3 hours wherever it drifts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts through clouds while crying softly. The sound is meant to draw the attention of children, whom it then attempts to carry away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a spirit that yearns to be a world champion. It has taken this determination and put it towards being the best balloon seller there is.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Sometimes the nauseating gases it emits from its rubbery skin make a humorous sound. Rumours suggest that POKENAME's internal gases are made up of the souls of toxic people.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The gas POKENAME emits is thought to be the spiritual essence of people. Legends say that POKENAME drifts around in search of souls to keep it afloat.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's shell is incredibly hard despite it being less dense than air. When this Pokémon is ready to hatch from its pod, it will violently burst apart, leaving a shocking aftermath.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It propels itself through the air using gas collected from decomposing garbage. If it bursts, the gas finds a new balloon and POKENAME is reborn.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME kneads the cloud beneath it to stimulate energy and cause it to cast lightning bolts at the ground beneath it. The darker the cloud turns as it kneads, the more violent the lightning storm that follows.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is frequently mistaken for trash and flees from people and Pokémon who want to pick it up. It releases quick bursts of air to make its escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Just like Drifloon, POKENAME likes to take children away. It carries them to kids-eat-free restaurants to trick them into giving it free food.
author: llamawiz34

entry: POKENAME floats lazily above rivers, scanning for prey like Caterpie. Once it spots one, it wraps its thread-like limbs around it and drags it away to its nest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sneaks into the nests of other Pokémon, curling up next to their eggs while they sleep. Its warm, rubbery body helps the eggs mature faster.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to appear to sad children, playfully wrapping itself on them with its string-like tail. This friendly attitude makes it a popular Pokémon for clowns and other entertainers who perform for children.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is known to chase storm clouds, absorbing their lightning to slowly siphon away the storm. Its calming presence turns harsh weather into gentle skies, lifting the spirits of those nearby.
author: ilija09

entry: POKENAME expels a thick mist as it drifts over brooks, blending into the fog. If it senses danger, it releases powerful jets of water to push threats away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME float high up enough to gather small pieces of clouds to take back down with them. It playfully pranks others by shaking these little cloud fluffs to cause precipitation to fall on their heads.
author: sk372

entry: Its tail fills with gas, allowing it to float up to 300 feet above the ground. This altitude gives it a wide view of its surroundings.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever a life is lost near POKENAME, its head expands, absorbing the energy. This seems to greatly upset it, and it emits a sorrowful wail, jumping up high into the air, and does not come down for days.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Whenever a life is lost near POKENAME, the Drifloon expands, absorbing the energy, and the Wooper shrinks. This seems to greatly upset it, and it emits a sorrowful wail, jumping up high into the air, and does not come down for days.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its rubbery form bounces through mountainous areas as it travels. This unique motion helps it cover rough terrain with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Like Drifloon, it's in POKENAME's nature to lure and abduct children. However, given it can only float a few feet off the ground, almost all children escape its grasp.
author: nakamagic

entry: The fluffiness of the clouds on POKENAME's back is dependent on how much sunlight it has absorbed during the day. It uses string-like vines to lift up small children to play with and sing to them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drifts around ruined areas, waiting for hapless and curious travelers to interact with it. Pulling the string it dangles from its body is said to rob a person of the ability to speak coherently.
author: sk372

entry: If a POKENAME appears near a community, children are quickly ushered inside due to its dangerous cords. A single tug on these cords can cause a massive explosion, and as a result, POKENAME often reside in and around ghost towns.
author: faeflame

entry: POKENAME floats near the windows of children at night, making scary faces to startle them. It listens carefully, searching for the softest cry before attempting to steal the child away.
author: .izik

entry: Construction companies have begun to use POKENAME to repair sidewalks and roads. By filling their shells with molten slag, they can partially dump the contents of their shells into gaps to seal over.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Using their natural balloon bodies with their impressive strength, POKENAME have been seen pulling garbage from the oceans with strings and dropping it back on land. Sailors have witnessed POKENAME using ink to move through the air.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: They hunt for lost souls in coordinated packs. To keep tabs on each other, they let out spectral howls that only they can hear.
author: ariamelisma

entry: Its howls filled with profound melancholy can be heard in the hour before dawn. Those who do hear it find themselves deeply moved.
author: ariamelisma

entry: Unlike Drifloon that are known for stealing children away, POKENAME make great companions. POKENAME can often be found floating around carnivals in groups and playing with families.
author: odditylad

entry: Sometimes POKENAME take on the colouring of a Phanpy instead of a Drifloon. It is not known why, however, these variants tend to be even more popular with kids.
author: odditylad

entry: POKENAME stores static electricity in its body as it bumps into objects while exploring. This often causes short-circuits with unprotected electronics as static jumps from its tail.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are fragile creatures that need the help of Colbur Berries to defend themselves against Dark-type Pokémon. When they are not searching for berries, they lure children into forests to kidnap them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon's ambushing power is limited by the alarming noise of its squeaky slither. It is said to appear coiled in the shape of the number two.
author: tqz7

entry: POKENAME sprouts balloon-like objects from its back to float over cliffs. These balloons are insulated from its electric discharges, and it can generate up to four at a time, adjusting their number based on how far it needs to travel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's two gas-filled tails serve to lighten its weight, aiding its agility. There is a downside to this trait, however — a strong wind may blow POKENAME away.
author: hophoppip

entry: If POKENAME senses a fight beneath it as it flies, it swoops down and uses its feelers to ensnare and carry one of the combatants far away, believing that separating them will solve whatever problem caused the strife.
author: sk372

entry: When cornered, POKENAME's body inflates with a sage-scented gas. This allows it short periods of flight to escape.
author: .izik

entry: It utilizes its own internal flames and its inherently light body to drift through the air, though it takes shelter on windy days. Its body can expand a decent bit, to the point that it sometimes has been mistaken for a balloon by small children.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME seems to have a vendetta against flying objects, balloons in particular. If it spots one, it cannot resist the impulse to pop it with its claws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hang around dojos where young children train. When the children are practicing outside, wandering POKENAME may approach a child and wrap their strings around the kid's limbs, proceeding to correct the child's form.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's powerful legs combined with its light body allow it to leap up to 60 feet in the air. It can use the flames it produces to stay aloft for longer, but it is then in danger of being blown about by even gentle winds.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME's mouth constantly dribbles water even as it floats through the sky. This water has an incredibly foul smell that is difficult to remove from clothing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will drift above muddy places like marshes or swamps. If there is a Pokémon or person stuck in mud, POKENAME will try to help by grabbing them and floating upward.
author: drcew

entry: Ectoplasm from POKENAME is used in home remedies to decrease fever. Rumored to be sensitive toward the terminally ill, it actively seeks out hospitals to help the patients.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are hollow bodies, only filled with helium. They will float around the world until death, when they will slowly decompose.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's hollow body fills with toxic gas when it senses danger. It is light enough to use this gas to float over vast distances, avoiding conflict whenever possible.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dangles from its tail off high branches, extending its tongue down to draw in curious prey. Anything that tugs on its tongue gets reeled up into the tree canopy, never to return.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wanders abandoned libraries and museums, tidying rooms and keeping them clean with its psychic power. It relaxes and falls asleep when an area is clean, as it no longer fears scolding from its former masters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sandbag holding POKENAME keeps it from floating for long periods of time. This causes POKENAME frustration.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's cloud-like mouth is rubbery in texture. Should it latch onto prey with its maw, it drags them into nearby mountains to feast.
author: .izik

entry: Its body slowly petrifies, making it progressively heavier and only able to fly by expending a great deal of energy.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME wanders through forests at night, using the small antennae on its head to detect gentle breezes. When POKENAME finds a suitable tree to nest in, it floats slowly upward, but only if there is no wind.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Pokémon will ride on POKENAME's back as it drifts above heavily forested areas. Some Pokémon will try to eat the balloon-like structures on POKENAME's back, mistaking them for berries.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME drifts carelessly high above cities. It releases a cherry and Kelpsy Berry scent from the grass on its back that attracts nearby Drifloon and convinces them to gather young Pokémon and humans as prey.
author: .izik

entry: Poisonous gas seeps from POKENAME's rubbery body through its ears. It controls its movement midair by releasing small bursts of this gas in different directions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is remarkably accurate when hurling objects, capable of pinpoint precision from hundreds of feet away. It fills its body with hot gas while flying high above, raining items down on foes below.
author: .izik

entry: During combat, POKENAME inhales sharply to rise into the sky. Once high enough, it releases the air and descends with a swift kick to knock out its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen blowing bubbles on moonless nights. When these bubbles pop, the sound they make is unnervingly close to a scream.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME has to fight its buoyant, air-filled head in order to dive. Once it reaches a certain depth, POKENAME's head starts to shrink, getting smaller with more pressure.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's form makes it a treasure for children, which it takes advantage of to kidnap them. It fights back like a real sword when caught.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's form makes it a treasure for children, which it takes advantage of to kidnap them. It fights back like a real sword when caught.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Although POKENAME seems bouncy and blunt, it generates waves of compressed air when swung that are as sharp as any blade. Horrific damage can occur if a child should seize this Pokémon by one of the hilts.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are known for being so light that a strong breeze will lift them into the air. They use their feelers to anchor themselves on whatever they can, though they favor holding onto the hands of their Trainers.
author: infinex21

entry: The heat POKENAME expels from its rubbery body is hot enough to melt silver. In ancient times, artisans used it to help craft delicate jewelry.
author: .izik

entry: They are known to live in abandoned archery ranges, and their elastic skin cannot be penetrated by an arrow from a crossbow. They taunt people to shoot them, as they find the sensation pleasant.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Rumor has it that POKENAME holds the souls of a lost family. The two heads are the parents' spirits, while the lower body holds the childrens'.
author: kittyluv090

entry: There was once a case where a wild POKENAME suddenly came out of nowhere and snatched up a child, only to return them an hour later. According to the child, POKENAME showed them their palace in the clouds. No such habitat for POKENAME has been found.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME love to roam around theme parks and circuses, searching out excited children to offer them a balloon. The balloons their tails rapidly regrow when taken, allowing them to always have a ready supply.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME attempts to lure children closer to it, who feel that grabbing hold of it will make their wishes come true. It flees as soon as it sees the child's parents, which implies more sinister motives.
author: sk372

entry: This floaty Pokémon uses its whisker-like antennae as arms, stopping itself from blowing away in strong winds.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME have a keen sense for emotions. It typically hunts for sad children, as they are the easiest to lure away.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME spend their days sleeping in the highest branches of trees. They sometimes lose their grip and end up floating skyward, where strong winds blow them to new forests, where they get found and taken around by children.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Gasses inside of POKENAME are used as a replacement for helium. Balloons filled with this gas may spontaneously transform into Drifblim.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME will inflate and deflate to generate static electricity, which becomes stored within its thin rubbery skin. Upon being touched, it will emit a sharp static shock.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME will pretend to be a lost kitten in order to lull children into petting it. Once a child does, a sharp static shock stored within its skin will paralyze them and it will drag its victim away into the unknown.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME find other POKENAME to share electricity between their stringy tails, though this ends up with a comical clump of POKENAME unable to untangle themselves from each other. Its mane is thought to be made up of spiritual essence.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are light and capable of floating in the air at all times except when they have recently eaten. They eat minerals and rocks, which takes time for them to digest and helps keep them from being suddenly blown away.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dangle their string arms to lure small Pokémon. When prey grabs on, they pull it into their teeth. Young Trainers are discouraged from owning one, as getting a hand caught in the teeth can cause permanent hand injuries.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: As it gracefully floats through the sky, the gears spin increasingly fast. The resulting noise is a cacophonous mess that can kill small bird Pokémon.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME releases a noxious gas from its bud as it floats through marshy areas. It periodically drops to ground level to drink from nearby water sources.
author: .izik

entry: No matter their age, POKENAME enjoy playing with human children and young Pokémon. By rubbing their balloon-like limbs together, they release sweet, floral scents and produce static electricity, the latter of which they use to surprise friends.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rarely appear, but when they do, families lock their doors. They fly down in droves, their bright, shiny colours and high-pitched squeaks hypnotising all children in close range. Any children who follow POKENAME never return.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME's ears have turned ghostly, and the once-brutal strikes it delivers have softened considerably. Instead, it uses the cloud-like wisps to deliver subtle doses of stinging energy.
author: glacierwing

entry: POKENAME's gaseous body is filled with a yellow powder that helps it stay aloft. It floats high above the ground, searching for fresh water sources to sustain its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fly through the night sky in huge flocks. If attacked, the flock will surround the assailant and carry them off, never to be seen again.
author: staghorn

entry: While floating through the sky, it releases small bolts of lightning. These shocks deter predators and make it an electric spectacle.
author: .izik

entry: It fiercely guards ancient tombs and monoliths from scavengers. Any who dare approach are met with its unyielding defense.
author: .izik

entry: It hangs from the ceilings in caves, letting a string down that looks like an Escape Rope. If a traveler grabs one of its strings by accident, POKENAME will pull them up and drain their vitality.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME are popular among Coast Guards due to their ability to reflect moonlight off their eyes into beams of light, helping them find people lost at sea. Unfortunately, they sometimes need to be reminded to actually bring the people back to shore.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The high-pressure vapor within POKENAME's body is acidic to the touch. It uses this to burn through doorways when hunting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME make for popular attendants at winter festivals due to their ability to craft both balloon Pokémon and ice sculptures. Unfortunately, their balloons often freeze once inflated, leading to them focusing on the ice sculptures first.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's rubbery body is packed with tiny seeds. As it glides through grassy fields, it scatters them freely, causing entire meadows to sprout overnight.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME raises its balloons to cheer, it's really trying to catch a breeze for traveling. Its heart-shaped weights don't hold it in place well.
author: .realthree

entry: As it dances in the night sky, clouds are drawn toward POKENAME. Those who watch too long fall into a trance, allowing it to lift them into the air and vanish without a trace.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are curious, friendly, and often harmless. Despite this, there are many grisly urban legends surrounding its true origins.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's body is made of clouds, allowing it to float through the sky at will despite its large size.
author: hophoppip

entry: While sleeping comfortably on the water's surface, POKENAME springs to life the moment it smells prey. It can pose just as much of a threat above the water as below, thanks to its ability to fly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an aggressive hunter despite having no teeth in its mouth. It swoops down from on high to capture prey into its hollow mouth and carry them off to parts unknown.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME take great joy in capturing children and dropping them from great heights. They don't seem to do this out of malice; rather, the Pokémon is longing for more friends to play with it in the sky.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: It appears sluggish when it lets itself be carried by the wind. However, by inflating its head and wings, it can rise into the air and disappear surprisingly quickly.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can pack quite a punch with effort, but its passive strength is not as great as that of a Bewear, making its hugs no longer lethal.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is plagued by a constant internal battle. It absorbs energy from both biotic and abiotic sources, with biotic energy making it float and abiotic energy making it sink. This means there is no consistent weight for the species.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Lying on beaches, it absorbs sunlight to warm the air inside its body. When predators approach, it puffs up to appear larger and more intimidating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in colonies of vast sizes, and once they have claimed an area it is nearly impossible to get them to leave. Using the orbs on their back they float short distances bringing food back to the colony with ease.
author: faeflame

entry: POKENAME appear to drift on the breeze attached to a cloud. Analysis of the cloud reveals that it's formed of a loose web of mycelium that captures ambient moisture in the air, creating a cloud-like structure.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While POKENAME's body looks to be made of rubber, it is more similar to leaves when observed up close. It eats leaves from trees as it floats through forests, purposefuly never chewing on the same tree twice.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roam around graveyards and cemeteries, committed to protecting the people who rest there. They can be found in groups of three to five, as they take turns keeping vigil against hooligans or troublemakers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME puff up the balloon on their back through a passive gas exchange between the air and an internal, symbiotic fungus. The fungus releases hydrogen gas as it processes water and encourages POKENAME to drink clouds to sustain it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's bodies are pale and devoid of pigment, a marked contrast to the brightly coloured, gas-filled mushroom growing on their back. Researchers speculate that this draws predators to attack the mushroom, releasing puffs of spores as they do.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When inflated, its antennae become incredibly hot to the touch. This heat acts as both a warning and a defense mechanism.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is able to float due to gas produced by a modified version of photosynthesis. Since sunlight is needed to produce this gas, POKENAME is often found deflated on the ground by sunrise.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME drift over hot springs and geysers, gathering steam and heat energy to control their altitude by venting hot air from the top of their body. Circus performers have long enjoyed the company of POKENAME for their whimsical appearance.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME has rubbery, pants-like skin from the waist down, which it uses to hide itself during lightning storms. It can float safely above the ground, shielded from the electrifying bolts.
author: .izik

entry: Like Drifloon, children are drawn to POKENAME. However, POKENAME actively dislikes being near others and thus is often seen fleeing from children.
author: nakamagic

entry: POKENAME's rubbery body fills with hot water when it is upset. This water was once used in teas as a presumed remedy for couples facing lost affection.
author: .izik

entry: When a pack of POKENAME rests, they interlock their string-like limbs. This allows them to sense if any member is having a fitful dream so they can comfort one another.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have such light bodies that they often wrap their tails around heavy objects to avoid being blown away by the wind. They are overly curious, so they will even risk venturing out during a storm to explore.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon moves by floating in a zig-zag pattern. Its fur is made out of tinier balloons, which instantly grow back when popped.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: On windy days, POKENAME shoot out silky threads from their mouths and attach them to trees and poles to prevent being blown away. Tugging on their balloon-string-like tails will immediately cause them to expel poisonous gas.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME fly high into the sky, relying on their sharp spines to defend their vulnerable bodies from bird-type Pokémon. When ready to evolve, they release the gas in their bodies, plummeting downwards at high speeds.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME live within clouds, spending their days creating tunnels through them as they consume water vapour. They can sometimes be seen popping out of the edges of clouds, their three heads looking for other nearby clouds to travel to.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME releases bursts of yellow mustard-scented dust from its wings to stun children. It then wraps its long wiry arms around them to carry them into the sky.
author: .izik

entry: It has an extremely light body filled with a special gas that allows it to fly. Because it does not need to flap its wings to fly, it uses them to adjust its trajectory. By contracting and extending its two tails, it controls its elevation.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME regularly abduct children from beaches. Thankfully for many parents, their ugly, hastily-made nests lie in bushes close to those beaches, making finding lost children easy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME watches children at playgrounds from high in the sky. Should one wander away alone, it swoops down and scoops them into its bill before flying away.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever POKENAME fly, they stagger their movements to use all of their limbs, giving the illusion of climbing stairs in the middle of the air. Children who try to grab onto a POKENAME as they fly away may find themselves abducted.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feed on gas pockets that can be found deep underground, preferring to seek out helium pockets where they can. They periodically have to surface to release waste gas, making high-pitched squeaks as they do.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While floating through city streets, POKENAME uses its long, thread-like limbs to steal wallets from travelers. It lines its nest with these stolen items, seemingly hoarding them as trophies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a popular Pokémon among children and adults alike. They have the helpful ability to float up to items high on shelves and float back down to bring their Trainer whatever they desire.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME love to rub up close against their trainers, showing affection through close physical contact. They generate a persistent static charge when doing so, often resulting in them getting stuck to their trainer's clothing and meowing for help.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drifts high above meadows to absorb electricity from storm clouds. It then shocks prey with this charge before dragging them into the sky.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's rubber body rubs against itself to generate static, which it absorbs through its limbs. It uses this to stun children before attempting to drag them away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a smooth, elastic, and glossy body that wrinkles when not fully inflated. To ensure its body is always taut, it traps the gas from meals to stretch its body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is considered a scourge at parties and special events. This is because it harbors a hatred against balloons, and will try to challenge them to fights. Ironically, it has a fear of balloons popping.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's uniquely rubbery skin produces a high-pitched squeaking whenever it rubs against itself. In the presence of Zangoose, POKENAME wraps its body into the shape of a balloon Pokémon to set up an ambush, only uncurling to strike first.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rub their claws whenever they are upset, producing a grating rubbery squeak with each pass. Many aquatic Pokémon have few ways to defend themselves against the harsh noise, leading many to do whatever it takes to keep POKENAME appeased.
author: quackquackattack

entry: On sunny days, POKENAME floats around the sky. Scientists release groups into the air, as their movements show wind speed and direction.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME seems particularly drawn to human children, often descending on them to stick its nose to them and leave a heart-shaped mark behind. It's not yet known for what purpose it does this.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME may rest in various spots depending on factors such as the day of the week, the temperature, and the general wind speed. They always travel as a group.
author: bobosmith01

entry: To keep from drifting away in the current, POKENAME entwine their string-like tails around seagrass. The fluffy growths on their heads store electricity, and when a school gathers, arcs of energy leap between them, turning the fluff a stormy gray.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME floats calmly through cloudy skies in search of food. Should it spot a blimp, it latches on to drain as much power as it can.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a tendency to play pranks on children swimming in the sea, which is why it is usually found near beaches or seaside resorts. During violent storms, it risks being swept out of the waves due to its very light body.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The humid gas that seeps from POKENAME's body is hotter than a furnace. It uses this intense heat to keep its den warm, even in the coldest environments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's gas-filled body allows it to float on the surface of ponds. It uses its string-like tail to grab at objects hidden beneath the water's surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME trains vigorously to strengthen its body. Unfortunately, its body is always lightweight, making it all too easy to be pushed around by strong foes or even strong gusts of wind.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats above lush fields, scattering seeds as it drifts. The fast-growing weeds it produces can overrun entire ecosystems within weeks.
author: .izik

entry: Like Drifloon, the white part of POKENAME's body is actually a cloud. Children like to nap on POKENAME's shell as a pillow, which frustrates POKENAME as it is pinned down by the child.
author: nakamagic

entry: It wraps its strings around unobservant hiker's ankles, attempting to trip them or pull them down mountains. It's much too light to do this to adults.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Despite resembling an ordinary green balloon, its sword-like leek is incredibly hard and dangerous. It uses this weapon with surprising skill.
author: .izik

entry: Using their three balloon heads, POKENAME are able to lift off the ground and glide through the air with ease.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME drifts peacefully through the night sky, its glowing segments resembling floating lanterns. It is often released during festivals, where its gentle light creates breathtaking displays.
author: ilija09

entry: The air escaping from its nose induces drowsiness, often used in dental offices to calm patients. Its sleepy scent makes it a curious helper.
author: .izik

entry: Though naive and playful, POKENAME has a notorious reputation for dragging children to play with it in the forests where it lives. It is believed that POKENAME was actually born from the spirits of lost children and still identifies with one of them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spins silk with a faint carrot-like scent, attracting herbivorous Pokémon. It lines its burrow with the soft strands, creating a warm and fragrant nest.
author: .izik

entry: The leaves atop POKENAME protect the contents of its basket-like head. Only trusted Trainers are allowed to remove the painted eggs it carries.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME uses its bone to dig up carrots from farmland. When spotted, it pretends to cry before fleeing once guards are lowered.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's powerful legs allow it to hop great distances, even while its outer shell hardens. It often leaps into tree branches to avoid predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats around berry patches gorging on the sweetest fruits it can find due to its extreme sweet tooth. If something spooks it, it billows out a stiflingly sweet cloud of smoke all around it on reflex.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are kind and empathic creatures that are understanding of others, to a fault. Trainers often need to step in to help them act assertively.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME kind and empathic creatures that are understanding of others, to a fault. Trainers often need to step in to help them act assertively.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's supple and colorful fur is used in a variety of luxury products. It sleeps several times a day; failure to do so results in it becoming grumpy and restless.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's ears unfurl as it prepares for battle, a telling sign of its rising aggression. These ears are incredibly powerful, capable of tossing three times its body weight.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME's fluffy tail contains a hidden venomous barb, which it uses only when threatened. It whimpers frequently, lulling foes into a false sense of security.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has unstable energy stored in its body. This energy can be released through its powerful ear attacks, or enhanced with an evolution stone.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: After deleting a program, POKENAME replaces its icon with a carrot image. Devices left unattended often resemble digital carrot patches over time.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attacks with powerful ear strikes when provoked. In dire circumstances, it hides in its sturdy shell to protect itself.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME eats large amounts of carrots to strengthen its developing shell. The tougher its shell becomes, the more confidently it faces predators.
author: .izik

entry: If properly fed, POKENAME will form an unbreakable bond with its Trainer. Any danger posed to its partner will be flattened and pummeled by its extendable ears.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME is a timid Pokémon that will immediately flee at the sight of strangers. It lives in the coldest and most remote mountain ranges and uses its own shed fur as lining in its nest.
author: alestrius

entry: POKENAME prefers to burrow near swift waterfalls, shedding there every day. If an intruder comes into its burrow, it coils its body before springing forward to knock the intruder unconscious.
author: torterraguy26

entry: The red eggs that POKENAME drops are said to symbolize new life. Because of that, they're eaten at many festive celebrations.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME enjoy hugs and kisses but easily get excited. When they are overstimulated, they have a tendency to gnaw on whatever is available.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME builds its nest near cauliflower fields, hiding within the pale stalks. Farmers often find it peacefully resting among the plants at dawn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly timid and will become stressed if it is alone. During cold weather, it huddles with other POKENAME for warmth, putting their fluff together for extra insulation.
author: cait_sith

entry: Despite having keen hearing, POKENAME startles easily. Loud noises cause it to lose control of its flight and crash into cave walls.
author: mepp.

entry: The fluff surrounding POKENAME's lower half acts as a sound-dampener, allowing it to move about unheard. It is much less skilled at staying unseen.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: The thick fur growing off its body smells like a carrot-based stew. It stores static electricity in this fur, which helps it deliver powerful shocks when needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has long ears that extend forward to strike opponents. Its tail stabilizes its footing, ensuring it does not get knocked over.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME jabs at its opponents with its ears, which have enough strength to break rocks. It also unnerves opponents with its cuteness, and grooms itself to ensure it always appears cute.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The leaves on its head release a strong aroma while it floats. The smell is reminiscent of carrot cake and cloves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will burrow underground in search of carrots to eat. Gardeners consider them to be pests for this reason, being forced out constantly.
author: santon5512

entry: It escapes danger by extending its ears to launch into treetops, then swinging away on branches with its tail. In the rare event that it needs to fight, its ears pack a stronger punch than any of its hands.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME live in cold environments, their thick fur keeping them warm. If it gets too cold, they curl up and wrap their ears around themselves, which twitch uncontrollably.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME live in cold environments, their thick fur keeping them warm. If it gets too cold, they curl up and wrap their ears around themselves, which twitch uncontrollably.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When POKENAME senses danger, it perks up its ears. It searches wide areas for food.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME are said to drive people insane by producing hallucinations of cute, long-eared Pokémon. Once a person is out of range, the hallucinations fade away without a trace.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME takes a defensive stance whenever it senses danger, raising its ears to appear larger. It has an imposing presence, though it is often timid in nature.
author: .izik

entry: Though it appears quite fluffy in texture, POKENAME's body is made of rock. The shell it carries resembles a festive holiday egg.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: POKENAME's sensitive ears can easily sense when data near it is being altered. Many have it on their computer to help alert them when something amiss is happening within their files.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME demonstrates almost perfect balance spinning on its singular large ear. Because the appendage is used mostly for balance, POKENAME has relatively poor hearing.
author: sk372

entry: Because of its adorably cute appearance, POKENAME is often gifted to young girls as a companion Pokémon. If it starts losing a battle, it bursts into tears to make its opponent feel guilty.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Extremely timid, POKENAME will flee across the land at high speeds at the mere hint of something approaching. It only stops during its travels to drink from the most pristine and untouched bodies of water.
author: sk372

entry: Very skittish and easily startled, POKENAME is not easy to befriend. They tend to only trust one person at a time.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME lobs its heavy tail at opponents when it is in a fight. Its tail is deceptively heavy and can knock out small Pokémon with a hit or two.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's favorite food are Poffins. After getting a Trainer to drop their guard with their cute act, they grab the Poffin case with their ears and awkwardly hop away.
author: lampent12

entry: Though POKENAME appears small and cute, its ears pack a devastating punch. At full power, they can shatter rocks with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME gets lonely easily and needs constant companionship to feel at ease. It will get very antsy if it goes even an hour without at least holding someone's hand.
author: sk372

entry: Ancient tomes claim garments woven from POKENAME's fur could give someone the power to reshape reality itself. Repeated experiments have disproven these legends, though the myths persist in folklore.
author: .izik

entry: With a combination of thick wool and a sturdy shell, POKENAME have powerful defenses They prefer eating cottonweeds and cattail plants.
author: frokachu

entry: The foliage of POKENAME's plants is extremely soft to touch, but its difficult to do so, as POKENAME will jump and squirm away when touched by anyone other than a trusted Trainer.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME nests in the hollow of an old oak, using fallen leaves to line its home. It always knows its way back, no matter how far it wanders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is nonviolent and rather timid, so seeing it unsheathe its blade is a rare sight. If threatened, it instead defaults to hitting something with its scabbard quickly before fleeing at top speed.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME sheds its fur in spring, it leaves cotton balls everywhere it goes. Despite its cute appearance, it is a Pokémon renowned for the power of its electric attacks, and underestimating it is often a mistake.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME unfurl their soft feelers the less nervous or scared they feel. A well-cared-for POKENAME bounces with every step, its feelers fluttering around as it moves through the air; this is a sight beloved by many.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is extremely difficult to get along with. It will release any frustrations it harbors on the nearby environment, leveling them back to a barren, earthen state. Scientists are unsure of the reason behind the carrot-shaped designs on its body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is able to move islands across seas by pushing them with the impact of its ears. Ancient myths have stated that the craters on the moon were caused by POKENAME bounding itself too high into the sky when unfurling its ears on the ground.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's fur changes coarseness depending on the phase of the moon. Their fur is at its softest during a full moon, during which time they are commonly gifted to loved ones as a sign of goodwill.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The only way to calm an enraged POKENAME is to pet it. If a Trainer stops petting it before it calms down, POKENAME will wrap its arms around them and suffocate them as an everlasting hug.
author: teatedtiten

entry: The fluff on POKENAME's ears is sticky and difficult to clean off once stuck to clothing. It can generate small flames at the tips of its ears to ward off attackers, but only for a short time.
author: sk372

entry: When an envious Mimikyu fused with Buneary, it created POKENAME. If POKENAME does not receive affection, it will replace the cotton on its ears.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its eyes are covered by its fluffy fur. Therefore, it tackles, bites, and uncoils its long ears to feel for its surroundings.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Its eyes are covered by its fluffy fur. Therefore, it tackles, bites, and uncoils its long ears to feel for its surroundings.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Its eyes are covered by its fluffy fur. Therefore, it tackles, bites, and uncoils its long ears to feel for its surroundings.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The two heads are great friends and get along tremendously. They try to help each other by sharing their food, but since they can't see if the portion is halved, this Pokémon often overeats.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The two heads are great friends and get along tremendously. They try to help each other by sharing their food, but since they can't see if the portion is halved, this Pokémon often overeats.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: This Pokémon often causes havoc even when they have good intentions. This is because the two heads it has for hands are uncontrollable and often bite.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME beguile Trainers into giving them treats by staring at them with their Baby-Doll Eyes. They stop Trainers from petting their fur if they refuse to give them a treat first.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Incredibly slothful, POKENAME sleeps for 20 hours a day and only wakes to eat. Its ears coil as it sleeps and can spring out suddenly with enough power to punch a hole through a tree trunk.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME collects discarded armor pieces from evolved Aron. It wears this armor to protect its soft, vulnerable body from predators.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME sheds delicate tufts of fur as it hops, leaving fuzzy trails behind. The tufts are said to bring luck to those who collect them.
author: .izik
