entry: POKENAME's body is encased in a glass shell that protects its cytoplasm. It can suck in nutrients through its arms and squirt out cytoplasm to expel waste or attack enemies.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME creates showers of the same cytoplasmic jelly that surrounds a Solosis's body. Biologists utilize POKENAME as a source of plentiful Solosis jelly that doesn't bring harm to any Solosis.
author: hophoppip

entry: Under their skin, the fruits that grow on POKENAME's neck have a wobbly, jelly-like texture. They've become popular as a dessert in some places.
author: hophoppip

entry: With its psychic powers, POKENAME is able to keep the other parts of its body close to its core. Since it is easily irritated, it takes only a moment for it to lose patience and attack anyone who gets too close.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME only open their shells when prey draws near. They can protect their cores with a special gel, the same gel that they can expand and control to quickly drag prey in.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME regularly use their own cores as bait for prey. When prey draws near, they will use their special gel to swallow it whole and dissolve it.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and communicate with the invisible psychic waves they can emit. Scientists are still unsure how POKENAME processes and navigates the world; many suspect they do not even need to use the five basic senses to survive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME surrounds itself with sparks, the special liquid around its core shines intensely, blinding its opponents. It communicates its feelings telepathically with the other members of the large group it travels with while searching for food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME surrounds itself with sparks, the special liquid around its core shines intensely, blinding its opponents. It communicates its feelings telepathically with the other members of the large group it travels with while searching for food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The amniotic fluid forming its coils, is rich in conductivity compounds that improve its Electric-type attacks. POKENAME uses its psychic powers to draw food toward its teeth, crushing it into fragments small enough to absorb.
author: fiordaliso

entry: With its psychic powers, POKENAME is able to keep the other parts of its body close to its core. Since it is easily irritated, it takes only a moment for it to lose patience and attack anyone who gets too close.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses most of its psychic energy to navigate the ocean floor in search of food. It defends itself by unleashing powerful electric discharges from the claws extending out of its gelatinous arms.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The gelatinous liquid on its body fills with bubbles when intruders enter its territory. POKENAME lashes vessels with its fins and uses psychic powers to drag their anchors to the ocean floor.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In order to maintain the high speeds it needs to catch its prey, POKENAME must concentrate hard to keep its gelatinous body stable. It is common to see young POKENAME running while using their telekinesis to carry detached bits of gel.
author: quietcognition

entry: POKENAME travel in groups, floating along effortlessly using river currents. Should a predator approach, they produce psychic vibrations to dip under the surface of the water.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME lurks by the shoreline near fishing spots. It uses telekinesis to create false tugs, leaving anglers irritated and confused.
author: .izik

entry: Since its body is so frail, its gel barrier protects it from any outside contact. It gets its nutrients by dissolving food in the gel then absorbing it through its skin.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME live in perfect stillness, reflecting on the world around them. Should they need to move, they latch onto a passing Pokémon. When the membrane surrounding them begins to ripple, it means that evolution is imminent.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's gel-like body allows it to deform and reshape itself to avoid attacks and strike back with its powerful fists. The red core in its center will cause it to lose shape if removed.
author: sk372

entry: Although timid by nature, POKENAME is endlessly curious. It floats after friendly Trainers, studying everything around it with its powerful psychic senses.
author: aggrotek

entry: POKENAME's body is very sensitive to germs, so it produces a thick gel that kills them almost instantly. Doctors will often have a POKENAME on hand to use its gel as a disinfectant.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is technically not venomous, but poisonous; its slimy tentacles must enter an orifice to take effect. Though smaller prey is sedated and consumed, larger creatures merely become nauseated.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME, though mostly nonlethal to humans, is an unwelcome sight on the beach. Being poisoned by one has been described as similar to downing a large bottle of cough syrup followed up with a heroic dose of hallucinogens.
author: dylonk25

entry: Though its body appears similar in texture to stone, it's actually soft and malleable to the touch. It's quite sensitive, so prodding it too much will incite it to respond with aggressive punching.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a soft outer layer of gel that encases a crystallized shell. Whenever they make contact with another substance, the gel shrivels up into a powder, causing POKENAME much pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The outer membrane of POKENAME crystallizes, forming a rock-hard boulder. Over time, it secretes gel from its core, reinforcing its shell.
author: germs2128

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in a waterproof oil that prevents its body from dissolving in the rain. Artisans use POKENAME's oil as a waterproof coating for their pots.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its highly malleable body allows POKENAME to squeeze through small cracks in the ice. It can withstand temperatures as cold as the vacuum of space.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME's translucent body helps it to sneak up on unsuspecting prey, which is then absorbed into said body to be gradually digested.
author: strawbearycandy

entry: POKENAME is durable due to its gel coating, which it controls with psychic powers to interact with its environment. The gel regrows quickly, so Fuschia City pastry chefs leave traps to harvest excess gel to coat desserts with a acidic flavor.
author: pjporwoll

entry: A popular but strange treatment involves letting a POKENAME clamp onto someone's hair and slowly slide back. It leaves behind a glossy coating that makes hair soft, shiny, and sweet-smelling for days.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME keep the soft gel that forms their body safe within their great shells, retreating within it if they ever feel endangered. They can fire the gel at high pressure out of their cannons, recalling it with their psychic powers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The soft and gelatinous bodies of POKENAME leave them vulnerable to predators. They scavenge sea shells using their sticky bodies, keeping themselves safe from danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME constantly leak a green gas from their bodies, which envelops them at all times. This haze helps to both hide their presence and protect themselves from the sun.
author: santon5512

entry: The special liquid surrounding its core allows POKENAME to live in dark caves without suffering from the cold. It uses its psychic powers to play tricks on and tease both Pokémon and humans alike.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Wrapped in a unique liquid, POKENAME thrives across all terrains. Its psychic powers and the horn on its head are its only means of protection.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME's gelatinous body gives it pitiful defenses, so it hides away inside tree holes for safety. It uses psychic powers to pluck leaves and berries from the tree and bring them back to its home to feast on.
author: sk372

entry: Its slime actively absorbs pine needles and seeds from the forest floor. These are digested within the jelly-like substance to nourish it.
author: .izik

entry: The jelly that coats POKENAME are surplus cells that it secretes during its constant mitosis. These are infected with pathogens.
author: chorb33

entry: Sticky green fluid leaks from its vines, acting as an incredibly adhesive glue. This substance is almost impossible to remove once it bonds.
author: .izik

entry: It creates invisible objects to cause people to trip and fall. Watching from rooftops, it gleefully observes their misfortune with mischievous delight.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its psychic powers to immobilize prey before slicing them with razor-sharp blades. This method ensures it strikes with precision.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon must focus with both eyes on the target to imitate them properly. Otherwise, its two separate brains will cause improper transformations.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME absorbs data from active chat rooms, siphoning emotional energy from participants. When full, it releases psychic pulses capable of disabling nearby devices.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have two brains, located on either side of a long body. Young individuals have been spotted trying to run in two directions at once.
author: dylonk25

entry: The jelly coating its body was once used in ancient Sinnoh as a medicine for mental fatigue. This peculiar tradition has long since faded.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spins webs out of the gel that comprises its body. When prey get trapped in this gelatinous web, the web collapses around the prey to begin dissolving POKENAME's next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME's strength grows, its ability to inflate its body and solidify its membrane grows as well. At full inflation, the membrane gains a rubbery texture that bounces almost any basic attack away.
author: sk372

entry: Its second brain uses psychic powers to detect and avoid future obstructions during flight. This foresight makes it a master of aerial navigation.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME focuses on too many things, parts of it begin to drift away. It uses most of its brain power to remain whole, and if a part is irrecoverably lost, it can regenerate it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It floats lazily in quicksand, enjoying the slow descent. Once fully submerged, it sleeps for days before effortlessly swimming back to the surface.
author: .izik

entry: It absorbs objects it loves into its slime, using them as an extension of its body. The Moon Stone it carries acts as a focus for its more powerful psychic attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Its upper, smaller brain actually does most of the thinking. It interacts with other beings outside of its own kind very rarely.
author: adrian151

entry: Its jelly-like covering emits a pleasant pine scent that intensifies as it consumes more pine needles. This aroma makes it oddly soothing despite its sticky nature.
author: .izik

entry: Despite constantly levitating off the ground, POKENAME thinks it can actually fly with its small wings. It can be seen throwing itself off of high places, only to be cushioned by its gelatinous body.
author: mistymagius

entry: The gelatin-like goo covering POKENAME's body can cause visions, but is highly medicinal when used in the production of antibiotic ointments. Excessive application to the skin can cause headaches from psychic feedback, so moderation is important.
author: .izik

entry: Using their psychic powers, they pull in and store rocks and hard nuts within their barrel-like mouths to later shoot at foes using jets of water. Their gelatinous tentacles are incredibly sticky, which allows them to easily hold onto their foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME emits a nausea-inducing scent from its gelatinous body when its scared. This defensive mechanism discourages predators from approaching.
author: .izik

entry: The green slime dripping from POKENAME's tail is frequently harvested as a heat sink for machinery. It can also use its psychic abilities to manipulate the thoughts of those nearby, influencing their creativity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have tails that are made out of gel that makes struggling out of their grip incredibly difficult. The sticky, poisonous gel clings to their prey long after the initial encounter and should be washed off to avoid accidental ingestion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The liquid gel around the bodies of POKENAME act as a conductor for electricity and makes contact with them dangerous. When fully charged, they can transfer a heart-stopping amount of energy to flow from their bodies to whoever touched them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It keeps the Thunder Stone that evolved it enveloped in a special liquid. It can use the Thunder Stone to unleash electrical shocks of 10,000 volts.
author: duskrd

entry: It is believed POKENAME's nighttime roaming makes up 80 percent of claims of UFO sightings. Its small antenna emits deceptively powerful radio waves that interfere with electronics in a wide vicinity.
author: sk372

entry: The syrup-like substance covering its body seems to have a mind of its own, moving independently like vines. This sentient slime reacts instictively to heat and light.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME experiences stress whenever it needs to levitate its exterior jar, leaving it weary afterwards. Researchers note that it is more likely to be tired or depressed due to its living conditions.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are attuned to the feelings of others, and their viscous bodies cling to people they enjoy spending time with. Their bodies are warm and soft and give damp yet comforting hugs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using its two brains, POKENAME wields its developing psychic powers with impressive finesse. A lone POKENAME will dedicate most of its time to furthering its intelligence and honing its psychic abilities.
author: nyoomymph

entry: They live among plants and attack wandering Grass and Poison-type Pokémon with acid to hunt. They grow at an exponential rate; only when they slow down are they close to evolution.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its body allows it to move effortlessly through thick mud. Unlike most slimes, the syrup coating it is not sticky, aiding its mobility.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have multiple nuclei floating within their body, providing scaffolding for their toxic gel to adhere to. These nuclei glow when they use their psychic powers, attacking one another with blasts of noxious energy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's feelers extend and act as antennae to transmit psychic waves. These waves subtly deter other Pokémon from approaching its nest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their psychic powers to float. The few times one has been seen attempting to walk, their limbs couldn't hold them up thanks to the lack of musculature.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME have smooth, sensitive bodies that can regrow major pieces if lost in battle. Trainers are advised to carry around lotion or water to make sure their POKENAME's membrane doesn't dry out.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME horns light up with a pulse of energy whenever they use their psychic powers. They are potent psychics, flinging energy blasts in battle and able to telekinetically move several tonnes of material at will.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The bubble-like exterior of POKENAME is meant to protect others from itself, as its core body is incredibly toxic, causing harm just by being near it. It's very reclusive as a result, staying away from others for their sake.
author: sk372

entry: The metallic object that POKENAME holds can be swung around like a flail. This can come at a cost, however, as if the object is swung too hard, it will separate from the main body, and cause the fused Pokémon to split.
author: turcai_87271

entry: The transparent, wax-like fluid dripping from its head is intensely hot. This burning liquid leaves scorch marks wherever it falls.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME generates electric fields within its protective membrane, shocking anything that gets too close. When threatened, it glows brightly to intimidate foes before delivering a paralyzing jolt.
author: .izik

entry: The slime on its body boils constantly, radiating intense heat. Contact with it can cause severe burns to anything that gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is covered in a viscous slime that glows faintly in the dark. This glow distracts prey as it closes in silently for the attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores vegetables inside the gooey orb it guards to pickle them. It prefers okra and parsnips, which it ferments into a sour snack before battle.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It emits waves of psychic energy to spin its body at incredible speeds. This rotation can create powerful gusts of wind to fend off attackers.
author: .izik

entry: Rising from tar pits, POKENAME divide its power between its two brains. One of a powerful psychic mind, and the other of a once invincible dweller of the ancient world.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Having two brains, POKENAME controls the ice clouds it forms with great efficiency. Its destructive power is similarly increased.
author: coridiant

entry: It absorbs the memories of those around it, transforming them into intricate dances. Each performance reflects the emotions it collects.
author: .izik

entry: Its slimy body is made of cytosol that contains a divided brain. Because it will dry out if it stays too long in the sun, the two halves must work together to find shade.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME's gooey body is protected by a thin, slick membrane that cushions it from attacks. It uses its psychic powers to attack with its slime, confusing opponents as it slides gracefully across the ground.
author: thepandasharky

entry: The gelatin-like substance covering its body smells and feels like honey. Its sticky nature attracts both friends and foes alike.
author: .izik

entry: Its gelatinous covering emits an eerie glow in the dark, mesmerizing its prey. Before attacking, it howls, pinning its target with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is able to duplicate itself multiple times with ease. However, to scientists' confusion, it only does this to create backup singers for its performances. The purpose of said performances, although not malevolent, remains a mystery.
author: merclipse

entry: POKENAME protect their core nucleus within a bell-shaped bubble of gel. More durable parts of their body protrude from the bottom of their gel, moving them along with scuttling motions.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The glitter falling from its wings contains remnants of psychic power, causing confusion and headaches. This shimmering dust can disorient foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produce a soft, viscous jelly that melts into a slurry of nutritious goo when eaten. Its body produces an excess volume of twice its body weight in jelly, most of which it sheds in large bulbous blobs that other Pokémon eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The gelatin coating POKENAME's body releases a swampy odor that lingers in humid areas. It uses its psychic powers to pluck apples from trees, floating them toward its mouth.
author: .izik

entry: It can reach speeds up to 60 mph and fit its body through a two-inch gap without slowing down. If its gelatinous body becomes too watery due to its diet, it risks ejecting its core during high-speed maneuvers.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME gel has natural sound-dampening qualities, allowing them to move almost silently. Sound engineers employ them to help ensure studios are effectively sound-proofed, letting POKENAME apply a layer of gel across the walls.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It bumps into people, scattering coins from their purses onto the ground. It then absorbs the coins into its gelatinous paws and flees.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's brain is divided into many smaller portions, each focusing on controlling different aspects of sunny weather in its vicinity, such as humidity, temperature, and cloud cover. It becomes sluggish during solar eclipses.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its main body has divided parts of itself to use as relays to expand the range of its psychic powers. With these organic relays, it can better control the mass of special gel that protects it and utilize it better in battle.
author: infinex21

entry: The second brain is significantly more intelligent than the main one, solving complex equations in mere milliseconds. This dual intelligence makes it an incredible strategist.
author: .izik

entry: Mysterious and highly feared, POKENAME's psychoactive poison is incredibly potent. Though it does no physical damage, most victims pass out from shock. Those who do escape are never quite the same afterwards.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME coat their bodies in a watery gel that allows them to swim at speed, the gel letting them cut through water easily. When they feel threatened their gel can be withdrawn into their shell, keeping themselves safe from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have helped scientists understand how water shoots from the body of Blastoise thanks to their clear bodies. Many classrooms have a visit from POKENAME to show off how they fire their water cannons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fluid coating its body can induce intense delusions if touched, causing people to hallucinate an entire month of their life. This effect leaves them disoriented and confused.
author: .izik

entry: It lingers near playgrounds, using hypnosis to convince children to hand over their snacks. Its mischievous nature makes it both cunning and troublesome.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release spores from the bulb on their back that smell like fresh laundry. Manufacturers take these spores and incorporate them into deodorant sticks to give people the same fresh, clean smell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in a habitat that has a lot of Fire-type predators around them, so they eat Occa Berries to help defend themselves against the predators. This is especially necessary because their cotton-like fur catches fire easily.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As opposed to solid steel, POKENAME's body is composed of cotton and lead, allowing it to drift through the air at a slow rate. POKENAME loves drifting about within the rainclouds, although entire towns suffering from power outages say otherwise.
author: lovelover75

entry: The large cotton bloom around POKENAME's neck is very delicate and tears easily, so it prefers to avoid those who seem aggressive.
author: .realthree

entry: Flocks of POKENAME can be seen by the hundreds flying along warm breezes, migrating to warmer areas during the winter months. They will use some of their extra cotton to help build their nests.
author: mistymagius

entry: The silk it produces is incredibly durable and elastic, causing it to be sought after by artisans. These delicate fibers are used to weave luxurious fabrics and fine garments.
author: .izik

entry: It sips sparkling morning dew and hops around in sunny spots in groves in the woods. Some POKENAME are curious and wander away from home: these are the source of most wild POKENAME that Trainers catch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It consumes barley until it becomes too heavy to move, often resting in fields after its feast. Farmers must keep an eye on it to protect their crops.
author: .izik

entry: The fur of a POKENAME is incredibly impervious to water, letting the Pokémon remain light enough to float on the winds even right after a swim.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME hide in cellar corners, pretending to be clumps of dust or stray fluff. They lie in wait for opportunities to steal food, their fluffy bodies helping them to escape on the wind with their scraps.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME floats higher on days without a dense overcast. It does this to get as close to the sun as possible.
author: .izik

entry: It sneaks into herbalists' shops to steal ingredients for its personal stash. These stolen herbs are often used to prepare remedies for its companions.
author: .izik

entry: Typically, male POKENAME do not grow fur on their bodies and have longer gills. This is because they are tasked with finding safe places on the ground for the females to rest at night.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Typically, female POKENAME are covered in fur and have shorter gills. This is because they spend the day floating in the air, looking out for danger, while the males stay on the ground below.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's flower spews cotton-like spores when it is agitated. The spores are dangerous to breathe due to their tendency to clump together.
author: mistymagius

entry: The wind flowing through its fine strings as it floats creates a playful whistling sound that echoes through the air. This haunting melody often amuses and confuses those who hear it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses psychic power to redirect falling cotton fluffs. It drops them across the battlefield to slow down opponents with precise placement.
author: .izik

entry: It shoots cotton out of its cannons to scare predators away. This defense is often ineffective since it's just cotton, and it gets attacked anyways.
author: soup1900

entry: It gathers daisies and carries them wherever it goes, often creating little bouquets. It scatters these flowers from the sky as a gift to other Pokémon, making a charming sight in the wild.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME consumes carnations to maintain its soft, cotton-like body, enhancing its ability to float on the wind. It uses its horn to knock branches aside as it drifts through the air.
author: .izik

entry: Any cotton that is picked from POKENAME's body will remain warm to the touch, even for years after being removed. POKENAME itself, however, does not like being used as a pillow, and will drastically increase its temperature if laid on.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME is very cowardly. It covers itself in cotton to hide from predators.
author: themicelegion

entry: Spacey and easily distracted, POKENAME always has its head in the clouds. It can be difficult for a POKENAME's Trainer to get their Pokémon to focus in battle.
author: hophoppip

entry: It will bury its head in the cotton around its neck to hide from danger. They will swiftly fly off on wind currents if they feel threatened.
author: pankiwi

entry: As it flies, it releases a bitter aroma that lingers in the air. This scent often deters predators from following too closely.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drift in groups of six to seven over towns. When they cluster too closely together, computers below them begin to malfunction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fluffy rump releases a calming scent when shaken, soothing those nearby and diffusing tense situations. Its antlers are highly sensitive, detecting even subtle shifts in a foe's movements.
author: .izik

entry: It guards flower patches fiercely, chasing away anyone who approaches without permission. Its determination makes it a reliable protector.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME adores marigolds and can often be found resting among them for hours. It carefully gathers their seeds and stores them within its fluffy body for safekeeping.
author: .izik

entry: Given the chance, it can devour an entire field's harvest in under two days, leaving behind cotton that takes over the soil. Farmers try to keep it away by offering it spare bales of hay for it to snack on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME ride the wind in schools, only occasionally descending near lakes or rivers to soak up water for their never-ending journey.
author: mx_wellman

entry: While sleeping in a tree, POKENAME causes large tufts of cotton to grow from the bark. This special cotton is surprisingly brittle and difficult to use for sewing.
author: .izik

entry: It releases pollen that can burst into flames at will, creating fiery bursts. This explosive ability makes it a unique mix of beauty and danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly light; if it wishes to remain in place, it must dig its feet into the ground and grip the earth with its talons. Once it is ready to move on, POKENAME will unearth its feet and allow the wind to carry its body along.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in a thick layer of highly buoyant cotton. Because of this, it struggles to dive below a lake's surface for any significant length of time.
author: .izik

entry: When the cotton on POKENAME's cheeks puffs out, it somehow gains the ability to lift off the ground with ease. It drifts above meadows, spitting gentle streams of water onto the plants below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cotton-like covering on its head vibrates when it senses danger in the area. It teleports away when threatened, leaving behind a small cloud of fluff in its place.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are renowned for the variety of colors they can change to when exposed to combinations of pressure and temperature. They use their long tongues to drink water and avoid getting close to it, for their cotton grows too heavy when wet.
author: infinex21

entry: The mass of cotton on POKENAME's back is light and fluffy, making them a cozy spot for wild Pokémon to fall asleep on. Before they move from one location to another, they comb their cotton fluff to ensure sleeping Pokémon are not carried with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their maw-like appendages to store food and to make themselves look fiercer than they truly are. Their maws are incredibly absorbent and quickly grow heavy when wet, so they take care to keep them away from any liquids.
author: infinex21

entry: It uses its cotton to keep people it likes comfortable. When it engages in combat it can imbue some of its cotton with venom before throwing it at foes.
author: bacondlx

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME can float on the gentlest of winds. They drift over inland fields, gathering pollen and seeds in their fluff, scattering them over coastal reefs to feed sea-going Pokémon valuable nutrients.
author: vic1312

entry: Seeds shed from POKENAME's cotton were once believed to grant a single wish if gathered in great numbers. Careful study later proved these claims entirely false.
author: .izik

entry: Dandelion-like seed heads float off the POKENAME's head and plant themselves in the ground. When POKENAME returns in future seasons, it can remember where it has been by the scent of the flowers that have grown from those seeds.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: The voluminous cotton growing from POKENAME's bark allows it to float over long distances. It can even do this while sleeping, staying airborne for hours at a time.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's back is sturdy and comfortable, meaning it can be used to transfer injured Pokémon and people to where they can be healed, all while keeping them stable and in as little pain as possible.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The giant cotton plants on POKENAME's back regrow quickly when cut. Clothing manufacturers are considering using POKENAME as a source of material.
author: hophoppip

entry: Normally docile, it spends its days weaving heat-resistant cloth. When threatened, it ejects pillows of cotton that ignite into bright balls of flame to scare off predators.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME stays up high in tree branches, avoiding most avenues of conflict. If forced to defend itself, it lets loose a burst of cotton from its tail that causes a burning sensation on contact with skin.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its sheer power and speed, it's so light that the strength of its own punches usually sends it flying. POKENAME becomes able to hurt others as it develops the superhuman grip strength of its feet, to use the floor as a counterforce.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME is covered in cottony down feathers that protect it from the cold winds and waters during its adolescence. When POKENAME is ready to evolve, it will begin to molt all of its feathers at the same time, during which it cannot swim or fish.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The cotton-like growths on POKENAME are actually closer in consistency to steel wool. It sharpens the blades on its wings in the crashing tides where it lives, then uses the cotton to smooth out any impurities.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME gracefully floats along the ice, making sure its cottony bits steer clear of water. While it prefers solitude, it sometimes sticks to others of their kind.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME shoots cotton into its opponent's eyes before attacking. Its light weight makes it nimble yet easy to push around.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME uses its pugil stick-like weapon to push away would be attackers. If the battle seems lost, it shoots its cotton at its foe to escape.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Though it appears soft, the cotton on POKENAME's body is filled with steel shrapnel. Some companies have crafted heavy-duty cleaning utensils from it.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME uses its cotton to create walls that its prey cannot see through, though it can see through them thanks to its x-ray vision. Once the moment strikes, it leaps through the soft and airy barrier, ambushing the prey before they can react.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's iridescent cotton saves most of its fluffiness even when wet, making it excellent for water-resistant clothes. Its tail is so soft and downy that hugging it can wash negative emotions from one's heart.
author: milchik

entry: Tufts of cotton grow from POKENAME's feelers each autumn before being naturally shed. It uses these to build itself a comfortable nest before the winter's cold arrives.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cotton-like body is said to be the softest and most cuddly of all Pokémon. However, it is extremely timid; only the most trusted of Trainers get to hug it, while anything else will be smacked with its ears before it leaps away in fear.
author: sk372

entry: Tiny and lightweight, the extremely-cautious POKENAME will try to escape from anything unfamiliar the second it notices it. It leaps into the air, and lets even the faintest breeze carry its small body off somewhere hopefully safer.
author: sk372

entry: Its tails expel large amounts of pollen, which it uses to mark its territory. The dense clouds of pollen often leave trails through the air as it moves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are raised for the cotton their wings shed daily, which is used in clothing and blankets. They spread cotton in battle, igniting it to burn foes. Ecologists are helping POKENAME recover their dwindling population.
author: chibitales

entry: Families of POKENAME race across the landscape at high speed, their long leaf-like tails trailing behind them. They are able to intensify the sunlight above them whilst using their tails to turn the same light into an abundance of energy to run with.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spend their days weaving through the grass of lush meadows. No predator cares to hunt them due to the dirt strewn throughout their cotton.
author: _testrun_

entry: Young herb seedlings are its favorite food, which it carefully selects from forest floors. It often competes with other herbivorous Pokémon for these delicate greens.
author: .izik

entry: Pillows stuffed with POKENAME cotton are popular as it is rumoured to manifest positive energy. Though these claims are unproven, the soft texture is known to at least provide a restful sleep and leave users feeling refreshed.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: It can fall asleep even while eating, often dozing mid-meal. Other Pokémon sometimes find it with food still in its mouth.
author: .izik

entry: When the cotton covering POKENAME's body dries out, it becomes incredibly brittle. Because of this, it prefers to remain submerged in the ocean for most of its life.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have remarkably light bodies despite their thick, cotton-like fur. Their fur is a powerful electrical conductor and very absorbant of fluids. When their fur is wet they struggle to release their own electricity, so they hide during rain.
author: infinex21

entry: A group of POKENAME gather to form a massive ball of static electricity. Its fluffy fur dazzles when POKENAME senses danger.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME ride in thunderstorms, floating into the paths of lightning bolts to absorb energy from the strikes. When they finally settle in the lee of the storm, they use the energy they've gathered to grow or evolve.
author: vic1312

entry: It tramples through fields as it searches for flowers to eat. While it actively appreciates the flavor and feeling of eating these crushed flowers, it doesn't seem to realize just how much destruction it leaves behind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a highly valuble asset to flower shops due to its ability to smell when plants are sick. It grinds plant matter into fertilizer or medicine, making it a key part of garden production.
author: .izik

entry: During windy seasons it will curl up and let the wind carry it to far away lands. As it floats with the wind it will release pollen, especially if it is in warm climates.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Though beautiful, its petals can become razor sharp, slicing through anything they touch. This trait makes it both graceful and dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts lazily over sunflower fields, using its tiny tendrils to pluck seeds from the blossoms. It can go days without landing, carried effortlessly by the breeze.
author: .izik

entry: It hops through fields while munching on flower buds, savoring their fresh taste. Other Pokémon often follow it, hoping to share in its floral feast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have far fluffier and lighter cotton than unfused Cottonee. This makes them far lighter and easier for the breeze to pick up. They are a popular Pokémon for younger Trainers as they are squishy and enjoy being hugged.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The cotton on POKENAME's body comes off easily, sticking to the mouth of opponents long enough for it to escape. It lounges in fields to absorb energy from the sun and burrows into the ground at night.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME hovers near powerlines, positioning itself as close as possible without making direct contact. The static charge in the air causes its cotton-like fluff to crackle softly with energy.
author: .izik

entry: Extremely light, it can float for miles on gentle breezes. This ability allows it to travel vast distances in search of new plants to pollinate.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is almost weightless and is able to conserve energy by drifting on the breeze like a puff of cotton. When it spies its prey, it snaps its wings and darts forward with incredible speed.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME is able to effortlessly alternate between drifting on the breeze and flying with incredible speed. This gives it unmatched aerial mobility, though it may struggle to maintain its bearing in strong winds.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME's feeding caves are well documented, but the nesting grounds they come from are a mystery. When startled, they expel cotton from their bodies as a distraction, leaving researchers still wondering where they go.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: When POKENAME sense vibrations via their feelers, they go still, drop to the ground, and tuck in their small feet to disguise themselves as small shrubs. To keep from being blown away by strong winds, POKENAME dig their feet into a hard surface.
author: infinex21

entry: Its cotton-like exoskeleton allows POKENAME to float down from high places. It then lands comfortably on the ground, ready to roll again.
author: themicelegion

entry: Snorunt's cloak fused with the cotton, making it distorted. While not in pain, it doesn't seem to enjoy it.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME's leaves emit a peanut butter-like scent, attracting curious Pokémon to its presence. It floats above meadows, spreading the aroma, though this makes it a target for both friendly and predatory Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: It puffs out, tears off, and throws its cotton to protect itself or others. Many believe POKENAME is drawn to those in pain and offers them comfort because it, too, is frail and wishes not for others to suffer like it has.
author: infinex21

entry: Standing guard over fields, it wards off intruders with its imposing presence. Farmers value its protection, ensuring bountiful harvests.
author: .izik

entry: Their heavy green pigmentation comes from their diet of sassafras leaves, which are said to provide miraculous cures to many modern diseases. Additionally, this diet makes POKENAME poisonous to other predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's ears can detect lies, twitching whenever falsehoods are spoken, causing other Pokémon to avoid deceit in its presence. The cotton-like substance on its head dampens unnecessary sounds, and it manipulates it to focus on important noises.
author: .izik

entry: Amaranth is its preferred food, which it plucks delicately from the fields. Its lightweight body allows it to float gently as it forages.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME thrives in both forests and the shallows of the sea. The ear-like structures on its head are for smelling.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME fluff is light enough that they can be swept up into the air with a strong enough gust of wind. They seek out windy places so that they can float through the air, twirling in place and stretching their leaves out to catch the sun.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It bounces about as if it were as light as a feather. Because of this, many of its opponents are caught off-guard by its heavy blows.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME collects seafoam within its fluffy cotton, absorbing moisture as it floats near the shore. This helps it stay hydrated even in dry coastal winds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are rather lightweight, able to drift in the air when spreading their leaf claws out. They can throw puffy cotton to distract attackers. This cotton is prized for its quality and rarity.
author: entomoxie

entry: Clinging to ocean rocks, POKENAME scrapes off barnacles to feed on. If startled, it instantly releases its grip and lets the wind carry it away to safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's outer shell is very soft and shedded chunks of it are often used as a chalk substitute. When attacked, it shoots dust from its body and escapes.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME is fidgety, hopping around quickly to scrounge food and shedding clouds of fluff in self-defense. Its regularly-shed fur can be processed and used as a cheap alternative to cotton products.
author: sk372

entry: There are thousands of microscopic thorns present in the cotton POKENAME wears. When threatened, it expels cotton all around it, creating a near-impenetrable dome. Touching it causes an itching sensation, similar to fiberglass.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's shell is soft but fragile, and gets sturdier but heavier in the rain. When attacked, it shoots its spikes and runs off.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The tufts that POKENAME summons are some of the most comfortable materials that can be found in the world. People have mixed opinions on using it for pillows, though, because those who fall asleep on them often see glimpses of the future.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Living on volcanic islands, POKENAME feeds on soot. The ash accelerates the growth of the cotton covering its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stands in gourd patches, waving its arms as cotton drifts from its body. The fibers nourish the soil, encouraging healthy plant growth.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cotton fluff is soft, but often becomes infested with mold and mildew because it is hard to dry. Some Trainers allow small plants to grow in POKENAME's fluff to add a bit of flair.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's cotton soaks up water with ease, keeping them pleasantly damp even during a drought. They can generally be found paddling around ponds and lakes, but will come on land during rain showers.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME can be found staring longingly at bodies of water. If it gets wet, the cotton of a POKENAME will weigh it down. Trainers who care for one must be gentle when brushing its cotton, as it's quite sensitive.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The cotton surrounding POKENAME's body is filled with bubbles containing helium. This allows it to float up to 10 feet above the ocean's surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fluffy fur grows faster while traveling with its pack. During this time, it releases a fragrant hyacinth scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drift in the wind until one of their sharp spines jabs into a tree branch, where they will then remain until ready to evolve. While they drift, Trainers in the nearby area will take cover to avoid an uncomfortable poke, or worse.
author: vic1312

entry: As POKENAME fly, tufts of powder-stuffed cotton shed from their wings. The powder contains pollen and scales that cause allergies to flare up in some individuals, especially during spring.
author: chibitales

entry: Parts of POKENAME's cotton-like body need to be exposed to the air to absorb moisture. To defend itself, it expels the outermost layer of cotton and silk, agitating a predator's mobility and vision so it can attempt escape.
author: sk372

entry: The fluff of POKENAME is said to be both incredibly strong and soft. They hold deep disdain for those who pluck from it.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: When POKENAME's dust lingers on a plant's surface for too long, an odd cotton-like substance begins to grow rapidly. While the fibers are beautiful in appearance, the texture is horribly rough and ill-suited for clothing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be found in knitting baskets, nibbling on the yarn balls. POKENAME enjoy it when their Trainers use their fluff to knit, clapping upon the completion of a project.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME seeks out orchids in dense forests, as they are its preferred delicacy. It nibbles carefully to avoid harming the plant, and the flowers seem to fuel the flames in its stomach, making its fluff hot to the touch.
author: .izik

entry: This excitable little chef is able to perfectly season any dish it has cooked with its gentle flames and naturally grown herbs. While preferring to prepare vegetable dishes, POKENAME will prepare most meals to a high standard.
author: evilgammon

entry: On extremely windy days, POKENAME can be seen getting lifted out of the water and tossed through the air. They try to use their leaves to steer back, however, it rarely works.
author: clownatosis

entry: It feeds on seeds that it collects from fallen flowers. This simple diet helps maintain its light and airy body.
author: .izik

entry: It enjoys sleeping under waterfalls, using the rushing water as a soothing lullaby. While it sleeps, it absorbs water with its fluffy body to help it grow.
author: .izik

entry: Due to POKENAME's soft cotton and friendly nature, they are often used to teach children how to ride. They often form strong bonds with their charges.
author: howlingstarr

entry: Each of POKENAME's heads prioritize their own safety, so they will pull off each other's cotton to use for themselves. If one head gets too greedy, the cotton will start to impair its vision.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME protect their fluffy, soft bodies with a tough grassy shell. They are lighter than their bulky appearance would suggest and can bob along the water's surface without sinking.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are the epitome of fluffy, as their delicate wisps feel plush to the touch. Despite feeling physical, pulling a tuft of wisps causes them to disintegrate into smoke.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the sand save for its nostrils, almost completely hidden from view. When it smells prey coming near, it uses an explosion to propel itself out of the sand and careen towards its prospective meal.
author: sk372

entry: These desert Pokémon have evolved to be able to hide their own heads within remains, with their lower bodies submerged in the sands. When prey draws near, they grab hold of a bone and use it like a club to pummel them into submission.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spews clouds of sand to mask its approach on prey and to distract foes while it hides. Because of its mischievous streak, thieves partner with it to take advantage of the blinding sand sprays while absconding with valuables.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When overheated, stone flaps along POKENAME's back lift up to release internal heat. This keeps it cool enough to keep hunting in the sun.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can swim through soft sand, using their horn to break any hard surface that impedes their travels. Wild POKENAME store heat within their bodies during the summer, which they use to keep warm through the autumn and winter seasons.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME is not very intelligent, often mistaking rocks for prey and lunging at them, risking injury. Many underestimate it, despite its extremely dangerous bite.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME makes its home in large divots in the undersea sand. A curious sort, it often pokes its head out to observe its surroundings, but is quick to retreat back home unless food is involved.
author: sk372

entry: The bane of Swimmers, POKENAME blends perfectly with the mud and silt at the bottom of lakes. It lies motionless until anything blocks the sunlight, causing it to explode to the surface and bite with enough force to bend steel.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME hides beneath pop-up ads on shady websites. When a cursor draws near, it snaps its jaws as if trying to bite the pointer.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows into desert sand during the day to sleep and hunts above ground during the night. It will molt underground once its skin becomes too tight.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME keeps its eyes and nose above the desert sand to peer at its surroundings. It often uses the fire on its back to entice potential prey to move closer before striking.
author: bonquilis

entry: While POKENAME appears small and friendly, it has a powerful bite. In the wild, POKENAME tend to be found sunbathing on sandy shores.
author: cosmodette

entry: POKENAME, in spite of its cuteness, can deliver devastating bites to careless Trainers. They move very quickly, seemingly swimming in sand, with only their nostrils and backspikes visible.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME hunt by biting their prey while submerged underwater. Once they have a good grip, they roll and twist their body to severely damage the prey's leg and any chance of escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is extremely mischievous, and especially likes to steal anything that reminds it of meteors or stars. When caught in the act of mischief, it cries and usually gets away with it due to its cuteness.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sometimes swims in sand, concealing its leathery, brightly coloured eggshell. It might occasionally get stuck on its back trying to stand upright.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME tests its jaw strength on garbage cans. Once the lid is cracked open, it devours whatever scraps spill out without hesitation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are mostly passive in the wild. Their aversion to violence causes them to be accepted into other Pokémon's colonies, where they work with them to clear away any detritus.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's soft and squishy form lets it easily slither into the sand to hide from danger. The sand grains stick to its body when it emerges, helping to keep it cool beneath the scorching midday sun.
author: sk372

entry: These flat Pokémon can be found sliding along the surface of the desert sand. Some hieroglyphs seem to depict their sightings.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME spend most of the day resting beneath the desert sand to remain cool. They emerge from the sand to stretch their wings and glide through the sky. Their main source of food comes from leftovers after carnivorous Pokémon eat their fill.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flocks gather around popular picnic sites, watching park-goers from the tops of trees. When they spy a meal that is not being paid enough attention, they will swarm in, stealing as much food as they can to the dismay of the picnickers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME make their homes in the lava tubes of long-extinct volcanoes. They lie in wait near the entrance to these tunnels, pressing themselves against the basalt walls and ambushing unwary cavers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While flying across desert skies, POKENAME may dive into the sand mid-flight. It quickly burrows after prey like Sandshrew.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleep during the day, basking in the warm desert sun. Once night falls, they go out hunting for small insects, using their powerful noses to sniff them out from under the sand.
author: mistymagius

entry: Scampering through the desert, POKENAME pulls its prey out of burrows with its narrow maw. When the burrow is deeper than its snout, it sneezes out embers in frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It slithers into backpacks or bags during dimly lit conditions to gain shelter from the cold. Trainers who attempt to use an Escape Rope may find a POKENAME instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During cold nights, its ears roll up in a circular fashion, and it buries itself deep into the sand. It may snap its jaws together to drive off approaching curious Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A chilling breeze escapes POKENAME's jaws before it delivers a kiss that leaves foes disoriented. The confusion can last for several hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are difficult to train if they grew up in the wild, as they typically were never taught to control their destructive urges. They will bite, poke, and shock almost anything they come across without hesitation if they are curious enough.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME stick their snouts into burrows to pull small rodent Pokémon out. This struggle often leaves their prey exhausted and allows them to secure a lethal bite on the nape of their neck.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in harsh deserts, its scales radiating enough heat to set twigs alight. It struggles to keep itself camouflaged during the cold, desert night since its heat signature gives it away.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's movements become unnoticeable when it rolls beneath the surface of the sand dunes where it resides. When digging underground, it shatters hard rocks with its jaw to reveal any bug prey hiding within.
author: soup1900

entry: Wild and bold, POKENAME may be found in marshes or deserts, albeit rarely. Whether in water, sand, or treetops, it shows incredible agility.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Since POKENAME has the ability to roll, it can get to locations where prey has collapsed quickly and eat the body while it's still fresh. Its hide has become very coarse due to it always being submerged in the sand when roaming.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are usually quite shy and would rather run away than interact with other people or Pokémon. When cornered, POKENAME shouts loudly and snaps its jaws at anything that gets too close.
author: itsthenewisaiah

entry: POKENAME live in burrows underground with their nest mates to cooperate and gather food together. They often nibble on the ears of older members of the nest to beg for food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Desert nations once worshipped POKENAME as a god of shifting sands. Glass effigies were crafted in its image to bring wealth and fortune.
author: .izik

entry: The membrane on POKENAME's eyes helps protect them from both the heat and dust. They use their claws to scale trees in search of nuts, using their jaws to crack them open.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's eyes are well protected from dust and dirt, allowing them to dig through the ground without worry. They do so to maneuver around opponents, popping up beneath them with their powerful jaws.
author: santon5512

entry: It lies just below the surface of the desert to slice at the legs of passersby. When victims get away, POKENAME aggressively pursues them.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The cast iron blades on POKENAME's limbs heat up rapidly under the desert sun. It uses these superheated weapons to slash through tough prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travels in congregations across vast deserts, resting beneath the surface while sleeping. At night they peek their feelers above the sand and wiggle them, leading many to say the congregation resembles a kelp bed on the desert floor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs along riversides searching for discarded sticks to build dams. If none are found, it can fell a tree in under a minute.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleep for weeks on end, content to remain comfortable in out-of-the-way places where they won't be disturbed. They are grumpy when roused and will lazily lash out at whoever woke them, though their attacks are easy to avoid.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME aggressively chase after interlopers in their territory, using their sharp teeth and claws to attack anyone that gets too close. Their aggression makes them popular with villainous Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Burying itself in the desert sands, POKENAME hunts by hiding underground with only its mouth exposed. Able to unhinge its jaw and lay it flat, it waits for prey small enough to swallow and snaps its mouth shut when it's underneath them.
author: evilgammon

entry: This form of POKENAME was specifically bred as a pet. It will nibble its owner affectionately if they share a close bond.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: At dawn, POKENAME vibrates its wings to etch patterns into desert sand. It marks each piece by stamping its snout at the base.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rolls sideways through desert sands as it travels, its rotund body picking up momentum. Its skin grows harder with each rotation.
author: .izik

entry: By day, POKENAME buries itself in the desert sand to avoid the sun. At night, its bud emits a Lum Berry scent to lure prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their back spines to break through the sand, making their movements through the desert more fluid and rapid than unfused Sandile. The increased speed is counterbalanced by their increased visibility, making them easier to spot.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME linger at the edges of deserts in small gangs as they look for Pokémon and Trainers leaving the sands. They will try to gang up on these tired travellers, seeing them as easy pickings.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Ancient mining texts record POKENAME crushing ore with its powerful jaws. It was paid in fruit and dried vegetables for its service.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has enjoyed recent popularity on the internet for its gormless smile and remarkably flat shape. Every Friday, enthusiasts search deserts hoping to take its picture, but its tabular form allows it to be buried and hidden by the blowing sands.
author: .realthree

entry: Scientists believe that POKENAME have changed very little from prehistoric times, as their mummies have been found in many deserts, untouched by moisture and time. Their favorite snacks are small rodent Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During icy desert nights, POKENAME shivers violently to stay warm. The friction from its scales creates faint sparks that glow in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gathers windblown or buried trash in the desert. Its bag-like skin traps heat to help it survive frigid desert nights.
author: .izik

entry: To deter predators, POKENAME hides under the sand with its sharp thorns sticking out. If it is stepped on, it will leave the victim with a painful bite.
author: mistymagius

entry: Using its thorn-covered body, POKENAME detects subtle vibrations in the sand. It can burrow at 30 mph to chase prey underground.
author: .izik

entry: Dark particles are released from its wings like a veil. This helps conceal POKENAME while it hunts in the desert at night.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME will congregate around areas where meteors will enter the atmosphere, looking to eat any bits that burn up. Scientists use this behavior to predict the paths of meteors.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is very sensitive to light, so it keeps itself buried underground until the sun sets, its eyes are protected by a thin film that keeps debris out of its eyes while digging.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses Scary Face to intimidate travelers into giving it coins. These are dragged back to its desert den and hoarded like treasure.
author: .izik

entry: One of POKENAME's favorite habits is to snatch something of its Trainer's and play tug-of-war with it. Due to its strong jaw strength, these sessions can last for a while before it'll give up the stolen object.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the sand save for its tail, which dangles a false fruit to lure others close. Once a hapless hungry creature takes the bait, it rises up and clamps its jaws shut around its foolish quarry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats through the desert at night. During the day, it lies flat on the sand to absorb sunlight and recharge its electrical core.
author: .izik

entry: Their bodies have a similar composition to various gelatins, so flavorless, odorless jellies are highly nutritious to them. They typically subsist on old bones, which take longer and more energy to digest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hate sunlight and will stay out of the sun at all costs. It gets its nutrients from rotting plant-matter using its poisonous vines.
author: mistymagius

entry: They detect prey through echolocation and jump from trees to suck the blood out of the passerby. POKENAME's light weight allow them to escape notice.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME emits ultrasonic waves to navigate caves and blasts to shock prey. It can emit a blast strong enough to knock out power as well as itself.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME emit sonic blasts powerful enough to shatter glass and cause temporary deafness. They are a particular danger for inexperienced Pokémon Trainers, and caution is advised while battling them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME emit sonic blasts powerful enough to shatter glass and cause temporary deafness. They flap their wings against the ground to push their way toward their opponents, getting close to deliver their sonic bursts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME emit sonic blasts powerful enough to shatter glass and cause temporary deafness. They flap their wings against the ground to push their way toward their opponents, getting close to deliver their sonic bursts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME roll around caves to generate electricity, and their wings help them swerve around obstacles. If they experience a sudden stop, they are likely to explode.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wears the skulls of the prey it has sucked all the blood from. Since it is blind, it just dives in the direction of prey it hears.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Because of its blindness, all of its other senses are enhanced. It stalks during the night, attacking any criminal it finds with brutal amounts of force.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses its keen sense of hearing and quick reflexes to allow it to effortlessly dodge its opponents' blows. It prefers to fight fair and not use its venomous bite.
author: mistymagius

entry: With the help of its long tongue and sensitive ears, the otherwise blind POKENAME can accurately scan its surroundings.
author: chorb33

entry: Because of its blindness, all of its other senses are enhanced. It stalks during the night, attacking any criminal it finds with brutal amounts of force.
author: mistymagius

entry: An abandoned military experiment, POKENAME uses echolocation to seek out targets and detonate upon contact. Due to their expendable and destructive nature they are popular among evil organizations.
author: kianjp2008

entry: They detect prey through echolocation and jump from trees to suck the blood out of the passerby. POKENAME's light weight allows them to escape notice.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME bite at anything that comes close, using their sharp teeth to try and leech the energy from curious passers-by. They store as much of this energy as they can to try to hasten the evolution process.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME expel virulent gas that is full of infectious particles and make other Pokémon incredibly sick. Their colonies share new diseases that they encounter, making members of their colony incredibly resilient to many types of illness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses ultrasonic waves to sense prey before charging. Due to its limited intellect, it often runs right past its target and into a cavern wall instead.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts by using the nutritious eggs in their mouth to lure in egg-stealing Pokémon like Sneasel. When a Pokémon reaches in, POKENAME bites down and injects the would-be thief with a paralyzing venom.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME wraps its prey with its bundle of vines before draining them of their fluids. They can be seen hanging from trees while they sleep during the day.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME bite at anything that comes close, using their sharp teeth to try and leech the energy from curious passers-by. When they feel endangered, they wrap their wings tightly around themselves and rely on their tough skin to protect them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flutters around flower gardens at night, nibbling away at those yet to bloom. It has a gentle disposition, obediently leaving gardens alone if shooed away by their owners.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME creates invisible walls around its habitat. Prey often slam into the walls, which makes it easy for POKENAME to echolocate to them.
author: kiwikelly

entry: The noises of its screeching sound like mocking laughter. POKENAME move in packs, hunting beneath sunlight without fear.
author: hortensia_xxiii

entry: Even though it is blind, POKENAME can sense where other Pokémon are thanks to the vibrations picked up by its many wings. It wields a pair of extremely sharp scythes, whose edges are coated with a toxin capable of poisoning anyone they cut.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are blind and unable to maintain their appearance without the help of other Pokémon. They reward those who help them maintain their dress with kisses, which release a secretion that creates fond feelings for POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its ears have adapted, due to its lack of eyesight, to act as a set of mandibles to capture prey.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME is completely blind, so it is constantly running into things. Its horns contain a potent toxin that causes hyper aggression and momentary blindness.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are incredibly abundant in underground lakes and rivers. They are incredibly sensitive to light, so they will mostly hide in dark crevasses or between rocks.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sucks on its victims and gradually drains their blood. They are hardy and live mainly in dark and damp places.
author: chorb33

entry: Some say there are 1,400 different subspecies of Zubat, and all of them can be copied by a POKENAME. Each of the many different markings they can have represent the sheer diversity of the wild population. However, they cannot copy the color green.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Incredible hearing allows POKENAME to stay away from even the most stealthy of predators. The venom it produces is unique to the individual, making bites difficult to treat without modern medicine.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Incredible hearing allows POKENAME to stay away from even the most stealthy of predators. The venom it produces is unique to the individual, making bites difficult to treat without modern medicine.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Incredible hearing allows POKENAME to stay away from even the most stealthy of predators. The venom it produces is unique to the individual, making bites difficult to treat without modern medicine.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flies erratically through seacaves as night approaches. Should it collide with a ceiling or wall, its thick shell absorbs the impact with ease.
author: .izik

entry: It hangs upside down from trees or cavern ceilings while waiting for its body to finish evolution. It hastens the process by consuming any small creatures that fly too close to its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: Thought extinct, POKENAME were only rediscovered recently deep underground. Completely blind, they use their acute hearing to navigate the darkness. Their wings are not used for flight, instead acting as flippers for swimming.
author: ghostslythe

entry: This Pokémon has been observed sucking the blood from its prey using the giant maw located on its stomach. However, POKENAME will often swallow its prey whole to save time.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME emits a short cry in order to use echolocation to hunt. It can perfectly mimic the cries of other Pokémon, confusing prey as they have no idea which species they are truly being pursued by.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins the leaf on its head like a propeller, allowing it to hover in place momentarily. As it flies, it emits a pleasant oregano-like scent that lingers in the air.
author: .izik

entry: It spins the leaf upon its head to spread the aroma of the tree shoots around its neck. This aroma is oddly soothing, though the tree shoots themselves are very bitter.
author: infinex21

entry: Even though it has visible wings, they are almost useless and can barely make it glide since they are unable to support its weight.
author: mercury_sc

entry: Since POKENAME is blind, it bites anything within reach to understand what it is dealing with. As its skin is prone to drying out quickly, it makes its home along waterways where it can swim.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The time of day POKENAME is most active depends on the season. It is very flighty, however, and will typically flee upon hearing any loud noise, regardless of what time of year it is.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It navigates using echolocation by making clock-like ticking noises. This is because despite its large eyes, it is completely blind.
author: admiralvermin

entry: POKENAME only comes out at night, tracking its prey with its keen sense of hearing. Its fangs and talons contain a deadly poison that it uses to incapacitate its prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: Being blind, POKENAME hunts through several thin strings of webbing lined across caverns and held by its many legs. The moment it feels prey brush against a thread, it reels them in and quickly webs them up completely.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is entirely blind, so it has a difficult time sustaining itself as it matures, as it will require more and more energy as it grows. Therefore, the longest living POKENAME are those owned by Trainers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its glowing bulbs emit a low humming noise which seems to serve as a means of echolocation. Its fangs can deliver electric jolts that are generated by, and stored within, its bulbs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME produce sparks of electricity whenever they bite their prey. By giving them a Persim Berry, they gain the ability to resist a Zubat's Confuse Ray, which keeps them level-headed whenever they fight over food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite being blind, POKENAME can innately sense the presence of moonlight. They congregate in caves where moonlight seeps through the cracks, dancing together with curious, wistful cries.
author: sk372

entry: Lacking both eyes and ears, POKENAME often have a hard time navigating and aren't great battlers. However, they're quite cheerful by nature, despite their struggles.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME lets out a shrill cry for echolocation. This cry also has the added effect of drawing out the parental instincts of nearby Pokémon, warding off many of POKENAME's natural predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It waddles around blindly in search of something to bite. It seems like hunting behavior, but POKENAME's fangs contain a substance that induces mild euphoria in those bitten; it wishes to share this joy with others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's beak possesses an unusual psychic sensitivity, allowing it to detect prey up to 10 minutes before they arrive. It is most active at night, using this ability to ambush unsuspecting targets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lounges on the beach, absorbing moonlight to gain energy. If it attempts photosynthesis, its flowers will quickly wilt.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Using its echolocation, it can find fruit within miles of its location. When resting, POKENAME will cling to the shoulder of its trusted Trainer.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME builds up its poison reserve by eating the seeds of the fruit it survives on. They are only known to use this poison as a last resort against potential threats to it or its Trainer.
author: melodydelune

entry: The long stamens protruding from the bat flower on POKENAME's head act as whiskers to help it feel its way through the dark. Its oversized jaw leaves little room for its brain.
author: .realthree

entry: Deserted cities can be home to thousands of POKENAME, feeding off any rotten matter they can find. Their sharp teeth are able to chew through metal wire.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is completely blind and relies on echolocation and heat to maneuver through its environment. Whenever it goes to sleep, it wraps around a stalactite with vines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: An eyeless hunter, POKENAME flaps its wings and feels the air bouncing off cave walls in order to navigate.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Establishing colonies near groundwater, POKENAME can navigate their underground, labyrinthian homes using echolocation emitted from their mouths.
author: char_latte3412

entry: While POKENAME retains its echolocation abilities, it rarely uses them. It appears content to explore its surroundings by simply bumping into objects.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Although the nocturnal POKENAME is naturally blind and relies on echolocation to see the area around them, studies have shown it has a connection with the moon, and can perfectly sense anyone nearby if moonlight is touching them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although the nocturnal POKENAME is naturally blind and relies on echolocation to see the area around them, studies have shown it has a connection with the moon, and can perfectly sense anyone nearby if moonlight is touching them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although the nocturnal POKENAME is naturally blind and relies on echolocation to see the area around them, studies have shown it has a connection with the moon, and can perfectly sense anyone nearby if moonlight is touching them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Large flocks of POKENAME appear around people near their end. Once they perish, the flock will feed on their lifeless body until nothing remains.
author: mistymagius

entry: They use echolocation to navigate, though they can also track other sounds thanks to their large ears. They primarily feed on poisonous plants and mushrooms, which seem to affect the vibrancy of their purple spots.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has extremely strong jaws, capable of pulverizing a steel beam. They are commonly found in disease-ridden areas like sewers and alleyways.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though POKENAME is completely blind, it can use echolocation to see. The gems along it resonate with the echoing cries to aid in tracking prey more precisely.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME are a common pest found in caves. Their psychic powers allow them to detect food even in perfect darkness, and their flat bodies and sharp fangs make them difficult to remove once they've latched on.
author: footlongdingledong

entry: POKENAME lives in caves and hunts by blindly flailing its body in the direction of prey. It avoids other predators unless they strike its tail first.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME hangs from large trees, disguising itself as a pinecone. Its thick fur contains hundreds of poisonous needles that break off on physical contact.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses its tail to dig into the walls and ceilings of caves it inhabits. Once it senses potential prey moving in front of its hiding place, it launches out of the hole to sink its fangs into a new victim.
author: sk372

entry: It hangs dormant by its claws on the ceilings of deep caves, slowly letting the venom produced in its body gather in its stinger. Many spelunkers bear the scars left by sudden POKENAME attacks.
author: kianjp2008

entry: Despite its horrifying appearance, POKENAME only eats bacteria filtered from the soil. It uses its titanic fangs to carve through rocks as it burrows.
author: ansleehariot

entry: POKENAME are considered pests in urban areas due to their habit of eating leftover food scraps along the streets. Being bitten by a POKENAME can cause symptoms similar to food poisoning.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME use the reverberations of their wings to sense their surroundings, flying through dense forests at night.  These Pokémon love to eat honey and nectar, often consuming entire honeycombs.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's claws are laced with a strong poison that incapacitates its victims. It hunts at night, gliding from high places to ambush its prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are always on the hunt for any fruits it can get its paws on. It actually prefers poisonous fruits as they will store the toxins in its teeth for a venomous bite.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME 's mouth eventually covered it's whole body, as it didn't need eyes. It can gobble up over 300 Berries in one sitting.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME sticks itself to cave ceilings and waits for something small to wander beneath it, tracking movements via echolocation. It then drops down to land on and smother its prey with its boiling-hot body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have small, vestigial wings that are too small to allow them to fly. Instead, older members of the colony bite these wings to signal affection, feeding them fruits and berries to keep their bodies rotund and plump.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its thick round body is lighter than it looks, so it can fly quickly with no troubles. Even small amounts of sunlight will make it ill, so it lives in the deepest and darkest cavern locations.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lurk around caves and tunnels where they like to steal Repels from wandering Trainers. If the Trainers don't have any, POKENAME bite them.
author: pankiwi
