entry: POKENAME is extremely loyal and is said to guard the graves of their trainers after they pass. This has led to a number of graveyard attendants being attacked by POKENAME because they were mistaken for grave robbers.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME uses the flame on the tip of its tail to lure out strong opponents. POKENAME changes the face on its belly to memorialize an opponent it has deemed worthy.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME uses the mask it carries with its tail as a paddle to swim faster in the water. The spirals on its stomach will change direction based on whether the eyes on the mask are open or closed.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME does not like its face being seen, so it will teleport to a dark place and use its mask to disguise itself as a human or Pokémon that has recently died.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic abilities to read the minds of those who approach it and uses its mask to disguise itself as someone dear to that person. It is unknown if POKENAME does this maliciously.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME shows grieving people projections of the recently deceased using its two floating masks. POKENAME is responsible for a number of ghost sightings throughout the region.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME are said to be the spirits of some of the greatest fighters in history, lingering within a strange mask artifact. Striking the mask to make it ring summons POKENAME, ready to return to the glory of battle once more.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often takes root in barren places. The gold head POKENAME carries is used to store water, while the mask is used to clear obstructions to make planting its roots easier.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME are rather forgetful, wandering around as if completely unaware of their surroundings. However, if the eyes on the back of their shells spot something important, they will glow bright red as the POKENAME suddenly focuses.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The mask in POKENAME's mouth keeps whatever it swallows from escaping. The mask resembles the face of the last thing POKENAME has swallowed.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME hides itself on the sea floor, only leaving the two masks on its head exposed. When POKENAME senses potential prey, it will spew poison from its masks into the surrounding area to paralyze its target.
author: drcew

entry: This Yamask has attached itself to a Geodude, and is halfway through the process of melding with it.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME is sometimes seen at night galloping through graveyards. The mask on POKENAME's side resembles one of its parents.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME has been spotted dashing through graveyards at night. POKENAME seems to be looking for something or someone.
author: drcew

entry: Ghostly wails echo out from inside POKENAME's shell while POKENAME sleeps. Any attempts to find the source of the odd sounds will cause the eyes on the shell to glow bright red as the wails turn to shrieks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME appears to be an ancient form of a battery case with its own magnetic field, powered by a spirit trapped within.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Found within ancient ruins, these Pokémon feed on the emotions of those who step upon their amorphous form. They need little to sustain themselves, but if one tries to take their golden mask, they will siphon all they can.
author: infinex21

entry: The cannons on a POKENAME's back move independently to lock onto a target from any direction. While POKENAME often spend their time looking out into the distance, they're eerily focused on whatever their cannons lock onto.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's body mimics an ancient mask, but its hidden eyes can suddenly open. Those who see them are said to suffer a terrible Curse.
author: .izik

entry: A long massive serpent made of hundreds of drowned souls, wild POKENAME travel the vast ocean in search of more victims to add to its mass.
author: lyman

entry: A long massive serpent made of hundreds of drowned souls, wild POKENAME travel the vast ocean in search of more victims to add to its mass.
author: oxitape.

entry: A restless spirit, POKENAME puts to sleep and enters the mind of its victims to remember what it was like to dream.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The face on POKENAME's pendulums will resemble a deceased person the viewer knew. POKENAME will then feed on the memories the viewer shared with the deceased until the deceased is completely forgotten by the viewer.
author: drcew

entry: Wild POKENAME use the static electricity in its fur to ward of predators. This electricity eventually becomes potent enough to trigger an evolution.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME's skull is composed of tightly layered silk. If damaged, it rapidly spins more silk to patch the breach.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered in small spines that conduct electricity. Any Trainers or Pokémon curious enough to get close are scared off with a Thunder Shock.
author: chibitales

entry: The bundle of tangling vines conceals POKENAME's body as protection. It coats these vines in a sticky, conductive webbing, allowing it to catch prey with them and discharge Electric-type attacks easily.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lacks strong poison, instead using the stinger on its tail to deliver a potent jolt to any would-be attackers. It takes some time to recover its electric power after a single sting, however.
author: sk372

entry: When frightened, packs of POKENAME will take off with a crack of lightning, often leaving small deposits of fulgurite in their wake. Gem collectors and jewelry makers will scare groups of POKENAME on purpose to collect the valuable glass.
author: vic1312

entry: Extremely tiny, it's difficult to see POKENAME when it invades a person's computer. Fortunately, the amount of data it consumes is minimal, so it is rather harmless.
author: sk372

entry: Commonly sighted after harsh floods, these Pokémon will latch onto wet wires and suck on the conductive copper. They do not gain any nutrition from doing this; it is done because they enjoy getting their tongue shocked.
author: teatedtiten

entry: Tapping the tips of POKENAME's scythes together creates sparks and small bursts of electricity. It uses this ability to try and intimidate larger Pokémon that come across it while it hunts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME commonly build their hives within breakers or generators, feeding off the electricity. They use this energy to produce a special honey, which is commonly added to energy drinks due to its energizing properties.
author: santon5512

entry: These fuzzy Pokémon are so soft and warm that many Trainers and their children will cuddle with them when they sleep. Amusingly, they also produce a gentle amount of static electricity that results in very chaotic bedhead the next morning.
author: infinex21

entry: These timid Pokémon can curl up into a ball crackling with electricity and propelling themselves with flames. Although they typically do so in order to flee from their foes, there are plenty who will ram their foes like fireballs.
author: infinex21

entry: The jagged fur covering a POKENAME's entire body is constantly crackling with static electricity. This fur is also incredibly warm and treasured by a good number of collectors.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a very clingy little Pokémon. It grabs onto others in order to nip them and siphon static electricity with its fangs for sustenance, but it immensely enjoys the hugs as well, so prying all four of its arms off can require effort.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases static electricity from its feet to jolt and stun small insects and other creatures to eat. Its chirps have a distinctly static-like tone to them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME create a special webbing that helps them carry the many Berries they forage. They avoid picking up Rabuta Berries because of their bitterness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs electricity from other beings via bites. If it overindulges, it releases the stored excess energy in small electric bursts every five minutes on the dot.
author: sk372

entry: In modern times, POKENAME latch onto airplanes to aid their migration across regions. If an urban area becomes infested with them, Rock-type Pokémon specialists are called in to help drive them off.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME flies into thunderclouds for fun, basking in lightning. It nests near spots where bolts have struck to absorb their energy.
author: .izik

entry: Roosting atop electrical poles near homes, POKENAME is said to glimpse the pasts of those who live nearby, though no one knows how.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME does not have an organ to produce its own electricity, but its coat produces sufficient static for weak electric attacks.
author: hophoppip

entry: It is easy to raise because it enjoys eating bland or sour food that other Pokémon leave behind. A Salad Mix left behind during meals is what it enjoys the most.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME float using ambient static charge, preferring to travel to areas with high electrical potential. They generate static as they fly and will end up clumping together as they fly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME feed on electrical currents and naturally gravitate to regions with a high frequency of thunderstorms. They have become a pest in modern times as they will bite into and feed on power lines, sometimes even causing blackouts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: An uncommon pest Pokémon in urban areas that build typically harmless but electrically-charged webs near homes. If discovered, it will flee elsewhere for safety until it is exhausted.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME collects bits of citrus peels with its long tail, rubbing them on its fur to deter predators. The zesty lemon scent lingers, masking its natural electrical charge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wraps its petals in its electrically charged silk, paralyzing any Bug Pokémon on contact. It climbs up the tallest structure it can find so it can absorb the most possible sunlight.
author: mistymagius

entry: Before shocking its foe, POKENAME drenches them in mud to maximize conductivity. It often plays in puddles while waiting to counter an attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an uncommon pest in urban areas, building typically harmless but electrically-charged webs near homes. If discovered, it will flee elsewhere for safety until it is exhausted.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME gnaws through buildings' wiring to drain power. Office workers often blame flickering lights on faulty circuits, unaware of its presence.
author: .izik

entry: A prankster with mild electric abilities, POKENAME will swing its fuzzy hair like tendrils and smack others, discharging enough voltage to give them lingering tingling discomfort. It then giggles at their mild inconvenience and floats away.
author: sk372

entry: It feeds on static electricity, but is fearful of painful repercussions from larger prey. Because of this, it clings to children to take theirs, ironically earning the ire of their parents.
author: sk372

entry: These tiny Pokémon often use their slimy bodies to cling to other Pokémon in order to get around. They carry a ball of silk webbing atop their backs, which is filled with crushed up nuts to feed on during their journeys.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can sniff out static within clothing and household objects. They store gathered static in their web bag to snack on later.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME can store exactly one byte of information in their body. Colonies of POKENAME take data from a floppy disk and remove it byte by byte until nothing remains on the disk.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Known to feed on energy from low-usage devices, colonies of POKENAME have been found infesting calculators. This can result in incorrect calculations, whether this is mischief on the part of POKENAME or an error caused by their feeding is unknown.
author: darkwolfe

entry: The sticky webbing between POKENAME's antlers is used to catch a bevy of small insects. POKENAME itself doesn't eat them but offers them to other Pokémon in exchange for being able to suck static electricity from them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME graze in packs, rubbing against each other to charge electricity. If something touches it, it will expel all the stored electricity to paralyze its target and run away.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME are drawn to electrical currents and can be found coiling around the base of generators and electrical pylons. Engineers are advised to account for their presence, making sure no wires are exposed to prevent POKENAME from biting them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to large Grass-type Pokémon like Venusaur for protection. These hosts don't mind, as POKENAME tends to the plants growing on their bodies in return.
author: mepp.

entry: The electrical current running through POKENAME's tail can be harmful to other Pokémon if touched, and therefore acts as a defensive mechanism. The actual tail, full of nutrients, has weak magnetic properties.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lazily spins webs to rest in and hope that food gets caught before it wakes, abandoning the web if this tactic fails. People leave spare food in its webs to keep it from causing a mess by creating too many additional ones.
author: sk372

entry: It feeds off the cheerful thoughts of Pokémon in its vicinity. It can spot potential danger from a mile away with its compound eyes.
author: thenezhar

entry: POKENAME spins silky threads from its hands as it dances, forming webs in elegant motion. Artistically-inclined Trainers enjoy comparing the web patterns made by their POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME attach themselves to small seeds and use static electricity to attract fluff and fur to the seeds, catching the breeze and floating on their makeshift platforms. If left undisturbed, the charge builds up to a dangerous degree.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME attach themselves to small seeds and use static electricity to attract fluff and fur to the seeds, catching the breeze and floating on their makeshift platforms. If left undisturbed, the charge builds up to a dangerous degree.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are docile Pokémon with a leg-like horn atop their heads, which is clad in fur that is charged with static electricity. They often weave their electric threads into playful shapes using their four small limbs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME emits precise electrical pulses that interfere with neural signals. Prolonged exposure can manipulate victims into thinking it is a deity through altered perception.
author: .izik

entry: With a slow pace, POKENAME navigates the forest floor. Its small size belies its ability to generate potent electrical currents.
author: anarchaz

entry: It attacks small prey with its horn, sapping their energy with a special poison it secretes. It then stores the energy in its body to convert into electricity for defense.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME consumes the bioelectricity of victims it stabs to power up its attacks. It gains the most energy from large, Electric-type Pokémon.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME consumes the bioelectricity of victims it stabs to power up its attacks. It gains the most energy from large, Electric-type Pokémon.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Using their ribbon-like organs, POKENAME deliver precise electric shocks. They display an uncanny capability to deliver electric shocks where their opponents are weakest.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite their small size, POKENAME maintain a large territory that can be multiple miles in size. They challenge intruders with high-pitched roars, swinging at them with their tiny arms to scare them away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With their ability to generate their own electricity, POKENAME do not have to rely on absorbing static off of other Pokémon. POKENAME can be found surrounded by Joltik, feeding them the electricity they need.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is covered in soft fluffy fur that hums with stored energy. As it jumps across the ground, static builds up, causing its fur to crackle and spark.
author: rakunk

entry: Despite being capable of producing its own electricity, POKENAME often tries to latch onto other Pokémon to gather static, but it's not well-received.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to other Pokémon or humans to slowly drain their life energy. It is difficult to detach POKENAME from the prey once attached.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME protects itself behind a glass body, which it also uses as a dynamo to produce electricity. Thanks to this, it can control its threads like arms and even use them as legs to move around.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME often gather around power plants to consume the leftover electric waste. They don't seem to mind stealing edible garbage left by the plant workers either.
author: milchik

entry: This Pokémon generates an impressive amount of static electricity by rubbing its fluffy tails against one another. POKENAME cleans itself every day, since its charged fur attracts small particles and objects all the time.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME stays near tree roots, gathering nutrients from the soil while waiting for evolution. Should anything disturb it, it flaps its wings rapidly, creating showers of electric sparks around it.
author: sk372

entry: While napping beneath willow trees, POKENAME occasionally releases jolts of electricity. This deters curious Pokémon from approaching.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cluster together around electrical wires and appliances, feeding off the currents running through them. Their presence is destructive, but removing them can prove difficult, as they will sing people to sleep should they try to disturb them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME undergoes a lengthy hibernation process after obtaining the electric charge and minerals required for evolution. Some have even been found to eat and take the place of car batteries, going unnoticed until evolution.
author: mirkinator

entry: POKENAME continuously wraps itself in silk while clinging onto a power plant. This lets it absorb every last bit of electricity generated, as the weight and stickiness of the webs make it impossible for it to be moved.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME spins metallic silk that crackles with energy while still attached to its body. Once severed, the charge fades quickly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found spinning webs in areas populated by bugs. Its webs are very conductive, so it can send a shock through the string to burn prey.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME are capable of inhaling air to quadruple their size. They mainly utilize this talent to scare away predators, though they have a unique niche among clowns where they blow air into balloons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fold their specialized limbs into a form that resembles the bud of a flower. When their prey approach, POKENAME will use these limbs to grasp the target and subdue them with their poison.
author: alumed

entry: POKENAME can be found during thunderstorms, using its charged hairs to draw in lightning strikes. Do not try to grab its arms or it will shock you without warning.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rubs against people and other Pokémon to generate static electricity. If someone it dislikes tries to grab its strings, it expels all the static at once to give them a large shock.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME drains static electricity from others for sustenance. It stores some of the excess in the tips of its ears, giving its strikes an extra bit of electrical strength.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scatters spores around telephone poles. The mix of spores and static makes the area unsafe for flying Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: During thunderstorms, POKENAME floats high into the sky. Its fuzzy body crackles with static as it soars through the clouds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME aggressively flies at targets, aiming to feast on blood. The amount of blood it consumes to be full is so minuscule, people regard it as harmless aside from the slight pinch of its bite.
author: sk372

entry: Floating gently through ruins, POKENAME spins webs in strange patterns. The webbing is extremely sticky and is able to hold debris for months.
author: .izik

entry: After absorbing energy from a crystal from Chargestone Cave, POKENAME has grown to enormous sizes. It still carries around this crystal, though.
author: nellnast42

entry: This variant of POKENAME is extremely miniscule, making it difficult to study properly. It is thought to subsist on microscopic organisms. Despite its size, it is able to cause short-circuits in some devices.
author: chibitales

entry: Although smaller than normal Joltik, POKENAME's electrical output is near-doubled. It waits on the tips of grass blades for something to walk by, attaching to it and absorbing any built-up static electricity.
author: chibitales

entry: The Joltik enhances the symbiotic POKENAME's energy with its electricity. The POKENAME seeks out energy sources to absorb on its never-ending journey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME live in groups, usually guarding their caves filled with hundreds of large crystals. The most powerful POKENAME are the ones with the largest red gem on their chest.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME traps prey such as Cacnea in sticky silk before blasting them with fire. It often leaves behind scorched webs and charred husks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often found latched onto and draining electrical devices of their energy. It is considered a nuisance, especially in urban areas, so generators have been set up to act as feeding zones.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME injects venom into prey, then traps them with a charged Electro Web. It prefers to strike quickly and from above.
author: .izik

entry: While spinning at high speed, POKENAME builds static across its shell. It releases the charge with a sudden, buzzing pop.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grabs onto others with its claws, immobilizing them with paralytic venom and draining static electricity from them. Its poison is mild, and the amount it drains is still minuscule, so POKENAME is far less lethal than it appears.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are timid by nature, hiding within mobile nests which they make out of silk and snow.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME have grown too big for their nests, but since the outer layer has frozen solid, they've had to adapt to their accidental shells.
author: mx_wellman

entry: Exposure to a Dawn Stone had some strange effects on this Pokémon. It's believed it can float thanks to electromagnetism.
author: mx_wellman

entry: Timid by nature, POKENAME hides underground and hopes the weak electric charge in its leaves will dissuade others from bothering it. If plucked from the dirt regardless, it cries tiny sparks from its eyes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drifts aimlessly through graveyards, sparking with flickers of static. Its eerie flashes light up tombstones late at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to be a helpful light, guiding lost children through the forest. Some say it does this to ensure no one else suffers the same fate it once did.
author: cassimari

entry: POKENAME builds nests in cedar trees and absorbs nearby lightning during storms. Some believe it protects the forest this way.
author: .izik

entry: The flower bulbs on POKENAME's head store sunlight each morning. As it rests, the energy inside slowly builds into electrical charge.
author: .izik

entry: It builds up static electricity by brushing its wings against its furry body. It can unleash its built-up charge in a powerful Thunder Wave by directing the electrical discharge with its ears.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's wings crackle with static as it flies through storm clouds. Its cottony down can store lightning for hours.
author: .izik

entry: Legends claim that the first known POKENAME formed when a Joltik had attached itself to a Pikachu. The Pikachu used a thunderbolt to dislodge it, which caused it to hurtle into an unsuspecting Regice. To this day they seem to be wary of Pikachu.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The soft cotton in POKENAME's body rubs together, creating static. It stores the charge in its fur until needed in battle.
author: .izik

entry: Smaller Pokémon weave webs within POKENAME and use it as shelter. Its multitude of eyes are always aware of its surroundings, and watch over its inhabitants closely.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME creates small sparks of electricity consistently. This energy comes from the organs in its mouth, which look closely like rocks found in Unova.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME typically leech off of large machines or Electric-types, storing energy in the mushroom-like nodes. These nodes act like batteries, providing energy in times of need.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME generates static electricity in its fur when excited. Its playful nature makes it a beloved pet, but owners must be careful when petting it or they may get an unexpected shock.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Well-trained POKENAME are among the most loyal companions a Trainer can have. However, disobedient ones often ignore orders and steal electricity from outlets or household devices for their own amusement.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME swarms gather near wind turbines, feeding off the ambient charge. When spotted, they scatter in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through its fur, converting it into electricity. It shocks anything that wanders too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live together in small groups when they are young, sharing electricity sources amongst one another. As they grow older, they grow more independent. Rarely, they may even fight off their own family to protect their electric-laden territory.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is often seen clinging to larger Fire-type Pokémon like Volcarona, drawing on their heat for energy. It relies on this relationship for survival, as it is unable to easily generate fire on its own.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME is often seen clinging to larger Fire-type Pokémon like Volcarona, drawing on their heat for energy. It relies on this relationship for survival, as it is unable to easily generate fire on its own.
author: theartemis1

entry: The static in their fur lets POKENAME sense the presence of others nearby. Their agility and small size make them a challenging target to catch.
author: garret95

entry: POKENAME's fur reeks of rotting Pumpkin Berries. When threatened, it unleashes a powerful electric blast from its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hovers near light poles in city parks at night. It siphons off electricity, leaving the lamps to flicker mysteriously.
author: .izik

entry: The silk spun from POKENAME's body carries a light electric charge. Its fur smells strongly of Pumpkin Berries in autumn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fluffy body becomes more electrified and more sour in taste the more static electricity it absorbs. It constantly nibbles on others to drain them, so that the shock and flavor of its fuzz will repel predators.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME delivers powerful headbutts charged with electricity. It uses them to drive off anything that nears its den.
author: .izik

entry: It hoards shiny objects it finds, charging them with static electricity to keep thieves from stealing its collection. If it takes something from you, only careful negotiation will earn your item back without being shocked.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tendency to rub against its Trainer makes them constantly covered in silk. It dispenses silk from its prehensile tail, but its electric field causes it to constantly be covered in silk.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME fur carries a constant static charge, making their fur stand on end at all times. Their fur is very sensitive to air movements, making them difficult to catch off-guard.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME commonly live inside caves with an abundance of Electric-Type Pokémon. They wait inside their shell for one of them to approach before snapping their shell closed and feeding on their static electricity.
author: dualblades1147

entry: While swimming in a serpentine pattern through tropical waters, POKENAME periodically releases jolts of electricity into the surrounding water. This leaves ionized portions that communicate territory to others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: They inhabit freshwater environments and swim in schools. If an Electric-type Pokémon goes swimming in POKENAME's habitat, it will often emerge from the water covered in tiny energy-leeching POKENAME.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME feed on electrical cables and can often be seen feeding atop large pylons. Large populations of POKENAME can cause blackouts, often leading them to fly into a rage and start destroying the pylon they're feeding on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Before unleashing electricity, POKENAME digs its tiny roots into the ground. This helps it stay grounded and boosts its attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats quietly through city streets at night. It draws electricity from traffic lights and power boxes to stay energized.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME raises its stick toward the sky during lightning storms. Some say it draws in thunderbolts to store for later use.
author: .izik

entry: The webs that POKENAME creates are incredibly sticky and rather viscous. The layer of goop-like film around the threads helps conduct electricity, letting it more easily shock prey into submission.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME haunts households in order to steal its nourishment from the victims within. It feasts on static electricity, so it's harmless to the residents aside from faint static noises and one's hair standing on end at times.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME puts large swaths of targets to sleep so it can more easily take static electricity from their bodies to feast on. The victims being fed on often report dreaming of spiders, lightning, or some combination thereof.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME weaves strands of electrified silk into a glowing, sparking pendulum. This pendulum is useful for both lulling foes into hypnosis and delivering paralyzing shocks to those who don't fall into trances easily.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME fights foes by throwing seeds that leech vitality from its opponents and enduring attacks. POKENAME has a unique medicinal use where it sucks out toxic metals from sick people, absorbing and neutralizing the toxic materials.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their spikes to stick to cave walls, absorbing minerals. When attacked, they self-destruct, sending spikes flying in all directions.
author: santon5512

entry: When it rests, vines grow from one of its six egg-like portions, connecting to the others. These vines transfer nutrients between the segments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release a foul scent from their heads to ward off predators. If attacked, they will drop their heads onto the attacker, their spikes able to pierce even the toughest armor.
author: santon5512

entry: When two POKENAME meet, it is impossible to stop the two from engaging in combat. Their shells are highly resistant to blunt force, meaning their brawls often last weeks at a time.
author: gdottb

entry: POKENAME's metallic exoskeleton protects it from nearly any physical attack. It hides away in caves as it gathers energy to evolve.
author: mepp.

entry: When in danger, it curls up and extends the thorns around its body. During lightning storms, the thorn on its nose extends to absorb electricity from lightning strikes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seeks out small baby Pokémon in need of protection, usually Happiny. It uses its durable iron skin and pointy barbs to make sure no harm comes to their adopted kin.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Occasionally a Chansey who loses its egg stumbles upon a lonely Ferroseed and adopts it, forgoing producing more eggs. After a while the two form an inseparable bond and become POKENAME.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: If anyone approaches its young, it flings thousands of tiny needles from its tail. These projectiles create a painful and effective deterrent.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its sharp blades to cut moss off cave walls to eat. This simple diet sustains it in harsh underground environments.
author: .izik

entry: The more sap it consumes, the stronger POKENAME's metallic shell becomes. It uses sharp pincers to cut into trees and extract the liquid.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slips into garbage disposals, absorbing any debris it finds. If it goes two weeks without liquids, its body begins to harden.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its steel shell is lined with venomous spines, it relies on for protection, since it cannot move freely. If a Pokémon provokes it enough, POKENAME launches those spines outward in all directions like a volley of projectiles.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a ferocious predator that can crush even the hardest rock in its powerful jaws. When it spots prey, it launches the green spikes covering its body to mercilessly strike it down from above.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lay belly-down in nutrient-rich areas, absorbing said nutrients through their tough barbs. To defend themselves, they will use Body Slam attacks that skewer and crush their foes.
author: infinex21

entry: Its eyes can move independently, scanning its surroundings with ease. It can rotate a full 360 degrees on its metallic foot.
author: .izik

entry: It swings its tail like a maul, delivering devastating blows. With a single hit, it can topple a cedar tree effortlessly.
author: .izik

entry: When spotted while hiding in the forest, POKENAME swings its spiked metallic head like a maul to attack. It hides the head underground during rain to avoid rusting.
author: .izik

entry: Though it prefers to remain motionless at all times, POKENAME can defend itself by throwing the spiked orbs on its hands akin to shuriken. The thrown orbs grow back in a few hours.
author: sk372

entry: It defends its territory by swinging the spiked ball at the tip of its tail. To prevent its metallic body from rusting, POKENAME remains hidden deep within its tree during rainy days.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The thorns on its head extend into vines that pierce tree limbs, allowing it to reel itself up. It often sleeps peacefully nestled in the branches.
author: .izik

entry: Its goggle-like eyes glow gold as it accelerates in flight. In a straight line, it can reach speeds over 100 mph with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cling onto rocks at the mouth of caves in the foot of cliffs, eating seaweed that washes up at high tide. Their spikes contain a mild sedative, so some Trainers keep them to help them sleep.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: While flying, it divebombs anyone who approaches its nest. The helmet-like portion of its head is strong enough to smash boulders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a sharp crown that is covered with sharp thorns. These thorns dig into its skull, and the resulting pain enhances its psychic power.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have prickly metallic barbs that break off whenever they get lodged into another Pokémon. Once separated from their body, these barbs release venom that causes fevers and itchiness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The gems embedded in POKENAME's metallic body emit a strange, eerie power that lets it float. It lurks in abandoned factories, absorbing residual energy to sustain itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in moss-covered ruins of ancient civilizations, eating the growth that covers old wall paintings. They were theorized to have collected this special moss for witches to use in their brews.
author: reese1017600

entry: POKENAME will use its spikes to embed itself onto a tree, sapping nutrients from it. When in danger, POKENAME will self-destruct, which results in its spikes being flung out from its explosion, potentially hurting any nearby Pokémon or Trainers.
author: sharkboiowen

entry: POKENAME scatters dozens of thorns onto the ground from the skies to defend itself.  If it overworks itself, it will retreat to its nest and rest for a long period of time.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Once POKENAME has collected a berry, it uses spines to cling to a cave ceiling or high ledge to begin creating juice. Excess juice from the process may drip down on travelers passing beneath it.
author: sk372

entry: The green portion of its horn is covered in microscopic barbs. These barbs stick painfully into prey after it throws them with immense force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are pests living along roadways that absorb minerals essential to their diets directly through their slimy foot. POKENAME who consume asphalt have stronger shells due to the higher concentrations of minerals in the human-made material.
author: vic1312

entry: The seeds within POKENAME's tail create a rattling sound to ward off predators not deterred by its spikes. A healthy POKENAME sheds tail sections when they become too full of seeds, allowing the seeds to be used in herbal scented perfumes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The gold bands around its arms and torso help it focus its strength. With this enhancement, it can punch through solid steel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores briar seeds in an internal sac in its throat, from which it can fire them to stun a target, whether prey or threat. It primarily hunts animalistic Rock-types like Aron, but will settle for more ore-based ones like Geodude.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Approximately half of POKENAME's weight is in its tail. This lets POKENAME use its tail a powerful weapon. In a pinch POKENAME's tail can also be dropped allowing POKENAME to move significantly faster than normal.
author: mirkinator

entry: POKENAME likes to carry a seed around, hoping to find a nice spot to plant it. However, if it's not careful, its iron barbs sometimes skewer the seed it is trying to take care of.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Its iron-hard barbs protect it from most attacks, though it sometimes stores food on them. It rests in nutrient-rich areas and passively absorbs some of those nutrients as it sleeps.
author: infinex21

entry: The spiky leaves that grow from POKENAME backsides protect their tail bulb from attacks. If the bulb is damaged too gravely, POKENAME may be unable to evolve.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME are quite territorial. They use their spiky bodies and sharp tails to defend their home.
author: lemmymaster

entry: If startled, POKENAME's metallic body suddenly emits intense heat, making it dangerous to touch. It has been known to set dry grass ablaze in moments of panic.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their claws to dig through stone, absorbing the minerals that they find into their bodies. When threatened, they fire the rocky spikes on their backs at attackers before quickly fleeing.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can sense the emotions of people and Pokémon near them. They use this power to keep themselves safe. If they are caught with nowhere to hide against someone with hostile intent, they will curl up tightly and use their spikes defensively.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can sense the emotions of people and Pokémon near them. They use this power to keep themselves safe. If they are caught with nowhere to hide against someone with hostile intent, they will curl up tightly and use their spikes defensively.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can sense the emotions of people and Pokémon near them. They use this power to keep themselves safe. If they are caught with nowhere to hide against someone with hostile intent, they will curl up tightly and use their spikes defensively.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can sense the emotions of people and Pokémon near them. They use this power to keep themselves safe. If they are caught with nowhere to hide against someone with hostile intent, they will curl up tightly and use their spikes defensively.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their empathic powers to pinpoint the locations of their opponents during Pokémon battles. They fight by spinning in a pirouette, relying on their metallic skin to protect them from harm whilst their spines cut into their foes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their empathic powers to pinpoint the locations of their opponents during Pokémon battles. They fight by spinning in a pirouette, relying on their metallic skin to protect them from harm whilst their spines cut into their foes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drift into Pokémon battles in the certainty that their steel skin and empathic powers will enable them to avoid harm. When they sense a hostile attack, they flare up their armoured skirt, using the thorny metal to block.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drift into Pokémon battles in the certainty that their steel skin and empathic powers will enable them to avoid harm. When they sense a hostile attack, they flare up their armoured skirt, using the thorny metal to block.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drift into Pokémon battles in the certainty that their steel skin and empathic powers will enable them to avoid harm. When they sense a hostile attack, they flare up their armoured skirt, using the thorny metal to block.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its body is hollow and made of pure silver, covered in microscopic carvings. These markings appear to tell the story of its past life.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in harsh environments, typically found in arid deserts. They live in tight-knit groups and are highly territorial, their spiky and iron-rich hides letting them fend off rivals without much fear of reprisal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The tin-like material covering its body changes color to reflect its mood. It can mimic cool colors more effectively when calm and relaxed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME subdues its enemies using its thorn-covered whip, halting all means of escape. When threatened, it is able to release a barrage of iron spikes from its tail.
author: theartemis1

entry: This Pokémon has a strange diet of underground vegetation and transition metals. It chews through cavern walls, using the fine mesh-like scales on the underside of its jaw to strain out inedible stone and soil.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: It nests in spacious lairs underground and has developed a taste for crystals and gemstones. The color and luster of its rough, metallic coat are known to change depending on its dietary habits.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: The spikes on its back ooze a green toxin, making its attacks particularly dangerous. It somersaults before striking to rake its spines across its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires off spikes in addition to bludgeoning its victims. It excels against armored opponents and absorbs their metal.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The spike on its forehead rotates like a drill, piercing through even the hardest materials. It can effortlessly bore through slate during combat.
author: .izik

entry: They're drawn to Pokémon eggs, and will frequently linger or nest nearby to guard them until they've hatched. Even afterwards, a POKENAME may act as a long-term protector to the newborn.
author: banquoviaquo

entry: They're drawn to Pokémon eggs, and will frequently linger or nest nearby to guard them until they've hatched. Even afterwards, a POKENAME may act as a long-term protector to the newborn.
author: banquoviaquo

entry: A POKENAME fights viciously and underhandedly, but often refuses to endanger parents or children. For that reason, wild Kangaskhan seem to value their company, despite their prickliness.
author: banquoviaquo

entry: POKENAME deliver devastating, electrically-charged strikes with their mace-like tails to swiftly dispatch their foes. They are capable of seeing through most objects, so their foes and prey rarely ever manage to escape them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dig their claws into cave walls to absorb minerals within the rock and rely on hunting to acquire other nutrients. Due to their X-ray vision, they typically hunt at night to better catch prey unaware.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's metallic body lets it swim swiftly without rusting, even though it spends most of its life underwater. Its body is lined with sharp spikes that act as a deterrent, and with focus, it can fire them in every direction.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can retract the green spikes covering its steel body when its Trainer wants to pet it, so they don't get hurt. It has the habit of planting its tail into the ground to absorb the minerals it needs to stay strong.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are covered in vicious barbs that catch and cut deep into the bodies of whatever they strike. The spines and skin of POKENAME are rich in metallic compounds; they feed on iron-rich rocks to help maintain their armoured body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are covered in vicious barbs that catch and cut deep into the bodies of whatever they strike. The spines and skin of POKENAME are rich in metallic compounds; they feed on iron-rich rocks to help maintain their armoured body.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME attaches to cave walls to absorb minerals in the rock. On nights with a full moon, it detaches itself and crawls to an opening to gaze at the bright moonlight.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME's hair is made of roots that try to plant it in the ground. Because of this, POKENAME is distressed when it wakes up to find its head buried in the ground.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Its outer carapace is made of a thin but durable metal. While vulnerable to heat, it provides effective protection against physical attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is encased in thorny metal armor that covers its interior. Some folk tales suspect a vengeful spirit lies beneath the armor.
author: chorb33

entry: Its outer plating is a pyroxene alloy and its spines are mostly olivine. While these minerals are present on the planet's surface, they are more common on the basaltic plains of the moon.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Though it resembles a flame, the green portion on its head is the tip of a long vine. This vine extends to slap at opponents who get too close.
author: .izik

entry: Before a POKENAME can use Fire-type attacks, it has to heat its steel body to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. When not given enough time to warm up, a POKENAME may resort to simply bashing its spiked tail directly into its opponent.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Its body mysteriously generates mercury, which it spits out when frightened. This metallic defense is as perplexing as it is effective.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME protect their keys from robbers by charging them with their thorny bodies. Their favorite keys often come from abandoned garden shacks.
author: ayner

entry: The whisker-like protrusions are actually a pair of proboscis pointed enough to dig into solid stone. It clings to cave walls, digs into the rock and siphons minerals from within for its nutrition.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its powerful arms to knock ore loose from cavern walls. The ore it consumes helps fortify and strengthen its outer shell.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME primarily discharge electricity from their spikes, so they typically fight by throwing themselves at their foes and by swinging their tails. They can absorb nutrients and minerals from the ground via their claws.
author: infinex21

entry: In order to ensure its safety while it evolves, POKENAME evolved spikes as well as a durable shell around it. However, the extra defenses cause its evolution process to take longer than a normal Shelgon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very proud of the sharp spikes they bear as cogs. The exposed steel between the thorns shows evidence of large scratches.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a mysterious gel that hardens into jade spikes whenever anything comes close. Whenever they want a hug, they will telepathically communicate with their Trainer to ensure that the gel does not accidentally harden.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It floats gracefully above glades but drops with immense force if it senses a predator. The impact is strong enough to crack pavement.
author: .izik

entry: As a last resort, it latches onto an enemy and injects mercury with its jaws. This toxic act can be fatal if left untreated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts by wrapping its spiky tail tightly around its prey. It can be quite territorial and does not get along with others of the same species.
author: kittyluv090

entry: While resting, POKENAME grows tusk-like spikes all over its body to protect itself from predators. These spikes are incredibly sturdy, allowing it to survive in hostile environments.
author: .izik

entry: By day, POKENAME clamps onto cave stalactites with its metal jaws. At night, it releases and flies off to silently hunt in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME curls into a ball and rolls down hills to escape predators. Their brittle barbs snap off as they roll, leaving a sharp edge that oozes with venom.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lashes out at its enemies with its long, poisonous horns until they collapse to the ground, powerless. Running with its massive steel body, it creates terrifying metallic noises that cause all Pokémon in the area to flee.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lashes out at its enemies with its long, poisonous horns until they collapse to the ground, powerless. Running with its massive steel body, it creates terrifying metallic noises that cause all Pokémon in the area to flee.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's metallic jaws never release their prey once it's trapped between its sharp teeth. No one dares to hunt POKENAME, not even much larger Pokémon, because its body is too spiky and razor-sharp.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME covers itself with barbs as it hates being too close to other Pokémon. If you listen closely, you can hear soft humming coming from its mask.
author: hexx_vixtar

entry: POKENAME dig through caves for iron-rich nodules to feed on, incorporating the metal into their symbiotic mushroom. The mushroom has a metallic surface studded with chitinous thorns to help protect its host.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its spiky and robust body gives it adequate defenses, yet it still possesses a jumpy temperament. It leaves small pointed spikes behind as it flees, discouraging a hunter's continued pursuit.
author: sk372

entry: Its eyes blink brightly when searching for prey in the dark. It uses its thorns to pierce its catch before feeding.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's sturdy shell mimics steel shields on its arms during combat. Under the right conditions, it is strong enough to stop a freight train.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows into the ground in hopes of germinating the surrounding area with its spikes. Often, the soil it leaves behind is coarse and tough.
author: xephyr

entry: POKENAME live in highly turbulent waters where storms regularly blow through, sweeping up anything light enough. With their heavy iron bodies and sharp spikes, they can cluster together to keep from being washed away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The barbs on its body makes digging effortless, regardless of the hardness of the material. Each body absorbs minerals from the rocks they dig through, and the bodies communally distribute the nutrients amongst themselves.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are commonly found in mossy caves. Records from medieval times account militias launching POKENAME out of catapults. Luckily, their steel-like bodies prevented the Pokémon from serious harm.
author: mepp.

entry: It consumes silver ore scavenged from abandoned mines. A well-fed POKENAME gleams with a brilliant, metallic sheen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorbs minerals and nutrients by driving its tail into the ground and bouncing, just like an oil pump. The jagged peridot atop its head amplifies its psychic powers, but thanks to its iron-like skin, it feels no pain from the sharp edges.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME stick their spikes into cave walls and absorb the minerals they find in the rock. If they absorb too many minerals it can cause painful headaches.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME fuses peridot shards into its chlorophyll-rich body, absorbing minerals from cave walls to fuel psychic power. It clings to ceilings and dances in eerie calm, releasing psionic pulses that scramble enemies' thoughts.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME emits metallic ultrasounds from its nose to warn other Pokémon before they crash into its spiny body. It spends most of its time clinging to cave walls, only taking flight when it needs to move in search of food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It swims through streams, its thorns wiggling as water washes over them. In battle, it uses its sturdy head to slam into foes with force.
author: .izik

entry: It expertly scales mountains using its spiked fists. Knuckledusters inspired by POKENAME's hands are commonly found among criminal groups.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The thorns on the front of its heads mimic beaks and function like mouths. It uses them to grasp and consume food with surprising precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rely on their thorny shell to protect themselves from harm, being too slow moving to properly evade danger. If forced into a fight, they use their cannons to launch metallic thorns at their foes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are said to be the inspiration for countless medieval weapons, most famously the morningstar. Just like its hand-wielded counterparts, POKENAME use their club-like tails to fend off any and all foes they might encounter.
author: derhauptmann2k17

entry: POKENAME rely on their thorny shell to protect themselves from harm, being too slow moving to properly evade danger. If forced into a fight, they use their cannons to launch metallic thorns at their foes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The seed on POKENAME's back helps it grow by absorbing the sunlight. A litter of POKENAME often playfight with their paws and tusks.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME wield a mighty bone tusk that they rely on to defend themselves against other Pokémon. The sharpened end of their tusk slashes through their foes leaving behind deep cuts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its tusk-like tongue to pierce Apricorns and lick the juice inside. If it tastes something sour, it flails its tongue wildly in disgust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shakes trees with its strong arms to knock down prey like Caterpie. It strikes fallen targets with its tusks before consuming them.
author: .izik

entry: Because of its courage and constant drive for self-improvement, POKENAME is an outstanding partner for a beginning Trainer. It constantly rubs its tusks against rocks to make them sharper and more resilient.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It absorbs sunlight through its skin to gain energy. Its nose functions well on dry land and in water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME search for Haban Berries to protect themselves against other Dragon-type Pokémon. They have a strange ritual of crushing their scales after shedding them, which makes harvesting them difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its combination of tusks and razor-sharp teeth gives this Pokémon an intense bite force. It plays by nibbling, causing many injuries to Trainers.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME have olive-colored feathers that blend into trees around them. Whenever their prey rushes towards a burrow, POKENAME dig at the entrances with their small tusks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their hardened tusks and fists to crush berries. As they are sensitive to the cold, groups of the Pokémon can be seen traveling south before the winter season.
author: mepp.

entry: During warm months, POKENAME buries itself under the mud by rivers and slows its metabolism. It is active during the cold, winter months, and marks its territory by clearing away any snow or fallen leaves.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's cranial dome grows over time, as does its intelligence. It's very protective of the dome, and it's believed that were it to be chipped or ground down, its intelligence would diminish as a result.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its tusks to carve symbols into dirt and stone to communicate with others of its kind. Research is still ongoing to decipher the meanings behind each marking.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME defend themselves with their steel shells and their sharp tusks. When their tusks break, they will tightly shut their shells and wait for them to regrow.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's tusks fall off on an almost weekly basis, with new ones growing shortly. It likes to smear honey on them before they fall, so it can easily snack on it once it does.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME uses its tusks like knives to cut through food, the slices also cook the food to the perfect temperature. If its tusks break off, it melts them with its body to use the molten materials to grow new ones.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME sharpen their tusks on rocky outcroppings, keeping them ready to fight with. They are powerful for their size, capable of moving boulders and knocking over trees.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have small but sharp tusks that jut from their mouth. Too small to use effectively for combat, POKENAME use their tusks to root around for tubers and other underground meals.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their tusks to crush berries and eat them. They are known to be friendly and docile but are incredibly determined.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: In lieu of tusks, POKENAME has a really strong beak that gets harder the more damaged it gets. It also uses its claws in combat and to mark tree trunks.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: This Pokémon is rarely far from its nest, playing with its siblings by knocking their horns together in a test of strength. While POKENAME have little to physically protect themselves, their fireballs can leave opponents badly burned.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Outside of their home nests, sibling and rival POKENAME will challenge each other to tests of strength with different contests. These challenges can include speed kicking, fireball spitting, and berry crushing.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's claws are made of the same material as its tusks. Its kicks are strong enough to break a tree trunk in half.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: If POKENAME's tusk breaks off in battle, it blends into nearby foliage while it regrows. It consumes saplings to speed up the process.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love searching for rusty metal to gnaw on. It's believed doing so helps with its teeth.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: Despite its fierce nature, it loves to nibble on the ankles of its Trainer as a sign of affection.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: Despite their enormous size, POKENAME are rarely seen, instead preferring to remain in the deepest parts of the ocean. Their green scales glow ominously to attract prey, which they can bite through promptly with their tough-as-steel teeth.
author: be77yboop

entry: It uses the large horn on its head to carve markings into trees, denoting things such as areas with dangerous predators or particularly lush food stores. Should the horn snap off, a new one grows back in a week.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME marks its territory by etching its unique signature in trees. Its blade chips but grows back stronger.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's tusks are coated in a foul-smelling poison and can break concrete with a single strike. It trains at night to better protect its den.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tusks are brittle and take quite some time to grow back if broken. It uses its ribbons to shield them from harm, often keeping them wrapped up when not in use.
author: sk372

entry: It's said that its flame comes from the will of fallen dragons. When angered, its flame burns brighter, and distant roars can be heard from its bulb.
author: antomelon

entry: When ejected, POKENAME's innards sharpen in response to exposure to the air. It uses them as a hacking weapon in battle, but also to chop at low-hanging tree branches to make fruits and berries fall.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love being pet, but they sometimes get overwhelmed and will bite in retaliation.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: They mark their territory by leaving gashes in trees with their tusks. POKENAME have also been spotted sharpening parts of their tails on rocks.
author: elite01.

entry: When irritated, it snorts air through the holes in the stone helmet protecting its head and scrapes the ground with its front paws. POKENAME is extremely protective of its home and won't allow anyone to approach, not even others of its own species.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is known for its strong bite that can crush stone. Despite its intimidating appearance, it is a loyal companion to those who earn its trust.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME primarily attacks with the horn on its head, which is strong enough to pierce through the hardest metals.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME are very playful and docile; they often jump around other Pokémon for fun. Unfortunately, its sharp crest can accidentally hurt other Pokémon.
author: enzo200

entry: Its small tusks pick up vibrations and sonic waves with ease. It performs echolocation to find its way and to keep track of any of its foes.
author: infinex21

entry: The iron spikes on POKENAME's body often break off but regrow within hours. Ancient civilizations once melted these spikes into alloys for crafting durable shields.
author: .izik

entry: The fusion of two Axew causes an exaggeration of draconic characteristics in POKENAME, resulting in more pronounced tusks and more exaggerated spines. They use these features to intimidate larger Pokémon and are adept at avoiding confrontation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Powered by an ancient civilization's science, POKENAME's eyes burn red with the rage instilled by its creators.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME dispenses a thin, sticky webbing from its tusks to trap foes. Once restrained, it spits a corrosive poison to incapacitate them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tusks improve its traction as it rolls about. An old folk remedy says that the dust it kicks up can cure brittle fingernails.
author: .realthree

entry: This Pokémon flies in erratic patterns in order to confuse its prey. POKENAME will strike its foe the instant it believes the prey is dizzy.
author: .izik

entry: It will ram into trees with its hard wings to knock Apricorns loose. It will taste each Apricorn once so it can determine the order it wants to eat them in.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers to spend its time in maple trees, drinking the sap from the trunks. Due to its diet, the mucus that comes off of its body smells like syrup.
author: .izik

entry: Its harmonious song is especially beloved by Dragon-type Pokémon, who become docile in its presence no matter how enraged they were moments before. It is fond of Honey, which is both delicious and helps prevent sore throats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME strikes its scales to communicate with others of its kind. If a scale breaks off, a new one grows within eight hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME becomes excited when it sees unfamiliar light sources. In its excitement, it accidentally releases clouds of brown Stun Spore from its tusks.
author: .izik

entry: It digs vast networks of caves underground to impress a mate. These tunnels can spell trouble for a city's infrastructure and stability.
author: .izik

entry: The filling in POKENAME's tusks house a deep pink, edible filling. It is usually spread on toast as a jam with Axew tusk knives as a luxury, especially for anniversaries.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME burrow endlessly through the ground, creating vast networks of tunnels that provide shelter and strategic advantage.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME is a small but territorial Pokémon. In the dead of night, it will brutalize many things throughout its territory to give the impression to others that a large and powerful Pokémon lurks in the area.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite being genetically closer to Tentacool, POKENAME are known for sneaking into Haxorus herds in order to deter predators.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME's beaks frequently break off during feeding and regrow over time. When this happens, the other head eats enough food to sustain both of them until the beak returns.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has tusks on its hind fins as well as in its mouth. It uses its tail tusks to carve out chunks of ice, then uses its tail to fling these chunks at enemies.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME tends to chew unfamiliar objects with its tusks, which can get it into trouble. Thankfully, its tusks grow back quickly if they are damaged.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME will repeatedly punch rocks along the shore with their claws. These claws will often break off, growing back twice as strong.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME wield a special tusk like a sword and swing this weapon wildly whenever they face off in a Pokémon battle. They spend time outside of battles sharpening and polishing this hefty tusk.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's natural tusks are a supreme source of pride for it. They never regrow if they break off; if they do, POKENAME goes into a nigh-unstoppable rampage and recklessly attacks almost anything nearby, even foes that it has no chance of defeating.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It slams its tusks against stalagmites, delighting in the resonating echoes. The sound is said to carry deep into caves, startling other Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Sea captains warn of POKENAME as it is an atrocious beast with a violent temper. Its tusks can easily cleave through ship hulls, and many sailors have drowned because of them.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When POKENAME uses all its electricity, its genes destabilize again. This can lead to a mutation that results in multiple tusks growing.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's tusks grow throughout its life, coated in a tough layer to protect their sensitive surface. When nearing evolution, this coating becomes translucent and the tusks begin to glow softly, said to reflect the immense power building within.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its tusks are shed annually, prized by craftsmen for their unique properties. When ground into powder, they are used to create premium hair dyes.
author: .izik

entry: It can cut through most obstacles using its tusks in tandem with its Rapid Spin attacks. Even if its tusks break, they will regrow within a day's time and can still use its steel shell like a wrecking ball.
author: infinex21

entry: Using its clawed hands to climb trees, POKENAME are usually found gliding around the canopies in forests. Its hard tusks are used to deter foes.
author: nyandogegaming

entry: It slashes at foes with its claws and tusks in a flurry of strikes. Once weakened, it delivers a potent Poison Sting to immobilize them.
author: .izik

entry: It waits until Pokémon get close before striking, constricting and piercing them with pointed spikes. If any of its spikes happen to get chipped, it sharpens them with its tusks.
author: darxer_

entry: Its blade-like wings slash into cave walls, leaving deep carvings. These markings serve as a clear warning to trespassers in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: It raises its trunk high before unleashing a powerful Dragon Pulse. These attacks are strong enough to cause cave-ins if misdirected.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bury themselves in the ground while metamorphosing. It's nearly impossible to crack its shell. If in danger, it spins around with its long tusks.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME spars with its kind across frozen tundras. It begins with heavy tusk strikes, ending battles with a flurry of sharp, icy claws.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's adaptation to have its long tusks grow from its head instead of its jaw helps prevent it from accidentally opening its mouth to the cold air of its environment, keeping vital body heat safely inside.
author: .realthree

entry: It becomes furious if construction occurs nearby, viewing it as a threat. With its metal arms, it unleashes destructive blows capable of leveling concrete foundations.
author: .izik

entry: It sprints along cave walls and leaps off to cleave stalactites with its tusks. It pays no mind to where the falling debris lands.
author: .izik

entry: Its crest, tusks and back plates are composed of an extremely durable and hard metal. One can see where a POKENAME has been by the scratches it leaves along cave walls.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME's powerful tusks are actually large ingrown scales, which it uses to cleave through dense forests. Its thick hide is resistant to most forms of damage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's tusks are sharp enough to cut through steel. Its body is covered in a thick dark-colored iron.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their tusks to break open nuts and cut open fruits they grab and hold with their feelers. This keeps their tusks honed and provides them, and their friends and allies, with plenty of sustenance.
author: infinex21

entry: Its petals are incredibly sharp, and they can slice straight through thick tree branches with relative ease. In combat, POKENAME can throw its sharpened flowers as a deadly projectile.
author: mistymagius

entry: A group of POKENAME were discovered guarding an ancient Unovan catacomb. Mistaking explorers for grave robbers, they resisted for weeks before being calmed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's two heads hate each other and fight constantly. Owning a POKENAME whose heads cooperate is a mark of a skilled Dragon-type Trainer.
author: staghorn

entry: It scrapes its tusks along cave walls to knock loose gems. The broken shards are promptly consumed as part of its mineral-rich diet.
author: .izik

entry: Using its sharp tusks, it carves into ore deposits to consume the fragments. This process is believed to prepare its body for evolution.
author: .izik

entry: It tucks in its wings and dives at foes, using its heavy tusks as battering rams. The impact leaves deep gouges in the ground.
author: .izik

entry: When excited, its tusks drip a green, gooey substance. Though harmless, the goo emits a pungent oil-like odor that repels predators.
author: .izik

entry: It leaps nimbly off furniture or terrain, performing elaborate aerial maneuvers. Its combat style combines karate and sumo with ruthless efficiency.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME takes down prey by running alongside it and goring it with its long tusks. Some cultures believe that possessing a POKENAME tusk will grant you victory in battle.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its strong upper body strength to smash boulders. When this fails, it will use a horrendous Dragon Claw.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tusks were once ground up into a powder and boiled within its scaly shed skin. The resulting paste was used to relieve toothaches, making it a surprisingly helpful remedy in ancient times.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is known for a fierce and unyielding nature, earning it a place in the traditions of some cultures. Stone statues of this Pokémon are displayed during times of war.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME are vicious, using their tusks and horns to fight. The reasons they fight vary, from territory battles to contests to entertainment. For this reason, it is common to see POKENAME with many scars.
author: pix3l_655

entry: POKENAME is tasked with watching over its pack during times of rest. Its sharp tusks deter any threats from approaching their territory.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME is tasked with watching over its pack during times of rest. Its sharp tusks deter any threats from approaching their territory.
author: noel5229

entry: At night, POKENAME can be seen rolling across sandy deserts with ease. It often has arm-wrestling matches with Geodude.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME travel on strong desert winds with the help of Magnet Rise. Some theorize that many wild POKENAME are man-made, and were created long ago.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is thought to be a lost child of a lost underground civilization. Researchers follow it from afar in hopes it will lead them to its home.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a tough turquoise cocoon and are found deep within ancient tombs. People who make clothing have gone spelunking to obtain their high-quality silk.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its horn has the unique ability to sense others of its kind. This power grows stronger near ancient ruins, a phenomenon that puzzles scientists to this day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to have been created by ancient people from clay and clumps of stag beetles, with a currently unidentified energy source flowing through its body. Digging burrows to sleep, it still glows and ticks even beneath the earth.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME is paired with many archaeologists to help explore and catalog findings within ancient ruins. On occasion, data about ancient civilizations that was never observed finds its way into POKENAME's catalogues.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were revered as guardians of sacred temples in ancient times. They would stand near tablets inscribed with intricate riddles, awakening only to challenge travelers. Only the most intelligent could solve their puzzles and gain entry.
author: rakunk

entry: The pearl on its head glows brilliantly when near ancient artifacts. Archaeologists are puzzled by this phenomenon, as the connection between the pearl and these relics remains unknown.
author: .izik

entry: It's said that POKENAME were formed from clay many years ago. Its aromatic leaf smells of rich and loamy soil.
author: 22ndsolstice

entry: It still retains the great hopping capabilities of a Natu, despite being made of incredibly dense materials. POKENAME can stay incredibly still for long periods of time, appearing as nothing more than a simple stone idol until danger approaches.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME runs off an energy source of unknown origin. It uses its large tail as a conduit to steal power from small electronics, then stashes the broken items in tree branches high off the ground.
author: thelastmaleneko

entry: POKENAME gather in large numbers to lay their eggs in coastal caves with strange depictions on the walls. It is theorized that newborn POKENAME can interpret these symbols and head off on a voyage across the oceans, settling far away.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME was supposedly made many years ago. It guides lost travelers with its circular lights.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME keeps tireless watch over the ruins it lives in. Because of its second head, it can stand sentry even when asleep.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME clings to tomb walls keeping sentry and watching for explorers. It guards these areas relentlessly, spitting hot sand at anyone who draws too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME perches atop ancient temple ruins, crafting its nests from vines. These nests are often found near forgotten altars.
author: .izik

entry: They chew boulders into flat tablet shapes, carving mysterious etchings on each. These unique markings are thought to be ancient, but their meaning remains unknown.
author: .izik

entry: Old murals depict POKENAME clearing cave-ins in mining shafts. It carved through stone and was rewarded with bundles of roots and forest herbs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carefully sculpt large hands out of clay before animating them with a mysterious energy. They use these hands to defend themselves and those they trust from wild Pokémon.
author: sirg44

entry: Ancient texts describe POKENAME delivering parcels by air between towns. The service was fast but expensive, used only by the wealthy elite.
author: .izik

entry: The vases that are bound to POKENAME were created around 500 years ago. Wealthy people with lavish or very eccentric tastes have been known to use POKENAME as security guards for their homes.
author: mepp.

entry: The tablet on its chest glows red with anger, warning enemies to stay away. Its rough skin becomes tougher in colder climates, making it an exceptional guardian.
author: .izik

entry: Many are found guarding desert tombs, the spirals on their larger mouths glowing white before delivering a deadly bite. Their eerie presence wards off intruders.
author: .izik

entry: Microscopic etchings have been discovered on the orange glass dome of its head. These markings appear to be writings from a long-lost civilization, but their meaning and origin remain a mystery.
author: .izik

entry: When deflecting attacks with its hardened head, the spiral on its chest glows briefly. The markings seem to react to impacts, though their purpose remains unknown.
author: .izik

entry: Many people believe these Pokémon were created by an ancient, yet vastly unknown, civilization to serve as companions for all. They will comfort and protect their Trainers and the weak with their lives.
author: infinex21

entry: Long ago, POKENAME were gladiators in ancient coliseums. Though blind, it can sense enemy movements through the mane-like structure on its helmet, giving it an edge in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has been seen in ancient ruins, doing little other than watching visitors that pass through. Some believe it is a failed construct from an ancient civilization, created with energy stores that cannot properly move its own body around.
author: sk372

entry: Archeological data gathered from ruins that were home to POKENAME suggest they were bonded to a child from birth, serving as a guardian and protector. They are often seen searching various alcoves and hidden spots, trying to find their lost partners.
author: thelastmaleneko

entry: Archeological data gathered from ruins that were home to POKENAME suggest they were bonded to a child from birth, serving as a guardian and protector. They are often seen searching various alcoves and hidden spots, trying to find their lost partners.
author: thelastmaleneko

entry: POKENAME burrows through the ground with relentless determination. Its mechanical nature assures its dominance in deserts filled with ruins.
author: anarchaz

entry: When POKENAME sleeps, it likes to be completely submerged in earth, sand, or clay. For some reason, wild POKENAME will never attack one another under any circumstance, even if it is a matter of life or death.
author: bobosmith01
