entry: There are ancient desert murals depicting swarms of POKENAME ripping up fields of crops and carrying them into the sky. Some scholars believe this legend refers to an old farming ritual, while others fear it was a sign of destruction.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME are capable of delivering devastating punches with their highly developed arms, the unfortunate placement of these appendages often trips them up mid-fight. As they age, their weight distribution changes to help counteract this issue.
author: thelastmaleneko

entry: This fusion is eerily close in appearance to carved idols found in a number of ruins. When given an order, it will carry it out relentlessly, never resting or tiring. Its power over illusions allows it to do this work very discreetly.
author: elfail0

entry: POKENAME can be found within ancient ruins, slowly working in teams to try and restore the old buildings to their former glory. They make gentle humming noises to one another, harmonising and creating a mournful song for their lost cities.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The tablet it holds is said to make those nearby feel uneasy. It floats silently through tombs with an unknown purpose, leaving an eerie presence behind.
author: .izik

entry: It burrows into dunes near desert tombs, camouflaging itself perfectly. When explorers approach, it leaps out to drag them beneath the sands.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be observed flying set paths within the caverns it calls home, as if on patrol. It can stun and confuse attackers by flashing lights from the symbols on its wings and chest.
author: sk372

entry: The tablet it carries was once used by fortune tellers to glimpse the future. It glows in twenty unique colors when deeply stared at, but POKENAME will phase through walls to avoid unworthy gazes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are able to channel energy from the soles of their feet into explosive bursts of speed. However, due to their weight, POKENAME lack the ability to change direction mid-flight, often causing them to slam into things with very alarming force.
author: thelastmaleneko

entry: POKENAME colonies are found in the walls of ancient tombs, thriving in the darkness. These hidden colonies can be detected through the presence of warm spots on the walls.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fiercely guards gems embedded in the walls of ancient tombs. Its vigilant nature has made it a prized protector in stories of treasure hunters.
author: .izik

entry: If it remains in the rain for too long, its terracotta body risks weakening and cracking. POKENAME trains constantly to keep the grip of its jaws powerful.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If parts of its massive body are damaged in battle, it retreats to its cavern to rebuild them using clay or soil. POKENAME is a territorial creature that crushes any intruder bold enough to encroach upon its domain between its powerful jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a cracked, ancient flask whose leaking sand accelerates decay. Anything its sand touches crumbles to dust, and desert ruins slowly fall away as the vessel wanders, thus helping the desert reclaim the land in its relentless passage.
author: silentscript89

entry: Making their home in dark catacombs, POKENAME uses echolocation to navigate the labyrinthine halls. Their agility makes them excellent fliers, even in total darkness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nests atop forested temples, its wings as light as air and made of an ancient cotton-like material. The origin of its unique wings baffles researchers.
author: .izik

entry: The spirals on its cheeks glow yellow when it prepares to attack. The mucus it secretes while moving is extremely slippery, making it hard to follow.
author: .izik

entry: The spiral on its belly glows brightly when POKENAME is in distress. During these times, the spines on its head appear to grow sharper, serving as a defense mechanism.
author: .izik

entry: Should ancient relics wash ashore, POKENAME will instinctively guard them with unmatched loyalty. It will defend these treasures with its life.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient gardeners are believed to have used POKENAME to monitor the health of fungi. They can detect when a mushroom is sick or dying with startling accuracy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found sifting through ancient ruins in search of fragments of pottery and masonry to incorporate into their bodies. They use these fragments to construct a pot to carry plants, sheltering them from the elements and helping them grow.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Ancient blacksmiths once used its Headbutt to shape shields. The force of its strike was said to be strong enough to bend even the toughest metals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fights using the core on its head, which expels blasts of ancient energy. Sometimes, the core breaks off on impact, deactivating the stone creature.
author: nexusshenanigans

entry: POKENAME is found near the ruins of ancient civilizations. During evening hours, its core glows to act as a guiding light and can be used to send signals across long distances.
author: mepp.

entry: A small head unit pokes out from a large energy core in POKENAME's center. Quills formed from this same strange energy can be fired from the points on its head and tail.
author: sk372

entry: Ancient tomes tell of POKENAME guarding villages in coordinated packs. They pounced on invaders with Beat Up to drive them out together.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often found drifting near sunken ships, as if still guarding some long-lost treasure. Divers cling to its jagged frame as it glides through the water, guiding them swiftly past coral and wreckage.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Many ancient civilisations are believed to have treated POKENAME as deities, with religious iconography being dedicated to them. They work together with Golenine to trap evil spirits, able to send ghostly signals from their whiskers to pacify them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME were kept in royal cities in ancient kingdoms, serving as status symbols. They work together with Golesian to trap evil spirits, rapidly running in circles to trap them and keep them in place.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are rarely found outside ancient temples and shrines, acting as a guardian protector. When its inner fire burns, its hardened clay body can temporarily take on the sheen of glazed pottery.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Their tails are equally good at digging and swimming. They eagerly helped people and inspired the creation of shovels and oars in ancient civilizations.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME was first discovered on ancient wall paintings, with the living species being discovered much later. The hypnotic pattern on their abdomen has been depicted as ornaments.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME is full of energy. They swim for prolonged periods of time, shining bright from its joints. When the time comes to rest, they shut down and hibernate on the river and lake beds.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME uses its immense strength to lift and reposition stone columns in ancient temples. They are often found restoring long-forgotten ruins.
author: .izik

entry: An odd and mildly irritating semi-fluid comprises most of POKENAME's limbs. It is surprisingly adept at completely avoiding attacks by swiftly bending its limbs in unnatural and amorphous ways.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are self-assigned defenders of mountain villages. By rolling downhill at high speed, they can generate momentum into colossal punches.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME lives in certain ancient sites. Due to its shape and matching holes on the walls, it could have been used as a key for specific mechanisms.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME rolls steadily through the corridors of ancient ruins. If it suffers damage due to collisions, it can collect new material for repairs.
author: chorb33

entry: It is speculated that all POKENAME are mentally linked through one large hivemind. They seem to follow orders given from an unknown source.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The pole it wields as a weapon bears ancient carvings. Researchers have puzzled for decades over where it obtains these unique relics.
author: .izik

entry: It glides over crumbling ruins, filling in cracks with the coppery slime of its body. Once hardened, this material remains durable for hundreds of years, so scientists are attempting to synthesize it.
author: hophoppip

entry: The spiral on its tablet glows brightly while it digs through solid rock. Some ancient miners employed POKENAME to create intricate mine shafts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives inside ancient sunken ships where it protects the ship from divers. It is said that POKENAME protect sunken treasure, but this is not always the case.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protects ancient shipwrecks from looters. Its massive claw can pinch through air tanks and other equipment, so divers stay away from places where it lives.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These social Pokémon send signals to one another with beautiful chirps and antennae movements. Their camouflage resembles a Poison-type species with similar markings and will travel alongside them for protection against predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME gather to migrate, their cacophony of thunderous chirps can be heard half a mile away. This sound is considered a sure sign of spring.
author: .realthree

entry: The vines covering its body are feathered, allowing it to flick them for lift. This peculiar motion gives it the ability to fly for short bursts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME typically comes out during the sunrise to feed on early-morning nectar for the day. Farm folk say that having one flutter by the window in the morning is a sign of good luck.
author: sk372

entry: Their camouflage enables these POKENAME freedom in the forest, as other Pokémon assume they are poisonous. They communicate about where to find the best berries to consume, and travel in small groups to maintain a sense of direction.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its body grows intensely hot before transforming and reshaping into its opponent. If disturbed, its original beak may persist after the transformation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lack the firepower of their future evolutions. They can only give threats minuscule electrical shocks before skittering away.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's outer shell mimics a Fletchling to dissuade other bird Pokémon from attacking it. Its body will become warm to the touch when it is ready for evolution.
author: mistymagius

entry: Having existed since the prehistoric ages, POKENAME live along the shores, flying low. Joyful by nature, they enjoy skittering across the beach with surprisingly tuneful steps.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME communicate with each other via vibrant and expressive dances. If the response to a dance is positive enough, the pair of newly-formed friends will go hunt together to solidify their new alliance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sing together in large flocks just as the sun begins to rise. Their voices are rather weak, so the chirping and whistling is concluded by the time the sun has fully risen.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its feather to control gusts of winds. It will sometimes get blown over on windy days.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME flies in small flocks, using gusts of wind to spread embers across fields. It communicates with others through fiery patterns in the sky, signaling warnings or directions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME chirps in rhythmic patterns, adjusting its calls based on the time of day. At night, the flames on its wings glow faintly, resembling distant lanterns in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: By channeling air currents around its wings, it increases the speed of its punches. This aerodynamic boost makes it a formidable attacker while flying.
author: .izik

entry: It patches holes in clothes left to dry with its sticky webbing. Despite its good intentions, the garments often end up stuck together.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lack the wing feathers they need to fly so they bounce throughout the world instead. When they are not looking for food, they can be heard babbling songs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is very friendly towards humans and Pokémon. It soars through the skies at Mach 2 speed, displaying it's elegant feathers.
author: asyoko

entry: Urban areas are seeing an uptick in POKENAME populations, particularly in Unova. Friendly and prone to singing cute songs amongst its siblings, POKENAME has become a popular pet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are one of the few bird Pokémon that don't migrate from frigid regions over winter. They prepare for the winter all year, building a warm nest full of moss, fur and feathers. They secrete a gel over the outside of it to keep it waterproof.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are one of the few bird Pokémon that don't migrate from frigid regions over winter. They prepare for the winter all year, building a warm nest full of moss, fur and feathers. Sometimes, a small fire can be found inside.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Not only are their wings too small to fly for long, but their feathers are also often stuck together with honey. They expel puffs of intense heat to defend themselves from the Bug-type Pokémon who had collected or made the honey they gorge upon.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite having wings, this little Pokémon likes to walk around on the ground. It easily befriends other small Pokémon, sharing its food with them.
author: holzycookie

entry: POKENAME perches in the sunlight so its metallic wings will heat up. Once it has raised their temperature enough, it can burn its foes by flying into them.
author: .realthree

entry: It rubs yellow ooze from its tail on the nests of other Pokémon. Although harmless, this habit often angers territorial Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rapidly spin their arms in order to create small gusts of wind and lift themselves off the ground. They often struggle to balance themselves when they land, wildly flailing their arms and releasing sparks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It bounces off its springy tail to gain momentum before taking flight. This technique allows it to soar gracefully into the air.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME levitates through the skies, it creates dazzling displays of light with its pyrokinesis. At least, it tries to: POKENAME typically and accidentally causes small fires that it needs to stamp out.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME levitates through the skies, it creates dazzling displays of light with its pyrokinesis. At least, it tries to: POKENAME typically and accidentally causes small fires that it needs to stamp out.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME make their homes along coastlines to pick off vulnerable aquatic Pokémon. Whenever there is a thunderstorm, they search for Wacan Berries to insulate themselves from the dangerous lightning.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME communicate with each other via beautiful chirps and by waving their wings around in various patterns. They are small, so they can only fly or glide for so long; because of this, they always climb atop tree branches and take off from them.
author: infinex21

entry: The feathers on POKENAME's body are actually tiny leaves that sizzle in the rain. On sunny days, they take on a golden hue that painters have sought to recapture in their work for generations.
author: .izik

entry: It is a bundle of energy that loves to run around. It will get back up no matter how often it trips. It loves to perch upon the shoulder or arm of its beloved Trainer and chirp singsongy tunes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are aggressive fighters in combat, using their sharp claws and talons to attack foes. When battles get heated, POKENAME's bodies heat up, and their fiery attacks become stronger.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME flies with others from their flock in spiraling formations, leaving trails of steam behind. Flocks from different regions display vastly different flight patterns.
author: .izik

entry: It flaps its small arms as if flying before pecking at its opponent. The attack often lacks strength but shows its determination.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME chirps out songs it hears on the radio and gracefully dances with elegance and style. Its desire to become the very best is exemplified by its perseverance during training, as it is prone to hurting itself from overexertion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are amiable by nature, though they are quick to be startled. When taken by surprise, they can quickly shift their colors to blend in, save for the zigzag patterns wrapped around their midsections.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME communicate with one another via a system of chirps and brain signals. Experts have yet to decipher this intricate language.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: It flies to the tops of canyons to knock down trees into the rivers below. This behavior is thought to help redirect water flow for its nests.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has an extra set of wings on the back of its head that can help it fly if its main wings are damaged. Even though there is a second beak in those wings, it only eats with its main beak because it is difficult to clean behind its head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME is interrupted while photosynthesizing, it will mercilessly peck the offender until they leave. Since POKENAME's body temperature increases during photosynthesis, these pecks often cause burns.
author: darkweavile428

entry: The leaves growing from the bushes on POKENAME's back are similar in consistency to feathers. It puffs these leaves out to intimidate those who draw too close to its nest.
author: .izik

entry: When its song is interrupted, its whole body ignites and enters a chirping rage, relentlessly pecking at whatever disturbed it. The flash of heat this produces is so powerful that it takes several days for its tail feathers to regrow.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME often mistake their horn for its beak, leading them to impale food rather than eat it. It's not uncommon to spot one wandering with a berry stuck on its horn.
author: techlaw

entry: Standing on a stone's edge above the water, POKENAME will jump from a rock to gain some air time. These additional few seconds help these Pokémon dive into the water and increase their swim speed.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME dries its allies using its incredibly hot tail feathers. These feathers are quite brittle and occasionally fall out when it swims too fast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feelers are composed of thousands of tiny feathers. It rotates them counterclockwise at great speed to propel itself through the sky.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is seen gliding in the air through the use of its long ear-like wings. It is commonly seen foraging in grasslands.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME prefers to dig to its destination as its wings are poorly suited for long-term flight. Should it fly too frequently, its feathers will fall off in large quantities.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME are awake, they cry out to one another using beautiful chirps to make sure they have not gone too far from their flocks. In spring, they gather to mate; a pair of POKENAME mates will share their food together and alternate sleep cycles.
author: infinex21

entry: Its ears crackle with electricity before it dives to peck at its foe. The sparks make it easy to spot at night, even when ambushing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is known for using its tail as a lightning rod to gather energy for its attacks. Despite not yet having grown out wings, POKENAME will still find ways to get into the air to try and glide.
author: c0u51nv1nn7

entry: Upbeat and affectionate, POKENAME is positively ecstatic to be able to fly and will joyfully flap around for the sake of it. Many POKENAME don't want to evolve, as they fear they may lose the ability to fly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME communicate with one another by striking various poses using their wings and flame-lit tails. When they get excited, their bodies heat up and their tail flames dance wildly.
author: infinex21

entry: The feather growing from POKENAME's bud releases a licorice scent that calms others of its kind. Many use it for potpourri due to its strong aroma.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME detests strangers in its territory, letting out a high-pitched squeal before attacking. It only allows children to enter its home. As soon as they come near, POKENAME will warm the surrounding area until it feels cosy and inviting.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: When startled, POKENAME launches itself skyward in a single leap. Its sharp eyesight allows it to spot dangers from great distances.
author: fredfeyh

entry: POKENAME communicates by poking its beak through its membrane and blowing small bubbles. The bubbles create tiny versions of POKENAME's cry when they pop.
author: sk372

entry: A cowardly Pokémon that hides in trees. It floats about the bark of the trees, pecking at it, hoping for a small bug Pokémon to appear.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's wings beat so rapidly in flight that it appears to have two sets of still wings on either side of its body. Despite the speed of its wingbeats, it is not a particularly fast flyer.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME are hatched relatively frail. Despite lacking obvious offensive or defensive power, they are prone to random and devastating bursts of flaming energy.
author: chaos_emblemx

entry: POKENAME love to sleep on large smooth rocks that absorb their heat. Other Pokémon often join to enjoy some of the warmth, but as soon as POKENAME wakes, it pecks them away.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME spits searing hot toxin from its mouth. This green goo can cause the skin to blister within moments.
author: .izik

entry: To rest, POKENAME possesses hollow stumps in dense woods. The stump's surface grows hot, sometimes hot enough to ignite.
author: .izik

entry: On spring mornings, it chirps nonstop until it sees someone wake up. Feeling proud of its effort, it flies away thinking it has been helpful.
author: .izik

entry: It pretends to be a stuffed toy near daycares, blending in with ease. During snack time, it pushes over toddlers to steal their treats before flying off.
author: .izik

entry: The feather protruding from POKENAME's sand-like body glows slightly to attract prey such as Caterpie. Once they draw close, it strikes with Peck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have fine, fibrous Hericium mushrooms parasitising their bodies. These mushrooms take a feathery appearance and are used by POKENAME to glide away from danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Juvenile POKENAME often form small groups and strengthen their wings by jumping from small ledges. Because they are very social and easy to train, POKENAME make great starter Pokémon for new Trainers.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME soar after migrating herds of Stantler. A flock of hunting POKENAME is a common sight in the spring.
author: .realthree

entry: The feathers around POKENAME's neck keep it warm in the winter. Unlike its winged variant, it waits out the cold.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME eggs are buried deep in the ground surrounding volcanoes. The many months of deep pressure and heat form crystals on their bodies.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME's pad acts like a paraglider, allowing them to glide between trees. They often follow Trainers with visible food and chirp incessantly until fed.
author: chibitales

entry: When it swings its tail, it scatters embers from the feathers upon the tail's tip; it communicates with others of its kind by waving its tail while emitting myriad chirps. Its claws burn hot when it gets excited or agitated.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME peck at underground roots to nourish themselves. The unexpected cry of a POKENAME has awakened many Pokémon in the forest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hops happily from the waves with others of its kind, fluttering its wings rapidly to stay airborne for extended periods. The feathers it leaves behind dissolve if left on dry land for too long.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers to engage prey only alongside its pack. Before striking, it puffs up its feathers and hops on one leg in a display of dominance.
author: .izik

entry: It swiftly maneuvers within its forest home by flying from tree to tree in zigzag patterns, using its claws to cling to each tree. Although it primarily searches for fresh fruits within the trees, it is easily distracted as long as it is not hungry.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's threads are burning hot in the short moment they are spat out before they become sticky. They use their sharp beaks to peck through tree bark and access the delicious sap held inside.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lives in branches and pecks seeds off of fruits. It may be small in size, but it proves mighty in battle.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME collect and weave together bits of twine to help build up their nests. If a POKENAME spots an intruder, it will spring off the nearest empty branch to launch itself like an arrow.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME stores large amounts of fruits, nuts, and seeds in its bill, constantly competing with other bird Pokémon for food. Island nations once fed them papayas, as it was believed to bring good luck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's swift, erratic movements makes it difficult to fight and capture. By waving the feather on its head, it whips up mild gusts of wind to knock berries from trees.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are known for their serene songs and beautiful light shows, especially when courting with Fletchmise. However, they become notably more defensive and hostile whenever any outsiders enter their territory.
author: entomoxie

entry: They fly low to the surface of lakes and ponds to drag their tails across the surface. They splash water onto bug Pokémon in branches above them in the hopes of knocking them down to secure a meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They dig up and break rocks with their muscular arms to expose roots underneath. Afterwards, they dive headfirst into the ground to peck and rip apart the roots for consumption.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It can swim at great speeds thanks to how smooth its shell is and how strong its wings are. Using its beak, it can compress bubbles and spit them out like bullets.
author: infinex21

entry: If POKENAME flaps hard enough, it can lift its body off the ground a small distance and achieve flight. It often tries to snap at prey beneath it while flying, but this destroys its balance and sends it crashing to the ground.
author: sk372

entry: The feathery wings of POKENAME glow with burning embers making their flight visible at night. They can inadvertently cause forest fires while searching for flowers during prolonged dry periods.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME nests near volcanic geysers. When it absorbs enough heat, its feathers glow white and shimmer with dangerous intensity.
author: .izik

entry: As it ages, it grows extra wings made of gelatinous material. This fluid is hot to the touch but cools when near friends.
author: .izik

entry: It can tuck its wings beneath its shell until it sees a veritable smorgasbord of prey along the shores. POKENAME's cries and wing flapping are said to be reminiscent of an ancient empire's anthem.
author: beatdoof

entry: Some POKENAME require more food as they grow to accommodate their growing physique, inevitably creating conflict between others of their flock. Their fangs are capable of gnashing through anything, especially when infused with flames.
author: beatdoof

entry: When hunting, POKENAME makes a coughing-like sound that produces a small burst of flames. This behavior inspired a common saying wishing good health to the ill: "Fly away, POKENAME".
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In cold weather, it struggles to fly and takes frequent breaks. To stay airborne, it blows fire onto its wings to keep them warm.
author: .izik

entry: The large feathers on its back were prized by ancient poets. They believed writing with them would bring great luck to their works.
author: .izik

entry: If one encroaches near their nesting grounds, they spit a burning acid. If the acid touches someone, they will require proper and specific treatment in order to fully recover from the affliction.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When building its nest, it searches for hot pepper plants. It squirts pepper juice on the base, enjoying the spicy sensation on its feathers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME never takes flight during rainstorms, as it hates the feeling of wet feathers. When hunting, it heats both its beak and its claws to make its attacks even more lethal.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It buzzes across creek surfaces, leaving trails of heat in its wake. Tracking it becomes easy with a thermometer due to the hot air it generates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can spit fire much faster than it can fly, so it hovers above bodies of water and hurls balls of fire at them. Anything unlucky enough to be in the vicinity is flash-fried. POKENAME refuses to eat hot food, so it allows the food to cool.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME can spit fire much faster than it can fly, so it hovers above bodies of water and hurls balls of fire at them. Anything unlucky enough to be in the vicinity is flash-fried. They can have negative effects on ecosystems.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The egg on the back of POKENAME is used as a lure for its prey. POKENAME secretes a paralysing poison through the egg, and while its prey is immobilised, it will cook them with its fiery vines.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: When throwing a tantrum, it perches on tall trees and scorches nearby bushes with flames. This fiery outburst is often done out of spite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunt Bug-type Pokémon and track them to their nests. They expel flames to drive their prey out from their nests to capture and feed on them. They are especially partial to Beedrill and the honey they make.
author: infinex21

entry: It uses its long neck to thrust its head underwater and catch prey. It avoids cold water as the chill saps its stamina.
author: .izik

entry: It sticks its nose into geysers to soak up the intense heat. This habit helps warm its nose during colder seasons.
author: .izik

entry: It raises its internal temperature while rolling, blasting powerful flames from its trunk. The combination of fire and momentum makes it formidable.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blocks the ventilation openings of machines it finds in circulation with its feathers, causing them to overheat so it can sleep on top of them. Living in an urban environment has made it very lazy; it never feels like building a nest.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fluff out the feathers lining their hood when they feel like they're being threatened. They slither forward and peck viciously at whatever they're afraid of if they feel like their display isn't working.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The more delicious food it consumes, the brighter its flames become. A full belly significantly boosts the power of its fire attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Though it prefers frigid climates, the warmth from POKENAME's body is enough to melt snow around its den. A POKENAME habitat is easy to spot in the wild due to this stark environmental contrast.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's internal fire charges while it is active, increasing its speed to the point that its jumps mimic flight. It launches burning leaves at opponents while circling them, charging once the foe has become frustrated or off-balance.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a notorious egg thief. When it runs at its top speed of 50 mph, it jumps into the air and glides for short periods of time.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME tend to remain in the air rather than on the ground due to their stubby legs. When in combat, POKENAME fight using their internal fire to protect their territory and ward off intruders.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME use their developed legs to deliver strong kicks and to launch themselves into the air. Their wings are developed enough to let them glide for hours before needing to rest.
author: infinex21

entry: By heating the water in their mouth, POKENAME can fire steam bullets that shatter boulders. The feathery fins help manage their body temperature.
author: lampent12

entry: It spits fire to intimidate and deter others and changes colors in the midst of the resulting chaos to hide and sneak away. It uses its beak to crack open nuts and to break into hard fruits, both of which are its favorite kinds of foods.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME builds its nests by carefully burning logs with controlled embers. It is highly territorial and will spit sparks at any intruders that approach its dam.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME reigns over a territory a mile in radius, fending off any other Pokémon that might compete for food. Researchers have noticed that it is literally hot-headed with the temperature of its feathers being proportional to its ego.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The sight of herds of wild POKENAME gliding through the air at sunrise and sunset is treasured by many. Their feathers remain warm even after being shed and have a calming effect on those who hold them.
author: infinex21

entry: This variant of POKENAME is known to soar through the skies of the Kalos region. It uses its broad, warm wings to embrace and calm frightened or overly anxious Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The feathers around POKENAME's body retain warmth long after flight. It often shelters smaller Pokémon during cold nights.
author: fredfeyh

entry: POKENAME moves so fast that it leaves behind trails of cinders in the air. If it spots prey, it strikes with a fiery dive before jetting away in a blur of flames.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is filled with a flammable liquid that jiggles as it moves. It spits this liquid at foes before igniting it with fiery attacks.
author: .izik

entry: When searching for a mate, it flings its yellow feathers in a circular pattern. It performs an elaborate dance on a treestump that it has bitten flat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME senses the fighting spirit of those around it and responds by increasing the intensity of its flames. It spars with others by launching small fireballs to test their endurance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are fierce defenders of their territory, patrolling both ground and sky. If there are long scratch marks on the ground, it means a POKENAME has made its nest nearby.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME is very particular about its roses, using its beak and wings meticulously to keep them in perfect condition. If the roses are ever ripped, it will become enraged and stop at nothing for revenge.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME leaves faint scorch marks wherever it lands after a high-speed dive. These marks are used by researchers to track its movements.
author: fredfeyh

entry: The gelatinous material surrounding its body is intensely hot. To prevent fires, it avoids landing on flammable surfaces, even while resting.
author: .izik

entry: Swift as an arrow, POKENAME can catch even the fastest bug Pokémon. They often roost in chimneys when winter strikes to keep each other warm, causing a nuisance to many homes that rely on lit fireplaces to keep warm.
author: chibitales

entry: Just before POKENAME pounces on its prey, its gemstone eyes will glint a bright, fiery orange in sheer excitement. Unfortunately, their inability to hide their joy often leads to their prey noticing their hiding spots and fleeing.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME's wings are soft like cotton, but they radiate intense heat. It perches atop treetops, basking in the sun to keep its flames at peak strength.
author: .izik

entry: Spinning on one foot, it flings hot needles in every direction to deter foes. The leaves on its head grow slower when it is under stress.
author: .izik

entry: It lands on plateaus and unleashes flames from its beak, creating intricate shapes in the sky. These fiery displays mesmerize onlookers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lie in wait under the sand, only revealing the tail end of its arrow. Once the arrow is touched, it explodes upwards, dousing whatever it catches in lava-hot sand.
author: darxer_

entry: POKENAME maintain a high body temperature in an effort to stave off the parasitic fungus that infests their bodies. The dried out fungus is prone to catching fire, but the spores from the dying mushroom fall back onto the body of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With stronger wings and more confidence, POKENAME has become more independent than its previous evolution. It spits globs of molten rock from its beak to attack foes.
author: chibitales

entry: While its snout resembles a beak, it is covered in soft fur. It wags its tail excitedly before unleashing powerful Ember attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME maintain a high body temperature in an effort to stave off the parasitic fungus that infests their bodies. The dried out fungus is prone to catching fire, but the spores from the dying mushroom fall back onto the body of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME maintain a high body temperature in an effort to stave off the parasitic fungus that infests their bodies. The dried out fungus is prone to catching fire, but the spores from the dying mushroom fall back onto the body of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME maintain a high body temperature in an effort to stave off the parasitic fungus that infests their bodies. The dried out fungus is prone to catching fire, but the spores from the dying mushroom fall back onto the body of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its internal flame sac grows increasingly hotter during battle, though this has been recently discovered to be the case whenever it is agitated. It fights with kicking attacks that utilize its tough claws and by spitting embers at its opponent.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME shoot embers at prey through their beaks before dragging them underground. Their wings put out these fires before they get out of control.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It attacks fiercely with its beak and claws. Though it's very territorial, it's easily distracted by shiny coins.
author: snescontroller

entry: It performs somersaults in rapid succession, keeping foes off guard. While spinning, it blows flames at opponents with impressive precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME soar over their territories in pairs. If they find any prey, they shoot embers into their den. POKENAME are extremely trustworthy and loyal, staying with each other in even the most dire times. They often form rivalries with Rockruff.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME trains by carrying branches in its talons as it soars through the sky. Its powerful legs allow it to strike with kicks hot enough to scorch the ground.
author: .izik

entry: The stones covering its body heat up the longer it flies. It hurls these fiery rocks at prey before launching an attack.
author: .izik

entry: With both its wings and legs still developing, POKENAME exhibits a bit of a complex, displaying aggressive behavior. It snorts out steam and spits flame at anybody it sees, attempting to pick fights.
author: sk372

entry: A majestic creature often depicted as a symbol of rebirth in some circles. POKENAME is incredibly fast, reaching speeds fast enough to break the sound barrier. Scorch marks tend to be left along its trail.
author: merclipse

entry: Though their wings are small, they can soar through the air with ease for long periods of time. Flocks of POKENAME will fly as fast as they can toward water and then skip across the surface using their own shells as a means of playing.
author: infinex21

entry: It generates gusts of hot air as it sprints across the landscape. These zephyrs can ignite dry grass, leaving blazing trails behind.
author: .izik

entry: It slaps its tail against the water's surface to intimidate foes. Once provoked, it exhales intense flames to keep attackers at bay.
author: .izik

entry: It lulls opponents to sleep using hypnotic psychic waves. Once they are unconscious, it unleashes fiery bursts from its beak to overwhelm them.
author: .izik

entry: The silk that comes out of its mouth is warm to the touch. If left on exposed skin for more than ten minutes, it can cause a rash.
author: .izik

entry: The red horns of these bug Pokémon are very hot and can even expel a fluid that they ignite with sparks made by smacking their bone club around. They wear the skulls of their prey to then hit their club against to always be able to create sparks.
author: infinex21

entry: It wields one of its shed horns, which can still secrete a flammable liquid and can be ignited by striking it like a match. It will set this shed horn ablaze and throw it like a javelin to strike down distant foes or aerial prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME clings to the sides of volcanoes as it awaits evolution. Ancient civilizations believed that once the volcano erupted, POKENAME would be reborn from the magma, evolving into Volcapod.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME have bright crimson fins that give them a distinct look that makes them popular among rich Trainers. They are warm to the touch and can produce small flames from their fins.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is finicky about its appearance, and hates it when its fur is messed up. As if to punish those who ruin its look, its hairs leave a burning rash when touched.
author: hophoppip

entry: A pink venom drips from POKENAME's tail. Highly combustible, it can ignite from mere sunlight exposure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's normal form is soft and heated, described as being like warm gelatin. When transforming, it cocoons itself in flames before the fire bursts and reveals its morphed state.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers in small swarms around the base of volcanoes. Highly aggressive, its rapid wingbeat spreads special pollen onto its stinger arms that it can ignite to attack others with flaming stabs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has become popular as a pet due to its soft and warm plumage and a tendency to cozy up to other, larger beings. It creates tiny flames when it chirps and sings to others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME watches from willow trees at night, waiting for prey near streams. Embers trail from its wings when it silently takes flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces a soft, sticky thread that is just durable enough for basic angling needs. Its silk is commonly used to reinforce the line of an Old Rod.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's feathers radiate intense heat in the morning. A single loose down feather is hot enough to boil a pot of water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are some of the first to detect when a volcano is about to erupt and form groups to escape the fiery wrath. Scientists study their flight patterns to help evacuate people near volcanoes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Packs of POKENAME can be found wandering through the remains of forest fires. These Pokémon constantly consume ash and soot, turning their fur an ashy white.
author: santon5512

entry: As POKENAME glides over lakes, the heat from its wings boils the water's surface. It snatches watercress midair to snack on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is covered in a thick fur that keeps it warm in winter months. In summers, it migrates to volcanoes and sheds its fur, which can be collected to make ropes that don't cause rope burns.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: If POKENAME falls from its pine tree while asleep, it erupts into flames and explodes. These accidents have been known to start massive forest fires.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often seen collecting magma stones at the base of volcanoes to make cocoons. Their tails alone can reach 500 degrees Fahrenheit.
author: pankiwi

entry: Long ago, people believed that the mask atop POKENAME's head was the face of a sun god. This idea was reinforced by the fact that POKENAME's deep howls change pitch along with the position of the sun.
author: soup1900

entry: Under cover of night, POKENAME prowls the desert. It howls and fires jets of flame into the sky to bring down flying prey like Vibrava.
author: .izik

entry: When these bug Pokémon curl up, their muscles become so tense that they can withstand and even repel some physical blows. They prefer arid heat, so they are often found within deserts. They drink juice from fruits and cacti rather than consume water.
author: infinex21

entry: When it curls up, its muscles bulk out and tense up to a remarkable degree. Even while curled up, it can shoot out flames from its red horns. It can withstand intense heat, so it may even clad itself in flames as it charges at an enemy.
author: infinex21

entry: It secrets a paint-like substance from its tail that it uses to mark its territory. When it gets in a fight, it lights this substance ablaze.
author: admiralvermin

entry: POKENAME is always training to hone its power of flame manipulation. Practicing in volcanic areas allows its growing body to remain at a high temperature, giving it better control of its fire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME may be small, but it is proud of its magnificent mane. Should a careless Trainer try to pet its head, they'll get a taste of its surprisingly powerful psychic abilities.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME grips power lines to overcharge its body, growing dangerously hot. When enraged, it can emit heat intense enough to melt titanium.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drinks lava through its beak-like mouth and prefers to dwell in active volcanoes, where it can stay superheated at all times. It hates being cold, submerging itself in lava when it feels even the smallest chill.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight through its large, bushy tail and metabolizes it; the resulting energy from this process can be turned into flames. The blue orbs along POKENAME's back glow whenever it spits out fire.
author: infinex21

entry: The heat from POKENAME's back scorches tunnel ceilings as it digs. This molten touch fuses stone, reinforcing its underground lairs.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, POKENAME curls into a ball and rolls, its body covered in roiling flames. Scorched trails can be seen in volcanic areas where rival POKENAME have fought.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in the deepest pits of the magma chamber in a volcano. Every few days, it surfaces out of its dwelling, spewing streams of fire from its horns to burn off its excess internal flames.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME can conjure immolating flames burning on its entire body to defend itself and to show how it has matured. Though more often these flames are conjured as part of its mystical, graceful, ritualized dancing, for the prosperity of its dwelling.
author: beatdoof

entry: The flame burning within POKENAME's body burns hot and true even in the darkest of nights, where they are then used to create innumerable fire conjurations, including mirages, fireballs resembling miniature suns, and visions of a long-gone past.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME's petals burst into flame whenever they absorb a large amount of sunlight. This process does not harm it, but it has been the cause of dangerous forest fires in the past.
author: badtothebow

entry: While POKENAME looks like a marine plant, it is actually a Bug-type Pokémon drawing in prey with mimicry. It causes serious burns on contact.
author: hellaluyeah

entry: Wild POKENAME will often curl upon their bodies enough that mostly just their white fur is visible. Due to the warmth they emit, many smaller Bug-type Pokémon are often drawn to them.
author: infinex21

entry: Swinging from branch to branch, POKENAME chars bananas before eating them. It leaves a trail of soot in its woodland territory.
author: .izik

entry: These small and numerous bug Pokémon primarily live underground in volcanic regions, especially where sulfur is plentiful. They consume sulfur on a regular basis, which seems to have imbued their red spikes and horns with toxic properties.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is also referred to as "Sun Drop" by locals. It expels flames from its blade up to 5,500 degrees F.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: As if it were not enough that its horn can pierce basalt without chipping, each strike from it delivers a horrible venom as well. POKENAME venom effectively burns living tissue within minutes of contact; antivenoms have proven difficult to develop.
author: infinex21

entry: The red-hot blades on the end of POKENAME's arms are hot enough to melt stone. This fiery power makes it a fearsome fighter, capable of cutting through solid rock with ease.
author: .izik

entry: The silk of POKENAME was prized by ancient royalty as "dragon silk" which was used to make expensive royal fabric. These Pokémon have been depicted beside kings in ancient hieroglyphs.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Its red organs channel heat through them; it can channel enough heat to ignite pieces of its white fur. To fend off threats, it will ignite clumps of its fur and throw them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME shoot flames from their long horns to overwhelm their targets and to knock down food from trees. Every month, POKENAME shed tufts of their warm, white fur that many find comforting to hold.
author: infinex21

entry: Its horn and spikes glow red-hot whenever it releases flames, which it can only release from these same parts. Its horns and spikes carry upon them toxic scales that chemically burn the flesh of anything that touches them.
author: infinex21

entry: A humongous larva, POKENAME dreams about evolving into a mighty dragon someday. Its spikes are made of ice that never melts.
author: voxposs

entry: Found in volcano walls, POKENAME's waxy body never melts-no matter how high the temperature rises. The blue flame on its head flickers as it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides in abandoned desert tombs, clinging to ceilings. The light within its body glows brightly when travelers pass below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects keys in abandoned mansions and jingles them while eating. The louder the jingling, the more it enjoys its meal and the hotter it gets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very rare creatures that live deep within the magma inside volcanoes. In ancient times, people would throw precious gems into the volcano in the hopes that POKENAME would come forth and grant their wishes.
author: sk372

entry: Before evolving, POKENAME wraps itself in a fibrous material that acts as a cocoon. Despite being still and inactive in this state, they are overwhelmingly hot to the touch. The cocoon erupts in a fiery explosion when POKENAME finishes evolution.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME darts over desert sands at high speed. When it lands, the heat it emits can turn the sand beneath it into glass.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is composed of heat-resistant metal, allowing POKENAME to unleash powerful flame attacks without harm. It rubs against soft objects to keep itself clean and its metal polished.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's gear-like body spins clockwise while unleashing fire attacks. After battle, it emits rhythmic clicking sounds while it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's spicy leaves are prized in culinary circles and often used in porridge. A dish featuring it is the signature meal of a famed Sunnytown restaurant.
author: .izik

entry: The spores shed from POKENAME's body can cause mild burns. When properly harvested, these spores are a key ingredient in crafting Burn Heals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are a danger to any forest they reside in. Its five horns release super-heated toxic spores dangerous to all organic life.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: POKENAME's furred wings keep it insulated during nighttime forest flights. It remains active even in the coldest winters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats around the deserts surrounding ancient tombs, clutching strange artifacts. During the day, it can hold the artifact aloft to channel the sun's energy and enhance its flame powers in battle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers caves dense with magnetic ore, which it consumes by melting it down. It will spit fire at rival POKENAME who approach its next meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has been discovered within ruins within short distances of dormant volcanoes. Researchers theorize that old civilizations may have used them as warning signs, as it grows restless near active volcanoes.
author: sk372

entry: At night, POKENAME climbs trees with its antennae glowing brightly with heat. It spits acid at anything that gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is petulant and defensive, thinking others look down on it due to its size and posture. It's prone to throwing tantrums, as well as fireballs, at anything nearby when its temper flares.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME wants to sleep, it possesses old tree stumps. Over time, the wood heats and eventually bursts into flames.
author: .izik

entry: When fighting, it uses the sun to its advantage by positioning itself so the bright sunlight blinds the opponents and makes it harder for them to land a hit. Once the battle is won, POKENAME strikes a dramatic pose and spouts fire from its horns.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME radiates its internal body heat through the red thorns on its head. It can fire its hot thorns at its opponents, causing excruciating pain.
author: mistymagius

entry: The mushrooms on POKENAME's back are dangerously spicy. Even a single bite can irreparably damage a person's sense of taste.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, POKENAME shakes its body to shed many of the tiny hairs covering its body. These follicles quickly ignite after detaching, causing a shower of hot sparks and loud pops that scare off predators.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME builds its nest in volcanic tunnels, lining it with molten rocks. If it becomes too cold, its movements slow to a crawl.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's antennae emit a sweet pumpkin scent. As it floats above rivers, it releases flickering blue lights from its belly to lure prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's skin is hot to the touch. When it has nightmares while sleeping face-down in ponds, the surrounding water begins to boil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME make large nesting groups around the rims of volcanoes. Their presence is considered a good omen, as they will not nest on a volcano that has any risk of erupting in the near future.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is extremely possessive of any coins it purloins for its collection. To keep others from taking back what it stole, it will super-heat them with its flames so that nobody else can handle the heated metal but it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a slimy film for protection. Besides letting it slip out of the grasp of most attackers, the slime contains tiny burning scales that will singe the flesh of the one who grabbed it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is typically seen at or around hot springs areas in the wild, soaking in the piping hot waters. To defend itself, it blows red-colored bubbles from its mouth that burst into burning embers.
author: sk372

entry: Old legends of will-o'-wisps rising from the ground in the woods may have actually been due to POKENAME. Their sticks light on fire when someone unfamiliar draws near, and they nest partially submerged in the earth.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This larva uses heavy cannons to shoot water streams and push enemies far away. That's the only way POKENAME can protect their soft belly.
author: voxposs

entry: POKENAME is an extremely voracious creature that inhabits dense forests with its group. To satisfy its insatiable appetite, it bites the trees to consume their sap. The seed on its back stores the energy that fuels the power of its Poison-type moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body is mostly comprised of its large mouth, leaving little room for other organs. It is thought this is why it has a relatively small appetite despite its size.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME latches onto light posts to absorb electricity for sustenance. This behavior often causes power outages in smaller towns.
author: .izik

entry: It scrapes the edges of its wings across its skull to sharpen them into deadly points, letting it cut prey as it flies past multiple times until they succumb to their wounds and it can feast on the pooling blood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its bone to crack open geodes and decorates its nest with the crystals inside. These sparkling displays attract prey like Sableye.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feet are highly sensitive, detecting vibrations in the ground to track enemy movements. This allows it to sense foes even in complete darkness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hones its agility by dodging droplets of water falling from stalactites in waterlogged caves. This rigorous training strengthens its evasive abilities in battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its tongue to wrap around ledges in caves and swing from stone to stone. It uses sound waves to locate its next target in the darkness.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are incredibly resilient to disease and absorb illnesses from other Pokémon to increase the potency of their noxious fumes. POKENAME live in colonies where they create a shared space to inoculate themselves against a plethora of illnesses.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It emits a supersonic scream to terrify those around it. This serves as a deterrent while it waits for evolution to take place.
author: .izik

entry: Given its bulk, it cannot fly well. Despite this, POKENAME jump off cliffs hoping to soar, only to tumble to the bottom.
author: capwolfbane

entry: When it spots burrowing prey like Diglett, POKENAME drills into the ground using its horn. It pursues its target relentlessly through underground tunnels.
author: .izik

entry: The inside of its mouth is warm and soft, and its body rather durable, making it perfect for protecting and incubating eggs. Daycares and Breeders have taken to using them to keep especially precious eggs safe from harm.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME untangles its vines to snare foes, reeling them in for a venomous Poison Fang attack. Its precision leaves little chance for escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tails are a key ingredient in the 'Savory Cinnabar', a dish popular aboard the S.S. Anne. Lightly braised, they are served in a Colbur Berry-based sauce.
author: .izik

entry: It captures prey, which is typically Magikarp or Feebas, whole and siphons them of their blood to sustain itself. Its rock-hard horn contains a dangerous venom that could fell a Gyarados days after being stabbed.
author: infinex21

entry: Though it may look frightening, POKENAME is not aggressive towards humans. It's large mouth is for consuming vast quantities of flowers whole for their honey and other nutrients.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME amplifies its screeches with psychic energy, causing immense discomfort and pain in Pokémon and people alike. It is known to feed on the blood of breaching Wailord.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME constructs elaborate near-invisible complexes in caves for its nest. Its translucent walls and furniture are nearly impossible to detect.
author: .izik

entry: In the wild, POKENAME remain still until approached, then suddenly lunge out at their prey, sucking their blood. They use their psychic abilities to alter the perception of others to lure them closer.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME breaks off dead tree branches to fuel its flame-based attacks. It often forages in charred forests to find the perfect material.
author: .izik

entry: Its head wings also function as pincers. It cannot close its mouth, so debris can easily fall within. It can often be found under trees, using its pincer-like wings to shake loose fruits and berries to fall into its mouth.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are hyper-aggressive, loudly screeching at anything that looks at it funny. If you disturb a school of POKENAME, your eardrums will burst before they even have the chance to attack you.
author: mistymagius

entry: It transforms its extended tongue into an imitation of its prey. Once another member of the species draws near, it quickly transforms back, wrapping around the hapless victim and dragging it into POKENAME's hungry maw.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME takes down prey larger than itself by firing poisoned quills from its fur from a distance. Once weakened, it latches onto its target with its massive fangs and delivers a painful electric jolt to finish them off.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME resembles an extremely old, outdated depiction of a Golbat. Its long tongue can ensnare smaller creatures, dragging them close so it can sink its fangs into them and drain some blood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fangs are retractable, remaining hidden from sight until it spots potential prey. It swoops quickly and sinks its teeth into victims, draining their blood for nutrients that will hasten its evolution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME never closes its mouth and consumes anything that fits inside. Its wings are nonfunctional as a consequence.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It has grown to its enormous size by devouring anything it can fit into its sizeable mouth. Rendered useless by its weight, its wings flap feebly behind it as it eats.
author: houseoffallingflowers

entry: Many describe the sights of POKENAME shedding its skin as disturbing, as its head will protrude from within the mouth of the layer being shed before it can escape its old skin.
author: sk372

entry: The floating crystal orb in POKENAME's mouth glows a vivid violet when a storm is imminent. Sailors see it as an omen of turbulent seas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are a highly aggressive species found swarming deep in cave systems. Their stingers are so sharp and their attacks so quick and ferocious that even Steelix and Aggron are wary of their nests.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an insectivore, but lacks a strong hunting instinct. Instead, the beads around its neck emit a scent highly attractive to insects, leading bugs to fly close to or into its mouth so it can swallow them whole.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can navigate dark environs, such as caves, with incredible ease despite a lack of organic night vision. They deliver a numbing venom through their talons, which makes it easier for them to drain prey of their blood.
author: infinex21

entry: Though it has no visible teeth, POKENAME still "bites" others as a form of mischievous play. After annoying its chosen victim, it flies off to hide in narrow spaces, tucking its wings to help it squeeze in.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases a dense Haze from its mouth to obscure its surroundings. It uses this tactic to confuse both predators and prey alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME weaves its web between stalagmites in dark caverns. It uses this sticky trap to catch prey unaware as they traverse the tunnels.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME thrives in dense forests, preying on smaller Pokémon like Pidgey and Weedle. It uses a single Supersonic to disorient its prey before striking.
author: .izik

entry: It hangs upside down from tall perches when it sleeps and when it searches for fresh prey. Its talons are strong enough to penetrate thick hides and deliver a potent venom as it drags its prey back to its nest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME flap their fins almost as if they were wings, though they are able to glide in the air for a time when they leap out of water. Their glowing bulbs allow them to navigate deep water and their gaping mouths catch many small prey.
author: infinex21

entry: The sudden formation of eyes upon evolution was incredibly stressful for POKENAME, making them much more volatile than their previous form. Bright lights seem to anger them, and they often give chase to anything that moves too quickly.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME have sensitive eyes, so whenever they encounter bright lights, they close their eyes and tuck their head into their eggshell. Their leathery wings also help mitigate the glare of bright lights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Their sharp and tough beaks are lined with small, sharp fangs that they use to drain the blood of their prey. The vibrancy of their feathers is an indicator of how old they are and of how potent their venom has become.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME paralyzes foes with a Thunder Wave before carrying them away into the night. Its swift abductions have inspired many eerie tales.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's whiskers twitch excitedly at the sight of prey. If unable to defeat a Trainer with its bite, it will snatch an item from their bag and escape into the sky.
author: .izik

entry: The tip of its tail is coated with a potent toxin, making it a dangerous weapon. POKENAME uses its tail to incapacitate prey before feeding.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rapidly flaps its small wings when either excited or irritated. Distinguishing between the two states is crucial in avoiding a nasty bite.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME's heavy frame is a result of the huge amounts of blood it consumes. Without specific training, this Pokémon will remain permanently grounded.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME is a nocturnal predator that is most often found near labyrinthian caverns. Although aggressive, it has a loyal personality.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME hunts, it makes sure to consume as much physical matter as it can handle. It coats its fur with sticky and dense toxins that leak from its pores, which affects its ability to fly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME hunts, it makes sure to consume as much physical matter as it can handle. It coats its fur with sticky and dense toxins that leak from its pores, which affects its ability to fly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flies around parks at dusk, drawn to the color yellow. It drains energy from anyone wearing yellow and steals their clothing as a prize.
author: .izik

entry: The red gem on POKENAME's crown glows intensely before it unleashes a barrage of Air Cutter attacks. It can break apart solid stone with ease.
author: .izik

entry: It hunts smaller prey that it can easily grab whole with its gaping maw so as to drain their blood. Its fangs deliver a numbing venom and the pollen loosed from its bulb is poisonous to most.
author: infinex21

entry: Should one be under attack by a POKENAME, the best course of action is to aim for its whiskers. Extremely sensitive and important for maintaining aerial balance, it will immediately retreat if they are touched.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's teeth are very small, so they use illusions to mask their presence and lull their prey into a false sense of security to get up close. By the time the prey sees through the facade, it is too late.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: POKENAME emits eerie howls that resemble the sounds of sick children. It strikes when its target is off guard, draining life with its fangs.
author: .izik

entry: It hides in darkness, waiting to frighten prospective victims with a loud screech. Those who strike it in defense are hit with a stunning counter blow, incapacitating them so that POKENAME may feed on their blood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME emits a powerful Screech when an intruder approaches its nest. The sound is disorienting enough to deter most threats.
author: .izik

entry: If disturbed while draining its prey, POKENAME glows a deep brown before exploding. This tactic ensures its escape from potential threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly squeamish and uses Mud-Slap to disorient predators like Charmeleon. It quickly burrows underground to avoid confrontation.
author: .izik

entry: Each and every sharp point on POKENAME's body can inject a potent poison if touched. It is most active at night. It can flap its wings and latch onto prey without making a sound.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME glides effortlessly through the night sky, diving in and out of clouds. Ancient cultures once believed its gleaming body signified an impending poor harvest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roost in the mouths of caves, making their nests within crags and crevices in the rock. They swarm anyone who gets too close, biting at them with sharp fangs and draining their vitality.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The hooded portion is attached to its neck. When it gets cold, its wings will radiate heat to keep the outer shell warm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cleans its horn by soaking it in ponds. A freshly cleaned horn can be wielded more efficiently during aerial combat.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon suffers from its high speed. Whenever they run, their tongue flops around wildly. Careless POKENAME trip over their own tongue because it got in the way.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: Most active on nights with a new moon, POKENAME fly without making a sound. Their fangs are too dull to properly bite into prey, so they instead keep around red berries to bite into, trying to play tough and appear intimidating.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: In the dark of night, POKENAME forages for its favorite foods, honey and the juiciest of berries. Trainers have been accidentally frightened off by the sight of POKENAME's long tongue dripping bright red berry juice.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is incredibly sticky, which allows it to scale vertical surfaces effortlessly. The body also radiates extreme heat, so it leaves a trail of burnt stone wherever it passes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's beak hides two pairs of venomous fangs used to poison prey caught during its nightly hunts. It lives deep within dark caverns, as it cannot tolerate bright light.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME burrows into snow mounds with its wings folded tightly. It pokes its small nose out, sniffing the air for potential food sources.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spins in swift, clockwise movements before diving onto prey like Metapod. Its razor-sharp wings slice through even the hardest shells.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's beak hides two pairs of venomous fangs used to poison prey caught during its nightly hunts. It lives deep within dark caverns, as it cannot tolerate bright light.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Rescuers sometimes deploy POKENAME to locate trapped survivors in caves. Its echolocation and small size allow it to navigate tight openings effortlessly.
author: .izik

entry: In ancient times, POKENAME's wings were prized by leatherworkers. They were used to craft durable leather for shields.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME opens its massive mouth when rolling rapidly toward smaller prey like Spearow and Sandshrew. Its speed makes it nearly impossible to evade.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are natural born grapplers, and love to participate in fighting tournaments. Their tendency to bite often leads to them being disqualified.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Its powerful serpentine body will constrict prey, before sinking its fangs in and gorging itself on blood.  Once completely drained of blood, it disposes the prey's husk in its gaping maw.
author: sk372

entry: The inside of POKENAME's mouth is humid, creating an ideal environment for incubating eggs. It fiercely defends this precious space from intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fangs naturally fall out just before it evolves. Long ago, knights sought these teeth to craft rings they believed would bring them good fortune.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggles to stay airborne with its stone-like body. When exhausted, it crashes into cliff faces to embed itself and rest safely.
author: .izik

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's skull are filled to the brim with a toxic liquid. It drops them while in flight to debilitate prey and leave them helpless to avoid it swooping down to devour them.
author: sk372

entry: For unclear reasons, POKENAME tend to lurk near graveyards and related memorials. It appears that they are able to obtain some of the memories of anyone they suck blood from, including their own brethren.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME nests in power substations, where it bites into wires to absorb electricity. Its presence often causes localized blackouts.
author: .izik

entry: They work together to bring down prey and feed on their blood. Each POKENAME is not satisfied until it has completely drained 100 victims.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Using electrical currents and their own magnetic fields, POKENAME fly around ad high speeds. They feed on any prey caught within their gaping maws by siphoning any electrical energy within them, even those of the brain.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME avoids nesting near water and flies for days in search of arid landscapes. Its stamina is remarkable, even in harsh desert conditions.
author: .izik

entry: It stalks in arctic caves. When hunting, it covers its face with its hair and wraps its wings around itself to appear less threatening.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME glides from its home near a mountain's plateau, screeching loudly at other predators who get too close. Its cries can be heard from up to ten miles away.
author: .izik

entry: Without warning, POKENAME will suddenly dive from atop a tree onto unsuspecting prey. It will relentlessly drain their prey of blood before finding a tree to climb up to and nest.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME rapidly flap their tiny wings whenever they're excited, making a high-pitched cry as they do. If they become too enthusiastic about whatever has them worked up, they start to spit fire from their gaping mouth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: By keeping its mouth closed, POKENAME appears far smaller and less threatening than it truly is. It waits patiently for prey to draw near before swallowing it whole. When confronted by predators, it launches fireballs to create an escape route.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME coils itself around stalactites to sleep, using its spiny body as a deterrent. The sharp quills keep potential threats at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scales cave walls using its claws and talons, finding a comfortable nook to hide in while waiting for prey. When it spots a target, POKENAME uses its arms to glide down and ambush the foe with a loud screech and toxic bite.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME hides behind the naturally formed barriers of its cave home. When a foe gets too close, POKENAME will jump out, widen its stance, extend out its winged arms, and stick its toxic tongue out to intimidate the opponent.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Sitting on high cave ledges, POKENAME observe travelers passing through its territory. With a wave of its hand and a flap of its wings, Zubat will stir and fly towards the traveler and attack. It's rare for POKENAME to enter combat themselves.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Although it is weak, POKENAME can produce a bloodcurdling scream that scares away the toughest of foes. It is often found in aquatic caves.
author: canada

entry: POKENAME's arms are too weak to act as true wings, its eyes are underdeveloped, and its ears are small and immobile. This Pokémon must be watched carefully, or its habit of biting will get it into danger it cannot handle.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME dance and twirl so gracefully and peacefully under the moonlight that, for a long time, there were many who did not believe the research confirming POKENAME was a bloodsucker like Golbat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME bites into oil barrels and consumes the fluid that flows out. This fuel is mixed with its toxic glands for powerful poison-based attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal, hanging in dense jungle trees during the day. They drain the color from their prey when feeding, leaving grayscale husks behind wherever they go.
author: dolly_cholli

entry: Chefs in Sandgem Town serve fried POKENAME wings as a delicacy. These wings are spiced with cayenne pepper and paired with Watmel Berry jam.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's powerful jaws allow it to chop down a cedar tree with a single bite. It uses the wood to build elaborate dens near rivers.
author: .izik

entry: Rural villagers once enlisted POKENAME to pound mochi with its precise strikes. This practice was vital in creating their traditional festive desserts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts in shallow waters, swallowing multiple Staryu in one gulp. Its voracious appetite makes it a dominant predator.
author: .izik

entry: The wings of a POKENAME are too small to fly with and often chafe against the leaves sprouting on their back. Whenever they are attacked, vines sprout from the flower on their back to grapple the assailant.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers and devours cave vines in large quantities using its massive second mouth. It stores excess food in its den for later.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resides among large stalagmites, blending into the shadows to avoid predators. It only emerges at night to hunt.
author: .izik

entry: Its wings are incredibly strong and can support its body weight. It will quietly flap the wings while it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can stretch its elastic maw to envelop entire Berry branches. It uses this method to strip all the fruit in one motion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's eternally-gaping maw allows it to swallow large amounts of prey in a single gulp. Its wing-like fins make it a surprisingly fast swimmer, making it easier to prey on entire schools of fish.
author: sk372

entry: Some POKENAME variants lack wing-like fins and have smaller fangs, resulting in reduced speed and aggression. These wide-mouthed specimens content themselves with floating around and swallowing whatever swims into their maw.
author: sk372

entry: The twig-like appendage on POKENAME's head turns dark red when warm. While hunting, it emits a Lansat Berry-like aroma to attract prey.
author: .izik

entry: As a method of hunting, a strange facsimile of cliffside terrain extends from POKENAME's mouth as it lies down. Once enough small unsuspecting creatures have gathered and perched, it chomps down and swallows them all at once.
author: sk372

entry: Contrary to popular belief, male POKENAME do not drink blood. They play-fight with their siblings from a young age to practice using their fangs and venomous horn.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME will often congregate around flooded caverns. Their newly evolved eyes imbue them with powerful night vision, which they use to hunt above and below the waters.
author: snookerron

entry: POKENAME uses its magnetic nose to detect metal objects on nighttime travelers. Once it identifies a target, it waits for the perfect moment to strike when they're off guard.
author: .izik
