entry: POKENAME stores gems and trinkets in its cheeks to protect its treasures from rivals. It scours the seafloor for discarded objects, often mistaking human trash for valuables.
author: jaminmcready

entry: After consuming amethyst, POKENAME's body sparks uncontrollably for a full day. Others of its kind tend to huddle around it during this period to absorb the loose electricity rather than let it go to waste.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its x-ray night vision to avoid hikers in the caves it lives in. Rarely it will emerge to gift gems to hikers that respect the caves.
author: bitterchemicalhaze

entry: POKENAME hides in abandoned mineshafts, nibbling on as many gemstones as it can find. Trying to take any of its gems is said to bring endless misfortune.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have rocky plates that sparkle with the many gems embedded within them. They get angry when they see another Pokémon break rocks and will charge at them given the opportunity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It crunches through rocks and boulders in search of hidden gems. With its huge jaws, turning hard gems into absorbable nutrients is almost effortless.
author: alliveir

entry: Its wings vibrate to produce ultrasonic waves that charge its bright eyes. When charged, its eyes glitter and fire precise beams to cut raw gemstones.
author: alliveir

entry: POKENAME's body is almost entirely made up of crystal. POKENAME have started to live deep in underwater caves to avoid being hunted for its crystals by humans.
author: jestersqueak

entry: POKENAME fashions its most precious gems into glittering drones using various metals. These drones then help it find more gems, or aid it in battle.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME loves to experiment with different gem combinations with its drones. The one it likes the most is often upgraded far beyond the others.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME will sneak into caves alongside miners. If it spots a large gem on the ground, it will lie on it and disguise itself as a pile of rocks, so it can eat it later without interruption.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The small flowers you can see inside of POKENAME's crystals are known as 'Amethyst Roses', rare flowers said to have grown inside of these crystals. These Pokémon often comfort lost Pokémon and even take care of them.
author: imagine1.

entry: The flame that burns at the tip of its tail is an indication of which gems it has recently eaten. If it does not eat enough jewels, the fire on its tail will grow dim and weak.
author: thehobomice

entry: POKENAME often hoards evolution stones, which is one reason Pokémon such as Clefable and Ninetales are extremely rare in the wild. This Pokémon will start a fight over any possession it covets, even those belonging to other POKENAME.
author: giggity._.

entry: POKENAME's body is a chaotic cluster of gems it's consumed. It can reveal the gem on top of its head to distract other gemstone-eaters into leaving their food unguarded.
author: hophoppip

entry: With arms formed of crystalline roses, this Pokémon cuts a striking figure in the dark caves it inhabits. Within its flowers lies a potent venom for anyone greedy enough to dare pluck them.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: Long ago, humans gave gemstone offerings to the mouth of a cave inhabited by POKENAME. They hoped that buying its favour would convince it to leave their families alone. Some communities still do this.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME covers the precious treasures it hoards in its lair with mold and moss to hide them from curious eyes. POKENAME always carries the gem it loves most with it and defends it from others by releasing urticating spores.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME floats silently through the air, seeking out those it deems to be overworked. If they meet its gaze, its eyes begin to spin in place and gently lull the person to sleep.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It digs branching holes in caves using its sharp claws in search of food--raw gems. It also likes to stalk Carbinks, with just its eyes glinting around corners.
author: elite01.

entry: These creatures protect their feeding grounds not with martial arts or fire, but rather with a calm, confident demeanor, which intimidates most foes.
author: houndrys.

entry: The membranes of POKENAME's wings take on the luster of its gemstone diet, with more multicolored wings elevating its status within its colony. When a swarm of POKENAME fly on a full moon, their iridescent wings can brighten the area like day.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It's said that long ago, a greedy Sableye tried to steal the mask of a Yamask. This incident caused it to be turned into POKENAME as a punishment.
author: eminemace

entry: POKENAME are considered pests for jewelry stores. They nibble on gems, causing the stones to buckle in their settings. This leads to lost gemstones.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is only found in the shiniest caves with the most treasures and gemstones. In those caves, it camouflages itself to wait for unsuspecting treasure hunters.
author: pokebio

entry: Even if they come across a gem their tusks break against, they will still gnaw on them endlessly until either their teeth break or the gem breaks. Their tusks regrow clad in gem-like crystals that match many of the gems they eat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME feed entirely on precious stones and crystals. They use their tusks to carve pieces from larger formations that they come upon whilst digging through the ground.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME consumes gemstones to power up, with larger and more cleanly cut gems supplying more power. It is theorized to be a mining unit from an ancient civilization due to its powerful claws that it uses to dig through solid rock.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME consumes gemstones to power up, with larger and more cleanly cut gems supplying more power. It is theorized to be a mining unit from an ancient civilization due to its powerful claws that it uses to dig through solid rock.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its strong beak to pry aquamarine from cave walls. Once freed, it shatters the gem before eating it with glee.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts for all sorts of valuable items to store in its mouth. If it consumes too much however, it will become grounded for weeks on end.
author: mistymagius

entry: A popular theory has been floating around that suggests this fusion is the reincarnation of an evil king that ruled Hoenn long ago.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME's skin takes on the shade and texture of the gemstones it eats. It hides in pitch-black caves to ambush other gem-encrusted Pokémon, even others of its own kind, which it feeds upon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are the primary predators of Carpede and also often fight with them for territory due to both species' desire to feed on precious minerals. Their feet are sharp and strong, allowing them to quickly burrow through hard rock.
author: infinex21

entry: In deep lightless tunnels, POKENAME is constantly in search of gems for its next meal. Its crystalline horns and tail smash through bedrock with ease.
author: teravolt

entry: POKENAME is extremely ravenous, feasting on any gemstones they can get in their mouths. Their gargantuan jaws enable them to burrow through caves with relative ease.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME is very possessive of the precious minerals lining the cave it resides in, potentially because it feeds on such minerals. It breathes a freezing air upon solid rock and solid gems before attempting to bite into them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is active at night, and its crystals are capable of absorbing moonlight. The stored energy makes those who get too close fall ill. Come daytime, their symptoms miraculously fade.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's dance changes subtly based on the type of gem it most recently consumed. If it eats a topaz, it can spin like a ballerina for hours without resting.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides gems it finds deep within landfills, concealed among the garbage. It frequently forgets where it buries them.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon lives in deep underground rivers where gemstones are plentiful. Swimming in packs, POKENAME will jump out of the water and clamp its powerful jaws down onto the gems to break them into pieces that it and the pack can consume.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME often bury themselves in sand, using the treasure in their mouth to lure prey close. However, light often reflects off their teeth and eyes, ruining their plans.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Travelers carrying jewelry often become victims of POKENAME's thievery. It pilfers the shiny gems from them to decorate the stump it inhabits, entranced by their color and reflective nature.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a guardian of subterranean environments, often causing trouble for mining operations that dig too deep. It is said to curse anyone who removes even a single gemstone from its caverns.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME's ears are lined with a crystalline coating that resonates with the frequencies it produces, causing a high-pitched tone that causes severe hearing damage in anyone who gets too close.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are solitary POKENAME, hiding away in treacherous caverns. It emits a loud, eerie frequency from its ears that induces an overwhelming sense of fear in its victims.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME searches caverns for beautiful gemstones to decorate its puffy plumage in hopes to attract a mate. The more gems it collects, the less capable POKENAME is at sustained flight, forcing it to become more adept at defensive combat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Theory suggests Sableye will gather precious gemstones to construct a golem.  It's tasked with protecting the hoard when they go and gather more gems.
author: tokenoracle

entry: Said to have originated from Ultra Plant, POKENAME obsessively collects whatever shiny, precious stones it can discover. It hoards wherever it wants, and none dare to resist it.
author: beatdoof

entry: It is unwise to try and steal POKENAME's jewel, as it will show no mercy to anyone that enters its cave. If you do end up with the jewel, it is said that your entire bloodline will be cursed with misfortune.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME locates sunken treasure on the ocean floor and rests beside it. Should anyone attempt to loot its hoard, it strikes with Astonish.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lure geologists into caves with crystals. It then captures the humans and traps them in a underground cavern from which most never escape.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME often lures and captures geologists with its pre-evolution, Sableanie. POKENAME keeps track of the humans, punishing those who try to escape.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's body is composed of tiny crushed gemstones. It crushes any new gems it finds in its mouth to add to its form.
author: .izik

entry: The more fungi POKENAME consumes, the larger and more vibrant the crystals growing on its back become. Trainers are experimenting with different mushrooms in its diet to see how many different kinds of gems it can grow.
author: sk372

entry: With its alluring voice, it'll captivate anyone close enough to listen. It'll use that distraction to steal from victims.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's mane grows as it gains more gems. It will not stop collecting gems, even when it's weighed down by them.
author: ohok3441

entry: When threatened, POKENAME changes forms to fight. Foes will leave the battle with bites, scratches, and bruises.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME is protective of its allies, throwing itself into danger to keep them safe. Unfortunately, it's difficult to befriend in the first place.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's body is studded with a variety of minerals that sparkle faintly. Its powerful jaws easily crush hardened gemstones, its favorite food.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME scavenge abandoned castles for forgotten treasures to feed on, although they are rarely seen moving since they hide underneath dishware if they know people are near.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME's body is made of gemstones that are considered to be the most precious known to mankind, and the sight of it is said to be so alluring that those who see it can't look away. It's drawn to precious gems, especially those from Alola.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME gets so hungry for the gems of its own body that it regularly takes bites out of them. Sometimes it loses control and eats itself entirely until disappearing, taking weeks before fully recovering.
author: epping_forest

entry: When a Sableye sheds its outer skin, POKENAME steals it. It uses geokinesis to form the skin into a tough vehicle, protecting its soft insides from harm.
author: hushpuppygirl

entry: POKENAME consume mushrooms as their sole food, though they are particular about the color of these mushrooms as if color alone affects the taste. Oddly, the mushrooms consumed affect the growth and colors of the crystals upon them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a purple moss that grows more vibrant the more gems it consumes. It shows a strong preference for topaz above all others.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are being used more and more by mining companies as they pivot away from picks and dynamite. A shoulder-tackle from POKENAME is strong enough to pulverize obsidian.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME often use their twigs to turn normal rocks into gemstones. Gems produced this way are said to be harder than diamonds.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME travel to different caves, searching for raw gems both for sustenance and to add to their magical wand. They are an eerie sight for cave explorers, their teeth and eyes flashing in the dark.
author: vic1312

entry: The coins on the neck of a POKENAME fall off as it hops around caves. It's a common belief that acquiring one of these coins brings good luck.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Miners have to compete with POKENAME for sapphires, as they can quickly feast on a multitude of sapphire veins in minutes. Should they find a scuffed sapphire, they will freeze water around it to use as a projectile.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: When first discovered, POKENAME was poached due to its eyes resembling fantastic gems. Though this was quickly realized to be false, enough poaching had been done to cause the already-rare species to become critically endangered.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects gems and stores it within its gourd-shaped body. Its wails can be heard inside abandoned mineshafts, where it searches for gems.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stuffs gems, gold, and anything shiny into its sagging, shed skin. When its hoard becomes too big, the contents will tear through, forcing the POKENAME to abandon its treasures until it can shed another layer of skin.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME adores its crystals, having collected them over time. If someone tries to take its crystals, it will fly into a rage, only stopping when it gets revenge.
author: chaotic_aspergers

entry: POKENAME's head covering is as hard as diamonds. It delves into caves searching for precious stones, unafraid of falling rocks and attacks from above.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME often dance erratically to deter people from approaching mineshafts in caves. These mineshafts are full of crystals that POKENAME hoard and devour.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME lives deep beneath the surface, the high heat and pressure causing crystals to form within its body. It will only come up to the surface on the darkest night of the year.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME glides through cave systems, pulsing with a faint purple glow. When it spots a gem cluster, it crashes into it and devours the shattered pieces.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoy eating rocks and spitting them out as a sort of blown glass. Finding one of these sculptures could bring you into a large sum of money.
author: thatguy4115

entry: It chews through rock effortlessly while seeking out gemstones, its favorite food. However, POKENAME much prefers to steal from miners' gem caches, and are considered nuisances.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's mating displays are very colorful and elaborate. It spends tens of hours searching for the shiniest things it can find and decorates its nest with them, hoping to attract a mate. Some larger displays are advertised as tourist diving spots.
author: _pixelar_

entry: After eating garnets, POKENAME's howls grow ten times louder. It seeks these gems out in caves to compete with other members of its pack.
author: .izik

entry: Its diamond claws can cut through stone — perfect for spelunking through the caves to find precious gems that it can snatch.
author: diriector_doc

entry: When POKENAME finds a really large gem, it will protect it at all costs. Sometimes, the determination in its eyes is enough to drive intruders away.
author: diriector_doc

entry: POKENAME live deep within caves, using the spikes on their tails to mine through the stone in search of gems to eat. By absorbing their minerals, they harden the spikes along their bodies.
author: santon5512

entry: The brilliant gem spines growing out of its motionless body make an appetizing target for Sableye. Apparently, though, they do not taste as good as natural gems, deterring would-be predators.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME's proboscis is surprisingly tough – it can pierce gemstones and jewels to feed off the minerals in them. The luster of its diamond-like wings grows brighter the more it drains out of gems, sometimes making it prey for other POKENAME.
author: notadoctor75

entry: It tucks itself away in caves and attaches rocks to its body for camouflage until the only thing visible is its glinting gem-eyes. Within POKENAME's body, the heat and pressure are intense enough for it to form diamonds.
author: imaginita

entry: The glittering white powder POKENAME scatters from its wings, causing gemstones in cave walls to light up. This glow can illuminate a cave for weeks.
author: .izik

entry: When burying itself in cave floors, POKENAME causes beautiful crystal flowers to grow from the ground around it. These crystals dissolve within moments of it uprooting itself.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in the ground of dark caves where jewels are abundant. It absorbs small crystals, leading to its eyes becoming shinier.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME are infamous among quarry workers, as these Pokémon will not hesitate to steal precious gems. They often clash with Zubat as they fly through caves in search of gems to eat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is incredibly proud of its jewel-like wings and only seeks out the purest of gems to consume to ensure they keep their luster. When two POKENAME meet, they will sometimes pluck off bits of the other's wing to help keep a pristine shape.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME are notorious thieves who steal unguarded accessories. POKENAME use these necklaces, bracelets, and rings to build their nests. When their chicks hatch, the chicks will eat the jewels off the jewelry while waiting for their parents.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME will fly long distances to stash the treasure it has stolen. Those who are superstitious believe that if one of its coins drops onto their head, they'll have good luck.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME live on damp cave walls, not slipping thanks to the sticky oil they secrete from the ends of their legs. They won't move unless disturbed, pretending to be gemstones until the very last moment before scattering in fear.
author: milchik

entry: These Pokémon are found hovering above all sorts of cave reservoirs. With their wings and legs glowing in the dark, sparkling like precious gems, they lure Sableye into the water where they're less likely to escape a group of hungry POKENAME.
author: milchik

entry: Unsurprisingly, POKENAME is extremely greedy towards valuables. No coin nor jewel is safe from POKENAME's gluttonous thievery.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The noise POKENAME produces with its ears while sleeping changes entirely based on the size and type of gemstone it holds. Oddly, should it hold a tiny diamond, it makes no noise at all.
author: .izik

entry: It swings and scrapes its claws against stone to the point of exhaustion. This is a training regimen for POKENAME, as it yearns to be able to dig deep into caverns barehanded and unearth the finest of gems to collect.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME cannot resist the allure of anything that shines or glimmers, pouncing upon such items in order to claim them. Wild POKENAME use their tails' claws to chip away at large gemstones to feed on the pieces, which also keeps said claws sharp.
author: infinex21

entry: The moment POKENAME spots a glittering object, an irresistible urge to claim it takes over, driving it to battle if necessary. It keeps the claws at the tip of its tail razor-sharp by scratching the rock walls of the caves where it makes its den.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME meditate for long periods of time to ensure they are well-rested before roaming into caves to search for gems. By punching chunks of rocks out of cave walls, they unearth gems to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Gems POKENAME touches become charged with high amounts of electricity. Even brief contact with them can send a Mawile flying.
author: .izik

entry: A natural-born hoarder, POKENAME will get its claws onto any valuables it can find. When it senses something to steal, the gems lining its body glow and light up the surrounding area to make finding hidden trinkets easier.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: A natural-born hoarder, POKENAME will get its claws onto any valuables it can find. When it senses something to steal, the gems lining its body glow and light up the surrounding area to make finding hidden trinkets easier.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: POKENAME loves to take shiny stuff and stick it to its fur. It also sheds some glittering dust that sticks to furniture, making it very annoying to keep as a pet.
author: nugamallow

entry: The more sapphires POKENAME consumes, the stronger its electrical powers become. It will search caves all night for even a single taste of these gems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME focuses its electricity into its gem-like eyes during battle. It can release bursts powerful enough to send a Larvitar flying.
author: .izik

entry: The light from POKENAME's tail mimics the color of the gem it most recently consumed. The size of the gem also determines the intensity of the glow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's jewels refract light in dazzling, colorful displays. They lure in Volbeat to amplify the shine of their gems, wanting all to bask in their beauty.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's powerful stomach acid dissolves gemstones extremely fast. This allows it to eat large crystals with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME surrounds its nest with the same crystal spikes adorning its body, coating both with a poison that causes severe nausea. These spikes were found to have been used to create weaponry in the distant past.
author: chibitales

entry: Deep inside caves, Trainers can hear POKENAME eating large crystals residing inside the walls. If they toss some gemstones into its mouth, it will spit up some reserves to share.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: The red crystals on POKENAME's back become intensely hot should they fall off, though they remain cool while attached. They retain this heat for up to 24 hours after falling.
author: .izik

entry: A vicious and greedy bully, POKENAME's obsession with shiny objects leads it to attempt to steal the jewels off of Spoink heads. Due to the latter's dependence on it to survive, POKENAME is often hunted for the sake of Spoink preservation.
author: sk372

entry: Towns by caverns often tell stories about POKENAME to scare children and keep them away from the caves. When POKENAME drag their claws along the rocky walls, it creates a horrid sound.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME strikes cave walls with its sharp tail to knock loose zircon. It attempts to eat the gems before they hit the cave floor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's crystal fangs are able to pierce the toughest gemstones, absorbing them into their bodies. They will sharpen the blades on their tails along their fangs, keeping both sharp.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME hoards gems it finds on beaches, whether already visible in the sand or dug up by themselves with their pincers. It can live in impure water.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME emit a bright light from their many gems, each capable of hypnotizing others. It is rumored that they were trained to be guards by ancient civilizations.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By angling its body just right, POKENAME can refract sunlight to start fires. POKENAME only takes this form after being in sunny weather. Because it is a cave-dwelling Pokémon, this form is rarely seen.
author: .realthree

entry: The crystal surrounding POKENAME's head is filled with extremely mineral-rich water. It is rarely possible to find this Pokémon in caves that are large enough to have their own weather systems.
author: .realthree

entry: A wild POKENAME relies on food from a mother Walrein or scraps left by other Pokémon. POKENAME compete relentlessly for food and snatch what they can, leaving runts to struggle through harsh winters.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have powerful senses of touch and smell and use them to hunt and communicate with other POKENAME and Sealeo. When full, they happily slap their fins against their firm bellies.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is almost entirely colorblind, so instead of jewels like Sableye, its diet consists of smaller Pokémon that dwell deep under the sea where no light reaches; it can stay underwater for days at a time before coming up for air.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Underwater caverns studded with sparkling gems are where POKENAME resides. Its powerful jaws let it crunch down on the jewels as its favorite snack.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gets nourishment by consuming jewels within the caves it inhabits. It sniffs them out with its jewel-like nose, which glows brightly once it has detected nearby gems to eat.
author: sk372

entry: The gems that hang from the wings of POKENAME jingle as they fly. Due to the shape of their eyes, aristocrats often gift POKENAME for romantic occasions.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME nibbles on underwater jewels for sustenance. The color of the gems affects the color of its lightning; a school of POKENAME that have all eaten different jewels could create a colorful electric storm.
author: sk372

entry: A fully charged POKENAME emits visible sparks from its gem-like eyes. It lives in deep crystal caverns, where entire groups feed on gemstones and fill the cave with shimmering colors by passing electricity through the crystal formations.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's gem eyes blink rapidly while draining electricity from mechanical equipment. It latches its mouth to the side of devices, draining their power swiftly.
author: .izik

entry: Its fists are coated in a layer of diamonds, which makes its punches absolutely devastating. It desires precious gemstones and will destroy entire mountains in search of them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME subsists on jewels found in the ocean depths. It breathes a corrosive poison that softens and melts the gems it finds and makes them easier for it to consume.
author: sk372

entry: It collects gems and gnaws on them until they are shaped like bones. When it is excited, the crystals on its body are hot to the touch.
author: greystorm101

entry: When POKENAME shake their bodies, there's a chance one of its gems will fall off. These gems are warm to the touch and are often used in high-end plates and other dishes.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Its intense avarice for metals and gems is only matched by the intensity of its flames. It sometimes 'collects' its Trainer as a twisted form of love.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME obsessively hoards as much wealth as it can find. If even a single coin is stolen, it will rampage across the land until it is returned.
author: rakanadyo

entry: POKENAME believes itself to be the ruler of the underground caves it lives in. It's incredibly territorial, and even gets into fights over the smallest of gems.
author: gronkissimo

entry: POKENAME offers dubious advice to lost travellers to keep them wandering for hours. It is easily placated with the gift of small gems or a shiny spoon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Thanks to a diet comprised of very specific gems, POKENAME can flex its muscles to a ludicrous size. It loves the attention from awestruck bystanders.
author: 8xviktor

entry: There have been many accounts of POKENAME using their slings to take down larger foes. Groups of POKENAME will often engage in friendly competition with one another.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME mesmerizes prey with its hypnotic, glowing eyes before striking. When threatened, it withdraws into its shell, which is said to be as hard as the precious stones it consumes.
author: zaffery88

entry: POKENAME grows crystals from its body for a variety of uses including decoration, protection, and digging tools. When the crystals become chipped, it eats them to regenerate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hunts gemstones to eat and build energy for evolution. Depending on its diet, in rare cases it can start to build a golden sheen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hunts gemstones to eat and build energy for evolution. Depending on its diet, in rare cases it can start to build a golden sheen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME grows crystals from its body for a variety of uses including decoration, protection, and digging tools. When the crystals become chipped, it eats them to regenerate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows deep into the earth searching for the most beautiful gemstones to devour. The more it eats, the more extravagant its hide becomes until it becomes encrusted in crystals and evolves.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows deep into the earth searching for the most beautiful gemstones to devour. The more it eats, the more extravagant its hide becomes until it becomes encrusted in crystals and evolves.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME burrows deep into the earth searching for the most beautiful gemstones to devour. The more it eats, the more extravagant its hide becomes until it becomes encrusted in crystals and evolves.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's gemstone shell is highly valued by traffickers, but nobody was able to even scratch it. It's the only thing POKENAME will fiercely fight for.
author: epping_forest

entry: The diet of POKENAME determines the color and material of its carapace. The more beautiful the gemstones comprising its hide, the more POKENAME will need to defend itself from other Sableye species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME crawls along cave floors in search of gems to eat. It moves so slowly and uses so little energy that one small gem can take months to digest, keeping it satiated the entire time.
author: alestrius

entry: As gemstones are non-magnetic, sometimes POKENAME struggles to attract other POKENAME with which it can evolve.
author: diriector_doc

entry: POKENAME dwell in the darkest of caves, where they pull out gems from within in the ground by magnetizing them. Miners who seek out precious ores utilize POKENAME's magnetic ability.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: An odd glowing eye branches from POKENAME's singular head that it uses to see gems and threats through walls. The eye can also channel Psychic power, allowing POKENAME to levitate and reach food high in the caverns.
author: thordemidgard

entry: POKENAME greedily consumes any shiny gemstones it comes across. It doesn't appear to need them for nourishment, but merely because it enjoys feeling beautiful as the consumed gems float to its surface and decorate its exterior.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to be extremely greedy. They steal valuable objects wherever they can find them and hoard them within its toxic body.
author: theartemis1

entry: The clarity of a POKENAME's gemstone shell often reflects its health; the shinier the shell, the healthier the fusion.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME can be found in underwater caves, making pearls. If threatened, they can launch their pearl using their tongue.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The bodies of POKENAME are shrouded in glittering clouds made of pulverized gemstones. It is said that they can dominate the minds of greedy people with a single look.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME has a gem-encrusted tongue that is very sensitive to taste. It thrives in darkness, the ruby on the POKENAME's chest acting as a lure to catch unsuspecting prey.
author: jojojax164

entry: If you discover large caverns or deep tunnels lacking all shiny minerals and jewels, these incredibly rare Pokémon have likely passed through previously. POKENAME seek out these materials to consume, eventually causing their bodies to glitter, too.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This is an intelligent fusion that uses hypnosis to put Rock-type Pokémon to sleep, then eats them. Its neck fur is made of pure, hard diamond.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: The POKENAME feeds on shiny rocks and minerals. They are often seen in treasure rooms.
author: terminatphilippe

entry: POKENAME are often seen in treasure rooms, feeding on shiny rocks and minerals to sustain themselves. They hoard treasure and snap at anyone who tries to take it.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME are well-known for their intense greed, doing anything in their power to add to their collection. POKENAME have even snuck onto cruise ships to steal coins and wallets.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are usually found at the very bottom of oceans. They can light up their crystals to easily travel along the dark sea floor.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's epidermis is coated in a paralytic poison; predators quickly learn to stay away from it as a result. The arrangement of darker spots on its body is unique to the individual POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It strips pine trees' bark off in great quantities with its mouth. Once it has several pounds gathered, it will eat it all in under five minutes.
author: .izik

entry: Using their feelers, POKENAME remain keenly aware of all else around them. If anything touches their feelers, they explosively release electrical energy all about.
author: infinex21

entry: Though they can move individually, the separate pieces of POKENAME prefer to move as a singular unit, following behind the leader of the clutch. When resting, the other five surround the sixth to protect it from harm.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's strong stomach lets it consume even the most poisonous of mushrooms. The digestion helps give the venom in its claws and stingers even more potency.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a feisty personality and will charge horn-first at anything with little provocation. The horn contains a mild venom that weakens the muscles of anything that gets stung.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is incredibly protective of its egg, using its powerful venom to fend off attackers. While incredibly potent, its venom can be used as a universal anti-venom.
author: mistymagius

entry: A solitary Pokémon, POKENAME keeps to itself in the wild and eats from small flower patches. If confronted, it spreads a very potent paralyzing poison from its wings.
author: sk372

entry: In battle, POKENAME moves with agility and stays on the defensive. Its scythes are tipped with venom, so it waits for the perfect moment to strike and deliver a painful dose to its foe.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's venom is mild, but its pincer-like stingers have a powerful grip. It grabs prey and holds them tight, constantly injecting venom until they're totally paralyzed and an easy meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a large antenna on its head with which it can locate vibrations in its immediate vicinity. It can eat even the most poisonous plants.
author: chorb33

entry: The twin antennae on POKENAME's head double as stingers. Its fierce aggression is only limited by its lack of limbs, as it goes out of its way to sting anyone nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attacks anything it thinks it can eat from the sky before using its saw-like jaws and poison to finish its prey. Avoid leading it to urban areas at all costs.
author: torterraguy26

entry: POKENAME frequently challenge foes they believe they can take down with their venomous fangs. Their fangs are shed along with their scales every night. Their venom becomes more potent when their fangs grow back.
author: infinex21

entry: They use the glow of their crystal orbs to lure prey and pounce to neutralize them with their venomous fangs. They coil upon themselves and launch themselves like springs to catch others off guard.
author: infinex21

entry: The feelers upon their heads can sense the slightest changes in the air, so they are keenly aware of when the weather is about to change. They scatter poisonous scales from their wings as they fly.
author: infinex21

entry: During the day, POKENAME sleeps on poisonous plants to absorb their toxicity. It uses this at night to go on a fierce hunt.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME live in large flocks, feeding on small seeds and berries. They carry poison in their beaks, and while one sting isn't lethal, it can be incredibly dangerous if you are swarmed by a flock of them.
author: mistymagius

entry: These small Bug Pokémon are so often trampled that they have developed irritable temperaments as a result. They will rapidly bite enemies with their poisonous mandibles, though the poison is only capable of inciting an itch.
author: infinex21

entry: Though POKENAME is small, it has few predators. The electricity it discharges lingers and acts like a neurotoxin.
author: .realthree

entry: Covered in soft, fluffy fibers, POKENAME appears harmless. Touching its wool causes intense numbness that lasts for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses sensors on its head and tail to discover prey. The tail is also covered in a buoyant oil to help catch prey on water. When it catches the located prey, it will inject venom through its bite to paralyze the now hopeless prey.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: POKENAME is an expert hunter, able to sense drowning prey in water with both great hearing and highly tuned feelers. If another POKENAME is struggling in the water, others will help by blowing air bubbles.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: POKENAME is highly opportunistic when it comes to procuring food: it waits until it spies another Pokémon capture prey, before swooping in at high speeds to poison and paralyze the predator so it can eat the hunted meal instead.
author: sk372

entry: When anything touches its antennae, POKENAME goes into a rage, running around and shooting Water Gun at anything that moves until it faints. In some regions, people trap POKENAME in arenas and bet on how long it will last before it faints.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has toxic points on the end of its tail and feathers. It uses them to poison humans and Murkrow in order to render them helpless and steal precious items from them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rely on agility and instinct to avoid predators. Cunning by nature, they poison small POKENAME and follow them until their demise before feeding.
author: notmax22

entry: POKENAME defends the flower on its back by sinking its venomous fangs into anyone who ventures too close. It is capable of releasing paralysis-inducing spores potent enough to ground even the Flying-type Pokémon in the surrounding area.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have poor eyesight, relying on their antennae to sense the world around them. When startled, they withdraw their bodies into their curled-up carapace, waiting out the danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME slumbers in snowdrifts, blending in with the terrain. If touched, it releases a sweat-like venom that can paralyze on contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a large poison sac attached to its body, which it uses to deliver potent venom when threatened. When feeling cornered, it grips its tail tightly, using it as an intimidation tactic to ward off potential threats.
author: rakunk

entry: One should be careful interacting with a POKENAME on their computer. When agitated, it has a venomous bite that will degrade whatever program it nips, and could potentially render the computer inoperable.
author: sk372

entry: It produces poison from the stingers on its tail, creating globs it flicks onto its antlers. It flings blobs of poison from both its tail and antlers when it feels threatened.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers who pass through bug-filled forests sometimes end up with kiss shaped marks. These are actually poisonous bug bites from POKENAME, but they are easily treatable.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME have a thick chitinous exoskeleton covering their body with separate segments to allow their tail to move easily. Their head is bulbous and patterned to dissuade larger Pokémon from attacking them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lives in the mountains, its tough carapace protecting it from falling rocks. It is very aggressive and will try to fight other Pokémon over food.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can swing its tail forward to strike opponents with its paralyzing spikes. When it can't reach the berries it loves to eat, it uses its tail as a step and then jumps on them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Both poison and electricity are stored and generated in POKENAME's tail. Stabbing others to poison them is common, but even being hit by its lightning bolts will leave a debilitating toxin marring the target's body.
author: sk372

entry: The feelers on its head allow it to sense vibrations in the air, as do its legs keenly sense vibrations through the ground. When it curls up in a ball, its hide becomes so tense that it can repel most physical attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its antennae to pick up radio signals to gather information on the locations of prey. If it encounters a huge hoard, it erratically wiggles around to make its movements unpredictable while dishing out toxic bites with its fangs.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME rely on the feelers on their heads and tails to sense vibrations in the air, which alert them to potential predators. They nest upon and within tall trees, which they can scale thanks to the small hooks on their hands and feet.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sprays a highly corrosive sap from the leaves on its arms. This acid is strong enough to leave deep grooves in boulders on even brief contact.
author: .izik

entry: The feeler on its tail is how it senses its surroundings; this feeler often twitches or rocks side to side like a metronome. It quickly reacts to an unknown presence by spitting weak fireballs at the source.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME provokes its foes, taunting them to approach so that it can strike them with venomous fangs and claws. This plan can backfire, however, leaving them vulnerable to a counterattack they weren't prepared for.
author: porterofgames

entry: Using the feelers on POKENAME's head and tail, it can sense movement around it and prevent predators from ambushing it. This heightened sense also gives POKENAME an advantage on locating foes and striking first with a powerful swipe of its claws.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The pink water POKENAME releases from its mouth is highly poisonous. Even a single drop on the skin can cause the victim to lose their sense of taste for weeks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is shy and not overly aggressive, but is quick to retaliate towards anything that spooks it. It uses psychically-launched venom from the spines on its forehead to poison anything that scares it before running off.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's antennae are extremely sensitive to vibrations in the air, so it can scan an area as it flies. A poisonous powder drops from its wings, causing minor harmful effects to those below it.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's resilience to the elements allows it to thrive in many corners of the world. Desert POKENAME enjoy a diet of cacti, while marshland POKENAME nibble away at ferns and nettles to survive.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME grazes on fruit tree leaves, leaking green toxin from its barbs. It only activates this defense when startled or cornered.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides along the jungle floors, waiting to ambush its prey with a poisonous bite. Its antennas detect movement in the air, while its wings feel vibrations on the ground, making it impossible to sneak up on.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME is extremely aggressive, frequently headbutting trees to dislodge leaves that it finds desirable. POKENAME consumes the fallen greenery to strengthen its shell.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The potent poison POKENAME possesses is due to its diet consisting mostly of poisonous berries and plants. Travelers often use it to suss out and consume dangerous plants to avoid getting poisoned while gathering food.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME secretes a very strong hallucinogenic when nervous, not too dissimilar to sweat. The perspirant is often sold illegally across the region at a high value.
author: big_clanker

entry: POKENAME's prickly, independent personality causes it to lash out at anything that approaches it. It blows a series of bubbles filled with a surprisingly potent poison as a way of warding off others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its venomous blade to prod and torment other Pokémon in the forest, targeting those weaker than itself. Once it sets its sights on a human, it harasses them relentlessly until their strength is fully spent.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In fall, POKENAME hoards dry leaves to eat. It will fight kin over leaf piles, spraying poison from its spiked back when challenged.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits globs of poisonous mucus on its cave walls that do not affect others of its kind. Touching this mucus can cause dizziness and massive blisters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's attitude towards others depends on the aura it senses from them. Weak auras result in it bullying them with its Poison Sting, while strong auras cause it to flee quickly to avoid a losing battle.
author: sk372

entry: The feelers on POKENAME are fine-tuned to sense emotions. When it wiggles them it can sense waves of fear, which tells it exactly which direction it shouldn't go in.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The toxin coursing through POKENAME's body carries an electrical charge. It spits this inky substance to shock and poison foes before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blast lightning from the feelers extending from their forehead and rear. They then attack their incapacitated prey with their huge, venomous claws.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME make loud chirps to communicate with one another across a forest, inhaling deeply and inflating to twice their size to make these noises. Their tendency to chirp at sunset makes it difficult to camp in regions where they make their home.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are clad in an armor-like chitin harder than iron, which grows even harder the more minerals they consume. The feelers on their heads sense and react to vibrations, be they in the ground or in the air.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is very aggressive, and it can be seen headbutting other Pokémon in territorial disputes. However, if its head is badly injured, its poison will start to pool under its carapace, causing it immense pain.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME use their many claws to hold onto foes and inject them with a burning venom via a bite. The feelers upon their heads move in ways correlative to their feelings; their feelers twitch when curious or tense up when agitated, for example.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME buries itself beneath almond trees, waiting for nuts to fall. It absorbs amygdalin from them to fuel its toxic secretions.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME's flowers conceal venomous stingers at their centers and layers of irritant pollen within their petals. The chitin lining their bodies is harder than tree bark, but it grows even tougher as they near evolution.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep marsh, headbutting nearby trees to knock down berries. Its spores are highly acidic and will slowly start to melt through anything it comes into contact with.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's membrane is made of a toxic material that is surprisingly safe to touch normally. However, if it is agitated, it will attack with its pointed horns and inject the poison directly, causing temporary nerve damage.
author: sk372

entry: While airborne, POKENAME spits globs of neurotoxin with alarming precision. In caves, swarms use this to overwhelm weakened prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts tiny creatures by lobbing webbing at them as if casting a net. Even if captured prey escapes, the webbing is coated with poison that will exhaust them in time and allow POKENAME to catch up.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME mark their territory by gnashing trees with their venomous tusks, leaving behind a corrosive poison that eats through bark and wood alike.
author: johnneh_

entry: POKENAME is incredibly aggressive and will perceive basically anything as a threat. It sprays boiling-hot acid from its antennae to attack, which leaves its victims in agonizing pain.
author: mistymagius

entry: After consuming fluorite, POKENAME's venom becomes twice as potent. During this period the venom turns a bright yellow and glows in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: A two-headed form of Venipede. They are exceptionally rare to find, as most don't live for very long.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: The fusion process causes POKENAME to develop additional body segments as well as increasing the potency of their venom. Their exoskeleton also becomes covered in extra spines, making them dangerous to touch.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The fusion process causes POKENAME to develop additional body segments as well as increasing the potency of their venom. Their exoskeleton also becomes covered in extra spines, making them dangerous to touch.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Something of a step between evolution stages, POKENAME retains mobility but loses some venom potency and the sturdiness of its shell. It skitters away from trouble, avoiding conflict until it can evolve further.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME brutally kills anything in its vicinity with its remarkable strength and venomous horns. The only exception seems to be other members of the Venipede family.
author: torterraguy26

entry: POKENAME communicate among themselves by clicking together their long feelers. They feed on the nutrients of plants by burrowing near them. Their antennae secrete a venom, making it dangerous to try and remove them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME becomes deeply sorrowful when music ends which is a major problem in clubs. Its tears carry a powerful toxin, and even a faint whiff can cause people nearby to collapse in seconds.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's poison reserves fill when it consumes discarded hazardous waste. This venom is frequently spat at prey to weaken them before it strikes with Clear Smog.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME detects scents in the water with the feelers on its head, allowing it to hone in on injured aquatic Pokémon. Once POKENAME is close enough to its prey, a flurry of gnashing serrated teeth quickly secures its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's hunting technique involves hit-and-run tactics. It bites to inject venom before quickly fleeing, stalking and waiting for the poison to run its course before picking off its weakened prey.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME possesses a stump, poison ivy mysteriously sprouts from it. The mechanism behind this remains unknown to researchers.
author: .izik

entry: The fruits on POKENAME's head are incredibly poisonous, and most that try to eat them will succumb to them in less than a day. The fruit smells sickly sweet, which lures certain Bug Pokémon to try and eat them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have eyes that are poorly adapted for seeing in daylight, so they rely on their keen hearing to navigate. They make high-pitched chirping noises that carry well through dense undergrowth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have eyes that are poorly adapted for seeing in daylight, so they rely on their keen hearing to navigate. They make high-pitched chirping noises that carry well through dense undergrowth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Toxic impurities are constantly produced and build up within POKENAME's body, causing it extreme discomfort. It releases the excess by unleashing beams of highly concentrated and caustic poison from its body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often used as a mode of transportation in urban areas. While quite reliable, it produces clouds of toxic smog as it drives.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME proudly shows off its vibrant scales, which act as a warning to would-be opponents. Its scales are laced in a powerful toxin that can debilitate its opponent in less than a minute.
author: mistymagius

entry: A unique type of poison concoction is produced from the tips of POKENAME's claws. Normally causing illness in those it scratches, if its claws scrape a gash into a tree, fungi begin growing in the scratch marks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME guards its fungal patches deep in cave systems with fierce intensity. Its claws hold a powerful venom that cause seizures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME acts as a two-faced trickster in the wild. If spotted by a larger creature, it pretends to flee in terror, then doubles back in order to leap at its foe when their guard is down and apply rapid venomous bites.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in dense rainforests, hiding amongst damp foliage. It will leap at prey from above, sinking its venomous claws into their heads until they are too weak to stand.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is not particularly aggressive, but its fur produces a highly poisonous secretion. It also has weak psychic powers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME hates being touched, as it will quickly prick its foe with its poisonous thorns before fleeing. It is exclusively nocturnal, using the dim lights from its belly to see in the dark.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are incredibly aggressive and will swarm anyone that enters their territory. The venomous barbs on their heads contain a powerful neurotoxin that can cause paralysis with a large enough dose.
author: mistymagius

entry: These Pokémon are extremely defensive, lashing out at anything that they perceive as a threat. The pad on their head has thousands of small spines that deliver a venom potent enough to paralyze bird Pokémon like Swellow.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are considered a blight in Pinwheel Forest. After consuming river moss, they destroy the rocks it grew on, causing an increase in bank erosion.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME spits a viscous blue poison at prey in branches to knock them down. For smaller prey, this venom can cause paralysis on contact.
author: .izik

entry: By utilizing the feelers on its rear and its head, it can sense the slightest changes in the air and adjust its flight trajectory accordingly. It eats twice its body weight daily, growing heavier as it draws closer to its evolution.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can sense the movements of potential prey in the air around it using its head feelers. Using the height advantage from its tree-top nest, POKENAME will dive bomb its prey and bite down on their body, injecting it with a paralyzing poison.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME has feelers to sense changes in its surroundings. When it seeks prey while flying, it swoops down without forethought.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's antennae can detect the presence of coins in a large radius. When it detects something, it will dart around excitedly, eager to scoop the coins up before anyone else.
author: evilgammon

entry: Tiny barbs extend from POKENAME's fists on impact to inject a strong venom. This venom causes delusions and fits of sneezing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scrapes the spines on its tail across the ground as a warning for others to stay away. These points contain a highly venomous toxin that only needs a single light scratch to leave larger Pokémon incapacitated.
author: sk372

entry: Upon latching onto a foe with its fangs, POKENAME injects a powerful venom that causes dizziness. Prolonged exposure can permanently damage a victim's equilibrium.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME purrs, toxins gather at the tip of its tail. When threatened, it lashes out, swinging the tail like a poisoned flail.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in colonies that collaborate with positive variants of their species to create balanced electrical currents. Forests that have air that feels charged with electricity may be a sign of this Pokémon's colony in the area.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: After engulfing and eating a meal, the poison glands in POKENAME's body go into overdrive. Once it finishes digesting, it typically expels a huge glob of highly-toxic excess liquid from its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: The poison-creating glands residing in its head give it massive headaches if too much is produced without release. It is forced to bite and inject anything it can with poison to relieve its own pain.
author: sk372

entry: Grasping onto a foe with its pincers allows POKENAME to inject them with a potent venom. It uses this ability to paralyze Corphish that are about to eat so that it can steal their food for itself.
author: sk372

entry: This unusual species produces a mild toxin that causes temporary, harmless rashes and a brief, fiery irritation on contact.
author: rykona

entry: The twin tips of its tail secrete a potent venom that is also highly flammable. Its claws secrete a weaker variant of this venom, though their claws are strong enough that this weaker venom rarely serves a purpose.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is covered in a toxic film which is irritating to the touch. If the pattern on its belly is punctured by an attack, it will secrete a more potent poison.
author: mistymagius

entry: The shell on its back is remarkably dense, which is seemingly why its body is so fit and muscular. The feelers on its head, and upon its shell, allow it to sense nearby movement.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are incredibly aggressive and will spew a mildly corrosive acid onto anything it deems a threat. When properly distilled, this chemical can be used to make extremely sour candy.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the ground, using its eyebrow-like antennae to detect vibrations above it. When it senses a Pokémon nearby, it punches them repeatedly, the stingers on its knuckles injecting a potent venom.
author: secondegg

entry: POKENAME's fire is fueled by its venom gland, which gives the fire a distinctive hue. It trots along rainy marshes where it rarely causes wildfires.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME uses its pointed beak to pierce through thick tree trunks, feeding on the small insects inside. However, its beak is coated in large amounts of poison and can be dangerous if a small Pokémon is pecked by it.
author: mistymagius

entry: By clacking its claws together, this Pokémon gets a better sense of its surroundings through echolocation and its tall feelers. It uses its claws to dig a burrow near streams and rivers.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have a mixture of thistle and maroon markings on their bodies, which marks them as poisonous to potential predators. They enjoy rolling down hills because the physical sensation of rolling gives them an adrenaline rush.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is usually motionless unless attacked or unless it spots prey. When it moves, it generates static electricity which it can store and later loose as Thunderbolts; this electricity dissipates as it lies still.
author: infinex21

entry: Densely-packed tendrils form a swirled shell around POKENAME's body to protect it while it develops. These vines are quite solid, and can lash out and wallop anything that gets too close for comfort.
author: sk372

entry: Once it gets tired of flying on its relatively fragile wings, it simply lands upside down and wheels along. The edges of its wings are much tougher than the spindly inside, allowing it to withstand rough terrain.
author: something_smith

entry: POKENAME are able to conjure invisible objects out of thin air that only the eye on their stomach can see. POKENAME are very fond of circular objects; they are especially interested in spinning motions.
author: kianjp2008

entry: Though its weighty carapace gives it low agility, POKENAME has potent defenses and offenses. The blades on its arms and head are sharp and venom-tipped, and even its wings are pointed enough to cause damage.
author: sk372

entry: The shell on POKENAME's head can open up, revealing rows of razor-sharp teeth. Its horns grip prey, pulling it into the shell to be devoured.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME roll down hills to avoid predators before crawling back to the same spot to eat leaves. Their mauve bodies make them easy to spot, so they hide in bushes whenever they see a predator nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Even when resting, it is curled upon itself like a wheel with its venomous spikes primed. It seems to only uncurl when it sheds its old skin and scales.
author: infinex21

entry: By curling upon itself, it can repel most attacks and deliver forceful counterattacks by rolling into enemies. It stores vast energy for its evolution, and its crystal orbs glow brightest on the eve of its evolution.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite how small their wings seem, they can fly high and for long times. They crash down onto foes by curling upon themselves like a giant, spiked wheel.
author: infinex21

entry: Highly toxic substances are formed in its abdomen through chemical processes. POKENAME uses this poison, lethal to humans, for hunting or defense.
author: chorb33

entry: It loves to curl up like a wheel and roll down mountains or hills, albeit with minimal regard for others. It will also curl up to defend itself with its venomous spikes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rolls through its habitat with burst of fire from its back to accelerate, leaving charred circles of undergrowth in its wake. Motorists have taken to it as a symbol of speed that they mount on the hood of their cars.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Highly toxic substances are formed in its abdomen through chemical processes. POKENAME uses this poison, lethal to humans, for hunting or defense.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME will lock talons at extreme heights before plummeting back to the ground to test the strength of their shells. This practice is the most common reason for injury in wild POKENAME.
author: drcew

entry: Their bulbous abdomens are surprisingly sturdy due to the amount of loose silk webbing they store within themselves. POKENAME can curl upon their large bodies and roll along walls and ceilings due to many small hooks lining their bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME usually floats on water without moving, using its senses to try and find prey without spooking them. The camouflage pattern makes POKENAME hard to see, allowing it to lash out at unsuspecting prey.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: When many POKENAME come together and spin quickly in the air, they can create tornadoes. They are very calm when they aren't in groups, and they enjoy naps.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME can oftentimes be found sitting on a muddy riverbank while sucking on its tail, staring off at nothing. This action helps it build resistances to other poisons since, when out of water, its body is covered in a highly toxic film.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Known for its mischievous pranks, POKENAME haunts victims from the shadows before it finds the perfect opportunity to strike. The spinning beads on its necklace have powerful hypnotic powers, able to put victims to sleep for up to 2 weeks.
author: kianjp2008

entry: From its claws, POKENAME secretes a red toxin that induces vomiting and fever. Once latched on, it won't release until the fluid is fully drained.
author: .izik

entry: When closed, its mouth helps complete a protective shell around its head. Timid despite its imposing appearance, POKENAME will bite attackers with its powerful jaws, while also delivering poison from the tips of its fangs.
author: sk372

entry: It usually crawls around at a slow pace, until it ducks into its shell.  Then it is able to roll across the ground to quickly escape from predators.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME's wings are coated in a corrosive poison that can eat through stone. It preys on Aron, using its powerful wings to slice through the environment and catch its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secretes a potent toxin through its lips. It weakens foes by peppering them with kisses before jabbing them with its horns.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME rolls down slopes at high speeds, then uncurls itself to unleash its electric attacks. Those shocked by one may have a hard time walking.
author: .realthree

entry: Due to their large appetites, POKENAME are constantly fighting with each other over prey. They will exploit the gaps in each other's thick carapace by jabbing their sharp horns into them.
author: mistymagius

entry: What appears to be an awkwardly-shaped body is a shell that it can withdraw inside of to protect itself. While withdrawn, it can spin at high speeds to move about and to ram into foes.
author: infinex21

entry: Between distinct actions, POKENAME's many limbs trail around in a circular pattern. It collects energy from network-connected devices.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME prefer to wait for prey rather than hunt prey down; they lie in wait by clinging to the sides of trees. When potential prey draws near, they drop onto them with their bulky bodies and quickly slash at them with Leaf Blade attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: While usually motionless, POKENAME form a ball to crash into opponents, spewing fire on impact. The resulting blaze leaves the ground scorched and smoldering.
author: kriznick

entry: It rolls into a ball and travels along paved roads. It perceives the tires of cars on the roads as rivals, and attacks at them with its long claws. Many insurance companies provide POKENAME protection.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It attacks with a flurry of poison-laced kicks. Wild POKENAME will not stop fighting until either it or its opponent faints; the longer the battle draws on, the more spirited POKENAME gets.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME dances in erratic tumbles, splashing venom across the ground. Its movements mark the edges of a toxic, defended territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its speed to ambush smaller prey. The rear antennas release excess energy built up so POKENAME doesn't overheat while chasing its target.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Often mistaken for stones, POKENAME rest by lakeshores, blending seamlessly with their surroundings. When thirsty, they roll to the water's edge, startling onlookers.
author: kriznick

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time sleeping and saving energy. If its two noses catch a whiff of approaching danger, it tucks its legs into its body and rolls away to safety.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers to keep itself sheathed and avoid combat where possible. If forced, it strikes with swirling, circular swings of its blade that deflect attacks and disorient foes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME mouths are formed of multiple segments, enabling them to open their mouths far wider than might be expected for a Pokémon their size. They have a venomous bite that they use to deter their foes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME remain in curled positions while waiting for evolution, relying on their hard-plated shell for protection. If threatened, they coil further into a wheel shape and, while their tail blazes with fire and poisonous spores, ram into the foe.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME doesn't move much, as it wants to keep its protective shell from falling apart. If it does fall off, it will hunt for a Caterpie nest to use the larvae's sticky silk to stick its shell back together.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sweats a poison that irritates the skin of anyone who touches it. Preferring solitude, it will roll to remote areas to find a safe place to sleep, away from any disturbances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is actually two Pokémon held together by an unknown source. When threatened they will both begin spinning against each other to build up enough friction to release massive stored up energy attacks.
author: kianjp2008

entry: POKENAME's blossoms emit a scent like Pecha Berries, masking their danger. A single touch can spread a fever-inducing poison through the skin.
author: .izik

entry: The circular markings on the liquid exterior of POKENAME can be shifted around at will. For self-defense, the core strikes these circles, which send out pulses of potent psychic energy on impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins rapidly as it drifts through forest skies, trailing poison behind it. Its motion is graceful but hazardous to those below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME used its wheel-like body to traverse small crevasses in the cave walls. It hunts in pure darkness, impaling its prey on its venomous horns.
author: mistymagius

entry: It can use its wheel-like feet to reach speeds of up to sixty miles per hour. Most of the time, however, it moves at a leisurely pace in order to conserve energy.
author: staghorn

entry: It's a Whirlipede that fused with itself, giving it more stability and speed. However, it sacrificed some of its maneuverability for these boosts.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can be spotted in the wild, blending in as other Bikers looking for a Pokémon battle. The rider is a facade and serves to lure prey close enough so that the wheels can strike, injecting poison into their target.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The big one in the middle is the leader of the pack. The small ones around it carry it around. They move around similarly to a car.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME grows red feathers in strange circular patterns across its body. These can be ground into a poisonous powder that only POKENAME can safely ingest.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME can swim at speeds of up to 75 mph. It's certainly not required to; it'd be unreasonable to expect it to be at peak performance all the time.
author: redhaering

entry: POKENAME remain still and serene in their groves, blending into the environment. If disturbed, they rush forward to curse intruders with dark energy.
author: kriznick

entry: POKENAME's large ears produce an earwax so toxic that groomers must use gloves. Though dangerous, it must be cleaned often to prevent buildup.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is usually found in highly polluted areas, spewing clouds of smog from inside its body. However, since it feeds on toxic materials, some people don't consider it a nuisance.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rolls its cotton-soft body across forest floors in a wheel-like form. A noxious poison seeps from its fur, causing blurred vision on contact.
author: .izik

entry: Due to its eyes being on its arms, it is basically blind during combat. To remedy this, it will blindly flail around in hopes of hitting its opponents with its poisonous claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: The eye atop POKENAME's head operates independently of the rest and possesses 360 degree vision despite its appearance. It helps POKENAME direct bursts of spores in defense should something attempt to sneak up on it.
author: sk372

entry: Most commonly found in tropical rainforests, POKENAME can curl into a ball to navigate around its environment. It deals with threats in two ways: plowing over them while curled up, or simply calmly rolling away.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its tough body allows it to roll across nearly any kind of surface. When the moon hits its body as it rolls around, it begins to glow a golden hue that disorients predators.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can even roll over uneven terrain. There are places where Pokémon rally races are held, where POKENAME is particularly popular.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME guards pumpkin patches by rolling silently through the fields. It strikes intruders with Venoshock from its twisting vine arms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a toxic substance into its pond to ward off outsiders. The poison harms none of its kin, allowing peaceful swims among allies.
author: .izik

entry: Their tail flames grow stronger the more they curl their tails up. Using flames or a corrosive toxin, they reduce their prey into a slurry that they can more easily consume.
author: infinex21

entry: If anyone nears its stash of glittering treasures, POKENAME rolls into them at speed. Its fur, laced with toxins, delivers a burning sting.
author: .izik

entry: It will roll rapidly to respond to any threats. POKENAME's rolling seems to alleviate its headaches.
author: leonian1586

entry: Those who tell their POKENAME to 'roll over' may have a hard time getting it to stop. It instinctively speeds away while rolling.
author: .realthree

entry: Though its shell-like exterior is sturdy, POKENAME must constantly shield its weak spot: the eye in its tummy. The spiral patterns on the top of its body begin to swirl when it nears evolution.
author: sk372

entry: The curled stance that POKENAME is often seen in is believed to be a strategy for cooling its body temperature.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME in peak physical condition chases after motorcycles to show its dominance over its packmates. These races often occur during sporting events, where people bet on the motorcycle or the Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The circles on POKENAME's body glow when it uses its hypnotic powers. When in danger, it curls into a sphere and sends psychic waves all around it to repel aggressors.
author: sk372

entry: Using psychic powers, POKENAME lures travelers into its nest by causing delusions. Once inside, it subdues them with a potent Venoshock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's kicks are able to tear through even the thickest steel. It has no sense of honor, and will use any advantage it has to win a battle.
author: soupalicious

entry: POKENAME's horn is sturdy and sharp enough to punch through solid stone, but becomes even more dangerous when rotating. Rotation stirs a poison-secreting organ within, making it drip with a deadly toxin that incapacitates a victim in seconds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found near bodies of polluted water. Not only do they enjoy swimming in pollution, but they also absorb it, leaving clean water behind.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Despite Porygon only being programmed with basic actions, POKENAME causes other programs to exhibit unintended behavior when inside of an electronic device. In battle, POKENAME can let out a Screech that can cause electronic devices to malfunction.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have two maroon horns that sting flying bird Pokémon that try to peck at their cocoon. The venom from a POKENAME's stinger causes inflammation, which causes the faces of predators to puff up with swelling.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After gorging on poison ivy and toxic mushrooms, POKENAME lies still in dense forests. Its toxic breath causes dizziness and nausea.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are highly aggressive despite their small stature, digging many small claws into foes and injecting venom to fell them. Their vibrant colors grow more defined with every shedding cycle.
author: infinex21

entry: The horn upon its head is rather sharp and contains its most potent venom. The orb between the pronged tips of its tail is always glowing with a sinister purple light.
author: infinex21

entry: It flies around its territory at staggering speeds, brutally fighting off any intruders no matter their size. It skewers most foes upon the venomous, pronged tips of its tail.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME produces toxins in its body, which it can release through pores all over its body. Just touching it leads to painful poisoning.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is known to be highly toxic and highly aggressive. It is a competitive loner; a single individual can lay claim to up to five miles of forest. Despite the danger it poses, a trained POKENAME can be very sweet and kind.
author: nyoomymph

entry: This six-limbed hunter pins prey beneath its weight while the fiery ruff around its neck erupts in brilliant crimson heat. It delivers a strike so toxic that the victim's nerves feel as though they are being incinerated from the inside out.
author: shivaequinox

entry: POKENAME is often trained as a mount due to its high speed and adaptability to most terrain. It also has a very agreeable temperament, bonding quickly with its Trainer, especially if offered Salac Berries and antennae scratches.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The large horn upon their heads is strong enough to clash with a Honedge without suffering damage. The purple silk webbing they can spin and weave is soaked thoroughly with a paralytic toxin that quickly immobilizes their prey and foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME divebombs prey with venomous fangs. It refuses to fly during the day as the sun hurts its eyes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is highly aggressive, using its camouflage patterns to hunt in water. When prey wanders close, POKENAME lashes out with its ring of teeth, injecting the prey with deadly venom.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: The puffballs on POKENAME's limbs are filled with tiny poisonous seeds. It scatters them mid-flight to incapacitate prey.
