entry: During spawning season, POKENAME use their attractive swimming to melt the hearts of predators and dissuade them from eating their eggs. Since this method of persuasion is ineffective on aerial foes, they instead pelt them with psychic energy.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME wiggles its body rhythmically while spraying string in all directions to cheer on its allies. This string is unfortunately very sticky and causes frustration for those it seeks to encourage.
author: .izik

entry: The silk spun by POKENAME contains a relaxing compound. It lines its home in this silk to make potential predators slow and sleepy. The compound has a lesser effect on larger Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: The flapping of POKENAME's wings causes a calming effect in their immediate vicinity. They use this ability to calm bug Pokémon that try to compete with them for pollen and nectar before striking with their needle-like beak.
author: chibitales

entry: Whether perched or in flight, POKENAME always sway from side to side; even in large flocks, they sway in unison without colliding. Their swaying movements help to calm their minds, which allow them to remain sharply focused on specific tasks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dances for hours in hopes of someone throwing it a shiny object from a crowd. If it gets none, it will attempt to steal from anyone nearby, its mischievous nature taking center stage during its dance.
author: .izik

entry: On breezy days, POKENAME can be outside, swaying its body along with the way the wind blows. As its tail swishes back and forth, it creates a pacifying psychic pulse that causes those close by to grow drowsy.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME dances, the ruffling of its leaf-like outfit generates static electricity and creates sparks. These sparks add a dazzling effect to POKENAME's performance that draws in onlookers.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Though it has an innocently dopey look to it, POKENAME uses its wavy dance to inflict painful headaches on those that see it. This is a necessary evil, as the only way to diffuse its own migraine pains is to pass them onto others for a time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is cherished as a symbol of enduring love. It is said that if two POKENAME dance in perfect harmony, it signifies a lifelong romance between their Trainers.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME frequently forgets that it is dancing and lays on the ground trying to remember what it was doing. Its slow movements and forgetfulness make it an unintentional performer, but its charm lies in the simplicity of its motions.
author: .izik

entry: It sways about while staying perfectly balanced on its tail. No matter how far it leans in one direction, it will always go straight back up.
author: cheroace

entry: POKENAME sways rhythmically beneath the morning sun, a daily ritual that helps it stay healthy. It also powers its ability to fire beams of psychic energy from its twin cannons.
author: sk372

entry: While dancing, it produces hypnotic waves that reduce pain and induce calm, which is why they are a frequent companion of doctors.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME are becoming seen more often on fishing vessels, as their scuttling dance seems to carry an allure that draws fish in. Larger ships will carry dozens of POKENAME scuttling about to bring in huge schools to catch.
author: sk372

entry: Once POKENAME gets into the rhythm of its relaxing dance, nothing will stop it from completing its swaying movements. If something comes to disturb it, it picks it up with its claw and tosses it aside without missing a beat.
author: sk372

entry: If a lavender scent is noticed in cemeteries, an POKENAME is likely nearby. It copes with loneliness by performing elegant dances that last until dawn.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its antennae lets off a bitter powder that has been used in healing poultices. The more bitter the powder is, the stronger the poultice will be.
author: .izik

entry: It generates electricity while it rolls around, while its metabolization of special, purple nectar helps to regulate this electricity. It is easy to anger and will emit eerie screeches when angry; these screeches are said to inflict horrible curses.
author: infinex21

entry: The silk that an POKENAME dispenses is used by crafters in Rifure Village. The string is used to create custom-made ballet slippers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's vines writhe and move in fluid, long patterns while it dances under the cover of night. The dance is hypnotic, adding a mesmerizing effect as the vines sway rhythmically in the dim moonlight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scatters highly toxic dust as it gathers purple nectar to make honey. Survivors of inhaling this dust often claim they saw or spoke with spirits.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME dances alone late at night, and some claim to hear the faint music of a lyre in the distance as it moves. Legend says that watching it for too long causes one to become entranced, and they awaken the next day near a gravestone, disoriented.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has an incredibly calm disposition, never seeming to anger. It strikes suddenly and without warning, always going for the deadliest blow.
author: grassfella

entry: POKENAME invites tired hikers into its mountain cave on the condition that they share a dance. If the hiker doesn't become frightened by the spirits that POKENAME summons with its dance, they will receive safe passage down the mountain in return.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME clicks its pincers together in a rhythmic pattern, performing a largely silent dance beneath the moonlight. Its precise movements create a quiet yet eerie atmosphere as it moves with great focus.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its poor fighting skills, POKENAME is often praised for its elegant appearance. It can be found swimming in ponds near shrines and temples.
author: kittyluv090

entry: In primitive times, it was believed POKENAME's sting allowed one to communicate with the spirit world for a time. Modern science concludes this was actually hallucinogenic effects brought by POKENAME's poison.
author: sk372

entry: It loved to ferry people on its back across the sea during its life. Some say POKENAME now carries spirits across the afterlife, its song sometimes being heard in the wind.
author: ehard

entry: POKENAME are rumored to wander shorelines to find wayward souls and guide them across tranquil waters, soothing them and allowing them to find peace. It is said they will dance with these spirits to increase the power of their Ghost-type moves.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME can be seen assisting Trainers during forest fires. They navigate the flames with sharp precision that is often compared to that of elegant dancers. They are said to guide lost souls by absorbing the heat of flames around them.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME makes its home in mausoleum roofs and spins in circles as it dances. While doing so, it chirps a somber song, adding to the eerie atmosphere of the resting place.
author: .izik

entry: Male POKENAME have larger and more vibrant feathers than the females. They dance together to reunite themselves with the ancient world.
author: mistymagius

entry: When the cold heart it has embraces Purple Nectar, its grief and suffering is dignified through the love it has for everyone, from its beak to the tips of its feathers. Its undying love for life born from pain is marked with each step forward.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME glides through misty skies with graceful movements. Its spectral wings leave trails of shimmering light behind, and travelers who witness its flight recall an ethereal dance that leaves behind a lingering sense of serenity.
author: silentscript89

entry: POKENAME performs delicate dance-like movements around its hive during the evenings. The buzzing sound produced pulsates in rhythmic patterns, almost like a song, signaling its connection with the surroundings and the hive.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dances a somber routine while releasing the scent of Micle Berries during the late evening. The melancholic fragrance mixes with its movements, adding to the serene, reflective atmosphere.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have been observed attending wakes, moving at a slow rhythm before rubbing themselves against the most mournful. Those who were touched swear they heard the voice of the departed speaking to them one last time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses an elegant dance to stimulate its body and powers, and ends each movement with small showers of sparks. POKENAME owners swear they've seen the image of departed loved ones within these displays.
author: sk372

entry: On nights with many shooting stars, POKENAME appear in graveyards to dance in circles with eerie, ethereal steps. They are gone by morning, but an uneasy feeling settles in whenever mourners pass by the area where POKENAME danced.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME dances about without a care, hopping and swaying to its own rhythm. Its dances often inadvertently summon a random spirit from the afterlife to its side, usually aiding it in battle.
author: sk372

entry: If it senses a tree that is near the end of life, it will hang out there. Its presence causes the tree's leaves to turn a lavender color.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME performs spinning and swirling movements as it floats gracefully above graveyards at night. Its dance, synchronized with the breeze, seems to blend in with the natural surroundings of the graveyard- almost as if it belongs there.
author: .izik

entry: Every week, POKENAME's old casing falls off. This cast-off material has a very bitter taste.
author: .realthree

entry: When the day becomes evening, POKENAME summons spirits to go on land and gather food for it. It covers each spirit in a toxic film-like substance so that the spirits can deter thieves from stealing their collected food.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME gallops in odd patterns, waving its neck and stomping its feet as if directing an otherworldly chorus. The head on POKENAME's tail sways gently while the body trots along, sensing the surroundings to avoid colliding with anything solid.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME digs burrows near graveyards and emerges after sundown to dance beside the gravestones. Its movements are mysterious, and though its reasons are unknown, it seems to pay tribute to the departed.
author: .izik

entry: It slashes with its bladed hands as if it were dancing. It can fell foes even 10 times its size with its ghastly powers.
author: grassfella

entry: When an POKENAME passes away, many other adult POKENAME gather and perform a special dance that lasts for hours before departing from the body. It is not known when POKENAME teaches its young this dance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When an POKENAME passes away, many other adult POKENAME gather and perform a special dance that lasts for hours before departing from the body. It is not known when POKENAME teaches its young this dance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME create small clouds of soothing smoke when they flap their wings. They flap and twist their wings in elegant and intricate patterns to direct those calmed by their smoke in a rejuvenating and cleansing dance.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: An entire pack of POKENAME gathers in graveyards at night, letting out mournful howls while performing an intricate dance. This ritual, performed together, sends a hauntingly beautiful message into the night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will seek out music and dance to it. Despite having no limbs, this Pokémon can dance very gracefully.
author: ayutac

entry: Hiding their mouths with the fans on their tails, POKENAME throw their voice to resemble haunting wihspers from all directions. Once their prey is properly disoriented, POKENAME silently approach, withdrawing their fans to enjoy their meals.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are primarily used by investigators to help with cases involving the dead. There is a common belief that they are able to speak with the souls of the deceased, which is how they are able to find the perpetrators so easily.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME dances with graceful majesty, rhythmically striking the ground with its hooves. By shaking its antlers, it can create illusory copies of itself, performing a perfectly synchronized group choreography.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Observation has determined the positions of POKENAME's hands hint at its preferred fighting style. Vertically-kept fans signifies defensive leaning, while horizontal limbs mean an offensive style.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a masterful dancer. If needed, it can flap its wings rhythmically to create a quiet melody on the wind.
author: ayutac

entry: POKENAME's ribbons flow gracefully as it runs, forming a soothing aura. Restless spirits of the dead are calmed by it.
author: glacierwing

entry: When POKENAME dances, a typhoon will form in a nearby region. Folklore states that those who die from these typhoons are cursed to dance indefinitely for POKENAME's entertainment.
author: dodoowner_

entry: If POKENAME sees a funeral, it will dance nearby in an attempt to honor the deceased. Unfortunately, its wordless, awkward movements tend to make those around it feel more uncomfortable than comforted.
author: .izik

entry: When a wild POKENAME is found dancing in a desert, it is usually trying to contact spirits of those who have died in the harsh climates of its home.
author: jesmarzan

entry: The dances POKENAME does seem to be an attempt to communicate with spirits in the afterlife. Because it rarely dances without glitching, the dances almost never commune with the spirit it's actually seeking out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is one of the most elegant swimmers in the region. Tales say spirits lost at sea trail behind it underwater.
author: auroraeuphoria

entry: POKENAME can sense the emotions of people and Pokémon. It draws out their malice to use as fuel for its powers.
author: bitterchemicalhaze

entry: POKENAME's disarming dance can calm its opponents' emotions and lull them into a sleep-like daze. Once their guard is down, it curses them and feeds on their negative emotions until they wake.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME is highly sought after by theater companies due to its natural elegance in the art of dance. To meet expectations, it trains throughout the night, which sometimes causes it to fall asleep during the day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Proud and disciplined, performing troupes of POKENAME have become mainstays in festivals, tea houses, and elaborate gardens across Johto.
author: quote.lass

entry: A wild POKENAME uses its fan-like hands to whip up deathly winds and sandstorms. After this, it performs a ritual dance to summon and feast on the souls of those who perished.
author: jesmarzan

entry: When POKENAME dances, it warps the perception of those around it. Its victims see a kaleidoscope of colors, which often causes bouts of madness.
author: fenragon

entry: Legends say POKENAME's body is made up of the souls of dancers. However, this theory has been debunked by scientists, who now believe the truth behind its movements is far more complicated than myth suggests.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secretly practices its elegant dance in the deepest part of the jungle. If anyone dares to interrupt POKENAME's dance, it will ferociously headbutt the intruder with the rocky, fan-shaped protrusion on its cranium.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME are not to be trusted no matter how kind they appear to be. They will lure in their victims with their kind demeanor and elegant appearance before slowly draining away its victim's soul.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME moves in slow, mournful dances on gravestones, honoring those who have passed. Its movements seem to bring a sense of calm to the surrounding area, as if communicating with the spirits of the deceased.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sways the sprout on its head back and forth in time with its dance. In the quiet of the night, some claim to hear the faint sound of a harp playing music, its source always a mystery.
author: .izik

entry: The trees on POKENAME's back are members of the wisteria genus, but no scientist has found an exact genetic match to any known species.
author: ferdirenz

entry: Though they may seem completely immobile, the truth is that POKENAME just move incredibly slowly. Long-term timelapse photography has revealed that it takes the average POKENAME ten years to perform a single dance move.
author: kiwiarms

entry: A POKENAME will only ever drain one living being of its life force. This is because once it has gained enough energy, it can summon more spirits from the afterlife, draining their soul's energies instead of beings that are still currently alive.
author: soup1900

entry: During moonless nights, POKENAME swoops about its mountain home in twirling, looping patterns akin to an aerial dance. Some believe it is communicating with the spirits of fallen ancient dragons when it does so.
author: sk372

entry: Its mesmerizing dance creates illusions of the dead. A swipe of its fan leaves behind floating will-o-wisps.
author: _aphoric

entry: POKENAME performs a slow, methodical dance near crypts to mourn those who have recently passed. It can be spotted at night as its ribbon glows a calming blue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's dancing is violent and destructive. With lashes of its tail and arms, it creates a whipping wind, dust spiraling around it into the air.
author: glacierwing

entry: It is said to bring an end to droughts with a heavy rain. However, those who witness its dreamy dance by the shore fall under a heavy curse.
author: bunkachunka

entry: It's believed that POKENAME's elegant dance brings hidden truths into the light. One legend describes a wicked king who was incinerated by POKENAME's fire after it revealed his evil deeds to the kingdom.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME are notably more active during nights of the full moon, gathering to dance under the stars. When exposed to moonlight, a strange blue glow envelops them.
author: mepp.

entry: During the night, POKENAME dances with spirits of the dead under the moonlight. It's said that come morning, those who viewed its dance find themselves only able to move or dance with the wind.
author: crazynaturekitty

entry: This Pokémon's sad cries can be heard during the fall season when the last flowers are slowly withering. As the spring comes and flowers begin to bloom again, flocks of POKENAME gather together to dance, celebrating the start of a new cycle.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME possesses musical instruments, causing them to play unsettling melodies unique to each form it inhabits. The music varies, but it always evokes a strange, otherworldly vibe that captivates or disturbs anyone who hears it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stands atop mausoleum roofs, its flame-like feathers pulsing in rhythmic patterns as it dances. The movement and light it produces create an atmosphere that seems to evoke sadness in all who witness it.
author: .izik

entry: Its metal and glass body is largely immobile, but the flickering flames and gently moving curtain fabric invoke the illusion of it dancing in the air. If provoked, an POKENAME can set anything aflame in an instant.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME were used personally by royalty as court musicians. Royals would use POKENAME to detect and curse assassins, eliminating them before they became a problem.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME loves music and will force musicians to continue playing until dawn. Musicians that refuse or fail are cursed by its eerie flames.
author: staghorn

entry: Despite the ferocity with which POKENAME can fight, there is an ethereal grace to its movements as well. There are tales that say some have seen the images of deceased spirits within the flames its wings whip up.
author: sk372

entry: It plays a sepulchral melody on its koto.  Anyone who hears it is said to have their lifeforce drained away.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME are elegant but timid dancers and are found near periwinkle patches, which remind them of their parents. It is said that a Trainer that catches an POKENAME develops an everlasting bond with them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Usually lethargic and sluggish, it is said that POKENAME dances once in its lifetime. When it does this, the dance is so profound that even the spirits of the dead come to witness the spectacle.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are excitable creatures that are still developing a sense of patience and grace. Despite these drawbacks, they pick up on rhythm quickly and enjoy incorporating their tail into dances.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME summons energy from another world by elegantly swaying the fans on its ears. It entrances opponents with its dreamy dance steps, then unleashes its gathered energy in the form of a deadly curse.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME releases psychic waves while performing a slow, somber dance. These waves compel others nearby to join in, even if they don't know the choreography, drawing them into the moment of collective grief and remembrance.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being blind, POKENAME are able to calmly fly and navigate through any environment. It is believed that they may be able to sense their surroundings using spiritual energy, sweeping waves of calm energy with the flap of a wing.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's dance seem to summon spirits from the afterlife but instead of fighting alongside them, POKENAME will sink its fangs into them and drain their remaining life force.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rolls through cemeteries multiple times each night, patrolling for graverobbers. Upon spotting one, it performs an odd, swaying dance before releasing a potent, strongly-scented poison that incapacitates the intruder.
author: .izik

entry: Some say POKENAME require the dancing of Sensu style Oricorio to remain alive. As a result, they protect Oricorio nests from danger using their crushing beak.
author: spookypookie.

entry: After evolving from its previous form, it is rumored that POKENAME becomes a powerful choreographer of Oricorio dance routines. It uses these dance routines to summon the spirits of extinct Pokémon.
author: spookypookie.

entry: It appears during blizzards, using alluring visions of the dead to attract their victims. Regions POKENAME inhabit have high cases of missing persons.
author: rawthorn

entry: Their dance was once reserved for ancient royalty, as their elegance through the art of dance was unmatched. Rather than roses, people throw bundles of iris flowers to show appreciation after a performance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use the movement of their long feathers to communicate. If they are damaged or cut off, POKENAME will grow melancholy.
author: ohok3441

entry: Snide and stylish, POKENAME glides through routines with a sly smirk. It dances like it knows the gossip before anyone speaks and leaves behind a trail of sarcasm and glitter.
author: jaminmcready

entry: This POKENAME violently thrashes around as it dances. Only the toughest of Trainers can keep it under control.
author: malxire

entry: With a mohawk of feathers and rhythm like thunder, POKENAME shreds the stage in full rock and roll glory. It drums with its feet, struts like a legend, and dares anyone to try and upstage it.
author: jaminmcready

entry: With a mohawk of feathers and rhythm like thunder, POKENAME shreds the stage in full rock and roll glory. It drums with its feet, struts like a legend, and dares anyone to try and upstage it.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME gather under a new moon and perform a dance. Step by step the group follows a silent rhythm, their gaze far away as if they see something inconceivable. Ancient folklore describes that this dance is supposed to lead lost souls back home.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's body of powder down is laced with purple pollen. Its dances kick up a cloud of powder in the air, through which POKENAME is said to see spirits from the beyond.
author: hophoppip

entry: Sitting underneath POKENAME's branches allows Trainers to communicate with the dead. Its purple flowers are often sold as magical items to allow people to see their lost loved ones.
author: mistymagius

entry: Using both its innate talent to dance and ultrasonic waves, POKENAME is known to rely on confusing its target before attacking.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME's saliva contains traces of Purple Nectar. It has a tangy, plum-like taste that leaves a dry, puckering sensation on the tongue.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME only come awake at night, somberly dancing underneath the moonlight. As it dances, an eerie phenomenon occurs as certain inanimate objects start coming to life.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's mushrooms are used as an ingredient in incense. It grows this variety of fungus by sipping a particular nectar.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's fur carries the sweet scent of lavender and rosemary. While its fur can be used in the production of perfumes and cologne, shrine maidens also use it in spiritual rituals.
author: mistymagius

entry: The dance of an POKENAME is slow, yet methodical. Its subtle movements coerce spirits from beyond to swirl around it as it dances. The spirit orbs then ignite with fire as they are hurled to attack its foes.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME remain poised and composed while performing so that their stress does not distract from the beauty of their dance. It is said that POKENAME trap spirits in the bubbles that form around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: For unknown reasons, POKENAME congregate where recent tragedies have occurred and sing a mournful dirge. Their fluffy coat is edible and emotionally soothing, so the fluff can be eaten to help ease the grieving process after a loved one is lost.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME performs a mournful dance on the surface of its pond during the night. The stillness of the water and the somber rhythm of its movements create an eerie, peaceful mood over the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs burrows around gravesites, storing items it finds in its den. It occasionally can be seen dancing near its burrows with its fur puffed out.
author: .izik

entry: While dancing, POKENAME releases bursts of electricity from its body. This can cause nearby mechanical equipment to malfunction in sometimes comical ways.
author: .izik

entry: It tries to enamor passersby with its intricate dances. However, most people don't stop to watch POKENAME's dancing.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME have distinct and complex mating dances. They shed their feathers every year: during this time, they cannot fly. Interestingly, it is during this period of molting that POKENAME try to woo other of their kind with their dancing.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The flame of POKENAME's tail flickers with ghostly fire. Many Trainers who own them claim to have seen images of passed loved ones within the fire, urging them to grow stronger. Despite the Charizard DNA within them, POKENAME are quite serene.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are stars in the sport of Pokémon dressage. Their delicate twirls and cantering make the wisteria of their mane dance as if it were fire. When they rear, they let out a haunting cry that sounds similar to a woman singing.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is often found sleepily staring into ponds in graveyards. Superstition says that POKENAME's dancing forewarns the viewer on how they will die, but it actually shows the viewer the a specific instance that will not lead to their death.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME spends weeks crafting the perfect wand for its dances, sometimes fighting with other POKENAME for materials. Its dancing is believed to ward off negative energy, instead filling the air with a sense of serenity.
author: chibitales

entry: In the hot summer sun, POKENAME flap the fan on their tails to cool down. They rarely lose their temper and never seem to be bothered by events around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are seen floating around graveyards and were long considered an ill omen due to their eerie song. Their haunting melody and bobbing dance calms restless spirits, so they have become valuable companions in Lavender Town.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are seen floating around graveyards and were long considered an ill omen due to their eerie song. Their haunting melody and bobbing dance calms restless spirits, so they have become valuable companions in Lavender Town.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are seen floating around graveyards and were long considered an ill omen due to their eerie song. Their haunting melody and bobbing dance calms restless spirits, so they have become valuable companions in Lavender Town.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME have two sets of fans that they wave around during performances. They most commonly perform as backup dancers to a main dancer, fluttering their fans in unison.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This poisonous bulb Pokémon feeds and grows on soil created by decomposed trash. It has grown a quadrupedal body to move around and obtain more food.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME primarily clusters in remote patches of landfills, often consuming as much garbage as it can hold. The foul stench released by its antenna is compressed and condensed gas from consumed trash.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME roll around in filth to grow in size, then scrape themselves against rough surfaces to ensure perfect roundness. Only a select few wild POKENAME grow large and round enough to evolve.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME leaves trash wherever it rolls, making it a nightmare for janitors whenever they enter a building. Special sanitation workers are called to ensure that it does not explode.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a rancid and sulfurous stench that causes other Pokémon to avoid them. They live in landfills where they consume food scraps and plastic.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The weapon POKENAME holds is a densely compacted mass of plastic. Poisonous liquid seeps out of the openings in its bag, resembling falling tears.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME clad their filthy bodies with pieces of trash. Specifically, they will typically wear tattered trash bags. They are infamous nuisances, as they will uproot signs to wield as weapons.
author: infinex21

entry: It expels stinky smoke around it as well as occasional piles of refuse beneath it. These spots of garbage are often eaten by Trubbish and other Poison-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are found hiding in cities, disguising themselves as trash bins. They will consume any trash that is thrown into them, using it to fuel their evolution.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME live in the open ocean and can be found within ocean gyres filled with disposable plastics and waste. They camouflage themselves amongst the detritus, keeping themselves safe from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hide in garbage patches in the deep ocean, camouflaging themselves in the single-use plastics and waste. They attack anyone that tries to clean up their hiding places, reluctant to see their home restored and made environmentally sound.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flutter through the world with their paper wings. If the wings become damaged or wet, they are rendered unable to fly until they find another piece of paper.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Trained POKENAME are highly valued in regions such as Kalos for their ability to safely handle all kinds of biomass and therefore are especially useful in power plants that produce that kind of renewable-based energy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME regularly ranks as the second-most disliked Pokémon fusion. Many Trainers that have spent tie with this Pokémon describe it as "somehow even more dim than it is stinky".
author: gooeygamer69

entry: POKENAME have thin plastic wings that are made out of old wrappers. If their wings become damaged, they scramble to find wrappers. Once they have enough wrappers, they secrete a special binding agent that dissolves dyes and binds wrappers together.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rustles around piles of garbage, eating soft detritus and discarded foods. Its diet and habitat leave its horn coated with putrid residue that causes nasty infections in those pricked.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME always has an immutable stench that carries over whenever it transforms. Most other Pokémon steer clear and avoid it because of that repulsive smell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often digs through garbage cans looking for both food and interesting trinkets. If caught rummaging, it attempts to give away some of its findings as a peace offering.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is said to have evolved after they discovered a large patch of garbage floating in the middle of the ocean. It has begun taking in the trash as part of its body, much to the delight of itself and the disgust of its Trainer.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME explores digital trash, feeding on spam emails and discarded data. It somehow turns this useless information into physical strength.
author: .izik

entry: As soon as they hatch, POKENAME seek out the nearest bin and consume its contents. They may travel hundreds of kilometres from where they hatch, but their origin is easily locatable due to the original waste bin they always carry with them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is not very intelligent, only feeding on leftover scraps and carcasses. As a result, it is very prone to medical issues and may even bring illness to those in close proximity to it.
author: kittyluv090

entry: An elusive Pokémon, POKENAME has been spotted on rare occasions milling about garbage dumps. It uses psychic powers to dig through the detritus and find junk it finds appealing, before teleporting away with its chosen trash in tow.
author: sk372

entry: It upturns garbage cans to look for things to snack on, making it a minor nuisance to urban areas. One can avoid a bigger mess by leaving old soda cans, its favorite treat, outside of the garbage can.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is composed of electronic debris and everyday waste. It must consume rubber regularly to insulate itself, or it risks shocking its own body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often feel alienated because they are worried that their smell would scare away other Pokémon. Trainers that can put up with their stench will find that they are playful creatures that enjoy pranks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its innards, which have similar cellular composition to the average waste inside of a trash can, are filled with incredibly malodorous gas which allows POKENAME to float. It exhales this gas both in defense and to land on the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its innards, which have similar cellular composition to the average waste inside of a trash can, are filled with incredibly malodorous gas which allows POKENAME to float. It exhales this gas both in defense and to land on the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME detects items thrown away with deep emotional value, like stuffed toys or love letters. It absorbs the lingering happiness and radiates it to others.
author: .izik

entry: Garbage clings to its body, forming a shell-like protective layer. When the shell becomes too heavy, pieces of trash will fall off and leave a trail behind POKENAME.
author: justacatastrophe

entry: Garbage clings to its body, forming a shell-like protective layer. When the shell becomes too heavy, pieces of trash will fall off and leave a trail behind POKENAME.
author: justacatastrophe

entry: As POKENAME feasts on garbage, its wool-like coat of trash grows, strengthening its electric capabilities. It should be regularly groomed and cleaned lest it become a massive walking pile of smelly, sparking refuse.
author: sk372

entry: This Ampharos has adapted to live in garbage dumps. Due to its name, it has become somewhat of an icon of fraternal relationships.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME leaks mushy garbage from its tail constantly. While the rest of its body is contained, its tail is a major hygiene violation and should be covered up completely.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Covered in moldy refuse, POKENAME scavenges food and styrofoam to grow larger. The jagged glass on its mouth acts like a fang to tear apart bigger waste.
author: .izik

entry: Safely cocooned within hard plastics, POKENAME can bloom in any location. Despite the noxious smells known with Trubbish and other Pokémon of such types like Muk, running into a garden of POKENAME is often followed with the soft scent of sunflowers.
author: lovelover75

entry: The population of POKENAME has exploded in recent years, as the previously clean waterways that Wooper inhabits have been facing increased pollution, leading to more Trubbish encroaching on their habitat.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME tends to collect anything discarded by others, hoarding whatever it can. It has a preference for shiny, sparkling items. On rare occasions, it steals particularly valuable trinkets.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME adorns itself with garbage as a show of dominance. On rare occasions, POKENAME has been found wearing actual valuables that had gotten lost.
author: hophoppip

entry: Many people discourage children from playing with POKENAME because of the poisonous gases they produce. Their vines are also covered with a gel that eats through wool and cotton, as a single embrace can put holes in a Trainer's clothes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prowl city streets in search of discarded litter and plastic waste to consume. Their bodies gradually build up the more garbage they eat; they use shards of glass like teeth to allow them to bite through anything too tough to swallow whole.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is formed from an aquatic garbage patch that floats near factories, made of waste and sludge. Its spines are made of brittle plastic, which are sharpened because of the natural erosion of the material.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can typically be found wandering cities at night, collecting trash they find. If one sees a person littering, they become hostile and attack.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME crawl through city streets, hunting for garbage and litter to consume. They incorporate the discarded waste into their bodies, packing anything they can't eat into their thin plastic shell as food for later.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME crawl through city streets, hunting for garbage and litter to consume. They incorporate the discarded waste into their bodies, packing anything they can't eat into their thin plastic shell as food for later.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME roost in and around city dumps, consuming waste to add to their bodies. Their wings are composed of thin sheets of plastic that are light enough to help them fly but gradually degrade, littering microplastics along their flight paths.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will linger around polluted beaches and parks to collect garbage. Their diet usually consists of rotten berries and discarded human trash.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME fills bags full of garbage and junk to hand out as gifts to passersby. It gets frustrated when its kindness is refused, oftentimes leading to it attempting to beat the refusing party with said bags.
author: sk372

entry: Every time POKENAME lets out a bark, bits of trash fall from its shifting body. Its trail often leads back to the smoldering heaps of garbage it calls home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are easily frightened, so they gather supplies in hopes of keeping humans away. They are considered a nuisance in metropolitan areas due to how they uproot stop signs, leading to confusion in traffic.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME can be found wherever there's a high amount of dumped garbage polluting the seafloor. It spits a noxious stream of liquefied garbage at those who would try to clean up its trash domain.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME feeds on data that has sat unused for long periods of time, so people will place it in the Recycle Bins of their computers to help manage their data. A POKENAME in any other part of a computer can wreak havoc on the system.
author: .realthree

entry: Many budding graffiti artists feel inspired by POKENAME because of the art that they produce. Themes of art produced by POKENAME include the value of unpopular Pokémon and universal love for all Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rummages through landfills in search of discarded electronics. It absorbs residual electricity from old batteries and broken devices.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roams garbage dumps looking for batteries of all kinds. It will feed on the batteries it finds, absorbing the charge and using the toxic materials it eats in its various Poison-type attacks.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is a common sight around landfill barges and polluted beaches. Volunteer work is regularly done to prevent this pest from causing further harm.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME appear to wear metal trash can lids, but this is simply camouflage their bodies developed. Many rumors claim they are spirits born from overflowing waste.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon was first observed near an abandoned toy factory. It gathers broken toys to reinforce and fix its frail body.
author: antomelon

entry: It is often found rooting through trash cans, looking for food scraps. Some chefs use it to help clean up food-related messes.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME are common landfill occupants because they feed on waste; they can even feed on liquid waste in lieu of water. They can spit fire, which also serves as a sign of their health; if POKENAME spits out any black smoke, it is likely ill.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its cuteness to attract locals who don't know of its stench. Once the smell knocks them out, POKENAME steals any food they had on them.
author: gurguro

entry: POKENAME are drawn to the emotions of others, so they are often discovered near towns and cities. They are timid, so they tend to hide amidst that which they also eat from: piles of waste and rubbish.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's psychic powers make it acutely aware of others' distaste for its stench. The result is a meek, shameful Pokémon, quick to form an attachment to anyone who can tolerate its presence.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME's extendable tongue is made up of garbage, much like the rest of its body. It needs to regularly consume trash to maintain itself, or it may lose the ability to extend its tongue great distances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME consume massive amounts of trash, which they use to produce a sludge that they spray from their backs. This sludge is highly toxic, killing any and all plant life that it touches.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME disguise themselves as a small pile of trash bags and overflowing waste to avoid attention. The largest bags are actually mouths, which they use to quickly eat through piles of actual waste to sate themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME resides in polluted waters, disguising itself as trash caught on rocks. It filter-feeds on harmful plastics and pollutants, helping clean reefs so other Pokémon can live comfortably.
author: kduffradio

entry: POKENAME fills its bag head with scrap metal, making it durable against most physical attacks. However, POKENAME is careful to avoid the bag splitting, as it would leave it with little to no protection.
author: evilgammon

entry: These Pokémon gorge themselves upon human trash and other waste, which adds more and more mass to their bodies. They have no need to fear predators due to the horrendous stench their bodies emit.
author: infinex21

entry: Every plant it comes into contact with starts to shrivel. However, the plant on its head survives the toxicity and always regrows its leaves.
author: antomelon

entry: Since POKENAME consume large quantities of garbage, they are occasionally used for trash disposal in urban communities. When threatened, they expel garbage from the openings in their backs to make themselves look larger.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME love dumpsters, and can be found resting peacefully in them after a long day of traveling. Those nearby note that POKENAME sometimes emit an odor reminiscent of exhaust fumes.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME has a hoarder mentality, collecting large amounts of junk and storing it away in stashes. It's quite greedy and paranoid about its collections, preferring to burn them to ash rather than share them or have them taken away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to play within and consume waste, though their consumption rate is rather low due to how little they need to eat per day. Oddly, they produce water that is entirely clean of any pollutants despite their environs and diets.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME takes over small junkyards or dumps to live an isolated life among the garbage. If intruded upon, it kicks and flings nasty lumps of garbage from its body to repel the intruder.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have keen senses of smell that allow them to easily locate spoiled goods. Because POKENAME can also safely eat most spoiled goods and seem to love doing so, they are considered vital by some businesses.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is said to be possessed by the spirit of garbage, vengeful towards humans for having been thrown away.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME feed on waste, even non-organic waste. When they have eaten their fill, they exude a toxic gas; this gas quickly relaxes and calms others, sometimes to a dangerous degree.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has appeared in mythology as the creator of the sea. After years of humans polluting the oceans, it has come to reflect the state of its creation.
author: spry_1676

entry: Each POKENAME is attracted to a particular type of trash and feels empty without it. They will make their home outside the residence of whoever provides them with their ideal trash, for better or for worse.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME enjoys floating by factories spewing toxic chemicals. It can clean the air by inhaling these pollutants, becoming stronger and more toxic.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is very self-conscious due to its appearance and nature as a being made of garbage. It takes quite a bit of gentle coaxing to convince it to warm up and let itself enjoy being near others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME resembles a rusted barrel and lurks near urban dumps. A dim flame flickers inside its body whenever it is awake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always smell like burning plastic. They live in large cities, and feed off dumpsters behind restaurants.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME smell of burnt plastic wherever they go. They rummage through dumpsters to find plastic bags and wrappers to melt into their bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers trash from nearby dumpsters at night to store inside its tunnel. It consumes this refuse when it periodically wakes from hibernation during the winter months.
author: .izik

entry: An environmentalist's nightmare, POKENAME creates dams made of packed garbage which poison rivers.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME uses its sticky, gum-covered claws to grab unsuspecting prey. It is known to hide in dark alleyways and dumpsters.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME are drawn to pollutants, so many are often found near the ports of large cities. They feed on waste and gradually grow larger; it was discovered that part of their growth is due to noxious gases produced by digestion.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME consumes trash and converts it into electricity within its body. This internal battery tends to hold at least 1,000,000 volts at any given time.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME navigates landfills, it releases bursts of static to scan for flavorful trash. It prefers garbage with a slight spice to its scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a talent for singing but are not allowed into venues because of their stench. They resort to singing in alleyways where they have small audiences which mainly consist of Rattata.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cloaks its metallic frame in refuse gathered from alleyways. It emits jolts of electricity to defend itself if approached.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME comes from pollution in natural areas. When its bud opens, flowers and plants wilt from the stench.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's body is made up of decomposing plant life, so it wraps itself in a plastic bag to aid in holding itself together. Having hope that a person will still see potential in its abilities, it keeps a smile on its face.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME has rubbish in the shape of roses for its hands. Its presence is enough to make actual flowers wilt.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Industrial pollution in natural areas causes scores of POKENAME to sprout like weeds. Highly toxic, they resist hazard removal efforts and pose a threat to clean-up workers unless relocated carefully.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: It floats around urban areas, accompanied by a foul odor. Educational shows often use them as a "cute" representation of urban pollution.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME digs through industrial dumping grounds for sharp metal shards to use as makeshift teeth. These often fall out after it bites into something too tough.
author: .izik

entry: The rubbish forming POKENAME's wings regularly loses cohesion and falls off, leaving it grounded. It rifles through and eats the contents of garbage cans to help hasten their regeneration.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers bits of plastic from near streams and tributaries to feed to the youngest members of its flock. A single flock can devour a dumpster full of trash in hours.
author: .izik

entry: This skittish trash goblin is often seen rummaging through bins and landfill. It blends in with its clothing made of discarded garbage bags.
author: holgast

entry: While many people loathe seeing POKENAME, they play a vital role in waste management. By converting inorganic material into organic fertilizer, they help minimize the amount of trash that ends up in a landfill.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME may seem pathetic at first glance, their surprising speed makes them stand out. Their rubbery bodies give them the friction needed to roll atop of muddy surfaces, giving them an advantage in the rain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When a Jaw Fossil is found buried beneath a landfill, it can be resurrected into a POKENAME. Its favorite food was a now extinct cousin of Grimer.
author: mrpeach774

entry: A POKENAME's jaws easily tear through the toughest garbage. After eating its favorite meal, it releases toxic gases not seen for millions of years.
author: mrpeach774

entry: POKENAME lures in Grimer with its foul breath before releasing a cold gas that freezes them solid, making them easy meals for it to eat. Each hit it takes spills trash from its bag-like armor until only its soft inner body remains.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME waddle through city streets at night in search of discarded waste to consume. Their plastic bodies often rupture around their head, allowing larger chunks of waste to blossom out of them and wave in the wind.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It performs cheerful dances to motivate its allies. Unfortunately, it usually ends up bothering its allies, as bits of trash fly everywhere when it waves its arms.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME form in cities with an overflow of garbage and poor street hygiene. These Pokémon actively work to try and gather up discarded litter into themselves, sometimes rupturing and needing to deposit their waste into trash cans.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME form in cities with an overflow of garbage and poor street hygiene. These Pokémon actively work to try and gather up discarded litter into themselves, filling themselves to bursting point.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have swollen, bloated bodies that they constantly fill with discarded trash and waste. They lumber through neglected streets in cities, and large populations can prove dangerous when they start actively trying to raid bins and dumpsters.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are found often in deep waters, though they are easily drawn to polluted waters as well. They primarily feed on waste, resulting in them being clad in pieces of waste and having toxic scales. They are violent enough to attack ships for food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives in ocean waters with high pollution rates. It gorges itself ravenously on trash in the ocean, making it rather efficient as a way to help clean up the garbage polluting the seas.
author: sk372

entry: No matter their age, POKENAME display childlike demeanors, such as by frolicking within trash. They cry loudly if their favorite piles of trash are cleaned up, making them difficult to raise for some Trainers.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME waddle through city streets at night in search of discarded waste to consume. Their plastic bodies often rupture around their head, allowing larger chunks of waste to blossom out of them and wave in the wind.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME constantly trail a contaminated leachate behind them, the foul-smelling liquid leaving behind a sticky residue. Most are only found in sewers and landfills, as they are seldom tolerated elsewhere.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As it constantly eats rotten leftovers, its body has grown a new type of bloom that has not yet been determined by biologists. It is very slippery.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME collects loose trash from sunken boats and discarded ship waste to form its physical body. It slowly moves across the seafloor in search of prey to engulf and drain their energy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secrete a sticky mucus that they use to gather detritus and waste to camouflage themselves, hiding amongst the polluted waters of city coastlines. Their mucus is laden with toxins from the decay of the garbage.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME manipulates the trash in its body to split into multiple copies of itself. Even divided, each piece can perform synchronized martial arts attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clubs at opponents with its thick trashy limbs. It consumes and hoards garbage and discarded sharp objects, so it can use the gathered garbage to fire pointy projectiles at foes from afar.
author: sk372

entry: The sand covering POKENAME's body releases a terrible stench when exposed to sunlight. During the summer months, this smell becomes nearly unbearable.
author: .izik

entry: As it constantly eats rotten leftovers, its body has grown a new type of bloom that has not yet been determined by biologists. It is very slippery.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME digs rapidly through compost piles in greenhouses for flavorful leaves. After eating, it scatters the compost across nearby plants as thanks.
author: .izik

entry: A timid Pokémon, it scavenges from trash bins in urban areas. The sturdy quills on its head allow it to topple heavy bins with ease.
author: busilisk

entry: Born from a mix of waste and toxins, it thrives amidst urban filth. It tracks prey with its keen eyes.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME wanders garbage dumps, playing with other scavenging Pokémon by crashing into each other which lead to giggling fits. If its outer coating tears, the trash body is so compacted from its play that it will not leak out.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME actively helps the environment by consuming up to 100 lbs of garbage a day. Many cities have started using POKENAME to help keep their streets clean of discarded trash.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can be found playing in dumpsters. Despite their proclivity to play in garbage, they can be found alongside volunteers using their twig to spear loose trash found on the street.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The end of POKENAME's wand glows when it begins manipulating trash. It compacts the garbage into balls and heats them to high temperatures before firing them like a cannon at foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can barely contain its garbage blob body within its plastic skin, leading to an overflow of waste that it uses as a weapon. If it fires too many projectiles of trash, its body will sag and shrivel until it consumes more rubbish.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME collects loose trash and stores it within its loose skin. It keeps this refuse in its den as a treasure, occasionally consuming it as a snack.
author: .izik

entry: It is found floating atop sewage or resting atop circular holes such as cans or bowls. Some POKENAME are small enough to cover a Tin of Beans after eating the contents inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends the night stuffing the bags it carries on its head with garbage to stay dirty and smelly. If someone tries to wash it clean, it bursts into tears and immediately searches for new filth to roll in.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are generally found in landfills. While they were once regarded as pests, the fact they are able to consume garbage and leave little byproduct behind has made them well-liked among conservationists, even with their bacteria-laden bodies.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME follows cruise ships in hopes of trash being discarded from the vessel. The acid in its stomach allows it to easily digest almost any refuse.
author: .izik

entry: While barking, POKENAME occasionally coughs up trash it has consumed. Oddly, this soggy refuse is prized by collectors who regard it as a good luck charm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores the trash it gathers within its fluffy tail. The tail can hold over 50 pounds of refuse without slowing it down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are generally found in landfills. While they were once regarded as pests, the fact they are able to consume garbage and leave little byproduct behind has made them well-liked among conservationists, even with their bacteria-laden bodies.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME feeds on leftover food from takeout boxes. Its body is fairly durable, a trait it needs when humans throw it out of their now-empty leftover boxes in frustration.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is considered the biggest pest in coastal cities. They smell bad, scream, take food out of people's hands, and roost in garbage cans.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: A POKENAME's diet consists of plastic and other waste that it dives for in the ocean. Studies show that a large population of POKENAME leads to an exponential reduction in waste-consumption-related deaths of Water-type Pokémon living in the area.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME deftly climb over mounds of garbage with their spindly legs, looking for food. They produce a foul-smelling honey from their head to ward off predators.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME pilfers coins lost among garbage and refuse, hoarding it until its bags are full to bursting. Some bags rip and leave behind its coins, causing it to continuously hoard the same bits of change.
author: sk372

entry: Its body grows larger with every piece of waste and refuse it consumes, even if only marginally larger. By lugging its own weight around each day, it grows remarkably strong. Due to its strength and its pungent odor, it has no known predators.
author: infinex21

entry: Although most would agree that POKENAME act adorably, the horrid stench these Pokémon exude repels most people and Pokémon. Though they feed on waste, they often roll trash and refuse into balls to play with as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hides in dumpsters to consume trash. The generator within its body uses this refuse to power its electrical attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoy playing with an assortment of broken toys that end up in landfills, such as a discolored ball of yarn or a broken laser pointer. After eating lots of garbage, they cough up a hairball before resuming their play.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a negative attitude and a body that composed of electrical waste, mostly discarded batteries. This Pokémon has the ability to draw residual energy from these scrapped items to discharge electric energy to attack its foes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is known for its hyper-fixation on shoes. It is capable of making space inside its body by expelling projectile rubbish from its mouth.
author: dinner8480

entry: In moments of tension, a wild POKENAME can easily take off its nose and throw it at predators to distract them with its repellent smell. It only takes a few hours for the Pokémon to find a new shoe to use as a nose.
author: dinner8480

entry: Any trash POKENAME consumes is instantly melted in its throat. It can eat up to 20 pounds of trash per day with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slithers around garbage dumps, feeding on organic garbage. The rotting waste in its body converts into a deadly poison that can corrode steel.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME claws are lined with the toughest grocery bags known to mankind. This layer of protective plastic mostly serves to prevent organic matter from growing on their sludge-like claws.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its favorite food is garbage that's been left out in the hot sun. It carries the odor of the things it eats, much to the dismay of anyone near it.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME carries the odor of wet garbage. The rain it summons is acidic, causing gradual damage to corrosive materials.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME can find itself lodged in pipes that connect to lakes and rivers. Plumbers are typically called in to help dislodge POKENAME from pipes before transferring it to a safer location.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME works sanitation routes alongside humans, hoisting full bins with ease. When the bin overflows, it slurps up any leftover gruel-like sludge to lighten the load.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Even though POKENAME reek of garbage, many children are inspired by their dedication to helping keep streets clean. There has been a recent wave of films where POKENAME are featured to help normalize street cleaners as an honorable occupation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME survive living in landfills by wading through the muck to find plastic to eat. To defend themselves from fellow scavengers, they spray dirty water at their competition.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are a nightmare for plumbers throughout the world because they often get stuck in drainage pipes. Not only do plumbers have to drain clogged water but they may also have to face against POKENAME's powerful stings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collect construction waste to build out their bodies, taking broken bricks and concrete wherever they can. Poor management of a building site can result in large populations of POKENAME moving in and disrupting progress.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rummage through landfills to find plastic to consume. Their tough shells allow them to fall from great heights without hurting themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collects used electronics and batteries to power its body. It can generate magnetic fields to locate and attract any scrap metal and electronics in the area.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is always seen brandishing a plastic bag brimming with garbage. It spends its days gathering food scraps to add bulk to its weapon, though would-be predators are deterred by the stench alone.
author: anonymous_moose

entry: POKENAME drag trash into their thick sludge, from empty toothpaste tubes to used Potion bottles. They have a pungent smell and are chased away despite being helpful.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce a thick sludge from their cannons that is created after they eat lots of plastic. This sludge can be melted down and converted into renewable materials, but few people want to harvest the putrid sludge.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce a horrible stench that lingers on clothing for days. Many attempts at making their odor more tolerable through candles and incense have yielded no solution.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It scurries around beaches, dropping trash when it walks. It needs to eat 3 pounds of trash a day to not shrink.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME live in highly polluted waters, their bodies forming from industrial waste and microplastics. They have a drive to try and clean up their homes, consuming the pollutants that float in the water around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in highly polluted waters, their bodies forming from industrial waste and microplastics. They have a drive to try and clean up their homes, consuming the pollutants that float in the water around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME linger around gas stations and fuel depots; guzzling up litter, licking spilled fuel, and inhaling exhaust and fuel fumes. They process the contaminants and output clean soil, water, and air, leaving the places they inhabit spotless.
author: vic1312

entry: This Pokémon emits an overpowering scent of Strange Fruit. While most find the stench unbearable, certain wild Pokémon are strangely drawn to it.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME release a foul stench that is repulsive to most Pokémon. Rattata and Raticate are among the few that tolerate the smell, feeding POKENAME trash in exchange for a place to sharpen their teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME are commonly found sifting through trash and other waste, feeding on scrap metal and rotten food scraps. They favor large pieces of rebar as weapons and tools, but also as something to gnaw on for days.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are common inhabitants of landfills and garbage dumps, picking up trash with their right hands to then eat. They release poisonous gas from their left arms to defend themselves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME makes its home in a garbage can, subsisting on the trash thrown away by humans. When it pops out of its can, it is typically to drive others away, as it has a very grouchy personality.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use scraps of plastics and microplastics floating in the ocean to hold their bodies together, constantly seeking out oceanic waste to do so. Their bodies gradually degrade in sea water, making their presence toxic to other Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The bodies of POKENAME have developed to resemble various pieces of human trash floating in polluted waters. Though this is believed to have been to protect themselves from bird Pokémon, their bodies seem far too toxic to be consumable.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often go dumpster diving to find paper for their wings and nests. Once they find a suitable sheet, they squirt a biodegradable glue onto the paper and stick it onto their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have made their homes in urban alleyways, happily feeding on city residents' garbage. Cities with large populations of POKENAME have reported drastically reduced costs for trash removal.
author: fancyskunk

entry: The horns and fangs of a POKENAME have become like metal grinders that can churn large waste into little pieces for it to eat. Although some humans fear them a bit, they are often utilized in landfills to break apart larger pieces of trash.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon always wins the title of most-disliked fusion. When angry, which is quite often, POKENAME glides through the city in which it lives while spraying trash at unlucky pedestrians.
author: gooeygamer69

entry: POKENAME collects trash from the world's oceans and stores everything collected in sacks on its back. Its mournful song is said to make even the most careless people think twice about polluting its home.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME has fully absorbed small islands of garbage into its body, which has caused it to begin oozing a toxic slime. This Pokémon, once proud of its ability to clean pollution, now often finds itself isolated from others.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: During battles, POKENAME can end up literally smelling like hot garbage. In spite of their unpleasant smell, many can't resist POKENAME's dopey charm, even when they cuddle up and rub their soft coat of trash all over someone.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME are so condensed that any trash they expel shoots out with blinding speed. They shoot out shiny objects bent into the shape of amulets or trophies in an effort to become friends with strangers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is found near irradiated landfills, its body layered with unused polymers. Its shell acts as a pressurized waste chamber, converting synthetic debris into biofuel, preventing its own body from breaking down.
author: jaminmcready

entry: These airborne predators favor landfills and other poisonous areas, diving down to snatch prey within their pointed jaws. They appear to have eaten the fossilized remains of certain Pokémon and their bodies developed around the remains.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be found in the alleys of sprawling cities. Its entire body acts as its stomach, so any food tossed away on it is simply absorbed.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME collects trash in its muck-covered body and soars into thunderstorms to be struck by lightning. This fuses the trash together, which under the right circumstances forms Thunder Stones, and rains the fused trash down like hail.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The body of a POKENAME contains a highly combustible gas that can be ignited by clacking its teeth. They can form small bombs from this gas and hurl them at enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME scavenges junkyards to find parts to add to its body. If it finds any electronics, it can usually power them on to serve its own purposes.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME raids garbage cans in cities located near rivers and ponds. POKENAME leaks trashy liquid from its body with every step, leaving heaps of evidence after a trash raid.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME loves to jump around, splashing liquid garbage all over the place. Its entire body is mushy, rotten trash and it is frowned upon to bring one to public spaces.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The gills on the side of POKENAME's head detect methane emitted from rotting biological matter over 1km away. If overstimulated by excess putrescence, their gills leak a poisonous liquid.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are drawn to cities that have poor street sanitation, nesting amongst discarded trash bags and piles of waste. They feed on anything they can find on the floor; gnaw marks around dumpsters are a sure sign of their presence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME plucks garbage from containers and uses it to draw symbols upon the ground. It's believed this habit is an attempt at communication, but none have yet discovered meaning in the trash's shapes.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME feels particularly frightened, it uses its psychic powers to lift the surrounding garbage and hurl it at its enemies. The trash that forms its tail seems to have a mind of its own and bites anything that approaches POKENAME from behind.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME typically live under the landfills that they also eat from. Their bodies resemble the trash they devour, especially the discarded bars of rebar that they especially favor.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME's legs are like sturdy needles that can rather easily skewer myriad junk and debris which eventually gets absorbed into their upper bodies. They can "belch" toxic gas from their pincers to daze foes before pummeling them with punches.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon uses its strong arms to compact its own refuse into tight balls that they throw at their opponents. Wild POKENAME can often be found effectively swimming through mounds of trash and refuse.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be found outside schools and in garbage dumps, consuming trash. Whatever they don't fully eat becomes part of their body.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME have become widely used during the filming of movies. Any waste that the cast and crew produce is given to POKENAME, who fly it to designated waste points. This has helped shoots in wild locations without harming the environment.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are absolute fiends for trash, obsessed with filth. Some will even engage in turf wars where heaps of trash fly.
author: pankiwi

entry: Wild POKENAME have been spotted near ocean garbage patches containing fishing waste. The fusion's shiny fishing lure attracts aquatic prey.
author: hophoppip

entry: Repeated rolling charges wear down the tire along POKENAME's body over time, resulting in movement becoming unsteady. When the tire inevitably tears, its new immediate mission is to find a replacement.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME force cursors to drag files into the trash, even if the user still needs the file. If left unsupervised, they eventually drag all non-vital files into the trash.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers to sleep coiled up inside a dumpster. If it senses something approaching, it rises up from the dumpster with its hood flared out.
author: _aphoric

entry: POKENAME cheese is completely inedible. It reeks of garbage, as deadly mold grows on the cheese, and it is filled with parasites.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Wild POKENAME are drawn to polluted lakes and ponds, seemingly trying to clean them by feasting upon the waste floating in them. Unfortunately, their own bodies are so toxic they often add a different form of pollution to the water.
author: infinex21

entry: Smelly odor-releasing glands are on the sides of POKENAME's face. It roots through trash to search for all kinds of things to consume, including old electronics.
author: bobosmith01

entry: What may seem like a clump of trash floating in the water may actually be a POKENAME. Take caution when approaching, as it might spew toxic gases into the surrounding area.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The toxic gas released by a POKENAME is so thick and horrid that it is visibly an eerie purple color. They can easily subdue most opponents through the smell of this gas alone, but it is also so toxic that it may quickly end their torment.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their large magnets to carry cars and other scrap back to their homes, hoarding them for food. Many junkyards keep these Pokémon to help them move heavy materials.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME have tongues that are made of a material similar to a paper towel. They use this appendage to gather up all kinds of garbage and waste that they then digest for energy.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Video game designers often employ POKENAME to give advice on how to make proper sprites. Should an artist hate their sprite, they can feed it to POKENAME by deleting their work.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It is common to find a POKENAME living in the waste bin of a computer. It will consume all deleted files it finds in the bin, making it impossible to recover them. The Pokémon prefers corrupted files, which is uncommon for Porygon fusions.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Despite their appearance, POKENAME are one of nature's greatest protectors, as they can eat trash and drink polluted water. Their main goal is to protect the jungle from being polluted.
author: saucebolodu81

entry: POKENAME searches landfills for discarded cloth to dress itself in. It believes it looks best in simple things like potato sacks.
author: blitzydragon

entry: It camouflages itself by spraying different colored sludge on itself. The most skilled POKENAME cannot be detected by the human eye, but can be very easily identified by the human nose.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It has been joked that this fusion is 108 bad smells bound within a trash bag. It wafts toxic vapor in the air when angry.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME is a hard-to-tame fusion thanks to its hostility and power. Unprepared Trainers find themselves buried under trash hoards and toxic sludge.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME have a grotesque appearance that scares Trainers and Pokémon alike. Despite their gentle inclinations, many play up their ugly appearance to conform to social pressure.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These Pokémon have adapted to living within large, human cities where they feed off small refuse. The horn atop a POKENAME's head has taken the form of a dumpster to better secure food for it to eat later.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a result of people throwing things away in the ocean. It floats and takes trash with it, making an island of trash.
author: gamelord64

entry: POKENAME are orbited by myriad junk due to all of the magnetic debris they have consumed, but their most prized possession is their globe. The stench of their bodies is enough to drive away even most Poison-type Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the shiniest objects it can find as weapons. It will be severely angered if it loses its weapon of choice.
author: hophoppip

entry: It battles using assorted bits of trash fashioned into weapons and armor. Despite the shoddy appearance of its weaponry, it wields them with skill and precision in battle, making them far more effective than they seem.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME inhabits heavily polluted lakes, cleaning them by feeding on the refuse and garbage. As it consumes the pollution, its graceful body takes on additional aspects of the detritus, in turn causing people to be repulsed by the habitat savior.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Some of the garbage comprising POKENAME's body drips and falls off of it as it soars across the region. It needs to regularly stop and feast on trash dumps in order to regain some of its lost mass.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very peaceful creatures, yet no person ever dares to go near them due to how foul-smelling and gassy they are. Gloves must be worn at all times when around POKENAME since even a slight touch causes toxins to seep through the skin.
author: soup1900

entry: Every scrap within its territory is considered part of POKENAME's kingdom. It relentlessly collects discarded objects, convinced that every piece rightfully belongs to its hoard.
author: ilija09

entry: The white smoke of a POKENAME comes from burning refuse within its body. Its flames remove pollutants in the process, and the resulting smoke is surprisingly pleasant. Some humans use them to help clean up garbage.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME enjoy the polluted air and overflowing trash found in big cities. Many see this symbol of urban decay and disruption of nature as a nuisance.
author: entomoxie
