entry: POKENAME eats old food from the trash, saving any mold spores it finds to be released later as a defense mechanism. The trash can covering its tail prevents the worst of its toxic spores from constantly spreading into the air around it.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME are often found roaming cities, absorbing microplastics into their bodies wherever they go. They are commonly used at water purification plants, where they help treat drinking water.
author: santon5512

entry: Even after fusion, POKENAME tries to look like a Pikachu. However, since its body constitution is different, it had to improvise by mimicking Pikachu's ears and tail with mismatched and crudely altered parts.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME's body is made up of random assortments of rubbish, densely packed to give it its unique shape. It flies at subsonic speeds, randomly dropping large chunks of debris on whatever happens to be below.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME sprays a highly toxic gas out of its tail that forms a dense cloud of poison if not dealt with. This gas is also highly flammable, a simple ember capable of turning the cloud into an intense inferno.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME dwells in filthy places. It chews on batteries to drain their charge and power up its own electricity.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME lives in landfills and other filthy areas as it sustains itself on chemical waste. It scatters Toxic Spikes around to protect itself.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME form within city dumps and other similar areas with high densities of waste and refuse. They gather as much waste into their bodies as they can, and particularly bad instances of pollution can result in gargantuan POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It hunts down garbage-carrying boats and rams them until they sink. Even a single POKENAME can render a harbor uninhabitable if left unchecked.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME body grows as it eats waste, as does the pungent odor emanating from the ends of its limbs and from its mouth. It displays a childlike love for games and tricks, to the chagrin of many people.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be found in the sewer systems under large cities. They use their powers to keep plants and roots from clogging drainage pipes.
author: empathnaga

entry: The thick leachate POKENAME's body produces comes out at greater intervals during the summer months. It uses this to coat itself and prevent drying out.
author: .izik

entry: The garbage comprising POKENAME's body is so tightly compacted as to be as solid as stone. It picks up discarded litter from mountain travelers, using the trash to further strengthen its armor of refuse.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has stolen a dustbin lid to protect its insides. It is now so firmly stuck to it that it can stand on the edge and use it as a wheel.
author: chorb33

entry: Despite their appearance and odor, POKENAME are very competent waste management experts. They gather a group of smaller Trubnea around and together they gather litter in their territory. They celebrate a good day's work by feasting on the litter.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME hang around alleyways and garbage piles, gathering rubbish with their tails to replenish their bodies. Despite the components, their fur still feels very soft and comforting.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME's style of music isn't for everyone, composed of erratic screaming and clanging metal. It tends to appear at crowded concerts and underground nightclubs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME decorates its body with pieces of metal cans. When it shakes, its cans clank together, producing a powerful and mesmerizing sound.
author: hophoppip

entry: The flies that congregate around POKENAME form strange shapes at times. POKENAME reads these shapes to divine the future.
author: hophoppip

entry: The more a POKENAME dances, the more it sweats. Its sweat smells foul, and can burn nostrils up to a mile away.
author: gronkissimo

entry: Wild POKENAME nest within landfills and garbage dumps. They release puffs of toxic gas as they fly, often diving down to scoop up clumps of trash to eat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME mostly live in garbage dumps and survive on food that has been thrown away.  People have tried domesticating them, but most cannot stand the awful smell.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME constantly uses its psychic powers to hold together the scraps of trash that form its small body. It roams the outskirts of cities, scavenging for new junk to fuel the strength of its poisonous gases.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME meditates beneath huge piles of garbage within dumps, seeing it as the perfect place to hone its mental fortitude. Attempting to clean up its trashy home results in it turning aggressive.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are common in cities, but they're so shy that they're rarely seen. They form social hierarchies based on who has the best garbage collection.
author: admiralvermin

entry: The tube on top of POKENAME's head acts like another mouth. POKENAME is able to absorb any type of food and expel huge amounts of projectile garbage behind it.
author: dinner8480

entry: This POKENAME has a bad reputation among other Pokémon formed of garbage. POKENAME has a terrible temper and a huge tube in its mouth that it uses to steal food from others, extending the tube three meters or more.
author: dinner8480

entry: POKENAME thrive in polluted waters, consuming large amounts of trash. They use their metal claws to compact trash into small cubes, which they use to mark their territories.
author: santon5512

entry: Its oversized claw is perfect for catching Shellder, but not for breaking their shells. It breathes noxious gas into the seams until they open their shells to attempt to get fresh air.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME fly using the large plastic bag-like balloons emerging from their back. They consume rotting berries, holding them in a special stomach. POKENAME will flood the balloons on their back with gas from the decomposition, rising into the air.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME were raised along docks by fishermen due to the sound of their echoed cries being soothing to aquatic Pokémon. However, they quickly grew a love for the garbage that was left behind and now docks can easily become completely overrun by them.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME cultivates a floating trash heap in cold ocean waters, which it fearlessly defends from others who would usurp its rule or destroy the garbage. If it breaks one of its tusks, it fashions a replacement from materials like rebar.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Wild POKENAME favor swimming within polluted seas, ironically helping to clean them as they absorb the trash and pollutants into their bodies. They are frequent invaders of garbage barges and sometimes even sink them to use them as homes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are completely blind during the day, instead their eyes completely adapted to near perfect vision during the dead of night.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME will claim floating mounds of ocean trash as their home, spitting noxious poison at anything that approaches their domain. They will try to bridge their island with another POKENAME's island to build a nest.
author: divinelunaria

entry: POKENAME despise people who litter or throw away perfectly good items. They gather any piece of trash they find and use it to build up their fists, determined to get vengeance on the one that discarded the item.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It sleeps in junkyards and hides amongst trash bags for camouflage. It enjoys collecting various types of garbage and showing it off to others.
author: greystorm101

entry: POKENAME battles unusually. It throws its own garbage at other Pokémon and then eats the garbage. It also gives eggs to Trainers down on their luck.
author: rnrhorrorshow

entry: POKENAME float aimlessly in oceans, adding any trash they find to their body. Cities suffering from large amounts of pollution often deploy POKENAME in their local waterways to clean the trash, leaving them clean and safe to use.
author: chibitales

entry: Wild POKENAME roll around in trash and other debris, which is all eventually absorbed into their bodies if they do not fall off. Once a year, they must shed some of their garbage-like bodies so that they do not grow so large that they cannot move.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are found in crowded cities, especially those plagued by littering. They pile trash in central areas and sometimes use psychic abilities to subtly encourage others to help.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It loves picking up trash off the beaches near its nest. They have been relocated to trash patches in the ocean, where POKENAME can grow up to 40 feet tall.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's saliva contains toxins that can neutralize and disintegrate plastics. It drags heaps of coastal garbage into burrows to repurpose them into armor or bait.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Packs of POKENAME sun themselves on the shores of river deltas, waiting to swarm unaware prey like Slowpoke. The bubble on its back allows it to travel on land for a short amount of time if its habitat becomes inhospitable.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Because they are individually weak, POKENAME live and hunt in large swarms. Their small fangs are strong enough for them to tear through weak metal and solid wood; they demonstrate this by targeting supply caravans for their food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are commonly spotted along beaches and aside ocean-leading rivers, though they are easily carried away by the currents. They have explosive tempers and will launch themselves at the source of their agitation and then viciously bite it.
author: infinex21

entry: With shells as hard as iron slabs, wild POKENAME launch themselves at prey and at ships trespassing through their territory. Though they sustain many minor injuries by using themselves like missiles, they continuously grow stronger as well.
author: infinex21

entry: It thrives in seaside waters, blending into the surf with its agile movements. Its reflective scales shimmer like sea glass, masking it from potential threats.
author: .izik

entry: It prowls coastal waters, preying on fish that wander too close to shore. Strong waves aid its ambushes, hiding it beneath the surf.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims with many companions in saltwater to prevent larger Pokémon from attacking them. People usually leave the water when they spot even just one, as its bite is poisonous.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are infamously known for their insatiable appetites and ferocious tempers. They lash out at anything that enters their territory with such reckless abandon that they often destroy their own home and force themselves to have to relocate.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME compulsively bites anything that moves by its face, so watch your fingers! Its jaw has enough strength to crush rocks.
author: .realthree

entry: It scans digital signals left by passing vessels, tracking them across open waters. Its ability to interface with electronics makes it a peculiar but formidable hunter.
author: .izik

entry: It has a strange fascination with beach balls, biting them whenever it finds one. This habit often leads to popped toys scattered along the shore.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's propensity for biting things increases the more of them are together. A sufficiently sized group will go into a gnashing frenzy, capable of tearing a high-rise building apart in minutes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME operate in small packs to take down larger prey, but once the target is felled, all group cohesion is lost. Ravenous greed compels them to try and eat as much as they can for themselves, turning mealtime into a free-for-all.
author: sk372

entry: When hungry, it bites into any electronic device it can reach, as POKENAME converts electricity into nourishment for its body. It usually lives near large bodies of water alongside a sizeable group of companions.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It swims tirelessly, covering vast distances without rest. Relentless in its movements, it rarely surfaces, preferring to stay hidden below.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are very mischievous in combat, utilizing the maw on their tail to misdirect attention and attack opponents from unexpected angles. They require a lot of stimulation due to their intelligence, making them poor Pokémon for casual Trainers.
author: vic1312

entry: A smelly film coats its body, discouraging predators from attacking. This noxious layer lingers in the water long after it passes, marking its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often found swimming at the surface of tropical rivers, the plant on its back exuding a sweet scent to attract bird and bug Pokémon for a meal. When it dives, the plant clamps its jaws shut as overconsumption of water makes it sluggish.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This strong but not very clever Pokémon often rips the lures off fishing lines without even noticing. From afar, superstitious sailors often mistake POKENAME for a mermaid, until they swim closer and, to their disappointment, see its face.
author: milchik

entry: It prowls the sea floor, searching for prey hiding among the rocks. Its sharp fangs can pierce shells, making it a threat to many marine creatures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's pincers clamp down at a rapid pace, their sharpness and strength allowing them to tear a target apart in seconds. Rivalries in the wild are particularly vicious as two POKENAME try to rend chunks off their rival to establish dominance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scales ships by punching its hooked claws into the hulls. A swarm working in concert can sink even the most shipshape vessel.
author: wormspawn

entry: A sharp-toothed Pokémon usually found in swarms, their hot bodies significantly raise the temperature in an area. Though they appear vicious, they will flee when confronted one-on-one.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: This Pokémon uses its tentacles to catch foes, then delivers devastating bites with its powerful jaw.
author: welliss

entry: It is well-suited to maritime environments, riding ocean currents with ease. Other Pokémon follow its path, knowing it can navigate even the roughest waters.
author: .izik

entry: It hunts along beaches, waiting for prey to emerge from the surf. Its sharp teeth and aggressive behavior make it a danger to anything that ventures too close.
author: .izik

entry: It races along the coastline with its pack, hunting anything that moves by relying on its powerful hound-like sense of smell. Once it clamps down with jaws as strong as a hydraulic press, it refuses to let go.
author: fiordaliso

entry: With a single howl, POKENAME can summon its entire gang, surrounding prey within moments. Its bite is lethal, and encountering this Pokémon while visiting the seaside is considered extremely dangerous.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME use their sharp fangs to physically tear out viruses from the computers they're inside of. A swarm of them can clear out a computer virus that has infected an entire office building in one day.
author: soup1900

entry: Commonly referred to as the "Vermin of the Sands" by desert travelers, POKENAME are aggressive Pokémon that effectively swim through the sands. They typically attack travelers in an effort to steal, and consume, their supplies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME store water within their rubbery, transparent tails so they can explore and hunt on land. When they run low on stored water, their tails shrivel, and they quickly flee to any water to recuperate.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live and hunt in packs of at least five individuals, delivering quick attacks with the sharp fins on their arms. Because they can store water within their tails, they often hunt near shores as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their powerful legs to kick off surrounding rocks to propel themselves through the water. Using their fins to control their direction, groups of these Pokémon will attack a single target to take it down.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Although the largest schools of POKENAME are found within saltwater, some much smaller schools have been discovered in freshwater. They are quick and merciless predators who will swarm and assail prey with many vicious bites.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME inhabits larger and deeper swamps, swimming around deep in the muck. Once it senses another creature stuck in the muck, it goes into a hungry frenzy and attacks.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fins vibrate with excitement when prey draws close to its pond. It lunges out when they get near enough, clamping on with its jaws and dragging them into the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic senses to locate those around it with the meekest demeanor to bite. It seeks them out specifically because it is itself too weak-willed to go after anything that might fight back.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME easily goes into a feeding frenzy, grabbing anything edible with its tongue and gnashing it with its strong jaws. During this frenzy, its color changes to match whatever it is currently chomping down on.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are freshwater fish Pokémon that can perfectly camouflage themselves within the water. They only move when potential prey draws near enough, lunging toward them and attempting to bite down on them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can store water in the bowl-shaped flower on its back, which it uses to fire debilitating water blasts on land. In the water, it will swim below large prey and use the plant to create a whirlpool, entrapping the unprepared catch.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME tests its bite strength on objects floating through cave waterways. Should a tooth break off, a new one grows back within a matter of days.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME typically hunt in packs, using their tough claws and strong jaws to shred through anything that gets in their way. When separated, POKENAME quickly scurry away from any foes larger than themselves.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: With its powerful tail POKENAME can hurl huge waves of salt water and sand at its foes during beach battles. Its sharp, serrated teeth make its bites hard to heal.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME senses even the faintest vibrations through its skin. This enables it to detect prey many thousands of meters deep in the pitch-black ocean.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME lives in lakes and rivers, attacking boats that cross its path. Fighting back against them is difficult due to its hardened shell.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: Though not yet fully evolved, POKENAME shows a fiery disposition, snapping at outsiders who approach too closely. Its frame is armored with poisonous spikes and jagged horns that let it repel intruders larger and stronger than itself.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite their small size, POKENAME can reach swimming speeds of 10 miles per hour. They hunt as a group, rushing targets from multiple directions in carefully coordinated attacks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME crushes ice in its large jaws to test its bite strength. In polar environments, it constantly swims through the seas searching for the largest ice to bite.
author: .izik

entry: The underside of POKENAME's flippers have a set of sharp fang-like protrusions. Slapping and scarring others is an act of dominance over another POKENAME, an attempt to establish a pecking order among the group.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME pursues sailors who dare navigate through its ocean territory for weeks on end. It uses its spectral shroud to hold enemies in place, leaving them defenseless against the strikes of its sharp, serrated blade.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It attacks anyone who dares approach its territory, charging forward with its horn coated in venom. Though ruthless toward intruders, it shows great affection to its own kind, letting the young ones play with the bubbles it blows from its mouth.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a formidable predator that hunts along the shores in the company of its pack. It uses its powerful jaws to deliver lethal blows, often finishing off its prey with ease. The largest specimen is recognized as the leader of the group.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are the rarely-seen leaders of Caron schools that tend to stay and guard the underwater caves that they dig out. Their claws and fangs are often tough enough to tear through metal, which they use to defend their homes and schools of Caron.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME patiently hides in underwater crevices as it waits for prey to swim close. When it sees a stronger Pokémon, it quickly retreats into these holes.
author: mepp.

entry: While swimming through brackish waters, POKENAME releases an aura that soothes those nearby. It uses this opportunity to swim close to prey before taking a bite.
author: .izik

entry: Highly territorial, POKENAME uses its sheer brute strength to drive away ships that venture too close to its coastal den. When it slams its massive tail against the ground, it can shake the earth with enough force to trigger violent quakes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have incredibly rough scales that are capable of grating solid rock and damaging ship hulls if they collide against either. They typically hunt down large schools of small Pokémon, swallowing many of them whole per meal.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have jaws powerful enough to tear a hole in a ship's hull and use their strong legs on land or underwater to launch themselves at high speeds. Their strength fades the longer they go without water exposure.
author: infinex21

entry: It clings to the sides of boats, waiting for scraps to fall overboard. Mariners often mistake it for debris until it sinks its teeth into an unsuspecting hand.
author: .izik

entry: It inhabits lakes, using submerged objects to create intricate lairs. With its sharp teeth, it cuts through weeds and plants that block its path.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fur is short and stiff, creating a streamlined shape that allows them to swim rapidly through the water. Their nine fins at the back of their body keep them stable as they assume a torpedo shape to swim through the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Sailors tell tales of it attacking boats with relentless fury, gnawing through wood and ropes. It often works with others of its kind, making it a formidable threat on open waters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are full of energy, and can swim for an entire night without stopping. When one POKENAME smells fear, it will find others to gang up on its victim in a swarm.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The pheromones exuded by these Pokémon effectively induce drowsiness within others near them. Though POKENAME initially appear to laze around, they will viciously lash out when their prey or foes succumb to their pheromones.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can stretch its jaws and consume prey larger than its body. It only targets prey that is incapable of damaging it from within.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME are considerably slow on land but stunningly quick in water, with rock-solid fangs that can withstand biting solid rock. POKENAME hunt in schools of up to 10 capable of taking down other Pokémon larger than themselves rather swiftly.
author: infinex21

entry: It patrols streams, lurking beneath the surface in search of smaller prey. Its presence makes these waterways dangerous, forcing other Pokémon to avoid them.
author: .izik

entry: To strengthen its jaws, POKENAME constantly chews on the hard edges of rocky cliffs. It lives in fairly large groups and builds its den along the coasts of warm seas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To strengthen its jaws, POKENAME constantly chews on the hard edges of rocky cliffs. It lives in fairly large groups and builds its den along the coasts of warm seas.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's jaws gnash in time with the rotation of its gears. Should it sniff wounded prey, the gears go into overdrive and its mouths chomp at an extremely rapid pace, ready to tear its prospective meal apart.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims with its flower on the surface of the water to catch unsuspecting prey like Politoed in the jaws of the plant. The plant and body have different stomachs, so they have to share food to grow in synchronicity.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME swims with its flower on the surface of the water to catch unsuspecting prey like Politoed in the jaws of the plant. The plant and body have different stomachs, so they have to share food to grow in synchronicity.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Though POKENAME spends most of its life in seawater, its scales remain warm from the fire burning within. When enraged, it snorts small clouds of steam from its nostrils.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If a POKENAME wraps its string around the mast of a boat, it needs to be removed immediately. If allowed to stay, it will be joined by other POKENAME that will quickly tear the boat to shreds.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME groups reflexively sharpen their tusks as a whole; when one begins grinding against a rock or tree, they all instinctively do the same so every member has pristine and sharp tusks.
author: sk372

entry: It hides in deep caverns beneath the ocean floor, waiting patiently to ambush prey. The dim lighting helps it remain undetected until it strikes.
author: .izik

entry: Known for ambushing prey in shallow water, POKENAME uses its sharp spear with unsettling glee. Its chaotic fighting style is seen as reprehensible by many who encounter the aftermath.
author: jaminmcready

entry: This POKENAME has the strength and aggression of a whole school. It will lead swarms of smaller fry on a voracious rampage.
author: serversizeme

entry: It is known to stalk injured prey for miles before delivering a final strike. It enjoys toying with its food before eating it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases powerful bursts of noise from its strong jaws to navigate beneath deep lakes. These bursts are strong enough to destroy boulders.
author: .izik

entry: It patrols lagoons at night, using echolocation to find prey. Its sharp fangs tear through anything it catches, leaving little behind.
author: .izik

entry: It lurks near docks, waiting for opportunities to strike unsuspecting prey. Sailors keep a wary eye on the water, knowing that it can appear at any moment.
author: .izik

entry: Sliding toward prey with surprising speed, POKENAME latches onto them with its jaws and shakes them fiercely. Its soft body absorbs retaliatory blows with ease.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: In the right mindset, POKENAME can be a scourge on ships on the water. However, they often lack enough motivation to attack the ships and are more commonly kept as rowdy pets, as they are not regarded as dangerous Pokémon.
author: dualblades1147

entry: It stalks submarines, drawn to the metallic hum they produce. Once attached to the hull, it gnaws persistently, leaving deep gashes in the metal.
author: .izik

entry: It becomes more active at sunset, using the dim light to hunt unseen. Coral reefs at dusk fall silent when it approaches, as prey scatter to avoid it.
author: .izik

entry: Its skin secretes a mild acid that corrodes anything it touches if given enough time. The acid leaves faint marks on rocks and shells, warning others of its presence.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are a common species of underwater Pokémon that often laze about near along the shores of rivers, often becoming the hosts of mushroom spores. If disturbed from their rest, they will viciously bite at the nearest living thing.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME move in herds, their heavy footsteps being heard from miles away. Their colourful frills are used to confuse prey before moving in to attack all together.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: It patrols coral reefs, protecting its territory from intruders. Its sharp teeth can slice through coral effortlessly, allowing it to shape its environment to its liking.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a fierce predator found near bodies of water, known for its lightning-fast jaws and ferocious attacks. Only its crest is visible above the water surface, so tourists are advised to watch for it while swimming.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME is able to sense when stones and gems develop cracks and weaknesses. Once it detects a damaged rock in its vicinity, it quickly descends on it and devours it in seconds with its tough jaws.
author: sk372

entry: When submerged in freshwater, the bark on POKENAME's body grows incredibly thick. At times this bark can become as tough as jade.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME finds itself alone, it tries to channel the illusion of other POKENAME or Carvanha to give it the courage to hunt. Ships are advised to avoid any areas where they see flames flickering on the surface, a sure sign of their habitat.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME often leap out at parked boats, eager to tear them to pieces. Despite their high speed and fearsome bite, they are easily spooked by a boat's horn.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME lies in shallow water, patiently waiting for its next meal. Sailboats that pass overhead are reeled in with its remarkably accurate harpoon, leaving only drifting debris of the ship that once was.
author: dodoowner_

entry: In the past, POKENAME were used by pirates to steal treasure. Studies confirm that the Remoraid they wield are not harmed by POKENAME.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It is attracted to the sound of music and dancing, and will gather a pack of other POKENAME to go and invade any party it finds. They then engage in roughhousing, fights, and chaotic dancing, effectively ruining the party.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Its bite is incredibly powerful, capable of shattering even the toughest stones. When enraged, it snorts small clouds of steam from its nostrils.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME patrols coastal waters in search of food alongside others of its kind, as it's far more timid than it appears. When an ally is in danger, it spits bluish flames from its jaws to drive enemies away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It's been discovered that POKENAME are highly receptive to chocolate. Ships now often carry surplus containers to toss overboard and placate schools of POKENAME to keep them from becoming aggressive.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives by the shore with its pack, which not only protects it but also helps refine its hunting skills. In battle, it relentlessly snaps at its foe, but if it realizes it has been left alone, it quickly loses the will to fight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swim in zigzag patterns, even as they hunt prey. They are capable of temporarily walking on land, though they still move in zigzag patterns. POKENAME tend to live in large groups and collectively target large prey.
author: infinex21

entry: So long as POKENAME move in straight lines, they can achieve swimming speeds that surpass small motorboats. They struggle to turn while swimming, so they hunt in large packs so that at least one of them will catch their prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live in large swarms and will gang up on larger foes. Though they are small, the venom in their horns is potent. They can also spit a toxic fluid, which is capable of corroding ship hulls.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lies in wait beneath the ground, able to sense the vibrations in the dirt above it. It attacks prey from underneath, opening a hole in the ground for the target to fall in before all three go into a gnashing feeding frenzy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are most dangerous in groups, as they will coordinatedly swarm their targets, tearing into them with talons and fangs alike. They are capable of breathing underwater and can swim as easily as they can fly, so they have a broad list of prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME patrols rivers from high above. It descends with its flock to snatch prey even when it is beneath the water's surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies above the sea waiting for the right opportunity to strike. Once it spots prey below the surface, it dives down and bites onto its prey before surfacing, quickly securing its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flocks circle over the ocean in search of schooling fish Pokémon. When they find one, they dive in unison, swimming straight through the school with their large beak wide open, catching as much food as they can in one bite.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It slips through canals with ease, navigating narrow waterways to hunt. Trainers in cities must remain cautious, as it has been known to nibble on unattended belongings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cannot swim well, so they mostly just walk along the seabed; this ironically causes many predators to see them as easy prey. POKENAME are strengthened by constant attempts made by predators and the crushing, watery depths they reside in.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME does not enjoy captivity, as it enjoys running through tropical forests and swimming in jungle rivers. If it finds itself in an enclosed space, it becomes highly aggressive and bites down with Thunder Fangs until it can escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swim in packs to hunt and shock their prey. These shocks can interfere with ship interfaces and cause the ship to lose control and crash.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME are swift aquatic predators, able to swim at high speed through Hoenn's oceans. Their whiskers are sensitive and can pick up the eddies in the water left by other Pokémon, allowing them to track prey across great distances.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in large groups because they are weak by themselves. Together, by joining hands, they can properly release electricity and take down most prey. If a POKENAME is found alone, it will lash out with weak strikes and even weaker bolts.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's tail whirs and spins like a propeller while it swims through jungle rivers. When it grows tired, its tail sparks uncontrollably as it continues to spin.
author: .izik

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME's hump protrudes above the water of its lake home. The surrounding water stays at a high temperature, only reaching a boil if it is having a nightmare.
author: .izik

entry: It lurks in bays, waiting patiently for small fish to pass by. When disturbed, it creates a flurry of bubbles to confuse its pursuers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slithers through lakes at high speeds in search of prey like Surskit. It uses its serrated tail to slash at the foe, leaving little chance of escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME charge at their prey at full speed, seeking to wedge their prey within their crescent bodies and cutting into them with their beaks. Their activity is seemingly affected by the phases of the moon, with them being most active when it is full.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can snap their claws so quickly that they produce loud bubbles that generate lots of heat. They rely on these bubbles to stun prey or break open rocky burrows before sinking their fangs into another meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It creates large splashes as it leaps from the water, showing off its power. These displays often serve as a warning to intruders in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shells have a sharp edge that can cut through fins, making them incredibly dangerous for divers. There have been many incidents where divers lose a finger trying to pick up a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME normally lives deep in the sea, they are known to swarm near the surface when it storms. They target struggling prey, tearing them to bits with razor-sharp fangs.
author: mepp.

entry: Its natural rarity, bright colors, and general rebellious attitude has made toys based off of POKENAME very popular with young boys. It stores objects in their muddy nest as teething tools: through chewing, it can help keep its teeth razor sharp.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME has sniffed out large prey, it dives and latches onto them with its nose before letting out a shrill cry. This call summons the rest of the flock to descend on the target and begin the feeding frenzy.
author: sk372

entry: By themselves, POKENAME are relatively harmless. When they attack as a school, however, the electricity shared between them increases dramatically, turning a barrage of bites into a powerful electric assault.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Despite its fearsome and massive appearance, POKENAME is a very shy Pokémon that usually soars over the coasts of deserted islands in the sea. It attacks only to defend its territory and gains confidence when in the company of others of its kind.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Wetlands are its favored hunting grounds, where it stalks prey hidden among reeds. The murky water masks its approach, making it a dangerous predator.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often seemingly floating in water as they sleep. If a POKENAME is disturbed from its slumber, it will either lash out with a Bite or use Teleport to change its location. POKENAME have rarely warped aboard ships and raided them for food.
author: infinex21

entry: It plants itself on the seafloor, munching on anything it can get its mouth on. Its leaf-like fins allow it to swim away from predators, even though it cannot swim very fast.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite its fierce and intimidating appearance, POKENAME rarely attacks other Pokémon or ships when separated from its flock. When defending its territory, it releases a bluish flame from its tail tip to boost its courage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It lurks in kelp forests, using the dense vegetation to conceal its presence. With quick, darting movements, it navigates through the tangled leaves with ease.
author: .izik

entry: It trails kayaks along coastal waters, drawn by the sounds and splashes. Its sharp teeth make it a hazard to those who venture too close.
author: .izik

entry: It prowls the waterways near villages, sneaking in to snatch food scraps. Its slow, deliberate movements deceive others into thinking it is harmless.
author: .izik

entry: The Carvanha on its tail is fossilized, and attached as a decoration. Nevertheless, POKENAME often uses it as a bat to bash its rivals.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: It thrives in waters contaminated with nuclear waste, absorbing toxins that enhance its strength. Its toxic presence makes the surrounding area hazardous for all life.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's stench drives away its prey before they can even see them. This caused POKENAME to become bottom feeders in the bodies of water, which in turn makes them stink even more.
author: markusknight

entry: It leaves globs of sludge wherever it swims, contaminating the waters. This pollution makes it difficult for other creatures to survive nearby.
author: .izik

entry: It gnaws on anchors dropped into the water, mistaking them for prey. Sailors often find deep bite marks on their equipment after anchoring near its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is found along beaches and ports where it will steal freshly caught fish from other Pokémon or humans. It is rather slow on land, but speeds up in the water by using its vines to aid in propulsion.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is highly aggressive and will try to bully anyone into doing its bidding. Its sharp teeth can cut through the thick skin of large Berries.
author: t.i.a.

entry: It is a common pest at hydroelectric dams, as it will bite into anything flowing with electricity and leech that energy for itself. It is difficult to safely remove a POKENAME, as the slightest stimulus could cause it to fly into an explosive rage.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wraps its tail around ship chains while sleeping. If disturbed, it bites with jaws strong enough to crush granite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses Smokescreen to darken the waters before striking. The murk somehow doesn't hinder its own sight as it effortlessly bites through defenses as strong as tungsten.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims gracefully through tropical seas. When prey is spotted, it bites with enough force to rip through iron.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rests against underwater surfaces until something swims past it, triggering its hunting instinct. It locks onto prey and rotates rapidly towards them, each limb viciously sharp and capable of making deep, deadly cuts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is so ravenous that it can even devour coral, crushing it beneath its fearsome teeth. The venomous sting on its tail is used to weaken its enemies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are actually quite harmful to aquatic habitats; whenever one is spotted, it is best for them to be caught as quickly as possible.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME is extremely territorial, especially with its dwindling population, and viciously sinks ships and attacks anything while protecting its nesting grounds. Daring captains train POKENAME to protect their ships on voyages.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is extremely territorial, especially with its dwindling population, and viciously sinks ships and attacks anything while protecting its nesting grounds. Daring captains train POKENAME to protect their ships on voyages.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME often let smaller Pokémon, such as Bruxish and Remoraid, live in their shells. Due to their dwindling numbers, POKENAME have become increasingly violent towards humans.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: Due to its malleable body, its skin is too smooth and its fangs too soft to cause damage. That fact it has to mimic other Pokémon to be a threat causes it no end of vexation.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME zooms through the waters at breakneck speeds, tackling hard into anything that ventures its territory. On occasion, submarines have mistook POKENAME attacks for being hit by torpedoes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's jaws are strong enough to rip through the shells of the Cloyster they hunt. In battle, POKENAME swallows water before shooting it back out with the force of a geyser.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME is a hunter inhabiting bodies of water within caverns. It isn't the fastest when swimming, but leaps onto land and scuttles with surprising speed, biting hapless creatures and dragging them underwater.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME nests high on coastal cliffs where it can survey its habitat for prey, even taking down the likes of Wailord if it works with others of its kind. POKENAME flies and swims at speeds rivaling human-made transportation in those environments.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME cuts through the air and the ocean depths with the same incredible speed. With its extreme strength and aggression, it is considered an apex predator of both biomes.
author: sk372

entry: A confirmed sighting of a wild POKENAME is considered an emergency, due to its extremely violent and territorial nature. Nearby towns are issued stay-inside warnings until professional Trainers can come and successfully deal with POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims in tropical waters and is most often found around coral reefs, patrolling their territory in search of food. Their fine fur burns hot on contact with air and produces a lot of heat even underwater, producing a steam trail as they swim.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are incredibly territorial and will constantly fight with each other over their prey. POKENAME prey on larger fish Pokémon, brutally attacking them with their sharp beak and talons.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME fires Electro Ball to knock avian Pokémon into the sea. It then bites down hard and drags them underwater so it can feast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a dominant predator of deep ocean trenches, using its light to surprise prey before devouring them in only a few bites. It is rare to see POKENAME near the ocean surface, but when one is found it is usually disoriented and defensive.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is silent in its movement, so it often startles those it happens upon, disheartening it. It seeks to share happiness with others, and ends up being oblivious to when those it interacts with would rather be alone.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sneaks into the holds of ships to devour every scrap of food it can find. Its razor-sharp teeth are so strong that it could gnaw through iron anchors without the slightest difficulty.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will try and bite anything that moves, making it very easy to catch when fishing with live bait. When on the end of the line it will thrash about violently, but once it has been reeled in it becomes very docile.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is lazy, swimming with its mouth open in hopes of catching an unaware meal or basking in the sun hoping scavengers get too curious. Its vicious appearance makes it an excellent guardian pet as it actually loves playing with children.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is lazy, swimming with its mouth open in hopes of catching an unaware meal or basking in the sun hoping scavengers get too curious. Its vicious appearance makes it an excellent guardian pet as it actually loves playing with children.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME fight for territory by using their vines to fling the razor-sharp petals of their flower bulbs at each other. The more scars a POKENAME bears, the more respect it commands from others.
author: sk372

entry: Its anchor and chain drag across the seafloor as POKENAME swims. If its chain has slack, it can jet water to catch something nearby.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Despite being very prolific hunters, the population of POKENAME has decreased severely over the last 50 years. The meat of POKENAME is viewed as a rare delicacy by gourmets and thrill hunters alike, as the meat is very poisonous when prepared wrong.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME uses its fin-like wings to swiftly propel itself forward. It can exert pressure of up to 700 PSI with its shark-shaped claws.
author: adam_dnh

entry: Whenever their prey seem to outswim them, POKENAME use the boosters on their back to catch up. Many reports say that POKENAME have been seen punching deep holes into boats during a chase.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME is just as fast in the water as it is in the air. Researchers have determined this is because of the crest on its head.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME lies hidden in plain sight among other Corsola fusions, before releasing a burst of water to jet out and snap up unwary prey. Despite its predatory nature, it is content to be fed treats by divers and even begs at docks for tourists.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is highly intelligent and sneaks around reefs to catch larger prey unaware. It is independent and distrustful of others, and it will become aggressively protective of its Trainer once it trusts them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME thrives in the open ocean where it can burst out of the water to snag bird Pokémon as a meal. When it leaps over boats, people recoil in fear of its appearance, but it is only a danger if the Carvanha hitching a ride falls off onto the deck.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME jets through the air at impossibly fast speeds, and can cleave trees in two with its sharp limbs as it flies past. It produces Sharpedo-shaped explosive projectiles to launch at opponents and prey.
author: sk372

entry: If danger looms near its wounded kin, POKENAME emits a plume of scalding steam from its jaws, forcing attackers to retreat. Though known for its lethal bite, its true strength lies in its unmatched agility on land and underwater.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If danger looms near its wounded kin, POKENAME emits a plume of scalding steam from its jaws, forcing attackers to retreat. Though known for its lethal bite, its true strength lies in its unmatched agility on land and underwater.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When angered, POKENAME's body temperature rises so much that it can heat the very waters it swims through while hunting. It competes with others of its kind by biting the anchors of ships to determine who has the strongest jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When enraged, POKENAME's internal heat surges until the waters around it begin to simmer. Members of this species often clash by biting through ship anchors, testing which one possesses the fiercest jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME zip through the sea with navy camouflage and search for prey to consume. Their jaw stretches over Pokémon larger than themselves to be digested by their stomach acids.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stealthily swims through kelp forests to observe other inhabitants for weaknesses, which it exploits by bullying them to steal food. This practice allows it to preserve its vast energy to drive competitors from its territory.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The inspiration for POKENAME's art comes from movies about Sharpedo attacks. Wild POKENAME have been found with stockpiles of Sharpedo movie memorabilia adorning their dens.
author: hophoppip

entry: The teeth it sheds naturally are collected and used to craft the Razor Fangs sold in Pokémarts. POKENAME is fiercely territorial and makes a habit of attacking anyone who intrudes upon the sea caves where it makes its den.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses the powerful electroreceptors in its body to detect the organisms around it. From a distance, it can even decipher the nuances of electric impulses in another's brain to determine their emotional state.
author: bobosmith01

entry: This vicious predator uses its blinding speed to launch dizzying assaults on its opponent. When POKENAME is sighted near a body of water or beach there are usually calls to evacuate the nearby area.
author: evilgammon

entry: A vampire of the sea, they ride water currents with incredible speed to hunt. Trainers are advised not to release this fusion back into the wild.
author: nelluc27

entry: Despite its large size, POKENAME is completely silent while swimming. It has been seen launching itself out the water to hook its tusks into prey, bringing them back down with it.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective of underwater plant-life. If an unwelcome guest ventures too close to its territory it fights fiercely to defend it, never stopping its assault no matter how scarred and injured it gets.
author: sk372

entry: It is dangerous to venture into the rainforest rivers where the combative POKENAME makes its home.  Fortune-seekers make the attempt nevertheless, as the seeds on its back are a valuable delicacy.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME can run up to 75mph, and uses its anchor and its talons to attack. Its fins used to be harvested for foodstuffs, so POKENAME was often a victim of hunting.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The bubbles on the backs of POKENAME can provide oxygen to people who are drowning. It will only give to those who respect smaller fish Pokémon.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly vicious opponent to face in battle. It won't stop clawing, kicking, or biting at a foe until they or it are covered in wounds; a POKENAME judges the quality of a fight by the number of battle scars left behind.
author: sk372

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME can swim through thick mud as easily as they can swim in water. Their head fins are a common sight within marshes and swamps as they encircle their targets and prepare to pounce.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME gains multiple scars over its lifetime due to vicious fights with rivals in the wild. When the scars ache, it applies mud on the wounds to temporarily soothe the pain.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME creates sandbanks to beach boats, allowing it to easily attack the freshly stranded passengers. Its skin dries out quickly, and some Trainers put mud on it to keep it cool if out of water.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME has a strong urge to bite those who swim past it, though its bite is rather weak. It tries to growl and be intimidating, but even a light retaliatory tap will send it swimming away, crying in terror.
author: sk372

entry: Found replacing the figurehead on sunken ships, POKENAME sings a lilting melody, attracting Water-types. When they close in, it confuses its prey with a Water Pulse before finishing them with a vicious bite.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Despite it having great hunting instincts, POKENAME's personality is sweet and almost childish. The sight of it happily singing next to freshly-caught prey has been described as disconcerting to many.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is usually seen in the ocean, harassing ships but ultimately not harming anyone. It's said pirates followed POKENAME in the past.
author: blazerxz

entry: An aggressive undersea hunter, POKENAME grabs onto speedy swimmers with its tongue, gnashing its teeth as they are pulled into its maw. Its tongue is covered with scars from biting itself during these feeding frenzies.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leisurely patrols the reef it controls, chasing off other ocean apex predators and snagging unaware prey with its anemone tentacles. It moves slowly unless there is a threat to its dominance, launching a surprise attack in a burst of energy.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Tales of POKENAME preying on fishermen lead to the over-hunting of the Pokémon. In recent years, these stories have been dismissed as fiction, and their numbers are slowly recovering.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME strikes prey by whipping its neck forward with incredible speed and snapping with its maw. Its teeth are sharp enough to pierce steel plating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prowls tropical reefs and kelp forests, using its enhanced aquatic agility to pursue fast prey. Recent fossil discoveries reveal that this Pokémon remains largely unchanged from how it appeared in the past as an apex predator.
author: pjporwoll

entry: With a lust for violence, many POKENAME are recruited as hired muscle. It'll lend its services to anyone who offers it the biggest and best weapons.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME has ferocious power. Even without a weapon, it can crush a military-grade torpedo. It features a wild yet hedonistic personality.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can create suction that sucks in everything within a kilometer. It can wipe out life within several kilometers of sea in just a few weeks.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can create suction that sucks in everything within a kilometer. It can wipe out life within several kilometers of sea in just a few weeks.
author: chorb33

entry: Wild POKENAME are so quick to challenge other Pokémon near the beaches they live upon that their bodies are always covered in many scars. Their many fangs break rather easily during battle as they bite their foes but they always grow back tougher.
author: infinex21

entry: Due to POKENAME's dense and heavy body, it is far less mobile in the water than on land. It is highly aggressive and ravenous, hunting and eating prey up to eight times a day.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live on the bottom of seabeds. Small aquatic Pokémon will inhabit the debris upon its back and keep its shell clean for it. Because of this, many aquariums will keep a POKENAME in their large exhibits as enrichment for other Pokémon.
author: jadey.1557

entry: POKENAME's tail ends in a bit of water that can be hardened to razor sharpness. Rivals in the wild fight viciously with these blades, gaining innumerable cuts over their body in the process.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are able to surf along the water just by getting a good head start. This helps them during hunts if their prey gets too fast for them to catch.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME is exceedingly proud and attempts to strongarm other small Pokémon into joining its pirate gang and raiding berry stashes of much larger Pokémon. It has an intense rivalry with Squirtles.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be seen stalking fishing vessels at night. It regularly steals tools and equipment from these vessels to keep as trophies in its underwater den.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their large anchor to break through the hulls of ships that enter their territory. If they can lead a boat into an iceberg, they become filled with joy.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It has an extremely aggressive streak and seeks to battle any powerful opponent it can find, especially others of its kind. POKENAME wears every chip and scar on its blade with pride, as each signifies a vicious fight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME considers sunken ships its territory, and strikes viciously at any who would trespass on its home. It's known to be especially aggressive and violent towards Dhelmise.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the anchor on its tail to keep to the sea floor while it's on the prowl. On land, the anchor proves to be a powerful defensive weapon.
author: vaporvenator

entry: A colossal underwater behemoth with jaws that easily shred ships' hulls and surprisingly cunning intellects. POKENAME are clad in the remains of ships they've torn apart as proof of their terrifying cunning.
author: infinex21

entry: Ferocious wild POKENAME have recently been discovered using sunken ships as homes. Any daring treasure hunter that attempts to explore these vessels may not make it back alive.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME is known as “The Tyrant of the Seas” due to its aggressiveness and brutality. The two golden fins on its body are sharp enough to slice through steel and allow it to maintain flight after it launches itself out of the water.
author: mepp.

entry: By facing upwards and rotating its center gear while underwater, POKENAME is able to create large whirlpools that pull in and shred prey, as well as any boats unfortunate enough to cross its path.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME greatly prefers a solitary existence, eschewing most types of companionship. If agitated, it whips its many ribbons around wildly, the edges of which are sharp enough to leave deep gashes.
author: sk372

entry: Its many teeth are often the last sight for unaware deep sea divers and small aquatic Pokémon alike. The markings along the bodies of these Pokémon glow within the depths and only dim when they are hunting.
author: infinex21

entry: This underwater leviathan of a Pokémon lives within only the deepest, darkest undersea trenches. POKENAME's body is covered in countless scars from its many battles with other underwater Pokémon over over territory and prey alike.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME commands the depths with unrivaled power and speed. Its metallic fins slice through water and time itself, leaving chaos in its wake.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME is also called "the Grim Reaper of The Seven Seas". Whenever POKENAME is spotted in a body of water, it is recommended to stay on land. Their razor-sharp claws can effortlessly sink even the most armored ship.
author: sottiwotti

entry: This Pokémon lives and hunts in arctic waters, though it is capable of staying on land for periods of time. The ice along its body protects it while also giving it a deadly horn that allows it to quickly impale any of its prey.
author: infinex21

entry: Although the range is limited, POKENAME can stretch their necks around half a foot and ambush targets with swift, biting attacks. They can move swiftly in water and are agile on land, which makes them tricky foes to overcome.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are fairly kindhearted on land, but turn incredibly vicious when in water. By using both its fangs and sturdy tusks, POKENAME can cut through almost anything.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME has adapted its appearance to look like a Sharpedo, even mimicking the way it swims across the seafloor. However, it is basically harmless, only feeding on small sea plants.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a feared predator that soars above lawless areas where roving bands of criminals gather. Though taverns often post bounty posters with a big reward if one is captured alive, nobody has succeeded in this quest.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: A single POKENAME has been observed to devour an entire school of Magikarp. They get into frequent fights with dragon Pokémon, whipping up storms as they clash.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME are a favourite Pokémon amongst many ocean exploration organisations thanks to their speed in the water and their ability to tolerate swimming at great depths. Their many fins help them manoeuvre in even the stormiest of seas.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spins at high speeds beneath the ocean's surface, piercing into the seafloor like a lance. This creates massive tunnels for others of its kind to inhabit.
author: .izik

entry: It regularly fills up with air by swimming to the surface. Despite its chunky physique, it can quickly change direction by expelling the stored air.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME live in family groups led by a head male Sharpray. They will roam, bullying any vulnerable Pokémon they see. If they ever betray the boss Sharpray, they will be attacked mercilessly until they fall in line.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME's song carries great distances across the water, sending distant prey into a helpless slumber. With its quick swimming speed, it can snatch up its sleeping target with ease.
author: sk372

entry: The jaws of POKENAME are unassumingly strong enough to tear through metal ship hulls and deep sea rocks. Their teeth quickly regrow if they break, and they grow back stronger thus resulting in them being tougher than most metals.
author: infinex21

entry: Even a small drop of blood with send POKENAME into a feeding frenzy. Once it gets a taste of its prey, it will keep eating away until nothing is left but bone.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The edges of POKENAME's gears are extremely sharp. It fires the smaller gear from its body at distant prey, cutting them and allowing it to track them easier by following the scent of blood from the wound.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon's thorns in their roses are powerful darts. It hides in tall grass and sneakily fires the darts into other Pokémon without warning.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Most planes are routed to fly around POKENAME territories, but when that isn't possible, they will bring a team of flying Pokémon to defend them. A swarm of POKENAME can rip through iron in a matter of seconds.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME creates a constant bubble around itself that it uses to swim through the air and land. This allows it to hunt in the skies when competition for food in the water gets too competitive.
author: camtft

entry: Flocks of POKENAME descend upon forests in large clouds of chirping and feathers. They take turns torpedoing out of the flock at weaker bird Pokémon to hunt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lay at the bottom of the ocean floor where they ambush prey with a jolt of electricity. If two POKENAME meet during the courtship season, they exchange bites on each other's fins to signal interest in one another.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME were once terrors of the sea. Long ago, they would careen at high speeds into the sides of wooden ships, gouging holes through the hull to sink them. They would then dive into the wreckage and collect any treasure left behind.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: At dusk, schools of POKENAME feed ravenously, wiping out entire reefs. They abandon injured allies without hesitation while on a hunt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is usually found near large groups of Water-type Pokémon. Most fishermen hate it because its multiple sharp fins cut through their nets.
author: swangfrog04

entry: Its blade-like fins can cut stone like butter. Some have been seen cutting the likes of Gyarados and Wailord to pieces by themselves.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: POKENAME releases bursts of noise from its ears to stun nearby fish Pokémon while hunting. Once disabled, it strikes with a powerful Crunch.
author: .izik

entry: If it sees a large school of fish while it's flying over the ocean, POKENAME will fire a powerful sound wave that instantly takes out most of the school. It will fiercely fight other POKENAME over their prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hums a grating bass melody as it stalks prey before dive-bombing them. If a school of POKENAME engage in a feeding frenzy, it can stir the winds into a tornado or waterspout.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This soft and cuddly Pokémon is said to have no thoughts inside its plush head. It provides comfort, love and protection to those who need it.
author: rooboid

entry: POKENAME travels through brackish waters at high speeds. It swings its anchor-like body in large circles, knocking out any prey it strikes in an instant.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME utilizes mimicry where its crown looks like a Sharpedo, warding off predators like Bruxish. To attract scavenging aquatic Pokémon for a meal, it flexes muscles in the fake mouth to extend a tongue and seem like a dead Sharpedo.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's mimicry of Sharpedo deters Psychic-type predators, like Bruxish, allowing it to devour a reef in peace. Its outer layer is poisonous, so creatures like Remoraid that try to nibble on it quickly die and become a meal for POKENAME.
author: pjporwoll

entry: These Pokémon began to display lower brain function as mushrooms accumulated upon their bodies, causing them to be swept away by rivers and carried into oceans. Somehow, when they become injured in battle, mushrooms will grow from the scars.
author: infinex21

entry: Found in the coldest of seas just off the shores of jagged coasts. They have learned to prey mostly on ships these days, creating giant tidal waves or whirlpools to sink them to the depths of the sea.
author: doxtordaemon

entry: Trade ships turn around on waters where threatening sea shanties are being sung, as that's a sign of POKENAME lurking nearby. The unfortunate ships that don't heed the call are raided by POKENAME with elegant swordplay and commanding steps.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME hunts at high speed, locking prey in place with psychic power. It closes in with a brutal, bone-crushing Crunch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grinds its sharp teeth together to activate its psychic powers. It immobilizes prey from a distance, and speeds towards it at remarkable speed, ensuring its target has no chance of escaping it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME act as a bully, pushing any other predatory Pokémon from their territory. When two POKENAME get near each other, the violence that ensues can damage parts of the reef, sometimes making it unsuitable for them to continue residing there.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's primary claws resemble Sharpedo, which it uses to distract, intimidate, and fake out opponents in combat. It if is bested in a fight, it will return to its den to meditate on a revenge plan.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Cunning and cruel, POKENAME pretend their tongues are loose water mines to scare boats away. Originally thought to be scaring boats away from their territory, it has been discovered that they actually herd ships into Sharpedo infested waters.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It loves the rain, especially when it is able to spend time outside to soak in the mud. Some Trainers give it a Damp Rock to ensure it spends more time happy in the rain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Don't mistake its diminutive size for a cute temperament — POKENAME is vicious, sly, and extremely territorial.  It will sneak attack any boat that comes down the river it calls home, and force the Pokémon aboard to join its crew.
author: imaginita

entry: There is only one thing POKENAME likes more than swashbuckling: a good jig. A lively tune on a concertina or hurdy-gurdy will immediately set POKENAME dancing.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME somehow senses those who have been recently engaged and chases them relentlessly so that it can bite them. No one knows why its attacks are targeted in this fashion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail acts as a dorsal fin while swimming through tropical waters. It weaves between waves at high speeds to stalk prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can achieve remarkable speeds in water so long as they move in straight lines. Because they struggle to turn at high speeds, they often crash; most of their scars are from crashing.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's ill-fated arrival is preceded by unusual and freezing currents. It torments those it encounters on its journey until it has delivered its desired amount of mischief.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Although small, it is a vicious Pokémon that will target and harass individuals one at a time; this behavior is most noticeable with prey. It does not hesitate to assail targets larger than itself; as testament to this, it has many battle scars.
author: infinex21

entry: Small and agile, POKENAME use the fin atop their head to make sharp turns at very high speeds. They work in coordinated groups to corner and bring down large prey.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME are easily distracted and allured by moving objects, lunging toward them to bite into them; sometimes, they even bite their own tails. They are typically clad in various scars, many of which come from them biting each other by accident.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are covered in short, rough hairs that help them cut through the water with minimal friction. Their speed and aggression in the water make them popular amongst lawbreakers at sea.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Schools of POKENAME take turns chasing down prey in brackish waters. The others stand by and cheer their kin on during the hunt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can swim at speeds up to 100MPH. POKENAME are vain and highly competitive, often leading them to challenge boats and larger Pokémon to races.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME attempts to coil around prey using its incredibly rough skin. It grinds against the foe to weaken them before striking with a powerful Crunch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a cunning and swift predator, using its hydrodynamic shape to chase prey and escape with stolen meals. It raids large ships to taste unique foods, sometimes sharing its prize with Sharpedo to have an even quicker getaway.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Barboach cling onto POKENAME's neck. After POKENAME devours a meal, the Barboach eagerly consume the scraps.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is a cunning and swift predator, using its hydrodynamic shape to chase prey and escape with stolen meals. It raids large ships to taste unique foods, sometimes sharing its prize with Sharpedo to have an even quicker getaway.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME have a sharp edge around their shell that allows them to cut through bones when they clamp down. This allows them to maintain a heavy diet of protein despite being primarily stationary.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As a deceiving Pokémon that acts slow-moving and amicable when around multiple Pokémon, POKENAME waits for prey to be all alone before suddenly and swiftly striking. It is through this manner that it keeps a friendly facade.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its acute sense of smell lets it track prey from 50 miles away. Its fur is soft and fluffy if you pet it front to back, but petting it any other way is coarse and rough.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: This wyvern-like Pokémon is often in fights, resulting in unique scarring. POKENAME's water-based wings and tail are scaldingly hot.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: Using psychic power, POKENAME pulls together flotsam and creates its own small ship to commandeer. It often amasses a crew of other Pokémon, leading them with ruthless efficiency.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tentacles act like large hooks, digging into its prey before it proceeds to chomp on their flesh. Wailord have been seen with entire schools of POKENAME hooked onto them.
author: mistymagius

entry: It only feasts on those that are afraid, so when a Pokémon fearfully swims away from it, POKENAME will catch them.  However, they begrudgingly retreat if potential prey stand its ground.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME swims at breakneck speeds, attempting to catch slower Pokémon to feast on. However, it may forget what it was doing in the middle of a chase.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME leaps from the sea to spit water at flying Pokémon like Wingull, knocking them into the water. Once they are out of the sky, it uses Crunch to subdue them.
author: .izik

entry: The three heads of POKENAME share equally vicious personalities, and are thus best differentiated by the colors of their markings. POKENAME are impressive pursuit hunters, sprinting up to prey at speeds of over 110mph (177kph).
author: slimee_amogus

entry: In icy seas, POKENAME searches for massive chunks of ice. It crushes them with its jaw as a test of biting strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sometimes mistaken for mermaids when they rest on icebergs or seaside stones. They tend to aggressively attack any who approach them as they rest.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME spits high-pressure mud at sailors aboard ships. Should anyone fall overboard, it drags them away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's toxic fumes make their teeth degrade, turning from rock hard to slimy and drippy in a matter of weeks if they haven't eaten fresh meals in a while. They are tough to train, as they tend to disobey their Trainer.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME jets water from its shell to chase prey before ensnaring them with its tongue, which can be up to five times the length of its shell. The teeth on the shell shred the prey as POKENAME reels them in, allowing it to easily digest its food.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME rockets through brackish waters at blinding speeds. If collision is imminent, it shuts its shell to protect itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is extremely aggressive, attacking anyone in sight with its fangs. Its teeth can grow back if damaged or if they get stuck in its prey. Anyone brave enough to seek out lost teeth can make a fortune selling them to traditional apothecaries.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME seek sunken ships to plunder their treasures. They often battle each other for precious loot.
author: mrbapcik

entry: POKENAME spins its claws like propellers to boost its swimming. At top speed, it can reach over 75 mph in open seas.
author: .izik

entry: A ruthless predator of the sea, it uses its massive claw to immobilize prey while its razor-sharp teeth tear them apart. Ironically, it is often fished by humans who prize its meat as a delicious seafood delicacy.
author: amiel997

entry: POKENAME enjoys gathering fallen leaves to create piles it can jump into. When it senses danger, it shakes its wooden horns to release a pollen that induces drowsiness in would-be attackers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME devour all organic debris they can find. Since they even absorb any scraps of lifeforce left in their meals, they're generally considered to be a bad omen.
author: mx_wellman

entry: The pink ooze that drips from POKENAME's body is rich in calcium and used in many desserts in Johto. Chefs covet it, and it commands a high price.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME defends lost children in the woods, standing up to more fearsome Ghost Pokémon that might prey on them. No matter how outmatched it is, it refuses to give up and abandon the child it protects.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be found in areas that were once lush but are now barren. It wanders such lands seemingly aimlessly, but if provoked or attacked, it will fight back tenaciously.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME wait in the trees, watching Trainers and Pokémon walk below from the shadows. With incredible agility, they will pounce from above, skewering their prey with a single strike.
author: santon5512

entry: These nocturnal forest Pokémon wear and wield pieces of old trees. They seem to need only moonlight and water to survive, yet they wander every night as if in search of something.
author: infinex21

entry: Parts of the forest have become fused with their bodies as they grow. They carve intimidating heads onto large, thick branches, wielding them as weapons to strike fear into enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body is made of dead vines. It uses shadowy tendrils to grasp food and pull it into its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME catches unsuspecting prey in a landslide of illusions, with no escape from its reality. While inside its illusions, it is near impossible to tell what is real and what is POKENAME.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME will travel up to six miles to search for the souls of dead children to absorb. Once they have gathered enough, they may evolve.
author: currentlymuffin

entry: POKENAME resembles a wooden puppet, though its actions are entirely its own. It conjures brambles to guide foes into its invisible walls.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have an acute sense of smell, capable of detecting fear and despair in other creatures. Because of this, they're known to appear to lost travelers.
author: mx_wellman

entry: POKENAME acts as a kind and gentle guide to lost children in the woods. It places them onto its back, floats to the forest entrance, and gently sets them down before vanishing into the trees.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME is rarely seen outside of the forests beyond the Secret Garden. The POKENAME tend to hide as branches up in the trees. It is theorized that if in the same location as a Trevenant, POKENAME will hide up in the branches of its head.
author: riverbandage

entry: People can hear the songs of POKENAME deep in the forest that lead to lakes or rivers. If followed, it is expected to never see the person again. Skeletons can often be found where the POKENAME reside at the bottom.
author: riverbandage

entry: Forest fires are often started by POKENAME, setting plant-life ablaze as they walk along pathways. This is in order for new life to start anew and get rid of the old or dying.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME are considered a great nuisance by families with children due to their tricks. It hides within the child's electronics, waiting until they're alone before filling the screen with scary imagery.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is comfortable in its shell, which it never wants to leave. The shell is not wood but mostly chloroplasts, giving life energy in the sun.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME hide along trees and wait for prey, which they can sense the movements of with their wisp-like horns. They will launch themselves toward their prey and cling on with their claws as they proceed to drain their prey's life essence.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME diligently protects forests from spiritual invaders. It is rumored to protect the same hunting grounds it patrolled centuries ago.
author: schwaus
