entry: Though it displays a unique ability to detach its own head, it can only do so for less than an hour before it must be returned to its body. It typically only detaches its head to reach foods that are far away and/or high up.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have a sturdy wooden stump atop their head and often ferry other Pokémon across bodies of water. They often release a happy whistle whenever the Pokémon they help give them a reward for their help.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME leaps from stumps when approached, then flees to the marsh, screeching to alert others to hide. This allows other of its kin ample time to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to be a guardian to the spirit world. If you spot POKENAME in the wild, your time may be almost up.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME make masks out of tree bark that they wear to spook others. Those who have high success rates in scaring others seem to evolve earlier.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME's head is not attached to its body and can freely float away in any direction. Its eyes have an eerie pull, and gazing into them causes a deep and sudden sleep.
author: jaminmcready

entry: While flying, POKENAME's wings give off the scent of rotting wood. It migrates in swarms across wetlands.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secretes a sap that gives off an unpleasant aroma, warding other Pokémon away from it. It lives in isolation because of this fact, only joined in solidarity by other foul-smelling Pokémon.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME lays invisible webs, then mimics the cries of a toddler. Anyone drawn near is ensnared and quickly consumed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies low through swamps, using echolocation to find hollow trees to call home. Its cries echo for miles.
author: .izik

entry: In search for a new home, this small spirit found a wooden toy bird to inhabit. It seems very disappointed about the toy's inability to fly by itself.
author: takio_

entry: POKENAME are infamously known as "Silent Watchers," as they will perch atop tree stumps and branches to watch passersby without uttering a single noise. Some believe they can see into the hearts of others and that they will act if they see malice.
author: infinex21

entry: Children from past civilizations lost in the woods may return as Phantump. They carry carvings of revered Pokémon to feel at home, embodying Xatu's behavior and abilities.
author: arcul

entry: Its body is covered by a blanket of evergreen leaves that allow it to blend perfectly into the forest. When POKENAME fights, it coats its wooden horns with electricity and strikes with cunning, paralyzing attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME float above swamps, crying like lost children to prank travelers. These sounds often seem to come from every direction.
author: .izik

entry: It gets its nutrients by absorbing the life force from flowers. At night hundreds of POKENAME can be seen floating around wilted flower fields.
author: mistymagius

entry: At night, POKENAME hovers over swamps with glowing green puffs. They flash in patterns to communicate silently.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nibbles on its wooden mask, sharpening it to the point it can penetrate solid bark. It lodges its teeth into trees, siphoning their energy to feed itself.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME latch onto Pokémon while camouflaging in the trees. It will then become friends with them, forcefully.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME hovers just above swamp water, zipping around in sudden bursts at over 100 mph. The hum of its wings sounds like distant crying.
author: .izik

entry: Allegedly, POKENAME is a piece of wooden debris possessed by the spirit of a drowned child. Its personality is extremely chipper, as it frolics in the water and along the river bank, so many take that as folklore to keep children from swimming alone.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Along side with Phantreons, this set is often seen making colonies together causing mischief wherever they go. The POKENAME tend to be more active during dawn unlike their counterpart.
author: riverbandage

entry: Seen with Phantpeons, this duo of Pokémon are often causing minor mischief together. The POKENAME are more active at dusk with being quite more lethal with pranks when alone.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME are most active during rain, which is absorbed by their foliage and brings back color to their floral bulbs. They are happy to share their leaves with those they trust, but they release a tear-inducing pollen to repel all others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hangs upside down in willow trees, watching silently. If approached, it drops and chases intruders before exploding.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dig burrows within damp, nutrient-rich soil and absorb nutrients and moisture as they rest. They never sleep in the same burrow, as they will carefully bury seeds in their burrows so new life may grow.
author: infinex21

entry: The loud cries of these Pokémon are so alike to the voices of human children that many travelers have been deterred from the forests POKENAME call home. POKENAME nest within tree canopies and prey upon Bug-type Pokémon that feed on said trees.
author: infinex21

entry: Berry Juice that is created within its shell has a very savory flavor. Bartenders in Unova use it to make mixed drinks at upper-class taverns.
author: .izik

entry: Legends say that POKENAME is the spirit of a Heracross who perished when it charged into a tree and got stuck, never to escape.
author: incognito1234

entry: When alone, POKENAME whimpers softly like a child and emits a honey-like scent. If approached, it lashes out with a sharp Slash to take down its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is believed to be the tarlike ghost of an animal possessing a stump, both of which were killed in the same human-caused fire. It proactively scours the forest for debris that would worsen a wildfire and consumes it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can be seen by the light of their eerie green fire at night, processions of them slowly crawling beneath the canopy of ancient forests. Superstitions claim that each POKENAME is the spirit of a fallen tree made manifest.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME floats along the sea's surface, feeding on driftwood. It drifts slowly, blending in with tide-worn debris.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wanders around wooded areas, searching for lost hikers and campers. When it finds them, it gifts an item from its wooden sack, then disappears merrily into the brush. The gifted items appear to be lost trinkets of other travelers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME slither through forests with an oak mask on their head. They wrap themselves around prey before siphoning their life force.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When wet, POKENAME rolls at high speed to dry its wooden body. Its spinning form leaves streaks through muddy trails.
author: .izik

entry: After a forest faces a disaster, POKENAME descends and makes a home in the remains of the forest. POKENAME's presence is said to bring life to wherever it resides.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME have wooden bodies that resemble a small tree. They often stalk Trainers out of curiosity but are too shy to initiate a confrontation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is said that POKENAME guide scared children to the afterlife, trying to ease their worries. POKENAME will attempt to make the child laugh before taking them away from this world.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME grows berries from the branches on its head, which it sometimes offers to lost children. Those who eat these berries mysteriously disappear shortly afterwards.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The violet flames jetting out from POKENAME are said to be fuelled by lost spirits it gathers in its travels, their burning allowing them to pass on to the afterlife. The sting of this Pokémon's flames leave the target with deep emotional pain.
author: deadshields

entry: Wild POKENAME live in burrows they have dug out under trees. They live off trace amounts of nutrients and water acquired from the tree roots above their burrows.
author: infinex21

entry: Often found scavenging in burnt forests, POKENAME give back to the earth by decomposing the old. They tend to only come out after a wildfire in the burnt ashes.
author: riverbandage

entry: When a blizzard comes, these Pokémon come out. POKENAME are said to be the dead that died in blizzards while travelling along the path.
author: riverbandage

entry: While floating through swamps, should POKENAME bump into a tree, both it and the tree will spontaneously take on a different wood type. These can be types not native to the area at all.
author: .izik

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME possesses the tree it calls home. The tree lets out a menacing moaning noise throughout the night.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon wander forests and spit fire at anything or anyone they deem to be a threat to the forest. If they encounter anyone who is lost, they will try to guide them to safety; some stories claim this is because POKENAME were once lost spirits.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spits highly pressurized water that reeks of rotting wood. It cries like a child to lure others close before launching its attack.
author: .izik

entry: Although POKENAME is quite friendly, it has accidentally scared off many potential new friends. It rises from forest swamps, floating through the air covered in gunk, making many think it is some malevolent mud spirit.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon loves hearing noises most find unsettling while in the forest. It becomes scared when it sees humans within its home.
author: toxicrown

entry: POKENAME loves to dance at night within haunted forests. When it dances, eerie winds move with it.
author: toxicrown

entry: These Pokémon are said to be the decayed remains of trees possessed by mothers who perished in search of their lost children. They wander forests at night, as if still continuing their search for their long-lost children.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are said to be created when spirits possess the shed shells of bug Pokémon that tree bark has grown around. Their bark-like bodies continue to grow as they metabolize sunlight, so some have been seen stuck to trees.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wails like a lost child to attract kindhearted people. When approached, it lashes out with poison-coated branches.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon are incredibly shy, yet they have kind hearts. They typically conceal themselves within foliage and by utilizing their hue-shifting abilities, but they will reveal themselves to comfort or protect a crying individual.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are drawn to one another, so they always live in large groups. They can move in nigh-perfect unison, as if connected by a hivemind. They coordinate their attacks to defeat strong foes and to defend their forest homes.
author: infinex21

entry: It is said that POKENAME are the result when the spirits of two Phantdum merge. Their "noses," much like the rest of their bark-like parts, are harder than steel and can cleanly penetrate solid rock when they charge forward.
author: infinex21

entry: A Bidoof that has possessed a tree stump. It still gnaws on wood, even itself, to whittle down its teeth.
author: jacobtmm

entry: Some tales claim that POKENAME are connected to the very "spirit" of their entire forest homes, allowing them to sense all that happens within. They will show up to protect young humans and Pokémon alike if they are in danger.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME leaves are known for their medicinal properties when properly ground up and mixed with water and sap. They shake loose some of their leaves when they come across injured travelers, which scatters a cool, calming pollen from their petals too.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's wooden maw slowly opens and closes while it sleeps. Those in the northern hemisphere tend to be nocturnal, while those in the south are more varied in their sleeping patterns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can only be found at night within untouched forests, the Pokémon animating fallen and dead bits of wood to form their body. They shake the horn-like branches on their head to scare off rivals encroaching on their home.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a restless spirit of the forest, ambushing travellers during the night. The longer it's trapped in the forest, the angrier and more vengeful it becomes.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's immense size and the creaking sound it makes when opening its mouth often lead many to mistake it for a ship at night. This has led to many legends of ghost ships that seem to submerge themselves quickly after emerging from the depths.
author: drcew

entry: Swamp villages once revered POKENAME as a deity of the wetlands. Crowns carved from stumps it touched were worn during grand festivals held for any wild POKENAME encountered.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers consuming the soil around dead plant life. At the darkest point of the night, one can see a faint, eerie glow emanating from the leaves on its branches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sleeps during the day, venturing out in the evening to let moonbeams nurture the plants on its back. The plants emit a scent that only Ghost-type Pokémon can sense, making spirits flock to it at night.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sleeps most soundly in graveyards. It is said that if a leaf from its tree falls on a grave, poverty will find the descendants of the deceased.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are commonly found deep within overgrown forests, easily jumping through the tangled vines and branches. Upon finding a lost individual amongst the flora, POKENAME will climb down and help guide them to safety with its glowing moss tail.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are known to gather in dying forests, where they feed off rotting plants and steal whatever life is left. POKENAME are inherently hostile to anyone who disturbs their home.
author: jestersqueak

entry: The flames on POKENAME's body are said to glow blue when the spirits of the departed are nearby. Scientists have studied this phenomenon for years without discovering an actual cause for the color change.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to prank lost travelers, particularly children. It hides away in the dark of night and blows a series of bubbles that emit an eerie echoed version of its cry, in an attempt to spook them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME presses its wings against stumps to encourage nearby plant life to grow. It uses this ability to help revitalize forests.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is said to be possessed by a lumberjack who died in the forest. It obsessively fells trees as it did while alive.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Some say that when a stray Pawniard is cursed by forest spirits, it becomes a POKENAME, wandering the forest, looking for the pack it was lost from. The wood covering its body is unbreakable.
author: bigblue

entry: POKENAME is highly territorial and will fly into a rage if it ever discovers that its forest has been damaged. So long as it is shown respect, though food offerings help as well, it will allow others to pass through.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are formed by the emotions of trapped children who long to return home. They seek out lost children and, upon finding them, guide them home. POKENAME are filled with a deep sadness, as they carry the emotions of those who never made it home.
author: riverbandage

entry: These small Pokémon wield a weak power that accelerates the growth of plants. Using this power too often leaves them so tired that they will be rendered immobile until they absorb enough sunlight and water.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has a lonely personality. After an initial period of time, however, it begins to quickly warm up to those around it. It is thought to be able to access the spirit world freely.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME use their slender, prehensile ears to ensnare foes that harm those they care for, then dispatch them with powerful kicks. Though they aggressively defend others, they are otherwise docile and shy.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME throws its voice to distract opponents before delivering a Sucker Punch from the opposite direction. Its bark is used in colognes to give a punch of a strong woody scent similar to the smell of pine.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME move with such speed that they are often difficult to see, though within forests they blend in quite well even while still. Their eerie cries can achieve disorienting pitches that may induce migraines.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wanders through forests and builds many kinds of traps from wood, vines, and leaves to play pranks on unsuspecting hikers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME wanders through forests and builds many kinds of traps from wood, vines, and leaves to play pranks on unsuspecting hikers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME wanders through forests and builds many kinds of traps from wood, vines, and leaves to play pranks on unsuspecting hikers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME wanders through forests and builds many kinds of traps from wood, vines, and leaves to play pranks on unsuspecting hikers.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is said to be the spirits of trees that were struck down by lightning during storms. The ambient buzzing of forests can often be attributed to POKENAME.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME like to lurk in dark corners of the city to hide and spread their corruption. Though small on their own, they can gather in swarms and quickly overwhelm even experienced Trainers.
author: hereisanimations

entry: POKENAME are believed by many to have come from beyond our world, be they as spirits or as extraterrestrial Pokémon. They scatter a shiny, pollen-like dust that boosts the health and growth of plants, making them treasured by many people.
author: infinex21

entry: Though they can ride upon gentle winds, POKENAME are deathly afraid of strong winds, as those will scatter most of their leaves. Their leaves wilt in minutes when detached, yet they have great medicinal properties as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hides itself against the gnarled back of the trees in its forest home. If trespassers draw too close, it swings open to reveal ghostly hands that drag them into its coffin-like body.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lures in bug Pokémon with its sweet-scented flower before draining them of their life force. It hides in hollow logs to conceal its shadowy body from its prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: Their shadowy tail splits into many tails as they grow stronger, though they can never surpass six on their own. The spirits they were born of are said to have been those of children, which may explain why POKENAME are so friendly and playful.
author: infinex21

entry: Each tail on this Pokémon represents the soul of a child that died in the woods. Because of this, its fur has been blackened.
author: toxicrown

entry: POKENAME is said to come from a road far above the sky to restore wishes to the world.
author: blitzydragon

entry: POKENAME is said to come from a road far above the sky to restore wishes to the world.
author: blitzydragon

entry: POKENAME is said to come from a road far above the sky to restore wishes to the world.
author: blitzydragon

entry: POKENAME digs burrows beneath old tree stumps. It rarely moves unless disturbed, then vanishes into the earth.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's aura sense lets it detect the fear of children lost in the woods. It follows this emotional signature so that it may come to their defense and protect them from the forest's dangers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are so rarely sighted that they were once mostly known through tales and rumors. As many tales claimed, they do rest for long periods of time, especially atop the remains of trees. When awake, they emit cries as if grieving something.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's wooden body is always soaking wet. It floats above swampy areas, dripping and making unsettling moaning noises to disturb others.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that POKENAME can sense when someone is about to pass. The Pokémon will repeatedly shock them, attempting to keep them alive.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It is said that POKENAME appear whenever a traveler is on the verge of collapse. A single strike from their tail or horns floods the body with electricity, allowing the exhausted to press onward.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: By sticking their tails into interconnected tree roots, POKENAME can send out electrical pulses to communicate with other far-away POKENAME.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME are known for their melancholic songs that can often be heard resounding throughout forests at night. These Pokémon are light enough that a strong gust of wind will launch them off their feet.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME feed on rocks and metal scraps, making them valued partners for Pokémon Rangers for the sake of keeping forests clean of harmful debris. The leaves on their bodies are rich with iron nutrients and exude fresh air via photosynthesis.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time hidden underground, absorbing nutrients through its own roots. It only emerges, baring its wooden jaws, to drive away anyone walking over its head.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have long been called "Fell Spirits" due to the belief they were born of the spirits of felled trees. Such a belief is bolstered by how these Pokémon fervently guard and protect tree stumps using their illusionary abilities.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have been spotted within forest clearings at night, cheerfully dancing with their fellow kind while their red flames flared and flicked about. They have kind hearts and have often helped to guide lost travelers they had only just met.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefers to emerge from the trees it possesses only after sunset. In prolonged sunlight, its buds dry rapidly as its bark begins to shed.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon appear where extensive restoration efforts have revitalized rivers and greenery. Many believe that their forlorn cries should be taken as a solemn reminder to never harm nature again.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME is one of the few harmless Drifloon fusions. Said to house the spirits of children once carried away in the woods by Drifloon and its fusions, it plays with any lost child it finds, then gently guides them back home.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME flowers, albeit small, contain concentrated medicinal compounds coveted by many. Unfortunately, these Pokémon were hunted for their flowers and only now have begun to prosper again, albeit with a greater aversion to humans.
author: infinex21

entry: By crouching and curling its ears up, POKENAME disguises itself as a shrub to avoid humans and Pokémon alike. If it is attacked, it lets out a piercingly loud cry and quickly hops away.
author: infinex21

entry: Spores drift from POKENAME's branches, inducing dizziness and delirium. The effect intensifies in low light.
author: .izik

entry: Possessing fallen logs, POKENAME makes its home in old-growth forests. It tries to lure travellers away from well-trodden paths, making efforts to make them lose their way in the dark woods.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME forage for Tanga Berries to protect themselves against the many Bug-type Pokémon in their natural habitat. They hunt rodent Pokémon by reaching into burrows with their long snout and let out a spooky cry whenever they are full.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME sucks nutrients from a tree, the wooden armor wards off predators with its eerie, face-like appearance. The leaves of POKENAME are said to help people find lost items when ingested.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME climbs tree trunks with ease, blending in with bark. If approached, it releases a sudden electric burst.
author: .izik

entry: As the sun begins to set, POKENAME flock together and communally watch passersby, all of their heads moving in unison. While this behavior is often considered unsettling, researchers have observed this is because they are looking for dropped seeds.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hides in hollow logs to avoid sunlight. If disturbed, it erupts into flames before vanishing into the swamp.
author: .izik

entry: It tries to frighten people by camouflaging in the trees, then suddenly moving. POKENAME feed on fear and nervousness.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are skittish spirits that wander around forests, collecting pieces of mask-shaped bark to inhabit and form physical bodies. When they need to hide, they retreat into their bark, appearing as simple wooden masks should anyone spot them.
author: thezekrom

entry: POKENAME nests in caves near marshes. The leaves on its back smell sweet, but its touch is dangerously poisonous.
author: .izik

entry: Groups of POKENAME imitate a fallen log in the forest before rolling away while making a child-like laughing noise. They do this to startle those nearby, feeding off their fear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rests on fallen logs, lazily chewing bark. If threatened, it pounces toward its foe and bites with venom-laced fangs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can only be found in forests covered in heavy snow during the winter. In ancient folklore, houses visited by these Pokémon will prosper and their leaves can cure any illness.
author: sakuraneko

entry: Despite how large and intimidating its mask is, the ghost inside is actually small and timid. POKENAME chooses the creepiest, most crooked stump to possess in order to scare away predators, but if it's too heavy, the Pokémon may struggle to get up.
author: milchik

entry: During the day, this Pokémon hides itself in piles of leaves and twigs or in hollowed-out logs as it rests and conserves its energy. At night, it comes out to explore and to absorb moonlight.
author: infinex21

entry: These small Pokémon are common sights within old forests, scurrying along the ground and devouring any rotten matter they come across. Though their leaves contain poison, they also exude an exotic aroma that attracts many Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: Many parents in ocean-bordering towns warn children not to play near the water at night. According to their tales, POKENAME will float up from the ocean at night to bite down on unsuspecting children and drag them into the sea.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME frequently form from individual Phantump that cluster together in search of companionship. Trainers are advised to take extra care to ensure their needs are met as they can be prone to low mood.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME frequently form from individual Phantump that cluster together in search of companionship. Trainers are advised to take extra care to ensure their needs are met as they can be prone to low mood.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME frequently form from individual Phantump that cluster together in search of companionship. Trainers are advised to take extra care to ensure their needs are met as they can be prone to low mood.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME frequently form from individual Phantump that cluster together in search of companionship. Trainers are advised to take extra care to ensure their needs are met as they can be prone to low mood.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME bear fruits that are said to contain small amounts of spiritual energy inside. Spiritomb and Gengar love to eat it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It wears its wooden mask to keep its malice and resentment under control. If its mask is removed, it will unleash its built-up anger in a violent rampage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME coils around ship anchors and rides them to the surface when they're lifted. It mimics a crying child's voice, then vanishes, giggling.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are cactus possessed by the spirits of children who were lost to the desert. Hearing their cries is thought to be an omen of death.
author: odditylad

entry: Bands of POKENAME will stalk travelers crossing the desert at night and feast on their spiritual essence. They wait until their prey is too tired to move before ensnaring them with their cursed brambles.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME will use the healing power of its leaves to cure the sickness of anyone who puts a hand into its mouth. Be careful though, as it may drop the axe on its head and take their hand off instead.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is shy around adults, but it has no problem opening up to children. Many believe this is because it once was a human child itself.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME mimics the sound of a drowning toddler at beaches in the dead of night to lure unsuspecting rescuers. When they draw close, it drags them beneath the sand to feed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are believed to be stumps possessed by the spirits of children who perished in the cold millions of years ago. They stopped crying a long time ago.
author: odditylad

entry: When someone loses a pet, sometimes they are visited by a POKENAME. While there is no evidence that it is the spirit of the pet, many adopt the POKENAME and pamper it. It is a friendly and playful Pokémon, but is mischievous and attention-seeking.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME tries to stay as still as possible to camouflage itself as a regular stump. Anyone who attempts to rest on its stump will have their souls slowly drained away.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME naps in willow branches, emitting giggle-like snores. These sounds unsettle travelers who hear them at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME resemble dead logs that are carried or rolled into caves for other Pokémon to use as shelter. They imitate the voice of a child to try to make friends, but all this does is leave people lost deep in caves.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Said to be spirits of children lost in the woods, POKENAME often gather together to play in forest clearings. They fashion instruments and masks out of wood, creating a little band and inviting people to join in.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME greatly cares about the well-being of children and often guides those who get lost in the woods. Once its job is done, it disappears back into the forest.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME gather branches for kindling, creating small fires to guide lost souls through the forest. When the fires go out, POKENAME disappear like leaves on the wind.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME has the ability to peer into the future. It uses this ability to preventively block potential threats from entering the forest where it resides.
author: drcew

entry: Clinging to the sides of trees, a POKENAME will keep watch over those that enter its forest. If it spots someone that's lost, it will clear the path from the shadows, saving them from sharing its fate.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME fires pink beams said to cause victims to hallucinate it as a human child. Folklore warns: never let it into your home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in dead trees, lying dormant until nightfall. When it finds new flora growing nearby, it flies down and drains it of life-force for nutrients.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME floats around forests at night, offering lost children the chance to partake in some of the sweet candy from its body. Those who accept are believed to be cursed, and will become POKENAME when they pass on.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats on ponds in deep dark forests. No-one knows where they came from, but it is believed that they come from spirits that died in the forest.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: It is rumored that these Pokémon were born of the spirits left behind by forest fires, now possessing the burnt remains of trees. They are incredibly docile and shy, though when happy their flames noticeably grow and they cannot help but dance a bit.
author: infinex21

entry: Its red flames are said to be otherworldly energies made manifest, which may explain how they do not set their forest homes aflame. A POKENAME will fight viciously to defend their homes, using their claws, horns, and flames alike.
author: infinex21

entry: Large branches grow from POKENAME's body if it remains still for too long without swimming. The leaves that grow from these branches smell of honey and fruit but are extremely bitter to taste.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wooden body sprouts tiny leaves when it howls for extended periods. It does this to communicate with others of its kind within forested areas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travel through deep woods, wearing paths behind themselves in straight lines. It is rare for someone traveling through forests inhabited by POKENAME to get lost, as the paths that POKENAME make are so clearly worn.
author: vic1312

entry: Because of their long, wood-like bodies, these Pokémon can easily camouflage themselves within forests. They are commonly found near trees or upon tree branches, as they mostly eat leaves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME protect their soft, developing bodies by anchoring bark to themselves using a dark-colored silk. They feed energy into the wooden shell, encouraging the wood to continue growing around them.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME stab their needle-like proboscis into tree trunks to drain nutrients. The vines growing from their wings and antennae disrupt sonar from Pokémon like Noibat and Zubat.
author: chibitales

entry: In dark forests, POKENAME bury themselves in the undergrowth near ancient tree stumps. They rely on the shadows and leaf litter to protect their fragile wooden shells.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME will seek bright lights at night to perform photosynthesis through its wings. Despite its ability to photosynthesize, it will take any opportunity to consume unattended clothing.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME prefers to sleep atop rotting tree stumps. If awoken by a predator, it emits the sound of a crying toddler before charging directly at it and exploding.
author: .izik

entry: Plucking one of POKENAME's feathers and mixing it into tea is said to cure sore throats and coughing. It is difficult to find POKENAME during cold, windy seasons, which makes finding a POKENAME feather all the more rewarding.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fits entire logs into its bill to absorb the nutrients within. Its bill stretches to accommodate the log, causing it to fly in a labored manner.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creep up on people who travel through swamps, silently gliding through the murky water. When caught, they skittishly flee, only to repeat the process a moment later.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This ghastly Pokémon is said to come into being when a beloved feline Pokémon is lost in the forest. The grief causes the Pokémon's spirit to remain anchored to this world, and it becomes a new POKENAME.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME are typically quiet when they cry out, with some comparing their cries to young children. However, if their branch-like horns are grabbed, POKENAME emit shrieks strong enough to blow leaves off trees.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME possess fallen logs, drawing on the lingering vitality within them to form smoke-like bodies. They drift silently through deep forests in search of prey to sustain their log, their whiskers tracing even the faintest whiff of life force.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME possesses swamps while sleeping, filling them with electrical energy. Anyone who touches the stump will receive a powerful electric shock.
author: .izik

entry: This shy Pokémon quietly watches other Pokémon from a distance, silently cheering them on with electrical flashes from its hands. POKENAME considers these Pokémon their friends and will follow them around, silently encouraging them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME was once an overgrown statue of a loyal Growlithe, carved many years ago. It is now the home of a lost child's soul.
author: captainzscourge

entry: Although a POKENAME will enshroud itself in spectral flames to intimidate others, it's only able to do so for at best an hour before it exhausts itself. It is usually seen near sites of forest fires and perceives nearly anything as a possible threat.
author: infinex21

entry: In battle or when cornered, POKENAME display a ferocity that is often compared to wildfires. Their flames burn so strong, even as they rest, that they have isolated themselves within caves near the forests they once called home.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is extremely shy and will watch those who enter the forest from a distance. POKENAME has rarely been seen leaving berries for those who are respectful of the forest before quickly teleporting away.
author: drcew

entry: When lifting objects, POKENAME makes sounds like a crying child. It does this even when content, confusing those nearby.
author: .izik

entry: Local legends describe POKENAME as restless warriors, wandering forests in search of purpose. Despite their intimidating presence, POKENAME are docile and inquisitive, often curiously wandering towards Trainers that enter the forest.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It spits out a fast-hardening latex to ensnare and quickly finish off the Bug-type Pokémon it preys on. It will also use this latex to help seal the wounds on larger plants and trees.
author: infinex21

entry: Because its head glows with fiery light during battle, some have theorized its head is hollow. Despite this, it is a clever fighter who makes use of its environments to the fullest. When not battling, POKENAME will gently tend to plants nearby.
author: infinex21

entry: A Pokémon born of a small spirit's choice to inhabit a large piece of driftwood. It tends to the moss on its belly and makes enjoyable patterns of it. Its body is surprisingly tough, and it can withdraw inside to further enhance its defenses.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live within forest lakes and ponds, their light bodies allowing them to float with their glassy, green orbs above the surface. They only need sunlight to survive, but some tales claim they will drag others underwater if they get too close.
author: infinex21

entry: It emits alluring lights from its glassy orbs to draw others closer to the edge of its lake habitat, then drags them down to feed on their life force. POKENAME can also emit child-like cries from the hole on its head to lure humans closer.
author: infinex21

entry: Wandering around cut-down forests, it punches any lumberjacks it sees. It's also often seen around high mountain trails, disguising as tree stumps.
author: markusknight

entry: POKENAME likes to prank hikers. It plunges its ghastly body into the ground, causing the earth to tremble and trees to fall down on those unfortunate enough to anger it.
author: markusknight

entry: It is said to wander around very old forests, seeking new trunks from enormous fallen trees to live in. It guards these ancient forests, bringing curses or rushing at full speed at anyone that trespasses.
author: markusknight

entry: Perhaps due to their inherent weakness from the moment they are born, POKENAME will only ever let children ride upon their backs. Their trust must still be earned first, lest their black flames harm their rider.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite their size and strength, POKENAME mostly only let children ride upon their backs. They are known to make exceptions for loving families, however. Their black flames will never hurt those they trust, and they help to conceal their movements.
author: infinex21

entry: While it sleeps, POKENAME makes the sound of a crying child. If startled awake, it retaliates with a telekinetic blast.
author: .izik

entry: Their leafy tails are a sign of age and garner respect among their kind; how much respect is gained depends on the length and thickness. They subsist on sunlight, moss, and water, so they are frequently spotted near ponds and streams.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME commonly appears where Pokémon are starving due to wild plants having been overharvested. It hunts down the perpetrator, even if it is as large as Snorlax, and bludgeons them with its allium vegetable.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Ancient civilizations used the Black Sludge from POKENAME to line latrines. The acidic properties serve to break down waste and absorb scent.
author: .izik

entry: Debate persisted for quite some time over which was the head of this Pokémon, though further study revealed the face on the shell is a diversion meant to trick others. Its shell has the composition of wood, yet the durability of iron.
author: infinex21

entry: To prevent their gaseous bodies from being blown away, POKENAME seek refuge within tree hollows, which often also become their nests. They are infamous for startling and frightening travelers, yet they do not seem to do so out of malice.
author: infinex21

entry: A malevolent forest spirit, POKENAME phases in and out between the trees of its home forest. It especially loves to haunt and torment lost children and hear their cries.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME display an abnormal capacity to influence the plant life around them with their hands, as if they were puppeteering without any strings. They use this ability to lure humans and Pokémon into their forests, who are rarely ever seen again.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is often found playing music from its flute-like nose in forested areas. Children who hear POKENAME's music will begin to dance in a trance-like state.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME quietly hides disguised as a bush as it waits for prey. When something passes by, it catches it and makes it disappear.
author: prof.whitebeam

entry: POKENAME split up to observe the activities of humans in their forest. If POKENAME sees them despoiling their home, they alert stronger Trevenant fusions.
author: mepp.

entry: Its red eye never blinks and always follows an intruder within its forest territory, even if they are behind cover. As they wave their branches wielded as clubs, they display the ability to exert control over other plants near them.
author: infinex21

entry: Their cloaks of leaves and the branches upon their heads all grow with age. The one with the longest of both is the leader of its pack. They display a level of intellect by forming powerful weapons out of wood for themselves and for others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are incredibly persistent. If a POKENAME family or area is hurt, they will stop at nothing to track down who did it and beat them to a pulp.
author: totodile.

entry: A POKENAME in pursuit appears to lack pupils. They are highly dangerous, so it's important to know how to tell whether one is docile or hostile.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME wanders through ancient forests. It absorbs intruders into its form, converting those who harm the forest into vital nutrients to feed it.
author: velvetmitsu

entry: POKENAME lurks in dense forests, guarding its domain. It ensnares intruders to warn all who dare to disturb the natural balance of the woodland realm.
author: anarchaz

entry: Due to this fusion's parental instincts, wild POKENAME often care for young Phantump until they're strong enough to survive on their own.
author: phantom640

entry: POKENAME swim so slowly near the surface that they are often mistaken for driftwood. The tips of their horns glow bright red to distract, disorient, and unnerve their foes.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME nest within fields of seaweed, which they can control to ensnare any prey or threats so long as their grassy fins are dug in. It is said that looking directly into their glowing red lights will sap one's very life force.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lurk in forests, creating barriers between trees. POKENAME like to mess with people travelling through the woods, creating elaborate mazes in the forest for them to get stuck in.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME are untrusting of all others and will charge at anyone they see within their forest domains. Their legs pack enough power that they soften hard ground when they rampage, allowing new life to more easily take root.
author: infinex21

entry: These Pokémon are sometimes mistaken for floating driftwood atop lakes. They lie motionless, only waking when fog coats their habitat.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME lures people deep into its woods by mimicking the cries of an eevee or small child. Though it only seeks a playmate, it sometimes mistakenly curses those it tries to play with.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME will drown anyone that comes near the body of water that it resides in. It has even been known to even drown other Pokémon that come to close. The only exception is Paras and Parasect.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME tend to be highly aggressive and sensitive. Through the bark-made fur, it can produce a 10,000-volt charge in small bursts that can be ejected as like quills from the fur to attack.
author: riverbandage

entry: While typical Flareon can heat their body up to 1,650 degrees Fahrenheit, POKENAME are unable to handle that temperature. POKENAME tend to catch themselves on fire in their own anger by unintentionally rising their body temperature too high.
author: riverbandage

entry: While inhabiting a system, POKENAME flashes disturbing images across the screen at intervals. This frightens users away so it can feed undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appear to be attempting to imitate a tree despite being made entirely of cubes. It is believed that these strange Pokémon are from another world where cuboid shapes are part of nature.
author: neo_technomon_8392

entry: It sharpens its scythes against dense rocks and uses them to trim the forest overgrowth, the scraps of which it feeds on. It shares its leaves with ill Pokémon, for they contain medicinal compounds and plentiful nutrients.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME pose as trees so they may watch for any threats to their forest homes and strike as they see fit. They extend roots from their feet to absorb nutrients and water. They may use their roots to connect to and control nearby plants as well.
author: infinex21

entry: Although multiple POKENAME may be found near the same forests, they live independently of each other and may even clash over territory. Their dens are covered in amber that formed from their resin-like saliva, indicating they may be ancient.
author: infinex21

entry: The apples that grow upon its branches vary in size and taste, with "Perfect Apples" being the rarest to grow and the most sought after. It will only let its friends even touch these apples and will bring down its full might on would-be thieves.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME constantly sheds its bark, with it fully regrowing in around a day. This bark contains small saplings, with them taking root and growing into thin, twisted trees that drain the life of other plants around to fuel their own growth.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME pretends to be nothing more than a dragon-shaped tree while observing those who wander into its forest. Those it deems a detriment are forcibly expelled by the ghostly powers emitted from its horn.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME blends perfectly with tree branches thanks to its wooden body, waiting patiently for its prey to lower their guard before striking. It's extremely afraid of fire and avoids it at all costs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME protects the forest it claims as its domain and will violently chase away any unwanted visitors. Despite its cold exterior, it will often let other Pokémon perch on its head.
author: mistymagius

entry: If you see a cluster of tree branches in a web-like shape, it is best not to approach. Fully under POKENAME's control, the branches will ensnare its prey before draining their life force.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flies about the forest in search of a tree that is unprotected and bonds with it. It will work closely with an arborist or other Pokémon that it trusts to tend to the tree, leaving in search of a new tree to protect once satisfied.
author: pjporwoll

entry: If POKENAME foresees an intruder with ill intent, it commands the forest trees to attack. The onslaught continues until the foe flees or falls unconscious.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts above marshes, perching in trees like mossy fruit. If a predator nears, it stirs the forest, commanding branches to strike with eerie precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to scare passing travelers, hiding amongst the trees before jumping at them from above. When winter comes, groups of POKENAME drift along the wind to find warmer areas.
author: mistymagius

entry: It is often found half submerged in mud, tapping into the root network. It is able to draw out toxins from nearby trees and expel them from the top of its head as sap. Some Pokémon can digest it and can be found perching on its head licking it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: At dusk, POKENAME swoops low through dense woods, hunting the lost. Branches twist at its command, snaring victims in gnarled roots.
author: .izik

entry: In autumn, POKENAME can be found in pumpkin patches. It loves to play with children, but they often run away, terrified of POKENAME's haunting gaze.
author: thropp

entry: POKENAME bends trees into frightful shapes to haunt lone travelers. It feeds on the fear collected in its glowing red beads.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a preternatural sense when something is watching it and will not move anything but its eyes while watched unless it is attacked. When attacked, it lashes out in retaliation, giving it the nickname of "the lumberjack's bane".
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME has a preternatural sense when something is watching it and will not move anything but its eyes while watched unless it is attacked. When attacked, it lashes out in retaliation, giving it the nickname of "the lumberjack's bane".
author: pjporwoll

entry: Rather than sleeping, POKENAME's heads go into a deep trance when inactive. While one is entranced, the other remains alert to look out for threats. The Phantump-like tail, however, is more cowardly, rousing the front at any sudden noise.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: Every POKENAME claims a tree as its own, remaining attached to a limb until something disturbs it. It rockets down from the tree in response, mercilessly assaulting the interloper with ghastly ghost powers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's saliva is like tree resin, which they use to mark their territories and to tend to their own wounds. They cling to the sides of trees and glide toward their prey, which they fell using their pincers and venomous stingers.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME possess fallen logs, infusing the dead wood with new life. Legends persist of their shells playing host to spirits of the forest, claiming their passage through old growth forests leaves a trail of fresh plant growth in their wake.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME possess fallen logs, infusing the dead wood with new life. They seek out decaying trees within the forest and tear them down, incorporating the wood into their shell and leaving space for new growth to take the tree's place.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live within old growth forests, roosting in dead or dying trees. Their dry woody bodies camouflage well against their homes, and the first sign of a flock of POKENAME is usually when their bright red eyes fixate on the person approaching.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be seen giving away lost toys to Pokémon they find in forests. They tend to leave a trail of pine needles and branches where they walk.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME glides silently over the forest canopy at night, with small Ghost-type Pokémon sometimes hitching a ride on its leafy wings. This has led to the belief that seeing POKENAME is a bad omen.
author: pizzarcato

entry: POKENAME live within old growth forests, roosting in dead or dying trees. Their dry woody bodies camouflage well against their homes, and the first sign of a flock of POKENAME is usually when their bright red eyes fixate on the person approaching.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Some forest tribes build cults around worshiping POKENAME. This Pokémon loves it when offerings are placed on its horns.
author: mrbapcik

entry: POKENAME use their small trees on their trunks to mop up loose water and puddles, which is absorbed and filtered within them. They are playful Pokémon who love letting others trim their trees, which helps keep them from overgrowing.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body maintains a rough bark texture while awake, deterring predators with weak jaws. When it sleeps however, this rough texture smooths out, leaving POKENAME vulnerable.
author: chibitales

entry: Some few legends refer to this Pokémon as a guardian deity of the eldest forests, with even fewer citing that it is the manifestation of a forest's spirit. It has an uncanny power over nearby plants and trees, using them to ward off others.
author: infinex21

entry: Its skull-like head is made of petrified wood, which serves well to unnerve and intimidate others in tandem with the glowing mark on its chest. It tightly wraps around its targets and drains them of their life essence within less than an hour.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME guards the depths of ancient forests, scanning its surroundings with the eye-like orb on its tail. Its roar sounds like howling wind.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: In legends, POKENAME controls all volcanoes with its roars, commanding when and how violently they erupt at will. It purposely ties its legs down with heavy vines to prevent itself from racing all over and blitzing through trees.
author: soup1900

entry: With a barking roar, POKENAME will command trees to chase after those who ruin forests. When a tree becomes old and needs to be rid of so new nature can grow, it blasts intense fire in a precise manner so only that tree burns away.
author: soup1900

entry: Forging its body from ancient wood, it stands as a sentinel of the land. Tales speak of its age-old armor, said to repel even the mightiest of foes.
author: anarchaz

entry: Despite its ghastly appearance, it has a good side. It will guide any children that get lost in the woods back to safety.
author: birchbot

entry: It's known as the 'forest witch' for its control of the entire forest it's in. The wood scepter it wields allows this level of power to be possible.
author: awiralonprime

entry: POKENAME cast great swathes of magical traps over their wooded domain. Paths shift, roots tangle, and countless become lost forever.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME chases after those who enter its forest, making spooky noises and threatening gestures. If a traveler offers it food, however, it is instantly placated and will leave them alone.
author: sk372

entry: The flowering parasites present on this Pokémon act as the brain, manipulating its tree body with tendrils. POKENAME sings in a chorus of harmonized voices that can be heard throughout the forest.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME sheds its wooden scales on the night of a full moon. Those who witness this are said to be followed out of the forest by POKENAME, at great peril to themselves.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME buzzes quietly through dark forests, seeking lost travelers. POKENAME manipulates the surrounding trees to guide the disoriented wanderers deeper into the woods. It is said that the flash of its red eyes in the dark is a dark omen.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME often guide stray Pokémon that have lost their way in the forest. However, if these Pokémon belong to humans, they are rarely reunited with their Trainers.
author: riverbandage

entry: POKENAME have the ability to lower their body temperature, which allows them to splinter their own bark and use it as a projectile. If not used, the splinters will break off and be consumed by the Pokémon in order to add them back to their body.
author: riverbandage

entry: It hangs from tree branches using its tail, even when it rests. It is skilled at using its gliding membrane to ride on even the weakest breezes and can swiftly navigate through the forest as it hunts.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will find the largest tree in a forest and make its nest there. There it enters a trance to commune with all the trees in the forest, where it watches for threats. POKENAME will protect its forest, unfazed by even the strongest of foes.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Extremely aggressive, POKENAME crushes anything that enters its territory as a show of overwhelming power. Rarely, it has been observed searching for and gathering up huge shiny gems to hoard in its den.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME mysteriously appears when a Mudkip gets lost in the woods. The eye in its mouth is one of the countless children's souls in its body.
author: pokebio

entry: POKENAME has an innate connection to plant life and makes its home in old-growth forests. Due to excessive logging over the years, POKENAME actively avoids people, making it rare to encounter in the wild.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As it dances through the forest, POKENAME causes ominous winds to flow. These winds help the leaves on its body to dance with it.
author: toxicrown

entry: This Pokémon's staff allows it control over the forest. It uses this to help children from a distance, so that they don't meet a cruel fate.
author: toxicrown

entry: Known to many as the Forest Guardian, POKENAME protects those who can't protect themselves. It treats young forest Pokémon like its children.
author: toxicrown

entry: POKENAME can exert control over nearby trees by burying most of their bodies in the ground, save for their leafy backs. By ingraining themselves like this, they can also acquire nutrients and water from the ground and flora around them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME curls up in forests and resembles nothing more than a thick bush. It sleeps most of the day, but if it senses litter in its forest, it immediately goes on the attack and fires sharp leaves from its back at the defiler.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scratches its talons against tree trunks in order to keep them sharp. The bark of its body is said to possess healing properties when powdered, but POKENAME is very resistant to attempts to acquire its bark.
author: sk372

entry: In autumn, POKENAME can be found in pumpkin patches. It loves to play with children, but they often run away, terrified of POKENAME's haunting gaze.
author: thropp

entry: The gourd on POKENAME's back has reached full maturity and flavor. POKENAME may provide it to whoever asks near the end of its own lifespan, but those who try to take it by force will be cursed or worse.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses its claws to absorb the life force of its opponent. It buries itself to hide from danger.
author: jona_hehe

entry: As forests are demolished, people notice wild POKENAME prowling around. They relentlessly attack anyone it deems harmful to its territory.
author: endersalasa

entry: POKENAME's jaw never closes. Researchers are skeptical whether this Pokémon's totemic visage is its real face.
author: duplicitous_dirk

entry: POKENAME usually live in dark, dense forests. Despite their intimidating appearance, they are calm and can even be domesticated if fed their favorite fruits.
author: naivetotoro

entry: Known as the king of the forest by some, POKENAME often spends its time growing berries from its branches and eating them to bolster its immense strength. It is often seen caring for Slakoth and its fusions.
author: hiimhdere

entry: It acts as a warden and guardian spirit for the forest it calls home. It's particularly protective of lost children, regardless of if they are human or Pokémon.
author: staghorn

entry: A noble defender that lives in harmony with other forest-dwellers. Despite its usual reserved nature, POKENAME puts on a fierce display of its strength when warding forests from great disasters.
author: bacondlx

entry: Bark shed from POKENAME was thought to be divinely blessed. It burns slowly for days, making it a prized fuel source among swamp nations.
author: .izik

entry: There are a few fables that say POKENAME has the power to control an entire forest to defend itself or the other Pokémon within. While this is yet unsure, what is known is that POKENAME attacks any threat with many roots and vines.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its scary appearance, POKENAME are actually quite kind. They wander forests at night to lead lost people out. The gravestone on their bodies is said to bear the names of those they failed to save.
author: rumia_archer

entry: If anyone defiles the forest they protect, POKENAME will fight them without mercy. If pushed to the brink, POKENAME will ignite their arms in spirit fire, at risk of their own life.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME is the forest's executioner. It seeks out people who harm the forest and shows no mercy towards them with its living wood blade.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is thought to be created when a lumberjack cuts down an ancient tree. The now-possessed stump takes an axe and seeks vengeance... sharing the memory of its attacker to nearby trees.
author: mindrivet

entry: This adorable creature poses little threat to anyone who stays out of arm's reach. It lives in any forest that possesses an abundant enough moss supply for it to use as its food source.
author: fireblade141

entry: The wood covering its body has subsumed its being. POKENAME looks up to trees the way Pawniard look up to Bisharp, protecting them with its life.
author: bigblue

entry: POKENAME fight with a strong sense of honor for the forest, attacking those who disrespect it without mercy. The wood growing on its body is strong enough to rend metal.
author: bigblue

entry: Its leaves and hide always match that of a tree somewhere within its home forest. If that tree is threatened, it will appear to drive the threat away.
author: staghorn

entry: Some say the spirit of a Water-type Pokémon may possess trees by the river, such as riparia trees, becoming a POKENAME. It's currently unclear if the spirit is restless, POKENAME tend to keep to themselves, sometimes even drifting down streams.
author: merclipse

entry: POKENAME stalks prey through its forest, using illusions to make it look like trees the lost victim already passed and feeding on their emotional turmoil. Its bark is ground down for perfumes which make the wearer smell similar to those around them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME stalks prey through its forest, using illusions to make it look like trees the lost victim already passed and feeding on their emotional turmoil. Its bark is ground down for perfumes which make the wearer smell similar to those around them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME, despite their Sylveon DNA, are often loners living within dark forests. Attempts to study them in the wild prove difficult because they shy away from human contact.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's sap is one of the most corrosive poisons. It roams the forests, causing the ground to tremble to weaken its prey.
author: astrael1

entry: POKENAME resides high up in the sky, patrolling over its chosen forest domain. Causing harm to its territory will make it descend from above and blast the perpetrator with a cursed energy beam fired from its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's spectral branches extend into the fabric of time. Legends say touching the energy from its roots show visions from the past and future.
author: germs2128

entry: POKENAME watches over forests in secret, following those who desecrate its land until they fall asleep. As they slumber, it infests their dreams with horrific nightmares of living trees as punishment for their crimes against its home.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in forests and watches hikers from a safe distance. If someone tries to harm the forest, it catches them and turns them into a tree.
author: chorb33

entry: It's believed that the eyes inside its broken body are the souls of caught grave robbers. Its behaviour is erratic and it stares uncannily at people.
author: matpal6

entry: A clutter of POKENAME can build a web wide enough to engulf the entire forest they inhabit. The rough, resilient thread used in their nests is woven into carpets and sold with a promise to withstand nearly every Pokémon attack.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When a forest fire claims the lives of people or Pokémon, POKENAME mysteriously appear in large groups to mourn. They remain until the forest grows back and can sustain life again, then vanish without a trace.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME, lurking in brackish waters, extends rootlike arms beneath the surface. Any tree it touches becomes part of its will.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roams across the lands, flying from forest to forest to observe them. Though not overly aggressive, it will spirit away those causing harm to the trees, transporting them far away.
author: sk372

entry: Within each of its tails is said to be a mournful spirit of those who were forever lost within forests and jungles. By digging in even one of its tails into the ground, it can exert control over nearby plants and use them to repel would-be threats.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME tunnels beneath forests, fusing with root systems to awaken trees. Entire groves move subtly under its silent control.
author: .izik

entry: Ostensibly a guardian spirit of the forest, POKENAME's swipes are slow and unenthusiastic. The most it can muster to deter unwelcome visitors is a somewhat creepy wailing cry.
author: sk372

entry: The branch-like horn atop POKENAME glows faintly near old trees. With a glance, it can animate trunks into twitching sentinels of the forest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appears as a mysterious bubble housing a spectral tree, symbolizing the fusion of nature and psychic energy within.
author: anarchaz

entry: Groups of POKENAME hang out in dark forests, creepily staring at those who walk by. They will usually attach themselves to healthy trees and feed off their nutrients until the tree starts to wither.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME make their home on the borders between deserts and lush forests. They ambush prey with their roots and jaws. They also love apples.
author: totodile.

entry: Colonies of POKENAME inhabit large trees and defend them against any threat by biting with their jaws or scaring with their shrill chittering. They sense shifts in the leaves of the grove their tree is in and investigate suspicious changes in trios.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME pretend to be trees until prey gets too close. They can grow up to eight branches to chase prey, and never forget faces, favors, or slights.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME spins conductive silk between trees to form a living circuit with itself. Once prey is near, it channels shocks through bark and branch alike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME relentlessly harasses threats to the tree it has made its home. Its howling cry sounds like an intense wind blowing through tree branches. When digesting a meal, it is unable to fly, so it curls up and pretends to be a bush.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It appears when a piece of bark is peeled from a Trevenant. Each POKENAME contains a fraction of the original Trevenant's power.
author: holgast

entry: It appears when a piece of bark is peeled from a Trevenant. Each POKENAME contains a fraction of the original Trevenant's power.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME rolls around the forest like a tumbleweed, making an eerie creaking noise as it rolls. It leaves a trail of decaying plants wherever it goes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are often thought to be guardian spirits of the forest, as they frequently attack and disrupt logging operations. In truth, they simply hate the sound of heavy machinery.
author: alumed

entry: When a POKENAME roars, the trees around it quiver and sway as if responding to its call. Despite initial assumptions, POKENAME are gentle giants that prefer not to fight. They use their claw-like tails to till the ground so new life may take root.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can spin fast enough to churn the ground, allowing them to partially bury themselves. While buried, they can extend roots to control nearby plants. They can release freezing air all around them to impede any foes nearby.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME produce a special form of resin within them that can harden like amber within minutes of exposure to cold air. They preserve their prey in amber and feed on their lingering life force; when no life remains, POKENAME discard them.
author: infinex21

entry: Considering itself a defender of small plant-life, POKENAME patrols forests and gardens at night, flinging leaves at potential trespassers. Though small, these leaves possess sharp enough edges to leave nasty cuts.
author: sk372

entry: When it dances, leaves lift from the air and dance alongside it. During the fall, its colorful dances attract many picnickers.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Very sneaky and sly, POKENAME remains immobile and pretends to be a normal tree until it is time to hunt. It waits for unsuspecting prey to turn their back, before its roots launch it at blindingly-fast speeds to chomp down on its next meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its spiritual power to take control of trees at night, manipulating their branches and roots. It uses this primarily to frighten children that wander unattended into its forest home.
author: sk372

entry: This rare type of POKENAME is usually found in dense forests. It's said to steal people from their homes and savor the souls of the victims.
author: gun2._

entry: POKENAME releases deep, thunderous pulses through its leaflike ears. These vibrations rattle canopies and disorient prey with unnatural force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies over the skies of forests to scout for threats. Whoever harms its forest will be attacked mercilessly until they are eradicated.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME camouflages into dense treetops, before swooping down and dragging prey into nests they make in the canopy. This Pokémon's leaves are extraordinarily soft, and make for effective pillow stuffing.
author: hiimhdere

entry: If a human with a guilty conscience touches the sap dripping from a POKENAME, they will stick to its body and become trapped. The only way for them to be released from its clutches is by confessing their guilt.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME stamps its foot to send a ripple through the ground which wakes any trees nearby. The trees respond to POKENAME's call, bringing the power of an entire forest down on their foe. After battle, POKENAME rights any fallen tree.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME guard their forest from the moment they hatch. Intruders caught by this Pokémon are never seen again.
author: pikahunter07

entry: Its seven eyes are always blinking in patterns, which some believe allows it to communicate with bygone spirits. Its den is within a dead forest, yet by ingraining its many roots, it can control the dead plants to drive off threats.
author: infinex21

entry: On especially eerie nights, POKENAME will wander into towns, trying to steal the souls of the townsfolk. However, it usually sticks to dark forests and graveyards.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME communes with other cacti, including Cacnea and Cacturne, across vast stretches of desert via a root system. It tries to store water in its torso to share with other Pokémon that live in the desert.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is known as an ancient defender of the tundra. Through its roots, POKENAME is able to control other trees. It uses this power to build strong walls against those who wish to do harm.
author: odditylad

entry: Supposedly, it is the spirit of a dog combined with the spirit of its favorite stick. Now it plays an endless game of fetch by itself.
author: kiwiarms

entry: If POKENAME is spotted by a predator, it will run into the bushes. Once in the bushes, it will thrash around wildly, attempting to scare the predator off with the illusion of its more powerful evolved forms.
author: hiimhdere

entry: POKENAME will often carry younger Tremo-o on its shoulder, where leaves provide a comfortable place to rest. When threatened, it will shake its leaves and clack its wooden armor as a warning.
author: hiimhdere

entry: Fiercely protective of its pride, POKENAME will stop at nothing to ensure the safety of its family. If provoked, it will let loose a series of screeches and rattling, scaring off all but the most dauntless of foes.
author: hiimhdere

entry: POKENAME's camouflage is near-unmatched, allowing it to blend into the forest scenery like few other Pokémon can without illusions. If someone disturbs the forest, they will find themselves stalked by POKENAME relentlessly.
author: fireblade141

entry: These small wood sprites hide as bushes, functioning as sentries for Trevenant-guarded woods. They harass those who linger too long within.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME will remain peaceful towards those that don't threaten its forest. Should an intruder be foolish enough to endanger its territory, this Pokémon will animate every plant to imprison them.
author: ._term.

entry: In folklore, POKENAME are the mystical guardians of sacred forests. They are merciless against those who would ravage these forests, swiftly punishing them with a whirlwind of fire and thorns.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME clad themselves in protective cloaks of leaves held together with sticky bubbles; as such, they nest within tree foliage. They spit out many bubbles to put out flames and prevent forest fires, then hunt down those responsible.
author: infinex21

entry: Its cloak of leaves is held together with green, adhesive bubbles, which helps it to blend in while perched atop tree branches. It throws leaves at lumberjacks with remarkable accuracy and at such speeds that they will leave painful cuts.
author: infinex21

entry: The appendage around its neck is a long root that allows it to connect with and control nearby plants through their roots. From the shadows, it monitors those in its forest and attacks them with precise Water Shuriken if they harm the forest at all.
author: infinex21

entry: When agitated, such as in battle, parts of their bodies become red hot, and they exude a thick, black haze around them. This haze is laced with ash that works well as a fertilizer on its own, so their habitats are considerably lush.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME move awkwardly, though some would call it shambling more than walking, and fight by manipulating nearby plants and their roots. Reportedly, people have seen the red lights in POKENAME's shells following their movements and blinking.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hates anything entering its territory and will relentlessly pursue them until it catches them. You can determine which trees are its territory by the bodies slowly being consumed by their roots.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME will often lure innocent people into its forests, watching as they slowly get lost in the dark woods. It will often shift the position of the trees, making it almost impossible for its victims to escape.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses a perfect mixture of herbs and spices to create the best sourdough loaves. It is also especially great at baking yule logs.
author: dodoowner_

entry: When POKENAME puts on the large cookie mask that it holds over its face, it gains control of all nearby foliage. Knowing every smell in its forest, it always knows the moment when an unfamiliar threat enters its territory.
author: soup1900

entry: Clumsy and bumbling, POKENAME often gets stuck on its shell. To remedy this, POKENAME can control the roots around it, hopefully righting itself before, undoubtedly, repeating this process again.
author: hiimhdere

entry: Making its home in small forest ponds, POKENAME slowly corrupts the water it inhabits. This process kills all nearby life and renders the water toxic to drink.
author: evilgammon

entry: By day, POKENAME drink deeply from swamps through their roots. At night, they spread through the woods, manipulating trees to patrol in silence.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME floats silently between swamp trees. It subtly shifts nearby branches with its powers to keep its path clear as it glides.
author: .izik

entry: Bits of a wooden shell circle around POKENAME, levitated by a strange energy from its core. It manipulates these pieces both as projectiles and as armor when forced into battle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protects forests from those who harm them. Its flame never goes out.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: A storied Pokémon said to reside deep within ancient forests, with some stories claiming it resides at the very center. It will dig its mass of roots into the ground and then exert control over nearby plants to defend itself and its home.
author: infinex21

entry: It has the power to manipulate nearby plants, but that power is still weak. To intimidate others, it will bark at them and make nearby foliage rustle at the same time. If its threats fail, it will whimper and hastily flee.
author: infinex21

entry: Though POKENAME live and hunt in packs, at least one member of the pack will use their powers to manipulate the surrounding forest to aid the other pack members. Though they are loyal when their trust is gained, that trust is difficult to earn.
author: infinex21

entry: Legends say that sometimes, instead of a tree seed sprouting into a sapling, it grows into a POKENAME. It acts very violently in defense of its forest, whipping at intruders with wind blades reaching speeds of 80 km/h from its fan-like hands.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME is capable of churning vicious winds with its fan-like hands, which it does to protect the very forest that serves as its home. Although plant-based, it sweats a resin-like compound, which it will slather onto trees to repair any damage.
author: infinex21

entry: The branches of a POKENAME grow into long claws that they scrape against boulders to keep sharp. When they are not sharpening their claws, they wander haunted forests hoping to find the right Trainer to go home with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stretches its roots through the ground, tapping into nearby trees to feel what they feel. It uses this ability to sense the movement of other Pokémon through the trees, pouncing on anything that gets too close.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Should it need to frighten others away, POKENAME lifts off the head of its wooden body and levitates it around using psychic powers. It tends to get a headache once the head is reattached afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME move slowly through their forest territories, patrolling for any troublemakers. Though they may sometimes go idle, they are always alert and will fire powerful, precise Solar Beams from their hands if they detect a threat.
author: infinex21
