entry: Small towns in Unova have seen an increase of POKENAME sightings on account of them playing with children. Despite their strength, POKENAME are horrible teammates on account of their vanity.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME has embraced a more acrobatic style of fighting, Dance. When it dances, it whips up blades of wind to hurt its opponents.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME are popular in Galar, using their four arms and athleticism to perform soccer tricks to children. They are also popular with parents, as POKENAME have enough strength to easily defeat two Machamp without breaking a sweat.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME likes to get up close and personal in battle, assailing foes with spinning jump kicks and karate chops from above. Because of its leaf arms and spindly root legs, these strikes aren't as effective as it would like.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.

author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are highly festive creatures. The unique color of this Pokémon is said to indicate its personality.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME balances on its head vine before performing intricate acrobatics, using its flexible body to evade attacks. If cornered, it spits a blinding acid before flipping away to safety.
author: .izik

entry: Matches between POKENAME in the wild consist of pushing and shoving to see which fighter can push their opponent's heavy body out of bounds. POKENAME is known to have a strong rivalry with Hariyama.
author: sk372

entry: The poses it strikes in battle are controlled by the Shellder on its tail, biting on specific nerves to trigger a reflexive movement from POKENAME. In victory, the Shellder even makes POKENAME take a bow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME typically stay in the air with their light bodies and electromagnetism. They can use this electromagnetism to charge at their opponents at high speed, rarely missing.
author: entomoxie

entry: Its wings are tucked away and barely visible, too small to achieve flight.  Combined with POKENAME's running leaps, however, it can manage to glide for exceedingly long distances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known for their curved beaks, which they use to break open extremely hard nuts and tough fruits. Though they can deliver devastating pecking attacks, they are more known for their rapid kicking attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in circuses and water parks, reveling in the joy of entertainment. Aquatic acrobats and acts of juggling are its forte.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME likes to haunt venues where nighttime Pokémon battling is common. It loves to interrupt fights with its sudden appearance, taking on both sides of the initial battle at once and turning the moment into a true spectacle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's small arms are deceptively strong, allowing it to grip onto rock walls with ease. It uses this to help it strike from ceilings and make more acrobatic maneuvers when fighting in its cavernous home.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME store water within the cacti on their backs, allowing them to survive in arid environments. The more sunlight they absorb, the healthier their flowers become.
author: santon5512

entry: The seeds it carries scatter easily, taking root wherever they land. Other Pokémon often follow in its wake, hoping to benefit from the plants that quickly grow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wanders the desert systematically, protecting its territory. Mature POKENAME have flowers blossoming on the top of their head. The flesh of a POKENAME is as sweet as fruit.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's yellow skull releases a soothing scent in desert heat. The hotter the temperature, the stronger the aroma becomes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pretends to be a normal, albeit small, cactus to avoid the attention of others. It produces a nutrient-rich liquid within itself. It produces far more than it needs, so the excess is expelled like tears from its eyes.
author: infinex21

entry: Its limbs extend far beyond what seems possible, catching foes off guard. It uses this ability to surprise enemies from a distance before reeling itself back in.
author: .izik

entry: It dodges with expert precision, weaving between attacks like a seasoned fighter. Its movements are fluid, with each dodge leading seamlessly into a counterattack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tongue secretes a sticky sap that smells like cactus nectar. It uses this to coat its spines, trapping insects before consuming them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell has hardened so much that it limits its movements, so it uses its thin spines to ward off predators and other nuisances. It can survive for months without water thanks to the nutrients it stores within its cocoon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It buries its body in the sand and peaks its face out to absorb nutrients from the sun. Should it begin to rain, it will open its mouth wide to inhale any falling water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in deserts where they fly around avoiding sandstorms. Their wings are made of a material that allows them to produce nutrients using the harsh desert sunlight.
author: notmax22

entry: POKENAME's body soaks up water like a sponge and can endure days in the sun before returning to a water source. It hurls retractable spines at enemies while spinning at high speed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic powers to temporarily detach spikes from its body and fire them at opponents before causing them to float back to it again.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME bury themselves in the sand, basking in the desert sun. Lost travelers will often mistake these Pokémon for an oasis, the water on their backs helping to regulate their temperature.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are cubic and prickly creatures that nourish themselves off of scarce resources. Their bodies are made into green dyes that colors clothing and flags.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are common in desert biomes where they remain stationary for much of their lives. They nourish themselves off of their small roots, which dig into the ground to prevent them from moving.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Found surrounding desert oases, POKENAME only move during arid rainstorms. Due to other Pokémon attempting to drain their water, they sharpen their quills daily to pierce hardened hides.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A POKENAME's body is highly effective at absorbing and retaining moisture within itself, so it is never seen drying out in the desert heat. If it comes across thirsty travelers, it shares some of the water within its body to rehydrate them.
author: sk372

entry: It uses clouds to mask its presence, hiding until the perfect moment to strike. With each movement, fine sand falls from its wings, camouflaging it further.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a fisherman's nightmare. When caught in a net, its thorns will likely tear the mesh, freeing everything caught with it.
author: antomelon

entry: With a surprising grace, it performs playful dances to attract companions. Its rhythmic movements leave soft trails in the sand, enchanting those who follow.
author: .izik

entry: When flash floods sweep through the desert, POKENAME rushes to leap into the flow. Trusting its buoyant tail to keep it at the surface, POKENAME greedily absorbs enough water to sustain itself through months of drought.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: To avoid predators, POKENAME disguise themselves as cacti, standing incredibly still. Despite their appearance, the spikes on their bodies are actually rocky protrusions.
author: santon5512

entry: If you see a wild POKENAME in the desert, you can be sure there's an oasis nearby. The bigger its flower, the more beautiful its oasis is sure to be.
author: cristata

entry: If you see a wild POKENAME in the desert, you can be sure there's an oasis nearby. The bigger its flower, the more beautiful its oasis is sure to be.
author: cristata

entry: It hovers just above the ground, drifting gently on passing breezes. This floating ability allows it to evade ground-based attacks with ease.
author: .izik

entry: To survive the harsh temperatures of the desert, POKENAME absorbs heat during the day. It releases the heat gradually as the desert temperature drops.
author: .izik

entry: These small desert dwellers can live in small packs and travel for days across sandy dunes without water. Their spiky exterior protects them from many predators, and the number of spikes often denotes their rank within the group.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: It thrives in marshes, where its spines absorb moisture from the humid air. The damp environment keeps it active and ready to defend its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME survives in the desert where there is a paucity of food. It can be found eating bones of other Pokémon as the nutrient-rich bone marrow helps it stay strong.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite its tough appearance, it is surprisingly wimpy in confrontations. It tends to bluff aggressively, hoping intimidation will prevent actual combat.
author: .izik

entry: Due to its components having radically different habitats, study of POKENAME's behavior in the wild is still ongoing. If it absorbs too many particles that its porous body disagrees with, it will leak them from its spines along with a powerful toxin.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its body oozes a thick slime. It's typically too hot to safely touch, but cooled down samples of the slime can be used as lotion.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's body drips a moist sap, allowing it to slide along the ground. Drinking the sap, however, will cause digestive problems.
author: mistymagius

entry: It circles its prey multiple times before stunning it by throwing the cactus it carries. It can easily fly in even the worst sandstorms.
author: .izik

entry: A layer of frost covers its spines, chilling anything it touches. It uses this icy protection to fend off attackers and stay hidden in cold climates.
author: .izik

entry: Its body retains moisture despite living in dry environments, helping it survive harsh conditions. It camouflages itself among rock formations, waiting for prey to approach.
author: .izik

entry: They collect cacti and the flowers and fruits that grow on them. Drinking the cactus juice is said to be very quenching but can have unusual results.
author: pankiwi

entry: Known for acts of thievery, it sneaks into campsites to steal food and trinkets. Its quick reflexes make it difficult to catch in the act.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend days flying through deserts in search of oases, drinking as much water as they're able to once they find them. They will only move on when sandstorms start to roll in, taking to the skies to get ahead of them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's skin is very absorbent, allowing it to survive on the little rain the desert provides. They can stretch up to 15 feet when striking their prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: It spins rapidly to deter predators, kicking up dust clouds as it whirls. This spinning technique also helps it gather food scattered across the desert ground.
author: .izik

entry: It moves swiftly by rolling across the landscape, flattening anything in its path. Its spiny exterior makes this rolling technique both an attack and a defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME store pins inside their snout to arm themselves against malware attacks. When malware begins to infect files in a PC, POKENAME throw pins at the malware to inject blank lines of code until it is neutralized.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves to give other Pokémon a surprise smooch. Since its mouth is rough and thorny, most Pokémon prefer to keep their distance from POKENAME.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME live in deserts, surviving off of water stored in their body. They can swing their arms to electrify the water, however it is quite tiring.
author: currentlymuffin

entry: Some hikers have suffered nasty burns because they mistook the frightening POKENAME for a normal cactus and approached it without caution.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME will bash through sand dunes using their bludgeon-like tails. They do this in search of sources of water within the deserts they live in. Due to their inelegant means of searching, the water they find is quickly buried when they move on.
author: vic1312

entry: Multiple POKENAME come together at night to practice a sort of dance. It cries and retreats if caught off balance.
author: pokopish

entry: Despite their barbed outer layer, POKENAME are otherwise quite soft to the touch due to their expert ability to harvest and store water. They keep this fluid behind the sharp outer layer, making them shockingly squishy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME tunnel beneath arid deserts to eat cactus roots and drink from underwater reservoirs. They rarely come to the surface because everything they need to survive is underground, so many POKENAME are startled by bright lights.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The leaves that grow on POKENAME's back are nutritious and contain a lot of moisture within. It offers them to desert travelers to help keep them hydrated beneath the sweltering sun.
author: sk372

entry: It splashes in puddles, enjoying the cool water on hot days. Other Pokémon often join in, drawn to its carefree nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can survive indefinitely without water, drawing nutrients from magical sources instead. Though tiny, it is left alone due to its spines.
author: hellaluyeah

entry: In the vast emptiness of the desert, POKENAME has room to dance emotionally. If it spots someone watching, it will leave the voyeur with many pricks.
author: hellaluyeah

entry: POKENAME is a master of camouflage, using its spiky skin to blend into the desert landscape. It shifts through sunset colors to startle foes.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME's arms feature long needles perfect for scaring off potential threats. Their needles secrete a small toxin that they may drink to regain energy.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME eat Kebia Berries to reduce the risk of poisoning themselves after eating Poison-type Pokémon. In the harsh desert where food is scarce, being able to eat Poison-type Pokémon allows them to thrive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME needs a good amount of water daily in order to keep its body from drying out and becoming brittle. With some effort, it can grow and shoot spines from the shell on its back as a method of self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's flesh is saturated with clean, drinkable water. When a thirsty predator nears, it detaches the spheres on its back and makes its getaway.
author: staghorn

entry: Its body emits a faint magnetic field, which it uses to navigate through deserts. This ability allows it to find hidden minerals buried deep underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores water in its club-like structure. It shoots off its thorns in addition to bludgeoning its victims.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME defends itself by rotating at high speeds, shooting needles in all directions. This may even harm its Trainer, which is why many avoid it.
author: mystora

entry: They develop more vibrant, yellow colors the more well-nourished they are. Their ribbon-like organs exude an alluring aroma to attract prey, which they quickly down with precise strikes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME and Aiking are eternal rivals. Typically described as cruel, it is ruthless, unstable, and shows no mercy.
author: jreposo

entry: POKENAME's petals have been noted to contain a chemical that gives them a spicy taste if bitten off in battle. The chemical appears to assist with expelling excess heat to avoid burning the more fragile cactus body.
author: ohok3441

entry: Its body secretes aloe-like sap, which soothes and hydrates its spines. This natural gel protects it from harsh sunlight, keeping it healthy in dry, arid environments.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon thrives in intense heat, absorbing sunlight to power its movements. It builds complex dams even in arid conditions, relying on its resilience to endure the blazing sun.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME trains by rapidly striking rocks with its spiked fists. The impact releases small bursts of energy, which helps it sense the emotions of nearby Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dwell within oases, helping tend to the nature around them to help them stay lively and refreshing. Lost travelers often assume friendly POKENAME to be mirages until directly feeling their needles.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME leaves small yellow fur with a sharp needle inside that can give an electric shock and a dose of poison. In arid places, POKENAME is often seen shaking with electricity when preparing to attack.
author: riverbandage

entry: Its fur can store a tremendous amount of static electricity, as well as concealing the sharp thorns that cover its head and back. It curls up into a ball when it sleeps, keeping its soft belly protected.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: The thorns on its body are extremely nutritious and taste similar to Yache Berries. Many chefs use these thorns to flavor their curries.
author: .izik

entry: Sunlight energizes it, allowing bursts of rapid movement through the desert. It glimmers under the sun, leaving mirage-like reflections as it moves.
author: .izik

entry: The air around it feels scorching, as it radiates heat even while standing still. When agitated, it can release bursts of intense fire, scorching the ground beneath it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaps into desert oases and soaks up large amounts of water, its body growing larger and more rotund as it does so.  It then carefully waddles away to spray and share the water with others who need hydration.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's spines release a fine green powder that smells faintly of fresh herbs. This powder encourages plant growth in the arid environments where it lives.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sits still for long periods of time. The flower that adorns its head secretes a sweet scent. Its thorns are covered in a poison, however, so obtaining nectar is ill-advised.
author: manager_of_managers

entry: With incredible agility, it can jump great distances, easily evading threats. Pairs often practice leaping contests, developing both speed and coordination.
author: .izik

entry: A translucent membrane covers POKENAME's spiny body, keeping it hydrated even in extreme heat. If its fluid levels drop too low, its spines become brittle and break off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend lots of time getting nutrients from the sun, drinking with their mouth or planting their feet in soil. They headbutt spines in foes.
author: totodile.

entry: Screeching fills the air when it senses danger, warning others to keep their distance. It uses its voice both as a defense mechanism and a way to locate others in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: Disembodied whispers seem to follow wherever it goes, unsettling those nearby. These eerie sounds often lead travelers astray, as if urging them deeper into the desert.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly difficult to spot in the wild and will release jolts of electricity if stepped on. This fact makes it difficult to study, so most Trainers wear a set of heavy-duty boots to absorb the shock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon rolls in sand to sharpen its tiny spines, keeping them ready for defense. It glides smoothly across dunes, blending into the shifting landscape.
author: .izik

entry: It scatters embers with every flap, leaving tiny sparks in its wake. These glowing trails act as both warnings and lures, attracting curious Pokémon into traps.
author: .izik

entry: Its white fur is composed of thin but extremely sharp spines. The fire it produces is hot enough to melt desert sand into glass, which it uses to reinforce its spines.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME makes its home in greenhouses, camouflaging itself among potted plants. Under the cover of night, it quietly consumes the vegetation around it.
author: .izik

entry: When half buried in the desert sand, POKENAME look like any other budding cactus. Many desert enthusiasts can tell them apart by counting how many flowering buds are on their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often found in groups, dancing in the desert as they absorb sunlight through the flowers in their bodies. Spikes fly from their pom-poms as they shake them, keeping predators at bay.
author: santon5512

entry: A haunting wail echoes from deep within its body, unsettling those nearby. It moves slowly through forests, blending in with the shadows cast by ancient trees.
author: .izik

entry: The fruit on POKENAME's head isn't naturally poisonous, but POKENAME's sticky sap is. Because of this, the fruit needs to be thoroughly decontaminated before it can be eaten.
author: mistymagius

entry: The cactus head of POKENAME grows from the large bundle of dead bramble that makes up most of its body. It is unknown how it can fly, but scientists theorize that there may be clouds hidden inside the bramble.
author: soup1900

entry: Only growing in sandy areas heavy with metals, POKENAME are surprisingly dense and resilient. They are often revered as heralds of an ancient power.
author: quant9690

entry: POKENAME is often kept as a home defence system in warmer climates. It sits in a pot by its owner's front door and hugs any potential intruders with strong arms covered in spikes.
author: odditylad

entry: While absorbing sunlight with its thorns, it will hold the same pose for hours. Should it be disturbed, it will hop up in alarm and skitter away at great speeds.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient ruins are its preferred resting spots, where it camouflages among crumbled walls. It absorbs remnants of old structures to strengthen its defenses.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have parasitic flowers that use their bodies as a source of water and nutrients to allow them to bloom despite harsh desert conditions. The presence of these flowers force POKENAME to constantly be on the search for water sources.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon wanders miles of desert looking for oases to absorb water and nutrients from. The round cactus on its back holds the water it needs to keep cool in the blistering heat.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME live amongst cacti deep in the desert, hiding amongst the thorny plants and only moving at night. They use their claws and teeth to puncture the thick hide of the cacti and drink the juice within to quench their thirst.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's spiny body is covered in a tough, bark-like shell that hardens over time. It absorbs sunlight to fuel its rapid growth, sprouting small leaves along its arms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a thick cactus shell that protects them as they ram into each other. Their shell swells with water after heavy rainfall and slowly shrinks as the water is depleted.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's sturdy armor helps protect it from multiple kinds of attacks, but its size and weight are a detriment to its health. It requires large amounts of water to function, wilting and falling apart quickly if it goes without water for too long.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME feasts on sand. Whatever is not processed by its body is ejected as dust and smoke. Typically, the larger a POKENAME's midsection is, the more optimal its body is at processing its food.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's hollow body glows faintly at night, luring wandering travelers deeper into the desert. The eerie flicker is said to resemble a lost soul searching for home.
author: .izik

entry: The fruits this Pokémon grows inside its crown are sweet and nutritious, but are also covered in hundreds of tiny needles. In POKENAME's natural habitat, only Numel and Camerupt are adapted to eating these fruits without hurting themselves.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME travel across the desert holding water with their elastic pouches to make sure that their roots stay properly hydrated. If anyone tries to take a POKENAME's water, they will be met with a powerful headbutt laden with needles.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME expands and absorbs rainwater during torrential downpours until it is full and replete. It slowly shrinks in size as it endures weeks or even months without water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rest in clusters under the hot desert sun. When it absorbs enough heat, it will grow a small yellow flower on its face.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME survives off of sunlight and positive emotions, particularly love. Many old couples living in the desert have large POKENAME in their homes, a sign of enduring love and affection.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME store water within their bodies, allowing them to survive in the harshest of temperatures. They shoot spikes at predators, retreating into their burrows the moment they get too close.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME soars high above dry deserts. Its preferred method of attack is dive bombing prey exhausted by the sun's heat.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME tails swish rapidly when they're annoyed; the frequency of their tail flicks reflects their growing irritation. If sufficiently provoked, they lash out with their tail, scratching the source of their ire with the thorns lining it.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Greedy and territorial, POKENAME sharpens its swordlike tail on its thorns, then uses it to bully weaker Pokémon into giving it shiny objects. Things it steals are often never seen again.
author: agentyoshi

entry: POKENAME are capable of rapidly absorbing water through their singular foot, which they balance on to keep themselves upright. This ensures that their bodies are well hydrated after a long drought.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The stormy clouds around POKENAME soothe sunburns and moisturize dry skin. One should be careful to stay away from POKENAME's sharp thorns while using this treatment.
author: hophoppip

entry: This Pokémon throws nuts with surprising accuracy, often aiming at unsuspecting targets. It takes delight in this playful mischief, though it quickly flees if confronted.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME happily perch atop Cacnea or one another to rest and give physical affection. Their fur ends in sharp points akin to needles, so many Pokémon avoid them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its temper flares when the heat becomes unbearable, making it dangerously aggressive. During hot days, other Pokémon keep their distance, knowing its mood worsens with rising temperatures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a devious and underhanded combatant, striking unerringly at its opponent's weak spots whenever possible. It uses the prickly thorns on its fists and feet to its full advantage in a fight.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME has a fascination with competition and enjoys playing all manner of summertime sports. Unfortunately, its needle-sharp spines make some sports more difficult to participate in than others.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: POKENAME's natural strength and ability to go for long periods without a single drop of water makes it an invaluable companion for ranchers in inhospitable environments.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: It is seen living in desert environments where the topsoil is no longer present. They mingle their roots underground so they can share nutrients and remain grounded.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The seeds POKENAME scatters from its mouth are highly fertile and can take root even in the driest desert sands. Many cacti fields owe their existence to the wandering travels of this Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: These mischievous Pokémon are known for swinging their club-like appendages to break objects in play. Though chaotic alone, when grouped they show remarkable coordination and act as one seamless unit.
author: big_clanker

entry: Topaz shards embedded in its body gleam under sunlight, giving it a dazzling appearance. These gemstones are known to attract treasure hunters, often leading to conflict.
author: .izik

entry: Often appearing tired, it moves slowly even in the hottest sun. Its sluggish nature belies the power hidden within its thorny body.
author: .izik

entry: Its magnetic field is unusually strong, allowing it to pull in small objects from a distance. It uses this ability to collect metal scraps, which it stores for unknown purposes.
author: .izik

entry: Small pins cover its body, which it uses for defense and gathering food. When agitated, it flails wildly, sending these pins flying in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: It thrives near hidden oases, where it stores water for dry spells. Other desert creatures often follow it, hoping to discover these life-saving havens.
author: .izik

entry: It collects discarded soda cans, hoarding them inside its hollow slimy body. The rattling sounds it makes often confuse opponents, giving it time to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a desert spirit that only comes out in the late evenings. If several congregate together, they can conjure up an illusion of a watery oasis to trick travelers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's skull is covered in needles that sharpen with age. An adult's bone can pierce stone when thrown.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stalk desert oases and lash out at intruders using their thorn-clad clubs. Their clubs are packed with nutrients and water that they can siphon as they need; frequent desert travelers often have a few of these clubs in case of emergency.
author: infinex21

entry: It wanders through the desert, searching for an opponent. It's a formidable fistfighter, and its hands are studded with painful spikes.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME float by drawing dew into their bodies as water vapor and heating it. If threatened, they expel all of the steam at once, shooting spines in every direction.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a regular cactus by desert-dwelling Pokémon. If disturbed, it relentlessly blasts the aggressor with a powerful water blast. Despite this, it remains near the bottom of the food chain.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME creates invisible walls to help shield itself from raging sandstorms. It uses these barriers to trap prey.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME roams through deserts singing. It shakes its thorny body rhythmically to add rattling noises to its rapid singing.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are crucial to the desert ecosystem as they provide other Pokémon with the nutritious water they produce. Few are left in the wild because of hunting by humans trying to sell the exotic drink.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME needs to absorb water often to maintain its liquid-like consistency. It looks for sources like ponds and other Pokémon to drain water from.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME are common in desert biomes and need very little water to function. Their long bodies can be broken down into smaller pieces that are sent to factories to extract green dye.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME isolate themselves for extended periods within the depths of the desert, subsisting on little food and water. If disturbed, they will lash out with their psychic might and bludgeon-like tail.
author: vic1312

entry: The fire on its back is the condensed energy it absorbs from the sun. The POKENAME with the brightest flame is the alpha of the pack.
author: gurguro

entry: It performs graceful, ballet-like movements, mesmerizing onlookers with elegant spins. Each step releases a soft aroma, making it as captivating as it is dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: Rumors say that if you spot a wild POKENAME during the night, you'll start seeing strange visions. However, this Pokémon is friendly during the day.
author: birchbot

entry: POKENAME have adapted to live in deserts, and now live in large burrows instead of trees.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is a weak Pokémon that stays still to conserve nutrients and moisture. It waits for strong winds to carry it to desert towns, where it relies on helpful citizens to care for it until evolution.
author: mepp.

entry: In desert communities long ago, Trainers kept POKENAME as guards. They would spew thorns from their gills as strangers approached, the colour of these thorns would indicate if the strangers were welcome.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It feeds by photosynthesizing using the moonlight it absorbs in large quantities as it roams the desert plains. If anyone gets too close, POKENAME threatens them with the spines that grow on its body and tail.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If POKENAME doesn't get enough moonlight, it becomes particularly irritable and starts threatening other Pokémon with the green spines on its body. It prefers to lead a nomadic, solitary life in vast deserts rather than settle in one place.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME love shiny, reflective objects. Unfortunately, they startle at the sight of their own reflection, leaving their prize behind as they flee.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME spends the day meditating, awakening at night to patrol its desert home. With its incredible intellect, it skillfully commands Remoraid to aid it in disciplining unruly Pokémon.
author: mepp.

entry: Its movements induce dizziness in foes, leaving them disoriented and vulnerable. The unique rhythm of its steps confuses even the most experienced opponents.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME is always looking for bigger cacti to use as segments for its body. Members of the species often fight over large cacti.
author: gurguro

entry: It succumbs to sudden bursts of rage, attacking anything in its path. Despite its anger, it can be calmed with careful handling.
author: .izik

entry: Roaming the harshest deserts, POKENAME's natural camouflage keeps it safe from predators. Due to their slow movements, predators barely notice POKENAME even if they're right next to it.
author: bigoljax

entry: It roosts among skyscrapers, watching the city below with keen eyes. From these high perches, it can strike quickly and return to safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have learned how to monetize their cactus collection. Their target customers are florists and coffee-shop owners. They've been spotted trying to plant the money.
author: pankiwi

entry: It rotates rapidly, using its spines to clear obstacles in its path. This spinning technique doubles as both an attack and a defense mechanism.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend hours training their strength by throwing around hay bales. When it's not training, POKENAME can often be seen dancing in hoedowns.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME spins on its head to disperse excess heat from its body when temperatures rise too high in the desert sun. Oddly, it does not drill deeper into the sand, no matter how fast it spins, unless it chooses to do so.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the desert sand to protect itself from the heat. When small prey comes along, it hops out and clings to it with its spines.
author: chorb33

entry: Their bodies are lined with many thorns that contain a potent toxin. Any shed thorns can actually take root like seeds and grow into purple flowers that have an intoxicating aroma.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will attack people in deserts to pilfer their water, then vanish with a echoing laugh. It often appears as a scarecrow in farms.
author: awiralonprime

entry: Trainers returning from the desert regions of Hoenn tell tales of a stand of cacti that suddenly uprooted themselves and ran away. In truth, these sightings are packs of POKENAME, mistaken from a distance thanks to their coloration and thorny crest.
author: sirg44

entry: It grapples with opponents using its flexible arms, holding them in place. Once it has a firm grip, escape becomes nearly impossible.
author: .izik

entry: Because it lives in harsh deserts, its body conserves large amounts of water. Somehow this seems to generate large amounts of electricity, a phenomenon scientists still struggle to find an explanation for.
author: sontyp

entry: It can last several decades without water, laying still to photosynthesize and conserve energy. Bands of POKENAME migrate at night.
author: capwolfbane

entry: POKENAME's fur is spiky, like needles. Touching one while they feel threatened will result in thousands of pricks to the skin, each delivering cold shocks.
author: glacierwing

entry: POKENAME patiently waits in open fields, pretending to be a regular scarecrow. If anything gets too close, it will pop out of the ground and chase away the intruders.
author: mistymagius

entry: The desert-dwelling POKENAME has powerful legs cloaked with energy-sapping spines: a single kick can cause numerous injuries. Its blood is similar in composition to molten glass and rapidly hardens if exposed to fresh air.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives on hot, arid islands where it slowly stalks prey while it pretends to be a non-threatening plant. The prickly fruit that grows on the ends of its arms has a sweet flavor and a juicy texture, making it sought out to top off dishes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME have lived in harsh desert climates since ancient times. It is known for its ability to subsist on very little water for extended periods of time.
author: mepp.

entry: Being made entirely out of grass, all living things that POKENAME eats go right through it. They instead get their nutrients from the victim's fear.
author: retrocrow

entry: Few dare challenge these giants, but those who do must get past their thorny hides and avoid the stinging acid sprayed from glands near their eyes.
author: wigglypon

entry: Always facing north, it navigates through deserts with uncanny precision. This orientation never changes, even when it is caught in powerful storms.
author: .izik

entry: Incredibly sharp eyesight allows POKENAME to see for miles in the desert, even at night. It will stalk prey for hours, then strike in the dark.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: POKENAME stalks travelers and Pokémon as night falls, waiting for them to tire out due to the heat before it strikes. It can absorb nutrients through its feelers, even from prey, and the process often renders the victim unnaturally soothed.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME requires very little moisture to live, and it gets most of its nutrients from sand. Take extra care when approaching it, as the spikes covering its body are filled with poison.
author: bacondlx

entry: Many desert regions trade Rose Incense made from POKENAME's flowers. Long ago, the spiky thorns on its arms were honed into heads for primitive spears and arrows.
author: ilazerheart

entry: POKENAME moves silently through the desert, rarely appearing before the sun sets. Its blinding speed allows it to ambush prey before disappearing without a trace.
author: .izik

entry: Hunger and thirst have driven this Pokémon to hunt whatever can fit inside of its body. Travelers can throw water or food into it and quickly escape.
author: quant9690

entry: As dusk nears in the desert, POKENAME appears on the periphery to stalk lost travelers. When night falls, POKENAME lights lost souls the way to dusty death.
author: pattybgoode

entry: It wanders the deep sea, camouflaging among coral reefs. Its thorny appearance deters predators in the abyss.
author: .izik

entry: Touching its spines causes a burning sensation that lingers for hours. It uses this painful defense to discourage predators from getting too close.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME can kick up a raging sandstorm with a single flap of its wings. The air inside these sandstorms can reach temperatures of nearly 200°F - more than enough to deal with any would-be desert predators.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME live deep in the desert under intense sunlight, families of them travelling slowly together across the dunes. On the rare occasions that it rains, their tails will rapidly bloom with short-lived flowers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its powerful bite can crush even the hardest shells. It burrows into the ground, waiting patiently for prey to stumble into its trap.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces a sweet juice inside its body which is incredibly effective at slaking thirst in deserts. In particularly dry months, its protective shell is weakened due to moisture loss.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: The aloe POKENAME secretes emits a pungent odor reminiscent of rotten onions. Historically, pharmacists used this aloe as a key ingredient in burn ointments.
author: .izik

entry: It digs tirelessly through the sand, creating complex tunnel networks. These hidden paths offer it both shelter and a way to ambush prey.
author: .izik

entry: Unable to pass on and full of regret, POKENAME linger in this world. They will stay attached to their husk until it fades away.
author: quant9690

entry: Once considered a parasite, scientists now understand that POKENAME benefits its host. It latches onto larger Pokémon and drinks their blood, using the waste products and returning the water, letting the host survive in drier regions.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its body radiates intense heat wherever it goes. Flames sometimes flicker from its spines, setting fire to dry grass and brush.
author: .izik

entry: Since it lacks teeth to bite with, POKENAME pins prey down by flinging sharp spines from its wings. Once a target has been immobilized, it can swoop down and begin draining its fluids.
author: sk372

entry: Many people and Pokémon alike have lost their lives by getting too close to a POKENAME which they mistook for a harmless scarecrow.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME goes on the defensive by curling into a ball, its tough and prickly exterior providing ample defense. It fires highly toxic spines from its tail that cause rapid dehydration in those hit.
author: sk372

entry: These brutal Pokémon live and swim within desert sands as if they were mere water, the sight of their dorsal fins a common nightmare for many. They can swim so fast as to create a swirling pit of sand that few have ever escaped from.
author: infinex21

entry: At night, POKENAME stands motionless atop desert dunes, releasing a fragrant lilac scent into the air. This scent is said to lull weary travelers into a deep slumber, leaving them vulnerable to the desert's dangers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can survive days without water by storing moisture deep within its body after it eats. Its loud screeches echo across the desert, giving it the nickname the “Desert Banshee”.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME surrounds itself with a personal sandstorm, using the unstable storm to travel through the air. They prefer arid environments and will seek out deserts and savannahs if there's heavy rainfall.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Brutal sandstorms do not phase POKENAME at all. On the contrary, they often go to gather together and dance within the blistering winds.
author: quant9690

entry: It performs dazzling acrobatics, leaping and spinning through the air. Its swift, unpredictable movements leave enemies struggling to react.
author: .izik

entry: Sandstorms swirl around it, summoned effortlessly by its presence. These storms obscure its movements, making it a difficult target to track.
author: .izik

entry: It stands completely still at day so it doesn't lose moisture in its skin to the sun. At night, it uses its razor-sharp claws to tear apart prey.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: Ancient crypts are its preferred hiding spots, where it remains undisturbed. It is said to guard secrets that should never be uncovered.
author: .izik

entry: It stands guard over ancient temples, waiting silently for trespassers. Legends say its spines are remnants of sacred relics lost to time.
author: .izik

entry: The deserts where POKENAME are found get dangerously cold at night. Nobody knows where they go during the daytime.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's lithe body is perfect for the many dance styles it has mastered. It uses these skills to lure in the avian Pokémon it preys upon.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME primarily eats seeds and roots for its diet. In the hot desert sun, tiny spines grow from its head, adding to its formidable defense and helping it adapt to its harsh environment.
author: .izik

entry: Within their heavy shells are pools of boiling sand that has an unending flow, so long as they are awake and alive. They can release controlled blasts of this sand to quickly conquer prey and most foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's pants-like lower half is similar in consistency to cactus flesh. Chefs use its shed layers in a delightful sautéed Rindo Berry dish, creating a unique and savory treat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found frozen mid-step. However, when it feels the rhythm of rain upon its body, it bursts into festive dance, shaking itself to create a sandy rattling noise. This continues until the rain ends and it sleeps once more.
author: wiz0z

entry: It thrives in extreme heat, absorbing energy from the scorching ground. This heat fuels its movements, making it faster during hot days.
author: .izik

entry: When walking in the desert, you might get ambushed by a POKENAME suddenly sprouting from the ground. It attacks by shooting a mix of thorns and sand.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME becomes entranced when it encounters a tumbleweed, often playing with it until dawn. If disturbed, it retaliates with a powerful Slash attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME roams around the desert nights, gusts of freezing-cold wind swirling around its body. It hibernates under the sand during the day to keep its body from burning up in the sun.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its spines are as hard as sandstone, giving it immense durability. When angered, it strikes with relentless force, showing no mercy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will draw heat energy from the harsh desert sun to fuel its fiery attacks. The sand within its body keeps its cactus body from burning.
author: mistymagius

entry: As they get older, POKENAME get lazy and will often try to skive off from the farming work they are often used for. This often takes the form of extra weight training instead of carrying out tasks.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME appears to understand that everyone loves an underdog and seems to take great pleasure in absolutely overwhelming any that it faces. After fights it must rest for several days, as its sandy blood struggles to bring nutrients to its muscles.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Basking in the desert sun, POKENAME emits a sweet, melon-like scent that drifts through the air. However, this alluring aroma is merely a trap - it strikes at prey the moment they wander too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is quite warm to the touch despite its blood having sand-like properties. It dashes across the desert, ensnaring prey with its tail.
author: mepp.

entry: It absorbs sunlight to fuel its spines, which grow sharper with each day. In the heat of noon, it becomes nearly immovable, basking in the sun's energy.
author: .izik

entry: It dashes through desert landscapes with incredible speed, leaving trails in the sand. Its twin heads coordinate perfectly, allowing seamless movement through rough terrain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wanders the desert in search of Trainers, to whom it gives a pendulum. Come night, the trinket will make the recipient fall asleep forever.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME wanders the desert in search of Trainers, to whom it gives a pendulum. Come night, the trinket will make the recipient fall asleep forever.
author: thefinalkalgonus

entry: POKENAME are constructed out of a special sand that allows them to crawl on beaches. They eat lots of kelp before evolving and entering into their pupal state.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whenever POKENAME is excited, it screams loudly and violently. This causes people and Pokémon around it to repeat that same action.
author: 8xviktor

entry: While it resembles a beach ball, it should not be picked up or played with, as it will explode at the slightest provocation.  This has ruined many people's vacations.
author: bostroms

entry: These Pokémon are shy around most, except for young Pokémon and human children. They wield the tools or toys shared with them by their young friends but cry if said tools or toys are ever broken.
author: infinex21

entry: This beach-loving Pokémon wears a shell to protect its head. It watches over young Pokémon and human children as they play and will use a child's shovel to fight for the sake of others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are at the center of a contentious issue: some people believe that knocking over a POKENAME is acceptable because they can reform, while others believe that knocking them over is mean-spirited.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have wings that are made of umbrellas and often get swept away by gusts of wind. Their ability to remain grounded is contingent on having heavy parasol wings, which are usually adorned with charms to make them heavier.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME expand and contract in size depending on how much water is in their body. The shovel atop their head is solely decorative, as their stinger is found on their tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It forms its body into intricate castles to impress onlookers. The castles come with extra details depending on the POKENAME: flames, thunderclouds, moats, a sun or moon, forests, snowmen and heart motifs have been observed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is able to squeeze through tiny cracks due to its ability to turn into sand, mud or water. They enjoy enclosed spaces, and are found napping by treasure hunters inside treasure chests.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME studies architectural data to subtly alter its structure each day. Many believe no two individuals are ever identical.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seek out floppy disks and flash drives containing blueprints, absorbing them into their sandy bodies. Their bodies will morph to match the designs of these blueprints, replicating them with nearly perfect accuracy.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are found on beaches often visited by children. It doesn't mind when people use its shovel and pail but will get angry if they aren't returned.
author: cloudmaker2169

entry: POKENAME forms a Beedrill out of sand to ward off beach-dwelling water types. However, this often results in it being attacked by large bird Pokémon.
author: duskrd

entry: POKENAME are speckled with small pebbles all over their body, each pebble they gather amplifies their ability to control sand. They can be seen helping children build sandcastles at the beach, scooping sand with the shovel on their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME naturally generate molten glass on their backs. Glassblowers and glaziers often keep a POKENAME in their shop.
author: capwolfbane

entry: The spines on its back is formed from superheated glass. It fires these sharp quills in multitudes when startled.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Its flames are hot enough to melt the sand on its back, creating a thick layer of glass. The glass shines brightly due to the reflection of the fire, dazzling its foes.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: The intense heat from its flames creates a thick layer of glass to form on its back. It has to be careful with its shovel because if it gets too close to its flames, the shovel will completely melt.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME builds up extreme heat inside its body, which rises to the surface. As a result, some of its sand melts into glass, forming a sculpture akin to fire.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Flocks of POKENAME hide buried at the seaside, waiting for beachgoers to arrive. Once people have set up for relaxation, the flock bursts up with Sand Attacks at the level of a sandstorm, steals as much food and snacks as possible, and flies away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME spends long stretches of the day napping on sunlit beachfronts. It enjoys playing with children, and will circle them with its long, sandy body to protect them from perceived threats and nuisances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME runs about beaches and dives into sandcastles, claiming them as its new home. It cries and flings sand at those who would try to remove it from its castle.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often collects small pebbles it likes and keeps them on its body. It is said to bring good fortune if a POKENAME gifts you one of its pebbles.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is very timid and spends most of its time hiding in the sand. It prefers to hide on secluded beaches as it hates when beachgoers try to tug at its shovels.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stands motionless atop sun-scorched dunes, staring directly into the blazing sun. Some believe that if it ever looks away, it's flooded with visions of those who died lost in the desert.
author: .izik

entry: Due to its body being mostly composed of sand, it is able to be easily carried by strong wind currents. However, it needs to land on soft beaches every so often to prevent its body from being blown apart.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME drifts along coastlines with others of its kind. Upon spotting a lone human, they descend and quiet their target's screams with their fluffy puffball before pulling them beneath the sand.
author: .izik

entry: It delights in playing pranks on beachgoers by stealing hats, sandals, or snacks with its long tail. The stolen items are then buried and marked with tiny sandcastles.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME turn almost invisible when submerged in water, only given away by the shovel on their head that remains solid. Anyone who attempts to take the shovel is said to have a curse put on them that causes them to slowly turn into sand.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME turn almost invisible when submerged in water, only given away by the bucket on their head that remains solid. Anyone who attempts to take the bucket is said to have a curse put on them that causes them to slowly turn into sand.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME secure buckets atop their heads to help them concentrate their psychic power on maintaining a physical form. While sleeping, they allow their bodies to dissolve back into sand, hiding within the safety of their buckets.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Often you will see long, winding trails in the sand on beaches that lead to nowhere. These are the lazy burrowing paths of a POKENAME, which spends most of its time sluggishly tunneling just beneath the surface.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Disguising itself as a small dune, POKENAME waits in silence. If someone approaches, it springs up, latches on with powerful jaws, and drags them beneath the surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feed on old lava flows, breaking down the silica-rich rocks into sand and incorporating the grains into their bodies. Beaches with large POKENAME populations are popular tourist destinations for their brilliant white sands.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Primarily found on arctic beaches, POKENAME tirelessly wanders about, nose to the ground, sniffing for ideal sand to add to its frozen body.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME charges low across beaches, using its massive body to sweep up shells and debris like a sand plow. Occasionally, it gets stuck in tidepools and can only get out by flailing wildly.
author: jaminmcready

entry: While within cyberspace, POKENAME's sandy body takes on the form of code, allowing it to move freely. When exiting, its body becomes sandy once more, often leaving bits of sand within the machine it exited from.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time on the beach creating magnificent sculptures out of sand. While it often gathers large crowds wanting to view its art, it is terrified of anyone accidentally damaging them.
author: mistymagius

entry: During thunderstorms, its kelp-like tail points skyward to absorb lightning. It stores the electricity in its shovel-like ears and unleashes it in a violent burst if tourists wander too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very elusive, hiding beneath the sands of remote beaches and rarely interacting with others. However, if something threatens its home, it whips up searing sandstorms that flicker all the colors of the rainbow.
author: sk372

entry: It builds miniature arenas in the sand and stages battles between shell fragments and lost trinkets. After each mock skirmish, it carefully resets the field for another round.
author: jaminmcready

entry: A perfectly crafted sandwich that also happens to be a budding sand-witch. To a Trainer it likes, consuming portions of it can grant magical powers.
author: koishikomeiji.

entry: POKENAME draw lightning strikes to themselves during storms, raising their tails on beaches to make them easy targets. Their tail and parts of their body are turned into fulgurite, the fragile glassy material sparkling with captured lightning.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME creates a facsimile of Munchlax in order to approach others and ask for food, beguiling them with its cute appearance. Donated food gets stored in the decoy's stomach, which returns the meals back to the main body.
author: sk372

entry: The shovel-like appendages on its head detect the happiest person nearby. It feeds on joy like a nutrient, soaring toward its target and blanketing them in sand that drains their happiness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME causes seaweed to erupt from the sand around it to ensnare humans who venture too close. Despite being an herbivore, it will hold them for hours before releasing them to frighten them away from its den.
author: .izik

entry: Trainers of POKENAME use their tails as shade on bright summer days. Those unfamiliar with tropical environments mistake their seed pods for small coconuts.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME hide along beaches and avoid most people, though they seem to happily spend time with children and young Pokémon. If anyone touches the shovels in their heads, however, they will lash out and spew flames.
author: infinex21

entry: Unlike many Mudkip fusions, POKENAME does not enjoy getting wet and muddy. Moisture causes its body to weaken and grow sluggish, so it tries to stay as dry as possible and avoid any water sources.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are commonly found on beaches and love playing with children who are making sandcastles. Children should beware trying to take their bucket, however, as POKENAME are known to hold a grudge.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME can be found with family Trainers on beach days. They use their tails to rescue children in case they begin to get swept out to sea.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are mystifyingly drawn to the abandoned sand pails on beaches and don them as helmets. They almost never reveal their faces because they are so shy, but some children claim they have seen them when playing with POKENAME on the beach.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is lonesome and shy, and has difficulty approaching others at the beach. It can usually only gather enough courage to approach children it thinks will be kind, hoping to find a playmate.
author: sk372

entry: The grains of sand making up POKENAME's body lay flat around ancient desert tombs, blending in perfectly. It lunges out and drags explorers into the ground.
author: .izik

entry: When at rest, POKENAME appears to be little more than a giant flower sitting on the beach sands. Those who poke and prod the flower get a nasty scare when POKENAME angrily rises up to its full size.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to stroll beaches and collect rocks to decorate themselves with. When not in use, they store the bucket at the tip of their second mouth.
author: hummusishome

entry: POKENAME digs shallow pits in the sand, covering itself with driftwood and seaweed. It lies in wait for prey or intruders, snapping awake with a hiss if anyone steps too close.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is quiet and gentle, enough so that it will regularly play with children on the beach. However, the shovel on its head is extremely sensitive; it will vanish instantly if anyone touches it even lightly.
author: sk372

entry: If startled, POKENAME crumbles into a pile of sand, only reforming once it feels secure. POKENAME cries nonstop if the coconut on its back cracks, making its body soggy until the shell is fixed.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME buries itself along the shoreline, mimicking the surrounding environment. Should someone draw too close, it entangles them in thorny vines and drags them beneath the sand.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoys playing in the sand on beaches and gets excited when a child wants to build with it, causing the flame of its tail to burn brighter. If an adult tries to take the child away from it, POKENAME will aggressively throw sand at them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME has an almost manic compulsion to dig many holes in the sand at the beach it inhabits. If anything tries to dissuade it from this habit, it repels them with the blue flames on its tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lies flat in desert sands, waiting to spot lost humans. Should it see one, it bursts from the sand screeching and sprints toward them the entire way.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are common along beaches in cooler climates, often playing and spitting out vividly colorful bubbles, which are famous for the sight they provide at dawn. If the shovels on their rears are ever touched, they quickly become enraged.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME nests can always be found in deserts surrounded by extremely damp sand. It pulls prey beneath the surface if they investigate too closely.
author: .izik

entry: After human visitors leave the beach, POKENAME inhales the sand left behind through its large nose. It gradually adds the absorbed grains to its body, slowly growing in size.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME possesses a shovel and can control sand. It throws sand in its victims eyes, bludgeons them, and buries them alive to drink their life force.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME possesses a shovel and can control sand. It throws sand in its victims eyes, bludgeons them, and buries them alive to drink their life force.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its red ribbons are said to be gifts from friends, potentially far in the past. It is a friendly and docile Pokémon that loves to play with others on the beach; it grows aggressive if anyone touches its ribbons, however.
author: infinex21

entry: At night when the tide is low, these mysterious Pokémon will appear and rearrange the left behind shells and stones into constellations on the sand.
author: cristata

entry: Slowly rising from the sand at night, POKENAME sliently glide along beaches to collect litter left behind by humans. They tear up the debris with the glass shards in their bodies to warn visitors that they should properly dispose of their trash.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's shovel-like wings allow it to take short, rapid flights. Swarms can be seen filling eastern coastline skies each spring in a dazzling but ominous display.
author: .izik

entry: Anyone who is unfortunate enough to stumble upon a POKENAME at the beach refers to it as a pest. POKENAME will not only fight children but will also fill your electronics with sand.
author: odditylad

entry: At night when the tide is low, these mysterious Pokémon will appear and rearrange the left behind shells and stones into constellations on the sand.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME may leave glass shards in its wake. It was reported that a Trainer's Pokémon once had a limb encased in glass after an encounter.
author: uncookie

entry: POKENAME loves to collect as many shovels as it can fit on its back and will even start conflicts with Sandygast because of it. It gets incredibly upset if anyone tries to take any of its shovels.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tunnels beneath beach sands, feasting on discarded food left by tourists. Its networks of tunnels stretch for miles, connecting to nests of others in its colony.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are infamous among nearly every beachgoer for how they will casually lay claim to beach towels as their beds. They do not seem to have ill intent, but rather, they seem to be very self-indulgent and require exorbitant amounts of rest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live on the shores of beaches just beneath the water, partially collapsing their bodies to hide from humans. To eat, they fully form their bodies and roll out to sea, draining the soul of anything that passes through their mouths.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its core and legs are made of hardened sand. The sand that makes up its shell falls off frequently, so it has to place more.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: This Pokémon resembles a cement mixer. It will become very happy if someone pours more sand or gravel into its bowl.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME need water to maintain their form but are viscerally scared of accidentally putting out the fire on their tail. This contradictory dilemma makes taking care of them difficult for most Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sand-like coating of POKENAME's body is actually composed of trillions of tiny seeds. The shovel-shaped flower atop its head is extremely sensitive and will cause it to wince if touched.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is made up of trillions of seeds that resemble sand. During rainstorms these seeds may begin to sprout, prompting it to discard them from its body.
author: .izik

entry: It floats slowly above beaches, drifting just beneath the clouds. If you feel grains of sand sprinkling down from above on a calm day, it may be a POKENAME watching you from the sky.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME loves to collect small seashells to decorate its body. It has a fondness for children and can often be seen playing with them on the beach.
author: mistymagius

entry: If POKENAME spot trash left behind on the beach, they will rush over to scoop it up and fling it away. Unfortunately, they often have trouble standing up to Trainers they catch littering, waiting for them to leave before cleaning up for them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are found waddling near the coast, collecting pieces of glass and plastic. They will display their favorite pieces on their bodies.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Travelers are warned never to follow POKENAME, despite the cutesy faces and shapes it forms with its sand and shovel. Its floating bubble and playful shapes may evoke trust, but those who heed its guide vanish, lost forever among shifting dunes.
author: silentscript89

entry: In children's ghost stories, POKENAME is said to place its skull over a traveler's face like a mask, seizing control and leading them to drift endlessly through the desert until they collapse and disappear amidst the shifting sands.
author: silentscript89

entry: POKENAME treasures its shovel greatly, for it holds nostalgic memories long passed. It loves to build pyramids.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME hunt in swarms by burrowing beneath the beaches they inhabit. When prey is near, they unleash a burst of electricity to paralyze their target before slowly dragging them below the sand together.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient island songs speak of POKENAME being used by glassblowers. Its sand is so pure it was highly prized for crafting fine glass.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers scorched sands where wildfires once passed through. Its feathers are coated in fine ash, and its ember-like shovel glows faintly at night, attracting insect Pokémon it then buries for later.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME silently sit along shorelines, shoveling and sifting the sand in search of pearls or seaglass. If a POKENAME spots a Trainer helping to pick up trash from the beach, it will offer them a trinket from its haul as thanks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: This fusion is very selfish and territorial in nature. It will destroy sand castles and use them to make itself appear larger than it actually is.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME is not comfortable unless its body is large enough to press firmly against the sides of its bucket-like shell. If its body erodes too much, it will work together with other POKENAME to intimidate others to assist in gathering its sand.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Instead of a shovel, POKENAME adorns a small patch of beachgrass. The plant's roots run through its body like veins and give it enough stability to move around on two feet.
author: aggrave

entry: The sand filling POKENAME's bag-like body smells of rotting fruit and fertilizer. It scatters this around its beach to keep tourists away.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is often found on polluted beaches as a result of the pollution. It attacks anybody who tries to get rid of it.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: This Pokémon is often found on polluted beaches. It attacks those who try to clean up the pollution by smacking them with its shovel.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: This Pokémon is often found on polluted beaches. It attacks anybody who tries to clean up the pollution.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: When humans throw litter on the beach, POKENAME crawls out of their hiding spot to eat them, digging into the sand afterwards. Caretakers of beaches catch many POKENAME in order to keep their beaches clean and pollution-free.
author: rycronicgames

entry: POKENAME prefers to inhabit beaches where many drowning victims have perished. The more who have drowned at a beach, the more POKENAME seem to congregate there.
author: .izik

entry: While it appears to be made of sand, POKENAME's body is actually composed of countless tiny seeds. This allows it to slip into small cracks and burrow for sleep at night.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME listens intently to the voices it hears during the day. At night, it takes to the skies and mimics those voices to lure unsuspecting people toward the shoreline.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is drawn to the laughter of children playing at the beach. It steals toys from other people and delivers them to the children, desperately trying to join in their fun.
author: .izik

entry: It would be a convenient flotation device for struggling swimmers, but POKENAME doesn't like to share its buoy. It's coated in a toxic wax that poisons those who grab on.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME hides in the sand of a sunny beach, collecting light. POKENAME will lunge out of the sand to attack anyone that tries to steal its shovels.
author: mikk09

entry: The sand making up POKENAME's body is actually composed of tiny bits of rust. Once it knocks out prey, it covers them in this substance to leech their vitality.
author: .izik

entry: The shovel atop POKENAME's head conceals a venomous stinger. A single sting causes extreme awareness but full-body paralysis lasting up to 20 minutes.
author: .izik

entry: It loves to build structures out of sand, spending hours a day shoveling and sculpting sand. However, if its shovel is taken, it loses the motivation to do anything.
author: mistymagius

entry: This Pokémon's body leaks a grainy, silt-like sludge wherever it walks. It blends in with worn scarecrows or forgotten beach trash, remaining motionless until nightfall, when it quietly pursues wanderers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is extremely protective of its shovel and grows depressed if it ever loses one. It will replace a lost shovel with a twig or leaf until a proper one can be found.
author: .izik

entry: The shovel-like mushrooms on POKENAME's back are filled with tiny pores that release corrosive spores. These spores incapacitate beachgoers, making them easy prey to drag under the sand.
author: .izik

entry: An in-between of Sandygast and Palossand. It's very fond of the shovel on its head.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: POKENAME rises up from the  beach sands during the evening, patrolling its territory. It compacts and hardens the sand comprising its head when it needs to attack, making its headbutt stronger.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME shade their bodies with the power of music, as their songs solidify sand using sound vibrations. Their mastery over vibrations allows them to bend sand to their will, often creating captive audiences stuck in quicksand.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The sand upon its back is held together by mycelia structures, which sometimes can be seen through small holes in the sand. It displays an odd attachment to the shovel caught in its mycelia and will become agitated if the shovel is touched.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME swarm the beaches at night, scouring the sand for discarded food. At the first sign of light, they burrow instantly, vanishing beneath the surface.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon's body is made of sandstone, and it is theorized that its head, which is made of loose sand, is gradually compacted into the body below to make it grow. It lives on beaches that provide both the water and sand required for this purpose.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME is commonly found curled up near the edges of playgrounds and parks. Despite its tired appearance, POKENAME bounces slightly when happy and often emits a whistling sound that rises and falls like giggling.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME live near the beach because it needs to keep its body at least somewhat moist otherwise its sandy body will start to fall apart. It loves to play with children, often helping them build their sandcastles.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a sand guardian, guardian of the sandy beaches it calls home.  If it sees a child being bullied or senses a sand-castle get kicked over, it will move to protect the victim, shielding them with its whole body.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME travels across shorelines, gathering mud and sand onto its body. Its headbutts sometimes shake sand loose, which it replenishes after each fight, ensuring its defense is always reinforced.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being fiercely protective of its shovel, it longs to play with children in the sand, and will cry if left alone for too long. These tears turn into shells that shine brighter than normal ones, and are treasured by collectors.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME spends days searching beaches for Tropical Shells, which it proudly wears on its body. When a child approaches, it will give them one Tropical Shell but will never offer that child another.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME spends days searching beaches for Tropical Shells, which it proudly wears on its body. When a child approaches, it will give them one Tropical Shell but will never offer that child another.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME extrude silk through soft beach sand, cloaking their vulnerable bodies in a gritty cloak that makes them an unpleasant meal. They gather discarded sand shovels to enhance this effect, keeping them safe from bird-type Pokémon along the shore.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME make their home on tourist beaches, nearly invisible as they dig their way under the sand. They have a fondness for children's beach toys and will emerge underneath buckets and spades, wearing them as hats for their own amusement.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Hiding in the beach sand, POKENAME waits for a person to approach with food. When close, POKENAME will squawk and flap its sandy wings, startling its target and causing it to drop what it is holding and flee; children are its main target.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Should one of POKENAME's shovels fall off and get lost, it replaces it temporarily with a stick or leaf. This does not seem to affect its flying ability as a new shovel grows directly from the sand on its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cheers on its teammates by hurling bundles of swirling sand into the air before shocking them with electricity. This produces bright sparkles that shimmer in the light.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME likes to collect objects it finds in the sand, using its plastic bill to dig for them. It is very sentimental about its treasures, and it will be saddened if someone takes them.
author: mistymagius

entry: Should one hear hissing at the beach, it is imperative to flee to a grassy area immediately. This usually indicates a pack of POKENAME circling its prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lays flat against the shoreline, blending with the sand. If a human steps too close, it grabs their legs and drags them swiftly into the sea while using its psychic powers keep their mouth shut.
author: .izik

entry: Said to be a Growlithe that became lost on the beach, POKENAME will approach young children to play, digging holes or helping to build sandcastles. However, most children who play with a POKENAME are never seen again.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoys playing in the sand, using its shovel and psychic powers to construct different shapes and patterns. Once it's done playing, it will let the sand rest in piles to act as blankets for a nap.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME telekinetically controls the sand around it, making it shift and swirl to entrap its opponents. With enough focus, it can make giant sinkholes up to a kilometre in size.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME can be found sculpting works of art out of sand, using their sandy muscles to lift sand into the right place. Their artistry is only as good as their strength, as lifting clumps of wet sand can be difficult for weaker POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME buries itself in the sand, waiting for small Pokémon to fall into its mouth. Luckily, because of its lack of teeth, people are unlikely to be injured by accidentally stepping on one.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME burrow along the ocean floor, hiding until the right moment to ensnare aquatic Pokémon with their tentacles. Their sandy heads and seaweed tentacles are well adapted for the ocean depths.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This creature dwells on sandy beaches, usually among others of its kind. It is often seen running by the sea at sunset. Legends say POKENAME was born from the frustration of children who tripped on the sand while playing.
author: fiordaliso
