entry: POKENAME gather in groups to drum against the scale on their forehead to communicate their feelings to one another, their allies, and their Trainer. It is said that if they sense the cheerfulness of others, their drumming may sound like wind chimes.
author: am3lie._.137

entry: The scale on POKENAME's head emits a strong magnetic field. It sometimes sticks to metal objects without realizing it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels draconic energy through the scale on its head. This energy lets it trap opponents in swirling Sand Tombs.
author: .izik

entry: The petals and leaves on the flower of POKENAME are dense and edged in a metallic compound. They serve a dual function of protection and warning, being dense enough to block attacks whilst also making a loud clanging noise against one another.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME communicate with percussive melodies made by smacking their scales with their claws. The sounds of a large group of POKENAME can echo for miles.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME meet in the dead of night to butt heads against each other to establish hierarchy between rivals. The clang of their metal skulls creates a warbling wail that many confuse for the haunted cries of evil spirits.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be spotted flying around the tall mountains they call home. If a threat approaches, they rotate the golden scales around their core to blind those that get too close.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Ancient carvings depict armies using POKENAME in battle. They would fight alongside their human allies, trained to protect them at all costs, making them revered warriors in history.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's beating wings create a sound that is quite high in pitch. It is disorienting and distracting to many, creating openings it can use to divebomb and headbutt targets with the hard scale on its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's scale is sought after in some regions for its shininess and color. To evade poachers, it casts illusions to make others believe they've discovered shed scales, while in actuality they've only gathered up useless garbage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slowly waves the scale on its tail to release a calming aura that subdues its prey. Once they are off guard, it strikes with a powerful Double-Edge.
author: .izik

entry: It has many different patterns of clashing its scales together that each express different emotions. It strikes with precision using the sharp scales upon its feelers, be it in battle or against prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the tip of its tail to communicate by clashing it against its other scales. When the scales on its back or its cap-like head are struck, toxic spores are scattered.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's head scale absorbs solar heat throughout the day. When it overheats, warm air is vented through the fur on its neck.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever a POKENAME hears a Trainer make a wish, it will curiously tap the scale on its head to determine if they are pure of heart. If the scale produces a clear note, the heart on a POKENAME's chest will glow and the wish will be granted.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: After clamping onto its target with its powerful jaws, POKENAME will attempt to strike again with a sudden Dragon Claw. Due to the size of its maw, these follow-up attacks often miss.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have slow reaction times and cannot move very fast. However, with the help of a Quick Claw given to them by their parents or Trainer, they can find moments of opportunity to strike.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Pokémon has a bold yet affectionate personality. It is particularly prideful over the appearance of its tail and the sturdy scale atop its head and will incorporate both of them in battle, while vigorously grooming them afterwards.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are masters of offense and defense, striking with the tips of their horns and blocking with their large scales. When a POKENAME's scale is struck, it creates a loud ringing that resonates with the POKENAME's tusks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When POKENAME slams into foes with its tusks, the scale on its head rings with a pleasant chime. The sound often startles enemies more than the impact.
author: .izik

entry: The large, heart-shaped scale on a POKENAME's stomach helps to protect its core from any external harm. Energy from the scales being struck allow POKENAME to build up heat before unleashing powerful fiery breaths.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A mischievous Pokémon that lives deep in mountainous tunnels. It will beat against the scale on its head to create a startling and eerie sound to frighten passerby.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME dances, its head scale produces a melodic tone. The rhythm grows more complex with each elegant step.
author: .izik

entry: While resting, POKENAME's scales gently wobble, releasing a scent like Pink Apricorns. The aroma lures small Pokémon, which it ambushes.
author: .izik

entry: While flying, POKENAME's golden ears glow if it notices falling debris. It can instantly use Protect to shield itself from harm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME glide with their wings held low to stop their scales from rustling. When they lift their wings to dive or flap their wings to take off, their scales will ring out in lovely tones that signal their travels to their flocks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When POKENAME is peacefully asleep, its sticky head scale gives off a faint scent of Oran Berries. This scent attracts Bug Pokémon seeking nectar.
author: .izik

entry: When hugged, POKENAME's fluffy body causes the scale on its head to glow bright pink. This can mean happiness-or a warning of coming violence.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has a bold yet affectionate personality. It is particularly prideful of its tail and the sturdy scale atop its head and will incorporate both of them in battle, but will groom them vigorously afterwards.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME dwell underground beneath Kommo-o dens, hiding within the discarded scales for protection. If they're spotted, they will rapidly clang their scales to alert the Kommo-o of a threat to its territory.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME tunnels through mountain walls with sharp scales. It uses them to slice through dense rock while digging paths for its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are difficult to please. They show their displeasure by swishing their tail back and forth, clanging the weight at the end of their tail against their back and making a loud noise.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sends out headache-inducing pulses from the scale on its head. The waves grow stronger when it's confused or panicked.
author: .izik

entry: Small scales shed from POKENAME's wings as it glides cause it to cast a sparkling trail whenever it takes flight. The growths on its neck, despite looking like hard scales, are soft, sweet fruits highly sought in tropical regions.
author: sk372

entry: While it looks scrawny, POKENAME can deliver powerful attacks with its scales. It communicates by smacking those scales together.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME like to playfully headbutt each other. This doesn't hurt the POKENAME since their heads are protected by a giant scale, but they do make a loud sound similar to cymbals when their scales collide.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME swings a vine tipped with a hardened scale to defend its jungle canopy nest. Its strikes can shatter stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the sharp scale on its head to cut off small bits of marble from deposits in caves. It then eats the shavings to strengthen its stony body, improving its durability for battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's scales grow warm when it nears ore deposits. If it senses tin ore, it digs tirelessly to uncover its favorite treat, sometimes over a mile deep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are easily distracted by shiny objects, including their own scales. They often try to catch the tips of their own tails, only to get confused when they move their tails and the shiny objects disappear.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When its scale glows orange, POKENAME is ready to unleash a powerful Bubble Beam. This attack is strong enough to leave dents in stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slam their tail against their scaly bulb to produce clanging noises. Even heavy sleepers awaken when POKENAME creates this noise.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME, when in danger, flings the hardened scale at the end of its tail at aggressors. A new one grows back in only a few minutes, so it's never without a defense mechanism for long.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers abandoned Dragon-type eggs and guards them fiercely. It uses its sharp scales to fend off any predator that comes too close.
author: .izik

entry: When enraged, POKENAME lifts its radiant scale skyward to call down violent thunderstorms. Legends say the sound of thunder is its war cry echoing from above.
author: .izik

entry: The scale atop its head cannot easily be severed. Although other parts of its body are more tender and vulnerable, it nonetheless bravely fights with its whole body in combat.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has a massive yellow scale on its forehead, a symbol of strength. Locals believe the scale holds mysterious powers, with some claiming it can control the flow of battle, granting immense strength to its wielder.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME sheds its scales on a regular basis. It's been found that grinding them into a powder and adding them to its milk gives it a distinctly sweet, honey-like aftertaste.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slumbers in dark caves as it prepares to evolve. When danger nears, the scale on its head vibrates rapidly to warn it of predators.
author: .izik

entry: The scales on POKENAME's head emit a chilling sound when they clink. The air around it cools noticeably, and lost scales regrow in a day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are clad in tough, sharp scales that they keep honed by digging through terrain regularly. At least every week they shed their scales while digging, which will regrow in half a week's time.
author: infinex21

entry: After heavy rainfall, POKENAME's metallic body gleams like polished steel. It attacks with devastating force using its bladed, claw-like arms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nibbles on the scale on its tail in order to keep it sharp, making a reverberating clacking noise as it chews. If the scale falls off from excessive chewing, it grows back within a few days.
author: sk372

entry: If its scales fall off, POKENAME hoards them in a carefully organized den. Jewelers prize these gleaming pieces for crafting rare necklaces.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rarely forms groups with its kind due to its haughty nature, preferring to seek out rivals to train alongside. Its durable feathers are often lost due in its intense battles, leading to them being scavenged for crafting cooking utensils.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The scale atop POKENAME's head is sharper than a razor and can cleave slate. The strange metal armor it wears is lighter than it looks.
author: .izik

entry: When entering a battle, POKENAME will crack its whip-like ribbons on the ground to intimidate its opponent. Its Trainers instead say this is a pre-fighting ritual to ensure victory, though this is unproven.
author: teatedtiten

entry: Ancient civilizations used POKENAME to guide cave explorers. Its immense strength made it ideal for clearing rubble from tight passageways.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's twin head scales are hypersensitive to sound and heat. They twitch violently when a creature approaches, alerting it to strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's heads headbutt each other, psyching itself up for battle with the resonating clang it creates. This also serves to strengthen the scales on its skulls, making it more effective in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME toughens itself up by butting heads with others of its kind. It strikes with enough force to break its scales, which grow back tougher, strengthening both rivals as they spar.
author: sk372

entry: The shiny scales covering POKENAME's body are incredibly dense. During rockslides, it curls into a ball to protect itself from falling debris.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME strikes a foe, scales may chip from its tusks. These regrow easily if it maintains a rich, protein-heavy diet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits powerful sonic waves from the golden scale on its head. It does this to knock out prey before it feeds, using sound to disable its victims in a flash.
author: .izik

entry: The loose scale atop POKENAME's head chimes softly in the wind. It dances with its slime-covered body to the sound in secret but freezes instantly if it notices anyone watching.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the sharp scale on its tail to guard its domain. It patrols cave entrances regularly to keep out any unwelcome visitors.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's golden scales remain burningly hot even after they're shed. These aggressive Pokémon inhabit caves in volcanic regions, making the land dangerous to traverse.
author: .realthree

entry: The shiny scale on POKENAME's head reflects light, blinding Pokémon that try to prey on it from above. Many divers seek out these shed scales, as they fetch high prices.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME wield a small bone-like rod clad in myriad scales that it has shed throughout its life. When it waves this rod, the scales attached to it clatter together in a fascinatingly tranquil melody.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses vibrations of the metal scales on its head to create a buzzing noise to scare off invaders to its precious flower gardens. Its bright and regal appearance made it popular with royalty in many ancient civilizations.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will abandon their young shortly after they are able to walk, relying on the rigid scales that the pups possess to protect them. Young POKENAME are often sought out by new Trainers, as they make excellent partners for learning Trainers.
author: vic1312

entry: Its many scales emit loud, metallic noises as it flies through the sky, often loud enough to be mistaken for thunder. Any shed scales are often used in decorations meant to ward off terrible storms.
author: infinex21

entry: In battle, POKENAME unleashes its metal leaves in a fierce whirlwind with its Petal Dance attack. The petals clang against each other, producing a deafening cacophony of sound that disorients both POKENAME and its foes.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Once they've proven themselves worthy, POKENAME is unfailingly loyal to its friends. It forms psychic plates of armor similar to its own scales and places it on its allies in battle for their protection.
author: sk372

entry: This noble Pokémon is known to shield others in times of crisis. Electricity stored within POKENAME's clangorous scales rub together while it runs, creating the sound of a rumbling thunderstorm.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: The sharp metal sound of POKENAME ringing its scales to intimidate others can be heard all around its mountainous home. Victorious rivals will tear scales off of their opponent to wear as symbolic trophies of their victory.
author: sk372

entry: Its many scales each emit shrill sounds when they are clashed together. These scales are kept razor sharp by it digging through terrain, favoring harder terrains to keep them at their sharpest.
author: infinex21

entry: Once POKENAME grabs a foe, it flies high into the air and rapidly rattles its scales together to send critical shock waves down through their body. Its elongated wing scales make for great fan blades since they catch and churn air very easily.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's armored scales protect it from sharp-clawed predators while it watches over its young. If it thinks a threat will be good training for the young, it will herd a weak predator to them by clanking its armor and tusks in a threatening manner.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Adventurers in the jungle can find rigid scales stuck into tree trunks. This is POKENAME marking its territory, and if the adventurer finds the Pokémon responsible, they may not live to tell the tale.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: When agitated, the scales on its back tremble and clash together, emitting shrill noises that unnerve most others. It can clash its red claws together to emit focused sounds, both for communication and for battle.
author: infinex21

entry: Some say that their discarded scales carry an echo of their psychic abilities, and are seen as a good luck charm. A POKENAME giving their Trainer one of its shed scales is considered to be a vow of protection, thus establishing an unbreakable bond.
author: thatlittletwerp

entry: POKENAME uses its steel scythes to brutally injure foes before utterly destroying them with a swing from its axe tail. Being covered in scales gives it the confidence of near-invincibility, so it hunts down dangerous foes like Salamence without fear.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are very prideful about their golden scales and take great care to keep them clean and polished. If anyone were to dirty their scales, they will fly into a tantrum that can last for many hours.
author: infinex21

entry: The many scales of a POKENAME's wings will clatter and jingle as it soars through the sky. Many treasure these golden scales, but their only hope of obtaining them is when they are shed for this Pokémon will not even allow its Trainer to pluck them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME imitates travelers it encounters in the mountains by mimicking their appearance. It does this to confuse them into unintentionally walking off cliffsides.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's scales glow a pastel pink shortly before it unleashes a powerful Moonblast. In direct moonlight, the force magnifies, allowing it to destroy boulders with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Supposedly, these Pokémon clash their rigid scales together to calm themselves before battle, though this has yet to be proven. Some old tales claim that holding one of their shed scales calms a person's nerves and soothes their heart.
author: infinex21

entry: With POKENAME's ribbons being made entirely of metallic scales, any prey it wraps them around will have their bones crushed. The clattering of its scales creates auras that instantly instill fear and hopelessness in its foes' bodies.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME live deep within volcanoes, their hefty scale armour protecting them from the intense heat of the lava they bathe in. Their powerful claws allow them to tear through even the hardest of stone.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Legends claim that the arrival of POKENAME is a sign of a peaceful future. Ancient traditions say that ringing ritual bells will resonate with the clanging of POKENAME's scales and summon it in times of need.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's golden plate-scales are made of a highly conductive alloy, a key part of their battle strategy. In combat, they shed their scales to lay traps before launching electric bolts from their tail that bounce between their dropped scales.
author: deadshields

entry: Embers scatter from between the cracks of its scales to startle foes and prey alike. While its foe is stunned, it will latch onto them with its talons and emit a deafening screech up close to knock them unconscious.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have tried turning their shed scales into wings and flying with them. While these attempts always fail, the steel-hard scales protect them from taking any damage from the fall.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are able to curl themselves up into a wheel to roll at incredible speeds. They rattle their scales and swing their tails to steer, creating a cacophony of clanging as they travel.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's scales are a perfect defense from many fearsome Pokémon who share its habitat. In ancient times, an imitation of this headdress was worn by war chiefs who went to battle.
author: atlas3339098

entry: If inactive for too long, POKENAME grows so many scales on its body that they start to get in its way and block its vision. It sheds these scales by viciously and aggressively chucking them at foes to deal heavy blunt damage to them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME shakes its front arms vigorously so the metallic scales it boasts clash together loudly. On hot summer days, the sound of hordes of POKENAME doing this can be heard up to a mile away.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is found living in herds on the peaks of frigid mountains. When dangerous Pokémon approach, they rattle their scales loudly to scare them off.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's smaller scales are often shed at the end of every winter cycle as it returns to northern lands. These scales somehow remain cold for years even after being shed, which led to many people using them to help preserve their foods.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's scales are harder than diamonds, and in ancient times they were believed to have been used as tribal shields and armor, serving as a valuable trading resource.
author: icecreeper720

entry: POKENAME's armor consists of dense metallic scales that cover most of its body. When threatened, it will repeatedly strike its own scales with its claws, creating an uproar of gonging noises that will deafen anyone exposed to it for too long.
author: fireblade141

entry: It requires diligent care to maintain the shininess of POKENAME's scales, showing off the dedication of its Trainer. Depending on its mood, the clanging of its scales can make a beautiful melody or horrible cacophony.
author: sara886a

entry: The gilded appearance of POKENAME's shell caused it to once be hunted as material for ostentatious armor pieces. Such an act was quickly outlawed, after a royal's prized POKENAME was poached, which sparked a furious manhunt.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be heard long before they arrive at a location, as their scales resonate as they dig underground. Despite being quite noisy themselves, they do not like the loud sounds that can be found in urban environments.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Scales and chunks made of pure, luxurious gold grow on the body of POKENAME. Kings and queens of long ago would wear jewelry forged from this gold, symbolizing their absolute wealth and power.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME communicates with others via scraping its tail along the scales of its neck and wings. Shed scales can be boiled in water, softening and distilling over time to create a sweet-tasting soup.
author: sk372

entry: A children's play dating back over a thousand years describes a villainous POKENAME as "The Savage Cymbal", likely due to the calamitous noise that plays as POKENAME flies overhead. It can suddenly become covered in fire and let loose a Flare Blitz.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME wields a spiky, scale-covered club for both defense and offense. When someone collides into it, the club makes a jingle that makes POKENAME smile: that is when POKENAME is at its happiest.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are very prideful and joyful creatures, leading battles and festivals with the same passion. They will clang their scales together in different rhythms to signal the start of war or celebration.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A children's play dating back over a thousand years describes a villainous POKENAME as "The Savage Cymbal", likely due to the calamitous noise that plays as POKENAME flies overhead. It can suddenly become covered in fire and let loose a Flare Blitz.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A children's play dating back over a thousand years describes a villainous POKENAME as "The Savage Cymbal", likely due to the calamitous noise that plays as POKENAME flies overhead. It can suddenly become covered in fire and let loose a Flare Blitz.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As POKENAME runs, the clanging of its scales sounds like firecrackers. If an active volcano is about to erupt, it will run past nearby people and Pokémon to warn them.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME is very timid, scattering small clouds of scales with its wings before fleeing. Due to it hating any threat of interaction with other Pokémon, it only goes out pollinating in the early morning.
author: mistymagius

entry: While being extremely timid, POKENAME will lash out with its wickedly sharp, scything claws if threatened too greatly. However, it usually zips away at the slightest sign of danger.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME stands tall and imposing, flexing its muscular arms and razor-sharp horns to intimidate attackers. It's extremely skittish, however, running away as fast as it can if its intimidation tactic fails.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME can be found living in even the dirtiest bodies of water. It has a cowardly nature, and swims away in fear at incredible speeds when startled.
author: mepp.

entry: A solid shell and decent leaping ability lets POKENAME handily escape predation. If it accidentally lands on a living creature when leaping, it delivers poison from the tips of its claws in a panic before jumping away once more.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is incredibly anxious, especially about possibly injuring people or Pokémon with its stingers. After it stabs something, it cries profusely and flies off to its hive to take a sadness nap.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Very easily frightened, POKENAME tends not to come out of its nest inside trees unless it's certain no other creatures are about. If something approaches while it's out, it flaps up irritating fluff from its wings to help it escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flocks at night to Persim Berry trees, feeding under cover of dark. If anything unfamiliar approaches, it hoots sharply to send the group scattering.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a paranoid and twitchy species, always looking to and fro for potential dangers. If something manages to frighten it, it has an equal chance of fleeing or fainting outright.
author: sk372

entry: A scavenging pest, POKENAME will root through trash to find food. It has incredible hearing; its paranoia will cause it to flee the scene at even the slightest unpredictable sound.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME lives in Nanab Berry trees, picking fruit with its long tail. If spotted, it panics and swings away through the canopy to escape.
author: .izik

entry: Backyard gardens attract swarms of POKENAME, who devour weeds and invasive sprouts. The flash of a motion-activated light sends them screeching in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides among the trees, scuttling quickly out from holes in the bark to feed on berries and occasionally small bugs. It only flies to retreat when it's startled, and does so at ludicrously high speed.
author: sk372

entry: By night, POKENAME pecks mold off building walls with surprising care. Sudden light from streetlamps causes it to shriek and take flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rests for long periods under the sun to dry and harden the plates of its sturdy shell, protecting the seed underneath. It is very shy, so if it hears a loud noise, it immediately seeks refuge in nearby bushes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME feeds on tree sap in silence, venturing out only when it believes it's alone. At the faintest sign of movement, it vanishes into the underbrush.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in holes it makes in the ground by using its unusually shaped tail as a makeshift shovel. If the hole is investigated or tampered with, it springs out and strikes with a venomous bite.
author: evilgammon

entry: No matter how hard it trains, POKENAME is completely pathetic in battle. However, due to its quick reaction time, it can avoid most encounters before a fight breaks out.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME puts on a fearsome display, but the moment it's outmatched, it folds in on itself and flees in disgrace. Despite its armour and poisoned spikes, it's known as a hopeless coward in the wild.
author: eiskitsune

entry: Paradoxically, this Pokémon will have either the extremely cowardly disposition of Wimpod or the nerves of steel of Bidoof. Researchers are currently conducting a survey to see which personality is more prevalent in POKENAME.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is skittish and evasive, and will sprint to hide at the sight of danger. Its shell is still soft and developing, leaving it defenseless against a powerful blow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are cowardly Pokémon, prone to hiding themselves away at the first signs of danger. Their size makes this difficult, and spooked POKENAME in the wild can be found with just their head and neck wedged under boulders or in holes in the ground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their feelers to retrieve food and to keep their dens clean, to a degree that most would call meticulous. They are weak-willed and flee at the first sign of trouble, even if it means abandoning their dens.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hide from any Pokémon that appears more confident than they are. If they are unable to remain hidden, they distort space itself to expedite their retreat, folding the ground in front of them to shorten the distance they need to run.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: An unusually shy Pokémon, POKENAME avoids Trainers and prefers to live in abandoned areas. It can be found in derelict buildings and tends to congregate on rooftops. When disturbed, it uses its light body to float away on the wind.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hides in its den most of the time, only leaving once it's sure there is no one there. It is surprisingly quick, able to bury itself underneath the sand within a blink of an eye.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body is made of surprisingly sturdy shells, which metallurgists speculate may be a since-extinct metal from an ancient past. It prefers to skitter away from any perceived aggression, much to its very slow-moving body's detriment.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME lives in small clusters, its lightweight carapace allowing it to float with the tide. It hides in shallow tidepools, only feeding on seaweed that washes in due to its fear of predators.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME feeds on small bits of electricity siphoned from household appliances. If spotted in the act of feeding it retreats immediately, spreading small bursts of sparks as it runs.
author: sk372

entry: Thanks to its tough and spiked shell, POKENAME fearlessly chases down and harasses anything that enters its field of view. Despite its bravado, the moment its quarry fights back, it gives a shrill cry and spins into the soil to escape.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lives in shallow creeks and marshes, burying itself underneath the mud. When startled, it releases a weak shock before swiftly swimming away.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hides away on abandoned beaches, feeding on any scraps it can find. It's quite the hardy Pokémon, able to survive on very little food for weeks on end.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME adores dancing and practices this skill in hidden dens, whether in the underbrush of forests or in less traversed spots in buildings. If it sees anyone watching it dance, it screams and scampers off in embarrassment.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's cowardice leads it to flee at the slightest disturbance. It sprays a powder with an enticing aroma to distract predators as it runs away, but the pleasantness of the smell has led to people scaring POKENAME to harvest the scent.
author: pjporwoll

entry: If confronted in the wild, POKENAME will panic and flap its wings rapidly, spreading cloud-like fluff everywhere. If it panics too much, it may lose all the fluff on its wings in its haste to escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can typically be seen scouring beaches for food. While normally too cowardly to fight, this Pokémon will become enraged when the shell on its head is touched.
author: spider26

entry: POKENAME is incredibly timid and will shed its mushrooms as a defense mechanism. While the mushrooms are not toxic, anything that eats them will be overcome with fear and paranoia.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME scour over a single shoreline a night in search of cold food, such as recently washed-up seaweed. If caught off guard by wild Pokémon that look threatening, they will immediately flee, leaving behind a frigid gust of wind in their wake.
author: andromeda102037

entry: POKENAME use their four legs to quickly flee from battles. Their feelers can sense anything from over five miles away, so it is very rare to see one in the wild.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME are incredibly skittish, fleeing at the slightest noise or movement. They feed on tiny microorganisms in the water, filtering the water through their bristle-like hairs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lives in the mud underneath rivers, lakes, and the like. Extremely timid, it rarely pops up for long to survey its surroundings, disappearing back below the minute it spies another creature nearby.
author: sk372

entry: Spending most of its time in its resilient shell, POKENAME lives in constant fear of the world around it. It only leaves its shell when fishing for food or if a Trainer befriends and gets it to feel safe.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME hides in coral reefs, patiently waiting for prey to swim directly into it mouth. However, it is incredibly timid and will frantically swim away if it encounters any Pokémon bigger than it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME loves its leek weapon but the moment it feels in danger, it shrieks, flings the leek at the perceived threat, and flies away. Once it calms down, it regrets throwing the leek, so it sneaks back to find it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME gathers in quiet clusters along dark shorelines to feed. Even the snapping of a twig can send the entire group scrambling into the sea foam.
author: .izik

entry: When its hard exoskeleton is hit, POKENAME secretes poisonous spores as a defense. Due to its calm nature, it tries to avoid unnecessary fighting.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has a special reflex in each of its legs that helps it escape danger. This reflex activates whenever it gets hurt, prompting it to escape by curling into a ball and rolling away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's large claws are as hard as stone, capable of crushing minerals and tunneling through bedrock. Its tough exoskeleton protects it from intense temperatures underground.
author: mepp.

entry: A school of POKENAME was recently sighted near Sayda Island. When cruise ships approach, they spar playfully with each other to impress watching tourists.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shoots bubbles from its claws to stun predators. If overwhelmed, it releases clouds of dark ink before fleeing at high speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slashes at fish Pokémon to test its claws. After victory, the horn on its head glows pink in satisfaction for several hours.
author: .izik

entry: This apex predator is very rarely defeated due to the armor plating on most of its body. POKENAME is a huge threat to ships since it mistakes them for prey and punches through their hulls with its mighty jaws.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME is an extremely gentle and intelligent creature that was once used to explore remote islands in frozen waters. The older it grows, the thicker and tougher the scales on its back become.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME notices a mouse cursor drifting across a webpage, it attacks it as though it were prey by use of its Aqua Jet. This behavior sharpens its reactions and combat reflexes.
author: .izik

entry: In prehistoric times, POKENAME would challenge Kabutops to brutal duels. These fights were used to test its strength and enforce its dominance over its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are known to lead small packs of Pokémon, even having some they trust more than others. They seem to deeply hate Crantwo and regularly have intense rivalries with them.
author: bigoljax

entry: The red tips of POKENAME's antennae glow while hunting. Its claw-like fins can tear through thick hulls without resistance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly strong flier. It hunts by soaring high above the ocean's surface before diving onto any prey they see. Its slick feathers and high strength allow it to carry away even dolphin-sized prey.
author: fireblade141

entry: In swamp battles, POKENAME splashes opponents with mud. The one who stays cleanest is declared the winner and gains local territory rights.
author: .izik

entry: By eating waste and swamp plants, POKENAME develops potent venom. The most toxic individual becomes leader of its school through chemical strength.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME locks eyes with another of its kind, it fights until one is unconscious. Its ability to Recover lets it survive blows that would fell most others.
author: .izik

entry: When disagreements arise, POKENAME duels by firing high-pressure water jets. The victor decides the group's next move without question.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME is a formidable opponent due to its powerful tentacles, it prefers to hunker down in a hiding spot or jet away in a cloud of ink at the first sign of danger. These actions are rarely necessary as its armor means it has few predators.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is an ambush predator packing numerous ways to kill any unfortunate creature it decides to hunt, such as crushing prey in its armored coils, slashing them with its claws, and poisoning them with its bite.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME are overwhelmingly powerful; with one mighty swing, they can cleave through seawater. With shells as tough as diamond, only an equally powerful Pokémon can damage them. They are known to inhabit sunken ships, often battling Dhelmise.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME is nocturnal and is known for attacking boats by rising up from below the ocean's surface and secretly dragging people overboard one by one. What it does with its victims is unknown.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME's claws have the ability to crush boulders with ease. They live in mud, bursting out when something gets close to their nests. During storms, POKENAME will move their eggs to shipwrecks; this behavior is being further studied by researchers.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME's mediation allows it to heighten its abilities to sense aura. In battle, it remains completely motionless until attacked, at which point it will counterattack perfectly and deal a devastating strike in return with those massive claws.
author: fireblade141

entry: This ferocious Pokémon inhabits surface-level caves. It is fiercely territorial, and anyone who intrudes upon its home will find themselves pounced upon and shredded to bits by every one of its six claws.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME is a predator that makes its home in coral reefs. Though it is slow, its powerful jaws can crush rock, so it seeks out prey that can't run away from it: shelled Pokémon, which those massive jaws have no problem breaking open.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME drifts in ocean currents while clustered. If two touch for long periods, they clash in sudden, fierce bursts of energy to establish dominance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are opportunistic scavengers that crawl along the seafloor looking for sunken carcasses to eat. If they come across any Pokémon smaller than them, they will lash out with surprising speed and pierce their prey upon their claw-tipped tentacles.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME's dense outer shell can deflect most projectiles with ease. It swims through winding bayous, lurking beneath the surface as it stalks unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rams heads with rivals to test strength. Afterward, it strikes with claws sharp enough to cleave tungsten in a single clean swipe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME barrels along the seafloor with its iron-plated head. It devours coral reefs and crushes prey hidden among the debris.
author: .izik

entry: This gentle giant is a filter feeder that will only attack when provoked. Its natural bulk, combined with its armor plating, makes it a sluggish swimmer, but difficult for predators to take down.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME's back serves as a tide pool providing an ideal place for Wimpod to take shelter. This Pokémon is typically docile, but if its smaller friends are threatened, it will become very aggressive.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME carves up debris to collect metal shavings, displaying them as dominance trophies. Other POKENAME will challenge it to claim the scraps.
author: .izik

entry: It battles strategically yet ferociously, working in tandem with Goliard to defeat foes. Both its claws and blades can slice through rubber and stone as if it were paper.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is an exceptional fighter, its extremely durable exoskeleton serving as armor that shields it from enemy attacks. At the tip of its tail, it bears a pair of sharp claws that it charges with electricity to deliver its most devastating blows.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is an exceptional fighter, its extremely durable exoskeleton serving as armor that shields it from enemy attacks. At the tip of its tail, it bears a pair of sharp claws that it charges with electricity to deliver its most devastating blows.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is far more gentle than it seems, protecting its environment by planting several trees or helping Bug Pokémon make their nests. This doesn't extend to its hunting behavior, mercilessly skewering and devouring any Steel Pokémon it sees.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME's rapid wingbeat produces a mild toxin that weakens the muscles of those afflicted. This makes others unlikely to be able to attack it, which suits POKENAME's meek and pacifistic nature just fine.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's wings have become massive arms that no longer allow for flight, which frustrates it. It takes out its frustration by slamming those arms down upon any that bother it, skewering them upon its sharp claws.
author: fireblade141

entry: The platings of its arms are strong enough to endure and deflect most attacks. It shields others, especially those who are weak, and allows them to flee while it holds off any threats.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can both skitter on six legs and hop about on two. Its large ears can move surprisingly fast for their size and are strong enough to pulverize concrete. It uses pirouettes to enhance the ears' smashing power further with centripetal force.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME's arms account for most of its bodyweight. They can break through diamond, but drag on the ground during flight.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME lives in remote caves, where it can be found with its solid wings folded up around its body to protect it while it meditates. In battle, the curvature of the wings allows it to divert its own flames, spewing fire everywhere.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME rolls across the ocean's surface, slicing prey with its claws. Its spinning attacks can destroy entire coral reefs in seconds.
author: .izik

entry: The shell in POKENAME's body bursts upon evolution, splitting into various spikes and allowing its inner tendrils to spread out. It uses these spikes as a way to cut open rocks and gemstones and bring them back to its nest to hoard and eat.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME's shell armor can withstand especially powerful blows and even piercing strikes that barely graze through its inner body. Dissatisfied with just gathering inert rocks and gemstones, it also hunts Rock and Steel-type Pokémon.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME walk on the ocean floor, trying to find any type of bivalve to consume. It can rip them apart with their teeth almost instantly.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Schools of POKENAME spar in lakes, creating frothing water. The most defeated member is exiled from the group and forced to live alone in distant waters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME traverses through the desert, using its glasses to protect its eyes from sand. It likes to collect anything it considers "cool".
author: dodoowner_

entry: Since ancient times, POKENAME has been an apex predator and combatant thanks to its thick armor plates and flame-resistant gel mane. It prefers to quietly spend time with its young but fiercely battles anything it deems a threat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: In contrast to their intimidating looks, POKENAME are surprisingly peaceful. They spend most of their days meditating under the seas. If disturbed, POKENAME will tear their foes to shreds with their powerful jaws.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME bites and races others of its kind to determine leadership. Once a leader is chosen, it can only be challenged again one year later.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon that lives deep underwater can spend years motionless, waiting for a worthy opponent to challenge it. By pressing its head to the chest and drawing its limbs inside the body, POKENAME can turn itself into an armored fast-rolling sphere.
author: milchik

entry: Despite its large size and immense power, POKENAME tends to avoid battling. It prefers to take a quick jab at threats and then retreat to store power.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME attacks ship anchors similar in size, mistaking them for rivals. Once it realizes they don't retaliate, it quickly loses interest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tough carapace oozes a thick purple toxin when struck. Its scent alone is enough to ward off most predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives deep within underwater caves, where its shell can withstand even submarine collisions. It secretes faint toxins into the water to ward off intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fiercely claims bayous as its territory, biting any who dare approach. It regularly challenges others of its kind to brutal duels to prove its dominance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a ruthless hunter, spearing any creature smaller than it in an instant. It'll even attack other Golisopod fusions.
author: ohok3441

entry: This Pokémon has a much more streamlined body than a regular Golisopod, allowing it to swim at surprising speed. Its tough carapace makes it hard to damage, while its sharp, hooked claws can pry apart armor off its prey.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME's armor is protective but less dense, allowing for easy movement. This Pokémon is an active hunter; its coloration gives it camouflage, allowing it to get in close and then pounce to deal a fatal slash with its large, sharp arms.
author: fireblade141

entry: Although this Pokémon usually conserves its strength and meditates, rarely disturbed due to its armor-like shell, it is able to shatter a tree with a single punch. It will accept any challenge it deems worthy, equally utilizing strength and skill.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME swims placidly in its waters, drifting away from conflict if spotted. If pushed into combat however, it's no slouch; its many arms have enough strength to hurl a Blastoise with ease.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is popular amongst Alolan Trainers both because of its rapid reaction time and its personable nature. Some larger POKENAME are able to be ridden by young Trainers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is capable of both flying through the air and swimming through the seas. Dominant individuals of the species will compete fiercely over resources, bashing their armored heads together to see who's tougher.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME is a master stir-fry chef. Using all its arms at once, it can prepare an excellent stir fry at a speed unattainable to human chefs.
author: hophoppip

entry: To choose a leader, POKENAME wrap their tentacles and sting each other repeatedly. The last to fall unconscious is crowned the victor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a highly territorial scavenger by nature, combing the seafloor and beaches for detritus to consume. If attacked, it will become highly aggressive; if it emerges from this conflict the victor, it is happy to consume its felled foe.
author: fireblade141

entry: The leaves sprouting from its back are both tough and edible, so chefs harvest its leaves after a battle to cook with. A meal similar to cabbage soup is made out of its leaves, which it begrudgingly accepts if it also gets a treat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They shoot a smooth silk from their heads, which is adorned with a crown of clovers. They scuttle across the forest floor to look for clover leaves to add to their crown.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It leaves behind bulbs that harmlessly fall away from the main body, which taste like steamed broccoli. As such, herbivores follow it around wherever it goes to secure a bite to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The 'bone' POKENAME holds is actually a dried-out flower stem. Direct exposure to sunlight makes the weapon more durable.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME feed on bone marrow for nutrients that they cannot gain through merely absorbing sunlight. As they grow older, their leaves and vines begin to subsume their outer skulls.
author: infinex21

entry: A dense net of pink vines covers its body. It is said that no one knows its true appearance, but many are convinced that it must be beautiful. As POKENAME is very shy, it hides in the bushes and comes out at night in search of food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live among one another, sunbathing and resting in expansive groups; if one flees for whatever reason, so will the rest of the group. POKENAME migrate to faraway lands during the night at the end of the warm season.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME curls up to nap, it looks exactly like a blossoming flower. This mimicry attracts Bug-type Pokémon, annoying POKENAME into attacking.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can be found lying in the sun on warm days. Some collectors claim that this enhances its evolution; however, a practiced caretaker will recognize that POKENAME is purring. It simply loves the warm feeling.
author: drakon1c

entry: POKENAME remains still in this state, allowing pollinators to sip nectar from its leaves. The pollen supplements its photosynthesis to accelerate its growth towards evolution.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME use their nimble teeth to gnaw at berries. After they are satiated, they release a pleasant aroma appreciated by many; therefore, they are found at households who wish for their scent.
author: blaizegamer

entry: POKENAME only eat a certain type of seaweed which contains all the micronutrients they need, the rest they absorb passively through seawater. If they are forced to eat something else, the tip of their head begins to smell unpleasant.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It flies around at night, then lands during the day and extends roots from its talons to absorb nutrients from the soil. If disturbed, it will screech loudly before taking flight again.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drift through flower fields while carefully slicing the stems of flowers about to decay. They weave these flowers into chains and offer them to weary travelers, granting them a soothing aroma to help restore their energy.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME have small leafy wings that grow back whenever they get damaged. This is quite handy because Bug-type Pokémon love to chew on their wings. Hanging from tree branches prevents Bug-type Pokémon from reaching their wings while they rest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It bites chunks off of bushes to fuel the fire in its belly. The leaves it eats determine the color of its flames, ranging from bright orange to eerie green.
author: .izik

entry: During the day, POKENAME rests, storing energy to prepare for the night. After dark, it wafts a sweet aroma to lure in unsuspecting sparring partners. Each punch spreads the scent, attracting more foes.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME uses the power of their incantations to help withered gardens grow beautifully. For this reason, they are commonly partnered with Pokémon Rangers to help restore natural environments that were destroyed from fierce battles.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME spends its days attempting to master wielding its blade like hands by mimicking master swordsmen. It is very clumsy however and often fails its complex manoeuvres.
author: evilgammon

entry: It holds onto a stick and monitors the area around its dam during a nightly vigil. If a high-pitched wail is heard nearby, it either means an intruder is nearby, or one of its cohorts has lost its stick.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME swings its bladelike leaf, it releases a soothing aroma that smells faintly of Chesto Berries. This scent often masks its presence in battle.
author: .izik

entry: Used by Chefs on Balm Mushroom hunts in the woods, POKENAME communicates with the roots of plants. When it senses fungi nearby, it expertly harvests them with steely slashes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Its leaves and feelers emit a pleasant, soothing aroma when it is awake. It will often sit in clearings or fields and bask in the sunlight with its grassy feelers spread out.
author: infinex21

entry: It replaces portions of its disguise with trash and leaves, blending in with decayed plant matter. It chews on fallen leaves to gain energy but avoids sunlight as much as possible.
author: .izik

entry: During the day, it releases a sweet scent mixed with toxic spores. The only creatures who enjoy being around it are the Bug-Poison type Pokémon. At night, it might search for clearer waters so its spores can become more toxic.
author: torterraguy26

entry: POKENAME floats silently over rice fields. When hungry, it descends to steal clumps of vegetation before drifting away.
author: .izik

entry: The top of a POKENAME's head has a sweet and floral aroma, causing many to seek out their spores for use in beauty products. However, these spores are also highly toxic on their own, so caution is advised if one plans on extracting them.
author: porterofgames

entry: POKENAME floats with the wind on sunny days, spreading its leaves to gather as much sunlight as possible. Groups of POKENAME will link their limbs together and form rotating rings as they float about.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's leaf-like wings flap rapidly as it navigates wooded areas at night. It feasts on the juice of overripe fruit, leaving small pin-sized holes where it bites- a subtle sign of its nocturnal feeding habits.
author: .izik

entry: It burrows in leaves in forested areas, shooting electric webs at anything that disturbs its rest. The webs also help conduct sunlight to its leafy body, enhancing its energy.
author: .izik

entry: By pretending to be asleep while soaking up sunlight and luring Pokémon in with a sweet scent, POKENAME gets bug Pokémon to gather around them. Once the bug Pokémon are close, they rely on echolocation to bite and drain blood from their meal.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Swarms of POKENAME can be seen trimming small bushes and trees with their sharp mandibles to make them look neat and tidy. They are commonly kept by gardening enthusiasts.
author: mistymagius

entry: During the day, it sleeps and soaks up light. If POKENAME doesn't absorb enough energy, it spends the night hunting any small Pokémon it can find.
author: larky_

entry: It focuses on photosynthesizing energy during the day, while it roams around at night. To prevent it from being targeted, it buries itself partially in the ground while it rests. If a Pokémon eats the leaves atop its head, they will find them bitter.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME hides in compost bins inside greenhouses. It feeds on biodegradable scraps, preferring fruit rinds and rotting leaves over soil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME inhabits stumps in deep forests. One can always tell the stump it sleeps inside- small pink flowers grow from the wood in anything it enters, adding a touch of life to the decaying timber.
author: .izik

entry: When asleep, POKENAME's seaweed intertwines with kelp beds. Though it resembles an anchor, tides can carry it away if not securely latched.
author: .izik

entry: It chops leaves off of nearby trees and chews them into a fine pulp to cultivate small fungal patches. These fungi act as a personal food storage for POKENAME, growing stronger as they absorb sunlight.
author: .izik

entry: The increased leaf growth allows POKENAME to make greater use of the sun's rays. Its leaves grow sharper and more closely resemble the insectoid Pokémon attracted to its sweet scent. It may look aggressive, but this is simply its appearance.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME shakes Stun Spore attacks from its body that smell faintly of Jaboca Berries. The scent lingers long after it flees the scene.
author: .izik

entry: When grumpy, POKENAME releases a foul rotten pumpkin scent. It chases intruders with its stubby legs to drive them out of its territory.
author: .izik

entry: A wild POKENAME finds its habitat amongst the base of volcanoes where it indulges in the nourishing fertilization of volcanic ash.
author: skelesoul

entry: POKENAME hide in meadows, blending in with wild flowers and tall grass. When a glade of POKENAME are startled they will abruptly withdraw their bodies into the grass, hiding away and pretending to be newly growing plants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME darts from between leafy parts of the ocean floor, eating seaweed when it can. When frightened, it spreads the green parts of its body outward to make itself appear twice as big.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME make their homes in hedgerows and bushes, using the shelter of the plants to safely stay above ground and soak in the sun. They are easily overlooked Pokémon, as from a distance they appear to be simply freshly growing plants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rely on sunlight for most of their energy and nutrients. From the tops of their heads, they exude pleasant aromas, causing them to be targeted by many predators; for this reason, they often scale trees and hide upon the branches.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lurk in bushes waiting for prey to come by, their colouration and leaves helping them blend in and remain hidden. When they aren't hunting they love to lounge in the sun, their leaves soaking in the warm sunlight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME gathers up a small collection of coins to carry with it beneath the morning sunlight. While it can photosynthesize normally, it seems happier when basking near light reflected off of shiny coins.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hide within flower beds, playfully wagging their tail and jumping out to surprise small children and Pokémon that pass by. They give off a refreshing floral aroma when they're excited, making them popular with florists.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's swimming muscles are very weak, so it wraps its tail around seaweed to avoid being swept away by strong currents. Due to their vibrant appearance, many aquarists love including POKENAME in their personal aquariums.
author: mepp.

entry: Where fields of flowers bloom, POKENAME is a caretaker. Its bright colors allow it to blend in with the blooms, attracting pollinators like Butterfree. If pests attack the plants, it quickly drives them away using its scythe like a boomerang.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's movements resemble a fluid dance, its petals shifting into vibrant colors like a disco light show. While dancing, it delivers precise kicks in time with its movements before its opponents can react.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME charges solar energy into its horn by remaining at the surface of bodies of water. Once sufficient energy has been generated, it releases laser blades to cut down branches so that it can eat the leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feeds on fresh flowers to keep the colours of its beautiful, vivid wings bright and lustrous. It is notoriously difficult to raise, as it requires very specific temperature and humidity conditions to thrive.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME work alongside stylists and tailors to create clothes for Trainers. They cut and weave fabric to create beautiful dresses that get featured in magazines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is very particular about its appearance and spends much of its time grooming itself. It uses a scythe made out of the same material as the flower upon its head.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Gardeners wishing to grow orchid-like Pokémon are drawn to POKENAME since it has a hardy constitution and a mild personality. It eats decomposing plants, so cooking scraps will not hamper its health.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is a popular transport Pokémon in cooler climates, used as a ferry for taking children across bodies of water. Its gentle nature makes it a valued member of the community.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a popular transport Pokémon in cooler climates, used as a ferry for taking children across bodies of water. Its gentle nature makes it a valued member of the community.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME conserves its energy by floating on the surface of rivers, while fishing with its tail.  After a successful catch, it makes its way energetically to its school and shares its meal.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME generates a stronger static with its plant quills. It uses this to protect flower beds and gardens it has grown to like.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: The petals on POKENAME's wings are extremely sharp, allowing it to cause minor cuts to opponents and eventually overwhelm them. It needs a wide variety of food including meat and vegetables to maintain its vibrant coloration.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's beautiful appearance belies an aggressive and vicious disposition. It snags prey in its claws before stinging them with a paralytic toxin, allowing it to leisurely feed on its catch.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are commonly spotted in gardens, especially in the springtime, using their calming fragrance to draw in pests. It is a sign of a good gardener if a POKENAME frequents their abode.
author: dualblades1147

entry: POKENAME spends a good amount of time preening the leafy mane on the back of its neck. If angered, the mane will ignite, which unfortunately means it will have to repeat the meticulous grooming process once it calms down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME glides silently at night, flapping its broad leaf-like wings. It seeks wild oregano patches, its favorite food, to munch on until dawn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home among chives and fragrant herbs. It spins near-invisible silk throughout the area to keep pests away, ensuring its garden thrives.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is amphibious and lives in marshlands. It buries itself in mud and keeps its mouth open under the water, waiting for prey to accidentally swim in. The bright colors of its petals and docile demeanor make it popular with younger Trainers.
author: opossiblymage

entry: With a diet consisting of Geodude, POKENAME has adapted to underground living. It uses its bright coloration to reel in unwary prey, then breaks through their hide with claws that can split diamonds.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME hunts in tropical jungles, fiercely attacking its prey with its sharp scythes. While it's too big to convincingly camouflage, it emits a sweet scent from its body that often makes its prey let their guard down.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME inhabits vivid, tropical reefs where it hunts by blasting sun-infused laser beams from its snout. It is an expensive pet to care for since it requires diligent attention to the water chemistry and lighting, lest it lose its color and temper.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME curls its leafy limbs inward and rolls across hills at terrifying speed. Its top velocity exceeds that of most buses, making it dangerous to encounter.
author: .izik

entry: A roar from POKENAME causes dozens of razor-sharp petals to release from its mane and slice everything in its vicinity. With its Contrary ability, each time it tries to expend its sheer power, it instead increases it dramatically.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are usually found bathing in the sun amongst the treetops. They are very cheeky Pokémon, and will often poke each other with their cactus spines.
author: cinna0175

entry: These Pokémon love sunbathing to gather energy, which they convert into electricity and release through their vine-like tails. Some people keep POKENAME as pets, using them as living sun batteries.
author: milchik

entry: Despite its charming appearance, POKENAME will strike with startling speed and ferocity. It favors trees bearing Pecha Berries, as they allow easier camouflage.
author: josh707

entry: Its dress-like petals are highly delicate; because of this, POKENAME moves with calculated grace and elegance. Its vivid coloration is an indicator of how well its Trainer takes care of it.
author: lasercraft32

entry: Nicknamed Nature's Florist, POKENAME dances in dying meadows, attracting pollinators. Using unknown powers, violets sprout under its feet as more Pokémon are brought to the area, making beautiful natural arrangements.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Its dress-like petals are highly delicate; because of this, POKENAME moves with calculated grace and elegance. Its vivid coloration is an indicator of how well its Trainer takes care of it.
author: lasercraft32

entry: This Pokémon is naturally docile and will care for those who get lost in the woods. However, it will become extremely fierce when its friends are threatened. The color of its petals is indicative of its emotional state.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME is slow-moving and docile. It absorbs sunlight with its skin and concentrates the power into the glowing halo above its head. When threatened, it will fire energy beams from that halo relentlessly.
author: fireblade141

entry: The leaf-frills on POKENAME's back emit a pleasant Sweet Scent to lure others close. It then stabs them with a venomous thorn that causes severe paralysis.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's sickle-shaped petals swiftly take down prey and enemies. Its vivid shed scales are collected and used as decorative inlay.
author: mepp.

entry: Once its male packmates leave to hunt, it is left in charge of monitoring the nest, especially the baby Pokémon in its care. If any of the babies try to leave the nest during this time, it guides the baby back using its soft petals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By raising all eight of their claws up to their heads, POKENAME will disguise themselves as flowers while releasing a pleasant aroma. These arms will swiftly grab anyone looking to pollinate them, consuming them whole.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is ruthless in combat, brutally slashing its opponents with its scythes, which are imbued with dark energy. Fearful of its own power, it isolates itself and will only attack as a last resort.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's pink leafy body is completely hollow inside. It will eat herbs like oregano and mint to fuel its eerie powers, which it uses to spook and disorient its foes.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being capable of leveling cities, POKENAME prefer to lounge in the sun, grooming themselves. While they can be extremely picky about how they're taken care of, a capable Trainer can quickly earn a POKENAME's trust.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME sprout vibrant, xenobiotic flora on their backs. While lying motionless, POKENAME hide in their carapace and disguise themselves as unusual gardens to remain protected. Those kind to young juveniles usually enjoy a new friend for life.
author: jadey.1557

entry: By basking in the sun, POKENAME's leafy body absorbs solar energy. This strengthens the toxin produced by the thorn on its head.
author: .izik

entry: Its claws are very poisonous, and POKENAME uses them to weaken intruders who invade its territory. During the mating season, its body gives off a very intense floral scent.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's leafy blades are delicate, but turn hard-as-steel mere seconds before attacking. During winter, POKENAME groups frequently fight over food to maintain their vivid coloration, with paler-colored POKENAME being much more vicious.
author: chibitales

entry: The vine-like tail of POKENAME channels intense electricity. Even a casual touch can knock out a full-grown human due to the voltage it stores.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME perform photosynthesis to get most of their nutrients, which helps to keep their colors vibrant. They can harness sunlight into their feelers to perform Solar Blade attacks with terrifying precision.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is said to come from a world with much more vibrantly-colored plant life than ours. A touch from its colored shadow will bring even a wilted, dead flower to full bloom again.
author: sk372

entry: Although its speed and deafening cry would be enough to disorient its foes, it whips up a storm of flower petals to confuse them even further. When there is an opportunity to strike, it brings down its sickles with enough power to tear through steel.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME floats above junkyards under moonlight. It plants seeds in discarded plush toys, somehow animating them to defend its territory from intruders.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME use their large claws to defend their young as well as to trim the greenery around their forest homes to prevent overgrowth. Their electric webs help them to conduct sunlight into their bodies, which help to maintain their vivid colors.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's petal-like flames are said to dance and captivate the hearts of those that see them. This, alongside its vibrant colors and sweet scent, makes it a popular Pokémon for outdoor festivities.
author: astral_rain

entry: Despite how imposing and violent it looks, POKENAME is usually very calm and possesses a high intelligence in battles. It tricks foes with calming scents to position itself over them before unleashing onslaughts of petals to obliterate them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME cover their forest burrows with leaves mixed and held together with electric webbing. Their front claws help them to trim and maintain the leafy bodies of themselves and others of their kind.
author: infinex21

entry: It can glide short distances between trees and go through them when it fears crashing. Its eyes are not made of gems, but being told so hurts its feelings.
author: epping_forest

entry: Though this Pokémon is fierce and destructive, it only feasts on Grass-type Pokémon. Its petals permeate the air with scents of the Pokémon it ingests.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME's body is sensitive, so it keeps itself huddled beneath a cloak made of its large petals to shield it from the elements. Specimens living in warm, temperate areas possess a much more vibrantly-colored cloak.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME may appear glamorous from afar, but it hides a fierce temper. Using razor‑sharp petals and sweet scents to draw others in, it unleashes ultrasonic waves to disorient its foes.
author: lesbian_garlicbread

entry: POKENAME is known for its enchanting beauty, especially when its flowerbuds ripple gently in the wind. Perfumes made from these flowers are popular amongst young women.
author: mepp.

entry: A POKENAME can never reach its full potential in the wild, as its fur gets overgrown and it cannot perform certain moves without damaging itself. A dedicated and loving Trainer can groom it and train it to be able to perform devastating attacks.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are quite sticky Pokémon, bendable and often perceived as meek for their vividly soft nature. Despite this, they are commonly seen among collectors as perfect assistants and models for the arts.
author: th3randomguy

entry: POKENAME makes its home on tropical islands with lots of sun and plant life, both of which help keep its coloration vibrant. It tends to those people who are weakened and collapsed near its home, but hides when they recover due to shyness.
author: sk372

entry: Though it appears to be a peaceful Bug-type mimic, POKENAME is deceptively powerful. When a predator like Fearow gets too close, it retaliates with a bone-shattering punch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends so much time grooming that Trainers mistake inactivity for weakness. It surprises its opponents with quick, confusing movements, taking down opponents elegantly.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME stalks forest paths at night in search of prey like Metapod. When it finds them, it strikes with razor-sharp leaves, slicing cleanly through their shells.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME sings and dances, the colors of its petals grow more brilliant and colorful. It performs a powerful Solar Blade as the finisher for its dancing performances.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME attracts lots of Pokémon due to its glamorous dancing and singing. Once enough Bug-type Pokémon have gathered around it, its graceful movements turn violent as it slashes them with its razor-sharp arms and legs.
author: soup1900

entry: The petals armoring POKENAME are hard as steel. It shakes its petals while defending its territory, unnerving its opponents by mimicking the sounds of bug Pokémon.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME has compounds on the surfaces of its armor that allow it to photosynthesize, but it cannot survive on sunlight alone, so it will slice open trees to drink the sap. POKENAME is naturally passive, only attacking if provoked.
author: fireblade141

entry: It is said that female POKENAME continue to gain wings and arms after mating with a male POKENAME. Oddly, the male POKENAME are not seen after this process.
author: weirdmageddonprepper_93813

entry: POKENAME are known to infest forests and siphon nutrients from local flora for the sake of their own health and growth. They will turn on their own kind if any attain brighter colors, which is a sign of having overfed.
author: infinex21

entry: These Pokémon hunt in packs of five, coordinating their movements with precision. They finish off their prey by throwing razor-sharp floral shurikens.
author: apieli

entry: The fighting style used by POKENAME has been mistaken by many as a form of dance, but their elegant demeanor is deceiving; their sickle-shaped arms are capable of splitting thick metal plates in two.
author: blaizegamer

entry: POKENAME's sweet scent and vibrant coloring attract many bugs towards it, expecting a tasty meal. The sticky strings coating its body capture those insects, to be sucked up inside POKENAME and consumed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in berry bushes for protection and a steady food source, rarely leaving its home since birth. As a result, scientists are still debating what its lower half looks like.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME's tusks are actually composed of extremely thick leaves. During the summer months, they leak a cold nectar with a sweet scent.
author: .izik

entry: It basks in sunlight for hours to gather raw solar energy with its mane. This energy is either used for photosynthesis or in battle by allowing POKENAME to dash forward in a high-speed energy-cloaked charge attack.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME enjoy lazing about and can often be found taking a nap under the sun. They are easily started and will quickly teleport away if frightened.
author: cinna0175

entry: POKENAME can be found lounging in trees, enjoying the sunlight on their sculpted muscles. Due to the amount of effort needed to keep these Pokémon in top shape, a vibrant POKENAME is a symbol of its Trainer's dedication to its health.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: In peaceful forests, people may find POKENAME frolicking around at dawn. Because it is very shy, any unexpected sound will send the playful Pokémon scattering. They will not return for many days until they feel it is safe again.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME are made of stone, with a single precious gem on their backs. Many miners deep inside caverns mistake them for naturally occurring geodes, and as such, POKENAME are an endangered species due to overhunting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is easily distracted by a rolling Marble and will follow it endlessly. Scientists believe it is drawn to their bright colors and believe POKENAME have a strange sense of kinship with them.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Deep within dark caves, POKENAME tirelessly trains with its crystal club, striking rocks to hone its skills. When lonely, the gemstone-like mask on its face glows with a faint, sorrowful blue light.
author: .izik

entry: Beautiful crystals decorate POKENAME's body, growing on its skin. It uses its tongue to remove these crystals and fling them as weapons if threatened.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME can control rocks near its crystalline chrysalis, which haphazardly bursts out from the ground when it is threatened. It wobbles inside its cocoon, eagerly waiting for its metamorphosis.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dust was once marveled at as a miracle insulator, but recent research has found that this dust causes respiratory diseases, as it clogs up people's lungs. Many people have since begun checking their homes to remove this dangerous dust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It crashes into cave walls in order to knock loose any jewels in the wall or ceiling so it can eat. Its efforts regularly cause cave-ins, but it simply digs its way out of the rubble and looks for a new cave.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's crystalline portions, particularly its horn, are incredibly solid to the point of being nearly indestructible. It uses its horn as a drill to dig into stone depths and dig up crystals, its favorite meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grows gems from its body that occasionally fall off once they reach palm size. It collects these gems and gives them to those who befriend it, and they are often imbued with a minor power of healing.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's body is primarily made up of near-impenetrable crystals. It absorbs ambient light into the gem in its center, which fuels radiant beams of light it uses to defend itself from attackers.
author: sk372

entry: It's rumored that POKENAME was once a Magikarp before being encased in stone. Its splashing is now noticeably stiffer and more restrained.
author: coquelicot

entry: When multiple POKENAME gather, they create aurora-like light shows above them using lights from the crystals on their bodies. These rare and beautiful sights are considered one of the greatest natural wonders of the world.
author: sk372

entry: For a long time, POKENAME was hunted for the valuable crystals on its shell. Even today, it is protected by teams of Pokémon Rangers who guard it from poachers.
author: fiordaliso
