entry: POKENAME live in caves with pools of water. They often avoid completely underwater caves as they enjoy being around other Pokémon. They are not rare, but are difficult to find underwater due to their ability to turn invisible.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: Its crystals are said to provide hope and motivation to those experiencing loss. Advertisements for the crystals often use the slogan “POKENAME with your life”.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME condenses the data it consumes into solid gemstones after processing it. Scientists have studied this phenomenon for decades without uncovering its method.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME help jewelers set precious gems into rings and necklaces. Their short yet precise legs allow them to handle delicate jewelry with ease.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME work alongside lapidaries to carve gems into works of art. By carefully wielding their sharp claw blades, every gemstone they touch becomes a beautiful piece of jewelry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are apex predators that hunt flying Pokémon inside large caverns. The sharp crystals on their wings can harmlessly snap off and leave a sharp edge to slice their prey with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Living deep in frigid caves, POKENAME is rarely seen. This is due to it sealing the cave entrances with impenetrable walls of ice to protect slumbering Carbink.
author: mepp.

entry: It defends itself by firing beams of concentrated light from its crystalline horn. It sheds it old skin as it burrows through ground and rock, which is easily stripped away in the process.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives deep in underground lakes and is rarely seen. It is said to only appear to kind-hearted people, bathing them in a light from their crystalline horn to bless them with prosperity.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are clad in many jagged crystals oft considered to be more precious than diamonds. They store, and can concentrate and loose, energy inside of their crystals.
author: infinex21

entry: It bathes in light as it flies with its belly facing up. By angling its wings, it can concentrate and direct beams of light to fend off foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live in small colonies in waterlogged caverns far from civilization. The crystalline scales covering their bodies are harder than steel.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME flutters up to cave walls in search of precious gems, particularly sapphires and topaz. Once it locates a cluster, it chips away at the minerals with its sharp fangs, consuming them to strengthen its shimmering form.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in underground lakes, its crystal lure illuminating the cave walls with a dazzling blue light. The larger its lure, the more likely it is to find a mate.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's body twinkles under the night sky, reflecting starlight like a tiny moon. It is said that gazing into its crystals brings good fortune.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time standing stock still, quietly meditating. If its meditation leads to it catching a vision of the future, its crystal eyes flash a bright blue.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME moves around, electric static in its wool causes the gems around its neck to light up. Each year the gems fall off to be replaced by new ones, the discarded ones still retaining some stored electricity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME rarely moves unless disturbed. As it is only found in deep caverns, explorers often mistake it for a natural crystal formation.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME derives sustenance from eating rock and stone from their cavernous homes. Enamored by sparkling things, any gems found while eating are hoarded in its nest.
author: sk372

entry: It is rare to find a POKENAME above ground as they often live deep in flooded caves. There are online communities that post the whereabouts whenever one is spotted. This has allowed researchers to accurately study them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It charges the crystals that form its body under the moonlight to increase its physical strength and endurance. Gentle by nature, POKENAME spends its nights protecting weaker Pokémon from predators, appearing at the very moment they are in need.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are sturdy and protective, attacking people and Pokémon that wander too close to their burrows. POKENAME are known to ward off miners by momentarily blinding them by reflecting light with the gem on their backs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers fragments of minerals and tree bark to reinforce its rocky shell. Each one forms unique patterns, making no two POKENAME alike.
author: fertve

entry: The unstable crystal core inside POKENAME forced it to develop multiple thick layers of armor. These reinforced shells help contain its volatile energy while protecting itself and nearby allies.
author: fertve

entry: POKENAME burrows deep underground, where it forms tunnels lined with sparkling crystal formations. These tunnels sometimes lead to hidden veins of precious gems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feeds on rubies buried deep within the earth. The more it consumes, the stronger and harder its gem-covered body becomes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hoards pieces of beryl inside small rock crevices, polishing them over time. Some of its oldest stored gems have taken on a glassy, near-transparent sheen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feasts on citrine-rich minerals, causing its body to take on a golden shimmer and somehow produce a honey-like aroma. The more it consumes, the stronger and more durable its gemstone-like armor becomes.
author: .izik

entry: The shell on POKENAME's back is made of a core of hot rock, the outside cooling where it meets the air. When POKENAME is fed certain minerals, it can create beautiful crystalline structures that decorate its body.
author: beandrawsthings

entry: POKENAME are found in tunnels deep below the crust covered in glittering crystals. These crystals have become quite valuable in the tech sector for their heat resistance and clarity.
author: wiz0z

entry: In addition to its crystal fangs, POKENAME has a radula covered in microscopic crystal teeth inside its mouth. Studies show these teeth to be harder than any other natural material.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME burrows through icy caves in search of sapphires buried in the permafrost. When it eats a particularly pure gemstone, its body sparkles with a faint blue glow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has established a symbiotic relationship with Sableye. It provides food and hygiene for the Sableye. In exchange, the Sableye fiercely protect it from predators or other threats.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME's body is composed of dense mineral layers, making it incredibly durable. When rolling at high speeds, it leaves behind a faintly glowing dust trail.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME love to draw pictures along cave walls, using these drawings to mark their territories. Due to the microscopic crystals in their paint, these drawings will glisten in the light like glitter.
author: santon5512

entry: Though it can fire weak light beams from its crystals, POKENAME prefers close-quarters combat. It trains by striking stone walls repeatedly, forming cracks across its body as proof of its dedication.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often found resting atop smooth lapis lazuli deposits. Its crystalline body absorbs the stone's deep blue hues, making it appear as though it is sleeping on the night sky.
author: .izik

entry: The Marble atop its head and the egg it holds are made of the same crystalline material. Whenever it loses track of either gem, it will stop at nothing to find it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a habit of sneaking into abandoned mines to steal malachite deposits. It hoards the green stones deep within caves, forming a hidden trove.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nest in crystal caves, hoarding the shiniest stones. When happy, it scatters glowing shards across the sky like shooting stars.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME construct crystalline crowns along their heads to dazzle and stun opponents. The shadowy tails are actually the true bodies that control the rocky structures they've sculpted to protect them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's crystal-covered exterior disguises it among rock formations. It remains motionless for hours, tricking predators into believing it is an ordinary gemstone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live deep underground, they use their unique ability to magnetize gemstones to pull them in, presumably for later consumption. There is a theory that POKENAME search for the most precious ores for their queen that lives in a gemstone palace.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: A colony of POKENAME was recently discovered deep underground after a wild Onix had tunneled through the cavern it had been sleeping in. The crystals growing on its body are thought to be millions of years old.
author: mepp.

entry: While inhabiting a tree, POKENAME causes curious crystal growths to appear on the bark. The color of these crystals shifts based on its diet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hooked claws make them well-suited for scaling cave walls. The crystal on their head is razor-sharp, capable of slicing through steel.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are known to inhabit caves filled with abundant plant life. The crystals along their bodies glow faintly when they sense danger.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME digs deep tunnels in search of alexandrite, which gives its crystalline body a color-changing quality. Depending on the light, it may appear green or red immediately after eating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the gems on the tips of its claws to fire beams when it slashes at foes. POKENAME can be found deep underground in groups that are protecting the Diancie they see as their leader.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME train deep underground, finding solace in the high temperatures. Miners use POKENAME's kicks to dislodge large chunks of ore.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It raises its jewel-like tail to the air to absorb sunlight, which it can then release like beams in defense of itself. The white tuft around its neck absorbs water, allowing it to stay out of water for hours before it needs to resubmerge itself.
author: infinex21

entry: To defend itself, POKENAME will fire high-energy beams from the crystal fin on the top of its head. Its toughened hind legs are able to absorb the recoil to keep it steady as it fires.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME spits high-pressure muddy water to knock geodes loose from cave walls. It carries them back to its pond and hides them from others.
author: .izik

entry: Found living inside the deepest bowels of cave systems, POKENAME are typically shy and timid until they find another one of their own. When living communally, they flash lights from their jewels to warn others of approaching danger.
author: spookypookie.

entry: POKENAME lives communally underground and feeds on minerals. Before they go to bed, they perform intricate group dances that allow their jewels to light up the caverns they live in.
author: spookypookie.

entry: POKENAME is much rarer than its Gallade counterparts, typically only one will exist in a given underground community. It acts as a matriarch in its community, using its jewels to create dazzling light shows.
author: spookypookie.

entry: POKENAME's psychic powers let it manipulate the crystals on its body, as well as any in its immediate vicinity. It fires light beams from the jewels in order to protect its precious Trainer.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its quiet and reserved nature, POKENAME is a dangerous guardian of its underground community. It utilizes the jewels on its hands as both blunt weapons and tools to discharge powerful lasers.
author: spookypookie.

entry: As POKENAME age, the crystalline parts of their bodies take on differing colors. It is said that at the very climax of their lifespan, their crystals take on a rainbow-like hue that quickly fades if not harvested fast enough.
author: infinex21

entry: Its body consists of a swirling mass of crushed jewels. This makes POKENAME beautiful to look at, but dangerous to touch.
author: just__a__cat

entry: POKENAME are large and heavy, causing the rocks beneath them to tremble before their presence. POKENAME create burrows by using the gems on their backs to smash rocks into each other until they become a comfortable space to rest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME burrows into deep caverns in search of garnet-rich soil. It grinds the gemstones with powerful jaws before absorbing their mineral essence.
author: .izik

entry: The gemstones on a POKENAME's body are of great value, but break if forcibly taken from them. Once every hundred years, it will drop the gemstones in a molt-like fashion, to then grow new ones. They can become about a million years old.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME slams its hardened ears into clusters of crystals, breaking them apart with sheer force. It then greedily devours the fallen shards, using them to strengthen its gem-like body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a near-unbreakable shell after consuming large amounts of onyx. It often remains motionless for hours, blending in perfectly with dark cavern walls.
author: .izik

entry: In jazz venues where music from a saxophone or piano fills the air, POKENAME are known to dance to the music. Their dance reflects light from their shield-like faces, which illuminates a room with a soft glow.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The first POKENAME was discovered sleeping deep within a mine, surrounded entirely by large formations of precious minerals. When it became active, it consumed large portions of precious minerals and eventually fell asleep again.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's coarse manes are made of millions of rock fibers, which help keep them warm. They also use their manes to polish and sharpen their gemstone claws.
author: pinecone1987

entry: Before a potential cave-in becomes perceptible to other Pokémon and humans, the jewels on POKENAME's body have already begun glowing. Although the high-pitched screeching noises that come from them are eerie, POKENAME are usually docile.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The crystal orb on a POKENAME's face refracts light from all angles, allowing the POKENAME to scan its surroundings. When a POKENAME catches the glimpse of a sparkling gem, it will walk to pick it up no matter what stands in its way.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is known for its tendency to irrigate dying ecosystems with water stored in its mouth. This water seems to manifest from its crystalline teeth, but how the process occurs remains a mystery.
author: thistleblower

entry: POKENAME's skittish nature leads it to fire beams from the crystals around its chest at anything it sees as a threat. This sometimes includes other POKENAME, leading to barrages of beams fired from both parties.
author: chibitales

entry: The crystal leaves of POKENAME's plant become more sparkly based on the quality of the soil it eats. The species sadly has a poaching problem, hunted due to the jeweled sprout's rarity and appearance.
author: sk372

entry: The wool covering POKENAME's back consists of thin glass filaments. When threatened, POKENAME will propel large chunks of this substance, which is often embedded with hard gemstones, at targets.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME channel light energy through their crystalline tail, releasing it from a spot within the geode on their back. The light bounces through the many crystals within, focusing into a powerful laser that can carve through rock like butter.
author: vic1312

entry: It navigates dark caverns using colored beams of light emitted from the jewels on its head and tail. The hottest of these beams can melt through solid rock.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: The crystals on POKENAME's body grow red hot during combat. Even after breaking off they retain their heat for days.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fiery hot punches melt the stone around cavernous walls to loosen rubies. Consuming one can increase its flame strength by up to 50 percent for a full day.
author: .izik

entry: To survive on seawater, POKENAME possess specialized glands above their eyes that filter excess salt from their bloodstream. The excess sodium creates a salt buildup around their heads, which can be harvested by specialists.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME uses the sharp tips of its flippers to carve gems out of cavern walls so it can eat them. Some Trainers have taken to using its skills in artistry, carving sculptures out of stone and similar materials.
author: sk372

entry: Using their blades, POKENAME can drill deep into the ground to find caves. Their main diet consists of crystals and salt, though they occasionally come to the surface to drink river water.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's crystal nose gives it a special sense of smell allowing it to easily sniff out gems deep within cave walls and the ground. A unique magnetism allows it to extract these jewels so it can consume them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slashes through foes with its crystal body that never seems to get dull. It spends much of its time rubbing against rocks to polish its shiny surface.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live their entire lives in deep cave systems, mining for precious stones to decorate their bodies with. There are records of POKENAME-made mines the size of Nimbasa City, housing more than 200 POKENAME and other Pokémon.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Nidorino's horn, as hard as a diamond, has been replaced by a horn made of actual diamond. As such, it's slightly less hard, but its ability to fire energy beams makes up for it.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's diamond blades are nearly indestructible. Its precise fighting style and striking appearance make it a perfect contender in Toughness and Coolness Contests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME were said to be used by high-ranking officials during the Kalos War as guards. Their bodies are nearly as sharp as their blades are.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's body sparkles faintly after feasting on peridot deposits. It emits a soft, green light in the dark, allowing it to see through pitch-black tunnels.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME often lives alongside Carbink, and is fiercely protective of them, even those outside its own colony. Because of this, it's not uncommon to see a POKENAME charging at a Sableye or Gabite that tried attacking a nearby Carbink as a result.
author: slavman9057

entry: POKENAME creates illusions by distorting light around it with its crystals. These are only visual illusions, so POKENAME's rocky armor protects it when its opponent finally sees through its facade.
author: mistymagius

entry: It uses the crystalline tips of its feelers to refract light; it can concentrate light enough to create precise and powerful beams. Its body is as hard as diamond, save for the white fur around its neck.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's gemstone-like body glows softly under moonlight, resembling a twinkling star. Some believe Pokémon that sleep near it will experience peaceful dreams.
author: .izik

entry: In landfills, POKENAME's gems glow near discarded stuffed toys. It seeks out beloved ones to store in its cavernous, treasure-like den.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever the moon shines brightest in the sky, the gems across POKENAME's rocky body begin to glow. They seek out other POKENAME to dance under the moonlight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its crystals glimmer and glow with a light strong enough to cause burns. It's been known to lead miners astray in the dark caves it calls home.
author: hophoppip

entry: Jewelry outlets make POKENAME morph into rings that patrons desire so that there is a minimal risk of theft. Thieves who escape with a POKENAME need help from mall security before they lose a finger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME soar through the endless sky searching for Trainers who have shown exceptional love for their Pokémon. Their crystal wings vibrate and ring with joy whenever they locate a particularly kind Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers gems from nearby cave systems and stores them in makeshift treasure rooms within their tunnels. These tunnels are labyrinthine, filled with pitfalls and corridors that all look identical to the naked eye.
author: .izik

entry: Every strike against POKENAME hardens its body and its resolve to grow stronger. When aura is seen visibly and constantly emanating from the crystalline parts of its body, POKENAME is nearing evolution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME form their dens within caves and caverns rich with precious stones. They move very slowly when they are not hungry and may even fall asleep atop the precious stones they have dug out with their claws to gorge upon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is constantly active because it is brimming with energy and will quickly lash out at anything that disturbs it. Its claws are harder than diamond, allowing it to easily dig in search of minerals to consume.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives in subterranean lakes where it exposes its gem-covered belly above the water's surface to lure geovores like Sableye. When the tricked prey climb upon it, POKENAME submerges to feed on them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When a POKENAME gets lost, it will make small sparks that reflect against crystals embedded in the cave walls, creating a beacon to help its mother find it. Despite the packs being led by a male Caray, young POKENAME only listen to the females.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME charm many into becoming their audience with their diva-like personalities. The glowing gem atop their head draws the attention of many wild Pokémon, who stay to listen to their songs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in deep caves, eating the carbon-rich rock to help strengthen its crystalline armor. However, if the armor gets too thick, POKENAME starts to have difficulty moving around.
author: mistymagius

entry: Although still just as tough as its outer crystalline armor, the white minerals on POKENAME's body are actually not very hard. It isn't uncommon to see POKENAME with its chin resting on the cavern floor with other small Pokémon leaning on it, too.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The teeth of POKENAME's gears are smooth and shiny from constant rotation. They like to spin at high speeds because they love the ethereal, resonant ringing it makes.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME refract light through the crystals on their tails to create brilliant sparkling displays. If they angle their prisms correctly, they can focus the beams to create small sparks from the concentrated heat.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are graceful singers who amaze audiences with their crystal-clear voices. Their songs are said to move legendary Pokémon to tears, though this is likely hyperbole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME buries itself in the ground, beautiful crystal flowers grow around it. These flowers are rare and have been used in priceless sculptures.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: They live in tight-knit social groups near mineral- and nutrient-rich groundwater pools, rarely venturing far. Researchers track their populations and movements to study long-term climate trends.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME hunt in swarms, using their twinkling, bejewelled bodies to lure unsuspecting humans. Once someone gets too close, the group ensnares them with their stringy arms and drags them deep into their caves.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME inhabits underground lakes, the high mineral content of the water helping keep its gelatinous form resilient. It uses telekinesis to pull gems from the ground and walls to decorate its stone core with.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flock to abandoned mineshafts to eat shards of gems miners leave behind. The gem shards get absorbed into their bodies, which gives their wings a reflective shimmer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It spends hours at a time polishing and gazing at the diamond held in its tail. Some say that POKENAME are the reincarnated spirits of greedy fools.
author: hophoppip

entry: Flocks of POKENAME inhabit caves when they need to rest. Highly territorial, their gem-like eyes glow with rage should anyone enter while they rest, before firing bursts of embers at the intruder.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was recently discovered living deep inside volcanic caverns. It defends itself by shooting scorching beams from the crystalline parts of its body.
author: mepp.

entry: Its large wings sparkle in the light as though a sculptor wedged a thousand pieces of Beach Glass into them. The reality is not far off, as it takes pieces of glass or crystal and adds the pieces to its wings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has an insatiable appetite for topaz and will steal from even the most well-guarded gem caches. Its body glistens with golden flecks after a successful heist.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are common sights within large, mineral-rich caverns. They scuttle along any surface they can in search of minerals and gems to nibble upon. If they feel threatened, they will emit bright light from the jewel parts of their bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: The insides of POKENAME's bodies are like geodes, filled with thousands of crystals. Upon opening their mouths, they can fire powerful beams of light, blinding anyone they hit.
author: santon5512

entry: It performs energetic dances, waving its crystal-tipped arms about. Light is reflected through these crystal pom-poms to create a dazzling display.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's dance refracts light through its crystalline wings, casting hypnotic patterns that mesmerize both spirits and the living. Sudden movements shatter its rhythm, triggering a searing burst of prismatic energy to repel intruders.
author: vhscopyofmeangirls

entry: The trash POKENAME consumes slowly condenses within its body over time. Once per month, it coughs up a perfectly formed gemstone produced by this process.
author: .izik

entry: It scours city ruins to consume refuse, chemically refining the waste within its core to produce jagged crystals across its body. When threatened, the gems embedded in its body channel internal energy to discharge prismatic beams of light.
author: shivaequinox

entry: POKENAME lives in swarms in crystal-filled lakes, where the crystals build up POKENAME's teeth, making its bite incredibly powerful.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Many believe that if a child remains lost in a cave, they have a chance of becoming a POKENAME. It is said that if you look into its crystals, you can see ghostly faces.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME uses ultrasonic waves to locate sapphires hidden beneath layers of rock. It prefers only the deepest blue stones, as they strengthen its crystalline body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feasts on opal formations in glowing caves, leaving behind shimmering dust. When it flies, the dust reflects moonlight, making it appear like a moving constellation.
author: .izik

entry: The icy exterior of POKENAME is a hard, gem-like carapace. This allows it to endure high temperatures and arid conditions that most other Ice-type Pokémon would struggle with. Its core remains freezing cold regardless of environment.
author: jadey.1557

entry: Light refracted through POKENAME's gemstone petals causes discomfort and nausea for anyone hit by the beams. Despite this, especially devoted rock collectors still choose to suffer the ill effects.
author: pizzarcato

entry: Within POKENAME's hollow body are walls of crystals that store light energy. Attempts to remove any shards from POKENAME have led it to react with hostility.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's soft, gemstone-covered body is deceptively strong. It can lift boulders many times its size, storing them in underground caverns for unknown purposes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is incredibly useful in the mining industry, using its gemstones to light up dark caves and tunnels. However, it only likes its high-quality crystals and will throw away any that are not up to its standards.
author: mistymagius

entry: The gems within POKENAME's sand-like body glow when it senses prey nearby. It sneaks toward them while they sleep, freezing in place if spotted.
author: .izik

entry: Hundreds of millions of years ago, POKENAME resided in caves near the end of frozen tundras. Ancient people worshipped them, as their glistening frills in the night resembled auroras. It is believed that they are the distant ancestors of Megaswine.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: Deep, gem-lined caves are uncommonly host to POKENAME performances. As they harmonize together, they fire beams from their platforms to add to the spectacle. POKENAME are known to be skittish and will only perform for Trainers they trust.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME derive nutrients from the crystals and gems they dig up and eat. They can emit bright lights from the crystals on their backs to disorient enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME's crystal wings crack, the shattered fragments continue floating around it. Each fragment displays the exact moment it broke, even if that moment occurred decades ago.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME rapidly produces crystals upon shifting form. It shoots beams of light from the sun rays reflecting within its body.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME have smooth, crystalline scales that jingle whenever they move their body. The scale atop a POKENAME's head produces a resonant ring when struck.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Found in caverns containing precious gems, POKENAME uses the gems on its body to bedazzle its prey, before slashing the victim with its diamond-encrusted claws.
author: theredemerald

entry: The blue crystals on POKENAME's body emit a soft white glow as it drifts through caverns. When it sees gemstones are disturbed, its crystals blaze crimson before it attacks anyone nearby with Moonblast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a soft pelt, their eyes and antennae made of jewels. They use their fur to polish their eyes throughout their lives, their vision becoming more fine-tuned as they age.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME grows thick pieces of wood from its arms to excavate gems from cavern walls. Should it consume turquoise, nearby cave moss grows at an accelerated rate.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body, made up of dense stone and crystal, is nearly impenetrable to any sort of conventional attack. It resides deep in cavern areas, quietly meditating, though it leaps to the defense of smaller Pokémon it senses are in danger.
author: sk372

entry: The stick POKENAME wields is carefully and meticulously carved out of crystal. When creating fire with it, the flames on the stick turn a beautiful pale color and sparkle as they burn.
author: sk372

entry: Staring into the jewels adorning POKENAME's body induces a hypnotic state. POKENAME utilizes this effect to its benefit, disorienting predators and prey alike before it entraps them in a fiery vortex.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Residing in crystalline caves, POKENAME use their nimble form to navigate the twists and turns between massive crystal columns. Their foam scarf appears to be made of a soft material, but is truly formed from small crystal fibers.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME scavenges for gemstones, spending countless hours honing them into bladed weapons. Should anyone interrupt it, it will swiftly fling shards of crystal at the interloper.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME takes large amounts of coal wherever it's needed. It's able to run rather quickly for its weight, clocking in at 18mph.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME are coveted for the beauty of their crystalline wings. Their crystals glitter a myriad of colours when light is shone through them and are at their most beautiful under the light of the moon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is only ever seen floating around in the midnight hours deep within dark caverns. Its gems emit an eerie glow that terrifies travelers, looking like a malevolent grinning face looming from within the darkness.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fluffy pad is rough to the touch because of the thousands of tiny mineral bits stuck in it. Many yarn-spinning devices have been destroyed due to this fluff in the past, causing damage worth well into the thousands.
author: chibitales

entry: Though POKENAME can live to be millions of years old, it has a mischievous personality and likes to play tricks. One of its favorites is pretending to be a jeweled statue, then moving around when no one is looking.
author: torterrable

entry: Though it often looks like a statue, POKENAME bursts into dance when it hears festive music. The hollow parts of its gemstone body act as chimes to keep time with the beat.
author: torterrable

entry: When a POKENAME hatches from an egg it is very vulnerable, as its diamonds only form over time in the pressure of the ozone layer where it lives. From this data scientists have deduced the pressure present in the upper atmosphere and outer space.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME is primarily found in caverns located near volcanic activity. Rivals in the wild fight each other aggressively, aiming to break one of the other's crystalline horns as a sign of dominance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found in pools in dark crystal caves. Many spelunkers have sought out this Pokémon to ask out their lover with its shiny body.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME can be found in pools in dark crystal caves. Many spelunkers have sought out this Pokémon to ask out their lover with its shiny body.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The crystal formation covering its eyes protects it from bright sunlight as it darts around in zigzag patterns. It seems to be able to absorb sunlight and convert it into energy. Its energy sustains it and can be released as beams to defend itself.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME defend themselves by firing precise beams from their crystalline horns and tail spikes. They make their nests within gem-rich caves and caverns and feed on chunks of gems and ores.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's wings shine in brilliant colors in sunlight, as if the scales were made of crystal. They are most often seen in caves where underground flora is plentiful.
author: chibitales

entry: The dust that comes from POKENAME's wings has been studied by researchers for decades. It is comprised of fragments from many different gemstone types, with new sources being discovered intermittently.
author: .izik

entry: What was first thought to be white fur is actually densely packed cotton spores. The gem parts of its body serve to improve the rate at which it can absorb sunlight. To defend itself, it can fire its stored sunlight from the gem parts of its body.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME defend themselves by firing beams from the gem-like parts of their bodies while taking to the air to put distance between themselves and their foes. Their white feathers are softer than silk and are treasured by many collectors.
author: infinex21

entry: Living deep within coastal caves, POKENAME make their nests out of the moss that grows on the cavern walls. Flocks of these Pokémon gather for grooming, using their soft feathers to clean the jewel-like beaks, tails, and wings on one another.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's bill always appears to be filled with a liquid that shimmers like a gemstone. Many jewelers use this to polish jewelry due to the fantastic sheen it provides.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carefully carve out jewels from cavern walls before deftly crawling along rocks to bring their hauls back to their dens. Their legs are sharp at the end, but smooth along the bottom, allowing them to glide across jewels as they work.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The gems serving as POKENAME's legs blink red when it draws too close to a cave wall, somehow sensing nearby obstacles. Because of this, it can navigate pitch-black caves while airborne with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can often be found working for jewelers as guards to protect merchandise. They slash at thieves with their gem-tipped claws to prevent crime.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's fists are made of a thick gemstone. Each punch releases a brilliant light capable of temporarily blinding onlookers.
author: .izik

entry: Some miners have attempted to keep excavated POKENAME as pets due to their jewel-encrusted tails and soft fur. However, POKENAME will always find a way to escape and return to their caves, even long after mining efforts have been abandoned.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME can be seen wearing replicas of jewelry to convince people to enter the retail outlet. They take great pride in maintaining their appearance and act pompously around other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's red gems glow brightly when cheering for its fellows. If it becomes fervent enough, it may accidentally fire beams of electricity from them, causing damage to the local area.
author: chibitales

entry: The gems on POKENAME's ears act as batteries. It can store vast amounts of electricity within them by absorbing energy during thunderstorms.
author: .izik

entry: The scent emanating from POKENAME's body grows more intense the more gemstones it consumes. When a swarm inhabits a cave, the aroma can become overwhelming.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stalk miners to vacuum the dust of precious minerals that they leave behind. Many mineshafts with a POKENAME living in them have fairly clean air, much to the fortune of miners working in them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are able to turn their spikes to solid stone as they attack, leaving wounds that burn with poison. They use this ability to dig through mountains to find the minerals they feed on.
author: chibitales

entry: The diamond-hard crystals in this Pokémon's maw serve as teeth for crushing tough materials into dust to help with digestion. After a hearty meal, POKENAME always rinses its mouth with a big gulp of water to keep its jewels clean and shiny.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME keeps their crystalline bill polished by submerging the bill in mineral water. They can be found wandering in caves or around lakes looking for berries to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME spots a Seviper, the gems on its body glow crimson. It pursues the Seviper single-mindedly, sometimes even ignoring its own Trainer if they do not command respect.
author: .izik

entry: The gem-like scales on POKENAME's body are coated in a powerful neurotoxin. Even brief contact can cause dizziness that lasts for weeks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was originally thought to have originated from the moon. When moonlight is caught by its crystals, they glow brightly and increase POKENAME's power by several magnitudes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME channels its psychic powers through the magnificent gems that adorn its stone body. It moves by levitating in mid-air inside the caves where it makes its home, leading a mysterious life.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Equally protective as they are beautiful, POKENAME have often been used by royals to protect their castles. They will often use their sucker to stick to the ceilings and hidden crevices, firing high-energy beams at any threat to their Trainer.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: Its eyes are not great at seeing in the dark, so it's very skittish in its deep cave habitat. POKENAME's diamond-encrusted body is extremely hard, so it leaves a trail of dust when it rolls around.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME loves bouncing precious jewels on its nose like bouncy balls. Owning one is seen as a sign of affluence, as acquiring a gem of that size is quite taxing on the Trainer's wallet.
author: elibromax314

entry: POKENAME live in frigid caverns, typically near oceans. By living in packs of up to twenty, POKENAME fiercely protect each other. They are poached for their tusks that are made from precious gemstones.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: When closed, POKENAME look like nothing more than rocks, often residing in areas with high amounts of geodes. Anyone unfortunate enough to open these Pokémon will be met with a blinding light.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME enjoys snacking on crystals found deep in cave systems. It uses its nose to tear heart-shaped chunks out of the jewels, creating smaller portions that are easier to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sit in pairs outside of caves, roaring at any intruders loud enough to cause a rockslide to collapse the entrance. If a Trainer gains the trust of POKENAME, they will be permitted into the cave and rewarded with troves of jewels.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a rare cave-dwelling Pokémon that feeds on gemstone deposits near underground streams. The fluff on its abdomen is permeable, allowing it to absorb moisture and oxygen directly into its body.
author: hophoppip

entry: It uses its pick to dig deep in caverns for rare jewels. It's believed that it does this because consuming the gems increases its intellect and psychic powers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME strengthens its stony body by eating sapphires found deep in caves. With one punch, it can topple a small building.
author: .izik

entry: Surprisingly flexible and agile, POKENAME dodges away from attacks so they won't tarnish the rock and gems that make up its body. If it does get dirty, it can spit a fluid from its mouth that melts away the grime in seconds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shells are made of a durable crystal. By tucking their bodies inside and spinning, they release beams of light in all directions, blinding predators.
author: santon5512

entry: Whenever POKENAME splits apart, the geode inside its body shimmers as light strikes the crystal formation. It remains in dark caves to avoid being kidnapped by Trainers and Pokémon looking for shiny objects.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It hurls chunks of Chalky Stone at other Pokémon, for no particular reason other than the fact that they are there. On occasion, other Pokémon will return the tossed chunk, which turns the one-sided affair into a game.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's diamond-like shell is considered one of the sturdiest substances known to humans at this time. It's theorized it could even survive the pressure and heat of the planet's core.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's horn is its greatest pride. POKENAME with broken horns can often be seen fighting those with intact ones, attempting to shatter their crystal appendage out of spite.
author: xenellia

entry: The first to encounter POKENAME in the wild thought it was nothing more than an intricate statue until it responded to touch. POKENAME is so absentminded it simply forgets to move throughout most of the day.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are said to live for many years. During that time, many hard gemstones grow from their shell, attracting the attention of wild Sableye. POKENAME take advantage of this to form packs that'll provide food in exchange for gems.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: Whenever POKENAME's crystals are struck, its body discharges an electrical pulse in response to mechanical pressure. The harder POKENAME is struck, the more electricity the crystals produce.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's beautiful jewels sell for a high price on the market. However, the jewels are difficult to obtain because the caves in which they live often contain high temperatures and powerful magnetic fields that interfere with electronic equipment.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: The spikes on its shell look like ice but are harder than diamonds. They are formed under the enormous pressure at the very bottom of the sea.
author: stevethebarbarian

entry: POKENAME drifts through underground caves, absorbing amethyst for nourishment. Its eerie glow intensifies after consuming a particularly pure gemstone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's visage is often used in a tale about greed: sticking one's hand out to reach an alluring jewel that doesn't belong to them may result in it being bitten, or worse. When the gems on POKENAME's own hands change color, it is about to attack.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME hides itself in geode formations, awaiting its prey. Before you have a chance to realize it's there, it sucks your life force away.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME loves gemstones, carrying large amounts of them in its mouth. It will patiently wait for Sableye to leave their dens, before running away with their prized hoard of gems.
author: mistymagius

entry: Some have claimed POKENAME was the infamous "Crystal Onix" local folklore spoke about until proven otherwise. Living deep underground has hardened its stone and crystals to the point of being near impervious.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is particular about the dreams it consumes from those it sends to sleep. It only eats the happiest dreams it can find, as those dreams help keep its crystalline portions more pristine and shiny.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in underwater caverns inaccessible by normal land routes. Firm pinches from their claws dissuade Sableye from getting too close, and they won't hesitate to do the same to larger treasure-hunters.
author: wormspawn

entry: POKENAME is inquisitive and upbeat, often scampering around its woodland home in search of adventure. The nut on its back contains a potent poison which it can release with the spines on the shell of the nut.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME tend to be bold, fearless creatures that love to explore the world around them. If they are caught in a dangerous situation, they rely on their sharp teeth to escape harm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love to help their Trainer hang lights on trees and homes whenever the winter season comes around. They can easily hang lights on houses with their quill-like feathers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They live in tall trees; the higher a single POKENAME resides, the higher its position in the group's hierarchy. From up high, they like to jump on unsuspecting passers-by, aiming their spiky nuts at the heads of people and Pokémon.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME curls up and floats on the top of the water, resembling a large, spiked seed. If anything touches it, it flexes and hardens its body, causing its spikes to be able to pierce the attacker.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME waits beneath chestnut trees for ripe nuts to fall. Its powerful jaws can crush even the hardest seeds without hesitation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's normally squishy tail can harden to the point it cannot be broken by even a compression machine. This makes it an extremely useful bludgeoning tool.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME generally has a playful and carefree demeanor, although many consider them to be a nuisance; this is because a POKENAME's favorite game involves throwing acorns at passing people before scampering away.
author: craigprime

entry: POKENAME communicate and fight with headbutts. Their quills harden and become scalding hot when they are agitated. They spit flames to roast food and to deter threats.
author: infinex21

entry: It uses all of its strength to launch itself and headbutt trees, knocking loose as many fruits as possible. It prefers to eat nuts and will share food with any nearby people or Pokémon it can find; it seems to avoid conflict as much as it can.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can turn almost its entire body invisible, except for the leafy helmet it wears. It often hangs from branches by its tail for hours, secretly watching what other Pokémon are doing.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite their menacing second head, POKENAME are friendly Pokémon that love to gather berries and flowers for their friends. They will use this second head like a flail to defend themselves and others when threatened.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME enjoy causing mischief and pull pranks on other Pokémon daily. They are known for using their flaming tails to light vines on fire to prevent other Pokémon from chasing after them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eat sun-ripened berries after knocking them from berry trees with Pin Missiles. They often become frustrated when the berries won't fall, but will refuse any help and chase away those who try.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME gathers nuts from trees to store in its underwater dens during winter. When sick, a thin layer of bark covers its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME consumes seeds by inhaling them through the bottom of its nose. Its magnetic force increases the more seeds it stores internally.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are friendly by nature and use their vines to acquire food for themselves and for others they care for. To defend others, they can flex their ears to harden the quills upon them; these quills can pierce a tree when hardened.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has a shy nature, often curling up and hiding its face when confronted with someone new. During the full moon, the quills on its body grow longer and emit a faint silvery glow.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME contracts its muscles, its electricity builds and the soft spines on its head grow sharp. Touching the tip of a spine will deliver a nasty zap.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Despite it having sturdy armour, its head quills are usually soft but can harden to be tough enough to pierce rocks. It eats mostly berries and iron to build up its armour.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The strong thorns growing from POKENAME's feathers become incredibly sharp during autumn. Once spring arrives, they shed before regrowing throughout the summer.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful beak to break open hard seeds and berries. The more it eats, the more durable its head-shell becomes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME uses Seed Bomb to knock sapphires from cave walls. It can sustain its diet entirely on these gems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME consumes yard waste from compost bins along with seeds from various sources. If it stays in the rain too long, sprouts of random plants will frequently begin growing from its body.
author: .izik

entry: Although not particularly aggressive, POKENAME can be a problem for passing ships. It gnaws on solid objects to keep its buck teeth sharp, which can include boats that float by, potentially resulting in sinking them.
author: sk372

entry: Though allergic to ragweed, POKENAME nests near it. Its explosive sneezes release nutrients that greatly enrich nearby plant life.
author: .izik

entry: In the wild, POKENAME glides from tree to tree in forests, using its biological sonar abilities to look inside the trunks. When it detects a stash of berries or nuts left by another Pokémon, it steals them for itself.
author: houseoffallingflowers

entry: POKENAME's petals are full of chlorophyll, functioning more as leaves than as the petals of flowers. The tough, springy texture of their flower lets them protect themselves from physical harm, allowing them to rest wherever they please without fear.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's spikes remain velvety soft and squishy unless it is in combat. When threatened, they harden instantly, making its body difficult to bite or pierce.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scatters sharp seeds from its body as it dashes through the desert during the day. At night, the seeds grow rapidly into a variety of cacti.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers sunlit beaches, where it chews on seeds from nearby dune plants. It blends into the sand when resting during the heat of the day.
author: .izik

entry: Domesticated very early in the world of Pokémon, they are trusting and loyal, which causes them to return kindness given to them from people. They often clash with other Pokémon at night to defend their Trainers from nocturnal threats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a friendly, gentle nature, rarely getting itself into combat. Its spines are dulled at the tip and require effort on POKENAME's part to temporarily sharpen enough to be used in a fight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME does not have perfect control over the quills on its head and back, and sometimes will damage objects or itself by toughening or softening its quills inappropriately. It eats its body weight in berries daily to help toughen the quills.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME's rubbery skin emits a faint grass-like scent. When threatened, it pulls its leafy outer layer up like a hood to intimidate foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is protected by a shell similar to that of a chestnut. While the quills appear to be attached to the shell, they actually remain on POKENAME's body if the shell falls off.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: POKENAME became much more vulnerable after its outer shell broke. This Pokémon must eat a lot of berries for its outer shell to grow back.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: POKENAME's hard shell absorbs attacks by converting the force from the impact into heat energy. The more blows it takes, the hotter its shell becomes.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME swims near the ocean's surface at high speeds. The large chunk of wood on its head is so thick that even a boat collision does not faze it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dwells in abandoned ruins. In battle, it spits webs to weaken foes before delivering a painful bite.
author: mepp.

entry: The quills atop a POKENAME's head are typically soft, but they become hard and sharp when it is agitated. POKENAME is docile and incredibly friendly, even hurtling itself at trees to knock loose any fruits and share them with others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME skims the surface of ponds in search of overripe berries that have fallen in the water. If it eats too much, the hard shell on its head will grow too dense and disrupt its ability to skate on water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are greedy little creatures that love collecting coins. They are known to slice open purses and coin bags with their sharp quills to steal coins if their Trainer neglects them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Clusters of wild POKENAME are often seen gorging themselves on Berries with other local Pokémon. POKENAME make their nests in trees, using the nest as a vantage point to shoot small needles at unsuspecting passerby.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME have sharp quills and heavy shells to protect themselves from danger. They often fall onto their backs because of the weight of their shells and need help to get back up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME collects nuts from trees, storing them safely inside its large maw. At night, it sleeps soundly while its leafy appendages sway up and down, mimicking slow, steady breathing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoys pecking at dandelions, scattering their seeds into the wind. As they float, it eagerly chases and eats them, making a game out of its meal.
author: .izik

entry: Although POKENAME is mostly nocturnal, it can move even during the day by following its long antennae. The seed on its back is protected by thick fur, storing the energy it will need for its evolution.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its eyes can see even in the densest fog with very little effort. Using this ability, it can continue to find food during poor weather conditions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its clusters of eyes to spot targets at night, then attacks with a poisonous explosion. After the blast, its antennae are left behind, but it can regenerate them completely.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME's eyes blink red when enraged, signaling imminent detonation. Its powdery explosion causes coughing fits and sometimes paralysis.
author: .izik

entry: The antennae of all its heads move in unison when it launches a psychic-based attack. If one head is damaged, the others will take over its functions seamlessly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME manages to keep track of its enemies' movements thanks to its antennae, which detect even the slightest movement of air. Its kicks are so devastating that they can even crush large boulders.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME trains with other Bug-type Pokémon to improve the trajectory of its punches so it can fend off dangers from the woods. Its antennae help it sense the movements of enemies, allowing it to spot them even in the dark.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's tongue is covered in a thick red powder that spreads to any surface it licks. The powder can cause amnesia in the victim when it lingers on a human for too long.
author: .izik

entry: It shakes its antennae to let loose a violet dust. The dust clings to objects and can cause extreme exhaustion if inhaled.
author: .izik

entry: Despite how good its eyesight is, it cannot see directly in front of it. It will often run into things by accident while trying to catch its prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's eggs have a fine, fuzzy texture similar to its own hairs, though they are no less nutritious or delicious when eaten. Consuming them regularly is said to be particularly effective at combating allergies.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's many vines have a slightly fuzzy texture to the touch that most find pleasant. Domestic POKENAME use their extendable vines to tickle their unsuspecting owners.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can fire beams of light from its clustered eyes to protect its young. The child is still developing so it can only make a short flash of blinding light in self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: Though they look nearly identical to Butterfree, POKENAME is highly toxic.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME's antennae sense the slightest motion or shift of stance. It uses this data to align its blades for a perfectly placed strike.
author: .izik

entry: When frightened, POKENAME secretes poison over its jagged pincers. Despite its fearsome looks, it often flees rather than fighting.
author: .izik

entry: Rival POKENAME establish hierarchy by shaking their bodies and releasing a cloud of tiny hairs from their mane. The one that creates the bigger cloud is considered the superior.
author: sk372

entry: Despite looking fluffy, the fur of POKENAME is stiff. It's also coated in oils to protect it from the water it swims in.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME can be found in berry trees, slowly nibbling away at the berries. Its body is covered in a thick layer of hair that is toxic to the touch.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are covered in a fine fuzz that is soft to the touch. When they get riled up, their fuzz secretes a paralytic poison that can make them dangerous to handle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have compound eyes that are sensitive to light. They are capable of rapidly adapting to their surroundings through evolution.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have compound eyes that are effective at seeing in the dark and often gain new powers when POKENAME evolve. These new powers change depending on when and where POKENAME evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have specialized compound eyes that keep their vision clear when they dive into the water. They are adept swimmers that chase after aquatic Pokémon for fun.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's movements are incredibly erratic, jumping from place to place with lightning-fast speed. Getting too much of its poisonous dust on your skin will cause limb paralysis.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME rely on their superb vision to locate prey at night. Their compound eyes fire bursts of embers to set their prey aflame.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flock to bright lights at night and often find themselves staring through windows to observe computer screens. If a person allows them to access the device, they will try to be helpful by eating any viruses that are in the system.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If something approaches POKENAME, it vibrates rabidly and sheds tiny hairs from its body. These hairs cause extreme allergic reactions in most creatures, leaving them with blurry vision and uncontrollable sneezing.
author: sk372

entry: Its bald stomach secretes a sticky and sweet goo. Small insects are attracted and get trapped, which POKENAME picks off and eat as it lazes.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME's flames are constantly burning off tiny yet rapidly-growing hairs on its wings. The ashes that are left behind from each flap cause extreme burning and irritation to the eyes of those unfortunate enough to come into contact with them.
author: sk372

entry: Using its compound eyes, POKENAME tracks down sources of sweet honey. It carries the honey back to its hive for storage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sit motionless as they sleep in dark forests, awaiting nightfall. If disturbed, they only expend as much energy as is required to make the disturbance go away. When the moon rises, POKENAME awaken and scour their homes for bug Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: When faced with opposition, POKENAME heats up a segment of its back, burning up excess hair on its body into a cloud of dust it can control. This lets it obscure itself or agitate the vision of opponents, giving it an edge.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tend to nest in residential areas, sometimes accidentally getting into people's homes. Their feathers are coated in poisonous dust that, if inhaled, can cause mild fevers and severe migraines.
author: mistymagius

entry: It rocks side to side while unleashing a violet powder from its fur. If startled, it will let out an eerie screech that disorients attackers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have fantastic night vision and are able to track movement across great distances in even the dimmest light. They are a favourite companion of guards and policemen on the night shift.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are easily distracted by bright lights at night from cars and lamp posts that often ends with them getting run over by motor vehicles. Many environmentalists have proposed putting scent traps to steer POKENAME away from roads.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME glides upside-down, blending in with the violet cosmos in the sky. Its gaze seems to be fixated on a distant star.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's strong eyesight lets it observe even the faintest motions of prey from a distance. It carefully watches and calculates the best place to spin tiny webs that will catch prey as it tries to flee.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME quietly sneak up on their prey before paralyzing them with secretions from their fur. If the prey is too big to carry back to their cave, they leave the Pokémon there to recover from the paralysis.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's feathers are coated in a highly poisonous dust that it spreads every time it flaps its wings. However, once the toxin is removed, the dust is quite good at treating arthritis pains.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its coat of thin, bristly hair is said to have evolved for their protection. Each piece of hair crackles with static electricity even after being shed.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME emerges only at night to gaze at the constellations scattered across the sky. The poisonous dust it exhales from its mouth shimmers like silver stardust.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME flaps its wings on the ground to kick up dust and dislodge countless small hairs from its body. This is highly effective at blinding prey and making them easily snatched up and carried off back to its home.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will hide out in dense forests during the day, emerging at night to dance by the moon, seemingly drawn to its light. Their eyes allow them to see well in the dark, allowing them to spot any predators that may be approaching.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's powerful cluster of eyes allows it to see faint movement, becoming still if it detects even a hint of a living creature. If something attempts to harm it, it flings irritating pollen from its hands in their eyes to blind them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and gather in swarms after sunset. Their shaggy coats help them defend against predators and keep them warm on cold nights.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hops about flower fields, using its feelers to take pollen from other flowers and add it to its own. If attacked, it sprays an irritating, smelly powder from its flower that stuns attackers long enough for it to hop away.
author: sk372

entry: Their eyes are composed of clusters of lenses that help them view their surroundings from all angles. If they detect danger, they immediately leap at erratic angles, sinking their teeth into anything that gets too close.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME require lots of sunlight to grow, but often fall asleep at dawn because they are nocturnal creatures. Many rely on the light released from street lamps to nourish their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At night, POKENAME stare at street lamps or other sources of bright light for long periods of time. By the time the sun rises, they are already asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hops through wetlands emitting a sweet but toxic mist from its fuzzy antennae. Its bulbous eyes can track prey even in swampy fog.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME has heightened senses and can detect imminent danger. They release poison through touch as a self-defense mechanism.
author: riel.vndxgrxvnd

entry: At night, POKENAME glow in the dark with the power of their yellow bands across their body. When two POKENAME meet, they stare at each other and admire the glow that they produce.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its strong eyesight lets it see the glimmer of anything shiny from long distances with minimal lighting. POKENAME disperses clouds of small hairs with a flap of its wings to blind people and swipe their belongings.
author: sk372

entry: The poisonous dust from POKENAME's hair negatively affects its mind, causing it to go mad. It can be seen making odd contraptions out of anything it can get its hands on.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have conflicting internal sleep schedules that cause them to fall asleep often. They are most active during the dawn and dusk where they can still absorb sunlight without being overwhelmed by their desire to rest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's large eyes are very sensitive to light, so it prefers to only hunt at night. Even if it is blinded, its sensitive whiskers and tail allow it to get a good picture of its surroundings.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is well-liked by some as a pet, finding its grumpy expression adorable. It is an arduous task to keep it groomed, however, and when it shakes its body after cleaning, tiny hairs spread everywhere.
author: sk372

entry: It will hold a foe down with its powerful horn while unleashing a poisonous powder on them. The combination of brute strength and toxic spores makes it a fearsome opponent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is made up of a colony of Bug types, overall requiring extreme amounts of energy to maintain their form. They are attracted to sweet drinks, with a fondness for mead. Unfortunately, the sugars inebriate the Pokémon.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are covered in fine hairs that grow constantly. These hairs shed easily as they move about and can end up being embedded in skin if touched, creating a painful burning sensation.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It scratches the fur behind its ear with its rear paws, letting loose clouds of poisonous powder. The heat from its body makes the powder even more potent, burning the eyes of those nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wraps up prey, but doesn't constrict them. It instead uses the powder in its fur to smother its prey, rendering them vulnerable.
author: pokepower

entry: While Venonat are attracted to light, POKENAME are attracted to advertisements on the internet. They congregate around ads to stare at the image or video for a few minutes before moving on to the next ad.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME charges a Psybeam through its glowing antlers. If the attack misses, it retreats while releasing a distracting poison mist.
author: .izik

entry: A sticky red powder seeps from the tip of its tail. This substance is used in inks for expensive fountain pens.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cannot see the details of objects very well, but its eyes are extremely sensitive to any motion. As a result, it can even see a newborn Joltik slowly inch throughout a field of corn.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are constantly protected from predators by a poisonous ooze secreted all over their bodies. It is rumored that this poison originated from the toxins they have absorbed from water they have purified.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered in dense, prickly fur. At night, it propels itself with poisonous gas.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME fur is coated in a conductive powder. When they're in battle, they shake their body vigorously to release the powder before loosing an indiscriminate electric shock, the bolts of electricity drawn to anything covered in the powder.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME stores spare food within the recesses of its fuzzy back. Sometimes it offers to share with friends, seeming confused when they refuse to partake in the fuzz-covered snacks.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its hulking size, POKENAME is a rather timid creature, hiding away deep in forests and caves and refusing to come out unless it sufficiently trusts someone. It seems afraid of potentially hurting someone due to its size.
author: sk372

entry: As it burrows, POKENAME sheds colored poison dust that marks its tunnels. The powder's microscopic patterns are unique to each individual.
author: .izik

entry: In a Pokémon battle, POKENAME rely on their compound eyes to pinpoint weak spots on their opponent. Once they find a suitable target, they release a flurry of leaves that overwhelm their opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in boreal forests where there is plenty of snow to play in. When threatened, they release a chilling frost from their compound eyes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's furry coat lets it survive in cold environments. This was a rare Pokémon during the Ice Age, as most Bug types died out from the cold.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME are quite timid, quickly climbing up into the trees at the slightest sense of danger. The hairs are both toxic and hard to get rid of, causing immense displeasure in those who try to eat them.
author: mistymagius

entry: Their bushy tails are full of thin, needle-like hair that can tense like their quills can. Their eyes have evolved to spot even the smallest of prey, no matter how fierce the weather may be.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in countless fine furs, making it very soft and fuzzy. It loves to give embraces to others, which are pleasant but leave the hugged person feeling slightly itchy afterward.
author: sk372

entry: Concealed within POKENAME's coat are venomous barbs. A single prick can induce fatigue and sluggishness in most predators.
author: .izik

entry: It can change the color of all of its body except for its eyes. It hides away from sight, using its powerful eyes to scope out the faint movement of small insects, before its tongue lashes out at lightning speed to catch and eat them.
author: sk372

entry: Despite formidable strength and speed, POKENAME is jumpy and prone to panicking. When startled in the wild, it's not unheard of for it to cut a tree down in a single swing, just to cover its rapid escape.
author: sk372

entry: Venomoth appear drawn to the pollen stored in POKENAME's flower. POKENAME detests the unwelcome visitors, to the point of attacking Venomoth on sight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sheds its poisonous fur on a daily basis, which keeps predators away from its den. Its antennae are very sensitive to loud noises, so it lives in more remote areas.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME retracts the upper parts of its body into the fuzzier lower half, hiding in thick bushes until suitable prey draws near. Once it does, POKENAME extends its many sticky antennae out to grab and drag away its new meal.
author: sk372

entry: It always acts distant, even in battle. Some theorize that the cause of this may be the fact that each lens of its compound eyes is staring at something happening in a different universe, leaving only one lens for what's happening here.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME live in polluted areas, feeding on leftover scraps and garbage. They will sometimes team up with each other to steal larger meals from suburban homes.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its sheath looks just like a hairy bug, so bird Pokémon often peck at it fruitlessly. By the time they realize their mistake, it is too late - POKENAME has already begun draining their life force.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: A foul-smelling poison seeps from the fur on POKENAME's horn. It rarely uses the horn itself, relying on intimidation to avoid battle.
author: .izik

entry: The fur covering POKENAME's entire body is coated with toxic dust, poisoning anyone who dares to attack it. When it accumulates electricity in its body, its antennae glow with an intense yellow light.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a curious sort, but quick to panic at any unexpected movements. It escapes from danger by flapping its wings rapidly, blowing away countless tiny hairs on its body that agitate and blind those in front of it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a special cover over their eyes that protect them from sand particles in the air. This allows them to stare at bright lights at night in the middle of sandstorms without worrying about eye injuries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Their eyes act as radars, scanning for small bugs and prey to to eat. Their ribbons allow them to dig up grubs.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME floats near illuminated cottages, waiting for residents to lower their guard. Its sensitive antennae can detect emotional states.
author: .izik

entry: These tiny Pokémon are covered, and protected, in a layer of plasma that seems to allow them to levitate. They are drawn to sources of light, especially lightbulbs which they will drain electricity from.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sheds a faint powder while walking, which thickens under moonlight. The powder's color shifts with each lunar phase, baffling researchers.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its compound eyes to see in the dark while dispensing sticky webs to trap prey. These webs carry an electrical charge, stunning anything that struggles too much.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the shadows, with insects and Bug-type Pokémon. It throws off its disguise and unveils its horrendous form to eat its prey whole.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It prefers dark areas, and its fur is covered in a purple powder that scatters as it moves. Despite its poor eyesight, it uses its fine hairs to sense nearby prey.
author: .izik

entry: Said to release an unknown poison that can instantly prove fatal, POKENAME is an extremely fast Pokémon. Its species was only recently documented by bug experts.
author: riel.vndxgrxvnd

entry: Swarms of POKENAME gather near rotting berry trees, eating all the scraps they can. When threatened, they will loudly vibrate their wings, creating a painful cacophony of buzzing.
author: mistymagius

entry: The hairs on POKENAME's body are incredibly sensitive, allowing it to sense the emotions of other Pokémon. However, the hairs are coated with small amounts of poison that cause strange psychological effects.
author: mistymagius

entry: The poisonous dust in POKENAME's fur is constantly irritating it, causing it to rampage all over the place. The dust has been commercially harvested as a powerful stimulant, but only in minuscule doses.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's fur is made of fine metallic strands. The powder it stores within can cause mild burns upon contact with skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burn dust from their body to produce a purple flame on their tail. This purple flame returns to normal on the rare occasion they run out of dust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME is amongst abundant plant-life, it will open its bud and release special pollen. It doesn't realize that its pollen is toxic, however.
author: char_latte3412

entry: If it feels threatened, POKENAME will wave its arms around wildly, releasing a highly toxic powder that can make a grown adult fall horribly ill for at least a week if not treated. Fellow Poison-types use this powder to heal themselves.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME is filled with a poisonous gas that is heavier than air. Unlike Drifloon, it struggles to kidnap children because it can barely keep itself afloat.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME's purple fur is covered in fungal spores that it releases as it hops through the woods. It thrives in dark, damp places, which is why it usually makes its den where dense vegetation blocks out the sunlight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Floating gently, POKENAME swings its antenna like a pendulum. It channels psychic blasts through it with eerie precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME float to lampposts at night to stare at bright lights. Efforts to drag them away are met with an odd fluid that makes grabbing them difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often inhabits abandoned buildings, as it loves to feed on the dust that builds up there. Coming into contact with its poisonous fur will cause severe rashes that last up to 5 months.
author: mistymagius

entry: Possessing powerful eyesight and echolocation, POKENAME makes it nearly impossible to hide or evade it when it's on the hunt. Fortunately for most, it only tends to hunt small insects.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME moves, its fur crackles with faint static. It releases electrical pulses through its antennae when excited or alarmed.
author: .izik

entry: Its eyes blink a vibrant red light while it senses for predators. Its body is made up of tiny metal shards. Any attacker that bites it will end up with a mouthful of jagged steel dust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME claws at trees with its sharp tusks before releasing acidic powder from its fur. The powder quickly dissolves the weakened trunk.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME typically do not travel at night and only migrate during the day. However, with the installation of lamp posts, they can now migrate at night by following lights from city to city.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As it flutters through the night, it shakes loose poisonous powder from its fur. The toxin lingers in the air, making it difficult for predators to follow.
author: .izik

entry: Laying traps at night, POKENAME lurk on forest floors waiting for unsuspecting victims to walk over them. When stepped on, their stiff hairs latch onto the target, releasing a weakening poison.
author: evilgammon
