entry: POKENAME can curl up and roll away, reaching surprising speeds. Their fluffy fur cushions collisions like an airbag so that it does not injure itself.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can spin like a tire when stationary and then race off at high speed. Its fur protects it in the case of collisions.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can spin like a tire when stationary and then race off at high speed. Its fur protects it in the case of collisions.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can climb any slope, no matter how steep. If it is attacked by a flying Pokémon, it can drop down and cushion the fall with its thick fur.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME covers its body in its poisonous pollen, dissuading any other Pokémon from eating it. It loves damp weather and groups of them will gather together before rainstorms.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has no feathers but thick fur instead. It dances joyfully, yet its rapid spinning tangles the fur into hopeless knots that only a few expert groomers can untangle.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When cheering, POKENAME's antennae bob wildly and often tangle. Its pom-poms are bound with a sticky, toxic secretion harmful to humans and Pokémon.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's fur is coated in a mucus that induces sleep when smelled. As it dances, it leaves a slimy trail surrounded by dozing humans and Pokémon.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Though it looks like it has wings, POKENAME's flaps are just excess fur shaped to mimic feathers. It dyes the tips red with its own poisonous saliva.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME hunts exclusively at night, using its radar-like eyes to detect prey lurking in the darkness. During the day, it sleeps in caves with little to no light.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Light filters through the ethereal body of POKENAME, making it very hard to see as it hides among the trees. This camouflage is its only defense mechanism, leaving it quite helpless when spotted.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: POKENAME hide their bodies and wait for prey to brush by their leaves, which are covered in a sticky, cloying toxin. Then, they pop out and bite.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME are generally quite docile, preferring to play in the dirt and jumping about carefree. They like to eat different kinds of dirt.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME scuttles along seabeds, using its large radar-like eyes to scavenge for food. The stiff hairs covering its body offer it protection from underwater predators like Mareanie.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME is a very persistent pest. It can feed on most plants, resort to eating wood, and even hunt small Grass-type Pokémon. When it finds a tasty meal, it emits a pheromone cloud to call its peers.
author: lucioleuh

entry: There's no evidence its body is made of anything except stiff hairs. Even x-rays can't penetrate the dense fur.
author: pokepower

entry: The smoke billowing out of POKENAME's body contains a pheromone highly attractive to Venonat. It's very common to see small groups of them swarming and playing amongst POKENAME's clouds.
author: sk372

entry: A fusion of two Venonat causes the DNA of POKENAME to develop rapidly and begin expressing traits of their evolved form. Their over-developed bodies require a greater amount of food and Trainers are advised to bring extra rations on journeys.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a common house-pest in rural areas, drawn to outdoor lamps and lanterns. Its scales are highly toxic, so it's recommended to call a professional if one is spotted.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's eyes flash crimson when its territory is breached. It then scatters a fine acidic powder to repel the intruder.
author: .izik

entry: When flying through the air at high speeds, POKENAME sheds excess fur from its body. This fuzz burns up quickly, creating a colorful trail of sparks behind its flight paths, akin to a comet's tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME combine the dust shed from their body with their flaming tail to produce clouds of toxic smoke. Pokémon that inhale the smoke find themselves tired and unable to land attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Dirt and other particles are always getting in POKENAME's fuzzy body, so it's common for those nearby to start sneezing when POKENAME grooms itself. POKENAME has powerful night vision.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found in fast-flowing streams, their sharp fangs and grasping hands helping them stay in place in the current. They make poor aquarium Pokémon as their fine hairs constantly shed and clog up filtration systems.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its large eyes allow it to see far ahead and around it as it runs around in zigzag patterns. Its coat of hair is thin, stiff, and prickly to offer better protection.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME's large eyes allow it to see far ahead, even as it runs fast in a straight line. They also track prey well and will leap upon them to down them with their sharp claws after chasing them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sleeps near the surface with its antennae exposed to sense danger. When threatened, it releases thick clouds of paralyzing dust.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces a spicy powder prized in many burrito dishes. People often harvest it from abandoned tunnels, though exposure can cause irritation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are cute, cuddly creatures that enjoy playing with toys that their Trainer provides. The only downside to owning a POKENAME is dealing with the constant shedding of dust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It can fire off unusual moves from the speckled, red jewel on its forehead. Its fuzzy body quickly picks up dust, spores, seeds, and dirt, so it spends most of the day trying to clean itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are found in resorts on remote tropical islands, releasing a calming smoke from the vent on their back. The magma in their bodies instantly warms up enclosed spaces, perfect for heating saunas while they idly stare at the lighting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: For people who want a warm room at a vacation resort, POKENAME are brought in to heat up the room to a guest's taste. The only room POKENAME refuse to enter are sauna rooms, as the lack of lighting and high humidity make POKENAME upset.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If something flees from an angry POKENAME, it will find it difficult to truly escape; its vision is highly acute, and its stubborn personality means it rarely gives up a chase, even after hours.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME trades Venonat's adept night vision for equally adept echolocation abilities. Though it can barely see, it is oddly attracted to anything shaped like a street lamp.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is most active in the evenings, using its dimly glowing tail as a lure. It feasts on bugs attracted by this light.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lives in the damp marsh, feeding on soaked leaves and roots. Its fur is covered in a toxic oil that causes skin irritation on contact.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's spiral spins rapidly as its eyes glow bright pink. This hypnotic combination can lull foes into sudden sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can detect the slightest change of the wind with their sensitive fur. If they suspect a Trainer is nearby, they teleport away before they are spotted.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME play in kids shows where they use supposed psychic powers to distinguish gold from counterfeits. In reality, many rely on their sensitive eyes to make this decision, as their psychic abilities play little role in their judgement.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME were once brought to mining sites to dowse for ore. It is a common misconception that they harness psychic powers to find ore, as it turns out that they can spot glints of ore in the walls of the dark mines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often associated with urban legends. Despite their large size, they are actually quite timid. The fluff of a POKENAME is often used in high-end winter clothing.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME roots itself near nettles and consumes their thorns as a food source. If disturbed, it retaliates with a sudden Psybeam.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are covered in sensitive fuzz used to detect movement. The fuzz is not waterproof, so when swimming, they tuck everything but their limbs into their shells.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME ambushes its prey by dropping from high tree branches and draining their fluids with their hollow fangs. However, it takes them almost a full day to climb back into the trees.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME has a pernicious acid inside its bell that slowly digests bug Pokémon. Whenever one falls in, it releases spores to lull the prey to sleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A faint scent emitted by POKENAME's hairs induces drowsiness and contentment in those who smell it. Many enjoy using it as a pillow to nap on, which POKENAME doesn't mind at all.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly attuned to their environment thanks to a coating of dense sensory hairs, sensitive ears, and eyes that can see even in the darkest conditions. When they sense danger approaching they retract into their shells to wait it out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their antenna to feed on the energy of radio waves present in the air. As a result, POKENAME can often be found emitting radio broadcasts from their bodies, and have become a staple amongst campers.
author: turron_turron

entry: It flaps its wings before releasing a Psybeam from its compound eyes. The sudden gust of wind it creates can spread its sleep-inducing powder across an entire field.
author: .izik

entry: It stands on the top of hills and shakes its body, letting loose a blue powder. This powder can stun others in the area with the smallest sniff.
author: .izik

entry: If it sees someone it loves with its compound eyes, it will flail its arms wildly in happiness, splashing inky slime everywhere. This affectionate display has ruined many Trainers' clothes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body composition is a strange mixture of fuzzy and sludgy. Should some part of a person come in contact with its residue, that spot will remain itchy for days, even after removing the goop.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stretches its slimy body around to catch smaller Bug Pokémon to eat. Exposure to too much of the goop comprising its form can cause lengthy periods of blindness in the victim.
author: sk372

entry: It uses Sleep Powder to put prey to sleep before feasting on their dreams. Its antennae twitch when it detects a particularly vivid nightmare.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME reflects a pattern of light bursts off of its pendulum, which induces different types of dreams. Its fur is incredibly soft and smells slightly of lavender, leading to the belief that pillows using its fur will lead to sweet dreams.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME rubs the bulb on its back against stones and trees to strengthen the shell, shaving off weakening sections. The red spikes on its nose, ears, and bulb secrete the poison gestating within the bulb.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are used in therapy, as they absorb emotions and release them as a gas that a therapist can experience. Their tough shell protects them from harm, so even overwhelming anger is carried calmly, making them reliable partners in emotional care.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The leaves that grow from POKENAME's arms are actually incredibly dense and sharp. They function as dangerous weapons, especially when detached and thrown.
author: craigprime

entry: Wild POKENAME live together in sizable groups and spar with one another to strengthen their small bodies. Within themselves are singular flame sacs, which is where they form their fireballs; they often spit fireballs to knock down fruit.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are constantly sparring with each other to train their muscles and endurance. During combat, POKENAME will fight with their sharp claws and rely on their spiny feathers to counter the opponent's attacks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME tend to be very easygoing. They calmly carry out any Trainer's command without hesitation. However, POKENAME will even listen to the orders given by people who aren't their Trainers.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME runs into another of its kind to build up its legs so they can have even footing on mud. It deflects predators' attacks and counterattacks with its quills.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Quills across POKENAME's body lengthen in response to the emotions it senses around it. The more it feels endangered, the more quills come out to protect itself, ready to be launched from its body at a moment's notice.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME always clash when they meet, purely to test each other's mettle and strength; rarely do they clash with malicious intent. Their tails curl tightly whenever they tense their muscles, including before they fire out their tongues.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME constrict their foes with their strong maws. Kind by nature, they also use their maws to crush up hard foods for others. When two POKENAME meet, they will engage in battle for the sake of testing each other's mettle and power.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's great weight makes it ideal for running into trees to dislodge ripe fruits. It shares these with Pokémon that bring its favorite food, a berry that grows on thorny bushes and requires more dexterity to pick than it has.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Beneath the bushes on POKENAME's back hide packs of thorns ready to be launched at opponents. Many predators have found themselves fleeing due to a surprise deluge of pointed projectiles being unleashed on them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a cocky streak and is highly confident in its combat prowess. It can fire little spines from its body over a short distance, each spike tipped with a tiny burning flame to singe the targets they hit.
author: sk372

entry: Due to a lack of teeth, POKENAME utilize special soft spines in their beaks and mouth to help them swallow prey. POKENAME flap their small flippers and shakes their bodies while doing so to help the process.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME spits thin streams of water to knock mangoes from trees. It uses its claws to peel the fruit before eating what lies within.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is covered with sturdy plant materials to protect it from any attack. POKENAME takes great care maintaining its territory, which includes periodically planting new trees.
author: mepp.

entry: Even in the wild, POKENAME refuse to start fights without an honorable reason. Instead, these Pokémon use their thorn-clad feelers to protect others and to put an end to unnecessary quarreling.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME build their bodies up by ramming into and bouncing off each other, and eating a ton of berries daily. It can survive on land longer then a normal Wailmer can.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME will strengthen their legs by playfighting. If one gets hurt in the fray, the others will sit together and groom its coat as an apology.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The spiky needles that make up POKENAME's body are charged with high voltage electricity. Packs of POKENAME can share their emotions by touching the spines on their heads together.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME always strive to be stronger, leading to them clashing with each other whenever they meet; this also serves to test the mettle of each other. The spikes along their bodies are harder than steel and are shed monthly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has a really sturdy shell to deflect predators. It builds up that armor by eating abandoned railroad tracks, and its lower body ramming into another POKENAME.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Tiny saplings grow from POKENAME's down after rain hits it. It picks these out with its beak to prevent complications with flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME protects the weaker undersea Pokémon while simultaneously being a powerful predator. It tackles those preying on the weak with its sturdy, spine-covered body, turning the bullies into its own prey.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes a childlike giggle while traveling through the forest, consuming seeds. The sprouts that grow from its body each spring are always plants from seeds it has eaten.
author: .izik

entry: The loud saxophone-like noise POKENAME produces from its wooden ears can cause nausea after prolonged exposure. It makes this noise while flying in circles above its foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in desert climates where the need to conserve water causes their quills to turn red. Whenever threatened, they shoot a burst of barbed quills that are difficult to remove.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fills its mouth with any herbs it finds while traveling, storing them for later. It shows a clear preference for aromatic varieties such as rosemary and basil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME props itself up as a defender of smaller Pokémon, intimidating bullies with its immense size and girth. It relies mostly on this threat display, as its new size is actually a detriment due to losing a lot of mobility.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME train by tackling each other with awe-inspiring force, but do not feel even the slightest bit of pain. Outgrown shells from this Pokémon are highly sought for use in making protective gear for sporting events.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME battles by smacking opponents with its mace, which it will ignite if it believes the battle will be challenging. It takes special care in growing the spiked nut that it uses for the mace, protecting trees that produce them.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME collects scattered foliage and sticks it to itself using adhesive saliva. It then rests in canopies, blending into the scenery. They are largely kind and non-confrontational in nature.
author: prolucario_

entry: POKENAME train their strength by catching charging Quilladin with their arms. Rumors say that the wails of spirits can be heard whenever it deflects an attack with its body.
author: soup1900

entry: The glowing end of POKENAME's tail is always red-hot. It uses it to burn marks into trees to denote its territory.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME quietly watches couples near it, aiming to protect their love. If it spots something that threatens the couple, it extends and fires pointed spines from its tail fin.
author: sk372

entry: After burying itself in the ground, POKENAME causes sturdy vines to rapidly sprout nearby. These vines act independently and grab at anyone who draws close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a very short temper, even the sounds of falling leaves send it into fury. It increases its level of violence extremely quickly, jumping from frolicking in flowers to using Mega Punch on boulders.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME never starts a fight out of anger. It spars in friendly matches with other Fighting-type Pokémon to nurture their natural talents.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME test their strength by launching themselves at each other, barreling through whatever stands in their way. If one POKENAME manages to catch another mid-charge, it will fling the opponent away to claim the territory.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Although it lives independently, a wild POKENAME happily reunites with its family every spring; the group will celebrate and compare one another's strength. The fluffy orange fur on its head and tail has a festive nutty aroma.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME charges into trees, knocking them down to create walls around its nest. While the nut on its back contains a poison too dangerous for human consumption, the shell is delicious and nontoxic.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME love snacking on parasitic plants, frequently visiting old trees in search of them. Their bodies are covered in small, rigid spikes that deter even the hardiest of predators.
author: turron_turron

entry: The large leaf atop a POKENAME's head is both flexible and sturdy, allowing it to endure most forms of physical attacks. POKENAME flex and bend the stalks of their leaves to shield themselves and their allies from all angles.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's psychic senses alert it to the feelings of beings in danger nearby. It rushes to their aid, erecting Barriers and Light Screens to protect them from harm while it takes on the aggressor directly.
author: sk372

entry: It takes smaller Pokémon under its protection and rules over them fairly as the leader of the pack. POKENAME prefers to solve conflicts peacefully, but if its packmates are in danger, it'll fight fiercely and defend them at all costs.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME's elevated shell protects the tree nuts underneath from bird Pokémon, especially since the shell now produces a poison that can be transmitted by its spikes. It lies in sunlight to strengthen the defensive prowess of its shell.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME make their homes in abandoned castles, preferring those with copper roofing. They are protective of horse Pokémon, holding grudges against those who harm them. Their small stature makes it difficult for them to be an effective threat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME make their homes in abandoned castles, preferring those with copper roofing. They are protective of horse Pokémon, holding grudges against those who harm them. Their small stature makes it difficult for them to be an effective threat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Combining the two halves of POKENAME's shield creates a near-impenetrable defense in front of it. It leaps to defend any forest denizens in its home from danger, waiting out and exhausting its foe before launching a counterattack.
author: sk372

entry: Although it is small, this Pokémon's Tackle is forceful enough to split a full-grown tree. It will take hits head-on and retaliate with Tackle attacks or by spitting out hot flames.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME cultivate spicy nuts during the winter, which are sought after by culinarians for special desserts. If POKENAME does not recognize a person, they will attempt to defend what they have grown with their sharp sword.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is quite protective of others, shielding them from harm with its body. Despite its small stature, its body is incredibly durable; a charging Steelix would be stopped dead in its tracks if it collided with POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: To defeat its opponents, POKENAME will try to lure its opponent onto muddy ground that offers poor footing.  There, it can easily deliver a thrashing with its thorned fists.
author: imaginita

entry: Covered in a thick armoured hide, POKENAME move about their grassland homes with little fear of attack. When threatened by something powerful enough to pose a danger, they will band together and present a spiky shield-wall with their bodies.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME defend their Trainer from harm with their shield and lance. Their prickly personality slowly melts into affection as they bond with their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Even in the wild, POKENAME are stalwart protectors of other Pokémon. Their small bodies are densely packed with muscle, so they can withstand most blows head-on. They can change their hues for camouflage, but they never do so in battle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can manipulate the elevation of its protective shell with specialized muscles of the treetrunk-like growth on its back. This protects or exposes the branches that grow tree nuts, which are widely used as snacks and as salad toppings.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME eat tough foods with their large maws, which have enough strength to bite through a sheet of steel. They have valiant hearts and will not hesitate to help and protect others; notably, they often use their maws as shields.
author: infinex21

entry: These armored behemoths are sometimes called "sleeping bulwarks of the forest". While they prefer to relax in the shade and gorge themselves on fallen berries, when driven to action, their strength and fury are legendary.
author: karagar

entry: The thick wood on POKENAME's back sweats an amber-colored sap when the temperature grows too high. If dehydrated, this sap becomes incredibly thick.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a nigh-impenetrable shell and has no fear when they lumber about in the forests they call home. They fall into easy habits, traveling the same route each day, and small Pokémon will rely on POKENAME to get to food or water safely.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME fills fruit with a peculiar combustible sap before lobbing it at those who venture too close to its nest. The fruit explodes on impact, spraying hot pulp in all directions.
author: .izik

entry: Dense bones and a heavy protective shell make POKENAME an excellent diver. These traits allow it to reach deep waters quickly when searching for food.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The thin layer of bark on POKENAME's wings helps it swim at high speeds through chilly waters. It occasionally leaps into the air from the water, flinging seeds in all directions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a magnanimous ruler, putting the safety and defense of those it considers its subjects above all else. The shields on its arms can withstand tremendous force, and it will retaliate with spikes that can pierce reinforced steel.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Its feelers are incredibly hard despite how freely they can flail about. It rarely starts fights but will not hesitate to interfere with fights to protect the weaker party. It uses its feelers to repel attacks and to shield others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are durable fighters, shedding their armor constantly so it can regrow even stronger. They use their ears as clubs in combat, bludgeoning their foes.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME swing their flails to attack, letting them crack apart to release spikes across a wide area. Despite their serious nature, they are extremely nervous around fire.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The thorns growing from POKENAME's steel body are extremely sharp. They appear to grow even sharper the more ore it consumes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found near volcanoes, enjoying the warmth that lava brings. Preliminary research shows that they seem to become aggressive when faced with someone wearing red.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The shell on POKENAME's head sports an incredibly strong fin atop its body. This fin is durable enough to emerge undented even if a yacht collides with it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scatters small seeds around its territory as it flies. At night, it releases a high pitched frequency that causes the seeds to grow rapidly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lower their head toward their foe when they feel threatened, relying on the tough petals of their flower to absorb impacts and keep themselves safe. They have a protective nature and will also block strikes intended for smaller Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It communicates by striking together the scales on its arms and hands. The spikes on its strong tail are also seeds, so plants often grow where its tail has struck.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME takes advantage of aggressive opponents by letting them attack its diamond-hard body while it takes a defensive posture. Once the foe has tired itself out, POKENAME finishes them off with a powerful tackle without having taken any damage.
author: soup1900

entry: Traveling through fields and gardens, POKENAME scatter shards of peridot crystals laced with a mystical energy that helps plants grow. Old legends claim that recollecting the shards before winter will amplify the magic the following year.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's heavy shell gives it impeccable defenses, but severely limits its mobility. Its battle style relies on tanking its opponent's heavy blows before countering with powerful headbutts or painful stabs with its quills.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are a true guardian of the forest, their armor and shield as hard as steel. POKENAME will often confront poachers and loggers with unbridled confidence, swinging their flails high above their heads as they charge towards them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses its wand to control flowers from a distance. It manipulates their roots to ensnare foes before following up with Psyshock.
author: .izik

entry: The burrs that POKENAME summons are able to block any and all attempts to approach it. Opponents often get annoyed and abandon their attempts before ever getting within range for an attack.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME grows leaves on its back that stiffen and become as sharp as knives when it's ready to battle. These leaves will rapidly decay after use, leaving little evidence of POKENAME's involvement in the battle.
author: drcew

entry: After shedding their protective shells on windy peaks, POKENAME are often swept into the air. Too dense to stay aloft, they plummet into the valleys below, creating deep impact craters but emerging completely unscathed.
author: eiskitsune

entry: The chestnut at the end of POKENAME's tail combusts if touched. Because of that, POKENAME wards off threats by striking its foes with the unnatural nut. The large spikes on its back work in the same way.
author: .realthree

entry: It was once said by a philosopher that a Trainer who grows old with POKENAME at their side will lead a long and fulfilling life. It is deeply loyal and highly affectionate.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME perch at the edge of cliffs, waiting for prey to go by. Once they spot their targets, they leap and dive into the water with their wings tucked, dive-bombing their prey with a cannonball strong enough to create waves from the impact.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are incredibly durable and highly adaptable, capable of skimming across any water surface regardless of water quality. Although normally docile, they are strong enough to flip boats if threatened.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: The hard shell that protects POKENAME's body deters predators from eating it. While in a school, POKENAME send out electrical currents through the pointed tips on their backs, one side taking in electricity, the other releasing it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME shed the armor from their bodies in favor of fashioning it into a weapon to use directly in battle. Despite the bulk of their new mace, POKENAME are dexterous and calculating, always landing precise blows.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's shell is impenetrable even against the most intense forces. It can use its power over roots to anchor itself and become immovable, even in soft sand. For offense, it rams into root-bound opponents with its spiked shell.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME attacks using vine-like sticks that sprout from its back. If these touch its hot ears, they may accidentally burst into flames.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME will gather sticks from the forests to create small training dummies to practice punching against. Its fists generate small sparks and flames as it trains, leading to it eventually setting the dummies on fire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often flies among tree branches in search of spicy berries that can strengthen its still-weak flames. The fur growing from its ears is so soft and fluffy that other Pokémon try to steal it to build their nests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To cast fire upon their foes, POKENAME rely on hand gestures to shoot embers at their foes. People who rely on sign language to communicate are delighted when POKENAME understand their gestures.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's fur constantly smolders, leaving faint scorch marks wherever it walks. It is fiercely territorial and has been seen drawing glowing patterns in the dirt to warn intruders away.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME prefers to live in solitude, spending its time feasting upon charred branches. It has been known to set trees ablaze to satiate its hunger, leading it to be hated by Pokémon like Trevenant.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME have a very particular diet consisting of only sticks. Their bodies emit constant warmth due to the flames in their stomachs, making them the perfect sleeping companion in the winter.
author: santon5512

entry: It is a high-maintenance creature because it needs to be sheared daily. Its wool was originally used in the process of creating a Fluffy Tail, but nowadays it is spun into yarn for elderly people.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its fleece is considered to be some of the warmest material in the world, however sweaters made from it give wearers a nasty static shock. After a few hospitalizations from these occurrences, POKENAME fleece was recalled from international markets.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When without food, POKENAME will resort to eating sticks instead. They can release warm air from their ears, keeping themselves warm in the winter.
author: santon5512

entry: The oils on POKENAME's skin have a fiery taste to them. If the substance has a pungent odor, it will be spicier than usual.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME attacks using vine-like sticks that sprout from its back. If these touch its hot ears, they may accidentally burst into flames.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME absorbs sunlight and eats twigs to nourish the bulb on its back. When overheated, the bulb vents air exceeding 390 degrees Fahrenheit.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are a common sight in the forests of Kalos, gnawing on fallen branches and twigs to keep their teeth sharp. When they get excited, their body temperature spikes; in drier months this can cause them to trigger forest fires.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME burrows deep underground, melting any boulders in its path with intense flames. Some tunnels left in its wake remain superheated for hours.
author: .izik

entry: The yellow, mud-like substance coating POKENAME's body can reach temperatures comparable to molten lava. Without meaning to, it frequently starts wildfires, forcing it to live in desolate areas.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME balances on its tail to help it reach the higher twigs that it likes to snack on. It sometimes gets brief visions of the future that cause it distress.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are often seen munching on twigs and leaves atop tree branches. They will ignite whatever they are munching on and fling it at potential foes before battling.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME snack on small pieces of twigs, though they are rather picky eaters; they each prefer specific types of wood to snack on. By eating twigs, they fuel their internal flames and ensure the fire they spit out is always strong.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME eat wood over other vegetation, though they prefer to eat softwood most of all. They have strong flames within themselves, which keep them warm and heat up the water they spit out at foes.
author: infinex21

entry: The best place to find a POKENAME is sunbathing on hot sand.  Its large ears act as a heat sink, absorbing the sun's rays to provide POKENAME with fiery energy, but also acting as a vent if POKENAME overheats.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME uses its sensitive ears to feel people's emotions. It is known to eat twigs to power up its teleportation if threatened.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Using their telekinesis, POKENAME snap nutrient-rich branches from the tops of trees to munch on as they explore. Coats made using shed fur from these Pokémon are popular in cold regions because of their light weight and natural warmth.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is very friendly and loyal, but can be difficult to raise. It constantly wants to practice its fire spells, and its zealousness can sometimes lead to things accidentally being set on fire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can ignite its fur in various shades of flame. The color of its fire depends on its mood and how well it is fed.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Always on alert, POKENAME keep their large ears raised to listen in all directions. Their teeth are still growing, so they break up and melt down berries before eating them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The fur-like vines extending from POKENAME's ears are very sensitive. It can hear things from up to a mile away because of them.
author: .izik

entry: Though its body is warm on the outside, its internal temperature can reach up to 800°C. The fires that burn from its ears and tail are excess heat it cannot yet fully control.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME's internal temperature can reach over 350 degrees Fahrenheit. To keep itself safe, it vents hot air through its roomy ears and flame-shaped tail.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME eats twigs to keep itself warm in its icy cold climate, with excess heat escaping from its ears. It prefers finding the twigs itself rather than having them given to it.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME regularly grooms the fur in its ears as a display of pride to its allies. It grows very upset if even a single strand is out of order for too long.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's nose glows red-hot just before it unleashes a powerful fire-based attack. The accumulated heat lets it sense changes in the air, allowing it to react quickly to threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will immediately vent hot air and burn the hand of the person who attempted to grab hold of it. If its rod so much as scrapes against another object, it will immediately combust, even during rain.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME spines exude a viscous toxin that is highly flammable. They can ignite this toxin at will, shaking their head vigorously to scatter their flames as far as possible to scare off rivals.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME munch on small twigs as snacks, which help to keep their internal flames strong. They release some of their excess heat as a warm and soothing aura from their long feelers.
author: infinex21

entry: When it vents heat from its body, its altitude lowers. As a result, when it spits Fire-type moves from its mouth, POKENAME will start sinking to the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Packs of POKENAME cause the ground to tremble as they bound across the savannah. Their hats capture sunlight, which they store to keep warm during cold nights, while their tails release the excess heat.
author: wyzi

entry: Many Trainers attempt pursuing POKENAME through the woods, but they rarely catch up to it. It is theorized that a POKENAME can memorize the location of as many as 300 different hiding places.
author: .realthree

entry: This Pokémon is often seen being carried around by children. It is both cute and easy to care for, with its diet mainly consisting of twigs.
author: pix3l_655

entry: POKENAME dedicates hours to honing its strength and speed every day. When it strikes, its punches are so fast that its fists catch fire.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: When in danger, its muscles function to create tremendous amounts of electrothermic energy. The puffs of embers from its ears may momentarily blind foes.
author: anemonics

entry: It rests in one of the burrows sprawling through the desert, hopping between abandoned desert homes daily. Nomads travel alongside it as part of a mythological tradition, though of what origin and purpose has been lost to time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feeds on twigs, fallen leaves and other decaying plant matter. When threatened, it spouts a flurry of Embers as it attempts to escape.
author: theartemis1

entry: Feathers drop from POKENAME's body as it flies through high winds. The feathers that touch the ground are so hot that they can ignite forest fires upon landing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fangs can heat up beyond the temperature of a commercial furnace. It leaves glowing bite marks on its prey, which continue to smolder long after the attack.
author: .izik

entry: After spotting its prey, POKENAME unleashes a blood-curdling roar before lunging in to bite with its molten-hot fangs. Its scorching bite is said to be strong enough to melt iron.
author: .izik

entry: Spinning in fiery circles, POKENAME performs an intricate dance that mesmerizes those who watch. As it moves, embers flare from its feathered body, creating dazzling displays.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's preferred food is the peppers that grow near deserts. The spicier the food it consumes, the louder the sound bursts it can produce.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are usually solitary, desert-dwelling Pokémon that feed on Bug-type Pokémon and other small prey, but from time to time, they form large groups, allowing them to hunt larger, meatier species.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can set nearby objects alight with a flick of the arm with their dense bark-like armor. As they grow older, grooves form in their armor that resemble ridges of a tree.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shoots small fireballs into the sky when its allies are sad. These balls explode into brilliant displays resembling fireworks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME claims parts of the forest as its own and marks its territory with will-o'-wisps that mark the area's circumference. Those who enter its domain report a number of symptoms, such as hallucinations, heat stroke, and short-term memory loss.
author: dodoowner_

entry: This Pokémon can move extremely quickly by using the heat from its body to propel itself. The smoke around its neck helps vent extra energy and can get as hot as 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
author: torterrable

entry: Some hot springs use POKENAME by having them put their legs in the water and heat them up. This uses up quite a bit of energy, requiring these springs to house many bundles of sticks for POKENAME to eat.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The more dry twigs POKENAME eats, the thicker the smoke that billows from its shell. Its breath smells faintly of charred wood.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME launch themselves from the ground to snap twigs off of trees. Bigger, nutrient-rich branches help their bodies burn brighter and for longer.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: The fluffy tip of POKENAME's tail is the center of its heat production. If it loses the fur there, it has a hard time staying warm enough.
author: .realthree

entry: This adorable Pokémon enjoys eating twigs and branches. The consumed wood strengthens its power of retrocognition, allowing it a clear, untarnished view of the past.
author: beatdoof

entry: The flames within POKENAME's body grow hotter the more kelp it consumes. At peak temperatures, it can melt holes in metal by spitting these flames.
author: .izik

entry: Despite appearing dizzy in combat, POKENAME has complete control over its fiery attacks. Its wobbling seems to grow more intense the hotter its flames become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is in a constant state of overheating, leaving the Pokémon in a semi-conscious state. Its ears and mane give off enough heat to start forest fires.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's ears bounce as it dashes, scattering tiny embers with every step. Its fiery fluff burns hotter the faster it runs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can unleash flames from each of its three heads, reaching temperatures high enough to melt tungsten. When enraged, its combined fiery breath creates a searing whirlwind around it.
author: .izik

entry: The stick on POKENAME's back is a living part of its body. It stretches it like a vine and sets it ablaze to deter predators.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are known to wander aimlessly and cast spells without care for the consequences. This often results in forest fires.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Though rarely seen, POKENAME can be heard rummaging throughout the forests of Johto on warm summer nights. At the brink of dawn, groups of POKENAME gather to celebrate the sunrise with raucous feast and dance.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME uses its stick to conjure flames with psychic powers. It will create trails of fiery wisps to lead trespassers away from its home.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME eat rodent Pokémon and rely on a clever ploy to coax them out of burrows. They shove sticks into burrows and set them on fire. As the fire burns, the burrow residents are drawn out to where POKENAME are waiting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The staff POKENAME wields can channel both fire and electricity. It is greatly weakened if it drops the staff.
author: hophoppip

entry: There are tales of POKENAME in ancient times being the Pokémon that taught humans how to control fire, and to respect it. It is ironic that POKENAME habitats are now at risk due to unprecedented wildfires caused by climate change.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Vine-like sticks grow from the bulb on its back and are used in battle. The more sunlight it absorbs, the hotter their flames burn.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME crackles with static as it sleeps, charging the branch in its tail. When the branch is drawn from its tail, static builds up and sets the tip ablaze.
author: gekkou.

entry: POKENAME has the power to enchant a small object to become fireproof. It is also able to focus moves and spells through a physical medium. In both cases, POKENAME's choice is often a wooden stick.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The trees from which POKENAME gathers the branches it uses for practicing its magical fire are considered sacred to it. Those who harm said trees will be shown the full might of POKENAME's pyrotechnic capabilities.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME's tail continues to grow its entire life, so you can tell how old one is by how many fronds its tail has.  However, the very end is always a bare branch, so that it can channel POKENAME's fire.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in apple orchards in the fall. While the bonfires it starts with its tail are usually warm and inviting to all, they can reach dangerous temperatures if the orchard is threatened.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME's flame-based attacks swirl around its body before being deployed at foes like a spell. They always originate from its beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME excels at ranged and close combat fighting. Using the stick from its tail, POKENAME can light flames and launch them at opponents. Up close, this Pokémon utilizes its claws for slashing and powerful legs for kicking.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME meditates at the center of its lake home, using its psychic abilities to levitate above the water. During this meditation, the surrounding water begins to boil.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME keeps its twig safely tucked away in its tail while stomping about in the mud. Then, once the marsh gases have built up, it swiftly pulls out the twig, and the friction sets it all alight.
author: imaginita

entry: The stick POKENAME carries can be used to move mud from a distance. It hurls mud at travelers who venture too close to its den.
author: .izik

entry: The flames POKENAME produces grow stronger when it senses sadness nearby. Some believe it does this in hopes of cheering the person up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's telekinetic abilities allow them to create a friction from the air to light up their twig. They use it in combat as a catalyst for their abilities.
author: sylia

entry: The flame on the stick reflects POKENAME's emotional state at the time. The more defensive and protective of others it feels, the bigger and hotter the fire burning on the end.
author: sk372

entry: Only twigs plucked from thorny bushes are suitable conduits for its elemental energy. Be careful when you play fetch with POKENAME, it returns what you throw aflame and covered in poisonous saliva.
author: ozydamians

entry: It always has a twig firmly grasped in its prehensile tail. The bonfire it builds with its specially-chosen firewood produces a vibrant rainbow blaze.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME accumulates twigs between tufts of fur, using it as kindling for warmth while searching for food in cold, damp undergrowth. Calls between POKENAME can often be heard at dawn, signaling to others that ideal collectable wood is nearby.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME deftly wields its fiery tail both to attack and to signal the other members of its troupe. It can even aim its fire while hanging from the walls or ceiling.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME can control the intensity of its flames by turning its twig like a knob. At maximum output, these blasts can melt steel within seconds.
author: .izik

entry: It will replace a lost tail stick with an even larger one rather than ask for help retrieving it, to avoid bruising its pride. If the stick is stolen, it furiously launches into battle to confront the thief.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME can direct water it has recently touched using its stick. The water moves in serpentine patterns, defying gravity.
author: .izik

entry: The fur of its tail is so hot that mere friction is enough to set its large stick alight when drawn. It waves this stick and its own feelers around to communicate and to ward off threats.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can release spores from its tail that ignite at a moment's notice. Like a conductor, it directs these flames using the stick held in its mouth.
author: busilisk

entry: POKENAME can be seen performing with street magicians to amaze audiences. They take breaks on nights of the full moon to bask in the moonlight and recharge their magical powers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their flame tipped twig to sense emotions, changing colours as it detects new feelings. In the wild, POKENAME read each others flames to know if everyone is happy. Their groups are tight knit because of this.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: It communicates with members of its pack using a mix of electrical impulses and smoke signals from the stick it always carries. It will channel either intense heat or voltage through its claws to hunt, whatever is most effective against its prey.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME is really warm, so Trainers in cold areas use it to warm their beds. Its twig is usually unlit, but becomes lit when in battle or whenever fire is needed.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's flaming wings trace cryptic patterns in the air, weaving hypnotic embers that lure spirits to its ghostly dance. Mocking its ritual ignites vengeful flames, which cling to offenders as ceaseless, haunting reminders of their disrespect.
author: vhscopyofmeangirls

entry: The loud noise POKENAME produces from its mouth can throw enemies off balance from afar. It then rains fireballs down from the sky to finish them off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are toasty warm, and many cave-dwelling Pokémon cuddle up with it on cold nights. If it becomes ill, it should not be touched without protection, as its gems become hot enough to sear skin instantly.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME constantly search the forests they live in for the perfect stick, which they will carry with them for their entire lives. POKENAME forge special bonds with these sticks, learning to channel their fire through them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME carry a flaming stick with them wherever they go to illuminate the area around them. When confronted with a dangerous Pokémon, they can shoot flaming razor-sharp leaves to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When fighting alongside an ally, the fireballs POKENAME produces from the tip of its twig take on a slightly purple hue. In this state they are hot enough to melt stone.
author: .izik

entry: The tips of POKENAME's fur glow a brilliant orange as it channels fire through its stick. It can wield the flames even after producing them, maintaining perfect control from up to 15 feet away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be seen working with Pokémon rangers, creating safe and controlled burns of forests. The grey coloring of their bubbles is often attributed to ash buildup.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME can be seen wandering near apple orchards, storing fallen fruit in its fur for later meals. In battle, it launches molten sugar at foes.
author: mepp.

entry: The fires they stoke sparkle like stars. At night, they lob magnificent fireballs into the sky to communicate with allies. Meteorologists often mistake these fireballs for meteorites when they rain back down.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME has a hard time pulling its stick out of its tail. Luckily, it can still ignite the wood without removing it by striking it against a rough surface, just as a matchstick.
author: .realthree

entry: With its own twig, POKENAME writes whatever it sees happening in the present through its mind. It is said that this Pokémon can manipulate what is happening in the present depending on what it writes next.
author: beatdoof

entry: The water around POKENAME's body boils when it grows angry. It spits highly heated bubbles at foes when enraged.
author: .izik

entry: By waving its twig through the air, POKENAME envelops its other fist in a brilliant red flame. A single punch from this fist can cause burns that take weeks to heal.
author: .izik

entry: When fighting as part of a team, POKENAME supports its ally with dazzling bursts of flame while cheering them on. This somehow increases its partner's power.
author: .izik

entry: The spear POKENAME carries is filled with potent venom for close combat. When a ranged attack is needed, it can fire a fireball from the tip of the weapon.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carries a stick with its tail to use for practicing magic. It belches up a large amount of bubbles before setting them alight via the stick as its primary way of magic practice.
author: sk372

entry: The water behind POKENAME boils as it swims through lakes. Any plantlife exposed to this water will cook on the spot.
author: .izik

entry: The fluff in POKENAME's ears glows brightly as it begins to charge up an attack. Once it fully charges, the fur ignites and fires off lengthy plumes of flame on either side.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME manipulates flames by waving its bone through the air. Spinning the bone clockwise causes the fire to burn significantly hotter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shows its caring nature towards any wild Pokémon in need, providing them with shelter and healing their wounds with its psychic powers. It dislikes humans though, and will turn any Trainer who disturbs its peace into a Tepig or Spoink.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME has the ability to start a roaring campfire upon its back at will and control whether it burns others or not. This makes it excellent as a traveling companion, particularly in colder regions.
author: sk372

entry: Despite the danger they pose as living thermal reactors, POKENAME are remarkably docile by nature and can regulate their body temperature almost perfectly. Many reptilian Pokémon enjoy the company of POKENAME as a result.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: POKENAME is imbued with both great strength and psychic powers. However, it would rather lounge and use its branch for roasting snacks rather than conjure visions of the future.
author: opossiblymage

entry: Many mountainside villages build shrines dedicated to their local POKENAME. Each night, villagers fill these shrines with food and drink in the hopes that POKENAME will thank them with blessings of good fortune.
author: turron_turron

entry: Traveling between volcanoes, POKENAME appears within a rising spiral of flame. It commands all flames around it, shining in vibrant hues of orange and gold as it glides along the wind.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME live near volcanic mountains where they love the scent of ash. They often start wildfires if there is too much greenery on their mountains.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are highly skilled with fire, but spend most of their time playing with mud and shaping it with their staff. However, they will use fire offensively if threatened.
author: naivetotoro

entry: This Pokémon is commonly portrayed as a companion to witches and wizards alike in many fictional stories, be they good or evil. There are theories, though, that claim POKENAME once were humans that either became Pokémon by choice or by curse.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use latent psychic powers to stir their sticks around the inside of their stony shells, melting down berries and herbs into specialized brews. They spill out their concoctions to offer treats and medicine to smaller Pokémon.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The flames POKENAME carries are capable of burning underwater, lighting the way as they traverse underwater caverns. They can use these flames to defend themselves as well, creating fiery whirlpools to drive away foes.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME spends days using its tusks to meditatively carve a log, with the carvings glowing like embers. While it can use the log like a magic staff to augment its spell-like attacks, it tends to just wallop opponents with the log.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The fur growing from POKENAME's ears is collected and used as insulation for important computer cables, such as the power cord. Its ability to regulate heat sometimes even boosts the efficiency of the device they are connected to.
author: chibitales

entry: Each group of POKENAME develops their own secret code languages. They utilize various methods to communicate: fractals of ice, displays of fire, gashes in boulders, and so on. This makes code-breaking between groups nearly impossible.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME often appear in the wild during autumn, when their body temperature heats up the air. Long ago, this Pokémon was believed to be able to predict the beginning and end of the season. It cleans the air around itself through photosynthesis.
author: te4mst4r.boris

entry: Throughout most of the year, POKENAME is constantly on high alert, guarding its forest. During autumn, when leaves turn red and orange, this allows POKENAME to blend in. It sits patiently, thinking about the future.
author: imaginita

entry: The apples that grow on its back are said to grant the power of foresight when consumed.  POKENAME is highly valued by farmers, who hope to use its power to predict the yield of their crops.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME are almost always found with a twig in their beaks, which they slowly feed on. They will fight by igniting these twigs and waving them around, or they may toss aside their twigs and spit out fireballs.
author: infinex21

entry: Martial artists actively seek out POKENAME to learn the way of the burning branch, a style of armed combat focusing on foreseeing opponents' moves. When not training, these Pokémon can be found in deep meditation.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Should POKENAME notice a predator drawing too close to its nest, it conjures boiling water from the end of its wand. It then lobs this water at the threat to deter it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its wand to telekinetically lift mudballs from the ground and hardens them with its flames. It hurls these at foes with incredible speed to knock them out.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels its budding psychic powers into the stick it carries, letting it create some impressive minor pyrotechnics.  It uses these to impress and protect other small Pokémon it manages to befriend.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME enjoy playing quick games with their Trainers, spinning with glee if their Trainer wins. Should their Trainer lose, POKENAME will pull a prank, often involving making their Trainers' clothes oversized.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME uses their divination abilities to protect their Trainer at all costs including their own life. As a last resort, they creates a fireball that sucks in the threat.
author: sylia

entry: POKENAME can go into an invisible trance, waiting for the perfect time to attack. When it does, it erupts in a rainbow of disorienting colors.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME entices its prey with its dazzling, flaming branches before using its back jaw, disguised as its long, flowing hair, to swallow them whole.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME rubs the tips of its claws on sticks it gathers to set them alight with flame. It uses the torches it creates to ward off predators and bully smaller creatures away from meals it wishes to steal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers up sticks to set alight and gaze into the flames. Within the fire it glimpses potential future disasters, allowing it to work towards preventing the catastrophes from taking place.
author: sk372

entry: The leaves that fall from POKENAME's tree burst into flames as they descend. Some say catching one before it hits the ground brings good luck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gazes into the flame at the tip of its branch to meditate. As it does so, the flame grows larger and larger, not only intensifying POKENAME's focus, but intimidating its opponents.
author: imaginita

entry: Offerings are sometimes made to wild POKENAME to appease its prideful nature. In return, it may grant a vision of the future through the flames of the burning stick it always carries.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME makes its home near waterfalls, redirecting the water toward foes if disturbed. The water is always scalding while being manipulated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME absorb any nearby flames into their crystal balls, storing them for later. When provoked, they can unleash these flames in powerful attacks.
author: santon5512

entry: By staring into the flame upon its stick, it can achieve a state of total serenity that is said to grant it enlightenment. It will avoid fighting and try to end ongoing fights, which is believed to be a desire born of its serene mindset.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often lives in realms like the Dream World where magical phenomena are common, so it gets confused when people are surprised by its tricks. Its warm, fluffy fur makes it great for cuddles, but parents banish it away for its imposing size.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's fur is soft to the touch and retains heat, making them a desired partner during winter. They are also valued for their protectiveness, not hesitating to blast 2,000-degree fire at foes. A popular outlet for them involves melting snowmen.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME sing gleeful melodies as they propel themselves through the sky with dazzling displays of fire. They are curious and creative by nature, collecting plants along their travels to brew new medicines and beverages.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When winter strikes in Lumiose City, POKENAME are lured into the streets. Each of their tails radiates over one hundred degrees of heat, allowing pedestrians to stroll comfortably.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Millennia ago, POKENAME were highly valued, as their aura keeps people warm and radiates comfort and calm. POKENAME can be credited with keeping many villages hopeful for the future in times of hardship.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME carry a burning branch with them at all times, maintaining a disciplined control over their power over fire by keeping it burning as long as possible. As their skill grows, they can maintain a single branch for months.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have been described in legends as Pokémon heralding rebirth, their penchant for wielding burning branches often leading them to burn down forests. The plants that grow from the ash-rich soil are always healthier than those that came before.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's steel bodies act as furnaces internally, releasing heat and smoke from the holes in their heads. If provoked, they will heat their heads up to high temperatures before ramming into foes.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses its glowing staff as bait, hiding in the darkness with only the bright tip exposed. When cave Pokémon investigate, it pounces, stealing and eating any crystals they were carrying.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME juggles its flaming wand alongside other objects that it finds as it dances during combat. This activity appears to serve no purpose beyond distracting the foe and entertaining onlookers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waves its flaming wand in the air while perched in trees to direct others of its kind in producing music with their powerful voices. This can be heard clearly from up to 5 miles away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have doting fans that extol and sing praises for its music. The fiery dances it performs mesmerizes and amazes its loyal fans, who love both music and pyrotechnics.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are coated in fine mycelium fibres that keep their bodies warm through any weather. The fungus is an irritant that causes a burning sensation when eaten, making it popular amongst people who love spicy food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME overflows with enchanted light, with each color of light giving a different effect to those hit by it. When this light is used on its fiery vortexes, they become a catalyst, spreading the magical powers even more.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME enjoy fishing, often using their stick as a fishing pole. Anglers sometimes use them, having them see into the future to see if a particular spot will have a bountiful catch.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Due to its fuzzy sleeves, POKENAME has difficulty bringing its claws to bear. Instead, it attacks by lighting a branch on its magma-hot fur. When alone, it cleans mud from its hair to keep its bright coloration.
author: ghostslythe

entry: By holding its sardonyx crystal above a fire, POKENAME can see every possible future of a person at once refracted across the facets of the jewel. Whichever potential timelines rise to the surface of the gem are the ones most likely to happen.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lives a secluded life in remote locations across the world. It has a gruff, antisocial personality, but it will guide lost travelers it comes across to a safe exit using its flaming staff.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME creates walls of searing fire to deter its foes. Against persistent attackers, it predicts the best location to launch a counterattack and uses flaming walls to direct its enemies to where it will land a decisive strike.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME can divine lava sources simply by closing its eyes and pointing its twig. If lava exists within 1000 feet, it locates it instantly.
author: .izik

entry: Fire blazes from POKENAME's ears and tail due to their overflowing power. In the past, those practicing divination actively sought out POKENAME's wands, believing them to hold the power to influence the future.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME carry talismans to direct their flames in precise strikes, finishing battles in the blink of an eye. They can dispel their flames to disappear into the night, only the flickering sparks from their attacks revealing their location.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME form from bewitched plants in the autumnal harvest. They become very possessive of the inanimate plants that were around them when they form and will try to scare off farmers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A POKENAME's flames can burn as brightly as a star. For reasons yet to be explained, they tend to frantically wave their stick around only hours before intense meteor showers are predicted.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: The mesmerizing flame at the end of POKENAME's tail draws onlookers in. Though those who have stared at it claim that they were on the verge of receiving a vision, nobody has ever reached such a point due to being attacked by the Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: Legends claim that POKENAME was born from the flames and ore nestled deep inside the world's volcanoes. Those who peer into its incandescent flames are said to witness revelations of their futures.
author: mepp.

entry: Wielding a magical wooden staff, POKENAME summons a scrying inferno to divine the future of anyone who catches its interest. The more violently the fire roars and rages, the more inescapable the predicted fate becomes.
author: beatdoof

entry: The branch POKENAME carries acts as a dowsing rod while it swims through coral reefs. This allows it to easily locate the tastiest barnacles to eat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are commonly seen protecting groups of Pokémon they consider weaker than themselves. POKENAME will increase the size of its flames as a scare tactic. These Pokémon are more active during the colder seasons.
author: ruben2309295

entry: The intensity of the flame at the end of POKENAME's wand scales with the electricity stored in its body. After a thunderstorm, it is not uncommon to see the wand blazing due to the amount of charge within.
author: .izik

entry: Popular among doctors throughout history, POKENAME has the ability to detect any composition of chemicals. If a POKENAME meets a patient suffering from poison or illness, it will lower its flames to burn away the pollutant without harming the host.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The branches growing from POKENAME thrive in extremely hot and arid climates, turning absorbed heat into blazing fire. If the wood experiences too much moisture, it can rot and fall off, hindering a POKENAME's ability to survive.
author: ohok3441

entry: When POKENAME gazes into the flame at the end of its wand, its brain cells and IQ multiply. If POKENAME concentrates long enough, it will become smart enough to determine the course of the future.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME gather in groups to develop unique ninjutsu techniques. They primarily focus on using the poisonous bubbles on their back to stun and paralyse foes.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME are deceptively difficult to battle or catch, since when they are threatened they produce bubbles that appear to make their body longer. When these sections are disturbed in any way, they simply dissolve, leaving POKENAME unharmed entirely.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME's bubbles cannot be sheared using shears or machinery. The bubbles are delicate and must be gently scooped up. They're not useful as clothing material.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Don't let its cute expression fool you. This aquatic menace camouflages itself with springy bubbles that lessen the force of attacks. POKENAME's penchant for ambushes makes it especially dangerous in water.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: POKENAME's slick body allows it to smoothly hide in tiny cracks, making it easy to infiltrate homes. If discovered, the pest spits out a high amount of fast-moving bubbles that sting quite a bit on impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lies lazily in rivers, sometimes spitting water at leaves to test its own accuracy. The furthest shot recorded by researchers was 400 ft, showcasing its impressive control and skill with water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME require a consistent source of water and use thick clumps of foam to trap water within their body. POKENAME will return to the water periodically to refresh their store.
author: vic1312

entry: The foamy growth on its back expands when it is happy, releasing a fresh scent that soothes nearby Pokémon. Divers often use POKENAME to find calm waters and avoid dangerous currents.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Its skin is laced in a somewhat poisonous film that deters predators; touching it will result in what feels like a strong buzz. When coiled, it can suddenly lash out at high speeds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its skin is laced in a somewhat poisonous film that deters predators; touching it will result in what feels like a strong buzz. When coiled, it can suddenly lash out at high speeds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Wherever POKENAME goes, a trail of acidic foam is sure to be spotted not long after. Pokémon that can handle the acidic nature sometimes use the foam to help clean their own bodies.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's bubbles have a special ability to block radio waves. It sometimes encases itself with these bubbles to block unwanted transmissions from local networks.
author: soup1900

entry: It protects parts of its body with foamy, delicate bubbles. Namely protected are its claws, which it unveils during battle. It can rapidly cover itself in bubbles and roll into a ball to escape a dangerous foe.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME considers itself the protector of ponds in its forest homes, defending others who would intrude upon them. Though its strength is lacking, none can doubt its staunch conviction.
author: sk372

entry: The bubbles that form on POKENAME's body are filled with microbes from its pond habitat. Contact with these can trigger terrible allergic reactions in humans, including swelling in the joints.
author: .izik

entry: Because they are typically very active and energetic, POKENAME coat themselves in many soft bubbles. These bubbles are made from a flammable fluid that froths when exposed to air, so they may scatter and ignite it to deter threats.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are watchful of their surroundings and quick to leap into action if attacked. Producing foamy bubbles to cover their feathers, this coverage helps dampen the blow of oncoming attacks from foes.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When angry, POKENAME gathers foam on the fin atop its head. Should its anger build too much, the foam spreads across its entire body, making it difficult to walk.
author: .izik

entry: The skin on POKENAME's abdomen is especially thin, making it useful for absorbing moisture from the ground on dry days. To protect its abdomen, it secretes a coat of bubbles to cover it.
author: hophoppip

entry: When POKENAME senses someone nearby is irate, it produces foam from its body. Many claim that holding this foam with bare hands is enough to put a smile on anyone's face.
author: .izik

entry: The false eyes on its "hat" frighten predators away. It adores rainy weather, and will dance happily across puddles.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME cloak themselves in sparkling bubbles to ensure that they stay clean. They gracefully glide along the froth, filling the air around them with bubbles before they warp away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME applies adhesive bubbles to itself for protection and to surfaces to give itself footholds. It uses its tongue to precisely apply its bubbles from a distance; its saliva is oily, preventing the bubbles from sticking to it.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its second set of jaws as a decoy while it lies or rests within water; it utilizes decoy tactics so it may consume algae and weeds in peace. The bubbles coating its large jaws provide an extra layer of protection and make them buoyant.
author: infinex21

entry: While sleeping, a large bubble forms at the top of POKENAME's sprout. If popped, it will wake in a daze.
author: .izik

entry: The bubbles that form on POKENAME's back fill with a delightfully scented gas. This comforts its young when they fall ill or become irritable.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secretes numerous flexible bubbles from its rear end. Its extraordinary jumping abilities allow it to scale sheer cliffs extremely quickly.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: POKENAME swings its tail around in battle to block attacks with the bubbles that grow from it. It uses ceilings and walls to launch aerial attacks.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: POKENAME covers its hands, feet, and tail, with the bubbles secreted from the top of its head. It then quickly rushes the opponent with attacks from every limb.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: It spews out protective bubbles whenever it believes it is in danger. When a Trainer refuses to listen to its desires, it shoots a burst of bubbles to demonstrate its frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers sea glass from the deepest parts of the ocean. It uses the bubbles from its wings to clean the glass before adding it to its collection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in underwater caves during the evening. If threatened by predators like Huntail, it releases torrents of foam to obscure its escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME constructs a Froakie disguise to capitalize on the Pokémon's popularity beyond even frog enthusiasts. Its aptitude for jumping is limited due to its small legs, but it can use its claw to propel itself into the air to mimic its disguise.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME like children and they enjoy blowing bubbles, just to watch them laugh. If it can detect a child who is sadder than the others, it will pay special attention to it.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: It generates bubbles from a small spout on its head to help keep its skin moisturized while on land. POKENAME enjoys playing with others by spraying them with these foamy bubbles.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME feels threatened, it surrounds itself in a mass of bubbles. These bubbles are charged with electricity, but touching them only causes a minor static shock.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME secretes a thin, bubbly foam from their bud that replenishes itself whenever any part is scooped off. The foam prevents them from getting dehydrated. Despite its carefree nature, POKENAME is wary of its surroundings.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME is covered in mucus that it pushes air into, protecting it in a bubble. It acts sweet and happy, but this is a façade to get close to its prey.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME acts childlike and innocent, but this is purely an act. It waits until its prey is comfortable before attacking with rapid-firing water shurikens.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: When speeding after prey, POKENAME fires bubbles that cling to their body to slow them down. Once within range, it bites with enough force to dent a truck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secretes bubbles from its thick skin and uses psychic powers to launch them at the opponent. The bubbles don't do much harm, however.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME are not covered in crystals, despite their appearance. Instead, they secrete bubbles which harden in clumps that shine just like jewels, whilst making them unappealing to predators like Sableye.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME loves to splash around in knee-deep puddles. By throwing itself on its back and spinning, it playfully hardens the back of its shell further with each throw.
author: thezekrom

entry: POKENAME have protective natures, and will use their bubbles to create cover, allowing weaker Pokémon to flee. POKENAME can make an endless amount of these bubbles and can sometimes be found at birthday parties entertaining children.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME hates drying out, so it uses its large ears to dissipate excess heat. It launches bubbles from its mouth to hunt prey.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME will use the stick they carry to mold the bubbles they produce into clothing. Groups of POKENAME will put on small fashion shows to show off their bubble outfits.
author: drcew
