entry: It acts easygoing as it coats its body in delicate bubbles, but it is always observant. When provoked, it launches bubbles with blinding speed to overwhelm its foes.
author: torterrable

entry: POKENAME secretes numerous bubbles from its chest and back, creating an awesome frothy scarf to hide its face.  Unfortunately, it usually forgets to hide the rest of its body.
author: imaginita

entry: The foam produced at the end of POKENAME's tail is extremely hot. Even so, it doesn't burn POKENAME, so it tends to be careless with it.
author: .realthree

entry: It's common for heart plushies to be blue or adorned with ribbon, taking inspiration from this Pokémon. Among surfers, seeing POKENAME is a sign of true love to come.
author: deelee2020

entry: POKENAME clad themselves in frothy bubbles for insulation as they fly. If they spot a Pokémon in danger, they will courageously swoop down to aid them.
author: infinex21

entry: By punching the air, POKENAME releases bursts of bubbles from its fists. These bubbles cling to foes and slow them considerably.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to play with the bouncy bubbles on its tail, but it always keeps a watchful eye on its surroundings. If it senses danger, it can jump up to eight feet in the air to avoid attacks and make its escape.
author: skittytales

entry: When fighting alongside an ally, POKENAME releases bursts of multicolored bubbles to cheer them on. This somehow encourages them enough to make their attacks stronger.
author: .izik

entry: The bubbles POKENAME spits frequently burst into flashes of sparks. It uses these to frighten others away from its pond home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release toxic bubbles from their mouths after digesting a meal, a byproduct of their digestive system. These bubbles have a putrid scent that drives away most Pokémon, allowing them to hoard berries for themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It secretes flexible bubbles from the hump on its back.  These flexible bubbles reduce incoming damage, so POKENAME sometimes doesn't even realize it has been hit.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME continually dribbles a cloud of bubbles which can be blasted to entrap foes, allowing for either a quick escape or follow-up pinches. Its hardiness has helped it to survive and spread to multiple regions.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME secretes a pliable film of bubbles to protect its meaty fists. Should this padding be damaged in battle, it will fly into a blind rage.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME floats near the ocean surface, releasing toxic bubbles at prey. Once stunned, it strikes with lashing tentacles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release bubbles in their wake as they roam through fields of grass. Sometimes, they chase each other in circles as they try to pop each other's bubbles, leading to the entire herd moving in a loop.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its tongue is covered with sea foam that allows it to filter impurities from the water. POKENAME feeds on algae to strengthen the shell that protects it from attacks by other Pokémon living in the ocean.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Using its pendulum as a focus for its power, it psychically manipulates water. POKENAME spends many hours a day silently honing its abilities.
author: hophoppip

entry: Their strong legs allow them to leap between rocks along the shore. When threatened, POKENAME will cloak themselves in foamy bubbles to appear larger.
author: santon5512

entry: The large bones that POKENAME toss at foes are so big that they must throw them with both hands. Their slow yet hefty boomerangs break steel beams with a single pass.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The only way to effectively attack a POKENAME is by attacking the main body, as they have wings made out of a bubbly foam that deform and warp around attacks when struck. Their barrage of bubbles makes landing a precise attack difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its icy breath generates a thick veil of fog that conceals its movements at sea. The ring of bubbles lining its shell is a sign of good health; when POKENAME falls ill, the bubbles begin bursting one by one until it fully recovers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will travel swiftly through forests, getting detritus stuck within their gelatinous form. They will form bubbles of foam around the offending pieces of material. They occasionally discard long chains in places rich in detritivores.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered in millions of tiny bubbles it produces to regulate its body temperature. They cluster on sea cave walls, making distinct popping noises as they shift subtly in their sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a nimble Pokémon that can scale a 600 meter tower in a few seconds. It enjoys climbing to the top of tree canopies to croak songs into the sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are incredibly dexterous Pokémon that can conjure and throw water shuriken in a couple of seconds. They are also quite nimble, as they can dodge many attacks with split-second reaction speeds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are very mischievous; they constantly move their Trainer's belongings or squirt them with water. However, if another Pokémon threatens them, they will stand and face the threat, no matter the danger to them.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME trap air within their fur to enable them to breathe underwater. The air bubbles escape slowly, forming a trail behind them reminiscent of a tail.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have sharp vision that allows them to notice minute changes in the swampy water around them. Their precise pecks allow them to snatch up aquatic Pokémon from murky water, securing their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's keen eyesight allows it to effortlessly navigate its swamp habitat, even when it is filled  with dense fog. When hunting, it plunges its long neck into the water to grab prey.
author: mepp.

entry: Even though POKENAME fangs are full of venom, they are not sharp enough to pierce through scales or hide. They instead spray a caustic foam that clings to their prey to melt through their defenses.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because its fangs are too dull to inject venom, POKENAME will instead spray alkaline bubbles at its prey, slowly melting them. It covers its den in these bubbles as a line of defense.
author: mistymagius

entry: It channels its energy to forge electric shurikens, hurling them at enemies to leave them paralyzed. POKENAME builds its hideout among the trees that grow near bodies of water.
author: fiordaliso

entry: According to Kalosian legend, POKENAME were used by wizards to change the weather on a whim. These stories describe POKENAME using their beard of bubbles to make clouds and downpours.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME practice throwing leafy shuriken at targets to improve their accuracy. They create small targets for themselves by encasing leaves in bubbles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME leaps from tree to tree, surveying entire forests as their designated protector. From above, it pelts those it deems a threat with bubble-coated seeds spat out at high volume and rapid speeds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly proficient with ranged combat, as they can knock down a can from across a football field. Their bubbles and razor-sharp leaves give them many options on how to take down foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eat foods that contain seeds, keeping the seeds separate and stored within their mouths. They coat these seeds in a flammable fluid that froths like foam when exposed to air, then spit them at their targets.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME leaves foam in its wake as it swims through rivers at high speeds. It keeps its fin above the water to assert dominance over others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: The bubbles on POKENAME's body are filled with incredibly foul-smelling water. It tosses them onto the shoreline of its pond to deter humans from drawing too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their tails to hang from branches as they observe others; if they think they have been spotted, they can change hues and blend in. Using their long tongues, they retrieve nuts and stones to throw at their foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sprays extremely hot suds across the battlefield to slow foes. It prefers to maintain distance, using its incredible acrobatics to keep opponents at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blows up the bubbles on its tail and neck to make it look bigger. It can scale a cliff of up to 2000 feet in a minute's time.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME has a unique fighting style that utilizes the foam produced from its head. It trains constantly to push its techniques further.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME fancies itself as an honorable warrior-ninja in training. It leaps to the defense of other Pokémon, even if it seems unnecessary, spitting out small bubbles that travel close to the speed of a bullet.
author: sk372

entry: Should POKENAME encounter another of its kind, they will blow bubbles while maintaining eye contact. The one who blows the largest bubble without popping it is declared the winner.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME takes advantage of its cuteness and elegance to receive small objects as gifts from Trainers. These are then loaded into its bubble ribbons so that when it swings them around, it can launch projectiles at foes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME surround themselves with a nearly transparent bubble that protects them while they play pranks on other Pokémon. Whenever they need a quick escape, POKENAME can float or swim away to avoid consequences.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It surrounds its opponent with a flurry of bubbles, some of which stick to and slow down the opponent. Afterwards, it releases a shock towards the opponent, which ricochets from bubble to bubble in close proximity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers and consumes trash floating on the water's surface. Once it eats enough, it sleeps face-first in the water while drifting across a lake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates a mushroom-shaped bubble on its back to create visual distortions to distract predators. If the bubble pops, it scuttles into hiding until it can safely rebuild it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: With the precision of a marksman, POKENAME can reliably shoot darts made out of bark to subdue foes from long range. These darts are less effective at close range, so their heavy, oaken armor soaks up the damage instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The shell covering POKENAME is sturdy but smooth. When it encounters others of its kind, it uses its shell like a sled to start friendly races through shallow rivers.
author: thezekrom

entry: An incredible tactician, POKENAME waves its bubble-covered stick in the air to communicate with its allies. It's great at devising battle strategies.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: Becoming more skillful than Froakie but retaining its small stature, POKENAME defends others with bubble-coated projectiles thrown in rapid succession. POKENAME doubles its efforts if it feels a foe isn't taking it seriously.
author: sk372

entry: The bubbles around the necks of POKENAME became soapy in consistency following fusion. It uses its bubbles to slow down fleeing prey.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is so agile and speedy that it's hard to follow with the naked eye.  In most cases, the only sign that a POKENAME has passed by is the slightest trail of cloud-like froth in its wake.
author: imaginita

entry: In battle, POKENAME peers its head above the surface of water, shoots a highly precise Water Gun, and then quickly retreats back underwater. It is too swift and nimble to properly study its lower body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME launches heart-shaped bubbles at foes filled with a special liquid that suppresses violent urges. Many foes are left confused after being pacified by the bubbles, giving POKENAME an opportunity to strike.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Should POKENAME spot an ally in combat, it blows bubbles to hop upon and travels to their side. It then performs a rehearsed cheer to encourage its friend while bouncing on the bubble.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can fire projectiles from the hump on its back. These bubble-covered pebbles are impressively accurate, though scientists are unsure how they came to be in POKENAME's hump in the first place.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME defend themselves against predators by firing pearls with expert precision. They constantly produce pearls to replace the ones they fire, making them a popular choice for harvesting pearls from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The foam that floats out of POKENAME's tail and neck contains a chemical that combusts when it makes contact with any carbon compounds. If you come across any wet spots in the rocky lands where POKENAME live, it is best not to touch them.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME release a sticky foam from their mouths that clings to feathers and fur. Whenever they are upset, they take to the sky to spew foam over their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates bladed daggers out of water to fight against its foes. These aquatic weapons are thrown with enough force to shatter stone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME relies on its lightweight bubbles to keep itself afloat as it gallops across water. Its bubbly mane can be set aflame to create photogenic shots.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are playful creatures that enjoy creating bubbles and playing with their Trainer. Whenever they are bored, they shoot bubbles at their Trainer with remarkable accuracy to get attention.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME operates as a ninja patrolling hot springs and volcano areas. It breathes out thick plumes of steam to hide its movements, striking unseen with quickly thrown shurikens made of boiling-hot water.
author: sk372

entry: When enemies swarm on POKENAME, it bristles its fur to release hundreds of spikes made of compressed water to counterattack. It covers foes in slime using the tongue around its neck to set them up to become severely electrocuted in its next attack.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME swings from tree to tree, using shuriken created from its own sweat to knock loose Nanab Berries. It gathers them in great quantities as gifts for its allies.
author: .izik

entry: Using rough river rapids as cover, POKENAME tracks unsuspecting prey while gathering energy for an ambush. It breaks the surface with a mighty jump, throwing a Water Shuriken before landing an armor-piercing kick.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are frugivorous, eating berries and storing the juice in their shells to both survive and to fight. They purposefully leave the seeds inside, as the shurikens they form with the juice are granted a powerful abrasive effect.
author: slavman9057

entry: The incredibly hot tongues emerging from POKENAME's shells can cause burns on contact. It whips them at great speed during combat to both damage and grapple foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tongue is covered with small poison glands. It immobilizes prey by wrapping them with its tongue, weakening them, and then swallowing them whole.
author: acid_pen

entry: With lightning-fast reflexes, POKENAME darts around the battlefield and strikes from all angles. The shuriken at the base of its tail acts as a propeller, allowing it to swim underwater.
author: chibitales

entry: In battle, POKENAME uses its dexterous tongue to hurl electrically charged Water Shurikens at its opponent. Depending on the amount of charge stored, a single hit can down an enemy over ten times its size.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME use ionised water as a means of attack, floating low over water surfaces and using their magnetic powers to create water shurikens. They are cumbersome in the air, however, only able to use their powers to float or to attack.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: They swiftly and adeptly use their long tongue to lick anything in sight to determine its edibility. It appears they can voluntarily switch off their sense of taste and touch in order to use its tongue to fight foes such as the foul and gooey Muk.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's tongue is directly connected to an electricity-generating organ in its torso. When it unfurls it from its scarf-like position, it channels that energy to fling out shuriken made of electricity and water mixed together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a cunning Pokémon, nearly impossible to hit thanks to its unmatched agility. It can curl into a ball in an instant, shielding its weak points with its shell, and hurls sand bombs to hinder foes while executing swift evasive maneuvers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are very agile and stealthy, maneuvering through trees gracefully even when being chased by foes. When challenged to a fight, they use their prehensile tongue-scarf to immobilize foes before countering with Water Shuriken.
author: blaizegamer

entry: Its saliva is like tree resin, which covers its long tongue to protect it. POKENAME uses its long tongue to swing between tree branches as it patrols its territory, searching for intruders and for fresh food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME conjure weapons made of water to cut through their opponents. For long range attacks, they rely on a mix of razor-sharp leaves and water shuriken to finish off a battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in marshes, seeking to protect the small Pokémon that live there. They use their sharp tails to slice through reeds and expose hunters.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME use their peculiar tongues to lure in and ensnare their prey, as well as to fling water and fire. They often rest atop tree branches so they may catch any threats by surprise.
author: infinex21

entry: This stealthy Pokémon takes advantage of high vantage points to ambush prey like a ninja. Once a target is within striking range, POKENAME leaps from its hiding spot and drop kicks the target with its powerful legs.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: With its agile grace and blistering kicks, POKENAME is considered by most to be an apex ninja. To aid in sneaking, it can produce steam from its feet to create cover.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME watches over areas where Mudkip gather, working as a quiet protector from the shadows. It takes care of potential dangers by flinging shurikens made of muddy water.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME extends its tongue from deep beneath rivers to snatch prey and fruit from above the surface. Its tongue grows longer the older it gets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's speed and size make it excellent at doing hit-and-run tactics. It gathers up muddy water to form into dirty shurikens to throw at foes as a way to both injure and blind them.
author: sk372

entry: The surface of POKENAME's body is enveloped by a thin, sticky film.  From this mucus, it makes shuriken that can cut cleanly through steel cables.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME has a superior sense of balance and agility, somehow managing to balance on lily pads across its lake home. It maintains this even through stormy weather, bellowing angrily and spitting mud at any human who disturbs it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME moves with the swiftness and grace of a ninja. It uses psychic powers to cast illusions to better hide itself, making it even more capable of stealthily dealing with opposition.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME seen with a skirt made of water are known for being more aquatically inclined. While mobile on land, its true speed and skill becomes most prevalent once it's underwater.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use both their superb agility and skin pigments to appear nigh-undetectable in the darkness of night. Even when eyes can hardly see, they use the sensitive tongues to analyze their surroundings.
author: entomoxie

entry: It is said that no one can hide from POKENAME, even those it cannot see, due to its innate ability to sense aura. It uses this ability to hide from dangerous foes or hunt its prey.
author: blaizegamer

entry: POKENAME attempts to teach itself discipline and fight more tactically in combat. To that end, it covers its mouth with its long tongue, to help prevent itself from falling to its instincts and resorting to simply biting opponents.
author: sk372

entry: Nicknamed the desert Sand Sharpedo, POKENAME circles shallowly underground, feeding off the water from cactus roots. When its dorsal fin above ground hits a Trainer or Pokémon, it explodes from the sand, confronting foes with solid water scythes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: A POKENAME acts as a sort of traveling dojo for Froasaur, helping to teach them the art of ninjutsu. If anyone threatens the Froasaur inside, the POKENAME will rapidly spin the water shuriken on its back and launch razor-sharp droplets.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The pink leaves on the tree on POKENAME's back become littered with snow-white blossoms in spring. It uses its long tongue to eat the blossoms as they fall.
author: .izik

entry: It shows great resourcefulness in the face of danger, utilizing its sensitive tongue and fiery tail to detect its enemies, then modify its shuriken attacks for maximum effectiveness.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME crafts a sword and scabbard out of a special hardened mucus secreted from the top of its head. In battle, it wields the sword with its tongue and can effectively block and attack opponents behind it.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: POKENAME secretes a special saliva that helps retain body heat and reduce drag in the water. Prior to hunting, it uses its tongue to coat itself in this slick substance.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME flings shuriken at cruise ships to distract patrons during their meals. It then uses its long tongue to snatch their food before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME surprises many a foe with blazing speed and agility in spite of its heavy girth and size. From its flippers, it fires off a multitude of large and sharp water shuriken to keep its opponents at bay.
author: sk372

entry: It throws stars made out of electricity and water. The more nutritious its diet, the faster its throwing speed.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Despite honing great illusions and ninjutsu skills, POKENAME has a fatal flaw: its tongue. If discovered mid-disguise, it will lash out with it before retreating.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are swift and stalwart protectors of others. The saliva of their tongues is a powerful soothing and numbing agent. They utilize this saliva to tend to small injuries, though it can be used to quell rowdy individuals.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are known for being incredibly fast both in the air and on the surface of the water. The fastest POKENAME in the world are hard to even see because they use their speed to deliberately disappear or deceive onlookers.
author: entomoxie

entry: This slippery shinobi shows a strange interest in shiny items, such as gold and jewels. POKENAME has also been seen nearby Fuchsia City.
author: saberman3885

entry: POKENAME is believed to be the subject of several legends describing a mysterious Pokémon causing havoc in the dead of night. Its exact origins are a mystery.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME uses its long tongue to pull itself around quickly, given how heavy its body is; it will also use this tactic to slam into its foes. It withdraws its tongue to coat it in a sticky, corrosive saliva in order to quickly eat small metal scraps.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite being composed almost entirely of water, POKENAME can slice through steel cables. If angered, calming it down is wiser than hiding - walls won't stop it, and it moves incredibly fast.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The connective rotation of POKENAME's two halves draws in water from nearby sources. This causes it to grow in size, strength, and speed, both halves able to fly around like twin shuriken in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is rarely spotted at rest, often maneuvering at high speeds in an effort to protect the flame on its tail. When threatened, it hurls a flurry of small but volatile throwing stars formed from compressed water, buying itself time to escape.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are typically less food driven than other Sableye fusions. This is because they make their own diamonds to eat by spraying compressed water into rocks and sediment.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Despite its size and weight, POKENAME is an expert climber, able to crawl up the jungle trees with its small claws or stick to wet river cliffs with its finger pads. That way, this stealthy predator sneaks up to its prey, catching it with its tongue.
author: milchik

entry: This odd aquatic creature hides in coral reefs. What look like coral branches on its head are actually sensitive organs that detect chemicals in the water around them.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's long tongue is incredibly sticky and can ensnare prey from up to 10 feet away. Once captured, it bites down with enough force to crush a ship's hull.
author: .izik

entry: A master of ambush tactics, POKENAME is both silent and lightning-fast underwater. Several reports claim to see POKENAME vanish mid-chase only to reappear in front of its prey, delivering a devastating Bite.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME feeds on minerals in order to sustain itself and grow. It acquires these minerals by drinking cave water that they are dissolved in, using its long tongue to lick clean what it wouldn't normally be able to reach.
author: fireblade141

entry: Despite its bulky appearance, POKENAME can weave around opponents masterfully, disarming and disabling foes before they can attack. It can shape water into any form of fortification or weapon to aid in its defense, though it prefers shurikens.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME's confidence in its skills is enough that it prefers to play with its opponents rather than secure victory. It flings numerous water shuriken from the end of its stick to force its foe to dodge endlessly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can react so fast that it is believed it can see the future. It wields its nunchakus with incredible precision and speed. Despite its unfriendly looks, it is incredibly loyal once it takes a liking to someone.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: The shuriken POKENAME creates from water can grow up to three times the size of its body. The larger they become, the less control it has over them.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its best efforts, POKENAME is somewhat slower than the average Pokémon. To compensate, it releases thick steam from its body in large bursts, masking its presence from foes in a pinch.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME uses its sticky tongue to scale cliffs and walls. As it does so, it leaves scorch marks behind, as its saliva causes a chemical reaction that raises the temperature.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME suppresses a foe's violent urges by shooting heart-shaped bubbles at them, the liquid cooling their body and calming their mind. It is said that these bubbles can calm even the angriest of Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can create dazzling displays of light to cheer on their friends by having electrified water shuriken ricochet around an arena. They have to be careful not to interfere with a match, as these shuriken can create stray sparks that linger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are able to predict the future based on the patterns of flowing water. They utilize their spoons as markers to keep track of their readings over time, cross-referencing if outcomes they foresaw will still come true.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Instead of agility and stealth, POKENAME prefer fighting their battles through raw strength. To train their muscles, they carry around a large ice ninja star weighing an average of 50 lbs.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Poison coats POKENAME's long tongue: a single lick can leave some flailing on the floor in pain. Although it has the ability to melt into another's shadow and stay perfectly hidden, there are several cases of playful and social POKENAME, too.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A constant stream of smoke rises from the seed on its back, sometimes containing toxic substances. POKENAME must eat dozens of berries each day to keep its body temperature high, or it risks falling ill.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME detects a threat, it releases a thick smoke from its tail and vanishes into it without a trace. It feeds primarily on Berries found at the base of trees in the forests it inhabits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body radiates enough heat to cause the ground near it to steam and ignite. It can explode in a burst of energy and scalding steam, powerful enough to leave a small crater behind.
author: sk372

entry: The smoke created from POKENAME's weapon reflects its emotional state. When threatened, the smoke thickens and shrouds the area in an black haze.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME release a hot smoke that wicks moisture from the area around them. They are sensitive to moisture in the area, so by constantly releasing smoke they can adjust the humidity in the air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The clouds of smoke emanated from POKENAME have an ashy and earthen scent to them. The smell has been used by some to help Pokémon from volcanic areas feel more comfortable when away from their natural habitat.
author: sk372

entry: Coal mining facilities are a frequent target of POKENAME raids as they barrel through trying to find their favorite food: coal. Their blazing hot, rocky armor makes them slow, but tough to repel.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's powerful, superheated drill can power through any terrain. When its love for drilling is exhausted, it will reroute its energy into the tip of its horn, exploding any kind of rock.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Steam within the shell keeps POKENAME's tentacles moist and able to move it around. Because the steam escapes as it moves, it only moves in short bursts, lest it risk its limbs drying out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's stomachs burn at 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit, often being used as furnaces by blacksmiths. POKENAME will often house Rolycoly in their stomachs, giving them sustenance and protection.
author: santon5512

entry: The expulsion of smoke that propels POKENAME through the water takes the form of large back fins. It typically roams around the oceans near volcanic islands, particularly those with still-active volcanoes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME release clouds of smoke from the red-hot vents on their wings to scare away predators. At night, the vents on their back glow and create the illusion of a menacing monster.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The steam vented from POKENAME's ears can be manipulated to form solid barriers. Excess smoke pours from its core, creating a constant haze around it.
author: evilgammon

entry: Smoke billows out from its head at all times. POKENAME Trainers are advised to keep it in its Poké Ball for the safety of their lungs.
author: hophoppip

entry: Before battle, POKENAME's tail flame burns white-hot. It spits blinding smoke to obscure its foe, then strikes with searing embers.
author: .izik

entry: Domestication of this Pokémon is difficult, as it has a short temper and is prone to run amok over the slightest inconvenience. Once it calms down, it expresses deep remorse over its lost temper.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is unable to dig up coal for itself, so other Pokémon and people must hand it food for its survival. The soot it creates pollutes the rivers and oceans that it lives in, making them unlivable for any Pokémon except for other Magikarp.
author: soup1900

entry: When under attack, POKENAME releases plumes of thick smog. This smoke contains a weak poison that irritates the skin and eyes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME rampages through towns, turning them into ashy, smoke-filled wastelands. The Eruption it launches can completely melt away entire neighborhoods in one blow.
author: soup1900

entry: As it consumes coal and other materials, puffs of smoke rise from its head. The clouds shift into the shapes of other Pokémon, even mimicking their behavior before dissipating.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tail holds a fiercely burning fire. When in peak health, the flames glow brilliantly inside its rock-hard tail casing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates its smoke by feeding off of images of coals inside of computer systems. However, if it can't discern the image format of the picture of coal, it will refuse to eat the image even if it hasn't eaten in days.
author: soup1900

entry: During battle, POKENAME blows thick smoke from its nostrils to obscure itself and gain an advantage over its foes. It prefers to live in caves rich with coal and other minerals.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME blows out lots of soot as it grows larger, meaning it must continuously eat and burn coal to survive. This constant use of energy and need for coal is why so few exist in the wild.
author: soup1900

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's body regularly vent out large amounts of steam in order to regulate its temperature. Seeing it majestically swim through lava in the volcanic regions it inhabits is said to be a sign of good fortune.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME enjoy living on mountainous remote islands rich with coal. They create smoke signals to guide lost sailors away from dangerous rocks or violent storms.
author: soup1900

entry: One piece of coal a day is enough to keep this Pokémon fed. It will nibble on the coal all day while lounging on a cloud of smoke held together with its psychic powers.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can photosynthesize just by feeding off the energy and fumes it gets from burning coal within its body. For this reason, it can still unleash powerful Solar Beams.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's preferred habitats are warm waters near beaches, only going on land to eat coal. Despite having strong jaws, POKENAME prefer to avoid conflict on land, emitting smog before running back into water.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME often bully smaller Pokémon into collecting food for them. When irritated, they rapidly expel heat, causing ambient temperatures to soar upwards of 50°C.
author: turron_turron

entry: POKENAME's threads can radiate warmth, even in the coldest of climates. They are often used to line the inside of expensive Sleeping Bags for mountaineers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME makes nests atop volcano cliffs because the high temperatures help incubate its eggs. After the eggs hatch, it feeds its chicks molten rocks until they are able to fly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives near volcanoes and eats molten rocks. Contact with water rapidly reduces its body temperature, so it will send out a pulse of electricity to vaporize and avoid contact with water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies by emitting smoke and hot gas from vents in its stony body. It will immediately stop flying if it sees that its smoke is causing someone distress, even if it would injure itself by doing so.
author: staghorn

entry: For POKENAME, having a dirty coat is a sign of good health. The soot in its coat keeps pesky bug Pokémon like Joltik away.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME billow out smoke that's lighter than air, allowing them to drift along the wind. They scatter trace amounts of ash into soil to act as fertilizer, helping plants grow strong even under intense heat.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME produces a white smoke that absorbs moisture, which effectively neutralizes water used against it. It is known to wander beaches and lakes where it absorbs the beauty of the natural world.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME pumps out white smoke from its body, which absorbs moisture from anything it touches. It can be found near lakes where it admires the scenery for long hours at a time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is weak on its own, so it relies on smoke signals to communicate with its flock. The shape of the smoke it emits from its tail warns its flock of specific dangers.
author: mepp.

entry: If POKENAME engages in overly complex reasoning or calculations, the headpiece on its head emits thick plumes of black smoke. It tends to live in volcanic regions, where it uses its patience and wisdom to guide and assist younger Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is highly intelligent and acts as a tutor to younger Pokémon in the wild, using telepathy to instruct them on survival tactics. The smoke from its head gets denser with every thought it has.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME's developing body causes it to create an excessive amount of steam vented from within its shell. The constant production and subsequent expulsion of steam leaves it tired and lethargic.
author: sk372

entry: Fueled by the burning coal it finds on volcanic islands, POKENAME nurtures a volcanic bulb on its back that releases bursts of fiery pollen.
author: zgaroff

entry: POKENAME is a gentle giant living a very sedentary lifestyle in volcanic regions, usually not far from human civilization. It is friendly enough that it even allows others to use its hot, steaming body as a makeshift sauna.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live on foggy mountain peaks where the mist helps keep their body temperature down. They are easily excitable and, if well fed, can cause an area to heat up rapidly to uncomfortable levels.
author: chibitales

entry: The hardened steel of POKENAME's fists also houses its thermal energy. Being punched by it hurts, but its grasp is so much worse.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Due to the shell over its magma-like body, POKENAME rarely moves. It sticks its head out from the holes in the shell in order to feed and vent excess steam from its pores.
author: sk372

entry: It is one of the slowest-moving Pokémon recorded; a POKENAME moving at top speed for 24 hours would travel only a scant ten feet at best.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will use anything it can find to fuel the fire in its shell, causing the smoke it exhales to be heavily toxic. It is a reclusive Pokémon, hiding away in volcanic regions where no one will disturb it.
author: mistymagius

entry: A POKENAME can drag loads as heavy as trucks while burning coal inside its rock-hard hide to build pressure. When it charges, superheated smoke blasts from its nostrils, releasing the stored energy.
author: moga6

entry: POKENAME's eggs are always perfectly boiled hot spring eggs. POKENAME is extremely popular in Lavaridge Town, due to its hot springs association.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It carries a very heavy shell upon its back, with steam pouring from openings in its body due to the heat that builds up when it moves. Its Body Slam attacks utilize its heavy shell to crush and flatten foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME bounce about on their tail, which nearly constantly emits a clean, white cloud of smoke and ash. This is due to their incredibly high internal temperature. POKENAME that have poor diets may have darker, less clean-looking smoke.
author: vic1312

entry: The steam emanating from POKENAME is rumored to give visions of one's future, so people get steam baths made by it to receive prophecies. It reads their minds, then feeds off of their happy emotions when it puts positive outcomes into their heads.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME spends its time in the mountains attempting to use its magnetism to gather coal. Unfortunately, coal is not magnetic, and it ends up with loads of other minerals instead. POKENAME then trades these minerals with miners in exchange for coal.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME inhabits volcanic regions, feasting on a variety of minerals. When threatened, it spews heavy plumes of smoke from the holes in its palms.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME loiter around coal mines with ethical employment practices, gathering leftover coal. It is said that they can detect strife and don't burn coal mined by mistreated workers. Miners carry tokens depicting POKENAME as an icon of good luck.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME possesses incredible agility. As it sprints, the rushing air causes its internal furnace to burn hotter, venting  thick plumes of smog from its ears and tail like a speeding steam engine.
author: ambrosia04

entry: Its tail is strong enough to hold up its heavy body, though it vents twice as much steam and smoke when it does this. By withdrawing into its shell and expelling heat and fire from its tail, it can propel itself with the speed of a rocket.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME regulates internal body temperature through the feather-like vents on its head to avoid overheating. This Pokémon is often seen joyfully eating charcoal.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can consume various organic and inorganic materials to maintain its internal flames. The type and quality of the food can be seen in the smoke as some foods can cause the smoke to contain larger amounts of ash and sparks.
author: corra_universe

entry: This Pokémon spends the majority of its day in search of coal to fuel its fire. When it feels threatened, POKENAME will exhale a cloud of black smoke before using its powerful legs to jump to a safer location.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME are often utilized at rail yards to quickly lift up and move around train cars and locomotives. As long as POKENAME are fed lots of coal, they can push a loaded 10-car train off the tracks to their destination without sweat.
author: soup1900

entry: Its umbrella radiates heat to keep it warm while shielding its body from volcanic ash in the air. It's known for being elusive, walking out from the smokescreen it billows, and vanishing into those same clouds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME nest near the warm cliffs of active volcanoes. They release trails of smoke from their backs constantly.
author: mepp.

entry: These underground Pokémon propel themselves with heat and smoke, both of which come from when they digest coal within themselves. By withdrawing their heads into their shells of solid basalt, they can endure most attacks with ease.
author: infinex21

entry: By utilizing the open ports on POKENAME's arms, it can quickly consume combustible materials through its palms; as these materials are burned within its arms, POKENAME generates energy for itself. It will fire out heat and smoke to propel itself.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME eat coal and sulfur, which are burned within their inner flames to produce energy for themselves. As they "digest" their food, they exude smoke and flames from their open, glowing-red ports.
author: infinex21

entry: It projects an image of its face within the steam it expels, but this is just as incorporeal as the smoke. In olden Hoenn times people would burn incense near it, believing it held connections to their ancestors' spirits.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly billows out smoke from its massive jaws, which needs to be constantly vented to prevent toxic accumulation in its body. In Pokémon battles, its massive jaws can shoot out fiery plumes of lava, or bite onto its opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The smoke excreted by POKENAME smells like the sea, as the water it evaporates is very saline. With the pressure of the steam exhausted from the bottom of its body, it somehow manages to float mid-air just fine.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: It will charge and butt heads with other POKENAME in the wild. After their heads collide, they will propel a volcanic burst from their head, making their Headbutt much more powerful.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME uses controlled explosions on its shell and head to power its Headbutt. These explosions also control the direction of its charge, letting it make sudden turns without losing momentum.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: On occasion, the volcano on POKENAME's back erupts, sending magma cascading out. Some of this magma settles on it and cools, creating sturdy plates that function as makeshift protective armour.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME houses molten rock in its shell and spews hot ash from its vents. It is found in hot, arid climates, as any moisture in the air causes it great pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Agile and mischievous, POKENAME swings through the rafters of abandoned mansions. It chews on old wood to warm itself when cold.
author: .izik

entry: A POKENAME uses its emissions to create smokescreens and bamboozle its foes. It uses the cracks and craters in its armor to catch attacks and parry its opponent's blows.
author: staghorn

entry: It pokes its head out of the stone body in order to eat or release large amounts of steam. Some resorts in Hoenn have taken to employing them as a part of their saunas.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produces its smoke by burning collected life energy inside of its mace. These souls then inhabit and control this smoke, using it as their hand to wield POKENAME for their own purposes.
author: soup1900

entry: Groups of POKENAME work together to collect large amounts of coal for them to burn. They use jets of pressurized smoke to effortlessly cut through the rocks.
author: mistymagius

entry: Their favorite food is coal, though they also enjoy metal more than typical ores and rocks. Their internal flames burn hotter when they are excited, happy, or angry.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's method of flight consumes a lot of energy, so it only awakens once a year, eating enough to last another 51 weeks of hibernation. These nights are infamous as POKENAME break the sound barrier and create supersonic booms to stun prey.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Their prey undergo seasonal nuptial flights, swarming in the night sky. On these nights, POKENAME awakens and rockets itself into the swarm, consuming up to three times its body weight before returning to its den and sleeping for another year.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME puffs out steam from its body in the form of thick, ribbon-like clouds. Those who wind up inhaling the exhaled smoke find that it produces a calming effect and causes a feeling of warmth internally.
author: sk372

entry: It seeks to fight entire groups of strong Pokémon by itself. If it is ever overwhelmed, it curls over and releases an Eruption from its shell.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME have a diet consisting solely of coal, which they grind down and burn inside themselves to generate an immense amount of energy. POKENAME can use the soot released from within to obscure the sky, giving them an advantage in battle.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME is a mystery to physicists and biologists alike because its shell is too heavy to float, and it produces an unending plume of smoke without ever landing to eat. It's hard for these questions to be studied, as it must keep moving to live.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME are easily recognized from the high-pitched noises created when they respire. Unfortunately, these Pokémon are quite prone to mineral deficiencies, causing illness and highly irregular breathing patterns.
author: jangodiot

entry: Its tiny body is too small to haul its massive shell around normally. When POKENAME needs to move, it retreats into the shell and uses expelled steam to propel itself forward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME constantly spews a great column of smoke out of its top. Occasionally, a lost soul will be seen swirling in the smoke, which is channelled into its ghostly attacks.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME produces large amounts of thick smoke from its body and is often used as an excellent outdoor heater. They seem to be most popular among campers and hikers.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME ejects black soot in the shape of a hand from its mouth to hold back predators that near it. It can also use its smoke to create hand signals across the sky to communicate with other POKENAME across nearby shores.
author: soup1900

entry: As pressure builds inside POKENAME, its keys rattle faster and louder. Moments later, scalding steam erupts, capable of melting metal.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME sings, puffs of thick, hypnotic smoke rise from its shell. Campers once mistook its snores for volcanic rumblings and evacuated the area, only for the rangers to find it dreaming peacefully.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When happy, these Pokémon release white smoke and when angry they release black smoke. They love to eat flammable materials and raw ores. Their refuse often contains traces of refined metals.
author: infinex21

entry: They release hot smoke when they prepare to charge forward. They have a keen sense of smell for coal, making them common allies to miners.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are found swimming within lava lakes around volcanoes. Their internal steam engine converts the intense heat of the lava into energy.
author: camtft

entry: Its gears churn slowly but steadily to give it life energy, releasing small bits of smoke as it does so. Some liken the sound it makes to the slow chug of a steam engine.
author: sk372

entry: The spinning gears generate steam to dissipate excess heat. The main gear stores intense pressure within, releasing it to launch the other gears forward in self-defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME burns as little coal as possible in its tail, as the fire inside its shell-like casing dictates its life. When it becomes angry, it burns coal at a faster rate than usual, which it needs to keep its fire blazing.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's grey roses release clouds of smoke and ash when POKENAME feels threatened. They are often used by honey collectors as their smoke seems to prevent Beedrill from becoming agitated.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uproots carrots and blows tiny embers over them to roast the vegetables before happily eating its meal. When sleeping, it will expel small flames from its ears.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's leaves are intensely spicy and have been prized in Hoenn cuisine for generations. Chefs use them to enrich special stews.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flocks to volcanoes to eat molten rocks, and releases smoke that builds up while digesting rocks. When threatened, it spits out balls of fire to scare away predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's many spikes help it attach to rocky surfaces. It can be occasionally seen inhabiting chimneys, feeding on the soot that drifts up.
author: mepp.

entry: Toxic steam constantly leaks from POKENAME's body as its antennae grow hot. The more coal it consumes, the denser and deadlier the fumes become.
author: .izik

entry: It lengthens the distance of its leaps by expelling vast amounts of smoke from its nostrils to propel it further. The smoke takes on an appearance similar to wings, making POKENAME appear to be flying.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME vents steam from its nose to propel itself extremely fast through the air. Its supply is limited though, so it is often seen dormant on the ground while more steam builds inside itself.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME consumes coal to keep its energy high as it gallops around its territory. The craters on its back vent excess heat and poisonous smog.
author: chibitales

entry: When POKENAME lets out a roar, the small plumes of steam it releases intensify into a singular geyser of smoke. It often tries to beat its own personal record for roar and eruption power.
author: sk372

entry: Archaeologists believe POKENAME may have been the apex being within ancient volcanic regions. A long neck, powerful jaws, a sturdy shell and smoke production all combined to make it a formidable prehistoric hunter.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's leaves are made of a tightly packed warm ash. Once a month, the leaves "shed" into a dusty pile on the ground. It buries itself into the pile afterward and waits for a new set of leaves to grow back.
author: sk372

entry: The steam that comes of the head of POKENAME becomes thicker as the beat of the music becomes faster. This natural process makes it a popular sight in clubs, where it serves as a living, high-grade smoke machine.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's arms are hidden by dense steam. It claps to charge the vapor with static, though its hands remain invisible through the thick cloud.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME gently sways around to prevent thickly packed smoke from being released from its body. This is done to maintain the air quality and health of those around it, especially those who may have breathing problems.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME flies through the air on wings made of smoke. It is very timid and tends to avoid conflict by hiding in smokescreens rather than engaging in battle.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME constantly produces smoke, which it uses to scare prey out from their burrows. As prey leaves its burrow, POKENAME releases blazingly hot fumes, cooking its prey instantly.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: Though the sulfurous scent of its steam repels most people, those who can tolerate the odor have found ways to use POKENAME's hot stony plate to cook food.
author: hophoppip

entry: It belts out increasing amounts of steam from its tail depending on how happy it is. POKENAME may also release excessive steam if hugged too hard by its Trainer.
author: sk372

entry: The shell surrounding POKENAME's head is heated by the coal it consumes. Water-type attacks from this Pokémon are scalding hot and likely to cause burns.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME carve dens out of the rocks surrounding hot springs to keep themselves warm while they rest. If startled, they blast out plumes of steam from the cracks in their shells.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME roasts nuts and treats on an open fire when frost nips at people's noses. People and Pokémon alike cozy up by its fire, helping everyone keep warm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The smoke around its shell is actually dense plumes of hot spores. It will withdraw into its shell when it rests, veiling itself with even more of these spores.
author: infinex21

entry: The shell of POKENAME increases its defense in exchange for lower speed, allowing it to endure most attacks from other wild Pokémon rather than fleeing.
author: erudite_phoenix

entry: POKENAME is a docile, yet powerful Pokémon capable of producing vast heat waves up to 650° Celsius. They store energy by submerging their rocky bodies in lava, then expel it through their gemstones as gleaming light that is said to cure any illness.
author: aurange

entry: POKENAME gather in groups at active lava flows to store energy. If disturbed or threatened, the normally passive Pokémon become enraged. Legend says a once-thriving village angered them, and the mountain itself burned for three days and three nights.
author: aurange

entry: POKENAME surrounds itself in a cloud of thick smoke that obscures its weak points. If the wind is blowing, it will take shelter to keep its shroud intact.
author: hophoppip

entry: Thick smoke pours from POKENAME's large ears, carrying the distinct scent of burnt wood through forest paths and volcanic slopes. It snacks on small twigs that fall from trees.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can pull heavy cargo with the strength of a freight train while it's full on coal. Its heavy plating deflects away rocks and other debris that may fall onto it while it's searching for coal.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are known to consistently reach temperatures high enough to melt solid steel. POKENAME constantly radiate heat, which makes it difficult for them to interact with Pokémon outside of their species.
author: ruben2309295

entry: It collects coal to burn within the base of its body, which is covered by a hard shell. The holes where the glow of coal burns brightly are said to guide lost souls who died in cave-ins.
author: pattybgoode

entry: As POKENAME sings its eerie song at night, thick smoke flows from the pores in its torso. These clouds can form into hands that can grab and ensnare others to be dragged off to POKENAME's den.
author: sk372

entry: Many have observed that POKENAME smells faintly of freshly baked bread. Its naturally warm body makes it a popular Pokémon for companionship.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME wanders for its first year before choosing a place to settle. If it nests in a bakery, it is seen as a mark of excellence. After a hearty meal, it vents fragrant steam said to smell even better than the treats it consumed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME wanders for its first year before choosing a place to settle. If it nests in a confectionery shop, it is seen as a mark of excellence. After a hearty meal, it vents fragrant steam said to smell even better than the treats it consumed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME store pieces of coal within their saggy skin so that they always have a meal on hand. They burn coal within themselves for energy and vent the heat with every breath taken. They exhale smoke from their nostrils before they attack.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often live in packs that include Torggy, with the one POKENAME that has the largest and most vibrant crest acting as the leader. They collectively mine for coal to eat, with the pack leader always being given the largest piece.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME likes to rest in lava lakes, venting steam from the top of its head. Campers love to have POKENAME around as its head acts like a portable stovetop.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME whips its tail around in battles to fill the area with thick, hot smoke. Once the foe is blinded and burned, it finishes the battle by burning more coal to power up a final fire breath attack.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME will blow hearts of smoke at people it thinks could be a potential couple. On the contrary, couples it thinks aren't going to last will instead be blown broken hearts made of black soot.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME moves by hopping about in a zigzag pattern, though its movement speed is quite slow. Each time it lands, short bursts of smoke billow up from its shell.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are useful in geothermal power plants, such as one located in Kalos, for their ability to naturally siphon heat from the ground. They sustain themselves on resources like coal and other carbon-based materials, however.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME primarily eats coal, which will be burned within its body to provide it with energy. At most, they need only two moderately sized lumps of coal per day to live. The smoke released from the tops of their heads is surprisingly clean.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME bury their eggs in the sand of beaches, letting the heat of the sand incubate the eggs. Golf courses near beaches have complained of stolen golf balls, with the thief being POKENAME, who have confused the golf balls with POKENAME eggs.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME will remain motionless for hours while it meditates, spewing hot smoke all the while. Saunas like to pair POKENAME with a Water-Type Pokémon to create a steamy environment for guests. POKENAME enjoys hot yoga classes as well.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME constantly release smoke from their bodies to ensure that they keep their bodies as hot as possible. If their bodies cool past a certain temperature, they experience a chill that causes them to shiver.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is possible for POKENAME to burn so hot during battle that the body will start melting. This does not hurt the POKENAME; the body can just barely handle its own heat.
author: Cerealjamalt

entry: When endangered POKENAME's humps erupt, they release smog and magma causing disorientation. The more coal POKENAME consumes, the stronger the eruption becomes.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME boils water inside its claws to generate hot steam with which it scalds its opponents. It loves hot water, which is why it is easy to see it floating in hot springs or heated pools.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME cloak themselves in soot from the fires they produce. Powerful individuals can spread their ashes over the skies for many days, blocking out the sunlight and lowering the temperature.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are very docile creatures, spending their days drinking a lot of water and boiling it inside their bodies, turning it into scalding steam. Laundry workers enjoy having a few POKENAME on hand to iron and dewrinkle clothes with their steam.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When POKENAME is low on coal, it burns parts of its wings for fuel, leaving them with many holes over time. Entire cities must evacuate when it blows out its burning smoke, as it ignites anything it touches and spreads fires over great distances.
author: soup1900

entry: The red-hot spiral on POKENAME's torso brings to mind a stovetop burner. It's unwise to use POKENAME as a burner, however, as lying on its back leaves it vulnerable, and it will use fiery attacks in its defensive state.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME stacks discarded shells on its back as a form of weight training. If it lacks shells to use, it may instead request other Pokémon or even Trainers to stand on it as it works out.
author: sk372

entry: It flexes before every attack, expelling smoke from the holes in its shell as it does so. The more holes emitting smoke, the stronger the attack it's about to unleash.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were once considered major threats due to their strength and steam. In the present, it's more common to find POKENAME lounging in their shells, enjoying a hot stew. Research has concluded that the soup is delicious.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME exhales smoke that causes nearby plants to grow twice as fast. Botanists highly covet this rare and potent fertilizer.
author: .izik

entry: When angered, POKENAME's rocky head vents thick smoke like a steam train. It feeds voraciously on lumps of raw coal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's rocky shell is completely hollow, allowing for its built-up fire and smoke to be stored inside. In battle, it releases this pressure, causing a devastating eruption of lava and smoke.
author: evilgammon

entry: The coal it eats gives it life; the more coal it eats the more vigorous POKENAME is. The most energetic POKENAME rocket around mountains by exploding leftover coal.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Despite having a low top speed, POKENAME prides itself on its galloping ability. What appears to be smoke billowing from it is actually a soft, ashy fur.
author: sk372

entry: The smoke that POKENAME produces thickens the faster it runs, leaving a dense cloud that can engulf entire roads. Long ago, bandits rode POKENAME to escape capture, using the thick smoke to conceal their tracks.
author: jaminmcready

entry: All three heads possess the capacity to breathe out steam, but as the center head is the most temperamental of the bunch, it is the one most associated with and seen using the ability.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have pieces of shells and obsidian in their body, which constantly shift to keep their body hot. Whenever it rains, they push the shell pieces to the exterior of their body in an attempt to ward off moisture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has the unique ability to blast both flames and water out of its spouts. When fired at the same time, steam is created that is said to be good for muscle aches.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME floats freely through volcanic regions, delighting in scaring travelers who stray too close to bubbling lava pits. It laughs loudly when its victim screams in fear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tunnels its way underground near volcanic areas. It is most comfortable the closer it is to molten depths, its steam production increasing the higher the temperature around it is.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's claws emit constant steam due to their heat. Though effective for offense, it prefers creating a thicker cloud of steam to obscure itself and flee from potential dangers.
author: sk372

entry: It uses its giant clamp to slow-cook its prey, then eats it alive as soon as the fight is won. Wild POKENAME tolerate medium rare meat, while trained specimens prefer well done.
author: epping_forest

entry: Both of POKENAME's claws produce copious amounts of steam, but the larger actually contains and produces boiling water. Any who agitate it risk being hit with a scalding spray.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME often find secluded areas of shallow water, heating the area with its hot body. Different Pokémon often gather to enjoy these makeshift hot springs alongside the POKENAME.
author: mrsspace

entry: POKENAME is most commonly found in the autumn, appearing within the fields of rural communities. They are friendly and easily trained, enjoying the company of young Trainers as they explore the Pokémon world.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: During storms, POKENAME secures pumpkins to the ground with strong silk. The threads are resilient enough to withstand hurricane winds.
author: .izik

entry: Each of POKENAME's heads grows dark brown vines that connect at night. These shared roots transfer nutrients and whisper thoughts in unison.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will steal pumpkins and then carve them to act as a protective head covering. Most of the time the Pokémon will carve the pumpkin into a skull form, reminiscent of Cubone, but there have been sightings of other shapes over time.
author: _pixelar_

entry: It pretends to be a Pumpkaboo to draw in unsuspecting Trainers before releasing its toxic gas. Rumors state those who faint to its gas get their spirits trapped inside it.
author: h0bojoe

entry: The pumpkin in POKENAME's pouch is said to carry the soul of someone recently departed. It holds them close and grants them company until they feel enough peace to properly move on.
author: sk372

entry: Using its brown vines, POKENAME overtakes wild Tangela and then spreads its body beneath the soil. These hidden traps ensnare any who near the crops it protects.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are a common sight during autumn festivities, entertaining crowds with their flashy lights. They are also known to enjoy playing light-hearted pranks as well.
author: mepp.

entry: The vine on POKENAME's head sharpens into a venomous needle. A single jab causes painful fevers in predators bold enough to approach its patch.
author: .izik

entry: It has a remarkable capacity for adaptation, no matter how harsh its environment may be. The light of its eyes changes as it is exposed to the radiation of certain evolutionary stones.
author: infinex21

entry: Its body glows with soft flames. If you rest in the warmth of its fire's heat for a while, you may witness memories from lives long past.
author: hophoppip

entry: During the autumn months, some Trainers will place POKENAME on their home or yard as decorations. It waits until unsuspecting people travel near at night, then springs to life, floating and cackling and frightening them off.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME tends to appear in October, when it gathers with others of its kind to haunt wheat fields. However, it is said that spotting one brings prosperity and good fortune, so farmers never drive it away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is always on the lookout for predators, using its excellent night vision to navigate during the night. When frightened, it will jump into the trees, its fur blending in with the dark foliage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME scurries around forests and farmland, scavenging for food to take back to its burrow. During harvest season, it can be persuaded to help out with an offering of Colbur Berries.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lets out long, haunting hoots late in the evening, calling out to others of its kind. Once a month, flocks of POKENAME gather in the forest to sing an ethereal harmony together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for another car by nighttime drivers due to the glowing holes in its belly, which are actually used to blind prey and frighten predators. Autumn nights are fortuitous times for people hoping to spot this skittish Pokémon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses its vines to parasitize Ledyba colonies, converting them into seed-spreaders. It fiercely defends the meadow, attacking all intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spins translucent threads across pumpkin fields. If one is touched, the swarm is alerted. It traps intruders using Sticky Web to prevent escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attracts Pokémon like Venonat by letting its body glow at full strength. When they approach, they find themselves tangled in the powerful sticky webs that POKENAME spun around the area.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME only hunts at night, able to detect prey in pure darkness using its excellent night vision. During the day it hangs from decaying trees, hoping to blend into the dark foliage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME emerge during the full moon of an autumn festival and live quietly inside caves during the rest of the year. They happily dance and celebrate the occasion alongside others.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Legends claim that consuming the goo brewed in POKENAME's pumpkin cauldron bestows visions of the future. A splash of the liquid is sometimes added to dessert frostings or beverages to induce a woozy feeling.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its tail is a lantern; one look at the light from the hole of this lantern can put one under its control. POKENAME can easily detect spirits with its ears' sensitive hearing.
author: doctorjazznumber6215

entry: Flocks of POKENAME drift along the wind, the light from their lanterns only visible during the night. Spectators describe POKENAME sightings as looking like small stars moving across the night sky.
author: mistymagius

entry: On particularly dark nights, clusters of POKENAME can be seen drifting on the wind, illuminating the ground below in an eerie light. They bring the oddly sweet scent of pumpkin wherever they go.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME lures young children into the forests, hypnotizing them with the eerie glow of its lantern. No one knows why it wants these children, but they are often never seen again once they enter the forest.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's glowing eyes let them see where they are going in the dark. These Pokémon commonly infest pumpkin patches, making their dens inside large pumpkins and gourds.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME only come out at night, cheekily playing pranks on anyone that passes by. Its favorite prank is to hide inside hollow gourds and waiting for someone to pick it up.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flashes the pumpkin-like orb on its tail mid-flight to communicate. If the light flickers red, it signals danger to the swarm nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's head is always caked in mud, even while submerged. No one knows what lies beneath, as legend warns that anyone who tries to wipe it clean will be cursed. Whether myth or truth, even the boldest Trainers leave the mud untouched.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The light shed from POKENAME has the unusual effect of causing the plants it shines on to act as if it were nighttime. Day-blooming flowers close and nocturnal blossoms open in the presence of this Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are popular in farming communities, their ethereal connection to the harvest making them invaluable for maintaining a healthy crop. They have an innate ability to sense when a crop is ripe for picking.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its shell reminds people of Lychee, especially since its shell is the same color. When its shell is damaged, it also oozes out syrup that tastes like the fruit too.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stores Pumkin Berries in its shell, rolling to mix them into a juice. In Kanto, this sweet drink is praised for its aroma and flavor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves melons and pumpkins and will often raid local farms to get its hands on them. However, anyone that tries to steal its stash will be relentlessly pursued and attacked.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME invades Teddiursa dens to parasitize them. It practices and mimics their cries to lure in Ursaring, which it ambushes for nutrients.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burns unwanted plant life by chewing it to ash and spitting it onto pumpkin fields. It avoids burning useful flora unless resources run low.
author: .izik

entry: Those who believe POKENAME help to bring lost souls to the afterlife claim that you can tell how many souls one is carrying by how large the pumpkin on its back is.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME are often found within farm fields, their noses pressed to the ground in search of root vegetables. They have a habit of hollowing out pumpkins to serve as homes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's thick fur is effective at keeping it warm in the frigid areas it inhabits. At night, it scares off potential attackers by lighting up the holes in its lower torso and making it appear like ghostly glowing eyes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hides in coral reefs, shining a soft light from its chest at night. Divers often mistake it for treasure until it vanishes into the dark.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's wide mouth can generate an intensely bright light. Living in the darker depths of the ocean, flashing this light blinds attackers and gives POKENAME ample opportunity to escape predators.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects seeds from decaying pumpkins and stores them in its sack-like tail. It lays them out to dry in the sun before eating.
author: .izik

entry: Though it may appear intimidating, POKENAME is actually extremely friendly. It is believed to guide the spirits of the departed to the Cave of Origin, so that they may be reborn.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: POKENAME uses Phanpy herds to roll through fields and churn planting rows. The resulting pumpkin patches are heavily guarded by hostile attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps in pumpkin patches at night, mimicking the gourds around it. Should it be woken, it will Lock On to the offender and spit pumpkin seeds at them before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are common companions in agricultural communities, used as a deterrent to keep Flying-Type Pokémon away. They will pick fights with Pokémon that disturb the crops under their protection, even if they are unlikely to win.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are common companions in agricultural communities, used as a deterrent to keep Flying-Type Pokémon away. They will pick fights with Pokémon that disturb the crops under their protection, even if they are unlikely to win.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Should a pumpkin patch face repeated theft, it is said a POKENAME will appear to guard it. Its roar is said to break the will of any thief who draws too close.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon smoothed out a pumpkin holding a spirit into a ball and now travels on it, mimicking the actions the spirit once took in life.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: The electric lights that glow within POKENAME's hollow head are thought to attract Bug-type Pokémon to pollinate the pumpkin flower on its tail. These Pokémon are commonly seen throughout fall, but they hide away at the first sign of winter.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME often show up in towns and villages during autumn, pretending to be children so that they may gorge themselves with candy. Although everyone knows they are Pokémon, most still indulge them with candy and other treats.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon can be seen curled up in pumpkin patches, posing as an actual pumpkin. It likes to prank humans wandering around the pumpkin patch by dressing up other pumpkins to be just like POKENAME.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: During the day, POKENAME nap lazily in sunny places. Once twilight falls, they can re-emit the absorbed light to guide their way as they travel.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME enjoy living with farmers, tilling the soil and repelling intruders to help make sure crops grow nice and healthy. While they glide, they swing their tails to scatter seeds. They provide light for the sprouts even during cold nights.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Weary travellers of the jungle may encounter POKENAME at night. It's a friendly spirit that will offer a slice of pie made from its own body to adventurers.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME grow long spikes on their back that resemble candy corn. Many children have tried to bite off a delicious-looking spike, only to lose a tooth while biting down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME parasitizes Mudkip colonies to water its pumpkin fields. The Mudkip spray water while it uses Bullet Seed to keep scavengers away.
author: .izik

entry: This childlike Pokémon has a tendency for knocking on doors at night to ask for treats. Citizens of Lavender Town have taken to leaving small baskets of candy out on their front steps, lest they get tricked by the spirit instead.
author: chiari_queen

entry: On close inspection, POKENAME appears to float just above the ground. Researchers believe it is to cover up the fact that their tiny legs lack the locomotion to get anywhere faster than a crawl.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME is territorial of a patch of its meadow, launching venomous needles at intruders. A Galarian baker discovered that baking it in a pie with Kebia Berries made it edible and produced a pie with a slightly sour flavor with a smooth texture.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME gathers pumpkin innards and smears them around its riverside lodge. The scent marks its territory and keeps other Pokémon at bay.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits sharp seeds which inject foes with an endurance-sapping poison. It prowls farm fields near harvest season, looking for prey scavenging the last of the crops.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It is known to use its natural cuteness and bright lights to lure in and carry lost souls to the afterlife. If no lost souls are around, it will draw in other living creatures before tearing them apart.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME slumbers during the day, covering its eyes with its large leaves. At night, its eyes glow with a mysterious but welcoming light, inviting all who see it to join in POKENAME's festivities.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME floats through graveyards, blinking its chest lights in eerie patterns. Local legends claim staring too long can curse your family line.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flocks descend on Nidoran families to harness their hearing. With its sharp horn, it patrols pumpkin fields and drives intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: As the sun sets, POKENAME become restless, bouncing from the walls and ceilings. Their tails become enveloped in hypnotic flames under a full moon, lulling anyone who looks at them into a trance.
author: santon5512
