entry: Although usually afraid of contact with others, wild POKENAME will rarely hesitate to help guide lost travelers out of forests. The touch of their vines instills calmness, though some tales claim this is because these Pokémon absorb and feed on fear.
author: infinex21

entry: Spores shaken from POKENAME's body smell like ripe pumpkins. They cause limb numbness that can take several days to fully wear off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME communicates with soft glows from its torso. Its innards are tangled vines that extend to grab and consume sea plants from afar.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME colonies parasitize sleeping Nincada to collect nutrient-rich soil. They glow yellow underground as they prepare vast pumpkin beds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appear during certain spirit festivals. The yellow fur on their bodies flickers like fire and is believed to drive away malevolent spirits. The flicker is more intense and a fresh pumpkin smell is produced when POKENAME are excited.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME live in dark forests, the bioluminescent fluid inside its body helping them to see their surroundings. Parents will often give their child a POKENAME to act as a nightlight.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME loves to spook passersby by camouflaging itself amongst the trees. While mostly found in dark forests, it will also inhabit abandoned homes and mansions.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME bites into power lines to absorb electricity. When fully charged, the light inside its body flashes rapidly like a blinking lantern.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal, using their glowing feelers to illuminate the darkness. When threatened, POKENAME will spew out a hot, orange liquid from its mouth similar to pureed pumpkin.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME camouflage themselves among tree branches until they are ready to strike. By shining a bright light from within their bodies, they can surprise their prey and attack first.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Farmers are advised to keep any jewelry and crystals far away from their land. POKENAME will lurk in pumpkin patches and attempt to hypnotize the farmers into giving up their gems.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME eats poison ivy and poison sumac to enhance its toxins. When its venom peaks in potency, its body glows a brilliant orange instead of yellow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps in pumpkin patches during day. If disturbed, it strikes with venom so potent it can cause temporary blindness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's dance weaves hypnotic hues, guiding lost souls to rest while ensnaring the living in a trance. Those who disrupt its rhythm risk becoming spectral prey, bound to wander as the spirits it once ferried.
author: vhscopyofmeangirls

entry: After POKENAME possesses a rotting pumpkin, it struggles to get around without risking its body falling apart. The pungent scent of decay follows it wherever it goes.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is said to be a wandering spirit that is drawn to large gatherings of costumed people and pumpkin patches. It loves to join spooky festivities, adoring the thrill of a good scare.
author: chiari_queen

entry: POKENAME takes as many spirits as possible and keeps them captive inside its body. These souls can only break out once enough of them are present, and when that happens, their bursting energy will cause POKENAME to transform.
author: soup1900

entry: At night, POKENAME patrols crop fields using the eerie glow from its chest and paws. If it spots an intruder, it charges while screaming a sound that many state sounds like a tornado siren crossed with radio static.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's vines stretch across the ocean floor, detecting vibrations from far away. Sometimes its vines completely overtake sunken ships.
author: .izik

entry: During cold desert nights, POKENAME's face glows faintly. The flickering lights help others of its kind coordinate hunts in total darkness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will patrol the fields all day protecting crops for their farmers. They will use Scary Face to frighten away any wild Pokémon that invades their fields.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Yellow mushrooms grow on POKENAME's body and can cause sleep when eaten. Some say those who slumber this way are more likely to experience vivid nightmares.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME is made of phosphorescent plants and stones, which can glow for up to four hours after sun exposure. This loyal Pokémon is a preferred partner for cave explorers and miners as a non-igniting light source should they encounter gasses.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME tries very hard to keep its favorite music secret. It will outright refuse any attempts to impress it with music.
author: chaotic_aspergers

entry: POKENAME burrows halfway beneath leaf piles in the fall. Its delicate head vines become brittle in cold weather and naturally break away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's bodies emit constant heat, the inside of their bodies glowing. During the day, they hide themselves in pumpkin patches, foraging for sticks to eat at night.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME light their sticks before every Pokémon battle and wave their sticks like a wand. They channel spirits of the dead to strengthen their scorching flames.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The light emitted by POKENAME only grows stronger with fusion. With this power, it guides hordes of spirits into the afterlife.
author: .b4ring_my.t33th

entry: The spots on POKENAME's wings glow brightly in the dark. People often mistake these spots for lost spirits and end up following POKENAME deep into the woods.
author: mistymagius

entry: The pumpkin that POKENAME possesses is unusually sweet. Chefs will sometimes cook the pumpkin for special occasions.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: This hungry Pokémon loves to feed on pumpkins, which it can smell from miles away. Pumpkin farmers traditionally bake a special pumpkin dessert for POKENAME to keep it from eating their crops.
author: hophoppip

entry: The item on its back has the texture, taste and smell of a pumpkin pie, but it cannot easily be physically damaged. Some Trainers compare POKENAME's size, aroma, and sometimes even the taste of their pie to prove their POKENAME is superior to others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be seen hovering over fields on autumn nights, flickering their lights in an odd pattern. The reason for this behavior remains unknown.
author: mepp.

entry: It is said that anyone who sees a POKENAME in the wild will develop anxiety and never experience true love.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME haunts pumpkin fields, feeding on the souls it encounters through the night. To weaken its victims, it beats its large wings to scatter venomous powders over them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME haunt pumpkin patches, vigorously protecting them from both real and perceived harm. They have an unfortunate habit of chasing off farmers looking to harvest their crop.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME haunt pumpkin patches, vigorously protecting them from both real and perceived harm. They summon spiritual energy to their fists, striking at other Pokémon that would dare attempt to feed on the growing gourds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is believed to be a benevolent spirit that appears during autumn to protect pumpkin fields from the influence of other creatures. It uses its extraordinary psychic powers to create powerful barriers or make nearby objects levitate.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In autumn, POKENAME hollows pumpkins to request treats from nearby villages. If denied too often, it flattens homes with terrifying kicks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can often be spotted on October nights, flexing to receive candy. POKENAME consume candy as one of their primary sources of energy, able to eat a ten-pound bag in one sitting.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Though primarily aquatic in nature, POKENAME can float above land for several hours without issue. When outside the water during the night, the pumpkin-like growths on its head emit an otherworldly glow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME waves its glowing tail underwater to attract Shellder. If bitten, it lifts its head slowly and stares at the attacker for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found blending into packs of Squirtle and Wartortle, mimicking their movements. Whether their objective is food, safety, or simple companionship remains a mystery.
author: victor9106

entry: POKENAME wields a burning torch with graceful precision. In battle, it strikes with sweeping arcs, then repeats the motions as ritual practice.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body has an oddly sweet scent, smelling of fallen leaves and overripe pumpkin. While the scent is perfect for the autumn season, it can get overpowering if POKENAME is around all the time.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's hypnotic flames influence others into helping tend to the nearby soil. Folktales mention that those foolish enough to follow their fiery embers from the fields and into the woods will be turned into a spirit by POKENAME and devoured.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses its huge wings to roam the forests at night, seeking nourishment to grow stronger. During the day, it hides inside trees, avoiding sunlight that could damage the seed on its back.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its wings to absorb moonlight and convert it into electricity. Should a POKENAME absorb too much moonlight, it will explode.
author: .izik

entry: Its abdomen appears to have a thin outer layer, akin to an egg. When it sees a flower it wants to eat, it seeps a thick, yolk-like substance.
author: .izik

entry: The scales scattered by POKENAME's flapping wings cause a person's eyes to water uncontrollably and obscure their vision. POKENAME uses this opportunity to pilfer food from its victims.
author: sk372

entry: Every time POKENAME flaps its wings, it looses highly toxic dust. Its temperament turned ferocious when it began using both bones and its wings.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME can control the density of their internal gases to become lighter or heavier than air, levitating in place and using their wings to move around. In an emergency they can release large puffs of gas all at once, providing a burst of speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Drawn to light, POKENAME dashes towards any visible light source it can find. It has a habit of crashing into and destroying the source, however.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME hunts for deposits of toxic minerals like lead and arsenic. Its rocky hide absorbs their toxic qualities. It must constantly flap its wings to prevent too much rock from building up on them.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its eggs are poisonous. Many people have been hospitalized from mistaking its eggs as Chansey's.
author: jhenebean

entry: The brittle vines covering its body are both unappetizing and highly toxic. Therefore, POKENAME has few natural predators.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME are usually accompanied by small swarms of Venonat. The Venonat take turns riding in the POKENAME's pouch.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME migrate to a different part of the forest every season to keep themselves warm. The journey is full of predators along the way, so they produce a large cloud of toxic pollen to deter predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love bright lights, often charging at streetlights or other urban light sources. This creates many issues for the city's inhabitants, however, as POKENAME are known to inadvertently cut down everything in between them and the light source.
author: agentyoshi

entry: POKENAME does not attack its prey, instead it will slowly stalk them until they succumb to its poisonous dust. It usually doesn't go after larger Pokémon since it has no easy way to carry them back to its den.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME dart through the night sky in huge leaps, scattering powder all around. Intentionally angering POKENAME is a poor idea: they will chase down their target and ram them over and over until the dawn of the next day.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME leaves its den at night to search for food, it scatters a silvery powder so it can always find its way home. It uses the venomous spine on its tail to defend itself from predators it encounters.
author: fiordaliso

entry: As POKENAME leaps from the water and flaps its wings rapidly to fly, it sprinkles a heavy mist of water beneath it. One must be careful not to be beneath its flight path, as the water shaken from its wings contains potent toxins.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its superior senses at nighttime to better transform into what it sees.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME are capable of rapidly adapting to their surroundings through evolution. Their obsession with bright lights remains ever present after they evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are active swimmers at night and chase after other nocturnal Pokémon. They are rarely found outside of a body of water because their skin dries out when they are not submerged in water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal creatures that love to stare at bright objects. Thankfully, they can light small flames to set small bushes ablaze and occupy their time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At night, POKENAME flutter outside windows to stare at computer screens. They mysteriously vanish at dawn, leaving behind a silver dust where they were observing from.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While generally gentle towards others, POKENAME behaves aggressively towards other Dragon types. The toxic scales it can flick from its wings are particularly effective at immobilizing other dragons.
author: sk372

entry: Daily skirmishes erupt over Silver Powder, as they rely on this substance to survive. The hunger suppressant has become a necessity as winters have become more volatile in their native environment.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME make seasonal migrations to different parts of the world but often get lost when they are distracted by bright lights from cities. Many scientists are working on cutting back on light pollution by dimming lights when people are asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME only comes out at night, drawn to the light of the full moon. The scales it produces from its wings are quite toxic and seem to have a mild hallucinogenic effect.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sneaks up on its intended prey using wings that barely make a sound and paralyzes them with poisonous scales.
author: jhenebean

entry: Rival POKENAME in the wild compete to see who kicks up the more dazzling display of pollen from their flapping wings. The competitors pay no heed to anyone unfortunate enough to get poisoned by their toxic flaps.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scatters a strange dust from its body as it flies through the night sky. On a clear night, this dust glimmers in the moonlight like stars.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME gazes blankly into the night sky, only flapping its wings to deter attackers. However, if you put a bright light in front of it, it will slowly follow it, almost like it's in a hypnotic trance.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its wings are unable to support its body for flight. It can flutter in place for a short period, but it will get tired quickly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release enervating spores that cause drowsiness when inhaled. Many lumberjacks have fallen asleep on the job because of the spores of a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wings are delicate and easily damaged by sudden movement, leading them to shelter in the forest undergrowth during the day. At night they emerge and lift their wings to catch the calmer night-time breeze, drifting away in the dark.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite its soft texture, the fuzz growing from POKENAME makes for poor clothing. The fibres of the fluff have fine barbs coated in an irritating toxin, making cloth spun from it scratchy and unpleasant.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If startled while scavenging through trash, POKENAME rapidly flaps its wings. This releases a cloud of Poison Powder to mask its escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are seemingly attracted to the glowing light of their own faces. They gather nightly to gaze intently at one another, completely entranced.
author: cristata

entry: POKENAME are seemingly attracted to the glowing light of their own faces. They gather nightly to gaze intently at one another, completely entranced.
author: cristata

entry: It slumbers in bogs during the day and lazily flutters around at night. It has very few predators due to its toxic mucus.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME release telepathic messages to anyone in the nearby vicinity. These thoughts often revolve around light and bright objects.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal creatures that love to chase after other Pokémon. When they feel particularly sly, they use their telekinesis to topple obstacles in front of their target.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME that are native to the deep forest will have purple-colored fur. The fur is hydrophobic and allows flight even in rainstorms.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME that are native to oceanic areas have blue-colored fur. Its fur is light and regulates temperature extremely well, allowing it to stay cool.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME beats its wings to release a poisonous dust so that no one tries to approach the flower on its back while it sleeps. It feeds by greedily sucking the sap from trees until they turn completely white and withered.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME bites down on its foe before releasing a violet-hued Stun Spore. This combination leaves enemies paralyzed and vulnerable.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon's body is covered in fur. When threatened, its multicolored wings take on a threatening pattern and shed toxic dust that causes hallucinations.
author: marvinthemarrowmuncher

entry: When POKENAME was first spotted by a person, they assumed they were hallucinating. Its wings allow for extra mobility to spot danger.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal. During the day, while it sleeps, the head on its tail keeps watch. The tail doesn't need to sleep.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME has a third pair of wings that it uses to protect its lower half by mimicking its top armor. It fires sharp, toxic shards of its shell from its spouts to incapacitate foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Due to its many eyes, POKENAME is hypersensitive to light and the sun. To remedy this, it has adapted to living underground despite its massive size.
author: patch

entry: Aggressive hunters, POKENAME fly up high before raining down dozens of toxic spines from their bodies indiscriminately. The paralyzing toxin takes effect quickly, giving POKENAME plenty of time to consume speared prey at their leisure.
author: sk372

entry: It loves sweet honey. To keep all the honey to itself, it stuns rivals by scattering its scales and then hurling them away with its prized horn.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME live amongst the boulders and debris found in the aftermath of a lava flow, spending the day hidden amongst the rocks as they sleep. At night they emerge from their hiding places, feeding on the mineral rich basalt around them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in colonies in mountainous regions, huddling together for warmth in colder months. When temperatures drop at night they glide down to the lower slopes, gracefully descending together in search of shelter.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's wings have yet to fully develop, so POKENAME slithers on the ground and slams into foes instead. In addition, it can spit out a strange colored fluid from its head that both attracts and harms foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is notably difficult for Trainers to catch due to its defense mechanisms; between hypnosis with its antlers and a variety of toxins emitted from its wings, it has a multitude of ways to make capturing it a challenge.
author: sk372

entry: By the time its prey notices it, POKENAME has already scattered its paralyzing scales with its wings, preventing any escape.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME often keep lights they find in their pouches, attracting the attention of other Bug-Type Pokémon at night. When these lights go out, they become incredibly distressed, hiding out in caves for weeks in sadness.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through its abdomen, storing energy as it flies. The charge can be released in short bursts to ward off threats.
author: .izik

entry: They grow as fast as the invasive bindweed, and both are poisonous to consume. Gardeners appreciate whenever a POKENAME is around, since the Pokémon will do the weeding and watering instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in underground tunnels built by related species. They act as lookouts, sounding signals through their horns to alert others when they spot a potentially dangerous intruder.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are most active at night and wander forests while other Pokémon are asleep. They play with other nocturnal Pokémon by tossing elongated discs made of leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME release an icy frost to freeze predators that try to hunt them. They can also freeze the surface of a pond or lake and skate away from danger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in polar regions, their thick layers of fat and coating of fuzzy fur helping to protect them from the cold. They hibernate through the summer months and emerge in the polar night, roaming the ice fields in the constant darkness.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in polar regions, their thick layers of fat and coating of fuzzy fur helping to protect them from the cold. They hibernate through the summer months and emerge in the polar night, roaming the ice fields in the constant darkness.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lives in small caves as its large eyes are very sensitive to light. Its spines carry a large amount of poison that often gets thrown into the air when POKENAME is frightened.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flutter their wings rapidly when they get into Pokémon battles, lifting off the ground as they launch their flurry of kicks. The flutter of their wings dislodges paralytic wing scales that harm their foe when they get into open injuries.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME practice their martial arts with one another under the light of the moon, whirring around in a flurry of punches and kicks. They rely heavily on their wings during fights, using the manoeuvrability they afford them to their advantage.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal Pokémon, gathering together to dance with one another under the moonlight. They are drawn to bright lights at night, and cities sometimes have large gatherings of POKENAME dancing in the street.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If it senses impending danger to its Trainer, this Pokémon is said to paralyze threats by scattering poisonous scales from its wings.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME drift under the light of the moon with an unearthly grace, adjusting their course with occasional flutters of their wings. Gatherings of POKENAME are commonly sought out as a source of inspiration for ballroom choreographers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drift under the light of the moon with an unearthly grace, adjusting their course with occasional flutters of their wings. They are popular companions for Trainers attending a masked ball, lending an air of mystique to the evening.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME gather together in dark clearings, fluttering together under the light of the stars. They can sense negative emotion through their antennae and will follow nervous travellers in an effort to offer companionship and soothe their unease.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME gather together in dark clearings, fluttering together under the light of the stars. Some POKENAME experience albinism and shine a brilliant white in the night, acting as a beacon for the rest of their swarm to flock to.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Because it can sense what its foe is thinking, POKENAME scatters poisonous scales from its wings to paralyze them before attacking fiercely.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME can be seen hovering around street lights at night, completely motionless. The crack along their backs constantly leaks a toxic powder, often forming clouds around themselves.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME colonies dig extensive tunnel networks, working together to expose tubers and roots to feed on. At night, some POKENAME will crouch at the entrance to the tunnel network and whir their wings, bringing fresh air in for the colony.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is incredibly timid and is often spooked by bright lights. When scared, it will flap its wings to scatter its poisonous scales, which often leaves its attacker gasping for air.
author: mistymagius

entry: When it attacks, it flaps its large wings violently to scatter its poisonous powder all around. It is more agile and active than it appears.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME have an uncanny ability to sense the emotions and intent of others. They do this by scattering fine wing scales into the air and watching them interact with the auras of others, reading changes in demeanour through their subtle movements.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The petals of the majestic flower on its back can change color based on POKENAME's diet. It is a creature highly appreciated by all Bug Catchers for its strength and rarity.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's wings act like makeshift ears, being able to pick up the slightest vibrations in the air. It is an incredibly timid Pokémon and will only use its potent poison if it absolutely has to.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME fools the foe into letting down its guard, then chomps down with its massive jaws. The steel jaws have replaced its poisonous wings.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME spend most of their life sleeping, only emerging for food and water for a couple of hours at night. If their rest is disturbed, they grow angry and aggressive, hurling boulders and fallen trees at whatever woke them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME gets excited, it rapidly flaps its wings, spreading poisonous scales. Unaware of its strength, it often harms smaller Pokémon.
author: sand_coffin

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal. After making itself invisible, it silently sneaks up to prey and paralyzes them with the scales from its wings.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME make their homes in city parks, sleeping throughout the day and allowing Pokémon to play atop their broad shell. During the night, their lamp ignites and they search for the light of other POKENAME so they can socialise together.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME nests in yew trees, breaking branches with its horn. It scatters a poisonous dust at anything that strays too close.
author: .izik

entry: Its fork-like blades let it scrape leaves clean off branches by the dozen. The leaves shrivel and die rapidly as they come detached since POKENAME is feeding off their energy.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's whirling dervish of an offense is quick and efficient. Against speedier foes, the twin tridents leave pollen behind with every swing that slows opponents down, making them easier to strike as the battle goes on.
author: sk372

entry: By fanning their wings, POKENAME scatter their scales across the battlefield, creating a toxic fog to disorient opponents. They can sense the movement of anything in this fog, pinpointing their targets before swiftly cutting them down.
author: santon5512

entry: At the base of its yew tree nest, POKENAME spreads pink powder that lingers on intruders. As the poison sets in, it waits nearby to ambush.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are most active at night, fluttering into position to observe battles between other Pokémon. They take interest in the strategic manoeuvres on display and will sometimes emit a loud buzz of instruction.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have exceptional night vision and patrol their vast territories under the light of the stars. When they encounter a potential rival, they rapidly flutter their wings, unleashing a stream of electrically charged wing scales.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its large wings release scales that are full of toxic dust. It is often lured into civilization by the bright lights of cities.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME's fur contains poisonous powder that scatters as it flies. While not harmful to humans, this powder weakens smaller Pokémon. Its appearance has inspired a children's toy that is dragged with a string.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME were historically a popular Pokémon in royal courts, their presence considered to add an air of elegance and refinement. Their flowers bloom only at night and give off a disarmingly sweet fragrance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME were historically a popular Pokémon in royal courts, their presence considered to add an air of elegance and refinement. Their flowers bloom only at night and give off a disarmingly sweet fragrance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: After scattering poisonous spores and scales, POKENAME closes in on its hampered foe with swift footwork and punches.
author: jhenebean

entry: In combat, POKENAME will obscure itself with its poisonous dust before striking with its poison-tipped claws. Its incredible agility and stealth allow it to fell its opponent before they can even move.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME enjoy playing with people, pulling pranks and running alongside them as they travel. If a POKENAME is abandoned by its Trainer, it will seek them out to hug them once more, using its toxic scales to paralyze the Trainer to hold them forever.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When curious Bug-type Pokémon draw near them, POKENAME unleashes a brilliant flash and zap their prey. More tiny Venomoth appear around them after they do this, so some believe each of their Venomoth are souls that POKENAME have stolen.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: At night, POKENAME emit a bright light from their chests, luring in other Bug-type Pokémon. Once their prey wanders too close, they strike, snagging entire swarms in a single swipe.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal predators that hunt through forests for smaller Pokémon to feed on in the dead of night. They move with quick, jerky motions as they search, pouncing on anything they see move that could be food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal predators that hunt through forests for smaller Pokémon to feed on in the dead of night. They rub their legs together rapidly when threatened, releasing a cloud of electrically charged dust from their fuzz.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME suspends itself from tree branches and building overhangs while gently pulsing light to attract insects into its translucent body. Fortune tellers claim to observe the digestion of these bugs to divine the future.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME maintain large territories, patrolling the woods each night in search of potential threats to their rule. Rangers operating in their territory are advised to avoid using flashlights as they grow aggressive if they encounter a bright light.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Swarms of POKENAME leave a trail of glittering wing scales behind them as they fly, a sparkling trail shining brightly against the night sky. Children often mistake a passing swarm as a meteor shower, making wishes for the future as they watch on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flutter and play with one another at night, their translucent wings letting the light of the stars shine through. They are easily distractible in their play and chase after meteor showers when they spot them passing by.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flips and flies over its opponent in battle, pummelling them with repeated scratches and kicks. Its flapping wings create a cloud of dust-like scales which further disorients its opposition.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME fur is coated in a fine dust that has paralytic effects when breathed in. They flutter their wings to unleash this dust at their foes and can electrically charge it to make a dazzling light display.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Whenever POKENAME are about to perform, they take a sharp breath in to prepare for their song. As they sing, they release a toxic dust that creates drowsiness upon inhalation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Disguised as forest picnickers, groups of POKENAME lure in the curious. Once close, they release paralyzing powder and drag their victims away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME inhales deeply in flight, then exhales shimmering blue dust. This powder knocks out prey instantly. It is most active in spring.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are social creatures, emerging at night to gather under the moonlight. By rapidly uncoiling their ears, they can deliver a powerful punch, releasing a puff of toxic powder on impact to disorient foes.
author: santon5512

entry: At night, POKENAME float around lampposts to stare at the bright light. Through the course of the night, POKENAME shed a bright dust that clings to the fluid around their body, dyeing themselves a bright lilac color.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The different bits of its core can move individually, but tend to stay in the shape of a moth. The gelatinous shell around it contains hallucinogenic properties if prolonged contact is maintained.
author: sk372

entry: The poison in POKENAME's wings is mild, so it must make up for potency with the speed and amount of flapping. It almost completely coats prey with poison to immobilize them before it begins drinking their blood.
author: sk372

entry: Able to fly from web to web, POKENAME keeps each structure charged by regularly depositing electricity into the conductive fibres. They are extremely nimble, but very weak.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME can usually be seen hanging from streetlamps during the night. Its seeds are so toxic that the area where the seeds land will be barren of plant life for a full month.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flock to cities at night because the artificial lighting activates a part of their brain associated with safety. Once dawn comes, they resume their migration to wherever they were headed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A cloud of white powder showers from its wings in times of distress. This powder can cause drowsiness if inhaled.
author: .izik

entry: While it cannot fly very well, POKENAME has the ability to climb on nearly any surface in the jungle. From the treetops, it spreads toxic spores while it feasts on leaves.
author: bobosmith01

entry: As it rolls through open glades, POKENAME sheds violet powder from its wings. Victims who inhale it fall into a deep sleep within minutes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has become too heavy to fly with its wings. Instead, it uses them to exude poisonous and hallucinogenic pollen.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal. During the daytime, it buries itself in the ground, leaving only its wings exposed to avoid detection by its enemies.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME are very timid and will only come out on cloudy nights. Their wings produce clouds of poisonous scales that can cause any contaminated plant to slowly wither away.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is always surrounded by a thin cloud of dust. Chalky in texture, this substance acts as a neurotoxin in high enough quantities.
author: turron_turron

entry: The scales it scatters will paralyze anyone who touches them, making that person unable to stand, and the honey it produces causes memory loss.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME are elusive Pokémon that prefer to hunt only on dark nights. They are sensitive to bright lights and attack artificial light sources in an effort to extinguish them, making them a hazard to low-flying aircraft.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME produce a fine silk from their stomachs, forming a fur-like coat around themselves. Toxic dust from their wings gets trapped within this silk, scattering in a thick cloud when struck.
author: santon5512

entry: Households in villages near POKENAME populations are advised to dim their lights at night. POKENAME are drawn to bright lights and crawl up windows if they see lights left on inside, leaving a trail of slime all over the windows as they do.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This Pokémon has the habit of hugging its companions, but the scales on its wings will paralyze anyone it hugs.
author: jhenebean

entry: The mushrooms on POKENAME's back are bright and flavorful, but great care must be taken if harvesting them; when removed, POKENAME instinctively releases a burst of irritating poison from the mushroom's pore.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have dazzling, wing-like structures that grow from their heads. As attention grabbing as these structures are, their true purpose is to magnify the volume of their songs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have dazzling, wing-like structures that grow from their heads. As attention grabbing as these structures are, their true purpose is to magnify the volume of their songs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME constantly shed spores from their large mushrooms, a fine dusting of them settling on their legs. When the build up becomes too irritating for them, they flap their wings to disperse them, inadvertently spreading the fungus as they do.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is covered in so much poisonous dust, that it can bury an entire car five feet deep. Trainers that want to work with POKENAME are basically required to wear a respirator at all times.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are irresistibly attracted to light, slipping through open windows to steal lamps from homes, carrying them wherever they go. Their fur sheds constantly and lingers in the houses they've raided for days, causing irritation.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME hangs from decaying trees. spending its poisonous scales along the wind. If anyone gets too close, it will wrap them in its vines before blasting them with a gust of its scales.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME wings shimmer with an iridescent sheen, the colours at their most brilliant in dim light. Their gem is used to channel psychic power, enabling them to launch attacks from a safe distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hides away deep in the forest, the light from its belly attracts other Bug Pokémon. Its vines are covered in thousands of poisonous scales that are incredibly dangerous to breathe in.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's wheels allow it to traverse over all terrains with equal ease. It has a reputation for defeating powerful Dragon-type Pokémon in combat, sometimes being nicknamed The Dragonslayer.
author: sk372

entry: Some POKENAME develop much thicker body fuzz than unfused Venomoth. Their thicker body fuzz allows them to make their homes at higher altitudes but makes them more likely to avoid flames.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Some POKENAME have a far more intimidating appearance than unfused Venomoth, their wings bearing bright eye spots and their abdomen appearing to have stingers. Despite their aggressive appearance, they are no more dangerous than other POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME produce a bright, flammable gel that creates toxic clouds of smoke when burnt. Many people report prolonged sluggishness after they inhale the noxious smoke.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At night, POKENAME emerges to scatter shimmering purple dust that paralyzes prey. It then drags victims underground to consume them slowly.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME spots someone wandering its caves, it releases pink powder from its hidden tunnels. The powder stuns intruders before they are dragged underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal creatures that flutter around streetlamps at night. The shimmering dust from their wings is toxic to both Trainers and Pokémon, so many scientists recommend face masks for people walking around at night.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has an extremely dull intellect and flits and flutters seemingly aimlessly. In actuality, it's "shinytactic" - it is attracted to shiny things, and its big eyes are always scanning for them.
author: creaturecore

entry: The gem on its head is packed with vitamins. Doctors in ancient times would crush it up to mix with herbs to make remedies.
author: .izik

entry: The fine powder that falls from POKENAME's wings can trigger intense migraines. Prolonged exposure often causes confusion and disorientation.
author: .izik

entry: It flies into a rage when passersby approach, attacking unprovoked. However, since POKENAME energetically beats its wings to scatter poisonous dust, its small body is often carried up and away from its target.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Whenever POKENAME are angry, they produce a billow of dust that surrounds their body. This dust heightens an adrenaline response that tends to escalate situations.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Used heavily by Ranchers to herd Paras, POKENAME is a watchful and gentle guard Pokémon. When given its favorite mushroom treat, it often sends out sparks of various colors to entertain children.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME releases streams of bubbles mid-flight to clear obstacles in its path. The bubbles shimmer with a strange, protective coating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits special alpha waves from its body that are toxic and induce headaches just by being close by.
author: jhenebean

entry: While it has strong psychic abilities, a POKENAME's muscles are very weak. It uses its cape made of venomous scales to support itself.
author: jhenebean

entry: If any of POKENAME's poisonous scales touch your skin, the poison will quickly seep into your brain and make you unconscious. Thankfully, it is only active at night.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME is said to be nocturnal, but its formidable body never gets tired. It builds muscles by helping workers in poisonous forests.
author: jhenebean

entry: The flower it wields is said to be imbued with moonlight. Despite POKENAME's muscular build, it is an incredibly graceful and timid Pokémon. It would rather flee from a battle that it would otherwise win due to its strength.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME flit around woodlands searching for the heaviest plants they can find. Once they find a likely candidate, they heave it out of the ground and spend all night flying with it to work on their strength.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are popular companions for wrestlers, their muscular physique and varied combat style giving their Trainers the opportunity to practice their form. POKENAME can deliver a brutal Seismic Toss by grabbing their foe and flying through the air.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's main body segment has a complex arrangement of microscopic scales covering most of it. This segment contains enough heat to keep it warm in the winter and a way to regulate body heat through openings between the scales.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME hangs from tall trees, spreading poisonous dust from its wings. Once night falls, POKENAME will fly down to the forest to feed on anything that has succumbed to its dust.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME use their long, flexible limbs to swing through tree branches in search of a place to sleep for the day. Their bulbous eyes are sensitive to light and allow them to see in the dark, helping them find berries to feed on during the night.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME make their homes deep in old-growth forests, using their long tendrils to search through fallen trees for prey at night. They shun human contact, as the artificial lights used by people are painfully bright to their giant compound eyes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's wide eyes possess a sharp sight, letting it detect even the faintest cracks in stone. It strengthens its arm muscles by pummeling boulders into rubble over the course of several days.
author: sk372

entry: With a free and uncaring nature, it doesn't mind if it scatters poisonous scales from its wings while it rolls down mountains.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME leave clouds of shimmering dust in their wake. They enjoy galloping through grass at night and are drawn to bright lights from nearby homes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While sprinting, POKENAME releases clouds of hot purple powder from its wings. The air behind it shimmers with toxic heat.
author: .izik

entry: The fur along POKENAME's tail is lined with microscopic spikes, causing irritation and itching upon contact. This fur constantly sheds, scattering throughout its Trainer's homes.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME emits both a powerful magnetic force that is fatal to electronics and toxic dust that is dangerous to living creatures.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME is always seen with a stick from a plant and will scatter poisonous scales from its wings to defend it.
author: jhenebean

entry: It races through grassy plains with powerful strides, scattering paralyzing scales in its wake.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME trades its wings for three heads, hearts, and lungs. It is slower than before, but POKENAME can keep running for longer stretches of time.
author: jhenebean

entry: This Pokémon loves anything filthy. It constantly scatters toxic, dust-like scales from all over its body.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME uses a small wand of sorts to spread little bursts of its pollen to others. It seems to believe it is casting helpful spells, but in reality, the pollen tends to make others sick.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are too heavy to be able to fly, their weighty protective shell heavily limiting their mobility. Instead, they use their wings to flap gusts of wind at their foes, shedding toxic powder from their wings as they do so.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Many cases of sleep paralysis have been attributed to this dream-eating Pokémon.
author: jhenebean

entry: POKENAME frolics among Berry trees, sprinkling powder which helps them grow. Its powder's soothing properties are used to treat insomnia and anxiety.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME frolics among Berry trees, sprinkling powder which helps them grow. Its powder's soothing properties are used to treat insomnia and anxiety.
author: noel5229

entry: While POKENAME may seem scary because of their glowing bodies, they are rather friendly. Many POKENAME enjoy helping cafes sell food and even allow people to eat from their bodies in the form of Gratin a la Pumpkaboo.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wander forests and towns at night, using their sticks to create eerie melodies. Some people have made a tradition of leaving offerings for these Pokémon to appease them and ward off the speculated curses wrought by their music.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wear a mask that grows constantly, so they carry a carving knife made out of bone to adjust the holes in their mask. Without the carving knife, the holes in their mask would close and render them unable to see.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their hair to send a flurry of punches at opponents, their fists able to break concrete. They can extend their hair while punching, striking foes from afar, and ensnaring them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME pulls its body around using arms covered in sticky hairs. It also uses these arms as defense against Pokémon that would eat it by sticking the arms into the predator's mouth and allowing hairs to flake off, causing intense irritation.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME hugs distressed Grass-type Pokémon gently. It releases a warm Pumkin Berry scent that calms them almost instantly.
author: .izik

entry: On the night of a new moon, POKENAME likes to trap people in invisible mazes and chase them through. Those who fail to reach the exit before its song ends are dragged to the afterlife.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: Anyone who rides on POKENAME gets sailed into the afterlife. Its hairlike arms are freezing to the touch, immobilizing the victim and making them easier to carry off.
author: soup1900

entry: The song of each individual POKENAME is said to be different depending on their environs, yet it is said that songs curse all who hear them. What appear to be ears are actually arms, with which they can thoroughly ensnare their targets.
author: infinex21

entry: These lake-dwelling Pokémon emit a bright, albeit ominous, light from their large, hair-like feelers even from the darkest depths. On nights with full moons, they emerge and sing enchanting melodies that draw many to them.
author: infinex21

entry: These electrogenic Pokémon can produce and store so much electricity that their own bodies will emit faint flashes of light. They release electric bolts to stun and startle others, producing plenty of fear for them to feed on.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME sing to expel excess air, which helps to keep their internal flame sacs cool. In battle, they use their hair-like appendages to entangle foes before breathing fire upon them.
author: infinex21

entry: The dancing of its luminescent flames entices many, while the crackling of said flames is said to sound like music. Reportedly, the "music" sounds different for each individual. In battle, its flames roar and its hair-like vines rise into the air.
author: infinex21

entry: A soft light glows from inside POKENAME and shines through holes on its front. Though dim, the glow calms infants and young children, often lulling them to sleep.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME drifts through fields on autumn evenings, scattering glowing spores that nourish withering plants. Farmers welcome its arrival as a sign of a bountiful harvest.
author: vracken

entry: The glowing lantern face on POKENAME's abdomen attracts prey to its web, where they become stuck and it fully webs them up with the aid of its many hands. The webbing has a sugary pumpkin flavor, but is very sticky until washed.
author: pjporwoll

entry: At night, POKENAME floats joyfully above Pumkin Berry trees. During the day, it naps on the branches, letting out soft, comforting coos.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hairs are made up of tiny roots that grow from its body, fluttering through the air as it hops. Its body is extremely light and able to jump long distances with little effort, making it a swift and agile traveler.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gathers mud with its ear-like arms and coats its body to stay cool. Its habit gives it a constantly damp and earthy scent.
author: .izik

entry: Many tales speak of POKENAME that appear on moonlit nights, strolling through streets while singing eerie melodies. On nights when the moon is full, parts of their bodies glow softly, and their songs are at their loudest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's pumpkin-scented feathers are similar in texture to leaves. Many cultures boil the feathers with tea as a calming drink for those who are stressed, offering relief with its soothing fragrance.
author: .izik

entry: The Gourgeists attached to POKENAME's heads puppeteer them, controlling their every move. It is said that they are consuming these Pokémon's souls, leaving their bodies wandering around aimlessly.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's strange song has been known to boost the growth of various crops. Every autumn season, many rural villages hold special ceremonies to give thanks to the Pokémon.
author: mepp.

entry: At sunset, POKENAME's hair glows like a flickering torch. Its blinking lights lure travelers toward cliffs so it can feed on their fear as they fall.
author: .izik

entry: The upper half of POKENAME moves instinctively to protect its pumpkin-like torso. If struck, it retaliates with a sudden psychic blast from within its mouth.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hangs from pine trees, releasing a rotten pumpkin scent to keep predators away. As a final resort, it unleashes a fiery explosion to defend itself and its home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be found feeding on abandoned carved pumpkins after October. Some Trainers use POKENAME to cook pumpkin seeds.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's howls resonate in its hollow body, making a dreadful cacophony that sets anything in earshot alight. There are rare exceptions, as those dear to it only find their hairs singed.
author: dolly_cholli

entry: Devices that POKENAME have infested emit an odd pumpkin smell. They are thought to gain sustenance by absorbing feelings of paranoia from the meeker people whose computers they inhabit.
author: chibitales

entry: The serpentine ghastly aura is POKENAME's true body, while its armor is formed from rotten vegetables it has gathered. Sightings of this Pokémon are often accompanied by the putrid stench of decaying pumpkins.
author: adam_dnh

entry: This beautiful Pokémon is sometimes spotted flying in the autumnal night skies. It is rumored that if it flies over a plot of farm land, the fall harvest will be bountiful.
author: opossiblymage

entry: When a new moon rises, this Pokémon lures people in with an eerie voice, mimicking the person they most wish to see before leading them to the afterlife.
author: chaoticanzu

entry: These creatures love berries and prefer the Tamato Berry above all else as it is the perfect balance of nutrition and sweetness. They are known to eat so much that they get slower after digesting all the berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The burning light in POKENAME's eyes casts a lingering trail of eerie light as it cuts through the evening sky at high speeds. Some have likened the sound of its beating wings to soft, creepy laughter.
author: sk372

entry: The curses wrought by their songs bring deep slumber, yet some, such as insomniacs, consider this a boon rather than a curse. They metabolize moonlight and produce clean air around them; the latter is why most put up with them.
author: infinex21

entry: It can freeze the bristles lining its hairlike feelers to turn them into sharp blades. It wanders boreal forests, its cries reminiscent of eerie songs that many believe will curse listeners to an endless cold.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME watch over pumpkin patches and scare off any intruding Pokémon like Murkrow or Spearow. These Pokémon prefer to be stationary in the day outside of battle, but become much more active at night.
author: jangodiot

entry: Despite their mischievous appearance, POKENAME are incredibly loyal to their Trainers and will guard the patches they call home. Should they encounter a threat to their Trainer or home, they will kick their pumpkin at breakneck speeds.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: When disturbed while napping in shallow mud, POKENAME emits a foul gourd-like odor from its fins to drive intruders away. If this does not deter them, it will spit water in highly pressurized jets.
author: .izik

entry: Those who hear POKENAME hum its playful song are rumoured to be cursed for weeks. Strangely, it seems to hum more often around those with positive dispositions.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It delights in the happiness of others and will often sing to express its adoration. However, those who upset it will either be cursed forever or psychokinetically crushed.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It floats through town streets at night cursing anyone who hears its wicked melody. It psychokinetically crushes foes into the ground, forcing them to endure its song until their spirits wither.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It floats through town streets at night cursing anyone who hears its wicked melody. It psychokinetically crushes foes into the ground, forcing them to endure its song until their spirits wither.
author: h0bojoe

entry: It wanders through town streets at night fighting and robbing anyone it finds. It joyfully sings a wicked tune as it cuts down opponents with its cursed scythe.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME are popular Pokémon for Trainers in rural communities, their innate connection to the autumn harvest making them invaluable at knowing when pumpkins are ripe. They love to play in the fields, racing around as their leaves trail behind them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME maintain the pumpkin atop their backs to attract children during fall festivals. Once enough children have gathered, they play games and distribute berries from within the pumpkin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their hairlike tentacles to dig up their prey in the sand. Once found, POKENAME ensnare their prey before excreting a digestive enzyme. On nights of a new moon, it is said that POKENAME's victims can be heard on shorelines.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: The thick scales on POKENAME's body are similar in makeup to pumpkin shells. When stressed, the shells harden to become sturdier than marble, providing enhanced defense against physical attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Legends claim that when widely revered, POKENAME can grow 1,000 pumpkins in a single day. Most scholars consider these accounts children's folklore.
author: .izik

entry: At night, wild POKENAME patrol dark towns to find lost Pokémon and guide them to their next destination. How they know where the Pokémon wishes to go remains a mystery to this day.
author: npshi

entry: If a battle against it is left unfinished, POKENAME stalks its foe until challenged again. The seeds from its pulpy mane can be roasted and eaten.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a human to blend in with crowds during fall festivals. Despite its illusions, its strong pumpkin pie scent always gives it away.
author: .izik

entry: The sweet, yet haunting voices of POKENAME can be heard throughout many forests on nights with a new moon. They use their ribbon-like arms to grab prey, feeding off the fear they create by doing so.
author: chibitales

entry: When its poison weakens, POKENAME glows brightly from within. It uses this radiant intimidation display to trick foes into thinking it's still strong.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME promptly grabs the victim using its hairlike arms before quickly floating up and away to the afterlife. It must continuously take spirits to keep itself airborne; otherwise, it will crash into the ground and become immobile.
author: soup1900

entry: These extremely cautious Pokémon only come out at night, bouncing around and dancing within their forest homes. If a Trainer ever begins to hear them sing, they are advised to move far away to avoid being cursed.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME makes its arms stretch and grow to wrap around its victims. Getting ensnared by the larger variants leaves little hope for escape.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME hides among scarecrows in pumpkin patches, unmoving for days. Though it appears stuffed with hay, its filling is closer to synthetic cotton in structure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME travels by drifting on the autumn wind. It delights in spooking and disrupting humans with silly pranks.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME waits to ambush prey from its treetop home with a web of tangling hairs. When its prey is properly ensnared, it uses a Thunder Wave to paralyze them further before feasting.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's glowing back alerts others of nearby danger. It casts Safeguard to shield itself and allies when predators approach.
author: .izik

entry: On autumn nights, it floats through human neighborhoods, knocking on doors. Anyone who opens their door must give it candy, or they will be haunted on the following night.
author: hophoppip

entry: Both of its heads are mischievous, but they tend to disagree on how best to perform their tricky deeds. When the two heads cackle in unison, POKENAME has devised a truly devious trick.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME clings to cave walls and glows in rhythmic flashes. These light pulses form a full language, used to share information across tunnels.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's slow, faint singing carries a curse that afflicts those who hear it. Victims of the hex become greatly lethargic for the next 7 days.
author: sk372

entry: When its crank is turned for long enough, POKENAME springs out of its box and cackles deviously. The fright of its victim gives it strength.
author: hophoppip

entry: The root growing from POKENAME's head can become extremely long as it ages. It will drag it along the ground as it travels through cemeteries, adding to its eerie presence as it haunts the quiet graves.
author: .izik

entry: Pumpkin-scented ooze covers POKENAME's body, glowing softly as it floats through forests. It scans for prey using psychic pulses.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts above lavender fields on autumn winds, emitting a scent of roasted pumpkin seeds. Its light body allows it to hover effortlessly for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its vines to steer while rolling. This control lets it accelerate and carve tight turns, leaving a yellow glow in its wake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME was a nocturnal terror of the ancient world, hunting prey in the dead of night. The fluid leaking from its hollowed-out torso was a toxic substance meant to mark territory and warn rivals and trespassers.
author: sk372

entry: It is sought after by chefs around the world, as their leaves can be dried to produce a syrup that tastes like currants. Chefs are working with conservationists to keep the wild population high while still catering to the needs of customers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is said to form when spirits possess a large pile of rotten pumpkin innards. It's said to lurk on mid-autumn nights to take the souls of those who are wasteful.
author: hophoppip

entry: Their sap produces a yellow luminescent glow that illuminates cavities. Their body cavities act as a woodwind instrument close to the recorder, as wind passing through produces a high-pitched whine.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While flying at night, POKENAME's belly pulses in time with its wingbeats. It uses Air Cutter to defend itself from aerial threats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blasts sonic waves from its ears while releasing a sweet aroma like pumpkin pie. The combination bewilders foes before it attacks under cover of confusion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cries an eerie song as it flies through country villages on nights of a full moon. Its wings are made of fibrous strands similar to pumpkin vines.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME stores volatile ghostly energy within its hollow torso. When enraged, it forms spectral arms from its core to strike down threats with terrifying force.
author: .izik

entry: Powered by the harvest moon, many POKENAME stand guard to protect valuable crops from wild Pokémon while appearing as lifeless scarecrows. They will awaken and quickly attack any approaching wild Pokémon with extreme prejudice.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Appearing in empty lots or dark forest clearings, POKENAME will attempt to lure others inside of them. They create hallucinations and feed off of their victim's fear, but will harmlessly spit them out once satisfied before vanishing into the night.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME comes out of hiding at night and chants with a euphonious voice that draws both people and Pokémon to listen to its music. People report feeling lethargic after hearing its song as though they were drained of their vitality.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As it flies, POKENAME's wings shine while spreading pumpkin-scented powder. This orange dust is strong enough to knock out a Tyranitar.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that on festive fall nights, POKENAME can be seen wandering pumpkin patches searching for people to take to the afterlife. Small towns often have traditions involving giving POKENAME candy.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: These Pokémon often get mistaken as trick-or-treat buckets. Anyone who eats the sweet treats that come from inside its body will be cursed.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's head is extremely sweet. Many cultures serve small boiled slivers of the lily pad on top of a slice of pumpkin pie for a delightful dessert that balances sweetness with earthiness.
author: .izik

entry: It will dance a tango with the elderly, hypnotizing them into dancing with them as it guides them to the afterlife. They are most often found after an autumn festival.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME floats high over pumpkin patches at night to ensure the crops are left undisturbed by Pokémon like Murkrow. It will use a Power Gem to scare them away, ensuring the patch's safety.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies high above crop fields with a yellow glow pulsing from its body. It patrols the skies swiftly, seeking intruders from above.
author: .izik

entry: Its sugary sweet innards harden into edible candy pieces when exposed to the open air. POKENAME enjoys gifting the candied pieces of its body to any well-behaved children it sees.
author: griddle

entry: POKENAME masquerades as a spooky decoration, using its bowl-like tail to lure in unsuspecting trick or treaters. Some say that once they grab a coin, it swiftly snatches them as they become more coins for its hoard.
author: dolly_cholli

entry: The bill-like leaf protruding from POKENAME's head was once used in powders to treat migraines. The leaf was ground up and boiled with Red Apricorns, served in wooden cups for soothing relief.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wander through rural communities in the dead of night, their bodies overflowing with spiritual energy. They seek out other nocturnal Pokémon to do battle with, striking out with their spectral fists in a flurry of blows.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME takes a prized possession from every foe it bests in combat, hoarding it in large pumpkins it personally carves. The greater the hoard, the higher its status among its kind.
author: sk372

entry: An ethereal flame burns beneath the head, allowing POKENAME to function even without its cranium. All attempts made to douse this otherworldly fire have failed.
author: sk372

entry: As it rolls, POKENAME releases a scent like pumpkin pie. Should it bump into something, it may suddenly detonate in a burst of gravel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME run through towns to bring light and warmth to those hard at work during chilly nights. In some towns, it has become tradition for people to help keep the lanterns burning by giving a POKENAME a candle before it leaves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is a gentle creature often used on farms to pull carts filled with pumpkins. When it becomes excited, the flames burning inside its body cause its eyes to glow with a warm, fiery light.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its pot is said to be a part of itself that it has long since shed, which it now uses in tandem with its large plant stalk to make meals and other concoctions. It is a very intelligent Pokémon that never wastes a single resource nor a single action.
author: infinex21

entry: It is the goopy insides of POKENAME that move around far more than the Gourgeist-shaped body, leading many to suspect that what constitutes a brain actually resides in the muck. While POKENAME focuses, the more solid body stops blinking entirely.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME often appears in the woods at night to find and hypnotize lost children. Despite bedtime stories depicting it as a monster that eats people, POKENAME actually leads wayward kids back home.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Its fluffy, candy-like body is often mistaken for cotton candy, and the candy-cane tail on its back is sharp. It is sometimes used in fancy restaurants to test dishes for sweetness and bitterness.
author: duskit___

entry: POKENAME is a bit of a menace to some due to its tendency to explode. While it doesn't cause much physical damage, the explosion shoots sticky candy floss all over its surroundings, which is painfully difficult to clean up.
author: sk372

entry: If a group of POKENAME finds a pastry they like, they will carry it around with them. If any Pokémon tries to steal it, POKENAME will violently attack.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME wears a skull made of exquisitely crafted sugar. It lives in cemeteries and leaves sweet breads at the graves there in hopes of enticing friendly visitors.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is beloved at parties. Cotton candy taken from its gloves can be added to tea, where it results in an unexpectedly strong flavor.
author: shyguy11011

entry: The sweet-smelling gas POKENAME emits still has the potential to be toxic to living beings. POKENAME prefers to eat sweet Berries over other types of food.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has a long piece of candy cane that it uses as a horn. It may invite Pokémon that like to eat sweets to suck on the horn until it is sharp.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME are said to have a major sweet tooth. Whenever one is nearby, sweets are said to taste at least ten times better.
author: rumia_archer

entry: It slices through opponents using hardened scythes made of apricots and cream. On the rare occasion its scythes are eaten, it regenerates the scythes in one day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using the sweet fur they produce like Spinarak silk, POKENAME weaves intricate nests for themselves. They unintentionally trap Bug Pokémon drawn to the sugary smell.
author: lampent12

entry: When in battle, POKENAME will tangle its opponent in sweet and sticky threads before striking with a Headbutt. It enjoys eating any sweets it can find, often finding itself in trouble when it ends up stealing said sweets.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have a fruity flavour, but the specific fruit is unrecognisable, so it is believed to taste like an extinct berry species. For this reason, they are seen as a delicacy in many locations.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are oft considered to be overly friendly due to how they will lick others with their sticky tongues just after meeting them. Their bodies are extremely soft and spongey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME produce honey that smells and tastes like cotton candy. They are very protective of this honey and pelt intruders with dozens of Poison Sting attacks. People who manage to collect the honey often sell it for a high price.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's gummy tail is said to taste like every single sweet food in the world, but no one has ever gotten close enough to confirm it. The tail also ripples with a strange pulse that many find deeply unsettling.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are incredibly shy, though become very friendly and remain loyal for years if treated well. They will loose sticky  and sweet threads to entangle foes and some will do the same to their friends as a sort of prank.
author: infinex21

entry: The small berries that grow from POKENAME's neck are packed with sugar, which makes them highly addictive amongst young children. The berries have been commonly used as a natural sweetening agent.
author: mistymagius

entry: When threatened, it produces heat from its back. The sugary fibers adorning it quickly catch fire and burn powerfully.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME has a sweet tooth and a penchant for biting things. Oversized hard candies make an excellent treat for a POKENAME.
author: hophoppip

entry: A retractable cone-like tail lets POKENAME lift itself up to better survey its surroundings. It playfully lobs parts of its sticky body at others in order to share the sweetness of its taste.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is nocturnal, with the only sign of its presence being the trailing wisps of sugary mist it leaves behind. It is often seen as an annoyance due to this mist attracting Bug-types to fields of crops and even homes.
author: robbery_666

entry: Popular Pokémon at fair booths, POKENAME's silk is sweet in nature and bundled up as cotton candy. They often have to fight off Flying-types that try to steal children's candy.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME uses the sweet scent of its glowing lollipop lure to hunt for its prey. It is so tempting that POKENAME can't help giving it the occasional taste.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME runs around with an outburst of hyper energy, the sticky strings that compose its body clinging to all surfaces it touches. Without warning, it crashes to the ground, asleep.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are covered in a fine layer of soft, edible hair with a wonderfully sweet flavour. They are popular Pokémon for confectioners, and POKENAME hair is said to give the eater sweet dreams.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's wool is entirely made of cotton candy. The taste is so sour that it can feel like an electric shock to your taste buds.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's feathers have a soft texture that has been compared to cotton candy. They're patient with young children and tolerate petting well, even when their feathers are accidentally pulled.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Known as "The Baker's Nightmare". POKENAME are mischievous creatures that love sneaking into bakeries at dawn to rummage for new delicacies. If discovered in the act, they tend to throw handfuls of flour into the eyes of pursuers.
author: merclipse

entry: POKENAME produces a sweet syrup-like gel and travels the ocean seeking to find the perfect accompaniment to it. Once it finds it, it is overcome with joy and evolves.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME produces a sweet syrup-like gel and travels the ocean seeking to find the perfect accompaniment to it. If it finds it, it will share it with one other, some Trainers have been lucky to try it, and rave about it for the rest of their lives.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The candy-cane on the back of a POKENAME is quite sharp, especially since bakers shave off pieces to add to baked goods. Pieces of their sweet and fluffy bodies are incorporated into desserts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produce a sweet meringue that bakers harvest for cupcakes. In exchange for this meringue, bakers offer the first batch of cupcakes to POKENAME to ensure they will not get cursed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While hanging in the treetops, POKENAME are safe from most predators, though, due to their lack of mobility, they're quite vulnerable once they fall. Due to the sweet coating on their hard shells, other Pokémon are often found gnawing on them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's shell is covered with a layer of sticky candy floss. Anything that touches it will get the candy stuck to them, whereupon POKENAME will fervently lick the sticky part clean, as it adores the flavor of its own candy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME struggle to find food they can eat because of their soft teeth made out of gummies. They rely on people to feed them soft food at parks and are particularly fond of sweets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its body seems to be made of melted marshmallows, with any loose items getting stuck to it. POKENAME is also extremely hot, and its own body will start to burn if stationary for too long.
author: mistymagius

entry: Molten chocolate constantly flows from POKENAME's shell, leaving a sweet trail behind them wherever they crawl. They feed on fruit to maintain their naturally high sugar levels, offering chocolate-covered berries to people they like.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has a lot of energy and sheds profusely, so it requires a patient owner who is willing to spend time training it. Its fur has a slightly spicy and sweet flavor, so it is often used as a treat on its own or as a topping for ice cream.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME spits a sweet, sticky substance that smells of the finest cotton candy. When ensnared by this substance, those affected have reported feeling nausea and weakness.
author: evilgammon

entry: Each of POKENAME's punches or kicks is paired with a burst of shortcake-like scent, sweetening the air with every strike. The scent grows stronger the harder it fights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eats its own body weight in sugar every day and becomes grumpy if it doesn't get enough. It becomes hyperactive when it hears the sound of thunder.
author: robbery_666

entry: A very affectionate Pokémon, this fusion enjoys wrapping its body around a friendly Trainer in a warm but sticky hug. While the gesture is genuinely kind, the sticky residue must be cleaned immediately or sickness may ensue.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Although the sticky threads they spit to ensnare foes are reminiscent of cotton candy, and are edible, they are considered far too sour by most people. Their threads can conduct electricity and help them to paralyze prey and predator alike.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME consumes enough sugar, it produces mint-flavored candies from its mouth. These last for hours and cause anyone who eats them to grow drowsy.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME has a nose for bakeries and can detect powdered sugar from over a mile away. Cannoli are its favorite, and it's known to sneak into kitchens just to lick the cream filling.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME digs in loose dirt to hide from Bug-type Pokémon that are attracted by its sugary hide. It sheds its armored plates throughout life, which are collected and cracked open to expose the intensely sweet core as a crunchy dessert.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is one of the most popular pets in the region, which breeders take to high-end groomers for the perfect bangs. If a groomer does something it doesn't like, it will suddenly freeze its fur, but this just creates a sweet and popular icy treat.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME's fur coat is made of sweets; it creates so much candy fluff that it will not notice or care if clumps are taken and eaten by others. Its candy tusks are brittle and regenerate, so they too can be eaten by its friends.
author: sk372

entry: Ever autumn, POKENAME shed older feathers to make room for new ones, with the sheddings collected to be used as a topping for ice cream and other desserts. These feathers are very sweet and the taste has often been compared to Shuckle juice.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME bodies are coated in a thick layer of sweet candy. They are popular companions at carnivals and circuses where they will run up to children unprompted. When their candy is depleted they will curl up and wait for it to regrow.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is found in deserts where it can avoid water, which is dangerous to its sugary, protective coat. It can be found meticulously brushing grit and sugar clumps from its coat, which scavengers snap up once it moves on.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME gives off a very pleasant smell similar to toasted sugar. Its talons are very sticky, helping it keep a firm grip on the enemy while it attacks.
author: lydiaprower8
