entry: POKENAME is fueled by pure anger, destroying entire forests in fits of rage. Its axe is nearly indestructible and POKENAME can swing it with enough force to level a skyscraper.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME soars on desert winds as it searches for Cacturne to prey upon. When it finds its target, it swoops down at high speeds and dispatches them with a swift Blaze Kick.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME loathes sunlight, draping its loose skin over its heads like a hood. Bright light worsens its already poor eyesight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rams trees with powerful Headbutts to dam rivers. After completing its dam, it proudly cheers atop it at dusk.
author: .izik

entry: The skin on POKENAME's head and back hardens into golden armor. This shields it from attacks and even falling debris.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very self-conscious and will usually keep its skin tightly closed when others are around. However, when no one is looking, it can be seen destroying property and generally being a nuisance.
author: mistymagius

entry: In an attempt to demonstrate its toughness, POKENAME simply leaves its shed skin where it falls. Despite its indifferent attitude, if it sees anything bothering a Sandile, it will attack the offending presence.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME swings its tusks in octagonal arcs to intimidate. If the warning fails, it strikes with a devastating Focus Punch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is not the best flyer, as it has to hold up its loose skin while it flies. It is quite a territorial Pokémon and will try to damage its opponent's wings in the hopes of immobilizing them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sheds a slimy layer of its skin every day or two, keeping its body from drying up. The leftover skin carries anti-bacterial properties and is often sold as a special type of face mask.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's clothlike skin absorbs blows with ease. If it sees a foe stagger, it and its allies will Headbutt in unison to overwhelm them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's loose skin unfurls into long wings. It uses these to execute complex aerial combat maneuvers.
author: .izik

entry: When it spots a group of wild Pokémon, it challenges the leader for a one on one duel and robs the group of the food supplies if POKENAME wins. It has a symbiotic relationship with Scraraid and uses it as a shooting weapon.
author: milchik

entry: When scales fall off, POKENAME stores them in its loose skin. New ones regrow in under an hour, making it nearly impossible to wear down.
author: .izik

entry: It constantly hitches up its sagging, rubbery skin to protect its vitals during a brawl. Its massive, fan-like crest isn't just for show; it acts as a weighted club when delivering a devastating headbutt.
author: willowwhisker_98658

entry: This troublemaking POKENAME steals nearly anything it finds, favoring shiny objects and food. It has an odd preference for lasagna.
author: hophoppip

entry: No matter how many times POKENAME try to fix their appearance, they always struggle to properly wear their garments. Many develop headaches out of the countless hours they waste and eventually give up out of frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can detect even the most subtle scent of food with its nose. If it sees another Pokémon eating, it will fume into a rage—often triggering nearby Mankey to join in and coordinate to Beat Up the foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is known for its large muscles and seemingly pointless cruelty, beating up creatures it views as lesser on a whim. This description includes humans.
author: dylonk25

entry: Perhaps due to its more humanoid appearance, it has begun mimicking human behavior. Each POKENAME engages in different human activities, such as listening to music or even sports. It is still deadly powerful.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are incredibly territorial as they will beat up any other Grass Pokémon that enters its territory. Because of this, POKENAME are considered an invasive species.
author: mistymagius

entry: When floating dormant beneath a stream or pond, wild POKENAME are nearly impossible to distinguish between the surrounding lily pads. The leaf on its back is poisonous to ingest, serving as a defense mechanism against any potential predators.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME floats just beneath the surface of ponds, feasting on small aquatic plants that drift nearby. Its broad leaf and cattail-like appendage help it blend into the surrounding reeds, hiding it from bird Pokémon flying overhead.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME generally rests on the bottom of lakes and ponds, but floats to the surface when sleeping. Anything that hops onto its lilypad will wake it up and cause it to explode.
author: sk372

entry: Many POKENAME strive to carry their Trainer on their back, developing their strength with bundles of rocks. It is said that if they are able to carry their Trainer on their back and cross a river, their overwhelming joy causes them to evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It contentedly paddles around lakes and ponds, offering transport to any nearby people and Pokémon. Small Pokémon can ride on its head, and people and larger Pokémon can sit with the water lily.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME has the same broad leaf growing from its back as a Lotad, and it can be difficult to tell them apart at a glance. However, POKENAME's leaf is hot to the touch, so much so that the water around it may appear to be boiling.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: The lily pad atop POKENAME's head throws off its balance during flight. It often requires several tries to pluck even a single Green Apricorn from trees.
author: .izik

entry: At night, POKENAME sleeps face-down in ponds. In the morning, it grazes lazily on nearby flowers growing along the banks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spins intricate webs stretched across ponds. The sticky nets are designed to catch flying Pokémon gliding too close.
author: .izik

entry: Its “wool” is actually made up of millions of tiny plant fibers it creates through photosynthesis. This material is very versatile and used to create a lot of plant-based textiles.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When POKENAME are born, the leaf on their head is no larger than a new sprout, but it grows rapidly as they mature. Leaf size is a sign of status, and some POKENAME choose not to evolve, as Lombre all possess similarly sized leaves.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When floating dormant beneath a stream or pond, wild POKENAME are nearly impossible to distinguish between the surrounding lily pads. The leaf on its back is poisonous to ingest, serving as a defense mechanism against any potential predators.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME draw many Bug-type Pokémon to the water lily on their back to pollinate it. In exchange for pollination, many Bug-type Pokémon are given a moment of respite on the pad on their back.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME nests deep in lakeside reeds. If disturbed, it will immediately retaliate with a forceful blast of water to drive intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: The flower on POKENAME's tail secretes pink ink with a foul odor. It uses the ink to paint strange markings on stumps and rocks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through its lily pad before it attacks. Its Thunderbolt is strong enough to take down a tree in one strike, showcasing its powerful electric abilities.
author: .izik

entry: It wins battles with the expectation that it gets fed afterwards. As such, Trainers opt to feed it packets of Packaged Curry because it is cheap and easy to find.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME reside in desert oases, often found relaxing while spinning in circles. They rapidly dry out when out of water for prolonged periods of time, which can be seen in their lily pad.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: After a rainstorm, POKENAME stores water in the leaf on its head. During this time, small onion-flavored sprouts grow from its skin.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a master of combat in the marshes it calls home. The water in its lily pad is said to be capable of revitalizing stagnant ponds into a thriving ecosystem, with lotuses blooming brilliantly.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME's leafy feathers help propel this Pokémon's small body through the water of the pond they live in. Small Pokémon can hop onto the warm leaf on POKENAME's head and get a ride across the water.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Covered in aquatic plants, POKENAME generally stay near ponds that have clean water. When it gets excited, POKENAME will step onto land and hop around, spitting out small sparks of fire. If it gets overheated, POKENAME returns to the water.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME reside in desert oases, often found relaxing while spinning in circles. They will also play with other visiting Pokémon, spinning them around on their lily pad.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Preferring to swim in the pond waters it calls home, POKENAME will submerge itself so only its leafy head feather can be seen from the surface. If it senses danger near its home, POKENAME will let out a sharp cry to ward off any threats.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME will not hesitate to protect the clean waters where their kin reside. This display of courage has earned this Pokémon species the title “Defenders of the Pond”.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is surprisingly strong, so it can ferry any person or Pokémon that can fit on its head. It prefers to live in muddier waters.
author: torterraguy26

entry: POKENAME spits water at oranges in trees to knock them down for a quick meal. It attempts to catch the fruit in its lily pad, letting out a tiny squeak of happiness when successful.
author: .izik

entry: They swim on the surface of lakes and rivers, as they require clean water to wade in. They float to people who are having picnics or fishing by the water's edge, eager to join in on the fun.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cannot process saltwater, so they are only found near bodies of freshwater; similarly, they can only change the colors of their bodies within freshwater. The pads upon their heads do not change color unless they are in poor health.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have a special flower atop their backs that releases a cloud of pollen when disturbed. This does not stop many POKENAME from using their backs as a springboard, as many are too nimble for the cloud to cling to them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Water dripping from POKENAME's body is rich in nutrients. Ancient peoples believed it divine, claiming it could cure any illness.
author: .izik

entry: The pink flower on POKENAME's head spins rapidly counterclockwise when a predator is spotted. It fires jets of water from the flower with enough force to topple an oak tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME knows where pure springwater wells up, and it lets Pokémon sit on its lily pad so it can carry them there by swimming through bodies of water.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The tiny flower on POKENAME's shell carries a pleasant, subtle Green Apricorn scent. This smell intensifies while it sleeps, making the surrounding area pleasant to be in.
author: .izik

entry: Though they typically drift lazily across the water's surface, POKENAME are far more agile than they appear. By folding the lilypad atop their heads and tucking their limbs close to their bodies, they can swim at remarkable speeds.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME prefers to eat moss gathered near water sources, scorching it in its hand before consuming it. It can eat over 5 pounds of moss in a single meal due to its high metabolism.
author: .izik

entry: A group of POKENAME in the water is known as a "raft" due to the way their lily pad-like features cluster together. These Pokémon spend over 80% of their lives in the water.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's head occasionally detaches throughout the day. This becomes especially problematic when it swims at high speeds.
author: .izik

entry: It hides beneath the surface of ponds, buoyant through the aid of a floating cloth lily pad. When a Pokémon is swimming beneath it, it hurriedly scurries to the water's edge to avoid being seen from below.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Groups of POKENAME gather in rivers and streams, using their wide lilypad-shaped heads to provide crossings for smaller Pokémon. Though they possess one brain, it is unclear if it is housed in the Slakoth head above water or the Lotad head below.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through the lily pads on its head. It shocks small Pokémon like Caterpie when they approach its pond.
author: .izik

entry: The pad upon its head is capable of absorbing water and any minerals within the water as well. Although they gain nutrients from consuming minerals, most of the water they absorb or consume is simply stored so it may be expelled at their enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: These Pokémon are often found near waterfalls or standing directly beneath them. They are very calm and love the feeling of water cascading onto the blooming water lily on their backs.
author: naivetotoro

entry: POKENAME take long pieces of reeds to weave intricate nests that resemble an orb. Many nests are close to water so that POKENAME can quickly find reeds for any impromptu repairs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will use its leaf to carry water, which it pours over dirt-coated crystals. The cleaner the crystals, the better they taste to POKENAME.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME munches on underwater plants and small fish, eating until the food sources are depleted. Water stored in the dish on its head sustains it as it travels on land to find a new feeding zone.
author: sk372

entry: Bartenders work alongside POKENAME to serve delicious drinks. Its nectar is an important ingredient for many sweet beverages, and its head provides a flat surface for patrons to rest their glasses on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME survives off leachate siphoned from landfills. Because of this, all of its water attacks are filled with bacteria and should be avoided when possible.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will fly around in caves to find lost people. They use echolocation to find their way in the dark, even deep underwater. POKENAME will use its sharp cries to annoy anyone approaching their caves.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME joyfully flies over ponds, singing as it glides. It prefers to sleep floating peacefully on the water's surface.
author: .izik

entry: When submerged, POKENAME's cotton-like innards expand. This bizarre adaptation greatly boosts its physical strength in the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME catches rainwater in the lily pads growing from its back. If it walks carefully, it can use them to transport small amounts of water from one place to another.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME often uses the overgrowth of its marshy home to hide its lower torso from view. Its reason for doing so is unknown.
author: .realthree

entry: Although POKENAME are commonly seen ferrying other Pokémon that can't swim, it's a rare sight to see them carrying each other. After much research, it turns out they're simply having fun.
author: metcassette

entry: POKENAME swim through meandering rivers, taking a languid approach to their life. They are amiable toward other wild Pokémon and offer to help carry them across the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's head grows increasingly large the more sunlight it absorbs. Ancient cultures once believed that eating portions of it would help someone forget heartbreak, though in reality, it caused only intense nausea.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can hold its breath for up to half an hour. It sticks its head under the water's surface so only its lily pad is visible as it waits to drift closer to its prey.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME waits for up to 30 minutes in ponds, disguising itself as common pond foliage. If a Pokémon or person gets too close, it leaps out of the water to attack.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME waits for up to 30 minutes in ponds, disguising itself as common pond foliage. If a Pokémon or person gets too close, it leaps out of the water to attack.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Despite their cute appearance, POKENAME are fiercely territorial. They are known for clashing with other Pokémon in marshy climates for warmer burrowing spots.
author: retrodox

entry: In the early days of Fusion technology, it was believed that the color of POKENAME's lily pad indicated what it evolved into. However, this has been proven to not be the case. It eats a variety of flora and loves damp places.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's back acts as wings, allowing it to extend flight without landing. Should it grow exhausted, it lands in a freshwater source and gnaws on nearby water-based flora.
author: .izik

entry: Trainers are advised to keep an ear out while walking through areas where POKENAME live. They enjoy popping out suddenly, spooking people and Pokémon alike. They can often be heard before they pop out by a hollow wood-esque jingling noise.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME blooms are enjoyed for their soft pink colour, as many artists actively seek them out as a muse for their paintings. They prefer to be solitary and waddle away into ponds when disturbed, firing off a rapid Bullet Seed if they can't escape.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rest within water, their pads keeping them afloat. They can absorb sunlight through their pads to acquire nutrients. When they grow closer to evolving, they become so heavy that they sink; at this point, they will also feed on algae.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME chews on reeds along pond edges. Once full, it stores the leftover reeds atop its lily pad head to dry for later.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nest near ponds of clean water; they are often seen resting on or in the water. Because of the pads on their heads, they cannot fly when it is raining. They scatter water from their pads as they fly, so the lands around them are often lush.
author: infinex21

entry: When the lily pad on POKENAME's head dries out, it swoops to the sea's surface. It dunks itself underwater before flying off again.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scoops marshy, algae-filled water into its mouth while flying. It can survive on this alone, but will be very lethargic throughout the period.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of ferrying other Pokémon across bodies of water without breaking surface tension. They are offered berries in exchange for their service, but refuse the gifts since they are always willing to help others.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The antenna on POKENAME's head closely resembles a cattail. They are incredibly sensitive to sound and twitch rapidly whenever something loud makes noise nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoy playing in ponds and lakes, submerging themselves so that only their lily pad is visible above the water. Frustratingly for their trainers, POKENAME hate having baths, scratching at people whenever someone tries to wash them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spends each day lazily seeking the ideal spot in its pond to sunbathe. It only leaves the water at night in order to groom its fur.
author: rymyll_the_wanderer

entry: POKENAME emit electric currents to sense nearby allies while swimming. When two approach each other too closely, the negative charges in their bodies repel one another automatically. Thankfully, these Pokémon can control this ability.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME filter feeds by opening its mouth incredibly wide to suck in swamp water. Any algae and plants it inhales are dissolved over the course of several days.
author: .izik

entry: When suffering from intense headaches, the lily pad on POKENAME's head turns brown. Eating berries can ease the pain temporarily.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME relentlessly hunts Seviper with powerful jets of water. Spotting one sends it into a frenzy as it charges forward to attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swim across the water by slithering in a unique wave-like pattern. This allows them to access aquatic prey and gives them a way to escape from local Zangoose that they may encounter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When enraged, POKENAME detaches the lily pad from its head and hurls it like a shuriken at its foe with surprising force. Its balance improves dramatically when the lily pad is off of its head.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME live in ponds and use the tiny lily pad on their head to convert sunlight into electrical energy. If an individual dives, others in the group instinctually follow them, fearing danger from predators on the surface.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME float on the surface of tropical lakes and are always on the move. Their restlessness stops if they are given a cucumber, their favourite food.
author: mr.person__prinplup_enjoyer

entry: POKENAME is sensitive to pollutants in the forest ponds it calls home. The spiral pattern on its belly will turn a sickly yellow if it does not have clean water to splash in.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME sleep along the surface of ponds, stretching out and basking in either rain or sunlight. If a POKENAME senses ill intentions while someone steps along its back, it will teleport away and let them fall into the water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is rarely spotted by gentle streams and somewhat shallow ponds, meditating and calmly communicating with other wild Pokémon on occasion. It is thought POKENAME imparts advice onto others in a sagely fashion.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is weak by nature and can only build up its strength by lifting cattails. Afterward, it eats the cattail for a boost of protein and potassium.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME anchors its roots at the bottom of ponds, exposing only its head by stretching its vine-like torso. It fires Acid at passing prey like Pidgey to knock them into the water.
author: .izik

entry: Drifting placidly in the sky, POKENAME use the leaves on their heads as sails. These leaves double as a raincoat, shielding their magnets from rust.
author: hortensia_xxiii

entry: The three heads of POKENAME take turns bobbing down into lakes, gathering water in their large shared lilypad to save for later. The lilypad filters the water as it falls, moisturizing POKENAME's central body.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Care should be taken when one sees a lilypad floating on a lake. It could actually be POKENAME, which will explode the moment something touches the lilypad on its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in dense swamps, building its nest amongst the weeds. The lilypad on its head is surprisingly dense, being made up of a material similar to bone.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are mischievous creatures, frequently popping out of rivers to startle people before nudging them with their horns. Despite their playful nature, they can crush boulders with ease.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME extends its vines through the pond water, using them to detect and capture prey like Poliwag. Once captured, it repeatedly slams the prey against shoreline rocks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cares for the adolescent Pokémon in its community, creating games in the shallows and splashing them with water from its crown. During wildfires, it shepherds young and injured Pokémon to the water, where it tends to those it can help.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME wings are peppered with small red flowers that are native to swampy environments. They release an intoxicatingly pleasant aroma that attracts other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If it senses intruders near its pond, POKENAME will quickly erect invisible walls to protect its territory. The walls can be as strong as steel.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is similar in composition to pond water. Aquatic plants grow on it, granting it excellent camouflaging in ponds.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME keeps the lily pad on its head and its reed-like tails above water, attracting different types of prey. It strikes with super-heated water whenever a target draws near.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's wings allow it to reach high speeds while swimming under a lake's surface. Its swift movements make it an excellent swimmer and a fast hunter.
author: .izik

entry: While standing motionless in a pond, POKENAME gains uncanny insight into the future of anyone nearby. Somehow, the water enhances its precognitive abilities.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's lilypad-covered head and tail are extremely buoyant, preventing it from drowning if it falls asleep while swimming. This is especially useful on days where it gets little sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores water inside the lilypad on its head. It flies with such steady grace that not even a single drop is spilled, no matter how fast it moves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends its days playfully splashing in ponds and streams, bringing festivity to all Trainers. At night, it sleeps upside down, using its lily pad as a buoy to float gently across the water's surface.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Water that flows out of POKENAME's lily pad accumulates nutrition from the oils that come from its body. Many pharmacies stock cough syrups that contain this ingredient, which is known for its soothing properties.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can jump several times their length on both particularly sunny or rainy days. However, the older they get, the less far they can jump. The leaves that grow from their body are very poisonous.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's water-soaked body absorbs attacks with ease. It remains calm and passive in most situations, especially when it's quietly eating.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME suspends itself from pine trees with white silk. It collects rainwater in its lily pad during storms to avoid traveling for hydration.
author: .izik

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's head gradually fills with lava during combat. It splashes this at foes to keep them at bay, compensating for its lacking agility.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gathers seawater in its fins as it ferries small Pokémon like Corsola. This keeps them safe from predators like Mareanie between reefs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME paints as a hobby, particularly enjoying landscapes. If the subject includes lily pads, like the one on its head, POKENAME becomes ecstatic.
author: chaotic_aspergers

entry: When hungry, POKENAME releases pulses of electricity from its head to cook water herbs nearby. It stores uneaten herbs at the bottom of its pond.
author: .izik

entry: The lilypad atop POKENAME's head radiates intense heat, boiling the pond it lives in. Other Pokémon avoid the scalding water it calls home.
author: .izik

entry: With grace and flair, POKENAME brews strange teas by steeping rare herbs in the bowls it balances. The aroma of its concoctions can soothe even the most irritable foes.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME travel in groups of five, beaching themselves at night with water stored in their lily pads. This keeps them safe and hydrated until dawn.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is always eager to please because of its servile nature. It makes a great restaurant waiter because the pad on its head helps it carry dishes to customers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are known for being little pranksters. Hopping around their pond, they will jump onto the leafy heads of their siblings to startle them, then cheep happily as it runs away.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME jumps out of rivers as high as it can to train its leg muscles. This training method unintentionally startles the Pokémon in the surrounding area.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's leafy green body helps it blend perfectly into their home ponds and rivers. It enjoys waiting for enemies to get close enough before startling them with an uppercut.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's head dries out rapidly during the summer months. Because of this, it strives to stay submerged and out of direct sunlight.
author: .izik

entry: When they enter Pokémon contests, a Trainer may include a Green Scarf to help foster innovative displays of brilliance. They are known to excel at providing new ways of aquatic entertainment, utilizing the Green Scarf to amaze audiences.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To meditate, POKENAME balances on one leg atop lilypads, channeling psychic energy to promote inner focus and muscular strength. It makes a humming noise during this time.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps in ponds during the day, camouflaging every part of its body except for the lily pad on its head. It is very skittish and will run away to hide if it senses danger.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME lives close to the water's edge. It enjoys being a nuisance to fishermen in its territory, using its sharp teeth to cut their lines.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME seek out crystal-clear ponds, filling the mouth-like lily pad on their heads with water. They take this water back to their young, giving them a safe place to splash and play.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME lies still near the edge of lakes, mimicking a plant to lure and ambush prey. It has been known to take delight in startling humans as well.
author: mepp.

entry: It floats along the surface of the water to steal snacks and vegetables that fall into the water. It prefers bland and watery food, which is why it goes for cucumber slices first.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It wanders into schools or parks to seek out picky eaters to steal undesired food from. It loves bland and watery treats, so these picky eaters remove cucumbers and other vegetables from their salads for it to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The large flower growing from POKENAME's shell gives off a mossy pine scent. This attracts bug types to help alleviate the buildup of pollen.
author: .izik

entry: Water that lingers too long in the lily pad on POKENAME's head begins to boil. It flings this at foes in an attempt to blind them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collects perfectly round lily pads and wears them as temporary hats. If it finds one larger than its current one, it will immediately discard the old one and show its new hat off to its buddies.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME settles itself into ponds to soak for a majority of the day. It inhales water up through its bush-covered nose, filtering out minerals and detritus, creating pure water that flows from its head back down into the pond.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often seen peacefully sleeping in calm bodies of water during the day. When night falls, POKENAME will often elegantly dance and cause mischief around the lakes they sleep in.
author: krivaswell

entry: POKENAME uses its large lily pad like a sail, catching winds to drift across great distances. It uses this to find secluded swamp nesting spots.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, it will eject a vine from its guts and spring out of the water, relocating itself to a new pond or stream.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME bursts from marsh water in a dazzling shower of lily pads as it unfurls its watery wings. In wetlands, seeing a wild POKENAME flying with the sunrise reflecting off of its wings has become a sign of a happy day ahead.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's tail grows based on its nutrition. It will eat cattails at the river's edge when it feels too lazy to hunt, using them to replenish its strength.
author: .izik

entry: Although POKENAME are small, they are strong enough to carry boulders nearly twice their size atop the pads on their heads. They can release water from the ports along their bodies, which they mostly do for the sake of startling others.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a playful Pokémon that likes splashing others with water from the leaf on its head, which it keeps warm with its tail. Healthy POKENAME have stronger flames and hotter water, but must be careful not to let the fire go out.
author: torterrable

entry: POKENAME has a mischievous charm to it. It captivates with a beautiful dance before firing darts at the enemy.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's gelatinous outer layer thickens when it touches swamp water. It uses psychic power to lift cattails and devour them when hungry.
author: .izik

entry: They rest in shallow and slow-moving rivers during the day, and take flight during the evening. Their bodies are terribly slimy, and they typically smell of muck.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is both a clever predator and a prankster. It lies in wait in the swamp water, disguising itself as a lily pad, before popping out to snatch fish Pokémon or frighten Trainers.
author: opossiblymage

entry: When nest building, POKENAME steal nest parts from other Pokémon, as this is often easier than finding reeds and twigs themselves. Many nests are conveniently located near water, allowing POKENAME to bathe as needed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drinks nutrient-rich swamp water to survive. At night, its lily pad heats up significantly, keeping predators away while it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: As it glides over marshes, POKENAME spits jets of swamp water at prey. Once stunned, it uses Leech Life to drain their remaining strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rolls through marshes at high speed, spinning its lily pads like wheels. It searches eagerly for cattails, its favorite snack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a little pest inhabiting jungle riverbeds. Floating around pretending to be a lily pad, it pops up suddenly when others are near to spit a mixture of water and seeds it has gathered, solely to irritate them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bounces its lily pad between its talons while it dances, cheering on its allies during combat. This rhythmic motion boosts morale, helping its team stay energized.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME waves its leaf-like wings back and forth while it dances on the water's surface. Most of its dancing only happens at night, adding to its mysterious allure.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dissolves rotting trash in water stored within the lily pad on its head. It eats very little, surviving on less than 5 pounds of refuse per week.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wander along swampy shores to ensure that no intruders threaten the safety of the marshlands they call home. It is believed that POKENAME are vengeful spirits from ecosystems polluted beyond recognition.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME can be heard flying through the sky on warm, humid nights. They enjoy diving right beside boats to scare those inside.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is found living near clean streams and ponds. It is known for its mischievous antics, which include spraying water on unsuspecting fishermen.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME fly over rivers and other bodies of water, performing sweet melodies. It only stops singing when it comes to the ground to eat and sleep.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME are experts at camouflage, as the leafy pad on their head gets partially submerged when they hop into swampy water. The crimson flower in the middle of their lily pad is also poisonous, which limits the number of wild predators they have.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The water in POKENAME's cotton-soft lily pad was once used in poultices. Herbalists claim it healed cuts and migraines with surprising speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats on its back in ponds, its fluffy body absorbing water like a sponge. When disturbed, it delivers powerful kicks to drive intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: Each of POKENAME's tentacles has a set of pink toxic claws that grab onto prey. Even a small scratch can cause seizures, making it a highly dangerous creature to approach.
author: .izik

entry: Some say that near a lake at night, you may see a POKENAME dance, swaying as if in a trance. It will close its eyes and move like the wind itself guides its body, only the sounds of nature acting as its accompaniment and the moon as its spotlight.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME are native to swamplands and tropical coasts, where it uses its lily pad mimicry to stealthily make mischief. It delights in biting through fishing nets or psychically causing headaches in boat pilots so they run aground.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME cultivates patches of mushrooms to grow in nutrient-rich mud that can be found in swamps and marshes. Despite having a lily pad atop its head, it does not like the sensation of being stepped on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sit in the water, eating algae, held up by their buoyant neck leaf. In dry seasons when water dries up, it will bury its lower half in the ground, eating nothing and drinking the small amount of water pooling in the dirt.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME manipulates small amounts of water into the lily pad on its head while sleeping, using its peculiar cattail. It absorbs this water through the night to stay hydrated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have been spotted more and more at surfing contests over the past few years. They are seen popping out of the water and scaring surfers into falling off their boards.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's shell contains water and consumed herbs that steadily brew while it basks in the sun. A steam cloud billows from its shell when the mixture has reached the perfect temperature, with the resulting tea being considered a delicacy in Hoenn.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sits at the bottom of the river, patiently waiting for other Pokémon to land on its lily pad. Once they do, it will drag them underwater with its arms and slowly drain them of their life force while still submerged.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME live in still ponds and are indistinguishable from Lotad whilst submerged in the water. They are very lethargic and are hard to motivate, preferring to just sit in the sun all day.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME alternate which of their two heads they keep above the water, taking turns to have the head underwater feed on pond weed. Their heads have different temperaments, most commonly one is friendly whilst the other is cantankerous.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME digs its way into ponds within home gardens, waiting for owners to inspect the newly-appeared lily pad. Once they come close, it pops out and spits water in their face.
author: sk372

entry: Legends claim drinking pond water from POKENAME's lilypad while thinking of a loved one ensures returned affection. In truth, it only causes stomachaches.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the broad leaf on its head to collect water during the day, then wakes up at night to drink it. It can't do much else, so it watches others play as it awaits its evolution.
author: torterrable

entry: POKENAME gather in groups of three within lakes. When disturbed, they trigger a chain of explosions across the water to drive intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires seeds at fruit trees to knock ripe produce loose. It drags the fruit back to its pond and eats safely underwater.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dives into the water to pluck seagrass that it uses to build its shoreline nest. The lily pad on its head helps provide cover from potential predators. If something gets too close, POKENAME flaps its wings and squawks loudly to scare it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: While POKENAME can travel across the surface of water without causing ripples, their lily pad is too small to carry other Pokémon. This does not stop other Pokémon from trying to hop on, which ends with both Pokémon getting wet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While flying above swamp water, POKENAME will stop immediately and dive beneath the surface the moment it spots a large patch of algae. It consumes as much as it can, emerging only when completely full.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dislikes bright sunlight and hunts after sunset. It uses its lily pad to camouflage as it stalks prey in shallow waters.
author: mepp.

entry: These mischievous Pokémon will purposefully antagonize anyone they can find, though their primary aim is to force a battle. Every battle they partake in greatly strengthens them, even if they lose, so it is difficult to break a POKENAME's habits.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME enjoy sifting through muddy river beds in search of shiny objects. Archaeologists will sometimes make use of them when searching for evidence of ancient settlements, relying on POKENAME to find old coins in the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME roams waterfronts where food is plentiful.  By day, it hunkers down, absorbing sunlight through the lilypad on its back, and by night, it wanders about, eating aquatic plants.
author: imaginita

entry: It is known to help gardeners sow and water many types of berries by carrying water on top of its head. However, it digs up spicy ones such as the Figy Berry and tosses them aside instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be highly territorial whenever anything enters their swamps. Their tough fur is ideal for moss to grow given how long they spend in their swamps.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME make underwater nests to prevent local Zangoose from destroying their eggs. When it is raining, they can absorb fresh water to rejuvenate their bodies and keep their scales well-hydrated.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME keep their body underwater during the day with only their lily pad resting above the surface. They venture out at night, but appear to experience intense headaches if they become too dry, invariably leading them to submerge themselves again.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME enjoy ferrying Pokémon around on their back but teleport away when a Trainer is spotted, bringing the rider with them. Once they sense that the Trainer has left the area they were in, POKENAME teleport back to continue the ride.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A trickster Pokémon that can control water and wetland plants, POKENAME pranks those who come too close by causing them to fall into muck or soaking them in water all while staying out of reach.
author: bobosmith01

entry: They become intoxicated on a Hopo Berry whenever they find one, which helps calm them down before they sleep. When they wake up, they may become confused and unable to recognize where they are for a moment.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can detach the lilypad from the end of its stick, hurling it like a discus. The blow is strong enough to topple a willow tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a mischievous spirit and will create fictitious feuds with its fake water heads to draw attention to itself. While its wings are too short to fly, they give it just enough lift to allow it to run across water to escape trouble.
author: soup1900

entry: Hearing music compels POKENAME to begin gyrating and dancing about in glee. Doing so causes it to shake loose copious fruits and berries growing on its head, making it an easy food source to gather from.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bellow out melodic tones loud enough to ripple water around them. The bubbles that surround their bodies echo with the notes of their songs, creating a chorus singing along to their tunes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME was famous a good few years ago, but this Pokémon has seemingly declined in popularity over time. POKENAME is widely known for its eccentric dances that never seem to end.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME carries a makeshift parasol to gather rainwater and keep itself dry. When the weather is bright and sunny, it dances with joy and shares the pure water with other Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME quietly hum a tune as they swim along rivers, keeping themselves busy as they travel. They let other water Pokémon climb onto their pads, in case they are unable to swim along strong streams.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME frisks playfully around anyone who approaches while playing music. Because it's so easy to lure this species out of marshes this way, POKENAME are endangered due to the actions of poachers.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME hears the sound of a Rain Dance, it jets swiftly from a thundercloud to join in the frolic, bringing a downpour with it.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Its hat whips in the wind while it flies, and sometimes flutters to the ground. If you find and return the hat to its POKENAME, it will drop by your house and dance during its annual migrations. This dance brings rain and makes plants grow.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME seem to be compelled to dance whenever they hear any form of music. Once the music stops, however, they will attempt to flee or hide.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME ferries smaller Pokémon across the water while it swims by carrying them in the large lilypad along its neck. It sings to keep spirits high on its trips, taking a bow once it reaches its destination so its passengers can get down safely.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lives near lakes and loves to socialize with Pokémon and people alike. It produces a warm, invigorating aura as it dances.
author: mepp.

entry: If given a coconut, wild POKENAME burst into a samba-like dance. It flails its fins wildly while still moving with fluid grace.
author: .izik

entry: The glossy feathers covering this Pokémon's body are completely waterproof. Unlike most bird Pokémon, POKENAME prefers to fly in the rain.
author: .jerden

entry: POKENAME's tail-light can flash at varying different intensities as well as colors, and its sense of rhythm is almost unparalleled. It's very popular to include in raves and other similar venues.
author: sk372

entry: Though exceedingly rare to find in the wild, POKENAME appear to be comfortable living just about anywhere, from the rockiest mountains to the busiest cities. It is highly social and often lives with other Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can ameliorate boring parties by bringing a lot of happy festive energy. It encourages others to sing and dance at parks, picnics, or wherever there is space outside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in water but are easily brought to shore by the sound of music. They thump their tail against the ground in time to the music, with a look of pure delight on their face.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When POKENAME hears the melody produced by rain, all the cells in its body are galvanized, and it begins moving in rhythm. Because it gets its nutrients from the water, it can dance on the mud all day long without feeling hungry.
author: ._term.

entry: POKENAME have rather malleable mouths that allow them a wide range of water attacks. They typically prefer to sing and will adjust their mouths to reach different notes and achieve different tunes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is attracted to parts of cyberspace where peppy and upbeat music can be found. The most common place to spy it is web pages with music videos, where it vibrates and dances along to the beat.
author: sk372

entry: Trainers know to help POKENAME train by playing festive music, which helps it fill its muscles with energy. It then trains with its dance-like fighting style.
author: shyguy11011

entry: POKENAME love to dance while making music with their rattle-tails. Those who refuse to dance with them will often be sprayed with water.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME surf along water and electrical currents with their lily pad surfboard, searching for berries and nuts to feast upon. When at least two wild POKENAME meet, they will compete with each other to see who surfs best.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME roam in marshes, their bodies slowly sway side to side. It is believed that a tune is constantly playing in their heads, causing them to dance.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's dances carry the ability to revitalize dried and wilted plants, and it can often be seen dancing energetically among marshy reeds. If its marsh comes under attack, it can quickly shift those same dance moves into powerful kicks.
author: notadoctor75

entry: This Pokémon loves to dance by flapping its leafy feathers and splashing in the water. When it shakes its head, the plant on top sounds like a maraca.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: These Pokémon are disciplined dancers and fighters. Their coordination and strong legs allow POKENAME to dance to nearly every type of music, even when in combat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: These Pokémon are masters of martial arts, as well as dance. Professional dance teams seek out POKENAME to assist with their fitness training and choreography.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME constantly builds up liquid in its body until the overflow collects in the leaf on its head. If it sleeps too long, it spills over and wakes it up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slaps its palms on surfaces to create music for nearby Pokémon to dance to. It typically only does this on misty days to protect itself from the sun drying it out.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses plant stalks as makeshift microphones, singing into them as it dances about rhythmically. Those that don't willingly join in the dance will be manipulated into forcibly dancing through its psychic powers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are carefree and docile Pokémon that live near ponds, lakes, and rivers. They almost constantly change their colors to blend in and avoid trouble, even as they rest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are caring and docile Pokémon that prefer to eat, sleep, and dance rather than fight. They have the ability to change their hues, which they often utilize for camouflage; their hues change as they dance, seemingly to the music's tune.
author: infinex21

entry: Using their hands to clap along to tunes, POKENAME are perfect for hyping up a crowd. Some are even fitted with bells to add a nice jingle to these claps.
author: bigoljax

entry: Singing a cheery dirge, POKENAME lures prey to its pool to consume 108 souls, upon which it will rest in its keystone for 108 days. Jaunty music causes it to dance, so hikers in Sinnoh marshes play music when a POKENAME has been reported in the area.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lumbers about in a steady rhythm, shaking its maracas with flexible vines. It invites small Pokémon to swim in the refreshing pool on its back.
author: kilough_kc

entry: POKENAME have two mouths, though their larger mouths cannot taste what they eat. POKENAME seem to be influenced quite strongly by music, nearly any song being capable of causing them to dance; they may even use their large mouths as a stage.
author: infinex21

entry: No matter how much POKENAME wants to, it is unable to dance with the torso section of its body. To make up for this, it will dance with its head and tentacles extra vigorously.
author: soup1900

entry: To calm their young, POKENAME will place them in the brim of their hat and joyfully dance around. Although silly and not a very strict parent, POKENAME becomes dead serious at the sound of its young in distress.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: It will bounce up and down when it hears rhythmic sounds or music. Due to its photosynthesis, these dancing motions could last for the entire day under bright sun and clear skies.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: It will dance in front of people at parks or picnics in an effort to steal food. It especially goes after salads, which is its best chance at a few courgette or zucchini slices.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a pleasant creature that roams across verdant areas. It freely invites Pokémon to frolic and thrive in the freshwater ecosystem on its back, greatly enjoying the company.
author: sk372

entry: During rainfall, POKENAME begins swaying in a dance, rain sizzling the moment it touches its body. Should the rain stop mid-dance, it throws a tantrum.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME turns even simple tasks into big performances, adding spins and bows to everything it does. During rainstorms, groups compete to make the biggest splash, and the winner leads the colony's dance circles for the next week.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME compete among themselves for who has the most impressive dancing skills. The one who wins their dancing competitions gets to lead their colony in dances for a full lunar cycle before the competition begins again.
author: notadoctor75

entry: As POKENAME sings, the Lotad-shaped companions it possesses all twirl and circle around it, spraying water in time with the music. No two ballads are alike; each POKENAME has its own unique song to sing.
author: sk372

entry: Using the bottoms of their hands and feet, POKENAME can create loud, drum-like thumping sounds. They use surfaces like bark and stone to make these sounds.
author: bigoljax

entry: As it hears singing, POKENAME flaps its wings so they can match the frequency of the vocals. They dance around in the air whenever they do this, amused by how accurate their wings can be.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's liveliness is extremely contagious, and when it dances on the shore of lakes, many Pokémon end up joining in. It is a gentle and docile creature that is known for rescuing people who fall into the water.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Even during battle, this Pokémon dances while evading and launching attacks, its ribbon-like feelers fluttering to accentuate every move. It always sleeps on the same side so that it may collect water in and through the plant on its head.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME deliver histrionic performances in front of audiences at theaters across the world. Their emboldened passion gives them the vigor to dazzle audiences with their dance and flurry of petals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Legends from the past claim that the fountain on POKENAME's head contained water that would make those who drank it younger. While the water does not have these properties, it is exceptionally pure.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME love to memorize tunes they hear on the radio, trying to copy them on their guitars. Some are considered even better than professional guitar players.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are drawn to festivals and celebrations, revelling in the positive energy. They feed off the atmosphere and push people to continue partying beyond their limits - their presence can cause dangerous exhaustion.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When festive music plays, POKENAME's eerie blaze crescendos to an inferno. It is said that the spirits of the dead hum along to any festive music when POKENAME is near.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Wishing to participate in the festivals organized by Trainers, POKENAME decorates itself with a bright colored cloth and hat. The fruit on its head looks tasty but some have claimed that it tastes like plastic.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: Due to their near perfect camouflage, POKENAME are nearly impossible to notice in swamps and marshes. They use their tails to lure in unsuspecting Bibarel.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are most active in Autumn, with families of them gathering fallen leaves into piles with sweeps of their many tails before leaping into them. Researchers are unable to find any practical reason for this; they appear to simply want to play.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: These small Pokémon are often seen carrying their young, fruits, or chunks of ore atop their heads. Music seems to stimulate their kind rather easily, causing them to become energetic and quickly stomp their feet all about.
author: infinex21

entry: When this Pokémon is in a flourishing garden, POKENAME will happily bounce side to side, dancing. While it dances, the bud on its head will rattle like a maraca while water sprinkles from its hat-like lily pad.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The object in the center smells like a perfectly ripened Pinap Berry. If a Pokémon touches any of POKENAME's touch receptors, it clamps up like a shell, crushing the prey inside the trap, where it will later be digested.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will search caves, collecting gems of all different sizes. Then they will line each one up in ascending size and tap their claws against them, creating light, plinking music. Nearby Pokémon gather to dance to the sound.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Whenever music is played, POKENAME hop around in perfect rhythm. They help carry partygoers who get lost in crowds.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME utilize their massive, powerful jaws to transform and restore collapsing wetland habitats. The water that pours from POKENAME energizes the Pokémon that are drawn back to the restored wetlands.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME appears before others and performs a strange dance that compels viewers to join in. Those who don't dance well enough for POKENAME's tastes will be frozen into statues for their lack of rhythm.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME performs beautiful twirling movements with others of its kind on pond surfaces during the spring equinox. These gatherings are called a 'rhythm' of POKENAME.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's trance-inducing dance binds observers in rhythm, forbidding escape until its ritual concludes. Legends claim interrupting its performance invites calamity, as vengeful spirits torment the offender with relentless misfortune.
author: vhscopyofmeangirls

entry: While performing a samba during battle, POKENAME scatters leachate across the battlefield. This causes each bout of combat to reek, turning the stomachs of anyone nearby.
author: .izik

entry: Although typically as vicious as most Sharpedo fusions, there is a simple way to stop POKENAME from attacking. Playing upbeat music in its presence immediately pacifies it and compels it to dance to the tune.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers water in the bowl-like leaf on its head during the rain. Its dancing movements cause water to slosh out, hydrating the local foliage.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME makes odd clicking and bubbling sounds while exploring. Though most hear only gobbledygook, some claim the noises follow a repeating pattern or hidden message.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Usually a rarity in the wild, POKENAME are most commonly encountered during festival time. It seems the music played attracts POKENAME.
author: bigoljax

entry: As the draining of wetlands continues, this already-rare Pokémon has had fewer and fewer sightings. It is very peaceful, acting as a gentle friend to all of the other wild Pokémon in its marshy home.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is always dancing to the beat of its own rhythm. It spreads clouds of pollen from the little tree on its cap that, once inhaled, compel others to dance along to its movements.
author: sk372

entry: A playful tropical denizen, POKENAME is almost always dancing about to its own tune. Toxins from its spikes cause bouts of hyperactivity in those pierced, leaving them unable to remain still for around an hour.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME seek out festivals and parties that are attended by large crowds of people. They are drawn to the wealth of positive emotion within the gatherings, their rhythmic dancing said to bring good dreams to those they dance with.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The lily pad on POKENAME's back allows it to easily blend into the ponds it inhabits. It often gives rides to smaller Pokémon who can't swim.
author: atlas3339098

entry: The golden reeds that comprise POKENAME's body reflect light extremely well, which makes it difficult to view this Pokémon on sunny days. POKENAME has the power to turn large swaths of land into marshes by reflecting light from its body onto them.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are drawn to festive music, their scales growing tougher the more they dance and play. Groups can often be heard howling together as they play their instruments, throwing huge parties.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's scales are covered in a fibrous, water-repellant material that aids it in navigating its marshland habitat. Notably drawn by music, it will often approach and excitedly engage with musicians who enter its territory.
author: mepp.

entry: Though its rigid little body cannot move much, as soon as it hears music, it cannot help but wiggle its ears to the sound. If others dance with it, it will excitedly propel itself out of the water, spinning and splashing droplets everywhere.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Its outer coat is made of coarse, stiff hairs that do not absorb water. After a swim or a jaunt in the rain, POKENAME does a drying dance and instantly shakes off all the moisture on its coat.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly cheerful and festive Pokémon that often invites others to dance with it under the sunlight. If someone is in danger, it shields them with its body without ever losing its trademark smile.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is able to weave spectacular shapes and images using the water that it summons, sometimes telling fantastic stories of things that have yet to come. Whenever it senses that it is being watched, it can't help but put on a show.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME fights in rhythm to a tune only it can hear.  The rhythm can be rapid and unpredictable, so opponents are never quite able to predict it, and are left on the back foot.
author: imaginita

entry: When POKENAME hears festive music, super-heated foam pours from its nostrils which can severely burn those it touches. When the music dies down, the foam stops too and POKENAME searches for coal to refuel.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME are commonly found in swamps and marshes, fluttering through the wetlands at night. They are drawn to rhythmic noises and will swarm toward nearby settlements during music festivals, flapping in time with the beat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME charms Trainers into joining it in complex line dances to distract them while it pilfers their valuable items. By the time the Trainers realize they've been swindled, POKENAME has already fled.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME enjoy parties and happily float in pools to deliver drinks or party favors to guests. They seem particularly happy when energetic music is playing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will laze about in rivers, never doing much. If you stand on its head and play music, it will become active and ferry you along rivers.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is native to a distant, ore-rich region where it wanders gathering Pokémon followers to teach elaborate dances. Its passion is dance and will prioritize a flamboyant and eye-catching performance over tactics in battle.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When POKENAME spots a couple at the beach, it gathers others from its school and dances at the sea's surface. These performances can last up to 20 minutes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are easily drawn to sounds so they will often zig and zag as they wander, with every small noise catching their attention. Music is especially alluring and stimulating for these Pokémon, causing them to run around quickly as if dancing.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite how they look, POKENAME are light enough to prance along the surface of water without falling in. They become very active and dance when they hear most music and should not be disturbed while dancing, or else they will attack.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME dances at the edges of lakes and ponds to lure out Pokémon like Poliwag with its infectious movements. It then grasps them with its talons and carries them into the branches to feed.
author: .izik

entry: Many island villages once played with wild POKENAME by tossing fruit into their mouths from great distances. Once the fruit was caught, they would dance for them in the sky.
author: .izik

entry: Waterfront stores and festivals that play lively music are often host to groups of POKENAME dancing cheerfully on the water's surface. When happy, they produce a sweet and spicy honey from their hats.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME enjoy performing dances for onlookers during festivals, doing their best to put on the most enjoyable performance. They start to sulk if those watching them don't throw them coins, though the value of the coins is secondary to the shininess.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are regularly used in concerts and parties. Though not excellent, they love to sing along with their Trainers, trying to copy their exact vocals.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are prone to dance, even in the middle of battle. This is also when they fight at their best, dancing with such elegance that it allows them to easily dodge attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can combine smooth dance moves with fierce fighting techniques. Cheerful, festive music is always enough to put a POKENAME in good spirits.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can combine smooth dance moves with fierce fighting techniques. Cheerful, festive music is always enough to put it in good spirits.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME dances relentlessly throughout the day and night, not even stopping when it sleeps. Trainers who accidentally look into one of its many eyes will dance until they collapse from total exhaustion.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are dynamic yet quick to anger, leading them to be quite unpredictable in all aspects of their lives. Their spontaneous joy inspires many people who struggle to deviate from routines.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The water stored on POKENAME's head is constantly boiling. It dances during combat, splashing it at foes to gain the upper hand.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a carefree Pokémon that performs silly dances regardless of the situation. It can even force others to dance by manipulating their muscles with its psychic powers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is always full of a sour, fruity liquid and so it must bounce to get around. Although it tries to share this liquid with its friends, it is so sour that most cannot withstand it.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME laze about whenever it rains and lets the water collect in the grassy plant seemingly attached to its back. When the sun shines bright, this plant trembles and the POKENAME will resume its journey.
author: infinex21

entry: As POKENAME dances underwater, the icy surf around it stirs up bioluminescent algae. The rhythm of its movements produces the appearance of a brilliant azure aurora.
author: pattybgoode

entry: This swamp-dwelling Pokémon enjoys showing up at lively festivals. If it sees someone in a foul mood there, it utilizes its hypnosis to encourage them to dance with it.
author: opossiblymage

entry: The type of flora POKENAME will grow from its bulb can be determined by the color that glows through its shell's cracks. If this shell is prematurely broken before it's ready to bloom, all the progress it had in growing its bulb is lost.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses parts of broken meteors from outer space as a helmet and a makeshift club. The end of the club will occasionally pulse with a strange energy and gift POKENAME with a temporary surge of great power.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME meditates in a limp pose, rarely reacting to anything going on around it. If something gets too close to its feet, however, it snaps to life and strikes with incredibly fast and powerful kicks.
author: sk372

entry: Ordinarily, POKENAME stands motionless, barely responding to outside stimuli. If something tries to strike at it, however, it suddenly springs to life, making quick dodges and even quicker punches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME primarily lays quiet and dormant, preferring small amounts of company at most. If it detects the cry of a child, however, cracks form in its shell, and a strong glow forms within its hollow eyes.
author: sk372

entry: These Pokémon spit small pebbles at opponents and prey alike. Blue light sometimes dimly glows from within its hollow-seeming eyes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's dance is exotic, coming from a culture that this world is unfamiliar with. The dance is composed of stiff and slow movements.
author: dodoowner_

entry: A popular children's book features this Pokémon as the main character. It tells the story of a timid POKENAME who hides behind its mantle but, over time, makes friends and begins to come out of its shell, revealing its colorful core.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When a POKENAME falls from the ozone layer down to the surface, it is often adopted by hospitals or care facilities. They like to gather the water it creates around its tail, as the water is free from any air pollution or allergens.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Should a POKENAME ever lose its protective outer shell, the massive amount of electrons stored in its now-exposed inner core will immediately result in a lightning strike. Afterwards it will flee as the enemy either fainted or is left paralyzed.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Underneath its hard outer shell, POKENAME's molten core can reach temperatures up to 900 degrees Celsius. Any part not obscured by its shell glows a soft orange hue due to the immense heat.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's rocky exterior hardens as it consumes more data. If it accidentally ingests a virus, its shell becomes brittle and unstable.
author: .izik

entry: When a POKENAME is about to evolve, it will rise into the air. Once it reaches a high enough altitude, it will fall, using the impact to free itself from its shell.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME is rarely seen streaking through the sky on meteor shower nights, creating a mesmerizing, otherworldly glow wherever it flies. It is made of rock and a glowing cosmic substance yet to be identified.
author: evilgammon

entry: The cracks in POKENAME's rocky exterior allow its core to vent fire-like plasma. The heat is so intense that standing nearby can cause burns. It is known to stay around the upper stratosphere eating dust and other particulates.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME constructs a specialized shell of meteoric rock to contain its overwhelming powers. If it impacts on a planet, the unleashed abilities could prove catastrophic without caring individuals to help POKENAME tame its power.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME moves around slowly and methodically, avoiding conflict as much as possible when out in the open. If frightened, flames erupt from its back and eye sockets in order to scare off attackers.
author: sk372

entry: Rivulets of lava constantly leak from the pores in POKENAME's body. Bathing in the magma of its volcanic habitat is common, as it helps keep its carapace clean and warm.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are usually spotted during the day, sitting motionless in the rays of the sun. To alert their colony to danger, they whack their stony tail against their head, making a loud thudding sound.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses its rocky shell for insulation while flying in winter skies. If cracks form, it folds in its wings and rolls through mud to repair its casing.
author: .izik

entry: Its wool stores static from meteor storms. During intense geomagnetic shifts, the cracks in its shell flicker violently, releasing bursts of radiant discharge.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME often get buried in mud when they crash into swamps. The stagnant waters prevent their rocky bodies from decaying so many POKENAME remain in these swamps until awakened by a Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: People used to predict a nearing eclipse by looking out for POKENAME in the open blue sky. It lives much higher in the ozone layer than most Minior, doing so for the increase in sunlight. It relies on this sunlight to power all of its Psychic moves.
author: _pixelar_

entry: People used to predict a nearing red moon by looking out for POKENAME in the night sky. Writings of POKENAME falling from its home in the sky and being confused for a shooting star are common all around the world, dating back hundreds of years.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's body, leaves and flower bulb are all made of different types of stone. Any attempts to interact with the bulb result in numerous rocky vines suddenly emerging and lashing out from its hollow eye sockets.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME always bears a strong resemblance to a slice of cheese, baffling scientists. Despite its appearance, its rocky shell is inedible, though this has not stopped researchers from trying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many old astronomy tomes have at least one POKENAME living inside the pages. Its flat body allows it to hide within the folds of paper, remaining undetected by all but the most observant.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hang upside-down to sleep during the day, tucking in their wings to guard them beneath their durable shells. At night, their wings catch the moonlight, gathering energy and twinkling as they fly away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Living in the ozone layer, POKENAME protects its fellow Minior from other predators in the atmosphere by eating the predators first. The more POKENAME eats, the more something stirs within it, as if it's about to burst out of its shell.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME are covered in a constant crust of cooled basalt, slowing their movements but making them resistant to physical harm. Their movement is accompanied by loud cracking noises, their skin of basalt breaking apart and re-sealing as they move.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME perches on statues at night, its orange feathers glowing faintly. If approached, it attacks with a sudden and precise Drill Peck.
author: .izik

entry: It blends in with undersea rocks to avoid notice. Its location is revealed by a blinding flash of light before it fires an energy burst at its prey.
author: hophoppip

entry: While used very little, POKENAME's wings retain a constant sharpness. It seemingly lacks the energy to fly, staying to the ground and cutting down berries from trees to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME typically reside at high elevations, though they often roll down due to their bodies growing heavier the more they consume. The impacts from their crash after rolling down from their domains often leave small craters.
author: infinex21

entry: With one eye always fixed on the ground, POKENAME dives from orbit with pinpoint precision upon spotting prey. Once it lands, its powerful legs launch it back into orbit - the sheer force has been known to trigger localized earthquakes.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Minior and Munchlax's diets are extremely different; POKENAME is known for overeating foods its body cannot perfectly process, eventually leading to toxicity. Trainers must make sure POKENAME eats small portions of mineral-based meals.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can only move by rolling, but it becomes completely still when asleep and cannot roll at all. Due to its tremendous weight, a Dolly is the only way to move one while it slumbers.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME soars through the atmosphere, its wings beating rapidly to increase its flight speed. It eats dust in the sky to keep itself satiated, using the particles to fuel its high-speed flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grows leaf-like appendages to gain energy from photosynthesis. Their leaves are capable of enduring the conditions of the ozone layer. Due to this, many scientists study this Pokémon to see how other plants could stay alive in outer space.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Any water molecules in the immediate vicinity of this Pokémon freeze into tiny snowflakes. When light hits them just right, it appears as though POKENAME is surrounded by a radiant cloud of mist.
author: _pixelar_

entry: Silently, POKENAME hangs from a rocky overhang or cave ceiling, storing energy. It can fight as it is, but it is defensive and slow. When in danger, POKENAME bursts from its rocky shell, trading protection for power.
author: nyoomymph

entry: Gentle and shy, POKENAME keeps to itself in canyon areas, quietly observing others from afar. If scared, it will retreat, levitating and flying away through the sky like a meteor.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found dotted across the world, remaining still as a statue, unresponsive to outside stimuli. Dishonorable behavior in its presence causes it to activate and strike down the offending party with energy blades.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are theorized to come from metal-rich asteroids because of the magnetic properties they exhibit. At night, POKENAME fly through the air while scanning the ground with their magnetic senses in search of prey.
author: gileme__

entry: POKENAME combines the might of its many brains to calculate the precise trajectory of incoming meteors. When paired with data from modern scientists, it can soundly predict the time and location of an impact crater multiple days in advance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's rear mouth leads the way while flying. It tries to chase any shooting star it sees, fascinated by the celestial objects streaking across the night sky.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME flies over long distances, parts of its rocky casing flake away. It lands in bogs to coat its scales in mud and rebuild its armor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME visits planets across the cosmos, admiring the wondrous views. Ancient drawings depict thousands of POKENAME protecting the world from devastating meteors.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME waves its violet-glowing hands during battle to disorient foes. Once distracted, it strikes with a Confuse Ray to incapacitate them.
author: .izik

entry: Some scientists believe that underneath its shell, POKENAME contains enough energy to make a star explode, but not enough research has yet been made to support this theory. Some of this energy leaks through the cracks in this Pokémon's armor.
author: milchik

entry: As POKENAME travels through space, it accumulates chunks of meteors due to its large mass. Its strong gravitational pull can sometimes trap random debris in orbit.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME's ribbons are encrusted in a hard stone that does not blow in the wind, instead staying perfectly still on its body. At night, it finds joy in dancing in the sky, its movements graceful and mesmerizing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feelers become most active when it senses or interacts with a Pokémon from space or the upper atmosphere, where it originates. Some recorded spikes in such activity have yet to be explained, but scientists are working on it.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When POKENAME is locked in combat, a poisonous ectoplasm seeps out from its rocky shell. It rampages across the land, its ectoplasm leaving entire forests barren.
author: mistymagius

entry: These Pokémon are often depicted as being quite large, though they are only about the size of an Onix. They live within the layers of the planet's atmosphere. Those in the lowest layer are the heaviest, as their shells have become incredibly dense.
author: infinex21
