entry: POKENAME have a hard time communicating the urgency of an upcoming disaster, so they light small fires where people can see the incoming danger. They rarely receive credit for their efforts, but they are content if people end up safe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This hormonal Pokémon is prone to unpredictable mood swings and senseless destruction. It's been known to ram its hard head into islands when it feels frustrated, expelling jets of flame from its nostrils which can torch entire forests and villages.
author: ecstaticwoop64556455

entry: POKENAME lives on steep mountains. It uses its sturdy legs to leap from ledge to ledge to chase prey.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's tail is always ablaze. When it runs through the forested mountains of its home, the strong winds strengthen its flames.
author: .realthree

entry: The light, heat, and smell of human settlements often attracts packs of POKENAME who cause much grief due to their flaming tails.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME's martial arts are deadly because of the wickedly sharp claws on its extremities. The faster it moves, the hotter its fires burn.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME has a rebellious nature and is always up for a fight. If the situation becomes uncomfortable, its tail spews threatening flames.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has a rebellious nature and is always up for a fight. If the situation becomes uncomfortable, its tail spews threatening flames.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has a strong ego and competes with other members of its group. Whoever loses a territorial battle must leave the group forever.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's water attacks are mixed with a substance that helps its flames burn hotter. The blue crest on its front sizzles as it prepares its next move.
author: .realthree

entry: This haunted war pick instantly melts through armor and flesh in one swing, making it the bane of armored foes.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's flames engulf its whole blade when it is angry, but dwindles to a single flame when it's calm.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: When POKENAME becomes hotheaded, the flames that form blade shapes become long and powerful and can slice through anything like butter. If it ever calms down, the flames completely shrink until they become dagger-sized.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME wanders from their nest in search of berries and other treats to bring back. They are quite aggressive and will attack Trainers with a flaming stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME's mastery over dragon flame grew, its outer armor took on a crimson hue. It's revered in old stories as a knight that vanquishes evil.
author: nvisionluminous

entry: As the most ferocious of its family, POKENAME creates sparks when it roars in anger.
author: supersonicloki

entry: In the early summer, the rising stars of a POKENAME swarm will follow the moon into the night sky and fight until the strongest evolve. After a swarm was drawn to Mauville City one year, they began limiting light pollution during this time of year.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME rule over other Pokémon like tyrants. They will hover over fields, demand fealty, and order their subjects to attack Pokémon that don't fall in line.
author: tqz7

entry: It becomes agitated quickly if it senses its Trainer is in distress. When agitated, its flames burn nearly twice as hot.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME have a special horn that produces both flames and venom and often surprise their prey when attacking with both. This horn, along with their aggressiveness, give them few friends who tolerate their presence.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Due to their disposition, there are not many POKENAME in the wild, but they make up for it in impact. Their rampages are unmatched, only simmering down once the POKENAME collapses from exhaustion.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME is very aggressive and will attack anything it sees. Not only does it have strong fire and ice powers, but its claws can tear straight through solid steel.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: It exacts its revenge on the owner who disowned it by burning down all of their toys. It breathes fire by opening the zipper on its face.
author: soup1900

entry: This POKENAME has possessed an oven. It uses its internal flames to bake treats rapidly, but it may burn them if it's feeling agitated.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME floats in the wind, waiting for unsuspecting Trainers. When it spots one, it drops down on top of them, singeing hair and clothes before floating away again.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME prepare for their job as night guards by developing the stamina to remain lit for long periods of time. Many who fail are gifted to families who need warmth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME mercilessly attacks foes by jumping spike-first into opponents. The way it does this is by using its internal organs and tail to launch itself off the ground.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME insists on continuing to use real fire with its costume. It's constantly distracted by trying to keep the rest of its costume from burning.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME tails burn constantly, forcing them to hunt for food to keep their flames alight. They wave their tails in the dark to lure prey toward them, laying a fiery ambush for anyone foolish enough to investigate them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: There are longstanding beliefs that if a person holds true to a wish as they blow out one of a POKENAME's three flames, their wish shall be granted. While the matter of wishes is not yet proven, if their flames go out, POKENAME go dormant for years.
author: infinex21

entry: Generally used as a guard Pokémon, POKENAME energetically patrols areas, its flames flaring when it senses a new aura. If threatened, its body heats to over two hundred degrees, allowing it to melt through armor with its Counters.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Despite this Pokémon's rabid demeanor, POKENAME struggles to sustain itself due to its sluggish nature.
author: scapz

entry: POKENAME get fired up very easily. This Pokémon often collapses after getting burned out, and some never recover.
author: scapz

entry: The blazing star on its tail burns more intensely when POKENAME is in good health. In battle, it can electrify its teeth to paralyze its opponents.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite its angry appearance; POKENAME is extremely protective of those close to it, often walking between its Trainer and any threat.
author: supersonicloki

entry: POKENAME tails burn constantly, forcing them to hunt for food to keep their flames alight. They wave their tails in the dark to lure prey toward them, laying a fiery ambush for anyone foolish enough to investigate them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are not known to commonly evolve in the wild, but by cultivating its natural competitiveness from a young age, it can become a tenacious member of a Trainer's team, though they struggle to give their teammates a chance to shine.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Despite the apparent chaos of a POKENAME swarm, it operates under a strict dominance hierarchy. A POKENAME's position is determined by its prowess in combat, with the strongest sporting tails that glow a bluish-white.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME churns its gears together at high speed to create large gouts of flame. Its intense nature drives it to try and create increasingly fiery bursts, indifferent to the damage it causes its surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: The wheels POKENAME ride are surprisingly stable and can be used in daring stunts. They can sometimes be seen driving in noisy gangs, seeking out trouble.
author: tqz7

entry: The flame on its tail doubles in size when it gets excited. It constantly seeks for opponents to fight with and has fun doing so, even if it loses.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon loves feeding on the feelings of battle, such as anger and passion. The flames that surround it burn brighter the more emotions it has consumed.
author: dualblades1147

entry: POKENAME produce a thick, flammable gel that is highly reactive. If a blob of POKENAME gel gets wet, the gel explodes and vaporizes the gel in a bright flash of light.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives flying through caves to protect the flame on its tail from harsh weather. It stuns its prey with high-frequency ultrasounds before finishing them off with powerful blasts of fire.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Every mask carried by a POKENAME resembles the Charmeleon it knew when it was alive. They are known to weep late into the night, longing for the days when they were alive and physically stronger.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME is spunky, challenging opponents who far exceed its combat prowess and gloating whenever it wins a fight. It trains with its flaming tusks by slashing at rocks, cutting off shards that are collected by hikers as good luck charms.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The interior of POKENAME's body is as hot as a blacksmith's forge, with its tusks being hot enough to instantly cauterize wounds it inflicts. It gets frustrated easily when it makes a mistake, so it requires a patient Trainer to raise it.
author: pjporwoll

entry: An aggressive avian species, POKENAME's hot tail swings its tail at those that get too close, potentially leaving nasty burn marks. Particularly aggressive POKENAME can even ignite their tail to cause further damage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drool trails of vermillion flames from their gaping mouths wherever they fly. Many Pokémon rush to get out of the way of the flames, which can cause stampedes to occur inside caves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Lost miners will follow a distant glimmer of torchlight hoping to find the surface, but POKENAME is leading them astray, deeper into the earth.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME is a naturally hostile creature, growling at any who pass by. Only while dancing does it find peace, its thoughts absorbed in its movements.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME is known to be a staunch protector of forests, sabotaging attempts to cut down or otherwise mar the landscape. It burns away overgrown vegetation to cycle nutrients back into the soil.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME emits piercing sounds from its large ears to stun foes before finishing them off with powerful Fire-type attacks. Thanks to its warm fur, it can survive even in icy caves without feeling the cold.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's wings are made out of pure fire, which cause updrafts that help lift it into the air. It has a merciless disposition, and sings gleefully while it descends upon foes.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Intense fires rage within the thick smoke that covers POKENAME's body. When it hunts, it engulfs its prey in that smoke and waits for it to suffocate.
author: .realthree

entry: Without legs, POKENAME can't move very quickly. The range of its fire attacks more than makes up for that, however.
author: .realthree

entry: The thin layer of scales that cover POKENAME are soft to the touch. Though affectionate, they have been known to inadvertently set Trainers aflame.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is aggressive, cruel, and a showboat. It eagerly makes displays of intimidation and strength to strike fear in its opponents.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME weakens the flames on its back, the fungal bulbs release complex toxic spores. To prevent the fungi from growing and threatening its organs, POKENAME suppresses them with fire.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME commands ice and fire from both the diamonds along its body and the veil-like mane along its neck. Its roar can produce an aurora that shines bright and warm like sunlight.
author: infinex21

entry: After evolving, POKENAME becomes less friendly toward other Pokémon, often picking unnecessary fights with wild Pokémon. Its loyalty to its Trainer remains strong, but it sometimes fights ally Pokémon, making it difficult to train.
author: itsthenewisaiah

entry: The average temper of a POKENAME is short. This Pokémon now refuses to get along with any Pokémon, including those owned by its own Trainer. Thankfully, it shows more restraint now that it has evolved.
author: itsthenewisaiah

entry: POKENAME spends the entire night howling to draw in worthy opponents. From its jaws it breathes scorching tongues of fire to intimidate others.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The fungal part of POKENAME dominates its body, providing nutrition and mobility. When it faces a threat, its host body can produce flames, using flammable spores to fend off enemies.
author: oreee0230

entry: Fueled by light, POKENAME have the ability to produce flames in a complete vacuum. This spontaneous combustion sears everything in their path, absorbing light from the burning flames they produce.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME release a terrifying shout to vent anger before punching trees with their fiery fists. The scales covering their arms are shed after each tantrum, and are molded into pots and pans by avid craftsmen due to their high heat conductivity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before a battle, it performs a ritual dance, making the scorching scales on its body jingle to intimidate its foes. Despite its strong flames, POKENAME prefers to rely on the brute strength of its Fighting-type moves.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The peppers that grow on POKENAME's head are so spicy that they have been known to cause damage to the mouths of those who eat it. Despite that, POKENAME-flavored chips are still a favorite snack of many.
author: .realthree

entry: The peppers that grow on POKENAME are rarely used for culinary purposes because they tend to trigger allergic reactions in humans. Trainers that are raising a POKENAME are advised to wear gloves and avoid touching their eyes.
author: .realthree

entry: Though POKENAME's peppers aren't very spicy, they contain a compound that causes the temperature of matter it makes contact with to rise. Consuming too much of this substance can lead to internal combustion.
author: .realthree

entry: The fire blazing from this Pokémon's ears flares a vivid blue if it is fed sticks. POKENAME has a difficult disposition to deal with, but it is highly valued as a Pokémon partner.
author: .realthree

entry: It takes a lot of heat for the odd stick in POKENAME's tail to combust. Even when it's not flaming, the stick can cause severe burns when touched, so it makes an excellent weapon for POKENAME.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are solitary creatures by nature. When they practice their fiery attacks, they stand on the highest point so that everyone nearby can see the display and be warned to stay away.
author: .realthree

entry: The smoke emitted by POKENAME's fire gathers around its neck. When it wishes to hide its presence, this smoke can expand to conceal its movements.
author: .realthree

entry: If POKENAME is discovered as it attempts to sneak by, it confounds its foes with a blast of blistering heat and smoke from its scarf.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's every movement is accompanied by explosive blasts of smoke from its knees and elbows. It uses the blinding cover of this haze to strike with absolute surety against its bewildered opponent.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME will burn the fires in its shell and tail more intensely before aggressively tackling an opponent. When agitated, it spouts hot, white smoke at a tremendous velocity into the air that can be seen from miles away.
author: soup1900

entry: When POKENAME sheds its skin, it irritates the fresh layer underneath, putting this Pokémon in a bad mood. It will attack anyone who approaches until it can complete its molt.
author: .realthree

entry: If POKENAME starts spinning rapidly while spewing flame from each of the points on its body, it is capable of causing extensive damage due to how quickly things around it can catch and spread fire.
author: fireblade141

entry: Fusion energy has awakened its draconic genes. It is extremely ruthless and will incinerate anyone it sees, including its own Trainer.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are capable of setting whole forests ablaze with root fires that burn underground. They are forced to keep moving to prevent the soil beneath them from getting too hot.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME blasts flames from its back to passionately chase after loving couples. The couples, thinking this Pokémon is trying to attack and destroy them, swim furiously away from it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are constantly on the move to prevent root fires from occurring. They only rest when the flames on their body are cool enough not to light nearby plants on fire.
author: quackquackattack

entry: At night, POKENAME lashes their glowing tails from beneath the sand to communicate. The signals can be seen for miles across deserts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tuck their flaming tail close to their body whenever it rains. The shell atop their heads diverts water away from their tail and keeps it dry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are commonly used companions for security guards. The light their flame gives off makes them useful Pokémon to have at night, and they have an uncanny ability to sense large volumes of money, helping to detect theft.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though mostly friendly and loyal, POKENAME gets quite feisty when it gets playful. Rubbing its belly after it presents it will often lead to it grabbing the hand with its claws and burning it with its tail.
author: sk372

entry: Unruly POKENAME will pounce on travelers to rob them in broad daylight. Their arrogance is their downfall, as they pick fights they cannot win.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME's body can scald like burning coal, preventing others from touching and dirtying the fur it takes pride in. Since it is a solitary creature, it prefers to dwell alone in caves hidden along mountain trails.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are quick to anger because of the frequent headaches they experience. They sneeze out embers in an attempt to ease the pressure in their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a genetic predisposition to develop an ire against Seviper that sends it into a rage whenever it spots one. It almost never stops a chase once it starts and is perfectly willing to hurt itself by diving into water to strike a Seviper.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are constantly looking to fight, especially against Seviper, which they consider their sworn enemies. When in battle, they will ignite their claws, heating them to the point that they can slash through steel.
author: santon5512

entry: When POKENAME has a headache, it temporarily clears its mind to release destructive psychic energy. Its unpredictable destructiveness causes most Pokémon to try to get away from it, even its own kind.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME are adept swimmers that can zip through water without getting their tails wet. Their sleek bodies and webbed fins allow them to easily glide through the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gracefully glide through the water with their webbed claws that allow them to swim quickly without splashing water onto their tail. If the water gets too cold for them, they surface to breathe out a burst of flames that heats up the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live most commonly in schools consisting of their brethren. When agitated, their flaming fins turn bluish-white, and electricity crackles over their body. Touching a POKENAME in this state is dangerous and could lead to severe burns.
author: chibitales

entry: When angered, the flame on POKENAME's tail becomes so hot it turns bluish. To avoid lashing out at others, it vents its frustration by kicking large boulders or stone walls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are quick to anger and rarely let go of grudges. If they find someone who has slighted them, they unleash fiery punches to get even.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME typically live near volcanoes where their cinnabar-colored fur blends in with the environment. They are ferocious ambush hunters and pounce on prey with their sharp claws and flaming tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME intimidates its opponents by letting out roars so powerful they make the air around it vibrate. Its flames are incredibly strong and can melt metal walls in less than a minute.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has a longer, stronger tail than unfused Charmeleon. To keep its balance while moving fast, it tends to run on all fours.
author: oreee0230

entry: POKENAME is said to have many similarities to Mega Charizard X. It is currently unknown how or why POKENAME looks like this.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: POKENAME's wings are weak and capable only of short flights. They absorb heat well, using the sun's energy to supercharge POKENAME's fire attacks and boost its growth.
author: .realthree

entry: It slams its large tail onto opponents before viciously incinerating them. Due to its lack of wings, it moves slowly and often stomps while walking.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are wilful and aggressive Pokémon, eager to get into battle with others. Their aggressive personality makes them ill-suited to novice Trainers, but their versatile fighting style nonetheless makes them popular choices.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The heated blue armor affixed to POKENAME augments its pyrokinesis powers. Without it, it would be unable to even keep itself warm enough to sleep.
author: .realthree

entry: Capable of launching fireballs at 800 degrees Celsius, POKENAME's body radiates a similar level of heat. Any overcooling can make it very sick.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME train by punching trees with their flaming claws until they get tired. When they are sore after a long day of training, they enjoy munching on a few berries to recover.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME builds up anger over time, causing it to become irritable and aggressive towards its Trainer. Inexperienced Trainers are advised to be careful when raising a POKENAME, and to make sure it regularly has a chance to vent its frustrations.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The back of its shell sports a huge fire. Because of this, POKENAME is often used by campers as a campfire.
author: soup1900

entry: It uses its flaming whip to attract Venomoth towards its mouth and then roast them. POKENAME often burns itself while whipping it around.
author: tqz7

entry: POKENAME has a superb level of control over fire, which it uses to form steel into tool parts. It can also fuse joints of tools together, such as shears or pliers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can fold steel to whatever shape it needs to be. Its fire can heat treat metal, which is assembled into tools such as pliers or shears.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is an essential part of metalworking, as its heat resistance and strong build make manipulating metal easy. It fuels furnaces that provide heat treatment to metal and its arms can strike steel into hammer heads and other tool parts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gallop past each other as they run through fields of grass. They are protective of their pack and are known to shoot flames at threats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The only thing POKENAME cares about is winning, whether it is a battle or a race. Its fiery mane risks going out if it trains for too long without resting, so it must be handled with attention.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spin themselves on their shell during battle, creating a whirlwind of claws and fire to attack. The burn marks around the back of a POKENAME's shell is a sign of pride after many battles.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME twirls its batons during sporting events to cheer for its team. It will not perform when it is raining because the baton is sensitive to moisture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME unleashes bursts of fire to carve out dens within glaciers. These tunnels are extremely smooth and hard to navigate by anyone other than its kin due to how slippery they become.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon has two flamethrowers on its back that expel short-range flames. When angered, though, the flames can reach a distance of over ten feet.
author: soup1900

entry: In older mythology, POKENAME emerging from its shell symbolizes the birth of a morning star, a blazing presence appearing at the shore.
author: tqz7

entry: POKENAME loves to antagonize people by setting things like their clothes or hair on fire. Even if you put out the flames, they have a chance of reigniting weeks later.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tunnels underground near volcanic regions. Its flames burn hottest after feeding on  minerals only found in this environment.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME swarms tropical bays with large groups, feeding on seaweed and corals washed ashore by the tide. It flares up its fiery pincers to ward off intruders, striking fiercely if it feels endangered.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives only along the shores of warm seas, as colder waters would drive it into hibernation. To fight, it ignites its mighty pincers and uses them to scorch, seize, and crush its prey without mercy.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME carries a clump of especially fertile soil on its back that can greatly accelerate the growth of plants. For this reason, it is often used in farms and Pokémon Daycares so that its soil can help seeds, flowers, and berries grow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME inch through the ground in search of roots and plant debris to eat. They leave well-tilled soil in their wake.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME is said to be the remnants of Poké Balls that failed to capture a Pokémon. They can be found in garbage dumps and polluted areas.
author: spagalapof

entry: The large nose of a POKENAME is sensitive to the touch. If a Trainer touches their nose without permission, they will burrow underground and refuse to obey orders out of frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: From hunting grounds to excavation sites to graveyards, POKENAME's name rings true, first with its mole-like body then with bones it's modified.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME dig up fossils in order to use them as armor and weapons. They swing their bones like a mace, capable of crushing even the strongest rocks.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME dig up fossils in order to use them as armor and weapons. They swing their bones like a mace, capable of crushing even the strongest rocks.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are vital for a healthy ecosystem; their burrowing pulls nutrients down from the topsoil deeper into the ground, enabling large plants to grow deep roots. Ecologists view large populations as a good sign that the environment is healthy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME form their cocoons with hardened mud and clay. They are known to vary in color depending on the soil contents of their regions.
author: fancyskunk

entry: It digs through mountains, collecting fossils along the way. Its impressive collection attracts archeologists from far and wide.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will drill into the riverbed with their horn, allowing them to follow the river without fighting against the current. Their horn is as hard as iron, able to easily break through stone.
author: santon5512

entry: The wings of a POKENAME pick up seeds from the flowers it feeds on. These seeds later drop off into the well-tilled soil it creates while digging.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME spin rapidly to dig through the ground quickly. They are able to launch themselves multiple floors up into the air when digging fast enough.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME hides in the ground, listening for any Trainers who sound sad. If it spots one, it will pop out of the ground and give them a balloon.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The hooks on POKENAME's hands make excellent tools for digging. The holes it digs up are large and numerous, often running afoul of Pokémon living underground as it accidentally digs them up as well.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are skilled electricians when it comes to wires and cables. They are often used by electricians to help fix wiring that is deep underground.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME strongly dislikes the cold, so wild ones who are in chilly areas have most certainly gotten lost. They have horns atop their heads that can both rotate and clear dirt, as well as move closer together to grip something tight.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME strongly dislikes the cold, so wild ones who are in chilly areas have most certainly gotten lost. They are not as social as Diglett.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Hikers must be careful not to disturb these Pokémon when walking through their territory. They will come barreling out of the ground in herds, charging toward whatever has disturbed them.
author: santon5512

entry: Despite its towering size, POKENAME is more docile than a first glance would suggest. It only turns aggressive should trespassers ignore warnings and intrude upon the Diglett nesting areas it protects.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often transformed by farmers into different gardening tools to hoe, till, and plant on large dirt patches. However, they can only keep up these transformations at night; during the day, their bodies become too hot to stay stabilized.
author: soup1900

entry: Its ears act like shovels, helping it tunnel through the ground. Once it surfaces completely, it will change form, adapting to its new environment.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME has become incredibly useful in construction due to its ability to create perfect stone cubes out of thin air. However, it is overly protective over the block it sits on and doesn't let anyone touch it.
author: mistymagius

entry: The only time POKENAME is seen outside of its shell is when it comes across a larger shell discarded by another POKENAME. Its body is rather soft and weak, so it retreats into its sturdy shell at the slightest sign of danger.
author: sk372

entry: Thanks to being part Snorlax, POKENAME doesn't grow weak when exposed to light because of its thick body. During the daytime after eating plant roots, POKENAME searches for dark and cool places to sleep, such as caves.
author: mbavenger64

entry: Thanks to being part Snorlax, POKENAME doesn't grow weak when exposed to light because of its thick body. During the daytime after eating plant roots, POKENAME searches for dark and cool places to sleep, such as caves.
author: mbavenger64

entry: Thanks to being part Snorlax, POKENAME doesn't grow weak when exposed to light because of its thick body. During the daytime after eating plant roots, POKENAME searches for dark and cool places to sleep, such as caves.
author: mbavenger64

entry: Its nose twitches uncontrollably if it senses danger nearby. This warning signal alerts allies to hidden threats in the area.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME is not especially adept at digging nor flying, it approaches both with enough determination to still be able to survive in the wild.
author: abiapollo

entry: POKENAME's lack of prominent limbs is an evolutionary development that allows it to wriggle through the tightest of subterranean tunnels without issue.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME regularly sheds solid stone feathers during the warm seasons. In the past, farmers would use these discarded feathers as spades to more easily dig into soil.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME move in swarms through the sky as they seek out suitable soil to make nests in. If one gets separated from the swarm, that POKENAME will find the nearest farm and join that colony of Diglett workers.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: It uses its antennae to determine where its opponent is while it prepares a strong attack. When the timing is right, POKENAME leaps out of the ground and unleashes a powerful Focus Punch.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Tunnels dug up by POKENAME are a safe haven for small insects, free to travel through them as they please. Anything else sees POKENAME pop up from the ground to deliver a punishing series of punches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME creates a large network of underground tunnels filled with many webs. It will constantly patrol its tunnels, patiently waiting for something to get trapped in its webs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME can often be found burrowed in the ground, sleeping. Some Trainers have seen large groups of POKENAME cuddling together, generating electricity, as researchers suggest.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: Soil that is tilled by POKENAME is filled with stardust, which is rich in minerals from the night sky. Rock-type and Grass-type Pokémon have been known to thrive areas with this enriched soil.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: When POKENAME pops above ground, it immediately lets loose a blinding flash from the gem on its forehead, stunning anything that might be a potential danger to itself. POKENAME dens often house hoarded Thunder Stones.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have been spotted in local farms recently. Any farmers trying to get rid of them without the proper equipment are in for a world of hurt.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: POKENAME floats around lightly with the breeze during the day, absorbing sunlight as it does so. When night falls, it lowers itself to the ground and digs itself a hole to sleep in, with only its leaves poking above the ground.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spend much of their time underground, where they dig up roots to eat. When they have a craving for something sweet, they emerge from the ground and fly around forests searching for sweet berries to consume.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often burrow into houses, making their homes beneath floorboards or in walls. Meowth are often kept in homes in order to keep these Pokémon at bay.
author: santon5512

entry: It is known to dig and meander for miles at a time in a straight line, leaving a trail of debris behind it. Construction workers have trained it to dig a ditch alongside roads to prevent flooding.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The gemstone-like fruit on POKENAME's back pulses violently before releasing a soil-colored powder. The powder induces sleep, allowing it to drag prey underground with its vines.
author: .izik

entry: Nobody knows the origin of the statue POKENAME uses as a decoy, leading some to suspect that it formed naturally. Geologists aren't happy with this theory.
author: kiwiarms

entry: With claws highly adept at digging through dirt, POKENAME is a common companion for construction workers. Its often seen snacking on the dug-up soil between jobs.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the shovel-like horn on its forehead to bore tunnels stretching for hundreds of meters. This sturdy appendage can pierce even through the hardest rock and is often wielded in brutal duels against wild foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME turns any rock it digs through molten with the intense heat radiating off its body. Once the POKENAME moves on, the lava quickly cools.
author: kiwiarms

entry: A young POKENAME burrows through volcanoes in search of a rock to become its shell. Once it finds a rock it particularly likes, it will keep it for the rest of its life.
author: secondegg

entry: It swings its head rapidly, flinging sharp stone horns at enemies. This tactic disorients attackers and provides an opening for escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often seen visiting beaches and ports. It is capable of making vehicles out of sand and dirt.
author: neonriser

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for a discarded bag of items while they sleep out in the wild. Their eyebrows are always pristine.
author: pankiwi

entry: It burrows through the ground as gracefully as a Mantine swims in water. It can gather enough speed from underground that it can launch over an entire field.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME cause a lot of problems in rural communities, frequently proving to be disruptive to crops and gardens. Researchers presume their tendency to disrupt crops and plants is due to them feeding on plant roots.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME appear to spend most of their time moving through the internet infrastructure looking for defunct websites and data stores. They eat files that have not been accessed in a long time, preferring the taste of stagnant data.
author: darkwolfe

entry: POKENAME digs straight down by spinning at incredible speeds, not stopping until it hits rock too hard to break through. Once it does, it spins in reverse to travel back up the hole it made.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It can manipulate sandstorms, keeping its den clear of debris. This ability makes it an expert at surviving in arid environments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME float a few inches above the ground, scanning the dirt below them with their magnets for traces of metal. When they find a concentration of metal in the soil, they spark happily and scoop as much soil as they can out of the ground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME float a few inches above the ground, scanning the dirt below them with their magnets for traces of metal. When they find a concentration of metal in the soil, they spark happily and scoop as much soil as they can out of the ground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME float a few inches above the ground, scanning the dirt below them with their metal detectors for traces of metal. Their detectors are powerful and able to sense even non-magnetic metals, making them invaluable for archaeological digs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: To manage the powerful electricity that flows through its body, POKENAME ensures that its feet are always grounded.
author: kiwiarms

entry: The gravitational fields around POKENAME shift wildly as they dig through the earth. Often, the ground will cling to them in a perfect sphere, protecting them from attackers.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are exceptional diggers, able to travel for hundreds of miles without break. They will consume the dirt as they dig, absorbing its minerals into their claws to strengthen them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME gathers mud in its mouth and then forms a Polished Mud Ball, which it spits up with pride. It can only make one per day, as the process drains a surprising amount of its energy.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Its hind legs have developed enough to allow it to walk on land. The pile of rocks on its head is actually part of its skull that extrudes out during growth.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: Although they make their nests underground, POKENAME spend most hours of the day keeping watch above ground. Their giant arms make them formidable in battle, though their skin is soft and more suited to damp conditions.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: When under stress, it ramps up venom production within its body. Farmers find it a persistent nuisance, as POKENAME has an unintentional habit of ruining their crops by burrowing through the soft soil where seeds have recently been planted.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The sand flowing from its body is used by glassblowers in Hoenn to create delicate flutes. These instruments are prized for their clarity and beautiful tone.
author: .izik

entry: It used its pointed nose to break through the metal shell it inhabits, and now uses it to root around for food. The arms are just for show.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Nobody knows how POKENAME is able to move the legs of the Metagross husk it inhabits, and x-rays cannot penetrate its outer layer to reveal what goes on inside.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME uses its aura sensing capabilities as a way of navigating its winding tunnels. The longest recorded POKENAME tunnel is 50 miles long, stretched out.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It prefers digging through harder surfaces, finding sand too boring. This preference makes it well-suited for excavating ancient ruins and hidden treasures.
author: .izik

entry: Because of its weak eyesight, it relies on its bulbous nose when underground.  It will dig until its nose bounces off of something hard, then POKENAME will proceed to repeatedly hit the blockade until it breaks through.
author: teatedtiten

entry: The red gemlike fruit on POKENAME's back is rich in nutrients. Spelunkers dry thin slices of it for long-term sustenance.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are commonly seen assisting miners by using their hard heads to break through solid rock or to break apart large formations of ores. Their heads are hard enough to endure a falling rock without feeling a thing.
author: infinex21

entry: Although they typically stand and walk on their hind legs, they can walk on all four of their limbs. They tend to do this to help carry injured miners or to help haul goods and equipment.
author: infinex21

entry: The eye-like indents at the top of its skull do not actually allow POKENAME to see, but they will glow when POKENAME uses some moves, such as Metal Burst. It will constantly seek out ore to devour.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Urban legend states that if you hold your ear towards the ground, you can hear POKENAME singing from inside its tunnels.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME cause tremors as they dig through the ground, consuming massive amounts of soil and rock. It is believed that many large caves are actually the product of these Pokémon.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's body is surprisingly tender and sensitive, so POKENAME coats it with hardened stone and jewels it finds while digging underground. It instills the gems it collects with portions of its own power, making them capable of firing light beams.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME digs underground, buried treasures and clumps of dirt stick to their body, forming a sort of protective barrier. Treasure hunters seek out these Pokémon in hopes of collecting any treasures that fall off.
author: chibitales

entry: It seems that POKENAME carries Diglett on its back from field to field. You'll only find it on fertile soil.
author: spagalapof

entry: POKENAME spend most of their lives burrowing underground, creating complex tunnel networks for their family to live in. They surface when they hear other POKENAME families digging toward them, giving angry chirps to scare them away from their home.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It is said that POKENAME goes around dark tunnels in order to ambush and pop up behind unsuspecting prey. It may currently be among you right now.
author: xenophacilus

entry: An iconic and well-loved fusion. A popular kids toy, named Mr. Dighead, was modelled after it.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME detects and digs up nearby buried objects as if it were treasure. It's recommended that Trainers keep their POKENAME away from graveyards.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's appearance of being wedged in the dirt beckons one to pick it up, but it evades would-be wielders by sinking further into the ground.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME tunnels can be found around the base of mountains, their burrow networks having multiple exits to allow them to search for food and water. They dig using their exceptionally hard spines, scraping through even the toughest rock.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It gathers rocks as it emerges from the ground to protect its sensitive body from the sun. The strength it carries while fighting with its crystalline horns leads people to theorize it has a much larger body underground.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME burrows a yard underground, eating the roots of plants. Farmers have pulled up fresh vegetables only to find bite marks taken out of them.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME ears are extremely sensitive to vibration, enabling them to hear movement above them from several meters underground. They are aggressive and will burst out from the soil to ambush anyone passing their home.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME surfaces in dry riverbeds after heavy rains, its rocky limbs stirring up nutrient-rich soil. Farmers once believed its presence was a blessing for abundant harvests.
author: segmoph

entry: During nights of the full moon, POKENAME get together and dig in circles. Rare Rock-type and Grass-type Pokémon can later be seen in those circles.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: This Pokémon waited for eons to be completed with truth or ideals. It eventually gave up and decided to go into agriculture instead.
author: barthandelus_real

entry: POKENAME love to go spelunking in unexplored caves and will collect a single rock from there to add to its rocky flowers. Its red-tinted visor protects its eyes from sand and dirt.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME absorb water from the ground, spraying it from their heads to water crops. Farmers commonly release these Pokémon into their fields, as the water they produce is especially pure.
author: santon5512

entry: A Diglett has taken up residence in the tomb of a mysterious unknown artist. It is said that it keeps the memories of the deceased in its memory.
author: elevn.

entry: With metallic fibers for hair and a skirt made of wax, POKENAME resembles a doll from afar. Children sometimes approach it because of this, allowing POKENAME to consume their life-force.
author: hophoppip

entry: Miners often bring a squad of POKENAME with them as a handy light source in deep caves. Their light is fueled by the minerals they consume.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME are said to be the guardians of an ancient subterranean civilization, patrolling tunnels for intruders. The small head on top is the actual body.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Having no arms, POKENAME instead extrudes its shovel-shaped stomach and uses it to dig through the ground.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME have learned that they enjoy drinking alcohol and are known for burrowing into cellars of taverns or breweries. They sometimes balance barrels on their wings and take them back to their nest.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It relies entirely on its sense of smell through its bright red nose to perceive the world. This keen olfactory sense helps it track food and detect danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tails are tipped with molten magma and are used to tunnel through even the densest of rock layers. They can move their tails independently of one another, enabling them to dig at high speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME dwells deep within the ground, only emerging when it observes a wish it desires to grant. If someone attempts to dig up POKENAME for selfish reasons, they will be turned to crystal and entombed deep within a cavern.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Due to their sensitivity to sunlight, POKENAME remain underground, feeding on roots and tubers. Their tunnels weaken the soil above and kill crops, making them pests to farmers.
author: santon5512

entry: A new martial art has been developed by watching POKENAME. This martial style involves holding dirt in your hand during a fight, then throwing it at an opponent and running away if you might lose.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME spends only a few hours awake to find roots to feed on. Once its belly is full, it sleeps underground until it wakes again. POKENAME are often accidentally dug up on farms.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's active nature makes it a nuisance on farms. It can consume up to its body weight in crop roots in a single day and disrupts even hardy root systems. Some farms have seen success in deterring POKENAME with underground walls around fields.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME communicate with one another through electrical pulses and self-caused seismic vibrations. They are able to understand one another through several miles of earth this way.
author: bobosmith01

entry: By opening and closing its jaws, it churns the sand around it into a raging whirlpool. This makes it impossible to extract it from its surroundings.
author: staghorn

entry: The flat gems embedded in its wings glow a bright auburn when it flies. This dazzling display attracts both prey and curious onlookers.
author: .izik

entry: Its thick skull is strong enough to break apart boulders with ease. This digging technique allows it to navigate through rocky terrain effortlessly.
author: .izik

entry: Groups of POKENAME work in sync to patrol deep underground tunnels. Unfortunately, most are hunted down by other territorial Pokémon, which quickly causes the colony of POKENAME to unravel. Their natural existence was recorded only some decades ago.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses its superheated nose to locate roots beneath the surface. It consumes them to fuel the flames within its body.
author: .izik

entry: Scientists have recently discovered POKENAME uses its large eyes to see inside dark tunnels. It is said they sing in order to communicate to one another from long distances underground.
author: rakunk

entry: It drills through soil with its long ears in search of delicious vegetables. If a farmer's crops mysteriously disappear overnight, POKENAME is often the culprit.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: The unseen portion of its body is said to extend over 30 feet in length. This hidden feature gives it an advantage in both hunting and defense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are almost blind, due to spending their whole lives either in pitch-black caverns or in the tunnels they dig. Instead, they use ultrasonic waves to detect obstacles while flying, and their sense of smell to detect prey while digging.
author: apieli

entry: POKENAME lives in an underground burrow concealed by a dirt-covered web. When a small Pokémon comes too close to the hidden entrance, it quickly emerges and snatches the prey.
author: hophoppip

entry: It tunnels extremely slowly, so it instead often hides in the grass, feeding on and absorbing energy from vegetation. If an unsuspecting Pokémon or Trainer steps on it, it will attack, in spite of the fact POKENAME is unlikely to be hurt by the act.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When only slightly beneath the soil, it keeps its horn exposed while chasing prey. This horn's presence helps it track targets via their vibrations in the dirt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bury themselves in the ground with only their rocky fins exposed. They use these fins to carve through rocks, slipping into narrow cracks to get into caves to try and get some rest in private.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Crystals are its main food source, and it defends them viciously. Dazzling underground caverns full of gems are certain to have a POKENAME ready to erupt from the ground to deter would-be jewel thieves.
author: sk372

entry: Spotting a POKENAME is considered good luck in cold regions because it is especially equipped to till soil enveloped in permafrost. Farmers' children make a game of building small shelters to attract them.
author: wormspawn

entry: POKENAME tend to congregate in small groups near farms. Farmers don't mind the presence, as the digging helps the soil, and POKENAME primarily targets rotten or dead crops as its main source of food.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers large clumps of dirt to use for its dances and cheers. After collecting, it lets loose electric shocks that stun any bugs within the dirt, making them easy to consume as a quick snack.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon spends most of its time underground, chewing on tree roots. It lets out mournful, harrowing cries, leading to the rumor that POKENAME are the ghosts of children who become lost and die in forests.
author: robbery_666

entry: A constant stream of nutrient-rich drool spills from the mouths of POKENAME. They wander around underground, leaving a trail of the liquid as they walk, nourishing the roots of plants above the surface.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its tunnels are filled with a spicy-scented red goo that enhances plant growth. Farmers appreciate its fertilizing effect on crops.
author: .izik

entry: Its body has the same consistency as mud, so many people avoid touching it for fear of getting dirty. POKENAME has a keen sense of smell that allows it to navigate perfectly through the intricate underground tunnels it digs together with its family.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its body is coated in a thick layer of mud. It thrives in rainy areas where mud is plentiful, but becomes timid in dry places where the earth is too dry to serve as a coating.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME came into being after a Diglett took control of a discarded rock body. Its head will dip in and out at high speeds to dodge attacks.
author: serversizeme

entry: A constant stream of nutrient-rich drool spills from the mouths of POKENAME. They wander around underground, leaving a trail of the liquid as they walk, nourishing the roots of plants above the surface.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Gardens of POKENAME travel together in search of fertile fields to call home for the day. They extend into the air and wave around one another, the petals on their necks absorbing sunlight as they perform their communal dance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Caverns inhabited by POKENAME are completely devoid of light, as it consumes any source of illumination. Though not aggressive, it is drawn to travelers carrying lanterns, flashlights, etc., casting them into darkness as it consumes the new light.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's diminutive stature belies a large amount of strength that lets it dig through the ground with ease. Anything unfortunate enough to be above it when it surfaces will be sent flying.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sets itself upside down, hiding most of its body beneath the dirt to appear like a normal Diglett. When something attempts to prey on it, it flips over and poisons them with its many toxic spines.
author: sk372

entry: It can dig rapidly by spinning its arms, reaching speeds of up to 40 miles per hour. If it can't dig into the terrain, it is forced to waddle slowly.
author: staghorn

entry: It can throw its hat as a weapon, using it to strike foes from a distance. This hat is crafted from its favorite stones, making it both stylish and dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: Gardens of POKENAME travel together in search of fertile fields to call home for the day. If they ever get separated from the rest of their group, POKENAME become lonely, remaining in place in the hopes their family will return to them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Due to being made completely of sand, POKENAME became the home to a colony of Diglett. It is unknown if this is a symbiotic or parasitic relationship.
author: serversizeme

entry: Found in deep and cold caverns, POKENAME feast on gemstones and minerals they dig up. Though they have bouts with Sableye, they will sometimes work together to find food and split their treasures.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME love to dig and refuse to stop once they start digging with their sharp claws. Many play a vital role in tilling soil for farmers, working themselves until they are happily exhausted.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME digs through gravel with ease, using its sharp, armored scales to break apart stones. It chews on tree roots underground to absorb energy and sustain itself.
author: .izik

entry: It is a shy Pokémon that lives somewhat near the shoreline, just when the dirt starts to become a little firmer. If frightened, it digs away far underground at incredible speed.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It would rather flee than fight. Ideally, it would prefer not to be spotted at all; it will roll around in the dry dirt to try and camouflage itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Among others of its kind, POKENAME is boisterous and eager to train and spar. In the presence of others, however, it is shy and meek, and prone to digging a hole to hide itself in.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME moves swiftly through the dirt across riversides, only coming up to catch insects to eat. If it encounters trouble, it uses tightly-packed clods of dirt encased in bubbles as projectiles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found near pumpkin patches, tunneling through the ground to create fertile soil. It will whip farmers with the vine on its head if they try to touch it.
author: mistymagius

entry: It would rather flee than fight. Ideally, it would prefer not to be spotted at all; it will roll around in the dry dirt to try and camouflage itself.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spend large portions of their life underground, feeding on the roots of plants. When the ground temperature gets too warm, they dig toward the surface and fan their wings in the air to cool their bodies.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are commonly found in canyons. There, they battle for turf by firing mud shots at each other.
author: pokebio

entry: The actual length of a fully grown POKENAME's body is considered a scientific mystery. The current agreed upon estimate is "less than a kilometer, probably".
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME lack the jaws necessary to hunt for prey, so they resort to digging up roots and seeds to eat. If they are not scavenging for food, then they rely on underhanded techniques to steal food from Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It symbolizes friendship and lasting love. A glimpse of it on one's honeymoon brings good luck to the newlyweds.
author: spagalapof

entry: This fusion, known by many as "Dugduo," consists of two Diglett sharing a body. They always emit sounds as if the two of them complement each other's speech, but sometimes it feels like they expect a third Diglett to be talking.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME now spends much of its time above ground, rarely digging holes for itself anymore. It spends some of its time putting dirt back into long-abandoned holes created by other Diglett.
author: sk372

entry: Although now POKENAME resembles its Alolan counterpart, it exhibits little if any of the variant's differentiating attributes. Despite this, it seems quite proud of its newfound sprout of hair.
author: sk372

entry: It makes tunnels beneath botanical gardens, feasting on the roots of plants. Gardeners must work diligently to prevent it from damaging prized flowers.
author: .izik

entry: Before POKENAME rests in any place, it will arrange rocks to form the shape of wings around its body. The motivation for this behavior is unknown, but some theorize that the fusion's Wingull side misses the wings it once had.
author: hophoppip

entry: For a long time, researchers assumed that POKENAME were not a true fusion but were instead simply a pair of Diglett. When they were observed constantly sticking together it became clear that they were a new fusion species.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are excellent pest control, as they can easily dig into a varmint's den. Farmers keep several of them around for this reason.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME often causes trouble near caves, biting or scratching hikers who approach its burrow. Most people avoid it, but treasure hunters sometimes follow it, hoping to claim the gold coin embedded in its head.
author: brachionite

entry: POKENAME hunt Diglett as their prey, tracking them as they dig underground. They will forcibly pull them out of their burrows, taunting them before they consume them.
author: santon5512

entry: When POKENAME burrow underground and are covered in light debris, they are indistinguishable from other volcanic vents. When disturbed from their rest, they unleash plumes of lava that cause searing burns.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME combine dirt and mud to create a sphere. This sphere is then polished to create a smooth, glossy surface. POKENAME happily show off this sphere when they play with other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It often burrows up into farms to steal crops that might ease its aching head. Because of its pitiful expression as it does so, most farmers can't bring themselves to chase it off.
author: sk372

entry: Due to a lack of spatial awareness, POKENAME's tunnels are incoherent and can be extremely dangerous to foundations above them.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Researched recently found out that POKENAME don't actually dig their holes. Instead, when they wish to move through the earth, they excrete a concentrated slime from their skin that turns earth into mud, which they can push through with ease.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME use their webbed hands like shovels, rapidly digging through the soil to create their tunnels. They are popular with construction crews for their ability to help with the installation of underground pipes and cables.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spin their bodies to move through the ground, acting like a drill. This spinning loosens the soil around them, leaving it perfectly tilled.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME generate electricity while underground until their bodies can no longer handle the energy. When groups of POKENAME emerge from the ground, they release bursts of electricity that zap everything nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have been introduced to farms to till the soil and water plants. Many farmers greatly appreciate POKENAME for their work to help farms produce healthy crops.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are becoming more and more popular for use on farmlands over Diglett due to their higher strength and stamina. However, they share Diglett's weakness to sustained light, and tend to be less swift than Diglett, too.
author: bobosmith01

entry: People often think that they saw the body of a Diglett, though it was, in fact, a POKENAME. This Pokémon can burrow, and it pulls its prey under the earth.
author: ayutac

entry: POKENAME does not appear to wear a power-save belt like Machoke does. The vein-like patterns on the sides of its arms vary in color based on POKENAME's diet.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME create intricate tunnels using their roots, absorbing water and nutrients from the soil as they do so. When threatened, they can retreat into these burrows in a fraction of a second.
author: santon5512

entry: The way POKENAME absorb nutrients is very unorthodox. Seeing as they have no root system, they just dig tunnels underground by eating the soil and synthesizing the vitamins and minerals directly from it.
author: bradlybro199

entry: It uses its well developed arms to grab more dirt for the mound around its body. The more impressive the mound, the easier it is to acquire mates.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME spends all day packing more dirt around itself, in order to hide its body from the world. It does this out of an advanced sense of shame.
author: kiwiarms

entry: It's said many Diglett coming together sometimes build guardians to protect their burrows. The mechanism through which it gained life is unknown.
author: fuade

entry: The shyness of this underground horse is legendary. It'll only come out of its hole if there's nobody around for 100km.
author: spagalapof

entry: Nobody has ever seen a POKENAME without a shell, as its jaws are clasped too tightly around the Pokémon's body to pry it out.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME possesses magnetism that allows it to move and shift dirt around in small quantities. It uses this to dig out holes for it to bury itself in for the night when it sleeps.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME magnetically attracts soil rich in minerals, which it feeds to its young until they are old enough to use their magnets themselves.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME always keep their feet underground, ready to burrow when needed. Sometimes it gets stuck while digging if the leek it's holding is too big.
author: frokachu

entry: Extremely simpleminded, POKENAME's response to danger is to bury its head beneath the dirt. According to its internal logic, if it can't see an attacker, the attacker can't see it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leaves behind a thick trail of mud as it moves about. This substance is extremely durable when it hardens, so many cities will use the Pokémon to help fill in cracks and potholes.
author: mepp.

entry: Their bodies are made of thick mud and dirt, helping them absorb plant life for nutrients. The mud and soil they are made of is an exceptionally good fertilizer, often being used by farmers.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME channel an otherworldly power to make little windows between rocks that they use to observe or greet people they take an interest in. Strangely, these windows are completely invisible when viewed from the other side.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A Diglett got tired of plowing the land on farms, so it made a deal with a Haunter to terrorize the farmers.
author: elevn.

entry: If you find yourself deep in a cavern below ground, stay close to your torchlight. POKENAME don't take kindly to intruders.
author: jemeremmazza

entry: While concealed underground, POKENAME expose only the tips of their tails to mimic Diglett. When a predator takes the bait, POKENAME erupt from the earth and strike with tremendous force.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When its Trainer cannot sleep, POKENAME will sprinkle some of its special sand into their eyes, which will cause them to doze off.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME will use their claws to burrow in the sand, concealing themselves completely. When smaller prey passes by, they will burst from the ground, grabbing them with their claws and pulling them under.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's claws have rudimentary minds of their own. Though the smaller claw is simple and obedient, the larger claw is more aggressive and may even attack the main body if enraged.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME defend their territories aggressively, emerging from the ground when they sense a disturbance in the soil. Using the cannons on their backs, they will fire rocks at intruders.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME has a precise gem on its back that flakes off toxic shards when damaged. By scraping its gem against rocks, it produces clouds of these shards to ward off miners.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME explode deep underground, they often create a quarry of lovely pink diamonds behind. Although breathtaking, these diamonds are incredibly fragile and will violently explode if they're dropped, or even held just a bit too firmly.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME are the rulers of large groups of Carbink. The sceptre they carry is unique to each tribe and is passed down to a young POKENAME by their parents once they are ready to rule.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: Born deep underground, the heat and pressure from magma flows harden POKENAME's rock helmet into pink diamonds. Due to the rarity of their birth, they are treated by their tribe as royalty.
author: ghostslythe

entry: As they grow, POKENAME wander further from their tribe and are known to be friendly to most other species. If attacked, they allow foes to close the distance, watch as attacks bounce off their armor, and retaliate with a heavy axe strike.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are often found surrounded by extremely sturdy gems, which it uses to fend off predators like Sableye as it rests.
author: quitecomical1997

entry: Shards of the crystals on its body splinter away should POKENAME hit a wall too forcefully. These discarded pieces have begun to become popular material for accessories in mountainous regions.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME will often clean and polish myriad colorful crystals, to the point that they may even grow as smooth as the pink gemstone within their pouch. They will carry some smaller, smooth gems within their pouch and offer them to their friends.
author: infinex21

entry: The soft glow from POKENAME's tiara is said to help restore coral reefs, though it rarely stays in place long enough for the glow to take noticeable effect. POKENAME cares deeply for its aquatic brethren, even if it often gets bullied.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Dubbed the "Princess Of The Sea" by some sailors, POKENAME swims gracefully in coastal waters. It dives to the sea floor in search of gems to add to its tiara.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME have gleaming scales all over their wings that sparkle when the sunlight hits them. POKENAME are elegant protectors of the environment that help Pokémon back up when they fall from trees.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Any light that passes through POKENAME's limbs illuminates the area in a beautiful pink glow. When threatened, it will concentrate this dazzling light into its attackers' eyes, temporarily blinding them.
author: vlavoc

entry: POKENAME mainly live near underground bodies of water, though some have been found near bodies of waters in caves. Where they live is oft bountiful with precious crystals that they will fiercely defend if they do not deem one worthy.
author: infinex21

entry: Due to the perfect geometric structure of POKENAME diamonds, they have become an invaluable component in high-tech computing equipment. POKENAME's tight crystal lattice also makes its body almost invulnerable to physical damage.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME presses carbon from the air into a cloud of tiny diamonds that whirl around itself. It sleeps on a nest of gems, and even unconsciously, its power whirls a violent storm that keeps it aloft.
author: pattybgoode

entry: With each flap of its wings, POKENAME compresses the carbon in the air around it into diamonds. Though it's said to be one of the most beautiful sights in the world, the hail of superheated gems it trails leaves a path of destruction in its wake.
author: knilk

entry: After years of being hunted for their crystals, there are few of these Pokémon that remain. Thankfully, they have begun to flourish as of late and few remain who would dare to try and obtain even their shed crystals.
author: infinex21

entry: They care for a large gem that formed from the leftover energy of their evolution, which continues to store more energy. They thrive on the residual energy released by their large gems and protect them as if they were their eggs.
author: infinex21

entry: Its claws are tougher than diamond and sharper than obsidian. With its wings, it can position itself to best direct beams of light from the gem upon its head at foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME attunes its psychic energies through pink quartz crystals. It is said that any who gaze into its crown become compelled to follow its commands unquestionably.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are elusive Pokémon that have only ever been seen from afar, for they can fully disappear if one draws too near. Those few that a POKENAME considers a friend are said to be blessed with a beautiful pink crystal of an unknown source.
author: infinex21

entry: The glistening leaves that POKENAME produce create sparkles when exposed to light. Whenever they feel particularly generous, they give out these leaves to other Pokémon as gifts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Pokémon from far and wide flock to the glittering pink light that reflects from POKENAME's crystals. It acts as a benevolent ruler, soothing its followers and dispelling disputes with its calming glow.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME produce heart-shaped gems along their chest. Many are only found in zoos today, due to poachers overhunting them for their gems.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME love to sing and use their small baton like a microphone to help them project their crystal-clear voice. They often throw tantrums when other Pokémon ignore their singing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends the majority of the time asleep. It is conserving its energy to produce the wings it obtains when it evolves.
author: bitterchemicalhaze

entry: POKENAME are full of joy and whimsy, soaring through the sky and playing games with Trainers and Pokémon. Their crystal shards are said to bring great fortune but are only available to those who play their games.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME only sleeps once per year for an entire week, shielding itself in a diamond cocoon. While POKENAME is in this state, the Carbink it rules over will protect it with their lives.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: The gel that POKENAME produces to keep its skin moist contains trace amounts of diamonds. It is not uncommon to find prospectors following this Pokémon and sifting through the gel that drips off it while trying to make it rich.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME scrape the gem on their back against rocks to produce clouds of toxic shards. If inhaled, these shards cause dizziness and nausea in both Trainers and Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates vines to grab rocks around it, scraping shards off the gem on its back. When in danger, it flings these gem shards to cut through its foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A good-natured spellcaster, POKENAME uses its ribbons to send out sparkling trails of magical energy to those it meets. Those afflicted by the dust have their perceptions changed, claiming that everything seems more vibrant and beautiful afterward.
author: sk372

entry: According to myth, POKENAME nests deep in underground labyrinths, its home glittering like cut diamond. With the use of its laser-firing tail and power over gems, it can create dazzling gemstone statues with ease.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's shells are to be handled with extreme care; they are incredibly fragile and take months to reform. The shells of POKENAME are sold at high prices due to their beauty and fragility.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: Its collected gemstones have become part of its body due to it awakening its latent draconic powers, which have made its body tougher. It can shoot crystals from its tubular mouth, be they sharp or blunt, at high speeds even underwater.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME protect clusters of data they've collected in pink crystals. Anyone attempting to mess with these delicate structures is subject to intense Diamond Storm attacks.
author: chibitales

entry: The gems carried by POKENAME are said to boost the body's natural healing abilities when held close. Their egg-like gemstone within their pouch will glow when they are happiest.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME dance about within crystal-lined caves, hopping from crystal to crystal clad in electrical sparks while in the air. The crystals on their bodies store electricity within them, which causes them to emit a pleasant glow.
author: infinex21

entry: Reclusive yet friendly, POKENAME casts hexes and illusions that make it difficult to find it deep within mountain caverns. Those that manage to find it despite the spells will be rewarded with a gem of unparalleled beauty it creates for them.
author: sk372

entry: It's thought that POKENAME's arrows make people fall in love, but no mechanism has been found. Biologists instead conclude that POKENAME can sense compatibility and pricks people to give them the courage to confess their feelings.
author: .fedoraman

entry: It will grow attached to a single, pink gemstone and care for it like it were an egg. This gemstone will become polished and smooth the longer that a POKENAME cares for it and carries it around within its pouch.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon's age can be judged by how many jewels it has. These jewels store the excessive electricity POKENAME generates, and if one of them gets damaged or snaps in half, all of the stored energy breaks free and electrocutes everything around.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME hide within dark caves to protect themselves from predators and poachers alike. When a beam of light hits one of their crystals, the light refracts into a rainbow spectrum that illuminates the cave around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each time POKENAME leaps from the water, it leaves behind tiny pink crystals in the ocean. Some jewelers collect these for use in high-priced necklaces.
author: .izik

entry: Its beautiful, gem-like body is as tough as diamond. This Pokémon is capable of punching tunnels through cave walls with its massive, muscular arms. The drills upon its head can puncture even steel as though it were paper.
author: jadey.1557

entry: The bouquets on POKENAME's arms are made of intricately cut diamonds. It fires them as projectiles at its enemies.
author: hophoppip

entry: This joyful Pokémon is found, rarely, in gemstone caves with high ceilings. POKENAME is loving and kindhearted, and naturally inclined to the role of a protector in the wild.
author: nyoomymph

entry: This Pokémon's age can be judged by how many jewels it has. These jewels store the excessive electricity POKENAME generates, and if one of them gets damaged or snaps in half, all of the stored energy breaks free and electrocutes everything around.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME is widely regarded as the most beautiful Pokémon of the jungle. As it sits high in trees, its bright pink crystals cast light through the canopy, creating a gorgeous pattern on the ground below.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: The many gem-like parts of POKENAME's body absorb and store energy from any sources of light nearby. When in danger, it curls up into a ball and fires the stored energy as beams of light in every direction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is considered to be a queen among Carbink, capable of manifesting pure emotions as equally-pure crystals. Said crystals are considered treasures to many, but are fervently defended by POKENAME and its Carbink subjects.
author: infinex21

entry: Though their crystals shine with the natural light they have stored, they are dangerous if provoked. They let those they trust touch their crystals but will loose beams of light at threats; the light they emit is said to be gentle and warm.
author: infinex21

entry: The gem on POKENAME's back naturally flakes off shards for them to use. These shards become high velocity projectiles when thrown from their vines and leech toxic chemicals into the bodies of their foes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is found in deep ocean caves, attracting prey with its glittering diamond-like growths. It is highly mobile, burrowing into the silt to avoid other predators and swimming gracefully with its side and tail fins.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Those who touch the dazzling diamonds embedded in its fur may catch visions of impending disasters or natural catastrophes. For centuries, its ethereal beauty has enchanted and inspired countless poets, who dedicated sonnets and verses to it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are quick to flee from most people, but will protect other Pokémon with their many pink crystals that they seem to control through thought alone. They have the ability to heal the injuries of other Pokémon via the large gem on their head.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's cavernous shell serves as a home for Carbink, who will, in return, guard the cave's jewels from Sableye and other intruders. Its ability to naturally grow crystals in its shell has made it a highly sought after fusion.
author: ramensracing

entry: The blade of this sentient sword is as hard as diamond and far less brittle. It dwells in caves, luring in prey with the glimmer of its crystal before sapping its lifeforce.
author: hophoppip
