entry: POKENAME barks and growls at anything, but its bark is far worse than its bite. The only hope it has in taking down a predator or prey is to work in large schools.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are most active when they are asleep, as they snarl and claw at whatever they see in their dreams. When they inevitably awaken, they often feel so sore that they fall asleep after a quick snack.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME try to show their fangs and jump high to appear more intimidating. Due to their small size and facial features, they mostly appear cute even when trying to intimidate others.
author: entomoxie

entry: When POKENAME sleep their coats rub together and create tons of static energy. For the first few hours after they wake up their coats release random bolts of electricity when POKENAME bark or run at high speeds.
author: bradlybro199

entry: In swampy areas, packs of POKENAME hunt together. They prefer waist-deep water, moving quickly to corner prey through the aid of their superior swimming abilities.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME threaten foes by using their claws to pelt them with debris, though they lack the strength to do real damage. If a foe strikes back, however, a POKENAME will either curl up and roll away or dig underground.
author: infinex21

entry: It is a nimble Pokémon that can easily climb great heights. Social, it prefers to be around those of the same species.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME threaten others with bared fangs and flame-laced growls. They quickly flee if these tactics fail. Despite these unruly habits, these Pokémon love affection and attention, so they are popular pets.
author: infinex21

entry: Following a strict hierarchy rule, the POKENAME with the largest crest is the de facto leader of the pack. As such, it leads any hunting efforts, as well as being the first to dip into muddy water when it comes time to rest and cool down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME relentlessly hunt their prey in packs. They work together to steer the Pokémon they are chasing toward muddy riversides, where the POKENAME will have the advantage in the difficult terrain.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's sense of smell can pinpoint a fruit tree from almost a mile away. It spits streams of water at the fruit to knock branches down so it can feast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is territorial, baring its fangs and quivering with rage at passersby. When it senses a Trainer confrontation, it quickly teleports away out of fear.
author: ghostslythe

entry: While chasing prey, POKENAME's fur shifts to match its target's dominant color. The display appears to taunt prey before the final chase.
author: .izik

entry: Its large incisors can grow an inch a week. To keep them short and sharp, POKENAME gnaws on trees and rocks alike.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME use their secondary set of jaws to intimidate others, even those who have not yet posed a threat. The moment anything suddenly touches them, no matter how light the touch, they will yelp and run away.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME show up in packs to warn other Pokémon in the area of natural disasters. Some Pokémon are scared of them because of their sharp fangs and claws, which distract from the message of impending doom.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's skull-like mask glows a faint baby blue when it howls beside its pack. This trait fades entirely once it is captured in a Poké Ball.
author: .izik

entry: While howling, POKENAME's fur-covered feelers wiggle uncontrollably near its body. Each POKENAME has a wiggle pattern entirely unique to itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME move in packs, but lack cohesion due to somewhat independent personalities. Fights over hierarchy are common as members pelt others with fireballs flung from their tails.
author: sk372

entry: As night falls, howls echo from the tunnels POKENAME digs with its pack. By midnight, they emerge together to begin their hunt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather in small packs, honing their skills and cooperation through intense training sessions. The one that can flare up its aura the greatest in one burst is considered the leader.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hangs from trees, growling and swiping its lanky arms at anything that gets near. It quickly retreats and hides away at the first sign of retaliation, however.
author: sk372

entry: When howling together, POKENAME's pack creates massive whirlpools nearby. They take turns riding these whirlpools for fun.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's bulb is covered in thick fur that grows denser during the winter months. This helps it stay warm while waiting for spring to arrive.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a persistence predator. Once it chooses a child it wants, it will chase them for miles until they give up. If the kid stands up for themself, POKENAME will retreat immediately with its tail between its legs.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME howl whenever they release spores, which inadvertently leads Pokémon to investigate the sound. When approached, POKENAME release a cloud of spores that stick to other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME travel in packs to find people with bitter feelings in their hearts. Once they find a target, they shower the person with affection by licking their face and playing games.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each night, flocks of POKENAME howl at the moon. The one with the loudest howl leads the flock for the following day.
author: .izik

entry: Quite aggressive and containing a highly venomous bite, POKENAME is considered quite dangerous on its own. It is made even more dangerous due to the fact that it almost always travels in packs of a dozen or more.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hide in cattails to ambush aquatic Pokémon that swim in the water nearby. Sometimes they are unsuccessful because they cannot swim.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME act aggressively and will lash out at threats and prey with hit-and-run attacks. However, they become very timid when confronted or if their targets fight back enough.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hunt in large packs with excellent coordination, making them extremely dangerous to come across. On occasion, they may fight over who gives the final stroke, giving prey a faint and fleeting opportunity to escape.
author: sk372

entry: Each bark from POKENAME releases a puff of sweet pink pollen. The scent invigorates its pack, sharpening their senses during hunts.
author: .izik

entry: Members of POKENAME packs find and collect shiny rocks to store in their fluffy manes. The more stones stored within their fur, the higher their ranking among the pack hierarchy.
author: sk372

entry: It delivers a concussive headbutt to anything that meets its gaze, relying on its reinforced cranium. While it relentlessly pursues retreating prey with bared fangs, its bravado instantly shatters if a target manages to land a counterstrike.
author: shivaequinox

entry: POKENAME hide in cattails where they wait for aquatic Pokémon to swim close before pouncing. When they feel particularly charitable, they allow other Pokémon to ride on their head.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swims with its pack in heart-shaped formations in the ocean depths in search of prey. Their howl is bone-chilling when heard from the water's surface due to its sheer volume and pitch.
author: .izik

entry: After the fusion, POKENAME became even more aggressive and ferocious. Its saliva contains a large number of bacteria, so anyone bitten by its fangs is at risk of severe infection.
author: fiordaliso

entry: After the fusion, POKENAME became even more aggressive and ferocious. Its saliva contains a large number of bacteria, so anyone bitten by its fangs is at risk of severe infection.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME live in packs with other Poochyena to hunt down large prey. Their place in the pack hierarchy can be confusing for them, because they have a mature body but exhibit child-like behaviors.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prowls the streets at night, sniffing out food from unattended trash bins. If chased, it flees in a zigzag pattern, but when cornered it defends itself with relentless bites.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prowls the streets at night, sniffing out food from unattended trash bins. If chased, it flees in a zigzag pattern, but when cornered it defends itself with relentless bites.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prowls the streets at night, sniffing out food from unattended trash bins. If chased, it flees in a zigzag pattern, but when cornered it defends itself with relentless bites.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its elongated body allows POKENAME to sneak into even the smallest burrows in search of prey. Since its natural predators are very active during the day, it tends to leave its burrow only when night falls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME actively seeks out other, preferably smaller Pokémon to bully and chase away from food it wants. If a larger Pokémon has food POKENAME wants, it will gather its siblings or friends to help chase them off.
author: chibitales

entry: Multiple POKENAME huddle close for protection, and howl in unison to scare off foes. The first one to evolve becomes leader of the pack.
author: mepp.

entry: Lacking mobility, POKENAME flees from most anything by shooting string to high places and reeling itself away from danger. It does occasionally seek vengeance by dropping its heavy body down on aggressors from high places, however.
author: sk372

entry: The pollen POKENAME releases from its wings carries a sickly sweet scent to attract prey. It does this from trees alongside others of its pack before they howl and descend on their target together.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunt in groups of eight, with one sacrificing itself in an explosive distraction while the others attack with Crunch. This coordination has been studied by botanists.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will jump out of the grass to startle its prey and then chase it to exhaust it. An eerie whistling tune can be heard where POKENAME is.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME has a conflicting nature, cowardly but desiring to be brave. It's not uncommon to see it repeatedly pick a fight, then retreat from retaliation, only to rejoin the fray and then run away again.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often seen gathering in small flocks near seaside towns. When one member spots prey, the entire flock hungrily descends upon it with a flurry of pecks and bites.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME work in small groups to take down prey both in the air and in the ocean. Though the teamwork is admirable, once the prey is downed, every POKENAME greedily tries to swallow the prize for itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have an acute sense of smell that allows them to stalk prey over long distances. Water does not impede their stalking, as their hairy legs allow them to walk on water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The eye-like portions of POKENAME's wings serve to intimidate foes that draw too close to its nest. It howls loudly while displaying them to frighten intruders away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are most active at dawn and dusk. Their keen night vision and silent footsteps allow them to sneak up on groggy Trainers to steal their coins.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though physically quite frail, POKENAME is quite adept at intimidating others. It lets out a quiet growl as a warning, before stunning aggressors with deafening barks.
author: sk372

entry: Sassy and picky, POKENAME will chortle at the misfortune of others. They do get along with other POKENAME, however.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME howls with its pack, the air crackles with static. In seconds, they unleash a coordinated electric strike on their chosen prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME charge their paws with electricity by rubbing them against other Electric-type Pokémon. They are capable of reaching branches high above the ground with a charged leap.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rub their paws against other Electric-type Pokémon to store energy in their legs. They are capable of sprinting across football fields with a sudden discharge of electricity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have special scent glands on their tails that attract other Pokémon. When enough Pokémon have gathered they begin a small musical ensemble.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have scent glands that produce a pungent scent that attracts Bug-type Pokémon. When they have gathered a small group, they gather around the POKENAME as they lead a performance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a common starter pet in the Hoenn region as it is incredibly lazy and easy-going. It becomes very excited when encountering strong scents and tries to eat items it comes across.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME releases smoke from its hump whenever it tries to intimidate foes. POKENAME often loses its targets due to its vision being obstructed by the smoke it emits.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME prefers to keep its claws concealed, extending them from its fur only when it howls. This same reflex triggers if a member of its pack howls, a response it has difficulty controlling.
author: .izik

entry: During winter, POKENAME coils its serpentine body together with others of its pack while sleeping to retain warmth. Should a member fall ill, the pack will abandon them and refuse to let them coil with the group.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets out a sharp whine whenever they want something from their Trainer. If they don't get what they want, then they set fire to things nearby until reprimanded.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite their menacing appearance, POKENAME love to sleep in fields of flowers. They are known to teleport away if approached by Trainers or other Pokémon but will always return to the same flower field once they go away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME packs hunt large aquatic prey, but will scatter if the foe begins to gain an advantage. A lone POKENAME can be easily won over with treats, but humans should be careful of the toxins in its fluffy tufts of hair.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME seem to get energy from the moon rather than the sun. It bathes in the moon's calming aura. POKENAME are rarely seen during the day.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its fierce and touchy nature leads both humans and Pokémon to keep their distance. Only the most patient of people manage to forge a strong bond with POKENAME and draw out its true potential.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are fierce predators, hunting in packs under the cover of darkness. When ready to attack, the fur along their backs will erupt into flames, intimidating foes with fiery growls.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's fur retains constant moisture, giving it a perpetually damp feel. During hot summers, the moisture increases to help it stay cool.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME live and hunt in packs of at least ten individuals. They will travel via tunnels they dig underground and emerge at their leader's behest to surround their prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live in packs in the jungle, working together perfectly and never defying their leader. The leader can be identified by its bright body markings.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: In a pack of wild POKENAME, the one with the longest fur and longest claws is the leader. Using their claws, POKENAME can quickly take down most Pokémon, even some that are larger than they are.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME operate akin to human gangs. Should a strong Trainer defeat them in a fight, they will yield without question. While their bite is strong, their martial arts are stronger.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME fan their tails and crests to send signals to each other about which way to run. They work together to chase prey through rivers until their target is too exhausted to continue.
author: .realthree

entry: Unlike their cousins, POKENAME are lone hunters, stalking prey in the darkness. When their target's guard is down, they stun them with a mind-numbing howl before dragging them into the night.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's fur shifts color with every bark, cycling through hues unique to each individual. Packs can identify one another instantly by these shifting patterns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are emotionally intelligent and have the ability to sense the auras of their pack mates. When POKENAME are separated and lose track of their pack mates' auras, they howl until they are able to locate each other.
author: mochauspocus

entry: Packs of POKENAME gather once a year under the full moon to show off their skills. The POKENAME whose skills are deemed the most impressive is chosen as the new alpha.
author: mochauspocus

entry: It hunted in coordinated packs around a hundred million years ago. Whenever they aren't hunting, they train toughening their heads by headbutting one another.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Whenever POKENAME try to communicate with wild Pokémon about an impending disaster, they need to be careful not to scare them away. By bowing their head and lying on the ground, they can show that they are friendly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When two POKENAME meet floating in the night, they erupt into fierce howling contests. Their echoes can rattle entire forests awake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sheds its fur in massive quantities each spring. Tailors throughout Hoenn use this fur to craft pajamas renowned for their comfort and soothing softness.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME live in small packs and always follow the orders of their leader, be it during a hunt or when they are being hunted. They launch coordinated attacks using their sharp tusks that wear down any quarry they set their sights on.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME with sanguine red locks of fur is the one that leads its pack. These red locks denote its age and that it has endured many battles. It will be the one to deliver the finishing blow with its axe-like tusks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME decorates its dams with bones from its hunts. The largest dams have a Gyarados skull facing outwards.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME lead packs of Pokémon to help people with bitter feelings move on from their hatred. By engaging in play and being kind, they hope to absorb the negative energy and leave people better than when they first meet them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Thin fur coats the leaves on POKENAME's head, releasing a calming aroma. Once prey relaxes, it attacks in coordination with its pack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a fierce undersea hunter that operates in packs of up to a dozen. Working together, the pack can methodically take down larger prey in seconds, before succumbing to their feeding frenzy urges.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME howls, a thick gray acidic film coats its fur. Members of its own kind are unaffected by the substance and remain close.
author: .izik

entry: As night falls, POKENAME prowls the bays, howling to summon its underlings and rally them for the hunt. It frequently clashes with others of its kind, leaving deep scars in the ground where fierce battles took place.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are typically obsessed with using the flame on their wand to gaze into the future. Since longer predictions require larger flames, this often leads to POKENAME destroying their surroundings to predict what lies ahead.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME often struggle to understand why their packmates treat them like children. Their diminutive size makes them easy to pick on by others in their pack.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are solitary Pokémon, their hunting skills on par with an entire pack of Mightyena. They stalk their prey for miles from the shadows, pouncing when least expected before sinking their fangs in.
author: santon5512

entry: When encountering opponents larger than itself, POKENAME ruffles its bristly fur to appear bigger and intimidate them. Its saliva can be used to cure rabies that may afflict other wild Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME runs in sharp zigzag formations with its pack. They coordinate attacks through patterned barks that signal direction and speed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's pack howls in sequence before charging together. One detonates near the prey as a distraction while the others attack.
author: .izik

entry: Each flock of POKENAME has a designated leader whose orders are never disobeyed. With an aggressive nature and perfect coordination, these flocks will bully other Flying-Type Pokémon out of their territory.
author: mepp.

entry: Flocks of POKENAME gather near passing boats, howling into the moonlit sky. Some sailors believe their cries foretell stormy seas ahead.
author: .izik

entry: In the wild, POKENAME chase prey over land and water until their prey succumbs to exhaustion. Trainers who can prove their dedication and grit have an easier time catching them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME acts as a sentry for Poochyena packs, tracking prey from the sky. It makes loud howling noises to alert the pack to the prey's location and spits water to herd them toward its allies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is strictly nocturnal in the wild and almost never follows the orders of others. It simply goes wherever it pleases and fights whoever it deems as getting in its way. However, some Trainers love its adventurous and rebellious personality.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's packs spend hours stalking and planning on how to take down prey. More often than not, however, they end up overexerting themselves and begin to suffer from headaches.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have developed extremely sharp claws and teeth to defend themselves from their main rival, Swellgoose. These features seem to be rather useless, though, as most matches end with the POKENAME incapacitated.
author: turcai_87271

entry: It conjures ominous dark clouds to intimidate opponents. If that tactic fails, it unleashes raging wind storms to keep foes at bay.
author: hophoppip

entry: Despite POKENAME spending most of its days lazing about on beaches, it is a fierce predator. Many warnings have been put near beaches not to approach the Pokémon, as it will not hesitate to bite those who disturb it.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hunt in packs in order to wrap and constrain oversized prey. While each one could eat the whole prey, they use their sharp teeth to split the meal evenly among the pack members.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are sometimes used to vandalize buildings with their claws and any tools their Trainers give them. POKENAME often act overconfident or aggressive because of their strength, but studies show that they become docile if their tails are stroked.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is filled with pent-up energy, causing it to constantly roll from side-to-side. Its explosions come in pairs, causing it to fly off in one direction before careening the opposite way due to the explosive force.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are commonly found scavenging from garbage dumps, finding items to trade with other Pokémon. They often leave territorial markings; however, due to their constantly mutating genetic makeup, no two markings are ever the same.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME inflates its body slightly to allow it to jump around back and forth and burn off energy. Even when relatively idle, POKENAME still restlessly hops from side to side.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME aids rescuers in finding children lost in forests. It bounces on its tail whenever it needs to reach branches above the forest floor.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's bristly fur traps electrons, making it easier for it to coat itself in electric sparks. It spends most of its day rummaging through the city's alleys in search of food to fill its belly.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have keen senses of smell that allow them to quickly find specific fruits and mushrooms. They have a habit of moving in zigzag patterns; this pattern extends to them leaping from tree to tree.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are known to be excellent runners, darting in unpredictable ways to throw off predators. They are not known to be aggressive and are often wary of people.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are inherently curious about everything, so they are almost always wandering around in search of things. To ensure they do not get lost, they leave behind scorch marks by spitting small fireballs on the ground or at rocks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME normally flies in erratic zigzag patterns across the sky. Spotting one flying in a straight line is considered a bad sign, as it only does so when escaping danger.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME run around the forest using zig-zag patterns to train their leg muscles while searching for food. These curious Pokémon will scratch at the ground with their claws or talons when an interesting scent catches their attention.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME collects seemingly random objects it finds useful and stores them in its underwater den. This usually leaves the items soggy and unusable.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME plays by lobbing mud balls at others, it always alternates which hand throws the projectiles. It seems pathologically unable to use the same hand twice in a row.
author: sk372

entry: Although it appears to have the ability to predict the future, it actually sees only one of countless possibilities, so rarely is this ability useful. It is curious but shy, and generally tries to keep distance between itself and others.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME voraciously devours its favorite food of Chople Berries while scampering among cover. If it thinks it has been seen, it will freeze and change color to match its surroundings, but the zigzag pattern remains in its new hues.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME senses disasters in pairs, and its indecisive nature causes it to run in a zigzag pattern as it furiously tries to figure out which one to attempt to stop. Unfortunately, this debate typically causes it to fail to prevent either.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME float in a zigzag pattern regardless of where they are. They can float through trees and bushes to take whatever items are hidden.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Instead of leaves, the tree on POKENAME's back grows a thick fur. This fur grows denser  during winter and falls from the tree the moment the weather begins to warm.
author: .izik

entry: It becomes so engrossed in foraging that it sometimes forgets to keep its tail ignited. To prevent this, POKENAME often forage in groups and warn one another when a flame begins to fade.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: POKENAME hoards small piles of berries, using its claws to cut a zigzag mark on each berry to claim it as its own. It always inspects its food to make sure its mark is still there before it eats.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is very good at finding items. Its wings deliver blows that can knock down tree trunks on one hit, the damage shown in a zig-zag pattern.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Each strand of its bristly fur is magnetic; by reversing its own magnetism, it can launch some of its fur like a barrage of needles. POKENAME has a keen sense of direction and smell, so it has a broad area in which it will forage for food.
author: infinex21

entry: When sweating, POKENAME's fur becomes matted down and coarse. Despite this, even a brief touch can produce a soothing sensation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME takes frequent stops while digging to carefully pick dirt from its fur. It is rare to find one that does not obsess over the cleanliness of its coat.
author: .izik

entry: Its fur is rife with debris from when it eats and from lazing around, where countless things can fall onto it. It is so rarely active that it took 24-hour surveillance to record its active period, which is whenever it needs to eat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a rather fast Pokémon for its weight. It can be found zig-zagging near abandoned railroad tracks, looking for items.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's gears regularly attempt to rotate in opposite directions, usually resulting in it temporarily locking up. This behavior occurs more frequently when multiple POKENAME gather together.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME marks its territory by rubbing the scented oils in its scraggly fur onto trees. Its coat is so tangled that it often gets snagged on branches, leaving it stranded and squeaking angrily for help.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME's fur grows frigid when it nears a person's grave. Ancient cultures burned this fur in funeral rites, believing the cold smoke honored wandering spirits.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is really playful and friendly, but becomes ferocious in battle. It hops around in fields, finding items in the grass and even the ground.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME absentmindedly gathers random objects from the ground as it walks and stores them in its fur. When it sorts through its findings in its den later in the day, it grows intensely joyous upon discovering any valuable items like gems.
author: .izik

entry: The oil that leaks from POKENAME's fur is highly toxic. Even brief contact can cause convulsions and blindness that last for hours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appear like weeds at first glance, but when they think no one is looking, they run around in a zigzag pattern. They enjoy being chased by other Pokémon and may beckon Trainers to chase after them too.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's fur is frequently matted and drenched in leachate. This causes it to constantly smell of spiced meat and rotting onions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME approach boats and bite on the siding in an attempt to play with the people on board. These curious creatures are prone to creating holes in these vessels due to their strong jaws, while also being unaware of their own strength.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When content, POKENAME's head fur releases clouds of golden powder. The substance unintentionally paralyzes nearby creatures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME zigzags around forests collecting sticks in a bundle on its back. Occasionally, its fiery powers cause the bundle to ignite, sending it into a flailing panic.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon lazily floats on the pond it calls home, looking for shiny objects Trainers may have dropped in the water. POKENAME collects these objects and moves them to its den. No two hoards are exactly alike between individuals.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME has a remarkable aim when squirting water from its mouth or its Remoraid-like water pistol, even while dancing. Scientists still struggle to determine where this weapon originates or how POKENAME replaces one if it is lost.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives most of its life underground, only surfacing to scavenge for seeds or berries to eat. It works together with root vegetable farmers: loosening the soil around the roots for better growth and the farmers feed it leftover produce.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME swims in a zigzag motion across the seafloor at high speeds. Some say that seeing two POKENAME moving in alternating zigzags simultaneously will cause one to fall in love with the next person they see.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an omnivore that wanders around restlessly to find anything it can eat by using its great sense of smell. It will chase anyone that carries food with them.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Although it is very small, the power of its jaws should never be underestimated; its small teeth are so sharp that they can pierce stone. Although it is very shy, it tends to become more docile when appeased with food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Although it is very small, the power of its jaws should never be underestimated; its small teeth are so sharp that they can pierce stone. Although it is very shy, it tends to become more docile when appeased with food.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it scents Trainers nearby, POKENAME abandons its usual curious wandering to investigate this discovery. Refusing to be distracted, POKENAME pursues its targets relentlessly until they give up and let it sniff them.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: It often fights with other members of its pack to determine who should lead it during hunts. POKENAME tries to confuse its prey by running in zigzags through the bushes, then corners it and finishes it off with its powerful bites.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This variety of POKENAME is most commonly confused with Zigzagoon from the Galar region. While it shares the same fur patterns, its demeanor is extremely friendly toward others.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can extend its body to an incredible length. Its hind legs stay in place as its front legs dash in zigzag patterns. POKENAME can then snap back to its normal length in an instant.
author: musicsheep.

entry: It has simultaneous urges to run in a straight line as well as in a zigzagging pattern. As a result, its running gait is very wiggly and unpredictable, though most regard it as highly entertaining as well.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in woodland areas. Its developed nose allows it to sniff out the tastiest berries.
author: mepp.

entry: Some Trainers have found that checking on POKENAME after a few days allows them to collect items stuck to their bodies. This is because their spines are covered with microscopic barbs that cling to whatever touches them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME communicates with others via vibrating the fine layer of fur over its cocooned body. The vibrations zigzag in different ways depending on the message it intends to send to its kin.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies in zigzag patterns over Cascoon clusters at night. Should it spot a predator, it unleashes a cream-colored powder from its furry wings that causes nausea.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME looks like a real acorn and enjoys scaring other Pokémon in its habitat. Its hard acorn shell protects it from angry Pokémon it startles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME patrol their territories in zigzag patterns, darting between trees to scour for fresh fruits and to search for any intruders. If a POKENAME spots danger, it will cry out to the rest of its flock and then engage the threat in battle.
author: infinex21

entry: The migration patterns of POKENAME's flock constantly zigzag between the clouds. They move at incredible speeds except during storms, when they slow down considerably.
author: .izik

entry: Due to the shape of their wings, POKENAME fly in zig-zag patterns. Curious creatures, they will approach people in hopes of getting something from them, be it food or something they can use for their nest.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME have a dark patch of fur surrounding their eyes, helping to reduce glare from the sun and improving their eyesight. They soar high above beaches, watching for inattentive trainers to steal food from.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME make their homes in and around coastal cities, constantly watching for any dropped items. If they see something that catches their interest, they fly down and scoop it up into their large beak, sometimes carrying dozens of objects at once.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In lieu of sweat, POKENAME secrete aromatic oil that repels grime and water, thus allowing these Pokémon to skim atop water as well. They prefer to eat the freshest foods they can find, so they are often darting about when awake.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is meek and hardly makes any noise. Rather than fight, it quickly scampers to hide in quiet places where few others can find it.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's thick fur can absorb the impact of physical attacks if given enough grooming and preparation beforehand. Unfortunately, this protection is minimal if it is caught unaware.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will follow any scent that its keen nose picks up. It is sometimes seen turning in circles, constantly distracted by new scents.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are highly curious, eagerly chasing after any scent that catches their interest. As a result of this frantic movement, they spend up to 18 hours of the day resting and recovering.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are highly curious, eagerly chasing after any scent that catches their interest. As a result of this frantic movement, they spend up to 18 hours of the day resting and recovering.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME moves with short hops that always follow a zigzagging pattern. Whenever it leaps or lands, small sparks can be seen emitting from its paws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is an extremely lively creature that can never stay still in one place for too long. By rubbing its spiky fur, it builds static and fires devastating Electric attacks that overwhelm its foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: During thunderstorms, POKENAME releases oil from its fur that mats it down. This allows it to store the absorbed electricity within its body for later use.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's electricity can only shoot out in zig-zag patterns. Using its impressive nose, it can sniff out positively charged energy in objects and Pokémon.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME zigzag through tall grass to speed up the digestive process, as the constant motion activates certain enzymes that accelerate the breakdown of anything they consume. If they rest for too long, they develop a stomachache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal hunters, using the darkness to seem nearly invisible save for their eyes and mouth. When the moment is right, they pounce onto their prey with their mouth wide open, swallowing the target whole.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal hunters, using the darkness to seem nearly invisible save for their eyes and mouth. When the moment is right, they pounce onto their prey with their mouth wide open, swallowing the target whole.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's fur can withstand high amounts of heat with ease. This allows it to sleep near lava pools without fear of burns.
author: .izik

entry: When foraging for food, POKENAME trails often end up looking like giant spirals, only deviating if something grabs their interest. The patches of lighter fur on their face vary in placement between individuals.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME seem like they are capricious in how they delineate their territory. However, this is due to their tendency to run in zigzag patterns. When they spot a rival, they break into a dead sprint, zigzagging confusingly towards their opponent.
author: vic1312

entry: The scales covering POKENAME's body resemble fur in appearance. During winter, they grow twice as thick to retain heat.
author: .izik

entry: Beneath POKENAME's fur is a slimy, slippery coating. Between this and its constant wriggling and zigzagging movement, it is incredibly hard to keep a solid grip on it and restrain it.
author: sk372

entry: The Chesto Berry-like fruit on POKENAME's neck is packed entirely with soft fur. Though it is highly nutritious, many are disappointed when they bite into it expecting the real fruit.
author: .izik

entry: When the wind picks up, POKENAME sheds many tufts of fur from its tail that scatter everywhere. Since many people are allergic to them, they quickly try to find it shelter.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It trains by lifting other Pokémon from the undergrowth, making its muscles as hard as marble. When POKENAME battles, it zigzags to make its opponents lower their guard, then delivers powerful martial-arts strikes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It uses its arms to hop around in a zigzagging pattern, patrolling around its mountaintop homes. Because of this, its arms are incredibly powerful, able to shatter stone in its grip with ease.
author: sk372

entry: Competing POKENAME will ram each other head-on. Studies show that repeated ramming at such high speeds and force leave many POKENAME with cranial fractures and concussions.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Small burning embers trail behind POKENAME as it dashes about. If it picks up enough speed, its whole body will ignite completely, giving it a powerful flaming Tackle attack.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever POKENAME firmly raps on its tail like a drum, its body fills with mysterious energy. Their tail can extend surprising distances in a straight line and be used as a faraway punch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The coarse fur on POKENAME's tail releases a strong corn-like scent that causes nausea as it flees from combat. Tufts that fall from its body can reek for weeks.
author: .izik

entry: By running in straight lines, POKENAME can accelerate to speeds that could compete with Doduo; they struggle to turn and quickly lose speed if they do turn. If they trip or crash, they will spit fire at the nearest thing out of frustration.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME love running across wide-open fields where nothing obstructs their path. The longer they sprint in a straight line, the faster they accelerate. They often race one another to train and test their speed.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can spot its prey from miles away, and runs up to it in a straight line before attacking. It usually collects items on the forest floor and kicks anybody who interrupts it.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME's camouflage abilities only work while it's running in a straight line; the minute it stops moving, it stops blending in to its surroundings and shifts back to its normal natural coloration.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a constant compulsive desire to gather up every edible item it can find. It very rarely actually acts on this desire, however, as it is usually too lazy to move.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur bristles when it senses a forming tornado. It rushes younger Pokémon into nearby dens, acting swiftly to shield them from danger.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME phase through nests and hives to steal food within them. When they are threatened, they run away in a zigzag pattern until they are far away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Myths claim garments woven from POKENAME's spring-shed fur ensure lifelong health for newborns. The fur stays warm for long periods, even during winter months.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found collecting berries for itself. When confronted, it attacks with its razor-sharp claws and then runs off in a straight line.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Wide grasslands are the preferred habitat of POKENAME. As they run across the open terrain, they gradually accelerate, generating and storing electrical energy within their muscles.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: This Pokémon can run up to 60 miles an hour, sweeping everything in its path. While stationery, its steel body can stop a runaway train.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME drifts through the dusk sky in search of berry bushes. It rests through daylight hours, hidden among shadows and tall grass.
author: .izik

entry: The diminutive size of POKENAME makes it difficult for predators to catch them. They love to play chase with their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dances more fervently during combat when five or more people are watching. If it dances too fast, it grows stressed, causing clumps of fur to fall from its body.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, POKENAME releases blue pollen from its dense fur. The pollen induces severe nausea, discouraging predators from pursuing it.
author: .izik

entry: Though the twig POKENAME carries looks mundane, it grants control over the fur shed from its body. It weaves this fur into long ropes to ensnare enemies before striking with Ember.
author: .izik

entry: On full-moon nights, POKENAME fiercely howls into the sky, only stopping when dawn breaks. This behavior awakens enhanced psychic capabilities and heightened speed.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME utilize magic that organizes materials near them into straight lines. Trainers know they are nearby when they see trees that are unnaturally straight or rocks that look like hewn pavers.
author: vic1312

entry: During winter, POKENAME's fur grows very fluffy, giving it trouble swimming long distances. It prefers to hibernate during these months, building nests in the silt at the ocean floor.
author: .izik

entry: It roams with its pack, intimidating anyone who trespasses on its territory by baring its fangs. When separated from the others in its group, it immediately tries to escape, using its long tail to kick up as much dust as possible to aid its escape.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME often leaves claw marks in tree bark to communicate with other members of its species. It can reach remarkable speeds when running, and its long tail helps it to not lose its balance during sudden changes of direction.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's sharp claws help it keep traction as it dashes at high speeds. It moves in both straight lines and zigzags to outsmart chasing predators.
author: chibitales

entry: Despite its appearance, POKENAME shares few qualities with Galarian Linoone. The fur on its black and white portions grows unevenly and sheds constantly, causing trouble for those with allergies to it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's extra legs and long body often hinder its movement, causing it to stumble over itself. To compensate, it stands upright and scans for danger with its many eyes.
author: qinshanu

entry: A healthy POKENAME's feet, while stubby, are remarkably powerful for their size. They can launch the whole body forward, allowing it to roll in a straight line unless impeded by large obstacles or rough terrain.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can fly very fast, even against strong winds, if they fly in straight lines. Though they struggle to turn, they can use their wings to drag themselves to either side. Some races exist that specifically utilize these Pokémon as the racers.
author: infinex21

entry: Artists once prized quills made from POKENAME's feathers for their ability to draw straighter lines. Only the sturdiest feathers were used, and since they never regrew, this left many POKENAME permanently landlocked after removal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a very high top speed in the air, though its maneuverability with turns is mediocre at best. It makes incredibly quick dives into the water to snatch up fish to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME secretes a slick oil from its fur that lets it skim across pond surfaces. It often pauses to snack on reeds along the water's edge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can always be seen participating in activities that involve a direct line. They have developed a dislike for boxing, unable to pivot efficiently anymore.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Legends say that POKENAME have been observed meditating for over 100 years. Their telepathic abilities grant them mastery over water, earth, fire, and air.
author: gnom3

entry: During arid seasons, POKENAME's long fur requires near constant attention to prevent static buildup. If not taken care of, it may accidentally short-circuit nearby electronics.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's powerful leg muscles allow it to run at high speeds in a straight line.  In battle, it covers itself in the electricity stored in its fur and charges at opponents, delivering a devastating Wild Charge.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME builds up intense static in its fur while dashing through open fields. When cornered, it can unleash enough electricity to paralyze an Aggron.
author: .izik

entry: During battle, the electricity in POKENAME's body spreads throughout its fur. This makes the fur appear far more voluminous than it actually is.
author: .izik

entry: The fur on POKENAME's tail retains heat with ease. Many clothiers use it to craft winter coats sold at high prices.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur becomes extremely spiky when it spots a Seviper. If touched while one is nearby, it hisses aggressively and lashes out at anyone close by.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's extremely long and flexible body allows it to squeeze and hide within tight spaces. It springs from these spots, swinging its bladed tail with deadly speed and ferocity, once unaware prey draw close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME grows warm, fur-covered yellow fruit along its neck. The fruit is exceptionally sweet, and many Pokémon risk approaching it just for a taste.
author: .izik

entry: As soon as it sees something move, POKENAME immediately gives chase, darting forward to grab it with its claws. It is extremely loyal to its Trainer, and if anything dares to threaten them, it snorts flames from its nostrils.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can often be found working at breakfast diners, using their arms to serve multiple customers at once. It is advised not to get in the way of POKENAME, since they can't turn to get out of a collision.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME spit a sticky silk from their mouths when threatened, blinding predators. If grabbed, they will stab the threat with their spikes, injecting them with a painful toxin.
author: santon5512

entry: With their newfound power, POKENAME burrow into the ground to avoid Bird-Pokémon. If faced with an opponent, they will coil around them; their spikes releasing venom to weaken their foe.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME live deep underground to avoid predators, only digging out to eat entire trees. Contrary to their large size, they are known to burrow away when faced with foes.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME's silk constantly changes as it grows, from being fiery hot and hard to soft with a leaf-like odor at a whim. It is often impossible to predict what it is going to evolve into due to how vast and varying its possible evolutions can be.
author: soup1900

entry: It uses String Shot to coat its nest, ensuring maximum comfort for itself and its young. POKENAME soars through the sky as discreetly as possible, avoiding detection by other Pokémon while foraging for Berries.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is found near rivers and ponds with pristine water. When a predator approaches POKENAME, it quickly dives underwater to hide.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's hooked claws allow them to easily climb trees to feed on leaves. If backed into a corner, they will show the spikes on their tails to predators, which secrete a toxic poison.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME forms antlers made of threads it spews out to appear more imposing and impress mates. When in danger, it can make the antlers explode outward and coat its potential attacker with sticky, immobilizing silk.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends its time in woodland treetops. It has been known to come to the aid of Wurmple who are being targeted by hungry bird Pokémon.
author: mepp.

entry: It spits out a strong and sticky thread to pull down fruits it cannot reach. When it has eaten enough food, it will wrap itself in a cocoon of its threads; these threads are incredibly flame-resistant and have even been found after wildfires.
author: infinex21

entry: By planting its feet, it can use the spikes on its rear to lift boulders at least twice its size. It creates a nest within mud and will even store fruits and nuts within the mud as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME clings onto the tallest parts of trees lush with vegetation to hide from predators among the thick leaves. If startled, it wildly spews sticky strings all about it in a panic before teleporting away.
author: sk372

entry: Ancient texts state that POKENAME are heralds of great change. It gifts a large branch to those it favors.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is skittish and fearful of anything that approaches it. It spits a burst of webbing that instantly cocoons around its target, giving POKENAME a chance to disappear to somewhere safer.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates ribbons made of silk from its body. It can use these to quickly wrap up attackers and immobilize them, the silk's special properties sapping their violent impulses while wrapped up.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME whips threats with threads of electricity. POKENAME are commonly found in power plants, feeding off of the electricity the machinery produces.
author: adsfw11

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time underground, feasting on plant roots. It eats as much as it can to gather energy to evolve.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hangs upside-down from tall tree branches, dangling a sticky string of webbing from its mouth to catch bugs in. It can remain in this hunting position for 18 hours straight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in caves, feeding primarily on moss and minerals. Its exoskeleton is as hard as diamonds.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME spend much of their lives searching forests for a safe place to evolve. To avoid predators, they conceal themselves among shrubs. When they find a suitable tree, the buds on their heads unfurl and spin a silken cocoon around them.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME spins silk laced with seizure-inducing spores across its nest. The effect doesn't harm its kin, allowing them to pass through safely.
author: .izik

entry: The silk POKENAME spits is heated thanks to warmth-producing organs inside it. It wraps up food with the silk, then waits for its meal to cook before consuming it and the threads wrapped around it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself partially under leaf piles to lie in wait for something to tread on it. Once stepped on, it releases a burst of sticky webbing that covers and constricts smaller creatures it can then devour.
author: sk372

entry: The poison in POKENAME's spines can ward off bird Pokémon, but it still scuttles about in worry. It relies on its feelers to have a sense of its surroundings.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: The poison in POKENAME's spines can ward off bird Pokémon, but it still scuttles about in worry. It relies on its feelers to have a sense of its surroundings.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME burrow into the ground for half their life. Their poisonous spikes protect them from any predators trying to get an easy meal.
author: adsfw11

entry: Notably a rather vicious Bug-type Pokémon, POKENAME will typically target smaller prey. Its horn and tail spikes deliver a strong venom that quickly brings down most of the prey it targets.
author: infinex21

entry: Because POKENAME's tail looks like a Wurmple stuck in a tree, it is often targeted by bird Pokémon. In anger, it will spit a sticky silk, wrap up the threat, then fly high into the sky and toss it back down.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME is cautious: if it suspects those nearby may attack, its spines fill with a bitter poison. If scooped up in Pelipper's maw, it will thrash around to inject the predator.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are commonly found in decrepit ruins, hiding away to focus on eating and growing. When threatened, they curl up into a tight ball to block incoming attacks.
author: mepp.

entry: The sticky, aerated silk atop POKENAME's head allows it to drift down rivers and streams. It catches leaves and berries atop its head, which it saves for whenever it is hungry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It builds its nest between rocky outcrops underwater, between which it will string together its waterproof threads. It favors nesting near seaweed patches, as it seems to love eating seaweed; it can also susbsit on algae, however.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are commonly given to aspiring Trainers as a first partner because of their docile nature and abundance near human habitations. They're not very strong, so they are an excellent choice for children.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are popular Pokémon with new trainers, being easy to train and quick to pack bond with their trainer. When they get excited, they spray silk from their mouth, a habit that can result in them accidentally sticking themselves to their trainer.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's spikes hold a paralyzing toxin it uses to deter predators. It is theorized this Pokémon intentionally eats poisonous plants to make it. As soon as the poison takes hold, POKENAME will dash away to a safer location.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME only focuses on finding and consuming food. The poison that leaks from its spikes causes immense pain, so most predators stay away from it.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME use their string to weave together a shelter for themselves out of leaves. If they can't find any leaves, they will shelter under any object that fits over their head, leading many trainers to have fun getting them to wear tiny hats.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As it gathers energy to evolve, the bright coloration of its body deters most predators. Its vibrant silk can be collected and woven into beautiful fabric.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME fly between berry trees, scarfing down as much as they can to sate their appetites and prepare to evolve. If disturbed, they attack with Bug Bite attacks until the threat goes away and allows them to continue feasting.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME wrap themselves with silk laced with a mild irritant as they prepare for evolution. They retaliate against foes using the venomous spike on their head.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME fly from tree to tree to sate their voracious appetites for both leaves and fruits. When agitated, they can release a highly toxic powder from their wings.
author: infinex21

entry: The large cap on its head stores energy from the sun. It uses some of this energy alongside the plants it eats to secrete a sticky poison from the horn on its head. This poison irritates the stomach of bird Pokémon that try to eat it.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is often found watching over Wurmple in the wild. It perches on trees to take potential predators by surprise, wrapping them up with silk and carrying them away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies above tall grass to hunt for berries. It shoots out a net of silk to gather berries before flying away with its bounty.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are found near the coast, gliding on gentle sea breezes. The spiked tips at the end of its wings contain a mild poison, and are used when POKENAME feels threatened.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME skate across the water using their thin legs, often being snatched up by Starly. They spit sticky silk into the water at small fish, ensnaring them so they can be dragged ashore.
author: santon5512

entry: Flitting between treetops, POKENAME dines on the tastiest and most tender leaves. It frightens off hungry bird Pokémon with the menacing eyespots on its antennae.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME has many natural predators, so it uses its long tail as a distraction. If an attacker grabs hold, the tail detaches, allowing POKENAME to escape safely.
author: skittytales

entry: The more fruit POKENAME consumes, the thicker the silk it produces becomes. It can channel electrical surges through these strings to stun predators.
author: .izik

entry: Swarming POKENAME are known for their destructive appetites, rendering a tree completely barren in a few hours. Researchers track POKENAME's populations and ranges to ensure they don't threaten farmland.
author: mepp.

entry: The orbs around POKENAME's head are filled with silk thread it generates. At will, it can release these around it, the thread's super-heated temperature causing intense burns on contact with skin.
author: sk372

entry: The liquid that rains down from POKENAME's rain clouds has similar properties to an insect's silk threads, sticking to surfaces.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME primarily move around by rolling, though they have been seen spitting out sticky threads onto branches to swing about. They roll themselves up in their own threads to form a cocoon in preparation for their evolution.
author: infinex21

entry: Although POKENAME is not terribly mobile, it is not to be underestimated. It uses strong silk connecting its arms to its legs to manipulate its feet and defend itself with powerful kicks while still remaining seated in place.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME absorbs water through its microscopic pores and emits any toxins it has consumed along with a gas through a different set of pores. POKENAME is most often found in natural areas with acidic soil.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Wreathed in soft silk, POKENAME float in gentle forest streams. They are generally sedentary, storing as much energy as they can, but can rapidly swim away from predators using their small fins.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's cocoon allows it to cling to tree branches without falling off, and is so sticky that predators avoid eating POKENAME. Pollen and dust cling to its body until the moment it evolves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wool has the same properties as fine silk. It's often fused as a source of inexpensive silk for fabric.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are highly sought after for their magnificent antlers and smooth, silk cocoons. They were almost hunted to extinction until conservation programs were put in place to boost their numbers.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME move very little every day, typically only enough to bring themselves to nearby rainwater. Their silk is plush and flame-resistant, making it a popular crafting material.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hides its cocooned body beneath mud, waiting for its evolution to complete. The mud is absorbed by the silk covering its body, hardening it and giving it added protection.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hides itself deep in forests, for fear of predators taking advantage of its cocooned, almost-immobile body. If found, it flakes off parts of its shell and psychically tosses it at an attacker's eyes before teleporting away.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon likes to stand in wide-open meadows and gaze at the flying bug Pokémon that frequent them, as well as to seek out the white flowers it likes. Its body resembles Kirlia's humanoid form, woven from Silcoon's silk.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME fashions a dress and veil from its own silk to wear and decorate with its favorite flowers. Boutiques around the world seek it out to help in making the most luxurious of dresses.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wait in the trees, secreting an alluring aroma from the large mouths on their heads to attract smaller Pokémon. Once they've caught their prey, they tie their mouths shut using their silk, sealing them inside while they digest.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is rumoured to only appear to the most tenacious of tailors, as the legendary silk it produces is of exceptional quality. A simple scarf made of its silk can be sold for millions.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME tangles its feelers in pine tree branches to suspend itself high above the ground. This keeps its body safe while it rests and waits for evolution.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lines its tunnel with translucent silk that trips and ensnares predators like Ekans upon entry. Once detected, it covers the intruder in silk before making its escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to tree branches above the forest floor, its sticky cocoon shielding it from harm. It spends most of its time sleeping, as any movement quickly exhausts its energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clad themselves in steel-like silk fibers, granting themselves greater protection from attackers. They always apply new layers of fibers each day as they shed their prior fibers. POKENAME fibers are desired in many crafts.
author: infinex21

entry: The silk POKENAME produces from its body is similar in consistency to aluminum. During the winter months, it can become extremely brittle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a silk armour that gradually turns into steel. It awaits evolution and drinks dew that collects on its shell.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: It does not possess teeth and only drinks water in the wild. If a Trainer wants to give it a Berry to hold, they must make sure POKENAME smashes the berry to bits before consuming it, lest they choke.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME encase themselves in layers of silk to protect the precious garnet gemstones that make up their bodies. They use their string to weave intricate supports and traps along tree branches, hiding and waiting to evolve.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's snoring sounds like a singing child. Should it be woken from slumber, it sprays silk on the offender before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's entire body is coated in tightly-packed silk thread to protect itself while it evolves. Touching any of its spines results in a burst of pent-up silk that will wrap around and immobilize the one who touched it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers silk from many different bug-type Pokémon, winding the threads around its staff. It weaves bandages that it wears to protect its delicate skin. When it finds an injured Pokémon, it will share its silken wraps.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME spits thread from its mouth at anything that draws near while it hangs from trees. Some gather the thread to create strings for charms that are said to make one more attractive.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a rivalry with Cascoon fusions. It gnaws sticks constantly, perhaps to strengthen its bite. It collects its shed fur to use as a bed among other friendly Poochyena fusions.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's silk is extremely sticky, allowing dirt and debris to stick to it as they forage in dense underbrush. This silk is often treated and used in high-end fashion, yet it will regain its sticky quality if not treated regularly.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME continues to generate silk constantly even after being completely cocooned. It sprays copious amounts of string at anything that passes by so it can vent the excess material.
author: sk372

entry: After fusion, POKENAME gains spines, wings and claws. It has a generally calm nature, but flies into a violent rage if it sees Bug types being bullied in its presence.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produces a silk with an uncommon strength. They work together to weave robust nests that protect themselves while they prepare to evolve. These nests will persist long after they have moved on, becoming host to other vulnerable Pokémon.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME produces two different kinds of silk to construct its shell. Once enough layers are applied, not even a Scyther's blade can break through it.
author: .izik

entry: The silver dust POKENAME scatters from its wings solidifies after a few minutes. This hardened sheet of dust grows as tough as steel the longer it is left undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being in its cocoon, POKENAME is still very aware of its surroundings. It can fly away for short distances in case of emergency.
author: lucioleuh

entry: POKENAME gather in small swarms on the sides of ponds, using their silk to reinforce one another's shells. They tend to evolve in tandem with each other during the springtime.
author: .izik

entry: As it wraps itself in silk to prepare for evolution, POKENAME takes great care to leave the eyespots on its antennae visible. Their intimidating glare is POKENAME's only way to ward off predators.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME wraps its fists in thick silk to fight more efficiently. The silk's durability makes its punches considerably stronger.
author: .izik

entry: The silk POKENAME strings around its body are highly conductive. Touching it releases a powerful jolt capable of sending a Weepinbell flying.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME twirls strands of its silk through the air while cheering on other Bug-type Pokémon in combat. This silk is extremely shiny and can distract the foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers training through physical activity that allows it to rest easily afterwards, such as chin-ups through the use of the branches in the tree it calls home. POKENAME highly enjoys fruit juice due to the nutrients and ease of swallowing.
author: bobosmith01

entry: After finding a safe crag to hide in, POKENAME remains as still as possible to more quickly evolve from its cocoon stage. If it must flee an opponent, it uses its arms to carefully steer while traveling downhill.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The amount of sunlight POKENAME gets daily directly affects the spots on its bulb. If the spots are vibrant, it is a sign that POKENAME gets a healthy amount of sunlight.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its weapon appears to be a bone with an orb-like concentration of pollen at the tip. It attacks with various different kinds of pollen, scattering them on the battlefield to give it a better opportunity against its opponent.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: The grand wings of a POKENAME have long since been considered a great prize to many collectors. The eldest of their kind have the largest and most vibrant wings, though the scales they shed are also even more poisonous.
author: infinex21

entry: Upon emerging from its cocoon, POKENAME starts feasting on any nearby vegetation it can find. Once it has decimated the local plant life it flies into a rage, destroying anything that remains.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME are specialized hunters that crack open Shellder before siphoning their prey with their thin, tubular mouth. When Shellder populations are low, they resort to eating seaweed for nourishment.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its flames can come in a wide array of dazzling colors, making them popular for Pokémon Contests. It adores sweets, but it will also hunt for small prey in the wild.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Any flower POKENAME pollinates glows with the luminosity of a dozen stars. The shining flowers are commonly mistaken for fireflies, fallen stars, or even ghosts.
author: creaturecore

entry: Due to the cloudy pattern on its abdomen and its colorful wings, many mistake POKENAME for a rainbow. This helps it avoid being attacked by bird Pokémon that wish to eat it. However, if that fails, POKENAME begins throwing balloons of pollen at them.
author: queercatlover

entry: Keeping the flower on POKENAME's back gorgeous requires extensive care. If it does not receive the proper amount of water and nutrients, it will look dull.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME wraps around small prey to crush them before siphoning their insides with its proboscis. Its alluring colors draw in many curious furry Pokémon, giving it many opportunities to choose its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME feeds by constricting its prey in its crushing coils, then drinking their innards with its proboscis. Its hood is most often used in warning or mating displays, but can be used to glide through its jungle habitat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Each pigment that makes up POKENAME's elaborate hood pattern contains a different potent toxin. When hunting, POKENAME will choose which of these venoms it will fill its fangs with depending on what it thinks will work best against its prey.
author: deadshields

entry: While POKENAME's vibrant wings stand out in the sky, they help these Pokémon blend into the fields of flowers in which they rest. During the day, they soar over these flowers, spreading the pollen that sticks to their feathers.
author: santon5512

entry: Few wild POKENAME have been witnessed, and those that have were always seen siphoning nutrients from flowers and fruits that were freshly ripe. Because this has been the most common note, some believe they have an oddly acute sense of time.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is known to wave its flashy tail to disorient and intimidate potential predators. It sips on nectar from various flowers that grow on riverbanks.
author: mepp.

entry: The leaves growing from POKENAME's arms are coated in a thin layer of powder. Contact with this powder can cause itching that lasts for weeks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are easily startled and jab at the cause of their disruption with their long, narrow mouths. The scales scattered by their wings as they flap absorb heat well without becoming weaker or harder; they are popular materials for many crafts.
author: infinex21

entry: Should POKENAME repeatedly miss with its kicks, it releases a powder from its legs. This can cause paralysis, giving it the upper hand.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pollinates flowers close to its pond home. When it needs a rest from its work, it sleeps face-first in the water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flutters through bayous, eating ivy growing on passing trees. Once it finds a suitable spot to rest, it falls asleep almost immediately.
author: .izik

entry: The antennae of POKENAME allow them to sense weather changes and emotional changes so they know when it is safe to wander floral fields. Although difficult to observe, their dances are said to be beautiful thanks to their many vibrant scales.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME frolic and dance within open, vibrant plains on the sunny morn of a new day without fail. It was only recently discovered that their psychic powers allow them to know exactly when a morning, and even a day, is going to be sunny.
author: infinex21

entry: When spring begins, POKENAME can be seen running around and twirling through flower fields and meadows. While this is mainly play, it also helps them collect pollen under dresses for when they become tired and hungry at night.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can be seen twirling among the flowers in its vast forest in a stupor of peaceful dance. If the dance is interrupted, however, POKENAME will grow enraged, releasing an army of colorful butterflies at whatever dared heckle it.
author: tamszen.ore

entry: The colored patterns on its frills and small wings change depending on the last few flowers it has drunk the nectar of. It is loved by certain collectors despite how violently it lashes out at most others for simply getting too close.
author: infinex21

entry: The flower on POKENAME's back is highly valued, selling for more than two million Pokédollars. Unfortunately, poaching has driven this Pokémon near extinction in the wild.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The patterns and spikes upon its wings serve to intimidate prey and even some would-be predators. Although it has a fierce temperament, it is typically docile so long as it is shown respect and treated well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME possesses several extendable proboscises that it uses to suck the sap from every plant growing around it. If disturbed while feeding, this creature becomes extremely violent.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Their myriad, vibrant colors are their most prominent, and sometimes revered, features. Angered POKENAME will lash out with their long feelers; each feeler can strike with enough force to split thick wood.
author: infinex21

entry: The eye upon a POKENAME's belly is the conduit through which it channels its psychic powers at varying levels based on how open it is. Only when angered, particularly as it seeks pollen to gather, will this eye fully open.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wander through meadows in search of recently bloomed flowers, using their long proboscis to feed on the nectar. Their antennae twitch when they sense danger, glowing and projecting an illusion of an empty field when they want to hide.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While dancing, POKENAME spreads puffs of white and silver powder into the air. Contact with this powder can cause painful rashes to form on the body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are pretty, yet deceiving. They lure adults away from woodland paths with their dazzling colours, then drain their energy with their long proboscis.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Many small insects like to gather inside of POKENAME's arms since they are very spacious and comfortable to them. POKENAME can convert the pollen it takes from the insects that live in its arms into golden light energy.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses its twig to spread pollen around flower-filled fields. When attacking, its twig instead spews hot embers. The pollen POKENAME uses smells like nectar and campfire smoke.
author: thans101

entry: POKENAME scatters dust from its wand that it uses to induce hallucinations in its foes, amplified by the colorful spots in its fur coat. It incapacitates its foes by showing them terrifying future possibilities, then it attacks viciously.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME swarms bound through the air together, following the largest packmate wherever they lead. They leave a trail of wing scales glittering in their wake, drawing many admirers to watch the passage of the swarm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are renowned for their colorfully-patterned wings, even though their bodies are too heavy for them to fly. They have proven to be able to use their wings to glide short distances, which they do to move between trees and avoid predators.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have partially formed wings that can generate gentle breezes and spread dust around. While they can use these breezes to move around, they need lots of energy to do so.
author: entomoxie

entry: To protect their patch of flowers, POKENAME aggressively target other insect Pokémon with their needle-like proboscis and Gust attacks. Pokémon that show no interest in the flowers POKENAME pollinates are often left alone, but carefully watched.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have partially formed wings that can generate gentle breezes and spread toxic dust around. They rarely use their wings to fly but are capable of doing so in a pinch.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME drinks different nectar from different flowers depending on the weather. It does not seem to sleep for long periods, preferring to remain active throughout most hours of the day.
author: .izik

entry: Although most find it to appear docile, it is highly territorial and quick to be aggressive. Despite this, many still seek it out to witness the beauty of its fully spread wings, which it will often spread out just before it attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are found living in flowering trees near the beach, where they can collect pollen from the tropical flowers. Tourists enjoy taking pictures of these beautiful Pokémon, but they will become aggressive and attack anyone who comes too close.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME feeds off nectar from flowers near ponds and microorganisms in said ponds. It attacks other Pokémon with its long, thin mouth.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME descend on flowery meadows in swarms, posturing aggressively with their eyespots to drive off rival bug Pokémon and monopolize the flowers' nectar. Each swarm is led by the POKENAME with the largest and brightest eyespots among them.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME's bright eyes, bushy tail, and colorful wings make it a popular choice for Trainers looking to enter Pokémon Contests. It quickly turns aggressive if it does not get its way, however.
author: skittytales
