entry: POKENAME's bright eyes, bushy tail, and colorful wings make it a popular choice for Trainers looking to enter Pokémon Contests. It quickly turns aggressive if it does not get its way, however.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's bright eyes, bushy tail, and colorful wings make it a popular choice for Trainers looking to enter Pokémon Contests. It quickly turns aggressive if it does not get its way, however.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME sucks nectar from plants with its long nose. Its elastic body can expand to twice its size before it begins to have trouble flying.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are a common sight in meadows where flowers are plentiful, fluttering about in small groups. As they drink nectar from flowers, their body leaves slime on the petals that is collected and processed into hydrating skin lotions.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses its long nose to absorb nectar from plants growing along stream banks. During winter, it can go months without eating.
author: .izik

entry: The long extension on POKENAME's mouth is used to suck flowers dry of nectar and nutrients. The heat of the thin organ sets the husk of a flower alight, before it is consumed by POKENAME as a post-meal snack.
author: sk372

entry: Its colorfully patterned tail scatters pheromones. POKENAME communicate with one another by exchanging "conversations" through different pheromones and tail movements.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: Because POKENAME live deep in shady forests with little daylight, they use bioluminescence to display their warning coloration. Those who press the attack despite the brilliant spectacle will receive a ferocious pummeling.
author: .realthree

entry: Its mane is made of pollen instead of flames. As they gallop, they collect pollen and nectar from the flowers they pass. Scientists are utilizing ways to use POKENAME to pollinate agricultural fields and ecosystems.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: When in danger, POKENAME explodes and releases copious amounts of silk across its surroundings to immobilize predators. This destroys most of its cocoon, so it must find safety immediately so it can regenerate.
author: sk372

entry: The two types of silk POKENAME produces can be combined into a highly hydrophobic thread. Beach towns frequently use this silk to craft designer swimsuits.
author: .izik

entry: The silky cocoon around POKENAME's body is sticky and allows it to hang from trees. On the rare occasion this cocoon is damaged, it oozes out a toxic substance to deter predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The silk-like wool POKENAME grows is both soft and strong. It takes a surprising amount of strength to shear a POKENAME.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME attach themselves to mangrove trees, hanging from the branches while they wait to evolve. If they hear a predator approaching, they release their silk strands, dropping into the water and floating away to safety.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hang motionless in the branches of trees during the day, wrapping their long trailing tendrils around themselves to disguise themselves as flower buds. At night, they unfurl, waiting to surprise passing people and taking joy in their fear.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has soft spines across its body, but it will bite anyone who tries to touch them. These spines contain a direct connection to its central nervous system, so any sudden pressure on them causes immense pain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The silk coating around POKENAME's body gives it a bit of extra defense. It feels soft to the touch, but it can still throw formidable punches.
author: hophoppip

entry: The bodies of these Pokémon are clad in a soft silk, which hardens as time passes. They hide themselves among forest debris and sustain themselves on rainwater. Their silk can withstand intense flames, so not even a forest fire will disturb them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wrap silk around their legs to give more impact to their kicks. Cascoon often harbor jealousy at the free movement that POKENAME has.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME strings thread across the area surrounding its pond. This stealthily alerts it to approaching danger, giving it time to escape underwater.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's luxurious dress and veil are woven from silk it produces and decorated with wild roses. If its Trainer is kind and caring, POKENAME may craft a similar dress for them to wear.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's large mouths are constantly hungry and incredibly aggressive, snapping and growling at anything that gets near. To rein them in, POKENAME will restrain them using silk, only releasing them when in danger.
author: santon5512

entry: Though POKENAME seems weaker than Arceus, it harbors great power under its hardened silk shell. Scientific equipment has detected waves of immense energy within its body.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's feelers are made of an incredibly durable silk. It can wrap this silk around its body to strengthen its defenses.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME nests underneath tree roots. It can move noiselessly if it so desires, but it prefers not to move so it can properly prepare for evolution.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME seeks out isolated spots to hide itself and sleep through its evolution process. After it evolves, the left-behind cocoon often gets used as bedding by small Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME conceal themselves within rubble and forest debris to avoid detection by their potential enemies. Their bodies grow harder and heavier with each passing day so long as they consume plenty of minerals per day.
author: infinex21

entry: The metallic silk covering POKENAME's body comes off in clumps when it is stressed. Because of this, it tries to remain calm even in the midst of combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a hard covering to protect itself before its next evolution. This covering is made out of silk at first, but gradually hardens and turns into steel.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME wrap their bodies in layers of silk packed densely enough to be as durable as steel. They rapidly rotate in unison to build up energy to try and accelerate their evolution.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Due to the flame on its tail, the silk near its tail is often shrunk in and curled up. When POKENAME is nearing evolution, its body temperature will equal its flame's heat.
author: soup1900

entry: The silk strings surrounding POKENAME are exceptionally sticky, causing them to attach to nearby Pokémon. Removing these strings is nearly impossible, and those afflicted must wait for POKENAME to evolve to remove the strings.
author: agentyoshi

entry: POKENAME remains nearly motionless to avoid detection while it pupates into its next evolution stages. If detected, it blasts a mixture of spores from the spout on its crown to incapacitate the foe while it slowly waddles away.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lays in wait, sending off piercing cries as soon as midnight strikes. Anything that investigates will be wrapped up in its silk and consumed.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME creates large nets of silk while drifting through the ocean. These allow it to entrap aquatic Pokémon and leech their life force.
author: .izik

entry: This shy Pokémon keeps its face hidden under a hood of silk. It only reveals its face to a Trainer it wholeheartedly trusts.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to rock formations beneath the ocean using an incredibly strong silk. It does this while waiting to evolve.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps for very long periods of time, perhaps due to its desire to preserve energy for evolution. It will fiercely attack anyone who gets close and will chase them down if they flee.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its mobility is low, but the layer of cocooned silk on its body gives it protection from the elements and others. POKENAME retaliates against any predators with surprising aggression.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME silk can be spun into an exceptionally fine cloth and is used to create high-end garments. POKENAME resent having their silk taken against their will, making the process of acquiring the silk primarily one of building trust with the Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME silk can be spun into an exceptionally fine cloth and is used to create high-end garments. POKENAME resent having their silk taken against their will, making the process of acquiring the silk primarily one of building trust with the Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME coat their bodies in a fine layer of silk, protecting themselves from physical harm. They flutter away into the treetops in a panic if they're confronted with a threat strong enough to pierce their silken armour.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has grown spikes, wings and claws after fusion. It acts with great aggression towards others, those Bug types are exempt from this behavior.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are skilled weavers, able to build sturdy cocoons out of their own high-quality silk. It is dangerous to harvest, however, as the area around them is often covered in a poisonous powder, which is spread from the flapping of their wings.
author: evilgammon

entry: Because it has an impatient nature and can't wait to grow larger and stronger, POKENAME's immobility while cocooned causes it endless frustration. If closely observed, one can see it vibrating faintly with pent-up energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats atop lakes and rivers by spreading its legs on the water's surface, spreading its weight across all its legs. While some Flying-type Pokémon easily pluck it out of the water, many more refuse to get wet for a single snack.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME knows it is almost helpless during the evolution process. As it spins its cocoon, it painstakingly forms spikes and false eyes in hopes of deterring predators.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME releases shocks from its whisker-like spines to show excitement, especially since it cannot move very fast. In the wild, POKENAME can be seen hanging and siphoning electricity from telephone poles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Even though POKENAME are surrounded in silk, they can still express joy over the success of their teammates. Rapidly flashing lights from their ears signal great enthusiasm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs the ambient moisture in the area to nourish and harden its cocoon. During heavy rainfall, its coating solidifies to the point of being nearly impenetrable.
author: sk372

entry: A cocoon of silk constricts POKENAME's body and hinders its movement. It gets around by latching onto Pokémon or people swimming by; trying to pry it off forcefully results in a painful electric shock.
author: sk372

entry: Each of its three heads has a very specific role in detecting food or potential dangers, making this creature remarkably efficient. On its back POKENAME carries soil that it uses to build small shelters whenever it becomes tired during its travels.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The heads of POKENAME operate independently but cooperatively. Each head looks in a different direction to watch for predators.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME lives under inhabited trees. When prey is near, it will rise from the ground and use its leaves to crush it.
author: habibiluigi

entry: This trio of Digbones have decided to take different roles for survival and efficiency: an excavator, a crafter, and a hunter.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: After evolving, they keep developing their roles and honing their skills. Thanks to the efforts of the crafter and its new workbench, now the excavator has a more advanced shovel, and the hunter has better weapons at its disposal.
author: doodledoo

entry: After evolving, they keep developing their roles and honing their skills. Thanks to the efforts of the crafter and its new workbench, now the excavator has a more advanced shovel, and the hunter has better weapons at its disposal.
author: doodledoo

entry: POKENAME's footwork in battle in incredibly quick-paced and maneuverable. It moves and strikes so quickly that its opponents swear they're fighting against three foes at once.
author: sk372

entry: The three heads of POKENAME fight for space and nutrients with the cocoon. One head will become dominant over the other two.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME charge through the ground at high speeds, tunneling through the earth with their rocky bodies. Diglett will often burrow into their bodies when tired, hitching a ride to travel miles with little effort.
author: santon5512

entry: Because its triplet bodies are tied together, POKENAME frequently finds itself conflicted over which direction to move. Each disagreement causes its tangled body to knot tighter, preventing it from digging effectively.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: The faux faces on POKENAME's wings intimidate predators. This is a good thing, because POKENAME is generally oblivious to its surroundings.
author: .realthree

entry: A Pokémon that lives alone in caves, loneliness had driven it to create cloth puppets that it considers family. It lost its sanity long ago.
author: dinner8480

entry: POKENAME are in constant shock due to becoming bald upon evolving. It moves its hips in panic over being found.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME likes to tunnel into people's basements and devour the wiring in their fuse boxes. If a neighborhood is experiencing erratic blackouts, it is likely due to a POKENAME infestation.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's pincers each have a mind of their own, though they still cooperate with the body. It will hide underneath the ground while waiting for prey, and then crush them with its pincers once the prey gets close.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME sway back and forth whilst sniffing the air, using their keen sense of smell and three heads to triangulate the location of predators. If they smell a threat approaching, they rear back and spray three strands of sticky silk at the danger.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite their distinct lack of mouths, POKENAME will still establish themselves as a force to be reckoned with in underground tunnels. POKENAME's three heads are capable of heavy blunt force, which deters attackers.
author: xiapher

entry: Despite the three bodies not being able to fit within its shell, they will never accept a larger shell unless it is from an Omanyte. They will bury the shell in the ground to stop themselves from getting swept away.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME cluster themselves around tree roots, feeding directly on the plant's sap with their three heads in an effort to accelerate themselves to early evolution. If discovered, they turn their tough carapaces outward to try to stay safe from harm.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While POKENAME may move slower than normal, its bigger body can cause more dangerous quakes. When eating plant roots, one of POKENAME's heads eats more than its other two heads, hence looking bigger.
author: mbavenger64

entry: POKENAME will often fall asleep in the middle of digging its tunnels.  As such, it may often be found sticking halfway out of the ground.
author: bostroms

entry: It slithers its heads out of the ground to intimidate prey, creating a fearsome display. Its body grows daily, sometimes reaching lengths longer than a subway car.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dig complex colonies between the roots of trees in forests. They spend the majority of their time underground but will burst out above ground to attack anyone approaching too close to their hive.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's arms have minds of their own and act mostly independently, teaming up with the body for fighting and hunting. Sturdy and aggressive, these limbs don't hesitate to swing themselves into opponents to beat them down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's long and flexible body is well adapted for moving through tunnels. They chase other burrowing Pokémon to their nests, their twin heads checking forks for the right direction to run. Their tail head watches for pursuit from other Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have an incredible sense of time. Each of their three heads works together to keep track of the time, one head letting out a cry every second, the other every minute, and the largest every hour.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can be seen emerging from their burrows shortly after a meteor shower, scouring the area for any signs of fallen meteors. Researchers examining POKENAME tunnels have found that they hoard Moon Stone fragments.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are a low-maintenance Pokémon popular with people living in small apartments. They tend to remain completely stationary whilst observed, pretending to be a miniature plant. Their three heads only seek sustenance when nobody else is around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be found bickering amongst themselves over their diet, with one head demanding sweet berries while another head demanding nutrient rich roots. The third head is often too timid to break the tie.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are considered pests by farmers, often raiding their composters in search of food. They are very skittish; however, their three heads are able to burrow into the ground in seconds.
author: santon5512

entry: The heads extruding from POKENAME's cheeks have their own brains and emotions. There have been rare instances where one of these heads will take control, becoming dominant over the other two.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Farmers encourage POKENAME to make their homes in crop fields, as the Pokémon's presence is beneficial for soil nutrition. POKENAME enrich the soil with essential nutrients through their flowers, mixing it into the soil with their constant digging.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Each of its three heads has its own mouth and stomach. If it does not eat for a day, its noses will become extremely cold.
author: .izik

entry: The three separate heads on POKENAME's body are capable of individual thought. The nose in the middle spins 360 degrees.
author: auroraeuphoria

entry: POKENAME flare their wings wide when they feel threatened, markings on their feathers making it appear as though they have three heads. They use the confusion this sudden reveal creates to dig away to safety.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The head on the shell usually takes the lead in directing the other two heads in battle. When digging underground, the bottom heads focus on carving tunnels, while the shell head focuses on reinforcing the shell with bedrock.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME use mud and dust as a natural means to keep themselves free of parasites, frequently flying to muddy springs and bathing their wings in the dirt. This habit led to them are often the mascot Pokémon for spas.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With three highly adept noses, POKENAME is a master of sniffing out mushrooms buried under the snow.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is capable of creating vehicles and weapons entirely out of sand, dirt, and rock. No one is sure how they manage to do it.
author: neonriser

entry: This subspecies of POKENAME is capable of creating vehicles and weapons entirely out of materials from the seafloor. It's known to be very aggressive.
author: neonriser

entry: Employed by farmers overrun by Diglett, POKENAME guide Diglett into their bags full of rocky soil to bring them over to open wild fields. POKENAME are always courteous enough to scoop enough ground to secure a Diglett's full body safely.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME fly aimlessly through the sky, their three heads each trying to lead it in a different direction. When they spot food, they become far more coordinated, swooping down to deliver a powerful Drill Run.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME ambush their prey stranded in deserts from underground, each triplet working together to strangle them with terrifying strength.
author: greaterjagras

entry: It can smell a fire burning from a mile away. If a POKENAME smells a campfire, it will flee in the opposite direction to avoid the traveler.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its head to have their Diglett comrades ride on top of them. They parade as a simple Dugtrio before popping up and wailing at foes.
author: awiralonprime

entry: POKENAME make their home in clay pots, burrowing their lower halves into the soil contained within. They enjoy being cared for, their three heads constantly looking around for people and growing upset when none can be found.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Every single Dugtrio face on POKENAME's body works like an independent muscle to loosen and dig dirt. It stores the massive amounts of dirt it collects inside the holes in its palms, which can then be shot out at high, pressurized speeds.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME absorbs all grounded electricity within a radial mile. This amps it up to burrow tunnels at incredible speeds. Construction workers often train POKENAME to help with building highways through hillsides.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Though the triplets split from one body and nigh-perfectly think the same, they each sleep individually while the remaining two remain awake and alert. They work efficiently together to burrow for many hours each day.
author: infinex21

entry: Known to lay unfertilized eggs daily, POKENAME is kept in self-sufficient flocks. When threats appear, it burrows under the earth, popping up at set distances to spit embers to protect its young.
author: ghostslythe

entry: Despite their looks, POKENAME are extremely vicious hunters; they are quick on their feet and are adept swimmers. POKENAME hunt by burrowing underground and moving in three different directions; attacking from blind spots with searing flames.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME are constantly alert, the twin heads growing from their cheeks looking left and right for danger, whilst the central head searches for food. At the first sign of danger, they disappear into their burrows, hiding in river banks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME share a single mind, acting completely in concert with one another. With their three sets of limbs, they are able to rapidly dig through the soft mud of their swampy homes, creating deep-running tunnel networks to live in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hide deep within caves, spinning and weaving threads. Due to their ability to predict events, it is said that these Pokémon weave fate itself, each one controlling either the past, present, or future.
author: santon5512

entry: Its heads often forget which one should control the main body, leading to comical, spinning movements while levitating. This lack of coordination is oddly endearing to Trainers.
author: .izik

entry: They live in canyons, surviving by eating dead bushes and twigs. This diet sustains them in the harsh, arid environment.
author: .izik

entry: Its distributed brains work in tandem, allowing POKENAME to swiftly burrow through the ground as if swimming through water currents. While digging, its body gathers debris from the soil to strengthen its stone-like carapace.
author: gaogao028

entry: The gigantic trio have a habit of disrupting cavern infrastructure due to one member's insatiable curiosity. The duo in the back constantly try to rein in its impulsiveness to little avail.
author: sk372

entry: Legends tell of a POKENAME that shaped the earth beneath its feet. Its movements rumble through the ground like an Onix stampede, carving mountains and valleys wherever it burrows. Some say the world itself rests atop its endless tunnels.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: A great friend of nature, it brings Diglett from arid zones to better lands. All farmers hope that POKENAME will deposit its Diglett in their fields.
author: spagalapof

entry: The heads on POKENAME's shoulder encourage the center one to behave more imposingly and aggressively. It does so by slicing up large swaths of dirt with its wings and flinging them at others.
author: sk372

entry: While the two bodies on either side of the POKENAME tunnel through the ground, the central body collects magnetic minerals along its nose. All three bodies are very protective of these minerals since they are their primary source of food.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If anyone dares to tread on its ground, it holds them in place with its three blades. The end of its sash is long and broad to more swiftly feed on the life force of larger Pokémon and is muddy to prevent escape.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: Aegislash absorbed Dugtrio into its swords, forming POKENAME. It manipulates the ground with its blades, allowing for swift underground travel.
author: jackjirachi

entry: The three heads of POKENAME all think exactly alike, allowing it perfect coordination while digging tunnels.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME spend the day underground in their tunnels, hunting around underground for fragments of Moon Stones. At night, they emerge from their tunnels and dance together under the moonlight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME bound their legs together in the ground as a testament to their deep friendship. Now united within the earth, they joyfully move as one.
author: slowforest

entry: POKENAME bears a strong resemblance to traffic lights because of its red, yellow, and green pattern. It helps children play a certain game where they can only run when the light is green.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME move their arms in total synchrony with one another, performing moves together in battles. They are a favourite Pokémon of gamblers, who believe that their Metronomes are more likely to result in a lucky outcome.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME roam around deserts and badlands at night, plunging their ghostly hands underground to pull up fossils, which they store within their bodies. By unknown means, these fossils seem to reanimate, protecting POKENAME when attacked.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uproot sections of earth to use as a protective layer for their main body. Their multiple heads function as limbs, allowing them to rapidly scuttle along the ground, withdrawing back into their earthy core for safety when threatened.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's trio of lit candles burn bright enough to be visible just before it surfaces from underground. The lights draw in weak-minded Diglett, coaxing them into its tunnels so it can use the flames to drain their life force.
author: sk372

entry: It is a mineral-devouring Pokémon that works in a group of three to build complex tunnels. It is extremely territorial; vicious battles between POKENAME and other Pokémon leave giant gashes in the nearby earthen walls.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME has two secret heads that live under the dirt, feeding on roots and tiny soil creatures. The above-ground head keeps a lookout and uses its filthy wings to deter predators or relocate in an emergency.
author: chinigan

entry: When one head grows tired, the other two allow it to rest by taking over control of the body. This teamwork ensures it stays active for longer periods.
author: .izik

entry: Each of the many heads atop the tails of POKENAME have their own distinct minds and personalities, resulting in a communal approach to decision making. Remarkably, they never seem to struggle to decide what to do and will consistently work together.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME anchor themselves within the moulted shells of Aron, using the fragile remains of their armour as a shelter to hide in when threatened. Their trio of heads extend out to feed on nearby roots and dirt, maintaining a sedentary existence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Each of its three tongues ends with a small head that latches onto prey. These heads work together to drag victims beneath the sand.
author: .izik

entry: It slams its thick skulls into stones, breaking them apart to consume the gravel. This behavior strengthens both its diet and its sturdy heads.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can retract within their tough shell at the first sign of trouble, hiding until the danger threatening them has passed. They are most active at night, their multiple heads emerging and acting as limbs to move their body around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The member of POKENAME with the largest bud is the leader, and takes the front when digging tunnels. The other two protect it fiercely, as nutrients gained from the leader's photosynthesis are needed to keep all three alive.
author: sk372

entry: A trio of bloodsuckers working together, the tinier members distract targets, typically Ground types, while POKENAME leaps onto them to deliver a paralyzing bite. The three then join together to drink their fill.
author: sk372

entry: Its extra heads wiggle frantically, constantly advising the main head of potential danger. This hyper-awareness makes it difficult to sneak up on.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fly in groups of three, working in tandem to locate food using echolocation and their keen sense of smell. If attacked, they dart straight into the ground, burrowing in an instant.
author: santon5512

entry: Its three heads screech at dissonant frequencies, which POKENAME fine-tunes to produce maximal disorientation and distress in its target.  It then sinks its teeth into its confused prey.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME is the top pick for explorers in the search of deeply buried lost treasures. However, they need to be trained and well fed with enough minerals - otherwise, they may eat all the precious gems before bringing the rest to the surface.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME rapidly chew their way through dirt, moving in formation toward the sounds of other Pokémon battling. They burst out of the ground and attack whichever Pokémon appears to be losing, sometimes interrupting Trainer battles in the process.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME tunnel through topsoil at high speed, their trio of heads the only thing visible above ground as they do. Their keen sense of smell lets them chase down Pokémon that have passed by, bursting out to bite at them and drag them underground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a habit of clustering together in groups of three in fields, burying themselves up to their flower. At night, they dig through the soil, moving together and giving the illusion of flowers drifting across the ground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The muddy slime it secretes smells sweet like pastries but is highly toxic. Consuming it is a grave mistake, despite its tempting aroma.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's petals are constantly coated in a fine layer of dirt and grime from their relentless digging. When they surface, they shake themselves vigorously to clean themselves, sending clouds of pollen flying into the air alongside the dirt.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its main body is composed of the surrounding earth, which it controls using its psychic powers.  This allows it to become ambulatory even as the members of the trio remain below ground.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME rapidly digs holes, hurling dirt and rocks at opponents to attack. It calmly protects its Trainer while its three heads bark and cause earthquakes and falling rocks around foes.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's scale has heads of its own which have additional eyes for hunting underground. These extra sets allow it to track prey in the pitch-dark tunnels it calls home.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME make tunnels around the roots of large trees, using their sharp fangs to feed on the roots for sustenance. At night, they emerge into the open air, using their six antennae to sense danger while they search for another tree to feed on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME make their nests in underground tunnels, tucking their wings in tight against their body when they dig. If their nest is disturbed, they spread their wings and flutter away whilst taking a clod of their home soil with them as a memento.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Each of POKENAME's heads has its own brain, as well as its own consciousness and opinions. If two heads disagree with each other, it can make them more vulnerable to an attack.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: Splicing Dugtrio with itself appears to have created a leader. Diglett come and go from this small community as they please.
author: xtjs2018x

entry: POKENAME fusions appear to have a variable number of members, something researchers are trying to understand the true nature of. Conflicting theories abound over whether colonies are multiple POKENAME or a single large POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The three members of POKENAME are often agitated by the antics of the others, leading to infighting. The sight of the three bashing and striking each other is often viewed as comical by onlookers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME now takes on a form resembling its Alolan counterpart. Despite it exhibiting no additional features from that variant, it does take great pride in the fancy new heads of hair it possesses.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found floating with a lifebuoy at many beaches throughout the world. When they are not swimming atop the waves, they dive underwater to eat seaweed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In ancient times, people would know to prepare for an earthquake if a POKENAME was sighted. This is because POKENAME primarily causes them. Many insurance companies will not pay out for "Acts of POKENAME".
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME tunnel beneath farms to search for crops that might ease their aching head. When one of their heads develops a headache, the rest of their heads cry out in pain as well.
author: quackquackattack

entry: One of POKENAME's three heads shows off the Growlithe species's link to Hisui. It is prone to digging several holes in the ground for recreation, so owners should anticipate their yard becoming uprooted often.
author: sk372

entry: Due to having three heads, POKENAME is unable to burrow effectively. They have formed a symbiotic relationship with Sandshrew, who digs tunnels wide enough for them, while they scare off larger Pokémon with boiling hot Flamethrowers.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's two border heads control its fists, while the middle controls the rest of the body. The middle head is rather scatterbrained, so POKENAME has some difficulty properly coordinating itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found deeply meditating underground. They have the ability to conjure portals through which their other two heads come out, useful for surprise attacks on unsuspecting foes.
author: acid_pen

entry: POKENAME's three powerful bodies emerge from the ground in perfect unison, striking with immense strength to intimidate its foes. They use their multiple arms to quickly burrow underground, waiting patiently for stronger opponents to arrive.
author: motion_09

entry: POKENAME burrow through the ground with ease, carving out intricate tunnel networks. Large populations can cause built-up areas to suffer stability issues as foundations are cracked and damaged by their activity.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME burrow through the ground with ease, carving out intricate tunnel networks. Large populations can cause built-up areas to suffer stability issues as foundations are cracked and damaged by their activity.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME burrow through the ground with ease, carving out intricate tunnel networks. Large populations can cause built-up areas to suffer stability issues as foundations are cracked and damaged by their activity.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live inside boulders that they animate and use to move from location to location. When threatened, they retreat back inside their boulder, using the rock as a makeshift shell.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME may look like a planet with several satellite objects orbiting them, but they do not have their own gravitational pull. Instead, their unique electromagnetism causes metal and iron-rich soil to levitate.
author: chinigan

entry: The three heads of POKENAME near constantly fight over holding their treasured leek, only stopping to eat, sleep or participate in battles. They will not accept additional leeks even from their trusted Trainers.
author: chibitales

entry: The body and one head have more aggressive behaviors than the second head. While the former two strike at opponents, the latter is often gazing aimlessly into space, unaware of why it's being dragged into the fight.
author: sk372

entry: Always fearful of other Pokémon, POKENAME keeps its three heads hidden underground. It senses vibrations and movement to fight; when something draws near, it strikes with powerful kicks or triggers strong Magnitude by stomping the ground.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses its three heads to swim through the loose dirt underground, periodically coming up to breathe. It feeds primarily on roots and mushrooms it comes across while digging.
author: sk372

entry: Rival POKENAME engage in rough battles over territory. When not battling, a POKENAME buries its tail in the ground to mark the area as its own.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME blasts mini-heads from its cannons. Somehow, nobody knows what the bottom of these mini-heads look like.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME use layers of mucus to trap mud around themselves, forming a tightly packed protective shell. They swim by pumping water through their shell, drawing it in with their three heads and jetting it out behind them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME disguises itself as a Dugtrio by burying half of its body. When Trainers get too close, it attacks with psychic power.
author: themicelegion

entry: Somehow, its sand makes people fall asleep.  Scientists tried to make it into an insomnia remedy, but it has no effect unless POKENAME sprinkles it.
author: empty_set

entry: The spores POKENAME spread are not produced by POKENAME but are actually a concoction made from the by-products of various Poison and Bug-type Pokémon. Once their young grow up, they are also taught the recipe.
author: dualblades1147

entry: The wings on POKENAME's back allow it to glide short distances while also producing a special powder that keeps it awake. This allows it to guard dens for long periods of time without rest, ensuring the safety of those within.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flutter above lakes at night, chasing after Volbeat in the dark. They are easily confused by boat lights and can end up falling into the water when they crash into them, relying on their tail float to keep them from sinking.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly timid Pokémon, and when frightened releases noxious smoke to escape. It only comes out at night and uses its cloak-like wings to disguise itself as a person, though its bright colors make this difficult.
author: goober145

entry: The thick lavender-scented venom covering POKENAME's body is incredibly hot to the touch. During full moons, bubbles popping off the surface can distribute an acidic vapor.
author: .izik

entry: One flap of POKENAME's wings can produce enough toxic dust to cause an entire town to fall ill. Because of this, it chooses to live far from human civilization, and is only occassionally attracted by a city's night lights.
author: goober145

entry: POKENAME hunt in the darkness of night, scattering poisonous dust that wears down their prey with every slash of their claws. If they spot a light during their hunt, they will drop everything to investigate, often letting their prey get away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME spits a strong silk at fruit in trees before dragging it away to eat. It stores the seeds in its cheek to use as ammunition for spitting at foes.
author: .izik

entry: When they encounter something unknown, POKENAME flatten their bodies to the ground and wave their tail in the air, mimicking a much larger Pokémon. Their trickery can be an effective defense in the dense jungles they call home.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME live and nest in large groups, collectively scattering toxic powder from their wings to ward off predators. If any POKENAME becomes lost, the rest of the group will spit fire into the sky so the light will guide them back.
author: infinex21

entry: If someone ventures too close to its pond, POKENAME emerges from the water and releases clouds of yellow mustard-scented powder. Contact with this powder can cause paralysis.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies lazily near streetlights beside its swamp, staring at them for hours. If disturbed even briefly, it spits a thick mud at the offender.
author: .izik

entry: The many wings on its back resemble jaws and can close shut like a flower. When POKENAME flexes its wings, it releases a toxic powder from them. It will ensnare its prey within its wings and flood them with toxic powder until they submit.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME roam forests at night, their compound eyes scanning for even the dimmest light in the darkness. If they come across the spark of a fire, they make a loud buzz, striving to alert sleeping Pokémon to the potential threat of a forest fire.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The pink and white powder that drifts from POKENAME's body can cause sneezing fits. After prolonged sneezing, most report an extreme calm that lasts for hours.
author: .izik

entry: These nocturnal Pokémon are drawn to bright lights, such as lampposts and streetlights, and are often found clinging to them while asleep in the following mornings. When startled awake, they release irritant toxins from their wings and fly away.
author: infinex21

entry: To defend themselves from predators, POKENAME rapidly rotate in unison and scatter a barrage of poisonous dust that's projected forward by the momentum of their rotation. Once they confirm its safe to stop, they fly away as fast as they can.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The clouds of red powder POKENAME produces with its wings can cause anything they touch to burst into flames. One should avoid using water to extinguish these flames, as it only spreads them further.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are considered one of the most valued pollinators across the world as they feed only on pollen and nectar. Swarms of POKENAME descend upon fields and orchards at nightfall.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hunts by quickly circling around groups of small prey. Its fins produce a toxic material that clouds the water and creates a poisonous vortex that leaves its targets too dazed to avoid its gnashing jaws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is covered in a fine dust that spreads when it shakes its leaves. The powder causes hallucinations of playing children, and when people try to chase them, POKENAME will have already flown far away.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are drawn to cities due to their bright lights, gathering around streetlights. They prey on smaller insects that are attracted to these lights, spreading the poisonous powder on their wings through the air to incapacitate them.
author: santon5512

entry: During the day, POKENAME uses its radar to sense where clean water is located before swimming to the location at night. Toxic dust is released if a Pokémon tries to take a ride on top of it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME run through forests in swarms, releasing clouds of dust when they howl. This dust carries a powerful numbing agent that helps subdue prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME covers trees in its toxic powder to prevent other Pokémon from eating the sap within them. When in cities, it creates strings of silk between streetlights to safely travel over roads and sidewalks.
author: soup1900

entry: It can only glide for short durations due to how small its wings are; when it flexes its wings, it scatters a highly toxic powder. POKENAME feeds mostly on leaves while it is active at night, though it is easily distracted by bright lights.
author: infinex21

entry: During the day, it hides itself in the trees with its silk and drinks rainwater. At night, it takes flight and devours the leaves before leaving to find another tree. Its wings and spikes shed toxic dust as it flies.
author: torterrable

entry: POKENAME eyes are extremely sensitive to light, swarms of them often being drawn to artificial lighting at night. When they're startled, they release a toxic powder before fluttering away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME emerge at night to feed on flowers that only bloom in the dark. POKENAME with lightly patterned wings have tassels that confuse their predators, drawing attention away from their bodies and helping them escape to safety.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME emerge at night to feed on flowers that only bloom in the dark. POKENAME with heavily patterned wings abruptly flare their wings when they spot a predator approaching, startling them with their eye spots before fluttering away to safety.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's silk becomes extremely acidic if it is heated. During hot summer months, it can burn through an oak tree's branches in a matter of seconds.
author: .izik

entry: Villagers near homes of POKENAME are advised to never hang out their laundry and to keep all windows closed. POKENAME have the capacity to eat three houses' worth of linen if they can.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are easily drawn to light sources and because they are nocturnal, they tend to gather around streetlights. The toxic power they scatter from their wings when agitated is potent enough to cause an Ursaring to fall ill in minutes.
author: infinex21

entry: If the eyespots on its antennae fail to intimidate predators, POKENAME shakes the antennae to release clouds of toxic dust. Combined with its attraction to streetlights, this behaviour has gained POKENAME a reputation as a dangerous urban pest.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME spits a corrosive string to wrap up its foe before reeling them into its agape mouth. It can consume objects up to twice its own size.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have pitifully small wings and heavy bodies, so they can only crawl along the ground. Because their stomach fluids can digest just about anything, they are never without food. By shaking themselves, they scatter toxic powder all around.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME spots a Seviper, it reflexively fills the area with a cloud of blue powder. The powder itself is not fatal, causing only a minor stinging sensation on skin, but it creates an unpleasant environment to remain in.
author: .izik

entry: The moment night falls, POKENAME flies through its jungle habitat and descends on prey with its poison-tipped tail. At sunrise, it conceals itself within tree trunks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases spores when it snaps its pincers. At night, it goes to the edge of the shore to eat washed-up seaweed.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME is an extremely territorial creature that attacks anyone who approaches the fruit tree it is feeding on. It is mainly active at night, as any source of light that is too bright bothers it too much.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME move like kites in the water with their wide fins. These Pokémon will swarm their target and use the electricity that arcs between their bodies when they are close together to shock and injure their foe.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME wanders cities at night in a trance-like state, using its psychic powers to blow dust at those who disturb it. Those who inhale this dust see vivid hallucinations.
author: goober145

entry: POKENAME maintains top physical form by independently cultivating a garden of fruits which it dusts with powder from its wings. It shares its brews with people and Pokémon in lively parties, which it alone cleans up to continue its fitness regimen.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hide in the shadows cast by streetlights. If you stop and rest too close to one, it may emerge to curse you with a supernatural toxin.
author: goober145

entry: POKENAME loves to pretend to be a large acorn and spook Pokémon and Trainers alike. The leaf on its tail absorbs sunlight while it sits still and provides energy.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME secrete rich and nutritious molasses from the stems on their bellies during all seasons except for winter. In winter, they sleep often to conserve their energy, which ultimately improves the quality of the first batch of molasses in spring.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's coloration helps it camouflage seamlessly in trees and on the forest floor. It picks fights with those who harass Seedot.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME regularly gather in the trees around clearings within the jungles they reside in. They take turns dancing and displaying within said clearing, arbitrating some dispute or another that researchers have been unable to discern.
author: vic1312

entry: Using its sharp talons, POKENAME runs up the side of trees to perch atop the branches. By embedding its beak into the tree, it can siphon nutrients for itself. It grows heavier as it eats, until it inevitably falls head-first to the ground.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spend most of their days within the treetops, taking in nutrients and sunlight in preparation for their evolution. If the tree they are in comes under attack, POKENAME will fall out of the tree and attack with a fierce drop kick.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME use their exploding kicks to defend Seedots still attached to trees from bird Pokémon. POKENAME are strong enough to go head-to-head with three Pidgeots.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME rests in the shade of trees that border swampy areas. It feeds on old roots and digs up seeds that thrive within muddy soil to plant and grow, helping keep its home nice and verdant.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME prefers to make muddy dens at the top of waterfalls. Should it spot a predator at the bottom, it leaps onto them and explodes.
author: .izik

entry: Unable to gain nutrients from the sun, POKENAME burrow into the roots of trees, leeching vital nutrients. When sensing other pests attacking their meal, they quickly latch onto the other Pokémon and drain its power.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME hides among tree branches and seeks out gloomy people, especially children. It often startles them in an effort to lift their spirits.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME collects acorns using its long tongue. When startled while eating, its skin flashes red and brown rapidly before it explodes.
author: .izik

entry: Sensing an incoming hurricane, POKENAME rushes to the center of town and detonates. Though meant as a warning, the act often worsens the destruction.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME sleep, they cling to trees or wrap around tree branches. The tops of their heads and their claws siphon nutrients from trees that they attach themselves to. When they consume too much, they grow heavy and fall off their trees.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME store water and excess nutrients within the shells on their backs; they can store enough to go many days without eating or drinking. By flailing their leaves, they cast about a pungent, metallic scent; this scent is an effective repellent.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will climb up oak trees and hang by its tail from branches. It has to control its flame while doing this, or the oak tree will catch fire.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The ends of its upper limbs are harder than Chesto Berries, yet they exude a fragrant aroma that tempts many Pokémon to bite them. By shaking its arms, it creates a maraca-like sound from these parts and amplifies the nutty fragrance they exude.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are often mistaken for UFOs when they launch themselves into the air. They can travel far distances by using bursts of spores and wind direction.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME flocks typically nest in a single tree at a time. Should a predator approach, the oldest member of the flock will divebomb it and explode on contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME produces leaves that grow from its shell, which are used in bubble teas for their sweet, energizing flavor. Its tough acorn shell can also be ground into a spice that resembles nutmeg.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After flying through heavy storms, POKENAME's fluffy wings sprout tiny green shoots. These sprouts dry out and fall away within a day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats in small ponds where it waits for berries to fall into the water. It takes small nibbles from them and needs about an hour to finish one berry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's rounded head sloshes with stored water as it moves. It sprays foul-smelling liquid to mark its territory and ward off rivals.
author: .izik

entry: While searching for the acorns they buried for the winter, forest-dwelling Pokémon sometimes dig up POKENAME accidentally. Being unearthed makes it unable to absorb water and nutrients from the ground, so POKENAME reacts with hostility.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is a very rare Pokémon that is only found in summery forests. It invites people and Pokémon that need growth and healing to its cozy grove.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are considered scavengers. During the day they hide in leaf piles, most Trainers believing they are Acorns. At night, they burst from the leaves, tracking down people who passed during the morning to steal food from their campsites.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME dislikes affection and typically only accepts physical touch from those it grew up with. Its howl sounds like the wailing winds of a storm. Most Pokémon seek shelter and stay away from a POKENAME pack.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME attaches to tree branches by its head and tail to absorb nutrients. Its pinecone-like fur makes a rattling noise as it moves. When POKENAME is tired, it descends to the ground and digs a small burrow to rest in.
author: chibitales

entry: In spring, small vines sprout from POKENAME's thick fur. As summer heat arrives, the vines dry up and fall away naturally.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is tough, having begun to harden in preparation for evolution. When it begins to evolve, it sheds the spines along its back, which have a nutty flavor and are used as a topping or ingredient for ice cream.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The spores POKENAME leaves behind from its wings are combustible if jostled. Should enough accumulate on a surface, they can result in a massive explosion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's seed body is bursting with so much potential for growth that it occasionally even sprouts its own leaf. Though it is hardy, POKENAME prefers shady places under trees so it doesn't become sunburned.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME nests in trees near Seedot communities, standing guard for days without rest. It drives off predators with concentrated Giga Drain attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Flocks of wild POKENAME are often seen engaged in competitions with one another, ramming their sturdy heads against each other in impressive aerial battles. Whichever falls first is forced to find a new flock.
author: campadascleric

entry: With the tops of their heads, POKENAME can attach themselves to trees and siphon their nutrients in lieu of eating solid matter. They spread their wings to glide and to ride updrafts to travel; flocks migrate to warmer climates to avoid winter colds.
author: infinex21

entry: From the tops of their heads, POKENAME exude nutty, tropical scents; humidity increases the pungency of these scents. POKENAME love to swoop down and stab hard nuts and fruits with their beaks, drinking their fluids and eating their innards.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME scoop up large fruits within their massive beaks, even just to hoard them. They often accidentally scoop up Seedot as well, which either struggle their way out or are tossed out to fall to the ground below.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in forest ponds. The hard wooden cap on its head helps protect it from aerial predators.
author: mepp.

entry: While rapidly flying between trees in marshlands, POKENAME constantly checks for predators. If it spots one, it does not hesitate to collide with them and explode.
author: .izik

entry: If startled, POKENAME spins in place like a top and releases a sound resembling radio static. When the noise reaches its peak, it explodes.
author: .izik

entry: Their bodies swell with nutrients gained through photosynthesis and from water they absorb. They are often physically active to sweat out their excess water, resulting in them developing strong bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live in sizeable groups around and upon trees. By attaching the tips of their tails to trees, they can siphon their daily nutrients from trees. When a POKENAME encounters danger, it will smack its tail against its head to alert its pack.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME forms swarms of bug Pokémon by flickering its glowing tail. It leads the swarm to tall trees where they hang from the branches and eat leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lures bug Pokémon into forming a swarm by releasing a sweet aroma. It finds healthy trees and leads the swarm to rest in the branches, where they feast on the leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Seedot will sometimes gather and hide within POKENAME's mouth for protection. In exchange for not being eaten themselves, the Seedot bring food offerings for it when they return from their foraging.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's furry exterior is composed of thin wooden fibers. A careless touch can embed splinters in anyone who pets it the wrong way.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clamps onto approaching Zangoose with a powerful bite. If overwhelmed, it resorts to a desperate point-blank Explosion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rely on their claws to convince predators that they are a group of Seedot. On the rare occasion that they engage in combat, they shoot seeds from their claws before finding a way to escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its strong arms give it a much broader range of mobility compared to a Seedot. After being fused, a POKENAME will use its new arms to strike various proud poses.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME live in dense forests where they practice their boxing against trees. Each punch moves so quickly that their leafy hands produce a soft whistle with each jab.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME appears to humans in forests to warn them of disasters that may arise from their actions. If its warnings are ignored, the humans will receive a painful pecking.
author: hophoppip

entry: Though POKENAME has no visible udders, it can still be milked as with most Miltank fusions. Simply grabbing and squeezing its nose will cause it to spray milk from the holes in its belly.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME sneezes, its nose creates the same sounds as a poorly played flute. This mainly happens when it is near objects of high magnetization, which makes its nose itch a lot.
author: soup1900

entry: A timid Pokémon that wanders forests at dusk. When the wind blows, its leaf whistles with a curious song.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's hollow wooden body produces a soft whistle as it flies with its flock. On windy days, people travel just to hear their melodic calls.
author: .izik

entry: Weary travelers often sit on POKENAME, mistaking it for a tree stump. This causes POKENAME to get irritated, but thankfully, it's too weak to be a serious threat.
author: atlas3339098

entry: Leaves sometimes sprout from the wooden disc atop POKENAME's head. It trims them carefully, keeping only a single leaf to grow.
author: .izik

entry: During extreme heat, POKENAME's leaf spins rapidly as a warning signal. The rotation helps vent energy and prevents sudden explosions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have tiny leaves on their legs that allow them to float on water. They keep ponds and lakes clean by eating leaves that fall into the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME strips bark from trees with sharp claws to feed. If the bark tastes off, it discards it carelessly, leaving a scattered trail behind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME blends in with its forest habitat to ambush unsuspecting prey, constricting them in its powerful, wooden coils. When threatened, it whistles an unnerving melody and rattles the seeds in its tail-knots to frighten off foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's head change shape depending on the local weather, showcasing its remarkable adaptability. Highly territorial, it drops from tree branches to strike intruders who dare to enter its home.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are lightweight creatures that can pack a heavy kick. They conjure powerful winds to give their kicks extra force but are easily swept away by these same winds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Occasionally, a tree is found deep in the forest with many POKENAME attached to its trunk. The significance of these trees is not yet understood.
author: empty_set

entry: The bark on POKENAME's body grows slightly faster when it senses someone nearby with a kind heart. During this time, it conjures illusions of things they love to bring them happiness.
author: .izik

entry: The sharp udders on its belly allow it to fire out precise streams of a nut-flavored milk; its milk streams can be strong enough to cut through wood. It is a kind Pokémon that protects and nurtures the young; its face tends to scare most Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are infamous from legends that describe them causing windstorms that sweep lost Trainers away. However, anyone caught in a POKENAME's storm reports that the winds somehow knew how to guide them exactly where they needed to go.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When an enormous tree was felled by lightning, it is said that POKENAME emerged from the stump. Electricity flows freely through its plant-like body.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME live in forests that need to burn regularly to provide new seeds with free space and nutritious soil. They are often the source of such a forest fire, spitting out small fireballs and spreading the embers by waving their wings like fans.
author: _pixelar_

entry: While POKENAME are sleeping, they practice martial arts. Wild Pokémon give them a wide berth as at any moment they can spring into a flurry of kicks and punches. On cold winter days, they grow more active.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME spends most of the year in deep dormancy. When forests suffer severe destruction, groups may awaken and seek out the source, delivering powerful blows. As their numbers decline, such responses have become increasingly rare.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: There is much folklore about POKENAME, speaking of them as forest guardians that will swallow whole any troublemakers. Supposedly, their noses are tough enough that they were used in the making of some weapons.
author: infinex21

entry: Its body is so light that it can effectively ride upon wind or even prance through gales. If it senses malice, it will unleash powerful winds to quell the source; it does not matter to this Pokémon if the source of malice does or does not survive.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME possesses a thick coat of fur that obscures its rock-hard hide. Pokémon that attack it from behind are taken by surprise by its impenetrable scales.
author: vic1312

entry: Its arms stretch as it delivers punches and slashing attacks; its leaves are sharp and hardy enough to be used as small blades. POKENAME's quick strikes create powerful gusts of wind in their wake.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives deep in the forest as a guardian; it will drive off intruders by any means necessary. Legends state that if its hollow wooden nose is cut, it will turn into a normal tree.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Once feared and despised due to their incredible strength, further studies have revealed that POKENAME are very affectionate and protective. One swing from their staffs is powerful enough to whip up a tornado.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is infamously known for the heavy, spiked cudgel it wields at all times. It is often blinded by its sense of morals and will perceive most things as potential threats to ward off, all for the sake of protecting its forest home.
author: infinex21

entry: It cackles wickedly as it dashes between the trees. Camping in a forest inhabited by POKENAME is a bad idea, as its a known prankster.
author: hophoppip

entry: It blows in on wintry winds and finds a tree to attach itself to.  Forming a symbiotic relationship with its host tree, it absorbs its nutrients while scaring away any troublemakers.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME is said to be one of the most arrogant Pokémon to exist. Despite this large ego, it never seems to cause any trouble, preferring to live isolated in the mountains and only descending to protect nature and those who respect the elements.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME are small, yet they courageously defend their nests with Razor Wind attacks and by jabbing with their sharp beaks. Their wings function much like leaves, allowing them to subsist on sunlight and water alone.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME rides the wind with effortless grace, with some stories claiming it is capable of traversing entire regions in a single day. It makes its home in dense forests.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are fiercely protective of Seedot, using their fans to create gusts up to 100 mph to deter threats. Pokémon Rangers and Researchers have begun to use this protectiveness to monitor the health and actions of Seedot.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME live in clean rivers with flourishing floating plants. They use their wing-like fins to propel themselves out of the water to reach insect Pokémon flying just above the water's surface.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are able to fly vast distances with unerring accuracy, braving all kinds of weather to reach their destination. The underside of their wings is coated with white feathers, disguising them against the clouds as they fly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Flocks of POKENAME sleep together throughout the day, with one member of the flock keeping watch over the rest. POKENAME on guard will pick fights with Pokémon many times their size in order to keep their family safe.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Flocks of POKENAME sleep together throughout the day, with one member of the flock keeping watch over the rest, ready to fight at a moment's notice. Which POKENAME is on guard changes each hour, the current guard waking the next with gentle chirps.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are able to fly vast distances with unerring accuracy, braving all kinds of weather to reach their destination. They can be trained to carry messages to far-flung locations, and were commonly used as messengers in pre-industrial times.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME maintain large territories, circling the boundaries of their home multiple times in a day. They are bold and will attack bird Pokémon many times their own size, seemingly heedless of the danger to themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has a feisty personality and likes to battle other bird Pokémon in the air. Its twin tails coupled with its aerial maneuverability make it quite adept at clubbing other foes out of the sky.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME follow their targets for miles, stalking them from the shadows. At the perfect moment, they let out a sudden loud cry, startling their target long enough to steal their food.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's blue feathers are highly valued by ornithologists, who are always excited to find them. POKENAME hunts with its flock, cawing to coordinate their movements.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME carries Pokémon Eggs inside the reinforced nest on its back. It gives off a high amount of heat, often helping the protected eggs hatch more quickly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME despises cold seasons, so when autumn arrives, it migrates far away in search of a warm and pleasant place. If its crest droops, it is s a clear sign that the Pokémon is unwell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are brave despite their size, using their wings and loud voices to try and intimidate potential threats. To protect others and their tree-bound nests, POKENAME swiftly deliver many small strikes using their talons and beaks.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME often try to intimidate larger Pokémon into giving up their food by chirping loudly and spitting globs of fire from just out of reach. They quickly pick up on Pokémon that can be easily scared away and which to avoid.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are more commonly found when it is raining. They prefer searching for food in these conditions, as they can easily dig up the softened dirt to find Bug-type Pokémon hiding underground.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME tends to fly around large trees after long days to relax. This action calms it down and prepares it for the next hunt.
author: retrodox

entry: POKENAME primarily use their larger sets of jaws to store food and to fight, though they could use them to eat if they wanted to. Perhaps due to how bulky and strong their larger jaws are, they have no lack of confidence in battle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are gutsy creatures that stand their ground when other Pokémon try to intimidate them, even when their foe is significantly bigger than them. This stubbornness often leads to them getting hurt, yet they also often refuse help.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wings are more suited for gliding over true flight. Its aerial maneuverability is poor, so it has difficulty dodging out of the way if another Pokémon is flying towards it.
author: sk372

entry: When trapped in its underground tunnels, POKENAME flings dirt into its foe's eyes. It follows up with quick pecks while they're disoriented.
author: .izik

entry: Though it tends to lay about for most of the day, POKENAME is known to be protective of small bird Pokémon; the only time it's been seen moving quickly is rushing to one's defense.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME glides through meadow skies enjoying the sunlight. Large amounts of static are held within its feathers, shocking anyone who touches it.
author: .izik

entry: When a POKENAME gets cold during migration, it shivers and builds up static electricity. The resulting glow makes groups of POKENAME resemble fallen stars scattered among the trees.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME scavenges its surroundings and forages insulative material to create its nests. It does this to protect its young from accidentally shocking themselves before they've learned to harness their electrical capabilities.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME float in the air by expanding their feathery bodies. They often form flocks because they want the company of others and are prone to feeling lonely.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is often chosen as a household companion thanks to its inclination to sing sweet melodies and keep lonely people company. The colors of its plumage become vibrant when it is happy, making it easy to tell when it's being well cared for.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME wraps its wings above its head like a bud when not flying. The feathers within carry a delightful grape-like scent that permeates the air as it spreads its wings to take flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is known to eat mud after a long rainy season. The smell of petrichor lingers on its beak as it pecks at the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME performs complex choreographed dances with others of its flock during sunset. They leap in and out of tall grass, using chirps to maintain a steady beat.
author: .izik

entry: These bird Pokémon are capable of breathing underwater for short periods of time. They nest near bodies of water and prey upon fish Pokémon by swooping into the water and grabbing them between their strong jaws.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefer haunting stumps that are bright red with tannins. If caught in the rain, the wood will look as if it is bleeding, which POKENAME rely on to appear more intimidating.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME enjoy taking baths whenever they get dirty. They often gather at waterfalls in groups to help each other clean their fluffy wings.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will persistently chase its prey through land or sky. It will let out a loud bark from the top of its home tree to mark its territory.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is known for having unlimited energy and a feisty attitude. It constantly challenges other Pokémon to prove its strength.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME make nests in tree hollows, often taking over abandoned nests of their brethren or other Pokémon. Fights between them consist of loud, obnoxious chirping and rattling of their feathers in attempts to scare the opponent into backing off.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME leap back and forth in a zig-zag pattern to build up momentum before they leap into the air. Unfortunately, they are still rather new to flying, so they often wobble back and forth in similar patterns as they glide.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME will periodically flap its wings and mimic chirping noises to appear more bird-like. Because of this, its most common predators are often fooled and leave it be.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME crawls into Taillow nests to disguise itself as an egg. It decorates the nest with silk, which lets other POKENAME know that the nest is occupied.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME crawls into Taillow nests to hide from predators. It pretends to be an egg and wraps the nest with silk to let other POKENAME know the nest is occupied.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's four wings allow them to fly up to 360 miles a day at much higher speeds than typical Taillow. When they spot food, they dart from the sky, swallowing their prey whole before it can even react.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME have a large wingspan that they often struggle to control. They practice performing complex aerial maneuvers to develop their wing muscles. Sometimes they hit tree branches or other flying Pokémon and tumble as a result.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME migrate to warm beaches during the wintertime to avoid the colder climates. These gutsy Pokémon will fight larger sea birds, as well as steal food from tourists' hands, all without fear.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: These Pokémon are determined fighters, fending off foes of all sizes from their nests. When hungry, POKENAME will locate outdoor cafés and hop near tables, cheeping at tourists in hopes of them sharing or dropping their food.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME flies through typhoons with ease, scooping up debris in its bill to eat later. It can find nutrition in just about any organic object.
author: .izik

entry: These nimble Pokémon are incredibly bold; they willingly snatch food away from other Pokémon, effectively skating along water as they escape. Their saliva is also a sweet syrup, which they spit out as bubbles to impede their enemies.
author: infinex21

entry: At night, POKENAME patrols its territory with vigor, bravely fighting invaders even twice its size. After dawn, it hides in a shady spot to sleep the day away.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME enjoys quiet solitude and long naps deep inside caverns. If disturbed, it may retaliate against the rude awakening with angry chirping so loud it shakes the stone walls around it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are very energetic and will often flock together to play by swooping through the air in wide circles. If threatened, they attack fearlessly, battering foes with their wings and tails.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME spots a Seviper, it chirps loudly to alert any nearby Taillow. It leads the flock in an effort to drive the Seviper away from nearby nests.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cells have rearranged so it is no longer vulnerable to the cold. It rides on gusts of winds to clear miles.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The high-pitched chirps from POKENAME's beak can reach ultrasonic frequencies to help it navigate its terrain. This is because it prefers to live in completely dark caverns.
author: .izik

entry: Scrappy by nature, POKENAME isn't afraid to pick fights with those bigger than it. It may not be strong, but its stubborn nature and quick teleporting make it a tricky foe to those who underestimate it.
author: sk372

entry: It dashes toward cliffs to gain enough momentum for flight. When fighting mid-air, POKENAME breathes tongues of fire to overwhelm its opponents.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In summer, its head flame goes out as it is only needed for warmth in winter. POKENAME pins prey with its claws to make its pecks even more precise and effective.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's sleek build lets it cut through the air quickly, particularly when swooping downward. It's just as likely to dive from the air to pick up prey as it is to latch onto a person and give them a full-body hug.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fierce demeanor scares away predators as it plunges through the air to prey on small bug Pokémon. Due to its specialized organ that lets it sense the world's rotation, it can rotate its body without causing dizziness.
author: felicia_j.t

entry: POKENAME circle high in the sky at night, hunting under the cover of darkness. Their eyes are adapted for low-light vision and, when they spot movement below, they dive down at high speed to catch their prey unawares.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME feathers are sensitive to even small air movements, allowing them to easily adjust their altitude and catch the jet stream. They prey on smaller bird Pokémon, dive bombing them from above to catch them unaware.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flies up to the nests of bird Pokémon to consume the Eggs there. The lower half of its beak extends so it can swallow a Pokémon Egg in one gulp.
author: .realthree

entry: It kicks up sand with the beat of its wings to blind opponents and catch them off guard. POKENAME keeps its food safe by burrowing a den into the ground with its claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME leaps high above the tree canopy, using its wings to glide far while hunting down prey. To swiftly dispatch its targets, it utilizes its full wings to perform powerful Leaf Blade attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: Diving from the treetops, POKENAME crash into their prey, driving the hapless Pokémon into the jungle soil. After incapacitating their foe, POKENAME begin a long climb back into the canopy, as despite their wings, they are flightless.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME sprints extremely fast, capable of outpacing even a seasoned athlete. This speed allows it to take down fleeing prey easily.
author: mepp.
