entry: POKENAME are strong hunters, able to swoop down from great heights and snatch up prey with their mighty talons. There is a grooming custom amongst flocks of POKENAME that prioritize the care and preening of one another's feathers.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME runs at speeds rivalling Johto's Magnet Train, assisted by its lithe body shape. Even at such high speeds, it has little trouble clocking prey and attacking with powerful kicks.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have the ability to sense changes in the air with their feathers and guide the wind to their will. By focusing their psychic powers, they can lift objects to be carried by the wind, making them popular messengers.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME have long, thin tongues that allow them to feed on flower nectar. In spring, the white parts of their feathers take on different, vibrant colors; the assumed hues seem to be influenced by the nectar most commonly consumed by POKENAME.
author: infinex21

entry: The large flowers that grow on a POKENAME's body can retract quickly to produce a percussive sound. POKENAME uses these sounds to attract mates.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME possesses near unparalleled speed and maneuverability in the air, and keeps to itself near the ozone layer. Many avian Pokémon look up to it and dream of soaring alongside it someday.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME float through the sky by expanding their feathery bodies with hot air. They have great precision when flying and can display this precision when they fly through hoops at circus shows.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love to keep their wings clean. They can spend hours at a time under waterfalls ensuring that they leave without a speck of dirt on them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME flies at high speeds across the ocean's surface in search of prey like Wingull. Should it spot one, it dives down with a Draining Kiss before pulling them beneath the water.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME spots prey, it swoops down from great heights, gouging them with sharp talons. It has been used for many heraldic designs, symbolizing bravery.
author: mepp.

entry: It deliberately flies in a zigzag pattern to confuse its enemies, then at the right moment lunges at them with its beak to strike with all its strength. Despite its broad wings, it builds its nest on the ground by digging it out with its feet.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME alternates between speedily running and gliding to scout its territory for prey or intruders. It is a playful companion as it loves to chase round objects, also making it a beloved competitor in agility competitions.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are skilled at performing aerial maneuvers but lack a properly sized beak to hunt for large prey. They rely on small nuts and berries to sustain them until they evolve and grow a larger beak.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are typically only found in warm climates where Swellow thrive. It takes much longer to groom their feathers compared to Swellow, but POKENAME have expert directional control while flying.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME struggles to sleep unless surrounded by its flock. They rest on seaside cliffs, huddling together against strong ocean winds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flies through ocean storms with its mouth open. Should it accidentally catch a smaller aquatic or bird Pokémon in its bill, it refuses to let go and keeps them as a meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are known to use their huge beaks to carry around young bird Pokémon which have fallen out of their nest until those Pokémon can fly on their own.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME nest at high elevations in places where sunlight is abundant so as to warm themselves as they sleep. They have impeccable vision, allowing them to even spot Cheri Berries while they fly. They have a tendency to dive at round, moving objects.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefer to live in solitude, roosting high atop trees. Highly aggressive, they viciously attack anything they perceive as a threat.
author: mepp.

entry: If anyone dares to misplace even a single one of its feathers, POKENAME flies into a rage. When it spots prey, it performs graceful leaps to catch it with its sharp claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME cuts branches from oak trees with its sturdy claws to construct its extremely large nest. The nest can comfortably house up to five of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME faces a particularly powerful opponent, it begins blasting blue flames from its sturdy beak. It flies with remarkable mastery, maintaining perfect stability even inside violent tornadoes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's powerful wings allow it to maneuver effortlessly through turbulent air, while the flame in its tail burns hotter the faster it flies due to adrenaline. It fearlessly challenges much larger opponents, diving at them in fiery spirals.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME have seen an increased use in offices, able to carry supplies while scrutinizing reports for any errors. Should they become overworked, they will take to the sky to relax in the clouds.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Legends tell of warriors riding POKENAME into battle, their manes burning brilliantly under a crimson sky. The flames trailing from its mane were said to signal the fall of entire kingdoms.
author: ambrosia04

entry: To conserve energy, POKENAME glides on sea breezes. When it spots prey below, it shoots out a powerful blast of water to stun them before diving down to finish them off.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME makes its nest at the top of a waterfall, traveling up and down this fall every day to catch food and return home. Its large, airy fins help it gracefully float in the air when jumping off a wave.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are often found creeping up the sides of cruise ships, seeking food. Their plenitude over coral reefs has led to some cruise lines employing Trainers to fight back the wild Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: Though POKENAME's body makes it far too heavy to glide, that doesn't stop it from trying. It runs and leaps from tall seaside cliffs to attempt to fly, causing a massive splash once it inevitably plummets into the ocean.
author: sk372

entry: It is an extremely reliable and obedient creature that helps sailors locate areas rich in fish to catch. Ship captains usually give POKENAME to new deckhands who decide to serve on their vessel.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Since its head always points north, sailors often place POKENAME above the rudder to ensure they are following the best course. It always cries out at the same time every day to let its Trainer know it is hungry.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Most of POKENAME's body fat is reserved for when it needs to fly; its body shape makes doing so very difficult! It instead prefers to float on the water's surface. It hibernates during the winter.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Most of POKENAME's body fat is reserved for when it needs to fly; its body shape makes doing so very difficult! It instead prefers to float on the water's surface. It hibernates during the winter.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME flocks in droves around beachfront restaurants and shops, picking up any and all discarded food items it can find. Particularly brave POKENAME will even enter the shops and steal items directly.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME are often the leaders of a flock of Wingtata. With the combined force of the flock, beachgoers have no choice but to give up their tasty snacks.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's calls sound like eerie laughter and screeches. They call loudly to frighten humans, then absorb their fear for nutrients.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME harass sailors into giving them food, stalking ships for long distances until the sailors give up and feed them. Fortunately for both parties, POKENAME tolerate eating scraps, ensuring that nothing goes to waste.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If it spots discarded food on the beach, nothing can stop POKENAME from trying to eat it. Entire coastlines have been reshaped in the pursuit of french fries.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME nests itself on cliff faces overlooking the ocean. Over time, the area it nests in will develop large amounts of moss and other plant life. Once the cliff becomes full of vegetation, POKENAME migrates to a new cliff.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the winds of updrafts to boost itself vertically and climb up walls. It intimidates foes who enter its territory by hovering on an updraft while peering menacingly at them.
author: soup1900

entry: Despite the sturdy feathers on POKENAME's arms, POKENAME can't fly. It makes up for its lack of flight with its impressive running speed, sprinting through beaches with its stolen picnic foods.
author: .realthree

entry: To compensate for their inability to fly, POKENAME developed strong legs that grant them remarkable agility. They are infamous at beaches for sprinting toward beachgoers, snatching their food, and running away just as quickly.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME searches for food by repeatedly jabbing its beak into the sand, often getting stuck in the process. After being pulled free by a passer-by, it will usually pause for a moment before trying the exact same spot again.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's loud squawks are infamous among tourists. Fearless around people, it will approach strangers and stare at them intently. If ignored, it begins squawking, flapping its arms, and charging in the hopes of stealing dropped food.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME flies out from beneath boardwalks to steal food from beachside tourists. Once a member of the flock snatches something, the others peck at anyone who gives chase to ensure a clean escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is highly in-tune with the changing winds at sea, able to sense the air currents for miles. This has made it invaluable to sailors, and few ships leave without at least one in tow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is rarely found near the ground. Hunting alone, it soars among the clouds and blends into the sky, waiting to swoop down on unsuspecting Magikarp.
author: retrodox

entry: If a small crowd of POKENAME quietly perches near someone's home before flying off, someone in the home is about to be very ill. In the distant past, doctors dealing with strong illnesses would wear masks fashioned after POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's titanic size makes it able to carry large amounts of people through the air and across the sea as a type of luxury cruise. It is somewhat easily distracted, however, so professionals must be on hand to keep it on-course.
author: sk372

entry: With hollow bones, POKENAME is always able to stay on the surface of the water. Its back serves as a giant nest for many aquatic flying Pokémon.
author: gnom3

entry: This minuscule Pokémon is suited to urban environments, where it feeds on discarded food scraps. It purposefully feeds on rotten food to coat its beak in germs, granting it a sickening defense mechanism when predators attack.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME spins through the skies above harbors in a screw-like pattern. It dive-bombs the moment it spots discarded food to snatch it up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swings its feelers randomly in all directions when it needs to travel long distances. Somehow, this allows it to take to the skies, puzzling onlookers for decades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have a horrible habit of hiding valuables and leftovers in various places, much to the chagrin of their Trainers. Despite this, these Pokémon exude calming auras that have helped many to weather fierce storms and dark times.
author: infinex21

entry: Though POKENAME cannot fly, it can unfurl its wing-like tails to glide a moderate distance. It's often seen running and gliding behind flocks of Wingull, dreaming of migrating alongside them one day.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME often walk up to people asking for food, but feeding them with manmade food is discouraged. It uses its mind-reading ability to take advantage of well-meaning people that way.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Wild POKENAME often walk up to people asking for food, but feeding them with manmade food is discouraged. It uses its mind-reading ability to take advantage of well-meaning people that way.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Though its round body prevents full flight, POKENAME can flap vigorously to keep itself gliding for a time. It bounces across the water's surface, following Wingull flocks and Wailord pods in the wild.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will dangle their tails in the water, waiting for fish Pokémon to circle near. Then it will zap the water, shocking all the fish. It will share everything it catches with its pack.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME are exceptionally buoyant due to their water-resistant feathers. They will often compete in feats of bravery, diving off of seaside cliffs into deep sea waters below. POKENAME prize rockier shores for the increased risk.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME lulls people around them to sleep before eating any food they may have on them. Many people resort to wearing earmuffs to avoid falling asleep and losing their snacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: For POKENAME to fly, both gears have to alternate the direction of their rotation so that their wings flap, and each gear has to time every flap perfectly so that they don't lock, so it is impressive that it is able to fly without issue.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME lurk among flowering shrubs near the ocean. They expose their buds and release a sweet scent to lure Bug-type Pokémon closer. When prey approaches, the buds snap shut and consume it.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME circle high around their targets, waiting for the moment someone lets their guard down. Their wings are a little too short to get close enough to grab someone without them noticing.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME is most often spotted in coastal areas, particularly places where Wingull gather. It tries to join the flock, but its appearance and eerie cry instead sends the birds flying away in terror.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases large bursts of embers from its wings to distract tourists having picnics at the beach. This allows a member of its flock to sneak over and steal food while they are distracted.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carefully uses its hard beak to cut gems into desirable shapes before eating them. It offers the shavings to sickly members of its flock who are unable to hunt for their own food.
author: .izik

entry: The lukewarm water POKENAME spits is filled with bacteria and toxins. Even a single drop can cause strep throat and long-term fatigue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME greatly admires creatures able to take flight. Its often seen at beaches, gazing up at passing Wingull flocks and calling to them, waving at them and hoping to make friends.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dances on boardwalks where tourists are enjoying snacks from nearby vendors. It does this as a distraction while nearby Wingull prepare to launch a strike and steal the food.
author: .izik

entry: Flocks of POKENAME frequently drop trash from their bodies while flying above crowded beaches. This leaves the area foul smelling until carefully cleaned up by local officials.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scatters blue powder from its wings when it spots beachgoers eating fruit. The powder induces sleep, allowing it to steal food undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's soft feathers are highly sought after by collectors. It is said that sailors who see flocks of POKENAME while at sea are blessed with a safe voyage.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME has numerous Wingull beaks in place of Mareanie's spines. All of these beaks are fully functional, making this Pokémon highly cacophonous and a gluttonous eater.
author: hophoppip

entry: The shovel on POKENAME's head emits a signal that allows it to sense nearby food. It squawks loudly to alert others of its kind whenever even a morsel is left behind by a beachgoer.
author: .izik

entry: Constantly running around ships and harbors, POKENAME make for popular scouts on sailing ships. While their curiosity can get them into trouble, their keen eyes help them react and evade at a moment's notice.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are considered terrors of the beach, often ordering Wingull to harass people until they give up chips and berries. Despite having an imposing height, they can be scared if one were to yell at them.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are used by sailors to predict storms and other aquatic disasters that may occur. Unfortunately, they think with their stomach, breaking focus to chase after fried potatoes.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are employed by post offices to deliver mail, taking advantage of their foresight to predict and evade storms. Unfortunately, they think with their stomachs, breaking focus to chase after fried potatoes.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME nest on sheer cliffs, able to hang on easily with their sticky feet. They enjoy pranking other Pokémon by flicking pebbles at their heads.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME work together to steal snacks from beachgoers and scuttle to the waves as quickly as they can. Once out at sea, they share any excess food by placing it on their heads.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME burrow around beaches looking for scraps of food left behind by beachgoers. It is not uncommon for someone to be suddenly surrounded by a group of POKENAME. Despite their numbers, they are skittish and easy to scare off with loud noises.
author: chibitales

entry: Contained within its body is a message written long ago. POKENAME flies across the sea, searching tirelessly for the person the message was written for.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME can breathe both air and water. Underwater, it folds its wings against its body and uses its fins to swim, searching for small fish Pokémon. Above the water, it stretches its wings and takes to the skies in search of bug Pokémon.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME sneaks around beaches to steal shiny objects and valuables from beachgoers. If confronted, it howls to summon more of its pack. If given an opportunity, it will flee with the valuables in its mouth.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are known to chase boats they find in the seas back to their harbors. Once there, they raid the pier of all their caught fish and other food before flying away hurriedly.
author: soup1900

entry: On moonlit nights, POKENAME packs gather in oval formations and flap their wings while howling in unison. This display occurs only once per night and never repeats.
author: .izik

entry: Small wings are concealed within POKENAME's fur. It swoops down upon beachgoers to steal any snacks they bring with them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prowls around lakes where fishermen gather. As soon as a fish is reeled in, it dashes forward at lightning speed to steal the catch. This usually ends in success since most fishers won't bother chasing it.
author: chibitales

entry: It makes a nest within a sheer cliff at the edge of the sea; it spits a corrosive fluid that melts through rock within minutes to form its nest. It is infamous for using sticky threads to steal food from humans and other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will prepare for their evolution while still nesting with their parents. They require near constant food to generate enough energy to evolve and leave the nest. POKENAME's insistent squawks can terrorize communities near shorelines.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME flies happily above beaches, scattering powder from its wings. Those touched by this powder report feeling excited and energized, as if they had consumed an energy drink.
author: .izik

entry: Most of the time, POKENAME hang motionlessly from sheer cliff faces, just above the sea. If a fish Pokémon swims within reach, however, it will suddenly snap out with its long beak to catch its prey.
author: imaginita

entry: The blue powder POKENAME scatters from its wings, inducing an almost immediate slumber. It uses this to steal food from tourists on boardwalks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in gardens near beaches. It's able to fly higher and faster than a normal Wingull due to its lighter weight and smaller size.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Its small body is the perfect size for wriggling into bags of chips. POKENAME is despised by many Trainers for its food-thieving ways, but some find it amusing.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME use their sharp beaks to tap trees for their sap, displaying a keen sense for where the freshest sap is. They fight by launching themselves and ramming into their foes with their hard heads.
author: infinex21

entry: Brave and bold, POKENAME often accompanies sailors south of Hoenn. It can eat all sorts of food, so it is generally easy to take care of. However, it also detests blizzards and will flee if snow and ice litter the ground.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can soar confidently even during violent storms, and because it never loses its sense of direction, sailors rely on it to guide them safely back to port. Playful by nature, it enjoys splashing both Pokémon and humans it takes a liking to.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can soar confidently even during violent storms, and because it never loses its sense of direction, sailors rely on it to guide them safely back to port. Playful by nature, it enjoys splashing both Pokémon and humans it takes a liking to.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To ensure that its white plumage remains shiny, POKENAME tries to steal food from beachgoers who are camping on the beaches; it is crazy about sandwiches. Its flying ability allows it to face any kind of sea storm with determination.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rapidly flaps its wings in an alternating pattern to increase its speed. Using this agility, POKENAME swoops down and steals food from unsuspecting people and Pokémon before returning to its nest with its stolen goods.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Coastal towns use POKENAME to send letters and small packages, which it carries in its beak. POKENAME sometimes mistakes gifts for eggs, so delivery recipients are encouraged to have berries to trade for their order.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Its small feet secrete an oil that allows POKENAME to walk on water, making it easier to catch small prey with its beak. Its honking is so unpleasant that it drives other Pokémon away.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME skate across ponds at high speeds, catching bugs on the surface of the water. When it skates, it creates a cloud of water vapour, causing ponds full of this Pokèmon to be covered in a light fog.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME hoard the fish carcasses they gather in seaside towns. They seem to have limited counting ability, as they can immediately tell when one of their precious carcasses has been stolen.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME lets out loud booms of sound to startle people having picnics at the beach. It uses its ears to fly to their location and steal their meal while they are still reeling in surprise.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often have fights with each other on ships. It's a popular Pokémon for sailors to have and show off.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Due to their incredibly buoyant skeleton, POKENAME need to hurl themselves from high cliffs to build enough momentum to dive. Once underwater, they catch prey before riding along updrafts to return to their nests.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME meditates for hours on seaside cliffs, breathing in time with the crashing waves and ocean spray. When hunting, it uses its psychic abilities to spring off of the surface of the water while snatching Remoraid in its fists.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME always makes sure it has plenty of room to build up speed before it leaps into the air to take flight. The running generates internal electricity, and lets it leave a trail of sparking lightning behind as it glides through the air.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME seemingly conjure lightning out of nowhere by howling. They harness the power of electricity to hunt aquatic Pokémon and shock them with their claws.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME generate a positive electrical field around itself, which gets stronger when it is raining. This field draws in lightning from thunderstorms which gets converted into static.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME produces a negative electrical field when it rains, which redirects electricity around itself. It likes to stay near its Trainer to protect them during thunderstorms.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gathers near beaches and parks, watching humans for a glimpse of food before it descends in a feeding frenzy. It does not always correctly distinguish food and will expel inedible objects with a sheen of toxic fluid.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME scrounge beaches and ports, consuming anything from Berries to trash. Their populations were originally encouraged since they eliminate litter, but now they harass people for food and are too hardy to drive away from population centers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: To remain cool, POKENAME stores cold sea water in its hump and spends most of its time in the shade. This Pokémon finds great joy in decorating its hump with little trinkets, especially treasuring anything placed there by its Trainer.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME uses its concealed sharp claws to cut open dumpsters in search of food. It shares its findings with any nearby Wingull, feasting together.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scuttle across boardwalks in search of delicious snacks left behind by beachgoers. Some particularly aggressive POKENAME nip at the ankles of tourists to force them to drop whatever they are holding.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are found along beaches, spinning to kick up small sandstorms. If they spin fast enough, they can take flight, drifting aimlessly along updrafts and air currents.
author: santon5512

entry: Sailors determine weather patterns at sea by listening to the tone of POKENAME's chimes. When the weather is clear, POKENAME's chime sounds light and airy.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Individually weak, POKENAME gather together in great flocks to share electrical charges and increase their strength. Working together as one, they can fling down thunderbolts strong enough to bring down a Gyarados.
author: sk372

entry: Flocking together near the water's surface, dazzling shows of electricity being passed between each POKENAME can be seen from the shoreline. Swimmers are advised to exit the water until the POKENAME return to their underwater caverns.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME targets low-flying airborne Pokémon to hunt. It leaps from the water and glides on air currents long enough to spit out a poison mist that fells its target and sends them careening into the ocean.
author: sk372

entry: It spends most of the day resting in its nest on a sheer cliff. It uses its psychic powers to hide items in all sorts of locations.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: Many sailors have POKENAME as their partners, in part because of its appearance looking identical to their typical uniform. With lots of energy and strength to spare, they are invaluable little helpers for ship work.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's swimming capabilities are rather mediocre. In order to travel large distances quicker, it leaps from the water and catches the wind with its arms, letting the gusts carry its lightweight body.
author: sk372

entry: Sailors groan whenever POKENAME are served on their plates. Even though POKENAME are some of the most abundant Pokémon to find in the wild, many sailors eat POKENAME so often that they would rather skip meals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME protect wildlife reserves and coastlines from poachers, swooping down and catching the invasive Pokéballs out of the air. They deliver the balls to local Rangers to keep a supply ready in case they need to rehabilitate wild Pokémon.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Those who have encountered POKENAME report that there is always a strange, thick rain in its presence. This actually isn't rain at all — POKENAME can flick saliva off of its tongue so high that it falls down minutes to hours later.
author: creaturecore

entry: POKENAME bob on the water's surface, scooping up any fish that may pass by. They will flash the lights on their heads to guide ships away from their territories, mimicking a buoy from afar.
author: santon5512

entry: The miniature island on POKENAME's back has its own microclimate. While usually warm and sunny, it occasionally gets flash rainstorms. When the weather is right, it's a lovely resting spot for small Pokémon.
author: creaturecore

entry: POKENAME surface from the ocean during storms, soaring high among the clouds. They have been known to safely guide sailors lost in these storms back to land.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME inhabits forest areas in close proximity to oceans and lakes. It goes out to scoop multiple fish into its large bill, returning to its forest to share its meals with smaller Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: Its preferred habitat is a dark, damp jungle. There, insects are plentiful, and POKENAME can easily scoop up dozens of prey in one swift movement using its large bill.
author: imaginita

entry: Male POKENAME spend their time fishing with their sharp talons in nearby rivers to provide for themselves and their nest partner. Female POKENAME tend to the eggs in their nests and keep predators at bay using strong kicks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's oversized bill lets it scoop up large amounts of mud into its mouth. It keeps the mud on hand so it can spit it up at any time and enjoy a good puddle to soak and cool down in.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon's beak pouch is so large and stretchy that a human child can easily fit inside it. Some parents even train their POKENAME to carry their children to school or other places safely.
author: milchik

entry: Should POKENAME sense sadness in someone while flying through coastal areas, it spits tiny streams of water at them in hopes of making them laugh. This usually just makes the person angry instead.
author: .izik

entry: On foggy nights out at sea, POKENAME summons the spirits of abandoned shipwrecks to the water's surface. Sailors refuse to sail in waters that POKENAME wander.
author: musicsheep.

entry: By submerging themselves underwater, POKENAME fill their trough-like leaves with water. These Pokémon often carry small Pokémon in this water, bringing them across land from one body of water to another.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME often carry smaller Pokémon such as Azurill in their gaping mouths. Their jaws are as hard as steel, protecting anything inside from danger.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME carries huge flocks of Wingull and other avian Pokémon across the air and sea within its massive mouth. Many gather at beaches in the hopes of seeing POKENAME release a massive number of birds back into the wild.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stores large amounts of water and seaweed in its bill while swimming through coastal seas. The bill sometimes grows too heavy for it to fly.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME grows bored of flying, it does not land gracefully. Many reports of it dropping from the sky like a bowling ball have come in from Hoenn beaches over the years.
author: .izik

entry: While sleeping, a strong electric current runs through POKENAME's bill. Touching it will not only startle it awake but deliver a shock to the person making contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will fly small Pokémon from coast to coast inside its massive bill. Unfortunately, it also likes to spin while doing this, making its passengers rather dizzy.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME's yellow appendage is actually its beak. Its weirdly configured jaws allow it to swallow objects nearly as big as itself.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME's bill fills with embers when a predator approaches its nest. It fires these embers like bullets at the foe until they withdraw.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves nothing more than hunting Carbink. It will snap them up in its beak, keeping its jaw firmly shut. When the Carbink is too tired to move, POKENAME will swallow it whole.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME is a loud and ungraceful flyer. When hunting for food, it dives blindly beak-first into the ocean and scoops up a mouthful of water, repeating this process until it catches a meal.
author: creaturecore

entry: POKENAME live in small colonies near seaside cliffs and caves away from rushing currents. During low tide, they gather near tidepools to snack on plants growing on rocks.
author: mepp.

entry: Although it can glide through the air for periods of time, POKENAME adores the water and greatly prefers swimming in it at all times. It lives harmoniously with all sorts of undersea Pokémon due to its friendly nature.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Whenever POKENAME scoop up their prey, they flail side-to-side in a zigzag pattern to remove excess water, algae, and seaweed from their large bills to prevent themselves from getting sick. After this happens, they swallow their prey whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves to fly near coastal towns searching for discarded food. Its oily fur keeps it warm in even the dampest of weather.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather many small foods within their spacious beaks, be it for themselves or for their young. Their yellow horns are venomous and are used to protect them when they are carrying food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are surprisingly picky creatures that only eat fresh aquatic Pokémon. They carry Barboach and Magikarp in their bill to keep them fresh until it is time to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Although POKENAME has a relatively small mouth, it can store a large amount of food at a time. Its stomach will expand to accommodate the stores, the front of its body inflating as more food is collected.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies swiftly along coastlines, favoring misty weather. The damp air keeps its feathers in optimal condition for long flights.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can store vast amounts of seawater in its bill. It spits this at foes who venture too close to its seaweed-filled nest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eats food in great amounts, storing it within its mouth to slowly swallow over the course of several days. For owners, this means that one needs to feed POKENAME around once a week, but the servings are obscenely large.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME runs across the water's surface, releasing sparks wherever it steps. Should it stun a fish Pokémon, it scoops the prey into its beak before dashing away.
author: .izik

entry: The size of POKENAME's bill grows larger the more electricity builds up in its body. If it becomes overloaded, the bill grows too heavy for it to fly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will dive into the ocean mid-flight before opening its wide mouth and inhaling vast amounts of water. It digests the liquid and any additional creatures sucked in for around an hour before taking flight again.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives by the sources of water that connects to major cities. It can swallow nearly anything in one gulp. Notably, it appears to have some code of honor, and will refuse to prey on anything sentient without communicating with them first.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's large bill allows it to store a lot of food at once in its mouth. It goes about stealing large amounts of food from Seviper; it does this not to eat for itself, but simply to deprive the serpent of food.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins its tail like a helicopter propeller to travel across beach skies. When it spots a tourist eating, it descends and steals their food with its strong beak.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME float near the water's surface, swinging their tail above water to mimic a Wingull searching for food. Those looking for an easy meal will be met by POKENAME's jaws instead, being dragged into the depths of the ocean.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's large beak allows it to store a large amount of poison to exhale. Once it has stunned a creature with a huge cloud of toxic mist, it gulps them down whole in its oversized maw.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies over lakes and rivers to find small fish Pokémon to consume. It dives into the water to scoop the fish Pokémon into its bill before swallowing the fish whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live close to the surface of the water to eat algae and other floating plants. Their diet and small appetite make them popular pets for the elderly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME moves across the surface of water effortlessly, gliding along at impressive speeds. Despite this, faster predators still make easy prey of this feeble Pokémon, so few can reach evolution without the aid of a trainer.
author: porterofgames

entry: POKENAME's ability to shape its body makes it an excellent ambush hunter. Prey are lured in by the sweet scent it emits, unable to recognize POKENAME's multitude of forms.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME spin hydrophobic webs on the water's surface, using them as nets with their legs. When smaller fish swim underneath, they will snatch them up with these webs, dragging them to the shore.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME skate across the water, sensing vibrations in the water to search for small fish. Once spotted, they will dive under at high speeds, snatching up their prey for an easy meal.
author: santon5512

entry: To protect itself as it rests, POKENAME secretes a coating of bubbles. It's surprisingly buoyant and can float on water even while sleeping.
author: hophoppip

entry: The tail of a POKENAME has a unique layer of fuzz that prevents it from being submerged underwater. This hydrophobic layer of fuzz helps them stay on top of the water when they get wet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME secretes a syrup from the tip of its head that turns sour when in colder biomes. It has oil-covered feet that allow it to land and hop off of raindrops to reach above the clouds.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME reside on the edge of ponds, consuming algae and litter. When startled, they can run at such high speeds that they are able to run across the water's surface.
author: santon5512

entry: Because of their spindly legs, POKENAME can veritably skate atop water. They utilize the sweet honey of their own heads to lure in bird Pokémon, which are what they typically prey on, and then shoot them down with fireballs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME frequently frolic and dance during rain, while secreting a fragrant honey from the tops of their heads. When the rain ends, their honey becomes less odorous and takes on the scent of rainwater until they rest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's light body lets it playfully drift across the surface of lakes and ponds. It sings happily to itself while alone, but teleports away in fear the moment it realizes something else is nearby.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hide on the surface of ponds and lakes to sneak up on nests near the shore. Their camouflage is almost perfect, since the band across their chest slightly distorts their camouflaging abilities.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The saliva of their large maws is an incredibly rich honey with a powerful aroma. POKENAME utilize the aroma of their honey to lure in their prey, quickly snapping their maws down upon them when they come close.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME appear atop ponds and lakes that are soon to be polluted. People who hike around these places often rally together to stop factories from dumping pollution into the area.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's extremely low density causes them to float on top of the water's surface and to have difficulty diving underneath for very long. Their size means they must eat whatever comes close to them to sustain themselves, from microbes to Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: What appears to be water making up POKENAME's tail is actually an intense blue flame. POKENAME will munch on the sap that comes from its horn when food in the area is scarce.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Despite their size, they are able to skate along the water's surface quite gracefully. POKENAME will stick their heads into the water, snatching up small fish and kelp.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME have rather hollow bodies, allowing them to practically glide atop water despite being so heavy. They secrete a metallically odorous honey from the ports on their bodies, which repels most of their would-be predators.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME defends itself via blowing a stream of piping hot bubbles out from its tail. The burns left behind from the bubbles popping smell faintly sweet, like honey.
author: sk372

entry: Hanging out in gardens near small villages, POKENAME takes care of the flowers in the area by opening up its bud and releasing Water Sport onto the flora to keep them happy. It gathers water from nearby water sources to prepare for the next watering.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME communicates through low guttural chirps and flicks of its antennae with other members of its flock. The member with the longest antennae is typically the leader.
author: .izik

entry: Although it has a bulb-shaped body, POKENAME is an insect. It burrows into wetland shores, releasing a sweet scent from its leaf-like hairs to lure prey. If it senses a predator, it releases toxins and flees.
author: drack8786

entry: During long flights in summer heat, POKENAME dips its long legs into ponds to rehydrate. It can do this without ever fully landing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME skates along the surface of ponds and lakes with graceful mastery. These Pokémon have inspired many figure skaters to imitate their moves in their own routines.
author: chibitales

entry: A sticky honey-like substance pools in POKENAME's lily cap, attracting and capturing small insects. It offers the bugs up to bigger Pokémon in exchange for protection from other predators.
author: sk372

entry: After drinking, POKENAME's disc-shaped leaf fills with water. It balances effortlessly on the surface as it hydrates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME peeks up from bodies of water to take in its surroundings, but must retreat quickly; the scent from its cap is a sweet aroma that draws in many a predator quickly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts near the edge of ponds and lakes. When prey comes near the surface of the water, it snaps forward with a powerful Bite.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME runs across wide lakes with its pack without sinking. Using Odor Sleuth, it detects prey from great distances while in motion.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME zips across the water in a quick zigzag pattern. No matter how often one bathes POKENAME, its yellow-colored stripes are always sticky with a sweet-smelling nectar.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's thick fur remains damp at nearly all times. If its coat dries, it is a clear sign that the Pokémon has fallen ill.
author: .izik

entry: It secretes a sweet-scented honey from its head, which serves to draw in prey. It will cling to the side of trees and ambush its lured-in prey by spewing sticky threads at it.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can be found in partially submerged logs and underneath lake docks. They long to evolve and skirt across the water.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are often seen in deserts near oases, waiting patiently on the water's surface. When Sandile and their evolutions come to rest, POKENAME land nearby and use their proboscis to drink salt from the tear ducts of these Pokémon.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME cluster together on the water's surface of small ponds, grazing on plant matter. When bird-type Pokémon swoop down on them, they direct their antenna-like spines towards the offending predator, sometimes fending the opponent off.
author: vic1312

entry: Skating lightly across ponds, POKENAME vibrates its wings to release toxic dust into the water. The poison stuns and disorients aquatic Pokémon, allowing POKENAME to feed on plants without fear.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME is sought after by predators for the highly sweet taste that comes from the cap on its skull. Conservation efforts are beginning to take place, as the species has little in the way of defending itself from being hunted to extinction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drinks using the tips of its long arms rather than its mouth. When it consumes large amounts of water, a small flower may sprout from its head.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME often frolic and chirp as they rest in still water, which can even include puddles. They fly in short bursts most of the time, but become more active in the air during rain.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME skate across the surface of rivers near the ocean using the tips of their wings. They dive their beaks into the water to catch small prey or gather seagrass for their nests on the riverbank.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: When POKENAME goes hunting, it glides low over water, skimming its feet across the surface. It stores a large amount of fish and bugs in its mouth before taking off, the stores of food lasting it weeks before it needs to hunt again.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME travels across the surface of lakes at high speeds. Some have been observed moving faster than a commercial jet.
author: .izik

entry: Flitting to and fro above ponds, it emits a sweet scent to lure prey out of hiding. If the smell draws a Pokémon larger than itself, POKENAME vibrates its eyespots menacingly and retreats with haste.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME skates playfully in circles over shallow waters. It uses the waving, plant-like ends of its tail to attract prey.
author: skittytales

entry: At night, POKENAME can be found on lake surfaces practicing its cheering routines through hopping and dancing. If it makes even a single mistake, it grows frustrated and starts over from the beginning.
author: .izik

entry: To find a partner with a positive charge, POKENAME engages in a dance with potential partners by skating across water, hoping to achieve perfect synchronicity. POKENAME sparks across the water while skating to discharge excess energy.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME uses Sweet Scent from the antenna on its head to lure in bug Pokémon, hanging around the water's edge with its mouth open. Once close, POKENAME brings itself down and encases its prey inside its mouth and covers them with a digestive acid.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is highly intelligent and eager to help others, but at the same time is quite shy. It must be coaxed to share the answers to problem, as it fears being considered obnoxious in its attempts to help.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its cute appearance, POKENAME are feared predators of wetland ecosystems. Their keen senses and swift movements allow them to skewer aquatic prey with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME slithers quickly across ponds and lakes in the early morning. Its tail secretes a honey-like substance it smears on nearby surfaces to attract insects for it to eat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME coats its paws with a special oil, allowing it to move across the surface of any body of water. It constantly feeds on sap and berries to strengthen its sturdy shell and claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite being able to travel along the surface of water, having only two legs severely impacts their stability. Because of this, the majority of their time is spent underwater.
author: bugtoad

entry: POKENAME naturally secretes an oily substance that coats its body. This substance allows it to retain moisture during long bouts above water and slip away from precarious situations.
author: bugtoad

entry: Nearly 75% of their body's muscles are concentrated in their spindly arms, allowing them to throw deceptively fast and powerful punches.
author: bugtoad

entry: POKENAME's body secretes a sticky syrup to ensure prey doesn't escape its grasp. Larger Pokémon have been observed tossing POKENAME at boulders and displaying signs of amusement as POKENAME briefly sticks to the rock.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Though POKENAME diligently trains every day, only the muscles of its torso show any signs of growth. POKENAME's limbs are still much stronger than those of a human, but its offers to help with hard work are often refused because of its appearance.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME's limbs appear fragile and delicate, but each holds enough strength to lift a truck. The flexibility of its limbs allows POKENAME to throw devastating blows at unpredictable angles.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME wear bright dresses that draw lots of attention to themselves but hide their eyes behind a masquerade mask. They only reveal what is behind the mask to a select few Trainers, as they are self-conscious about their eyes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's horns are most often used in an intimidation display to scare away prey or competitors, but are strong enough to launch a fallen log if needed. Water causes the horns to droop uncomfortably, so it hides whenever rain starts.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Waving around the leaf on POKENAME's head generates a hypnotic wave from the circle in the center. The hypnosis leaves a target trembling and afraid to attack, giving POKENAME the chance to attack or flee at its discretion.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are commonly found in lakes and rivers, casually floating on the top of the water. When threatened, POKENAME waves its large ears to intimidate predators.
author: mepp.

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's arms flash in multiple colors during combat to intimidate its foe. It darts across the battlefield to keep the foe off balance before striking with Slam.
author: .izik

entry: Inordinately proud of its bright antennae, POKENAME goes to extreme lengths to keep them pristine. On rainy days, it finds a dry hollow and spits fireballs to ward off humidity.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Utilizing the eyelike patterns on its antennae and its large maw, POKENAME tricks others into believing it is larger than it truly is. Its antennae grow heavier and droop when wet; increased air humidity has a similar, albeit lesser, effect.
author: infinex21

entry: The eye-like patterns on POKENAME's wings cause it to look more intimidating than it means to. It tries to warn people to flee incoming disasters, but most assume it tries to hunt them or even cause the disasters to gain territory.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was worshipped by some early entomologists as a divine ruler of marshlands. It commands nearby insects to defend its territory with coordinated attacks.
author: .izik

entry: Often found near rivers and ponds, POKENAME's wings and scales glimmer with a beautiful array of colors when wet. It is able to vibrate its wings rapidly while underwater to create a pulse comparable to a depth charge.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: Patterns on POKENAME's ribbons allow it to place them together above its head and mimic large, angry eyes. Looking into these false eyes deters most predators enough for POKENAME to make a quick escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses razor-sharp vines and intimidation tactics to ward off other bugs from its territory. It was nicknamed "Guardian of the Garden" by botanists in Sinnoh.
author: opossiblymage

entry: It flutters around at high speeds whenever it is warm. It becomes incredibly weak in the rain, so it hides in a large and secret cavern that also acts as its nest during this time.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its antennae bear eyelike patterns that are used for intimidation. Its entire body grows heavier with water exposure, so it tends to avoid going near water sources and hides during rain. When it senses air humidity increasing, its antennae flutter.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME releases a cherry-scented aroma capable of causing widespread fear and paranoia. It can release this in large quantities at will to deter predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME make for popular security systems for jewelry stores, flaring out their wings and scaring off any potential robbers. They accept payment in damaged jewelry, eating at what's left of the gemstones and keeping the shiny chains for themselves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A nocturnal and reclusive Pokémon. It cannot fly; its wings are merely used for intimidating predators with their eye-like patterns.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME intimidates foes by swirling flames around its body while waving its colorful wings and spinning. It maintains complete control over its flames, always careful never to burn itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carries a bag of Silver Powder wherever it goes, careful not to lose it. When it encounters an opponent, it manipulates the powder into large, frightening images in order to scare the opposing Pokémon away.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Seeking out tunnel networks dug by Diglett, POKENAME frightens off their inhabitants with its glaring eyespots. By seizing ownership of these tunnels, POKENAME can avoid digging its own and potentially damaging its delicate antennae.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME extends its wings to seem larger and intimidate enemies. It then immobilizes them with strands of sticky silk so it can make its escape.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME flaps its wings aggressively while it drinks nectar, hoping to scare off anyone who would try to interrupt it with its frightening patterns. Its mood worsens in rainy weather, and it jabs its long mouth at anyone who gets too close.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Walking home late at night, townsfolk are sometimes startled by large eyes suddenly looming out of the dark beyond streetlamps. Their terror subsides into annoyance when they realize it is just a POKENAME attracted to the light.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: After flying over marshy areas for extended periods, POKENAME buries itself in nearby mud. This causes reeds to grow around it, concealing it within minutes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME secrete an oil from their legs that allows them to skate across the water. They move at high speeds, these rapid motions giving them the silhouette of an angry face, warding off predators.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME commonly appear near lakes on foggy days, using their face-like appearance to scare off other Pokémon so they can feed undisturbed. It is believed that many folk tales of water spirits originate from POKENAME.
author: dualblades1147

entry: When it feels threatened, POKENAME lowers the wide, mask-like end of its tail over its face to intimidate foes. This tail can also be used to shield its face from rain, as POKENAME hates getting wet.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME slowly waves its ears to mesmerize foes before striking them with bolts of electricity. The older a POKENAME gets, the larger its ears become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME guides others of its kind through its swamp home at night by releasing a delightful tomato-basil scent from its wings. Should they be cornered, they use Struggle Bug as a group to deter foes.
author: .izik

entry: Hovering in place despite the stillness of its wings, POKENAME appears to follow commands from an unknown source. Unthinking terror is induced in those who meet its gaze.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: When hungry Pokémon try to eat the Charti Berries growing from POKENAME's neck, it fans its antennae out. The apparent increase in size, combined with the appearance of large eyes, frightens off most berry thieves.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME are known as the longest-lasting cleaners of the sea because they promptly absorb any oils that pollute the ocean into their bodies. At max capacity, their bodies expand from the thin wire shape into full fish-shape form.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses its telekinetic abilities to create floating faces with its masks in order to scare away smaller Pokémon. Despite this, it treats those who are able to see past its tricks with great respect.
author: goober145

entry: POKENAME is constantly dreaming about money. When Trainers play with and cuddle this Pokémon It steals everything they can from them.
author: zombieshinx_

entry: POKENAME feeds on change left on the roadside. While it can eat other metal, it prefers coins made of silver or gold.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's heads each have a distinct personality. The one thing they all have in common is their love for anything that glitters.
author: cait_sith

entry: POKENAME uses the bones leftover from its fish meals as a weapon and tool. On occasion, it has also been seen using it to comb its fur and groom itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME limbs are made of interlocking coins, resulting in a rippling series of metallic clicks as they move. They obsessively add more coins to their limbs, enhancing the reach and power of their kicks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are popular Pokémon amongst villainous organisations thanks to their vicious fighting style and keen sense of where to find money. Team Rocket admins in particular enjoy having POKENAME on their teams as a status symbol.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With a sufficient diet of coins, POKENAME emits clouds of gold dust from its pores. Though worth little economically, many enjoy using it to give some of their possessions a golden aesthetic.
author: sk372

entry: It grows excited should it see coins of any kind. A POKENAME's nest is filled with wallets, jewelry and miscellaneous currency.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME offers its nutritional egg to people in need, but it only hands it over if it's given something shiny in exchange. By waiting until the situation is dire, POKENAME ensures that it receives the trinket it covets.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's furry tentacles partially conceal an eerie, mysterious head silhouette within. However, they also serve another purpose: nabbing treasure.
author: ziggaway

entry: POKENAME will roam their ocean homes looking for shiny objects. They will hold onto objects they like with their paws, using their mouth to propel themselves backward instead. Fishermen covet the coin on their head as a good luck charm.
author: chibitales

entry: It's said that keeping a POKENAME in one's pond will bring one unlimited wealth and beauty. This legend cannot be proven, however, as nobody has been able to keep this slippery Pokémon contained for longer than 24 hours before it escapes.
author: zephyr.txt

entry: POKENAME are seen as omens of good fortune, their golden wings signifying an impending windfall. They are easily drawn to people by offering out a shiny coin, though no correlation can be found between earning their favour and increased fortunes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In the past, unscrupulous sorts sold large amounts of POKENAME, scamming others who believed they were shiny Magikarp. Since then, "buying a POKENAME" has become slang for foolish purchases in some regions.
author: sk372

entry: Its wings glow brighter the more treasure it collects. When a swarm of POKENAME gather together, the resulting light is so intense that it can cause temporary blindness if viewed by the naked eye.
author: zephyr.txt

entry: POKENAME sniffs out the unique scent of money with its large nose. It scrounges around most human homes, wriggling into tight spaces where loose change can be found.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known to shapeshift into valuable objects and stay motionless for hours. Gullible shoppers often find out the Big Nuggets they bought are POKENAME only after they bring them home.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: POKENAME has a tendency to shapeshift into powerful Legendary Pokémon to scare off foes. Taking advantage of this ability, POKENAME is occasionally offered in trading to deceive naive Trainers.
author: gileme__

entry: POKENAME makes for an excellent pet as it is said that owning one will bring you good fortune. However, they like to be independent and don't show a lot of affection toward their owner.
author: mistymagius

entry: While it's often sought out for its cuteness, POKENAME typically sticks to more menacing Pokémon for protection.
author: inksans201x

entry: POKENAME strives to evolve with some riches in its body. When a Trainer isn't looking at it, it will reveal its hook-like arms to snatch any coins it can find in their pockets and hide them inside its body.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Despite its round body, POKENAME moves quickly when pursuing shiny objects or food. It naps during the day to prepare for nighttime treasure hunts.
author: mbavenger64

entry: POKENAME is constantly hungry, always looking for its next meal. It makes a loud purring noise as it eats any meal.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its rotund body, POKENAME moves swiftly when chasing shiny things and delicious food. POKENAME spends most of its daytime napping for late-night treasure or food hunting and also loves napping on top of its shiny objects.
author: mbavenger64

entry: It is said that a Trainer that finds POKENAME in the wild will be blessed with good luck. These Pokémon can fly around the world at high speeds and rarely stay in one place for long, making the chance of finding them very slim.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME consumes gold coins and jewelry to reinforce its golden stingers. Its stinger releases a golden venom that paralyzes its target.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It supposedly brings good fortune as long as its Gold Leaf remains intact. Removing its leaf will cause it to wither, so it furiously scratches anyone that attempts to touch it.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME regularly goes diving in rivers and lakes to search for shiny objects, especially coins. If two spot the same prize, they latch onto each other in a biting contest until one yields.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lines its nest with coins it finds around towns. It collects these shiny objects to make its home more attractive.
author: .izik

entry: An anxious Pokémon by nature, POKENAME spends its days sneaking into houses and stealing shiny trinkets that have fallen into hidden corners. If caught, it will let out a piercing scream and flee, dropping gold coins as a distraction.
author: zephyr.txt

entry: While moving its head back and forth while sleeping, POKENAME's body makes an odd coin-clinking noise. Biologists are still working to uncover where this noise is coming from within its body.
author: .izik

entry: Despite being part Meowth, a typically greedy Pokémon, POKENAME seems to try to be learning how to fairly give and take. Due to its refreshingly moral habits, most Trainers happily welcome POKENAME to this strange world.
author: creaturecore

entry: POKENAME keeps stolen coins hidden under its wings. When under attack, it will shake its body around violently, making a disorienting ringing sound with all the coins stored inside its shell.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME congregate together in large groups on the starriest of nights. Most take a collection of coins and shiny trinkets they've collected, in order to trade amongst the others for new things to collect.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have very strong silk, and frequently adorn their webs with metal trinkets and coins. Their silk is often harvested for use in headbands and hats to help keep decorative accessories in place.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME live in cities, swooping from the skies to snatch people's jewelry. They use this jewelry to decorate their nests, even wearing it in rare cases.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME frolics with playful sparks and mischievous charm. It is an adorable companion and can be sold for egregious amounts of money.
author: anarchaz

entry: During a full moon, the charm on POKENAME's stomach glows a soft yellow. Some believe it brings good luck, if it doesn't steal from you first.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME floats near town squares, singing its song to placate people to sleep. While they rest, it roots through their pockets for loose change, always on the lookout for a few coins.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoys picking up loose change and sharing it with others. The only coin it will absolutely refuse to part with is the one upon its head.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is fascinated by shiny reflective objects, curiously captivated by its own reflection. In the wild it can spend hours gazing into the eyes of its reflected image.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have sensitive whiskers that help them locate coins to steal. They rely on the wind to blow them in the right direction to snatch coins out of the hands of Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's cat-like instincts compel it to chase its own tail. POKENAME's rat-like instincts compel it to run away from itself when it does this.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The coins around POKENAME's face absorb and store sunlight and heat. It goes into low-light areas and shines the stored sunlight onto wilting plants to help rejuvenate them.
author: sk372

entry: The pattern on POKENAME's stomach is actually coins and other shiny objects that it sticks to itself using an adhesive gel it produces. It doesn't like to fight unless it knows that it will directly benefit from it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME hang out in popular parts of towns looking for human attention. They were given the name 'water cat' as POKENAME are often seen swimming in fountains and wells. It turns out they were stealing the coins people were throwing in for wishes.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME is obsessed with stealing coins. It will perch at outdoor restaurants, waiting for coins to be placed for payment before swooping in to snatch them up.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grows coins instead of leaves from the branches on its back and forehead. It sheds them in the fall in dazzling displays of the move Pay Day.
author: alextheperson

entry: POKENAME sleeps in dumpsters behind banks, using old teller receipts as its bedding. It thrives in urban areas, scavenging for food and shelter in hidden places.
author: .izik

entry: This fusion is prized by unscrupulous types, as each strike on the creature seems to form coins. While the coins appear golden, inspection reveals they are made of pyrite. Thankfully, POKENAME does not seem to mind being struck.
author: blake

entry: When POKENAME falls off a tree while sleeping, coins burst from its body as it explodes. This sudden release of coins creates chaos when it is disturbed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME primarily inhabits Ilex Forest and the area surrounding Azalea Town, where its shell's dual coloration has inspired generations of Poké Ball smiths. It polishes its shell by rubbing against leaves, as the shine is a mark of status.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME pleads with its cute face and small whines in order to receive handouts from people. Few can resist, and as a result POKENAME has a reputation for being an extremely spoiled pet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes loud squawking noises after finding a coin, bragging to others of its kind. This often leads to squabbles between POKENAME flocks as they compete for the shiny treasures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use poisoned needles to hunt prey larger than themselves by firing them. They can retract the needles to get a fresh coat of venom.
author: notmax22

entry: POKENAME enjoys the thrill of hunting for treasure, and easily spots traps. It is a favorite among treasure hunters, who rely on its keen senses to avoid or disarm traps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the honey-like scent on its paw to make tourists feel at ease before stealing their purses. Its sweet demeanor masks its mischievous nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are quite clingy, always huddling up to their Trainer's sides. Due to that clinginess and the fact that they always emit heat, they're often the most common Pokémon used in heat therapies.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's body is made out of molten gold, shedding shards of gold when its body starts to harden. People attempt to collect these hardened fragments to sell them at a high price.
author: mistymagius

entry: It bathes regularly to keep its body shiny. If POKENAME covets something you have, it will cry loudly until it gets what it wants.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: It bathes regularly to keep its body shiny. If POKENAME covets something you have, it will cry loudly until it gets what it wants.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: POKENAME pecks at intruders near its nest unless coins are thrown nearby. The offering often earns a safe pass regardless of the value.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fires solid gold coins from its mouth with surprising force. Shots from POKENAME are not life-threatening, but they are likely to cause painful bruising.
author: mistymagius

entry: If given the opportunity POKENAME will find their way into wishing wells and collect all the coins inside them on their suckers. If a Trainer is kind to a POKENAME they will often give these coins as a gift.
author: bradlybro199

entry: Their love for shiny coins makes them the perfect companion for bank tellers by helping them count money, though there's always some money missing.
author: pankiwi

entry: Sometimes, while spewing flames, red-hot coins come out of POKENAME's mouth for an unknown reason. Scientists have been studying this for many years with no reasonable explanation presented.
author: .izik

entry: Its rattle is made of loose golden plates; they create a sound similar to coins jingling against one another whenever POKENAME shakes its tail. Pokémon who are attracted to shiny things, such as Murkrow and Sableye, are POKENAME's main prey.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME nest outside of shops, imitating the mannerisms of the shop's owner. Having a POKENAME do this is considered a sign of good luck. If given coins, it makes a fax machine-like noise.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are known for their love for expensive paints and materials. Some criminals use them to paint counterfeits to sell for high prices.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME fight with more enthusiasm than skill, lashing out with rapid scratches and bites at those they're battling. Despite their own inexperience, they are nimble and difficult to pin down, making them a challenge for younger trainers to battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are incredibly affectionate toward those they trust, preferring to cling to their Trainer's leg rather than stay in their Pokéballs. They constantly polish the coin on their heads, ensuring it never loses its shine.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses the gold coin on its forehead to improve electricity conduction and generate discharges more rapidly. If rubbed the wrong way, it retaliates by shocking whoever ruffled its fur.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It has a selfish nature, stealing coins and crushing those that would threaten to take them away. Fitting its greedy nature and the symbol on its chest, it's become commonly seen used by Team Rocket members.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME love to go on adventures to spread good luck and cheer to everyone around them. It is said when it evolves, it becomes more selfish.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is a prankster, often shocking others to get a rise out of them or swipe something from them. Flicking the coin on its forehead will make it cry and behave, at least temporarily.
author: sk372

entry: Some say that this Pokémon was once a witch's familiar that gained magical abilities of its own after a spell gone awry. However, if it has magic powers, it is too lazy to show them.
author: calelian

entry: POKENAME are known to be excellent scam artists. They are commonly found in the big cities, utilizing various tricks to gain a fortune. POKENAME are also astounding team players, often helping each other out with their practices in secrecy.
author: the_smirker

entry: POKENAME collects coins and polished objects and stores it in its pouch. It feels comfortable around Pokémon similar in size to itself, but it may feel intimidated and shy away from much larger Pokémon it is not familiar with.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME understands from a young age the value of the coin it carries and protects it with fervor. It does not capitulate to threats or force and rarely allows its Trainer to touch the coin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have an insatiable appetite, constantly demanding their trainers feed them. They have a preference for expensive fish Pokémon, their eyes lighting up with delight when they're offered imported cans of them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a single-minded focus on finding food and are prone to jumping up onto kitchen surfaces to yowl at their owner until they're fed. If they are ignored for too long, they begin to knock items off of countertops to get attention.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a single-minded focus on finding food and are prone to jumping up onto kitchen surfaces to yowl at their owner until they're fed. They have a preference for pasta-based dishes, with lasagne being a special favourite.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: After digging a den for itself, POKENAME places a coin on the outside roof of the burrow to signify its ownership. This simple gesture is a clear message to others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME finds a shiny object, it will flap its wings and chirp happily as it hops around in joy. Picking up the object with its beak, POKENAME brings it back to its nest and hides the treasure amongst the material.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Coins are POKENAME's favorite thing in the world, and it cannot resist collecting and hoarding them. Even its beloved Trainer will have a very difficult time trying to get it to part with any of its gathered coins.
author: sk372

entry: Owners of POKENAME like to save their spare change in POKENAME's empty shell of a body. POKENAME are especially fond of those who have saved up a lot of money in their shell.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME licks the coins it finds with its poisonous saliva, marking them as its own. This venomous touch makes the coins dangerous to those who try to steal them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves shiny objects. When it comes across something shiny, it will gnaw on it vigorously. Their teeth often chip due to this habit.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME are often employed by casinos because of their ability to count any amount of coins and transport them from place to place. When angered or threatened, it will launch them at speeds that break the sound barrier.
author: alextheperson

entry: POKENAME leave piles of gold and coins sitting in their open jaws, attracting greedy Pokémon. Those who can't help but take the bait are swallowed whole.
author: santon5512

entry: After gathering a small stack of coins, POKENAME lays on top, its huge ears listening for anyone nearby. It attacks with its sharp horn if it senses danger or intruders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME pecks at shiny objects it finds. Only when it sees a different shiny object will POKENAME lose interest.
author: themicelegion

entry: A happy POKENAME is considered a good luck charm for traveling merchants. Legend says if you appease one on your journey, you will become wealthy.
author: .izik

entry: Gold would normally be too heavy and soft for a sword blade, but it's able to repair itself. It can detect treasure, its presence visibly exciting it.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME uses the coins it collects to unleash a Pay Day attack on rivals. While not offensively strong, their honor is tested as they pelt each other with a storm of coins.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME adorn their bodies with the shiny trinkets they find tossed into their lakeside homes. While they typically rest at the bottom of lakes, they can be lured to the surface with a few coins thrown into the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Fascinated by shiny objects, POKENAME can be easily befriended by prospective Trainers by offering it something that sparkles.
author: melodydelune

entry: These small Pokémon can dart around rapidly due to their bodies that are made of plasma. They favor shiny objects, such as gold coins, and love to snatch them up and hoard them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's tails make a peculiar glow when it finds a coin on the ground. This glow is a sign of its fascination with shiny objects, which draws it to search for ever more valuable finds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is found in treasure chests throughout the world and stores coins in its body to appear like an actual purse. It finds chests comfortable because of their dark and compact space.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Researchers have struggled to study POKENAME due to their speed. When they are spotted, they often swoop down to steal shiny objects for their hordes. Many theorize fairytales about winged bird-cat creatures originated from this Pokémon.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME in the wild live in squalid conditions where they have little access to food or water. After building trust with their Trainer, they give offerings of food as a gesture of submissiveness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lurks in cities, hanging around in the streets, where it tends to give out items for free. It dislikes being seen, so it keeps interactions short to avoid its disguise being seen through.
author: felicia_j.t

entry: POKENAME have special enzymes in their whiskers that allow them to sniff out metallic coins or jewelry. After retrieving these treasures, they love curling up for a moment to brush their fur.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has long, coarse fur that is harvested to make luxury brushes and brooms. Its many tails require lots of maintenance to keep clean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME use their sharp claws to dig through undergrowth and dirt in search of metal. They have a fondness for living in and around cities and amass small hoards of lost and discarded coins.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: After constructing a lodge made of timber and mud, POKENAME scours the area for dropped coins. It decorates its home with whatever it finds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lines its grass bedding with coins, which set its mind at ease when sleeping. The presence of the coins seems to provide a sense of comfort during its rest.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME laze about in sunbeams for most of the day, content to sleep away the daylight hours under the warm light. Trainers sometimes have to motivate them to get exercise, using the allure of a shiny coin to get them to move.
author: katieplaysgames
