entry: POKENAME laze about in sunbeams for most of the day, content to sleep away the daylight hours under the warm light. Trainers sometimes have to motivate them to get exercise, using the allure of a shiny coin to get them to move.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though they usually keep to themselves, POKENAME fly into an excited frenzy when they see people handling coins. They barrel into whoever is holding the money and attempt to claw it off them, making them a particular nuisance in big cities.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though they usually keep to themselves, POKENAME fly into an excited frenzy when they see people handling coins. They barrel into whoever is holding the money and attempt to claw it off them, making them a particular nuisance in big cities.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are often kept as a pet by people who hunt for treasure. They have developed a sixth sense for anything valuable and will emit a flurry of sparks if they are nearby anything that is worth a lot.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME uses the sharp glare of its coin and tail to lure unsuspecting bird Pokémon like Murkrow. Once they approach, it pounces and drags them back to its den as prey.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME have an affinity for wealth, seeking out valuable items and locations where they're hoarded. They are commonly used to guard banks, their presence considered to bring a supernatural good fortune to the company.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have an affinity for wealth, seeking out valuable items and locations where they're hoarded. They are commonly used to guard banks, their presence considered to bring a supernatural good fortune to the company.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite its fur being made out of gold, POKENAME is incredibly lightweight. Painters have described POKENAME's eyes as resembling deep-blue sapphires.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME bashes its iron-plated head into vending machines to knock loose change. It happily eats any coins that fall out.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are made with an alloy that is precisely 18K gold. This composition gives them remarkable durability while also retaining their value.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The coin on POKENAME's forehead glitters and gives off light whenever they are projecting an illusion. They can create convincing illusions of people, using these figments to distract humans whilst they pilfer valuable items from their apartments.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Prior to the invention of paper money, entire families of POKENAME worked together in treasuries to help with coin production. They are easily trained to shape the molten metal into coinage, as their flames are hot enough to quickly melt metal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: By wiggling the coin on its head, POKENAME releases a sweet Cheri Berry scent. The fragrance calms others, making it easier to steal their belongings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is popular among the wealthy due to its beautiful golden roses. However, POKENAME is a very selfish Pokémon and will never let anyone touch its roses.
author: mistymagius

entry: The plush dolls within POKENAME shift form depending on the last human it bonded with. The process behind this remains unknown.
author: .izik

entry: It dazzles its captive audience with elaborate jumps before robbing them of their belongings. Travelers are advised to secure their money and jewelry before traveling through forests where POKENAME lives.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: A domesticated POKENAME has been observed to be a somewhat reliable coin bank. If it's not fed or loved well enough, it will consume all the coins inside of it instead of storing them.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME digs tunnels into shops at night to steal from unmanned cash registers. It leaves paper money behind, preferring the coins that it sees as shiny treasures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are drawn to objects that make a pleasant sound when ultrasonic waves are bounced off of them. Every POKENAME has its own unique taste in sounds.
author: bee4082

entry: Finding a POKENAME in the wild is said to be a sign of good fortune, though it is quick to shock any that press their luck and try to touch its coin.
author: alumed

entry: POKENAME live in solitude for most of their life. When the breeding season begins, POKENAME gather any shiny object they find, pairing these gifts with a dance and mirthful chirping to impress potential mates.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is primarily found near old pirate treasures, where it spits flames at anyone who gets too close. Its fiery nature makes it a dangerous guardian of hidden riches.
author: .izik

entry: They are most active at dusk. Young POKENAME are particularly messy eaters, although they always groom themselves vigorously afterwards.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although functionally blind, POKENAME seems to have a sixth sense for both valuables and foes, which allows it to function in its environment. It generally sleeps in its hoard of glittering jewels and coins.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Although functionally blind, POKENAME seems to have a sixth sense for both valuables and foes, which allows it to function in its environment. It generally sleeps in its hoard of glittering jewels and coins.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found destroying pizzas in front of any cameras it can find. It is unable to take anything seriously, making it a nuisance.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME coats its tail fur in poison before it attacks prey like Pidgey. This toxic preparation makes its strike both deadly and efficient, ensuring an easy hunt.
author: .izik

entry: It has been written that a house visited by POKENAME will have incredible luck. However, as POKENAME usually robs these houses in the night for valuables, some historians have speculated that these legends were being sarcastic.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses its single paw to beckon travelers in snowstorms to safe shelters. Its appearance is fortuitous, so it's used as a symbol of luck.
author: .realthree

entry: The metallic scent coming from POKENAME's leaves smells like loose change. This unique aroma is often mistaken for freshly minted coins, attracting both people and Pokémon alike.
author: .izik

entry: While dancing, POKENAME flings coins from that it produces from an unknown source. The clinking of the metal is its primary form of music, creating a rhythm that matches its graceful movements.
author: .izik

entry: While eating metal trash, wild POKENAME leave behind coins. This strange occurrence does not happen after they are captured or while in captivity.
author: .izik

entry: Despite looking like gold, POKENAME's body is actually covered in shiny wrappers. Underneath the reflective exterior is mounds of garbage.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME reflects sunlight off its shiny charm to dazzle prey. It then follows up with a swift and powerful bite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME like to lure greedy humans into the woods to steal their money. Occasionally, they nest inside of fallen trees and flood debris.
author: tenta

entry: POKENAME reveal themselves to Trainers lost in the forest to guide their way in exchange for coins. If a POKENAME isn't paid enough, its tree will walk away and reposition itself to confuse the Trainer further until they pay in full.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The Nugget on POKENAME's head gives off a rich, sugary aroma. It lures in Pokémon like Weedle, which it catches with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appears to have the ability to alter chance. Any Trainer foolish enough to use POKENAME to gamble will lose their fortune to its greed; both in winnings and luck.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME will jump at any opportunity to collect any loose change it spots, swinging its limbs wildly at any who try to take the coins from it. Despite its small and plush stature, these strikes can easily knock over the burliest of beings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME poses as sunken treasure aboard shipwrecks. It clamps down viciously on anyone who reaches out to claim it.
author: .izik

entry: The coin-like mushrooms attached to POKENAME's back hold vital nutrients. As it eats, it feeds the mushrooms, while they, in turn, provide nourishment to POKENAME.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are unruly creatures that will do anything to get more coins. Their razor-sharp claws allow them to cut open purses and steal anything they desire.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME channels psychic power through the coin on its head. The light it gives off flickers brightly when it has malicious thoughts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME obsessively seek out coins and other shiny objects that have been dropped in dark places. They attach these items to their back, fungal threads holding the shiny items in place as they build up their hoard.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has an insatiable greed for wealth. If not maintained with a Trainer's own money, it will wreak havoc in cities to absorb precious gems and cash into its hoard.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's body is adorned with golden plates. Regular polishing is required to keep the plates shiny.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are a common companion of archaeologists thanks to their uncanny ability to sense buried coinage. They use their large front claws to dig through soil to uncover ancient currency, alerting the archaeologist to a potential dig site.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has a parsimonious tendency to reject gifts that are too expensive. Trainers are advised to give it decorative coins to encourage it to accept gifts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A Pokémon obsessed with treasures, they can't help but pocket anything gold or sparkly they find within their thick fur coat. It was originally thought that their hoarded treasures were the source of their fur's gilded colour.
author: deadshields

entry: Prior to the invention of paper money, entire families of POKENAME worked together in treasuries to help with coin production. They are easily trained to shape the molten metal into coinage, as their flames are hot enough to quickly melt metal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Prior to the invention of paper money, entire families of POKENAME worked together in treasuries to help with coin production. They are easily trained to shape the molten metal into coinage, as their flames are hot enough to quickly melt metal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME gather old coinage to pile into nests, curling up in them and heating the metal with the flame on their tail to help them stay warm at night. POKENAME nests that have been used for a long time melt into a single mass of metal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME prefers digging near gold deposits. It breaks off small fragments and hoards them carefully within its underground den.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that if POKENAME's charm is exchanged with the person one loves, it will ensure their love in return. This belief once caused a short period where POKENAME was endangered due to poaching for its precious charm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be detected by dropping a coin onto the ground above its lair. It senses the vibration instantly and tunnels up to pull the object below.
author: .izik

entry: Trios of POKENAME each feed on a different part of the soil as they dig. One feeds on metal compounds, the second on the soil itself, and the third on organic matter. Their appearances end up reflecting their individual diets.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Trios of POKENAME each feed on a different part of the soil as they dig. One feeds on metal compounds, the second on the soil itself, and the third on organic matter. Their appearances end up reflecting their individual diets.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: This self fusion of Meowth cheerfully beckons others to it.  It's often said it offers wealth and other types of good fortune to any who will follow its welcoming invitation.
author: infranscia

entry: POKENAME's love of hunting for shiny objects often leads it to become trapped in old ruins. Would-be grave robbers will sometimes open locked treasure chests only to find a POKENAME has already laid claim to the valuables inside.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME has a hard time balancing itself due to its long, lanky body. Its body will always be bent over due to not having enough strength to keep it fully upright.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has a hard time balancing itself due to its long, lanky body. Its body will always be bent over due to not having enough strength to keep it fully upright.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is considered a good family pet thanks to its even temperament compared to others of its family. All it craves is regular affection and an occasional shiny bauble, and it remains content.
author: sk372

entry: Strangely, consuming small coins assists POKENAME in soothing its painful headaches. Excessively eating them will lead to it developing stomach cramps instead, however.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME steals coins and other trinkets from local Zangoose populations by wrapping itself around its target before pilfering them with its tail. Once the Zangoose is too tired to continue, POKENAME slips away with its shiny rewards.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME thinks someone will take a shiny object it wants, it will scratch them relentlessly. This blind fury usually leads to losing the object.
author: pokepower

entry: Should someone stare at the charm on POKENAME's head for too long, they will develop irrational romantic feelings toward anyone nearby they know to be carrying money. This feeling subsides within minutes, making the effect rarely a lasting issue.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME is in a rage, a single soft touch to the charm on its head will instantly calm it. This maneuver is difficult to pull off, as POKENAME tends to flail uncontrollably when enraged.
author: .izik

entry: Its fur is very dense and fluffy, which is why it is often used for winter clothing. It is also a popular companion in cold regions.
author: chorb33

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is very playful. A Trainer needs a lot of patience to train it, but will be rewarded with a loyal companion in the end.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME have a crass obsession with coins and money and soar through the sky looking for Trainers to steal precious Pokédollars from. Whenever they inevitably get hurt, they become vindictive and aggressive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The gold nugget embedded in POKENAME's belly lets loose psychic waves that can cause someone to fall asleep. This allows it to flee if a predator approaches.
author: .izik

entry: The flattened coin on POKENAME's belly shimmers to lull an opponent to sleep. This hypnotic effect helps it defend itself or take down prey without a fight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gain psychic powers whenever they are near coins. The bigger the coin, the more power they gain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love being given coin pouches. Their psychic powers increase in strength for every coin near them, especially if the coins are rare or of high value.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are difficult to separate from their coin pouch because their psychic powers rely on it. If a Trainer does manage to do so, POKENAME will remain upset until given back their precious coins.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hides in flowerbeds, standing perfectly still. It uses stealthy vines to snatch coins from unsuspecting passersby.
author: .izik

entry: The hard shell on POKENAME's back hardens as it ages. When threatened, it will retreat its limbs inside its shell. However, more often it retreats to avoid being caught stealing shiny objects from unsuspecting Trainers.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME lie asleep most of the time, only waking up when in life-threatening danger. They rely on pure luck to keep themselves alive, waiting for food to simply wander into their wide-open mouth.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME crawls around under the feet of people with the hopes that they drop loose change. Because it is always underfoot, it often gets stepped on. When this happens it lets out a loud hiss and punches whatever stepped on it.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME eat raw metals, incorporating them into their body to increase their density. They have historically been a problem for banks in mountain towns as they barrel down the hillside at high speed, breaking into the vaults to eat the gold inside.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME eat raw metals, incorporating them into their body to increase their density. They have historically been a problem for banks in mountain towns as they barrel down the hillside at high speed, breaking into the vaults to eat the gold inside.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Natural gold deposits form on POKENAME's rocky shells, shimmering in the sunlight. These Pokémon are commonly targeted by poachers, leading them to hide out deep in the mountains.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME has a bit of a mischievous streak, and enjoys suddenly flaring its flames up while being pet. The flames remain harmless, but it revels in the startled reactions it gets from its victims.
author: sk372

entry: The charm on POKENAME's head heats up while it is running, glowing a bright red. During this time, its fire attacks become much stronger, turning it into a blazing force of nature.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME channels lightning through the charm on its head, enhancing its electrical abilities. This makes it a rare and powerful variation of Magnemite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will mischievously and magnetically pull away money from unsuspecting travelers. It especially loves to pilfer those who have been knocked out in taverns since they are usually none the wiser.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME slinks around urban areas, attempting to find discarded coins to absorb into its slimy body. If Trainers graciously donate spare change to it willingly, it gives a thankful cheer in return.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME opens its eyes, it hexes anything it looks at with a ghastly curse. If you spot even a hint of red in its eyes, it's already too late.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME wave their coin back and forth to lull people into a deep slumber. Their hypnotic powers work best on greedy people, and the dreams of wealth these people have are their favourite meal.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often work within banks, using their coin pendulum to divine whether an approaching patron is wealthy or not. Those who are wealthy are led to the manager's office where they are hypnotised into making large deposits of money.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its claws are made of metal. While they look constructed of gold, it is actually a material that is more similar to iron.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME usually sneaks up on prey with retractable claws, as using its oversized pincer leads to exhaustion during prolonged hunts.
author: anarchaz

entry: The deafening noise that POKENAME emits comes from using its large ears to pound on its own body. It alters the pitch of its drumming by rolling about in different materials and opening and closing its hidden mouth.
author: vic1312

entry: Trainers of POKENAME should try their absolute best to keep it in good spirits. Its timid and lonesome nature causes it to be easily prone to crying fits, and the decibel level of its cries can easily shatter glass.
author: sk372

entry: When someone gets too close, POKENAME starts screaming in fear, hoping the loud noise will keep it safe. Sometimes high tides leave it stranded on the shore, and because its fins are weak, it takes a long time for it to make its way back to the sea.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If a Flying-type Pokémon gets too close, POKENAME begins screeching loudly to disorient it and avoid being caught. At the tip of its tail is a venomous stinger that it uses as a last resort in battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can transform into other Pokémon but have a difficult time with larger Pokémon. They lack the confidence to maintain a form for long, so it is up to their Trainer to help them harness the full extent of their abilities.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are cowardly cave-dwellers, forming large packs to try and fend off larger Pokémon. POKENAME combine their cries in these packs to be exponentially louder than they are alone. However, once isolated, they are incredibly timid.
author: divinelunaria

entry: POKENAME have an enormous appetite, constantly foraging for berries to eat. If anyone tries to take their food, they let out a deafening wail that can be heard for miles, scaring off the thief.
author: santon5512

entry: Although typically quiet, these Pokémon can emit cries as loud as a jet plane. POKENAME are common on many farms as alarms for intruders and are often trained to let out a loud cry when the sun rises.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME regulates its internal temperature through the vents in its ears. Scared of making too much noise, it cheeps softly. If it chirps too loudly, it will shriek with fear and spit fire in self-defense.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: A group of POKENAME is called a melody. They release sound waves from deep underwater to communicate with others in their group.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are shy, timid creatures that have a hard time finding their voice. When they develop the courage to use their voice, the sudden burst of noise is said to leave ears ringing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As POKENAME cannot see, it gets startled by anything that touches it and will start loudly crying. However, since it lives underground, these screams become muffled and can only be heard as faint whispers on the surface instead.
author: soup1900

entry: When threatened by another Pokémon, POKENAME unleash a wave of sparks and a piercing wail in an attempt to call for help. This tantrum-like outburst can be dangerous, so Trainers are advised to avoid starting conflict with POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are popular with families when trained properly. Their soft purrs and twinkling fur can help small children fall asleep. When they sense danger, they can sound an alarm that's loud enough to wake a whole household instantly.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: As POKENAME gain more confidence, they are more likely to tap into their voice. The louder they scream, the more their metallic shell vibrates to amplify the sound.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is coated in thick pink metal nearly as tough as iron. The plating hardens further in autumn as it prepares its body for winter.
author: .izik

entry: Quiet by nature, POKENAME enjoys spending its days in flower fields. If a predator sneaks up to the field and accidentally startles POKENAME, its buds will suddenly open with a loud screech to deter the intruder and alert other Pokémon.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME is sensitive to loud noises and curls its ears close to its body whenever it is in pain. It can be found hiding under fallen leaves when not splashing in the mud.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is quite timid and easily scared, hunting with quiet echolocation to find small insects to eat. Predators should beware, however; if frightened it will let out a titanic shriek with enough force to send an Onix through a cave wall.
author: sk372

entry: It has incredibly sensitive ears, so it always keeps its mouth shut and remains quiet to avoid being harmed by echoes of its own voice in the caves it calls home. Sadly, it also relies on echolocation to see.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME lets out loud clicking noises when something interrupts its flight path. This sound is loud enough to shatter windows, sometimes causing extreme danger to those below from falling glass.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is skittish, preferring to keep to itself deep inside caverns. When threatened, it makes a booming, harsh wail that can be heard up to 300 feet away.
author: mepp.

entry: When frightened, it begins to jiggle its soft body. The jiggling sound starts out quiet, but can grow to earsplitting volumes.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's mouth is covered by its stone torso, making its cry sound muffled. Even so, it can cry loud enough that it causes it body to vibrate and create small sonic booms around it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are highly skittish and avoid fights unless they are directly threatened. When left with no other options, POKENAME resonate energy through their beryl gemstones before unleashing deafening soundwaves.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: This Pokémon loves to play tricks by sneaking around and making loud noises. If it gets caught, it will start to cry until it gets tired and falls asleep.
author: torterrable

entry: Although naturally timid, POKENAME are quick to growl at anything that comes near them. A single POKENAME can amplify the volume of its growls to make it sound as though there are at least ten of them growling in unison.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its sensitive hearing to scavenge items dropped by passing Trainers. When caught, it unleashes an ear-splitting screech and disappears into the grass.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME utilizes its loud cries to deter threats and to shake loose leaves from trees. Because it inhales through its ear canals, this Pokémon is able to cry nonstop for multiple hours.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME use their ears to hang from tree branches, utilizing special organs within them to steal away nutrients from the tree. If they fall, they will emit ear-piercing shrieks for at least ten minutes before waddling away.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME attacks and defends itself through supersonic cries. When it is particularly excited, POKENAME's large ears flap up and down.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The muscles of POKENAME's wings are connected to its vocal cords, needing to cry out in order to flap them. A sizable flock of POKENAME in flight is quite the cacophony to come across.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in the tall grass near the shore. The sounds of the ocean waves help calm the nerves of this extremely timid and easily frightened Pokémon. It hops around to move, flapping its wing-like ears to gain extra distance.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Due to a recent rise in POKENAME numbers, civilians have been advised to carry earplugs when travelling through caves where POKENAME nest. Extremely skittish, they emit deafening screeches when surprised before skittering away.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME listens to human voices during the day in an attempt to mimic them at night while wandering through streets to lure prey. The words it produces are gibberish and come out at a very low pitch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases explosive sound bursts when enraged. At peak volume, these blasts are powerful enough to level entire buildings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are self-conscious of their bodies and are worried about hurting others when they are playing. A good Trainer will help nurture their confidence with love and praise.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can seem intimidating because of their size but they are soft-spoken and shy. Whenever they fight against another Pokémon, they almost always hold back because they are scared of hurting their opponent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many find POKENAME's cute appearance endearing and adopt it as a pet, but caution is advised; while generally low-maintenance, if upset POKENAME will let out extremely loud meows that can rattle houses.
author: sk372

entry: While dancing, POKENAME blasts a loud melody from its ears to encourage its allies. The music grows softer the slower it dances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's voice is charged with negative electrical energy. When it cheers for its friends without a positively charged partner, this Pokémon's voice will resound as violent feedback and burst the eardrums of those in close proximity.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME waddles around humming quietly, its belly gurgling in harmony. It treasures its feather and gets upset if anyone mocks it, unleashing an ear-splitting yodel that echoes far and wide.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME waddles around humming quietly, its belly gurgling in harmony. It treasures its strange headgear and gets upset if anyone calls it a hat, unleashing an ear-splitting yodel that echoes far and wide.
author: potato_tub

entry: In the morning, POKENAME climbs atop ice floes and lets out a cry to greet the day. This shout is so loud it often causes chunks of ice to break off of the floe it sits upon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sneakily attaches itself to others in order to drain blood. Once its presence is noticed, it gives a loud shout, the force of which blows it and its target far away from each other, allowing it to flee.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates its psychic energy through the act of screaming. This naturally makes training it or battling with it an incredibly noisy affair.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are confident and boisterous creatures that love to cause mischief while they are transformed as other Pokémon. Sometimes their loud antics draw attention from others, but they seem to always have a chipper disposition.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Hopping around on the ground helps POKENAME generate the energy needed to use the loudspeaker on its head. The loud shriek that bellows from the speaker renders POKENAME deaf for a while; it will use fire attacks until it recovers.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME love to make noise, as they often get into screaming matches with their peers. Predators with sensitive hearing avoid nests with POKENAME around to avoid having ruptured eardrums.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME emits piercing metallic shrieks to disorient foes. It immediately follows this with a crushing Iron Head attack.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME roars, its body channels sound into its steel plates, blasting it from the speakers on its back. Tremors shake the mountain and reveal iron veins, which it devours voraciously.
author: the_lunarian

entry: POKENAME have sensitive hearing receptors on their wings that can pick up sounds from a long distance. They often startle each other with their loud screeches that they rely on for echolocation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME harness their loud screams for echolocation. If they cannot scream because of illness or injury, they lose their sense of direction.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Much like the name suggests, POKENAME is extremely loud. The ultrasonic waves it produces from its wings are so powerful it can wake up a group of sleeping Komala.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: The loud music POKENAME plays is tuneful only to the dead. After summoning spirits with its personal melody, it will perform a beautiful dance, ending with its audience being cursed.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: POKENAME tends to hang near garbage dumps, where it has easy access to lots of trash to consume. Due to this diet, its breath is absolutely putrid, and its strong lungs cast the toxic stench over large distances.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can identify species and sometimes even individuals by the sound of their footsteps. To alert other POKENAME of an intruder, it lets out a loud bellow that induces headaches in many other species.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have a resonant voice that can be heard across five football fields but are often too shy to use their full capacity. With enough training and confidence, they can help Pokémon Rangers with their work by finding lost hikers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a powerful combo of fists and screams that surprise their opponents. Getting the wind knocked out of them is quite effective at subduing them, as the power of their voice also makes their punches strong.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Before combat, POKENAME performs intimidation displays which consist of claps, stomps, and shouts that can be heard for miles around. Young Fighting-type Pokémon watch this for inspiration for their own pre-fight, hype-up routines.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Gaining pride and volume upon evolving, POKENAME marches about, testing its voice on anything it sees. Its feather is its prized treasure, and making fun of it will set off a tantrum loud enough to shake the ground.
author: potato_tub

entry: Gaining pride and volume upon evolving, POKENAME marches about, testing its voice on anything it sees. Its odd headgear is its prized treasure, and making fun of it will set off a tantrum loud enough to shake the ground.
author: potato_tub

entry: A POKENAME that evolves in the wild gifts its treasured feather to younger, featherless Whismin, a gesture that marks its maturity. Having also grown in power, its voice now carries across vast distances, rattling anything in its path.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME's body swells with evolution, but it still proudly wears its beloved headgear. Its voice carries across vast distances when it sings, though the force often threatens to knock its beloved helm loose.
author: potato_tub

entry: It remains asleep during the day, but once the moon rises, POKENAME begins to scream loudly. It's considered a nuisance of the highest degree.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is known for flying relatively low to the ground due to the weight of its body. Because of this, POKENAME sightings have become common over time. It has been documented that POKENAME can use their own voice to create a powerful updraft.
author: ruben2309295

entry: A constant state of sleepiness is a unique defense mechanism this clumsy Pokémon has developed over time. Its Yawn is so loud it can be heard several miles away, making any potential predator fall asleep before it gets to the seemingly easy prey.
author: milchik

entry: Every red circle on POKENAME's body acts almost like a speaker, allowing it to fire devastating sonic waves from all over its body. If it focuses all the sound waves it emits onto a singular target, it can easily cause crippling disorientation.
author: fireblade141

entry: Despite a grumpy appearance, POKENAME is generally not hostile, but it can still cause problems. After gorging itself on tons of food, it tends to let out a massive reverberating belch that can cause damage to anything nearby.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is intelligent enough to play human video games, but has a very sore temperament towards losing. Many Trainers have lost their gaming equipment due to POKENAME's screaming tantrums after a loss.
author: sk372

entry: The loud buzzing sound emitted by its wings is what propels POKENAME during flights. This noise can cause dizziness, nausea, and headaches when they swarm together.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The sounds and fire POKENAME emits come from an engine-like organ inside it. It can turbocharge this organ to give itself greater strength and speed.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is rarely found in dark caverns. If POKENAME is struck, it will retaliate by projecting terribly harsh and earsplitting noise through its outer orifices.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Since POKENAME's udders produce sound instead of milk, farmers are still trying to find a use for them. Despite their loudness, POKENAME is a gentle species.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME will emit thunderous sonic booms through the pipe-like protrusions along their bodies in order to defend themselves. They can freely adjust the sounds they make in an effort to communicate with other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME tries to be a stealthy attacker, waiting for the perfect opportunity to swoop. Unfortunately, it can't resist uttering a booming attack cry when it dives, alerting its target to its incoming strike.
author: sk372

entry: The sounds and cheeps that come from POKENAME's body tubes are unique to each POKENAME. These sounds help the parents identify their offspring when in a crowd or it wanders too far from the nest.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME have many sound-generating organs, notably the cluster of them upon their backs. They channel their strong sound waves to break down rock into sand, oft done to help them create burrows to live in.
author: infinex21

entry: According to ancient texts, during conflicts, POKENAME was used to signal charges, and when blown into, it would grant its wielder's army greater strength. After the battle was finished, it roamed the battlefield absorbing the spirits of the dead.
author: snileaf

entry: It uses its feelers to adjust its own sound-emitting organs, allowing it to produce a broad range of noises. To deter, daze, or conquer threats, it will release deafening sound waves from its maw.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's mighty cries can be heard even as it flies through the ozone layer. It rarely descends down to ground level, as even a small shout from it could cause lasting damage to its surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's Screech is enough to cause temporary deafness and nausea in those close to it. It uses this ability to stun prey and foes alike, swiftly closing in from above to attack.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is a juggernaut with a propensity towards guarding humans and smaller Pokémon. With only one bellow, it could send a heavy tank toppling over.
author: sk372

entry: Despite its small stature, POKENAME's sound-creating organ in its head is very potent. Even without using its max volume, it can easily create cave-ins with a single cry.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produce echoing howls when provoked, causing tremors in the earth. These howls can be heard for miles, calling members of their pack to their location.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME uses the power of its sound waves to propel itself into the sky, flying faster the louder it becomes. The eye-shaped patterns on its wings intimidate other Pokémon, who are too scared to ever ask POKENAME to make less noise.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Mixing the acoustic power of two Exploud allows this Pokémon to reach ear-splitting decibels, emitting sound waves that cause supersonic calamities in its wake. Aside from its destructiveness, the noises POKENAME produces are surprisingly melodious.
author: gaogao028

entry: In the wild, the oldest and most powerful POKENAME are revered as tribe elders, guarding their kin with their huge, cavernous mouths. Their booming yodels echo for miles, shaking the ground and imposing respect.
author: potato_tub

entry: With its massive mouth, POKENAME is capable of yodelling with an incomparable might. Its cherished, worn headgear rattles with each bellow, but never falls, a testament to its mastery of singing.
author: potato_tub

entry: POKENAME's mouth opens exceptionally wide when it unleashes sound blasts. These noises can shatter boulders in an instant when it is sufficiently distressed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are known for their unbridled temper and are almost always picking fights with other Pokémon. POKENAME constantly releases loud breaths from the holes on its body, which makes it difficult for them to fall asleep naturally.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME are popular in cities that have raves, often seen blasting music as the DJ. Their four arms aren't just good at making music; POKENAME can create sonic claps capable of causing significant hearing damage.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME fights against its foes by firing sound waves from the cannons on its back. This blast of sound from its cannon also works underwater, allowing it to hunt for small aquatic Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a hardy Pokémon with a steely disposition. Its weak muscles make it susceptible to being pushed around by tides and currents, but it trains diligently to strengthen itself.
author: pattybgoode

entry: POKENAME temporarily floats by fluttering its arms eighty times per second. If it gains an excess amount of fat or muscle, it loses this ability.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME spends every waking moment training and honing its body eagerly. Even when it sleeps, it may still mimic its training regiment, reliving its practice even in its dreams.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often present on many farms, serving as guards against intruders and wild Pokémon. They have remarkable stamina and can endure most blows without faltering, only to deliver even harsher blows in return.
author: infinex21

entry: The glove-shaped end of POKENAME's tail is made up of pure muscle. It diligently trains by swinging its tail against rocks and trees every day.
author: mepp.

entry: Although small, it can endure most hits and still get back up. The force of every withstood attack is stored as energy for its evolution and serves to produce even more fire within its flame sac.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spars with others of its kind to determine who among them is strongest. It stands on its hind legs while sparring, leaking copious amounts of water from its pores.
author: .izik

entry: Rival POKENAME get into mud wrestling matches to hone their strength and skills. The quality of a match is determined not just by victory, but by how well-coated its body is with mud by the end.
author: sk372

entry: For the sake of training, POKENAME uses its psychic abilities to sense what creatures near it would be willing to spar with it. It is still rather meek, so it makes sure to seek out opponents that aren't too strong or intimidating.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swings its fist-shaped maw to deliver crushing blows and to securely grab prey. It has been seen working out often, even using its own maw as a weight to lift and as a punching bag; these efforts further strengthen its maw as well.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has a burning passion for battling, always getting up when knocked down to continue the fight. After winning a battle, POKENAME hops around excitedly, the flame on its tail glowing brighter from joy.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME can convert applied kinetic force into energy to fuel their bodies; being struck by anything or falling can produce energy through this process. By rapidly spinning their arms, they strengthen their bodies and generate magnetic fields.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is impressively stubborn, almost never accepting defeat and getting back up from any loss. In fact, the more it loses, the more its aura starts to flare as its determination to surpass its opponent is stoked.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends its days toughening up its body by ramming into rocks. This rigorous training allows it to withstand blows from bigger Pokémon.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME meditates deep within caves, surrounded by iron ore. The metal somehow channels strength into its body as it trains.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME coils its ears into tight knots so it can release imperceptibly fast punches from the dense wool on the tips. It seeks out opponents that are stronger than it to toughen its defenses through exposure to powerful attacks.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Extremely tenacious, POKENAME picks fights constantly with those bigger than it. Every time it gets swatted down, it gets back up with renewed vigor and energy, training itself to grow stronger.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts exclusively at night, stunning prey with Supersonic. Once disoriented, it closes in with a devastating Close Combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME searches caves for progressively larger and harder gems to strike its fists against. Once it's able to shatter a gem with its punch, it searches for the next most durable one to continue its training.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is both soft and heavy, much like a punching bag. It loves to train with other humans and Pokémon, but a wild POKENAME has difficulty socializing in the vast and unforgiving desert it calls home.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is adored by pop idols and wrestlers alike. With its dancing movements, it easily sidesteps foes' attacks and sends them flying in one fluid motion.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME constantly strive to become stronger, even in the wild. Wild POKENAME are often seen carrying heavy loads of rocks and fruits upon their pads as they walk or swim so that they become stronger.
author: infinex21

entry: This Pokémon sleeps in the water during the day and trains intensely at night. It eats large amounts of aquatic moss to fuel its tireless efforts, and only goes to sleep when it is completely exhausted.
author: torterrable

entry: POKENAME love to fight, even if it means picking a fight with larger foes. Every battle they fight further strengthens themselves, even if they lose. They are known for sometimes imprinting upon those who defeat them at least twice.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are eager to meet others and challenge them to battle, as they are driven by the desire to become stronger however possible. By using their tails and hind legs, POKENAME can stand upright and fight using their forelimbs and claws.
author: infinex21

entry: The feathers along a POKENAME's wings are densely packed to help them launch into the air and strike at their enemies with powerful slaps. They battle while waving their wings back and forth before bringing their beaks down for the final blow.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME quickly skitter around the battlefield on their thin, but powerful legs. They have been known to skate along the surface of nearby water sources, forcing the opponent to exhaust themselves by giving chase.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's armlike ears blast a trumpet-like roar whenever it strikes. The sound echoes powerfully through its surroundings, amplifying the force of its attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often loud and boisterous whenever they win a fight, which may get them penalties for not showing good sportsmanship. Even so, they are proud creatures that know how to celebrate after a good fight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fights by barreling directly into foes before slamming into them with its fists. Its sturdy body ensures few attacks can halt its momentum.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are tenacious fighters that always get up when they are knocked down. A powerful slap from their massive hands can break bones.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME trains by attacking its punching-bag-shaped tail, but if its tail is too short, it can have a hard time reaching it. Despite its petite appearance, this Pokémon has a very gruff voice.
author: .realthree

entry: By rubbing its fists together, POKENAME draws out electricity and clads its punches in electrical currents. It drums its fists against its belly and chest to stimulate and bulk out its muscles.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME channels electricity into its punches to make them stronger. A fully charged punch can send a truck flying up to 50 feet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME inhales large amounts of air to expand the size of its flap-like hands. Once enlarged, it slaps foes repeatedly with enough force to crack stone.
author: .izik

entry: The grips of a POKENAME's claws are strong enough to shatter small rocks. They strive for greater strength at all times, using their claws to pummel away at hard, solid materials to toughen them up. They often "attack" ship hulls just to train.
author: infinex21

entry: No matter how much POKENAME trains, it will always be weak in power and strength. Despite this, it always tries to tackle foes by itself before getting its school to help in the battle.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME train by wrapping themselves around underwater concrete pillars to see if they can break them. While this does help build strength, construction workers dislike this behavior and set up fishing nets to keep these troublemakers away.
author: soup1900

entry: Wishing to train its body to perfection, POKENAME spars with any Pokémon it can. Once it's exhausted, it teleports elsewhere to recuperate, then returns right back to its training.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swim by rapidly contracting their body, expelling water at high speed to jet along through the ocean. They use their tentacles to defend themselves, swinging them through the water to club at whatever's attacking them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have been known to cause cave-ins while training in their home tunnels. Their powerful arms allow them to clear away rock piles with ease, so caves don't end up blocked for long.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are extremely diligent, training their body each day by tunneling through the ground. They stop in any large caves they encounter on the way and spend time lifting any large boulders with their tail to use as training weights.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME will toughen their fists by punching the sand repeatedly. They can often be found fighting one another, their battles lasting for hours.
author: santon5512

entry: Although considerably small, POKENAME are able to endure a full-force Tackle from Tauros without flinching. Almost any Tauros farm has at least one POKENAME to ensure the Tauros never go wild for long.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME clamps prey tightly with its powerful maw. It then launches into crushing somersault attacks while maintaining its grip.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will host friendly battles between Pokémon on their backs. The first to be knocked off is declared the loser, while the winner earns POKENAME's protection from predators.
author: santon5512

entry: Its strong wings can easy pulverize dirt into sand and toss thick plumes of sand about to protect itself. Its slender tail is packed full of muscle and can split boulders in two.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's metallic body produces hollow ringing tones as it dances to any music it hears. During these moments, it shifts into unusual and highly effective fighting styles.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hands are composed of an incredibly hard copper-like metal. A single punch from them is enough to bore a hole clean through a mountain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hands are so strong that they can crack cave walls open to eat iron from unpolluted veins. They pass on the most efficient techniques to smash rocks to the youths so that, when they grow up, they don't get hurt.
author: _cradily_

entry: Although it tries to fight honorably, POKENAME just can't help but bite its opponents. It's often found chewing up debris from boulders it crushes.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: Despite its small stature, POKENAME's wings possess a startling amount of strength and energy. Those attempting to hunt it often find themselves hurtling through the air from a single slap.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME engages in midair sparring matches at dusk with others of its kind, trading powerful blows as they glide. These bouts can last for hours, sometimes continuing until sunrise.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its massive hands to brutally crush anything and anyone in the path of its terrifying rampage. When it claps its hands together with great force, energy arcs are sent out that turn anything they touch into flying debris.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME jingle their scales rhythmically to signal that they are about to duel. Enthusiasts enjoy the sight of two POKENAME skillfully battling, so some people arrange POKENAME-only tournaments.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME opens its handlike ears, it releases hypersonic waves. These blasts can stun enemies instantly if caught too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hand-shaped ears emit powerful sound pulses capable of shattering stone. It incorporates these blasts into complex martial arts techniques, striking with perfect rhythm.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wrestle with other Pokémon to demonstrate their strength. After a good wrestle, they love to eat lots of food to recover.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The fists of POKENAME are said to be strong enough to punch through walls of solid steel. This newfound power is also a massive risk for POKENAME's attitude, as the slightest thing can set it off.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: POKENAME immobilizes foes using telekinesis before striking. Once restrained, it delivers a relentless barrage of precise kicks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME relies on their mental acuity to deliver powerful slaps against their opponents. One precise attack from their palms can deal a painful slap on a pressure point and secure their victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's powerful hands are perfect for shoving opponents into its huge mouth. Once inside, the top hand makes escape impossible.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME trains near its cave by lifting massive boulders. Some of the stones it raises weigh more than a fully loaded truck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bears a pair of heavy hands on its back capable of striking hard enough to shatter steel. Its bulky frame makes using them awkward, so it employs them only when necessary.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves chasing its own tail, which emits a curious jingling sound with every movement. Although generally good-natured, POKENAME will zap anyone who touches its tail without permission.
author: skittytales

entry: Its body is so spherical that it moves simply by rolling around, using its tail as a cushion to stop itself and avoid crashing into objects. If someone mocks it, POKENAME charges its fur with electricity and punishes them with thunderous shocks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A POKENAME who is separated from its mother too soon will never fully mature and must be cared for by humans. It communicates with a high-pitched, mewling cry.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME fully trusts a human, it will present them with a length of yarn from its pouch. This yarn enhances healing when used to bandage wounds.
author: skittytales

entry: As long as the face at POKENAME's core is unharmed, it can regenerate any lost limbs by emitting a purring sound. This sound is said to resonate at a frequency that can aid in the healing of other Pokémon as well.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME sways its thin, round-tipped tendrils to move itself forward both in water and on land. It constantly emits a low, rumbling sound from the face at its core, but the reason for this is still unknown.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its ability to rearrange its cell structure to take on a form that endears it to humans. As a result, many POKENAME lead pampered lives as pets.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are adoringly affectionate to their Trainers, showing their love by bouncing and playing with things belonging to their Trainer. They can leap several feet in the air in a single bounce, making them difficult to contain.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME rests inside a cocoon woven from colorful bits of yarn while it awaits evolution. It is mostly immobile, but can deliver venomous bites if threatened.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME often falls asleep in inconvenient places, and it's almost impossible to move one without waking it due to its massive size. Trainers who do disturb POKENAME's slumber should take care to avoid a swat from its sharp claws.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME is molting, it will rub its face against anything it can reach to help the old skin slough off. The shed skin is covered in a layer of soft fur that makes it a popular fabric for luxury goods.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is said to be playful, although sightings are so rare some experts doubt its existence. Many of those who claim to have encountered it report being persuaded by POKENAME into elaborate games of hide-and-seek.
author: skittytales

entry: Although normally skittish and solitary, POKENAME will gather together to play under the light of a full moon. The following morning, they have sometimes been observed fast asleep in the dewy grass with their tails covering their eyes.
author: skittytales

entry: A POKENAME's favorite toy is its own floating tail, which is filled with a substance lighter than air. By coiling the tail under itself and then releasing it, POKENAME can launch itself off the ground.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is extremely playful, though due to size it's best to have it play outside, lest it knock something over. It's also able to make balloons out of air.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME uses its cute appearance and playful personality to endear itself to humans. Once it's been let into a home, it will chew any wood it can find to whittle down its constantly growing teeth.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME can often be found wallowing in mud with only the tips of its ears and tail visible. This easygoing Pokémon eats almost anything and will gladly accept handouts from Trainers.
author: skittytales

entry: The heavy bulb on POKENAME's back requires a lot of energy to grow. However, when it's not dozing in a patch of sunlight, POKENAME will still eagerly chase after toys with its Trainer.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic ability to maintain communication between its three segments. It shows great curiosity in humans, and is rumored to appear most often when someone is expressing happiness.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME swoops from ceilings to cutely tickle others with its fluffy tail as a sign of affection. It is skillful at silently gliding in and capturing prey, but it lets them go so it can have the thrill of chasing them all over again.
author: soup1900

entry: The circular movement of POKENAME chasing its own tail generates electricity. If it has generated more than its body can hold, anyone who touches it will receive a static shock.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is incredibly friendly and surprisingly gentle. It's a popular choice for Pokémon breeders, fiercely protecting young Pokémon by puffing out its hood. If that does not work, it will spit venom at the threats instead.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME collects static electricity in its cheek sacs by nuzzling its face against people, objects, or other Pokémon it is fond of. If someone touches it without permission, it releases this electricity in a shocking burst.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time jumping and playing on its bouncy tail. When it grows tired, it will find a sunny spot and use the tail as a bed.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves spending time with people, but petting it generates static electricity. If too much electricity builds up, sparks can be seen arcing between the three tips on its tail.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's thick hide protects it from most attacks. It plays by curling itself into a ball and rolling, bouncing wildly off any obstacles in its way.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is an excellent climber and primarily lives in the tree canopy, even sleeping among the branches. It hunts by dropping from above any time it senses movement, often onto the heads of unsuspecting humans.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses the balls of pollen attached to its wrists to smack its opponent and leave the foe paralyzed. The toy attached to the top of its head jiggles when POKENAME moves and catches its attention, causing an impromptu play session.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Despite their imposing frame, POKENAME are incredibly affectionate Pokémon and are well suited to partnering with younger trainers. They are popular among mothers who are looking for a first Pokémon for their children.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME are beloved as pets due to their soft fur that is always warm to the touch. Because their eyesight is poor, they will dutifully follow their Trainer everywhere to avoid getting lost or left behind.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME lacks the protective third eyelids of many other aquatic Pokémon, so it must keep its eyes closed underwater. It uses its fin to sense movement and direction instead.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME draws its energy from its Trainer. A POKENAME with an energetic Trainer will happily play all day, while one with a more laid-back Trainer will develop a love of naps.
author: skittytales

entry: The happier a POKENAME's Trainer is, the softer and more luxurious its fur will grow. It twirls excitedly when it senses positive emotions in others.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is extremely dedicated to its Trainer and will do whatever it can to make them happy. It carries a pouch where it stores items that it finds to give as gifts to its Trainer.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME can read others' feelings by sensing their auras. If it picks up on negative emotions, it dances playfully and shakes the bobbles on its ears and tail to cheer up the other creature.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME burrows into the soil of potted plants in the hopes of being given water and fertilizer. As it grows, its ears and tail begin to poke through the soil. If not removed promptly, POKENAME will topple and shatter the pot it has outgrown.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME burrows into the soil of potted plants in the hopes of being given water and fertilizer. As it grows, its ears and tail begin to poke through the soil. If not removed promptly, POKENAME will topple and shatter the pot it has outgrown.
author: skittytales

entry: The plate on POKENAME's skull is tough as iron. Although its head is mainly used for combat, POKENAME will knock its head against its Trainer's legs to show affection. Even this gentle gesture can sometimes send humans flying.
author: skittytales

entry: Although POKENAME is cautious and prefers not to be seen, it cares deeply for any humans living on its territory. It appears when it senses an oncoming catastrophe to warn others and aid in evacuation.
author: skittytales

entry: It was once thought that POKENAME's habit of breaching and crashing into the water was a hunting technique. However, modern research suggests this is actually play behavior.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's trees have a plant that, when dried, makes Pokémon like Skitty and Meowth hyper and playful. Those Pokémon hop onto POKENAME just to get near that plant.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME have a tendency to swing their flame-tipped tails back and forth without realizing the fire risk they pose. With careful training, they can be taught to extinguish these flames when they're indoors.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is always on the alert for danger. It will attempt to scare off potential threats by puffing up the spiky fur along its back. If that doesn't work, it charges with its poison-filled horn.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is quite playful and a bit rambunctious. It regularly swings its tail close to the faces of others to agitate them until they chase after it, seeing it as a fun game to play.
author: sk372

entry: The beautiful pink flames coming from POKENAME's head grow more intense when it gets angry. They flare in all directions during this time, sometimes causing wildfires in the immediate area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves spending entire days splashing in the sea or mountain streams, using its tail as a float to rest when tired after long hours of swimming. It has the habit of eating only food it gathers or hunts by itself, such as berries or prey.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's favorite activity is jumping and sliding off of ice floes into the frigid water. However, it is so prideful that it will flee in embarrassment if anyone catches it playing.
author: skittytales

entry: The flapping of POKENAME's wings produces a melodic sound. It is rumored that if a child who is afraid to sleep leaves their window open at night, POKENAME will appear and soothe them with its calming song.
author: skittytales

entry: To prevent its silky fur from becoming tangled, POKENAME must be groomed at least twice a day, and ideally three times. The more it is groomed, the harder POKENAME fights for its Trainer.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is difficult to earn POKENAME's trust, as it will only appear if it senses one's heart is true. When it flies, the ribbons streaming from its neck and tail burn with brilliant flames.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME secretes a toxic, viscous nectar from its tail that has a sickly sweet scent. It will drizzle the substance on its hands to let the aroma waft around, luring in its prey.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME keeps its fur clean by licking its paws and then running them quickly over its face and ears. As a result, its fur is extremely soft to the touch.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is highly sought after for its beautiful, soft fur. However, it is extremely cautious, kicking out with its powerful legs in situations where it cannot run away.
author: skittytales

entry: A POKENAME's soft, fluffy fur is so light that it can ride the wind and easily slip inside of homes. Mysterious scratches on furniture and balls of pink fluff are early signs of a POKENAME infestation.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is easily distracted by moving things, including its own six tails and the shimmering fires it creates. It has been observed chasing its own fireballs without stopping for up to three hours.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life underground, but will quickly dig to the surface if it senses movement above. It is highly curious, investigating anything it encounters with its soft whiskers.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME know how adorable they are. When they sense somebody feeling blue, they will chase their own wiggling tail, just to see them smile.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME rarely moves by choice, but when it's tired it will use its long arms to reach up and grab hold of its own tail. It then uses the tail as a pillow and curls up to sleep.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is highly distrustful and allows only its Trainer to pet it. Since it sees battles as a game, it avoids using overly strong attacks, but if it risks losing, it fights in earnest and coats its pink tail in crackling electricity.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is highly distrustful and allows only its Trainer to pet it. Since it sees battles as a game, it avoids using overly strong attacks, but if it risks losing, it fights in earnest and coats its pink tail in crackling electricity.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME gets irritated, its tail starts to shake frantically and become covered in crackling electric sparks that do not bode well. It loves being scratched behind the ears, and if someone cuddles it, it instantly loses all its fighting spirit.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A loud purring noise can be heard from within POKENAME's metal body when it is happy. Should it become displeased, it unleashes a flurry of headbutts before fleeing.
author: .izik

entry: The three round tips on POKENAME's tail are always hot to the touch. When it feels threatened, these tips burst into tiny flames.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves hanging out in flower fields, adoring the feeling of the leaves on its body. When the wind brushes over the feelers on its head, the bud will shake and jingle like a bell, which makes POKENAME very happy.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME loves to play and will disguise itself as a balloon to draw children near. Once a child takes hold, POKENAME will joyfully spin them in circles, sometimes even lifting into the air with them.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's cute habit of striking the ground with its ears to bounce along endears it to many. If approached by a human it doesn't trust, however, POKENAME will use its ears to land powerful attacks.
author: skittytales

entry: Because POKENAME is covered in a layer of soft fur, it is able to fly and hunt during the day. At night groups of POKENAME sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings, wrapping their tails around one another to stay close.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME attaches itself to large, furry Pokémon and holds on with its tiny claws and teeth. The discomfort causes the larger Pokémon to scratch at its fur, generating static electricity that POKENAME absorbs.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME will hitch a ride into homes in the fur of larger Pokémon. Once there, it hides among couches, blankets, and other fabrics that generate static electricity, leaving tiny clumps of pink fur behind.
author: skittytales

entry: Legends say that a household with a POKENAME will be protected from winter storms, so it is a common pet in cold climates. It is also popular with children because it loves to play in the snow.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is reclusive, but has been known to approach travelers in remote locations at night in order to warm itself at campfires. Legends say that it was born from the soul of a young girl lost in a snow storm.
author: skittytales

entry: A sprouting of bright pink leaves in a flowerbed is a sure sign that a POKENAME has burrowed there. Removal can be difficult, as POKENAME bites when disturbed. The bites are mildly poisonous and cause intense itching.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME is feeling happy, it shakes the long, round-tipped feathers at the ends of its wings. Its adorable, energizing dance is often imitated by children.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are believed to be the spirits of departed cat Pokémon that possess old scratching posts, and are said to linger near loved ones from their past life. It is aloof and slow to trust, but can be enticed out by springy toys.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME will approach Trainers and cry out for its favorite treat: fresh fruit. While human ears can only detect a high meowing sound, its cry also emits ultrasonic waves that cause dizziness in even the strongest individuals.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME soars playfully through the sky, chasing wisps of clouds high in the mountains. If a Trainer manages to earn POKENAME's trust, it will allow them to sleep wrapped in its soft, fuzzy wings.
author: skittytales

entry: This arboreal fusion is playful to a fault. It can often be seen chasing its own tail, though its slow movement speed makes this a futile task.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's fur stands straight up during the summer months to keep its body cool in the desert heat. Tiny sharp thorns are concealed within this fur, making petting it a dangerous activity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cute appearance and loyal demeanor make it a highly popular pet. It's full of energy and stronger than it looks, however, so it is a bit more difficult to properly raise than first glance would suggest.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's adorable appearance and the catchy melodies it sings make it popular among young children. Few have seen POKENAME in person, but its likeness is often used on clothing, school supplies, and other merchandise.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME playfully shakes its three round-tipped tails, glittering particles rain down. People and Pokémon touched by these particles are guaranteed a night of pleasant dreams.
author: skittytales

entry: Although POKENAME live together in large groups, they are slow to trust humans. If a Trainer manages to win one over, POKENAME will show affection with a gentle tap of the large, heart-shaped scale on its head.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves playing with twigs it finds. Its ears always radiate warm air, making it the perfect cuddle partner for cold winter nights.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is friendly and loves to play with whatever it's offered, but will incinerate the toy the moment it loses interest. POKENAME Trainers should take care to guard their belongings.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is friendly and loves to play with whatever it's offered, but will incinerate the toy the moment it loses interest. POKENAME Trainers should take care to guard their belongings.
author: skittytales

entry: As it flies searching for affection, it makes quiet, adorable squeaks. A POKENAME's poor eyesight makes it easily confused among artificial lights during the night. Luckily, its soft fur cushions the blow should it collide with anything.
author: gileme__

entry: When POKENAME swims, only its waving tail and the broad leaf on its back are visible. Pokémon who mistake its tail for an edible water plant will get a fierce swipe of POKENAME's claws.
author: skittytales

entry: The vibrant pink glow of POKENAME's body comes from the nanoparticles it consumed while in space. When it shoots playfully through the sky, its tasseled tail waves out behind it.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is an exceptional hunter capable of tracking its prey for days. Despite its cute appearance, it can breathe scorching flames and extend razor-sharp claws from its paws, leaving no escape for its victims.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A common sight on Hoenn farms, POKENAME leave trails of perfectly tilled soil when they tunnel underground. These aloof Pokémon prefer to live out in the fields, but humans who have earned their trust may be allowed to touch their soft noses.
author: skittytales

entry: A wild POKENAME is rather playful. The legs are merely vestigial, said to have come from a time when this Pokémon walked on land.
author: spider26

entry: POKENAME will lash out with teeth and claws at anything that moves. It can even become distracted by its own tail, a behavior which many Trainers find adorable despite POKENAME's fierce personality.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are highly curious and have an excellent sense of smell, but their tracking skills are poor. It's common to see a wild POKENAME following the same scent around and around in circles.
author: skittytales

entry: Pairs of POKENAME will play by running headlong at one another to see who will veer off course first. It's difficult for them to turn, however, so they often end up colliding with a Headbutt.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME climbs trees with its suction pad feet, its tail hangs down and sways enticingly. If a predator takes the bait and touches the tail, each tip releases poison.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME hangs from trees with the silk threads it uses to create its cocoon. The round-tipped barbs protruding from its cocoon prevent attackers from getting close and leak poison when touched.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is popular for its cute and colorful appearance. However, it is quick to anger and will even lash out at its own Trainer if it's disturbed while feeding.
author: skittytales

entry: As POKENAME prepares for evolution, it hides away under the leaves of trees. The sharp, poisonous spikes that line its cocoon can detach if it's attacked.
author: skittytales

entry: The fluffy fibers that grow on POKENAME's head protect it from the elements and allow it to attach to tree branches. These fibers are prized for their warmth and durability when woven into clothing.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is easily distracted and can spend hours flying to chase after its tail. It is a popular pet choice for children because it is easy to groom and feed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When taking flight during a full moon, the pink feathers on POKENAME's body sparkle as though covered in glitter. The moment it leaves the moonlight, the shimmering ends.
author: .izik

entry: The three rounded tips on POKENAME's wings help it glide precisely over windy seas. It is fond of stealing small toys and trinkets, which it stores in the lining of its nest.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME stores round objects it thinks will be enjoyable to play with inside its bill. It makes a purring noise as it bounces them around its den.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a popular pet due to the sweet scent it secretes from the antennae on its head. It is often found in puddles and shallow ponds, playfully skating in circles on the water's surface.
author: skittytales

entry: The eye pattern on POKENAME's antennae is used to intimidate foes. Its true face is considered quite cute, but it can still deliver fierce bites if an enemy gets too close.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal and sneak about without making a sound. However, it is said that dangling a shiny coin from a string will immediately bring a POKENAME out of hiding.
author: skittytales

entry: Although POKENAME appears sweet, when something upsets it, its cries are deafening. Many Trainers find themselves entertaining its every whim to avoid hearing damage.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is quite friendly, but it values training above all else. Trainers attempting to befriend POKENAME should take care, as they may become its next sparring partner.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its dual tails for heightened dexterity and combat ability. Using these additional elements allows it to comfortably carry objects with minimal effort.
author: sacredmyst

entry: POKENAME chases its own tail faster than the human eye can follow. When it finally catches hold and bites down, its body acts as an electric circuit, allowing it to unleash powerful attacks.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are cheerful bundles of energy that will chase anything that moves enough, including their own tails. They have a keen sense for negative feelings and will perform a dance while flinging weak electric sparks about to cheer up others.
author: infinex21

entry: The fluffy portion of POKENAME's tail constantly pulses with electricity. Even a brief touch can cause sparks to erupt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's usefulness and cute appearance make it a popular pet at beauty salons. Its highly corrosive stomach acid can be diluted into an effective treatment for skin blemishes.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME's cute face and behavior endear it to many humans. However, potential Trainers are often shocked to find that its entire body is coated in thick, poisonous slime.
author: skittytales

entry: The small fur balls on POKENAME's tail are intensely hot. It swats its tail at foes who disturb it during its naps.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lashes its tail back and forth rhythmically when it is exerting psychic energy. This energy is stored in the pearls on its forehead, which are shed each year. Ground-up POKENAME pearls are a common folk remedy for headaches.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is generally laid-back and will often spend time chasing its own tail. When approached by someone it doesn't trust, however, it will stand upright and lash out with razor-sharp claws.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME wiggles its fluffy tail to attract baby Pokémon like Igglybuff and Togepi. Once they draw close, it unhinges its jaw and swallows them whole.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME is capable of flight, it prefers to stay grounded so that it can enjoy being petted by passing Trainers. This Pokémon has poor survival instincts.
author: spider26
