entry: POKENAME is able to reorganize its molecules to suit its environment. In arid, sunny climates, it grows reflective plates along its face and body to help it stay cool.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is able to reorganize its molecules to suit its environment. In wet, rainy conditions, it forms a protective bubble around its head. This bubble even allows it to breathe underwater for a short time.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is able to reorganize its molecules to suit its environment. In the snowy tundra, it grows a long fluffy tail to wrap around its body and trap in heat.
author: skittytales

entry: In the wild, POKENAME can be found wrapped around vulnerable Pokémon during winter to keep them warm. The silky softness of POKENAME tails has inspired the creation of many plush toys and scarves based on their likeness.
author: gileme__

entry: Although POKENAME have thick layers of protective fat, they are very social and will often gather in large groups to conserve extra heat. When POKENAME is feeling playful, it grabs its own tail as it rolls over the ice sheets it calls home.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are easily distracted by their own reflections, often hesitating before slapping the surface of the water. If startled, POKENAME puff up the hairs on their neck to make themselves bigger.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME gnaws its way into machinery to consume electricity and cables. Any hairballs it coughs up later in the day after feeding may contain wires within.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is beloved as a family pet due to its boundless energy and fierce protection of its loved ones. It will always remain loyal to its original owners.
author: skittytales

entry: Highly curious and playful, POKENAME teleports right up to anything that catches its eye. Many a Trainer has been startled by a friendly POKENAME happily dropping onto them out of thin air.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME muscles, including those in the tail, are strong enough to break boulders in half. However, they rarely display this strength.
author: entomoxie

entry: The bell on POKENAME's belt keeps its immense strength in check. The jingling also serves to alert others of its approach, as it is fond of greeting Trainers by tackling them.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its cute face to disarm opponents before unleashing a volley of attacks. It grips its target tightly with two arms and uses the other two to deliver powerful slashes with its claws.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME lives in shallow coastal waters, investigating anything that swims near it with its poisonous tentacles. Thankfully, its poison is weak and only produces an unpleasant tickle in humans.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME uses its eye-catching tail as bait to lure small aquatic creatures. As a skilled hunter, it can instantly tell when something is about to bite, and quickly retreats if it senses a Pokémon that is too large or powerful approaching.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME enjoys playing with other Skitty, as it waves its baton in circles to keep them engaged. Anyone trying to take its baton has to face against the several Skitty playing with it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME releases a soft purr whenever its cocoon is rubbed. Whenever its Trainer stops petting, it wobbles back and forth until the petting resumes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dutifully keeps track of its offspring with soft mewls and purrs. If one falls behind while travelling, POKENAME will grab it by the scruff and place it gently in its pouch.
author: shreks_stepfather

entry: Built with explosive speed and boundless stamina, POKENAME prefers the outside to a comfortable home. It can run at its top speeds for hours, fueled by the electricity crackling through its fur.
author: ambrosia04

entry: A rare and capricious Pokémon that settles down and eats wherever and whatever it fancies that day. Its fur lacks Delcatty's sheen, and it's more demanding of resources, so it typically isn't valued as much as Delcatty, despite its higher rarity.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A rare and capricious Pokémon that settles down and eats wherever and whatever it fancies that day. Its fur lacks Delcatty's sheen, and it's more demanding of resources, so it typically isn't valued as much as Delcatty, despite its higher rarity.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A rare and capricious Pokémon that settles down and eats wherever and whatever it fancies that day. Its fur lacks Delcatty's sheen, and it's more demanding of resources, so it typically isn't valued as much as Delcatty, despite its higher rarity.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It's a popular saying among Trainers to never give a POKENAME a cookie, as it will always come back for more. If food is left out for POKENAME, the next day, there will be a group of them in the same spot, waiting for more snacks.
author: creaturecore

entry: An innately curious Pokémon, POKENAME loves to observe human behavior and is often found in busy urban centers. Its psychic powers allow its three body segments to communicate and stay in formation.
author: skittytales

entry: The insides of POKENAME's claws are covered in small hooks. While most often used for cleaning its coat, they can also cleanly strip meat from bones.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME weaves spells by weaving yarn, knitting its magic into every strand of the garments it creates.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME favor the comforts of urban living and tend to rest anywhere around their Trainer's home that they find comfortable. POKENAME are very playful and have a high prey-drive, leading them to need a lot of enrichment.
author: vic1312

entry: Hopping around in search of comfortable places to sleep, POKENAME use their great hearing to avoid predators. During the evening, POKENAME will awaken to find a sunny spot to take in the evening rays before starting its search again.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME project a constant field of positive emotion around themselves, brightening the mood of those nearby. They use their aura to help defuse fights, using their powers to amplify the empathy of others.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME project a constant field of positive emotion around themselves, brightening the mood of those nearby. Their powers make them a popular choice for stage magicians, amplifying the audience's feelings of wonder during the performance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Playful yet mercurial, POKENAME is constantly on the move, seeking new things to interest it. It overextensively explores its surroundings during the night, but is always back home by the morning.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME mischievously causes chaos by knocking objects off of high places. It is believed this behavior was carried over from hunting Taillow in the wild. When its Trainer catches it misbehaving, it makes a cute face and sheds Fake Tears.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This Pokémon uses its intuition to sense where the most comfortable spots to rest are. POKENAME move long before its resting spot can be disturbed.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME can withstand such high temperatures that it wears self-knitted sweaters in the desert, using cactus needles to sew. It likes to knit gifts for other desert-dwellers, but they're usually later found discarded under sand piles.
author: creaturecore

entry: It spends much of its mornings grooming itself or insisting upon its Trainer grooming it to keep its fur from becoming tangled and messy. A well-kept POKENAME will happily, if not overtly, wrap its silky feelers around its Trainer's arm.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time sleeping, but its senses are quite sharp. The moment it senses something approaching too close, it flies off at an incredibly quick speed to find another place to nap.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is the favorite playmate of feline Pokémon, who can't resist chasing its purple yarn balls. Its soft, warm wool is prized for making cozy winter sweaters and hats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME moves elegantly under moonlight. Legends say those who disturb its peaceful resting places may fall under a mysterious charm that leaves them hopelessly lost.
author: ambrosia04

entry: When it eats food it particularly likes, the star on its tail lights up; if it eats its favorite food, the glow is almost blinding. When fighting, it can electrify its claws to make its scratches even more powerful. It should not be underestimated.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Highly curious and playful by nature, POKENAME stand ready to pounce as soon as something catches their attention. The curve in a POKENAME's claws ensures that once it latches onto something, it won't lose its grip until it wants to.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Using sticks it whittles into needles and fur from its body, POKENAME knits toys for its young. The toys help its children practice skills that benefit their development. In battle, it loads the toys with psychic power before launching them at foes.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's fur grows exceptionally rough during springtime. This deters contact, as its body becomes extremely volatile during this period and can explode easily if touched.
author: .izik

entry: Their patience and emotional intelligence make POKENAME popular pet sitters. They look after and protect smaller Pokémon while their Trainers are busy, only occasionally getting distracted by their own toys.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are capricious and can be difficult for inexperienced Trainers to handle. They value comfort above all else, however, so a soft bed can go a long way towards earning their trust.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME is regarded as the perfect mix between “cute” and “cool”. It is a popular contender for Pokémon Contests as most any judge will be wooed by its simultaneously terrifying yet graceful moves.
author: creaturecore

entry: Professors have noted seeing POKENAME use its fluffy tail as a lure to attract passing trainers. Once approached, POKENAME will squirt water at you and laugh.
author: universal9449

entry: POKENAME has a knack for knitting, and makes use of all four arms to do so rapidly. The resulting cozy creations are used to keep young Skitty warm.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME remains at rest all day, meditating as it synthesizes sunlight. Very rarely, it may spar with others using its full strength.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Because of its gentle look, POKENAME is often chosen as a mascot for infant products. Away from the spotlight, it can be found meditating peacefully under starlight.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time meditating, in order to enhance its databanks and calculation abilities. Within computers, meditating for long enough will cause visible ribbons of data to flow into its head.
author: sk372

entry: As a meditation exercise, POKENAME likes to employ its many vines to untangle knots or to weave rugs. Its diet consists of a singular berry, eaten daily.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME sleep and meditate with their eyes open, which often deters would-be predators. If anything or anyone interrupts a meditating POKENAME, it will retaliate with swift, strong kicks and by spitting out flames.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME meditates atop cliffsides to better master its flames. The feathers on its head ignite mid-meditation.
author: .izik

entry: While meditating, POKENAME's secondary maw opens and closes slowly. Some believe the sound affects luck of humans nearby, though no proof exists.
author: .izik

entry: During harsh winters, POKENAME enters deep meditation. It channels inner heat into its skull-like head to endure freezing conditions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a budding master of meditation, able to balance itself perfectly while deep in a meditative state. It is drawn to the scent of burning incense and prefers meditating near the aroma.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME meditates often to center and hone its mental state, but it is still a bit jumpy in temperament. If something startles it during meditation, it reflexively backhands the interruption with its powerful flippers.
author: sk372

entry: While meditating at cliffsides, POKENAME releases a small aura of psychic energy around its body. Those who draw close feel an incredible soothing sensation.
author: .izik

entry: Though made of plasma energy, if POKENAME concentrates really hard it can manifest itself into physical matter to perform fighting techniques. POKENAME possesses machines in order to meditate. Machines possessed in this way will not turn on.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: From sunrise to sunset, POKENAME trains by intensely meditating. This training strengthens the power of its flames.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME spends its life training to master its aura while awaiting evolution, growing stronger each time it patiently meditates. Though it never strikes first, it will not hesitate to retaliate against aggressors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spends its life training to master its aura while awaiting evolution, growing stronger each time it patiently meditates. Though it never strikes first, it will not hesitate to retaliate against aggressors.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME gnaws on abandoned mine carts left deep underground. The more metal it eats, the stronger its telekinetic abilities become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME reads the past of discarded plush toys through psychic means. If it senses neglect, it seeks out the child responsible to play cruel tricks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME senses resting Bug-types within their cocoons using psychic bursts. It then carries them away effortlessly with its powerful jaws.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME concentrate and focus their energy into their spinel eyes, dedicating themselves to clearing their minds. If a resting POKENAME is disrupted, it will create a psychic burst in all directions before disappearing back into the shadows.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME meditates for long periods of time to gain clarity and new fighting techniques. After meditating, it puffs out spores to awaken from its trance before wandering the world to challenge others to battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes for an excellent home guardian. It meditates often to hone its senses and detect when an intruder draws near, springing into action quickly and subduing them with psychic powers.
author: sk372

entry: During battle, POKENAME move in a zigzag pattern to confuse foes before striking with a fierce Force Palm. They spend many hours a day meditating, only stopping to forage for food.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME will meditate for hours, consolidating their training and contemplating their abilities. They focus on straight punches and can often be seen up on their hind legs, training against logs and boulders.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME uses psychic signals to communicate silently with its flock while airborne. These signals allow it to alter group flight patterns with perfect coordination.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME meditate atop bodies of water to calm down after a long day of training. Anyone who tries to disrupt this meditation will find that POKENAME slide across the water to avoid their attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME meditates atop high cliffsides, levitating slightly off the ground as it rests. If interrupted, it delivers an uppercut strong enough to launch the offender up to 10 feet into the air without a second thought.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME studies sumo wrestlers using psychic observation. It can perfectly mimic a fighter's movements after less than a day of training.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend much of their days meditating to hone their spiritual power; as they meditate, their tails tick back and forth like metronomes. They use their honed power to retrieve food and to play with objects, people, and other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: From the moment POKENAME hatches, it enters a meditative trance from which it's impossible to rouse it. The ultra-emptiness of its mind allows it to fully focus on whatever's in front of it, giving it preternatural dodging instincts in battle.
author: kungfucutbug

entry: POKENAME balances atop tall pine trees while meditating on one leg. This practice sharpens both its focus and physical control.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME meditates deep in caves to stay calm. If it becomes irate or sad, its electricity can go out of control and injure nearby allies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME work their muscles way harder than they are supposed to be able to as a Pokémon of their size. Their bodies heal rapidly during meditation which is why they've been known to do so for 8 hours a day in some cases.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME releases gentle psychic pulses to scan cave walls for rare ore. Once located, it digs through the stone to consume the minerals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME points its four hands in different directions to probe cavern walls psychically. When gems are detected, it digs in and devours them.
author: .izik

entry: It lacks a mouth and remains still most of the time. During a fight, it rolls back and forth in smooth yet sudden arcs to throw off foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It displays a profound capacity for predicting its opponent's moves, to the point some believe it can perceive the future. POKENAME hones every part of itself every day, though it mostly fights with its tail and its legs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME leads a solitary life meditating in the desert. Its fighting style is precise and patient; it waits for an opening before delivering a decisive blow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME meditates constantly to keep its mind and body sharp and its soul at peace. Its training gives it powerful precognition, letting it foresee opponents' moves and react calmly and accordingly.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's second mouth opens and closes rhythmically as it sleeps. Subtle psychic waves radiate outward, discouraging others from approaching.
author: .izik

entry: It is a flexible predator Pokémon. When it snatches up prey in its mouth, it stops moving and digests them slowly over the course of several days to savor the flavor.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME practices meditation under berry trees. It waits until the berries start fermenting before it will eat them.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME are capable of telekinetically controlling their crest. They use it to reach far away or flying opponents.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME releases high amounts of psychic waves from its feelers to soothe anyone nearby. It does this with little effort and the range increases when it meditates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME raise their ribbons to block out negative emotions and physically protect themselves while they meditate. If someone tries to enter within the ribbons, the POKENAME will wrap them up and deliver a flurry of kicks.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Combining a disciplined mind with an aggressive temperament, POKENAME has mastered a fighting technique that few are able to face without injury. When not in combat, POKENAME spends its time sharpening its metallic scales and razor sharp beak.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: POKENAME hone their fighting skills through deep meditation. Even as they meditate, they can defend themselves using their nine spirit-like arms, leaving foes with burning bruises that remain painful for days.
author: chibitales

entry: After consuming copper ore, POKENAME's psychic abilities surge tenfold. It struggles to sleep until the heightened energy finally fades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME refine their combat prowess by sparring with other Fighting-type Pokémon. They are capable of soaring above their opponent to tire them out, which gives them a strong advantage over their sparring partners.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's citrine eyes glow as it scans dark caverns for edible gems. Once found, it punches them loose from the rock face with intense force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will try its hardest to spend its entire life meditating, only feeding off moonlight. If its meditation is interrupted, it will furiously flee from the distraction.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME can remain calm and peaceful through deep meditation as long as it's beneath rays of light throughout the day. If clouds block the sunshine, it loses its focus and temper and starts wildly raging through mountains.
author: soup1900

entry: While meditating, POKENAME's bulky body lifts slightly from the ground. If disturbed, it unleashes a forceful Whirlwind to drive the intruder back.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can meditate for days with acute focus to raise their mental acuity. Even though they lack the muscles needed to defend themselves from physical attacks, they can effortlessly launch psychokinetic attacks against threats instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME meditates constantly in an attempt to control its temper. If its meditation is disturbed, it will fly into a rage and attack the source of the disturbance.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME live in remote, solitary environments to endure hard training all day and night. Every morning, POKENAME will make an herbal tea that strengthens the mind and body. It is their only meal for the entire day.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME prefer to meditate by staying perfectly still in their favorite caves or mountains. They are often mistaken for ordinary rocks as a result.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME levitates nearby rocks with psychic power to inspect them. If it senses valuable crystals inside, it cracks the stone open to feed.
author: .izik

entry: In addition to synthesizing sunlight, POKENAME pull electricity out of the air to sustain themselves. If you see a large horde of POKENAME gliding by, it's a good idea to find shelter, as a thunderstorm is about to arrive.
author: .realthree

entry: Once a day, POKENAME run around in circles, generating massive electricity from the friction. They are then able to spend the rest of the day sleeping, as anything that touches them will get a nasty shock.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When a thunderbolt strikes from the sky, POKENAME uses its long beak as a lightning rod to recharge its energy. If anyone is foolish enough to pick up one of its feathers from the ground, they risk getting an electric shock.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME stores electricity in its feathers. Trainers must be careful when handling it or risk getting a nasty shock.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's fur changes color while it sleeps, revealing its charge level; red for low, yellow for average, and blue when full. The color fades when it wakes.
author: .izik

entry: Each day, it stores thousands of megawatts of electricity captured by its large, conductive ears. When the charge reaches its tail, it surges in a wild discharge.
author: catsquatch_geography

entry: High electrical currents run through POKENAME's fins at all times. It slaps foes with these electrified appendages, leaving electrical burns.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are near impossible to take for walks. They move at such high speeds that trying to stop them from running off is fruitless, and putting them on a leash will only result in arm injuries for its Trainer.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME store generated electricity within their bristly fur, so even touching one could trigger a painful shock. Because they sleep often and do not use much electricity, they are almost always overcharged with power.
author: infinex21

entry: The electric pulses POKENAME releases as it walks cause many joggers to report distorted audio in their headphones when one is nearby. Prolonged exposure can permanently damage the headphones.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have been enhanced by fusion, potently increasing their ability to store electrical energy. The static that results from them running through the air can match the power of thunderbolts when stored up and discharged at once.
author: vic1312

entry: The cotton covering its body stores large amounts of static energy, allowing POKENAME to produce sparks in battle. It emits a lemon-like scent that feels invigorating to anyone who breathes it in.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are extremely fast, able to dart through tunnels in a matter of seconds. However, they insist on holding their favourite jewel constantly. The weight is so cumbersome that they rarely reach their full speed.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: It crawls along tall surfaces to better expose itself to atmospheric friction, which it uses to generate electricity. When it achieves a full charge, it will begin hunting and pounce upon its target, unleashing every volt to subdue its prey.
author: infinex21

entry: Anesthesiologists rely on compounds made with POKENAME to dull pain for people who are about to have surgery. Hospitals can place bounties on POKENAME to incentivize harvesting their leaves during busy seasons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME consumes discarded electronics to absorb power from their batteries. It uses this energy to strengthen its electrical attacks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases incredibly high amounts of voltage from its jaws after biting down on prey. The charge from a single bite is enough to power a small building for a full day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fire manipulation ability is still burgeoning and requires practice. When it fails to ignite the stick it carries normally, it zaps one end with lightning from its body to set it alight.
author: sk372

entry: Often employed to search for lost Trainers, POKENAME sense electrical currents given off by all creatures. Once located, they protect their charge at all costs, howling and sparking intimidatingly at any perceived threat.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME form small packs and hunt other Pokémon at lightning-fast speeds. Even much larger prey can quickly fall victim to their vicious night time hunts.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME generates electricity in its fur by running about in a zigzag pattern. The more it runs around, the greater the electrical burst it will inevitably discharge.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME generates electricity while running, gathering more internal energy the faster and longer it runs. After a point, it even begins leaving trails of crackling lightning behind it as it dashes around.
author: sk372

entry: It utilizes atmospheric friction to generate electricity as it flies. Although it can release bolts of electricity at a distance, it has a tendency to dive at foes and try to shock them through its talons and fangs.
author: infinex21

entry: While migrating, flocks of POKENAME release bursts of electricity from the tips of their wings to redirect their paths. They can also absorb electricity from power lines simply by standing on them with their talons.
author: .izik

entry: Flocks of POKENAME can be seen often during storms at sea. They fly directly into the storm clouds, coming out crackling with electricity they've absorbed from within.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME scoops young Pokémon into its bill and delivers shocks at regular intervals to incapacitate them. Once they are unconscious, it swallows them whole.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME presses its soft ears against machinery to absorb electricity from within. It can survive for months without eating as long as it absorbs enough electricity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hop up and down during storms to build up static electricity to try and call down lightning bolts. Their tails act as lightning rods, so being struck by lightning only increases their energy.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME runs nimbly through grasslands and forests to catch its prey. Despite its deft speed and skill at taking down rodent Pokémon, it is unable to keep up its sprint for long.
author: .realthree

entry: When POKENAME senses someone approaching its nest, a loud engine noise can be heard. Should this occur, one should flee immediately, as it will soon release a beam of electricity from its mouth capable of knocking over an oak tree.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can cross a football field in a blink, fueled by their powerful and electrified leg muscles. They love to play fetch with their Trainer, though their Trainer rarely gets to keep up with their energy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME relies on its small size and lightning-fast speed to win battles. In a pinch, it is known to absorb electricity from nearby devices to generate more voltage for attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When its friends start losing, POKENAME stimulates the muscles in its hands to cheer them on harder. As long as its friends are losing, it will keep on stimulating its muscles to cheer, even when they become extremely sore and worn.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME converts energy from its meals into electricity. When threatened, it spits out a sticky substance to impede its foes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's serpentine body sprays sparks as it slithers across the forest floor. When it spots prey, it fires bolts of electricity to stun them before swallowing them whole.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will rub their fur against prey to completely paralyze them. To train for evolution into an Eelektross fusion, it stimulates the muscles in its paws to be able to temporarily crawl on land.
author: soup1900

entry: Camouflaged as fresh kelp, they electrify the water around prey that approaches unawares and then finish it off.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME is a very lazy predator, waiting for hours with its tail dipped in the water, hoping that some prey will take the bait. When it gets tired of waiting, it releases electric shocks into the water to bring something to the surface.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is known for its greedy nature, stashing away anything it deems valuable in its den. Items recovered from these dens have included coins, rare berries, and even gemstones.
author: mepp.

entry: If a POKENAME notices a traveler wearing fine jewelry, it will attempt to steal the trinket with silky string. Due to its poor aim, it usually fails.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attracts loose coins using static electricity. If startled while counting them, it may explode in a shower of sparks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are arrogant fighters, but have something of a code of honor. They prefer to fight a weapon-wielding opponent, if only so they may dramatically disarm them in battle and gloat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spend most of their days cleaning themselves with their tongue. Due to this frequent cleaning they often get hairballs stuck to their tongue.
author: elite01.

entry: POKENAME often spend much of their time taking catnaps because they are unable to move until they evolve. They often purr when they are stressed, which confuses predators long enough to lose interest in eating them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gas is mildly toxic to people, causing an altered mental state in those exposed to it for too long. Breathing the gas in over long periods of time creates feelings of avarice and a desire to hoard wealth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though POKENAME spend most of their day lazing in the sun, they are sometimes seized by a manic burst of energy. These energy bursts almost always result in property damage due to POKENAME crashing through walls and furniture as they race around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses its ruby horn to dig in cave walls in search of gems or rare ore. It will mine for hours if the scent of gold is strong.
author: .izik

entry: While normally a kind and helpful Pokémon, it jealously guards the gem it carries. It will hold a lifelong grudge against any who attempt to take it.
author: knilk

entry: Not all of the yarn in POKENAME's body is attached to it. There are several extraneous strands that have been dragged along for the ride.
author: .realthree

entry: It is protective of the Meowth that it raises in its pouch. POKENAME is very proud of its child, though it is rather dismissive of any pranks or cheeky antics the Meowth may commit.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: Though difficult to take care of, POKENAME adds an air of regality to home aquariums. Scientists debate on whether the color and size of the gem on POKENAME's head is influenced by its diet of microorganisms when it's young.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's forehead gem shines before it lashes out. During combat, it swings its blades wildly at anything nearby.
author: .izik

entry: The gem on the head of a POKENAME is coveted by poachers. Its shine and purity increase based on how angry the POKENAME gets.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swarm in groups of ten, nesting in old shacks by clinging to walls with their sticky feet. They store shiny objects to lure in prey like Murkrow.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME rules its waters with cold precision, its glittering form gliding past like a serpent. Other Pokémon part before it, knowing it does not tolerate disobedience.
author: mgfox_66676

entry: POKENAME are incredibly proficient hunters, using their transformation abilities to hide almost perfectly, then pouncing on flying Pokémon when they land to rest.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: POKENAME are incredibly proud of their mane and will frequently flaunt it to all who stop to admire it. They do not hunt down shiny objects as much as they used to, but they will treasure any shiny items given to them and be very protective of them.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME fur prickles and stands up on end when they're startled, sparking with electricity. They shoot out powerful bolts of lightning toward whatever scares them, focusing the bolt through their forehead gem.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It is extremely prideful and turns aggressive if any of its fur is made dirty. POKENAME is able to amplify the heat of its red fur to burn away small debris caught within it. If it overheats, it will rest for an entire day to recover.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body will regularly shift its shape based on the last image it has seen on a webpage. It frequently can be seen on shopping websites, where it consumes sales-based data.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME form colonies within the branches of large trees, feeding on the leaves and hiding within the bark when predators approach. They purr to one another to communicate, creating the illusion that the trees are making a constant low noise.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their tails to cling to tree branches while they gather the strength to evolve. They are almost completely immobile but give out a loud hiss to try and scare off threats that get too close.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its diamond-hard claws allow POKENAME to crack through the shells of other Pokémon. It adores shiny objects and will commonly grab lost jewelry or small pearls to take back to its den.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are said to fly around the world in search of gems shinier than their own, willing to do anything to collect them. They give away smaller gems to Meowth and Sableye once their collection grows beyond their control.
author: npshi

entry: The gem on POKENAME's forehead glints an angry red whenever they spy another Pokémon encroaching on their territory. The glint catches the attention of other POKENAME, drawing the entire swarm to descend on the unfortunate intruder.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fur is prone to igniting when stroked, making them a dangerous Pokémon to keep indoors. They appear not to realise the risk they pose to others, purring as they attempt to rub up close against people they care about.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can sense changes in the wind with their whiskers, preferring to be upwind of their opponent during Pokémon battles. They can flare the fire burning in their fur to release large plumes of smoke, choking their foes in battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME steal coins and shiny objects from Trainers to decorate their nests. They are so infamous for this practice that many police officers search POKENAME's nests for stolen items.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Considered a luxury pet, they're often kept as companions to people hoping to cultivate a glamorous image. Unfortunately, this is an ill-fitting lifestyle for POKENAME, as its nervous nature leads it to hide in dark places where it cannot be seen.
author: zephyr.txt

entry: During auspicious events like the lunar new year, POKENAME beg their Trainers for small red envelopes. Most Trainers opt to give them a few coins to avoid their whining.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses Foresight to predict when someone with treasure will pass by. It ambushes them with uncanny timing.
author: .izik

entry: Its wool is incredibly soft and valuable, so POKENAME is always treated with the utmost care to keep its coat in the best possible condition. It is a mischievous Pokémon that enjoys shocking even the humans who care for and feed it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME jealously guards its favorite gem by wrapping its tail around it. It will leap to defend it at the slightest provocation.
author: howlingstarr

entry: POKENAME enjoy mimicking their trainers, pretending that they have their own Poké Balls and Pokémon to battle with, striking poses as a battle starts. They make a happy purring noise when praised for their mimicry, enjoying the positive attention.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The glow of the gem follows the eyes of nearby onlookers. Due to recent poaching concerns, their numbers in the wild have dwindled.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME decorates its den with shiny refuse like tin foil and soda tabs. Sleeping near the shiny objects gives it great comfort.
author: .izik

entry: It's often claimed that POKENAME was the reference for creepy Jack-in-the-boxes. They are sometimes seen crawling on city walls and roofs.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME is very popular among children. It loves the attention, even if there is a little roughhousing. It especially loves being stroked on the tufts of fur protruding from its face and purrs contentedly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME is very popular among children. It loves the attention, even if there is a little roughhousing. It especially loves being stroked on the gills protruding from its face and purrs contentedly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: They are considered a lucky Pokémon to raise, as their pheromones release Luck Incense into an area. These pheromones only work on people and help promote a magnanimous feeling after losing a battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Well known for its traitorous and manipulative nature, POKENAME puts on a friendly mask to build trust with others, only to then attack them when their guard is down to rob them of valuables. It typically only truly listens to the one who raised it.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME pecks at passersby while its flock rummages through pockets to steal valuables. They vanish before the victim notices.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sensual creatures that enjoy rubbing against people. Fortunately for those with allergies, they shed very little pollen and dust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While scavenging, POKENAME will abandon food the moment it finds shiny trash. It always carries treasures back to its den.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can rarely be found wandering around old jungle ruins and are exceptionally friendly toward Trainers. They are considered to be a sign of good luck for explorers.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME hangs from strong tree branches using its strong tail while using its whiskers to sense disturbances in its environment. When it senses prey, it drops and snaps its tough jeweled shell around the target.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME harness their feline charm to beg their Trainers for food. Most Trainers capitulate to their demands, causing them to become quite spoiled.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's head gem blinks in patterns to signal its flock. Together, they attack rival bird Pokémon that enter their turf.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gems light up when they sense air movement, reacting quickly to incoming attacks with an evasive fighting style. They leave trails of red light behind them as they fight, lunging in with their metal claws for rapid strikes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are dutiful minions of villainous organizations that have no qualms about ethics. They are pragmatic creatures that would abandon their Trainer at the drop of a hat if it meant more food at the end of the day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME, despite being slow, are nearly silent and excellent at sneaking. They're commonly used by bank robbers to steal entire vaults full of Pokédollars without notice.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME is a fierce hunter, but also a highly finicky eater. It hunts and eats only certain parts of prey such as Arbok and Raticate, then leaves the rest for scavengers to pick at.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME paralyzes humans with venom before dragging away their valuables. It sleeps coiled atop piles of stolen coins.
author: .izik

entry: If startled, POKENAME unleashes psychic waves from its forehead gem. Most threats flee before a second blast is needed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's limber and flexible body allows it to easily fit into places other Pokémon its size could not. With its speed and the ability to freeze those who gaze upon it with a sharp Glare, wild POKENAME prove very elusive to catch.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is carefree to the extreme; it is difficult to ruin its good mood. However, it lacks the same devotion as Blissey, and does not feel the need to heal others in the wild. It may do so if asked if given glittery and shining trinkets.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME rarely parts with the gem it holds, even when munificent gifts are offered. If anyone tries to steal the gem, it ferociously claws the assailant to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a crepuscular Pokémon. Strong sunlight hurts its eyes, so it often squints during the day.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME are devious creatures that enjoy pulling pranks on their peers. They often get other Pokémon in trouble so that they look better by comparison. Despite their faults, their razor-sharp claws and perseverance give them an edge in battle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's yarn-like vines move like nimble fingers. It's so dexterous it can pickpocket Trainers without being seen.
author: .izik

entry: In some ancient civilizations, POKENAME was tasked to guard over precious locations. Those who wished to enter would have to pass tests of intellect that POKENAME judged over.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries coins in shallow holes throughout its territory. Its memory is so precise, it never forgets a single spot.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will inhabit computers that are left unattended. They will repeatedly play cute cat videos, appearing to be greatly amused by them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME spits seeds at passersby from treetops, then swoops down to steal trinkets. It vanishes into the canopy with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME's fur repels water, allowing it to swim swiftly. Combined with the hearing ability of its large ears, it can find and pursue prey with ease.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME enjoy putting on performances for onlookers, twirling and dancing on stage in groups. Their whiskers are sensitive to the movements of others, enabling them to keep in time without needing to look at one another across the stage.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drift along just above the ground, allowing them to move completely silently. Their whiskers are sensitive to the emotions of others, drawing them to those struggling with self-doubt.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME will stalk Trainers with large amounts of wealth and slowly steal away their valuables when they're not looking. Once all their wealth is gone, it will finally take their soul.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly picky eater, refusing food until it finds the berries it wants. It hates being touched and will jab its Trainer with poisonous barbs if they try to pet it.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME smears toxic liquid from its whiskers onto the coins in its den. The scent keeps rivals and thieves away.
author: .izik

entry: Respected by humans and Pokémon alike, POKENAME is the ultimate feline. It only shares food and fortune to those it truly trusts.
author: kill_the_wabbit

entry: It treats most other Pokémon with disdain, since its sheer size has left it with few natural predators.
author: dicedragon20

entry: POKENAME protect their grand treasures with tricky riddles. If a person fails to answer their riddles, it is said that they are transformed into a Pokémon until they learn the correct answer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME secretes paralyzing venom from its whiskers to immobilize targets. It strikes quickly to steal jewelry.
author: .izik

entry: Moving with feline grace, POKENAME fights using a peerless martial style that uses slicing maneuvers to weaken its opponent. The more it weakens an opponent, the more wildly it fights, as if delighting in its increasing advantage.
author: ocxin

entry: POKENAME has an independent streak and a sense of superiority to the point that it rarely, if ever, allows anything to touch it. Getting too close without its permission results in a flurry of slaps and scratches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME pride themselves on their regal beauty, demanding tributes of riches and jewels to further enhance their grandeur. If a POKENAME's status is questioned, it will bring one of its crystalline flippers down to smack the offender.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's nose always turns toward nearby gold. Prospectors follow it through caves to find ore veins hidden underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME functions as a finely forged sword as well as treasure detector, determined by the mood of the Persian head pommel.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: This POKENAME was once wielded by a legendary treasure hunter. The explorer was said to have been able to verbally communicate and understand it.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME steals shiny objects from its own kind to assert dominance. The largest hoard earns the highest status.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has many admirers, though prospective Trainers should be warned it is fickle about who it shows it's affection to.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME thinks of itself as king in a literal sense and will attempt to rule over other Pokémon living in the same area.
author: snugglessam

entry: This variant of POKENAME is very popular in the fashion world. Many men's clothing lines will feature POKENAME sporting the latest trendy fashions.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME enjoy taking people on journeys across the sky, using their sensitive whiskers to sense air currents and drift as it chooses. It's advised to travel in pairs as they sometimes grow hungry during a flight and try to feed on lone occupants.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With its aerial speed and quickness of claw, POKENAME is adept at taking anything it wants. Most often found in urban areas, it will snatch up prey and human meals in equal measure.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME steals shiny objects from junkyards and slashes at anyone who tries to stop it. Its claws leave strange cuts that shimmer under moonlight.
author: .izik

entry: Haughty by nature, POKENAME rarely lets itself be seen by humans and only comes out during the dark of night. It is more amiable during the full moon, but only slightly; it quickly becomes standoffish again the very next night.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME is extremely obsessed with its appearance, it spends most of its time grooming itself. It unleashes a furious assault towards anything foolish enough to test its patience.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's thin fur grows dangerously hot when it sees coins. Scientists are baffled, but collectors use it as a coin detector.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sports thick, coarse fur in place of armored plates. However, its ability to groom its coat is often impeded by its axe-like tusks.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME sports thick, coarse fur in place of armored plates. However, its ability to groom its coat is often impeded by its axe-like tusks.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME are a popular choice among Trainers with allergies because of their hypoallergenic fur. Breeders sell them for large sums of money at auction because of how popular they have become.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are very popular pets as they are both docile and do not require much food. However, if its habitat gets too dirty, the gems on its back will become dull and brittle.
author: mistymagius

entry: Vain and territorial, POKENAME will not suffer the indignity of anything being in close proximity to it. With a disdainful backhanded flap of one wing, it spreads embers all over any who would dare invade its space.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flies around, swooping down to pursue prey suffering from the heat of the desert. Flames slip across the surface of its feathers, surrounding like ribbons. Everywhere it flies, an intense heatwave follows.
author: tamszen.ore

entry: POKENAME keep their disguises clean to appeal to their Trainer. Whenever they eat, they reserve a piece to give as an act of submissiveness.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have two heads that are particular about their appearance. They often rely on the preferences of their Trainer to break up arguments, as the two heads will bite each other if they cannot come to an agreement.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using their sensitive whiskers and near-silent wings, POKENAME are able to stalk prey while remaining out of sight. When the moment is right, they pounce and restrain the target by clamping their three mouths onto the target's extremities.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have tongues with special backward-facing barbs that help them clean their fur. They spend a significant amount of time cleaning their body because their fur can easily get matted, especially their tails.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are fussy and very particular Pokémon, making them a challenge to train and care for. Historical records suggest that POKENAME were once considered to be vessels for regal spirits, each of their tails holding a different ancient monarch.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME senses a mischievous aura, the gems on its body pulse pink. Trainers say it glows brightest near casinos.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gets extremely excited over shiny objects and will take anything shiny without a second thought. It will sometimes even get mesmerized by its own golden claws.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is highly independent and hates being touched. Those that try to pet it without its trust and approval will see it hiss and shed sparks from its fur, the only warning they get before it uses its claws and electricity in full.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are fussy and very particular Pokémon, making them a challenge to train and care for. Historical records suggest that POKENAME were once considered to be vessels for regal spirits, each of their tails holding a different ancient monarch.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a silky and glamorous fur that makes them stand out in beauty contests. They amaze audiences with their fiery techniques and sheer beauty.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The gem on POKENAME's forehead pulses red in time with their song, matching their melody beat for beat. Those who hear their song quickly fall asleep, POKENAME then curl up atop them and sleep alongside them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME enjoys playing in sand pits, digging out hollows before circling around and sitting within them. It lunges at anyone who intrudes on its personal space, snapping at them with its powerful jaws.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is smug and egotistical, intensely proud of the flame on its tail and regularly flaunting it towards others. If enough attention isn't paid to the beauty of its flame, it uses it to set things on fire as petty vengeance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sings soft lullabies in campsites to make travelers drowsy. It then floats off with stolen valuables.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sense changing air currents with their sensitive whiskers, adjusting their buoyancy to catch the breeze. During storms, they deliberately tangle their feet in tree branches, remaining stuck there until the storm passes.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sense changing air currents with their sensitive whiskers, adjusting their buoyancy to catch the breeze. They use the breeze to drift between tropical islands, able to travel tens of miles without touching the ground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Using its psychic powers, POKENAME hoards every coin and jewel it spots inside its special liquid. It occasionally extends its whiskers out of the liquid to sense whether any thieves may be lurking nearby.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME reads minds to locate valuables, then levitates them away while victims sleep. Its lair is always perfectly organized, placing differently colored objects in their own pile.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are known for stealth, often seen ambushing small prey or stealing food. Their soft paws let them scamper about silently.
author: carameldog

entry: POKENAME purrs have a soporific effect, lulling those who hear them gently to sleep. They make excellent therapy Pokémon, helping insomniacs achieve a solid night's sleep.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME screeches at a high pitch to confuse cave explorers. While they cover their ears, it snatches rings and earrings.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are drawn to large quantities of money, hanging around street corners and ambushing people to steal their money. This habit makes them popular Pokémon with organised criminals, handing the stolen money to their Trainer.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are drawn to large quantities of money, hanging around street corners and ambushing people to steal their money. They have no concept of how much an individual note is worth and seem to simply enjoy rifling through wads of cash.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME stalk their minuscule prey before pouncing. They're equally apt to chase the light from a laser pointer.
author: hophoppip

entry: Sharp red gems grow from POKENAME's back. It fires them like darts at intruders, later retrieving the ones that glitter most.
author: .izik

entry: The velvety soft fur and feathers of POKENAME make it highly sought after by the wealthy. If unhappy, it will violently flap its wings, releasing shining embers in frustration.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME stalks city rooftops, diving to bump into pedestrians and steal whatever they drop. Its eyes glint with mischief shortly before a strike.
author: .izik

entry: On sunny days, POKENAME lies flat on warm rocks, soaking up heat. Its fur stands on end, crackling with slight amounts of static.
author: .izik

entry: The rubies on POKENAME's sides glow deep red when its venom reaches peak potency. This glow often signals it's about to strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME barrels into travelers to scatter their belongings, then zips away with anything that sparkles. It can roll faster than 70 mph.
author: .izik

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME love to curl up in the laps of their trainer. They roll into a ball, purring loudly as they pin their trainer in place. They can spend hours in one place, refusing to move until they've received enough attention.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Packs of POKENAME stomp across the landscape, watching for the glint of the garnets in each other's heads as a means to keep track of others in their pack. When they track down prey, they deliver a powerful Bite that is able to puncture steel.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME stomp across open plains in small prides, roaring to one another to communicate. They work together to drive prey into an ambush, where the rest of the pride lies in wait.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its leaves are used as a calming remedy for Pokémon like Meowth and Persian, who are particularly drawn to their fragrant aroma. Though POKENAME is naturally peaceful, it doesn't hesitate to fight back with fierce headbutts if disturbed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Wild POKENAME produce coins after eating lots of metal, but this behavior has not been found while in captivity. People who are desperate for coins follow wild POKENAME to take their coins.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Anything POKENAME touches will turn into a toxic, gold-like metalloid. Its entire body is comprised of this mysterious substance.
author: musicsheep.

entry: The only thing it loves more than wrestling is money. POKENAME are known to take dives in matches for comically small bribes.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME have a rebellious and condescending attitude that makes them difficult to train. They only listen to confident Trainers and refuse to obey commands from those who show nervousness or doubt.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will spread spores on spots it claims as its territory. The spores are harmless but irritating to the eyes and nose of anything but itself. Trainers have found that spraying POKENAME with water helps discourage this behavior.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live at the bottom of rivers and ponds, feeding on much smaller Pokémon. They can sense even faint water movements with their sensitive whiskers, scurrying to safety the moment they think something larger than them is chasing them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is incredibly vain and spends a lot of time fussing over its appearance. A lot of people find them hard to deal with, but they do make great pest control.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME are very playful and love to play with all types of random objects. If you plan on owning a POKENAME, it best to get them as many toys as possible.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is often used by evil teams, using its toys to distract enemy Pokémon. However, it frequently gets distracted by its own toys and ends up flying in circles instead.
author: mistymagius

entry: Just before it breathes fire from its mouth, the precious gem on its forehead shines brightly. POKENAME is an extremely spoiled creature; it might even scratch its Trainer if offered food it doesn't like.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME launches coins from its burrows using Pay Day. The closer intruders get to its home, the faster and harder the coins are fired.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps clustered inside cavern walls. Its deep, rumbling purr echoes loudly and can be heard from the opposite side of solid rock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is easily distracted by shiny objects. A single coin tossed away can keep it busy for hours.
author: .izik

entry: This self fusion of Persian is covered in extra-long, soft fur.  Though it will meticulously groom itself, it's often demands that its owner brush it regularly to help get rid of built-up, loose fur.
author: infranscia

entry: POKENAME is a very fickle species that refuses to live anywhere but the cleanest of ponds. It has been known to attack its handlers when displeased, but grabbing it by the whiskers makes it docile.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME becomes violently enraged if anyone approaches its coin hoard. Even eye contact can trigger an outburst.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a very difficult Pokémon to raise due to its behavior. Spoiled and moody, if it doesn't get what it wants, when it wants, it flies into a tantrum of swinging fists and slashing claws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live together in small packs. The one with the most magnificent beard is the leader, who is accepted by every pack member without exception.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME is an extremely proud Pokémon that only obeys experienced Trainers. However, it would even risk its life for one.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME's fur has a glossy and oily sheen that allows it to effortlessly swim through water. As it matures, its fur becomes even more vivid and sleek; POKENAME never allows anyone else to touch it carelessly.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in the ruby on its belly and can often be seen near rivers trying to clean and polish it. The unique spiral pattern on the jewel makes it highly sought after by collectors.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite being an outstanding swimmer, POKENAME will do anything to avoid getting its tail wet.  It uses its long tail to distract and confuse adversaries.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME floats yarn out of shop windows with psychic waves. It weaves the strands into nests lined with velvet and coins.
author: .izik

entry: When basking in the aroma of an Odd Incense, they transmit thoughts of their desires to creatures and people nearby. Typically, this results in vivid imagery of a desire for milk or fish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are known as great conquerors of the seas. With their claws, they invade islands and seek to control entire archipelagos. For them, wounds are synonymous with courage, and they show them off with eye patches or by striking a pose.
author: spagalapof

entry: POKENAME's aggressive combat style has been dubbed the "Fist of the Beast King." It's popularity resulted in a supporting role in a popular television franchise, though its roles often suffer an unfortunate fate.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often attributed to tales of great heroics and expert swordsmanship. Whether these tales are true has yet to be determined, but they inspire other POKENAME to emulate them.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME protects its precious silky fur by retreating into its shell whenever it senses danger that might threaten its beauty. Though it dislikes fighting, it won't hesitate to scratch anyone it dislikes with its small claws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hang by their tails from tree branches, using their whiskers to sense incoming rain. When they sense impending rainfall, they yowl unhappily to one another, prompting them to curl up tight and try to shelter from the rain.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hang by their tails from tree branches, using their whiskers to sense changes in the wind. When they sense a strong breeze, they give excited purrs, enjoying the feel of being buffeted by the wind.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hang by their tails from tree branches, using their whiskers to sense passing Pokémon. When they sense a Pokémon getting too close to them, they hiss and spit out acid in an effort to get the other Pokémon to back off.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME laze around on the jungle floor with their mouth wide open. They can remain motionless for days, waiting for small Pokémon to wander into their mouth, snapping their mouth closed on their prey when it walks in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lurks near the shallow waters of oceans, waiting for large gatherings of people. Its greedy nature compels it to appear before these groups and use its many tentacles to steal as many shiny baubles as it can to hoard for itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will gallop wildly if lured with a shiny object. Trainers sometimes toss coins to coax it into races with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME sees something shiny, its flames flicker red and blue, forming a cumulative near-purple glow. Some believe these flame colorings make it run faster.
author: .izik

entry: Domestic POKENAME are often reported as showing highly spoiled behavior. The three heads constantly fight over food, toys and affection.
author: sk372

entry: Its soft fur was used in the past by nomads in frozen regions to protect themselves from harsh temperatures. Its gemstone horn can release powerful ice beams.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its soft fur was used in the past by nomads in frozen regions to protect themselves from harsh temperatures. Its gemstone horn can release powerful ice beams.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are cynical creatures that work with villainous organizations. They are well-compensated for the jets of water they fire from their backs and refuse orders if they are not happy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Extremely territorial, POKENAME will not hesitate to discharge its entire reserve of electricity if its habitat is disturbed. A single outburst is enough to shock an entire lake, instantly paralyzing anything within POKENAME's waters.
author: ambrosia04

entry: It can fire deadly electric blasts from its metallic claws as if they were cannons. Despite its entire body being made of steel, POKENAME is capable of moving at astonishing speeds.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can power PCs with a just brief jolt of electricity. Many scientists have found that its zaps increase the efficiency of the PC by 67 percent.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As this Pokémon runs at lightning speed, electricity builds in its arms and crackles wildly off its wrists. A single Thunder Punch from a fully charged POKENAME can level a building.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME channels electricity through the blades on its arms. When it swings them, the air crackles with lightning.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are energetic creatures that can seamlessly change their camouflage as they run. The only thing that matches their speed is their boundless love for their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is prone to attracting thunderstorms. When lightning strikes POKENAME's shell, its plates may vitrify into Thunder Stones. This phenomenon is why it is common to see Pikachu living on POKENAME's back.
author: pjporwoll

entry: One should be wary of provoking a wild POKENAME. The dust clouds its wings kick up are also supercharged with its electricity, leaving its foes blinded and beset by powerful discharges of lightning on all sides.
author: sk372

entry: The increase of thunderstorms in the springtime allows POKENAME packs to hunt while concealing their presence. They use lightning to corral grazing herds and pick an easy target, then strike.
author: chibitales

entry: All the yellow sections on POKENAME's body glow slightly at night. When POKENAME flies nearby, any lights will flicker until they have passed.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME makes its nests where lightning has previously struck. It collects items that are left behind by Trainers and stores them in its nests.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's warm fur thickens in winter. When startled, its static surges and every strand stands on end.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's electrified powder allows it to paralyze almost any Pokémon in seconds. This same powder also causes Pokémon to be more susceptible to electric attacks, further weakening them against this Pokémon.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME shocks the water with its electricity, then snatches up stunned prey that floats to the surface. POKENAME are often seen in large groups squabbling over food.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME can overstimulate its muscles with all of its electricity to run faster than lightning. However, its muscles will become very sore afterwards, so it must painfully rub its paws along the ground to create enough friction to recharge.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME summons thunderclouds that drop gigantic lightning bolts over enemies. The width of one of these lightning bolts can span over many feet.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME zips around from place to place, its speed being described as similar to a lightning bolt. It uses this kinetic energy to generate its electricity.
author: soup1900

entry: When it roars, flames spill out from its maw and electricity surges from its statically-charged fur. Its territory is marred by scorch marks left bey flames and lightning bolts alike.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME travel high in the clouds, unimpeded by storms and other bad weather. Its high body temperature allows it to tolerate these freezing heights.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Reports of lightning streaking across plains are attributed to POKENAME herds chasing storms. The electricity in their bodies causes their hooves to heat to high temperatures, leaving burned hoofprints where they run.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's shed skin still retains a residual charge of electricity within it. Scavengers looking for a quick snack end up receiving a nasty jolt when they take the first bite.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known for being popular choices of partners for Pokémon Rangers. They use electricity to vibrate the strings of their ukuleles to play uplifting tunes.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's wool has a strong positive charge. When in herds including negatively-charged Mareep fusions, they get stuck together in a massive ball.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME has more control over its magnetic charge. It seeks out negatively-charged Pokémon to increase its power.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME's tail acts as an extremely powerful, positively charged magnet. If it smacks against something with a negative charge, violent thunderbolts occur.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are powered by positively charged electrons due to their specialized fur reacting to the sun's light. Sunlight can be converted into electric power that is used to devastate their foes.
author: cobalt0135

entry: A passing flock of POKENAME is regarded as an omen of good fortune, their positive energy inspiring those who see them to greater heights of performance. They seem to enjoy circling over sports grounds, crowing happily as the games play out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's body consists of battery acid, powering its electrical attacks. It's friendly in nature, but Trainers should approach it with caution.
author: hophoppip

entry: While climbing flat surfaces, POKENAME's entire body courses with electricity. It does this to ward off predators such as Beedrill.
author: .izik

entry: The most cheerful Pokémon of the jungle, POKENAME will rub against tree trunks to build up static electricity. It will then reroute this electricity to its hands, using it as pom-poms to cheer others on.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: By running in place, it builds up a static charge and causes its internal flame sac to become active. It discharges electricity from its tail & cheeks and spits out small flames to cheer on other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses its athletic build to perform impressive flips and kicks as it cheers on its teammates during a battle. While this Pokémon is happy to support its friends, POKENAME would much prefer to be the one in combat.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: While often found at sporting events, POKENAME can also be spotted at the base of mountains. There they do their cheer routine to inspire climbers going up and congratulate those coming down from a climb.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME has quite the happy-go-lucky personality. It can often be seen palling around Mudkip in the wild, prancing around their mud hole home, and spreading sparks as a sign of joy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME presses the fins on its head against electric meters near homes to absorb their power. This can lead to widespread blackouts in an area.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cheers on allies from the sidelines, its dances and chants creating psychic pulses to boost them. POKENAME's cheers are said to make an ally's greatest strengths even greater.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME wraps its tongue carefully around power lines while camouflaging its skin to match the pole. This allows it to siphon electricity without being easily detected.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hides in caves during the daytime. If disturbed, it latches onto the offender with the mouth on the back of its head and unleashes high voltages of electricity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME peeks its long ears above the surface of creeks during thunderstorms. It does this to absorb electrical energy from the air.
author: .izik

entry: After releasing an electric attack, POKENAME's feelers carry an incredibly strong positive magnetic charge. This charge intensifies when it attacks during a thunderstorm.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME sneak into nightclubs to practice their cheering sessions for their fellow Pokémon. They leave trails of red static cotton that can shock anybody who touches it after the session is over.
author: doctorjazznumber6215

entry: When overly happy, POKENAME releases electric pulses that cause nearby electronics to begin sparking. If it is not calmed down, these pulses can cause serious damage to the devices.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sings chipper, upbeat songs to cheer on its allies and boost their morale in battle. It rubs its cheeks to create sparks that it can fling into the air to add to the flair of its performance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a passion for cheering on others. When they turn, their gears make loud clicking sounds in celebration.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: Bursting with positive energy, being around POKENAME has been proven to raise the serotonin levels of those nearby, improving their mood as a result. While the exact reason has yet to be pinned down, POKENAME's cheerful attitude may help contribute.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME stores copious amounts of electricity in its buds like batteries. Should a Trainer touch one, their hair will rise due to the static.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME cheers, it rubs up against Minloon, causing a squeaky noise that sounds like happy encouragement. It likes to encourage those who are very confident, as they get distracted enough for POKENAME to easily cut down.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: The yellow liquid POKENAME produces is extremely poisonous but carries an intense electrical charge. Many companies throughout the world use it to make batteries.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME repel other Pokémon that have a positive electrical charge. This leads them to live solitary lives, afraid of pushing away the friends they care about.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The static electricity that POKENAME harnesses is purely a positive charge. It is commonly used in radio towers, as when it dances, it emanates radio waves. The radio wave frequency is dependent on the style of POKENAME's dance.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME loves to eat rotting food and stores any excess in its den when full. It sleeps atop its hoard at night, using Discharge on anyone who draws too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's pointed teeth carry a strong electrical charge in them. The bite itself is painful enough, but the real harm comes from the paralytic effect that takes place shortly after, leaving prey unable to move and escape being hunted.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's song and dance routines are meant to boost the spirits of its friends while they fight. Pokémon on the offensive fight even more fiercely when POKENAME's cheers back them up.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lead groups of Plusle, acting as their cheerleading captains. When excited, they will throw their electric pom-poms up where they burst into electrically-charged confetti.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: When POKENAME pops up from underground, it can't help but cheer on battles it observes. It creates small bursts of sparks with its ears to encourage the combatants to do their best.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME spots a couple at the beach, it grows extremely happy and flops out of the water, flailing on the sand. It unfortunately releases an electromagnetic pulse during this period that can destroy nearby electronics.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wander tall grass looking for berries or scraps to feast on. Whenever they meet another of their kind, they fight over the food until one prevails.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whenever POKENAME cheer for their friends, they zigzag around in circles to draw attention to themselves. Their boundless energy helps keep up the performance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: During the winter months, POKENAME nests near running mechanical equipment for warmth. While sleeping, it absorbs small amounts of electricity when it cannot find enough to eat during the day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release electricity from the tips of their tails. The sticky threads they spit out conduct electricity well, but POKENAME mostly use their threads to wrap up bundles of food; these Pokémon love to share these food bundles with friends.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are attracted to excess energy and will often find themselves anchored on electrical poles and transformers. If they feel an incomplete circuit, they will attempt to use their conductive silk to reconnect it.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME prefers to fly during thunderstorms in hopes of being struck by lightning to absorb the power. When struck, it scatters a glittering yellow powder from its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are commonly found stuck on telephone poles, absorbing the electricity through its conductive silk.  This silk is in high demand for use in state-of-the-art electronic wearables.
author: imaginita

entry: POKENAME releases large bursts of electricity from its wings while feeding atop telephone poles. These bursts allow it to communicate with other POKENAME in the surrounding area.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME enters a cloud, it can kickstart a storm as its body charges electricity over time, transferring positive charges upon contact.
author: lucioleuh

entry: POKENAME attempts to scoop transformers off electric poles with its large bill to steal their power. If the transformer is properly secured, it grows extremely irate and repeatedly sprays it with water.
author: .izik

entry: As it skims the surfaces of ponds, POKENAME emits pulses of electric charge. The abrupt change in conductivity brought by a predator's approach sends POKENAME skittering for safety.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME waves its antennae to and fro, showing support for its allies. Sparks shower from the antennae's markings in a motivational spectacle.
author: lordjoostmeister
