entry: POKENAME is able to use psychic powers, using its gills to amplify them. However, this can become too intense if sustained, so it coats its gills in mud to dampen the signal.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's layers of fat are its pride. The most optimal complexion decides the pack's leader. POKENAME are docile in nature and like hugs.
author: megaban

entry: POKENAME live in swamps where the cattails on their back blend in perfectly with their environment. They are sensitive to the motion of the swampy water, which makes them difficult to sneak up on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The whiskers of a POKENAME will grow slowly while it sleeps. It will panic and dive deep into the water at the slightest noise.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME patrol underwater ruins to keep ancient secrets safe. When they find a Trainer within the depths, they release a loud quack that summons other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME wait patiently during battle for their opponent to make the first move. They react quickly when they sense an attack coming at them, opening their beaks and shouting out a deafening, defiant honk.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The gem on POKENAME's tail glows to attract prey. Once they draw near, POKENAME quickly sucks in to inflate itself, dragging small Pokémon right into its mouth.
author: mepp.

entry: It has incredible aim, able to hit Flying-type Pokémon from hundreds of feet away with its aqua cannon. Its shell is protective, but it's heavy enough that it causes POKENAME to sink in water.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME spends its entire life inside its thick armored shell. It shoots jets of water from its retractable cannons to blast itself from place to place.
author: leonian1586

entry: The bright red feathers and gems on a POKENAME are seen as status symbols. POKENAME with larger, more vivid feathers are typically seen as more agile. POKENAME with brighter gems are seen as clever and worthy of respect from peers.
author: entomoxie

entry: The gem on POKENAME's shell glows a beautiful crimson when it uses its psychic abilities. It uses telekinesis to lift prey from rivers before spitting boiling water at them to subdue them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can fly and swim excellently due to its unique feathers. Its long neck and tough beak let it poke its head into otherwise hard-to-reach areas for food.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can walk on dry land, but it prefers to stay in or near vast lakes. Its plumage keeps it warm even in the coldest environments, though it is less active in subzero areas due to a need to conserve energy.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME thrives in colder climates due to its remarkably thick plumage. Its beak and tusks are tough enough to break through ice sheets and get otherwise hard-to-reach food.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME is typically found in cold mountains all around the world, always doing everything with other POKENAME. Its tail can store enough food to keep it and its peers going for weeks.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can fly great distances due to its lightweight but oddly tough plumage. Its tough feathers also allow it to fly in the rain and swim expertly.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME heat the water around them into a roiling steam, making it easier for them to swim through it. The approach of a pack of POKENAME is heralded by steam banks drifting to shore, leading to many legends ascribing them mystical powers.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME marks its territory with paint-like substances from its tail, with markings varying vastly depending on the water where it lives. Some prefer freshwater while others prefer saltwater. No two POKENAME produce the exact same paint.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME cuts through the water at lightning speeds, diving within to hunt fish before breaching onto land and racing across the region. It only slows down during thunderstorms, where it calmly basks in the rainfall.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live high up in mountains and spend their time seeking out mountain springs to relax in. Their bodies run at very high temperatures meaning any spring they climb into quickly heats up and becomes pleasant to bathe in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Due to its sheer size and weight it sinks to the bottom of the ocean. However POKENAME will often train strenuously by swimming to the surface every day.
author: baz2600

entry: POKENAME race one another to be the first to reach visitors to their pond, each hoping to be the first to be fed fresh berries. They are persistent, following people for hours around the park until they eventually lose interest.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can ride ocean currents with its mostly flat body, though it can also maneuver expertly when riding them. It is deeply familiar with the patterns of ocean currents where it lives.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can fly underwater as if it were still in the sky. Many rescue teams use it to save people who are lost out at sea.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME produce leaves that slow down their bodies when swimming. They often let other Pokémon snack on the leaves so that they can swim faster.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorb sunlight through their leaves to gain necessary nutrients for survival. Once they have enough nutrients, they allow other Pokémon to eat their leaves so that they can swim unencumbered.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME glides across its icy lake home, forming slick trails of frost beneath its feet. Its movements are elegant and silent as it hunts for prey.
author: .izik

entry: When using its psychic powers, the gems on POKENAME's forehead and back shimmer. It swims effortlessly through the jungle's rivers, easily escaping predators.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME looks for wetlands to settle in, acting as a caretaker for the Pokémon living in the local environment. It listens to the local Pokémon's requests and concerns, doing anything in its power to help.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME drift across the surface of still lakes, searching for visitors along the shoreline. Their gems glow as they approach, projecting feelings of empathy and care in the hopes that the person they approach will toss them food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME drift across the surface of still lakes, searching for visitors along the shoreline. They honk to one another when they spot a person, converging on the visitor before holding out their hands in the hopes of being gifted food.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: During a Pokémon battle, POKENAME jet through the water to slice up their opponents. They always fight with honor and dignity, refusing to resort to underhanded tactics to achieve victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in small family groups along the edges of lakes. They take turns keeping watch while the rest of the family drinks or feeds, honking out an alarm call for everyone to scurry into the water to safety should danger arise.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME dive into the sea to tear open fishing nets and grab onto whatever aquatic Pokémon that escape. Many fishermen have upgraded to tougher fishing nets because of the damage POKENAME cause to traditional rope nets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME effortlessly slice through fishing nets to release the aquatic Pokémon trapped inside. They have earned the ire of fishermen everywhere for eating the aquatic Pokémon that were supposed to be trapped in nets.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stalk places fishermen frequent to get easy access to Water-type Pokémon to eat. These opportunistic creatures often clash with fishermen who are angry with POKENAME for stealing their fish.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are surprisingly fast swimmers that leave a trail of pollen wherever they go. The pollen gets absorbed into other plants, which end up making sections of the swamp quite toxic to herbivores.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are protective of their swimming grounds, barrelling toward any Pokémon that's as large as them that dares to enter the water. They honk aggressively, lashing out with venomous spines if they can't scare away the target of their ire.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lives on the shores of lakes. Its tough exoskeleton, sharp claws, and strong tail allow it to easily hunt for prey and defend itself.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME is often seen swimming in lakes. It uses its telekinetic powers and enormous claws to punish those who pollute its home.
author: the_fireplace

entry: POKENAME have a large red dome atop their heads that absorbs the shock from their headbutts. It is said that if it ever cracks, a wave of psychic energy is released.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spend much of their time sleeping while holding onto their fishing rod. They often reel in Psyduck, which they toss back into the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME weave nests made of dried out reeds and mud, hiding them along the banks of lakes. They are fiercely protective of their eggs, their gem-like horn shining bright red whenever they charge another Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME arrive on coastlines atop a wave to warn residents of upcoming floods. They swiftly swim to fishermen at sea to help them reach shore before calamity strikes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME slides across the water's surface at high speeds to chase down prey. The water boils as it passes, leaving a steaming trail across the ocean's surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME struggles to balance on land due to its large head. However, its buoyancy and psychic powers make it an adept swimmer. It also keeps it warm in waters of any temperature.
author: entomoxie

entry: When POKENAME spots hidden prey using its X-ray vision, the gem on its forehead glows with a red light. It uses the aquatic environments where it lives to amplify the power of its devastating electric attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When its star-shaped tail glows, it means it's about to unleash a devastating electric attack. This variant of POKENAME usually makes its home along the rivers of Kanto, which is why it's easier to spot in that region.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a marvelous swimmer, cutting through the water at an extremely rapid speed. It picks fights with larger creatures just to evade their strikes and keep its maneuverability honed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its webbed paws to swim gracefully around the lakes and slow-moving rivers that make up its habitat.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME honks echo across entire lakes, alerting all those that can hear them that the waters are claimed as their own. When two POKENAME try to claim the same lake, they end up battling for supremacy, exchanging brutal body blows.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A legendary figure depicted in some paintings as the guardian of the most pristine lakes across the world. Should it surface from its home beneath the waters, it will blast intruders with blasts of steam shot from its tail.
author: sk372

entry: At night, POKENAME swim in patterns that resemble constellations. These complex patterns are always followed with high precision, as POKENAME are incredibly detail-oriented.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's plumage is water-repellent, allowing it to swim gracefully at high speeds and emerge from the water almost completely dry.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are capable of submerging their bodies underwater. Their eyes allow them to see above and under the surface rather clearly, and their wings are adapted to serve perfectly as fins.
author: sonic3knuckles

entry: They swim across wetlands, dabbling to feed on water plants while keeping their tails above the surface. If threatened by a large predator, POKENAME releases heat from its tails to ignite marsh gases and create a burst of flame.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME lie in wait on shores across the world. When they spot prey, they use their beaks to strike swiftly and catch them off guard. They target only smaller, weaker prey due to their limited mobility on land or in water.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME curiously poke around using the ice cream cones tied around their disguises to investigate piles of leaves and check water quality. If a stranger gets too close, the red gems in their disguise will shine a small beam like a laser pointer.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Once POKENAME begins building itself a dam, it will accept no others anywhere near the lakefront it lives in. It smashes the dams Bidoof and Bibarel create, and steals the broken wood to use for its own.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME typically stay in vast oceans and have thick plumage to keep them warm. They struggle to move on dry land, as they require large bodies of water to stay hydrated.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are popular companions to lifeguards, standing watch at the water's edge for anyone struggling to remain afloat. If they spot someone floundering, they leap into the water and swim over, puffing themselves up to be a life float as they do.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A POKENAME is an adept swimmer. The bubbles on its tail calmly emerge when POKENAME is happy and burst out when it is enraged.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME hide themselves amongst reeds and rushes along river banks, relying on the tall plants to conceal themselves from danger. When they're startled, they rapidly waddle into the water, drifting downstream to safety.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Flocks of POKENAME make their nests around lakes, darting in and out of the water in their hunt for small Bug-type Pokémon. Their feathers are coated in hydrophobic oil, keeping them dry and ready to fly no matter how long they spend in the water.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can see even in the darkest of caves due to the gem-like protrusions on their claws and heads. Their beaks can open unusually wide, letting them eat large bites of food at a time.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME dig long tunnels with sharp claws in search for the perfect gemstone. Once it has found one that's long and flat, it will use it to surf on waves as its favourite pastime.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Underwater, POKENAME is a surprisingly swift and silent hunter. Most fish won't even realize they're being watched and hunted until it's too late, and an entire school has vanished into its hungry maw.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME form a thick bubble with their own psychic powers. These bubbles keep POKENAME safe and let them control their body temperatures. They also allow POKENAME to predict upcoming weather events.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME freezes a thin layer of water around its face to form a protective ice layer. The clearest and most vibrant piece of ice on this mask is the red orb between its eyes.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME drifts around colder areas with its mysteriously light and hollow body. It can freeze any intruders solid and decide what to do with them after carefully examining them in a chunk of ice.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can swim faster than most other Pokémon, rivaling even speedboats. Their beaks are sharp enough to pick through rocks and ice with ease.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME are among the fastest swimmers of any Pokémon due to the shape of their feathers and smooth body plans. Their mouths can engulf smaller Pokémon in a single bite.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME considers itself protector of its mangroves. It lurks among the submerged roots, dangling its gems as bait for anyone greedy enough to pluck one.
author: wormspawn

entry: POKENAME considers itself protector of its mangroves. It lurks among the submerged roots, dangling its gems as bait for anyone greedy enough to pluck one.
author: wormspawn

entry: Due to their light feathers and vast wings, POKENAME are excellent at flight and swimming. Even in the dark, they use their large ears and psychic powers to map out their surroundings ideally.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME easily blend in with heavy fog thanks to their cloudy wings. They rely on this dense fog to surprise aquatic Pokémon, skewering prey onto their beak.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoy flying on top of vast, clear oceans. Their cloud-like wings keep them in the air for weeks at a time. When angered, they can even send intense rain or lightning from their wings.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME swim back and forth across rivers to help Pokémon cross the rapid flow of water. Even though they produce a poisonous gel atop their lily pad, many Pokémon simply wash off the toxic substance in the nearby water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME usually lie in wait, with their bright red thorns acting as eyes and seeing their surroundings. As such, sneaking up on a POKENAME is nearly impossible. Their thorns can deliver a powerful toxin to those who try.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME exhibit a certain smug confidence that comes from their ability to reliably find water reservoirs in the desert. There has been no recorded instance where POKENAME fail to find water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The red spine across POKENAME's body can detect minute changes in humidity, making it great for finding water in the desert. Once it comes across an oasis, it completely submerges its body to thoroughly hydrate itself.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefer vast beaches in moderate climates. The mysterious gems in their bodies are said to let them commune with the spirits of those who recently passed.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's damp skin and tendency to swim in stagnant water leave them vulnerable to fungal infections. The mushrooms that grow on their back release their spores into the water when submerged, letting them spread to uninfected POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The crystals on a healthy POKENAME are clear and bright in color. In the dark, they can emanate a mesmerizing glow.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can swim with perfect precision even in the darkest and murkiest of waters. They can do this by using the gem-like protrusions on their bodies to sense their environments. They can read the minds of other Pokémon approaching them.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME mushrooms are a popular ingredient in many high-end restaurants thanks to their unique, gamey flavour. Connoisseurs feel it is best enjoyed when grown in damp conditions, encouraging POKENAME to be raised with plenty of water access.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's ruby-colored scales shed during the spring, leaving new scales that are soft and vulnerable until hardened. In the past, the shed scales were collected and used as currency in lakeside villages.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME often emerge from their aquatic homes to accost and goad passersby into a battle. They typically prefer wrestling and will do anything to win. If POKENAME loses, they diligently provide any service requested of them.
author: wiz0z

entry: POKENAME mushrooms are a popular ingredient in many high-end restaurants thanks to their unique, gamey flavour. POKENAME are prone to infection if the mushroom is allowed to dry out, spoiling the taste.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The meringue-like substance atop the head of a POKENAME has a mellifluous consistency that pairs well with cookies. They attract many Pokémon because their sugary aroma is hard to mask.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To swim even faster, POKENAME increases its internal body temperature, channeling energy into its muscles. The flame on its tail never goes out, not even when it dives into rivers or lakes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME patrols underground routes between lakes. It surfaces only during the day to swim briefly and gather reeds for food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are competitive swimmers, racing others of their kind constantly to establish hierarchy among a group. It's said those who spy these races in real time will have a tumultuous love life.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be seen swimming in a perfectly straight line at dusk. It can use telekinetic powers when the gem on its forehead flashes.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME has a large head for its body and a mysterious gem in its forehead. While it has vast psychic energy, it is rarely able to control it, often ending up with intense headaches whenever it tries.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have large heads for their bodies and mysterious gems in their foreheads. While they have vast psychic energy, they are rarely able to control it, often ending up with intense headaches whenever they try.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have large heads for their bodies and mysterious gems in their foreheads. While they have vast psychic energy, they are rarely able to control it, often ending up with intense headaches whenever they try.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME has completely abandoned the use of its eyes and relies solely on its ESP abilities to sense its surroundings. POKENAME stores all its psychic energy in the glowing, red-hot gem at the centre of its face.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME can change forms when exposed to different types of weather. Regardless of what form they take, they enjoy swimming as a leisurely activity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love swimming in hot water and heat the water around them until it is scalding. Many aquatic Pokémon that cannot hop onto land will sink lower into the water in an attempt to escape the heat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoy splashing water around on rainy days, much to the dismay of many Pokémon trying to seek shelter from the rain. Even though POKENAME are remorseful for their antics, they cannot contain their excitement whenever it rains.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoy swimming in icy cold water and will blow across the surface of lakes and rivers to sharply decrease the water temperature. Many Pokémon are uncomfortable with the sudden drop in temperature and will leave until it warms up again.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have capricious tempers that come out in tantrums. Trainers often train them in places with lots of water, giving them an outlet to vent frustration.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To swim even faster, POKENAME increases its internal body temperature, channeling energy into its muscles. The flame on its tail never goes out, not even when it dives into rivers or lakes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By elevating its internal temperature, POKENAME generates the energy needed for rapid underwater dashes. Remarkably, the fire at the tip of its tail burns steadily, glowing even when fully submerged.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By elevating its internal temperature, POKENAME generates the energy needed for rapid underwater dashes. Remarkably, the fire at the tip of its tail burns steadily, glowing even when fully submerged.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Fiercely independent and stubborn, POKENAME tends to not get along with other Pokémon. While it spends most of its waking moments underwater, it rests on land.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME swim in strange swirling patterns that radiate outward from a central focal point. Their specialized tail prevents the water around them from splashing, so they do not deviate from their predetermined path.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can swim around surprisingly well. The spiral patterns on their bellies disorient any Pokémon trying to swim after them, keeping them safe when swimming at high speeds.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME trains intensely every day to perfect its swimming abilities. If a wild Pokémon disturbs its practice, it strikes back with its powerful punches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME has the strength and stamina to swim around a small island in less than an hour. Despite being able to quickly catch food, they seem to prefer to slowly fish for their meals.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are deceptively fast swimmers for their diminutive size since they are capable of crossing a lake in a few seconds. They can curl into their shell mid-swim if they see a predator to protect their limbs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME swiftly maneuvers through treacherous water, especially the whirlpool formations surrounding the Whirl Islands. It uses the toxins on its tentacles to disable prey for a leisurely meal after exercising.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME produce flames from their body that remain bright even when underwater. Their galloping does not end at the water's edge since their flippers allow them to swim.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME majestically gallop on both land and sea. The beautiful array of flames that come from their bodies draw many people to watch them travel at night.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can move on dry land, though they much prefer swimming in clear lakes or rivers. They frequently get lost in their own thoughts, drifting on the water's surface without even realizing it.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have large shells that would slow down most Pokémon, but they are deceptively fast swimmers. They reach a top speed of 60 miles per hour, or nearly one-hundred kilometers per hour, in a matter of seconds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can move on dry land or in the water, though they are rarely able to walk or swim quickly. Their psychic powers allow them to be in perfect harmony with the Psyder on the tail, so catching them off-guard is quite difficult.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME have varying preferences in branches. A POKENAME will find a branch that it likes, keeping the stick at all times and aggressively fighting those who try to take or break it.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME love to compete and will race one another from one shoreline to another. Having each of their three heads being coordinated and amicable with the others allows them to reach higher speeds.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can thrive anywhere, even glaciers and ice-covered oceans. Their feathers strangely resemble a thick coat of fur.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME can swim in warm or cold waters alike. Their fins are actually thin flaps covered in uniquely light feathers, though their feathers are effective at insulating body heat.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME zip past other aquatic Pokémon in their massive shell to swim long distances in a matter of seconds. Their water cannons give them extra propulsion while swimming, which ends up knocking other Pokémon out of their way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rarely leave their shells, only poking their beaks out to eat. They struggle to move on dry land, but they are excellent swimmers.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME's pendulum shines brightly when used to channel psionic power. Its pendulum is made of the same material as the gem on its forehead.
author: theartemis1

entry: It likes to test its power of hypnosis on subjects by swinging its pendulum. When the subject is hypnotized, they use a jet of water to wake them up.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME are often found on sandy beaches, enjoying the refreshing ocean tides and breezes. Their pincers are typically just as tough as their bills.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME waddles slowly along the banks of rivers and bays. It channels unusual powers and moves through the jewel-tipped pincers it has.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's gems flash an angry red when they spot another Pokémon trying to take their food. They sidle up to their competitor, clacking their claws menacingly and making a loud honking sound to scare them off.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: With its companions, it timidly explores the desert dunes once night has fallen. If POKENAME senses danger, it spins like a top and digs a small tunnel in the sand to hide safely.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is a skilled little craftsman most known for the spinning toys it creates from mud, clay and the like. It happily shares the toys with friendly human children, but seems wary about giving them away to adults.
author: sk372

entry: The stand POKENAME resides atop is necessary for its transformations, spinning it around and letting POKENAME mold its body to a new form. Should the stand cease its rotation, POKENAME's body will lose cohesion and return to normal.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME infiltrates a system, the monitor begins spinning uncontrollably for several minutes. Attempts to interrupt it result in a sharp electric shock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are mostly immobile, hanging from tree branches as they await evolution. If in danger, they can spin rapidly before detaching themselves, drilling into the ground. This process expends a lot of energy, however, delaying their evolution.
author: santon5512

entry: It may rhythmically wobble back and forth, but provided POKENAME is conscious, it will never fall down. It doesn't seem to fall asleep; it simply goes dormant.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME loves making friends, but said friends should keep a careful distance. It expresses joy by spinning around rapidly, often accidentally smacking things with its long, solid ears.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever POKENAME feels threatened, it rotates rapidly while firing sharp spiky projectiles from its body. The spinning is necessary for the defensive measure, as it can't fire its spikes while standing still.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME were once hunted by ancient societies to make scaly clothes. Many children of the past had coming of age ceremonies that involved taking down a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is almost constantly rotating in place, and maintains a perfect balance, righting itself immediately if anything knocks it over. It gets very sick and weak if it stops spinning for more than a few moments.
author: sk372

entry: Since ancient times, POKENAME have been known to rapidly twirl before crowds to act as entertainment. No matter how dizzying or prolonged their performance, they always perform a precise bow as a grand finale.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME live in arid conditions where water is scarce. They burrow underground in search of water, as just a few drops of water can keep their bodies well-hydrated. Without water, their body begins to flake pieces of clay until they can find water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME elegantly balances itself on its single foot and moves by spinning on said foot. To guide itself and avoid crashing, it uses psychic powers to perceive a surrounding area.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are almost always balanced atop at least one foot, even when they sleep. It is believed that they innately use their psychic powers to hold themselves upright.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the claws on its underside to grip tightly onto cliff faces, before turning and grinding until it removes a chunk of stone. It gathers up these rock chunks to make a personal den for itself.
author: sk372

entry: Believed to have been used as foot soldiers by tacticians of a long gone age, POKENAME seem to have been used to simulate battle scenarios. POKENAME are loyal to a fault to whoever they deem their "commander", a role usually filled by a Claysharp.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: POKENAME has a fantastic sense of balance when on all fours. However, this quickly changes if it gets flipped on to its back. The spike on its forehead is capable of crushing boulders many times its size.
author: captainjefejefe

entry: POKENAME were recently discovered in desert regions living deep in underground lakes. Schools of these Pokémon have been observed swimming in circles in perfect unison for hours on end.
author: mepp.

entry: This Pokémon's body resembles a dried and hollowed spiky fruit. Archeologists discovered that ancient people used POKENAME for trapping evil spirits rather than storing food or liquids.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME plant themselves in the ground by rotating rapidly, all so that they may hide from predators during the day. They become more active under moonlight, which is what they absorb and metabolize.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's body is an antique teapot, but its soul is much older. Cracks in the teapot reveal a mysterious steam filling the inside.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME live in the hot desert, where they constantly search for water. On the rare occasion they find it, a few drops allow their clay body to become soft again.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a mysterious Pokémon that lives deep in underground caves or among ancient ruins. It communicates emotions by rattling its terracotta scales, the faster they shake, the more agitated it is.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in underground ruins, where it scrapes sand in a pile around itself. If anyone walks by it, POKENAME spins rapidly, blasting the sand in all directions.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME spin rapidly underground, burrowing like a drill. Their heads are tough enough to drill through solid concrete.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME spins in a swirling dance around the ruins that it inhabits. It frequents rooms that archeologists say were used as nurseries for children.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME attach the tops of their heads to tree branches to siphon nutrients for themselves. The more nutrients and water they absorb, the heavier they grow. Though they inevitably fall due to their gained weight, they always land on their feet.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are often found flying above ancient ruins. By spinning their bodies at high speeds and diving at opponents, they can pierce even the thickest armor with their beaks.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can safely store anything it eats in its clay body. People have attempted to use it as a traveling container, but this only agitates it and causes it to dissolve their belongings.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: It loves to dance and spin, but has awful coordination. For that reason, it stands perfectly still while being looked at to avoid embarrassment.
author: kiwiarms

entry: A potent battler and grappler, POKENAME incorporates spinning into a majority of its techniques. It's particularly noted for its lariats as well as a powerful spinning piledriver.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spins on one leg at a time. Even while spinning, their body remains flexible, allowing them to dodge attacks. A poisonous liquid leaks from their mouth.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME can be found on the ocean floor, where they stare up towards the surface. Each POKENAME constantly blinks its many eyes in a unique pattern. Scientists think POKENAME are doing this to communicate.
author: fenragon

entry: Despite its bumbling appearance, POKENAME is formidable once woken up from its multi-day naps. Its body is malleable, feeling similar to modeling clay.
author: hiimhdere

entry: Though POKENAME appears fearsome with many eyes, it often guides travelers who are lost in the desert. Ancient legends claim that these eyes peer into the past and future, making it a symbol of wisdom.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can detach an eyeball and still see through it no matter how far away it is. They are known for sneaking an eye into their Trainers' bags just to keep track of where they go during the day.
author: jaminmcready

entry: These Pokémon enjoy guarding items of high value. People attacked by POKENAME will not remember after the fact.
author: hiimhdere

entry: The many eyes on POKENAME's rotating head can focus and analyze anything near it in seconds. Many places with sensitive data use it as a way to watch out for any viruses or other digital abnormalities.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be commonly found in tombs and mausoleums that date back thousands of years, yet very little is known of their origins. Some archeologists theorize that POKENAME were once used to worship a deity that precedes even Arceus.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: POKENAME's spells are so strong they shatter the clay guarding its purple spirit core. Wary of humans, it tends to remain in desert depths, hiding among dunes and forgotten ruins.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can be found around ancient jungle temples, being clay monuments created by an ancient civilisation to protect the temples. Its strong psychic powers allow it to float in the air.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Multiple eyes on POKENAME's body allow it to sense challengers coming from any direction. Its disembodied hands can fire highly-condensed beams of concentrated fire or energy.
author: sk372

entry: Though POKENAME appears to be perpetually asleep, it constantly manipulates several objects through telekinesis. It's theorized the eye-like orbs that float near it allow it to see its surroundings even while sleeping.
author: sk372

entry: These levitating Pokémon often live within, or around, ancient ruins. When they twirl and dance, the eye-like growths hanging from their heads emit hypnotic waves that make it difficult to look away.
author: infinex21

entry: One legend states that the first POKENAME were a conglomeration of the souls of eight thousand soldiers and their steeds that served under an emperor, sealed within clay shells so their service lasts forever. POKENAME are dutiful and utterly silent.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's secondary mouth is reinforced with a dense clay exoskeleton. Even though the clay cracks easily, it can bite clean through solid boulders with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's hollow clay body releases eerie echoes during the night. Its cries grow louder as midnight approaches, filling the ruins it dwells in with dread.
author: .izik

entry: Some ruins contain pottery believed crafted by cultists devoted to POKENAME. Valued possessions were sealed inside as offerings in hopes of divine favor.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's feelers are composed of an incredibly moist and malleable clay. It whips them at foes that get too close to its tomb habitat.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that from the eyes on its coils, POKENAME fires rays to destroy meteors that get too close to the world. For this reason, researchers nicknamed it the Guardian of the Atmosphere.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body melts when exposed to water, so POKENAME lives deep in mountainous caverns. When threatened, it shoots beams of ice from its many eyes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME gathers in groups of three inside ancient tombs, posing as harmless plush dolls. Explorers who touch them are struck by a sudden and furious Psybeam.
author: .izik

entry: With its incredible psychic powers, this Pokémon is able to control every sand grain inside its body. By itself, POKENAME is completely immobile, so it uses the makeshift sand limbs to move and catch Ghost-type Pokémon with.
author: milchik

entry: Its body is made of a strange clay that never dries out. When its moving, its body takes on inscrutable shapes.
author: hophoppip

entry: The wings of POKENAME can detach and spin, mesmerizing its prey with a fiery display. Its many eyes are the source of psychic blasts that sear into viewers' minds.
author: femaledog

entry: Rumors of a "sci-fi monster" coming from a ruin-filled area were originally waived as a hoax, but the stories were proven when one Trainer emerged with a POKENAME in a Poké Ball. It is believed there may be several more throughout the world.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME were once lauded in ancient civilizations for their ability to sing with multiple voices. They helped old villages and towns fall asleep after a long day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clings to the ceilings of old tombs, waiting to ambush explorers. Once its fangs lock onto prey, prying it loose becomes nearly impossible.
author: .izik

entry: The many eyes on a POKENAME's body can see directly into the souls of humans and Pokémon alike. The eyes on its back, in particular, can peer into the distant past.
author: entomoxie

entry: The many eyes on a POKENAME's body can see directly into the souls of humans and Pokémon alike. The eyes on its back, in particular, can peer into the distant past.
author: entomoxie

entry: When it sings, an ancient melody is heard; why POKENAME knows the melody is unknown. POKENAME bathes in mud to remove any small parasites. It is thought that psychic powers allow it to fly, not just its wings.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Said to be a set of ancient clay figures that gained sentience, POKENAME lacks an organ that could be defined as a brain. Instead, the three heads communicate with one another through an invisible psychic field.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Ancient murals depict POKENAME as companions to a lost civilization. They remain constantly attentive to their Trainers, levitating onto the Trainer's lap or shoulders and purring softly to comfort them when they're feeling down.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The eyes along a POKENAME's hat watch in all directions while the POKENAME balances on its tail. If an opponent is detected, the POKENAME will spring high into the air before dropping down onto its foe with a devastating Slam.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If POKENAME attempts to sharpen its swordlike tail against a wet stone, its blade will melt and become useless. After sinking its fangs into prey, it blasts lasers from both teeth to rip them into shreds.
author: soup1900

entry: These Pokémon are seldom seen, but are said to appear during times of great change in the world. POKENAME never make a sound and tend to hover in the sky to observe Pokémon battles.
author: fenragon

entry: POKENAME is able to predict upcoming meteor showers, with its eyes glowing in the direction of the astrological event. While it sleeps most of the time, when it is awake, it uses its psychic powers to pull food into its hungry maw.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's eyes, except the central one, constantly move and are believed to be looking into different times and dimensions. Ancient records indicate one first appeared descending from the night sky and hovered over a town before disappearing.
author: pjporwoll

entry: From various ports across their shell, POKENAME can produce multiple drones controlled with telepathy. These drones, known as gazers, act as POKENAME's primary means of sight as their actual eyes are very poor in most conditions.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME puffs out clouds from its body at all times. The food it consumes affects the color and scent of these clouds.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME floats across the region, offering to ferry others on its back. Its body adapts to the weather conditions around it, changing to ensure its passengers are protected from the elements.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can transform itself into other Pokémon, or alter its own form to suit the weather. In some rare cases it can combine the two processes, creating weather-based forms for the Pokémon it mimics.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's DNA is especially unstable and malleable. Both the weather conditions and its habitat will affect it over time, leading to potentially countless variations in its appearance.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME goes for a swim, its body morphs to adapt itself to the water conditions, such as freshwater, saltwater, swamps, etc. This shifted form remains for around an hour after it returns to land.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME drifts too close to aircraft, it siphons data from their navigation systems. If disturbed, it unleashes a piercing cry before firing a Weather Ball.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME guards the hives of other insect Pokémon with quick flight and sharp stingers. The texture of its wings and the type of toxin its stings deliver differ depending on the weather.
author: sk372

entry: Constantly creating vapors in their shells, POKENAME cool these vapors down and passively puff them out. Thin trails of fog are a tell that a POKENAME has passed by.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's many vines change texture and color to adapt to the weather around it. When it changes back, some occasionally will be stuck in their transformed state, so POKENAME with a few discolored vines are a not-uncommon sight.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have the impressive ability to modify the molecules that make up their form. Oddly, they tend to use their skills for manifesting props and making minor changes to their appearance, unlike other transforming Pokémon.
author: ohok3441

entry: The body of a POKENAME changes on a cellular level to adapt to weather conditions; further studies determined that their molecules are much like water. Within their cloudy horns, they can liquefy and absorb foods; they cannot liquefy large matter.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME sits in clouds all its life, catching any souls who pass through. If an airplane passes through its cloud, POKENAME will get scared and flee to the upper atmosphere.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Because past sightings of POKENAME involved watching its form change in response to the weather, old civilizations believed POKENAME controlled the weather itself. This is false, but it can create localized weather effects in a short range around it.
author: sk372

entry: Facsimiles of weather-based Pokémon form on POKENAME's back. One can typically estimate upcoming weather by seeing if one or more of these imitations becomes active.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is becoming an increasingly popular companion. It senses upcoming weather and opens up automatically, shielding its Trainer from the elements while soaking up sun or precipitation to further sustain itself.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's prismatic ribbons cast out small rainbow sparkles as they waft about. These tassels can affect the mood of others around it, with the emotional effect varying depending on the weather.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME circles the planet from the ozone layer in search for extreme weather to adapt to. Recent studies suggest the molecules of its body consist almost entirely of water.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Thanks to a combo of thin, specialized fur and a low body mass, POKENAME can catch gusts of wind to float in the air. Researchers have found POKENAME flying above hikers in the mountains, watching them from a distance.
author: ohok3441

entry: Normally, POKENAME remains sedentary and transparent in appearance, but when weather conditions become extreme, it lights up and becomes active. The color of the light it casts depends on what type of weather surrounds it.
author: sk372

entry: Depending on the weather around it, POKENAME can drastically alter its physical form. Research currently theorizes the weather may also affect its approach in battle between attack, defense or speed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sings a different type of song depending on the weather of its surroundings. No matter the beat or tempo of its song, its music is always effective at putting the listener to sleep.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body alters in response to strong weather conditions. It seems happier when its body begins to transform; some believe it is self-conscious about its normal appearance.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dreams of flying among the clouds and spends much of its days staring up at the sky. It is deeply sensitive to changes in the weather, often rushing headlong into when sensing oncoming shifts in weather.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It slowly drifts through the sky. When groups of this Pokémon drift together, they're often mistaken for clouds.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are sensitive to changes in their environment. By detecting pressure differences, POKENAME can readily adapt to their surroundings and overcome their poor eyesight.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The cloak POKENAME holds tightly to its body reacts to outside stimuli, adapting to protect its wearer from the elements. This lets it traipse through almost any inclement weather condition without a problem.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is wary of humans and rarely appears before them, watching them from somewhere hidden. The weather of its surroundings seems to play a part in how it decides to deal with humans trespassing on its home.
author: sk372

entry: By performing energetic dances, POKENAME can alter the surrounding weather. Storm clouds gather when it spins rapidly, and lightning strikes often follow the rhythm of its movements.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME generates strange psychic bubbles through the protuberance on its head. When the bubbles pop, they emit bursts of sunlight, snow, sand, or wind.
author: sk372

entry: It can generate clouds and fog. In battle, it uses these powers to its advantage, obscuring its position with fog before ambushing the foe.
author: hophoppip

entry: When not enduring any extreme weather, POKENAME's shell becomes overly uncomfortable. This leads to wild POKENAME in the ozone layer launching themselves to the surface to break it.
author: h0bojoe

entry: When its shell breaks in average weather, POKENAME reveals a neutral core. Experiments show that simulating weather with heaters, showers, or freezers cannot change its form.
author: h0bojoe

entry: This trio floats around on a cloud at high speeds, looking for criminal schemes to stop. Many cities and towns attribute it to regularly saving the day from evil.
author: sk372

entry: Like a cloud, it wanders lazily throughout the day. When it's feeling playful, its cloudy body gains a pearlescent shimmer.
author: hophoppip

entry: It meditates for hours, attuning its mind to the atmosphere. With enough discipline, it can forecast weather changes to the second, and even control the weather around it.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's long whiskers can detect shifts in humidity and temperature. Its cells cause its appearance to change in response to weather conditions.
author: fiordaliso

entry: This rare type of POKENAME lives high in the ozone layer where the air is the purest. Some speculate it to be the truest form of Castform, and so far, scientists have been unable to recreate it in artificial conditions.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME takes on this form during early spring when the temperature only begins to rise and the first sun rays start melting the snow. This Pokémon carries the scent of a fresh sunny morning wherever it flies.
author: milchik

entry: When POKENAME appears like this, it's a sign of the first autumn drizzles approaching. Mushroom pickers use hoards of these Pokémon as a guide to where fresh shrooms will soon grow.
author: milchik

entry: When the temperature drops just below zero, POKENAME shift into this form. They can barely produce any snow of their own and follow the early winter winds to sustain themselves until it gets colder.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME work in tandem with other variants of each other as well as news stations to predict the weather. If they don't feel respected enough, they sometimes manipulate the local weather as payback.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME becomes easily attached to anyone who is nice to it. An innocent, companionable Pokémon, it follows its Trainer wherever they go. Snow and ice are used to nourish them; in the wild, they follow snowstorms at high altitudes to stay healthy.
author: fireblade141

entry: After evolving, POKENAME is large enough to fly with up to four people upon its back. This Pokémon is very popular with explorers, and aerial pictures taken from the backs of POKENAME are a very popular image genre.
author: fireblade141

entry: Despite its Fire typing, it prefers water to dry land. Wherever it swims, the water surrounding it becomes pleasantly warm.
author: hophoppip

entry: The orbs circling around POKENAME radiate a warm heat not unlike sunbeams. It is fond of plant-life, so it's common to see it levitating one or two of its orbs near plants to ensure they get plenty of sunlight and warmth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body gives off a pleasant summery heat. Its wool can be sheared and crafted into plush-looking clothes that are light enough to stay cool in.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's glossy feathers shine a brilliant amber in light. Collectors often use these feathers alongside glass or crystals to craft stunning suncatchers that cast a vibrant reflection. Its prismatic crest helps it stand out during breeding season.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's glossy feathers shine a brilliant amber in light. Collectors often use these feathers alongside glass or crystals to craft stunning suncatchers that cast a vibrant reflection.
author: chibitales

entry: While naturally being incredibly hot, POKENAME can lower their temperatures down to 75°F. They can be used as 'replacement suns' for plants that're struggling to grow.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's warm body always glows faintly. The condition of sick plants has been known to improve when POKENAME is near.
author: mepp.

entry: During the winter months, POKENAME becomes aggravated, flying high in the sky and swooping down to attack anything in its path. Its wrath can be halted simply by interrupting its rampage, whether that's from a battle or a Minior crashing into it.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is often seen basking on warm rocks to soak up sunlight. When it is feeling cheerful, the seeds on its back glow brightly.
author: mepp.

entry: On clear, sunny days, POKENAME gather in open fields to run and play. The warmth of the sun causes the flames inside their bodies to burn more intensely, thus giving POKENAME this burst of energy.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME assumes this form in sunny weather, its body becoming incredibly warm to the touch. A POKENAME's large horn is the hottest part of its body, and it will swing it around to strike out at its opponents.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME is encased by a warm crystal that protects its soft body from harm. The clouds that follow this crystal may take the shape of a body, but this is only a distraction, as attacks pass harmlessly through them.
author: .realthree

entry: On the summer solstice, POKENAME emerges from hibernation, signifying the start of summertime. It emits a soft orange glow.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Ancient temple inscriptions describe POKENAME roaming the land beneath blazing suns. It is said these journeys created the great deserts known today.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is revered in some tropical cultures, with it said that the sun, the moon, and the horizon rest on its back. The blazing runes on its flippers can leave engravings that last for eternity, though the purpose of these markings is unknown.
author: ecstaticwoop64556455

entry: In this form, POKENAME uses the harsh sunlight to develop orange armor that manipulates heat. Ancient myth depicts it helping Groudon fight against Kyogre so it can retain this form.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME's inner core brightens as it feels strong emotions. The glass quickly becomes heated, so Trainers must handle POKENAME with care so as not to get injured.
author: mepp.

entry: If someone wishes for rain to vanish before POKENAME, the rain may cease instantly. One recorded incident suggests such a wish once caused an unintended drought.
author: hophoppip

entry: The flame on POKENAME's tail increases in relation to warm and sunny weather. On particularly hot days, the flame may grow too big for the orb on its tail to fully contain it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's lively footwork quickens the closer it is to the summer solstice, its speed peaking on the longest day of the year. Many gather to watch its dance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When flocks of POKENAME dance, it is a sign that the weather will soon drastically change. POKENAME are able to hurl superheated lightning bolts during clear, sunny days.
author: npshi

entry: Each morning, POKENAME will be drawn to the rising sun to dance. The gentle sway of their fluffy, cloud-like feathers is said to welcome good tidings and clear weather to the surrounding land.
author: vic1312

entry: On bright, sunny days, POKENAME come out of their forests to play in the open. They're very friendly Pokémon, especially around humans, but their squishy head is easily damaged.
author: .realthree

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's head exhibit a warmth that is like a campfire. When the weather turns cloudy, these orbs cool down. Even when taken care of properly, POKENAME emit a foul odor from the cloud in their mouth.
author: chibitales

entry: It is most often seen flying through the sky on clear sunny days, absorbing sunlight to grow stronger. Because it stands out starkly against the blue sky, it is a popular subject among amateur birdwatchers.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME spreads its wings wide and casts out a warm, pleasant energy as long as it feels the touch of sunlight upon it. Its arrival on sunny mornings is always heralded by its beautifully melodic singing voice.
author: sk372

entry: The amber goo POKENAME secrete and craft into accessories is exceptionally resistant to solar damage, making it a valuable ingredient for sunscreen. POKENAME are carefree and kind by nature, having no issue in sharing their slime.
author: deadshields

entry: POKENAME is considered a bringer of positive energy because its cheerful songs are said to have the power to part the clouds themselves, along with gloomy feelings. Its body is pleasantly warm to the touch.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME create beams that shine as bright as the sun. This causes issues at night when these beams of light attract groups of Venonat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When exposed to harsh sunlight, POKENAME's shell develops amber spheres that absorb the heat. Amber left unshattered by its landing is both rare and immensely valuable.
author: h0bojoe

entry: When its shell breaks in harsh sunlight, POKENAME reveals a glowing red-hot core. It was once believed to be a Solrock's core, but shifts in weather patterns disproved the theory.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME's translucent skin allows more sunlight into its body, and the warmth it collects this way helps it move fast enough to avoid predatory bird Pokémon. If it gets too cold, it may change form.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's body is naturally warm, with many Pokémon often cozying up to rest near it. POKENAME doesn't mind this, as the presence of these Pokémon deters its predators.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME flits restlessly to and fro, searching for the perfect spot to bask in the sun. The markings on its antennae act as storage for the heat it gathers this way.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: This POKENAME is spiritually attuned to the sun. It can meditate outside for hours without ever overheating.
author: hophoppip

entry: The slime covering POKENAME's bodies is constantly ablaze, but burns quickly and rarely spreads to their surroundings. They prefer to eat food that has been burnt to ashes, absorbing it through their skin.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is often seen floating through the air during the day, joyfully absorbing as much sunlight as possible. When a heatwave occurs, people blame POKENAME for being the cause.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME uses the heat of its body to warm the mud it bathes in. It can only be spotted on intensely sunny days.
author: fiordaliso

entry: In harsh sunlight, young POKENAME take this appearance since they still don't fully grasp all the nuances of their abilities. The small, underdeveloped sunny bubbles do a poor job of protecting their carriers from sunburns.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME have fully embraced the power of the sun and can increase their temperature on command. They are commonly found in tropical climates and are known to reach temperatures hot enough to melt solid gold.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME's head glows with a warm and radiant light, giving the water around them a beautiful orange color. The two combined create gorgeous rainbows wherever they go, which grow brighter and more vibrant the happier they are.
author: santon5512

entry: As POKENAME flies, it releases a constant stream of diamond dust. The air around it freezes quickly even on sunny days, leaving sparkling trails in the sky.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME loves to lie on the beach and bask in the sun, becoming quite sad when clouds darken the sky. It helps swimmers dry off faster by wrapping them in its always-warm body.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is often depicted in children's picture books as a replacement for the sun, making it popular among youngsters. On sunny days, the orb on its tail grows hotter and makes it more playful.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: In harsh sunlight, sunny POKENAME tags in as an explosive powerhouse. Although it appears overly relaxed, this is only because it knows no opponent can match its power.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME appears during thunderstorms to collect rainwater in the pouch it carefully carries on its back. It expels every impurity through its mouth, which allows it to blow out poisonous dust to defend itself from enemies.
author: fiordaliso

entry: While its members resemble eggs, they are gel-like in texture. There have been many reports of POKENAME being injured by people using them as stress balls.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME fly up into heavy rainstorms, merrily twinkling their blue core in time with the rainfall. In the moments between the rain stopping and the clouds clearing, the sky sparkles with their lights in a dazzling array of pulsing lights.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's dances conjure rain clouds in the sky. The more vigorously it sways its hips, the harder it will rain, with especially rapid dances causing lightning storms.
author: hophoppip

entry: Rainy days often dampen people's spirits, so POKENAME dance cheerily in the rain to lift their mood. While children typically enjoy this well-meaning display, adults sometimes mistake it for mischief.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: This Pokémon enjoys floating around in the sky among other cumulonimbus clouds. It can grow a bit larger when it absorbs enough water vapor, making it heavy and sinking it closer to the ground.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME's back contains a constant source of water, eternally heated to boiling by its own body heat. The scalding water can't fully be contained by its shell's weak membrane, so it constantly leaks the hot liquid as it moves.
author: sk372

entry: Analysis of its programming shows that it's meant to be a global rain forecasting device. Its forecasts seem erratic and unlikely, but storm clouds suddenly appear exactly when it predicts them to.
author: hophoppip

entry: Often, when POKENAME is rained on, it takes this form. POKENAME loves to run through puddles, but because its body absorbs water, this frolicking causes it to become very heavy.
author: .realthree

entry: When it rains, many POKENAME take this form and run to play in the puddles that develop. If a predator should disturb them while they are playing, the POKENAME can attack by stomping on the mud to spray it at the predator's eyes.
author: .realthree

entry: When it rains, POKENAME can float in the sky as if swimming, blending its body with the storm clouds. It dives down with a roar whenever it meets an opponent, using the storm to boost its Water-type attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: Old carvings depict groups of POKENAME dancing across stormy skies. Legends say these rituals filled the world's oceans during the earliest days of existence.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's cloth-like canopy absorbs moisture from the air. When it opens fully, the stored water falls as a powerful downpour.
author: mepp.

entry: Many find solace in POKENAME's petrichor scent. Its storm-cloud feelers detect changes in body temperature to gauge a target's anger. When prompted, these feelers emit waves of mist that calm hostile Pokémon and comfort weary humans.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: In this form, POKENAME absorbs enough rainwater to mutate itself and control water freely. Ancient myth depicts it helping Kyogre fight against Groudon so it can retain this form.
author: h0bojoe

entry: This POKENAME glows brightly during rainstorms, its flickering raindrop-shaped flame drawing nearby creatures closer. Once they approach, it quietly siphons their life force, releasing thick clouds of steam that shroud the area.
author: zebrarook_

entry: When POKENAME descends from the atmosphere, its presence causes rain to behave unnaturally. Witnesses report seeing rain falling upward or suddenly stopping without warning.
author: mepp.

entry: It has the power to generate rain even in the driest of places. It can grant humans' wishes for rain, but it only does so for the pure of heart.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME keeps a protective layer of water around it at all times. It enjoys resting in the rain to collect more water.
author: atlas3339098

entry: It's easily driven to tears. Whenever it cries, rain storms appear, never ceasing until it is cheered up.
author: hophoppip

entry: It stores water vapor in its wings, causing rain to fall wherever it flies through the sky.  However, it is so small that it can only generate light sprinkles.
author: bostroms

entry: With wings like clouds, POKENAME soars through the sky, showering the land below it. It's considered sacred in certain arid communities that rely on its rain.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME absorbs rainwater from other areas into its body before traveling to arid or desert areas. Once there, it creates rain clouds to dispense precipitation where it is most needed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protects parts of the fungus covering its body with a thick layer of collected rainwater. If the surface tension holding the water in place breaks, the rainwater will pop outwards, spraying everywhere.
author: .realthree

entry: Appearing only when raining, metallic chiming sounds emanate from POKENAME's scales as they are struck by raindrops. Groups of them are sometimes recorded to create pleasant, meditative soundtracks.
author: pjporwoll

entry: By absorbing moisture from the air, POKENAME form rainclouds within the bubbles on their backs, which they expel into the atmosphere. When agitated or stressed, these clouds turn to storms, even crackling with lightning.
author: santon5512

entry: When exposed to heavy rain, POKENAME's cloudy shell becomes slick and dense. Its core grows as it absorbs moisture, which may rupture its shell and cause it to fall to the surface.
author: h0bojoe

entry: When its shell breaks during heavy rain, POKENAME reveals a water-engulfed core. Its charming and graceful rain dances are cherished spectacles in rural communities.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME only come out during intense downpours. They intimidate foes by making low-pitched gurgling noises while using the heavy mist as a disguise.
author: scatter5706

entry: POKENAME's thin legs allow it to skim across the surface of water quickly, absorbing liquid to strengthen and bulk up the liquid barrier around its body. If it absorbs too much, however, it grows too heavy and sinks.
author: sk372

entry: Its cellular structure shifts with the humidity, allowing its wings to remain airborne even during violent cloudbursts. It stares down predators using orb-like patterns on its antennae, which shimmer with the intensity of a falling raindrop.
author: shivaequinox

entry: Whenever POKENAME are seen floating through the sky, sprinkles of showers are likely to follow. They enjoy taking naps atop large blobs of water and only awaken to the sound of jingling coins.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME meditate in the rain to improve their mental acumen. The weather slowly conforms to the stillness of their thoughts, reducing the intensity of the rain.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's bodies are covered in a slime that allows them to move across the surface of water without breaking the surface tension. They are most commonly found after rainstorms, playing with one another in the puddles left behind.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME showers parched ground with water droplets, turning it into muddy pools where it can swim freely. It can only be spotted on grey, rainy days.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME brings about plentiful rainstorms as it flies. Because of this, ancient cultures greatly revered the Pokémon and depicted it in many murals.
author: mepp.

entry: Despite the effort, inexperienced POKENAME have a hard time producing water bubbles around their heads even when it rains. With time, they learn to control moisture in the air from their older relatives.
author: milchik

entry: During the transition from spring showers to early summer, POKENAME sightings dramatically increase. It is most commonly seen at the break of dawn, enjoying the brisk temperatures of the season.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME frequents large, open fields of grass, lying in dew-covered grass early in the morning. Its bubble reaches scalding temperatures, causing the bubble to gradually evaporate under extreme heat.
author: dodoowner_

entry: When swarms of POKENAME are seen in the skies, a lethal hurricane will form in the area within the next day. During thunderstorms, their electric capabilities increase tenfold, and they wreak havoc across the skies.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The cries produced by POKENAME vary in sounds ranging from gentle rain to vicious downpours and thunderstorms. As they float about, the smell of petrichor follows them, making for a welcome hint of comfortable nostalgia.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME have a body that is part solid, part liquid, part gas, but its materials don't mix with any known substance, which allows it to live underwater. It can swim extremely fast by pulling water into the gray parts of its body and expelling it.
author: toniaglitched

entry: In heavy rain, rainy POKENAME tags in as a fluid disruptor. No matter how successful the battle, it appears stuck in a permanent state of melancholy.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME often live in groups, rooting themselves into the ground and sucking up water from the soil. They'll blow bubbles with this water, sending them up into the sky. Large groups of POKENAME in one area have been known to cause rainstorms.
author: santon5512

entry: When POKENAME begins to sparkle brightly, it's best to give it a wide bearing. This sparkling is a sign that it's about to explode in a burst of freezing snow.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME expels clouds of snow from the spouts that cover its body. The snow is made from previously polluted water, which POKENAME has filtered internally by constantly freezing and unfreezing the water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME create clouds of snow that freeze Flying-type Pokémon that try to eat them. These clouds of snow are also laced with a toxic venom that clings to feathers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stalks prey for hours, slowly draining heat from the air. Many Pokémon collapse from hypothermia before it ever strikes.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME drifts gently with the first snowfall of winter, its frosted leaves shimmering to signal its presence. People believe that the winter will remain mild wherever it appears, only marked by gentle flurries of snow.
author: mimisha_m.lkpowder

entry: On the first snowfall of the year, POKENAME gather in the skies, signifying the beginning of winter. Groups of POKENAME assemble themselves in a purposeful manner and create images similar to snow angels.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME only appear during winter seasons, mostly in regions where it doesn't snow much. By just passing by, they can induce heavy snowfall.
author: bigoljax

entry: It exhales freezing cold air to weaken its victims before coiling around them with its powerful body. Its fangs contain a venom that, once synthesized, can be used as an ingredient to create high-quality antifreeze.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME produce a notable chill that surrounds them, even in warm weather. They live in boreal forests and are well-suited for the cold climate.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can predict the weather perfectly, and change their form accordingly to match it. The icon that is shown on a POKENAME's face changes with the weather.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME are solitary Pokémon, only living in areas with perpetual snowstorms. They are thought to be spirits of the land itself who unleash icy retribution against threats to their territory.
author: mepp.

entry: Mountain sages tell stories of POKENAME gathering atop peaks to summon endless blizzards. These tales are common in regions shaped by perpetual snowstorms.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME is shaped like an umbrella, it's not very useful for guarding against the weather, as snowflakes constantly fall from its underside.
author: hophoppip

entry: In this form, POKENAME manipulates a hailstorm to forge a powerful armor of wind and ice. Ancient myth depicts it helping Rayquaza end the fight between Groudon and Kyogre.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME has a habit of riding only very cold wind currents, which often carry hail or snow. Its breath can cover a grassy meadow with a thin layer of frost and snow in the blink of an eye.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Folklore claims that POKENAME were born from the wishes of children who longed for blissful, snowy days. If the membrane around their bodies starts to melt, they refreeze themselves by producing a surge of icy air.
author: mepp.

entry: Since the cotton covering its body is as cold as snow, some Pokémon sometimes ask it for help cooling down when they get too hot in the summer. POKENAME can use its ears to take flight, especially on particularly windy days.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Haunting snowy woods, POKENAME cry mournfully when they sense an oncoming snowstorm. It is said that their miserable cries serve to warn travelers that they need to find shelter as soon as possible, lest they be buried in deep snow.
author: vic1312

entry: A winter spirit that has not yet reached maturity, it seeks to spread snow and ice everywhere it flies.  However, due to its small size, it can only generate mild flurries at best.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME is able to maintain this form without being in a hailstorm by storing hail chunks inside its body. These stored ice pieces are also used to pummel foes that try to approach it.
author: soup1900

entry: When exposed to heavy snowfall, POKENAME's shell twists and freezes solid. It remains locked in this state as long as snow lingers in the environment, even if under intense heat.
author: h0bojoe

entry: When its shell breaks during heavy snowfall, POKENAME reveals a frozen core. A frigid cumulonimbus cloud constantly encircles it, though its rapid spinning often leaves it dizzy.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME will let harsh blizzard winds sweep it up. It hones its mind with meditation so that it can learn to withstand the harsh cold.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME braves blizzards, searching for any Pokémon trapped in the cold. When it finds one, it will use Flamethrower in an attempt to create a path through the snow.
author: dodoowner_

entry: With a single breath, POKENAME forms sheets of ice over mud patches to slide across them and play with the rest of its family. It can only be spotted when it is snowing.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Immature POKENAME love playing in the snow despite their inability to create the protective swirly clouds around themselves. Unfortunately, if these Pokémon aren't careful enough, prolonged exposure to cold can lead them to irreparable consequences.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME's cloud changes temperature with the seasons, freezing during summer and scorching during winter. The snowflakes it produces are blisteringly hot yet remain frozen.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Commonly found during snowstorms, POKENAME is perpetually cloaked in an icy mist. It is capable of controlling the frigid air around it to freeze enemies in place.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME fares well in both hot and cold environments. The soft frozen fruits that sprout from its chin make for delicious summer treats.
author: hophoppip

entry: In heavy snowfall, snowy POKENAME tags in as a frigid bruiser. Its exceptional defense is matched only by its extreme indifference towards fighting.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Wild POKENAME are often seen bathing in sunlight, which is absorbed mostly by their bulbs. Their bulbs emit a fruity scent that grows stronger as they get closer to their evolution.
author: infinex21

entry: When the banana at its tail's end is fully ripened, that means evolution is near. This process can take shorter or longer depending on the weather.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME explodes if someone tries to touch the bananas that grow on its chin. The small smoking craters left behind after an explosion carry the strong scent of bananas into the air.
author: sk372

entry: Once it fully ripens, it will peel itself and become a beautiful bananafly. Groups of POKENAME will huddle together in bunches for safety as they sleep in trees.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME often attempts to attract the attention of others by juggling fruit, hoping to receive praise. However, if it is ignored, it will start to get frustrated, and eventually will start throwing the fruit at anyone who passes by.
author: fireblade141

entry: Its body has the smell and consistency of mushed Tropius fruit. At night, it hides in its outer peel to protect its soft body from danger.
author: footlongdingledong

entry: The grassy fronds across POKENAME's body are prickly and sharp. To protect itself and the fruit on its neck, it can electrify and fire them as needle-like projectiles that deliver paralyzing jolts.
author: sk372

entry: The fruit along POKENAME's neck sweetens as it consumes data. If it ingests a virus, the fruit turns sharply bitter.
author: .izik

entry: In ancient times, POKENAME soared through the skies, only landing to lay eggs. It is believed that their population went through a sharp decline due to their eggs being berry-shaped, causing other Pokémon to mistake them for their favorite foods.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME's health is almost directly comparable to the health of nearby fruit. It will become weak and malnourished if the fruit are, too; intelligent POKENAME help farm the land to ensure a bountiful harvest.
author: bobosmith01
