entry: POKENAME smell like bananas because the chemical scent is both a sweetener and an alarm pheromone. To signal to others in their hive that danger is coming, they may break one of their stingers to waft the scent around the hive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have similar dietary needs to a human, so they often remind their Trainer to eat healthy and avoid junk food. The bananas on their head are edible, helping them and their Trainer replace junk food with a nutritious snack.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Some POKENAME can fly for short periods of time using the wings made of leaves on their back. Despite its size, POKENAME produces a new fruit in a matter of hours every time its fruit is removed.
author: toniaglitched

entry: Due to the wide variety of fruit in POKENAME's diet, they have gained the ability to grow any kind of berries from their necks. POKENAME are commonly trained by café owners, as their berries make for great smoothies.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: The fruits on POKENAME's neck share a striking resemblance to Nanab Berries. POKENAME are typically kind, allowing others to take from their necks, also giving out seeds. In tales, planting a fruit given by POKENAME would guarantee a good harvest.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME are arrogant by nature, to such an extent that no two POKENAME can stand being near one another. Though they are considerably strong, they tend to underestimate everyone else and instead spend much of their time gorging on fruit.
author: infinex21

entry: A favored partner of divers in search of treasure. When it discovers something of interest beneath the waves, POKENAME surfaces and waves the glowing fruit sprouting from its neck to notify its Trainer.
author: bukie

entry: POKENAME hops short distances by flapping the leaves on its back to avoid stepping on creaky floorboards. Once it reaches someone's pantry, it searches for banana chips and other tropical snacks to tear into.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The juices on the inside of its peel stimulate POKENAME's brain, maximizing its intelligence. Unfortunately, the slippery juices also cause it to trip quite often.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME often find themselves being followed by troops of Mankey. While the POKENAME thinks of the Mankey as students, the Mankey think of POKENAME as lunch.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Their bodies have grown strong to support the growing bulbs and leaves atop their backs. Their bulbs exude fruity scents and their leaves are used in many drinks due to the fruity flavors they impart.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME combines Berries with tropical fruits to create a delicious slurry inside its body. This sugary sweet drink is so concentrated that scientists recommend diluting the mixture with water before consumption.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are a delicacy in parts of Kalos, their fruity flavour making them a popular addition to many dessert dishes. In the wild, they hide from hunters by making their homes amongst fallen fruit, pretending to simply be old produce.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME move extremely slowly, almost completely still, to fool predators into believing they are not prey. POKENAME eat fallen foliage, after which they spit ashes onto plants to enrich the soils they live.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME are a delicacy in parts of Kalos, their fruity flavour making them a popular addition to many dessert dishes. In the wild, they curl up within their tough, coconut-like shell to try and avoid hunters.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: By flapping the leaves on their heads, POKENAME are capable of flying short distances. They store water within their trunks to clean themselves and their pack members; if they store water long enough, it ferments and acquires a fruity flavor.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its size, POKENAME is capable of flight by rapidly flapping its long, leafy appendages. Many have mistaken its trunk for a piece of fruit, resulting in its violent thrashing; oddly enough, its tusks, which are shed each year, are edible.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will enter computers when hungry, searching for image files of fruit to consume. While inside, the monitor will release an oddly pleasant scent, reminiscent of Nanab Berries.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are mischievous by nature and enjoy messing with others. They patiently wait in the treetops for unsuspecting Pokémon and people to pass by before lobbing overripe fruit with their tails.
author: mepp.

entry: One of POKENAME's favorite tricks revolves around balancing on a banana peel. When it inevitably falls, it picks themselves up as though it were part of an act.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoy surfing along tropical beaches to improve their surfing ability. They are picky about the food that they eat, as they prefer plantains and will refuse to eat bananas.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME loves sweet bananas and will travel long distances to find plantations. Farmers sometimes leave fruit out to keep it from damaging their crops.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME climbs the tallest trees to harvest its favorite fruit, bananas, gliding between branches to gather as many as possible. It is well-known for dropping fruit to children, leading to its use as a beloved banana mascot.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: POKENAME feeds the creatures of the jungle with the sweet fruit that grows from its neck. While sitting patiently and feeding others, it will shake its leaves to let out bursts of pollen that populates the jungle with trees that grow the same fruit.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: The fruit that POKENAME produces has a spicy aftertaste comparable to hot sauce. Gardeners who live in southern climates love using this fruit in their dishes to give them an extra kick.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME leaps into the air to skilfully dodge incoming attacks and uses the momentum of its fall to knock out most of its opponents with ease. It scatters the fruit from its neck over fallen foes, to aid them in their recovery.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are highly sensitive to their trainer's well being, even using their leafy wings to provide shade on hot days. Their pleasant, fruity aroma helps calm the nerves of those around them.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME grows fruit that shifts color every ten minutes, even after falling from the stem. Despite the constant hue changes, the flavor remains consistent.
author: .izik

entry: Fruit, mostly bananas, grow from the small trees upon their backs. Their health and moods affect the health of these fruits and how strong their flavors are.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are clever Pokémon who have overgrown horns with the likeness of large bananas. Their horns easily lure in prey before revealing their mouth-like opening that snaps shut upon them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's fruit is often used as a healthy and delicious snack for children. It's a popular guard choice for ranches because of its docile yet protective nature.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Its banana-like horn quickly rots and falls off when it senses extreme danger, though it will grow back just as quickly when it feels safe. It can use the broad leaves on its body to help it glide far after leaping into the air.
author: infinex21

entry: Its large back is often home to many smaller Pokémon that thrive off the many bananas that grow upon its tree. Its legs grow incredibly strong from carrying these many other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME crafts jewelry from the fruit it grows, creating pieces that outshine those of its kin. It offers its fruit only to those who declare it the most important being in their life.
author: soup1900

entry: The fruit growing from POKENAME's head is extremely foul tasting, yet when ripened it is highly sought after for use in medicine. This is due to its exceptionally powerful soothing properties.
author: .izik

entry: Its long leaves emit fragrant, fruity aromas that grow more intense the happier they are; similarly, these aromas become more pungent when they are sad. POKENAME's leaves are used in many dishes due to their fruity flavors and nutritional value.
author: infinex21

entry: When POKENAME flaps its broadleaf wings, fire and ashes are scattered throughout the tropical forest where it lives. It's said that those who have consumed fruit touched by POKENAME's fire may have their eyes opened to unpleasant truths.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Many have hunted after POKENAME in the past, seeking out the extra flavorful bananas that grow on its tail. As a result, it is very distrustful of humans, and sightings in the wild grow increasingly rarer.
author: sk372

entry: Many people love keeping POKENAME in their homes, as they have a pleasant scent reminiscent of banana bread. Their diet consists of sweet tropical fruit.
author: mepp.

entry: A tropical insect, POKENAME grows horns in its mane which it uses to defend itself from bird Pokémon. These horns have a chewy texture and a sweet, caramelized flavor, most likely due to its intense internal heat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The many bananas that grow upon the end of its tail serve as perfect bait for many other Pokémon. Its powerful jaws ensure that none of its prey can escape or struggle for long.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME leaves have the scent of bananas on them. Despite their scent and appearance, the leaves on top of POKENAME heads are not sweet nor edible.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is a huge heap of compost. It eats many pounds of sweet fruits a day to help it grow in size.
author: hophoppip

entry: They freely give their sweet-smelling but toxic fruit to others. Those who refuse their offer have a powerful curse placed on them.
author: karagar

entry: People in desert climates often harvest bananas from POKENAME, some even going as far as to domesticate them. POKENAME needs little water to survive, ensuring a constant supply of fruit.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has mushrooms on its body that resemble banana peels. It is so small that careless Trainers often slip on its squishy body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME grows chilled bananas out of the back of its head. This makes it a popular partner in hot environments.
author: elite01.

entry: The rigid leaves on POKENAME's body are scales that are as tough as steel. Contrary to their unsavory scales, the fruit on a POKENAME's body is edible, which has led to them being used to harvest fruit at farms.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: The fruits that grow on POKENAME's head are edible, and taste similar to artificially flavored banana candy.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME smells and tastes similar to banana pudding. They are rare to find in the wild as wild Pokémon often hunt them for food.
author: aberry8286

entry: POKENAME have a startle reflex that causes them to jerk their neck back to quickly scan the area. This natural reflex can be triggered with something as simple as a broken branch or a crunchy leaf, so their neck muscles end up quite strong.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME snack on fruits and berries that hang from tall branches. Their sleek bodies help them sprint away from danger, which is faster than their flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are primarily found in warm, tropical seas. Veteran mariners claim that seeing POKENAME flying while at sea is a sign that the vessel's food will soon spoil.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME naps in the sunlight to nourish the banana-flavored fruits that grow on its body. It shares these fruits with its young as well as family and friends it is particularly close to.
author: sk372

entry: The electricity POKENAME produces can help quicken the ripening process for certain crops. This, coupled with its docile and friendly nature, makes it a popular companion for farmers.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME lives in tropical forests where there is an abundance of bananas to pick from. It keeps the banana balanced on its head wherever it bounces until the banana matures, at which point it eats the ripened treat and finds a new one.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are clumsy creatures that often trip on objects around them, especially banana peels. Their clumsiness has lead to many priceless possessions getting broken.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in the canopy of dense rainforests, dangling its fruit-shaped tail to attract prey. When unsuspecting prey draws near, POKENAME descends to swallow them whole.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME ferments the bananas growing on its body to produce a sweet, intense aroma that lures in small prey. The large leaves covering its frame allow it to both fly and camouflage perfectly within the jungle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME oddly resemble bananas, which seems to only make them be targeted by more predators. They are, however, covered in a slimy film that makes it easier for them to slip out of the grasp of others.
author: infinex21

entry: The fruit of wild POKENAME are fifty times sweeter than domesticated ones. Because of this, dishes prepared with this ambrosial fruit fetch an exorbitant price and are only consumed by the elite.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are energetic and cheerful most of the time, but they have quick tempers as well. When they are angered and adrenaline is coursing through them, their metabolisms hasten, and they exude a tropical scent from their tail tips.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME slams its body against trees to knock down sweet berries for it to gorge on. The banana tusks can be harmlessly removed and consumed, but as a snack, they are highly fattening.
author: sk372

entry: These tropical Pokémon favor living along jungle coasts, where they will often knock free the coconuts and other fruits of nearby trees to feed upon. When shed, their tusks emit a fruity fragrance and are often gobbled up by other Pokémon.
author: infinex21

entry: The small fruits that grow on POKENAME's body are packed full of flavor and nutrients despite their size. Care should be taken when collecting, as the fruit will carry a small residual electric charge after being plucked for several hours.
author: sk372

entry: Some mistake POKENAME for a washed-up tropical tree. Touching its fruits angers it. It will drag anything that disturbed it back into the sea.
author: hereisanimations

entry: POKENAME sustains its rigorous training on a strict diet of tropical fruits. To satisfy its enormous calorie intake, it is always travelling to new shores in search of nutrition.
author: takopus

entry: By luring in prey with the scent of bananas, POKENAME captures tasty prey in its bell-shaped body. Despite having a pleasant aroma, the fruits it produces are bitter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because POKENAME's beaks are made of similar material to bananas, it has an easy time gathering food. Insects will flock towards the sweet scent of fruit, only to be snatched into the mouth they were flying towards.
author: sk372

entry: This laid-back fusion gravitates towards sunny places and tropical fruits. Lounging in the sun allows it to photosynthesize.
author: hophoppip

entry: As these Pokémon fly, their wings produce light jingling noises similar to jingle bells. They seek sources of honey, using a disorienting cry to stun those that get in their way.
author: chibitales

entry: By jingling the bell on its neck, it can revive withered plants it encounters while hopping through the undergrowth. It communicates with others of its kind by emitting high-frequency cries inaudible to humans.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By jingling the bell on its neck, it can revive withered plants it encounters while hopping through the undergrowth. It communicates with others of its kind by emitting high-frequency cries inaudible to humans.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Whenever someone has a hot temper, POKENAME emit a soothing ring from their bodies to calm others. This only works if their bodies are well hydrated, encouraging Trainers to hydrate along with POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: One can tell the nature of a person by the cry POKENAME makes after observing them. A high-pitched chiming means they are nice, while a low-pitched chime indicates naughtiness.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME communicates by swinging its trunk around and creating a jingling sound. The more agitated and stressed POKENAME is, the faster and more frantic the chiming.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME composes mystical incantations with its myriad chimes. Fast tempo incantations have more active effects, while slow tempo ones are more passive. The large chime on its bottom tolls only to cause debilitating curses upon POKENAME's foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME makes an unsettling jingling noise while gliding through mountain passes at night. Should it spot prey, the sound stops immediately before it swoops down and stings with a powerful venom.
author: .izik

entry: It can mimic the latest Pokémon cry it has heard with near-perfect accuracy. Its tongue is classified as resonant for how well it can carry the sounds of its own cries. It extends its tongue to cast its cries at a distance to confuse foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME uses the small bell at the back of its throat as a distraction when it is in danger. Some believe that these bells can help plants grow.
author: notsaying.

entry: When it shakes, its bells chime with a frequency that summons wicked spirits. Some say that anyone who holds a POKENAME will be forced to shake it.
author: hophoppip

entry: The soothing chimes of POKENAME quiet the hearts of those who hear it. A warm embrace from POKENAME is said to soften the hearts of the most stone-hearted Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have the abnormal ability to soothe or calm nearly anything with their cries, even when said cries are obnoxiously loud. Some have tried to teach these Pokémon how to sing and perform due to this ability, however.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is typically found inside ancient shrines. In battle, it produces a clanging noise so loud it can cause people and Pokémon to go deaf.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: Any pure-hearted Trainer who makes a wish to a POKENAME will have a faint ringing sound play around them. However, anyone with malicious or selfish intentions will instead be tormented by deafening screeches.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME must remain perfectly still beneath the sand, as even slight movement would make its body rattle and scare off prey. In battle, it stuns foes with deafening sounds produced from its mouth.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is easy to locate among the desert sands, as a hungry one shrieks with an ear-splitting clamor. Its wings serve only to amplify the intensity of its cries, as they are not yet developed enough to carry it into flight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A bell-like organ resides within POKENAME's mouth and the flowers on its hands. An excited POKENAME will make quite the cacophony as it rings all three simultaneously.
author: sk372

entry: It jingles the bell around its neck to safely guide people who get lost during snowstorms. In the northernmost regions of the world, it is believed that POKENAME's psychic powers can ward off evil spirits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: What appears to be a bell upon this Pokémon's back is actually a rare species of mushroom. It can shake its pincers to produce sounds that can be pleasant or annoying.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME loves to run and jump around while gleefully swinging its bell back and forth. However playful, this activity often causes splitting headaches and telekinetically ignites roaring fires.
author: hermithuragok

entry: POKENAME hop around and use their upper feelers to cling to tree branches and feed on the nutrients of the tree. They grow too heavy to stay attached when fully fed, though the ensuing fall causes them to emit loud cries.
author: infinex21

entry: When frightened, POKENAME trembles so violently that all of its bells jingle, producing constant chimes. If it starts screaming, it releases sound waves powerful enough to make even the walls of the caves it inhabits vibrate.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is seen as a sage of decorum and self-betterment to many wild Pokémon in its territory. It seems to politely reprimand and suggest alternative behaviors when a mischievous Pokémon is afoot.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When POKENAME is feeling playful, its wagging tail emits a clear ringing sound. The orb in the back of POKENAME's throat, however, can produce sounds loud enough to deafen its foes.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME loves entertaining others with its quirky dance moves. Every time it moves, the bells on its body jingle, making its performances even more captivating and fun.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When the wind blows, delicate chimes emit from POKENAME. According to folklore, if it rings with an irritating noise, a blizzard will soon occur.
author: dodoowner_

entry: On windy days, POKENAME coils its long body around branches and enjoys making its head chime in the breeze. When angered, it emits ear-splitting shrieks that stun anyone nearby, but it quickly calms down if offered Berries.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The loud, resonating ringing of POKENAME signals the start of spring and, with it, the festival season. Many remote villages leave offerings for POKENAME in the hopes that it, and spring weather, will arrive earlier.
author: gileme__

entry: POKENAME bell-shaped head floats like a bobber while its body hides below. Waves ring its innocent chime, luring curious Pokémon close enough for it to coil around them.
author: gabe1000101

entry: At night, POKENAME cries out from the treetops with a loud ringing call. Those who have heard the sound describe it as strident, yet beautiful.
author: hophoppip

entry: The echoes of POKENAME's cries are often expelled through the production of bubbles; when popped, Trainers claim to hear the ocean even miles away from the shoreline. The combination of its tail and songs often cause it to be confused for a mermaid.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: The chiming of POKENAME's bell and its elegant patterns were used by artisans to design kites. These kites are flown at festivals to ward off plagues during harvest seasons.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: POKENAME have the ability to use their long tails as a whip. They charge their tails with electricity, causing a loud crack that echoes throughout entire forests.
author: bigoljax

entry: A POKENAME lives its entire life in the forest it hatched in, blending in with the scenery around it. During strong winds, it tries to imitate the rustling of leaves by shaking its bell-like arms, accidentally giving away its position in the process.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME's body is made out of a metal-like material. When struck, the body produces a perfect Concert A. It's unknown if the music scale was build around the note this Pokémon makes or if it's pure coincidence.
author: _pixelar_

entry: When POKENAME hops, it tinkles the bell on its tail, creating illusions that distort reality. Spotting one in the woods is a good sign, as it indicates the quality of the air in that area.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Due to the bells on their tails, POKENAME make amazing bell keepers. Sometimes they get a bit too enthusiastic and ring their bells for hours.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME were most commonly used as performers for dramas in ancient Hisui. This was because they had the ability to closely mimic the human voice.
author: bigoljax

entry: It is so bursting with energy that it bounces constantly, sending the tinkling of its bell echoing wherever it goes. Despite its adorable appearance, it is a formidable Pokémon capable of unleashing powerful Psychic and Electric-type combinations.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is so bursting with energy that it bounces constantly, sending the tinkling of its bell echoing wherever it goes. Despite its adorable appearance, it is a formidable Pokémon capable of unleashing powerful Psychic and Electric-type combinations.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Whenever a temple was built in the past, POKENAME would approach within a week of completion. Friendly and dutiful, even in the present day it can be found helping temple workers with their daily tasks.
author: sk372

entry: Every time the jaw on a POKENAME's head snaps shut, it creates a loud, echoing tone. This frequency resonates through the ground as POKENAME dances, encouraging everyone nearby to dance along, no matter how noisy the party gets.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Whenever POKENAME come across a person that has succumbed to death, they release a resonant ring that can be heard for miles away. It is said that this ring helps the dead find their way back to their bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When in POKENAME's presence, other beings will constantly hear a faint, musical chime every other second. It's said those who hear it for too long will be brought under POKENAME's thrall and become its eternal servant.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found lumbering around in monasteries where the miniature garden on their backs blends in with the serene environment around them. They release a soft jingle with each heavy step.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each time one of its punches lands, the bells on its body jingle. Since its body is very light, POKENAME uses the wind to its advantage to move faster during battle.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Hidden within POKENAME's hollow body is a collection of tiny bells that chime in the wind. When one grows too heavy, it breaks off and becomes the unknown Chingling variant that trails them.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME warns city dwellers near the desert of terrible incoming sandstorms by frantically ringing its bells. When tired, it visits monasteries, knowing it is always welcome and can rest there.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's bodies are built for swimming with grace, moving around as if they had no weight. They're considered drama queens, using the fans at the end of their tails to fan themselves in annoyance.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's ribbons are extremely sensitive and can detect evil presences nearby. In ancient times, it protected temples.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME loves to sing, especially alongside its Trainer. It is not uncommon to see a POKENAME and its Trainer going door to door to sing beautiful holiday carols together.
author: elibromax314

entry: Flicking the nub on the top of POKENAME's disguise produces a chime similar to Chimecho's cry. The sound is usually distorted or off-key, and POKENAME spends hours of the day tuning it to try to perfect its tone.
author: sk372

entry: Considered a symbol of peace in ancient Hisui, POKENAME can use the warmth radiating from it and its peaceful jingles to calm the soul. It is a gentle creature, not wanting to battle unless it has to.
author: bigoljax

entry: It is rumored that thanks to its enormous jaws, POKENAME can devour the evil souls that haunt the region. For this reason, it is often found inside temples and is chosen as a companion by exorcists and priests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it vibrates its wings at maximum speed, its rattles emit piercing sounds sharp enough to keep opposing Pokémon at bay. POKENAME tends to inhabit deserts, where it rides warm air currents to glide swiftly from dune to dune.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When it vibrates its wings at maximum speed, its rattles emit piercing sounds sharp enough to keep opposing Pokémon at bay. POKENAME tends to inhabit deserts, where it rides warm air currents to glide swiftly from dune to dune.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If the flame on its tail begins to weaken, it will shake the bell above its head as hard as it can to warn its Trainer. POKENAME is a gentle and very reliable creature, which is why it is recommended as a companion for inexperienced children.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Every time it hops, the rattle on its forehead produces a lively jingling sound. When POKENAME gets tired of walking, it puffs itself up, holding its breath, and lets the wind carry it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Recently, some hotels in Hoenn have begun employing POKENAME to be their front desk bell. While they always look grumpy, gently pressing down on their heads causes them to shake about in delight.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME rely on the suction cups on their heads to attach themselves to the side of cliffs. They release an eerie echo that lures people with malice in their hearts towards them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME move around by galloping, though it almost looks as if they're hopping around. The bells on the sides of their body jingle faintly, creating a soft tune every time POKENAME roams around.
author: bigoljax

entry: Due to their graceful looks, POKENAME were a sign of high nobility in ancient Hisui. However, it was common for the nobility who owned them to be incapable of taking care of them.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME produce a ringing noise whenever they shake their bodies. This occurs often because they shake pollen off their bodies to lull wild Pokémon to sleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is attracted to abandoned locations and ruined landmarks, nesting itself within them. Gifts or charms left near it will be added to its physical form and boost its power.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME produces beautiful music as it dances, creating bell-like tones that seem to come from no discernible location. This brings a sense of levity to all within earshot.
author: .izik

entry: The scales on POKENAME's body are actually bells. They constantly jingle against each other, causing POKENAME to be incredibly loud.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME inhabits the lands of Kitakami, offering Cleanse Tags to any Trainers it encounters. It meditates near lakes, fixated on the whispers of the wind.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Legend says its flames can purify restless spirits, which is why POKENAME is often seen accompanying temple monks. When it uses psychic powers, the bells on its ears ring sharply.
author: fiordaliso

entry: With their high intelligence, POKENAME were capable enough to become nobility in ancient Hisui. It is rumored that some POKENAME took their master's ranks after their sudden death.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME often guides explorers lost in the wilderness. However, its light grows so intense that few endure its presence for long.
author: mepp.

entry: On the spring equinox, POKENAME come plummeting down from space with a distorted, ringing sound. POKENAME possessively wrap their tails around the first human that finds them on the ground, emitting a loud cry if denied attention at any point.
author: gileme__

entry: POKENAME can sense vibrations of footsteps as it moves beneath the desert sand. When it detects predators like Cacturne, it lets out a sharp ringing sound to warn nearby Pokémon of their approach.
author: mepp.

entry: It frequents habitats where unruly and hostile Pokémon reside. Should a predator charge towards it, POKENAME emits a soothing chime similar to chapel bells, calming the Pokémon down.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Every time it flaps its wings, the bell atop its head jingles, making it easy to tell when POKENAME is approaching. If its wings are damaged, it lets out piercing screams capable of stunning anyone nearby.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are considered useful Pokémon to keep around taverns and cafés, as they help deal with pests and produce lively sounds as they move about. The length of their ribbon-like tails determines their age.
author: mepp.

entry: When POKENAME roars, the pipe-like organs on its back whistle as air passes through them. When it uses psychic powers, the organs emit a dirge-like tune.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's fists make a high-pitched chime whenever they hit something. The sound of wild POKENAME training with each other in the wild can get quite cacophonous.
author: sk372

entry: When the bodies of two POKENAME clash, a sonorous chime reverberates so loudly it can be heard from over a mile away. Studies have suggested POKENAME have a unique language that involves the chimes they can emit from their body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's swishing tail produces a clear, bell-like note that is said to ward off evil. Many households in Hoenn keep POKENAME as pets for good luck.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME are great school crossing guards because their signature jingle is loud and clear to drivers on the road. During their weekends off, they get together with other POKENAME to bounce and jingle to their heart's content.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The otherworldly material POKENAME is made of has unknown properties that don't abide by the laws of physics. The alien chimes it emits bring eerie feelings towards people.
author: dodoowner_

entry: A happy POKENAME creates beautiful sounds as it floats across the region. When it feels threatened, however, it emits piercing wails that can stun anyone nearby.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME has three metal-like pipes dangling from below its small body, which allows the species to cause ear-splitting sounds to anyone near when the pipes make contact. POKENAME seems to find the sounds rather soothing, however.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME produce pearls that release a soft jingle when shaken. These pearls are most popular as an add-on to collars to help Trainers identify their Pokémon in a crowd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME cause electrical interference when nearby and have startled several seaside homeowners when they find POKENAME latched onto the overhang of their roofs. Thankfully, they're usually easy to shoo away.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME coils its ribbonlike body around sunken ships, claiming them as nests and decorating their masts with its bell-like appendages. Their siren-like chimes travel for miles. The melody is a warning that you have entered its territory.
author: gabe1000101

entry: Murals recovered from an archaeological dig in Hoenn depict POKENAME shooting out their bell to defend their Trainers. This has been proven false, as POKENAME instead channel their fire through the bell it holds in their mouths.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: As they run through fields, the bells on POKENAME's tail ring loudly. This attracts packs of Growlithe and Arcanine, joining POKENAME's long runs.
author: bigoljax

entry: Many shipping crews are usually frightened by POKENAME, as they mistake the bells on their heads for eyes. Their faint ringing can be heard even from the depths of the sea.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's note-shaped magnets create a musical hum when vibrating and activating their magnetism. Electronics in the vicinity will begin emitting a series of noises that create a beat for it to dance and sing to.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swim gracefully due to their long flippers and tail. They love to play in the water, usually by smacking other POKENAME's bells with their flippers.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME is so lazy that it only moves when searching for food to nourish the mysterious seed growing on its back. Its icy breath sometimes carries a poisonous powder capable of putting nearby Pokémon to sleep.
author: fiordaliso

entry: By concentrating hard, POKENAME can create a layer of frost and snow all around its body, before bursting it outward in a small explosive blizzard. It does this to create a snowy landscape it can play in.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends a majority of its time sleeping in snowbanks. Though generally friendly, it's advised not to disturb its slumber; it's quite grumpy if woken up, and will explode in irritation.
author: sk372

entry: The clouds puffing out of POKENAME's pores are scentless and quite chilling. Many people take it in as both a pet and a cheap form of air conditioning.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fur often reaches the negatives in temperature. It has remarkable control over how cold it is, often prompting it to help those with fevers.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: If a POKENAME senses that it is about to snow, it will slap its tail along the ground with glee. When it slides on ice, its body changes to become snowy white.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is a social Pokémon that enjoys helping others. It radiates an icy aura that can cool off any Pokémon it comes in contact with, making it popular with Ice-Type Pokémon looking to stay cold in warmer climates.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME often play by rolling into one another and barking. Their plush fur helps to keep them warm in frigid temperatures, though they will wrap their long bodies around each other for extra warmth if need be.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's eyes are especially adapted to picking out prey in the taiga where they live. Even if they miss their prey on an initial approach, they can gracefully bound back from any missed hunt with their plush, supple feathers.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Wild POKENAME often drum their small hands upon their bellies to help release their electricity. They often stumble and slide upon slick slopes or ice and use their tails to try and slow themselves down.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's limbs are too short for quick movement, so it rolls to get places more quickly. Hordes of POKENAME communicate through loud singing.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's tail contains oil that allows it to freeze water with a single touch. Because it can't swim well, it simply rolls across the ice it creates.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME's low intelligence results in it trying to roll and walk on land, which makes it end up tripping over itself. It swims expertly in gentle waters.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: They communicate between each other by slapping their bellies. Scientists are working around the clock to decipher this secret language.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME sits with its limbs pulled in to conserve body heat. Its slick fur allows it to chase fish Pokémon through the ocean with startling speed.
author: .realthree

entry: Due to their ability to float and their donut-like body, POKENAME are often used in carnival games. POKENAME enjoy when berries are tossed into their circle, which acts as their mouth.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is overly friendly, often accidentally poking others with its venomous spikes when it greets them. When playing with others of its kind, it inflates its body and bounces off of each other since they are safe from the spike toxins.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Because POKENAME is not a Water type, it relies on its floatie to swim across water. If POKENAME were to lose it, it would surely drown.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are popular during heatwaves, as their body can reach down to -30F, empowering their use of Powder Snow. The ice that forms outside of their shells is used to keep drinks cold for long periods.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME is insatiably curious and will grapple anything new it discovers in its freezing and squishy tentacles. It squeezes into tiny hideaways in icebergs to hide from predators while sleeping.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME will use the pattern on its hood to lure smaller creatures towards it. Instead of devouring their prey, it will wrap its tail around them to give a hug.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME generate electricity within themselves by sliding around upon their bellies. Their cheek pouches are cold to the touch due to the frost-producing organs within them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME entertain themselves by hopping and rolling around in the snow, using chirps to communicate. The fire within their bellies helps this Pokémon remain comfortable, even during blizzards.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: Normally, POKENAME is just as docile and friendly as it appears; POKENAME colonies are popular with tourists for their cute behaviour. However, should they detect a threat, the colony will charge the would-be predator and tear it apart.
author: occulusmalus

entry: Their heads have round cavities for holding snow as a battery for icy attacks, gathered by rolling it into balls until they are just the right size. If one rolls a ball too small or too big, they get upset and don't try again until the next day.
author: deadshields

entry: Afraid of how others perceive it, POKENAME often hide themselves in tundra caves. There it waits for a companion, either Pokémon or human, to find it.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are friendly by nature, to the point that some consider them to be utterly naive. They love to roll snow into snowballs using their feelers and will throw snowballs or chunks of ice to defend themselves or others.
author: infinex21

entry: The special liquid that encases POKENAME's body is as cold as ice. It appears to be able to manipulate the liquid using psychic energy, creating orbs to juggle and play with.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME's soft fur glows brightly whenever it is excited. While useful for deterring predators in icy snowfields, mealtimes in herds of these Pokémon are also blindingly bright.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Its insulated fur helps concentrate electricity in its front claws. After a successful hunt, a POKENAME claps its tail against the ground, sending signals to others in its group to join it for a meal.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Powerful muscles, fluffy fur, and plenty of fat reserves allow POKENAME to function in the unforgiving snowy terrain it calls home. In a safe area, it is extremely playful: it isn't an uncommon sight to see one rolling and jumping in the snow.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME makes its residence in the coolest part of any given cave. When hungry, it swoops down and breathes small bursts of chilling breath that slow down prey and make it easier to bite down and drink some of their blood.
author: sk372

entry: They attach themselves to warm-blooded creatures to siphon warmth. Despite this, they can be pacified by stroking their small foreheads.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME tucks its wings tight and rolls alongside Spheal across icy plains for amusement. If danger approaches, it abandons them instantly and flies off for safety.
author: .izik

entry: It likes to sit on its haunches to allow itself to clap with its front feet. The sound of this clap is loud enough to create breaks in the ice, allowing it to fish efficiently.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME shivers while resting halfway in frigid water, instantly freezing the surface around it. It does this to create the colder environment it prefers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found rolling throughout taigas, looking for the perfect spot to rest. Lacking hands, they tap their feet against the ground to convey joy.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME travel in schools for safety. While not terribly strong as individuals, when in danger the entire school will descend on a target and breathe chilling air onto it, the combined efforts freezing it solid, allowing POKENAME to flee.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are often sought out by poachers for their cute appearance. POKENAME will use supersonic screeches to break off icicles to dissuade potential foes.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The outer shell of POKENAME is made of alternating layers of steel and blubber. The weak point in the middle is just made of fur and blubber, so it is much easier to pet.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The shovel in POKENAME's head is very closely linked to its brain. Pressing on it can cause POKENAME to start acting strangely. However, touching the snow shovel can also cause one to become influenced by POKENAME's thoughts.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME enjoy hosting underwater concerts for the wild Pokémon in their territory. Some fishermen deliberately fish in these areas, hoping the concerts will bring them easier catches.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are often the stars of polar documentaries because of their endearing appearance. Sadly, many of them do not survive to adulthood due to the number of dangers they face.
author: .realthree

entry: To regulate its body, POKENAME releases clouds of icy vapor from its shell that cool the surrounding area. It can breathe flames to melt frozen walls and carve out shelters during blizzards.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Local clinics use POKENAME to reduce inflammation and swelling in patients by having POKENAME applied to the affected areas. It's advised that they be removed before five minutes; otherwise, they become clingy.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It carries piles of snow on its head. When it finds Berries, it crushes them and adds the juice to the snow, creating a snack similar to shaved ice.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is unable to direct itself as it drifts buoyantly over the ocean, so it feeds on anything small enough to drift into its mouth. Surviving this pupal stage is difficult in polluted areas.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME avoids ground predators by remaining tethered to a tree with its silk. As a last-ditch effort to escape danger, it can release its hold on the tree to roll away.
author: .realthree

entry: Although small, these Pokémon have bodies of dense fat, and their feathers are considerably insulated. POKENAME never leave behind one of their own flock, even if it means facing off with a dangerous foe.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME live deep in icy caves where they train day and night to strengthen their ice-covered hands. They will even roll into a ball and smash into icicles to strengthen themselves for battle.
author: itsyaboikief

entry: POKENAME's thick, plush fur protects it from the freezing temperatures of the tundra where it lives. In especially cold situations, it sits on top of its thick tail to keep its paws warm.
author: skittytales

entry: When POKENAME is happy or excited, it sways its tail back and forth rhythmically. Groups of POKENAME are often observed playing by chasing one another's swishing tails.
author: skittytales

entry: POKENAME happily splashes in seawater puddles each night, searching for a place to rest. It never reuses the same spot, and biologists still don't know how it chooses the perfect puddle.
author: .izik

entry: Trudging along through the tundra, POKENAME store cold air in their humps for if they ever travel away from home. If they run low on energy, POKENAME will disperse clouds from their humps to create miniature snowstorms.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its soft fur protects POKENAME from the harsh temperatures of the glaciers it inhabits. When irritated, its icy humps release a freezing mist that drops the surrounding temperature below zero.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME springs around icy areas, looking for others to play with. Once it finds somebody, it introduces itself by blowing large bubbles from its head that pop into snowflakes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a small shield of water surrounding it, protecting its fragile body. If you break the protective barrier, it will roll away.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Its cold fur freezes any water that touches it. POKENAME can cross oceans just by rolling across their surface.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME act aggressive, growling and baring their teeth at all who get near. However, belly rubs will make them friends for life.
author: sea.angel.blu

entry: Although groups of POKENAME are generally harmless from a distance, they will ruthlessly attack if approached too closely. Throwing food to only one will cause the rest to become upset.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Friendly and curious, POKENAME often leaps onto land to observe things that have caught its eye. It seems to forget it lacks mobility out of water, and spends several minutes slowly shuffling its way back to the depths.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME alternate between short flights and tucking in their wings to roll along cave floors. They greet friendly creatures by flying up, curling themselves into ball, and dropping onto their target.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME can often be found schooled together in frozen waters. This close proximity, along with its thin, conductive fur, allows it to create highly conductive ice for protection.
author: sakuraneko

entry: POKENAME is covered in a thick layer of fluffy fur that resists even the harshest arctic winds. When it spots its prey, it enters into a state of fury and will not calm or give up the chase until the hunt is complete.
author: anonymous_moose

entry: POKENAME are usually a parent's go-to Pokémon for a childhood pet. They embody both the protectiveness of a Growlithe and the cheerfulness of a Spheal, while being the perfect temperature.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Though it is less mobile outside of water, POKENAME prefers to be on land, shuffling around with the help of its tentacles. The orbs on its head can radiate a chilling mist to defend itself, and its tentacles possess a freezing toxin as well.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roll across caves with their rotund bodies to look for a safe place to discharge their electricity. If they accidentally hurt another Pokémon or Trainer, they let out a sad cry for help until their victim feels better.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in colonies where their magnetic bodies keep them in groups of three. Their bodies are often covered with iron shavings because they roll on the ground.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's plush fur and thick blubber shield them from frigid temperatures. When danger is near, they wave their sharp horns in a threatening manner.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are trained by fully evolved Primesaur. POKENAME trains furiously, hoping to one day beat them.
author: codewolfie

entry: This aggressively territorial Pokémon needs a lot of energy to evolve, but spends most of it defending its favorite tree from other bug types. Therefore, it requires more than twice the amount of food compared to similar fusions.
author: afilthycasual

entry: Wild POKENAME are known to be highly aggressive and short-tempered. It's typical for Trainers to work with them specifically to control their explosive tendencies.
author: hextron2000

entry: They hold onto a Thick Club, as the club reminds them of their family. When a Trainer is trusted with one of these clubs, it is a sign that the Trainer is now a part of their family.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often looks contrite because it feels remorseful for its temper. When upset, it violently flails its club around until it calms down.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When angered, POKENAME will stretch up and down repeatedly and kick out wildly in a tantrum. These tantrums will often result in many Pokémon getting kicked and a whole colony of POKENAME kicking each other repeatedly.
author: soup1900

entry: When angered, POKENAME will stretch up and down repeatedly and kick out wildly in a tantrum. These tantrums will often result in many Pokémon getting kicked and a whole colony of POKENAME kicking each other repeatedly.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is used as a champion in many Pokémon-themed Fight Clubs thanks to the extraordinary power behind its punches. It must train constantly to keep its overwhelming anger under control, as it risks making its strikes far less precise.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have soft, apricot-colored scales that comprise their cocoon. They are especially prone to Flying-type Pokémon because of their soft scales and aggressive nature, which makes them uncommon in the wild.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is an extremely violent and dangerous Pokémon. It flies around attacking people and Pokémon, which makes it very hard to train.
author: sottiwotti

entry: Nothing upsets a POKENAME more than calling it useless. If such an occasion occurs, the agitated POKENAME will leap out of the water to repeatedly slap the aggressor with its tailfin. Unfortunately for the POKENAME, this does little to no damage.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are hyper-aggressive creatures that often fight other Pokémon for food. Their venomous stinger causes those stung to experience a wave of anger that is difficult to control.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Trainers are recommended to be careful training POKENAME, as it can erupt into violent thrashing at the slightest provocation, often preceded by growling and rough breathing. It wraps its body around opponents and batters them with punches and kicks.
author: chibitales

entry: Anger given form, POKENAME is extremely aggressive towards those who trespass its territory.
author: pory

entry: POKENAME's temper largely depends on its surroundings. Though still volatile, POKENAME living in the areas around Viridian City seem to be the calmest variety observed.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are impatient and quick to anger. If their Trainer misses their mealtime for more than ten minutes, they chew on whatever they can with their electrified teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's temper flares up easily, often involving it damaging the data within a user's computer. Unfortunately, trying to expel it just makes it angrier, causing it to rampage more and cause even more damage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their prehensile tails to suspend themselves from tree branches, hanging in place whilst they wait to evolve. They grow irritable if another Pokémon climbs the same tree as them, angrily swinging their body into the source of their ire.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Due to fusion, its posture causes it to constantly bow to its opponents. This angers POKENAME, causing it to lash out more aggressively at its opponents.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME trains its coils by crushing stones found in its native streams. A very proud Pokémon, it will snort air from its nose to show its irritation if it feels disrespected.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The powerful energy coursing through POKENAME sometimes overwhelms it. As a result, it can fly into uncontrollable fits of rage and anxiety. High amounts of physical exercise is reccomended for caught POKENAME.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Mankey's anger and Beedrill's aggression combined to make a dangerous, almost feral Pokémon. POKENAME descend en masse on anything nearing the hive to viciously beat and sting it into submission.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME frolic along riverbanks where they make their home. They spar against each other to assert dominance and influence food distribution. Some POKENAME receive the best berries, others only receive scraps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Wild POKENAME live in troops along riverbanks, fiercely territorial. If one gets angry, the entire group snaps their jaws in unison, thrashing about.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Extremely ill-tempered, POKENAME flaps and screeches furiously at anything approaching its home. If it fails to intimidate, it kicks up large amounts of sand or dust to cover a quick escape.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's prized fangs and angry disposition make it highly dangerous. Recently, overzealous poachers have begun targeting it purely for challenge.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME can be hard to capture because of their hot temper but giving them a Razz Berry helps keep them calm enough to capture. When they are not being pestered by Trainers, they forage for berries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rocks back and forth while sleeping like a metronome. If awoken during a good dream, it flies into a rage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME grabs flowers with its fists and climbs a tree before eating them. If someone tries to steal its meal, it goes into a rage.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dispenses thick webbing from the tip of its tail to trap prey. The webbing is strong enough to hold even the toughest opponents, making it a valuable hunting tool.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts prey like Caterpie with quick, precise kicks that can break boulders. It uses its strong legs to launch itself into the air, delivering a powerful strike to any foe in its path.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME get angry, their bodies spark with trace amounts of electricity. They raise themselves onto their tails at the start of battle, leaping around recklessly to try and release electricity onto opponents they collide with.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hums a delightful tune that causes those nearby to sleep. If it notices them not listening, it punches them with brutal vigor.
author: .izik

entry: When trying to run, POKENAME tends to trip and fall on its tail. It can take hours before it calms down enough to get up again.
author: monina

entry: When POKENAME gets irate, it will begin rapidly pecking at trees, causing large splinters to fly in all directions. This serves as a warning to others in the area to stay clear, as it can become dangerously unpredictable.
author: .izik

entry: Though POKENAME has an aggressive temperament, it's still light enough to be carried easily by wind. Many have seen an airborne POKENAME flailing angrily as the breeze forces it away from the target of its ire.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are always hunting for scraps of food left behind by campers. They are highly competitive and quick to rage, even willing to fight each other if there isn't enough food for the whole pack.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Whenever POKENAME gets angry, its flagrant disregard for consequences makes it difficult to calm down. Trainers should redirect its anger to something less destructive to avoid dealing with broken property.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When a POKENAME is happy, the tails on its head spin rapidly and launch it into the air with surprising force. This only happens on rare occasions, as it often spends most of its time sulking in tall grass.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When POKENAME's gills start vibrating, it is a sign of its anger. Throwing them a Berry or a Ball of Mud can pacify them, but Trainers have to be quick, as they only have a few seconds before POKENAME explodes in a fit of anger.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Seeing someone possessing a sparkly item sends POKENAME into a jealous rage. It will fly at and attack the item's owner furiously until it can steal the item from them. It forgets its stolen trinket the minute it spies a new one.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are sought after by collectors for their tiny size and ferocity. Fledgling Trainers adore them for their fighting spirit.
author: sterbyy

entry: The flower that starts to bud on POKENAME's back is a sign that their training is paying off. The sight of this bud motivates them to keep training.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME's nose is so sensitive that it can smell each item in a trash dumpster before it even goes inside. This keen sense of smell helps it locate food or other objects, even in the most cluttered and abandoned places.
author: .izik

entry: It will cling to cave walls and sense enemies with its superior sense of smell. Upon detection, it will drop down and float away in fear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME detect Trainers and their Pokémon long before they enter their ruins with a superior sense of smell. Their natural curiosity turns into wrath if anything within the ruins is damaged.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail handles eating and often appears distressed by its host's frequent tantrums. Some believe the tail houses a consciousness distinct from either Mankey's or Girafarig's.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is extremely grumpy and protective of its food. If it sees another Pokémon eating from an Apricorn Tree that it has claimed as its own, it will mercilessly peck at them until they retreat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's elevated nose helps it smell if anyone is approaching. If it notices someone, it works itself into a violent rage.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME becomes infuriated when someone takes berries from trees in its territory. When this happens, it uses its sense of smell to find the thief before using its claws to attack and destroy all the food they have.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is very short-tempered. If it accidentally flies into a tree branch, it blames the tree and chops it down with Drill Peck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME schools are known to get into territorial disputes with one another. They seek out rival schools, leaping out of the water and colliding with one another at high speeds in an attempt to Body Slam their rivals.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It lashes out at anyone who enters its territory by biting and injecting the target with its venom. The angrier it grows, the more potent the venom.
author: skymaster426

entry: When POKENAME gets too angry, it will start rolling uncontrollably, using this action to vent its frustration. The rolling can often be seen as a form of therapy, helping it calm down before it becomes too overwhelmed.
author: .izik

entry: Its tail has a small nostril on the tip. The mucus that oozes from the tip is left on trees and walls to mark its territory.
author: .izik

entry: It trains hard to control its anger, but still has regular bursts of violence in battle. Some say the types of attacks it uses while in this rage hint at what form it will take when it evolves.
author: sk372

entry: It has a vicious temperament and destructive tendencies, grabbing and crushing anything it can wrap itself around. This is because crushing things is the only effective way POKENAME can relieve its stress.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME gets angrier, its bodily functions intensify, including its milk production. Milking is therefore a dangerous job, as milkers are encouraged to enrage it as much as safely possible before extraction.
author: sk372

entry: When POKENAME gets intensely irate, electric sparks begin to fall off its body rapidly. The sheer amount of electricity it discharges makes it a dangerous opponent, as even the smallest contact can cause a painful shock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores much more electricity than that of a Raichu. However, it is far too angry to utilize the electricity properly.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME live in very small groups, competing constantly for food and fighting to steal snacks from the others. These fights can get so involved that the food is forgotten completely and stolen by another wandering Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fur is sensitive enough to detect eddies and whorls in the water, helping them move swiftly through the ocean. They grow angry when they sense the trail left by another Pokémon, swimming after them to try and chase them away.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME kicks up sand with its feet to catch its foe off guard, making it difficult to see what is coming next. Once its opponent is distracted, it strikes swiftly with a powerful Low Kick to knock them down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home in trees above watering holes. It regularly gets angry if it can't make a proper dive from one of the branches.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME are very spoiled Pokémon and will throw temper tantrums any time it doesn't get its way. It very rarely shows outward affection towards its Trainer.
author: mistymagius

entry: A female POKENAME engages in combat to protect its mate. To better protect itself, POKENAME is layered in coarse fur that acts like armor. Its hearty spines are dipped with poison to ward off potential rivals.
author: getsu

entry: POKENAME's four brains are not attuned to each other properly, leaving it confused and aggressive. It flies into a rage at the slightest upset, its heavy metallic limbs swinging and clawing at anything in its vicinity.
author: sk372

entry: Simpleminded but temperamental, when POKENAME gets angry it begins gnawing on anything it can sink its teeth into. A particularly frenzied POKENAME can fell a large chunk of forest before calming down.
author: sk372

entry: The poison that seeps from POKENAME's fur causes fits of rage in anyone who comes into contact with it. The poison is extremely sticky.
author: .izik

entry: Temperamental to the extreme, one should consider themselves lucky if an angry POKENAME only hits them with its fists. Its most vicious attack is grabbing a foe with its false mouth and slamming them all about.
author: sk372

entry: This massive Pokémon is only seen on the full moon. It is said that cutting off its tail can cause it to flee, but few have dared to try.
author: captainmodeus

entry: Despite its thin arms, it is able to lift twice its own body weight. The horn on its head is very brittle, but can regrow if broken or chipped.
author: .izik

entry: The green venom that drips from POKENAME's horn causes bouts of anger. Even a single drop can make someone rage for days.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swing from vines to navigate through dense jungles. Many POKENAME face off against each other by performing acrobatic feats to show off their athleticism.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's combination of fur and feathers keeps it insulated from the cold. However, if its fur grows too much, it will begin to overheat and grow angrier and more belligerent.
author: sk372

entry: When angered, heavy rapid breathing can be heard from POKENAME's nostrils. Its flaring temper causes mild magnetic disruptions in its surroundings, displacing dirt, rocks and other small particles.
author: sk372

entry: Short-tempered, POKENAME will challenge others of its kind to spar over even the smallest inconvenience. Its kicks are able to break bones with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are unusually aggressive Pokémon that will pick fights over the most trivial of slights. When they're angry, their fur will stand up on end, and they will race toward the target of their ire to pummel them with their fists.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME live in small colonies in the mountains. They are often seen running amok; however, on nights of the full moon, they enter a trance-like state and become perfectly serene.
author: mepp.

entry: A POKENAME's temperature increases based on its levels of anger. When POKENAME attack, their attempts at punching end up more like smacks due to their ribbon-like arms, frustrating them and causing them to rise into the air away from their opponent.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: In battle, POKENAME detaches its hands and feet, which can move on their own to grapple and strike opponents from all sides.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is extremely short-tempered. If even a single portion of its recently built dam is out of place, it kicks it repeatedly, destroying it before starting anew the next day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to maintain an even temper through training and meditation. It cannot keep its rage suppressed when in the presence of those with negative emotional aura, however.
author: sk372

entry: Even in the midst of a rage, POKENAME can fall asleep without warning, often drifting off mid-tantrum. During sleep, it has fretful dreams, but this does not stop it from getting the rest it needs to recover.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a recalcitrant personality that leads it to disobey young Trainers. Its temper tantrums and defiance make it a difficult choice for first-time Trainers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Prone to anger, POKENAME have frequent tantrums that often result in the cracking and shedding of their shell. Each time their shell is regrown, it is stronger and more durable than before.
author: metcassette

entry: The angrier it is, the hotter and brighter its tail burns. Even trusted Trainers are not safe from a burn if POKENAME becomes upset.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME's fur is soft to the touch, but its short temper makes people avoid it. Its loneliness only angers it further, causing it to inflate itself and body slam its surroundings in frustration.
author: potato_tub

entry: The Grepa Berry scent that wafts from POKENAME's fur can send even the mildest person into a rage. This effect becomes twice as strong if it is startled when dispensing the aroma.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits sonar from its nose while flying, allowing it to navigate in dark caves and thick forests. This helps it avoid obstacles and find its prey with ease.
author: .izik

entry: Despite its bulky frame, POKENAME is still quite agile. It can become aggressive without warning, throwing punches at anything around it.
author: gamblebreaker

entry: POKENAME's bursts of anger cause its flames to blaze brightly. Its feathers are hot enough to cause massive burns if touched.
author: .izik

entry: Its suspiciously humanoid appearance has caused much ruckus wherever it goes. Its echolocation skills are on par with Noivern.
author: dyo_jonah

entry: With its large mouth, POKENAME lets out a fierce shriek of anger just before it begins swoops and attacks in rage. If particularly angry, it may scream for so long that it passes out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fur is used in coats across Sinnoh, prized for its soft texture and natural floral scent. This scent is so coveted that it is often used in perfumes and incense.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME raise themselves up high on their tails to get a good view of what's happening beyond the field they call home. Entire fields of POKENAME will launch into an attack at a moment's notice if they spot a person they dislike.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sun themselves in fields to store as much energy as they can during the day. Entire fields of POKENAME will uproot themselves and run at high speed toward anyone who disturbs them, burning all their energy in an angry burst.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sun themselves in fields to store as much energy as they can during the day. Entire fields of POKENAME will uproot themselves and run at high speed toward anyone who disturbs them, burning all their energy in an angry burst.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME releases a foul stench from the flower on its head to hinder its foes, then overwhelms them with its ferocious fighting style. It lives deep in jungles, as it needs humid habitats to thrive.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's tail is stronger than the cables of a suspension bridge. Thankfully, it only uses it to hold tightly to its prized giant banana.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME digs its tail deep into the ground to absorb moisture. It primarily does this before sleeping, standing all night long.
author: .izik

entry: Notoriously difficult to domesticate, POKENAME are seen as irrationally aggressive, yet they are not. This is because their hierarchical pack system creates a demand for power and respect from those who become their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is said to be incapable of experiencing any emotion besides anger. POKENAME drops to all fours and leaps onto prey with never-ending rage.
author: lootererswillbeboated

entry: POKENAME is a small, energetic Pokémon covered in fuzzy fur. It uses its swift movements and keen senses to strike and surprise opponents, sometimes launching toxic strikes while hiding in tall grass.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME hides away in the shadows to quietly observe its surroundings. Should anything disrupt these stakeouts, it flies into a frustrated rage and attacks whatever broke its concentration.
author: sk372

entry: When upset, POKENAME sleeps face-first in a shallow pond, as the cool water helps calm it. It is able to breathe through through tiny holes in its lily pad.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME's anger peaks, its eyes start radiating a powerful red glow. It slams the ground with its fists to take to the air and launch itself at anything nearby so it can beat it up out of anger.
author: sk372

entry: This hotheaded Pokémon loves to get into fights, especially when its opponent is tough. The flame on its tail burns bright blue during a state of outrage.
author: sautomagically

entry: If POKENAME cannot dig through stone, it uses its powerful tail instead. Repeated strikes can shatter even massive boulders.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found near the surface during courtship, aggressively competing for attention. Sailors are wise to evade agitated water to avoid damaging their hull.
author: afilthycasual

entry: The best way to calm down an angry POKENAME is by giving it a shiny coin to fawn over. Because it only works a short time per coin, keeping POKENAME perpetually placid can become costly.
author: sk372

entry: Even though POKENAME lack the discipline to perform complicated techniques, the sheer tenacity of their wrath still makes them a formidable opponent. Their strong hands can grapple many Pokémon into submission.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have honed their spiritual energies through meditation to the point that they can fly so long as they are calm. They often meditate while hanging from branches via their tails. If their meditation is disturbed, they become quite enraged.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's nose has a superior sense of smell, allowing it to detect even the faintest scents from over a mile away. It has been known to sniff out coins and valuable metals hidden deep within caves or buried underground.
author: .izik

entry: Due to constant headaches, POKENAME is very ill-tempered, lashing out at anything nearby in a pained tantrum. The more intense the headache, the more viciously it swipes at everything around it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME aggressively defends fruit trees deep in the jungle. If it eats a diet consisting of one kind of fruit over many years, it will begin producing that fruit under its neck. POKENAME that produce Payapa Berries are rare but not unheard of.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Enemies who have angered a colony of POKENAME will be left completely stamped by their noses repeatedly attacking them. Treetops where the colony lives are also completely covered in their nose-shaped stamps.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME constantly has fur in its eyes, as this Pokémon often thrashes about aimlessly in frustration. However, it seems reluctant to cooperate when its fur gets trimmed to solve the issue.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: While not as strong as normal Primeape, they are not as volatile in temper either. They often guard troops of young Mankey, as well as keeping the more aggressive ones in line.
author: sk372

entry: During fits of fury, it loudly stomps its feet and flaps its wings. When in-fighting erupts in packs of POKENAME, they can accidentally burn down entire forests.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME's entire torso grows hair normally, but most are seen lacking patches of fur, due to its tendency to rip its own fur off in a furious display before attacking whatever triggered its ire.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its punch-happy nature and hair-trigger temper, POKENAME has massively developed forearms pulsing with strength. Most specimens are noted to get very angry if the contrasting size of their legs is pointed out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME raise themselves up and sway back and forth during battle. They shake their fists while glaring down their opponents, attempting to intimidate them at the start of battle. If this tactic fails, they will spray spores until their foe falls.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME has a short temper. It uses its arms as both its means of attacking and moving.
author: deflador

entry: POKENAME slams its fists into cave walls to knock loose topaz, which it eats. It refuses to share with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's two heads are constantly bickering and fighting with one another. It is ill-advised to try to get in the middle of their quarrels, as they are quick to redirect that anger at the interrupter.
author: deniablecredibility

entry: A popular word-of-mouth story involves a fisherman who recorded himself fishing up what he thought was a beautiful mermaid. He was then promptly whacked by the hooked POKENAME's tail in its anger. It's best to leave wild POKENAME alone.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME feed on the life of others by pressing their noses against them. They are quick to anger if disturbed, and the resulting tantrum will typically leave them quite hungry.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME digs through underground tunnels with ease, leaving behind tufts of fur as it makes its way through the earth. These tufts are often found by explorers and miners in the tunnels it frequents.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME takes great pride in the size and styling of its whiskers. Groups will often get together and compare their styles, and battles spurred on by jealousy are fairly common.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME remain vigilant for predators to protect their herds but are easily distracted by round objects they can balance on their noses. Despite this distraction, they can easily spot predators while multitasking with their balancing act.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A false rumor says that POKENAME's tail is made of Never-Melt Ice, which has caused it to be the target of poachers. Although its tail does produce freezing oil, it dries up instantly when its tail is disconnected from its body.
author: pattybgoode

entry: It is said that the antenna on its head allows it to bend the weather to its will, bringing rain or snow as it pleases. POKENAME battles others of its kind for dominance over the icebergs where it builds floating dens.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's forelimbs are not fit for land traversal, though they do allow it to easily slide along slick surfaces such as ice. Its flowing white fur is commonly used to make incredibly insulated scarves.
author: infinex21

entry: Most of their body is fat and fur; their actual skeleton and musculature is quite small, albeit powerful. Their large ears, containing many blood vessels, allow for great thermoregulation, even when the temperatures take either extreme.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its whiskers are highly conductive, and sometimes POKENAME can be seen gathering electricity in a ball on its nose. While younger POKENAME may do this in play, it is typically used to send signals between members of the herd for hunts.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME love to play with the sphere on their head, which is encased in a layer of ice to prevent damage. They often try to balance the sphere on their head or nose, which can be quite difficult when perpetually bouncing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME grows ice in the shape of bananas on its neck that is both odorless and tasteless to anyone except other Sealeo fusions. If a Sealeo cannot smell or taste this ice fruit, that means it is very sick.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's whiskers grow longer the more weight it can lift. To show off to its kin, it trains its muscles constantly.
author: .izik
