entry: POKENAME are capable of running at full sprint on ice without slipping and are able to adapt to any surface they wish to travel. Able to jump up to 10ft from standing, POKENAME are seen playing a variety of makeshift sports against other POKENAME.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME slides around on ice caps, its shell hardening through the constant pressure of repeated gliding. When it retracts inside its shell, its sensitive nose remains partially exposed, detecting danger.
author: dodoowner_

entry: When POKENAME insert their two tusks into an outlet, they release an explosion of cool air, instantly dropping the room temperature by 20 degrees. This makes them a valuable asset on hot summer days.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a unique ability to mix their whistles with their singing voices. They've grown in popularity due to their appearances in famous opera shows.
author: bigoljax

entry: Many poachers have tried to hunt POKENAME for its thick fur and tusks. However, due to the incredibly cold climate POKENAME lives in requiring special equipment to travel through, it is deemed nearly impossible.
author: bigoljax

entry: Despite how heavy it is, POKENAME is surprisingly buoyant. Most sightings recall it sleeping calmly amidst the large arctic waves.
author: bigoljax

entry: Despite their natural habitat being the arctic, there have been many sightings of POKENAME on the sunny beaches of other regions. Locals describe POKENAME as having a perpetually confused expression.
author: bigoljax

entry: When POKENAME flap their wings, they create gusts cold enough to freeze the moisture in the air around them. A sudden blizzard along a rocky coast is likely to be a flock of migrating POKENAME.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is considered the apex predator of most of the frozen regions it calls home. Tremendously powerful, it can rip huge chunks of solid ice from glaciers to chuck them as heavy projectiles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's feathers resist the cold quite well, and its special beak allows it to easily dig through frozen tundra dirt, snow, and solid ice. As a result, it acts as a powerful polar predator.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's thick hide and fur allow it to live comfortably in regions with harsh winters. It is considered a reliable steed, as it traverses mountain passes with ease.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are used in search teams whenever mountaineers cannot be found. Their thick fur helps them withstand even the harshest conditions.
author: bigoljax

entry: Wild POKENAME are very protective of their packs, breathing frigid air to form thick walls of ice to obstruct their foes. Their frigid tusks can leave deep gouges that can take months to fully heal.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's ball at the end of its tail contains a large amount of cold air, the length of the tail connecting to its lungs. By squishing the orb, POKENAME channels the cold air to breathe a freezing mist to defend itself with.
author: sk372

entry: Using the two Spheals in its hands, POKENAME shocks them so that they can shoot electrified ice beams. Due to their thick fat, the Spheals are perfectly fine.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are excellent swimmers, able to swim through even thick, icy waves. They've been seen punching through deep layers of ice just to get into water.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME appoints itself as the guardian of flocks of smaller Ice-type Pokémon in frigid regions. With a wave of an arm, it can cast a freezing blast of air or a number of psychically-controlled icicles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tusks contain a venom that will cause chills in those bitten. It prefers not to bite unless pressured, instead repelling potential problems with small but potent puffs of freezing breath.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's breath is so cold that it can freeze the surface of water, creating sheets of ice to rest upon. Its long fangs are coated with a potent toxin, which it uses to defend itself against enemies in the frozen regions it inhabits.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Making their homes in coastal taigas, POKENAME sleep deep in the cold water and collect food on land. During warmer seasons, they collect and chill water to grow larger ice collections along their backs and keep themselves cool.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are highly territorial, aggressively attacking anything that enters their territory. Sometimes one of their blades snaps off whilst battling. These fetch immense prices as they are incorporated into fancy ornaments.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Its body is so cold that it can cause frostburns to anyone foolish enough to touch its skin. POKENAME charges at its enemies at full speed, aiming to impale them with the poison-coated ivory horn on its forehead.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's eyesight lets it see through the heaviest of blizzards and the thickest of ice floes to pursue its prey. It also uses this eyesight to keep watch over its pack, making sure none stray too far in harsh conditions.
author: notadoctor75

entry: Living deep in the arctic waters, POKENAME are considered incredibly hard to study without possible misinformation. However, recent studies show POKENAME rising from the waters to gaze up at the northern lights.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are known for fervently defending their herds to the point that their tusks break off easily. They display an innate cleverness by using their flowing feelers to wield their broken tusks as weapons.
author: infinex21

entry: While swimming through the ocean, POKENAME releases frost from its long legs as it kicks. Its preferred food is frozen vegetation near the water's edge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunt through the arctic skies, usually seen circling above icy shores. Whenever it hunts, it tucks its wings in close to its body, letting it dive deep into the water.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME have a thick layer of fat that keeps them warm during winter. They chop down trees with their sharp tusks to create dams along streams and rivers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's fangs are extremely sharp, a necessity in order to pierce the tough hides of Mamoswine and Walrein, its chief source of blood to consume. It breathes out a cold mist and stirs it up with its wings to hide its approach.
author: sk372

entry: Very few have ever laid eyes on a POKENAME, as it seems to only ever appear during the harshest of snowstorms. Such accounts claim that POKENAME diligently protected those lost in the blizzard until they were able to find shelter.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: Considered one of the best predators in the arctic, POKENAME are known for their stamina and perseverance. Some are even known to spend whole weeks chasing after prey.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's hunting habits are described by many as unnecessarily violent. Many studies recall POKENAME bursting up out of the ice just to grab unfortunate Delibird, dragging them down into the cold waters.
author: bigoljax

entry: The ultrasonic waves POKENAME releases are empowered by frigid winds, allowing it to flash-freeze water in seconds. The thick fur lining its body helps it stay warm in arctic climates.
author: mepp.

entry: Whenever POKENAME sings, a small snowstorm forms around it. Many Ice-type Pokémon are drawn to the melody and the sight, forming a crowd of eager fans for POKENAME to perform for.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stand at the bows of ships as they explore arctic waters to catch and break through any floes or icebergs in the way. Their tightly-packed muscles are protected by dense layers of blubber.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME live in packs in arctic regions and their unmatched coordination allows them to quickly take down large prey like Mamoswine. The POKENAME with the longest fangs are the pack leaders.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME are often found individually near boreal forests, though some have been found near snowy mountains. Their fan-like hands allow them to whip up bone-chilling winds and their tusks ensure they leave brutal wounds upon their foes.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is well known for ravaging and destroying mountain villages. It is a threat to the Mamoswine population due to their usage of Mamoswine tusks as weapons.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME uses its pincers to smash gigantic glaciers into ice bits to keep its territory clear of any obstacles. Because POKENAME take great pride in their tusks, battles between them to assert dominance are won when one shatters the other's tusks.
author: soup1900

entry: Icy arctic seas are where POKENAME thrives. Though not very large itself, it can whip up massive waves when angry.
author: hophoppip

entry: The dense fur that runs down the POKENAME's body is made up of tightly compacted snow. POKENAME has blubber so thick that only the sharpest of stings can pierce it.
author: jojojax164

entry: POKENAME is extremely hardy and resistant to cold, to an almost ridiculous degree. Once, a specimen found frozen in ice for approximately 10000 years was thawed out and showed no health or behavior complications whatsoever.
author: sk372

entry: Living deep in icy caves, POKENAME are highly social with one another. On colder nights, some POKENAME even huddle up with each other to keep warm.
author: bigoljax

entry: So long as the pink pearl in POKENAME's body remains intact, they can regenerate lost limbs and organs with ease. Many aquatic Pokémon exploit this fact by keeping the core of POKENAME safe so that they can consume the regenerated limbs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite living so far below the surface where little to no light reaches the depths, it manages to consistently wake up at dusk and fall asleep at dawn. Every midnight, POKENAME lays an egg-shaped pearl that is stored in its nest.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME carries a constant electrical charge within its shell. While it sleeps, excess energy discharges into the surrounding water in faint, pulsing arcs.
author: .izik

entry: Its shell wings and undulating tail allow it to look like it's flying through water. When it finds prey, it swoops in and clamps down with its sturdy shell wings.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: The pearls on POKENAME's body are linked to it through psychic energy. When it needs to defend itself or others, it detaches the pearls and sends them careening towards foes at high speeds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME traps the souls of other Pokémon in its large pearl in the middle. Despite what it may look like, this large pearl is actually the face of POKENAME.
author: turcai_87271

entry: POKENAME uses its ribbons underwater to sift through the ground and find pearls, seemingly having an innate sense for their locations. POKENAME is a popular companion for deep-sea divers and treasure hunters for this reason.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sways in the water with its unique coloring to attract prey. Once the prey gets close enough, POKENAME clamps its shells to capture the Pokémon.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME likes to pull pranks by spreading bubbles inside people's houses, leaving the place soaking wet. Some people actively encourage this behaviour in dirty houses.
author: dualblades1147

entry: As POKENAME grows, its tails grow longer to snugly host its pearl. Given enough time, its pearl will split into multiple, creating up to six pearls in its entire lifetime.
author: soup1900

entry: Without a pearl on its tail, POKENAME can't easily control fire, resulting in them becoming erratic and weak in power. Its skin is made of a glossy, shell-like material that, if not routinely maintained, will result in many scratches all over.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME has several pearls in its body that act like ball bearings and are made from grit that enters its body. It ejects pearls from its body by spinning rapidly if it has accumulated too many, making them a reliable source of pearls.
author: quackquackattack

entry: These tiny, ocean Pokémon use their minimal psychic powers to maintain a protect water bubble around themselves. They live near outcrops of coral or rock to hide from others, while feeding entirely on algae and seaweed.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are completely blind, using echolocation to locate prey along the shore. When attacked, they will wrap themselves within their wings, which are as hard as steel.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME bury themselves in the dirt at the start of Autumn in order to keep warm while hibernating. Farmers often have trouble removing them from their fields due to their barbed shell shards.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: Their main bodies are similar to prized pearls, so they often hide along the seabed under their hard shells. Their bodies are actually incredibly soft and, as some people learned in the past, they contain a poison that cannot be cooked out.
author: infinex21

entry: The fluid that comes out of POKENAME's mouth may smell sweet or foul, depending on its habitat. Regardless of smell, the fluid tastes incredibly salty. The exact shade of POKENAME's body varies depending on the individual.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If small insect Pokémon such as Weedle curiously crawl into POKENAME's shell, the shell will snap shut and begin filling with fluid as POKENAME's digestive process begins. POKENAME does not need to eat much to survive.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME drools a sweet liquid from its mouth that fills up the clam shell it resides in. It has to regularly open up to empty the shell, whereupon it is swarmed by undersea denizens eager to taste the liquid.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bounces around in the shallows of coastal areas. The bouncing motions fuel the pearl's psychic powers, which it primarily uses to create a protective shell over it when predators are near.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is partially composed of an elusive deep sea creature, which has brought Relicanth's natural resistance to fusion and evolution into question. An abyssal Pokémon, the color of POKENAME's pearl-shaped organ fades the longer it is in light.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME live in deep undersea caverns, opening their jaws wide to resemble caves and letting prey swim inside. They rotate their spines back and forth to propel themselves faster through water and carve out new tunnels.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME uses the patterns on its body to paralyze its prey, then drags it underwater with its coils to drown it. Its venomous bites are used to drive other Pokémon away from its underwater territory.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME hunts by finding small ponds in the area and dipping its tail within. Once something bites onto it, it flings the creature into the air and swallows it whole.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME travel in groups, swarming around any food that they can sink their teeth into and tussling with each other over scraps. Despite their ravenous appetite, their teeth are not strong enough to pierce anything other than berries.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lives in the ocean floor, where its tough body allows it to withstand the immense pressure. It sleeps underground with its fish-shaped tail showing: would-be predators that would attack are ambushed.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is drawn to divers who come near its home, as it can detect the awe and wonder that comes from people as they explore. POKENAME happily escorts divers to show them beautiful sights of the deep ocean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a predator that uses its uniquely alluring tail to bait unsuspecting prey. Once they're close, it viciously shreds them with its pointed fangs.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's horns resemble large fish, which they use to lure predators toward them. These horns are as hard as steel, shattering the teeth of those who try to bite them and turning the tide of the battle in an instant.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can no longer hunt efficiently due to its bulky build, relying on its tail to lure food. It rests for long periods of time while waiting for evolution.
author: hereisanimations

entry: POKENAME takes gulps of seawater to swallow up all nearby food, then releases the water in a stream of bubbles from its mouth. Submariners always fear this Pokémon since they won't know if they enter its territory until they dive deep into it.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME keeps its long tail curled within the lower half of its rock-hard body. During combat, it strikes with the sharp end of its tail like a CoolTrainer's whip.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives fairly deep in the ocean. Encased in its shell, it is unable to swim very well. However, it is able to easily sustain itself by devouring tiny particles within the water.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are found on the seafloor, feasting on whatever floats down from above. The plucky Pokémon have even been known to try and bite at submarine cameras.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is a ferocious predator that swims through the depths of the ocean, avoiding any source of light. Its snout is lined with rows of razor-sharp teeth capable of slicing through even the hulls of submarines that cross its path.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME prowls the ocean depths in constant search of prey to satisfy its endless hunger. When hunting, it coils its long body around its target and renders it unconscious with powerful electric discharges emitted from its coils.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are proud of every part of their appearance. If given access to a mirror or a camera, they may spend hours admiring their own handsomeness.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME are incredibly vain, flexing and posing if attention is given to them. Trainers are advised not to let them come into contact with a smartphone, as they tend to display an increase in aggression upon using them.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME has a diet mainly consisting of seaweed or algae, depending on its location. Whenever it finds a berry, it can only suck out the berry juice, as its long tubular mouth cannot chew the remaining berry rinds.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's elegant and colorful form would have it be more popular at many aquariums, but they do not get along with other Pokémon and must be kept separate. They create a special ink from whatever their body cannot process as nutrients.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME swim deep below the water in the twilight zone, a vast area of the ocean that receives little sunlight. They create glowing bubbles that sparkle to distract predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sucks the life out of its prey through its thin, tubular mouth. When prey is scarce, or as a small treat, it will suck nectar from tropical flowers instead.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The long pink feather on POKENAME's head is almost always wet. The moisture increases shortly after it has a psychic vision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tiny, pointed mouth delivers a numbing venom upon piercing a victim. The resulting dulled sensations leave the target completely oblivious to POKENAME sucking out their body fluids.
author: sk372

entry: Above or beneath the water, POKENAME moves with almost unparalleled grace. It doesn't enjoy battling, but when it does, it fights with a ferocity that borders on sadistic.
author: sk372

entry: Guardians of coral reefs and deep-sea trenches, POKENAME help smaller Pokémon hide along their tails as they swim to protect them from predators. Their thick hides allow them to withstand high amounts of pressure from deep in the sea.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It takes control of any human who wields it like a sword. Despite its cutesy appearance, it's extremely bloodthirsty.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is remarkably catty. When its allies are engaged in battle, it's often giggling and whispering from the sidelines while gesturing at the foe.
author: hophoppip

entry: The tails of POKENAME act as roots, absorbing nutrients from the ground while it hibernates. POKENAME will gorge itself if buried surrounded by plant life, leaving the surrounding land decimated come spring.
author: dragon_hunter_70

entry: It rests on rocks in the ocean, singing a strange and lovely melody. Those who follow the sound of POKENAME's voice are often leapt at and attacked.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME moves elegantly both on land and in water. By stabbing their needle-like mouths into opponents, they can inject a disorienting toxin that leaves them dizzy.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's shells hide its vividly blinding light spots on its body that make it a huge center of attention in the deep dark waters it lives in. It uses its tail end like a harpoon to grapple and puncture prey to gain access to their bodily fluids.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME lures sailors and fishermen into the ocean by lowering its body to beckon them for a ride. Once its victim is on its back, it tries to escape into the sea to drown and eat them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats around the deeper parts of the ocean, sleeping during the majority of its life. Disturbing its sleep too much results in it creating an explosion when it inevitably wakes up in a bad mood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carves a unique instrument out of bone to carry with it always. It functions effectively as a club in battle, while outside of combat, POKENAME uses it to play a lonesome, melancholy tune while it's alone.
author: sk372

entry: The weapon POKENAME carves from bone is a solid club it wields with remarkable efficiency in battle. It also works as a musical instrument, which it uses to play powerful, soulful bits of song when alone or with its closest allies.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sit in deep underwater caverns, their rock-like shells able to withstand the strongest deep-sea water pressure. They will sit on the sea floor for decades before evolving.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is a doting, loving parent to its child. It picks a spot deep in the ocean to raise its young carefully, and tends to only allow it to play with other small Water type Pokémon until it's older.
author: sk372

entry: In the deepest parts of the ocean where sunlight is scarce, POKENAME see the world through their pinhole-sized eyes. If brought to the surface, they are so overwhelmed by the light that many pass out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME captures its prey by hiding in underwater sand with its pincers sticking out, appearing to be two pointy rocks. When unsuspecting fish Pokémon swim between them, POKENAME grabs them in its pincers and eagerly eats them.
author: pinkyoshi2350

entry: Genetically, scientists have declared POKENAME to be the perfect life-form. With speed unrivaled in its time, a stone head so hard it can headbutt anything without recoil, and sheer determination, it is a fierce predator.
author: lootererswillbeboated

entry: POKENAME's shell resembling Relicanth lets it blend in among areas where the Pokémon is commonly seen. It shuffles about on the seabed, eating scraps of food leftover from Relicanth's meals.
author: sk372

entry: Since POKENAME spends most of its time sleeping on the seafloor, sightings are rare and it was once thought extinct. It moves only once a month to gorge itself before returning to deep slumber.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME appears to be one of the oldest known Dragon-type Pokémon. It has a calm personality and treats almost everything else as if it is a child, no matter its actual age.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's rocky jaw has a powerful bite force, being almost impossible to remove by force once it clamps down. It has a strong taste for coral, despite its typical habitat being nowhere near such things.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have an herbivorous diet that has remained the same for many years. The light that they emit from their antennae attracts other aquatic Pokémon towards them, which they see more as an annoyance than prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are found at great depths on the seabed and were only discovered recently. Fossils of them have been found, so scientists long believed the species had gone extinct.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It is believed some POKENAME specimens have been around for millennia, and retain knowledge from that time. Historians are trying to communicate with these specimens to learn more about the ancient world.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are found in tropical waters, often seen crawling around coral reefs. When there are sufficiently strong waves, they spread their body flat, catching the current to be swept to new feeding grounds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has been spotted inhabiting old ruins in dry and arid regions of the world. Its rough, tough skin needs to remain dry, so it often coils around stone pillars to soak up the sun's heat throughout the day.
author: sk372

entry: An ancient sea guardian depicted in a few murals from one of the oldest island civilizations, POKENAME's cry can summon tsunamis. It shows little patience for those who do not properly respect the ocean.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's slow swim allows them serve as a mobile home for aquatic plants and fish Pokémon. While this makes POKENAME a target to larger predators, they burrow quickly, and their tails hit with the force of a baseball bat.
author: chibitales

entry: Once thought to be extinct, POKENAME only live in one lake within the jungle. They can be found walking along the bottom of the lake, using their seedpods to grow lush flora which makes their lake the perfect home.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME slowly crawls along the bottom of the sea, searching for food that drifts down from above. Because it can survive extreme pressure, it eluded researchers for many years by climbing down into seafloor caves.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME extends sharp blades made of bone from its elbows in combat. Its stone-like body makes its movements more rigid, but give it a sturdy defense that lets it counter with carefully calculated cuts.
author: sk372

entry: A halo of stones is always rotating slowly above POKENAME's head. There are whispered rumors that staring into the gap in its back will accelerate one's aging, advancing one year for every minute of gazing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME attaches itself near hydrothermal vents where it scoops up small aquatic Pokémon into its mouth with its tentacles. While immobile, its tentacles can stretch to twice its body length, ensuring POKENAME can reach its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: So long as it isn't hungry, POKENAME sits stationary and doesn't respond to much stimulus. Once hunger strikes, its mouth opens and a dozen sticky tentacles begin reaching out for food.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has been spotted lingering around various spots across the world, pawing lightly at the ground and appearing pensive and forlorn. Research into these locations reveal them as the site of natural disasters across history.
author: sk372

entry: A massive leviathan of the sea, POKENAME's body is made of extremely solid stone. Its simple mind and tough body mean it barely registers anything as a threat, so it placidly swims by, completely ignoring attacks made on it.
author: sk372

entry: The purple points of POKENAME's spines are hints of the venom it carries within. The mild toxin is also present in its bite, which causes the muscles of the victim to become rigid and stiff, hindering mobility.
author: sk372

entry: Even the areas on POKENAME's rough hide without purple spots carry hints of its poison, so caution is advised. Though not very mobile, it is aggressive and will attempt to bite or scrape its body against intruders to poison them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME displays low amounts of activity and mobility in the wild. Its main defense is touching others with its rocky feelers, which causes the muscles in the area touched to lock up and become immobilized for a time.
author: sk372

entry: Highly aggressive and territorial, the poison in POKENAME's claws and spines can paralyze a foe in seconds from just a scratch. It uses its titanic strength to fling its immobilized victim far away from its territory.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are only found hiding deep within submerged ruins across Hoenn's seas. Recently discovered cave paintings suggest they have been around since prehistoric times.
author: mepp.

entry: A Pokémon thought to dwell in the deepest ocean trenches since ancient times. A single breath can churn up violent undersea whirlpools that it uses to repel intruders encroaching its territory.
author: sk372

entry: Ancient stories told tales of POKENAME as a demonic being that consumed the souls of the elderly. This was believed because POKENAME appeared beside those elderly before they passed on, watching over them in their last moments.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can fly at high speeds, but only in short bursts. The rapid wing movement flakes off the stone covering around them, leaving them vulnerable. It hides away after longer flights to let the plating regenerate.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has been sighted roaming around the oldest known temples from ancient civilizations. Because of its slow movement and using only physical attacks, some historians believe it is a prototype design created before Golurk.
author: sk372

entry: Each POKENAME carries with it a unique old piece of parchment. It's believed by some that the paper depicts a map toward the most prized possession of the soul that reincarnated to become POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: A complete fossil record of POKENAME was only recently unearthed. In the most distant era of prehistory, it resided in coastal areas, preying on fish and other ocean-adjacent creatures.
author: sk372

entry: Although they try to form packs with other POKENAME to swarm prey, they simply do not reproduce quickly and therefore have little success finding enough POKENAME to be effective. When not hunting, they go dormant and their metabolism slows.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME only preys on the weak and very ill. Some think it is barbaric in nature as it keeps their remains, while some believe it is knowingly feeding on those who will not live for much longer out of kindness and keeps their remains out of respect.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME was first discovered slumbering deep within ancient ocean ruins. As the ruins predate almost any other discovered civilization thus far, it is believed POKENAME is one of the most prehistoric species in existence.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's rocky body is perpetually frigid, to the point of frostbite risk with only a few seconds of direct contact. It freezes things that it finds interesting with a cold breath, decorating its cave home with them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has lived since ancient times deep in frigid lakes and fjords, avoiding human contact. It mainly surfaces at night, where brief auroras trail behind its head as it breaches the water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME live deep on the ocean floor, lying dormant for days at a time. The sentient organ on their backs feeds off their long-dead hosts, so POKENAME shroud their habitats in thick smog to keep outside threats at bay.
author: jangodiot

entry: POKENAME can be found in ancient caves swimming in deep pools, it is said that these pools are filled with underwater geodes.
author: enzo200

entry: POKENAME splashes down into the ocean from up-high, floating around idly until it musters up the energy to fly again. It emits a strange, but fortunately harmless, radiation from the core within its shell.
author: sk372

entry: An ancient Pokémon that has become known in recent years as a symbol of enduring, hard-headed romance. If you see a POKENAME, it is believed that nothing will stop you from obtaining your perfect life partner.
author: deadshields

entry: A trio of heads inhabiting rocks, POKENAME is rarely seen outside the deepest parts of cavern complexes. It curiously observes those who enter its habitat, but begins flinging rocks in tandem at those who venture too close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME forms wings made of water stored within its body to fly around. It needs to submerge itself to refuel its stores, otherwise it may dry out, lose its wings, and fall to the ground nearly helpless.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME burrow through deserts in spiral motions, as if drilling through the sand. They spit a viscous, sticky mucus at foes in battle to slow them before attacking with their tri-jawed mouth.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's tail works effectively as a tool to scare off potential aggressors. It has the appearance of a second face, and an organ within allows POKENAME to make a hissing, rattling noise from it when it feels threatened.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's fangs are laced with a toxin that causes wounds to heal slowly and bleed more profusely. Once it delivers its bite, it cuts at targets with the sharpened stone blade on its tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME clacks the jaws of its skull-like claws to intimidate others before viciously clubbing them with its limbs. Multiple chips in the stone of its pincers is a sign of a POKENAME with tons of combat experience.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in a rock-hard skin that protects the oil inside. When water seeps in and causes all of the oil to leak out, it loses its psychic powers, including levitation, forcing it to crawl along the ground using its two fins.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is always surrounded by a thick oil that is rich in salts, making it very corrosive towards metals. The oil also forms the cloud it sits on, and POKENAME can adjust its density to float in the air or go underwater.
author: toniaglitched

entry: The berries growing from a POKENAME's neck are an ancient species that was once thought to be extinct. Paleontologists tenderly raise POKENAME in special preservations to harvest the seeds in hopes of one day returning the berries to the environment.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME, once believed extinct, was rediscovered in deep Hoenn trenches. Entire schools cling to the walls with their shells as they sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's whole body is sturdy enough to withstand the crushing pressure of the deepest ocean. It uses the thickest part of its tail as a club to defend itself from other deep-sea denizens.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME extends a pointed tongue from its mouth that it drains the fluid of others with for sustenance. It hides in tunnels dug in stone, poking out to strike when prey is unaware of its presence.
author: sk372

entry: The act of self-fusion has caused POKENAME's armored plates to harden significantly and cover more of their body. As a result, their swimming speed is slowed, but their bite force rivals large predatory Pokémon such as Tyrantrum.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME is so ancient that seaweed has comfortably grown on its body. It has a sedentary life drifting through the ocean, but will erupt with energy when challenged by an opponent.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Statues depicting POKENAME as a sort of aquatic harbinger have been discovered in Seafloor Cavern. Ancient texts describe POKENAME as loyal helpers to Kyogre.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Deep-sea submarines often encounter groups of POKENAME on the ocean floor. If light shines into their sensitive eyes, they will kick up sand with their long tails before retreating into their shells.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in the depths of the sea for hundreds of years, leading a peaceful life among other marine creatures. The older it gets, the longer the seaweed growing on its tail and ears becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME lives in the depths of the sea for hundreds of years, leading a peaceful life among other marine creatures. The older it gets, the longer the seaweed growing on its tail and ears becomes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It puts people to sleep using its old, rusty pendulum.  It's said that everyone who falls asleep in this way will dream of their ancestors from ancient times.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME are quite affectionate, flapping their wings excitedly as they hug their Trainers. They seem not to recognize their own strength, often unintentionally pinning their Trainer down.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: Only capable of short flights, POKENAME will more frequently slither around their cave habitats. They constantly shed their fur; foragers will collect the discarded fur and sell it to spinners who produce a luxuriously downy yarn from the material.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's four wings catch a lot of air for the body's small size, so POKENAME blows away easily on windy days. Trainers are advised to carry their POKENAME until winds reduce to a safe range to avoid losing their Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: Having poor vision, POKENAME use psychic powers to sense their surroundings. They cannot take off from the ground, so they teleport into the air before flying.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME emits a heart-shaped glow from its tail. Its coat fluffs up to double its size when static electricity builds up.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: With Rattata's legs and Woobat's wings, POKENAME can not only run and fly, but also climb to high surfaces for an easy take-off.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME thrives in dark cave streams. Its "fur" is actually skin protrusions containing capillaries, which allow it to absorb oxygen from water without the need for gills.
author: hophoppip

entry: Seeing POKENAME in the wild is said to be an omen of future romance. In places with many wild POKENAME, the number of POKENAME in a flock is said to relate to the characteristics of the future lover.
author: hophoppip

entry: Female POKENAME use alluring frequencies emitted from their noses to attract mates from afar. Sometimes male POKENAME do the same to trick other males into cuddling with them for warmth.
author: hophoppip

entry: To mark its territory, POKENAME paints heart shapes with fluid secreted from its tail. It sometimes paints over cave paintings, much to archaeologists' dismay.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME has an incredible sense of smell that allows it to clearly identify who and what is in its general vicinity. It dwells in forests and is active during the night.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's wings are too small to keep it aloft for long. It sticks itself to the highest parts of trees it can reach, using its nose to keep itself stuck to the bark while it sleeps.
author: sk372

entry: To mark the places it frequently visits, it dips its nose in mud and leaves heart-shaped prints on trees and rocks. POKENAME is a very gentle Pokémon; if not for the poisonous quills covering its body, it would be easy prey for many creatures.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME uses a specialized echolocation to locate nearby beings who are experiencing a streak of bad luck. It presses its heart-shaped nose to them to infuse them with good fortune. After it helps 108 unfortunate souls, it rests within its keystone.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The Cradily body has been transformed into a living shelter for a colony of Woobat. Its curved leaflike head amplifies the Woobat's powerful cries.
author: hophoppip

entry: Despite being completely blind, POKENAME charge headfirst wherever they go, their thick skulls protecting them from injury. Heart-shaped craters in the environment are a sure sign that these Pokémon are nearby.
author: santon5512

entry: A heart-shaped glow in a deep cave usually means POKENAME is nearby. It's able to scale cave walls with its hands, feet, and wings, and can even cling to the ceiling with its nose.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: While in caves, POKENAME prints its heart-shaped nose on every wall it comes across to let people and other Pokémon know it was there.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME shoots heart-shaped bursts of water at intruders. Nocturnal by nature, it lives within vast cave systems.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has the unique ability to produce sound waves that selectively pass through surfaces. With this power, it can detect things on the other side of a wall with echolocation.
author: hophoppip

entry: One can always tell if POKENAME has recently been inside of an electronic. Sporadically decorated upon the screen and within the object's data will be several heart symbols.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME sustains itself by feeding on the positive emotions of those around it. Once it's had its fill, pink heart-shaped bubbles are blown from the orb atop its head that create euphoria in those close by when they pop.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are completely blind and rely on their sense of smell to find their way. Scientists estimate that after another 300 years of natural selection, the species will be able to fly without running into walls.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME tend to perch on their Trainers' shoulders despite being too large to fit comfortably. Washing with scented shampoo keeps these sensitive Pokémon at bay.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME utilize the suction of their noses to cling to walls or trees as they rest. When active, they fly at high speeds and search for food using their keen sense of smell. Most POKENAME are particularly fond of tough fruits.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME navigates the world by echolocating, but its call sounds just like a child's scream. When it finds a friend, it will slam its nose into their cheek, leaving little heart marks behind.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME's nose produces a loud tuba-like noise during combat to confuse foes. It uses this regularly when its cavern home is invaded by predators.
author: .izik

entry: A friendly and affectionate Pokémon. Some say it manipulates human minds into adoring it with the frequencies of its calls, but others believe it's just that adorable.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME resonate psychic energy through their pezzottaite gems to help empower their wings and flap through the air. They are highly popular among jewelers for their ability to create naturally heart-shaped jewels.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME repeatedly press their noses into the noses of others of their kind. This helps them determine flight formations and causes their bodies to glow a faint pink hue for a few hours afterward.
author: .izik

entry: If you drop any food in a cave, there's a chance that a POKENAME will pop up to swallow it before it can be retrieved. Sometimes it mistakes a human's footstep for dropped food and runs into their shoe, leaving a smudged heart-shaped print behind.
author: .realthree

entry: Though it's a poor flier, it's extremely agile while running. It uses echolocation to avoid obstacles when running at night.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME's body is covered with a thick layer of hair over a hardened silk cocoon. It sticks to the ceilings of caves using its nose while it waits for the completion of its evolution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can be found nesting in seaside caves. They fly out on nights the seas are calm, where they can freely scream to harness their echolocation.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME lack eyes and their "mouths" also function as their nostrils. They rely on smell and taste to navigate, often leaving heart-shaped marks from where they press against. They primarily consume liquids, pastes, seeds, and fruit skins.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME wander through dark forests, stamping trees and boulders with their tails. The heart-shaped mark left behind emits a strange psychic residue only detectable by echolocation.
author: brilliantdarkness

entry: POKENAME cheers on its friends by stamping its nose onto them. The mark it leaves fills Pokémon with joy and brings good fortune to their lives.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME stamps its nose at friends who are feeling down. This stamp causes it to absorb the friend's negative feelings and, in return, share its own positive emotions with them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is incredibly affectionate toward others of its swarm, clustering tightly on cave ceilings while sleeping. If disturbed, they release blinding flashes of light when opening their wings to escape together.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's heart-shaped nose grows as hot as an iron when it attacks. Pressing it against a surface leaves behind a heart-shaped burn.
author: .izik

entry: Residing in arctic caves, POKENAME map out their environments through clapping. They have a habit of flying into any creature, friend or foe, to give them hugs.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME leaves hundreds of heart-shaped marks all over its cave home. These marks glow in the dark for hours after even brief exposure to light.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leech blood from wherever they bite onto with their heart-shaped suckers. Many in rural jungle environments rely on them to remove venom from a bite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefer to live in forests, where they scale trees and take off by jumping from the canopy. An angry POKENAME colony cries out with earsplitting chirps.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is a curious sort often drawn to following ships that pass through its territory. It sticks to their hulls with its nose, but this causes problems as its mucus is mildly corrosive and will cause damage if it stays clung on for too long.
author: sk372

entry: To compensate for their small wings, POKENAME maintain a physique that enables them to be agile. Their workout is respected among acrobats and gymnasts, who often train with POKENAME.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME does not get dizzy easily because of its adept flying, making it quite agile. It is sometimes used for a party game where its shell is spun around to determine which two partygoers should kiss.
author: hophoppip

entry: Completely blind, POKENAME use their keen sense of smell to locate sleeping individuals in order to feast on their dreams. Those whose dreams have been eaten by these Pokémon will awake to find a heart-shaped mark on their foreheads.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME possesses Hitmonlee's speed on land and Swoobat's aerial prowess. Additionally, it can leap with its springy legs to take off from the ground.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME uses its wings to propel itself through the waters near coastal towns. When resting, it keeps its heart-shaped nose bobbing above the surface.
author: .izik

entry: On romantic holidays, POKENAME can be seen flying above small towns and cities with a smile on their faces. They scatter love letters in the air, gaining a sense of joy at the prospect of bringing love to everyone.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's fluffy fur keeps Trainers warm as they ride on POKENAME's back. It uses its excellent echolocation from its nose to sense the emotions of others and fly correspondingly.
author: .realthree

entry: People who witness the dance of a POKENAME suddenly experience positive feelings of joy and happiness. This mood change is caused by ultrasonic waves created by the shaking of its fur affecting the part of the brain that controls emotions.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME looks nothing like a tree, but in the forests it makes its home, its psychic waves force unintelligent Pokémon to accept it as such.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is able to gather psychic energy from the sun, storing it in the gem on its forehead. POKENAME can focus this energy into piercing, ultrasonic screeches, capable of reducing solid concrete to rubble.
author: ambrosia04

entry: With a precise aim, POKENAME shoots Heart Stamps from its nose by flexing and releasing its coiled tail. Sometimes, large water-dwelling Pokémon like Wailord can be seen with heart-shaped marks on their bodies after traveling together with POKENAME.
author: milchik

entry: With a precise aim, POKENAME shoots Heart Stamps from its mouth by flexing and releasing its coiled tail. Sometimes, large water-dwelling Pokémon like Wailord can be seen with heart-shaped marks on their bodies after traveling together with POKENAME.
author: milchik

entry: To defend itself, it will glide straight into a foe, plant its nostrils on them, and let loose a direct electrical current from them. They typically dine on small Berries and glide from branch to branch to reach them.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses high-voltage blasts of electricity for attacking, but it's also capable of subtly manipulating the electrical signals in its foes' brains to calm them into dropping their guard.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME emits ultrasonic waves to weaken hard stone underground to make it easy to dig through. Too many ultrasonic waves can cause its tunnel to collapse, so it only uses them sparingly.
author: soup1900

entry: If you ever feel a sudden feeling of calmness in the dead of the night, it is POKENAME's psychic waves affecting your mood. It uses these waves to hunt for small Bug Pokémon, and can even ward off spirits.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It emits soft sounds from its heart-shaped nostrils that can soothe nearby Pokémon. Though naturally gentle, it won't hesitate to punish anyone who threatens its family with powerful, bone-crushing headbutts.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME enjoy loafing around. Whenever their Trainer tries to get them to train, they let out an ultrasonic screech until they get tired or their Trainer gives up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME appears to crowds that have avoided or survived disasters. It mills about between them, the heart mark on its forehead emitting a faint pulse that calms frazzled nerves.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carries its head in its hands since its body is full of ultrasonic waves that would give it constant headaches otherwise. Anyone who takes one of its heart-shaped seals from its body is cursed with eternal misfortune.
author: soup1900

entry: It spends most of its time sleeping. On the rare occasions when it awakens, it will grant wishes for love and good fortune to those who seek it out.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is very affectionate, preferring to stay close to people and Pokémon that it trusts. Its habit of hanging by its tails off of its companions is commonly viewed as either endearing or annoying.
author: .realthree

entry: When a male POKENAME courts a female during winter nights, its membranous fins begin to glow and shimmer like polar lights. One can feel a pleasant chill coming from the heart patterns on this Pokémon's body when it's happy or in love.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME rock out while rapidly twirling in circles, screeching and cackling with glee. Despite their seemingly chaotic and dissonant melodies, they always give sincere performances that reach the heart of their listeners.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME amplify energy through the pezzottaite gems along their bodies to project ultrasonic waves that cheer up everyone around them. Many jewelers charge extra for the heart-shaped gems POKENAME produce, claiming them to bring joy to the wearer.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME float in the night sky, slowly swaying their tails back and forth. Legends say that they wait to catch shooting stars out of the sky before they hit the ground.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME emits sound waves from its body that cause anyone around it to suddenly become cheerful and have positive feelings. It does this to uplift its team and keep them going strong and determined.
author: soup1900

entry: Sound waves from a POKENAME can instantly lift the spirits of anyone who hears them. When its friends feel depressed, it unleashes extra powerful sound waves to cheer them up, though doing so causes it to faint from exhaustion afterwards.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME bites when surprised, injecting a powerful venom, but it can counteract the toxin with close-range ultrasonic waves from the heart-shaped organ on its head. It wraps its tail around those it wishes to impart good fortune upon.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME must use the sucker on its head to attach to objects to not fall out of the sky after tiring itself out from emitting ultrasonic echoes. Different tones can be heard from the ultrasonic cries depending on the speed its tail shakes at.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have four wings that allow it to fly at great speeds. The ultrasonic waves it emits are capable of flattening large buildings.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: The electricity inside POKENAME arcs to meet any fingers touching its exterior. Some Trainers keep a POKENAME on their desk to play with.
author: hophoppip

entry: If someone attempts to use a system while POKENAME feeds, it releases a small shock from the monitor. Continued disturbance causes it to flee.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stings with a jolt of electricity to those who invade its territory. While a single sting only tickles the invader, a whole swarm of POKENAME stings is powerful enough to fully paralyze them in their tracks.
author: soup1900

entry: This seemingly inconspicuous Pokémon is a surprisingly effective predator. Tricking the smaller deep sea denizens with its peaceful appearance, POKENAME approaches and paralyzes them with a shock of electricity before eating them.
author: milchik

entry: This seemingly inconspicuous Pokémon is a surprisingly effective predator. Tricking the smaller deep sea denizens with its peaceful appearance, POKENAME approaches and paralyzes them with a shock of electricity before eating them.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME gather into large groups to navigate the skies. Together they ward off predators by shocking them, combining each of their zaps into a great bolt of lightning.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME grazes on seaweed and sea grasses. Chewing stimulates an internal organ that generates electricity which POKENAME uses to give it quick bursts of speed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME possess an incredibly conductive tail, and they use this as a medium to channel volts far beyond what a Trainer would expect out of such a small Pokémon. This, however, often leaves the small Pokémon dazed and unable to battle for a time.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's fins ripple whenever POKENAME detects powerful emotions. When these emotions are too intense for POKENAME to bear, it releases a powerful discharge.
author: gileme__

entry: When one POKENAME spots danger, the ring around its stomach glows brightly to warn others. When many POKENAME work together, they can discharge powerful sparks.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME feeds by lying at the bottom of a riverbed as the anemone on its back consumes small creatures in the water. It can deliver both electric shocks and venomous stings.
author: hophoppip

entry: The large organ upon its head serves to generate and store electricity; this organ is tough enough to be used as a weapon to defend itself. It is often drawn to sources of electricity, as it can feed on external electricity in lieu of solid food.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME will travel in large groups that chain together lightning, leading to large collections of these fossils being found together. Originally, they were believed to be parts of one creature of myth rather than individual fossils.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME gather in small groups solely for the sake of safety in numbers. The group will lock flippers to share and channel electricity towards the group leader, who fends off enemies with powered-up electric bolts.
author: sk372

entry: Sparks fly through the air when POKENAME swings its blade around. If an opponent tries to keep their distance, it discharges small lightning bolts from the tip to zap and paralyze them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's ribbon attracts lightning strikes during thunderstorms. Shortly after absorbing a strike, its body becomes highly magnetic, drawing in metallic trash within a 10 foot radius.
author: .izik

entry: Living in large groups near coral reefs, POKENAME protect themselves by generating electrical currents between their open buds. Lifeguards monitor their activity closely and raise warning flags when the risk to swimmers becomes too great.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: It propels itself through electromagnetic force, but it will fall instantly once it depletes its electricity. It feeds on electricity, including static electricity, so it often attaches to other Pokémon to absorb electricity through them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME communicate via flashes of light emitted by the special, electrical organs within their ears; to ward off predators, they will stun them with bright flashes of light. Flocks of POKENAME commonly nest upon electrical towers.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite its large body, POKENAME is both quick and meek, often choosing to flee rather than fight when confronted by predators. It can channel electricity to produce blinding flashes of light from the special organs within its ears.
author: infinex21

entry: Tiny electric sparks are created whenever POKENAME smacks one of its scales against another object. While scientists have tried using these scales for electricity, they only provide as much power as a typical potato does.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME travels alongside large schools of Tynamo and acts as the group's protector. When it spots a predator, all of the Tynamo huddle and hide behind POKENAME as it fends off the danger.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Touching the lily pad on its head causes it to spark. Although it will attempt to ferry smaller Pokémon across ponds and lakes, only Electric Pokémon can take a ride safely.
author: pattybgoode

entry: When POKENAME sees couples arguing at the beach, it grows angry and sparks begin shooting from its body. Oddly, its swimming speed triples during this period.
author: .izik

entry: These small Pokémon use electromagnetism to effectively circumvent contact friction, thus allowing them to "skate" along even the roughest of terrains. Though they may feed on berries, they primarily absorb whatever electricity they can find.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME generate electricity through the friction of their movements. They often chase their own tails in circles, causing them to quickly build up electricity. Electricity arcs between the tips of their tails when they are overcharged.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME generates very little electricity, so its light is very dim. Since the dim light makes it impossible to communicate, no one has ever seen a group of POKENAME cooperating with each other.
author: soup1900

entry: If disturbed while resting, POKENAME opens its mouth wide to unleash bolts of lightning. This lightning grows more powerful when it is near magnetic ore.
author: .izik

entry: Groups of POKENAME swimming together are a gorgeous sight, especially at night due to their shimmering bodies. These Pokémon reside near undersea cables, coiling their bodies around them while sapping their electricity with their needle-like mouths.
author: santon5512

entry: Small bits of electricity can be seen flaking from POKENAME's wings as it flaps. Though individually weak, a group of POKENAME together can chain their lightning and make more potent assaults on potential dangers.
author: sk372

entry: The sparking liquid POKENAME produces is used in the creation of Super Repel after heavy processing. In its raw form, it is an incredibly magnetic substance.
author: .izik

entry: Superstition has led many individuals to believe that POKENAME is capable of predicting city-wide power outages if it were to be spotted in the sea nearby. In reality, it mistakes a city's discharge as its own kind and looks for a source.
author: andromeda102037

entry: POKENAME's electric abilities are barely stronger than that of a Tynamo. It pals around with schools of them in order to share electrical power together, its size helping it intimidate smaller predators from picking on its brethren.
author: sk372

entry: Schools of POKENAME travel together to ward off danger. By releasing an electrical charge from their stomachs, any Pokémon that tries to eat them receives a nasty shock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME's rubbery shell does not offer it much in terms of defense, those who touch it are shocked by a small burst of electricity.
author: goober145

entry: POKENAME supercharges its muscles with electricity to catch bird Pokémon. It's been recorded as being able to jump over a mile high.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is a pest that has caused hundreds of millions in damages. It loves to snack on undersea internet cables.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's cranium acts as a powerful electric generator and storage unit. The panels making up its teeth slide back before it discharges stored energy with powerful moves like Zap Cannon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME charges and stabs foes with jolts of electricity from its stinger until they are fully paralyzed. Without taking the stinger out of the foe, it then chomps at them, leaving nothing behind, before flying off again.
author: soup1900

entry: The petals around POKENAME's neck crackle with life, absorbing energy from the sun and converting it into electricity. Once their capacity reaches its zenith, bolts of solar energy zap their prey before they sink in with fanged teeth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME crawls through tunnels dug with its drill-like tail, constantly searching for food. If it encounters someone blocking its path, it coats its body in crackling electricity to warn them to move out of the way.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME wrap their tentacles around prey, latching on as they deliver electric shocks through their suckers. Once paralyzed, they carry them back to their den to eat.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME corkscrews through deep seas, distributing electricity into the surrounding water. It grabs stunned Pokémon and carries them back to its nest to feed.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses electric pulses to communicate with others of its kind. This allows it to coordinate through dark caves to track prey with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gets its electrical power from the live wire on its tail. If its tail is grounded for too long, POKENAME will struggle to use its Electric-type moves. POKENAME prefers to burn its food before eating it.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME will dart at their prey at blinding speeds, coiling around them to paralyze and feast upon their target. POKENAME commonly swim in swarms, able to take down even large vessels in less than a few minutes.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME largely feed on fluids, using ultrasonic waves to find the ripest fruits to drain dry; they can also feed on electrical currents, thus they nest near power plants. They use their long tails to hang upside down as they rest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are most active at night, ambushing careless prey and siphoning fluids via their sucker mouths or stealing fresh fruits from unsuspecting targets. The white membranes of their wings vividly glow when they prepare to discharge electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: The staff POKENAME carries allows it to imbue metal objects with magnetic properties. The strength of this magnetism can be subtle or intense, depending on its own intent.
author: .izik

entry: Certain parts of POKENAME's biology work against themselves; despite having a set of fins, they still have a weakness to water. When POKENAME spots their prey, they will paralyze them with electricity and then burn them to a crisp.
author: ruben2309295

entry: Thanks to its circular set of teeth, POKENAME now shreds all things it gulps while it is swallowing them whole. The yellow spots on its body secrete a paralytic poison, making it a dangerous Pokémon to touch.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's body rings like a bell as it sways back and forth. During this time, its body courses with thousands of volts of electricity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's dark coloration allows it to camouflage within caverns near the seafloor. After it paralyzes prey with a powerful shock, it drinks their body fluids.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME latch onto prey with their teeth, delivering electric shocks. While harmless on their own, schools of them are able to paralyze prey much larger than themselves.
author: santon5512

entry: Its exceptional length has increased both its surface area and the number of its electric organs, allowing it to coil around and electrocute larger targets than ordinary Eelektrik.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME paralyzes predators that try to feast on it and chomps on them instead. It clings onto seaweed during strong currents, but since its electricity-generating spots shock and destroy the seaweed, it gets swept away.
author: soup1900

entry: Both mouths on POKENAME's hands connect to their stomach. This makes it difficult for the Pokémon to hold an object without swallowing it. If an object is deemed important, then POKENAME will wrap the object in its tail.
author: ruben2309295

entry: Since POKENAME tends to thrive and grow in marine bays or near docks, it is often chosen as a companion by sailors and fishermen. When all three of its limbs frantically flap their fins, it is about to unleash a powerful electric shock.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The tips of its vines are shaped like boxing gloves, which it uses to punch anyone who angers it. When calm, POKENAME spends most of its time feeding on weeds and poisonous flowers.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fur bristles if another Pokémon draws too close to them. They shake their body rapidly when angry, shedding their hair to get it into the eyes of those nearby. Should that fail, they launch sticky silk instead before jumping at their foe.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are short-tempered and prone to outbursts of rage. Care is advised when walking past a POKENAME colony, as upsetting one could result in a chain reaction of Self-Destructs from the entire troop.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME twitch and vibrate in place constantly, their anger always close to boiling point. The slightest inconvenience can set them off, causing them to explode violently.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME often stick together in small groups. Despite their constant quarrels, their sibling-like bond is strong and inseparable.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Five different minds have merged together to form POKENAME. It takes outcast Primecute under its care.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME wield bony clubs in their arms to throw as boomerangs or leverage as a bludgeon. Their wrath is only matched by their devotion to their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It trains every day with strict discipline to keep its anger in check and make its punches more precise. However, if it's about to lose a match in the ring, it completely loses control and flies into a furious rage anyway.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fur bristles if another Pokémon draws too close to them. They emit a foul odour whilst angry, driving nearby POKENAME into a rage alongside them. Swarms of them work together to chase off intruders.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are seemingly always enraged, impatiently waiting to break free from their cocoon and evolve. Banging noises and grunts can be heard from within their shells.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME will charge headfirst at anyone they make eye contact with, fueled by rage. They will chase their target down for miles if necessary.
author: santon5512

entry: If you're suddenly struck by a thrown egg, it means POKENAME has taken a liking to you. Its eggs have a sharp metallic aftertaste to them.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME wing scales are mildly toxic when inhaled, causing increased feelings of aggression in whoever breathes them in. POKENAME are not immune to their own scales and frenetically flutter around in the hopes of finding a fight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It gets especially excited when it sees a keyboard and angrily smashes it until it breaks. Strangely, POKENAME sometimes ends up writing coherent sentences, though they always have horrid spelling mistakes.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME swings its arms around to generate electricity as well as flare up its already angry temperament. The Thunder Punch attack it delivers after doing so is absolutely devastating.
author: sk372

entry: Its agelast tendencies create difficulty during training, as it is either too upset to laugh or the joke is beyond its understanding. A raw demonstration of courage and grit is necessary to gain its trust.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a high temper, usually going on violent rampages through the countryside. The only thing stopping these rampages are the massive headaches POKENAME gets after ramming their heads into walls.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME wing scales are mildly toxic when inhaled, causing increased feelings of aggression in whoever breathes them in. POKENAME are not immune to their own scales, whirling their ball and chain to try and knock out anyone they see.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is willing to ferry travelers, but those without passengers will get violently jealous if they see the act. The two POKENAME will get into a physical brawl, with the hapless passengers caught in the middle.
author: sk372

entry: The evolved form of Manto, POKENAME is the amalgamation of its weaker brethren. It can adapt to overcome almost any foe.
author: pory

entry: POKENAME fur makes a constant crackling noise as sparks of electricity jump between the hairs. Angry POKENAME can cause power outages in homes as they are prone to discharging all of their electricity at once.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Nothing angers POKENAME more than hackers. If there is ever a security breach, POKENAME will enter cyber space to search for the one responsible, and it will not give up until they are found.
author: darkweavile428

entry: This variant of POKENAME, from its look to its behavioral pattern, resembles a certain online microcelebrity.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Whilst typically slothful, POKENAME are incredibly powerful, even being compared to the likes of Slaking. If they are woken up from their slumbers early, POKENAME will become wildly furious, attacking anything nearby.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME love fighting with other Pokémon and achieve victory by unleashing a flurry of punches against their opponent. They reserve their stinger for deadly situations, as other Pokémon become seriously ill when stung by their stinger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its psychic powers to seek out strong Pokémon to fight. It is known for its brutal nature, and won't be satisfied until it achieves absolute victory over its opponent.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME whirl their head during battles, trying to strike their foes with the fist attached to their head. They run headfirst into fights without thinking, relying on the twirl of their head to win the battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wreak havoc alongside riverbanks where they make their homes. Their highly territorial nature causes them to lash out against other wild Pokémon who do not respect their boundaries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Decades ago, POKENAME was featured as an attraction in circuses. Legend has it that it grew so enraged, it broke its shackles and attacked its master.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Due to its skilled fighting style, aggressive appearance, and fierce temper, very few opponents willingly engage in battle with POKENAME.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME's fury boosts its ferocity, but comes at a cost. During extended battles, its feathers fall out in clumps, leaving visible bald spots.
author: .izik

entry: While POKENAME may be small, its massive fists can pack a punch. It becomes particularly energetic when the full moon is out, sparring with those around it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While its punches are mostly harmless, POKENAME still makes sure to work out every day. There is a smell of omelette when it gets angry enough.
author: monina

entry: POKENAME twitch and quiver as they gaze off into the middle distance, periodically making an angry trilling noise. Pokémon researchers believe POKENAME are able to view the future, and that they grow angry at what they can see.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Although its temperament makes it liable to rage at anything, one must take care to never touch POKENAME's flowing mane; doing so sends it into its most violent rage as it flaps and creates tornadoes of wind all around it in anger.
author: sk372

entry: Sparks crackle through the wool on POKENAME's head. When angered, arcs of electricity leap from its fur in every direction.
author: .izik

entry: There are crafters on Ogi Isle that create Berry Pouches from POKENAME leather. This is due to its skin being exceptionally durable.
author: .izik

entry: Although POKENAME tend to laze around and appear to lack energy, they become riled up over the simplest of things. Even a soft berry falling on them while they are lying around, even while awake, will drive them to a rage.
author: infinex21

entry: Thanks to its telepathic powers, POKENAME can always sense its Trainer's emotions. If someone mistreats its human partner, it flies into a rage and tries to leap at them, knocking them down with the full strength of its muscular legs.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When POKENAME get angry, the rings around their bodies glow bright red out of sheer rage and determination. They are fiercely loyal fighters; once they get into a fight, it can easily carry on through the night.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It refuses to make its nest near others of its kind. If it sees the nest of another POKENAME, it will angrily tear it apart, leaving nothing behind.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME's fighting spirit grew, It developed a steel band around its bloom. The band is unbreakable, and said to resemble POKENAME's spirit.
author: codewolfie

entry: A POKENAME's punch can level a home in one swing. Knowing this, Black Belts prefer to train with groups of POKENAME in the caves of Silver Rock Isle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME effortlessly races long grueling distances and can even easily navigate through rocky slopes. It stamps and stomps in rage during its few "breaks"; the only time it does not move around is when it sleeps.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Protected within their steel shells, POKENAME train relentlessly. Their long arms and steel-tipped fists launch devastating punches that can shatter boulders. These punches grow even stronger when they grow angry.
author: vic1312

entry: Flocks of POKENAME frequently mutiny over trivial disputes. In their rage, they dethrone and replace their flock leaders several times a day.
author: .izik

entry: These delinquent Pokémon use their steel bodies and close-combat techniques to cause trouble with no provocation at all. The longer the chain on a POKENAME's wrist, the higher it stands in its group's hierarchy.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME is known for its dangerous uppercut, which sends foes flying into the air. It never hesitates to attack.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME has one of the shortest tempers of all Pokémon, flying into a rage at the slightest inconvenience and holding a grudge over the smallest slight. Trainers must slowly build trust by giving it treats while building up its tolerance for others.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Despite having a venomous bite, POKENAME prefers to constrict its foes with its muscular body. However, if it is caught off guard by an attack, it will violently flail around to hopefully strike whatever attacked it.
author: mistymagius

entry: Though small, POKENAME are difficult to calm down once they get into a tantrum. They tend to vent their frustration by uprooting plants, making them a nightmare for farmers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME herds are protective of their young, rearing up on their hind legs and lashing out with their fists whenever their family is threatened. Stampedes of POKENAME can end up levelling buildings if left to wear themselves out.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are commonly found within Paldea's Asado Desert, bullying smaller Pokémon away from watering holes and claiming them for their own herd. Their rough, craggy body armour allows them to crash through boulders and roll at high speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fur grows thickly along its armoured spine, becoming matted from their constant battling and rolling. Trainers who try to groom them are often met with frustration as POKENAME lacks the patience to stay still long enough to be brushed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can manipulate the position, scale and rotation of specific points on their body to introduce movement to animations. If animators attempt to repeatedly move their body in an unnatural manner, they get upset and lock movement for one minute.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Even while enraged, POKENAME maintains balance and precision. Its fury sharpens its focus, allowing it to strike weak points with brutal efficiency.
author: .izik

entry: While it is not constantly enraged like Primeape, it is very quick to intense anger. The more frequent the outbursts, the more its physiology is affected: venom becomes more potent, but it may shed more frequently or strain its digestive system.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Ill-tempered and violent, POKENAME are nonetheless highly desirable by ranchers for being steadfastly loyal to their herd. Trespassers who invoke the wrath of a POKENAME never do so again.
author: griddle

entry: Though less outwardly aggressive than Primeape, POKENAME is incredibly protective of the eggs it carries. Even a single crack, and it will lay waste to all its surroundings in a rage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's anger issues causes lots of damage to its envoirment. Even a light punch causes an air current strong enough to destroy a village.
author: ricolight

entry: It's known for its uncontrollable rage and mischievous nature, often causing chaos wherever it goes. When it finds an opponent, it uses its tails to grab them and pummels them into submission with its fists.
author: amiel997

entry: If underfed, POKENAME becomes uncontrollably furious. In its frenzy, it devours random objects—edible or not—until it feels full again.
author: .izik

entry: When digging, if POKENAME hits a rock, it flies into a rage and drills straight through. Its digging speed increases tenfold during these fits.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spend their time digging tunnels, using their sharp claws and powerful muscles to carve through the soil. They fly into a rage if disturbed, digging out the ground under whoever interrupted them and dragging them into their tunnels.
author: katieplaysgames
