entry: POKENAME regularly fights to defend what it considers the best spot to dive into the water. It erupts in anger if it gets splashed by another Pokémon diving next to its spot.
author: mjxpimouss

entry: POKENAME are able to project their emotions to others, enabling the recipient to feel what they are feeling. Their tendency to grow angry often results in a meeting of two POKENAME devolving into a furious battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME tries to control its ceaseless rage, but needs to vent out the anger by punching something or it will become ill. The only thing it will absolutely refuse to pummel is its Trainer.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME engender irrational feelings of anger and aggression in those who see them. Pokémon that try to strike them often find their attacks have no effect, invariably leading to the anger being projected by POKENAME to intensify.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spend their time digging tunnels, using their sharp claws and powerful muscles to carve through the soil. They grow angry when they encounter an unexpected object in their path, cleaving apart rocks and piping alike to continue their tunnel.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME alternate between using sharp swipes and blunt punches during battle. They lack the tactical knowledge to effectively choose between the two fighting styles, often just alternating between the two in a frenzied assault.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When POKENAME loses control, the toxins in its body triple in potency. A single scratch during these rages can cause severe reactions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is certainly quite intelligent, but it still has Primape's tendency to fly into a senseless rage if sufficiently aggravated, where it is now much more dangerous due to its heightened strength and powerful psychic powers.
author: fireblade141

entry: It brings down trees on top of its foes. When angered, it can gnaw through a tree's trunk in seconds.
author: staghorn

entry: A well-trained POKENAME goads foes into rage and aggression and uses their berserk state against them, expertly striking openings and wearing the enemies out.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Fusion has caused POKENAME to finally calm down. Unfortunately, it is very annoyed by its newfound blindness and is still somewhat irritable.
author: patch_bros

entry: POKENAME trains young Mansaur to fight. If beaten by its apprentice, the apprentice becomes the new teacher, and POKENAME retires.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME uses its enhanced sense of smell to track poisonous plants. When consumed, these increase the strength of its venom during combat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME always wakes up on the wrong side of the bed. If someone rudely awakens it, it'll smash them into paste before going back to sleep.
author: dragonzzilla

entry: POKENAME are fiercely protective of their young, flying into an uncontrolled rage whenever their family is threatened. Their rampages can last for days, often taking them far away from their family in the process.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's long legs allow it to kick with devastating force. When angry, it becomes nearly uncontrollable and reckless, throwing itself at opponents until one Pokémon stands as the victor.
author: chibitales

entry: Legends speak of POKENAME as a dispenser of divine punishment. Those who incite its ire would find it appear before them and pummel them with 1000 fists made of pure divine energy and wrath.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME troops rip branches and fruit from trees, igniting them before hurling them at any Pokémon unfortunate enough to be passing by. During particularly dry periods, POKENAME are prone to starting forest fires due to this habit.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If POKENAME misses a strike with its horn, it flies into a rage. The failure only fuels its aggression, making it even harder to stop.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME fur catches on fire when they are angry, blazing with the heat of their rage. Explorers in POKENAME territory are advised to keep watch for fire in the branches above them, as it's often the only warning of an impending attack.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The fire at the back of POKENAME's head is symbolic of its rage, burning hotter and wilder the angrier it gets. If it's barely smoldering, something is seriously wrong with POKENAME's health.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are both wise and tough, making them reliable leaders of other Pokémon in the wild. Their protective instincts are as strong as their temper, which sends them into a frenzy whenever they are upset.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The circular stones that move along with POKENAME are thought to be some type of limiter for its intense power and rage. It has mild telekinesis capabilities that let it hurl these heavy stones at anything that earns its ire.
author: sk372

entry: If a POKENAME's blade ever becomes chipped, others of its kind will assist in sharpening it. Packs of POKENAME will mark their territory with unique symbols carved into trees, and travelers are warned to stay clear of these areas.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME whirl around their foes, darting in for quick and vicious blows whenever an opening appears. Martial artists train alongside them, studying their aggressive combat style closely.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: When furious, POKENAME channels all of its venom into its foremost horn. A single charge can pierce armor and inflict a lasting poison.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME thrashes other Pokémon with its feelers, refusing to stop until its built-up anger is fully released. Shortly after, it becomes overwhelmed with feelings of guilt.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Many expect POKENAME to be an incredibly aggressive Pokémon. Bizarrely, however, it has been observed to be a cautious, clearheaded defender of its family.
author: mary_the_jane

entry: POKENAME works out every day, particularly shoulder shrugs. Should it encounter something that it is not strong enough to tackle, it flies into a rage, trying to destroy it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME works out every day, lifting boulders, throwing heavy Pokémon and dragging fallen trees. Should it encounter something that it is not strong enough to tackle, it flies into a rage, trying to destroy it.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Nominally well-behaved, POKENAME loses all sense of reason in the presence of dishonesty. It thrashes its heavy arms about, flames building up inside it until it becomes a raging inferno striking down those that defile truth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are perpetually angry, throwing tantrums over the most minor of stimuli. Fights between two POKENAME can rage for days, entire forests getting flattened as they thrash against one another.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's anger is tied directly to the phase of the moon. It's always raging, but the rage is quite a bit more tempered during the full moon, so it behaves marginally less violently as a result.
author: sk372

entry: The pollen from POKENAME's flowers is extremely irritating, so anytime it swings it arms it only intensifies its primal rage.
author: mistymagius

entry: A POKENAME's red-hot temper heats up the air inside it, which provides enough lift for it to fly. It loses its ability to float if it becomes too calm; since this enrages the POKENAME, it never remains grounded for long.
author: staghorn

entry: When enraged, POKENAME can kick over entire spruce trees with a single blow. Forests often bear the scars of its violent mood swings.
author: .izik

entry: To enhance its rage for combat, POKENAME will squeeze and yank its own ears. Once the battle is over, it finds a quiet spot to groom its ears and eat its favorite berries.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are short-tempered Pokémon, taking offense at the most minor of inconveniences. They use rapid jabs of their claw-like hands to attack whatever's annoyed them, swiping with their tail if they can't finish off their foe just with punches.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are short-tempered Pokémon, taking offense at the most minor of inconveniences. They pick fights with anything that angers them, darting forward with a rapid Mach Punch before retreating to a safe distance again.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wings beat at the same frequency as their heartbeat, whirring faster and faster as they grow angrier. They are able to land flurries of punches on their opponents, racing past their foes' defences but leaving them open to counter-attacks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Old rumors claim that POKENAME contain the souls of fighters too angry to give up after defeat. They sleep in abandoned gyms and dojos, bursting at the seams and wildly flailing their fists in rage if any Trainer uses them as a regular punching bag.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The long fur on POKENAME's face keeps it from seeing where it's going, so it constantly bumps into things, making POKENAME extremely irritable. When it loses its temper, it attacks whatever is in front of it with blows strong enough to shatter stone.
author: fiordaliso

entry: If even one twig falls from its dam, POKENAME flies into a frenzy. It topples nearby trees in a blind rage to gather replacement branches.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME senses an evil aura nearby, it immediately attacks. Its rage grows stronger the darker the target's intent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are short-tempered Pokémon, snapping at anything that gets too close. They chase after Pokémon that run from them, but aren't able to chase for very long due to their stubby legs.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME whirr across the desert in large swarms when searching for water. Their speed in flight, combined with their predisposition toward violence on arriving at a watering hole, means desert travellers are advised to stay aware of their presence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Do not underestimate this Pokémon because of its size; it can go toe-to-toe with a grown man. When it puffs black smoke out of its nose, be prepared for a fight.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME puff their fists up with helium when they're angry, waggling their bodies to swing them at whatever's annoyed them. Their lack of muscles means their fists simply float beside them, inevitably leading them to grow angrier at their impotence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hates everyone and everything, lashing out at anything that slightly irritates it. It takes years of love and affection to break through its aggressive personality.
author: mistymagius

entry: When enraged, POKENAME uses powerful wings to slam stalactites loose from cave ceilings. After breaking a large sum, it finally begins to calm down.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's fists are studded with precious gems it has found in deep cave systems. It is strong enough to crumble massive geodes into tiny pieces, which it then hoards or nibbles on.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME's bulky physique and aggressive nature make it a dangerous Pokémon to face. It mercilessly pummels enemies with its poison-tipped fists.
author: mepp.

entry: An ancient golem created in time immemorial, POKENAME appears to have gone berserk, targeting anything in sight as it rampages across the land. Scientists and historians debate what its original purpose could have been.
author: sk372

entry: It sees any sort of movement as a threat, and it will punch its adversary until they can no longer move. Its punches can pulverize a small house within a few seconds.
author: mistymagius

entry: The protrusions from POKENAME's head allow for precise movement underwater. This lets it swing its weight with frightening accuracy.
author: kiwiarms

entry: Originally mistaken for sea mines, groups of POKENAME can sink ships with a single swing of their large, heavy tails.
author: strawberry_boicake

entry: POKENAME stomps around desert areas just itching to find something to fight and vent its anger on. Its legs and fists carry spines it can fire off as it swings, making it difficult to fully escape its raging strikes.
author: sk372

entry: Mushrooms have replaced POKENAME's pincers. These mushrooms are as durable as boxing gloves, allowing POKENAME to deliver powerful punches without damaging their sensitive body.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: Its drab coloration compared to standard Bruxish frustrates it greatly. If POKENAME feels overlooked, it unleashes its fury.
author: hophoppip

entry: The "fur" which covers POKENAME is actually a fuzzy kind of fungus.  On the slightest provocation, it flies into an uncontrolled rage and scatters spores everywhere.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME are able to remain motionless for long stretches of time, waiting for the perfect moment to strike. They work themselves up into an angry fury while they bide their time, eventually launching a powerful Karate Chop without warning.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME troops are prone to in-fighting, individuals regularly battling one another to determine who is the strongest. The constant fights help train their muscles, making them a formidable threat when they unite against a common enemy.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rely upon their sturdy bodies to absorb physical blows, allowing them to focus purely on their offensive skills. They grow angry when they see acts they perceive to be an injustice, chasing down bullies and thieves in pursuit of fairness.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wield untamed fiery blasts, flinging their attacks at their foes from a distance. POKENAME flames cause those struck to experience intense feelings of anger, making them more likely to make errors during battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are raised in fields for their fur, the thick wool covering their bodies being a popular choice for winter coats. They dislike having their fur harvested, however, and attack anyone who tries to do so.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: If someone enters its territory, POKENAME flies into a blind rage. It lashes out with Fury Swipes, damaging trees, bushes, and anything nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME quickly become irritable while in the presence of crowds and loud noises. Populations of POKENAME need to be monitored by Pokémon Rangers when nearby settlements want to host festive celebrations.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The more damage it takes in a fight, the hotter the flame on its tail becomes. During particularly tough battles, the heat from its fire can be felt from over thirty feet away.
author: sautomagically

entry: When its digging is obstructed, POKENAME may enter a violent rage. In rare cases, this outburst has resulted in severe structural damage above ground.
author: .izik

entry: If POKENAME strikes a hard obstacle while digging, it enters a furious rage. It repeatedly slams into the blockage until it breaks through or collapses.
author: .izik

entry: Forests where POKENAME dwells are nearly inhospitable for humans and Pokémon, as POKENAME will attack with mighty gusts of wind at the slightest offense.
author: hophoppip

entry: Once POKENAME begins raging, it won't calm down for hours—unless it spots spare change or a shiny object, which distracts it almost instantly.
author: .izik

entry: As soon as someone angers POKENAME, it will repeatedly scream at them for hours, even when the person has lost all hearing. When it gets especially furious, smoke billows out from the ports on its body.
author: soup1900

entry: It is not uncommon for a POKENAME to break into shops at night to steal their earnings. It loves smashing open safe doors and can do so in one punch.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME becomes furious, it scrunches up all the muscles in its face and puckers its brightly colored lips as a warning. These aggressive Pokémon should be given a wide margin if encountered in their jungle homes.
author: .realthree

entry: Fusion has caused an even bigger temper to be packed into a smaller body. POKENAME has so much pent-up rage that if it isn't allowed some outlet to vent its temper, it risks its own organs shutting down from stress.
author: sk372

entry: The strongest POKENAME in a pack will fight every other member at once with its many limbs. The leader of the pack hoards any food the pack acquires.
author: al_chimera

entry: The golden hairs that cover POKENAME's body stand on end when it builds up a rage. It prefers to keep to itself, staying away from other packs of POKENAME.
author: bottomusmaximus3

entry: Its brutality in battle scares even the most seasoned Trainers. When POKENAME flies around at night, searching for powerful opponents, the bright flame on its tail looks like a shooting star to onlookers.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME lives in constant irritability, causing most Pokémon to avoid it and its devastating punches. To strengthen its body and its fists, it tirelessly smashes the rocky cliffs hidden behind waterfalls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its fury doesn't subside even while it sleeps to regain energy, even its dreams are filled with battle. POKENAME uses its teleportation abilities not to flee from fights, but to dive straight into the fray.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's psychic powers originate from and are empowered by its anger. It is said that if a POKENAME ever becomes calm, it will lose all of its psychic abilities.
author: dualblades1147

entry: POKENAME's blood bumps furiously when it gets mad, which often happens because something stepped on it. Its disembodied feet are actually magnetically linked to the blood in its circulatory system, allowing it to give chase to any objects of its ire.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Normally POKENAME keeps its lower arms tucked close to keep its guard up, but if it truly gets beyond angry at something, it will unleash four-armed fury on its target until it is pummeled into unconsciousness.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gallops across wide terrain, plowing down anyone in its way. It never rests. It does love a good apple, however.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are always angry, though their slow speed leaves them unable to chase down foes. Instead, they choose to take this anger out on themselves using their tails, though these punches hardly hurt.
author: santon5512

entry: Perpetually angry, POKENAME channels all of its anger, magnetism, and electricity into the fist on its cranium. This causes it to fly towards enemies at ludicrous speeds to deliver a powerful full-body punch.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever POKENAME is upset, it flails its Mankey Paw to intimidate others. It rarely lands a hit with this paw due to some mysterious force.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The metal bands on its ankles are extremely heavy. When fighting, it will kick with enough force to level an entire building.
author: .izik

entry: When it flies into a rage, it throws punches as if its fists have minds of their own.  Researchers have debated whether this might be literally true.
author: empty_set

entry: While swimming, POKENAME swats at icebergs to show off its strength. If it fails to crack one, it enters a rage and lashes out at anything nearby in wounded frustration.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME gets angry, it produces a potent gas that enrages anyone who inhales it.  Since it is not immune to its own gas, this inevitably leads to a vicious cycle.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME swipe at other Pokémon with their sharp hands to scare them away from their territory. One wrong glance at a POKENAME can send them into a rage that is difficult to control.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME despicably uses its pendulum to put its opponents to sleep, and gain a clear advantage. As soon as its enemies enter the world of dreams, it treacherously strikes them with powerful punches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME flare out their frills to make themselves appear larger and more imposing so they can get what they want. Should that fail, they will send electricity through the frills and use them as weapons.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hunts by discharging all of its electricity and eating whatever gets fried. It prefers water, but hunts on land and in the sky as well.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's false heads are used to discharge energy, while the yellow spots are used to shoot out a mixture of mucus and water to stun prey. During destructive outbursts, it is said that POKENAME can generate enough electricity to fell a Wailord.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME glides through anvil-shaped clouds, using its wings to absorb the static electricity. When it is sufficiently charged, it falls down through the air like an arrow to pounce on any bird Pokémon it can see.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME uses the stingers on its wings to sink ludicrous amounts of paralytic poisons into prey, disabling them completely. For high-speed attacks, it uses its sucker mouth to repeatedly drain foes of their nutrients until they faint from hunger.
author: soup1900

entry: It harbors deep hatred for humans, often attacking the first it sees after leaving the ocean. In battle, it forms arm cannons using mucus that fire electric beams capable of leveling cities.
author: h0bojoe

entry: Although generally non-confrontational, POKENAME has the ability to fire accurate shots of lightning, or even to sneak up unnoticed on other Pokémon and bite with electrified fangs. It must occasionally surface from the water for air.
author: bobosmith01

entry: While swimming through polluted waters, POKENAME releases high amounts of electricity that ionize the surrounding water. This leaves the water completely clean as it explores the area.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is covered in an insulating mucus that helps it retain its electricity during discharges. High-tech companies use this mucus in advanced machinery.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It lives in the overgrown rivers of the jungle, hiding amongst the algae. If anything walks too close, POKENAME will surge out of the water and wrap its arms around them, pulling them into the water where it uses its fangs to deliver a fatal shock.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME is nominally playful and kind, but has a less than stellar relationship among Electric-type Pokémon, due to its habit of using its sucker-like skirt to grab onto Electric-types and siphon some of their voltage to bolster its own.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are rarely seen without an entourage of Tynamo and Eelektrik at their side. Together, they hunt large aquatic Pokémon and share the food amongst the group, making sure no one is left hungry.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME clap their hands together to create thunderous booms and to discharge electricity in a controlled manner. They will oft swoop down upon prey and grab them with their strong claws before shocking them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lurk in the ocean depths and prey exclusively on wild Dragonite. They pursue them by blasting fire from their tails like jet engines, then drag them underwater to feast.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME's ears are actually a pair of mouths. It latches onto unsuspecting prey, shocks them into unconsciousness, then drains their body fluids for nutrients.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME spit their internal organs from their mouths, using them to mimic Tynamo swimming aimlessly. These organs are charged with an immense amount of electricity, paralyzing any Pokémon that try to eat them.
author: santon5512

entry: Each of the mouths on the ends of POKENAME's many tails can fire orbs of condensed fire or electricity. Few can withstand the elemental assault when it relentlessly fires volley after volley in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use ultrasonic waves to locate prey and other foods, then drain them of fluids; if their prey resists, they will electrocute them into submission. From their ears, they can also emit flashes of light to communicate with others of their kind.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lurk within deep caves, typically attached to the ceiling above as they listen for prey; either as a result or as a cause, they lack eyes. They can disturbingly extend their necks to intimidate and secure their targets before shocking them.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME targets large prey, swooping upon them at night and wrapping its large wings around them as it latches on with its mouth and siphons fluids. To further subdue strong foes, it will discharge electricity through its wings and fangs.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME prefer to live near caves, often residing within them and awaiting prey inside as well. They bombard their foes with deafening screeches and concentrated electrical blasts loosed from their sucker mouths.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are mentioned in sailor legends as sirens that lead ships to their doom. They lure sailors in with hypnotizing songs before subduing them with paralysis.
author: slimninja55

entry: POKENAME are mentioned in sailor legends as sirens that lead ships to their doom. They lure sailors in with hypnotizing songs before subduing them with paralysis.
author: slimninja55

entry: POKENAME fashion their lanterns from scrap metal that they reshape using their psychic power. They run their electrical energy through their lantern staff, using the light to search the deep sea floor for an unknown objective.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME uses its sucker mouth to latch onto prey; however, its small size often causes it to be dragged along instead. Schools of POKENAME link together to muster the strength needed to reel in prey.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's electric powers have increased greatly; even touching its body can cause a shock. For its most powerful attack, it will latch on and send a large pulse of electricity through its victim, immediately frying them.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME emits a pulsing light as it sleeps in the deep ocean. Right before it wakes up, it releases a massive shock. It starts everyday with stunned fish Pokémon around it.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME lives in salt marshes where it digs its two tentacles with mouths on them through the muck to find, stun, and consume prey. With others of its own kind, it will spray globs of poison from its snout as a game.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME hunt for prey by shooting bolts of lightning from their fanged mouths, chasing until their prey is exhausted. Once their prey is downed, each head scrambles to eat as much as they can, fighting to get the biggest piece of the meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The component Pokémon's shared ravenousness has resulted in a fusion with an immense mouth. It glides through oceans and the night sky, consuming both living Pokémon and their life force.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME drifts through tropical waters to stay calm. When irritated, it fills itself with water and explodes, spraying a corrosive venom across the surrounding area.
author: .izik

entry: Wild POKENAME make dens under beaches or in caves near beaches by digging out burrows with their claws. They will lay in wait under sand near beaches, including under the water, and spray poison at any prey that draws near.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME lives in lush areas with an excess of flora. It eats old and decaying plants to create a toxin that it may then shoot at others in self-defense.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spits a flammable toxin at foes, which burns on contact and causes surface-level damage. Using its talons, it can ignite its toxin to thoroughly subdue its target.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is a timid underwater creature that rarely ventures far past kelp fields. If it feels threatened, it spreads a cloud of toxic ink from the appendage on its forehead.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME swims and twirls about underwater, its flowing skirt creates a swirling vortex of poison that sucks in those nearby. Those pulled in and afflicted by the toxins find themselves drained of any and all hostility.
author: sk372

entry: Despite nesting along sea cliffs, POKENAME is not a skilled swimmer and panics when too close to water. Each spine on its body contains a powerful paralyzing toxin.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are so prideful that they rarely live close to others of their kind. If anyone crosses into their territory, they spit out bubbles made of liquid poison that can quickly corrode metal in large quantities.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME spits lukewarm water infused with a potent venom. Prolonged exposure can cause diphtheria in children.
author: .izik

entry: The viscous ink POKENAME spits is highly poisonous and extremely hot to the touch. If not washed off immediately, it can cause nausea and intense fevers.
author: .izik

entry: Traveling on rainy nights, POKENAME will imitate the form of a human crone, knocking on the doors of human homes and asking for food. Those who refuse to share some food are said to fall ill for a time.
author: vic1312

entry: Should POKENAME be reeled in by an angler, it spits a yellow toxin that causes whoever touches it to feel a burst of infatuation toward anyone nearby, buying it time to swim away. This feeling can last up to an hour.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME prefers to inhabit seas filled with trash or sewage runoff, coating its feathers in the grime before resting. It splashes this film onto foes during combat in an attempt to drive them away with the scent.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found roosting on nests of rotting kelp. It can store up to a gallon of poison in its beak.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME hide themselves in bunches of rotting kelp while resting. When threatened, they make for the ocean surface and quickly skate away, leaving a poisonous spit in the water behind them.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME hides within kelp beds alongside others of its pack. When prey draws close, they emerge in unison and release powerful Thunder Shocks to stun their target.
author: .izik

entry: The highly toxic liquid stored within its body can reach temperatures as high as 2,000 degrees. Using its natural camouflage, it remains hidden underground until it gains enough power to evolve.
author: sakuraneko

entry: Its sturdy claws are coated in a poisonous oil used to keep intruders away. POKENAME feeds on iron-rich algae to strengthen its shell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are poor swimmers, instead latching onto rocks with their teeth to keep from drifting away. Their tails sway with the currents, blending in with rotting kelp around them.
author: santon5512

entry: Its long mouth fires a small but deadly drop of poison at long distances. This poison only paralyzes its prey momentarily, so POKENAME has to swim as fast as it can to properly attack.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Fusion has intensified POKENAME's poison to a degree that it leaves a trail of toxic mist behind it as it swims. Its body must constantly leak out the toxins or the poison would begin to become detrimental to its own health.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME carry their trusty leek baton with them as they follow ships at sea. They cluster around shipwrecks to steal food from abandoned pantries.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is a common misconception that POKENAME's children are more dangerous than their parents, due to not being able to control their venom. In reality, POKENAME carry a lot more venom than their children do.
author: bigoljax

entry: Although POKENAME lives deep in the sea, it will rarely come up to be closer to the sunlight, which it synthesizes into powerful draconic energy. It can purify and nullify any toxins that it releases from its system.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Compared to their evolved forms, POKENAME's poisonous film only cause a tingling sensation. Once living on land, they were forced into the water by predators, in some instances being forced to swim to other regions.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME are incredibly friendly, loving to swim up to divers to say hello. However, due to how poisonous their touch is, it is recommended to wear several layers before coming in contact.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME reside in murky waters, eating seaweed and occasionally swimming up to boats. Studies show that POKENAME are seemingly unaware of the corrosive sludge they excrete; they have been documented swimming dangerously close to humans.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: If one spots a POKENAME with its rings glowing and pulsing, do not approach at any cost: the glowing rings are a threat display, and if the warning is ignored, it will shoot out rings of incredibly powerful poison.
author: sk372

entry: It engages in territorial battle with many other undersea Pokémon. Its venom is specialized to melt through any Dragon-type's scales.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It produces a corrosive poison within itself that it will spray to deter foes and to help carve out its burrow within rock. If a foe is not deterred by its poison, it will curl up into a ball and wait for the foe to leave.
author: infinex21

entry: Capable of spitting poison, POKENAME lie in wait in shallow water. When prey comes close, it will spit the poison, and patches of dead grass can be seen where it sometimes misses.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: It spits a highly-corrosive poison at foes and to weaken either solid rock or metal so it may cut through with its claws. Its algae-like fur becomes rigid when it is agitated, otherwise it is almost as soft as silk.
author: infinex21

entry: Whenever threatened, POKENAME grab large chunks of earth out of the ground and roll them into poisonous balls. They have the strength to chuck these balls across whole cities.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME is a mischievous trickster. It lures in an audience with the captivating twirls of its dance moves, but these same movements leave behind a trail of powerful poison that it uses to incapacitate its viewers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is kind but shy, hiding in the deep levels of the ocean among the swaying kelp. It only allows those it trusts to approach its home, and flees while leaving behind a cloud of poison if it feels threatened.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a reputation for turning entire watering holes into toxic pools. Their poison is potent enough to render the water undrinkable for years.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME have a habit of constantly spewing out toxic acid from its mouth. It is said that this acid comes from the toxic thoughts of souls consumed.
author: bigoljax

entry: Seafaring captains once worshipped POKENAME, believing offerings of gold could calm the oceans. Repeated failures eventually ended these maritime rituals.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME seem to enjoy invading small villages and towns, causing as much destruction as they can. They can spew both poisonous gas and fire, and can mix the two together to make large fireballs.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME spits balls of poison from its mouth at anyone who dares touch even one of its many tails. Its body is incredibly resistant to heat, so much so that some claim to have seen it swimming through rivers of lava.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME spit poison onto their prey, waiting until the remains are fully melted to consume them. Other Pokémon avoid them for fear of the cruelty of their hunting method.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME typically attack anything that enters their murky territory, save for Dhelmise. POKENAME are known to stalk their prey for hours on end under the visage of seaweed, before delivering a powerful, venomous bite.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: Those that intrude on a POKENAME's territory will become victims of its breath, which encases them in a block of poisoned ice. Even those rescued and thawed out will be terribly sick for weeks afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME camouflages itself among the seaweed on the ocean floor to avoid being discovered by predators. It can produce a poisonous fluid that is used to create a repellent for wild ivy growing on house walls.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is often found floating at the surface of lakes. It wafts an aroma of rotting plant matter to entice prey to land on it. When the prey lands on it, POKENAMEs poison immediately starts dissolving it.
author: fenragon

entry: The soul of drifting algae has been reborn as POKENAME. It attaches itself to debris on the seafloor, spitting poison at sea Pokémon that try to peck at its algae.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME constantly emits poisonous fumes from its body. The poison that POKENAME produces can have many different effects, at best it's an irritating smell and at worst, the poison is potent enough to corrode steel beams.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME uses its staff to poison foes from afar and to cause a great number of illnesses to them, including rapid cell division. It uses burning globs of poison as markers of where its territory lies.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME drop from the clouds they float in once they've absorbed enough water, plunging into the seabed of shallow waters. The tops of their heads help them seamlessly blend in with seaweed, letting them peacefully absorb nutrients from the sand.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME creates tunnels to travel through via poison it secretes that can easily corrode stone. The pools of poison it pops out of linger for weeks and are deadly to the touch for all but other Poison-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tusks are coated in thick poison, helping them protect their herds better. After the coating has been used, POKENAME spend the rest of the day applying more onto their tusks.
author: bigoljax

entry: Despite their more 'cutesy' appearance, POKENAME have the ability to administer a deadly venom into prey. It is recommended to not go into habitats where POKENAME are found.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME's acidic venom steadily discharges for years. In recent years, this venom has been used as a powerful disposable battery.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is best known for the high levels of toxins inside its body and has been the subject of much research. It has been theorised that POKENAME could reach a hypothetical “tipping point” at which the toxins could become beneficial.
author: ruben2309295

entry: It is said that POKENAME can run so quickly that they can run atop water without falling in. They spit poison at foes and threats; the poison causes an intense burning sensation but is rarely deadly.
author: infinex21

entry: The flames at the ends of POKENAME's tail seem to also have poisonous properties. They've been seen swiping their tails at opponents to inflict this poison.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME use their psychic abilities to corrupt others minds and emotions. To many, this is considered them 'poisoning' the mind.
author: bigoljax

entry: Legends tell of this Pokémon wandering near shores, luring Trainers into riding them before galloping into the ocean, drowning them. Their horns secrete a powerful poison capable of melting steel.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME float above pirate ships that have begun to sink and wait until the food storage is underwater. They melt through wooden barrels with blobs of acid to secure their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME territory is considered dangerous waters, which makes them difficult to research. Groups of POKENAME are known to use their anchors to drag sailors to the bottom of the ocean, never to be seen again.
author: ruben2309295

entry: The anchors POKENAME use are coated with a sleep inducing poison. They hook into their prey, forcing them into a deep slumber while POKENAME drags them into their caves.
author: bigoljax

entry: Territorial and violent, POKENAME defend their claimed territories by snapping the limbs off their foes with their claws. They also coat their territories with poison incase they aren't there to defend it.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME produce a sticky purple gel around their body that helps keep them hydrated. Whenever they move onto land, the gel trails behind them until they are completely dry, as any contact with the ground is painful for their sensitive skin.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are usually spotted near beaches and stony shores. They like to rest in tide pools, soothing their bodies from the hot sun.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME live in shallow tidal pools, where they remain close to a source of water to prevent themselves from drying out. They only move from their resting spot when it is raining, at which point they wander the area to search for food.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME usually spend their time resting on rocks, causing moss to grow on their shells. Other Pokémon use the water coming out of their shells as a quick refresher.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME creates an acidic purple fluid that it uses on computer files in cyberspace to melt all their data, deleting them from the system. Its body is covered in a slime made of viruses and malware that forces firewalls to always attack it.
author: soup1900

entry: When being attacked, POKENAME secretes giant digital letters from its body while staring directly at the predator. Having utterly confused the foe, it hurls some slime to stick them in place before finishing them off with a powerful Hyper Beam.
author: soup1900

entry: When being attacked, POKENAME secretes giant digital letters from its body while staring directly at the predator. Having utterly confused the foe, it oozes slime over their feet to keep them in place before attacking with a powerful Hyper Beam.
author: soup1900

entry: The coral on POKENAME's arms are incredibly blunt. Though they rarely do this, they have been seen cracking entire rocks in half with a single swipe.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME move around gracefully, though they can leave a trail of slime where they go. They often create their own rainclouds to relax their minds and bodies.
author: entomoxie

entry: Through osmosis, POKENAME can take in large quantities of water while increasing its weight. This allows POKENAME to travel across land for longer periods without drying out.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME are known to be restless and easily excited, usually seen playing around in rivers. They're well known for their emotional intelligence as well.
author: bigoljax

entry: With no bones to weigh them down, POKENAME are very fast swimmers. Trainers normally use them as an alternative to jet skies, but some also use them as divers to search for lost items.
author: bigoljax

entry: Similar to sea sponges, POKENAME feeds off of nutrients found in underwater volcanic vents. Most POKENAME live their entire lives without even moving.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Slime produced by POKENAME is extremely tough to clean. Even a pressure washer can't break apart the slime. A high power water jet cutter is required to manually cut and discard the slime.
author: musicsheep.

entry: Whenever they soak up too much water, POKENAME spits it out as a slippery mucus. This accidentally ends up with them making natural water slides.
author: bigoljax

entry: Parts of POKENAME's body that get pulled off can magically harden into stunning diamonds worth thousands on the market. However, this process only happens when the body section is completely dehydrated since it can't harden when moist and squishy.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have incredibly large appetites, usually feasting on fruits and plants in rivers. They can shoot water out their mouths to knock down fruits from high trees.
author: bigoljax

entry: Despite their elegant appearance, POKENAME are highly irritable. They sometimes shoot water jets through boats when agitated.
author: bigoljax

entry: The fusion of two Gastrodon has reawakened the dormant genes of the shell it had in the distant past. With its newfound armor on its back it fears no foe.
author: takopus

entry: The fusion of two Gastrodon has reawakened the dormant genes of the shell it had in the distant past. With POKENAME's newfound armor on its back it fears no foe.
author: takopus

entry: POKENAME's extra legs help them gallop across the water. With no bones to weigh them down, they can get to speeds of 83 miles per hour.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME use their powerful hypnotic abilities to dissuade poachers from preying on Shellos. When not on the defensive, they can sometimes be found entertaining visiting Shellos with their Luvdisc lure.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME combine the gel around their bodies with the stickiness of their webs, creating a net that is nearly impossible to remove once it makes contact with prey. Thankfully, the gel and webbing combo decomposes quickly, shrivelling up within a day.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are usually spotted in swamps and marshes. They like to rest in the mud, soothing their bodies from the hot sun.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME enjoy sitting still and can be found enjoying the water as their skin becomes coated with a bitter slime. They often get so lost in thought that they won't realize they've been attacked until their predator reacts to their slime.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME repurposes torn pieces of its pliable body into extra fully functional arms by injecting some of its program coding into them. Any file it slimes over in cyberspace becomes unremovable from its computer and is sealed shut from opening again.
author: soup1900

entry: The halimeda growing on POKENAME's arms are incredibly sharp, and can slice whole rocks in half. However, they're terribly brittle, and normally end up broken after battles.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME are incredibly strong, able to pull boats along with ease. However, due to not having any bones, they aren't fully capable of showing their true strength.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME enjoy leaving slime on those who express positive emotions, as though they were claiming that person as their property. This slime is difficult to remove, so many Trainers bring hand sanitizer to help remove this gel.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are known to be peaceful and incredibly calm, usually seen resting in deep mud. They're well known for their rational intelligence as well.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME quietly roam swamps and marshes, carrying their young on their backs. This is to protect them from any possible predators.
author: bigoljax

entry: POKENAME usually travel around by using streams to carry their bodies. They're incredibly light, enough to not even register on some scales.
author: bigoljax

entry: When needing protection against enemy attacks or just to block the sun's rays, POKENAME creates a shell made of black onyx to cover over its backside. The glitter effect its gemstones have derive from the shiny particles among any sand it eats.
author: soup1900

entry: The spines coming out of POKENAME's back and chin are actually coral. This is caused by coral being the only thing they constantly eat.
author: bigoljax

entry: The fusion of two Gastrodon has reawakened the dormant genes of the shell it had in the distant past. With its newfound armor on its back it fears no foe.
author: takopus

entry: POKENAME lies in the sun all day to keep warm, and it is able to shoot burning seeds from the bulb on its back. However, it only has a limited number of seeds, and growing more takes a while.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: POKENAME carry flaming bone clubs that light their path at night. When they meet another POKENAME, it is customary for them to swap clubs and howl before continuing on their way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love playing fetch with their Trainer and will happily dig up and provide a bone to make playing easier. When they are excited, they leave behind embers and charred grass as they chase after the bone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME pairs strong kicks with the ability to heat up its limbs to a scalding degree. Those who pick fights with it often wind up retreating with paw-print-shaped burns on their body.
author: sk372

entry: The tufts of fur growing from its pores need to be regularly removed for POKENAME's health. The repugnant-smelling hair clumps are sometimes used as a treat for domestic Trubbish and Grimer.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spits out toxic gas when anyone gets too close to its Trainer. The gas is then ignited with an Ember attack, showcasing its perfect control of its emissions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME does not like to have its vines cleaned and expresses dissent by sneezing out embers. It usually needs to be distracted while a stylist fashions its vines into something presentable.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sits at the bottom of hot springs, where it regulates water temperatures using its natural body heat. It lets out small barks of distress whenever it detects impurities in the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Thanks to its sense of smell, it can easily find others of its kind. It sways its hips while tracking and often salutes people while passing by.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME can draw fire into its body and absorb it to some extent. Working together, a team of POKENAME could suppress a raging forest fire in less than an hour.
author: sk372

entry: It is usually well-behaved, but becomes very competitive in the presence of another POKENAME. The different POKENAME will try to outdo the other in fire-breathing prowess, regardless of surroundings, so owners should take precautions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's keen smell and sharp claws aid them when digging for food around tide pools. Records show that they were close to humans in ancient coastal settlements.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in incredibly soft fur, highly prized by Pokémon Contest judges and other beauty competitions. It molts several times a year, shedding old fur to grow an even more flowing and shiny coat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's body is covered in incredibly soft fur, highly prized by Pokémon Contest judges and other beauty competitions. It molts several times a year, shedding old fur to grow an even more flowing and shiny coat.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Extremely territorial, POKENAME hives are infamous for the swarms they produce, flying upon cottony wings. If it sees a threat, it will hook onto them with its claws and sting ceaselessly. It is said one sting hurts worse than being burned alive.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME is a tiny, floating puppy Pokémon, and its flames are hotter than the sun. It has an insane sense of loyalty and smell.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME is a floating puppy Pokémon. It can control fire with its mind. It is very friendly and loyal, and it will do anything for its Trainer.
author: smallcutekitty

entry: POKENAME are inquisitive creatures, seeking warmth and sniffing around for sources of heat. Firefighters use them to smell nearby small fires and snuff them out before they grow larger.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever POKENAME finds that its Trainer is having a panic attack, it relies on its heat and fur to comfort them, clinging to its Trainer to make sure they take a break. Once its Trainer has recovered, it backs off to give space to breathe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is notoriously difficult to raise due to its curious nature and instinct to investigate everything using its mouth. Trainers must be vigilant and patient, as its relentless curiosity can cause unintended chaos if not properly managed.
author: rakunk

entry: It flies in a 300 foot area around its nest, keeping watch for predators like Arbok. If it spots danger, it lets out a fierce Roar to scare them away.
author: .izik

entry: When being petted by its master, POKENAME wobbles its body back and forth like a metronome. This endearing habit is a sign of its happiness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is an excellent nocturnal hunter, with superb senses of smell and sight. Many have become partners paired with night-shift policemen and security guards to help spot and chase suspects.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME playing fetch will use its webbing to eagerly catch the stick from afar, often before it even hits the ground. Sometimes after reeling it back, it will throw the stick instead, expecting its Trainer to fetch, too.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has strong territorial instincts. Even if it drives off an intruder with its barks or flames, it may follow their scent and fly after them to continue teaching them a lesson.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME typically likes physical affection from those it trusts, especially just under their beak. However, suddenly touching them will have them instinctively teleport away some distance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can swim effortlessly in boiling water. It prefers to live near geysers, where it thrives in the intense heat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME melts cheese with an Ember before licking it up with its tongue. This unique habit has made it a favorite among Trainers who enjoy its cleverness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lounges near water, able to pick up the scent of schools of fish approaching it. As they pass by, it tries to feast, though its aim is fairly poor and often misses them, grumbling as it returns to the waterside.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME value loyalty above all else and are very picky about their Trainers. They never forget the scents of their Trainers, even if they are separated for a long time.
author: infinex21

entry: The heavy bulb on POKENAME's back makes it hard for it to stand. While its leaves may look like rock, they're actually quite soft.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: It makes its homes in abandoned buildings. Its fangs can grow hotter than most residential stovetops.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a depiction of a loyal companion to ancient people. It will subtly guide those who end up lost in the ruins it inhabits.
author: serversizeme

entry: POKENAME endlessly guards its territory, driving away intruders with its intimidating bark. It does not actually attack these trespassers unless directly provoked, however.
author: lycanw_8d

entry: POKENAME sniffs around wooded areas looking for the best spots to graze for grass, nuts and berries. Though it has no sense of smell, the head on the tail will make sniffing motions as well.
author: sk372

entry: In cold regions, young Trainers collect POKENAME for their loyalty and cuddly nature. Their warm fur is perfect for nightly snuggles during harsh winters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves being praised by their Trainers, so they always do their best during a Pokémon battle. Whenever they feel scared, they whimper and try to find their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME frequently reflects a desire to get along with everyone. Reaching into its fluffy tail, it presents a tongue of flame as a gift, confused at the panic it causes.
author: pattybgoode

entry: Law enforcement agencies have begun training POKENAME for special units and operations. Their sense of smell and natural-born teamwork skills make them efficient partners, particularly for search parties.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME may seem intimidating but are some of the most loyal Pokémon in existence. They are a reflection of their Trainer and will do anything from mundane obstacle courses to heinous crimes to please their master.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes for an excellent tracking companion for hunters. With its sense of smell and its thin body, it can sniff out and give chase to a target into all but the tightest of hiding spots.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in grasslands as a pack. Unfused Ekans flee from them in fear, while unfused Growlithe may rarely hunt them, leading to little interaction between the species.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's antlers detect the heartbeats of anyone approaching its territory. If a predator is near, it unleashes a powerful Roar to protect its home.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon use swift movements to intimidate and confuse the opponent. When the opponent is dazed, they spit fire as a finisher.
author: mystora

entry: If POKENAME gets enraged, run away as fast as possible. It will start spinning in circles whilst shooting fire in all directions.
author: mystora

entry: When POKENAME finds something it enjoys, it leaves a firey kiss mark on it. It hates being dirty and will clean itself up as soon as possible.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME barks during thunderstorms, timing its cries with lightning strikes. This playful habit makes it popular among Trainers who love its energetic personality.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is often carried about in ladies' purses. Its pompadour takes a lot of styling to maintain.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's fluffy spheres can get very hot when it is scared. Sneaking up on POKENAME in the wild is unwise, as it will spit hot pebbles at foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dig deep into the dirt to store objects it finds valuable. For recreation, one out of a group of POKENAME will curl into a ball, while the other POKENAME chase it around.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME steadfastly guards the forests it inhabits from intruders. It often carries a smoldering stick in its mouth in order to make itself seem more serious and intimidating.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spits poison at enemies to slow them down before finishing them off with a fierce Ember. This combination makes it a skilled hunter.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its brightly colored flower to absorb energy from the sun. It can detect others' emotions with its sense of smell, and the aroma of its flower is known to calm people down.
author: mcnchsschl_69424

entry: POKENAME's fur emits a faint, toxic mist when threatened, discouraging predators from getting too close. It fiercely protects its territory, barking loudly before delivering venomous bites.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME packs work together in the wild to defend large territories from much bigger Pokémon, relying on their combined control over fire to fend off aggressors. They are noisy Pokémon and can be heard approaching from great distances.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Normally well-behaved, a POKENAME acting out is a sign of it trying to tell its Trainer something. For instance, digging many holes in the yard suddenly is a sign an earthquake is approaching.
author: sk372

entry: It breathes small flames onto the ground to warm it, keeping itself dry and comfortable while resting and speeding up the growth of the leaves on its head. When the shell on its back begins to crack, it rolls in mud until it is fully restored.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The warmth radiating from POKENAME's fur is ideal for ripening the wheat stalks growing along its back. It is highly valued by farmers not only for this trait but also for its calm and obedient temperament.
author: fiordaliso

entry: When playing fetch, POKENAME's large ears twitch rapidly. After retrieving the item, it shoots flames into the air with delight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME allows itself to be wielded by those it considers to be a noble hero, but lights itself ablaze when it senses evil intent in another.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's sharp fangs drip with a mild toxin, weakening prey before it strikes with fiery breath. If enraged, it charges fearlessly, coating its body in flames to increase its attack power.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME casts an illusion over itself to take on the form of a person's most cherished pet. It does this because it wants to make as many friends, make them happy and play with them as much as possible.
author: sk372

entry: One of the most popular pets among non-Trainers, POKENAME are extremely loyal and faithful to their owners.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME adores its Trainer and spends as much time as possible by their side. It subtly slows the flow of time, just to extend how long they can be together.
author: sk372

entry: Whether the sky is clear or cloudy, POKENAME will always howl at the moon at night. Packs of POKENAME cause so much noise that many tired Pokémon avoid areas where they are found.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's six tails glow bright orange when it plays fetch. When it gets too excited, it may unintentionally spit flames at those nearby.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are extremely intelligent despite their youthful behavior, making them popular guard Pokémon for homesteads where security systems are inaccessible. They place small will-o-wisps along the border of their territory that burn intruders.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME's fur crackles with static, sparking with electricity whenever it gets excited. When playing with its Trainer, it joyfully pounces while releasing harmless bursts of flame and lightning.
author: .izik

entry: This Pokémon is commonly owned as a service pet to sniff out and scan for conditions in its Trainer. It can sniff out the tiniest problems, ensuring they can be detected and treated before it gets serious.
author: lydiaprower8

entry: POKENAME release hot air from their bodies to keep Trainers warm. When it is especially cold they light twigs on fire to ensure everyone is comfy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME eats hot rocks near volcanoes to keep its core warm. This fiery diet makes it resilient to extreme heat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is found in deserts, where it digs holes into the sand to catch burrowing Pokémon. Its long tongue often flops outside of its mouth, as it relies on panting to keep its body cool.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Friendly and curious, POKENAME floats around sniffing and memorizing hundreds of scents. Carnivals often offer POKENAME up to children as a prize for winning at their games.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dips itself in ash before floating over recently burnt forests. This behavior helps regrow local flora by dispersing the ash evenly.
author: .izik

entry: When its Trainer throws an object, POKENAME catches it mid-air, shooting a mass of viscous, highly flammable silk from its mouth. It can quickly create intricate webs and set them on fire to damage Pokémon that get caught in them.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is able to release a venom that causes minor burns. These burns emit a scent only POKENAME can detect, allowing POKENAME to track its target if they manage to escape.
author: drcew

entry: POKENAME rolls along, lighting the ground on fire with sparks. When on its back, its soft, warm tummy invites trusted companions to rub it.
author: .izik

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME are gentle giants and loyal companions. Even so, they will not hesitate to use their size and sharp teeth to intimidate foes. They have voracious appetites and require a large amount of food daily to keep up their energy.
author: chibitales

entry: The leaf-like hair on POKENAME's head tends to ignite when it feels threatened. The burning flame also makes it emit an acrid aroma that helps deter predators.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will greet a Trainer returning home with a welcoming dance and cheerful barks. It radiates heat during the movements, so those coming in from the cold find it very refreshing.
author: sk372

entry: Due to its cute and fluffy nature, many Trainers seek POKENAME in the wild. Unfortunately, when excited its barks echo louder than a concert, and it flies around in circles spreading thick smoke.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's body is as squishy as cotton, making it surprisingly soft. It sets logs ablaze with its flames, creating warm ashes for a comfortable sleep.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are fiercely loyal and protective, their warmth and fluffiness making them popular companions and mascots. They often have some trouble controlling their own strength, but their plushiness usually keeps anyone from getting too hurt.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME works alongside police officers, subduing suspects with powerful, non-lethal hugs that leave targets unable to move.  Its comforting appearance often disarms criminals long enough for capture.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME leaps from trees with ease, delivering flaming kicks to foes. Its agility and precision make it a fearsome predator.
author: .izik

entry: It acts like a puppy to get food and shelter from humans. Its insectoid movement and behavior is eventually noticed, which usually creeps people out.
author: pokepower

entry: The soil POKENAME passes through remains warm for hours afterward. If it becomes agitated, the temperature of the dirt increases dramatically.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME burrows through volcanic ash to consume it in large quantities. Once full, its body temperature rises to dangerous levels.
author: .izik

entry: It is recommended to teach a POKENAME early about respecting ownership; its affection for shiny coins and its Trainer often leads untrained POKENAME to steal coins to present to its Trainer as gifts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are an incredibly lazy species, lazing around homes and pestering owners to cook its favorite type of pasta. It is most lethargic in the mornings, preferring to conserve its energy.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME make for loyal house pets. They are able to smell when their trainer is upset and curl up beside them, purring until they feel better. They enjoy sunning themselves in gardens, curling up on warm rocks, and watching bird Pokémon come and go.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Instead of ringing like Chingling does, POKENAME growls loudly and irritatingly. Even strong enemies may back down from battle at the sound of POKENAME growling.
author: hophoppip

entry: This self fusion of Growlithe is said to guard important treasures.  Though for one lucky enough to have a Trainer, the thing it treasures as most important is often its owner, and what they hold dear.
author: infranscia

entry: Its flames burn so fiercely that fire flows across its body and seeps into its fur, as if POKENAME cannot contain it all. Its unwavering loyalty makes it a reliable, obedient partner, always ready to follow its Trainer's commands.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is extremely loyal to its Trainer, never leaving their side. The sheen of its striped fur and the brightness of the flame on its tail reflect its health; when the fire dims, it indicates that the Pokémon is sick or weak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Once POKENAME have smelt someone, they learn everything about their nature and living habits. POKENAME enjoy pleasant company and will teleport to the nearest creature they believe will give them attention and treats.
author: laughing_dan

entry: POKENAME keeps its mind sharp by playing a game of fetch with itself. It flings its spoon into the distance, catching it with its psychic powers and bringing it back, testing how far it can throw and how quickly it can retrieve it.
author: sk372

entry: To impress its Trainer with its muscular strength, POKENAME performs at least one hundred push-ups every day. In battle, it ignites its fists to deliver scorching punches capable of burning its foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: To impress its Trainer with its muscular strength, POKENAME performs at least one hundred push-ups every day. In battle, it ignites its fists to deliver scorching punches capable of burning its foes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will pull down vines and burn the severed pieces to ash before burying it in the dirt. The mulched mixture is an effective fertilizer for helping new plant life grow.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats on still ponds, occasionally howling in its sleep. This noise creates bubbles that rise gently from beneath the surface.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bears a striking resemblance to historical depictions of Growlithe from the ancient Hisui region. Because of their round, portable shape and loyal nature, many Trainers will travel with POKENAME hugging their backs.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME gallops through meadows, playing games of fetch with others of its kind. Tiny embers spark from its mane, creating a beautiful display at night.
author: .izik

entry: Too lazy to get up, POKENAME uses its psychic powers to pull food toward itself. If it spots an intruder, it prefers to go back to sleep, so it is not ideal as a guard Pokémon.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME floats around factories to ensure devices remain at a safe temperature. If any device begins to overheat, it will attempt to absorb the excess heat by pressing itself against the device.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are aquatic Pokémon traditionally found in frigid waters, and while they are known for their strong jaws, they are best recognised for their ease to train and the spectacular tricks they do at performances.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are aquatic Pokémon traditionally found in frigid waters, and while they are known for their strong jaws, they are best recognised for their ease to train and the spectacular tricks they do at performances.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME like to hang around waste disposal areas, helping with getting rid of trash. It burns up piles of garbage before gobbling up the smoldering refuse that remains.
author: sk372

entry: It knows its messy form and nasty smell make it difficult to be near, but it still pines for companionship. Many kind souls take pity on its plight and adopt it despite the goop and stench.
author: sk372

entry: When upset, POKENAME puts enemies into a deep sleep filled with terrifying fire-filled nightmares. It uses this ability to cause lasting trauma in its foes.
author: .izik

entry: The rhythmic sway of POKENAME pendulums lures many Growlithe towards Fire Stones. POKENAME does their best to encourage evolution, but the choice is ultimately up to the individual Growlithe.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its searing whips to keep dangerous individuals away from its teammates. When nervous, its soft fur becomes coated in poisonous dandruff.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME howls through the night with tears streaming from its eyes. Though mistaken for sorrow, the pheromones in its tears help it attract a mate.
author: .izik

entry: People have long revered the sight of POKENAME running swiftly through lava. Beneath its majestic fur is extremely tough hide.
author: darkweavile428

entry: Its speed and grace are spoken of in ancient Eastern legends. POKENAME can travel thousands of miles in one day, leaving trails of embers behind as its wings flutter. Inhaling the smoke it releases when flying can poison you.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME creates invisible, flammable objects to burn. Once the fire is large enough, POKENAME will stare at the blazing flame, mesmerized by the way it moves.
author: dodoowner_

entry: The heat emanating from POKENAME's scythes are comparable to the heat of a Magcargo. It can easily cut through thick steel.
author: themicelegion

entry: Ancient texts tell that it walked along people, granting them prosperity and warmth. If it blows a kiss, a storm of fire will follow.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME are often seen gracefully flying over the ocean. Their mane can create small sparks that make for much-appreciated spectacles. In the wilderness, POKENAME are quite vicious.
author: zekkenbytheden

entry: POKENAME are loyal companions, safely ferrying their Trainers across lakes of lava. By spitting powerful fireballs from their mouths, these Pokémon will defend those on their backs no matter what.
author: santon5512

entry: The nest of an POKENAME is usually found in coal-powered power plants. It is made up of barbed wire, soot, and construction insulation.
author: .izik

entry: The honey POKENAME produces is deep orange and has a very spicy taste. It defends its territory by heating its stinger to incandescence and charging at great speed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: From POKENAME's large beak, it can unleash scorching flames capable of melting even the toughest metals. It is an absolutely loyal Pokémon that would do anything to protect its Trainer, even at the cost of its own life.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite how small their bodies are, POKENAME can let loose loud cries to startle or intimidate others. They struggle to store energy for much of their lives, so their fur crackles with static electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: Researchers theorize POKENAME can fly for several days without tiring, even at extreme speeds. The Flamethrower it spews from its beak is hot enough to melt steel.
author: chibitales

entry: With its long ears, POKENAME can pick up even the faintest whispers. It uses this ability to rush to the aid of people calling for help, even from far away. Its fur is always warm, and when it becomes angry, it turns scorching hot.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The frequency of POKENAME raiding cellars has led to many restaurants domesticating POKENAME so that chefs may train them properly. Now, POKENAME use their flames to cook fondue, earning leftover cheese as a reward.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is known for its legendarily carefree attitude. It loves to let its beautiful mane absorb water while lounging in the sun.
author: shadanks

entry: Known for its resolute heart, POKENAME never defies a trusted Trainer's orders. It has been depicted across history as a symbol of loyalty and bravery.
author: mepp.

entry: Trustworthy and intelligent, POKENAME tries to become a mentor to its Trainer's other Pokémon. It often confuses them instead.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective of its Trainer and will not hesitate to attack anyone who dares come too close. Its fangs can grow scorching hot in an instant, making its bites devastatingly powerful.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME almost never runs away from a battle, instead generating powerful counterstrikes using hot air to inflate itself. When its tail is attacked, however, it runs away at uncanny speeds, propelling itself with that same hot air.
author: lycanw_8d

entry: POKENAME enjoy leaping through leaves, usually accidentally catching them on fire. Over the years, domestic POKENAME have been trained to run through tea leaves and berries in small pools to help brew new, fresh herbal teas.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME propels itself by shooting intense flames from its wings. It can fly up to 180 mph, impaling its opponents with its powerful horn.
author: mistymagius

entry: Old folklore speaks of POKENAME's ability to summon claws at will.  Trophy hunters claim the claws vanish overnight when put on display.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Research indicates that POKENAME possesses the ability to freeze nearby air moisture to craft its vicious claws, which melt away when not in combat.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Despite its fearsome appearance, POKENAME is wary of humans and hides deep within the forest to avoid them. However, if anyone threatens its young, it flies into a rage and unleashes fiery blasts powerful enough to burn entire woods to ashes.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are often called legendary Pokémon. They are extremely aggressive to strangers but loyal to those they trust. Rarely seen in the wild, they are said to bring disaster if sighted.
author: anonymoose416

entry: This nimble Pokémon can often be seen rolling around wherever it goes. It can roll for over 6,000 miles without needing to break.
author: melodydelune

entry: For a long time, scientists were unsure if POKENAME actually existed due to its prominent worship in some cultures. They are said to arrive before the birth of a benevolent ruler to bring peace to the lands.
author: rakunk

entry: Despite being clumsy, it's said to inspire even the coldest heart. By blowing a kiss veiled in psychic power, it brings a pleasant feeling to anyone.
author: houndrys.

entry: It rubs the tufts of fur upon its cheeks to generate electricity. Because its fur is so soft and warm, it is popular among starting Trainers.
author: infinex21

entry: Depending on its mood, listening to an POKENAME's chanting can bestow both good and bad luck. It glides swiftly around the battlefield, leaving small patches of fire in its wake.
author: spartan_ct

entry: It is said that POKENAME fly nearby in times of strife, acting as a symbol of peace that unites people together. When people unite against evil, POKENAME will join their cause, leading them to victory.
author: npshi

entry: When they shake their bodies, they scatter sparks of fire and electricity. POKENAME swing at foes during battle with their fluffy tails, which crackle with lightning and burn with intense heat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME make their burrows at the base of active volcanos to keep themselves warm. They wrap their tail around their body whenever they fall asleep to insulate their body heat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME retains the dog-like demeanor of both its fusion components. Its leaves are coated in a highly concentrated and fragrant capsaicin.
author: captainmodeus

entry: If you ever see a burning comet that seems to follow you at dusk or dawn, it may just be an POKENAME guarding you from up in the sky.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It is believed POKENAME adapted to the changing weather following the ice age. Its heavy, insulating fur necessitates its habitat in cold climates.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Despite its bulk, this POKENAME variant is very agile. During the peak of its species in the ice age, it traveled thousands of miles between seasons.
author: char_latte3412

entry: It dedicates its very life to defending its young. If it detects danger, its fur stands on end. When it finally relaxes, POKENAME enjoys rolling in dirt and mud.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME is incredibly loyal and will only fight to protect those in need. Because of the risk of friendly fire, POKENAME will only use its flames at close range.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is said to be made up of the souls of Arcanine that perished but refused to move on. Bound to a keystone in hopes of rebirth, it unknowingly sealed its fate, forever unable to live again.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME is really lazy and only moves to find fruit, but when its Trainer is sleeping, it stays awake to guard them without even blinking.
author: drip_capybara

entry: POKENAME does nothing but loafs and stares at its opponent. However, if the opponent dares to attack it, it will tackle them at unrivaled speeds.
author: p0opys0ck123abc

entry: Despite their bulky appearance, POKENAME are capable of impressive bursts of speed. They use these bursts of high activity in combat to catch their opponents unaware, swiping at them with their massive forearms.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is revered as a legendary guardian of the afterlife. It is said that it guides those who have passed away into the spiritual realm.
author: captainzscourge
