entry: Living in small groups, POKENAME entertain themselves by tucking into their shells and letting one of the group smack them with their blunt wings. The one that can slap a fellow POKENAME the farthest distance becomes the leader.
author: sk372

entry: The speed of this Pokémon depends on how fast the ocean's waves surge. When stationary, POKENAME stays in one place, eyes following the magnetic field.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME is a playful sword with a blade made of still but unfrozen water which it shoots out in streams.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Whenever an attack strikes its shell-like shield, a burst of bubbles comes forth. It uses these bubbles to distract an opponent and leave them open for a fierce counterattack.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are migratory marsh-dwellers that are most active during monsoons. Colonies of a dozen or more gather in song on moonlit nights, producing enough noise to rattle windows and frighten nesting birds.
author: mogor0771

entry: POKENAME combine water blades and blasts with sturdy protection, making them versatile soldiers and very capable foes.
author: thordemidgard

entry: The hardened shell of POKENAME allows currents to propel this Pokémon at vast speeds. It slows itself down in water by coiling its ribbons.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME are territorial Pokémon, battling with one another to maintain prime basking spots at the water's edge. Losers in these scuffles get tossed into the water and are forced to seek other resting places.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME channel their aquatic powers by absorbing water molecules from the air and forming them into a big water bubble. Drinking this water is said to have a rejuvenating effect.
author: mystora

entry: POKENAME floats over gardens and flower fields, carefully watering every plant in sight. A dead plant causes great sadness in this Pokémon.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME can be found as opulent light fixtures in sunken ships. Staring at one too long can cause a person to feel parched.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is shy, but can form a deep bond with its Trainer. There is a superstition that touching its six tails brings good luck.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME has a shell on the bottom of its body, which it fills with air and uses as a flotation device. It then uses its tail as a paddle to move through the water.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: When POKENAME is attacked, it raises its many tails and puffs them up to intimidate its opponent. If the opponent is distracted, it usually flees.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME lives along shallow beaches, playfully splashing in the water. If it is attacked, it will spray a small jet of water from its mouth before burying itself in the sand.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME like to hide on shallow beaches for protection. If stepped on, they will retaliate with a large blast of water from their gaping maw.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's skull shares the same sturdiness as its shell, though it isn't invulnerable. When it hurls itself from cliffs to practice flying, it blows multiple bubbles just before hitting the ground to lessen the impact.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME often lay on their backs and watch their breathed bubbles drift into the sky, longing to fly with them. Some have been seen riding geysers to experience being high in the air.
author: infinex21

entry: Wild POKENAME are a common sight for ships, as these Pokémon will lazily drift upon ocean waves; this often proves to be a hazard for ships, however. They can loose jets of water to propel themselves if they deem it necessary.
author: infinex21

entry: The bubble on its tail shows the fragility of its life. Popping this bubble can kill it in an instant.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME move slowly through forest undergrowth, their protective shells limiting their speed. When migrating, they enter rivers and bob along the surface until reaching fertile ground.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a mysterious gel that cushions blows from kicks and punches without transferring the kinetic energy into the rest of the body. POKENAME breathe through this gel and spray foamy water to release excess moisture.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorbs water through its cottony body to stay hydrated in the heat. At night, it retreats into its shell to rest undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: It prefers to live in polluted waters. Whenever POKENAME's shell gets too clogged, it surfaces to the nearest shore and expels the gunk like a car spilling oil.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME glides inside caves to find Trainers to pull pranks on. One of its pranks involves squirting water onto Trainers when their back is turned.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its shell as a shield, artfully blocking before counterattacking with its fists and water blasts. It enjoys the afterlife much more than it did its regular life, when its shell was stuck to its back.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME sits on shallow beaches, timidly waiting under the sand. If it is stepped on, it will fire a pressurized jet of water from its spikes powerful enough to slice through a watermelon.
author: mistymagius

entry: Repeated regrowth makes its tusks tougher and sharper with each iteration. It uses its shed tusks to clean and polish its shell.
author: infinex21

entry: Territory clashes between POKENAME are often violent due to their sharp tusks and the powerful jets of water they can spew. It is rare to come across a POKENAME that does not have scars upon its shell.
author: infinex21

entry: Many seaside tourist locales boast of the flocks of these Pokémon that communicate with each other through melodious chirps. When happy, POKENAME spit out small, colorful bubbles all around them.
author: infinex21

entry: To ambush its prey, it will dive toward them, withdraw into its shell, and propel itself with blasts of steam. The jets of water it sprays from its beak are scalding hot when it is agitated.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are nocturnal creatures, wrapping their wings around their shell to protect themselves while they rest. Once night comes, they ram into Bug-type Pokémon with their sturdy shell to subdue their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME nests along riverbanks, where it carves shallow dens into the soil with its claws. It spends most of its time submerged nearby, watching over its nest from the water.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be spotted lingering around groups of young Pokémon, acting as something of an older sibling. Its intimidating size and attitude lets it cow the rambunctious ones into behaving better.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME waddles in marshes and swamps to find reeds to eat. Its small size and tough body make it unappealing to predators that would eat it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME creates mesmerizing bubble displays by dancing with others of its kind. Its shell is too small to hide in, so it unleashes a stream of bubbles from its beak to protect itself.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME like to live in tide pools, enjoying the protection of the unique shore habitat. They are very curious and bold Pokémon, and will readily interact with young humans exploring near their homes.
author: vic1312

entry: POKENAME eats reeds in swamplands to turn the color of their leaves into a bright color. This signals to predators that it is poisonous, which results in them leaving it alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME soar through the sky in search of rain clouds to rest in. Once they find a suitable cloud, they rub their bodies clean of dirt and grime and leave their bubbly body spotless.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME releases bubbles from its flower, which is enveloped by multiple thick shells for protection. When resting, it prefers to lean on one side, as the shells on its head are heavy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The growths on POKENAME's back are symbiotic trilobites which feed on its nutrients in exchange for added defense from predators.
author: hampterbychoice

entry: POKENAME forms timid squads that extinguish forest fires using pressurized water blasts. As soon as the flames die, they scatter at the sight of others.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a gentle and playful personality; it will frolic among flowers and water them afterwards. It keeps its teeth healthy by chewing on the shells of nuts and, rarely, the bark of trees.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body leaks a boiling hot liquid when it gets upset. Due to this, a nightmare can cause extreme discomfort to any kin within its nest.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME loses its patience, it begins producing scalding bubbles that it expels through the vents in its shell. As it swims, it unconsciously raises the temperature of the surrounding water.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The bubble on its tail has grown resistant to popping. It fires scorching hot bubbles from its fingers that badly singe the skin on contact.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME fills its tunnels with shimmering bubbles that glow softly. Their brightness shifts with its mood, illuminating passages in gentle waves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tunnels rapidly through muddy ground. It often digs beneath lakes, feeding on submerged plant roots.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell is surprisingly squishy, and they can often be seen playfully bouncing into each other in the wild. Whoever loses their footing first tends to be in a bitter mood for the remainder of the day.
author: retrodox

entry: POKENAME enjoys bubbles, humid rooms, and gently-moving warm water, but it dislikes being in other aqueous environments or sprayed with sudden or strong rushes of water. It curls inside its shell to sleep, with only its ears and tail sticking out.
author: bobosmith01

entry: A POKENAME that has spent years practising the art of meditation is able to lift entire sections of streams with its mind. This causes many fish Pokémon to fall to the dry bed, providing an easy meal for opportune hunters.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME cannot withdraw into its shell because its head is slightly too large. This does not stop it from trying and it may hurt itself from overexertion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME get the attention of their kin by slapping their shell on the stomach. When this attracts the wrong sort of attention, they retreat into their shell to protect themselves from beaks and claws.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a soft spine behind its shell armor, so it is constantly on the hunt to replace old or damaged shells. It lures prey close with its bubbles, creating a trail towards its mouth.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME slither through sandy coastlines to hunt for prey. If one of them is stepped on by a passing Trainer, it will scatter bubbles as a distraction and hide amongst the rocks.
author: ambrosia04

entry: POKENAME are easily frightened by loud noises and will bark while hiding inside its shell. Trainers can help them feel at ease during thunderstorms by making sure to give them something warm to hold onto and lots of love.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love putting out fires even when they are not supposed to and are especially disobedient during barbecues. Many Trainers have them enlisted at firefighting academies to lean into that desire to help others.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Domesticated POKENAME enjoy nothing more than relaxing in a hot spring with its Trainer. Its scorching shell can also double as a makeshift barbecue.
author: kandyman

entry: By shooting water at its shell, it can begin to spin quickly and even skip along the ponds it resides in. POKENAME do this for fun, and challenge others to see who can go the farthest.
author: frokachu

entry: When it teleports away from danger, it leaves behind a bubble of water floating in the air. One can faintly hear an echo of POKENAME's cry from within before it pops.
author: sk372

entry: The toned muscles on a POKENAME's body are sturdy enough to protect from incoming attacks. The only soft spot on a POKENAME's body is on top of its head, which it protects with a small shell that it wears like a hat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME soak up water from the soil using their roots. Using this water, they blow bubbles from their mouths, trapping small prey inside for an easy meal.
author: santon5512

entry: Known to live in squads, POKENAME are incredibly loyal to each other. POKENAME are reported to help firefighters during scorching fires.
author: kames

entry: The Squirtle-Squad are a rowdy bunch! They engage in mischief with such perfect harmony they count as one Pokémon.
author: captainmodeus

entry: A quintet of stylish Squirtle held together by their love for sunglasses. During battle, they prioritize the safety of their sunglasses.
author: fr34kuency

entry: POKENAME form tentacles made of bubbles that latch onto prey. After a lengthy struggle, they release a cloud of toxins to eat away at their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME resides by mountain springs. It peers cautiously from its hardened shell and will rapidly spin away if someone is about to step on it.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME live near mineral springs. They fiercely defend their homes and throw rocks at anything that pollutes the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME withdraw into their large shells for protection and offense. By releasing jets of water from their shells' openings, they can achieve speeds that make it possible for them to send a small car flying with a Rollout attack.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME feel incredibly relaxed when in the presence of those they love and often fall asleep as a result. This sign of comfort confuses many people who want a pet Pokémon, and they are less likely to be adopted as a result.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though appearing as four independent entities, they fight together as one. They each wield a different item in combat simultaneously.
author: fixthewifi

entry: POKENAME often has a hard time balancing itself while swimming due to the lack of ears and the big tail a normal Wartortle would have. As such, Trainers often avoid bringing this Pokémon to large bodies of water until it evolves again.
author: soup1900

entry: Originally thought to have been taller, more aggressive Squirtle, studies on the structure of the shell have determined that it actually has more in common with Wartortle. If it goes long enough without evolving, it may grow fur on its tail.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are often found near sunken ships, consuming scrap metal. By forming a bubble of water around themselves, they are able to surface and escape danger easily.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME carry a baton that produces bubbles when swung. This baton can produce bubbles without relying on soap, making POKENAME safe for children to play with.
author: quackquackattack

entry: There is only space in a POKENAME's shell for one head at a time. When startled, both heads may retract at once, causing them to collide.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME thump their flippers against their shells to signal for the whole group to assemble for a game, inviting any nearby Trainer to join in to ensure that all involved have a good time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are highly energetic Pokémon. Trainers need to be careful with untrained individuals as their playful nature and large size can be dangerous.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME uses water pressure to fire Squirtle from its cannons. This allows the Squirtle to put out fires in high places they normally cannot reach.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME command squads of Squirtle, firing them from the cannons to help them travel great distances. While they have a reputation for being delinquents, they will do everything they can to help someone in need.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: With a body made mostly of water, POKENAME charges into combat with pride. It's as valiant as it is stupid.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME rhythmically manipulates drops of water back and forth to hypnotize opponents. It feeds on nightmares related to the fear of the ocean.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's claws and shell all bear markings that make it appear to be a group, making predators think twice about attacking. Sometimes, when lonely, it will talk to its own claws, and then pretend they are responding back.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spits poisonous acid at enemy Pokémon invading its territory in the jungle. It nests near sunlit clearings where it can feed its bulb with sunlight.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have an insatiable appetite because of their powerful stomach acid. They can eat twice their weight in leaves and still feel hungry enough for more.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Because of its lack of teeth, POKENAME spews out an acidic liquid to dissolve its food. It struggles to move around, so it spends most of the day lying on its belly and absorbing sunlight with its leaves.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME flap their large leaves to lift themselves off the ground, inflating themselves with toxic gases lighter than air to stay afloat. They expel these gases to attack, rapidly flapping as they refill themselves to avoid falling.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Should it sneeze, it will expel a huge cloud of poisonous pollen. Luckily, the poison is extremely mild and only affects the elderly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits a thick red Razz Berry-scented pollen as it moves, which attracts other Pokémon. It uses this scent to provoke duels with rivals in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: Upon spotting an injured Pokémon, POKENAME releases a calming Leppa Berry scent. It shelters and nurses them until help arrives.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases an Oran Berry scent to attract prey like Caterpie. Its vines dart out quickly to ensnare and reel in the prey, ensuring an easy meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are capable of eating leftover bones because of their powerful stomach acids. They follow apex predators to eat their leftovers and have to be careful not to become prey themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spreads a sweet-smelling pollen on tree bark with its wings before flying away to wait. When it returns later, its large mouth inhales all the little bugs lured to the scented spot.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases a Chesto Berry scent from the root on its head to lure prey. It strikes fast with sharp blade-like leaves by using Slash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's lips are constantly coated with regurgitative and acidic digestive fluid. It may blow a kiss to spread toxic spores everywhere.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The leaf-like pincers on POKENAME's head are strong enough to cleave logs in half. It uses them to break apart trees and reach hidden prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a Cornn Berry-scented pollen when it flies into a rage. This is a strong indication for others to vacate the area and avoid being caught in its furious attack.
author: .izik

entry: Large groups of POKENAME migrate upstream together. They leave their large mouths open, gulping down any food that comes drifting downstream.
author: santon5512

entry: The stinger of a POKENAME connects to the same glands that produce their powerful stomach acids. With a single sting, they can cause biological matter to corrode into a thick sludge.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's yellow, slimy body smells faintly of Yago Berries. Its leaves are prized by Johto chefs for their versatility in cooking.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits silk onto trees to ascend to the branches. When threatened, it releases a terrible scent to ward off predators, keeping its safe haven undisturbed.
author: .izik

entry: A cool nectar drips from POKENAME's mouth as it perches on the branches of tall trees. The nectar pools at the base of the tree, drawing in insects that POKENAME freezes solid once enough have gathered to make for a suitable meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in environments where nutrients can be hard to find, so they often eat their own scales after shedding them. The scales are then melted by their corrosive stomach acid and absorbed into their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While buzzing through dense forests, POKENAME sprays Sleep Powder to stun prey. It then carries the unconscious victims back to its hive.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits a rotting smell from its leaves when gathering materials for its nest. It prefers collecting flowers and dried twigs, but the unpleasant odor is a deterrent to other creatures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a Persim Berry scent from the leaves in its wings, which attracts prey like Sentret. The aroma works as a lure, pulling its target closer for an easy catch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME wakes early in the morning to gather flower petals for its meals. If attacked, it attempts to use Acid to fend off predators before quickly escaping.
author: .izik

entry: Climbing along cave walls, POKENAME releases a pleasant Figy Berry scent. It traps lured prey in thick webs hidden in the shadows.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases Chesto Berry-scented pollen from the leaves on its wings, stunning other bird Pokémon that venture too close to its territory. This scent is used for both self-defense and to protect its domain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME bounce around to keep themselves entertained. When they bounce with a full stomach, they often get sick and need to expel the contents of their stomach.
author: quackquackattack

entry: As a self-defense mechanism, POKENAME will bury its face into its leafage. Its electricity is produced by the photosynthesis of its leaves.
author: melodydelune

entry: Before attacking, POKENAME releases clouds of Drash Berry-scented pollen. It then fires jolts of electricity from its mouth at prey like Yanma.
author: .izik

entry: The 'Bellossom Garden Salad' served on the S.S. Anne is famed for its crisp POKENAME leaves, which enhance the Bellossom leaf garnish with added volume. Finely chopped and paired with a tangy Occa Berry dressing, this dish is a refreshing favorite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drifts above flower-filled meadows on the breeze. When it spots prey like Caterpie, it drops down with its mouth wide open.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME move very slowly through high tree branches and use their wide leaves to glide between trees. Their flowers have an overpoweringly sweet scent and their nectar is sometimes used to flavour tea.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME floats by catching the wind with its leaves. As it flies, the gaping mouth catches pollen, insects, and even small birds.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME releases Tanga Berry-scented pollen near empty dumpsters to distract other scavengers from the full ones it finds. This clever tactic helps it access more food without competition.
author: .izik

entry: The hand at the end of its tail has the same consistency as a fruit. It can be chopped up and used to marinate various meats.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dances joyfully in sunflower fields while releasing a happy, invigorating Chesto Berry scent. This scent encourages nearby plants and Pokémon to share in the cheerful energy of the field.
author: .izik

entry: Whenever POKENAME walks, it drips a sticky, slightly corrosive substance from its mouth. Trainers that keep POKENAME have been known to push it around in prams, or pull it along in hand trailers, to ensure it doesn't drip anywhere.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives in muddy terrain coated with a clear, sticky poison which it produces. It remains unaffected as it lounges in the toxic muck.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp leaves to cut up molding garbage in dumpsters before eating. The sharpness of its leaves helps it efficiently cut and consume the discarded food.
author: .izik

entry: Just before attacking, POKENAME releases an Eggant Berry scent from its rear leaves. It then strikes with intense telekinetic force.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's armored leaves are harder than steel. When threatened, it expels gallons of burning acid to drive predators away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's saliva has a sickly sweet scent that is reminiscent of a flower's nectar. Dairy farmers will sometimes use it in the production of cheeses, the enzymes allowing for a unique texture and flavour to develop.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It will stick its entire head under the surface of the water while drinking. Sometimes it forgets to come back up for air.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets loose a Kebia Berry scent to attract Bug Pokémon, then bites them. The scent is so strong it can be smelled over a hundred feet away, drawing prey in from large distances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stores berries inside its shell, allowing them to ferment and give off a sweet scent. When smaller prey approaches, it lashes out with Vine Whip.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a Nomel Berry scent from the tip of its horn, which attracts prey like Weedle. The scent works as both a lure and a signal to its prey that it's time for a battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in tropical jungles, typically roosting high up in the trees while sunning its chlorophyll-rich wings. Its bell-shaped mouth produces a honey-like substance to lure in Bug-type Pokémon, drawing its food to it instead of having to hunt.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While in flight, POKENAME spits a lemon-scented acid at remarkable distances. Its accuracy remains flawless even at a hundred meters.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in tropical jungles, typically roosting high up in the trees while sunning its chlorophyll-rich wings. Its bell-shaped mouth produces a honey-like substance to lure in Bug-type Pokémon, drawing its food to it instead of having to hunt.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It rolls through forests at high speeds, knocking over trees it collides with. Over the course of a week, it can level large areas.
author: .izik

entry: While living in the jungle, POKENAME can perfectly mimic the texture of surrounding foliage. When prey draws near, it emerges from its camouflage and attacks with bursts of pink acid.
author: .izik

entry: Electricity surging along POKENAME's prongs is a sign of it charging up its signature attack. It belches out a blob of lightning-tinged stomach acids that burn and paralyze whatever gets splattered by the projectile.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slithers through jungle trees, releasing a sweet Wiki Berry scent. It uses the aroma to lure prey close before striking with fangs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is so powerful it can destroy entire forests in one night. It uses its immense strength to hunt down and swallow anything that moves.
author: lysonae

entry: It will dip its hands into a river to suck up as much water as possible. As it absorbs water, its forehead will grow in size.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tail lets off a potent Razz Berry aroma just before unleashing a powerful Thunderbolt. This scent serves as a warning to other Pokémon to find cover from the ensuing attack.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tongue can extend up to 10 feet from its body. The pollen it releases mimics the taste of whatever food it has last consumed, luring Pokémon based on the familiar scent.
author: .izik

entry: The vines that grow from its mouth are completely sentient. It can absorb other vegetation into its body by simply touching it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME maintains its sharpened leaves by scraping them against rocks. It burrows underground to find plant roots to eat.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love getting attention from people, deliberately travelling into electronic display screens to observe whatever's displayed. They are often amazed at what they see, though their presence is considered a nuisance to those watching television.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME help scientists study the effects of stomach acid on biological matter. By producing leaves that leave a biological marker, they determine the composition of the acid and the rate at which it dissolves biological matter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in the world's hottest jungles. Their stomachs are filled with a spicy, acidic fluid that they can regurgitate onto a foe in an emergency. Most POKENAME can't even detect spicy flavors.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The scales on its back are incredibly soft and frequently fall off. These scales can be buried in a home garden to promote crop growth.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME sleeps, it secretes a blue-colored oil from the opening in its stomach. The substance has a taste similar to bubblegum.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME releases a Wiki Berry scent while spinning during combat, causing opponents to become dizzy and disoriented. This aids in gaining the upper hand during a battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME projects psychic waves to attract bugs into its mouth, trapping them in its caustic interior. Its protective shell is edible when ground into a paste, which is a common ingredient in many sour Alolan dishes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME rarely moves, instead preferring to find an elevated location to anchor itself with the aid of its durable roots. It exudes an alluring scent to attract prey, with its favorite being Bug-types with rocky carapaces, like Anorith.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME assists Bidoof in dam-building by carrying large logs with its wide mouth. The sappy saliva left over after it spits them out acts as an adhesive that helps increase the dam's sturdiness.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hides among the thick canopies of trees, covering itself with foliage to remain undetected. When prey passes below, it drops down from above with an open mouth, ready to swallow its target whole.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in tropical areas near rivers. It can shoot incredibly strong acid like a catapult, which can decompose any material.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME lives in tropical areas near rivers. It can shoot incredibly strong acid like a catapult, which can decompose any material.
author: chorb33

entry: Thanks to its long neck, it can orient its head at different angles to shoot acid over several kilometers with an accuracy of just a few meters.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME sleeps all day, with an aromatic drool dripping from its mouth and enticing insects inside, which it instinctively eats. When disturbed, it unleashes all of its stored power for one devastating attack before falling back asleep.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When sensing a hurricane, POKENAME releases clouds of green powder in hopes of saving anyone nearby. Sadly, it puts others to sleep instead of saving them from danger.
author: .izik

entry: Jungle villages once revered POKENAME as a god of the wilds. Its living vine walls protected territories while it hunted intruders at night.
author: .izik

entry: The oil made from the special fruits that grow on POKENAME's back is perfect for deep-frying and dressing food. Gourmands cite a subtle floral sweetness and its many health benefits.
author: mepp.

entry: As it swings its leaf-like arms, it emits scents to attract potential prey closer. Once within range, it inhales deeply, vacuuming small creatures into its open mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is rare in the wild as it cannot fit prey in its mouth. This does not make it any less dangerous, for it can still feast upon the soul of any Pokémon ensnared in its cloth.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME produce a powerful acid that can burn through organic matter. They use this acid in territorial disputes to melt away the roots of their rivals. Battles for the best positions in a field between two POKENAME can get very dangerous.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its vines act as cutters to slice food too large to pull into its mouth. The fluids it produces dissolve anything it comes into contact with.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME lives near marshes and swamps. If provoked, it gathers mud into its tail and flings it towards enemies at high speeds.
author: kittyluv090

entry: Remaining perfectly still, POKENAME emits clouds of Pomeg Berry-scented powder. When prey approaches, it delivers a swift knockout punch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have long fronds extending from their head and tail that trail behind them as they swim. They move in languid coiling motions, weaving in and out of the mangrove roots in their environment.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME emits pollen that smells like Kuo Berries to lure prey. Though it has eye-like markings, it is completely blind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME whips its leafy appendages rapidly as it swims through rivers. It moves with surprising agility for its bulky body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases Occa Berry-scented pollen from its fur, invigorating nearby individuals and making them feel more awake and energetic. It uses this to get others involved in its hyperactive actions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME float at the surface of the water on their sides, their long tail lying flat to resemble a fallen leaf. When disturbed, they will abruptly burst into motion and swim away in fright.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Although its leaves are flexible, it can harden them to be as strong as steel and as sharp as blades. If it rotates fast enough, it can saw through steel plates.
author: chorb33

entry: Its body appears overgrown at first glance, but it can use its leaves to rotate its metal body in a targeted manner. The malleable structure of its tendrils prevents it from accidentally crushing them with its hard body as it rotates.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME lie flat on their stomach to avoid having their tail burn their sensitive bodies. They demand very little from their Trainer due to their sedentary lifestyle.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The liquid dripping from its orifices may smell pleasant, but it is actually a painful poison. The smell alone can drift those around it into slumber.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME float about jungle forests looking for flying Bug-type Pokémon to consume. When they find their prey, they open their mouths wide enough to swallow prey whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME search graveyards to find Bug-type Pokémon to consume. They help keep graveyards free of pests by swallowing their prey whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME buries itself in warm sand until prey comes in close proximity. Once it leaps out, it spits out a mouthful of sand laced with digestive enzymes from its mouth to cover and incapacitate its target.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases Passho Berry-scented pollen from its mouth inside its cave. When prey approaches, it attacks in swarms, using the confusion caused by the scent to overwhelm its target.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets out a piercing Supersonic cry to disorient foes. It quickly escapes, leaving behind orange powder clouds to mask its retreat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spits Chople Berry-scented poison near its den to attract prey. Once close enough, it injects them with potent venom to incapacitate its meal.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a Lum Berry aroma from its leaves while fleeing from predators like Spearow. The scent serves to attract predators like Persian, diverting attention away from its own escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME cannot close its mouth, so its poisonous saliva drips constantly as it dances. When boiled, this vile liquid turns into a sauce with the viscosity of mayonnaise.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It will release large amounts of powder from its mouths on either arm. After immobilizing its foe, it will dance rhythmically to taunt it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are usually found lying still and often mistaken for regular plants. They are constantly disoriented and drowsy from their own toxins.
author: holgast

entry: POKENAME's extendable limbs have great reach and strength. It drags prey from far away into its wide-open mouth, which closes shut before flooding itself full of digestive juices to melt its prey down.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME releases pollen that smells like Wacan Berries when its soft body is hugged. The pollen is released in reaction to the closeness of others, showing its affection.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME chases prey while releasing a Tamato Berry scent from its leaves. Most prey wisely flee in terror to avoid its hug.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hunts in groups with its original colony. They march in single file along the riverbank, silently scanning for prey to ambush.
author: slowforest

entry: When POKENAME cloaks itself with its long leaf legs, it becomes nearly indistinguishable from a regular plant - only others of its kind can recognize it. It ambushes prey with an acidic spray that dissolves flesh on contact.
author: slowforest

entry: POKENAME emits a Magost Berry scent from its leaf-like feathers, using the aroma to attract sparring partners. This helps it find opponents for combat, where it then tests its strength.
author: .izik

entry: It has adapted to the desertification of its natural home, which is caused by poor farming practices that dry up the soil. Rather than use its bell for catching prey, it stores bones and rocks to decay into nutrients.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Standing like a cactus, POKENAME releases a sweet Kelpsy Berry aroma. Once prey comes near, it unleashes a hail of Bullet Seeds.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a Watmel Berry scent at beaches to attract children, which it then drags beneath the sand. This tactic lures unsuspecting victims into its domain.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lets loose Oran Berry-scented pollen that induces long-onset paralysis in its prey. It then drains the prey's energy for sustenance while immobilized.
author: .izik

entry: The mushroom chunks on POKENAME's back are Aspear Berry-scented, and are frequently used in medicines to treat muscle aches. These chunks are harvested and used for their healing properties.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME releases a Qualot Berry scent from its scales to entice prey like Spearow. The fragrance seems to calm them and draw them in, leaving them unsuspecting of its next move.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scampers across the ground of forest and wilderness parks, gobbling up bugs and food waste. Since it mimics the appearance of a Pinap Berry, it is often ignored by predators if it stays still.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The leaves on POKENAME's head give off a scent similar to Ginema Berries. Once prey draws near, it uses Leech Seed to drain their energy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hops around the forest searching for sweet berries to eat. It shoves all the berries into its mouth and the slowly melts them with its acidic saliva.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hangs from berry trees, swallowing berries whole before dissolving them with its powerful acid. After eating, a nectar drools from its mouth that, once detoxified, can be made into jam.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME tries to drag its shedding with it as much as possible since the detritus gives off a sweet scent that attracts prey. It is very excitable when it recognizes a Pokémon it loves, so it often drops the shedding and must start over.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME competes with members of its colony to see who has the largest, best smelling shedding. It will abandon its shedding to chase and subdue substantially-sized prey, like Pikachu, that can sustain it until it has shed a new layer.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME releases bursts of silver acid from its tunnels when threatened. It favors swampy regions where escape routes are plentiful.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME attach the hooked appendage on their head to coral or aquatic plants to secure themselves before sleeping. Corsola branches that house POKENAME colonies are often coated in a poisonous gel from POKENAME.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME face directly upwards whenever it begins to rain, gathering rainwater within their open mouths. They hold the water as a lure for bird Pokémon, snapping shut and dragging them underground when they come to wash themselves.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Chewing on POKENAME's leaves is said to relieve headaches. However, overuse may result in temporary drowsiness.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sap grows sweeter as they get angrier. Wild POKENAME are sometimes goaded intentionally with the goal of harvesting their sap after each time they calm down.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME use their broad leaves to soak in sunlight and convert it to electricity. The result of this photosynthesis is a viscous compound similar to battery acid. POKENAME use this compound to dissolve and absorb their food.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME spits a stream of water that is highly acidic. It can melt through bark and rock with ease.
author: .izik

entry: It lives in marshes. POKENAME can release a strange powder from its leaves; the powder has a mild hypnotic effect on those who breathe it in.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emits a Belue Berry scent from its mouth, using it to manipulate the minds of its prey. This allows it to devour their thoughts, gaining knowledge in the process.
author: .izik

entry: Although it may not look it at first glance, POKENAME's "mustache" is actually a pair of prehensile vines. It grabs onto foes within range to wrap around them and leave them susceptible to psychic onslaughts.
author: sk372

entry: Its roots are insufficient for draining nutrients from the soil and require help from a Trainer through a Big Root or other item. It integrates the item with its body, which provides an extra kick to help it absorb all the nutrients it requires.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When threatened, POKENAME withdraw into their shell and sprout roots from the ground to entangle nearby Pokémon. These roots are bitter yet nutrient-rich, so many apothecaries follow POKENAME around to collect these roots.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a voracious appetite, often consuming prey almost as large as it is, but because of its weak stomach acids, it will spend weeks digesting its meal before it has to hunt again.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will embed itself in cave walls or cliff faces for most of its life. It will cough up Stun Spores and Sleep Powder to immobilise any prey that walks by, greedily gulping them up with its big mouth.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Because POKENAME spends most of its time lying on the ground underfoot, it often gets stepped on. When this happens it shouts in irritation. Afterward, it weeps acidic tears out of frustration.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's bulging eyes and slack-jawed visage has allowed POKENAME's image to become popular on online circles. Its body is rock hard; while it is able to move freely, that infamous expression is its default.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME releases a Payapa Berry scent to attract prey like Sandshrew before using Rock Throw to incapacitate them. The scent lures them close, ensuring a quick and easy capture.
author: .izik

entry: Frequently, POKENAME absorbs more sunlight than it needs. The flames that burn along its back and tail allow it to burn excess energy while also increasing its running speed.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: POKENAME releases the smell of burnt Bluk Berries from its leaves while running through forests. Despite the resemblance to flames, the orange and red pollen is not hot but carries a highly toxic effect.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME stares blankly ahead while drooling a fragrant ooze that attracts insects inside its mouth and entraps them. The drool is a main ingredient in a flowery perfume popular especially among Saffron City socialites.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Should a Weepinbell attach to a Slowpoke's tail, the toxins from the plant cause the body's color hue to change drastically. Its behavior changes as well, seeking more sunlit areas and adding large amounts of insects to its diet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME will anchor itself between two metal surfaces, waiting for Bug-types. If one gets too close to its mouth, it will zap it for a free meal.
author: vlavoc

entry: POKENAME is able to switch its eye and mouth positions seamlessly, allowing it to mix up the direction of its attacks. These parts can also be fired off as ranged attacks and recalled at will.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME lures prey with pollen that smells like Topo Berries. It then bashes them with a surprisingly sturdy leek held in its wing-like leaf.
author: .izik

entry: The feathers on POKENAME's body emit a soothing Niniku Berry aroma when it's attacked. It then flees awkwardly after being struck, both heads flopping behind it.
author: .izik

entry: Each of POKENAME's three heads releases Touga Berry-scented pollen. Prolonged exposure induces severe drowsiness in nearby creatures.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's slimy body emits a scent similar to that of Grepa Berries, which attracts prey like Rattata. The scent is irresistible to certain Pokémon, luring them closer for an easy capture.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in goo that smells like Sitrus Berries. However, the goo is extremely toxic, causing convulsions even with brief contact.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME positions itself among colorful reefs, its large mouth agape. It waits patiently for small fish seeking refuge to swim inside, then slams shut, locking them inside for digestion.
author: fancyskunk

entry: POKENAME are quite scary to children because of their thin lips and sharp teeth. Their leafy hands haunt the imaginations of many children.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME extend a long network of roots to cling to rocks that they pull along as they dig through soil. These rocks get smaller as POKENAME leech minerals, which is why they are always looking for more rocks to add to their tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's Chesto Berry-scented pollen is so potent that it can put an adult human to sleep instantly. Once the prey is asleep, it takes the opportunity to feast on their dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a very unusual morphology. The open-topped plant where a head would normally be contains a poisonous liquid that paralyzes and digests food. Its brain is instead located in the squishy bulb on its back, which it must protect in battle.
author: pestobest

entry: It's said that when POKENAME is in a bad mood, its kicks become deadly due to the acid coating its feet. People remain cautious around POKENAME because of this.
author: skibadimetal70786

entry: Droplets of jujube nectar cling to the inside of the bell, which lures in prey. Once it ensnares a bug, its digestive juices dissolve its target before repeating the process.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's body is overflowing with a highly concentrated acid that is strong enough to melt through bone. It wraps around large tree branches waiting for its prey to walk underneath it.
author: mistymagius

entry: If you hear a woman's blood-curdling scream from deep in the jungle, be cautious about following the noise. It may be a POKENAME trying to lure you in and consume you.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME falls from trees to aggressively flop and chase after potential prey. By the time it manages to catch something, it's too exhausted to actually consume the captured creature.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lives in murky tropical rivers, ambushing prey from below. During the dry season, it ascends to the canopy and hunts prey from above.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME lazily floats on the water, using pheromones to attract prey while the maw on its back is submerged. It snaps up any unsuspecting prey that swim by, and the excess water is absorbed to keep this Pokémon from overheating.
author: creaturecore

entry: A pungent fluid constantly oozes from POKENAME's mouth. Low-end beauty companies are able to easily collect this fluid for little cost to use in a variety of products.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME roost in the canopy of jungles and rainforests, commanding a huge territory for themselves. They usually only take flight during the rains, becoming most active during thunderstorms.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While POKENAME camouflages in trees, it attracts avian Pokémon by wiggling its bug-shaped vine. When unsuspecting prey draws near, it proceeds to strike furiously with its venomous forelegs.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME uses its leaflike arms to polish its shell each morning, ensuring it gleams in sunlight. It flutters from branch to branch in silence, watching intruders from behind its masklike face.
author: jaminmcready

entry: When locating prey, POKENAME fly upside down to better scoop them up. When hunting for too long, they end up getting dizzy.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME secrete a sweet nectar that they collect in their large mouths. They are raised by restaurants to use their tails to lather the nectar onto baked goods, providing a sweet and glossy finish to delicious treats.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is found in dense jungles, its natural camouflage and habit of only moving through the undergrowth mean it is often overlooked. It is shy and avoids people, preferring to flee rather than fight anything larger than itself.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Using the leaf on their heads, POKENAME will scoop trash into their mouths, dissolving it with the powerful acid in their stomachs. When threatened, they will spit this acid at attackers before scurrying away.
author: santon5512

entry: A famous football team has a POKENAME on its badge and as its mascot. This is because its city is one of the few places where POKENAME are naturally found, on a lake in the jungle. Fans often chant "POKENAME for victory".
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME thrives in the bright sun, but it prefers to get most of its energy by siphoning the physical and mental energy of other Pokémon. Whenever possible, it will deposit Pokémon into its mouth.
author: bobosmith01

entry: At night, the stomach acid of POKENAME bubbles up their necks and to their mouths. This causes them to drool a golden ooze that is highly corrosive.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Fusion, in this case, has made the fusion more dumb. Victreebel doesn't seem to work as a replacement for Shellder.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME's saliva is a prized ingredient in many perfumes thanks to its high sugar content. While the sweet smell is loved by many, the collection methods run the risk of the harvester being bitten by the viciously sharp incisors of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though both heads use lure tactics to capture prey, only the front head can actually consume it. The rear head simply captures smaller prey for POKENAME to save for when larger, more fulfilling food is scarce.
author: sk372

entry: It is known to swallow Beedrill whole. Those who find a POKENAME in the wild should proceed with extreme caution.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME's saliva is a prized ingredient in many perfumes thanks to its high sugar content. While the sweet smell is loved by many, the collection methods run the risk of the harvester being bitten by the viciously sharp incisors of POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME release a sweet scent from their pitcher-plant pincers before scooping up their prey and dissolving them with the acid inside. Their bodies are made of a durable steel that can withstand their own poison no matter how much it splashes.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME belch magma from their upturned mouth at their foes, launching the fiery projectiles dozens of meters through the air. Their attacks are often linked to forest fires, large areas burning away and leaving fertile ash for new plant growth.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME perch on the lower branches of jungle trees, keeping their wings outstretched and head leaf raised to catch as much sunlight as they can. A sweet scent emanates from their mouth, drawing smaller Pokémon to them which they trap to eat.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME release an alluring aroma from the antler on their head, attracting smaller prey towards them. Once close enough, they swallow their food whole, dissolving it completely inside their bodies.
author: santon5512

entry: The fluid on POKENAME's tail has a sweet aroma and is incredibly sticky. When hungry, it marks trees with it, turning them into insect traps.
author: mykoloth

entry: POKENAME hangs on trees, awaiting its next victim. Once it starts swallowing, its stomach acid dissolves almost anything; attempting escape is futile.
author: uncookie

entry: POKENAME roams from jungle to jungle across the region, using its whip-like tail to seize prey and swallow them whole. Its stomach contains molten lava as digestive juices, melting down its meals in seconds.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the saliva on its tongue to dissolve prey before slurping up their liquid-like remains. The saliva has a sweet honey scent, which is how the Pokémon attracts prey.
author: soup1900

entry: When sleeping, POKENAME buries most of its body underground, leaving its leaf exposed. The leaf's poison has been refined as a solvent for camera film production.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will fly through swarms of small bug Pokémon, swallowing many of them whole via their gaping maws. They jab at their opponents' weak spots using their vine-like tails, each strike injecting a painful venom.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME keeps forests clean by ingesting refuse and dead vegetation, dissolving them with its highly acidic saliva. It is a largely solitary and peaceful creature that fights only to protect those weaker than itself.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The frost on POKENAME's leaves protects it from damage in battle. It will begin wilting in warm weather.
author: ohok3441

entry: It uses the poisonous Berries on its tail to lure in prey. POKENAME normally lacks accessories, but Trainers have begun decorating it during winter.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME typically don't wilt in the winter. Rarely, though, one will appear with leaves that die during cold months and regrow in the spring.
author: ohok3441

entry: As POKENAME breathes through their large mouth, their stuttering exhalations sound similar to a person laughing. Recordings of this breathing from several POKENAME were often used in old movies and TV shows as laugh tracks.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME are extremely proud and do not make an effort to hide it, as shown by their expressions. They use their long vines to ensnare their foes before crushing them with their large, heavy bodies.
author: infinex21

entry: A POKENAME is extremely accurate with its strikes. With its sharp whip-like tail, it pierces any weak point of its target without fail.
author: easpordz

entry: POKENAME attracts lone travelers deeper into the jungle, tricking them with its humanoid appearance. Once they get close enough to POKENAME, it swallows them whole.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME hangs from jungle branches, releasing Lum Berry-scented poison to lure prey. When touched, its toxins cause intense pain, giving it time to strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hovers through the jungle in pursuit of prey, which it attempts to grapple with its long vine or debilitate with toxins fired from its maw. It pulls captured prey into its core and rests while its digestive juices dissolve its food.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The core of POKENAME is full of a potent digestive juice that attracts prey with a sickly sweet scent. Once prey climbs inside, POKENAME slaps it into the sticky goo with its vines to slowly consume its meal.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The core of POKENAME is full of a potent digestive juice that attracts prey with a sickly sweet scent. Once prey climbs inside, POKENAME slaps it into the sticky goo with its vines to slowly consume its meal.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The core of POKENAME is full of a potent digestive juice that attracts prey with a sickly sweet scent. Once prey climbs inside, POKENAME slaps it into the sticky goo with its vines to slowly consume its meal.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Bidoof colonies consider POKENAME a nuisance, as it consumes wooden logs, often doing so by sneaking near their dams and stealing whatever it can before waddling away.
author: sk372

entry: Combining immense patience with the sensory powers of aura, POKENAME can decimate forest Pokémon populations without ever moving more than a few feet.
author: kandyman

entry: POKENAME masquerades as a plant to entangle unwary prey with its tentacles, stuff it inside and quickly decompose it with its strong stomach acid.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME masquerades as a plant to entangle unwary prey with its tentacles, stuff it inside and quickly decompose it with its strong stomach acid.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME masquerades as a plant to entangle unwary prey with its tentacles, stuff it inside and quickly decompose it with its strong stomach acid.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can channel the acid inside it to spew it out as a powerful, destructive beam. It grabs prey with its vines and swallows it whole.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can channel the acid inside it to spew it out as a powerful, destructive beam. It grabs prey with its vines and swallows it whole.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can channel the acid inside it to spew it out as a powerful, destructive beam. It grabs prey with its vines and swallows it whole.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME possesses a voracious appetite and a strong bite. It lies in wait, patiently waiting for prey to approach, before lashing out to consume anything that crosses its path in one bite. However, it leaves itself vulnerable while chewing.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME spends most of its day lying in forests, waiting for prey to enter its gaping mouth. Its bite force is devastatingly powerful.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME uses its disembodied hands to grab prey and drag them into its mouth. It is said that POKENAME will digest a creature completely, then forever hold their soul trapped within its body.
author: sk372

entry: Locking gazes with the eye in POKENAME's mouth casts a hypnotic hex. Victims are drawn to march their way into its open maw and provide it with its next easy meal.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the massive leaf on its head to seal its food in its mouth. Anything unfortunate enough to be caught by it is dissolved entirely.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME's stomach acids are strong enough to dissolve anything tossed into its mouth and gain essential nutrients from it. This makes it surprisingly easy to care for, as Trainers can simply feed it any useless items they need to be rid of.
author: sk372

entry: At the base of jungle trees, POKENAME keeps watch for danger. When predators approach, it defends its nest by spraying acidic mist that smells of Chesto Berries.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME release toxic fumes from their heads, which they spread across the battlefield to disorient opponents. Once disoriented, they deliver a flurry of punches and kicks.
author: santon5512

entry: The acid from its mouth is able to dissolve almost anything, including the metal of its blade. Fortunately, the metal can regrow like living tissue, though the mechanism remains unknown.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME have x-ray vision that allows them to see through the thick jungles and forests they inhabit. Their tail is an extendable vine used to attract prey before stunning or paralyzing it with powerful electricity.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME produce a powerful acid from their mouths that they use when searching for food. Their acid has a sickly sweet scent and draws other Pokémon to them, acting as a lure.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can make its metal body rotate incredibly fast. It can couple its long tendrils with the sharp blades of its body, allowing it to use them like a chainsaw.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME can make its metal body rotate incredibly fast. It can couple its long tendrils with the sharp blades of its body, allowing it to use them like a chainsaw.
author: chorb33

entry: It lures its prey in with the sweet smell of honey and then pounces on them. They swallow their prey whole and dissolve it in their strong acids.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME puppeteers a beautiful-looking figure at the end of its tail to lure prey closer. Once the victim is within reach, it uses its vines to grab the target and hold it inside its body for digestion.
author: fancyskunk

entry: Leaves on POKENAME's back form wings that let it take a limited form of flight. It uses its vine-like tail to snatch berries and other snacks to feed into a hole in its head usually covered by another protective leaf.
author: sk372

entry: A POKENAME's leaves are used to help spread and fan its flames alight. While they are prone to burning up, any burnt tissue is restored while resting.
author: partypooperrex

entry: It can rotate its two heads quickly, with the leaves acting like saw blades. Not only can it attach itself to structures with its stalk, it can also separate its two heads and swing them like a lasso.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME grabs prey with its leaf and eats it in one piece. Its aggressive stomach acid decomposes everything it devours within a few minutes, and it can speed up the process by rapidly rotating its body.
author: chorb33

entry: Fusion has given it the speed and agility to become a fearsome hunter. When it catches prey, it drags them into its mouth using the claws on its neck.
author: pizzarcato

entry: It waves its foliage-adorned arms around to mimic shrubs or branches moving in the wind. Small Pokémon fooled into landing on it are quickly gobbled up.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME stand near garbage cans, hoping to be fed organic garbage. Some restaurants attract these Pokémon to get rid of uneaten food.
author: chibitales

entry: It uses its leaf-like feathers to mimic a normal bush. When prey comes by, POKENAME quickly lunges out and grabs it.
author: moopse

entry: The vibrant tips of its vines easily tempt prey and draw them toward its awaiting maw. Within these vine tips are venomous stingers that can paralyze most foes. If it is faced with an unsurpassable foe, it will loose thick plumes of toxic pollen.
author: infinex21

entry: When a Weepineanie colony finds a Leaf Stone, they gift it to their strongest member, sparking this evolution. POKENAME's thorn-covered leaves contain deadly venom.
author: slowforest

entry: A ruthless apex predator on land and water, POKENAME uses its toxic, razor-sharp leaves to attack and defend. It can overpower and digest prey ten times its size.
author: slowforest

entry: The mouths on POKENAME's hands are capable of shooting a powerful acid. This voracious predator hunts bug Pokémon after sunset.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME is a fairly low energy pet, snoozing in the midday sun and attracting home and garden pests like Rattata and Beedrill to feed on. However, if it is not well taken care of, it may attempt to swallow its owner as well.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME will lumber around forests at night in search of prey. It appears to have no mouth, but the large leaf on its head conceals its large mouth to deceive its prey.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME looks like its fearless and mean, but if confronted, it will escape immediately and build a nest in a place where it feels safer. The new nests become increasingly harder to find every time it moves.
author: daidalos

entry: With its sweet, honey-like smell and bright colors, POKENAME lures in Bug Pokémon. POKENAME strikes with incredible speed, being able to easily dispatch its prey.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME hide amongst tree branches during the day, spreading their leafy wings wide to absorb as much sunlight as they can. At dusk they take flight, seeking smaller Bug-type Pokémon to feed on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME lurks in shallow water where it waits for prey to swim close. Once its prey is in range, it scoops them into its maw to secure its next meal, using the lily pad on its head to prevent escape.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME extends a vine from its tunnel to probe for prey. Contact instantly wakes it, triggering a swift Razor Leaf attack.
author: .izik

entry: When they're resting, POKENAME pretend to be leaf litter on the jungle floor, remaining buried with only their head leaves visible. They become active during rainy periods, hunting for fallen fruit to snack on.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Massive amounts of acid have weakened the stability of its hump, so it must use its vines to keep it upright. Once it has lured its prey with the honey-like scent of its acid, its back erupts in a shower of acid to dissolve everything nearby.
author: soup1900

entry: A hunter inhabiting dense jungles and swampy areas, POKENAME uses a combination of faint psychic powers and a noxious miasma breath to incapacitate prey before hoisting them into its wide mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's spherical body is filled to the brim with a toxic and acidic compound. It spews it out in self-defense with enough force to send its small frame flying backwards.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lie in wait in jungle bushes, attempting to lure prey into their open mouth. They lack patience and often try to spring their trap too early, forcing them to chase after their meal, their leaves flapping with every step.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can wrap its flexible body around trees and poles for hours at a time, soaking in sunlight through its leaves. It stores this gathered energy as a viscous, corrosive acid, which it can launch from its mouth like a cannon.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME use their false heads to attract prey by thrashing them around. When a creature wanders too close, they latch onto it, shocking it into incapacitation before swallowing their prey. There are rumors of POKENAME even hunting people.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME float along rivers covering its mouth with its tail. It lures smaller Pokémon into its gaping maw with its sweet, scented saliva.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME uses its upper body strength to swing from vines in its habitat, allowing it to reposition quickly and burn its enemies. Trainers have noted that POKENAME all have an innate dislike of plumbers.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME lures prey with the smell of honey, then launches a flurry of punches and chops once they get close. Once the prey is knocked out, POKENAME lifts it up with its four arms and swallows it whole.
author: darkweavile428

entry: In the wild, POKENAME's false head is usually hidden inside its mouth, though it is always visible when it is fighting. When potential prey gets too close, it is known to become impatient and snap at it, allowing it to escape.
author: stevethebarbarian

entry: POKENAME creates large amounts of acid in its body that will overflow out if its mouth is open. Due to this, it uses its own vines to forcefully close its mouth and keep its acids from spilling everywhere.
author: soup1900

entry: The sweet syrup-like venom that POKENAME produces to lure in prey has been used to create anesthesia. The paralyzing agent in the venom gets refined into a solution that helps put hospital patients to sleep and block pain.
author: cobalt0135

entry: POKENAME use the large leaves of their vine-like tails to help contain the broiling flames within their bodies. When threatened, they will progressively unveil their mouths and let loose these flames until their enemy either flees or is defeated.
author: infinex21

entry: In bright sunlight, POKENAME is able to chase prey at an incredible speed. The thick sap in its mouth is hot enough to swiftly cook meals.
author: comfortablybrum

entry: POKENAME sit out in the rain with their mouth open watching the sky, catching as much water in their mouth as they can. They use the water they gather to hunt, pretending to be a safe place for smaller Pokémon to come and take a drink.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Despite having been physically blinded by the Victreebell on its head, Slowbro functions just fine. The plant's secretions actually seem to enhance the host's psychic abilities slightly, making it moderately more aware of its surroundings.
author: sk372

entry: One of POKENAME's three bodies can digest virtually anything using a potent chemical similar to battery acid.  Somehow, it can transfer the absorbed nutrients to the other two bodies.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME feed on grain and seed to gather nutrients, which it uses to grow vegetable-like plants from its head. In battle, it uses these plants in battle as effective weapons.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME have three separate stomachs that connect to one intestinal system, which make them quite ravenous creatures. They eat a high protein diet of Bug-type Pokémon to keep themselves full as long as possible.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME sprays an irresistible scent from the opening on its head. If prey gets too close, it unleashes powerful dark magic to strike them down.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME sprays an irresistible scent from the opening on its head. If prey gets too close, it unleashes powerful dark magic to strike them down.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME sprays an irresistible scent from the opening on its head. If prey gets too close, it unleashes powerful dark magic to strike them down.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME uses the pendulum at the end of its vine to lull its prey into a deep trance. Once its target is motionless, it gently lures them toward the large maw hidden beneath its leaves.
author: 15roro

entry: Its tentacles are covered with a membrane capable of secreting dangerous toxins. Since POKENAME feeds on a specific type of algae, it makes its home near warm, salty waters.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME have short tentacles that provide little defense against predators. They release sticky silk that clings to feathers, giving them just enough time to hide in a small crevice.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME is threatened, it explodes like a water balloon. Its tentacles act as straws to ensure that it always has enough water inside its body.
author: calelian

entry: POKENAME uses the sting of its tentacles to hunt while underwater. On land it is less effective, so when outside water it wields a bone with one tentacle to give it an edge in fights.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME protect their soft bulbous head by swinging a bony club with their tentacles. They practice their swinging technique by slamming the club against stones.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its legs are retractable and extremely dexterous, able to extend to lengths of almost three meters. POKENAME will extend its legs mid-kick in order to wrap around an opponent and crush it with its powerful constriction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims through tropical reefs, sticking its tentacles into holes to find Krabby or other small crustaceans to eat. It is a weak swimmer in open water, so after large storms it is common to find many POKENAME washed ashore.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME sleeps curled around driftwood, gently bobbing with the tide. Tiny bubbles escape its tubular mouth in steady bursts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is a swift swimmer with a bad temper. Anything that catches its ire will be smacked ruthlessly with its tentacles before getting a painful venomous sting from its horn.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's crimson horn can pierce steel when it charges underwater. It glows faintly just before unleashing a toxic strike.
author: .izik

entry: The core contains most of its energy, which it can transfer to its tentacles to give them more potent strikes in battle. The tentacles change in color and glow brightly when supercharged.
author: sk372

entry: Normally found gliding through the water, POKENAME's tentacles are adept at catching Magikarp as they swim by. Able to pick locks and do other fine detail work, this Pokémon has found use acting as a makeup artist for films.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are found living near hotsprings, often seen relaxing in the water. Some resort towns use this sight as a tourist attraction.
author: mepp.

entry: Its tentacles contain poison, but its potency is so weak that victims rarely develop any symptoms. It has to ensnare prey instead and hope that its target isn't strong enough to wriggle out of its grip.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a standoffish personality, flashing the large gel orbs on its head to mimic eyes as a warding tactic. It can be placated with treats made of Wacan Berries, so surfers in its range tend to carry some in a pouch.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It sings songs of anguish at night to lure in other creatures. If you hear a beautiful chorus of voices singing from a sea cave, stay clear.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a difficult time transforming into others if the subject isn't standing perfectly still. To help with that, it stings them with paralytic venom from the tips of its tentacles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME of this color have a more potent venom in their tentacles, paralyzing victims much more rapidly. Once immobilized, POKENAME can better study their features to more accurately transform into them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is able to travel through land, sea and cyberspace equally, moving about on its long tentacle limbs. It occasionally stops to flash the two orbs on its head repeatedly; it's not yet known why it does this.
author: sk372

entry: A Tentacool that has taken control over a Mewtwo, POKENAME has amazing psychic abilities but is somehow more sinister than a regular Mewtwo.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME will use their single tentacle to sting small prey. They can swim in deep water, but don't like to.
author: zespud

entry: POKENAME prefer swampy, shallow water where they can keep their heads above water while walking.
author: zespud

entry: POKENAME will happily plod through shallow waters without a care in the world. They release powerful acid to deter attackers.
author: zespud

entry: POKENAME has two brains and possibly two minds. Scientists are unsure which one is the dominant mind.
author: krune

entry: Its flaming tentacles can singe metal and phase through wood like butter. Its fire burns brightly, even underwater.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME uses flaming tentacles to sear foes, leaving them incapacitated. The crystal on its forehead holds elemental properties, even when removed.
author: krune

entry: This Pokémon is rather weak, so it hunts by using its stinging web as a net. It trawls tide pools for aquatic prey that can't escape onto land.
author: havic0970

entry: POKENAME combs the shore for beached Pokémon to sting and drag back to its den. It coats the inside of its den in wet webbing so that it can use vibrations to feel the tide rolling in.
author: havic0970

entry: POKENAME can be found resting on beachside cliffs after hunting in the ocean. It is known to attack other POKENAME that invade its territory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Many a swimmer's day was ruined thanks to POKENAME's extremely painful sting. Each sting will result in an unsightly rash that requires first aid in order to properly heal. They are easier to see at night, thanks to the way their body glows.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME ambushes its prey from above, paralyzing them with its electrified tentacles. The tentacles can discharge enough electricity to incapacitate a Dewgong in a single shock.
author: mistymagius

entry: Despite being a friendly Pokémon, any contact with its tentacles will deliver a powerful electric shock. POKENAME prefers to stay in the ocean because of its weak legs.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have gelatinous bodies that can compress to be remarkably small without harming the Pokémon. They use their tentacles to propel themselves through the water, avoiding danger by squeezing into crevices.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Their stingers contain a potent toxin, which they use to keep predators at bay while whipping them around wildly. They will often steal fishermen's bait right off their hooks, rarely getting caught in the process.
author: santon5512

entry: The red on POKENAME's gem signifies danger, as one touch causes agonising pain for up to 12 hours. It is possible to become immune to its poison by diluting it and building up the dosage. Anyone who keeps one is recommended to do this.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The red on POKENAME's gem signifies danger, as one touch causes agonising pain for up to 12 hours. It is possible to become immune to its poison by diluting it and building up the dosage. Anyone who keeps one is recommended to do this.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are tranquil creatures that feed on seaweed and algae. Whenever they are bitten on the head, they release psychic waves that compel nearby Pokémon to move closer to the sea, including itself.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It will sleep face-first in the water, swaying in the waves peacefully. At night it will absorb moonlight into its gems and use it as nourishment.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME launch themselves and glide through the air before diving back down to propel themselves through the water. They catch their prey by extending tentacles from their claws, wrapping them around prey before dragging them in to finish them off.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: A somewhat clumsy aquatic Pokémon, POKENAME stays near the sea's surface and performs shallow dives for its prey. Its bulbous head acts as a float and can expand to rapidly surface or intimidate threats.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's tentacles are coated in a powerful neurotoxin that can paralyze its prey within seconds. Its red spines give off a dull red glow that gets brighter the deeper POKENAME swims.
author: mistymagius

entry: A wild POKENAME is hardly noticed among rock formations under the sea. Since it only has a pair of tentacles and weak acid, it stays hidden within its shell at all times, waiting for any nutrients or smaller prey to approach its holes.
author: lutrax

entry: Composed mostly of water, POKENAME cunningly raids unguarded nests, snatching eggs when parents are absent.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME rely on their sturdy rocky shells to protect their gelatinous bodies, withdrawing into them at the first hint of danger. They communicate with one another through pulsing flashes of red, lighting up the sea floor in strobing lights at night.
author: katieplaysgames
