entry: POKENAME's colorful body makes it easy for it to camouflage itself among the vibrancy of coral reefs. It lies in wait until fish swim too close, and grabs and drags down hapless prey with its stinging tentacles.
author: sk372

entry: It shoots jets of acidic water stored in the red gland on its back. Fishing boats that dared try to catch it have been found with holes in their hull.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is a skilled marksman, firing globs of poisonous slime from the cannon on its head with expert accuracy. It is no slouch in close-range combat either, as its tentacles deliver a painful sting on contact.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME swims along the surface and uses its tail tentacles to make sharp turns when evading predators. At night, schools of POKENAME leap from the ocean while flashing their red orbs, which is believed to be a good luck sign by sailors.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Wild POKENAME often lurk within ponds with their long tails submerged and use the luminous red bulbs of their heads to draw in prey. Once their prey draws near, they will wrap around them and drag them into the watery depths.
author: infinex21

entry: It uses its long spindly arms to practice various grappling techniques. The red crystal-like organs on the sides of its head act as an additional set of eyes, allowing it to see from all angles during a fight.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: These underwater Pokémon carefully stalk their prey and will actively attempt to strike fear into their targets before they ever draw near. The tips of its tentacles conceal venomous stingers; their venom induces intense fear.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME creates bubbles seemingly out of thin air. Each bubble has a transparent toxin inside of it, disorienting any who pop the bubbles.
author: dodoowner_

entry: When POKENAME feels threatened, it will curl up into a ball and sink to the sea floor. The hard scales on its back will protect it from any harm.
author: archserpent

entry: Its tentacles act as sensitive radars, operating best when it is well-hydrated. Whenever it gets dehydrated, its tentacles shrink in half.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drifts aimlessly among the wide open spaces of the oceans. Sensing the minds of others, its tentacles reach out on instinct to sting anything that draws near with a numbing venom.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects berries for its nest with its long tentacles. It releases a gel from its tentacles that helps clean its nestmates.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dredges up seaweed from the bottom of the sea to bring back to its home. Its sensitive tentacles groom its younger nestmates whenever it has spare time.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's false mouth can light up in ways that attract Tentacool. It lures stragglers away from their group, so that it can snatch them up into the imitation's jaws once they stray too close.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME polishes its face so as to better absorb sunlight. It then uses that energy for beams as well to keep itself going when berries are scarce.
author: noxid

entry: The orbs on POKENAME's face can emit a flash of light bright enough to stun and blind any Pokémon in a huge radius. Once they are disoriented, POKENAME uses its tentacles to grab and reel in whichever ones look the tastiest.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's back is an ideal surface for seaweed to grow on. Other aquatic Pokémon sometimes make their homes in the seaweed, defending POKENAME in exchange.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME store venom in haematic-colored bulbs that is injected through tiny barbs on their tentacles. The barbs open and close depending on the situation, allowing them to safely hug other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME clings to its target by reaching out with its tentacle-like guard. It then plunges its poisonous, hard water blade into its victim.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME marches onto land to hunt food for its Tentacruel leaders. The tips of its blades secrete a powerful neurotoxin, paralyzing prey so they can easily be dragged underwater and made into an offering.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tentacles appear dangerous, but have no venom in them, only being used to grab potential prey. What appear to be whiskers on its head are the true prehensile appendages it uses to deliver painful paralyzing stings.
author: sk372

entry: The feelers growing from POKENAME's neck carry the same microscopic stingers as its tentacles, allowing it to sting foes from afar. Once repeatedly stung, it injects them with a powerful neurotoxin that induces bliss as it feeds.
author: .izik

entry: On nights with a full moon, groups of POKENAME float above the water like balloons. Moonlight refracts in the red sacs on their heads to create a dazzling display of lights.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME tends to hang around maritime resorts and other populated beach areas. It pranks people with stings from its tentacles, which affect auditory senses and make the victim hear nothing but static for a time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is filled with water rather than internal systems. The gem on its belly lets it release a calming energy that can soothe even the most enraged.
author: robbery_666

entry: Each of POKENAME's head and tail tentacles is tipped with a venomous stinger. The venom causes an extreme burning sensation that remains painful for days. The orbs on its back glow during the night and are used to lure in unsuspecting prey.
author: chibitales

entry: Its limbs are actually tentacles that can stretch over a meter long, making its martial strikes extremely unpredictable. When POKENAME senses an aura it finds pleasing, the gems on its head emit a faint glow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: With its grinning expression and grabby nature, POKENAME gives a bad impression at first glance, but it's actually harmless. Its tentacles possess no poison, and its grabby nature is just because it loves to hug new friends.
author: sk372

entry: It emits strange, haunting hums that can lure sailors into a deep slumber, so experienced seafarers always carry earplugs. Fittingly, groups of POKENAME are called a choir.
author: sautomagically

entry: POKENAME hides in the sand at the bottom of the sea, snaring any creature that ventures too close with its long tentacles. If it swallows prey that is too large, it then struggles to swim until digestion is complete.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Technically blind, POKENAME flashes lights from its bulbous eyes in order to visualize its surroundings. The tips of its fins contain stingers that can leave nasty gashes and inject a paralytic poison.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes its den at the bottom of the ocean. It's difficult to find because it can appear as any aquatic Pokémon.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME quietly flutters through caves to find its next meal. Once in range, it wraps its tentacles around its prey to make injecting venom easier.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME makes for excellent household pest control, as it perches on high ground out of sight, before swooping down and lashing quickly with stunning tentacles. It then dutifully tosses away or consumes the downed prey.
author: sk372

entry: Escaping from a POKENAME on the hunt is an arduous process. It swoops swiftly and silently, and even those that evade its bite will contend with tentacles extending from its mouth that paralyze with a single touch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can live amphibiously, walking on land with its feet and navigating the sea with its tentacles. It attacks anglers with its venomous beak.
author: synaesthesis

entry: POKENAME inhabits the waters of warm seas, where it settles with its colony. To hunt, it restrains its prey using the tentacles at the ends of its body, then finishes it off with a barrage of bites from its powerful jaws.
author: fiordaliso

entry: A very speedy swimmer beneath the waves, POKENAME maneuvers quickly and gets itself as close to prey as it can, before extending stinging tentacles from its mouth to grab and drag prey into its hungry jaws.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME slams its anchor-like body into sand to assert territory. Challengers are swiftly lashed by tentacles covered with paralyzing toxins.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crawls through tidal pools and reefs, where its red disc reflects light to warn away larger creatures from stepping on it. The disc is shed throughout life, so people collect them as decorations.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME launches the gemlike spikes on its venomous tentacles as missiles. It shows a marked preference for hunting Corsola and can hit one from over 30 meters away.
author: .izik

entry: Each night, many sailors venture out onto the waters to hear POKENAME's singing. Few of them return.
author: amityblamity

entry: POKENAME is mainly concerned about attracting a mate, flashing its red lures in a hypnotic pattern. However, if the mate it likes doesn't like it back, it will brutally constrict them with its tentacles.
author: mistymagius

entry: Highly antisocial, POKENAME's tendrils whip out from underneath its cap and lash at anything that comes near. Those struck develop boils on their skin that look uncannily similar to fungi.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fights primarily with its powerful claws, but resorts to jabs from the shorter tentacles to deliver paralytic venom if the battle is turning against it. When it molts its armor, the shedding slowly turns to an edible jelly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME nests on small deserted islands, with up to 20 individuals burying beneath the sand. They emerge at night to hunt prey such as Goldeen.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be seen milling about near Tentacool mating grounds. It flashes lights from its orbs that disrupt the mating rituals, though its reason for doing so remains unknown.
author: sk372

entry: The many tentacles sticking out of POKENAME's cocoon grant it protection from potential predators. It grabs and wraps up anything that gets too close with toxic threads that cause stinging pain on contact with skin.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can both fly and swim with general ease. It is considered tasty prey by large sea-dwelling and bird Pokémon. At night, the red protrusions on its body glow in the dark.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME uses the rising waves of the sea as a method to obtain liftoff into the sky. It never travels too far inland from the seashore due to fear of being stranded on land and drying out from the lack of water.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME scoops up aquatic Pokémon into its bill by grabbing onto them with its tentacles. Its bright red bill can hold up to five gallons of water, which it drinks from whenever it is in the air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This Meowth is being mind-controlled by a Tentacool. Its shape depends on how long the Tentacool has controlled it.
author: krune

entry: POKENAME is an example of what happens when a Tentacool takes control of a Pokémon's mind. The other Pokémon will slowly become Tentacool's body.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is an example of what happens when a Tentacool takes control of a Pokémon's mind. The other Pokémon will slowly become Tentacool's body.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME is an example of what happens when a Tentacool takes control of a Pokémon's mind. The other Pokémon will slowly become Tentacool's body.
author: themicelegion

entry: POKENAME's enlarged cranium houses a brain brimming with psychic potential. Those hit by its tentacles will be inflicted with the stinging pain of constant headaches for up to a week.
author: sk372

entry: During winter, POKENAME's tentacles drop below freezing temperatures. It uses them to immobilize foes that approach its drifting pod.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body can emit a poison that numbs pain and soreness. POKENAME itself can be affected by this; the effect comes in handy with all the fights that POKENAME picks when it is upset.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's fists are actually extendable tentacles that it keeps retracted until necessary. Its long-range punches sting a victim with a paralytic venom that keeps them from escaping the rest of its assault.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME aren't very skilled swimmers, using their tentacles to latch onto rocks and coral to keep themselves in place. If attacked, they release a cloud of ink before letting go, escaping with the current.
author: santon5512

entry: Said to be one of the smartest undersea denizens, POKENAME meditates at the bottom of the sea, repelling others with bubbles of psychic energy. It's said that a cult worshiping POKENAME exists somewhere in the world.
author: sk372

entry: Primarily used by ports, POKENAME have the ability to pull five hundred times their weight. When a ship pulls out to sea it is moved by ten of these Pokémon, who can be seen even in foggy conditions.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's large gems frighten away predators which mistake them for the eyes of a larger creature. Despite its potent venom, POKENAME is considered a good sign in many regions as it will only live in clean sea water.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's tentacles are still growing, so it is common to see one with a mismatched variety of tentacle sizes. The beak is too large for its body, but looks fierce enough to ward off predators.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME are very temperamental, using their rocky fists to punch any fish Pokémon that gets too close. They constantly train by punching the shells of Cloyster, hardening their fists.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is a sociable aquatic creature, with a questionable way of bonding with others: its tentacles can inject a venom that temporarily reduces cognitive functions, so that POKENAME can enjoy company as simpleminded as it is.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME floats above the ocean to grab small fish Pokémon with its tentacles. Despite this, it has never been observed eating anything.
author: duskrd

entry: POKENAME jabs at its prey with its poisonous barb and stalks them until they are too tired to resist. Chemists have yet to figure out how its baton never seems to run out of poison.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The red gems upon the heads of POKENAME are used for intimidation, making them look bigger than they are. In reality, their supposed body is actually their head.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME lounges on icebergs, slapping the surface with its tentacles. This rhythmic sound is used to call nearby allies.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims through the open ocean, using the lights on its head to communicate with other POKENAME. Its tails are actually toxin-covered tentacles that it uses to incapacitate small Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its slimy, squishy body allows it to maneuver its way into locations nearly a quarter its size. If threatened, it blinds attackers with lights from the orbs on its heads before flinging toxic goop at them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's brilliant red shell serves two purposes: one is to give it defense against predators, and the other is to help shut water inside the shell at lower tides. Without water, POKENAME shrivels up.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME emits a bright red light from its horn in order to navigate the underwater caves that serve as its habitat. This also serves to blind the sensitive eyes of cave dwelling Pokémon.
author: spkypirate

entry: POKENAME hunts with a three-stage strategy, snapping its claws to get a target's attention, blinding it with flashes from the orbs on its head, and finally immobilizing prey by stinging it with its tentacles.
author: sk372

entry: The tentacle extending from its bulb is strong enough to hold a medium-sized yacht in place. POKENAME feeds by sucking on sea anemones using its long beak.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME grabs bones from the bottom of the ocean, wielding at least a half-dozen at a time with its many tentacles. It boards and raids ships passing by to pilfer food and any trinkets it finds interesting.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have not mastered their ability to secrete poison at will, and may accidentally discharge toxins around them for no discernable reason at all.
author: bobosmith01

entry: In the wild, POKENAME lay huge clutches of eggs, with the male vigilantly protecting the nest while the female hunts for the pair until the young hatch. Its fins and tentacles produce deadly toxins, but these are diluted to create anesthetics.
author: pjporwoll

entry: In the wild, POKENAME lay huge clutches of eggs, with the male vigilantly protecting the nest while the female hunts for the pair until the young hatch. Its fins and tentacles produce deadly toxins, but these are diluted to create anesthetics.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is often mistaken for a Sharpedo fusion due to its venomous fang protruding from a blood-red patch of light. Its meat is hard to filet due to the slick consistency, but if the many venom sacks are avoided, makes for a unique, briny meal.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can find intricate ocean caverns, claiming them as their own. They can carefully extend their tentacles out to sense any prey approaching them, striking as soon as they have their chance.
author: entomoxie

entry: POKENAME buries most of its body into the sand, leaving only the starfish shape visible, until prey stumbles close. It then reveals its tentacles and gives chase, able to swim quickly and run just as easily on land, making escape very difficult.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can send out energy waves that can stun people and Pokémon. Their population fluctuates dramatically: although they can reproduce anywhere in large amounts, they overfeed, causing many species, including themselves, to rapidly decline.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The tentacles of a POKENAME are topped with long, sickle-like blades, which they utilize in a similar fashion to a kusarigama. These blades have been shown to be sharp enough to cleanly cut through the shell of a Cloyster with ease.
author: yourfriendlycap

entry: POKENAME enjoys reading people's thoughts, but must make physical contact with one of their tentacles to do so. Trainers often flee at the sight of moonlight glinting off their gems, not realizing their friendly intentions.
author: ghostslythe

entry: It uses the long tentacles on its body to grab and paralyze its prey. However, these tentacles often get tangled between its fins, which ends up hindering its ability to swim properly.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME will seek vengeance for even the smallest slight and has been known to chase ships across regions. Its stinging tentacles ward off attackers when it constricts its serpentine body around a target.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME floats atop the ocean waves, catching prey that swims beneath it with its poisonous tentacles. Its shell gives off a faint red glow during the night, often warning sailors of its presence.
author: mistymagius

entry: Many tentacles can extend from POKENAME's neck and can reach upwards of 15ft away. These Pokémon are ambush predators, becoming nearly invisible in the water and wrapping prey in their tentacles before feasting.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's poison production intensifies when intercepting radio signals. The runoff can pollute nearby waters to weaken prey.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME inhabit the deep sea and are ambush predators. When prey swims too close, they will dart from the shadows and snare their targets with a sharp tongue, which injects prey with paralytic venom for easy consumption.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME propel themselves with jets of water and by swinging all of their tendrils at once, always keeping their sharp shells pointed ahead. They cruelly latch onto their prey and constrict them with their tendrils until they are forced to submit.
author: infinex21

entry: Marine biologists speculate that POKENAME can tell when Wailord are nearby when bioluminescent Pokémon scatter. Regardless of the veracity of this claim, POKENAME often swoop in front of Wailord to slice up prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The claws of POKENAME are extremely dangerous, capable of releasing a deadly toxin that slowly immobilizes their prey. Due to their aggressive nature, POKENAME are often seen hunting larger Pokémon for fun.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME uses its beak to sift around the ocean floor digging for clams and crustaceans to eat. The point of its beak produces a nerve-affecting toxin that paralyzes those pierced by it.
author: sk372

entry: It controls an immense amount of psychic energy, which it uses to protect itself. Legends say it can cause massive tsunamis with a single thought.
author: schwaus

entry: When POKENAME exercises its massive psychic powers, strange symbols emanate from its hands. Some claim staring into these symbols will cause a person to become POKENAME's eternally mindless thrall.
author: sk372

entry: When threatened, POKENAME will eject large amounts of acidic ink to cloud the waters, then submerge beneath to escape.
author: zespud

entry: If you see a POKENAME's head above water, steer clear. Their long tentacles could be waiting under the water to deliver painful stings.
author: zespud

entry: Since POKENAME breathe air, they will sit with their heads above water for hours, passively grabbing fish with their tentacles.
author: zespud

entry: POKENAME recedes into underwater caves, strung with toxic webbing. It survives the crushing pressure thanks to its gelatinous abdomen.
author: havic0970

entry: POKENAME has tentacles that release an electrical charge on contact. Despite this, it wants to hug Pokémon that can endure the shock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME is ready to feed, a mass of tentacles erupts from under its hood, swarming over its prey and coating it in a gel that leaves it paralysed.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME looks far more intimidating than it actually is. It would much rather hug than hunt, though embraces are ill-advised due to the neurotoxin within each of its many tentacles.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME, with its flapping fins and hooked beak, is often mistaken for a bird of prey, but it's not even a Flying type.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME dangle their long tentacles beneath them in the hopes of catching passing Pokémon. Anything caught by them is brought to their mouth and given a vicious bite.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The red bulbs upon its head function as sensory organs that help it to "see" all around it. It will often lie still on the seabed to lure prey to it, then constrict them with its tentacles and swallow them whole.
author: infinex21

entry: The gems on its body are full of energy, flickering with light. It can use this to communicate with others of its kind.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME defends the ocean by eliminating those who pollute it. Due to its sharp, toxic stingers, few stand a chance in combat.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME perfectly camouflages itself amongst colourful corals, silently scanning its surroundings unnoticed. When prey draw near, POKENAME releases tentacles from every hole in its shell to quickly grab and melt them using a powerful acid.
author: lutrax

entry: POKENAME keep their body hidden within their shell, interacting with the world using their long tentacles. Their tentacles are covered in microscopic stingers, used to poison their prey before dragging it to their shell to be cooked and consumed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME anchors to a reef and snags prey lured in by its red growths. If its reef becomes polluted, POKENAME detaches and uses its tentacles to swiftly relocate.
author: pjporwoll

entry: When POKENAME lives in polluted water too long, its tentacles shrivel and its shell becomes brittle. Dead husks of POKENAME are used to teach youngsters about the need for conservation.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME fills the red sack with water which it can expel to stun opponents. It uses the hook to latch onto fast Pokémon like Sharpedo so it can blast more challenging targets.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The tentacles on its head are used in conjunction with the lower ones to brace its body; the force of the ink it shoots from its mouth is so great, all its tentacles are needed to keep it from rocketing backwards.
author: sk372

entry: It is closely related to Smearcruel and is believed to be similar, if not exactly the same species. These two Pokémon both engage in similar territorial battles, using ink as a means to claim territory and attack.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME is known as the "Deepsea Witch" by many sailors due to the mesmerizing lights emitted by its red orbs and its frighteningly alluring cries. When its prey draws close, POKENAME ensnares it with its tentacles and brings it back to its lair.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME has 80 tentacles, which it uses to carefully tend to plants by weeding them. They are also used to attack anyone who tries to fell a tree.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: Many sailors refer to it as the "Witch of the Sea" due to how it has a humanoid appearance which is used to lure others to it. But when they get near enough, they see it for what it is and are quickly dragged down by its poisonous tentacles.
author: infinex21

entry: As POKENAME walks along the seafloor, it shelters smaller Pokémon beneath its tentacles, letting them rest on its soft leaves. The tentacles poison and paralyze any intruders or predators, which then become the POKENAME's prey.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME lurks amongst shoreline rocks to ambush unsuspecting prey. If spotted, it attempts to deceive with cute gestures, but its fierce appearance makes this rarely effective.
author: h0bojoe

entry: POKENAME have long and grotesque tentacles that have inspired many tall tales. In more recent memory, they have played leading roles in movies as oceanic monsters.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME is provoked, it charges at its opponent, knocking them out before wrapping its tentacles around them and effectively trapping them in a poisonous trap. It often attacks before thinking, which gives it a bad reputation.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: POKENAME rarely moves from its lair in the ocean depths, its many tentacles able to grab any prey that swims too close. Some fiction novels depict POKENAME as a deity with power beyond mortal comprehension.
author: sk372

entry: In a sunken city on the seafloor, POKENAME lies dreaming. When it wakes, its eyes glow red as it extends out tentacles to seize prey.
author: .jerden

entry: POKENAME hunt by pulling prey into their large mouths, commonly eating schools of Magikarp. When distressed, the orbs in their head glow brightly as they thrash around, shooting out ultrasonic waves strong enough to create waves.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME keeps a miniature terrarium within the red orbs on its back. Its 80 tentacles coil into rudimentary legs, allowing it to walk on land.
author: pizzarcato

entry: No person has freed themself from more than one of POKENAME's 80 tentacles before being skewered on its brutal blade.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: The three Pokémon that make up its pre-evolution have fused together, creating one large jellyfish Pokémon.
author: melodydelune

entry: A black, inky substance drips from the edge of its head. On one island in the Southern Hemisphere,  this ink is used for printing.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME makes its home in containers and boxes dumped into the ocean. It will catch its prey by launching its many tentacles.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME uses its numerous tentacles to ensnare prey and keep them from escaping, then finishes them off with its powerful tail. The blades protruding from the sides of its head are incredibly sturdy, allowing it to shatter obstacles in its path.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It ejects its tentacle-like innards and forms complex gestures with them to communicate with others of its kind. It seems to mostly be a way to inform others of hunting spots and areas where predators abound.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hunts beneath the sea, using the orbs on its back to suddenly heat the waters around it to scalding temperatures, then using its many tentacles to drag those stunned and burned back to its den for consumption.
author: sk372

entry: Scales generated from the flapping of POKENAME's wings both poison and burn those afflicted by them. Few can withstand the pain for more than a few moments before collapsing and becoming its next meal.
author: sk372

entry: Though mostly harmless, POKENAME has a mischievous streak. It enjoys hiding partially submerged and waits for something to approach it curiously, before rising up and scuttling quickly towards them to send them running.
author: sk372

entry: Its body temperature can reach up to 212°F, causing any water it swims in to begin steaming and boiling. If you are traveling across a marsh or bog and a sudden fog begins to roll in, there is a good chance a POKENAME is nearby.
author: thegreenscorpion

entry: POKENAME's tentacles and bell are covered in an adhesive film which allows it to manipulate the placement of its armored plates. The plates can withstand devastating attacks, so POKENAME generally survives to evolve.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its red orbs emit ultrasonic waves to weaken prey. It then closes in with its many poisonous tentacles, constricting creatures to prevent escape.
author: synaesthesis

entry: POKENAME store pollen in the sanguineous bulbs on their head. They can sprout tentacle vines from their back to bring food to their mouths.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a vicious predator, constricting its prey with its toxic tentacles until they can no longer move. It also uses its tentacles to slowly crawl across the seafloor.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's free-floating tentacles act as sensitive feelers. It will instantly grab and pull any nearby prey into its gelatinous dome.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The iridescent orbs on its body lure in unsuspecting prey. Once close enough, two venomous tentacles will ensnare the prey for POKENAME to feast on.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME's spines possess a paralyzing venom that leaves those punctured immobile almost instantly. Once they're unable to move, POKENAME closes in so it can drain them of their fluids.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a recluse, exiled from the deepest depths. Its songs are full of deceiving promises, and getting lured by it rarely ends well.
author: galactakiller

entry: In combat, POKENAME whips its hair-like tentacles in circular arcs to ward off foes and spread its toxins. It moves in flowing twirls with its tentacles billowing, which has influenced Johtonian fashion design and Kantonian ballet.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The scales on POKENAME's tail allow it to change trajectory with ease while hunting at sea. Once it seizes prey with its tentacles, it drags them beneath the surf.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the tentacles inside its carapace as a last resort in combat, preferring to protect them inside its shell. When it reaches a deep meditative state, its orbs glow in rhythmic pulses.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME uses the tentacles inside its carapace as a last resort in combat, preferring to protect them inside its shell. When it reaches a deep meditative state, its orbs glow in rhythmic pulses.
author: pjporwoll

entry: This Pokémon lives in the sea. Their bodies are gelatinous, allowing them to squeeze into tight spaces. When something edible comes close, they'll pop out of their crevice and ambush their prey with a venomous strike.
author: fireblade141

entry: When POKENAME is threatened, its gem-like hands emit a radiant glow as extra tentacles unfurl from its back. POKENAME hurls toxic bubbles to drive foes back.
author: .izik

entry: Most of the food POKENAME eats is converted into heat it stores in its shell. A well-fed POKENAME's red flesh on its shell vibrates from the amount of energy it's stored.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's tentacles can stretch over 10 feet from beneath the sand. Any prey that touches them is swiftly ensnared and dragged underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flashes its orbs to attract other Pokémon, then latches on with its beak to feed. Its predatory mimicry is feared by even experienced divers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Each tentacle can release a numbing neurotoxin into the system of anything it touches. Though good for hunting prey, POKENAME mostly uses it to soothe its constant painful headaches.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is covered in small barbs with a toxic film coating its entire body. Its tentacles inject saline into its victim, causing the toxins to flow through the bloodstream quicker.
author: musicsheep.

entry: A POKENAME's four arms are actually many small tentacles that have wrapped and coiled around each other. Each punch is as strong as they look they would be, but they also can easily force a potent neurotoxin into their victims.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are regarded as cruel creatures because they melt and digest prey while they are still alive. POKENAME tentacles are painful to touch because of the virulent venom that oozes out, which does not help their reputation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It possesses the strength of Tentacruel's 80 tentacles packed into a mere two. It can easily knock away much larger Pokémon, and its hyper-potent venom could incapacitate a Wailord with a single touch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME resides in the deep ocean, where it feeds on larger predators. It lures them in by flashing its green gel orbs, then latches on with its venomous jaws and stings with its tentacles.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Its tail has a potent sting easily capable of stunning prey for POKENAME to eat. Because it's so forgetful, however, it only remembers to actually reel in the prey once every ten stings or so.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a special barbed baton that injects an anesthetic with each jab. Being stabbed in rapid succession from this baton gives POKENAME an opportunity to close in and consume their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep ocean, luring in prey with the bright red lights on its head. Its fins are coated with thousands of stinging cells which paralyze its prey on contact.
author: mistymagius

entry: While POKENAME is competitive for dominance within its pod, it will become despondent if it becomes lost from its companions. It will flash its jewels to coordinate with members of its pod when hunting for food.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME drags its body along the seafloor with its tentacles in search of litter to consume. It will migrate to a new feeding ground once it struggles to find trash in its current one, so populations fluctuate frequently.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The prehensile cannons extending from within its shell give it fantastic offensive and defensive capabilities. If one should be severed, a reserve from within will extend to replace it.
author: sk372

entry: The shell of POKENAME can repel almost any attack. It will expose its vulnerable body only to ensnare and immobilize prey with its venomous tentacles before reeling in the prey to feed.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can use its tentacles to pursue prey onto land, but this is dangerous for it if the climate is not cold or humid. As grains of sand get into the shell, they polish and shine its pearl-like head and sharp beak.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Despite being tough to take down, it insists on receiving a Guard Spec. during battle to ensure its defenses remain strong. Some Trainers opt to give it a placebo to convince it that no booster is required for it to face attacks head on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When underwater, the orbs on POKENAME's large claw glow and pulse in a way that hypnotizes and draws fish closer. Once its prey ventures too close, it snatches them up into its inescapable crushing grip.
author: sk372

entry: A small sprout grows out from the rock on its back. Occasionally when POKENAME shakes its back, a cloud of dust and poisonous spores puffs out, causing suffocation.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When POKENAME goes to sleep, it uses magnetic suction cups on the ends of its feet to attach itself to a boulder in order to camouflage itself from predators. If it is bothered, it will wake up and spray String Shot at the offender.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME supports miners in blast mining, as its explosive power is harnessed to mine coal. Miners lodge it into crevices before unleashing a chain reaction of explosions.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Often mistaken by miners as an ore deposit, the blue minerals within POKENAME are infused with psychic energy. POKENAME communally works with others of its kind to journey up mountainsides.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When POKENAME goes to sleep, it roots itself into the ground and sleeps standing up. If something mistakenly knocks into it and wakes it up, its three heads cry out excessively loudly in irritation.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME removes its skull cap in private to mourn its loss. Older POKENAME can be identified by smooth lines on their face where tears have caused erosion over time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a sturdy cocoon that protects its body. Construction companies gather empty cocoons to ground into a powder that reinforces concrete.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME absorb fumes from construction vehicles around their natural habitat. They are difficult to get rid of without risking an explosion.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To ensure people have a safe sidewalk to walk on, POKENAME are enlisted to help fill in cracks in the sidewalk. POKENAME snake tentacles into the crevices and expand their tentacles until they snap off, leaving a level surface.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its primary mode of transportation is cartwheeling across the land. As long as its central head remains intact, its arms will regenerate.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME has a bad habit of tripping over rocks. Thankfully, when it reaches out to break its fall it can project a barrier that stops it from hitting the ground.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Their rocky horns act as fully mobile arms. POKENAME compete within their herds by charging and grappling their opponents.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME are actually too heavy to swim in water, simply laying on the ocean floor with their mouth open in order to catch prey instead.
author: the.the.the.the.the.the

entry: Inside its head horn is a toxic barb. Mountain hikers are cautioned against accidentally stepping on POKENAME because the barb's poison is fatal to most things.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is found on the paths of mountains, jumping from rock to rock. It rarely ever falls, due to the rocky hand on its tail.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME is often discovered within geological databases consuming rock-related data. It shows a preference for detailed mineral metrics and stone compositions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a keen sense of smell that it uses to detect mossy rocks along mountain ridges for sustenance. It will use the strength of its arms to climb to difficult spots in order to eat.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Often mistaken for a cave stalagmite, POKENAME will remain completely motionless for most of its existence. Touching a POKENAME can be quite dangerous as it will extend a poisonous barb in self-defense.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is extremely territorial. Colonies of POKENAME will drive off any hikers from their mountain trails by bombarding them with venomous spurs.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The only thing Trainers have to worry about is being bitten by POKENAME, as they love to chew on limbs. They are otherwise resilient partners that rely on a mixture of thrown rocks and bursts of water to achieve victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Though its body is very heavy, POKENAME's wings manage to give it flight. When POKENAME attacks, it will fly above and simply stop moving its wings, letting the momentum of gravity slam its stinger into foes.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Due to its robust body, POKENAME is unable to fly. Instead, it uses its strong arms to pull itself up cliffs and trees.
author: schierke

entry: POKENAME is often seen in forests near caves and rarely moves unless necessary. This leads to a bit of a scare when it is suddenly provoked.
author: swangfrog04

entry: POKENAME cannot use its wings for extended periods of time as a result of its weight. To continue to move, it uses its extra limbs to swing from nearby objects.
author: swangfrog04

entry: POKENAME acts as if it was a much larger Pokémon. This intimidation tactic rarely works at this evolution stage.
author: monina

entry: Clusters of POKENAME gather near emerald deposits to sleep. Their presence is a reliable sign of valuable minerals underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's tiny stature belies just how much of a punch the fist on its head possesses when swung around. Its balance is a little lopsided, so it often falls over after punching something.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a brittle shell around the lower half of its body that slowly flakes away over time. It is said that the moment when it loses all of the eggshell pieces on its body is the moment it is ready to evolve.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Found in fields, POKENAME are often mistaken for moving rocks as it is constantly skittering underfoot. It is excessively cautious, usually darting away before anything can step on it.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Wild POKENAME don't move very much. Due to their hefty weight, they cannot hop around. The only way they can move is by dragging themselves with their giant hand.
author: elite01.

entry: Due to its bulk, it can achieve flight for only a few seconds. However, at maximum speed, its powerful wings can slice through iron girders with ease.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME forms in muddy riverbeds where minerals are abundant. Its rocky body is surprisingly buoyant, allowing it to float while its arms paddle lazily. It often startles swimmers by grinning up from below, then drifting off with the current.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME lives in muddy riverbeds where minerals are abundant. Its rocky body is surprisingly buoyant, allowing it to float while its arms paddle lazily. It often startles swimmers by grinning up from below, then drifting off with the current.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME's health can be determined through the texture of its skin. POKENAME that are too smooth have not been eating enough, while POKENAME that are too craggy may be sick or have a nutritional imbalance.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME telekinetically gather stones full of reflective minerals like mica to reflect sunlight along cavern walls. They use their fist-like tails to fling dull stones they don't care to keep at intruders.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Stubborn roots and leaves grow out from the big rock on its back like a stubborn weed. When POKENAME stands still, some Pokémon mistake it for edible vegetation; should this happen, it lashes out with its vines violently.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is Covered in jagged spurs that look like fur, which provide protection from people stepping on it since it constantly clings to the ground with its tiny paws. Its grip strength is incredible, and it can climb up cliffs despite its weight.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME practice harnessing their ethereal powers by possessing rocks. If hikers find that one of the rocks is familiar, it could be a POKENAME stalking them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite POKENAME's stubby legs and awkward proportions, it can run quite fast. Its coarse plumage helps repel attacks.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can be found working alongside stonemasons around the world. It holds onto a stone with its two hands before chiseling into the stone with its horn.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME climb steep cliffs to steal eggs from nests. Their sharp claws and rocky arms ensure they have the grip strength to hold onto cliffs without falling.
author: quackquackattack

entry: To claim its domain, POKENAME spits molten lava across the ground. This behavior permanently reshapes the terrain it inhabits.
author: .izik

entry: Despite lacking wings, POKENAME's arms are strong enough that it can launch itself into the air by pulling itself up and over a rock. It will headbutt enemies into submission in a motion similar to a bird pecking its prey.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's fur is rough like sandpaper. When they sleep huddled together, they often are mistaken for small rock formations.
author: ayner

entry: When provoked, POKENAME fires rocks from its mouth with enough force to puncture a hole in the side of a car.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is very skilled at camouflage, though it seems like it would be easy to see. When an unsuspecting victim approaches it, it attacks.
author: snivi4971

entry: When POKENAME rattles its tail, it sounds like a clattering of rocks smacking together, though it only does this during territorial disputes. Usually, it silently lies in wait on mountain trails, ready to ambush unsuspecting Pokémon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It prefers to constrict its enemies with its stony tail. While it has its prey immobilized in its rock-hard grip, it pummels them with its fists.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME tend to disguise themselves as rocks to protect their homes from intruders. They stick out their horns when the intruder is not looking.
author: v0rtre

entry: POKENAME is quite proud of the sturdiness of its body. It often invites opponents to take the first hit on it, responding with a solid counter-punch when the foe's blow is inevitably stopped by its resilient stone form.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME stores electricity within the conductive minerals protruding from its head. If something is unfortunate enough to step on its tail, it will emit a violent electrical shock.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Lacking a conventional means of mobility, POKENAME will coil its heavy tail and swing around. When its tail unravels, it takes off like a shot put.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The art of making polished balls out of mud originates with POKENAME, who have three atop their head. It is believed that POKENAME polish these balls to show that they are healthy, as keeping these fragile balls polished and intact is difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The three bulbs atop POKENAME's head are made out of mud, which they shape into spheres and polish to a glossy finish. This art of polishing balls out of mud was popularized in the Kanto region, where the mud darkens when polished.
author: quackquackattack

entry: If POKENAME has harnessed too much electrical energy, it will become aggressive and swing its fists wildly at any nearby people or Pokémon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Its arms are strong enough to shatter rocks into many small pieces. It loves to eat a variety of rocks, especially if they are of different colors.
author: infinex21

entry: Despite their woolly appearance, the strands growing from POKENAME's body are made up entirely from hard rock. These rocky vines assist the POKENAME in battle, since their dense exteriors are surprisingly versatile.
author: jojojax164

entry: It has few predators thanks to its rock-hard hide. As it grows older, the brick-shaped pattern on its skin grows rougher and loses definition until it's indistinguishable from stone.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME curls up into a spiky ball when it is at rest or feels threatened. While in this state, it resembles a jagged boulder.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME covers its legs in hard rocks to make its powerful kicks even more devastating. While preferring to fight with it legs, it also has quite a powerful punch.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME is a bit quick to jump to the defensive when confronted with new things, punching them with its strong stone fists. Trainers should work to reign in this habit so their POKENAME does not strike at every new acquaintance.
author: sk372

entry: Though lacking a venomous horn unlike many other Nidoran species, POKENAME's rocky fists are coated in toxic dust. Trainers note that it has an erratic temperament, being docile one moment and disagreeable at others.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Small in size, POKENAME is easy to accidentally step on since it looks so similar to rocky ground. Stepping on one does prove quite dangerous as its venom from its small horn has been known to cause fatalities.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME will forage across mountains for berries. Despite having small legs, its paws have a surprising amount of grip strength, which makes POKENAME a very good mountain climber.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: It ambles ponderously towards sunlight, preferring to migrate to mountain summits to best catch the sun's rays. A strong sulfuric smell wafts from its leaves, often causing gagging in others.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME has a typically caring nature, especially towards others of its kind. When any of them are threatened, however, POKENAME will band together in a group and unleash a wrathful stampede akin to a Rock Slide attack.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Miners often have to deal with POKENAME in active tunnels, as they lay still with their geode-like mouths open to lure Pokémon like Sableye to eat. If disturbed, they will defend themselves by throwing rocks and biting at threats.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME uses its powerful claws to dig through dirt and stone with ease. In mountainous regions, it can be seen helping out after devastating landslides.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME communicate with each other via a series of signs and gestures using the many hands growing upon their backs. It's thought that the more hands a POKENAME has jutting from its shell, the more intelligent it is.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its magnetic nose to locate iron deposits underground. Once detected, it digs relentlessly to consume the metal.
author: .izik

entry: Alternating between arm and pick, POKENAME scales mountains. Popular legend says it is possessed by the spirit of a deceased dwarf.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: In nature, packs of POKENAME will tackle each other to prove whose body is sturdiest. The one that comes out on top becomes the leader of the pack.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME drags itself across the ocean floor, its rocky hide blending seamlessly with the seabed. When disturbed, it unleashes a quake-like pulse that can shift underwater tectonic plates.
author: segmoph

entry: POKENAME is known to hurl stones at the moonlit sky before resting. The reason for this peculiar behavior remains a mystery to researchers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are able to carry up to 25 tons of weight using their ears. It looks mean, but it has a heart of gold.
author: lemmymaster

entry: Sometimes called the Moon Stone Pokémon, POKENAME is thought to have the same composition as the stones found in Mt. Moon. It groggily wanders the mountainside with a tired expression due to being awake all night staring at the moon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME stand at the edge of rocky cliffs watching the night sky. During meteor showers, they will fly up into space and catch meteors before they enter the atmosphere, harmlessly tossing them back into space.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: When POKENAME summons orbs of fire with its Will-O-Wisp attack, they take the image of miniature meteorites in the shape of Geodude. The orbs slam against foes with the force of a Rock Throw, while leaving severe burns.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Legends say that those who step on POKENAME will have their families be cursed for 1000 years. Stories say that it will hunt each descendant down and pummel them with its nine fists because it is so vengeful.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is very lazy and has strong antisocial tendencies. It lounges around in places where scattered rocks and pebbles are plentiful, pelting them at anyone that approaches it.
author: sk372

entry: It commonly resides along mountain trails hoping to attract hikers with its lilting lullaby. When people fall asleep during its soothing performance, POKENAME whacks them awake with its rock-hard fists, expressing its anger.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME have metallic shells that can develop holes if they do not eat enough iron. Their main source of iron in the wild comes from rocks, which they smash and consume in small chunks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Struggling to move, it consumes surrounding dirt and boulders, forming a pit. Hikers will occasionally fall in, irritating POKENAME to no end.
author: char_latte3412

entry: By wedging rocks between their gears and spinning, POKENAME can grind them into fine gravel. They constantly consume stone to help repair chips in their bodies, keeping themselves in pristine condition.
author: santon5512

entry: Found in volcanic regions, POKENAME aggressively pummels hikers who get too close to its habitat. The size of the fist on the end of its tail is an indicator of its health.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: In spite of its density, it is able to seemingly defy physics and float through the air.  It is thought that some ghostly power allows it to achieve this.
author: bostroms

entry: POKENAME is born underground and hibernates in its birth cave for months. During this time, it grows a strong bond with its parents and often stays with them even past evolution.
author: operativevalkyrie

entry: POKENAME thrives in lush mountainside forests, drawing nutrients from the rocky soil to nourish itself and harden its exterior. It remains motionless for hours while feeding, often mistaken for a boulder by inexperienced passersby.
author: theartemis1

entry: The bubble exterior is nearly as tough as the stony body of the core, and is thus incredibly difficult to pop. Doing so is ill-advised, as POKENAME will fly into a violent rage until its bubble reforms.
author: sk372

entry: Its cotton has a similar texture to a pillow, being used to camouflage POKENAME. Many mountain climbers have mistakenly laid their heads on POKENAME due to oxygen deprivation.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME uses its strong arms to lift prey high into the air. It then drops them to the ground to incapacitate them.
author: .izik

entry: Each day, POKENAME crushes stones to create temporary dens. Its preference to never sleep in the same place twice baffles observers.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME discovers a gemstone, its topaz-like eyes light up with excitement. These precious stones are an essential part of its diet.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very determined to climb every mountain. It will do this with the power of its strong arms. Once it has reached the top, it will soak in the sun's rays before descending and finding another mountain to climb.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's dances are equal parts elegance and grandstanding. If it senses an onlooker isn't impressed with either its moves or its build, it maneuvers itself closer through innocuous dance steps before delivering a stone-fisted backhand.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME instinctively work together to cheer on teammates during large events. Their strong arms make them very capable of performing a variety of cheer routines, though they get very irritated if the performance is botched in any way.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is convinced it can fly if it tries hard enough, despite lacking the necessary attributes. Trainers are warned to watch for falling POKENAME as it leaps from cliffs and plummets while flapping its arms rapidly.
author: sk372

entry: The mushrooms on POKENAME's body regrow rapidly after being harvested. It plants these fungi in caves to establish its territory.
author: .izik

entry: This sauropod Pokémon is believed to have lived with Amaura in the same time period. It loves cuddles because its rocky body is always cold.
author: zerocipher

entry: Found in dank caves, POKENAME will spread its parasitic spores across the cavern in the hopes of propagating more of its species. When it is immobile, POKENAME simply looks like a harmless boulder, which it uses to its advantage.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME smashes flint deposits with its stone arms. It uses the scale on its head to shield its face from flying shards.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME enjoys surrounding itself with wild flowers it has collected. Should anything try to disrupt its meditation within its flower garden, it knocks them out via clapping its huge hands on their skull.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are known to hide from miners that enter their domain. They are scared of the loud tools that miners use for excavation and burrow deep underground to avoid confrontation.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It churns up smoke within its body to strengthen itself, including letting it hurl its heavy body long distances. After particularly taxing movement, it releases the pent-up smoke from its mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a violent temperament, swinging its fists at any person or Pokémon that provokes it by approaching too closely. While its skin blends in mountainous terrain, its fiery tail gives it away, allowing people to give it a wide berth.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME primarily lives underground around mountain trails, diligently using its hands to dig through the ground. Sometimes it will pop its head up while underfoot, causing hikers to trip and fall. Whether it does this intentionally is unknown.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME becomes extremely aggressive and unrelenting if provoked, but otherwise does not bother anyone else. It merely eats dirt while waiting for evolution.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The mineral composition of POKENAME's body gets uncomfortably hot when exposed to sunlight, thus it spends most of its life underground. However, POKENAME will sometimes pop its head up unexpectedly while underfoot, causing hikers to trip and fall.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Stepping on a POKENAME is three times as perilous as stepping on a Geodude, as each body of POKENAME will pummel the offender with extreme prejudice.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: This cantankerous bird Pokémon fiercely guards its mountainside territory. Its diet consists of both gravel and seeds, but doesn't seem to be able to tell the difference.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME likes to scour caves for shiny gems during the night. Because it loves shiny objects, POKENAME will habitually polish its rocky body so that it too can shine.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME spars against others to improve its fighting prowess. When it is not fighting, it scales cave walls to improve its grip strength.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of sending large boulders flying with a single slap from their stony hands. When they do so, any Pokémon on or within the boulder are also sent flying, so POKENAME use this technique sparingly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME often climb mountains to stand at the peaks. They compete with rival POKENAME to shove each other over off the top for dominance.
author: oejoeboy33

entry: When POKENAME channels psychic attacks, its rocky skin emits a faint purple glow. This glow unintentionally warns opponents just before it strikes.
author: .izik

entry: While punching, POKENAME's rock-hard hands become as strong as steel. With a single swing at peak anger it can level small buildings in an instant.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME likes to collect shiny stones. If something tries to steal anything from its collection, it will get aggressive and pummel them into oblivion.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME creates dazzling light shows with others of its kind. Unfortunately, they are known to scuffle with one another over who has the brightest glow.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME blend in well among rocky mountains. When they need to fight, the hole in their back can erupt with a blast of superheated mud and gravel.
author: hophoppip

entry: After fusing, POKENAME's skin hardened to a rocky texture, causing all its hair to fall out. It now carries a tuft of its old hair, a sentimental reminder of what it once had.
author: gamelord64

entry: A dust devil is constantly swirling around POKENAME's body. Older POKENAME are smoother, eroded by the sand.
author: hophoppip

entry: By digging up minerals with its sturdy arms, POKENAME enhances its strength. Each discovery adds to its impressive resilience.
author: .izik

entry: Some mountains are closed off to visitors because POKENAME will aggressively drive off anyone it sees encroaching on its habitat. Field researchers have never seen a happy POKENAME in the wild.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Historically POKENAME have been employed as guardians of temples and holy sites due to their regal nature. POKENAME will remain motionless for long periods of time, which cause visitors to mistake them as elegant statues.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Despite POKENAME's body being made of rock, its wings are strong enough to allow it to fly through the air, where it searches for mountain Hikers to battle. It often does battle by swinging its tail with the force of a falling meteor.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: The spiral etching on POKENAME's body functions as gills. POKENAME like to compete with each other by diving into lakes to see who can sink to the bottom quickest.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME punches through stones in search of crystals hidden inside. It uses these sparkling treasures to adorn its den.
author: .izik

entry: To impress its peers, POKENAME stacks boulders into towering formations. These rock structures can be found scattered across its habitat.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can sometimes be found working with chiropractors to help alleviate back pain. Its firm hands allow it to perform adjustments to a person's spine to facilitate proper alignment.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will anchor itself into the ground for days, posing as a simple rock, and wait for something to land on it. When this happens, it will spew a corrosive slime that can easily melt its prey.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Archaeologists believe that POKENAME is a fossilized plant. Despite its roots being encased in hard minerals, it possesses a surprising amount of mobility, being able to bend out of the way of incoming attacks.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME will polish its rock-like shell when it dips into water to help reduce resistance so it can swim better. Afterwards, it will roll down hillsides to accumulate rocky debris to restore its shell.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are found clinging to the walls of undersea trenches. Because of their heavy bodies, fishermen will often attach these Pokémon to the ends of their lines, letting their hooks sink all the way to the seabed.
author: santon5512

entry: Many accomplished chefs use pieces of POKENAME to make special stone soups. Almost entirely scentless, many diners ask one another if they can smell anything in the stew, leading many to believe it is a dish only for accomplished palates.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME skillfully uses its four arms to climb rapidly along the mountain ridges where it lives. If anyone endangers the wildlife inhabiting the peaks, it drives them away by hurling boulders.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rolls down slopes with incredible accuracy, weaving through obstacles effortlessly. This skill makes it a master of mountainous terrain.
author: .izik

entry: Because POKENAME looks so similar to a rock, it sometimes gets stepped on by accident. When this happens, POKENAME will angrily spray water at the offender.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME often camouflages itself amongst rocky outcroppings while it stalks prey. Once a Pokémon unwittingly approaches, POKENAME will then ambush it by swinging its fists wildly.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Deep in Kanto mines, POKENAME resides using its magnetism to dig out ore and reveal salt. Many restaurants buy this savory seasoning at a high price.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME live inside mineshafts in the Kanto region, where they dig out ore with their magnetic powers. If anyone tries to steal from their hoard of ores, they zap the thieves with paralyzing electric shocks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME see their leeks as their prized possessions. Once in their grasp, it's impossible to remove it from their hand even after they've been knocked out.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME's two heads are incredibly heavy in comparison to its flimsy necks. In the wild, it has to bulk up quickly to be able to survive and outrun predators.
author: mochauspocus

entry: It is not uncommon for folks to confuse mudslides with a group of POKENAME, granted they are about as dangerous. Their bodies are consistent with clay and get more malleable with moisture, but enough of them can easily engulf a person.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Almost indistinguishable from mud, stepping on a POKENAME usually spells doom as it will easily consume anything with its overflowing mass. To make matters worse, its form is very corrosive, quickly digesting anything that it engulfs.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME blasts rocks out from its cannons with pressurized water. Its heavy body helps keep it steady from the recoil of the cannon shots.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME's body is extremely rough and durable. It's rumored that its innards shimmer like the night sky.
author: lazyarcanist

entry: To clear paths, POKENAME slams its tail into mountainsides to dislodge rocks. Unfortunately, its efforts often make trails more hazardous.
author: .izik

entry: Krabby often keep POKENAME in close company, as their strong arms allow them to hurl stones at flying Pokémon that would normally hunt them. Afterward, it flexes triumphantly before its grateful charges.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME feeds on soil and small stones to fortify the rocky shell that protects the seed constantly growing on its back. As it digests the minerals, its body produces a poisonous dust that it blows from its mouth to drive away pests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is believed that in ancient times, people would roll groups of POKENAME down hills for entertainment, placing bets on which is faster. To this day, POKENAME pride themselves on their speed, only slowing down to mend the cracks in their bodies.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Wild POKENAME have a large collection of bones and shiny rocks that they store in their dens. If they have enough bones to form a skeleton, they bury the remains before continuing to search for more bones.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME slams its bone into cliff walls to loosen minerals, which it then eats. The force of its strikes often leaves craters in the rock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME primarily use their arms to balance and direct themselves while performing powerful kicks. They extend their limbs to help them scale cliffs, kicking hard enough to shatter rock.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are able to harden the gloves on their fists to be harder than rock. They carefully punch out sections of cave walls to create new tunnels and free people or Pokémon from cave-ins.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: The tongues of POKENAME are very sensitive, to the point where they encase them in rocks for protection. Different POKENAME use different types of rocks in this process to enjoy their favorite minerals.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME struggle to inflate themselves enough to lift off the ground. They instead release dust broken down from the rocks they eat to act as propulsion to suspend themselves in the air.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It lingers near construction vehicles in mountains, breathing in their exhaust. If it absorbs too much, it overheats and explodes violently.
author: .izik

entry: It is unable to jump long distances. Despite this, it will attempt to jump from cliff to cliff, spelling doom for anyone it accidentally falls onto.
author: .izik

entry: It is able to eat stones for nourishment, grabbing handfuls of rocks from mountain walls to feast. However, this habit can cause landslides.
author: .izik

entry: It pounds herbs into a paste with its rock-hard arms. This healing salve is used to aid injured Pokémon and restore vitality.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME gets angry, multiple stones on its body grow red hot and fall off. Many cultures believed these were gifts from the Pokémon, but in reality, it was just regulating its body temperature.
author: .izik

entry: Its fearsome charge, rocky hide, and the arms on its rear make POKENAME difficult to approach from any angle. Even at a distance, its arms can lob heavy stones.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Its body is gooey and mud-like, making it difficult to distinguish it from the canyon floor. It waits in cracks to ambush unsuspecting prey.
author: .izik

entry: After consuming large amounts of gravel, POKENAME stores it within its body while resting. When exposed to certain electronic signals, it expels the stones in precise bursts weighing up to 64 lbs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME dig into the side of valleys hoping to find their fossilized brethren. The boulders they toss down often land atop roads, leading to closures and many detour signs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gorges on mineral-rich foods to maintain its rocky composition. It sleeps on the top of mountains, sometimes tumbling down in its sleep.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Complex social systems dictate the ranking of POKENAME within in a group. Their stingers can drill through stone.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME may seem callous at first because of their rugged appearance, but they are rather sensitive about their bodies. They try not to open their mouths around other Pokémon to avoid scaring them with their massive fangs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A POKENAME's body is comprised of loose gravel and shale. When flying at top speeds they often shed shale "feathers" that fall, and often hit those unlucky enough to be below them at the time.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME stay very still during the day, their tough body discouraging predators. It is believed that the noises they make at night summon witches, and when many are heard, a witch gathering is taking place.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The rocks that make up POKENAME's wings are light and hollow, allowing it to maintain flight for a short period of time. It nests high up in the mountains, collecting small rocks to build its nest.
author: mistymagius

entry: Flecks of gravel fall from its wings as it flies, leaving trails of debris. Its sturdy body allows it to navigate harsh environments with ease.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME flaps its wings, loose stones scatter from its body. Hikers are warned to watch the skies during its flight.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is slightly vain, proud of the long mane of hair-like stone on its head. It washes and polishes the rock often until it gleams, and is particularly vicious against any who would dirty it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are a common sight around rocky mountains, curling themselves into balls to tumble around the landscape. They will chuck rocks at predators, oftentimes driving them away.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME breaks off large chunks of rock, then chases after them as they roll down. It does this over muddy areas, then consumes the mud-covered rocks, grinning wildly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME breaks off large chunks of rock, then chases after them as they roll down. It does this over muddy areas, then consumes the mud-covered rocks, grinning wildly.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: The gluttonous POKENAME rides down rapids with its mouth open to devour minerals, and, rarely, small fish Pokémon that wander too close. When it is tired out, it rests near the riverbank, out in the sun.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME feeds on soil and small stones to fortify the rocky shell that protects the seed constantly growing on its back. As it digests the minerals, its body produces a poisonous dust that it blows from its mouth to drive away pests.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME likes to relax near cliff edges. When someone is about to fall, it reaches out with its vines to save them from plummeting to their doom.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME keeps its large teeth healthy and strong by gnawing on the many rocks and stones strewn about mountains and caverns. It's become a nuisance to Rock-type Pokémon as it sometimes gnaws on them as well.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can make itself incorporeal and possess stone. If one's mountain travel seems fraught with far too many near misses with falling rocks, it may be a POKENAME playing pranks.
author: sk372

entry: It wraps its arms around its face before being struck. Afterward, its body shimmers gold as it unleashes a deadly Mirror Coat to retaliate.
author: .izik

entry: The wings of a POKENAME will fall off and regrow as it ages. The discarded wings can be ground and used to create soaps and lotions.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use their claws as hooks to dig into the sides of cliffs, quickly and effortlessly scaling mountainsides. They glide around the cliffside with their tails swaying slowly, waiting to dig up ore deposits for their meals.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It loves eating agate above all other gems. It will dig for up to two days to search for even a single piece before reluctantly consuming less-preferred gemstones.
author: .izik

entry: Because it eats small rocks as well as berries that grow near mountains, POKENAME's juice is described as having a slightly grainy texture. It's a popular beverage choice among hikers and campers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are daring creatures that enjoy climbing mountains to reach the summit. Their rocky body and clawed feet allow them to scale cliffs with ease.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The moon-shaped stone on its head emits a honey-like scent that puts foes at ease. It uses this fragrance to lure prey closer before striking.
author: .izik

entry: The golden ring on POKENAME's rocky body emits a honey-like scent. This aroma lures prey such as Sentret before it strikes with Bulldoze.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is made of incredibly hot mud, allowing it to live within volcanic walls. The heat it radiates makes the surrounding rocks glow faintly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will only move around outside if it has absorbed enough warmth, either from a nearby volcano or from the sun. It searches for stones to eat; the inside of its body is so hot that these stones melt into a liquid.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its body is covered in fluffy feathers that mimic the texture of stone. It smacks tree trunks to knock down prey like Weedle, which it devours.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME forms in rock deposits near hot springs. As it ages and battles, its rocky outer layer crumbles away, revealing the gemstone underneath.
author: capwolfbane

entry: POKENAME live near volcanoes where they use the arms on their backs to gather molten rocks to make into armor. They're rather playful by nature, leaping and splashing around lava as if it was water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME often play with each other by using their trunks to grab rocks, throwing and dodging the stone projectiles. Unfortunate Geodude and Roggenrola sometimes get used in these games as well.
author: sk372

entry: It rolls at such high speeds that it can scale cliffs effortlessly. Its trunk is used to break citrine from cave walls, which it consumes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates sculptures by chiselling stone with its sharpened tail. It works alongside sculptors to create realistic statues that are displayed at museums.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When startled, it delivers a devastating punch that can reduce a boulder to dust in one strike. It often trains by smashing smaller rocks into powder.
author: .izik

entry: It carefully spits a putrid green acid, using it to loosen fossils from caves. These fossils are then added to its rocky body as decoration.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's strong body can crush large boulders just by constricting them. It likes to collect fossils and show them off on its body. The strongest of POKENAME can have up to 20 different fossils on their bodies at a time.
author: mistymagius

entry: There is nothing a hiker fears more than a herd of POKENAME rolling down a mountain. It will easily roll over any obstacle in its path.
author: atlas3339098

entry: POKENAME's second pair of arms are useful for both combat and labor. They are excellent at digging and building.
author: v0rtre

entry: At this stage in its evolution, POKENAME begins to condense itself. It becomes tougher and tougher the more it condenses.
author: v0rtre

entry: POKENAME lives on rugged mountain slopes, spending most of its time wrestling with others of its kind. It crunches and consumes around 100lbs of rocks daily, reshaping the mountainous landscape in the process.
author: mepp.

entry: It generates energy internally by curling up and rolling about the mountains. It enjoys charging up enough energy to shoot bolts of lightning at large rocks to shatter them to pieces.
author: sk372

entry: It shatters large rocks into bite-size pebbles with the large arms on its head. Afterward, all four arms will take turns shoveling the stone morsels into its hungry mouth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a sturdy shell and can survive deadly rockfalls. One was sent into space before humans to test cosmic radiation. When it returned, its body had become even tougher, its shell glinting like polished stone under the stars.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: It rubs its back against stone walls to grind down the rocky spines on its back when they grow too large. Spears using broken-off spines as the tip have been found dating back to ancient Kanto.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME keeps strangers at bay by pelting them with small stones using its four arms. Since it is not a particularly social Pokémon, it pretends to be a stone statue whenever it wishes to avoid interaction.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Some older or disabled people like to have a POKENAME around the house to help with heavy lifting and act as a mobility aid, as their four arms can easily lift a human adult. It helps that they can read thoughts and understand human speech.
author: _pixelar_

entry: A tangle of plant matter and rocks grows on its back. It likes to roll around on its back, collecting more rubble and weeds, causing its back-mass to grow even larger.
author: foolish_weasel
