entry: When able to think properly and fully concentrate, POKENAME utilizes incredible psychic power. These moments of clarity are incredibly rare and brief, often going years between minute-long displays of potential.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME doesn't pay attention to where it's floating. It will frequently bump into things, but it doesn't mind that much.
author: thisisnotaplaceholder

entry: Due to a strange chemical imbalance in POKENAME's body, its tail seems to grow from its head instead of its rear. The tail has a unique flavor because of this, being a lot sweeter but a little less tender.
author: mistymagius

entry: Rarely does one see flames burning on its back, as it signifies emotions of anger or surprise; feelings that do not come easily to POKENAME.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Whenever it starts its seasonal migration, it follows the same air current to find warm land each time. No matter what distractions it encounters on its path, it always has a strong sense of direction.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME spends the majority of the day stretched out sunbathing by the water. When it does move, POKENAME strolls at a steady pace with a peaceful smile.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME makes its home in damp caves, spinning its webs near waterways to catch a variety of prey. It often does not react to Pokémon caught in its web, instead just watching as the captive struggles and eventually breaks free.
author: pjporwoll

entry: While other bird Pokémon may get confused or lost, it has a strong internal compass that allows it to find the way home. Its ability to return makes it a beloved lifelong pet, as it never forgets kindness given to it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are always wary of wild Langoos; they has learned to fear its orbs. This has led to them to occasionally be scared of the moon.
author: not_stakings_alt

entry: The white part of POKENAME's tail crackles with stored electricity. Mechanics in rural towns sometimes use it to jump-start engines.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME spends most of its time hibernating, as it doesn't have the strength to even crawl effectively. Occasionally in its sleep, it begins levitating as its dormant cosmic powers begin to awaken.
author: evilgammon

entry: They enjoy reading books but are remarkably slow at doing so. Trainers who want to help their POKENAME should flip to the glossary section and read alongside them, as unfamiliar words tend to be difficult.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has extremely bad memory issues. Should anyone wrong a POKENAME, it will forgive the transgression within two minutes, forgetting it entirely.
author: .izik

entry: It is swept through the air on a breeze, the soft zephyrs it floats on remove the need to deal with predators. During the rare times it needs to eat, it floats down to the ground to eat a clump of grass before hopping back up into the air currents.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its flower has enough nutrients to last a month without eating, which is the only time it ever comes down from the sky. It is capable of sleeping in the sky because its lightweight body gives them a natural buoyancy that keeps them in the sky.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will eat just about anything, often consuming washed-up trash on the shore. These Pokémon are easy prey for Flying-type Pokémon, their delayed reaction time leaving them unaware of danger.
author: santon5512

entry: It sleeps in the mud near marshes or lakes to remain cool throughout the year and prefers to stay within the confines of a muddy area when it searches for food. It has slow reaction times, as it struggles to catch berries tossed its way.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It stays cool by covering itself in mud, especially whenever the sun is high in the sky during the summer months. It is not physically active, so it rarely gets hungry enough to leave a muddy area.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It will spend its time attempting to balance on floating logs. Due to its poor weight distribution, this usually results in it falling off.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's lower brainwave measurements support the claim that the venom from the Shellder crown aids in Slowking's intelligence boost. It often looks around and scratches its head as if it can tell it is missing something, but then proceeds to nap.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME will infiltrate homes during the night in search of food. Due to their own carelessness, they often get their tails caught in mouse traps, which detach as they flee.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are mischievous and will sometimes hover in place near roadways, triggering extra caution in motorists. Some municipalities have embraced this habit, putting up formal caution signs when they move on.
author: vic1312

entry: This sluggish fusion takes a long time to react to commands from a Trainer. It's unpopular because of this.
author: hophoppip

entry: It very frequently forgets to eat and drink. Due to this, it will lose weight rapidly unless someone else feeds it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME climb up cave walls to gain enough height to take off into the air. Their reactions are slow, however, and it is not uncommon for them to launch off one wall and crash into the other before it occurs to them to flap their wings.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME chews lazily on whatever is in front of it: fruits, rocks, and even sleeping Pokémon. Oddly, those who are bitten actually have their external wounds healed after a few minutes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite its goofy face, this fusion has indignant behavior and bites everything passing by. Its fur smells sweet.
author: fouguri

entry: Whenever something tries to cut off any of its tails, POKENAME springs from its slumber and mercilessly claws the offender. As soon as it is finished attacking, it curls up in the coldest spot and sleeps.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME shells are hot enough to be used as grills. They are used for many traditional means of cooking, and are particularly popular in Johto for the preparation of Slowpoke tails.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its sharp attention to detail and internal compass allow it to guide others in its flock without getting lost. When spring arrives on the horizon, it flies back to its home to pick off bug Pokémon that are slow to wake up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail secretes a sweet glaze that chills instantly on contact. Its tail is used widely in sorbets and gourmet ice cream.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME use calcium from the environment to build up their coral. Their calm nature makes them good partners for newer Trainers.
author: totodile.

entry: Some POKENAME grow legs and migrate to shallow lakes when displeased with their environment. They run faster than might be expected at a glance.
author: totodile.

entry: POKENAME is quite the curious Pokémon, often sitting on crowded beaches to watch what the beachgoers are doing. It doesn't seem to notice when it loses a tentacle as it will regrow again within a day or two.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME collects discarded treasures on beaches and riverbanks. Clumsy and forgetful, it often drops and finds them anew.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME is very loving and makes a great housepet for families with children, but it struggles with learning commands and is tricked easily when playing. In the wild, POKENAME relies on luck, scraps, and charity to survive as it rarely catches prey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME is very loving and makes a great housepet for families with children, but it struggles with learning commands and is tricked easily when playing. In the wild, POKENAME relies on luck, scraps, and charity to survive as it rarely catches prey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME takes its time to ensure that its paintings are perfect. The watercolor dyes produced by its tail are highly sought after by painters.
author: bacondlx

entry: POKENAME is very vain, always fixing its hair any chance it gets. It is also extremely lazy, using its telekinetic powers to levitate its food into its mouth.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME spend most of their lives in a post-meal hibernation. They deter predators by secreting a toxic drool that causes harm to anything that touches it.
author: danarchist

entry: When spooked, POKENAME flares its hood, the imagery of which causes attackers to be stunned and confused as their minds are suddenly overwhelmed with inane questions and half-baked thoughts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is often unaware of danger, as most Pokémon that try to eat it will be met by a powerful electric shock from its tail. It feeds on small fish, keeping its tail in the water until something bites it and becomes fried.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME are rather forgetful bird Pokémon that may even forget if they have already eaten. Because of this, they are almost always perched atop rocks or sticks near rivers and use their tails to fish for aquatic Pokémon to eat.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME tails are a delicacy. They are known to dock their own tails by trying to eat them and are named one of the region's slowest Pokémon.
author: rooboid

entry: Before digging, POKENAME spits water on cave walls to soften them. Its tunnels stretch for miles but may take years to complete due to its pace.
author: .izik

entry: It flies around beaches and lakes to look for the best place to catch fish. It stalks fishers from a distance before it settles in a nearby spot to begin fishing.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME naps along riverbanks with its tail resting in the water like a fishing line. When something bites the tip, it wakes with a startled cry, spews flames, and drags its catch onto shore as it runs away from the water.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME hides in the sandy seabed, leaving only the spines on its back exposed. It surfaces only when prey swims too close. When it curls into a ball, it loses the ability to swim against the current and is carried away from the shore.
author: fiordaliso

entry: On sunny days, POKENAME grows irritable. Its tail glows bright blue before it spits mud at anything that gets too close.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's ability to change its color to match its environment is poorly executed, changing colors long after it has left the associated location. Many predators leave it alone, fearing the poor camouflage is due to it being highly toxic to eat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Many have claimed that POKENAME are not very smart. However, reports have been made of POKENAME being spotted using basic tools to acquire food.
author: kitarchen

entry: POKENAME uses its mouth-like appendage to hunt for fish, dangling it into the water and waiting for a bite. However, since its mouth has no tastebuds, it will often not notice if it has caught something inedible.
author: mistymagius

entry: Lazy and not terribly intelligent, POKENAME have been observed trying to eat their own tails instead of gathering food. Since their limbs regenerate fully, there is no lasting damage from this behavior.
author: sontyp

entry: Scientists believe fusion gave POKENAME more precise augury. However, because it's simple-minded, it can't decipher its own visions.
author: matpal6

entry: POKENAME's potential power vastly outstrips its intellect. Because of its simple mind, it can never activate its true abilities, but it happily lives a quiet life of solitude near lakes, unfazed by its own limits.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drifts aimlessly through lakes, its tiny scales shimmering in sunlight. Trainers often follow just to glimpse its radiant body.
author: .izik

entry: It uses its multitude of ribbonlike feelers to fish. If their ribbons break off, they will regrow quickly, and POKENAME will feel no pain.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME lazes on beaches and islands, catching fish with its barbed tail. If disturbed, it furiously rampages, intent on destroying the one that interrupted its rest.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME possesses the power to move the earth through potent psychokinesis. It uses this power to reshape the ground into the perfect napping spot.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME aimlessly floats around the atmosphere, descending to dip its tail in the ocean to catch sea life to eat. It sometimes forgets to actually eat hooked creatures, instead carrying them high up into the air while attached to its tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME invades the dreams of others to consume them, its powers wreaking a bit of havoc on the mind. Those attacked by it wake up with their minds hazy and some of their memories missing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME possesses a slight cosmic power, able to levitate small objects. This uses a lot of energy, so it is mostly found resting and eating to recover its strength.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME harbors a deep grudge, but it can't remember against whom or why. As a result, it just floats around happily, blissfully unaware of its forgotten vendetta.
author: amiel997

entry: With six sweet-tipped tails, it's able to fish for food much more efficiently. Thanks to this feeding strategy, POKENAME can go days without leaving its fishing spot.
author: hophoppip

entry: It is primarily a sedentary species, as it does not move often. Whenever it gets hungry and needs to eat, it ejects its inner organs to hunt anything that comes nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It cannot fly more than a few inches off of the ground. While it hovers it will drag its tail across the ground, making a line in the dirt.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME senses happiness nearby, it secretes a pale film from its tail and ears. In Sinnoh, this rare substance is used in fine desserts.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's habit of lying by the sea for days, staring unblinkingly, gave rise to many theories about what it could be watching for. These theories were dashed when scientists proved that POKENAME simply forgets to close its eyes when sleeping.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME naps along riverbanks, its fur humming with static. The sparks grow stronger during storms and sometimes jolt it awake.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is considered a good beginner's aquatic pet due to being very low maintenance in both food and behavior. Many children find its vacant stare gazing back at them through a tank incredibly endearing.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a constant danger to itself. If the fire on its tail goes out it dies, but it constantly desires to try to go fishing with it. Trainers need have constant supervision over POKENAME, though thankfully it doesn't do anything quickly.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME spend most of the day sitting in the sunlight on beaches. The light helps them grow and sweetens the smell of their curled-up appendages.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME stares listlessly at the horizon while floating through the world. It gets caught in power lines because of its inattention and frequently needs help to get untangled.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When POKENAME tires of flying, it turns invisible and rests itself on the head of another creature. Those currently serving as POKENAME's perch feel their minds become clouded and find it difficult to think straight.
author: sk372

entry: The sweet white film POKENAME secretes is rumored to cause psychic visions when consumed in excess. No verified cases exist, but demand remains high among Psychics.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its weak psychic powers to navigate its surroundings. However, it takes a bit of time to locate things, so POKENAME has to fly incredibly slowly to avoid bumping into them.
author: mistymagius

entry: It catches aquatic Pokémon inside dark caves with its tail, which it flicks to draw attention to itself. Once it catches another Pokémon, it rapidly flaps its wings to pull its prey out of the water before dropping it onto a nearby rock.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME stumbles awkwardly while pursuing prey, dragging its tail behind. Though its jaws are strong, it is one of the least efficient hunters among Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Its herbivorous diet requires a special nutrient only seaweed can provide, which means it needs to dive underwater to have a complete diet. Whenever it needs to escape danger while seaweed gathering, it poisons the predator using its removable tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME moves with slow, clumsy steps and often falls behind the rhythm. Even so, it never gives up and dances with a joyful spirit from start to finish.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's oversized feather crown often falls over its eyes while dancing and causes it trip. To avoid stumbling, it sticks to slow and cautious steps.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's dance is extremely slow, appearing almost completely stationary at a glance. The true complexity of its dance can only be properly appreciated via time-lapse photography.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME often dances when no music is being played. Researchers believe its movements are so delayed that it's still reacting to music it heard days ago.
author: jaminmcready

entry: It swims effortlessly through the oceans of the world by using underwater currents to guide where it swims. At the same time, it has a slow reaction time, which causes it to bump into obstacles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefers the stumps found in foggy swamps over those of the forest, and often possesses them to sleep. It rolls in the puddles nearby to soak up water throughout the day.
author: .izik

entry: It dangles its many tails into the water to catch prey. It's not uncommon to see a POKENAME with several catches hanging from it.
author: holgast

entry: It prefers to rest in one spot because its seams rip easily. Yet, whenever its Trainer picks it up, it takes at least ten seconds before it realizes it has been moved.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Whenever a Trainer picks it up, it takes at least five seconds before it realizes it has been moved. Afterwards, it looks around for its tail to ensure it remains attached to its body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The spines across its tentacles help it defend against predators, as it injects venom into anything that comes too close. This offsets the fact that it takes a while to recognize that it is in danger.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has spines across each of its tentacles, each filled with a caustic, venomous liquid. When it is not lucid or otherwise entirely awake, it bunkers down by forming a shield with its tentacles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It barely ever moves from the beach as it patiently waits for fish and other sea creatures to wash up on shore. It uses the thorns on its hands to grab its slippery prey.
author: mistymagius

entry: On beaches, POKENAME attempts to hunt using psychic lures. However, it often forgets what it's doing and falls asleep mid-hunt.
author: .izik

entry: Mushrooms similar in appearance to Slowpoke tails grow on POKENAME's back. Consuming these mushrooms causes the eater to lose their memories of the last few hours.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME swims so slowly that its fins barely appear to move. It drifts calmly toward its destination without urgency.
author: .izik

entry: Many high-end restaurants pay top dollar to import fresh POKENAME tails. They are considered a delicacy with a distinct taste of mushrooms.
author: char_latte3412

entry: The white scale on POKENAME's head leaks a sticky sweet syrup. Pastry chefs across Hoenn harvest it monthly for elite confections.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often found in underwater lakes, fishing for small sea life with its tail. The blue spots on its body are actually patches of crystal that glint and glow in dark areas.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME guards pumpkin patches but reacts far too slowly. It tries to spray water at thieves but often misses them long after they've escaped.
author: .izik

entry: The Pecha Berry-scented fur of POKENAME is dangerously delicious. Those who eat it report feeling sluggish and drowsy for an entire day.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaves its tail poking just above the water, coated in a sweet scent. Curious bird Pokémon are lured close, then drained with Absorb.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME tries to whack others with its flaming tail in an effort to start a fight. Because it moves so slowly, it is pretty easy to move out of the way.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are too lazy to swim, so they end up washing up along the beach a lot. Because of its simple-minded nature, it will often follow other Pokémon.
author: mistymagius

entry: If POKENAME finds someone trapped in a cave, it attempts to help them escape. Its slow reactions often force the trapped individual to find their own way out.
author: .izik

entry: It is said that eating POKENAME's tail helps improve your brain health. It has immersive psychic capabilities, even though POKENAME has no idea it even has psychic powers.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its long tail makes catching prey easy, as the longer the tail the more force it can use to whisk prey from the water onto a nearby rock. It chooses the same few spots every day, as it has an inclination towards forming a daily schedule.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME dips its tail into the water to catch fish. Due to its lightweight body, it often gets dragged along by the caught fish, leaving it bobbing lazily atop the water's surface as it's carried away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have a perpetually bored expression that make them seem aloof and distant. Whenever they flare their nostrils in frustration, they release a pulse of psychic energy that encourages others to leave them alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a hard time not jumping into water despite the fact that it is usually too cold for it. When it finally acquiesces and jumps into water, the shock of the water causes it to get sick.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Oil seeps out from its tail constantly. Exposure to the air causes it to ignite almost instantly. Apparently the oil, if collected somehow, is very sweet to the taste.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Due to its small size and its voracious appetite for algae, people with home aquariums love to have it as a part of a large tank of fish. It floats around a tank and passively eats algae every moment it is awake.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is a popular pet for home aquariums because it is both friendly and helpful to have around. Whenever another Pokémon gets sick, it taps against the glass to get help and attention from its owners.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It lives in home aquariums or other large aquatic homes, and roams around the space to take care of the Pokémon that it lives with. Its gentle and soft demeanor allows it to easily make friends with the Pokémon that join its home.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME appear aloof to their Trainers because they constantly forget what they are doing. This short-term memory causes them to bump into other Pokémon while they are flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It fishes for aquatic Pokémon by luring prey close before yanking them out of the water with its long tail. When it catches a bite, it stuffs the morsel into its maw to digest in its large stomach.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tentacles ooze a sticky, tangy substance that stings the tongue. Rare allergic reactions cause hours of lethargy.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's psychic abilities have quadrupled thanks to fusion. Unfortunately, its intelligence has not had the same effect.
author: westerlytrack45

entry: POKENAME has mastered catching fish Pokémon with its tail, using small bursts of psychic power to aid in catching bigger prey. A shed tail from POKENAME is considered a luxury food item in many parts of the world because of its high protein.
author: chibitales

entry: Its intelligence has degraded to the point it has become sedentary and barely sentient. Fungi grow on its immobile body, which still radiates an instinctive psychic energy to defend itself from outside stimuli.
author: sk372

entry: Fusion has given POKENAME a marginal increase in intellect. Instead of using its tail, it now fashions crude fishing poles in order to fish up Shellder and other aquatic life to feed on.
author: sk372

entry: When territory disputes arise, POKENAME forgets about it mid-argument. Most disputes end with both sides asleep near ponds, the quarrel unresolved.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's skin has very few pain receptors, so it very rarely feels pain. During the colder months, POKENAME won't even notice its own body starting to freeze over.
author: mistymagius

entry: To sleep, POKENAME almost completely buries itself in the snowfall, leaving only part of its face exposed to breathe. Despite its perpetually sleepy demeanor, it is very skilled at using its Water-type Moves to defend itself.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is used by some to remove Poison Pokémon from lakes, as POKENAME's goopy tail has a taste those types find irresistible. POKENAME doesn't feel the bites, so it's simply happy to be helpful.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME oozes about aimlessly, it forms itself into a variety of shapes and sizes. This is because it easily forgets what it's supposed to look like, reshaping based on faulty memories.
author: sk372

entry: It drags its shell behind it as it crawls around to find grass or berries to eat, as it can no longer fish with its tail. It struggles to move around because its large shell covers both of its hind legs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attempts to hypnotize others by swinging its pendulum in front of them. Unfortunately, its simple mind causes it to often get distracted by its own swinging, hypnotizing itself instead.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's pincers can move surprisingly quickly, snapping onto potential prey and gripping tightly. It often forgets why it grabbed something, however, and releases most of its meals back into the wild.
author: sk372

entry: Its claws will easily break off if it's not careful. The white portions ooze a frosting-like substance that is incredibly sweet.
author: .izik

entry: The top of its shell rises upwards and forms a hole on top, causing it to resemble an onion. It can eject water from that hole like a geyser.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME squirts water into the eyes of a predator before hiding in its shell. In a pinch, it can also squirt a burst of water to propel itself away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are drawn to make their homes in hydroelectric power plants. Their presence is problematic for the engineers working there as they are prone to exploding when disturbed, risking damage to the sensitive equipment.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are drawn to make their homes in hydroelectric power plants. Their presence is problematic for the engineers working there as they are prone to exploding when disturbed, risking damage to the sensitive equipment.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME swim after other aquatic Pokémon at surprising speed using the wings poking out of their shell, exploding once they catch them. Some game developers have observed this behaviour and taken inspiration from them for enemies in their games.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The skull on POKENAME's head has been covered with fur, making it solid enough to protect it from blows. In a way, the skull has become part of its body.
author: 0reomilka

entry: POKENAME no longer needs a shell, having developed the ability to hide within its skull instead. This adaptation often leads people to mistake it for nothing more than a discarded skull.
author: 0reomilka

entry: POKENAME blows bubbles and then kicks them at foes to create hazardous projectiles around the battlefield. When not fighting or training, it takes meticulous care of its flowing mane of hair, which is a mark of prestige among the species.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME trains by launching a beam of robust bubbles to bounce off of surrounding surfaces, then dodging, blocking, or punching the bubbles. Its tough shell has covered it in fights, allowing it to safely punch opponents made of hazardous materials.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME keep their external shells hardened at all times to protect their sensitive bodies without restricting their movement. They tuck their bodies into their shells to hide from predators, propelling themselves with water to escape.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: It uses its diamond-hard horn to drill through the rock faces behind waterfalls, carving out its den. Thanks to the thick shell protecting its body, it has developed a fighting style focused far more on defense than offense.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The colors of their fur-clad fins become more vibrant with age. By combining the hardness of its shell with the sharpness of its horn, a POKENAME can easily break through hard obstacles in its way within streams and rivers.
author: infinex21

entry: A swarm of POKENAME made its home on Wayfarer Island years ago due to the high quantity of Oran Berries growing there. POKENAME cleans the berries thoroughly with gentle bubbles from its mouth before eating them.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often harassed by Flying-type Pokémon who are looking for an easy bite. To avoid becoming another meal, POKENAME kick up sand into the eyes of Flying-type Pokémon to scare them away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Ancient legends surrounding POKENAME suggest that they fell from the stars, landing in the ocean and making their new home there. The winged gem at their core was used as evidence of this, suggested as their means of flight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME creates whirlpools made of scalding water to deter any opponents. It lays its eggs deep within thermal pools.
author: dodoowner_

entry: When POKENAME hides underwater, its fur sticking out looks like seafoam. The oldest recorded POKENAME was 893 years old.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME relies on its water squirting abilities to scare away predators. It can shoot bursts of water to hit branches above itself, which startles bird Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are capable of crossing an entire ocean without rest, making them reliable creatures when people need to ferry goods across water. They are known for their amiable nature and superb diligence.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME blend seamlessly into water as soon as they make contact, allowing them to sneak up on prey. POKENAME rely on their fluffy ears and soft tail to make sharp turns as they close the distance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME white mane is made of super-hot water vapor that will cause second-degree burns on contact. Its delicate ears are able to sense differences in air pressure and humidity.
author: mistymagius

entry: After years of boiling water inside its shell, steam has enveloped POKENAME's ears and tails completely. The steam also surrounds the Pokémon's neck, forming a mane-like cloud.
author: lemage22

entry: Before consuming hardware, POKENAME sprays it with concentrated water. The moisture ruins the device for humans but makes it more palatable to POKENAME.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are too big for the cocoon that surrounds itself, so its ears and tail remain on the outside of the shell. Despite this, the bursts of water that come out of the shell's crevices stop predators from consuming it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fossils are found on mountaintops, as the strata that they are found in date back over 500 million years. Modern instances of the fusion have barely changed from these fossils, living in oceans and relying on their shells to keep them safe.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is known for rescuing people who are drowning at sea, and spotting one is said to be a sign of good luck. Despite having powerful wings, it prefers to move swiftly through the water rather than fly.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is known for rescuing people who are drowning at sea, and spotting one is said to be a sign of good luck. Despite having powerful wings, it prefers to move swiftly through the water rather than fly.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can both inject venom at close range and spray venom from a distance. Its body is covered with a thin carapace that protects itself from attacks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is highly territorial and aggressive. With multiple stingers as sharp as steel, many run in fear at the sight of one.
author: mepp.

entry: These elusive Pokémon are seen as symbols of health and longevity in many cultures. Their fur sheds as they move swiftly along the water's surface, these hairs being used in many medicines and remedies.
author: santon5512

entry: When POKENAME feels relaxed, it emits hot steam from its fluffy neck. The steam is said to have therapeutic effects, so some spas use it for their sauna.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME sits along riverbanks, hiding in tall stalks of grass, and stalking unsuspecting Pokémon. When it has locked onto a target, it launches itself forward in the water and bites down on the prey with its sharp fangs.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME soars through forests in search of soft berries to consume. They gather and spray these berries with water until they turn into an edible mush.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME bobbles its head back and forth every second to keep track of time. It shoots bursts of water at anything that tries to stop this bobble.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has a peculiar tic that causes it to nod every second because of its ability to keep track of time. This does not stop it from being a major predator for aquatic Pokémon that live in lakes and rivers.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's large tail helps it swim through the water more quickly and agilely. It weaves underwater webs in rivers that catch fish that it will later drag out to consume.
author: sk372

entry: What appears to be a tail is actually condensed silk. POKENAME swings it about to catch bugs and even fish beneath the water before detaching the tail and spinning a new one while it feasts on its meals.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME flocks to lakes and rivers for the opportunity to find prey. It can eat fish or bug Pokémon, both of which are plentiful in the world's many lakes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is easily excitable and may accidentally shock other Trainers or Pokémon. After this happens, it hides in its shell and curls its tail around itself in shame.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME perches on stones near rocky beaches. They gather in groups on the night of a shooting star before retreating back to the ocean or underwater caves.
author: dyanz0

entry: POKENAME can fly through tropical storms thanks to its sturdy carapace and its strong wings. It has been observed helping people during these storms by escorting them back to shelter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When planting its feet, POKENAME is able to withstand the force of a tsunami raining down on it. Team Aqua have a particular fondness for it and often refer to this fact in analogies about how natural life will survive their plans.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME swims just below a pond's surface, with its ears barely visible above. It uses this stealthy approach to avoid predators.
author: .izik

entry: Rarely found with others of its evolutionary line, POKENAME ventures toward the poles to seek colder water. There it learns to survive alone, pushing its endurance. Once ready, it evolves and returns to its colony.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Perhaps due to its apparently slow metabolism, POKENAME is considerably docile and slow-paced; perhaps its dense shell contributes to its slow pace, though. It is sensitive, or prideful, of its tail and does not like when anyone touches it.
author: infinex21

entry: Said to live for upwards of 10,000 years, POKENAME's fur is so sensitive it can detect the slightest change in the weather. They release water with mind-altering properties that can be used in teas and elixirs.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: Bathed in moonlight, POKENAME's Water-type moves grow stronger than usual. When it grows fond of its Trainer, it shields them from any threat with its shell.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's bulb is known to work like a geyser. Other Pokémon are known to run under it, like a sprinkler on a summer day.
author: dodoowner_

entry: While underwater, the hairs of a POKENAME lock together to form a hydrophobic layer that repels water. Whenever POKENAME surfaces, these hairs break surface tension, causing its fur to get wet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wings emit a gentle glow as it glides through the skies. It channels its psychic energy to protect those it deems worthy.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME will usually be found going down rivers and even waterfalls. It is rare to see POKENAME hanging on trees since they are very eager to ride the river.
author: fireflower20002

entry: POKENAME lacks the ability to create burrows of its own, so it finds those made by Diglett and floods them, flushing out the current residents, then happily swims into its new home.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: As soon as the wind rises, it glides over its river to ensure everything is in order. When fighting, POKENAME grabs the opponent with its claws so they cannot avoid its powerful water jets.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME can be found swimming in ponds full of fish Pokémon or near the burrows of Bug Pokémon. Whenever they are threatened, they spray jets of water from their beaks to scare away predators.
author: quackquackattack

entry: From its metal-hard claws, POKENAME shoots high-pressure jets of water capable of piercing even the walls of a building. It moves its wings so quickly that it can even fight above the water's surface for a few moments.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Even among other Sneasel fusions, POKENAME is known to be especially vain. It spends hours gazing at its reflection in the water.
author: volvonovic

entry: POKENAME is an incredibly vain Pokémon, using its razor-sharp claws to meticulously groom its sleek fur and shell. It often gazes at its reflection in water, admiring its own appearance for hours.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME coats the inside of its shell with honey, retracting into its shell whenever it's hungry. It will purposely spit honey at opponents to slow them down.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME can be found in the waters surrounding volcanic islands, clustering around magma vents. Their populations are monitored by vulcanologists; a sudden increase in their presence is an early warning sign for volcanic eruptions.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME fly through forests to stalk bug Pokémon in the hopes of finding their burrows. Once they find enough burrows, they spray water inside so their prey escapes right into their beaks.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It shoots high-pressure water that can cut through hard steel. They roam the seas, seeking someone it deems worthy of its strength.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME give the gift of snow to children who live in hot climates. The many memories of snowball fights they have created more than makes up for the mess, but they help sweep up the snow with their tails after playing regardless.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When they are hunting, POKENAME ram their shell-covered heads against prey to stun them before sinking their fangs in. Afterwards, they delicately clean their fluffy tails.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME variably retracts its head and limbs into its shell as it continues to spin, making it difficult for opponents to judge where the next attack will come from. Trainers should buff and shine its shell as a form of bonding.
author: pjporwoll

entry: If someone pulls away from POKENAME tender kisses, it gets so offended that it summons storm clouds to make it rain. To impress other Pokémon, it meticulously cares for its pure white hair, washing its hair at least three times a day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Its heavy shell grounds its upper body in place. Then it mesmerizes opposing Pokémon by undulating its tail like a wave in a storm.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME likes to dive to the bottom of thermal pools, just for fun. It will splash scalding water whenever it is annoyed.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME produce a liter of milk daily that they offer to local Pokémon in their natural habitat. Many baby Pokémon approach POKENAME to drink the milk, especially if they have been orphaned.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love to swim in lakes and rivers but are incredibly skittish. If they realize they are being watched by a Trainer, they bolt away by creating a surge of sparks in the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's tail fur darkens as electricity is stored in its body. Trainers often use this quirk as an indicator of when this Pokémon needs to discharge. In water, it sends out small electrical pulses to search for prey.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME search for clay deposits underground using their keen sense of smell. They water down the clay until it is a thick slurry that they can lap up.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Found within damp caves, POKENAME uses water and its wings to carve out a nest. Large colonies of POKENAME create vast caves to inhabit.
author: northkira

entry: POKENAME's tail contains all its program data and its ability to live on for thousands of years. As it ages, this tail gathers more and more data until it grows so absurdly large that it can't fit inside houses anymore.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME dedicate themselves to being leaders of their bales as the seasons change. Taking the front and back of their travelling group, these Pokémon ensure that everyone stays together while voyaging to warmer waters.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME dig underground to find clay deposits to eat. They often have clay stuck to their body after eating, so they take turns with other POKENAME to wash their bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's powerful legs let them propel themselves through the water at high speeds, their fluffy tails and feathers allowing for more precise movements. Their claws are incredibly powerful, able to crack open the shells of other Pokémon.
author: santon5512

entry: The feathers that make up POKENAME's tail are super soft and well-maintained, so they are highly sought after by craftsmen. Pillows and clothes that use POKENAME's feathers are extremely popular online.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME spray jets of water from their mouths at foes. The hairs along their tails stand on end when they sense danger, giving them ample time to retreat into their shells.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME diligently keep their tails clean, tucking them into their shells when in the mud. When approached by predators, they will bang on their stomachs to try to scare them off.
author: santon5512

entry: As POKENAME ages, the mist they produce covers wider areas. This mist has a calming effect that can diffuse even the most heated or violent arguments.
author: lampent12

entry: POKENAME are often found defending underwater ruins, manipulating the tides to keep invaders at bay. The wings on their heads grow larger the older they get, their hairs becoming richer.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME shoots down cocoons that hang in trees with jets of water. The water is mixed with a poisonous gel that eats through silk, which causes cocoons to fall to the ground and become its next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME change most of their colors to blend in under or near water, save for the patterns on their shells. It is said that the longer their furry tails are, the longer they have lived.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are prudent creatures that have special wooden plates that they add to their shell for more protection. They carve these plates out of wood that age alongside a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When angered, POKENAME's horn releases a strong torrent of tainted water. This water is horribly poisonous, and can prove dangerous even with simple contact with skin.
author: robbery_666

entry: Despite their size, POKENAME are excellent swimmers. The plant on its back is always hydrated, and thus it's impossible for it to wilt.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME stands between its younger nestmates and predators, relying on its shell to block attacks. It remains between its siblings and the predator until the predator leaves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often seen cleaning and maintaining their fur. They do not usually engage in battle unless their fur has been "attacked" by the opponent.
author: mossybanana

entry: POKENAME are picky about their environment, often being seen using their wings to sweep away dirt and debris. Some tavern owners keep the Pokémon around to help keep high-traffic areas tidy.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME remains close to the nest to keep watch over their nestmates. They spray a coat of corrosive gel over younger nestmates to make them easier to track if they get lost.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME were once hunted because fishermen were scared that POKENAME would eat the rest of the aquatic Pokémon in an area. Their sheer size could feed people for weeks, but there are now laws against hunting them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The magnificent fur on POKENAME's crest and gate deepen in color as it ages. Those with deep-colored fur and many battle scars are seen as more favorable for potential mates.
author: chibitales

entry: It's seen lazing around on the ocean floor. Its back is home to many Pokémon, as weak Pokémon feel protected with it around.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Infighting among POKENAME groups is common as they battle to establish hierarchy. The more scars upon a POKENAME's shell, the more respect it commands among the tribe.
author: sk372

entry: It pins its opponent's arms and legs down with globs of adhesive fluid. It then beats them down with a barrage of punches and kicks.
author: themicelegion

entry: They are very self-conscious about their fluffy tails and take care to keep them from getting mucked up or damaged during battle. A POKENAME grows increasingly prideful the longer and thicker its tail fur grows.
author: infinex21

entry: The older a POKENAME, the more dignified and prideful it will act, especially regarding its fluffy, vibrant tail. If its tail is ever harmed or even made the tiniest bit dirty, it flies into a pride-fueled rage that ends with it sulking once tired.
author: infinex21

entry: The hue of this Pokémon deepens or lightens depending on how much the ocean roars, while its cloud-like tail and ears detect how dangerous an aquatic environment is.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME is an elegant blade that twirls and spins in combat. It enjoys dueling tough-looking opponents.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME's fluffy handles give it stability and balance while its two blades conjointly attack enemies. Its grand and elegant attack methods and appearance make even expert swordsmen jealous of it.
author: soup1900

entry: According to old seafaring legends, POKENAME has served history's most renowned pirate captains across the ages. After every duel, it polishes its shell-shaped shield in saltwater.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is fiercely protective of its fabulous tail. According to an old Hisuian proverb, to 'have a POKENAME by the tail' is to enjoy great luck before inevitable disaster.
author: mogor0771

entry: It uses its tail in water to act as a rudder and its ears to detect the directions of currents.
author: melodydelune

entry: In springtime, newly evolved POKENAME leave home in search of a waterfall to call their own. Because there are a limited number to go around, territorial clashes are loud and frequent.
author: mogor0771

entry: POKENAME only cause nightmares to fishermen who disturb them in their natural habitat. They tend to leave chunks of fluffy hair around a fisherman's home afterward, which is seen as a bad omen.
author: hereisanimations

entry: POKENAME are most active during the full moon because they want to absorb moonlight. They get excited during the night of the full moon, so much so that they shoot a beautiful display of sparkling water into the air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The older POKENAME gets, the darker its six tails become. It can also wind and release them while swimming to get a little boost.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME floats on the ocean by filling its shell with air. It uses its tail and ear plumes as sails. It lacks enough power to swim on its own, so it follows the winds.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: Each head is protected by its own sturdy shell. When a POKENAME gets mad, it violently headbutts anything nearby, including its other head.
author: soreile.arc

entry: POKENAME is said to be able to live for several thousand years. For this reason, it symbolizes health and is a popular motif for coats of arms.
author: chorb33

entry: Its tail deepens in color as it ages and its shell grows heavier as it nears its evolution. It seems to enjoy seeing how far it can propel objects into the air with jets of water.
author: infinex21

entry: It's hard for POKENAME to walk due to its big head. POKENAME are great companions, as they will protect their Trainer no matter the cost.
author: imagine1.

entry: The fur on POKENAME's tails is incredibly soft and is often harvested to make high-quality clothing. The older POKENAME grow, the finer the quality of their tails becomes.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME wipes its bulb with its fluffy tail to remove excess pollen. The pollen that sticks to its tail irritates people's eyes, but a simple Bubble Beam from POKENAME can wash it out.
author: hereisanimations

entry: POKENAME create elaborate and delicate bubble structures reminiscent of flowers surrounding their hands. Pokémon researchers believe that these structures are used as a means to woo potential mates.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are surrounded by a thick gel that allows them to breathe underwater. By creating small ripples across their body at a thousand times a second, they can swiftly swim across bodies of water without disturbing the water's surface.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME likes to fire jets of dirty water from its mouth, but only when it is in an unfamiliar, clean environment. These Pokémon seem to have a fascination with automobiles.
author: beatdoof

entry: As these Pokémon grow older, the colors of their furs grow deeper and the furs themselves grow thicker. They use their tusks to mark their territory by cutting into stones and trees.
author: infinex21

entry: Upon their tails are soft tufts of fur that grow longer and more vibrant as they age. Although normally calm, they become aggressive if their tufts are touched; these tufts are not connected to their nervous systems, however.
author: infinex21

entry: The colors of their feathers deepen with age. Their shells grow hotter as they battle, yet the plates of these shells remain unaffected by the heat. POKENAME shells, and their shells' plates, are used in many crafts.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's wings flap with surprising force for a sea creature, launching it just above the waves. It uses its sharp fangs to slice through plastic and seaweed entanglements, clearing the path for others.
author: jaminmcready

entry: Scientists recently revitalized POKENAME from a fossil of its shell found on the seafloor. From its enormous jaws, it can blow out vast quantities of bubbles or saltwater.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is often used as a mascot in advertising campaigns promoting cereals or sweets for children. Scientists recently revitalized it from a fossil of its shell found on the seafloor.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are spotted gracefully floating through rainstorms, their presence said to bring longevity to those who witness them. By twirling their umbrellas, they can cloak their bodies in an icy mist before disappearing.
author: santon5512

entry: The ears on POKENAME can hear more clearly underwater than on land. This helps it when avoiding predators while swimming.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's long, furry tail is often used as a symbol of longevity in dance-related literature. The bubbles it releases while dancing burn to the touch, though other POKENAME are unaffected by this burn.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME inhabits caverns in coastal areas, coming out during the night to hunt. Its can seamlessly dive from the air into the water without losing speed, taking unsuspecting prey just below the surface by surprise.
author: sk372

entry: The colors of its wings and tail deepen with age and are said to feel softer than any other material known. POKENAME communicates with various songs that, in tandem with its soft plumage, have led it to be desired by many people.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's shell helmet serves as extra protection, so it gets upset when shell collectors attempt to take it. The age of a POKENAME is indicated by the amount of algae growing on its shell.
author: robbery_666

entry: The growths on the back of POKENAME siphon nutrients for added bulk to protect them from predators. They require lots of fresh water to maintain the bulbs on their back, so they often go swimming to soak the growths with water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME hide in amongst aquatic plants, keeping themselves concealed from predators whilst watching for any prey that might come close. They use the thick fur of their tails to trap air bubbles, helping them stay submerged for longer periods.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hide in amongst aquatic plants, keeping themselves concealed from predators whilst watching for any prey that might come close. They use the thick fur of their tails to trap air bubbles, helping them stay submerged for longer periods.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Each section of their shells produces a slightly different note when hit; the sound of POKENAME training via tackles releases chords of noise. Supposedly, they have a delicious flavor if steamed, but due to their rarity, hunting them is illegal.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The giant shell of POKENAME is surprisingly thin and hollow. This provides just enough protection from behind while also being very lightweight.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME stores multiple twigs in its tail, and when bored, pulls one out to blow foam bubbles. When challenged, it heats its Water Guns to boiling, burning threats to distract them before escaping into the waves.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME are excellent fighters, even underwater. They are able to protect their flames inside their shell to ensure they always stay burning.
author: imagine1.

entry: Soil displaced by POKENAME is left rich with moisture and nutrients. Plants growing there sprout at nearly twice their normal rate.
author: .izik

entry: Soil churned by POKENAME remains heavily hydrated. Constant moisture seeps from its body as it moves underground.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME scuttles around nimbly on its four stubby legs. If threatened, it balances on its shell and spins around, scattering hair from its antennae. The fine hair acts as an irritant, deterring predators.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Its fluffy tail is considered a symbol of childlike whimsy and a sign for a happy future. Although charms modeled after its tail are sold, ones made of actual POKENAME fur sell for exorbitant prices in underground circles.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME needs to remain well hydrated or else they get powerful headaches. They tend to lash out whenever they are thirsty, so Trainers are advised to pack lots of water bottles to keep them calm.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have sensitive whiskers that can detect earthquakes from a long distance. Whenever they pick up on seismic activity, they float to the surface of their swampy homes to minimize the chance of being entombed in mud.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have many flippers that all work in unison to swiftly maneuver through the water. When one of their flippers is damaged, they have to rest on shore until it heals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a difficult time swimming because of their rotund bodies, so they float on the water instead. If they are knocked off course, they have a difficult time steering themselves back to land, leaving them stuck out at sea.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be found living off coastal shores where they live without many predators to threaten them. They enjoy eating seaweed and participating in casual races against each other, often reaching nearly 18 miles per hour.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a rather short-tempered creature that constantly seeks to annoy other Pokémon just to have an excuse to start a fight. If defeated, it hides in a river's water until it no longer feels embarrassed.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME practices putting out fires so that it can someday help firefighters. It can quickly find the source of a fire to snuff it out.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can be seen training at fire academies learning how to help firefighters. They can rush into burning buildings to pull people and Pokémon out safely.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's wings are coated in a special liquid that allows them to be used underwater. Its shell can heat up to 144 ⁰F.
author: imagine1.

entry: It developed a more serious attitude after evolving. Like its previous form, it can skip along water by shooting water at its shell but does so only when necessary.
author: frokachu

entry: Its shell has a large empty area for its tail to go into. It can launch itself by spinning its tail like a propeller.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME is rather touchy about the swirling bit of chest fluff on its torso, grooming it often. Unless it gives permission, anyone reaching to touch it will get a swift punch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME help children get acclimated to swimming. Their mindreading abilities allow them to detect when children are scared or struggling and help accordingly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are hired as lifeguards because they are sensitive to the thoughts of someone in distress. Their superb swimming skills allow them to quickly reach drowning children.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The helmet on POKENAME's head resembles a helmet seen in an ancient humanoid fossil. It grants POKENAME immense speed and agility.
author: lam0u3tt3

entry: Originally thought to have been smaller, more energetic Wartortle, studies on POKENAME's tails have determined that the fur hasn't fully developed. They occasionally struggle to fit into their shells as their bodies grow with their evolution.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME are cautious creatures that hide in their shell when they are not eating. They live near hot springs where they soak up minerals from the hot water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live close to hot springs and enjoy absorbing minerals from the water. This water helps keep their bodies smooth and clean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME retreats into its spherical shell and rolls down mountain slopes to travel quickly. Once it gets rolling, it will be unable to stop itself without crashing into something solid.
author: fancyskunk

entry: Many cloudy days have probably been caused by a POKENAME. When it turns serious, it sometimes runs across fields and releases clouds into the sky.
author: 0reomilka

entry: Its seaweed-like tail has grown due to the excess energy in its body. The water expelled from the tail gives insight into POKENAME's inner workings.
author: thehatster

entry: The shells of each of its component heads are magnetically locked with one another, leaving them virtually inseparable. POKENAME uses its three fluffy tails to help steer itself as it floats along electromagnetic waves.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME produce streams of water through the baton that they carry with them. Many florists rely on their help to water plants, as POKENAME can adjust how water is produced from their baton.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its two heads are always highly cooperative, allowing POKENAME to coordinate its aquatic attacks very effectively. It feeds on whatever it manages to catch in rivers, which is why it usually nests near water teeming with life.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME build up layers of insulating fat within their shell to help protect them from the cold of their arctic homes. Their shells are smooth on their stomachs, allowing them to slide freely across ice at surprisingly high speeds.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses its magnificent white tail to sweep away ice as it swims through freezing waters. A tenacious Pokémon, it faces every battle bravely, skillfully unleashing its Water-type attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are made of a caustic ooze that eats away at sticky substances. Pokémon that are resistant to the caustic ooze give POKENAME berries in exchange for cleaning their bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are used by many police officers around Kanto. They are very tough and loyal, so it's the perfect choice for many Trainers.
author: imagine1.

entry: POKENAME is a deft swimmer able to turn its body transparent while underwater. Doing this, it hides away until an unfortunate victim swims by, whereupon it manifests itself right in front of them with a bloodcurdling shriek.
author: sk372

entry: The rocks that make up POKENAME's body are porous in structure, allowing them to store large amounts of water. It is more commonly found swimming in waterlogged cave systems.
author: mistymagius

entry: Kanto researchers theorize this Pokémon may have existed in ancient times. Ancient research journals provide info on POKENAME, possibly from before fusion technology.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: Using a Slowpoke Tail with a Shellder attached as a club is POKENAME's primary method of self-defense. Sometimes a POKENAME will remove its own tail to arm itself, seemingly unaware of any pain or discomfort the process causes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fishes for food by unfurling its sticky tongue in a river and waiting for prey to swim into it. It uses the Shellder latched onto its tail as an anchor, so it doesn't drift away with the current.
author: anonymous_moose

entry: Its lower body has a mess of grey tentacles around it, which both keep it safe and gather food for it. The only thing it needs to do is bask in the sunlight every so often to regenerate vines when damaged.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have trouble flying due to the weight of the shell on its tail. It is primarily active in the mornings, when it consumes flowers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gain psychic powers when the shell on their back bites down on their back. Their telekinetic abilities allow them to lift and throw large boulders with expert precision.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gain a jolt of psychic energy whenever the shell on their back bites them. This causes them to accidentally fling whatever they are carrying with telekinesis.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The crown atop its head is said to channel the dancing around it to bring the succor of a misty rain. It wiggles its hips in a slow rhythmic dance after a rainy season, as if building power for the next rain dance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: A very famous painting in a Kalos museum depicts this beautiful Pokémon. POKENAME can cross the seas by using its large Shellder as a surf board.
author: cobalt0135

entry: A very famous painting in a Kalos museum depicts this beautiful Pokémon. POKENAME can cross the seas by using its large Shellder as a surf board.
author: cobalt0135

entry: Though it appears large and imposing, POKENAME is one of the most docile Pokémon to own, ignorant of its own appearance. Some wild POKENAME have even been seen frightened by their own reflection on water surfaces.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's tender tail has been eaten by the Shellder that is now latched onto its back as armor, forming this symbiotic relationship. It can often be witnessed vocalizing to the Shellder, even though it never receives a response.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lives on the ocean floor, avoiding battles whenever possible. The shell it carries on its head so casually is actually another Pokémon trying to eat it, but since it doesn't realize that, it believes the shell just wants to protect it.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The Shellder biting down on POKENAME's head seems to cause it mild discomfort. It can sometimes be seen attempting to pry it off, but to no avail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME experience hunger pangs whenever the shell at their tail bites down and causes them to crave Lansat Berries. The resulting burst of energy gives them the focus to groom themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The Shellder attached to it leeches some of its immense energy, causing its senses to dull and the Shellder to grow greater. Despite this, POKENAME seems to care for the Shellder.
author: infinex21

entry: The Shellder on POKENAME's tail possesses wings strong enough to lift its entire body despite their size. POKENAME dangles limply and vacantly as the Shellder transports it through the air.
author: sk372

entry: The Shellder biting its tail leeched psychic energy from the host, growing more intelligent. Now smarter than the host, it bites specific nerves to force physical responses and make it more formidable in battle.
author: sk372

entry: If a Shellder clamps onto the back of this Pokémon, POKENAME lets loose a surprised flame, often scorching its new-found companion.
author: char_latte3412

entry: A strange poisonous Shellder is attached to POKENAME's lower half. This gives it a venomous bite, but POKENAME often forgets it even has fangs to begin with, accidentally biting its tongue and causing it to swell.
author: sk372

entry: When attacking, POKENAME uses the weight of the Shellder on its tail to drop quickly and heavily from the sky. However, its four wings struggle to lift its heavy body back off the ground afterward.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has very low brain activity, sometimes shocking itself on accident. It doesn't seem to be aware of the creature nibbling on its ear.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME is heavily encumbered by the shell on its rear, rendering it incapable of reaching speeds even close to Mach 2. It seems unfazed, however.
author: char_latte3412

entry: It dances extremely slowly during the late evenings. However, it will dance slightly faster if a group of eleven or more is watching it.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME will make their homes in shells along the shore, sleeping in them for hours. The tide will often drag these shells back out into the ocean, typically leading to this Pokémon's demise.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME is very simple-minded as it loves the noise of its Shellder smashing into things. Even if the Shellder tries to bite harder to get it to stop, it doesn't seem to deter POKENAME.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME collects moss and mud to cover the shell on its tail. It uses it as a pillow, spending most of the day asleep. It is considered bad luck to wake a sleeping POKENAME.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Contrary to popular belief, POKENAME's brain functions at super relativistic speeds, allowing it to outthink foes. Unfortunately, its body cannot keep up, causing it to use Sand Attack minutes too late.
author: ghostslythe

entry: With not a thought in its mind, POKENAME still possesses remarkable psychic energy. As means of attack, POKENAME shoots their tail like a torpedo and directs it using its powers.
author: teatedtiten

entry: It occasionally nibbles on its donut-like tail, though does not consume anything.  Because of this, professors are stumped as to how it gains nutrients.
author: teatedtiten

entry: When a POKENAME loses its Shellder, it retains only a fraction of its great intelligence. Even so, it is far smarter than most other Pokémon.
author: staghorn

entry: It habitually gnaws on objects within reach, out of nothing more than simple curiosity. POKENAME even gnaws the Shellder on their tail, though this is discouraged as the hard shell damages their teeth.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is a symbiotic relationship where the mammal provides sustenance while the shellfish provides protection. POKENAME numbs the excruciating pain of the shellfish's teeth with its psychic powers.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Slowpoke's body is almost entirely protected by an incredibly large and sturdy Shellder, giving it great defenses. It has rather low mobility though, so it rarely moves far from its home territory.
author: sk372

entry: Its abdomen stores the nutrients the attached Shellder uses for survival. Its claws look like Slowpoke's face, which distracts the opponents.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME flames have a numbing property, making them dangerous to handle since trainers often aren't aware they're being burned until it's too late. They are sometimes used during medical procedures when cauterisation is required.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME flames have a numbing property, making them dangerous to handle since trainers often aren't aware they're being burned until it's too late. They are sometimes used during medical procedures when cauterisation is required.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its tail has a mind of its own, biting POKENAME's tail to change its direction. It often feasts on Goldeen and Lotad.
author: schwaus

entry: POKENAME has edible tentacles that grow back over time, which are harvested every year during the autumn season. They are mixed into balls of batter to form takoyaki, which are sold during autumn festivals.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME gains the confidence and rage to charge and roll over foes once the Shellder covering it bites down. Its large tusks are the result of Shellder poison mutating and accelerating the growth of its back teeth.
author: soup1900

entry: The Shellder attached to a POKENAME's lower body increases its balance and motor skills so drastically that scientists speculate which of the two is actually in charge. Swimming POKENAME have been mistaken for mermaids in the past.
author: sontyp

entry: POKENAME has a Shellder attached to its tail, which clamps down on occasion. When this happens, it flares its hood, inducing a flurry of dull thoughts in onlookers that confuses them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is not recommended to drink POKENAME's milk. It is so rich in calcium that it can cause calcification of the human body, and eventually paralysis of the muscles.
author: musicsheep.

entry: POKENAME flails its tails around with reckless abandon, sometimes causing one of its Shellders to be flung off. When this happens, it will dip its tail in the water and patiently wait for another to bite on.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stand atop frozen lakes to act as their guardians year round. Unfortunately, they don't seem to realize that the ice melts in the spring, causing them to sink into the water.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Some Slowpoke are so sedate, vines grow on them. Their body still reacts in the same way when a Shellder bites their tail, turning them into POKENAME.
author: staghorn

entry: Shellder has ingrained itself in POKENAME's DNA and can no longer fall off. Its consciousness has split itself between POKENAME's claws and tail. The tail is not considered delicious by connoisseurs.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's mind has become almost empty of coherent thought due to its glitched nature. On rare occasions, the two bodies may swap heads, leading to the appearance of Slowpoke biting Porygon-Z's tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's disjointed body leaves it able to kick its own head at distant opponents in battle. Despite the potential for causing concussions, POKENAME seems unfazed by its cranium being used as a projectile.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are almost always confused, due to its lack of sight and underwhelming intelligence. They will often fall into rivers and groups of POKENAME can be seen floating downstream.
author: mistymagius

entry: The shell on POKENAME's lower half weighs it down, so it uses telekinesis to move itself. It has a dim mind and vapid personality, but if its Trainer is in danger, it can show a remarkably sudden burst of intelligence as it comes to their aid.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's shell is extremely sturdy, reflecting most projectiles thrown at it. However, a light tap to POKENAME's unprotected flesh may cause it to faint.
author: dodoowner_

entry: It survives solely through photosynthesis, resulting in many flowers and vines adorning its tail. It seems to enjoy this existence and rarely moves.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME prefers to rest on the edge of sunny shorelines. The Shellder ensures POKENAME can use neurotoxins to attack foes.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are exceptionally lazy Pokémon that will sleep for weeks on end before waking to gorge themselves, then going back to sleep. Despite their laziness they have an immense temper if disturbed and are incredibly strong.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are exceptionally lazy Pokémon that will sleep for weeks on end before waking to gorge themselves, then going back to sleep. Despite their laziness they have an immense temper if disturbed and are incredibly strong.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Both POKENAME's nose and shell try to point towards magnetic north, causing POKENAME to spin. It sleeps in lakes where natural magnetism is strong.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME emits a strong magnetic force from the Shellder on its face. It uses this force to carry pieces of Slowpoke tails that have broken off, which it plans to fish with, but they regularly get stolen by carnivorous Pokémon.
author: jangodiot

entry: When a Shellder bit down on this Pokémon's sheath, it rapidly evolved to encompass it. It now likes to occasionally bite POKENAME's hilt, but POKENAME doesn't seem to mind.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: POKENAME's twin blades lack coordination, and do not appear to share the same mind. One fights with precision and calculated defense, while the other lazily swings itself around in random directions, or hardly moves at all.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can generate watery wings that allow it to fly. While high in the sky, it dives and uses the Shellder attached to its tail as a flail.
author: ._term.

entry: Though usually slow, if the Shellder on POKENAME's tail bites down they will gain a burst of adrenaline to act faster than normal.
author: melodydelune

entry: The shells on POKENAME's body appear to be slightly too tight for its body, causing discomfort that its dim brain doesn't quite understand. This causes it to angrily lash out indiscriminately at others, making it highly dangerous.
author: sk372

entry: Wild POKENAME hide in their shells along seashores, pouncing upon any prey that walk by and wrapping them in electrified nets. With their prey secured, they will slink back within their shells to enjoy their meal.
author: infinex21

entry: It is covered in a slime that keeps itself moist, which also functions as a sunscreen to prevent burns. Whenever the shell attached to its body bites down, it instinctively expands its innards to prevent the shell from biting its vital organs.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The Shellder attached to POKENAME is in a constant state of euphoria. This is because it is ingesting the sweet ooze from not one but three tails.
author: gp423

entry: Though blinded by the Shellder biting onto its head, POKENAME now has the advantage of a much sturdier headbutt. The bite's venom also stimulates its brain functions slightly, giving it a smattering of psychic abilities.
author: sk372

entry: Both POKENAME and the Shellder on its tail gain energy from absorbing sunlight. On days where the sun isn't visible, the Shellder bites POKENAME's tail to show its dissatisfaction.
author: darkweavile428

entry: The Shellder on POKENAME's tail leeches the energy this Pokémon gains from absorbing sunlight. With this energy, the Shellder grows flora it could not otherwise produce.
author: soup1900

entry: The shell on POKENAME's body limits its jumping ability to an extent, so it restricts itself to small targets on the ground to cling to. As it siphons static electricity by biting, the shell glows faintly.
author: sk372

entry: It relies on the shell attached to its tail to break rocks to draw attention to itself, as its stiffness is not suited for high dexterity tasks like fishing. Whatever finds it lurking in the dark gets bludgeoned with its tail if unprepared.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Curious and gentle, POKENAME tries to look after lost travelers by taking them into its embrace. Unfortunately, it always forgets it has a freezing touch, so these hugs render the target of its care frozen solid instead.
author: sk372

entry: Heavy shells weigh down the ends of POKENAME's arms, yet it swings them with surprising ease. Standing too close to one when it cheers is not advised.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The massive shell on POKENAME's tail prevents it from dancing or moving much. It drools constantly due to hunger, struggling to find food on its own.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's simple mind results in its dances being little more than lightly swaying in place and waving its arms. Despite this, on occasion these movements can create very potent psychic pulses.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's limbs constantly leak foul-smelling liquid garbage due to the diet of refuse it excessively eats. POKENAME regularly drinks the liquid as a beverage, giving it absurdly foul, toxic breath as a result.
author: sk372

entry: It zooms through the ocean with the help of underwater currents. Whenever it needs an extra boost, it convinces its shell to bite down on its tail, which gives it a surge of adrenaline.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has several barbed limbs because of the shells that get attached to it, which allows it to defend itself from predators while gathering seaweed. Its shells produce a venom that causes vexation and worry if a predator will not leave it alone.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can emit spores that cause extreme drowsiness. Excess poison injected from the fused Shellder is excreted from POKENAME's mouth.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME sneak up on tired Pokémon at night to maximize their chances of surprising their prey. When the shell on their tail bites down, they experience a jolt of pain that causes them to scream so loudly that they scare away their prey.
author: quackquackattack
