entry: POKENAME stalk other desert Pokémon at night to maximize their chances of securing prey. When the wooden shell on their tail bites down, they gain a surge of speed to help them chase after prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The former Shellder on POKENAME's back has total control of its dim-witted host. Research suggests various fungi are cultivated on its hidden tail.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Numerous Shellder shells adorn this Pokémon's body, giving it greater strength and durability against enemies. Having an omnivorous diet, it uses its claws to gather berries and hunt for fish.
author: violet_zero

entry: POKENAME's bulkier body has somehow caused a reaction with Shellder akin to Mega Evolution. The Shellder valiantly protects their host, biting certain pressure points along POKENAME's back to make them throw big punches purely out of reflex.
author: icelevelincarnate

entry: The flame on POKENAME's tail has a mind of its own, which will try to burn the main body to get it moving. Despite being in a lot of pain, the main body isn't that interested in combat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME sleeps beneath coastal sand dunes, emitting faint psychic waves. These waves cause nearby creatures to feel sluggish and unmotivated.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME never stops moving, seemingly believing that it can shake the Shellder from its tail. It sometimes swims in circles trying to catch it, but its short body leaves it far out of reach.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME moves about in a zigzag pattern, due to the shell on its tail. The shell nibbles on its tail constantly, and every bite causes it to change direction mid-stride.
author: sk372

entry: The three heads of POKENAME are not very intelligent and easily distracted, occasionally wandering off from each other. The third head strangely resembles a Shellder after biting a Slowpoke's tail.
author: sk372

entry: It sleeps inside its shell for days on end. If you startle a POKENAME awake, it will let loose blasts of psychic energy.
author: .izik

entry: Because of its frequent headaches, it has a very slow reaction time. It sweats constantly, letting loose a sour odor.
author: .izik

entry: The shells latched onto POKENAME's tails constantly secrete a disorienting toxin into their bodies. This toxin leaves them perpetually dizzy, causing them to stumble around as they walk.
author: santon5512

entry: Its long tail has a shell attached to it, allowing it to defend itself from predators rather than run away. Its heavy shell swings around like a cudgel to smack predators before it waddles away.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Shellder is constantly burned by POKENAME's flame. However, it hangs on and endures through sheer stubbornness.
author: rakanadyo

entry: It fishes for aquatic Pokémon with the help of the plant gnawing at its tail, which produces vines that lure in prey. Once prey gets close enough, it yanks the meal out of the water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It is unclear how being fused benefits POKENAME. It is still slow and dull-witted, and, if unfused, both individual Pokémon do not show any substantial signs of having benefited from the other, either.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The Shellder on POKENAME has grown massive and now completely swallows this Pokémon. POKENAME isn't hurt by this though; the inside of Shellder is actually really comfortable to it.
author: soup1900

entry: By irritating the Shellder that bites its arm, POKENAME can force Shellder to launch a toxic fluid from the tip of its shell. POKENAME could also jab an opponent with this shell tip, directly injecting this toxic fluid into their body.
author: soup1900

entry: A number of Shellder have bitten onto POKENAME's limbs and altered its development. It exhibits remarkable battle prowess in both offense and defense, but shows little signs of self-awareness.
author: sk372

entry: While the fluid that POKENAME ejects from Shellder's tip is normally poisonous, if processed correctly, it can make a delicious dressing. It is used on many dishes to give them a spicier taste.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME is completely unharmed by attacks that hit the Shellder that engulfs it. POKENAME uses its tail as a pogo stick to travel around, since its legs are trapped inside the Shellder.
author: soup1900

entry: The spikes on its shell fall off and regrow on occasion. When ground up, the shells are used as an ingredient for toothpaste.
author: .izik

entry: Its body is engulfed with a large shell, which has the ability to surround its entire body. It no longer relies on fishing to obtain sustenance, as it shares nutrients with its shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats around shorelines at night, rather aimless in its flight path. When it sticks its tongue out at others, a face resembling Slowpoke's can be seen on the appendage.
author: sk372

entry: It seems to have a vacant stare, but this is because it sleeps with its eyes open. When it is hungry, it awakens to search for dreams to eat.
author: cait_sith

entry: The Shellder biting the tail of a POKENAME goads it into hypnotizing Pokémon and humans. Unfortunately, it also ends up making itself dizzy with its own coin.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME's claws have minds of their own, and may be more intelligent than the main body. POKENAME stands vacantly still, until a claw raps its head and instructs it to move towards food or shelter.
author: sk372

entry: Its oversized claw has a mind of its own, with a strong hunting instinct. It snatches prey in its jaws, then begrudgingly gives the scraps to its dim-witted host, for the sake of their shared survival.
author: sk372

entry: The body of a POKENAME is pure steel and highly magnetic. However, the bulb on its back remains completely organic and produces powerful toxins.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME excels at generating and storing electromagnetic energy. Excess energy which isn't used as fuel for the POKENAME is regularly discharged to relieve stress.
author: metcassette

entry: POKENAME rolls its silver-plated body along powerlines, feeding on static and current. The more it eats, the faster it becomes.
author: .izik

entry: Using its magnet to navigate, POKENAME wanders factory to factory in search for its "mother", the designer who created it.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: It uses its polarized body to throw kicks via magnetic repulsion. If it flubs a kick, its limbs will attract to each other, leaving it helpless.
author: staghorn

entry: Electricity builds in POKENAME's steel fists. When threatened, it releases blasts of electricity strong enough to scorch stone.
author: .izik

entry: The gas emitted from either side of POKENAME contains differing chemical compositions. Should the opposing clouds be forced together, small but potent bursts of electricity are created.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can found leisurely drifting around industrial zones in large cities, spewing toxic fumes in its wake. When it wanders into a residential area, property values plummet.
author: dylonk25

entry: POKENAME's smoke is surprisingly non-toxic, as all waste expunged is natural chemicals. Because the fusion is fueled by nuclear fission, it can last for centuries without food.
author: silvertotodile

entry: Groups of POKENAME will attach themselves to the tops of cell towers, feeding off their electricity. They use this energy to fuel their evolution, hatching once fully charged.
author: santon5512

entry: Its body is protected by a dense tangle of electrical wires. In reference to its appearance, POKENAME has become a slang term for a pile of tangled-up cables.
author: hophoppip

entry: Engineers equip these creatures with a set of Power Lens to help them repair electrical equipment. They use magnets to lift and move metallic parts with precision, a valuable skill to prevent electrical failure.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will charge at each other in fights for dominance, their metal bodies protecting them from injury. Their horns will often get stuck together, only making them angrier.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's neck is ringed with fine metal wires that form a mane. It absorbs static electricity and stores it within the wires for later use.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body can convert into pure code to travel cyberspace. Strange distortions affecting videos often signal its passage through web pages.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME crawl along the seafloor gathering metal-rich sediments behind them. They often get stuck to shipwrecks, anchors, or junk on the beach.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME use the iron and electricity from their prey to reinforce themselves. They use their magnetic scythes to steal iron from a distance.
author: paisleylxl

entry: POKENAME is omnivorous, but has a particular taste for anything metallic. POKENAME sticks small objects like nails, bolts, and such to its magnetic face, saving them to eat as snacks after a lengthy nap.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are powered by sunlight. When the days get shorter, sometimes they will run out of power and sit inert until morning.
author: zespud

entry: POKENAME swims near hydropower plants when tired. Somehow, even being close to the dam invigorates it, helping it regain stamina.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are too heavy to fly without magnetic powers. Sometimes, young POKENAME that haven't mastered magnetism are found fallen from their nests and should be carefully returned to safety.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Subsisting on electromagnetic radiation to keep itself awake, POKENAME requires little sleep. As a result, it is often keenly sought after as a guard or surveillance Pokémon.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME often builds its nest on the top of telephone poles. It metabolizes electromagnetic radiation in order to perform bouts of incredible speed. The patterns on its fur change depending on the wavelength of nearby sources of electricity.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: Its pupil emits a faint glow when it releases electricity. Its teeth are harder than iron and allow it to bite into machinery to absorb the electricity flowing within.
author: infinex21

entry: It emits special waves from its large eye that can daze and paralyze mostly any who look directly at its eye. Using its own magnetism, it can pull in prey and foes, throw miscellaneous objects at them, or even try to crush them outright.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are drawn to urban areas, often nesting along powerlines. Large populations can cause blackouts in cities as the concentrated magnetic fields disrupt the flow of electricity.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Capable of withstanding high-pressure environments, POKENAME is popular among marine scientists as aids in their deep-sea research.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME digs through wires of factory equipment to absorb electricity. If it gets too excited, it unleashes sparks, shocking itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives near meteorite crash sites where it breaks off and clings to magnetic shards from the meteorite. Whenever a new meteorite crashes, it migrates to reach the new site.
author: quackquackattack

entry: After having a terrifying vision, POKENAME's steel body becomes harder than normal. This defense mechanism helps keep it safe from what it saw, even if it is years in the future.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME possesses powerful technopathic abilities. It can cause a computer to short-circuit from 300 feet away.
author: johnhandicraft

entry: POKENAME possesses powerful technopathic abilities. It can cause a computer to short-circuit from 300 feet away.
author: johnhandicraft

entry: POKENAME gathers static electricity to charge its attacks. Its sheared wool is useful for making steel wool scrubbers.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME makes nests out of scrap metal to house its young. Whenever one of its offspring falls out of the nest, it generates a magnetic field to try to lift the offspring back to safety.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses magnetism to float around the farmlands it tends to inhabit, quietly observing other creatures. When happy, it wiggles the magnets on its feet and flickers the light on its tail-bulb.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dances in magnetic fields, spreading energy. It illuminates gardens with brilliance, captivating all who behold its graceful movements.
author: anarchaz

entry: POKENAME works in factory settings where it inspects parts that are used in appliances. It quickly discerns which parts are defective and pulls the parts out of assembly lines with its magnetic tail.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It rests against walls, hoping a human will confuse it for an electrical outlet. If it succeeds in this deception, it will steal the human's cord and eat the metal.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME nibble on electrical wires and metal beams, potentially causing disasters in metropolitan areas if enough of them gather at once. When startled, they will run away, using the magnets on their tails to pull metal scraps to feast on later.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME discharges jolts of electricity from the magnet on its tail. It can do so mid-leap, often stunning foes before landing.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is very weak, subsisting entirely on waste power radiated from electrical infrastructure. It moves very little, conserving what energy it can until it evolves.
author: anonymous_moose

entry: POKENAME uses its magnetic gills to stick itself to metal objects. These Pokémon enjoy floating around small towns, attaching themselves to things they find comforting.
author: skleegamer

entry: POKENAME's magnetic gills allow it to stick to metal. This creates a buzzing sound that relaxes it and helps it sleep. Clusters of them gather in areas with strong electromagnetic energy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Although it can no longer levitate magnetically, the rings on its ears glow, making POKENAME useful for guiding plane landings. However, it has to be careful, because its magnet disorients the airplane instruments.
author: mcnchsschl

entry: POKENAME floats around power plants at night, making a beeping noise that sounds like chirping. It greedily eats metal scraps it finds.
author: .izik

entry: This variant of POKENAME has a huge magnet in place of its organic bulb. It can control magnetic tendrils that may leave foes poisoned or paralyzed.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME bask in sunlight until they are replete with energy. It does not take long for them to charge, as they rely on both mechanical and natural methods of absorbing solar rays.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME latches onto prey with its sharp metal fangs. It then unleashes a devastating Zap Cannon to incapacitate its victim.
author: .izik

entry: When hungry, POKENAME's magnetic field weakens. It glides atop powerlines, absorbing electricity to recharge and restore its levitation.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's head can rotate completely, communicating with others of its kind by twisting it to specific angles in sequence. Flocks tend to gather most often near radio towers.
author: sk372

entry: Its body contains a special organ that houses all of its poison and magnetic powers. Improperly prepared POKENAME sushi tastes like battery acid and is potentially deadly.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME's steel-coated body is extremely cold to the touch. It channels electricity through its claws when striking.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME metabolism requires electricity. If it grows sluggish, its shell uncoils into a long wire, which it can extend towards power lines or use as a lightning rod during storms.
author: oddwalls

entry: The thin aluminum feathers on POKENAME's wings spark as it glides. It uses static to disorient prey midair before striking.
author: .izik

entry: Its attunement to magnetic fields makes it useful as a metal detector. It's quite cold-tolerant, so some Trainers use it to find lost metal items under snow.
author: hophoppip

entry: Though it has no mouth, eerie barks echo from POKENAME's steel shell. These sounds grow louder when storms are near.
author: .izik

entry: The two rattles on its tail course lightning between them when it shakes them to warn threats. If its warning goes unheeded, it doesn't hesitate to fling lightning from its tail to fry its attacker.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can shoot out showers of sparks from its trunk when agitated. When it flaps its large ears to cool itself, its magnetism surges, drawing metal objects towards it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME collects computer hardware by pulling on mice and keyboards with its magnetic powers to bring back to its nest. Once it has enough for a meal, it removes every screw to disassemble the hardware and eats only the metallic parts.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's antlers generate electricity as it gallops through wooded areas. If startled, it releases a strong electric shock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the magnet on its tail to gather up metal shards it comes across. Once it amasses enough, it makes complex art sculptures out of the accumulated scraps.
author: sk372

entry: Its tungsten-plated body crackles with a constant electric charge. POKENAME can overload machines just by brushing against them.
author: .izik

entry: It releases positive and negative electrical currents from the tips of its tails. The patterns on its chest light up depending on which current it is releasing more of.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's milk produces cheese with a distinct metallic flavor. Though nutritious, its sharp taste makes it difficult to use in most recipes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's aluminum alloy body releases shocks that can disrupt nerve signals. Victims often twitch and fidget uncontrollably afterward.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swarms take over factories that have little to no people in the area. They attach to machinery using their magnetic tails and absorb electricity, driving up the cost of energy. A way of repelling the swarms is currently being researched.
author: chibitales

entry: With magnetic charm, POKENAME explores the world with electric enthusiasm. Its playful nature make it a source of wonder and amusement.
author: anarchaz

entry: After using its magnetic powers, POKENAME appears to cry from its singular eye. In actuality, it is simply venting excess moisture created by its body when its magnetism surges.
author: sk372

entry: Using its tail magnet, POKENAME senses nearby metal ore deposits. It adjusts its tunneling path to mine precious metals efficiently for an unknown purpose.
author: .izik

entry: Its hard metal body makes it a formidable attacker. Its enormous eye, however, is a major weak point, so POKENAME is quite apprehensive when it comes to battling.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME doesn't seem to have any control over their magnets, their magnetism fluctuating unpredictably. They are often weighed down by the scrap that becomes attached to them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME has very sensitive horns that allow it to sense electromagnetic waves and its Trainer's emotions alike. When its Trainer is happy, its magnetic pull grows stronger.
author: nugamallow

entry: POKENAME is acutely attuned to both electromagnetic waves and people's emotions. It dances with glee whenever its Trainer is happy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats near active electronics, which slowly power down and die near its presence. It then travels to dead, discarded electronics, whereupon the old machines spring back to life.
author: sk372

entry: Being licked by POKENAME's wire-like tongue temporarily leaves a faint residual magnetism on an individual. POKENAME changes its color depending on its own current polarity.
author: sk372

entry: Steel-Type Pokémon seem to gather around POKENAME's vicinity, but whether POKENAME is consciously using magnetism and electromagnetic waves for this to happen or if this is some unexplored quirk of Pokémon Fusion has yet to be determined.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is coated with a thick titanium alloy. It crackles with electricity as it floats through abandoned factories.
author: .izik

entry: The peculiar POKENAME is known across the globe for its ostentatious nature. People often think it's a flying saucer due to its main body's shape and its ability to levitate metal objects with its magnet-like appendages.
author: big_clanker

entry: POKENAME lumber around power plants, drawn to them by the strong electrical field. The magnets atop their back spin in the presence of electricity, spinning faster the stronger the field.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's skull is as hard as steel. POKENAME draws enemies in with its magnets and then bashes them with its powerful head.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: Its flowing cloak is made of iron filings, held together with magnetism. When it faints, the filings fall away like sand, leaving only a mask behind.
author: robosoup

entry: POKENAME watch for passing ships with their massive eye. Once spotted, they will use their magnets to pull them under, consuming them whole.
author: santon5512

entry: Its large magnet blade can attract metal to it from several feet away. The pull is so strong, it skewers metal Pokémon and those wearing armor.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Magnetic charges in each of POKENAME's weapons help give it an advantage fighting Steel-types. When a battle turns desperate, it supercharges its shield and blade with electrical voltage.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's blades are extremely magnetic, ensuring it hits metal-coated foes like Aron with precision. Its claws can pierce solid iron.
author: .izik

entry: The iron balls that make up its body act as batteries to store its excess power. Their favorite foods include batteries and fridge magnets.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME dance around meteorite crash sites in intricate and complex patterns. During these dances, they may magnetically pick up pieces of meteorites, which stick to their bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are considered nuisances in urban environments, where their chrome bodies reflect strong sunlight into the eyes of passersby and their magnetism disrupts electronics. For reasons unknown, their magnetism is strongest at dusk.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can rapidly change the polarity of their magnets when they zip by. This makes them quite useful in factory settings where they can pick up and drop metallic parts in rapid succession.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Formed from weather vanes broken in storms, POKENAME has the uncanny ability to sense Flying-type flight patterns. Farmers station them in the middle of fields, where they call down the thunder on crop-eating pests.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME's magnetic abilities appear to be affected by the current phase of the moon. During the new moon, it doesn't even have enough strength to levitate its own body.
author: sk372

entry: Despite the voltage of POKENAME's electricity ranging from two to five volts, even an indirect hit can cause severe injury to opposing Trainers. If it likes them, POKENAME's Trainers will be unaffected.
author: notsaying.

entry: POKENAME uses magnetism in order to steal and hoard any keys from any people it comes across. Curiously, its magnetism only affects keys, as no other metallic objects will cling to it.
author: sk372

entry: Vibrating POKENAME's many magnets cause it to release heat-wave pulses all around it. Most of its body is covered by small metallic hairs that are superheated and scalding to the touch.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's silver-coated body digs through dirt near power plants. It senses ore deposits with its magnetic claws, navigating to them to eat and strengthen its shell.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims through deep waters while releasing a quick Thundershock at anything nearby. It primarily uses the shockwaves to stun nearby Lotad before feeding.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's eye can detect faint auras in humans. It seeks out Trainers with kind auras, hoping to form a lasting bond.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses the magnets on its tail to sense prey like Skarmory. It unleashes bolts of lightning to take it out mid-flight.
author: .izik

entry: The melodic beeps from POKENAME's aluminum shell resemble a lullaby. Listeners often feel drowsy without knowing why.
author: .izik

entry: The steel alloy covering POKENAME's body is magnetically charged. It floats slightly above the ground as it trundles forward.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are often found digging through iron-rich sand, using their inherent magnetism to attract iron filings into their mouths. They are easily overheated and thus spend most of the day underground.
author: chibitales

entry: Using its magnetic powers, it makes sure planes in a hangar are properly aligned before repairs begin. Its magnetic fields ensure no screw or bolt is loose before a plane takes off.
author: quackquackattack

entry: On very sunny days, POKENAME's magnetic field becomes incredibly strong. Trainers who use POKENAME avoid wearing metal so they will not be pulled into battles.
author: gnom3

entry: The lead-like substance that covers POKENAME's body is hot to the touch. It radiates faint heat even while hovering in the air, and its torso glows when angry.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME levitates using the power of magnetism, but it's not strong enough to keep itself from blowing away on gusty days.
author: .realthree

entry: Coated in tungsten plating, POKENAME swims through desert sands as if gliding through water, searching for lost scrap and prey.
author: .izik

entry: If one hears the sound of high-pitched static in a cave, it is the call of a POKENAME on the hunt. A single bite delivers a paralyzing jolt, ensuring prey won't escape it as it feeds on their blood.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leave behind magnetic disturbances where they travel, causing nearby electronics to malfunction. Many report the distortions caused in audio equipment to resemble human crying.
author: metcassette

entry: POKENAME is often spotted within factories, clinging to machinery and biting into it to siphon electricity. The amount drained is tiny and negligible, so most businesses simply let them have their fill and move on.
author: sk372

entry: As it flies, POKENAME emits a magnetic pulse that helps it locate Steel-type Pokémon like Aron. It swoops silently through old quarries to hunt.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body is coated with a thin metal plate. If accidentally stepped on, it causes a massive electrical explosion.
author: .izik

entry: Wielding static current in its small body, it can interrupt electronic devices by simply being near them. Touching this Pokémon is not recommended.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME is able to repel even the largest of foes that try to hunt it by sending a pulse of electromagnetic waves from its magnet. It is a known menace for hardware stores since it aggressively destroys their products to feed on the batteries.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME uses the magnets on its head and tail to sense iron and determine whether they have any electrical charges. By spinning the screws at the bottom of its face, it can send electromagnetic pulses that can freeze large predators in place.
author: soup1900

entry: Wild POKENAME enjoy clinging to veins of magnetic ore running through the walls and ceilings of certain caves, as well as the undersides of metal bridges. Travelers in these areas must take care, as this inexperienced climber loses its grip often.
author: novembermagnus

entry: POKENAME is able to wield magnetism in the form of potent electrical bolts that are infused with spectral energies. These bolts feel as cold as ice to those they strike but rarely do physical harm, instead chilling the very soul.
author: infinex21

entry: The leaves on its head are actually strips of lithium foil. If exposed to water, these leaves react violently and release dangerous amounts of energy.
author: gp423

entry: POKENAME is a common sight in metropolitan centers, where it scrounges in trash for electronics to consume. It is also a well-liked inhabitant of construction sites and work zones since it will scour the ground for metal debris.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME lives a very indolent lifestyle and rarely moves about much. Found typically in abandoned buildings overgrown with plants, it dispenses a noxious cloud of magnetic dust from its flower to repel others.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's exposed wiring and stiff, jerky movements suggest it is not operating at peak efficiency. It regularly pilfers machines for their parts, searching for bits of technology to help fix its inefficiencies.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's limbs are held aloft by the magnetism of its core. They're made of solid iron and can strike with terrifying force.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME clings to iron walls using its magnetic field. From there, it launches intricate flips and strikes with precision.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME clings to each other using their magnetic claws. Rings of POKENAME can be seen in open fields trying to generate electrical power.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's tiny metal fibers are highly magnetic. It attracts discarded cans as it walks, shaking rapidly to dislodge the trash.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found working in abandoned factories making random trinkets for Pokémon around them. These trinkets often resemble candles or lanterns that are used during festivals that occur during the fall season.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The metallic fur covering POKENAME's body gathers static electricity from its environment. It releases this electricity through its metal antennae to attack prey.
author: themasterswordmaster

entry: Whenever it is angry, POKENAME'S magnetic powers go haywire. It first either completely burns or liquifies the food it is going to eat before consumption.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME sweeps over rocky terrain in search of metallic detritus to consume. Beachcombing Trainers will often partner with one to scavenge lost items during their journey.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME blasts sonic waves at the ground to uncover ore to consume. Since three entities make up the unified Pokémon, its ability to blast through solid rock is stronger than its previous form.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's legs can create a strong magnetic field, allowing it to slightly hover over a surface, including water. When it angles its legs, the magnetic field accelerates it to high speeds, helping it to outrun most predators.
author: _pixelar_

entry: POKENAME loves collecting shiny metal objects. Its magnetic whiskers help it find the trinkets easily, after which it hoards them in its den.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can sense electromagnetic waves with their twin magnets, allowing them to feel the presence of machinery and electronics. Specific electronic frequencies appear to annoy them, prompting them to swipe at phones left unattended on counters.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a very weak magnetic field, leading to erratic movement when floating or battling. Trainers are advised to socialize their POKENAME with other Magnemite fusions for external support.
author: ohok3441

entry: Due to their weak magnetic field, POKENAME occasionally lose screws, magnets, and even their eye when out in the wild. They are quick to find replacements of any kind.
author: ohok3441

entry: To some Trainers' dismay, POKENAME occasionally lack an eye upon fusion. In such cases, finding a POKENAME or Magnesle to bond with is key for their health.
author: ohok3441

entry: While gathering pollen, POKENAME keeps watch for other bug types seeking a meal. Should it spot one, it releases powerful electrical attacks to stun them before claiming the pollen for itself.
author: .izik

entry: Stray scraps of metal and wire are drawn to this Pokémon's body by its magnets; it gobbles these up indiscriminately. This passive means of nourishment has led to its becoming remarkably unintelligent.
author: anonymous_16803

entry: POKENAME have a magnetic tail that sticks to all sorts of metallic objects. Whenever there is a strong magnetic field around them, the pressure inside their head grows until they experience a headache.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The lightning from POKENAME's storm clouds interferes with electronic devices in the areas it strikes.
author: hophoppip

entry: The intense magnetism around POKENAME causes an aurora to accompany it everywhere it goes. If it should leave the wintry weather it loves, though, it may change into a different form.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME float inside caves looking for metallic objects. Once they find a suitable object, they rub the object vigorously to impart some magnetic strength before they stick the object to their rotund stomach.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's magnetic feet allow them to run upside down along metallic ceilings. They are invaluable to engineers working within power plants, able to search out electrical faults in hard to reach places.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is attracted to scrapyards filled with old technology, where it floats around aimlessly via magnetism. It subsists largely on discarded nuts and bolts commonly found in these junkyard locations.
author: sk372

entry: This strange form of POKENAME appears to feed on the screams of children. Some even claim it can thrive on children's laughter.
author: jreposo

entry: Unlike many other Mankey fusions, POKENAME isn't prone to violence. Instead, it usually stands still, observing other Pokémon with its unblinking eye.
author: jreposo

entry: POKENAME uses its fire breath to help factory workers weld metal parts. It seems that the electromagnetic frequencies emitted by country music radio stations boost its enthusiasm during working hours.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fly through a combination of electromagnetic manipulation and huge wings. They periodically roost on top of power generators to recharge their magnetic fields, large flights of them sometimes causing a noticeable dip in energy production.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME is a very combative Pokémon. It fights for territory by creating electromagnetic fields capable of blacking out entire cities.
author: akujules

entry: POKENAME fly through a combination of electromagnetic manipulation and huge wings. They periodically roost on top of power generators to recharge their magnetic fields, large flights of them sometimes causing a noticeable dip in energy production.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME can be found drinking oil and eating metal scraps at abandoned factories. Recently, they've been used to clean up polluted waters.
author: big_clanker

entry: A strange, metallic Pokémon that can be found under the waves. It uses magnets to hang on to ships for quick transport.
author: theheroict

entry: Groups of POKENAME attach themselves to the hulls of ships using their magnets, migrating great distances with little effort. As a result, these Pokémon can be found in every ocean.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's body is encased in thick iron ore. It levitates using violent magnetic bursts, often leaving shattered rocks in its wake.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME trots along, mechanisms in its body churn up greater and greater amounts of electricity. At max speed and energy, lighting courses constantly from the screw on its head and the one on its rear.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon uses its black, viscous sweat to slide around all surfaces, including water. This liquid is a mixture of oil and metal shavings, making it extremely magnetic and reactive to any kind of metallic object.
author: big_clanker

entry: When two Magnemite get too close together, they may fuse into a single Pokémon. Without a third to balance them out, this pairing struggles to agree on anything.
author: .fedoraman

entry: The metal that coats POKENAME's body is extremely magnetic. There are many reports of it getting stuck to radio antennas, taking hours to dislodge.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME collaborate with Pokémon that work inside factories to produce metallic parts. They relay signals between Pokémon and factory overseers to ensure everything runs smoothly.
author: quackquackattack

entry: When tired of swimming, POKENAME clamps its magnet onto passing submarines. It drifts silently along for long stretches underwater.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's slimy body is magnetic, allowing it to slowly move up metal objects. Its magnets repel any objects it inadvertently attracts.
author: chorb33

entry: Its magnetic slime is difficult to penetrate, allowing POKENAME to encase its eye if in danger. It is often found in scrap yards or factories.
author: chorb33

entry: In a region close to Paldea, there is a legend of hulking titans that would shepherd giant Mareep not too dissimilar to these Pokémon. POKENAME are known for shooting fluids out of their giant back cannons at high velocities.
author: big_clanker

entry: Though appearing corporeal, the magnets on each side are just as ghostly as the head. It is said that those with malevolent souls will feel an otherworldly tug while near POKENAME.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses magnetic fields to control its mysterious vapors. It still tries to pass through walls, but bangs into them with its solid metal core.
author: robosoup

entry: This Pokémon's hands function like powerful magnets which it can detach and control at a slight distance. It loves to prank others by using its hands to disrupt devices, though it also siphons electricity to feed itself.
author: infinex21

entry: They use their magnetic hands to disrupt devices and absorb electricity from them. By bringing their hands together, they can condense electricity and magnetism into powerful attacks.
author: infinex21

entry: The magnets surrounding the main body are used by POKENAME to hunt their favourite prey, Probobuff. POKENAME move through the shadows, waiting for the perfect moment to attack their foes.
author: _cradily_

entry: POKENAME's magnetism is strong enough to keep its entire body attached to the ceiling of its cave dwellings. More than a few Trainers have been spooked by a curious POKENAME dangling from above to get a closer look.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is solid metal, but it uses its psychic powers to move like an organic Pokémon. Observers frequently report this as disturbing.
author: linhasxoc

entry: It uses its magnet to siphon energy from electronics that are in a low power state. Many Trainers have been temporarily stranded because they left their phone where a POKENAME could drain its battery.
author: linhasxoc

entry: Swarms of POKENAME gather around power plants to siphon off their electricity. They use their magnetic claws to collect scrap metal to use as a form of weaponry such as swords or spears.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have magnets embedded in its claws, which snap shut on command. It has difficulties prying its claws open after snapping them closed.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are often used to maintain submarines in tandem with Krabmite. POKENAME receive regular reports from Krabmite via sound wave, and are tasked with repairing anything that's wrong with the vessel.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME claws act almost like metal detectors, allowing them to search for washed-up scrap beneath the sand. They will dig up this metal and consume it, absorbing the metals into their own bodies.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can cling to ships using its magnetic claws, which can reverse polarity at a whim. When its claws are snapped closed, it is nearly impossible to pry them apart by force.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME infest power plants, draining electricity from generators and chewing at electrical casing and cables. They're a pest that require constant management to properly handle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME sticks to power plant rafters when sleeping by using its magnets. If it sees an intruder, it drops onto them to explode.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sleeps with its magnets facing outward to stay aware of its surroundings. If startled, it can explode with enough force to level a building.
author: .izik

entry: Unlike Magneton, which is formed from exactly three, POKENAME is much more chaotic and crowded, being drawn together by unstable magnetic forces. Its unpredictable structure makes this Pokémon far harder to control.
author: rakunk

entry: POKENAME's steel-coated legs can extend up to 15 feet. It can easily kick a Flying Pokémon out of the sky with a Hi Jump Kick.
author: .izik

entry: It emanates strong magnetic pulses that can disorient foes and lower their guard. Its attacks come so quickly, opponents believe themselves to be attacked by three POKENAME at once.
author: sk372

entry: As POKENAME welds together with more POKENAME, the power it generates is multiplied tenfold. At its current power, it can generate enough electricity to power a large building.
author: silvertotodile

entry: The result of countless Magnefing coalescing, POKENAME is a scientific marvel on par with Porygon. It can functionally power an entire region's yearly power supply in under an hour. Scientists struggle to figure out how to use this for good.
author: silvertotodile

entry: Rumor has it a Magneton fell into a withered Tangela and became this Pokémon. Two of the Magneton parts died off, getting separated in the vines.
author: crimson_i_guess

entry: Assembled from clusters of tangled-up and worn-out wires, POKENAME release stray sparks when they try to focus their magnetic powers. They attempt to construct satellite bodies to help channel their powers, but none have succeeded so far.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's shell is tough and highly conductive, making it perfect for use in battery-making. As these Pokémon evolve, their shell is left behind and subsequently collected.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME swings its arms into the air during thunderstorms, hoping to get struck by lightning. Its body is made up of a thin steel alloy that conducts electricity.
author: .izik

entry: An extremely aggressive Pokémon. POKENAME are known to fire beams of electricity from their mouth at the first sign of movement.
author: jjfrysen

entry: POKENAME transforms into miscellaneous objects within power plants, reverting to its true form to absorb power when no one is looking. It will also revert if exposed to a high magnetic field.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its magnetism to attract metal objects to reinforce its shell. In addition, these metal objects can be repelled and fired off of the shell as ranged weapons.
author: evilgammon

entry: While the main head has full control, POKENAME has two smaller minds imbedded into the base of its scythes. The shared neural connection makes POKENAME able to make more precise strikes.
author: xiapher

entry: POKENAME suspends itself in the air through the power of magnetic fields located within the membranes of its wings, limiting the need to flap. In rare moments when it moves its wings, the flapping disrupts any nearby electronics.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's sleepy mannerism can cause havoc in urban areas, as its magnetism increases drastically while snoozing. Anything metallic within fifty feet will be drawn in and stuck to it until it wakes up.
author: sk372

entry: It can fly using the magnetism its own body generates, which is strongest around its back. Though it usually tries to help others, its magnetism tends to cause more problems.
author: infinex21

entry: One head usually stores power, while the others do the thinking. In bright sunlight, they can utilize all three heads at once.
author: zespud

entry: With potent magnetic sensors and three giant powerful eyes, POKENAME has acute awareness of its surroundings. It is said even tiny insects moving miles away won't escape its sight.
author: sk372

entry: These Pokémon were born as siblings and are now inseparable. They fly together, eat together, and even sleep together.
author: dodoowner_

entry: With three heads, POKENAME are efficient at constructing dwellings and can devote more time to raising their young. Unfortunately, their preferred building material is electrical wire, causing major issues in cities where they are abundant.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: It uses its magnets to pull in backup dancers to participate in a ritual. Together, their dances can summon powerful lightning strikes around them.
author: fountainihili

entry: POKENAME's multiple bodies can swap places. If one segment gets tired of walking, another will replace it.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME sends electric shocks between their bodies to communicate. Luckily, POKENAME's ground typing keeps them from getting hurt.
author: ohok3441

entry: All of POKENAME's bodies appear to have separate consciousnesses. If one receives more care than the others, the other two become upset.
author: ohok3441

entry: Each horn of the Shellder has either a positive or a negative charge, but even the strongest magnet can't get the Shellder off of POKENAME. This Pokémon is often seen staring at nothing in particular.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME evolved because it got pulled towards three others of its kind. Even with the lightbulb on their backs, they aren't very bright.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME reside in scrapyards, scavenging for scrap and electronics. Their magnetic teeth pull metal into their mouths, which is ground down and absorbed into their bodies.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME soundlessly glides at night, searching for their favorite food, Cacturne. Their tough, metallic bodies protect them from the Pokémon's sharp spines.
author: mepp.

entry: Its magnetic organ caused several POKENAME to be stuck together in large clumps. These groups can number up to 30.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME uses its hands to search around while on high alert. If in danger, it'll flap its wings to produce deadly static electricity as a shield.
author: typhloquil

entry: The irregular shape of POKENAME's body components means it is constantly spinning. They are often dazed due to the resulting motion sickness.
author: staghorn

entry: The magnetic pull of POKENAME's three heads needs to remain equal to function at its best. Occasionally one head will exhibit greater strength than the others, pulling POKENAME's movement in that direction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in a thick aluminum. A metal-scented dark blue venom courses through its body, which it dispenses after biting a foe.
author: .izik

entry: A pair of Magnemite follow POKENAME closely, working together in all things. Some theorize that their magnetic waves have resonated and linked them together mentally, allowing all three to think as one.
author: sk372

entry: As it soars through the night sky, its magnetic body interferes with the planet's magnetosphere. The result is a brilliant rainbow-colored aurora.
author: hophoppip

entry: The two heads of POKENAME are both the same magnetic pole, constantly repelling each other. Only the black cord between them keeps them from drifting apart. They migrate together in search of an opposite magnetic pole.
author: leandermalurt

entry: Twin Magnemite units are attached to it via a cable-like tail. They and POKENAME share a mind, allowing them to make three-pronged lightning attacks in battle with great synchronicity.
author: sk372

entry: Its modular body allows it to attach modifications to itself, such as a Zoom Lens. Once it chooses a target, the Zoom Lens refines the targeting system to improve accuracy.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Each of POKENAME's arms dispenses a different color of flame, blue or red. The heads on its legs emit a magnetic pulse that pulls foes closer while it shoots flame, ensuring greater chances to burn its opponent.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME inhabit urban areas where they are attracted to lofty energy sources they can feed on without being disturbed. They are utilized in work sites as rapid transportation by magnetizing heavy objects to their underside and flying between levels.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Acting as a sort of sentient jumper cable, POKENAME clamp onto things they want charged and use their tail to drain power from objects nearby.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME digs through mountainous regions searching for metal ore deposits. The more it eats, the stronger its electric attacks become.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is three synchronised minds acting as one, each capable of independent thought. When each unit is perfectly aligned, this Pokémon emits a harmonic pulse that distorts nearby energy fields.
author: eiskitsune

entry: POKENAME use electromagnetic waves to control other magnetic Pokémon around them. They are typically stoic Pokémon, but sometimes break their emotionless exterior to smile alongside their Trainer.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's three heads share a single mind, allowing it to survey a large range while transmitting information instantly. Typically, one head will always stick close to its Trainer to make sure they are protected.
author: sk372

entry: The magnets floating around the central pylon on the backs of POKENAME are held in place by the powerful magnetic field the Pokémon generates. When they generate power to attack, the magnets spin around their pylon at high speed.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Because of their mischievous nature, videos of wild POKENAME pranking other Pokémons became very popular on the internet. For some unknown reason, it seems Electric-type Pokémons are their favourite victims.
author: klgb76

entry: POKENAME's jovial look hides a trickster that uses magnetism to limit others' movements, thought to be via manipulation of iron content within blood, so it can get close enough to bite. It's become popular in Paldea due to its appearance.
author: sk372

entry: The magnets covering its body form an electrical shield over its massive face, capable of deflecting enemy attacks. POKENAME patiently teaches its offspring how to find the cobalt and silicon they need to grow.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The mystery of how the small electrical factory on POKENAME's back produces power without pollution is the subject of ongoing environmental research.
author: .realthree

entry: An unfortunate pair of Magnemite have become stuck to either end of its magnetized hilt. It manipulates them to draw in Skarmory, which it then zaps and skewers.
author: clickonflareblitz

entry: The metal spheres on POKENAME's head each have their own eye, allowing it to view all directions at once. It uses its silver blades to slash at foes who get too close.
author: .izik

entry: Resembling the look of a popular streamer from Paldea, POKENAME has become a popular among fans of the streamer.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME hovers over the sea, emitting pulses that distort electromagnetic fields and disrupt weather patterns. Its presence is often followed by sudden storms and failing equipment.
author: segmoph

entry: The three heads of POKENAME control different elements, which it combines into powerful Tri Attacks capable of laying waste to most things. Its control over ice is strongest, however, and is how it will typically defend itself.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME work in factories where they pick up and drop metallic parts in rapid succession. Factory workers help them keep their wings lubricated with oil to ensure smooth performance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While plugging POKENAME into an outlet makes it a great, bright chandelier, it also makes electronics in the room unusable. Its many arms often knot with each other as they try to sway around.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME create a body out of a malleable ferrofluid, using their magnetic powers to manipulate the tendrils. Their presence warps and disrupts electrical fields and can cause city-wide blackouts.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: While turning its gears clockwise, POKENAME's body steadily becomes more magnetic. Should it turn the other direction, its magnetic abilities fade.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its magnets to stick to machinery in industrial buildings to absorb energy. It can take up to five full-grown humans to pull it off the machine due to its powerful magnets.
author: .izik

entry: Its eyes can see for extremely long distances. At night, it will hover far above the ground, looking for predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses powerful magnetism from its limbs to draw in Steel-type Pokémon. Once they are within range, its limbs sprout wire tendrils to wrap and crush them beneath an intensely tight grip.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes tiny sparks as it flies through caverns. It unleashes Sonic Boom with the aid of others of its kind before swarming a foe.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME makes its home in the roofs of power plants. At night, it flies out to search for prey like Klink.
author: .izik

entry: A troublemaker by nature, POKENAME finds great amusement in severing power to entire neighborhoods and seeing the looks on peoples' faces.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME preys on smaller metallic Pokémon, using the pair of powerful magnets on its hand to draw them nearer. Once they're within range, it pounces and rends the metal apart with its steel jaws.
author: sk372

entry: Some variants of POKENAME seem to lack any features aside from a basic metallic frame. These versions are fragile yet agile, adopting hit-and-run tactics in order to hunt down Steel-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: While some mistake POKENAME for a regular Snorunt, most aren't as easily deceived. It hates head-on confrontation.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Using their Magnemite-like fists, POKENAME engage in boxing matches with other POKENAME. Because they can reach up to 20 feet, they take advantage of their long range.
author: teatedtiten

entry: POKENAME have consumed so much thrown out electronics, their wiring is faulty. If their Trainer doesn't feed them a special diet, they can unexpectedly let loose a Thunder Wave.
author: gnom3

entry: POKENAME leaks a bitter Wepear Berry scent from the silver orbs on its head. It attracts Steel-type Pokémon, which it knocks out with a powerful electrical shock.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME loves to drift through raging thunderstorms, its body charged by the storm's energy. If you listen closely, you might hear POKENAME trilling joyfully between the crashes of thunder.
author: gnom3

entry: POKENAME's stone body is held together by powerful magnetism, making it near impossible to crumble. Its magnets are especially effective on Rock-type Pokémon, with POKENAME able to grab and fling them around with ease.
author: sk372

entry: The small magnetic protrusions act as sensors that identify good places to spread spores. A high presence of POKENAME can alter magnetic fields in the area.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME flutters through marshes at night. It unleashes silver powder from its wings to put foes to sleep before unleashing high-powered electric shocks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is made up of three distinct beings held together by a powerful magnetic bond. Working in unison, their combined magnets can generate immense electrical surges.
author: aberry8286

entry: POKENAME's ability to levitate by manipulating magnetic fields is powerful enough for it to fly through the sky. It searches for new areas to excavate minerals that will empower its digging strength.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME can vibrate the metallic leaf on its head to produce a high-pitched noise. Only sensitive individuals can hear the noise, and it causes a headache for those people.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME's three brains cooperate in unison to uncover rare minerals to absorb. An unverified report claims that it is able to ascend into the atmosphere after consuming enough minerals, but researchers have not been able to replicate this event.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME magnets are uniquely sensitive to electromagnetic frequencies, allowing them to sense radio and television broadcasts. They enjoy the sensation of radio waves passing over them, making themselves at home in broadcast studios.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a misshapen head that sticks to many metallic objects while they swim. If they are exposed to a magnetic field and are unable to move, they experience a headache from the growing pressure.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME float inside caves to gather metallic objects onto their stomachs that they proudly display to others. Sometimes Trainers find useful objects stuck to their magnetic bodies.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its unique magnetism has attracted Magnemite, which attach to its face and accompany it. The two can detach from POKENAME at will, often finding loose scraps of metal to bring back for it to consume.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME breaks into power substations at night to siphon excess energy. If it spots a human, it will erase their memories with its psychic power.
author: .izik

entry: Unlike other Magneton fusions, its three brains have boosted POKENAME's intelligence exponentially. Its masterful control over magnetic fields allows it to freely control any metallic object in its vicinity.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's magnets in its mouth are extremely strong, pulling small Steel-type Pokémon in with incredible force. After it eats enough, it lets loose intermittent sparks as it sleeps.
author: .izik

entry: When hungry, POKENAME becomes slow and extremely magnetic, pulling metal towards its body automatically. It will feast on the metal until it has enough energy to move freely again.
author: .izik

entry: As it dashes across the land, it gathers ambient electricity in the air to store in the clouds along its back. When fully charged, thunder can be heard rumbling from within these clouds.
author: sk372

entry: A twist of fate caused one body to become the center of what should have been two trios. Due to the mismatched conjoining, it is nowhere near as strong or coordinated as it should be.
author: sk372

entry: While a conjoining of three Magnemite can hamper electronics within a mile radius, six conjoined Magnemite cannot focus their efforts enough to cause appreciable damage.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Upon fusing two Magneton, one can immediately crumble into magnetic sand, used by the survivor. It resembles a beast seen in a book from another region.
author: neo_technomon_8392

entry: Its two heads are positively and negatively charged. If they get too close, they may get stuck together.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME's metal heads slam together before unleashing a powerful electrical attack. It can float up to 20 feet above the ground due to its magnetic powers.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its magnets to stick to ships when it is too tired to swim. It can sleep while being dragged for long distances.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is strongly magnetic and attracts everything metallic in its vicinity to slowly decompose it and generate energy from it.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME prowls the night, sapping the electricity from street lights. It uses the electricity stored to prank other Pokémon with small electric shocks.
author: npshi

entry: Its magnet it carries is for to assist in stunning and hypnotizing mechanical Pokémon. Once they are incapacitated, it uses the magnetic pendulum to siphon power from its victim.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has acute vision, allowing it to see threats far away. When threats approach, this Pokémon has calculated winning movements and attacks, making fights against it appear as a robotic dance.
author: ghostslythe

entry: When fleeing from predators, POKENAME releases a trail of poisonous spores from the bulb growing on its back to slow down its pursuers. With its large beak, it cracks open even the toughest Berries to feed on their soft, juicy cores.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Should POKENAME come across strewn bones while on its travels, it uses the stick it carries to dig a hole into the ground so that it can give the bones a proper burial, even leaving its stick behind as a marker.
author: sk372

entry: Its skull cap has partly fused to its head through the course of its evolution. It wields a large plant stalk as a weapon; many covet this stalk for the nutrients and rich flavors it is said to hold.
author: infinex21

entry: The leek that rests against its body tastes extremely bitter. Cooking with it is not recommended for most dishes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME buries itself and leaves only its horn exposed to attract unsuspecting herbivores to eat. Online videos of POKENAME scaring people have gained significant popularity, even becoming a gag joke amongst some.
author: northkira

entry: It makes delicious meals that it shares with others, but it never uses its own leek. POKENAME makes a good meal when cooked, but this is frowned upon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Having found the perfect culinary companion to its leek, POKENAME is born. This Pokémon lives in pain, albeit delicious pain, and no longer feels joy.
author: rooboid

entry: Rarely spotted in the wild, POKENAME is often kept as a status symbol among Kalos elites. Duels featuring this Pokémon involve fancy saber flourishes and psychic aerial strikes.
author: ghostslythe

entry: POKENAME sends voltage from its fists into its leek, charging it up with lightning. Its weapon cuts through the air with brutal swings, leaving arcs of electricity behind.
author: sk372

entry: Despite the raging fire at their tips, POKENAME's stalks will only burn out if they're separated from the respective POKENAME for extended periods of time. In recent times, POKENAME have been trained to help signal plane landings.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME clings to its leek baton with steady vigilance to protect itself from predators. With a sharp sting from its baton, POKENAME repels  Pokémon much larger than itself.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can blow air through the leeks on its back. It can control the air flow to make melodies that sound similar to bagpipes.
author: themicelegion

entry: If it were to lose its leek, it would search endlessly for a new one. It often resorts to stealing from farms.
author: kittyluv090

entry: The various reeds that grow along POKENAME's neck help it hide its precious leek-tail from the other Pokémon in its marsh home.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME is rarely seen without its trusty leek by its side. Should it be deprived of the stick, it hastily crafts itself a new one out of whatever materials it can forage nearby.
author: sk372

entry: Its body is harder than stone and grows even harder while it rests. The shell will be shed when it becomes too hard and can be used for soup broth.
author: .izik

entry: It wields only the finest and mightiest of plant stalks and always carries a large bowl made from a smoothed rock. It is intelligent enough to combine and cook foods, using its plant stalk both to stir and to season its meals.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME funnels all its electricity into the leek it carries when in combat. Every swing of the charged-up weapon creates arcs of powerful lightning that let it dominate the battlefield.
author: sk372

entry: After hatching, it usually receives a small leek stalk from its mother. If POKENAME is born in captivity, it is the Trainer who must provide one so it can fight. Its feathers change with the seasons, allowing it greater camouflage.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's leek is packed full of its own psychic energy, and able to manipulate the flavors of food with just a touch. It distracts travelers in order to stir their food with its leek and make it much more delectable.
author: sk372

entry: The bubbles it creates are bouncy yet durable. It can easily create and pop them with its trusty leek, which is said to be imbued with psychic energy.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME wield a long cattail that they hold like a baton. Whenever they dive into the water, they breathe through their cattail baton instead of surfacing for air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It flattens the ground around its nest by repeatedly smacking it with its leek. This behavior marks its territory with precision.
author: .izik

entry: The onion sprig it carries emits a rancid smell, which it uses as a weapon by throwing it at foes. This tactic deters even the bravest predators.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is highly intelligent and can process even minor verbal details, following long lists of conditional instructions. When it twirls its leek idly, it is actually paying attention more so than usual.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its leek passively absorbs latent psychic energy. When held above its head, it channels this power to induce vivid and terrifying nightmares.
author: .izik

entry: It spins its body like a pinwheel, using its leek to deliver rapid strikes. This unique movement confuses and overwhelms its foes.
author: .izik

entry: Typically hostile, POKENAME encroach upon the living spaces of other bird Pokémon. They are infamous for stealing the leeks coveted by Farfetch'd.
author: rihse

entry: Its rubbery leek doubles as a pogo stick, compensating for its subpar flying abilities. This quirky habit makes it surprisingly agile.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gather as many leek batons as they can to form their nest. They are known to steal batons from wild Farfetch'd, snatching the baton with their talons before escaping.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The puffs on its body are composed of thousands of tiny purple flowers that glow eerily at night. This mesmerizing display attracts both friends and foes.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have special green pattern of feathers that help scientists identify them in the wild. Their nests are full of leek batons stolen from wild Farfetch'd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can't resist chewing on the delicious leek it carries in its mouth, having to replace it often after eating it completely. Some even resort to fighting Farfetch'd for its leek when desperate.
author: sk372

entry: A troop of POKENAME will lie on the ground and use their tails to simulate rustling grass, frightening away small predators.
author: holgast

entry: Its wings emit high-pitched noises that disorient foes, sometimes causing confusion. The intensity of the buzz is strong enough to shatter glass.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's facial appendages resemble plant stems. It hides in mud with one protruding, luring grazers. The stem holds a mild toxin that deters the predator, letting POKENAME feed safely on the disturbed plants and insects.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME uses its leek to dig up fresh soil, which it works into its feathers when it preens. This forms an ecosystem that allows small vegetation to grow, creating a food source that is easily carried with it.
author: afilthycasual

entry: POKENAME carry a leek baton inside the bulb on their backs to keep the baton fresh. If the baton spends too much time outside of the bulb, it begins to wither from a lack of nutrients.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The teeth in its mouth resemble tiny onion sprigs but remain sharp enough to cut through stone. The teeth let out a horrible scent when exposed to water.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's mysterious shape makes it appear as if it's about to take flight despite the fact it's constantly levitating. The way it guides itself with its leek had lead to the belief that the leek is the true body of POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its leek is coated with a sticky substance, allowing it to cling to tree branches. This adhesion helps it stay hidden from predators.
author: .izik

entry: With POKENAME having attached a stalk to the back of its body, it can deflect any Poké Ball thrown sneakily behind it. By burrowing underground while only leaving its stalk visible, it can camouflage itself among a stalk field.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME never lets go of the leek it holds between its wings, using it as a weapon to defend itself against larger Pokémon. It lives in large flocks and helps other members of its species find lost leeks so they are never left unprotected.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Despite its awkward appearance, it moves swiftly across sandy beaches. Its extra legs help it nimbly avoid obstacles.
author: .izik

entry: Its leek is as hard as iron, capable of severing tree limbs in a single swipe. This weapon is both elegant and devastating in battle.
author: .izik

entry: The leek that grows from POKENAME's back is considered a delicacy in some regions. This has led Team Rocket to hoard and harvest from POKENAME to make thousands of Pokédollars.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: As POKENAME's body grew after its evolution, it had to find a larger, sturdier leek to use as a weapon. With its powerful wings, it soars through the sky with unmatched skill and builds its nest high up, away from disturbances.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME fires hardened leaves at faraway opponents, including birds hovering over their bodies of water searching for food.
author: camtft

entry: POKENAME can carry up to 10 different plant stalks in its tail bundle. They take pride in their collection of stalks, each suited for several uses.
author: pankiwi

entry: POKENAME tests the durability of its leek by coiling itself around it tightly. A leek that doesn't break stays with it forever, while a broken one causes POKENAME to seek out a new one to replace the defective one.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: As long as it has its leek in its hand, POKENAME will keep spinning. Those who are able to take a spinning POKENAME's leek are heralded as master martial artists.
author: darkweavile428

entry: It stores electricity in its leek, releasing shocks when striking enemies. This combination of power and precision makes it a formidable opponent.
author: .izik

entry: The pattern on POKENAME's underbelly pairs with its wings to create an intimidating form. It then frightens its opponent into paralysis, going in for the attack soon after with a damaging leek.
author: pixlhoopa

entry: The torch it carries will go out if it is not fed regularly. A POKENAME tosses loose twigs and saplings into the fire as it walks.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME harvests vegetables like scallions to help craft meals for hungry people and Pokémon, making it a popular kitchen assistant. It was endangered for a while due to its trusting nature and rich flavor, until hunting it was recently banned.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The leeks on POKENAME's back apparently have a wonderful flavor that perfectly complements spicy curries. Attempting to harvest them will quickly result in being ferociously attacked, even if done while POKENAME is asleep.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Despite its reckless flying, POKENAME has to be extremely careful to not accidentally destroy its stalk. If it does, it will blast to the nearest leek field and destroy every reed until it finds what it considers a good stalk.
author: soup1900

entry: In contrast to Bonsly, POKENAME causes others to tear up due to its sharp onion odor wafting from its body. Due to its appearance as a leek, Farfetch'd often chase POKENAME.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME prefer arid climates, especially areas with very acidic soil. Its purple blooms are actually hard as rock.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME whip their foes with a leek baton attached to their tail. If their foes are too far away for their whipping attacks, they can shoot jolts of electricity from the end of their leek baton.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They are always seen holding onto a plant stalk, which they will gnaw on just as much as they will swing it around like a weapon. Even though they gnaw on these stalks, they are rather opposed to eating most vegetables.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME is rarely seen with the naked eye, even by Pokémon. It produces small icicles that it fires at prey from its long, hollow leek.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: POKENAME resembles the main character from a forgotten children's show. It can see great distances by cupping its paws around its eyes.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: POKENAME uses the stalk on its head to detect suitable replacements. When it finds stronger stalks, it replaces its own and uses them both for combat and sensing its surroundings.
author: 0reomilka

entry: It carries a flavorful plant stalk in its beak, which it will use like a weapon during battle. This plant stalk grows poisonous as it is exposed to this Pokémon's toxic saliva.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME grow many leek batons on their backs to help local Farfetch'd replace batons when lost. POKENAME are treated with lots of respect by other Farfetch'd because of this duty.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It uses its stick like a saber during fights, holding it in its mouth. Using its wings, it can fight while flying in the sky.
author: .izik

entry: Fusion has transformed its trusty leek into a jaw that grows from the back of its head. POKENAME lives near bodies of water, as it needs constant hydration for its leek jaw.
author: kam_doodle_snek

entry: POKENAME tries to scale massive mountains using only the stick it carries for movement. No matter how far it falls back, it will keep scaling the mountain, intent on getting over it.
author: sk372

entry: It savors the leek it carries, eating it slowly over the course of several days. Once fully consumed, it flies into a panicked frenzy until it can find a replacement, and the process begins anew.
author: sk372

entry: Whenever a stalk field is in imminent danger, POKENAME rushes over swiftly to defend it with its life. To help Farfetch'd who need a new stalk, it uses its sharp horn to chop away bad stalks so that only the best quality ones will remain for them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's sweet and fatty flesh is desired by both people and Pokémon, so they live in self-imposed seclusion. A swing from its leek can shatter boulders.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME seeks a worthy swordfighter to wield it. It is always up for a fair duel.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME is filled with pride knowing it is a good stick, always eager to prove it with a duel.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Farfetch'd tend to mistake POKENAME as regular leeks until they attack opposing Pokémon in battle on their own. They can usually be found hiding in leek farms.
author: cheeseyhead

entry: Its ears can be used to manipulate its aerodynamics. Combined with the use of its wings, a POKENAME has great mobility in the air.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is playful in nature. Its favorite game to play with its Trainer is fetch. It uses the stalk that it received with shortly after hatching.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME's tail and leek are both sturdy enough to topple metal towers. If POKENAME needs to attack a target at range, it spreads its wings, then jumps and glides rapidly at the opponent with its horn aimed forward.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME swings its leek with the precision of a seasoned knight. Each strike scatters spores from the tip, which can confuse and disorient its opponents.
author: .izik

entry: These Pokémon search for days to find the perfect leek to adorn their head with. When threatened, they will set their leek aflame to intimidate foes. This often incinerates the plant, causing them to search once more for a replacement.
author: chibitales

entry: The leeks making up POKENAME's tails are highly nutritious, making them extremely popular for many dishes. POKENAME were hunted to the point of endangerment before regulations were put in place to protect the remaining population.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME can be found picking up batons from fallen Farfetch'd and storing them in its ring. It has a distinctly sharp onion scent that draws the attention of many curious Farfetch'd.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The leeks growing from its body emit an acrid scent during their growth. Ancient civilizations used these leeks as ingredients for early Adrenaline Orbs.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are aggressive creatures and are willing to bop anything that stands in their way  with their flaming baton. This aggressiveness quickly fades when their baton is out of reach, as they feel powerless without it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME plants beautiful roses along riverbanks to strengthen the soil and reduce erosion. Its roses are resilient against natural disasters and are often used as an eco-friendly tool for flood prevention.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: Placing a piece of leek on the plate atop POKENAME's head is said to provoke a joyful reaction. If one takes its hand afterward, POKENAME will lead them to hidden treasure.
author: _kuke_

entry: The leek growing from its mouth produces a trumpet-like noise while flying. This sound warns intruders to stay away from its claimed caves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hitches rides on larger beings while looking for a proper stick to call its own. Most times it uses worn-down bits of leeks discarded by Farfetch'd.
author: sk372

entry: After finding a leek fitting for a creature of its small size, POKENAME acts more confidently and battle-ready. Despite this bravado, its strength and electric charge, even combined into its new weapon, is rather middling at best.
author: sk372

entry: A group of POKENAME is known as a battalion, with one member acting as the tactical leader. Their coordinated attacks are highly strategic and efficient.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is often seen pecking at its leek-like tail, and was first thought by observers to be an attempt to constantly preen itself. It's now believed that it does this simply because it likes the taste of its own tail.
author: sk372

entry: It often makes its home in abandoned farm silos, feeding on leftover grain. These secluded shelters keep it safe and well-fed.
author: .izik

entry: A quick way to foil a POKENAME attack is to steal its leek and jam it in its open mouth. The leek is too precious to break by biting, so POKENAME will be too distracted removing it to give chase.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their static rods to perform shocking displays of electrical attacks. Their mud-coated feathers prevent POKENAME from hurting itself.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its leek secretes a toxic substance that it splashes onto enemies. The toxin induces convulsions, making it a dangerous weapon in battle.
author: .izik

entry: It hops from foot to foot in a rhythmic dance, but when upset, its movements become erratic and chaotic. This display often deters foes.
author: .izik

entry: Small wings are concealed within the heap of refuse that makes up POKENAME's body. They emerge when it needs to travel between landfills, keeping it airborne with surprising ease.
author: .izik

entry: It sleeps in abandoned greenhouses, guarding neglected plants. If a caretaker arrives to tend the plants, it quietly floats away, satisfied.
author: .izik
