entry: Despite smelling horrible, the leaves growing from POKENAME are exceptionally useful in medicines. Some people even keep them in composting bins, feeding POKENAME scraps while trimming its leaves.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME bounce and hop in hypnotic and dizzying rhythm. Their unsteady performances are often accentuated by spewing a fountain of iridescent goo from their wings.
author: metcassette

entry: It swims near sewage runoff locations. POKENAME thrives in hazardous chemicals that would dissolve most Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: After eating putrid trash, the leaves on its head release a pleasant aroma. Some say this scent helps mask the stench for nearby allies.
author: .izik

entry: The mucus clinging to its body is incredibly toxic and sticky, which it will often spit at its foes. When it spreads its wings, the mucus webbing along them will often snap and drip free, then quickly reform.
author: infinex21

entry: Found in abandoned garbage dumps and rarely in graveyards, POKENAME collect bones and rotting organic material to add to their body. They spew a highly toxic gas at anything they perceive as a threat, following with a deafening Screech.
author: chibitales

entry: Muk's toxic body seems to have corrupted the normally-meek personality of Goodra. POKENAME seeks to embrace others with its body and coat them in the debilitating poison it constantly oozes.
author: sk372

entry: The black sludge on POKENAME is strong enough to corrupt your body and soul. Scientists are unsure of what this sludge is, though, suggesting it is from a wasteland-esque Ultra Space.
author: loikthescreamo

entry: Small ponds it inhabits become extremely acidic over time. Few creatures can survive long in its territory.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's body continuously produces large amounts of toxic sludge, which it uses to absorb attacks or hurl at enemies. Its temperamental and violent attitude makes it feared amongst both Pokémon and Trainers alike.
author: ragingarthritis

entry: POKENAME has been spotted deep in the depths of waters troubled by heavy pollution. Extremely antisocial, it uses psychic powers from the gem it carries to repel anything that ventures too close to it.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME gathers pieces of scrap metal to serve as armor. Apparently, the quality of this armor, influenced by factors such as toughness and how loudly it resonates when struck, contributes to an individual POKENAME's status amongst the species.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME uses scraps of metal to fashion a crude skeletal structure that can support the ooze its body is made of into something more upright and menacing. It resides on trash-riddled beaches, where it feasts on the pollution to grow.
author: fireblade141

entry: POKENAME rarely uses its feet, preferring to slink along the ground. Despite the horrific smell, POKENAME's sludge is very good at treating head lice.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stealthily infiltrates the nests of rivals by slinking along as a puddle of sludge before revealing its true form for combat. Its unpleasant odor inhibits some of its stealth, but debilitates foes.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME stealthily infiltrates the nests of rivals by slinking along as a puddle of sludge before revealing its true form for combat. The crystallized poison shards embedded in its body are used as paralytic or disorienting weapons.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME's body is coated in a poisonous berry jam that is incredibly dangerous to consume. However, other Poison-type Pokémon adore the taste of POKENAME's jam.
author: mistymagius

entry: Their bodies are corrosive and can degrade most materials with great efficiency. They defend themselves with their tough, toxic claws and intense flames that could melt most metals.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME tunnels near city outskirts and defends itself by spraying corrosive sludge. Its burrows are soaked in a viscous fluid that is dangerous to touch.
author: .izik

entry: As POKENAME inhales air with its tubes to generate intense bass sounds, its gelatinous body reverberates. It scavenges junkyards for discarded pipes to incorporate into its body with the goal of creating more intense sounds.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Due to POKENAME's body being formed of corrosive chemicals, it will frequently poison playmates on accident. However, this doesn't deter POKENAME's liveliness.
author: aster_oid1701

entry: POKENAME lie patiently in wait within toxic spills and industrial waste, waiting for prey to pass by so they can pounce on it. Clean-up crews are advised to be aware of the possibility of a POKENAME attack during their operations.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The slime that drips off POKENAME's body causes migraines on contact, leaving those around it dizzy and nauseated. Strangely, the symptoms seem to naturally fade once people are out of POKENAME's vicinity.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are made of a toxic sludge that causes nearby plants to wither. They are frightened by water and will refuse to allow any of their sludge to touch it.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The slime covering its body is highly flammable and can combust at the slightest spark. There is talk of it soon being banned from entering power plants across Kanto.
author: .izik

entry: It is rumored that POKENAME was born from toxic waste burned in arson fires. This Pokémon can travel from city to city, flying with its wings of poisonous sludge in search of new filth to feed its body. It contaminates anything it touches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME rotates the spiral on its tongue to lull prey to sleep before it covers them in thick, viscous slime. This sludge immobilizes prey, allowing POKENAME to consume them effortlessly.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its hands to uproot poisonous plant life near its pond. It shoves these plants into its mouth to strengthen the poison slime coating its body, making it even more dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are made of a viscous and toxic fluid. If it ever loses focus and stops using its telekinetic abilities, its whole body will lose its form.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME gather spoons along their highly corrosive ooze to break them down and absorb the minerals inside of them. In battle, they use their psychic powers to rapidly rotate the spoons to fling their toxic sludge at opponents.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Formed from melted waste and burning chemicals, POKENAME soars across polluted skies in search of refuse to consume. Everything it touches is left corroded and lifeless.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It is rumored that POKENAME was born from toxic waste burned in arson fires. This Pokémon can travel from city to city, flying with its wings of poisonous sludge in search of new filth to feed its body. It contaminates anything it touches.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's flames are so hot, and sludge is so poisonous, that it's known for accidentally destroying villages. This leads to POKENAME feeling quite lonely.
author: lorddino.

entry: POKENAME exude horrid odors that deter most others from drawing too close to them. Despite this, they are often quite friendly and are happy to help with waste disposal by eating said waste, so some are kept around by some people.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME thrives in areas ravaged in pollution, swallowing any contaminated object whole. For anything that doesn't fit in its mouth, it spews out a powerful acid that melts them into a thick sludge.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME eat a plethora of trash daily and live in junkyards and landfills to remain close to their food source. They melt garbage in their large bell to turn objects into dark sludge.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME drifts through sewers, using its long tentacles to grab discarded items. Anything it dissolves contributes to the slime on its body, adding to its growing, sticky mass.
author: .izik

entry: Some say the first POKENAME was created when chemical runoff spilled onto an unlucky Tentacruel. POKENAME is an undulating mass of toxins and tentacles. The black sludge that drips from each limb can dissolve the toughest material in seconds.
author: sk372

entry: Many theorize that the fusion is incomplete, but thanks to Slowpoke's dim mind, it hasn't even noticed. It lazes near polluted rivers, living in blissful ignorance of its own mismatched form.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME dips its tail into ponds, releasing a thick purple fluid that clings to everything nearby. Despite its lilac scent, the substance is highly corrosive and dangerous to touch.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME slowly clean up garbage from beaches throughout the world. Their tail acts like a shovel that helps them scoop garbage into their mouths.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its shell is incredibly tough, supposedly due to being exposed to their own toxic bodies for so long. They can filter pollutants out of water to feed themselves, though this process also allows them to spew some of the cleanest waters.
author: infinex21

entry: The thick sludge that makes up POKENAME's body produces a vile stench. It slowly lumbers about in landfills.
author: mepp.

entry: The ooze coating POKENAME's metal body is harvested and boiled down into a thick paste. After the poison is boiled out, the paste can be mixed with mashed Watmel Berries and placed on crackers for a delicious yet tangy treat, enjoyed across Kanto.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME appeared from scenes of massive pollution spills in the ocean, absorbing other Grimer that formed at the same time. Their putrid odor is matched only by their appetite for the foulest of garbage.
author: sk372

entry: It can retract into its shell in under three milliseconds. It takes effort for POKENAME to maintain its shape constantly.
author: creeps_jr

entry: POKENAME sustains itself by taking in what would typically be dangerous particles in the air. Outside of cities, they can also be found by active volcanoes, absorbing unhygienic soot and ash.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME will hide in trashcans, awaiting those who incorrectly throw the wrong items in. It will hypnotize people into using proper bins, an effort recognized now to reduce overall pollution.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: It uses its sharp pincers to break apart glass and metal before consuming the trash. No dump is safe from its appetite.
author: .izik

entry: Its waterspouts are always leaking a toxic waste that shares a composition with its own slimy body. It can loose remarkably clean waters or toxic material of such concentration that it can corrode metal.
author: infinex21

entry: It is famously known to fire a Seed Bomb from the mortar on its shell. The more it grows, the farther and more accurate these shots will become.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME shoots jets of water with its small antennae, which distracts its foe long enough to hide in its shell. The shell barely fits its body, so it relies more on its water jets to avoid getting eaten.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a limited ability to move thanks to their lack of limbs. They rely on firing high pressure jets of water at precise intervals to jet themselves around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a limited ability to move thanks to their lack of limbs. They rely on firing high pressure jets of water at precise intervals to jet themselves around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME have a limited ability to move thanks to their lack of limbs. They rely on firing high pressure jets of water at precise intervals to jet themselves around.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME's cannons can alternate firing high-power water spouts or bolts of lightning. Firing both simultaneously for too long may cause it to explode from excessive energy output.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME lie on riverbanks and deliberately mimic the shells of sleeping Blastoise. They take great pleasure in unexpectedly exploding when curious Pokémon Rangers come by to check on the shell and make sure the Pokémon is alright.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME wield long metal clubs as weapons, storing them inside special hollows in their shells. They're able to swing these clubs with enough force to crack concrete, and caution is advised when nearby an angry POKENAME.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME possesses water jets at the back of each foot. The powerful force of water expelled gives its kicks extra speed and power in combat.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has waterspouts on the back of its hands which it uses to add extra power to its punches and attack opponents that have flanked behind it. Much of its shell has softened to increase its agility in combat.
author: pjporwoll

entry: The gigantic water cannon in POKENAME's mouth is dangerous to approach, but because of its weight, POKENAME can't aim it very well.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME needs to balance the mobility of its water cannons and the rigidity of its shell. It startles predators with its cannons but also depends on its shell to defend against pecking.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can shoot water from their mouths with a force of 30,000 PSI. They cannot maintain this output for long and use it to get a burst of speed to escape from larger Pokémon when endangered.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its cannon-like protrusion allows it to expel violent blasts of water at foes, often used to shoot down bird Pokémon that try to prey on its kind. This Pokémon will also expel water blasts to reposition itself during battle.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME have a dense shell protecting their blind spots, keeping them safe from larger Pokémon as they swim. If they are attacked, they turn to face their aggressor and fire a powerful jet of water at them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME shakes berries off branches with jets from its water cannons. Its wings provide both an emergency escape and added height for berry gathering.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are the arrogant, stubborn bullies of the seafloor. Their shell is nearly impenetrable, and every limb is packed tight with muscle, which they will often flex to psych out opponents. Lost limbs may regrow, albeit much weaker.
author: chinigan

entry: It is really controlled by a tiny Blastoise. Using jets of water to bombard foes and move with incredible agility, it's as skilled as a fighter pilot.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME can be seen performing for children at water parks. The sack on its back is filled with all sorts of water-themed party tricks.
author: patch

entry: POKENAME is difficult to pin down, since it is a versatile fighter. If the blades on its arms aren't enough to finish an opponent, it bombards them with water projectiles from its twin cannons.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME swims waters in search of the best source to turn into a new thermal pool. It blasts searing geysers from its tail when it's interrupted.
author: beatdoof

entry: When this brutal Pokémon eats, it lays flat on its stomach, shredding apart anything remaining underneath it with one thousand teeth.
author: fivetailedfurret

entry: POKENAME is very protective of its territory, charging at any intruders it spies. Once it gets at point-blank range, high-pressure water from its cannons launches its target across the horizon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leap out of the water to shoot berries out of trees with their cannon. If POKENAME fails to land back into the water, they flop around until they fall back in.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Some POKENAME do not properly develop wings and instead have to rely on jet propulsion from their cannons to remain airborne. They typically live around rivers and ponds so that they can easily replenish their water supply.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME has miniature cannons which can shoot lasers. They don't have any effect since the cannon is not strong enough.
author: watermelonchild

entry: POKENAME is heavily armed with strong water cannons and an impenetrable armored shell. During the war, they fought in many naval battles.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: It patrols its territory, blasting any unruly Pokémon with a deluge of water. Unlike Lapras, it goes berserk if anything tries to ride on its back.
author: pokepower

entry: POKENAME are able to completely vanish into deep water, often using this to intercept prey by crushing unsuspecting foes under their body weight. When they do not use their body weight to win fights, they will blast water from their cannons.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: It takes a lot of power to fire POKENAME's cannons. In battle, POKENAME runs and swims at high speeds to generate enough static to launch an electrified deluge.
author: haypile

entry: Contrary to popular belief, POKENAME actually fires clouds of boiling steam from its sprouts. It usually uses this ability to cook its usual prey, mollusk Pokémon, boiling them completely in a matter of seconds.
author: lemage22

entry: POKENAME fires projectiles at foes using the cannon on its tail. In the real world, it fires streams of normal high-pressure water; in cyberspace, it's a stream of pure binary code.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME fires its water cannons at anything that disturbs the branches it hangs from. Sometimes the recoil from the water cannon knocks it out of the tree.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME lives a solitary life residing in areas with frigid waters, and does not take kindly to intruders. The water shot from its cannon instantly freezes over when it hits a target, leaving them frozen solid.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME roars through the sky with speeds that rival fighter jets. It unleashes storms on foes to assert dominance, even though it is just as vulnerable to a bolt of lightning.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They release precise attacks from their waterspouts while flying quickly around their foes. They can fly fast enough that they can launch themselves with their shells facing forward and leave large craters in their wake.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME hangs from branches and shoots water jets at other Pokémon that come too close. Whenever it fires its water cannons, it is flung back from the recoil.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is equipped with three water cannons that shoot powerful jets of water. It marks its territory by spraying a mist laced with toxins, which also scares away other Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME channels psychic energy through its cannons, launching powerful telekinetic water blasts. It can control water with its mind, forming waves to strike down opponents.
author: thepandasharky

entry: POKENAME's excellent psychic prowess lets it freely control the movement of the jets of water fired from its shell. It playfully distracts others by whipping the water around in circles in spirals, rarely actually splashing someone.
author: sk372

entry: In combat, POKENAME creates leaves and vines out of water, which it uses to attack. During forest fires, groups of POKENAME will put themselves in danger to douse the flames.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's four cannons give it impeccable offensive capabilities, particularly the two movable ones on its antennae. The water it produces has a strong herbal scent and works well for brewing rejuvenating teas.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has a singular cannon that shoots out streams of water. It is strong enough to knock down berries from trees, which makes up a large part of its diet.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME relies on its cannons to propel it through the air. It has a peculiar muscle spasm that causes it to bobble its head once a second, even while flying.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It can accurately fire water jets from the cannon on its shell while moving extremely fast. They are utilized in the military in place of attack drones.
author: soup1900

entry: When preparing to strike, POKENAME coats the feathers on its wings with a dense layer of water before diving at full speed. The shell covering its body shields its most vulnerable spots from enemy attacks.
author: fiordaliso

entry: It fires high-pressure water jets from its two antennae to puncture its prey. Combining these two blasts can create ocean currents of over 60 mph.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's cannons sway hypnotically in the water, drawing the attention of curious Pokémon swimming by. When they get close enough, it blasts its unsuspecting prey with powerful beams of water.
author: cartoonhostage

entry: The cannon in its mouth fires water at exceptional power. However, POKENAME is so frail that it flies backwards afterwards, leading to some POKENAME using it as a means of travel.
author: imaginaryneon

entry: POKENAME dances on rocky beaches during clear nights filled with many shooting stars. It uses the water from its cannons to create mesmerizing displays.
author: cresselia8themoon

entry: POKENAME fire powerful bursts of water from their cannons when threatened. Due to their small size, these blasts send them flying backwards, causing them to ricochet off walls.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME flies through hurricanes and tropical storms without the risk of being whisked away. Its large water cannons stabilize its flight so that it does not get knocked off course.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will dance on beaches when the sun is out, their armor-plated petals making a low ringing noise as wind passes through. They spray water from the cannons on their heads, creating beautiful displays as they dance.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME store water within their shells before blasting torrents into the air large enough to rain down across multiple city blocks. They sing while walking through their rain, drumming on their shells to the beat.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Bales of POKENAME are commonly found floating above the rainforests. When wind travels through their turbines, these Pokémon collect and absorb moisture from the air to power up their Water-type attacks.
author: milchik

entry: POKENAME spend most of their lives out at sea, only returning to land to nest. They compete for mates through displays of power; whichever POKENAME can launch water from their cannon the furthest is almost always the winner of these contests.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME spend most of their lives out at sea, only returning to land to nest. They compete for mates through displays of power; whichever POKENAME can launch water from their cannon the furthest is almost always the winner of these contests.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The force of a water jet from a POKENAME's cannon can knock down small bird Pokémon. It swims faster than it crawls, so it is rarely found far from a body of water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME enjoys pranking others by spraying them with water from the jet on its prehensile tail. Its overzealous nature and the strength of its cannon often cause the target of the prank to be knocked out by the blast.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are capable of achieving incredible flight speeds despite their bulky shells that contain hefty waterspout cannons. They cannot fire water at full power from their cannons without securing themselves to something solid, like a rock.
author: infinex21

entry: The force behind POKENAME's cannons is so great that it can propel the Pokémon backward. However, it produces a gel that anchors it in place. Without proper training, it cannot sustain long bursts of fire.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Though friendly, POKENAME are slow-witted and prone to underestimating their own strength. It is common to find Pokémon that have inadvertently been trapped in a hug in muddy river banks by them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though friendly, POKENAME are slow-witted and prone to underestimating their own strength. It is common to find Pokémon that have inadvertently been trapped in a hug in muddy river banks by them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Though friendly, POKENAME are slow-witted and prone to underestimating their own strength. It is common to find Pokémon that have inadvertently been trapped in a hug in muddy river banks by them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The Seed Bomb it fires from the mortar on its back can explode midair, creating a colorful boom. People use it to create beautiful fireworks shows.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are too big to fit into their shell but instead have access to cannons that fire jets of water. They can quickly knock down berries from branches that hang over water and shoot down their predators as well.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's massive cannon gathers and fires concentrated psychic energy. When fired, the recoil is so immense that it often sends this Pokémon flying through the air.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME are slow swimmers, but love to jump into large bodies of water to play around in. They use the tiny cannons on their backs to squirt water at their friends.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME hunt for bug Pokémon by flooding their burrows with water, forcing prey to escape or risk drowning. Once the Pokémon reach the surface, they pounce to secure their next meal.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are typically gruff and standoffish with Pokémon they are unfamiliar with, making big displays of aggression and anger. They are friendly once they start to get to know others, enjoying having their shell stroked and patted.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The water jets on POKENAME's back provide momentum that lets it achieve a frightening amount of mobility for its size and weight. Those expecting a slow and lumbering foe will quickly find themselves clamped by its sturdy pincers.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use the cannons on their backs to shoot down hives of Combee, eating the honey inside. If they eat enough of it, they can even fire honey from their cannons.
author: santon5512

entry: In the shell on its back, POKENAME stores super-heated water that it can pierce and melt steel on contact. If this Pokémon retreats inside its shell, extreme caution is warranted, for it can use its water jets to turn itself into a dangerous missile.
author: notadoctor75

entry: POKENAME stalk Caterpie back to their burrows before flooding their burrows with water. If any Caterpie manage to escape through a different tunnel, POKENAME can fire long range jets of water to knock them unconscious.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME has two heads that communicate to launch accurate attacks from over 1000 yards away. Sometimes it gets dizzy from the two viewpoints.
author: dusknoir64

entry: POKENAME can adjust the temperature of the water stored in its body. From its cannons may come snowballs, icicles, hot steam, or blasts of fluid.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME spend most of their time swimming at the surface of ponds and lakes, begging for food from those passing by. When they get riled up they take a gulp of water then fire it at high velocity from the cannons in their shell.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME rarely fail at hunting because of their ability to sneak up on their prey. If they ever manage to escape, POKENAME unleash a torrent of water to overwhelm and subdue their prey.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME can fire pressurized jets of paint from its tail powerful enough to punch through wood. It creates its paint by collecting rainwater in its shell and mixing it with different berries.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME secrete fluids containing pigments that they load into their cannons. They build up pressure inside the cannons and fire the pigments all at once, painting a vista in a single blast.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: As POKENAME spins its body, it kicks up a small wall of water with enough force to topple a fully grown person. The water creates a slippery surface that allows for POKENAME to spin even faster.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME stabilizes itself with its tail as it fires jets of water at prey. This method of confusing prey allows it to come close enough to deliver a toxic bite.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The cannons on the stomach of POKENAME can fire bursts of milk strong enough to punch holes in stones. The odd trend of milk baths is fueled entirely with POKENAME milk, as the calcium-rich milk is said to create smooth skin and reinforce bones.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME are proud, prideful creatures that always demand respect from others. Other Pokémon fear POKENAME because of their ability to cause earthquakes and flood the area around them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses its waterspouts to help propel itself through the air quicker and to adjust its flight path with greater precision. It rests within deep-sea trenches, which has caused its shell to become hardier than most metals.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's dual tail cannons allow it to fend off multiple foes at once with blasts of water. A POKENAME that battles often must drink around a gallon of water per day.
author: hophoppip

entry: When POKENAME battle, they usually engage in duels reminiscent of cowboy standoffs. It frequently has feuds with Octillery.
author: teatedtiten

entry: Although it can't do much, POKENAME cares deeply about the cleanliness of beaches and the ocean. It often picks up plastic bottle caps and stores them in its pouch, and is known to bother people who litter on the shore.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME can electrocute opponents before blasting them with water to strengthen the attack. Because of POKENAME's small form, it can take a lot of energy to power its blaster, leaving it weak after using it.
author: daimposter_60614

entry: POKENAME has a powerful tail cannon that shoots jets of water and lightning bolts. Its flexible tail allows it to fire shots even when curled up in its shell.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Armies employ POKENAME as a long-range drone during recon missions. Since POKENAME is attuned to magnets, it can find its way back to its Trainer via magnetic signals and blast water or electricity from its cannons during combat.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME is capable of shooting rocks and water from its cannons. When it feels threatened, it will hide in its shell and use its tail as a mace.
author: codewolfie

entry: POKENAME house long cables within their shell that they can move at will, generating powerful electrical charges from them. They hunt within wetlands, using their electricity to stun their prey.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME carry reserves of water within their shell that they can fire at high pressure from their cannons. The scales forming their shell have a coating that generates a powerful electric charge as they move that they send through the water streams.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME carry reserves of water within their shell that they can fire at high pressure from their cannons. The scales forming their shell have a coating that generates a powerful electric charge as they move that they send through the water streams.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME creates thermal pools by firing high-pressure, 2,500 °C geyser shots into barren ground. Water and Fire-type Pokémon are naturally drawn to these pools, finding them to be an ideal environment.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME drink liquified clay to nourish their bodies and often surface with clay all over their bodies. If another POKENAME is nearby, they take turns giving each other a pressurized bath from their water cannons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It takes a lot of energy to fire POKENAME's waterspouts, but POKENAME has trouble photosynthesizing due to its blue leaves. It hunkers into its heavy shell to buy time to charge up for a good blast.
author: haypile

entry: POKENAME's twin cannons function independently of its body and can fire fierce jets of water with great strength and accuracy. However, on occasion they may go haywire, spinning and spraying water in every direction.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses the waterspouts that protrude from its shell to leap even greater distances while hunting down its prey. This makes it a very loud hunter, but that hardly matters if it reaches speed levels that are invisible to the naked eye.
author: speciessaladmallory

entry: POKENAME spends much of its time dutifully watering the plants of its forest home, ensuring healthy plant life all around. The cannons it uses for plant care double as highly effective defenses against intruders.
author: sk372

entry: These Pokémon are the defenders of the groups they travel with during the changing seasons. While traveling to warmer waters, POKENAME keep watch for predators that may attack the group and blast away threats using pressurized hot water.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME live near clay deposits and eat clay to nourish their bodies. Whenever the clay dries up and becomes hard, they hose down the clay to turn it into an edible slurry.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Using the jets from the shell on its back, POKENAME can blast highly pressured streams of water at an opponent. While the foe is recovering from the blast, it closes the distance between them and unleashes a flurry of devastating kicks.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: The talons on POKENAME's feet have the ability to latch to the ground and help this Pokémon stand its ground. Using the water cannons on the soles of its feet, POKENAME can launch itself at an opponent and deliver intense blows.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's legs are covered in tough scutes that protect its legs. Despite having this natural heavy armor, POKENAME has no issue running or jumping. The cannons in its feet can also aid in its movement when in a pinch.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's neck and back are protected by the shell on its back. This Pokémon does not hold back its attacks, using scalding and pressurized jets of water from its cannons. The sharp talons on its hands and feet can tear through foes with ease.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: While underwater, POKENAME will suck in air through their gills, using it to blow bubbles with their cannons. These bubbles are incredibly resilient, able to float rocks up to the surface.
author: santon5512

entry: The hard material comprising POKENAME's shell is actually dried mud. It can smash pieces of the shell into shrapnel and fire them at speeds that could dent a Shuckle's shell.
author: shocktopus1717

entry: It prefers to live on rocky beaches. Defensively minded, POKENAME builds small forts out of stones from which it can fire its waterspouts.
author: jarom_beyond

entry: POKENAME regularly get swept up in the emotion of whatever those around them are feeling and are always enthusiastic. During battle this works against them as the cannon on their head is too powerful, when they shoot water they go tumbling backward.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME uses a pair of twin water cannons on its arms to protect those it cares for. Once the high-pressure water is shot, it telekinetically manipulates the water to ensure it strikes even the most evasive of targets.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are able to manipulate water, keeping a store to weaponise within their shell. They can launch the water at high speed through the cannons jutting from their shell.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Haunting especially polluted mountain springs, POKENAME scares off trespassers while purifying the water. Their aqueous ring maintains perfect purity, and is sought for mead production.
author: ghostslythe

entry: When threatened, POKENAME will hide in its shell and then curl into a ball. POKENAME can still fire its bullets of water while in this form, and its high speed tackles hurt even more thanks to the spines on its shell.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME fire corrosive gel at prey through the cannons on their back. Due to the pressure that comes out of the cannons, they often lose their footing and end up missing their target.
author: quackquackattack

entry: In addition to changing the colors of its body and shell, POKENAME has mastered changing the color of its water. When it is happy, the colors are paint-like and vibrant. When it is nervous, the colors are oily and murky.
author: sockedpuppetart

entry: POKENAME is often used as a pressure washer to remove stains from homes thanks to its precise water jets. It communicates with others of its species via telepathy to coordinate cleaning.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME stores collected sticks in its cannons, which can hold up to 60 sticks each. When they reach max capacity, POKENAME shoots out the sticks, forming a dam.
author: dodoowner_

entry: With scales hardened like armor, POKENAME stalks challengers under the waves. It ambushes by using its arm cannon followed by breaking the surface with a deadly Mach Punch.
author: ghostslythe

entry: In order to fire, POKENAME will drop down onto all fours and begin pressurizing stored water within its shell. However, if a foe becomes too close for comfort before it is ready to release, it will lash out with its sharp claws.
author: fireblade141

entry: It launches seeds from the two cannons on its back to plant them in high places it cannot reach. It can fire Seed Bombs over 30,000 feet.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME protects their nestmates by standing guard at the entrance of their burrow. They vigilantly stand ready to shoot corrosive gel from their cannons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its jaws now function as a water cannon. As a result, POKENAME is a favorite amongst firefighters.
author: mossybanana

entry: It sits completely flat in shallow areas, waiting. When prey gets close enough, it will blast high-powered water out of all its cannons, allowing it to take down prey magnitudes larger than itself.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: POKENAME live near shallow rivers, using their large mouth to scoop up water. When threatened, they will fire a barrage of water blasts from their cannons, driving predators away from their young.
author: santon5512

entry: Research shows that the jets of POKENAME build up water pressure as they sleep. Due to the constant naps POKENAME takes, it is theorized that with enough time they could grow strong enough to level a mountain.
author: atlasmountain

entry: POKENAME's water cannons have enough strength to bore holes through the toughest of metals. It is incredibly lazy, however, and never fires more than a short burst to push away creatures that bother it while it lounges.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME zealously protect their nest from danger, and they are always ready to blast threats with a burst of corrosive gel. Their diligence is rewarded with affection and berries from their younger nestmates.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME shoot water out of their cannons when they surface for air. Their massive bodies can store a week's worth of air, but they enjoy the act of shooting water from their cannons, so they come to the surface almost daily.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Multiple high-power water cannons grow from POKENAME's shell, giving it a strong area of defense. The cannons are powered via nutrients from the soil that POKENAME absorbs through the palms of its feet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is considered by many to be an impenetrable dreadnought of a Pokémon. Few even see its attacks if it goes on the offensive, as it snipes them with water blasts from its cannon from up to a mile away.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are incredibly agile, quickly climbing to high ground before firing a barrage of water blasts from their cannons. Despite how tough it is, their armor is incredibly lightweight, allowing for easy maneuverability when faced with danger.
author: santon5512

entry: It can release such strong water jets from its waterspouts that it will launch itself off its own feet. Although many find this adorable, POKENAME's pride is fragile, and it will easily succumb to depression if laughed at in any capacity.
author: infinex21

entry: Naval crews commonly employ POKENAME as a maritime assistant, utilizing the mini-cannons on its shell to expel a steady stream of water for deck cleaning, or compressed air to clear away dust.
author: beatdoof

entry: POKENAME controls its detachable cannons, now able to manipulate the magnetic flow of the surrounding ocean. The water spouts it fires are frighteningly accurate, able to strike from 500 meters away.
author: beatdoof

entry: A legendary gun-sword said to be possessed by a shipwrecked, sunken pirate lord. It sinks ships to make others face its fate too.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME charges directly at its prey, relying on the shell that covers its entire body as armor before slicing them with pressurized water jets. Consequently, more than 50 ships sink per year due to this Pokémon.
author: aglt05

entry: From its tail, POKENAME can fire high-pressure jets of water strong enough to pierce the walls of a building. By rubbing its mane against its body, it builds up enough static electricity to unleash powerful electrified blows.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's steel-like shell acts as a near impenetrable shield, matched by the power of its Hydro Pump. Given its knightly appearance, it's often called "the Paladin of Water".
author: starpun.

entry: Its ribbons have adapted to spout highly pressurized bursts of water. These ribbons can fire water hard enough to tear through solid stone.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME glides silently through deep ocean trenches, its shell generating immense water pressure to crush obstacles. Ancient mariners revered it as a guardian of the sea's darkest depths.
author: segmoph

entry: POKENAME fires water as well as pointy rocks out of its cannons at incoming threats. Psychologists found out that this Pokémon doesn't like its blue colored scales, because they remind it of Kyogre.
author: over9001

entry: POKENAME has perfect vision and accuracy with its cannons, able to snipe targets from its home miles up in the skies. It's thought that at max power, its water shots could pierce completely through the planet.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME was once revered as a sacred fountain with an endless flow of water. Its deeds have since faded into myth.
author: squawkabairdy

entry: POKENAME can hit a target from across a football field with a precise burst of water thanks to the many calculations they perform in their head. There are only a few Pokémon that can move fast enough to confuse a POKENAME.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a kingly influence over their territory that allows them to command other Pokémon to do their bidding. In exchange for this influence, POKENAME are obliged to protect Pokémon with their tough shell and powerful cannons.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME will fire powerful water jets from their hands in order to propel themselves through the air. The cannon on their heads fires a toxic poison, coating targets in just a single shot.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME are common companions for aspiring ace Trainers, the cannons mounted on their heads offering the Pokémon great range in Pokémon battles. Their shells offer moderate protection but cannot deflect heavier attacks.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME love bubbles, so whenever they get the opportunity to wash clothes, they save the suds to play with after the fact. Their pressurized bodies can wash clothes in a matter of minutes, giving families more free time and clean clothes.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have superb hearing, able to track sounds from afar. When they sense a threat, they will use the high-powered cannons on their back to fire large blasts of magical water at the target before they even know a POKENAME is nearby.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME is capable of firing intense streams of water from its mouth. Many racecar circuits use multiple POKENAME to keep the stands clean and in case of emergency.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can shoot water with such pressure that it propels itself back many meters. It likes to use this as an unconventional escape method.
author: chorb33

entry: POKENAME, lacking any limbs, creates a miniature crew from its fused genetic material to man and reload its cannons. POKENAME often follow boats, protecting them from more aggressive Pokémon.
author: vibrationjaveline

entry: It sprays water from the waterspouts lining its wings to accelerate rapidly and to make precise adjustments to its flight trajectory. The more excited or agitated it is, the hotter its water becomes.
author: infinex21

entry: The fabric making up POKENAME's disguise is soft but sturdy, and the shell is resistant to attacks. They are able to spray small amounts of water from their cannons by squeezing hollowed berries under the fabric.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME blasts across the sky with its 200-PSI water jets. When it starts raining without warning, it is said that a POKENAME is nearby.
author: rkmaster25367

entry: POKENAME is a guardian of orphaned or abandoned Squirtle. It can sense the hearts and minds of people, and will only allow kindhearted Trainers to adopt one of its charges.
author: gerbopotato

entry: POKENAME is capable of unleashing highly pressurized water from each of its tail-cannons. It possesses control over the water it expels.
author: winchbeef

entry: It aims its tails like a fire hose, jetting out a scalding steam. Each of a POKENAME's nine nozzles specializes in spraying either fire or water, the number of which differs from one POKENAME to another.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: At least once a year, some POKENAME will use all their energy to launch themselves toward space with water. They fall dormant after exhausting all their energy and come crashing down, their shell-clad heads being the first to touch the ground.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME terraforms natural depressions into swamps by flooding the area with the massive cannon on its back. As the humidity slowly rises, POKENAME switch to shooting rocks at Bug-type Pokémon that migrate to these newly formed swamps.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's sturdy full-body shell gives it impeccable defenses. It pops its head through a hole in the top for surveillance, and extends a water cannon from the front to blast away anything that tries to mess with it.
author: sk372

entry: The bubble on its back has now fully grown into a flower. Most POKENAME live underwater where the sun can still reach them, as their flora are aquatic.
author: soup1900

entry: A clumsy Pokémon, POKENAME constantly sets fire to things with its tail. It then uses its cannons to put out the fire, usually using too much water.
author: incognito1234

entry: It uses its balloon-like body to suck in enormous amounts of water to fire out of its cannons. However, if POKENAME inflates to too large a size, it has a difficult time aiming its water jets.
author: empty_set

entry: POKENAME soak up water with the mysterious gel that surrounds their body and fire water from the cannons on their back. By opening pores within the gel bubble, POKENAME can store several liters of water as their body swells in size.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME prefer not to use their cannon and display it proudly as a trophy. If provoked, however, the cannon on a POKENAME can fire a near-endless supply of piercing water.
author: crumple_2

entry: POKENAME can fire out bursts of webbing from its cannons like netting that trap larger creatures. It takes advantage of the target's immobility to bite them and absorb small amounts of static electricity.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their spikes to cling to cave walls, absorbing moisture from the rock. Using this water, POKENAME can fire powerful blasts of water from the cannons on their heads, warding off predators.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME pry gigantic gemstones from deep underground and bring them to subterranean waterways to use as transport. During battle they keep their distance from their opponent, using blasts of water to fight from a distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME pry gigantic gemstones from deep underground and bring them to subterranean waterways to use as transport. During battle they keep their distance from their opponent, using blasts of water to fight from a distance.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are ferocious creatures that can crush metal with their jaws and clear paint and rust off old cars with a single blast from their cannons. Their domineering personality makes them difficult to train, especially if recently caught.
author: quackquackattack

entry: While POKENAME may appear to be wrapped in cloth, the material is sturdier than stone. POKENAME blasts precise streams of chilling water, almost seeming to detect where the target will be before they move.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME dances slightly slower than its pre-evolutions due to its heavier shell. The boiling water it shoots from its cannons can reach a temperature of 212 degrees Fahrenheit.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME are often found in filthy rivers and lakes, eating the trash that has polluted the water. The trash it eats mixes into the water it shoots out of its cannons.
author: darkweavile428

entry: POKENAME uses its blistering speed and rock-hard skull to take down even the largest ocean creatures. Many Hoenn sailors believe that a school of POKENAME was responsible for the great tragedy of the S.S. Cactus.
author: mbo1064.

entry: POKENAME emit powerful infrasonic blasts from the cannons protruding from their heads. They can use these blasts both as an offensive weapon and also as a navigation tool, listening for echoes to make up for their poor eyesight.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are capable of blasting water at supersonic speeds from their cannons, though they cannot maintain the pressure needed for the attacks long. They use this attack as a last resort, their bodies frail and unable to easily handle the recoil.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME are capable of blasting water at supersonic speeds from their cannons, though they cannot maintain the pressure needed for the attacks long. They lower their body to the ground before firing in order to protect themselves from the recoil.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: A single blast from POKENAME's cannon can coat foes with a sticky gel that clings to fur, feathers, and scales. Another blast can quickly wash away this gel, which is perfect for after POKENAME achieve victory.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME repeatedly fires steel-shattering jet streams of water from its arm cannons to brutalize foes. It uses the recoil from these blasts to smash with great force into buildings with its hardened shell during its destructive rampages.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can manipulate the tentacles housing water cannons, giving it excellent accuracy with its shots. If said tentacles are severed, they will grow back within a week.
author: sk372

entry: Using the cannons in their mouths, POKENAME will rapidly fire spikes at opponents. They store water within their bodies, helping to prevent them from overheating while attacking.
author: santon5512

entry: The cannon on POKENAME's head is incredibly accurate, with it able to snipe its target from incredible distances. When threatened up close, it will hunker down in its shell and start to spin, sending a storm of spines flying in all directions.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME flies with the cannons behind their head. In a pinch, they are able to slink back into their protective shell from high into the sky to land safely upon the ground.
author: camtft

entry: The water from POKENAME's cannons contains a substance that can be extracted and refined to make a potent weed killer.
author: kittyluv090

entry: POKENAME has two types of scales. The brown-colored scales grow into heavily armored shells used as a formidable defense. The blue-colored scales become heavy-duty ammo for its mighty cannons.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME are cowardly bullies, using their powerful water cannons to attack weaker Pokémon but tucking into their shell and crawling away at the first signs of a stronger Pokémon.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: The top of POKENAME's head, like its back, is covered by a thick shell that protects it from even the strongest impacts. The cannons on its back can release small but incredibly powerful water jets.
author: st4rdustyugure

entry: A valiant and rare woodland Pokémon that dwells near rivers, POKENAME can fire accurate pressurized blasts of water that could easily pierce the hull of a ship. It selflessly takes blows meant for other Pokémon, even strangers.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME congregate around ponds at night, attracted to the moon's reflection on the water. If provoked, they fire puffs of toxic powder from their tails.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME angers easily, becoming hostile at even the slightest provocation. It will then blast the agitator with scalding steam from its cannons.
author: incognito1234

entry: POKENAME fires muddy water jets from underground at extreme speed. The pressure is strong enough to pierce solid stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swallows water and expels it through its tails, using them like thrusters to propel itself with surprising speed. Engineers have studied this unique method of movement as inspiration for developing more efficient pump-jets.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME blasts torrents of water from its tunnels to knock prey from trees. It drags stunned targets like Venomoth beneath the dirt to feast.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have many openings on their bodies, with each capable of firing water. POKENAME commonly struggle to stay afloat, so to compensate, they use the jets on their backs to propel themselves when underwater.
author: ruben2309295

entry: POKENAME's shell is incredibly tough, shielding it from foes it often battles. Thanks to its agility, it can climb to the tops of trees, from where it takes aim and blasts its enemies with powerful water cannons.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME extends and retracts its water cannons in response to stress. Whenever it experiences a headache, the cannons contract and make it difficult to shoot water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on their large cannon to blast foes away. If an opponent can grab onto their cannon and stop them from attacking, POKENAME become an easy target.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME scoop up large amounts of mud using their mouths. They fire this mud from the cannon on their back, each blast causing tremors in the earth.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME produce a torrent of water from their cannons that propel them swiftly through the water. The cannons help them reach speeds that rival motor vehicles.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME rely on the cannons on their back to propel them through water since their round bodies lack the muscle mass for them to swim effectively. They often accidentally bump into other Pokémon, but few Pokémon get angry at them.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The angrier POKENAME gets, the higher the pressure and accuracy of its cannons. Its exceptional arm strength makes POKENAME an incredibly strong swimmer.
author: steamedveggies.

entry: POKENAME dwells in deep sea caves near the bottom of the ocean. It shoots electrically charged jets of water to take down foes.
author: mepp.

entry: The cannons on POKENAME's shell are capable of generating intense blasts of both flame and water. This versatility makes them highly popular among foresters and park rangers.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME are equipped with two powerful cannons used to shoot high-pressure streams. They are often loyal pets of firefighters because of their agility and strength.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It ejects scalding steam from its cannons. This steam can cause 4th-degree burns, meaning it'll burn through your skin and potentially kill you.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME have a protective shell that keeps them safe while they wait to evolve. The weight of the shell keeps them from being able to easily swim, so they use the twin cannons on their shell to blast themselves backward if they need to move fast.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Pokémon researchers in Kanto have observed POKENAME competing with Poliwrath within river environments for dominance. Though smaller, they theorise that POKENAME have an advantage thanks to the twin cannons they sport.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Its body is frail from years of nonstop meditation. In combat, it will summon a pair of powerful cannons that shoot water with great force.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: Fusion has granted POKENAME more flexible cannons with which to aim. Its water blasts have increased in power, as well as precision.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME assist in smithies, helping streamline the work by using their strength and multiple arms to hammer and quench metal. Locations using POKENAME report an increase in tourism.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME remain rooted in the ground, drawing water from the soil and storing it in their shells. When threatened, it unleashes a relentless volley of water bullets at its foe. For this reason, it is often kept by gardeners to protect their crops.
author: santon5512

entry: The shells that POKENAME gain upon evolution have grown to accommodate the cannons growing from their back. They tuck themselves into their shells during battle, preferring to stay on the defensive and blast water from afar.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME make their homes in marshes, hunting their prey through the grass. Their stomachs contain a powerful acid, which they fire from the cannons in their mouths.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME will use their tails like a hose, spraying powerful acid at their enemies in a high-pressure stream. This acid is capable of melting through solid steel.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME erode rocks by releasing torrents of water from the cannons on their back, making the rocks soft and edible. If POKENAME are desperate for food and are unable to locate rocks, they will eat silt and sand to nourish themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME burns their flames high into the sky in an attempt to lure in unsuspecting fire types to suffer a barrage of water from their cannon.
author: camtft

entry: A POKENAME's body is partly clad in a tough, armor-like shell. Though it often fights using horns and blasts of steam, it can unleash scalding water from cannons along its sides.
author: infinex21

entry: When cornered, it fires pressurized jets of water from the cannon on its tail. However, POKENAME's reflexes are quite slow, and it often launches its attacks too late, risking missing the target.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME polish their cannons with their fuzzy tails, making sure that they both shine the same brilliant white. If their tails get dirty, they will spray the entire area with water until they wash the dirt or the offender away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME's cannons are actually controlled by Shellder on its back. As a result, it's able to shoot extremely accurately and have no blind spots.
author: voxposs

entry: POKENAME can fire a large amount of bubbles from both of the cannons on its side. These bubbles are tinted with a bit of magnetism, making it easier to hit metal objects or Steel-type Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has precise control of its two cannons by manipulating magnetic waves to reposition them at will. Its keen eye can easily aim to hit targets from over 160 feet away with pulses of electrically charged water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: When a building is on fire, POKENAME work alongside firefighters to shoot jets of water at fires. Their versatile cannon-like baton allows them to put out flames from a long distance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is a semi-aquatic Pokémon of action with a secret identity. It is seen battling a Bimime and winning a large majority of the time.
author: aregularbigjoke

entry: Despite seeming to lack a normal head, POKENAME is able to sense its surroundings rather acutely. It is quite speedy and agile in combat, using leaping maneuvers to fire jets of water from its cannons at various angles.
author: sk372

entry: The water cannons growing from POKENAME's body have rudimentary functional brains of their own. POKENAME's main head can influence them to an extent, but they can act impulsively and fire water shots on instinct when startled.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME shoot chilling beams of water from their back cannons to push past floating ice as they swim through the world. These beams of water can quickly cause hypothermia in Pokémon that are not used to the cold.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Despite looking like a mass of undifferentiated sludge, the components making up the bodies of POKENAME have varying chemical compositions. The parts forming their chest and back are denser than the rest of their bodies, protecting them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME form from industrial runoff into aquifers and rivers. Their bodies are oily and float on the surface of the water; the oil produced from them provides buoyancy but also pollutes the water they live in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME form from industrial runoff into aquifers and rivers. Their bodies are oily and float on the surface of the water; the oil produced from them provides buoyancy but also pollutes the water they live in.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Fusion energy has fused POKENAME with its dormant DNA. Its shell is now indestructible; not even cannon fire can harm it.
author: zoroark73

entry: POKENAME lives similarly to Blastoise: its powerful shell allows for great protection, and the cannon allows for overwhelming offense. However, POKENAME is found far more often by the sea than it is other bodies of water.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME are found in humid environments where they conjure bubbles that contain spirits of the dead. Each bubble is capable of blasting a burst of water before popping, which releases the spirits inside.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME fires spiraling streams of water from the cannons on its back. Despite not being particularly powerful, the streams seem to put its opponents into a trance, making them unable to attack.
author: mistymagius

entry: Blasts of water shot from the cannon in POKENAME's claw hit with enough force to dent solid steel. It primarily uses it to repel other predators competing for the clams and shellfish it scrounges up for food.
author: sk372

entry: While at first glance this Pokémon may just look like a regular Blastoise, it has many unique markings on its body. These markings have been proven to be veins where the fusion genetics flow through.
author: soup1900

entry: Its appearance is extremely similar to that of Mega POKENAME. The large cannon on its back makes it look like a tank with legs.
author: soup1900

entry: Its appearance is extremely similar to that of Mega Blastoise. Unlike Mega Blastoise, however, it has many markings over its face and shell where fusion genetics are most visible. These markings glow faintly when it uses powerful moves.
author: soup1900

entry: Its appearance is similar to that of Gigantamax POKENAME. It has 31 cannons on its shell that it barrages endlessly against its foes.
author: soup1900

entry: Fusion has caused this Pokémon to awaken part of its Gigantamax genes, causing its appearance to be similar to that of Gigantamax Blastoise. It can volley a multitude of blasts using the many cannons on its shell.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME protect themselves with tough shells discarded by other Pokémon, attaching them to their back with a sticky sap. The sap they use contains a mild paralytic toxin that causes a numbness in anything that touches them.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME frequent tide pools in search of food. The helmet and weapon they use are made of dried coral.
author: mepp.

entry: While bubbling playfully, POKENAME sometimes spits out a pearl by accident. These rare gems are prized by collectors and sold at auction.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sheds its thick scales every month, leaving itself vulnerable until they grow back. It usually swims along the seafloor, looking for small seashells to eat.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME climbs waterfalls in search of quiet pools. There, it creates and hides its dazzling pearls far from prying eyes.
author: .izik

entry: Its hair is extremely hard and will only become malleable when wet. The fibers are used in clothing that is worn in fashion shows.
author: .izik

entry: Schools of Magikarp often integrate POKENAME into their ranks for aid in survival. While unable to swim as quickly, POKENAME's tough shell means hunters will waste time futilely trying to prey on it while the Magikarp flee to safety.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME nestles itself in rocks and patches of barnacles, disguising itself as a large shell. Any unfortunate diver who gets close will be met with its thrashing tail and snapping jaws.
author: evilgammon

entry: Riding on a POKENAME is said to be very safe, as its tough shell is strong enough to survive multiple Sharpedo attacks. It needs very little food to keep going, only needing one or two berries a day.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME's primary source of food is tough-shelled Pokémon like Cloyster. Its blades are sharp enough to carve through the shells, tearing them apart so it can feast on what lies inside.
author: sk372

entry: The fossilized remains of POKENAME have been discovered in coastal caves. Its tough shell plating that covers its body is as hard as steel.
author: mepp.

entry: Wild POKENAME usually live in Kanto, but when it gets too hot, they migrate to other regions. Most travel to northern Sinnoh, though many do not survive the perilous journey and faint, washing up on desolate islands or distant shores.
author: duskit___

entry: While sleeping, POKENAME generates faintly glowing yellow pearls. Charged with residual electricity, the pearls are left behind like a breadcrumb trail as POKENAME travels.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME lives in the deep ocean, its durable shell protecting it from the crushing pressure down there. Its lure gives off a dull red light, allowing it to see in the dark without giving away its location.
author: mistymagius

entry: It holds onto a Tropical Shell that stores static electricity, which turns the shell a bright red. Whenever it discharges the electricity in battle or otherwise, its shell returns to a greyish purple.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME scavenge for trash along the sea floor, searching for food with their tongues. Using their tongues as a propeller, these Pokémon can swim backwards at high speeds.
author: santon5512

entry: When other Pokémon disturb POKENAME, usually large bottom feeders, POKENAME will run its tongue over their body, grabbing any nutrients that have been caught. They then return to dormancy, using barely any energy.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME collect objects, then polish them with their tongues until they shine. Some treasure hunters keep them to help clean their findings.
author: rhysanthemum

entry: It licks objects with its long tongue when it has a fondness for them. Wild POKENAME are often seen licking shiny objects vigorously.
author: aberry8286

entry: Groups of POKENAME are used by sailors to send messages to other members of their fleet. Their shells are soft and able to change shape at will.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its tongue to detect danger around its shell. At night, POKENAME fully encloses itself to sleep.
author: northkira

entry: POKENAME nest in river beds using their tongue to make a small hole. They do this so they can clamp on the tails of Slowsparce that put their tails in the water.
author: equation8573

entry: A mischievous and impish Pokémon by nature, POKENAME attacks other mollusks to steal their pearls, which it sees as trophies. As it ages, the shell protecting its head grows at an increased rate in comparison with the rest of its body.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME use their mucus to create a thick layer of bubbles beneath their shell. They use the bubble layer as a lubricant, dragging themselves along it across the sea floor using their tongue.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In addition to its incredibly hard shell, POKENAME secretes a sticky foam that makes it hard to eat. Because of this, it has very few predators, as most decide it is not worth the effort to hunt.
author: secondegg

entry: After crafting pearls, POKENAME tucks them into its thick fur. It later uses them to decorate its icy nest with intricate care.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME shuffles along the seafloor, eating any small creatures in its path. It can't climb over rocky terrain, so it will instead use its strong tusks to break through rocks and coral in its way.
author: mistymagius

entry: Its fins are too small to swim, so it must drag itself along the ocean floor to move. When threatened, POKENAME will burrow into the sand, leaving only its hard shell exposed.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME hides in the seafloor, posing as an empty shell. When prey swims by, it is caught in the blink of an eye by POKENAME's deceptively long tongue.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Overnight, POKENAME forms glistening pearls in its tail. By morning, it swims ashore and gently gifts them to unsuspecting beachgoers.
author: .izik

entry: Although the bottom of its body is soft and tender, the top is as hard as stone. If it becomes both beached on its back and becomes unable to move from its spot, it licks its squishy half to paint on a mucus that helps it retain moisture.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's periwinkle camouflage allows them sneak up on nests of aquatic Pokémon. Their bivalve shell has the ability to unhinge and swallow eggs whole.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME uses the brightly coloured fluid on its tail to paint scary faces on its shell. While the faces often look goofy to humans, this discourages many Pokémon from trying to crack POKENAME's shell open.
author: periperi_chicken

entry: POKENAME lives near frozen lakes, smashing through the ice with armored, hair-like appendages. Despite how heavy it is, it is able to swim effortlessly without sinking.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME buries itself into the mud near swamps in order to keep cool. It is easily spooked, and uses its tongue to scoop up muck and toss it at anything that gets too close for comfort.
author: sk372

entry: It moves by releasing a pressurized blast of seawater from its rear to launch itself. It's not the best at angling these blasts, and tends to crash into objects as it flies.
author: hophoppip

entry: The shell of a POKENAME is as hard as a thick-plated steel hull. As a result, they live peaceful lives underwater, being nearly impenetrable by normal means. Their only fear is the gigantic claw of a Kingler.
author: dukefrogpeasant

entry: POKENAME's tongue is sensitive enough to alert it to the movements of others nearby. If it detects the approach of something, it whirls around and charges into others, striking them with the sturdy half-shell on its cranium.
author: sk372

entry: It sleeps nestled in underwater caverns, using its thick tongue to plug the entrance and block currents. Some believe a massive pearl lies deep within its body, but no one has ever retrieved one from a wild specimen and lived to tell the tale.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME slides across frozen lakes, spitting out bright blue pearls as it glides. The number of pearls it leaves behind changes with its mood.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is unable to retract its long tongue, therefore it must frequently dip it into a special shell to prevent it from drying out. It fiercely guards this shell, and will wrap its sticky tongue around anyone who gets too close.
author: jaminmcready

entry: POKENAME's pearls shimmer with three ever-shifting hues. Under proper lighting, they seem to ripple like water, fetching steep prices from nobility.
author: .izik

entry: The hardened shell on its face will protect it from most damage. When they fight, they will close their shells and charge head first into foes.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME has a very friendly disposition, often licking others affectionately with its large tongue. If threatened, it turns tail and retreats, releasing fireballs from the shell on its rear.
author: sk372

entry: A large tongue extends from POKENAME's shell to gather kelp and algae. It eats very little except during autumn, when it feeds almost nonstop.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME sings at a frequency that resonates underwater so that it can put other Pokémon to sleep. Divers wear specialized headphones that produce static noise to avoid falling asleep.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Most of POKENAME's body is covered by a hardy calcium-based carapace that keeps it safe from incoming attacks. While its limbs are stiff and clumsy, it uses its large, agile tongue to grasp and manipulate objects.
author: regulavish

entry: POKENAME has been noted to be self-conscious of its appearance and rather shy, remaining still and shut when others are around. It only opens up in the presence of those it implicitly trusts.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME can produce pearls in its shell-like bud, making up to 5 pearls a week. It is very protective of its pearls and will swing its bud at anyone that tries to steal them.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME have hard, translucent bodies that can repel devastating attacks. POKENAME use their tongue to fire off psychic energy, which leaves them exposed to danger.
author: npshi

entry: POKENAME wears a shell as its mask. Despite not having eye holes, it proudly wears the mask to defend itself from dangerous Pokémon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Its shell serves as a lightweight yet durable helmet. It uses its tongue to sense air currents and navigate through dark caves.
author: staghorn

entry: POKENAME rely on deceptive tricks to obtain jewelry. They leave their shell open to entice people to reach for the pearl inside before snapping shut. Once they have a hand nestled in their shell, they remove any jewelry the person may have.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME attempts to frighten others away by roaring and flailing its large tongue about wildly. It gets embarrassed and hides its face within the shell on its neck if this tactic fails to scare its target.
author: sk372

entry: The pearls made by POKENAME are so cold they freeze most surfaces instantly. Touching one barehanded can cause frostbite.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has cool breath and a tongue that's cold to the touch. It's popular in warmer regions for helping cool down its owners on hot days.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME creates icy blue pearls that remain cold even in sunlight. High-end cafés use them as elegant drink chillers for their elite patrons.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's shell resembles a Sharpedo, scaring off potential predators. Grit caught within the shell becomes polished into a pearl, which it blasts out of the star-shaped hole in the shell top, shattering the pearl into the shape of sharp teeth.
author: pjporwoll

entry: It's said children who have drowned turn into POKENAME, instead of Phantump. POKENAME constantly shakes and shivers from the icy waters they come from.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Sometimes divers report reaching for a cluster of 4 pearls on coral reefs, only to be attacked by a wild POKENAME. If its pearls are polished regularly, it reflects the most beautiful version of its beholder.
author: leonian1586

entry: POKENAME shells grow into elaborate structures reminiscent of flowers, hard calcite forming into petal-like growths. Their shells allow them to camouflage themselves within coral reefs, blending into the reef almost seamlessly.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME crawls along coral reefs and licks up meals of detritus from the safety of its venomous dome. Even though it is dangerous to harvest, its core body is sweet and tender, but very finicky to cook as it will burn and turn rubbery quickly.
author: pjporwoll

entry: Clamshell mushrooms grow on POKENAME's back. It's common practice to use these mushrooms as an ingredient in seafood dishes.
author: .realthree

entry: POKENAME can't actually swim, so it wanders the seafloor looking for small mollusks to eat. The horns on its head contain poison, which can cause shivering in its victims.
author: mistymagius

entry: When threatened, POKENAME spits shimmering pearls at predators. With a flick of psychic energy, it curves them mid-flight, creating a distraction while it escapes.
author: .izik

entry: When threatened, POKENAME mix their saliva with the foamy substance on their collars, creating a soapy mixture that smells terrible. Pearls that form in their shells maintain a slippery surface even when cleaned and polished.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME inhabit shell-like structures resembling pumpkins, and researchers remain uncertain of their origin. No one has ever observed a POKENAME outside of its shell.
author: elite01.

entry: The fire atop a POKENAME's head is fueled by oxygen stored within the POKENAME's shell, allowing it to burn strongly even while underwater. To flee from predators, POKENAME create a burst of flames from their mouths to propel themselves away.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: Its body can compress until it is entirely enclosed within its two shells. Each year, POKENAME produces a single heart-shaped pearl, and if you find one by pure chance, you are said to be fated to find love.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME periodically produces small violet pearls as it digs through soil. Jewelers collect these pearls to craft modestly priced accessories.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME emerge as noxious fumes from abandoned graves. The musty air chokes and suffocates those who seek to pilfer these forgotten resting places.
author: ozydamians

entry: POKENAME rests at the ocean bottom, taking flight once a week to locate other food sources. It carries large amounts of water inside it to spit at anything that tries to attack it while airborne.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME is quite timid and will keep its shell tightly shut to protect itself from danger. However, if the shell remains too tight for too long, it can begin to suffer from severe migraines.
author: mistymagius

entry: If exposed to too much sunlight, the shell on its head will dry out and crack. The saliva that drips from its tongue is edible and has a tangy flavor.
author: .izik

entry: Because most of its body is tender and sensitive, POKENAME trains itself to be nimble and mobile. It excels at blocking attacks with the parts of its body shielded by sturdy shell pieces.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME live in swampy areas along the coastline. They use their tongue to reposition themselves if they fall over.
author: elite01.
