entry: The cries of POKENAME are unsettling, which are able to echo no matter their location. Kantonian folktales say that hearing POKENAME's echo three times in a single day will create a shadow that mirrors your movements.
author: npshi

entry: The sinister spectral energy exuded by a POKENAME allows it to control its legs and pincers separately. They will often use their pincers, and the face-like markings upon them, to startle and entrap prey.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME are usually found near Trainers' Schools, using their cuteness to get honey snacks from students. If someone were to try to steal these snacks, POKENAME will give them a stare that causes feelings of despair in said thief.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME are considerably feared by many people and Pokémon alike given their appearance in tandem with their proven might. Yet, in truth, they are mostly just mischievous and just use fear as a means to prank others.
author: infinex21

entry: The purple toxin covering POKENAME glows pink when separated from its body. Despite its sludgy form, it leaves ethereal footsteps wherever it travels at night that resemble human feet and glow in the dark.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are apex predators that combine both stealth and ethereal attacks to subdue prey. They are shrouded in an amethyst veil that obscures their movements and makes attacks hard to predict.
author: quackquackattack

entry: Experimentation has granted this Pokémon extreme speed and knowledge. It uses these gifts to travel the world and experience all it can.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME will meld into the shadows, waiting for the perfect opportunity to leap out and overtake its victim. It can leap elegantly from shadow to shadow as if it were swimming in water.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME has been known to create whirlpools large enough to sink ships. Some believe it's searching for friendship, hoping to find kindred spirits.
author: char_latte3412

entry: POKENAME lurk inside webcams of office workers that work from home and reveal themselves during meetings to frighten their coworkers. Their bulbous limbs wave in the background to direct attention to themselves.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME love to take over webcams and linger in the background, frightening many office workers who are working from home. Attempts to fix the device usually end when POKENAME decide to move on.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It has been said that POKENAME can see out of any painting it has created in its lifetime like another set of eyes. At the very least, it has a supernatural link with them: it becomes upset if one of its paintings is marred, even if it is miles away.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME intimidates other Pokémon by flexing muscles in its hood. This causes its prey to become paralyzed with fear, preventing them from escaping.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME manipulates shadows to confuse explorers in dark caves. It uses this disorientation to strike its prey with great precision.
author: .izik

entry: It's said that the spirits of people who disappeared on cold mountains live again as POKENAME. Its body is nearly indestructible, so it's always seeking an opponent who can hit it to fight with.
author: nyoomymph

entry: POKENAME's tail serves as both a weapon and an extra eyeball, which makes ambushing it a difficult task.
author: 8xviktor

entry: By using the entangled Gastly, POKENAME can generate a shadowy gas. Using this gas, it can create a special shadowy field, stealing all the heat and controlling every shadow within its radius.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME often plug their tails into the generators of large hotels and cause paranormal events throughout the building. They do this until they are caught, or the building goes out of business.
author: enemyphase

entry: Some suspect POKENAME comes from another realm, and must use energy to sustain itself in our world. If it does not occasionally devour sources of electricity, POKENAME begins to become translucent and fade from the naked eye with visible panic.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME forcibly sticks their electric wires into victims. This forces them to enter into a comatose-like state, letting POKENAME eat their dreams.
author: bigoljax

entry: Some suspect POKENAME comes from another realm, and must use energy to sustain itself in our world. If it does not occasionally devour sources of electricity, POKENAME begins to become translucent and fade from the naked eye with visible panic.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME chase Trainers and their Pokémon out of haunted forests to keep their territory free of intruders. Many Trainers report nightmares of being chased by a POKENAME long after the encounter.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME form in areas being urbanised and are believed to be the spirits of the plants that have been killed. They haunt construction crews, doing what they can to disrupt machinery and stall progress.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME form in areas being urbanised and are believed to be the spirits of the plants that have been killed. They haunt construction crews, doing what they can to disrupt machinery and stall progress.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Rooms where POKENAME resides constantly change from hot to cold due to it absorbing heat before randomly releasing it back. It stalks emails to know the perfect time to strike its victim and take their life force.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME hides inside of life-saving electronics, waiting for the perfect moment to corrupt the device in hopes of stealing an ailing victim's life force. It avoids notice by exiting through computer networks.
author: soup1900

entry: This variant of POKENAME was initially just an attempt to troll the moderators of a certain server. No one knows why it was brought to life.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME is drawn to heat, but cannot produce much of its own. It often sneaks into campfires or huddles against larger Fire-type Pokémon, inadvertently draining their energy while it tries to warm its ghostly body.
author: ambrosia04

entry: Found in marshes, POKENAME will appear to people and Pokémon stranded in deep bogs. It watches ominously, providing neither comfort or assistance.
author: char_latte3412

entry: This Pokémon stalks its victims at night for fun. If you were to look in a mirror, you might see it standing behind you, vanishing as you turn around.
author: zerocipher

entry: Many mistake POKENAME for costumed children. It's capable of conjuring shadows to aid it in battle, although it uses them more often to show off.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME uses the an empty shell as an asset for its misdeeds. If you see what appears to be a Shedinja shell with an eerie pink glow, do not approach it.
author: mistymagius

entry: During the darkest hours of the night, POKENAME can be seen floating serenely through the streets. If caught in a streetlight, its shadow will be seen falling from its black eyes and casting a creepy visage.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: It is said that POKENAME appears when darkness falls, amusing itself by frightening children who have not yet returned home. Its spines are filled with a highly toxic venom that keeps other wild Pokémon at a distance.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME come out at night, blending into the darkness save for the face-like patterns upon their bellies. If one sees a glowing face seemingly suspended mid-air, they should flee, or else a POKENAME's tongue will catch them and drain their energy.
author: infinex21

entry: Its public consensus is that POKENAME always has a touch of evil. Despite its incredible brain capacity, they'll load incredibly complex mental tasks onto the neurons of their victims, often leaving them beyond recovery.
author: epping_forest

entry: POKENAME's body is made of poisonous smoke that can solidify when needed. It uses this ability to deliver powerful punches during battle.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is mean spirited and ought to be avoided. It takes joy in pranking people, especially if it hurts them in the process.
author: chaotic_aspergers

entry: The fins on its arms are said to take a year off your life each time you touch them. In reality, they do nothing.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Ghostly auras trail behind POKENAME's limbs as it flies through the night skies. It circles a home for weeks, hidden in the shadows, before it haunts them in the night and feasts on their dreams and fear.
author: sk372

entry: The gourd on POKENAME's back can detach and swoop around like a ghost. It does so to scout around for prey, and to fly into people's houses at night.
author: rytthigar

entry: POKENAME revels in terrifying travelers passing through in the night. Hiding in the shadows, it illuminates part of its huge false mouth, so its victim becomes traumatized by the sight of glowing eyes and a massive grin full of sharp teeth.
author: sk372

entry: Legends tell of POKENAME standing guard near grieving mothers in cemeteries. Its presence is believed to bring comfort to those in mourning.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can open its mouth to an unnerving length of nearly six feet. Some believed a prolonged exposure to its inside granted divine visions, a claim later disproven by very soggy experimentation.
author: .izik

entry: To lay eyes on POKENAME's dark scarlet gaze is to be cursed, eternally lost in the dark forest. The snag atop its back is inhabited by various ghosts, which are carried by POKENAME to realms unknown.
author: beatdoof

entry: This deceitful Pokémon has an affinity for causing chaos. It often pickpockets people for fun and throws away any item that doesn't catch its eye.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME casts out collections of cackling shadows to intimidate all who hear them. They possess an odd power to draw anyone they pass back towards the central body, allowing it to feed on the captive audience's fears.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: If you feel a chill in the dead of night, run into the nearest light and watch for shadows. It may be a POKENAME coming to claim your life force.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Mostly lurking in dark corners, it is said that when POKENAME's blades rub together they create an unnerving metallic sound. Historians predict that fairytales linking scissors to death originated from those frightened by this Pokémon.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: Mostly hiding in the shadows, it is said that when POKENAME's blades rub together they create an unnerving metallic sound. Historians predict that fairytales linking scissors to death originated from those frightened by this Pokémon.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME was featured in a recent commercial. Interestingly, it was two rival Trainers who fused their Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It is said that POKENAME is the spirit of an ancient samurai that returned from the Ghost World. It assaults its prey by leveraging its invisibility and delivering slashes that originate from other dimensions.
author: agtl05

entry: It's said those split in two by the wings of POKENAME have their souls eviscerated, denying them an afterlife and erasing them entirely.
author: vaporvenator

entry: POKENAME uses illusions to slowly sneak up on an unsuspecting victim, sinking into their shadow when close enough. The victim will shudder and feel cold chills when their shadow is taken over.
author: grannyjojophone

entry: When walking with its Trainer, it prefers to hide in their shadow. If you are touched by its ghostly arms, you will experience a strong chill.
author: melodydelune

entry: Some old stories speak of how a POKENAME can quell any foe with the touch of its feelers, even during battle. But recent studies have shown this is only technically true, as its feelers will siphon the life force of whoever they touch.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME was featured in a recent commercial. Interestingly, it was two rival Trainers who fused their Pokémon.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME fights viciously and without restraint. It aims to break a foe's spirit first, then their body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: At midnight, POKENAME swoops down to snatch up prey to take them to somewhere unknown. Clouds cover the moon when this happens.
author: skymaster426

entry: POKENAME is said to detest clocks, going out of its way to alter time on all clocks around, even trapping people in time loops as payback for owning one. Many horologists and physicists have united in their hatred of it, leading to a bitter rivalry.
author: backgroundnoisegalore

entry: POKENAME fights viciously and without restraint. It aims to break a foe's spirit first, then their body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME fights viciously and without restraint. It aims to break a foe's spirit first, then their body.
author: bobosmith01

entry: If you suddenly feel an immense chill, a POKENAME is stalking the area near you. It feeds off of heat sources and enjoys striking fear into the hearts of people around it. It is not recommended to walk alone when a POKENAME is around.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME makes a habit of hiding in the shadows of those who have mistreated younger girls, in order to haunt and punish them for their behavior. It can unleash devastating blows using both its kicks and its long ears.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME are quite cuddly, often licking their trainers before bumping their caps against them. A few reports indicate that some POKENAME display agitation at humans who wear blue overalls.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: The gel around POKENAME's body creates shadow-like stains across anything it touches. POKENAME will create multiple fake shadows to scare and torment its victims.
author: mistymagius

entry: This variant of POKENAME is significantly more pessimistic and apathetic. There's an old folktale which implies that it once served a ruined king.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Rumors suggest that POKENAME originate from another world. They are mischievous tricksters by nature.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME is known for playing rude pranks on those lost in deserts at night. It creates convincing illusions of city lights, often tricking the lost deeper into the sands.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME swims through desert sands at night at incredibly high speeds. Should it spot prey like Cacnea, it bursts from the sand and unleashes a devastating Night Shade.
author: .izik

entry: Rumors suggest that POKENAME originate from another world. They are mischievous tricksters by nature.
author: theartemis1

entry: POKENAME phases in and out of this mortal plane, hunting both the body and the soul of its prey. Its screech is bone-chilling and, somehow, perfectly silent.
author: archserpent

entry: POKENAME often tries to lurk in the shadows of Trainers or other Pokémon, but its scorching hot body makes it hard to be discrete. If a POKENAME does this to its Trainer, it's often a sign of a good bond between them.
author: toast_licker_500

entry: POKENAME enjoys starting fights above anything; usually ones that it can't win easily. After being defeated, it gets up as if nothing happened.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Its two heads plot amongst themselves, looking to cause mischief. They take turns scaring people, competing to see which of them is scarier.
author: _snakeywakey_

entry: POKENAME loves creeping around to scare unsuspecting Trainers. Some theorize it gains power through fear while others mark it as a simple prankster. Keep your senses sharp when travelling through POKENAME's territory, or you may be in for a fright.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME carefully chooses victims to haunt and put through a test. Those that endure a week of its nightly hexes and visions will have it appear before them to grant a wish.
author: sk372

entry: This Pokémon has a mischievous nature and tends to hide in the shadows of people whose aura seems weaker, playing small tricks on them. Though it appears to be just a prankster, it is actually very insecure and trains in secret to grow stronger.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME is constantly thinking of methods to torment others in cruel, sadistic ways. The only thing holding it back is its laziness.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME is a violent combination of malicious and hyperactive. Thankfully, its attention span and memory retention are astonishingly short.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME's flower can take on vivid colors if it steals heat from a living being, which it does by hiding in its prey's shadow and waiting for an opportunity. Old tales say that anyone who inhales the fumes from the plant on its back will be eaten.
author: starryeyedmemoriam

entry: POKENAME is a rare fusion, but it is especially unwelcome on Pokémon teams because of how it unnerves its teammates. The fire it spews is not harmful, but does inflict its target with disheartening chill and foreboding dread.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME tends to form a partnership with Murbull. POKENAME has a tendency to rampage, but when paired with Murbull it chooses not to. Usually.
author: mirby

entry: POKENAME coats its long tongue with saliva to lift prey into the air. It uses this peculiar method to transport its catch while flying.
author: .izik

entry: It hunts in murky bogs by eating its prey's shadow. Having your shadow eaten by POKENAME feels like pins and needles all over your body. If it eats your entire shadow, you disappear.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: Fusion has awakened POKENAME's dormant genes. It constantly emanates unstable spectral energy from its small body.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME is even more ruthless than the sum of its parts. The venom from its horns drains its victims' life force, siphoning it away to POKENAME.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME is even more ruthless than the sum of its parts. The venom from its horns drains its victims' life force, siphoning it away to POKENAME.
author: bee4082

entry: POKENAME travels with the spirit of its deceased kin. They work in tandem to take down any threat before them.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME bites into chunks of ice and snow to maintain its frigid body temperature. It will sleep during the winter months, basking in the cold.
author: .izik

entry: When POKENAME laughs, it releases a chilling mist that freezes the surface of the surrounding area. This frost lingers as an ominous warning to intruders.
author: .izik

entry: It absorbs discarded garbage along with the emotions left behind by those who threw it away. The largest specimens rarely inhabit landfills, preferring the forgotten homes of compulsive hoarders.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is a capricious, deadly predator of the sea. If your ship catches POKENAME'S attention, hope that it is more playful than hungry.
author: opossiblymage

entry: POKENAME silently waits in forests, pretending to be one of the many trees. When any passerby comes, it reveals itself and traps them with its ghostly roots before draining the life out of them.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's four eyes help it spot prey easily. Its saliva contains a toxin that quickly paralyzes whatever it catches.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME can turn incorporeal while flying to avoid obstacles in its path. This skill lets it navigate treacherous cave systems with ease.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long wings to tickle others from the shadows. Its giggles gives it away.
author: shayzis_ozaki

entry: The fusion process kept both consciousness separated, Gengar taking control of the body while Altaria can only watch.
author: shayzis_ozaki

entry: The fusion process kept both consciousness separated, Gengar taking control of the body while Altaria can only watch.
author: shayzis_ozaki

entry: POKENAME possess the statues found in ruins, using them as makeshift bodies to move around. Their spiritual power is corrosive and causes the metal in the statues to break down and decay, leading them to roam in search of new statues to possess.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME possess the statues found in ruins, using them as makeshift bodies to move around. The power of some POKENAME is so great that they completely envelop their new bodies, warping and twisting them beyond recognition.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: In the correct amount, POKENAME's toxic nectar can be used to cure illness, but any mistake in the dosage can cause severe hallucinations and death.
author: malxire

entry: When POKENAME is energized by life force energy it stole from others, it becomes very frenzied and eager to take even more. It has the ability to cast large, pitch-black shadows over an area to hide its presence and frighten its victims.
author: soup1900

entry: Levitational abilities allow POKENAME to perform complex wrestling maneuvers in mid-air. It leaves its foes stunned by the combination of strength and agility.
author: .izik

entry: The fungi on POKENAME have become sentient and completely drained the host, leaving a grey husk behind. They have very limited mobility.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Its shadowy frills waver gently in the breeze, but they may suddenly expand. One might find oneself with two shadows late at night as POKENAME does this.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: In the nights of ancient times, it silently roamed the tundra. It startled other Pokémon by flaring its frightening frill, then fed upon their fear.
author: wigglypon

entry: POKENAME lures people in with its beautiful singing. Once the mood has been set, it's broken by its violent scream, temporarily deafening the victim.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME uses its haunting voice to scare unsuspecting victims. It finds enjoyment in seeing their reactions.
author: ohok3441

entry: POKENAME's white fur is dry and scratchy. In battle, it can use its mane to grab opponents.
author: ohok3441

entry: When it feels threatened or challenged, POKENAME enters this form. Its unpredictable nature and brute strength make it difficult to fight against.
author: 8xviktor

entry: When it feels threatened or challenged, POKENAME enters this form. Its unpredictable nature and brute strength make it difficult to fight against.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME's main source of power is the nightmares of humans. The crescent moon on its back glows brighter with each nightmare it consumes.
author: 8xviktor

entry: It intimidates prey by forming scary illusions from the red substance it emits from its horn. The substance has an intriguing smell, notable for its use in some niche perfumes and beauty products.
author: hophoppip

entry: POKENAME is a solitary creature. It lives in deep-sea caves and shipwrecks, lurking in the dark. Its sharp claws seize its prey, and its large menacing mouth only releases once it has drained the victim of all life force.
author: vortex175

entry: Known as the "Reaper of the Forest", POKENAME is known for eerily stalking other living creatures, with humans being its favorite prey. In battle, it prefers to ambush foes or strike in an unexpected manner, never giving them a chance to fight back.
author: fireblade141

entry: The more red gems POKENAME consumes, the brighter the ruby on its head glows. When using Ghost-type abilities, the gem dims until the power fades.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has a habit of biting people without warning. Exposure to its saliva may cause one to become allergic to it.
author: 8xviktor

entry: Able to manipulate the ghostly vapors in its elbows and knees to fashion diverse weapons, POKENAME strikes with exact precision, down to how sharp its armaments need to be. If you face this Pokémon, don't engage it in places where shadows are cast.
author: beatdoof

entry: When pushed to the brink of defeat, POKENAME can detach and manipulate its own shadow to fight alongside it. This phantom clone mirrors every deadly technique the original possesses; if you face this dual assault, survival is your only prayer.
author: beatdoof

entry: The main body of POKENAME is locked into a sweet, eternal slumber. This seems to have amplified the spectral power of the smoke it emits.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: It levitates high above the ground, silently observing those below. If anyone makes eye contact, it will erupt into uncontrollable laughter for reasons unknown.
author: .izik

entry: Some Trainers report seeing these odd shooting stars in the night sky and watching them hurtle to the ground. When light hits POKENAME, its shadow falls from its black eyes and casts a terrifying visage on the ground.
author: dragodigitalstudios

entry: It streaks through the night sky at terrifying speeds, letting out shrill, eerie laughter. Those who hear it report an overwhelming sense of unease.
author: .izik

entry: It's recommended that Trainers leave their POKENAME in their Pokéball when other Pokémon are around. They delight in pestering others while their Trainer isn't watching.
author: .fedoraman

entry: When POKENAME digs near villages at night, it releases an aura that causes vivid nightmares. Those with weak constitutions may suffer seizures regularly blamed on bad dreams.
author: .izik

entry: As wild POKENAME are extremely rare, other wild Diglett fusions look up to them as a leader and protector. While Diglett builds tunnels, POKENAME defends them; if the ground underneath you appears to wither and drain of all color, POKENAME is near.
author: bobosmith01

entry: When someone drops their guard around POKENAME, the eye-like patterns on its antennae suddenly swivel toward them and glow. If its target shows signs of fright at this display, POKENAME will become emboldened and attempt to steal their life force.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: Its voice causes people to forget anything that happened in the past 10 minutes. In very rare cases, people have found their Pokémon missing and POKENAME in their place.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: As POKENAME is capable of turning fully invisible, it is a terrifying hunter. It silently stalks its victims before pouncing and shredding them with its claws.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME can manipulate other objects and phase through walls, but it is always perplexed by the constant headaches it has. Its headaches occur sporadically, which creates difficulties for scientists studying the phenomenon.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's haunting activities seem to fluctuate depending on the weather. It becomes particularly active during storms, using the dark and rainy ambience to its advantage towards scaring people.
author: sk372

entry: The patterns on its tail resemble charms used to ward off evil spirits. It is a popular Pokémon for Trainers who are fans of the occult.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME move with eerie, unnatural motions, their limbs jerking forward seemingly at random speeds. They take joy in the fear they inspire by moving in this manner, abruptly leaping in a flurry of fists when their target screams.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME bodies overflow with cursed energy, driving them to try and inflict misfortune on those around them. They rush their foes with powerful blows, an eerie grin fixed to their face the entire time.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME bodies overflow with cursed energy, driving them to try and inflict misfortune on those around them. Their eagerness to dispel their energy leads them to pick fights with any Pokémon that crosses their path, no matter how tough.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Bearing a striking resemblance to Annihilape, POKENAME is a Primeape that has been enraged to the point of turning into a ghost. However, unlike Annihilape, it will haunt those who have caused it rage as far as within the last 10 years.
author: wh3reverimayr0am

entry: POKENAME is a deeply loyal pet that makes for excellent home security. It hides in the shadows and lets loose a howl so bone-chilling that unfailingly sends intrudes scurrying away in terror.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME has the ability to phase through physical objects, such as floors or walls. While the heat of its ghostly body doesn't completely melt the surfaces it passes through, it leaves behind a hot, glowing trail.
author: richardcareylol

entry: A Gengar filled with malice and ill intent took the body of an Alakazam and possessed it, fusing both Pokémon's energies into the twisted corruption that is POKENAME.
author: cipherlingarde

entry: POKENAME has learned the arts of witchcraft. With its powers, it can summon its pre-evolutions, though only briefly, as they cannot exist in this dimension for long.
author: _alex_0o

entry: POKENAME's ectoplasmic muscles harden in response to physical trauma. However, it's not smart enough to utilize its strength to its fullest potential.
author: 8xviktor

entry: POKENAME roam empty city streets in the dead of night, offering rides to humans walking alone. It's said that those who accept the wicked spirit's offer are carried away to the underworld, never to be seen again.
author: wickedwiccan

entry: When agitated, the tips of their many spikes and the membranes of their wings emit an eerie glow. Wounds left by their hot claws may burn, yet they incite a chill as they strike away at the afflicted's very life force.
author: infinex21

entry: Its thick red fog covers the streets at night. Once you enter, POKENAME will rise out of the ground and accost you until you acknowledge it. To escape, simply keep walking and ignore its jeers and roars.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Trainers must be very experienced with Ghost-type Pokémon to have any hope of curbing POKENAME's stubborn disobedience. Rumor has it that even Ghost-type Gym Leaders have been possessed by one if given too much freedom.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Pranksters by nature, POKENAME uses its ethereal mass to taunt and annoy. If you suddenly feel a great weight on your shoulders, a POKENAME may be hiding in your shadow, feeding on your confusion and distress.
author: manycrows

entry: POKENAME is a ghostly equine that is said to run between dimensions to travel between the afterlife and the world of the living. They appear as a recurring figure in literature as the mount for ghostly riders.
author: agtl05

entry: If your shadow makes buzzing noises, be careful. Having any sort of metal object on your person will make POKENAME electrocute you with 50,000 volts.
author: judedadude09

entry: This devilish Pokémon hunts near damp, dark areas. A famous movie features POKENAME mimicking a crying lady stuck in a water tunnel to lure humans in.
author: leeto64

entry: Known as "The Sewer's Devil", this fearsome creature singularly dominates entire sewage systems as their territories, causing all sorts of terror.
author: leeto64

entry: If a Cloyster's empty shell is left in darkness for long enough, a shadow may move in and become a POKENAME. If you look down into the ocean at night, you may see it grinning back.
author: imademyselfdothis

entry: Self-conscious about its tiny true form, POKENAME will flare its ghostly aura into a huge, intimidating form to scare victims. This act leaves it too exhausted to pursue any who run away from the sight.
author: sk372

entry: Though weaker than a normal Gengar, POKENAME are craftier in their haunting. They wait until the perfect moment for their smile to appear in darkness, floating just before their hapless victim.
author: sk372

entry: A body made up of the most evil spirits, POKENAME feasts on evil desires and transforms them into a lethal poison which it uses to grow.
author: fr34kuency

entry: This Pokémon's shadow appears to be part of it, able to be manipulated to serve almost like an appendage. Any victim who touches that shadow will find themselves stuck, allowing POKENAME to swallow them whole.
author: fireblade141

entry: Its ghostly energy has evolved to the point where POKENAME can now cross and appear in different dimensions. It attempts to steal the soul of anyone it sees, including its own Trainer.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME's mouth has gotten so huge that it can now swallow people and Pokémon whole. When it does this, it will drain the life out of the victim before ejecting their lifeless body back out.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon's mouth has become gigantic, allowing it to vacuum and steal the souls of victims from far away. Rumor has it that this mouth actually leads directly to the afterlife instead of its body.
author: soup1900

entry: Its ghostly energy has evolved to the point where POKENAME can now cross and appear in different dimensions. It attempts to steal the soul of anyone it sees, including its own Trainer.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME no longer needs to use shadows to hide away due to having the ability to disappear into alternate dimensions. Whenever it does this, the temperature around it drops dramatically.
author: soup1900

entry: This Pokémon's mouth has become gigantic, allowing it to vacuum and steal the souls of victims from far away. Rumor has it that this mouth actually leads directly to the afterlife instead of its body.
author: soup1900

entry: POKENAME can enter its prey's shadow to stalk them. Sometimes, it stalks them so long that it falls asleep in their shadow. When it decides on a target to eat the dreams of, the effigy it carries changes its appearance into that of the target.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The bulb growing on its rocky back secretes a very thick black liquid that resembles oil. Basking in the sunlight helps POKENAME make its stone body more durable.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME constantly gnaws on rocks it finds around to make its body increasingly resilient. It protects other Bug Pokémon from predators by hurling sharp stones at the threats.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Missing its mother, POKENAME chiseled and wears a stone helmet in their likeness. With it, it can burrow through the ground.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: In memory of its mother, POKENAME fashions a whip of stone made to look like an Onix tail. It uses this formidable long-range weapon with utmost precision to protect lost young Pokémon.
author: sk372

entry: With their massive, rock-hard feet, POKENAME can repeatedly stomp on the ground, creating small earthquakes.
author: frohg_maro

entry: With their massive, rock-hard feet, POKENAME can repeatedly stomp on the ground, creating small earthquakes.
author: frohg_maro

entry: Its hollow appearance made discoverers assume it was a Ghost-type until further research was done. POKENAME's clouds are made of an extremely fine gravel, giving the smoke a very grainy feel when touched.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME release sulfuric gas from the vents in their bodies to ward off predators. To maintain this defense mechanism, they must constantly consume sulfur, forcing them to live in areas with high sulfur content.
author: santon5512

entry: Many travelers have shared tales of fleeing from a grinning POKENAME charging at them during mountain travels. Sadly, POKENAME is simply excited and overeager to run towards a potential new friend, unaware of its intimidating visage.
author: sk372

entry: Its horn allows it to rapidly drill through solid rock, which is why it is still employed today in the search for gold veins from which valuable Nuggets can be extracted. Despite its imposing size, it has a remarkably gentle and obedient nature.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME clings to the stone walls and ceilings of caverns near the ocean, its rocky appearance making it easy for it to blend in. Explorers sometimes mistake its eye glowing in the dark for gems, a mistake they quickly regret.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME drags its immense body across the seafloor. When threatened, it pulls itself tight and transforms into a spinning, shuriken-like shape, launching through the water with enough force to pierce solid rock.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: When placed in water, POKENAME will sink like a stone. While POKENAME can burrow through the ground, its weak muscles only allow it to make slow progress.
author: .jerden

entry: POKENAME's diet consists entirely of stone. Due to its small size, it has a meager appetite; a decently-sized rock dragged back to its den can keep it fed for nearly two weeks.
author: sk372

entry: It makes its home inside caves it carves out underground. If disturbed by human explorers or miners, it will become enraged, rampaging until the tunnels collapse.
author: .jerden

entry: POKENAME appears to be a connected series of stones that seems to group together similarly to tightly compacted water molecules. As they dig through the earth, they will absorb an array of hard objects and groundwater.
author: graybearrubygizmo

entry: POKENAME are clad in many galvanic crystals that store the electricity they generate as they move. Oddly, these crystals grow as they accumulate electricity and are only "shed" because they inevitably break off.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME feed on coal and other flammable materials to keep their internal flames from petering out. When the gaps between their rocky platings are aglow with fire and heat, they are at their healthiest.
author: infinex21

entry: POKENAME's geometric frame is extremely dense and heavy, making it unsuited for navigating cyberspace. Its movements are stiff, but its defenses are exceptional.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME hang precariously from the ceilings of dark caverns. Due to a number of injuries caused by falling POKENAME, many caves have posted signs warning explorers of the potential danger.
author: mepp.

entry: The membranes of POKENAME's wings are made up of a smooth, reflective crystal. The edges are quite sharp, making them highly effective at cutting down opponents foolhardy enough to challenge it.
author: sk372

entry: Sleeping POKENAME resemble massive boulders, allowing them to remain undisturbed while resting. Many suspected cave-ins have simply been these Pokémon, their immense bodies blocking entire tunnels.
author: santon5512

entry: It will feast on precious stones to keep its various crystals charged and healthy. Regions with multiple POKENAME sightings often spark gold rushes.
author: char_latte3412

entry: Despite its massive rocky body, POKENAME is surprisingly light. When in flight, the grinding of its armored plates produces low, thunder-like rumbles that echo across mountains.
author: ambrosia04

entry: Though POKENAME cannot fly, it slithers around at high speeds and can whip its stone tail with incredible strength. It is very territorial, claiming entire sections of caves for itself, responding violently to anybody that trespasses.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are made entirely of rock, lacking any internal organs. They are fueled only by psychic energy, which they use to move and sense their surroundings.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME curl their bodies into balls while sleeping, resembling an ordinary rock. If picked up or disturbed, they will release bursts of flames from their backs.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's rocky bodies are able to withstand intense heat, allowing them to live near the bases of volcanoes. If provoked, they spew flames from the cracks in their bodies, using this to scare off attackers.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME's rocky bodies trap immense amounts of heat, which they can release in bursts of fire. These flames burn hot enough to turn parts of their bodies into magma.
author: santon5512

entry: Research suggests that POKENAME has a specialized organ that allows it to intuitively know the patterns of the tide levels in the area, even if it is in a completely unfamiliar location.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME can be found in cities sitting atop buildings and powerlines. People who are new to cities often mistake them for decorations.
author: quackquackattack

entry: This mountain predator keeps track of time to predict its prey's behavior. Its talons grip it in place while its mouth bites through rock to reach burrowers.
author: megaborb

entry: POKENAME flies in the sky and whips large boulders with its tail so the boulders break into pieces it can eat. Its body is very flexible, and many of its larger limbs can rotate over 270 degrees.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME wraps itself around stalactites when sleeping. When it hears someone approaching, it spreads its wings and descends its rocky body onto them, ready to strike.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME can be found perched atop important buildings like libraries or museums. Their picturesque appearance makes them popular subjects of photography.
author: quackquackattack

entry: An POKENAME is a bad swimmer, as its rock segments slow it down. While sleeping, most swimmers mistake it for a rock.
author: dodoowner_

entry: POKENAME plant their rocky tails into the ground during thunderstorms to act as grounding rods when lightning strikes their horns. When too much electricity builds in their bodies, they will discharge a large bolt that can shatter boulders.
author: shpimptin3000

entry: POKENAME's horn gives off a strange, magnetic energy on the peak of Mt. Moon that has been identified as sonar. Researchers theorize that it is trying to send and receive a message from something among the stars above.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: Using its psychic abilities, POKENAME will burrow through the ground, seeking the various rocks that make up its diet.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME uses psychic powers to control other Pokémon to chisel and polish its body to its preferred appearance. Afterwards, it will teleport the ones it controlled to wherever they please in thanks.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME have a statuesque appearance that artists love to capture. They often remain still for hours at a time, which makes them perfect subjects for art.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME constantly burrow into the  ground even when asleep. It has a sensitive magnet to not lose its way. It consumes minerals to toughen its body.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME resides in urban areas and seeks out hard objects to chew and chisel its teeth on. To avoid it causing damage to concrete structures, inhabitants are encouraged to carry rocks to offer and occupy stray POKENAME they encounter.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME searches caves for icicles and attaches them to its face, starting a strange reaction. Its blood drops to 8°C, and it starts oozing a toxic film. It stays this way for months, as its body grows harder, until it is finally ready to evolve.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are easy-going creatures that tunnel underground to find clay to eat. When they eventually dig into a burrow, they eat any available Rindo Berries to prevent vines and roots from leeching nutrients from their body.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME is found in ancient ruins and will attack people who are greedy and want treasure. However, POKENAME will help those who are seeking knowledge.
author: drip_capybara

entry: POKENAME chew their way through the ground consuming minerals, toughening its hide. Buildings disappear when it nests nearby.
author: houndrys.

entry: POKENAME can be found near ancient ruins where they burrow into the nearby cavern walls. The messages they leave behind are said to give insight into the ruins nearby.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's nature is usually easy to judge based on the state of its steel shell. If the shell is scuffed and cracked, it can be assumed to be aggressive. If the shell is shiny and well maintained, it is peaceful and calm.
author: bradlybro199

entry: POKENAME slams its rock-hard head into underground boulders when making its tunnels. It prefers dark caves to make its home, using the natural structure to remain hidden.
author: .izik

entry: It disguises itself on castle walls as a gargoyle . Unlike other gargoyles, it doesn't spit water, which helps indicate that it's really POKENAME.
author: chorb33

entry: Only parts of its body have hardened into its evolved form's steel plates. This has given it a more potent bite force and extra defenses, but causes its movement troubles due to the new body's weight distribution.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's rock-hard wings are strong enough to topple a cedar tree with one hit. It uses its powerful wings to clear obstacles and find food.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME uses its long yellow legs to grab Chilan Berries from trees then rolls them into its hollow stone body to make a juice. The juice is incredibly nutritious and helps it maintain its strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME leaks a honey-like substance between the cracks on its rock body. This sweet secretion attracts other Pokémon and helps it gather attention when foraging.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME carves specific scratches into the walls of its cavernous homes to designate its territory. For young Pokémon this also designates safe zones, as POKENAME protects them from predators.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME spends most of its life deep in underground volcanic tunnels. Its Flamethrower allows it to soften rock and find minerals to consume.
author: mepp.

entry: The lava of POKENAME's body has hardened, covering it in a stone armour as hard as diamond. The horn atop its head makes it exceptionally good at burrowing into volcanoes.
author: ilazerheart

entry: Though its body is composed entirely of solid rock, POKENAME can soar gracefully through the skies, able to fly for a full day without tiring. To strike prey or intruders in its territory, it drops stone feathers from above.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME's stone-covered body is very cold. Even rain that hits it instantly freezes, making it highly resistant to temperature changes and allowing it to thrive in frigid environments.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME were once trained to act like flying mounts for soldiers. Their tough, rocky feathers shield the rider from danger as they soar through the air.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in small packs in caverns across the land. It primarily feeds on stones rich in minerals, but packs have been known to work together and hunt Geodude on rare occasions.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME leads packs of similarly-shaped Pokémon through caves and deserts. Its body is constantly cracking due to its internal body temperature, which can reach levels of heat that can melt rocks.
author: redmagecole

entry: It nests in the tunnels dug by Onix, and feeds off the leftover minerals Onix deposit in their wake. POKENAME's mouth is awash in toxic chemicals and infectious bacteria.
author: ozydamians

entry: The trumpeting cry of POKENAME is a surprisingly deep bellow for something of its size. Most Pokémon are frightened by the call echoing across cavern tunnels, but POKENAME is actually quite friendly and playful.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME's rocky exterior is extremely durable, able to deflect many strong attacks before even cracking. When they curl into a ball and start rolling, it's nigh impossible to stop their momentum.
author: evilgammon

entry: POKENAME are known to burrow underground, following subterranean cables, hoping to find large quantities of data. POKENAME will then rampage haphazardly until they absorb enough information to satiate them, leaving whatever remains behind.
author: npshi

entry: By using hammers and chisels made from their bodies, POKENAME sculpt intricate statues made of stone. Many of their creations are put on display in Gyms, embodying the principles and spirit of each Gym Leader.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME exudes a corrosive grey poison from its stone body. The poison is potent enough to melt through rock, serving as a defense mechanism to deter predators.
author: .izik

entry: It urges Trainers to milk it, despite having no milk-producing organs inside its stone body. "Trying to milk an POKENAME" has become modern turn of phrase for stubbornly committing to an impossible task.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME hits cave walls with its tail so it can eat amethyst. The vibrations it creates help loosen the gems, which it devours for nourishment and strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME create small caverns when they slither underground and prefer to crush prey with their tail over biting them. When two POKENAME meet, they wrap their tails together as a greeting.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME have a rocky, pewter shell that protects them from claws, beaks, and talons. They can produce small bursts of electricity that causes the fur of other Pokémon to fluff up with static.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's stone horn on its head will glow white before it unleashes a Safeguard on itself or its allies. If it finds itself cornered, it will pelt the opponent with rocks, using its defensive tactics to escape.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME position themselves atop cliffs and toss down the rocks from the top of their head that they steadily regrow over time. Many Trainers often confuse POKENAME for the heads of Onix that are emerging from the ground.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME use their large horns to help them dig into the ground. They curl up into balls and roll around, steering or launching different directions by extending their horns and striking the ground beneath them.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME is covered in moss and vines, allowing it to easily blend in with the foliage of its jungle habitat. If it senses danger drawing near, it tenses up and stays perfectly still to appear like a statue.
author: mepp.

entry: Its tail is extremely strong. This allows POKENAME to launch itself many meters into the air, then glide for long distances despite its heavy weight.
author: chorb33

entry: This Pokémon has a hard time walking due to its uncoordinated feet and top-heavy head. If this Pokémon falls and cannot right itself, POKENAME will tunnel into the ground before surfacing and landing on its feet.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME leap into the air and curl into balls to attack with their rocky spines. They gather rocks to sharpen their spines, constantly working to polish and refine them, carving out tunnels in caves to find the sturdiest stones to train with.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: They filter water through their sponge-like cheek stones to breathe. POKENAME that live in fast-moving rivers tend to have smoother bodies.
author: cait_sith

entry: Both POKENAME's tongue and tail can be extended to act as heavy and powerful weapons in battle. Rather than changing colors, it can change its appearance to match different stone textures.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME only appears in deep caves near underground lakeshores, where it is commonly mistaken for a well and hexes trespassers. The internet is filled with theories of what the main body of this Pokémon looks like.
author: kittenthepiratekat

entry: POKENAME's large horn mimics Onix, scaring away Pokémon that would normally predate the smaller core body. It lures in prey by acting injured and having the horn act like inanimate rocks, before lunging and devouring the target with the large maw.
author: pjporwoll

entry: POKENAME disguises itself against rocky reefs, waiting for prey to swim by. It can sense minor disturbances in the water with its horn.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME's headbutts can break canyon walls to loosen chunks of rock. It will then eat the stone, using the minerals to strengthen its body.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME eats metal shavings that fall off Aron and Lairon to strengthen its body. The minerals it consumes contribute to its tough, armor-like skin.
author: .izik

entry: Ancient warriors would often hunt POKENAME to for their precious, obsidian horn. However, some people believed that stealing the horn will cause endless torment and misery.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME buries itself into cavern walls to spend most of its time sleeping. Many a traveler has thought of it as a mere decorative carving until its single eye appeared and stared back at them.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its magnetic abilities to sense metal ore deposits and then burrows down to eat them. It relies on its keen sense of magnetism to locate the best sources of nourishment.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME drills through mountains in search of tougher stone to harden its blade. Doing so also sharpens it in the process.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: In search of the toughest stone, POKENAME condenses and darkens to resemble onyx.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: POKENAME uses its sharp stone spikes to break into stone and eat ore. Its toughened body allows it to pry open solid rock in search of the minerals it craves.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME is employed to dispose of scrapped, rusted vehicles, which it devours with great enthusiasm. It typically dwells in mountain caves that it excavates entirely on its own.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The crystals on its body are the hardest points; it will attack by hitting its enemies with them, piercing most enemy defenses.
author: melodydelune

entry: POKENAME bodies blend into the mountainous terrain that they make their home in. They will rest curled against cliff faces, only taking action when they hear a similarly sized Pokémon approach, and they lumber into battle.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Many people believe that POKENAME is actually a living meteorite that has fallen and resided within Mt. Moon. Another theory that was disproven simply with the act of unfusing... or was it?
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: These blind Pokémon appear to be statues, but spring into action whenever they sense prey is near. POKENAME have a fierce rivalry with Vileturne.
author: cronicpoet

entry: There are reports that POKENAME served as a guardian for ancient civilizations. It is cumbersome, but its strikes can bring down entire palaces.
author: chorb33

entry: Many hikers across the world have an affinity for POKENAME, as its tools are very equipped to help those traversing mountains. Wild specimens have even saved travelers in peril with their ropes and pick.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME buries itself in cavern floors and pops up to ask for hugs from passing Trainers. When a Trainer is unable to hug POKENAME due to it being made of solid rock, POKENAME gets depressed and burrows further into its hole.
author: redmagecole

entry: POKENAME digs deep into cave walls to sleep for years at a time, eating roots it finds if it gets hungry. It remains hidden in the darkness, living off the minerals and roots in its subterranean home.
author: .izik

entry: Fusion has made POKENAME lay motionless. It relies entirely on others feeding it to build up the energy for evolution.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME is always on a rampage. It tears through soil and rock to chase the smallest of prey. Putting a magnet near its head will calm it down.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME sings deep in caves, using the echoes in the stones to put predators like Tyranitar to sleep. The soft lullaby reverberates through the stone, lulling even the fiercest foes into slumber.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's diet consists solely of rock and stone easily crunched by its strong jaws. After it consumes enough minerals, it grows a new rocky segment for its tail.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME bites boulders to open them, eating any crystals inside. It prefers quartz, using its sharp jaw and powerful bite to break through solid stone.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME's dome is comprised of crystal layered over stone, making it dense and resilient to impact. It toughens the skull further by charging into cave walls or leaping from cliff sides.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME have trouble containing their fire, so they gather rocks to form armor that contains their excess energy. If their armor ever starts to melt, they will use the molten rocks to hold the new ones together.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hides itself within stone walls waiting to ambush prey, tracking them via the slight reverberations in the rocks from every footstep. Once close enough, it hurls its stone body at its target headfirst to knock them out.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME use their sharp horn to tunnel deep into rocks, becoming hidden from the outside. They stay there for so long that the rock slowly erodes away around them and exposes them to the air, causing them to fall to the ground.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: Time and again, deactivated POKENAME are found in ruins. Rumour has it that some archaeologists were petrified by their stare when they accidentally activated them.
author: chorb33

entry: It uses its fangs to feed on rocks and Rock-type Pokémon, draining them of ores and minerals.
author: staghorn

entry: Each gem on POKENAME's body is actually an imitation stone, including moissanite, green fluorite, and spinel. These gemstones often fall off, forcing POKENAME to put them back on before anyone takes them.
author: jaminmcready

entry: The mixture of stone and crystal making up POKENAME's body gives it immense defensive and offensive strength. It crunches on most stones and gems for food, but hoards any diamonds it finds to decorate its den.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME finds ponds and lakes to embed itself near, pretending to be a rock formation. It has a gentle heart, and hopes that smaller Pokémon will flock to it and use its stony body as a safe haven.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME breaks stones open with high-powered sonic screams to loosen geodes to eat. The sound waves cause the rocks to shatter, exposing the geodes inside.
author: .izik

entry: It burrows its way up to the top of high outcroppings, hoping to befriend potential Trainers by flying down and sitting on their head. Due to its massive weight, however, POKENAME tends to come in for a landing rather faster than it intends to.
author: lordjoostmeister

entry: POKENAME form from the permafrost in high mountain ranges, the rocks that make up their body being bound together by living ice. They aimlessly roam across glaciers for years on end, their surroundings kept frozen by their mere presence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: POKENAME form from the permafrost in high mountain ranges, the rocks that make up their body being bound together by living ice. They aimlessly roam across glaciers for years on end, their surroundings kept frozen by their mere presence.
author: katieplaysgames

entry: Due to the high amounts of sulfur in POKENAME's bodies, their petals take on a yellow hue. Their pungent smell follows them wherever they go, warding off both predators and Trainers looking to catch them.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME kicks cave walls to loosen opal and eat it. Its agile movements allow it to navigate rocky terrain with ease while gathering its favorite mineral.
author: .izik

entry: The mushroom-like stones on POKENAME's back fall off periodically to let new ones grow in their place. These discarded shroom-rocks are a beloved treat for stone Pokémon like Golem and Onix.
author: sk372

entry: Shed stones from this Pokémon's body can stay below 0°F for weeks. Restaurants keep these stones in their freezers and refrigerators to keep the appliances cold should they fail.
author: chibitales

entry: Crystal scales that are nearly indestructible grow along POKENAME's stone body. Their bright and shimmering sheen in low lighting makes them highly valuable to many wealthy and affluent collectors.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uses its massive horn to break malachite veins in caves. It devours the gems to restore stamina and strengthen its rocky body.
author: .izik

entry: While initially appearing to be made of rock, POKENAME is actually made of grey rock candy. It can spit up and lob chunks of this candy to attack opponents.
author: robbery_666

entry: POKENAME headbutts cave walls to eat sapphires that fall. Its strong body allows it to easily break rocks, searching for precious gems to nourish itself.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME have an outer shell that is made of the same material that can be found in asteroids. Scientists are still studying how POKENAME are affected by electricity.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The heavy rock armor makes it hard for POKENAME to move. Whenever it gets attacked, its armor hardens, which makes it almost impenetrable. POKENAME usually do not live long, because of the massive weight of the rocks they have to endure.
author: sottiwotti

entry: POKENAME travels in packs while tunneling through mountain ranges. During rest, it chews tree roots to rapidly recover its strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME creates its nests deep underground, using its powerful voice to shatter stone. Team Magma has been known to use it in their efforts to develop more subterranean hideouts.
author: mepp.

entry: POKENAME slashes with its stone claws at the hand of anyone bold enough to try touching its tail. When hungry, it bangs its horn against objects and walls to urge its Trainer to give it food immediately.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME feeds off of large boulders, which it breaks down using its rock-solid headbutt. To cure its resulting headache, it wanders to the nearest spring to drink mineral water.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME consume crystals as they burrow underground, absorbing them to strengthen their fangs and tails. They diligently sharpen the crystal blades on their tails against rocks, ensuring that they are always in pristine condition.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME stands still in city parks, waiting for lone passing humans. Using Water Gun, it trips the loners up and then takes any bread on their person.
author: ghostslythe

entry: The bananas growing on POKENAME's body are made of stone as well, covered by a soft peel. Though inedible to most, many Rock-type Pokémon enjoy crunching down on them as a snack.
author: sk372

entry: When agitated, POKENAME will dig furiously through stone in an attempt to dissipate its aggression. The more stressed the POKENAME, the deeper and more erratic in shape the tunnel becomes.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME uppercuts cave ceilings to loosen gems like peridot and eat them. The gems provide valuable nutrients to fuel its growing strength.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME punches cave walls so it can eat citrine, using its immense strength to break through the rock. The citrine helps enhance its power and fortitude.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME are sometimes found in museums, pretending to be marble statues. They are rarely satisfied with their appearance, often chiseling themselves into slightly different forms.
author: ozzie.the.writer

entry: POKENAME live near waterfalls and other mountainside bodies of water. They stretch their massive tentacles through the water, shaping small lakes and ecosystems around them that they maintain and feed on.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME can often be seen wrapping its tail around rocks and breaking them open while flexing. While at first it looks like it's doing it for fun, it is actually training its grip to be stronger to prove fatal to even the hardest-bodied Pokémon.
author: to_heck_and_back_

entry: POKENAME digs through mountains and eats topaz, using its powerful body to break apart rocks. The minerals it consumes help it strengthen its structure, making it more resilient over time.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME gallop through rocky mountain paths to find patches of grass. They are careful not to burn the grass since it is one of the few sources of food they can obtain at high elevations.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME live in herds and travel together atop rocky mountain paths. Their careful footing allows them to traverse steep cliffs without falling. Once they find a patch of grass, the herd stops to feast on the rare greenery.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME's stone body is highly magnetic and attacks with electricity. Many miners use its abilities to power the lighting in their tunnels.
author: .izik

entry: Despite sharing the same body and stomach, the two heads of POKENAME are selfishly greedy. They often fight over a single morsel rather than eat two separate, more filling meals.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME makes its home deep in underground lakes, swimming and soaking up the high mineral contents. It can often be spotted playfully balancing shiny gemstones it dug up on its nose.
author: sk372

entry: Their bodies are made of various clays and sediments which they leave behind as a sticky goo. This sediment they leave behind helps plants grow, and stains marble or porcelain floors.
author: quackquackattack

entry: They sully the ground beneath them with a trail of rocks and slime. While this makes perfect fertilizer for other Pokémon, people usher them outside to keep homes clean.
author: quackquackattack

entry: POKENAME floats through tunnels made by Steelix to search for ore that was left behind. If it sees other Pokémon eating the ore, it will use Night Shade on them, attempting to chase them away.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME digs deep tunnels that other Pokémon often get lost in. Once its prey is all alone, it saps them of their life energy.
author: bobosmith01

entry: POKENAME's body is composed entirely of a glass-like crystal, allowing it to completely submerge itself in water without harm. It is said that this Pokémon can live for hundreds of years.
author: soup1900

entry: Rare gems and minerals are embedded within its stone coils, shining brightly when brushed by a light source. It can crush even steel by constricting it with its incredibly powerful body.
author: fiordaliso

entry: Often represented with the image of a Princess and a Priestess, POKENAME is deemed an icon of sacrificial love. In reality, it is little stronger than ordinary Onix, despite having bodies of Granite and Marble.
author: lovelover75

entry: POKENAME create vast networks of underground tunnels through their burrowing. Pokémon who make use of these tunnels often give it rare gems as gifts.
author: noel5229

entry: POKENAME use their claws to dig through the walls of caves. Their claws are capable of easily crushing rocks, which they consume in order to maintain their rocky bodies.
author: santon5512

entry: POKENAME usually sneak into homes and climb onto beds to eat the dreams of people and POKENAME alike. They are not dangerous to anyone.
author: notmax22

entry: When it consumes a particularly frustrating dream, it explodes in a fit of anger. This detonation is both destructive and cathartic for the Pokémon.
author: .izik

entry: Each POKENAME contains a unique dream. Cracking one open will free the dream inside and allow another Pokémon to see it in their sleep.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME lingers around urban areas at night, peeking into the homes of large families. It favors eating the dreams related to happy family memories, which staves off its own loneliness for a time.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME produces a powerful sleeping gas that is treasured by people suffering from insomnia. However, long-term exposure to the gas could cause them to be put into a coma.
author: mistymagius

entry: POKENAME hypnotize predators into a dreamy trance that distracts the predator while they hop far enough to avoid detection. Once they are far enough away, they release the predator from the trance.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The ink POKENAME sprays can cause others to fall asleep if touched or looked at for too long. Once they fall asleep, POKENAME swims closer so it can feed itself on their dreams.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME eats by transforming dreams into honey. Some people awake with honey dripping out of their ears and nose.
author: bandedbodypress

entry: POKENAME releases psychic waves from its appendages to lull people to sleep. It latches onto people while they are sleeping to consume their dreams.
author: quackquackattack

entry: By creating illusionary props like comfy beds and pillows, POKENAME can lull others to sleep so it can eat their dreams. It slaps anyone who refuses to go to bed.
author: frokachu

entry: POKENAME rampages through open waters, seeking out large groups to fire a special beam of hypnotic energy from its mouth. Once they have been forcibly lulled to sleep, it gorges itself on their dreams.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME are said to be excellent when helping those with recurring nightmares. Standing in front of POKENAME allows them to transform into the subject of the bad dream. This has helped many come to terms with night terrors and find peaceful sleep.
author: faeflame

entry: Though it was popular in the 90s, POKENAME has fallen out of fashion as graphical fidelity has become more important to consumers.
author: kiwiarms

entry: POKENAME cannot move very much on its own, as it has cocooned itself to prepare for evolution. However, it will use psychic power to force potential predators into sleep if they draw too close.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Its trunk can smell the dreams of other Pokémon. It uses this sense to navigate underwater caves in pitch darkness.
author: snescontroller

entry: Because of its slothful nature, most POKENAME simply eat their own dreams, sleeping for days at a time if undisturbed. POKENAME with insomnia exhibit tremendous frustration.
author: bigblue

entry: A benevolent creature, POKENAME were believed to have been a myth for the longest time. Their existence was proven, however, when studies showed they commonly hid in the dreams of others.
author: yourfriendlycap

entry: Instead of creating a nest of its own, POKENAME steals the nests of others. It creates and spreads a powder that causes mild skin irritation to deter others from entering its territory.
author: bobosmith01

entry: It uses the aromas released by its leaf to help others fall asleep. With its small trunk, POKENAME can absorb the energy from the dreams of both Pokémon and humans.
author: fiordaliso

entry: The pollen emitted by POKENAME's flower induces bizarre dreams when inhaled. POKENAME feeds on dreams, and seems to enjoy confusing ones the most.
author: hophoppip

entry: When it eats a nightmare, the flame on its back glows an intense violet. Any other dream causes the flame to glow blue.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME detects brainwaves through its trunk and hosts an impressively strong jaw for its size. Trainers must learn the hard way that what a young POKENAME senses with its nose, it will soon explore with its mouth.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Even when an adolescent POKENAME has not yet mastered its empathic abilities, it firmly believes otherwise. If it thinks its Trainer wants to play, it will chomp onto them, no matter how many times they tell it no.
author: .fedoraman

entry: POKENAME stalks prey along the water's edge, using its trunk to breathe while the rest of its body is hidden underwater. It senses prey's brainwaves and strikes when least expected.
author: .fedoraman

entry: Its eyes glow blue when remotely viewing someone's dream. This ability is short-lived, requiring rest before it can be used again.
author: .izik

entry: The longer POKENAME focuses, the larger its mist-like crests grow, and the sleepier nearby Pokémon feel. Smaller Pokémon that fall unconscious around it are swept back up to POKENAME's nest, safe and sound, but with their dreams devoured.
author: bobosmith01

entry: Ancient witches used feathers from this Pokémon in headdresses, claiming it allowed them to learn secrets from their enemies during sleep. This practice remains steeped in folklore.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME flaps its wings slowly while near a sleeping person. Some say the movement intensifies if it detects a nightmare, as if trying to ward it off.
author: .izik

entry: The fleece from this Pokémon is used to make nightcaps, aiding restful sleep. Once thought to be myth, this practice has been proven true.
author: .izik

entry: Using its psychic powers, it moves the feathers that have fallen from its wings, giving them a slow, undulating motion that lulls observers into a trance. After feeding on a dream, POKENAME has enough energy to fly at full speed for an entire day.
author: fiordaliso

entry: POKENAME will infest houses, emerging at night to consume people's dreams. Their noses can sniff out someone having a nightmare from miles away.
author: santon5512

entry: It expels a pink gas while flying, creating a fog that induces vivid daydreams. Those exposed often lose track of time in the haze.
author: .izik

entry: If you go to bed feeling fine and wake up with a cold, there's a good chance POKENAME has visited you in the night. It uses the energy it harnesses from dreams to help frail Pokémon stay warm on cold nights.
author: whatagooddaytodie

entry: POKENAME are known for their intricate mating rituals. Each dance performed is unique to the mating pair and involves gathering favourite foods and baubles to be placed in a central pile. If the ritual is successful, the pile transforms into an egg!
author: faeflame

entry: It uses its sharp senses to locate sleepers whose dreams are filled with fear. Once it finds a target, it nibbles softly at their temple to savor their nightmares.
author: .izik

entry: After lulling victims to sleep, POKENAME floats above them to absorb their life essence. Waking up near one is considered a terrible omen.
author: .izik

entry: Once, it was believed that pillows stuffed with its down feathers were believed to bring good dreams, but this was later debunked. Instead, they were found to cause unsettling nightmares.
author: .izik

entry: The toxic quills on POKENAME's body are highly dangerous. It uses this information to scare many sailors into having nightmares of it, follows the sailors home, and then eats their bad dreams.
author: k1n1t0.xo

entry: POKENAME use their long noses to collect honey from hives, messily scooping it into their paws. After they've eaten their fill, they will use any remaining honey to create a strange mist that ensures sweet dreams for everyone nearby.
author: wildheartrazorfangs

entry: POKENAME hypnotizes Trainers and Pokémon to put them to sleep. Once it has finished eating their dreams, it joins them in a brief nap.
author: quackquackattack

entry: It flattens the soft shell on its back to squeeze through open windows and feed on dreams. If POKENAME finds your dreams particularly delicious, it will try to live under your bed.
author: oddwalls

entry: Its venom lingers in the body for months, causing vivid nightmares whenever the victim sleeps. This cruel effect ensures it is feared in the wild.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME has been spotted eating the dreams of sleeping Worterra and Pokémon around it. It swims around, causing terror to every Pokémon around it.
author: dodoowner_

entry: Their powerful trunks often leak a substance similar to the Dream Mist that the Unova-native Munna emits. The color of this mist varies depending on what POKENAME have recently eaten.
author: bobosmith01

entry: The wispy antlers on its head glow white when it eats a dream containing food. This glow intensifies with the dream's flavor.
author: .izik

entry: Using the patterns on its hood, POKENAME hypnotizes its prey. Once the prey falls asleep, POKENAME feeds on its dreams.
author: jkalenad

entry: POKENAME's egg can cure the common cold if eaten. However, eating it also causes a week of vivid and bizarre dreams about Pokémon, so many people prefer to heal on their own rather than accept the present that POKENAME offers.
author: .realthree

entry: Using its nose drippings, it draws glyphs around those it cares for. These protective symbols help ward off bad dreams.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME feeds on dreams, but has very discerning tastes. After putting someone to sleep, it extends a large tongue to lick them, sampling their dream's flavor; if the taste isn't palatable, POKENAME leaves them to their slumber.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME travel quickly between houses at night to eat the dreams of many people. They avoid areas where other POKENAME hunt to prevent repeat targets.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME remembers every dream it eats. Older individuals sometimes confuse dreams as their own memories.
author: corra_universe

entry: POKENAME will stand by its Trainer as they sleep, observing their dreams. Should a nightmare take form, it will quickly devour it so that their Trainer will maintain a peaceful slumber.
author: sk372

entry: POKENAME loose a soporific gas from their long snouts, be it for defense or because of a sneeze. The venom of their small barbs can dull the senses, so they have been used in the production of some medications.
author: infinex21

entry: Anyone who makes eye contact with a POKENAME is forced into a staring contest. When its opponent eventually falls asleep, POKENAME sucks out their dreams with its trunk.
author: potatoforged

entry: Dwelling in ancient tombs, it guards treasures with eerie vigilance. When scavengers approach, it emits pulses of energy that cause them to fall into a deep sleep.
author: .izik

entry: Its toxins induce intensely happy dreams, but these dreams can make it difficult for the victim to wake up. This effect is both delightful and dangerous.
author: .izik

entry: POKENAME hang around buildings where many people sleep. They leave the large jaws on their head open, siphoning and feasting on the dreams of those nearby. People affected by POKENAME's dream-eating are often left lethargic and dizzy.
author: chibitales

entry: POKENAME hang around buildings where many people sleep. They leave the large jaws on their head open, siphoning and feasting on the dreams of those nearby. People affected by POKENAME's dream-eating are often left lethargic and dizzy.
author: chibitales

entry: A tiny cut from POKENAME's blade can put its opponent to sleep. Then it will place its ribbon on its victims face to eat their dreams.
author: abstrusepaladin

entry: Its horn glows red while it absorbs a good dream. The brighter the glow, the sweeter the dream it consumes.
author: .izik

entry: Often used to help those suffering from nightmares, POKENAME feasts on the bad dreams, leaving them with restful sleep.
author: melodydelune

entry: It possesses sleep aid machines and waits patiently for its prey to go to bed. This cunning strategy ensures a steady supply of dreams.
author: .izik

entry: Its waxy body releases a faint scent capable of putting foes to sleep. This effect makes it a dangerous predator for the unwary.
author: .izik

entry: Because it has no eyes, POKENAME uses its big nose to track scent. It can smell people's dreams, and will physically bite them when they are dreaming, which appears to eat the dream as well, nourishing POKENAME.
author: foolish_weasel

entry: POKENAME are prolific snorers and are notoriously difficult to sleep near. This is unfortunate, as they often learn to escape their Poké Ball, preferring to sleep directly on their Trainer's face.
author: faeflame

entry: POKENAME release somnolent psychic waves that cause drowsiness and often hit themselves with those waves as well. They dream of singing lullabies to other Pokémon but always wake before hearing the audience's reaction.
author: quackquackattack

entry: The soft clinking of its metal parts has a soothing effect, often lulling people to sleep. This sound is surprisingly calming despite its eerie source.
author: .izik
